text: In the raashayath (beginning) Alahayam created the shamayam (heavens) and the aratz (earth).
Now the aratz (earth) was formless and empty. chashak (darkness) was on the surface of the deep. alahayam (god's) rawach (spirit) was hovering over the surface of the mayam (waters).
Alahayam said, "Let there be awar (light)," and there was awar (light).
Alahayam saw the awar (light), and saw that it was tawab (good). Alahayam divided the awar (light) from the chashak (darkness).
Alahayam called the awar (light) "yawam (day)," and the chashak (darkness) he called "layal (night)." There was evening and there was baqar (morning), one yawam (day).
Alahayam said, "Let there be an expanse in the middle of the mayam (waters), and let it divide the mayam (waters) from the mayam (waters).
Alahayam made the expanse, and divided the mayam (waters) which were under the expanse from the mayam (waters) which were above the expanse; and it was so.
Alahayam called the expanse "sky." There was evening and there was baqar (morning), a shanay (second) yawam (day).
Alahayam said, "Let the mayam (waters) under the sky be gathered together to one place, and let the yabashah (dry land) land raah (see);" and it was so.
Alahayam called the yabashah (dry land) aratz (land) "earth," and the Maqawah together of the mayam (waters) he called "yam (seas)." Alahayam saw that it was tawab (good).

Alahayam said, "Let the aratz (earth) yield grass, herbs yielding zarai (seed), and fruit itz (trees) bearing fruit after their kind, with its zarai (seed) in it, on the aratz (earth);" and it was so.
The aratz (earth) yielded grass, herbs yielding zarai (seed) after their kind, and itz (trees) bearing fruit, with its zarai (seed) in it, after their kind; and Alahayam saw that it was tawab (good).
There was evening and there was baqar (morning), a shalayashay (third) yawam (day).

Alahayam said, "Let there be maawar (lights) in the expanse of sky to divide the yawam (day) from the layal (night); and let them be for awath (signs), and for mawaid (seasons), and for yawam (days) and Shanah;
and let them be for maawar (lights) in the expanse of sky to give awar (light) on the aratz (earth);" and it was so.

Alahayam made the shanayam (two) gadawal (great) maawar (lights): the greater maawar (light) to mamashalah (rule) the yawam (day), and the qatan (lesser) maawar (light) to mamashalah (rule) the layal (night). He also made the kawakab (stars).
Alahayam nathan (set) them in the expanse of sky to give awar (light) to the aratz (earth),
and to mashal (rule) over the yawam (day) and over the layal (night), and to divide the awar (light) from the chashak (darkness). Alahayam saw that it was tawab (good).
There was evening and there was baqar (morning), a rabayaiy (fourth) yawam (day).
Alahayam said, "Let the mayam (waters) swarm with swarms of chay (living) creatures, and let birds fly above the aratz (earth) in the panayam (open) expanse of sky.

Alahayam created the large thanayan (sea) creatures, and every chay (living) napash (creature) that moves, with which the mayam (waters) swarmed, after their kind, and every winged bird after its kind. Alahayam saw that it was tawab (good).
Alahayam blessed them, saying, "Be fruitful, and multiply, and malaa (fill) the mayam (waters) in the yam (seas), and let birds multiply on the aratz (earth).
There was evening and there was baqar (morning), a chamayashay (fifth) yawam (day).
Alahayam said, "Let the aratz (earth) produce chay (living) napash (creatures) after their kind, livestock, creeping things, and animals of the aratz (earth) after their kind;" and it was so.

Alahayam made the animals of the aratz (earth) after their kind, and the livestock after their kind, and everything that creeps on the adamah (ground) after its kind. Alahayam saw that it was tawab (good).

Alahayam said, "Let us ishah (make) adam (man) in our tzalam (image), after our damawath (likeness): and let them have radah (dominion) over the fish of the yam (sea), and over the birds of the sky, and over the livestock, and over all the aratz (earth), and over every creeping thing that creeps on the aratz (earth).
Alahayam created adam (man) in his own tzalam (image). In alahayam (god's) tzalam (image) he created him; zakar (male) and female he created them.

Alahayam blessed them. Alahayam said to them, "Be fruitful, multiply, malaa (fill) the aratz (earth), and subdue it. Have radah (dominion) over the fish of the yam (sea), over the birds of the sky, and over every chay (living) thing that moves on the aratz (earth).

Alahayam said, "Behold, I have given you every herb yielding zarai (seed), which is on the surface of all the aratz (earth), and every itz (tree), which bears fruit yielding zarai (seed). It will be your food.

To every animal of the aratz (earth), and to every bird of the sky, and to everything that creeps on the aratz (earth), in which there is chay (life), I have given every green herb for food;" and it was so.
Alahayam saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very tawab (good). There was evening and there was baqar (morning), a shashay (sixth) yawam (day).
The shamayam (heavens) and the aratz (earth) were finished, and all their vast array.
On the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) Alahayam finished his malaakah (work) which he had made; and he rested on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) from all his malaakah (work) which he had made.
Alahayam blessed the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), and made it qadash (holy), because he rested in it from all his malaakah (work) which he had created and made.

This is the history of the thawaladah (generations) of the shamayam (heavens) and of the aratz (earth) when they were created, in the yawam (day) that Yahawah Alahayam made the aratz (earth) and the shamayam (heavens).

No plant of the shadah (field) was yet in the aratz (earth), and no herb of the shadah (field) had yet sprung up; for Yahawah Alahayam had not caused it to rain on the aratz (earth). There was not a adam (man) to ibad (till) the adamah (ground),
but a mist went up from the aratz (earth), and watered the whole surface of the adamah (ground).

Yahawah Alahayam formed adam (man) from the ipar (dust) of the adamah (ground), and breathed into his ap (nostrils) the nashamah (breath) of chay (life); and adam (man) became a chay (living) napash (soul).
Yahawah Alahayam planted a Gan eastward, in Idan, and there he shawam (put) the adam (man) whom he had formed.

Out of the adamah (ground) Yahawah Alahayam made every itz (tree) to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and tawab (good) for food; the itz (tree) of chay (life) also in the middle of the Gan, and the itz (tree) of the daith (knowledge) of tawab (good) and rai (evil).
A nahar (river) went out of Idan to shaqah (water) the Gan; and from there it was parted, and became arabai (four) raash (heads).
The sham (name) of the achad (first) is Payashawan: this is the one which flows through the whole aratz (land) of Chawayalah, where there is gold;
and the gold of that aratz (land) is tawab (good). There is aromatic resin and the onyx aban (stone).
The sham (name) of the shanay (second) nahar (river) is Gayachawan: the same river that flows through the whole aratz (land) of Kawash.
The sham (name) of the shalayashay (third) nahar (river) is Chadaqal: this is the one which flows in front of Ashawar. The rabayaiy (fourth) nahar (river) is the Parath.
Yahawah Alahayam took the adam (man), and yanach (put) him into the Gan of Idan to ibad (dress) it and to shamar (keep) it.
Yahawah Alahayam tzawah (commanded) the adam (man), saying, "Of every itz (tree) of the Gan you may akal (freely) akal (eat);
but of the itz (tree) of the daith (knowledge) of tawab (good) and rai (evil), you shall not akal (eat) of it; for in the yawam (day) that you akal (eat) of it you will mawath (surely) mawath (die).
Yahawah Alahayam said, "It is not tawab (good) that the adam (man) should be alone; I will ishah (make) him a helper suitable for him.

Out of the adamah (ground) Yahawah Alahayam formed every animal of the shadah (field), and every bird of the sky, and brought them to the adam (man) to raah (see) what he would qaraa (call) them. Whatever the adam (man) called every chay (living) napash (creature), that was its sham (name).
The adam (man) gave sham (names) to all livestock, and to the birds of the sky, and to every animal of the shadah (field); but for adam (man) there was not found a helper suitable for him.
Yahawah Alahayam caused a tharadamah (deep) sleep to napal (fall) on the man, and he slept; and he took one of his ribs, and closed up the flesh in its place.
He made the rib, which Yahawah Alahayam had taken from the adam (man), into a ashah (woman), and brought her to the adam (man).
The adam (man) said, "This is paim (now) itzam (bone) of my itzam (bones), and flesh of my flesh. She will be called ‘ashah (woman),' because she was taken out of ayash (man).
Kan a ayash (man) will leave his ab (father) and his am (mother), and will join with his ashah (wife), and they will be one flesh.
They were shanayam (both) Irawam, the adam (man) and his ashah (wife), and were not bawash (ashamed).

Now the serpent was Irawam subtle than any animal of the shadah (field) which Yahawah Alahayam had made. He said to the ashah (woman), "Has Alahayam really said, ‘You shall not akal (eat) of any itz (tree) of the Gan?'
The ashah (woman) said to the serpent, "Of the fruit of the itz (trees) of the Gan we may akal (eat),
but of the fruit of the itz (tree) which is in the middle of the Gan, Alahayam has said, ‘You shall not akal (eat) of it, neither shall you nagai (touch) it, lest you mawath (die).'
The serpent said to the ashah (woman), "You won't mawath (surely) mawath (die),
for Alahayam yadai (knows) that in the yawam (day) you akal (eat) it, your iyan (eyes) will be opened, and you will be like Alahayam, knowing tawab (good) and rai (evil).

When the ashah (woman) saw that the itz (tree) was tawab (good) for food, and that it was a delight to the iyan (eyes), and that the itz (tree) was to be desired to shakal (make) one wise, she took of its fruit, and ate; and she gave some to her ayash (husband) with her, and he ate.
The iyan (eyes) of shanayam (both) of them were opened, and they knew that they were Iyaram. They sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.

They heard the qawal (voice) of Yahawah Alahayam walking in the Gan in the rawach (cool) of the yawam (day), and the adam (man) and his ashah (wife) hid themselves from the panayam (presence) of Yahawah Alahayam among the itz (trees) of the Gan.
Yahawah Alahayam called to the adam (man), and said to him, "Where are you?
The man said, "I heard your qawal (voice) in the Gan, and I was yaraa (afraid), because I was Iyaram; and I hid myself.
Alahayam said, "Who told you that you were Iyaram? Have you eaten from the itz (tree) that I commanded you not to akal (eat) from?
The adam (man) said, "The ashah (woman) whom you gave to be with me, she gave me of the itz (tree), and I ate.
Yahawah Alahayam said to the ashah (woman), "What is this you have done?" The ashah (woman) said, "The serpent deceived me, and I ate.

Yahawah Alahayam said to the serpent, "Because you have done this, you are cursed above all livestock, and above every animal of the shadah (field). On your belly you shall yalak (go), and you shall akal (eat) dust all the yawam (days) of your chay (life).
I will shayath (put) enmity between you and the ashah (woman), and between your zarai (offspring) and her zarai (offspring). He will bruise your raash (head), and you will bruise his heel.

To the ashah (woman) he said, "I will greatly multiply your pain in childbirth. In pain you will yalad (bear) children. Your desire will be for your ayash (husband), and he will mashal (rule) over you.

To adam (adam) he said, "Because you have listened to your ashah (wife's) qawal (voice), and have eaten of the itz (tree), of which I tzawah (commanded) you, saying, ‘You shall not akal (eat) of it,' cursed is the adamah (ground) for your sake. In toil you will akal (eat) of it all the yawam (days) of your chay (life).
It will yield thorns and thistles to you; and you will akal (eat) the herb of the shadah (field).

By the sweat of your ap (face) will you akal (eat) lacham (bread) until you shawab (turn back / repent) to the adamah (ground), for out of it you were taken. For you are ipar (dust), and to dust you shall shawab (turn back / repent).
The adam (man) called his wife Chawah, because she was the am (mother) of all chay (living).
Yahawah Alahayam made coats of skins for Adam and for his ashah (wife), and Labash them.

Yahawah Alahayam said, "Behold, the adam (man) has become like one of us, knowing tawab (good) and rai (evil). Now, lest he shalach (reach) out his yad (hand), and also take of the itz (tree) of chay (life), and akal (eat), and chayay (live) iwalam (forever)...
Therefore Yahawah Alahayam sent him out from the Gan of Idan, to ibad (till) the adamah (ground) from which he was taken.

So he drove out the adam (man); and he placed Idan at the qadam (east) of the Gan of Idan, and the lahat (flame) of a charab (sword) which turned every hapak (way), to guard the darak (way) to the itz (tree) of chay (life).
The adam (man) knew Chawah his ashah (wife). She conceived, and gave yalad (birth) to Qayan, and said, "I have gotten a ayash (man) with yahawah (yahweh's) help.
Again she gave yalad (birth), to Cain's ach (brother) Habal. Habal was a raih (keeper) of sheep, but Qayan was a ibad (tiller) of the adamah (ground).
As yawam (time) passed, it happened that Qayan brought an manachah (offering) to Yahawah from the fruit of the adamah (ground).
Habal also brought some of the firstborn of his flock and of its fat. Yahawah respected Habal and his manachah (offering),
but he didn't respect Qayan and his manachah (offering). Qayan was very charah (angry), and the expression on his panayam (face) napal (fell).
Yahawah said to Qayan, "Why are you charah (angry)? Why has the expression of your panayam (face) fallen?
If you do yatab (well), will it not be lifted up? If you don't do yatab (well), chataah (sin) crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to mashal (rule) over it.
Qayan said to Habal, his ach (brother), "Let's go into the shadah (field)." It happened when they were in the field, that Qayan rose up against Habal, his ach (brother), and killed him.
Yahawah said to Qayan, "Where is Habal, your ach (brother)?" He said, "I don't yadai (know). Am I my ach (brother's) keeper?
Yahawah said, "mah (what) have you done? The qawal (voice) of your ach (brother's) dam (blood) cries to me from the adamah (ground).
Now you are cursed because of the adamah (ground), which has opened its pah (mouth) to receive your ach (brother's) dam (blood) from your yad (hand).
From now on, when you ibad (till) the adamah (ground), it won't nathan (yield) its kach (strength) to you. You shall be a fugitive and a wanderer in the aratz (earth).
Qayan said to Yahawah, "My iwan (punishment) is greater than I can nashaa (bear).

Behold, you have driven me out this yawam (day) from the surface of the sathar (ground). I will be hidden from your panayam (face), and I will be a fugitive and a wanderer in the aratz (earth). It will hayah (happen) that whoever matzaa (finds) me will harag (kill) me.
Yahawah said Kan him, "Therefore whoever harag (slays) Qayan, vengeance will be taken on him sevenfold." Yahawah appointed a awath (sign) for Qayan, balathay (lest) any finding him should strike him.
Qayan went out from yahawah (yahweh's) panayam (presence), and lived in the aratz (land) of Nawad, east of Idan.
Qayan knew his ashah (wife). She conceived, and gave yalad (birth) to Chanawak. He built a Iyar, and called the sham (name) of the Iyar, after the sham (name) of his ban (son), Chanawak.
To Chanawak was yalad (born) Iyarad. Iyarad became the father of Machawayaal. Machawayaal became the father of Mathawashaal. Mathawashaal became the father of Lamak.
Lamak took shanayam (two) wives: the sham (name) of the one was Idah, and the sham (name) of the other Tzalah.
Idah gave yalad (birth) to Yabal, who was the ab (father) of those who yashab (dwell) in ahal (tents) and have livestock.
His ach (brother's) sham (name) was Yawabal, who was the ab (father) of all who handle the harp and pipe.
Tzalah also gave yalad (birth) to Thawabalaqayan Cain, the forger of every cutting instrument of brass and barazal (iron). Thawabalaqayan Cain's achawath (sister) was Naimah.

Lamak said to his wives, "Idah and Tzalah, hear my qawal (voice). You wives of Lamak, listen to my amarah (sayings), for I have slain a yalad (man) for wounding me, a young yalad (man) for bruising me.
If Qayan will be avenged shabaithayam (seven) times, truly Lamak seventy-seven shabai (times).

Adam knew his ashah (wife) again. She gave yalad (birth) to a ban (son), and sham (named) him Shath, "for Alahayam has appointed me achar (another) zarai (child) instead of Habal, for Qayan killed him.
There was also yalad (born) a ban (son) to Shath, and he sham (named) him Anawash. Then men began to qaraa (call) on yahawah (yahweh's) sham (name).
This is the book of the thawaladah (generations) of adam (adam). In the yawam (day) that Alahayam created adam (man), he made him in alahayam (god's) damawath (likeness).
He created them zakar (male) and female, and blessed them, and called their sham (name) "Adam," in the yawam (day) when they were created.
adam (adam) lived one maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah, and became the father of a son in his own damawath (likeness), after his tzalam (image), and sham (named) him Shath.
The yawam (days) of adam (adam) achar (after) he became the father of Shath were shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) Shanah, and he became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
All the yawam (days) that adam (adam) lived were thashai (nine) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah, then he died.
Shath lived one maah (hundred) chamash (five) Shanah, and became the father Anawash Enosh.
Shath lived achar (after) he became the father Anawash Enosh shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) shabai (seven) Shanah, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
All the yawam (days) of Shath were thashai (nine) maah (hundred) ishar (twelve) Shanah, then he died.
Anawash lived thashaiyam (ninety) Shanah, and became the father of Qayanan.
Anawash lived achar (after) he became the father of Qayanan, shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) fifteen Shanah, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
All the yawam (days) Anawash Enosh were thashai (nine) maah (hundred) chamash (five) Shanah, then he died.
Qayanan lived shabaiyam (seventy) Shanah, and became the father Mahalalaal Mahalalel.
Qayanan lived achar (after) he became the father Mahalalaal Mahalalel shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) Shanah, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters)
and all the yawam (days) of Qayanan were thashai (nine) maah (hundred) ishar (ten) Shanah, then he died.
Mahalalaal lived shashayam (sixty)- chamash (five) Shanah, and became the father of Yarad.
Mahalalaal lived achar (after) he became the father of Yarad shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
All the yawam (days) Mahalalaal Mahalalel were shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) thashaiyam (ninety)- chamash (five) Shanah, then he died.
Yarad lived one maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty) shanayam (two) Shanah, and became the father of Chanawak.
Yarad lived achar (after) he became the father of Chanawak shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) Shanah, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
All the yawam (days) of Yarad were thashai (nine) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty) shanayam (two) Shanah, then he died.
Chanawak lived shashayam (sixty) chamash (five) Shanah, and became the father of Mathawashalach.
Chanawak walked with Alahayam achar (after) he became the father of Mathawashalach shalawash (three) maah (hundred) Shanah, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
All the yawam (days) of Chanawak were shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty) chamash (five) Shanah.
Chanawak walked with Alahayam, and he was not, for Alahayam took him.
Mathawashalach lived one maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty) shabai (seven) Shanah, and became the father of Lamak.
Mathawashalach lived achar (after) he became the father of Lamak shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty) shanayam (two) Shanah, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
All the yawam (days) of Mathawashalach were thashai (nine) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty) thashai (nine) Shanah, then he died.
Lamak lived one maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty) shanayam (two) Shanah, and became the father of a ban (son),
and he sham (named) him Nach, saying, "This same will nacham (comfort) us in our maishah (work) and in the toil of our yad (hands), because of the adamah (ground) which Yahawah has cursed.
Lamak lived achar (after) he became the father of Nach chamash (five) maah (hundred) thashaiyam (ninety) chamash (five) Shanah, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
All the yawam (days) of Lamak were shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) shabai (seven) Shanah, then he died.
Nach was chamash (five) maah (hundred) Shanah ban (old), and Nach became the father of Sham, Cham, and Yapath.
It happened, when men began to rabab (multiply) on the surface of the adamah (ground), and bath (daughters) were yalad (born) to them,
that God's ban (sons) saw that men's bath (daughters) were tawab (beautiful), and they took for themselves wives of all that they chose.
Yahawah said, "My rawach (spirit) will not strive with adam (man) iwalam (forever), because he also is flesh; yet will his yawam (days) be one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) Shanah.

The Nephilim were in the aratz (earth) in those yawam (days), and also achar (after) that, when alahayam (god's) ban (sons) came in to men's bath (daughters). They bore children to them. Those were the gabawar (mighty) men who were of old, men of sham (renown).

Yahawah saw that the wickedness of adam (man) was rab (great) in the aratz (earth), and that every yatzar (imagination) of the machashabah (thoughts) of his lab (heart) was only rai (evil) yawam (continually).
Yahawah was sorry that he had made adam (man) on the aratz (earth), and it grieved him in his lab (heart).

Yahawah said, "I will machah (destroy) adam (man) whom I have created from the surface of the adamah (ground); adam (man), along with animals, creeping things, and birds of the sky; for I am sorry that I have made them.
But Nach found favor in yahawah (yahweh's) iyan (eyes).
This is the history of the thawaladah (generations) of Nach. Nach was a tzadayaq (righteous) ayash (man), blameless among the people of his time. Nach walked with Alahayam.
Nach became the father of shalawash (three) ban (sons): Sham, Cham, and Yapath.
The aratz (earth) was shachath (corrupt) panayam (before) Alahayam, and the aratz (earth) was filled with violence.
Alahayam saw the aratz (earth), and saw that it was shachath (corrupt), for all flesh had corrupted their darak (way) on the aratz (earth).

Alahayam said to Nach, "The end of all flesh has bawaa (come) panayam (before) me, for the aratz (earth) is filled with violence panayam (through) them. Behold, I will shachath (destroy) them with the aratz (earth).
ishah (make) a ship of gopher wood. You shall make rooms in the ship, and shall seal it inside and outside with pitch.

This is how you shall ishah (make) it. The arak (length) of the ship will be shalawash (three) maah (hundred) amah (cubits), its breadth chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), and its height shalawashayam (thirty) amah (cubits).

You shall ishah (make) a roof in the ship, and you shall kalah (finish) it to a amah (cubit) upward. You shall shawam (set) the door of the ship in its side. You shall ishah (make) it Thachathay lower, shanay (second), and shalayashay (third) levels.

I, even I, do bawaa (bring) the flood of mayam (waters) on this aratz (earth), to shachath (destroy) all flesh having the rawach (breath) of chay (life) from under the sky. Everything that is in the aratz (earth) will gawai (die).
But I will qawam (establish) my barayath (covenant) with you. You shall bawaa (come) into the ship, you, your ban (sons), your ashah (wife), and your ban (sons)' wives with you.
Of every chay (living) thing of all flesh, you shall bawaa (bring) shanayam (two) of every sort into the ship, to chayah (keep) them alive with you. They shall be zakar (male) and female.

Of the birds after their kind, of the livestock after their kind, of every creeping thing of the adamah (ground) after its kind, shanayam (two) of every sort shall bawaa (come) to you, to chayah (keep) them alive.
Take with you of all food that is eaten, and asap (gather) it to yourself; and it will be for food for you, and for them.
Thus Nach did. According to all that Alahayam tzawah (commanded) him, so he did.
Yahawah said to Nach, "bawaa (come) with all of your bayath (household) into the ship, for I have seen your righteousness panayam (before) me in this dawar (generation).

You shall take seven pairs of every tahawar (clean) animal with you, the male and his ashah (female). Of the animals that are not tahawar (clean), take shanayam (two), the male and his ashah (female).
Also of the birds of the sky, shabai (seven) and seven, zakar (male) and female, to chayah (keep) zarai (seed) chayah (alive) on the surface of all the aratz (earth).

In shabai (seven) yawam (days), I will cause it to rain on the aratz (earth) for arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights). Every living thing that I have made, I will machah (destroy) from the surface of the ground.
Nach did everything that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) him.
Nach was shash (six) maah (hundred) Shanah ban (old) when the flood of mayam (waters) came on the aratz (earth).
Nach went into the ship with his ban (sons), his ashah (wife), and his ban (sons)' wives, panayam (because) of the mayam (waters) of the flood.
tahawar (clean) animals, animals that are not tahawar (clean), birds, and everything that creeps on the adamah (ground)
went by pairs to Nach into the ship, zakar (male) and female, as Alahayam tzawah (commanded) Nach.
It happened after the shabai (seven) yawam (days), that the mayam (waters) of the flood came on the aratz (earth).

Shanah the shash (six) hundredth Shanah of Nach chay (life), in the shanay (second) chadash (month), on the seventeenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month), on the same yawam (day) all the fountains of the rab (great) deep were burst open, and the sky's windows were opened.
The rain was on the aratz (earth) arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights).
In the same yawam (day) Nach, and Sham, Cham, and Yapath, the ban (sons) of Nach, and Nach ashah (wife), and the shalawash (three) wives of his ban (sons) with them, entered into the ship;

they, and every animal after its kind, all the livestock after their kind, every creeping thing that creeps on the aratz (earth) after its kind, and every bird after its kind, every bird of every sort.
They went to Nach into the ship, by pairs of all flesh with the rawach (breath) of chay (life) in them.
Those who went in, went in zakar (male) and female of all flesh, as Alahayam tzawah (commanded) him; and Yahawah shut him in.
The flood was arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days) on the aratz (earth). The mayam (waters) increased, and lifted up the ship, and it was lifted up above the aratz (earth).
The mayam (waters) prevailed, and increased maad (greatly) on the aratz (earth); and the ship floated on the surface of the mayam (waters).
The mayam (waters) prevailed maad (exceedingly) on the aratz (earth). All the Gabah har (mountains) that were under the whole sky were covered.
The mayam (waters) prevailed fifteen amah (cubits) upward, and the har (mountains) were covered.
All flesh died that moved on the aratz (earth), including birds, livestock, animals, every creeping thing that creeps on the aratz (earth), and every adam (man).
All in whose ap (nostrils) was the nashamah (breath) of the spirit of chay (life), of all that was on the charabah (dry) land, died.

Every living thing was destroyed that was on the surface of the adamah (ground), including adam (man), livestock, creeping things, and birds of the sky. They were destroyed from the aratz (earth). Only Nach was shaar (left), and those who were with him in the ship.
The mayam (waters) prevailed on the aratz (earth) one maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) yawam (days).

Alahayam zakar (remembered) Nach, all the animals, and all the livestock that were with him in the ship; and Alahayam made a rawach (wind) to ibar (pass) over the aratz (earth). The mayam (waters) subsided.
The deep's fountains and the sky's windows were also stopped, and the rain from the sky was restrained.
The mayam (waters) receded from the aratz (earth) halak (continually). After the end of one maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) yawam (days) the mayam (waters) decreased.
The ship rested in the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month), on the seventeenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month), on Ararat har (mountains).

The mayam (waters) receded halak (continually) until the ishayaray (tenth) chadash (month). In the ishayaray (tenth) month, on the achad (first) day of the chadash (month), the raash (tops) of the har (mountains) were seen.
It happened at the end of arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days), that Nach opened the window of the ship which he had made,
and he sent out a raven. It went back and forth, until the mayam (waters) were dried up from the aratz (earth).
He sent out a dove from him, to raah (see) if the mayam (waters) were abated from the surface of the adamah (ground),

but the dove found no place to manawach (rest) her ragal (foot), and she returned to him into the ship; for the mayam (waters) were on the surface of the whole aratz (earth). He shalach (put) out his yad (hand), and took her, and brought her to him into the ship.
He stayed yet achar (another) shabai (seven) yawam (days); and again he sent the dove out of the ship.
The dove came back to him at ith (evening), and, behold, in her pah (mouth) was an olive leaf Tarap off. So Nach knew that the mayam (waters) were abated from the aratz (earth).
He stayed yet another shabai (seven) yawam (days), and sent out the dove; and she didn't shawab (turn back / repent) to him any more.

It happened in the shash (six) maah (hundred) first Shanah, in the raashawan (first) month, the achad (first) day of the chadash (month), the mayam (waters) were dried up from the aratz (earth). Nach removed the covering of the ship, and looked. He saw that the surface of the adamah (ground) was dried.
In the shanay (second) chadash (month), on the twenty-seventh yawam (day) of the chadash (month), the aratz (earth) was yabash (dry).
Alahayam spoke to Nach, saying,
"yatzaa (go) out of the ship, you, and your ashah (wife), and your ban (sons), and your ban (sons)' wives with you.

yatzaa (bring) out with you every chay (living) thing that is with you of all flesh, including birds, livestock, and every creeping thing that creeps on the aratz (earth), that they may breed abundantly in the aratz (earth), and be fruitful, and multiply on the aratz (earth).
Nach went out, with his ban (sons), his ashah (wife), and his ban (sons)' wives with him.
Every animal, every creeping thing, and every bird, whatever moves on the aratz (earth), after their mashapachah (families), went out of the ship.
Nach built an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah, and took of every tahawar (clean) animal, and of every tahawar (clean) bird, and offered burnt ilah (offerings) on the mazabach (altar).

Yahawah smelled the pleasant aroma. Yahawah said in his lab (heart), "I will not again qalal (curse) the adamah (ground) any more for adam (man's) sake, because the yatzar (imagination) of adam (man's) lab (heart) is rai (evil) from his youth; neither will I ever again strike everything chay (living), as I have done.
While the aratz (earth) remains, zarai (seed) time and harvest, and cold and heat, and qayatz (summer) and winter, and yawam (day) and layal (night) shall not shabath (cease).
Alahayam blessed Nach and his ban (sons), and said to them, "Be fruitful, and multiply, and malaa (replenish) the aratz (earth).

The mawaraa (fear) of you and the chath (dread) of you will be on every animal of the aratz (earth), and on every bird of the sky. Everything that the adamah (ground) teems with, and all the fish of the yam (sea) are delivered into your yad (hand).
Every moving thing that chay (lives) will be food for you. As the green herb, I have given everything to you.
But flesh with its napash (life), its dam (blood), you shall not akal (eat).

I will ak (surely) require your dam (blood) of your lives. At the yad (hand) of every animal I will require it. At the yad (hand) of adam (man), even at the yad (hand) of every adam (man's) ach (brother), I will require the napash (life) of adam (man).
Whoever sheds adam (man's) dam (blood), his dam (blood) will be shed by adam (man), for Alahayam made adam (man) in his own tzalam (image).
Be fruitful and multiply. Increase abundantly in the aratz (earth), and multiply in it.
Alahayam spoke to Nach and to his ban (sons) with him, saying,
"As for me, behold, I qawam (establish) my barayath (covenant) with you, and with your zarai (offspring) achar (after) you,

and with every chay (living) napash (creature) that is with you: the birds, the livestock, and every animal of the aratz (earth) with you, of all that yatzaa (go) out of the ship, even every animal of the aratz (earth).

I will qawam (establish) my barayath (covenant) with you: all flesh will not be karath (cut) off any more by the mayam (waters) of the flood, neither will there ever again be a flood to shachath (destroy) the aratz (earth).

Alahayam said, "This is the awath (token) of the barayath (covenant) which I nathan (make) between me and you and every chay (living) napash (creature) that is with you, for perpetual dawar (generations):
I nathan (set) my rainbow in the cloud, and it will be for a awath (sign) of a barayath (covenant) between me and the aratz (earth).
It will happen, when I bring a cloud over the aratz (earth), that the rainbow will be seen in the cloud,

and I will zakar (remember) my barayath (covenant), which is between me and you and every chay (living) napash (creature) of all flesh, and the mayam (waters) will no more become a flood to shachath (destroy) all flesh.

The rainbow will be in the cloud. I will raah (see) at it, that I may zakar (remember) the iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant) between Alahayam and every chay (living) napash (creature) of all flesh that is on the aratz (earth).
Alahayam said to Nach, "This is the awath (token) of the barayath (covenant) which I have established between me and all flesh that is on the aratz (earth).
The ban (sons) of Nach who went out from the ship were Sham, Cham, and Yapath. Cham is the ab (father) of Kanain.
These three were the sons of Noah, and from these, the whole aratz (earth) was populated.
Nach began to be a farmer, and planted a vineyard.
He drank of the yayan (wine) and got Shakar. He was uncovered within his ahal (tent).
Cham, the ab (father) of Kanain, saw the irawah (nakedness) of his ab (father), and told his shanayam (two) ach (brothers) outside.

Sham and Yapath took a garment, and laid it on shanayam (both) their shoulders, went in backwards, and covered the irawah (nakedness) of their ab (father). Their panayam (faces) were backwards, and they didn't raah (see) their ab (father's) irawah (nakedness).
Nach awoke from his yayan (wine), and knew what his youngest ban (son) had done to him.
He said, "Kanain is cursed. He will be ibad (servant) of ibad (servants) to his ach (brothers).
He said, "Blessed be Yahawah, the Alahayam of Sham. Let Kanain be his ibad (servant).
May Alahayam enlarge Yapath. Let him shakan (dwell) in the ahal (tents) of Sham. Let Kanain be his ibad (servant).
Nach lived shalawash (three) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) Shanah achar (after) the flood.
All the yawam (days) of Nach were thashai (nine) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) Shanah, then he died.
Now this is the history of the thawaladah (generations) of the ban (sons) of Nach and of Sham, Cham, and Yapath. ban (sons) were yalad (born) to them achar (after) the flood.
The ban (sons) of Yapath: Gamar, Magawag, Maday, Yawan, Thawabal, Mashak, and Thayaras.
The ban (sons) of Gamar: Ashakanaz, Rayapath, and Thawagaramah.
The ban (sons) of Yawan: Alayashah, Tharashayash, Kathay (Kittim), and Dadanayam.
Of these were the islands of the gawayam (nations) divided in their aratz (lands), everyone after his lashawan (language), after their mashapachah (families), in their gawayam (nations).
The ban (sons) of Cham: Kawash, Matzarayam, Pawat, and Kanain.
The ban (sons) of Kawash: Sabaa, Chawayalah, Sabathaa, Raimah, and Sabathakaa. The ban (sons) of Raimah: Shabaa and Dadan.
Kawash became the father of Namarawad. He began to be a gabawar (mighty) one in the aratz (earth).
He was a gabawar (mighty) hunter panayam (before) Yahawah. Kan it is said, "Like Namarawad, a gabawar (mighty) hunter panayam (before) Yahawah.
The raashayath (beginning) of his mamalakah (kingdom) was Babal, Arak, Akad, and Kalanah, in the aratz (land) of Shanair.
Out of that aratz (land) he went into Ashawar, and built Nayanawah, Rachabawath- Iyar, Kalach,
and Rasan between Nayanawah and Kalach (the same is the gadawal (great) Iyar).
Matzarayam became the father of Lawaday (Ludim), Inamayam, Lahabayam, Napathachayam,
Patharasay, Kasalachayam (which the Palashathay (Philistines) descended from), and Kapatharay (Caphtorim).
Kanain became the father of Tzayadawan (his firstborn), Chath,
the Yabawasay (Jebusite), the Amaray (Amorite), the Garagashay (Girgashite),
the Chaway (Hivite), the Iraqay, the Sayanay,
the Arawaday, the Tzamaray, and the Chamathay. Afterward the mashapachah (families) of the Kanainay (Canaanites) were spread abroad.
The border of the Kanainay (Canaanites) was from Tzayadawan, as you bawaa (go) toward Garar, to Izah; as you bawaa (go) toward Sadam, Imarah, Adamah, and Tzabaayam, to Lashai.
These are the ban (sons) of Cham, after their mashapachah (families), after their lashawan (languages), in their aratz (lands), in their gaway (nations).
To Sham, the ab (father) of all the children of Ibar, the gadawal (elder) ach (brother) of Yapath, to him also were yalad (children) born.
The ban (sons) of Sham: Iyalam, Ashawar, Arapakashad, Lawad, and Aram.
The ban (sons) of Aram: Iwatz, Chawal, Gathar, and Mash.
Arapakashad became the father of Shalach. Shalach became the father of Ibar.
To Ibar were yalad (born) shanayam (two) ban (sons). The sham (name) of the one was Palag, for in his yawam (days) the aratz (earth) was divided. His ach (brother's) sham (name) was Yaqatan.
Yaqatan became the father of Alamawadad, Shalap, Chatzaramawath, Yarach,
Hadawaram, Awazal, Daqalah,
Iwabal, Abayamaal, Shabaa,
Awapayar, Chawayalah, and Yawabab. All these were the ban (sons) of Yaqatan.
Their mawashab (dwelling) was from Mashaa, as you bawaa (go) toward Sapar, the har (mountain) of the qadam (east).
These are the ban (sons) of Sham, after their mashapachah (families), after their lashawan (languages), in their aratz (lands), after their gaway (nations).

These are the mashapachah (families) of the ban (sons) of Nach, after their thawaladah (generations), in their gaway (nations). Of these were the gaway (nations) divided in the aratz (earth) achar (after) the flood.
The whole aratz (earth) was of one shapah (language) and of one dabar (speech).
It happened, as they traveled qadam (east), that they found a Baqaih in the aratz (land) of Shanair, and they lived there.
They said one to rai (another), "Come, let's make bricks, and sharap (burn) them thoroughly." They had brick for aban (stone), and they used tar for mortar.

They said, "Come, let's banah (build) ourselves a Iyar, and a magadal (tower) whose raash (top) reaches to the sky, and let's ishah (make) ourselves a sham (name), lest we be scattered abroad on the surface of the whole aratz (earth).
Yahawah came down to raah (see) the Iyar and the magadal (tower), which the children of men built.
Yahawah said, "Behold, they are one im (people), and they have all one shapah (language), and this is what they chalal (begin) to do. Now nothing will be withheld from them, which they intend to do.
Come, yarad (let's) go down, and there confuse their shapah (language), that they may not understand one rai (another's) shapah (speech).
So Yahawah scattered them abroad from there on the surface of all the aratz (earth). They stopped building the Iyar.

Therefore its qaraa (name) was called Babal, because there Yahawah confused the shapah (language) of all the aratz (earth). From there, Yahawah scattered them abroad on the surface of all the aratz (earth).
This is the history of the thawaladah (generations) of Sham. Sham was one maah (hundred) Shanah ban (old) and became the father Arapakashad Arpachshad two Shanah achar (after) the flood.
Sham lived chamash (five) maah (hundred) Shanah achar (after) he became the father Arapakashad Arpachshad, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
Arapakashad lived shalawashayam (thirty)- chamash (five) Shanah and became the father of Shalach.
Arapakashad lived arabai (four) maah (hundred) shalawash (three) Shanah achar (after) he became the father of Shalach, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
Shalach lived shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah, and became the father of Ibar:
and Shalach lived arabai (four) maah (hundred) shalawash (three) Shanah achar (after) he became the father of Ibar, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
Ibar lived shalawashayam (thirty)- arabai (four) Shanah, and became the father of Palag.
Ibar lived arabai (four) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah achar (after) he became the father of Palag, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
Palag lived shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah, and became the father of Raiw.
Palag lived two maah (hundred) thashai (nine) Shanah achar (after) he became the father of Raiw, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
Raiw lived shalawashayam (thirty)- shanayam (two) Shanah, and became the father of Sharawag.
Raiw lived two maah (hundred) shabai (seven) Shanah achar (after) he became the father of Sharawag, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
Sharawag lived shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah, and became the father of Nachawar.
Sharawag lived two maah (hundred) Shanah achar (after) he became the father of Nachawar, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
Nachawar lived isharayam (twenty)- thashai (nine) Shanah, and became the father of Tharach.
Nachawar lived one maah (hundred) nineteen Shanah achar (after) he became the father of Tharach, and became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
Tharach lived shabaiyam (seventy) Shanah, and became the father of Abaram, Nachawar, and Haran.
Now this is the history of the thawaladah (generations) of Tharach. Tharach became the father of Abaram, Nachawar, and Haran. Haran became the father of Lawat.
Haran died panayam (before) his ab (father) Tharach in the aratz (land) of his birth, in Awar of the Kashaday.

Abaram and Nachawar took wives. The sham (name) of Abaram ashah (wife) was Sharay, and the sham (name) of Nachawar ashah (wife), Malakah, the bath (daughter) of Haran who was also the ab (father) of Yasakah.
Sharay was Iqar. She had no child.

Tharach took Abaram his ban (son), Lawat the ban (son) of Haran, his ban (son's) ban (son), and Sharay his kalah (daughter-in-law), his ban (son) Abaram ashah (wife). They went from Awar of the Kashaday, to yalak (go) into the aratz (land) of Kanain. They came to Charan and lived there.
The yawam (days) of Tharach were two maah (hundred) chamash (five) Shanah. Tharach died in Charan.
Now Yahawah said to Abaram, "yalak (get) out of your aratz (country), and from your relatives, and from your ab (father's) bayath (house), to the aratz (land) that I will show you.
I will ishah (make) of you a gadawal (great) gaway (nation). I will barak (bless) you and make your sham (name) great. You will be a barakah (blessing).
I will barak (bless) those who barak (bless) you, and I will arar (curse) him who arar (curses) you. All of the mashapachah (families) of the adamah (earth) will be blessed in you.
So Abaram went, as Yahawah had spoken to him. Lawat went with him. Abaram was shabaiyam (seventy)- chamash (five) Shanah ban (old) when he departed out of Charan.

Abaram took Sharay his ashah (wife), Lawat his ach (brother's) ban (son), all their rakawash (substance) that they had gathered, and the napash (souls) whom they had gotten in Charan, and they went to yalak (go) into the aratz (land) of Kanain. Into the aratz (land) of Kanain they came.
Abaram passed ibar (through) the aratz (land) to the place of Shakam, to the oak of Mawarah. The Kanainay (Canaanite) was then in the aratz (land).
Yahawah raah (see) to Abaram and said, "I will nathan (give) this aratz (land) to your zarai (seed)." He built an mazabach (altar) there to Yahawah, who raah (see) to him.

He left from there to the har (mountain) on the qadam (east) of Bayathaal, and pitched his ahal (tent), having Bayathaal on the yam (west), and Iy on the qadam (east). There he built an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah and called on the sham (name) of Yahawah.
Abaram traveled, going on still toward the Nagab.
There was a famine in the aratz (land). Abaram went down into Matzarayam to live as a foreigner there, for the famine was Kabad in the aratz (land).
It happened, when he had qarab (come) near to bawaa (enter) Matzarayam, that he said to Sharay his ashah (wife), "See now, I yadai (know) that you are a Yapah ashah (woman) to look at.
It will happen, when the Matzaray (Egyptians) will raah (see) you, that they will amar (say), ‘This is his ashah (wife).' They will harag (kill) me, but they will chayah (save) you alive.
Please amar (say) that you are my achawath (sister), that it may be yatab (well) with me for your sake, and that my napash (soul) may chayah (live) because of you.
It happened that when Abaram had bawaa (come) into Matzarayam, the Matzaray (Egyptians) saw that the ashah (woman) was very Yapah.
The shar (princes) of Paraih saw her, and praised her to Paraih; and the ashah (woman) was taken into Paraih bayath (house).
He dealt yatab (well) with Abaram for her sake. He had sheep, cattle, male donkeys, male ibad (servants), female shapachah (servants), female donkeys, and camels.
Yahawah plagued Paraih and his bayath (house) with gadawal (great) nagai (plagues) dabar (because) of Sharay, Abaram ashah (wife).
Paraih called Abaram and said, "What is this that you have done to me? Why didn't you nagad (tell) me that she was your ashah (wife)?
Why did you say, ‘She is my achawath (sister),' so that I took her to be my ashah (wife)? Now therefore, see your ashah (wife), take her, and go your yalak (way).
Paraih tzawah (commanded) men concerning him, and they brought him on the way with his ashah (wife) and all that he had.
Abaram went up out of Matzarayam: he, his ashah (wife), all that he had, and Lawat with him, into the Nagab.
Abaram was very kabad (rich) in livestock, in kasap (silver), and in gold.
He went on his journeys from the Nagab even to Bayathaal, to the place where his ahal (tent) had been at the thachalah (beginning), between Bayathaal and Iy,
to the place of the mazabach (altar), which he had made there at the raashawan (first). There Abaram called on the sham (name) of Yahawah.
Lawat also, who went with Abaram, had flocks, and herds, and ahal (tents).
The aratz (land) was not nashaa (able) to bear them, that they might live together: for their rakawash (substance) was rab (great), so that they could not live together.

There was a rayab (strife) between the herdsmen of Abaram livestock and the herdsmen of Lawat livestock: and the Kanainay (Canaanite) and the Parazay (Perizzite) lived in the aratz (land) at that time.
Abaram said to Lawat, "Please, let there be no Marayabah between me and you, and between my herdsmen and your herdsmen; for we are relatives.

Isn't the whole aratz (land) panayam (before) you? Please separate yourself from me. If you go to the left shamaawal (hand), then I will yaman (go) to the right. Or if you go to the right yamayan (hand), then I will shamaal (go) to the left.

Lawat lifted up his iyan (eyes), and saw all the plain of the Yaradan, that it was well-watered everywhere, panayam (before) Yahawah destroyed Sadam and Imarah, like the Gan of Yahawah, like the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, as you bawaa (go) to Tzair.
So Lawat chose the Plain of the Yaradan for himself. Lawat traveled qadam (east), and they separated themselves the one from the other.
Abaram lived in the aratz (land) of Kanain, and Lawat lived in the Iyar of the plain, and moved his ahal (tent) as far as Sadam.
Now the men of Sadam were maad (exceedingly) rai (wicked) and chataa (sinners) against Yahawah.

Yahawah said to Abaram, achar (after) Lawat was separated from him, "Now, nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eyes), and raah (see) from the place where you are, northward and Nagab and eastward and westward,
for all the aratz (land) which you raah (see), I will nathan (give) to you, and to your zarai (offspring) iwalam (forever).

I will shawam (make) your zarai (offspring) as the ipar (dust) of the aratz (earth), so that if a ayash (man) can number the ipar (dust) of the aratz (earth), then your zarai (seed) may also be numbered.
qawam (arise), halak (walk) through the aratz (land) in its arak (length) and in its breadth; for I will nathan (give) it to you.
Abaram moved his ahal (tent), and came and lived by the oaks of Mamaraa, which are in Chabarawan, and built an mazabach (altar) there to Yahawah.
It happened in the yawam (days) of Amarapal, malak (king) of Shanair, Arayawak, malak (king) of Alasar, Kadaralaimar, malak (king) of Iyalam, and Thadail, malak (king) of Goiim,

that they made war with Barai, malak (king) of Sadam, and with Barashai, malak (king) of Imarah, Shanaab, malak (king) of Adamah, and Shamaabar, malak (king) of Tzabaayam, and the malak (king) of Balai (the same is Tzair).
All these joined together in the valley of Shadayam (the same is the Malach yam (sea)).
ishar (twelve) Shanah they served Kadaralaimar, and in the thirteenth Shanah, they rebelled.

In the fourteenth Shanah Kadaralaimar came, and the malak (kings) who were with him, and struck the Rapaa (Rephaim) in Ashteroth Ishatharathaqaranayam, and the Zawazayam (Zuzim) in Ham, and the Ayamayam (Emim) in Shaveh Kiriathaim,
and the Charay (Horites) in their harar (mount) Shaiyar, to Ayalapaaran, which is by the madabar (wilderness).

They returned, and came to Iyanamashapat Mishpat (the same is Qadash), and struck all the shadah (country) of the Imalaqay (Amalekites), and also the Amaray (Amorites), that lived in Hazazon Chatzatzawanathamar.

The malak (king) of Sadam, and the malak (king) of Imarah, and the malak (king) of Adamah, and the malak (king) of Tzabaayam, and the malak (king) of Balai (the same is Tzair) went out; and they set the battle in array against them in the valley of Shadayam;

against Kadaralaimar malak (king) of Iyalam, and Thadail malak (king) of Goiim, and Amarapal malak (king) of Shanair, and Arayawak malak (king) of Alasar; arabai (four) malak (kings) against the chamash (five).
Now the valley of Shadayam was full of tar baar (pits); and the malak (kings) of Sadam and Imarah fled, and they napal (fell) there, and those who remained fled to the har (hills).
They took all the rakawash (goods) of Sadam and Imarah, and all their food, and went their yalak (way).
They took Lawat, Abaram ach (brother's) ban (son), who lived in Sadam, and his rakawash (goods), and departed.

palayat (one) who had escaped came and told Abaram, the ibaray (hebrew). Now he lived by the oaks of Mamaraa, the Amaray (Amorite), ach (brother) of Ashakal, and ach (brother) of Inar; and these were allies of Abaram.
When Abaram heard that his relative was taken captive, he led out his trained men, yalayad (born) in his bayath (house), shalawash (three) maah (hundred) and eighteen, and pursued as Dan as Dan.
He divided himself against them by layal (night), he and his ibad (servants), and struck them, and pursued them to Chawabah, which is on the left shamaawal (hand) of Damashaq.
He brought shawab (turn back / repent) all the rakawash (goods), and also brought shawab (turn back / repent) his relative, Lawat, and his rakawash (goods), and the women also, and the im (people).

The malak (king) of Sadam went out to qaraah (meet) him, achar (after) his shawab (turn back / repent) from the slaughter of Kadaralaimar and the malak (kings) who were with him, at the valley of Shawah (that is, the malak (king's) Valley).
Malakayatzadaq malak (king) of Shalam brought out lacham (bread) and yayan (wine): and he was kahan (priest) of Al Most Ilayawan.
He blessed him, and said, "Blessed be Abaram of Al Most Ilayawan, qanah (possessor) of shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth):
and blessed be Al Most Ilayawan, who has delivered your tzar (enemies) into your yad (hand)." Abram gave him a maishar (tenth) of all.
The malak (king) of Sadam said to Abaram, "nathan (give) me the people, and take the rakawash (goods) to yourself.
Abaram said to the malak (king) of Sadam, "I have lifted up my yad (hand) to Yahawah, Al Most Ilayawan, qanah (possessor) of shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth),
that I will not take a thread nor a sandal strap nor anything that is yours, lest you should amar (say), ‘I have made Abaram rich.'
I will accept nothing from you except that which the young men have eaten, and the chalaq (portion) of the men who went with me: Inar, Ashakal, and Mamaraa. Let them take their chalaq (portion).
achar (after) these things the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Abaram in a vision, saying, "Don't be yaraa (afraid), Abaram. I am your magan (shield), your maad (exceedingly) great reward.
Abaram said, "Adanay Yahawah, what will you nathan (give) me, since I halak (go) Irayaray, and he who will inherit my estate is Alayaizar of Damashaq?
Abaram said, "Behold, to me you have given no zarai (seed): and, behold, one ban (born) in my bayath (house) is my heir.
Behold, the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to him, saying, "This man will not be your heir, but he who will yatzaa (come) out of your own body will be your heir.
Yahawah brought him outside, and said, "Look now toward the sky, and count the kawakab (stars), if you are yakal (able) to count them." He said to Abram, "So shall your zarai (seed) be.
He believed in Yahawah; and he reckoned it to him for tzadaqah (righteousness).
He said to him, "I am Yahawah who brought you out of Awar of the Kashaday, to nathan (give) you this aratz (land) to yarash (inherit) it.
He said, "Adanay Yahawah, mah (how) will I yadai (know) that I will yarash (inherit) it?
He said to him, "Bring me a Igalah shalash (three) years old, a female goat shalash (three) years old, a ayal (ram) shalash (three) years old, a turtledove, and a young pigeon.
He brought him all of these, and divided them in the middle, and laid ayash (each) half opposite the other; but he didn't divide the birds.
The birds of prey came down on the carcasses, and Abaram drove them away.
When the shamash (sun) was going down, a tharadamah (deep) sleep napal (fell) on Abaram. Now ayamah (terror) and gadawal (great) chashakah (darkness) napal (fell) on him.

He said to Abaram, "yadai (know) for yadai (sure) that your zarai (seed) will live as foreigners in a aratz (land) that is not theirs, and will ibad (serve) them. They will afflict them arabai (four) maah (hundred) Shanah.
I will also dayan (judge) that gaway (nation), whom they will ibad (serve). Afterward they will yatzaa (come) out with gadawal (great) wealth,
but you will bawaa (go) to your abawath (fathers) in shalawam (peace). You will be buried in a tawab (good) shayabah (old) age.
In the rabayaiy (fourth) dawar (generation) they will come here again, for the iwan (iniquity) of the Amaray (Amorite) is not yet Shalam.
It came to pass that, when the shamash (sun) went down, and it was dark, behold, a ishan (smoking) furnace, and a ash (flaming) lapayad (torch) passed between these pieces.

In that yawam (day) Yahawah made a barayath (covenant) with Abaram, saying, "To your zarai (seed) I have given this aratz (land), from the nahar (river) of Matzarayam to the gadawal (great) nahar (river), the nahar (river) Parath:
the Qayanay (Kenites), the Qanazay (Kenizzites), the Qadamanay (Kadmonites),
the Chathay (Hittites), the Parazay (Perizzites), the Rapaa (Rephaim),
the Amaray (Amorites), the Kanainay (Canaanites), the Garagashay (Girgashites), and the Yabawasay (Jebusites).
Now Sharay, Abaram ashah (wife), bore him no yalad (children). She had a handmaid, an Matzaray (Egyptian), whose sham (name) was Hagar.

Sharay said to Abaram, "See now, Yahawah has restrained me from bearing. Please bawaa (go) in to my handmaid. It may be that I will banah (obtain) children by her." Abaram listened to the qawal (voice) of Sharay.

Sharay, Abaram ashah (wife), took Hagar the Matzaray (Egyptian), her handmaid, after Abaram had lived ishar (ten) Shanah in the aratz (land) of Kanain, and gave her to Abaram her ayash (husband) to be his ashah (wife).
He went in to Hagar, and she conceived. When she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her iyan (eyes).

Sharay said to Abaram, "This wrong is your fault. I gave my handmaid into your bosom, and when she saw that she had conceived, I was despised in her iyan (eyes). Yahawah shapat (judge) between me and you.
But Abaram said to Sharay, "Behold, your shapachah (maid) is in your yad (hand). Do to her whatever is tawab (good) in your eyes." Sharay dealt harshly with her, and she fled from her panayam (face).
The malaak (angel) of Yahawah found her by a iyan (fountain) of mayam (water) in the madabar (wilderness), by the iyan (fountain) in the darak (way) to Shawar.
He said, "Hagar, Sharay handmaid, where did you yalak (come) from? Where are you going?" She said, "I am fleeing from the panayam (face) of my mistress Sharay.
The malaak (angel) of Yahawah said to her, "shawab (turn back / repent) to your mistress, and submit yourself under her yad (hands).
The malaak (angel) of Yahawah said to her, "I will greatly multiply your zarai (seed), that they will not be numbered for multitude.

The malaak (angel) of Yahawah said to her, "Behold, you are with harah (child), and will yalad (bear) a ban (son). You shall qaraa (call) his sham (name) Yashamaial, because Yahawah has heard your affliction.
He will be like a wild donkey among men. His yad (hand) will be against every man, and every man's yad (hand) against him. He will live opposite all of his ach (brothers).
She called the sham (name) of Yahawah who spoke to her, "You are a Al who sees," for she said, "Have I even stayed alive after seeing him?
Therefore the baar (well) was called Baaralachayaraay Lahai Roi. Behold, it is between Qadash and Barad.
Hagar bore a ban (son) for Abaram. Abaram called the sham (name) of his ban (son), whom Hagar bore, Yashamaial.
Abaram was shamanayam (eighty) shash (six) Shanah ban (old) when Hagar bore Yashamaial to Abaram.
When Abaram was thashaiyam (ninety)- thashai (nine) Shanah ban (old), Yahawah raah (see) to Abaram, and said to him, "I am Al Shaday. halak (walk) panayam (before) me, and be blameless.
I will nathan (make) my barayath (covenant) between me and you, and will multiply you maad (exceedingly).
Abaram napal (fell) on his panayam (face). Alahayam talked with him, saying,
"As for me, behold, my barayath (covenant) is with you. You will be the ab (father) of a multitude of gawayam (nations).
Neither will your sham (name) any more be called Abaram, but your sham (name) will be Abaraham; for I have made you the ab (father) of a multitude of gawayam (nations).
I will make you maad (exceedingly) fruitful, and I will nathan (make) gawayam (nations) of you. malak (kings) will yatzaa (come) out of you.

I will qawam (establish) my barayath (covenant) between me and you and your zarai (seed) achar (after) you throughout their dawar (generations) for an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant), to be a Alahayam to you and to your zarai (seed) achar (after) you.

I will nathan (give) to you, and to your zarai (seed) achar (after) you, the aratz (land) where you are traveling, all the aratz (land) of Kanain, for an iwalam (forever) achazah (possession). I will be their Alahayam.
Alahayam said to Abaraham, "As for you, you will shamar (keep) my barayath (covenant), you and your zarai (seed) achar (after) you throughout their dawar (generations).
This is my barayath (covenant), which you shall shamar (keep), between me and you and your zarai (seed) achar (after) you. Every male among you shall be circumcised.
You shall be circumcised in the flesh of your foreskin. It will be a awath (token) of the barayath (covenant) between me and you.

He who is shamanah (eight) yawam (days) ban (old) will be circumcised among you, every zakar (male) throughout your dawar (generations), he who is yalayad (born) in the bayath (house), or maqanah (bought) with kasap (money) from any foreigner who is not of your zarai (seed).

He who is yalayad (born) in your bayath (house), and he who is maqanah (bought) with your kasap (money), must be circumcised. My barayath (covenant) will be in your flesh for an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant).
The Iral zakar (male) who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin, that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people). He has broken my barayath (covenant).
Alahayam said to Abaraham, "As for Sharay your ashah (wife), you shall not qaraa (call) her sham (name) Sharay, but her sham (name) will be Sharah.

I will barak (bless) her, and moreover I will nathan (give) you a ban (son) by her. Yes, I will barak (bless) her, and she will be a mother of gawayam (nations). malak (kings) of im (peoples) will come from her.

Then Abaraham napal (fell) on his panayam (face), and laughed, and said in his lab (heart), "Will a yalad (child) be born to him who is one maah (hundred) Shanah ban (old)? Will Sharah, who is thashaiyam (ninety) Shanah bath (old), give yalad (birth)?
Abaraham said to Alahayam, "Oh that Yashamaial might chayah (live) panayam (before) you!

Alahayam said, "No, but Sharah, your ashah (wife), will yalad (bear) you a ban (son). You shall qaraa (call) his sham (name) Yatzachaq. I will qawam (establish) my barayath (covenant) with him for an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant) for his zarai (seed) achar (after) him.

As for Yashamaial, I have heard you. Behold, I have blessed him, and will make him fruitful, and will multiply him maad (exceedingly). He will become the father of ishar (twelve) nashayaa (princes), and I will nathan (make) him a gadawal (great) gaway (nation).
But my barayath (covenant) I qawam (establish) with Yatzachaq, whom Sharah will yalad (bear) to you at this mawaid (set) time achar (next) Shanah.
When he finished talking with him, Alahayam went up from Abaraham.

Abaraham took Yashamaial his ban (son), all who were yalayad (born) in his bayath (house), and all who were maqanah (bought) with his kasap (money); every zakar (male) among the men of Abaraham bayath (house), and circumcised the flesh of their foreskin in the same yawam (day), as Alahayam had said to him.
Abaraham was thashaiyam (ninety)- thashai (nine) Shanah ban (old), when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
Yashamaial, his ban (son), was thirteen Shanah ban (old) when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
In the same yawam (day) both Abaraham and Yashamaial, his ban (son), were circumcised.
All the men of his bayath (house), those yalayad (born) in the bayath (house), and those maqanah (bought) with kasap (money) of a foreigner, were circumcised with him.
Yahawah raah (see) to him by the oaks of Mamaraa, as he sat in the ahal (tent) door in the heat of the yawam (day).

He lifted up his iyan (eyes) and looked, and saw that shalawash (three) men stood opposite him. When he saw them, he ran to qaraah (meet) them from the ahal (tent) door, and bowed himself to the aratz (earth),
and said, "My Adanay, if now I have found favor in your iyan (sight), please don't ibar (go) away from your ibad (servant).
Now let a Mait mayam (water) be fetched, wash your feet, and shain (rest) yourselves under the itz (tree).

I will get a morsel of lacham (bread) so you can refresh your lab (heart). achar (after) that you may go your ibar (way), now that you have ibar (come) to your ibad (servant)." They said, "Very well, do as you have said.
Abaraham hurried into the ahal (tent) to Sharah, and said, "Quickly prepare shalawash (three) measures of fine meal, knead it, and ishah (make) cakes.
Abaraham ran to the herd, and fetched a Rak and tawab (good) ban (calf), and gave it to the nair (servant). He hurried to ishah (dress) it.
He took butter, milk, and the ban (calf) which he had ishah (dressed), and nathan (set) it panayam (before) them. He stood by them under the itz (tree), and they ate.
They asked him, "Where is Sharah, your ashah (wife)?" He said, "See, in the ahal (tent).

He said, "I will shawab (turn back / repent) shawab (turn back / repent) to you when the ith (season) comes round. Behold, Sharah your ashah (wife) will have a ban (son)." Sharah heard in the ahal (tent) door, which was achar (behind) him.
Now Abaraham and Sharah were zaqan (old), well advanced in yawam (age). Sharah had passed the yawam (age) of childbearing.
Sharah laughed qarab (within) herself, saying, "achar (after) I have grown old will I have Idan, my Adawan being zaqan (old) also?
Yahawah said to Abaraham, "mah (why) did Sharah laugh, saying, ‘Will I really yalad (bear) a child, yet I am zaqan (old)?'
Is anything palaa (too) hard for Yahawah? At the mawaid (set) time I will shawab (turn back / repent) to you, when the ith (season) comes round, and Sharah will have a ban (son).
Then Sharah denied, saying, "I didn't laugh," for she was yaraa (afraid). He said, "No, but you did laugh.
The men rose up from there, and looked panayam (toward) Sadam. Abaraham went with them to see them on their way.
Yahawah said, "Will I hide from Abaraham what I do,
since Abaraham has surely become a gadawal (great) and itzawam (mighty) gaway (nation), and all the gaway (nations) of the aratz (earth) will be blessed in him?

For I have yadai (known) him, to the end that he may tzawah (command) his children and his bayath (household) achar (after) him, that they may shamar (keep) the darak (way) of Yahawah, to do righteousness and tzadaqah (justice); to the end that Yahawah may bawaa (bring) on Abaraham that which he has spoken of him.
Yahawah said, "Because the cry of Sadam and Imarah is rab (great), and because their chataah (sin) is very kabad (grievous),
I will yarad (go) down now, and raah (see) whether their deeds are as bad as the reports which have bawaa (come) to me. If not, I will yadai (know).
The men turned from there, and went toward Sadam, but Abaraham stood yet panayam (before) Yahawah.
Abaraham drew near, and said, "Will you sapah (consume) the tzadayaq (righteous) with the rashai (wicked)?
What if there are chamashayam (fifty) tzadayaq (righteous) within the Iyar? Will you sapah (consume) and not nashaa (spare) the place for the chamashayam (fifty) tzadayaq (righteous) who are in it?

Be it far from you to do things like that, to mawath (kill) the tzadayaq (righteous) with the rashai (wicked), so that the tzadayaq (righteous) should be like the rashai (wicked). May that be far from you. Shouldn't the shapat (judge) of all the aratz (earth) do mashapat (right)?
Yahawah said, "If I matzaa (find) in Sadam chamashayam (fifty) tzadayaq (righteous) within the Iyar, then I will nashaa (spare) all the place for their sake.
Abaraham answered, "See now, I have taken it on myself to dabar (speak) to the Adanay, who am but ipar (dust) and ashes.

What if there will lack chamash (five) of the chamashayam (fifty) tzadayaq (righteous)? Will you shachath (destroy) all the Iyar for lack of chamash (five)?" He said, "I will not shachath (destroy) it, if I matzaa (find) arabaiyam (forty)- chamash (five) there.
He spoke to him yet again, and said, "What if there are arabaiyam (forty) found there?" He said, "I will not do it for the arabaiyam (forty's) sake.

He said, "Oh don't let the Adanay be charah (angry), and I will dabar (speak). What if there are shalawashayam (thirty) found there?" He said, "I will not do it, if I matzaa (find) shalawashayam (thirty) there.

He said, "See now, I have taken it on myself to dabar (speak) to the Adanay. What if there are isharayam (twenty) found there?" He said, "I will not shachath (destroy) it for the isharayam (twenty's) sake.

He said, "Oh don't let the Adanay be charah (angry), and I will dabar (speak) just paim (once) more. What if ishar (ten) are found there?" He said, "I will not shachath (destroy) it for the ishar (ten's) sake.
Yahawah went his yalak (way), as soon as he had finished communing with Abaraham, and Abaraham returned to his place.

The shanayam (two) malaak (angels) came to Sadam at evening. Lawat sat in the gate of Sadam. Lawat saw them, and rose up to qaraah (meet) them. He bowed himself with his ap (face) to the aratz (earth),

and he said, "See now, my adawan (lords), please sawar (turn) aside into your ibad (servant's) bayath (house), stay all lawan (night), wash your feet, and you can shakam (rise) up early, and halak (go) on your darak (way)." They said, "No, but we will stay in the street all lawan (night).
He urged them maad (greatly), and they came in with him, and entered into his bayath (house). He made them a feast, and baked unleavened matzah (bread), and they ate.
But before they shakab (lay) down, the men of the Iyar, the men of Sadam, surrounded the bayath (house), both nair (young) and zaqan (old), all the im (people) from every quarter.
They called to Lawat, and said to him, "Where are the men who came in to you this layal (night)? yatzaa (bring) them out to us, that we may have sex with them.
Lawat went out to them to the door, and shut the door achar (after) him.
He said, "Please, my ach (brothers), don't act so wickedly.

See now, I have shanayam (two) virgin bath (daughters). Please let me yatzaa (bring) them out to you, and you may do to them what seems tawab (good) to you. Only don't do anything to these men, because they have bawaa (come) under the shadow of my roof.

They said, "Stand back!" Then they said, "This one fellow came in to live as a foreigner, and he appoints himself a shapat (judge). Now will we raii (deal) worse with you, than with them!" They pressed hard on the ayash (man) Lawat, and drew near to shabar (break) the door.
But the men reached out their yad (hand), and brought Lawat into the bayath (house) to them, and shut the door.
They struck the men who were at the door of the bayath (house) with blindness, both qatan (small) and gadawal (great), so that they wearied themselves to matzaa (find) the door.
The men said to Lawat, "Do you have anybody else here? Sons-in-law, your ban (sons), your bath (daughters), and whoever you have in the Iyar, yatzaa (bring) them out of the place:
for we will shachath (destroy) this place, because the outcry against them has grown great panayam (before) Yahawah that Yahawah has sent us to shachath (destroy) it.

Lawat went out, and spoke to his sons-in-law, who were pledged to marry his bath (daughters), and said, "qawam (get) up! yatzaa (get) out of this place, for Yahawah will shachath (destroy) the Iyar." But he seemed to his sons-in-law to be joking.

When the shachar (morning) came, then the malaak (angels) hurried Lawat, saying, "qawam (get) up! Take your ashah (wife), and your shanayam (two) bath (daughters) who are here, lest you be consumed in the iwan (iniquity) of the Iyar.

But he lingered; and the men grabbed his yad (hand), his ashah (wife's) yad (hand), and his shanayam (two) bath (daughters)' yad (hands), Yahawah being merciful to him; and they took him out, and yanach (set) him outside of the Iyar.

It came to pass, when they had taken them out, that he said, "malat (escape) for your napash (life)! Don't look achar (behind) you, and don't imad (stay) anywhere in the plain. malat (escape) to the har (mountains), lest you be consumed!
Lawat said to them, "Oh, not so, my Adawan.

See now, your ibad (servant) has found favor in your iyan (sight), and you have magnified your loving chasad (kindness), which you have shown to me in saving my napash (life). I can't malat (escape) to the har (mountain), lest rai (evil) overtake me, and I mawath (die).
See now, this Iyar is qarawab (near) to flee to, and it is a little matzair (one). Oh let me malat (escape) there (isn't it a little matzair (one)?), and my napash (soul) will chayah (live).
He said to him, "Behold, I have granted your dabar (request) concerning this thing also, that I will not hapak (overthrow) the Iyar of which you have spoken.
Hurry, malat (escape) there, for I can't do anything until you bawaa (get) there." Therefore the sham (name) of the Iyar was called Tzair.
The shamash (sun) had yatzaa (risen) on the aratz (earth) when Lawat came to Tzair.
Then Yahawah rained on Sadam and on Imarah sulfur and ash (fire) from Yahawah out of the sky.
He overthrew those Iyar, all the plain, all the yashab (inhabitants) of the Iyar, and that which grew on the adamah (ground).
But his ashah (wife) looked back from achar (behind) him, and she became a pillar of Malach.
Abaraham got up shakam (early) in the baqar (morning) to the place where he had stood panayam (before) Yahawah.

He looked panayam (toward) Sadam and Imarah, and panayam (toward) all the aratz (land) of the plain, and looked, and saw that the qayatawar (smoke) of the aratz (land) went up as the qayatawar (smoke) of a furnace.

It happened, when Alahayam destroyed the Iyar of the plain, that Alahayam zakar (remembered) Abaraham, and sent Lawat out of the middle of the overthrow, when he overthrew the Iyar in which Lawat lived.

Lawat went up out of Tzair, and lived in the har (mountain), and his shanayam (two) bath (daughters) with him; for he was yaraa (afraid) to live in Tzair. He lived in a cave with his shanayam (two) bath (daughters).
The firstborn said Tzaiyar the younger, "Our ab (father) is zaqan (old), and there is not a ayash (man) in the aratz (earth) to bawaa (come) in to us in the darak (way) of all the aratz (earth).
yalak (come), shaqah (let's) make our ab (father) shaqah (drink) yayan (wine), and we will shakab (lie) with him, that we may chayah (preserve) our ab (father's) zarai (seed).

They made their ab (father) shaqah (drink) yayan (wine) that layal (night): and the firstborn went in, and shakab (lay) with her ab (father). He didn't yadai (know) when she shakab (lay) down, nor when she qawam (arose).

It came to pass on the next macharath (day), that the firstborn said Tzaiyar the younger, "Behold, I shakab (lay) last amash (night) with my ab (father). Let us shaqah (make) him drink yayan (wine) again, tonight. You bawaa (go) in, and shakab (lie) with him, that we may chayah (preserve) our ab (father's) zarai (seed).
They made their ab (father) shaqah (drink) yayan (wine) that layal (night) Tzaiyar. The younger went and shakab (lay) with him. He didn't yadai (know) when she shakab (lay) down, nor when she got up.
Thus shanayam (both) of Lawat bath (daughters) were with child by their ab (father).
The firstborn bore a ban (son), and sham (named) him Mawaab. He is the ab (father) Mawaab the Moabites to this yawam (day).
The Tzaiyar also bore a ban (son), and called his sham (name) Banaimay Ammi. He is the ab (father) of the children of Imawan to this yawam (day).
Abaraham traveled from there toward the aratz (land) of the Nagab, and lived between Qadash and Shawar. He lived as a foreigner in Garar.
Abaraham said about Sharah his ashah (wife), "She is my achawath (sister)." Abayamalak malak (king) of Garar sent, and took Sharah.

But Alahayam came to Abayamalak in a chalawam (dream) of the layal (night), and said to him, "Behold, you are a mawath (dead) man, because of the ashah (woman) whom you have taken. For she is a bail (man's) wife.
Now Abayamalak had not qarab (come) near her. He said, "Adanay, will you harag (kill) even a tzadayaq (righteous) gaway (nation)?

Didn't he amar (tell) me, ‘She is my achawath (sister)?' She, even she herself, said, ‘He is my ach (brother).' In the tham (integrity) of my labab (heart) and the innocence of my kap (hands) have I done this.

Alahayam said to him in the chalawam (dream), "Yes, I yadai (know) that in the tham (integrity) of your labab (heart) you have done this, and I also withheld you from sinning against me. Therefore I didn't allow you to nagai (touch) her.

Now therefore, shawab (turn back / repent) the ayash (man's) ashah (wife). For he is a nabayaa (prophet), and he will palal (pray) for you, and you will chayah (live). If you don't shawab (turn back / repent) her, yadai (know) for sure that you will mawath (die), you, and all who are yours.
Abayamalak rose shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and called all his ibad (servants), and told all these things in their ear. The men were very scared.

Then Abayamalak called Abaraham, and said to him, "What have you done to us? How have I sinned against you, that you have brought on me and on my mamalakah (kingdom) a gadawal (great) chataah (sin)? You have done maishah (deeds) to me that ought not to be done!
Abayamalak said to Abaraham, "mah (what) did you see, that you have done this thing?
Abaraham said, "Because I thought, ‘raq (surely) the yaraah (fear) of Alahayam is not in this place. They will harag (kill) me for my ashah (wife's) dabar (sake).'
Besides, she is indeed my achawath (sister), the bath (daughter) of my ab (father), but not the bath (daughter) of my am (mother); and she became my ashah (wife).

It happened, when Alahayam caused me to thaih (wander) from my ab (father's) bayath (house), that I said to her, ‘This is your chasad (kindness) which you shall show to me. Everywhere that we bawaa (go), amar (say) of me, "He is my ach (brother)."'
Abayamalak took sheep and cattle, male ibad (servants) and female shapachah (servants), and gave them to Abaraham, and restored Sharah, his ashah (wife), to him.
Abayamalak said, "Behold, my aratz (land) is panayam (before) you. yashab (dwell) where it pleases you.

To Sharah he said, "Behold, I have given your ach (brother) a alap (thousand) pieces of kasap (silver). Behold, it is for you a covering of the iyan (eyes) to all that are with you. In front of all you are vindicated.
Abaraham prayed to Alahayam. Alahayam healed Abayamalak, and his ashah (wife), and his female amah (servants), and they bore yalad (children).
For Yahawah had closed up tight all the wombs of the bayath (house) of Abayamalak, dabar (because) of Sharah, Abaraham ashah (wife).
Yahawah visited Sharah as he had said, and Yahawah did to Sharah as he had spoken.
Sharah conceived, and bore Abaraham a ban (son) in his old age, at the mawaid (set) time of which Alahayam had spoken to him.
