Abaraham called his ban (son) who was yalad (born) to him, whom Sharah bore to him, Yatzachaq.
Abaraham circumcised his ban (son), Yatzachaq, when he was shamanah (eight) yawam (days) ban (old), as Alahayam had tzawah (commanded) him.
Abaraham was one maah (hundred) Shanah ban (old) when his ban (son), Yatzachaq, was yalad (born) to him.
Sharah said, "Alahayam has made me laugh. Everyone who hears will laugh with me.
She said, "Who would have said to Abaraham, that Sharah would nurse children? For I have borne him a ban (son) in his old age.
The yalad (child) grew, and was weaned. Abaraham made a gadawal (great) feast on the yawam (day) that Yatzachaq was weaned.
Sharah saw the ban (son) of Hagar the Matzaray (Egyptian), whom she had borne to Abaraham, mocking.
Therefore she said to Abaraham, "Cast out this handmaid and her ban (son)! For the ban (son) of this handmaid will not be heir with my ban (son), Yatzachaq.
The thing was very grievous in Abaraham iyan (sight) on account of his ban (son).

Alahayam said to Abaraham, "Don't let it be grievous in your iyan (sight) because of the nair (boy), and because of your handmaid. In all that Sharah amar (says) to you, listen to her qawal (voice). For from Yatzachaq will your zarai (seed) be called.
I will also shawam (make) a gaway (nation) of the ban (son) of the handmaid, because he is your zarai (seed).

Abaraham rose up shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and took lacham (bread) and a bottle of mayam (water), and gave it to Hagar, putting it on her shoulder; and gave her the yalad (child), and sent her shalach (away). She departed, and wandered in the madabar (wilderness) Baarashabai Beersheba.
The mayam (water) in the bottle was spent, and she cast the yalad (child) under one of the shrubs.

She went and sat down opposite him, a rachaq (good) way off, about a bow shot away. For she said, "Don't let me raah (see) the mawath (death) of the yalad (child)." She sat over against him, and lifted up her qawal (voice), and wept.

Alahayam heard the qawal (voice) of the nair (boy). The malaak (angel) of Alahayam called to Hagar out of the sky, and said to her, "What ails you, Hagar? Hagar be afraid. For Alahayam has heard the qawal (voice) of the nair (boy) where he is.
Get up, nashaa (lift) up the nair (boy), and chazaq (hold) him in your yad (hand). For I will shawam (make) him a gadawal (great) gaway (nation).
Alahayam opened her iyan (eyes), and she saw a baar (well) of mayam (water). She went, filled the bottle with mayam (water), and gave the nair (boy) shaqah (drink).
Alahayam was with the nair (boy), and he grew. He lived in the madabar (wilderness), and became, as he grew up, an archer.
He lived in the madabar (wilderness) of Paaran. His am (mother) took a ashah (wife) for him out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
It happened at that ith (time), that Abayamalak and Payakal the shar (captain) of his tzabaa (army) spoke to Abaraham, saying, "Alahayam is with you in all that you do.

Now, therefore, shabai (swear) to me here by Alahayam that you will not deal falsely with me, nor with my nayan (son), nor with my nakad (son's) son. But according to the chasad (kindness) that I have done to you, you shall do to me, and to the aratz (land) in which you have lived as a foreigner.
Abaraham said, "I will shabai (swear).
Abaraham complained to Abayamalak because of a mayam (water) baar (well), which Abayamalak ibad (servants) had violently taken away.
Abayamalak said, "I don't yadai (know) who has done this thing. You didn't nagad (tell) me, laa (neither) did I hear of it, until today.
Abaraham took sheep and cattle, and gave them to Abayamalak. Those two made a barayath (covenant).
Abaraham natzab (set) shabai (seven) ewe lambs of the flock by themselves.
Abayamalak said to Abaraham, "What do these shabai (seven) ewe lambs which you have natzab (set) by themselves mean?
He said, "You shall take these shabai (seven) ewe lambs from my yad (hand), that it may be a idah (witness) to me, that I have dug this baar (well).
Therefore he called that place Baarashabai, because they both swore there.

So they made a barayath (covenant) Baarashabai Beersheba. Abayamalak rose up with Payakal, the shar (captain) of his tzabaa (army), and they returned into the aratz (land) of the Palashathay (Philistines).
Abraham planted a tamarisk tree Baarashabai Beersheba, and called there on the sham (name) of Yahawah, the iwalam (forever) Al.
Abaraham lived as a foreigner in the aratz (land) of the Palashathay (Philistines) many yawam (days).
It happened achar (after) these things, that Alahayam tested Abaraham, and said to him, "Abaraham!" He said, "Here I am.

He said, "Now take your ban (son), your only ban (son), whom you ahab (love), even Yatzachaq, and go into the aratz (land) of Mawarayah. ilah (offer) him there for a burnt ilah (offering) on one of the har (mountains) which I will amar (tell) you of.

Abaraham rose shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and saddled his donkey, and took shanayam (two) of his nair (young) men with him, and Yatzachaq his ban (son). He split the itz (wood) for the burnt ilah (offering), and rose up, and went to the place of which Alahayam had told him.
On the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) Abaraham lifted up his iyan (eyes), and saw the place Rachawaq off.
Abaraham said to his nair (young) men, "Stay here with the donkey. The nair (boy) and I will yalak (go) kah (yonder). We will shachah (worship), and shawab (turn back / repent) back to you.
Abaraham took the itz (wood) of the burnt ilah (offering) and laid it on Yatzachaq his ban (son). He took in his yad (hand) the ash (fire) and the knife. They shanayam (both) went together.

Yatzachaq spoke to Abaraham his ab (father), and said, "My ab (father)?" He said, "Here I am, my ban (son)." He said, "Here is the ash (fire) and the itz (wood), but where is the lamb for a burnt ilah (offering)?
Abaraham said, "Alahayam will raah (see) himself the lamb for a burnt ilah (offering), my ban (son)." So they shanayam (both) went together.

They came to the place which Alahayam had told him of. Abaraham built the mazabach (altar) there, and laid the itz (wood) in order, bound Yatzachaq his ban (son), and laid him on the mazabach (altar), on the itz (wood).
Abaraham stretched out his yad (hand), and took the knife to kill his ban (son).
The malaak (angel) of Yahawah called to him out of the sky, and said, "Abaraham, Abaraham!" He said, "Here I am.

He said, "Don't shalach (lay) your yad (hand) on the nair (boy), neither do anything to him. For now I yadai (know) that you yaraa (fear) Alahayam, since you have not withheld your yachayad (son), your only ban (son), from me.

Abaraham lifted up his iyan (eyes), and looked, and saw that achar (behind) him was a ayal (ram) caught in the thicket by his qaran (horns). Abaraham went and took the ayal (ram), and offered him up for a burnt ilah (offering) instead of his ban (son).
Abaraham called the sham (name) of that place Yahawah Will Provide. As it is said to this yawam (day), "On yahawah (yahweh's) har (mountain), it will be provided.
The malaak (angel) of Yahawah called to Abaraham a shanay (second) time out of the sky,
and said, "I have sworn by myself, says Yahawah, because you have done this thing, and have not withheld your ban (son), your only yachayad (son),

that I will barak (bless) you barak (greatly), and I will multiply your zarai (seed) greatly like the kawakab (stars) of the shamayam (heavens), and like the sand which is on the shapah (seashore). Your zarai (seed) will yarash (possess) the gate of his ayab (enemies).
In your zarai (seed) will all the gawayay (nations) of the aratz (earth) be blessed, because you have obeyed my qawal (voice).
So Abaraham returned to his nair (young) men, and they rose up and went together Baarashabai Beersheba. Abaraham lived at Beersheba.
It happened achar (after) these things, that it was told Abaraham, saying, "Behold, Malakah, she also has borne children to your ach (brother) Nachawar:
Iwatz his firstborn, Bawaz his ach (brother), Qamawaal the ab (father) of Aram,
Kashad, Chazaw, Paladash, Yadalap, and Bathawaal.
Bathawaal became the father of Rabaqah. These shamanah (eight) Malakah bore to Nachawar, Abaraham ach (brother).
His concubine, whose sham (name) was Raawamah, also bore Tabach, Gacham, Thachash, and Maikah.
Sharah lived one hundred twenty-seven Shanah. This was the Shanah of Sharah chay (life).
Sharah died Qarayathaarabai Kiriath Arba (the same is Chabarawan), in the aratz (land) of Kanain. Abaraham came to mourn for Sharah, and to weep for her.
Abaraham rose up from panayam (before) his mawath (dead), and spoke to the children of Chath, saying,
"I am a stranger and a foreigner living with you. nathan (give) me a achazah (possession) of a burying-place with you, that I may bury my mawath (dead) out of my panayam (sight).
The children of Chath answered Abaraham, saying to him,
"Hear us, my Adawan. You are a nashayaa (prince) of Alahayam among us. Bury your mawath (dead) in the best of our tombs. laa (none) of us will withhold from you his tomb. Bury your mawath (dead).
Abaraham rose up, and bowed himself to the im (people) of the aratz (land), even to the children of Chath.
He talked with them, saying, "If it be your napash (mind) that I should bury my mawath (dead) out of my panayam (sight), hear me, and pagai (entreat) for me to Iparawan the ban (son) of Tzachar,

that he may nathan (give) me the cave of Makapalah, which he has, which is in the end of his shadah (field). For the Malaa kasap (price) let him nathan (give) it to me among you for a achazah (possession) of a burying-place.

Now Iparawan was sitting in the middle of the children of Chath. Iparawan the Chathay (Hittite) answered Abaraham in the hearing of the children of Chath, even of all who went in at the gate of his Iyar, saying,

"No, my Adawan, hear me. I give you the shadah (field), and I give you the cave that is in it. In the iyan (presence) of the children of my im (people) I nathan (give) it to you. Bury your mawath (dead).
Abaraham bowed himself down panayam (before) the im (people) of the aratz (land).

He spoke to Iparawan in the audience of the im (people) of the aratz (land), saying, "But if you will, please hear me. I will nathan (give) the kasap (price) of the shadah (field). Take it from me, and I will bury my mawath (dead) there.
Iparawan answered Abaraham, saying to him,
"My Adawan, listen to me. What is a piece of aratz (land) worth arabai (four) maah (hundred) shekels of kasap (silver) between me and you? Therefore bury your mawath (dead).

Abaraham listened to Iparawan. Abaraham weighed to Iparawan the kasap (silver) which he had named in the audience of the children of Chath, arabai (four) maah (hundred) shekels of kasap (silver), according to the ibar (current) merchants' standard.

So the shadah (field) of Iparawan, which was in Makapalah, which was panayam (before) Mamaraa, the shadah (field), the cave which was in it, and all the itz (trees) that were in the shadah (field), that were in all of its borders, were deeded
to Abaraham for a maqanah (possession) in the iyan (presence) of the children of Chath, before all who went in at the gate of his Iyar.
achar (after) this, Abaraham buried Sharah his ashah (wife) in the cave of the shadah (field) of Makapalah panayam (before) Mamaraa (that is, Chabarawan), in the aratz (land) of Kanain.
The shadah (field), and the cave that is in it, were deeded to Abaraham for a achazah (possession) of a qabar (burying) place by the children of Chath.
Abaraham was zaqan (old), and well bawaa (stricken) in yawam (age). Yahawah had blessed Abaraham in all things.
Abaraham said to his ibad (servant), the zaqan (elder) of his bayath (house), who ruled over all that he had, "Please shawam (put) your yad (hand) under my thigh.

I will make you shabai (swear) by Yahawah, the Alahayam of shamayam (heaven) and the Alahayam of the aratz (earth), that you shall not take a ashah (wife) for my ban (son) of the bath (daughters) of the Kanainay (Canaanites), qarab (among) whom I live.
But you shall yalak (go) to my aratz (country), and to my relatives, and take a ashah (wife) for my ban (son) Yatzachaq.

The ibad (servant) said to him, "What if the ashah (woman) isn't abah (willing) to yalak (follow) me to this aratz (land)? Must I shawab (turn back / repent) your ban (son) again to the aratz (land) you came from?
Abaraham said to him, "Beware that you don't shawab (turn back / repent) my ban (son) there again.

Yahawah, the Alahayam of shamayam (heaven), who took me from my ab (father's) bayath (house), and from the aratz (land) of my birth, who spoke to me, and who swore to me, saying, ‘I will nathan (give) this aratz (land) to your zarai (seed).' He will shalach (send) his malaak (angel) panayam (before) you, and you shall take a ashah (wife) for my ban (son) from there.
If the ashah (woman) isn't abah (willing) to yalak (follow) you, then you shall be clear from this my shabawaih (oath). Only you shall not shawab (turn back / repent) my ban (son) there again.
The ibad (servant) shawam (put) his yad (hand) under the thigh of Abaraham his adawan (master), and swore to him concerning this dabar (matter).

The ibad (servant) took ishar (ten) camels, of his adawan (master's) camels, and departed, having a variety of tawab (good) things of his adawan (master's) with him. He qawam (arose), and went to Aramanaharayam, to the Iyar of Nachawar.
He made the camels barak (kneel) down outside the Iyar by the baar (well) of mayam (water) at the ith (time) of evening, the ith (time) that women yatzaa (go) out to draw shaab (water).
He said, "Yahawah, the Alahayam of my adawan (master) Abaraham, panayam (please) give me success this yawam (day), and show chasad (kindness) to my adawan (master) Abaraham.
Behold, I am standing by the spring of mayam (water). The bath (daughters) of the men of the Iyar are coming out to shaab (draw) mayam (water).

Let it happen, that the young lady to whom I will amar (say), ‘Please let down your pitcher, that I may drink,' and she will amar (say), ‘Drink, and I will also shaqah (give) your camels a drink,'—let her be the one you have appointed for your ibad (servant) Yatzachaq. By this I will yadai (know) that you have shown chasad (kindness) to my adawan (master).

It happened, before he had finished speaking, that behold, Rabaqah came out, who was yalad (born) to Bathawaal the ban (son) of Malakah, the ashah (wife) of Nachawar, Abaraham ach (brother), with her pitcher on her shoulder.
The young lady was very tawab (beautiful) to look at, a virgin, neither had any ayash (man) yadai (known) her. She went down to the spring, filled her pitcher, and came up.
The ibad (servant) ran to qaraah (meet) her, and said, "Please give me a drink, a Mait mayam (water) from your pitcher.
She said, "Drink, my Adawan." She hurried, and let down her pitcher on her yad (hand), and gave him shaqah (drink).
When she had kalah (done) giving him shaqah (drink), she said, "I will also shaab (draw) for your camels, until they have kalah (done) drinking.
She hurried, and emptied her pitcher into the trough, and ran again to the baar (well) to shaab (draw), and drew for all his camels.
The ayash (man) looked steadfastly at her, remaining charash (silent), to yadai (know) whether Yahawah had made his darak (journey) prosperous or not.

It happened, as the camels had kalah (done) drinking, that the ayash (man) took a golden ring of half a shekel weight, and shanayam (two) bracelets for her yad (hands) of ishar (ten) shekels weight of gold,
and said, "Whose bath (daughter) are you? Please nagad (tell) me. Is there room in your ab (father's) bayath (house) for us to lawan (lodge) in?
She said to him, "I am the bath (daughter) of Bathawaal the ban (son) of Malakah, whom she bore to Nachawar.
She said moreover to him, "We have both straw and provender rab (enough), and room to lawan (lodge) in.
The ayash (man) bowed his qadad (head), and worshiped Yahawah.

He said, "Blessed be Yahawah, the Alahayam of my adawan (master) Abaraham, who has not forsaken his loving chasad (kindness) and his truth toward my adawan (master). As for me, Yahawah has led me in the darak (way) to the bayath (house) of my adawan (master's) relatives.
The young lady ran, and told her am (mother's) bayath (house) about these dabar (words).
Rabaqah had a ach (brother), and his sham (name) was Laban. Laban ran out to the ayash (man), to the spring.

It happened, when he saw the ring, and the bracelets on his achawath (sister's) yad (hands), and when he heard the dabar (words) of Rabaqah his achawath (sister), saying, "This is what the ayash (man) said to me," that he came to the ayash (man). Behold, he was standing by the camels at the spring.
He said, "bawaa (come) in, you blessed of Yahawah. Why do you imad (stand) outside? For I have prepared the bayath (house), and room for the camels.
The ayash (man) came into the bayath (house), and he unloaded the camels. He gave straw and provender for the camels, and mayam (water) to wash his feet and the feet of the men who were with him.
Food was shawam (set) panayam (before) him to akal (eat), but he said, "I will not akal (eat) until I have told my dabar (message)." He said, "dabar (speak) on.
He said, "I am Abaraham ibad (servant).

Yahawah has blessed my adawan (master) maad (greatly). He has become great. He has given him flocks and herds, kasap (silver) and gold, male ibad (servants) and female shapachah (servants), and camels and donkeys.
Sharah, my adawan (master's) ashah (wife), bore a ban (son) to my adawan (master) when she was old. He has given all that he has to him.
My adawan (master) made me shabai (swear), saying, ‘You shall not take a ashah (wife) for my ban (son) of the bath (daughters) of the Kanainay (Canaanites), in whose aratz (land) I live,
but you shall yalak (go) to my ab (father's) bayath (house), and to my relatives, and take a ashah (wife) for my ban (son).'
I asked my adawan (master), ‘What if the ashah (woman) will not yalak (follow) me?'

He said to me, ‘Yahawah, panayam (before) whom I halak (walk), will shalach (send) his malaak (angel) with you, and tzalach (prosper) your darak (way). You shall take a ashah (wife) for my ban (son) of my relatives, and of my ab (father's) bayath (house).
Then will you be clear from my alah (oath), when you bawaa (come) to my relatives. If they don't nathan (give) her to you, you shall be naqay (clear) from my alah (oath).'
I came this yawam (day) to the spring, and said, ‘Yahawah, the Alahayam of my adawan (master) Abaraham, if now you do tzalach (prosper) my darak (way) which I halak (go)—

behold, I am standing by this spring of mayam (water). Let it happen, that the maiden who yatzaa (comes) out to shaab (draw), to whom I will amar (say), "Please shaqah (give) me a Mait mayam (water) from your pitcher to shaqah (drink),
and she will tell me, "Drink, and I will also shaab (draw) for your camels,"—let her be the ashah (woman) whom Yahawah has appointed for my adawan (master's) ban (son).'
Before I had finished speaking in my lab (heart), behold, Rabaqah came out with her pitcher on her shoulder. She went down to the spring, and drew. I said to her, ‘Please let me shaqah (drink).'
She hurried and let down her pitcher from her shoulder, and said, ‘Drink, and I will also shaqah (give) your camels a shaqah (drink).' So I drank, and she also gave the camels a shaqah (drink).

I asked her, and said, ‘Whose bath (daughter) are you?' She said, ‘The bath (daughter) of Bathawaal, Nachawar ban (son), whom Malakah bore to him.' I shawam (put) the ring on her ap (nose), and the bracelets on her yad (hands).

I bowed my qadad (head), and worshiped Yahawah, and blessed Yahawah, the Alahayam of my adawan (master) Abaraham, who had led me in the amath (right) darak (way) to take my adawan (master's) ach (brother's) bath (daughter) for his ban (son).

Now if you will ishah (deal) chasad (kindly) and truly with my adawan (master), nagad (tell) me. If not, nagad (tell) me, that I may panah (turn) to the right yamayan (hand), or to the shamaawal (left).
Then Laban and Bathawaal answered, "The thing yatzaa (proceeds) from Yahawah. We can't dabar (speak) to you rai (bad) or tawab (good).
Behold, Rabaqah is panayam (before) you. Take her, and yalak (go), and let her be your adawan (master's) ban (son's) ashah (wife), as Yahawah has spoken.
It happened that when Abaraham ibad (servant) heard their dabar (words), he bowed himself down to the aratz (earth) to Yahawah.
The ibad (servant) brought out jewels of kasap (silver), and jewels of gold, and clothing, and gave them to Rabaqah. He also gave precious things to her ach (brother) and her am (mother).
They ate and drank, he and the men who were with him, and stayed all lawan (night). They rose up in the baqar (morning), and he said, "shalach (send) me away to my adawan (master).
Her ach (brother) and her am (mother) said, "Let the young lady stay with us a few yawam (days), at least ishawar (ten). achar (after) that she will yalak (go).
He said to them, "Don't hinder me, since Yahawah has prospered my darak (way). shalach (send) me away that I may yalak (go) to my adawan (master).
They said, "We will qaraa (call) the young lady, and shaal (ask) her.
They called Rabaqah, and said to her, "Will you yalak (go) with this ayash (man)?" She said, "I will yalak (go).
They sent shalach (away) Rabaqah, their achawath (sister), with her nurse, Abaraham ibad (servant), and his men.

They blessed Rabaqah, and said to her, "Our achawath (sister), may you be the mother of alap (thousands) of rababah (ten) thousands, and let your zarai (seed) yarash (possess) the gate of those who shanaa (hate) them.
Rabaqah qawam (arose) with her ladies. They rode on the camels, and followed the ayash (man). The ibad (servant) took Rabaqah, and went his yalak (way).
Yatzachaq came from the bawaa (way) of Baaralachayaraay Lahai Roi, for he lived in the aratz (land) of the Nagab.
Yatzachaq went out to meditate in the shadah (field) at the evening. He lifted up his iyan (eyes), and saw, and, behold, there were camels coming.
Rabaqah lifted up her iyan (eyes), and when she saw Yatzachaq, she dismounted from the camel.

She said to the ibad (servant), "Who is the ayash (man) who is walking in the shadah (field) to qaraah (meet) us?" The ibad (servant) said, "It is my adawan (master)." She took her tzaiyap (veil), and covered herself.
The ibad (servant) told Yatzachaq all the things that he had done.
Yatzachaq brought her into his am (mother) Sharah ahal (tent), and took Rabaqah, and she became his ashah (wife). He loved her. Yatzachaq was comforted achar (after) his am (mother's) death.
Abaraham took another ashah (wife), and her sham (name) was Qatawarah.
She bore him Zamaran, Yaqashan, Madan, Madayan, Yashabaq, and Shawach.
Yaqashan became the father of Shabaa, and Dadan. The ban (sons) of Dadan were Ashawaray, Latawasham, and Laamayam.
The ban (sons) of Madayan: Iyapah, Ipar, Chanawak, Abayadai, and Aladaih. All these were the children of Qatawarah.
Abaraham gave all that he had to Yatzachaq,

but to the ban (sons) of Abaraham concubines, Abaraham gave mathanah (gifts). He sent them shalach (away) from Yatzachaq his ban (son), while he yet lived, eastward, to the qadam (east) aratz (country).
These are the yawam (days) of the Shanah of Abaraham chay (life) which he lived: one maah (hundred) seventy-five Shanah.
Abaraham gave up the spirit, and died in a tawab (good) shayabah (old) age, an old zaqan (man), and Shabai of years, and was gathered to his im (people).
Yatzachaq and Yashamaial, his ban (sons), buried him in the cave of Makapalah, in the shadah (field) of Iparawan, the ban (son) of Tzachar the Chathay (Hittite), which is panayam (before) Mamaraa,
the shadah (field) which Abaraham purchased of the children of Chath. Abaraham was buried there with Sharah, his ashah (wife).
It happened achar (after) the mawath (death) of Abaraham that Alahayam blessed Yatzachaq, his ban (son). Yatzachaq lived by Baaralachayaraay Lahai Roi.
Now this is the history of the thawaladah (generations) of Yashamaial, Abaraham ban (son), whom Hagar the Matzaray (Egyptian), Sharah handmaid, bore to Abaraham.
These are the sham (names) of the ban (sons) of Yashamaial, by their sham (names), according to the order of their birth: the firstborn of Yashamaial, Nabayawath, then Qadar, Adabaal, Mabasham,
Mashamai, Dawamah, Mashaa,
Hadad, Thayamaa, Yatawar, Napayash, and Qadamah.
These are the ban (sons) of Yashamaial, and these are their sham (names), by their villages, and by their encampments: shanayam (twelve) nashayaa (princes), according to their amah (nations).
These are the Shanah of the chay (life) of Yashamaial: one hundred thirty-seven Shanah. He gave up the spirit and died, and was gathered to his im (people).
They lived from Chawayalah to Shawar that is panayam (before) Matzarayam, as you bawaa (go) toward Ashawar. He lived opposite all his relatives.
This is the history of the thawaladah (generations) of Yatzachaq, Abaraham ban (son). Abraham became the father of Yatzachaq.

Yatzachaq was arabaiyam (forty) Shanah ban (old) when he took Rabaqah, the bath (daughter) of Bathawaal the Aramay (Syrian) Padan Paddan Aram, the achawath (sister) of Laban the Aramay (Syrian), to be his ashah (wife).
Yatzachaq entreated Yahawah for his ashah (wife), because she was Iqar. Yahawah was entreated by him, and Rabaqah his ashah (wife) conceived.
The children struggled ratzatz (together) qarab (within) her. She said, "If it be so, why do I live?" She went to inquire of Yahawah.

Yahawah said to her, "shanayam (two) gayayam (nations) are in your womb. shanayam (two) laam (peoples) will be separated from your body. The one laam (people) will be amatz (stronger) than the other laam (people). The rab (elder) will ibad (serve) the Tzaiyar.
When her yawam (days) to be yalad (delivered) were fulfilled, behold, there were twins in her womb.
The raashawan (first) came out Adamanay all over, like a hairy adarath (garment). They sham (named) him Ishaw.
achar (after) that, his ach (brother) came out, and his yad (hand) had achaz (hold) on Ishaw heel. He was sham (named) Yaiqab. Yatzachaq was shashayam (sixty) Shanah ban (old) when she bore them.
The nair (boys) grew. Ishaw was a skillful hunter, a ayash (man) of the shadah (field). Yaiqab was a quiet ayash (man), living in ahal (tents).
Now Yatzachaq loved Ishaw, because he ate his venison. Rabaqah loved Yaiqab.
Yaiqab boiled stew. Ishaw came in from the shadah (field), and he was Iyap.
Ishaw said to Yaiqab, "Please feed me with that Adam Adam Iyap, for I am famished." Therefore his sham (name) was called Adam.
Yaiqab said, "makar (first), sell me your birthright.
Ishaw said, "Behold, I am halak (about) to mawath (die). What bakawarah (good) is the birthright to me?
Yaiqab said, "shabai (swear) to me first." He swore to him. He sold his birthright to Yaiqab.
Yaiqab gave Ishaw lacham (bread) and stew of lentils. He ate and drank, rose up, and went his yalak (way). So Ishaw despised his birthright.

There was a famine in the aratz (land), bad (besides) the raashawan (first) famine that was in the yawam (days) of Abaraham. Yatzachaq went to Abayamalak malak (king) of the Palashathay (Philistines), to Garar.
Yahawah raah (see) to him, and said, "Don't yarad (go) down into Matzarayam. Live in the aratz (land) I will amar (tell) you about.

Live in this aratz (land), and I will be with you, and will barak (bless) you. For to you, and to your zarai (seed), I will nathan (give) all these aratz (lands), and I will qawam (establish) the shabawaih (oath) which I swore to Abaraham your ab (father).

I will multiply your zarai (seed) as the kawakab (stars) of the sky, and will nathan (give) to your zarai (seed) all these aratz (lands). In your zarai (seed) will all the gawayay (nations) of the aratz (earth) be blessed,
because Abaraham obeyed my qawal (voice), and kept my requirements, my matzawah (commandments), my chaqah (statutes), and my thawarah (laws).
Yatzachaq lived in Garar.

The men of the place asked him about his ashah (wife). He said, "She is my achawath (sister)," for he was yaraa (afraid) to amar (say), "My ashah (wife)," lest, he thought, "the men of the place might harag (kill) me for Rabaqah, because she is tawab (beautiful) to look at.

It happened, when he had been there a long yawam (time), that Abayamalak malak (king) of the Palashathay (Philistines) looked out at a window, and saw, and, behold, Yatzachaq was caressing Rabaqah, his ashah (wife).

Abayamalak called Yatzachaq, and said, "Behold, ak (surely) she is your ashah (wife). Why did you amar (say), ‘She is my achawath (sister)?'" Yatzachaq said to him, "Because I said, ‘Lest I mawath (die) because of her.'
Abayamalak said, "What is this you have done to us? One of the im (people) might Mait have lain with your ashah (wife), and you would have brought guilt on us!
Abayamalak tzawah (commanded) all the im (people), saying, "He who touches this ayash (man) or his ashah (wife) will mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death).
Yatzachaq sowed in that aratz (land), and reaped in the same Shanah one maah (hundred) times what he planted. Yahawah blessed him.
The ayash (man) grew great, and grew more and more until he became very great.
He had maqanah (possessions) of flocks, maqanah (possessions) of herds, and a rab (great) ibadah (household). The Palashathay (Philistines) envied him.
Now all the baar (wells) which his ab (father's) ibad (servants) had dug in the yawam (days) of Abaraham his ab (father), the Palashathay (Philistines) had stopped, and filled with ipar (earth).
Abayamalak said to Yatzachaq, "yalak (go) from us, for you are much itzam (mightier) than we.
Yatzachaq departed from there, encamped in the nachal (valley) of Garar, and lived there.

Yatzachaq dug again the baar (wells) of mayam (water), which they had dug in the yawam (days) of Abaraham his ab (father). For the Palashathay (Philistines) had stopped them achar (after) the mawath (death) of Abaraham. He called their sham (names) after the sham (names) by which his ab (father) had called them.
Yatzachaq ibad (servants) dug in the nachal (valley), and found there a baar (well) of chay (springing) mayam (water).
The herdsmen of Garar argued with Yatzachaq herdsmen, saying, "The mayam (water) is ours." He called the sham (name) of the baar (well) Ishaq, because they contended with him.
They dug achar (another) baar (well), and they argued over that, also. He called its name Shatanah.

He left that place, and dug achar (another) baar (well). They didn't argue over that one. He called it Rachabawath. He said, "For now Yahawah has made room for us, and we will be fruitful in the aratz (land).
He went up Baarashabai there to Beersheba.

Yahawah raah (see) to him the same layal (night), and said, "I am the Alahayam of Abaraham your ab (father). Don't be yaraa (afraid), for I am with you, and will barak (bless) you, and multiply your zarai (seed) for my ibad (servant) Abaraham sake.
He built an mazabach (altar) there, and called on the sham (name) of Yahawah, and pitched his ahal (tent) there. There Yatzachaq ibad (servants) dug a baar (well).
Then Abayamalak went to him from Garar, and Achazath his friend, and Payakal the shar (captain) of his tzabaa (army).
Yatzachaq said to them, "Why have you bawaa (come) to me, since you shanaa (hate) me, and have sent me shalach (away) from you?
They said, "We saw plainly that Yahawah was with you. We said, ‘Let there now be an alah (oath) between us, even between us and you, and let us karath (make) a barayath (covenant) with you,

that you will do us no rai (harm), as we have not touched you, and as we have done to you raq (nothing) but tawab (good), and have sent you shalach (away) in shalawam (peace).' You are now the blessed of Yahawah.
He made them a feast, and they ate and drank.
They rose up some time in the baqar (morning), and swore one to ach (another). Yatzachaq sent them shalach (away), and they departed from him in shalawam (peace).
It happened the same yawam (day), that Yatzachaq ibad (servants) came, and told him concerning the baar (well) which they had dug, and said to him, "We have found mayam (water).
He called it Shabaih. Therefore the sham (name) of the Iyar is Baarashabai to this yawam (day).

When Ishaw was arabaiyam (forty) Shanah ban (old), he took as ashah (wife) Yahawadayath, the bath (daughter) of Baaray the Chathay (Hittite), and Bashamath, the bath (daughter) of Ayalawan the Chathay (Hittite).
They grieved Yatzachaq and Rabaqah rawach (spirits).

It happened, that when Yatzachaq was zaqan (old), and his iyan (eyes) were dim, so that he could not raah (see), he called Ishaw his gadawal (elder) ban (son), and said to him, "My ban (son)?" He said to him, "Here I am.
He said, "See now, I am zaqan (old). I don't yadai (know) the yawam (day) of my mawath (death).
Now therefore, please nashaa (take) your weapons, your quiver and your qashath (bow), and yatzaa (go) out to the shadah (field), and take me venison.
ishah (make) me savory food, such as I ahab (love), and bawaa (bring) it to me, that I may akal (eat), and that my napash (soul) may barak (bless) you before I mawath (die).
Rabaqah heard when Yatzachaq spoke to Ishaw his ban (son). Ishaw went to the shadah (field) to hunt for venison, and to bawaa (bring) it.
Rabaqah spoke to Yaiqab her ban (son), saying, "Behold, I heard your ab (father) dabar (speak) to Ishaw your ach (brother), saying,
‘bawaa (bring) me venison, and ishah (make) me savory food, that I may akal (eat), and barak (bless) you panayam (before) Yahawah panayam (before) my mawath (death).'
Now therefore, my ban (son), obey my qawal (voice) according to that which I tzawah (command) you.
yalak (go) now to the flock, and get me from there shanayam (two) tawab (good) young goats. I will ishah (make) them savory food for your ab (father), such as he ahab (loves).
You shall bawaa (bring) it to your ab (father), that he may akal (eat), so that he may barak (bless) you panayam (before) his mawath (death).
Yaiqab said to Rabaqah his am (mother), "Behold, Ishaw my ach (brother) is a Shaiyar ayash (man), and I am a Chalaq ayash (man).
What if my ab (father) touches me? I will seem to him as a deceiver, and I would bawaa (bring) a qalalah (curse) on myself, and not a barakah (blessing).
His am (mother) said to him, "Let your qalalah (curse) be on me, my ban (son). Only obey my qawal (voice), and yalak (go) get them for me.
He went, and got them, and brought them to his am (mother). His am (mother) made savory food, such as his ab (father) loved.
Rabaqah took the chamadah (good) clothes of Ishaw, her gadawal (elder) ban (son), which were with her in the bayath (house), and Labash them on Yaiqab, her younger ban (son).
She Labash the skins of the young goats on his yad (hands), and on the chalaqah (smooth) of his neck.
She gave the savory food and the lacham (bread), which she had prepared, into the yad (hand) of her ban (son) Yaiqab.
He came to his ab (father), and said, "My ab (father)?" He said, "Here I am. Who are you, my ban (son)?

Yaiqab said to his ab (father), "I am Ishaw your firstborn. I have done what you asked me to do. Please qawam (arise), yashab (sit) and akal (eat) of my venison, that your napash (soul) may barak (bless) me.
Yatzachaq said to his ban (son), "How is it that you have found it so quickly, my ban (son)?" He said, "Because Yahawah your Alahayam gave me success.
Yatzachaq said to Yaiqab, "Please come near, that I may feel you, my ban (son), whether you are really my ban (son) Ishaw or not.
Yaiqab went near to Yatzachaq his ab (father). He felt him, and said, "The qawal (voice) is Yaiqab qawal (voice), but the yad (hands) are the yad (hands) of Ishaw.
He didn't recognize him, because his yad (hands) were Shaiyar, like his ach (brother), Ishaw yad (hands). So he blessed him.
He said, "Are you really my ban (son) Ishaw?" He said, "I am.

He said, "Bring it near to me, and I will akal (eat) of my ban (son's) venison, that my napash (soul) may barak (bless) you." He brought it near to him, and he ate. He brought him yayan (wine), and he drank.
His ab (father) Yatzachaq said to him, "Come near now, and kiss me, my ban (son).

He came near, and kissed him. He smelled the rayach (smell) of his clothing, and blessed him, and said, "raah (see), the rayach (smell) of my ban (son) is as the rayach (smell) of a shadah (field) which Yahawah has blessed.
Alahayam nathan (give) you of the dew of the sky, of the fatness of the aratz (earth), and plenty of grain and new thayarawash (wine).

Let im (peoples) ibad (serve) you, and laam (nations) shachah (bow) down to you. Be Adawan over your ach (brothers). Let your am (mother's) ban (sons) shachah (bow) down to you. Cursed be everyone who arar (curses) you. Blessed be everyone who blesses you.

It happened, as soon as Yatzachaq had made an kalah (end) of blessing Yaiqab, and Yaiqab had just gone out from the panayam (presence) of Yatzachaq his ab (father), that Ishaw his ach (brother) came in from his hunting.

He also made savory food, and brought it to his ab (father). He said to his ab (father), "Let my ab (father) qawam (arise), and akal (eat) of his ban (son's) venison, that your napash (soul) may barak (bless) me.
Yatzachaq his ab (father) said to him, "Who are you?" He said, "I am your ban (son), your firstborn, Ishaw.
Yatzachaq trembled violently, and said, "Who, then, is he who has taken venison, and brought it me, and I have eaten of all before you came, and have blessed him? Yes, he will be blessed.
When Ishaw heard the dabar (words) of his ab (father), he cried with an maad (exceeding) gadawal (great) and Mar cry, and said to his ab (father), "barak (bless) me, even me also, my ab (father).
He said, "Your ach (brother) came with deceit, and has taken away your barakah (blessing).

He said, "Isn't he rightly named Yaiqab? For he has supplanted me these paim (two) times. He took away my birthright. See, now he has taken away my barakah (blessing)." He said, "Haven't you reserved a barakah (blessing) for me?

Yatzachaq answered Ishaw, "Behold, I have made him your Adawan, and all his ach (brothers) have I given to him for ibad (servants). With grain and new thayarawash (wine) have I sustained him. What then will I do for you, my ban (son)?
Ishaw said to his ab (father), "Have you but one barakah (blessing), my ab (father)? barak (bless) me, even me also, my ab (father)." Ishaw lifted up his qawal (voice), and wept.
Yatzachaq his ab (father) answered him, "Behold, of the fatness of the aratz (earth) will be your mawashab (dwelling), and of the dew of the sky from above.
By your charab (sword) will you chayah (live), and you will ibad (serve) your ach (brother). It will happen, when you will paraq (break) loose, that you shall shake his yoke from off your neck.

Ishaw hated Yaiqab because of the barakah (blessing) with which his ab (father) blessed him. Ishaw said in his lab (heart), "The yawam (days) of mourning for my ab (father) are at qarab (hand). Then I will harag (kill) my ach (brother) Yaiqab.

The dabar (words) of Ishaw, her gadawal (elder) ban (son), were told to Rabaqah. She sent and called Yaiqab, her younger ban (son), and said to him, "Behold, your ach (brother) Ishaw nacham (comforts) himself about you by planning to harag (kill) you.
Now therefore, my ban (son), obey my qawal (voice). qawam (arise), flee to Laban, my ach (brother), in Charan.
Stay with him a achad (few) yawam (days), until your ach (brother's) fury shawab (turn back / repent) away;

until your ach (brother's) ap (anger) shawab (turn back / repent) away from you, and he forgets what you have done to him. Then I will shalach (send), and get you from there. mah (why) should I be bereaved of you shanayam (both) in one yawam (day)?

Rabaqah said to Yatzachaq, "I am weary of my chay (life) panayam (because) of the bath (daughters) of Chath. If Yaiqab takes a ashah (wife) of the bath (daughters) of Chath, such as these, of the bath (daughters) of the aratz (land), what mah (good) will my chay (life) do me?
Yatzachaq called Yaiqab, blessed him, and tzawah (commanded) him, "You shall not take a ashah (wife) of the bath (daughters) of Kanain.

qawam (arise), yalak (go) Padan Paddan Aram, to the bayath (house) of Bathawaal your am (mother's) ab (father). Take a ashah (wife) from there from the bath (daughters) of Laban, your am (mother's) ach (brother).
May Al Shaday barak (bless) you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, that you may be a qahal (company) of im (peoples),
and nathan (give) you the barakah (blessing) of Abaraham, to you, and to your zarai (seed) with you, that you may yarash (inherit) the aratz (land) where you travel, which Alahayam gave to Abaraham.
Yatzachaq sent Yaiqab shalach (away). He went Padan Paddan Aram to Laban, ban (son) of Bathawaal the Aramay (Syrian), Rabaqah ach (brother), Yaiqab and Ishaw am (mother).

Now Ishaw saw that Yatzachaq had blessed Yaiqab and sent him shalach (away) Padan Paddan Aram, to take him a ashah (wife) from there, and that as he blessed him he gave him a tzawah (command), saying, "You shall not take a ashah (wife) of the bath (daughters) of Kanain,
and that Yaiqab obeyed his ab (father) and his am (mother), and was gone to Paddan Padan.
Ishaw saw that the bath (daughters) of Kanain didn't iyan (please) Yatzachaq, his ab (father).
Ishaw went to Yashamaial, and took, besides the wives that he had, Machalath the bath (daughter) of Yashamaial, Abaraham ban (son), the achawath (sister) of Nabayawath, to be his ashah (wife).
Yaiqab went out from Beersheba, and went toward Charan.

He came to a certain place, and stayed there all lawan (night), because the shamash (sun) had bawaa (set). He took one of the aban (stones) of the place, and shawam (put) it under his maraashah (head), and shakab (lay) down in that place to sleep.
He dreamed. Behold, a stairway natzab (set) upon the aratz (earth), and its top reached to shamayam (heaven). Behold, the malaak (angels) of Alahayam ascending and descending on it.

Behold, Yahawah stood above it, and said, "I am Yahawah, the Alahayam of Abaraham your ab (father), and the Alahayam of Yatzachaq. The aratz (land) whereon you shakab (lie), to you will I nathan (give) it, and to your zarai (seed).

Your zarai (seed) will be as the ipar (dust) of the aratz (earth), and you will spread abroad to the yam (west), and to the qadam (east), and to the tzapawan (north), and to the Nagab. In you and in your zarai (seed) will all the mashapachah (families) of the adamah (earth) be blessed.

Behold, I am with you, and will shamar (keep) you, wherever you yalak (go), and will shawab (turn back / repent) you again into this adamah (land). For I will not leave you, until I have done that which I have spoken of to you.
Yaiqab awakened out of his shanah (sleep), and he said, "Surely Yahawah is in this place, and I didn't yadai (know) it.
He was yaraa (afraid), and said, "How yaraa (dreadful) is this place! This is none other than alahayam (god's) bayath (house), and this is the gate of shamayam (heaven).

Yaiqab rose up shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and took the aban (stone) that he had shawam (put) under his maraashah (head), and shawam (set) it up for a matzabah (pillar), and poured shaman (oil) on its raash (top).
He called the sham (name) of that place Bayathaal, but the sham (name) of the Iyar was Lawaz at the raashawan (first).

Yaiqab vowed a nadar (vow), saying, "If Alahayam will be with me, and will shamar (keep) me in this darak (way) that I halak (go), and will nathan (give) me lacham (bread) to akal (eat), and clothing to Labash on,
so that I shawab (turn back / repent) again to my ab (father's) bayath (house) in shalawam (peace), and Yahawah will be my Alahayam,

then this aban (stone), which I have shawam (set) up for a matzabah (pillar), will be alahayam (god's) bayath (house). Of all that you will nathan (give) me I will ishar (surely) give the ishar (tenth) to you.
Then Yaiqab went on his ragal (journey), and came to the aratz (land) of the children of the qadam (east).

He looked, and behold, a baar (well) in the shadah (field), and, behold, shalawash (three) flocks of sheep lying there by it. For out of that baar (well) they watered the flocks. The aban (stone) on the baar (well's) pah (mouth) was large.

There all the flocks were gathered. They rolled the aban (stone) from the baar (well's) pah (mouth), and watered the sheep, and shawab (turn back / repent) the aban (stone) again on the baar (well's) pah (mouth) in its place.
Yaiqab said to them, "My relatives, where are you from?" They said, "We are from Charan.
He said to them, "Do you yadai (know) Laban, the ban (son) of Nachawar?" They said, "We yadai (know) him.
He said to them, "Is it shalawam (well) with him?" They said, "It is shalawam (well). See, Rachal, his bath (daughter), is coming with the sheep.
He said, "Behold, it is still the middle of the yawam (day), not ith (time) to gather the livestock asap (together). shaqah (water) the sheep, and yalak (go) and raih (feed) them.
They said, "We can't, until all the flocks are gathered asap (together), and they roll the aban (stone) from the baar (well's) pah (mouth). Then we shaqah (water) the sheep.
iwad (while) he was yet speaking with them, Rachal came with her ab (father's) sheep, for she kept them.

It happened, when Yaiqab saw Rachal the bath (daughter) of Laban, his am (mother's) ach (brother), and the sheep of Laban, his am (mother's) ach (brother), that Yaiqab went near, and rolled the aban (stone) from the baar (well's) pah (mouth), and watered the flock of Laban his am (mother's) ach (brother).
Yaiqab kissed Rachal, and lifted up his qawal (voice), and wept.
Yaiqab told Rachal that he was her ab (father's) ach (brother), and that he was Rabaqah ban (son). She ran and told her ab (father).

It happened, when Laban heard the news of Yaiqab, his achawath (sister's) ban (son), that he ran to qaraah (meet) Yaiqab, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his bayath (house). Jacob told Laban all these things.
Laban said to him, "ak (surely) you are my itzam (bone) and my flesh." He lived with him for a chadash (month).
Laban said to Yaiqab, "Because you are my ach (brother), should you therefore ibad (serve) me for nothing? nagad (tell) me, what will your wages be?
Laban had shanayam (two) bath (daughters). The sham (name) of the gadawal (elder) was Laah, and the sham (name) of the younger was Rachal.
Laah iyan (eyes) were Rak, but Rachal was Yapah Yapah form and attractive.
Yaiqab loved Rachal. He said, "I will ibad (serve) you shabai (seven) Shanah for Rachal, your younger bath (daughter).
Laban said, "It is tawab (better) that I nathan (give) her to you, than that I should nathan (give) her to achar (another) ayash (man). Stay with me.
Yaiqab served shabai (seven) Shanah for Rachal. They seemed to him but a achad (few) yawam (days), for the ahabah (love) he had for her.
Yaiqab said to Laban, "Give me my ashah (wife), for my yawam (days) are fulfilled, that I may bawaa (go) in to her.
Laban gathered asap (together) all the men of the place, and made a feast.
It happened in the evening, that he took Laah his bath (daughter), and brought her to him. He went in to her.
Laban gave Zalapah his handmaid to his bath (daughter) Laah for a handmaid.
It happened in the baqar (morning) that, behold, it was Laah. He said to Laban, "What is this you have done to me? Didn't I ibad (serve) with you for Rachal? Why then have you deceived me?
Laban said, "It is not done so in our place, to nathan (give) the Tzaiyar panayam (before) the firstborn.
Fulfill the shabawai (week) of this zaath (one), and we will nathan (give) you the other also for the ibadah (service) which you will ibad (serve) with me yet shabai (seven) other Shanah.
Yaiqab did so, and fulfilled her shabawai (week). He gave him Rachal his bath (daughter) as ashah (wife).
Laban gave to Rachal his bath (daughter) Balahah, his handmaid, to be her handmaid.
He went in also to Rachal, and he loved also Rachal more than Laah, and served with him yet shabai (seven) other Shanah.
Yahawah saw that Laah was hated, and he opened her womb, but Rachal was Iqar.
Laah conceived, and bore a ban (son), and she sham (named) him Raawaban. For she said, "Because Yahawah has looked at my affliction. For now my ayash (husband) will ahab (love) me.
She conceived again, and bore a ban (son), and said, "Because Yahawah has heard that I am hated, he has therefore given me this son also." She sham (named) him Shamaiwan.

She conceived again, and bore a ban (son). Said, "paim (now) this time will my ayash (husband) be joined to me, because I have borne him shalawash (three) ban (sons)." Therefore was his sham (name) called Laway.
She conceived again, and bore a ban (son). She said, "This time will I yadah (praise) Yahawah." Therefore she sham (named) him Yahawadah (Judah). Then she stopped bearing.
When Rachal saw that she bore Yaiqab no children, Rachal envied her achawath (sister). She said to Yaiqab, "Give me children, or else I will mawath (die).
Yaiqab ap (anger) was kindled against Rachal, and he said, "Am I in alahayam (god's) place, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?
She said, "Behold, my amah (maid) Balahah. bawaa (go) in to her, that she may yalad (bear) on my knees, and I also may banah (obtain) children by her.
She gave him Balahah her handmaid as ashah (wife), and Yaiqab went in to her.
Balahah conceived, and bore Yaiqab a ban (son).
Rachal said, "Alahayam has judged me, and has also heard my qawal (voice), and has given me a ban (son)." Therefore called she his sham (name) Dan.
Balahah, Rachal handmaid, conceived again, and bore Yaiqab a shanay (second) ban (son).
Rachal said, "With alahayam (mighty) wrestlings have I wrestled with my achawath (sister), and have prevailed." She sham (named) him Napathalay.
When Laah saw that she had finished bearing, she took Zalapah, her handmaid, and gave her to Yaiqab as a ashah (wife).
Zalapah, Laah handmaid, bore Yaiqab a ban (son).
Laah said, "How fortunate!" She sham (named) him Gad.
Zalapah, Laah handmaid, bore Yaiqab a shanay (second) ban (son).
Laah said, "Happy am I, for the bath (daughters) will ashar (call) me happy." She sham (named) him Ashar.

Raawaban went in the yawam (days) of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the shadah (field), and brought them to his am (mother), Laah. Then Rachal said to Laah, "Please nathan (give) me some of your ban (son's) mandrakes.

She said to her, "Is it a Mait matter that you have taken away my ayash (husband)? Would you take away my ban (son's) mandrakes, also?" Rachal said, "Therefore he will shakab (lie) with you tonight for your ban (son's) mandrakes.

Yaiqab came from the shadah (field) in the evening, and Laah went out to qaraah (meet) him, and said, "You must bawaa (come) in to me; for I have surely hired you with my ban (son's) mandrakes." He shakab (lay) with her that layal (night).
Alahayam listened to Laah, and she conceived, and bore Yaiqab a chamayashay (fifth) ban (son).
Leah said, "God has given me my hire, because I gave my handmaid to my husband." She named him Issachar.
Laah conceived again, and bore a shashay (sixth) ban (son) to Yaiqab.
Laah said, "Alahayam has endowed me with a tawab (good) dowry. paim (now) my ayash (husband) will live with me, because I have borne him shash (six) ban (sons)." She sham (named) him Zabawalawan.
Afterwards, she bore a bath (daughter), and sham (named) her Dayanah.
Alahayam zakar (remembered) Rachal, and Alahayam listened to her, and opened her womb.
She conceived, bore a ban (son), and said, "Alahayam has taken asap (away) my reproach.
She sham (named) him Yawasap, saying, "May Yahawah add achar (another) ban (son) to me.
It happened, when Rachal had borne Yawasap, that Yaiqab said to Laban, "shalach (send) me away, that I may yalak (go) to my own place, and to my aratz (country).
nathan (give) me my wives and my children for whom I have served you, and let me yalak (go); for you yadai (know) my ibadah (service) with which I have served you.
Laban said to him, "If now I have found favor in your iyan (eyes), stay here, for I have divined that Yahawah has blessed me for your sake.
He said, "naqab (appoint) me your wages, and I will nathan (give) it.
He said to him, "You yadai (know) how I have served you, and how your livestock have fared with me.
For it was Mait which you had panayam (before) I came, and it has increased to a multitude. Yahawah has blessed you wherever I turned. Now when will I ishah (provide) for my own bayath (house) also?
He said, "What shall I nathan (give) you?" Yaiqab said, "You shall not nathan (give) me anything. If you will do this thing for me, I will again raih (feed) your flock and shamar (keep) it.

I will ibar (pass) through all your flock today, removing from there every Naqad and spotted shah (one), and Chawam black shah (one) among the sheep, and the spotted and Naqad among the goats. This will be my hire.

So my tzadaqah (righteousness) will answer for me hereafter, when you bawaa (come) concerning my hire that is panayam (before) you. Every kal (one) that is not Naqad and spotted among the goats, and Chawam among the sheep, that might be with me, will be counted stolen.
Laban said, "Behold, let it be according to your dabar (word).

That yawam (day), he removed the male goats that were Iqad and spotted, and all the female goats that were Naqad and spotted, every one that had Laban Chawam it, and all the black kashab (ones) among the sheep, and gave them into the yad (hand) of his ban (sons).
He shawam (set) shalawash (three) yawam (days)' darak (journey) between himself and Yaiqab, and Yaiqab fed the yathar (rest) of Laban flocks.
Yaiqab took to himself maqal (rods) Lach fresh poplar, almond, plane tree, peeled Laban streaks in them, and made the Laban appear which was in the maqal (rods).
He set the maqal (rods) which he had peeled opposite the flocks in the gutters in the watering-troughs where the flocks came to drink. They conceived when they came to drink.
The flocks conceived before the maqal (rods), and the flocks produced Iqad, Naqad, and spotted.

Yaiqab separated the lambs, and nathan (set) the panayam (faces) of the flocks toward the Iqad and all the Chawam in the flock of Laban: and he shayath (put) his own droves apart, and didn't shayath (put) them into Laban flock.

It happened, whenever the qashar (stronger) of the flock conceived, that Yaiqab laid the maqal (rods) before the iyan (eyes) of the flock in the gutters, that they might conceive among the maqal (rods);
but when the flock were feeble, he didn't shawam (put) them in. So the feebler were Laban, and the qashar (stronger) Yaiqab.
The ayash (man) increased maad (exceedingly), and had large flocks, female shapachah (servants) and male ibad (servants), and camels and donkeys.
He heard the dabar (words) of Laban ban (sons), saying, "Yaiqab has taken away all that was our ab (father's). From that which was our ab (father's), has he gotten all this wealth.
Yaiqab saw the expression on Laban face, and, behold, it was not toward him as shalashawam (before).
Yahawah said to Yaiqab, "shawab (turn back / repent) to the aratz (land) of your abawath (fathers), and to your relatives, and I will be with you.
Yaiqab sent and called Rachal and Laah to the shadah (field) to his flock,
and said to them, "I raah (see) the expression on your ab (father's) panayam (face), that it is not toward me as shalashawam (before); but the Alahayam of my ab (father) has been with me.
You yadai (know) that I have served your ab (father) with all of my strength.
Your ab (father) has deceived me, and changed my wages ishar (ten) times, but Alahayam didn't allow him to raii (hurt) me.
If he said this, ‘The Naqad will be your wages,' then all the flock bore Naqad. If he said this, ‘The Iqad will be your wages,' then all the flock bore Iqad.
Thus Alahayam has taken away your ab (father's) livestock, and given them to me.
It happened during mating ith (season) that I lifted up my iyan (eyes), and saw in a chalawam (dream), and behold, the male goats which leaped on the flock were Iqad, Naqad, and Barad.
The malaak (angel) of Alahayam said to me in the chalawam (dream), ‘Yaiqab,' and I said, ‘Here I am.'
He said, ‘Now nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eyes), and raah (see), all the male goats which ilah (leap) on the flock are Iqad, Naqad, and Barad, for I have seen all that Laban does to you.

I am the Al of Bayathaal, where you mashach (anointed) a matzabah (pillar), where you vowed a nadar (vow) to me. Now qawam (arise), yatzaa (get) out from this aratz (land), and shawab (turn back / repent) to the aratz (land) of your birth.'
Rachal and Laah answered him, "Is there yet any chalaq (portion) or nachalah (inheritance) for us in our ab (father's) bayath (house)?
Aren't we accounted by him as nakaray (foreigners)? For he has sold us, and has also akal (quite) devoured our kasap (money).
For all the riches which Alahayam has taken away from our ab (father), that is ours and our children's. Now then, whatever Alahayam has said to you, do.
Then Yaiqab rose up, and nashaa (set) his ban (sons) and his wives on the camels,

and he took away all his livestock, and all his rakawash (possessions) which he had gathered, including the livestock which he had gained Padan Paddan Aram, to bawaa (go) to Yatzachaq his ab (father), to the aratz (land) of Kanain.
Now Laban had gone to shear his sheep: and Rachal stole the tharapayam (teraphim) that were her ab (father's).
Yaiqab deceived Laban the Aramay (Syrian), in that he didn't tell him that he was running away.
So he fled with all that he had. He rose up, passed over the nahar (river), and shawam (set) his panayam (face) toward the har (mountain) of Galaid.
Laban was told on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) that Yaiqab had fled.
He took his relatives with him, and pursued achar (after) him shabai (seven) yawam (days)' darak (journey). He overtook him in the har (mountain) of Galaid.

Alahayam came to Laban, the Aramay (Syrian), in a chalawam (dream) of the layal (night), and said to him, "shamar (take) heed to yourself that you don't dabar (speak) to Yaiqab either tawab (good) or rai (bad).
Laban caught up with Yaiqab. Now Yaiqab had pitched his ahal (tent) in the har (mountain), and Laban with his relatives encamped in the har (mountain) of Galaid.
Laban said to Yaiqab, "What have you done, that you have deceived me, and carried away my bath (daughters) like captives of the charab (sword)?
Why did you flee secretly, and deceive me, and didn't nagad (tell) me, that I might have sent you shalach (away) with mirth and with songs, with tambourine and with harp;
and didn't allow me to kiss my ban (sons) and my bath (daughters)? Now have you done foolishly.

It is in the al (power) of my yad (hand) to rai (hurt) you, but the Alahayam of your ab (father) spoke to me last amash (night), saying, ‘shamar (take) heed to yourself that you don't speak to Yaiqab either tawab (good) or rai (bad).'
Now, you want to be gone, because you greatly longed for your ab (father's) bayath (house), but why have you stolen my Alahayam?
Yaiqab answered Laban, "Because I was yaraa (afraid), for I said, ‘Lest you should take your bath (daughters) from me by force.'

Anyone you matzaa (find) your Alahayam with shall not chayah (live). Before our relatives, nakar (discern) what is yours with me, and take it." For Yaiqab didn't yadai (know) that Rachal had stolen them.

Laban went into Yaiqab ahal (tent), into Laah ahal (tent), and into the ahal (tent) of the shanayam (two) female amah (servants); but he didn't matzaa (find) them. He went out of Laah ahal (tent), and entered into Rachal ahal (tent).
Now Rachal had taken the tharapayam (teraphim), shawam (put) them in the camel's saddle, and sat on them. Laban felt about all the ahal (tent), but didn't matzaa (find) them.

She said to her ab (father), "Don't let my Adawan be charah (angry) that I can't qawam (rise) up panayam (before) you; for I'm having my period." He searched, but didn't matzaa (find) the tharapayam (teraphim).
Yaiqab was charah (angry), and argued with Laban. Yaiqab answered Laban, "What is my pashai (trespass)? What is my chataah (sin), that you have hotly pursued achar (after) me?
Yaiqab that you have felt Laban in all my Laban, what have you found of all your household stuff? Set it here before my relatives and your relatives, that they may judge between us two.
"These isharayam (twenty) Shanah I have been with you. Your ewes and your female goats have not shakal (cast) their young, and I haven't eaten the ayal (rams) of your flocks.
That which was torn of animals, I didn't bawaa (bring) to you. I bore its chataa (loss). Of my yad (hand) you required it, whether stolen by yawam (day) or stolen by layal (night).
This was my situation: in the yawam (day) the drought consumed me, and the frost by layal (night); and my shanah (sleep) fled from my iyan (eyes).

These isharayam (twenty) Shanah I have been in your bayath (house). I served you fourteen Shanah for your shanayam (two) bath (daughters), and shash (six) Shanah for your flock, and you have changed my wages ishar (ten) times.

Unless the Alahayam of my ab (father), the Alahayam of Abaraham, and the pachad (fear) of Yatzachaq, had been with me, surely now you would have sent me shalach (away) empty. Alahayam has seen my affliction and the yagayai (labor) of my kap (hands), and rebuked you last amash (night).

Laban answered Yaiqab, "The bath (daughters) are my bath (daughters), the children are my children, the flocks are my flocks, and all that you raah (see) is mine: and what can I do this yawam (day) to these my bath (daughters), or to their children whom they have borne?
Now come, let us karath (make) a barayath (covenant), you and I; and let it be for a witness between me and you.
Yaiqab took a aban (stone), and set it up for a matzabah (pillar).
Yaiqab said to his relatives, "Gather aban (stones)." They took aban (stones), and made a heap. They ate there by the heap.
Laban called it Yagarashahadawathaa Sahadutha, but Yaiqab called it Galaid.
Laban said, "This heap is witness between me and you this yawam (day)." Therefore it was sham (named) Galaid
and Matzapah, for he said, "Yahawah watch between me and you, when we are absent one from rai (another).
If you afflict my bath (daughters), or if you take wives besides my bath (daughters), no ayash (man) is with us; raah (see), Alahayam is witness between me and you.
Laban said to Yaiqab, "See this heap, and see the matzabah (pillar), which I have set between me and you.

May this heap be a idah (witness), and the matzabah (pillar) be a idah (witness), that I will not ibar (pass) over this heap to you, and that you will not ibar (pass) over this heap and this matzabah (pillar) to me, for rai (harm).
The Alahayam of Abaraham, and the Alahayam of Nachawar, the Alahayam of their ab (father), shapat (judge) between us." Then Yaiqab swore by the pachad (fear) of his ab (father), Yatzachaq.
Yaiqab offered a zabach (sacrifice) in the har (mountain), and called his relatives to akal (eat) lacham (bread). They ate lacham (bread), and stayed all lawan (night) in the har (mountain).
shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), Laban rose up, and kissed his ban (sons) and his bath (daughters), and blessed them. Laban departed and returned to his place.
Yaiqab went on his darak (way), and the malaak (angels) of Alahayam met him.
When he saw them, Yaiqab said, "This is alahayam (god's) machanah (army)." He called the sham (name) of that place Machanayam.
Yaiqab sent malaak (messengers) in panayam (front) of him to Ishaw, his ach (brother), to the shadah (land) of Shaiyar, the shadah (field) of Adam.

He tzawah (commanded) them, saying, "This is what you shall amar (tell) my Adawan, Ishaw: ‘This is what your ibad (servant), Yaiqab, amar (says). I have lived as a foreigner with Laban, and stayed until now.
I have cattle, donkeys, flocks, male ibad (servants), and female shapachah (servants). I have sent to nagad (tell) my Adawan, that I may matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (sight).'
The malaak (messengers) returned to Yaiqab, saying, "We came to your ach (brother) Ishaw. Not only that, but he halak (comes) to qaraah (meet) you, and four maah (hundred) men with him.

Then Yaiqab was maad (greatly) yaraa (afraid) and was distressed. He divided the im (people) who were with him, and the flocks, and the herds, and the camels, into shanayam (two) machanah (companies);
and he said, "If Ishaw bawaa (comes) to the one machanah (company), and strikes it, then the machanah (company) which is shaar (left) will palayatah (escape).

Yaiqab said, "Alahayam of my ab (father) Abaraham, and Alahayam of my ab (father) Yatzachaq, Yahawah, who said to me, ‘shawab (turn back / repent) to your aratz (country), and to your relatives, and I will do you yatab (good),'

I am not worthy of the least of all the loving kindnesses, and of all the truth, which you have shown to your ibad (servant); for with just my maqal (staff) I passed over this Yaradan; and now I have become shanayam (two) machanah (companies).
Please natzal (deliver) me from the yad (hand) of my ach (brother), from the yad (hand) of Ishaw: for I yaraa (fear) him, lest he bawaa (come) and strike me, and the am (mothers) with the children.
You said, ‘I will yatab (surely) do you yatab (good), and shawam (make) your zarai (seed) as the sand of the yam (sea), which can't be numbered because there are so many.'
He lodged there that layal (night), and took from that which he had with him, a manachah (present) for Ishaw, his ach (brother):
two maah (hundred) female goats and isharayam (twenty) male goats, two maah (hundred) ewes and isharayam (twenty) ayal (rams),
shalawashayam (thirty) milk camels and their ban (colts), arabaiyam (forty) cows, ishar (ten) bulls, isharayam (twenty) female donkeys and ishar (ten) foals.

He delivered them into the yad (hands) of his ibad (servants), every herd by itself, and said to his ibad (servants), "ibar (pass) over panayam (before) me, and shawam (put) a space between herd and herd.

He tzawah (commanded) the raashawan (foremost), saying, "When Ishaw, my ach (brother), meets you, and shaal (asks) you, saying, ‘Whose are you? Where are you going? Whose are these panayam (before) you?'
Then you shall amar (say), ‘They are your ibad (servant), Yaiqab. It is a manachah (present) sent to my Adawan, Ishaw. Behold, he also is achar (behind) us.'
He commanded also the shanay (second), and the shalayashay (third), and all that followed the herds, saying, "This is how you shall dabar (speak) to Ishaw, when you matzaa (find) him.

You shall say, ‘Not only that, but behold, your ibad (servant), Yaiqab, is achar (behind) us.'" For, he said, "I will kapar (appease) him with the manachah (present) that goes panayam (before) me, and afterward I will raah (see) his panayam (face). Perhaps he will nashaa (accept) me.
So the manachah (present) passed over panayam (before) him, and he himself lodged that layal (night) in the machanah (camp).
He rose up that layal (night), and took his shanayam (two) wives, and his shanayam (two) handmaids, and his ishar (eleven) yalad (sons), and passed over the ford of the Yabaq.
He took them, and sent them over the stream, and sent over that which he had.
Yaiqab was yathar (left) abaq (alone), and wrestled with a ayash (man) there until the breaking of the shachar (day).
When he saw that he didn't yakal (prevail) against him, he touched the hollow of his thigh, and the kap (hollow) of Yaiqab thigh was strained, as he wrestled.
The man said, "Let me shalach (go), for the shachar (day) ilah (breaks)." Jacob said, "I won't let you shalach (go), am (unless) you barak (bless) me.
He said to him, "What is your sham (name)?" He said, "Yaiqab.
He said, "Your sham (name) will no longer be called Yaiqab, but Yasharaal (Israel); for you have fought with Alahayam and with men, and have prevailed.
Yaiqab asked him, "Please nagad (tell) me your sham (name)." He said, "Why is it that you shaal (ask) what my sham (name) is?" He blessed him there.
Yaiqab called the sham (name) of the place Panawaal: for, he said, "I have seen Alahayam panayam (face) to panayam (face), and my napash (life) is preserved.
The shamash (sun) rose on him as he passed over Panawaal, and he limped because of his thigh.

Therefore the children of Yasharaal (Israel) don't akal (eat) the sinew of the hip, which is on the kap (hollow) of the thigh, to this yawam (day), because he touched the kap (hollow) of Yaiqab thigh in the sinew of the hip.

Yaiqab lifted up his iyan (eyes), and looked, and, behold, Ishaw was coming, and with him arabai (four) maah (hundred) men. He divided the children between Laah, Rachal, and the shanayam (two) handmaids.
He shawam (put) the handmaids and their children in front, Laah and her children Acharawan, and Rachal and Yawasap Acharawan the rear.
He himself passed over in panayam (front) of them, and bowed himself to the aratz (ground) shabai (seven) paim (times), until he came near to his ach (brother).
Ishaw ran to qaraah (meet) him, embraced him, napal (fell) on his neck, kissed him, and they wept.
He lifted up his iyan (eyes), and saw the women and the children; and said, "Who are these with you?" He said, "The children whom Alahayam has graciously given your ibad (servant).
Then the handmaids came near with their children, and they bowed themselves.
Laah also and her children came near, and bowed themselves. achar (after) them, Yawasap came near with Rachal, and they bowed themselves.
Esau said, "What do you mean by all this machanah (company) which I met?" Jacob said, "To matzaa (find) favor in the iyan (sight) of my Adawan.
Ishaw said, "I have rab (enough), my ach (brother); let that which you have be yours.

Yaiqab said, "Please, no, if I have now found favor in your iyan (sight), then receive my manachah (present) at my yad (hand), because I have seen your panayam (face), as one raah (see) the panayam (face) of Alahayam, and you were pleased with me.
Please take the barakah (gift) that I brought to you, because Alahayam has dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough." He urged him, and he took it.
Esau said, "Let us take our nasai (journey), and let us yalak (go), and I will yalak (go) before you.

Jacob said to him, "My Adawan yadai (knows) that the children are Rak, and that the flocks and herds with me have their young, and if they overdrive them one yawam (day), all the flocks will mawath (die).

Please let my Adawan ibar (pass) over panayam (before) his ibad (servant), and I will lead on gently, ragal (according) to the pace of the livestock that are panayam (before) me and ragal (according) to the pace of the children, until I bawaa (come) to my Adawan to Shaiyar.
Ishaw said, "Let me now leave with you some of the im (folk) who are with me." He said, "mah (why)? Let me matzaa (find) favor in the iyan (sight) of my Adawan.
So Ishaw returned that yawam (day) on his darak (way) to Shaiyar.
Yaiqab traveled to Sakawath, built himself a bayath (house), and made shelters for his livestock. Therefore the sham (name) of the place is called Sakawath.
Yaiqab came Shalam peace to the Iyar of Shakam, which is in the aratz (land) of Kanain, when he came Padan Paddan Aram; and encamped panayam (before) the Iyar.

He bought the chalaqah (parcel) of shadah (ground) where he had natah (spread) his ahal (tent), at the yad (hand) of the children of Chamawar, Shakam ab (father), for one maah (hundred) pieces of money.
He erected an mazabach (altar) there, and called it El Elohe Israel.
Dayanah, the bath (daughter) of Laah, whom she bore to Yaiqab, went out to raah (see) the bath (daughters) of the aratz (land).
Shakam the ban (son) of Chamawar the Chaway (Hivite), the nashayaa (prince) of the aratz (land), saw her. He took her, shakab (lay) with her, and humbled her.
His napash (soul) joined to Dayanah, the bath (daughter) of Yaiqab, and he loved the young lady, and spoke lab (kindly) to the young lady.
Shakam spoke to his ab (father), Chamawar, saying, "Get me this young lady as a ashah (wife).
Now Yaiqab heard that he had defiled Dayanah, his bath (daughter); and his ban (sons) were with his livestock in the shadah (field). Yaiqab held his charash (peace) until they came.
Chamawar the ab (father) of Shakam went out to Yaiqab to dabar (talk) with him.

The ban (sons) of Yaiqab came in from the shadah (field) when they heard it. The men were grieved, and they were very charah (angry), because he had done folly in Yasharaal (Israel) in lying with Yaiqab bath (daughter); a which thing ought not to be done.
Chamawar talked with them, saying, "The napash (soul) of my ban (son), Shakam, chashaq (longs) for your bath (daughter). Please nathan (give) her to him as a ashah (wife).
chathan (make) marriages with us. nathan (give) your bath (daughters) to us, and take our bath (daughters) for yourselves.
You shall yashab (dwell) with us, and the aratz (land) will be panayam (before) you. Live and trade in it, and get achaz (possessions) in it.
Shakam said to her ab (father) and to her ach (brothers), "Let me matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (eyes), and whatever you will amar (tell) me I will nathan (give).
Ask me a maad (great) amount for a dowry, and I will nathan (give) whatever you ask of me, but nathan (give) me the young lady as a ashah (wife).
The ban (sons) of Yaiqab answered Shakam and Chamawar his ab (father) with deceit, and spoke, because he had defiled Dayanah their achawath (sister),
and said to them, "We can't do this thing, to nathan (give) our achawath (sister) to one who is uncircumcised; for that is a reproach to us.
Only on this condition will we consent to you. If you will be as we are, that every zakar (male) of you be circumcised;
then will we nathan (give) our bath (daughters) to you, and we will take your bath (daughters) to us, and we will yashab (dwell) with you, and we will become one im (people).
But if you will not listen to us, to be circumcised, then we will take our sister, and we will be gone.
Their dabar (words) pleased Chamawar and Shakam, Chamawar ban (son).
The nair (young) man didn't wait to do this thing, because he had delight in Yaiqab bath (daughter), and he was honored above all the bayath (house) of his ab (father).
Chamawar and Shakam, his ban (son), came to the gate of their Iyar, and talked with the men of their Iyar, saying,

"These men are Shalam with us. Therefore let them live in the aratz (land) and trade in it. For behold, the aratz (land) is Rachab yad (enough) for them. Let us take their bath (daughters) to us for wives, and let us nathan (give) them our bath (daughters).
Only on this condition will the men consent to us to live with us, to become one im (people), if every zakar (male) among us is circumcised, as they are circumcised.
Won't their livestock and their possessions and all their animals be ours? Only let us give our consent to them, and they will yashab (dwell) with us.
All who went out of the gate of his Iyar listened to Chamawar, and to Shakam his ban (son); and every zakar (male) was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his Iyar.

It happened on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), when they were sore, that shanayam (two) of Yaiqab ban (sons), Shamaiwan and Laway, Dayanah ach (brothers), ayash (each) took his charab (sword), came upon the unsuspecting Iyar, and killed all the zakar (males).
They killed Chamawar and Shakam, his ban (son), with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), and took Dayanah out of Shakam bayath (house), and went yatzaa (away).
Yaiqab ban (sons) came Chalal the dead, and plundered the Iyar, because they had defiled their achawath (sister).
They took their flocks, their herds, their donkeys, that which was in the Iyar, that which was in the shadah (field),
and all their wealth. They took captive all their little ones and their wives, and took as plunder everything that was in the bayath (house).

Yaiqab said to Shamaiwan and Laway, "You have troubled me, to yashab (make) me odious to the inhabitants of the aratz (land), among the Kanainay (Canaanites) and the Parazay (Perizzites). I am few in number. They will asap (gather) themselves together against me and strike me, and I will be destroyed, I and my bayath (house).
They said, "Should he ishah (deal) with our achawath (sister) as with a prostitute?

Alahayam said to Yaiqab, "qawam (arise), ilah (go) up to Bayathaal, and live there. ishah (make) there an mazabach (altar) to Al, who raah (see) to you when you fled from the panayam (face) of Ishaw your ach (brother).
Then Yaiqab said to his bayath (household), and to all who were with him, "sawar (put) away the foreign Alahayam that are among you, tahar (purify) yourselves, change your garments.

Let us qawam (arise), and ilah (go) up to Bayathaal. I will ishah (make) there an mazabach (altar) to Al, who answered me in the yawam (day) of my tzarah (distress), and was with me in the darak (way) which I went.
They gave to Yaiqab all the foreign Alahayam which were in their yad (hands), and the rings which were in their ears; and Yaiqab hid them under the oak which was by Shakam.
They traveled, and a terror of Alahayam was on the Iyar that were around them, and they didn't pursue the ban (sons) of Yaiqab.
So Yaiqab came to Lawaz (that is, Bayathaal), which is in the aratz (land) of Kanain, he and all the im (people) who were with him.
He built an mazabach (altar) there, and called the place El Beth El; because there Alahayam was revealed to him, when he fled from the panayam (face) of his ach (brother).
Dabawarah, Rabaqah nurse, died, and she was buried below Bayathaal under the oak; and its sham (name) was called Alawanabakawath Bacuth.
Alahayam raah (see) to Yaiqab again, when he came from Paddan Padan, and blessed him.
Alahayam said to him, "Your sham (name) is Yaiqab. Your sham (name) shall not be Yaiqab any more, but your sham (name) will be Yasharaal (Israel)." He sham (named) him Yasharaal (Israel).
Alahayam said to him, "I am Al Shaday. Be fruitful and multiply. A gaway (nation) and a qahal (company) of gaway (nations) will be from you, and malak (kings) will yatzaa (come) out of your body.
The aratz (land) which I gave to Abaraham and Yatzachaq, I will nathan (give) it to you, and to your zarai (seed) achar (after) you will I nathan (give) the aratz (land).
Alahayam went up from him in the place where he spoke with him.
Yaiqab natzab (set) up a matzabah (pillar) in the place where he spoke with him, a pillar of aban (stone). He poured out a drink nasak (offering) on it, and poured shaman (oil) on it.
Yaiqab called the sham (name) of the place where Alahayam spoke with him "Bayathaal.
They traveled from Bayathaal. There was still some distance to bawaa (come) to aparath (ephrath), and Rachal travailed. She had hard labor.
When she was in hard labor, the yalad (midwife) said to her, "Don't be yaraa (afraid), for now you will have another ban (son).
It happened, as her napash (soul) was departing (for she died), that she sham (named) him Banaawanay, but his ab (father) sham (named) him Banayamayan.
Rachal died, and was buried in the darak (way) to aparath (ephrath) (the same is Bayathalacham).
Yaiqab natzab (set) up a matzabah (pillar) on her qabawarah (grave). The same is the Pillar of Rachal qabawarah (grave) to this yawam (day).
Yasharaal (Israel) traveled, and natah (spread) his ahal (tent) beyond the magadal (tower) of Magadalaidar.
