It happened, while Yasharaal (Israel) lived in that aratz (land), that Raawaban went and shakab (lay) with Balahah, his ab (father's) concubine, and Yasharaal (Israel) heard of it. Now the ban (sons) of Yaiqab were shanayam (twelve).
The ban (sons) of Laah: Raawaban (Yaiqab firstborn), Shamaiwan, Laway, Yahawadah (Judah), Yashashakar, and Zabawalawan.
The ban (sons) of Rachal: Yawasap and Banayamayan.
The ban (sons) of Balahah (Rachal handmaid): Dan and Napathalay.
The ban (sons) of Zalapah (Laah handmaid): Gad and Ashar. These are the ban (sons) of Yaiqab, who were yalad (born) to him in Paddan Padan.
Yaiqab came to Yatzachaq his ab (father), to Mamaraa, to Kiriath Qarayathaarabai (which is Chabarawan), where Abaraham and Yatzachaq lived as foreigners.
The yawam (days) of Yatzachaq were one maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty) Shanah.
Yatzachaq gave up the spirit, and died, and was gathered to his im (people), zaqan (old) and Shabai of yawam (days). Ishaw and Yaiqab, his ban (sons), buried him.
Now this is the history of the thawaladah (generations) of Ishaw (that is, Adam).

Ishaw took his wives from the bath (daughters) of Kanain: Idah the bath (daughter) of Ayalawan, the Chathay (Hittite); and Ahalayabamah the bath (daughter) of Inah, the bath (daughter) of Tzabaiwan, the Chaway (Hivite);
and Bashamath, Yashamaial bath (daughter), achawath (sister) of Nabayawath.
Idah bore to Ishaw Alayapaz. Bashamath bore Raiwaal.
Ahalayabamah bore Yaiyash, Yailam, and Qarach. These are the ban (sons) of Ishaw, who were yalad (born) to him in the aratz (land) of Kanain.

Ishaw took his wives, his ban (sons), his bath (daughters), and all the members of his bayath (household), with his livestock, all his animals, and all his possessions, which he had gathered in the aratz (land) of Kanain, and went into a aratz (land) away from his ach (brother) Yaiqab.
For their rakawash (substance) was rab (too) great for them to yashab (dwell) together, and the aratz (land) of their travels couldn't nashaa (bear) them panayam (because) of their livestock.
Ishaw lived in the har (hill) country of Shaiyar. Ishaw is Adam.
This is the history of the thawaladah (generations) of Ishaw the ab (father) of the Adam (Edomites) in the har (hill) country of Shaiyar:
these are the sham (names) of Ishaw ban (sons): Alayapaz, the ban (son) of Idah, the ashah (wife) of Ishaw; and Raiwaal, the ban (son) Bashamath Basemath, the ashah (wife) of Ishaw.
The ban (sons) of Alayapaz were Thayaman, Awamar, Tzapaw, and Gaitham, and Qanaz.
Thamanai was concubine to Alayapaz, Ishaw ban (son); and she bore to Alayapaz Imalaq. These are the ban (sons) of Idah, Ishaw ashah (wife).
These are the ban (sons) of Raiwaal: Nachath, Zarach, Shamah, and Mazah. These were the ban (sons) Bashamath Basemath, Ishaw ashah (wife).
These were the ban (sons) Ahalayabamah Oholibamah, the bath (daughter) of Inah, the bath (daughter) of Tzabaiwan, Ishaw ashah (wife): she bore to Ishaw Yaiyash, Yailam, and Qarach.
These are the Alawap of the ban (sons) of Ishaw: the ban (sons) of Alayapaz the firstborn of Ishaw: Alawap Thayaman, Alawap Awamar, Alawap Tzapaw, Alawap Qanaz,
Alawap Qarach, Alawap Gaitham, Alawap Imalaq: these are the Alawap who came of Alayapaz in the aratz (land) of Adam; these are the ban (sons) of Idah.

These are the ban (sons) of Raiwaal, Ishaw ban (son): Alawap Nachath, Alawap Zarach, Alawap Shamah, Alawap Mazah: these are the Alawap who came of Raiwaal in the aratz (land) of Adam; these are the ban (sons) Bashamath Basemath, Ishaw ashah (wife).

These are the ban (sons) Ahalayabamah Oholibamah, Ishaw ashah (wife): Alawap Yaiwash, Alawap Yailam, Alawap Qarach: these are the Alawap who Ahalayabamah of Oholibamah the bath (daughter) of Inah, Ishaw ashah (wife).
These are the ban (sons) of Ishaw (that is, Adam), and these are their Alawap.
These are the ban (sons) of Shaiyar the Charay (Horite), the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land): Lawatan, Shawabal, Tzabaiwan, Inah,
Dayashawan, Atzar, and Dayashan. These are the Alawap who came of the Charay (Horites), the children of Shaiyar in the aratz (land) of Adam.
The children of Lawatan were Charay and Hayamam. Lawatan achawath (sister) was Thamanai.
These are the children of Shawabal: Ilawan, Manachath, Iyabal, Shapaw, and Awanam.
These are the children of Tzabaiwan: Ayah and Inah. This is Inah who found the hot springs in the madabar (wilderness), as he fed the donkeys of Tzabaiwan his ab (father).
These are the children of Inah: Dayashawan and Ahalayabamah, the bath (daughter) of Inah.
These are the children of Dayashawan: Chamadan, Ashaban, Yatharan, and Karan.
These are the children of Atzar: Balahan, Zaiwan, and Iqan.
These are the children of Dayashan: Iwatz and Aran.
These are the Alawap who came of the Charay (Horites): Alawap Lawatan, Alawap Shawabal, Alawap Tzabaiwan, Alawap Inah,
Alawap Dayashawan, Alawap Atzar, and Alawap Dayashan: these are the Alawap who Charay of the Horites, Alawap to their chiefs in the aratz (land) of Shaiyar.
These are the malak (kings) who reigned in the aratz (land) of Adam, panayam (before) any malak (king) reigned over the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
Balai, the ban (son) of Baiwar, reigned in Adam. The sham (name) of his Iyar was Danahabah.
Balai died, and Yawabab, the ban (son) of Zarach of Batzarah, reigned in his place.
Yawabab died, and Chawasham of the aratz (land) of the Thayamanay reigned in his place.
Chawasham died, and Hadad, the ban (son) of Badad, who struck Madayan in the shadah (field) of Mawaab, reigned in his place. The sham (name) of his Iyar was Iwayath.
Hadad died, and Shamalah of Masharaqah reigned in his place.
Shamalah died, and Shaawal of Rachabawath by the nahar (river), reigned in his place.
Shaawal died, and Bailachanan Hanan, the ban (son) of Ikabawar reigned in his place.

Bailachanan Hanan the ban (son) of Ikabawar died, and Hadar reigned in his place. The sham (name) of his Iyar was Paiw. His ashah (wife's) sham (name) was Mahayatabaal, the bath (daughter) of Matarad, the bath (daughter) of Mayazahab.

These are the sham (names) Alawap the chiefs who came from Ishaw, according to their mashapachah (families), after their places, and by their sham (names): Alawap Thamanai, Alawap Ilawah, Alawap Yathath,
Alawap Ahalayabamah, Alawap Alah, Alawap Payanan,
Alawap Qanaz, Alawap Thayaman, Alawap Mabatzar,

Alawap Magadayaal, and Alawap Iyaram. These are the Alawap of Adam, according to their habitations in the aratz (land) of their achazah (possession). This is Ishaw, the ab (father) of the Adam (Edomites).
Yaiqab lived in the aratz (land) of his ab (father's) travels, in the aratz (land) of Kanain.

This is the history of the thawaladah (generations) of Yaiqab. Yawasap, being seventeen Shanah ban (old), was feeding the flock with his ach (brothers). He was a nair (boy) with the ban (sons) of Balahah and Zalapah, his ab (father's) wives. Yawasap brought an rai (evil) dabah (report) of them to their ab (father).
Now Yasharaal (Israel) loved Yawasap more than all his children, because he was the ban (son) of his old age, and he made him a coat of many colors.
His ach (brothers) saw that their ab (father) loved him more than all his ach (brothers), and they hated him, and couldn't dabar (speak) peaceably to him.
Yawasap dreamed a chalawam (dream), and he told it to his ach (brothers), and they hated him all the more.
He said to them, "Please hear this chalawam (dream) which I have dreamed:
for behold, we were binding sheaves in the shadah (field), and behold, my sheaf qawam (arose) and also stood natzab (upright); and behold, your sheaves came around, and bowed down to my sheaf.

His ach (brothers) said to him, "Will you malak (indeed) malak (reign) over us? Or will you mashal (indeed) have mashal (dominion) over us?" They hated him all the more for his chalawam (dreams) and for his dabar (words).

He dreamed yet achar (another) chalawam (dream), and told it to his ach (brothers), and said, "Behold, I have dreamed yet another chalawam (dream): and behold, the shamash (sun) and the yarach (moon) and ishar (eleven) kawakab (stars) bowed down to me.

He told it to his ab (father) and to his ach (brothers). His ab (father) rebuked him, and said to him, "What is this chalawam (dream) that you have dreamed? Will I and your am (mother) and your ach (brothers) bawaa (indeed) bawaa (come) to shachah (bow) ourselves down to you to the aratz (earth)?
His ach (brothers) envied him, but his ab (father) kept this dabar (saying) in mind.
His ach (brothers) went to raih (feed) their ab (father's) flock in Shakam.
Yasharaal (Israel) said to Yawasap, "Aren't your ach (brothers) feeding the flock in Shakam? yalak (come), and I will shalach (send) you to them." He said to him, "Here I am.

He said to him, "yalak (go) now, raah (see) whether it is shalawam (well) with your ach (brothers), and shalawam (well) with the flock; and shawab (turn back / repent) me dabar (word) again." So he sent him out of the valley of Chabarawan, and he came to Shakam.
A certain ayash (man) found him, and behold, he was wandering in the shadah (field). The ayash (man) asked him, "What are you looking for?
He said, "I am looking for my ach (brothers). nagad (tell) me, please, where they are feeding the flock.
The ayash (man) said, "They have left here, for I heard them amar (say), ‘Let us yalak (go) to Dathan.'" Yawasap went achar (after) his ach (brothers), and found them in Dathan.
They saw him Rachawaq off, and before he came qarab (near) to them, they conspired against him to mawath (kill) him.
They said one to ach (another), "Behold, this bail (dreamer) bawaa (comes).

yalak (come) now therefore, and let's harag (kill) him, and cast him into one of the bawar (pits), and we will amar (say), ‘An rai (evil) animal has devoured him.' We will raah (see) what will become of his chalawam (dreams).
Raawaban heard it, and delivered him out of their hand, and said, "Let's not take his nakah (life).

Raawaban said to them, "Shed no dam (blood). Throw him into this bawar (pit) that is in the madabar (wilderness), but shalach (lay) no yad (hand) on him"—that he might natzal (deliver) him out of their yad (hand), to shawab (turn back / repent) him to his ab (father).
It happened, when Joseph came to his brothers, that they stripped Joseph of his coat, the coat of many colors that was on him;
and they took him, and threw him into the bawar (pit). The bawar (pit) was rayaq (empty). There was no mayam (water) in it.

They sat down to akal (eat) lacham (bread), and they lifted up their iyan (eyes) and looked, and saw a caravan of Yashamaialay (Ishmaelites) was coming from Galaid, with their camels bearing spices and balm and myrrh, going to yarad (carry) it down to Matzarayam.
Yahawadah (Judah) said to his ach (brothers), "What profit is it if we harag (kill) our ach (brother) and conceal his dam (blood)?
yalak (come), and let's sell him to the Yashamaialay (Ishmaelites), and not let our yad (hand) be on him; for he is our ach (brother), our flesh." His ach (brothers) listened to him.

Madayanay (Midianites) who were merchants passed by, and they drew and lifted up Yawasap out of the bawar (pit), and sold Yawasap to the Yashamaialay (Ishmaelites) for isharayam (twenty) pieces of kasap (silver). They brought Yawasap into Matzarayam.
Raawaban returned to the bawar (pit); and saw that Yawasap wasn't in the bawar (pit); and he tore his clothes.
He returned to his ach (brothers), and said, "The yalad (child) is no more; and I, where will I bawaa (go)?
They took Yawasap coat, and killed a Shaiyar goat, and dipped the coat in the dam (blood).
They took the coat of many colors, and they brought it to their ab (father), and said, "We have found this. Examine it, now, whether it is your ban (son's) coat or not.
He recognized it, and said, "It is my ban (son's) coat. An rai (evil) animal has devoured him. Yawasap is without doubt torn in pieces.
Yaiqab tore his clothes, and shawam (put) sackcloth on his waist, and mourned for his ban (son) many yawam (days).

All his ban (sons) and all his bath (daughters) rose up to nacham (comfort) him, but he refused to be comforted. He said, "For I will yarad (go) down to shaawal (sheol) to my ban (son) Abal." His ab (father) wept for him.
The Madanay (Midianites) sold him into Matzarayam to Pawatayapar, an officer of Paraih, the shar (captain) of the guard.
It happened at that ith (time), that Yahawadah (Judah) went down from his ach (brothers), and visited a ayash (certain) Idalamay, whose sham (name) was Chayarah.
Yahawadah (Judah) saw there a bath (daughter) of a ayash (certain) Kanainay (Canaanite) whose sham (name) was Shawai. He took her, and went in to her.
She conceived, and bore a ban (son); and he sham (named) him Ir.
She conceived again, and bore a ban (son); and she sham (named) him Awanan.
She yet again bore a ban (son), and sham (named) him Shalah: and he was at Kazayab, when she bore him.
Yahawadah (Judah) took a ashah (wife) for Ir, his firstborn, and her sham (name) was Thamar.
Ir, Yahawadah firstborn, was rai (wicked) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah. Yahawah killed him.

Yahawadah (Judah) said to Awanan, "bawaa (go) in to your ach (brother's) ashah (wife), and perform the duty of a husband's ach (brother) to her, and qawam (raise) up zarai (seed) to your ach (brother).

Awanan knew that the zarai (seed) wouldn't be his; and it happened, when he went in to his ach (brother's) ashah (wife), that he spilled it on the aratz (ground), balathay (lest) he should nathan (give) zarai (seed) to his ach (brother).
The thing which he did was evil in the sight of Yahawah, and he killed him also.

Then Yahawadah (Judah) said to Thamar, his kalah (daughter-in-law), "yashab (remain) a alamanah (widow) in your ab (father's) bayath (house), until Shalah, my ban (son), is grown up;" for he said, "Lest he also mawath (die), like his ach (brothers)." Thamar went and lived in her ab (father's) bayath (house).

After many yawam (days), Shawai bath (daughter), the ashah (wife) of Yahawadah (Judah), died. Yahawadah (Judah) was comforted, and went up to his sheepshearers to Thamanah, he and his rai (friend) Chayarah, the Idalamay.
It was told Thamar, saying, "Behold, your father-in-law is going up to Thamanah to shear his sheep.

She took off of her the bagad (garments) of her widowhood, and covered herself with her tzaiyap (veil), and wrapped herself, and sat in the gate of Enaim, which is by the darak (way) to Thamanah; for she saw that Shalah was grown up, and she wasn't given to him as a ashah (wife).
When Yahawadah (Judah) saw her, he thought that she was a prostitute, for she had covered her panayam (face).

He turned to her by the darak (way), and said, "Please come, let me bawaa (come) in to you," for he didn't yadai (know) that she was his kalah (daughter-in-law). She said, "What will you nathan (give) me, that you may bawaa (come) in to me?
He said, "I will shalach (send) you a young goat from the flock." She said, "Will you nathan (give) me a pledge, until you shalach (send) it?

He said, "What pledge will I nathan (give) you?" She said, "Your signet and your cord, and your matah (staff) that is in your yad (hand)." He gave them to her, and came in to her, and she conceived by him.
She qawam (arose), and went yalak (away), and sawar (put) off her tzaiyap (veil) from her, and Labash on the bagad (garments) of her widowhood.
Yahawadah (Judah) sent the young goat by the yad (hand) of his rai (friend), the Idalamay, to receive the pledge from the ashah (woman's) yad (hand), but he didn't matzaa (find) her.
Then he asked the men of her place, saying, "Qadashah is the prostitute, that was at Enaim by the road?" They said, "Qadashah has been no prostitute here.
He returned to Yahawadah (Judah), and said, "I haven't found her; and also the men of the place said, ‘Qadashah has been no prostitute here.'
Yahawadah (Judah) said, "Let her keep it, lest we be shamed. Behold, I sent this young goat, and you haven't found her.

It happened about shalawash (three) chadash (months) later, that it was told Yahawadah (Judah), saying, "Thamar, your kalah (daughter-in-law), has played the prostitute; and moreover, behold, she is with harah (child) by prostitution." Yahawadah (Judah) said, "yatzaa (bring) her out, and let her be burnt.

When she was brought out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, "By the ayash (man), whose these are, I am with harah (child)." She also said, "Please nakar (discern) whose are these—the signet, and the cords, and the matah (staff).
Yahawadah (Judah) acknowledged them, and said, "She is more tzadaq (righteous) than I, because I didn't nathan (give) her to Shalah, my ban (son)." He knew her again no more.
It happened in the ith (time) of her yalad (travail), that behold, twins were in her womb.
When she travailed, one nathan (put) out a yad (hand), and the yalad (midwife) took and tied a scarlet thread on his yad (hand), saying, "This came out raashawan (first).

It happened, as he drew shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand), that behold, his ach (brother) came out, and she said, "Why have you made a breach for yourself?" Therefore his sham (name) was called Paratz.
Afterward his ach (brother) came out, that had the scarlet thread on his yad (hand), and his sham (name) was called Zarach.

Yawasap was brought down to Matzarayam. Pawatayapar, an officer of Paraih, the shar (captain) of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him from the yad (hand) of the Yashamaialay (Ishmaelites) that had brought him down there.
Yahawah was with Yawasap, and he was a prosperous ayash (man). He was in the bayath (house) of his adawan (master) the Matzaray (Egyptian).
His adawan (master) saw that Yahawah was with him, and that Yahawah made all that he did tzalach (prosper) in his yad (hand).
Yawasap found favor in his iyan (sight). He ministered to him, and he made him paqad (overseer) over his bayath (house), and all that he had he nathan (put) into his yad (hand).

It happened from the time that he made him paqad (overseer) in his bayath (house), and over all that he had, that Yahawah blessed the Matzaray bayath (house) for Yawasap sake; and the barakah (blessing) of Yahawah was on all that he had, in the bayath (house) and in the shadah (field).
He left all that he had in Yawasap yad (hand). He didn't concern himself with anything, am (except) for the lacham (food) which he ate. Yawasap was well-built and handsome.
It happened achar (after) these things, that his adawan (master's) ashah (wife) nashaa (cast) her iyan (eyes) on Yawasap; and she said, "shakab (lie) with me.

But he refused, and said to his adawan (master's) ashah (wife), "Behold, my adawan (master) doesn't yadai (know) what is with me in the bayath (house), and he has nathan (put) all that he has into my yad (hand).

He isn't greater in this bayath (house) than I, laa (neither) has he kept back anything from me but you, because you are his ashah (wife). How then can I do this gadawal (great) wickedness, and chataa (sin) against Alahayam?
As she spoke to Yawasap yawam (day) by yawam (day), he didn't listen to her, to shakab (lie) by her, or to be with her.
About this yawam (time), he went into the bayath (house) to do his malaakah (work), and there were ayash (none) of the men of the bayath (house) inside.
She caught him by his bagad (garment), saying, "shakab (lie) with me!" He left his bagad (garment) in her yad (hand), and ran outside.
When she saw that he had left his bagad (garment) in her yad (hand), and had run outside,

she called to the men of her bayath (house), and spoke to them, saying, "raah (see), he has brought in a Hebrew to us to mock us. He came in to me to shakab (lie) with me, and I cried with a gadawal (loud) qawal (voice).
It happened, when he heard that I lifted up my qawal (voice) and cried, that he left his bagad (garment) by me, and ran outside.
She laid up his bagad (garment) by her, until his adawan (master) came bayath (home).
She spoke to him according to these dabar (words), saying, "The ibaray (hebrew) ibad (servant), whom you have brought to us, came in to me to mock me,
and it happened, as I lifted up my qawal (voice) and cried, that he left his bagad (garment) by me, and ran outside.

It happened, when his adawan (master) heard the dabar (words) of his ashah (wife), which she spoke to him, saying, "This is dabar (what) your ibad (servant) did to me," that his ap (wrath) was kindled.
Joseph's adawan (master) took him, and put him into the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were bound, and he was there in custody.
But Yahawah was with Yawasap, and showed chasad (kindness) to him, and gave him favor in the iyan (sight) of the shar (keeper) of the bayath (prison).
The shar (keeper) of the bayath (prison) committed to Yawasap yad (hand) all the prisoners who were in the bayath (prison). Whatever they did there, he was responsible for it.
The shar (keeper) of the bayath (prison) didn't look after anything that was under his yad (hand), because Yahawah was with him; and that which he did, Yahawah made it tzalach (prosper).
It happened achar (after) these things, that the butler of the malak (king) of Matzarayam and his baker offended their Adawan, the malak (king) of Matzarayam.
Paraih was qatzap (angry) with his shanayam (two) officers, the shar (chief) cupbearer and the shar (chief) baker.
He nathan (put) them in custody in the bayath (house) of the shar (captain) of the guard, into the bayath (prison), the place where Yawasap was bound.
The shar (captain) of the guard assigned them to Yawasap, and he took care of them. They stayed in prison many yawam (days).

They shanayam (both) dreamed a chalawam (dream), each ayash (man) his chalawam (dream), in one layal (night), each ayash (man) according to the interpretation of his chalawam (dream), the cupbearer and the baker of the malak (king) of Matzarayam, who were bound in the bayath (prison).
Yawasap came in to them in the baqar (morning), and saw them, and saw that they were sad.
He asked Paraih officers who were with him in custody in his adawan (master's) bayath (house), saying, "Why do you panayam (look) so rai (sad) today?
They said to him, "We have dreamed a chalawam (dream), and there is no pathar (one) who can interpret it." Yawasap said to them, "Don't interpretations belong to Alahayam? Please tell it to me.
The shar (chief) cupbearer told his chalawam (dream) to Yawasap, and said to him, "In my chalawam (dream), behold, a vine was in panayam (front) of me,
and in the vine were shalawash (three) branches. It was as though it budded, it blossomed, and its clusters produced ripe inab (grapes).
Paraih cup was in my yad (hand); and I took the inab (grapes), and pressed them into Paraih cup, and I gave the cup into Paraih kap (hand).
Yawasap said to him, "This is its interpretation: the shalawash (three) branches are shalawash (three) yawam (days).

Within shalawash (three) more yawam (days), Paraih will nashaa (lift) up your raash (head), and shawab (turn back / repent) you to your kan (office). You will nathan (give) Paraih cup into his yad (hand), the way you did when you were his cupbearer.
But zakar (remember) me when it will be yatab (well) with you, and please show chasad (kindness) to me, and zakar (make) mention of me to Paraih, and yatzaa (bring) me out of this bayath (house).
For indeed, I was stolen away out of the aratz (land) of the ibaray (hebrews), and here also have I done nothing that they should shawam (put) me into the bawar (dungeon).

When the shar (chief) baker saw that the interpretation was tawab (good), he said to Yawasap, "I also was in my chalawam (dream), and behold, shalawash (three) baskets of white bread were on my raash (head).
In the Ilayawan basket there was all kinds of baked food for Paraih, and the birds ate them out of the basket on my raash (head).
Yawasap answered, "This is its interpretation. The shalawash (three) baskets are shalawash (three) yawam (days).
Within shalawash (three) more yawam (days), Paraih will nashaa (lift) up your raash (head) from off you, and will hang you on a itz (tree); and the birds will akal (eat) your flesh from off you.

It happened the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), which was Paraih birthday, that he made a feast for all his ibad (servants), and he lifted up the raash (head) of the shar (chief) cupbearer and the head of the shar (chief) baker among his ibad (servants).
He restored the shar (chief) cupbearer to his position again, and he gave the cup into Paraih kap (hand);
but he hanged the shar (chief) baker, as Yawasap had interpreted to them.
Yet the shar (chief) cupbearer didn't zakar (remember) Yawasap, but forgot him.
It happened at the end of chawal (two) full years, that Pharaoh dreamed: and behold, he stood by the sapar (river).
Behold, there came up out of the yaar (river) shabai (seven) cattle, Yapah and Barayaa, and they fed in the marsh grass.
Behold, shabai (seven) other cattle came up achar (after) them out of the yaar (river), ugly and Daq, and stood by the other cattle on the shapah (brink) of the yaar (river).
The ugly and Daq cattle ate up the shabai (seven) Yapah and Barayaa cattle. So Paraih awoke.
He slept and dreamed a shanay (second) time: and behold, shabai (seven) shabal (heads) of grain came up on one stalk, Barayaa and tawab (good).
Behold, shabai (seven) shabal (heads) of grain, Daq and blasted with the east qadayam (wind), sprung up achar (after) them.
The Daq shabal (heads) of grain swallowed up the shabai (seven) Barayaa and Malaa ears. Paraih awoke, and behold, it was a chalawam (dream).

It happened in the baqar (morning) that his rawach (spirit) was troubled, and he sent and called for all of Matzarayam magicians and chakam (wise) men. Paraih told them his chalawam (dreams), but there was no pathar (one) who could interpret them to Paraih.
Then the shar (chief) cupbearer spoke to Paraih, saying, "I zakar (remember) my chataa (faults) today.
Paraih was qatzap (angry) with his ibad (servants), and nathan (put) me in custody in the bayath (house) of the shar (captain) of the guard, me and the shar (chief) baker.
We dreamed a chalawam (dream) in one layal (night), I and he. We dreamed each ayash (man) according to the interpretation of his chalawam (dream).

There was with us there a nair (young) man, a ibaray (hebrew), ibad (servant) to the shar (captain) of the guard, and we told him, and he interpreted to us our chalawam (dreams). To each ayash (man) according to his chalawam (dream) he interpreted.
It happened, as he interpreted to us, so it was: he restored me to my kan (office), and he hanged him.
Then Paraih sent and called Yawasap, and they brought him hastily out of the bawar (dungeon). He shaved himself, changed his clothing, and came in to Paraih.
Paraih said to Yawasap, "I have dreamed a chalawam (dream), and there is no pathar (one) who can interpret it. I have heard it said of you, that when you hear a chalawam (dream) you can interpret it.
Yawasap answered Paraih, saying, "It isn't in me. Alahayam will give Paraih an answer of shalawam (peace).
Paraih spoke to Yawasap, "In my chalawam (dream), behold, I stood on the shapah (brink) of the yaar (river):
and behold, there came up out of the yaar (river) shabai (seven) cattle, Barayaa and sleek. They fed in the marsh grass,
and behold, shabai (seven) other cattle came up achar (after) them, Dalah and very ugly and Raq, such as I laa (never) saw in all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam for ugliness.
The Raq and ugly cattle ate up the raashawan (first) shabai (seven) Barayaa cattle,
and when they had eaten them up, it couldn't be yadai (known) that they had eaten them, but they were still ugly, as at the thachalah (beginning). So I awoke.
I saw in my chalawam (dream), and behold, shabai (seven) shabal (heads) of grain came up on one stalk, Malaa and tawab (good):
and behold, shabai (seven) shabal (heads) of grain, withered, Daq, and blasted with the east qadayam (wind), sprung up achar (after) them.
The Daq shabal (heads) of grain swallowed up the shabai (seven) tawab (good) shabal (heads) of grain. I told it to the magicians, but there was no one who could explain it to me.
Yawasap said to Paraih, "The chalawam (dream) of Paraih is one. What Alahayam is ishah (about) to do he has declared to Paraih.
The shabai (seven) tawab (good) cattle are shabai (seven) Shanah; and the shabai (seven) tawab (good) shabal (heads) of grain are shabai (seven) Shanah. The chalawam (dream) is one.

The shabai (seven) Raq and ugly cattle that came up achar (after) them are shabai (seven) Shanah, and also the shabai (seven) rayaq (empty) shabal (heads) of grain blasted with the east qadayam (wind); they will be shabai (seven) Shanah of famine.
That is the thing which I spoke to Paraih. What Alahayam is ishah (about) to do he has shown to Paraih.
Behold, there bawaa (come) shabai (seven) Shanah of gadawal (great) plenty throughout all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
There will qawam (arise) achar (after) them shabai (seven) Shanah of famine, and all the plenty will be forgotten in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam. The famine will kalah (consume) the aratz (land),
and the plenty will not be yadai (known) in the aratz (land) by panayam (reason) of that famine which achar (follows); for it will be very Kabad.
The chalawam (dream) was doubled to Paraih, dabar (because) the thing is established by Alahayam, and Alahayam will shortly ishah (bring) it to pass.
"Now therefore let Paraih raah (see) for a discreet and chakam (wise) ayash (man), and shayath (set) him over the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
Let Paraih do this, and let him paqad (appoint) overseers over the aratz (land), and take up the chamash (fifth) part of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam produce in the shabai (seven) plenteous Shanah.
Let them gather all the food of these tawab (good) Shanah that bawaa (come), and lay up grain under the yad (hand) of Paraih for food in the Iyar, and let them shamar (keep) it.

The food will be for a store to the aratz (land) against the shabai (seven) Shanah of famine, which will be in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam; that the aratz (land) not karath (perish) through the famine.
The thing was yatab (good) in the iyan (eyes) of Paraih, and in the iyan (eyes) of all his ibad (servants).
Paraih said to his ibad (servants), "Can we matzaa (find) such a one as this, a ayash (man) in whom is the rawach (spirit) of Alahayam?
Paraih said to Yawasap, "Because Alahayam has shown you all of this, there is none so discreet and chakam (wise) as you.
You shall be over my bayath (house), and according to your pah (word) will all my im (people) be ruled. Only in the kasaa (throne) I will be greater than you.
Paraih said to Yawasap, "raah (see), I have nathan (set) you over all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
Paraih took off his signet ring from his yad (hand), and nathan (put) it on Yawasap yad (hand), and arrayed him in bagad (robes) of Shash linen, and shawam (put) a gold chain about his neck,
and he made him to ride in the mashanah (second) chariot which he had. They cried panayam (before) him, "Bow the knee!" He set him over all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
Paraih said to Yawasap, "I am Paraih, and balaiday (without) you shall no ayash (man) lift up his yad (hand) or his ragal (foot) in all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.

Paraih called Yawasap sham (name) Tzapanathapainach; and he gave him Asanath, the bath (daughter) Pawatayaparai Potiphera kahan (priest) Awan On as a ashah (wife). Yawasap went out over the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.

Yawasap was shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah ban (old) when he stood panayam (before) Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam. Yawasap went out from the panayam (presence) of Paraih, and went throughout all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
In the shabai (seven) plenteous Shanah the aratz (earth) produced abundantly.

He gathered up all the food of the shabai (seven) Shanah which were in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and laid up the food in the Iyar: the food of the shadah (field), which was around every Iyar, he laid up in the same.
Yawasap laid up grain as the sand of the yam (sea), very much, until he stopped counting, for it was without number.
To Yawasap were yalad (born) shanayam (two) ban (sons) before the Shanah of famine came, whom Asanath, the bath (daughter) Pawatayaparai Potiphera kahan (priest) Awan On, bore to him.
Yawasap called the sham (name) of the firstborn Manashah, "For," he said, "Alahayam has made me forget all my imal (toil), and all my ab (father's) bayath (house).
The sham (name) of the shanay (second), he called Aparayam: "For Alahayam has made me fruitful in the aratz (land) of my affliction.
The shabai (seven) Shanah of plenty, that were in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, came to an kalah (end).
The shabai (seven) Shanah of famine began to bawaa (come), just as Yawasap had said. There was famine in all aratz (lands), but in all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam there was lacham (bread).

When all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam was famished, the im (people) cried to Paraih for lacham (bread), and Paraih said to all the Matzarayam (Egyptians), "yalak (go) to Yawasap. What he amar (says) to you, do.

The famine was over all the surface of the aratz (earth). Yawasap opened all the store shabar (houses), and sold to the Matzarayam (Egyptians). The famine was severe in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
All aratz (countries) came into Matzarayam, to Yawasap, to buy grain, because the famine was severe in all the aratz (earth).
Now Yaiqab saw that there was grain in Matzarayam, and Yaiqab said to his ban (sons), "Why do you raah (see) at one another?
He said, "Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Matzarayam. yarad (go) down there, and buy for us from there, so that we may chayah (live), and not mawath (die).
Yawasap ishar (ten) ach (brothers) went down to buy grain from Matzarayam.
But Yaiqab didn't shalach (send) Banayamayan, Yawasap ach (brother), with his ach (brothers); for he said, "Lest perhaps harm happen to him.
The ban (sons) of Yasharaal (Israel) came to buy among those who came, for the famine was in the aratz (land) of Kanain.

Yawasap was the shalayat (governor) over the aratz (land). It was he who sold to all the im (people) of the aratz (land). Yawasap ach (brothers) came, and bowed themselves down to him with their ap (faces) to the aratz (earth)

Yawasap saw his ach (brothers), and he recognized them, but acted like a stranger to them, and spoke Qashah with them. He said to them, "Where did you bawaa (come) from?" They said, "From the aratz (land) of Kanain to buy food.
Yawasap recognized his ach (brothers), but they didn't recognize him.
Yawasap zakar (remembered) the chalawam (dreams) which he dreamed about them, and said to them, "You are spies! You have bawaa (come) to raah (see) the irawah (nakedness) of the aratz (land).
They said to him, "No, my Adawan, but your ibad (servants) have bawaa (come) to buy food.
We are all one ayash (man's) ban (sons); we are Kan men. Your ibad (servants) are not spies.
He said to them, "No, but you have bawaa (come) to raah (see) the irawah (nakedness) of the aratz (land)!

They said, "We, your ibad (servants), are shanayam (twelve) ach (brothers), the ban (sons) of one ayash (man) in the aratz (land) of Kanain; and behold, the youngest is this yawam (day) with our ab (father), and one is no more.
Yawasap said to them, "It is like I told you, saying, ‘You are spies!'
By this you shall be tested. By the chay (life) of Paraih, you shall not yatzaa (go) out from here, unless your youngest ach (brother) bawaa (comes) here.

shalach (send) one of you, and let him get your ach (brother), and you shall be bound, that your dabar (words) may be tested, whether there is truth in you, or laa (else) by the chay (life) of Paraih surely you are spies.
He asap (put) them all together into custody for shalawash (three) yawam (days).
Yawasap said to them the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), "Do this, and chayah (live), for I yaraa (fear) Alahayam.
If you are Kan men, then let one of your ach (brothers) be bound in your prison; but you yalak (go), bawaa (carry) grain for the famine of your bayath (houses).
bawaa (bring) your youngest ach (brother) to me; so will your dabar (words) be aman (verified), and you won't mawath (die)." They did so.

They said one to ach (another), "We are certainly Asham concerning our ach (brother), in that we saw the tzarah (distress) of his napash (soul), when he begged us, and we wouldn't listen. Therefore this tzarah (distress) has bawaa (come) upon us.
Raawaban answered them, saying, "Didn't I amar (tell) you, saying, ‘Don't chataa (sin) against the yalad (child),' and you wouldn't listen? Therefore also, behold, his dam (blood) is required.
They didn't yadai (know) that Yawasap understood them; for there was an Lawatz between them.
He turned himself sabab (away) from them, and wept. Then he returned to them, and spoke to them, and took Shamaiwan from among them, and bound him before their iyan (eyes).

Then Yawasap gave a tzawah (command) to malaa (fill) their bags with grain, and to shawab (turn back / repent) each ayash (man's) kasap (money) into his sack, and to nathan (give) them food for the darak (way). So it was done to them.
They loaded their donkeys with their grain, and departed from there.
As one of them opened his sack to nathan (give) his donkey food in the lodging place, he saw his kasap (money). Behold, it was in the pah (mouth) of his sack.

He said to his ach (brothers), "My kasap (money) is restored! Behold, it is in my sack!" Their lab (hearts) failed them, and they turned trembling one to ach (another), saying, "What is this that Alahayam has done to us?
They came to Yaiqab their ab (father), to the aratz (land) of Kanain, and told him all that had happened to them, saying,
"The ayash (man), the Adawan of the aratz (land), spoke Qashah with us, and took us for spies of the aratz (country).
We said Kan him, ‘We are honest men. We are no spies.
We are ishar (twelve) ach (brothers), ban (sons) of our ab (father); one is no more, and the youngest is this yawam (day) with our ab (father) in the aratz (land) of Kanain.'

The ayash (man), the Adawan of the aratz (land), said to us, ‘By this I will yadai (know) that you are Kan men: yanach (leave) one of your ach (brothers) with me, and take grain for the famine of your bayath (houses), and go your yalak (way).

bawaa (bring) your youngest ach (brother) to me. Then I will yadai (know) that you are not spies, Kan that you are honest men. So I will nathan (deliver) your ach (brother) to you, and you shall trade in the aratz (land).'

It happened as they emptied their sacks, that behold, each ayash (man's) tzarawar (bundle) of kasap (money) was in his sack. When they and their ab (father) saw their tzarawar (bundles) of kasap (money), they were yaraa (afraid).
Yaiqab, their ab (father), said to them, "You have bereaved me of my sons Yawasap is no more, Shamaiwan is no more, and you want to take Banayamayan away. All these things are against me.

Raawaban spoke to his ab (father), saying, "mawath (kill) my shanayam (two) ban (sons), if I don't bawaa (bring) him to you. Entrust him to my care, and I will shawab (turn back / repent) him to you again.

He said, "My ban (son) shall not yarad (go) down with you; for his ach (brother) is mawath (dead), and he only is shaar (left). If harm happens to him along the darak (way) in which you yalak (go), then you will yarad (bring) down my shayabah (gray) hairs with sorrow to shaawal (sheol).
The famine was severe in the land.
It happened, when they had eaten up the grain which they had brought out of Matzarayam, their ab (father) said to them, "shawab (turn back / repent) again, buy us a Mait more food.
Yahawadah (Judah) spoke to him, saying, "The ayash (man) iwad (solemnly) warned us, saying, ‘You shall not raah (see) my panayam (face), unless your ach (brother) is with you.'
If you'll shalach (send) our ach (brother) with us, we'll yarad (go) down and buy you food,
but if you'll not shalach (send) him, we'll not yarad (go) down, for the ayash (man) said to us, ‘You shall not raah (see) my panayam (face), unless your ach (brother) is with you.'
Yasharaal (Israel) said, "Why did you treat me so badly, telling the ayash (man) that you had another ach (brother)?

They said, "The ayash (man) asked directly concerning ourselves, and concerning our relatives, saying, ‘Is your ab (father) still chay (alive)? Have you another ach (brother)?' We just answered his dabar (questions). Is there any way we could yadai (know) that he would amar (say), ‘yarad (bring) your ach (brother) down?'

Yahawadah (Judah) said to Yasharaal (Israel), his ab (father), "shalach (send) the nair (boy) with me, and we'll qawam (get) up and yalak (go), so that we may chayah (live), and not mawath (die), both we, and you, and also our little ones.
I'll be collateral for him. From my yad (hand) will you require him. If I don't bawaa (bring) him to you, and set him panayam (before) you, then let me chataa (bear) the blame forever,
for if we hadn't delayed, shawab (turn back / repent) we would have returned a paim (second) time by now.

Their ab (father), Yasharaal (Israel), said to them, "If it must be so, then do this. Take from the choice fruits of the aratz (land) in your bags, and yarad (carry) down a manachah (present) for the ayash (man), a Mait balm, a Mait honey, spices and myrrh, nuts, and almonds;
and take mashanah (double) kasap (money) in your yad (hand), and shawab (turn back / repent) back the kasap (money) that was returned in the pah (mouth) of your sacks. Perhaps it was an oversight.
Take your ach (brother) also, qawam (get) up, and shawab (turn back / repent) to the ayash (man).

May Al Shaday nathan (give) you racham (mercy) panayam (before) the ayash (man), that he may release to you your other ach (brother) and Banayamayan. If I am bereaved of my shakal (children), I am bereaved.
The men took that manachah (present), and they took mashanah (double) kasap (money) in their yad (hand), and Banayamayan; and got up, went down to Matzarayam, and stood panayam (before) Yawasap.

When Yawasap saw Banayamayan with them, he said to the steward of his bayath (house), "bawaa (bring) the men into the bayath (house), and butcher an animal, and kawan (prepare); for the men will akal (dine) with me at tzahar (noon).
The ayash (man) did as Yawasap commanded, and the ayash (man) brought the men to Yawasap bayath (house).

The men were yaraa (afraid), because they were brought to Yawasap bayath (house); and they said, "dabar (because) of the kasap (money) that was returned in our sacks at the thachalah (first) time, we're brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, attack us, and seize us as ibad (slaves), along with our donkeys.
They came near to the ayash (steward) of Yawasap bayath (house), and they spoke to him at the door of the bayath (house),
and said, "Oh, my Adawan, we yarad (indeed) came down the thachalah (first) time to buy food.

When we came to the lodging place, we opened our sacks, and behold, each ayash (man's) kasap (money) was in the pah (mouth) of his sack, our kasap (money) in full weight. We have brought it shawab (turn back / repent) in our yad (hand).
We have brought down other kasap (money) in our yad (hand) to buy food. We don't yadai (know) who shawam (put) our kasap (money) in our sacks.

He said, "shalawam (peace) be to you. Don't be yaraa (afraid). Your Alahayam, and the Alahayam of your ab (father), has given you treasure in your sacks. I received your kasap (money)." He brought Shamaiwan out to them.
The ayash (man) brought the men into Yawasap bayath (house), and gave them mayam (water), and they washed their feet. He gave their donkeys fodder.
They prepared the manachah (present) for Yawasap coming at tzahar (noon), for they heard that they should akal (eat) lacham (bread) there.
When Yawasap came bayath (home), they brought him the manachah (present) which was in their yad (hand) into the bayath (house), and bowed themselves down to him to the aratz (earth).
He asked them of their shalawam (welfare), and said, "Is your ab (father) shalawam (well), the old zaqan (man) of whom you spoke? Is he yet chay (alive)?
They said, "Your ibad (servant), our ab (father), is shalawam (well). He is still chay (alive)." They bowed down shachah (humbly).

He lifted up his iyan (eyes), and saw Banayamayan, his ach (brother), his am (mother's) ban (son), and said, "Is this your youngest ach (brother), of whom you spoke to me?" He said, "Alahayam be gracious to you, my ban (son).
Yawasap hurried, for his heart yearned over his ach (brother); and he sought a place to weep. He entered into his room, and wept there.
He washed his panayam (face), and came out. He controlled himself, and said, "Serve the meal.

They served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Matzaray (Egyptians), that ate with him, by themselves, because the Matzaray (Egyptians) don't akal (eat) lacham (bread) with the ibaray (hebrews), for that is an thawaibah (abomination) to the Matzarayam (Egyptians).
They sat panayam (before) him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the Tzaiyar according to his youth, and the men marveled one with rai (another).
He sent portions to them from panayam (before) him, but Banayamayan portion was chamash (five) yad (times) as much as any of theirs. They drank, and were Shakar with him.

He tzawah (commanded) the steward of his bayath (house), saying, "malaa (fill) the men's sacks with food, as much as they can nashaa (carry), and shawam (put) each ayash (man's) kasap (money) in his sack's pah (mouth).

shawam (put) my gabayai (cup), the kasap (silver) gabayai (cup), in the sack's pah (mouth) of the youngest, with his grain kasap (money)." He did according to the dabar (word) that Yawasap had spoken.
As soon as the baqar (morning) was awar (light), the men were sent shalach (away), they and their donkeys.

When they had gone out of the Iyar, and were not yet rachaq (far) off, Yawasap said to his bayath (steward), "Up, follow achar (after) the men. When you overtake them, ask them, ‘Why have you rewarded rai (evil) for tawab (good)?
Isn't this that from which my Adawan drinks, and by which he indeed divines? You have done raii (evil) in so doing.'
He overtook them, and he spoke these dabar (words) to them.
They said to him, "Why does my Adawan dabar (speak) such dabar (words) as these? Far be it from your ibad (servants) that they should do such a thing!

Behold, the kasap (money), which we found in our sacks' pah (mouths), we brought again to you out of the aratz (land) of Kanain. How then should we steal kasap (silver) or gold out of your adawan (lord's) bayath (house)?
With whomever of your ibad (servants) it is found, let him mawath (die), and we also will be my adawan (lord's) ibad (bondservants).
He said, "Kan also let it be according to your words: he with whom it is found will be my ibad (bondservant); and you will be naqay (blameless).
Then they hurried, and each ayash (man) took his sack down to the aratz (ground), and each ayash (man) opened his sack.
He searched, beginning with the gadawal (eldest), and ending at the youngest. The gabayai (cup) was found in Banayamayan sack.
Then they tore their clothes, and each ayash (man) loaded his donkey, and returned to the Iyar.
Yahawadah (Judah) and his ach (brothers) came to Yawasap bayath (house), and he was still there. They napal (fell) on the aratz (ground) panayam (before) him.
Yawasap said to them, "What maishah (deed) is this that you have done? Don't you know that such a ayash (man) as I can indeed divine?

Yahawadah (Judah) said, "What will we tell my Adawan? What will we dabar (speak)? Or how will we tzadaq (clear) ourselves? Alahayam has found out the iwan (iniquity) of your ibad (servants). Behold, we are my adawan (lord's) ibad (bondservants), both we, and he also in whose hand the gabayai (cup) is found.

He said, "Far be it from me that I should do so. The ayash (man) in whose yad (hand) the gabayai (cup) is found, he will be my ibad (bondservant); but as for you, ilah (go) up in shalawam (peace) to your ab (father).

Then Yahawadah (Judah) came near to him, and said, "Oh, my Adawan, please let your ibad (servant) dabar (speak) a dabar (word) in my adawan (lord's) ears, and don't let your ap (anger) charah (burn) against your ibad (servant); for you are even as Paraih.
My Adawan asked his ibad (servants), saying, ‘Have you a ab (father), or a ach (brother)?'

We said to my Adawan, ‘We have a ab (father), an old zaqan (man), and a yalad (child) of his old age, a qatan (little) one; and his ach (brother) is mawath (dead), and he alone is yathar (left) of his am (mother); and his ab (father) ahab (loves) him.'
You said to your ibad (servants), ‘yarad (bring) him down to me, that I may shawam (set) my iyan (eyes) on him.'
We said to my Adawan, ‘The boy can't leave his ab (father): for if he should leave his ab (father), his ab (father) would mawath (die).'
You said to your ibad (servants), ‘Unless your youngest ach (brother) yarad (comes) down with you, you will see my panayam (face) no more.'
It happened when we came up to your ibad (servant) my ab (father), we told him the dabar (words) of my Adawan.
Our ab (father) said, ‘shawab (turn back / repent) again, buy us a Mait food.'

We said, ‘We can't yarad (go) down. If our youngest ach (brother) is with us, then we will yarad (go) down: for we may not raah (see) the ayash (man's) panayam (face), unless our youngest ach (brother) is with us.'
Your ibad (servant), my ab (father), said to us, ‘You yadai (know) that my ashah (wife) bore me shanayam (two) sons:
and the one went out from me, and I said, "Surely he is torn in pieces;" and I haven't seen him hanah (since).
If you take this im (one) also from me, and harm qarah (happens) to him, you will yarad (bring) down my shayabah (gray) hairs with rai (sorrow) to shaawal (sheol).'
Now therefore when I bawaa (come) to your ibad (servant) my ab (father), and the nair (boy) is not with us; since his napash (life) is bound up in the boy's napash (life);

it will happen, when he raah (see) that the nair (boy) is no more, that he will mawath (die). Your ibad (servants) will yarad (bring) down the shayabah (gray) hairs of your ibad (servant), our ab (father), with sorrow to shaawal (sheol).
For your ibad (servant) became collateral for the nair (boy) to my ab (father), saying, ‘If I don't bawaa (bring) him to you, then I will chataa (bear) the blame to my ab (father) forever.'
Now therefore, please let your ibad (servant) stay instead of the nair (boy), a ibad (bondservant) to my Adawan; and let the nair (boy) ilah (go) up with his ach (brothers).
For how will I ilah (go) up to my ab (father), if the nair (boy) isn't with me?—lest I raah (see) the rai (evil) that will matzaa (come) on my ab (father).

Then Yawasap couldn't control himself before all those who stood before him, and he cried, "yatzaa (cause) everyone to yatzaa (go) out from me!" No one else stood with him, while Yawasap made himself yadai (known) to his ach (brothers).
He wept aloud. The Matzarayam (Egyptians) heard, and the bayath (house) of Paraih heard.
Yawasap said to his ach (brothers), "I am Yawasap! Does my ab (father) still chay (live)?" His ach (brothers) couldn't answer him; for they were terrified at his panayam (presence).
Yawasap said to his ach (brothers), "Come near to me, please." They came near. "He said, I am Yawasap, your ach (brother), whom you sold into Matzarayam.
Now don't be grieved, nor charah (angry) with iyan (yourselves), that you sold me here, for Alahayam sent me panayam (before) you to preserve machayah (life).
For these two Shanah the famine has been in the aratz (land), and there are yet chamash (five) Shanah, in which there will be neither plowing nor harvest.
Alahayam sent me panayam (before) you to shawam (preserve) for you a remnant in the aratz (earth), and to chayah (save) you alive by a gadawal (great) palayatah (deliverance).
So now it wasn't you who sent me here, but Alahayam, and he has made me a ab (father) to Paraih, Adawan of all his bayath (house), and ruler over all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
Hurry, and ilah (go) up to my ab (father), and amar (tell) him, ‘This is what your ban (son) Yawasap amar (says), "Alahayam has made me Adawan of all Matzarayam. yarad (come) down to me. Don't wait.
You shall yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land) of Gashan, and you will be qarawab (near) to me, you, your children, your children's children, your flocks, your herds, and all that you have.
There I will nourish you; for there are yet chamash (five) Shanah of famine; lest you yarash (come) to poverty, you, and your bayath (household), and all that you have."'
Behold, your iyan (eyes) raah (see), and the iyan (eyes) of my ach (brother) Banayamayan, that it is my pah (mouth) that dabar (speaks) to you.
You shall nagad (tell) my ab (father) of all my kabawad (glory) in Matzarayam, and of all that you have seen. You shall hurry and bring my ab (father) down here.
He napal (fell) on his ach (brother) Banayamayan neck, and wept, and Banayamayan wept on his neck.
He kissed all his ach (brothers), and wept on them. achar (after) that his ach (brothers) talked with him.
The report of it was heard in Paraih bayath (house), saying, "Yawasap ach (brothers) have bawaa (come)." It pleased Paraih yatab (well), and his ibad (servants).
Paraih said to Yawasap, "amar (tell) your ach (brothers), ‘Do this. Load your animals, and yalak (go), travel to the aratz (land) of Kanain.

Take your ab (father) and your bayath (households), and bawaa (come) to me, and I will nathan (give) you the tawab (good) of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and you will akal (eat) the fat of the aratz (land).'
Now you are tzawah (commanded): do this. Take wagons out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam for your little ones, and for your wives, and nashaa (bring) your ab (father), and bawaa (come).
Also, don't concern yourselves about your belongings, for the tawab (good) of all of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam is yours.
The ban (sons) of Yasharaal (Israel) did so. Yawasap gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Paraih, and gave them provision for the darak (way).
He gave ayash (each) one of them changes of clothing, but to Banayamayan he gave shalawash (three) maah (hundred) pieces of kasap (silver) and chamash (five) changes of clothing.

He sent the following to his ab (father): ishar (ten) donkeys loaded with the tawab (good) things of Matzarayam, and ishar (ten) female donkeys loaded with grain and lacham (bread) and provision for his ab (father) by the darak (way).
So he sent his ach (brothers) shalach (away), and they departed. He said to them, "See that you don't quarrel on the darak (way).
They went up out of Matzarayam, and came into the aratz (land) of Kanain, to Yaiqab their ab (father).
They told him, saying, "Yawasap is still chay (alive), and he is ruler over all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam." His lab (heart) fainted, for he didn't aman (believe) them.

They told him all the dabar (words) of Yawasap, which he had said to them. When he saw the wagons which Yawasap had sent to nashaa (carry) him, the rawach (spirit) of Yaiqab, their ab (father), revived.
Yasharaal (Israel) said, "It is rab (enough). Yawasap my ban (son) is still chay (alive). I will yalak (go) and raah (see) him before I mawath (die).
Yasharaal (Israel) traveled with all that he had, and came Baarashabai Beersheba, and offered zabach (sacrifices) to the Alahayam of his ab (father), Yatzachaq.
Alahayam spoke to Yasharaal (Israel) in the visions of the layal (night), and said, "Yaiqab, Yaiqab!" He said, "Here I am.
He said, "I am Al, the Alahayam of your ab (father). Don't be yaraa (afraid) to yarad (go) down into Matzarayam, for there I will shawam (make) of you a gadawal (great) gaway (nation).
I will yarad (go) down with you into Matzarayam. I will also surely ilah (bring) you up again. Yawasap will close your iyan (eyes).

Yaiqab rose up Baarashabai Beersheba, and the ban (sons) of Yasharaal (Israel) carried Yaiqab, their ab (father), their little ones, and their wives, in the wagons which Paraih had sent to nashaa (carry) him.
They took their livestock, and their rakawash (goods), which they had gotten in the aratz (land) of Kanain, and came into Matzarayam— Yaiqab, and all his zarai (seed) with him,
his ban (sons), and his ban (sons)' ban (sons) with him, his bath (daughters), and his ban (sons)' bath (daughters), and he brought all his zarai (seed) with him into Matzarayam.
These are the sham (names) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), who came into Matzarayam, Yaiqab and his ban (sons): Raawaban, Yaiqab firstborn.
The ban (sons) of Raawaban: Chanawak, Palawaa, Chatzarawan, and Karamay.
The ban (sons) of Shamaiwan: Yamawaal, Yamayan, Ahad, Yakayan, Tzachar, and Shaawal the ban (son) of a Kanainay (Canaanite) woman.
The ban (sons) of Laway: Garashawan, Qahath, and Mararay.
The ban (sons) of Yahawadah (Judah): Ir, Awanan, Shalah, Paratz, and Zarach; but Ir and Awanan died in the aratz (land) of Kanain. The ban (sons) of Paratz were Chatzarawan and Chamawal.
The ban (sons) of Yashashakar: Thawalai, Pawaah, Yawab, and Shamarawan.
The ban (sons) of Zabawalawan: Sarad, Ayalawan, and Yachalaal.

These are the ban (sons) of Laah, whom she bore to Yaiqab in Paddan Padan, with his bath (daughter) Dayanah. All the napash (souls) of his ban (sons) and his bath (daughters) were shalawashayam (thirty) - shalawash (three).
The ban (sons) of Gad: Tzapayawan, Chagay, Shawanay, Atzabawan, Iray, Arawaday, and Araalay.
The ban (sons) of Ashar: Yamanah, Yashawah, Yashaway, Barayaih, and Sharach their achawath (sister). The ban (sons) of Barayaih: Chabar and Malakayaal.
These are the ban (sons) of Zalapah, whom Laban gave to Laah, his bath (daughter), and these she bore to Yaiqab, even sixteen napash (souls).
The ban (sons) of Rachal, Yaiqab ashah (wife): Yawasap and Banayamayan.
To Yawasap in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam were yalad (born) Manashah and Aparayam, whom Asanath, the bath (daughter) Pawatayaparai Potiphera, kahan (priest) Awan On, bore to him.
The ban (sons) of Banayamayan: Balai, Bakar, Ashabal, Garaa, Naiman, Achay, Raash, Mapayam, Chapayam, and Arad.
These are the ban (sons) of Rachal, who were yalad (born) to Yaiqab: all the napash (souls) were fourteen.
The ban (son) Dan Dan: Chawashayam.
The ban (sons) of Napathalay: Yachatzaal, Gawanay, Yatzar, and Shalam.
These are the ban (sons) of Balahah, whom Laban gave to Rachal, his bath (daughter), and these she bore to Yaiqab: all the napash (souls) were shabai (seven).
All the napash (souls) who came with Yaiqab into Matzarayam, who were his direct descendants, besides Yaiqab ban (sons)' wives, all the napash (souls) were shashayam (sixty) - shash (six).

The ban (sons) of Yawasap, who were yalad (born) to him in Matzarayam, were shanayam (two) napash (souls). All the napash (souls) of the bayath (house) of Yaiqab, who came into Matzarayam, were shabaiyam (seventy).
He sent Yahawadah (Judah) panayam (before) him to Yawasap, to show the way before him to Gashan, and they came into the aratz (land) of Gashan.

Yawasap prepared his chariot, and went up to qaraah (meet) Yasharaal (Israel), his ab (father), in Gashan. He presented himself to him, and napal (fell) on his neck, and wept on his neck a iwad (good) while.
Yasharaal (Israel) said to Yawasap, "paim (now) let me mawath (die), achar (since) I have seen your panayam (face), that you are still chay (alive).

Yawasap said to his ach (brothers), and to his ab (father's) bayath (house), "I will ilah (go) up, and amar (speak) with Paraih, and will amar (tell) him, ‘My ach (brothers), and my ab (father's) bayath (house), who were in the aratz (land) of Kanain, have bawaa (come) to me.
These men are raih (shepherds), for they have been keepers of livestock, and they have brought their flocks, and their herds, and all that they have.'
It will happen, when Paraih summons you, and will amar (say), ‘What is your maishah (occupation)?'

that you shall amar (say), ‘Your ibad (servants) have been keepers of livestock from our youth even until now, both we, and our abawath (fathers):' that you may yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land) of Gashan; for every raih (shepherd) is an thawaibah (abomination) to the Matzarayam (Egyptians).

Then Yawasap went in and told Paraih, and said, "My ab (father) and my ach (brothers), with their flocks, their herds, and all that they own, have bawaa (come) out of the aratz (land) of Kanain; and behold, they are in the aratz (land) of Gashan.
From among his ach (brothers) he took chamash (five) men, and presented them to Paraih.
Paraih said to his ach (brothers), "What is your maishah (occupation)?" They said to Paraih, "Your ibad (servants) are raih (shepherds), both we, and our abawath (fathers).

They said to Paraih, "We have bawaa (come) to live as foreigners in the aratz (land), for there is no pasture for your ibad (servants)' flocks. For the famine is Kabad in the aratz (land) of Kanain. Now therefore, please let your ibad (servants) yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land) of Gashan.
Paraih spoke to Yawasap, saying, "Your ab (father) and your ach (brothers) have bawaa (come) to you.

The aratz (land) of Matzarayam is panayam (before) you. yashab (make) your ab (father) and your ach (brothers) yashab (dwell) in the best of the aratz (land). Let them yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land) of Gashan. If you yadai (know) any able men among them, then shawam (put) them in charge of my livestock.
Yawasap brought in Yaiqab, his ab (father), and imad (set) him panayam (before) Paraih, and Yaiqab blessed Paraih.
Paraih said to Yaiqab, "mah (how) many are the yawam (days) of the years of your life?

Yaiqab said to Paraih, "The yawam (days) of the Shanah of my pilgrimage are one maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah. Mait and rai (evil) have been the yawam (days) of the Shanah of my chay (life), and they have not attained to the yawam (days) of the Shanah of the chay (life) of my abawath (fathers) in the yawam (days) of their pilgrimage.
Yaiqab blessed Paraih, and went out from the panayam (presence) of Paraih.

Yawasap placed his ab (father) and his ach (brothers), and gave them a achazah (possession) in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, in the best of the aratz (land), in the aratz (land) of Raimasas, as Paraih had tzawah (commanded).
Yawasap nourished his ab (father), his ach (brothers), and all of his ab (father's) bayath (household), with lacham (bread), according to their tap (families).
There was no lacham (bread) in all the aratz (land); for the famine was very Kabad, so that the aratz (land) of Matzarayam and the aratz (land) of Kanain fainted by panayam (reason) of the famine.

Yawasap gathered up all the kasap (money) that was found in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and in the aratz (land) of Kanain, for the grain which they bought: and Yawasap brought the kasap (money) into Paraih bayath (house).

When the kasap (money) was all thamam (spent) in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and in the aratz (land) of Kanain, all the Matzarayam (Egyptians) came to Yawasap, and said, "Give us lacham (bread), for why should we mawath (die) in your presence? For our kasap (money) apas (fails).
Yawasap said, "Give me your livestock; and I will nathan (give) you food for your livestock, if your kasap (money) is apas (gone).

They brought their livestock to Yawasap, and Yawasap gave them lacham (bread) in exchange for the horses, and for the flocks, and for the herds, and for the donkeys: and he fed them with lacham (bread) in exchange for all their livestock for that Shanah.

When that Shanah was ended, they came to him the shanay (second) Shanah, and said to him, "We will not hide from my Adawan how our kasap (money) is all thamam (spent), and the maqanah (herds) of livestock are my adawan (lord's). There is nothing shaar (left) in the panayam (sight) of my Adawan, but our bodies, and our adamah (lands).

Why should we mawath (die) before your iyan (eyes), both we and our adamah (land)? qanah (buy) us and our adamah (land) for lacham (bread), and we and our adamah (land) will be ibad (servants) to Paraih. nathan (give) us zarai (seed), that we may chayah (live), and not mawath (die), and that the adamah (land) won't be desolate.

So Yawasap bought all the adamah (land) of Matzarayam for Paraih, for every ayash (man) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians) sold his shadah (field), because the famine was severe on them, and the aratz (land) became Paraih.
As for the im (people), he moved them to the Iyar from qatzah (one) end of the border of Matzarayam even to the other end of it.

Only he didn't buy the adamah (land) of the kahan (priests), for the kahan (priests) had a chaq (portion) from Paraih, and ate their chaq (portion) which Paraih gave them. That is why they didn't sell their adamah (land).
Then Yawasap said to the im (people), "Behold, I have bought you and your adamah (land) today for Paraih. Behold, here is zarai (seed) for you, and you shall zarai (sow) the adamah (land).

It will happen at the harvests, that you shall nathan (give) a chamayashay (fifth) to Paraih, and arabai (four) yad (parts) will be your own, for zarai (seed) of the shadah (field), for your food, for them of your bayath (households), and for akal (food) for your little ones.
They said, "You have saved our chayah (lives)! Let us matzaa (find) favor in the iyan (sight) of my Adawan, and we will be Paraih ibad (servants).

Yawasap made it a chaq (statute) concerning the adamah (land) of Matzarayam to this yawam (day), that Paraih should have the chamash (fifth). Only the adamah (land) of the kahan (priests) alone didn't become Paraih.
Yasharaal (Israel) lived in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, in the aratz (land) of Gashan; and they got themselves achaz (possessions) therein, and were fruitful, and multiplied maad (exceedingly).
Yaiqab lived in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam seventeen Shanah. So the days of Yaiqab, the years of his life, were one maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - shabai (seven) Shanah.

The yawam (time) drew qarab (near) that Yasharaal (Israel) must mawath (die), and he called his ban (son) Yawasap, and said to him, "If now I have found favor in your iyan (sight), please shawam (put) your yad (hand) under my thigh, and ishah (deal) chasad (kindly) and truly with me. Please don't bury me in Matzarayam,
but when I sleep with my abawath (fathers), you shall nashaa (carry) me out of Matzarayam, and bury me in their qabawarah (burying) place." He said, "I will do as you have dabar (said).
He said, "shabai (swear) to me," and he swore to him. Yasharaal (Israel) bowed himself on the bed's raash (head).
It happened achar (after) these things, that someone said to Yawasap, "Behold, your ab (father) is chalah (sick)." He took with him his shanayam (two) ban (sons), Manashah and Aparayam.
Someone told Yaiqab, and said, "Behold, your ban (son) Yawasap bawaa (comes) to you," and Yasharaal (Israel) strengthened himself, and sat on the bed.
Yaiqab said to Yawasap, "Al Shaday raah (see) to me at Lawaz in the aratz (land) of Kanain, and blessed me,

and said to me, ‘Behold, I will make you fruitful, and multiply you, and I will nathan (make) of you a qahal (company) of im (peoples), and will nathan (give) this aratz (land) to your zarai (seed) achar (after) you for an iwalam (forever) achazah (possession).'

Now your shanayam (two) ban (sons), who were yalad (born) to you in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam before I came to you into Matzarayam, are mine; Aparayam and Manashah, even as Raawaban and Shamaiwan, will be mine.
Your issue, whom you become the father of achar (after) them, will be yours. They will be called after the sham (name) of their ach (brothers) in their nachalah (inheritance).

As for me, when I came Padan Paddan, Rachal died by me in the aratz (land) of Kanain in the darak (way), when there was still some distance to bawaa (come) to aparath (ephrath), and I buried her there in the darak (way) to aparath (ephrath) (the same is Bayathalacham).
Yasharaal (Israel) saw Yawasap ban (sons), and said, "Who are these?
Yawasap said to his ab (father), "They are my ban (sons), whom Alahayam has given me here." He said, "Please bring them to me, and I will barak (bless) them.
Now the iyan (eyes) of Yasharaal (Israel) were kabad (dim) for age, so that he couldn't raah (see). He brought them near to him; and he kissed them, and embraced them.
Yasharaal (Israel) said to Yawasap, "I didn't think I would raah (see) your panayam (face), and raah (see), Alahayam has let me see your zarai (seed) also.
Yawasap brought them out from between his knees, and he bowed himself with his ap (face) to the aratz (earth).

Yawasap took them shanayam (both), Aparayam in his right yamayan (hand) toward Yasharaal left shamaawal (hand), and Manashah in his left shamaawal (hand) toward Yasharaal right yamayan (hand), and brought them near to him.

Yasharaal (Israel) stretched out his right yamayan (hand), and laid it on Aparayam raash (head), who was the Tzaiyar, and his left shamaawal (hand) on Manashah raash (head), guiding his yad (hands) knowingly, for Manashah was the firstborn.
He blessed Yawasap, and said, "The Alahayam panayam (before) whom my abawath (fathers) Abaraham and Yatzachaq walked, the Alahayam who has fed me all my iwad (life) long to this yawam (day),

the malaak (angel) who has redeemed me from all rai (evil), barak (bless) the nair (lads), and let my sham (name) be named on them, and the sham (name) of my abawath (fathers) Abaraham and Yatzachaq. Let them grow into a multitude in the qarab (midst) of the aratz (earth).

When Yawasap saw that his ab (father) laid his yamayan (right) yad (hand) on the raash (head) of Aparayam, it displeased him. He held up his ab (father's) yad (hand), to sawar (remove) it from Aparayam raash (head) to Manashah raash (head).
Yawasap said to his ab (father), "Not so, my ab (father); for this is the firstborn; shawam (put) your right yamayan (hand) on his raash (head).

His ab (father) refused, and said, "I yadai (know), my ban (son), I yadai (know). He also will become a im (people), and he also will be great. However, his younger ach (brother) will be greater than he, and his zarai (seed) will become a multitude of gawayam (nations).

He blessed them that yawam (day), saying, "In you will Yasharaal (Israel) barak (bless), saying, ‘Alahayam shawam (make) you as Aparayam and as Manashah'" He shawam (set) Aparayam panayam (before) Manashah.
Yasharaal (Israel) said to Yawasap, "Behold, I am dying, but Alahayam will be with you, and shawab (turn back / repent) you again to the aratz (land) of your abawath (fathers).
Moreover I have given to you one portion above your ach (brothers), which I took out of the yad (hand) of the Amaray (Amorite) with my charab (sword) and with my qashath (bow).
Yaiqab called to his ban (sons), and said: "asap (gather) yourselves together, that I may nagad (tell) you that which will happen to you in the yawam (days) to come.
Assemble yourselves, and hear, you ban (sons) of Yaiqab. Listen to Yasharaal (Israel), your ab (father).
"Raawaban, you are my firstborn, my might, and the raashayath (beginning) of my awan (strength); excelling in dignity, and excelling in iz (power).
Boiling over as mayam (water), you shall not yathar (excel); because you went up to your ab (father's) bed, then defiled it. He went up to my couch.
"Shamaiwan and Laway are ach (brothers). Their makarah (swords) are weapons of violence.

My napash (soul), don't bawaa (come) into their council. My kabawad (glory), don't be united to their qahal (assembly); for in their ap (anger) they killed men. In their self-will they hamstrung cattle.
Cursed be their ap (anger), for it was iz (fierce); and their ibarah (wrath), for it was cruel. I will divide them in Yaiqab, and scatter them in Yasharaal (Israel).
"Yahawadah (Judah), your ach (brothers) will yadah (praise) you. Your yad (hand) will be on the neck of your ayab (enemies). Your ab (father's) ban (sons) will shachah (bow) down before you.
Yahawadah (Judah) is a aray (lion's) cub. From the Tarap, my ban (son), you have gone up. He stooped down, he crouched as a labayaa (lion), as a labayaa (lioness). Who will qawam (rouse) him up?
The scepter will not sawar (depart) from Yahawadah (Judah), nor the ruler's staff from between his feet, until he bawaa (comes) to whom it belongs. To him will the obedience of the im (peoples) be.
Binding his foal to the vine, his donkey's ban (colt) to the sharaq (choice) vine; he has washed his garments in yayan (wine), his robes in the dam (blood) of inab (grapes).
His iyan (eyes) will be Chakalayal with yayan (wine), his teeth Laban with milk.
"Zabawalawan will shakan (dwell) at the haven of the yam (sea). He will be for a haven of ships. His border will be on Tzayadawan.
"Yashashakar is a strong donkey, lying down between the saddlebags.
He saw a resting place, that it was tawab (good), the aratz (land), that it was pleasant. He natah (bows) his shoulder to the burden, and becomes a ibad (servant) doing forced mas (labor).
"Dan will dayan (judge) his im (people), as one of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Dan will be a serpent in the darak (way), an adder in the arach (path), That bites the horse's heels, so that his rider napal (falls) backward.
I have waited for your yashawaih (salvation), Yahawah.
"A gadawad (troop) will press on Gad, but he will press on their heel.
"Ashar lacham (food) will be Shaman. He will nathan (yield) malak (royal) dainties.
"Napathalay is a doe shalach (set) free, who bears beautiful fawns.
"Yawasap is a fruitful vine, a fruitful vine by a spring. His branches run over the wall.
The bail (archers) have severely grieved him, shot at him, and persecute him:

But his qashath (bow) remained ayathan (strong). The zarawai (arms) of his yad (hands) were made strong, by the yad (hands) of the abayar (mighty) One of Yaiqab, (from there is the raih (shepherd), the aban (stone) of Yasharaal (Israel)),

even by the Al of your ab (father), who will help you; by the Shaday, who will barak (bless) you, with barakah (blessings) of shamayam (heaven) above, barakah (blessings) of the deep that lies below, barakah (blessings) of the breasts, and of the racham (womb).

The barakah (blessings) of your ab (father) have prevailed above the barakah (blessings) of your ancestors, above the boundaries of the ancient Gabaih. They will be on the qadaqad (head) of Yawasap, on the qadaqad (crown) of the head of him who is separated from his ach (brothers).
"Banayamayan is a ravenous wolf. In the baqar (morning) he will akal (devour) the prey. At evening he will divide the spoil.
All these are the ishar (twelve) shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), and this is what their ab (father) spoke to them and blessed them. He blessed everyone according to his barakah (blessing).
He instructed them, and said to them, "I am to be gathered to my im (people). Bury me with my abawath (fathers) in the cave that is in the shadah (field) of Iparawan the Chathay (Hittite),

in the cave that is in the shadah (field) of Makapalah, which is panayam (before) Mamaraa, in the aratz (land) of Kanain, which Abaraham bought with the shadah (field) from Iparawan the Chathay (Hittite) as a burial qabar (place).
There they buried Abaraham and Sharah, his ashah (wife). There they buried Yatzachaq and Rabaqah, his ashah (wife), and there I buried Laah:
the shadah (field) and the cave that is therein, which was purchased from the children of Chath.
When Yaiqab made an kalah (end) of charging his ban (sons), he gathered up his feet into the bed, and yielded up the spirit, and was gathered to his im (people).
Yawasap napal (fell) on his ab (father's) panayam (face), wept on him, and kissed him.
Yawasap tzawah (commanded) his ibad (servants), the physicians, to embalm his ab (father); and the physicians embalmed Yasharaal (Israel).
arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days) were fulfilled for him, for that is how many the yawam (days) it takes to embalm. The Matzarayam (Egyptians) wept for him for shabaiyam (seventy) yawam (days).

When the yawam (days) of weeping for him were past, Yawasap spoke to the bayath (house) of Paraih, saying, "If now I have found favor in your iyan (eyes), please dabar (speak) in the ears of Paraih, saying,

‘My ab (father) made me shabai (swear), saying, "Behold, I am dying. Bury me in my qabar (grave) which I have dug for myself in the aratz (land) of Kanain." Now therefore, please let me ilah (go) up and bury my ab (father), and I will shawab (turn back / repent) again.'
Paraih said, "ilah (go) up, and bury your ab (father), just like he made you shabai (swear).
Yawasap went up to bury his ab (father); and with him went up all the ibad (servants) of Paraih, the zaqan (elders) of his bayath (house), all the zaqan (elders) of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam,
all the bayath (house) of Yawasap, his ach (brothers), and his ab (father's) bayath (house). Only their little ones, their flocks, and their herds, they left in the aratz (land) of Gashan.
There went up with him both chariots and horsemen. It was a very Kabad machanah (company).

They came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is ibar (beyond) the Yaradan, and there they lamented with a very gadawal (great) and Kabad lamentation. He mourned for his ab (father) shabai (seven) yawam (days).

When the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land), the Kanainay (Canaanites), saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said, "This is a Kabad mourning by the Matzarayam (Egyptians)." Therefore, its qaraa (name) was called Abalamatzarayam Mizraim, which is ibar (beyond) the Yaradan.
His ban (sons) did to him just as he tzawah (commanded) them,

for his ban (sons) carried him into the aratz (land) of Kanain, and buried him in the cave of the shadah (field) of Makapalah, which Abaraham bought with the shadah (field), for a achazah (possession) of a burial site, from Iparawan the Chathay (Hittite), panayam (before) Mamaraa.
Yawasap returned into Matzarayam— he, and his ach (brothers), and all that went up with him to bury his ab (father), achar (after) he had buried his ab (father).

When Yawasap ach (brothers) saw that their ab (father) was mawath (dead), they said, "It may be that Yawasap will shatam (hate) us, and will fully shawab (turn back / repent) us back for all of the rai (evil) which we did to him.
They sent a message to Yawasap, saying, "Your ab (father) tzawah (commanded) panayam (before) he mawath (died), saying,

‘You shall amar (tell) Yawasap, "Now please nashaa (forgive) the disobedience of your ach (brothers), and their pashai (sin), because they did rai (evil) to you."' Now, please nashaa (forgive) the disobedience of the ibad (servants) of the Alahayam of your ab (father)." Yawasap wept when they spoke to him.
His ach (brothers) also went and napal (fell) down before his panayam (face); and they said, "Behold, we are your ibad (servants).
Yawasap said to them, "Don't be yaraa (afraid), for am I in the place of Alahayam?
As for you, you meant rai (evil) against me, but Alahayam meant it for tawab (good), to ishah (bring) to pass, as it is this yawam (day), to chayah (save) many im (people) chayah (alive).
Now therefore don't be yaraa (afraid). I will nourish you and your little ones." He comforted them, and spoke lab (kindly) to them.
Yawasap lived in Matzarayam, he, and his ab (father's) bayath (house). Yawasap lived one maah (hundred) ishar (ten) Shanah.
Yawasap saw Aparayam children to the shalash (third) generation. The children also of Makayar, the ban (son) of Manashah, were yalad (born) on Yawasap knees.
