Yawasap said to his ach (brothers), "I am dying, but Alahayam will paqad (surely) paqad (visit) you, and ilah (bring) you up out of this aratz (land) to the aratz (land) which he swore to Abaraham, to Yatzachaq, and to Yaiqab.
Yawasap took an shabai (oath) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "Alahayam will paqad (surely) paqad (visit) you, and you shall ilah (carry) up my itzam (bones) from here.
So Yawasap died, being one maah (hundred) ishar (ten) Shanah ban (old), and they embalmed him, and he was put in a arawan (coffin) in Matzarayam.
Now these are the names of the Yaiqab of Israel, who came Yawasap Egypt (Matzarayam man and his bayath (household) came with Yaiqab):
Raawaban, Shamaiwan, Laway, and Yahawadah (Judah),
Yashashakar, Zabawalawan, and Banayamayan,
Dan and Napathalay, Gad and Ashar.
All the napash (souls) who came out of Yaiqab body were shabaiyam (seventy) napash (souls), and Yawasap was in Matzarayam already.
Yawasap died, as did all his ach (brothers), and all that dawar (generation).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and grew maad (exceedingly) itzam (mighty); and the aratz (land) was filled with them.
Now there qawam (arose) a Chadash malak (king) over Matzarayam, who didn't yadai (know) Yawasap.
He said to his im (people), "Behold, the im (people) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) are more and mightier than we.

Come, let us chakam (deal) wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it happen that when any war breaks out, they also join themselves to our shanaa (enemies), and fight against us, and escape out of the aratz (land).
Therefore they shawam (set) taskmasters over them to afflict them with their burdens. They built storage Iyar for Paraih: Patham and Raimasas.
But the more they afflicted them, the Kan they multiplied and the more they spread out. They were grieved panayam (because) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
The Matzarayam (Egyptians) ruthlessly made the children of Yasharaal (Israel) ibad (serve),

and they made their chay (lives) bitter with Qashah ibadah (service), in mortar and in brick, and in all kinds of ibadah (service) in the shadah (field), all their ibadah (service), in which they ruthlessly made them ibad (serve).
The malak (king) of Matzarayam spoke to the ibaray (hebrew) midwives, of whom the sham (name) of the one was Shaparah, and the sham (name) of the other Pawaih,

and he said, "When you perform the duty of a yalad (midwife) to the ibaray (hebrew) women, and raah (see) them on the birth stool; if it is a ban (son), then you shall mawath (kill) him; but if it is a bath (daughter), then she shall chayay (live).
But the midwives feared Alahayam, and didn't do what the malak (king) of Matzarayam commanded them, but saved the baby yalad (boys) chayah (alive).
The malak (king) of Matzarayam called for the midwives, and said to them, "Why have you done this thing, and have saved the yalad (boys) chayah (alive)?

The midwives said to Paraih, "Because the ibaray (hebrew) women aren't like the Matzaray (Egyptian) women; Chayah they are vigorous, and give yalad (birth) before the yalad (midwife) bawaa (comes) to them.
Alahayam dealt yatab (well) with the midwives, and the im (people) multiplied, and grew very itzam (mighty).
It happened, because the midwives feared Alahayam, that he gave them bayath (families).
Paraih tzawah (commanded) all his im (people), saying, "You shall cast every ban (son) who is Yalawad into the yaar (river), and every bath (daughter) you shall chayah (save) alive.
A ayash (man) of the bayath (house) of Laway went and took a bath (daughter) of Laway as his wife.
The ashah (woman) conceived, and bore a ban (son). When she saw that he was a tawab (fine) child, she hid him shalawash (three) yarach (months).

When she could no iwad (longer) hide him, she took a papyrus basket for him, and coated it with tar and with pitch. She shawam (put) the yalad (child) in it, and laid it in the reeds by the yaar (river's) shapah (bank).
His achawath (sister) stood Rachawaq off, to see what would be done to him.
Paraih bath (daughter) came down to bathe at the yaar (river). Her maidens walked along by the riverside. She saw the basket among the reeds, and sent her handmaid to get it.
She opened it, and saw the yalad (child), and behold, the baby cried. She had compassion on him, and said, "This is one of the ibaray (hebrews)' children.
Then his achawath (sister) said to Paraih bath (daughter), "Should I yalak (go) and qaraa (call) a nurse for you from the ibaray (hebrew) women, that she may nurse the yalad (child) for you?
Paraih bath (daughter) said to her, "yalak (go)." The maiden went and called the yalad (child's) am (mother).

Paraih bath (daughter) said to her, "yalak (take) this yalad (child) yalak (away), and nurse him for me, and I will nathan (give) you your wages." The ashah (woman) took the yalad (child), and nursed it.
The yalad (child) grew, and she brought him to Paraih bath (daughter), and he became her ban (son). She sham (named) him Mashah, and said, "Because I drew him out of the mayam (water).

It happened in those yawam (days), when Mashah had grown up, that he went out to his ach (brothers), and looked at their burdens. He saw an Matzaray (Egyptian) striking a ibaray (hebrew), one of his ach (brothers).
He looked this kah (way) and that kah (way), and when he saw that there was no one, he killed the Matzaray (Egyptian), and hid him in the sand.

He went out the shanay (second) yawam (day), and behold, shanayam (two) men of the ibaray (hebrews) were fighting with each other. He said to him who did the rashai (wrong), "Why do you strike your rai (fellow)?

He said, "Who made you a shar (prince) and a shapat (judge) over us? Do you plan to harag (kill) me, as you killed the Matzaray (Egyptian)?" Mashah was yaraa (afraid), and said, "Surely this thing is yadai (known).
Now when Paraih heard this thing, he sought to harag (kill) Mashah. But Mashah fled from the panayam (face) of Paraih, and lived in the aratz (land) of Madayan, and he sat down by a baar (well).
Now the kahan (priest) of Madayan had shabai (seven) bath (daughters). They came and drew water, and filled the troughs to shaqah (water) their ab (father's) flock.
The raih (shepherds) came and drove them away; but Mashah stood up and helped them, and watered their flock.
When they came to Raiwaal, their ab (father), he said, "How is it that you have returned so early today?
They said, "An Matzaray (Egyptian) delivered us out of the yad (hand) of the raih (shepherds), and moreover he drew dalah (water) for us, and watered the flock.
He said to his bath (daughters), "Where is he? Why is it that you have left the ayash (man)? qaraa (call) him, that he may akal (eat) lacham (bread).
Mashah was content to yashab (dwell) with the ayash (man). He gave Mashah Tzaparah, his bath (daughter).
She bore a ban (son), and he sham (named) him Garasham, for he said, "I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign aratz (land).

It happened in the course of those many yawam (days), that the malak (king) of Matzarayam died, and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) sighed because of the ibadah (bondage), and they cried, and their cry came up to Alahayam because of the ibadah (bondage).
Alahayam heard their groaning, and Alahayam zakar (remembered) his barayath (covenant) with Abaraham, with Yatzachaq, and with Yaiqab.
Alahayam saw the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and Alahayam was concerned about them.

Now Mashah was keeping the flock of Yatharaw, his father-in-law, the kahan (priest) of Madayan, and he led the flock to the achar (back) of the madabar (wilderness), and came to alahayam (god's) har (mountain), to Charab.
The malaak (angel) of Yahawah raah (see) to him in a labah (flame) of ash (fire) out of the middle of a bush. He looked, and behold, the bush burned with ash (fire), and the bush was not consumed.
Mashah said, "I will sawar (turn) aside now, and raah (see) this gadawal (great) sight, why the bush is not burnt.
When Yahawah saw that he turned sawar (aside) to raah (see), Alahayam called to him out of the middle of the bush, and said, "Mashah! Mashah!" He said, "Here I am.
He said, "Don't qarab (come) close. Take your sandals off of your feet, for the place you are standing on is qadash (holy) adamah (ground).

Moreover he said, "I am the Alahayam of your ab (father), the Alahayam of Abaraham, the Alahayam of Yatzachaq, and the Alahayam of Yaiqab." Mashah hid his panayam (face); for he was yaraa (afraid) to look at Alahayam.
Yahawah said, "I have raah (see) seen the affliction of my im (people) who are in Matzarayam, and have heard their cry panayam (because) of their taskmasters, for I yadai (know) their sorrows.

I have yarad (come) down to natzal (deliver) them out of the yad (hand) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and to ilah (bring) them up out of that aratz (land) to a tawab (good) and Rachab aratz (land), to a aratz (land) flowing with milk and honey; to the place of the Kanainay (Canaanite), the Chathay (Hittite), the Amaray (Amorite), the Parazay (Perizzite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite).
Now, behold, the cry of the ban (sons) of Yasharaal (Israel) has bawaa (come) to me. Moreover I have seen the oppression with which the Matzarayam (Egyptians) lachatz (oppress) them.
yalak (come) now therefore, and I will shalach (send) you to Paraih, that you may bring my im (people), the ban (sons) of Yasharaal (Israel), out of Matzarayam.
Mashah said to Alahayam, "Who am I, that I should yalak (go) to Paraih, and that I should bring the ban (sons) of Yasharaal (Israel) out of Matzarayam?

He said, "Certainly I will be with you. This will be the awath (token) to you, that I have sent you: when you have brought the im (people) out of Matzarayam, you shall ibad (serve) Alahayam on this har (mountain).

Mashah said to Alahayam, "Behold, when I bawaa (come) to the ban (sons) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them, 'The Alahayam of your abawath (fathers) has sent me to you;' and they ask me, 'What is his sham (name)?' What should I amar (tell) them?
Alahayam said to Mashah, "I AM WHO I AM," and he said, "You shall amar (tell) the ban (sons) of Yasharaal (Israel) this: 'I AM has sent me to you.'

Alahayam said moreover to Mashah, "You shall amar (tell) the ban (sons) of Yasharaal (Israel) this, 'Yahawah, the Alahayam of your abawath (fathers), the Alahayam of Abaraham, the Alahayam of Yatzachaq, and the Alahayam of Yaiqab, has sent me to you.' This is my sham (name) iwalam (forever), and this is my zakar (memorial) to all dawar (generations).

yalak (go), and asap (gather) the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) asap (together), and amar (tell) them, 'Yahawah, the Alahayam of your abawath (fathers), the Alahayam of Abaraham, of Yatzachaq, and of Yaiqab, has raah (see) to me, saying, "I have paqad (surely) visited you, and seen that which is done to you in Matzarayam;

and I have said, I will ilah (bring) you up out of the affliction of Matzarayam to the aratz (land) of the Kanainay (Canaanite), the Chathay (Hittite), the Amaray (Amorite), the Parazay (Perizzite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite), to a aratz (land) flowing with milk and honey."'

They will listen to your qawal (voice), and you shall bawaa (come), you and the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel), to the malak (king) of Matzarayam, and you shall amar (tell) him, 'Yahawah, the Alahayam of the ibaray (hebrews), has met with us. Now please let us yalak (go) shalawash (three) yawam (days)' darak (journey) into the madabar (wilderness), that we may zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah, our Alahayam.'
I yadai (know) that the malak (king) of Matzarayam won't nathan (give) you permission to halak (go), no, not by a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand).
I will shalach (reach) out my yad (hand) and strike Matzarayam with all my wonders which I will do in its middle and achar (after) that he will let you shalach (go).
I will nathan (give) this im (people) favor in the iyan (sight) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and it will happen that when you yalak (go), you shall not yalak (go) empty-handed.

But every ashah (woman) shall shaal (ask) Shakan her neighbor, and of her who visits her bayath (house), jewels of kasap (silver), jewels of gold, and clothing; and you shall shawam (put) them on your ban (sons), and on your bath (daughters). You shall plunder the Matzarayam (Egyptians).
Mashah answered, "But, behold, they will not aman (believe) me, nor listen to my qawal (voice); for they will amar (say), ‘Yahawah has not raah (see) to you.'
Yahawah said to him, "What is that in your yad (hand)?" He said, "A matah (rod).
He said, "Throw it on the aratz (ground)." He threw it on the aratz (ground), and it became a snake; and Mashah ran away from it.

Yahawah said to Mashah, "shalach (stretch) out your yad (hand), and achaz (take) it by the tail." He stretched out his yad (hand), and took chazaq (hold) of it, and it became a matah (rod) in his kap (hand).
"That they may aman (believe) that Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers), the Alahayam of Abaraham, the Alahayam of Yatzachaq, and the Alahayam of Yaiqab, has raah (see) to you.

Yahawah said iwad (furthermore) to him, "Now bawaa (put) your yad (hand) inside your cloak." He bawaa (put) his yad (hand) inside his cloak, and when he took it out, behold, his yad (hand) was leprous, as white as snow.

He said, "shawab (turn back / repent) your yad (hand) inside your cloak again." He shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) inside his cloak again, and when he took it out of his cloak, behold, it had turned again as his other flesh.

"It will happen, if they will neither aman (believe) you nor listen to the qawal (voice) of the raashawan (first) awath (sign), that they will aman (believe) the qawal (voice) of the Acharawan awath (sign).

It will happen, if they will not aman (believe) even these shanayam (two) awath (signs), neither listen to your qawal (voice), that you shall take of the mayam (water) of the yaar (river), and pour it on the yabashah (dry land) land. The mayam (water) which you take out of the yaar (river) will become dam (blood) on the dry yabashath (land).

Mashah said to Yahawah, "O Adanay, I am not dabar (eloquent), neither shalashawam (before) now, nor since you have spoken to your ibad (servant); for I am Kabad of pah (speech), and of a Kabad lashawan (tongue).
Yahawah said to him, "Who made adam (man's) pah (mouth)? Or who shawam (makes) one mute, or Charash, or Paqach, or iwar (blind)? Isn't it I, Yahawah?
Now therefore yalak (go), and I will be with your pah (mouth), and teach you what you shall dabar (speak).
He said, "Oh, Adanay, please shalach (send) someone else.

The ap (anger) of Yahawah was kindled against Mashah, and he said, "What about Aharawan, your ach (brother), the Lawayay (Levite)? I yadai (know) that he can dabar (speak) dabar (well). Also, behold, he yatzaa (comes) out to qaraah (meet) you. When he raah (see) you, he will be Shamach in his lab (heart).
You shall dabar (speak) to him, and shawam (put) the dabar (words) in his pah (mouth). I will be with your pah (mouth), and with his pah (mouth), and will teach you what you shall do.
He will be your dabar (spokesman) to the im (people); and it will happen, that he will be to you a pah (mouth), and you will be to him as Alahayam.
You shall take this matah (rod) in your yad (hand), with which you shall do the awath (signs).

Mashah went and returned to Yathar his father-in-law, and said to him, "Please let me yalak (go) and shawab (turn back / repent) to my ach (brothers) who are in Matzarayam, and raah (see) iwad (whether) they are still chay (alive)." Yatharaw said to Mashah, "yalak (go) in shalawam (peace).
Yahawah said to Mashah in Madayan, "yalak (go), shawab (turn back / repent) into Matzarayam; for all the men who sought your napash (life) are mawath (dead).
Mashah took his ashah (wife) and his ban (sons), and set them on a donkey, and he returned to the aratz (land) of Matzarayam. Mashah took alahayam (god's) matah (rod) in his yad (hand).

Yahawah said to Mashah, "When you yalak (go) shawab (turn back / repent) into Matzarayam, raah (see) that you do panayam (before) Paraih all the mawapath (wonders) which I have shawam (put) in your yad (hand), but I will chazaq (harden) his lab (heart) and he will not let the im (people) shalach (go).
You shall amar (tell) Paraih, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, Yasharaal (Israel) is my ban (son), my firstborn,
and I have said to you, "Let my ban (son) shalach (go), that he may ibad (serve) me;" and you have refused to let him shalach (go). Behold, I will harag (kill) your ban (son), your firstborn.'
It happened on the darak (way) at a lodging place, that Yahawah met Moses and wanted to mawath (kill) him.
Then Tzaparah took a tzar (flint), and karath (cut) off the foreskin of her ban (son), and nagai (cast) it at his feet; and she said, "Surely you are a chathan (bridegroom) of dam (blood) to me.
So he let him rapah (alone). Then she said, "You are a chathan (bridegroom) of dam (blood)," because of the circumcision.
Yahawah said to Aharawan, "yalak (go) into the madabar (wilderness) to qaraah (meet) Mashah." He went, and met him on alahayam (god's) har (mountain), and kissed him.
Mashah told Aharawan all the dabar (words) of Yahawah with which he had sent him, and all the awath (signs) with which he had instructed him.
Mashah and Aharawan went and gathered asap (together) all the zaqan (elders) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
Aharawan spoke all the dabar (words) which Yahawah had spoken to Mashah, and did the awath (signs) in the iyan (sight) of the im (people).
The im (people) believed, and when they heard that Yahawah had visited the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and that he had seen their affliction, then they bowed their qadad (heads) and worshiped.

Afterward Mashah and Aharawan came, and said to Paraih, "This is what Yahawah, the Alahayam of Israel, amar (says), ‘Let my im (people) shalach (go), that they may hold a feast to me in the madabar (wilderness).'

Paraih said, "Who is Yahawah, that I should listen to his qawal (voice) to let Yasharaal (Israel) shalach (go)? I don't yadai (know) Yahawah, and moreover I will not let Yasharaal (Israel) shalach (go).

They said, "The Alahayam of the ibaray (hebrews) has met with us. Please let us yalak (go) shalawash (three) yawam (days)' darak (journey) into the madabar (wilderness), and zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah, our Alahayam, lest he pagai (fall) on us with dabar (pestilence), or with the charab (sword).
The malak (king) of Matzarayam said to them, "Why do you, Mashah and Aharawan, take the im (people) from their maishah (work)? yalak (get) back to your burdens!
Paraih said, "Behold, the im (people) of the aratz (land) are now many, and you make them shabath (rest) from their burdens.
The same yawam (day) Paraih tzawah (commanded) the taskmasters of the im (people), and their shatar (officers), saying,
"You shall no longer nathan (give) the im (people) straw to make brick, as shalashawam (before). Let them yalak (go) and gather straw for themselves.

The number of the bricks, which they made shalashawam (before), you require from them. You shall not diminish anything of it, for they are rapah (idle); therefore they cry, saying, ‘Let us yalak (go) and zabach (sacrifice) to our Alahayam.'
Let heavier ibadah (work) be kabad (laid) on the men, that they may labor therein; and don't let them pay any attention to lying dabar (words).
The taskmasters of the im (people) went out, and their shatar (officers), and they spoke to the im (people), saying, "This is what Paraih amar (says): ‘I will not nathan (give) you straw.
yalak (go) yourselves, get straw where you can matzaa (find) it, for nothing of your ibadah (work) shall be diminished.'
So the im (people) were scattered abroad throughout all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam to gather stubble for straw.
The taskmasters were urgent saying, "Fulfill your maishah (work) quota yawam (daily), as when there was straw!

The shatar (officers) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), whom Paraih taskmasters had shawam (set) over them, were beaten, and demanded, "Why haven't you fulfilled your quota both thamawal (yesterday) and today, in making brick as shalashawam (before)?
Then the shatar (officers) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) came and cried to Paraih, saying, "Why do you ishah (deal) this way with your ibad (servants)?
No straw is given to your ibad (servants), and they amar (tell) us, ‘ishah (make) brick!' and behold, your ibad (servants) are beaten; but the chataa (fault) is in your own im (people).
But he said, "You are rapah (idle)! You are rapah (idle)! Therefore you amar (say), ‘Let us yalak (go) and zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah.'
yalak (go) therefore now, and ibad (work), for no straw shall be given to you, yet you shall nathan (deliver) the same number of bricks!
The shatar (officers) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) saw that they were in rai (trouble), when it was said, "You shall not diminish anything from your yawam (daily) quota of bricks!
They met Mashah and Aharawan, who stood in the qaraah (way), as they came out from Paraih:

and they said to them, "May Yahawah raah (see) at you, and shapat (judge), because you have made us a stench to be baash (abhorred) in the iyan (eyes) of Paraih, and in the iyan (eyes) of his ibad (servants), to nathan (put) a charab (sword) in their yad (hand) to harag (kill) us.
Mashah returned to Yahawah, and said, "Adanay, why have you brought trouble on this im (people)? Why is it that you have sent me?
For since I came to Paraih to dabar (speak) in your sham (name), he has brought trouble on this im (people); neither have you delivered your im (people) at all.

Yahawah said to Mashah, "Now you shall raah (see) what I will do to Paraih, for by a chazaq (strong) yad (hand) he shall let them shalach (go), and by a chazaq (strong) yad (hand) he shall drive them out of his aratz (land).
Alahayam spoke to Mashah, and said to him, "I am Yahawah;
and I raah (see) to Abaraham, to Yatzachaq, and to Yaiqab, as Al Shaday; but by my sham (name) Yahawah I was not yadai (known) to them.
I have also established my barayath (covenant) with them, to nathan (give) them the aratz (land) of Kanain, the aratz (land) of their travels, in which they lived as aliens.
Moreover I have heard the groaning of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), whom the Matzarayam (Egyptians) ibad (keep) in bondage, and I have zakar (remembered) my barayath (covenant).

Kan amar (tell) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘I am Yahawah, and I will yatzaa (bring) you out from under the burdens of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and I will natzal (rid) you out of their ibadah (bondage), and I will gaal (redeem) you with an natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm), and with gadawal (great) shapat (judgments):

and I will take you to me for a im (people), and I will be to you a Alahayam; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who yatzaa (brings) you out from under the burdens of the Matzarayam (Egyptians).
I will bawaa (bring) you into the aratz (land) which I swore to nathan (give) to Abaraham, to Yatzachaq, and to Yaiqab; and I will nathan (give) it to you for a mawarashah (heritage): I am Yahawah.'
Mashah spoke so to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), but they didn't listen to Mashah for anguish of rawach (spirit), and for Qashah ibadah (bondage).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"bawaa (go) in, dabar (speak) to Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam, that he let the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shalach (go) out of his aratz (land).
Mashah spoke panayam (before) Yahawah, saying, "Behold, the children of Yasharaal (Israel) haven't listened to me. How then shall Paraih listen to me, who am of Iral shapah (lips)?

Yahawah spoke to Mashah and to Aharawan, and gave them a tzawah (command) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and to Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam, to yatzaa (bring) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.

These are the raash (heads) of their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses). The ban (sons) of Raawaban the firstborn of Yasharaal (Israel): Chanawak, and Palawaa, Chatzarawan, and Karamay; these are the mashapachah (families) of Raawaban.
The ban (sons) of Shamaiwan: Yamawaal, and Yamayan, and Ahad, and Yakayan, and Tzachar, and Shaawal the ban (son) of a Kanainay (Canaanite) woman; these are the mashapachah (families) of Shamaiwan.

These are the sham (names) of the ban (sons) of Laway according to their thawaladah (generations): Garashawan, and Qahath, and Mararay; and the Shanah of the chay (life) of Laway were one maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - shabai (seven) Shanah.
The ban (sons) of Garashawan: Labanay and Shamaiy, according to their mashapachah (families).
The ban (sons) of Qahath: Imaram, and Yatzahar, and Chabarawan, and Izayaal; and the Shanah of the chay (life) of Qahath were one maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - shalawash (three) Shanah.
The ban (sons) of Mararay: Machalay and Mawashay. These are the mashapachah (families) Laway the Levites according to their thawaladah (generations).

Imaram took Yawakabad his dawadah (father's) sister to himself as ashah (wife); and she bore him Aharawan and Mashah: and the Shanah of the chay (life) of Imaram were a maah (hundred) and shalawashayam (thirty) - shabai (seven) Shanah.
The ban (sons) of Yatzahar: Qarach, and Napag, and Zakaray.
The ban (sons) of Izayaal: Mayashaal, and Alayatzapan, and Satharay.
Aharawan took Alayashabai, the bath (daughter) of Imayanadab, the achawath (sister) of Nachashawan, as his ashah (wife); and she bore him Nadab and Abayahawaa, Alaizar and Ayathamar.
The ban (sons) of Qarach: Asayar, and Alaqanah, and Abayaasap; these are the mashapachah (families) of the qarachay (korahites).

Alaizar Aharawan ban (son) took one of the bath (daughters) of Pawatayaal as his ashah (wife); and she bore him Payanachas. These are the raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' Lawayay of the Levites according to their mashapachah (families).
These are that Aharawan and Mashah, to whom Yahawah said, "yatzaa (bring) out the children of Yasharaal (Israel) from the aratz (land) of Matzarayam according to their tzabaa (armies).
These are those who spoke to Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam, to yatzaa (bring) out the children of Yasharaal (Israel) from Matzarayam. These are that Mashah and Aharawan.
It happened on the yawam (day) when Yahawah spoke to Mashah in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam,
that Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying, "I am Yahawah. dabar (speak) to Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam all that I dabar (speak) to you.
Mashah said panayam (before) Yahawah, "Behold, I am of Iral shapah (lips), and how shall Paraih listen to me?
Yahawah said to Mashah, "raah (see), I have made you as Alahayam to Paraih; and Aharawan your ach (brother) shall be your nabayaa (prophet).
You shall dabar (speak) all that I tzawah (command) you; and Aharawan your ach (brother) shall dabar (speak) to Paraih, that he let the children of Yasharaal (Israel) go out of his aratz (land).
I will harden Paraih lab (heart), and multiply my awath (signs) and my mawapath (wonders) in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.

But Paraih will not listen to you, and I will nathan (lay) my yad (hand) on Matzarayam, and yatzaa (bring) out my tzabaa (armies), my im (people) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam by gadawal (great) shapat (judgments).
The Matzarayam (Egyptians) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on Matzarayam, and yatzaa (bring) out the children of Yasharaal (Israel) from among them.
Mashah and Aharawan did so. As Yahawah tzawah (commanded) them, so they did.
Mashah was shamanayam (eighty) Shanah ban (old), and Aharawan shamanayam (eighty)- shalawash (three) Shanah ban (old), when they spoke to Paraih.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah and to Aharawan, saying,

"When Paraih dabar (speaks) to you, saying, ‘nathan (perform) a mawapath (miracle)!' then you shall amar (tell) Aharawan, ‘Take your matah (rod), and cast it down panayam (before) Paraih, that it become a thanayan (serpent).'

Mashah and Aharawan went in to Paraih, and they did so, as Yahawah had tzawah (commanded): and Aharawan cast down his matah (rod) panayam (before) Paraih and panayam (before) his ibad (servants), and it became a thanayan (serpent).
Then Paraih also called for the chakam (wise) men and the sorcerers. They also, the magicians of Matzarayam, did the Kan thing with their enchantments.
For they ayash (each) cast down their matah (rods), and they became thanayan (serpents): but Aharawan matah (rod) swallowed up their matah (rods).
Paraih lab (heart) was hardened, and he didn't listen to them; as Yahawah had spoken.
Yahawah said to Mashah, "Paraih lab (heart) is Kabad. He refuses to let the im (people) shalach (go).

Go to Paraih in the baqar (morning). Behold, he goes out to the mayam (water); and you shall natzab (stand) by the yaar (river's) shapah (bank) to qaraah (meet) him; and the matah (rod) which was turned to a serpent you shall take in your yad (hand).

You shall amar (tell) him, ‘Yahawah, the Alahayam of the ibaray (hebrews), has sent me to you, saying, "Let my im (people) shalach (go), that they may ibad (serve) me in the madabar (wilderness):" and behold, until now you haven't listened.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "In this you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah. Behold, I will strike with the matah (rod) that is in my yad (hand) on the mayam (waters) which are in the yaar (river), and they shall be turned to dam (blood).
The fish that are in the yaar (river) shall mawath (die), and the yaar (river) shall become foul; and the Matzarayam (Egyptians) shall loathe to drink mayam (water) from the yaar (river)."'

Yahawah said to Mashah, "Tell Aharawan, ‘Take your matah (rod), and natah (stretch) out your yad (hand) over the mayam (waters) of Matzarayam, over their yaar (rivers), over their streams, and over their Maqawah, and over all their ponds of mayam (water), that they may become dam (blood); and there shall be dam (blood) throughout all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, both in vessels of itz (wood) and in vessels of aban (stone).'

Mashah and Aharawan did so, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded); and he lifted up the matah (rod), and struck the mayam (waters) that were in the yaar (river), in the iyan (sight) of Paraih, and in the iyan (sight) of his ibad (servants); and all the mayam (waters) that were in the yaar (river) were turned to dam (blood).

The fish that were in the yaar (river) died; and the yaar (river) became foul, and the Matzarayam (Egyptians) couldn't drink mayam (water) from the yaar (river); and the dam (blood) was throughout all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
The magicians of Matzarayam did the same thing with their enchantments; and Paraih lab (heart) was hardened, and he didn't listen to them; as Yahawah had spoken.
Paraih turned and went into his bayath (house), and he didn't even shayath (take) this to lab (heart).
All the Matzarayam (Egyptians) dug around the yaar (river) for mayam (water) to drink; for they couldn't drink of the mayam (water) of the yaar (river).
shabai (seven) yawam (days) were fulfilled, achar (after) Yahawah had struck the yaar (river).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, bawaa (go) in to Paraih, and amar (tell) him, "This is what Yahawah amar (says), ‘Let my im (people) shalach (go), that they may ibad (serve) me.
If you refuse to let them shalach (go), behold, I will nagap (plague) all your borders with frogs:

and the yaar (river) shall swarm with frogs, which shall ilah (go) up and bawaa (come) into your bayath (house), and into your bedroom, and on your bed, and into the bayath (house) of your ibad (servants), and on your im (people), and into your ovens, and into your kneading troughs:
and the frogs shall ilah (come) up both on you, and on your im (people), and on all your ibad (servants).'

Yahawah said to Mashah, "amar (tell) Aharawan, ‘natah (stretch) out your yad (hand) with your matah (rod) over the nahar (rivers), over the streams, and over the pools, and cause frogs to ilah (come) up on the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.'
Aharawan stretched out his yad (hand) over the mayam (waters) of Matzarayam; and the frogs came up, and covered the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
The magicians did the same thing with their enchantments, and brought up frogs on the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.

Then Paraih called for Mashah and Aharawan, and said, "Entreat Yahawah, that he sawar (take) away the frogs from me, and from my im (people); and I will let the im (people) shalach (go), that they may zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah.

Mashah said to Paraih, "I give you the honor of setting the time that I should pray for you, and for your ibad (servants), and for your im (people), that the frogs be destroyed from you and your bayath (houses), and shaar (remain) in the yaar (river) only.
He said, "Tomorrow." He said, "Be it according to your dabar (word), that you may yadai (know) that there is none like Yahawah our Alahayam.
The frogs shall sawar (depart) from you, and from your bayath (houses), and from your ibad (servants), and from your im (people). They shall shaar (remain) in the yaar (river) only.
Mashah and Aharawan went out from Paraih, and Mashah cried to Yahawah dabar (concerning) the frogs which he had brought on Paraih.
Yahawah did according to the dabar (word) of Mashah, and the frogs died out of the bayath (houses), out of the courts, and out of the shadah (fields).
They gathered them together in heaps, and the aratz (land) stank.
But when Paraih saw that there was a respite, he hardened his lab (heart), and didn't listen to them, as Yahawah had spoken.

Yahawah said to Mashah, "amar (tell) Aharawan, ‘natah (stretch) out your matah (rod), and strike the ipar (dust) of the aratz (earth), that it may become lice throughout all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.'

They did so; and Aharawan stretched out his yad (hand) with his matah (rod), and struck the ipar (dust) of the aratz (earth), and there were lice on adam (man), and on animal; all the ipar (dust) of the aratz (earth) became lice throughout all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
The magicians tried with their enchantments to produce lice, but they couldn't. There were lice on adam (man), and on animal.
Then the magicians said to Paraih, "This is the finger of Alahayam:" and Paraih lab (heart) was hardened, and he didn't listen to them; as Yahawah had spoken.

Yahawah said to Mashah, "shakam (rise) up early in the baqar (morning), and stand panayam (before) Paraih; behold, he yatzaa (comes) out to the mayam (water); and amar (tell) him, ‘This is what Yahawah amar (says), "Let my im (people) shalach (go), that they may ibad (serve) me.

Else, if you will not let my im (people) shalach (go), behold, I will shalach (send) swarms of flies on you, and on your ibad (servants), and on your im (people), and into your bayath (houses): and the bayath (houses) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians) shall be malaa (full) of swarms of flies, and also the adamah (ground) whereon they are.

I will set apart in that yawam (day) the aratz (land) of Gashan, in which my im (people) imad (dwell), that no swarms of flies shall be there; to the end you may yadai (know) that I am Yahawah in the qarab (midst) of the aratz (earth).
I will shawam (put) a padawath (division) between my im (people) and your im (people): by tomorrow shall this awath (sign) be."'

Yahawah did so; and there came Kabad swarms of flies into the bayath (house) of Paraih, and into his ibad (servants)' bayath (houses): and in all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam the aratz (land) was corrupted by panayam (reason) of the swarms of flies.
Paraih called for Mashah and for Aharawan, and said, "yalak (go), zabach (sacrifice) to your Alahayam in the aratz (land)!

Mashah said, "It isn't appropriate to do so; for we shall zabach (sacrifice) the thawaibah (abomination) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians) to Yahawah our Alahayam. Behold, shall we zabach (sacrifice) the thawaibah (abomination) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians) before their iyan (eyes), and won't they saqal (stone) us?
We will yalak (go) shalawash (three) yawam (days)' darak (journey) into the madabar (wilderness), and zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah our Alahayam, as he shall command us.
Paraih said, "I will let you shalach (go), that you may zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah your Alahayam in the madabar (wilderness), only you shall not yalak (go) very rachaq (far) away. Pray for me.

Mashah said, "Behold, I yatzaa (go) out from you, and I will pray to Yahawah that the swarms of flies may sawar (depart) from Paraih, from his ibad (servants), and from his im (people), tomorrow; only don't let Paraih deal deceitfully any more in not letting the im (people) shalach (go) to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah.
Mashah went out from Paraih, and prayed to Yahawah.
Yahawah did according to the dabar (word) of Mashah, and he removed the swarms of flies from Paraih, from his ibad (servants), and from his im (people). There remained not one.
Paraih hardened his lab (heart) this paim (time) also, and he didn't let the im (people) shalach (go).

Then Yahawah said to Mashah, "bawaa (go) in to Paraih, and dabar (tell) him, ‘This is what Yahawah, the Alahayam of the ibaray (hebrews), amar (says): "Let my im (people) shalach (go), that they may ibad (serve) me.
For if you refuse to let them shalach (go), and chazaq (hold) them still,

behold, the yad (hand) of Yahawah is on your livestock which are in the shadah (field), on the horses, on the donkeys, on the camels, on the herds, and on the flocks with a very Kabad dabar (pestilence).

Yahawah will make a distinction between the livestock of Yasharaal (Israel) and the livestock of Matzarayam; and nothing shall mawath (die) of all that belongs to the children of Yasharaal (Israel)."'
Yahawah appointed a mawaid (set) time, saying, "Tomorrow Yahawah shall do this thing in the aratz (land).
Yahawah did that thing on the next macharath (day); and all the livestock of Matzarayam died, but of the livestock of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), not one died.

Paraih sent, and, behold, there was not so much as one of the livestock Yasharaal the Israelites mawath (dead). But the lab (heart) of Paraih was stubborn, and he didn't let the im (people) shalach (go).
Yahawah said to Mashah and to Aharawan, "Take to you chapan (handfuls) of ashes of the furnace, and let Mashah sprinkle it toward the sky in the iyan (sight) of Paraih.
It shall become small dust over all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and shall be a boil breaking out with boils on adam (man) and on animal, throughout all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
They took ashes of the furnace, and stood panayam (before) Paraih; and Mashah sprinkled it up toward the sky; and it became a boil breaking out with boils on adam (man) and on animal.
The magicians couldn't imad (stand) panayam (before) Mashah panayam (because) of the boils; for the boils were on the magicians, and on all the Matzarayam (Egyptians).
Yahawah hardened the lab (heart) of Paraih, and he didn't listen to them, as Yahawah had spoken to Mashah.

Yahawah said to Mashah, "shakam (rise) up early in the baqar (morning), and stand panayam (before) Paraih, and amar (tell) him, ‘This is what Yahawah, the Alahayam of the ibaray (hebrews), amar (says): "Let my im (people) shalach (go), that they may ibad (serve) me.

For this paim (time) I will shalach (send) all my magapah (plagues) against your lab (heart), against your officials, and against your im (people); that you may yadai (know) that there is none like me in all the aratz (earth).
For now I would have stretched out my yad (hand), and struck you and your im (people) with dabar (pestilence), and you would have been cut off from the aratz (earth);
but indeed for this cause I have made you imad (stand): to show you my kach (power), and that my sham (name) may be declared throughout all the aratz (earth);
as you still exalt yourself against my im (people), that you won't let them shalach (go).
Behold, tomorrow about this ith (time) I will cause it to rain a very Kabad hail, such as has not been in Matzarayam since the yawam (day) it was founded even until now.

Now therefore command that all of your livestock and all that you have in the shadah (field) be brought into shelter. Every adam (man) and animal that is found in the shadah (field), and isn't brought bayath (home), the hail shall yarad (come) down on them, and they shall mawath (die)."'
Those who feared the dabar (word) of Yahawah among the ibad (servants) of Paraih made their ibad (servants) and their livestock flee into the bayath (houses).
Whoever didn't respect the dabar (word) of Yahawah left his ibad (servants) and his livestock in the shadah (field).

Yahawah said to Mashah, "natah (stretch) out your yad (hand) toward the sky, that there may be hail in all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, on adam (man), and on animal, and on every herb of the shadah (field), throughout the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.

Mashah stretched out his matah (rod) toward the shamayam (heavens), and Yahawah sent qawal (thunder), hail, and lightning flashed down to the aratz (earth). Yahawah rained hail on the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
So there was very severe hail, and lightning mixed with the hail, such as had not been in all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam since it became a gaway (nation).

The hail struck throughout all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam all that was in the shadah (field), both adam (man) and animal; and the hail struck every herb of the shadah (field), and broke every itz (tree) of the shadah (field).
Only in the aratz (land) of Gashan, where the children of Yasharaal (Israel) were, there was no hail.
Paraih sent, and called for Mashah and Aharawan, and said to them, "I have sinned this paim (time). Yahawah is tzadayaq (righteous), and I and my im (people) are rashai (wicked).
Pray to Yahawah; for there has been rab (enough) of alahayam (mighty) qawal (thunderings) and hail. I will let you shalach (go), and you shall imad (stay) no longer.

Mashah said to him, "As soon as I have gone out of the Iyar, I will spread abroad my kap (hands) to Yahawah. The qawal (thunders) shall chadal (cease), neither shall there be any more hail; that you may yadai (know) that the aratz (earth) is yahawah (yahweh's).
But as for you and your ibad (servants), I yadai (know) that you don't yet yaraa (fear) Yahawah Alahayam.
The flax and the barley were struck, for the barley was in the ear, and the flax was in bloom.
But the wheat and the spelt were not struck, for they had not Apayal up.
Mashah went out of the Iyar from Paraih, and spread abroad his kap (hands) to Yahawah; and the qawal (thunders) and hail ceased, and the rain was not poured on the aratz (earth).
When Paraih saw that the rain and the hail and the qawal (thunders) were ceased, he sinned yet more, and hardened his lab (heart), he and his ibad (servants).
The lab (heart) of Paraih was hardened, and he didn't let the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shalach (go), just as Yahawah had spoken yad (through) Mashah.
Yahawah said to Mashah, "bawaa (go) in to Paraih, for I have hardened his lab (heart), and the lab (heart) of his ibad (servants), that I may show these my awath (signs) in their qarab (midst),

and that you may tell in the hearing of your ban (son), and of your ban (son's) ban (son), what things I have done to Matzarayam, and my awath (signs) which I have done among them; that you may yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Mashah and Aharawan went in to Paraih, and said to him, "This is what Yahawah, the Alahayam of the ibaray (hebrews), amar (says): ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself panayam (before) me? Let my im (people) shalach (go), that they may ibad (serve) me.
Or else, if you refuse to let my im (people) shalach (go), behold, tomorrow I will bawaa (bring) locusts into your country,

and they shall cover the surface of the aratz (earth), so that one won't be yakal (able) to raah (see) the aratz (earth). They shall akal (eat) the yathar (residue) of that which has palayatah (escaped), which shaar (remains) to you from the hail, and shall akal (eat) every itz (tree) which grows for you out of the shadah (field).

Your bayath (houses) shall be filled, and the bayath (houses) of all your ibad (servants), and the bayath (houses) of all the Matzarayam (Egyptians); as neither your abawath (fathers) nor your abawath (fathers)' abawath (fathers) have seen, since the yawam (day) that they were on the adamah (earth) to this yawam (day).'" He turned, and went out from Paraih.

Paraih ibad (servants) said to him, "How long will this mawaqash (man) be a snare to us? Let the men shalach (go), that they may ibad (serve) Yahawah, their Alahayam. Don't you yet yadai (know) that Matzarayam is destroyed?
Mashah and Aharawan were brought again to Paraih, and he said to them, "yalak (go), ibad (serve) Yahawah your Alahayam; but who are those who will halak (go)?

Mashah said, "We will yalak (go) with our nair (young) and with our zaqan (old); with our ban (sons) and with our bath (daughters), with our flocks and with our herds will we yalak (go); for we must hold a chag (feast) to Yahawah.
He said to them, "Yahawah be with you if I will let you shalach (go) with your little ones! raah (see), rai (evil) is clearly before your panayam (faces).
Not so! yalak (go) now you who are men, and ibad (serve) Yahawah; for that is what you desire!" They were driven out from Paraih panayam (presence).

Yahawah said to Mashah, "natah (stretch) out your yad (hand) over the aratz (land) of Matzarayam for the locusts, that they may ilah (come) up on the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and akal (eat) every herb of the aratz (land), even all that the hail has shaar (left).

Mashah stretched out his matah (rod) over the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and Yahawah brought an qadayam (east) rawach (wind) on the aratz (land) all that yawam (day), and all the layal (night); and when it was baqar (morning), the qadayam (east) rawach (wind) brought the locusts.

The locusts went up over all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and rested in all the borders of Matzarayam. They were very Kabad. panayam (before) them Kan were no such locusts as they, neither achar (after) them shall be such.

For they covered the surface of the whole aratz (earth), so that the aratz (land) was darkened, and they ate every herb of the aratz (land), and all the fruit of the itz (trees) which the hail had yathar (left). There remained nothing green, either itz (tree) or herb of the shadah (field), through all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
Then Paraih called for Mashah and Aharawan in haste, and he said, "I have sinned against Yahawah your Alahayam, and against you.
Now therefore please nashaa (forgive) my chataah (sin) again, and pray to Yahawah your Alahayam, that he may also sawar (take) away from me this mawath (death).
He went out from Paraih, and prayed to Yahawah.

Yahawah turned an maad (exceeding) chazaq (strong) yam (west) rawach (wind), which took up the locusts, and drove them into the Red yam (sea). There remained not one locust in all the borders of Matzarayam.
But Yahawah hardened Paraih lab (heart), and he didn't let the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shalach (go).
Yahawah said to Mashah, "natah (stretch) out your yad (hand) toward the sky, that there may be chashak (darkness) over the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, even chashak (darkness) which may be felt.
Mashah stretched out his yad (hand) toward the sky, and there was a apalah (thick) chashak (darkness) in all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam shalawash (three) yawam (days).

They didn't raah (see) one ach (another), neither did anyone qawam (rise) from his place for shalawash (three) yawam (days); but all the children of Yasharaal (Israel) had awar (light) in their mawashab (dwellings).
Paraih called to Mashah, and said, "yalak (go), ibad (serve) Yahawah. Only let your flocks and your herds stay behind. Let your little ones also yalak (go) with you.
Mashah said, "You must also nathan (give) into our yad (hand) ishah (sacrifices) and burnt ilah (offerings), that we may ishah (sacrifice) to Yahawah our Alahayam.

Our livestock also shall yalak (go) with us. Not a hoof shall be shaar (left) behind, for of it we must take to ibad (serve) Yahawah our Alahayam; and we don't yadai (know) with what we must ibad (serve) Yahawah, until we bawaa (come) there.
But Yahawah hardened Paraih lab (heart), and he wouldn't let them shalach (go).
Paraih said to him, "yalak (get) away from me! Be careful to raah (see) my panayam (face) no more; for in the yawam (day) you raah (see) my panayam (face) you shall mawath (die)!
Mashah said, "You have spoken Kan. I will raah (see) your panayam (face) again no more.

Yahawah said to Mashah, "Yet one nagai (plague) more will I bawaa (bring) on Paraih, and on Matzarayam; afterwards he will let you shalach (go). When he shalach (lets) you go, he will surely thrust you out altogether.
dabar (speak) now in the ears of the im (people), and let them shaal (ask) every ayash (man) of his neighbor, and every ashah (woman) of her neighbor, jewels of kasap (silver), and jewels of gold.

Yahawah gave the im (people) favor in the iyan (sight) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians). Moreover the ayash (man) Mashah was very gadawal (great) in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, in the iyan (sight) of Paraih ibad (servants), and in the iyan (sight) of the im (people).
Mashah said, "This is what Yahawah amar (says): ‘About layal (midnight) I will yatzaa (go) out into the midst of Matzarayam,

and all the firstborn in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam shall mawath (die), from the firstborn of Paraih who yashab (sits) on his kasaa (throne), even to the firstborn of the female servant who is achar (behind) the mill; and all the firstborn of livestock.
There shall be a gadawal (great) cry throughout all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, such as there has not been, nor shall be any more.

But against any of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) a dog won't even bark or move its lashawan (tongue), against ayash (man) or animal; that you may yadai (know) that Yahawah makes a distinction between the Matzarayam (Egyptians) and Yasharaal (Israel).

All these your ibad (servants) shall yarad (come) down to me, and bow down themselves to me, saying, "yatzaa (get) out, with all the im (people) who ragal (follow) you;" and achar (after) that I will yatzaa (go) out.'" He went out from Paraih in hot ap (anger).
Yahawah said to Mashah, "Paraih won't listen to you, that my mawapath (wonders) may be multiplied in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.

Mashah and Aharawan did all these mawapath (wonders) panayam (before) Paraih, and Yahawah hardened Paraih lab (heart), and he didn't let the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shalach (go) out of his aratz (land).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah and Aharawan in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, saying,
"This chadash (month) shall be to you the raash (beginning) of chadash (months). It shall be the raashawan (first) chadash (month) of the Shanah to you.

dabar (speak) to all the idah (congregation) of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, ‘On the tenth day of this chadash (month), they shall take to them every ayash (man) a lamb, according to their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), a lamb for a bayath (household);

and if the bayath (household) is too little for a lamb, then he and his Shakan qarawab (next) to his bayath (house) shall take makasah (one) according to the number of the napash (souls); according to ayash (what) everyone can eat you shall make your count for the lamb.
Your lamb shall be thamayam (without) blemish, a zakar (male) a Shanah old. You shall take it from the sheep, or from the goats:
and you shall keep it until the fourteenth yawam (day) of the same chadash (month); and the whole qahal (assembly) of the idah (congregation) of Yasharaal (Israel) shall kill it at evening.
They shall take some of the dam (blood), and nathan (put) it on the shanayam (two) doorposts and on the lintel, on the bayath (houses) in which they shall akal (eat) it.
They shall akal (eat) the flesh in that layal (night), roasted with ash (fire), and unleavened matzah (bread). They shall akal (eat) it with bitter herbs.
Don't akal (eat) it raw, nor boiled at all with mayam (water), but roasted with ash (fire); with its raash (head), its legs and its inner qarab (parts).
You shall let nothing of it yathar (remain) until the baqar (morning); but that which yathar (remains) of it until the baqar (morning) you shall sharap (burn) with ash (fire).

This is how you shall akal (eat) it: with your belt on your waist, your shoes on your feet, and your maqal (staff) in your yad (hand); and you shall akal (eat) it in haste: it is yahawah (yahweh's) pasach (passover).

For I will ibar (go) through the aratz (land) of Matzarayam in that layal (night), and will strike all the firstborn in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, both adam (man) and animal. Against all the Alahayam of Matzarayam I will ishah (execute) shapat (judgments): I am Yahawah.

The dam (blood) shall be to you for a awath (token) on the bayath (houses) where you are: and when I raah (see) the dam (blood), I will Pasach over you, and there shall no nagap (plague) be on you to mashachayath (destroy) you, when I strike the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.

This yawam (day) shall be to you for a zakarawan (memorial), and you shall keep it a chag (feast) to Yahawah: throughout your dawar (generations) you shall keep it a feast by an chaqah (ordinance) iwalam (forever).

"‘shabai (seven) yawam (days) you shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread); even the raashawan (first) yawam (day) you shall shabath (put) away yeast out of your bayath (houses), for whoever akal (eats) leavened chamatz (bread) from the raashawan (first) yawam (day) until the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from Yasharaal (Israel).

In the raashawan (first) yawam (day) there shall be to you a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation), and in the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation); no kind of malaakah (work) shall be done in them, except that which every napash (man) must akal (eat), that only may be done by you.

You shall shamar (observe) the feast of unleavened matzah (bread); for in this same yawam (day) have I brought your tzabaa (armies) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam: therefore you shall shamar (observe) this yawam (day) throughout your dawar (generations) by an chaqah (ordinance) iwalam (forever).

In the raashawan (first) month, on the fourteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month) at evening, you shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread), until the isharayam (twenty) achad (first) yawam (day) of the chadash (month) at evening.

There shall be no yeast found in your bayath (houses) for shabai (seven) yawam (days), for whoever akal (eats) that which is leavened, that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from the idah (congregation) of Yasharaal (Israel), whether he be a foreigner, or azarach (one) who is born in the aratz (land).
You shall akal (eat) nothing leavened. In all your habitations you shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread).'
Then Mashah called for all the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel), and said to them, "Draw out, and take lambs according to your mashapachah (families), and kill the pasach (passover).

You shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the dam (blood) that is in the basin, and nagai (strike) the lintel and the shanayam (two) doorposts with the dam (blood) that is in the basin; and ayash (none) of you shall yatzaa (go) out of the door of his bayath (house) until the baqar (morning).

For Yahawah will ibar (pass) through to nagap (strike) the Matzarayam (Egyptians); and when he raah (see) the dam (blood) on the lintel, and on the shanayam (two) doorposts, Yahawah will Pasach over the door, and will not allow the destroyer to bawaa (come) in to your bayath (houses) to nagap (strike) you.
You shall shamar (observe) this thing for an chaq (ordinance) to you and to your ban (sons) iwalam (forever).
It shall happen when you have bawaa (come) to the aratz (land) which Yahawah will nathan (give) you, according as he has promised, that you shall shamar (keep) this ibadah (service).
It will happen, when your children ask you, ‘What do you mean by this ibadah (service)?'

that you shall amar (say), ‘It is the zabach (sacrifice) of yahawah (yahweh's) pasach (passover), who Pasach over the bayath (houses) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) in Matzarayam, when he struck the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and spared our bayath (houses).'" The im (people) bowed their qadad (heads) and worshiped.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) went and did so; as Yahawah had tzawah (commanded) Mashah and Aharawan, so they did.

It happened at chatzay (midnight), that Yahawah struck all the firstborn in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, from the firstborn of Paraih who sat on his kasaa (throne) to the firstborn of the Shabay who was in the bayath (dungeon); and all the firstborn of livestock.

Paraih rose up in the layal (night), he, and all his ibad (servants), and all the Matzarayam (Egyptians); and there was a gadawal (great) cry in Matzarayam, for there was not a bayath (house) where there was not one mawath (dead).

He called for Mashah and Aharawan by layal (night), and said, "qawam (rise) up, yatzaa (get) out from among my im (people), both you and the children of Yasharaal (Israel); and yalak (go), ibad (serve) Yahawah, as you have said!
Take both your flocks and your herds, as you have said, and be gone; and barak (bless) me also!
The Matzarayam (Egyptians) were chazaq (urgent) with the im (people), to shalach (send) them out of the aratz (land) in haste, for they said, "We are all mawath (dead) men.
The im (people) took their dough before it was leavened, their kneading troughs being bound up in their clothes on their shoulders.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) did according to the dabar (word) of Mashah; and they asked of the Matzarayam (Egyptians) jewels of kasap (silver), and jewels of gold, and clothing.
Yahawah gave the im (people) favor in the iyan (sight) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), so that they let them have what they asked. They despoiled the Matzarayam (Egyptians).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) traveled from Raimasas to Sakawath, about shash (six) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) on ragalay (foot) who were men, bad (besides) tap (children).
A irab (mixed) rab (multitude) went up also with them, with flocks, herds, and even very Kabad livestock.

They baked unleavened cakes of the dough which they brought out of Matzarayam; for it wasn't leavened, because they were thrust out of Matzarayam, and couldn't wait, neither had they prepared for themselves any food.
Now the time that the children of Yasharaal (Israel) lived in Matzarayam was arabai (four) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah.

It happened at the end of arabai (four) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah, even the same yawam (day) it happened, that all the tzabaa (armies) of Yahawah went out from the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.

It is a layal (night) to be much observed to Yahawah for bringing them out from the aratz (land) of Matzarayam. This is that layal (night) of Yahawah, to be much observed of all the children of Yasharaal (Israel) throughout their dawar (generations).
Yahawah said to Mashah and Aharawan, "This is the chaqah (ordinance) of the pasach (passover). No foreigner shall akal (eat) of it,
but every ayash (man's) ibad (servant) who is maqanah (bought) for kasap (money), when you have circumcised him, then shall he akal (eat) of it.
A foreigner and a hired shakayar (servant) shall not akal (eat) of it.
In one bayath (house) shall it be eaten; you shall not yatzaa (carry) out anything of the flesh abroad out of the bayath (house); neither shall you shabar (break) a itzam (bone) of it.
All the idah (congregation) of Yasharaal (Israel) shall ishah (keep) it.

When a stranger shall live as a foreigner with you, and will ishah (keep) the pasach (passover) to Yahawah, let all his zakar (males) be circumcised, and then let him qarab (come) near and ishah (keep) it; and he shall be as azarach (one) who is born in the aratz (land): but no Iral person shall akal (eat) of it.
One thawarah (law) shall be to him who is born at home, and to the stranger who lives as a foreigner among you.
All the children of Yasharaal (Israel) did so. As Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah and Aharawan, so they did.
It happened the same yawam (day), that Yahawah brought the children of Yasharaal (Israel) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam by their tzabaa (armies).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"qadash (sanctify) to me all of the firstborn, whatever opens the womb among the children of Yasharaal (Israel), both of adam (man) and of animal. It is mine.

Mashah said to the im (people), "zakar (remember) this yawam (day), in which you came out from Matzarayam, out of the bayath (house) of ibad (bondage); for by chazaq (strength) of yad (hand) Yahawah brought you out from this place. No leavened chamatz (bread) shall be eaten.
This yawam (day) you yatzaa (go) out in the chadash (month) Abib.

It shall be, when Yahawah shall bawaa (bring) you into the aratz (land) of the Kanainay (Canaanite), and the Chathay (Hittite), and the Amaray (Amorite), and the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite), which he swore to your abawath (fathers) to nathan (give) you, a aratz (land) flowing with milk and honey, that you shall ibad (keep) this ibadah (service) in this chadash (month).
shabai (seven) yawam (days) you shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread), and in the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) shall be a chag (feast) to Yahawah.
Unleavened matzah (bread) shall be eaten throughout the shabai (seven) yawam (days); and no leavened chamatz (bread) shall be seen with you, neither shall yeast be seen with you, in all your borders.
You shall nagad (tell) your ban (son) in that yawam (day), saying, ‘It is because of that which Yahawah did for me when I came out of Matzarayam.'

It shall be for a awath (sign) to you on your yad (hand), and for a zakarawan (memorial) between your iyan (eyes), that the thawarah (law) of Yahawah may be in your pah (mouth); for with a chazaq (strong) yad (hand) Yahawah has brought you out of Matzarayam.
You shall therefore shamar (keep) this chaqah (ordinance) in its mawaid (season) from yawam (year) to yawam (year).
"It shall be, when Yahawah shall bawaa (bring) you into the aratz (land) of the Kanainay (Canaanite), as he swore to you and to your abawath (fathers), and shall nathan (give) it you,
that you shall ibar (set) apart to Yahawah all that opens the womb, and every firstborn which you have that comes from an animal. The zakar (males) shall be yahawah (yahweh's).

Every firstborn of a donkey you shall padah (redeem) with a lamb; and if you will not padah (redeem) it, then you shall break its neck; and you shall padah (redeem) all the firstborn of adam (man) among your ban (sons).

It shall be, when your ban (son) shaal (asks) you in time to come, saying, ‘What is this?' that you shall amar (tell) him, ‘By chazaq (strength) of yad (hand) Yahawah brought us out from Matzarayam, from the bayath (house) of ibad (bondage);

and it happened, when Paraih would hardly let us shalach (go), that Yahawah killed all the firstborn in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, both the firstborn of adam (man), and the firstborn of animal. Therefore I zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah all that opens the womb, being zakar (males); but all the firstborn of my ban (sons) I padah (redeem).'
It shall be for a awath (sign) on your yad (hand), and for symbols between your iyan (eyes): for by chazaq (strength) of yad (hand) Yahawah brought us out of Matzarayam.

It happened, when Paraih had let the im (people) shalach (go), that Alahayam didn't lead them by the darak (way) of the aratz (land) of the Palashathay (Philistines), although that was qarawab (near); for Alahayam said, "Lest perhaps the im (people) change their minds when they raah (see) war, and they shawab (turn back / repent) to Matzarayam;

but Alahayam led the im (people) around by the darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness) by the Red yam (sea); and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) went up armed out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.

Mashah took the itzam (bones) of Yawasap with him, for he had made the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shabai (swear), saying, "Alahayam will paqad (surely) paqad (visit) you, and you shall ilah (carry) up my itzam (bones) ilah (away) from here with you.
They took their nasai (journey) from Sakawath, and encamped in Atham, in the edge of the madabar (wilderness).

Yahawah went panayam (before) them by yawamam (day) in a pillar of cloud, to lead them on their darak (way), and by layal (night) in a pillar of ash (fire), to give them awar (light), that they might yalak (go) by yawamam (day) and by layal (night):
the pillar of cloud by yawamam (day), and the pillar of ash (fire) by layal (night), didn't depart from panayam (before) the im (people).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), that they shawab (turn back / repent) back and chanah (encamp) panayam (before) Payahachayarath, between Magadawal and the yam (sea), before Bailatzapawan Zephon. You shall chanah (encamp) opposite it by the yam (sea).
Paraih will amar (say) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘They are entangled in the aratz (land). The madabar (wilderness) has shut them in.'

I will chazaq (harden) Paraih lab (heart), and he will follow achar (after) them; and I will kabad (get) honor over Paraih, and over all his chayal (armies); and the Matzarayam (Egyptians) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah." They did so.

It was told the malak (king) of Matzarayam that the im (people) had fled; and the labab (heart) of Paraih and of his ibad (servants) was changed towards the im (people), and they said, "What is this we have done, that we have let Yasharaal (Israel) shalach (go) from serving us?
He prepared his chariot, and took his army with him;
and he took shash (six) maah (hundred) chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Matzarayam, and shalayash (captains) over all of them.

Yahawah hardened the lab (heart) of Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam, and he pursued achar (after) the children of Yasharaal (Israel); for the children of Yasharaal (Israel) went out with a high yad (hand).

The Matzarayam (Egyptians) pursued achar (after) them: all the horses and chariots of Paraih, his horsemen, and his chayal (army); and overtook them encamping by the yam (sea), beside Payahachayarath, panayam (before) Bailatzapawan Zephon.

When Paraih drew qarab (near), the children of Yasharaal (Israel) lifted up their iyan (eyes), and behold, the Matzarayam (Egyptians) were marching achar (after) them; and they were very yaraa (afraid). The children of Yasharaal (Israel) cried out to Yahawah.

They said to Mashah, "Because there were no qabar (graves) in Matzarayam, have you taken us away to mawath (die) in the madabar (wilderness)? Why have you treated us this way, to yatzaa (bring) us out of Matzarayam?

Isn't this the dabar (word) that we spoke to you in Matzarayam, saying, ‘Leave us chadal (alone), that we may ibad (serve) the Matzarayam (Egyptians)?' For it were tawab (better) for us to ibad (serve) the Matzarayam (Egyptians), than that we should mawath (die) in the madabar (wilderness).

Mashah said to the im (people), "Don't be yaraa (afraid). Stand still, and raah (see) the yashawaih (salvation) of Yahawah, which he will ishah (work) for you today: for the Matzarayam (Egyptians) whom you have seen today, you shall never raah (see) them again.
Yahawah will fight for you, and you shall be still.
Yahawah said to Mashah, "Why do you cry to me? dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), that they nasai (go) forward.

Lift up your matah (rod), and natah (stretch) out your yad (hand) over the yam (sea), and divide it: and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shall bawaa (go) into the midst of the yam (sea) on dry yabashah (dry land).

I, behold, I will chazaq (harden) the lab (hearts) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and they shall bawaa (go) in after them: and I will kabad (get) myself honor over Paraih, and over all his chayal (armies), over his chariots, and over his horsemen.
The Matzarayam (Egyptians) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I have gotten myself honor over Paraih, over his chariots, and over his horsemen.

The malaak (angel) of Alahayam, who went panayam (before) the machanah (camp) of Yasharaal (Israel), moved and went achar (behind) them; and the pillar of cloud moved from panayam (before) them, and stood achar (behind) them.

It came between the machanah (camp) of Matzarayam and the machanah (camp) of Yasharaal (Israel); and there was the cloud and the chashak (darkness), yet gave it awar (light) by layal (night): and the one didn't qarab (come) near the other all the layal (night).

Mashah stretched out his yad (hand) over the yam (sea), and Yahawah caused the yam (sea) to yalak (go) back by a iz (strong) qadayam (east) rawach (wind) all the layal (night), and made the yam (sea) charabah (dry) land, and the mayam (waters) were divided.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) went into the midst of the yam (sea) on the yabashah (dry land) ground, and the mayam (waters) were a wall to them on their right yamayan (hand), and on their shamaawal (left).
The Matzarayam (Egyptians) pursued, and went in achar (after) them into the midst of the yam (sea): all of Paraih horses, his chariots, and his horsemen.

It happened in the baqar (morning) watch, that Yahawah looked out on the Matzarayam (Egyptian) machanah (army) through the pillar of ash (fire) and of cloud, and confused the Matzarayam (Egyptian) machanah (army).

He took off their chariot wheels, and they drove them heavily; so that the Matzarayam (Egyptians) said, "Let's flee from the panayam (face) of Yasharaal (Israel), for Yahawah fights for them against the Matzarayam (Egyptians)!

Yahawah said to Mashah, "natah (stretch) out your yad (hand) over the yam (sea), that the mayam (waters) may shawab (turn back / repent) again on the Matzarayam (Egyptians), on their chariots, and on their horsemen.

Mashah stretched out his yad (hand) over the yam (sea), and the yam (sea) returned to its ayathan (strength) when the baqar (morning) appeared; and the Matzarayam (Egyptians) fled qaraah (against) it. Yahawah overthrew the Matzarayam (Egyptians) in the midst of the yam (sea).
The mayam (waters) returned, and covered the chariots and the horsemen, even all Paraih chayal (army) that went in achar (after) them into the yam (sea). There remained not so much as one of them.

But the children of Yasharaal (Israel) walked on yabashah (dry land) thawak (land) in the midst of the yam (sea), and the mayam (waters) were a wall to them on their right yamayan (hand), and on their shamaawal (left).

Thus Yahawah saved Yasharaal (Israel) that yawam (day) out of the yad (hand) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians); and Yasharaal (Israel) saw the Matzarayam (Egyptians) mawath (dead) on the shapah (seashore).

Yasharaal (Israel) saw the gadawal (great) yad (work) which Yahawah did to the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and the im (people) feared Yahawah; and they believed in Yahawah, and in his ibad (servant) Mashah.

Then Mashah and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) sang this song to Yahawah, and said, "I will shayar (sing) to Yahawah, for he has triumphed gloriously. The horse and his rider he has thrown into the yam (sea).
Yah is my iz (strength) and song. He has become my yashawaih (salvation). This is my Al, and I will praise him; my ab (father's) Alahayam, and I will exalt him.
Yahawah is a ayash (man) of war. Yahawah is his sham (name).
He has cast Paraih chariots and his chayal (army) into the yam (sea). His chosen shalayash (captains) are sunk in the Red yam (sea).
The deeps cover them. They went down into the depths like a aban (stone).
Your right yamayan (hand), Yahawah, is glorious in kach (power). Your right yamayan (hand), Yahawah, dashes the ayab (enemy) in pieces.
In the greatness of your excellency, you haras (overthrow) those who qawam (rise) up against you. You shalach (send) forth your charawan (wrath). It akal (consumes) them as stubble.
With the rawach (blast) of your ap (nostrils), the mayam (waters) were piled up. The nazal (floods) stood natzab (upright) as a heap. The deeps were congealed in the lab (heart) of the yam (sea).

The ayab (enemy) said, ‘I will pursue. I will overtake. I will divide the spoil. My napash (desire) shall be satisfied on them. I will draw my charab (sword), my yad (hand) shall yarash (destroy) them.'
You blew with your rawach (wind). The yam (sea) covered them. They sank like lead in the adayar (mighty) mayam (waters).
Who is like you, Yahawah, among the Al? Who is like you, glorious in qadash (holiness), fearful in thahalah (praises), doing palaa (wonders)?
You stretched out your right yamayan (hand). The aratz (earth) swallowed them.
"You, in your loving chasad (kindness), have led the im (people) that you have redeemed. You have guided them in your iz (strength) to your qadash (holy) Nawah.
The im (peoples) have heard. They tremble. Pangs have taken achaz (hold) on the yashab (inhabitants) of Palashath.
Then the Alawap of Adam were dismayed. Trembling achaz (takes) hold of the ayal (mighty) men of Mawaab. All the yashab (inhabitants) of Kanain are melted away.

ayamah (terror) and pachad (dread) napal (falls) on them. By the greatness of your zarawai (arm) they are as still as a aban (stone)— until your im (people) ibar (pass) over, Yahawah, until the im (people) ibar (pass) over who you have purchased.

You shall bawaa (bring) them in, and plant them in the har (mountain) of your nachalah (inheritance), the place, Yahawah, which you have made for yourself to yashab (dwell) in; the maqadash (sanctuary), Adanay, which your yad (hands) have established.
Yahawah shall malak (reign) id (forever) and ever.

For the horses of Paraih went in with his chariots and with his horsemen into the yam (sea), and Yahawah brought shawab (turn back / repent) the mayam (waters) of the yam (sea) on them; but the children of Yasharaal (Israel) walked on yabashah (dry land) thawak (land) in the midst of the yam (sea).
Marayam the prophetess, the achawath (sister) of Aharawan, took a tambourine in her yad (hand); and all the women went out achar (after) her with tambourines and with dances.
Marayam answered them, "shayar (sing) to Yahawah, for he has triumphed gloriously. The horse and his rider he has thrown into the yam (sea).

Mashah led Yasharaal (Israel) nasai (onward) from the Red yam (sea), and they went out into the madabar (wilderness) of Shawar; and they went shalawash (three) yawam (days) in the madabar (wilderness), and found no mayam (water).
When they came to Marah, they couldn't drink from the mayam (waters) of Marah, for they were Mar. Therefore its sham (name) was called Marah.
The im (people) murmured against Mashah, saying, "What shall we drink?

Then he cried to Yahawah. Yahawah showed him a itz (tree), and he threw it into the mayam (waters), and the mayam (waters) were made sweet. There he made a chaq (statute) and an mashapat (ordinance) for them, and there he tested them;

and he said, "If you will diligently listen to the qawal (voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam, and will do that which is yashar (right) in his azan (eyes), and will pay attention to his matzawah (commandments), and shamar (keep) all his chaq (statutes), I will shawam (put) none of the diseases on you, which I have shawam (put) on the Matzarayam (Egyptians); for I am Yahawah who heals you.
They came to Ayalam, where there were shanayam (twelve) springs of mayam (water), and shabaiyam (seventy) palm trees: and they encamped there by the mayam (waters).

They took their nasai (journey) from Ayalam, and all the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) came to the madabar (wilderness) of sayan (sin), which is between Ayalam and Sayanay, on the fifteenth yawam (day) of the shanay (second) chadash (month) yatzaa (after) their departing out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
The whole idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) murmured against Mashah and against Aharawan in the madabar (wilderness);

and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) said to them, "We wish that we had died by the yad (hand) of Yahawah in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, when we sat by the meat pots, when we ate our fill of lacham (bread), for you have brought us out into this madabar (wilderness), to mawath (kill) this whole qahal (assembly) with hunger.

Then Yahawah said to Mashah, "Behold, I will rain lacham (bread) from the sky for you, and the im (people) shall yatzaa (go) out and gather a day's dabar (portion) every yawam (day), that I may test them, whether they will yalak (walk) in my thawarah (law), or not.
It shall come to pass on the shashay (sixth) yawam (day), that they shall kawan (prepare) that which they bawaa (bring) in, and it shall be mashanah (twice) as much as they gather yawam (daily).
Mashah and Aharawan said to all the children of Yasharaal (Israel), "At evening, then you shall yadai (know) that Yahawah has brought you out from the aratz (land) of Matzarayam;
and in the baqar (morning), then you shall raah (see) the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah; because he hears your murmurings against Yahawah. Who are we, that you lawan (murmur) against us?

Mashah said, "Now Yahawah shall nathan (give) you meat to akal (eat) in the evening, and in the baqar (morning) lacham (bread) to satisfy you; because Yahawah hears your murmurings which you lawan (murmur) against him. And who are we? Your murmurings are not against us, but against Yahawah.
Mashah said to Aharawan, "amar (tell) all the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘qarab (come) near panayam (before) Yahawah, for he has heard your murmurings.'

It happened, as Aharawan spoke to the whole idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), that they looked toward the madabar (wilderness), and behold, the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah raah (see) in the cloud.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"I have heard the murmurings of the children of Yasharaal (Israel). dabar (speak) to them, saying, ‘At evening you shall akal (eat) meat, and in the baqar (morning) you shall be filled with lacham (bread): and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah your Alahayam.'
It happened at evening that quail came up and covered the machanah (camp); and in the baqar (morning) the dew shakabah (lay) around the machanah (camp).
When the dew that shakabah (lay) had gone, behold, on the surface of the madabar (wilderness) was a Daq round thing, Daq as the frost on the aratz (ground).

When the children of Yasharaal (Israel) saw it, they said one to ach (another), "What is it?" For they didn't yadai (know) what it was. Mashah said to them, "It is the lacham (bread) which Yahawah has given you to eat.

This is the thing which Yahawah has tzawah (commanded): "Gather of it everyone according to his eating; an omer a galagalath (head), according to the number of your napash (persons), you shall take it, every ayash (man) for those who are in his ahal (tent).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) did so, and gathered some more, some less.
