When they measured it with an omer, he who gathered much had nothing over, and he who gathered little had no lack. They gathered every ayash (man) according to his eating.
Mashah said to them, "Let no one yathar (leave) of it until the baqar (morning).
Notwithstanding they didn't listen to Mashah, but some of them yathar (left) of it until the baqar (morning), and it bred worms, and became foul: and Mashah was qatzap (angry) with them.
They gathered it baqar (morning) by morning, everyone according to his eating. When the shamash (sun) grew hot, it melted.

It happened that on the shashay (sixth) yawam (day) they gathered mashanah (twice) as much lacham (bread), shanayam (two) omers for achad (each) one, and all the nashayaa (rulers) of the idah (congregation) came and told Mashah.

He said to them, "This is that which Yahawah has spoken, ‘Tomorrow is a solemn shabathawan (rest), a qadash (holy) shabath (sabbath) to Yahawah. Bake that which you want to bake, and boil that which you want to boil; and all that remains over yanach (lay) up for yourselves to be kept until the baqar (morning).'
They laid it up until the baqar (morning), as Mashah asked, and it didn't become foul, neither was there any worm in it.
Mashah said, "akal (eat) that today, for today is a shabath (sabbath) to Yahawah. Today you shall not matzaa (find) it in the shadah (field).
shash (six) yawam (days) you shall gather it, but on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) is the shabath (sabbath). In it there shall be none.
It happened on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that some of the im (people) went out to gather, and they found none.
Yahawah said to Mashah, "How long do you refuse to shamar (keep) my matzawah (commandments) and my thawarah (laws)?

raah (see), because Yahawah has given you the shabath (sabbath), therefore he nathan (gives) you on the shashay (sixth) yawam (day) the lacham (bread) of yawam (two) days. Everyone stay in his place. Let no one yatzaa (go) out of his place on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day).
So the im (people) rested on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day).
The bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) called its sham (name) Manna, and it was like coriander zarai (seed), Laban; and its taim (taste) was like wafers with honey.

Mashah said, "This is the thing which Yahawah has tzawah (commanded), ‘Let an omer-full of it be kept throughout your dawar (generations), that they may raah (see) the lacham (bread) with which I fed you in the madabar (wilderness), when I brought you yatzaa (forth) from the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.'
Mashah said to Aharawan, "Take a pot, and nathan (put) an omer-full of manna in it, and yanach (lay) it up panayam (before) Yahawah, to be kept throughout your dawar (generations).
As Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah, so Aharawan laid it up panayam (before) the idawath (testimony), to be kept.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) ate the manna arabaiyam (forty) Shanah, until they came to an inhabited aratz (land). They ate the manna until they came to the borders of the aratz (land) of Kanain.
Now an omer is the ishayaray (tenth) part of an ephah.

All the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) traveled from the madabar (wilderness) of sayan (sin), by their journeys, according to yahawah (yahweh's) commandment, and encamped in Rapayadayam; but there was no mayam (water) for the im (people) to drink.
Therefore the im (people) quarreled with Mashah, and said, "nathan (give) us mayam (water) to drink." Mashah said to them, "Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you test Yahawah?

The im (people) were thirsty for mayam (water) there; and the im (people) murmured against Mashah, and said, "Why have you brought us up out of Matzarayam, to mawath (kill) us, our children, and our livestock with thirst?
Mashah cried to Yahawah, saying, "What shall I do with these im (people)? They are Mait ready to saqal (stone) me.

Yahawah said to Mashah, "Walk on panayam (before) the im (people), and take the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) with you, and take the matah (rod) in your yad (hand) with which you struck the Nile, and halak (go).

Behold, I will imad (stand) panayam (before) you there on the tzawar (rock) in Charab. You shall strike the tzawar (rock), and mayam (water) will yatzaa (come) out of it, that the im (people) may drink." Mashah did so in the iyan (sight) of the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel).
He called the sham (name) of the place Masah, and Marayabah, because the children of Yasharaal (Israel) quarreled, and because they tested Yahawah, saying, "Is Yahawah qarab (among) us, or not?
Then Imalaq came and fought with Yasharaal (Israel) in Rapayadayam.
Mashah said to Yahawashawai, "Choose men for us, and go out, fight with Imalaq. Tomorrow I will natzab (stand) on the raash (top) of the Gabaih with alahayam (god's) matah (rod) in my yad (hand).
So Yahawashawai did as Mashah had told him, and fought with Imalaq; and Mashah, Aharawan, and Chawar went up to the raash (top) of the Gabaih.
It happened, when Mashah held up his yad (hand), that Yasharaal (Israel) prevailed; and when he let down his yad (hand), Imalaq prevailed.

But Mashah' yad (hands) were Kabad; and they took a aban (stone), and shawam (put) it under him, and he sat on it. Aharawan and Chawar held up his yad (hands), the one on the one side, and the other on the other side. His yad (hands) were amawanah (steady) until sunset.
Yahawashawai defeated Imalaq and his im (people) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).

Yahawah said to Mashah, "kathab (write) this for a zakarawan (memorial) in a book, and shawam (rehearse) it in the ears of Yahawashawai: that I will machah (utterly) machah (blot) out the zakar (memory) of Imalaq from under the sky.
Mashah built an mazabach (altar), and called its sham (name) Yahawah our Banner.
He said, "Yah has sworn: ‘Yahawah will have war with Imalaq from dawar (generation) to dawar (generation).'

Now Yatharaw, the kahan (priest) of Madayan, Mashah' father-in-law, heard of all that Alahayam had done for Mashah, and for Yasharaal (Israel) his im (people), how that Yahawah had brought Yasharaal (Israel) out of Matzarayam.
Yatharaw, Mashah' father-in-law, received Tzaparah, Mashah' ashah (wife), achar (after) he had sent her away,
and her shanayam (two) ban (sons). The sham (name) of one son was Garasham, for Moses said, "I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign aratz (land)".
The sham (name) of the other was Alayaizar, for he said, "My ab (father's) Alahayam was my help and delivered me from Paraih charab (sword).
Yatharaw, Mashah' father-in-law, came with his ban (sons) and his ashah (wife) to Mashah into the madabar (wilderness) where he was encamped, at the har (mountain) of Alahayam.
He said to Mashah, "I, your father-in-law Yatharaw, have bawaa (come) to you with your ashah (wife), and her shanayam (two) ban (sons) with her.
Mashah went out to qaraah (meet) his father-in-law, and bowed and kissed him. They asked ayash (each) other of their shalawam (welfare), and they came into the ahal (tent).

Mashah told his father-in-law all that Yahawah had done to Paraih and to the Matzarayam (Egyptians) for Yasharaal sake, all the hardships that had matzaa (come) on them on the darak (way), and how Yahawah delivered them.
Yatharaw rejoiced for all the goodness which Yahawah had done to Yasharaal (Israel), in that he had delivered them out of the yad (hand) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians).

Yatharaw said, "Blessed be Yahawah, who has delivered you out of the yad (hand) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and out of the yad (hand) of Paraih; who has delivered the im (people) from under the yad (hand) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians).
Now I yadai (know) that Yahawah is greater than all Alahayam dabar (because) of the thing in which they dealt arrogantly against them.

Yatharaw, Mashah' father-in-law, took a burnt ilah (offering) and zabach (sacrifices) for Alahayam. Aharawan came with all of the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel), to akal (eat) lacham (bread) with Mashah' father-in-law panayam (before) Alahayam.
It happened on the next macharath (day), that Mashah sat to shapat (judge) the im (people), and the im (people) stood around Mashah from the baqar (morning) to the evening.

When Mashah' father-in-law saw all that he did to the im (people), he said, "dabar (what) is this thing that you do for the im (people)? Why do you yashab (sit) alone, and all the im (people) natzab (stand) around you from baqar (morning) to evening?
Mashah said to his father-in-law, "Because the im (people) bawaa (come) to me to inquire of Alahayam.

When they have a dabar (matter), they bawaa (come) to me, and I shapat (judge) between a ayash (man) and his neighbor, and I yadai (make) them know the chaq (statutes) of Alahayam, and his thawarah (laws).
Mashah' father-in-law said to him, "The thing that you do is not tawab (good).
You will surely wear away, both you, and this im (people) that is with you; for the thing is too Kabad for you. You are not yakal (able) to ishah (perform) it yourself alone.
Listen now to my qawal (voice). I will give you yaitz (counsel), and Alahayam be with you. You represent the im (people) before Alahayam, and bawaa (bring) the dabar (causes) to Alahayam.
You shall teach them the chaq (statutes) and the thawarah (laws), and shall show them the darak (way) in which they must yalak (walk), and the maishah (work) that they must do.

Moreover you shall chazah (provide) out of all the im (people) chayal (able) men, such as yaraa (fear) Alahayam: men of truth, hating unjust gain; and shawam (place) such over them, to be shar (rulers) of alap (thousands), shar (rulers) of maah (hundreds), shar (rulers) of chamashayam (fifties), and shar (rulers) of ishar (tens).

Let them shapat (judge) the im (people) at all ith (times). It shall be that every gadawal (great) dabar (matter) they shall bawaa (bring) to you, but every qatan (small) dabar (matter) they shall shapat (judge) themselves. So shall it be easier for you, and they shall share the load with you.
If you will do this thing, and Alahayam tzawah (commands) you so, then you will be yakal (able) to imad (endure), and all of these im (people) also will bawaa (go) to their place in shalawam (peace).
So Mashah listened to the qawal (voice) of his father-in-law, and did all that he had said.

Mashah chose chayal (able) men out of all Yasharaal (Israel), and made them raash (heads) over the im (people), shar (rulers) of alap (thousands), shar (rulers) of maah (hundreds), shar (rulers) of chamashayam (fifties), and shar (rulers) of ishar (tens).
They judged the im (people) at all ith (times). They brought the Qashah dabar (causes) to Mashah, but every qatan (small) dabar (matter) they judged themselves.
Mashah let his father-in-law depart, and he went his aratz (way) into his own land.

In the shalayashay (third) chadash (month) after the children of Yasharaal (Israel) had gone out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, on that same yawam (day) they came into the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay.

When they had departed from Rapayadayam, and had bawaa (come) to the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay, they encamped in the madabar (wilderness); and there Yasharaal (Israel) encamped before the har (mountain).

Mashah went up to Alahayam, and Yahawah called to him out of the har (mountain), saying, "This is what you shall amar (tell) the bayath (house) of Yaiqab, and amar (tell) the children of Yasharaal (Israel):
‘You have seen what I did to the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and how I bore you on eagles' wings, and brought you to myself.

Now therefore, if you will indeed obey my qawal (voice), and shamar (keep) my barayath (covenant), then you shall be my own sagalah (possession) from among all im (peoples); for all the aratz (earth) is mine;

and you shall be to me a mamalakah (kingdom) of kahan (priests), and a qadawash (holy) gaway (nation).' These are the dabar (words) which you shall dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
Mashah came and called for the zaqan (elders) of the im (people), and set before them all these dabar (words) which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) him.
All the im (people) answered together, and said, "All that Yahawah has spoken we will do." Mashah reported the dabar (words) of the im (people) to Yahawah.

Yahawah said to Mashah, "Behold, I bawaa (come) to you in a thick cloud, that the im (people) may hear when I dabar (speak) with you, and may also aman (believe) you iwalam (forever)." Mashah told the dabar (words) of the im (people) to Yahawah.
Yahawah said to Mashah, "yalak (go) to the im (people), and qadash (sanctify) them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments,

and be kawan (ready) against the shalayashay (third) yawam (day); for on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) Yahawah will yarad (come) down in the iyan (sight) of all the im (people) on har (mount) Sayanay.

You shall set bounds to the im (people) all around, saying, ‘Be careful that you don't ilah (go) up onto the har (mountain), or nagai (touch) its border. Whoever touches the har (mountain) shall be mawath (surely) put to mawath (death).

No yad (hand) shall nagai (touch) him, but he shall saqal (surely) be stoned or shot through; whether it is animal or ayash (man), he shall not chayah (live).' When the yawabal (trumpet) sounds long, they shall ilah (come) up to the har (mountain).
Mashah went down from the har (mountain) to the im (people), and sanctified the im (people); and they washed their clothes.
He said to the im (people), "Be kawan (ready) by the shalawash (third) yawam (day). Don't have sexual relations with a ashah (woman).

It happened on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), when it was baqar (morning), that there were qawal (thunders) and lightnings, and a Kabad cloud on the har (mountain), and the qawal (sound) of an maad (exceedingly) chazaq (loud) trumpet; and all the im (people) who were in the machanah (camp) trembled.
Mashah led the im (people) out of the machanah (camp) to qaraah (meet) Alahayam; and they stood Thachathay the lower part of the har (mountain).

har (mount) Sayanay, all it, smoked, panayam (because) Yahawah descended on it in ash (fire); and its ishan (smoke) ascended like the ishan (smoke) of a furnace, and the whole har (mountain) quaked maad (greatly).
When the qawal (sound) of the trumpet grew louder and Chazaq, Mashah spoke, and Alahayam answered him by a qawal (voice).
Yahawah came down on har (mount) Sayanay, to the raash (top) of the har (mountain). Yahawah called Mashah to the top of the har (mountain), and Mashah went up.
Yahawah said to Mashah, "yarad (go) down, warn the im (people), lest they haras (break) through to Yahawah to raah (see), and many of them napal (perish).
Let the kahan (priests) also, who come near to Yahawah, qadash (sanctify) themselves, lest Yahawah break forth on them.
Mashah said to Yahawah, "The im (people) can't ilah (come) up to har (mount) Sayanay, for you warned us, saying, ‘Set bounds around the har (mountain), and qadash (sanctify) it.'

Yahawah said to him, "yalak (go) down and you shall bring Aharawan up with you, but don't let the kahan (priests) and the im (people) haras (break) through to ilah (come) up to Yahawah, lest he break forth on them.
So Mashah went down to the im (people), and told them.
Alahayam spoke all these dabar (words), saying,
"I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who brought you out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, out of the bayath (house) of ibad (bondage).
"You shall have no other Alahayam panayam (before) me.

"You shall not ishah (make) for yourselves an idol, nor any pasal (image) of anything that is in the shamayam (heavens) above, or that is in the aratz (earth) beneath, or that is in the mayam (water) under the aratz (earth):

you shall not shachah (bow) yourself down to them, nor ibad (serve) them, for I, Yahawah your Alahayam, am a Qanaa Alahayam, visiting the iwan (iniquity) of the abawath (fathers) on the children, on the shalash (third) and on the rabai (fourth) generation of those who shanaa (hate) me,
and showing loving chasad (kindness) to alap (thousands) of those who ahab (love) me and shamar (keep) my matzawah (commandments).
"You shall not nashaa (take) the sham (name) of Yahawah your Alahayam in vain, for Yahawah will not hold him guiltless who nashaa (takes) his sham (name) in vain.
"zakar (remember) the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day), to keep it qadash (holy).
You shall labor shash (six) yawam (days), and do all your malaakah (work),

but the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) is a shabath (sabbath) to Yahawah your Alahayam. You shall not do any malaakah (work) in it, you, nor your ban (son), nor your bath (daughter), your male ibad (servant), nor your female amah (servant), nor your livestock, nor your stranger who is within your gates;

for in shash (six) yawam (days) Yahawah made shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth), the yam (sea), and all that is in them, and rested the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day); therefore Yahawah blessed the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day), and made it qadash (holy).
"Honor your ab (father) and your am (mother), that your yawam (days) may be long in the adamah (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you.
"You shall not ratzach (murder).
"You shall not naap (commit) adultery.
"You shall not steal.
"You shall not give false id (testimony) against your neighbor.

"You shall not covet your neighbor's bayath (house). You shall not covet your neighbor's ashah (wife), nor his male ibad (servant), nor his female amah (servant), nor his ox, nor his donkey, nor anything that is your neighbor's.

All the im (people) perceived the qawal (thunderings), the lapayad (lightnings), the qawal (sound) of the trumpet, and the har (mountain) Ishan. When the im (people) saw it, they trembled, and stayed Rachawaq a distance.
They said to Mashah, "dabar (speak) with us yourself, and we will listen; but don't let Alahayam dabar (speak) with us, lest we mawath (die).
Mashah said to the im (people), "Don't be yaraa (afraid), for Alahayam has bawaa (come) to test you, and that his yaraah (fear) may be panayam (before) you, that you won't chataa (sin).
The im (people) stayed Rachawaq a distance, and Mashah drew near to the thick irapal (darkness) where Alahayam was.
Yahawah said to Mashah, "This is what you shall amar (tell) the children of Yasharaal (Israel): ‘You yourselves have seen that I have talked with you from shamayam (heaven).
You shall most ishah (certainly) not make alongside of me Alahayam of kasap (silver), or Alahayam of gold for yourselves.

You shall ishah (make) an mazabach (altar) of adamah (earth) for me, and shall zabach (sacrifice) on it your burnt ilah (offerings) and your peace ilah (offerings), your sheep and your cattle. In every place where I zakar (record) my sham (name) I will bawaa (come) to you and I will barak (bless) you.
If you ishah (make) me an mazabach (altar) of aban (stone), you shall not banah (build) it of cut aban (stones); for if you lift up your charab (tool) on it, you have polluted it.
Neither shall you ilah (go) up by steps to my mazabach (altar), that your irawah (nakedness) may not be exposed to it.'
"Now these are the mashapat (ordinances) which you shall shawam (set) panayam (before) them.
"If you qanah (buy) a ibaray (hebrew) ibad (servant), he shall ibad (serve) shash (six) Shanah and in the shabayaiy (seventh) he shall yatzaa (go) out Chapashay without paying anything.
If he bawaa (comes) in by himself, he shall yatzaa (go) out by himself. If he is bail (married), then his ashah (wife) shall yatzaa (go) out with him.

If his adawan (master) nathan (gives) him a ashah (wife) and she yalad (bears) him ban (sons) or bath (daughters), the ashah (wife) and her children shall be her adawan (master's), and he shall yatzaa (go) out by himself.
But if the ibad (servant) shall amar (plainly) amar (say), ‘I ahab (love) my adawan (master), my ashah (wife), and my children. I will not yatzaa (go) out Chapashay;'

then his adawan (master) shall bring him to Alahayam, and shall bring him to the door or to the doorpost, and his adawan (master) shall bore his ear through with an awl, and he shall ibad (serve) him for ever.
"If a ayash (man) sells his bath (daughter) to be a female amah (servant), she shall not yatzaa (go) out as the male ibad (servants) do.

If she doesn't rai (please) her adawan (master), who has married her to himself, then he shall let her be padah (redeemed). He shall have no right to sell her to a foreign im (people), since he has dealt bagad (deceitfully) with her.
If he marries her to his ban (son), he shall ishah (deal) with her as a bath (daughter).
If he takes achar (another) wife to himself, he shall not diminish her food, her clothing, and her marital rights.
If he doesn't do these shalawash (three) things for her, she may yatzaa (go) free without paying any kasap (money).
"nakah (one) who strikes a ayash (man) so that he dies shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death),
but not if it is unintentional, but Alahayam allows it to happen: then I will shawam (appoint) you a place where he shall flee.
If a ayash (man) schemes and comes presumptuously on his neighbor to harag (kill) him, you shall take him from my mazabach (altar), that he may mawath (die).
"Anyone who attacks his ab (father) or his am (mother) shall be mawath (surely) put to mawath (death).
"Anyone who kidnaps someone and sells him, or if he is found in his yad (hand), he shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death).
"Anyone who qalal (curses) his ab (father) or his am (mother) shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death).
"If men quarrel and one strikes the other with a aban (stone), or with his fist, and he doesn't mawath (die), but is confined to bed;

if he qawam (rises) again and halak (walks) around with his mashainah (staff), then he who struck him shall be cleared: only he shall nathan (pay) for the loss of his time, and shall provide for his healing until he is thoroughly healed.
"If a ayash (man) strikes his ibad (servant) or his amah (maid) with a shabat (rod), and he dies under his yad (hand), he shall surely be punished.
ak (notwithstanding), if he gets up after a yawam (day) or shanayam (two), he shall not be punished, for he is his property.

"If men fight and nagap (hurt) a pregnant ashah (woman) so that she gives birth prematurely, and yet no harm follows, he shall be surely fined as much as the ashah (woman's) bail (husband) demands and the palayal (judges) allow.
But if any harm follows, then you must nathan (take) napash (life) for napash (life),
iyan (eye) for iyan (eye), tooth for tooth, yad (hand) for yad (hand), ragal (foot) for ragal (foot),
burning for burning, wound for wound, and bruise for bruise.
"If a ayash (man) strikes his ibad (servant's) iyan (eye), or his amah (maid's) iyan (eye), and shachath (destroys) it, he shall let him shalach (go) Chapashay for his iyan (eye's) sake.
If he strikes out his male ibad (servant's) tooth, or his female amah (servant's) tooth, he shall let him shalach (go) Chapashay for his tooth's sake.

"If a bull gores a ayash (man) or a ashah (woman) to mawath (death), the bull shall saqal (surely) be stoned, and its flesh shall not be eaten; but the owner of the bull shall not be held responsible.

But if the bull had a Nagach of goring in the thamawal (past), and it has been testified to its owner, and he has not kept it in, but it has killed a ayash (man) or a ashah (woman), the bull shall be stoned, and its owner shall also be put to mawath (death).
If a kapar (ransom) is laid on him, then he shall nathan (give) for the padayawam (redemption) of his napash (life) whatever is laid on him.
Whether it has gored a ban (son) or has gored a bath (daughter), according to this mashapat (judgment) it shall be done to him.
If the bull gores a male ibad (servant) or a female amah (servant), shalawashayam (thirty) shekels of kasap (silver) shall be given to their adawan (master), and the ox shall be stoned.
"If a ayash (man) pathach (opens) a bawar (pit), or if a ayash (man) digs a bawar (pit) and doesn't cover it, and a bull or a donkey napal (falls) into it,
the owner of the bawar (pit) shall make it shalam (good). He shall shawab (turn back / repent) kasap (money) to its owner, and the mawath (dead) animal shall be his.
"If one ayash (man's) bull injures rai (another's), so that it dies, then they shall sell the chay (live) bull, and divide its kasap (price); and they shall also divide the mawath (dead) animal.

Or if it is yadai (known) that the bull was Nagach the habit of goring in the thamawal (past), and its owner has not kept it in, he shall shalam (surely) shalam (pay) bull for bull, and the mawath (dead) animal shall be his own.
"If a ayash (man) steals an ox or a sheep, and kills it, or sells it; he shall shalam (pay) chamash (five) oxen for an ox, and arabai (four) sheep for a sheep.
If the thief is found breaking in, and is struck so that he dies, there shall be no guilt of bloodshed for him.
If the shamash (sun) has risen on him, guilt of bloodshed shall be for him; he shall shalam (make) shalam (restitution). If he has nothing, then he shall be sold for his theft.
If the stolen property is found in his yad (hand) chay (alive), whether it is ox, donkey, or sheep, he shall shalam (pay) shanayam (double).

"If a ayash (man) causes a shadah (field) or vineyard to be eaten, and shalach (lets) his animal loose, and it grazes in another achar (man's) shadah (field), he shall shalam (make) restitution from the best of his own shadah (field), and from the best of his own vineyard.

"If ash (fire) yatzaa (breaks) out, and catches in thorns so that the shocks of grain, or the standing grain, or the shadah (field) are consumed; he who kindled the bairah (fire) shall shalam (surely) shalam (make) restitution.

"If a ayash (man) nathan (delivers) to his neighbor kasap (money) or stuff to shamar (keep), and it is stolen out of the ayash (man's) bayath (house); if the thief is found, he shall shalam (pay) shanayam (double).
If the thief isn't found, then the bail (master) of the bayath (house) shall qarab (come) near to Alahayam, to find out if he hasn't shalach (put) his yad (hand) to his neighbor's goods.

For every dabar (matter) of pashai (trespass), whether it be for ox, for donkey, for sheep, for clothing, or for any kind of lost thing, about which one amar (says), ‘This is mine,' the dabar (cause) of shanayam (both) parties shall bawaa (come) before Alahayam. He whom Alahayam rashai (condemns) shall shalam (pay) shanayam (double) to his neighbor.
"If a ayash (man) nathan (delivers) to his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any animal to shamar (keep), and it dies or is injured, or driven away, no man seeing it;

the shabawaih (oath) of Yahawah shall be between them shanayam (both), whether he hasn't shalach (put) his yad (hand) to his neighbor's goods; and its owner shall accept it, and he shall not shalam (make) restitution.
But if it is stolen from him, he shall shalam (make) restitution to its owner.
If it is torn in pieces, let him bawaa (bring) it for evidence. He shall not make shalam (good) that which was torn.
"If a ayash (man) shaal (borrows) anything of his neighbor's, and it is injured, or dies, its owner not being with it, he shall shalam (surely) shalam (make) restitution.
If its owner is with it, he shall not make it shalam (good). If it is a leased thing, it came for its lease.
"If a ayash (man) entices a virgin who isn't pledged to be married, and lies with her, he shall surely pay a dowry for her to be his ashah (wife).
If her ab (father) utterly refuses to nathan (give) her to him, he shall pay kasap (money) according to the dowry of virgins.
"You shall not allow a sorceress to chayah (live).
"Whoever has sex with an animal shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death).
"He who zabach (sacrifices) to any Alahayam, balathay (except) to Yahawah only, shall be charam (utterly) destroyed.
"You shall not wrong an alien, neither shall you lachatz (oppress) him, for you were aliens in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
"You shall not take advantage of any alamanah (widow) or fatherless child.
If you take advantage of them at all, and they cry at all to me, I will surely hear their cry;
and my ap (wrath) will grow charah (hot), and I will harag (kill) you with the charab (sword); and your wives shall be alamanah (widows), and your children fatherless.
"If you lend kasap (money) to any of my im (people) with you who is Inay, you shall not be to him as a creditor; neither shall you shawam (charge) him interest.
If you take your neighbor's garment as collateral, you shall shawab (turn back / repent) it to him before the shamash (sun) goes down,
for that is his only covering, it is his garment for his skin. What would he sleep in? It will happen, when he cries to me, that I will hear, for I am Chanawan.
"You shall not blaspheme Alahayam, nor arar (curse) a nashayaa (ruler) of your im (people).
"You shall not delay Malaah offer from your harvest and from the outflow of your presses. "You shall nathan (give) the firstborn of your ban (sons) to me.
You shall do Kan with your cattle and with your sheep. shabai (seven) yawam (days) it shall be with its am (mother), then on the eighth yawam (day) you shall nathan (give) it to me.
"You shall be qadash (holy) men to me, therefore you shall not akal (eat) any flesh that is torn by animals in the shadah (field). You shall cast it to the dogs.
"You shall not spread a false report. Don't join your yad (hand) with the rashai (wicked) to be a malicious witness.
"You shall not achar (follow) a crowd to do rai (evil); neither shall you testify in court to side with a rab (multitude) to natah (pervert) justice;
neither shall you favor a Dal man in his rayab (cause).
"If you pagai (meet) your ayab (enemy's) ox or his donkey going thaih (astray), you shall shawab (turn back / repent) shawab (turn back / repent) it back to him again.
If you raah (see) the donkey of him who shanaa (hates) you fallen down under his mashaa (burden), don't leave him, you shall surely help him with it.
"You shall not deny justice to your Abayawan people in their lawsuits.
"rachaq (keep) far from a false charge, and don't harag (kill) the naqay (innocent) and tzadayaq (righteous): for I will not justify the rashai (wicked).
"You shall take no shachad (bribe), for a shachad (bribe) blinds those who have Paqach and perverts the dabar (words) of the tzadayaq (righteous).
"You shall not lachatz (oppress) an alien, for you yadai (know) the napash (heart) of an alien, since you were aliens in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
"For shash (six) Shanah you shall zarai (sow) your aratz (land), and shall asap (gather) in its increase,

but the shabayaiy (seventh) year you shall let it shamat (rest) and lie fallow, that the Abayawan of your im (people) may akal (eat); and yathar (what) they leave the animal of the shadah (field) shall akal (eat). In the same way, you shall ishah (deal) with your vineyard and with your olive grove.

"shash (six) yawam (days) you shall do your maishah (work), and on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) you shall shabath (rest), that your ox and your donkey may have nawach (rest), and the ban (son) of your handmaid, and the alien may be refreshed.
"Be careful to do all things that I have said to you; and don't invoke the sham (name) of other Alahayam, neither let them be heard out of your pah (mouth).
"You shall observe a feast to me shalawash (three) ragal (times) a Shanah.

You shall shamar (observe) the chag (feast) of unleavened matzah (bread). shabai (seven) yawam (days) you shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread), as I tzawah (commanded) you, at the mawaid (time) appointed in the chadash (month) Abib (for in it you came out from Matzarayam), and no one shall raah (see) panayam (before) me empty.

And the chag (feast) of harvest, the bakawar (first) fruits of your maishah (labors), which you zarai (sow) in the shadah (field): and the chag (feast) of harvest, at the yatzaa (end) of the Shanah, when you asap (gather) in your maishah (labors) out of the shadah (field).
shalawash (three) paim (times) in the Shanah all your males shall raah (see) panayam (before) the Adawan Yahawah.
"You shall not zabach (offer) the dam (blood) of my zabach (sacrifice) with leavened chamatz (bread), neither shall the fat of my chag (feast) lawan (remain) all night until the baqar (morning).

The raashayath (first) of the bakawar (first) fruits of your adamah (ground) you shall bawaa (bring) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah your Alahayam. "You shall not boil a young goat in its am (mother's) milk.
"Behold, I shalach (send) an malaak (angel) panayam (before) you, to shamar (keep) you by the darak (way), and to bawaa (bring) you into the place which I have prepared.
Pay attention to him, and listen to his qawal (voice). Don't provoke him, for he will not nashaa (pardon) your disobedience, for my sham (name) is in him.
But if you indeed listen to his qawal (voice), and do all that I dabar (speak), then I will be an ayab (enemy) to your ayab (enemies), and an tzarar (adversary) to your tzawar (adversaries).

For my malaak (angel) shall yalak (go) panayam (before) you, and bawaa (bring) you in to the Amaray (Amorite), the Chathay (Hittite), the Parazay (Perizzite), the Kanainay (Canaanite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite); and I will cut them off.

You shall not shachah (bow) down to their Alahayam, nor ibad (serve) them, nor ishah (follow) their practices, but you shall haras (utterly) haras (overthrow) them and demolish their matzabah (pillars).
You shall ibad (serve) Yahawah your Alahayam, and he will barak (bless) your lacham (bread) and your mayam (water), and I will sawar (take) sickness sawar (away) from your qarab (midst).
No one will shakal (miscarry) or be Iqar in your aratz (land). I will fulfill the number of your yawam (days).

I will shalach (send) my ayamah (terror) panayam (before) you, and will confuse all the im (people) to whom you bawaa (come), and I will nathan (make) all your ayab (enemies) irap (turn) their backs to you.
I will shalach (send) the hornet panayam (before) you, which will drive out the Chaway (Hivite), the Kanainay (Canaanite), and the Chathay (Hittite), from panayam (before) you.
I will not drive them out from panayam (before) you in one Shanah, lest the aratz (land) become desolate, and the animals of the shadah (field) rab (multiply) against you.
Mait by Mait I will drive them out from panayam (before) you, until you have increased and nachal (inherit) the aratz (land).

I will shayath (set) your border from the Red yam (sea) even to the yam (sea) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and from the madabar (wilderness) to the nahar (river); for I will nathan (deliver) the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land) into your yad (hand), and you shall drive them out panayam (before) you.
You shall karath (make) no barayath (covenant) with them, nor with their Alahayam.
They shall not yashab (dwell) in your aratz (land), lest they make you chataa (sin) against me, for if you ibad (serve) their Alahayam, it will surely be a snare to you.

He said to Mashah, "ilah (come) up to Yahawah, you, and Aharawan, Nadab, and Abayahawaa, and shabaiyam (seventy) of the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel); and shachah (worship) Rachawaq a distance.
Mashah nagash (alone) shall come near to Yahawah, but they shall not come near, neither shall the im (people) ilah (go) up with him.

Mashah came and told the im (people) all the dabar (words) of Yahawah, and all the mashapat (ordinances); and all the im (people) answered with one qawal (voice), and said, "All the dabar (words) which Yahawah has spoken will we do.

Mashah wrote all the dabar (words) of Yahawah, and rose up shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and built an mazabach (altar) under the har (mountain), and twelve matzabah (pillars) for the shanayam (twelve) shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel).
He sent nair (young) men of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), who offered burnt ilah (offerings) and sacrificed shalam (peace) ilah (offerings) of cattle to Yahawah.
Mashah took chatzay (half) of the dam (blood) and shawam (put) it in basins, and chatzay (half) of the dam (blood) he sprinkled on the mazabach (altar).
He took the book of the barayath (covenant) and qaraa (read) it in the hearing of the im (people), and they said, "All that Yahawah has spoken will we do, and be obedient.

Mashah took the dam (blood), and sprinkled it on the im (people), and said, "Look, this is the dam (blood) of the barayath (covenant), which Yahawah has made with you concerning all these dabar (words).
Then Mashah, Aharawan, Nadab, Abayahawaa, and shabaiyam (seventy) of the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) went up.
They saw the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel). Under his feet was like a paved maishah (work) of sapphire sapayar (stone), like the skies for tahar (clearness).
He didn't shalach (lay) his yad (hand) on the atzayal (nobles) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel). They saw Alahayam, and ate and drank.

Yahawah said to Mashah, "ilah (come) up to me on the har (mountain), and stay here, and I will nathan (give) you the tables of aban (stone) with the thawarah (law) and the commands that I have written, that you may teach them.
Mashah rose up with Yahawashawai, his sharath (servant), and Mashah went up onto alahayam (god's) har (mountain).
He said to the zaqan (elders), "Wait here for us, until we shawab (turn back / repent) again to you. Behold, Aharawan and Chawar are with you. Whoever is involved in a dispute can go to them.
Mashah went up on the har (mountain), and the cloud covered the har (mountain).

The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah settled on har (mount) Sayanay, and the cloud covered it shash (six) yawam (days). The shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) he called to Mashah out of the midst of the cloud.
The appearance of the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah was like devouring ash (fire) on the raash (top) of the har (mountain) in the iyan (eyes) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
Mashah entered into the midst of the cloud, and went up on the har (mountain); and Mashah was on the har (mountain) arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), that they take an tharawamah (offering) for me. From everyone whose lab (heart) makes him willing you shall take my tharawamah (offering).
This is the tharawamah (offering) which you shall take from them: gold, kasap (silver), brass,
blue, purple, scarlet, Shash linen, goats' hair,
ayal (rams)' skins dyed red, thachash (sea) cow hides, acacia itz (wood),
shaman (oil) for the maawar (light), spices for the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil) and for the sweet incense,
onyx aban (stones), and aban (stones) to be set for the apawad (ephod) and for the breastplate.
Let them ishah (make) me a maqadash (sanctuary), that I may shakan (dwell) among them.
According to all that I show you, the thabanayath (pattern) of the mashakan (tabernacle), and the thabanayath (pattern) of all of its furniture, even so you shall ishah (make) it.

"They shall ishah (make) an arawan (ark) of acacia itz (wood). Its arak (length) shall be chatzay (two) and a half amah (cubits), its breadth a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half), and a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) its height.
You shall overlay it with tahawar (pure) gold. You shall overlay it bayath (inside) and outside, and you shall ishah (make) a gold molding around it.

You shall cast arabai (four) rings of gold for it, and nathan (put) them in its arabai (four) feet. shanayam (two) rings shall be on the one side of it, and shanayam (two) rings on the other side of it.
You shall ishah (make) poles of acacia itz (wood), and overlay them with gold.
You shall bawaa (put) the poles into the rings on the sides of the arawan (ark) to nashaa (carry) the arawan (ark).
The poles shall be in the rings of the arawan (ark). They shall not be taken from it.
You shall nathan (put) the idawath (testimony) which I shall nathan (give) you into the arawan (ark).
You shall ishah (make) a kaparath (mercy) seat of tahawar (pure) gold. chatzay (two) and a half amah (cubits) shall be its arak (length), and a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) its breadth.
You shall ishah (make) shanayam (two) karawab (cherubim) of hammered gold. You shall ishah (make) them at the shanayam (two) ends of the kaparath (mercy) seat.

ishah (make) one karawab (cherub) at the qatzah (one) end, and one karawab (cherub) at the other end. You shall ishah (make) the karawab (cherubim) on its shanayam (two) ends of one piece with the kaparath (mercy) seat.

The karawab (cherubim) shall spread out their wings upward, covering the kaparath (mercy) seat with their wings, with their panayam (faces) toward one ach (another). The panayam (faces) of the karawab (cherubim) shall be toward the kaparath (mercy) seat.
You shall nathan (put) the kaparath (mercy) seat on top of the arawan (ark), and in the arawan (ark) you shall nathan (put) the idawath (testimony) that I will nathan (give) you.

There I will meet with you, and I will dabar (tell) you from above the kaparath (mercy) seat, from between the shanayam (two) karawab (cherubim) which are on the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony), all that I tzawah (command) you for the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
"You shall ishah (make) a table of acacia itz (wood). Two amah (cubits) shall be its arak (length), and a amah (cubit) its breadth, and one and a chatzay (half) amah (cubits) its height.
You shall overlay it with tahawar (pure) gold, and ishah (make) a gold molding around it.
You shall ishah (make) a rim of a tapach (handbreadth) around it. You shall ishah (make) a golden molding on its rim around it.
You shall ishah (make) arabai (four) rings of gold for it, and nathan (put) the rings in the arabai (four) corners that are on its arabai (four) feet.
the rings shall be close to the rim, for bayath (places) for the poles to nashaa (carry) the table.
You shall ishah (make) the poles of acacia itz (wood), and overlay them with gold, that the table may be carried with them.
You shall ishah (make) its dishes, its kap (spoons), its ladles, and its bowls to pour out nasak (offerings) with. You shall ishah (make) them of tahawar (pure) gold.
You shall nathan (set) lacham (bread) of the presence on the table panayam (before) me always.

"You shall ishah (make) a lampstand of tahawar (pure) gold. Of hammered maqashah (work) shall the lampstand be made, even its base, its shaft, its gabayai (cups), its buds, and its flowers, shall be of parach (one) piece with it.

There shall be shash (six) branches yatzaa (going) out of its sides: shalawash (three) branches of the lampstand out of its one side, and shalawash (three) branches of the lampstand out of its other side;

shalawash (three) gabayai (cups) made like almond blossoms in one branch, a bud and a flower; and shalawash (three) gabayai (cups) made like almond blossoms in the other branch, a bud and a flower, so for the shash (six) branches yatzaa (going) out of the lampstand;
and in the lampstand arabai (four) gabayai (cups) made like almond blossoms, its buds and its flowers;

and a bud under shanayam (two) branches of kapathar (one) piece with it, and a bud under shanayam (two) branches of kapathar (one) piece with it, and a bud under shanayam (two) branches of one piece with it, for the shash (six) branches yatzaa (going) out of the lampstand.
Their buds and their branches shall be of one piece with it, all of it one beaten maqashah (work) of tahawar (pure) gold.
You shall ishah (make) its nayar (lamps) shabai (seven), and they shall ilah (light) its nayar (lamps) to give ilah (light) to the space in front of it.
Its snuffers and its snuff dishes shall be of tahawar (pure) gold.
It shall be made of a talent of tahawar (pure) gold, with all these accessories.
raah (see) that you ishah (make) them after their thabanayath (pattern), which has been shown to you on the har (mountain).

"Moreover you shall ishah (make) the mashakan (tabernacle) with ishar (ten) curtains; of fine twined Shash, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, with cherubim. The maishah (work) of the skillful workman you shall ishah (make) them.

The arak (length) of achad (each) curtain shall be isharayam (twenty) shamanah (eight) amah (cubits), and the breadth of achad (each) curtain arabai (four) amah (cubits): all the curtains shall have one measure.
chamash (five) curtains shall be coupled together one to achawath (another); and the other chamash (five) curtains shall be coupled one to achawath (another).

You shall ishah (make) loops of blue on the shapah (edge) of the one curtain from the edge in the coupling; and likewise you shall ishah (make) in the shapah (edge) of the curtain that is Qayatzawan in the shanay (second) coupling.

You shall ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) loops in the one curtain, and you shall ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) loops in the edge of the curtain that is in the shanay (second) coupling. The loops shall be opposite one to achawath (another).
You shall ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) clasps of gold, and couple the curtains one to another with the clasps: and the mashakan (tabernacle) shall be a unit.
"You shall ishah (make) curtains of goats' hair for a ahal (covering) over the mashakan (tabernacle). You shall ishah (make) them ishathay (eleven) curtains.

The arak (length) of achad (each) curtain shall be shalawashayam (thirty) amah (cubits), and the breadth of achad (each) curtain arabai (four) amah (cubits): the ishathay (eleven) curtains shall have one measure.
You shall couple chamash (five) curtains by themselves, and shash (six) curtains by themselves, and shall double over the shashay (sixth) curtain in the forefront of the ahal (tent).

You shall ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) loops on the shapah (edge) of the one curtain that is Qayatzawan in the coupling, and chamashayam (fifty) loops on the shapah (edge) of the curtain which is outmost in the shanay (second) coupling.
You shall ishah (make) chamashayam (fifty) clasps of brass, and bawaa (put) the clasps into the loops, and couple the ahal (tent) achad (together), that it may be one.
The overhanging part that remains of the curtains of the ahal (tent), the chatzay (half) curtain that remains, shall hang over the back of the mashakan (tabernacle).

The amah (cubit) on the one zah (side), and the amah (cubit) on the other side, of that which remains in the arak (length) of the curtains of the ahal (tent), shall hang over the sides of the mashakan (tabernacle) on this side and on that side, to cover it.
You shall ishah (make) a covering for the ahal (tent) of ayal (rams)' skins dyed red, and a covering of thachash (sea) cow hides above.
"You shall ishah (make) the boards for the mashakan (tabernacle) of acacia itz (wood), standing up.
ishar (ten) amah (cubits) shall be the arak (length) of a board, and one and a chatzay (half) amah (cubits) the breadth of achad (each) board.
There shall be shanayam (two) tenons in achad (each) board, joined to one achawath (another): thus you shall ishah (make) for all the boards of the mashakan (tabernacle).
You shall ishah (make) the boards for the mashakan (tabernacle), isharayam (twenty) boards for the Nagab side southward.

You shall ishah (make) arabaiyam (forty) sockets of kasap (silver) under the isharayam (twenty) boards; shanayam (two) sockets under one board for its shanayam (two) tenons, and shanayam (two) sockets under another board for its shanayam (two) tenons.
For the shanay (second) side of the mashakan (tabernacle), on the tzapawan (north) side, isharayam (twenty) boards,
and their arabaiyam (forty) sockets of kasap (silver); shanayam (two) sockets under one board, and shanayam (two) sockets under another board.
For the far part of the mashakan (tabernacle) westward you shall ishah (make) shash (six) boards.
You shall ishah (make) shanayam (two) boards for the corners of the mashakan (tabernacle) in the far part.
They shall be Thaam beneath, and Thaam the same way they shall be whole to its raash (top) to one ring: thus shall it be for them shanayam (both); they shall be for the shanayam (two) corners.
There shall be shamanah (eight) boards, and their sockets of kasap (silver), sixteen sockets; shanayam (two) sockets under one board, and shanayam (two) sockets under another board.
"You shall ishah (make) bars of acacia itz (wood): chamash (five) for the boards of the one side of the mashakan (tabernacle),
and chamash (five) bars for the boards of the other side of the mashakan (tabernacle), and chamash (five) bars for the boards of the side of the mashakan (tabernacle), for the far part westward.
The Thayakawan bar in the Thayakawan of the boards shall pass through from end to end.
You shall overlay the boards with gold, and ishah (make) their rings of gold for bayath (places) for the bars: and you shall overlay the bars with gold.
You shall qawam (set) up the mashakan (tabernacle) according to the way that it was shown to you on the har (mountain).
"You shall ishah (make) a parakath (veil) of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined Shash, with karawab (cherubim). The maishah (work) of the skillful ishah (workman) shall it be made.
You shall nathan (hang) it on arabai (four) pillars of acacia overlaid with gold; their hooks shall be of gold, on arabai (four) sockets of kasap (silver).

You shall nathan (hang) up the parakath (veil) under the clasps, and shall bawaa (bring) the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony) in there bayath (within) the parakath (veil): and the parakath (veil) shall separate the qadash (holy) place from the most qadash (holy) for you.
You shall nathan (put) the kaparath (mercy) seat on the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony) in the most qadash (holy) place.

You shall shawam (set) the table outside the parakath (veil), and the lampstand over against the table on the side of the mashakan (tabernacle) toward the thayaman (south): and you shall nathan (put) the table on the tzapawan (north) side.
"You shall ishah (make) a screen for the door of the ahal (tent), of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined Shash, the maishah (work) of the raqam (embroiderer).
You shall ishah (make) for the screen chamash (five) pillars of acacia, and overlay them with gold: their hooks shall be of gold: and you shall cast chamash (five) sockets of brass for them.

"You shall ishah (make) the mazabach (altar) of acacia itz (wood), chamash (five) amah (cubits) arak (long), and chamash (five) amah (cubits) broad; the mazabach (altar) shall be foursquare: and its height shall be shalawash (three) amah (cubits).
You shall ishah (make) its qaran (horns) on its arabai (four) corners; its qaran (horns) shall be of tzapah (one) piece with it; and you shall overlay it with brass.
You shall ishah (make) its pots to take away its ashes, its shovels, its basins, its flesh hooks, and its machathah (fire) pans: all its vessels you shall ishah (make) of brass.
You shall ishah (make) a grating for it of network of brass: and on the net you shall ishah (make) arabai (four) bronze rings in its arabai (four) corners.
You shall nathan (put) it under the ledge around the mazabach (altar) beneath, that the net may reach halfway up the mazabach (altar).
You shall ishah (make) poles for the mazabach (altar), poles of acacia itz (wood), and overlay them with brass.
Its poles shall be bawaa (put) into the rings, and the poles shall be on the shanayam (two) sides of the mazabach (altar), when carrying it.
You shall ishah (make) it with hollow planks. They shall ishah (make) it as it has been shown you on the har (mountain).

"You shall ishah (make) the court of the mashakan (tabernacle): for the Nagab side southward there shall be hangings for the court of fine twined Shash one maah (hundred) amah (cubits) arak (long) for one side:
and its pillars shall be isharayam (twenty), and their sockets isharayam (twenty), of brass; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets shall be of kasap (silver).

Likewise for the tzapawan (north) side in arak (length) there shall be hangings one maah (hundred) cubits arak (long), and its pillars isharayam (twenty), and their sockets isharayam (twenty), of brass; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of kasap (silver).
For the breadth of the court on the yam (west) side shall be hangings of chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits); their pillars ishar (ten), and their sockets ishar (ten).
The breadth of the court on the qadam (east) side eastward shall be chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits).
The hangings for the kathap (one) side of the gate shall be chamash (fifteen) amah (cubits); their pillars shalawash (three), and their sockets shalawash (three).
For the other side shall be hangings of chamash (fifteen) cubits; their pillars shalawash (three), and their sockets shalawash (three).

For the gate of the court shall be a screen of isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits), of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined Shash, the raqam (work) of the embroiderer; their pillars arabai (four), and their sockets arabai (four).
All the pillars of the court around shall be filleted with kasap (silver); their hooks of kasap (silver), and their sockets of brass.

The arak (length) of the court shall be one maah (hundred) amah (cubits), and the breadth chamashayam (fifty) every where, and the height chamash (five) amah (cubits), of fine twined Shash, and their sockets of brass.
All the instruments of the mashakan (tabernacle) in all its ibadah (service), and all its pins, and all the pins of the court, shall be of brass.

"You shall tzawah (command) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), that they bring to you zak (pure) olive shaman (oil) Kathayath for the maawar (light), to cause a nayar (lamp) to ilah (burn) continually.

In the ahal (tent) of Meeting, outside the parakath (veil) which is before the idawath (testimony), Aharawan and his ban (sons) shall keep it in order from evening to baqar (morning) panayam (before) Yahawah: it shall be a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) throughout their dawar (generations) on the behalf of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

"qarab (bring) Aharawan your ach (brother), and his ban (sons) with him, near to you from among the children of Yasharaal (Israel), that he may kahan (minister) to me in the priest's office, even Aharawan, Nadab and Abayahawaa, Alaizar and Ayathamar, Aharawan ban (sons).
You shall ishah (make) qadash (holy) bagad (garments) for Aharawan your ach (brother), for kabawad (glory) and for thapaarah (beauty).

You shall dabar (speak) to all who are chakam (wise) lab (hearted), whom I have filled with the rawach (spirit) of chakamah (wisdom), that they ishah (make) Aharawan bagad (garments) to qadash (sanctify) him, that he may kahan (minister) to me in the priest's office.

These are the bagad (garments) which they shall ishah (make): a breastplate, and an apawad (ephod), and a robe, and a coat of checker thashabatz (work), a turban, and a sash: and they shall ishah (make) qadash (holy) bagad (garments) for Aharawan your ach (brother), and his ban (sons), that he may kahan (minister) to me in the priest's office.
They shall take the gold, and the blue, and the purple, and the scarlet, and the Shash linen.
"They shall ishah (make) the apawad (ephod) of gold, of blue, and purple, scarlet, and fine twined Shash, the maishah (work) of the skillful chashab (workman).
It shall have shanayam (two) shoulder straps joined to the shanayam (two) ends of it, that it may be joined together.
The skillfully woven band, which is on it, that is on him, shall be like its maishah (work) and of the same piece; of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined Shash.
You shall take shanayam (two) onyx aban (stones), and pathach (engrave) on them the sham (names) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel):
shash (six) of their sham (names) on the one aban (stone), and the sham (names) of the shash (six) that yathar (remain) on the other aban (stone), in the order of their thawaladah (birth).

With the maishah (work) of an engraver in aban (stone), like the engravings of a signet, you shall pathach (engrave) the shanayam (two) aban (stones), according to the sham (names) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel): you shall ishah (make) them to be enclosed in settings of gold.

You shall shawam (put) the shanayam (two) aban (stones) on the shoulder straps of the apawad (ephod), to be aban (stones) of zakarawan (memorial) for the children of Yasharaal (Israel): and Aharawan shall nashaa (bear) their sham (names) panayam (before) Yahawah on his shanayam (two) shoulders for a zakarawan (memorial).
You shall ishah (make) settings of gold,
and shanayam (two) chains of tahawar (pure) gold; you shall ishah (make) them like cords of braided maishah (work): and you shall nathan (put) the braided chains on the settings.

"You shall ishah (make) a breastplate of mashapat (judgment), the maishah (work) of the skillful workman; like the maishah (work) of the apawad (ephod) you shall ishah (make) it; of gold, of blue, and purple, and scarlet, and fine twined Shash, you shall ishah (make) it.
It shall be square and folded double; a span shall be its arak (length) of it, and a span its breadth.
You shall malaa (set) in it settings of aban (stones), arabai (four) rows of aban (stones): a row of ruby, topaz, and beryl shall be the achad (first) row;
and the shanay (second) row a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald;
and the shalayashay (third) row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
and the rabayaiy (fourth) row a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper: they shall be enclosed in gold in their settings.

The aban (stones) shall be according to the sham (names) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), shanayam (twelve), according to their sham (names); like the engravings of a signet, everyone according to his sham (name), they shall be for the shanayam (twelve) shabat (tribes).
You shall ishah (make) on the breastplate chains like cords, of braided maishah (work) of tahawar (pure) gold.
You shall ishah (make) on the breastplate shanayam (two) rings of gold, and shall nathan (put) the shanayam (two) rings on the shanayam (two) ends of the breastplate.
You shall nathan (put) the shanayam (two) braided chains of gold in the shanayam (two) rings at the ends of the breastplate.

The other shanayam (two) ends of the shanayam (two) braided chains you shall nathan (put) on the shanayam (two) settings, and nathan (put) them on the shoulder straps of the apawad (ephod) in its forepart.

You shall ishah (make) shanayam (two) rings of gold, and you shall shawam (put) them on the shanayam (two) ends of the breastplate, on its shapah (edge), which is toward the ibar (side) of the apawad (ephod) inward.

You shall ishah (make) shanayam (two) rings of gold, and shall nathan (put) them on the shanayam (two) shoulder straps of the apawad (ephod) underneath, in its forepart, close by its coupling, above the skillfully woven band of the apawad (ephod).

They shall bind the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the apawad (ephod) with a lace of blue, that it may be on the skillfully woven band of the apawad (ephod), and that the breastplate may not swing out from the apawad (ephod).

Aharawan shall nashaa (bear) the sham (names) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) in the breastplate of mashapat (judgment) on his lab (heart), when he goes in to the qadash (holy) place, for a zakarawan (memorial) panayam (before) Yahawah continually.

You shall nathan (put) in the breastplate of mashapat (judgment) the awarayam (urim) and the thamayam (thummim); and they shall be on Aharawan lab (heart), when he goes in panayam (before) Yahawah: and Aharawan shall nashaa (bear) the mashapat (judgment) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) on his lab (heart) panayam (before) Yahawah continually.
"You shall ishah (make) the robe of the apawad (ephod) all of blue.

It shall have a pah (hole) for the raash (head) in its midst: it shall have a shapah (binding) of woven maishah (work) around its pah (hole), as it were the pah (hole) of a coat of mail, that it not be torn.
On its hem you shall ishah (make) pomegranates of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, around its hem; and bells of gold between and around them:
a golden bell and a pomegranate, a golden bell and a pomegranate, around the hem of the robe.

It shall be on Aharawan to sharath (minister): and its qawal (sound) shall be heard when he goes in to the qadash (holy) place panayam (before) Yahawah, and when he yatzaa (comes) out, that he not mawath (die).
"You shall ishah (make) a plate of tahawar (pure) gold, and pathach (engrave) on it, like the engravings of a signet, ‘qadash (holy) TO Yahawah.'
You shall shawam (put) it on a lace of blue, and it shall be on the sash; on the front of the sash it shall be.

It shall be on Aharawan forehead, and Aharawan shall nashaa (bear) the iwan (iniquity) of the qadash (holy) things, which the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shall make qadash (holy) in all their qadash (holy) mathanah (gifts); and it shall be always on his forehead, that they may be accepted panayam (before) Yahawah.
You shall weave the coat in checker work of Shash linen, and you shall ishah (make) a turban of Shash linen, and you shall ishah (make) a sash, the raqam (work) of the embroiderer.
"You shall ishah (make) coats for Aharawan ban (sons), and you shall ishah (make) sashes for them and you shall ishah (make) headbands for them, for kabawad (glory) and for thapaarah (beauty).

You shall Labash them on Aharawan your ach (brother), and on his ban (sons) with him, and shall mashach (anoint) them, and malaa (consecrate) them, and qadash (sanctify) them, that they may kahan (minister) to me in the priest's office.
You shall ishah (make) them linen breeches to cover the flesh of their nakedness; from the waist even to the thighs they shall reach:

They shall be on Aharawan, and on his ban (sons), when they bawaa (go) in to the ahal (tent) of Meeting, or when they come near to the mazabach (altar) to sharath (minister) in the qadash (holy) place; that they don't nashaa (bear) iwan (iniquity), and mawath (die): it shall be a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) to him and to his descendants achar (after) him.

"This is the thing that you shall do to them to make them qadash (holy), to kahan (minister) to me in the priest's office: take one ban (young) bull and shanayam (two) ayal (rams) thamayam (without) blemish,
unleavened lacham (bread), unleavened cakes mixed with shaman (oil), and unleavened wafers mashach (anointed) with shaman (oil): you shall ishah (make) them of fine wheat flour.
You shall nathan (put) them into one basket, and qarab (bring) them in the basket, with the bull and the shanayam (two) ayal (rams).
You shall qarab (bring) Aharawan and his ban (sons) to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and shall wash them with mayam (water).

You shall take the bagad (garments), and Labash on Aharawan the coat, the robe of the apawad (ephod), the apawad (ephod), and the breastplate, and clothe him with the skillfully woven band of the apawad (ephod);
and you shall shawam (set) the turban on his raash (head), and nathan (put) the qadash (holy) nazar (crown) on the turban.
Then you shall take the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and pour it on his raash (head), and mashach (anoint) him.
You shall qarab (bring) his ban (sons), and Labash coats on them.

You shall clothe them with belts, Aharawan and his ban (sons), and bind headbands on them: and they shall have the kahanah (priesthood) by a perpetual chaqah (statute): and you shall malaa (consecrate) Aharawan and his ban (sons).
"You shall qarab (bring) the bull panayam (before) the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and Aharawan and his ban (sons) shall samak (lay) their yad (hands) on the raash (head) of the bull.
You shall kill the bull panayam (before) Yahawah, at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

You shall take of the dam (blood) of the bull, and nathan (put) it on the qaran (horns) of the mazabach (altar) with your finger; and you shall pour out all the dam (blood) at the base of the mazabach (altar).
You shall take all the fat that covers the innards, the cover of the liver, the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), and the fat that is on them, and qatar (burn) them on the mazabach (altar).
But the flesh of the bull, and its skin, and its dung, you shall sharap (burn) with ash (fire) outside of the machanah (camp): it is a chataah (sin) offering.
"You shall also take the one ayal (ram); and Aharawan and his ban (sons) shall samak (lay) their yad (hands) on the raash (head) of the ayal (ram).
You shall kill the ayal (ram), and you shall take its dam (blood), and sprinkle it around on the mazabach (altar).
You shall cut the ayal (ram) into its pieces, and wash its innards, and its legs, and nathan (put) them with its pieces, and with its raash (head).
You shall qatar (burn) the whole ayal (ram) on the mazabach (altar): it is a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah; it is a pleasant aroma, an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah.
"You shall take the other ayal (ram); and Aharawan and his ban (sons) shall samak (lay) their yad (hands) on the raash (head) of the ayal (ram).

Then you shall kill the ayal (ram), and take some of its dam (blood), and nathan (put) it on the tip of the right ear of Aharawan, and on the tip of the Yamanay ear of his ban (sons), and on the thumb of their Yamanay yad (hand), and on the big toe of their Yamanay ragal (foot), and sprinkle the dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar).

You shall take of the dam (blood) that is on the mazabach (altar), and of the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and sprinkle it on Aharawan, and on his bagad (garments), and on his ban (sons), and on the bagad (garments) of his ban (sons) with him: and he shall be made qadash (holy), and his bagad (garments), and his ban (sons), and his ban (sons)' bagad (garments) with him.

Also you shall take some of the ayal (ram's) fat, the fat tail, the fat that covers the innards, the cover of the liver, the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), the fat that is on them, and the yamayan (right) thigh (for it is a ayal (ram) of consecration),
and one loaf of lacham (bread), one cake of shaman (oiled) bread, and one wafer out of the basket of unleavened matzah (bread) that is panayam (before) Yahawah.
You shall shawam (put) all of this in Aharawan kap (hands), and in his ban (sons)' kap (hands), and shall wave them for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah.

You shall take them from their yad (hands), and qatar (burn) them on the mazabach (altar) on the burnt ilah (offering), for a pleasant aroma panayam (before) Yahawah: it is an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah.
"You shall take the breast of Aharawan ayal (ram) of consecration, and wave it for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah: and it shall be your portion.

You shall qadash (sanctify) the breast of the wave thanawapah (offering), and the thigh of the wave thanawapah (offering), which is waved, and which is heaved up, of the ayal (ram) of consecration, even of that which is for Aharawan, and of that which is for his ban (sons):

and it shall be for Aharawan and his ban (sons) as their chaq (portion) iwalam (forever) from the children of Yasharaal (Israel); for it is a wave tharawamah (offering): and it shall be a wave tharawamah (offering) from the children of Yasharaal (Israel) of the zabach (sacrifices) of their shalam (peace) offerings, even their wave tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah.
"The qadash (holy) bagad (garments) of Aharawan shall be for his ban (sons) achar (after) him, to be mashachah (anointed) in them, and to be consecrated in them.

shabai (seven) yawam (days) shall the ban (son) who is kahan (priest) in his place Labash them on, when he bawaa (comes) into the ahal (tent) of Meeting to sharath (minister) in the qadash (holy) place.
"You shall take the ayal (ram) of consecration, and boil its flesh in a qadawash (holy) place.
Aharawan and his ban (sons) shall akal (eat) the flesh of the ayal (ram), and the lacham (bread) that is in the basket, at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
They shall akal (eat) those things with which kapar (atonement) was made, to malaa (consecrate) and qadash (sanctify) them: but a stranger shall not akal (eat) of it, because they are qadash (holy).

If anything of the flesh of the consecration, or of the lacham (bread), yathar (remains) to the baqar (morning), then you shall sharap (burn) the remainder with ash (fire): it shall not be eaten, because it is qadash (holy).
"You shall do so to Aharawan, and to his ban (sons), according to all that I have tzawah (commanded) you. You shall malaa (consecrate) them shabai (seven) yawam (days).

Every yawam (day) you shall ishah (offer) the bull of chataah (sin) offering for kapar (atonement): and you shall chataa (cleanse) the mazabach (altar), when you make kapar (atonement) for it; and you shall mashach (anoint) it, to qadash (sanctify) it.

shabai (seven) yawam (days) you shall make kapar (atonement) for the mazabach (altar), and qadash (sanctify) it: and the mazabach (altar) shall be most qadash (holy); whatever touches the mazabach (altar) shall be qadash (holy).
"Now this is that which you shall ishah (offer) on the mazabach (altar): shanayam (two) lambs a Shanah old yawam (day) by yawam (day) continually.
The one lamb you shall ishah (offer) in the baqar (morning); and the other lamb you shall ishah (offer) at evening:

and with the one lamb a isharawan (tenth) part of an ephah of fine flour mixed with the rabai (fourth) part of a hin of Kathayath shaman (oil), and the rabayaiy (fourth) part of a hin of yayan (wine) for a drink nasak (offering).

The other lamb you shall ishah (offer) at evening, and shall do to it according to the meal manachah (offering) of the baqar (morning), and according to its drink nasak (offering), for a pleasant aroma, an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah.

It shall be a continual burnt ilah (offering) throughout your dawar (generations) at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting panayam (before) Yahawah, where I will meet with you, to dabar (speak) there to you.
There I will meet with the children of Yasharaal (Israel); and the qadash (place) shall be sanctified by my kabawad (glory).
I will qadash (sanctify) the ahal (tent) of Meeting and the mazabach (altar): Aharawan also and his ban (sons) I will qadash (sanctify), to kahan (minister) to me in the priest's office.
I will shakan (dwell) among the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and will be their Alahayam.
They shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah their Alahayam, who brought them yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, that I might shakan (dwell) among them: I am Yahawah their Alahayam.
"You shall ishah (make) an mazabach (altar) to maqatar (burn) incense on. You shall ishah (make) it of acacia itz (wood).
Its arak (length) shall be a amah (cubit), and its breadth a amah (cubit). It shall be square, and its height shall be two amah (cubits). Its qaran (horns) shall be of one piece with it.
You shall overlay it with tahawar (pure) gold, its top, its sides around it, and its qaran (horns); and you shall ishah (make) a gold molding around it.

You shall ishah (make) shanayam (two) golden rings for it under its molding; on its shanayam (two) ribs, on its shanayam (two) sides you shall ishah (make) them; and they shall be for bayath (places) for poles with which to nashaa (bear) it.
You shall ishah (make) the poles of acacia itz (wood), and overlay them with gold.

You shall nathan (put) it panayam (before) the parakath (veil) that is by the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony), panayam (before) the kaparath (mercy) seat that is over the idawath (testimony), where I will meet with you.
Aharawan shall qatar (burn) incense of sweet spices on it every baqar (morning). When he tends the nayar (lamps), he shall qatar (burn) it.
When Aharawan ilah (lights) the nayar (lamps) at evening, he shall qatar (burn) it, a perpetual qatar (incense) panayam (before) Yahawah throughout your dawar (generations).
You shall ilah (offer) no zawar (strange) incense on it, nor burnt ilah (offering), nor meal manachah (offering); and you shall pour no drink nasak (offering) on it.

Aharawan shall make kapar (atonement) on its qaran (horns) achad (once) in the Shanah; with the dam (blood) of the chataah (sin) offering of kapar (atonement) achad (once) in the Shanah he shall make kapar (atonement) for it throughout your dawar (generations). It is most qadash (holy) to Yahawah.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"When you nashaa (take) a census of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), according to those who are numbered among them, then each ayash (man) shall nathan (give) a kapar (ransom) for his napash (soul) to Yahawah, when you paqad (number) them; that there be no nagap (plague) among them when you paqad (number) them.

They shall nathan (give) this, everyone who passes over to those who are numbered, half a shekel after the shekel of the qadash (sanctuary); (the shekel is isharayam (twenty) gerahs;) half a shekel for an tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah.
Everyone who passes over to those who are numbered, from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, shall nathan (give) the tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah.

The Ishayar shall not give more, and the Dal shall not give less, than the half shekel, when they nathan (give) the tharawamah (offering) of Yahawah, to make kapar (atonement) for your napash (souls).

You shall take the kapar (atonement) kasap (money) from the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and shall nathan (appoint) it for the ibadah (service) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting; that it may be a zakarawan (memorial) for the children of Yasharaal (Israel) panayam (before) Yahawah, to make kapar (atonement) for your napash (souls).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"You shall also ishah (make) a basin of brass, and its kan (base) of brass, in which to wash. You shall nathan (put) it between the ahal (tent) of Meeting and the mazabach (altar), and you shall nathan (put) mayam (water) in it.
Aharawan and his ban (sons) shall wash their yad (hands) and their feet in it.

When they bawaa (go) into the ahal (tent) of Meeting, they shall wash with mayam (water), that they not mawath (die); or when they come near to the mazabach (altar) to sharath (minister), to qatar (burn) an offering made by ashah (fire) to Yahawah.

So they shall wash their yad (hands) and their feet, that they not mawath (die): and it shall be a chaq (statute) iwalam (forever) to them, even to him and to his descendants throughout their dawar (generations).
Moreover Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"Also take fine spices: of liquid myrrh, chamash (five) maah (hundred) shekels; and of fragrant cinnamon half as much, even two maah (hundred) and chamashayam (fifty); and of fragrant cane, two maah (hundred) and chamashayam (fifty);
and of cassia chamash (five) maah (hundred), after the shekel of the qadash (sanctuary); and a hin of olive shaman (oil).

You shall ishah (make) it a qadash (holy) mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), a perfume compounded after the maishah (art) of the perfumer: it shall be a qadash (holy) mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil).
You shall use it to mashach (anoint) the ahal (tent) of Meeting, the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony),
the table and all its articles, the lampstand and its accessories, the mazabach (altar) of incense,
the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering) with all its utensils, and the basin with its kan (base).
You shall qadash (sanctify) them, that they may be most qadash (holy). Whatever touches them shall be qadash (holy).
You shall mashach (anoint) Aharawan and his ban (sons), and qadash (sanctify) them, that they may kahan (minister) to me in the priest's office.
You shall dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, ‘This shall be a qadash (holy) mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil) to me throughout your dawar (generations).
It shall not be poured on adam (man's) flesh, neither shall you ishah (make) any like it, according to its composition: it is qadash (holy). It shall be qadash (holy) to you.
Whoever compounds any like it, or whoever nathan (puts) any of it on a stranger, he shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people).'
Yahawah said to Mashah, "Take to yourself sweet spices, gum resin, and onycha, and galbanum; sweet spices with zak (pure) frankincense: there shall be an equal weight of bad (each);
and you shall ishah (make) incense of it, a perfume after the maishah (art) of the perfumer, seasoned with salt, tahawar (pure) and qadash (holy):

and you shall beat some of it very small, and nathan (put) some of it panayam (before) the idawath (testimony) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting, where I will meet with you. It shall be to you most qadash (holy).
The incense which you shall ishah (make), according to its composition you shall not ishah (make) for yourselves: it shall be to you qadash (holy) for Yahawah.
Whoever shall ishah (make) any like that, to rawach (smell) of it, he shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"raah (see), I have called by sham (name) Batzalaal the ban (son) of Awaray, the ban (son) of Chawar, of the matah (tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah):
and I have filled him with the rawach (spirit) of Alahayam, in chakamah (wisdom), and in thabawan (understanding), and in daith (knowledge), and in all kinds of workmanship,
to chashab (devise) skillful machashabah (works), to ishah (work) in gold, and in kasap (silver), and in brass,
and in cutting of aban (stones) for setting, and in carving of itz (wood), to ishah (work) in all kinds of workmanship.

I, behold, I have appointed Ahalayaab him Oholiab, the ban (son) of Achayasamak, of the matah (tribe) Dan Dan; and in the lab (heart) of all who are wise-hearted I have nathan (put) chakamah (wisdom), that they may ishah (make) all that I have tzawah (commanded) you:
the ahal (tent) of Meeting, the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony), the kaparath (mercy) seat that is on it, all the furniture of the ahal (tent),
the table and its vessels, the tahawar (pure) lampstand with all its vessels, the mazabach (altar) of incense,
the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering) with all its vessels, the basin and its kan (base),
the finely worked garments—the qadash (holy) bagad (garments) for Aharawan the priest—the bagad (garments) of his ban (sons) to kahan (minister) in the priest's office,
the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and the incense of sweet spices for the qadash (holy) place: according to all that I have tzawah (commanded) you they shall do.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (speak) also to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, ‘Most ak (certainly) you shall shamar (keep) my shabath (sabbaths): for it is a awath (sign) between me and you throughout your dawar (generations); that you may yadai (know) that I am Yahawah who qadash (sanctifies) you.

You shall shamar (keep) the shabath (sabbath) therefore; for it is qadash (holy) to you. Everyone who chalal (profanes) it shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death); for whoever does any malaakah (work) therein, that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from qarab (among) his im (people).

shash (six) yawam (days) shall malaakah (work) be done, but on the shabayaiy (seventh) day is a shabath (sabbath) of solemn shabathawan (rest), qadash (holy) to Yahawah. Whoever does any malaakah (work) on the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day) shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death).
