Therefore the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shall shamar (keep) the shabath (sabbath), to ishah (observe) the shabath (sabbath) throughout their dawar (generations), for a perpetual barayath (covenant).

It is a awath (sign) between me and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) iwalam (forever); for in shash (six) yawam (days) Yahawah made shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth), and on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) he rested, and was refreshed.'
He gave to Mashah, when he finished speaking with him on har (mount) Sayanay, the shanayam (two) tablets of the idawath (testimony), aban (stone) tablets, written with alahayam (god's) finger.

When the im (people) saw that Mashah delayed to yarad (come) down from the har (mountain), the im (people) gathered themselves together to Aharawan, and said to him, "Come, ishah (make) us Alahayam, which shall yalak (go) panayam (before) us; for as for this Mashah, the ayash (man) who brought us up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, we don't yadai (know) what has become of him.
Aharawan said to them, "Take off the golden rings, which are in the ears of your wives, of your ban (sons), and of your bath (daughters), and bawaa (bring) them to me.
All the im (people) took off the golden rings which were in their ears, and brought them to Aharawan.

He received what they yad (handed) him, and fashioned it with an engraving tool, and made it a molten calf; and they said, "These are your Alahayam, Yasharaal (Israel), which brought you up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
When Aharawan saw this, he built an mazabach (altar) panayam (before) it; and Aharawan made a proclamation, and said, "Tomorrow shall be a chag (feast) to Yahawah.

They rose up shakam (early) on the next macharath (day), and offered burnt ilah (offerings), and brought shalam (peace) offerings; and the im (people) sat down to akal (eat) and to drink, and rose up to play.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, "yalak (go), yarad (get) down; for your im (people), who you brought up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, have corrupted themselves!

They have turned aside Mahar out of the darak (way) which I tzawah (commanded) them. They have made themselves a molten calf, and have worshiped it, and have sacrificed to it, and said, ‘These are your Alahayam, Yasharaal (Israel), which brought you up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.'
Yahawah said to Mashah, "I have seen these im (people), and Qashah, they are a stiff-necked im (people).
Now therefore leave me yanach (alone), that my ap (wrath) may charah (burn) hot against them, and that I may kalah (consume) them; and I will ishah (make) of you a gadawal (great) gaway (nation).

Mashah begged Yahawah his Alahayam, and said, "Yahawah, why does your ap (wrath) charah (burn) hot against your im (people), that you have brought out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam with gadawal (great) kach (power) and with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand)?

Why should the Matzarayam (Egyptians) amar (speak), saying, ‘He brought them forth for rai (evil), to harag (kill) them in the har (mountains), and to kalah (consume) them from the surface of the adamah (earth)?' shawab (turn back / repent) from your charawan (fierce) ap (wrath), and nacham (repent) of this rai (evil) against your im (people).

zakar (remember) Abaraham, Yatzachaq, and Yasharaal (Israel), your ibad (servants), to whom you swore by your own self, and said to them, ‘I will multiply your zarai (seed) as the kawakab (stars) of the sky, and all this aratz (land) that I have spoken of I will nathan (give) to your zarai (seed), and they shall nachal (inherit) it iwalam (forever).'
Yahawah repented of the rai (evil) which he said he would do to his im (people).

Mashah turned, and went down from the har (mountain), with the shanayam (two) tablets of the idawath (testimony) in his yad (hand); tablets that were written on shanayam (both) their ibar (sides); on the one side and on the other they were written.
The tablets were the maishah (work) of Alahayam, and the writing was the writing of Alahayam, engraved on the tables.
When Yahawashawai heard the qawal (noise) of the im (people) as they shouted, he said to Mashah, "There is the qawal (noise) of war in the machanah (camp).
He said, "It isn't the qawal (voice) of those who shout for victory, neither is it the qawal (voice) of those who cry for being overcome; but the qawal (noise) of those who sing that I hear.

It happened, as soon as he came qarab (near) to the machanah (camp), that he saw the calf and the dancing: and Mashah' ap (anger) grew charah (hot), and he threw the tablets out of his yad (hands), and broke them beneath the har (mountain).

He took the calf which they had made, and burnt it with ash (fire), tachan (ground) it to powder, and scattered it on the mayam (water), and made the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shaqah (drink) of it.
Mashah said to Aharawan, "What did these im (people) do to you, that you have brought a gadawal (great) chataah (sin) on them?
Aharawan said, "Don't let the ap (anger) of my Adawan grow charah (hot). You yadai (know) the im (people), that they are set on rai (evil).

For they said to me, ‘ishah (make) us Alahayam, which shall yalak (go) panayam (before) us; for as for this Mashah, the ayash (man) who brought us up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, we don't yadai (know) what has become of him.'
I said to them, ‘Whoever has any gold, let them take it off:' so they gave it to me; and I threw it into the ash (fire), and out came this calf.
When Mashah saw that the im (people) had broken loose, (for Aharawan had let them loose for a derision among their qawam (enemies)),
then Mashah stood in the gate of the machanah (camp), and said, "Whoever is on yahawah (yahweh's) side, come to me!" All the ban (sons) of Laway gathered themselves asap (together) to him.

He said to them, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘Every ayash (man) shawam (put) his charab (sword) on his thigh, and ibar (go) shawab (turn back / repent) and forth from gate to gate throughout the machanah (camp), and every ayash (man) harag (kill) his ach (brother), and every ayash (man) his rai (companion), and every ayash (man) his neighbor.'
The ban (sons) of Laway did according to the dabar (word) of Mashah: and there napal (fell) of the im (people) that yawam (day) about shalawash (three) alap (thousand) men.

Mashah said, "malaa (consecrate) yourselves today to Yahawah, yes, every ayash (man) against his ban (son), and against his ach (brother); that he may nathan (bestow) on you a barakah (blessing) this yawam (day).

It happened on the next macharath (day), that Mashah said to the im (people), "You have sinned a gadawal (great) chataah (sin). Now I will ilah (go) up to Yahawah. Perhaps I shall make kapar (atonement) for your chataah (sin).
Mashah returned to Yahawah, and said, "Oh, this im (people) have sinned a gadawal (great) chataah (sin), and have made themselves Alahayam of gold.
Yet now, if you will, nashaa (forgive) their sin—and if not, please machah (blot) me out of your book which you have written.
Yahawah said to Mashah, "Whoever has sinned against me, him will I machah (blot) out of my book.

Now yalak (go), lead the im (people) to the place of which I have spoken to you. Behold, my malaak (angel) shall yalak (go) panayam (before) you. Nevertheless in the yawam (day) when I paqad (punish), I will paqad (punish) them for their chataah (sin).
Yahawah struck the im (people), because they made the calf, which Aharawan made.

Yahawah spoke to Mashah, "Depart, ilah (go) up from here, you and the im (people) that you have brought up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, to the aratz (land) of which I swore to Abaraham, to Yatzachaq, and to Yaiqab, saying, ‘I will nathan (give) it to your zarai (seed).'

I will shalach (send) an malaak (angel) panayam (before) you; and I will drive out the Kanainay (Canaanite), the Amaray (Amorite), and the Chathay (Hittite), and the Parazay (Perizzite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite):
to a aratz (land) flowing with milk and honey: for I will not ilah (go) up in the qarab (midst) Qashah you, for you are a stiff-necked im (people), lest I kalah (consume) you in the darak (way).
When the im (people) heard this rai (evil) news, they mourned: and no one shayath (put) on his jewelry.

Yahawah said to Mashah, "amar (tell) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘You are a Qashah im (people). If I were to ilah (go) up into your qarab (midst) for one moment, I would kalah (consume) you. Therefore now yarad (take) off your jewelry from you, that I may yadai (know) what to do to you.'
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) stripped themselves of their jewelry from har (mount) Charab onward.

Now Mashah used to take the ahal (tent) and to natah (pitch) it outside the machanah (camp), rachaq (far) away from the machanah (camp), and he called it "The ahal (tent) of Meeting." It happened that everyone who sought Yahawah went out to the ahal (tent) of Meeting, which was outside the machanah (camp).
It happened that when Mashah went out to the ahal (tent), that all the im (people) rose up, and stood, everyone at their ahal (tent) door, and watched Mashah, until he had gone into the ahal (tent).
It happened, when Mashah entered into the ahal (tent), that the pillar of cloud descended, stood at the door of the ahal (tent), and spoke with Mashah.
All the im (people) saw the pillar of cloud imad (stand) at the door of the ahal (tent), and all the im (people) rose up and worshiped, everyone at their ahal (tent) door.

Yahawah spoke to Mashah panayam (face) to panayam (face), as a ayash (man) dabar (speaks) to his rai (friend). He turned again into the machanah (camp), but his sharath (servant) Yahawashawai, the ban (son) of Nawan, a nair (young) man, didn't depart out of the ahal (tent).

Mashah said to Yahawah, "raah (see), you amar (tell) me, ‘ilah (bring) up this im (people):' and you haven't let me yadai (know) whom you will shalach (send) with me. Yet you have said, ‘I yadai (know) you by sham (name), and you have also found favor in my iyan (sight).'

Now therefore, if I have found favor in your iyan (sight), please show me now your darak (ways), that I may yadai (know) you, so that I may matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (sight): and raah (see) that this gaway (nation) is your im (people).
He said, "My panayam (presence) will yalak (go) with you, and I will give you nawach (rest).
He said to him, "If your panayam (presence) doesn't halak (go) with me, don't ilah (carry) us up from here.

For how would people yadai (know) that I have found favor in your iyan (sight), I and your im (people)? Isn't it in that you yalak (go) with us, so that we are separated, I and your im (people), from all the im (people) who are on the surface of the adamah (earth)?
Yahawah said to Mashah, "I will do this thing also that you have spoken; for you have found favor in my iyan (sight), and I yadai (know) you by sham (name).
He said, "Please show me your kabawad (glory).

He said, "I will make all my goodness ibar (pass) before you, and will qaraa (proclaim) the sham (name) of Yahawah panayam (before) you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show racham (mercy) on whom I will show racham (mercy).
He said, "You cannot raah (see) my panayam (face), for adam (man) may not raah (see) me and chayay (live).
Yahawah also said, "Behold, there is a place by me, and you shall natzab (stand) on the tzawar (rock).
It will happen, while my kabawad (glory) passes by, that I will shawam (put) you in a cleft of the tzawar (rock), and will cover you with my kap (hand) until I have passed by;
then I will sawar (take) away my kap (hand), and you will raah (see) my back; but my panayam (face) shall not be seen.

Yahawah said to Mashah, "Chisel shanayam (two) aban (stone) tablets like the raashawan (first): and I will kathab (write) on the tablets the dabar (words) that were on the raashawan (first) tablets, which you broke.
Be kawan (ready) by the baqar (morning), and ilah (come) up in the baqar (morning) to har (mount) Sayanay, and natzab (present) yourself there to me on the raash (top) of the har (mountain).
No one shall ilah (come) up with you; neither let anyone be seen throughout all the har (mountain); neither let the flocks nor herds raih (feed) before that har (mountain).

He chiseled shanayam (two) tablets of aban (stone) like the raashawan (first); and Mashah rose up shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and went up to har (mount) Sayanay, as Yahawah had tzawah (commanded) him, and took in his yad (hand) shanayam (two) aban (stone) tablets.
Yahawah descended in the cloud, and stood with him there, and proclaimed the sham (name) of Yahawah.
Yahawah passed by panayam (before) him, and proclaimed, "Yahawah! Yahawah, a Rachawam and Chanawan Al, Arak to anger, and abundant in loving chasad (kindness) and truth,

keeping loving chasad (kindness) for alap (thousands), forgiving iwan (iniquity) and disobedience and chataah (sin); and that will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iwan (iniquity) of the abawath (fathers) on the children, and on the children's children, on the shalash (third) and on the rabai (fourth) generation.
Mashah hurried and bowed his qadad (head) toward the aratz (earth), and worshiped.

He said, "If now I have found favor in your iyan (sight), Adanay, please let the Adanay yalak (go) in the midst Qashah us; although this is a stiff-necked im (people); pardon our iwan (iniquity) and our chataah (sin), and take us for your nachal (inheritance).

He said, "Behold, I karath (make) a barayath (covenant): before all your im (people) I will do marvels, such as have not been worked in all the aratz (earth), nor in any gawayam (nation); and all the im (people) qarab (among) which you are shall raah (see) the maishah (work) of Yahawah; for it is an awesome thing that I do with you.

shamar (observe) that which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day). Behold, I drive out panayam (before) you the Amaray (Amorite), the Kanainay (Canaanite), the Chathay (Hittite), the Parazay (Perizzite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite).
Be careful, lest you karath (make) a barayath (covenant) with the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land) where you are going, lest it be for a snare in the qarab (midst) of you:
but you shall shabar (break) down their mazabach (altars), and dash in pieces their matzabah (pillars), and you shall karath (cut) down their Asharah;
for you shall shachah (worship) no other Al: for Yahawah, whose sham (name) is Qanaa, is a Qanaa Al.

"Don't karath (make) a barayath (covenant) with the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land), lest they play the prostitute achar (after) their Alahayam, and zabach (sacrifice) to their Alahayam, and one qaraa (call) you and you akal (eat) of his zabach (sacrifice);

and you take of their bath (daughters) to your ban (sons), and their bath (daughters) play the prostitute achar (after) their Alahayam, and make your ban (sons) play the prostitute achar (after) their Alahayam.
"You shall ishah (make) no cast idols for yourselves.

"You shall shamar (keep) the chag (feast) of unleavened matzah (bread). shabai (seven) yawam (days) you shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread), as I tzawah (commanded) you, at the mawaid (time) appointed in the chadash (month) Abib; for in the chadash (month) Abib you came out from Matzarayam.
"All that opens the womb is mine; and all your livestock that is zakar (male), the firstborn of cow and sheep.

The firstborn of a donkey you shall padah (redeem) with a lamb: and if you will not padah (redeem) it, then you shall break its neck. All the firstborn of your ban (sons) you shall padah (redeem). No one shall raah (see) panayam (before) me empty.
"shash (six) yawam (days) you shall ibad (work), but on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) you shall shabath (rest): in plowing time and in harvest you shall shabath (rest).
"You shall ishah (observe) the chag (feast) of shabawai (weeks) with the bakawar (first) fruits of wheat harvest, and the chag (feast) of harvest at the Shanah end.
Three times in the Shanah all your males shall raah (see) panayam (before) the Adawan Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).

For I will yarash (drive) out gawayam (nations) panayam (before) you and enlarge your borders; neither shall any ayash (man) desire your aratz (land) when you ilah (go) up to raah (see) panayam (before) Yahawah, your Alahayam, three times in the Shanah.

"You shall not offer the dam (blood) of my zabach (sacrifice) with leavened bread; neither shall the zabach (sacrifice) of the chag (feast) of the pasach (passover) be lawan (left) to the baqar (morning).

"You shall bring the raashayath (first) of the raashayath (first) bakawar (fruits) of your adamah (ground) to the bayath (house) of Yahawah your Alahayam. "You shall not boil a young goat in its am (mother's) milk.
Yahawah said to Mashah, "kathab (write) you these dabar (words): for in accordance with these dabar (words) I have made a barayath (covenant) with you and with Yasharaal (Israel).

He was there with Yahawah arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights); he neither ate lacham (bread), nor drank mayam (water). He wrote on the tablets the dabar (words) of the barayath (covenant), the ishar (ten) commandments.

It happened, when Mashah came down from har (mount) Sayanay with the shanayam (two) tablets of the idawath (testimony) in Mashah' yad (hand), when he came down from the har (mountain), that Mashah didn't yadai (know) that the skin of his panayam (face) shone by reason of his speaking with him.
When Aharawan and all the children of Yasharaal (Israel) saw Mashah, behold, the skin of his panayam (face) shone; and they were yaraa (afraid) to come near him.
Mashah called to them, and Aharawan and all the nashayaa (rulers) of the idah (congregation) returned to him; and Mashah spoke to them.
Afterward all the children of Yasharaal (Israel) came near, and he gave them all of the commandments that Yahawah had spoken with him on har (mount) Sayanay.
When Mashah was kalah (done) speaking with them, he nathan (put) a masawah (veil) on his panayam (face).

But when Mashah went in panayam (before) Yahawah to dabar (speak) with him, he took the masawah (veil) off, until he came out; and he came out, and spoke to the children of Yasharaal (Israel) that which he was tzawah (commanded).

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) saw Mashah' panayam (face), that the skin of Mashah' panayam (face) shone: and Mashah shawab (turn back / repent) the masawah (veil) on his panayam (face) again, until he went in to dabar (speak) with him.
Mashah assembled all the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and said to them, "These are the dabar (words) which Yahawah has tzawah (commanded), that you should do them.

‘shash (six) yawam (days) shall malaakah (work) be done, but on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) there shall be a qadash (holy) day for you, a shabath (sabbath) of solemn shabathawan (rest) to Yahawah: whoever does any malaakah (work) in it shall be put to mawath (death).
You shall bair (kindle) no ash (fire) throughout your habitations on the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day).'
Mashah spoke to all the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "This is the thing which Yahawah tzawah (commanded), saying,

‘Take from among you an tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah. Whoever is of a nadayab (willing) lab (heart), let him bawaa (bring) it, yahawah (yahweh's) tharawamah (offering): gold, kasap (silver), brass,
blue, purple, scarlet, Shash linen, goats' hair,
ayal (rams)' skins dyed red, thachash (sea) cow hides, acacia itz (wood),
shaman (oil) for the maawar (light), spices for the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil) and for the sweet incense,
onyx aban (stones), and aban (stones) to be set for the apawad (ephod) and for the breastplate.
"‘Let every wise-hearted man among you bawaa (come), and ishah (make) all that Yahawah has tzawah (commanded):
the mashakan (tabernacle), its outer covering, its roof, its clasps, its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its sockets;
the arawan (ark), and its poles, the kaparath (mercy) seat, the parakath (veil) of the screen;
the table with its poles and all its vessels, and the show bread;
the lampstand also for the maawar (light), with its vessels, its nayar (lamps), and the shaman (oil) for the maawar (light);
and the mazabach (altar) of incense with its poles, the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), the sweet incense, the screen for the door, at the door of the mashakan (tabernacle);
the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering), with its grating of brass, it poles, and all its vessels, the basin and its kan (base);
the hangings of the court, its pillars, their sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court;
the pins of the mashakan (tabernacle), the pins of the court, and their cords;

the finely worked bagad (garments), for ministering in the qadash (holy) place, the qadash (holy) bagad (garments) for Aharawan the kahan (priest), and the bagad (garments) of his ban (sons), to kahan (minister) in the priest's office.'
All the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) departed from the panayam (presence) of Mashah.

They came, everyone whose lab (heart) stirred him up, and everyone whom his rawach (spirit) made willing, and brought yahawah (yahweh's) tharawamah (offering), for the malaakah (work) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and for all of its ibadah (service), and for the qadash (holy) bagad (garments).

They came, both men and women, as many as were willing-hearted, and brought brooches, earrings, signet rings, and armlets, all jewels of gold; even every ayash (man) who offered an thanawapah (offering) of gold to Yahawah.
Everyone, with whom was found blue, purple, scarlet, Shash linen, goats' hair, ayal (rams)' skins dyed red, and thachash (sea) cow hides, brought them.

Everyone who offered an tharawamah (offering) of kasap (silver) and brass brought yahawah (yahweh's) tharawamah (offering); and everyone, with whom was found acacia itz (wood) for any malaakah (work) of the ibadah (service), brought it.
All the women who were wise-hearted spun with their yad (hands), and brought that which they had spun, the blue, the purple, the scarlet, and the Shash linen.
All the women whose lab (heart) stirred them up in chakamah (wisdom) spun the goats' hair.
The nashayaa (rulers) brought the onyx aban (stones), and the aban (stones) to be set, for the apawad (ephod) and for the breastplate;
and the spice, and the shaman (oil) for the maawar (light), for the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and for the sweet incense.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) brought a freewill nadabah (offering) to Yahawah; every ayash (man) and ashah (woman), whose lab (heart) made them willing to bawaa (bring) for all the malaakah (work), which Yahawah had tzawah (commanded) to be made by Mashah.

Mashah said to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), "raah (see), Yahawah has called by sham (name) Batzalaal the ban (son) of Awaray, the ban (son) of Chawar, of the matah (tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah).
He has filled him with the rawach (spirit) of Alahayam, in chakamah (wisdom), in thabawan (understanding), in daith (knowledge), and in all kinds of workmanship;
and to make skillful machashabah (works), to ishah (work) in gold, in kasap (silver), in brass,
in cutting of aban (stones) for setting, and in carving of itz (wood), to ishah (work) in all kinds of skillful workmanship.
He has nathan (put) in his lab (heart) that he may teach, Ahalayaab he, and Oholiab, the ban (son) of Achayasamak, of the matah (tribe) Dan Dan.

He has filled them with chakamah (wisdom) of lab (heart), to ishah (work) all kinds of workmanship, of the engraver, of the skillful chashab (workman), and of the raqam (embroiderer), in blue, in purple, in scarlet, and in Shash linen, and of the weaver, even of those who do any workmanship, and of those who make skillful malaakah (works).

"Batzalaal and Ahalayaab shall ishah (work) with every wise-hearted ayash (man), in whom Yahawah has nathan (put) chakamah (wisdom) and thabawan (understanding) to yadai (know) how to ishah (work) all the ishah (work) for the ibadah (service) of the qadash (sanctuary), according to all that Yahawah has tzawah (commanded).

Mashah called Batzalaal and Ahalayaab, and every wise-hearted ayash (man), in whose lab (heart) Yahawah had nathan (put) chakamah (wisdom), even everyone whose lab (heart) stirred him up to qarab (come) to the malaakah (work) to do it:

and they received from Mashah all the tharawamah (offering) which the children of Yasharaal (Israel) had brought for the malaakah (work) of the ibadah (service) of the qadash (sanctuary), with which to ishah (make) it. They brought yet to him freewill nadabah (offerings) every baqar (morning).
All the chakam (wise) men, who performed all the malaakah (work) of the qadash (sanctuary), ayash (each) came from his malaakah (work) which they did.
They spoke to Mashah, saying, "The im (people) bawaa (bring) much more than enough for the ibadah (service) of the malaakah (work) which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) to ishah (make).

Mashah gave commandment, and they caused it to be proclaimed throughout the machanah (camp), saying, "Let neither ayash (man) nor ashah (woman) ishah (make) anything else for the tharawamah (offering) for the qadash (sanctuary)." So the im (people) were restrained from bringing.
For the stuff they had was sufficient for all the malaakah (work) to ishah (make) it, and yathar (too) much.

All the wise-hearted men among those who did the malaakah (work) made the mashakan (tabernacle) with ishar (ten) curtains; of fine twined Shash, blue, purple, and scarlet, with karawab (cherubim), the maishah (work) of the skillful ishah (workman), they made them.
The arak (length) of achad (each) curtain was isharayam (twenty) shamanah (eight) amah (cubits), and the breadth of achad (each) curtain arabai (four) amah (cubits). All the curtains had one measure.
He coupled chamash (five) curtains to one another, and the other chamash (five) curtains he coupled one to another.
He made loops of blue on the shapah (edge) of the one curtain from the edge in the coupling. Likewise he made in the shapah (edge) of the curtain that was Qayatzawan in the shanay (second) coupling.

He made chamashayam (fifty) loops in the one curtain, and he made chamashayam (fifty) loops in the edge of the curtain that was in the shanay (second) coupling. The loops were opposite one to another.
He made chamashayam (fifty) clasps of gold, and coupled the curtains one to another with the clasps: so the mashakan (tabernacle) was a unit.
He made curtains of goats' hair for a ahal (covering) over the mashakan (tabernacle). He made them ishathay (eleven) curtains.

The arak (length) of achad (each) curtain was shalawashayam (thirty) amah (cubits), and arabai (four) amah (cubits) the breadth of achad (each) curtain. The ishathay (eleven) curtains had one measure.
He coupled chamash (five) curtains by themselves, and shash (six) curtains by themselves.

He made chamashayam (fifty) loops on the shapah (edge) of the curtain that was Qayatzawan in the coupling, and he made chamashayam (fifty) loops on the shapah (edge) of the curtain which was outmost in the shanay (second) coupling.
He made chamashayam (fifty) clasps of brass to couple the ahal (tent) together, that it might be a unit.
He made a covering for the ahal (tent) of ayal (rams)' skins dyed red, and a covering of thachash (sea) cow hides above.
He made the boards for the mashakan (tabernacle) of acacia itz (wood), standing up.
ishar (ten) amah (cubits) was the arak (length) of a board, and a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) the breadth of achad (each) board.
achad (each) board had shanayam (two) tenons, joined one to another. He made all the boards of the mashakan (tabernacle) this way.
He made the boards for the mashakan (tabernacle): isharayam (twenty) boards for the Nagab side southward.

He made arabaiyam (forty) sockets of kasap (silver) under the isharayam (twenty) boards; shanayam (two) sockets under one board for its shanayam (two) tenons, and shanayam (two) sockets under another board for its shanayam (two) tenons.
For the shanay (second) side of the mashakan (tabernacle), on the tzapawan (north) side, he made isharayam (twenty) boards,
and their arabaiyam (forty) sockets of kasap (silver); shanayam (two) sockets under one board, and shanayam (two) sockets under another board.
For the far part of the mashakan (tabernacle) westward he made shash (six) boards.
He made shanayam (two) boards for the corners of the mashakan (tabernacle) in the far part.
They were Thaam beneath, and Thaam the same yachad (way) they were all the way to its raash (top) to one ring. He did this to shanayam (both) of them in the shanayam (two) corners.
There were shamanah (eight) boards, and their sockets of kasap (silver), sixteen sockets; under achad (every) board shanayam (two) sockets.
He made bars of acacia itz (wood); chamash (five) for the boards of the one side of the mashakan (tabernacle),
and chamash (five) bars for the boards of the other side of the mashakan (tabernacle), and chamash (five) bars for the boards of the mashakan (tabernacle) for the hinder part westward.
He made the Thayakawan bar to pass through in the midst of the boards from the qatzah (one) end to the other.
He overlaid the boards with gold, and made their rings of gold for bayath (places) for the bars, and overlaid the bars with gold.
He made the parakath (veil) of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined Shash: with karawab (cherubim). He made it the maishah (work) of a skillful chashab (workman).
He made arabai (four) pillars of acacia for it, and overlaid them with gold. Their hooks were of gold. He cast arabai (four) sockets of kasap (silver) for them.
He made a screen for the door of the ahal (tent), of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined Shash, the raqam (work) of an embroiderer;
and the chamash (five) pillars of it with their hooks. He overlaid their capitals and their fillets with gold, and their chamash (five) sockets were of brass.

Batzalaal made the arawan (ark) of acacia itz (wood). Its arak (length) was chatzay (two) and a half amah (cubits), and its breadth a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half), and a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) its height.
He overlaid it with tahawar (pure) gold bayath (inside) and outside, and made a molding of gold for it around it.
He cast arabai (four) rings of gold for it, in its arabai (four) feet; even shanayam (two) rings on its one side, and shanayam (two) rings on its other side.
He made poles of acacia itz (wood), and overlaid them with gold.
He bawaa (put) the poles into the rings on the sides of the arawan (ark), to nashaa (bear) the arawan (ark).
He made a kaparath (mercy) seat of tahawar (pure) gold. Its arak (length) was chatzay (two) and a half amah (cubits), and a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) its breadth.
He made shanayam (two) karawab (cherubim) of gold. He made them of beaten maqashah (work), at the shanayam (two) ends of the kaparath (mercy) seat;
one karawab (cherub) at the qatzah (one) end, and one karawab (cherub) at the other end. He made the karawab (cherubim) of one piece with the kaparath (mercy) seat at its shanayam (two) ends.

The karawab (cherubim) spread out their wings on high, covering the kaparath (mercy) seat with their wings, with their panayam (faces) toward one ach (another). The panayam (faces) of the karawab (cherubim) were toward the kaparath (mercy) seat.
He made the table of acacia itz (wood). Its arak (length) was two amah (cubits), and its breadth was a amah (cubit), and its height was a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half).
He overlaid it with tahawar (pure) gold, and made a gold molding around it.
He made a border of a tapach (handbreadth) around it, and made a golden molding on its border around it.
He cast arabai (four) rings of gold for it, and nathan (put) the rings in the arabai (four) corners that were on its arabai (four) feet.
The rings were close by the border, the bayath (places) for the poles to nashaa (carry) the table.
He made the poles of acacia itz (wood), and overlaid them with gold, to nashaa (carry) the table.
He made the vessels which were on the table, its dishes, its kap (spoons), its bowls, and its pitchers with which to pour out, of tahawar (pure) gold.
He made the lampstand of tahawar (pure) gold. He made the lampstand of beaten maqashah (work). Its base, its shaft, its gabayai (cups), its buds, and its flowers were of parach (one) piece with it.

There were shash (six) branches yatzaa (going) out of its sides: shalawash (three) branches of the lampstand out of its one side, and shalawash (three) branches of the lampstand out of its other side:

shalawash (three) gabayai (cups) made like almond blossoms in one branch, a bud and a flower, and shalawash (three) gabayai (cups) made like almond blossoms in the other branch, a bud and a flower: so for the shash (six) branches yatzaa (going) out of the lampstand.
In the lampstand were arabai (four) gabayai (cups) made like almond blossoms, its buds and its flowers;

and a bud under shanayam (two) branches of kapathar (one) piece with it, and a bud under shanayam (two) branches of kapathar (one) piece with it, and a bud under shanayam (two) branches of one piece with it, for the shash (six) branches yatzaa (going) out of it.
Their buds and their branches were of one piece with it. The whole thing was one beaten maqashah (work) of tahawar (pure) gold.
He made its shabai (seven) nayar (lamps), and its snuffers, and its snuff dishes, of tahawar (pure) gold.
He made it of a talent of tahawar (pure) gold, with all its vessels.

He made the mazabach (altar) of incense of acacia itz (wood). It was square: its arak (length) was a amah (cubit), and its breadth a amah (cubit). Its height was two amah (cubits). Its qaran (horns) were of one piece with it.
He overlaid it with tahawar (pure) gold, its top, its sides around it, and its qaran (horns). He made a gold molding around it.
He made shanayam (two) golden rings for it under its molding zar (crown), on its shanayam (two) ribs, on its shanayam (two) sides, for bayath (places) for poles with which to nashaa (carry) it.
He made the poles of acacia itz (wood), and overlaid them with gold.
He made the qadash (holy) mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil) and the tahawar (pure) incense of sweet spices, after the maishah (art) of the perfumer.

He made the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering) of acacia itz (wood). It was square. Its arak (length) was chamash (five) amah (cubits), its breadth was chamash (five) amah (cubits), and its height was shalawash (three) amah (cubits).
He made its qaran (horns) on its arabai (four) corners. Its qaran (horns) were of tzapah (one) piece with it, and he overlaid it with brass.
He made all the vessels of the mazabach (altar), the pots, the shovels, the basins, the forks, and the machathah (fire) pans. He made all its vessels of brass.
He made for the mazabach (altar) a grating of a network of brass, under the ledge around it beneath, reaching halfway up.
He cast arabai (four) rings for the arabai (four) ends of brass grating, to be bayath (places) for the poles.
He made the poles of acacia itz (wood), and overlaid them with brass.
He bawaa (put) the poles into the rings on the sides of the mazabach (altar), with which to nashaa (carry) it. He made it hollow with planks.
He made the basin of brass, and its kan (base) of brass, out of the mirrors of the ministering women who ministered at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
He made the court: for the Nagab side southward the hangings of the court were of fine twined Shash, one maah (hundred) amah (cubits);
their pillars were isharayam (twenty), and their sockets isharayam (twenty), of brass; the hooks of the pillars and their fillets were of kasap (silver).

For the tzapawan (north) side one maah (hundred) amah (cubits), their pillars isharayam (twenty), and their sockets isharayam (twenty), of brass; the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of kasap (silver).
For the yam (west) side were hangings of chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), their pillars ishar (ten), and their sockets ishar (ten); the hooks of the pillars, and their fillets, of kasap (silver).
For the qadam (east) side eastward chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits).
The hangings for the kathap (one) side were chamash (fifteen) amah (cubits); their pillars shalawash (three), and their sockets shalawash (three);
and so for the other side: on this hand and that hand by the gate of the court were hangings of chamash (fifteen) amah (cubits); their pillars shalawash (three), and their sockets shalawash (three).
All the hangings around the court were of fine twined Shash.

The sockets for the pillars were of brass. The hooks of the pillars and their fillets were of kasap (silver); and the overlaying of their capitals, of kasap (silver); and all the pillars of the court were filleted with kasap (silver).

The screen for the gate of the court was the raqam (work) of the embroiderer, of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined Shash. isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) was the arak (length), and the height in the breadth was chamash (five) amah (cubits), like to the hangings of the court.
Their pillars were arabai (four), and their sockets arabai (four), of brass; their hooks of kasap (silver), and the overlaying of their capitals, and their fillets, of kasap (silver).
All the pins of the mashakan (tabernacle), and around the court, were of brass.

This is the amount of material used for the mashakan (tabernacle), even the mashakan (tabernacle) of the idawath (testimony), as they were counted, according to the commandment of Mashah, for the ibadah (service) Lawayay the Levites, by the yad (hand) of Ayathamar, the ban (son) of Aharawan the kahan (priest).
Batzalaal the ban (son) of Awaray, the ban (son) of Chawar, of the matah (tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah), made all that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.

Ahalayaab him was Oholiab, the ban (son) of Achayasamak, of the matah (tribe) Dan Dan, an engraver, and a skillful chashab (workman), and an raqam (embroiderer) in blue, in purple, in scarlet, and in Shash linen.

All the gold that was used for the malaakah (work) in all the malaakah (work) of the qadash (sanctuary), even the gold of the thanawapah (offering), was isharayam (twenty) thashai (nine) talents, and shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) shekels, after the shekel of the qadash (sanctuary).

The kasap (silver) of those who were numbered of the idah (congregation) was one maah (hundred) talents, and one alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) five shekels, after the shekel of the qadash (sanctuary):

a beka a galagalath (head), that is, half a shekel, after the shekel of the qadash (sanctuary), for everyone who passed over to those who were numbered, from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, for shash (six) maah (hundred) shalawash (three) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) men.

The one maah (hundred) talents of kasap (silver) were for casting the sockets of the qadash (sanctuary), and the sockets of the parakath (veil); one maah (hundred) sockets for the one maah (hundred) talents, a talent for a socket.
Of the one alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) chamash (five) shekels he made hooks for the pillars, overlaid their capitals, and made chashaq (fillets) for them.
The brass of the thanawapah (offering) was shabaiyam (seventy) talents, and two alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred) shekels.
With this he made the sockets to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, the bronze mazabach (altar), the bronze grating for it, all the vessels of the mazabach (altar),
the sockets around the court, the sockets of the gate of the court, all the pins of the mashakan (tabernacle), and all the pins around the court.

Of the blue, purple, and scarlet, they made finely worked bagad (garments), for ministering in the qadash (holy) place, and made the qadash (holy) bagad (garments) for Aharawan; as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
He made the apawad (ephod) of gold, blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined Shash.

They beat the gold into thin plates, and cut it into wires, to ishah (work) it in the blue, in the purple, in the scarlet, and in the Shash linen, the maishah (work) of the skillful chashab (workman).
They made shoulder straps for it, joined together. At the shanayam (two) ends it was joined together.

The skillfully woven band that was on it, with which to fasten it on, was of the same piece, like its maishah (work); of gold, of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined Shash; as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
They worked the onyx aban (stones), enclosed in settings of gold, engraved with the engravings of a signet, according to the sham (names) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
He shawam (put) them on the shoulder straps of the apawad (ephod), to be aban (stones) of zakarawan (memorial) for the children of Yasharaal (Israel), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
He made the breastplate, the maishah (work) of a skillful workman, like the maishah (work) of the apawad (ephod); of gold, of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined Shash.
It was square. They made the breastplate double. Its arak (length) was a span, and its breadth a span, being double.
They malaa (set) in it arabai (four) rows of aban (stones). A row of ruby, topaz, and beryl was the achad (first) row;
and the shanay (second) row, a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald;
and the shalayashay (third) row, a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst;
and the rabayaiy (fourth) row, a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper. They were enclosed in gold settings.

The aban (stones) were according to the sham (names) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), shanayam (twelve), according to their sham (names); like the engravings of a signet, everyone according to his sham (name), for the shanayam (twelve) shabat (tribes).
They made on the breastplate chains like cords, of braided maishah (work) of tahawar (pure) gold.
They made shanayam (two) settings of gold, and shanayam (two) gold rings, and nathan (put) the shanayam (two) rings on the shanayam (two) ends of the breastplate.
They nathan (put) the shanayam (two) braided chains of gold in the shanayam (two) rings at the ends of the breastplate.

The other shanayam (two) ends of the shanayam (two) braided chains they nathan (put) on the shanayam (two) settings, and nathan (put) them on the shoulder straps of the apawad (ephod), in its panayam (front).
They made shanayam (two) rings of gold, and shawam (put) them on the shanayam (two) ends of the breastplate, on its shapah (edge), which was toward the ibar (side) of the apawad (ephod) inward.

They made shanayam (two) rings of gold, and nathan (put) them on the shanayam (two) shoulder straps of the apawad (ephod) underneath, in its panayam (front), close by its coupling, above the skillfully woven band of the apawad (ephod).

They bound the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the apawad (ephod) with a lace of blue, that it might be on the skillfully woven band of the apawad (ephod), and that the breastplate might not come loose from the apawad (ephod), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
He made the robe of the apawad (ephod) of woven maishah (work), all of blue.
The opening of the robe in its midst was like the opening of a coat of mail, with a shapah (binding) around its opening, that it should not be torn.
They made on the skirts of the robe pomegranates of blue, purple, scarlet, and twined linen.
They made bells of tahawar (pure) gold, and nathan (put) the bells between the pomegranates around the skirts of the robe, between the pomegranates;
a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, around the skirts of the robe, to sharath (minister) in, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
They made the coats of Shash linen of woven maishah (work) for Aharawan, and for his ban (sons),
and the turban of Shash linen, and the Shash headbands of Shash linen, and the Shash breeches of fine twined Shash,
and the sash of fine twined Shash, and blue, and purple, and scarlet, the raqam (work) of the embroiderer, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
They made the plate of the qadash (holy) nazar (crown) of tahawar (pure) gold, and wrote on it a writing, like the engravings of a signet: "qadash (holy) TO Yahawah.
They tied to it a lace of blue, to nathan (fasten) it on the turban above, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.

Thus all the ibadah (work) of the mashakan (tabernacle) of the mashakan (tent) of Meeting was finished. The children of Yasharaal (Israel) did according to all that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah; so they did.
They brought the mashakan (tabernacle) to Mashah, the mashakan (tent), with all its furniture, its clasps, its boards, its bars, its pillars, its sockets,
the covering of ayal (rams)' skins dyed red, the covering of thachash (sea) cow hides, the parakath (veil) of the screen,
the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony) with its poles, the kaparath (mercy) seat,
the table, all its vessels, the show bread,
the tahawar (pure) lampstand, its nayar (lamps), even the nayar (lamps) to be mairakah (set) in order, all its vessels, the shaman (oil) for the maawar (light),
the golden mazabach (altar), the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), the sweet incense, the screen for the door of the ahal (tent),
the bronze mazabach (altar), its grating of brass, its poles, all of its vessels, the basin and its kan (base),

the hangings of the court, its pillars, its sockets, the screen for the gate of the court, its cords, its pins, all the instruments of the ibadah (service) of the mashakan (tabernacle), for the mashakan (tent) of Meeting,

the finely worked bagad (garments) for ministering in the qadash (holy) place, the qadash (holy) bagad (garments) for Aharawan the kahan (priest), and the bagad (garments) of his ban (sons), to kahan (minister) in the priest's office.
According to all that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah, so the children of Yasharaal (Israel) did all the ibadah (work).
Mashah saw all the malaakah (work), and behold, they had done it as Yahawah had tzawah (commanded), even so had they done it: and Mashah blessed them.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"On the raashawan (first) yawam (day) of the achad (first) chadash (month) you shall qawam (raise) up the mashakan (tabernacle) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
You shall shawam (put) the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony) in it, and you shall screen the arawan (ark) with the parakath (veil).
You shall bawaa (bring) in the table, and set in order the things that are on it. You shall bawaa (bring) in the lampstand, and ilah (light) its nayar (lamps).
You shall nathan (set) the golden mazabach (altar) for incense panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony), and shawam (put) the screen of the door to the mashakan (tabernacle).
"You shall nathan (set) the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering) panayam (before) the door of the mashakan (tabernacle) of the mashakan (tent) of Meeting.
You shall nathan (set) the basin between the ahal (tent) of Meeting and the mazabach (altar), and shall nathan (put) mayam (water) therein.
You shall shawam (set) up the court around it, and hang up the screen of the gate of the court.

"You shall take the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and mashach (anoint) the mashakan (tabernacle), and all that is in it, and shall make it qadash (holy), and all its furniture: and it will be qadash (holy).
You shall mashach (anoint) the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering), with all its vessels, and qadash (sanctify) the mazabach (altar): and the mazabach (altar) will be most qadash (holy).
You shall mashach (anoint) the basin and its kan (base), and qadash (sanctify) it.
"You shall qarab (bring) Aharawan and his ban (sons) to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and shall wash them with mayam (water).
You shall Labash on Aharawan the qadash (holy) bagad (garments); and you shall mashach (anoint) him, and qadash (sanctify) him, that he may kahan (minister) to me in the priest's office.
You shall qarab (bring) his ban (sons), and Labash coats on them.

You shall mashach (anoint) them, as you mashach (anointed) their ab (father), that they may kahan (minister) to me in the priest's office. Their mashachah (anointing) shall be to them for an iwalam (forever) kahanah (priesthood) throughout their dawar (generations).
Mashah did so. According to all that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) him, so he did.
It happened in the raashawan (first) chadash (month) in the shanay (second) Shanah, on the raashawan (first) day of the chadash (month), that the mashakan (tabernacle) was raised up.
Mashah raised up the mashakan (tabernacle), and laid its sockets, and shawam (set) up its boards, and nathan (put) in its bars, and raised up its pillars.
He spread the ahal (covering) over the ahal (tent), and shawam (put) the roof of the mashakan (tabernacle) above on it, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
He took and nathan (put) the idawath (testimony) into the arawan (ark), and shawam (set) the poles on the arawan (ark), and nathan (put) the kaparath (mercy) seat above on the arawan (ark).

He brought the arawan (ark) into the mashakan (tabernacle), and shawam (set) up the parakath (veil) of the screen, and screened the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
He nathan (put) the table in the ahal (tent) of Meeting, on the side of the mashakan (tabernacle) northward, outside of the parakath (veil).
He irak (set) the lacham (bread) in order on it panayam (before) Yahawah, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
He shawam (put) the lampstand in the ahal (tent) of Meeting, opposite the table, on the side of the mashakan (tabernacle) Nagab.
He lit the nayar (lamps) panayam (before) Yahawah, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
He shawam (put) the golden mazabach (altar) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting panayam (before) the parakath (veil);
and he burnt incense of sweet spices on it, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
He shawam (put) up the screen of the door to the mashakan (tabernacle).

He shawam (set) the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering) at the door of the mashakan (tabernacle) of the mashakan (tent) of Meeting, and offered on it the burnt ilah (offering) and the meal manachah (offering), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
He shawam (set) the basin between the ahal (tent) of Meeting and the mazabach (altar), and nathan (put) mayam (water) therein, with which to wash.
Mashah, Aharawan, and his ban (sons) washed their yad (hands) and their feet there.
When they went into the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and when they came qarab (near) to the mazabach (altar), they washed, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
He raised up the court around the mashakan (tabernacle) and the mazabach (altar), and nathan (set) up the screen of the gate of the court. So Mashah finished the malaakah (work).
Then the cloud covered the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah filled the mashakan (tabernacle).
Mashah wasn't yakal (able) to bawaa (enter) into the ahal (tent) of Meeting, because the cloud stayed on it, and yahawah (yahweh's) kabawad (glory) filled the mashakan (tabernacle).
When the cloud was taken up from over the mashakan (tabernacle), the children of Yasharaal (Israel) went nasai (onward), throughout all their journeys;
but if the cloud wasn't taken up, then they didn't travel until the yawam (day) that it was taken up.

For the cloud of Yahawah was on the mashakan (tabernacle) by yawamam (day), and there was ash (fire) in the cloud by layal (night), in the iyan (sight) of all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), throughout all their journeys.
Yahawah called to Mashah, and spoke to him out of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, saying,

"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them, ‘When anyone of you qarab (offers) an qaraban (offering) to Yahawah, you shall qarab (offer) your qaraban (offering) of the livestock, from the herd and from the flock.

"‘If his qaraban (offering) is a burnt ilah (offering) from the herd, he shall qarab (offer) a zakar (male) thamayam (without) blemish. He shall qarab (offer) it at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, that he may be accepted panayam (before) Yahawah.
He shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the burnt ilah (offering), and it shall be accepted for him to make kapar (atonement) for him.

He shall kill the bull panayam (before) Yahawah. Aharawan ban (sons), the kahan (priests), shall qarab (present) the dam (blood) and sprinkle the dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar) that is at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
He shall flay the burnt ilah (offering), and cut it into pieces.
The ban (sons) of Aharawan the kahan (priest) shall nathan (put) ash (fire) on the mazabach (altar), and lay itz (wood) in order on the ash (fire);
and Aharawan ban (sons), the kahan (priests), shall lay the pieces, the raash (head), and the fat in order on the itz (wood) that is on the ash (fire) which is on the mazabach (altar);

but its innards and its legs he shall wash with mayam (water). The kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) the whole on the mazabach (altar), for a burnt ilah (offering), an ashah (offering) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.
"‘If his qaraban (offering) is from the flock, from the sheep, or from the goats, for a burnt ilah (offering), he shall qarab (offer) a zakar (male) thamayam (without) blemish.

He shall kill it on the tzapawan (north) side of the mazabach (altar) panayam (before) Yahawah. Aharawan ban (sons), the kahan (priests), shall sprinkle its dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar).
He shall cut it into its pieces, with its raash (head) and its fat. The kahan (priest) shall lay them in order on the itz (wood) that is on the ash (fire) which is on the mazabach (altar),

but the innards and the legs he shall wash with mayam (water). The kahan (priest) shall qarab (offer) the whole, and qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar). It is a burnt ilah (offering), an ashah (offering) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.
"‘If his ilah (offering) to Yahawah is a burnt ilah (offering) of birds, then he shall qarab (offer) his qaraban (offering) of turtledoves, or of ban (young) pigeons.

The kahan (priest) shall qarab (bring) it to the mazabach (altar), and wring off its raash (head), and qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar); and its dam (blood) shall be drained out on the side of the mazabach (altar);
and he shall sawar (take) away its crop with its filth, and cast it beside the mazabach (altar) on the qadam (east) part, in the place of the ashes.

He shall tear it by its wings, but shall not divide it apart. The kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar), on the itz (wood) that is on the ash (fire). It is a burnt ilah (offering), an ashah (offering) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.

"‘When anyone qarab (offers) an qaraban (offering) of a meal offering to Yahawah, his qaraban (offering) shall be of fine flour; and he shall pour shaman (oil) on it, and nathan (put) frankincense on it.

He shall bawaa (bring) it to Aharawan ban (sons), the kahan (priests); and he shall take his handful of its fine flour, and of its shaman (oil), with all its frankincense; and the kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) its azakarah (memorial) on the mazabach (altar), an ashah (offering) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.
That which is yathar (left) of the meal manachah (offering) shall be Aharawan and his ban (sons)'. It is a most qadash (holy) thing of the ashah (offerings) of Yahawah made by ashah (fire).

"‘When you qarab (offer) an manachah (offering) of a meal manachah (offering) baked in the oven, it shall be unleavened cakes of fine flour mixed with shaman (oil), or unleavened wafers mashach (anointed) with shaman (oil).
If your manachah (offering) is a meal manachah (offering) of the griddle, it shall be of unleavened fine flour, mixed with shaman (oil).
You shall cut it in pieces, and pour shaman (oil) on it. It is a meal manachah (offering).
If your manachah (offering) is a meal manachah (offering) of the pan, it shall be made of fine flour with shaman (oil).
You shall bawaa (bring) the meal manachah (offering) that is made of these things to Yahawah: and it shall be presented to the kahan (priest), and he shall bring it to the mazabach (altar).

The kahan (priest) shall take from the meal manachah (offering) its azakarah (memorial), and shall qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar), an ashah (offering) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.
That which is yathar (left) of the meal manachah (offering) shall be Aharawan and his ban (sons)'. It is a thing most qadash (holy) of the ashah (offerings) of Yahawah made by ashah (fire).

"‘No meal manachah (offering), which you shall qarab (offer) to Yahawah, shall be made with yeast; for you shall qatar (burn) no yeast, nor any honey, as an ashah (offering) made by ashah (fire) to Yahawah.
As an qaraban (offering) of firstfruits you shall qarab (offer) them to Yahawah: but they shall not ilah (ascend) for a pleasant aroma on the mazabach (altar).

Every qaraban (offering) of your meal qaraban (offering) you shall season with Malach; neither shall you allow the Malach of the barayath (covenant) of your Alahayam to be shabath (lacking) from your meal manachah (offering). With all your manachah (offerings) you shall qarab (offer) Malach.

"‘If you qarab (offer) a meal manachah (offering) of bakawar (first) fruits to Yahawah, you shall qarab (offer) for the meal manachah (offering) of your bakawar (first) fruits grain in the ear parched with ash (fire), bruised grain of the fresh ear.
You shall nathan (put) shaman (oil) on it, and nathan (lay) frankincense on it: it is a meal manachah (offering).

The kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) as its azakarah (memorial), part of its bruised grain, and part of its shaman (oil), along with all its frankincense: it is an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah.

"‘If his qaraban (offering) is a zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings; if he qarab (offers) it from the herd, whether zakar (male) or female, he shall qarab (offer) it thamayam (without) blemish panayam (before) Yahawah.

He shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on the raash (head) of his qaraban (offering), and kill it at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and Aharawan ban (sons), the kahan (priests) shall sprinkle the dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar).
He shall qarab (offer) of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah; the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,
and the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kalayah (kidneys), he shall sawar (take) away.

Aharawan ban (sons) shall qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar) on the burnt offering, which is on the itz (wood) that is on the ash (fire): it is an offering made by ash (fire), of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.
"‘If his qaraban (offering) for a zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings to Yahawah is from the flock; zakar (male) or female, he shall qarab (offer) it thamayam (without) blemish.
If he qarab (offers) a lamb for his qaraban (offering), then he shall qarab (offer) it panayam (before) Yahawah;

and he shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on the raash (head) of his qaraban (offering), and kill it panayam (before) the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and Aharawan ban (sons) shall sprinkle its dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar).

He shall qarab (offer) from the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah; its fat, the entire tail fat, he shall sawar (take) away close to the backbone; and the fat that covers the qarab (inwards), and all the fat that is on the qarab (inwards),
and the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kalayah (kidneys), he shall sawar (take) away.
The kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar): it is the lacham (food) of the ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah.
"‘If his qaraban (offering) is a goat, then he shall qarab (offer) it panayam (before) Yahawah:

and he shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on its raash (head), and kill it panayam (before) the ahal (tent) of Meeting; and the ban (sons) of Aharawan shall sprinkle its dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar).
He shall qarab (offer) from it as his qaraban (offering), an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah; the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,
and the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kalayah (kidneys), he shall sawar (take) away.
The kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) them on the mazabach (altar): it is the lacham (food) of the ashah (offering) made by fire, for a pleasant aroma; all the fat is yahawah (yahweh's).
"‘It shall be a perpetual chaqah (statute) throughout your dawar (generations) in all your mawashab (dwellings), that you shall akal (eat) neither fat nor dam (blood).'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, ‘If anyone chataa (sins) unintentionally, in any of the things which Yahawah has commanded not to be done, and does any hanah (one) of them:

if the mashayach (anointed) kahan (priest) chataa (sins) so as to bring guilt on the im (people), then let him qarab (offer) for his chataah (sin), which he has sinned, a young bull thamayam (without) blemish to Yahawah for a chataah (sin) offering.

He shall bawaa (bring) the bull to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting panayam (before) Yahawah; and he shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the bull, and kill the bull panayam (before) Yahawah.
The mashayach (anointed) kahan (priest) shall take some of the dam (blood) of the bull, and bawaa (bring) it to the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

The kahan (priest) shall dip his finger in the dam (blood), and sprinkle some of the dam (blood) shabai (seven) paim (times) panayam (before) Yahawah, panayam (before) the parakath (veil) of the qadash (sanctuary).

The kahan (priest) shall nathan (put) some of the dam (blood) on the qaran (horns) of the mazabach (altar) of sweet incense panayam (before) Yahawah, which is in the ahal (tent) of Meeting; and he shall pour out all of rest of the dam (blood) of the bull at the base of the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering), which is at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
He shall take all the fat of the bull of the chataah (sin) offering off of it; the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,
and the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kalayah (kidneys), he shall sawar (take) away,
as it is taken off of the bull of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings. The kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) them on the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering).
The bull's skin, all its flesh, with its raash (head), and with its legs, its innards, and its dung,

even the whole bull shall he yatzaa (carry) forth outside the machanah (camp) to a tahawar (clean) place, where the ashes are poured out, and sharap (burn) it on itz (wood) with ash (fire). Where the ashes are poured out it shall be burned.

"‘If the whole idah (congregation) of Yasharaal (Israel) shagah (sins), and the thing is hidden from the iyan (eyes) of the qahal (assembly), and they have done any of the things which Yahawah has commanded not to be done, and are asham (guilty);

when the chataah (sin) in which they have sinned is yadai (known), then the qahal (assembly) shall qarab (offer) a young bull for a chataah (sin) offering, and bawaa (bring) it panayam (before) the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
The zaqan (elders) of the idah (congregation) shall samak (lay) their yad (hands) on the raash (head) of the bull panayam (before) Yahawah; and the bull shall be killed panayam (before) Yahawah.
The mashayach (anointed) kahan (priest) shall bawaa (bring) of the dam (blood) of the bull to the ahal (tent) of Meeting:
and the kahan (priest) shall dip his finger in the dam (blood), and sprinkle it shabai (seven) paim (times) panayam (before) Yahawah, panayam (before) the parakath (veil).

He shall nathan (put) some of the dam (blood) on the qaran (horns) of the mazabach (altar) which is panayam (before) Yahawah, that is in the ahal (tent) of Meeting; and the rest of the dam (blood) he shall pour out at the base of the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering), which is at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
All its fat he shall take from it, and qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar).

Thus shall he do with the bull; as he did with the bull of the chataah (sin) offering, so shall he do with this; and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for them, and they shall be forgiven.
He shall yatzaa (carry) forth the bull outside the machanah (camp), and sharap (burn) it as he burned the raashawan (first) bull. It is the chataah (sin) offering for the qahal (assembly).
"‘When a nashayaa (ruler) chataa (sins), and unwittingly does any one of all the things which Yahawah his Alahayam has commanded not to be done, and is asham (guilty);
if his chataah (sin), in which he has sinned, is made yadai (known) to him, he shall bawaa (bring) as his qaraban (offering) a Shaiyar, a zakar (male) thamayam (without) blemish.
He shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the Shaiyar, and kill it in the place where they kill the burnt ilah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah. It is a sin ilah (offering).

The kahan (priest) shall take some of the dam (blood) of the chataah (sin) offering with his finger, and nathan (put) it on the qaran (horns) of the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering). He shall pour out the rest of its dam (blood) at the base of the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering).

All its fat he shall qatar (burn) on the mazabach (altar), like the fat of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings; and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him concerning his chataah (sin), and he will be forgiven.
"‘If anyone of the aratz (common) im (people) chataa (sins) unwittingly, in doing any of the things which Yahawah has commanded not to be done, and is asham (guilty);

if his chataah (sin), which he has sinned, is made yadai (known) to him, then he shall bawaa (bring) for his qaraban (offering) a goat, a female thamayam (without) blemish, for his chataah (sin) which he has sinned.
He shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the chataah (sin) offering, and kill the chataah (sin) offering in the place of burnt chataah (offering).

The kahan (priest) shall take some of its dam (blood) with his finger, and nathan (put) it on the qaran (horns) of the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering); and the rest of its dam (blood) he shall pour out at the base of the mazabach (altar).

All its fat he shall sawar (take) away, like the fat is taken sawar (away) from off of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings; and the kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar) for a pleasant aroma to Yahawah; and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him, and he will be forgiven.
"‘If he bawaa (brings) a lamb as his chataah (offering) for a sin qaraban (offering), he shall bawaa (bring) a female thamayam (without) blemish.
He shall samak (lay) his yad (hand) on the raash (head) of the chataah (sin) offering, and kill it for a chataah (sin) offering in the place where they kill the burnt ilah (offering).

The kahan (priest) shall take some of the dam (blood) of the chataah (sin) offering with his finger, and nathan (put) it on the qaran (horns) of the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering); and all the rest of its dam (blood) he shall pour out at the base of the mazabach (altar).

All its fat he shall sawar (take) away, like the fat of the lamb is taken sawar (away) from the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings; and the kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) them on the mazabach (altar), on the offerings of Yahawah made by ashah (fire); and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him concerning his chataah (sin) that he has sinned, and he will be forgiven.

"‘If anyone chataa (sins), in that he hears the qawal (voice) of adjuration, he being a witness, whether he has seen or yadai (known), if he doesn't nagad (report) it, then he shall nashaa (bear) his iwan (iniquity).

"‘Or if anyone touches any tamaa (unclean) thing, whether it is the carcass of an tamaa (unclean) animal, or the carcass of tamaa (unclean) livestock, or the carcass of tamaa (unclean) creeping things, and it is hidden from him, and he is tamaa (unclean), then he shall be asham (guilty).

"‘Or if he touches the tamaah (uncleanness) of adam (man), whatever his tamaah (uncleanness) is with which he is tamaa (unclean), and it is hidden from him; when he yadai (knows) of it, then he shall be asham (guilty).

"‘Or if anyone shabai (swears) rashly with his shapah (lips) to do raii (evil), or to do yatab (good), whatever it is that a adam (man) might utter rashly with an shabawaih (oath), and it is hidden from him; when he yadai (knows) of it, then he shall be asham (guilty) of one of these.
It shall be, when he is asham (guilty) of one of these, he shall yadah (confess) that in which he has sinned:

and he shall bawaa (bring) his asham (trespass) offering to Yahawah for his chataah (sin) which he has sinned, a female from the flock, a lamb or a goat, for a chataah (sin) offering; and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him concerning his chataah (sin).

"‘If he can't afford a lamb, then he shall nagai (bring) his asham (trespass) ath (offering) for that in which he has sinned, shanayam (two) turtledoves, or shanayam (two) ban (young) pigeons, to Yahawah; one for a chataah (sin) offering, and the other for a burnt chataah (offering).

He shall bawaa (bring) them to the kahan (priest), who shall first qarab (offer) the one which is for the chataah (sin) offering, and wring off its raash (head) from its neck, but shall not sever it completely.

He shall sprinkle some of the dam (blood) of the chataah (sin) offering on the side of the mazabach (altar); and the shaar (rest) of the dam (blood) shall be drained out at the base of the mazabach (altar). It is a chataah (sin) offering.

He shall ishah (offer) the shanay (second) for a burnt ilah (offering), according to the mashapat (ordinance); and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him concerning his chataah (sin) which he has sinned, and he shall be forgiven.

"‘But if he can't afford shanayam (two) turtledoves, or shanayam (two) ban (young) pigeons, then he shall bawaa (bring) his qaraban (offering) for that in which he has sinned, the ishayaray (tenth) part of an ephah of fine flour for a chataah (sin) offering. He shall shawam (put) no shaman (oil) on it, neither shall he nathan (put) any frankincense on it, for it is a chataah (sin) offering.

He shall bawaa (bring) it to the kahan (priest), and the kahan (priest) shall take his handful of it as the azakarah (memorial) portion, and qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar), on the offerings of Yahawah made by ashah (fire). It is a chataah (sin) offering.

The kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him concerning his chataah (sin) that he has sinned in any of these things, and he will be forgiven; and the rest shall be the kahan (priest's), as the meal manachah (offering).'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"If anyone commits a mail (trespass), and sins unwittingly, in the qadash (holy) things of Yahawah; then he shall bawaa (bring) his asham (trespass) offering to Yahawah, a ayal (ram) thamayam (without) blemish from the flock, according to your irak (estimation) in kasap (silver) by shekels, after the shekel of the qadash (sanctuary), for a asham (trespass) offering.

He shall shalam (make) restitution for that which he has chataa (done) wrong in the qadash (holy) thing, and shall add a chamayashay (fifth) part to it, and nathan (give) it to the kahan (priest); and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him with the ayal (ram) of the asham (trespass) offering, and he will be forgiven.

"If anyone chataa (sins), and does any of the things which Yahawah has commanded not to be done; though he didn't yadai (know) it, yet he is asham (guilty), and shall nashaa (bear) his iwan (iniquity).

He shall bawaa (bring) a ayal (ram) thamayam (without) blemish from of the flock, according to your irak (estimation), for a asham (trespass) offering, to the kahan (priest); and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him concerning the thing in which he sinned and didn't yadai (know) it, and he will be forgiven.
It is a asham (trespass) offering. He is asham (certainly) asham (guilty) before Yahawah.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"If anyone chataa (sins), and commits a mail (trespass) against Yahawah, and deals falsely with his neighbor in a matter of deposit, or of bargain, or of robbery, or has oppressed his neighbor,
or has found that which was lost, and dealt falsely therein, and swearing to a lie; in any of all these things that a adam (man) does, sinning therein;

then it shall be, if he has sinned, and is asham (guilty), he shall shawab (turn back / repent) that which he took by robbery, or the thing which he has gotten by oppression, or the deposit which was committed to him, or the lost thing which he found,

or any thing about which he has sworn falsely; he shall shalam (restore) it even in full, and shall add a chamayashay (fifth) part more to it. To him to whom it belongs he shall nathan (give) it, in the yawam (day) of his being found guilty.

He shall bawaa (bring) his asham (trespass) offering to Yahawah, a ayal (ram) thamayam (without) blemish from the flock, according to your irak (estimation), for a asham (trespass) offering, to the kahan (priest).
The kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him panayam (before) Yahawah, and he will be forgiven concerning whatever he does to become guilty.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"tzawah (command) Aharawan and his ban (sons), saying, ‘This is the thawarah (law) of the burnt ilah (offering): the burnt ilah (offering) shall be on the hearth on the mazabach (altar) all layal (night) until the baqar (morning); and the ash (fire) of the mazabach (altar) shall be kept yaqad (burning) on it.

The kahan (priest) shall Labash on his linen mad (garment), and he shall Labash on his linen breeches upon his body; and he shall remove the ashes from where the ash (fire) has consumed the burnt ilah (offering) on the mazabach (altar), and he shall shawam (put) them beside the mazabach (altar).
He shall take off his bagad (garments), and Labash on other bagad (garments), and yatzaa (carry) the ashes outside the machanah (camp) to a tahawar (clean) place.

The ash (fire) on the mazabach (altar) shall be kept yaqad (burning) on it, it shall not go out; and the kahan (priest) shall bair (burn) itz (wood) on it every baqar (morning): and he shall lay the burnt ilah (offering) in order upon it, and shall qatar (burn) on it the fat of the shalam (peace) offerings.
ash (fire) shall be kept yaqad (burning) on the mazabach (altar) continually; it shall not go out.
"‘This is the thawarah (law) of the meal manachah (offering): the ban (sons) of Aharawan shall qarab (offer) it panayam (before) Yahawah, panayam (before) the mazabach (altar).

He shall take from there his handful of the fine flour of the meal manachah (offering), and of its shaman (oil), and all the frankincense which is on the meal manachah (offering), and shall qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar) for a pleasant aroma, as its azakarah (memorial), to Yahawah.

That which is yathar (left) of it Aharawan and his ban (sons) shall akal (eat). It shall be eaten matzah (without) yeast in a qadawash (holy) place. They shall akal (eat) it in the court of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

It shall not be baked with yeast. I have given it as their chalaq (portion) of my ashah (offerings) made by fire. It is most qadash (holy), as the chataah (sin) offering, and as the trespass chataah (offering).

Every zakar (male) among the children of Aharawan shall akal (eat) of it, as their chaq (portion) iwalam (forever) throughout your dawar (generations), from the ashah (offerings) of Yahawah made by ashah (fire). Whoever touches them shall be qadash (holy).'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"This is the qaraban (offering) of Aharawan and of his ban (sons), which they shall qarab (offer) to Yahawah in the yawam (day) when he is mashach (anointed): the ishayaray (tenth) part of an ephah of fine flour for a meal manachah (offering) perpetually, half of it in the baqar (morning), and half of it in the evening.
It shall be made with shaman (oil) in a griddle. When it is soaked, you shall bawaa (bring) it in. You shall offer the meal manachah (offering) in baked pieces for a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.

The mashayach (anointed) kahan (priest) that will be in his place from among his ban (sons) shall ishah (offer) it. By a chaq (statute) iwalam (forever), it shall be kalayal (wholly) burnt to Yahawah.
Every meal manachah (offering) of a kahan (priest) shall be kalayal (wholly) burned. It shall not be eaten.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (speak) to Aharawan and to his ban (sons), saying, ‘This is the thawarah (law) of the chataah (sin) offering: in the place where the burnt ilah (offering) is killed, the chataah (sin) offering shall be killed panayam (before) Yahawah. It is most qadash (holy).
The kahan (priest) who offers it for chataa (sin) shall akal (eat) it. It shall be eaten in a qadawash (holy) place, in the court of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

Whatever shall nagai (touch) its flesh shall be qadash (holy). When there is any of its dam (blood) sprinkled on a bagad (garment), you shall wash that on which it was sprinkled in a qadawash (holy) place.
But the charash (earthen) vessel in which it is boiled shall be shabar (broken); and if it is boiled in a bronze vessel, it shall be scoured, and rinsed in mayam (water).
Every zakar (male) among the kahan (priests) shall akal (eat) of it: it is most qadash (holy).

No chataah (sin) offering, of which any of the dam (blood) is brought into the ahal (tent) of Meeting to make kapar (atonement) in the qadash (holy) Place, shall be eaten: it shall be burned with ash (fire).
"‘This is the thawarah (law) of the asham (trespass) offering. It is most qadash (holy).
In the place where they kill the burnt ilah (offering), he shall kill the asham (trespass) offering; and its dam (blood) he shall sprinkle around on the mazabach (altar).
He shall qarab (offer) all of its fat: the fat tail, and the fat that covers the innards,
and the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kalayah (kidneys), shall he sawar (take) away;
