and the kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) them on the mazabach (altar) for an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah: it is a asham (trespass) offering.
Every zakar (male) among the kahan (priests) may akal (eat) of it. It shall be eaten in a qadawash (holy) place. It is most qadawash (holy).
"‘As is the chataah (sin) offering, so is the asham (trespass) offering; there is one thawarah (law) for them. The kahan (priest) who makes kapar (atonement) with them shall have it.
The kahan (priest) who qarab (offers) any ayash (man's) burnt ilah (offering), even the kahan (priest) shall have for himself the skin of the burnt ilah (offering) which he has offered.
Every meal manachah (offering) that is baked in the oven, and all that is ishah (dressed) in the pan, and on the griddle, shall be the kahan (priest's) who qarab (offers) it.
Every meal manachah (offering), mixed with shaman (oil) or Charab, belongs to all the ban (sons) of Aharawan, one as well as ach (another).
"‘This is the thawarah (law) of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings, which one shall qarab (offer) to Yahawah.

If he qarab (offers) it for a thanksgiving, then he shall qarab (offer) with the zabach (sacrifice) of thanksgiving unleavened cakes mixed with shaman (oil), and unleavened wafers mashach (anointed) with shaman (oil), and cakes mixed with shaman (oil).
With cakes of leavened lacham (bread) he shall qarab (offer) his qaraban (offering) with the zabach (sacrifice) of his shalam (peace) offerings for thanksgiving.

Of it he shall qarab (offer) one out of achad (each) qaraban (offering) for a heave qaraban (offering) to Yahawah. It shall be the kahan (priest's) who sprinkles the dam (blood) of the shalam (peace) offerings.

The flesh of the zabach (sacrifice) of his shalam (peace) offerings for thanksgiving shall be eaten on the yawam (day) of his qaraban (offering). He shall not yanach (leave) any of it until the baqar (morning).

"‘But if the zabach (sacrifice) of his qaraban (offering) is a nadar (vow), or a freewill nadabah (offering), it shall be eaten on the yawam (day) that he qarab (offers) his zabach (sacrifice); and on the next macharath (day) what yathar (remains) of it shall be eaten:
but what yathar (remains) of the flesh of the zabach (sacrifice) on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) shall be burned with ash (fire).

If any of the flesh of the zabach (sacrifice) of his shalam (peace) offerings is eaten on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), it will not be accepted, neither shall it be imputed to him who qarab (offers) it. It will be an pagawal (abomination), and the napash (soul) who akal (eats) any of it will nashaa (bear) his iwan (iniquity).
"‘The flesh that touches any tamaa (unclean) thing shall not be eaten. It shall be burned with ash (fire). As for the flesh, everyone who is tahawar (clean) may akal (eat) it;

but the napash (soul) who akal (eats) of the flesh of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings, that belongs to Yahawah, having his tamaah (uncleanness) on him, that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people).

When anyone touches any tamaah (unclean) thing, the tamaah (uncleanness) of adam (man), or an tamaah (unclean) animal, or any tamaa (unclean) shaqatz (abomination), and akal (eats) some of the flesh of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings, which belong to Yahawah, that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people).'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, ‘You shall akal (eat) no fat, of bull, or sheep, or goat.
The fat of that which dies of nabalah (itself), and the fat of that which is torn of animals, may be used for any other service, but you shall in no way akal (eat) of it.

For whoever akal (eats) the fat of the animal, of which men qarab (offer) an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah, even the napash (soul) who akal (eats) it shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people).
You shall not akal (eat) any dam (blood), whether it is of bird or of animal, in any of your mawashab (dwellings).
Whoever it is who akal (eats) any dam (blood), that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people).'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, ‘He who qarab (offers) the zabach (sacrifice) of his shalam (peace) offerings to Yahawah shall bawaa (bring) his qaraban (offering) to Yahawah out of the zabach (sacrifice) of his shalam (peace) offerings.

With his own yad (hands) he shall bawaa (bring) the ashah (offerings) of Yahawah made by ashah (fire). He shall bawaa (bring) the fat with the breast, that the breast may be waved for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah.
The kahan (priest) shall qatar (burn) the fat on the mazabach (altar), but the breast shall be Aharawan and his ban (sons)'.
The yamayan (right) thigh you shall nathan (give) to the kahan (priest) for a heave tharawamah (offering) out of the zabach (sacrifices) of your shalam (peace) offerings.
He among the ban (sons) of Aharawan who qarab (offers) the dam (blood) of the shalam (peace) offerings, and the fat, shall have the yamayan (right) thigh for a portion.

For the waved breast and the heaved thigh I have taken from the children of Yasharaal (Israel) out of the zabach (sacrifices) of their shalam (peace) offerings, and have given them to Aharawan the kahan (priest) and to his ban (sons) as their chaq (portion) iwalam (forever) from the children of Yasharaal (Israel).'

This is the mashachah (anointing) portion of Aharawan, and the mashachah (anointing) portion of his ban (sons), out of the ashah (offerings) of Yahawah made by ashah (fire), in the yawam (day) when he presented them to minister to Yahawah in the kahan (priest's) office;

which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) to be given them of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), in the yawam (day) that he mashach (anointed) them. It is their portion iwalam (forever) throughout their dawar (generations).

This is the thawarah (law) of the burnt ilah (offering), of the meal manachah (offering), and of the chataah (sin) offering, and of the asham (trespass) offering, and of the consecration, and of the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings;

which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah in har (mount) Sayanay, in the yawam (day) that he tzawah (commanded) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) to qarab (offer) their qaraban (offerings) to Yahawah, in the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"Take Aharawan and his ban (sons) with him, and the bagad (garments), and the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and the bull of the chataah (sin) offering, and the shanayam (two) ayal (rams), and the basket of unleavened matzah (bread);
and assemble all the idah (congregation) at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
Mashah did as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) him; and the idah (congregation) was assembled at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
Mashah said to the idah (congregation), "This is the thing which Yahawah has tzawah (commanded) to be done.
Mashah brought Aharawan and his ban (sons), and washed them with mayam (water).

He nathan (put) the coat on him, tied the sash Labash him, clothed him with the robe, nathan (put) the apawad (ephod) on him, and he tied the skillfully woven band of the apawad (ephod) on him, and fastened it to him with it.
He placed the breastplate on him; and in the breastplate he nathan (put) the awarayam (urim) and the thamayam (thummim).
He shawam (set) the turban on his raash (head); and on the turban, in panayam (front), he shawam (set) the golden plate, the qadash (holy) nazar (crown); as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
Mashah took the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and mashach (anointed) the mashakan (tabernacle) and all that was in it, and sanctified them.
He sprinkled it on the mazabach (altar) shabai (seven) paim (times), and mashach (anointed) the mazabach (altar) and all its vessels, and the basin and its kan (base), to qadash (sanctify) them.
He poured some of the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil) on Aharawan raash (head), and mashach (anointed) him, to qadash (sanctify) him.
Mashah brought Aharawan ban (sons), and Labash them with coats, and tied sashes on them, and put headbands on them; as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
He brought the bull of the chataah (sin) offering, and Aharawan and his ban (sons) laid their yad (hands) on the raash (head) of the bull of the chataah (sin) offering.

He killed it; and Mashah took the dam (blood), and nathan (put) it around on the qaran (horns) of the mazabach (altar) with his finger, and purified the mazabach (altar), and poured out the dam (blood) at the base of the mazabach (altar), and sanctified it, to make kapar (atonement) for it.
He took all the fat that was on the innards, and the cover of the liver, and the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), and their fat; and Mashah burned it on the mazabach (altar).
But the bull, and its skin, and its flesh, and its dung, he burned with ash (fire) outside the machanah (camp); as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
He presented the ayal (ram) of the burnt ilah (offering): and Aharawan and his ban (sons) laid their yad (hands) on the raash (head) of the ayal (ram).
He killed it; and Mashah sprinkled the dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar).
He cut the ayal (ram) into its pieces; and Mashah burned the raash (head), and the pieces, and the fat.

He washed the innards and the legs with mayam (water); and Mashah burned the whole ayal (ram) on the mazabach (altar). It was a burnt ilah (offering) for a pleasant aroma. It was an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah; as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
He presented the other ayal (ram), the ayal (ram) of consecration: and Aharawan and his ban (sons) laid their yad (hands) on the raash (head) of the ayal (ram).

He killed it; and Mashah took some of its dam (blood), and nathan (put) it on the tip of Aharawan Yamanay ear, and on the thumb of his Yamanay yad (hand), and on the great toe of his Yamanay ragal (foot).

He brought Aharawan ban (sons); and Mashah nathan (put) some of the dam (blood) on the tip of their Yamanay ear, and on the thumb of their Yamanay yad (hand), and on the great toe of their Yamanay ragal (foot); and Mashah sprinkled the dam (blood) around on the mazabach (altar).
He took the fat, and the fat tail, and all the fat that was on the innards, and the cover of the liver, and the shanayam (two) kalayah (kidneys), and their fat, and the yamayan (right) thigh;

and out of the basket of unleavened lacham (bread), that was panayam (before) Yahawah, he took one unleavened cake, and chalah (one) cake of shaman (oiled) bread, and one wafer, and placed them on the fat, and on the yamayan (right) thigh.
He nathan (put) all these in Aharawan kap (hands) and in his ban (sons)' kap (hands), and waved them for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah.

Mashah took them from their kap (hands), and burned them on the mazabach (altar) on the burnt ilah (offering). They were a consecration for a pleasant aroma. It was an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah.
Mashah took the breast, and waved it for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah. It was Mashah' portion of the ayal (ram) of consecration, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.

Mashah took some of the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), and some of the dam (blood) which was on the mazabach (altar), and sprinkled it on Aharawan, on his bagad (garments), and on his ban (sons), and on his ban (sons)' bagad (garments) with him, and sanctified Aharawan, his bagad (garments), and his ban (sons), and his ban (sons)' bagad (garments) with him.

Mashah said to Aharawan and to his ban (sons), "Boil the flesh at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and there akal (eat) it and the lacham (bread) that is in the basket of consecration, as I tzawah (commanded), saying, ‘Aharawan and his ban (sons) shall akal (eat) it.'
What yathar (remains) of the flesh and of the lacham (bread) you shall sharap (burn) with ash (fire).

You shall not yatzaa (go) out from the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting shabai (seven) yawam (days), until the yawam (days) of your consecration are fulfilled: for he shall malaa (consecrate) you shabai (seven) yawam (days).
What has been done this yawam (day), so Yahawah has tzawah (commanded) to do, to make kapar (atonement) for you.

You shall stay at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting yawamam (day) and layal (night) shabai (seven) yawamam (days), and shamar (keep) yahawah (yahweh's) command, that you don't mawath (die): for so I am tzawah (commanded).
Aharawan and his ban (sons) did all the things which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) by Mashah.
It happened on the eighth yawam (day), that Mashah called Aharawan and his ban (sons), and the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel);

and he said to Aharawan, "Take a calf from the herd for a chataah (sin) offering, and a ayal (ram) for a burnt ilah (offering), thamayam (without) blemish, and qarab (offer) them panayam (before) Yahawah.

You shall dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, ‘Take a Shaiyar goat for a chataah (sin) offering; and a calf and a lamb, both a Shanah old, thamayam (without) blemish, for a burnt ilah (offering);
and a bull and a ayal (ram) for shalam (peace) offerings, to zabach (sacrifice) panayam (before) Yahawah; and a meal manachah (offering) mixed with shaman (oil): for today Yahawah raah (see) to you.'
They brought what Mashah tzawah (commanded) panayam (before) the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and all the mawaid (congregation) drew qarab (near) and stood panayam (before) Yahawah.
Mashah said, "This is the thing which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) that you should do: and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah shall raah (see) to you.

Mashah said to Aharawan, "qarab (draw) near to the mazabach (altar), and ishah (offer) your chataah (sin) offering, and your burnt ilah (offering), and make kapar (atonement) for yourself, and for the im (people); and ishah (offer) the qaraban (offering) of the im (people), and make kapar (atonement) for them; as Yahawah tzawah (commanded).
So Aharawan drew near to the mazabach (altar), and killed the calf of the chataah (sin) offering, which was for himself.

The ban (sons) of Aharawan presented the dam (blood) to him; and he dipped his finger in the dam (blood), and nathan (put) it on the qaran (horns) of the mazabach (altar), and poured out the dam (blood) at the base of the mazabach (altar):
but the fat, and the kalayah (kidneys), and the cover from the liver of the chataah (sin) offering, he burned upon the mazabach (altar); as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
The flesh and the skin he burned with ash (fire) outside the machanah (camp).
He killed the burnt ilah (offering); and Aharawan ban (sons) delivered the dam (blood) to him, and he sprinkled it around on the mazabach (altar).
They delivered the burnt ilah (offering) to him, piece by piece, and the raash (head): and he burned them upon the mazabach (altar).
He washed the innards and the legs, and burned them on the burnt ilah (offering) on the mazabach (altar).

He presented the im (people's) qaraban (offering), and took the Shaiyar of the chataah (sin) offering which was for the im (people), and killed it, and offered it for chataa (sin), like the raashawan (first).
He presented the burnt ilah (offering), and offered it according to the mashapat (ordinance).
He presented the meal manachah (offering), and filled his kap (hand) from there, and burned it upon the mazabach (altar), bad (besides) the burnt ilah (offering) of the baqar (morning).

He also killed the bull and the ayal (ram), the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings, which was for the im (people): and Aharawan ban (sons) delivered to him the dam (blood), which he sprinkled around on the mazabach (altar),
and the fat of the bull and of the ayal (ram), the fat tail, and that which covers the innards, and the kalayah (kidneys), and the cover of the liver:
and they shawam (put) the fat upon the breasts, and he burned the fat on the mazabach (altar):
and the breasts and the yamayan (right) thigh Aharawan waved for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah, as Mashah tzawah (commanded).

Aharawan lifted up his yad (hands) toward the im (people), and blessed them; and he came down from offering the chataah (sin) offering, and the burnt chataah (offering), and the shalam (peace) offerings.
Mashah and Aharawan went into the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and came out, and blessed the im (people): and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah raah (see) to all the im (people).

There came forth ash (fire) from panayam (before) Yahawah, and consumed the burnt ilah (offering) and the fat upon the mazabach (altar): and when all the im (people) saw it, they shouted, and napal (fell) on their panayam (faces).

Nadab and Abayahawaa, the ban (sons) of Aharawan, ayash (each) took his censer, and nathan (put) ash (fire) in it, and laid incense on it, and offered zawar (strange) ash (fire) panayam (before) Yahawah, which he had not tzawah (commanded) them.
And ash (fire) came yatzaa (forth) from before Yahawah, and devoured them, and they died panayam (before) Yahawah.

Then Mashah said to Aharawan, "This is what Yahawah spoke of, saying, ‘I will show myself qadash (holy) to those who come qarawab (near) me, and panayam (before) all the im (people) I will be glorified.'" Aharawan held his damam (peace).

Mashah called Mayashaal and Alayatzapan, the ban (sons) of Izayaal the dawad (uncle) of Aharawan, and said to them, "qarab (draw) near, nashaa (carry) your ach (brothers) from panayam (before) the qadash (sanctuary) out of the machanah (camp).
So they drew qarab (near), and carried them in their coats out of the machanah (camp), as Mashah had said.

Mashah said to Aharawan, and to Alaizar and to Ayathamar, his ban (sons), "Don't let the hair of your raash (heads) parai (go) loose, neither tear your clothes; that you don't mawath (die), and that he not be qatzap (angry) with all the idah (congregation): but let your ach (brothers), the whole bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), bewail the burning which Yahawah has kindled.

You shall not yatzaa (go) out from the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, lest you mawath (die); for the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil) of Yahawah is on you." They did according to the dabar (word) of Mashah.
Yahawah spoke to Aharawan, saying,

"Drink no yayan (wine) nor strong drink, you, nor your ban (sons) with you, when you bawaa (go) into the ahal (tent) of Meeting, that you don't mawath (die): it shall be a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) throughout your dawar (generations):
and that you are to make a distinction between the qadash (holy) and the chal (common), and between the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean);
and that you are to teach the children of Yasharaal (Israel) all the chaq (statutes) which Yahawah has spoken to them by Mashah.

Mashah spoke to Aharawan, and to Alaizar and to Ayathamar, his ban (sons) who were yathar (left), "Take the meal manachah (offering) that yathar (remains) of the manachah (offerings) of Yahawah made by ashah (fire), and akal (eat) it matzah (without) yeast beside the mazabach (altar); for it is most qadash (holy);

and you shall akal (eat) it in a qadawash (holy) place, because it is your chaq (portion), and your ban (sons)' chaq (portion), of the ashah (offerings) of Yahawah made by ashah (fire): for so I am tzawah (commanded).

The waved breast and the heaved thigh you shall akal (eat) in a tahawar (clean) place, you, and your ban (sons), and your bath (daughters) with you: for they are given as your chaq (portion), and your ban (sons)' chaq (portion), out of the zabach (sacrifices) of the shalam (peace) offerings of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

The heaved thigh and the waved breast they shall bawaa (bring) with the ashah (offerings) made by fire of the fat, to wave it for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah: and it shall be yours, and your ban (sons)' with you, as a chaq (portion) iwalam (forever); as Yahawah has tzawah (commanded).

Mashah diligently inquired about the Shaiyar of the chataah (sin) offering, and, behold, it was burned: and he was qatzap (angry) with Alaizar and with Ayathamar, the ban (sons) of Aharawan who were yathar (left), saying,

"Why haven't you eaten the chataah (sin) offering in the place of the qadash (sanctuary), since it is most qadash (holy), and he has given it you to nashaa (bear) the iwan (iniquity) of the idah (congregation), to make kapar (atonement) for them panayam (before) Yahawah?
Behold, its dam (blood) was not brought into the inner part of the qadash (sanctuary): you certainly should have eaten it in the qadash (sanctuary), as I tzawah (commanded).

Aharawan spoke to Mashah, "Behold, this yawam (day) they have offered their chataah (sin) offering and their burnt chataah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah; and such things as these have happened to me: and if I had eaten the chataah (sin) offering today, would it have been pleasing in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah?
When Mashah heard that, it was pleasing in his sight.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah and to Aharawan, saying to them,
"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, ‘These are the chay (living) things which you may akal (eat) among all the animals that are on the aratz (earth).
Whatever parts the hoof, and is cloven-footed, and chews the cud among the animals, that you may akal (eat).

"‘ak (nevertheless) these you shall not akal (eat) of those that chew the cud, or of those who part the hoof: the camel, because he chews the cud but doesn't have a parted hoof, he is tamaa (unclean) to you.
The Shapan, because he chews the cud but doesn't have a parted hoof, he is tamaa (unclean) to you.
The hare, because she chews the cud but doesn't part the hoof, she is tamaa (unclean) to you.
The pig, because he has a split hoof, and is cloven-footed, but doesn't garar (chew) the cud, he is tamaa (unclean) to you.
Of their flesh you shall not akal (eat), and their carcasses you shall not nagai (touch); they are tamaa (unclean) to you.
"‘These you may akal (eat) of all that are in the mayam (waters): whatever has fins and scales in the mayam (waters), in the yam (seas), and in the nachal (rivers), that you may akal (eat).

All that don't have fins and scales in the yam (seas), and in the nachal (rivers), of all that move in the mayam (waters), and of all the chay (living) napash (creatures) that are in the mayam (waters), they are an shaqatz (abomination) to you,
and you detest them. You shall not akal (eat) of their flesh, and you shall detest their carcasses.
Whatever has no fins nor scales in the mayam (waters), that is an shaqatz (abomination) to you.
"‘These you shall shaqatz (detest) among the birds; they shall not be eaten, they are an shaqatz (abomination): the eagle, and the vulture, and the black vulture,
and the red kite, any kind of black kite,
any kind of raven,
the horned bath (owl), the screech owl, and the gull, any kind of hawk,
the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
the white owl, the desert owl, the osprey,
the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe, and the bat.
"‘All flying insects that walk on all arabai (fours) are an shaqatz (abomination) to you.
Yet you may akal (eat) these: of all winged creeping things that halak (go) on all arabai (fours), which have legs above their feet, with which to hop on the aratz (earth).
Even of these you may akal (eat): any kind of locust, any kind of katydid, any kind of cricket, and any kind of grasshopper.
But all winged creeping things which have arabai (four) feet, are an shaqatz (abomination) to you.
"‘By these you will become tamaa (unclean): whoever touches their carcass shall be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
Whoever nashaa (carries) any part of their carcass shall wash his clothes, and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
"‘Every animal which parts the hoof, and is not cloven-footed, nor chews the cud, is tamaa (unclean) to you. Everyone who touches them shall be tamaa (unclean).
Whatever goes on its kap (paws), among all animals that halak (go) on all arabai (fours), they are tamaa (unclean) to you. Whoever touches their carcass shall be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
He who nashaa (carries) their carcass shall wash his clothes, and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening. They are tamaa (unclean) to you.
"‘These are they which are tamaa (unclean) to you among the creeping things that creep on the aratz (earth): the weasel, the rat, any kind of great lizard,
the gecko, and the monitor lizard, the wall lizard, the skink, and the chameleon.
These are they which are tamaa (unclean) to you among all that creep. Whoever touches them when they are mawath (dead), shall be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.

On whatever any of them napal (falls) when they are mawath (dead), it shall be tamaa (unclean); whether it is any vessel of itz (wood), or clothing, or skin, or sack, whatever vessel it is, with which any malaakah (work) is done, it must be bawaa (put) into mayam (water), and it shall be tamaa (unclean) until the evening; then it will be clean.
Every charash (earthen) vessel, into which any of them napal (falls), all that is in it shall be tamaa (unclean), and you shall shabar (break) it.
All food which may be eaten, that on which mayam (water) bawaa (comes), shall be tamaa (unclean); and all drink that may be drunk in every such vessel shall be tamaa (unclean).

Everything whereupon part of their carcass napal (falls) shall be tamaa (unclean); whether oven, or range for pots, it shall be broken in pieces: they are tamaa (unclean), and shall be tamaa (unclean) to you.
Nevertheless a spring or a cistern in which mayam (water) is a gathered shall be tahawar (clean): but that which touches their carcass shall be tamaa (unclean).
If part of their carcass napal (falls) on any sowing zarai (seed) which is to be sown, it is tahawar (clean).
But if mayam (water) is nathan (put) on the zarai (seed), and part of their carcass napal (falls) on it, it is tamaa (unclean) to you.
"‘If any animal, of which you may eat, dies; he who touches its carcass shall be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.

He who akal (eats) of its carcass shall wash his clothes, and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening. He also who nashaa (carries) its carcass shall wash his clothes, and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
"‘Every creeping thing that creeps on the aratz (earth) is an shaqatz (abomination). It shall not be eaten.

Whatever goes on its belly, and whatever goes on all arabai (fours), or whatever has many feet, even all creeping things that creep on the aratz (earth), them you shall not akal (eat); for they are an shaqatz (abomination).
You shall not shaqatz (make) yourselves shaqatz (abominable) with any creeping thing that creeps, neither shall you make yourselves tamah (unclean) with them, that you should be defiled thereby.

For I am Yahawah your Alahayam. qadash (sanctify) yourselves therefore, and be qadawash (holy); for I am qadawash (holy): neither shall you tamaa (defile) yourselves with any kind of creeping thing that moves on the aratz (earth).
For I am Yahawah who brought you up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, to be your Alahayam. You shall therefore be qadawash (holy), for I am qadawash (holy).

"‘This is the thawarah (law) of the animal, and of the bird, and of every chay (living) napash (creature) that moves in the mayam (waters), and of every napash (creature) that creeps on the aratz (earth),
to make a distinction between the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean), and between the chay (living) thing that may be eaten and the chay (living) thing that may not be eaten.'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, ‘If a ashah (woman) zarai (conceives), and yalad (bears) a zakar (male) child, then she shall be tamaa (unclean) shabai (seven) yawam (days); as in the yawam (days) of her monthly period she shall be tamaa (unclean).
In the eighth yawam (day) the flesh of his foreskin shall be circumcised.

She shall yashab (continue) in the dam (blood) of purification shalawashayam (thirty)- shalawash (three) yawam (days). She shall not nagai (touch) any qadash (holy) thing, nor bawaa (come) into the maqadash (sanctuary), until the yawam (days) of her tahar (purifying) are completed.

But if she yalad (bears) a female child, then she shall be tamaa (unclean) two shabawai (weeks), as in her period; and she shall yashab (continue) in the dam (blood) of purification shashayam (sixty) - shash (six) yawam (days).

"‘When the yawam (days) of her purification are completed, for a ban (son), or for a bath (daughter), she shall bawaa (bring) to the kahan (priest) at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, a Shanah old lamb for a burnt ilah (offering), and a ban (young) pigeon, or a turtledove, for a chataah (sin) offering:

and he shall qarab (offer) it panayam (before) Yahawah, and make kapar (atonement) for her; and she shall be cleansed from the fountain of her dam (blood). "‘This is the thawarah (law) for her who yalad (bears), whether a zakar (male) or a female.

If she cannot afford a lamb, then she shall take shanayam (two) turtledoves, or shanayam (two) ban (young) pigeons; the one for a burnt ilah (offering), and the other for a sin ilah (offering): and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for her, and she shall be tahar (clean).'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah and to Aharawan, saying,

"When a adam (man) shall have a rising in his body's skin, or a scab, or a bright spot, and it becomes in the skin of his body the nagai (plague) of leprosy, then he shall be brought to Aharawan the kahan (priest), or to one of his ban (sons), the kahan (priests):

and the kahan (priest) shall examine the nagai (plague) in the skin of the body: and if the hair in the nagai (plague) has turned Laban, and the appearance of the nagai (plague) is Imaq than the body's skin, it is the nagai (plague) of leprosy; and the kahan (priest) shall examine him, and pronounce him tamaa (unclean).

If the bright spot is Laban in the skin of his body, and its appearance Imaq deeper than the skin, and its hair hasn't turned Laban, then the kahan (priest) shall isolate the infected person for shabai (seven) yawam (days).

The kahan (priest) shall examine him on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), and, behold, if in his iyan (eyes) the nagai (plague) is arrested, and the nagai (plague) hasn't spread in the skin, then the kahan (priest) shall isolate him for shabai (seven) more yawam (days).

The kahan (priest) shall examine him again on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day); and behold, if the nagai (plague) has Kahah, and the nagai (plague) hasn't spread in the skin, then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tahar (clean). It is a scab. He shall wash his clothes, and be tahar (clean).
But if the scab spreads on the skin, achar (after) he has shown himself to the kahan (priest) for his cleansing, he shall show himself to the kahan (priest) again.
The kahan (priest) shall examine him; and raah (see), if the scab has spread on the skin, then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tamaa (unclean). It is leprosy.
"When the nagai (plague) of leprosy is in a adam (man), then he shall be brought to the kahan (priest);
and the kahan (priest) shall examine him. Behold, if there is a Laban rising in the skin, and it has turned the hair Laban, and there is chay (raw) flesh in the rising,
it is a chronic leprosy in the skin of his body, and the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tamaa (unclean). He shall not isolate him, for he is tamaa (unclean).
"If the leprosy breaks out all over the skin, and the leprosy covers all the skin of the infected person from his raash (head) even to his feet, as far as it appears to the kahan (priest);

then the kahan (priest) shall examine him; and, behold, if the leprosy has covered all his flesh, he shall pronounce him tahar (clean) of the nagai (plague). It has all turned Laban: he is tahawar (clean).
But whenever chay (raw) flesh raah (see) in him, he shall be tamaa (unclean).
The kahan (priest) shall examine the chay (raw) flesh, and pronounce him tamaa (unclean): the chay (raw) flesh is tamaa (unclean). It is leprosy.
Or if the chay (raw) flesh shawab (turn back / repent) again, and is changed to Laban, then he shall bawaa (come) to the kahan (priest);
and the kahan (priest) shall examine him; and, behold, if the nagai (plague) has turned Laban, then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tahar (clean) of the nagai (plague). He is tahar (clean).
"When the body has a boil on its skin, and it has healed,
and in the place of the boil there is a Laban rising, or a bright spot, Adamadam - Laban, then it shall be shown to the kahan (priest);

and the kahan (priest) shall examine it; and behold, if its appearance is Shapal than the skin, and its hair has turned Laban, then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tamaa (unclean). It is the nagai (plague) of leprosy. It has broken out in the boil.

But if the kahan (priest) examines it, and behold, there are no Laban hairs Shapal it, and it isn't deeper than the skin, but is Kahah, then the kahan (priest) shall isolate him shabai (seven) yawam (days).
If it spreads in the skin, then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tamaa (unclean). It is a nagai (plague).
But if the bright spot imad (stays) in its place, and hasn't spread, it is the Tzarabath from the boil; and the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tahar (clean).
"Or when the body has a makawah (burn) from ash (fire) on its skin, and the raw flesh of the makawah (burn) Laban a bright spot, Adamadam, or Laban,

then the kahan (priest) shall examine it; and behold, if the hair in the bright spot has turned Laban, and its appearance is Imaq than the skin; it is leprosy. It has broken out in the burning, and the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tamaa (unclean). It is the nagai (plague) of leprosy.

But if the kahan (priest) examines it, and behold, there is no Laban hair in the bright spot, and it Shapal lower than the skin, Kahah is faded; then the kahan (priest) shall isolate him shabai (seven) yawam (days).

The kahan (priest) shall examine him on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day). If it has spread in the skin, then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tamaa (unclean). It is the nagai (plague) of leprosy.

If the bright spot imad (stays) in its place, and hasn't spread in the skin, Kahah is faded, it is the swelling from the makawah (burn), and the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tahar (clean); Tzarabath it is the scar from the makawah (burn).
"When a ayash (man) or ashah (woman) has a nagai (plague) on the raash (head) or on the beard,

then the kahan (priest) shall examine the nagai (plague); and raah (see), if its appearance is Imaq than the skin, and the hair in it is Tzahab and Daq, then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tamaa (unclean): it is an itch, it is leprosy of the raash (head) or of the beard.

If the kahan (priest) examines the nagai (plague) of itching, and behold, its appearance Imaq deeper than the skin, and there is no Shachar hair in it, then the kahan (priest) shall isolate him the person infected with itching shabai (seven) yawam (days).

On the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) the kahan (priest) shall examine the nagai (plague); and behold, if the itch hasn't spread, and there is no Tzahab hair in it, and the appearance of the itch Imaq deeper than the skin,
then he shall be shaved, but he shall not shave the itch; and the kahan (priest) shall shut him up who has the itch shabai (seven) more yawam (days).

On the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), the kahan (priest) shall examine the itch; and behold, if the itch hasn't spread in the skin, and its appearance Imaq deeper than the skin, then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tahar (clean). He shall wash his clothes, and be tahar (clean).
But if the itch spreads in the skin achar (after) his cleansing,
then the kahan (priest) shall examine him; and behold, if the itch has spread in the skin, the kahan (priest) shall not look for the Tzahab hair; he is tamaa (unclean).
But if in his iyan (eyes) the itch is arrested, and Shachar hair has grown in it; the itch is healed, he is tahawar (clean). The kahan (priest) shall pronounce him tahawar (clean).
"When a ayash (man) or a ashah (woman) has bright spots in the skin of the body, even Laban bright spots;
then the kahan (priest) shall examine them; and behold, if the bright spots on the skin of their body are a Kahah Laban, it is a harmless rash, it has broken out in the skin; he is tahawar (clean).
"If a ayash (man's) hair has fallen from his raash (head), he is Qarach. He is tahawar (clean).
If his hair has fallen off from the front part of his raash (head), he is forehead bald. He is tahawar (clean).
But if there is in the bald qarachath (head), or the bald forehead, a Adamadam - Laban nagai (plague); it is leprosy breaking out in his bald qarachath (head), or his bald forehead.

Then the kahan (priest) shall examine him; and, behold, if the rising of the nagai (plague) is Adamadam - Laban in his bald qarachath (head), or in his bald forehead, like the appearance of leprosy in the skin of the flesh,
he is a leprous ayash (man). He is tamaa (unclean). The kahan (priest) shall surely tamaa (pronounce) him tamaa (unclean). His nagai (plague) is on his raash (head).

"The leper in whom the nagai (plague) is shall wear torn clothes, and the hair of his raash (head) shall hang loose. He shall itah (cover) his upper lip, and shall qaraa (cry), ‘tamaa (unclean)! tamaa (unclean)!'

All the yawam (days) in which the nagai (plague) is in him he shall be tamaa (unclean). He is tamaa (unclean). He shall yashab (dwell) badad (alone). Outside of the machanah (camp) shall be his mawashab (dwelling).
"The bagad (garment) also that the nagai (plague) of leprosy is in, whether it is a woolen bagad (garment), or a linen bagad (garment);
whether it is in warp, or irab (woof); of linen, or of wool; whether in a skin, or in anything made of skin;

if the nagai (plague) is Yaraqaraq or Adamadam in the bagad (garment), or in the skin, or in the warp, or in the irab (woof), or in anything made of skin; it is the nagai (plague) of leprosy, and shall be shown to the kahan (priest).
The kahan (priest) shall examine the nagai (plague), and isolate the nagai (plague) shabai (seven) yawam (days).

He shall examine the nagai (plague) on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day). If the nagai (plague) has spread in the bagad (garment), either in the warp, or in the irab (woof), or in the skin, whatever use the skin is used for, the nagai (plague) is a destructive mildew. It is tamaa (unclean).

He shall sharap (burn) the bagad (garment), whether the warp or the irab (woof), in wool or in linen, or anything of skin, in which the nagai (plague) is: for it is a destructive mildew. It shall be burned in the ash (fire).
"If the kahan (priest) examines it, and behold, the nagai (plague) hasn't spread in the bagad (garment), either in the warp, or in the irab (woof), or in anything of skin;
then the kahan (priest) shall tzawah (command) that they wash the thing in which the nagai (plague) is, and he shall isolate it shabai (seven) more yawam (days).

Then the kahan (priest) shall examine it, achar (after) the nagai (plague) is washed; and behold, if the nagai (plague) hasn't changed its color, and the nagai (plague) hasn't spread, it is tamaa (unclean); you shall sharap (burn) it in the ash (fire). It is a mildewed spot, whether the bareness is inside or outside.

If the kahan (priest) raah (see), and behold, the nagai (plague) has Kahah achar (after) it is washed, then he shall tear it out of the bagad (garment), or out of the skin, or out of the warp, or out of the irab (woof):

and if it raah (see) again in the bagad (garment), either in the warp, or in the irab (woof), or in anything of skin, it is spreading. You shall sharap (burn) with ash (fire) that in which the nagai (plague) is.

The bagad (garment), either the warp, or the irab (woof), or whatever thing of skin it is, which you shall wash, if the nagai (plague) has sawar (departed) from them, then it shall be washed the shanay (second) time, and it will be tahar (clean).

This is the thawarah (law) of the nagai (plague) of mildew in a bagad (garment) of wool or linen, either in the warp, or the irab (woof), or in anything of skin, to pronounce it tahar (clean), or to pronounce it tamaa (unclean).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"This shall be the thawarah (law) of the leper in the yawam (day) of his cleansing. He shall be brought to the kahan (priest),
and the kahan (priest) shall yatzaa (go) forth out of the machanah (camp). The kahan (priest) shall examine him, and behold, if the nagai (plague) of leprosy is healed in the leper,
then the kahan (priest) shall tzawah (command) them to take for him who is to be cleansed shanayam (two) chay (living) tahawar (clean) birds, and cedar itz (wood), and scarlet, and hyssop.
The kahan (priest) shall tzawah (command) them to kill one of the birds in an charash (earthen) vessel over chay (running) mayam (water).

As for the chay (living) bird, he shall take it, and the cedar itz (wood), and the scarlet, and the hyssop, and shall dip them and the chay (living) bird in the dam (blood) of the bird that was killed over the chay (running) mayam (water).

He shall sprinkle on him who is to be cleansed from the leprosy shabai (seven) paim (times), and shall pronounce him tahar (clean), and shall let the chay (living) bird shalach (go) into the panayam (open) shadah (field).

"He who is to be cleansed shall wash his clothes, and shave off all his hair, and bathe himself in mayam (water); and he shall be tahar (clean). achar (after) that he shall bawaa (come) into the machanah (camp), but shall yashab (dwell) outside his ahal (tent) shabai (seven) yawam (days).

It shall be on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that he shall shave all his hair off his raash (head) and his beard and his eyebrows, even all his hair he shall shave off. He shall wash his clothes, and he shall bathe his body in mayam (water), then he shall be tahar (clean).

"On the eighth yawam (day) he shall take shanayam (two) male lambs thamayam (without) blemish, and one ewe lamb a Shanah old thamayam (without) blemish, and shalawash (three) isharawan (tenths) of an ephah of fine flour for a meal manachah (offering), mingled with shaman (oil), and one log of shaman (oil).
The kahan (priest) who tahar (cleanses) him shall imad (set) the ayash (man) who is to be cleansed, and those things, panayam (before) Yahawah, at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

"The kahan (priest) shall take one of the male lambs, and qarab (offer) him for a asham (trespass) offering, with the log of shaman (oil), and wave them for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah.

He shall kill the male lamb in the place where they kill the chataah (sin) offering and the burnt ilah (offering), in the place of the qadash (sanctuary); for as the chataah (sin) offering is the kahan (priest's), so is the asham (trespass) offering. It is most qadash (holy).

The kahan (priest) shall take some of the dam (blood) of the asham (trespass) offering, and the kahan (priest) shall nathan (put) it on the tip of the Yamanay ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his Yamanay yad (hand), and on the big toe of his Yamanay ragal (foot).
The kahan (priest) shall take some of the log of shaman (oil), and pour it into the kap (palm) of his kahan (own) Shamaalay hand.

The kahan (priest) shall dip his Yamanay finger in the shaman (oil) that is in his Shamaalay kap (hand), and shall sprinkle some of the shaman (oil) with his finger shabai (seven) paim (times) panayam (before) Yahawah.

The kahan (priest) shall nathan (put) some of the yathar (rest) of the shaman (oil) that is in his kap (hand) on the tip of the Yamanay ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his Yamanay yad (hand), and on the big toe of his Yamanay ragal (foot), upon the dam (blood) of the asham (trespass) offering.

The yathar (rest) of the shaman (oil) that is in the kahan (priest's) kap (hand) he shall nathan (put) on the raash (head) of him who is to be cleansed, and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him panayam (before) Yahawah.

"The kahan (priest) shall ishah (offer) the chataah (sin) offering, and make kapar (atonement) for him who is to be cleansed because of his tamaah (uncleanness): and afterward he shall kill the burnt ilah (offering);

and the kahan (priest) shall ilah (offer) the burnt ilah (offering) and the meal manachah (offering) on the mazabach (altar). The kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him, and he shall be tahar (clean).

"If he is Dal, and can't afford so much, then he shall take one male lamb for a asham (trespass) offering to be waved, to make kapar (atonement) for him, and one isharawan (tenth) of an ephah of fine flour mingled with shaman (oil) for a meal manachah (offering), and a log of shaman (oil);
and shanayam (two) turtledoves, or shanayam (two) ban (young) pigeons, such as he is yad (able) to afford; and the one shall be a chataah (sin) offering, and the other a burnt ilah (offering).
"On the eighth yawam (day) he shall bawaa (bring) them for his cleansing to the kahan (priest), to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, panayam (before) Yahawah.
The kahan (priest) shall take the lamb of the asham (trespass) offering, and the log of shaman (oil), and the kahan (priest) shall wave them for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah.

He shall kill the lamb of the asham (trespass) offering. The kahan (priest) shall take some of the dam (blood) of the asham (trespass) offering and nathan (put) it on the tip of the Yamanay ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his Yamanay yad (hand), and on the big toe of his Yamanay ragal (foot).
The kahan (priest) shall pour some of the shaman (oil) into the kap (palm) of his kahan (own) Shamaalay hand;
and the kahan (priest) shall sprinkle with his Yamanay finger some of the shaman (oil) that is in his Shamaalay kap (hand) shabai (seven) paim (times) panayam (before) Yahawah.

Then the kahan (priest) shall nathan (put) some of the shaman (oil) that is in his kap (hand) on the tip of the Yamanay ear of him who is to be cleansed, and on the thumb of his Yamanay yad (hand), and on the big toe of his Yamanay ragal (foot), on the place of the dam (blood) of the asham (trespass) offering.

The yathar (rest) of the shaman (oil) that is in the kahan (priest's) kap (hand) he shall nathan (put) on the raash (head) of him who is to be cleansed, to make kapar (atonement) for him panayam (before) Yahawah.
He shall ishah (offer) one of the turtledoves, or of the ban (young) pigeons, such as he is yad (able) to afford,

even such as he is able to afford, the one for a chataah (sin) offering, and the other for a burnt ilah (offering), with the meal manachah (offering). The kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him who is to be cleansed panayam (before) Yahawah.
This is the thawarah (law) for him in whom is the nagai (plague) of leprosy, who is not able to afford the taharah (sacrifice) for his cleansing.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah and to Aharawan, saying,

"When you have bawaa (come) into the aratz (land) of Kanain, which I nathan (give) to you for a achazah (possession), and I nathan (put) a spreading mildew in a bayath (house) in the aratz (land) of your achazah (possession),
then he who owns the bayath (house) shall bawaa (come) and nagad (tell) the kahan (priest), saying, ‘There seems to me to be some sort of nagai (plague) in the bayath (house).'

The kahan (priest) shall tzawah (command) that they panah (empty) the bayath (house), before the kahan (priest) goes in to examine the nagai (plague), that all that is in the bayath (house) not be made tamaa (unclean): and afterward the kahan (priest) shall bawaa (go) in to inspect the bayath (house).
He shall examine the nagai (plague); and behold, if the nagai (plague) is in the walls of the bayath (house) with hollow streaks, Yaraqaraq or Adamadam, and it appears Shapal be deeper than the wall;
then the kahan (priest) shall yatzaa (go) out of the bayath (house) to the door of the bayath (house), and shut up the bayath (house) shabai (seven) yawam (days).
The kahan (priest) shall shawab (turn back / repent) again on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), and raah (see). If the nagai (plague) has spread in the walls of the bayath (house),
then the kahan (priest) shall tzawah (command) that they chalatz (take) out the aban (stones) in which is the nagai (plague), and cast them into an tamaa (unclean) place outside of the Iyar:
and he shall cause the bayath (inside) of the bayath (house) to be scraped all over, and they shall pour out the mortar, that they scraped off, outside of the Iyar into an tamaa (unclean) place.
They shall take other aban (stones), and bawaa (put) them in the place of those aban (stones); and he shall take other mortar, and shall plaster the bayath (house).

"If the nagai (plague) shawab (turn back / repent) again, and breaks out in the bayath (house), achar (after) he has taken out the aban (stones), and achar (after) he has scraped the bayath (house), and achar (after) it was plastered;

then the kahan (priest) shall bawaa (come) in and raah (see); and behold, if the nagai (plague) has spread in the bayath (house), it is a destructive mildew in the bayath (house). It is tamaa (unclean).
He shall nathatz (break) down the bayath (house), its aban (stones), and its itz (timber), and all the bayath (house's) mortar. He shall carry them out of the Iyar into an tamaa (unclean) place.
"Moreover he who goes into the bayath (house) yawam (while) it is shut up shall be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
He who lies down in the bayath (house) shall wash his clothes; and he who akal (eats) in the bayath (house) shall wash his clothes.

"If the kahan (priest) shall bawaa (come) in, and examine it, and behold, the nagai (plague) hasn't spread in the bayath (house), achar (after) the bayath (house) was plastered, then the kahan (priest) shall pronounce the bayath (house) tahar (clean), because the nagai (plague) is healed.
To chataa (cleanse) the bayath (house) he shall take shanayam (two) birds, and cedar itz (wood), and scarlet, and hyssop.
He shall kill one of the birds in an charash (earthen) vessel over chay (running) mayam (water).

He shall take the cedar itz (wood), and the hyssop, and the scarlet, and the chay (living) bird, and dip them in the dam (blood) of the slain bird, and in the chay (running) mayam (water), and sprinkle the bayath (house) shabai (seven) paim (times).

He shall chataa (cleanse) the bayath (house) with the dam (blood) of the bird, and with the chay (running) mayam (water), with the chay (living) bird, with the cedar itz (wood), with the hyssop, and with the scarlet;
but he shall let the chay (living) bird shalach (go) out of the Iyar into the panayam (open) shadah (field). So shall he make kapar (atonement) for the bayath (house); and it shall be tahar (clean).
This is the thawarah (law) for any nagai (plague) of leprosy, and for an itch,
and for the destructive mildew of a bagad (garment), and for a bayath (house),
and for a rising, and for a scab, and for a bright spot;
to teach when it is tamaa (unclean), and when it is tahawar (clean). This is the thawarah (law) of leprosy.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah and to Aharawan, saying,
"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them, ‘When any ayash (man) has a discharge from his body, because of his discharge he is tamaa (unclean).
This shall be his tamaah (uncleanness) in his discharge: whether his body runs with his discharge, or his body has stopped from his discharge, it is his tamaah (uncleanness).
"‘Every bed whereon he who has the discharge lies shall be tamaa (unclean); and everything he yashab (sits) on shall be tamaa (unclean).
ayash (whoever) touches his bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (water), and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
He who yashab (sits) on anything whereon the zawab (man) who has the discharge sat shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (water), and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
"‘He who touches the body of him who has the discharge shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (water), and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
"‘If he who has the discharge spits on him who is tahawar (clean), then he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (water), and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
"‘Whatever saddle he who has the discharge rides on shall be tamaa (unclean).

Whoever touches anything that was under him shall be tamaa (unclean) until the evening. He who nashaa (carries) those things shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (water), and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.

"‘Whoever he who has the discharge touches, without having rinsed his yad (hands) in mayam (water), he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (water), and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
"‘The earthen vessel, which he who has the discharge touches, shall be shabar (broken); and every vessel of itz (wood) shall be rinsed in mayam (water).

"‘When he who has a discharge is cleansed of his discharge, then he shall count to himself shabai (seven) yawam (days) for his cleansing, and wash his clothes; and he shall bathe his flesh in chay (running) mayam (water), and shall be tahar (clean).

"‘On the eighth yawam (day) he shall take shanayam (two) turtledoves, or shanayam (two) ban (young) pigeons, and bawaa (come) panayam (before) Yahawah to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and nathan (give) them to the kahan (priest):

and the kahan (priest) shall ishah (offer) them, the one for a chataah (sin) offering, and the other for a burnt ilah (offering). The kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him panayam (before) Yahawah for his discharge.
"‘If any ayash (man) has an emission of semen, then he shall bathe all his flesh in mayam (water), and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
Every bagad (garment), and every skin, whereon the semen is, shall be washed with mayam (water), and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
If a ayash (man) lies with a ashah (woman) and there is an emission of semen, they shall both bathe themselves in mayam (water), and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.

"‘If a ashah (woman) has a discharge, and her discharge in her flesh is dam (blood), she shall be in her impurity shabai (seven) yawam (days): and whoever touches her shall be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
"‘Everything that she lies on in her impurity shall be tamaa (unclean). Everything also that she yashab (sits) on shall be tamaa (unclean).
Whoever touches her bed shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (water), and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
Whoever touches anything that she yashab (sits) on shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (water), and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
If it is on the bed, or on anything whereon she yashab (sits), when he touches it, he shall be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
"‘If any ayash (man) lies with her, and her monthly flow is on him, he shall be tamaa (unclean) shabai (seven) yawam (days); and every bed whereon he lies shall be tamaa (unclean).

"‘If a ashah (woman) has a discharge of her dam (blood) many yawam (days) not in the ith (time) of her period, or if she has a discharge beyond the time of her period; all the yawam (days) of the discharge of her tamaah (uncleanness) shall be as in the yawam (days) of her period: she is tamaa (unclean).

Every bed whereon she lies all the yawam (days) of her discharge shall be to her as the bed of her period: and everything whereon she yashab (sits) shall be tamaa (unclean), as the tamaah (uncleanness) of her period.
Whoever touches these things shall be tamaa (unclean), and shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (water), and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
"‘But if she is cleansed of her discharge, then she shall count to herself shabai (seven) yawam (days), and achar (after) that she shall be tahar (clean).
On the eighth yawam (day) she shall take shanayam (two) turtledoves, or shanayam (two) ban (young) pigeons, and bawaa (bring) them to the kahan (priest), to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

The kahan (priest) shall ishah (offer) the one for a chataah (sin) offering, and the other for a burnt chataah (offering); and the kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for her panayam (before) Yahawah for the tamaah (uncleanness) of her discharge.

"‘Thus you shall nazar (separate) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) from their tamaah (uncleanness), so they will not mawath (die) in their tamaah (uncleanness), when they tamaa (defile) my mashakan (tabernacle) that is in their midst.'
This is the thawarah (law) of him who has a discharge, and of him who has an emission of semen, so that he is tamaa (unclean) thereby;
and Dawah her who has her period, and of a zakar (man) or naqabah (woman) who has a discharge, and of him who lies with her who is tamaa (unclean).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, achar (after) the mawath (death) of the shanayam (two) ban (sons) of Aharawan, when they drew near panayam (before) Yahawah, and died;

and Yahawah said to Mashah, "dabar (tell) Aharawan your ach (brother), not to bawaa (come) at all ith (times) into the Most qadash (holy) bayath (place) within the parakath (veil), panayam (before) the kaparath (mercy) seat which is on the arawan (ark); lest he mawath (die): for I will raah (see) in the cloud on the kaparath (mercy) seat.
"Herewith shall Aharawan bawaa (come) into the qadash (sanctuary): with a ban (young) bull for a chataah (sin) offering, and a ayal (ram) for a burnt chataah (offering).

He shall Labash on the qadash (holy) linen coat, and he shall have the linen breeches on his body, and shall put on the linen sash, and he shall be clothed with the linen turban. They are the qadash (holy) bagad (garments). He shall bathe his body in mayam (water), and Labash them on.
He shall take from the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shanayam (two) Shaiyar goats for a chataah (sin) offering, and one ayal (ram) for a burnt chataah (offering).
"Aharawan shall qarab (offer) the bull of the chataah (sin) offering, which is for himself, and make kapar (atonement) for himself and for his bayath (house).
He shall take the shanayam (two) Shaiyar, and imad (set) them panayam (before) Yahawah at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
Aharawan shall nathan (cast) lots for the shanayam (two) Shaiyar; one lot for Yahawah, and the other lot for the Izaazal.
Aharawan shall qarab (present) the Shaiyar on which the lot fell for Yahawah, and ishah (offer) him for a chataah (sin) offering.

But the Shaiyar, on which the lot fell for the Izaazal, shall be presented chay (alive) panayam (before) Yahawah, to make kapar (atonement) for him, to shalach (send) him away for the Izaazal into the madabar (wilderness).

"Aharawan shall qarab (present) the bull of the chataah (sin) offering, which is for himself, and shall make kapar (atonement) for himself and for his bayath (house), and shall kill the bull of the chataah (sin) offering which is for himself.

He shall take a censer full of coals of ash (fire) from off the mazabach (altar) panayam (before) Yahawah, and two handfuls of sweet incense beaten Daq, and bawaa (bring) it bayath (within) the parakath (veil):

and he shall nathan (put) the incense on the ash (fire) panayam (before) Yahawah, that the cloud of the incense may cover the kaparath (mercy) seat that is on the idawath (testimony), so that he will not mawath (die).

He shall take some of the dam (blood) of the bull, and sprinkle it with his finger on the kaparath (mercy) seat on the qadam (east); and panayam (before) the kaparath (mercy) seat he shall sprinkle some of the dam (blood) with his finger shabai (seven) paim (times).

"Then he shall kill the Shaiyar of the chataah (sin) offering, that is for the im (people), and bawaa (bring) his dam (blood) bayath (within) the parakath (veil), and do with his dam (blood) as he did with the dam (blood) of the bull, and sprinkle it on the kaparath (mercy) seat, and panayam (before) the kaparath (mercy) seat:

and he shall make kapar (atonement) for the qadash (holy) Place, because of the tamaah (uncleanness) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and because of their pashai (transgressions), even all their chataah (sins); and so he shall do for the ahal (tent) of Meeting, that shakan (dwells) with them in the midst of their tamaah (uncleanness).

No one shall be in the ahal (tent) of Meeting when he bawaa (enters) to make kapar (atonement) in the qadash (holy) Place, until he yatzaa (comes) out, and has made kapar (atonement) for himself and for his bayath (household), and for all the qahal (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel).

"He shall yatzaa (go) out to the mazabach (altar) that is panayam (before) Yahawah and make kapar (atonement) for it, and shall take some of the bull's dam (blood), and some of the Shaiyar dam (blood), and nathan (put) it around on the qaran (horns) of the mazabach (altar).

He shall sprinkle some of the dam (blood) on it with his finger shabai (seven) paim (times), and tahar (cleanse) it, and make it qadash (holy) from the tamaah (uncleanness) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
"When he has made an kalah (end) of atoning for the qadash (holy) Place, the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and the mazabach (altar), he shall qarab (present) the chay (live) Shaiyar.

Aharawan shall samak (lay) shanayam (both) his yad (hands) on the raash (head) of the chay (live) Shaiyar, and yadah (confess) over him all the iwan (iniquities) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and all their pashai (transgressions), even all their chataah (sins); and he shall nathan (put) them on the raash (head) of the Shaiyar, and shall shalach (send) him away into the madabar (wilderness) by the yad (hand) of a ayash (man) who is Ithay readiness.
The Shaiyar shall nashaa (carry) all their iwan (iniquities) Gazarah himself to a solitary aratz (land), and he shall let the Shaiyar shalach (go) in the madabar (wilderness).

"Aharawan shall bawaa (come) into the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and shall take off the linen bagad (garments), which he Labash on when he went into the qadash (holy) yanach (place), and shall leave them there.

Then he shall bathe himself in mayam (water) in a qadawash (holy) place, and Labash on his bagad (garments), and yatzaa (come) out and ishah (offer) his burnt ilah (offering) and the burnt ilah (offering) of the im (people), and make kapar (atonement) for himself and for the im (people).
The fat of the chataah (sin) offering he shall qatar (burn) on the mazabach (altar).
"He who lets the Shaiyar shalach (go) for the Izaazal shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in mayam (water), and afterward he shall bawaa (come) into the machanah (camp).

The bull for the chataah (sin) offering, and the Shaiyar for the chataah (sin) offering, whose dam (blood) was brought in to make kapar (atonement) in the qadash (holy) Place, shall be carried yatzaa (forth) outside the machanah (camp); and they shall sharap (burn) their skins, their flesh, and their dung with ash (fire).
He who sharap (burns) them shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in mayam (water), and afterward he shall bawaa (come) into the machanah (camp).

"It shall be a chaqah (statute) to you iwalam (forever): in the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month), on the tenth day of the chadash (month), you shall afflict your napash (souls), and shall do no kind of malaakah (work), the native-born, or the stranger who lives as a foreigner among you:
for on this yawam (day) shall kapar (atonement) be made for you, to tahar (cleanse) you; from all your chataah (sins) you shall be tahar (clean) panayam (before) Yahawah.
It is a shabath (sabbath) of solemn shabathawan (rest) to you, and you shall afflict your napash (souls); it is a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever).

The kahan (priest), who is mashach (anointed) and who is consecrated to be kahan (priest) in his ab (father's) place, shall make the kapar (atonement), and shall Labash on the linen bagad (garments), even the qadash (holy) bagad (garments).

Then he shall make kapar (atonement) for the qadash (holy) maqadash (sanctuary); and he shall make kapar (atonement) for the ahal (tent) of Meeting and for the mazabach (altar); and he shall make kapar (atonement) for the kahan (priests) and for all the im (people) of the qahal (assembly).

"This shall be an iwalam (forever) chaqah (statute) for you, to make kapar (atonement) for the children of Yasharaal (Israel) achad (once) in the Shanah because of all their chataah (sins)." It was done as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"dabar (speak) to Aharawan, and to his ban (sons), and to all the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (say) to them: ‘This is the thing which Yahawah has tzawah (commanded),
Whatever ayash (man) there is of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), who kills a bull, or lamb, or goat, in the machanah (camp), or who kills it outside the machanah (camp),

and hasn't brought it to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, to qarab (offer) it as an qaraban (offering) to Yahawah panayam (before) the mashakan (tabernacle) of Yahawah: dam (blood) shall be imputed to that ayash (man). He has shed dam (blood); and that ayash (man) shall be karath (cut) off from qarab (among) his im (people).

This is to the end that the children of Yasharaal (Israel) may bawaa (bring) their zabach (sacrifices), which they zabach (sacrifice) in the panayam (open) shadah (field), that they may bawaa (bring) them to Yahawah, to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, to the kahan (priest), and zabach (sacrifice) them for sacrifices of shalam (peace) zabach (offerings) to Yahawah.
The kahan (priest) shall sprinkle the dam (blood) on the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and qatar (burn) the fat for a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.

They shall no more zabach (sacrifice) their zabach (sacrifices) to the Shaiyar idols, achar (after) which they play the prostitute. This shall be a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) to them throughout their dawar (generations).'

"You shall amar (say) to them, ‘Any ayash (man) there is of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), or of the strangers who live as foreigners among them, who ilah (offers) a burnt ilah (offering) or zabach (sacrifice),
and doesn't bawaa (bring) it to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, to ishah (sacrifice) it to Yahawah; that ayash (man) shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people).

"‘Any ayash (man) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), or of the strangers who live as foreigners among them, who akal (eats) any kind of dam (blood), I will nathan (set) my panayam (face) against that napash (soul) who akal (eats) dam (blood), and will karath (cut) him off from qarab (among) his im (people).

For the napash (life) of the flesh is in the dam (blood); and I have given it to you on the mazabach (altar) to make kapar (atonement) for your napash (souls): for it is the dam (blood) that makes kapar (atonement) by reason of the napash (life).

Therefore I have said to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), "No napash (person) among you shall akal (eat) dam (blood), neither shall any stranger who lives as a foreigner among you akal (eat) dam (blood).

"‘Whatever ayash (man) there is of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), or of the strangers who live as foreigners among them, who takes in hunting any animal or bird that may be eaten; he shall pour out its dam (blood), and cover it with ipar (dust).

For as to the napash (life) of all flesh, its dam (blood) is with its napash (life): therefore I said to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), "You shall not akal (eat) the dam (blood) of any kind of flesh; for the napash (life) of all flesh is its dam (blood). Whoever akal (eats) it shall be karath (cut) off.

"‘Every napash (person) that akal (eats) what dies of itself, or that which is torn by animals, whether he is native-born or a foreigner, he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (water), and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening: then he shall be tahar (clean).
But if he doesn't wash them, or bathe his flesh, then he shall nashaa (bear) his iwan (iniquity).'
Yahawah said to Mashah,
"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (say) to them, ‘I am Yahawah your Alahayam.

You shall not do as they do in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, where you lived: and you shall not do as they do in the aratz (land) of Kanain, where I am bringing you; neither shall you yalak (walk) in their chaqah (statutes).
You shall do my mashapat (ordinances), and you shall shamar (keep) my chaqah (statutes), and yalak (walk) in them: I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
You shall therefore shamar (keep) my chaqah (statutes) and my mashapat (ordinances); which if a adam (man) does, he shall chayay (live) in them: I am Yahawah.
"‘None of you shall qarab (approach) anyone who are his close relatives, to galah (uncover) their irawah (nakedness): I am Yahawah.

"‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your ab (father), nor the irawah (nakedness) of your am (mother): she is your am (mother). You shall not galah (uncover) her irawah (nakedness).
"‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your ab (father's) ashah (wife): it is your ab (father's) irawah (nakedness).

"‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your achawath (sister), the bath (daughter) of your ab (father), or the bath (daughter) of your am (mother), whether born at bayath (home), or born abroad.

"‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your ban (son's) bath (daughter), or of your bath (daughter's) bath (daughter), even their irawah (nakedness): for theirs is your own irawah (nakedness).
"‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your ab (father's) ashah (wife's) bath (daughter), conceived by your ab (father), since she is your achawath (sister).
"‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your ab (father's) achawath (sister): she is your ab (father's) near kinswoman.
"‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your am (mother's) achawath (sister): for she is your am (mother's) near kinswoman.
"‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your ab (father's) ach (brother), you shall not qarab (approach) his ashah (wife): she is your dawadah (aunt).
"‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your daughter-in-law: she is your ban (son's) ashah (wife). You shall not galah (uncover) her irawah (nakedness).
"‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your ach (brother's) ashah (wife): it is your ach (brother's) irawah (nakedness).

"‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of a ashah (woman) and her bath (daughter). You shall not take her ban (son's) bath (daughter), or her bath (daughter's) bath (daughter), to galah (uncover) her irawah (nakedness); they are near kinswomen: it is wickedness.
"‘You shall not take a ashah (wife) to her achawath (sister), to be a rival, to galah (uncover) her irawah (nakedness), while her sister is yet chay (alive).
"‘You shall not qarab (approach) a ashah (woman) to galah (uncover) her irawah (nakedness), as long as she is impure by her tamaah (uncleanness).
"‘You shall not lie zarai (carnally) with your neighbor's ashah (wife), and tamaa (defile) yourself with her.
"‘You shall not give any of your children to sacrifice to Malak; neither shall you chalal (profane) the sham (name) of your Alahayam: I am Yahawah.
"‘You shall not shakab (lie) with a zakar (man), as with a ashah (woman). That is detestable.
"‘You shall not lie with any animal to tamaa (defile) yourself with it; neither shall any ashah (woman) give herself to an animal, to lie down with it: it is a perversion.
"‘Don't tamaa (defile) yourselves in any of these things: for in all these the gawayam (nations) which I am casting out panayam (before) you were defiled.
The aratz (land) was defiled: therefore I punished its iwan (iniquity), and the aratz (land) vomited out her yashab (inhabitants).

You therefore shall shamar (keep) my chaqah (statutes) and my mashapat (ordinances), and shall not do any of these thawaibah (abominations); neither the native-born, nor the stranger who lives as a foreigner among you;
(for all these thawaibah (abominations) have the men of the aratz (land) done, that were panayam (before) you, and the aratz (land) became defiled);
that the aratz (land) not vomit you out also, when you tamaa (defile) it, as it vomited out the gaway (nation) that was panayam (before) you.
"‘For whoever shall do any of these thawaibah (abominations), even the napash (souls) that do them shall be karath (cut) off from qarab (among) their im (people).

Therefore you shall shamar (keep) my requirements, that you do not practice any of these thawaibah (abominable) chaqah (customs), which were practiced panayam (before) you, and that you do not tamaa (defile) yourselves with them: I am Yahawah your Alahayam.'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"dabar (speak) to all the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them, ‘You shall be qadawash (holy); for I Yahawah your Alahayam am qadawash (holy).
"‘ayash (each) one of you shall respect his am (mother) and his ab (father). You shall shamar (keep) my shabath (sabbaths). I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
"‘Don't panah (turn) to idols, nor ishah (make) molten Alahayam for yourselves. I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
"‘When you zabach (offer) a zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings to Yahawah, you shall zabach (offer) it so that you may be accepted.

It shall be eaten the same yawam (day) you zabach (offer) it, and on the next macharath (day): and if anything yathar (remains) until the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), it shall be burned with ash (fire).
If it is eaten at all on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), it is an pagawal (abomination). It will not be accepted;

but everyone who akal (eats) it shall nashaa (bear) his iwan (iniquity), because he has profaned the qadash (holy) thing of Yahawah, and that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people).
"‘When you reap the harvest of your aratz (land), you shall not kalah (wholly) reap the corners of your shadah (field), neither shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest.
You shall not ilal (glean) your vineyard, neither shall you gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard; you shall leave them for the Inay and for the foreigner. I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
"‘You shall not steal. "‘You shall not lie. "‘You shall not deceive one another.
"‘You shall not shabai (swear) by my sham (name) falsely, and chalal (profane) the sham (name) of your Alahayam. I am Yahawah.
"‘You shall not oppress your neighbor, nor rob him. "‘The pailah (wages) of a shakayar (hired) servant shall not lawan (remain) with you all night until the baqar (morning).
"‘You shall not qalal (curse) the Charash, nor nathan (put) a stumbling block panayam (before) the iwar (blind); but you shall yaraa (fear) your Alahayam. I am Yahawah.

"‘You shall do no injustice in mashapat (judgment): you shall not be partial to the Dal, nor show favoritism to the gadawal (great); but you shall shapat (judge) your neighbor in tzadaq (righteousness).
"‘You shall not yalak (go) up and down as a slanderer among your im (people). "‘You shall not endanger the life of your neighbor. I am Yahawah.
"‘You shall not shanaa (hate) your ach (brother) in your labab (heart). You shall yakach (surely) yakach (rebuke) your neighbor, and not nashaa (bear) chataa (sin) because of him.
"‘You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your im (people); but you shall ahab (love) your neighbor as yourself. I am Yahawah.

"‘You shall shamar (keep) my chaqah (statutes). "‘You shall not crossbreed different kinds of animals. "‘you shall not zarai (sow) your shadah (field) with two kinds of kalaayam (seed); "‘neither shall there ilah (come) upon on you a bagad (garment) made of two kinds of material.

"‘If a ayash (man) lies zarai (carnally) with a ashah (woman) who is a slave girl, pledged to be married to another ayash (man), and not ransomed, or given her freedom; they shall be punished. They shall not be put to mawath (death), because she was not free.
He shall bawaa (bring) his asham (trespass) offering to Yahawah, to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, even a ayal (ram) for a asham (trespass) offering.

The kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for him with the ayal (ram) of the asham (trespass) offering panayam (before) Yahawah for his chataah (sin) which he has committed: and the chataah (sin) which he has committed shall be forgiven him.

"‘When you bawaa (come) into the aratz (land), and have planted all kinds of itz (trees) for food, then you shall count their fruit as forbidden. shalawash (three) Shanah shall they be Iral to you. It shall not be eaten.
But in the rabayaiy (fourth) Shanah all its fruit shall be qadash (holy), for giving halawal (praise) to Yahawah.
In the chamayashay (fifth) Shanah you shall akal (eat) its fruit, that it may yield its increase to you. I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
"‘You shall not akal (eat) any meat with the dam (blood) still in it; neither shall you use enchantments, nor practice sorcery.
"‘You shall not naqap (cut) the hair on the sides of your raash (heads), neither shall you clip off the edge of your beard.
"‘You shall not nathan (make) any cuttings in your flesh for the napash (dead), nor tattoo any marks on you. I am Yahawah.
"‘Don't chalal (profane) your bath (daughter), to make her a chalal (prostitute); lest the aratz (land) fall to prostitution, and the aratz (land) malaa (become) full of wickedness.
"‘You shall shamar (keep) my shabath (sabbaths), and yaraa (reverence) my maqadash (sanctuary); I am Yahawah.
"‘Don't panah (turn) to those who are mediums, nor to the wizards. Don't seek them out, to be defiled by them. I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
"‘You shall qawam (rise) up panayam (before) the gray shayabah (head), and honor the panayam (face) of an old zaqan (man), and you shall yaraa (fear) your Alahayam. I am Yahawah.
"‘If a stranger lives as a foreigner with you in your aratz (land), you shall not do him wrong.

The stranger who lives as a foreigner with you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall ahab (love) him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam. I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
"‘You shall do no iwal (unrighteousness) in mashapat (judgment), in measures of length, of weight, or of quantity.
You shall have tzadaq (just) balances, tzadaq (just) aban (weights), a tzadaq (just) ephah, and a tzadaq (just) hin. I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who brought you out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
"‘You shall shamar (observe) all my chaqah (statutes), and all my mashapat (ordinances), and do them. I am Yahawah.'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
