"Moreover, you shall amar (tell) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘Anyone of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), or of the strangers who live as foreigners in Yasharaal (Israel), who nathan (gives) any of his zarai (seed) to Malak; he shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death). The im (people) of the aratz (land) shall ragam (stone) him with ragam (stones).

I also will nathan (set) my panayam (face) against that ayash (person), and will karath (cut) him off from qarab (among) his im (people) because he has given of his zarai (seed) to Malak, to tamaa (defile) my maqadash (sanctuary), and to chalal (profane) my qadash (holy) sham (name).
If the im (people) of the aratz (land) all ilam (hide) their iyan (eyes) from that ayash (person), when he nathan (gives) of his zarai (seed) to Malak, and don't put him to mawath (death);

then I will shawam (set) my panayam (face) against that ayash (man), and against his mashapachah (family), and will karath (cut) him off, and all who play the prostitute achar (after) him, to play the prostitute with Malak, from qarab (among) their im (people).

"‘The napash (person) that panah (turns) to those who are mediums, and to the wizards, to play the prostitute achar (after) them, I will even nathan (set) my panayam (face) against that napash (person), and will karath (cut) him off from qarab (among) his im (people).
"‘qadash (sanctify) yourselves therefore, and be qadawash (holy); for I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
You shall shamar (keep) my chaqah (statutes), and do them. I am Yahawah who qadash (sanctifies) you.

"‘For everyone who qalal (curses) his ab (father) or his am (mother) shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death): he has cursed his ab (father) or his am (mother); his dam (blood) shall be upon him.

"‘The ayash (man) who naap (commits) adultery with another ayash (man's) ashah (wife), even he who naap (commits) adultery with his neighbor's ashah (wife), the naap (adulterer) and the naap (adulteress) shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death).

"‘The ayash (man) who lies with his ab (father's) ashah (wife) has uncovered his ab (father's) irawah (nakedness): shanayam (both) of them shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death); their dam (blood) shall be upon them.

"‘If a ayash (man) lies with his kalah (daughter-in-law), shanayam (both) of them shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death): they have committed a perversion; their dam (blood) shall be upon them.

"‘If a ayash (man) lies with a zakar (male), as with a ashah (woman), shanayam (both) of them have committed an thawaibah (abomination): they shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death); their dam (blood) shall be upon them.
"‘If a ayash (man) takes a ashah (wife) and her am (mother), it is wickedness: they shall be burned with ash (fire), both he and they; that there may be no wickedness among you.
"‘If a ayash (man) lies with an animal, he shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death); and you shall harag (kill) the animal.

"‘If a ashah (woman) approaches any animal, and lies down with it, you shall harag (kill) the ashah (woman), and the animal: they shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death); their dam (blood) shall be upon them.

"‘If a ayash (man) takes his achawath (sister), his ab (father's) bath (daughter), or his am (mother's) bath (daughter), and raah (see) her irawah (nakedness), and she raah (see) his irawah (nakedness); it is a shameful thing; and they shall be karath (cut) off in the iyan (sight) of the children of their im (people): he has uncovered his achawath (sister's) irawah (nakedness); he shall nashaa (bear) his iwan (iniquity).

"‘If a ayash (man) lies with a ashah (woman) Dawah her monthly period, and galah (uncovers) her irawah (nakedness); he has made naked her fountain, and she has uncovered the fountain of her dam (blood): and shanayam (both) of them shall be karath (cut) off from qarab (among) their im (people).

"‘You shall not galah (uncover) the irawah (nakedness) of your am (mother's) achawath (sister), nor of your ab (father's) achawath (sister); for he has made naked his close relative: they shall nashaa (bear) their iwan (iniquity).
If a ayash (man) lies with his dawadah (uncle's) wife, he has uncovered his dawad (uncle's) irawah (nakedness): they shall nashaa (bear) their chataa (sin); they shall mawath (die) Irayaray.
"‘If a ayash (man) takes his ach (brother's) ashah (wife), it is an impurity: he has uncovered his ach (brother's) irawah (nakedness); they shall be Irayaray.
"‘You shall therefore shamar (keep) all my chaqah (statutes), and all my mashapat (ordinances), and do them; that the aratz (land), where I am bringing you to yashab (dwell), may not vomit you out.
You shall not yalak (walk) in the chaqah (customs) of the gaway (nation), which I am casting out panayam (before) you: for they did all these things, and therefore I abhorred them.

But I have said to you, "You shall yarash (inherit) their adamah (land), and I will nathan (give) it to you to yarash (possess) it, a aratz (land) flowing with milk and honey." I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who has separated you from the im (peoples).

"‘You shall therefore make a distinction between the tahawar (clean) animal and the tamaa (unclean), and between the tamaa (unclean) fowl and the tahawar (clean): and you shall not make yourselves shaqatz (abominable) by animal, or by bird, or by anything with which the adamah (ground) teems, which I have separated from you as tamaa (unclean) for you.
You shall be qadawash (holy) to me: for I, Yahawah, am qadawash (holy), and have set you apart from the im (peoples), that you should be mine.

"‘A ayash (man) or a ashah (woman) that is a medium, or is a wizard, shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death): they shall ragam (stone) them with ragam (stones); their dam (blood) shall be upon them.'

Yahawah said to Mashah, "amar (speak) to the kahan (priests), the ban (sons) of Aharawan, and amar (say) to them, ‘A priest shall not tamaa (defile) himself for the napash (dead) among his im (people);
except for his relatives that are qarawab (near) to him: for his am (mother), for his ab (father), for his ban (son), for his bath (daughter), for his ach (brother),
and for his virgin achawath (sister) who is qarawab (near) to him, who has had no ayash (husband); for her he may tamaa (defile) himself.
He shall not tamaa (defile) himself, being a chief bail (man) among his im (people), to chalal (profane) himself.
"‘They shall not shave their raash (heads), neither shall they shave off the corners of their beards, nor make any cuttings in their flesh.

They shall be qadash (holy) to their Alahayam, and not chalal (profane) the sham (name) of their Alahayam; for they qarab (offer) the ashah (offerings) of Yahawah made by ashah (fire), the lacham (bread) of their Alahayam; therefore they shall be qadawash (holy).
"‘They shall not marry a ashah (woman) who is a prostitute, or Chalal; neither shall they marry a ashah (woman) divorced from her ayash (husband): for he is qadawash (holy) to his Alahayam.
You shall qadash (sanctify) him therefore; for he qarab (offers) the lacham (bread) of your Alahayam: he shall be qadawash (holy) to you: for I Yahawah, who qadash (sanctify) you, am qadawash (holy).
"‘The bath (daughter) of any kahan (priest), if she chalal (profanes) herself by playing the prostitute, she chalal (profanes) her ab (father): she shall be burned with ash (fire).

"‘He who is the gadawal (high) kahan (priest) among his ach (brothers), upon whose raash (head) the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil) is poured, and that is consecrated to Labash on the bagad (garments), shall not let the hair of his raash (head) hang loose, nor tear his clothes;
neither shall he bawaa (go) in to any mawath (dead) napash (body), nor tamaa (defile) himself for his ab (father), or for his am (mother);

neither shall he yatzaa (go) out of the maqadash (sanctuary), nor chalal (profane) the maqadash (sanctuary) of his Alahayam; for the nazar (crown) of the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil) of his Alahayam is upon him. I am Yahawah.
"‘He shall take a ashah (wife) in her virginity.
A alamanah (widow), or one divorced, or a woman who has been defiled, or a prostitute, these he shall not marry: but a virgin of his own im (people) shall he take as a ashah (wife).
He shall not chalal (profane) his zarai (seed) among his im (people): for I am Yahawah who qadash (sanctifies) him.'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"dabar (say) to Aharawan, ‘ayash (none) of your zarai (seed) throughout their dawar (generations) who has a blemish, may qarab (approach) to qarab (offer) the lacham (bread) of his Alahayam.
For whatever ayash (man) he is that has a blemish, he shall not qarab (draw) near: a iwar (blind) ayash (man), or a Pasach, or he who has a charam (flat) nose, or any deformity,
or a ayash (man) who has an injured shabar (foot), or an injured shabar (hand),
or Gaban, or a Daq, or thabalal (one) who has a defect in his iyan (eye), or an itching disease, or scabs, or who has Marawach testicles;

no ayash (man) of the zarai (seed) of Aharawan the kahan (priest) who has a blemish, shall come near to qarab (offer) the ashah (offerings) of Yahawah made by ashah (fire). Since he has a blemish, he shall not come near to qarab (offer) the lacham (bread) of his Alahayam.
He shall akal (eat) the lacham (bread) of his Alahayam, both of the most qadash (holy), and of the qadash (holy).

He shall not bawaa (come) near to the parakath (veil), nor come near to the mazabach (altar), because he has a blemish; that he may not chalal (profane) my maqadash (sanctuaries), for I am Yahawah who qadash (sanctifies) them.'
So Mashah spoke to Aharawan, and to his ban (sons), and to all the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (tell) Aharawan and his ban (sons) to nazar (separate) themselves from the qadash (holy) things of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), which they make qadash (holy) to me, and that they not chalal (profane) my qadash (holy) sham (name). I am Yahawah.

"amar (tell) them, ‘If anyone of all your zarai (seed) throughout your dawar (generations) approaches the qadash (holy) things, which the children of Yasharaal (Israel) make qadash (holy) to Yahawah, having his tamaah (uncleanness) on him, that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from before me. I am Yahawah.

"‘Whoever of the zarai (seed) of Aharawan is a leper or has an issue; he shall not akal (eat) of the qadash (holy) things, until he is tahar (clean). Whoever touches anything that is tamaa (unclean) by the napash (dead), or a ayash (man) whose zarai (seed) goes from him;
or ayash (whoever) touches any creeping thing, whereby he may be made tamaa (unclean), or a adam (man) of whom he may take uncleanness, whatever tamaah (uncleanness) he has;
the napash (person) that touches any such shall be tamaa (unclean) until the evening, and shall not akal (eat) of the qadash (holy) things, am (unless) he bathe his body in mayam (water).
When the shamash (sun) is down, he shall be tahar (clean); and afterward he shall akal (eat) of the qadash (holy) things, because it is his bread.
That which dies of nabalah (itself), or is torn by animals, he shall not akal (eat), defiling himself by it. I am Yahawah.
"‘They shall therefore follow my requirements, lest they nashaa (bear) chataa (sin) for it, and mawath (die) therein, if they chalal (profane) it. I am Yahawah who qadash (sanctifies) them.
"‘No stranger shall akal (eat) of the qadash (holy) thing: a foreigner living with the kahan (priests), or a hired shakayar (servant), shall not akal (eat) of the qadash (holy) thing.
But if a kahan (priest) qanah (buys) a slave, purchased by his kasap (money), he shall akal (eat) of it; and such as are yalayad (born) in his bayath (house), they shall akal (eat) of his bread.
If a kahan (priest's) bath (daughter) is married to an outsider, she shall not akal (eat) of the heave tharawamah (offering) of the qadash (holy) things.

But if a kahan (priest's) bath (daughter) is a alamanah (widow), or divorced, and has no zarai (child), and has returned to her ab (father's) bayath (house), as in her youth, she may akal (eat) of her ab (father's) bread: but no stranger shall akal (eat) any of it.

"‘If a ayash (man) akal (eats) something shagagah (holy) unwittingly, then he shall add the chamayashay (fifth) part of its value to it, and shall nathan (give) the qadash (holy) thing to the kahan (priest).
The priests shall not chalal (profane) the qadash (holy) things of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), which they offer to Yahawah,
and so cause them to nashaa (bear) the iwan (iniquity) that brings guilt, when they akal (eat) their qadash (holy) things: for I am Yahawah who qadash (sanctifies) them.'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (speak) to Aharawan, and to his ban (sons), and to all the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (say) to them, ‘ayash (whoever) is of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), or of the foreigners in Yasharaal (Israel), who qarab (offers) his qaraban (offering), whether it be any of their nadar (vows), or any of their freewill nadabah (offerings), which they qarab (offer) to Yahawah for a burnt ilah (offering);
that you may be accepted, you shall offer a zakar (male) thamayam (without) blemish, of the bulls, of the sheep, or of the goats.
But whatever has a blemish, that you shall not qarab (offer): for it shall not be acceptable for you.

ayash (whoever) qarab (offers) a zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings to Yahawah to palaa (accomplish) a nadar (vow), or for a freewill nadabah (offering), of the herd or of the flock, it shall be thamayam (perfect) to be accepted; no blemish shall be therein.

Blind, injured, maimed, having a wart, festering, or having a running sore, you shall not qarab (offer) these to Yahawah, nor nathan (make) an ashah (offering) by fire of them on the mazabach (altar) to Yahawah.
Either a bull or a lamb that has any deformity or lacking in his parts, that you may ishah (offer) for a freewill nadabah (offering); but for a nadar (vow) it shall not be accepted.
That which has its testicles bruised, kathath (crushed), broken, or karath (cut), you shall not qarab (offer) to Yahawah; neither shall you do thus in your aratz (land).

Neither shall you qarab (offer) the lacham (bread) of your Alahayam from the yad (hand) of a foreigner of any of these; because their corruption is in them. There is a blemish in them. They shall not be accepted for you.'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"When a bull, or a sheep, or a goat, is born, then it shall remain shabai (seven) yawam (days) with its am (mother); and from the eighth yawam (day) and thenceforth it shall be accepted for the qaraban (offering) of an qaraban (offering) made by ashah (fire) to Yahawah.
Whether it is a cow or ewe, you shall not kill it and its ban (young) both in one yawam (day).
"When you zabach (sacrifice) a zabach (sacrifice) of thanksgiving to Yahawah, you shall zabach (sacrifice) it so that you may be accepted.
It shall be eaten on the same yawam (day); you shall yathar (leave) none of it until the baqar (morning). I am Yahawah.
"Therefore you shall shamar (keep) my matzawah (commandments), and do them. I am Yahawah.
You shall not chalal (profane) my qadash (holy) sham (name), but I will be made qadash (holy) among the children of Yasharaal (Israel). I am Yahawah who makes you qadash (holy),
who brought you out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, to be your Alahayam. I am Yahawah.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them, ‘The mawaid (set) feasts of Yahawah, which you shall qaraa (proclaim) to be qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocations), even these are my mawaid (set) feasts.

"‘shash (six) yawam (days) shall malaakah (work) be done: but on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) is a shabath (sabbath) of solemn shabathawan (rest), a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation); you shall do no kind of malaakah (work). It is a shabath (sabbath) to Yahawah in all your mawashab (dwellings).
"‘These are the mawaid (set) feasts of Yahawah, even qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocations), which you shall qaraa (proclaim) in their mawaid (appointed) season.
In the raashawan (first) chadash (month), on the fourteenth irab (day) of the month in the evening, is yahawah (yahweh's) pasach (passover).
On the fifteenth yawam (day) of the same chadash (month) is the chag (feast) of unleavened matzah (bread) to Yahawah. shabai (seven) yawam (days) you shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread).
In the raashawan (first) yawam (day) you shall have a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation). You shall do no regular malaakah (work).

But you shall qarab (offer) an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah shabai (seven) yawam (days). In the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) is a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation): you shall do no regular malaakah (work).'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them, ‘When you have bawaa (come) into the aratz (land) which I nathan (give) to you, and shall reap its the harvest, then you shall bawaa (bring) the sheaf of the raashayath (first) fruits of your harvest to the kahan (priest):
and he shall wave the sheaf panayam (before) Yahawah, to be accepted for you. On the next macharath (day) after the shabath (sabbath) the kahan (priest) shall wave it.
On the yawam (day) when you wave the sheaf, you shall ishah (offer) a male lamb thamayam (without) blemish a Shanah old for a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah.

The meal manachah (offering) with it shall be shanayam (two) isharawan (tenth) parts of an ephah of fine flour mingled with shaman (oil), an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah for a pleasant aroma; and the drink nasak (offering) with it shall be of yayan (wine), the rabayaiy (fourth) part of a hin.

You shall akal (eat) neither lacham (bread), nor roasted grain, nor fresh grain, until this same yawam (day), until you have brought the qaraban (offering) of your Alahayam. This is a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) throughout your dawar (generations) in all your mawashab (dwellings).

"‘You shall count from the next macharath (day) after the shabath (sabbath), from the macharath (day) that you brought the sheaf of the wave thanawapah (offering); shabai (seven) shabath (sabbaths) shall be completed:

even to the next macharath (day) after the shabayaiy (seventh) shabath (sabbath) you shall number chamashayam (fifty) yawam (days); and you shall qarab (offer) a Chadash meal manachah (offering) to Yahawah.

You shall bawaa (bring) out of your habitations shanayam (two) loaves of bread for a thanawapah (wave) offering made of shanayam (two) isharawan (tenth) parts of an ephah of fine flour. They shall be baked with yeast, for bakawar (first) fruits to Yahawah.

You shall qarab (present) with the lacham (bread) shabai (seven) lambs thamayam (without) blemish a Shanah old, one young bull, and shanayam (two) ayal (rams). They shall be a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah, with their meal ilah (offering), and their drink ilah (offerings), even an manachah (offering) made by ashah (fire), of a sweet aroma to Yahawah.
You shall ishah (offer) one Shaiyar goat for a chataah (sin) offering, and shanayam (two) male lambs a Shanah old for a zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings.

The kahan (priest) shall wave them with the lacham (bread) of the bakawar (first) fruits for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah, with the shanayam (two) lambs. They shall be qadash (holy) to Yahawah for the kahan (priest).

You shall make proclamation on the same yawam (day): there shall be a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation) to you; you shall do no regular malaakah (work). This is a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) in all your mawashab (dwellings) throughout your dawar (generations).

"‘When you reap the harvest of your aratz (land), you shall not kalah (wholly) reap into the corners of your shadah (field), neither shall you gather the gleanings of your harvest: you shall leave them for the Inay, and for the foreigner. I am Yahawah your Alahayam.'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, ‘In the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month), on the achad (first) day of the chadash (month), shall be a solemn shabathawan (rest) to you, a zakarawan (memorial) of blowing of trumpets, a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation).
You shall do no regular malaakah (work); and you shall qarab (offer) an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah.'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"However on the tenth day of this shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month) is the yawam (day) of kapar (atonement): it shall be a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation) to you, and you shall afflict yourselves; and you shall qarab (offer) an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah.
You shall do no kind of malaakah (work) in that same yawam (day); for it is a yawam (day) of kapar (atonement), to make kapar (atonement) for you panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam.
For whoever it is who shall not deny himself in that same yawam (day); shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people).
Whoever it is who does any kind of malaakah (work) in that same yawam (day), that napash (person) I will abad (destroy) from qarab (among) his im (people).
You shall do no kind of malaakah (work): it is a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) throughout your dawar (generations) in all your mawashab (dwellings).

It shall be a shabath (sabbath) of solemn shabathawan (rest) for you, and you shall deny yourselves. In the ninth day of the chadash (month) at evening, from evening to evening, you shall shabath (keep) your shabath (sabbath).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (say), ‘On the fifteenth yawam (day) of this shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month) is the chag (feast) of sakah (tents) for shabai (seven) yawam (days) to Yahawah.
On the raashawan (first) yawam (day) shall be a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation): you shall do no regular malaakah (work).

shabai (seven) yawam (days) you shall qarab (offer) an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah. On the eighth yawam (day) shall be a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation) to you; and you shall qarab (offer) an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah. It is a solemn itzarah (assembly); you shall do no regular malaakah (work).

"‘These are the mawaid (appointed) feasts of Yahawah, which you shall qaraa (proclaim) to be qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocations), to qarab (offer) an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah, a burnt ilah (offering), and a meal ilah (offering), a zabach (sacrifice), and drink manachah (offerings), each on its own yawam (day);
besides the shabath (sabbaths) of Yahawah, and besides your mathanah (gifts), and besides all your nadar (vows), and besides all your freewill nadabah (offerings), which you nathan (give) to Yahawah.

"‘So on the fifteenth yawam (day) of the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month), when you have gathered in the fruits of the aratz (land), you shall keep the chag (feast) of Yahawah shabai (seven) yawam (days): on the raashawan (first) yawam (day) shall be a solemn shabathawan (rest), and on the eighth yawam (day) shall be a solemn shabathawan (rest).

You shall take on the raashawan (first) yawam (day) the fruit of hadar (goodly) itz (trees), branches of palm trees, and boughs of Ibath itz (trees), and willows of the nachal (brook); and you shall Shamach panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam shabai (seven) yawam (days).

You shall keep it a chag (feast) to Yahawah shabai (seven) yawam (days) in the Shanah: it is a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) throughout your dawar (generations); you shall keep it in the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month).
You shall yashab (dwell) in sakah (booths) shabai (seven) yawam (days). All who are native-born in Yasharaal (Israel) shall yashab (dwell) in sakah (booths),

that your dawar (generations) may yadai (know) that I made the children of Yasharaal (Israel) to yashab (dwell) in sakah (booths), when I brought them out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam. I am Yahawah your Alahayam.'
Mashah declared to the children of Yasharaal (Israel) the mawaid (appointed) feasts of Yahawah.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"tzawah (command) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), that they bring to you zak (pure) olive shaman (oil) Kathayath for the maawar (light), to cause a nayar (lamp) to ilah (burn) continually.

Outside of the parakath (veil) of the idawath (testimony), in the ahal (tent) of Meeting, shall Aharawan keep it in order from evening to baqar (morning) panayam (before) Yahawah continually: it shall be a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) throughout your dawar (generations).
He shall keep in order the nayar (lamps) on the tahawar (pure) gold lampstand panayam (before) Yahawah continually.
"You shall take fine flour, and bake ishar (twelve) cakes of it: shanayam (two) isharawan (tenth) parts of an ephah shall be in one cake.
You shall shawam (set) them in shanayam (two) mairakah (rows), shash (six) on a mairakath (row), on the tahawar (pure) gold table panayam (before) Yahawah.
You shall nathan (put) zak (pure) frankincense on each mairakath (row), that it may be to the lacham (bread) for a azakarah (memorial), even an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah.
Every shabath (sabbath) yawam (day) he shall set it in order panayam (before) Yahawah continually. It is on the behalf of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant).

It shall be for Aharawan and his ban (sons); and they shall akal (eat) it in a qadawash (holy) place: for it is most qadash (holy) to him of the ashah (offerings) of Yahawah made by ashah (fire) by a perpetual chaq (statute).

The ban (son) Yasharaalayath an Israelite ashah (woman), whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the children of Yasharaal (Israel); and the ban (son) Yasharaalayath the Israelite woman and a ayash (man) of Yasharaal (Israel) strove together in the machanah (camp).

The ban (son) Yasharaalayath the Israelite ashah (woman) blasphemed the sham (name), and cursed; and they brought him to Mashah. His am (mother's) sham (name) was Shalamayath, the bath (daughter) of Dabaray, of the matah (tribe) Dan Dan.
They yanach (put) him in custody, until the will of Yahawah should be declared to them.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"yatzaa (bring) out of the machanah (camp) him who cursed; and let all who heard him samak (lay) their yad (hands) on his raash (head), and let all the idah (congregation) ragam (stone) him.
You shall dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, ‘ayash (whoever) kay (curses) his Alahayam shall nashaa (bear) his chataa (sin).

He who naqab (blasphemes) the sham (name) of Yahawah, he shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death); all the idah (congregation) shall ragam (certainly) ragam (stone) him: the foreigner as well as the native-born, when he naqab (blasphemes) the sham (name), shall be put to mawath (death).
"‘He who strikes any adam (man) mortally shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death).
He who strikes an animal mortally shall make it shalam (good), napash (life) for napash (life).
If anyone injures his neighbor; as he has done, so shall it be done to him:
fracture for fracture, iyan (eye) for iyan (eye), tooth for tooth; as he has injured someone, so shall it be done to him.
He who kills an animal shall make it shalam (good); and he who kills a adam (man) shall be put to mawath (death).
You shall have one kind of mashapat (law), for the foreigner as well as the native-born: for I am Yahawah your Alahayam.'

Mashah spoke to the children of Yasharaal (Israel); and they brought out him who had cursed out of the machanah (camp), and stoned him with ragam (stones). The children of Yasharaal (Israel) did as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
Yahawah said to Mashah in har (mount) Sayanay,

"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them, ‘When you bawaa (come) into the aratz (land) which I nathan (give) you, then the aratz (land) shall shabath (keep) a shabath (sabbath) to Yahawah.
shash (six) Shanah you shall zarai (sow) your shadah (field), and shash (six) Shanah you shall prune your vineyard, and asap (gather) in its fruits;

but in the shabayaiy (seventh) Shanah there shall be a shabath (sabbath) of solemn shabathawan (rest) for the aratz (land), a shabath (sabbath) to Yahawah. You shall not zarai (sow) your shadah (field) or prune your vineyard.

What grows of itself in your harvest you shall not reap, and the inab (grapes) of your undressed vine you shall not batzar (gather). It shall be a Shanah of solemn shabathawan (rest) for the aratz (land).

The shabath (sabbath) of the aratz (land) shall be for food for you; for yourself, for your ibad (servant), for your amah (maid), for your hired ibad (servant), and for your stranger, who lives as a foreigner with you.
For your livestock also, and for the animals that are in your aratz (land), shall all its increase be for akal (food).

"'You shall count off shabai (seven) shabath (sabbaths) of Shanah, shabai (seven) paim (times) shabai (seven) Shanah; and there shall be to you the yawam (days) of shabai (seven) shabath (sabbaths) of Shanah, even forty - nine Shanah.

Then you shall ibar (sound) the loud trumpet on the tenth day of the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month). On the yawam (day) of kapar (atonement) you shall ibar (sound) the trumpet throughout all your aratz (land).

You shall make the fiftieth Shanah qadash (holy), and qaraa (proclaim) liberty throughout the aratz (land) to all its yashab (inhabitants). It shall be a jubilee to you; and ayash (each) of you shall shawab (turn back / repent) to his own property, and ayash (each) of you shall shawab (turn back / repent) to his mashapachah (family).
That fiftieth Shanah shall be a jubilee to you. In it you shall not zarai (sow), neither reap that which grows of itself, nor batzar (gather) from the undressed vines.
For it is a jubilee; it shall be qadash (holy) to you. You shall akal (eat) of its increase out of the shadah (field).
"‘In this Shanah of Jubilee ayash (each) of you shall shawab (turn back / repent) to his property.
"‘If you sell anything to your neighbor, or qanah (buy) from your neighbor, you shall not wrong one ach (another).
According to the number of Shanah achar (after) the Jubilee you shall qanah (buy) from your neighbor. According to the number of Shanah of the crops he shall sell to you.
According to the length of the Shanah you shall increase its price, and according to the shortness of the Shanah you shall diminish its price; for he is selling the number of the crops to you.
You shall not wrong one another; but you shall yaraa (fear) your Alahayam: for I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
"‘Therefore you shall do my chaqah (statutes), and shamar (keep) my mashapat (ordinances) and do them; and you shall yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land) in safety.
The aratz (land) shall nathan (yield) its fruit, and you shall akal (eat) your fill, and yashab (dwell) therein in safety.
If you said, "What shall we akal (eat) the shabayaiy (seventh) Shanah? Behold, we shall not zarai (sow), nor asap (gather) in our increase;
then I will tzawah (command) my barakah (blessing) on you in the shashay (sixth) Shanah, and it shall ishah (bring) forth fruit for the shalawash (three) Shanah.
You shall zarai (sow) the eighth Shanah, and akal (eat) of the fruits, the Yashan store; until the thashayaiy (ninth) Shanah, until its fruits bawaa (come) in, you shall akal (eat) the Yashan store.
"‘The aratz (land) shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the aratz (land) is mine; for you are strangers and live as foreigners with me.
In all the aratz (land) of your achazah (possession) you shall nathan (grant) a gaalah (redemption) for the aratz (land).
"‘If your ach (brother) becomes poor, and sells some of his achazah (possessions), then his kinsman who is next to him shall bawaa (come), and gaal (redeem) that which his ach (brother) has sold.
If a ayash (man) has no one to gaal (redeem) it, and he becomes prosperous and matzaa (finds) sufficient means to redeem it;
then let him chashab (reckon) the Shanah since its sale, and shawab (turn back / repent) the surplus to the ayash (man) to whom he sold it; and he shall shawab (turn back / repent) to his property.

But if he isn't able to matzaa (get) it back for himself, then what he has sold shall remain in the yad (hand) of him who has bought it until the Shanah of Jubilee: and in the Jubilee it shall be released, and he shall shawab (turn back / repent) to his property.

"‘If a ayash (man) sells a mawashab (dwelling) bayath (house) in a walled Iyar, then he may gaalah (redeem) it within a thamam (whole) Shanah after it has been sold. For a yawam (full) year he shall have the right of gaalah (redemption).

If it isn't redeemed within the malaa (space) of a thamayam (full) Shanah, then the bayath (house) that is in the walled Iyar shall be made sure in perpetuity to him who bought it, throughout his dawar (generations). It shall not be released in the Jubilee.

But the bayath (houses) of the villages which have no wall around them shall be reckoned with the shadah (fields) of the aratz (country): they may be redeemed, and they shall be released in the Jubilee.
"‘Nevertheless the Iyar Lawayay the Levites, the bayath (houses) in the Iyar of their achazah (possession), the Lawayay (Levites) may gaalah (redeem) at any time.

The Lawayay (Levites) may gaal (redeem) the bayath (house) that was sold, and the Iyar of his achazah (possession), and it shall be released in the Jubilee; for the bayath (houses) of the Iyar Lawayay the Levites are their achazah (possession) among the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
But the shadah (field) of the suburbs of their Iyar may not be sold; for it is their perpetual achazah (possession).
"‘If your ach (brother) has become poor, and his mawat (hand) can't support him among you; then you shall uphold him. He shall chay (live) with you like an alien and a temporary resident.
Take no interest from him or profit, but yaraa (fear) your Alahayam; that your ach (brother) may chay (live) among you.
You shall not nathan (lend) him your kasap (money) at interest, nor nathan (give) him your food for profit.
I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who brought you yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, to nathan (give) you the aratz (land) of Kanain, and to be your Alahayam.
"‘If your ach (brother) has grown poor among you, and sells himself to you; you shall not ibad (make) him to serve as a ibad (slave).
As a hired shakayar (servant), and as a temporary resident, he shall be with you; he shall ibad (serve) with you until the Shanah of Jubilee:
then he shall yatzaa (go) out from you, he and his children with him, and shall shawab (turn back / repent) to his own mashapachah (family), and to the achazah (possession) of his abawath (fathers).
For they are my ibad (servants), whom I brought out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam. They shall not be sold as ibad (slaves).
You shall not radah (rule) over him with harshness, but shall yaraa (fear) your Alahayam.
"‘As for your male and your female slaves, whom you may have; of the gawayam (nations) that are around you, from them you may qanah (buy) male and female slaves.

Moreover of the children of the aliens who live among you, of them you may qanah (buy), and of their mashapachah (families) who are with you, which they have conceived in your aratz (land); and they will be your property.

You may make them an nachal (inheritance) for your children achar (after) you, to hold for a achazah (possession); of them may you take your slaves iwalam (forever): but over your ach (brothers) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) you shall not radah (rule), one over ach (another), with harshness.

"‘If an alien or temporary resident with you becomes rich, and your ach (brother) beside him has grown poor, and sells himself to the stranger or foreigner living among you, or to a member of the stranger's mashapachah (family);
achar (after) he is sold he may be redeemed. One of his ach (brothers) may gaal (redeem) him;

or his dawad (uncle), or his dawad (uncle's) ban (son), may gaal (redeem) him, or any who is a close relative to him of his mashapachah (family) may gaal (redeem) him; or if he has grown rich, he may gaal (redeem) yad (himself).

He shall chashab (reckon) with him who bought him from the Shanah that he sold himself to him to the Shanah of Jubilee: and the kasap (price) of his sale shall be according to the number of Shanah; according to the yawam (time) of a hired shakayar (servant) shall he be with him.
If there are yet many Shanah, according to them he shall shawab (turn back / repent) back the price of his gaalah (redemption) out of the kasap (money) that he was maqanah (bought) for.

If there shaar (remain) but a Mait Shanah to the Shanah of jubilee, then he shall chashab (reckon) with him; according to his Shanah of service he shall shawab (turn back / repent) back the price of his gaalah (redemption).
As a shakayar (servant) hired Shanah by year shall he be with him: he shall not radah (rule) with harshness over him in your iyan (sight).
If he isn't redeemed by these means, then he shall be released in the Shanah of Jubilee, he, and his children with him.
For to me the children of Yasharaal (Israel) are ibad (servants); they are my ibad (servants) whom I brought out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam. I am Yahawah your Alahayam.

"‘You shall ishah (make) for yourselves no idols, neither shall you qawam (raise) up an engraved pasal (image) or a matzabah (pillar), neither shall you nathan (place) any figured aban (stone) in your aratz (land), to shachah (bow) down to it: for I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
"‘You shall shamar (keep) my shabath (sabbaths), and have yaraa (reverence) for my maqadash (sanctuary). I am Yahawah.
"‘If you yalak (walk) in my chaqah (statutes), and shamar (keep) my matzawah (commandments), and do them;
then I will nathan (give) you your rains in their ith (season), and the aratz (land) shall nathan (yield) its increase, and the itz (trees) of the shadah (field) shall nathan (yield) their fruit.

Your threshing shall reach to the vintage, and the vintage shall reach to the zarai (sowing) time; and you shall akal (eat) your lacham (bread) to the full, and yashab (dwell) in your aratz (land) safely.

"‘I will nathan (give) shalawam (peace) in the aratz (land), and you shall shakab (lie) down, and no charad (one) will make you afraid; and I will remove rai (evil) animals out of the aratz (land), neither shall the charab (sword) ibar (go) through your aratz (land).
You shall chase your ayab (enemies), and they shall napal (fall) panayam (before) you by the charab (sword).

chamash (five) of you shall chase a maah (hundred), and a maah (hundred) of you shall chase rababah (ten) thousand; and your ayab (enemies) shall napal (fall) panayam (before) you by the charab (sword).
"‘I will have panah (respect) for you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, and will qawam (establish) my barayath (covenant) with you.
You shall akal (eat) yashan (old) store long kept, and you shall move out the Yashan panayam (because) of the Chadash.
I will nathan (set) my mashakan (tent) among you: and my napash (soul) won't abhor you.
I will halak (walk) among you, and will be your Alahayam, and you will be my im (people).

I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who brought you yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, that you should not be their ibad (slaves); and I have shabar (broken) the bars of your yoke, and yalak (made) you go qawamamayawath (upright).
"‘But if you will not listen to me, and will not do all these matzawah (commandments);

and if you shall reject my chaqah (statutes), and if your napash (soul) abhors my mashapat (ordinances), so that you will not do all my matzawah (commandments), but parar (break) my barayath (covenant);

I also will do this to you: I will paqad (appoint) terror over you, even consumption and fever, that shall kalah (consume) the iyan (eyes), and make the napash (soul) to pine away; and you will zarai (sow) your zarai (seed) in vain, for your ayab (enemies) will akal (eat) it.

I will nathan (set) my panayam (face) against you, and you will be struck panayam (before) your ayab (enemies). Those who shanaa (hate) you will radah (rule) over you; and you will flee when no radap (one) pursues you.
"‘If you in spite of these things will not listen to me, then I will chastise you shabai (seven) times more for your chataah (sins).
I will shabar (break) the pride of your iz (power), and I will nathan (make) your sky like barazal (iron), and your soil like brass;
and your kach (strength) will be thamam (spent) in vain; for your aratz (land) won't nathan (yield) its increase, neither will the itz (trees) of the aratz (land) nathan (yield) their fruit.
"‘If you yalak (walk) contrary to me, and won't listen to me, then I will bring shabai (seven) times more makah (plagues) on you according to your chataah (sins).

I will shalach (send) the shadah (wild) animals among you, which will shakal (rob) you of your children, karath (destroy) your livestock, and make you few in number; and your roads will become shamam (desolate).
"‘If by these things you won't be reformed to me, but will halak (walk) contrary to me;
then I will also halak (walk) contrary to you; and I will strike you, even I, shabai (seven) times for your chataah (sins).

I will bawaa (bring) a charab (sword) upon you, that will execute the vengeance of the barayath (covenant); and you will be gathered asap (together) within your Iyar: and I will shalach (send) the dabar (pestilence) among you; and you will be delivered into the yad (hand) of the ayab (enemy).

When I shabar (break) your matah (staff) of lacham (bread), ishar (ten) women shall bake your lacham (bread) in one oven, and they shall shawab (turn back / repent) your lacham (bread) again by weight: and you shall akal (eat), and not be satisfied.
"‘If you in spite of this won't listen to me, but halak (walk) contrary to me;
then I will halak (walk) contrary to you in chamah (wrath); and I also will chastise you shabai (seven) times for your chataah (sins).
You will akal (eat) the flesh of your ban (sons), and you will akal (eat) the flesh of your bath (daughters).

I will destroy your bamah (high) places, and karath (cut) down your incense altars, and nathan (cast) your pagar (dead) bodies upon the pagar (bodies) of your idols; and my napash (soul) will abhor you.
I will nathan (lay) your Iyar waste, and will shamam (bring) your maqadash (sanctuaries) to desolation, and I will not take delight in the sweet fragrance of your nayachawach (offerings).
I will shamam (bring) the aratz (land) into desolation; and your ayab (enemies) that yashab (dwell) therein will be astonished at it.
I will scatter you among the gawayam (nations), and I will draw out the charab (sword) achar (after) you: and your aratz (land) will be a desolation, and your Iyar shall be a waste.

Then the aratz (land) will enjoy its shabath (sabbaths) as yawam (long) as it lies shamam (desolate) and you are in your ayab (enemies)' aratz (land). Even then the aratz (land) will shabath (rest) and enjoy its shabath (sabbaths).
As yawam (long) as it lies shamam (desolate) it shall have shabath (rest), even the shabath (rest) which it didn't have in your shabath (sabbaths), when you lived on it.

"‘As for those of you who are shaar (left), I will bawaa (send) a faintness into their labab (hearts) in the aratz (lands) of their ayab (enemies): and the qawal (sound) of a driven leaf will put them to flight; and they shall flee, as nawas (one) flees from the charab (sword); and they will napal (fall) when no radap (one) pursues.

They will stumble over one ach (another), as it were panayam (before) the charab (sword), when no radap (one) pursues: and you will have no thaqawamah (power) to stand panayam (before) your ayab (enemies).
You will abad (perish) among the gawayam (nations), and the aratz (land) of your ayab (enemies) will akal (eat) you up.

Those of you who are shaar (left) will pine away in their iwan (iniquity) in your ayab (enemies)' aratz (lands); and also in the iwan (iniquities) of their abawath (fathers) shall they pine away with them.

"‘If they yadah (confess) their iwan (iniquity), and the iwan (iniquity) of their abawath (fathers), in their mail (trespass) which they trespassed against me, and also that, because they walked contrary to me,

I also walked contrary to them, and brought them into the aratz (land) of their ayab (enemies): if then their Iral labab (heart) is humbled, and they then accept the punishment of their iwan (iniquity);

then I will zakar (remember) my barayath (covenant) with Yaiqab; and also my barayath (covenant) with Yatzachaq, and also my barayath (covenant) with Abaraham; and I will zakar (remember) the aratz (land).

The aratz (land) also will be left by them, and will enjoy its shabath (sabbaths) while it lies shamam (desolate) without them: and they will accept the punishment of their iwan (iniquity); because, even because they rejected my mashapat (ordinances), and their napash (soul) abhorred my chaqah (statutes).

Yet for all that, when they are in the aratz (land) of their ayab (enemies), I will not reject them, neither will I abhor them, to kalah (destroy) them utterly, and to parar (break) my barayath (covenant) with them; for I am Yahawah their Alahayam;

but I will for their sake zakar (remember) the barayath (covenant) of their raashawan (ancestors), whom I brought out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam in the iyan (sight) of the gawayam (nations), that I might be their Alahayam. I am Yahawah.'
These are the chaq (statutes), mashapat (ordinances) and thawarah (laws), which Yahawah made between him and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) in har (mount) Sayanay by Mashah.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (say) to them, ‘When a ayash (man) palaa (makes) a nadar (vow), the napash (persons) shall be for Yahawah by your valuation.

Your valuation shall be of a zakar (male) from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) even to shashayam (sixty) Shanah ban (old), even your valuation shall be chamashayam (fifty) shekels of kasap (silver), after the shekel of the qadash (sanctuary).
If it is a female, then your valuation shall be shalawashayam (thirty) shekels.

If the person is from chamash (five) Shanah ban (old) even to isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old), then your valuation shall be for a zakar (male) isharayam (twenty) shekels, and for a female ishar (ten) shekels.

If the person is from a chadash (month) ban (old) even to chamash (five) Shanah ban (old), then your valuation shall be for a zakar (male) chamash (five) shekels of kasap (silver), and for a female your valuation shall be shalawash (three) shekels of kasap (silver).
If the person is from shashayam (sixty) Shanah ban (old) and upward; if it is a zakar (male), then your valuation shall be chamash (fifteen) shekels, and for a female ishar (ten) shekels.

But if he is poorer than your valuation, then he shall be imad (set) panayam (before) the kahan (priest), and the kahan (priest) shall value him; according to the ability of him who vowed shall the kahan (priest) value him.
"‘If it is an animal, of which men qarab (offer) an qaraban (offering) to Yahawah, all that any man nathan (gives) of such to Yahawah becomes qadash (holy).

He shall not alter it, nor change it, a tawab (good) for a rai (bad), or a rai (bad) for a tawab (good): and if he shall at all change animal for animal, then both it and that for which it is changed shall be qadash (holy).
If it is any tamaa (unclean) animal, of which they do not qarab (offer) as an qaraban (offering) to Yahawah, then he shall imad (set) the animal panayam (before) the kahan (priest);
and the kahan (priest) shall value it, whether it is tawab (good) or rai (bad). As you the kahan (priest) values it, so shall it be.
But if he will indeed gaal (redeem) it, then he shall add the chamayashay (fifth) part of it to its valuation.

"‘When a ayash (man) qadash (dedicates) his bayath (house) to be qadash (holy) to Yahawah, then the kahan (priest) shall evaluate it, whether it is tawab (good) or rai (bad): as the kahan (priest) shall evaluate it, so shall it qawam (stand).
If he who qadash (dedicates) it will gaal (redeem) his bayath (house), then he shall add the chamayashay (fifth) part of the kasap (money) of your valuation to it, and it shall be his.

"‘If a ayash (man) qadash (dedicates) to Yahawah part of the shadah (field) of his achazah (possession), then your valuation shall be according to the zarai (seed) for it: the zarai (sowing) of a homer of barley shall be valued at chamashayam (fifty) shekels of kasap (silver).
If he qadash (dedicates) his shadah (field) from the Shanah of Jubilee, according to your valuation it shall qawam (stand).

But if he qadash (dedicates) his shadah (field) achar (after) the Jubilee, then the kahan (priest) shall chashab (reckon) to him the kasap (money) according to the Shanah that yathar (remain) to the Shanah of Jubilee; and an abatement shall be made from your valuation.
If he who dedicated the shadah (field) will indeed gaal (redeem) it, then he shall add the chamayashay (fifth) part of the kasap (money) of your valuation to it, and it shall qawam (remain) his.
If he will not gaal (redeem) the shadah (field), or if he has sold the shadah (field) to achar (another) ayash (man), it shall not be redeemed any more;
but the shadah (field), when it goes out in the Jubilee, shall be qadash (holy) to Yahawah, as a shadah (field) charam (devoted); it shall be owned by the kahan (priests).
"‘If he qadash (dedicates) to Yahawah a shadah (field) which he has maqanah (bought), which is not of the shadah (field) of his achazah (possession),

then the kahan (priest) shall chashab (reckon) to him the worth of your valuation up to the Shanah of Jubilee; and he shall nathan (give) your valuation on that yawam (day), as a qadash (holy) thing to Yahawah.
In the Shanah of Jubilee the shadah (field) shall shawab (turn back / repent) to him from whom it was bought, even to him to whom the achazah (possession) of the aratz (land) belongs.
All your valuations shall be according to the shekel of the qadash (sanctuary): isharayam (twenty) gerahs to the shekel.
"‘Only the firstborn among animals, which is made a bakar (firstborn) to Yahawah, no ayash (man) may qadash (dedicate) it; whether an ox or sheep, it is yahawah (yahweh's).

If it is an tamaa (unclean) animal, then he shall buy it back according to your valuation, and shall add to it the chamayashay (fifth) gaal (part) of it: or if it isn't redeemed, then it shall be sold according to your valuation.

"‘Notwithstanding, no charam (devoted) thing, that a ayash (man) shall charam (devote) to Yahawah of all that he has, whether of adam (man) or animal, or of the shadah (field) of his achazah (possession), shall be sold or redeemed: every charam (devoted) thing is most qadash (holy) to Yahawah.
"‘No one charam (devoted), who shall be charam (devoted) from among men, shall be ransomed; he shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death).
"‘All the maishar (tithe) of the aratz (land), whether of the zarai (seed) of the aratz (land) or of the fruit of the itz (trees), is yahawah (yahweh's). It is qadash (holy) to Yahawah.
If a ayash (man) gaal (redeems) anything of his maishar (tithe), he shall add a chamayashay (fifth) part to it.
All the maishar (tithe) of the herds or the flocks, whatever passes under the shabat (rod), the ishayaray (tenth) shall be qadash (holy) to Yahawah.

He shall not search whether it is tawab (good) or rai (bad), neither shall he change it: and if he changes it at all, then both it and that for which it is changed shall be qadash (holy). It shall not be redeemed.'
These are the matzawah (commandments) which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah for the children of Yasharaal (Israel) on har (mount) Sayanay.

Yahawah spoke to Mashah in the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay, in the ahal (tent) of Meeting, on the achad (first) day of the shanay (second) chadash (month), in the shanay (second) Shanah yatzaa (after) they had come out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, saying,

"nashaa (take) a census of all the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), according to the number of the sham (names), every zakar (male), one by one;
from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, all who are yatzaa (able) to go out to tzabaa (war) in Yasharaal (Israel). You and Aharawan shall paqad (number) them by their divisions.
With you there shall be a ayash (man) of ayash (every) matah (tribe); everyone raash (head) of his abawath (fathers)' bayath (house).
These are the sham (names) of the men who shall imad (stand) with you: Of Raawaban: Alayatzawar the ban (son) of Shadayaawar.
Of Shamaiwan: Shalamayaal the ban (son) of Tzawarayashaday.
Of Yahawadah (Judah): Nachashawan the ban (son) of Imayanadab.
Of Yashashakar: Nathanaal the ban (son) of Tzawair.
Of Zabawalawan: Alayaab the ban (son) of Chalan.
Of the children of Yawasap: Of Aparayam: Alayashamai the ban (son) of Imayahawad. Of Manashah: Gamalayaal the ban (son) of Padahatzawar.
Of Banayamayan: Abayadan the ban (son) of Gadainay.
Dan Dan: Achayaizar the ban (son) of Imayashaday.
Of Ashar: Pagaiyaal the ban (son) of Ikaran.
Of Gad: Alayasap the ban (son) of Daiwaal.
Of Napathalay: Achayarai the ban (son) of Iyanan.

These are those who were called of the idah (congregation), the nashayaa (princes) of the matah (tribes) of their abawath (fathers); they were the raash (heads) of the alap (thousands) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Mashah and Aharawan took these men who are mentioned by sham (name).

They assembled all the idah (congregation) together on the achad (first) day of the shanay (second) chadash (month); and they declared their ancestry by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), according to the number of the sham (names), from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, one by one.
As Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah, so he numbered them in the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay.

The children of Raawaban, Yasharaal firstborn, their thawaladah (generations), by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), according to the number of the sham (names), one by one, every zakar (male) from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, all who were yatzaa (able) to go out to tzabaa (war);
those who were numbered of them, of the matah (tribe) of Raawaban, were arabaiyam (forty) - shash (six) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred).

Of the children of Shamaiwan, their thawaladah (generations), by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), those who were numbered of it, according to the number of the sham (names), one by one, every zakar (male) from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, all who were yatzaa (able) to go out to tzabaa (war);
those who were numbered of them, of the matah (tribe) of Shamaiwan, were chamashayam (fifty) - thashai (nine) alap (thousand) shalawash (three) maah (hundred).

Of the children of Gad, their thawaladah (generations), by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), according to the number of the sham (names), from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, all who were yatzaa (able) to go out to tzabaa (war);
those who were numbered of them, of the matah (tribe) of Gad, were arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) shash (six) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty).

Of the children of Yahawadah (Judah), their thawaladah (generations), by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), according to the number of the sham (names), from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, all who were yatzaa (able) to go out to tzabaa (war);
those who were numbered of them, of the matah (tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah), were shabaiyam (seventy) - arabai (four) alap (thousand) shash (six) maah (hundred).

Of the children of Yashashakar, their thawaladah (generations), by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), according to the number of the sham (names), from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, all who were yatzaa (able) to go out to tzabaa (war);
those who were numbered of them, of the matah (tribe) of Yashashakar, were chamashayam (fifty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred).

Of the children of Zabawalawan, their thawaladah (generations), by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), according to the number of the sham (names), from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, all who were yatzaa (able) to go out to tzabaa (war);
those who were numbered of them, of the matah (tribe) of Zabawalawan, were chamashayam (fifty) - shabai (seven) alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred).

Of the children of Yawasap, of the children of Aparayam, their thawaladah (generations), by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), according to the number of the sham (names), from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, all who were yatzaa (able) to go out to tzabaa (war);
those who were numbered of them, of the matah (tribe) of Aparayam, were arabaiyam (forty) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred).

Of the children of Manashah, their thawaladah (generations), by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), according to the number of the sham (names), from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, all who were yatzaa (able) to go out to tzabaa (war);
those who were numbered of them, of the matah (tribe) of Manashah, were shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) two maah (hundred).

Of the children of Banayamayan, their thawaladah (generations), by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), according to the number of the sham (names), from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, all who were yatzaa (able) to go out to tzabaa (war);
those who were numbered of them, of the matah (tribe) of Banayamayan, were shalawashayam (thirty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred).

Of the children Dan Dan, their thawaladah (generations), by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), according to the number of the sham (names), from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, all who were yatzaa (able) to go forth to tzabaa (war);
those who were numbered of them, of the matah (tribe) Dan Dan, were shashayam (sixty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred).

Of the children of Ashar, their thawaladah (generations), by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), according to the number of the sham (names), from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, all who were yatzaa (able) to go forth to tzabaa (war);
those who were numbered of them, of the matah (tribe) of Ashar, were arabaiyam (forty) - one alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred).

Of the children of Napathalay, their thawaladah (generations), by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), according to the number of the sham (names), from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, all who were yatzaa (able) to go forth to tzabaa (war);
those who were numbered of them, of the matah (tribe) of Napathalay, were chamashayam (fifty) - shalawash (three) alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred).

These are those who were numbered, whom Mashah and Aharawan numbered, and the nashayaa (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel), being ishar (twelve) men: they were ayash (each) one for his abawath (fathers)' bayath (house).

So all those who were numbered of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, all who were yatzaa (able) to go out to tzabaa (war) in Yasharaal (Israel);
even all those who were numbered were shash (six) maah (hundred) shalawash (three) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty).
Lawayay the Levites after the matah (tribe) of their abawath (fathers) were not numbered among them.
For Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"Only the matah (tribe) of Laway you shall not paqad (number), neither shall you nashaa (take) a census of them among the children of Yasharaal (Israel);

but paqad (appoint) the Lawayay (Levites) over the mashakan (tabernacle) of the idawath (testimony), and over all its furnishings, and over all that belongs to it. They shall nashaa (carry) the mashakan (tabernacle), and all its furnishings; and they shall take care of it, and shall chanah (encamp) around it.

When the mashakan (tabernacle) is to move, the Lawayay (Levites) shall yarad (take) it down; and when the mashakan (tabernacle) is to be set up, the Lawayay (Levites) shall qawam (set) it up. The stranger who Qarab near shall be put to mawath (death).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) shall pitch their chanah (tents), every ayash (man) by his own machanah (camp), and every ayash (man) by his own standard, according to their divisions.

Lawayay the Levites shall chanah (encamp) around the mashakan (tabernacle) of the idawath (testimony), that there may be no qatzap (wrath) on the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel): and the Lawayay (Levites) shall be responsible for the mashakan (tabernacle) of the idawath (testimony).
Thus the children of Yasharaal (Israel) did. According to all that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah, so they did.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah and to Aharawan, saying,

"The children of Yasharaal (Israel) shall chanah (encamp) every ayash (man) by his own standard, with the banners of their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses): at a distance from the ahal (tent) of Meeting shall they chanah (encamp) around it.

Those who chanah (encamp) on the qadam (east) side toward the sunrise shall be of the standard of the machanah (camp) of Yahawadah (Judah), according to their divisions: and the nashayaa (prince) of the children of Yahawadah (Judah) shall be Nachashawan the ban (son) of Imayanadab.
His division, and those who were numbered of them, were seventy-four alap (thousand) shash (six) maah (hundred).
Those who chanah (encamp) next to him shall be the matah (tribe) of Yashashakar: and the nashayaa (prince) of the children of Yashashakar shall be Nathanaal the ban (son) of Tzawair.
His division, and those who were numbered of it, were chamashayam (fifty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred).
The matah (tribe) of Zabawalawan: and the nashayaa (prince) of the children of Zabawalawan shall be Alayaab the ban (son) of Chalan.
His division, and those who were numbered of it, were chamashayam (fifty) - shabai (seven) alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred).

All who were numbered of the machanah (camp) of Yahawadah (Judah) were one maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty) - shash (six) alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred), according to their divisions. They shall nasai (set) out raashawan (first).

"On the thayaman (south) side shall be the standard of the machanah (camp) of Raawaban according to their divisions. The nashayaa (prince) of the children of Raawaban shall be Alayatzawar the ban (son) of Shadayaawar.
His division, and those who were numbered of it, were arabaiyam (forty) - shash (six) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred).
"Those who chanah (encamp) next to him shall be the matah (tribe) of Shamaiwan. The nashayaa (prince) of the children of Shamaiwan shall be Shalamayaal the ban (son) of Tzawarayashaday.
His division, and those who were numbered of them, were chamashayam (fifty) - thashai (nine) alap (thousand) shalawash (three) maah (hundred).
"The matah (tribe) of Gad: and the nashayaa (prince) of the children of Gad shall be Alayasap the ban (son) of Raiwaal.
His division, and those who were numbered of them, were arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) shash (six) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty).

"All who were numbered of the machanah (camp) of Raawaban were one maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) - one alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty), according to their tzabaa (armies). They shall nasai (set) out shanay (second).

"Then the ahal (tent) of Meeting shall nasai (set) out, with the machanah (camp) Lawayay the Levites in the midst of the machanah (camps). As they chanah (encamp), so shall they nasai (set) out, every ayash (man) in his place, by their standards.

"On the yam (west) side shall be the standard of the machanah (camp) of Aparayam according to their divisions: and the nashayaa (prince) of the children of Aparayam shall be Alayashamai the ban (son) of Imayahawad.
His division, and those who were numbered of them, were arabaiyam (forty) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred).
"Next to him shall be the matah (tribe) of Manashah: and the nashayaa (prince) of the children of Manashah shall be Gamalayaal the ban (son) of Padahatzawar.
His division, and those who were numbered of them, were shalawashayam (thirty) - two alap (thousand) shanayam (two) maah (hundred).
"The matah (tribe) of Banayamayan: and the nashayaa (prince) of the children of Banayamayan shall be Abayadan the ban (son) of Gadainay.
His tzabaa (army), and those who were numbered of them, were shalawashayam (thirty) - chamash (five) thirty-five alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred).

"All who were numbered of the machanah (camp) of Aparayam were one maah (hundred) shamanah (eight) alap (thousand) one maah (hundred), according to their divisions. They shall nasai (set) out shalayashay (third).

"On the tzapawan (north) side shall be the standard of the machanah (camp) Dan Dan according to their divisions: and the nashayaa (prince) of the children Dan Dan shall be Achayaizar the ban (son) of Imayashaday.
His division, and those who were numbered of them, were shashayam (sixty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred).
"Those who chanah (encamp) next to him shall be the matah (tribe) of Ashar: and the nashayaa (prince) of the children of Ashar shall be Pagaiyaal the ban (son) of Ikaran.
His division, and those who were numbered of them, were arabaiyam (forty) - one alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred).
"The matah (tribe) of Napathalay: and the nashayaa (prince) of the children of Napathalay shall be Achayarai the ban (son) of Iyanan.
His division, and those who were numbered of them, were chamashayam (fifty) - shalawash (three) alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred).

"All who were numbered of the machanah (camp) Dan Dan were one maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) - shabai (seven) alap (thousand) shash (six) maah (hundred). They shall nasai (set) out Acharawan by their standards.

These are those who were numbered of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses). All who were numbered of the machanah (camps) according to their tzabaa (armies) were shash (six) maah (hundred) shalawash (three) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty).
Lawayay the Levites were not numbered among the children of Yasharaal (Israel); as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.

Thus the children of Yasharaal (Israel) did. According to all that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah, so they encamped by their standards, and so they nasai (set) out, everyone by their mashapachah (families), according to their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses).
Now this is the history of the thawaladah (generations) of Aharawan and Mashah in the yawam (day) that Yahawah spoke with Mashah in har (mount) Sayanay.
These are the sham (names) of the ban (sons) of Aharawan: Nadab the firstborn, and Abayahawaa, Alaizar, and Ayathamar.
These are the sham (names) of the ban (sons) of Aharawan, the kahan (priests) who were mashach (anointed), whom he consecrated to kahan (minister) in the priest's office.

Nadab and Abayahawaa died panayam (before) Yahawah, when they offered zawar (strange) ash (fire) panayam (before) Yahawah, in the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay, and they had no children. Alaizar and Ayathamar ministered in the kahan (priest's) office in the panayam (presence) of Aharawan their ab (father).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"qarab (bring) the matah (tribe) of Laway qarab (near), and imad (set) them panayam (before) Aharawan the kahan (priest), that they may sharath (minister) to him.
They shall shamar (keep) his requirements, and the requirements of the whole idah (congregation) panayam (before) the ahal (tent) of Meeting, to do the ibadah (service) of the mashakan (tabernacle).
They shall shamar (keep) all the furnishings of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and the obligations of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), to do the ibadah (service) of the mashakan (tabernacle).
You shall nathan (give) the Lawayay (Levites) to Aharawan and to his ban (sons). They are wholly given to him on the behalf of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
You shall paqad (appoint) Aharawan and his ban (sons), and they shall shamar (keep) their kahanah (priesthood). The stranger who Qarab near shall be put to mawath (death).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"Behold, I have taken the Lawayay (Levites) from among the children of Yasharaal (Israel) instead of all the firstborn who open the womb among the children of Yasharaal (Israel); and the Lawayay (Levites) shall be mine:

for all the firstborn are mine. On the yawam (day) that I struck down all the firstborn in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam I made qadash (holy) to me all the firstborn in Yasharaal (Israel), both adam (man) and animal. They shall be mine. I am Yahawah.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah in the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay, saying,

"paqad (count) the children of Laway by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), by their mashapachah (families). You shall paqad (count) every zakar (male) from a chadash (month) ban (old) and upward.
Mashah numbered them according to the pah (word) of Yahawah, as he was tzawah (commanded).
These were the ban (sons) of Laway by their sham (names): Garashawan, and Qahath, and Mararay.
These are the sham (names) of the ban (sons) of Garashawan by their mashapachah (families): Labanay and Shamaiy.
The ban (sons) of Qahath by their mashapachah (families): Imaram, and Yatzahar, Chabarawan, and Izayaal.
The ban (sons) of Mararay by their mashapachah (families): Machalay and Mawashay. These are the mashapachah (families) Lawayay the Levites according to their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses).
Of Garashawan was the mashapachah (family) of the Labanay, and the mashapachah (family) Shamaiy the Shimeites: these are the mashapachah (families) of the garashanay (gershonites).

Those who were numbered of them, according to the number of all the zakar (males), from a chadash (month) ban (old) and upward, even those who were numbered of them were shabai (seven) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred).
The mashapachah (families) of the garashanay (gershonites) shall chanah (encamp) achar (behind) the mashakan (tabernacle) westward.
The nashayaa (prince) of the abawath (fathers)' bayath (house) of the garashanay (gershonites) shall be Alayasap the ban (son) of Laal.

The duty of the ban (sons) of Garashawan in the ahal (tent) of Meeting shall be the ahal (tabernacle), and the mashakan (tent), its ahal (covering), and the screen for the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting,
and the hangings of the court, and the screen for the door of the court, which is by the mashakan (tabernacle), and around the mazabach (altar), and its cords for all of its ibadah (service).

Of Qahath was the mashapachah (family) of the Imaramay, and the mashapachah (family) of the Yatzaharay, and the mashapachah (family) of the Chabarawanay, and the mashapachah (family) of the Izayaalay: these are the mashapachah (families) of the Qahathay (Kohathites).

According to the number of all the zakar (males), from a chadash (month) ban (old) and upward, there were shamanah (eight) alap (thousand) shash (six) maah (hundred), keeping the requirements of the qadash (sanctuary).
The mashapachah (families) of the ban (sons) of Qahath shall chanah (encamp) on the thayaman (south) side of the mashakan (tabernacle).
The nashayaa (prince) of the abawath (fathers)' bayath (house) of the mashapachah (families) of the Qahathay (Kohathites) shall be Alayatzapan the ban (son) of Izayaal.

Their duty shall be the arawan (ark), the table, the manawarah (lamp) stand, the mazabach (altars), the vessels of the qadash (sanctuary) with which they sharath (minister), and the screen, and all its ibadah (service).

Alaizar the ban (son) of Aharawan the kahan (priest) shall be nashayaa (prince) of the nashayaa (princes) Lawayay the Levites, with the oversight of those who shamar (keep) the requirements of the qadash (sanctuary).
Of Mararay was the mashapachah (family) of the Machalay, and the mashapachah (family) of the Mawashay. These are the mashapachah (families) of Mararay.
Those who were numbered of them, according to the number of all the zakar (males), from a chadash (month) ban (old) and upward, were shash (six) alap (thousand) two maah (hundred).

The nashayaa (prince) of the abawath (fathers)' bayath (house) of the mashapachah (families) of Mararay was Tzawarayaal the ban (son) of Abayahayal. They shall chanah (encamp) on the tzapawan (north) side of the mashakan (tabernacle).
The appointed duty of the ban (sons) of Mararay shall be the mashakan (tabernacle's) boards, its bars, its pillars, its sockets, all its instruments, all its ibadah (service),
the pillars of the court around it, their sockets, their pins, and their cords.

Those who chanah (encamp) panayam (before) the mashakan (tabernacle) eastward, in panayam (front) of the mashakan (tent) of Meeting toward the sunrise, shall be Mashah, and Aharawan and his ban (sons), keeping the requirements of the maqadash (sanctuary) for the duty of the children of Yasharaal (Israel). The stranger who Qarab near shall be put to mawath (death).
All who were numbered of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron numbered at the commandment of Yahweh, by their families, all the males from a month old and upward, were twenty - two thousand.

Yahawah said to Mashah, "paqad (number) all the firstborn zakar (males) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) from a chadash (month) ban (old) and upward, and nashaa (take) the number of their sham (names).

You shall take the Lawayay (Levites) for me (I am Yahawah) instead of all the firstborn among the children of Yasharaal (Israel); and the livestock Lawayay the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the livestock of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
Mashah numbered, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) him, all the firstborn among the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

All the firstborn zakar (males) according to the number of sham (names), from a chadash (month) ban (old) and upward, of those who were numbered of them, were isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) two maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) - three.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"Take the Lawayay (Levites) instead of all the firstborn among the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and the livestock Lawayay the Levites instead of their livestock; and the Lawayay (Levites) shall be mine. I am Yahawah.
For the padaway (redemption) of the two maah (hundred) seventy - three of the ban (firstborn) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), who exceed the number Lawayay the Levites,
you shall take chamash (five) shekels apiece for each one; after the shekel of the qadash (sanctuary) you shall take them (the shekel is isharayam (twenty) gerahs):
and you shall nathan (give) the kasap (money), with which their remainder is redeemed, to Aharawan and to his ban (sons).
Mashah took the padayawam (redemption) kasap (money) from those who exceeded the number of those who were redeemed Lawayay the Levites;

from the firstborn of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) he took the kasap (money), one alap (thousand) shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty) - chamash (five) shekels, after the shekel of the qadash (sanctuary):
and Mashah gave the padaway (redemption) kasap (money) to Aharawan and to his ban (sons), according to the pah (word) of Yahawah, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah and to Aharawan, saying,
"nashaa (take) a census of the ban (sons) of Qahath from among the ban (sons) of Laway, by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses),

from shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah ban (old) and upward even until chamashayam (fifty) Shanah ban (old), all who bawaa (enter) into the tzabaa (service), to do the malaakah (work) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
"This is the ibadah (service) of the ban (sons) of Qahath in the ahal (tent) of Meeting, the most qadash (holy) things.

When the machanah (camp) moves nasai (forward), Aharawan shall bawaa (go) in, and his ban (sons), and they shall yarad (take) down the parakath (veil) of the screen, and cover the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony) with it,
and shall nathan (put) a covering of sealskin on it, and shall spread over it a bagad (cloth) all of blue, and shall shawam (put) in its poles.

"On the table of show bread they shall spread a blue bagad (cloth), and nathan (put) on it the dishes, the kap (spoons), the bowls, and the cups with which to pour out; and the continual lacham (bread) shall be on it.
They shall spread on them a scarlet bagad (cloth), and cover the same with a covering of sealskin, and shall shawam (put) in its poles.

"They shall take a blue bagad (cloth), and cover the lampstand of the maawar (light), and its nayar (lamps), and its snuffers, and its snuff dishes, and all its shaman (oil) vessels, with which they sharath (minister) to it.
They shall nathan (put) it and all its vessels within a covering of sealskin, and shall nathan (put) it on the frame.
"On the golden mazabach (altar) they shall spread a blue bagad (cloth), and cover it with a covering of sealskin, and shall shawam (put) in its poles.

"They shall take all the vessels of sharath (ministry), with which they sharath (minister) in the qadash (sanctuary), and nathan (put) them in a blue bagad (cloth), and cover them with a covering of sealskin, and shall nathan (put) them on the frame.
"They shall take away the ashes from the mazabach (altar), and spread a purple bagad (cloth) on it.

They shall nathan (put) on it all its vessels, with which they sharath (minister) about it, the machathah (fire) pans, the flesh hooks, the shovels, and the basins; all the vessels of the mazabach (altar); and they shall spread on it a covering of sealskin, and shawam (put) in its poles.

"When Aharawan and his ban (sons) have finished covering the qadash (sanctuary), and all the furniture of the qadash (sanctuary), as the machanah (camp) moves nasai (forward); achar (after) that, the ban (sons) of Qahath shall bawaa (come) to nashaa (carry) it: but they shall not nagai (touch) the qadash (sanctuary), lest they mawath (die). These things are the mashaa (burden) of the ban (sons) of Qahath in the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
