"The duty of Alaizar the ban (son) of Aharawan the kahan (priest) shall be the shaman (oil) for the maawar (light), the sweet incense, the continual meal manachah (offering), and the mashachah (anointing) shaman (oil), the requirements of all the mashakan (tabernacle), and of all that is in it, the qadash (sanctuary), and its furnishings.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah and to Aharawan, saying,
"Don't karath (cut) off the shabat (tribe) of the mashapachah (families) of the Qahathay (Kohathites) from among the Lawayay (Levites);

but thus do to them, that they may chayah (live), and not mawath (die), when they approach to the most qadash (holy) things: Aharawan and his ban (sons) shall bawaa (go) in, and shawam (appoint) them everyone to his ibadah (service) and to his mashaa (burden);
but they shall not bawaa (go) in to raah (see) the qadash (sanctuary) even for a moment, lest they mawath (die).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"nashaa (take) a census of the ban (sons) of Garashawan also, by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), by their mashapachah (families);

you shall paqad (count) them from shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah ban (old) and upward until chamashayam (fifty) Shanah ban (old); all who bawaa (enter) in to wait on the tzabaa (service), to do the ibadah (work) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
"This is the ibadah (service) of the mashapachah (families) of the garashanay (gershonites), in serving and in bearing mashaa (burdens):

they shall nashaa (carry) the curtains of the mashakan (tabernacle), and the mashakan (tent) of Meeting, its covering, and the covering of sealskin that is above on it, and the screen for the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting,

and the hangings of the court, and the screen for the door of the gate of the court, which is by the mashakan (tabernacle) and around the mazabach (altar), and their cords, and all the instruments of their ibadah (service), and whatever shall be done with them. Therein shall they ibad (serve).

At the commandment of Aharawan and his ban (sons) shall be all the ibadah (service) of the ban (sons) of the garashanay (gershonites), in all their mashaa (burden), and in all their ibadah (service); and you shall paqad (appoint) their duty to them in all their responsibilities.

This is the ibadah (service) of the mashapachah (families) of the ban (sons) of the garashanay (gershonites) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and their duty shall be under the yad (hand) of Ayathamar the ban (son) of Aharawan the kahan (priest).
"As for the ban (sons) of Mararay, you shall paqad (number) them by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses);

you shall paqad (count) them from shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah ban (old) and upward even to chamashayam (fifty) Shanah ban (old), everyone who bawaa (enters) on the tzabaa (service), to do the ibadah (work) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
This is the duty of their mashaa (burden), according to all their ibadah (service) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting: the ahal (tabernacle's) boards, its bars, its pillars, its sockets,

and the pillars of the court around it, and their sockets, and their pins, and their cords, with all their instruments, and with all their ibadah (service): and by sham (name) you shall paqad (appoint) the instruments of the duty of their mashaa (burden).

This is the ibadah (service) of the mashapachah (families) of the ban (sons) of Mararay, according to all their ibadah (service), in the ahal (tent) of Meeting, under the yad (hand) of Ayathamar the ban (son) of Aharawan the kahan (priest).

Mashah and Aharawan and the nashayaa (princes) of the idah (congregation) numbered the ban (sons) of the Qahathay (Kohathites) by their mashapachah (families), and by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses),
from shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah ban (old) and upward even to chamashayam (fifty) Shanah ban (old), everyone who entered into the tzabaa (service), for ibadah (work) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
Those who were numbered of them by their mashapachah (families) were two alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty).

These are those who were numbered of the mashapachah (families) of the Qahathay (Kohathites), all who served in the ahal (tent) of Meeting, whom Mashah and Aharawan numbered according to the commandment of Yahawah by Mashah.
Those who were numbered of the ban (sons) of Garashawan, their mashapachah (families), and by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses),
from shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah ban (old) and upward even to chamashayam (fifty) Shanah ban (old), everyone who entered into the tzabaa (service), for ibadah (work) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting,
even those who were numbered of them, by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), were two alap (thousand) shash (six) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty).

These are those who were numbered of the mashapachah (families) of the ban (sons) of Garashawan, all who served in the ahal (tent) of Meeting, whom Mashah and Aharawan numbered according to the commandment of Yahawah.
Those who were numbered of the mashapachah (families) of the ban (sons) of Mararay, by their mashapachah (families), by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses),
from shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah ban (old) and upward even to chamashayam (fifty) Shanah ban (old), everyone who entered into the tzabaa (service), for ibadah (work) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting,
even those who were numbered of them by their mashapachah (families), were shalawash (three) alap (thousand) two maah (hundred).
These are those who were numbered of the mashapachah (families) of the ban (sons) of Mararay, whom Mashah and Aharawan numbered according to the commandment of Yahawah by Mashah.

All those who were numbered Lawayay the Levites, whom Mashah and Aharawan and the nashayaa (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel) numbered, by their mashapachah (families), and by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses),

from shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah ban (old) and upward even to chamashayam (fifty) Shanah ban (old), everyone who entered in to do the ibadah (work) of ibadah (service), and the work of bearing mashaa (burdens) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting,
even those who were numbered of them, were shamanah (eight) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty).

According to the commandment of Yahawah they were numbered by Mashah, everyone according to his ibadah (service), and according to his mashaa (burden). Thus were they numbered by him, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"tzawah (command) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) that they shalach (put) out of the machanah (camp) every leper, and everyone who has an issue, and whoever is tamaa (unclean) by the napash (dead).
Both you shall shalach (put) zakar (male) and female outside of the machanah (camp); that they not tamaa (defile) their machanah (camp), in the midst of which I shakan (dwell).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) did so, and shalach (put) them out outside of the machanah (camp); as Yahawah spoke to Mashah, so did the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel): ‘When a ayash (man) or ashah (woman) ishah (commits) any chataah (sin) that men ishah (commit), so as to mail (trespass) against Yahawah, and that napash (soul) is asham (guilty);

then he shall yadah (confess) his chataah (sin) which he has done, and he shall shawab (turn back / repent) restitution for his guilt in full, and add to it the chamayashay (fifth) part of it, and nathan (give) it to him in respect of whom he has been asham (guilty).

But if the ayash (man) has no gaal (kinsman) to whom restitution may be made for the guilt, the restitution for guilt which is made to Yahawah shall be the kahan (priest's); besides the ayal (ram) of the kapar (atonement), by which kapar (atonement) shall be made for him.
Every heave tharawamah (offering) of all the qadash (holy) things of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), which they qarab (present) to the kahan (priest), shall be his.
Every ayash (man's) qadash (holy) things shall be his: whatever any ayash (man) nathan (gives) the kahan (priest), it shall be his.'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them: ‘If any ayash (man's) ashah (wife) goes astray, and is unfaithful to him,

and a ayash (man) lies with her shakabah (carnally), and it is hidden from the iyan (eyes) of her ayash (husband), and is kept close, and she is defiled, and there is no witness against her, and she isn't taken in the act;

and the rawach (spirit) of jealousy ibar (comes) on him, and he is jealous of his ashah (wife), and she is defiled: or if the rawach (spirit) of jealousy ibar (comes) on him, and he is jealous of his ashah (wife), and she isn't defiled:

then the ayash (man) shall bawaa (bring) his ashah (wife) to the kahan (priest), and shall bawaa (bring) her qaraban (offering) for her: the ishayaray (tenth) part of an ephah of barley meal. He shall pour no shaman (oil) on it, nor nathan (put) frankincense on it, for it is a meal manachah (offering) of jealousy, a meal manachah (offering) of zakarawan (memorial), bringing iwan (iniquity) to memory.
The kahan (priest) shall qarab (bring) her near, and imad (set) her panayam (before) Yahawah;

and the kahan (priest) shall take qadawash (holy) mayam (water) in an charash (earthen) vessel; and of the ipar (dust) that is on the floor of the mashakan (tabernacle) the kahan (priest) shall take, and nathan (put) it into the mayam (water).

The kahan (priest) shall imad (set) the ashah (woman) panayam (before) Yahawah, and let the hair of the ashah (woman's) raash (head) parai (go) loose, and nathan (put) the meal manachah (offering) of zakarawan (memorial) in her kap (hands), which is the meal manachah (offering) of jealousy. The kahan (priest) shall have in his yad (hand) the mayam (water) Mar bitterness that brings a arar (curse).

The kahan (priest) shall cause her to shabai (swear), and shall amar (tell) the ashah (woman), "If no ayash (man) has lain with you, and if you haven't gone shatah (aside) to tamaah (uncleanness), being under your ayash (husband), be free from this mayam (water) Mar bitterness that brings a arar (curse).
But if you have gone astray, being under your ayash (husband), and if you are defiled, and some ayash (man) has lain with you balaiday (besides) your ayash (husband):

then the kahan (priest) shall shabai (cause) the ashah (woman) to swear with the shabawaih (oath) of alah (cursing), and the kahan (priest) shall amar (tell) the ashah (woman), "Yahawah nathan (make) you a alah (curse) and an shabawaih (oath) among your im (people), when Yahawah allows your thigh to napal (fall) away, and your body to Tzabah;

and this mayam (water) that brings a arar (curse) will bawaa (go) into your maih (bowels), and make your body swell, and your thigh napal (fall) away." The ashah (woman) shall amar (say), "aman (amen), aman (amen).
"‘The kahan (priest) shall kathab (write) these alah (curses) in a book, and he shall machah (blot) them out into the mayam (water) Mar bitterness.

He shall make the ashah (woman) shaqah (drink) the mayam (water) Mar bitterness that causes the arar (curse); and the mayam (water) that causes the arar (curse) shall bawaa (enter) into her and become Mar.

The kahan (priest) shall take the meal manachah (offering) of jealousy out of the ashah (woman's) yad (hand), and shall wave the meal manachah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah, and qarab (bring) it to the mazabach (altar).

The kahan (priest) shall take a handful of the meal manachah (offering), as its azakarah (memorial), and qatar (burn) it on the mazabach (altar), and afterward shall make the ashah (woman) shaqah (drink) the mayam (water).

When he has made her shaqah (drink) the mayam (water), then it shall happen, if she is defiled, and has committed a mail (trespass) against her ayash (husband), that the mayam (water) that causes the arar (curse) will bawaa (enter) into her and become Mar, and her body will swell, and her thigh will napal (fall) away: and the ashah (woman) will be a alah (curse) qarab (among) her im (people).
If the ashah (woman) isn't defiled, but is tahawar (clean); then she shall be free, and shall zarai (conceive) zarai (seed).
"‘This is the thawarah (law) of jealousy, when a ashah (wife), being under her ayash (husband), goes astray, and is defiled;

or when the rawach (spirit) of jealousy ibar (comes) on a ayash (man), and he is jealous of his ashah (wife); then he shall imad (set) the ashah (woman) panayam (before) Yahawah, and the kahan (priest) shall ishah (execute) on her all this thawarah (law).
The ayash (man) shall be free from iwan (iniquity), and that ashah (woman) shall nashaa (bear) her iwan (iniquity).'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them: ‘When either ayash (man) or ashah (woman) shall palaa (make) a special nadar (vow), the nadar (vow) of a Nazirite, to nazar (separate) himself to Yahawah,

he shall nazar (separate) himself from yayan (wine) and shakar (strong) drink. He shall drink no vinegar of yayan (wine), or vinegar of fermented shakar (drink), neither shall he drink any juice of inab (grapes), nor akal (eat) Lach inab (grapes) or Yabash.
All the yawam (days) of his nazar (separation) he shall akal (eat) nothing that is made of the grapevine, from the charatzan (seeds) even to the skins.

"‘All the yawam (days) of his nadar (vow) of nazar (separation) no razor shall ibar (come) on his raash (head), until the yawam (days) are fulfilled, in which he nazar (separates) himself to Yahawah. He shall be qadawash (holy). He shall let the locks of the hair of his raash (head) grow long.
"‘All the yawam (days) that he nazar (separates) himself to Yahawah he shall not bawaa (go) near a mawath (dead) napash (body).

He shall not make himself tamaa (unclean) for his ab (father), or for his am (mother), for his ach (brother), or for his achawath (sister), when they mawath (die); because his nazar (separation) to Alahayam is on his raash (head).
All the yawam (days) of his nazar (separation) he is qadawash (holy) to Yahawah.

"‘If any mawath (man) dies very suddenly beside him, and he defiles the raash (head) of his nazar (separation); then he shall shave his raash (head) in the yawam (day) of his cleansing. On the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) he shall shave it.
On the eighth yawam (day) he shall bawaa (bring) shanayam (two) turtledoves or shanayam (two) ban (young) pigeons to the kahan (priest), to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

The kahan (priest) shall ishah (offer) one for a chataah (sin) offering, and the other for a burnt ilah (offering), and make kapar (atonement) for him, because he sinned by reason of the napash (dead), and shall make his raash (head) qadash (holy) that same yawam (day).

He shall nazar (separate) to Yahawah the yawam (days) of his nazar (separation), and shall bawaa (bring) a male lamb a Shanah old for a asham (trespass) offering; but the raashawan (former) yawam (days) shall be void, because his nazar (separation) was defiled.
"‘This is the thawarah (law) of the Nazirite: when the yawam (days) of his nazar (separation) are fulfilled, he shall be brought to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting,

and he shall qarab (offer) his qaraban (offering) to Yahawah, one male lamb a Shanah old thamayam (without) blemish for a burnt ilah (offering), and one ewe lamb a Shanah old thamayam (without) blemish for a chataah (sin) offering, and one ayal (ram) thamayam (without) blemish for shalam (peace) offerings,

and a basket of unleavened matzah (bread), cakes of fine flour mixed with shaman (oil), and unleavened wafers mashach (anointed) with shaman (oil), and their meal manachah (offering), and their drink nasak (offerings).
The kahan (priest) shall qarab (present) them panayam (before) Yahawah, and shall qarab (offer) his chataah (sin) offering, and his burnt chataah (offering).

He shall ishah (offer) the ayal (ram) for a zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings to Yahawah, with the basket of unleavened matzah (bread). The kahan (priest) shall ishah (offer) also its meal manachah (offering), and its drink nasak (offering).

The Nazirite shall shave the raash (head) of his nazar (separation) at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and shall take the hair of the raash (head) of his nazar (separation), and nathan (put) it on the ash (fire) which is under the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings.

The kahan (priest) shall take the Bashal zarawai (shoulder) of the ayal (ram), and one unleavened cake out of the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and shall nathan (put) them on the kap (hands) of the Nazirite, achar (after) he has shaved the head of his nazar (separation);

and the kahan (priest) shall wave them for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah. This is qadash (holy) for the kahan (priest), together with the breast that is waved and the thigh that is tharawamah (offered). achar (after) that the Nazirite may drink yayan (wine).

"‘This is the thawarah (law) of the Nazirite who nadar (vows), and of his qaraban (offering) to Yahawah for his nazar (separation), yad (besides) that which he is able to get. According to his nadar (vow) which he nadar (vows), so he must do after the thawarah (law) of his nazar (separation).'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"dabar (speak) to Aharawan and to his ban (sons), saying, ‘This is how you shall barak (bless) the children of Yasharaal (Israel).' You shall amar (tell) them,
‘Yahawah barak (bless) you, and shamar (keep) you.
Yahawah make his panayam (face) to awar (shine) on you, and be gracious to you.
Yahawah nashaa (lift) up his panayam (face) toward you, and shawam (give) you shalawam (peace).'
"So they shall shawam (put) my sham (name) on the children of Yasharaal (Israel); and I will barak (bless) them.

It happened on the yawam (day) that Mashah had finished setting up the mashakan (tabernacle), and had mashach (anointed) it and sanctified it, with all its furniture, and the mazabach (altar) with all its vessels, and had mashach (anointed) and sanctified them;

that the nashayaa (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel), the raash (heads) of their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), offered. These were the nashayaa (princes) of the matah (tribes). These are they who were over those who were numbered:

and they brought their qaraban (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah, shash (six) covered wagons, and ishar (twelve) oxen; a wagon for every shanayam (two) of the nashayaa (princes), and for achad (each) one an ox: and they presented them panayam (before) the mashakan (tabernacle).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"Accept these from them, that they may be used in doing the ibadah (service) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting; and you shall nathan (give) them Lawayay the Levites, to every ayash (man) according to his ibadah (service).
Mashah took the wagons and the oxen, and gave them Lawayay the Levites.
He gave shanayam (two) wagons and arabai (four) oxen to the ban (sons) of Garashawan, according to their ibadah (service):

and he gave arabai (four) wagons and shamanah (eight) oxen to the ban (sons) of Mararay, according to their ibadah (service), under the direction of Ayathamar the ban (son) of Aharawan the kahan (priest).
But to the ban (sons) of Qahath he gave laa (none), because the ibadah (service) of the qadash (sanctuary) belonged to them; they carried it on their shoulders.

The nashayaa (princes) gave offerings for the dedication of the mazabach (altar) in the yawam (day) that it was mashach (anointed), even the nashayaa (princes) gave their qaraban (offerings) panayam (before) the mazabach (altar).
Yahawah said to Mashah, "They shall qarab (offer) their qaraban (offering), achad (each) nashayaa (prince) on his yawam (day), for the dedication of the mazabach (altar).
He who offered his qaraban (offering) the raashawan (first) yawam (day) was Nachashawan the ban (son) of Imayanadab, of the matah (tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah),

and his qaraban (offering) was: one kasap (silver) platter, the weight of which was one maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) shekels, one kasap (silver) mazaraq (bowl) of shabaiyam (seventy) shekels, after the shekel of the qadash (sanctuary); shanayam (both) of them Malaa of fine flour mixed with shaman (oil) for a meal manachah (offering);
one golden ladle of ishar (ten) shekels, Malaa of incense;
one young bull, one ayal (ram), one male lamb a Shanah old, for a burnt ilah (offering);
one Shaiyar Shaiyar for a chataah (sin) offering;

and for the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings, shanayam (two) baqar (head) of cattle, chamash (five) ayal (rams), chamash (five) male goats, and chamash (five) male lambs a Shanah old. This was the qaraban (offering) of Nachashawan the ban (son) of Imayanadab.
On the shanay (second) yawam (day) Nathanaal the ban (son) of Tzawair, nashayaa (prince) of Yashashakar, gave his offering.

He offered for his qaraban (offering): one kasap (silver) platter, the weight of which was one maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) shekels, one kasap (silver) mazaraq (bowl) of shabaiyam (seventy) shekels, after the shekel of the qadash (sanctuary); shanayam (both) of them Malaa of fine flour mixed with shaman (oil) for a meal manachah (offering);

and for the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings, shanayam (two) baqar (head) of cattle, chamash (five) ayal (rams), chamash (five) male goats, chamash (five) male lambs a Shanah old. This was the qaraban (offering) Nathanaal Nethanel the ban (son) of Tzawair.

This was the dedication of the mazabach (altar), on the yawam (day) when it was mashach (anointed), by the nashayaa (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel): ishar (twelve) kasap (silver) platters, ishar (twelve) kasap (silver) mazaraq (bowls), ishar (twelve) golden ladles;

achad (each) kasap (silver) platter weighing one maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) shekels, and achad (each) mazaraq (bowl) shabaiyam (seventy); all the kasap (silver) of the vessels two alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred) shekels, after the shekel of the qadash (sanctuary);

the ishar (twelve) golden ladles, Malaa of incense, weighing ishar (ten) shekels apiece, after the shekel of the qadash (sanctuary); all the gold of the ladles weighed one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) shekels;

all the cattle for the burnt ilah (offering) shanayam (twelve) bulls, the ayal (rams) shanayam (twelve), the male lambs a Shanah old shanayam (twelve), and their meal manachah (offering); and the Shaiyar goats for a chataah (sin) offering shanayam (twelve);

and all the cattle for the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) bulls, the ayal (rams) shashayam (sixty), the male goats shashayam (sixty), the male lambs a Shanah old shashayam (sixty). This was the dedication of the mazabach (altar), achar (after) it was mashach (anointed).

When Mashah went into the ahal (tent) of Meeting to dabar (speak) with Yahawah, he heard his qawal (voice) speaking to him from above the kaparath (mercy) seat that was on the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony), from between the shanayam (two) karawab (cherubim): and he spoke to him.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"dabar (speak) to Aharawan, and amar (tell) him, ‘When you ilah (light) the nayar (lamps), the shabai (seven) nayar (lamps) shall give awar (light) in panayam (front) of the lampstand.'
Aharawan did so. He lit its nayar (lamps) to mawal (light) the area in front of the lampstand, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.

This was the workmanship of the lampstand, maqashah (beaten) maishah (work) of gold. From its base to its flowers, it was beaten maqashah (work): according to the pattern which Yahawah had shown Mashah, so he made the lampstand.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"Take the Lawayay (Levites) from among the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and tahar (cleanse) them.

You shall do this to them, to tahar (cleanse) them: sprinkle the mayam (water) of cleansing on them, let them shave their whole bodies with a razor, and let them wash their clothes, and tahar (cleanse) themselves.
Then let them take a ban (young) bull, and its meal manachah (offering), fine flour mixed with shaman (oil); and shanay (another) ban (young) bull you shall take for a chataah (sin) offering.
You shall qarab (present) the Lawayay (Levites) panayam (before) the ahal (tent) of Meeting. You shall assemble the whole mawaid (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
You shall qarab (present) the Lawayay (Levites) panayam (before) Yahawah. The children of Yasharaal (Israel) shall samak (lay) their yad (hands) Lawayay the Levites,

and Aharawan shall offer the Lawayay (Levites) panayam (before) Yahawah for a wave thanawapah (offering), on the behalf of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), that it may be theirs to do the ibadah (service) of Yahawah.

"The Lawayay (Levites) shall samak (lay) their yad (hands) on the raash (heads) of the bulls, and you shall ishah (offer) the one for a chataah (sin) offering, and the other for a burnt chataah (offering) to Yahawah, to make kapar (atonement) Lawayay the Levites.
You shall imad (set) the Lawayay (Levites) panayam (before) Aharawan, and panayam (before) his ban (sons), and offer them as a wave thanawapah (offering) to Yahawah.
Thus you shall separate the Lawayay (Levites) from among the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and the Lawayay (Levites) shall be mine.

"achar (after) that, the Lawayay (Levites) shall bawaa (go) in to do the ibad (service) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and you shall tahar (cleanse) them, and offer them as a wave thanawapah (offering).
For they are wholly given to me from among the children of Yasharaal (Israel); instead of all who open the womb, even the firstborn of all the children of Yasharaal (Israel), I have taken them to me.

For all the firstborn among the children of Yasharaal (Israel) are mine, both adam (man) and animal. On the yawam (day) that I struck all the firstborn in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, I sanctified them for myself.
I have taken the Lawayay (Levites) instead of all the firstborn among the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

I have given the Lawayay (Levites) as a gift to Aharawan and to his ban (sons) from among the children of Yasharaal (Israel), to do the ibadah (service) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and to make kapar (atonement) for the children of Yasharaal (Israel); that there be no nagap (plague) among the children of Yasharaal (Israel), when the children of Yasharaal (Israel) come near to the qadash (sanctuary).

Mashah, and Aharawan, and all the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) did so Lawayay the Levites. According to all that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah Lawayay the Levites, so the children of Yasharaal (Israel) did to them.

The Lawayay (Levites) purified themselves from kabas (sin), and they washed their clothes; and Aharawan offered them for a wave thanawapah (offering) panayam (before) Yahawah; and Aharawan made kapar (atonement) for them to tahar (cleanse) them.

achar (after) that, the Lawayay (Levites) went in to do their ibadah (service) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting panayam (before) Aharawan, and panayam (before) his ban (sons): as Yahawah had tzawah (commanded) Mashah Lawayay the Levites, so they did to them.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"This is that which Lawayay to the Levites: from isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) Shanah ban (old) and upward they shall bawaa (go) in to wait on the ibadah (service) in the work of the ahal (tent) of Meeting;
and from the ban (age) of chamashayam (fifty) Shanah they shall shawab (turn back / repent) tzabaa (waiting) on the ibadah (work), and shall ibad (serve) no more,

but shall sharath (minister) with their ach (brothers) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting, to perform the duty, and shall do no ibadah (service). You shall do Lawayay to the Levites concerning their duties.

Yahawah spoke to Mashah in the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay, in the raashawan (first) chadash (month) of the shanay (second) Shanah yatzaa (after) they had come out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, saying,
"Moreover let the children of Yasharaal (Israel) ishah (keep) the pasach (passover) in its mawaid (appointed) season.

On the fourteenth yawam (day) of this chadash (month), at evening, you shall ishah (keep) it in its mawaid (appointed) season—according to all its chaqah (statutes), and according to all its mashapat (ordinances), you shall ishah (keep) it.
Mashah spoke to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), that they should ishah (keep) the pasach (passover).

They kept the pasach (passover) in the raashawan (first) chadash (month), on the fourteenth yawam (day) of the month, at evening, in the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay. According to all that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah, so the children of Yasharaal (Israel) did.

There were anawash (certain) men, who were tamaa (unclean) because of the napash (dead) body of a adam (man), so that they could not ishah (keep) the pasach (passover) on that yawam (day), and they came panayam (before) Mashah and panayam (before) Aharawan on that yawam (day).

Those men said to him, "We are tamaa (unclean) because of the napash (dead) body of a adam (man). Why are we kept back, that we may not qarab (offer) the qaraban (offering) of Yahawah in its mawaid (appointed) season among the children of Yasharaal (Israel)?
Mashah answered them, "Wait, that I may hear what Yahawah will tzawah (command) concerning you.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (say) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘If any ayash (man) of you or of your dawar (generations) is tamaa (unclean) by reason of a napash (dead) body, or is on a darak (journey) Rachawaq away, he shall still ishah (keep) the pasach (passover) to Yahawah.
In the shanay (second) chadash (month), on the fourteenth yawam (day) at evening they shall ishah (keep) it; they shall akal (eat) it with unleavened matzah (bread) and bitter herbs.
They shall shaar (leave) none of it until the baqar (morning), nor shabar (break) a itzam (bone) of it. According to all the chaqah (statute) of the pasach (passover) they shall ishah (keep) it.

But the ayash (man) who is tahawar (clean), and is not on a darak (journey), and fails to ishah (keep) the pasach (passover), that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from his im (people). Because he didn't qarab (offer) the qaraban (offering) of Yahawah in its mawaid (appointed) season, that ayash (man) shall nashaa (bear) his chataa (sin).

"‘If a foreigner lives among you, and desires to ishah (keep) the pasach (passover) to Yahawah; according to the chaqah (statute) of the pasach (passover), and according to its chaqah (ordinance), so shall he do. You shall have one chaqah (statute), both for the foreigner, and for him who is born in the aratz (land).'

On the yawam (day) that the mashakan (tabernacle) was raised up, the cloud covered the mashakan (tabernacle), even the mashakan (tent) of the idawath (testimony): and at evening it was over the mashakan (tabernacle) as it were the appearance of ash (fire), until baqar (morning).
So it was continually. The cloud covered it, and the appearance of ash (fire) by layal (night).

Whenever the cloud was taken up from over the ahal (tent), then achar (after) that the children of Yasharaal (Israel) traveled; and in the place where the cloud remained, there the children of Yasharaal (Israel) encamped.

At the commandment of Yahawah, the children of Yasharaal (Israel) traveled, and at the commandment of Yahawah they encamped. As yawam (long) as the cloud remained on the mashakan (tabernacle) they remained encamped.
When the cloud stayed on the mashakan (tabernacle) many yawam (days), then the children of Yasharaal (Israel) kept yahawah (yahweh's) command, and didn't travel.

Sometimes the cloud was a few yawam (days) on the mashakan (tabernacle); then according to the commandment of Yahawah they remained encamped, and according to the commandment of Yahawah they traveled.

Sometimes the cloud was from evening until baqar (morning); and when the cloud was taken up in the baqar (morning), they traveled: or by yawamam (day) and by layal (night), when the cloud was taken up, they traveled.

Whether it was yawam (two) days, or a chadash (month), or a yawam (year) that the cloud stayed on the mashakan (tabernacle), remaining on it, the children of Yasharaal (Israel) remained encamped, and didn't travel; but when it was taken up, they traveled.
At the commandment of Yahawah they encamped, and at the commandment of Yahawah they traveled. They kept yahawah (yahweh's) command, at the commandment of Yahawah by Mashah.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"ishah (make) shanayam (two) trumpets of kasap (silver). You shall ishah (make) them of beaten maqashah (work). You shall use them for the maqaraa (calling) of the idah (congregation), and for the journeying of the machanah (camps).
When they blow them, all the idah (congregation) shall gather themselves to you at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
If they blow just one, then the nashayaa (princes), the raash (heads) of the alap (thousands) of Yasharaal (Israel), shall gather themselves to you.
When you blow an alarm, the machanah (camps) that chanah (lie) on the qadam (east) side shall nasai (go) forward.
When you blow an alarm the shanay (second) time, the machanah (camps) that chanah (lie) on the thayaman (south) side shall nasai (go) forward. They shall blow an alarm for their nasai (journeys).
But when the qahal (assembly) is to be gathered together, you shall blow, but you shall not rawai (sound) an alarm.
"The ban (sons) of Aharawan, the kahan (priests), shall blow the trumpets. This shall be to you for a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) throughout your dawar (generations).

When you bawaa (go) to war in your aratz (land) against the tzarar (adversary) who oppresses you, then you shall rawai (sound) an alarm with the trumpets. Then you will be zakar (remembered) panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam, and you will be saved from your ayab (enemies).

"Also in the yawam (day) of your gladness, and in your mawaid (set) feasts, and in the raash (beginnings) of your chadash (months), you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt ilah (offerings), and over the zabach (sacrifices) of your shalam (peace) offerings; and they shall be to you for a zakarawan (memorial) panayam (before) your Alahayam. I am Yahawah your Alahayam.

It happened in the shanay (second) Shanah, in the shanay (second) chadash (month), on the isharayam (twentieth) inan (day) of the month, that the cloud was taken up from over the mashakan (tabernacle) of the idawath (testimony).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) went nasai (forward) according to their journeys out of the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay; and the cloud stayed in the madabar (wilderness) of Paaran.
They raashawan (first) went nasai (forward) according to the commandment of Yahawah by Mashah.
raashawan (first), the standard of the machanah (camp) of the children of Yahawadah (Judah) went forward according to their tzabaa (armies). Nachashawan the ban (son) of Imayanadab was over his army.
Nathanaal the ban (son) of Tzawair was over the tzabaa (army) of the matah (tribe) of the children of Yashashakar.
Alayaab the ban (son) of Chalan was over the tzabaa (army) of the matah (tribe) of the children of Zabawalawan.
The mashakan (tabernacle) was taken down; and the ban (sons) of Garashawan and the ban (sons) of Mararay, who bore the mashakan (tabernacle), went nasai (forward).
The standard of the machanah (camp) of Raawaban went nasai (forward) according to their tzabaa (armies). Alayatzawar the ban (son) of Shadayaawar was over his tzabaa (army).
Shalamayaal the ban (son) of Tzawarayashaday was over the tzabaa (army) of the matah (tribe) of the children of Shamaiwan.
Alayasap the ban (son) of Daiwaal was over the tzabaa (army) of the matah (tribe) of the children of Gad.
The Qahathay (Kohathites) nasai (set) forward, bearing the maqadash (sanctuary). The others qawam (set) up the mashakan (tabernacle) before they arrived.
The standard of the machanah (camp) of the children of Aparayam nasai (set) forward according to their tzabaa (armies). Alayashamai the ban (son) of Imayahawad was over his tzabaa (army).
Gamalayaal the ban (son) of Padahatzawar was over the tzabaa (army) of the matah (tribe) of the children of Manashah.
Abayadan the ban (son) of Gadainay was over the tzabaa (army) of the matah (tribe) of the children of Banayamayan.

The standard of the machanah (camp) of the children Dan Dan, which was the rear guard of all the machanah (camps), nasai (set) forward according to their tzabaa (armies). Achayaizar the ban (son) of Imayashaday was over his tzabaa (army).
Pagaiyaal the ban (son) of Ikaran was over the tzabaa (army) of the matah (tribe) of the children of Ashar.
Achayarai the ban (son) of Iyanan was over the tzabaa (army) of the matah (tribe) of the children of Napathalay.
Thus were the travels of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) according to their tzabaa (armies); and they went nasai (forward).

Mashah said to Chabab, the ban (son) of Raiwaal the Madayanay (Midianite), Mashah' father-in-law, "We are journeying to the place of which Yahawah said, ‘I will nathan (give) it to you.' yalak (come) with us, and we will treat you tawab (well); for Yahawah has spoken tawab (good) concerning Yasharaal (Israel).
He said to him, "I will not yalak (go); but I will depart to my own aratz (land), and to my relatives.
He said, "Don't leave us, Kan; because you know how we are to chanah (encamp) in the madabar (wilderness), and you can be our iyan (eyes).
It shall be, if you yalak (go) with us, yes, it shall be, that whatever tawab (good) Yahawah does to us, we will do the same to you.

They nasai (set) forward from the har (mount) of Yahawah shalawash (three) yawam (days)' darak (journey). The arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah went panayam (before) them shalawash (three) yawam (days)' darak (journey), to seek out a resting place for them.
The cloud of Yahawah was over them by yawamam (day), when they nasai (set) forward from the machanah (camp).

It happened, when the arawan (ark) went nasai (forward), that Mashah said, "qawam (rise) up, Yahawah, and let your ayab (enemies) be scattered! Let those who shanaa (hate) you flee panayam (before) you!
When it rested, he said, "shawab (turn back / repent), Yahawah, to the rababah (ten) alap (thousands) of the thousands of Yasharaal (Israel).

The im (people) were complaining in the ears of Yahawah. When Yahawah heard it, his ap (anger) was kindled; and yahawah (yahweh's) ash (fire) burnt among them, and consumed some of the outskirts of the machanah (camp).
The im (people) cried to Mashah; and Mashah prayed to Yahawah, and the ash (fire) abated.
The sham (name) of that place was called Thabairah, because yahawah (yahweh's) ash (fire) burnt among them.
The mixed multitude that was qarab (among) them lusted exceedingly: and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) also wept again, and said, "Who will give us flesh to akal (eat)?
We zakar (remember) the fish, which we ate in Matzarayam for nothing; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic;
but now we have Yabash our appetite. There is balathay (nothing) at all except this manna to iyan (look) at.
The manna was like coriander zarai (seed), and its iyan (appearance) like the iyan (appearance) of bdellium.

The im (people) went around, gathered it, and tachan (ground) it in mills, or beat it in mortars, and boiled it in pots, and made cakes of it. Its taim (taste) was like the taim (taste) of fresh shaman (oil).
When the dew fell on the machanah (camp) in the layal (night), the manna fell on it.

Mashah heard the im (people) weeping throughout their mashapachah (families), every ayash (man) at the door of his ahal (tent); and the ap (anger) of Yahawah was kindled maad (greatly); and Mashah was displeased.

Mashah said to Yahawah, "Why have you treated with your ibad (servant) so badly? Why haven't I found favor in your iyan (sight), that you shawam (lay) the mashaa (burden) of all this im (people) on me?

Have I conceived all this im (people)? Have I brought them yalad (forth), that you should amar (tell) me, ‘nashaa (carry) them in your bosom, as a aman (nurse) nashaa (carries) a nursing infant, to the adamah (land) which you swore to their abawath (fathers)?'
Where could I get meat to nathan (give) to all this im (people)? For they weep to me, saying, ‘nathan (give) us meat, that we may akal (eat).'
I am not yakal (able) to nashaa (bear) all this im (people) bad (alone), because it is too Kabad for me.
If you treat me this way, please harag (kill) me right now, if I have found favor in your iyan (sight); and don't let me raah (see) my rai (wretchedness).

Yahawah said to Mashah, "asap (gather) to me shabaiyam (seventy) men of the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel), whom you yadai (know) to be the zaqan (elders) of the im (people), and shatar (officers) over them; and bring them to the ahal (tent) of Meeting, that they may stand there with you.

I will yarad (come) down and dabar (talk) with you there. I will take of the rawach (spirit) which is on you, and will shawam (put) it on them; and they shall nashaa (bear) the mashaa (burden) of the im (people) with you, that you not nashaa (bear) it yourself alone.

"amar (say) to the im (people), ‘qadash (sanctify) yourselves against tomorrow, and you will akal (eat) flesh; for you have wept in the ears of Yahawah, saying, "Who will give us flesh to akal (eat)? For it was tawab (well) with us in Matzarayam." Therefore Yahawah will nathan (give) you flesh, and you will akal (eat).
You will not akal (eat) one yawam (day), nor yawam (two) days, nor chamash (five) yawam (days), neither ishar (ten) yawam (days), nor isharayam (twenty) yawam (days),

but a whole chadash (month), until it yatzaa (come) out at your ap (nostrils), and it is loathsome to you; because that you have rejected Yahawah who is qarab (among) you, and have wept panayam (before) him, saying, "Why did we yatzaa (come) out of Matzarayam?"'

Mashah said, "The im (people), qarab (among) whom I am, are shash (six) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) men on foot; and you have said, ‘I will nathan (give) them flesh, that they may akal (eat) a yawam (whole) chadash (month).'
Shall flocks and herds be slaughtered for them, to be sufficient for them? Shall all the fish of the yam (sea) be gathered asap (together) for them, to be sufficient for them?
Yahawah said to Mashah, "Has yahawah (yahweh's) yad (hand) grown short? Now you will raah (see) whether my dabar (word) will qarah (happen) to you or not.
Mashah went out, and told the im (people) the dabar (words) of Yahawah; and he gathered shabaiyam (seventy) men of the zaqan (elders) of the im (people), and imad (set) them around the ahal (tent).

Yahawah came down in the cloud, and spoke to him, and took of the rawach (spirit) that was on him, and nathan (put) it on the shabaiyam (seventy) zaqan (elders): and it happened that when the rawach (spirit) rested on them, they prophesied, but they did so no more.

But shanayam (two) men remained in the machanah (camp). The sham (name) of one was Aladad, and the sham (name) of the other Mayadad: and the rawach (spirit) rested on them; and they were of those who were written, but had not gone out to the ahal (tent); and they prophesied in the machanah (camp).
A nair (young) man ran, and told Mashah, and said, "Aladad and Mayadad are nabaa (prophesying) in the machanah (camp)!
Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan, the sharath (servant) of Mashah, bacharawath (one) of his chosen men, answered, "My Adawan Mashah, forbid them!
Mashah said to him, "Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all yahawah (yahweh's) im (people) were nabayaa (prophets), that Yahawah would nathan (put) his rawach (spirit) on them!
Mashah went into the machanah (camp), he and the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel).

A rawach (wind) from Yahawah went out and brought quails from the yam (sea), and let them fall by the machanah (camp), about a yawam (day's) darak (journey) on this kah (side), and a yawam (day's) darak (journey) on the other kah (side), around the machanah (camp), and about two amah (cubits) above the surface of the aratz (earth).

The im (people) rose up all that yawam (day), and all the layal (night), and all the macharath (next) yawam (day), and gathered the quails. He who gathered least gathered ishar (ten) homers; and they spread them all abroad for themselves around the machanah (camp).

While the flesh was yet between their teeth, before it was karath (chewed), the ap (anger) of Yahawah was kindled against the im (people), and Yahawah struck the im (people) with a very rab (great) makah (plague).
The sham (name) of that place was called Qabarawathahathaawah Hattaavah, because there they buried the im (people) who lusted.
From Qabarawathahathaawah Hattaavah the im (people) traveled to Chatzarawath; and they stayed at Chatzarawath.
Marayam and Aharawan spoke against Mashah because of the Kawashayath (Cushite) ashah (woman) whom he had married; for he had married a Kawashayath (Cushite) ashah (woman).
They said, "Has Yahawah amar (indeed) spoken only with Mashah? Hasn't he spoken also with us?" And Yahawah heard it.
Now the ayash (man) Mashah was very Inaw, above all the men who were on the surface of the adamah (earth).
Yahawah spoke suddenly to Mashah, to Aharawan, and to Marayam, "You shalawash (three) yatzaa (come) out to the ahal (tent) of Meeting!" The shalawash (three) of them came out.
Yahawah came down in a pillar of cloud, and stood at the door of the ahal (tent), and called Aharawan and Marayam; and they shanayam (both) came forward.
He said, "Hear now my dabar (words). If there is a nabayaa (prophet) among you, I Yahawah will yadai (make) myself known to him in a vision. I will dabar (speak) with him in a chalawam (dream).
My ibad (servant) Mashah is not so. He is aman (faithful) in all my bayath (house).

With him I will dabar (speak) pah (mouth) to pah (mouth), even plainly, and not in riddles; and he shall see yahawah (yahweh's) form. Why then were you not yaraa (afraid) to dabar (speak) against my ibad (servant), against Mashah?
The ap (anger) of Yahawah was kindled against them; and he departed.
The cloud sawar (departed) from over the ahal (tent); and behold, Marayam was leprous, as white as snow. Aharawan looked at Marayam, and behold, she was leprous.
Aharawan said to Mashah, "Oh, my Adawan, please don't count this chataah (sin) against us, in which we have done foolishly, and in which we have sinned.
Let her not, I pray, be as one dead, of whom the flesh is chatzay (half) consumed when he yatzaa (comes) out of his am (mother's) womb.
Mashah cried to Yahawah, saying, "Heal her, Al, I beg you!

Yahawah said to Mashah, "If her ab (father) had but spit in her panayam (face), shouldn't she be kalam (ashamed) shabai (seven) yawam (days)? Let her be shut up outside of the machanah (camp) shabai (seven) yawam (days), and achar (after) that she shall be brought in again.
Marayam was shut up outside of the machanah (camp) shabai (seven) yawam (days), and the im (people) didn't travel until Marayam was brought in again.
Afterward the im (people) traveled from Chatzarawath, and encamped in the madabar (wilderness) of Paaran.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"shalach (send) men, that they may spy out the aratz (land) of Kanain, which I nathan (give) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel). Of ayash (every) matah (tribe) of their abawath (fathers), you shall shalach (send) a achad (man), every one a nashayaa (prince) among them.
Mashah sent them from the madabar (wilderness) of Paaran according to the commandment of Yahawah: all of them men who were raash (heads) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
These were their sham (names): Of the matah (tribe) of Raawaban, Shamawai the ban (son) of Zakawar.
Of the matah (tribe) of Shamaiwan, Shapat the ban (son) of Charay.
Of the matah (tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah), Kalab the ban (son) of Yapanah.
Of the matah (tribe) of Yashashakar, Yagaal the ban (son) of Yawasap.
Of the matah (tribe) of Aparayam, Hawashai the ban (son) of Nawan.
Of the matah (tribe) of Banayamayan, Palatay the ban (son) of Rapawaa.
Of the matah (tribe) of Zabawalawan, Gadayaal the ban (son) of Sawaday.
Of the matah (tribe) of Yawasap, of the matah (tribe) of Manashah, Gaday the ban (son) of Sawasay.
Of the matah (tribe) Dan Dan, Imayaal the ban (son) of Gamalay.
Of the matah (tribe) of Ashar, Sathawar the ban (son) of Mayakaal.
Of the matah (tribe) of Napathalay, Nachabay the ban (son) of Wapasay.
Of the matah (tribe) of Gad, Gaawaal the ban (son) of Makay.
These are the sham (names) of the men who Mashah sent to spy out the aratz (land). Mashah called Hawashai the ban (son) of Nawan Yahawashawai.
Mashah sent them to spy out the aratz (land) of Kanain, and said to them, "ilah (go) up this way by the Nagab, and ilah (go) up into the har (hill) country:
and raah (see) the aratz (land), what it is; and the im (people) who yashab (dwell) therein, whether they are chazaq (strong) or Rapah, whether they are Mait or many;
and what the aratz (land) is that they yashab (dwell) in, whether it is tawab (good) or rai (bad); and what Iyar they are that they yashab (dwell) in, whether in machanah (camps), or in strongholds;

and what the aratz (land) is, whether it is Shaman or Razah, whether there is itz (wood) therein, or not. Be courageous, and bring of the fruit of the aratz (land). yawam (now) the time was the yawam (time) of the first-ripe inab (grapes).
So they went up, and spied out the aratz (land) from the madabar (wilderness) of Tzan to Rachab, to the entrance of Chamath.

They went up by the Nagab, and came to Chabarawan; and Achayaman, Shashay, and Thalamay, the children of Inaq, were there. (Now Chabarawan was built shabai (seven) Shanah panayam (before) Tzain in Matzarayam.)

They came to the nachal (valley) of Ashakal, and karath (cut) down from there a branch with one cluster of inab (grapes), and they bore it on a mawat (staff) between shanayam (two). They also brought some of the pomegranates and figs.
That place was called the valley of Ashakal, because of the cluster which the children of Yasharaal (Israel) karath (cut) down from there.
They returned from spying out the aratz (land) at the end of arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days).

They went and came to Mashah, and to Aharawan, and to all the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), to the madabar (wilderness) of Paaran, to Qadash; and brought shawab (turn back / repent) dabar (word) to them, and to all the idah (congregation), and showed them the fruit of the aratz (land).
They told him, and said, "We came to the aratz (land) where you sent us; and surely it flows with milk and honey; and this is its fruit.
However the im (people) who yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land) are iz (strong), and the Iyar are fortified and very large. Moreover, we saw the children of Inaq there.

Imalaq yashab (dwells) in the aratz (land) of the Nagab: and the Chathay (Hittite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite), and the Amaray (Amorite), yashab (dwell) in the har (hill) country; and the Kanainay (Canaanite) yashab (dwells) by the yam (sea), and along by the yad (side) of the Yaradan.
Kalab stilled the im (people) before Mashah, and said, "Let us ilah (go) up at ilah (once), and yarash (possess) it; for we are well yakal (able) to yakal (overcome) it.
But the men who went up with him said, "We aren't yakal (able) to ilah (go) up against the im (people); for they are chazaq (stronger) than we.

They brought up an dabah (evil) report of the aratz (land) which they had spied out to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "The aratz (land), ibar (through) which we have gone to spy it out, is a aratz (land) that akal (eats) up its yashab (inhabitants); and all the im (people) who we saw in it are men of great stature.
There we saw the Nephilim, the ban (sons) of Inaq, who come of the Nephilim: and we were in our own iyan (sight) as grasshoppers, and so we were in their iyan (sight).
All the idah (congregation) lifted up their qawal (voice), and cried; and the im (people) wept that layal (night).

All the children of Yasharaal (Israel) murmured against Mashah and against Aharawan: and the whole idah (congregation) said to them, "Would that we had died in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam! or would that we had died in this madabar (wilderness)!

Why does Yahawah bawaa (bring) us to this aratz (land), to napal (fall) by the charab (sword)? Our wives and our little ones will be a prey: wouldn't it be tawab (better) for us to shawab (turn back / repent) into Matzarayam?
They said one to ach (another), "Let us nathan (make) a raash (captain), and let us shawab (turn back / repent) into Matzarayam.
Then Mashah and Aharawan napal (fell) on their panayam (faces) panayam (before) all the qahal (assembly) of the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan and Kalab the ban (son) of Yapanah, who were of those who spied out the aratz (land), tore their clothes:

and they spoke to all the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "The aratz (land), which we passed through to spy it out, is an maad (exceeding) tawab (good) aratz (land).
If Yahawah delights in us, then he will bawaa (bring) us into this aratz (land), and nathan (give) it to us; a aratz (land) which flows with milk and honey.

Only don't rebel against Yahawah, neither yaraa (fear) the im (people) of the aratz (land); for they are lacham (bread) for us: their defense is removed from over them, and Yahawah is with us. Don't yaraa (fear) them.

But all the idah (congregation) threatened to ragam (stone) them with ragam (stones). The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah raah (see) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting to all the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
Yahawah said to Mashah, "How long will this im (people) despise me? and how long will they not aman (believe) in me, for all the awath (signs) which I have worked qarab (among) them?
I will strike them with the dabar (pestilence), and yarash (disinherit) them, and will ishah (make) of you a gaway (nation) greater and mightier than they.
Mashah said to Yahawah, "Then the Matzarayam (Egyptians) will hear it; for you brought up this im (people) in your might from qarab (among) them;

and they will amar (tell) it to the yashab (inhabitants) of this aratz (land). They have heard that you Yahawah are in the qarab (midst) of this im (people); for you Yahawah are seen iyan (face) to iyan (face), and your cloud imad (stands) over them, and you halak (go) panayam (before) them, in a pillar of cloud by yawamam (day), and in a pillar of ash (fire) by layal (night).
Now if you killed this im (people) as one ayash (man), then the gawayam (nations) which have heard the fame of you will amar (speak), saying,
‘Because Yahawah was not yakal (able) to bawaa (bring) this im (people) into the aratz (land) which he swore to them, therefore he has slain them in the madabar (wilderness).'
Now please let the kach (power) of the Adanay be great, according as you have spoken, saying,

‘Yahawah is Arak to anger, and abundant in loving chasad (kindness), forgiving iwan (iniquity) and disobedience; and that will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iwan (iniquity) of the abawath (fathers) on the children, on the shalash (third) and on the rabai (fourth) generation.'

Please pardon the iwan (iniquity) of this im (people) according to the greatness of your loving chasad (kindness), and according as you have forgiven this im (people), from Matzarayam even until hanah (now).
Yahawah said, "I have pardoned according to your dabar (word):
but in very deed, as I chay (live), and as all the aratz (earth) shall be filled with the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah;

because all those men who have seen my kabawad (glory), and my awath (signs), which I worked in Matzarayam and in the madabar (wilderness), yet have tempted me these ishar (ten) paim (times), and have not listened to my qawal (voice);
am (surely) they shall not raah (see) the aratz (land) which I swore to their abawath (fathers), neither shall any of those who despised me raah (see) it:

but my ibad (servant) Kalab, because he had achar (another) rawach (spirit) with him, and has followed me fully, him will I bawaa (bring) into the aratz (land) into which he went; and his zarai (seed) shall yarash (possess) it.
Now the Imalaqay (Amalekite) and the Kanainay (Canaanite) yashab (dwell) in the valley: tomorrow panah (turn), and nasai (go) into the madabar (wilderness) by the darak (way) to the Red yam (sea).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah and to Aharawan, saying,

"How long shall I bear with this rai (evil) idah (congregation), that lawan (murmur) against me? I have heard the murmurings of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), which they lawan (murmur) against me.
amar (tell) them, ‘As I chay (live), amar (says) Yahawah, laa (surely) as you have spoken in my ears, so will I do to you:

your pagar (dead) bodies shall napal (fall) in this madabar (wilderness); and all who were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, who have murmured against me,

am (surely) you shall not bawaa (come) into the aratz (land), concerning which I swore that I would shakan (make) you dwell therein, except Kalab the ban (son) of Yapanah, and Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan.
But your little ones, that you said should be a prey, them will I bawaa (bring) in, and they shall yadai (know) the aratz (land) which you have rejected.
But as for you, your pagar (dead) bodies shall napal (fall) in this madabar (wilderness).

Your children shall be wanderers in the madabar (wilderness) arabaiyam (forty) Shanah, and shall nashaa (bear) your prostitution, until your pagar (dead) bodies be consumed in the madabar (wilderness).

After the number of the yawam (days) in which you spied out the aratz (land), even arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days), for every yawam (day) a yawam (year), you will nashaa (bear) your iwan (iniquities), even arabaiyam (forty) Shanah, and you will yadai (know) my alienation.'

I, Yahawah, have spoken, am (surely) this will I do to all this rai (evil) idah (congregation), who are gathered together against me: in this madabar (wilderness) they shall be consumed, and there they shall mawath (die).

The men, whom Mashah sent to spy out the aratz (land), who returned, and made all the idah (congregation) to lawan (murmur) against him, by bringing up an dabah (evil) report against the aratz (land),
even those men who brought up an rai (evil) dabah (report) of the aratz (land), died by the magapah (plague) panayam (before) Yahawah.
But Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan, and Kalab the ban (son) of Yapanah, remained chayah (alive) of those men who went to spy out the aratz (land).
Mashah told these dabar (words) to all the children of Yasharaal (Israel): and the im (people) mourned maad (greatly).

They rose up shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and went up to the raash (top) of the har (mountain), saying, "Behold, we are here, and will ilah (go) up to the place which Yahawah has promised: for we have sinned.
Mashah said, "Why now do you disobey the commandment of Yahawah, since it shall not tzalach (prosper)?
Don't ilah (go) up, for Yahawah isn't qarab (among) you; that you not be struck down panayam (before) your ayab (enemies).

For there the Imalaqay (Amalekite) and the Kanainay (Canaanite) are panayam (before) you, and you shall napal (fall) by the charab (sword): because you are turned achar (back) from following Yahawah, therefore Yahawah will not be with you.
But they presumed to ilah (go) up to the raash (top) of the har (mountain): nevertheless the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, and Mashah, didn't depart out of the machanah (camp).
Then the Imalaqay (Amalekite) came down, and the Kanainay (Canaanite) who lived in that har (mountain), and struck them and kathath (beat) them down, even to Charamah.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them, ‘When you have bawaa (come) into the aratz (land) of your habitations, which I nathan (give) to you,

and will ishah (make) an ashah (offering) by fire to Yahawah, a burnt ilah (offering), or a zabach (sacrifice), to palaa (accomplish) a nadar (vow), or as a freewill nadabah (offering), or in your mawaid (set) feasts, to ishah (make) a pleasant aroma to Yahawah, of the herd, or of the flock;

then he who qarab (offers) his qaraban (offering) shall qarab (offer) to Yahawah a meal manachah (offering) of a isharawan (tenth) part of an ephah of fine flour mixed with the rabayaiy (fourth) part of a hin of shaman (oil):
and yayan (wine) for the drink nasak (offering), the rabayaiy (fourth) part of a hin, you shall ishah (prepare) with the burnt nasak (offering), or for the zabach (sacrifice), for achad (each) lamb.

"‘Or for a ayal (ram), you shall ishah (prepare) for a meal manachah (offering) shanayam (two) isharawan (tenth) parts of an ephah of fine flour mixed with the shalayashay (third) part of a hin of shaman (oil):
and for the drink nasak (offering) you shall qarab (offer) the shalayashay (third) part of a hin of yayan (wine), of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.
When you ishah (prepare) a bull for a burnt ilah (offering), or for a zabach (sacrifice), to palaa (accomplish) a nadar (vow), or for shalam (peace) offerings to Yahawah;
then shall he qarab (offer) with the bull a meal manachah (offering) of shalawash (three) isharawan (tenth) parts of an ephah of fine flour mixed with chatzay (half) a hin of shaman (oil):
and you shall qarab (offer) for the drink nasak (offering) chatzay (half) a hin of yayan (wine), for an ashah (offering) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.
Thus shall it be done for achad (each) bull, or for achad (each) ayal (ram), or for each of the male lambs, or of the young goats.
According to the number that you shall ishah (prepare), so you shall do to everyone according to their number.
"‘All who are native-born shall do these things in this way, in offering an ashah (offering) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.

If a stranger lives as a foreigner with you, or whoever may be among you throughout your dawar (generations), and will ishah (offer) an ashah (offering) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah; as you do, so he shall do.

For the qahal (assembly), there shall be one chaqah (statute) for you, and for the stranger who lives as a foreigner, a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) throughout your dawar (generations): as you are, so shall the foreigner be panayam (before) Yahawah.
One thawarah (law) and one mashapat (ordinance) shall be for you, and for the stranger who lives as a foreigner with you.'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them, ‘When you bawaa (come) into the aratz (land) where I bawaa (bring) you,
then it shall be that when you akal (eat) of the lacham (bread) of the aratz (land), you shall offer up a wave tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah.
Of the raashayath (first) of your dough you shall offer up a cake for a wave tharawamah (offering): as the wave tharawamah (offering) of the threshing floor, so you shall heave it.
Of the raashayath (first) of your dough you shall nathan (give) to Yahawah a wave tharawamah (offering) throughout your dawar (generations).
"‘When you shall shagah (err), and not ishah (observe) all these matzawah (commandments), which Yahawah has spoken to Mashah,
even all that Yahawah has tzawah (commanded) you by Mashah, from the yawam (day) that Yahawah gave commandment, and onward throughout your dawar (generations);

then it shall be, if it be done unwittingly, without the iyan (knowledge) of the idah (congregation), that all the idah (congregation) shall ishah (offer) one ban (young) bull for a burnt ilah (offering), for a pleasant aroma to Yahawah, with the meal manachah (offering) of it, and the drink nasak (offering) of it, according to the mashapat (ordinance), and one Shaiyar Shaiyar for a chataah (sin) offering.

The kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for all the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and they shall be forgiven; for it was an error, and they have brought their qaraban (offering), an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah, and their chataah (sin) offering panayam (before) Yahawah, for their error:

and all the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shall be forgiven, and the stranger who lives as a foreigner among them; for in respect of all the im (people) it was done unwittingly.
"‘If one napash (person) chataa (sins) unwittingly, then he shall qarab (offer) a female goat a Shanah old for a chataah (sin) offering.

The kahan (priest) shall make kapar (atonement) for the napash (soul) who shagag (errs), when he chataa (sins) unwittingly, panayam (before) Yahawah, to make kapar (atonement) for him; and he shall be forgiven.
You shall have one thawarah (law) for him who does anything unwittingly, for him who is native-born among the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and for the stranger who lives as a foreigner among them.

"‘But the napash (soul) who does anything with a high rawam (hand), whether he is native-born or a foreigner, the same blasphemes Yahawah; and that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from qarab (among) his im (people).
Because he has despised the dabar (word) of Yahawah, and has broken his matzawah (commandment), that napash (soul) shall karath (utterly) be karath (cut) off; his iwan (iniquity) shall be on him.'
While the children of Yasharaal (Israel) were in the madabar (wilderness), they found a ayash (man) gathering itz (sticks) on the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day).
Those who found him gathering itz (sticks) brought him to Mashah and Aharawan, and to all the idah (congregation).
They yanach (put) him in custody, because it had not been declared what should be done to him.
Yahawah said to Mashah, "The ayash (man) shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death): all the idah (congregation) shall ragam (stone) him with ragam (stones) outside of the machanah (camp).
All the idah (congregation) brought him outside of the machanah (camp), and stoned him to mawath (death) with aban (stones); as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them that they should ishah (make) themselves fringes in the borders of their bagad (garments) throughout their dawar (generations), and that they nathan (put) on the fringe of each border a cord of blue:

and it shall be to you for a fringe, that you may raah (see) on it, and zakar (remember) all the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah, and do them; and that you not follow achar (after) your own labab (heart) and your own iyan (eyes), achar (after) which you use to play the prostitute;
that you may zakar (remember) and do all my matzawah (commandments), and be qadawash (holy) to your Alahayam.
I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who brought you out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, to be your Alahayam: I am Yahawah your Alahayam.

Now Qarach, the ban (son) of Yatzahar, the ban (son) of Qahath, the ban (son) of Laway, with Dathan and Abayaram, the ban (sons) of Alayaab, and Awan, the ban (son) of Palath, ban (sons) of Raawaban, took men:

and they rose up panayam (before) Mashah, with anawash (certain) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) nashayaa (princes) of the mawaid (congregation), Qarayaa to the idah (assembly), men of sham (renown);

and they assembled themselves together against Mashah and against Aharawan, and said to them, "You take rab (too) much on yourself, since all the idah (congregation) are qadawash (holy), everyone of them, and Yahawah is among them: why then nashaa (lift) yourselves up above the qahal (assembly) of Yahawah?
When Mashah heard it, he napal (fell) on his panayam (face):

and he spoke to Qarach and to all his idah (company), saying, "In the baqar (morning) Yahawah will show who are his, and who is qadawash (holy), and will cause him to qarab (come) near to him: even him whom he shall choose he will cause to qarab (come) near to him.
Do this: take censers, Qarach, and all his idah (company);

and nathan (put) ash (fire) in them, and shawam (put) incense on them panayam (before) Yahawah tomorrow: and it shall be that the ayash (man) whom Yahawah chooses, he shall be qadawash (holy). You have gone rab (too) far, you ban (sons) of Laway!
Mashah said to Qarach, "Hear now, you ban (sons) of Laway!

Is it a Mait thing to you, that the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) has separated you from the idah (congregation) of Yasharaal (Israel), to qarab (bring) you near to himself, to do the ibadah (service) of the mashakan (tabernacle) of Yahawah, and to imad (stand) panayam (before) the idah (congregation) to sharath (minister) to them;
and that he has brought you qarab (near), and all your ach (brothers) the ban (sons) of Laway with you? and do you seek the kahanah (priesthood) also?
Kan you and all your idah (company) are gathered together against Yahawah: and Aharawan, what is he that you lawan (murmur) against him?
Mashah sent to qaraa (call) Dathan and Abayaram, the ban (sons) of Alayaab; and they said, "We won't ilah (come) up:

is it a Mait thing that you have brought us up out of a aratz (land) flowing with milk and honey, to mawath (kill) us in the madabar (wilderness), but you must also sharar (make) yourself a sharar (prince) over us?

Moreover you haven't brought us into a aratz (land) flowing with milk and honey, nor given us nachalah (inheritance) of shadah (fields) and vineyards: will you put out the iyan (eyes) of these men? We won't ilah (come) up.
Mashah was very charah (angry), and said to Yahawah, "Don't panah (respect) their manachah (offering): I have not taken one donkey from them, neither have I raii (hurt) one of them.
Mashah said to Qarach, "You and all your idah (company) go panayam (before) Yahawah, you, and they, and Aharawan, tomorrow:

and each ayash (man) take his censer, and nathan (put) incense on them, and each ayash (man) qarab (bring) panayam (before) Yahawah his censer, two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) censers; you also, and Aharawan, ayash (each) his censer.
They ayash (each) took his censer, and nathan (put) ash (fire) in them, and laid incense thereon, and stood at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting with Mashah and Aharawan.
Qarach assembled all the idah (congregation) against them to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah raah (see) to all the idah (congregation).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah and to Aharawan, saying,
"Separate yourselves from among this idah (congregation), that I may kalah (consume) them in a moment!

They napal (fell) on their panayam (faces), and said, "Alahayam, the Al of the rawach (spirits) of all flesh, shall one ayash (man) chataa (sin), and will you be qatzap (angry) with all the idah (congregation)?
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"dabar (speak) to the idah (congregation), saying, ‘ilah (get) away from around the mashakan (tent) of Qarach, Dathan, and Abayaram!'
Mashah rose up and went to Dathan and Abayaram; and the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) followed him.

He spoke to the idah (congregation), saying, "sawar (depart), please, from the ahal (tents) of these rashai (wicked) men, and nagai (touch) nothing of theirs, lest you be consumed in all their chataah (sins)!

So they went away from the mashakan (tent) of Qarach, Dathan, and Abayaram, on every side: and Dathan and Abayaram came out, and stood at the door of their ahal (tents), and their wives, and their ban (sons), and their little ones.
Mashah said, "Hereby you shall yadai (know) that Yahawah has sent me to do all these maishah (works); for they are not from my own lab (mind).
If these men mawath (die) the common mawath (death) of all men, or if they be visited after the visitation of all men; then Yahawah hasn't sent me.

But if Yahawah baraa (make) a new thing, and the adamah (ground) open its pah (mouth), and balai (swallow) them up, with all that appertain to them, and they yarad (go) down chay (alive) into shaawal (sheol); then you shall yadai (understand) that these men have despised Yahawah.
It happened, as he made an kalah (end) of speaking all these dabar (words), that the adamah (ground) split apart that was under them;
and the aratz (earth) opened its pah (mouth), and swallowed them up, and their bayath (households), and all the men who appertained to Qarach, and all their rakawash (goods).
So they, and all that appertained to them, went down chay (alive) into shaawal (sheol): and the aratz (earth) closed on them, and they perished from among the qahal (assembly).
All Yasharaal (Israel) that were around them fled at their qawal (cry); for they said, "Lest the aratz (earth) balai (swallow) us up!
ash (fire) came yatzaa (forth) from Yahawah, and devoured the two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) men who offered the incense.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"amar (speak) to Alaizar the ban (son) of Aharawan the kahan (priest), that he take up the censers out of the burning, and scatter the ash (fire) yonder; for they are qadash (holy),

even the censers of these chataa (sinners) against their napash (own) lives; and let them be made beaten plates for a covering of the mazabach (altar): for they offered them panayam (before) Yahawah; therefore they are qadash (holy); and they shall be a awath (sign) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
Alaizar the kahan (priest) took the bronze censers, which those who were burnt had offered; and they beat them out for a covering of the mazabach (altar),

to be a zakarawan (memorial) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), to the end that no stranger, who isn't of the zarai (seed) of Aharawan, qarab (comes) near to qatar (burn) incense panayam (before) Yahawah; that he not be as Qarach, and as his idah (company): as Yahawah spoke to him by Mashah.

But on the next macharath (day) all the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) murmured against Mashah and against Aharawan, saying, "You have killed yahawah (yahweh's) im (people)!

It happened, when the idah (congregation) was assembled against Mashah and against Aharawan, that they looked toward the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and behold, the cloud covered it, and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah raah (see).
Mashah and Aharawan came to the front of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"Get away from among this idah (congregation), that I may kalah (consume) them in a moment!" They napal (fell) on their panayam (faces).

Mashah said to Aharawan, "Take your censer, and nathan (put) ash (fire) from off the mazabach (altar) in it, and shawam (lay) incense on it, and yalak (carry) it quickly to the idah (congregation), and make kapar (atonement) for them; for qatzap (wrath) has gone out from Yahawah! The nagap (plague) has begun.

Aharawan did as Mashah said, and ran into the midst of the qahal (assembly); and behold, the nagap (plague) has begun among the im (people): and he nathan (put) on the incense, and made kapar (atonement) for the im (people).
He stood between the mawath (dead) and the chay (living); and the magapah (plague) was stayed.
Now those who died by the magapah (plague) were fourteen alap (thousand) and shabai (seven) maah (hundred), besides those who died about the dabar (matter) of Qarach.
Aharawan returned to Mashah to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting: and the magapah (plague) was stayed.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and take of them matah (rods), one for each abawath (fathers)' bayath (house), of all their nashayaa (princes) according to their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), shanayam (twelve) matah (rods): kathab (write) every ayash (man's) sham (name) on his matah (rod).
You shall kathab (write) Aharawan sham (name) on the matah (rod) of Laway; for there shall be one matah (rod) for each raash (head) of their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses).
You shall yanach (lay) them up in the ahal (tent) of Meeting panayam (before) the idawath (testimony), where I meet with you.

It shall happen, that the matah (rod) of the ayash (man) whom I shall choose shall bud: and I will make to cease from me the murmurings of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), which they lawan (murmur) against you.

Mashah spoke to the children of Yasharaal (Israel); and all their nashayaa (princes) gave him matah (rods), for each nashayaa (prince) one, according to their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), even ishar (twelve) matah (rods): and the matah (rod) of Aharawan was among their matah (rods).
Mashah laid up the matah (rods) panayam (before) Yahawah in the ahal (tent) of the idawath (testimony).

It happened on the next macharath (day), that Mashah went into the ahal (tent) of the idawath (testimony); and behold, the matah (rod) of Aharawan for the bayath (house) of Laway was budded, and yatzaa (put) forth buds, and produced blossoms, and bore ripe almonds.
Mashah brought out all the matah (rods) from panayam (before) Yahawah to all the children of Yasharaal (Israel): and they looked, and took every ayash (man) his matah (rod).

Yahawah said to Mashah, "shawab (turn back / repent) shawab (turn back / repent) the matah (rod) of Aharawan panayam (before) the idawath (testimony), to be kept for a awath (token) against the children of rebellion; that you may kalah (make) an end of their murmurings against me, that they not mawath (die).
Mashah did so. As Yahawah tzawah (commanded) him, so he did.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) spoke to Mashah, saying, "Behold, we gawai (perish)! We are abad (undone)! We are all abad (undone)!
Everyone who Qarab near, who comes near to the mashakan (tabernacle) of Yahawah, dies! Will we all gawai (perish)?

Yahawah said to Aharawan, "You and your ban (sons) and your abawath (fathers)' bayath (house) with you shall nashaa (bear) the iwan (iniquity) of the maqadash (sanctuary); and you and your ban (sons) with you shall nashaa (bear) the iwan (iniquity) of your kahanah (priesthood).

Your ach (brothers) also, the matah (tribe) of Laway, the matah (tribe) of your ab (father), qarab (bring) near with you, that they may be joined to you, and sharath (minister) to you: but you and your ban (sons) with you shall be panayam (before) the ahal (tent) of the idawath (testimony).

They shall shamar (keep) your commands, and the duty of all the ahal (tent): only they shall not qarab (come) near to the vessels of the qadash (sanctuary) and to the mazabach (altar), that they not mawath (die), neither they, nor you.
They shall be joined to you, and shamar (keep) the responsibility of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, for all the ibadah (service) of the ahal (tent): and a stranger shall not qarab (come) near to you.
"You shall perform the duty of the qadash (sanctuary), and the duty of the mazabach (altar); that there be no more qatzap (wrath) on the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
