I, behold, I have taken your ach (brothers) the Lawayay (Levites) from among the children of Yasharaal (Israel): to you they are a mathanah (gift), given to Yahawah, to do the ibadah (service) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

You and your ban (sons) with you shall shamar (keep) your kahanah (priesthood) for everything of the mazabach (altar), and for that bayath (within) the parakath (veil); and you shall ibad (serve): I nathan (give) you the kahanah (priesthood) as a ibadah (service) of mathanah (gift): and the stranger who Qarab near shall be put to mawath (death).

Yahawah spoke to Aharawan, "I, behold, I have given you the command of my wave tharawamah (offerings), even all the qadash (holy) things of the children of Yasharaal (Israel); to you have I given them by reason of the mashachah (anointing), and to your ban (sons), as a chaq (portion) iwalam (forever).

This shall be yours of the most qadash (holy) things from the ash (fire): every qaraban (offering) of theirs, even every meal manachah (offering) of theirs, and every chataah (sin) offering of theirs, and every asham (trespass) offering of theirs, which they shall shawab (turn back / repent) to me, shall be most qadash (holy) for you and for your ban (sons).
You shall akal (eat) of it like the most qadash (holy) things. Every zakar (male) shall akal (eat) of it. It shall be qadash (holy) to you.

"This is yours, too: the wave tharawamah (offering) of their mathan (gift), even all the wave thanawapah (offerings) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel). I have given them to you, and to your ban (sons) and to your bath (daughters) with you, as a chaq (portion) iwalam (forever). Everyone who is tahawar (clean) in your bayath (house) shall akal (eat) of it.
"All the best of the yatzahar (oil), and all the best of the vintage, and of the grain, the raashayath (first) fruits of them which they nathan (give) to Yahawah, to you have I given them.
The first-ripe fruits of all that is in their aratz (land), which they bawaa (bring) to Yahawah, shall be yours; everyone who is tahawar (clean) in your bayath (house) shall akal (eat) of it.
"Everything charam (devoted) in Yasharaal (Israel) shall be yours.

Everything that opens the womb, of all flesh which they qarab (offer) to Yahawah, both of adam (man) and animal shall be yours: nevertheless you shall padah (surely) padah (redeem) the firstborn of adam (man), and you shall padah (redeem) the firstborn of tamaa (unclean) animals.

You shall padah (redeem) those who are to be padah (redeemed) of them from a chadash (month) ban (old), according to your irak (estimation), for chamash (five) shekels of kasap (money), after the shekel of the qadash (sanctuary) (the same is isharayam (twenty) gerahs).

"But you shall not padah (redeem) the firstborn of a cow, or the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat. They are qadash (holy). You shall sprinkle their dam (blood) on the mazabach (altar), and shall qatar (burn) their fat for an ashah (offering) made by fire, for a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.
Their flesh shall be yours, as the thanawapah (wave) chazah (offering) breast and as the yamayan (right) thigh, it shall be yours.

All the wave tharawamah (offerings) of the qadash (holy) things, which the children of Yasharaal (Israel) offer to Yahawah, have I given you, and your ban (sons) and your bath (daughters) with you, as a chaq (portion) iwalam (forever): it is a barayath (covenant) of Malach iwalam (forever) panayam (before) Yahawah to you and to your zarai (seed) with you.

Yahawah said to Aharawan, "You shall have no nachal (inheritance) in their aratz (land), neither shall you have any chalaq (portion) among them. I am your chalaq (portion) and your nachalah (inheritance) among the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

"To the children of Laway, behold, I have given all the tithe in Yasharaal (Israel) for an nachalah (inheritance), in chalap (return) for their ibadah (service) which they ibad (serve), even the ibadah (service) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
iwad (henceforth) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shall not qarab (come) near the ahal (tent) of Meeting, lest they nashaa (bear) chataa (sin), and mawath (die).

Lawayay the Levites shall do the ibadah (service) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and they shall nashaa (bear) their iwan (iniquity): it shall be a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever) throughout your dawar (generations); and among the children of Yasharaal (Israel) they shall have no nachalah (inheritance).

For the maishar (tithe) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), which they offer as a wave tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah, I have given Lawayay the Levites for an nachalah (inheritance): therefore I have said to them, ‘Among the children of Yasharaal (Israel) they shall have no nachalah (inheritance).'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"Moreover you shall dabar (speak) Lawayay the Levites, and amar (tell) them, ‘When you take of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) the maishar (tithe) which I have given you from them for your nachalah (inheritance), then you shall offer up a wave tharawamah (offering) of it for Yahawah, a maishar (tithe) of the maishar (tithe).
Your wave tharawamah (offering) shall be reckoned to you, as though it were the grain of the threshing Malaah, and as the fullness of the yaqab (winepress).

Thus you also shall offer a wave tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah of all your maishar (tithes), which you receive of the children of Yasharaal (Israel); and of it you shall nathan (give) yahawah (yahweh's) wave tharawamah (offering) to Aharawan the kahan (priest).
Out of all your mathanah (gifts) you shall offer every wave tharawamah (offering) of Yahawah, of all its best, even the maqadash (holy) part of it out of it.'

"Therefore you shall amar (tell) them, ‘When you heave its best from it, then it shall be reckoned Lawayay the Levites as the increase of the threshing floor, and as the increase of the yaqab (winepress).
You shall akal (eat) it in every place, you and your bayath (households): for it is your reward in chalap (return) for your ibadah (service) in the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

You shall nashaa (bear) no chataa (sin) by reason of it, when you have heaved from it its best: and you shall not chalal (profane) the qadash (holy) things of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), that you not mawath (die).'
Yahawah spoke to Mashah and to Aharawan, saying,

"This is the chaqah (statute) of the thawarah (law) which Yahawah has tzawah (commanded): dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), that they bring you a Adam heifer thamayam (without) spot, in which is no blemish, and which was laa (never) yoked.
You shall nathan (give) her to Alaizar the kahan (priest), and he shall yatzaa (bring) her forth outside of the machanah (camp), and shachat (one) shall kill her before his panayam (face):
and Alaizar the kahan (priest) shall take of her dam (blood) with his finger, and sprinkle her dam (blood) toward the panayam (front) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting shabai (seven) paim (times).
One shall sharap (burn) the heifer in his iyan (sight); her skin, and her flesh, and her dam (blood), with her dung, shall he sharap (burn):
and the kahan (priest) shall take cedar itz (wood), and hyssop, and scarlet, and cast it into the midst of the burning of the heifer.

Then the kahan (priest) shall wash his clothes, and he shall bathe his flesh in mayam (water), and afterward he shall bawaa (come) into the machanah (camp), and the kahan (priest) shall be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.
He who sharap (burns) her shall wash his clothes in mayam (water), and bathe his flesh in mayam (water), and shall be tamaa (unclean) until the evening.

"A ayash (man) who is tahawar (clean) shall asap (gather) up the ashes of the heifer, and yanach (lay) them up outside of the machanah (camp) in a tahawar (clean) place; and it shall be kept for the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) for a mayam (water) for impurity: it is a chataah (sin) offering.

He who asap (gathers) the ashes of the heifer shall wash his clothes, and be tamaa (unclean) until the evening: and it shall be to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and to the stranger who lives as a foreigner among them, for a chaqah (statute) iwalam (forever).
"He who touches the mawath (dead) napash (body) of any adam (man) shall be tamaa (unclean) shabai (seven) yawam (days):

the same shall chataa (purify) himself with water on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), and on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) he shall be tahar (clean): but if he doesn't chataa (purify) himself the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), then the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) he shall not be tahar (clean).

Whoever touches a mawath (dead) napash (person), the body of a adam (man) who has died, and doesn't chataa (purify) himself, tamaa (defiles) the mashakan (tabernacle) of Yahawah; and that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from Yasharaal (Israel): because the mayam (water) for impurity was not sprinkled on him, he shall be tamaa (unclean); his tamaah (uncleanness) is yet on him.

"This is the thawarah (law) when a adam (man) dies in a ahal (tent): everyone who bawaa (comes) into the ahal (tent), and everyone who is in the ahal (tent), shall be tamaa (unclean) shabai (seven) yawam (days).
Every pathach (open) vessel, which has no covering bound on it, is tamaa (unclean).

"Whoever in the panayam (open) shadah (field) touches one who is Chalal with a charab (sword), or a mawath (dead) body, or a itzam (bone) of a adam (man), or a qabar (grave), shall be tamaa (unclean) shabai (seven) yawam (days).
"For the tamaa (unclean) they shall take of the ashes of the burning of the chataah (sin) offering; and chay (running) mayam (water) shall be nathan (put) thereto in a vessel:

and a tahawar (clean) ayash (person) shall take hyssop, and dip it in the mayam (water), and sprinkle it on the ahal (tent), and on all the vessels, and on the napash (persons) who were there, and on him who touched the itzam (bone), or the Chalal, or the mawath (dead), or the qabar (grave):

and the tahawar (clean) person shall sprinkle on the tamaa (unclean) on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), and on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day): and on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) he shall chataa (purify) him; and he shall wash his clothes, and bathe himself in mayam (water), and shall be tahar (clean) at evening.

But the ayash (man) who shall be tamaa (unclean), and shall not chataa (purify) himself, that napash (soul) shall be karath (cut) off from the midst of the qahal (assembly), because he has defiled the maqadash (sanctuary) of Yahawah: the mayam (water) for impurity has not been sprinkled on him; he is tamaa (unclean).

It shall be a perpetual chaqah (statute) to them: and he who sprinkles the mayam (water) for impurity shall wash his clothes, and he who touches the mayam (water) for impurity shall be tamaa (unclean) until evening.
"Whatever the tamaa (unclean) person touches shall be tamaa (unclean); and the napash (soul) that touches it shall be tamaa (unclean) until evening.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel), even the whole idah (congregation), came into the madabar (wilderness) of Tzan in the raashawan (first) chadash (month): and the im (people) stayed in Qadash; and Marayam died there, and was buried there.
There was no mayam (water) for the idah (congregation): and they assembled themselves together against Mashah and against Aharawan.
The im (people) strove with Mashah, and spoke, saying, "We wish that we had died when our ach (brothers) died panayam (before) Yahawah!
Why have you brought the qahal (assembly) of Yahawah into this madabar (wilderness), that we should mawath (die) there, we and our animals?

Why have you made us to ilah (come) up out of Matzarayam, to bawaa (bring) us in to this rai (evil) place? It is no place of zarai (seed), or of figs, or of vines, or of pomegranates; neither is there any mayam (water) to drink.

Mashah and Aharawan went from the panayam (presence) of the qahal (assembly) to the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and napal (fell) on their panayam (faces): and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah raah (see) to them.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"Take the matah (rod), and assemble the idah (congregation), you, and Aharawan your ach (brother), and dabar (speak) to the salai (rock) before their iyan (eyes), that it nathan (give) forth its mayam (water); and you shall nathan (bring) forth to them mayam (water) out of the salai (rock); so you shall shaqah (give) the idah (congregation) and their livestock shaqah (drink).
Mashah took the matah (rod) from panayam (before) Yahawah, as he tzawah (commanded) him.

Mashah and Aharawan gathered the qahal (assembly) together panayam (before) the salai (rock), and he said to them, "Hear now, you rebels; shall we yatzaa (bring) you mayam (water) out of this salai (rock) for you?

Mashah lifted up his yad (hand), and struck the salai (rock) with his matah (rod) paim (twice): and mayam (water) came yatzaa (forth) abundantly, and the idah (congregation) drank, and their livestock.

Yahawah said to Mashah and Aharawan, "Because you didn't aman (believe) in me, to qadash (sanctify) me in the iyan (eyes) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), therefore you shall not bawaa (bring) this qahal (assembly) into the aratz (land) which I have given them.
These are the mayam (waters) of Marayabah; because the children of Yasharaal (Israel) strove with Yahawah, and he was sanctified in them.
Mashah sent malaak (messengers) from Qadash to the malak (king) of Adam, saying: "Thus amar (says) your ach (brother) Yasharaal (Israel): You yadai (know) all the travail that has happened to us:
how our abawath (fathers) went down into Matzarayam, and we lived in Matzarayam a rab (long) yawam (time); and the Matzarayam (Egyptians) dealt raii (ill) with us, and our abawath (fathers):

and when we cried to Yahawah, he heard our qawal (voice), and sent an malaak (angel), and brought us yatzaa (forth) out of Matzarayam: and behold, we are in Qadash, a Iyar in the uttermost of your border.

"Please let us ibar (pass) through your aratz (land): we will not ibar (pass) through shadah (field) or through vineyard, neither will we drink of the mayam (water) of the baar (wells): we will yalak (go) along the malak (king's) darak (highway); we will not natah (turn) aside to the right yamayan (hand) nor to the shamaawal (left), until we have passed your border.
Adam said to him, "You shall not ibar (pass) through me, lest I yatzaa (come) out with the charab (sword) qaraah (against) you.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) said to him, "We will ilah (go) up by the masalah (highway); and if we drink of your mayam (water), I and my livestock, then will I nathan (give) its price: let me only, without doing anything else, ibar (pass) through on my feet.
He said, "You shall not ibar (pass) through." Adam came out qaraah (against) him Kabad many im (people), and with a chazaq (strong) yad (hand).
Thus Adam refused to nathan (give) Yasharaal (Israel) passage through his border, so Yasharaal (Israel) turned natah (away) from him.
They traveled from Qadash: and the children of Yasharaal (Israel), even the whole idah (congregation), came to har (mount) Har.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah and Aharawan in har (mount) Har, by the border of the aratz (land) of Adam, saying,

"Aharawan shall be gathered to his im (people); for he shall not bawaa (enter) into the aratz (land) which I have given to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), because you rebelled against my pah (word) at the mayam (waters) of Marayabah.
Take Aharawan and Alaizar his ban (son), and ilah (bring) them up to har (mount) Har;
and strip Aharawan of his bagad (garments), and Labash them on Alaizar his ban (son): and Aharawan shall be taken, and shall mawath (die) there.
Mashah did as Yahawah tzawah (commanded): and they went up into har (mount) Har in the iyan (sight) of all the idah (congregation).

Mashah stripped Aharawan of his bagad (garments), and Labash them on Alaizar his ban (son); and Aharawan died there on the raash (top) of the har (mountain): and Mashah and Alaizar came down from the har (mountain).
When all the idah (congregation) saw that Aharawan was gawai (dead), they wept for Aharawan shalawashayam (thirty) yawam (days), even all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

The Kanainay (Canaanite), the malak (king) of Irad, who lived in the Nagab, heard tell that Yasharaal (Israel) came by the darak (way) Atharayam Atharim; and he fought against Yasharaal (Israel), and took some of them Shabay.
Yasharaal (Israel) vowed a nadar (vow) to Yahawah, and said, "If you will nathan (indeed) nathan (deliver) this im (people) into my yad (hand), then I will utterly charam (destroy) their Iyar.

Yahawah listened to the qawal (voice) of Yasharaal (Israel), and delivered up the Kanainay (Canaanites); and they charam (utterly) destroyed them and their Iyar: and the sham (name) of the place was called Charamah.

They traveled from har (mount) Har by the darak (way) to the Red yam (sea), to sabab (compass) the aratz (land) of Adam: and the napash (soul) of the im (people) was much discouraged because of the darak (way).

The im (people) spoke against Alahayam, and against Mashah, "Why have you brought us up out of Matzarayam to mawath (die) in the madabar (wilderness)? For there is no lacham (bread), and there is no mayam (water); and our napash (soul) loathes this qalaqal (light) lacham (bread).
Yahawah sent sharap (fiery) serpents among the im (people), and they bit the im (people); and many im (people) of Yasharaal (Israel) died.

The im (people) came to Mashah, and said, "We have sinned, because we have spoken against Yahawah, and against you. palal (pray) to Yahawah, that he sawar (take) away the serpents from us." Mashah prayed for the im (people).
Yahawah said to Mashah, "ishah (make) a sharap (fiery) serpent, and shawam (set) it on a nas (standard): and it shall happen, that everyone who is bitten, when he raah (see) it, shall live.
Mashah made a serpent of brass, and shawam (set) it on the nas (standard): and it happened, that if a serpent had bitten any ayash (man), when he looked to the serpent of brass, he lived.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) traveled, and encamped in Abath.
They traveled from Abath, and encamped Iyayahaibarayam Iyeabarim, in the madabar (wilderness) which is panayam (before) Mawaab, toward the sunrise.
From there they traveled, and encamped in the nachal (valley) of Zarad.

From there they traveled, and encamped on the other ibar (side) of the Aranawan, which is in the madabar (wilderness), that yatzaa (comes) out of the border of the Amaray (Amorites): for the Aranawan is the border of Mawaab, between Mawaab and the Amaray (Amorites).
Therefore it is said in the book of the Wars of Yahawah, "Wahab in Suphah, the nachal (valleys) of the Aranawan,
the slope of the nachal (valleys) that natah (incline) toward the yashab (dwelling) of Ir, shain (leans) on the border of Mawaab.
From there they traveled to Baar: that is the baar (well) of which Yahawah said to Mashah, "asap (gather) the im (people) asap (together), and I will nathan (give) them mayam (water).
Then sang Yasharaal (Israel) this song: "ilah (spring) up, baar (well); sing to it:
the baar (well), which the shar (princes) dug, which the nadayab (nobles) of the im (people) dug, with the scepter, and with their poles." From the madabar (wilderness) they traveled to Mathanah;
and from Mathanah to Nachalayaal; and from Nachalayaal to Bamawath;
and from Bamawath to the Gayaa that is in the shadah (field) of Mawaab, to the raash (top) of Pasagah, which shaqap (looks) down on the yashayamawan (desert).
Yasharaal (Israel) sent malaak (messengers) to Sayachawan malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), saying,

"Let me ibar (pass) through your aratz (land): we will not natah (turn) aside into shadah (field), or into vineyard; we will not drink of the mayam (water) of the baar (wells): we will yalak (go) by the malak (king's) darak (highway), until we have passed your border.

Sayachawan would not allow Yasharaal (Israel) to ibar (pass) through his border: but Sayachawan gathered all his im (people) asap (together), and went out qaraah (against) Yasharaal (Israel) into the madabar (wilderness), and came to Yahatz; and he fought against Yasharaal (Israel).

Yasharaal (Israel) struck him with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), and possessed his aratz (land) from the Aranawan to the Yabaq, even to the children of Imawan; for the border of the children of Imawan was iz (strong).
Yasharaal (Israel) took all these Iyar: and Yasharaal (Israel) lived in all the Iyar of the Amaray (Amorites), in Chashabawan, and in all its bath (towns).

For Chashabawan was the Iyar of Sayachawan the malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), who had fought against the raashawan (former) malak (king) of Mawaab, and taken all his aratz (land) out of his yad (hand), even to the Aranawan.
Therefore those who speak in proverbs amar (say), "bawaa (come) to Chashabawan. Let the Iyar of Sayachawan be built and established;
for a ash (fire) has gone out of Chashabawan, a lahabah (flame) from the city of Sayachawan. It has devoured Ir of Mawaab, The lords of the high places of the Aranawan.

Woe to you, Mawaab! You are abad (undone), im (people) of Kamawash! He has given his ban (sons) as fugitives, and his bath (daughters) into captivity, to Sayachawan malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites).
We have shot at them. Chashabawan has perished even to Dayabawan. We have laid shamam (waste) even to Napach, Which reaches to Mayadabaa.
Thus Yasharaal (Israel) lived in the aratz (land) of the Amaray (Amorites).
Mashah sent to spy out Yaizayar; and they took its bath (towns), and drove out the Amaray (Amorites) who were there.
They turned and went up by the darak (way) of Bashan: and Iwag the malak (king) of Bashan went out qaraah (against) them, he and all his im (people), to battle at Adaraiy.

Yahawah said to Mashah, "Don't yaraa (fear) him: for I have delivered him into your yad (hand), and all his im (people), and his aratz (land); and you shall do to him as you did to Sayachawan malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), who lived at Chashabawan.
So they struck him, and his ban (sons) and all his im (people), until there was balathay (none) shaar (left) him sharayad (remaining): and they possessed his aratz (land).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) traveled, and encamped in the irabah (plains) of Mawaab ibar (beyond) the Yaradan at Yarayachaw.
Balaq the ban (son) of Tzapawar saw all that Yasharaal (Israel) had done to the Amaray (Amorites).
Mawaab was very gawar (afraid) of the im (people), because they were many: and Mawaab was distressed panayam (because) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

Mawaab said to the zaqan (elders) of Madayan, "Now this qahal (multitude) will lick up all that is around us, as the ox licks up the grass of the shadah (field)." Balaq the ban (son) of Tzapawar was malak (king) of Mawaab at that ith (time).

He sent malaak (messengers) to Balaim the ban (son) of Baiwar, to Pathawar, which is by the nahar (river), to the aratz (land) of the children of his im (people), to qaraa (call) him, saying, "Behold, there is a im (people) who came out from Matzarayam. Behold, they cover the surface of the aratz (earth), and they are staying opposite me.

Please yalak (come) now therefore arar (curse) me this im (people); for they are too itzawam (mighty) for me: perhaps I shall yakal (prevail), that we may strike them, and that I may drive them out of the aratz (land); for I yadai (know) that he whom you barak (bless) is blessed, and he whom you arar (curse) is cursed.
The zaqan (elders) of Mawaab and the zaqan (elders) of Madayan departed with the rewards of divination in their yad (hand); and they came to Balaim, and spoke to him the dabar (words) of Balaq.

He said to them, "lawan (lodge) here this layal (night), and I will shawab (turn back / repent) you dabar (word) again, as Yahawah shall dabar (speak) to me." The shar (princes) of Mawaab stayed with Balaim.
Alahayam came to Balaim, and said, "Who are these men with you?
Balaim said to Alahayam, "Balaq the ban (son) of Tzapawar, malak (king) of Mawaab, has said to me,

‘Behold, the im (people) that has yatzaa (come) out of Matzarayam, it covers the surface of the aratz (earth): now, yalak (come) qabab (curse) me them; perhaps I shall be yakal (able) to fight against them, and shall drive them out.'
Alahayam said to Balaim, "You shall not yalak (go) with them. You shall not arar (curse) the im (people); for they are blessed.
Balaim rose up in the baqar (morning), and said to the shar (princes) of Balaq, "yalak (go) to your aratz (land); for Yahawah refuses to permit me to halak (go) with you.
The shar (princes) of Mawaab rose up, and they went to Balaq, and said, "Balaim refuses to halak (come) with us.
Balaq sent yet again shar (princes), more, and more honorable than they.
They came to Balaim, and said to him, "Thus amar (says) Balaq the ban (son) of Tzapawar, ‘Please let nothing hinder you from coming to me:
for I will kabad (promote) you to very kabad (great) honor, and whatever you amar (say) to me I will do. Please yalak (come) therefore, and qabab (curse) this im (people) for me.'

Balaim answered the ibad (servants) of Balaq, "If Balaq would nathan (give) me his bayath (house) full of kasap (silver) and gold, I can't ibar (go) beyond the pah (word) of Yahawah my Alahayam, to do qatan (less) or more.
Now therefore, please wait also here this layal (night), that I may yadai (know) what Yahawah will dabar (speak) to me more.

Alahayam came to Balaim at layal (night), and said to him, "If the men have bawaa (come) to qaraa (call) you, qawam (rise) up, yalak (go) with them; but only the dabar (word) which I dabar (speak) to you, that you shall do.
Balaim rose up in the baqar (morning), and saddled his donkey, and went with the shar (princes) of Mawaab.

alahayam (god's) ap (anger) was kindled because he went; and the malaak (angel) of Yahawah placed himself in the darak (way) for an shatan (adversary) against him. Now he was riding on his donkey, and his shanayam (two) nair (servants) were with him.

The donkey saw the malaak (angel) of Yahawah standing in the darak (way), with his charab (sword) drawn in his yad (hand); and the donkey turned natah (aside) out of the darak (way), and went into the shadah (field): and Balaim struck the donkey, to natah (turn) her into the darak (way).
Then the malaak (angel) of Yahawah stood in a narrow mashaiwal (path) between the vineyards, a wall being on this side, and a wall on that side.
The donkey saw the malaak (angel) of Yahawah, and she lachatz (thrust) herself to the wall, and crushed Balaim ragal (foot) against the wall: and he struck her again.
The malaak (angel) of Yahawah went further, and stood in a tzar (narrow) place, where there was no darak (way) to natah (turn) either to the right yamayan (hand) or to the shamaawal (left).
The donkey saw the malaak (angel) of Yahawah, and she rabatz (lay) down under Balaim: and Balaim ap (anger) was kindled, and he struck the donkey with his maqal (staff).
Yahawah opened the pah (mouth) of the donkey, and she said to Balaim, "What have I done to you, that you have struck me these shalawash (three) ragal (times)?
Balaim said to the donkey, "Because you have mocked me, I wish there were a charab (sword) in my yad (hand), for now I would have killed you.
The donkey said to Balaim, "Am I not your donkey, on which you have ridden all your yawam (life) long to this day? Was I ever in the habit of doing so to you?" He said, "No.

Then Yahawah opened the iyan (eyes) of Balaim, and he saw the malaak (angel) of Yahawah standing in the darak (way), with his charab (sword) drawn in his yad (hand); and he bowed his head, and fell on his ap (face).

The malaak (angel) of Yahawah said to him, "Why have you struck your donkey these shalawash (three) ragal (times)? Behold, I have yatzaa (come) forth as an shatan (adversary), because your darak (way) is yarat (perverse) before me:

and the donkey saw me, and turned aside panayam (before) me these shalawash (three) ragal (times). Unless she had turned aside from me, harag (surely) now I would have killed you, and saved her chayah (alive).

Balaim said to the malaak (angel) of Yahawah, "I have sinned; for I didn't yadai (know) that you stood in the darak (way) qaraah (against) me. Now therefore, if it raii (displeases) you, I will shawab (turn back / repent) back again.

The malaak (angel) of Yahawah said to Balaim, "yalak (go) with the men; but only the dabar (word) that I shall dabar (speak) to you, that you shall dabar (speak)." So Balaim went with the shar (princes) of Balaq.
When Balaq heard that Balaim had bawaa (come), he went out to qaraah (meet) him to the Iyar of Mawaab, which is on the border of the Aranawan, which is in the utmost part of the border.
Balaq said to Balaim, "Didn't I shalach (earnestly) shalach (send) to you to qaraa (call) you? Why didn't you halak (come) to me? Am I not yakal (able) indeed to kabad (promote) you to honor?

Balaim said to Balaq, "Behold, I have bawaa (come) to you: have I now any yakal (power) at all to dabar (speak) anything? The dabar (word) that Alahayam shawam (puts) in my pah (mouth), that shall I dabar (speak).
Balaim went with Balaq, and they came to Kiriath Huzoth.
Balaq sacrificed cattle and sheep, and sent to Balaim, and to the shar (princes) who were with him.
It happened in the baqar (morning), that Balaq took Balaim, and brought him up into the bamah (high) places of Bamawath; and he saw from there the utmost part of the im (people).
Balaim said to Balaq, "banah (build) me here shabai (seven) mazabach (altars), and kawan (prepare) me here shabai (seven) bulls and shabai (seven) ayal (rams).
Balaq did as Balaim had spoken; and Balaq and Balaim offered on every mazabach (altar) a bull and a ayal (ram).

Balaim said to Balaq, "Stand by your burnt ilah (offering), and I will yalak (go): perhaps Yahawah will qarah (come) to qaraah (meet) me; and whatever he shows me I will nagad (tell) you." He went to a bare height.
Alahayam met Balaim: and he said to him, "I have prepared the shabai (seven) mazabach (altars), and I have offered up a bull and a ayal (ram) on every mazabach (altar).
Yahawah shawam (put) a dabar (word) in Balaim pah (mouth), and said, "shawab (turn back / repent) to Balaq, and thus you shall dabar (speak).
He returned to him, and behold, he was standing by his burnt ilah (offering), he, and all the shar (princes) of Mawaab.

He took up his parable, and said, "From Aram has Balaq brought me, the malak (king) of Mawaab from the harar (mountains) of the qadam (east). yalak (come), arar (curse) Yaiqab for me. yalak (come), defy Yasharaal (Israel).
mah (how) shall I naqab (curse) whom Al has not cursed? How shall I defy whom Yahawah has not defied?

For from the raash (top) of the tzawar (rocks) I raah (see) him. From the Gabaih I see him. Behold, it is a im (people) that shakan (dwells) badad (alone), and shall not be reckoned among the gawayam (nations).

Who can count the ipar (dust) of Yaiqab, or number the rabai (fourth) part of Yasharaal (Israel)? Let me mawath (die) the mawath (death) of the yashar (righteous)! Let my acharayath (last) end be like his!
Balaq said to Balaim, "What have you done to me? I took you to qabab (curse) my ayab (enemies), and behold, you have blessed them barak (altogether).
He answered and said, "Must I not shamar (take) heed to dabar (speak) that which Yahawah shawam (puts) in my pah (mouth)?

Balaq said to him, "Please yalak (come) with me to achar (another) place, where you may raah (see) them; you shall raah (see) but the utmost part of them, and shall not raah (see) them all: and qabab (curse) me them from there.
He took him into the shadah (field) of Zophim, to the raash (top) of Pasagah, and built shabai (seven) mazabach (altars), and offered up a bull and a ayal (ram) on every mazabach (altar).
He said to Balaq, "Stand here by your burnt ilah (offering), while I qarah (meet) over there.
Yahawah met Balaim, and shawam (put) a dabar (word) in his pah (mouth), and said, "shawab (turn back / repent) to Balaq, and amar (say) this.
He came to him, and behold, he was standing by his burnt ilah (offering), and the shar (princes) of Mawaab with him. Balaq said to him, "What has Yahawah spoken?
He took up his parable, and said, "qawam (rise) up, Balaq, and hear! Listen to me, you ban (son) of Tzapawar.

Al is not a ayash (man), that he should lie, nor the ban (son) of adam (man), that he should nacham (repent). Has he said, and will he not do it? Or has he spoken, and will he not make it qawam (good)?
Behold, I have received a command to barak (bless). He has blessed, and I can't shawab (turn back / repent) it.
He has not seen awan (iniquity) in Yaiqab. Neither has he seen imal (perverseness) in Yasharaal (Israel). Yahawah his Alahayam is with him. The shout of a malak (king) is among them.
Al yatzaa (brings) them out of Matzarayam. He has as it were the thawaipah (strength) of the wild ox.
Surely there is no enchantment with Yaiqab; Neither is there any divination with Yasharaal (Israel). Now it shall be said of Yaiqab and of Yasharaal (Israel), What has Al done!

Behold, the im (people) qawam (rises) up as a labayaa (lioness), As a labayaa (lion) he nashaa (lifts) himself up. He shall not shakab (lie) down until he akal (eat) of the Tarap, and drinks the dam (blood) of the Chalal.
Balaq said to Balaim, "Neither naqab (curse) them at all, nor barak (bless) them at all.
But Balaim answered Balaq, "Didn't I dabar (tell) you, saying, ‘All that Yahawah dabar (speaks), that I must do?'
Balaq said to Balaim, "yalak (come) now, I will take you to achar (another) place; perhaps it will yashar (please) Alahayam that you may qabab (curse) me them from there.
Balaq took Balaim to the raash (top) of Paiwar, that shaqap (looks) down on the yashayamawan (desert).
Balaim said to Balaq, "banah (build) me here shabai (seven) mazabach (altars), and kawan (prepare) me here shabai (seven) bulls and shabai (seven) ayal (rams).
Balaq did as Balaim had said, and offered up a bull and a ayal (ram) on every mazabach (altar).

When Balaim saw that it pleased Yahawah to barak (bless) Yasharaal (Israel), he didn't halak (go), as at the other paim (times), to qaraah (meet) with enchantments, but he shayath (set) his panayam (face) toward the madabar (wilderness).
Balaim lifted up his iyan (eyes), and he saw Yasharaal (Israel) dwelling according to their shabat (tribes); and the rawach (spirit) of Alahayam came on him.
He took up his parable, and said, "Balaim the ban (son) of Baiwar amar (says), the gabar (man) whose iyan (eye) was closed says;
he says, who hears the amar (words) of Al, who chazah (sees) the vision of the Shaday, falling down, and having his iyan (eyes) galah (open):
How tawab (goodly) are your ahal (tents), Yaiqab, and your mashakan (tents), Yasharaal (Israel)!
As nachal (valleys) they are natah (spread) forth, as gardens by the riverside, as aloes which Yahawah has planted, as cedar trees beside the mayam (waters).
mayam (water) shall nazal (flow) from his buckets. His zarai (seed) shall be in many mayam (waters). His malak (king) shall be higher than Agag. His malakawath (kingdom) shall be exalted.

Al yatzaa (brings) him out of Matzarayam. He has as it were the thawaipah (strength) of the wild ox. He shall akal (eat) up the gawayam (nations) his tzar (adversaries), shall break their itzam (bones) in pieces, and pierce them with his chatz (arrows).
He couched, he shakab (lay) down as a aray (lion), as a labayaa (lioness); who shall qawam (rouse) him up? Everyone who blesses you is blessed. Everyone who arar (curses) you is cursed.

Balaq ap (anger) was kindled against Balaim, and he struck his kap (hands) together; and Balaq said to Balaim, "I called you to qabab (curse) my ayab (enemies), and, behold, you have barak (altogether) blessed them these shalawash (three) paim (times).
Therefore now flee you to your place! I thought to kabad (promote) you to kabad (great) honor; but, behold, Yahawah has kept you back from honor.
Balaim said to Balaq, "Didn't I also dabar (tell) your malaak (messengers) who you sent to me, saying,

‘If Balaq would nathan (give) me his bayath (house) full of kasap (silver) and gold, I can't ibar (go) beyond the pah (word) of Yahawah, to do either tawab (good) or rai (bad) of my own lab (mind). I will dabar (say) what Yahawah dabar (says)'?
Now, behold, I halak (go) to my im (people): yalak (come), I will inform you what this im (people) shall do to your im (people) in the acharayath (latter) yawam (days).
He took up his parable, and said, "Balaim the ban (son) of Baiwar amar (says), the gabar (man) whose iyan (eye) was closed says;

he says, who hears the amar (words) of Al, yadai (knows) the daith (knowledge) of the Most Ilayawan, and who chazah (sees) the vision of the Shaday, Falling down, and having his iyan (eyes) galah (open):

I raah (see) him, but not now. I raah (see) him, but not qarawab (near). A kawakab (star) will come out of Yaiqab. A scepter will qawam (rise) out of Yasharaal (Israel), and shall strike through the corners of Mawaab, and qawar (break) down all the ban (sons) of Shath.
Adam shall be a yarashah (possession). Shaiyar, his ayab (enemies), also shall be a yarashah (possession), while Yasharaal (Israel) does chayal (valiantly).
Out of Yaiqab shall one have radah (dominion), and shall abad (destroy) the sharayad (remnant) from the Iyar.
He looked at Imalaq, and took up his parable, and said, "Imalaq was the raashayath (first) of the gawayam (nations), But his acharayath (latter) end shall come to destruction.
He looked at the Qayanay (Kenite), and took up his parable, and said, "Your mawashab (dwelling) place is ayathan (strong). Your nest is shawam (set) in the salai (rock).
Qayan Kain shall be wasted, until Ashawar carries you away captive.
He took up his parable, and said, "Alas, who shall chayah (live) when Al does this?
But ships shall come from the yad (coast) of Kathay (Kittim). They shall afflict Ashawar, and shall afflict Ibar. He also shall come to destruction.
Balaim rose up, and went and returned to his place; and Balaq also went his darak (way).
Yasharaal (Israel) stayed in Shatayam; and the im (people) began to play the prostitute with the bath (daughters) of Mawaab:
for they called the im (people) to the zabach (sacrifices) of their Alahayam; and the im (people) ate, and bowed down to their Alahayam.
Yasharaal (Israel) joined himself to Bailapaiwar Peor: and the ap (anger) of Yahawah was kindled against Yasharaal (Israel).

Yahawah said to Mashah, "Take all the raash (chiefs) of the im (people), and yaqai (hang) them up to Yahawah before the shamash (sun), that the charawan (fierce) ap (anger) of Yahawah may shawab (turn back / repent) away from Yasharaal (Israel).
Mashah said to the shapat (judges) of Yasharaal (Israel), "ayash (every) one harag (kill) his men who have joined themselves to Bailapaiwar Peor.

Behold, one of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) came and brought to his ach (brothers) a Madayanay (Midianite) woman in the iyan (sight) of Mashah, and in the iyan (sight) of all the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), while they were weeping at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
When Payanachas, the ban (son) of Alaizar, the ban (son) of Aharawan the kahan (priest), saw it, he rose up from the midst of the idah (congregation), and took a spear in his yad (hand);

and he went achar (after) the ayash (man) of Yasharaal (Israel) into the pavilion, and thrust shanayam (both) of them through, the ayash (man) of Yasharaal (Israel), and the ashah (woman) through her body. So the magapah (plague) was stayed from the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
Those who died by the magapah (plague) were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"Payanachas, the ban (son) of Alaizar, the ban (son) of Aharawan the kahan (priest), has turned my chamah (wrath) shawab (turn back / repent) from the children of Yasharaal (Israel), in that he was jealous with my jealousy among them, so that I didn't kalah (consume) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) in my jealousy.
Therefore amar (say), ‘Behold, I nathan (give) to him my barayath (covenant) of shalawam (peace):

and it shall be to him, and to his zarai (seed) achar (after) him, the barayath (covenant) of an iwalam (forever) kahanah (priesthood); because he was jealous for his Alahayam, and made kapar (atonement) for the children of Yasharaal (Israel).'

Now the sham (name) of the ayash (man) of Israel that was slain, who was slain with the Madayanay (Midianite) woman, was Zamaray, the ban (son) of Salaw, a nashayaa (prince) of a abawath (fathers)' bayath (house) among the Shamainay (Simeonites).

The sham (name) of the Madayanay (Midianite) ashah (woman) who was slain was Kazabay, the bath (daughter) of Tzawar; he was raash (head) of the amah (people) of a abawath (fathers)' bayath (house) in Madayan.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"Harass the Madayanay (Midianites), and strike them;

for they harassed you with their wiles, with which they have deceived you in the dabar (matter) of Paiwar, and in the dabar (matter) of Kazabay, the bath (daughter) of the nashayaa (prince) of Madayan, their achawath (sister), who was slain on the yawam (day) of the magapah (plague) in the dabar (matter) of Paiwar.
It happened achar (after) the magapah (plague), that Yahawah spoke to Mashah and to Alaizar the ban (son) of Aharawan the kahan (priest), saying,

"nashaa (take) a census of all the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), all who are yatzaa (able) to go forth to tzabaa (war) in Yasharaal (Israel).
Mashah and Alaizar the kahan (priest) spoke with them in the irabah (plains) of Mawaab by the Yaradan at Yarayachaw, saying,

"Take a census, from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward; as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah and the children of Yasharaal (Israel)." These are those that came out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
Raawaban, the firstborn of Yasharaal (Israel); the ban (sons) of Raawaban: of Chanawak, the mashapachah (family) of the Chanakay; of Palawaa, the mashapachah (family) of the Palaay;
of Chatzarawan, the mashapachah (family) of the Chatzarawanay; of Karamay, the mashapachah (family) of the Karamay.

These are the mashapachah (families) of the Raawabanay (Reubenites); and those who were numbered of them were arabaiyam (forty) - shalawash (three) alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty).
The ban (sons) of Palawaa: Alayaab.

The ban (sons) of Alayaab: Namawaal, and Dathan, and Abayaram. These are that Dathan and Abayaram, who were Qarayaa of the idah (congregation), who strove against Mashah and against Aharawan in the idah (company) of Qarach, when they strove against Yahawah,

and the aratz (earth) opened its pah (mouth), and swallowed them up together with Qarach, when that idah (company) mawath (died); what time the ash (fire) devoured two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) men, and they became a nas (sign).
Notwithstanding, the ban (sons) of Qarach didn't mawath (die).

The ban (sons) of Shamaiwan after their mashapachah (families): of Namawaal, the mashapachah (family) of the Namawaalay; of Yamayan, the mashapachah (family) of the Yamayanay; of Yakayan, the mashapachah (family) of the Yakayanay;
of Zarach, the mashapachah (family) Zarachay the Zerahites; of Shaawal, the mashapachah (family) of the Shaawalay.
These are the mashapachah (families) of the Shamainay (Simeonites), isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) two maah (hundred).

The ban (sons) of Gad after their mashapachah (families): of Tzapawan, the mashapachah (family) of the Tzapawanay; of Chagay, the mashapachah (family) of the Chagay; of Shawanay, the mashapachah (family) of the Shawanay;
of Azanay, the mashapachah (family) of the Azanay; of Iray, the mashapachah (family) of the Iray;
of Arawad, the mashapachah (family) of the Arawaday; of Araalay, the mashapachah (family) of the Araalay.
These are the mashapachah (families) of the ban (sons) of Gad according to those who were numbered of them, arabaiyam (forty) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred).
The ban (sons) of Yahawadah (Judah): Ir and Awanan; and Ir and Awanan died in the aratz (land) of Kanain.

The ban (sons) of Yahawadah (Judah) after their mashapachah (families) were: of Shalah, the mashapachah (family) of the Shalanay; of Paratz, the mashapachah (family) Paratzay the Perezites; of Zarach, the mashapachah (family) Zarachay the Zerahites.
The ban (sons) of Paratz were: of Chatzarawan, the mashapachah (family) of the Chatzarawanay; of Chamawal, the mashapachah (family) of the Chamawalay.
These are the mashapachah (families) of Yahawadah (Judah) according to those who were numbered of them, shabaiyam (seventy) - six alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred).
The ban (sons) of Yashashakar after their mashapachah (families): of Thawalai, the mashapachah (family) of the Thawalaiy; Pawaah Puvah, the mashapachah (family) of the Pawanay;
of Yashawab, the mashapachah (family) of the Yashabay; of Shamarawan, the mashapachah (family) of the Shamaranay.
These are the mashapachah (families) of Yashashakar according to those who were numbered of them, shashayam (sixty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand) shalawash (three) maah (hundred).

The ban (sons) of Zabawalawan after their mashapachah (families): of Sarad, the mashapachah (family) Saraday the Seredites; of Ayalawan, the mashapachah (family) of the Alawanay; of Yachalaal, the mashapachah (family) of the Yachalaalay.
These are the mashapachah (families) Zabawalanay the Zebulunites according to those who were numbered of them, shashayam (sixty) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred).
The ban (sons) of Yawasap after their mashapachah (families): Manashah and Aparayam.
The ban (sons) of Manashah: of Makayar, the mashapachah (family) Makayaray the Machirites; and Makayar became the father of Galaid; of Galaid, the mashapachah (family) of the Galaiday (Gileadites).
These are the ban (sons) of Galaid: Ayaizar Iezer, the mashapachah (family) Ayaizaray the Iezerites; of Chalaq, the mashapachah (family) Chalaqay the Helekites;
and Asharayaal, the mashapachah (family) of the Asharaalay; and Shakam, the mashapachah (family) Shakamay the Shechemites;
and Shamayadai, the mashapachah (family) of the Shamayadaiy; and Chapar, the mashapachah (family) of the Chaparay.
Tzalapachad the ban (son) of Chapar had no ban (sons), but bath (daughters): and the sham (names) of the bath (daughters) of Tzalapachad were Machalah, and Naih, Chagalah, Malakah, and Tharatzah.
These are the mashapachah (families) of Manashah; and those who were numbered of them were chamashayam (fifty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred).

These are the ban (sons) of Aparayam after their mashapachah (families): of Shawathalach, the mashapachah (family) Shathalachay the Shuthelahites; of Bakar, the mashapachah (family) Bakaray the Becherites; of Thachan, the mashapachah (family) of the Thachanay.
These are the ban (sons) of Shawathalach: of Iran, the mashapachah (family) of the Iranay.

These are the mashapachah (families) of the ban (sons) of Aparayam according to those who were numbered of them, shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred). These are the ban (sons) of Yawasap after their mashapachah (families).

The ban (sons) of Banayamayan after their mashapachah (families): of Balai, the mashapachah (family) of the Balaiy; of Ashabal, the mashapachah (family) of the Ashabalay; of Achayaram, the mashapachah (family) of the Achayaramay;
Shapawapam Shephupham, the mashapachah (family) of the Shawapamay; of Chawapam, the mashapachah (family) of the Chawapamay.
The ban (sons) of Balai were Arad and Naiman: the mashapachah (family) of the Araday; of Naiman, the mashapachah (family) of the Naimay.
These are the ban (sons) of Banayamayan after their mashapachah (families); and those who were numbered of them were arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) shash (six) maah (hundred).

These are the ban (sons) Dan Dan after their mashapachah (families): of Shawacham, the mashapachah (family) of the Shawachamay. These are the mashapachah (families) Dan Dan after their mashapachah (families).
All the mashapachah (families) of the Shawachamay, according to those who were numbered of them, were shashayam (sixty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred).

The ban (sons) of Ashar after their mashapachah (families): of Yamanah, the mashapachah (family) Yamanah the Imnites; of Ishvi, the mashapachah (family) Yashaway the Ishvites; of Barayaih, the mashapachah (family) Barayaiy the Berites.
Of the ban (sons) of Barayaih: of Chabar, the mashapachah (family) of the Chabaray; of Malakayaal, the mashapachah (family) of the Malakayaalay.
The sham (name) of the bath (daughter) of Ashar was Sharach.
These are the mashapachah (families) of the ban (sons) of Ashar according to those who were numbered of them, chamashayam (fifty) - shalawash (three) alap (thousand) and arabai (four) maah (hundred).
The ban (sons) of Napathalay after their mashapachah (families): of Yachatzaal, the mashapachah (family) of the Yachatzaalay; of Gawanay, the mashapachah (family) of the Gawanay;
of Yatzar, the mashapachah (family) of the Yatzaray; of Shalam, the mashapachah (family) of the Shalamay.

These are the mashapachah (families) of Napathalay according to their mashapachah (families); and those who were numbered of them were arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred).
These are those who were numbered of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), shash (six) maah (hundred) one alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"To these the aratz (land) shall be divided for an nachalah (inheritance) according to the number of sham (names).

To the more you shall give the more nachalah (inheritance), and Mait the fewer you shall give the less nachalah (inheritance): to everyone according to those who were numbered of him shall his nachalah (inheritance) be given.
Notwithstanding, the aratz (land) shall be divided by lot: according to the sham (names) of the matah (tribes) of their abawath (fathers) they shall nachal (inherit).
According to the lot shall their nachalah (inheritance) be divided between the more and the Mait.

These are those who were numbered Lawayay the Levites after their mashapachah (families): of Garashawan, the mashapachah (family) of the garashanay (gershonites); of Qahath, the mashapachah (family) of the Qahathay (Kohathites); of Mararay, the mashapachah (family) of the Mararay (Merarites).

These are the mashapachah (families) Lawayay Levi: the mashapachah (family) of the Labanay, the mashapachah (family) of the Chabarawanay, the mashapachah (family) of the Machalay, the mashapachah (family) of the Mawashay, the mashapachah (family) of the qarachay (korahites). Qahath became the father of Imaram.

The sham (name) of Imaram ashah (wife) was Yawakabad, the bath (daughter) of Laway, who was yalad (born) to Laway in Matzarayam: and she bore to Imaram Aharawan and Mashah, and Marayam their achawath (sister).
To Aharawan were yalad (born) Nadab and Abayahawaa, Alaizar and Ayathamar.
Nadab and Abayahawaa died, when they offered zawar (strange) ash (fire) panayam (before) Yahawah.

Those who were numbered of them were isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three) alap (thousand), every zakar (male) from a chadash (month) ban (old) and upward: for they were not numbered among the children of Yasharaal (Israel), because there was no nachalah (inheritance) given them among the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
These are those who were numbered by Mashah and Alaizar the kahan (priest), who numbered the children of Yasharaal (Israel) in the irabah (plains) of Mawaab by the Yaradan at Yarayachaw.

But among these there was not a ayash (man) of them who were numbered by Mashah and Aharawan the kahan (priest), who numbered the children of Yasharaal (Israel) in the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay.

For Yahawah had said of them, They shall mawath (surely) mawath (die) in the madabar (wilderness). There was not yathar (left) a ayash (man) of them, except Kalab the ban (son) of Yapanah, and Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan.

Then drew near the bath (daughters) of Tzalapachad, the ban (son) of Chapar, the ban (son) of Galaid, the ban (son) of Makayar, the ban (son) of Manashah, of the mashapachah (families) of Manashah the ban (son) of Yawasap; and these are the sham (names) of his bath (daughters): Machalah, Naih, and Chagalah, and Malakah, and Tharatzah.

They stood panayam (before) Mashah, and panayam (before) Alaizar the kahan (priest), and panayam (before) the nashayaa (princes) and all the idah (congregation), at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, saying,

"Our ab (father) died in the madabar (wilderness), and he was not among the idah (company) of those who gathered themselves together against Yahawah in the idah (company) of Qarach: but he died in his own chataa (sin); and he had no ban (sons).

Why should the sham (name) of our ab (father) be taken away from among his mashapachah (family), because he had no ban (son)? nathan (give) to us a achazah (possession) among the ach (brothers) of our ab (father).
Mashah brought their cause panayam (before) Yahawah.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"The bath (daughters) of Tzalapachad dabar (speak) Kan: you shall nathan (surely) nathan (give) them a achazah (possession) of an nachalah (inheritance) among their ab (father's) ach (brothers); and you shall cause the nachalah (inheritance) of their ab (father) to ibar (pass) to them.

You shall dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, ‘If a ayash (man) dies, and has no ban (son), then you shall cause his nachalah (inheritance) to ibar (pass) to his bath (daughter).
If he has no bath (daughter), then you shall nathan (give) his nachalah (inheritance) to his ach (brothers).
If he has no ach (brothers), then you shall nathan (give) his nachalah (inheritance) to his ab (father's) ach (brothers).

If his ab (father) has no ach (brothers), then you shall nathan (give) his nachalah (inheritance) to his kinsman who is qarawab (next) to him of his mashapachah (family), and he shall yarash (possess) it: and it shall be to the children of Yasharaal (Israel) a chaqah (statute) and mashapat (ordinance), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.'
Yahawah said to Mashah, "ilah (go) up into this har (mountain) of Ibarayam, and raah (see) the aratz (land) which I have given to the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
When you have seen it, you also shall be gathered to your im (people), as Aharawan your ach (brother) was gathered;

because you rebelled against my pah (word) in the madabar (wilderness) of Tzan, in the Marayabah of the idah (congregation), to qadash (sanctify) me at the mayam (waters) before their iyan (eyes)." (These are the mayam (waters) of Marayabah of Qadash in the madabar (wilderness) of Tzan.)
Mashah spoke to Yahawah, saying,
"Let Yahawah, the Alahayam of the rawach (spirits) of all flesh, paqad (appoint) a ayash (man) over the idah (congregation),

who may yatzaa (go) out panayam (before) them, and who may bawaa (come) in panayam (before) them, and who may yatzaa (lead) them out, and who may bawaa (bring) them in; that the idah (congregation) of Yahawah not be as sheep which have no raih (shepherd).
Yahawah said to Mashah, "Take Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan, a ayash (man) in whom is the rawach (spirit), and samak (lay) your yad (hand) on him;
and imad (set) him panayam (before) Alaizar the kahan (priest), and panayam (before) all the idah (congregation); and commission him in their iyan (sight).
You shall nathan (put) of your honor on him, that all the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) may obey.

He shall imad (stand) panayam (before) Alaizar the kahan (priest), who shall inquire for him by the mashapat (judgment) of the awarayam (urim) panayam (before) Yahawah: at his pah (word) shall they yatzaa (go) out, and at his pah (word) they shall bawaa (come) in, both he, and all the children of Yasharaal (Israel) with him, even all the idah (congregation).
Mashah did as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) him; and he took Yahawashawai, and imad (set) him panayam (before) Alaizar the kahan (priest), and panayam (before) all the idah (congregation):
and he laid his yad (hands) on him, and commissioned him, as Yahawah spoke by Mashah.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"tzawah (command) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them, ‘My qaraban (offering), my food for my qaraban (offerings) made by ashah (fire), of a pleasant aroma to me, you shall shamar (observe) to qarab (offer) to me in their mawaid (due) season.'

You shall amar (tell) them, ‘This is the ashah (offering) made by fire which you shall qarab (offer) to Yahawah: male lambs a Shanah old thamayam (without) blemish, shanayam (two) yawam (day) by day, for a continual burnt ilah (offering).
You shall ishah (offer) the one lamb in the baqar (morning), and you shall ishah (offer) the other lamb at evening;
with the ishayaray (tenth) part of an ephah of fine flour for a meal manachah (offering), mixed with the rabayaiy (fourth) part of a hin of Kathayath shaman (oil).
It is a continual burnt ilah (offering), which was ordained in har (mount) Sayanay for a pleasant aroma, an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah.
Its drink nasak (offering) shall be the rabayaiy (fourth) part of a hin for the one lamb. You shall pour out a drink nasak (offering) of shakar (strong) drink to Yahawah in the qadash (holy) place.

The other lamb you shall ishah (offer) at evening: as the meal manachah (offering) of the baqar (morning), and as the drink nasak (offering) of it, you shall ishah (offer) it, an ashah (offering) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah.

"‘On the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day) shanayam (two) male lambs a Shanah old thamayam (without) blemish, and shanayam (two) isharawan (tenth) parts of an ephah of fine flour for a meal manachah (offering), mixed with shaman (oil), and the drink nasak (offering) of it:
this is the burnt ilah (offering) of every shabath (sabbath), besides the continual burnt ilah (offering), and the drink nasak (offering) of it.

"‘In the raash (beginnings) of your chadash (months) you shall qarab (offer) a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah: shanayam (two) young bulls, and one ayal (ram), shabai (seven) male lambs a Shanah old thamayam (without) blemish;

and shalawash (three) isharawan (tenth) parts of an ephah of fine flour for a meal manachah (offering), mixed with shaman (oil), for achad (each) bull; and shanayam (two) isharawan (tenth) parts of fine flour for a meal manachah (offering), mixed with shaman (oil), for the one ayal (ram);

and a isharawan (tenth) part of fine flour mixed with shaman (oil) for a meal manachah (offering) to achad (every) lamb; for a burnt ilah (offering) of a pleasant aroma, an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah.

Their drink nasak (offerings) shall be chatzay (half) a hin of yayan (wine) for a bull, and the shalayashay (third) part of a hin for the ayal (ram), and the rabayaiy (fourth) part of a hin for a lamb: this is the burnt ilah (offering) of every chadash (month) throughout the chadash (months) of the Shanah.
One Shaiyar goat for a chataah (sin) offering to Yahawah; it shall be offered besides the continual burnt ilah (offering), and the drink ilah (offering) of it.
"‘In the raashawan (first) chadash (month), on the fourteenth yawam (day) of the month, is yahawah (yahweh's) pasach (passover).
On the fifteenth yawam (day) of this chadash (month) shall be a chag (feast): shabai (seven) yawam (days) shall unleavened matzah (bread) be eaten.
In the raashawan (first) yawam (day) shall be a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation): you shall do no servile malaakah (work);

but you shall qarab (offer) an ashah (offering) made by fire, a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah: shanayam (two) young bulls, and one ayal (ram), and shabai (seven) male lambs a Shanah old; they shall be to you thamayam (without) blemish;

and their meal manachah (offering), fine flour mixed with shaman (oil): you shall ishah (offer) shalawash (three) isharawan (tenth) parts for a bull, and shanayam (two) isharawan (tenth) parts for the ayal (ram).
You shall ishah (offer) a isharawan (tenth) part for achad (every) lamb of the shabai (seven) lambs;
and one male Shaiyar for a chataah (sin) offering, to make kapar (atonement) for you.
You shall ishah (offer) these besides the burnt ilah (offering) of the baqar (morning), which is for a continual burnt ilah (offering).

In this way you shall ishah (offer) yawam (daily), for shabai (seven) yawam (days), the lacham (food) of the ashah (offering) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah: it shall be offered besides the continual burnt ilah (offering), and the drink ilah (offering) of it.
On the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) you shall have a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation): you shall do no servile malaakah (work).

"‘Also in the yawam (day) of the bakawar (first) fruits, when you qarab (offer) a Chadash meal manachah (offering) to Yahawah in your feast of shabawai (weeks), you shall have a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation); you shall do no servile malaakah (work);
but you shall qarab (offer) a burnt ilah (offering) for a pleasant aroma to Yahawah: shanayam (two) young bulls, one ayal (ram), shabai (seven) male lambs a Shanah old;
and their meal manachah (offering), fine flour mixed with shaman (oil), shalawash (three) isharawan (tenth) parts for achad (each) bull, shanayam (two) isharawan (tenth) parts for the one ayal (ram),
a isharawan (tenth) part for achad (every) lamb of the shabai (seven) lambs;
one Shaiyar Shaiyar, to make kapar (atonement) for you.
Besides the continual burnt ilah (offering), and the meal ilah (offering) of it, you shall ishah (offer) them (they shall be to you thamayam (without) blemish), and their drink nasak (offerings).

"‘In the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month), on the achad (first) day of the chadash (month), you shall have a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation); you shall do no servile malaakah (work): it is a yawam (day) of blowing of trumpets to you.
You shall ishah (offer) a burnt ilah (offering) for a pleasant aroma to Yahawah: one young bull, one ayal (ram), shabai (seven) male lambs a Shanah old thamayam (without) blemish;
and their meal manachah (offering), fine flour mixed with shaman (oil), shalawash (three) isharawan (tenth) parts for the bull, shanayam (two) isharawan (tenth) parts for the ayal (ram),
and one isharawan (tenth) part for achad (every) lamb of the shabai (seven) lambs;
and one Shaiyar Shaiyar for a chataah (sin) offering, to make kapar (atonement) for you;

besides the burnt ilah (offering) of the new chadash (moon), and the meal manachah (offering) of it, and the continual burnt ilah (offering) and the meal manachah (offering) of it, and their drink nasak (offerings), according to their mashapat (ordinance), for a pleasant aroma, an ashah (offering) made by fire to Yahawah.

"‘On the tenth day of this shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month) you shall have a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation); and you shall afflict your napash (souls): you shall do no kind of malaakah (work);

but you shall qarab (offer) a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah for a pleasant aroma: one young bull, one ayal (ram), shabai (seven) male lambs a Shanah old; they shall be to you thamayam (without) blemish;
and their meal manachah (offering), fine flour mixed with shaman (oil), shalawash (three) isharawan (tenth) parts for the bull, shanayam (two) isharawan (tenth) parts for the one ayal (ram),
a isharawan (tenth) part for achad (every) lamb of the shabai (seven) lambs:

one Shaiyar Shaiyar for a chataah (sin) offering; besides the chataah (sin) offering of kapar (atonement), and the continual burnt chataah (offering), and the meal ilah (offering) of it, and their drink manachah (offerings).

"‘On the fifteenth yawam (day) of the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month) you shall have a qadash (holy) maqaraa (convocation); you shall do no servile malaakah (work), and you shall keep a chag (feast) to Yahawah shabai (seven) yawam (days):

and you shall qarab (offer) a burnt ilah (offering), an ashah (offering) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah; thirteen young bulls, shanayam (two) ayal (rams), fourteen male lambs a Shanah old; they shall be thamayam (without) blemish;

and their meal manachah (offering), fine flour mixed with shaman (oil), shalawash (three) isharawan (tenth) parts for achad (every) bull of the thirteen bulls, shanayam (two) isharawan (tenth) parts for achad (each) ayal (ram) of the shanayam (two) ayal (rams),
and a isharawan (tenth) part for achad (every) lamb of the fourteen lambs;
and one Shaiyar goat for a chataah (sin) offering, besides the continual burnt chataah (offering), the meal chataah (offering) of it, and the drink nasak (offering) of it.
"‘On the shanay (second) yawam (day) you shall offer shanayam (twelve) ban (young) bulls, shanayam (two) ayal (rams), fourteen male lambs a Shanah old thamayam (without) blemish;
and their meal manachah (offering) and their drink nasak (offerings) for the bulls, for the ayal (rams), and for the lambs, according to their number, after the mashapat (ordinance);
and one Shaiyar goat for a chataah (sin) offering; besides the continual burnt chataah (offering), and the meal ilah (offering) of it, and their drink manachah (offerings).
"‘On the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) ishathay (eleven) bulls, shanayam (two) ayal (rams), fourteen male lambs a Shanah old thamayam (without) blemish;
and their meal manachah (offering) and their drink nasak (offerings) for the bulls, for the ayal (rams), and for the lambs, according to their number, after the mashapat (ordinance);
and one male Shaiyar for a chataah (sin) offering; besides the continual burnt chataah (offering), and the meal ilah (offering) of it, and the drink nasak (offering) of it.
"‘On the rabayaiy (fourth) yawam (day) ishar (ten) bulls, shanayam (two) ayal (rams), fourteen male lambs a Shanah old thamayam (without) blemish;
their meal manachah (offering) and their drink nasak (offerings) for the bulls, for the ayal (rams), and for the lambs, according to their number, after the mashapat (ordinance);
and one Shaiyar goat for a chataah (sin) offering; besides the continual burnt chataah (offering), the meal chataah (offering) of it, and the drink nasak (offering) of it.
"‘On the chamayashay (fifth) yawam (day) thashai (nine) bulls, shanayam (two) ayal (rams), fourteen male lambs a Shanah old thamayam (without) blemish;
and their meal manachah (offering) and their drink nasak (offerings) for the bulls, for the ayal (rams), and for the lambs, according to their number, after the mashapat (ordinance);
and one male Shaiyar for a chataah (sin) offering, besides the continual burnt ilah (offering), and the meal manachah (offering) of it, and the drink nasak (offering) of it.
"‘On the shashay (sixth) yawam (day) shamanah (eight) bulls, shanayam (two) ayal (rams), fourteen male lambs a Shanah old thamayam (without) blemish;
and their meal manachah (offering) and their drink nasak (offerings) for the bulls, for the ayal (rams), and for the lambs, according to their number, after the mashapat (ordinance);
and one male Shaiyar for a chataah (sin) offering; besides the continual burnt ilah (offering), the meal manachah (offering) of it, and the drink nasak (offerings) of it.
"‘On the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) shabai (seven) bulls, shanayam (two) ayal (rams), fourteen male lambs a Shanah old thamayam (without) blemish;
and their meal manachah (offering) and their drink nasak (offerings) for the bulls, for the ayal (rams), and for the lambs, according to their number, after the mashapat (ordinance);
and one male Shaiyar for a chataah (sin) offering; besides the continual burnt ilah (offering), the meal manachah (offering) of it, and the drink nasak (offering) of it.
"‘On the eighth yawam (day) you shall have a solemn itzarah (assembly): you shall do no servile malaakah (work);

but you shall qarab (offer) a burnt ilah (offering), an ashah (offering) made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to Yahawah: one bull, one ayal (ram), shabai (seven) male lambs a Shanah old thamayam (without) blemish;
their meal manachah (offering) and their drink nasak (offerings) for the bull, for the ayal (ram), and for the lambs, shall be according to their number, after the mashapat (ordinance):
and one male Shaiyar for a chataah (sin) offering, besides the continual burnt chataah (offering), and the meal ilah (offering) of it, and the drink nasak (offering) of it.

"‘You shall ishah (offer) these to Yahawah in your mawaid (set) feasts, besides your nadar (vows), and your freewill nadabah (offerings), for your burnt ilah (offerings), and for your meal manachah (offerings), and for your drink nasak (offerings), and for your shalam (peace) offerings.'
Mashah told the children of Yasharaal (Israel) according to all that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
Mashah spoke to the raash (heads) of the matah (tribes) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "This is the thing which Yahawah has tzawah (commanded).

When a ayash (man) nadar (vows) a nadar (vow) to Yahawah, or shabai (swears) an shabawaih (oath) to bind his napash (soul) with a bond, he shall not chalal (break) his dabar (word); he shall do according to all that yatzaa (proceeds) out of his pah (mouth).
"Also when a ashah (woman) nadar (vows) a nadar (vow) to Yahawah, and binds herself by a bond, being in her ab (father's) bayath (house), in her youth,

and her ab (father) hears her nadar (vow), and her bond with which she has bound her napash (soul), and her ab (father) holds his charash (peace) at her; then all her nadar (vows) shall qawam (stand), and every bond with which she has bound her napash (soul) shall qawam (stand).

But if her ab (father) disallow her in the yawam (day) that he hears, none of her nadar (vows), or of her bonds with which she has bound her napash (soul), shall qawam (stand): and Yahawah will forgive her, because her ab (father) disallowed her.
"If she has a ayash (husband), while her nadar (vows) are on her, or the rash utterance of her shapah (lips), with which she has bound her napash (soul),

and her ayash (husband) hears it, and hold his charash (peace) at her in the yawam (day) that he hears it; then her nadar (vows) shall qawam (stand), and her bonds with which she has bound her napash (soul) shall qawam (stand).

But if her ayash (husband) forbids her in the yawam (day) that he hears it, then he shall make void her mabataa (vow) which is on her, and the rash utterance of her shapah (lips), with which she has bound her napash (soul): and Yahawah will forgive her.
"But the nadar (vow) of a alamanah (widow), or of her who is divorced, everything with which she has bound her napash (soul), shall qawam (stand) against her.
"If she vowed in her ayash (husband's) bayath (house), or bound her napash (soul) by a bond with an shabawaih (oath),

and her ayash (husband) heard it, and held his charash (peace) at her, and didn't disallow her; then all her nadar (vows) shall qawam (stand), and every bond with which she bound her napash (soul) shall qawam (stand).

But if her ayash (husband) made them null and parar (void) in the yawam (day) that he heard them, then whatever proceeded out of her shapah (lips) concerning her nadar (vows), or concerning the bond of her napash (soul), shall not qawam (stand): her ayash (husband) has made them parar (void); and Yahawah will forgive her.
Every nadar (vow), and every binding shabawaih (oath) to afflict the napash (soul), her ayash (husband) may qawam (establish) it, or her ayash (husband) may parar (make) it void.

But if her ayash (husband) charash (altogether) hold his charash (peace) at her from yawam (day) to yawam (day), then he establishes all her nadar (vows), or all her bonds, which are on her: he has established them, because he held his charash (peace) at her in the yawam (day) that he heard them.
But if he shall parar (make) them null and parar (void) achar (after) that he has heard them, then he shall nashaa (bear) her iwan (iniquity).

These are the chaq (statutes), which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah, between a ayash (man) and his ashah (wife), between a ab (father) and his bath (daughter), being in her youth, in her ab (father's) bayath (house).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"Avenge the children of Yasharaal (Israel) for the Madayanay (Midianites). Afterward you shall be gathered to your im (people).
Mashah spoke to the im (people), saying, "chalatz (arm) men from among you for the tzabaa (war), that they may go against Madayan, to execute yahawah (yahweh's) vengeance on Madayan.
Of every matah (tribe) one alap (thousand), throughout all the matah (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), you shall shalach (send) to the tzabaa (war).
So there were delivered, out of the alap (thousands) of Yasharaal (Israel), a alap (thousand) of every matah (tribe), shanayam (twelve) alap (thousand) chalatz (armed) for tzabaa (war).

Mashah sent them, one alap (thousand) of every matah (tribe), to the tzabaa (war), them and Payanachas the ban (son) of Alaizar the kahan (priest), to the tzabaa (war), with the vessels of the qadash (sanctuary) and the trumpets for the alarm in his yad (hand).
They warred against Madayan, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah; and they killed every zakar (male).

They killed the malak (kings) of Madayan with the rest of their Chalal: Away, and Raqam, and Tzawar, and Chawar, and Rabai, the chamash (five) malak (kings) of Madayan: Balaim also the ban (son) of Baiwar they killed with the charab (sword).

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) took captive the women of Madayan and their little ones; and all their livestock, and all their maqanah (flocks), and all their chayal (goods), they took for a prey.
All their Iyar in the mawashab (places) in which they lived, and all their encampments, they burnt with ash (fire).
They took all the spoil, and all the prey, both of adam (man) and of animal.

They brought the Shabay, and the prey, and the spoil, to Mashah, and to Alaizar the kahan (priest), and to the idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), to the machanah (camp) at the irabah (plains) of Mawaab, which are by the Yaradan at Yarayachaw.
Mashah, and Alaizar the kahan (priest), and all the nashayaa (princes) of the idah (congregation), went yatzaa (forth) to qaraah (meet) them outside of the machanah (camp).
Mashah was qatzap (angry) with the paqad (officers) of the chayal (army), the shar (captains) of alap (thousands) and the shar (captains) of maah (hundreds), who came from the service of the war.
Mashah said to them, "Have you saved all the women chayah (alive)?

Behold, these caused the children of Yasharaal (Israel), through the dabar (counsel) of Balaim, to commit mail (trespass) against Yahawah in the dabar (matter) of Paiwar, and so the magapah (plague) was among the idah (congregation) of Yahawah.
Now therefore harag (kill) every zakar (male) among the little ones, and harag (kill) every ashah (woman) who has yadai (known) ayash (man) by lying with him.
But all the girls, who have not yadai (known) zakar (man) by lying with him, chayah (keep) alive for yourselves.

"chanah (encamp) outside of the machanah (camp) shabai (seven) yawam (days): whoever has killed any napash (person), and whoever has touched any Chalal, chataa (purify) yourselves on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) and on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), you and your Shabay.
As to every bagad (garment), and all that is made of skin, and all maishah (work) of goats' hair, and all things made of itz (wood), you shall chataa (purify) yourselves.
Alaizar the kahan (priest) said to the men of tzabaa (war) who went to the battle, "This is the chaqah (statute) of the thawarah (law) which Yahawah has tzawah (commanded) Mashah:
however the gold, and the kasap (silver), the brass, the barazal (iron), the tin, and the lead,

everything that may withstand the ash (fire), you shall ibar (make) to go through the ash (fire), and it shall be tahar (clean); nevertheless it shall be purified with the mayam (water) for impurity: and all that doesn't withstand the ash (fire) you shall ibar (make) to go through the mayam (water).
You shall wash your clothes on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), and you shall be tahar (clean); and afterward you shall bawaa (come) into the machanah (camp).
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"nashaa (take) the raash (sum) of the prey that was Shabay, both of adam (man) and of animal, you, and Alaizar the kahan (priest), and the raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' households of the idah (congregation);
and divide the prey into chatzah (two) parts: between the men skilled in war, who went out to tzabaa (battle), and all the idah (congregation).

Levy a tribute to Yahawah of the men of war who went out to tzabaa (battle): one napash (soul) of chamash (five) maah (hundred); of the adam (persons), of the cattle, of the donkeys, and of the flocks.
Take it of their half, and nathan (give) it to Alaizar the kahan (priest), for yahawah (yahweh's) wave tharawamah (offering).

Of the children of Yasharaal half, you shall take one drawn out of every chamashayam (fifty), of the adam (persons), of the cattle, of the donkeys, and of the flocks, of all the livestock, and nathan (give) them Lawayay the Levites, who perform the duty of the mashakan (tabernacle) of Yahawah.
Mashah and Alaizar the kahan (priest) did as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
Now the prey, over and above the booty which the im (men) of tzabaa (war) took, was shash (six) maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) sheep,
and shabaiyam (seventy) - two alap (thousand) baqar (head) of cattle,
and shashayam (sixty) - one alap (thousand) donkeys,
and shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) napash (persons) in all, of the women who had not yadai (known) zakar (man) by lying with him.

The half, which was the chalaq (portion) of those who went out to tzabaa (war), was in number shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - shabai (seven) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred) sheep:
and yahawah (yahweh's) tribute of the sheep was shash (six) maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) - five.
The cattle were shalawashayam (thirty) - shash (six) alap (thousand); of which yahawah (yahweh's) tribute was shabaiyam (seventy) - two.
The donkeys were shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred); of which yahawah (yahweh's) tribute was shashayam (sixty) - one.
The adam (persons) were sixteen alap (thousand); of whom yahawah (yahweh's) tribute was shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) napash (persons).
Mashah gave the tribute, which was yahawah (yahweh's) wave tharawamah (offering), to Alaizar the kahan (priest), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
Of the children of Yasharaal half, which Mashah divided off from the men who warred
