(now the idah (congregation's) half was shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - shabai (seven) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred) sheep,
and shalawashayam (thirty) - shash (six) alap (thousand) baqar (head) of cattle,
and shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand) chamash (five) maah (hundred) donkeys,
and sixteen alap (thousand) napash (persons)),

even of the children of Yasharaal half, Mashah took one drawn out of every chamashayam (fifty), both of adam (man) and of animal, and gave them Lawayay the Levites, who performed the duty of the mashakan (tabernacle) of Yahawah; as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
The paqad (officers) who were over the alap (thousands) of the tzabaa (army), the shar (captains) of alap (thousands), and the shar (captains) of maah (hundreds), came qarab (near) to Mashah;
and they said to Mashah, "Your ibad (servants) have taken the raash (sum) of the men of war who are under our command, and there paqad (lacks) not one ayash (man) of us.

We have brought yahawah (yahweh's) qaraban (offering), what every ayash (man) has gotten, of jewels of gold, armlets, and bracelets, signet rings, earrings, and necklaces, to make kapar (atonement) for our napash (souls) panayam (before) Yahawah.
Mashah and Alaizar the kahan (priest) took their gold, even all worked jewels.

All the gold of the wave tharawamah (offering) that they offered up to Yahawah, of the shar (captains) of alap (thousands), and of the shar (captains) of maah (hundreds), was sixteen alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) shekels.
(The men of tzabaa (war) had taken booty, every anawash (man) for himself.)

Mashah and Alaizar the kahan (priest) took the gold of the shar (captains) of alap (thousands) and of maah (hundreds), and brought it into the ahal (tent) of Meeting, for a zakarawan (memorial) for the children of Yasharaal (Israel) panayam (before) Yahawah.

Now the children of Raawaban and the children of Gad had a very itzawam (great) rab (multitude) of livestock: and when they saw the aratz (land) of Yaizayar, and the aratz (land) of Galaid, that behold, the place was a place for livestock;
the children of Gad and the children of Raawaban came and spoke to Mashah, and to Alaizar the kahan (priest), and to the nashayaa (princes) of the idah (congregation), saying,
"Itarawath, and Dayabawan, and Yaizayar, and Namarah, and Chashabawan, and Alailaa, and Shabam, and Nabaw, and Bain,
the aratz (land) which Yahawah struck panayam (before) the idah (congregation) of Yasharaal (Israel), is a aratz (land) for livestock; and your ibad (servants) have livestock.
They said, "If we have found favor in your iyan (sight), let this aratz (land) be given to your ibad (servants) for a achazah (possession); don't ibar (bring) us over the Yaradan.
Mashah said to the children of Gad, and to the children of Raawaban, "Shall your ach (brothers) bawaa (go) to the war, and shall you yashab (sit) here?
Why do you discourage the lab (heart) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) from going over into the aratz (land) which Yahawah has given them?
Your abawath (fathers) did so when I sent them Qadashabaranai Kadesh Barnea to raah (see) the aratz (land).

For when they went up to the nachal (valley) of Ashakal, and saw the aratz (land), they discouraged the lab (heart) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), that they should not bawaa (go) into the aratz (land) which Yahawah had given them.
yahawah (yahweh's) ap (anger) was kindled in that yawam (day), and he swore, saying,

‘am (surely) none of the men who came up out of Matzarayam, from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, shall raah (see) the adamah (land) which I swore to Abaraham, to Yatzachaq, and to Yaiqab; because they have not malaa (wholly) followed me:
except Kalab the ban (son) of Yapanah the Qanazay (Kenizzite), and Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan; because they have followed Yahawah completely.'

yahawah (yahweh's) ap (anger) was kindled against Yasharaal (Israel), and he made them wander back and forth in the madabar (wilderness) arabaiyam (forty) Shanah, until all the dawar (generation), who had done rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, was consumed.
"Behold, you have risen up in your abawath (fathers)' place, an increase of chataa (sinful) men, to sapah (augment) yet the charawan (fierce) ap (anger) of Yahawah toward Yasharaal (Israel).
For if you shawab (turn back / repent) away from achar (after) him, he will yet again yanach (leave) them in the madabar (wilderness); and you will shachath (destroy) all this im (people).
They came near to him, and said, "We will banah (build) Gadarah here for our livestock, and Iyar for our little ones:

but we ourselves will be ready chalatz (armed) to go panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), until we have brought them to their place: and our little ones shall yashab (dwell) in the fortified Iyar panayam (because) of the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land).
We will not shawab (turn back / repent) to our bayath (houses), until the children of Yasharaal (Israel) have inherited every ayash (man) his nachalah (inheritance).

For we will not nachal (inherit) with them on the other ibar (side) of the Yaradan, and forward; because our nachalah (inheritance) is bawaa (fallen) to us on this ibar (side) of the Yaradan eastward.
Mashah said to them, "If you will do this thing, if you will chalatz (arm) yourselves to go panayam (before) Yahawah to the war,
and every chalatz (armed) ibar (man) of you will pass over the Yaradan panayam (before) Yahawah, until he has driven out his ayab (enemies) from panayam (before) him,

and the aratz (land) is subdued panayam (before) Yahawah; then afterward you shall shawab (turn back / repent), and be naqay (guiltless) towards Yahawah, and towards Yasharaal (Israel); and this aratz (land) shall be to you for a achazah (possession) panayam (before) Yahawah.
"But if you will not do so, behold, you have sinned against Yahawah; and be yadai (sure) your chataah (sin) will matzaa (find) you out.
banah (build) Iyar for your little ones, and Gadarah for your sheep; and do that which has proceeded out of your pah (mouth).
The children of Gad and the children of Raawaban spoke to Mashah, saying, "Your ibad (servants) will do as my Adawan tzawah (commands).
Our little ones, our wives, our maqanah (flocks), and all our livestock, shall be there in the Iyar of Galaid;
but your ibad (servants) will ibar (pass) over, every chalatz (man) who is armed for tzabaa (war), panayam (before) Yahawah to battle, as my Adawan dabar (says).

So Mashah tzawah (commanded) concerning them to Alaizar the kahan (priest), and to Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan, and to the raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' households of the matah (tribes) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

Mashah said to them, "If the children of Gad and the children of Raawaban will ibar (pass) with you over the Yaradan, every chalatz (man) who is armed to battle, panayam (before) Yahawah, and the aratz (land) shall be subdued panayam (before) you; then you shall nathan (give) them the aratz (land) of Galaid for a achazah (possession):
but if they will not ibar (pass) over with you chalatz (armed), they shall have achaz (possessions) among you in the aratz (land) of Kanain.
The children of Gad and the children of Raawaban answered, saying, "As Yahawah has said to your ibad (servants), so will we do.

We will ibar (pass) over chalatz (armed) panayam (before) Yahawah into the aratz (land) of Kanain, and the achazah (possession) of our nachalah (inheritance) shall remain with us ibar (beyond) the Yaradan.

Mashah gave to them, even to the children of Gad, and to the children of Raawaban, and to the chatzay (half) - shabat (tribe) of Manashah the ban (son) of Yawasap, the mamalakah (kingdom) of Sayachawan malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), and the mamalakah (kingdom) of Iwag malak (king) of Bashan, the aratz (land), according to its Iyar and borders, even the Iyar of the surrounding aratz (land).
The children of Gad built Dayabawan, and Itarawath, and Irawair,
and Itarawathashawapan, and Yaizayar, and Yagabahah,
and Bayathanamarah Nimrah, and Bayathaharan Haran: fortified Iyar, and Gadarah for sheep.
The children of Raawaban built Chashabawan, and Alailaa, and Qarayathayam,
and Nabaw, and Bailamaiwan Meon, (their sham (names) being changed), and Shabam: and they gave other sham (names) to the Iyar which they built.
The children of Makayar the ban (son) of Manashah went to Galaid, and took it, and dispossessed the Amaray (Amorites) who were therein.
Mashah gave Galaid to Makayar the ban (son) of Manashah; and he lived therein.
Yaayar the ban (son) of Manashah went and took its towns, and called them Havvoth Chawawathayaiyar.
Nabach went and took Qanath, and its bath (villages), and called it Nabach, after his own sham (name).
These are the journeys of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), when they went yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam by their tzabaa (armies) under the yad (hand) of Mashah and Aharawan.
Mashah wrote their goings out according to their journeys by the commandment of Yahawah: and these are their journeys according to their goings out.

They traveled from Raimasas in the raashawan (first) chadash (month), on the fifteenth yawam (day) of the raashawan (first) chadash (month); on the next macharath (day) after the pasach (passover) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) went out with a high yad (hand) in the iyan (sight) of all the Matzarayam (Egyptians),
while the Matzarayam (Egyptians) were burying all their firstborn, whom Yahawah had struck among them: on their Alahayam also Yahawah executed shapat (judgments).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) traveled from Raimasas, and encamped in Sakawath.
They traveled from Sakawath, and encamped in Atham, which is in the edge of the madabar (wilderness).
They traveled from Atham, and turned shawab (turn back / repent) to Payahachayarath, which is before Bailatzapawan Zephon: and they encamped panayam (before) Magadawal.

They traveled from panayam (before) Hahiroth, and passed ibar (through) the midst of the yam (sea) into the madabar (wilderness): and they went shalawash (three) yawam (days)' darak (journey) in the madabar (wilderness) of Atham, and encamped in Marah.
They traveled from Marah, and came to Ayalam: and in Ayalam were shanayam (twelve) springs of mayam (water), and shabaiyam (seventy) palm trees; and they encamped there.
They traveled from Ayalam, and encamped by the Red yam (sea).
They traveled from the Red yam (sea), and encamped in the madabar (wilderness) of sayan (sin).
They traveled from the madabar (wilderness) of sayan (sin), and encamped in Dapaqah.
They traveled from Dapaqah, and encamped in Alawash.
They traveled from Alawash, and encamped in Rapayadayam, where there was no mayam (water) for the im (people) to drink.
They traveled from Rapayadayam, and encamped in the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay.
They traveled from the madabar (wilderness) of Sayanay, and encamped in Qabarawathahathaawah Hattaavah.
They traveled from Qabarawathahathaawah Hattaavah, and encamped in Chatzarawath.
They traveled from Chatzarawath, and encamped in Rathamah.
They traveled from Rathamah, and encamped in Ramanaparatz Perez.
They traveled from Ramanaparatz Perez, and encamped in Labanah.
They traveled from Labanah, and encamped in Rasah.
They traveled from Rasah, and encamped in Qahalathah.
They traveled from Qahalathah, and encamped in har (mount) Shapar.
They traveled from har (mount) Shapar, and encamped in Charadah.
They traveled from Charadah, and encamped in Maqahalath.
They traveled from Maqahalath, and encamped in Thachath.
They traveled from Thachath, and encamped in Tharach.
They traveled from Tharach, and encamped Mathaqah Mithkah.
They traveled Mathaqah Mithkah, and encamped in Chashamanah.
They traveled from Chashamanah, and encamped in Mawasarah.
They traveled from Mawasarah, and encamped in Banayayaiqan Jaakan.
They traveled from Banayayaiqan Jaakan, and encamped in Charahagadagad Haggidgad.
They traveled from Charahagadagad Haggidgad, and encamped in Yatabathah.
They traveled from Yatabathah, and encamped Ibaranah Abronah.
They traveled Ibaranah Abronah, and encamped in Itzayawanagabar Geber.
They traveled from Itzayawanagabar Geber, and encamped in the madabar (wilderness) of Tzan (the same is Qadash).
They traveled from Qadash, and encamped in har (mount) Har, in the edge of the aratz (land) of Adam.

Aharawan the kahan (priest) went up into har (mount) Har at the commandment of Yahawah, and died there, in the fortieth Shanah after the children of Yasharaal (Israel) had yatzaa (come) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, in the chamayashay (fifth) chadash (month), on the achad (first) day of the month.
Aharawan was one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three) Shanah ban (old) when he mawath (died) in har (mount) Har.
The Kanainay (Canaanite), the malak (king) of Irad, who lived in the Nagab in the aratz (land) of Kanain, heard of the coming of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
They traveled from har (mount) Har, and encamped in Tzalamanah.
They traveled from Tzalamanah, and encamped in Pawanan.
They traveled from Pawanan, and encamped in Abath.
They traveled from Abath, and encamped in Iye Iyayahaibarayam, in the border of Mawaab.
They traveled Iyayam Iyim, and encamped in Dayabawan Gad.
They traveled from Dayabawan Gad, and encamped Ilamanadabalathayamah Almon Diblathaim.
They traveled Ilamanadabalathayamah Almon Diblathaim, and encamped in the har (mountains) of Ibarayam, panayam (before) Nabaw.
They traveled from the har (mountains) of Ibarayam, and encamped in the irabah (plains) of Mawaab by the Yaradan at Yarayachaw.
They encamped by the Yaradan, from Bayathahayashayamawath Jeshimoth Abalahashatayam to Abel Shittim in the irabah (plains) of Mawaab.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah in the irabah (plains) of Mawaab by the Yaradan at Yarayachaw, saying,
dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them, "When you ibar (pass) over the Yaradan into the aratz (land) of Kanain,

then you shall yarash (drive) out all the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land) from panayam (before) you, abad (destroy) all their stone idols, abad (destroy) all their molten tzalam (images), and demolish all their bamah (high) places.
You shall take yarash (possession) of the aratz (land), and yashab (dwell) therein; for I have given the aratz (land) to you to yarash (possess) it.

You shall nachal (inherit) the aratz (land) by lot according to your mashapachah (families); to the more you shall give the more nachalah (inheritance), and Mait the fewer you shall give the less nachalah (inheritance): wherever the lot yatzaa (falls) to any man, that shall be his. You shall nachal (inherit) according to the matah (tribes) of your abawath (fathers).

"But if you do not yarash (drive) out the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land) from panayam (before) you, then those you let yathar (remain) of them will be as pricks in your iyan (eyes) and as thorns in your sides, and they will harass you in the aratz (land) in which you yashab (dwell).
It shall happen that as I thought to do to them, so will I do to you.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,

"tzawah (command) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them, ‘When you bawaa (come) into the aratz (land) of Kanain (this is the aratz (land) that shall napal (fall) to you for an nachalah (inheritance), even the aratz (land) of Kanain according to its borders),
then your Nagab quarter shall be from the madabar (wilderness) of Tzan along by the yad (side) of Adam, and your Nagab border shall be from the end of the Malach yam (sea) eastward;

and your border shall sabab (turn) Nagab southward of the ascent of Mailahaiqarabayam, and ibar (pass) along to Tzan; and the goings out Nagab it shall be southward Qadashabaranai Kadesh Barnea; and it shall yatzaa (go) forth to Chatzaraadar Addar, and ibar (pass) along to Itzamawan;
and the border shall sabab (turn) about from Itzamawan to the nachal (brook) of Matzarayam, and the goings out of it shall be at the yam (sea).
"‘For the western border, you shall have the gadawal (great) yam (sea) and its border: this shall be your yam (west) border.
"‘This shall be your tzapawan (north) border: from the gadawal (great) yam (sea) you shall mark out for you har (mount) Har;
from har (mount) Har you shall mark out to the entrance of Chamath; and the goings out of the border shall be at Tzadad;
and the border shall yatzaa (go) forth to Zaparan, and the goings out of it shall be at Chatzaraiyanan Enan: this shall be your tzapawan (north) border.
"‘You shall mark out your qadam (east) border from Chatzaraiyanan Enan to Shapam;

and the border shall yarad (go) down from Shapam to Rabalah, on the qadam (east) side of Iyan; and the border shall yarad (go) down, and shall machah (reach) to the side of the yam (sea) of Kanarawath eastward;
and the border shall yarad (go) down to the Yaradan, and the goings out of it shall be at the Malach yam (sea). This shall be your aratz (land) according to its borders around it.'

Mashah tzawah (commanded) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "This is the aratz (land) which you shall nachal (inherit) by lot, which Yahawah has tzawah (commanded) to nathan (give) to the thashai (nine) matah (tribes), and to the chatzay (half) - matah (tribe);

for the matah (tribe) of the children of Raawabanay according to their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), and the matah (tribe) of the children of Gaday according to their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), have received, and the chatzay (half) - matah (tribe) of Manashah have received, their nachalah (inheritance):
the shanayam (two) matah (tribes) and the chatzay (half) - matah (tribe) have received their nachalah (inheritance) ibar (beyond) the Yaradan at Yarayachaw eastward, toward the sunrise.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"These are the sham (names) of the men who shall nachal (divide) the aratz (land) to you for inheritance: Alaizar the kahan (priest), and Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan.
You shall take one nashayaa (prince) of every matah (tribe), to nachal (divide) the aratz (land) for nachal (inheritance).
These are the sham (names) of the men: Of the matah (tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah), Kalab the ban (son) of Yapanah.
Of the matah (tribe) of the children of Shamaiwan, Shamawaal the ban (son) of Imayahawad.
Of the matah (tribe) of Banayamayan, Alayadad the ban (son) of Kasalawan.
Of the matah (tribe) of the children Dan Dan a nashayaa (prince), Baqay the ban (son) of Yagalay.
Of the children of Yawasap: of the matah (tribe) of the children of Manashah a nashayaa (prince), Chanayaal the ban (son) of apad (ephod).
Of the matah (tribe) of the children of Aparayam a nashayaa (prince), Qamawaal the ban (son) of Shapatan.
Of the matah (tribe) of the children of Zabawalawan a nashayaa (prince), Alayatzapan the ban (son) of Paranak.
Of the matah (tribe) of the children of Yashashakar a nashayaa (prince), Palatayaal the ban (son) of Izan.
Of the matah (tribe) of the children of Ashar a nashayaa (prince), Achayahawad the ban (son) of Shalamay.
Of the matah (tribe) of the children of Napathalay a nashayaa (prince), Padahaal the ban (son) of Imayahawad.
These are they whom Yahawah tzawah (commanded) to divide the nachal (inheritance) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel) in the aratz (land) of Kanain.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah in the irabah (plains) of Mawaab by the Yaradan at Yarayachaw, saying,

"tzawah (command) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) that they nathan (give) Lawayay the Levites of the nachalah (inheritance) of their achazah (possession) Iyar to yashab (dwell) in; and you shall nathan (give) suburbs for the Iyar around them Lawayay the Levites.
The Iyar shall they have to yashab (dwell) in; and their suburbs shall be for their livestock, and for their rakawash (substance), and for all their animals.
"The suburbs of the Iyar, which you shall nathan (give) Lawayay the Levites, shall be from the wall of the Iyar and outward one alap (thousand) amah (cubits) around it.

You shall measure outside of the Iyar for the qadam (east) side two alap (thousand) amah (cubits), and for the Nagab side two alap (thousand) amah (cubits), and for the yam (west) side two alap (thousand) amah (cubits), and for the tzapawan (north) side two alap (thousand) amah (cubits), the Iyar being in the midst. This shall be to them the suburbs of the Iyar.

"The Iyar which you shall nathan (give) Lawayay the Levites, they shall be the shash (six) Iyar of refuge, which you shall nathan (give) for the manslayer to flee to: and besides them you shall nathan (give) arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two) Iyar.
All the Iyar which you shall nathan (give) Lawayay the Levites shall be arabaiyam (forty) - shamanah (eight) Iyar together with their suburbs.

Concerning the Iyar which you shall nathan (give) of the achazah (possession) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), from the many you shall take many; and from the Mait you shall take Mait: everyone according to his nachalah (inheritance) which he nachal (inherits) shall nathan (give) of his Iyar Lawayay the Levites.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah, saying,
"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them, ‘When you ibar (pass) over the Yaradan into the aratz (land) of Kanain,
then you shall qarah (appoint) you Iyar to be Iyar of refuge for you, that the manslayer who kills any napash (person) unwittingly may flee there.
The Iyar shall be to you for refuge from the gaal (avenger), that the manslayer not mawath (die), until he imad (stands) panayam (before) the idah (congregation) for mashapat (judgment).
The Iyar which you shall nathan (give) shall be for you shash (six) Iyar of refuge.
You shall nathan (give) shalawash (three) Iyar ibar (beyond) the Yaradan, and you shall nathan (give) shalawash (three) Iyar in the aratz (land) of Kanain; they shall be Iyar of refuge.

For the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and for the stranger and for the foreigner living among them, shall these shash (six) Iyar be for refuge; that everyone who kills any napash (person) unwittingly may flee there.
"‘But if he struck him with an instrument of barazal (iron), so that he died, he is a ratzach (murderer): the ratzach (murderer) shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death).

If he struck him with a aban (stone) in the yad (hand), by which a mawath (man) may die, and he died, he is a ratzach (murderer): the ratzach (murderer) shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death).

Or if he struck him with a weapon of itz (wood) in the yad (hand), by which a mawath (man) may die, and he died, he is a ratzach (murderer): the ratzach (murderer) shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death).
The avenger of dam (blood) shall himself ratzach (put) the murderer to mawath (death): when he pagai (meets) him, he shall put him to mawath (death).
If he thrust him of hatred, or hurled at him, lying in wait, so that he died,

or in enmity struck him with his yad (hand), so that he died; he who struck him shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death); he is a ratzach (murderer): the gaal (avenger) of dam (blood) shall ratzach (put) the murderer to mawath (death), when he pagai (meets) him.
"‘But if he thrust him suddenly laa (without) enmity, or hurled on him anything without lying in wait,
or with any aban (stone), by which a mawath (man) may die, not seeing him, and napal (cast) it on him, so that he died, and he was not his ayab (enemy), neither sought his rai (harm);
then the idah (congregation) shall shapat (judge) between the striker and the gaal (avenger) of dam (blood) according to these mashapat (ordinances);

and the idah (congregation) shall natzal (deliver) the manslayer out of the yad (hand) of the gaal (avenger) of dam (blood), and the idah (congregation) shall shawab (turn back / repent) him to his Iyar of refuge, where he was fled: and he shall yashab (dwell) therein until the mawath (death) of the gadawal (high) kahan (priest), who was mashach (anointed) with the qadash (holy) shaman (oil).
"‘But if the manslayer shall at any yatzaa (time) yatzaa (go) beyond the border of his Iyar of refuge, where he flees,

and the gaal (avenger) of dam (blood) matzaa (find) him outside of the border of his Iyar of refuge, and the gaal (avenger) of dam (blood) ratzach (kill) the manslayer; he shall not be guilty of dam (blood),

because he should have remained in his Iyar of refuge until the mawath (death) of the gadawal (high) kahan (priest): but achar (after) the mawath (death) of the gadawal (high) kahan (priest) the manslayer shall shawab (turn back / repent) into the aratz (land) of his achazah (possession).
"‘These things shall be for a chaqah (statute) and mashapat (ordinance) to you throughout your dawar (generations) in all your mawashab (dwellings).
"‘Whoever kills any napash (person), the ratzach (murderer) shall be slain at the pah (mouth) of witnesses: but one witness shall not testify against any napash (person) that he mawath (die).
"‘Moreover you shall take no kapar (ransom) for the napash (life) of a ratzach (murderer) who is rashai (guilty) of mawath (death); but he shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death).

"‘You shall take no kapar (ransom) for him who is fled to his Iyar of refuge, that he may shawab (turn back / repent) again to yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land), until the mawath (death) of the kahan (priest).

"‘So you shall not pollute the aratz (land) in which you are: for dam (blood), it pollutes the aratz (land); and no expiation can be made for the aratz (land) for the dam (blood) that is shed therein, but by the dam (blood) of him who shed it.
You shall not tamaa (defile) the aratz (land) which you yashab (inhabit), in the midst of which I shakan (dwell): for I, Yahawah, shakan (dwell) in the midst of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).'

The raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' households of the mashapachah (family) of the children of Galaid, the ban (son) of Makayar, the ban (son) of Manashah, of the mashapachah (families) of the ban (sons) of Yawasap, came qarab (near), and spoke panayam (before) Mashah, and panayam (before) the nashayaa (princes), the raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' households of the children of Yasharaal (Israel):

and they said, "Yahawah tzawah (commanded) my Adawan to nathan (give) the aratz (land) for nachalah (inheritance) by lot to the children of Yasharaal (Israel): and my Adawan was tzawah (commanded) by Yahawah to nathan (give) the nachalah (inheritance) of Tzalapachad our ach (brother) to his bath (daughters).

If they are married to any of the ban (sons) of the other shabat (tribes) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), then will their nachalah (inheritance) be taken away from the nachalah (inheritance) of our abawath (fathers), and will be added to the nachalah (inheritance) of the matah (tribe) whereunto they shall belong: so will it be taken away from the lot of our nachalah (inheritance).

When the jubilee of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shall be, then will their nachalah (inheritance) be added to the nachalah (inheritance) of the matah (tribe) whereunto they shall belong: so will their nachalah (inheritance) be taken away from the nachalah (inheritance) of the matah (tribe) of our abawath (fathers).
Mashah tzawah (commanded) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) according to the pah (word) of Yahawah, saying, "The matah (tribe) of the ban (sons) of Yawasap dabar (speaks) right.

This is the thing which Yahawah does tzawah (command) concerning the bath (daughters) of Tzalapachad, saying, Let them be married to whom they iyan (think) tawab (best); only into the mashapachah (family) of the matah (tribe) of their ab (father) shall they be married.

So shall no nachalah (inheritance) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) sabab (remove) from matah (tribe) to matah (tribe); for the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shall all keep the nachalah (inheritance) of the matah (tribe) of his abawath (fathers).

Every bath (daughter) who possesses an nachalah (inheritance) in any matah (tribe) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shall be ashah (wife) to one of the mashapachah (family) of the matah (tribe) of her ab (father), that the children of Yasharaal (Israel) may yarash (possess) every ayash (man) the nachalah (inheritance) of his abawath (fathers).

So shall no nachalah (inheritance) sabab (remove) from one matah (tribe) to achar (another) matah (tribe); for the matah (tribes) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shall ayash (each) keep his own nachalah (inheritance).
The bath (daughters) of Tzalapachad did as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah:
for Machalah, Tharatzah, and Chagalah, and Malakah, and Naih, the bath (daughters) of Tzalapachad, were married to their dawad (father's) brothers' ban (sons).

They were married into the mashapachah (families) of the ban (sons) of Manashah the ban (son) of Yawasap; and their nachalah (inheritance) remained in the matah (tribe) of the mashapachah (family) of their ab (father).

These are the matzawah (commandments) and the mashapat (ordinances) which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) by Mashah to the children of Yasharaal (Israel) in the irabah (plains) of Mawaab by the Yaradan at Yarayachaw.

These are the dabar (words) which Mashah spoke to all Yasharaal (Israel) ibar (beyond) the Yaradan in the madabar (wilderness), in the irabah (arabah) over against Suph, between Paaran, and Thapal, and Laban, and Chatzarawath, and Dayazahab.
It is achad (eleven) yawam (days)' journey from Charab by the darak (way) of har (mount) Shaiyar Qadashabaranai Kadesh Barnea.

It happened in the fortieth Shanah, in the ishathay (eleventh) chadash (month), on the achad (first) day of the chadash (month), that Mashah spoke to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), according to all that Yahawah had given him in commandment to them;
achar (after) he had struck Sayachawan the malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), who lived in Chashabawan, and Iwag the malak (king) of Bashan, who lived Ishatharawath Ashtaroth, at Adaraiy.
ibar (beyond) the Yaradan, in the aratz (land) of Mawaab, began Mashah to declare this thawarah (law), saying,
"Yahawah our Alahayam spoke to us in Charab, saying, You have lived rab (long) enough in this har (mountain):

panah (turn), and take your nasai (journey), and bawaa (go) to the har (hill) country of the Amaray (Amorites), and Shakan all the places near there, in the irabah (arabah), in the har (hill) country, and in the lowland, and in the Nagab, and by the seashore, the aratz (land) of the Kanainay (Canaanites), and Labanawan, as gadawal (far) as the great nahar (river), the nahar (river) Parath.

raah (see), I have nathan (set) the aratz (land) panayam (before) you: bawaa (go) in and yarash (possess) the aratz (land) which Yahawah swore to your abawath (fathers), to Abaraham, to Yatzachaq, and to Yaiqab, to nathan (give) to them and to their zarai (seed) achar (after) them.
I spoke to you at that ith (time), saying, "I am not yakal (able) to nashaa (bear) you myself bad (alone):
Yahawah your Alahayam has multiplied you, and behold, you are this yawam (day) as the kawakab (stars) of the sky for multitude.
Yahawah, the Alahayam of your abawath (fathers), make you a alap (thousand) paim (times) as many as you are, and barak (bless) you, as he has promised you!
How can I myself alone nashaa (bear) your encumbrance, and your mashaa (burden), and your rayab (strife)?
Take chakam (wise) men of bayan (understanding) and well yadai (known) according to your shabat (tribes), and I will shawam (make) them raash (heads) over you.
You answered me, and said, "The thing which you have spoken is tawab (good) to do.

So I took the raash (heads) of your shabat (tribes), chakam (wise) men, and yadai (known), and made them raash (heads) over you, shar (captains) of alap (thousands), and shar (captains) of maah (hundreds), and shar (captains) of chamashayam (fifties), and shar (captains) of ishar (tens), and shatar (officers), according to your shabat (tribes).

I tzawah (commanded) your shapat (judges) at that ith (time), saying, "Hear cases between your ach (brothers), and shapat (judge) righteously between a ayash (man) and his ach (brother), and the foreigner who is living with him.

You shall not show partiality in mashapat (judgment); you shall hear the qatan (small) and the gadawal (great) alike; you shall not be gawar (afraid) of the panayam (face) of ayash (man); for the mashapat (judgment) is alahayam (god's). The dabar (case) that is too hard for you, you shall qarab (bring) to me, and I will hear it.
I tzawah (commanded) you at that ith (time) all the things which you should do.

We traveled from Charab, and went through all that gadawal (great) and yaraa (terrible) madabar (wilderness) which you saw, by the darak (way) to the har (hill) country of the Amaray (Amorites), as Yahawah our Alahayam tzawah (commanded) us; and we came Qadashabaranai Kadesh Barnea.
I said to you, "You have bawaa (come) to the har (hill) country of the Amaray (Amorites), which Yahawah our Alahayam nathan (gives) to us.

raah (see), Yahawah your Alahayam has nathan (set) the aratz (land) panayam (before) you: ilah (go) up, take yarash (possession), as Yahawah, the Alahayam of your abawath (fathers), has spoken to you; don't be yaraa (afraid), neither be dismayed.

You came qarab (near) to me everyone of you, and said, "Let us shalach (send) men panayam (before) us, that they may search the aratz (land) for us, and shawab (turn back / repent) us dabar (word) again of the darak (way) by which we must ilah (go) up, and the Iyar to which we shall bawaa (come).
The thing pleased me yatab (well); and I took shanayam (twelve) men of you, one anawash (man) for ayash (every) tribe:
and they turned and went up into the har (hill) country, and came to the nachal (valley) of Ashakal, and spied it out.

They took of the fruit of the aratz (land) in their yad (hands), and brought it down to us, and brought us dabar (word) again, and said, "It is a tawab (good) aratz (land) which Yahawah our Alahayam nathan (gives) to us.
Yet you wouldn't ilah (go) up, but rebelled against the commandment of Yahawah your Alahayam:

and you murmured in your ahal (tents), and said, "Because Yahawah hated us, he has brought us yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, to nathan (deliver) us into the yad (hand) of the Amaray (Amorites), to destroy us.

Where are we going up? our ach (brothers) have made our labab (heart) to melt, saying, ‘The im (people) are greater and taller than we; the Iyar are gadawal (great) and fortified up to the sky; and moreover we have seen the ban (sons) of the Inaqay (Anakim) there.'
Then I said to you, "Don't iratz (dread), neither be yaraa (afraid) of them.
Yahawah your Alahayam who goes panayam (before) you, he will fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Matzarayam before your iyan (eyes),

and in the madabar (wilderness), where you have seen how that Yahawah your Alahayam bore you, as a ayash (man) does nashaa (bear) his ban (son), in all the darak (way) that you went, until you came to this place.
Yet in this thing you didn't aman (believe) Yahawah your Alahayam,

who went panayam (before) you in the darak (way), to seek you out a place to pitch your chanah (tents) in, in ash (fire) by layal (night), to show you by what darak (way) you should yalak (go), and in the cloud by yawamam (day).
Yahawah heard the qawal (voice) of your dabar (words), and was qatzap (angry), and swore, saying,
"Surely not one of these men of this rai (evil) dawar (generation) shall raah (see) the tawab (good) aratz (land), which I swore to nathan (give) to your abawath (fathers),

except Kalab the ban (son) of Yapanah: he shall raah (see) it; and to him will I nathan (give) the aratz (land) that he has trodden on, and to his children, because he has malaa (wholly) followed Yahawah.
Also Yahawah was angry with me for your sakes, saying, "You also shall not bawaa (go) in there:
Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan, who imad (stands) panayam (before) you, he shall bawaa (go) in there: chazaq (encourage) you him; for he shall cause Yasharaal (Israel) to nachal (inherit) it.

Moreover your little ones, whom you said should be a prey, and your children, who this yawam (day) have no yadai (knowledge) of tawab (good) or rai (evil), they shall bawaa (go) in there, and to them will I nathan (give) it, and they shall yarash (possess) it.
But as for you, panah (turn), and take your nasai (journey) into the madabar (wilderness) by the darak (way) to the Red yam (sea).

Then you answered and said to me, "We have sinned against Yahawah, we will ilah (go) up and fight, according to all that Yahawah our Alahayam tzawah (commanded) us." Every ayash (man) of you put on his weapons of war, and presumed to ilah (go) up into the har (hill) country.
Yahawah said to me, "amar (tell) them, ‘Don't ilah (go) up, neither fight; for I am not qarab (among) you; lest you be struck panayam (before) your ayab (enemies).'
So I spoke to you, and you didn't listen; but you rebelled against the commandment of Yahawah, and were presumptuous, and went up into the har (hill) country.
The Amaray (Amorites), who lived in that har (hill) country, came out qaraah (against) you, and chased you, as bees do, and kathath (beat) you down in Shaiyar, even to Charamah.
You returned and wept panayam (before) Yahawah; but Yahawah didn't listen to your qawal (voice), nor gave ear to you.
So you stayed in Qadash many yawam (days), according to the yawam (days) that you remained.
Then we turned, and took our nasai (journey) into the madabar (wilderness) by the darak (way) to the Red yam (sea), as Yahawah spoke to me; and we encircled har (mount) Shaiyar many yawam (days).
Yahawah spoke to me, saying,
"You have encircled this har (mountain) rab (long) enough. panah (turn) northward.

tzawah (command) the im (people), saying, ‘You are to ibar (pass) through the border of your ach (brothers) the children of Ishaw, who yashab (dwell) in Shaiyar; and they will be yaraa (afraid) of you: take maad (good) shamar (heed) to yourselves therefore;

don't contend with them; for I will not nathan (give) you of their aratz (land), no, not so much as for the sole of the ragal (foot) to tread on; because I have given har (mount) Shaiyar to Ishaw for a yarashah (possession).
You shall purchase food of them for kasap (money), that you may akal (eat); and you shall also buy mayam (water) of them for kasap (money), that you may drink.'

For Yahawah your Alahayam has blessed you in all the maishah (work) of your yad (hand); he has yadai (known) your yalak (walking) through this gadawal (great) madabar (wilderness): these arabaiyam (forty) Shanah Yahawah your Alahayam has been with you; you have lacked nothing.

So we passed by from our ach (brothers) the children of Ishaw, who yashab (dwell) in Shaiyar, from the darak (way) of the irabah (arabah) from Ayalawath and from Itzayawanagabar Geber. We turned and passed by the darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness) of Mawaab.

Yahawah said to me, "Don't bother Mawaab, neither contend with them in battle; for I will not nathan (give) you of his aratz (land) for a yarashah (possession); because I have given Ir to the children of Lawat for a yarashah (possession).
(The Ayamayam (Emim) lived therein panayam (before), a im (people) gadawal (great), and many, and tall, as the Inaqay (Anakim):
these also are accounted Rapaa (Rephaim), as the Inaqay (Anakim); but the Mawaabay (Moabites) qaraa (call) them Ayamayam (Emim).

The Charay (Horites) also lived in Shaiyar panayam (before), but the children of Ishaw succeeded them; and they destroyed them from panayam (before) them, and lived in their place; as Yasharaal (Israel) did to the aratz (land) of his yarashah (possession), which Yahawah gave to them.)
"Now qawam (rise) up, and cross over the nachal (brook) Zarad." We went over the nachal (brook) Zarad.

The yawam (days) in which we came Qadashabaranai Kadesh Barnea, until we had halak (come) over the nachal (brook) Zarad, were shalawashayam (thirty) - shamanah (eight) Shanah; until all the dawar (generation) of the men of war were consumed from the qarab (midst) of the machanah (camp), as Yahawah swore to them.
Moreover the yad (hand) of Yahawah was against them, to hamam (destroy) them from the qarab (midst) of the machanah (camp), until they were consumed.
So it happened, when all the men of war were consumed and mawath (dead) from qarab (among) the im (people),
that Yahawah spoke to me, saying,
"You are this day to ibar (pass) over Ir, the border of Mawaab:

and when you qarab (come) near over against the children of Imawan, don't bother them, nor contend with them; for I will not nathan (give) you of the aratz (land) of the children of Imawan for a yarashah (possession); because I have given it to the children of Lawat for a yarashah (possession).
(That also is accounted a aratz (land) of Rapaa (Rephaim): Rapaa (Rephaim) lived therein panayam (before); but the Imawanay (Ammonites) qaraa (call) them Zamazam (Zamzummim),
a im (people) gadawal (great), and many, and tall, as the Inaqay (Anakim); but Yahawah destroyed them panayam (before) them; and they succeeded them, and lived in their yashab (place);

as he did for the children of Ishaw, who yashab (dwell) in Shaiyar, when he destroyed the Charay (Horites) from panayam (before) them; and they succeeded them, and lived in their place even to this yawam (day):
and the Iwayam (Avvim), who lived in villages as far as Izah, the Kapatharay (Caphtorim), who came yatzaa (forth) out of Kapathar, destroyed them, and lived in their yashab (place).)

"qawam (rise) up, take your nasai (journey), and ibar (pass) over the nachal (valley) of the Aranawan: raah (see), I have given into your yad (hand) Sayachawan the Amaray (Amorite), malak (king) of Chashabawan, and his aratz (land); chalal (begin) to yarash (possess) it, and contend with him in battle.

This yawam (day) will I chalal (begin) to nathan (put) the pachad (dread) of you and the yaraah (fear) of you on the peoples who are under the whole sky, who shall hear the report of you, and shall tremble, and be in anguish panayam (because) of you.
I sent malaak (messengers) out of the madabar (wilderness) of Qadamawath to Sayachawan malak (king) of Chashabawan with dabar (words) of shalawam (peace), saying,
"Let me ibar (pass) through your aratz (land): I will yalak (go) darak (along) by the highway, I will sawar (turn) neither to the right yamayan (hand) nor to the shamaawal (left).
You shall sell me food for kasap (money), that I may akal (eat); and nathan (give) me mayam (water) for kasap (money), that I may drink: only let me ibar (pass) through on my feet,

as the children of Ishaw who yashab (dwell) in Shaiyar, and the Mawaabay (Moabites) who yashab (dwell) in Ir, did to me; until I shall ibar (pass) over the Yaradan into the aratz (land) which Yahawah our Alahayam nathan (gives) us.

But Sayachawan malak (king) of Chashabawan would not let us ibar (pass) by him; for Yahawah your Alahayam hardened his rawach (spirit), and made his labab (heart) amatz (obstinate), that he might nathan (deliver) him into your yad (hand), as at this yawam (day).

Yahawah said to me, "raah (see), I have begun to nathan (deliver) up Sayachawan and his aratz (land) panayam (before) you: chalal (begin) to yarash (possess), that you may yarash (inherit) his aratz (land).
Then Sayachawan came out qaraah (against) us, he and all his im (people), to battle at Yahatz.
Yahawah our Alahayam delivered him up panayam (before) us; and we struck him, and his ban (sons), and all his im (people).
We took all his Iyar at that ith (time), and charam (utterly) destroyed every inhabited Iyar, with the women and the little ones; we shaar (left) none sharayad (remaining):
only the livestock we took for a prey to ourselves, with the spoil of the Iyar which we had taken.

From Irawair, which is on the shapah (edge) of the nachal (valley) of the Aranawan, and the Iyar that is in the nachal (valley), even to Galaid, there was not a city too high for us; Yahawah our Alahayam delivered up all panayam (before) us:

only to the aratz (land) of the children of Imawan you didn't qarab (come) yad (near); all the side of the nachal (river) Yabaq, and the Iyar of the har (hill) country, and wherever Yahawah our Alahayam forbade us.
Then we turned, and went up the darak (way) to Bashan: and Iwag the malak (king) of Bashan came out qaraah (against) us, he and all his im (people), to battle at Adaraiy.

Yahawah said to me, "Don't yaraa (fear) him; for I have delivered him, and all his im (people), and his aratz (land), into your yad (hand); and you shall do to him as you did to Sayachawan malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), who lived at Chashabawan.
So Yahawah our Alahayam delivered into our yad (hand) Iwag also, the malak (king) of Bashan, and all his im (people): and we struck him until none was shaar (left) to him sharayad (remaining).
We took all his Iyar at that ith (time); there was not a city which we didn't take from them; shashayam (sixty) Iyar, all the region of Aragab, the mamalakah (kingdom) of Iwag in Bashan.
All these were Iyar fortified with Gabah walls, gates, and bars; besides the unwalled Iyar a maad (great) many.
We charam (utterly) destroyed them, as we did to Sayachawan malak (king) of Chashabawan, charam (utterly) destroying every inhabited Iyar, with the women and the little ones.
But all the livestock, and the spoil of the Iyar, we took for a prey to ourselves.

We took the aratz (land) at that ith (time) out of the yad (hand) of the shanayam (two) malak (kings) of the Amaray (Amorites) who were ibar (beyond) the Yaradan, from the nachal (valley) of the Aranawan to har (mount) Charamawan.
(The Tzayadanay (Sidonians) qaraa (call) Charamawan Sharayawan, and the Amaray (Amorites) qaraa (call) it Shanayar.)
We took all the Iyar of the mayashawar (plain), and all Galaid, and all Bashan, Salakah Salecah and Adaraiy, Iyar of the mamalakah (kingdom) of Iwag in Bashan.

(For only Iwag malak (king) of Bashan remained of the yathar (remnant) of the Rapaa (Rephaim); behold, his bedstead was a bedstead of barazal (iron); isn't it in Rabah of the children of Imawan? thashai (nine) amah (cubits) was its arak (length), and arabai (four) amah (cubits) its breadth, after the amah (cubit) of a ayash (man).)

This aratz (land) we took in yarash (possession) at that ith (time): from Irawair, which is by the nachal (valley) of the Aranawan, and chatzay (half) the har (hill) country of Galaid, and its Iyar, gave I to the Raawabanay (Reubenites) and to the Gaday (Gadites):

and the yathar (rest) of Galaid, and all Bashan, the mamalakah (kingdom) of Iwag, gave I to the chatzay (half) - shabat (tribe) of Manashah; all the region of Aragab, even all Bashan. (The same is called the aratz (land) of Rapaa (Rephaim).

Yaayar the ban (son) of Manashah took all the region of Aragab, to the border of the Gashawaray (Geshurites) and the Maikathay (Maacathites), and called them, even Bashan, after his own sham (name), Havvoth Jair, to this yawam (day).)
I gave Galaid to Makayar.

To the Raawabanay (Reubenites) and to the Gaday (Gadites) I gave from Galaid even to the nachal (valley) of the Aranawan, the middle of the nachal (valley), and its border, even to the nachal (river) Yabaq, which is the border of the children of Imawan;
the irabah (arabah) also, and the Yaradan and its border, from Kanarawath even to the yam (sea) of the irabah (arabah), the Malach yam (sea), under the slopes of Pisgah eastward.

I tzawah (commanded) you at that ith (time), saying, "Yahawah your Alahayam has given you this aratz (land) to yarash (possess) it: you shall ibar (pass) over chalatz (armed) panayam (before) your ach (brothers) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), all the men of valor.
But your wives, and your little ones, and your livestock, (I yadai (know) that you have much livestock), shall live in your Iyar which I have given you,

until Yahawah gives nawach (rest) to your ach (brothers), as to you, and they also yarash (possess) the aratz (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) them ibar (beyond) the Yaradan: then you shall shawab (turn back / repent) every ayash (man) to his yarashah (possession), which I have given you.

I tzawah (commanded) Yahawashawai at that ith (time), saying, "Your iyan (eyes) have seen all that Yahawah your Alahayam has done to these shanayam (two) malak (kings): so shall Yahawah do to all the mamalakah (kingdoms) where you ibar (go) over.
You shall not yaraa (fear) them; for Yahawah your Alahayam, he it is who fights for you.
I begged Yahawah at that ith (time), saying,

"Adanay Yahawah, you have begun to show your ibad (servant) your greatness, and your chazaq (strong) yad (hand): for what Al is there in shamayam (heaven) or in aratz (earth), that can do according to your maishah (works), and according to your gabawarah (mighty) acts?
Please let me ibar (go) over and raah (see) the tawab (good) aratz (land) that is ibar (beyond) the Yaradan, that goodly har (mountain), and Labanawan.
But Yahawah was angry with me for your sakes, and didn't listen to me; and Yahawah said to me, "Let it rab (suffice) you; dabar (speak) no more to me of this dabar (matter).

ilah (go) up to the raash (top) of Pasagah, and nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eyes) westward, and northward, and southward, and eastward, and raah (see) with your iyan (eyes): for you shall not ibar (go) over this Yaradan.

But commission Yahawashawai, and chazaq (encourage) him, and amatz (strengthen) him; for he shall ibar (go) over panayam (before) this im (people), and he shall nachal (cause) them to inherit the aratz (land) which you shall raah (see).
So we stayed in the Gayaa over against Bayathapaiwar Peor.

Now, Yasharaal (Israel), listen to the chaq (statutes) and to the mashapat (ordinances), which I teach you, to do them; that you may chayah (live), and bawaa (go) in and yarash (possess) the aratz (land) which Yahawah, the Alahayam of your abawath (fathers), nathan (gives) you.

You shall not add to the dabar (word) which I tzawah (command) you, neither shall you diminish from it, that you may shamar (keep) the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah your Alahayam which I tzawah (command) you.
Your iyan (eyes) have seen what Yahawah did because of Bailapaiwar Peor; for all the men who followed Bailapaiwar Peor, Yahawah your Alahayam has destroyed them from the qarab (midst) of you.
Dabaq you who were faithful to Yahawah your Alahayam are all chay (alive) this yawam (day).

raah (see), I have taught you chaq (statutes) and mashapat (ordinances), even as Yahawah my Alahayam tzawah (commanded) me, that you should do so in the midst of the aratz (land) where you bawaa (go) in to yarash (possess) it.

shamar (keep) therefore and do them; for this is your chakamah (wisdom) and your bayanah (understanding) in the iyan (sight) of the im (peoples), who shall hear all these chaq (statutes), and amar (say), "Surely this gadawal (great) gaway (nation) is a chakam (wise) and bayan (understanding) im (people).
For what gadawal (great) gaway (nation) is there, that has a Alahayam so qarawab (near) to them, as Yahawah our Alahayam is whenever we qaraa (call) on him?

What gadawal (great) gaway (nation) is there, that has chaq (statutes) and mashapat (ordinances) so tzadayaq (righteous) as all this thawarah (law), which I nathan (set) panayam (before) you this yawam (day)?

Only shamar (take) heed to yourself, and shamar (keep) your napash (soul) maad (diligently), lest you forget the things which your iyan (eyes) saw, and lest they sawar (depart) from your labab (heart) all the yawam (days) of your chay (life); but yadai (make) them known to your children and your children's children;

the yawam (day) that you stood panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam in Charab, when Yahawah said to me, "Assemble me the im (people), and I will make them hear my dabar (words), that they may learn to yaraa (fear) me all the yawam (days) that they chay (live) on the adamah (earth), and that they may teach their children.
You came qarab (near) and stood under the har (mountain); and the har (mountain) burned with ash (fire) to the lab (heart) of the sky, with irapal (darkness), cloud, and thick chashak (darkness).
Yahawah spoke to you out of the midst of the ash (fire): you heard the qawal (voice) of dabar (words), but you saw no form; you only heard a qawal (voice).
He declared to you his barayath (covenant), which he tzawah (commanded) you to ishah (perform), even the ishar (ten) commandments; and he wrote them on shanayam (two) tables of aban (stone).
Yahawah tzawah (commanded) me at that ith (time) to teach you chaq (statutes) and mashapat (ordinances), that you might do them in the aratz (land) where you ibar (go) over to yarash (possess) it.
Take therefore maad (good) shamar (heed) to yourselves; for you saw no kind of form on the yawam (day) that Yahawah spoke to you in Charab out of the midst of the ash (fire).
Lest you shachath (corrupt) yourselves, and ishah (make) yourself an engraved pasal (image) in the form of any samal (figure), the thabanayath (likeness) of zakar (male) or female,
the thabanayath (likeness) of any animal that is on the aratz (earth), the thabanayath (likeness) of any winged bird that flies in the sky,
the thabanayath (likeness) of anything that creeps on the adamah (ground), the thabanayath (likeness) of any fish that is in the mayam (water) under the aratz (earth);

and lest you nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eyes) to the sky, and when you raah (see) the shamash (sun) and the yarach (moon) and the kawakab (stars), even all the tzabaa (army) of the sky, you are drawn away and shachah (worship) them, and ibad (serve) them, which Yahawah your Alahayam has allotted to all the im (peoples) under the whole sky.
But Yahawah has taken you, and brought you yatzaa (forth) out of the barazal (iron) furnace, out of Matzarayam, to be to him a im (people) of nachalah (inheritance), as at this yawam (day).

Furthermore Yahawah was angry with me for your dabar (sakes), and swore that I should not ibar (go) over the Yaradan, and that I should not bawaa (go) in to that tawab (good) aratz (land), which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you for an nachalah (inheritance):
but I must mawath (die) in this aratz (land), I must not ibar (go) over the Yaradan; but you shall ibar (go) over, and yarash (possess) that tawab (good) aratz (land).

shamar (take) heed to yourselves, lest you forget the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah your Alahayam, which he made with you, and ishah (make) you an engraved pasal (image) in the form of anything which Yahawah your Alahayam has forbidden you.
For Yahawah your Alahayam is a devouring ash (fire), a Qanaa Alahayam.

When you shall father children, and children's children, and you shall have been yashan (long) in the aratz (land), and shall shachath (corrupt) yourselves, and ishah (make) an engraved pasal (image) in the form of anything, and shall do that which is rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah your Alahayam, to provoke him to kais (anger);

I iwad (call) shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth) to iwad (witness) against you this yawam (day), that you shall Mahar abad (utterly) abad (perish) from off the aratz (land) whereunto you ibar (go) over the Yaradan to yarash (possess) it; you shall not prolong your yawam (days) on it, but shall shamad (utterly) be destroyed.
Yahawah will scatter you among the im (peoples), and you shall be shaar (left) few in number among the gawayam (nations), where Yahawah shall lead you away.
There you shall ibad (serve) Alahayam, the maishah (work) of men's yad (hands), itz (wood) and aban (stone), which neither raah (see), nor hear, nor akal (eat), nor rawach (smell).
But from there you shall seek Yahawah your Alahayam, and you shall matzaa (find) him, when you search after him with all your labab (heart) and with all your napash (soul).

When you are in oppression, and all these things have matzaa (come) on you, in the acharayath (latter) yawam (days) you shall shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah your Alahayam, and listen to his qawal (voice):
for Yahawah your Alahayam is a Rachawam Alahayam; he will not rapah (fail) you, neither shachath (destroy) you, nor forget the barayath (covenant) of your abawath (fathers) which he swore to them.

For shaal (ask) now of the yawam (days) that are raashawan (past), which were panayam (before) you, since the yawam (day) that Alahayam created adam (man) on the aratz (earth), and from the qatzah (one) end of the sky to the other, whether there has been anything as this gadawal (great) thing is, or has been heard like it?
Did a im (people) ever hear the qawal (voice) of Alahayam speaking out of the midst of the ash (fire), as you have heard, and chayah (live)?

Or has Alahayam tried to bawaa (go) and take a gaway (nation) for himself from the qarab (midst) of another gaway (nation), by Masah, by awath (signs), and by mawapath (wonders), and by war, and by a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and by an natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm), and by gadawal (great) mawaraa (terrors), according to all that Yahawah your Alahayam did for you in Matzarayam before your iyan (eyes)?
It was shown to you so that you might yadai (know) that Yahawah is Alahayam. There is no one iwad (else) bad (besides) him.

Out of shamayam (heaven) he made you to hear his qawal (voice), that he might instruct you: and on aratz (earth) he made you to raah (see) his gadawal (great) ash (fire); and you heard his dabar (words) out of the midst of the ash (fire).

Because he loved your abawath (fathers), therefore he chose their zarai (seed) achar (after) them, and brought you out with his panayam (presence), with his gadawal (great) kach (power), out of Matzarayam;

to yarash (drive) out gawayam (nations) from panayam (before) you greater and mightier than you, to bawaa (bring) you in, to nathan (give) you their aratz (land) for an nachalah (inheritance), as at this yawam (day).

yadai (know) therefore this yawam (day), and shawab (turn back / repent) it to your labab (heart), that Yahawah he is Alahayam in shamayam (heaven) above and on the aratz (earth) beneath; there is none else.

You shall shamar (keep) his chaq (statutes), and his matzawah (commandments), which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), that it may yatab (go) well with you, and with your children achar (after) you, and that you may prolong your yawam (days) in the adamah (land), which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you, forever.
Then Mashah set apart shalawash (three) Iyar ibar (beyond) the Yaradan toward the sunrise;

that the manslayer might flee there, who ratzach (kills) his neighbor unawares, and didn't shanaa (hate) him in thamawal (time) shalashawam (past); and that fleeing to one of these Iyar he might chayay (live):

Batzar in the madabar (wilderness), in the mayashawar (plain) aratz (country), for the Raawabanay (Reubenites); and Raamawath in Galaid, for the Gaday (Gadites); and Gawalan in Bashan, for the Manashay (Manassites).
This is the thawarah (law) which Mashah shawam (set) panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel):
these are the idah (testimonies), and the chaq (statutes), and the mashapat (ordinances), which Mashah spoke to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), when they came yatzaa (forth) out of Matzarayam,

ibar (beyond) the Yaradan, in the Gayaa over against Bayathapaiwar Peor, in the aratz (land) of Sayachawan malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), who lived at Chashabawan, whom Mashah and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) struck, when they came yatzaa (forth) out of Matzarayam.

They took his aratz (land) in yarash (possession), and the aratz (land) of Iwag malak (king) of Bashan, the shanayam (two) malak (kings) of the Amaray (Amorites), who were ibar (beyond) the Yaradan toward the sunrise;
from Irawair, which is on the shapah (edge) of the nachal (valley) of the Aranawan, even to har (mount) Shayaan (the same is Charamawan),
and all the irabah (arabah) ibar (beyond) the Yaradan eastward, even to the yam (sea) of the irabah (arabah), under the slopes of Pasagah.

Mashah called to all Yasharaal (Israel), and said to them, Hear, Yasharaal (Israel), the chaq (statutes) and the mashapat (ordinances) which I dabar (speak) in your ears this yawam (day), that you may learn them, and shamar (observe) to do them.
Yahawah our Alahayam made a barayath (covenant) with us in Charab.
Yahawah didn't karath (make) this barayath (covenant) with our abawath (fathers), but with us, even us, who are all of us here chay (alive) this yawam (day).
Yahawah spoke with you panayam (face) to panayam (face) on the har (mountain) out of the midst of the ash (fire),

(I stood between Yahawah and you at that ith (time), to show you the dabar (word) of Yahawah: for you were yaraa (afraid) panayam (because) of the ash (fire), and didn't ilah (go) up onto the har (mountain);) saying,
"I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who brought you out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, out of the bayath (house) of ibad (bondage).
"You shall have no other Alahayam panayam (before) me.

"You shall not ishah (make) an engraved pasal (image) for yourself, any thamawanah (likeness) of what is in shamayam (heaven) above, or what is in the aratz (earth) beneath, or that is in the mayam (water) under the aratz (earth):

you shall not shachah (bow) down yourself to them, nor ibad (serve) them; for I, Yahawah, your Alahayam, am a Qanaa Alahayam, visiting the iwan (iniquity) of the abawath (fathers) on the children, and on the shalash (third) and on the rabai (fourth) generation of those who shanaa (hate) me;
and showing loving chasad (kindness) to alap (thousands) of those who ahab (love) me and shamar (keep) my matzawah (commandments).
"You shall not nashaa (take) the sham (name) of Yahawah your Alahayam in vain: for Yahawah will not hold him guiltless who nashaa (takes) his sham (name) in vain.
"shamar (observe) the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day), to shamar (keep) it holy, as Yahawah your Alahayam tzawah (commanded) you.
You shall labor shash (six) yawam (days), and do all your malaakah (work);

but the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) is a shabath (sabbath) to Yahawah your Alahayam, in which you shall not do any malaakah (work), you, nor your ban (son), nor your bath (daughter), nor your male ibad (servant), nor your female amah (servant), nor your ox, nor your donkey, nor any of your livestock, nor your stranger who is within your gates; that your male ibad (servant) and your female amah (servant) may nawach (rest) as well as you.

You shall zakar (remember) that you were a ibad (servant) in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and Yahawah your Alahayam brought you out of there by a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand) and by an natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm): therefore Yahawah your Alahayam tzawah (commanded) you to ishah (keep) the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day).

"Honor your ab (father) and your am (mother), as Yahawah your Alahayam tzawah (commanded) you; that your yawam (days) may be long, and that it may yatab (go) well with you, in the adamah (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you.
"You shall not ratzach (murder).
"Neither shall you naap (commit) adultery.
"Neither shall you steal.
"Neither shall you give false id (testimony) against your neighbor.

"Neither shall you covet your neighbor's ashah (wife); neither shall you desire your neighbor's bayath (house), his shadah (field), or his male ibad (servant), or his female amah (servant), his ox, or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbor's.

These dabar (words) Yahawah spoke to all your qahal (assembly) on the har (mountain) out of the midst of the ash (fire), of the cloud, and of the thick irapal (darkness), with a gadawal (great) qawal (voice): and he added no more. He wrote them on shanayam (two) tables of aban (stone), and gave them to me.

It happened, when you heard the qawal (voice) out of the midst of the chashak (darkness), while the har (mountain) was burning with ash (fire), that you came qarab (near) to me, even all the raash (heads) of your shabat (tribes), and your zaqan (elders);

and you said, "Behold, Yahawah our Alahayam has shown us his kabawad (glory) and his greatness, and we have heard his qawal (voice) out of the midst of the ash (fire): we have seen this yawam (day) that Alahayam does dabar (speak) with adam (man), and he chayay (lives).
Now therefore why should we mawath (die)? For this gadawal (great) ash (fire) will akal (consume) us: if we hear the qawal (voice) of Yahawah our Alahayam any more, then we shall mawath (die).
For who is there of all flesh, that has heard the qawal (voice) of the chay (living) Alahayam speaking out of the midst of the ash (fire), as we have, and lived?
qarab (go) near, and hear all that Yahawah our Alahayam shall amar (say): and amar (tell) us all that Yahawah our Alahayam shall dabar (tell) you; and we will hear it, and do it.

Yahawah heard the qawal (voice) of your dabar (words), when you spoke to me; and Yahawah said to me, "I have heard the qawal (voice) of the dabar (words) of this im (people), which they have spoken to you: they have yatab (well) said all that they have spoken.

Oh that there were such a labab (heart) in them, that they would yaraa (fear) me, and shamar (keep) all my matzawah (commandments) yawam (always), that it might be yatab (well) with them, and with their children iwalam (forever)!
"yalak (go) amar (tell) them, shawab (turn back / repent) to your ahal (tents).

But as for you, imad (stand) here by me, and I will dabar (tell) you all the matzawah (commandment), and the chaq (statutes), and the mashapat (ordinances), which you shall teach them, that they may do them in the aratz (land) which I nathan (give) them to yarash (possess) it.
You shall shamar (observe) to do therefore as Yahawah your Alahayam has tzawah (commanded) you: you shall not sawar (turn) aside to the right yamayan (hand) or to the shamaawal (left).

You shall yalak (walk) in all the darak (way) which Yahawah your Alahayam has tzawah (commanded) you, that you may chayah (live), and that it may be tawab (well) with you, and that you may prolong your yawam (days) in the aratz (land) which you shall yarash (possess).

Now this is the matzawah (commandment), the chaq (statutes), and the mashapat (ordinances), which Yahawah your Alahayam tzawah (commanded) to teach you, that you might do them in the aratz (land) where you ibar (go) over to yarash (possess) it;

that you might yaraa (fear) Yahawah your Alahayam, to shamar (keep) all his chaqah (statutes) and his matzawah (commandments), which I tzawah (command) you, you, and your ban (son), and your ban (son's) ban (son), all the yawam (days) of your chay (life); and that your yawam (days) may be prolonged.

Hear therefore, Yasharaal (Israel), and shamar (observe) to do it; that it may be yatab (well) with you, and that you may increase mightily, as Yahawah, the Alahayam of your abawath (fathers), has promised to you, in a aratz (land) flowing with milk and honey.
Hear, Yasharaal (Israel): Yahawah is our Alahayam; Yahawah is one:
and you shall ahab (love) Yahawah your Alahayam with all your labab (heart), and with all your napash (soul), and with all your might.
These dabar (words), which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), shall be on your labab (heart);

and you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall dabar (talk) of them when you yashab (sit) in your bayath (house), and when you yalak (walk) by the darak (way), and when you shakab (lie) down, and when you qawam (rise) up.
You shall qashar (bind) them for a awath (sign) on your yad (hand), and they shall be for symbols between your iyan (eyes).
You shall kathab (write) them on the door posts of your bayath (house), and on your gates.

It shall be, when Yahawah your Alahayam shall bawaa (bring) you into the aratz (land) which he swore to your abawath (fathers), to Abaraham, to Yatzachaq, and to Yaiqab, to nathan (give) you, gadawal (great) and goodly Iyar, which you didn't banah (build),

and bayath (houses) Malaa of all tawab (good) things, which you didn't malaa (fill), and bawar (cisterns) dug out, which you didn't chatzab (dig), vineyards and olive trees, which you didn't plant, and you shall akal (eat) and be full;
then beware lest you forget Yahawah, who brought you yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, out of the bayath (house) of ibad (bondage).
You shall yaraa (fear) Yahawah your Alahayam; and you shall ibad (serve) him, and shall shabai (swear) by his sham (name).
You shall not yalak (go) achar (after) other Alahayam, of the Alahayam of the im (peoples) who are around you;

for Yahawah your Alahayam in the qarab (midst) of you is a Qanaa Al; lest the ap (anger) of Yahawah your Alahayam be kindled against you, and he destroy you from off the panayam (face) of the adamah (earth).
You shall not tempt Yahawah your Alahayam, as you tempted him in Masah.
You shall diligently shamar (keep) the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah your Alahayam, and his idah (testimonies), and his chaq (statutes), which he has tzawah (commanded) you.

You shall do that which is yashar (right) and tawab (good) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah; that it may be yatab (well) with you, and that you may bawaa (go) in and yarash (possess) the tawab (good) aratz (land) which Yahawah swore to your abawath (fathers),
to thrust out all your ayab (enemies) from panayam (before) you, as Yahawah has spoken.

When your ban (son) shaal (asks) you in time to come, saying, "What do the idah (testimonies), the chaq (statutes), and the mashapat (ordinances), which Yahawah our Alahayam has tzawah (commanded) you mean?
then you shall amar (tell) your ban (son), "We were Paraih ibad (bondservants) in Matzarayam: and Yahawah brought us out of Matzarayam with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand);
and Yahawah showed gadawal (great) and awesome awath (signs) and mawapath (wonders) on Matzarayam, on Paraih, and on all his bayath (house), before our iyan (eyes);
and he brought us out from there, that he might bawaa (bring) us in, to nathan (give) us the aratz (land) which he swore to our abawath (fathers).

Yahawah tzawah (commanded) us to do all these chaq (statutes), to yaraa (fear) Yahawah our Alahayam, for our tawab (good) yawam (always), that he might chayah (preserve) us alive, as at this yawam (day).
It shall be tzadaqah (righteousness) to us, if we shamar (observe) to do all this matzawah (commandment) panayam (before) Yahawah our Alahayam, as he has tzawah (commanded) us.

When Yahawah your Alahayam shall bawaa (bring) you into the aratz (land) where you bawaa (go) to yarash (possess) it, and shall cast out many gawayam (nations) panayam (before) you, the Chathay (Hittite), and the Garagashay (Girgashite), and the Amaray (Amorite), and the Kanainay (Canaanite), and the Parazay (Perizzite), and the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite), shabai (seven) gawayam (nations) greater and mightier than you;

and when Yahawah your Alahayam shall nathan (deliver) them up panayam (before) you, and you shall strike them; then you shall charam (utterly) charam (destroy) them: you shall karath (make) no barayath (covenant) with them, nor show chanan (mercy) to them;
neither shall you chathan (make) marriages with them; your bath (daughter) you shall not nathan (give) to his ban (son), nor shall you take his bath (daughter) for your ban (son).
For he will sawar (turn) away your ban (son) from following me, that they may ibad (serve) other Alahayam: so the ap (anger) of Yahawah would be kindled against you, and he would destroy you Mahar.

But you shall ishah (deal) with them like this: you shall shabar (break) down their mazabach (altars), and dash their matzabah (pillars) in pieces, and cut down their Asharah, and sharap (burn) their engraved pasayal (images) with ash (fire).

For you are a qadawash (holy) im (people) to Yahawah your Alahayam: Yahawah your Alahayam has chosen you to be a im (people) for his own sagalah (possession), above all im (peoples) who are on the panayam (face) of the adamah (earth).
Yahawah didn't set his chashaq (love) on you, nor choose you, because you were more in number than any im (people); Mait you were the fewest of all im (peoples):

but because Yahawah loves you, and because he would shamar (keep) the shabawaih (oath) which he swore to your abawath (fathers), has Yahawah brought you out with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and padah (redeemed) you out of the bayath (house) of ibad (bondage), from the yad (hand) of Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam.

yadai (know) therefore that Yahawah your Alahayam, he is Alahayam, the aman (faithful) Alahayam, who shamar (keeps) barayath (covenant) and loving chasad (kindness) with them who ahab (love) him and shamar (keep) his matzawah (commandments) to a alap (thousand) dawar (generations),
and shalam (repays) those who shanaa (hate) him to their panayam (face), to abad (destroy) them: he will not be slack to him who shanaa (hates) him, he will shalam (repay) him to his panayam (face).
You shall therefore shamar (keep) the matzawah (commandment), and the chaq (statutes), and the mashapat (ordinances), which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), to do them.

It shall happen, because you listen to these mashapat (ordinances), and shamar (keep) and do them, that Yahawah your Alahayam will shamar (keep) with you the barayath (covenant) and the loving chasad (kindness) which he swore to your abawath (fathers):

and he will ahab (love) you, and barak (bless) you, and multiply you; he will also barak (bless) the fruit of your body and the fruit of your adamah (ground), your grain and your new thayarawash (wine) and your yatzahar (oil), the increase of your livestock and the Ishatharah of your flock, in the adamah (land) which he swore to your abawath (fathers) to nathan (give) you.
You shall be blessed above all im (peoples): Iqar shall not be male or female Iqar among you, or among your livestock.

Yahawah will sawar (take) away from you all sickness; and none of the rai (evil) diseases of Matzarayam, which you yadai (know), he will shawam (put) on you, but will nathan (lay) them on all those who shanaa (hate) you.

You shall akal (consume) all the im (peoples) whom Yahawah your Alahayam shall nathan (deliver) to you; your iyan (eye) shall not pity them: neither shall you ibad (serve) their Alahayam; for that will be a snare to you.
If you shall amar (say) in your labab (heart), "These gawayam (nations) are more than I; how can I yarash (dispossess) them?
you shall not be yaraa (afraid) of them: you shall zakar (well) zakar (remember) what Yahawah your Alahayam did to Paraih, and to all Matzarayam;

the gadawal (great) Masah which your iyan (eyes) saw, and the awath (signs), and the mawapath (wonders), and the chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and the natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm), by which Yahawah your Alahayam brought you out: so shall Yahawah your Alahayam do to all the im (peoples) of whom you are yaraa (afraid).
Moreover Yahawah your Alahayam will shalach (send) the hornet among them, until those who are shaar (left), and hide themselves, abad (perish) from panayam (before) you.
You shall not be scared of them; for Yahawah your Alahayam is in the qarab (midst) of you, a gadawal (great) and awesome Al.
Yahawah your Alahayam will cast out those gawayam (nations) panayam (before) you by Mait and Mait: you may not kalah (consume) them at Mahar, lest the animals of the shadah (field) increase on you.
But Yahawah your Alahayam will nathan (deliver) them up panayam (before) you, and will confuse them with a gadawal (great) mahawamah (confusion), until they be destroyed.

He will nathan (deliver) their malak (kings) into your yad (hand), and you shall make their sham (name) to abad (perish) from under the sky: no ayash (man) shall be able to stand panayam (before) you, until you have destroyed them.

You shall sharap (burn) the engraved pasayal (images) of their Alahayam with ash (fire). You shall not covet the kasap (silver) or the gold that is on them, nor take it for yourself, lest you be snared in it; for it is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah your Alahayam.

You shall not bawaa (bring) an thawaibah (abomination) into your bayath (house), and become a charam (devoted) thing like it. You shall shaqatz (utterly) shaqatz (detest) it, and you shall shaqatz (utterly) abhor it; for it is a charam (devoted) thing.

You shall shamar (observe) to do all the matzawah (commandment) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), that you may chayah (live), and multiply, and bawaa (go) in and yarash (possess) the aratz (land) which Yahawah swore to your abawath (fathers).

You shall zakar (remember) all the darak (way) which Yahawah your Alahayam has led you these arabaiyam (forty) Shanah in the madabar (wilderness), that he might humble you, to prove you, to yadai (know) what was in your labab (heart), whether you would shamar (keep) his matzawah (commandments), or not.

He humbled you, and allowed you to be hungry, and fed you with manna, which you didn't yadai (know), neither did your abawath (fathers) yadai (know); that he might yadai (make) you know that adam (man) does not chayah (live) by lacham (bread) only, but adam (man) chayah (lives) by everything that proceeds out of the pah (mouth) of Yahawah.
Your clothing didn't grow old on you, neither did your ragal (foot) swell, these arabaiyam (forty) Shanah.
You shall yadai (consider) in your labab (heart) that as a ayash (man) chastens his ban (son), so Yahawah your Alahayam chastens you.
You shall shamar (keep) the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah your Alahayam, to yalak (walk) in his darak (ways), and to yaraa (fear) him.

For Yahawah your Alahayam bawaa (brings) you into a tawab (good) aratz (land), a aratz (land) of nachal (brooks) of mayam (water), of springs, and underground mayam (water) flowing into Baqaih and har (hills);
a aratz (land) of wheat and barley, and vines and fig trees and pomegranates; a aratz (land) of olive trees and honey;

a aratz (land) in which you shall akal (eat) lacham (bread) laa (without) scarceness, you shall not lack anything in it; a aratz (land) whose aban (stones) are barazal (iron), and out of whose harar (hills) you may chatzab (dig) copper.
You shall akal (eat) and be full, and you shall barak (bless) Yahawah your Alahayam for the tawab (good) aratz (land) which he has given you.
Beware lest you forget Yahawah your Alahayam, in not keeping his matzawah (commandments), and his mashapat (ordinances), and his chaqah (statutes), which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day):
lest, when you have eaten and are full, and have built goodly bayath (houses), and lived therein;
and when your herds and your flocks multiply, and your kasap (silver) and your gold is multiplied, and all that you have is multiplied;
then your labab (heart) be lifted up, and you forget Yahawah your Alahayam, who brought you yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, out of the bayath (house) of ibad (bondage);

who led you through the gadawal (great) and yaraa (terrible) madabar (wilderness), with sharap (fiery) serpents and scorpions, and tzamaawan (thirsty) ground where there was no mayam (water); who brought you yatzaa (forth) mayam (water) out of the tzawar (rock) of flint;

who fed you in the madabar (wilderness) with manna, which your abawath (fathers) didn't yadai (know); that he might humble you, and that he might prove you, to do you yatab (good) at your acharayath (latter) end:
