and lest you amar (say) in your labab (heart), "My kach (power) and the might of my yad (hand) has gotten me this wealth.

But you shall zakar (remember) Yahawah your Alahayam, for it is he who nathan (gives) you kach (power) to ishah (get) wealth; that he may qawam (establish) his barayath (covenant) which he swore to your abawath (fathers), as at this yawam (day).

It shall be, if you shall forget Yahawah your Alahayam, and halak (walk) achar (after) other Alahayam, and ibad (serve) them, and shachah (worship) them, I iwad (testify) against you this yawam (day) that you shall abad (surely) abad (perish).
As the gawayam (nations) that Yahawah makes to abad (perish) panayam (before) you, so you shall abad (perish); because you wouldn't listen to the qawal (voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam.

Hear, Yasharaal (Israel): you are to ibar (pass) over the Yaradan this yawam (day), to bawaa (go) in to yarash (dispossess) gawayam (nations) greater and mightier than yourself, Iyar gadawal (great) and fortified up to the sky,
a im (people) gadawal (great) and tall, the ban (sons) of the Inaqay (Anakim), whom you yadai (know), and of whom you have heard say, "Who can stand panayam (before) the ban (sons) of Inaq?

yadai (know) therefore this yawam (day), that Yahawah your Alahayam is he who goes over panayam (before) you as a devouring ash (fire); he will destroy them, and he will bring them down panayam (before) you: so you shall yarash (drive) them out, and make them to abad (perish) Mahar, as Yahawah has spoken to you.

Don't amar (say) in your labab (heart), after Yahawah your Alahayam has thrust them out from panayam (before) you, saying, "For my tzadaqah (righteousness) Yahawah has brought me in to yarash (possess) this aratz (land);" because Yahawah yarash (drives) them out panayam (before) you because of the rashaih (wickedness) of these gawayam (nations).

Not for your tzadaqah (righteousness), or for the yashar (uprightness) of your labab (heart), do you bawaa (go) in to yarash (possess) their aratz (land); but for the rashaih (wickedness) of these gawayam (nations) Yahawah your Alahayam does yarash (drive) them out from panayam (before) you, and that he may qawam (establish) the dabar (word) which Yahawah swore to your abawath (fathers), to Abaraham, to Yatzachaq, and to Yaiqab.

yadai (know) therefore, that Yahawah your Alahayam doesn't nathan (give) you this tawab (good) aratz (land) to yarash (possess) it for your tzadaqah (righteousness); for you are a stiff-necked im (people).

zakar (remember), don't forget, how you provoked Yahawah your Alahayam to qatzap (wrath) in the madabar (wilderness): from the yawam (day) that you went yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, until you came to this place, you have been rebellious against Yahawah.
Also in Charab you provoked Yahawah to qatzap (wrath), and Yahawah was angry with you to destroy you.

When I was gone up onto the har (mountain) to receive the tables of aban (stone), even the tables of the barayath (covenant) which Yahawah made with you, then I stayed on the har (mountain) arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights); I neither ate lacham (bread) nor drank mayam (water).

Yahawah delivered to me the shanayam (two) tables of aban (stone) written with the finger of Alahayam; and on them were all the dabar (words) which Yahawah spoke with you on the har (mountain) out of the midst of the ash (fire) in the yawam (day) of the qahal (assembly).

It came to pass at the end of arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights), that Yahawah gave me the shanayam (two) tables of aban (stone), even the tables of the barayath (covenant).

Yahawah said to me, "qawam (arise), yarad (get) down Mahar from here; for your im (people) whom you have brought out of Matzarayam have corrupted themselves; they have Mahar turned sawar (aside) out of the darak (way) which I tzawah (commanded) them; they have made them a molten masakah (image).
Furthermore Yahawah spoke to me, saying, "I have seen this im (people), and behold, it is a stiff-necked im (people):
let me rapah (alone), that I may destroy them, and machah (blot) out their sham (name) from under the sky; and I will ishah (make) of you a gaway (nation) mightier and greater than they.
So I turned and came down from the har (mountain), and the har (mountain) was burning with ash (fire): and the shanayam (two) tables of the barayath (covenant) were in my shanayam (two) yad (hands).

I looked, and behold, you had sinned against Yahawah your Alahayam; you had made yourselves a molten calf: you had turned sawar (aside) Mahar out of the darak (way) which Yahawah had tzawah (commanded) you.
I took hold of the shanayam (two) tables, and cast them out of my shanayam (two) yad (hands), and broke them before your iyan (eyes).

I napal (fell) down panayam (before) Yahawah, as at the raashawan (first), arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights); I neither ate lacham (bread) nor drank mayam (water); because of all your chataah (sin) which you sinned, in doing that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, to provoke him to kais (anger).
For I was yagar (afraid) of the ap (anger) and chamah (hot) displeasure, with which Yahawah was qatzap (angry) against you to destroy you. But Yahawah listened to me that paim (time) also.
Yahawah was very angry with Aharawan to destroy him: and I prayed for Aharawan also at the same ith (time).

I took your chataah (sin), the calf which you had made, and burnt it with ash (fire), and stamped it, grinding it very yatab (small), until it was as fine as ipar (dust): and I cast its ipar (dust) into the nachal (brook) that descended out of the har (mountain).
At Thabairah, and at Masah, and at Qabarawathahathaawah Hattaavah, you provoked Yahawah to qatzap (wrath).

When Yahawah sent you Qadashabaranai Kadesh Barnea, saying, "ilah (go) up and yarash (possess) the aratz (land) which I have given you;" then you rebelled against the commandment of Yahawah your Alahayam, and you didn't aman (believe) him, nor listen to his qawal (voice).
You have been rebellious against Yahawah from the yawam (day) that I knew you.
So I napal (fell) down panayam (before) Yahawah the arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights) that I napal (fell) down, because Yahawah had said he would destroy you.

I prayed to Yahawah, and said, "Adawan Yahawah, don't shachath (destroy) your im (people) and your nachalah (inheritance), that you have padah (redeemed) through your greatness, that you have brought out of Matzarayam with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand).
zakar (remember) your ibad (servants), Abaraham, Yatzachaq, and Yaiqab; don't panah (look) to the stubbornness of this im (people), nor to their rashai (wickedness), nor to their chataah (sin),

lest the aratz (land) you brought us out from amar (say), ‘Because Yahawah was not yakal (able) to bawaa (bring) them into the aratz (land) which he promised to them, and because he hated them, he has brought them out to mawath (kill) them in the madabar (wilderness).'
Yet they are your im (people) and your nachalah (inheritance), which you brought out by your gadawal (great) kach (power) and by your natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm).

At that ith (time) Yahawah said to me, "Cut shanayam (two) tables of aban (stone) like the raashawan (first), and ilah (come) up to me onto the har (mountain), and ishah (make) an arawan (ark) of itz (wood).
I will kathab (write) on the tables the dabar (words) that were on the raashawan (first) tables which you broke, and you shall shawam (put) them in the arawan (ark).

So I made an arawan (ark) of acacia itz (wood), and cut shanayam (two) tables of aban (stone) like the raashawan (first), and went up onto the har (mountain), having the shanayam (two) tables in my yad (hand).

He wrote on the tables, according to the raashawan (first) writing, the ishar (ten) commandments, which Yahawah spoke to you on the har (mountain) out of the midst of the ash (fire) in the yawam (day) of the qahal (assembly): and Yahawah gave them to me.
I turned and came down from the har (mountain), and shawam (put) the tables in the arawan (ark) which I had made; and there they are as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) me.

(The children of Yasharaal (Israel) traveled from Baarathabanayayaiqan Bene Jaakan Mawasarah Moserah. There Aharawan died, and there he was buried; and Alaizar his ban (son) ministered in the kahan (priest's) office in his place.
From there they traveled to Gadagadah; and from Gadagadah to Yatabathah, a aratz (land) of nachal (brooks) of mayam (water).

At that ith (time) Yahawah set apart the shabat (tribe) of Laway, to nashaa (bear) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, to imad (stand) panayam (before) Yahawah to sharath (minister) to him, and to barak (bless) in his sham (name), to this yawam (day).
Therefore Laway has no chalaq (portion) nor nachalah (inheritance) with his ach (brothers); Yahawah is his nachalah (inheritance), according as Yahawah your Alahayam spoke to him.)

I stayed on the har (mountain), as at the raashawan (first) yawam (time), arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights): and Yahawah listened to me that paim (time) also; Yahawah would not shachath (destroy) you.

Yahawah said to me, "qawam (arise), yalak (take) your journey panayam (before) the im (people); and they shall bawaa (go) in and yarash (possess) the aratz (land), which I swore to their abawath (fathers) to nathan (give) to them.

Now, Yasharaal (Israel), what does Yahawah your Alahayam shaal (require) of you, but to yaraa (fear) Yahawah your Alahayam, to yalak (walk) in all his darak (ways), and to ahab (love) him, and to ibad (serve) Yahawah your Alahayam with all your labab (heart) and with all your napash (soul),
to shamar (keep) the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah, and his chaqah (statutes), which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day) for your tawab (good)?
Behold, to Yahawah your Alahayam belongs shamayam (heaven) and the shamayam (heaven) of shamayam (heavens), the aratz (earth), with all that is therein.
Only Yahawah had a chashaq (delight) in your abawath (fathers) to ahab (love) them, and he chose their zarai (seed) achar (after) them, even you above all im (peoples), as at this yawam (day).
mawal (circumcise) therefore the foreskin of your labab (heart), and be no more stiff-necked.

For Yahawah your Alahayam, he is Alahayam of Alahayam, and Adawan of adawan (lords), the gadawal (great) Al, the gabawar (mighty), and the awesome, who doesn't nashaa (respect) panayam (persons), nor takes shachad (reward).
He does ishah (execute) justice for the fatherless and alamanah (widow), and ahab (loves) the foreigner, in giving him lacham (food) and clothing.
Therefore ahab (love) the foreigner; for you were foreigners in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
You shall yaraa (fear) Yahawah your Alahayam; you shall ibad (serve) him; and you shall cling to him, and you shall shabai (swear) by his sham (name).
He is your thahalah (praise), and he is your Alahayam, who has done for you these gadawal (great) and awesome things, which your iyan (eyes) have seen.
Your abawath (fathers) went down into Matzarayam with shabaiyam (seventy) napash (persons); and now Yahawah your Alahayam has made you as the kawakab (stars) of the sky for multitude.
Therefore you shall ahab (love) Yahawah your Alahayam, and shamar (keep) his instructions, and his chaqah (statutes), and his mashapat (ordinances), and his matzawah (commandments), yawam (always).

yadai (know) this yawam (day): for I don't speak with your children who have not yadai (known), and who have not seen the chastisement of Yahawah your Alahayam, his greatness, his chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and his natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm),
and his awath (signs), and his maishah (works), which he did in the midst of Matzarayam to Paraih the malak (king) of Matzarayam, and to all his aratz (land);

and what he did to the chayal (army) of Matzarayam, to their horses, and to their chariots; how he made the mayam (water) of the Red yam (sea) to overflow them as they pursued achar (after) you, and how Yahawah has destroyed them to this yawam (day);
and what he did to you in the madabar (wilderness), until you came to this place;

and what he did to Dathan and Abayaram, the ban (sons) of Alayaab, the ban (son) of Raawaban; how the aratz (earth) opened its pah (mouth), and swallowed them up, and their bayath (households), and their ahal (tents), and every living thing that followed them, in the qarab (midst) of all Yasharaal (Israel):
but your iyan (eyes) have seen all the gadawal (great) maishah (work) of Yahawah which he did.

Therefore you shall shamar (keep) all the matzawah (commandment) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), that you may be chazaq (strong), and bawaa (go) in and yarash (possess) the aratz (land), where you ibar (go) over to yarash (possess) it;

and that you may prolong your yawam (days) in the adamah (land), which Yahawah swore to your abawath (fathers) to nathan (give) to them and to their zarai (seed), a aratz (land) flowing with milk and honey.

For the aratz (land), where you bawaa (go) in to yarash (possess) it, isn't as the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, that you came out from, where you sowed your zarai (seed), and watered it with your ragal (foot), as a Gan of herbs;
but the aratz (land), where you ibar (go) over to yarash (possess) it, is a aratz (land) of har (hills) and Baqaih which drinks mayam (water) of the rain of the sky,

a aratz (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam cares for: the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah your Alahayam are always on it, from the raashayath (beginning) of the Shanah even to the acharayath (end) of the Shanah.

It shall happen, if you shall listen diligently to my matzawah (commandments) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), to ahab (love) Yahawah your Alahayam, and to ibad (serve) him with all your labab (heart) and with all your napash (soul),

that I will nathan (give) the rain of your aratz (land) in its ith (season), the yawarah (former) rain and the latter yawarah (rain), that you may asap (gather) in your grain, and your new thayarawash (wine), and your yatzahar (oil).
I will nathan (give) grass in your shadah (fields) for your livestock, and you shall akal (eat) and be full.
shamar (take) heed to yourselves, lest your labab (heart) be deceived, and you sawar (turn) aside, and ibad (serve) other Alahayam, and shachah (worship) them;

and the ap (anger) of Yahawah be kindled against you, and he itzar (shut) up the sky, so that there shall be no rain, and the adamah (land) shall not nathan (yield) its fruit; and you abad (perish) quickly from off the tawab (good) aratz (land) which Yahawah nathan (gives) you.

Therefore you shall shawam (lay) up these my dabar (words) in your labab (heart) and in your napash (soul); and you shall qashar (bind) them for a awath (sign) on your yad (hand), and they shall be for symbols between your iyan (eyes).

You shall teach them your children, talking of them, when you yashab (sit) in your bayath (house), and when you yalak (walk) by the darak (way), and when you shakab (lie) down, and when you qawam (rise) up.
You shall kathab (write) them on the door posts of your bayath (house), and on your gates;

that your yawam (days) may be multiplied, and the yawam (days) of your children, in the adamah (land) which Yahawah swore to your abawath (fathers) to nathan (give) them, as the yawam (days) of the shamayam (heavens) above the aratz (earth).

For if you shall diligently shamar (keep) all this matzawah (commandment) which I tzawah (command) you, to do it, to ahab (love) Yahawah your Alahayam, to yalak (walk) in all his darak (ways), and to cling to him;
then will Yahawah yarash (drive) out all these gawayam (nations) from panayam (before) you, and you shall yarash (dispossess) gawayam (nations) greater and mightier than yourselves.

Every place whereon the kap (sole) of your ragal (foot) shall tread shall be yours: from the madabar (wilderness), and Labanawan, from the nahar (river), the nahar (river) Parath, Acharawan to the hinder yam (sea) shall be your border.

No ayash (man) shall be able to stand panayam (before) you: Yahawah your Alahayam shall nathan (lay) the pachad (fear) of you and the mawaraa (dread) of you on all the aratz (land) that you shall tread on, as he has spoken to you.
raah (see), I nathan (set) panayam (before) you this yawam (day) a barakah (blessing) and a qalalah (curse):
the barakah (blessing), if you shall listen to the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah your Alahayam, which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day);

and the qalalah (curse), if you shall not listen to the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah your Alahayam, but sawar (turn) aside out of the darak (way) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), to yalak (go) achar (after) other Alahayam, which you have not yadai (known).

It shall happen, when Yahawah your Alahayam shall bawaa (bring) you into the aratz (land) where you bawaa (go) to yarash (possess) it, that you shall nathan (set) the barakah (blessing) on har (mount) Garazayam, and the qalalah (curse) on har (mount) Iyabal.

Aren't they ibar (beyond) the Yaradan, achar (behind) the darak (way) of the going down of the shamash (sun), in the aratz (land) of the Kanainay (Canaanites) who yashab (dwell) in the irabah (arabah), over against Galagal, beside the oaks of Mawarah?

For you are to ibar (pass) over the Yaradan to bawaa (go) in to yarash (possess) the aratz (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you, and you shall yarash (possess) it, and yashab (dwell) therein.
You shall shamar (observe) to do all the chaq (statutes) and the mashapat (ordinances) which I nathan (set) panayam (before) you this yawam (day).

These are the chaq (statutes) and the mashapat (ordinances) which you shall shamar (observe) to do in the aratz (land) which Yahawah, the Alahayam of your abawath (fathers), has given you to yarash (possess) it, all the yawam (days) that you chay (live) on the adamah (earth).

You shall abad (surely) abad (destroy) all the places in which the gawayam (nations) that you shall yarash (dispossess) served their Alahayam, on the high har (mountains), and on the Gabaih, and under every Rainan itz (tree):

and you shall shabar (break) down their mazabach (altars), and dash in pieces their matzabah (pillars), and sharap (burn) their Asharah with ash (fire); and you shall cut down the engraved pasayal (images) of their Alahayam; and you shall abad (destroy) their sham (name) out of that place.
You shall not do so to Yahawah your Alahayam.

But to the place which Yahawah your Alahayam shall choose out of all your shabat (tribes), to shawam (put) his sham (name) there, even to his habitation you shall seek, and there you shall bawaa (come);

and there you shall bawaa (bring) your burnt ilah (offerings), and your zabach (sacrifices), and your maishar (tithes), and the wave tharawamah (offering) of your yad (hand), and your nadar (vows), and your freewill nadabah (offerings), and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock:

and there you shall akal (eat) panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam, and you shall Shamach in all that you put your yad (hand) to, you and your bayath (households), in which Yahawah your Alahayam has blessed you.
You shall not do after all the things that we do here this yawam (day), every ayash (man) whatever is yashar (right) in his own iyan (eyes);
for you haven't yet bawaa (come) to the manawachah (rest) and to the nachalah (inheritance), which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you.

But when you ibar (go) over the Yaradan, and yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nachal (causes) you to inherit, and he gives you nawach (rest) from all your ayab (enemies) around you, so that you yashab (dwell) in safety;

then it shall happen that to the place which Yahawah your Alahayam shall choose, to cause his sham (name) to shakan (dwell) there, there you shall bawaa (bring) all that I tzawah (command) you: your burnt ilah (offerings), and your zabach (sacrifices), your maishar (tithes), and the wave tharawamah (offering) of your yad (hand), and all your choice nadar (vows) which you nadar (vow) to Yahawah.

You shall Shamach panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam, you, and your ban (sons), and your bath (daughters), and your male ibad (servants), and your female amah (servants), and the Lawayay (Levite) who is within your gates, because he has no chalaq (portion) nor nachalah (inheritance) with you.
shamar (take) heed to yourself that you don't ilah (offer) your burnt ilah (offerings) in every place that you raah (see);
but in the place which Yahawah shall choose in one of your shabat (tribes), there you shall ilah (offer) your burnt ilah (offerings), and there you shall do all that I tzawah (command) you.

Notwithstanding, you may zabach (kill) and akal (eat) flesh within all your gates, after all the desire of your napash (soul), according to the barakah (blessing) of Yahawah your Alahayam which he has given you: the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean) may akal (eat) of it, as of the gazelle, and as of the hart.
Only you shall not akal (eat) the dam (blood); you shall pour it out on the aratz (earth) as mayam (water).

You may not akal (eat) within your gates the maishar (tithe) of your grain, or of your new thayarawash (wine), or of your yatzahar (oil), or the firstborn of your herd or of your flock, nor any of your nadar (vows) which you nadar (vow), nor your freewill nadabah (offerings), nor the wave tharawamah (offering) of your yad (hand);

but you shall akal (eat) them panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam in the place which Yahawah your Alahayam shall choose, you, and your ban (son), and your bath (daughter), and your male ibad (servant), and your female amah (servant), and the Lawayay (Levite) who is within your gates: and you shall Shamach panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam in all that you put your yad (hand) to.
shamar (take) heed to yourself that you don't forsake the Lawayay (Levite) as yawam (long) as you live in your adamah (land).

When Yahawah your Alahayam shall enlarge your border, as he has promised you, and you shall amar (say), "I want to akal (eat) meat," because your napash (soul) desires to akal (eat) meat; you may akal (eat) meat, after all the desire of your napash (soul).

If the place which Yahawah your Alahayam shall choose, to shawam (put) his sham (name) there, is rachaq (too) far from you, then you shall zabach (kill) of your herd and of your flock, which Yahawah has given you, as I have tzawah (commanded) you; and you may akal (eat) within your gates, after all the desire of your napash (soul).
Even as the gazelle and as the hart is eaten, so you shall akal (eat) of it: the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean) may akal (eat) of it alike.
Only be chazaq (sure) that you don't akal (eat) the dam (blood): for the dam (blood) is the napash (life); and you shall not akal (eat) the napash (life) with the flesh.
You shall not akal (eat) it; you shall pour it out on the aratz (earth) as mayam (water).
You shall not akal (eat) it; that it may yatab (go) well with you, and with your children achar (after) you, when you shall do that which is yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah.
Only your qadash (holy) things which you have, and your nadar (vows), you shall nashaa (take), and bawaa (go) to the place which Yahawah shall choose:

and you shall ishah (offer) your burnt ilah (offerings), the flesh and the dam (blood), on the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah your Alahayam; and the dam (blood) of your zabach (sacrifices) shall be poured out on the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah your Alahayam; and you shall akal (eat) the flesh.

shamar (observe) and hear all these dabar (words) which I tzawah (command) you, that it may yatab (go) well with you, and with your children achar (after) you iwalam (forever), when you do that which is tawab (good) and yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah your Alahayam.

When Yahawah your Alahayam shall karath (cut) off the gawayam (nations) from panayam (before) you, where you bawaa (go) in to yarash (dispossess) them, and you yarash (dispossess) them, and yashab (dwell) in their aratz (land);

shamar (take) heed to yourself that you not be ensnared to achar (follow) them, achar (after) that they are destroyed from panayam (before) you; and that you not inquire after their Alahayam, saying, "How do these gawayam (nations) ibad (serve) their Alahayam? I will do likewise.

You shall not do so to Yahawah your Alahayam: for every thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, which he shanaa (hates), have they done to their Alahayam; for even their ban (sons) and their bath (daughters) do they sharap (burn) in the ash (fire) to their Alahayam.
Whatever thing I tzawah (command) you, that you shall shamar (observe) to do: you shall not add thereto, nor diminish from it.
If there qawam (arise) in the qarab (midst) of you a nabayaa (prophet), or a chalam (dreamer) of chalawam (dreams), and he nathan (give) you a awath (sign) or a mawapath (wonder),

and the awath (sign) or the mawapath (wonder) bawaa (come) to pass, of which he spoke to you, saying, "Let us yalak (go) achar (after) other Alahayam" (which you have not yadai (known)) "and let us ibad (serve) them;

you shall not listen to the dabar (words) of that nabayaa (prophet), or to that chalam (dreamer) of chalawam (dreams): for Yahawah your Alahayam proves you, to yadai (know) whether you ahab (love) Yahawah your Alahayam with all your labab (heart) and with all your napash (soul).

You shall yalak (walk) achar (after) Yahawah your Alahayam, and yaraa (fear) him, and shamar (keep) his matzawah (commandments), and obey his qawal (voice), and you shall ibad (serve) him, and cling to him.

That nabayaa (prophet), or that chalam (dreamer) of chalawam (dreams), shall be put to mawath (death), because he has spoken sarah (rebellion) against Yahawah your Alahayam, who brought you out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and padah (redeemed) you out of the bayath (house) of ibad (bondage), to draw you aside out of the darak (way) which Yahawah your Alahayam tzawah (commanded) you to yalak (walk) in. So you shall bair (put) bair (away) the rai (evil) from the qarab (midst) of you.

If your ach (brother), the ban (son) of your am (mother), or your ban (son), or your bath (daughter), or the ashah (wife) of your bosom, or your rai (friend), who is as your own napash (soul), entice you secretly, saying, "Let us yalak (go) and ibad (serve) other Alahayam," which you have not yadai (known), you, nor your abawath (fathers);
of the Alahayam of the im (peoples) who are around you, qarawab (near) to you, or Rachawaq off from you, from the qatzah (one) end of the aratz (earth) even to the other end of the aratz (earth);
you shall not abah (consent) to him, nor listen to him; neither shall your iyan (eye) pity him, neither shall you spare, neither shall you conceal him:
but you shall harag (surely) harag (kill) him; your yad (hand) shall be raashawan (first) on him to put him to mawath (death), and Acharawan the yad (hand) of all the im (people).

You shall saqal (stone) him to death with saqal (stones), because he has sought to draw you away from Yahawah your Alahayam, who brought you out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, out of the bayath (house) of ibad (bondage).
All Yasharaal (Israel) shall hear, and yaraa (fear), and shall not do any more such wickedness as this is in the qarab (midst) of you.
If you shall hear tell concerning one of your Iyar, which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you to yashab (dwell) there, saying,

Certain base anawash (fellows) are gone out from the qarab (midst) of you, and have drawn away the yashab (inhabitants) of their Iyar, saying, "Let us yalak (go) and ibad (serve) other Alahayam," which you have not yadai (known);

then you shall inquire, and make search, and shaal (ask) yatab (diligently); and, behold, if it be truth, and the thing kawan (certain), that such thawaibah (abomination) is done in the qarab (midst) of you,

you shall surely strike the yashab (inhabitants) of that Iyar with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), destroying it charam (utterly), and all that is therein and its livestock, with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).

You shall gather all its spoil into the midst of its street, and shall sharap (burn) with ash (fire) the Iyar, and all its spoil kalayal (every) whit, to Yahawah your Alahayam: and it shall be a thal (heap) iwalam (forever); it shall not be built again.

Nothing of the charam (devoted) thing shall cling to your yad (hand); that Yahawah may shawab (turn back / repent) from the charawan (fierceness) of his ap (anger), and show you racham (mercy), and have racham (compassion) on you, and multiply you, as he has sworn to your abawath (fathers);

when you shall listen to the qawal (voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam, to shamar (keep) all his matzawah (commandments) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), to do that which is yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah your Alahayam.
You are the children of Yahawah your Alahayam: you shall not cut yourselves, nor shawam (make) any baldness between your iyan (eyes) for the mawath (dead).

For you are a qadawash (holy) im (people) to Yahawah your Alahayam, and Yahawah has chosen you to be a im (people) for his own sagalah (possession), above all im (peoples) who are on the face of the adamah (earth).
You shall not akal (eat) any thawaibah (abominable) thing.
These are the animals which you may akal (eat): the ox, the sheep, and the goat,
the hart, and the gazelle, and the tzabay (roebuck), and the wild goat, and the ibex, and the antelope, and the chamois.
Every animal that parts the hoof, and has the hoof cloven in shanayam (two) and chews the cud, among the animals, that may you akal (eat).

Nevertheless these you shall not akal (eat) of them that chew the cud, or of those who have the hoof cloven: the camel, and the hare, and the Shapan; because they chew the cud but don't part the hoof, they are tamaa (unclean) to you.
The pig, because it has a split hoof but doesn't chew the cud, is tamaa (unclean) to you: of their flesh you shall not akal (eat), and their carcasses you shall not nagai (touch).
These you may akal (eat) of all that are in the mayam (waters): whatever has fins and scales may you akal (eat);
and whatever doesn't have fins and scales you shall not akal (eat); it is tamaa (unclean) to you.
Of all tahawar (clean) birds you may akal (eat).
But these are they of which you shall not akal (eat): the eagle, and the vulture, and the osprey,
and the red kite, and the falcon, and the kite after its kind,
and every raven after its kind,
and the ostrich, and the bath (owl), and the seagull, and the thachamas (hawk) after its kind,
the little owl, and the great owl, and the horned owl,
and the pelican, and the vulture, and the cormorant,
and the stork, and the heron after its kind, and the hoopoe, and the bat.
All winged creeping things are tamaa (unclean) to you: they shall not be eaten.
Of all tahawar (clean) birds you may akal (eat).

You shall not akal (eat) of anything that dies of nabalah (itself): you may nathan (give) it to the foreigner living among you who is within your gates, that he may akal (eat) it; or you may sell it to a nakaray (foreigner): for you are a qadawash (holy) im (people) to Yahawah your Alahayam. You shall not boil a young goat in its am (mother's) milk.
You shall ishar (surely) ishar (tithe) all the increase of your zarai (seed), that which yatzaa (comes) forth from the shadah (field) Shanah by Shanah.

You shall akal (eat) panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam, in the place which he shall choose, to cause his sham (name) to shakan (dwell) there, the maishar (tithe) of your grain, of your new thayarawash (wine), and of your yatzahar (oil), and the firstborn of your herd and of your flock; that you may learn to yaraa (fear) Yahawah your Alahayam yawam (always).

If the darak (way) is too long for you, so that you are not yakal (able) to nashaa (carry) it, because the place is rachaq (too) far from you, which Yahawah your Alahayam shall choose, to shawam (set) his sham (name) there, when Yahawah your Alahayam shall barak (bless) you;
then you shall nathan (turn) it into kasap (money), and tzawar (bind) up the kasap (money) in your yad (hand), and shall halak (go) to the place which Yahawah your Alahayam shall choose:

and you shall nathan (bestow) the kasap (money) for whatever your napash (soul) desires, for cattle, or for sheep, or for yayan (wine), or for shakar (strong) drink, or for whatever your napash (soul) shaal (asks) of you; and you shall akal (eat) there panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam, and you shall Shamach, you and your bayath (household).
The Lawayay (Levite) who is within your gates, you shall not forsake him; for he has no chalaq (portion) nor nachalah (inheritance) with you.
At the end of every shalawash (three) Shanah you shall yatzaa (bring) forth all the maishar (tithe) of your increase in the same Shanah, and shall yanach (lay) it up within your gates:

and the Lawayay (Levite), because he has no chalaq (portion) nor nachalah (inheritance) with you, and the foreigner living among you, and the fatherless, and the alamanah (widow), who are within your gates, shall bawaa (come), and shall akal (eat) and be satisfied; that Yahawah your Alahayam may barak (bless) you in all the maishah (work) of your yad (hand) which you do.
At the end of every shabai (seven) Shanah you shall ishah (make) a release.

This is the way of the release: every creditor shall release that which he has lent to his neighbor; he shall not exact it of his neighbor and his ach (brother); because yahawah (yahweh's) release has been proclaimed.
Of a nakaray (foreigner) you may exact it: but whatever of your is with your ach (brother) your yad (hand) shall shamat (release).

However there shall be no Abayawan with you; (for Yahawah will surely barak (bless) you in the aratz (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you for an nachalah (inheritance) to yarash (possess) it;)
if only you diligently listen to the qawal (voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam, to shamar (observe) to do all this matzawah (commandment) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day).

For Yahawah your Alahayam will barak (bless) you, as he promised you: and you shall lend to many gawayam (nations), but you shall not borrow; and you shall mashal (rule) over many gawayam (nations), but they shall not mashal (rule) over you.

If a Abayawan man, Abayawan of your ach (brothers), is with you within any of your gates in your aratz (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you, you shall not amatz (harden) your labab (heart), nor qapatz (shut) your yad (hand) from your Abayawan ach (brother);
but you shall surely pathach (open) your yad (hand) to him, and shall surely lend him sufficient for his need, which he lacks.

Beware that there not be a base dabar (thought) in your labab (heart), saying, "The seventh Shanah, the Shanah of release, is at qarab (hand);" and your iyan (eye) be raii (evil) against your Abayawan ach (brother), and you nathan (give) him nothing; and he qaraa (cry) to Yahawah against you, and it be chataa (sin) to you.

You shall nathan (surely) nathan (give) him, and your labab (heart) shall not be grieved when you nathan (give) to him; because that for this thing Yahawah your Alahayam will barak (bless) you in all your maishah (work), and in all that you put your yad (hand) to.

For the Abayawan will never chadal (cease) out of the aratz (land): therefore I tzawah (command) you, saying, You shall surely pathach (open) your yad (hand) to your ach (brother), to your Abayawan, and to your Inay, in your aratz (land).

If your ach (brother), a ibaray (hebrew) man, or a Hebrew ibaray (woman), is sold to you, and ibad (serves) you shash (six) Shanah; then in the shabayaiy (seventh) Shanah you shall let him shalach (go) Chapashay from you.
When you let him go Chapashay from you, you shall not let him shalach (go) empty:
you shall furnish him liberally out of your flock, and out of your threshing floor, and out of your yaqab (winepress); as Yahawah your Alahayam has blessed you, you shall nathan (give) to him.
You shall zakar (remember) that you were a ibad (bondservant) in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and Yahawah your Alahayam padah (redeemed) you: therefore I tzawah (command) you this thing today.
It shall be, if he amar (tells) you, "I will not yatzaa (go) out from you;" because he ahab (loves) you and your bayath (house), because he is tawab (well) with you;
then you shall take an awl, and nathan (thrust) it through his ear to the door, and he shall be your ibad (servant) iwalam (forever). Also to your female amah (servant) you shall do likewise.

It shall not seem hard to you, when you let him shalach (go) Chapashay from you; for to the mashanah (double) of the hire of a shakayar (hireling) has he served you shash (six) Shanah: and Yahawah your Alahayam will barak (bless) you in all that you do.

All the firstborn zakar (males) that are yalad (born) of your herd and of your flock you shall qadash (sanctify) to Yahawah your Alahayam: you shall do no ibad (work) with the firstborn of your herd, nor shear the firstborn of your flock.
You shall akal (eat) it panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam Shanah by Shanah in the place which Yahawah shall choose, you and your bayath (household).
If it has any blemish, is Pasach or iwar (blind), or has any defect whatever, you shall not zabach (sacrifice) it to Yahawah your Alahayam.
You shall akal (eat) it within your gates: the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean) shall eat it alike, as the gazelle, and as the hart.
Only you shall not akal (eat) its dam (blood); you shall pour it out on the aratz (ground) as mayam (water).

shamar (observe) the chadash (month) of Abib, and ishah (keep) the pasach (passover) to Yahawah your Alahayam; for in the chadash (month) of Abib Yahawah your Alahayam brought you yatzaa (forth) out of Matzarayam by layal (night).
You shall zabach (sacrifice) the pasach (passover) to Yahawah your Alahayam, of the flock and the herd, in the place which Yahawah shall choose, to cause his sham (name) to shakan (dwell) there.

You shall akal (eat) no leavened chamatz (bread) with it. You shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread) with it seven days, even the matzah (bread) of affliction; for you came yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam in haste: that you may zakar (remember) the yawam (day) when you came yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam all the yawam (days) of your chay (life).

No yeast shall be seen with you in all your borders shabai (seven) yawam (days); neither shall any of the flesh, which you zabach (sacrifice) the raashawan (first) yawam (day) at evening, lawan (remain) all night until the baqar (morning).
You may not zabach (sacrifice) the pasach (passover) within any of your gates, which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you;

but at the place which Yahawah your Alahayam shall choose, to cause his sham (name) to dwell in, there you shall zabach (sacrifice) the pasach (passover) at evening, at the going down of the shamash (sun), at the mawaid (season) that you came yatzaa (forth) out of Matzarayam.
You shall roast and akal (eat) it in the place which Yahawah your Alahayam shall choose: and you shall panah (turn) in the baqar (morning), and halak (go) to your ahal (tents).

shash (six) yawam (days) you shall akal (eat) unleavened matzah (bread). On the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) shall be a solemn itzarah (assembly) to Yahawah your Alahayam; you shall do no malaakah (work).

You shall count for yourselves shabai (seven) shabawai (weeks): from the time you chalal (begin) to put the sickle to the standing grain you shall chalal (begin) to number shabai (seven) shabawai (weeks).

You shall ishah (keep) the chag (feast) of shabawai (weeks) to Yahawah your Alahayam with a tribute of a freewill nadabah (offering) of your yad (hand), which you shall nathan (give), according as Yahawah your Alahayam blesses you:

and you shall Shamach panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam, you, and your ban (son), and your bath (daughter), and your male ibad (servant), and your female amah (servant), and the Lawayay (Levite) who is within your gates, and the foreigner, and the fatherless, and the alamanah (widow), who are in the qarab (midst) of you, in the place which Yahawah your Alahayam shall choose, to cause his sham (name) to shakan (dwell) there.
You shall zakar (remember) that you were a ibad (bondservant) in Matzarayam: and you shall shamar (observe) and do these chaq (statutes).
You shall ishah (keep) the chag (feast) of sakah (tents) shabai (seven) yawam (days), after that you have gathered in from your threshing floor and from your yaqab (winepress):

and you shall Shamach in your chag (feast), you, and your ban (son), and your bath (daughter), and your male ibad (servant), and your female amah (servant), and the Lawayay (Levite), and the foreigner, and the fatherless, and the alamanah (widow), who are within your gates.

You shall keep a feast to Yahawah your Alahayam shabai (seven) yawam (days) in the place which Yahawah shall choose; because Yahawah your Alahayam will barak (bless) you in all your increase, and in all the maishah (work) of your yad (hands), and you shall be altogether Shamach.

shalawash (three) paim (times) in a Shanah shall all your males raah (see) panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam in the place which he shall choose: in the chag (feast) of unleavened matzah (bread), and in the chag (feast) of shabawai (weeks), and in the chag (feast) of sakah (tents); and they shall not raah (see) panayam (before) Yahawah empty:
every ayash (man) shall give as he is able, according to the barakah (blessing) of Yahawah your Alahayam which he has given you.

You shall nathan (make) shapat (judges) and shatar (officers) in all your gates, which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you, according to your shabat (tribes); and they shall shapat (judge) the im (people) with tzadaq (righteous) mashapat (judgment).

You shall not natah (wrest) justice: you shall not nakar (respect) panayam (persons); neither shall you take a shachad (bribe); for a shachad (bribe) does blind the iyan (eyes) of the chakam (wise), and pervert the dabar (words) of the tzadayaq (righteous).
You shall follow that which is altogether tzadaq (just), that you may chayah (live), and yarash (inherit) the aratz (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you.
You shall not plant Asharah yourselves an Asherah of any kind of itz (tree) beside the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah your Alahayam, which you shall ishah (make) for yourselves.
Neither shall you qawam (set) yourself up a matzabah (pillar); which Yahawah your Alahayam shanaa (hates).
You shall not zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah your Alahayam an ox, or a sheep, in which is a blemish, or anything rai (evil); for that is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah your Alahayam.

If there is found in the qarab (midst) of you, within any of your gates which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you, ayash (man) or ashah (woman), who does that which is rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah your Alahayam, in transgressing his barayath (covenant),
and has gone and served other Alahayam, and worshiped them, or the shamash (sun), or the yarach (moon), or any of the tzabaa (army) of the sky, which I have not tzawah (commanded);

and it be told you, and you have heard of it, then you shall inquire yatab (diligently); and behold, if it be amath (true), and the thing kawan (certain), that such thawaibah (abomination) is done in Yasharaal (Israel),

then you shall yatzaa (bring) forth that ayash (man) or that ashah (woman), who has done this rai (evil) thing, to your gates, even the ayash (man) or the ashah (woman); and you shall saqal (stone) them to mawath (death) with saqal (stones).

At the pah (mouth) of shanayam (two) witnesses, or shalawash (three) witnesses, shall he who is to mawath (die) be put to mawath (death); at the pah (mouth) of one witness he shall not be put to mawath (death).

The yad (hand) of the witnesses shall be raashawan (first) on him to put him to mawath (death), and Acharawan the yad (hand) of all the im (people). So you shall bair (put) bair (away) the rai (evil) from the qarab (midst) of you.

If there arises a dabar (matter) palaa (too) hard for you in mashapat (judgment), between dam (blood) and dam (blood), between plea and plea, and between nagai (stroke) and nagai (stroke), being dabar (matters) of rayab (controversy) within your gates; then you shall qawam (arise), and ilah (go) up to the place which Yahawah your Alahayam shall choose;

and you shall bawaa (come) to the kahan (priests) the Lawayay (Levites), and to the shapat (judge) who shall be in those yawam (days): and you shall inquire; and they shall show you the dabar (sentence) of mashapat (judgment).

You shall do according to the pah (tenor) of the sentence which they shall show you from that place which Yahawah shall choose; and you shall shamar (observe) to do according to all that they shall teach you:

according to the pah (tenor) of the thawarah (law) which they shall teach you, and according to the mashapat (judgment) which they shall amar (tell) you, you shall do; you shall not sawar (turn) aside from the dabar (sentence) which they shall show you, to the right yamayan (hand), nor to the shamaawal (left).

The ayash (man) who does presumptuously, in not listening to the kahan (priest) who imad (stands) to sharath (minister) there before Yahawah your Alahayam, or to the shapat (judge), even that ayash (man) shall mawath (die): and you shall bair (put) away the rai (evil) from Yasharaal (Israel).
All the im (people) shall hear, and yaraa (fear), and do no more presumptuously.

When you have bawaa (come) to the aratz (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you, and shall yarash (possess) it, and shall yashab (dwell) therein, and shall amar (say), "I will shawam (set) a malak (king) over me, like all the gawayam (nations) that are around me;

you shall surely shawam (set) him malak (king) over yourselves, whom Yahawah your Alahayam shall choose: one from qarab (among) your ach (brothers) you shall shawam (set) malak (king) over you; you may not nathan (put) a nakaray (foreigner) over you, who is not your ach (brother).

Only he shall not multiply horses to himself, nor cause the im (people) to shawab (turn back / repent) to Matzarayam, to the end that he may multiply horses; because Yahawah has said to you, "You shall not shawab (turn back / repent) back that darak (way) again.
Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his labab (heart) not sawar (turn) away: neither shall he maad (greatly) multiply to himself kasap (silver) and gold.

It shall be, when he yashab (sits) on the kasaa (throne) of his mamalakah (kingdom), that he shall kathab (write) him a mashanah (copy) of this thawarah (law) in a book, out of that which is panayam (before) the kahan (priests) the Lawayay (Levites):

and it shall be with him, and he shall qaraa (read) therein all the yawam (days) of his chay (life); that he may learn to yaraa (fear) Yahawah his Alahayam, to shamar (keep) all the dabar (words) of this thawarah (law) and these chaq (statutes), to do them;

that his labab (heart) not be lifted up above his ach (brothers), and that he not sawar (turn) aside from the matzawah (commandment), to the right yamayan (hand), or to the shamaawal (left): to the end that he may prolong his yawam (days) in his mamalakah (kingdom), he and his children, in the qarab (midst) of Yasharaal (Israel).

The kahan (priests) the Lawayay (Levites), all the shabat (tribe) of Laway, shall have no chalaq (portion) nor nachalah (inheritance) with Yasharaal (Israel): they shall akal (eat) the ashah (offerings) of Yahawah made by ashah (fire), and his nachalah (inheritance).
They shall have no nachalah (inheritance) qarab (among) their ach (brothers): Yahawah is their nachalah (inheritance), as he has spoken to them.

This shall be the kahan (priests)' mashapat (due) from the im (people), from those who zabach (offer) a zabach (sacrifice), whether it be ox or sheep, that they shall nathan (give) to the kahan (priest) the zarawai (shoulder), and the two Lachay, and the maw.
The raashayath (first) fruits of your grain, of your new thayarawash (wine), and of your yatzahar (oil), and the raashayath (first) of the fleece of your sheep, you shall nathan (give) him.
For Yahawah your Alahayam has chosen him out of all your shabat (tribes), to imad (stand) to sharath (minister) in the sham (name) of Yahawah, him and his ban (sons) for yawam (ever).

If a Lawayay (Levite) bawaa (comes) from any of your gates out of all Yasharaal (Israel), where he lives as a foreigner, and bawaa (comes) with all the desire of his napash (soul) to the place which Yahawah shall choose;
then he shall sharath (minister) in the sham (name) of Yahawah his Alahayam, as all his ach (brothers) the Lawayay (Levites) do, who imad (stand) there panayam (before) Yahawah.
They shall have like chalaq (portions) to akal (eat), besides that which comes of the sale of his ab (patrimony).
When you have bawaa (come) into the aratz (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you, you shall not learn to do after the thawaibah (abominations) of those gawayam (nations).

There shall not be found with you anyone who makes his ban (son) or his bath (daughter) to ibar (pass) through the ash (fire), qasam (one) who uses divination, inan (one) who practices sorcery, or an enchanter, or a sorcerer,
or a charmer, or a consulter with a familiar awab (spirit), or a wizard, or a necromancer.
For whoever does these things is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah: and because of these thawaibah (abominations) Yahawah your Alahayam does yarash (drive) them out from panayam (before) you.
You shall be thamayam (perfect) with Yahawah your Alahayam.
For these gawayam (nations), that you shall yarash (dispossess), listen to those who practice sorcery, and to diviners; but as for you, Yahawah your Alahayam has not allowed you so to do.
Yahawah your Alahayam will qawam (raise) up to you a nabayaa (prophet) from the qarab (midst) of you, of your ach (brothers), like me. You shall listen to him.

This is according to all that you desired of Yahawah your Alahayam in Charab in the yawam (day) of the qahal (assembly), saying, "Let me not hear again the qawal (voice) of Yahawah my Alahayam, neither let me raah (see) this gadawal (great) ash (fire) any more, that I not mawath (die).
Yahawah said to me, "They have yatab (well) said that which they have spoken.

I will qawam (raise) them up a nabayaa (prophet) from qarab (among) their ach (brothers), like you; and I will nathan (put) my dabar (words) in his pah (mouth), and he shall dabar (speak) to them all that I shall tzawah (command) him.
It shall happen, that ayash (whoever) will not listen to my dabar (words) which he shall dabar (speak) in my sham (name), I will require it of him.

But the nabayaa (prophet), who shall dabar (speak) a dabar (word) presumptuously in my sham (name), which I have not tzawah (commanded) him to dabar (speak), or who shall dabar (speak) in the sham (name) of other Alahayam, that same nabayaa (prophet) shall mawath (die).
If you amar (say) in your labab (heart), "How shall we yadai (know) the dabar (word) which Yahawah has not spoken?

when a nabayaa (prophet) dabar (speaks) in the sham (name) of Yahawah, if the thing doesn't bawaa (follow), nor happen, that is the thing which Yahawah has not spoken: the nabayaa (prophet) has spoken it presumptuously, you shall not be gawar (afraid) of him.

When Yahawah your Alahayam shall karath (cut) off the gawayam (nations), whose aratz (land) Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you, and you yarash (succeed) them, and yashab (dwell) in their Iyar, and in their bayath (houses);
you shall set apart shalawash (three) Iyar for you in the midst of your aratz (land), which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you to yarash (possess) it.

You shall kawan (prepare) you the darak (way), and divide the borders of your aratz (land), which Yahawah your Alahayam nachal (causes) you to inherit, into shalash (three) parts, that every manslayer may flee there.
This is the dabar (case) of the manslayer, that shall flee there and chayay (live): whoever kills his neighbor unawares, and didn't shanaa (hate) him in thamawal (time) shalashawam (past);

as when a man goes into the Yair with his neighbor to chop itz (wood), and his yad (hand) fetches a stroke with the axe to karath (cut) down the itz (tree), and the barazal (head) slips from the handle, and matzaa (lights) on his neighbor, so that he dies; he shall flee to one of these Iyar and chayay (live):

lest the gaal (avenger) of dam (blood) pursue the manslayer, while his labab (heart) is hot, and overtake him, because the darak (way) is long, and strike him mortally; whereas he was not mashapat (worthy) of mawath (death), inasmuch as he didn't shanaa (hate) him in thamawal (time) shalashawam (past).
Therefore I tzawah (command) you, saying, You shall set apart shalawash (three) Iyar for yourselves.
If Yahawah your Alahayam enlarges your border, as he has sworn to your abawath (fathers), and nathan (gives) you all the aratz (land) which he promised to nathan (give) to your abawath (fathers);

if you shamar (keep) all this matzawah (commandment) to do it, which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), to ahab (love) Yahawah your Alahayam, and to yalak (walk) yawam (ever) in his darak (ways); then you shall add shalawash (three) Iyar more for yourselves, besides these shalawash (three):
that naqay (innocent) dam (blood) not be shed in the midst of your aratz (land), which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you for an nachalah (inheritance), and so dam (blood) be on you.
But if any ayash (man) shanaa (hates) his neighbor, and lies in wait for him, and qawam (rises) up against him, and strikes him napash (mortally) so that he dies, and he flees into one of these Iyar;
then the zaqan (elders) of his Iyar shall shalach (send) and bring him there, and nathan (deliver) him into the yad (hand) of the gaal (avenger) of dam (blood), that he may mawath (die).
Your iyan (eye) shall not pity him, but you shall bair (put) away the naqay (innocent) dam (blood) from Yasharaal (Israel), that it may tawab (go) well with you.

You shall not nasag (remove) your neighbor's landmark, which they of raashawan (old) time have set, in your nachalah (inheritance) which you shall nachal (inherit), in the aratz (land) that Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you to yarash (possess) it.

One witness shall not qawam (rise) up against a ayash (man) for any iwan (iniquity), or for any chataah (sin), in any chataa (sin) that he chataa (sins): at the pah (mouth) of shanayam (two) witnesses, or at the pah (mouth) of shalawash (three) witnesses, shall a dabar (matter) be established.
If an unrighteous witness qawam (rise) up against any ayash (man) to testify against him of wrongdoing,

then shanayam (both) the men, between whom the rayab (controversy) is, shall imad (stand) panayam (before) Yahawah, panayam (before) the kahan (priests) and the shapat (judges) who shall be in those yawam (days);
and the shapat (judges) shall yatab (make) diligent inquisition: and, behold, if the witness is a false witness, and has testified falsely against his ach (brother);
then you shall do to him as he had thought to do to his ach (brother): so you shall bair (put) bair (away) the rai (evil) from the qarab (midst) of you.
Those who shaar (remain) shall hear, and yaraa (fear), and shall henceforth ishah (commit) no more any such rai (evil) in the qarab (midst) of you.
Your iyan (eyes) shall not pity: napash (life) for napash (life), iyan (eye) for iyan (eye), tooth for tooth, yad (hand) for yad (hand), ragal (foot) for ragal (foot).

When you yatzaa (go) forth to battle against your ayab (enemies), and raah (see) horses, chariots, and a im (people) more than you, you shall not be yaraa (afraid) of them; for Yahawah your Alahayam is with you, who brought you up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
It shall be, when you qarab (draw) near to the battle, that the kahan (priest) shall approach and dabar (speak) to the im (people),

and shall amar (tell) them, "Hear, Yasharaal (Israel), you Qarab near this yawam (day) to battle against your ayab (enemies): don't let your labab (heart) faint; don't be yaraa (afraid), nor tremble, neither be scared of them;
for Yahawah your Alahayam is he who goes with you, to fight for you against your ayab (enemies), to yashai (save) you.

The shatar (officers) shall dabar (speak) to the im (people), saying, "What ayash (man) is there who has built a Chadash bayath (house), and has not dedicated it? Let him yalak (go) and shawab (turn back / repent) to his bayath (house), lest he mawath (die) in the battle, and achar (another) ayash (man) dedicate it.

What ayash (man) is there who has planted a vineyard, and has not used its fruit? Let him yalak (go) and shawab (turn back / repent) to his bayath (house), lest he mawath (die) in the battle, and achar (another) ayash (man) use its fruit.

What ayash (man) is there who has pledged to be married a ashah (wife), and has not taken her? Let him yalak (go) and shawab (turn back / repent) to his bayath (house), lest he mawath (die) in the battle, and achar (another) ayash (man) take her.

The shatar (officers) shall dabar (speak) further to the im (people), and they shall amar (say), "What ayash (man) is there who is yaraa (fearful) and Rak? Let him yalak (go) and shawab (turn back / repent) to his bayath (house), lest his ach (brother's) labab (heart) melt as his labab (heart).

It shall be, when the shatar (officers) have made an kalah (end) of speaking to the im (people), that they shall paqad (appoint) shar (captains) of tzabaa (armies) at the raash (head) of the im (people).
When you qarab (draw) near to a Iyar to fight against it, then qaraa (proclaim) shalawam (peace) to it.

It shall be, if it makes you answer of shalawam (peace), and pathach (opens) to you, then it shall be, that all the im (people) who are found therein shall become tributary to you, and shall ibad (serve) you.
If it will make no shalam (peace) with you, but will ishah (make) war against you, then you shall tzawar (besiege) it:
and when Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (delivers) it into your yad (hand), you shall strike every male of it with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword):

but the women, and the little ones, and the livestock, and all that is in the Iyar, even all its spoil, you shall take for a prey to yourself; and you shall akal (eat) the spoil of your ayab (enemies), which Yahawah your Alahayam has given you.
Thus you shall do to all the Iyar which are very Rachawaq off from you, which are not of the Iyar of these gawayam (nations).
But of the Iyar of these im (peoples), that Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you for an nachalah (inheritance), you shall chayah (save) alive nothing that breathes;

but you shall charam (utterly) charam (destroy) them: the Chathay (Hittite), and the Amaray (Amorite), the Kanainay (Canaanite), and the Parazay (Perizzite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite); as Yahawah your Alahayam has tzawah (commanded) you;
that they not teach you to do after all their thawaibah (abominations), which they have done to their Alahayam; so would you chataa (sin) against Yahawah your Alahayam.

When you shall tzawar (besiege) a Iyar a rab (long) yawam (time), in making war against it to take it, you shall not shachath (destroy) its itz (trees) by wielding an axe against them; for you may akal (eat) of them, and you shall not karath (cut) them down; for is the itz (tree) of the shadah (field) adam (man), that it should be besieged of you?

Only the itz (trees) of which you yadai (know) that they are not itz (trees) for food, you shall shachath (destroy) and karath (cut) them down; and you shall banah (build) Matzawar against the Iyar that ishah (makes) war with you, until it yarad (fall).
If one be found Chalal in the adamah (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you to yarash (possess) it, napal (lying) in the shadah (field), and it isn't yadai (known) who has struck him;
then your zaqan (elders) and your shapat (judges) shall yatzaa (come) forth, and they shall measure to the Iyar which are around him who is Chalal:

and it shall be, that the Iyar which is nearest to the Chalal man, even the zaqan (elders) of that Iyar shall take a heifer of the herd, which hasn't been worked with, and which has not drawn in the yoke;

and the zaqan (elders) of that Iyar shall yarad (bring) down the Igalah to a nachal (valley) with running water, which is neither plowed nor sown, and shall break the Igalah neck there in the nachal (valley).

The kahan (priests) the ban (sons) of Laway shall come near; for them Yahawah your Alahayam has chosen to sharath (minister) to him, and to barak (bless) in the sham (name) of Yahawah; and according to their pah (word) shall every rayab (controversy) and every nagai (stroke) be.
All the zaqan (elders) of that Iyar, who are nearest to the Chalal rachatz (man), shall wash their yad (hands) over the Igalah whose neck was broken in the nachal (valley);
and they shall answer and amar (say), "Our yad (hands) have not shed this dam (blood), neither have our iyan (eyes) seen it.

kapar (forgive), Yahawah, your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), whom you have padah (redeemed), and don't allow naqay (innocent) dam (blood) in the qarab (midst) of your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel)." The dam (blood) shall be forgiven them.
So you shall bair (put) away the naqay (innocent) dam (blood) from the qarab (midst) of you, when you shall do that which is yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah.
When you yatzaa (go) forth to battle against your ayab (enemies), and Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (delivers) them into your yad (hands), and you carry them Shabay captive,
and raah (see) among the captives a beautiful ashah (woman), and you have a chashaq (desire) to her, and would take her to you as ashah (wife);
then you shall bawaa (bring) her home to your bayath (house); and she shall shave her raash (head), and ishah (pare) her nails;

and she shall sawar (put) the clothing of her Shabay from off her, and shall yashab (remain) in your bayath (house), and bewail her ab (father) and her am (mother) a yawam (full) yarach (month): and achar (after) that you shall bawaa (go) in to her, and be her bail (husband), and she shall be your ashah (wife).

It shall be, if you have no delight in her, then you shall let her shalach (go) where she will; but you shall not sell her at all for kasap (money), you shall not deal with her as a ashar (slave), because you have humbled her.

If a ayash (man) have shanayam (two) wives, the one beloved, and the other hated, and they have borne him children, both the beloved and the hated; and if the firstborn ban (son) be hers who was Shanayaa;

then it shall be, in the yawam (day) that he causes his ban (sons) to nachal (inherit) that which he has, that he may not make the ban (son) of the beloved the bakar (firstborn) panayam (before) the ban (son) of the hated, who is the firstborn:

but he shall nakar (acknowledge) the firstborn, the ban (son) of the hated, by giving him a shanayam (double) pah (portion) of all that he has; for he is the raashayath (beginning) of his awan (strength); the mashapat (right) of the firstborn is his.

If a ayash (man) have a stubborn and rebellious ban (son), who will not obey the qawal (voice) of his ab (father), or the qawal (voice) of his am (mother), and, though they chasten him, will not listen to them;
then shall his ab (father) and his am (mother) lay hold on him, and yatzaa (bring) him out to the zaqan (elders) of his Iyar, and to the gate of his place;
and they shall amar (tell) the zaqan (elders) of his Iyar, "This our ban (son) is stubborn and rebellious, he will not obey our qawal (voice); he is a glutton, and a drunkard.

All the men of his Iyar shall ragam (stone) him to mawath (death) with ragam (stones): so you shall bair (put) bair (away) the rai (evil) from the qarab (midst) of you; and all Yasharaal (Israel) shall hear, and yaraa (fear).
If a ayash (man) have committed a chataa (sin) mashapat (worthy) of mawath (death), and he be put to mawath (death), and you hang him on a itz (tree);

his nabalah (body) shall not remain all lawan (night) on the itz (tree), but you shall surely bury him the same yawam (day); for he who is hanged is accursed of Alahayam; that you don't tamaa (defile) your adamah (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you for an nachalah (inheritance).

You shall not raah (see) your ach (brother's) ox or his sheep go astray, and ilam (hide) yourself from them: you shall shawab (turn back / repent) shawab (turn back / repent) them again to your ach (brother).

If your ach (brother) isn't qarawab (near) to you, or if you don't yadai (know) him, then you shall asap (bring) it home to your bayath (house), and it shall be with you until your ach (brother) seek after it, and you shall shawab (turn back / repent) it to him.

So you shall do with his donkey; and so you shall do with his garment; and so you shall do with every lost thing of your ach (brother's), which he has lost, and you have found: you may not ilam (hide) yourself.
You shall not raah (see) your ach (brother's) donkey or his ox fallen down by the darak (way), and ilam (hide) yourself from them: you shall qawam (surely) qawam (help) him to lift them up again.
A ashah (woman) shall not wear men's clothing, neither shall a gabar (man) Labash on women's clothing; for whoever does these things is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah your Alahayam.

If a bird's nest chance to be panayam (before) you in the darak (way), in any itz (tree) or on the aratz (ground), with young aparach (ones) or eggs, and the hen sitting on the young, or on the eggs, you shall not take the hen with the ban (young):
you shall surely let the hen shalach (go), but the ban (young) you may take to yourself; that it may be yatab (well) with you, and that you may prolong your yawam (days).

When you banah (build) a Chadash bayath (house), then you shall ishah (make) a battlement for your roof, that you don't shawam (bring) dam (blood) on your bayath (house), if any man napal (fall) from there.
You shall not zarai (sow) your vineyard with two kinds of zarai (seed), lest the whole Malaah be forfeited, the zarai (seed) which you have sown, and the increase of the vineyard.
You shall not charash (plow) with an ox and a donkey together.
You shall not Labash a mixed stuff, wool and linen together.
You shall ishah (make) yourselves fringes on the arabai (four) borders of your cloak, with which you cover yourself.
If any ayash (man) takes a ashah (wife), and goes in to her, and shanaa (hates) her,

and accuses her of shameful things, and yatzaa (brings) up an rai (evil) sham (name) on her, and amar (says), "I took this ashah (woman), and when I came near to her, I didn't matzaa (find) in her the tokens of virginity;
then shall the ab (father) of the young lady, and her am (mother), take and yatzaa (bring) forth the tokens of the young lady's virginity to the zaqan (elders) of the Iyar in the gate;
and the young lady's ab (father) shall amar (tell) the zaqan (elders), "I gave my bath (daughter) to this ayash (man) to ashah (wife), and he shanaa (hates) her;

and behold, he has accused her of shameful things, saying, ‘I didn't matzaa (find) in your bath (daughter) the tokens of virginity;' and yet these are the tokens of my bath (daughter's) virginity." They shall spread the cloth panayam (before) the zaqan (elders) of the Iyar.
The zaqan (elders) of that Iyar shall take the ayash (man) and chastise him;

and they shall fine him one maah (hundred) shekels of kasap (silver), and nathan (give) them to the ab (father) of the young lady, because he has brought up an rai (evil) sham (name) on a virgin of Yasharaal (Israel): and she shall be his ashah (wife); he may not shalach (put) her away all his yawam (days).
But if this thing be amath (true), that the tokens of virginity were not found in the young lady;

then they shall yatzaa (bring) out the young lady to the door of her ab (father's) bayath (house), and the men of her Iyar shall saqal (stone) her to mawath (death) with saqal (stones), because she has done folly in Yasharaal (Israel), to play the prostitute in her ab (father's) bayath (house): so you shall bair (put) bair (away) the rai (evil) from the qarab (midst) of you.

If a ayash (man) be found lying with a ashah (woman) married to a bail (husband), then they shall shanayam (both) of them mawath (die), the ayash (man) who shakab (lay) with the ashah (woman), and the ashah (woman): so you shall bair (put) away the rai (evil) from Yasharaal (Israel).
If there is a young lady who is a virgin pledged to be married to a ayash (husband), and a ayash (man) matzaa (find) her in the Iyar, and shakab (lie) with her;

then you shall yatzaa (bring) them shanayam (both) out to the gate of that Iyar, and you shall saqal (stone) them to mawath (death) with aban (stones); the lady, because she didn't cry, being in the Iyar; and the ayash (man), because he has humbled his neighbor's ashah (wife): so you shall bair (put) away the rai (evil) from the qarab (midst) of you.

But if the ayash (man) matzaa (find) the lady who is pledged to be married in the shadah (field), and the ayash (man) chazaq (force) her, and shakab (lie) with her; then the ayash (man) only who shakab (lay) with her shall mawath (die):

but to the lady you shall do nothing; there is in the lady no chataa (sin) worthy of mawath (death): for as when a ayash (man) qawam (rises) against his neighbor, and ratzach (kills) him, even so is this dabar (matter);
for he found her in the shadah (field), the pledged to be married lady cried, and there was none to yashai (save) her.
If a ayash (man) matzaa (find) a lady who is a virgin, who is not pledged to be married, and lay hold on her, and shakab (lie) with her, and they be found;

then the ayash (man) who shakab (lay) with her shall nathan (give) to the lady's ab (father) chamashayam (fifty) shekels of kasap (silver), and she shall be his ashah (wife), because he has humbled her; he may not shalach (put) her away all his yawam (days).
A ayash (man) shall not take his ab (father's) ashah (wife), and shall not galah (uncover) his ab (father's) skirt.
He who is wounded in the patzai (stones), or has his privy member karath (cut) off, shall not bawaa (enter) into the qahal (assembly) of Yahawah.
A bastard shall not bawaa (enter) into the qahal (assembly) of Yahawah; even to the ishayaray (tenth) dawar (generation) shall none of his bawaa (enter) into the qahal (assembly) of Yahawah.

An Imawanay (Ammonite) or a Mawaabay (Moabite) shall not bawaa (enter) into the qahal (assembly) of Yahawah; even to the ishayaray (tenth) dawar (generation) shall none belonging to them bawaa (enter) into the qahal (assembly) of Yahawah iwalam (forever):

dabar (because) they didn't qadam (meet) you with lacham (bread) and with mayam (water) in the darak (way), when you came yatzaa (forth) out of Matzarayam, and because they hired against you Balaim the ban (son) of Baiwar from Pathawar of Aramanaharayam, to qalal (curse) you.
Nevertheless Yahawah your Alahayam wouldn't listen to Balaim; but Yahawah your Alahayam turned the qalalah (curse) into a barakah (blessing) to you, because Yahawah your Alahayam loved you.
You shall not seek their shalawam (peace) nor their tawab (prosperity) all your yawam (days) iwalam (forever).
You shall not abhor an Adamay (Edomite); for he is your ach (brother): you shall not abhor an Matzaray (Egyptian), because you lived as a foreigner in his aratz (land).
The children of the shalayashay (third) dawar (generation) who are yalad (born) to them shall bawaa (enter) into the qahal (assembly) of Yahawah.
When you yatzaa (go) forth in machanah (camp) against your ayab (enemies), then you shall shamar (keep) yourselves from every rai (evil) thing.

If there is among you any ayash (man) who is not tahawar (clean) by reason of that which happens him by layal (night), then shall he yatzaa (go) outside of the machanah (camp). He shall not bawaa (come) within the machanah (camp):
but it shall be, when evening panah (comes) on, he shall bathe himself in mayam (water); and when the shamash (sun) is down, he shall bawaa (come) within the machanah (camp).
You shall have a place also outside of the machanah (camp), where you shall yatzaa (go) forth abroad:

and you shall have a paddle among your weapons; and it shall be, when you yashab (sit) down abroad, you shall dig therewith, and shall shawab (turn back / repent) back and cover that which comes from you:

for Yahawah your Alahayam halak (walks) in the qarab (midst) of your machanah (camp), to natzal (deliver) you, and to nathan (give) up your ayab (enemies) panayam (before) you; therefore your machanah (camp) shall be qadawash (holy), that he may not raah (see) an irawah (unclean) thing in you, and shawab (turn back / repent) away from you.
You shall not deliver to his adawan (master) a ibad (servant) who is escaped from his adawan (master) to you:
he shall yashab (dwell) with you, in the qarab (midst) of you, in the place which he shall choose within one of your gates, where it pleases him tawab (best): you shall not yanah (oppress) him.
Qadashah shall be no prostitute of the bath (daughters) of Yasharaal (Israel), neither shall there be a qadash (sodomite) of the ban (sons) of Yasharaal (Israel).

You shall not bawaa (bring) the hire of a prostitute, or the wages of a dog, into the bayath (house) of Yahawah your Alahayam for any nadar (vow): for even shanayam (both) these are an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah your Alahayam.
You shall not lend on interest to your ach (brother); interest of kasap (money), interest of food, interest of anything that is lent on interest:

to a nakaray (foreigner) you may lend on interest; but to your ach (brother) you shall not lend on interest, that Yahawah your Alahayam may barak (bless) you in all that you put your yad (hand) to, in the aratz (land) where you bawaa (go) in to yarash (possess) it.

When you shall nadar (vow) a nadar (vow) to Yahawah your Alahayam, you shall not be slack to shalam (pay) it: for Yahawah your Alahayam will surely require it of you; and it would be chataa (sin) in you.
But if you shall chadal (forbear) to nadar (vow), it shall be no chataa (sin) in you.

That which is gone out of your shapah (lips) you shall shamar (observe) and do; according as you have vowed to Yahawah your Alahayam, a freewill nadabah (offering), which you have promised with your pah (mouth).
When you bawaa (come) into your neighbor's vineyard, then you may akal (eat) of inab (grapes) your fill at your napash (own) pleasure; but you shall not nathan (put) any in your vessel.
When you bawaa (come) into your neighbor's standing grain, then you may pluck the ears with your yad (hand); but you shall not move a sickle to your neighbor's standing grain.

When a ayash (man) takes a ashah (wife), and bail (marries) her, then it shall be, if she matzaa (find) no favor in his iyan (eyes), because he has found some unseemly thing in her, that he shall kathab (write) her a bill of divorce, and nathan (give) it in her yad (hand), and shalach (send) her out of his bayath (house).
When she is departed out of his bayath (house), she may halak (go) and be achar (another) ayash (man's) wife.

If the Acharawan ayash (husband) shanaa (hate) her, and kathab (write) her a bill of divorce, and nathan (give) it in her yad (hand), and shalach (send) her out of his bayath (house); or if the Acharawan ayash (husband) mawath (die), who took her to be his ashah (wife);

her raashawan (former) bail (husband), who sent her shalach (away), may not take her again to be his ashah (wife), achar (after) that she is defiled; for that is thawaibah (abomination) panayam (before) Yahawah: and you shall not cause the aratz (land) to chataa (sin), which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you for an nachalah (inheritance).

When a ayash (man) takes a Chadash ashah (wife), he shall not yatzaa (go) out in the tzabaa (army), neither shall he be assigned any dabar (business): he shall be naqay (free) at bayath (home) one Shanah, and shall Shamach his ashah (wife) whom he has taken.
No man shall take the mill or the upper millstone to chabal (pledge); for he takes a napash (life) in chabal (pledge).

If a ayash (man) be found stealing any of his ach (brothers) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and he deal with him as a makar (slave), or sell him; then that thief shall mawath (die): so you shall bair (put) bair (away) the rai (evil) from the qarab (midst) of you.

shamar (take) heed in the nagai (plague) of leprosy, that you shamar (observe) maad (diligently), and do according to all that the kahan (priests) the Lawayay (Levites) shall teach you: as I tzawah (commanded) them, so you shall shamar (observe) to do.
zakar (remember) what Yahawah your Alahayam did to Marayam, by the darak (way) as you came yatzaa (forth) out of Matzarayam.
When you do lend your neighbor any kind of loan, you shall not bawaa (go) into his bayath (house) to get his pledge.
You shall imad (stand) outside, and the ayash (man) to whom you do lend shall yatzaa (bring) forth the pledge outside to you.
If he be a Inay ayash (man), you shall not sleep with his pledge;

you shall shawab (turn back / repent) shawab (turn back / repent) to him the pledge when the shamash (sun) goes down, that he may sleep in his garment, and barak (bless) you: and it shall be tzadaqah (righteousness) to you panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam.
You shall not oppress a hired shakayar (servant) who is Inay and Abayawan, whether he be of your ach (brothers), or of your foreigners who are in your aratz (land) within your gates:

in his yawam (day) you shall nathan (give) him his hire, neither shall the shamash (sun) bawaa (go) down on it; for he is Inay, and nashaa (sets) his napash (heart) on it: lest he qaraa (cry) against you to Yahawah, and it be chataa (sin) to you.

The abawath (fathers) shall not be put to mawath (death) for the children, neither shall the children be put to mawath (death) for the abawath (fathers): every ayash (man) shall be put to mawath (death) for his own chataa (sin).
You shall not deprive the foreigner, or the fatherless of justice, nor take a alamanah (widow's) clothing in chabal (pledge);
but you shall zakar (remember) that you were a ibad (bondservant) in Matzarayam, and Yahawah your Alahayam padah (redeemed) you there: therefore I tzawah (command) you to do this thing.

When you reap your harvest in your shadah (field), and have forgot a sheaf in the shadah (field), you shall not shawab (turn back / repent) again to get it: it shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the alamanah (widow); that Yahawah your Alahayam may barak (bless) you in all the maishah (work) of your yad (hands).
When you beat your olive tree, you shall not paar (go) over the boughs again: it shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the alamanah (widow).
