When you harvest your vineyard, you shall not ilal (glean) it achar (after) yourselves: it shall be for the foreigner, for the fatherless, and for the alamanah (widow).
You shall zakar (remember) that you were a ibad (bondservant) in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam: therefore I tzawah (command) you to do this thing.

If there is a rayab (controversy) between men, and they come to mashapat (judgment), and the shapat (judges) judge them; then they shall justify the tzadayaq (righteous), and rashai (condemn) the rashai (wicked);

and it shall be, if the rashai (wicked) man be ban (worthy) to be beaten, that the shapat (judge) shall napal (cause) him to lie down, and to be beaten before his panayam (face), according to his rashaih (wickedness), by number.
arabaiyam (forty) stripes he may give him, he shall not exceed; lest, if he should exceed, and beat him above these with many makah (stripes), then your ach (brother) should qalah (seem) vile to you.
You shall not muzzle the ox when he treads out the grain.

If ach (brothers) yashab (dwell) together, and one of them mawath (die), and have no ban (son), the ashah (wife) of the mawath (dead) shall not be married outside to a stranger: her husband's yabam (brother) shall bawaa (go) in to her, and take her to him as ashah (wife), and perform the duty of a husband's yabam (brother) to her.
It shall be, that the firstborn whom she bears shall qawam (succeed) in the sham (name) of his ach (brother) who is mawath (dead), that his sham (name) not be blotted out of Yasharaal (Israel).

If the ayash (man) doesn't want to take his yabamath (brother's) wife, then his yabamath (brother's) wife shall ilah (go) up to the gate to the zaqan (elders), and amar (say), "My husband's yabam (brother) refuses to qawam (raise) up to his yabam (brother) a sham (name) in Yasharaal (Israel); he will not perform the duty of a husband's yabam (brother) to me.
Then the zaqan (elders) of his Iyar shall qaraa (call) him, and dabar (speak) to him: and if he imad (stand), and amar (say), "I don't want to take her;

then his yabamath (brother's) wife shall come to him in the iyan (presence) of the zaqan (elders), and chalatz (loose) his shoe from off his ragal (foot), and spit in his panayam (face); and she shall answer and amar (say), "So shall it be done to the ayash (man) who does not banah (build) up his ach (brother's) bayath (house).
His sham (name) shall be called in Yasharaal (Israel), The bayath (house) of him who has his shoe untied.

When men strive together one with ach (another), and the ashah (wife) of the one qarab (draws) near to natzal (deliver) her ayash (husband) out of the yad (hand) of him who strikes him, and shalach (puts) forth her yad (hand), and chazaq (takes) him by the secrets;
then you shall cut off her kap (hand), your iyan (eye) shall have no pity.
You shall not have in your bag diverse aban (weights), a gadawal (great) and a qatan (small).
You shall not have in your bayath (house) diverse measures, a gadawal (great) and a qatan (small).

You shall have a Shalam and tzadaq (just) aban (weight). You shall have a Shalam and tzadaq (just) measure, that your yawam (days) may be long in the adamah (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you.
For all who do such things, all who do iwal (unrighteously), are an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah your Alahayam.
zakar (remember) what Imalaq did to you by the darak (way) as you came yatzaa (forth) out of Matzarayam;
how he met you by the darak (way), and struck the hindmost of you, all who were feeble achar (behind) you, when you were Iyap and Yagai; and he didn't yaraa (fear) Alahayam.

Therefore it shall be, when Yahawah your Alahayam has given you nawach (rest) from all your ayab (enemies) all around, in the aratz (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you for an nachalah (inheritance) to yarash (possess) it, that you shall machah (blot) out the zakar (memory) of Imalaq from under the sky; you shall not forget.
It shall be, when you have bawaa (come) in to the aratz (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you for an nachalah (inheritance), and yarash (possess) it, and yashab (dwell) therein,

that you shall take of the raashayath (first) of all the fruit of the adamah (ground), which you shall bawaa (bring) in from your aratz (land) that Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you; and you shall shawam (put) it in a basket, and shall halak (go) to the place which Yahawah your Alahayam shall choose, to cause his sham (name) to shakan (dwell) there.

You shall bawaa (come) to the kahan (priest) who shall be in those yawam (days), and amar (tell) him, "I nagad (profess) this yawam (day) to Yahawah your Alahayam, that I am bawaa (come) to the aratz (land) which Yahawah swore to our abawath (fathers) to nathan (give) us.
The kahan (priest) shall take the basket out of your yad (hand), and yanach (set) it down panayam (before) the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah your Alahayam.

You shall answer and say panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam, "A Aramay (Syrian) ready to abad (perish) was my ab (father); and he went down into Matzarayam, and lived there, Mait in number; and he became there a gaway (nation), gadawal (great), itzawam (mighty), and rab (populous).
The Matzaray (Egyptians) dealt ill with us, and afflicted us, and laid on us Qashah ibadah (bondage):
and we cried to Yahawah, the Alahayam of our abawath (fathers), and Yahawah heard our qawal (voice), and saw our affliction, and our imal (toil), and our oppression;

and Yahawah brought us yatzaa (forth) out of Matzarayam with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and with an natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm), and with gadawal (great) mawaraa (terror), and with awath (signs), and with mawapath (wonders);
and he has brought us into this place, and has given us this aratz (land), a aratz (land) flowing with milk and honey.

Now, behold, I have brought the paray (first) of the fruit of the adamah (ground), which you, Yahawah, have given me." You shall yanach (set) it down panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam, and shachah (worship) panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam.

You shall Shamach in all the tawab (good) which Yahawah your Alahayam has given to you, and to your bayath (house), you, and the Lawayay (Levite), and the foreigner who is in the qarab (midst) of you.

When you have made an kalah (end) of tithing all the maishar (tithe) of your increase in the shalayashay (third) Shanah, which is the Shanah of maishar (tithing), then you shall nathan (give) it Lawayay the Levite, to the foreigner, to the fatherless, and to the alamanah (widow), that they may akal (eat) within your gates, and be filled.

You shall amar (say) panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam, "I have bair (put) away the qadash (holy) things out of my bayath (house), and also have given them Lawayay the Levite, and to the foreigner, to the fatherless, and to the alamanah (widow), according to all your matzawah (commandment) which you have tzawah (commanded) me: I have not transgressed any of your matzawah (commandments), neither have I forgotten them:

I have not eaten of it in my awan (mourning), neither have I bair (put) away of it, being tamaa (unclean), nor given of it for the mawath (dead): I have listened to the qawal (voice) of Yahawah my Alahayam; I have done according to all that you have tzawah (commanded) me.

shaqap (look) down from your qadash (holy) habitation, from shamayam (heaven), and barak (bless) your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), and the adamah (ground) which you have given us, as you swore to our abawath (fathers), a aratz (land) flowing with milk and honey.

This yawam (day) Yahawah your Alahayam tzawah (commands) you to do these chaq (statutes) and mashapat (ordinances): you shall therefore shamar (keep) and do them with all your labab (heart), and with all your napash (soul).

You have declared Yahawah this yawam (day) to be your Alahayam, and that you would yalak (walk) in his darak (ways), and shamar (keep) his chaq (statutes), and his matzawah (commandments), and his mashapat (ordinances), and listen to his qawal (voice):
and Yahawah has declared you this yawam (day) to be a im (people) for his own sagalah (possession), as he has promised you, and that you should shamar (keep) all his matzawah (commandments);

and to nathan (make) you Ilayawan above all gawayam (nations) that he has made, in thahalah (praise), and in sham (name), and in honor; and that you may be a qadawash (holy) im (people) to Yahawah your Alahayam, as he has spoken.
Mashah and the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) tzawah (commanded) the im (people), saying, "shamar (keep) all the matzawah (commandment) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day).

It shall be on the yawam (day) when you shall ibar (pass) over the Yaradan to the aratz (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you, that you shall qawam (set) yourself up gadawal (great) aban (stones), and plaster them with plaster:

and you shall kathab (write) on them all the dabar (words) of this thawarah (law), when you have passed over; that you may bawaa (go) in to the aratz (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you, a aratz (land) flowing with milk and honey, as Yahawah, the Alahayam of your abawath (fathers), has promised you.

It shall be, when you have passed over the Yaradan, that you shall qawam (set) up these aban (stones), which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), in har (mount) Iyabal, and you shall plaster them with plaster.
There you shall banah (build) an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah your Alahayam, an mazabach (altar) of aban (stones): you shall lift up no barazal (iron) on them.
You shall banah (build) the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah your Alahayam Shalam uncut aban (stones); and you shall ilah (offer) burnt ilah (offerings) thereon to Yahawah your Alahayam:
and you shall zabach (sacrifice) shalam (peace) offerings, and shall akal (eat) there; and you shall Shamach panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam.
You shall kathab (write) on the aban (stones) all the dabar (words) of this thawarah (law) very plainly.

Mashah and the kahan (priests) the Lawayay (Levites) spoke to all Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "Keep silence, and listen, Yasharaal (Israel): this yawam (day) you have hayah (become) the im (people) of Yahawah your Alahayam.
You shall therefore obey the qawal (voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam, and do his matzawah (commandments) and his chaq (statutes), which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day).
Mashah tzawah (commanded) the im (people) the same yawam (day), saying,

"These shall imad (stand) on har (mount) Garazayam to barak (bless) the im (people), when you have passed over the Yaradan: Shamaiwan, and Laway, and Yahawadah (Judah), and Yashashakar, and Yawasap, and Banayamayan.
These shall imad (stand) on har (mount) Iyabal for the qalalah (curse): Raawaban, Gad, and Ashar, and Zabawalawan, Dan, and Napathalay.
The Lawayay (Levites) shall answer, and tell all the men of Yasharaal (Israel) with a loud qawal (voice),

‘Cursed is the ayash (man) who ishah (makes) an engraved or molten masakah (image), an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, the maishah (work) of the yad (hands) of the craftsman, and shawam (sets) it up in secret.' All the im (people) shall answer and amar (say), ‘aman (amen).'
‘Cursed is he who sets qalah (light) by his ab (father) or his am (mother).' All the im (people) shall amar (say), ‘aman (amen).'
‘Cursed is he who nasag (removes) his neighbor's landmark.' All the im (people) shall amar (say), ‘aman (amen).'
‘Cursed is he who makes the iwar (blind) to shagah (wander) out of the darak (way).' All the im (people) shall amar (say), ‘aman (amen).'
'Cursed is he who deprives the foreigner, fatherless, and alamanah (widow) of justice.' All the im (people) shall amar (say), ‘aman (amen).'
‘Cursed is he who lies with his ab (father's) ashah (wife), because he has uncovered his ab (father's) skirt.' All the im (people) shall amar (say), ‘aman (amen).'
‘Cursed is he who lies with any kind of animal.' All the im (people) shall amar (say), ‘aman (amen).'
‘Cursed is he who lies with his achawath (sister), the bath (daughter) of his ab (father), or the bath (daughter) of his am (mother).' All the im (people) shall amar (say), ‘aman (amen).'
‘Cursed is he who lies with his mother-in-law.' All the im (people) shall amar (say), ‘aman (amen).'
‘Cursed is he who strikes his neighbor in secret.' All the im (people) shall amar (say), ‘aman (amen).'
‘Cursed is he who takes a shachad (bribe) to kill an naqay (innocent) napash (person).' All the im (people) shall amar (say), ‘aman (amen).'
‘Cursed is he who doesn't qawam (confirm) the dabar (words) of this thawarah (law) to do them.' All the im (people) shall amar (say), ‘aman (amen).'

It shall happen, if you shall listen diligently to the qawal (voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam, to shamar (observe) to do all his matzawah (commandments) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), that Yahawah your Alahayam will nathan (set) you on Ilayawan above all the gawayay (nations) of the aratz (earth):
and all these barakah (blessings) shall bawaa (come) on you, and overtake you, if you shall listen to the qawal (voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam.
You shall be blessed in the Iyar, and you shall be blessed in the shadah (field).
You shall be blessed in the fruit of your body, the fruit of your adamah (ground), the fruit of your animals, the increase of your livestock, and the Ishatharah of your flock.
Your basket and your kneading trough shall be blessed.
You shall be blessed when you bawaa (come) in, and you shall be blessed when you yatzaa (go) out.

Yahawah will nathan (cause) your ayab (enemies) who qawam (rise) up against you to be struck panayam (before) you. They will yatzaa (come) out against you one darak (way), and will flee panayam (before) you shabai (seven) darak (ways).

Yahawah will tzawah (command) the barakah (blessing) on you in your barns, and in all that you put your yad (hand) to; and he will barak (bless) you in the aratz (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you.

Yahawah will qawam (establish) you for a qadawash (holy) im (people) to himself, as he has sworn to you; if you shall shamar (keep) the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah your Alahayam, and halak (walk) in his darak (ways).
All the im (peoples) of the aratz (earth) shall raah (see) that you are called by the sham (name) of Yahawah; and they shall be yaraa (afraid) of you.

Yahawah will yathar (make) you plenteous for tawab (good), in the fruit of your body, and in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your adamah (ground), in the adamah (land) which Yahawah swore to your abawath (fathers) to nathan (give) you.

Yahawah will pathach (open) to you his tawab (good) treasure in the sky, to nathan (give) the rain of your aratz (land) in its ith (season), and to barak (bless) all the maishah (work) of your yad (hand): and you shall lend to many gawayam (nations), and you shall not borrow.

Yahawah will nathan (make) you the raash (head), and not the tail; and you shall be above only, and you shall not be beneath; if you shall listen to the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah your Alahayam, which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), to shamar (observe) and to do,

and shall not sawar (turn) aside from any of the dabar (words) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), to the right yamayan (hand), or to the shamaawal (left), to yalak (go) achar (after) other Alahayam to ibad (serve) them.

But it shall come to pass, if you will not listen to the qawal (voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam, to shamar (observe) to do all his matzawah (commandments) and his chaqah (statutes) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), that all these qalalah (curses) shall bawaa (come) on you, and overtake you.
You shall be cursed in the Iyar, and you shall be cursed in the shadah (field).
Your basket and your kneading trough shall be cursed.
The fruit of your body, the fruit of your adamah (ground), the increase of your livestock, and the Ishatharah of your flock shall be cursed.
You shall be cursed when you bawaa (come) in, and you shall be cursed when you yatzaa (go) out.

Yahawah will shalach (send) on you cursing, mahawamah (confusion), and rebuke, in all that you put your yad (hand) to do, until you are destroyed, and until you abad (perish) Mahar; panayam (because) of the rai (evil) of your mailal (doings), by which you have forsaken me.
Yahawah will make the dabar (pestilence) cling to you, until he has consumed you from off the adamah (land), where you bawaa (go) in to yarash (possess) it.

Yahawah will strike you with consumption, and with fever, and with inflammation, and with fiery heat, and with the charab (sword), and with blight, and with mildew; and they shall pursue you until you abad (perish).
Your sky that is over your raash (head) shall be brass, and the aratz (earth) that is under you shall be barazal (iron).
Yahawah will nathan (make) the rain of your aratz (land) powder and ipar (dust): from the sky shall it yarad (come) down on you, until you are destroyed.

Yahawah will nathan (cause) you to be struck panayam (before) your ayab (enemies); you shall yatzaa (go) out one darak (way) against them, and shall flee shabai (seven) darak (ways) panayam (before) them: and you shall be tossed back and forth among all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (earth).
Your nabalah (dead) body shall be food to all birds of the sky, and to the animals of the aratz (earth); and there shall be none to frighten them away.
Yahawah will strike you with the boil of Matzarayam, and with the tumors, and with the scurvy, and with the charas (itch), of which you can not be healed.
Yahawah will strike you with madness, and with blindness, and with astonishment of labab (heart);

and you shall grope at noonday, as the iwar (blind) gropes in apalah (darkness), and you shall not tzalach (prosper) in your darak (ways): and you shall be only oppressed and robbed yawam (always), and there shall be none to yashai (save) you.

You shall betroth a ashah (wife), and achar (another) ayash (man) shall shakab (lie) with her: you shall banah (build) a bayath (house), and you shall not yashab (dwell) therein: you shall plant a vineyard, and shall not use its fruit.

Your ox shall be slain before your iyan (eyes), and you shall not akal (eat) of it: your donkey shall be violently taken away from before your panayam (face), and shall not be restored to you: your sheep shall be given to your ayab (enemies), and you shall have none to yashai (save) you.

Your ban (sons) and your bath (daughters) shall be given to achar (another) im (people); and your iyan (eyes) shall raah (see), and Kalah with longing for them all the yawam (day): and there shall be nothing in the al (power) of your yad (hand).
The fruit of your adamah (ground), and all your yagayai (labors), shall a im (nation) which you don't yadai (know) akal (eat) up; and you shall be only oppressed and crushed yawam (always);
so that you shall be mad for the sight of your iyan (eyes) which you shall raah (see).
Yahawah will strike you in the knees, and in the legs, with a rai (sore) boil, of which you can not be healed, from the kap (sole) of your ragal (foot) to the qadaqad (crown) of your head.

Yahawah will yalak (bring) you, and your malak (king) whom you shall qawam (set) over you, to a gaway (nation) that you have not yadai (known), you nor your abawath (fathers); and there you shall ibad (serve) other Alahayam, itz (wood) and aban (stone).
You shall become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all the im (peoples) where Yahawah shall lead you away.
You shall yatzaa (carry) much zarai (seed) out into the shadah (field), and shall asap (gather) Mait in; for the locust shall consume it.
You shall plant vineyards and ibad (dress) them, but you shall neither drink of the yayan (wine), nor harvest; for the worm shall akal (eat) them.
You shall have olive trees throughout all your borders, but you shall not anoint yourself with the shaman (oil); for your olives shall drop off.
You shall father ban (sons) and bath (daughters), but they shall not be yours; for they shall yalak (go) into Shabay.
All your itz (trees) and the fruit of your adamah (ground) shall the locust yarash (possess).
The foreigner who is in the qarab (midst) of you shall ilah (mount) up above you higher and higher; and you shall yarad (come) down lower and lower.
He shall lend to you, and you shall not lend to him: he shall be the raash (head), and you shall be the tail.

All these qalalah (curses) shall bawaa (come) on you, and shall pursue you, and overtake you, until you are destroyed; because you didn't listen to the qawal (voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam, to shamar (keep) his matzawah (commandments) and his chaqah (statutes) which he tzawah (commanded) you:
and they shall be on you for a awath (sign) and for a mawapath (wonder), and on your zarai (seed) iwalam (forever).
Because you didn't ibad (serve) Yahawah your Alahayam with joyfulness, and with tawab (gladness) of labab (heart), by reason of the abundance of all things;

therefore you shall ibad (serve) your ayab (enemies) whom Yahawah shall shalach (send) against you, in hunger, and in thirst, and in Iyaram, and in want of all things: and he shall nathan (put) a yoke of barazal (iron) on your neck, until he has destroyed you.
Yahawah will nashaa (bring) a gaway (nation) against you from Rachawaq, from the end of the aratz (earth), as the eagle flies; a gaway (nation) whose lashawan (language) you shall not understand;
a gaway (nation) of iz (fierce) facial expressions, that shall not nashaa (respect) the panayam (person) of the zaqan (old), nor show favor to the nair (young),

and shall akal (eat) the fruit of your livestock, and the fruit of your adamah (ground), until you are destroyed; that also shall not shaar (leave) you grain, new thayarawash (wine), or yatzahar (oil), the increase of your livestock, or the Ishatharah of your flock, until they have caused you to abad (perish).

They shall besiege you in all your gates, until your Gabah and fortified walls yarad (come) down, in which you trusted, throughout all your aratz (land); and they shall besiege you in all your gates throughout all your aratz (land), which Yahawah your Alahayam has given you.

You shall akal (eat) the fruit of your own body, the flesh of your ban (sons) and of your bath (daughters), whom Yahawah your Alahayam has given you, in the Matzawar and in the distress with which your ayab (enemies) shall distress you.

The ayash (man) who is Rak among you, and very Inag, his iyan (eye) shall be evil toward his ach (brother), and toward the ashah (wife) of his bosom, and toward the yathar (remnant) of his children whom he has remaining;

so that he will not nathan (give) to any of them of the flesh of his children whom he shall akal (eat), because he has nothing shaar (left) him, in the Matzawar and in the distress with which your ayab (enemy) shall distress you in all your gates.

The Rak and Inag nasah (woman) among you, who would not adventure to set the kap (sole) of her ragal (foot) on the aratz (ground) for delicateness and tenderness, her iyan (eye) shall be evil toward the ayash (husband) of her bosom, and toward her ban (son), and toward her bath (daughter),

and toward her young shalayah (one) who yatzaa (comes) out from between her feet, and toward her children whom she shall yalad (bear); for she shall akal (eat) them for want of all things secretly, in the Matzawar and in the distress with which your ayab (enemy) shall distress you in your gates.

If you will not shamar (observe) to do all the dabar (words) of this thawarah (law) that are written in this book, that you may yaraa (fear) this kabad (glorious) and fearful sham (name), Yahawah YOUR Alahayam;

then Yahawah will palaa (make) your makah (plagues) palaa (wonderful), and the makah (plagues) of your zarai (seed), even gadawal (great) makah (plagues), and of aman (long) continuance, and severe sicknesses, and of aman (long) continuance.
He will shawab (turn back / repent) on you again all the diseases of Matzarayam, which you were yagar (afraid) of; and they shall cling to you.
Also every sickness, and every makah (plague), which is not written in the book of this thawarah (law), Yahawah will ilah (bring) them on you, until you are destroyed.
You shall be shaar (left) Mait in number, whereas you were as the kawakab (stars) of the sky for multitude; because you didn't listen to the qawal (voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam.

It shall happen that as Yahawah rejoiced over you to do you yatab (good), and to multiply you, so Yahawah will rejoice over you to cause you to abad (perish), and to abad (destroy) you; and you shall be plucked from off the adamah (land) where you bawaa (go) in to yarash (possess) it.

Yahawah will scatter you among all im (peoples), from the qatzah (one) end of the aratz (earth) even to the other end of the earth; and there you shall ibad (serve) other Alahayam, which you have not yadai (known), you nor your abawath (fathers), even itz (wood) and aban (stone).

Among these gawayam (nations) you shall ragai (find) no ease, and there shall be no manawach (rest) for the kap (sole) of your ragal (foot): but Yahawah will nathan (give) you there a Ragaz lab (heart), and failing of iyan (eyes), and pining of napash (soul);
and your chay (life) shall hang in doubt before you; and you shall pachad (fear) layal (night) and yawamam (day), and shall have no aman (assurance) of your chay (life).

In the baqar (morning) you shall amar (say), "I wish it were evening!" and at evening you shall amar (say), "I wish it were baqar (morning)!" for the pachad (fear) of your labab (heart) which you shall pachad (fear), and for the sight of your iyan (eyes) which you shall raah (see).

Yahawah will shawab (turn back / repent) you into Matzarayam again with ships, by the darak (way) of which I said to you, You shall raah (see) it no more again: and there you shall sell yourselves to your ayab (enemies) for ibad (bondservants) and for bondmaids, and no man shall qanah (buy) you.

These are the dabar (words) of the barayath (covenant) which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah to karath (make) with the children of Yasharaal (Israel) in the aratz (land) of Mawaab, besides the barayath (covenant) which he made with them in Charab.

Mashah called to all Yasharaal (Israel), and said to them, You have seen all that Yahawah did before your iyan (eyes) in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam to Paraih, and to all his ibad (servants), and to all his aratz (land);
the gadawal (great) Masah which your iyan (eyes) saw, the awath (signs), and those gadawal (great) mawapath (wonders):
but Yahawah has not given you a lab (heart) to yadai (know), and iyan (eyes) to raah (see), and ears to hear, to this yawam (day).
I have led you arabaiyam (forty) Shanah in the madabar (wilderness): your clothes have not grown old on you, and your shoes have not grown old on your feet.
You have not eaten lacham (bread), neither have you drunk yayan (wine) or shakar (strong) drink; that you may yadai (know) that I am Yahawah your Alahayam.
When you came to this place, Sayachawan the malak (king) of Chashabawan, and Iwag the malak (king) of Bashan, came out qaraah (against) us to battle, and we struck them:

and we took their aratz (land), and gave it for an nachalah (inheritance) to the Raawabanay (Reubenites), and to the Gaday (Gadites), and to the chatzay (half) - shabat (tribe) of the Manashay (Manassites).
shamar (keep) therefore the dabar (words) of this barayath (covenant), and do them, that you may shakal (prosper) in all that you do.

You natzab (stand) this yawam (day) all of you panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam; your raash (heads), your shabat (tribes), your zaqan (elders), and your shatar (officers), even all the men of Yasharaal (Israel),
your little ones, your wives, and your foreigner who is in the midst of your machanah (camps), from the chatab (one) who cuts your itz (wood) to the one who shaab (draws) your mayam (water);
that you may ibar (enter) into the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah your Alahayam, and into his alah (oath), which Yahawah your Alahayam karath (makes) with you this yawam (day);

that he may qawam (establish) you this yawam (day) to himself for a im (people), and that he may be to you a Alahayam, as he spoke to you, and as he swore to your abawath (fathers), to Abaraham, to Yatzachaq, and to Yaiqab.
Neither with you only do I karath (make) this barayath (covenant) and this alah (oath),
but with him who imad (stands) here with us this yawam (day) panayam (before) Yahawah our Alahayam, and also with him who is not here with us this yawam (day)
(for you yadai (know) how we lived in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and how we came qarab (through) the midst of the gaway (nations) qarab (through) which you passed;
and you have seen their shaqawatz (abominations), and their idols, itz (wood) and aban (stone), kasap (silver) and gold, which were among them);

lest there should be among you ayash (man), or ashah (woman), or mashapachah (family), or shabat (tribe), whose labab (heart) panah (turns) away this yawam (day) from Yahawah our Alahayam, to yalak (go) to ibad (serve) the Alahayam of those gaway (nations); lest there should be among you a root that bears gall and wormwood;

and it happen, when he hears the dabar (words) of this alah (curse), that he barak (bless) himself in his labab (heart), saying, "I shall have shalawam (peace), though I yalak (walk) in the stubbornness of my lab (heart), to sapah (destroy) the Rawah Tzamaa the dry.

Yahawah will not pardon him, but then the ap (anger) of Yahawah and his jealousy will ishan (smoke) against that ayash (man), and all the alah (curse) that is written in this book shall rabatz (lie) on him, and Yahawah will machah (blot) out his sham (name) from under the sky.

Yahawah will set him apart to rai (evil) out of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), according to all the alah (curses) of the barayath (covenant) that is written in this book of the thawarah (law).

The dawar (generation) to Acharawan, your children who shall qawam (rise) up achar (after) you, and the nakaray (foreigner) who shall bawaa (come) from a Rachawaq aratz (land), shall amar (say), when they raah (see) the makah (plagues) of that aratz (land), and the sicknesses with which Yahawah has made it chalah (sick);

and that the whole aratz (land) of it is sulfur, Malach, and burning, that it is not sown, nor bears, nor any grass ilah (grows) therein, like the overthrow of Sadam and Imarah, Adamah and Tzabaayam, which Yahawah overthrew in his ap (anger), and in his chamah (wrath):
even all the gaway (nations) shall amar (say), "Why has Yahawah done thus to this aratz (land)? What does the heat of this gadawal (great) ap (anger) mean?

Then men shall amar (say), "Because they forsook the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers), which he made with them when he brought them yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam,
and went and served other Alahayam, and worshiped them, Alahayam that they didn't yadai (know), and that he had not given to them:
therefore the ap (anger) of Yahawah was kindled against this aratz (land), to bawaa (bring) on it all the qalalah (curse) that is written in this book;

and Yahawah rooted them out of their adamah (land) in ap (anger), and in chamah (wrath), and in gadawal (great) qatzap (indignation), and cast them into achar (another) aratz (land), as at this yawam (day).
The secret things belong to Yahawah our Alahayam; but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children iwalam (forever), that we may do all the dabar (words) of this thawarah (law).

It shall happen, when all these things have bawaa (come) on you, the barakah (blessing) and the qalalah (curse), which I have nathan (set) panayam (before) you, and you shall shawab (turn back / repent) them to labab (mind) among all the gawayam (nations), where Yahawah your Alahayam has driven you,

and shall shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah your Alahayam, and shall obey his qawal (voice) according to all that I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), you and your children, with all your labab (heart), and with all your napash (soul);

that then Yahawah your Alahayam will shawab (turn back / repent) your captivity, and have racham (compassion) on you, and will shawab (turn back / repent) and gather you from all the im (peoples), where Yahawah your Alahayam has scattered you.
If your outcasts are in the uttermost parts of the shamayam (heavens), from there will Yahawah your Alahayam gather you, and from there he will bring you back:

and Yahawah your Alahayam will bawaa (bring) you into the aratz (land) which your abawath (fathers) possessed, and you shall yarash (possess) it; and he will do you yatab (good), and multiply you above your abawath (fathers).

Yahawah your Alahayam will mawal (circumcise) your labab (heart), and the labab (heart) of your zarai (seed), to ahab (love) Yahawah your Alahayam with all your labab (heart), and with all your napash (soul), that you may chay (live).
Yahawah your Alahayam will nathan (put) all these alah (curses) on your ayab (enemies), and on those who shanaa (hate) you, who persecuted you.
You shall shawab (turn back / repent) and obey the qawal (voice) of Yahawah, and do all his matzawah (commandments) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day).

Yahawah your Alahayam will yathar (make) you plenteous in all the maishah (work) of your yad (hand), in the fruit of your body, and in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your adamah (ground), for tawab (good): for Yahawah will again rejoice over you for tawab (good), as he rejoiced over your abawath (fathers);

if you shall obey the qawal (voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam, to shamar (keep) his matzawah (commandments) and his chaqah (statutes) which are written in this book of the thawarah (law); if you shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah your Alahayam with all your labab (heart), and with all your napash (soul).
For this matzawah (commandment) which I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day), it is not palaa (too) hard for you, neither is it Rachawaq off.
It is not in shamayam (heaven), that you should amar (say), "Who shall ilah (go) up for us to shamayam (heaven), and bring it to us, and make us to hear it, that we may do it?
Neither is it ibar (beyond) the yam (sea), that you should amar (say), "Who shall ibar (go) over the yam (sea) for us, and bring it to us, and make us to hear it, that we may do it?
But the dabar (word) is very qarawab (near) to you, in your pah (mouth), and in your labab (heart), that you may do it.
raah (see), I have nathan (set) panayam (before) you this yawam (day) chay (life) and tawab (good), and mawath (death) and rai (evil);

in that I tzawah (command) you this yawam (day) to ahab (love) Yahawah your Alahayam, to yalak (walk) in his darak (ways), and to shamar (keep) his matzawah (commandments) and his chaqah (statutes) and his mashapat (ordinances), that you may chayah (live) and multiply, and that Yahawah your Alahayam may barak (bless) you in the aratz (land) where you bawaa (go) in to yarash (possess) it.
But if your labab (heart) panah (turns) away, and you will not hear, but shall be drawn away, and shachah (worship) other Alahayam, and ibad (serve) them;

I nagad (denounce) to you this yawam (day), that you shall abad (surely) abad (perish); you shall not prolong your yawam (days) in the adamah (land), where you ibar (pass) over the Yaradan to bawaa (go) in to yarash (possess) it.

I iwad (call) shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth) to iwad (witness) against you this yawam (day), that I have nathan (set) panayam (before) you chay (life) and mawath (death), the barakah (blessing) and the qalalah (curse): therefore choose chay (life), that you may chayah (live), you and your zarai (seed);

to ahab (love) Yahawah your Alahayam, to obey his qawal (voice), and to cling to him; for he is your chay (life), and the arak (length) of your yawam (days); that you may yashab (dwell) in the adamah (land) which Yahawah swore to your abawath (fathers), to Abaraham, to Yatzachaq, and to Yaiqab, to nathan (give) them.
Mashah went and spoke these dabar (words) to all Yasharaal (Israel).

He said to them, "I am one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) this yawam (day); I can no more yatzaa (go) out and bawaa (come) in: and Yahawah has said to me, ‘You shall not ibar (go) over this Yaradan.'

Yahawah your Alahayam, he will ibar (go) over panayam (before) you; he will destroy these gawayam (nations) from panayam (before) you, and you shall yarash (dispossess) them. Yahawashawai shall ibar (go) over panayam (before) you, as Yahawah has spoken.
Yahawah will do to them as he did to Sayachawan and to Iwag, the malak (kings) of the Amaray (Amorites), and to their aratz (land); whom he destroyed.
Yahawah will nathan (deliver) them up panayam (before) you, and you shall do to them according to all the matzawah (commandment) which I have tzawah (commanded) you.

Be chazaq (strong) and amatz (courageous), don't be yaraa (afraid), nor be scared of them: for Yahawah your Alahayam, he it is who does halak (go) with you; he will not rapah (fail) you, nor forsake you.

Mashah called to Yahawashawai, and said to him in the iyan (sight) of all Yasharaal (Israel), "Be chazaq (strong) and amatz (courageous): for you shall bawaa (go) with this im (people) into the aratz (land) which Yahawah has sworn to their abawath (fathers) to nathan (give) them; and you shall nachal (cause) them to inherit it.
Yahawah, he it is who does halak (go) panayam (before) you; he will be with you, he will not rapah (fail) you, neither forsake you: don't be yaraa (afraid), neither be dismayed.

Mashah wrote this thawarah (law), and delivered it to the kahan (priests) the ban (sons) of Laway, who bore the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, and to all the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Mashah tzawah (commanded) them, saying, "At the end of every shabai (seven) Shanah, in the mawaid (set) time of the Shanah of release, in the chag (feast) of sakah (tents),

when all Yasharaal (Israel) has bawaa (come) to raah (see) panayam (before) Yahawah your Alahayam in the place which he shall choose, you shall qaraa (read) this thawarah (law) before all Yasharaal (Israel) in their hearing.

Assemble the im (people), the men and the women and the little ones, and your foreigner who is within your gates, that they may hear, and that they may learn, and yaraa (fear) Yahawah your Alahayam, and shamar (observe) to do all the dabar (words) of this thawarah (law);

and that their children, who have not yadai (known), may hear, and learn to yaraa (fear) Yahawah your Alahayam, as yawam (long) as you chay (live) in the adamah (land) where you ibar (go) over the Yaradan to yarash (possess) it.

Yahawah said to Mashah, "Behold, your yawam (days) qarab (approach) that you must mawath (die): qaraa (call) Yahawashawai, and present yourselves in the ahal (tent) of Meeting, that I may commission him." Mashah and Yahawashawai went, and presented themselves in the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
Yahawah raah (see) in the ahal (tent) in a pillar of cloud: and the pillar of cloud stood over the door of the ahal (tent).

Yahawah said to Mashah, "Behold, you shall sleep with your abawath (fathers); and this im (people) will qawam (rise) up, and play the prostitute achar (after) the strange Alahayam of the aratz (land), where they bawaa (go) to be qarab (among) them, and will forsake me, and parar (break) my barayath (covenant) which I have made with them.

Then my ap (anger) shall be kindled against them in that yawam (day), and I will forsake them, and I will hide my panayam (face) from them, and they shall be devoured, and many rai (evils) and tzarah (troubles) shall matzaa (come) on them; so that they will amar (say) in that yawam (day), ‘Haven't these rai (evils) matzaa (come) on us because our Alahayam is not qarab (among) us?'
I will surely hide my panayam (face) in that yawam (day) for all the rai (evil) which they shall have worked, in that they are turned to other Alahayam.

"Now therefore kathab (write) this song for yourselves, and teach it to the children of Yasharaal (Israel): shawam (put) it in their pah (mouths), that this song may be a witness for me against the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

For when I shall have brought them into the adamah (land) which I swore to their abawath (fathers), flowing with milk and honey, and they shall have eaten and filled themselves, and grown fat; then will they panah (turn) to other Alahayam, and ibad (serve) them, and despise me, and parar (break) my barayath (covenant).

It shall happen, when many rai (evils) and tzarah (troubles) have matzaa (come) on them, that this song shall testify panayam (before) them as a witness; for it shall not be forgotten out of the pah (mouths) of their zarai (seed): for I yadai (know) their yatzar (imagination) which they frame this yawam (day), before I have brought them into the aratz (land) which I swore.
So Mashah wrote this song the same yawam (day), and taught it the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

He commissioned Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan, and said, "Be chazaq (strong) and amatz (courageous); for you shall bawaa (bring) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) into the aratz (land) which I swore to them: and I will be with you.
It happened, when Mashah had made an kalah (end) of writing the dabar (words) of this thawarah (law) in a book, until they were finished,
that Mashah tzawah (commanded) the Lawayay (Levites), who bore the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, saying,
"Take this book of the thawarah (law), and shawam (put) it by the side of the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah your Alahayam, that it may be there for a witness against you.

For I yadai (know) your rebellion, and your Qashah neck: behold, while I am yet chay (alive) with you this yawam (day), you have been rebellious against Yahawah; and how much more achar (after) my mawath (death)?

Assemble to me all the zaqan (elders) of your shabat (tribes), and your shatar (officers), that I may dabar (speak) these dabar (words) in their ears, and iwad (call) shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth) to iwad (witness) against them.

For I yadai (know) that achar (after) my mawath (death) you will shachath (utterly) shachath (corrupt) yourselves, and sawar (turn) aside from the darak (way) which I have tzawah (commanded) you; and rai (evil) will happen to you in the acharayath (latter) yawam (days); because you will do that which is rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, to provoke him to kais (anger) through the maishah (work) of your yad (hands).
Mashah spoke in the ears of all the qahal (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel) the dabar (words) of this song, until they were finished.
Give ear, you shamayam (heavens), and I will dabar (speak). Let the aratz (earth) hear the amar (words) of my pah (mouth).
My doctrine shall drop as the rain. My amarah (sayings) shall condense as the dew, as the small rain on the tender grass, as the showers on the herb.
For I will qaraa (proclaim) the sham (name) of Yahawah. Ascribe greatness to our Alahayam!
The tzawar (rock), his pail (work) is thamayam (perfect), for all his darak (ways) are justice: a Al of amawanah (faithfulness) and without iwal (iniquity), tzadayaq (just) and yashar (right) is he.
They have dealt corruptly with him. They are not his children, because of their defect. They are a Iqash and Pathalathal dawar (generation).
Do you thus gamal (requite) Yahawah, foolish im (people) and unwise? Isn't he your ab (father) who has bought you? He has made you, and established you.

zakar (remember) the yawam (days) of old. bayan (consider) the Shanah of many dawar (generations). shaal (ask) your ab (father), and he will show you; your zaqan (elders), and they will amar (tell) you.

When the Most Ilayawan gave to the gawayam (nations) their nachal (inheritance), when he separated the children of men, he natzab (set) the bounds of the im (peoples) according to the number of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
For yahawah (yahweh's) chalaq (portion) is his im (people). Yaiqab is the lot of his nachalah (inheritance).
He found him in a madabar (desert) aratz (land), in the thahaw (waste) howling yashayamawan (wilderness). He surrounded him. He cared for him. He kept him as the apple of his iyan (eye).
As an eagle that stirs up her nest, that flutters over her young, he spread abroad his wings, he took them, he bore them on his feathers.
Yahawah badad (alone) led him. There was no foreign Al with him.

He made him ride on the bamah (high) places of the aratz (earth). He ate the increase of the shadah (field). He caused him to suck honey out of the salai (rock), shaman (oil) out of the flinty tzawar (rock);

Butter of the herd, and milk of the flock, with fat of lambs, ayal (rams) of the ban (breed) of Bashan, and goats, with the finest of the wheat. Of the dam (blood) of the inab (grape) you drank shathah (wine).

But Yasharawan grew fat, and kicked. You have grown fat. You have grown thick. You have become sleek. Then he forsook Alawah who made him, and lightly esteemed the tzawar (rock) of his yashawaih (salvation).
They moved him to jealousy with zawar (strange) Alahayam. They provoked him to anger with thawaibah (abominations).
They sacrificed to demons, not Alawah, to Alahayam that they didn't yadai (know), to Chadash Alahayam that came up recently, which your abawath (fathers) didn't dread.
Of the tzawar (rock) who became your father, you are unmindful, and have forgotten Al who gave you birth.
Yahawah saw and abhorred, because of the kais (provocation) of his ban (sons) and his bath (daughters).
He said, "I will hide my panayam (face) from them. I will raah (see) what their acharayath (end) shall be; for they are a very perverse dawar (generation), children in whom is no faithfulness.

They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not Al. They have provoked me to kais (anger) with their vanities. I will move them to jealousy with those who are not a im (people). I will provoke them to kais (anger) with a foolish gaway (nation).

For a ash (fire) is kindled in my ap (anger), yaqad (burns) Thachathay the lowest shaawal (sheol), akal (devours) the aratz (earth) with its increase, and sets the foundations of the har (mountains) on lahat (fire).
"I will sapah (heap) rai (evils) on them. I will kalah (spend) my chatz (arrows) on them.

They shall be Mazah with hunger, and devoured with burning heat and Marayaray destruction. I will shalach (send) the teeth of animals on them, With the chamah (poison) of crawling things of the ipar (dust).
Outside the charab (sword) shall shakal (bereave), and in the rooms, ayamah (terror); on both young bachawar (man) and virgin, The nursing infant with the gray-haired ayash (man).
I said, I would scatter them afar. I would make their zakar (memory) to shabath (cease) from among men;

were it not that I feared the kais (provocation) of the ayab (enemy), lest their tzar (adversaries) should judge wrongly, lest they should amar (say), ‘Our yad (hand) is exalted, Yahawah has not done all this.'
For they are a gaway (nation) abad (void) of itzah (counsel). There is no thabawan (understanding) in them.
Oh that they were chakam (wise), that they understood this, that they would bayan (consider) their acharayath (latter) end!
How could one chase a alap (thousand), and shanayam (two) put rababah (ten) alap (thousand) to flight, unless their tzawar (rock) had sold them, and Yahawah had delivered them up?
For their tzawar (rock) is not as our tzawar (rock), even our ayab (enemies) themselves being palayal (judges).
For their vine is of the vine of Sadam, of the fields of Imarah. Their inab (grapes) are inab (grapes) of gall, Their clusters are bitter.
Their yayan (wine) is the chamah (poison) of thanayan (serpents), The Akazar venom of asps.
"Isn't this laid up in store with me, sealed up among my treasures?

Vengeance is mine, and recompense, at the ith (time) when their ragal (foot) slides; for the yawam (day) of their calamity is at qarawab (hand). The things that are to Ithayad on them shall make haste.

For Yahawah will dayan (judge) his im (people), and have compassion on his ibad (servants), when he raah (see) that their yad (power) is azal (gone), There is apas (none) remaining, itzar (shut) up or left at large.
He will amar (say), "Where are their Alahayam, The tzawar (rock) in which they took refuge;
Which ate the fat of their zabach (sacrifices), And drank the yayan (wine) of their drink nasayak (offering)? Let them qawam (rise) up and help you! Let them be your protection.
"raah (see) now that I, even I, am he, There is no Alahayam with me. I mawath (kill), and I chayah (make) alive. I wound, and I heal. There is no one who can natzal (deliver) out of my yad (hand).
For I nashaa (lift) up my yad (hand) to shamayam (heaven), And amar (say), As I chay (live) iwalam (forever),

if I whet my glittering charab (sword), My yad (hand) achaz (take) hold on mashapat (judgment); I will shawab (turn back / repent) vengeance to my tzar (adversaries), and will shalam (recompense) those who shanaa (hate) me.

I will make my chatz (arrows) Shakar with dam (blood). My charab (sword) shall akal (devour) flesh with the dam (blood) of the Chalal and the captives, from the raash (head) of the leaders of the ayab (enemy).

Rejoice, you gawayam (nations), with his im (people), for he will avenge the dam (blood) of his ibad (servants). He will shawab (turn back / repent) vengeance to his tzar (adversaries), And will kapar (make) expiation for his adamah (land), for his im (people).
Mashah came and spoke all the dabar (words) of this song in the ears of the im (people), he and Hawashai the ban (son) of Nawan.
Mashah made an kalah (end) of speaking all these dabar (words) to all Yasharaal (Israel);

He said to them, "shawam (set) your labab (heart) to all the dabar (words) which I iwad (testify) to you this yawam (day), which you shall tzawah (command) your children to shamar (observe) to do, all the dabar (words) of this thawarah (law).

For it is no rayaq (vain) thing for you; because it is your chay (life), and through this thing you shall prolong your yawam (days) in the adamah (land), where you ibar (go) over the Yaradan to yarash (possess) it.
Yahawah spoke to Mashah that same yawam (day), saying,

"ilah (go) up into this har (mountain) of Ibarayam, to har (mount) Nabaw, which is in the aratz (land) of Mawaab, that is over panayam (against) Yarayachaw; and raah (see) the aratz (land) of Kanain, which I nathan (give) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel) for a achazah (possession);
and mawath (die) on the har (mountain) where you ilah (go) up, and be gathered to your im (people), as Aharawan your ach (brother) died on har (mount) Har, and was gathered to his im (people):

because you trespassed against me in the midst of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) at the mayam (waters) of Marayabah of Kadesh, in the madabar (wilderness) of Tzan; because you didn't qadash (sanctify) me in the midst of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
For you shall raah (see) the aratz (land) before you; but you shall not bawaa (go) there into the aratz (land) which I nathan (give) the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
This is the barakah (blessing), with which Mashah the ayash (man) of Alahayam blessed the children of Yasharaal (Israel) panayam (before) his mawath (death).

He said, "Yahawah came from Sayanay, And rose from Shaiyar to them. He shone forth from har (mount) Paaran. He came from the rababah (ten) thousands of qadash (holy) ones. At his right yamayan (hand) was a ashadath (fiery) dath (law) for them.
Yes, he chabab (loves) the im (people). All his qadawash (saints) are in your yad (hand). They sat down at your feet; each nashaa (receives) your dabarah (words).
Mashah tzawah (commanded) us a thawarah (law), An mawarashah (inheritance) for the qahalah (assembly) of Yaiqab.
He was malak (king) in Yasharawan, When the raash (heads) of the im (people) were gathered, All the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) together.
"Let Raawaban chayah (live), and not mawath (die); Nor let his men be few.

This is for Yahawadah (Judah). He said, "Hear, Yahawah, the qawal (voice) of Yahawadah (Judah). bawaa (bring) him in to his im (people). With his yad (hands) he contended for himself. You shall be a help against his tzar (adversaries).
Of Laway he said, "Your thamayam (thummim) and your awarayam (urim) are with your chasayad (godly) one, whom you proved at Masah, with whom you strove at the mayam (waters) of Marayabah;

who said of his ab (father), and of his am (mother), ‘I have not seen him;' Neither did he nakar (acknowledge) his ach (brothers), Nor did he yadai (know) his own children: For they have observed your amarah (sayings), and keep your barayath (covenant).

They shall teach Yaiqab your mashapat (ordinances), and Yasharaal (Israel) your thawarah (law). They shall shawam (put) incense ap (before) you, and whole burnt kalayal (offering) on your mazabach (altar).

Yahawah, barak (bless) his chayal (substance). Accept the pail (work) of his yad (hands). Strike through the hips of those who qawam (rise) up against him, of those who shanaa (hate) him, that they not qawam (rise) again.
Of Banayamayan he said, "The yadayad (beloved) of Yahawah shall shakan (dwell) in safety by him. He covers him all the yawam (day) long. He shakan (dwells) between his shoulders.
Of Yawasap he said, "His aratz (land) is blessed by Yahawah, for the precious things of the shamayam (heavens), for the dew, for the deep that couches beneath,
for the precious things of the fruits of the shamash (sun), for the precious things of the growth of the yarach (moons),
for the raash (chief) things of the qadam (ancient) harar (mountains), for the precious things of the iwalam (forever) Gabaih,

for the precious things of the aratz (earth) and its fullness, the ratzawan (good) will of him who lived in the bush. Let this bawaa (come) on the raash (head) of Yawasap, on the qadaqad (crown) of the head of him who was separate from his ach (brothers).

The firstborn of his herd, hadar (majesty) is his. His qaran (horns) are the qaran (horns) of the wild ox. With them he shall push all of the im (peoples), to the apas (ends) of the aratz (earth): They are the rababah (ten) thousands of Aparayam. They are the alap (thousands) of Manashah.
Of Zabawalawan he said, "Shamach, Zabawalawan, in your yatzaa (going) out; and Yashashakar, in your ahal (tents).

They shall qaraa (call) the im (peoples) to the har (mountain). There they will zabach (offer) zabach (sacrifices) of tzadaq (righteousness), for they shall draw out the abundance of the yam (seas), the hidden treasures of the sand.
Of Gad he said, "He who enlarges Gad is blessed. He shakan (dwells) as a labayaa (lioness), and tears the zarawai (arm), yes, the qadaqad (crown) of the head.

He provided the raashayath (first) part for himself, for there was the chaqaq (lawgiver's) chalaqah (portion) reserved. He came with the raash (heads) of the im (people). He executed the tzadaqah (righteousness) of Yahawah, His mashapat (ordinances) with Yasharaal (Israel).
Dan Dan he said, "Dan is a aray (lion's) cub that leaps out of Bashan.
Of Napathalay he said, "Napathalay, Shabai with favor, Malaa of the barakah (blessing) of Yahawah, yarash (possess) the yam (west) and the south.
Of Ashar he said, "Ashar is blessed with children. Let him be acceptable to his ach (brothers). Let him dip his ragal (foot) in shaman (oil).
Your bars shall be barazal (iron) and brass. As your yawam (days), so your dabaa (strength) will be.
"There is none like Al, Yasharawan, who rides on the shamayam (heavens) for your help, In his excellency on the shachaq (skies).
The qadam (eternal) Alahayam is your dwelling place. Underneath are the iwalam (forever) zarawai (arms). He thrust out the ayab (enemy) from panayam (before) you, and said, ‘Destroy!'
Yasharaal (Israel) shakan (dwells) in safety; the iyan (fountain) of Yaiqab badad (alone), In a aratz (land) of grain and new thayarawash (wine). Yes, his shamayam (heavens) drop down dew.

You are happy, Yasharaal (Israel). Who is like you, a im (people) saved by Yahawah, the magan (shield) of your help, the charab (sword) of your excellency! Your ayab (enemies) shall submit themselves to you. You shall tread on their bamah (high) places.

Mashah went up from the irabah (plains) of Mawaab to har (mount) Nabaw, to the raash (top) of Pasagah, that is over panayam (against) Yarayachaw. Yahawah showed him all the aratz (land) of Galaid, Dan Dan,
and all Napathalay, and the aratz (land) of Aparayam and Manashah, and all the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah), Acharawan the hinder yam (sea),
and the Nagab, and the Plain of the Baqaih of Yarayachaw the Iyar of palm trees, to Tzair.

Yahawah said to him, "This is the aratz (land) which I swore to Abaraham, to Yatzachaq, and to Yaiqab, saying, ‘I will nathan (give) it to your zarai (seed).' I have caused you to raah (see) it with your iyan (eyes), but you shall not ibar (go) over there.
So Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah died there in the aratz (land) of Mawaab, according to the pah (word) of Yahawah.
He buried him in the Gayaa in the aratz (land) of Mawaab over against Bayathapaiwar Peor: but no ayash (man) yadai (knows) of his tomb to this yawam (day).
Mashah was one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) when he mawath (died): his iyan (eye) was not dim, nor his natural force abated.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) wept for Mashah in the irabah (plains) of Mawaab shalawashayam (thirty) yawam (days): so the yawam (days) of weeping in the mourning for Mashah were ended.

Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan was Malaa of the rawach (spirit) of chakamah (wisdom); for Mashah had laid his yad (hands) on him: and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) listened to him, and did as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
There has not arisen a nabayaa (prophet) iwad (since) in Yasharaal (Israel) like Mashah, whom Yahawah knew panayam (face) to panayam (face),
in all the awath (signs) and the mawapath (wonders), which Yahawah sent him to do in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, to Paraih, and to all his ibad (servants), and to all his aratz (land),
and in all the chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and in all the gadawal (great) mawaraa (terror), which Mashah worked in the iyan (sight) of all Yasharaal (Israel).
Now it happened achar (after) the mawath (death) of Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah, that Yahawah spoke to Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan, Mashah' sharath (servant), saying,

"Mashah my ibad (servant) is mawath (dead); now therefore qawam (arise), ibar (go) over this Yaradan, you, and all this im (people), to the aratz (land) which I nathan (give) to them, even to the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
I have given you every place that the kap (sole) of your ragal (foot) will tread on, as I told Mashah.

From the madabar (wilderness), and this Labanawan, even to the gadawal (great) nahar (river), the nahar (river) Parath, all the aratz (land) of the Chathay (Hittites), and to the gadawal (great) yam (sea) toward the going down of the shamash (sun), shall be your border.
No ayash (man) will be able to stand panayam (before) you all the yawam (days) of your chay (life). As I was with Mashah, so I will be with you. I will not rapah (fail) you nor forsake you.
"Be chazaq (strong) and amatz (courageous); for you shall cause this im (people) to nachal (inherit) the aratz (land) which I swore to their abawath (fathers) to nathan (give) them.

Only be chazaq (strong) and very amatz (courageous), to shamar (observe) to do according to all the thawarah (law), which Mashah my ibad (servant) tzawah (commanded) you. Don't sawar (turn) from it to the right yamayan (hand) or to the shamaawal (left), that you may have shakal (good) success wherever you yalak (go).

This book of the thawarah (law) shall not depart out of your pah (mouth), but you shall meditate on it yawamam (day) and layal (night), that you may shamar (observe) to do according to all that is written therein: for then you shall tzalach (make) your darak (way) prosperous, and then you shall have shakal (good) success.
Haven't I tzawah (commanded) you? Be chazaq (strong) and amatz (courageous). Don't be iratz (afraid), neither be dismayed: for Yahawah your Alahayam is with you wherever you yalak (go).
Then Yahawashawai tzawah (commanded) the shatar (officers) of the im (people), saying,

"ibar (pass) qarab (through) the midst of the machanah (camp), and tzawah (command) the im (people), saying, ‘kawan (prepare) food; for within shalawash (three) yawam (days) you are to ibar (pass) over this Yaradan, to bawaa (go) in to yarash (possess) the aratz (land), which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) you to yarash (possess) it.'
Yahawashawai spoke to the Raawabanay (Reubenites), and to the Gaday (Gadites), and to the chatzay (half) - shabat (tribe) of Manashah, saying,

"zakar (remember) the dabar (word) which Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah tzawah (commanded) you, saying, ‘Yahawah your Alahayam gives you nawach (rest), and will nathan (give) you this aratz (land).

Your wives, your little ones, and your livestock, shall live in the aratz (land) which Mashah gave you ibar (beyond) the Yaradan; but you shall ibar (pass) over panayam (before) your ach (brothers) armed, all the gabawar (mighty) chayal (men) of valor, and shall help them

until Yahawah has given your ach (brothers) nawach (rest), as he has given you, and they have also possessed the aratz (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam nathan (gives) them. Then you shall shawab (turn back / repent) to the aratz (land) of your yarashah (possession), and possess it, which Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah gave you ibar (beyond) the Yaradan toward the sunrise.'
They answered Yahawashawai, saying, "All that you have tzawah (commanded) us we will do, and wherever you shalach (send) us we will yalak (go).
Just as we listened to Mashah in all things, so will we listen to you. Only may Yahawah your Alahayam be with you, as he was with Mashah.

ayash (whoever) rebels against your commandment, and doesn't listen to your dabar (words) in all that you tzawah (command) him, he shall be put to mawath (death). Only be chazaq (strong) and amatz (courageous).

Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan Charash sent shanayam (two) men out of Shatayam as spies, saying, "yalak (go), raah (see) the aratz (land), including Yarayachaw." They went and came into the house of a prostitute whose sham (name) was Rachab, and slept there.
The malak (king) of Yarayachaw was told, "Behold, men of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) came in here tonight to spy out the aratz (land).

The malak (king) of Yarayachaw sent to Rachab, saying, "yatzaa (bring) out the men who have bawaa (come) to you, who have entered into your bayath (house); for they have bawaa (come) to spy out all the aratz (land).
The ashah (woman) took the shanayam (two) men and hid them. Then she said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I didn't yadai (know) where they came from.
It happened about the time of the shutting of the gate, when it was chashak (dark), that the men went out. Where the men went, I don't yadai (know). Pursue them Mahar; for you will overtake them.
But she had brought them up to the roof, and hid them with the itz (stalks) of flax, which she had laid in order on the roof.
The men pursued them the darak (way) to the Yaradan to the fords: and as soon as those who pursued them had gone out, they shut the gate.
Before they had laid down, she came up to them on the roof;

and she said to the men, "I yadai (know) that Yahawah has given you the aratz (land), and that the ayamah (fear) of you has fallen on us, and that all the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land) melt away panayam (before) you.

For we have heard how Yahawah dried up the mayam (water) of the Red yam (sea) panayam (before) you, when you came out of Matzarayam; and what you did to the shanayam (two) malak (kings) of the Amaray (Amorites), who were ibar (beyond) the Yaradan, to Sayachawan and to Iwag, whom you charam (utterly) destroyed.

As soon as we had heard it, our labab (hearts) melted, neither did there qawam (remain) any more rawach (spirit) in any ayash (man), panayam (because) of you: for Yahawah your Alahayam, he is Alahayam in shamayam (heaven) above, and on aratz (earth) beneath.

Now therefore, please shabai (swear) to me by Yahawah, since I have dealt chasad (kindly) with you, that you also will ishah (deal) chasad (kindly) with my ab (father's) bayath (house), and nathan (give) me a amath (true) awath (token);
and that you will chayah (save) alive my ab (father), my am (mother), my ach (brothers), and my achawath (sisters), and all that they have, and will natzal (deliver) our lives from mawath (death).

The men said to her, "Our napash (life) for yours, if you don't talk about this dabar (business) of ours; and it shall be, when Yahawah nathan (gives) us the aratz (land), that we will ishah (deal) chasad (kindly) and truly with you.
Then she let them down by a cord through the window; for her bayath (house) was on the side of the wall, and she lived on the wall.

She said to them, "yalak (go) to the har (mountain), lest the pursuers find you; and hide yourselves there shalawash (three) yawam (days), until the pursuers have returned. Afterward, you may yalak (go) your darak (way).
The men said to her, "We will be naqay (guiltless) of this your shabawaih (oath) which you have made us to shabai (swear).

Behold, when we bawaa (come) into the aratz (land), you shall qashar (bind) this line of scarlet thread in the window which you used to let us down. You shall asap (gather) to yourself into the bayath (house) your ab (father), your am (mother), your ach (brothers), and all your ab (father's) bayath (household).

It shall be that whoever goes out of the doors of your bayath (house) into the street, his dam (blood) will be on his raash (head), and we will be naqay (guiltless). Whoever is with you in the bayath (house), his dam (blood) shall be on our raash (head), if any yad (hand) is on him.
But if you talk about this dabar (business) of ours, then we shall be naqay (guiltless) of your shabawaih (oath) which you have made us to shabai (swear).
She said, "According to your dabar (words), so be it." She sent them shalach (away), and they departed. She tied the scarlet line in the window.

They went, and came to the har (mountain), and stayed there shalawash (three) yawam (days), until the pursuers had returned. The pursuers sought them throughout all the darak (way), but didn't matzaa (find) them.
Then the shanayam (two) men returned, descended from the har (mountain), passed over, and came to Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan; and they told him all that had happened to them.
They said to Yahawashawai, "Truly Yahawah has delivered into our yad (hands) all the aratz (land). Moreover, all the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land) melt away panayam (before) us.

Yahawashawai rose up shakam (early) in the baqar (morning); and they moved from Shatayam, and came to the Yaradan, he and all the children of Yasharaal (Israel). They lodged there before they passed over.
It happened after shalawash (three) yawam (days), that the shatar (officers) went qarab (through) the midst of the machanah (camp);

and they tzawah (commanded) the im (people), saying, "When you raah (see) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah your Alahayam, and the kahan (priests) the Lawayay (Levites) bearing it, then you shall move from your place, and halak (follow) it.

Yet there shall be a Rachawaq between you and it, about two alap (thousand) amah (cubits) by measure. Don't qarab (come) near to it, that you may yadai (know) the darak (way) by which you must yalak (go); for you have not passed this darak (way) thamawal (before).
Yahawashawai said to the im (people), "qadash (sanctify) yourselves; for tomorrow Yahawah will do wonders qarab (among) you.

Yahawashawai spoke to the kahan (priests), saying, "nashaa (take) up the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant), and ibar (pass) over panayam (before) the im (people)." They took up the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant), and went panayam (before) the im (people).
Yahawah said to Yahawashawai, "Today I will chalal (begin) to magnify you in the iyan (sight) of all Yasharaal (Israel), that they may yadai (know) that as I was with Mashah, so I will be with you.

You shall tzawah (command) the kahan (priests) who nashaa (bear) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant), saying, ‘When you bawaa (come) to the brink of the mayam (waters) of the Yaradan, you shall imad (stand) still in the Yaradan.'
Yahawashawai said to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), "Come here, and hear the dabar (words) of Yahawah your Alahayam.

Yahawashawai said, "Hereby you shall yadai (know) that the chay (living) Al is qarab (among) you, and that he will yarash (without) fail drive the Kanainay (Canaanite), and the Chathay (Hittite), and the Chaway (Hivite), and the Parazay (Perizzite), and the Garagashay (Girgashite), and the Amaray (Amorite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite) out from panayam (before) you.
Behold, the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of the Adawan of all the aratz (earth) passes over panayam (before) you into the Yaradan.
Now therefore take shanayam (twelve) men out of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), for achad (every) shabat (tribe) a ayash (man).

It shall come to pass, when the kap (soles) of the feet of the kahan (priests) who nashaa (bear) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, the Adawan of all the aratz (earth), nawach (rest) in the mayam (waters) of the Yaradan, that the mayam (waters) of the Yaradan will be karath (cut) off, even the mayam (waters) that yarad (come) down from above; and they shall imad (stand) in one heap.

It happened, when the im (people) moved from their ahal (tents) to ibar (pass) over the Yaradan, the kahan (priests) who bore the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) being panayam (before) the im (people),

and when those who bore the arawan (ark) had bawaa (come) to the Yaradan, and the feet of the kahan (priests) who bore the arawan (ark) had dipped in the edge of the mayam (water) (for the Yaradan malaa (overflows) all its banks all the yawam (time) of harvest),

that the mayam (waters) which came down from above stood, and rose up in one heap, a maad (great) rachaq (way) off, at adam (adam), the Iyar that is beside Tzarathan; and those that went down toward the yam (sea) of the irabah (arabah), even the Malach yam (sea), were wholly karath (cut) off. Then the im (people) passed over right against Yarayachaw.

The kahan (priests) who bore the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah stood kawan (firm) on dry charabah (ground) in the middle of the Yaradan; and all Yasharaal (Israel) passed over on dry charabah (ground), until all the gaway (nation) had passed completely over the Yaradan.
It happened, when all the gaway (nation) had completely passed over the Yaradan, that Yahawah spoke to Yahawashawai, saying,
"Take shanayam (twelve) men out of the im (people), out of achad (every) shabat (tribe) a ayash (man),

and tzawah (command) them, saying, ‘nashaa (take) from out of the middle of the Yaradan, out of the place where the kahan (priests)' feet stood kawan (firm), shanayam (twelve) aban (stones), and ibar (carry) them over with you, and yanach (lay) them down in the lodging place, where you will lawan (lodge) tonight.'
Then Yahawashawai called the shanayam (twelve) men, whom he had prepared of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), out of achad (every) shabat (tribe) a ayash (man).

Yahawashawai said to them, "ibar (pass) over panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah your Alahayam into the middle of the Yaradan, and achad (each) of you pick up a aban (stone) and put it on your shoulder, according to the number of the shabat (tribes) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel);
that this may be a awath (sign) qarab (among) you, that when your children shaal (ask) in time to come, saying, ‘What do you mean by these aban (stones)?'

then you shall amar (tell) them, ‘Because the mayam (waters) of the Yaradan were karath (cut) off panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah. When it passed over the Yaradan, the mayam (waters) of the Yaradan were karath (cut) off. These aban (stones) shall be for a zakarawan (memorial) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel) iwalam (forever).'

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) did as Yahawashawai tzawah (commanded), and took up shanayam (twelve) aban (stones) out of the middle of the Yaradan, as Yahawah spoke to Yahawashawai, according to the number of the shabat (tribes) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel); and they carried them over with them to the place where they lodged, and laid them down there.

Yahawashawai qawam (set) up shanayam (twelve) aban (stones) in the middle of the Yaradan, in the place where the feet of the kahan (priests) who bore the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) stood; and they are there to this yawam (day).

For the kahan (priests) who bore the arawan (ark) stood in the middle of the Yaradan, until everything was finished that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Yahawashawai to dabar (speak) to the im (people), according to all that Mashah tzawah (commanded) Yahawashawai; and the im (people) hurried and passed over.
It happened, when all the im (people) had completely passed over, that the arawan (ark) of Yahawah passed over, with the kahan (priests), in the panayam (presence) of the im (people).
The children of Raawaban, and the children of Gad, and the chatzay (half) - shabat (tribe) of Manashah, passed over armed panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), as Mashah spoke to them.
About arabaiyam (forty) alap (thousand) men, chalatz (ready) and armed for tzabaa (war) passed over panayam (before) Yahawah to battle, to the irabah (plains) of Yarayachaw.
On that yawam (day), Yahawah magnified Yahawashawai in the iyan (sight) of all Yasharaal (Israel); and they feared him, as they feared Mashah, all the yawam (days) of his chay (life).
Yahawah spoke to Yahawashawai, saying,
"tzawah (command) the kahan (priests) who nashaa (bear) the arawan (ark) of the idawath (testimony), that they ilah (come) up out of the Yaradan.
Yahawashawai therefore tzawah (commanded) the kahan (priests), saying, "ilah (come) up out of the Yaradan!

It happened, when the kahan (priests) who bore the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah had ilah (come) up out of the middle of the Yaradan, and the kap (soles) of the kahan (priests)' feet were lifted up to the dry charabah (ground), that the mayam (waters) of the Yaradan returned to their place, and went over all its banks, as shalashawam (before).
The im (people) came up out of the Yaradan on the tenth day of the raashawan (first) chadash (month), and encamped in Galagal, on the east border of Yarayachaw.
Yahawashawai qawam (set) up those shanayam (twelve) aban (stones), which they took out of the Yaradan, in Galagal.
He spoke to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "When your children shaal (ask) their abawath (fathers) in time to come, saying, ‘What do these aban (stones) mean?'
Then you shall let your children yadai (know), saying, ‘Yasharaal (Israel) came over this Yaradan on dry yabashah (dry land).

For Yahawah your Alahayam dried up the mayam (waters) of the Yaradan from panayam (before) you, until you had passed over, as Yahawah your Alahayam did to the Red yam (sea), which he dried up from panayam (before) us, until we had passed over;
that all the im (peoples) of the aratz (earth) may yadai (know) the yad (hand) of Yahawah, that it is chazaq (mighty); that you may yaraa (fear) Yahawah your Alahayam forever.'

It happened, when all the malak (kings) of the Amaray (Amorites), who were ibar (beyond) the Yaradan westward, and all the malak (kings) of the Kanainay (Canaanites), who were by the yam (sea), heard how that Yahawah had dried up the mayam (waters) of the Yaradan from panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), until we had passed over, that their labab (heart) melted, neither was there rawach (spirit) in them any more, panayam (because) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
At that ith (time), Yahawah said to Yahawashawai, "ishah (make) flint knives, and mawal (circumcise) again the children of Yasharaal (Israel) the shanay (second) time.
Yahawashawai made himself flint knives, and circumcised the children of Yasharaal (Israel) at the Gabaih of the foreskins.

This is the dabar (reason) Yahawashawai circumcised: all the im (people) who came out of Matzarayam, who were zakar (males), even all the men of war, died in the madabar (wilderness) by the darak (way), yatzaa (after) they came out of Matzarayam.
For all the im (people) who came out were circumcised; but all the im (people) who were Yalawad in the madabar (wilderness) by the darak (way) as they came out of Matzarayam had not been circumcised.

For the children of Yasharaal (Israel) walked arabaiyam (forty) Shanah in the madabar (wilderness), until all the gaway (nation), even the men of war who came out of Matzarayam, were consumed, because they didn't listen to the qawal (voice) of Yahawah. Yahawah swore to them that he wouldn't let them raah (see) the aratz (land) which Yahawah swore to their abawath (fathers) that he would nathan (give) us, a aratz (land) flowing with milk and honey.
Their children, whom he raised up in their place, were circumcised by Yahawashawai; for they were Iral, because they had not circumcised them on the darak (way).
It happened, when they were thamam (done) mawal (circumcising) all the gaway (nation), that they stayed in their places in the machanah (camp) until they were healed.
Yahawah said to Yahawashawai, "Today I have rolled away the reproach of Matzarayam from off you." Therefore the sham (name) of that place was called Galagal, to this yawam (day).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) encamped in Galagal. They kept the pasach (passover) on the fourteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month) at evening in the irabah (plains) of Yarayachaw.
They ate unleavened matzah (cakes) and parched grain of the produce of the aratz (land) on the next macharath (day) after the pasach (passover), in the same yawam (day).

The manna ceased on the next macharath (day), after they had eaten of the produce of the aratz (land). The children of Yasharaal (Israel) didn't have manna any more; but they ate of the fruit of the aratz (land) of Kanain that Shanah.

It happened, when Yahawashawai was by Yarayachaw, that he lifted up his iyan (eyes) and looked, and behold, a ayash (man) stood in front of him with his charab (sword) drawn in his yad (hand). Yahawashawai went to him, and said to him, "Are you for us, or for our tzar (adversaries)?

He said, "No; but I have bawaa (come) now as commander of yahawah (yahweh's) tzabaa (army)." Yahawashawai napal (fell) on his panayam (face) to the aratz (earth), and worshipped, and said to him, "What does my Adawan amar (say) to his ibad (servant)?
The shar (prince) of yahawah (yahweh's) tzabaa (army) said to Yahawashawai, "Take your shoes off of your feet; for the place on which you imad (stand) is qadash (holy)." Yahawashawai did so.
Now Yarayachaw was tightly shut up panayam (because) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel). No one went out, and no one came in.
