Yahawah said to Yahawashawai, "raah (see), I have given Yarayachaw into your yad (hand), with its malak (king) and the gabawar (mighty) men of valor.
All your men of war shall march around the Iyar, going around the Iyar paim (once). You shall do this shash (six) yawam (days).

shabai (seven) kahan (priests) shall nashaa (bear) shabai (seven) trumpets of rams' yawabal (horns) panayam (before) the arawan (ark). On the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), you shall march around the Iyar shabai (seven) paim (times), and the kahan (priests) shall blow the trumpets.

It shall be that when they make a long blast with the yawabal (ram's) qaran (horn), and when you hear the qawal (sound) of the trumpet, all the im (people) shall rawai (shout) with a gadawal (great) rawai (shout); and the wall of the Iyar shall napal (fall) down flat, and the im (people) shall ilah (go) up every ayash (man) straight before him.

Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan called the kahan (priests), and said to them, "nashaa (take) up the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant), and let shabai (seven) kahan (priests) nashaa (bear) shabai (seven) trumpets of rams' yawabal (horns) panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah.
They said to the im (people), "Advance! March around the Iyar, and let the chalatz (armed) men ibar (pass) on panayam (before) yahawah (yahweh's) arawan (ark).

It was so, that when Yahawashawai had spoken to the im (people), the shabai (seven) kahan (priests) bearing the shabai (seven) trumpets of rams' yawabal (horns) panayam (before) Yahawah advanced, and blew the trumpets; and the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah followed them.
The chalatz (armed) men went panayam (before) the kahan (priests) who blew the trumpets, and the arawan (ark) went achar (after) them. The trumpets sounded as they went.

Yahawashawai tzawah (commanded) the im (people), saying, "You shall not rawai (shout), nor let your qawal (voice) be heard, neither shall any dabar (word) yatzaa (proceed) out of your pah (mouth), until the yawam (day) I amar (tell) you to rawai (shout). Then you shall rawai (shout).
So he caused the arawan (ark) of Yahawah to sabab (go) around the Iyar, going naqap (about) it paim (once). Then they came into the machanah (camp), and lodged in the machanah (camp).
Yahawashawai rose shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and the kahan (priests) took up the arawan (ark) of Yahawah.

The shabai (seven) kahan (priests) bearing the shabai (seven) trumpets of rams' yawabal (horns) panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah went on halak (continually), and blew the trumpets: and the chalatz (armed) men went panayam (before) them. The rear guard came achar (after) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah. The trumpets sounded as they went.
The shanay (second) yawam (day) they marched around the Iyar paim (once), and returned into the machanah (camp). They did this shash (six) yawam (days).

It happened on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that they rose shakam (early) at the dawning of the shachar (day), and marched around the Iyar in the same way shabai (seven) paim (times). Only on this yawam (day) they marched around the Iyar shabai (seven) paim (times).
It happened at the shabayaiy (seventh) paim (time), when the kahan (priests) blew the trumpets, Yahawashawai said to the im (people), "rawai (shout), for Yahawah has given you the Iyar!

The Iyar shall be charam (devoted), even it and all that is in it, to Yahawah. Only Rachab the prostitute shall chayah (live), she and all who are with her in the bayath (house), because she hid the malaak (messengers) that we sent.

But as for you, only shamar (keep) yourselves from the charam (devoted) thing, lest when you have devoted it, you take of the charam (devoted) thing; so would you shawam (make) the machanah (camp) of Yasharaal (Israel) accursed, and trouble it.
But all the kasap (silver), and gold, and vessels of brass and barazal (iron), are qadash (holy) to Yahawah. They shall bawaa (come) into yahawah (yahweh's) treasury.

So the im (people) shouted, and the thaqai (priests) blew the trumpets. It happened, when the im (people) heard the qawal (sound) of the trumpet, that the im (people) shouted with a gadawal (great) shout, and the wall napal (fell) down flat, so that the im (people) went up into the Iyar, every ayash (man) lakad (straight) before him, and they took the Iyar.

They charam (utterly) destroyed all that was in the Iyar, both ayash (man) and ashah (woman), both nair (young) and zaqan (old), and ox, and sheep, and donkey, with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).

Yahawashawai said to the shanayam (two) men who had spied out the aratz (land), "bawaa (go) into the prostitute's bayath (house), and yatzaa (bring) out from there the ashah (woman) and all that she has, as you swore to her.

The nair (young) men who were spies went in, and brought out Rachab with her ab (father), her am (mother), her ach (brothers), and all that she had. They also brought out all her relatives, and they yanach (set) them outside of the machanah (camp) of Yasharaal (Israel).

They burnt the Iyar with ash (fire), and all that was in it. Only they nathan (put) the kasap (silver), the gold, and the vessels of brass and of barazal (iron) into the treasury of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house).

But Rachab the prostitute, her ab (father's) bayath (household), and all that she had, Yahawashawai saved chayah (alive). She lived in the midst of Yasharaal (Israel) to this yawam (day), because she hid the malaak (messengers), whom Yahawashawai sent to spy out Yarayachaw.

Yahawashawai commanded them with an oath at that ith (time), saying, "Cursed is the ayash (man) panayam (before) Yahawah, who qawam (rises) up and banah (builds) this Iyar Yarayachaw. With the loss of his firstborn shall he yasad (lay) its foundation, and Tzaiyar the loss of his youngest son shall he natzab (set) up its gates.
So Yahawah was with Yahawashawai; and his fame was in all the aratz (land).

But the children of Yasharaal (Israel) committed a mail (trespass) in the charam (devoted) things; for Ikan, the ban (son) of Karamay, the ban (son) of Zabaday, the ban (son) of Zarach, of the matah (tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah), took some of the charam (devoted) things. Therefore yahawah (yahweh's) ap (anger) burned against the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

Yahawashawai sent men from Yarayachaw to Iy, which is beside Bayathaawan Aven, on the qadam (east) side of Bayathaal, and spoke to them, saying, "ilah (go) up and spy out the aratz (land)." The men went up and spied out Iy.

They returned to Yahawashawai, and said to him, "Don't let all the im (people) ilah (go) up; but let about two or shalawash (three) alap (thousand) men ilah (go) up and strike Iy. Don't make all the im (people) to toil there, for there are only a Mait of them.
So about shalawash (three) alap (thousand) men of the im (people) went up there, and they fled panayam (before) the men of Iy.

The men of Iy struck about shalawashayam (thirty) - shash (six) men of them, and they chased them from panayam (before) the gate even to Shabarayam, and struck them at the descent. The labab (hearts) of the im (people) melted, and became like mayam (water).

Yahawashawai tore his clothes, and napal (fell) to the aratz (earth) on his panayam (face) panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah until the evening, he and the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel); and they ilah (put) ipar (dust) on their raash (heads).

Yahawashawai said, "Alas, Adanay Yahawah, why have you brought this im (people) over the Yaradan at all, to nathan (deliver) us into the yad (hand) of the Amaray (Amorites), to cause us to abad (perish)? I wish that we had been content and lived ibar (beyond) the Yaradan!
Oh, Adanay, what shall I amar (say), achar (after) that Yasharaal (Israel) has turned their backs panayam (before) their ayab (enemies)!

For the Kanainay (Canaanites) and all the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land) will hear of it, and will surround us, and karath (cut) off our sham (name) from the aratz (earth). What will you do for your gadawal (great) sham (name)?
Yahawah said to Yahawashawai, "qawam (get) up! Why are you fallen on your panayam (face) like that?

Yasharaal (Israel) has sinned. Yes, they have even transgressed my barayath (covenant) which I tzawah (commanded) them. Yes, they have even taken of the charam (devoted) things, and have also stolen, and also deceived. They have even shawam (put) it among their own stuff.

Therefore the children of Yasharaal (Israel) can't qawam (stand) panayam (before) their ayab (enemies). They panah (turn) their backs panayam (before) their ayab (enemies), because they have become charam (devoted) for destruction. I will not be with you any more, unless you destroy the charam (devoted) things from qarab (among) you.

"qawam (get) up! qadash (sanctify) the im (people), and amar (say), ‘qadash (sanctify) yourselves for tomorrow, for Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (says), "There is a charam (devoted) thing in the qarab (midst) of you, Yasharaal (Israel). You cannot qawam (stand) panayam (before) your ayab (enemies) until you sawar (take) away the charam (devoted) thing from qarab (among) you.

"‘In the baqar (morning) therefore you shall be brought near by your shabat (tribes). It shall be that the shabat (tribe) which Yahawah selects shall qarab (come) near by mashapachah (families). The mashapachah (family) which Yahawah selects shall qarab (come) near by bayath (households). The bayath (household) which Yahawah selects shall qarab (come) near gabar (man) by gabar (man).

It shall be, that he who is taken with the charam (devoted) thing shall be burnt with ash (fire), he and all that he has, because he has transgressed the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, and because he has done a disgraceful thing in Yasharaal (Israel).'
So Yahawashawai rose up shakam (early) in the baqar (morning) and brought Yasharaal (Israel) near by their shabat (tribes). The shabat (tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah) was selected.

He brought near the mashapachah (family) of Yahawadah (Judah); and he selected the mashapachah (family) Zarachay the Zerahites. He brought near the mashapachah (family) Zarachay the Zerahites gabar (man) by gabar (man), and Zabaday was selected.

He brought near his bayath (household) gabar (man) by gabar (man), and Ikan, the ban (son) of Karamay, the ban (son) of Zabaday, the ban (son) of Zarach, of the matah (tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah), was selected.

Yahawashawai said to Ikan, "My ban (son), please shawam (give) kabawad (glory) to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), and nathan (make) thawadah (confession) to him. nagad (tell) me now what you have done! Don't hide it from me!
Ikan answered Yahawashawai, and said, "I have truly sinned against Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), and this is what I have done.

When I saw among the spoil a tawab (beautiful) Shanair (Babylonian) adarath (robe), two maah (hundred) shekels of kasap (silver), and a lashawan (wedge) of gold weighing chamashayam (fifty) shekels, then I coveted them and took them. Behold, they are hidden in the aratz (ground) in the middle of my ahal (tent), with the kasap (silver) under it.
So Yahawashawai sent malaak (messengers), and they ran to the ahal (tent). Behold, it was hidden in his ahal (tent), with the kasap (silver) under it.
They took them from the middle of the ahal (tent), and brought them to Yahawashawai and to all the children of Yasharaal (Israel). They laid them down panayam (before) Yahawah.

Yahawashawai, and all Yasharaal (Israel) with him, took Ikan the ban (son) of Zarach, the kasap (silver), the adarath (robe), the lashawan (wedge) of gold, his ban (sons), his bath (daughters), his cattle, his donkeys, his sheep, his ahal (tent), and all that he had; and they brought them up to the valley of Ikawar.

Yahawashawai said, "mah (why) have you troubled us? Yahawah will trouble you this yawam (day)." All Yasharaal (Israel) stoned him with aban (stones), and they burned them with ash (fire) and stoned them with aban (stones).

They raised over him a gadawal (great) heap of aban (stones) that remains to this yawam (day). Yahawah turned from the charawan (fierceness) of his ap (anger). Therefore the sham (name) of that place was called "The valley of Ikawar" to this yawam (day).

Yahawah said to Yahawashawai, "Don't be yaraa (afraid), neither be dismayed. Take all the im (people) of war with you, and qawam (arise), ilah (go) up to Iy. raah (see), I have given into your yad (hand) the malak (king) of Iy, with his im (people), his Iyar, and his aratz (land).

You shall do to Iy and her malak (king) as you did to Yarayachaw and her malak (king), except its spoil and its livestock, you shall take for a plunder for yourselves. shawam (set) an ambush for the Iyar achar (behind) it.

So Yahawashawai qawam (arose), and all the im (people) of war, to ilah (go) up to Iy. Yahawashawai chose shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand) men, the gabawar (mighty) men of valor, and sent them out by layal (night).
He tzawah (commanded) them, saying, "raah (see), you shall lie in ambush against the Iyar, achar (behind) the Iyar. Don't rachaq (go) very rachaq (far) from the Iyar, but all of you be kawan (ready).

I, and all the im (people) who are with me, will qarab (approach) to the Iyar. It shall happen, when they yatzaa (come) out qaraah (against) us, as at the raashawan (first), that we will flee panayam (before) them.

They will yatzaa (come) out achar (after) us, until we have drawn them away from the Iyar; for they will amar (say), ‘They flee panayam (before) us, like the raashawan (first) time.' So we will flee panayam (before) them,
and you shall qawam (rise) up from the ambush, and take yarash (possession) of the Iyar; for Yahawah your Alahayam will nathan (deliver) it into your yad (hand).

It shall be, when you have seized on the Iyar, that you shall yatzath (set) the Iyar on ash (fire). You shall do this according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah. raah (see), I have tzawah (commanded) you.
Yahawashawai sent them out; and they went to set up the ambush, and stayed between Bayathaal and Iy, on the yam (west) side of Iy; but Yahawashawai stayed among the im (people) that layal (night).
Yahawashawai rose up shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), mustered the im (people), and went up, he and the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel), panayam (before) the im (people) to Iy.

All the im (people), even the men of war who were with him, went up, and drew near, and came before the Iyar, and encamped on the tzapawan (north) side of Iy. Now there was a Gayaa between him and Iy.
He took about chamash (five) alap (thousand) men, and shawam (set) them in ambush between Bayathaal and Iy, on the yam (west) side Iy the city.

So they shawam (set) the im (people), even all the machanah (army) who was on the tzapawan (north) of the Iyar, and their ambush on the yam (west) of the Iyar; and Yahawashawai went that layal (night) into the midst of the valley.

It happened, when the malak (king) of Iy saw it, that they hurried and rose up shakam (early), and the men of the Iyar went out qaraah (against) Yasharaal (Israel) to battle, he and all his im (people), at the mawaid (time) appointed, panayam (before) the irabah (arabah); but he didn't yadai (know) that there was an ambush against him achar (behind) the Iyar.
Yahawashawai and all Yasharaal (Israel) made as if they were beaten panayam (before) them, and fled by the darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness).
All the im (people) who were Iy the city were called together to pursue achar (after) them. They pursued Yahawashawai, and were drawn away from the Iyar.
There was not a ayash (man) shaar (left) in Iy or Bayathaal El who didn't yatzaa (go) out achar (after) Yasharaal (Israel). They left the Iyar pathach (open), and pursued Yasharaal (Israel).

Yahawah said to Yahawashawai, "natah (stretch) out the javelin that is in your yad (hand) toward Iy, for I will nathan (give) it into your yad (hand)." Yahawashawai stretched out the javelin that was in his yad (hand) toward the Iyar.

The ambush qawam (arose) quickly out of their place, and they ran as soon as he had stretched out his yad (hand), and entered into the Iyar, and took it. They hurried and yatzath (set) the Iyar on ash (fire).

When the men of Iy looked achar (behind) them, they saw, and behold, the ishan (smoke) of the Iyar ascended up to shamayam (heaven), and they had no yad (power) to flee this hanah (way) or that way. The im (people) who fled to the madabar (wilderness) turned hapak (back) on the pursuers.
When Yahawashawai and all Yasharaal (Israel) saw that the ambush had taken the Iyar, and that the ishan (smoke) of the Iyar ascended, then they turned again, and killed the men of Iy.

The others came out of the Iyar qaraah (against) them, so they were in the midst of Yasharaal (Israel), some on this side, and some on that side. They struck them, so that they let none of them sharayad (remain) or escape.
They captured the malak (king) of Iy chay (alive), and brought him to Yahawashawai.

It happened, when Yasharaal (Israel) had made an kalah (end) of killing all the yashab (inhabitants) of Iy in the shadah (field), in the madabar (wilderness) in which they pursued them, and they had all fallen by the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), until they were consumed, that all Yasharaal (Israel) returned to Iy, and struck it with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).
All that napal (fell) that yawam (day), both of men and women, were shanayam (twelve) alap (thousand), even all the men of Iy.

For Yahawashawai didn't shawab (turn back / repent) shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand), with which he stretched out the javelin, until he had charam (utterly) destroyed all the yashab (inhabitants) of Iy.
Only the livestock and the spoil of that Iyar Yasharaal (Israel) took for prey to themselves, according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah which he tzawah (commanded) Yahawashawai.
So Yahawashawai burnt Iy, and made it a thal (heap) iwalam (forever), even a desolation, to this yawam (day).

He hanged the malak (king) of Iy on a itz (tree) until the ith (evening), and at the sundown Yahawashawai tzawah (commanded), and they took his nabalah (body) down from the itz (tree), and threw it at the entrance of the gate of the Iyar, and raised a gadawal (great) heap of aban (stones) on it that remains to this yawam (day).
Then Yahawashawai built an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), in har (mount) Iyabal,

as Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah tzawah (commanded) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), as it is written in the book of the thawarah (law) of Mashah, an mazabach (altar) Shalam uncut aban (stones), on which no nawap (man) had lifted up any barazal (iron). They offered burnt ilah (offerings) on it to Yahawah, and sacrificed peace ilah (offerings).
He wrote there on the aban (stones) a mashanah (copy) of the thawarah (law) of Mashah, which he wrote in the panayam (presence) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

All Yasharaal (Israel), and their zaqan (elders) and shatar (officers), and their shapat (judges), stood on this side of the arawan (ark) and on that side before the kahan (priests) the Lawayay (Levites), who carried the arawan (ark) of yahawah (yahweh's) barayath (covenant), the foreigner as well as the native; chatzay (half) of them in front of har (mount) Garazayam, and chatzay (half) of them in front of har (mount) Iyabal, as Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah had tzawah (commanded) at the raashawan (first), that they should barak (bless) the im (people) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Afterward he qaraa (read) all the dabar (words) of the thawarah (law), the barakah (blessing) and the qalalah (curse), according to all that is written in the book of the thawarah (law).

There was not a dabar (word) of all that Mashah tzawah (commanded), which Yahawashawai didn't qaraa (read) before all the qahal (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel), with the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who were qarab (among) them.

It happened, when all the malak (kings) who were ibar (beyond) the Yaradan, in the har (hill) country, and in the lowland, and on all the shore of the gadawal (great) yam (sea) in front of Labanawan, the Chathay (Hittite), the Amaray (Amorite), the Kanainay (Canaanite), the Parazay (Perizzite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite), heard of it
that they gathered themselves together to fight with Yahawashawai and with Yasharaal (Israel), with one pah (accord).
But when the yashab (inhabitants) of Gabaiwan heard what Yahawashawai had done to Yarayachaw and to Iy,
they also resorted to a ruse, and went and made as if they had been ambassadors, and took Balah sacks on their donkeys, and wineskins, Balah and torn and bound up,
and Balah and patched shoes on their feet, and wore Balah garments. All the lacham (bread) of their provision was yabash (dry) and moldy.

They went to Yahawashawai to the machanah (camp) at Galagal, and said to him, and to the men of Yasharaal (Israel), "We have bawaa (come) from a Rachawaq aratz (country). Now therefore karath (make) a barayath (covenant) with us.
The men of Yasharaal (Israel) said to the Chaway (Hivites), "What if you live qarab (among) us. How could we karath (make) a barayath (covenant) with you?
They said to Yahawashawai, "We are your ibad (servants)." Yahawashawai said to them, "Who are you? Where do you bawaa (come) from?

They said to him, "Your ibad (servants) have bawaa (come) from a very Rachawaq aratz (country) because of the sham (name) of Yahawah your Alahayam; for we have heard of his fame, all that he did in Matzarayam,

and all that he did to the shanayam (two) malak (kings) of the Amaray (Amorites) who were ibar (beyond) the Yaradan, to Sayachawan malak (king) of Chashabawan and to Iwag malak (king) of Bashan, who was Ishatharawath Ashtaroth.

Our zaqan (elders) and all the yashab (inhabitants) of our aratz (country) spoke to us, saying, ‘Take provision in your hand for the darak (journey), and yalak (go) to qaraah (meet) them, and amar (tell) them, "We are your ibad (servants). Now karath (make) a barayath (covenant) with us."'
This our lacham (bread) we took Cham for our provision out of our bayath (houses) on the yawam (day) we went out to yalak (go) to you; but now, behold, it is yabash (dry), and has become moldy.
These wineskins, which we filled, were Chadash; and behold, they are torn. These our garments and our shoes have become old because of the very long darak (journey).
The men sampled their provisions, and didn't shaal (ask) counsel from the pah (mouth) of Yahawah.
Yahawashawai made shalawam (peace) with them, and made a barayath (covenant) with them, to let them chayah (live). The nashayaa (princes) of the idah (congregation) swore to them.

It happened at the end of shalawash (three) yawam (days) achar (after) they had made a barayath (covenant) with them, that they heard that they were their neighbors, and that they lived qarab (among) them.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) traveled and came to their Iyar on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day). Now their Iyar were Gabaiwan, Kapayarah, Baarawath, and Kiriath Qarayathayairayam.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) didn't strike them, because the nashayaa (princes) of the idah (congregation) had sworn to them by Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel). All the idah (congregation) murmured against the nashayaa (princes).
But all the nashayaa (princes) said to all the idah (congregation), "We have sworn to them by Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): now therefore we may not nagai (touch) them.
This we will do to them, and let them chayah (live); lest qatzap (wrath) be on us, because of the shabawaih (oath) which we swore to them.

The nashayaa (princes) said to them, "Let them chayah (live), so they became itz (wood) cutters and drawers of mayam (water) for all the idah (congregation), as the nashayaa (princes) had spoken to them.
Yahawashawai called for them, and he spoke to them, saying, "Why have you deceived us, saying, ‘We are very Rachawaq from you,' when you live qarab (among) us?
Now therefore you are cursed, and some of you will never karath (fail) to be ibad (bondservants), both itz (wood) cutters and drawers of mayam (water) for the bayath (house) of my Alahayam.

They answered Yahawashawai, and said, "Because your ibad (servants) were nagad (certainly) told how Yahawah your Alahayam tzawah (commanded) his ibad (servant) Mashah to nathan (give) you all the aratz (land), and to destroy all the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land) from panayam (before) you. Therefore we were very yaraa (afraid) for our lives panayam (because) of you, and have done this thing.
Now, behold, we are in your yad (hand). Do to us as it seems tawab (good) and yashar (right) to you to do.
He did so to them, and delivered them out of the yad (hand) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), so that they didn't harag (kill) them.

That yawam (day) Yahawashawai made them itz (wood) cutters and drawers of mayam (water) for the idah (congregation) and for the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah, to this yawam (day), in the place which he should choose.

Adanayatzadaq it happened when Adoni-Zedek malak (king) of Yarawashalam heard how Yahawashawai had taken Iy, and had charam (utterly) destroyed it; as he had done to Yarayachaw and her malak (king), so he had done to Iy and her malak (king); and how the yashab (inhabitants) of Gabaiwan had made shalam (peace) with Yasharaal (Israel), and were qarab (among) them;
that they were very yaraa (afraid), because Gabaiwan was a gadawal (great) Iyar, as one of the mamalakah (royal) Iyar, and because it was greater than Iy, and all its men were gabawar (mighty).

Adanayatzadaq Adoni-Zedek malak (king) of Yarawashalam sent to Hawaham malak (king) of Chabarawan, to Paraam malak (king) of Yaramawath, to Yapayai malak (king) of Lakayash, and to Dabayar malak (king) of Igalawan, saying,
"ilah (come) up to me, and help me, and let us strike Gabaiwan; for it has made shalam (peace) with Yahawashawai and with the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

Therefore the chamash (five) malak (kings) of the Amaray (Amorites), the malak (king) of Yarawashalam, the malak (king) of Chabarawan, the malak (king) of Yaramawath, the malak (king) of Lakayash, the malak (king) of Igalawan, gathered themselves asap (together), and went up, they and all their machanah (armies), and encamped against Gabaiwan, and made war against it.

The men of Gabaiwan sent to Yahawashawai to the machanah (camp) to Galagal, saying, "Don't abandon your ibad (servants)! ilah (come) up to us quickly, and yashai (save) us, and help us; for all the malak (kings) of the Amaray (Amorites) that yashab (dwell) in the har (hill) country have gathered together against us.
So Yahawashawai went up from Galagal, he, and all the im (people) of war with him, and all the gabawar (mighty) chayal (men) of valor.
Yahawah said to Yahawashawai, "Don't yaraa (fear) them, for I have delivered them into your yad (hands). Not a ayash (man) of them will imad (stand) panayam (before) you.
Yahawashawai therefore came on them suddenly. He went up from Galagal all layal (night).

Yahawah confused them panayam (before) Yasharaal (Israel), and he killed them with a gadawal (great) makah (slaughter) at Gabaiwan, and chased them by the darak (way) of the ascent of Bayathachawarawan Horon, and struck them to Izaqah and to Maqadah.

It happened, as they fled from panayam (before) Yasharaal (Israel), while they were at the descent of Bayathachawarawan Horon, that Yahawah cast down gadawal (great) aban (stones) from the sky on them to Izaqah, and they died. There were more who died from the hailstones than who the children of Yasharaal (Israel) killed with the charab (sword).

Then Yahawashawai spoke to Yahawah in the yawam (day) when Yahawah delivered up the Amaray (Amorites) panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel); and he said in the iyan (sight) of Yasharaal (Israel), "shamash (sun), stand still on Gabaiwan! You, yarach (moon), stop in the valley of Ayalawan!

The shamash (sun) stood still, and the yarach (moon) stayed, until the gaway (nation) had avenged themselves of their ayab (enemies). Isn't this written in the book of Jashar? The shamash (sun) stayed in the chatzay (midst) of the sky, and didn't hurry to bawaa (go) down about a thamayam (whole) yawam (day).
There was no yawam (day) like that panayam (before) it or achar (after) it, that Yahawah listened to the qawal (voice) of a ayash (man); for Yahawah fought for Yasharaal (Israel).
Yahawashawai returned, and all Yasharaal (Israel) with him, to the machanah (camp) to Galagal.
These chamash (five) malak (kings) fled, and hid themselves in the cave at Maqadah.
Yahawashawai was told, saying, "The chamash (five) malak (kings) are found, hidden in the cave at Maqadah.
Yahawashawai said, "Roll large aban (stones) to the pah (mouth) of the cave, and paqad (set) men by it to guard them;
but don't imad (stay). Pursue your ayab (enemies), and strike them from the rear. Don't allow them to bawaa (enter) into their Iyar; for Yahawah your Alahayam has delivered them into your yad (hand).

It happened, when Yahawashawai and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) had finished killing them with a very gadawal (great) makah (slaughter) until they were consumed, and the sharayad (remnant) which remained of them had entered into the fortified Iyar,
that all the im (people) returned to the machanah (camp) to Yahawashawai at Maqadah in shalawam (peace). None moved his lashawan (tongue) against any of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
Then Yahawashawai said, "pathach (open) the pah (mouth) of the cave, and bring those chamash (five) malak (kings) out of the cave to me.

They did so, and brought those chamash (five) malak (kings) out of the cave to him: the malak (king) of Yarawashalam, the malak (king) of Chabarawan, the malak (king) of Yaramawath, the malak (king) of Lakayash, and the malak (king) of Igalawan.

It happened, when they brought those malak (kings) out to Yahawashawai, that Yahawashawai called for all the men of Yasharaal (Israel), and said to the chiefs of the men of war who went with him, "qarab (come) near, shawam (put) your feet on the necks of these malak (kings)." They came qarab (near), and shawam (put) their feet on their necks.
Yahawashawai said to them, "Don't be yaraa (afraid), nor be dismayed. Be chazaq (strong) and amatz (courageous), for Yahawah will do this to all your ayab (enemies) against whom you fight.
Afterward Yahawashawai struck them, put them to mawath (death), and hanged them on chamash (five) itz (trees). They were hanging on the itz (trees) until the evening.

It happened at the ith (time) of the going down of the shamash (sun), that Yahawashawai tzawah (commanded), and they took them down off the itz (trees), and cast them into the cave in which they had hidden themselves, and laid gadawal (great) aban (stones) on the pah (mouth) of the cave, which remain to this very yawam (day).

Yahawashawai took Maqadah on that yawam (day), and struck it with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), with its malak (king). He charam (utterly) destroyed them and all the napash (souls) who were in it. He shaar (left) none sharayad (remaining). He did to the malak (king) of Maqadah as he had done to the malak (king) of Yarayachaw.
Yahawashawai passed from Maqadah, and all Yasharaal (Israel) with him, to Labanah, and fought against Labanah.

Yahawah delivered it also, with its malak (king), into the yad (hand) of Yasharaal (Israel). He struck it with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), and all the napash (souls) who were in it. He shaar (left) none sharayad (remaining) in it. He did to its malak (king) as he had done to the malak (king) of Yarayachaw.
Yahawashawai passed from Labanah, and all Yasharaal (Israel) with him, to Lakayash, and encamped against it, and fought against it.

Yahawah delivered Lakayash into the yad (hand) of Yasharaal (Israel). He took it on the shanay (second) yawam (day), and struck it with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), with all the napash (souls) who were in it, according to all that he had done to Labanah.
Then Haram malak (king) of Gazar came up to help Lakayash; and Yahawashawai struck him and his im (people), until he had shaar (left) him none sharayad (remaining).
Yahawashawai passed from Lakayash, and all Yasharaal (Israel) with him, to Igalawan; and they encamped against it fought against it.

They took it on that yawam (day), and struck it with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword). He charam (utterly) destroyed all the napash (souls) who were in it that yawam (day), according to all that he had done to Lakayash.
Yahawashawai went up from Igalawan, and all Yasharaal (Israel) with him, to Chabarawan; and they fought against it.

They took it, and struck it with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), with its malak (king) and all its Iyar, and all the napash (souls) who were in it. He shaar (left) none sharayad (remaining), according to all that he had done to Igalawan; but he charam (utterly) destroyed it, and all the napash (souls) who were in it.
Yahawashawai returned, and all Yasharaal (Israel) with him, to Dabayar, and fought against it.

He took it, with its malak (king) and all its Iyar. They struck them with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), and charam (utterly) destroyed all the napash (souls) who were in it. He shaar (left) none sharayad (remaining). As he had done to Chabarawan, so he did to Dabayar, and to its malak (king); as he had done also to Labanah, and to its malak (king).

So Yahawashawai struck all the aratz (land), the hill aratz (country), and the Nagab, and the lowland, and the slopes, and all their malak (kings). He shaar (left) none sharayad (remaining), but he charam (utterly) destroyed all that breathed, as Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), tzawah (commanded).
Yahawashawai struck them Qadashabaranai Kadesh Barnea even to Izah, and all the aratz (country) of Gashan, even to Gabaiwan.
Yahawashawai took all these malak (kings) and their aratz (land) at one paim (time), because Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), fought for Yasharaal (Israel).
Yahawashawai returned, and all Yasharaal (Israel) with him, to the machanah (camp) to Galagal.
It happened, when Yabayan malak (king) of Chatzawar heard of it, that he sent to Yawabab malak (king) of Madawan, to the malak (king) of Shamarawan, to the malak (king) of Akashap,
and to the malak (kings) who were on the tzapawan (north), in the har (hill) country, in the irabah (arabah) Nagab of Kanarawath, in the lowland, and in the heights of Dawar on the yam (west),

to the Kanainay (Canaanite) on the east and on the yam (west), and the Amaray (Amorite), and the Chathay (Hittite), and the Parazay (Perizzite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite) in the har (hill) country, and the Chaway (Hivite) under Charamawan in the aratz (land) Matzapah Mizpah.
They went out, they and all their machanah (armies) with them, many im (people), even as the sand that is on the shapah (seashore) in multitude, with very many horses and chariots.
All these malak (kings) met together; and they came and encamped together at the mayam (waters) of Marawam, to fight with Yasharaal (Israel).

Yahawah said to Yahawashawai, "Don't be yaraa (afraid) panayam (because) of them; for tomorrow at this ith (time), I will nathan (deliver) them up all Chalal panayam (before) Yasharaal (Israel). You shall hamstring their horses and sharap (burn) their chariots with ash (fire).
So Yahawashawai came, and all the im (people) of war with him, against them by the mayam (waters) of Marawam suddenly, and napal (fell) on them.

Yahawah delivered them into the yad (hand) of Yasharaal (Israel), and they struck them, and chased them to rab (great) Tzayadawan, and to Masharapawathamayam Maim, and to the Baqaih of Matzapah eastward. They struck them until they shaar (left) them none sharayad (remaining).
Yahawashawai did to them as Yahawah told him. He hamstrung their horses and burnt their chariots with ash (fire).

Yahawashawai turned shawab (turn back / repent) at that ith (time), and took Chatzawar, and struck its malak (king) with the charab (sword): for Chatzawar used to be the raash (head) of all those mamalakah (kingdoms).

They struck all the napash (souls) who were in it with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), charam (utterly) destroying them. There was no one yathar (left) who breathed. He burnt Chatzawar with ash (fire).

Yahawashawai captured all the Iyar of those malak (kings), with their malak (kings), and he struck them with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), and charam (utterly) destroyed them; as Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah tzawah (commanded).
But as for the Iyar that stood on their mounds, Yasharaal (Israel) burned none of them, except Chatzawar only. Yahawashawai burned that.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) took all the spoil of these Iyar, with the livestock, as spoils for themselves; but every adam (man) they struck with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), until they had destroyed them. They didn't shaar (leave) any who breathed.
As Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah his ibad (servant), so Mashah tzawah (commanded) Yahawashawai. Yahawashawai did so. He left nothing sawar (undone) of all that Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.

So Yahawashawai captured all that aratz (land), the hill Nagab, all the Nagab, all the Nagab of Gashan, the lowland, the irabah (arabah), the har (hill) country of Yasharaal (Israel), and the lowland of the same;

from har (mount) Chalaq, that goes up to Shaiyar, even to Bailagad Gad in the Baqaih of Labanawan under har (mount) Charamawan. He took all their malak (kings), struck them, and put them to mawath (death).
Yahawashawai made war a rab (long) yawam (time) with all those malak (kings).
There was not a Iyar that made shalam (peace) with the children of Yasharaal (Israel), except the Chaway (Hivites), the yashab (inhabitants) of Gabaiwan. They took all in battle.

For it was of Yahawah to chazaq (harden) their lab (hearts), to come qaraah (against) Yasharaal (Israel) in battle, that he might charam (utterly) thachanah (destroy) them, that they might have no favor, but that he might destroy them, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.

Yahawashawai came at that ith (time), and karath (cut) off the Inaqay (Anakim) from the har (hill) country, from Chabarawan, from Dabayar, from Inab, and from all the har (hill) country of Yahawadah (Judah), and from all the har (hill) country of Yasharaal (Israel): Yahawashawai charam (utterly) destroyed them with their Iyar.
There were none of the Inaqay (Anakim) yathar (left) in the aratz (land) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel). Only in Izah, in gath (gath), and Ashadawad Ashdod, did some shaar (remain).

So Yahawashawai took the whole aratz (land), according to all that Yahawah spoke to Mashah; and Yahawashawai gave it for an nachalah (inheritance) to Yasharaal (Israel) according to their divisions by their shabat (tribes). The aratz (land) had shaqat (rest) from war.

Now these are the malak (kings) of the aratz (land), whom the children of Yasharaal (Israel) struck, and possessed their aratz (land) ibar (beyond) the Yaradan toward the sunrise, from the nachal (valley) of the Aranawan to har (mount) Charamawan, and all the irabah (arabah) eastward:

Sayachawan malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), who lived in Chashabawan, and ruled from Irawair, which is on the shapah (edge) of the nachal (valley) of the Aranawan, and the middle of the nachal (valley), and chatzay (half) Galaid, even to the nachal (river) Yabaq, the border of the children of Imawan;

and the irabah (arabah) to the yam (sea) of Kanarawath, eastward, and to the yam (sea) of the irabah (arabah), even the Malach yam (sea), eastward, the darak (way) to Bayathahayashayamawath Jeshimoth; and on the thayaman (south), under the slopes of Pisgah:
and the border of Iwag malak (king) of Bashan, of the yathar (remnant) of the Rapaa (Rephaim), who lived Ishatharawath Ashtaroth and at Adaraiy,

and ruled in har (mount) Charamawan, and Salakah Salecah, and in all Bashan, to the border of the Gashawaray (Geshurites) and the Maikathay (Maacathites), and chatzay (half) Galaid, the border of Sayachawan malak (king) of Chashabawan.

Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) struck them. Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah gave it for a yarashah (possession) to the Raawabanay (Reubenites), and the Gaday (Gadites), and the half-tribe of Manashah.

These are the malak (kings) of the aratz (land) whom Yahawashawai and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) struck ibar (beyond) the Yaradan westward, from Bailagad Gad in the Baqaih of Labanawan even to har (mount) Chalaq, that goes up to Shaiyar. Yahawashawai gave it to the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) for a yarashah (possession) according to their divisions;

in the har (hill) country, and in the lowland, and in the irabah (arabah), and in the slopes, and in the madabar (wilderness), and in the Nagab; the Chathay (Hittite), the Amaray (Amorite), and the Kanainay (Canaanite), the Parazay (Perizzite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite):
the malak (king) of Yarayachaw, one; the malak (king) of Iy, which is beside Bayathaal, one;
the malak (king) of Yarawashalam, one; the malak (king) of Chabarawan, one;
the malak (king) of Yaramawath, one; the malak (king) of Lakayash, one;
the malak (king) of Igalawan, one; the malak (king) of Gazar, one;
the malak (king) of Dabayar, one; the malak (king) of Gadar, one;
the malak (king) of Charamah, one; the malak (king) of Irad, one;
the malak (king) of Labanah, one; the malak (king) of Idalam, one;
the malak (king) of Maqadah, one; the malak (king) of Bayathaal, one;
the malak (king) of Thapawach, one; the malak (king) of Chapar, one;
the malak (king) of Apaq, one; the malak (king) Sharawan Lassharon, one;
the malak (king) of Madawan, one; the malak (king) of Chatzawar, one;
the malak (king) of Shimron Shamarawanamaraawan, one; the malak (king) of Akashap, one;
the malak (king) of Thainak, one; the malak (king) of Magadawan, one;
the malak (king) of Qadash, one; the malak (king) of Yaqanaim in Karamal, one;
the malak (king) of Dawar in the height of Dawar, one; the malak (king) of Goiim in Galagal, one;
the malak (king) of Tharatzah, one: all the malak (kings) thirty-one.

Now Yahawashawai was zaqan (old) and well advanced in yawam (years). Yahawah said to him, "You are zaqan (old) and advanced in yawam (years), and there shaar (remains) yet very much aratz (land) to be possessed.
"This is the aratz (land) that still shaar (remains): all the regions of the Palashathay (Philistines), and all the Gashawaray (Geshurites);

from the Shayachawar, which is panayam (before) Matzarayam, even to the border of Iqarawan northward, which is counted as Kanainay (Canaanite); the chamash (five) lords of the Palashathay (Philistines); the Izathay, and the Ashadawaday, the Ashaqalawanay, the Gathay (Gittites), and the Iqarawanay; Iwayam the Avvim,
on the thayaman (south); all the aratz (land) of the Kanainay (Canaanites), and Mairah that belongs to the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), to Apaq, to the border of the Amaray (Amorites);
and the aratz (land) of the Gebalites, and all Labanawan, toward the sunrise, from Bailagad Gad under har (mount) Charamawan to the entrance of Chamath;

all the yashab (inhabitants) of the har (hill) country from Labanawan to Masharapawathamayam Maim, even all the Tzayadanay (Sidonians); them will I yarash (drive) out from panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel): only allocate it to Yasharaal (Israel) for an nachalah (inheritance), as I have tzawah (commanded) you.
Now therefore divide this aratz (land) for an nachalah (inheritance) to the thashai (nine) shabat (tribes) and the half-tribe of Manashah.

With him the Raawabanay (Reubenites) and the Gaday (Gadites) received their nachalah (inheritance), which Mashah gave them, ibar (beyond) the Yaradan eastward, even as Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah gave them:
from Irawair, that is on the shapah (edge) of the nachal (valley) of the Aranawan, and the Iyar that is in the middle of the nachal (valley), and all the mayashawar (plain) of Mayadabaa to Dayabawan;
and all the Iyar of Sayachawan malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), who reigned in Chashabawan, to the border of the children of Imawan;
and Galaid, and the border of the Gashawaray (Geshurites) and Maikathay (Maacathites), and all har (mount) Charamawan, and all Bashan Salakah Salecah;

all the mamalakawath (kingdom) of Iwag in Bashan, who reigned Ishatharawath Ashtaroth and in Adaraiy (the same was shaar (left) of the yathar (remnant) of the Rapaa (Rephaim)); for Mashah attacked these, and drove them out.

Nevertheless the children of Yasharaal (Israel) didn't yarash (drive) out the Gashawaray (Geshurites), Maikathay the Maacathites: Gashawaray Geshur and Maikathay yashab (dwell) in the qarab (midst) of Yasharaal (Israel) to this yawam (day).

Only he gave no nachalah (inheritance) to the shabat (tribe) of Laway. The ashah (offerings) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), made by ashah (fire) are his nachalah (inheritance), as he spoke to him.
Mashah gave to the matah (tribe) of the children of Raawaban according to their mashapachah (families).

Their border was from Irawair, that is on the shapah (edge) of the nachal (valley) of the Aranawan, and the Iyar that is in the middle of the nachal (valley), and all the mayashawar (plain) by Mayadabaa;
Chashabawan, and all its Iyar that are in the mayashawar (plain); Dayabawan, Bamawath Baal, Bayathabailamaiwan Baal Meon,
Yahatz, Qadamawath, Mawapaith,
Qarayathayam, Shabam, Zereth Tzarathahashachar in the har (mount) of the valley,
Bayathapaiwar Peor, the slopes of Pisgah, Bayathahayashayamawath Jeshimoth,

all the Iyar of the mayashawar (plain), and all the mamalakawath (kingdom) of Sayachawan malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), who reigned in Chashabawan, whom Mashah struck with the nashayaa (chiefs) of Madayan, Away, Raqam, Tzawar, Chawar, and Rabai, the nasayak (princes) of Sayachawan, who lived in the aratz (land).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) alse killed Balaim also the ban (son) of Baiwar, the soothsayer, with the charab (sword), among the al (rest) of their Chalal.

The border of the children of Raawaban was the bank of the Yaradan. This was the nachalah (inheritance) of the children of Raawaban according to their mashapachah (families), the Iyar and its villages.
Mashah gave to the matah (tribe) of Gad, to the children of Gad, according to their mashapachah (families).
Their border was Yaizayar, and all the Iyar of Galaid, and chatzay (half) the aratz (land) of the children of Imawan, to Irawair that is panayam (before) Rabah;
and from Chashabawan to Ramathahamatzapah Mizpeh, and Batanayam; and from Machanayam to the border of Dabayar;

and in the valley, Bayathaharam Haram, Bayathanamarah Nimrah, Sakawath, and Tzapawan, the yathar (rest) of the mamalakawath (kingdom) of Sayachawan malak (king) of Chashabawan, the Yaradan bank, to the uttermost part of the yam (sea) of Kanarawath ibar (beyond) the Yaradan eastward.
This is the nachalah (inheritance) of the children of Gad according to their mashapachah (families), the Iyar and its villages.
Mashah gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manashah. It was for the half-tribe of the children of Manashah according to their mashapachah (families).
Their border was from Machanayam, all Bashan, all the mamalakawath (kingdom) of Iwag malak (king) of Bashan, and all the towns of Yaayar, which are in Bashan, shashayam (sixty) Iyar.

chatzay (half) Galaid, Ishatharawath, and Adaraiy, the Iyar of the mamalakawath (kingdom) of Iwag in Bashan, were for the children of Makayar the ban (son) of Manashah, even for the chatzay (half) of the children of Makayar according to their mashapachah (families).
These are the nachal (inheritances) which Mashah distributed in the irabah (plains) of Mawaab, ibar (beyond) the Yaradan at Yarayachaw, eastward.
But to the shabat (tribe) of Laway Mashah gave no nachalah (inheritance). Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), is their nachalah (inheritance), as he spoke to them.

These are the inheritances which the children of Yasharaal (Israel) took in the aratz (land) of Kanain, which Alaizar the kahan (priest), Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan, and the raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' houses of the matah (tribes) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), distributed to them,
by the lot of their nachalah (inheritance), as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) by Mashah, for the thashai (nine) matah (tribes), and for the half-tribe.
For Mashah had given the nachalah (inheritance) of the shanayam (two) matah (tribes) and the half-tribe ibar (beyond) the Yaradan; Lawayay to the Levites he gave no nachalah (inheritance) among them.

For the children of Yawasap were shanayam (two) matah (tribes), Manashah and Aparayam: and they gave no chalaq (portion) Lawayay the Levites in the aratz (land), except Iyar to yashab (dwell) in, with their suburbs for their livestock and for their property.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) did as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah, and they divided the aratz (land).

Then the children of Yahawadah (Judah) drew near to Yahawashawai in Galagal. Kalab the ban (son) of Yapanah the Qanazay (Kenizzite) said to him, "You yadai (know) the thing that Yahawah spoke to Mashah the ayash (man) of Alahayam concerning me and concerning you Qadashabaranai Kadesh Barnea.

I was arabaiyam (forty) Shanah ban (old) when Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah sent me Qadashabaranai Kadesh Barnea to spy out the aratz (land). I brought him dabar (word) again as it was in my labab (heart).
Nevertheless, my ach (brothers) who went up with me made the lab (heart) of the im (people) masah (melt); but I malaa (wholly) followed Yahawah my Alahayam.

Mashah swore on that yawam (day), saying, ‘Surely the aratz (land) where you walked shall be an nachalah (inheritance) to you and to your children iwalam (forever), because you have malaa (wholly) followed Yahawah my Alahayam.'

"Now, behold, Yahawah has kept me chayah (alive), as he spoke, these forty-five Shanah, from the time that Yahawah spoke this dabar (word) to Mashah, while Yasharaal (Israel) walked in the madabar (wilderness). Now, behold, I am eighty-five Shanah ban (old), today.

As yet I am as chazaq (strong) today as I was in the yawam (day) that Mashah sent me: as my kach (strength) was then, even so is my kach (strength) now for war, to yatzaa (go) out and to bawaa (come) in.

Now therefore nathan (give) me this har (hill) country, of which Yahawah spoke in that yawam (day); for you heard in that yawam (day) how the Inaqay (Anakim) were there, and gadawal (great) and fortified Iyar. It may be that Yahawah will be with me, and I shall yarash (drive) them out, as Yahawah spoke.
Yahawashawai blessed him; and he gave Chabarawan to Kalab the ban (son) of Yapanah for an nachalah (inheritance).

Therefore Chabarawan became the nachalah (inheritance) of Kalab the ban (son) of Yapanah the Qanazay (Kenizzite) to this yawam (day); because he malaa (wholly) followed Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
Now the sham (name) of Chabarawan panayam (before) was Kiriath Qarayathaarabai, after the greatest adam (man) among the Inaqay (Anakim). The aratz (land) had shaqat (rest) from war.

The lot for the matah (tribe) of the children of Yahawadah (Judah) according to their mashapachah (families) was to the border of Adam, even to the madabar (wilderness) of Tzan Nagab, at the uttermost part of the thayaman (south).
Their Nagab border was from the uttermost part of the Malach yam (sea), from the lashawan (bay) that panah (looks) Nagab;

and it went out Nagab Nagab the ascent of Mailahaiqarabayam, and passed along to Tzan, and went up Qadashabaranai the south of Kadesh Barnea, and passed along by Chatzarawan, went up to Adar, and turned sabab (about) Qaraqai Karka;
and it passed along to Itzamawan, went out at the nachal (brook) of Matzarayam; and the border ended at the yam (sea). This shall be your Nagab border.
The qadam (east) border was the Malach yam (sea), even to the end of the Yaradan. The border of the tzapawan (north) quarter was from the lashawan (bay) of the yam (sea) at the end of the Yaradan.
The border went up to Bayathachagalah Hoglah, and passed along by the tzapawan (north) of Bayathahairabah Arabah; and the border went up to the aban (stone) of Bahan the ban (son) of Raawaban.

The border went up to Dabayar from the valley of Ikawar, and so northward, looking toward Galagal, that is over against the ascent of Adamayam, which is on the Nagab side of the nachal (river). The border passed along to the mayam (waters) Iyanashamash En Shemesh, and ended at Iyanaragal Rogel.

The border went up by the Gayaa of the ban (son) of Hanam to the side of the Yabawasay (Jebusite) Nagab (the same is Yarawashalam); and the border went up to the raash (top) of the har (mountain) that lies panayam (before) the Gayaa of Hanam westward, which is at the farthest part of the valley of Rapaa (Rephaim) northward.

The border extended from the raash (top) of the har (mountain) to the spring of the mayam (waters) of Napathawach, and went out to the Iyar of har (mount) Iparawan; and the border extended to Bailah (the same is Kiriath Qarayathayairayam);

and the border turned about from Bailah westward to har (mount) Shaiyar, and passed along to the side of har (mount) Yairayam on the tzapawan (north) (the same is Kasalawan), and went down to Bayathashamash Shemesh, and passed ibar (along) by Thamanah;

and the border went out to the side of Iqarawan northward; and the border extended Shakarawan Shikkeron, and passed ibar (along) to har (mount) Bailah, and went out at Yabanaal; and the yatzaa (goings) out of the border were at the yam (sea).
The yam (west) border was to the shore of the gadawal (great) yam (sea). This is the border of the children of Yahawadah (Judah) according to their mashapachah (families).

To Kalab the ban (son) of Yapanah he gave a chalaq (portion) among the children of Yahawadah (Judah), according to the commandment of Yahawah to Yahawashawai, even Kiriath Arba, named after the ab (father) of Inaq (the same is Chabarawan).
Kalab drove out the shalawash (three) ban (sons) of Inaq: Shashay, and Achayaman, and Thalamay, the children of Inaq.
He went up against the yashab (inhabitants) of Dabayar: now the sham (name) of Dabayar panayam (before) was Kiriath Qarayathasanah.
Kalab said, "He who strikes Kiriath Qarayathasanah, and takes it, to him will I nathan (give) Ikasah my bath (daughter) as ashah (wife).
Ithanayaal the ban (son) of Qanaz, the ach (brother) of Kalab, took it: and he gave him Ikasah his bath (daughter) as ashah (wife).
It happened, when she came, that she had him shaal (ask) her ab (father) for a shadah (field). She got off of her donkey, and Kalab said, "What do you want?

She said, "nathan (give) me a barakah (blessing). Because you have nathan (set) me in the aratz (land) of the Nagab, nathan (give) me also springs of mayam (water)." He gave her the Ilay springs and the Thachathay springs.
This is the nachalah (inheritance) of the matah (tribe) of the children of Yahawadah (Judah) according to their mashapachah (families).
The farthest Iyar of the matah (tribe) of the children of Yahawadah (Judah) toward the border of Adam in the Nagab were Qabatzaal, Idar, Yagawar,
Qayanah, Dayamawanah, Idaidah,
Qadash, Chatzawar, Yathanan,
Zayap, Talam, Bailawath,
Chatzawar Chatzawarachadathah, Qarayawath Chatzarawan (the same is Chatzawar),
Amam, Shamai, Mawaladah,
Chatzaragadah Gaddah, Chashamawan, Bayathapalat Pelet,
Chatzarashawail Shual, Baarashabai, Bazayawathayah,
Bailah, Iyayam, Itzam,
Alathawalad, Kasayal, Charamah,
Tzaqalag, Madamanah, Sanasanah,
Labaawath, Shalachayam, Iyan, and Ramawan. All the Iyar are twenty-nine, with their villages.
In the lowland, Ashathaal, Tzaraih, Ashanah,
Zanawach, Iyanaganayam Gannim, Thapawach, Iyanayam,
Yaramawath, Idalam, Shawakah, Izaqah,
Shairayam, Idayathayam and Gadarah (or Gadarathayam); fourteen Iyar with their villages.
Tzanan, Chadashah, Magadalagad Gad,
Dalain, Matzapah, Yaqathaal,
Lakayash, Batzaqath, Igalawan,
Kabawan, Lachamas, Kathalayash,
Gadarawath, Bayathadagawan Dagon, Naimah, and Maqadah; sixteen Iyar with their villages.
Labanah, Ithar, Ishan,
Yapathach, Ashanah, Natzayab,
Qaiyalah, Akazayab, and Maraashah; thashai (nine) Iyar with their villages.
Iqarawan, with its bath (towns) and its villages;
from Iqarawan even to the yam (sea), all that were by the Ashadawad of Ashdod, with their villages.
Ashadawad, its bath (towns) and its villages; Izah, its bath (towns) and its villages; to the nachal (brook) of Matzarayam, and the gadawal (great) yam (sea) with its coastline.
In the har (hill) country, Shamayar, Yathayar, Shawakah,
Danah, Kiriath Qarayathasanah (which is Dabayar),
Inab, Ashathamai, Inayam,
Gashan, Chalawan, and Galah; achad (eleven) Iyar with their villages.
Arab, Dawamah, Ashain,
Yanayam, Bayathathapawach Tappuah, Apaqah,
Chamatah, Kiriath Qarayathaarabai (the same is Chabarawan), and Tzayair; thashai (nine) Iyar with their villages.
maiwan (maon), Karamal, Zayap, Yatah,
Yazaraial, Yaqadaim, Zanawach,
Qayan, Gabaih, and Thamanah; ishar (ten) Iyar with their villages.
Chalachawal, Bayathatzawar Zur, Gadar,
Mairath, Bayathainawath Anoth, and Alathaqan; shash (six) Iyar with their villages.
Qarayathabail Baal (the same is Kiriath Qarayathayairayam), and Rabah; shanayam (two) Iyar with their villages.
In the madabar (wilderness), Bayathahairabah Arabah, Madayan, Sakakah,
Nabashan, the City of Salt, and Iyanagaday Gedi; shash (six) Iyar with their villages.

As for the Yabawasay (Jebusites), the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, the children of Yahawadah (Judah) couldn't yarash (drive) them out; but the Yabawasay (Jebusites) live with the children of Yahawadah (Judah) at Yarawashalam to this yawam (day).

The lot came out for the children of Yawasap from the Yaradan at Yarayachaw, at the mayam (waters) of Yarayachaw on the east, even the madabar (wilderness), going up from Yarayachaw through the har (hill) country to Bayathaal.
It went out from Bayathaal to Lawaz, and passed ibar (along) to the border of the Arakay to Itarawath;
and it went down westward to the border Yapalatay the Japhletites, to the border of Bayathachawarawan Horon the Thachathawan, even to Gazar; and ended at the yam (sea).
The children of Yawasap, Manashah and Aparayam, took their nachal (inheritance).

This was the border of the children of Aparayam according to their mashapachah (families). The border of their nachalah (inheritance) eastward was Itarawathaadar Addar, to Bayathachawarawan Horon the Ilayawan.
The border went out westward at Makamathath on the tzapawan (north). The border turned sabab (about) eastward to Thaanathashalah Shiloh, and passed along it on the east of Yanawach.
It went down from Yanawach to Itarawath, to Nairah, reached to Yarayachaw, and went out at the Yaradan.

From Thapawach the border went along westward to the nachal (brook) of Qanah; and ended at the yam (sea). This is the nachalah (inheritance) of the matah (tribe) of the children of Aparayam according to their mashapachah (families);
together with the Iyar which were set apart for the children of Aparayam in the midst of the nachalah (inheritance) of the children of Manashah, all the Iyar with their villages.

They didn't yarash (drive) out the Kanainay (Canaanites) who lived in Gazar; but the Kanainay (Canaanites) yashab (dwell) in the qarab (midst) of Aparayam to this yawam (day), and have become ibad (servants) to do forced mas (labor).

This was the lot for the matah (tribe) of Manashah, for he was the firstborn of Yawasap. As for Makayar the firstborn of Manashah, the ab (father) of Galaid, because he was a ayash (man) of war, therefore he had Galaid and Bashan.

So this was for the yathar (rest) of the children of Manashah according to their mashapachah (families): for the children of Abayaizar, for the children of Chalaq, for the children of Asharayaal, for the children of Shakam, for the children of Chapar, and for the children of Shamayadai: these were the zakar (male) children of Manashah the ban (son) of Yawasap according to their mashapachah (families).

But Tzalapachad, the ban (son) of Chapar, the ban (son) of Galaid, the ban (son) of Makayar, the ban (son) of Manashah, had no ban (sons), but bath (daughters): and these are the sham (names) of his bath (daughters): Machalah, Naih, Chagalah, Malakah, and Tharatzah.

They came qarab (near) panayam (before) Alaizar the kahan (priest), and panayam (before) Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan, and panayam (before) the nashayaa (princes), saying, "Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah to nathan (give) us an nachalah (inheritance) among our ach (brothers)." Therefore according to the commandment of Yahawah he gave them an nachalah (inheritance) among the ach (brothers) of their ab (father).
ishar (ten) parts napal (fell) to Manashah, besides the aratz (land) of Galaid and Bashan, which is ibar (beyond) the Yaradan;
because the bath (daughters) of Manashah had an nachalah (inheritance) among his ban (sons). The aratz (land) of Galaid belonged to the yathar (rest) of the ban (sons) of Manashah.

The border of Manashah was from Ashar to Makamathath, which is panayam (before) Shakam. The border went halak (along) to the right yamayan (hand), to the yashab (inhabitants) of Iyanathapawach Tappuah.
The aratz (land) of Thapawach belonged to Manashah; but Thapawach on the border of Manashah belonged to the children of Aparayam.

The border went down to the nachal (brook) of Qanah, Nagab of the nachal (brook). These Iyar belonged to Aparayam among the Iyar of Manashah. The border of Manashah was on the tzapawan (north) side of the nachal (brook), and ended at the yam (sea).
Nagab it was Aparayam, and northward it was Manashah, and the yam (sea) was his border. They reached to Ashar on the tzapawan (north), and to Yashashakar on the east.

Manashah had shalawash (three) heights in Yashashakar, in Ashar Bayathashaan Shean and its bath (towns), and Yabalaim and its bath (towns), and the yashab (inhabitants) of Dawar and its bath (towns), and the yashab (inhabitants) of Iyanadaar and its bath (towns), and the yashab (inhabitants) of Thainak and its bath (towns), and the yashab (inhabitants) of Magadawan and its bath (towns).
Yet the children of Manashah couldn't yarash (drive) out the inhabitants of those Iyar; but the Kanainay (Canaanites) would yashab (dwell) in that aratz (land).

It happened, when the children of Yasharaal (Israel) had grown chazaq (strong), that they nathan (put) the Kanainay (Canaanites) to forced mas (labor), and didn't yarash (utterly) yarash (drive) them out.

The children of Yawasap spoke to Yahawashawai, saying, "Why have you given me just one lot and one part for an nachalah (inheritance), since I am a rab (great) im (people), because Yahawah has blessed me so far?

Yahawashawai said to them, "If you are a rab (great) im (people), ilah (go) up to the Yair, and clear aratz (land) for yourself there in the land of the Parazay (Perizzites) and of the Rapaa (Rephaim); since the har (hill) country of Aparayam is too awatz (narrow) for you.

The children of Yawasap said, "The har (hill) country is not matzaa (enough) for us. All the Kanainay (Canaanites) who yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land) of the valley have chariots of barazal (iron), both those who are in Bayathashaan Shean and its bath (towns), and those who are in the valley of Yazaraial.
Yahawashawai spoke to the bayath (house) of Yawasap, even to Aparayam and to Manashah, saying, "You are a rab (great) im (people), and have rab (great) kach (power). You shall not have one lot only;

but the har (hill) country shall be yours. Although it is a Yair, you shall baraa (cut) it down, and it's farthest extent shall be yours; for you shall yarash (drive) out the Kanainay (Canaanites), though they have chariots of barazal (iron), and though they are chazaq (strong).

The whole idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) assembled themselves together at Shayalah, and shakan (set) up the ahal (tent) of Meeting there. The aratz (land) was subdued panayam (before) them.
shabai (seven) shabat (tribes) remained among the children of Yasharaal (Israel), which had not yet divided their nachalah (inheritance).

Yahawashawai said to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), "How long will you neglect to bawaa (go) in to yarash (possess) the aratz (land), which Yahawah, the Alahayam of your abawath (fathers), has given you?

Appoint for yourselves shalawash (three) men from each shabat (tribe). I will shalach (send) them, and they shall qawam (arise), halak (walk) through the aratz (land), and kathab (describe) it according to their nachalah (inheritance); and they shall bawaa (come) to me.

They shall divide it into shabai (seven) chalaq (portions). Yahawadah (Judah) shall live in his borders on the Nagab, and the bayath (house) of Yawasap shall live in their borders on the tzapawan (north).
You shall survey the aratz (land) into shabai (seven) chalaq (parts), and bawaa (bring) the description here to me; and I will cast lots for you here panayam (before) Yahawah our Alahayam.

Lawayay the Levites have no chalaq (portion) qarab (among) you; for the kahanah (priesthood) of Yahawah is their nachalah (inheritance). Gad, Raawaban, and the half-tribe of Manashah have received their nachalah (inheritance) ibar (beyond) the Yaradan eastward, which Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah gave them.

The men qawam (arose) and went. Yahawashawai tzawah (commanded) those who went to survey the aratz (land), saying, "yalak (go) halak (walk) through the aratz (land), survey it, and shawab (turn back / repent) again to me. I will cast lots for you here panayam (before) Yahawah in Shayalah.
The men went and passed ibar (through) the aratz (land), and surveyed it by Iyar into shabai (seven) chalaq (portions) in a book. They came to Yahawashawai to the machanah (camp) at Shayalah.
Yahawashawai cast lots for them in Shayalah panayam (before) Yahawah. There Yahawashawai divided the aratz (land) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel) according to their divisions.

The lot of the matah (tribe) of the children of Banayamayan came up according to their mashapachah (families). The border of their lot went out between the children of Yahawadah (Judah) and the children of Yawasap.

Their border on the tzapawan (north) quarter was from the Yaradan. The border went up to the side of Yarayachaw on the tzapawan (north), and went up through the har (hill) country westward. It ended at the madabar (wilderness) of Bayathaawan Aven.

The border passed along from there to Lawaz, to the side of Lawaz (the same is Bayathaal), Nagab. The border went down to Itarawathaadar Addar, by the har (mountain) that lies on the Nagab of Bayathachawarawan Horon the Thachathawan.

The border extended, and turned around on the yam (west) quarter Nagab, from the har (mountain) that lies panayam (before) Bayathachawarawan Horon Nagab; and ended Qarayathabail Kiriath Baal (the same is Kiriath Qarayathayairayam), a Iyar of the children of Yahawadah (Judah). This was the yam (west) quarter.
The Nagab quarter was from the farthest part of Kiriath Qarayathayairayam. The border went out westward, and went out to the spring of the mayam (waters) of Napathawach.

The border went down to the farthest part of the har (mountain) that lies panayam (before) the Gayaa of the ban (son) of Hanam, which is in the valley of Rapaa (Rephaim) northward. It went down to the Gayaa of Hanam, to the side of the Yabawasay (Jebusite) Nagab, and went down to Iyanaragal Rogel.

It extended northward, went out Iyanashamash En Shemesh, and went out to Galayalawath, which is over against the ascent of Adamayam. It went down to the aban (stone) of Bahan the ban (son) of Raawaban.
It passed ibar (along) to the side over against the irabah (arabah) northward, and went down to the irabah (arabah).

The border passed ibar (along) to the side of Bayathachagalah Hoglah northward; and the border ended at the tzapawan (north) lashawan (bay) of the Malach yam (sea), at the Nagab end of the Yaradan. This was the Nagab border.
The Yaradan was its border on the qadam (east) quarter. This was the nachalah (inheritance) of the children of Banayamayan, by the borders around it, according to their mashapachah (families).
Now the Iyar of the matah (tribe) of the children of Banayamayan according to their mashapachah (families) were Yarayachaw, Bayathachagalah Hoglah, Emek Qatzayatz,
Bayathahairabah Arabah, Tzamarayam, Bayathaal,
Iwayam (Avvim), Parah, Iparah,
Kaparahaimawanay Ammoni, Ipanay, and Gabai; shanayam (twelve) Iyar with their villages.
Gabaiwan, Ramah, Baarawath,
Matzapah, Kapayarah, Matzah,
Raqam, Yarapaal, Tharaalah,

Tzalai, Alap, the Yabawasay (Jebusite) (the same is Yarawashalam), Gabaith, and Qarayathayairayam; fourteen Iyar with their villages. This is the nachalah (inheritance) of the children of Banayamayan according to their mashapachah (families).

The shanay (second) lot came out for Shamaiwan, even for the matah (tribe) of the children of Shamaiwan according to their mashapachah (families). Their nachalah (inheritance) was in the midst of the nachalah (inheritance) of the children of Yahawadah (Judah).
They had for their nachalah (inheritance) Baarashabai (or Shabai), Mawaladah,
Chatzarashawail Shual, Balah, Itzam,
Alathawalad, Bathawal, Charamah,
Tzaqalag, Bayathahamarakabawath Marcaboth, Chatzarasawasah Susah,
Bayathalabaawath Lebaoth, and Sharawachan; thirteen Iyar with their villages;
Iyan, Ramawan, Ithar, and Ishan; arabai (four) Iyar with their villages;

and all the villages that were around these Iyar to Bailathabaar Beer, Ramah of the Nagab. This is the nachalah (inheritance) of the matah (tribe) of the children of Shamaiwan according to their mashapachah (families).

Out of the part of the children of Yahawadah (Judah) was the nachalah (inheritance) of the children of Shamaiwan; for the chalaq (portion) of the children of Yahawadah (Judah) was rab (too) much for them. Therefore the children of Shamaiwan had nachal (inheritance) in the midst of their nachal (inheritance).
The shalayashay (third) lot came up for the children of Zabawalawan according to their mashapachah (families). The border of their nachalah (inheritance) was to Sharayad.
Their border went up westward, even to Marailah, and reached to Dabashath. It reached to the nachal (brook) that is panayam (before) Yaqanaim.
It turned from Sharayad eastward toward the sunrise to the border of Kasalathathabar Tabor. It went out to dabarath (daberath), and went up to Yapayai.
From there it passed ibar (along) eastward to Gathahachapar Hepher, Ithaqatzayan Ethkazin; and it went out at Ramawan which stretches to Naih.
The border turned around it on the tzapawan (north) to Chanathan; and it ended at the Gayaa of Iphtah Yapathachaal;
Qatath, Nahalal, Shamarawan, Yadaalah, and Bayathalacham: shanayam (twelve) Iyar with their villages.
This is the nachalah (inheritance) of the children of Zabawalawan according to their mashapachah (families), these Iyar with their villages.
The rabayaiy (fourth) lot came out for Yashashakar, even for the children of Yashashakar according to their mashapachah (families).
Their border was to Yazaraial, Kasalawath, Shawanam,
Chaparayam, Shayaawan, Anacharath,
Rabayath, Qashayawan, Abatz,
Ramath, Iyanaganayam, Iyanachadah Haddah, and Bayathapatzatz Pazzez.
The border reached to Thabawar, Shachatzawam, and Bayathashamash Shemesh. Their border ended at the Yaradan: sixteen Iyar with their villages.
This is the nachalah (inheritance) of the matah (tribe) of the children of Yashashakar according to their mashapachah (families), the Iyar with their villages.
The chamayashay (fifth) lot came out for the matah (tribe) of the children of Ashar according to their mashapachah (families).
Their border was Chalaqath, Chalay, Batan, Akashap,
Alamalak, Imaid, Mashaal. It reached to Karamal westward, and to Shayachawaralabanath.

It turned toward the sunrise to Bayathadagawan Dagon, and reached to Zabawalawan, and to the Gayaa Yapathachaal Iphtah El northward to Bayathahaimaq Emek and Naiyaal. It went out to Kabawal on the left shamaawal (hand),
and Ibaran, Rachab, Chamawan, and Qanah, even to rab (great) Tzayadawan.
The border turned to Ramah, to the fortified Iyar of Tzar; and the border turned to Chasah. It ended at the yam (sea) by the region of Akazayab;
Imah also, and Apaq, and Rachab: twenty-two Iyar with their villages.
This is the nachalah (inheritance) of the matah (tribe) of the children of Ashar according to their mashapachah (families), these Iyar with their villages.
The shashay (sixth) lot came out for the children of Napathalay, even for the children of Napathalay according to their mashapachah (families).
Their border was from Chalap, Alawan the oak Tzainanayam Zaanannim, Adamay, and Yabanaal, Laqawam Lakkum. It ended at the Yaradan.

The border turned westward to Azanawathathabawar Tabor, and went out from there to chaqaq (hukkok). It reached to Zabawalawan on the Nagab, and reached to Ashar on the yam (west), and to Yahawadah (Judah) at the Yaradan toward the sunrise.
The fortified Iyar were Tzadayam, Tzar, Chamath, Raqath, Kanarawath,
Adamah, Ramah, Chatzawar,
Qadash, Adaraiy, Iyanachatzawar Hazor,
Yaraawan, Magadalaal El, Charam, Bayathainath Anath, and Bayathashamash Shemesh; nineteen Iyar with their villages.
This is the nachalah (inheritance) of the matah (tribe) of the children of Napathalay according to their mashapachah (families), the Iyar with their villages.
The shabayaiy (seventh) lot came out for the matah (tribe) of the children Dan Dan according to their mashapachah (families).
The border of their nachalah (inheritance) was Tzaraih, Ashathaal, Iyarashamash,
Shailabayam, Ayalawan, Yathalah,
Ayalawan, Thamanah, Iqarawan,
Alathaqaa, Gabathawan, Bailath,
Yahad, Banayabaraq Berak, Gatharamawan Rimmon,
Me Mayahayaraqawan, and Raqawan, with the border over against Yapaw.

The border of the children Dan Dan went out beyond them; for the children Dan Dan went up and fought against Lasham, and took it, and struck it with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), and possessed it, and lived therein, and called Lasham, Dan, after the sham (name) Dan Dan their ab (father).
This is the nachalah (inheritance) of the matah (tribe) of the children Dan Dan according to their mashapachah (families), these Iyar with their villages.

So they made an kalah (end) of distributing the aratz (land) for nachal (inheritance) by its borders. The children of Yasharaal (Israel) gave an nachalah (inheritance) to Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan in their midst.
According to the commandment of Yahawah, they gave him the Iyar which he asked, even Thamanathacharas in the har (hill) country of Aparayam; and he built the Iyar, and lived there.

These are the nachalah (inheritances), which Alaizar the kahan (priest), Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan, and the raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' houses of the matah (tribes) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), distributed for nachal (inheritance) by lot in Shayalah panayam (before) Yahawah, at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting. So they made an kalah (end) of dividing the aratz (land).
Yahawah spoke to Yahawashawai, saying,
"dabar (speak) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, ‘Assign the Iyar of refuge, of which I spoke to you by Mashah,
that the manslayer who kills any napash (person) accidentally or unintentionally may flee there. They shall be to you for a refuge from the gaal (avenger) of dam (blood).

He shall flee to one of those Iyar, and shall imad (stand) at the entrance of the gate of the Iyar, and dabar (declare) his dabar (cause) in the ears of the zaqan (elders) of that Iyar. They shall asap (take) him into the Iyar with them, and nathan (give) him a place, that he may live among them.

If the gaal (avenger) of dam (blood) pursue achar (after) him, then they shall not deliver up the manslayer into his yad (hand); because he struck his neighbor unintentionally, and didn't shanaa (hate) him thamawal (before).

He shall yashab (dwell) in that Iyar until he imad (stands) panayam (before) the idah (congregation) for mashapat (judgment), until the mawath (death) of the gadawal (high) kahan (priest) that shall be in those yawam (days). Then the manslayer shall shawab (turn back / repent), and bawaa (come) to his own Iyar, and to his own bayath (house), to the Iyar he fled from.'

They set apart Qadash in Galayal in the har (hill) country of Napathalay, Shakam in the har (hill) country of Aparayam, and Kiriath Qarayathaarabai (the same is Chabarawan) in the har (hill) country of Yahawadah (Judah).

ibar (beyond) the Yaradan at Yarayachaw eastward, they assigned Batzar in the madabar (wilderness) in the mayashawar (plain) out of the matah (tribe) of Raawaban, Raamawath in Galaid out of the matah (tribe) of Gad, and Gawalan in Bashan out of the matah (tribe) of Manashah.

These were the appointed Iyar for all the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and for the alien who lives among them, that whoever kills any napash (person) unintentionally might flee there, and not mawath (die) by the yad (hand) of the gaal (avenger) of dam (blood), until he imad (stands) panayam (before) the idah (congregation).

Then the raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' Lawayay of the Levites came near to Alaizar the kahan (priest), and to Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan, and to the raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' houses of the matah (tribes) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
They spoke to them at Shayalah in the aratz (land) of Kanain, saying, "Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah to nathan (give) us Iyar to yashab (dwell) in, with their suburbs for our livestock.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) gave Lawayay the Levites out of their nachalah (inheritance), according to the commandment of Yahawah, these Iyar with their suburbs.

The lot came out for the mashapachah (families) of the Qahathay (Kohathites). The children of Aharawan the kahan (priest), who were Lawayay the Levites, had thirteen Iyar by lot out of the matah (tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah), out of the matah (tribe) of the Shamainay (Simeonites), and out of the matah (tribe) of Banayamayan.

The yathar (rest) of the children of Qahath had ishar (ten) Iyar by lot out of the mashapachah (families) of the matah (tribe) of Aparayam, out of the matah (tribe) Dan Dan, and out of the half-tribe of Manashah.

The children of Garashawan had thirteen Iyar by lot out of the mashapachah (families) of the matah (tribe) of Yashashakar, out of the matah (tribe) of Ashar, out of the matah (tribe) of Napathalay, and out of the half-tribe of Manashah in Bashan.

The children of Mararay according to their mashapachah (families) had shanayam (twelve) Iyar out of the matah (tribe) of Raawaban, out of the matah (tribe) of Gad, and out of the matah (tribe) of Zabawalawan.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) gave these Iyar with their suburbs by lot Lawayay the Levites, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) by Mashah.
They gave out of the matah (tribe) of the children of Yahawadah (Judah), and out of the matah (tribe) of the children of Shamaiwan, these Iyar which are mentioned by sham (name):
