and they were for the children of Aharawan, of the mashapachah (families) of the Qahathay (Kohathites), who were of the children of Laway; for theirs was the raashawan (first) lot.
They gave them Kiriath Arba, named after the ab (father) of Inaq (the same is Chabarawan), in the har (hill) country of Yahawadah (Judah), with its suburbs around it.
But they gave the shadah (fields) of the Iyar and its villages to Kalab the ban (son) of Yapanah for his achazah (possession).
To the children of Aharawan the kahan (priest) they gave Chabarawan with its suburbs, the Iyar of refuge for the manslayer, Labanah with its suburbs,
Yathayar with its suburbs, Ashathamai with its suburbs,
Chalawan with its suburbs, Dabayar with its suburbs,
Iyan with its suburbs, Yatah with its suburbs, and Bayathashamash Shemesh with its suburbs; thashai (nine) Iyar out of those shanayam (two) shabat (tribes).
Out of the matah (tribe) of Banayamayan, Gabaiwan with its suburbs, Gabai with its suburbs,
Inathawath with its suburbs, and Ilamawan with its suburbs; arabai (four) Iyar.
All the Iyar of the children of Aharawan, the kahan (priests), were thirteen Iyar with their suburbs.
The mashapachah (families) of the children of Qahath, the Lawayay (Levites), even the yathar (rest) of the children of Qahath, had the Iyar of their lot out of the matah (tribe) of Aparayam.
They gave them Shakam with its suburbs in the har (hill) country of Aparayam, the Iyar of refuge for the manslayer, and Gazar with its suburbs,
Qabatzayam with its suburbs, and Bayathachawarawan Horon with its suburbs; arabai (four) Iyar.
Out of the matah (tribe) Dan Dan, Alathaqaa with its suburbs, Gabathawan with its suburbs,
Ayalawan with its suburbs, Gatharamawan Rimmon with its suburbs; arabai (four) Iyar.
Out of the half-tribe of Manashah, Thainak with its suburbs, and Gatharamawan Rimmon with its suburbs; shanayam (two) Iyar.
All the Iyar of the mashapachah (families) of the yathar (rest) of the children of Qahath were ishar (ten) with their suburbs.

They gave to the children of Garashawan, of the mashapachah (families) Lawayay the Levites, out of the half-tribe of Manashah Gawalan in Bashan with its suburbs, the Iyar of refuge for the manslayer, and Be Baishatharah with its suburbs; shanayam (two) Iyar.
Out of the matah (tribe) of Yashashakar, Qashayawan with its suburbs, dabarath (daberath) with its suburbs,
Yaramawath with its suburbs, Iyanaganayam Gannim with its suburbs; arabai (four) Iyar.
Out of the matah (tribe) of Ashar, Mashaal with its suburbs, Ibadawan with its suburbs,
Chalaqath with its suburbs, and Rachab with its suburbs; arabai (four) Iyar.
Out of the matah (tribe) of Napathalay, Qadash in Galayal with its suburbs, the Iyar of refuge for the manslayer, Chamathadaar with its suburbs, and Qarathan with its suburbs; shalawash (three) Iyar.
All the Iyar of the garashanay (gershonites) according to their mashapachah (families) were thirteen Iyar with their suburbs.
To the mashapachah (families) of the children of Mararay, the yathar (rest) Lawayay the Levites, out of the matah (tribe) of Zabawalawan, Yaqanaim with its suburbs, Qarathah with its suburbs,
Damanah with its suburbs, and Nahalal with its suburbs; arabai (four) Iyar.
Out of the tribe of Raawaban, Batzar with its suburbs, Yahatz with its suburbs,
Qadamawath with its suburbs, and Mawapaith with its suburbs; arabai (four) Iyar.
Out of the matah (tribe) of Gad, Ramathagalaid in Galaid with its suburbs, the Iyar of refuge for the manslayer, and Machanayam with its suburbs,
Chashabawan with its suburbs, Yaizayar with its suburbs; arabai (four) Iyar in all.

All these were the Iyar of the children of Mararay according to their mashapachah (families), even the yathar (rest) of the mashapachah (families) Lawayay the Levites. Their lot was shanayam (twelve) Iyar.
All the Iyar Lawayay the Levites in the midst of the achazah (possession) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) were arabaiyam (forty) - shamanah (eight) Iyar with their suburbs.
Iyar of these Iyar included their suburbs around them. It was this way with all these Iyar.
So Yahawah gave to Yasharaal (Israel) all the aratz (land) which he swore to nathan (give) to their abawath (fathers). They possessed it, and lived in it.

Yahawah gave them nawach (rest) all around, according to all that he swore to their abawath (fathers). Not a ayash (man) of all their ayab (enemies) stood panayam (before) them. Yahawah delivered all their ayab (enemies) into their yad (hand).
Nothing failed of any tawab (good) thing which Yahawah had spoken to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel). All came to bawaa (pass).
Then Yahawashawai called the Raawabanay (Reubenites), the Gaday (Gadites), and the half-tribe of Manashah,
and said to them, "You have kept all that Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah tzawah (commanded) you, and have listened to my qawal (voice) in all that I tzawah (commanded) you.
You have not left your ach (brothers) these many yawam (days) to this yawam (day), but have performed the duty of the matzawah (commandment) of Yahawah your Alahayam.

Now Yahawah your Alahayam has given nawach (rest) to your ach (brothers), as he spoke to them. Therefore now panah (return) and yalak (go) to your ahal (tents), to the aratz (land) of your achazah (possession), which Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah gave you ibar (beyond) the Yaradan.

Only take diligent shamar (heed) to do the matzawah (commandment) and the thawarah (law) which Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah tzawah (commanded) you, to ahab (love) Yahawah your Alahayam, to yalak (walk) in all his darak (ways), to shamar (keep) his matzawah (commandments), to hold fast to him, and to ibad (serve) him with all your labab (heart) and with all your napash (soul).
So Yahawashawai blessed them, and sent them shalach (away); and they went to their ahal (tents).

Now to the one half-tribe of Manashah Mashah had given inheritance in Bashan; but to the other chatzay (half) gave Yahawashawai among their ach (brothers) ibar (beyond) the Yaradan westward. Moreover when Yahawashawai sent them shalach (away) to their ahal (tents), he blessed them,

and spoke to them, saying, "shawab (turn back / repent) with much wealth to your ahal (tents), with very much livestock, with kasap (silver), with gold, with brass, with barazal (iron), and with very much clothing. Divide the spoil of your ayab (enemies) with your ach (brothers).

The children of Raawaban and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manashah returned, and departed from the children of Yasharaal (Israel) out of Shayalah, which is in the aratz (land) of Kanain, to yalak (go) to the aratz (land) of Galaid, to the aratz (land) of their achazah (possession), which they owned, according to the commandment of Yahawah by Mashah.

When they came to the region about the Yaradan, that is in the aratz (land) of Kanain, the children of Raawaban and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manashah built there an mazabach (altar) by the Yaradan, a gadawal (great) mazabach (altar) to look at.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) heard this, "Behold, the children of Raawaban and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manashah have built an mazabach (altar) in the forefront of the aratz (land) of Kanain, in the region about the Yaradan, on the ibar (side) that pertains to the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

When the children of Yasharaal (Israel) heard of it, the whole idah (congregation) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) gathered themselves together at Shayalah, to ilah (go) up against them to tzabaa (war).

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) sent to the children of Raawaban, and to the children of Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manashah, into the aratz (land) of Galaid, Payanachas the ban (son) of Alaizar the kahan (priest),

and with him ishar (ten) nashayaa (princes), one nashayaa (prince) of a abawath (fathers)' bayath (house) for achad (each) of the matah (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel); and they were everyone of them raash (head) of their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses) among the alap (thousands) of Yasharaal (Israel).
They came to the children of Raawaban, and to the children of Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manashah, to the aratz (land) of Galaid, and they spoke with them, saying,

"Thus amar (says) the whole idah (congregation) of Yahawah, ‘What mail (trespass) is this that you have committed against the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), to shawab (turn back / repent) away this yawam (day) from following Yahawah, in that you have built yourselves an mazabach (altar), to rebel this yawam (day) against Yahawah?
Is the iwan (iniquity) of Paiwar too Mait for us, from which we have not cleansed ourselves to this yawam (day), although there came a nagap (plague) on the idah (congregation) of Yahawah,

that you must shawab (turn back / repent) away this yawam (day) from following Yahawah? It will be, since you rebel today against Yahawah, that tomorrow he will be qatzap (angry) with the whole idah (congregation) of Yasharaal (Israel).

However, if the aratz (land) of your achazah (possession) is tamaa (unclean), then ibar (pass) over to the aratz (land) of the achazah (possession) of Yahawah, in which yahawah (yahweh's) mashakan (tabernacle) shakan (dwells), and take achaz (possession) among us; but don't rebel against Yahawah, nor rebel against us, in building an mazabach (altar) other than the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah our Alahayam.

Didn't Ikan the ban (son) of Zarach commit a mail (trespass) in the charam (devoted) thing, and qatzap (wrath) fell on all the idah (congregation) of Yasharaal (Israel)? That ayash (man) didn't gawai (perish) achad (alone) in his iwan (iniquity).'
Then the children of Raawaban and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manashah answered, and spoke to the raash (heads) of the alap (thousands) of Yasharaal (Israel),

"The Mighty One, Al, Yahawah, the Mighty One, Al, Yahawah, he yadai (knows); and Yasharaal (Israel) shall yadai (know): if it was in rebellion, or if in mail (trespass) against Yahawah (don't yashai (save) us this yawam (day)),

that we have built us an mazabach (altar) to shawab (turn back / repent) achar (away) from following Yahawah; or if to ilah (offer) burnt ilah (offering) or meal ilah (offering), or if to ishah (offer) sacrifices of shalam (peace) zabach (offerings), let Yahawah himself require it.

"If we have not out of concern done this, and for a reason, saying, ‘In time to come your children might amar (speak) to our children, saying, "What have you to do with Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel)?

For Yahawah has made the Yaradan a border between us and you, you children of Raawaban and children of Gad. You have no chalaq (portion) in Yahawah."' So your children might shabath (make) our children shabath (cease) from fearing Yahawah.
"Therefore we said, ‘Let's now ishah (prepare) to banah (build) ourselves an mazabach (altar), not for burnt ilah (offering), nor for zabach (sacrifice);

but it will be a witness between us and you, and between our dawar (generations) achar (after) us, that we may perform the ibadah (service) of Yahawah panayam (before) him with our burnt ilah (offerings), with our zabach (sacrifices), and with our shalam (peace) offerings;' that your children may not amar (tell) our children in time to come, ‘You have no chalaq (portion) in Yahawah.'

"Therefore we said, ‘It shall be, when they amar (tell) us or our dawar (generations) this in time to come, that we shall amar (say), "raah (see) the thabanayath (pattern) of the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah, which our abawath (fathers) made, not for burnt ilah (offering), nor for zabach (sacrifice); but it is a witness between us and you."'

"Far be it from us that we should rebel against Yahawah, and shawab (turn back / repent) away this yawam (day) from following Yahawah, to banah (build) an mazabach (altar) for burnt ilah (offering), for meal manachah (offering), or for zabach (sacrifice), besides the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah our Alahayam that is panayam (before) his mashakan (tabernacle)!

When Payanachas the kahan (priest), and the nashayaa (princes) of the idah (congregation), even the raash (heads) of the alap (thousands) of Yasharaal (Israel) that were with him, heard the dabar (words) that the children of Raawaban and the children of Gad and the children of Manashah spoke, it pleased them yatab (well).

Payanachas the ban (son) of Alaizar the kahan (priest) said to the children of Raawaban, to the children of Gad, and to the children of Manashah, "Today we yadai (know) that Yahawah is in the midst of us, because you have not committed this mail (trespass) against Yahawah. Now you have delivered the children of Yasharaal (Israel) out of the yad (hand) of Yahawah.

Payanachas the ban (son) of Alaizar the kahan (priest), and the nashayaa (princes), returned from the children of Raawaban, and from the children of Gad, out of the aratz (land) of Galaid, to the aratz (land) of Kanain, to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and brought them dabar (word) again.

The thing pleased the children of Yasharaal (Israel); and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) blessed Alahayam, and spoke no more of going up against them to tzabaa (war), to shachath (destroy) the aratz (land) in which the children of Raawaban and the children of Gad lived.
The children of Raawaban and the children of Gad named the mazabach (altar) "A Witness Between Us that Yahawah is Alahayam.

It happened achar (after) many yawam (days), when Yahawah had given nawach (rest) to Yasharaal (Israel) from their ayab (enemies) all around, and Yahawashawai was zaqan (old) and well advanced in yawam (years),

that Yahawashawai called for all Yasharaal (Israel), for their zaqan (elders) and for their raash (heads), and for their shapat (judges) and for their shatar (officers), and said to them, "I am zaqan (old) and well advanced in yawam (years).
You have seen all that Yahawah your Alahayam has done to all these gawayam (nations) panayam (because) of you; for it is Yahawah your Alahayam who has fought for you.

raah (see), I have allotted to you these gawayam (nations) that shaar (remain), to be an nachalah (inheritance) for your shabat (tribes), from the Yaradan, with all the gawayam (nations) that I have karath (cut) off, even to the gadawal (great) yam (sea) toward the going down of the mabawaa (sun).

Yahawah your Alahayam will thrust them out from panayam (before) you, and yarash (drive) them from out of your panayam (sight). You shall yarash (possess) their aratz (land), as Yahawah your Alahayam spoke to you.

"Therefore be very courageous to shamar (keep) and to do all that is written in the book of the thawarah (law) of Mashah, that you not sawar (turn) aside from it to the right yamayan (hand) or to the shamaawal (left);

that you not bawaa (come) among these gawayam (nations), these that shaar (remain) among you; neither zakar (make) mention of the sham (name) of their Alahayam, nor cause to shabai (swear) by them, neither ibad (serve) them, nor shachah (bow) down yourselves to them;
but hold fast to Yahawah your Alahayam, as you have done to this yawam (day).
"For Yahawah has driven gadawal (great) and itzawam (strong) gawayam (nations) out from panayam (before) you. But as for you, no ayash (man) has stood panayam (before) you to this yawam (day).
One ayash (man) of you shall chase a alap (thousand); for it is Yahawah your Alahayam who fights for you, as he spoke to you.
Take maad (good) shamar (heed) therefore to yourselves, that you ahab (love) Yahawah your Alahayam.

"But if you do at all shawab (turn back / repent) back, and hold fast to the yathar (remnant) of these gawayam (nations), even these who shaar (remain) among you, and chathan (make) marriages with them, and bawaa (go) in to them, and they to you;

yadai (know) for a certainty that Yahawah your Alahayam will no longer drive these gawayam (nations) from out of your panayam (sight); but they shall be a snare and a trap to you, a scourge in your sides, and thorns in your iyan (eyes), until you abad (perish) from off this tawab (good) adamah (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam has given you.

"Behold, today I am going the darak (way) of all the aratz (earth). You yadai (know) in all your labab (hearts) and in all your napash (souls) that not one thing has failed of all the tawab (good) things which Yahawah your Alahayam spoke concerning you. All have happened to you. Not one thing has failed of it.

It shall happen that as all the tawab (good) things have bawaa (come) on you of which Yahawah your Alahayam spoke to you, so Yahawah will bawaa (bring) on you all the rai (evil) things, until he has destroyed you from off this tawab (good) adamah (land) which Yahawah your Alahayam has given you,

when you disobey the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah your Alahayam, which he tzawah (commanded) you, and halak (go) and ibad (serve) other Alahayam, and shachah (bow) down yourselves to them. Then the ap (anger) of Yahawah will be kindled against you, and you will abad (perish) quickly from off the tawab (good) aratz (land) which he has given to you.

Yahawashawai gathered all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) to Shakam, and called for the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel), for their raash (heads), for their shapat (judges), and for their shatar (officers); and they presented panayam (themselves) before Alahayam.

Yahawashawai said to all the im (people), "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘Your abawath (fathers) lived of old time ibar (beyond) the nahar (river), even Tharach, the ab (father) of Abaraham, and the ab (father) of Nachawar: and they served other Alahayam.
I took your ab (father) Abaraham from ibar (beyond) the nahar (river), and led him throughout all the aratz (land) of Kanain, and multiplied his zarai (seed), and gave him Yatzachaq.
I gave to Yatzachaq Yaiqab and Ishaw: and I gave to Ishaw har (mount) Shaiyar, to yarash (possess) it. Yaiqab and his children went down into Matzarayam.
"‘I sent Mashah and Aharawan, and I plagued Matzarayam, according to that which I did in its qarab (midst): and afterward I brought you out.

I brought your abawath (fathers) out of Matzarayam: and you came to the yam (sea). The Matzarayam (Egyptians) pursued achar (after) your abawath (fathers) with chariots and with horsemen to the Red yam (sea).

When they cried out to Yahawah, he shawam (put) maapal (darkness) between you and the Matzaray (Egyptians), and brought the yam (sea) on them, and covered them; and your iyan (eyes) saw what I did in Matzarayam: and you lived in the madabar (wilderness) many yawam (days).

"‘I brought you into the aratz (land) of the Amaray (Amorites), that lived ibar (beyond) the Yaradan: and they fought with you; and I gave them into your yad (hand). You possessed their aratz (land); and I destroyed them from panayam (before) you.
Then Balaq the ban (son) of Tzapawar, malak (king) of Mawaab, qawam (arose) and fought against Yasharaal (Israel). He sent and called Balaim the ban (son) of Baiwar to qalal (curse) you;
but I would not listen to Balaim; therefore he blessed you still. So I delivered you out of his yad (hand).

"‘You went over the Yaradan, and came to Yarayachaw. The men of Yarayachaw fought against you, the Amaray (Amorite), the Parazay (Perizzite), the Kanainay (Canaanite), the Chathay (Hittite), the Garagashay (Girgashite), the Chaway (Hivite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite); and I delivered them into your yad (hand).

I sent the hornet panayam (before) you, which drove them out from panayam (before) you, even the shanayam (two) malak (kings) of the Amaray (Amorites); not with your charab (sword), nor with your qashath (bow).
I gave you a aratz (land) whereon you had not labored, and Iyar which you didn't banah (build), and you live in them. You akal (eat) of vineyards and olive groves which you didn't plant.'

"Now therefore yaraa (fear) Yahawah, and ibad (serve) him in thamayam (sincerity) and in truth. sawar (put) away the Alahayam which your abawath (fathers) served ibar (beyond) the nahar (river), in Matzarayam; and ibad (serve) Yahawah.

If it seems raii (evil) to you to ibad (serve) Yahawah, choose this yawam (day) whom you will ibad (serve); whether the Alahayam which your abawath (fathers) served that were ibar (beyond) the nahar (river), or the Alahayam of the Amaray (Amorites), in whose aratz (land) you yashab (dwell): but as for me and my bayath (house), we will ibad (serve) Yahawah.
The im (people) answered, "Far be it from us that we should forsake Yahawah, to ibad (serve) other Alahayam;

for it is Yahawah our Alahayam who brought us and our abawath (fathers) up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, from the bayath (house) of ibad (bondage), and who did those gadawal (great) awath (signs) in our iyan (sight), and preserved us in all the darak (way) in which we went, and among all the im (peoples) qarab (through) the midst of whom we passed.
Yahawah drove out from panayam (before) us all the im (peoples), even the Amaray (Amorites) who lived in the aratz (land). Therefore we also will ibad (serve) Yahawah; for he is our Alahayam.

Yahawashawai said to the im (people), "You can't ibad (serve) Yahawah; for he is a qadawash (holy) Alahayam. He is a Qanawaa Alahayam. He will not nashaa (forgive) your disobedience nor your chataah (sins).
If you forsake Yahawah, and ibad (serve) foreign Alahayam, then he will shawab (turn back / repent) and do you raii (evil), and kalah (consume) you, achar (after) he has done you yatab (good).
The im (people) said to Yahawashawai, "No; but we will ibad (serve) Yahawah.
Yahawashawai said to the im (people), "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen Yahawah yourselves, to ibad (serve) him." They said, "We are witnesses.
"Now therefore sawar (put) away the foreign Alahayam which are qarab (among) you, and natah (incline) your labab (heart) to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
The im (people) said to Yahawashawai, "We will ibad (serve) Yahawah our Alahayam, and we will listen to his qawal (voice).
So Yahawashawai made a barayath (covenant) with the im (people) that yawam (day), and made for them a chaq (statute) and an mashapat (ordinance) in Shakam.

Yahawashawai wrote these dabar (words) in the book of the thawarah (law) of Alahayam; and he took a gadawal (great) aban (stone), and qawam (set) it up there under the oak that was by the maqadash (sanctuary) of Yahawah.

Yahawashawai said to all the im (people), "Behold, this aban (stone) shall be a idah (witness) against us; for it has heard all the amar (words) of Yahawah which he spoke to us. It shall be therefore a idah (witness) against you, lest you deny your Alahayam.
So Yahawashawai sent the im (people) shalach (away), every ayash (man) to his nachalah (inheritance).
It happened achar (after) these things, that Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan, the ibad (servant) of Yahawah, died, being one maah (hundred) and ishar (ten) Shanah ban (old).
They buried him in the border of his nachalah (inheritance) in Thamanathacharas, which is in the har (hill) country of Aparayam, on the tzapawan (north) of the har (mountain) of Gaish.

Yasharaal (Israel) served Yahawah all the yawam (days) of Yahawashawai, and all the yawam (days) of the zaqan (elders) who yawam (outlived) Yahawashawai, and had yadai (known) all the maishah (work) of Yahawah, that he had worked for Yasharaal (Israel).

They buried the itzam (bones) of Yawasap, which the children of Yasharaal (Israel) brought up out of Matzarayam, in Shakam, in the chalaqah (parcel) of shadah (ground) which Yaiqab bought of the ban (sons) of Chamawar the ab (father) of Shakam for a maah (hundred) pieces of money. They became the nachalah (inheritance) of the children of Yawasap.
Alaizar the ban (son) of Aharawan died. They buried him in the Gabaih of Payanachas his ban (son), which was given him in the har (hill) country of Aparayam.

It happened achar (after) the mawath (death) of Yahawashawai, the children of Yasharaal (Israel) asked of Yahawah, saying, "Who should ilah (go) up for us thachalah (first) against the Kanainay (Canaanites), to fight against them?
Yahawah said, "Yahawadah (Judah) shall ilah (go) up. Behold, I have delivered the aratz (land) into his yad (hand).

Yahawadah (Judah) said to Shamaiwan his ach (brother), "ilah (come) up with me into my lot, that we may fight against the Kanainay (Canaanites); and I likewise will halak (go) with you into your lot." So Shamaiwan went with him.
Yahawadah (Judah) went up; and Yahawah delivered the Kanainay (Canaanites) and the Parazay (Perizzites) into their yad (hand): and they struck of them in Bazaq ishar (ten) alap (thousand) men.
They found Adanayabazaq in Bazaq; and they fought against him, and they struck the Kanainay (Canaanites) and the Parazay (Perizzites).
But Adanayabazaq fled; and they pursued achar (after) him, and caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his ragal (great) toes.

Adanayabazaq said, "shabaiyam (seventy) malak (kings), having their thumbs and their ragal (great) toes cut off, scavenged under my table: as I have done, so Alahayam has requited me." They brought him to Yarawashalam, and he died there.
The children of Yahawadah (Judah) fought against Yarawashalam, and took it, and struck it with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), and shalach (set) the Iyar on ash (fire).
Afterward the children of Yahawadah (Judah) went down to fight against the Kanainay (Canaanites) who lived in the har (hill) Nagab, and in the South, and in the lowland.

Yahawadah (Judah) went against the Kanainay (Canaanites) who lived in Chabarawan (now the sham (name) of Chabarawan panayam (before) was Kiriath Qarayathaarabai); and they struck Shashay, and Achayaman, and Thalamay.
From there he went against the yashab (inhabitants) of Dabayar. (Now the sham (name) of Dabayar panayam (before) was Kiriath Qarayathasanah.)
Kalab said, "He who strikes Kiriath Qarayathasanah, and takes it, to him will I nathan (give) Ikasah my bath (daughter) as ashah (wife).
Ithanayaal the ban (son) of Qanaz, Kalab younger ach (brother), took it: and he gave him Ikasah his bath (daughter) as ashah (wife).
It happened, when she came, that she got him to shaal (ask) her ab (father) for a shadah (field): and she alighted from off her donkey; and Kalab said to her, "What would you like?

She said to him, "Give me a barakah (blessing); for that you have nathan (set) me in the aratz (land) of the Nagab, nathan (give) me also springs of mayam (water)." Then Kalab gave her the Ilay springs and the Thachathay springs.

The children of the Qayanay (Kenite), Mashah' brother-in-law, went up out of the Iyar of palm trees with the children of Yahawadah (Judah) into the madabar (wilderness) of Yahawadah (Judah), which is in the Nagab of Irad; and they went and lived with the im (people).

Yahawadah (Judah) went with Shamaiwan his ach (brother), and they struck the Kanainay (Canaanites) who inhabited Tzapath, and charam (utterly) destroyed it. The sham (name) of the Iyar was called Charamah.
Also Yahawadah (Judah) took Izah with its border, and Ashaqalawan with its border, and Iqarawan with its border.

Yahawah was with Yahawadah (Judah); and drove out the inhabitants of the har (hill) country; for he could not yarash (drive) out the yashab (inhabitants) of the valley, because they had chariots of barazal (iron).
They gave Chabarawan to Kalab, as Mashah had spoken: and he drove out there the shalawash (three) ban (sons) of Inaq.

The children of Banayamayan did not yarash (drive) out the Yabawasay (Jebusites) who inhabited Yarawashalam; but the Yabawasay (Jebusites) yashab (dwell) with the children of Banayamayan in Yarawashalam to this yawam (day).
The bayath (house) of Yawasap, they also went up against Bayathaal; and Yahawah was with them.
The bayath (house) of Yawasap sent to spy out Bayathaal. (Now the sham (name) of the Iyar panayam (before) was Lawaz.)
The watchers saw a ayash (man) yatzaa (come) forth out of the Iyar, and they said to him, "Please show us the entrance into the Iyar, and we will ishah (deal) chasad (kindly) with you.
He showed them the entrance into the Iyar; and they struck the Iyar with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); but they let the ayash (man) shalach (go) and all his mashapachah (family).
The ayash (man) went into the aratz (land) of the Chathay (Hittites), and built a Iyar, and called its sham (name) Lawaz, which is its sham (name) to this yawam (day).

Manashah did not yarash (drive) out the inhabitants of Bayathashaan Shean and its bath (towns), nor Thainak and its bath (towns), nor the yashab (inhabitants) of Dawar and its bath (towns), nor the yashab (inhabitants) of Yabalaim and its bath (towns), nor the yashab (inhabitants) of Magadawan and its bath (towns); but the Kanainay (Canaanites) would yashab (dwell) in that aratz (land).
It happened, when Yasharaal (Israel) had grown chazaq (strong), that they shawam (put) the Kanainay (Canaanites) to forced mas (labor), and did not yarash (utterly) yarash (drive) them out.
Aparayam didn't yarash (drive) out the Kanainay (Canaanites) who lived in Gazar; but the Kanainay (Canaanites) lived in Gazar qarab (among) them.

Zabawalawan didn't yarash (drive) out the yashab (inhabitants) of Qatarawan, nor the yashab (inhabitants) of Nahalal; but the Kanainay (Canaanites) lived qarab (among) them, and became subject to forced mas (labor).
Ashar didn't yarash (drive) out the yashab (inhabitants) Ikaw Acco, nor the yashab (inhabitants) of Tzayadawan, nor of Achalab, nor of Akazayab, nor of Chalabah, nor of Apaq, nor of Rachab;
but the Asharay (Asherites) lived qarab (among) the Kanainay (Canaanites), the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land); for they did not yarash (drive) them out.

Napathalay didn't yarash (drive) out the yashab (inhabitants) of Bayathashamash Shemesh, nor the yashab (inhabitants) of Bayathainath Anath; but he lived qarab (among) the Kanainay (Canaanites), the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land): nevertheless the yashab (inhabitants) of Bayathashamash Shemesh and of Bayathainath Anath became subject to forced mas (labor).
The Amaray (Amorites) forced the children Dan Dan into the har (hill) country; for they would not allow them to yarad (come) down to the valley;

but the Amaray (Amorites) would yashab (dwell) in har (mount) Charas, in Ayalawan, and in Shailabayam: yet the yad (hand) of the bayath (house) of Yawasap prevailed, so that they became subject to forced mas (labor).
The border of the Amaray (Amorites) was from the ascent of Mailahaiqarabayam, from the salai (rock), and upward.

The malaak (angel) of Yahawah came up from Galagal to Bakayam. He said, "I made you to ilah (go) up out of Matzarayam, and have brought you to the aratz (land) which I swore to your abawath (fathers); and I said, ‘I will never parar (break) my barayath (covenant) with you:

and you shall karath (make) no barayath (covenant) with the yashab (inhabitants) of this aratz (land); you shall nathatz (break) down their mazabach (altars).' But you have not listened to my qawal (voice): why have you done this?
Therefore I also said, I will not drive them out from panayam (before) you; but they shall be in your sides, and their Alahayam shall be a snare to you.
It happened, when the malaak (angel) of Yahawah spoke these dabar (words) to all the children of Yasharaal (Israel), that the im (people) lifted up their qawal (voice), and wept.
They called the sham (name) of that place Bakayam: and they sacrificed there to Yahawah.
Now when Yahawashawai had sent the im (people) shalach (away), the children of Yasharaal (Israel) went every ayash (man) to his nachalah (inheritance) to yarash (possess) the aratz (land).

The im (people) served Yahawah all the yawam (days) of Yahawashawai, and all the yawam (days) of the zaqan (elders) who yawam (outlived) Yahawashawai, who had seen all the gadawal (great) maishah (work) of Yahawah that he had worked for Yasharaal (Israel).
Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan, the ibad (servant) of Yahawah, died, being one maah (hundred) ishar (ten) Shanah ban (old).
They buried him in the border of his nachalah (inheritance) in Timnath Heres, in the hill country of Aparayam, on the north of the har (mountain) of Gaish.

Also all that dawar (generation) were gathered to their abawath (fathers): and there qawam (arose) achar (another) dawar (generation) achar (after) them, who didn't yadai (know) Yahawah, nor yet the maishah (work) which he had worked for Yasharaal (Israel).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, and served the Bail;

and they forsook Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers), who brought them out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and followed other Alahayam, of the Alahayam of the im (peoples) who were around them, and bowed themselves down to them: and they provoked Yahawah to kais (anger).
They forsook Yahawah, and served Bail and the Ishatharawath.

The ap (anger) of Yahawah was kindled against Yasharaal (Israel), and he delivered them into the yad (hands) of spoilers who despoiled them; and he sold them into the yad (hands) of their ayab (enemies) all around, so that they could not any iwad (longer) imad (stand) panayam (before) their ayab (enemies).
Wherever they went out, the yad (hand) of Yahawah was against them for rai (evil), as Yahawah had spoken, and as Yahawah had sworn to them: and they were very distressed.
Yahawah raised up shapat (judges), who saved them out of the yad (hand) of those who despoiled them.

Yet they didn't listen to their shapat (judges); for they played the prostitute achar (after) other Alahayam, and bowed themselves down to them: they turned aside Mahar out of the darak (way) in which their abawath (fathers) walked, obeying the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah. They didn't do so.

When Yahawah raised them up shapat (judges), then Yahawah was with the shapat (judge), and saved them out of the yad (hand) of their ayab (enemies) all the yawam (days) of the shapat (judge): for it grieved Yahawah panayam (because) of their groaning by reason of those who oppressed them and troubled them.

But it happened, when the shapat (judge) was mawath (dead), that they turned back, and dealt more corruptly than their abawath (fathers), in yalak (following) other Alahayam to ibad (serve) them, and to shachah (bow) down to them; they didn't napal (cease) from their mailal (doings), nor from their Qashah darak (way).

The ap (anger) of Yahawah was kindled against Yasharaal (Israel); and he said, "Because this gaway (nation) have transgressed my barayath (covenant) which I tzawah (commanded) their abawath (fathers), and have not listened to my qawal (voice);
I also will not henceforth yarash (drive) out any from panayam (before) them of the gawayam (nations) that Yahawashawai left when he died;
that by them I may prove Yasharaal (Israel), whether they will shamar (keep) the darak (way) of Yahawah to yalak (walk) therein, as their abawath (fathers) kept it, or not.
So Yahawah left those gawayam (nations), balathay (without) yarash (driving) them out Mahar; neither delivered he them into the yad (hand) of Yahawashawai.
Now these are the gawayam (nations) which Yahawah left, to prove Yasharaal (Israel) by them, even as many as had not yadai (known) all the wars of Kanain;
only that the dawar (generations) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) might yadai (know), to teach them war, at the least such as panayam (before) knew nothing of it:

the chamash (five) lords of the Palashathay (Philistines), and all the Kanainay (Canaanites), and the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), and the Chaway (Hivites) who lived on har (mount) Labanawan, from har (mount) Bailacharamawan Hermon to the entrance of Chamath.
They were left to test Yasharaal (Israel) by them, to yadai (know) whether they would listen to the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah, which he tzawah (commanded) their abawath (fathers) by Mashah.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) lived qarab (among) the Kanainay (Canaanites), the Chathay (Hittites), and the Amaray (Amorites), and the Parazay (Perizzites), and the Chaway (Hivites), and the Yabawasay (Jebusites):
and they took their bath (daughters) to be their wives, and gave their own bath (daughters) to their ban (sons) and served their Alahayam.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, and forgot Yahawah their Alahayam, and served the Bail and the Asharah.

Therefore the ap (anger) of Yahawah was kindled against Yasharaal (Israel), and he sold them into the yad (hand) Kawashanarashaithayam Cushan Rishathaim malak (king) of Aramanaharayam: and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) served Kawashanarashaithayam Rishathaim shamanah (eight) Shanah.

When the children of Yasharaal (Israel) cried to Yahawah, Yahawah raised up a savior to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), who saved them, even Ithanayaal the ban (son) of Qanaz, Kalab younger ach (brother).

The rawach (spirit) of Yahawah came on him, and he judged Yasharaal (Israel); and he went out to war, and Yahawah delivered Kawashanarashaithayam Rishathaim malak (king) of Aramanaharayam into his yad (hand): and his yad (hand) prevailed Kawashanarashaithayam Cushan Rishathaim.
The aratz (land) had shaqat (rest) arabaiyam (forty) Shanah. Ithanayaal the ban (son) of Qanaz died.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) again did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah: and Yahawah strengthened Igalawan the malak (king) of Mawaab against Yasharaal (Israel), because they had done that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah.
He gathered to him the children of Imawan and Imalaq; and he went and struck Yasharaal (Israel), and they possessed the Iyar of palm trees.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) served Igalawan the malak (king) of Mawaab eighteen Shanah.

But when the children of Yasharaal (Israel) cried to Yahawah, Yahawah raised them up a savior, Ahawad the ban (son) of Garaa, the Banayamayanay (Benjamite), a ayash (man) Atar. The children of Yasharaal (Israel) sent tribute by him to Igalawan the malak (king) of Mawaab.
Ahawad made him a charab (sword) which had shanayam (two) edges, a cubit in arak (length); and he wore it under his clothing on his yamayan (right) thigh.
He offered the tribute to Igalawan malak (king) of Mawaab: now Igalawan was a very Barayaa ayash (man).
When he had made an kalah (end) of offering the tribute, he sent shalach (away) the im (people) who bore the tribute.

But he himself turned shawab (turn back / repent) from the pasayal (quarries) that were by Galagal, and said, "I have a secret dabar (errand) to you, malak (king)." The king said, "Keep hasah (silence)!" All who stood by him went out from him.
Ahawad came to him; and he was sitting by himself maqarah (alone) in the cool upper room. Ahawad said, "I have a dabar (message) from Alahayam to you." He qawam (arose) out of his kasaa (seat).
Ahawad shalach (put) forth his shamaawal (left) yad (hand), and took the charab (sword) from his yamayan (right) thigh, and thrust it into his body:
and the handle also went in achar (after) the lahab (blade); and the fat closed on the lahab (blade), for he didn't draw the charab (sword) out of his body; and it came out behind.
Then Ahawad went yatzaa (forth) into the porch, and shut the doors of the upper room on him, and locked them.
Now when he was gone out, his ibad (servants) came; and they saw, and behold, the doors of the upper room were locked; and they said, "Surely he is covering his feet in the upper room.

They waited until they were bawash (ashamed); and behold, he didn't pathach (open) the doors of the upper room: therefore they took the key, and opened them, and behold, their Adawan was fallen down mawath (dead) on the aratz (earth).
Ahawad escaped while they waited, and passed ibar (beyond) the pasayal (quarries), and escaped Shaiyarah Seirah.

It happened, when he had bawaa (come), that he blew a trumpet in the har (hill) country of Aparayam; and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) went down with him from the har (hill) country, and he panayam (before) them.

He said to them, "Follow me; for Yahawah has delivered your ayab (enemies) the Mawaab (Moabites) into your yad (hand)." They followed him, and took the fords of the Yaradan Mawaab the Moabites, and didn't allow any ayash (man) to ibar (pass) over.
They struck of Mawaab at that ith (time) about ishar (ten) alap (thousand) men, every Shaman ayash (man), and every man of valor; and there escaped not a ayash (man).
So Mawaab was subdued that yawam (day) under the yad (hand) of Yasharaal (Israel). The aratz (land) had shaqat (rest) shamanayam (eighty) Shanah.
achar (after) him was Shamagar the ban (son) of Inath, who struck of the Palashathay (Philistines) shash (six) maah (hundred) men with an ox - goad: and he also saved Yasharaal (Israel).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) again did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, when Ahawad was mawath (dead).

Yahawah sold them into the yad (hand) of Yabayan malak (king) of Kanain, who reigned in Chatzawar; the shar (captain) of whose tzabaa (army) was Sayasaraa, who lived in Charashath of the gawayam (gentiles).

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) cried to Yahawah: for he had thashai (nine) maah (hundred) chariots of barazal (iron); and isharayam (twenty) Shanah he mightily oppressed the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
Now Dabawarah, a prophetess, the ashah (wife) of Lapayadawath, she judged Yasharaal (Israel) at that ith (time).
She lived under the palm tree of Dabawarah between Ramah and Bayathaal in the har (hill) country of Aparayam: and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) came up to her for mashapat (judgment).

She sent and called Baraq the ban (son) of Abayanaim out of Qadash Naphtali, and said to him, "Hasn't Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), tzawah (commanded), ‘yalak (go) and draw to har (mount) Thabawar, and take with you ishar (ten) alap (thousand) men of the children of Napathalay and of the children of Zabawalawan?

I will draw to you, to the nachal (river) Qayashawan, Sayasaraa, the shar (captain) of Yabayan tzabaa (army), with his chariots and his multitude; and I will nathan (deliver) him into your yad (hand).'
Baraq said to her, "If you will yalak (go) with me, then I will yalak (go); but if you will not halak (go) with me, I will not yalak (go).

She said, "I will halak (surely) yalak (go) with you: apas (nevertheless), the darak (journey) that you take shall not be for your honor; for Yahawah will sell Sayasaraa into the yad (hand) of a ashah (woman)." Dabawarah qawam (arose), and went with Baraq to Qadash.
Baraq called Zabawalawan and Napathalay together to Qadash; and there went up ishar (ten) alap (thousand) men at his feet: and Dabawarah went up with him.

Now Chabar the Qayanay (Kenite) had separated himself from the Qayanay (Kenites), even from the children of Chabab the brother-in-law of Mashah, and had pitched his ahal (tent) as far as the oak Tzainanayam Zaanannim, which is by Qadash.
They told Sayasaraa that Baraq the ban (son) of Abayanaim was gone up to har (mount) Thabawar.

Sayasaraa gathered together all his chariots, even thashai (nine) maah (hundred) chariots of barazal (iron), and all the im (people) who were with him, from Charashath of the gawayam (gentiles), to the nachal (river) Qayashawan.

Dabawarah said to Baraq, "Go; for this is the yawam (day) in which Yahawah has delivered Sayasaraa into your yad (hand). Hasn't Yahawah gone out panayam (before) you?" So Baraq went down from har (mount) Thabawar, and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) men achar (after) him.

Yahawah confused Sayasaraa, and all his chariots, and all his machanah (army), with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword) panayam (before) Baraq; and Sayasaraa alighted from his chariot, and fled away on his feet.

But Baraq pursued achar (after) the chariots, and after the machanah (army), to Charashath of the gawayam (gentiles): and all the machanah (army) of Sayasaraa napal (fell) by the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); there was not a achad (man) shaar (left).

However Sayasaraa fled away on his feet to the ahal (tent) of Yail the ashah (wife) of Chabar the Qayanay (Kenite); for there was shalawam (peace) between Yabayan the malak (king) of Chatzawar and the bayath (house) of Chabar the Qayanay (Kenite).

Yail went out to qaraah (meet) Sayasaraa, and said to him, "sawar (turn) in, my Adawan, sawar (turn) in to me; don't be yaraa (afraid)." He came in to her into the ahal (tent), and she covered him with a rug.
He said to her, "Please give me a Mait mayam (water) to shaqah (drink); for I am thirsty." She opened a bottle of milk, and gave him shaqah (drink), and covered him.

He said to her, "imad (stand) in the door of the ahal (tent), and it shall be, when any ayash (man) bawaa (comes) and inquires of you, and amar (says), ‘Is there any ayash (man) here?' that you shall amar (say), ‘No.'

Then Yail Chabar ashah (wife) took a ahal (tent) peg, and took a hammer in her yad (hand), and went softly to him, and struck the peg into his raqah (temples), and it pierced through into the aratz (ground); for he was in a radam (deep) sleep; so he swooned and died.

Behold, as Baraq pursued Sayasaraa, Yail came out to qaraah (meet) him, and said to him, "yalak (come), and I will show you the ayash (man) whom you seek." He came to her; and behold, Sayasaraa napal (lay) mawath (dead), and the yathad (tent) peg was in his raqah (temples).
So Alahayam subdued on that yawam (day) Yabayan the malak (king) of Kanain panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
The yad (hand) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) Qashah more and more against Yabayan the malak (king) of Kanain, until they had destroyed Yabayan malak (king) of Kanain.
Then Dabawarah and Baraq the ban (son) of Abayanaim sang on that yawam (day), saying,
"Because the leaders took the lead in Yasharaal (Israel), because the im (people) offered themselves willingly, be blessed, Yahawah!
"Hear, you malak (kings)! Give ear, you razan (princes)! I, even I, will shayar (sing) to Yahawah. I will zamar (sing) praise to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
"Yahawah, when you went yatzaa (forth) out of Shaiyar, when you marched out of the shadah (field) of Adam, the aratz (earth) trembled, the sky also dropped. Yes, the clouds dropped mayam (water).
The har (mountains) quaked at the panayam (presence) of Yahawah, even Sayanay, at the panayam (presence) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
"In the yawam (days) of Shamagar the ban (son) of Inath, in the yawam (days) of Yail, the highways were chadal (unoccupied). The halak (travelers) walked through iqalaqal (byways).
The parazawan (rulers) ceased in Yasharaal (Israel). They ceased until I, Dabawarah, qawam (arose); Until I qawam (arose) a am (mother) in Yasharaal (Israel).
They chose Chadash Alahayam. Then war was in the gates. Was there a magan (shield) or spear seen among arabaiyam (forty) alap (thousand) in Yasharaal (Israel)?
My lab (heart) is toward the chaqaq (governors) of Yasharaal (Israel), who offered themselves willingly among the im (people). barak (bless) Yahawah!
"Speak, you who ride on Tzachar donkeys, you who yashab (sit) on rich carpets, and you who halak (walk) by the darak (way).

Far from the qawal (noise) of archers, in the places of drawing mashaab (water), there they will rehearse the tzadaqah (righteous) acts of Yahawah, the tzadaqah (righteous) acts of his rule in Yasharaal (Israel). "Then the im (people) of Yahawah went down to the gates.
‘Awake, awake, Dabawarah! Awake, awake, dabar (utter) a song! qawam (arise), Baraq, and lead Shabay your captives, you ban (son) of Abayanaim.'
"Then a sharayad (remnant) of the adayar (nobles) and the im (people) came down. Yahawah came down for me radah (against) the gabawar (mighty).

Those whose root is in Imalaq came out of Aparayam, achar (after) you, Banayamayan, among your im (peoples). chaqaq (governors) yarad (come) down out of Makayar. Those who handle the marshal's shabat (staff) came out of Zabawalawan.

The shar (princes) of Yashashakar were with Dabawarah. As was Yashashakar, so was Baraq. They rushed into the valley at his feet. By the watercourses of Raawaban, there were gadawal (great) resolves of lab (heart).
Why did you yashab (sit) among the sheepfolds, To hear the whistling for the flocks? At the watercourses of Raawaban There were gadawal (great) searchings of lab (heart).
Galaid lived ibar (beyond) the Yaradan. Dan did Dan gawar (remain) in ships? Ashar sat still at the haven of the yam (sea), and lived by his creeks.
Zabawalawan was a im (people) that jeopardized their lives to the mawath (deaths); Napathalay also, on the high places of the shadah (field).
"The malak (kings) came and fought, then the malak (kings) of Kanain fought at Thainak by the mayam (waters) of Magadawan. They took no plunder of kasap (silver).
From the sky the kawakab (stars) fought. From their masalah (courses), they fought against Sayasaraa.
The nachal (river) Qayashawan swept them away, that ancient nachal (river), the nachal (river) Qayashawan. My napash (soul), march on with iz (strength).
Then the horse hoofs stamped because of the prancings, the prancings of their abayar (strong) ones.

‘arar (curse) Marawaz,' said the malaak (angel) of Yahawah. ‘arar (curse) arar (bitterly) its yashab (inhabitants), because they didn't bawaa (come) to help Yahawah, to help Yahawah against the gabawar (mighty).'
"Yail shall be blessed above women, the ashah (wife) of Chabar the Qayanay (Kenite); blessed shall she be above women in the ahal (tent).
He asked for mayam (water). She gave him milk. She brought him butter in a adayar (lordly) dish.

She shalach (put) her yad (hand) to the yathad (tent) peg, and her right yamayan (hand) to the workmen's hammer. With the hammer she struck Sayasaraa. She struck through his raash (head). Yes, she pierced and struck through his raqah (temples).
At her feet he bowed, he napal (fell), he shakab (lay). At her feet he bowed, he napal (fell). Where he bowed, there he napal (fell) down shadad (dead).
"Through the window she looked out, and cried: Sayasaraa am (mother) looked through the lattice. ‘Why is his chariot so long in coming? Why do the paim (wheels) of his chariots wait?'
Her chakam (wise) sharah (ladies) answered her, Yes, she returned amar (answer) to herself,

‘Have they not found, have they not divided the spoil? A lady, rachamah (two) ladies to raash (every) gabar (man); to Sayasaraa a spoil of dyed garments, a spoil of dyed garments embroidered, of dyed garments embroidered on both sides, on the necks of the spoil?'

"So let all your ayab (enemies) abad (perish), Yahawah, but let those who ahab (love) him be as the shamash (sun) when it rises yatzaa (forth) in its gabawarah (strength)." Then the aratz (land) had shaqat (rest) arabaiyam (forty) Shanah.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah: and Yahawah delivered them into the yad (hand) of Madayan shabai (seven) Shanah.

The yad (hand) of Madayan prevailed against Yasharaal (Israel); and panayam (because) of Madayan the children of Yasharaal (Israel) made them the dens which are in the har (mountains), and the caves, and the strongholds.
So it was, when Yasharaal (Israel) had sown, that the Madayan (Midianites) came up, and the Imalaq (Amalekites), and the children of the qadam (east); they came up against them;

and they encamped against them, and destroyed the increase of the aratz (earth), until you bawaa (come) to Izah, and shaar (left) no machayah (sustenance) in Yasharaal (Israel), neither sheep, nor ox, nor donkey.

For they came up with their livestock and their ahal (tents); they came in as locusts for multitude; both they and their camels were without number: and they came into the aratz (land) to shachath (destroy) it.
Yasharaal (Israel) was brought very low panayam (because) of Madayan; and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) cried to Yahawah.
It happened, when the children of Yasharaal (Israel) cried to Yahawah because of Madayan,

that Yahawah sent a prophet to the children of Yasharaal (Israel): and he said to them, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘I brought you up from Matzarayam, and brought you yatzaa (forth) out of the bayath (house) of ibad (bondage);

and I delivered you out of the yad (hand) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and out of the yad (hand) of all who oppressed you, and drove them out from panayam (before) you, and gave you their aratz (land);

and I said to you, "I am Yahawah your Alahayam; you shall not yaraa (fear) the Alahayam of the Amaray (Amorites), in whose aratz (land) you yashab (dwell)." But you have not listened to my qawal (voice).'

The malaak (angel) of Yahawah came, and sat under the oak which was in Iparah, that pertained to Yawaash the Abayahaizaray: and his ban (son) Gadaiwan was beating out wheat in the winepress, to hide it from the Madayan (Midianites).
The malaak (angel) of Yahawah raah (see) to him, and said to him, "Yahawah is with you, you gabawar (mighty) man of valor!

Gadaiwan said to him, "Oh, my Adawan, if Yahawah is with us, why then has all this happened to us? Where are all his wondrous palaa (works) which our abawath (fathers) told us of, saying, ‘Didn't Yahawah ilah (bring) us up from Matzarayam?' But now Yahawah has cast us off, and delivered us into the kap (hand) of Madayan.
Yahawah looked at him, and said, "yalak (go) in this your might, and yashai (save) Yasharaal (Israel) from the kap (hand) of Madayan. Haven't I sent you?
He said to him, "O Adanay, mah (how) shall I yashai (save) Yasharaal (Israel)? Behold, my alap (family) is the Dal in Manashah, and I am the Tzaiyar in my ab (father's) bayath (house).
Yahawah said to him, "Surely I will be with you, and you shall strike the Madayan (Midianites) as one ayash (man).
He said to him, "If now I have found favor in your iyan (sight), then show me a awath (sign) that it is you who dabar (talk) with me.

Please don't mawash (go) away, until I bawaa (come) to you, and yatzaa (bring) out my manachah (present), and yanach (lay) it panayam (before) you." He said, "I will wait until you shawab (turn back / repent) back.

Gadaiwan went in, and prepared a young goat, and unleavened matzah (cakes) of an ephah of meal. He shawam (put) the meat in a basket and he shawam (put) the broth in a pot, and brought it out to him under the oak, and presented it.
The malaak (angel) of Alahayam said to him, "Take the meat and the unleavened matzah (cakes), and yanach (lay) them on this salai (rock), and pour out the broth." He did so.

Then the malaak (angel) of Yahawah stretched out the end of the mashainah (staff) that was in his yad (hand), and touched the meat and the unleavened matzah (cakes); and ash (fire) went up out of the tzawar (rock), and consumed the meat and the unleavened matzah (cakes); and the malaak (angel) of Yahawah departed out of his iyan (sight).
Gadaiwan saw that he was the malaak (angel) of Yahawah; and Gadaiwan said, "Alas, Adawan Yahawah! Kan I have seen the malaak (angel) of Yahawah panayam (face) to panayam (face)!
Yahawah said to him, "shalawam (peace) be to you! Don't be yaraa (afraid). You shall not mawath (die).
Then Gadaiwan built an mazabach (altar) there to Yahawah, and called it "Yahawah is Peace." To this yawam (day) it is still in Iparah of the Abayahaizaray.

It happened the same layal (night), that Yahawah said to him, "Take your ab (father's) bull, even the shanay (second) bull shabai (seven) Shanah old, and haras (throw) down the mazabach (altar) of Bail that your ab (father) has, and cut down the Asharah that is by it;

and banah (build) an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah your Alahayam on the raash (top) of this stronghold, in an orderly way, and take the shanay (second) bull, and ilah (offer) a burnt offering with the itz (wood) Asharah the Asherah which you shall karath (cut) down.

Then Gadaiwan took ishar (ten) men of his ibad (servants), and did as Yahawah had spoken to him: and it happened, because he feared his ab (father's) bayath (household) and the men of the Iyar, so that he could not do it by yawamam (day), that he did it by layal (night).

When the men of the Iyar arose shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), behold, the mazabach (altar) of Bail was broken down, and the Asharah was cut down that was by it, and the shanay (second) bull was offered on the mazabach (altar) that was built.
They said one to rai (another), "Who has done this thing?" When they inquired and asked, they said, "Gadaiwan the ban (son) of Yawaash has done this thing.

Then the men of the Iyar said to Yawaash, "yatzaa (bring) out your ban (son), that he may mawath (die), because he has broken down the mazabach (altar) of Bail, and because he has karath (cut) down the Asharah that was by it.

Yawaash said to all who stood against him, "Will you rayab (contend) for Bail? Or will you yashai (save) him? He who will rayab (contend) for him, let him be put to mawath (death) by baqar (morning). If he is a Alahayam, let him rayab (contend) for himself, because someone has broken down his mazabach (altar).
Therefore on that yawam (day) he named him Yarabail, saying, "Let Bail rayab (contend) against him, because he has broken down his mazabach (altar).
Then all the Madayan (Midianites) and the Imalaq (Amalekites) and the children of the qadam (east) assembled themselves together; and they passed over, and encamped in the valley of Yazaraial.
But the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah Labash on Gadaiwan; and he blew a trumpet; and Abayaizar was gathered together achar (after) him.

He sent malaak (messengers) throughout all Manashah; and they also were gathered together achar (after) him: and he sent malaak (messengers) to Ashar, and to Zabawalawan, and to Napathalay; and they came up to qaraah (meet) them.
Gadaiwan said to Alahayam, "If you will yashai (save) Yasharaal (Israel) by my yad (hand), as you have spoken,

behold, I will put a fleece of wool on the threshing floor; if there is dew on the fleece only, and it is dry on all the aratz (ground), then shall I yadai (know) that you will yashai (save) Yasharaal (Israel) by my yad (hand), as you have spoken.
It was so; for he rose up shakam (early) on the next macharath (day), and pressed the fleece together, and wrung the dew out of the fleece, a bowl full of mayam (water).

Gadaiwan said to Alahayam, "Don't let your ap (anger) be kindled against me, and I will dabar (speak) but this paim (once). Please let me make a trial just this paim (once) with the fleece. Let it now be dry only on the fleece, and on all the aratz (ground) let there be dew.
Alahayam did so that layal (night): for it was dry on the fleece only, and there was dew on all the aratz (ground).

Then Yarabail, who is Gadaiwan, and all the im (people) who were with him, rose up shakam (early), and encamped beside the spring of Iyanacharad: and the machanah (camp) of Madayan was on the tzapawan (north) side of them, by the Gabaih of Mawarah, in the valley.

Yahawah said to Gadaiwan, "The im (people) who are with you are rab (too) many for me to nathan (give) the Madayan (Midianites) into their yad (hand), lest Yasharaal (Israel) paar (vaunt) themselves amar (against) me, saying, ‘My own yad (hand) has saved me.'

Now therefore qaraa (proclaim) in the ears of the im (people), saying, 'Whoever is yaraa (fearful) and Charad, let him shawab (turn back / repent) and depart from har (mount) Galaid.'" isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) of the im (people) returned, and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) remained.

Yahawah said to Gadaiwan, "The im (people) are still rab (too) many. yarad (bring) them down to the mayam (water), and I will test them for you there. It shall be, that of whom I amar (tell) you, ‘This shall yalak (go) with you,' the same shall yalak (go) with you; and of whoever I amar (tell) you, ‘This shall not yalak (go) with you,' the same shall not yalak (go).

So he brought down the im (people) to the mayam (water); and Yahawah said to Gadaiwan, "Everyone who laps of the mayam (water) with his lashawan (tongue), like a dog laps, you shall set him by himself; likewise everyone who bows down on his knees to drink.

The number of those who lapped, putting their yad (hand) to their pah (mouth), was shalawash (three) maah (hundred) men; but all the yathar (rest) of the im (people) bowed down on their knees to drink mayam (water).

Yahawah said to Gadaiwan, "By the shalawash (three) maah (hundred) men who lapped will I yashai (save) you, and nathan (deliver) the Madayan (Midianites) into your yad (hand). Let all the other im (people) yalak (go), ayash (each) to his own place.

So the im (people) took food in their yad (hand), and their trumpets; and he sent all the men of Yasharaal (Israel) every ayash (man) to his ahal (tent), but retained the shalawash (three) maah (hundred) men: and the machanah (camp) of Madayan was beneath him in the valley.
It happened the same layal (night), that Yahawah said to him, "qawam (arise), yarad (go) down into the machanah (camp); for I have delivered it into your yad (hand).
But if you are yaraa (afraid) to yarad (go) down, yarad (go) Parah Purah your nair (servant) down to the machanah (camp):

and you shall hear what they dabar (say); and afterward your yad (hands) will be strengthened to yarad (go) down into the machanah (camp)." Then went he down Parah Purah his nair (servant) to the outermost part of the armed men who were in the machanah (camp).

The Madayan (Midianites) and the Imalaq (Amalekites) and all the children of the qadam (east) napal (lay) along in the valley like locusts for multitude; and their camels were without number, as the sand which is on the shapah (seashore) for multitude.

When Gadaiwan had bawaa (come), behold, there was a ayash (man) telling a chalawam (dream) to his rai (fellow); and he said, "Behold, I dreamed a chalawam (dream); and behold, a cake of barley lacham (bread) tumbled into the machanah (camp) of Madayan, and came to the ahal (tent), and struck it so that it napal (fell), and turned it upside down, so that the ahal (tent) napal (lay) flat.

His rai (fellow) answered, "This is nothing other than the charab (sword) of Gadaiwan the ban (son) of Yawaash, a ayash (man) of Yasharaal (Israel). Alahayam has delivered Madayan into his yad (hand), with all the machanah (army).

It was so, when Gadaiwan heard the telling of the chalawam (dream), and its interpretation, that he worshiped; and he returned into the machanah (camp) of Yasharaal (Israel), and said, "qawam (arise); for Yahawah has delivered the machanah (army) of Madayan into your yad (hand)!

He divided the shalawash (three) maah (hundred) men into shalawash (three) raash (companies), and he nathan (put) into the yad (hands) of all of them trumpets, and rayaq (empty) pitchers, with torches within the pitchers.
He said to them, "Watch me, and do likewise. Behold, when I bawaa (come) to the outermost part of the machanah (camp), it shall be that, as I do, so you shall do.
When I blow the trumpet, I and all who are with me, then blow the trumpets also on every side of all the machanah (camp), and shout, ‘For Yahawah and for Gadaiwan!'

So Gadaiwan, and the maah (hundred) men who were with him, came to the outermost part of the machanah (camp) in the raash (beginning) of the Thayakawan watch, when they had but qawam (newly) qawam (set) the shamar (watch): and they blew the trumpets, and broke in pieces the pitchers that were in their yad (hands).

The shalawash (three) raash (companies) blew the trumpets, and broke the pitchers, and held the torches in their shamaawal (left) yad (hands), and the trumpets in their yamayan (right) yad (hands) with which to blow; and they shouted, "The charab (sword) of Yahawah and of Gadaiwan!
They ayash (each) stood in his place around the machanah (camp); and all the machanah (army) ran; and they shouted, and put them to flight.

They blew the shalawash (three) maah (hundred) trumpets, and Yahawah shawam (set) every ayash (man's) charab (sword) against his rai (fellow), and against all the machanah (army); and the machanah (army) fled as far as Bayathahashatah Shittah Tzararah Zererah, as far as the shapah (border) of Abalamachawalah Meholah, by Tabath.
The men of Yasharaal (Israel) were gathered together out of Napathalay, and out of Ashar, and out of all Manashah, and pursued achar (after) Madayan.

Gadaiwan sent malaak (messengers) throughout all the har (hill) country of Aparayam, saying, "yarad (come) down qaraah (against) Madayan, and take before them the mayam (waters), as far as Bayathabarah Barah, even the Yaradan!" So all the men of Aparayam were gathered together, and took the mayam (waters) as far as Bayathabarah Barah, even the Yaradan.

They took the shanayam (two) shar (princes) of Madayan, Irab and Zaab; and they killed Irab at the tzawar (rock) of Irab, and Zaab they killed at the yaqab (winepress) of Zaab, and pursued Madayan: and they brought the raash (heads) of Irab and Zaab to Gadaiwan ibar (beyond) the Yaradan.
The men of Aparayam said to him, "mah (why) have you treated us this way, that you didn't qaraa (call) us, when you went to fight with Madayan?" They rebuked him sharply.
He said to them, "What have I now done in comparison with you? Isn't the gleaning of the grapes of Aparayam tawab (better) than the vintage of Abayaizar?

Alahayam has delivered into your yad (hand) the shar (princes) of Madayan, Irab and Zaab! What was I yakal (able) to do in comparison with you?" Then their rawach (anger) was abated toward him, when he had dabar (said) that.
Gadaiwan came to the Yaradan, and passed over, he, and the shalawash (three) maah (hundred) men who were with him, Iyap, yet pursuing.

He said to the men of Sakawath, "Please nathan (give) loaves of lacham (bread) to the im (people) who ragal (follow) me; for they are Iyap, and I am pursuing achar (after) Zabach and Tzalamanai, the malak (kings) of Madayan.
The shar (princes) of Sakawath said, "Are the kap (hands) of Zabach and Tzalamanai now in your yad (hand), that we should nathan (give) lacham (bread) to your tzabaa (army)?
Gadaiwan said, "Therefore when Yahawah has delivered Zabach and Tzalamanai into my yad (hand), then I will tear your flesh with the thorns of the madabar (wilderness) and with briers.
He went up there to Panawaal, and spoke to them in the same way; and the men of Panawaal answered him as the men of Sakawath had answered.
He spoke also to the men of Panawaal, saying, "When I shawab (turn back / repent) again in shalawam (peace), I will nathatz (break) down this magadal (tower).

Now Zabach and Tzalamanai were in Qaraqar, and their machanah (armies) with them, about chamash (fifteen) alap (thousand) men, all who were yathar (left) of all the machanah (army) of the children of the qadam (east); for there napal (fell) one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) men who drew charab (sword).
Gadaiwan went up by the darak (way) of those who lived in ahal (tents) on the qadam (east) of Nabach and Yagabahah, and struck the machanah (army); for the machanah (army) was secure.
Zabach and Tzalamanai fled; and he pursued achar (after) them; and he took the shanayam (two) malak (kings) of Madayan, Zabach and Tzalamanai, and confused all the machanah (army).
Gadaiwan the ban (son) of Yawaash returned from the battle from the ascent of Heres.
He caught a nair (young) man of the men of Sakawath, and inquired of him: and he described for him the shar (princes) of Sakawath, and its zaqan (elders), seventy-seven men.

He came to the men of Sakawath, and said, "See Zabach and Tzalamanai, concerning whom you taunted me, saying, ‘Are the kap (hands) of Zabach and Tzalamanai now in your kap (hand), that we should nathan (give) lacham (bread) to your men who are Yaip?'
He took the zaqan (elders) of the Iyar, and thorns of the madabar (wilderness) and briers, and with them he taught the men of Sakawath.
He broke down the magadal (tower) of Panawaal, and killed the men of the Iyar.
Then he said to Zabach and Tzalamanai, "What kind of men were they whom you killed at Thabawar?" They answered, "They were like you. achad (each) one resembled the children of a malak (king).
He said, "They were my ach (brothers), the ban (sons) of my am (mother). As Yahawah chay (lives), if you had saved them chayah (alive), I would not harag (kill) you.
He said to Yathar his firstborn, "qawam (get) up, and harag (kill) them!" But the youth didn't draw his charab (sword); for he was yaraa (afraid), because he was yet a youth.

Then Zabach and Tzalamanai said, "qawam (rise) and pagai (fall) on us; for as the ayash (man) is, so is his gabawarah (strength)." Gadaiwan qawam (arose), and killed Zabach and Tzalamanai, and took the crescents that were on their camels' necks.
Then the men of Yasharaal (Israel) said to Gadaiwan, "mashal (rule) over us, both you, and your ban (son), and your ban (son's) ban (son) also; for you have saved us out of the yad (hand) of Madayan.
Gadaiwan said to them, "I will not mashal (rule) over you, neither shall my ban (son) mashal (rule) over you. Yahawah shall mashal (rule) over you.

Gadaiwan said to them, "I would make a request of you, that you would nathan (give) me every ayash (man) the earrings of his spoil." (For they had golden earrings, because they were Yashamaialay (Ishmaelites).)
They answered, "We will nathan (willingly) nathan (give) them." They spread a garment, and every ayash (man) threw the earrings of his spoil into it.

The weight of the golden earrings that he requested was one alap (thousand) and shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shekels of gold, besides the crescents, and the pendants, and the purple clothing that was on the malak (kings) of Madayan, and besides the chains that were about their camels' necks.

Gadaiwan made an apawad (ephod) of it, and put it in his Iyar, even in Iparah: and all Yasharaal (Israel) played the prostitute achar (after) it there; and it became a snare to Gadaiwan, and to his bayath (house).

So Madayan was subdued panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and they lifted up their raash (heads) no more. The aratz (land) had shaqat (rest) arabaiyam (forty) Shanah in the yawam (days) of Gadaiwan.
Yarabail the ban (son) of Yawaash went and lived in his own bayath (house).
Gadaiwan had shabaiyam (seventy) ban (sons) conceived from his body; for he had many wives.
His concubine who was in Shakam, she also bore him a ban (son), and he named him Abayamalak.
Gadaiwan the ban (son) of Yawaash died in a tawab (good) shayabah (old) age, and was buried in the tomb of Yawaash his ab (father), in Iparah of the Abayahaizaray.

It happened, as soon as Gadaiwan was mawath (dead), that the children of Yasharaal (Israel) turned again, and played the prostitute achar (after) the Bail, and made Bailabarayath Berith their Alahayam.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) didn't zakar (remember) Yahawah their Alahayam, who had delivered them out of the yad (hand) of all their ayab (enemies) on every side;
neither did they show chasad (kindness) to the bayath (house) of Yarabail, Gadaiwan, according to all the goodness which he had shown to Yasharaal (Israel).

Abayamalak the ban (son) of Yarabail went to Shakam to his am (mother's) ach (brothers), and spoke with them, and with all the mashapachah (family) of the bayath (house) of his am (mother's) ab (father), saying,

"Please dabar (speak) in the ears of all the men of Shakam, ‘Is it tawab (better) for you that all the ban (sons) of Yarabail, who are shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (persons), mashal (rule) over you, or that one mashal (rule) over you?' zakar (remember) also that I am your itzam (bone) and your flesh.

His am (mother's) ach (brothers) spoke of him in the ears of all the men of Shakam all these dabar (words): and their lab (hearts) inclined to achar (follow) Abayamalak; for they said, "He is our ach (brother).

They gave him shabaiyam (seventy) pieces of kasap (silver) out of the bayath (house) of Bailabarayath Berith, with which Abayamalak hired rayaq (vain) and pachaz (light) anawash (fellows), who followed him.

He went to his ab (father's) bayath (house) at Iparah, and killed his ach (brothers) the ban (sons) of Yarabail, being shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (persons), on one aban (stone): but Yawatham the youngest ban (son) of Yarabail was yathar (left); for he hid himself.
All the men of Shakam assembled themselves asap (together), and all the bayath (house) of Malawaa, and went and made Abayamalak malak (king), by the oak of the natzab (pillar) that was in Shakam.

When they told it to Yawatham, he went and stood on the raash (top) of har (mount) Garazayam, and lifted up his qawal (voice), and cried, and said to them, "Listen to me, you men of Shakam, that Alahayam may listen to you.
The itz (trees) went halak (forth) on a time to mashach (anoint) a malak (king) over them; and they said to the olive tree, ‘malak (reign) over us.'
"But the olive tree said to them, ‘Should I chadal (leave) my fatness, with which by me they honor Alahayam and anawash (man), and halak (go) to wave back and forth over the itz (trees)?'
"The itz (trees) said to the fig tree, ‘yalak (come) and malak (reign) over us.'
"But the fig tree said to them, ‘Should I chadal (leave) my sweetness, and my tawab (good) fruit, and halak (go) to wave back and forth over the itz (trees)?'
"The itz (trees) said to the vine, ‘yalak (come) and malak (reign) over us.'
"The vine said to them, ‘Should I chadal (leave) my new thayarawash (wine), which Shamach Alahayam and anawash (man), and halak (go) to wave back and forth over the itz (trees)?'
"Then all the itz (trees) said to the Atad, ‘yalak (come) and malak (reign) over us.'

"The Atad said to the itz (trees), ‘If in truth you mashach (anoint) me malak (king) over you, then bawaa (come) and take refuge in my shade; and if not, let ash (fire) yatzaa (come) out of the Atad, and akal (devour) the cedars of Labanawan.'

"Now therefore, if you have dealt truly and righteously, in that you have made Abayamalak malak (king), and if you have dealt tawab (well) with Yarabail and his bayath (house), and have done to him according to the deserving of his yad (hands)
(for my ab (father) fought for you, and risked his napash (life), and delivered you out of the yad (hand) of Madayan:

and you have risen up against my ab (father's) bayath (house) this yawam (day), and have slain his ban (sons), shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (persons), on one aban (stone), and have made Abayamalak, the ban (son) of his female amah (servant), malak (king) over the men of Shakam, because he is your ach (brother));
if you then have dealt truly and righteously with Yarabail and with his bayath (house) this yawam (day), then Shamach in Abayamalak, and let him also Shamach in you:

but if not, let ash (fire) yatzaa (come) out from Abayamalak, and akal (devour) the men of Shakam, and the bayath (house) of Malawaa; and let ash (fire) yatzaa (come) out from the men of Shakam, and from the bayath (house) of Malawaa, and akal (devour) Abayamalak.
Yawatham ran away, and fled, and went to Baar, and lived there, for panayam (fear) of Abayamalak his ach (brother).
Abayamalak was shawar (prince) over Yasharaal (Israel) shalawash (three) Shanah.
Alahayam sent an rai (evil) rawach (spirit) between Abayamalak and the men of Shakam; and the men of Shakam dealt bagad (treacherously) with Abayamalak:

that the violence done to the shabaiyam (seventy) ban (sons) of Yarabail might bawaa (come), and that their dam (blood) might be laid on Abayamalak their ach (brother), who killed them, and on the men of Shakam, who strengthened his harag (hands) to kill his ach (brothers).
The men of Shakam shawam (set) an ambush for him on the raash (tops) of the har (mountains), and they robbed all who came along that darak (way) by them: and it was told Abayamalak.
Gail the ban (son) of Ibad came with his ach (brothers), and went over to Shakam; and the men of Shakam batach (put) their trust in him.

They went out into the shadah (field), and harvested their vineyards, and trod the grapes, and held festival, and went into the bayath (house) of their Alahayam, and ate and drank, and cursed Abayamalak.

Gail the ban (son) of Ibad said, "Who is Abayamalak, and who is Shakam, that we should ibad (serve) him? Isn't he the ban (son) of Yarabail? and Zabal his officer? ibad (serve) the men of Chamawar the ab (father) of Shakam: but why should we ibad (serve) him?
Would that this im (people) were under my yad (hand)! Then I would sawar (remove) Abayamalak." He said to Abayamalak, "Increase your tzabaa (army), and yatzaa (come) out!
When Zabal the shar (ruler) of the Iyar heard the dabar (words) of Gail the ban (son) of Ibad, his ap (anger) was kindled.
He sent malaak (messengers) to Abayamalak Tharamah, saying, "Behold, Gail the ban (son) of Ibad and his ach (brothers) have bawaa (come) to Shakam; and behold, they incite the Iyar against you.
Now therefore, go up by layal (night), you and the im (people) who are with you, and lie in wait in the shadah (field):

and it shall be, that in the baqar (morning), as soon as the shamash (sun) is up, you shall shakam (rise) early, and rush on the Iyar; and behold, when he and the im (people) who are with him yatzaa (come) out against you, then may you do to them as you shall matzaa (find) occasion.
Abayamalak rose up, and all the im (people) who were with him, by layal (night), and they laid wait against Shakam in arabai (four) raash (companies).
Gail the ban (son) of Ibad went out, and stood in the entrance of the gate of the Iyar: and Abayamalak rose up, and the im (people) who were with him, from the ambush.

When Gail saw the im (people), he said to Zabal, "Behold, im (people) are yarad (coming) down from the raash (tops) of the har (mountains)." Zabal said to him, "You raah (see) the shadow of the har (mountains) as if they were men.
Gail spoke again and said, "Behold, im (people) are yarad (coming) down by the middle of the aratz (land), and one raash (company) bawaa (comes) by the darak (way) of the oak of Meonenim.

Then Zabal said to him, "Now where is your pah (mouth), that you said, ‘Who is Abayamalak, that we should ibad (serve) him?' Isn't this the im (people) that you have despised? Please yatzaa (go) out now and fight with them.
Gail went out panayam (before) the men of Shakam, and fought with Abayamalak.
Abayamalak chased him, and he fled panayam (before) him, and many napal (fell) Chalal, even to the entrance of the gate.
Abayamalak lived at Arawamah: and Zabal drove out Gail and his ach (brothers), that they should not yashab (dwell) in Shakam.
It happened on the next macharath (day), that the im (people) went out into the shadah (field); and they told Abayamalak.

He took the im (people), and divided them into shalawash (three) raash (companies), and laid wait in the shadah (field); and he looked, and behold, the im (people) came yatzaa (forth) out of the Iyar; He rose up against them, and struck them.

Abayamalak, and the raash (companies) that were with him, rushed forward, and stood in the entrance of the gate of the Iyar: and the shanayam (two) raash (companies) rushed on all who were in the shadah (field), and struck them.
Abayamalak fought against the Iyar all that yawam (day); and he took the Iyar, and killed the im (people) who were therein: and he nathatz (beat) down the Iyar, and sowed it with Malach.
When all the men of the magadal (tower) of Shakam heard of it, they entered into the stronghold of the bayath (house) of Barayath.
