It was told Abayamalak that all the men of the magadal (tower) of Shakam were gathered together.

Abayamalak went up to har (mount) Tzalamawan, he and all the im (people) who were with him; and Abayamalak took an axe in his yad (hand), and karath (cut) down a bough from the itz (trees), and took it up, and laid it on his shoulder: and he said to the im (people) who were with him, "What you have seen me do, make haste, and do as I have done!

All the im (people) likewise ayash (each) karath (cut) down his bough, and followed Abayamalak, and shawam (put) them at the base of the stronghold, and yatzath (set) the stronghold on ash (fire) on them; so that all the anawash (people) of the magadal (tower) of Shakam died also, about a alap (thousand) men and women.
Then went Abayamalak to Thabatz, and encamped against Thabatz, and took it.
But there was a iz (strong) magadal (tower) within the Iyar, and there fled all the men and women, and all they of the Iyar, and shut themselves in, and went up to the roof of the magadal (tower).
Abayamalak came to the magadal (tower), and fought against it, and drew near to the door of the magadal (tower) to sharap (burn) it with ash (fire).
A achad (certain) ashah (woman) cast an upper millstone on Abayamalak raash (head), and broke his galagalath (skull).

Then he called hastily to the nair (young) man his armor bearer, and said to him, "Draw your charab (sword), and mawath (kill) me, that men not amar (say) of me, ‘A ashah (woman) killed him.' His nair (young) man thrust him through, and he died.
When the men of Yasharaal (Israel) saw that Abayamalak was mawath (dead), they departed every ayash (man) to his place.
Thus Alahayam requited the wickedness of Abayamalak, which he did to his ab (father), in killing his shabaiyam (seventy) ach (brothers);
and all the wickedness of the men of Shakam did Alahayam shawab (turn back / repent) on their raash (heads): and on them came the qalalah (curse) of Yawatham the ban (son) of Yarabail.

achar (after) Abayamalak there qawam (arose) to yashai (save) Yasharaal (Israel) Thawalai the ban (son) of Pawaah, the ban (son) of Dawadaw, a ayash (man) of Yashashakar; and he lived in Shamayar in the har (hill) country of Aparayam.
He judged Yasharaal (Israel) isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three) Shanah, and died, and was buried in Shamayar.
achar (after) him qawam (arose) Yaayar, the Galaiday (Gileadite); and he judged Yasharaal (Israel) isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) Shanah.

He had shalawashayam (thirty) ban (sons) who rode on shalawashayam (thirty) donkey colts, and they had shalawashayam (thirty) Iyar, which are called Havvoth Chawawathayaiyar to this yawam (day), which are in the aratz (land) of Galaid.
Yaayar died, and was buried Qamawan Kamon.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) again did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, and served the Bail, and the Ishatharawath, and the Alahayam of Aram, and the Alahayam of Tzayadawan, and the Alahayam of Mawaab, and the Alahayam of the children of Imawan, and the Alahayam of the Palashathay (Philistines); and they forsook Yahawah, and didn't ibad (serve) him.
The ap (anger) of Yahawah was kindled against Yasharaal (Israel), and he sold them into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and into the yad (hand) of the children of Imawan.

They troubled and oppressed the children of Yasharaal (Israel) that year. For eighteen Shanah, they oppressed all the children of Yasharaal (Israel) that were ibar (beyond) the Yaradan in the aratz (land) of the Amaray (Amorites), which is in Galaid.

The children of Imawan passed over the Yaradan to fight also against Yahawadah (Judah), and against Banayamayan, and against the bayath (house) of Aparayam; so that Yasharaal (Israel) was very distressed.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) cried to Yahawah, saying, "We have sinned against you, even because we have forsaken our Alahayam, and have served the Bail.

Yahawah said to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), "Didn't I save you from the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and from the Amaray (Amorites), from the children of Imawan, and from the Palashathay (Philistines)?
The Tzayadanay (Sidonians) Imalaq, and the Amalekites, and the maiwan (maonites), oppressed you; and you cried to me, and I saved you out of their yad (hand).
Yet you have forsaken me, and served other Alahayam: therefore I will yashai (save) you no more.
yalak (go) and cry to the Alahayam which you have chosen. Let them yashai (save) you in the ith (time) of your tzarah (distress)!
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) said to Yahawah, "We have sinned: do you to us whatever seems tawab (good) to you; only natzal (deliver) us, please, this yawam (day).
They sawar (put) away the foreign Alahayam from qarab (among) them, and served Yahawah; and his napash (soul) was grieved for the misery of Yasharaal (Israel).
Then the children of Imawan were gathered together, and encamped in Galaid. The children of Yasharaal (Israel) assembled themselves asap (together), and encamped Matzapah Mizpah.

The im (people), the shar (princes) of Galaid, said one to rai (another), "What ayash (man) is he who will chalal (begin) to fight against the children of Imawan? He shall be raash (head) over all the yashab (inhabitants) of Galaid.
Now Yapathach the Galaiday (Gileadite) was a gabawar (mighty) man of valor, and he was the ban (son) of a prostitute: and Galaid became the father of Yapathach.

Galaid ashah (wife) bore him ban (sons); and when his ashah (wife's) ban (sons) grew up, they drove out Yapathach, and said to him, "You shall not nachal (inherit) in our ab (father's) bayath (house); for you are the ban (son) of achar (another) ashah (woman).
Then Yapathach fled from his ach (brothers), and lived in the aratz (land) of Tawab: and there were gathered rayaq (vain) anawash (fellows) to Yapathach, and they went out with him.
It happened after a yawam (while), that the children of Imawan made war against Yasharaal (Israel).
It was so, that when the children of Imawan made war against Yasharaal (Israel), the zaqan (elders) of Galaid went to get Yapathach out of the aratz (land) of Tawab;
and they said to Yapathach, "yalak (come) and be our chief, that we may fight with the children of Imawan.

Yapathach said to the zaqan (elders) of Galaid, "Didn't you shanaa (hate) me, and drive me out of my ab (father's) bayath (house)? Why have you bawaa (come) to me now when you are in tzarar (distress)?

The zaqan (elders) of Galaid said to Yapathach, "Therefore we have turned again to you now, that you may halak (go) with us, and fight with the children of Imawan; and you shall be our raash (head) over all the yashab (inhabitants) of Galaid.

Yapathach said to the zaqan (elders) of Galaid, "If you shawab (turn back / repent) me home again to fight with the children of Imawan, and Yahawah nathan (deliver) them panayam (before) me, shall I be your raash (head)?
The zaqan (elders) of Galaid said to Yapathach, "Yahawah shall be witness between us; surely according to your dabar (word) so will we do.

Then Yapathach went with the zaqan (elders) of Galaid, and the im (people) made him raash (head) and chief over them: and Yapathach spoke all his dabar (words) panayam (before) Yahawah Matzapah Mizpah.
Yapathach sent malaak (messengers) to the malak (king) of the children of Imawan, saying, "What have you to do with me, that you have bawaa (come) to me to fight against my aratz (land)?

The malak (king) of the children of Imawan answered to the malaak (messengers) of Yapathach, "Because Yasharaal (Israel) took away my aratz (land), when he came up out of Matzarayam, from the Aranawan even to the Yabaq, and to the Yaradan: now therefore shawab (turn back / repent) that territory again peaceably.
Yapathach sent malaak (messengers) again to the malak (king) of the children of Imawan;
and he said to him, "Thus amar (says) Yapathach: Yasharaal (Israel) didn't take away the aratz (land) of Mawaab, nor the aratz (land) of the children of Imawan,
but when they came up from Matzarayam, and Yasharaal (Israel) went through the madabar (wilderness) to the Red yam (sea), and came to Qadash;

then Yasharaal (Israel) sent malaak (messengers) to the malak (king) of Adam, saying, ‘Please let me ibar (pass) through your aratz (land);' but the malak (king) of Adam didn't listen. In the same way, he sent to the malak (king) of Mawaab; but he would not: and Yasharaal (Israel) stayed in Qadash.

Then they went through the madabar (wilderness), and went around the aratz (land) of Adam, and the aratz (land) of Mawaab, and came by the east side of the aratz (land) of Mawaab, and they encamped on the other ibar (side) of the Aranawan; but they didn't bawaa (come) within the border of Mawaab, for the Aranawan was the border of Mawaab.

Yasharaal (Israel) sent malaak (messengers) to Sayachawan malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), the malak (king) of Chashabawan; and Yasharaal (Israel) said to him, ‘Please let us ibar (pass) through your aratz (land) to my place.'

But Sayachawan didn't aman (trust) Yasharaal (Israel) to ibar (pass) through his border; but Sayachawan gathered all his im (people) asap (together), and encamped in Yahatz, and fought against Yasharaal (Israel).

Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), delivered Sayachawan and all his im (people) into the yad (hand) of Yasharaal (Israel), and they struck them: so Yasharaal (Israel) possessed all the aratz (land) of the Amaray (Amorites), the yashab (inhabitants) of that aratz (country).
They possessed all the border of the Amaray (Amorites), from the Aranawan even to the Yabaq, and from the madabar (wilderness) even to the Yaradan.
So now Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), has dispossessed the Amaray (Amorites) from panayam (before) his im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), and should you yarash (possess) them?
Won't you yarash (possess) that which Kamawash your Alahayam yarash (gives) you to possess? So whoever Yahawah our Alahayam has dispossessed from panayam (before) us, them will we yarash (possess).

Now are you anything tawab (better) than Balaq the ban (son) of Tzapawar, malak (king) of Mawaab? Did he rayab (ever) rayab (strive) against Yasharaal (Israel), or did he rayab (ever) fight against them?

While Yasharaal (Israel) lived in Chashabawan and its bath (towns), and in Irawair and its bath (towns), and in all the Iyar that are along by the yad (side) of the Aranawan, shalawash (three) maah (hundred) Shanah; why didn't you natzal (recover) them within that ith (time)?

I therefore have not sinned against you, but you do me rai (wrong) to war against me. Yahawah, the shapat (judge), be shapat (judge) this yawam (day) between the children of Yasharaal (Israel) and the children of Imawan.
However the malak (king) of the children of Imawan didn't listen to the dabar (words) of Yapathach which he sent him.

Then the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah came on Yapathach, and he passed over Galaid and Manashah, and passed over Matzapah of Galaid, and from Matzapah of Galaid he passed over to the children of Imawan.
Yapathach vowed a nadar (vow) to Yahawah, and said, "If you will nathan (indeed) nathan (deliver) the children of Imawan into my yad (hand),

then it shall be, that whatever yatzaa (comes) forth from the doors of my bayath (house) to qaraah (meet) me, when I shawab (turn back / repent) in shalawam (peace) from the children of Imawan, it shall be yahawah (yahweh's), and I will ilah (offer) it up for a burnt ilah (offering).
So Yapathach passed over to the children of Imawan to fight against them; and Yahawah delivered them into his yad (hand).

He struck them from Irawair until you bawaa (come) to Manayath, even isharayam (twenty) Iyar, and to Abelcheramim, with a very gadawal (great) makah (slaughter). So the children of Imawan were subdued panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

Yapathach came Matzapah Mizpah to his bayath (house); and behold, his bath (daughter) came out to qaraah (meet) him with tambourines and with dances: and she was his only yachayad (child); besides her he had neither ban (son) nor bath (daughter).

It happened, when he saw her, that he tore his clothes, and said, "Alas, my bath (daughter)! You have brought me very low, and you are ikar (one) of those who trouble me; for I have opened my pah (mouth) to Yahawah, and I can't shawab (turn back / repent) back.

She said to him, "My ab (father), you have opened your pah (mouth) to Yahawah; do to me according to that which has proceeded out of your pah (mouth), because Yahawah has taken vengeance for you on your ayab (enemies), even on the children of Imawan.

She said to her ab (father), "Let this thing be done for me: let me rapah (alone) shanayam (two) chadash (months), that I may depart and yarad (go) down on the har (mountains), and bewail my virginity, I and my companions.
He said, "yalak (go)." He sent her shalach (away) for shanayam (two) chadash (months): and she departed, she and her companions, and mourned her virginity on the har (mountains).

It happened at the end of shanayam (two) chadash (months), that she returned to her ab (father), who did with her according to his nadar (vow) which he had vowed: and she was a virgin. It was a chaq (custom) in Yasharaal (Israel),
that the bath (daughters) of Yasharaal (Israel) went yawam (yearly) to celebrate the bath (daughter) of Yapathach the Galaiday (Gileadite) arabai (four) yawam (days) in a Shanah.

The men of Aparayam were gathered together, and passed northward; and they said to Yapathach, "Why did you ibar (pass) over to fight against the children of Imawan, and didn't qaraa (call) us to yalak (go) with you? We will sharap (burn) your bayath (house) around you with ash (fire)!
Yapathach said to them, "I and my im (people) were at maad (great) strife with the children of Imawan; and when I called you, you didn't yashai (save) me out of their yad (hand).

When I saw that you didn't yashai (save) me, I shawam (put) my napash (life) in my kap (hand), and passed over against the children of Imawan, and Yahawah delivered them into my yad (hand). Why then have you ilah (come) up to me this yawam (day), to fight against me?

Then Yapathach gathered together all the men of Galaid, and fought with Aparayam; and the men of Galaid struck Aparayam, because they said, "You are fugitives of Aparayam, you Galaid (Gileadites), in the midst of Aparayam, and in the midst of Manashah.

The Galaid (Gileadites) took the fords of the Yaradan against the Aparayam (Ephraimites). It was so, that when the fugitives of Aparayam said, "Let me ibar (go) over," the men of Galaid said to him, "Are you an Aparathay (Ephraimite)?" If he said, "No;

then they said to him, "Now amar (say) ‘Shibboleth;'" and he said "Sibboleth;" for he couldn't manage to dabar (pronounce) it kawan (right): then they siezed him, and killed him at the fords of the Yaradan. At that ith (time), arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) of Aparayam napal (fell).
Yapathach judged Yasharaal (Israel) shash (six) Shanah. Then Yapathach the Galaiday (Gileadite) died, and was buried in the Iyar of Galaid.
achar (after) him Abatzan of Bayathalacham judged Yasharaal (Israel).

He had shalawashayam (thirty) ban (sons); and shalawashayam (thirty) bath (daughters) he sent abroad, and shalawashayam (thirty) bath (daughters) he brought in from abroad for his ban (sons). He judged Yasharaal (Israel) shabai (seven) Shanah.
Abatzan died, and was buried at Bayathalacham.
achar (after) him Ayalawan the Zabawalanay (Zebulunite) judged Yasharaal (Israel); and he judged Yasharaal (Israel) ishar (ten) Shanah.
Ayalawan the Zabawalanay (Zebulunite) died, and was buried in Ayalawan in the aratz (land) of Zabawalawan.
achar (after) him Ibadawan the ban (son) of Halal the Paraithawanay judged Yasharaal (Israel).
He had arabaiyam (forty) ban (sons) and shalawashayam (thirty) ban (sons)' sons, who rode on shabaiyam (seventy) donkey colts: and he judged Yasharaal (Israel) shamanah (eight) Shanah.
Ibadawan the ban (son) of Halal the Paraithawanay died, and was buried in Paraithawan in the aratz (land) of Aparayam, in the har (hill) country of the Imalaqay (Amalekites).

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) again did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah; and Yahawah delivered them into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines) arabaiyam (forty) Shanah.
There was a achad (certain) ayash (man) of Tzaraih, of the mashapachah (family) of the Danay (Danites), whose sham (name) was Manawach; and his ashah (wife) was Iqar, and didn't yalad (bear).
The malaak (angel) of Yahawah raah (see) to the ashah (woman), and said to her, "See now, you are Iqar, and don't yalad (bear); but you shall conceive, and yalad (bear) a ban (son).
Now therefore please beware and drink no yayan (wine) nor strong drink, and don't akal (eat) any tamaa (unclean) thing:

for, behold, you shall harah (conceive), and yalad (bear) a ban (son); and no razor shall ilah (come) on his raash (head); for the nair (child) shall be a Nazirite to Alahayam from the womb: and he shall chalal (begin) to yashai (save) Yasharaal (Israel) out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

Then the ashah (woman) came and told her ayash (husband), saying, "A ayash (man) of Alahayam came to me, and his maraah (face) was like the maraah (face) of the malaak (angel) of Alahayam, very awesome; and I didn't shaal (ask) him where he was from, neither did he nagad (tell) me his sham (name):

but he said to me, ‘Behold, you shall harah (conceive), and yalad (bear) a ban (son); and now shakar (drink) no yayan (wine) nor strong drink, and akal (eat) not any tamaah (unclean) thing; for the nair (child) shall be a Nazirite to Alahayam from the womb to the yawam (day) of his mawath (death).'

Then Manawach entreated Yahawah, and said, "Oh, Adawan, please let the ayash (man) of Alahayam whom you did shalach (send) bawaa (come) again to us, and teach us what we shall do to the nair (child) who shall be yalad (born).

Alahayam listened to the qawal (voice) of Manawach; and the malaak (angel) of Alahayam came again to the ashah (woman) as she sat in the shadah (field): but Manawach, her ayash (husband), wasn't with her.
The ashah (woman) made haste, and ran, and told her ayash (husband), and said to him, "Behold, the ayash (man) has raah (see) to me, who came to me that yawam (day).
Manawach qawam (arose), and went achar (after) his ashah (wife), and came to the ayash (man), and said to him, "Are you the ayash (man) who spoke to the ashah (woman)?" He said, "I am.
Manawach said, "Now let your dabar (words) happen. What shall the nair (child's) way of life and mission be?
The malaak (angel) of Yahawah said to Manawach, "Of all that I said to the ashah (woman) let her beware.

She may not akal (eat) of anything that yatzaa (comes) of the vine, neither let her drink yayan (wine) or strong drink, nor akal (eat) any tamaah (unclean) thing; all that I tzawah (commanded) her let her shamar (observe).
Manawach said to the malaak (angel) of Yahawah, "Please, let us itzar (detain) you, that we may make a young goat ready for you.

The malaak (angel) of Yahawah said to Manawach, "Though you itzar (detain) me, I won't akal (eat) of your lacham (bread); and if you will ishah (prepare) a burnt offering, you must ishah (offer) it to Yahawah." For Manawach didn't yadai (know) that he was the malaak (angel) of Yahawah.
Manawach said to the malaak (angel) of Yahawah, "What is your sham (name), that when your dabar (words) happen, we may honor you?
The malaak (angel) of Yahawah said to him, "Why do you shaal (ask) about my sham (name), since it is Palaay?

So Manawach took the young goat with the meal manachah (offering), and offered it on the tzawar (rock) to Yahawah. Then the angel did a palaa (wonderful) thing as Manawach and his ashah (wife) looked on.

For it happened, when the lahab (flame) went up toward the sky from off the mazabach (altar), that the malaak (angel) of Yahawah ascended in the lahab (flame) of the mazabach (altar): and Manawach and his ashah (wife) looked on; and they fell on their panayam (faces) to the aratz (ground).
But the malaak (angel) of Yahawah didn't raah (see) to Manawach or to his ashah (wife) any more. Then Manawach knew that he was the malaak (angel) of Yahawah.
Manawach said to his ashah (wife), "We shall mawath (surely) mawath (die), because we have seen Alahayam.

But his ashah (wife) said to him, "If Yahawah were pleased to mawath (kill) us, he wouldn't have received a burnt ilah (offering) and a meal ilah (offering) at our yad (hand), neither would he have shown us all these things, nor would at this ith (time) have told such things as these.
The ashah (woman) bore a ban (son), and named him Shamashawan: and the nair (child) grew, and Yahawah blessed him.
The rawach (spirit) of Yahawah began to move him in Mahaneh Dan, between Tzaraih and Ashathaal.
Shamashawan went down to Thamanah, and saw a ashah (woman) in Thamanah of the bath (daughters) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

He came up, and told his ab (father) and his am (mother), and said, "I have seen a ashah (woman) in Thamanah of the bath (daughters) of the Palashathay (Philistines): now therefore get her for me as ashah (wife).

Then his ab (father) and his am (mother) said to him, "Is there never a ashah (woman) among the bath (daughters) of your ach (brothers), or among all my im (people), that you halak (go) to take a ashah (wife) of the Iral Palashathay (Philistines)?" Shamashawan said to his ab (father), "Get her for me; for she yashar (pleases) me well.

But his ab (father) and his am (mother) didn't yadai (know) that it was of Yahawah; for he sought an occasion against the Palashathay (Philistines). Now at that ith (time) the Palashathay (Philistines) had mashal (rule) over Yasharaal (Israel).
Then went Shamashawan down, and his ab (father) and his am (mother), to Thamanah, and came to the vineyards of Thamanah: and behold, a young aray (lion) roared qaraah (against) him.

The rawach (spirit) of Yahawah came mightily on him, and he tore him as he would have torn a young goat; and he had nothing in his yad (hand): but he didn't nagad (tell) his ab (father) or his am (mother) what he had done.
He went down, and talked with the ashah (woman), and she pleased Shamashawan well.

After a yawam (while) he returned to take her; and he turned sawar (aside) to raah (see) the carcass of the aray (lion): and raah (see), there was a idah (swarm) of bees in the body of the aray (lion), and honey.

He took it into his kap (hands), and went on, eating as he went; and he came to his ab (father) and am (mother), and gave to them, and they ate: but he didn't nagad (tell) them that he had taken the honey out of the body of the aray (lion).
His ab (father) went down to the ashah (woman): and Shamashawan made there a feast; for so used the young men to do.
It happened, when they saw him, that they brought shalawashayam (thirty) companions to be with him.

Shamashawan said to them, "Let me tell you a riddle now. If you can nagad (declare) it to me within the shabai (seven) yawam (days) of the feast, and matzaa (find) it out, then I will nathan (give) you shalawashayam (thirty) linen garments and shalawashayam (thirty) changes of clothing;

but if you can't nagad (declare) it to me, then you shall nathan (give) me shalawashayam (thirty) linen garments and shalawashayam (thirty) changes of clothing." They said to him, "Put forth your riddle, that we may hear it.
He said to them, "Out of the eater came yatzaa (forth) food. Out of the iz (strong) came yatzaa (forth) Mathawaq." They couldn't in shalawash (three) yawam (days) nagad (declare) the riddle.

It happened on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that they said to Shamashawan ashah (wife), "Entice your ayash (husband), that he may nagad (declare) to us the riddle, lest we sharap (burn) you and your ab (father's) bayath (house) with ash (fire). Have you called us to impoverish us? Is it not so?

Shamashawan ashah (wife) wept before him, and said, "You just shanaa (hate) me, and don't ahab (love) me. You have put forth a riddle to the children of my im (people), and haven't told it me." He said to her, "Behold, I haven't told it my ab (father) nor my am (mother), and shall I nagad (tell) you?

She wept before him the shabai (seven) yawam (days), while their feast lasted: and it happened on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that he told her, because she pressed him severely; and she told the riddle to the children of her im (people).

The men of the Iyar said to him on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) before the charas (sun) went down, "Mathawaq is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a aray (lion)?" He said to them, "If you hadn't plowed with my Igalah, you wouldn't have found out my riddle.

The rawach (spirit) of Yahawah came mightily on him, and he went down to Ashaqalawan, and struck shalawashayam (thirty) men of them, and took their spoil, and gave the changes of clothing to those who declared the riddle. His ap (anger) was kindled, and he went up to his ab (father's) bayath (house).
But Shamashawan ashah (wife) was given to his companion, whom he had used as his raih (friend).

But it happened after a yawam (while), in the time of wheat harvest, that Shamashawan visited his ashah (wife) with a young goat; and he said, "I will bawaa (go) in to my ashah (wife) into the room." But her ab (father) wouldn't allow him to bawaa (go) in.

Her ab (father) said, "I most certainly thought that you had shanaa (utterly) hated her; therefore I gave her to your companion. Isn't her younger achawath (sister) more tawab (beautiful) than she? Please take her, instead.
Shamashawan said to them, "This time I will be blameless in regard of the Palashathay (Philistines), when I rai (harm) them.
Shamashawan went and caught shalawash (three) maah (hundred) foxes, and took torches, and turned tail to tail, and shawam (put) a lapayad (torch) in the midst between every shanayam (two) tails.

When he had bair (set) the lapayad (brands) on ash (fire), he let them shalach (go) into the standing grain of the Palashathay (Philistines), and burnt up both the shocks and the standing grain, and also the olive groves.

Then the Palashathay (Philistines) said, "Who has done this?" They said, "Shamashawan, the son-in-law of the Thamanay, because he has taken his ashah (wife), and given her to his companion." The Palashathay (Philistines) came up, and burnt her and her ab (father) with ash (fire).
Shamashawan said to them, "If you behave like this, surely I will be avenged of you, and achar (after) that I will chadal (cease).
He struck them hip and thigh with a gadawal (great) makah (slaughter): and he went down and lived in the cleft of the salai (rock) of Iyatam.
Then the Palashathay (Philistines) went up, and encamped in Yahawadah (Judah), and spread themselves in Lachay.
The men of Yahawadah (Judah) said, "Why have you ilah (come) up amar (against) us?" They said, "We have ilah (come) up to bind Shamashawan, to do to him as he has done to us.

Then shalawash (three) alap (thousand) men of Yahawadah (Judah) went down to the cleft of the salai (rock) of Iyatam, and said to Shamashawan, "Don't you yadai (know) that the Palashathay (Philistines) are rulers over us? What then is this that you have done to us?" He said to them, "As they did to me, so have I done to them.

They said to him, "We have yarad (come) down to bind you, that we may nathan (deliver) you into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines)." Shamashawan said to them, "shabai (swear) to me that you will not pagai (fall) on me yourselves.

They spoke to him, saying, "No; but we will bind you fast, and nathan (deliver) you into their yad (hand); but mawath (surely) we will not mawath (kill) you." They bound him with shanayam (two) Chadash ropes, and brought him up from the salai (rock).

When he came to Lachay, the Palashathay (Philistines) shouted as they met him: and the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah came mightily on him, and the ropes that were on his zarawai (arms) became as flax that was burnt with ash (fire), and his bands dropped from off his yad (hands).
He found a Taray Lachay of a donkey, and shalach (put) forth his yad (hand), and took it, and struck a alap (thousand) men therewith.
Shamashawan said, "Lachay the jawbone of a donkey, heaps on heaps; Lachay the jawbone of a donkey I have struck a alap (thousand) men.
It happened, when he had made an kalah (end) of speaking, that he cast away the Lachay out of his yad (hand); and that place was called Ramathalachay Lehi.

He was very thirsty, and called on Yahawah, and said, "You have given this gadawal (great) thashawaih (deliverance) by the yad (hand) of your ibad (servant); and now shall I mawath (die) for thirst, and napal (fall) into the yad (hand) of the Iral?

But Alahayam split the hollow place that is Lachay Lehi, and mayam (water) came out of it. When he had drunk, his rawach (spirit) came again, and he revived: therefore its sham (name) was called Iyanahaqawaraa Hakkore, which is in Lachay, to this yawam (day).
He judged Yasharaal (Israel) in the yawam (days) of the Palashathay (Philistines) isharayam (twenty) Shanah.
Shamashawan went to Izah, and saw there a prostitute, and went in to her.

The Izathay were told, "Shamashawan is here!" They surrounded him, and laid wait for him all layal (night) in the gate of the Iyar, and were charash (quiet) all the layal (night), saying, "Wait until baqar (morning) awar (light), then we will harag (kill) him.

Shamashawan shakab (lay) until chatzay (midnight), and qawam (arose) at chatzay (midnight), and laid achaz (hold) of the doors of the gate of the Iyar, and the shanayam (two) posts, and plucked them up, bar and all, and shawam (put) them on his shoulders, and carried them up to the raash (top) of the har (mountain) that is panayam (before) Chabarawan.
It came to pass afterward, that he loved a ashah (woman) in the nachal (valley) of Shawaraq, whose sham (name) was Dalayalah.

The lords of the Palashathay (Philistines) came up to her, and said to her, "Entice him, and raah (see) in which his gadawal (great) kach (strength) lies, and by what means we may yakal (prevail) against him, that we may bind him to afflict him; and we will ayash (each) nathan (give) you eleven hundred pieces of kasap (silver).
Dalayalah said to Shamashawan, "Please nagad (tell) me where your gadawal (great) kach (strength) lies, and what you might be bound to afflict you.
Shamashawan said to her, "If they bind me with shabai (seven) Lach yathar (cords) that were never dried, then shall I become chalah (weak), and be as another adam (man).
Then the lords of the Palashathay (Philistines) brought up to her shabai (seven) Lach yathar (cords) which had not been dried, and she bound him with them.

Now she had an ambush waiting in the inner room. She said to him, "The Palashathay (Philistines) are on you, Shamashawan!" He broke the yathar (cords), as a string of tow is broken when it touches the ash (fire). So his kach (strength) was not yadai (known).
Dalayalah said to Shamashawan, "Behold, you have mocked me, and told me lies: now please nagad (tell) me with which you might be bound.
He said to her, "If they only bind me with Chadash ropes with which no malaakah (work) has been done, then shall I become chalah (weak), and be as another adam (man).

So Dalayalah took Chadash ropes, and bound him therewith, and said to him, "The Palashathay (Philistines) are on you, Shamashawan!" The ambush was waiting in the inner room. He broke them off his zarawai (arms) like a thread.

Dalayalah said to Shamashawan, "Until hanah (now), you have mocked me and told me lies. nagad (tell) me with what you might be bound." He said to her, "If you weave the shabai (seven) locks of my raash (head) with the web.

She fastened it with the pin, and said to him, "The Palashathay (Philistines) are on you, Shamashawan!" He awakened out of his shanah (sleep), and plucked nasai (away) the pin of the beam, and the web.

She said to him, "How can you amar (say), ‘I ahab (love) you,' when your lab (heart) is not with me? You have mocked me these shalawash (three) paim (times), and have not told me where your gadawal (great) kach (strength) lies.
It happened, when she pressed him yawam (daily) with her dabar (words), and urged him, that his napash (soul) was troubled to mawath (death).

He told her all his lab (heart), and said to her, "No razor has ever ilah (come) on my raash (head); for I have been a Nazirite to Alahayam from my am (mother's) womb. If I am shaved, then my kach (strength) will sawar (go) from me, and I will become chalah (weak), and be like any other adam (man).

When Dalayalah saw that he had told her all his lab (heart), she sent and called for the lords of the Palashathay (Philistines), saying, "ilah (come) up this paim (once), for he has told me all his lab (heart)." Then the lords of the Palashathay (Philistines) came up to her, and brought the kasap (money) in their yad (hand).
She made him sleep on her knees; and she called for a ayash (man), and shaved off the shabai (seven) locks of his raash (head); and she began to afflict him, and his kach (strength) went from him.

She said, "The Palashathay (Philistines) are upon you, Shamashawan!" He awoke out of his shanah (sleep), and said, "I will yatzaa (go) out as at other paim (times), and shake myself free." But he didn't yadai (know) that Yahawah had sawar (departed) from him.
The Palashathay (Philistines) laid hold on him, and put out his iyan (eyes); and they brought him down to Izah, and bound him with fetters of brass; and he tachan (ground) at the mill in the prison.
However the hair of his raash (head) began to grow again after he was shaved.

The lords of the Palashathay (Philistines) gathered them asap (together) to zabach (offer) a gadawal (great) zabach (sacrifice) to Dagawan their Alahayam, and to rejoice; for they said, "Our Alahayam has delivered Shamashawan our ayab (enemy) into our yad (hand).

When the im (people) saw him, they praised their Alahayam; for they said, "Our Alahayam has delivered our ayab (enemy) and the charab (destroyer) of our aratz (country), who has Chalal many of us, into our yad (hand).

It happened, when their lab (hearts) were tawab (merry), that they said, "qaraa (call) for Shamashawan, that he may entertain us." They called for Shamashawan out of the prison; and he performed panayam (before) them. They imad (set) him between the pillars;
and Shamashawan said to the nair (boy) who held him by the yad (hand), "Allow me to feel the pillars whereupon the bayath (house) rests, that I may shain (lean) on them.

Now the bayath (house) was malaa (full) of men and women; and all the lords of the Palashathay (Philistines) were there; and there were on the roof about shalawash (three) alap (thousand) men and women, who saw while Shamashawan performed.

Shamashawan called to Yahawah, and said, "Adawan Yahawah, zakar (remember) me, please, and chazaq (strengthen) me, please, only this paim (once), Alahayam, that I may be at paim (once) avenged of the Palashathay (Philistines) for my shanayam (two) iyan (eyes).

Shamashawan took lapath (hold) of the shanayam (two) middle pillars on which the bayath (house) rested, and leaned on them, the one with his right yamayan (hand), and the other with his shamaawal (left).

Shamashawan said, "Let me mawath (die) with the Palashathay (Philistines)!" He bowed himself with all his might; and the bayath (house) napal (fell) on the lords, and on all the im (people) who were therein. So the mawath (dead) that he killed at his mawath (death) were more than those who he killed in his chay (life).

Then his ach (brothers) and all the bayath (house) of his ab (father) came down, and took him, and brought him up, and buried him between Tzaraih and Ashathaal in the burial site of Manawach his ab (father). He judged Yasharaal (Israel) isharayam (twenty) Shanah.
There was a ayash (man) of the har (hill) country of Aparayam, whose sham (name) was Mayakayahaw.

He said to his am (mother), "The eleven hundred pieces of kasap (silver) that were taken from you, about which you uttered a alah (curse), and also spoke it in my ears, behold, the kasap (silver) is with me; I took it." His am (mother) said, "Blessed be my ban (son) of Yahawah.

He restored the eleven hundred pieces of kasap (silver) to his am (mother); and his am (mother) said, "I most certainly qadash (dedicate) the kasap (silver) to Yahawah from my yad (hand) for my ban (son), to ishah (make) an engraved pasal (image) and a molten pasal (image). Now therefore I will shawab (turn back / repent) it to you.

When he restored the kasap (money) to his am (mother), his am (mother) took two maah (hundred) pieces of kasap (silver), and gave them to the founder, who made of it an engraved pasal (image) and a molten masakah (image): and it was in the bayath (house) of Mayakayahaw.
The ayash (man) Mayakah had a bayath (house) of Alahayam, and he made an apawad (ephod), and tharapayam (teraphim), and consecrated one of his ban (sons), who became his kahan (priest).
In those yawam (days) there was no malak (king) in Yasharaal (Israel): every ayash (man) did that which was yashar (right) in his own iyan (eyes).
There was a nair (young) man out of Bayathalacham Judah, of the mashapachah (family) of Yahawadah (Judah), who was a Lawayay (Levite); and he lived there.

The ayash (man) departed out of the Iyar, out of Bayathalacham Judah, to live where he could matzaa (find) a place, and he came to the har (hill) country of Aparayam to the bayath (house) of Mayakah, as he traveled.
Mayakah said to him, "Where did you bawaa (come) from?" He said Lawayay him, "I am a Levite of Bayathalacham Judah, and I am looking for a halak (place) to live.

Mayakah said to him, "yashab (dwell) with me, and be to me a ab (father) and a kahan (priest), and I will nathan (give) you ishar (ten) pieces of kasap (silver) per yawam (year), a irak (suit) of clothing, and your food." So the Lawayay (Levite) went in.
The Lawayay (Levite) was content to yashab (dwell) with the ayash (man); and the young ayash (man) was to him as one of his ban (sons).
Mayakah consecrated the Lawayay (Levite), and the nair (young) man became his kahan (priest), and was in the bayath (house) of Mayakah.
Then Mayakah said, "Now yadai (know) I that Yahawah will do yatab (good) Lawayay me, since I have a Levite to my kahan (priest).

In those yawam (days) there was no malak (king) in Yasharaal (Israel): and in those yawam (days) the shabat (tribe) of the Danay (Danites) sought an nachalah (inheritance) to yashab (dwell) in; for to that yawam (day), their nachalah (inheritance) had not fallen to them among the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel).

The children Dan Dan sent of their mashapachah (family) chamash (five) men from their whole number, men of valor, from Tzaraih, and from Ashathaal, to spy out the aratz (land), and to search it; and they said to them, "yalak (go), explore the aratz (land)!" They came to the har (hill) country of Aparayam, to the bayath (house) of Mayakah, and lodged there.

When they were by the bayath (house) of Mayakah, they knew the qawal (voice) of the nair (young) man the Lawayay (Levite); and they turned sawar (aside) there, and said to him, "Who brought you here? What do you do in this place? What do you have here?
He said to them, "Thus and thus has Mayakah dealt with me, and he has hired me, and I am become his kahan (priest).
They said to him, "Please ask shaal (counsel) of Alahayam, that we may yadai (know) whether our darak (way) which we halak (go) shall be prosperous.
The kahan (priest) said to them, "yalak (go) in shalawam (peace). Your darak (way) in which you yalak (go) is before Yahawah.

Then the chamash (five) men departed, and came to Layash, and saw the im (people) who were qarab (therein), how they lived in security, in the way of the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), shaqat (quiet) and batach (secure); for there was none in the aratz (land), possessing authority, that might kalam (put) them to shame in anything, and they were Rachawaq from the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), and had no dealings with any adam (man).
They came to their ach (brothers) to Tzaraih and Ashathaal: and their ach (brothers) said to them, "What do you amar (say)?

They said, "qawam (arise), and let us ilah (go) up against them; for we have seen the aratz (land), and behold, it is very tawab (good). Do you stand still? Don't be slothful to yalak (go) and to bawaa (enter) in to yarash (possess) the aratz (land).

When you bawaa (go), you shall bawaa (come) to a batach (secure) im (people), and the aratz (land) is Rachab; for Alahayam has given it into your yad (hand), a place where there is no want of anything that is in the aratz (earth).
There nasai (set) forth from there of the mashapachah (family) of the Danay (Danites), out of Tzaraih and out of Ashathaal, shash (six) maah (hundred) men girt with weapons of war.

They went up, and encamped in Kiriath Qarayathayairayam, in Yahawadah (Judah): therefore they called that place Machanahadan Dan, to this yawam (day); behold, it is achar (behind) Kiriath Qarayathayairayam.
They passed there to the har (hill) country of Aparayam, and came to the bayath (house) of Mayakah.

Then the chamash (five) men who went to spy out the aratz (country) of Layash answered, and said to their ach (brothers), "Do you yadai (know) that there is in these bayath (houses) an apawad (ephod), and tharapayam (teraphim), and an engraved pasal (image), and a molten masakah (image)? Now therefore yadai (consider) what you have to do.
They turned aside there, and came to the bayath (house) of the nair (young) man the Lawayay (Levite), even to the bayath (house) of Mayakah, and asked him of his welfare.
The shash (six) maah (hundred) men girt with their weapons of war, who were of the children Dan Dan, stood by the entrance of the gate.

The chamash (five) men who went to spy out the aratz (land) went up, and came in there, and took the engraved pasal (image), and the apawad (ephod), and the tharapayam (teraphim), and the molten masakah (image): and the kahan (priest) stood by the entrance of the gate with the shash (six) maah (hundred) men girt with weapons of war.

When these went into Mayakah bayath (house), and fetched the engraved pasal (image), the apawad (ephod), and the tharapayam (teraphim), and the molten masakah (image), the kahan (priest) said to them, "What are you doing?

They said to him, "Hold your charash (peace), put your yad (hand) on your pah (mouth), and yalak (go) with us, and be to us a ab (father) and a kahan (priest). Is it tawab (better) for you to be kahan (priest) to the bayath (house) of one ayash (man), or to be kahan (priest) to a shabat (tribe) and a mashapachah (family) in Yasharaal (Israel)?
The kahan (priest's) lab (heart) was yatab (glad), and he took the apawad (ephod), and the tharapayam (teraphim), and the engraved pasal (image), and went in the qarab (midst) of the im (people).
So they turned and departed, and shawam (put) the little ones and the livestock and the kabawadah (goods) panayam (before) them.

When they were a rachaq (good) way from the bayath (house) of Mayakah, the men who were in the bayath (houses) near to Mayakah bayath (house) were gathered together, and overtook the children Dan Dan.
They cried to the children Dan Dan. They turned their panayam (faces), and said to Mayakah, "What ails you, that you come with such a company?
He said, "You have taken away my Alahayam which I made, and the kahan (priest), and have gone yalak (away), and what more do I have? How then do you amar (say) to me, ‘What ails you?'

The children Dan Dan said to him, "Don't let your qawal (voice) be heard among us, lest Mar anawash (fellows) pagai (fall) on you, and you asap (lose) your napash (life), with the lives of your bayath (household).
The children Dan Dan went their darak (way): and when Mayakah saw that they were too chazaq (strong) for him, he turned and went shawab (turn back / repent) to his bayath (house).

They took that which Mayakah had made, and the kahan (priest) whom he had, and came to Layash, to a im (people) shaqat (quiet) and batach (secure), and struck them with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); and they burnt the Iyar with ash (fire).

There was no deliverer, because it was Rachawaq from Tzayadawan, and they had no dealings with any adam (man); and it was in the valley that lies by Bayatharachawab Rehob. They built the Iyar, and lived therein.

They called the sham (name) of the Iyar Dan, after the sham (name) Dan Dan their ab (father), who was yalad (born) to Yasharaal (Israel): however the sham (name) of the Iyar was Layash at the raashawan (first).

The children Dan Dan qawam (set) up for themselves the engraved pasal (image): and Yahawanathan, the ban (son) of Garasham, the ban (son) Manashah Moses, he and his ban (sons) were kahan (priests) to the shabat (tribe) of the Danay (Danites) until the yawam (day) of the captivity of the aratz (land).
So they shawam (set) them up Mayakah engraved pasal (image) which he made, all the yawam (time) that the bayath (house) of Alahayam was in Shayalah.

It happened in those yawam (days), when there was no malak (king) in Yasharaal (Israel), that there was a ayash (certain) Lawayay (Levite) living on the farther side of the har (hill) country of Aparayam, who took to him a concubine out of Bayathalacham Judah.
His concubine played the prostitute against him, and went yalak (away) from him to her ab (father's) bayath (house) to Bayathalacham Judah, and was there the space of arabai (four) chadash (months).

Her ayash (husband) qawam (arose), and went achar (after) her, to dabar (speak) lab (kindly) to her, to shawab (turn back / repent) her again, having his nair (servant) with him, and a tzamad (couple) of donkeys: and she brought him into her ab (father's) bayath (house); and when the ab (father) of the young lady saw him, he Shamach to qaraah (meet) him.
His father-in-law, the young lady's ab (father), retained him; and he stayed with him shalawash (three) yawam (days): so they ate and drink, and lodged there.

It happened on the rabayaiy (fourth) yawam (day), that they arose shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and he rose up to depart: and the young lady's ab (father) said to his son-in-law, "Strengthen your lab (heart) with a morsel of lacham (bread), and afterward you shall go your yalak (way).

So they sat down, ate, and drank, shanayam (both) of them together: and the young lady's ab (father) said to the ayash (man), "Please be pleased to stay all lawan (night), and let your lab (heart) be yatab (merry).
The ayash (man) rose up to depart; but his father-in-law urged him, and he lodged there again.

He arose shakam (early) in the baqar (morning) on the chamayashay (fifth) yawam (day) to depart; and the young lady's ab (father) said, "Please strengthen your labab (heart) and stay until the yawam (day) declines;" and they shanayam (both) ate.

When the ayash (man) rose up to depart, he, and his concubine, and his nair (servant), his father-in-law, the young lady's ab (father), said to him, "Behold, now the yawam (day) rapah (draws) toward evening, please stay all lawan (night): behold, the yawam (day) chanah (grows) to an end, lawan (lodge) here, that your labab (heart) may be yatab (merry); and tomorrow go on your darak (way) shakam (early), that you may halak (go) ahal (home).

But the ayash (man) wouldn't stay that lawan (night), but he rose up and departed, and came over against Yabawas (the same is Yarawashalam): and there were with him a tzamad (couple) of donkeys saddled; his concubine also was with him.

When they were by Yabawas, the yawam (day) was maad (far) spent; and the nair (servant) said to his adawan (master), "Please yalak (come) and let us sawar (turn) aside into this Iyar of the Yabawasay (Jebusites), and lawan (lodge) in it.
His adawan (master) said to him, "We won't sawar (turn) aside into the Iyar of a nakaray (foreigner), that is not of the children of Yasharaal (Israel); but we will ibar (pass) over to Gabaih.
He said to his nair (servant), "yalak (come) and let us qarab (draw) near to one of these places; and we will lawan (lodge) in Gabaih, or in Ramah.
So they passed on and went their yalak (way); and the shamash (sun) went down on them near to Gabaih, which belongs to Banayamayan.

They turned sawar (aside) there, to bawaa (go) in to lawan (lodge) in Gabaih: and he went in, and sat him down in the street of the Iyar; for there was no ayash (man) who took them into his bayath (house) to lawan (lodge).

Behold, there came an zaqan (old) ayash (man) from his maishah (work) out of the shadah (field) at evening: now the ayash (man) was of the har (hill) country of Aparayam, and he lived in Gabaih; but the men of the place were Banayamayanay (Benjamites).
He lifted up his iyan (eyes), and saw the wayfaring ayash (man) in the street of the Iyar; and the zaqan (old) ayash (man) said, "Where are you going? Where did you bawaa (come) from?

He said to him, "We are passing from Bayathalacham Judah to the farther side of the har (hill) country of Aparayam. I am from there, and I went to Bayathalacham Judah. I am going to the bayath (house) of Yahawah; and there is no ayash (man) who asap (takes) me into his bayath (house).

Yet there is both straw and provender for our donkeys; and there is lacham (bread) and yayan (wine) also for me, and for your handmaid, and for the nair (young) man who is with your ibad (servants): there is no want of anything.
The zaqan (old) ayash (man) said, "shalawam (peace) be to you; raq (howsoever) let all your wants lawan (lie) on me; only don't lodge in the street.
So he brought him into his bayath (house), and gave the donkeys fodder; and they washed their feet, and ate and drink.

As they were making their lab (hearts) yatab (merry), behold, the men of the Iyar, anawash (certain) base anawash (fellows), surrounded the bayath (house), beating at the door; and they spoke to the bail (master) of the bayath (house), the zaqan (old) ayash (man), saying, "yatzaa (bring) out the ayash (man) who came into your bayath (house), that we may have sex with him!

The ayash (man), the bail (master) of the bayath (house), went out to them, and said to them, "No, my ach (brothers), please don't act so wickedly; achar (since) this ayash (man) has bawaa (come) into my bayath (house), don't do this folly.

Behold, here is my virgin bath (daughter) and his concubine. I will yatzaa (bring) them out now. Humble them, and do with them what seems tawab (good) to you; but to this ayash (man) don't do any such folly.

But the men wouldn't listen to him: so the ayash (man) laid hold of his concubine, and brought her out to them; and they had sex with her, and abused her all layal (night) until the baqar (morning): and when the shachar (day) began to ilah (dawn), they let her shalach (go).
Then came the ashah (woman) in the panah (dawning) of the baqar (day), and napal (fell) down at the door of the ayash (man's) bayath (house) where her Adawan was, until it was awar (light).

Her Adawan rose up in the baqar (morning), and opened the doors of the bayath (house), and went out to yalak (go) his darak (way); and behold, the ashah (woman) his concubine was fallen down at the door of the bayath (house), with her yad (hands) on the threshold.
He said to her, "qawam (get) up, and let us be going!" but no one answered. Then he took her up on the donkey; and the ayash (man) rose up, and went to his place.

When he had bawaa (come) into his bayath (house), he took a knife, and laid chazaq (hold) on his concubine, and divided her, limb by limb, into shanayam (twelve) pieces, and sent her throughout all the borders of Yasharaal (Israel).

It was so, that all who saw it said, "There was no such deed done nor seen from the yawam (day) that the children of Yasharaal (Israel) came up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam to this yawam (day)! shawam (consider) it, take iwatz (counsel), and dabar (speak).

Then all the children of Yasharaal (Israel) went out, and the idah (congregation) was assembled as one ayash (man), Dan Dan Baarashabai to Beersheba, with the aratz (land) of Galaid, to Yahawah Matzapah Mizpah.

The chiefs of all the im (people), even of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), presented themselves in the qahal (assembly) of the im (people) of Alahayam, arabai (four) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) footmen who drew charab (sword).
(Now the children of Banayamayan heard that the children of Yasharaal (Israel) had gone up Matzapah Mizpah.) The children of Yasharaal (Israel) said, "dabar (tell) us, how did this wickedness happen?
The Lawayay (Levite), the ayash (husband) of the ashah (woman) who was murdered, answered, "I came into Gabaih that belongs to Banayamayan, I and my concubine, to lawan (lodge).
The men of Gabaih rose against me, and surrounded the bayath (house) by layal (night). They thought to have slain me, and they forced my concubine, and she is mawath (dead).

I took my concubine, and cut her in pieces, and sent her throughout all the shadah (country) of the nachalah (inheritance) of Yasharaal (Israel); for they have committed lewdness and folly in Yasharaal (Israel).
Behold, you children of Yasharaal (Israel), all of you, give here your dabar (advice) and itzah (counsel).
All the im (people) qawam (arose) as one ayash (man), saying, "ayash (none) of us will yalak (go) to his ahal (tent), neither will any of us sawar (turn) to his bayath (house).
But now this is the thing which we will do to Gabaih: we will go up against it by lot;

and we will take ishar (ten) men of one maah (hundred) throughout all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), and one maah (hundred) of one alap (thousand), and a alap (thousand) out of rababah (ten) thousand, to get food for the im (people), that they may do, when they bawaa (come) to Gabai of Banayamayan, according to all the folly that they have worked in Yasharaal (Israel).
So all the men of Yasharaal (Israel) were gathered against the Iyar, knit together as one ayash (man).
The shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) sent men through all the shabat (tribe) of Banayamayan, saying, "What wickedness is this that is hayah (happen) among you?

Now therefore nathan (deliver) up the men, the base fellows, who are in Gabaih, that we may put them to mawath (death), and bair (put) away rai (evil) from Yasharaal (Israel)." But Banayamayan would not listen to the qawal (voice) of their ach (brothers) the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
The children of Banayamayan gathered themselves asap (together) out of the Iyar to Gabaih, to yatzaa (go) out to battle against the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

The children of Banayamayan were numbered on that yawam (day) out of the Iyar isharayam (twenty) - shash (six) alap (thousand) men who drew the charab (sword), besides the yashab (inhabitants) of Gabaih, who were numbered shabai (seven) maah (hundred) chosen men.
Among all this im (people) there were shabai (seven) maah (hundred) chosen men yad (left-handed); everyone could sling aban (stones) at a hair-breadth, and not chataa (miss).
The men of Yasharaal (Israel), besides Banayamayan, were numbered arabai (four) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) men who drew charab (sword): all these were men of war.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) qawam (arose), and went up to Bethel, and asked counsel of Alahayam; and they said, "Who shall ilah (go) up for us thachalah (first) to battle against the children of Banayamayan?" Yahawah said, "Yahawadah (Judah) thachalah (first).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) rose up in the baqar (morning), and encamped against Gabaih.
The men of Yasharaal (Israel) went out to battle against Banayamayan; and the men of Yasharaal (Israel) set the battle in array against them at Gabaih.

The children of Banayamayan came yatzaa (forth) out of Gabaih, and destroyed down to the aratz (ground) Yasharaal the Israelites on that yawam (day) isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) men.
The im (people), the men of Yasharaal (Israel), encouraged themselves, and set the battle again in array in the place where they set themselves in array the raashawan (first) yawam (day).

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) went up and wept panayam (before) Yahawah until evening; and they asked of Yahawah, saying, "Shall I again draw near to battle against the children of Banayamayan my ach (brother)?" Yahawah said, "ilah (go) up against him.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) came qarab (near) against the children of Banayamayan the shanay (second) yawam (day).

Banayamayan went yatzaa (forth) qaraah (against) them out of Gabaih the shanay (second) yawam (day), and destroyed down to the aratz (ground) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) again eighteen alap (thousand) men; all these drew the charab (sword).

Then all the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and all the im (people), went up, and came to Bethel, and wept, and sat there panayam (before) Yahawah, and fasted that yawam (day) until evening; and they offered burnt ilah (offerings) and peace ilah (offerings) panayam (before) Yahawah.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) asked of Yahawah (for the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Alahayam was there in those yawam (days),

and Payanachas, the ban (son) of Alaizar, the ban (son) of Aharawan, stood panayam (before) it in those yawam (days)), saying, "Shall I yet again yatzaa (go) out to battle against the children of Banayamayan my ach (brother), or shall I chadal (cease)?" Yahawah said, "ilah (go) up; for tomorrow I will nathan (deliver) him into your yad (hand).
Yasharaal (Israel) shawam (set) ambushes all around Gabaih.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) went up against the children of Banayamayan on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), and set themselves in array against Gabaih, as at other paim (times).

The children of Banayamayan went out qaraah (against) the im (people), and were drawn away from the Iyar; and they began to strike and Chalal of the im (people), as at other paim (times), in the masalah (highways), of which one goes up to Bethel, and the other to Gabaih, in the shadah (field), about shalawashayam (thirty) men of Yasharaal (Israel).

The children of Banayamayan said, "They are struck down panayam (before) us, as at the raashawan (first)." But the children of Yasharaal (Israel) said, "Let us flee, and draw them away from the Iyar to the masalah (highways).

All the men of Yasharaal (Israel) rose up out of their place, and set themselves in array at Bailathamar Tamar: and the ambushers of Yasharaal (Israel) broke gayach (forth) out of their place, even out of Maareh Gabai.
There came over against Gabaih ishar (ten) alap (thousand) chosen men out of all Yasharaal (Israel), and the battle was severe; but they didn't yadai (know) that rai (evil) was close on them.

Yahawah struck Banayamayan panayam (before) Yasharaal (Israel); and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) destroyed of Banayamayanay that yawam (day) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) one maah (hundred) men: all these drew the charab (sword).
So the children of Banayamayan saw that they were struck; for the men of Yasharaal (Israel) gave place to Banayamayanay, because they trusted the ambushers whom they had shawam (set) against Gabaih.
The ambushers hurried, and rushed on Gabaih; and the ambushers drew themselves along, and struck all the Iyar with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).
Now the appointed mawaid (sign) between the men of Yasharaal (Israel) and the ambushers was that they should make a great cloud of ishan (smoke) ilah (rise) up out of the Iyar.

The men of Yasharaal (Israel) turned in the battle, and Banayamayan began to strike and Chalal of the men of Yasharaal (Israel) about shalawashayam (thirty) ayash (persons); for they said, "nagap (surely) they are struck down panayam (before) us, as in the raashawan (first) battle.

But when the cloud began to arise up out of the Iyar in a pillar of ishan (smoke), the Banayamayanay (Benjamites) looked achar (behind) them; and behold, the whole of the Iyar went up in smoke to the sky.
The men of Yasharaal (Israel) turned, and the men of Banayamayan were dismayed; for they saw that rai (evil) had nagai (come) on them.

Therefore they turned their backs panayam (before) the men of Yasharaal (Israel) to the darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness); but the battle followed hard after them; and those who came out of the Iyar destroyed them in its midst.
They surrounded the Banayamayanay (Benjamites), chased them, and trod them down at their resting place, as far as over against Gabaih toward the sunrise.
There napal (fell) of Banayamayan eighteen alap (thousand) men; all these were men of valor.

They turned and fled toward the madabar (wilderness) to the salai (rock) of Ramawan: and they gleaned of them in the masalah (highways) chamash (five) alap (thousand) men, and followed hard achar (after) them to Gadaim, and struck of them two alap (thousand) men.
So that all who napal (fell) that yawam (day) of Banayamayan were isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) men who drew the charab (sword); all these were men of valor.
But shash (six) maah (hundred) men turned and fled toward the madabar (wilderness) to the salai (rock) of Ramawan, and stayed in the salai (rock) of Ramawan arabai (four) chadash (months).

The men of Yasharaal (Israel) turned again on the children of Banayamayan, and struck them with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), both the entire Iyar, and the livestock, and all that they found: moreover all the Iyar which they found they shalach (set) on ash (fire).
Now the men of Yasharaal (Israel) had sworn Matzapah Mizpah, saying, "There shall not any of us nathan (give) his bath (daughter) to Banayamayan as ashah (wife).
The im (people) came to Bethel, and sat there until evening panayam (before) Alahayam, and lifted up their qawal (voices), and wept severely.
They said, "Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), why has this happened in Yasharaal (Israel), that there should be today one shabat (tribe) lacking in Yasharaal (Israel)?
It happened on the next macharath (day) that the im (people) rose shakam (early), and built there an mazabach (altar), and offered burnt ilah (offerings) and peace ilah (offerings).

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) said, "Who is there among all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) who didn't ilah (come) up in the qahal (assembly) to Yahawah?" For they had made a gadawal (great) shabawaih (oath) concerning him who didn't ilah (come) up to Yahawah Matzapah Mizpah, saying, "He shall mawath (surely) be put to mawath (death).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) grieved for Banayamayan their ach (brother), and said, "There is one shabat (tribe) cut off from Yasharaal (Israel) this yawam (day).
How shall we provide wives for those who yathar (remain), since we have sworn by Yahawah that we will not nathan (give) them of our bath (daughters) to wives?

They said, "What one is there of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) who didn't ilah (come) up to Yahawah Matzapah Mizpah?" Behold, there came ayash (none) to the machanah (camp) Yabash Jabesh Gilead to the qahal (assembly).
For when the im (people) were numbered, behold, there were ayash (none) of the yashab (inhabitants) Yabash Jabesh Gilead there.

The idah (congregation) sent there shanayam (twelve) alap (thousand) men of the most ban (valiant), and tzawah (commanded) them, saying, "yalak (go) and strike the yashab (inhabitants) Yabash Jabesh Gilead with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), with the women and the little ones.
This is the thing that you shall do: you shall utterly charam (destroy) every zakar (male), and every ashah (woman) who has lain with a yadai (man).

They found among the yashab (inhabitants) Yabash Jabesh Gilead arabai (four) maah (hundred) young virgins, who had not yadai (known) ayash (man) by lying with him; and they brought them to the machanah (camp) to Shayalah, which is in the aratz (land) of Kanain.
The whole idah (congregation) sent and spoke to the children of Banayamayan who were in the salai (rock) of Ramawan, and proclaimed shalawam (peace) to them.
Banayamayan returned at that ith (time); and they gave them the women whom they had saved chayah (alive) of the women Yabash Jabesh Gilead: and yet so they weren't matzaa (enough) for them.
The im (people) grieved for Banayamayan, because that Yahawah had made a breach in the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Then the zaqan (elders) of the idah (congregation) said, "How shall we ishah (provide) wives for those who yathar (remain), since the women are destroyed out of Banayamayan?
They said, "There must be an yarashah (inheritance) for those who are palayatah (escaped) of Banayamayan, that a shabat (tribe) not be blotted out from Yasharaal (Israel).
However we may not nathan (give) them wives of our bath (daughters), for the children of Yasharaal (Israel) had sworn, saying, ‘Cursed is he who nathan (gives) a ashah (wife) to Banayamayan.'

They said, "Behold, there is a chag (feast) of Yahawah from yawam (year) to year in Shayalah, which is on the tzapawan (north) of Bayathaal, on the east tzapawan (side) of the masalah (highway) that goes up from Bayathaal to Shakam, and on the Nagab of Labawanah.
They tzawah (commanded) the children of Banayamayan, saying, "yalak (go) and lie in wait in the vineyards,

and raah (see), and behold, if the bath (daughters) of Shayalah yatzaa (come) out to chawal (dance) in the dances, then yatzaa (come) out of the vineyards, and each ayash (man) catch his ashah (wife) of the bath (daughters) of Shayalah, and halak (go) to the aratz (land) of Banayamayan.

It shall be, when their abawath (fathers) or their ach (brothers) bawaa (come) to rayab (complain) to us, that we will amar (say) to them, ‘chanan (grant) them graciously to us, because we didn't take for each ayash (man) his ashah (wife) in battle, neither did you nathan (give) them to them, otherwise you would now be asham (guilty).'

The children of Banayamayan did so, and took them wives, according to their number, of those who danced, whom they carried off. They went and returned to their nachalah (inheritance), built the Iyar, and lived in them.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) departed there at that ith (time), every ayash (man) to his shabat (tribe) and to his mashapachah (family), and they went out from there every ayash (man) to his nachalah (inheritance).
In those yawam (days) there was no malak (king) in Yasharaal (Israel): every ayash (man) did that which was yashar (right) in his own iyan (eyes).

It happened in the yawam (days) when the shapat (judges) judged, that there was a famine in the aratz (land). A certain ayash (man) of Bayathalacham Judah went to live in the shadah (country) of Mawaab, he, and his ashah (wife), and his shanayam (two) ban (sons).

The sham (name) of the ayash (man) was Alayamalak, and the sham (name) of his ashah (wife) Naimay, and the sham (name) of his shanayam (two) ban (sons) Machalawan and Kalayawan, Aparathay of Bayathalacham Judah. They came into the shadah (country) of Mawaab, and continued there.
Alayamalak, Naimay ayash (husband), died; and she was shaar (left), and her shanayam (two) ban (sons).
They took them wives of the women of Mawaabay; the sham (name) of the one was Irapah, and the sham (name) of the other Rawath: and they lived there about ishar (ten) Shanah.
Machalawan and Kalayawan shanayam (both) died, and the ashah (woman) was bereaved of her shanayam (two) children and of her ayash (husband).

Then she qawam (arose) with her daughters-in-law, that she might shawab (turn back / repent) from the shadah (country) of Mawaab: for she had heard in the shadah (country) of Mawaab how that Yahawah had visited his im (people) in giving them lacham (bread).

She went yatzaa (forth) out of the place where she was, and her shanayam (two) daughters-in-law with her; and they went on the darak (way) to shawab (turn back / repent) to the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah).

Naimay said to her shanayam (two) daughters-in-law, "yalak (go), shawab (turn back / repent) ashah (each) of you to her am (mother's) bayath (house): Yahawah ishah (deal) chasad (kindly) with you, as you have dealt with the mawath (dead), and with me.

Yahawah nathan (grant) you that you may matzaa (find) manawachah (rest), ashah (each) of you in the bayath (house) of her ayash (husband)." Then she kissed them, and they lifted up their qawal (voice), and wept.
They said to her, "No, but we will shawab (turn back / repent) with you to your im (people).
Naimay said, "shawab (turn back / repent) back, my bath (daughters). Why do you want to yalak (go) with me? Do I still have ban (sons) in my maih (womb), that they may be your anawash (husbands)?

shawab (turn back / repent) back, my bath (daughters), yalak (go) your way; for I am too zaqan (old) to have a ayash (husband). If I should amar (say), ‘I have hope,' if I should even have a ayash (husband) tonight, and should also yalad (bear) ban (sons);

would you then wait until they were grown? Would you then refrain from having ayash (husbands)? No, my bath (daughters), for it grieves me much for your sakes, for the yad (hand) of Yahawah has gone out against me.
They lifted up their qawal (voice), and wept again: and Irapah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth joined with her.
She said, "Behold, your sister-in-law has gone shawab (turn back / repent) to her im (people), and to her Alahayam. Follow your sister-in-law.

Ruth said, "Don't pagai (entreat) me to leave you, and to shawab (turn back / repent) from following achar (after) you, for where you yalak (go), I will yalak (go); and where you lawan (lodge), I will lawan (lodge); your im (people) shall be my im (people), and your Alahayam my Alahayam;
where you mawath (die), will I mawath (die), and there will I be buried. Yahawah do so to me, and more also, if anything but mawath (death) part you and me.
When she saw that she was steadfastly amatz (minded) to yalak (go) with her, she left off speaking to her.
So they shanayam (two) went until they came to Bayathalacham. It happened, when they had bawaa (come) to Bayathalacham, that all the Iyar was moved about them, and they asked, "Is this Naimay?
She said to them, "Don't qaraa (call) me Naimay. qaraa (call) me Maraa; for the Shaday has dealt very bitterly with me.
I went out Malaa, and Yahawah has brought me shawab (turn back / repent) again empty; why do you qaraa (call) me Naimay, since Yahawah has testified against me, and the Shaday has afflicted me?

So Naimay returned, and Mawaabay the Moabitess, her kalah (daughter-in-law), with her, who returned out of the shadah (country) of Mawaab: and they came to Bayathalacham in the thachalah (beginning) of barley harvest.
Naimay had a kinsman of her ayash (husband's), a gabawar (mighty) ayash (man) of wealth, of the mashapachah (family) of Alayamalak, and his sham (name) was Baiz.

the Mawaabay said to Naimay, "Let me now yalak (go) to the shadah (field), and glean among the ears of grain achar (after) him in whose iyan (sight) I shall matzaa (find) favor." She said to her, "yalak (go), my bath (daughter).

She went, and came and gleaned in the shadah (field) achar (after) the reapers: and she happened to qarah (come) to the chalaqah (portion) of the shadah (field) belonging to Baiz, who was of the mashapachah (family) of Alayamalak.
Behold, Baiz came from Bayathalacham, and said to the reapers, "Yahawah be with you." They answered him, "Yahawah barak (bless) you.
Then Baiz said to his nair (servant) who was natzab (set) over the reapers, "Whose young lady is this?
The nair (servant) who was natzab (set) over the reapers answered, "It is the Mawaabay (Moabite) lady who came shawab (turn back / repent) with Naimay out of the shadah (country) of Mawaab.

She said, ‘Please let me glean and asap (gather) achar (after) the reapers among the sheaves.' So she came, and has continued even from the baqar (morning) until now, except that she stayed a Mait in the bayath (house).
Then Baiz said to Rawath, "Listen, my bath (daughter). Don't yalak (go) to glean in achar (another) shadah (field), and don't ibar (go) from here, but stay here close to my maidens.

Let your iyan (eyes) be on the shadah (field) that they reap, and halak (go) achar (after) them. Haven't I tzawah (commanded) the nair (young) men not to nagai (touch) you? When you are thirsty, halak (go) to the vessels, and drink from that which the nair (young) men have drawn.

Then she napal (fell) on her panayam (face), and bowed herself to the aratz (ground), and said to him, "Why have I found favor in your iyan (sight), that you should take nakar (knowledge) of me, since I am a nakaray (foreigner)?

Baiz answered her, "It has nagad (fully) been shown me, all that you have done to your mother-in-law achar (since) the mawath (death) of your ayash (husband); and how you have left your ab (father) and your am (mother), and the aratz (land) of your birth, and have yalak (come) to a im (people) that you didn't yadai (know) thamawal (before).
May Yahawah shalam (repay) your pail (work), and a Shalam reward be given you from Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), under whose wings you have bawaa (come) to take refuge.

Then she said, "Let me matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (sight), my Adawan, because you have comforted me, and because you have spoken lab (kindly) to your handmaid, though I am not as one of your handmaidens.

At meal ith (time) Baiz said to her, "Come here, and akal (eat) of the lacham (bread), and dip your morsel in the vinegar." She sat beside the reapers, and they reached her parched grain, and she ate, and was satisfied, and yathar (left) some of it.
When she had risen up to glean, Baiz tzawah (commanded) his nair (young) men, saying, "Let her glean even among the sheaves, and don't kalam (reproach) her.
Also pull out some for her from the bundles, and leave it, and let her glean, and don't rebuke her.
So she gleaned in the shadah (field) until evening; and she beat out that which she had gleaned, and it was about an ephah of barley.
She took it up, and went into the Iyar; and her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned: and she brought out and gave to her that which she had yathar (left) after she was sufficed.

Her mother-in-law said to her, "Where have you gleaned today? Where have you worked? Blessed be he who noticed you." She showed her mother-in-law with whom she had worked, and said, "The ayash (man's) sham (name) with whom I worked today is Baiz.

Naimay said to her daughter-in-law, "Blessed be he of Yahawah, who has not left off his chasad (kindness) to the chay (living) and to the mawath (dead)." Naimay said to her, "The ayash (man) is a close relative to us, one of our gaal (near) kinsmen.
the Mawaabay said, "Yes, he said to me, ‘You shall stay close to my nair (young) men, until they have ended all my harvest.'
Naimay said Rawath her kalah (daughter-in-law), "It is tawab (good), my bath (daughter), that you yatzaa (go) out with his maidens, and that they not pagai (meet) you in any other shadah (field).
So she stayed close to the maidens of Baiz, to glean to the kalah (end) of barley harvest and of wheat harvest; and she lived with her mother-in-law.
Naimay her mother-in-law said to her, "My bath (daughter), shall I not seek manawach (rest) for you, that it may be yatab (well) with you?
Now isn't Baiz our kinsman, with whose maidens you were? Behold, he winnows barley tonight in the threshing floor.

Therefore wash yourself, anoint yourself, shawam (get) dressed, and yarad (go) down to the threshing floor, but don't yadai (make) yourself known to the ayash (man) until he has finished eating and drinking.

It shall be, when he lies down, that you shall yadai (mark) the place where he shall shakab (lie), and you shall bawaa (go) in, and galah (uncover) his feet, and shakab (lay) down; then he will nagad (tell) you what you shall do.
She said to her, "All that you amar (say) I will do.
She went down to the threshing floor, and did according to all that her mother-in-law told her.
When Baiz had eaten and drunk, and his lab (heart) was yatab (merry), he went to shakab (lie) down at the end of the heap of grain. She came softly, uncovered his feet, and laid her down.
It happened at chatzay (midnight), that the ayash (man) was startled and turned himself; and behold, a ashah (woman) shakab (lay) at his feet.
He said, "Who are you?" She answered, "I am your handmaid. Therefore spread your skirt over your handmaid; for you are a gaal (near) kinsman.

He said, "Blessed are you by Yahawah, my bath (daughter). You have shown more chasad (kindness) in the Acharawan end than at the raashawan (beginning), inasmuch as you didn't yalak (follow) young men, whether Dal or Ishayar.
Now, my bath (daughter), don't be yaraa (afraid); I will do to you all that you amar (say); for all the city of my im (people) does yadai (know) that you are a chayal (worthy) ashah (woman).
Now it is true that I am a gaal (near) kinsman; however there is a gaal (kinsman) nearer than I.

Stay this layal (night), and it shall be in the baqar (morning), that if he will gaal (perform) for you the part of a kinsman, tawab (well); let him do the gaal (kinsman's) part. But if he will not do the gaal (part) of a kinsman for you, then will I do the gaal (part) of a kinsman for you, as Yahawah chay (lives). shakab (lie) down until the baqar (morning).

She shakab (lay) at his feet until the baqar (morning). She rose up before one could nakar (discern) rai (another). For he said, "Let it not be yadai (known) that the ashah (woman) came to the threshing floor.
He said, "Bring the mantle that is on you, and achaz (hold) it." She held it; and he measured shash (six) measures of barley, and laid it on her; and he went into the Iyar.
When she came to her mother-in-law, she said, "How did it go, my bath (daughter)?" She told her all that the ayash (man) had done to her.
She said, "He gave me these shash (six) measures of barley; for he said, ‘Don't bawaa (go) empty to your mother-in-law.'

Then she said, "yashab (sit) still, my bath (daughter), until you yadai (know) how the dabar (matter) will napal (fall); for the ayash (man) will not shaqat (rest), until he has finished the thing this yawam (day).

Now Baiz went up to the gate, and sat down there. Behold, the gaal (near) kinsman of whom Baiz spoke came by; to whom he said, "ibar (come) over here, friend, and yashab (sit) down!" He turned sawar (aside), and sat down.
He took ishar (ten) men of the zaqan (elders) of the Iyar, and said, "yashab (sit) down here." They sat down.

He said to the gaal (near) kinsman, "Naimay, who has shawab (turn back / repent) back out of the shadah (country) of Mawaab, is selling the chalaqah (parcel) of shadah (land), which was our ach (brother) Alayamalak.

I thought to galah (disclose) it to you, saying, ‘qanah (buy) it before those who sit here, and before the zaqan (elders) of my im (people).' If you will gaal (redeem) it, gaal (redeem) it; but if you will not gaal (redeem) it, then nagad (tell) me, that I may yadai (know). For there is no one to gaal (redeem) it zawalah (besides) you; and I am achar (after) you." He said, "I will gaal (redeem) it.

Then Baiz said, "On the yawam (day) you qanah (buy) the shadah (field) from the yad (hand) of Naimay, you must qanah (buy) it Rawath from the Mawaabay, the ashah (wife) of the mawath (dead), to qawam (raise) up the sham (name) of the mawath (dead) on his nachalah (inheritance).
