The gaal (near) kinsman said, "I can't gaal (redeem) it for myself, lest I shachath (mar) my own nachalah (inheritance). Take my gaalah (right) of redemption for yourself; for I can't gaal (redeem) it.

Now this was the custom in former panayam (time) in Yasharaal (Israel) concerning redeeming and concerning exchanging, to qawam (confirm) all things: a ayash (man) took off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbor; and this was the way of attestation in Yasharaal (Israel).
So the gaal (near) kinsman said to Baiz, "qanah (buy) it for yourself." He took off his shoe.

Baiz said to the zaqan (elders), and to all the im (people), "You are witnesses this yawam (day), that I have bought all that was Alayamalak, and all that was Kalayawan and Machalawan, from the yad (hand) of Naimay.

Rawath the Mawaabay, the ashah (wife) of Machalawan, I have purchased to be my ashah (wife), to qawam (raise) up the sham (name) of the mawath (dead) on his nachalah (inheritance), that the sham (name) of the mawath (dead) not be karath (cut) off from among his ach (brothers), and from the gate of his place. You are witnesses this yawam (day).

All the im (people) who were in the gate, and the zaqan (elders), said, "We are witnesses. May Yahawah nathan (make) the ashah (woman) who has bawaa (come) into your bayath (house) like Rachal and like Laah, which shanayam (two) built the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); and treat you chayal (worthily) in Ephrathah, and be qaraa (famous) in Bayathalacham.
Let your bayath (house) be like the bayath (house) of Paratz, whom Thamar bore to Yahawadah (Judah), of the zarai (seed) which Yahawah shall nathan (give) you of this young nairah (woman).
So Baiz took Rawath, and she became his ashah (wife); and he went in to her, and Yahawah gave her conception, and she bore a ban (son).
The women said to Naimay, "Blessed be Yahawah, who has not left you this yawam (day) without a gaal (near) kinsman; and let his sham (name) be qaraa (famous) in Yasharaal (Israel).

He shall be to you a restorer of napash (life), and sustain you in your shayabah (old) age, for your kalah (daughter-in-law), who ahab (loves) you, who is tawab (better) to you than shabai (seven) ban (sons), has borne him.
Naimay took the yalad (child), and laid it in her bosom, and became aman (nurse) to it.
The Shakan, her neighbors, gave him a sham (name), saying, "There is a ban (son) yalad (born) to Naimay;" and they sham (named) him Iwabad. He is the ab (father) of Yashay, the ab (father) of Dawad.
Now this is the history of the thawaladah (generations) of Paratz: Paratz became the father of Chatzarawan,
and Chatzarawan became the father of Ram, and Ram became the father of Imayanadab,
and Imayanadab became the father of Nachashawan, and Nachashawan became the father of Shalamah,
and Shalamawan became the father of Baiz, and Baiz became the father of Iwabad,
and Iwabad became the father of Yashay, and Yashay became the father of Dawad.

Now there was a achad (certain) ayash (man) Ramathayamatzawapayam Ramathaim Zophim, of the har (hill) country of Aparayam, and his sham (name) was Alaqanah, the ban (son) of Yaracham, the ban (son) of Alayahaw, the ban (son) of Thachaw, the ban (son) of Tzawap, an Aparathay (Ephraimite):
and he had shanayam (two) wives; the sham (name) of the one was Chanah, and the sham (name) of other Pananah: and Pananah had children, but Chanah had no children.

This ayash (man) went up out of his Iyar from yawam (year) to year to shachah (worship) and to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) in Shayalah. The shanayam (two) ban (sons) of Ilay, Chapanay and Payanachas, kahan (priests) to Yahawah, were there.
When the yawam (day) came that Alaqanah sacrificed, he gave to Pananah his ashah (wife), and to all her ban (sons) and her bath (daughters), portions:
but to Chanah he gave a double portion; for he loved Chanah, but Yahawah had shut up her womb.
Her rival provoked her severely, to make her fret, because Yahawah had shut up her womb.
As he did so Shanah by Shanah, when she went up to the bayath (house) of Yahawah, so she provoked her; therefore she wept, and didn't akal (eat).
Alaqanah her ayash (husband) said to her, "Chanah, why do you weep? Why don't you akal (eat)? Why is your labab (heart) grieved? Am I not tawab (better) to you than ishar (ten) ban (sons)?

So Chanah rose up achar (after) they had eaten in Shayalah, and achar (after) they had drunk. Now Ilay the kahan (priest) was sitting on his kasaa (seat) by the doorpost of the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah.
She was Mar bitterness of napash (soul), and prayed to Yahawah, and wept bitterly.

She vowed a nadar (vow), and said, "Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), if you will raah (see) raah (see) on the affliction of your handmaid, and zakar (remember) me, and not forget your handmaid, but will nathan (give) to your handmaid a boy, then I will nathan (give) him to Yahawah all the yawam (days) of his chay (life), and no razor shall ilah (come) on his raash (head).
It happened, as she continued praying panayam (before) Yahawah, that Ilay Ilay her pah (mouth).
Now Chanah spoke in her lab (heart). Only her shapah (lips) moved, but her qawal (voice) was not heard. Therefore Ilay thought she had been drunken.
Ilay said to her, "How long will you be Shakar? sawar (put) away your yayan (wine) from you.

Chanah answered, "No, my Adawan, I am a ashah (woman) of a Qashah rawach (spirit). I have drunk neither yayan (wine) nor shakar (strong) drink, but I poured out my napash (soul) panayam (before) Yahawah.
Don't nathan (count) your handmaid for a balayail (wicked) woman; for I have been speaking out of the abundance of my complaint and my kais (provocation).
Then Ilay answered, "yalak (go) in shalawam (peace); and may the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) nathan (grant) your petition that you have asked of him.
She said, "Let your handmaid matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (sight)." So the ashah (woman) went her darak (way), and ate; and her facial expression wasn't sad any more.

They rose up in the baqar (morning) shakam (early), and worshiped panayam (before) Yahawah, and returned, and came to their bayath (house) to Ramah: and Alaqanah knew Chanah his ashah (wife); and Yahawah zakar (remembered) her.
It happened, when the yawam (time) had come, that Chanah conceived, and bore a ban (son); and she named him Shamawaal, saying, "Because I have asked him of Yahawah.
The ayash (man) Alaqanah, and all his bayath (house), went up to zabach (offer) to Yahawah the yawam (yearly) zabach (sacrifice), and his nadar (vow).

But Chanah didn't ilah (go) up; for she said to her ayash (husband), "Not until the nair (child) is weaned; then I will bawaa (bring) him, that he may raah (see) panayam (before) Yahawah, and stay there iwalam (forever).

Alaqanah her ayash (husband) said to her, "Do what seems tawab (good) to you. Wait until you have weaned him; only may Yahawah qawam (establish) his dabar (word)." So the ashah (woman) waited and nursed her ban (son), until she weaned him.

When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with shalawash (three) bulls, and one ephah of meal, and a bottle of yayan (wine), and brought him to yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house) in Shayalah. The nair (child) was nair (young).
They killed the bull, and brought the nair (child) to Ilay.
She said, "Oh, my Adawan, as your napash (soul) chay (lives), my Adawan, I am the ashah (woman) who stood by you here, praying to Yahawah.
For this nair (child) I prayed; and Yahawah has given me my petition which I asked of him.
Therefore also I have granted him to Yahawah. As yawam (long) as he lives he is granted to Yahawah." He worshiped Yahawah there.
Chanah prayed, and said: "My lab (heart) exults in Yahawah! My qaran (horn) is exalted in Yahawah. My pah (mouth) is enlarged over my ayab (enemies), because I Shamach in your yashawaih (salvation).
There is no one as qadawash (holy) as Yahawah, For there is no one balathay (besides) you, nor is there any tzawar (rock) like our Alahayam.
"dabar (talk) no more so Gabah Gabah. Ithaq let arrogance yatzaa (come) out of your pah (mouth), For Yahawah is a Al of daih (knowledge). By him ilayalah (actions) are weighed.
"The qashath (bows) of the gabawar (mighty) men are chath (broken). Those who stumbled are armed with chayal (strength).
Those who were Shabai have hired themselves out for lacham (bread). Those who were Raib are satisfied. Yes, the Iqar has borne shabai (seven). She who has many children languishes.
"Yahawah mawath (kills), and chayah (makes) alive. He yarad (brings) down to shaawal (sheol), and ilah (brings) up.
Yahawah yarash (makes) poor, and makes rich. He brings low, he also lifts up.

He qawam (raises) up the Dal out of the ipar (dust). He lifts up the Abayawan from the dunghill, To yashab (make) them sit with nadayab (princes), and nachal (inherit) the kasaa (throne) of kabawad (glory). For the pillars of the aratz (earth) are yahawah (yahweh's). He has shayath (set) the world on them.
He will shamar (keep) the feet of his chasayad (holy) ones, but the rashai (wicked) shall be put to damam (silence) in chashak (darkness); for no ayash (man) shall gabar (prevail) by kach (strength).

Those who rayab (strive) with Yahawah shall be broken to pieces. He will thunder against them in the sky. "Yahawah will dayan (judge) the apas (ends) of the aratz (earth). He will nathan (give) iz (strength) to his malak (king), and exalt the qaran (horn) of his mashayach (anointed).
Alaqanah went to Ramah to his bayath (house). The nair (child) served Yahawah panayam (before) Ilay the kahan (priest).
Now the ban (sons) of Ilay were base men; they didn't yadai (know) Yahawah.

The mashapat (custom) of the kahan (priests) with the im (people) was that when any ayash (man) offered zabach (sacrifice), the kahan (priest's) nair (servant) came, while the flesh was boiling, with a fork of shalawash (three) teeth in his yad (hand);
and he struck it into the pan, or kettle, or caldron, or pot; all that the fork brought up the kahan (priest) took therewith. So they did in Shayalah Yasharaal all the Israelites who came there.

Yes, before they burnt the fat, the kahan (priest's) nair (servant) came, and said to the ayash (man) who sacrificed, "nathan (give) meat to roast for the kahan (priest); for he will not accept boiled meat from you, but chay (raw).

If the ayash (man) said to him, "Let the fat be burned first, and then take as much as your napash (soul) desires;" then he would amar (say), "No, but you shall nathan (give) it to me now; and if not, I will take it by force.
The chataah (sin) of the nair (young) men was very gadawal (great) panayam (before) Yahawah; for the men despised the manachah (offering) of Yahawah.
But Shamawaal ministered panayam (before) Yahawah, being a nair (child), clothed with a linen apawad (ephod).

Moreover his am (mother) made him a qatan (little) robe, and brought it to him from yawam (year) to yawam (year), when she came up with her ayash (husband) to zabach (offer) the yawam (yearly) zabach (sacrifice).
Ilay blessed Alaqanah and his ashah (wife), and said, "Yahawah shawam (give) you zarai (seed) of this ashah (woman) for the petition which was asked of Yahawah." They went to their own home.
Yahawah visited Chanah, and she conceived, and bore shalawash (three) ban (sons) and shanayam (two) bath (daughters). The nair (child) Shamawaal grew before Yahawah.
Now Ilay was very zaqan (old); and he heard all that his ban (sons) did to all Yasharaal (Israel), and how that they shakab (lay) with the women who served at the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.
He said to them, "Why do you do such things? for I hear of your rai (evil) dealings from all this im (people).
No, my ban (sons); for it is no tawab (good) report that I hear: you make yahawah (yahweh's) im (people) disobey.

If one ayash (man) chataa (sin) against ayash (another), Alahayam shall palal (judge) him; but if a ayash (man) chataa (sin) against Yahawah, who shall entreat for him?" Notwithstanding, they didn't listen to the qawal (voice) of their ab (father), because Yahawah intended to mawath (kill) them.
The nair (child) Shamawaal grew on, and increased in favor both with Yahawah, and also with men.

A ayash (man) of Alahayam came to Ilay, and said to him, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘Did I galah (reveal) myself to the bayath (house) of your ab (father), when they were in Matzarayam in bondage to Paraih bayath (house)?

Did I choose him out of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) to be my kahan (priest), to ilah (go) up to my mazabach (altar), to qatar (burn) incense, to nashaa (wear) an apawad (ephod) panayam (before) me? Did I nathan (give) to the bayath (house) of your ab (father) all the offerings of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) made by ashah (fire)?

Why do you kick at my zabach (sacrifice) and at my zabach (offering), which I have tzawah (commanded) in my habitation, and honor your ban (sons) above me, to baraa (make) yourselves fat with the best of all the manachah (offerings) of Yasharaal (Israel) my im (people)?'

"Therefore Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), says, ‘I naam (said) amar (indeed) that your bayath (house), and the bayath (house) of your ab (father), should halak (walk) panayam (before) me iwalam (forever).' But now Yahawah says, ‘Be it far from me; for those who honor me I will honor, and those who despise me shall be lightly esteemed.

Behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), that I will cut off your zarawai (arm), and the zarawai (arm) of your ab (father's) bayath (house), that there shall not be an old zaqan (man) in your bayath (house).
You shall see the tzar (affliction) of my habitation, in all the wealth which I shall yatab (give) Yasharaal (Israel); and there shall not be an old zaqan (man) in your bayath (house) forever.

The ayash (man) of yours, whom I shall not karath (cut) off from my mazabach (altar), shall kalah (consume) your iyan (eyes), and grieve your napash (heart); and all the increase of your bayath (house) shall mawath (die) in the anawash (flower) of their age.
"‘This shall be the awath (sign) to you, that shall bawaa (come) on your shanayam (two) ban (sons), on Chapanay and Payanachas: in one yawam (day) they shall shanayam (both) mawath (die).

I will qawam (raise) me up a aman (faithful) kahan (priest), that shall do according to that which is in my labab (heart) and in my napash (mind). I will banah (build) him a aman (sure) bayath (house); and he shall halak (walk) panayam (before) my mashayach (anointed) forever.

It shall happen, that everyone who is yathar (left) in your bayath (house) shall bawaa (come) and shachah (bow) down to him for a piece of kasap (silver) and a loaf of lacham (bread), and shall amar (say), "Please put me into one of the kahanah (priests)' offices, that I may akal (eat) a morsel of lacham (bread)."'
The nair (child) Shamawaal ministered to Yahawah panayam (before) Ilay. The dabar (word) of Yahawah was Yaqar in those yawam (days); there was no frequent vision.
It happened at that yawam (time), when Ilay was laid down in his place (now his iyan (eyes) had begun to grow Kahah, so that he could not raah (see)),
and the nayar (lamp) of Alahayam hadn't yet gone out, and Shamawaal had laid down in the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, where the arawan (ark) of Alahayam was;
that Yahawah called Shamawaal; and he said, "Here I am.
He ran to Ilay, and said, "Here I am; for you called me." He said, "I didn't qaraa (call); shakab (lie) down again." He went and shakab (lay) down.
Yahawah called yet again, "Shamawaal!" Shamawaal qawam (arose) and went to Ilay, and said, "Here I am; for you called me." He answered, "I didn't qaraa (call), my ban (son); shakab (lie) down again.
Now Shamawaal didn't yet yadai (know) Yahawah, neither was the dabar (word) of Yahawah yet revealed to him.
Yahawah called Shamawaal again the shalayashay (third) time. He qawam (arose) and went to Ilay, and said, "Here I am; for you called me." Ilay perceived that Yahawah had called the nair (child).

Therefore Ilay said to Shamawaal, "yalak (go), shakab (lie) down: and it shall be, if he qaraa (calls) you, that you shall amar (say), ‘dabar (speak), Yahawah; for your ibad (servant) hears.'" So Shamawaal went and shakab (lay) down in his place.
Yahawah came, and stood, and called as at other paim (times), "Shamawaal! Shamawaal!" Then Shamawaal said, "dabar (speak); for your ibad (servant) hears.
Yahawah said to Shamawaal, "Behold, I will do a thing in Yasharaal (Israel), at which shanayam (both) the ears of everyone who hears it shall tingle.
In that yawam (day) I will qawam (perform) against Ilay all that I have spoken concerning his bayath (house), from the beginning even to the kalah (end).

For I have told him that I will shapat (judge) his bayath (house) iwalam (forever), for the iwan (iniquity) which he knew, because his ban (sons) brought a qalal (curse) on themselves, and he didn't restrain them.
Therefore I have sworn to the bayath (house) of Ilay, that the iwan (iniquity) of Ilay bayath (house) shall not be removed with zabach (sacrifice) nor zabach (offering) iwalam (forever).
Shamawaal shakab (lay) until the baqar (morning), and opened the doors of the bayath (house) of Yahawah. Shamawaal feared to show Ilay the vision.
Then Ilay called Shamawaal, and said, "Shamawaal, my ban (son)!" He said, "Here I am.
He said, "dabar (what) is the thing that he has spoken to you? Please don't hide it from me. Alahayam do so to you, and more also, if you hide anything from me of all the things that he spoke to you.
Shamawaal told him every bit, and hid nothing from him. He said, "It is Yahawah. Let him do what seems tawab (good) to him.
Shamawaal grew, and Yahawah was with him, and let none of his dabar (words) napal (fall) to the aratz (ground).
All Yasharaal (Israel) Dan Dan Baarashabai to Beersheba knew that Shamawaal was established to be a nabayaa (prophet) of Yahawah.
Yahawah raah (see) again in Shayalah; for Yahawah revealed himself to Shamawaal in Shayalah by the dabar (word) of Yahawah.

The dabar (word) of Shamawaal came to all Yasharaal (Israel). Now Yasharaal (Israel) went out qaraah (against) the Palashathay (Philistines) to battle, and encamped beside Abanahaizar: and the Palashathay (Philistines) encamped in Apaq.

The Palashathay (Philistines) put themselves in array qaraah (against) Yasharaal (Israel): and when they joined battle, Yasharaal (Israel) was struck panayam (before) the Palashathay (Philistines); and they killed of the mairakah (army) in the shadah (field) about arabai (four) alap (thousand) men.

When the im (people) had bawaa (come) into the machanah (camp), the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) said, "Why has Yahawah struck us today panayam (before) the Palashathay (Philistines)? Let us get the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah out of Shayalah to us, that it may bawaa (come) qarab (among) us, and yashai (save) us out of the kap (hand) of our ayab (enemies).

So the im (people) sent to Shayalah; and they brought from there the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), who yashab (sits) above the karawab (cherubim): and the shanayam (two) ban (sons) of Ilay, Chapanay and Payanachas, were there with the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Alahayam.
When the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah came into the machanah (camp), all Yasharaal (Israel) shouted with a gadawal (great) shout, so that the aratz (earth) rang again.

When the Palashathay (Philistines) heard the qawal (noise) of the shout, they said, "What does the qawal (noise) of this gadawal (great) shout in the machanah (camp) of the ibaray (hebrews) mean?" They understood that the arawan (ark) of Yahawah had bawaa (come) into the machanah (camp).
The Palashathay (Philistines) were yaraa (afraid), for they said, "Alahayam has bawaa (come) into the machanah (camp)." They said, "Woe to us! For there has not been such a thing before.

Woe to us! Who shall natzal (deliver) us out of the yad (hand) of these adayar (mighty) Alahayam? These are the Alahayam that struck the Matzarayam (Egyptians) with all kinds of makah (plagues) in the madabar (wilderness).
Be chazaq (strong), and behave like men, O you Palashathay (Philistines), that you not be ibad (servants) to the ibaray (hebrews), as they have been to you. Strengthen yourselves like men, and fight!

The Palashathay (Philistines) fought, and Yasharaal (Israel) was struck, and they fled every ayash (man) to his ahal (tent): and there was a very gadawal (great) makah (slaughter); for there napal (fell) of Yasharaal (Israel) shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand) footmen.
The arawan (ark) of Alahayam was taken; and the shanayam (two) ban (sons) of Ilay, Chapanay and Payanachas, were slain.
There ran a ayash (man) of Banayamayan out of the mairakah (army), and came to Shayalah the same yawam (day), with his mad (clothes) torn, and with adamah (earth) on his raash (head).

When he came, behold, Ilay was sitting on his kasaa (seat) by the road watching; for his lab (heart) Charad for the arawan (ark) of Alahayam. When the ayash (man) came into the Iyar, and told it, all the Iyar cried out.
When Ilay heard the qawal (noise) of the crying, he said, "What does the qawal (noise) of this tumult mean?" The ayash (man) hurried, and came and told Ilay.
Now Ilay was thashaiyam (ninety) - shamanah (eight) Shanah ban (old); and his iyan (eyes) were qawam (set), so that he could not raah (see).
The ayash (man) said to Ilay, "I am he who came out of the mairakah (army), and I fled today out of the mairakah (army)." He said, "How did the dabar (matter) go, my ban (son)?

He who brought the news answered, "Yasharaal (Israel) has fled panayam (before) the Palashathay (Philistines), and there has been also a gadawal (great) magapah (slaughter) among the im (people). Your shanayam (two) ban (sons) also, Chapanay and Payanachas, are mawath (dead), and the arawan (ark) of Alahayam has been captured.

It happened, when he made zakar (mention) of the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, that Eli napal (fell) from off his kasaa (seat) backward by the yad (side) of the gate; and his neck broke, and he died; for he was an zaqan (old) ayash (man), and kabad (heavy). He had judged Yasharaal (Israel) arabaiyam (forty) Shanah.

His kalah (daughter-in-law), Payanachas' ashah (wife), was with harah (child), near to be yalad (delivered). When she heard the news that the arawan (ark) of Alahayam was taken, and that her father-in-law and her ayash (husband) were mawath (dead), she bowed herself and gave yalad (birth); for her tzayar (pains) came on her.

About the ith (time) of her mawath (death) the women who stood by her said to her, "Don't be yaraa (afraid); for you have given yalad (birth) to a ban (son)." But she didn't answer, neither did she shayath (regard) it.

She named the nair (child) Ayakabawad, saying, "The kabawad (glory) has departed from Yasharaal (Israel);" because the arawan (ark) of Alahayam was taken, and because of her father-in-law and her ayash (husband).
She said, "The kabawad (glory) has departed from Yasharaal (Israel); for the arawan (ark) of Alahayam is taken.
Now the Palashathay (Philistines) had taken the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, and they brought it from Abanahaizar Ashadawad Ashdod.
The Palashathay (Philistines) took the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, and brought it into the bayath (house) of Dagawan, and set it by Dagawan.

When they of Ashadawaday arose shakam (early) on the next macharath (day), behold, Dagawan was fallen on his panayam (face) to the aratz (ground) panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah. They took Dagawan, and shawab (turn back / repent) him in his place again.

When they arose shakam (early) on the next macharath (day) baqar (morning), behold, Dagawan was fallen on his panayam (face) to the aratz (ground) panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah; and the raash (head) of Dagawan and shanayam (both) the kap (palms) of his yad (hands) were karath (cut) off on the threshold. Only Dagawan torso was intact.
Therefore neither the kahan (priests) of Dagawan, nor any who bawaa (come) into Dagawan bayath (house), tread on the threshold of Dagawan Ashadawad Ashdod, to this yawam (day).
But the yad (hand) of Yahawah was kabad (heavy) on them of Ashadawaday, and he destroyed them, and struck them with tumors, Ashadawad Ashdod and its borders.

When the men Ashadawad Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, "The arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) shall not stay with us; for his yad (hand) is severe on us, and on Dagawan our Alahayam.

They sent therefore and gathered all the lords of the Palashathay (Philistines) to them, and said, "What shall we do with the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel)?" They answered, "Let the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) be carried over to gath (gath)." They carried the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) there.

It was so, that achar (after) they had carried it sabab (about), the yad (hand) of Yahawah was against the Iyar with a very gadawal (great) mahawamah (confusion): and he struck the men of the Iyar, both qatan (small) and gadawal (great); and tumors broke out on them.

So they sent the arawan (ark) of Alahayam to Iqarawan. It happened, as the arawan (ark) of Alahayam came to Iqarawan, that the Iqarawanay cried out, saying, "They have brought sabab (about) the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) to us, to mawath (kill) us and our im (people).

They sent therefore and gathered asap (together) all the lords of the Palashathay (Philistines), and they said, "shalach (send) away the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), and let it shawab (turn back / repent) again to its own place, that it not mawath (kill) us and our im (people)." For there was a mawath (deadly) mahawamah (confusion) throughout all the Iyar; the yad (hand) of Alahayam was very kabad (heavy) there.
The men who didn't mawath (die) were struck with the tumors; and the cry of the Iyar went up to shamayam (heaven).
The arawan (ark) of Yahawah was in the shadah (country) of the Palashathay (Philistines) shabai (seven) chadash (months).
The Palashathay (Philistines) called for the kahan (priests) and the diviners, saying, "What shall we do with the arawan (ark) of Yahawah? Show us with which we shall shalach (send) it to its place.

They said, "If you shalach (send) away the arawan (ark) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), don't shalach (send) it empty; but by all means shawab (turn back / repent) him a asham (trespass) offering: then you shall be healed, and it shall be yadai (known) to you why his yad (hand) is not removed from you.

Then they said, "What shall be the asham (trespass) offering which we shall shawab (turn back / repent) to him?" They said, "chamash (five) golden tumors, and chamash (five) golden mice, for the number of the lords of the Palashathay (Philistines); for one magapah (plague) was on you all, and on your lords.

Therefore you shall ishah (make) tzalam (images) of your tumors, and tzalam (images) of your mice that shachath (mar) the aratz (land); and you shall nathan (give) kabawad (glory) to the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): perhaps he will lighten his yad (hand) from off you, and from off your Alahayam, and from off your aratz (land).

Why then do you kabad (harden) your labab (hearts), as the Matzarayam (Egyptians) and Paraih hardened their lab (hearts)? When he had worked wonderfully among them, didn't they let the people shalach (go), and they departed?

"Now therefore take and ishah (prepare) yourselves a Chadash cart, and shanayam (two) milk cows, on which there has ilah (come) no yoke; and tie the cows to the cart, and shawab (turn back / repent) their calves bayath (home) from them;

and take the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, and nathan (lay) it on the cart; and shawam (put) the jewels of gold, which you shawab (turn back / repent) him for a asham (trespass) offering, in a coffer by its side; and shalach (send) it away, that it may halak (go).

raah (see); if it goes up by the darak (way) of its own border to Bayathashamash Shemesh, then he has done us this gadawal (great) rai (evil): but if not, then we shall yadai (know) that it is not his yad (hand) that struck us; it was a chance that happened to us.
The men did so, and took shanayam (two) milk cows, and tied them to the cart, and shut up their calves at bayath (home);
and they shawam (put) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah on the cart, and the coffer with the mice of gold and the tzalam (images) of their tumors.

The cows took the yashar (straight) darak (way) by the darak (way) to Bayathashamash Shemesh; they went halak (along) the masalah (highway), lowing as they went, and didn't sawar (turn) aside to the right yamayan (hand) or to the shamaawal (left); and the lords of the Palashathay (Philistines) went achar (after) them to the border of Bayathashamash Shemesh.
They of Bayathashamash Shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley; and they lifted up their iyan (eyes), and saw the arawan (ark), and Shamach to raah (see) it.

The cart came into the shadah (field) of Yahawashawai Bayathahashamashay Beth Shemesh, and stood there, where there was a gadawal (great) aban (stone): and they split the itz (wood) of the cart, and offered up the cows for a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah.

The Lawayay (Levites) took down the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, and the coffer that was with it, in which the jewels of gold were, and shawam (put) them on the gadawal (great) aban (stone): and the men of Bayathashamash Shemesh offered burnt ilah (offerings) and sacrificed zabach (sacrifices) the same yawam (day) to Yahawah.
When the chamash (five) lords of the Palashathay (Philistines) had seen it, they returned to Iqarawan the same yawam (day).

These are the golden tumors which the Palashathay (Philistines) returned for a asham (trespass) offering to Yahawah: Ashadawad Ashdod one, for Izah one, for Ashaqalawan one, for gath (gath) one, for Iqarawan one;

and the golden mice, according to the number of all the Iyar of the Palashathay (Philistines) belonging to the chamash (five) lords, both of fortified Iyar and of country kapar (villages), even to the gadawal (great) Abal, whereon they yanach (set) down the arawan (ark) of Yahawah. That stone remains to this yawam (day) in the shadah (field) of Yahawashawai Bayathahashamashay Beth Shemesh.

He struck of the men of Bayathashamash Shemesh, because they had looked into the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, he struck of the im (people) chamashayam (fifty) alap (thousand) shabaiyam (seventy) men; and the im (people) mourned, because Yahawah had struck the anawash (people) with a gadawal (great) makah (slaughter).
The men of Bayathashamash Shemesh said, "Who is yakal (able) to imad (stand) panayam (before) Yahawah, this qadawash (holy) Alahayam? To whom shall he ilah (go) up from us?

They sent malaak (messengers) to the yashab (inhabitants) of Kiriath Qarayathayairayam, saying, "The Palashathay (Philistines) have brought shawab (turn back / repent) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah; yarad (come) down, and ilah (bring) it up to yourselves.

The men of Kiriath Qarayathayairayam came, and fetched up the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, and brought it into the bayath (house) of Abayanadab in the Gabaih, and sanctified Alaizar his ban (son) to shamar (keep) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah.

It happened, from the yawam (day) that the arawan (ark) stayed in Kiriath Qarayathayairayam, that the yawam (time) was long; for it was isharayam (twenty) Shanah: and all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) lamented achar (after) Yahawah.

Shamawaal spoke to all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "If you do shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah with all your labab (heart), then sawar (put) away the foreign Alahayam and the Ishatharawath from among you, and kawan (direct) your labab (hearts) to Yahawah, and ibad (serve) him only; and he will natzal (deliver) you out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).
Then the children of Yasharaal (Israel) removed the Bail and the Ishatharawath, and served Yahawah only.
Shamawaal said, "Gather all Yasharaal (Israel) Matzapah Mizpah, and I will palal (pray) for you to Yahawah.

They gathered together Matzapah Mizpah, and drew mayam (water), and poured it out panayam (before) Yahawah, and fasted on that yawam (day), and said there, "We have sinned against Yahawah." Shamawaal judged the children of Yasharaal (Israel) Matzapah Mizpah.

When the Palashathay (Philistines) heard that the children of Yasharaal (Israel) were gathered together Matzapah Mizpah, the lords of the Palashathay (Philistines) went up against Yasharaal (Israel). When the children of Yasharaal (Israel) heard it, they were yaraa (afraid) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) said to Shamawaal, "Don't charash (cease) to cry to Yahawah our Alahayam for us, that he will yashai (save) us out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).
Shamawaal took a suckling lamb, and offered it for a kalayal (whole) burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah: and Shamawaal cried to Yahawah for Yasharaal (Israel); and Yahawah answered him.

As Shamawaal was offering up the burnt ilah (offering), the Palashathay (Philistines) drew near to battle against Yasharaal (Israel); but Yahawah thundered with a gadawal (great) qawal (thunder) on that yawam (day) on the Palashathay (Philistines), and confused them; and they were struck down panayam (before) Yasharaal (Israel).
The men of Yasharaal (Israel) went out Matzapah Mizpah, and pursued the Palashathay (Philistines), and struck them, until they came under Bayathakar Kar.
Then Shamawaal took a aban (stone), and shawam (set) it Matzapah Mizpah and Shan, and called its sham (name) Abanahaizar, saying, "Yahawah helped us until now.

So the Palashathay (Philistines) were subdued, and they came no more within the border of Yasharaal (Israel). The yad (hand) of Yahawah was against the Palashathay (Philistines) all the yawam (days) of Shamawaal.

The Iyar which the Palashathay (Philistines) had taken from Yasharaal (Israel) were restored to Yasharaal (Israel), from Iqarawan even to gath (gath); and Yasharaal (Israel) recovered its border out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines). There was shalawam (peace) between Yasharaal (Israel) and the Amaray (Amorites).
Shamawaal judged Yasharaal (Israel) all the yawam (days) of his chay (life).
He went from Shanah to Shanah in sabab (circuit) to Bayathaal and Galagal, and Matzapah; and he judged Yasharaal (Israel) in all those places.
His thashawabah (return) was to Ramah, for there was his bayath (house); and there he judged Yasharaal (Israel): and he built there an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah.
It happened, when Shamawaal was zaqan (old), that he made his ban (sons) shapat (judges) over Yasharaal (Israel).
Now the sham (name) of his ban (firstborn) was Yawaal; and the sham (name) of his mashanah (second), Abayah: they were shapat (judges) Baarashabai Beersheba.
His ban (sons) didn't halak (walk) in his darak (ways), but turned natah (aside) achar (after) lucre, and took shachad (bribes), and perverted justice.
Then all the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) gathered themselves together, and came to Shamawaal to Ramah;

and they said to him, "Behold, you are zaqan (old), and your ban (sons) don't halak (walk) in your darak (ways): now shawam (make) us a malak (king) to shapat (judge) us like all the gawayam (nations).
But the thing displeased Shamawaal, when they said, "nathan (give) us a malak (king) to shapat (judge) us." Shamawaal prayed to Yahawah.

Yahawah said to Shamawaal, "Listen to the qawal (voice) of the im (people) in all that they amar (tell) you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me, that I should not be malak (king) over them.

According to all the maishah (works) which they have done since the yawam (day) that I brought them up out of Matzarayam even to this yawam (day), in that they have forsaken me, and served other Alahayam, so do they also to you.
Now therefore listen to their qawal (voice): however you shall iwad (protest) iwad (solemnly) to them, and shall show them the way of the malak (king) who shall malak (reign) over them.
Shamawaal told all the dabar (words) of Yahawah to the im (people) who asked of him a malak (king).

He said, "This will be the way of the malak (king) who shall malak (reign) over you: he will take your ban (sons), and shawam (appoint) them to him, for his chariots, and to be his horsemen; and they shall run panayam (before) his chariots;

and he will shawam (appoint) them to him for shar (captains) of alap (thousands), and shar (captains) of chamashayam (fifties); and he will assign some to charash (plow) his charayash (ground), and to reap his harvest, and to ishah (make) his instruments of war, and the instruments of his chariots.
He will take your bath (daughters) to be perfumers, and to be cooks, and to be bakers.
He will take your shadah (fields), and your vineyards, and your olive groves, even their tawab (best), and nathan (give) them to his ibad (servants).
He will take the ishar (tenth) of your zarai (seed), and of your vineyards, and nathan (give) to his officers, and to his ibad (servants).
He will take your male ibad (servants), and your female ibad (servants), and your tawab (best) young men, and your donkeys, and ishah (put) them to his malaakah (work).
He will take the ishar (tenth) of your flocks: and you shall be his ibad (servants).
You shall cry out in that yawam (day) panayam (because) of your malak (king) whom you shall have chosen you; and Yahawah will not answer you in that yawam (day).
But the im (people) refused to listen to the qawal (voice) of Shamawaal; and they said, "No; but we will have a malak (king) over us,
that we also may be like all the gawayam (nations), and that our malak (king) may shapat (judge) us, and yatzaa (go) out panayam (before) us, and fight our battles.
Shamawaal heard all the dabar (words) of the im (people), and he rehearsed them in the ears of Yahawah.
Yahawah said to Shamawaal, "Listen to their qawal (voice), and malak (make) them a malak (king)." Shamawaal said to the men of Yasharaal (Israel), "Every anawash (man) yalak (go) to his Iyar.

Now there was a ayash (man) of Banayamayan, whose sham (name) was Qayash, the ban (son) of Abayaal, the ban (son) of Zeror, the ban (son) Bakawarath Becorath, the ban (son) of Apayach, the son of a Banayamayanay (Benjamite), a gabawar (mighty) ayash (man) of valor.

He had a ban (son), whose sham (name) was Shaawal, an impressive young bachawar (man); and there was not among the children of Yasharaal (Israel) a tawab (better) ayash (person) than he. From his shoulders and upward he was Gabah than any of the im (people).
The donkeys of Qayash, Shaawal ab (father), were lost. Qayash said to Shaawal his ban (son), "Take now one of the nair (servants) with you, and qawam (arise), yalak (go) seek the donkeys.

He passed ibar (through) the har (hill) country of Aparayam, and passed ibar (through) the aratz (land) Shalashah Shalishah, but they didn't matzaa (find) them: then they passed ibar (through) the aratz (land) Shailayam Shaalim, and there they weren't there: and he passed ibar (through) the aratz (land) of the Banayamayanay (Benjamites), but they didn't matzaa (find) them.

When they had bawaa (come) to the aratz (land) of Tzawap, Shaawal said to his nair (servant) who was with him, "yalak (come), and let us shawab (turn back / repent), lest my ab (father) stop caring about the donkeys, and be anxious for us.

He said to him, "See now, there is in this Iyar a ayash (man) of Alahayam, and he is a ayash (man) who is held in honor. All that he dabar (says) bawaa (comes) bawaa (surely) to pass. Now let us yalak (go) there. Perhaps he can nagad (tell) us concerning our darak (journey) whereon we halak (go).

Then Shaawal said to his nair (servant), "But, behold, if we yalak (go), what shall we bawaa (bring) the ayash (man)? For the lacham (bread) is spent in our vessels, and there is not a present to bawaa (bring) to the ayash (man) of Alahayam. What do we have?

The nair (servant) answered Shaawal again, and said, "Behold, I have in my yad (hand) the rabai (fourth) part of a shekel of kasap (silver). I will nathan (give) that to the ayash (man) of Alahayam, to nagad (tell) us our darak (way).

(In earlier times in Yasharaal (Israel), when a ayash (man) went to inquire of Alahayam, thus he said, "yalak (come), and let us yalak (go) to the seer;" for he who is yawam (now) called a nabayaa (prophet) was panayam (before) called a Seer.)
Then Shaawal dabar (said) to his nair (servant), "tawab (well) said. yalak (come), let us yalak (go)." So they went to the Iyar where the ayash (man) of Alahayam was.
As they went up the ascent to the Iyar, they found young maidens yatzaa (going) out to shaab (draw) mayam (water), and said to them, "Is the seer here?

They answered them, and said, "He is. Behold, he is panayam (before) you. Hurry now, for he has bawaa (come) today into the Iyar; for the people have a zabach (sacrifice) today in the bamah (high) place.

As soon as you have bawaa (come) into the Iyar, you shall Kan matzaa (find) him, before he goes up to the bamah (high) place to akal (eat); for the im (people) will not akal (eat) until he bawaa (come), because he blesses the zabach (sacrifice). Afterwards those who are invited akal (eat). Now therefore ilah (go) up; for at this yawam (time) you shall matzaa (find) him.
They went up to the Iyar. As they came within the Iyar, behold, Shamawaal came out toward them, to ilah (go) up to the bamah (high) place.
Now Yahawah had revealed to Shamawaal a yawam (day) panayam (before) Shaawal came, saying,

"Tomorrow about this ith (time) I will shalach (send) you a ayash (man) out of the aratz (land) of Banayamayan, and you shall mashach (anoint) him to be nagayad (prince) over my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel); and he shall yashai (save) my im (people) out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines): for I have looked on my im (people), because their cry has bawaa (come) to me.
When Shamawaal saw Shaawal, Yahawah said to him, "Behold, the ayash (man) of whom I spoke to you! this same shall have authority over my im (people).
Then Shaawal drew near to Shamawaal in the gate, and said, "Please nagad (tell) me where the seer's bayath (house) is.

Shamawaal answered Shaawal, and said, "I am the seer. ilah (go) up panayam (before) me to the bamah (high) place, for you shall akal (eat) with me today. In the baqar (morning) I will let you shalach (go), and will nagad (tell) you all that is in your labab (heart).

As for your donkeys who were lost shalawash (three) yawam (days) ago, don't shawam (set) your lab (mind) on them; for they are found. For whom is all that is desirable in Yasharaal (Israel)? Is it not for you, and for all your ab (father's) bayath (house)?

Shaawal answered, "Am I not a Banayamayanay (Benjamite), of the smallest of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel)? And my mashapachah (family) the Tzaiyar of all the mashapachah (families) of the shabat (tribe) of Banayamayan? Why then do you dabar (speak) to me like this?

Shamawaal took Shaawal and his nair (servant), and brought them into the guest room, and made them sit in the best place among those who were invited, who were about shalawashayam (thirty) ayash (persons).
Shamawaal said to the cook, "nathan (bring) the portion which I gave you, of which I said to you, ‘shawam (set) it aside.'

The cook took up the thigh, and that which was on it, and shawam (set) it panayam (before) Shaawal. Samuel said, "Behold, that which has been reserved! shawam (set) it panayam (before) yourself and akal (eat); because for the mawaid (appointed) time has it been kept for you, for I said, ‘I have invited the im (people).'" So Shaawal ate with Shamawaal that yawam (day).
When they had yarad (come) down from the bamah (high) place into the Iyar, he talked with Shaawal on the housetop.

They arose shakam (early): and it happened about the ilah (spring) of the shachar (day), that Shamawaal called to Shaawal on the housetop, saying, "qawam (get) up, that I may shalach (send) you away." Shaawal qawam (arose), and they went out shanayam (both) of them, he and Shamawaal, abroad.

As they were yarad (going) down at the end of the Iyar, Shamawaal said to Shaawal, "amar (tell) the nair (servant) ibar (pass) on panayam (before) us" (and he passed on), "but imad (stand) still first, that I may cause you to hear the dabar (word) of Alahayam.

Then Shamawaal took the vial of shaman (oil), and poured it on his raash (head), and kissed him, and said, "Isn't it that Yahawah has mashach (anointed) you to be nagayad (prince) over his nachalah (inheritance)?

When you have departed from me today, then you shall matzaa (find) shanayam (two) men by Rachal tomb, in the border of Banayamayan at Tzalatzach; and they will amar (tell) you, ‘The donkeys which you went to seek have been found; and behold, your ab (father) has stopped caring about the donkeys, and is anxious for you, saying, "What shall I do for my ban (son)?"'

"Then you shall go on forward from there, and you shall bawaa (come) to the oak of Thabawar; and shalawash (three) men shall matzaa (meet) you there going up to Alahayam to Bayathaal, one carrying shalawash (three) young goats, and another carrying shalawash (three) loaves of lacham (bread), and another carrying a bottle of yayan (wine):
and they will greet you, and nathan (give) you shanayam (two) loaves of lacham (bread), which you shall receive of their yad (hand).

"achar (after) that you shall bawaa (come) to the Gabaih of Alahayam, where is the garrison of the Palashathay (Philistines): and it shall happen, when you have bawaa (come) there to the Iyar, that you shall pagai (meet) a band of nabayaa (prophets) yarad (coming) down from the bamah (high) place with a psaltery, and a tambourine, and a pipe, and a harp, panayam (before) them; and they will be nabaa (prophesying):
and the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah will tzalach (come) mightily on you, and you shall nabaa (prophesy) with them, and shall be turned into achar (another) ayash (man).
Let it be, when these awath (signs) have bawaa (come) to you, that you do as matzaa (occasion) shall serve you; for Alahayam is with you.

"You shall yarad (go) down panayam (before) me to Galagal; and behold, I will yarad (come) down to you, to ilah (offer) burnt ilah (offerings), and to sacrifice zabach (sacrifices) of peace ilah (offerings): you shall wait shabai (seven) yawam (days), until I bawaa (come) to you, and show you what you shall do.
It was so, that when he had turned his back to yalak (go) from Shamawaal, Alahayam gave him achar (another) lab (heart): and all those awath (signs) happened that yawam (day).
When they came there to the Gabaih, behold, a band of nabayaa (prophets) met him; and the rawach (spirit) of Alahayam came mightily on him, and he prophesied among them.

It happened, when all who knew him before saw that, behold, he prophesied with the nabayaa (prophets), then the im (people) said one to rai (another), "What is this that has come to the ban (son) of Qayash? Is Shaawal also among the nabayaa (prophets)?
One of the same place answered, "Who is their ab (father)?" Therefore it became a proverb, "Is Shaawal also among the nabayaa (prophets)?
When he had made an kalah (end) of nabaa (prophesying), he came to the bamah (high) place.
Shaawal dawad (uncle) said to him and to his nair (servant), "Where did you halak (go)?" He said, "To seek the donkeys. When we saw that they were not found, we came to Shamawaal.
Shaawal dawad (uncle) said, "Please nagad (tell) me what Shamawaal said to you.

Shaawal said to his dawad (uncle), "He told us nagad (plainly) that the donkeys were found." But dabar (concerning) the matter of the malawakah (kingdom), of which Shamawaal spoke, he didn't nagad (tell) him.
Shamawaal called the im (people) together to Yahawah Matzapah Mizpah;

and he said to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘I brought up Yasharaal (Israel) out of Matzarayam, and I delivered you out of the yad (hand) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and out of the yad (hand) of all the mamalakah (kingdoms) that oppressed you:'

but you have this yawam (day) rejected your Alahayam, who himself yashai (saves) you out of all your rai (calamities) and your distresses; and you have said to him, ‘No! shawam (set) a malak (king) over us.' Now therefore present yourselves panayam (before) Yahawah by your shabat (tribes), and by your alap (thousands).
So Shamawaal brought all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) qarab (near), and the shabat (tribe) of Banayamayan was taken.

He brought the shabat (tribe) of Banayamayan qarab (near) by their mashapachah (families); and the mashapachah (family) Mataray the Matrites was taken; and Shaawal the ban (son) of Qayash was taken: but when they sought him, he could not be found.
Therefore they asked of Yahawah further, "Is there yet a ayash (man) to bawaa (come) here?" Yahawah answered, "Behold, he has hidden himself among the baggage.
They ran and fetched him there; and when he stood among the im (people), he was higher than any of the im (people) from his shoulders and upward.

Shamawaal said to all the im (people), "You raah (see) him whom Yahawah has chosen, that there is none like him among all the im (people)?" All the im (people) shouted, and said, "Let the malak (king) chayah (live)!

Then Shamawaal told the im (people) the regulations of the malawakah (kingdom), and wrote it in a book, and laid it up panayam (before) Yahawah. Shamawaal sent all the im (people) shalach (away), every ayash (man) to his bayath (house).
Shaawal also went to his bayath (house) to Gabaih; and there went with him the chayal (army), whose lab (hearts) Alahayam had touched.
But certain worthless fellows said, "How shall this man yashai (save) us?" They despised him, and brought him no manachah (present). But he held his charash (peace).

Then Nachash the Imawanay (Ammonite) came up, and encamped Yabash Jabesh Gilead: and all the men Yabash Jabesh said to Nachash, "karath (make) a barayath (covenant) with us, and we will ibad (serve) you.

Nachash the Imawanay (Ammonite) said to them, "On this condition I will karath (make) it with you, that all your yamayan (right) iyan (eyes) be put out; and I will shawam (lay) it for a reproach on all Yasharaal (Israel).

The zaqan (elders) Yabash Jabesh said to him, "Give us shabai (seven) yawam (days), that we may shalach (send) malaak (messengers) to all the borders of Yasharaal (Israel); and then, if there is no one to yashai (save) us, we will yatzaa (come) out to you.
Then the malaak (messengers) came to Gabaih of Shaawal, and spoke these dabar (words) in the ears of the im (people): and all the im (people) lifted up their qawal (voice), and wept.
Behold, Shaawal came following the oxen out of the shadah (field); and Shaawal said, "What ails the im (people) that they weep?" They told him the dabar (words) of the men Yabash Jabesh.
The rawach (spirit) of Alahayam came mightily on Shaawal when he heard those dabar (words), and his ap (anger) was kindled maad (greatly).

He took a tzamad (yoke) of oxen, and cut them in pieces, and sent them throughout all the borders of Yasharaal (Israel) by the yad (hand) of malaak (messengers), saying, "Whoever doesn't yatzaa (come) forth achar (after) Shaawal and achar (after) Shamawaal, so shall it be done to his oxen." The pachad (dread) of Yahawah napal (fell) on the im (people), and they came out as one ayash (man).
He numbered them in Bazaq; and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) were shalawash (three) maah (hundred) alap (thousand), and the men of Yahawadah (Judah) shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand).

They said to the malaak (messengers) who came, "Thus you shall amar (tell) the men Yabash Jabesh Gilead, ‘Tomorrow, by the time the shamash (sun) is hot, you shall have thashawaih (deliverance).'" The malaak (messengers) came and told the men Yabash Jabesh; and they were Shamach.
Therefore the men Yabash Jabesh said, "Tomorrow we will yatzaa (come) out to you, and you shall do with us all that seems tawab (good) to you.

It was so on the next macharath (day), that Shaawal shawam (put) the im (people) in shalawash (three) raash (companies); and they came into the midst of the machanah (camp) in the baqar (morning) watch, and struck the Imawan (Ammonites) until the heat of the yawam (day): and it happened, that those who remained were scattered, so that no shanayam (two) of them were shaar (left) together.
The im (people) said to Shamawaal, "Who is he who said, ‘Shall Shaawal malak (reign) over us?' nathan (bring) those men, that we may put them to mawath (death)!
Shaawal said, "There shall not a ayash (man) be put to mawath (death) this yawam (day); for today Yahawah has worked thashawaih (deliverance) in Yasharaal (Israel).
Then Shamawaal said to the im (people), "yalak (come), and let us yalak (go) to Galagal, and renew the malawakah (kingdom) there.

All the im (people) went to Galagal; and there they made Shaawal malak (king) panayam (before) Yahawah in Galagal; and there they offered zabach (sacrifices) of shalam (peace) offerings panayam (before) Yahawah; and there Shaawal and all the men of Yasharaal (Israel) Shamach maad (greatly).
Shamawaal said to all Yasharaal (Israel), "Behold, I have listened to your qawal (voice) in all that you said to me, and have made a malak (king) over you.

Now, behold, the malak (king) halak (walks) panayam (before) you; and I am zaqan (old) and gray-headed; and behold, my ban (sons) are with you: and I have walked panayam (before) you from my youth to this yawam (day).

Here I am. Witness against me before Yahawah, and before his mashayach (anointed). Whose ox have I taken? Whose donkey have I taken? Whom have I defrauded? Whom have I oppressed? Of whose yad (hand) have I taken a kapar (ransom) to ilam (blind) my iyan (eyes) therewith? I will shawab (turn back / repent) it to you.
They said, "You have not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither have you taken anything of any ayash (man's) yad (hand).
He said to them, "Yahawah is witness against you, and his mashayach (anointed) is witness this yawam (day), that you have not found anything in my yad (hand)." They said, "He is witness.
Shamawaal said to the im (people), "It is Yahawah who appointed Mashah and Aharawan, and that brought your abawath (fathers) up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
Now therefore stand still, that I may shapat (plead) with you panayam (before) Yahawah concerning all the tzadaqah (righteous) acts of Yahawah, which he did to you and to your abawath (fathers).

"When Yaiqab had bawaa (come) into Matzarayam, and your abawath (fathers) cried to Yahawah, then Yahawah sent Mashah and Aharawan, who brought your abawath (fathers) out of Matzarayam, and made them to yashab (dwell) in this place.

"But they forgot Yahawah their Alahayam; and he sold them into the yad (hand) of Sayasaraa, shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army) of Chatzawar, and into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Mawaab; and they fought against them.

They cried to Yahawah, and said, ‘We have sinned, because we have forsaken Yahawah, and have served the Bail and the Ishatharawath: but now natzal (deliver) us out of the yad (hand) of our ayab (enemies), and we will ibad (serve) you.'
Yahawah sent Yarabail, and Badan, and Yapathach, and Shamawaal, and delivered you out of the yad (hand) of your ayab (enemies) on every side; and you lived in safety.

"When you saw that Nachash the malak (king) of the children of Imawan came amar (against) you, you said to me, ‘No, but a malak (king) shall malak (reign) over us;' when Yahawah your Alahayam was your malak (king).
Now therefore see the malak (king) whom you have chosen, and whom you have asked for: and behold, Yahawah has nathan (set) a malak (king) over you.

If you will yaraa (fear) Yahawah, and ibad (serve) him, and listen to his qawal (voice), and not rebel against the commandment of Yahawah, then both you and also the malak (king) who malak (reigns) over you are followers of Yahawah your Alahayam.
But if you will not listen to the qawal (voice) of Yahawah, but rebel against the commandment of Yahawah, then will the yad (hand) of Yahawah be against you, as it was against your abawath (fathers).
"Now therefore stand still and raah (see) this gadawal (great) thing, which Yahawah will do before your iyan (eyes).

Isn't it wheat harvest today? I will qaraa (call) to Yahawah, that he may nathan (send) qawal (thunder) and rain; and you shall yadai (know) and raah (see) that your wickedness is rab (great), which you have done in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, in asking for a malak (king).
So Shamawaal called to Yahawah; and Yahawah sent qawal (thunder) and rain that yawam (day): and all the im (people) maad (greatly) feared Yahawah and Shamawaal.

All the im (people) said to Shamawaal, "palal (pray) for your ibad (servants) to Yahawah your Alahayam, that we not mawath (die); for we have added to all our chataah (sins) this rai (evil), to shaal (ask) us a malak (king).

Shamawaal said to the im (people), "Don't be yaraa (afraid). You have ishah (indeed) done all this rai (evil); yet don't sawar (turn) aside from following Yahawah, but ibad (serve) Yahawah with all your labab (heart).
Don't sawar (turn) aside to go achar (after) thahaw (vain) things which can't yail (profit) nor natzal (deliver), for they are thahaw (vain).
For Yahawah will not forsake his im (people) for his gadawal (great) sham (name's) sake, because it has pleased Yahawah to ishah (make) you a im (people) to himself.
Moreover as for me, far be it from me that I should chataa (sin) against Yahawah in ceasing to palal (pray) for you: but I will instruct you in the tawab (good) and the yashar (right) darak (way).
Only yaraa (fear) Yahawah, and ibad (serve) him in truth with all your labab (heart); for raah (see) how great things he has done for you.
But if you shall still do wickedly, you shall be consumed, both you and your malak (king).
Shaawal reigned a year; and when he had reigned shanayam (two) Shanah over Yasharaal (Israel),

Shaawal chose for himself shalawash (three) alap (thousand) men of Yasharaal (Israel), of which two alap (thousand) were with Shaawal in Makamas and in the har (mount) of Bayathaal, and one alap (thousand) were with Yawanathan in Gabaih of Banayamayan: and the yathar (rest) of the im (people) he sent every ayash (man) to his ahal (tent).

Yawanathan struck the garrison of the Palashathay (Philistines) that was in Gabai: and the Palashathay (Philistines) heard of it. Shaawal blew the trumpet throughout all the aratz (land), saying, "Let the ibaray (hebrews) hear!

All Yasharaal (Israel) heard that Shaawal had struck the garrison of the Palashathay (Philistines), and also that Yasharaal (Israel) was had in baash (abomination) with the Palashathay (Philistines). The im (people) were gathered together achar (after) Shaawal to Galagal.

The Palashathay (Philistines) assembled themselves asap (together) to fight with Yasharaal (Israel), shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand) chariots, and shash (six) alap (thousand) horsemen, and im (people) as the sand which is on the seashore in multitude: and they came up, and encamped in Makamas, eastward of Bayathaawan Aven.

When the men of Yasharaal (Israel) saw that they were in a tzarar (strait) (for the im (people) were distressed), then the im (people) hid themselves in caves, and in thickets, and in salai (rocks), and in coverts, and in bawar (pits).
Now some of the ibaray (hebrews) had gone over the Yaradan to the aratz (land) of Gad and Galaid; but as for Shaawal, he was yet in Galagal, and all the im (people) followed him trembling.
He stayed shabai (seven) yawam (days), according to the mawaid (time) set by Shamawaal: but Shamawaal didn't bawaa (come) to Galagal; and the im (people) were scattered from him.
Shaawal said, "Bring here the burnt ilah (offering) to me, and the shalam (peace) offerings." He offered the burnt ilah (offering).
It came to kalah (pass) that as soon as he had made an end of offering the burnt offering, behold, Shamawaal came; and Shaawal went out to qaraah (meet) him, that he might greet him.

Shamawaal said, "What have you done?" Shaawal said, "Because I saw that the im (people) were scattered from me, and that you didn't bawaa (come) within the yawam (days) mawaid (appointed), and that the Palashathay (Philistines) assembled themselves asap (together) at Makamas;

therefore I said, ‘Now the Palashathay (Philistines) will yarad (come) down on me to Galagal, and I haven't entreated the favor of Yahawah.' I forced myself therefore, and offered the burnt ilah (offering).

Shamawaal said to Shaawal, "You have done foolishly. You have not kept the matzawah (commandment) of Yahawah your Alahayam, which he tzawah (commanded) you; for now Yahawah would have established your mamalakah (kingdom) on Yasharaal (Israel) iwalam (forever).

But now your mamalakah (kingdom) shall not qawam (continue). Yahawah has sought for himself a ayash (man) after his own labab (heart), and Yahawah has appointed him to be nagayad (prince) over his im (people), because you have not kept that which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) you.
Shamawaal qawam (arose), and went from Galagal to Gabaih of Banayamayan. Shaawal numbered the im (people) who were matzaa (present) with him, about shash (six) maah (hundred) men.
Shaawal, and Yawanathan his ban (son), and the im (people) who were matzaa (present) with them, stayed in Gabai of Banayamayan: but the Palashathay (Philistines) encamped in Makamas.

The shachath (spoilers) came out of the machanah (camp) of the Palashathay (Philistines) in shalawash (three) raash (companies): one raash (company) turned to the darak (way) that leads to Iparah, to the aratz (land) of Shawail;

and another raash (company) turned the darak (way) to Bayathachawarawan Horon; and another raash (company) turned the darak (way) of the border that shaqap (looks) down on the Gayaa of Tzabaiyam toward the madabar (wilderness).
Now there was no smith found throughout all the aratz (land) of Yasharaal (Israel); for the Palashathay (Philistines) said, "Lest the ibaray (hebrews) ishah (make) them charab (swords) or spears;
Yasharaal all the Israelites went down to the Palashathay (Philistines), to sharpen every ayash (man) his plowshare, mattock, axe, and sickle;
yet they had a file for the mattocks, and for the plowshares, and for the shalawash (forks), and for the axes, and to natzab (set) the goads.

So it came to pass in the yawam (day) of battle, that there was neither charab (sword) nor spear found in the yad (hand) of any of the im (people) who were with Shaawal and Yawanathan: but with Shaawal and with Yawanathan his ban (son) was there found.
The garrison of the Palashathay (Philistines) went out to the pass of Makamas.

Now it fell on a yawam (day), that Yawanathan the ban (son) of Shaawal said to the nair (young) man who bore his armor, "yalak (come), and let us ibar (go) over to the Palashathay (Philistines)' garrison, that is on the other ibar (side)." But he didn't nagad (tell) his ab (father).
Shaawal stayed in the uttermost part of Gabaih under the pomegranate tree which is in Magarawan: and the im (people) who were with him were about shash (six) maah (hundred) men;

and Achayah, the ban (son) of Achayatawab, Ayakabawad ach (brother), the ban (son) of Payanachas, the ban (son) of Ilay, the kahan (priest) of Yahawah in Shayalah, wearing an apawad (ephod). The im (people) didn't yadai (know) that Yawanathan was gone.

Between the passes, by which Yawanathan sought to ibar (go) over to the Palashathay (Philistines)' garrison, there was a rocky crag on the one ibar (side), and a rocky crag on the other ibar (side): and the sham (name) of the one was Bawatzatz, and the sham (name) of the other Sanah.
The one crag rose up on the tzapawan (north) in front of Makamas, and the other on the Nagab in front of Gabai.

Yahawanathan said to the nair (young) man who bore his armor, "yalak (come), and let us ibar (go) over to the garrison of these Iral. It may be that Yahawah will ishah (work) for us; for there is no restraint on Yahawah to yashai (save) by many or by Mait.
His armor bearer said to him, "Do all that is in your labab (heart). natah (turn) and, behold, I am with you according to your labab (heart).
Then Yahawanathan said, "Behold, we will ibar (pass) over to the men, and we will galah (reveal) ourselves to them.
If they amar (say) thus to us, ‘damam (wait) until we nagai (come) to you!' then we will imad (stand) still in our place, and will not ilah (go) up to them.
But if they amar (say) this, ‘ilah (come) up to us!' then we will ilah (go) up; for Yahawah has delivered them into our yad (hand). This shall be the awath (sign) to us.

shanayam (both) of them revealed themselves to the garrison of the Palashathay (Philistines): and the Palashathay (Philistines) said, "Behold, the ibaray (hebrews) are coming out of the holes where they had hidden themselves!

The men of the matzabah (garrison) answered Yawanathan and his armor bearer, and said, "ilah (come) up to us, and we will show you something!" Yawanathan said to his armor bearer, "ilah (come) up achar (after) me; for Yahawah has delivered them into the yad (hand) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Yawanathan climbed up on his yad (hands) and on his feet, and his armor bearer achar (after) him: and they napal (fell) panayam (before) Yawanathan; and his armor bearer killed them achar (after) him.
That raashawan (first) makah (slaughter), which Yawanathan and his armor bearer made, was about isharayam (twenty) men, within as it were chatzay (half) a furrow's length in an acre of shadah (land).

There was a charadah (trembling) in the machanah (camp), in the shadah (field), and among all the im (people); the garrison, and the shachath (spoilers), they also trembled; and the aratz (earth) quaked: so there was an alahayam (exceeding) great charadah (trembling).
The watchmen of Shaawal in Gabaih of Banayamayan looked; and behold, the multitude melted away, and scattered.
Then Shaawal said to the im (people) who were with him, "paqad (count) now, and raah (see) who is missing from us." When they had counted, behold, Yawanathan and his armor bearer were not there.
Shaawal said to Achayah, "Bring the arawan (ark) of Alahayam here." For the arawan (ark) of Alahayam was with the children of Yasharaal (Israel) at that yawam (time).

It happened, while Shaawal talked to the kahan (priest), that the tumult that was in the machanah (camp) of the Palashathay (Philistines) went on and increased: and Shaawal said to the kahan (priest), "asap (withdraw) your yad (hand)!

Shaawal and all the im (people) who were with him were gathered together, and came to the battle: and behold, every ayash (man's) charab (sword) was against his rai (fellow): a very gadawal (great) mahawamah (confusion).

Now the ibaray (hebrews) who were with the Palashathay (Philistines) as before, and who went up with them into the machanah (camp), from all around, Yasharaal they also turned to be with the Israelites who were with Shaawal and Yawanathan.

Likewise all the men of Yasharaal (Israel) who had hidden themselves in the har (hill) country of Aparayam, when they heard that the Palashathay (Philistines) fled, even they also followed hard achar (after) them in the battle.
So Yahawah saved Yasharaal (Israel) that yawam (day): and the battle passed over by Bayathaawan Aven.

The men of Yasharaal (Israel) were distressed that yawam (day); for Shaawal had adjured the im (people), saying, "Cursed is the ayash (man) who akal (eats) any lacham (food) until it is evening, and I am avenged of my ayab (enemies)." So none of the im (people) tasted lacham (food).
All the people came into the Yair; and there was honey on the shadah (ground).
When the im (people) had bawaa (come) to the Yair, behold, the honey dropped: but no nashag (man) put his yad (hand) to his pah (mouth); for the im (people) feared the shabawaih (oath).

But Yawanathan didn't hear when his ab (father) commanded the im (people) with the shabai (oath): therefore he shalach (put) forth the end of the matah (rod) who was in his yad (hand), and dipped it in the honeycomb, and shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) to his pah (mouth); and his iyan (eyes) were enlightened.

Then one of the im (people) answered, and said, "Your ab (father) directly commanded the im (people) with an shabai (oath), saying, ‘Cursed is the ayash (man) who akal (eats) lacham (food) this yawam (day).'" The im (people) were faint.
Then Yawanathan said, "My ab (father) has troubled the aratz (land). Please raah (see) how my iyan (eyes) have been enlightened, because I tasted a Mait of this honey.

How much more, if perhaps the im (people) had eaten akal (freely) today of the spoil of their ayab (enemies) which they found? For now has there been no great makah (slaughter) among the Palashathay (Philistines).
They struck of the Palashathay (Philistines) that yawam (day) from Makamas to Ayalawan. The im (people) were very faint;
and the im (people) flew on the spoil, and took sheep, and cattle, and calves, and killed them on the aratz (ground); and the im (people) ate them with the dam (blood).

Then they told Shaawal, saying, "Behold, the im (people) are sinning against Yahawah, in that they akal (eat) meat with the dam (blood)." He said, "You have dealt bagad (treacherously). Roll a large aban (stone) to me this yawam (day)!

Shaawal said, "Disperse yourselves among the im (people), and amar (tell) them, ‘Bring me here every ayash (man) his ox, and every ayash (man) his sheep, and kill them here, and akal (eat); and don't chataa (sin) against Yahawah in eating meat with the dam (blood).'" All the im (people) brought every ayash (man) his ox with him that layal (night), and killed them there.
Shaawal built an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah. This was the chalal (first) mazabach (altar) that he built to Yahawah.

Shaawal said, "Let us yarad (go) down achar (after) the Palashathay (Philistines) by layal (night), and take spoil among them until the baqar (morning) awar (light), and let us not shaar (leave) a ayash (man) of them." They said, "Do whatever seems tawab (good) to you." Then the kahan (priest) said, "Let us qarab (draw) near here to Alahayam.

Shaawal asked counsel of Alahayam, "Shall I yarad (go) down achar (after) the Palashathay (Philistines)? Will you nathan (deliver) them into the yad (hand) of Yasharaal (Israel)?" But he didn't answer him that yawam (day).
Shaawal said, "Draw near here, all you chiefs of the im (people); and yadai (know) and raah (see) in which this chataah (sin) has been this yawam (day).

For, as Yahawah chay (lives), who yashai (saves) Yasharaal (Israel), though it is in Yawanathan my ban (son), he shall mawath (surely) mawath (die)." But there was not a man among all the im (people) who answered him.

Then he said to all Yasharaal (Israel), "You be on one ibar (side), and I and Yawanathan my ban (son) will be on the other ibar (side)." The im (people) said to Shaawal, "Do what seems tawab (good) to you.
Therefore Shaawal said to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), "Show the right." Yawanathan and Shaawal were chosen; but the im (people) escaped.
Shaawal said, "napal (cast) lots between me and Yawanathan my ban (son)." Yawanathan was selected.

Then Shaawal said to Yawanathan, "nagad (tell) me what you have done!" Yawanathan told him, and said, "I certainly did taste a Mait honey with the end of the matah (rod) that was in my yad (hand); and behold, I must mawath (die).
Shaawal said, "Alahayam do so and more also; for you shall mawath (surely) mawath (die), Yawanathan.

The im (people) said to Shaawal, "Shall Yawanathan mawath (die), who has worked this gadawal (great) yashawaih (salvation) in Yasharaal (Israel)? Far from it! As Yahawah chay (lives), there shall not shairah (one) hair of his raash (head) napal (fall) to the aratz (ground); for he has worked with Alahayam this yawam (day)!" So the im (people) rescued Yawanathan, that he didn't mawath (die).
Then Shaawal went up from following the Palashathay (Philistines); and the Palashathay (Philistines) went to their own place.

Now when Shaawal had taken the malawakah (kingdom) over Yasharaal (Israel), he fought against all his ayab (enemies) on every side, against Mawaab, and against the children of Imawan, and against Adam, and against the malak (kings) of Tzawabaa, and against the Palashathay (Philistines): and wherever he turned himself, he defeated them.
He did chayal (valiantly), and struck the Imalaq (Amalekites), and delivered Yasharaal (Israel) out of the yad (hands) of those who despoiled them.

Now the ban (sons) of Shaawal were Yawanathan, and Yashaway, and Malakayashawai; and the sham (names) of his shanayam (two) bath (daughters) were these: the sham (name) of the firstborn Marab, and the sham (name) of the younger Mayakal:

and the sham (name) of Shaawal ashah (wife) was Achayanaim the bath (daughter) of Achayamaitz. The sham (name) of the shar (captain) of his tzabaa (army) was Abanar the ban (son) of Nar, Shaawal dawad (uncle).
Qayash was the ab (father) of Shaawal; and Nar the ab (father) of Abanar was the ban (son) of Abayaal.

There was severe war against the Palashathay (Philistines) all the yawam (days) of Shaawal: and when Shaawal saw any gabawar (mighty) ayash (man), or any chayal (valiant) ayash (man), he took him to him.

Shamawaal said to Shaawal, "Yahawah sent me to mashach (anoint) you to be malak (king) over his im (people), over Yasharaal (Israel). Now therefore listen to the qawal (voice) of the dabar (words) of Yahawah.
Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), ‘I have marked that which Imalaq did to Yasharaal (Israel), how he shawam (set) himself against him in the darak (way), when he came up out of Matzarayam.

Now yalak (go) and strike Imalaq, and utterly charam (destroy) all that they have, and don't spare them; but mawath (kill) both ayash (man) and ashah (woman), infant and nursing baby, ox and sheep, camel and donkey.'
Shaawal summoned the im (people), and numbered them in Talaayam, two maah (hundred) alap (thousand) footmen, and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) men of Yahawadah (Judah).
Shaawal came to the Iyar of Imalaq, and laid rayab (wait) in the nachal (valley).

Shaawal said to the Qayanay (Kenites), "yalak (go), sawar (depart), yarad (go) down from among the Imalaq (Amalekites), lest I asap (destroy) you with them; for you showed chasad (kindness) to all the children of Yasharaal (Israel), when they came up out of Matzarayam." So the Qayanay (Kenites) sawar (departed) from among the Imalaqay (Amalekites).
Shaawal struck the Imalaq (Amalekites), from Chawayalah as you bawaa (go) to Shawar, that is panayam (before) Matzarayam.
He took Agag the malak (king) Imalaq the Amalekites chay (alive), and charam (utterly) destroyed all the im (people) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).

But Shaawal and the im (people) spared Agag, and the best of the sheep, and of the cattle, and of the mashanah (fatlings), and the lambs, and all that was tawab (good), and wouldn't utterly charam (destroy) them: but everything that was vile and refuse, that they destroyed charam (utterly).
Then the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Shamawaal, saying,

"It grieves me that I have malak (set) up Shaawal to be malak (king); for he is turned shawab (turn back / repent) from following me, and has not performed my commandments." Shamawaal was charah (angry); and he cried to Yahawah all layal (night).

Shamawaal rose shakam (early) to qaraah (meet) Shaawal in the baqar (morning); and it was told Shamawaal, saying, "Shaawal came to Karamal, and behold, he natzab (set) up a monument for himself, and turned, and passed on, and went down to Galagal.
Shamawaal came to Shaawal; and Shaawal said to him, "You are blessed by Yahawah! I have performed the commandment of Yahawah.
Shamawaal said, "Then what does this qawal (bleating) of the sheep in my ears, and the qawal (lowing) of the cattle which I hear mean?

Shaawal said, "They have brought them from the Imalaqay (Amalekites); for the im (people) spared the best of the sheep and of the cattle, to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah your Alahayam. We have charam (utterly) destroyed the yathar (rest).
Then Shamawaal said to Shaawal, "rapah (stay), and I will nagad (tell) you what Yahawah has said to me last layal (night)." He said to him, "dabar (say) on.

Shamawaal said, "Though you were qatan (little) in your own iyan (sight), weren't you made the raash (head) of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel)? Yahawah mashach (anointed) you malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel);
and Yahawah sent you on a darak (journey), and said, ‘yalak (go), and utterly charam (destroy) the chataa (sinners) the Imalaq (Amalekites), and fight against them until they are consumed.'
Why then didn't you obey the qawal (voice) of Yahawah, but took the spoils, and did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah?

Shaawal said to Shamawaal, "But I have obeyed the qawal (voice) of Yahawah, and have gone the darak (way) which Yahawah sent me, and have brought Agag the malak (king) of Imalaq, and have charam (utterly) destroyed the Imalaq (Amalekites).
But the im (people) took of the spoil, sheep and cattle, the raashayath (chief) of the charam (devoted) things, to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah your Alahayam in Galagal.

Shamawaal said, "Has Yahawah as great Chapatz in burnt ilah (offerings) and zabach (sacrifices), as in obeying the qawal (voice) of Yahawah? Behold, to obey is tawab (better) than zabach (sacrifice), and to listen than the fat of ayal (rams).

For rebellion is as the chataah (sin) of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as tharapayam (idolatry) and teraphim. Because you have rejected the dabar (word) of Yahawah, he has also rejected you from being malak (king).
Shaawal said to Shamawaal, "I have sinned; for I have transgressed the commandment of Yahawah, and your dabar (words), because I feared the im (people), and obeyed their qawal (voice).
Now therefore, please nashaa (pardon) my chataah (sin), and shawab (turn back / repent) again with me, that I may shachah (worship) Yahawah.

Shamawaal said to Shaawal, "I will not shawab (turn back / repent) with you; for you have rejected the dabar (word) of Yahawah, and Yahawah has rejected you from being malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel).
As Shamawaal turned sabab (about) to yalak (go) away, Saul grabbed the skirt of his robe, and it tore.
Shamawaal said to him, "Yahawah has torn the mamalakawath (kingdom) of Yasharaal (Israel) from you this yawam (day), and has given it to a neighbor of yours who is tawab (better) than you.
Also the natzach (strength) of Yasharaal (Israel) will not lie nor nacham (repent); for he is not a adam (man), that he should nacham (repent).

Then he said, "I have sinned: yet please honor me now before the zaqan (elders) of my im (people), and before Yasharaal (Israel), and shawab (turn back / repent) back with me, that I may shachah (worship) Yahawah your Alahayam.
So Shamawaal went shawab (turn back / repent) with Shaawal; and Shaawal worshiped Yahawah.
Then Shamawaal said, "Bring here to me Agag the malak (king) Imalaq the Amalekites!" Agag came to him cheerfully. Agag said, "Surely the Mar of mawath (death) is sawar (past).
