Shamawaal said, "As your charab (sword) has made women shakal (childless), so your am (mother) will be shakal (childless) among women!" Shamawaal cut Agag in pieces panayam (before) Yahawah in Galagal.
Then Shamawaal went to Ramah; and Shaawal went up to his bayath (house) to Gabaih of Shaawal.

Shamawaal came no more to raah (see) Shaawal until the yawam (day) of his mawath (death); for Shamawaal mourned for Shaawal: and Yahawah grieved that he had made Shaawal malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel).

Yahawah said to Shamawaal, "How long will you mourn for Shaawal, since I have rejected him from being malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel)? malaa (fill) your qaran (horn) with shaman (oil), and yalak (go). I will shalach (send) you to Yashay the Bayathahalachamay; for I have provided a malak (king) for myself among his ban (sons).
Shamawaal said, "How can I yalak (go)? If Shaawal hears it, he will harag (kill) me." Yahawah said, "Take a heifer with you, and amar (say), I have bawaa (come) to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah.
qaraa (call) Yashay to the zabach (sacrifice), and I will show you what you shall do. You shall mashach (anoint) to me him whom I amar (name) to you.
Shamawaal did that which Yahawah spoke, and came to Bayathalacham. The zaqan (elders) of the Iyar came to meet him trembling, and said, "Do you bawaa (come) peaceably?

He said, "Peaceably; I have bawaa (come) to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah. qadash (sanctify) yourselves, and bawaa (come) with me to the zabach (sacrifice)." He sanctified Yashay and his ban (sons), and called them to the zabach (sacrifice).
It happened, when they had bawaa (come), that he looked at Alayaab, and said, "Surely yahawah (yahweh's) mashayach (anointed) is before him.

But Yahawah said to Shamawaal, "Don't look on his maraah (face), or on the Gabah of his stature; because I have rejected him: for I see not as adam (man) raah (see); for adam (man) raah (see) at the iyan (outward) appearance, but Yahawah raah (see) at the labab (heart).
Then Yashay called Abayanadab, and made him ibar (pass) panayam (before) Shamawaal. He said, "Neither has Yahawah chosen this bachar (one).
Then Yashay made Shamah to ibar (pass) by. He said, "Neither has Yahawah chosen this bachar (one).
Yashay made shabai (seven) of his ban (sons) to ibar (pass) panayam (before) Shamawaal. Shamawaal said to Yashay, "Yahawah has not chosen these.

Shamawaal said to Yashay, "Are all your children here?" He said, "There shaar (remains) yet the youngest, and behold, he is keeping the sheep." Shamawaal said to Yashay, "shalach (send) and get him; for we will not sabab (sit) down until he bawaa (comes) here.
He sent, and brought him in. Now he was Adamanay, and withal of a Yapah iyan (face), and goodly to look on. Yahawah said, "qawam (arise), mashach (anoint) him; for this is he.

Then Shamawaal took the qaran (horn) of shaman (oil), and mashach (anointed) him in the qarab (midst) of his ach (brothers): and the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah came mightily on Dawad from that yawam (day) forward. So Shamawaal rose up, and went to Ramah.
Now the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah sawar (departed) from Shaawal, and an rai (evil) rawach (spirit) from Yahawah troubled him.
Shaawal ibad (servants) said to him, "See now, an rai (evil) rawach (spirit) from Alahayam troubles you.

Let our Adawan now command your ibad (servants) who are panayam (before) you, to seek out a ayash (man) who is a skillful player on the harp. It shall happen, when the rai (evil) rawach (spirit) from Alahayam is on you, that he shall play with his yad (hand), and you shall be tawab (well).
Shaawal said to his ibad (servants), "raah (see) me now a ayash (man) who can play yatab (well), and bawaa (bring) him to me.

Then one of the young men answered, and said, "raah (see), I have seen a ban (son) of Yashay the Bayathahalachamay, who is skillful in playing, a gabawar (mighty) man of valor, a ayash (man) of war, bayan (prudent) in dabar (speech), and a comely ayash (person); and Yahawah is with him.
Therefore Shaawal sent malaak (messengers) to Yashay, and said, "shalach (send) me Dawad your ban (son), who is with the sheep.
Yashay took a donkey loaded with lacham (bread), and a bottle of yayan (wine), and a young goat, and sent them by Dawad his ban (son) to Shaawal.
Dawad came to Shaawal, and stood panayam (before) him. He loved him maad (greatly); and he became his armor bearer.
Shaawal sent to Yashay, saying, "Please let Dawad imad (stand) panayam (before) me; for he has found favor in my iyan (sight).

It happened, when the rawach (spirit) from Alahayam was on Shaawal, that Dawad took the harp, and played with his yad (hand): so Shaawal was refreshed, and was tawab (well), and the rai (evil) rawach (spirit) sawar (departed) from him.

Now the Palashathay (Philistines) gathered asap (together) their machanah (armies) to battle; and they were gathered asap (together) at Shawakah, which belongs to Yahawadah (Judah), and encamped between Shawakah and Izaqah, in Apasadamayam.
Shaawal and the men of Yasharaal (Israel) were gathered asap (together), and encamped in the valley of Alah, and set the battle in array qaraah (against) the Palashathay (Philistines).
The Palashathay (Philistines) stood on the har (mountain) on the one side, and Yasharaal (Israel) stood on the har (mountain) on the other side: and there was a Gayaa between them.
There went out a ayash (champion) out of the machanah (camp) of the Palashathay (Philistines), sham (named) Galayath, of gath (gath), whose height was shash (six) amah (cubits) and a span.
He had a helmet of brass on his raash (head), and he was Labash with a coat of mail; and the weight of the coat was chamash (five) alap (thousand) shekels of brass.
He had brass shin armor on his ragal (legs), and a javelin of brass between his shoulders.

The itz (staff) of his spear was like a weaver's beam; and his spear's lahabah (head) weighed shash (six) maah (hundred) shekels of barazal (iron): and his tzanah (shield) bearer went panayam (before) him.

He stood and cried to the mairakah (armies) of Yasharaal (Israel), and said to them, "Why have you yatzaa (come) out to set your battle in array? Am I not a Palashathay (Philistine), and you ibad (servants) to Shaawal? Choose a ayash (man) for yourselves, and let him yarad (come) down to me.

If he be yakal (able) to fight with me, and kill me, then will we be your ibad (servants); but if I yakal (prevail) against him, and kill him, then you will be our ibad (servants), and ibad (serve) us.
The Palashathay (Philistine) said, "I defy the mairakah (armies) of Yasharaal (Israel) this yawam (day)! nathan (give) me a ayash (man), that we may fight together!
When Shaawal and all Yasharaal (Israel) heard those dabar (words) of the Palashathay (Philistine), they were dismayed, and maad (greatly) yaraa (afraid).

Now Dawad was the ban (son) of that Ephrathite of Bayathalacham Judah, whose sham (name) was Yashay; and he had shamanah (eight) ban (sons): and the ayash (man) was an old zaqan (man) in the yawam (days) of Shaawal, stricken among men.

The shalawash (three) gadawal (eldest) ban (sons) of Yashay had gone achar (after) Shaawal to the battle: and the sham (names) of his shalawash (three) ban (sons) who went to the battle were Alayaab the firstborn, and mashanah (next) to him Abayanadab, and the shalayashay (third) Shamah.
Dawad was the youngest; and the shalawash (three) gadawal (eldest) followed Shaawal.
Now Dawad went shawab (turn back / repent) and forth from Shaawal to raih (feed) his ab (father's) sheep at Bayathalacham.
The Palashathay (Philistine) drew near shakam (morning) and evening, and presented himself arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days).

Yashay said to Dawad his ban (son), "Now take for your ach (brothers) an ephah of this parched grain, and these ishar (ten) loaves, and carry them quickly to the machanah (camp) to your ach (brothers);
and bawaa (bring) these ishar (ten) cheeses to the shar (captain) of their alap (thousand), and paqad (see) how your ach (brothers) are doing, and bring back news.
Now Shaawal, and they, and all the men of Yasharaal (Israel), were in the valley of Alah, fighting with the Palashathay (Philistines).

Dawad rose up shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and left the sheep with a keeper, and took, and went, as Yashay had tzawah (commanded) him; and he came to the place of the wagons, as the chayal (army) which was yatzaa (going) forth to the mairakah (fight) shouted for the battle.
Yasharaal (Israel) and the Palashathay (Philistines) put the battle in array, mairakah (army) qaraah (against) mairakah (army).
Dawad left his baggage in the yad (hand) of the keeper of the baggage, and ran to the mairakah (army), and came and greeted his ach (brothers).

As he talked with them, behold, there came up the ayash (champion), the Palashathay (Philistine) of gath (gath), Galayath by sham (name), out of the mairakah (ranks) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and spoke according to the same dabar (words): and Dawad heard them.
All the men of Yasharaal (Israel), when they saw the ayash (man), fled from him, and were terrified.

The men of Yasharaal (Israel) said, "Have you seen this ayash (man) who has ilah (come) up? He has surely ilah (come) up to defy Yasharaal (Israel). It shall be, that the ayash (man) who kills him, the malak (king) will enrich him with gadawal (great) riches, and will nathan (give) him his bath (daughter), and ishah (make) his ab (father's) bayath (house) Chapashay in Yasharaal (Israel).

Dawad spoke to the men who stood by him, saying, "What shall be done to the ayash (man) who kills this Palashathay (Philistine), and sawar (takes) away the reproach from Yasharaal (Israel)? For who is this Iral Palashathay (Philistine), that he should defy the mairakah (armies) of the chay (living) Alahayam?
The im (people) answered him in this way, saying, "So shall it be done to the ayash (man) who kills him.

Alayaab his gadawal (eldest) ach (brother) heard when he spoke to the men; and Alayaab ap (anger) was kindled against Dawad, and he said, "Why have you yarad (come) down? With whom have you left those Mait sheep in the madabar (wilderness)? I yadai (know) your pride, and the rai (naughtiness) of your labab (heart); for you have yarad (come) down that you might raah (see) the battle.
Dawad said, "What have I now done? Is there not a dabar (cause)?
He turned away from him toward achar (another), and spoke like that again; and the im (people) answered him again the same way.
When the dabar (words) were heard which Dawad spoke, they rehearsed them panayam (before) Shaawal; and he sent for him.
Dawad said to Shaawal, "Let no adam (man's) lab (heart) napal (fail) because of him. Your ibad (servant) will yalak (go) and fight with this Palashathay (Philistine).
Shaawal said to Dawad, "You are not yakal (able) to yalak (go) against this Palashathay (Philistine) to fight with him; for you are but a youth, and he a ayash (man) of war from his youth.
Dawad said to Shaawal, "Your ibad (servant) was keeping his ab (father's) sheep; and when a aray (lion) or a bear came, and took a lamb out of the flock,
I went out achar (after) him, and struck him, and rescued it out of his pah (mouth). When he qawam (arose) against me, I caught him by his beard, and struck him, and killed him.
Your ibad (servant) struck both the aray (lion) and the bear. This Iral Palashathay (Philistine) shall be as one of them, since he has defied the mairakah (armies) of the chay (living) Alahayam.

Dawad said, "Yahawah who delivered me out of the paw of the aray (lion), and out of the paw of the bear, he will natzal (deliver) me out of the yad (hand) of this Palashathay (Philistine)." Shaawal said to Dawad, "yalak (go); and Yahawah shall be with you.
Shaawal Labash Dawad with his clothing. He nathan (put) a helmet of brass on his raash (head), and he Labash him with a coat of mail.

Dawad strapped his charab (sword) on his clothing, and he tried to move; for he had not tested it. Dawad said to Shaawal, "I can't yalak (go) with these; for I have not tested them." Dawad took them off.

He took his maqal (staff) in his yad (hand), and chose for himself chamash (five) Chalaq aban (stones) out of the nachal (brook), and shawam (put) them in the raih (shepherd's) bag which he had, even in his wallet. His sling was in his yad (hand); and he drew near to the Palashathay (Philistine).
The Palashathay (Philistine) came on and drew Qarab to Dawad; and the ayash (man) who bore the tzanah (shield) went panayam (before) him.
When the Palashathay (Philistine) looked about, and saw Dawad, he disdained him; for he was but a youth, and Adamanay, and withal of a Yapah maraah (face).
The Palashathay (Philistine) said to Dawad, "Am I a dog, that you bawaa (come) to me with sticks?" The Palashathay (Philistine) cursed Dawad by his Alahayam.
The Palashathay (Philistine) said to Dawad, "yalak (come) to me, and I will nathan (give) your flesh to the birds of the sky, and to the animals of the shadah (field).

Then Dawad said to the Palashathay (Philistine), "You bawaa (come) to me with a charab (sword), and with a spear, and with a javelin: but I bawaa (come) to you in the sham (name) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of the tzabaa (armies) of Yasharaal (Israel), whom you have defied.

Today, Yahawah will deliver you into my yad (hand). I will strike you, and sawar (take) your raash (head) from off you. I will nathan (give) the pagar (dead) bodies of the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines) this yawam (day) to the birds of the sky, and to the wild animals of the aratz (earth); that all the aratz (earth) may yadai (know) that there is a Alahayam in Yasharaal (Israel),

and that all this qahal (assembly) may yadai (know) that Yahawah doesn't yashai (save) with charab (sword) and spear: for the battle is yahawah (yahweh's), and he will nathan (give) you into our yad (hand).

It happened, when the Palashathay (Philistine) qawam (arose), and came and drew qarab (near) to qaraah (meet) Dawad, that Dawad hurried, and ran toward the mairakah (army) to qaraah (meet) the Palashathay (Philistine).

Dawad shalach (put) his yad (hand) in his bag, took a aban (stone), and slung it, and struck the Palashathay (Philistine) in his forehead; and the aban (stone) sank into his forehead, and he napal (fell) on his panayam (face) to the aratz (earth).

So Dawad prevailed over the Palashathay (Philistine) with a sling and with a aban (stone), and struck the Palashathay (Philistine), and killed him; but there was no charab (sword) in the yad (hand) of Dawad.

Then Dawad ran, and stood over the Palashathay (Philistine), and took his charab (sword), and drew it out of its sheath, and killed him, and karath (cut) off his raash (head) therewith. When the Palashathay (Philistines) saw that their gabawar (champion) was mawath (dead), they fled.

The men of Yasharaal (Israel) and of Yahawadah (Judah) qawam (arose), and shouted, and pursued the Palashathay (Philistines), until you bawaa (come) Gayaa Gai, and to the gates of Iqarawan. The Chalal of the Palashathay (Philistines) napal (fell) down by the darak (way) to Shairayam, even to gath (gath), and to Iqarawan.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) returned from chasing achar (after) the Palashathay (Philistines), and they plundered their machanah (camp).
Dawad took the raash (head) of the Palashathay (Philistine), and brought it to Yarawashalam; but he shawam (put) his armor in his ahal (tent).

When Shaawal saw Dawad yatzaa (go) forth qaraah (against) the Palashathay (Philistine), he said to Abanar, the shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army), "Abanar, whose ban (son) is this youth?" Abanar said, "As your napash (soul) chay (lives), O malak (king), I can't yadai (tell).
The malak (king) said, "Inquire whose ban (son) the young ilam (man) is!

As Dawad returned from the slaughter of the Palashathay (Philistine), Abanar took him, and brought him panayam (before) Shaawal with the raash (head) of the Palashathay (Philistine) in his yad (hand).
Shaawal said to him, "Whose ban (son) are you, you nair (young) man?" Dawad answered, "I am the ban (son) of your ibad (servant) Yashay the Bayathahalachamay.

It happened, when he had made an kalah (end) of speaking to Shaawal, that the napash (soul) of Yahawanathan was qashar (knit) with the napash (soul) of Dawad, and Yahawanathan loved him as his own napash (soul).
Shaawal took him that yawam (day), and would let him shawab (turn back / repent) no more home to his ab (father's) house.
Then Yahawanathan and Dawad made a barayath (covenant), because he loved him as his own napash (soul).
Yahawanathan stripped himself of the robe that was on him, and gave it to Dawad, and his clothing, even to his charab (sword), and to his qashath (bow), and Chagawar his sash.

Dawad went out wherever Shaawal sent him, and behaved himself shakal (wisely): and Shaawal shawam (set) him over the men of war, and it was yatab (good) in the iyan (sight) of all the im (people), and also in the iyan (sight) of Shaawal ibad (servants).

It happened as they came, when Dawad returned from the slaughter of the Palashathay (Philistine), that the women came out of all the Iyar of Yasharaal (Israel), singing and dancing, to qaraah (meet) malak (king) Shaawal, with tambourines, with joy, and with shalayash (instruments) of music.
The women sang shachaq (one) to another as they played, and said, "Shaawal has slain his alap (thousands), Dawad his ten alap (thousands).

Shaawal was very charah (angry), and this dabar (saying) displeased him; and he said, "They have ascribed to Dawad rababah (ten) thousands, and to me they have ascribed but alap (thousands). What can he have more but the malawakah (kingdom)?
Shaawal eyed Dawad from that yawam (day) and forward.

It happened on the next macharath (day), that an rai (evil) rawach (spirit) from Alahayam came mightily on Shaawal, and he prophesied in the midst of the bayath (house). Dawad played with his yad (hand), as he did yawam (day) by day. Shaawal had his spear in his yad (hand);
and Shaawal threw the spear; for he said, "I will pin Dawad even to the wall!" Dawad escaped from his panayam (presence) paim (twice).
Shaawal was yaraa (afraid) of Dawad, because Yahawah was with him, and was sawar (departed) from Shaawal.
Therefore Shaawal removed him from him, and made him his shar (captain) over a alap (thousand); and he went out and came in panayam (before) the im (people).
Dawad behaved himself shakal (wisely) in all his darak (ways); and Yahawah was with him.
When Shaawal saw that he behaved himself very shakal (wisely), he stood in gawar (awe) of him.
But all Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah) loved Dawad; for he went out and came in panayam (before) them.

Shaawal said to Dawad, "Behold, my gadawal (elder) bath (daughter) Marab, I will nathan (give) her to you as ashah (wife). Only be ban (valiant) for me, and fight yahawah (yahweh's) battles." For Shaawal said, "Don't let my yad (hand) be on him, but let the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines) be on him.
Dawad said to Shaawal, "Who am I, and what is my chay (life), or my ab (father's) mashapachah (family) in Yasharaal (Israel), that I should be son-in-law to the malak (king)?
But it happened at the ith (time) when Marab, Shaawal bath (daughter), should have been given to Dawad, that she was given to Idarayaal the Machalathay as ashah (wife).
Mayakal, Shaawal bath (daughter), loved Dawad; and they told Shaawal, and the thing pleased him.

Shaawal said, I will nathan (give) her to him, that she may be a snare to him, and that the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines) may be against him. Therefore Shaawal said to Dawad, "You shall this yawam (day) be my son-in-law a shanayam (second) time.

Shaawal tzawah (commanded) his ibad (servants), "dabar (talk) with Dawad secretly, and amar (say), ‘Behold, the malak (king) has delight in you, and all his ibad (servants) ahab (love) you: now therefore be the malak (king's) son-in-law.'

Shaawal ibad (servants) spoke those dabar (words) in the ears of Dawad. Dawad said, "Does it seems to you a qalal (light) thing to be the malak (king's) son-in-law, since I am a poor ayash (man), and qalah (lightly) esteemed?
The ibad (servants) of Shaawal told him, saying, "Dawad spoke like this.

Shaawal said, "You shall amar (tell) Dawad, ‘The malak (king) Chapatz no dowry except one maah (hundred) foreskins of the Palashathay (Philistines), to be avenged of the malak (king's) ayab (enemies).'" Now Shaawal thought to make Dawad napal (fall) by the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).
When his ibad (servants) told Dawad these dabar (words), it pleased Dawad well to be the malak (king's) son-in-law. The yawam (days) were not malaa (expired);

and Dawad qawam (arose) and went, he and his men, and killed of the Palashathay (Philistines) two maah (hundred) men; and Dawad brought their foreskins, and they gave them in malaa (full) number to the malak (king), that he might be the malak (king's) son-in-law. Shaawal gave him Mayakal his bath (daughter) as ashah (wife).
Shaawal saw and knew that Yahawah was with Dawad; and Mayakal, Shaawal bath (daughter), loved him.
Shaawal was yet the more yaraa (afraid) of Dawad; and Shaawal was Dawad ayab (enemy) yawam (continually).

Then the shar (princes) of the Palashathay (Philistines) went yatzaa (forth): and it happened, as often as they went yatzaa (forth), that Dawad behaved himself more shakal (wisely) than all the ibad (servants) of Shaawal; so that his sham (name) was highly esteemed.
Shaawal spoke to Yawanathan his ban (son), and to all his ibad (servants), that they should mawath (kill) Dawad. But Jonathan, Saul's son, delighted much in David.

Yahawanathan told Dawad, saying, "Shaawal my ab (father) seeks to mawath (kill) you. Now therefore, please shamar (take) care of yourself in the baqar (morning), and live in a secret place, and hide yourself.

I will yatzaa (go) out and imad (stand) yad (beside) my ab (father) in the shadah (field) where you are, and I will dabar (talk) with my ab (father) about you; and if I raah (see) anything, I will nagad (tell) you.

Yahawanathan spoke tawab (good) of Dawad to Shaawal his ab (father), and said to him, "Don't let the malak (king) chataa (sin) against his ibad (servant), against Dawad; because he has not sinned against you, and because his maishah (works) have been very tawab (good) toward you;

for he shawam (put) his napash (life) in his kap (hand), and struck the Palashathay (Philistine), and Yahawah worked a gadawal (great) thashawaih (victory) for all Yasharaal (Israel). You saw it, and Shamach. Why then will you chataa (sin) against naqay (innocent) dam (blood), to mawath (kill) Dawad without a cause?
Shaawal listened to the qawal (voice) of Yahawanathan: and Shaawal swore, "As Yahawah chay (lives), he shall not be put to mawath (death).
Yahawanathan called Dawad, and Yahawanathan showed him all those things. Yahawanathan brought Dawad to Shaawal, and he was in his panayam (presence), as before.
There was war again. Dawad went out, and fought with the Palashathay (Philistines), and killed them with a gadawal (great) makah (slaughter); and they fled panayam (before) him.
An rai (evil) rawach (spirit) from Yahawah was on Shaawal, as he sat in his bayath (house) with his spear in his yad (hand); and Dawad was playing with his yad (hand).
Shaawal sought to pin Dawad even to the wall with the spear; but he slipped away out of Shaawal panayam (presence), and he stuck the spear into the wall. Dawad fled, and escaped that layal (night).

Shaawal sent malaak (messengers) to Dawad bayath (house), to shamar (watch) him, and to mawath (kill) him in the baqar (morning). Mayakal, Dawad ashah (wife), told him, saying, "If you don't malat (save) your napash (life) tonight, tomorrow you will be killed.
So Mayakal let Dawad down through the window. He went, fled, and escaped.
Mayakal took the tharapayam (teraphim), and laid it in the bed, and shawam (put) a pillow of goats' hair at its maraashah (head), and covered it with the clothes.
When Shaawal sent malaak (messengers) to take Dawad, she said, "He is chalah (sick).
Shaawal sent the malaak (messengers) to raah (see) Dawad, saying, "ilah (bring) him up to me in the bed, that I may mawath (kill) him.
When the malaak (messengers) came in, behold, the tharapayam (teraphim) was in the bed, with the pillow of goats' hair at its iz (head).

Shaawal said to Mayakal, "Why have you deceived me thus, and let my ayab (enemy) go, so that he is escaped?" Mayakal answered Shaawal, "He said to me, ‘Let me shalach (go)! Why should I mawath (kill) you?'
Now Dawad fled, and escaped, and came to Shamawaal to Ramah, and told him all that Shaawal had done to him. He and Shamawaal went and lived in Nawayath.
It was told Shaawal, saying, "Behold, Dawad is at Nawayath in Ramah.

Shaawal sent malaak (messengers) to take Dawad: and when they saw the company of the nabayaa (prophets) nabaa (prophesying), and Shamawaal standing as head over them, the rawach (spirit) of Alahayam came on the malaak (messengers) of Shaawal, and they also prophesied.
When it was told Shaawal, he sent other malaak (messengers), and they also prophesied. Shaawal sent malaak (messengers) again the shalayashay (third) time, and they also prophesied.
Then went he also to Ramah, and came to the gadawal (great) bawar (well) that is Shakaw Secu: and he asked, "Where are Shamawaal and Dawad?" One said, "Behold, they are at Nawayath in Ramah.
He went there to Nawayath in Ramah. Then the rawach (spirit) of Alahayam came on him also, and he went on, and prophesied, until he came to Nawayath in Ramah.

He also stripped off his clothes, and he also prophesied panayam (before) Shamawaal, and napal (lay) down Irawam all that yawam (day) and all that layal (night). Therefore they amar (say), "Is Shaawal also among the nabayaa (prophets)?

Dawad fled from Nawayath in Ramah, and came and said panayam (before) Yahawanathan, "What have I done? What is my iwan (iniquity)? What is my chataah (sin) panayam (before) your ab (father), that he seeks my napash (life)?

He said to him, "Far from it; you shall not mawath (die). Behold, my ab (father) does nothing either gadawal (great) or qatan (small), but that he galah (discloses) it to me; and why should my ab (father) hide this thing from me? It is not so.

Dawad swore moreover, and said, "Your ab (father) yadai (knows) well that I have found favor in your iyan (eyes); and he amar (says), ‘Don't let Yahawanathan yadai (know) this, lest he be grieved:' but truly as Yahawah chay (lives), and as your napash (soul) chay (lives), there is but a step between me and mawath (death).
Then Yahawanathan said to Dawad, "Whatever your napash (soul) amar (desires), I will even do it for you.

Dawad said to Yahawanathan, "Behold, tomorrow is the new chadash (moon), and I should not yashab (fail) to akal (dine) with the malak (king); but let me shalach (go), that I may hide myself in the shadah (field) to the shalayashay (third) irab (day) at evening.

If your ab (father) paqad (miss) me at all, then amar (say), ‘Dawad shaal (earnestly) asked leave of me that he might run to Bayathalacham his Iyar; for it is the yawam (yearly) zabach (sacrifice) there for all the mashapachah (family).'
If he amar (says), ‘It is tawab (well);' your ibad (servant) shall have shalawam (peace): but if he be charah (angry), then yadai (know) that rai (evil) is determined by him.

Therefore ishah (deal) chasad (kindly) with your ibad (servant); for you have brought your ibad (servant) into a barayath (covenant) of Yahawah with you: but if there is iwan (iniquity) in me, mawath (kill) me yourself; for why should you bawaa (bring) me to your ab (father)?
Yahawanathan said, "Far be it from you; for if I should at all yadai (know) that rai (evil) were determined by my ab (father) to bawaa (come) on you, then wouldn't I nagad (tell) you that?
Then Dawad said to Yahawanathan, "Who shall nagad (tell) me if perchance your ab (father) answers you Qashah?
Yahawanathan said to Dawad, "yalak (come), and let us yatzaa (go) out into the shadah (field)." They shanayam (both) went out into the shadah (field).

Yahawanathan said to Dawad, "By Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), when I have sounded my ab (father) about this ith (time) tomorrow, or the shalayashay (third) machar (day), behold, if there is tawab (good) toward Dawad, shall I not then shalach (send) to you, and disclose it to you?

Yahawah do so to Yahawanathan, and more also, should it yatab (please) my ab (father) to do you rai (evil), if I don't galah (disclose) it to you, and shalach (send) you away, that you may halak (go) in shalawam (peace): and Yahawah be with you, as he has been with my ab (father).
You shall not only am (while) yet I chay (live) show me the loving chasad (kindness) of Yahawah, that I not mawath (die);

but also you shall not karath (cut) off your chasad (kindness) from my bayath (house) iwalam (forever); no, not when Yahawah has karath (cut) off the ayab (enemies) of Dawad everyone from the surface of the adamah (earth).
So Yahawanathan made a covenant with the bayath (house) of Dawad, saying, "Yahawah will require it at the yad (hand) of Dawad ayab (enemies).
Yahawanathan caused Dawad to shabai (swear) again, for the ahabah (love) that he had to him; for he loved him as he loved his own napash (soul).
Then Yahawanathan said Dawad him, "Tomorrow is the new chadash (moon): and you will be missed, because your mawashab (seat) will be paqad (empty).

When you have stayed shalash (three) days, you shall bawaa (go) down maad (quickly), and bawaa (come) to the place where you hid yourself when this started, and shall yashab (remain) by the aban (stone) Azal.
I will shoot shalawash (three) chatz (arrows) on its side, as though I shot at a mark.

Behold, I will shalach (send) the nair (boy), saying, ‘yalak (go), matzaa (find) the chatz (arrows)!' If I amar (tell) the nair (boy), ‘Behold, the chatz (arrows) are on this side of you. Take them;' then bawaa (come); for there is shalawam (peace) to you and no dabar (hurt), as Yahawah chay (lives).
But if I amar (say) this to the boy, ‘Behold, the chatz (arrows) are beyond you;' then go your yalak (way); for Yahawah has sent you shalach (away).
dabar (concerning) the matter which you and I have spoken of, behold, Yahawah is between you and me iwalam (forever).
So Dawad hid himself in the shadah (field): and when the new chadash (moon) had come, the malak (king) sat him down to akal (eat) lacham (food).

The malak (king) sat on his mawashab (seat), as at other paim (times), even on the mawashab (seat) by the wall; and Yahawanathan stood up, and Abanar sat by Shaawal side: but Dawad place was paqad (empty).
Nevertheless Shaawal didn't dabar (say) anything that yawam (day): for he thought, "Something has happened to him. He is not tahawar (clean). Surely he is not tahawar (clean).

It happened on the next macharath (day) after the new chadash (moon), the shanay (second) day, that Dawad place was paqad (empty). Shaawal said to Yahawanathan his ban (son), "Why doesn't the ban (son) of Yashay bawaa (come) to lacham (eat), neither thamawal (yesterday), nor today?
Yahawanathan answered Shaawal, "Dawad shaal (earnestly) asked leave of me to go to Bayathalacham.

He said, ‘Please let me shalach (go), for our mashapachah (family) has a zabach (sacrifice) in the Iyar. My ach (brother) has tzawah (commanded) me to be there. Now, if I have found favor in your iyan (eyes), please let me malat (go) away and raah (see) my ach (brothers).' Therefore he has not bawaa (come) to the malak (king's) table.

Then Shaawal ap (anger) was kindled against Yahawanathan, and he said to him, "You ban (son) of a iwah (perverse) rebellious woman, don't I yadai (know) that you have chosen the ban (son) of Yashay to your own bashath (shame), and to the bashath (shame) of your am (mother's) irawah (nakedness)?

For as yawam (long) as the ban (son) of Yashay chayay (lives) on the adamah (earth), you shall not be established, nor your malakawath (kingdom). Therefore now shalach (send) and bring him to me, for he shall ban (surely) die!
Yahawanathan answered Shaawal his ab (father), and said to him, "Why should he be put to mawath (death)? What has he done?
Shaawal cast his spear at him to strike him. By this Yahawanathan knew that his ab (father) was determined to put Dawad to mawath (death).

So Yahawanathan qawam (arose) from the table in fierce ap (anger), and ate no lacham (food) the shanay (second) yawam (day) of the chadash (month); for he was grieved for Dawad, because his ab (father) had done him kalam (shame).
It happened in the baqar (morning), that Yahawanathan went out into the shadah (field) at the mawaid (time) appointed with Dawad, and a qatan (little) nair (boy) with him.
He said to his nair (boy), "Run, matzaa (find) now the chatz (arrows) which I shoot." As the nair (boy) ran, he shot an arrow ibar (beyond) him.
When the nair (boy) had bawaa (come) to the place of the arrow which Yahawanathan had shot, Yahawanathan cried achar (after) the nair (boy), and said, "Isn't the arrow beyond you?
Yahawanathan cried achar (after) the nair (boy), "Go fast! Hurry! Don't delay!" Yahawanathan nair (boy) gathered up the chatz (arrows), and came to his adawan (master).
But the nair (boy) didn't yadai (know) anything. Only Yahawanathan and Dawad knew the dabar (matter).
Yahawanathan gave his weapons to his nair (boy), and said to him, "yalak (go), bawaa (carry) them to the Iyar.

As soon as the nair (boy) was gone, Dawad qawam (arose) out of the Nagab, and napal (fell) on his ap (face) to the aratz (ground), and bowed himself shalawash (three) paim (times). They kissed one rai (another), and wept one with rai (another), and Dawad wept the most.

Yahawanathan said to Dawad, "yalak (go) in shalawam (peace), because we have shanayam (both) sworn in the sham (name) of Yahawah, saying, ‘Yahawah shall be between me and you, and between my zarai (seed) and your zarai (seed), iwalam (forever).'" He qawam (arose) and departed; and Yahawanathan went into the Iyar.
Then came Dawad to Nab to Achayamalak the kahan (priest). Achayamalak came to qaraah (meet) Dawad trembling, and said to him, "Why are you alone, and no ayash (man) with you?

Dawad said to Achayamalak the kahan (priest), "The malak (king) has tzawah (commanded) me a dabar (business), and has said to me, ‘Let no ayash (man) yadai (know) anything of the dabar (business) about which I shalach (send) you, and what I have tzawah (commanded) you; and I have appointed the nair (young) men to such and Alamanay a place.'
Now therefore what is under your yad (hand)? nathan (give) me chamash (five) loaves of lacham (bread) in my yad (hand), or whatever there is matzaa (present).

The kahan (priest) answered Dawad, and said, "There is no chal (common) lacham (bread) under my yad (hand), but there is qadash (holy) lacham (bread); if only the nair (young) men have kept themselves from women.

Dawad answered the kahan (priest), and said to him, "Truly, women have been kept from us about these shalashawam (three) thamawal (days). When I came out, the vessels of the nair (young) men were qadash (holy), though it was but a chal (common) darak (journey). How much more then today shall their vessels be qadash (holy)?

So the kahan (priest) gave him qadash (holy) lacham (bread); for there was no bread there but the show lacham (bread), that was taken from panayam (before) Yahawah, to shawam (put) hot lacham (bread) in the yawam (day) when it was taken away.

Now a certain ayash (man) of the ibad (servants) of Shaawal was there that yawam (day), detained panayam (before) Yahawah; and his sham (name) was Daag the Adamay (Edomite), the best of the herdsmen who belonged to Shaawal.

Dawad said to Achayamalak, "Isn't there here under your yad (hand) spear or charab (sword)? For I have neither brought my charab (sword) nor my weapons with me, because the malak (king's) dabar (business) required haste.

The kahan (priest) said, "The charab (sword) of Galayath the Palashathay (Philistine), whom you killed in the valley of Alah, behold, it is here wrapped in a cloth achar (behind) the apawad (ephod). If you will take that, take it; for there is no other except that here." Dawad said, "There is none like that. nathan (give) it to me.
Dawad qawam (arose), and fled that yawam (day) for panayam (fear) of Shaawal, and went to Akayash the malak (king) of gath (gath).

The ibad (servants) of Akayash said to him, "Isn't this Dawad the malak (king) of the aratz (land)? Didn't they sing one to another about him in dances, saying, ‘Shaawal has slain his alap (thousands), Dawad his ten alap (thousands)?'
Dawad laid up these dabar (words) in his labab (heart), and was very yaraa (afraid) of Akayash the malak (king) of gath (gath).
He changed his behavior iyan (before) them, and pretended to be halal (mad) in their yad (hands), and scrabbled on the doors of the gate, and let his spittle yarad (fall) down on his beard.
Then Akayash said to his ibad (servants), "raah (see), you see the ayash (man) is mad. Why then have you brought him to me?
Do I Chasar madmen, that you have brought this fellow to play the madman in my presence? Shall this fellow bawaa (come) into my bayath (house)?
Dawad therefore departed there, and escaped to the cave of Idalam. When his ach (brothers) and all his ab (father's) bayath (house) heard it, they went down there to him.

Everyone who was in distress, and everyone who was in debt, and everyone who was Mar, gathered themselves to him; and he became shar (captain) over them: and there were with him about arabai (four) maah (hundred) men.

Dawad went there to Matzapah of Mawaab, and he said to the malak (king) of Mawaab, "Please let my ab (father) and my am (mother) yatzaa (come) out with you, until I yadai (know) what Alahayam will do for me.
He brought them panayam (before) the malak (king) of Mawaab; and they lived with him all the yawam (while) that Dawad was in the stronghold.
The nabayaa (prophet) Gad said to Dawad, "Don't stay in the stronghold. Depart, and bawaa (go) into the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah)." Then Dawad departed, and came into the Yair of Charath.

Shaawal heard that Dawad was discovered, and the men who were with him. Now Shaawal was sitting in Gabaih, under the tamarisk tree in Ramah, with his spear in his yad (hand), and all his ibad (servants) were standing about him.

Shaawal said to his ibad (servants) who stood about him, "Hear now, you Banayamayanay (Benjamites)! Will the ban (son) of Yashay nathan (give) everyone of you shadah (fields) and vineyards, will he shawam (make) you all shar (captains) of alap (thousands) and shar (captains) of maah (hundreds),

that all of you have conspired against me, and there is none who galah (discloses) to me when my ban (son) karath (makes) a treaty with the ban (son) of Yashay, and there is none of you who is chalah (sorry) for me, or galah (discloses) to me that my ban (son) has stirred up my ibad (servant) against me, to lie in wait, as at this yawam (day)?
Then Daag the Adamay (Edomite), who stood by the ibad (servants) of Shaawal, answered and said, "I saw the ban (son) of Yashay coming to Nab, to Achayamalak the ban (son) of Achayatawab.
He inquired of Yahawah for him, gave him food, and gave him the charab (sword) of Galayath the Palashathay (Philistine).

Then the malak (king) sent to qaraa (call) Achayamalak the kahan (priest), the ban (son) of Achayatawab, and all his ab (father's) bayath (house), the kahan (priests) who were in Nab: and they came all of them to the malak (king).
Shaawal said, "Hear now, you ban (son) of Achayatawab." He answered, "Here I am, my Adawan.

Shaawal said to him, "Why have you conspired against me, you and the ban (son) of Yashay, in that you have given him lacham (bread), and a charab (sword), and have inquired of Alahayam for him, that he should qawam (rise) against me, to lie in wait, as at this yawam (day)?

Then Achayamalak answered the malak (king), and said, "Who among all your ibad (servants) is so aman (faithful) as Dawad, who is the malak (king's) son-in-law, and is taken into your council, and is honorable in your bayath (house)?

Have I today begun to inquire of Alahayam for him? Be it far from me! Don't let the malak (king) shawam (impute) anything to his ibad (servant), nor to all the bayath (house) of my ab (father); for your ibad (servant) yadai (knows) nothing of all this, qatan (less) or more.
The malak (king) said, "You shall mawath (surely) mawath (die), Achayamalak, you, and all your ab (father's) bayath (house).

The malak (king) said to the guard who stood about him, "sabab (turn), and mawath (kill) the kahan (priests) of Yahawah; because their yad (hand) also is with Dawad, and because they knew that he fled, and didn't galah (disclose) it to me." But the ibad (servants) of the malak (king) wouldn't shalach (put) forth their yad (hand) to pagai (fall) on the kahan (priests) of Yahawah.

The malak (king) said to Daag, "sabab (turn) and attack the kahan (priests)!" Daag the Adamay (Edomite) turned, and he attacked the kahan (priests), and he killed on that yawam (day) shamanayam (eighty) - chamash (five) ayash (people) who wore a linen apawad (ephod).

He struck Nab, the Iyar of the kahan (priests), with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), both men and women, children and nursing babies, and cattle and donkeys and sheep, with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).
One of the ban (sons) of Achayamalak, the ban (son) of Achayatawab, sham (named) Abayathar, escaped, and fled achar (after) Dawad.
Abayathar told Dawad that Shaawal had slain yahawah (yahweh's) kahan (priests).

Dawad said to Abayathar, "I knew on that yawam (day), when Daag the Adamay (Edomite) was there, that he would nagad (surely) nagad (tell) Shaawal. I am responsible for the death of all the napash (persons) of your ab (father's) bayath (house).
Stay with me, don't be yaraa (afraid); for he who seeks my napash (life) seeks your napash (life). For with me you shall be in safeguard.
Dawad was told, "Behold, the Palashathay (Philistines) are fighting against Qaiyalah, and are robbing the threshing floors.

Therefore Dawad inquired of Yahawah, saying, "Shall I yalak (go) and strike these Palashathay (Philistines)?" Yahawah said to Dawad, "yalak (go) strike the Palashathay (Philistines), and yashai (save) Qaiyalah.
Dawad men said to him, "Behold, we are yaraa (afraid) here in Yahawadah (Judah): how much more then if we yalak (go) to Qaiyalah against the mairakah (armies) of the Palashathay (Philistines)?
Then Dawad inquired of Yahawah yet again. Yahawah answered him, and said, "qawam (arise), yarad (go) down to Qaiyalah; for I will nathan (deliver) the Palashathay (Philistines) into your yad (hand).

Dawad and his men went to Qaiyalah, and fought with the Palashathay (Philistines), and brought away their livestock, and killed them with a gadawal (great) makah (slaughter). So Dawad saved the yashab (inhabitants) of Qaiyalah.
It happened, when Abayathar the ban (son) of Achayamalak fled to Dawad to Qaiyalah, that he came down with an apawad (ephod) in his yad (hand).
It was told Shaawal that Dawad had bawaa (come) to Qaiyalah. Shaawal said, "Alahayam has delivered him into my yad (hand); for he is shut in, by entering into a Iyar that has gates and bars.
Shaawal summoned all the im (people) to war, to yarad (go) down to Qaiyalah, to tzawar (besiege) Dawad and his men.
Dawad knew that Shaawal was devising rai (mischief) amar (against) him; and he said to Abayathar the kahan (priest), "Bring the apawad (ephod) here.
Then Dawad said, "O Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), your ibad (servant) has surely heard that Shaawal seeks to bawaa (come) to Qaiyalah, to shachath (destroy) the Iyar for my sake.

Will the men of Qaiyalah deliver me up into his yad (hand)? Will Shaawal yarad (come) down, as your ibad (servant) has heard? Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), I beg you, nagad (tell) your ibad (servant)." Yahawah said, "He will yarad (come) down.
Then Dawad said, "Will the men of Qaiyalah deliver me and my men into the yad (hand) of Shaawal?" Yahawah said, "They will deliver you up.

Then Dawad and his men, who were about shash (six) maah (hundred), qawam (arose) and departed out of Qaiyalah, and went wherever they could halak (go). It was told Shaawal that Dawad was escaped from Qaiyalah; and he gave up yatzaa (going) there.

Dawad stayed in the madabar (wilderness) in the strongholds, and remained in the har (hill) country in the madabar (wilderness) of Zayap. Shaawal sought him every yawam (day), but Alahayam didn't nathan (deliver) him into his yad (hand).
Dawad saw that Shaawal had yatzaa (come) out to seek his napash (life). Dawad was in the madabar (wilderness) of Zayap in the Charash.
Yahawanathan, Shaawal ban (son), qawam (arose), and went to Dawad into the Charash, and strengthened his yad (hand) in Alahayam.

He said to him, "Don't be yaraa (afraid); for the yad (hand) of Shaawal my ab (father) shall not matzaa (find) you; and you shall be malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel), and I shall be mashanah (next) to you; and that also Shaawal my ab (father) yadai (knows).
They shanayam (both) made a barayath (covenant) panayam (before) Yahawah: and Dawad stayed in the Charash, and Yahawanathan went to his bayath (house).

Then the Zayapay came up to Shaawal to Gabaih, saying, "Doesn't Dawad hide himself with us in the strongholds in the Charash, in the Gabaih of Chakayalah, which is on the yamayan (south) of the yashayamawan (desert)?
Now therefore, O malak (king), yarad (come) down, according to all the desire of your napash (soul) to yarad (come) down; and our part shall be to deliver him up into the malak (king's) yad (hand).
Shaawal said, "You are blessed by Yahawah; for you have had compassion on me.
Please yalak (go) kawan (make) yet more yadai (sure), and know and raah (see) his place where his ragal (haunt) is, and who has seen him there; for it is told me that he deals very subtly.

raah (see) therefore, and take yadai (knowledge) of all the lurking places where he hides himself, and shawab (turn back / repent) again to me with kawan (certainty), and I will halak (go) with you: and it shall happen, if he is in the aratz (land), that I will search him out among all the alap (thousands) of Yahawadah (Judah).

They qawam (arose), and went to Zayap panayam (before) Shaawal: but Dawad and his men were in the madabar (wilderness) of maiwan (maon), in the irabah (arabah) on the yamayan (south) of the yashayamawan (desert).

Shaawal and his men went to seek him. When Dawad was told, he went down to the salai (rock), and stayed in the madabar (wilderness) of maiwan (maon). When Shaawal heard that, he pursued Dawad in the madabar (wilderness) of maiwan (maon).

Shaawal went on this side of the har (mountain), and Dawad and his men on that side of the har (mountain): and Dawad made haste to yalak (get) away for panayam (fear) of Shaawal; for Shaawal and his men surrounded Dawad and his men to take them.
But a malaak (messenger) came to Shaawal, saying, "Hurry and yalak (come); for the Palashathay (Philistines) have made a raid on the aratz (land)!
So Shaawal returned from pursuing achar (after) Dawad, and went qaraah (against) the Palashathay (Philistines): therefore they called that place Salaihamachalaqawath Hammahlekoth.
Dawad went up from there, and lived in the strongholds of Iyanagaday Gedi.
It happened, when Shaawal was returned from following the Palashathay (Philistines), that it was told him, saying, "Behold, Dawad is in the madabar (wilderness) of Iyanagaday Gedi.
Then Shaawal took shalawash (three) alap (thousand) chosen men out of all Yasharaal (Israel), and went to seek Dawad and his men on the tzawar (rocks) of the wild goats.
He came Gadarah the sheep pens by the darak (way), where there was a cave; and Shaawal went in to relieve himself. Now Dawad and his men were yashab (abiding) in the innermost parts of the cave.

The men of Dawad said to him, "Behold, the yawam (day) of which Yahawah said to you, ‘Behold, I will nathan (deliver) your ayab (enemy) into your yad (hand), and you shall do to him as it shall seem yatab (good) to you.'" Then Dawad qawam (arose), and karath (cut) off the skirt of Shaawal robe secretly.
It happened afterward, that Dawad lab (heart) struck him, because he had karath (cut) off Shaawal skirt.

He said to his men, "Yahawah forbid that I should do this thing to my Adawan, yahawah (yahweh's) mashayach (anointed), to shalach (put) forth my yad (hand) against him, since he is yahawah (yahweh's) mashayach (anointed).
So Dawad checked his men with these dabar (words), and didn't allow them to qawam (rise) against Shaawal. Shaawal rose up out of the cave, and went on his darak (way).

Dawad also qawam (arose) afterward, and went out of the cave, and cried achar (after) Shaawal, saying, "My Adawan the malak (king)!" When Shaawal looked achar (behind) him, Dawad bowed with his ap (face) to the aratz (earth), and showed respect.
Dawad said to Shaawal, "Why do you listen to men's dabar (words), saying, ‘Behold, Dawad seeks your rai (hurt)?'

Behold, this yawam (day) your iyan (eyes) have seen how that Yahawah had delivered you today into my yad (hand) in the cave. Some urged me to harag (kill) you; but I spared you; and I said, I will not shalach (put) forth my yad (hand) against my Adawan; for he is Yahweh's mashayach (anointed).

Moreover, my ab (father), raah (see), yes, raah (see) the skirt of your robe in my yad (hand); for in that I karath (cut) off the skirt of your robe, and didn't harag (kill) you, yadai (know) and raah (see) that there is neither rai (evil) nor disobedience in my yad (hand), and I have not sinned against you, though you tzadah (hunt) for my napash (life) to take it.
May Yahawah shapat (judge) between me and you, and may Yahawah avenge me of you; but my yad (hand) shall not be on you.
As the proverb of the Qadamawanay amar (says), ‘Out of the rashai (wicked) yatzaa (comes) forth rashai (wickedness);' but my yad (hand) shall not be on you.
Against whom has the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) yatzaa (come) out? Whom do you pursue? A mawath (dead) dog? A flea?
May Yahawah therefore be dayan (judge), and give sentence between me and you, and raah (see), and rayab (plead) my rayab (cause), and deliver me out of your yad (hand).

It came to pass, when Dawad had made an kalah (end) of speaking these dabar (words) to Shaawal, that Shaawal said, "Is this your qawal (voice), my ban (son) Dawad?" Shaawal lifted up his qawal (voice), and wept.
He said to Dawad, "You are more tzadayaq (righteous) than I; for you have done tawab (good) to me, whereas I have done rai (evil) to you.
You have declared this yawam (day) how you have dealt tawab (well) with me, because when Yahawah had delivered me up into your yad (hand), you didn't harag (kill) me.

For if a ayash (man) matzaa (finds) his ayab (enemy), will he let him shalach (go) darak (away) unharmed? Therefore may Yahawah shalam (reward) you tawab (good) for that which you have done to me this yawam (day).
Now, behold, I yadai (know) that you shall malak (surely) be malak (king), and that the mamalakah (kingdom) of Yasharaal (Israel) shall be established in your yad (hand).

shabai (swear) now therefore to me by Yahawah, that you will not karath (cut) off my zarai (seed) achar (after) me, and that you will not destroy my sham (name) out of my ab (father's) bayath (house).
Dawad swore to Shaawal. Shaawal went bayath (home); but Dawad and his men went up to the stronghold.

Shamawaal died; and all Yasharaal (Israel) gathered themselves together, and lamented him, and buried him in his bayath (house) at Ramah. Dawad qawam (arose), and went down to the madabar (wilderness) of Paaran.

There was a ayash (man) in maiwan (maon), whose maishah (possessions) were in Karamal; and the ayash (man) was very gadawal (great), and he had shalawash (three) alap (thousand) sheep, and a alap (thousand) goats: and he was shearing his sheep in Karamal.

Now the sham (name) of the ayash (man) was Nabal; and the sham (name) of his ashah (wife) Abayagayal; and the ashah (woman) was of tawab (good) shakal (understanding), and of a Yapah thaar (face): but the ayash (man) was Qashah and rai (evil) in his mailal (doings); and he was of the kalabaw (house) of Caleb.
Dawad heard in the madabar (wilderness) that Nabal was shearing his sheep.
Dawad sent ishar (ten) nair (young) men, and Dawad said to the nair (young) men, "ilah (go) up to Karamal, and bawaa (go) to Nabal, and shaal (greet) him in my sham (name).
You shall amar (tell) him, ‘Long life to you! shalawam (peace) be to you, and shalawam (peace) be to your bayath (house), and shalawam (peace) be to all that you have.

Now I have heard that you have shearers. Your raih (shepherds) have now been with us, and we didn't kalam (hurt) them, neither was there anything missing from them, all the yawam (while) they were in Karamal.

shaal (ask) your nair (young) men, and they will nagad (tell) you. Therefore, let the nair (young) men matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (eyes); for we bawaa (come) in a tawab (good) yawam (day). Please nathan (give) whatever matzaa (comes) to your yad (hand), to your ibad (servants), and to your ban (son) Dawad.'
When Dawad nair (young) men came, they spoke to Nabal according to all those dabar (words) in the sham (name) of Dawad, and ceased.
Nabal answered Dawad ibad (servants), and said, "Who is Dawad? Who is the ban (son) of Yashay? There are many ibad (servants) who break away from their adawan (masters) these yawam (days).
Shall I then take my lacham (bread), and my mayam (water), and my meat that I have killed for my shearers, and nathan (give) it to men who I don't yadai (know) where they come from?
So Dawad nair (young) men turned on their darak (way), and went shawab (turn back / repent), and came and told him according to all these dabar (words).

Dawad said to his men, "Every anawash (man) put on his charab (sword)!" Every ayash (man) put on his charab (sword). Dawad also put on his charab (sword). About arabai (four) maah (hundred) men followed Dawad; and two maah (hundred) stayed by the baggage.

But one of the nair (young) men told Abayagayal, Nabal ashah (wife), saying, "Behold, Dawad sent malaak (messengers) out of the madabar (wilderness) to Greet our adawan (master); and he railed at them.
But the men were very tawab (good) to us, and we were not kalam (hurt), neither missed we anything, as yawam (long) as we went with them, when we were in the shadah (fields).
They were a wall to us both by layal (night) and by yawamam (day), all the yawam (while) we were with them keeping the sheep.

Now therefore yadai (know) and raah (see) what you will do; for rai (evil) is determined against our adawan (master), and against all his bayath (house); for he is such a worthless fellow that one can't dabar (speak) to him.

Then Abayagayal hurried and took two maah (hundred) loaves of bread, shanayam (two) bottles of yayan (wine), chamash (five) sheep ready ishah (dressed), chamash (five) measures of parched grain, one maah (hundred) clusters of raisins, and two maah (hundred) cakes of figs, and laid them on donkeys.
She said to her nair (young) men, "ibar (go) on panayam (before) me. Behold, I bawaa (come) achar (after) you." But she didn't nagad (tell) her ayash (husband), Nabal.
It was so, as she rode on her donkey, and came down by the covert of the har (mountain), that behold, Dawad and his men came down toward her; and she met them.

Now Dawad had said, "Surely in vain have I kept all that this fellow has in the madabar (wilderness), so that nothing was missed of all that pertained to him. He has returned me rai (evil) for tawab (good).
Alahayam do so to the ayab (enemies) of Dawad, and more also, if I shaar (leave) of all that belongs to him by the baqar (morning) awar (light) so much as shathan (one) who urinates on a wall.
When Abayagayal saw Dawad, she hurried, and alighted from her donkey, and napal (fell) ap (before) Dawad on her panayam (face), and bowed herself to the aratz (ground).
She napal (fell) at his feet, and said, "On me, my Adawan, on me be the iwan (iniquity); and please let your handmaid dabar (speak) in your ears. Hear the dabar (words) of your handmaid.

Please don't let my Adawan lab (regard) this worthless ayash (fellow), even Nabal; for as his sham (name) is, so is he. Nabal is his sham (name), and folly is with him; but I, your handmaid, didn't raah (see) the nair (young) men of my Adawan, whom you sent.

Now therefore, my Adawan, as Yahawah chay (lives), and as your napash (soul) chay (lives), since Yahawah has withheld you from dam (blood) guiltiness, and from yashai (avenging) yourself with your own yad (hand), now therefore let your ayab (enemies), and those who seek rai (evil) to my Adawan, be as Nabal.
Now this barakah (present) which your shapachah (servant) has brought to my Adawan, let it be given to the nair (young) men who halak (follow) my Adawan.

Please nashaa (forgive) the pashai (trespass) of your handmaid. For Yahawah will ishah (certainly) ishah (make) my Adawan a aman (sure) bayath (house), because my Adawan fights the battles of Yahawah; and rai (evil) shall not be found in you all your yawam (days).

Though men may qawam (rise) up to pursue you, and to seek your napash (soul), yet the napash (soul) of my Adawan shall be bound in the tzarawar (bundle) of chay (life) with Yahawah your Alahayam. He will sling out the napash (souls) of your ayab (enemies), as from the hollow of a sling.
It shall come to pass, when Yahawah has done to my Adawan according to all the tawab (good) that he has spoken concerning you, and shall have appointed you nagayad (prince) over Yasharaal (Israel),

that this shall be no grief to you, nor offense of lab (heart) to my Adawan, either that you have shed dam (blood) without cause, or that my Adawan has avenged himself. When Yahawah has dealt yatab (well) with my Adawan, then zakar (remember) your handmaid.
Dawad said Abayagayal Abigail, "Blessed is Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), who sent you this yawam (day) to qaraah (meet) me!
Blessed is your taim (discretion), and blessed are you, that have kept me this yawam (day) from dam (blood) guiltiness, and from yashai (avenging) myself with my own yad (hand).

For indeed, as Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), chay (lives), who has withheld me from hurting you, unless you had hurried and bawaa (come) to qaraah (meet) me, surely there wouldn't have been yathar (left) to Nabal by the baqar (morning) awar (light) so much as shathan (one) who urinates on a wall.

So Dawad received of her yad (hand) that which she had brought him: and he said to her, "ilah (go) up in shalawam (peace) to your bayath (house). raah (see), I have listened to your qawal (voice), and have granted your request.

Abayagayal came to Nabal; and behold, he held a feast in his bayath (house), like the feast of a malak (king). Nabal lab (heart) was tawab (merry) within him, for he was very drunken. Therefore she told him nothing, qatan (less) or more, until the baqar (morning) awar (light).

It happened in the baqar (morning), when the yayan (wine) was gone out of Nabal, that his ashah (wife) told him these things, and his lab (heart) died qarab (within) him, and he became as a aban (stone).
It happened about ishar (ten) yawam (days) after, that Yahawah struck Nabal, so that he died.

When Dawad heard that Nabal was mawath (dead), he said, "Blessed is Yahawah, who has pleaded the rayab (cause) of my reproach from the yad (hand) of Nabal, and has kept back his ibad (servant) from rai (evil). Yahawah has returned the evildoing of Nabal on his own raash (head)." Dawad sent and spoke Abayagayal Abigail, to take her to him as ashah (wife).
When the ibad (servants) of Dawad had bawaa (come) Abayagayal Abigail to Karamal, they spoke to her, saying, "Dawad has sent us to you, to take you to him as ashah (wife).
She qawam (arose), and bowed herself with her ap (face) to the aratz (earth), and said, "Behold, your handmaid is a shapachah (servant) to wash the feet of the shapachah (servants) of my Adawan.

Abayagayal hurried, and qawam (arose), and rode on a donkey, with chamash (five) ladies of hers who followed her; and she went ragal (after) the malaak (messengers) of Dawad, and became his ashah (wife).
Dawad also took Achayanaim of Yazaraial; and they shanayam (both) became his wives.
Now Shaawal had given Mayakal his bath (daughter), Dawad ashah (wife), to Palatay the ban (son) of Layash, who was of Galayam.
The Zayapay came to Shaawal to Gabaih, saying, "Doesn't Dawad hide himself in the Gabaih of Chakayalah, which is panayam (before) the yashayamawan (desert)?

Then Shaawal qawam (arose), and went down to the madabar (wilderness) of Zayap, having shalawash (three) alap (thousand) chosen men of Yasharaal (Israel) with him, to seek Dawad in the madabar (wilderness) of Zayap.

Shaawal encamped in the Gabaih of Chakayalah, which is panayam (before) the yashayamawan (desert), by the darak (way). But Dawad stayed in the madabar (wilderness), and he saw that Shaawal came achar (after) him into the madabar (wilderness).
Dawad therefore sent out spies, and understood that Shaawal had certainly bawaa (come).

Dawad qawam (arose), and came to the place where Shaawal had encamped; and Dawad saw the place where Shaawal shakab (lay), and Abanar the ban (son) of Nar, the shar (captain) of his tzabaa (army): and Shaawal shakab (lay) within the place of the wagons, and the im (people) were encamped around him.

Then answered Dawad and said to Achayamalak the Chathay (Hittite), and to Abayashay the ban (son) of Tzarawayah, ach (brother) to Yawaab, saying, "Who will yarad (go) down with me to Shaawal to the machanah (camp)?" Abayashay said, "I will yarad (go) down with you.

So Dawad and Abayashay came to the im (people) by layal (night): and, behold, Shaawal shakab (lay) sleeping within the place of the wagons, with his spear stuck in the aratz (ground) at his maraashah (head); and Abanar and the im (people) shakab (lay) around him.

Then Abayashay said to Dawad, "Alahayam has delivered up your ayab (enemy) into your yad (hand) this yawam (day). Now therefore please let me strike him with the spear to the aratz (earth) at one stroke, and I will not strike him the shanah (second) time.
Dawad said to Abayashay, "Don't shachath (destroy) him; for who can shalach (put) forth his yad (hand) against yahawah (yahweh's) mashayach (anointed), and be guiltless?
Dawad said, "As Yahawah chay (lives), Yahawah will nagap (strike) him; or his yawam (day) shall bawaa (come) to mawath (die); or he shall bawaa (go) down into battle and sapah (perish).

Yahawah forbid that I should shalach (put) forth my yad (hand) against yahawah (yahweh's) mashayach (anointed); but now please take the spear that is at his maraashah (head), and the jar of mayam (water), and let us yalak (go).

So Dawad took the spear and the jar of mayam (water) from Shaawal raashath (head); and they went yalak (away): and no man saw it, nor knew it, neither did any qawatz (awake); for they were all yashan (asleep), because a tharadamah (deep) sleep from Yahawah was fallen on them.
Then Dawad went over to the other ibar (side), and stood on the raash (top) of the har (mountain) Rachawaq off; a rab (great) space being between them;
and Dawad cried to the im (people), and to Abanar the ban (son) of Nar, saying, "Don't you answer, Abanar?" Then Abanar answered, "Who are you who qaraa (cries) to the malak (king)?

Dawad said to Abanar, "Aren't you a ayash (man)? Who is like you in Yasharaal (Israel)? Why then have you not kept watch over your Adawan, the malak (king)? For one of the im (people) came in to shachath (destroy) the malak (king) your Adawan.

This thing isn't tawab (good) that you have done. As Yahawah chay (lives), you are ban (worthy) to mawath (die), because you have not kept watch over your Adawan, yahawah (yahweh's) mashayach (anointed). Now raah (see) where the malak (king's) spear is, and the jar of mayam (water) that was at his maraashah (head).
Shaawal knew Dawad qawal (voice), and said, "Is this your qawal (voice), my ban (son) Dawad?" Dawad said, "It is my qawal (voice), my Adawan, O malak (king).
He said, "Why does my Adawan pursue achar (after) his ibad (servant)? For what have I done? Or what rai (evil) is in my yad (hand)?

Now therefore, please let my Adawan the malak (king) hear the dabar (words) of his ibad (servant). If it is so that Yahawah has stirred you up against me, let him rawach (accept) an manachah (offering). But if it is the children of men, they are cursed panayam (before) Yahawah; for they have driven me out this yawam (day) that I shouldn't cling to yahawah (yahweh's) nachalah (inheritance), saying, ‘yalak (go), ibad (serve) other Alahayam!'

Now therefore, don't let my dam (blood) napal (fall) to the aratz (earth) away from the panayam (presence) of Yahawah; for the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) has yatzaa (come) out to seek a flea, as when radap (one) hunts a partridge in the har (mountains).

Then Shaawal said, "I have sinned. shawab (turn back / repent), my ban (son) Dawad; for I will no more do you raii (harm), because my napash (life) was precious in your iyan (eyes) this yawam (day). Behold, I have played the sakal (fool), and have erred exceedingly.
Dawad answered, "Behold the spear, O malak (king)! Then let one of the nair (young) men ibar (come) over and get it.

Yahawah will shawab (turn back / repent) to every ayash (man) his tzadaqah (righteousness) and his amawanah (faithfulness); because Yahawah delivered you into my yad (hand) today, and I wouldn't shalach (put) forth my yad (hand) against yahawah (yahweh's) mashayach (anointed).

Behold, as your napash (life) was respected this yawam (day) in my iyan (eyes), so let my napash (life) be respected in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, and let him natzal (deliver) me out of all oppression.
Then Shaawal said to Dawad, "You are blessed, my ban (son) Dawad. You shall both do mightily, and shall surely yakal (prevail)." So Dawad went his darak (way), and Shaawal returned to his place.

Dawad said in his lab (heart), "I shall now sapah (perish) one yawam (day) by the yad (hand) of Shaawal. There is nothing tawab (better) for me than that I should malat (escape) into the aratz (land) of the Palashathay (Philistines); and Shaawal will despair of me, to seek me any more in all the borders of Yasharaal (Israel). So shall I malat (escape) out of his yad (hand).
Dawad qawam (arose), and passed over, he and the shash (six) maah (hundred) men who were with him, to Akayash the ban (son) of Maiwak, malak (king) of gath (gath).

Dawad lived with Akayash at gath (gath), he and his men, every anawash (man) with his bayath (household), even Dawad with his shanayam (two) wives, Achayanaim the Yazaraialayath, and Abayagayal the Karamalayath, Nabal ashah (wife).
It was told Shaawal that Dawad was fled to gath (gath): and he sought no more again for him.

Dawad said to Akayash, "If now I have found favor in your iyan (eyes), let them nathan (give) me a place in one of the Iyar in the shadah (country), that I may yashab (dwell) there. For why should your ibad (servant) yashab (dwell) in the mamalakah (royal) Iyar with you?
Then Akayash gave him Tzaqalag that yawam (day): why Tzaqalag pertains to the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah) to this yawam (day).
The number of the days that Dawad lived in the shadah (country) of the Palashathay (Philistines) was a yawam (full) year and arabai (four) chadash (months).

Dawad and his men went up, and made a raid on the Gashawaray (Geshurites), and the Gazaray, and the Imalaqay (Amalekites); for those were the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land), who were of old, as you bawaa (go) to Shawar, even to the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.

Dawad struck the aratz (land), and saved neither ayash (man) nor ashah (woman) chayah (alive), and took away the sheep, and the cattle, and the donkeys, and the camels, and the clothing; and he returned, and came to Akayash.

Akayash said, "Against whom have you made a raid today?" Dawad said, "Against the Nagab of Yahawadah (Judah), against the Nagab of the Yarachamaalay (Jerahmeelites), and against the Nagab of the Qayanay (Kenites).

Dawad saved neither ayash (man) nor ashah (woman) chayah (alive), to bawaa (bring) them to gath (gath), saying, "Lest they should nagad (tell) of us, saying, ‘Dawad this, and this has been his way all the yawam (time) he has lived in the shadah (country) of the Palashathay (Philistines).'
Akayash believed Dawad, saying, "He has made his im (people) Yasharaal (Israel) baash (utterly) to abhor him. Therefore he shall be my ibad (servant) iwalam (forever).

It happened in those yawam (days), that the Palashathay (Philistines) gathered their machanah (armies) together for tzabaa (warfare), to fight with Yasharaal (Israel). Akayash said to Dawad, "yadai (know) yadai (assuredly) that you shall yatzaa (go) out with me in the machanah (army), you and your men.
Dawad said to Akayash, "Kan you shall yadai (know) what your ibad (servant) will do." Akayash said to Dawad, "Therefore will I shawam (make) you my bodyguard for yawam (ever).

Now Shamawaal was mawath (dead), and all Yasharaal (Israel) had lamented him, and buried him in Ramah, even in his own Iyar. Shaawal had sawar (put) away those who had familiar awab (spirits), and the wizards, out of the aratz (land).
The Palashathay (Philistines) gathered themselves together, and came and encamped in Shawanam: and Shaawal gathered all Yasharaal (Israel) together, and they encamped in Galabai.
When Shaawal saw the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines), he was yaraa (afraid), and his lab (heart) trembled maad (greatly).
When Shaawal inquired of Yahawah, Yahawah didn't answer him, neither by chalawam (dreams), nor by awarayam (urim), nor by nabayaa (prophets).

Then Shaawal said to his ibad (servants), "Seek me a ashah (woman) who has a familiar awab (spirit), that I may yalak (go) to her, and inquire of her." His ibad (servants) said to him, "Behold, there is a ashah (woman) who has a familiar awab (spirit) at Iyanadaar.

Shaawal disguised himself, and Labash on other clothing, and went, he and shanayam (two) men with him, and they came to the ashah (woman) by layal (night): and he said, "Please divine to me by the familiar awab (spirit), and ilah (bring) me up whomever I shall amar (name) to you.

The ashah (woman) said to him, "Behold, you yadai (know) what Shaawal has done, how he has karath (cut) off those who have familiar awab (spirits), and the wizards, out of the aratz (land). Why then do you lay a snare for my napash (life), to cause me to mawath (die)?
Shaawal swore to her by Yahawah, saying, "As Yahawah chay (lives), no iwan (punishment) shall qarah (happen) to you for this thing.
Then the ashah (woman) said, "Whom shall I ilah (bring) up to you?" He said, "Bring Shamawaal up for me.
When the ashah (woman) saw Shamawaal, she cried with a gadawal (loud) qawal (voice); and the ashah (woman) spoke to Shaawal, saying, "Why have you deceived me? For you are Shaawal!
The malak (king) said to her, "Don't be yaraa (afraid). For what do you raah (see)?" The ashah (woman) said to Shaawal, "I raah (see) a Alahayam coming up out of the aratz (earth).

He said to her, "What does he look like?" She said, "An zaqan (old) ayash (man) ilah (comes) up. He is covered with a robe." Shaawal perceived that it was Shamawaal, and he bowed with his ap (face) to the aratz (ground), and showed respect.

Shamawaal said to Shaawal, "Why have you disturbed me, to ilah (bring) me up?" Shaawal answered, "I am very distressed; for the Palashathay (Philistines) make war against me, and Alahayam has sawar (departed) from me, and answers me no more, neither by nabayaa (prophets), nor by chalawam (dreams). Therefore I have called you, that you may yadai (make) known to me what I shall do.
Shamawaal said, "Why then do you shaal (ask) of me, since Yahawah has sawar (departed) from you and has become your adversary?
Yahawah has done to you as he spoke by me. Yahawah has torn the mamalakah (kingdom) out of your yad (hand), and given it to your neighbor, even to Dawad.
Because you didn't obey the qawal (voice) of Yahawah, and didn't ishah (execute) his charawan (fierce) ap (wrath) on Imalaq, therefore Yahawah has done this thing to you this yawam (day).

Moreover Yahawah will nathan (deliver) Yasharaal (Israel) also with you into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines); and tomorrow you and your ban (sons) will be with me. Yahawah will nathan (deliver) the machanah (army) of Yasharaal (Israel) also into the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

Then Shaawal napal (fell) immediately his full length on the aratz (earth), and was terrified, because of the dabar (words) of Shamawaal. There was no kach (strength) in him; for he had eaten no lacham (bread) all the yawam (day), nor all the layal (night).

The ashah (woman) came to Shaawal, and saw that he was very troubled, and said to him, "Behold, your handmaid has listened to your qawal (voice), and I have shawam (put) my napash (life) in my kap (hand), and have listened to your dabar (words) which you spoke to me.

Now therefore, please listen also to the qawal (voice) of your handmaid, and let me shawam (set) a morsel of lacham (bread) panayam (before) you; and akal (eat), that you may have kach (strength), when you yalak (go) on your darak (way).

But he refused, and said, I will not akal (eat). But his ibad (servants), together with the ashah (woman), constrained him; and he listened to their qawal (voice). So he qawam (arose) from the aratz (earth), and sat on the bed.
The ashah (woman) had a fattened calf in the bayath (house). She hurried and killed it; and she took flour, and kneaded it, and baked unleavened matzah (bread) of it.
She brought it panayam (before) Shaawal, and panayam (before) his ibad (servants); and they ate. Then they rose up, and went yalak (away) that layal (night).
Now the Palashathay (Philistines) gathered together all their machanah (armies) to Apaq: and the Yasharaal (Israelites) encamped by the spring which is in Yazaraial.
The lords of the Palashathay (Philistines) passed on by maah (hundreds), and by alap (thousands); and Dawad and his men passed on Acharawan the rear with Akayash.

Then the shar (princes) of the Palashathay (Philistines) said, "What about these ibaray (hebrews)?" Akayash said to the shar (princes) of the Palashathay (Philistines), "Isn't this Dawad, the ibad (servant) of Shaawal the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), who has been with me these yawam (days), or rather these Shanah, and I have found no fault in him yawam (since) he napal (fell) away to this yawam (day)?

But the shar (princes) of the Palashathay (Philistines) were qatzap (angry) with him; and the shar (princes) of the Palashathay (Philistines) said to him, "shawab (turn back / repent) the ayash (man) shawab (turn back / repent), that he may shawab (turn back / repent) back to his place where you have appointed him, and let him not yarad (go) down with us to battle, lest in the battle he become an shatan (adversary) to us. For with what should this fellow reconcile himself to his Adawan? Should it not be with the raash (heads) of these men?
Is not this Dawad, of whom they sang machalah (one) to another in dances, saying, ‘Shaawal has slain his alap (thousands), Dawad his rababah (ten) thousands?'

Then Akayash called Dawad, and said to him, "As Yahawah chay (lives), you have been yashar (upright), and your yatzaa (going) out and your coming in with me in the machanah (army) is tawab (good) in my iyan (sight); for I have not found rai (evil) in you since the yawam (day) of your coming to me to this yawam (day). Nevertheless, the lords don't favor you.
Therefore now shawab (turn back / repent), and yalak (go) in shalawam (peace), that you not rai (displease) the lords of the Palashathay (Philistines).

Dawad said to Akayash, "But what have I done? What have you found in your ibad (servant) so yawam (long) as I have been panayam (before) you to this yawam (day), that I may not bawaa (go) and fight against the ayab (enemies) of my Adawan the malak (king)?

Akayash answered Dawad, "I yadai (know) that you are tawab (good) in my iyan (sight), as an malaak (angel) of Alahayam. Notwithstanding the shar (princes) of the Palashathay (Philistines) have said, ‘He shall not ilah (go) up with us to the battle.'

Therefore now shakam (rise) up early in the baqar (morning) with the ibad (servants) of your Adawan who have bawaa (come) with you; and as soon as you are up shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and have awar (light), depart.

So Dawad rose up shakam (early), he and his men, to depart in the baqar (morning), to shawab (turn back / repent) into the aratz (land) of the Palashathay (Philistines). The Palashathay (Philistines) went up to Yazaraial.

It happened, when Dawad and his men had bawaa (come) to Tzaqalag on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), that the Imalaqay (Amalekites) had made a raid on the Nagab, and on Tzaqalag, and had struck Tzaqalag, and burned it with ash (fire),
and had taken captive the women and all who were therein, both qatan (small) and gadawal (great). They didn't mawath (kill) any, but carried them off, and went their darak (way).
When Dawad and his men came to the Iyar, behold, it was burned with ash (fire); and their wives, and their ban (sons), and their bath (daughters), were taken captive.
Then Dawad and the im (people) who were with him lifted up their qawal (voice) and wept, until they had no more kach (power) to weep.
Dawad shanayam (two) wives were taken captive, Achayanaim the Yazaraialayath, and Abayagayal the ashah (wife) of Nabal the Karamalay.

Dawad was maad (greatly) distressed; for the im (people) spoke of stoning him, because the napash (soul) of all the im (people) was grieved, every ayash (man) for his ban (sons) and for his bath (daughters): but Dawad strengthened himself in Yahawah his Alahayam.
Dawad said to Abayathar the kahan (priest), the ban (son) of Achayamalak, "Please bring me here the apawad (ephod)." Abayathar brought the apawad (ephod) to Dawad.

Dawad inquired of Yahawah, saying, "If I pursue achar (after) this gadawad (troop), shall I overtake them?" He answered him, "Pursue; for you shall surely overtake them, and shall natzal (without) fail natzal (recover) all.
So Dawad went, he and the shash (six) maah (hundred) men who were with him, and came to the nachal (brook) Bashawar, where those who were yathar (left) behind stayed.
But Dawad pursued, he and arabai (four) maah (hundred) men; for two maah (hundred) stayed behind, who were so faint that they couldn't ibar (go) over the nachal (brook) Bashawar.
They found an Egyptian in the shadah (field), and brought him to Dawad, and gave him lacham (bread), and he ate; and they gave him mayam (water) to shaqah (drink).

They gave him a piece of a cake of figs, and shanayam (two) clusters of raisins. when he had eaten, his rawach (spirit) came again to him; for he had eaten no lacham (bread), nor drunk any mayam (water), shalawash (three) yawam (days) and shalawash (three) layal (nights).

Dawad asked him, "To whom do you belong? Where are you from?" He said, "I am a nair (young) man of Matzaray, ibad (servant) to an Amalekite; and my adawan (master) left me, because shalawash (three) yawam (days) ago I fell chalah (sick).
