We made a raid on the Nagab of the Karathay (Cherethites), and on that which belongs to Yahawadah (Judah), and on the Nagab of Kalab; and we burned Tzaqalag with ash (fire).

Dawad said to him, "Will you yarad (bring) me down to this gadawad (troop)?" He said, "shabai (swear) to me by Alahayam that you will neither mawath (kill) me, am (nor) deliver me up into the yad (hands) of my adawan (master), and I will yarad (bring) you down to this gadawad (troop).

When he had brought him down, behold, they were spread around over all the aratz (ground), eating, drinking, and dancing, because of all the gadawal (great) spoil that they had taken out of the aratz (land) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and out of the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah).

Dawad struck them from the nashap (twilight) even to the evening of the next macharath (day). Not a ayash (man) of them escaped from there, except arabai (four) maah (hundred) nair (young) men, who rode on camels and fled.
Dawad recovered all that the Imalaq (Amalekites) had taken; and Dawad rescued his shanayam (two) wives.
There was nothing lacking to them, neither qatan (small) nor gadawal (great), neither ban (sons) nor bath (daughters), neither spoil, nor anything that they had taken to them. Dawad brought back all.
Dawad took all the flocks and the herds, which they drove panayam (before) those other livestock, and said, "This is Dawad spoil.

Dawad came to the two maah (hundred) men, who were so faint that they could not yalak (follow) Dawad, whom also they had made to stay at the nachal (brook) Bashawar; and they went yatzaa (forth) to qaraah (meet) Dawad, and to qaraah (meet) the im (people) who were with him. When Dawad came near to the im (people), he greeted them.

Then all the rai (wicked) men and base ayash (fellows), of those who went with Dawad, answered and said, "Because they didn't go with us, we will not nathan (give) them anything of the spoil that we have recovered, except to every ayash (man) his ashah (wife) and his children, that he may lead them away, and depart.
Then Dawad said, "You shall not do so, my ach (brothers), with that which Yahawah has given to us, who has preserved us, and delivered the gadawad (troop) that came against us into our yad (hand).
Who will listen to you in this dabar (matter)? For as his share is who goes down to the battle, so shall his share be who yashab (tarries) by the baggage: they shall share alike.
It was so from that yawam (day) forward, that he made it a chaq (statute) and an mashapat (ordinance) for Yasharaal (Israel) to this yawam (day).

When Dawad came to Tzaqalag, he sent of the spoil to the zaqan (elders) of Yahawadah (Judah), even to his rai (friends), saying, "Behold, a barakah (present) for you of the spoil of the ayab (enemies) of Yahawah.
He sent it to those who were in Bayathaal, and to those who were in Ramawath of the Nagab, and to those who were in Yathayar,
and to those who were in Irawair, and to those who were in Shapamawath, and to those who were in Ashathamai,
and Rakal those who were in Racal, and to those who were in the Iyar of the Yarachamaalay (Jerahmeelites), and to those who were in the Iyar of the Qayanay (Kenites),
and to those who were in Charamah, and Kawaraishan those who were in Borashan, and to those who were in Ithak,
and to those who were in Chabarawan, and to all the places where Dawad himself and his men used to stay.

Now the Palashathay (Philistines) fought against Yasharaal (Israel): and the men of Yasharaal (Israel) fled from panayam (before) the Palashathay (Philistines), and napal (fell) down Chalal on har (mount) Galabai.
The Palashathay (Philistines) followed hard on Shaawal and on his ban (sons); and the Palashathay (Philistines) killed Yahawanathan, and Abayanadab, and Malakayashawai, the ban (sons) of Shaawal.
The battle went hard against Shaawal, and the archers overtook him; and he was maad (greatly) distressed by reason of the archers.

Then Shaawal said to his armor bearer, "Draw your charab (sword), and thrust me through with it, lest these Iral bawaa (come) and thrust me through, and ilal (abuse) me!" But his armor bearer would not; for he was terrified. Therefore Shaawal took his charab (sword), and napal (fell) on it.
When his armor bearer saw that Shaawal was mawath (dead), he likewise napal (fell) on his charab (sword), and died with him.
So Shaawal died, and his shalawash (three) ban (sons), and his armor bearer, and all his men, that same yawam (day) together.

When the men of Yasharaal (Israel) who were on the other ibar (side) of the valley, and those who were ibar (beyond) the Yaradan, saw that the men of Yasharaal (Israel) fled, and that Shaawal and his ban (sons) were mawath (dead), they forsook the Iyar, and fled; and the Palashathay (Philistines) came and lived in them.
It happened on the next macharath (day), when the Palashathay (Philistines) came to strip the Chalal, that they found Shaawal and his shalawash (three) ban (sons) fallen on har (mount) Galabai.

They karath (cut) off his raash (head), and stripped off his armor, and sent into the aratz (land) of the Palashathay (Philistines) all around, to bashar (carry) the news to the bayath (house) of their itzab (idols), and to the im (people).
They shawam (put) his armor in the bayath (house) Ishatharawath the Ashtaroth; and they fastened his body to the wall of Bayathashaan Shan.
When the yashab (inhabitants) Yabash Jabesh Gilead heard concerning him that which the Palashathay (Philistines) had done to Shaawal,

all the chayal (valiant) men qawam (arose), and went all layal (night), and took the body of Shaawal and the bodies of his ban (sons) from the wall of Bayathashaan Shan; and they came Yabash Jabesh, and burnt them there.
They took their itzam (bones), and buried them under the tamarisk tree Yabash Jabesh, and fasted shabai (seven) yawam (days).
It happened achar (after) the mawath (death) of Shaawal, when Dawad was returned from the slaughter Imalaq the Amalekites, and Dawad had stayed shanayam (two) yawam (days) in Tzaqalag;

it happened on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), that behold, a ayash (man) came out of the machanah (camp) from Shaawal, with his clothes torn, and adamah (earth) on his raash (head): and so it was, when he came to Dawad, that he napal (fell) to the aratz (earth), and showed respect.
Dawad said to him, "Where do you bawaa (come) from?" He said to him, "I have escaped out of the machanah (camp) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Dawad said to him, "mah (how) did it go? Please nagad (tell) me." He answered, "The im (people) have fled from the battle, and many of the im (people) also have fallen and are mawath (dead); and Shaawal and Yahawanathan his ban (son) are mawath (dead) also.
Dawad said to the nair (young) man who told him, "How do you yadai (know) that Shaawal and Yahawanathan his ban (son) are mawath (dead)?
The nair (young) man who told him said, "As I happened by chance on har (mount) Galabai, behold, Shaawal was leaning on his spear; and behold, the chariots and the horsemen followed hard after him.
When he looked achar (behind) him, he saw me, and called to me. I answered, ‘Here I am.'
He said to me, ‘Who are you?' I answered him, ‘I am an Imalaqay (Amalekite).'
He said to me, ‘Please imad (stand) beside me, and mawath (kill) me; for anguish has taken hold of me, because my napash (life) is yet whole in me.'

So I stood beside him, and killed him, because I was yadai (sure) that he could not chayah (live) achar (after) that he had fallen. I took the nazar (crown) that was on his raash (head), and the bracelet that was on his zarawai (arm), and have brought them here to my Adawan.
Then Dawad took chazaq (hold) on his clothes, and tore them; and likewise all the men who were with him.

They mourned, and wept, and fasted until evening, for Shaawal, and for Yahawanathan his ban (son), and for the im (people) of Yahawah, and for the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); because they were fallen by the charab (sword).
Dawad said to the nair (young) man who told him, "Where are you from?" He answered, "I am the ban (son) of a foreigner, an Imalaqay (Amalekite).
Dawad said to him, "How were you not yaraa (afraid) to shalach (put) forth your yad (hand) to shachath (destroy) yahawah (yahweh's) mashayach (anointed)?
Dawad called one of the nair (young) men, and said, "Go near, and pagai (fall) on him." He struck him, so that he died.
Dawad said to him, "Your dam (blood) be on your raash (head); for your pah (mouth) has testified amar (against) you, saying, ‘I have slain yahawah (yahweh's) mashayach (anointed).'
Dawad lamented with this lamentation over Shaawal and over Yahawanathan his ban (son)
(and he commanded them to teach the children of Yahawadah (Judah) the song of the qashath (bow): behold, it is written in the book of Jashar):
"Your glory, Yasharaal (Israel), is Chalal on your bamah (high) places! How the gabawar (mighty) have fallen!

Don't nagad (tell) it in gath (gath). Don't bashar (publish) it in the streets of Ashaqalawan, lest the bath (daughters) of the Palashathay (Philistines) Shamach, lest the bath (daughters) of the Iral triumph.

You har (mountains) of Galabai, let there be no dew nor rain on you, neither shadah (fields) of tharawamah (offerings); For there the magan (shield) of the gabawar (mighty) was vilely cast away, The magan (shield) of Shaawal was not mashayach (anointed) with shaman (oil).
From the dam (blood) of the Chalal, from the fat of the gabawar (mighty), Yahawanathan qashath (bow) didn't shawag (turn) back. Shaawal charab (sword) didn't shawab (turn back / repent) empty.

Shaawal and Yahawanathan were lovely and Naiyam in their chay (lives). In their mawath (death), they were not divided. They were qalal (swifter) than eagles. They were gabar (stronger) than aray (lions).
You bath (daughters) of Yasharaal (Israel), weep over Shaawal, who Labash you in scarlet Idan, who ilah (put) iday (ornaments) of gold on your clothing.
How are the gabawar (mighty) fallen in the midst of the battle! Yahawanathan is Chalal on your bamah (high) places.
I am distressed for you, my ach (brother) Yahawanathan. You have been very pleasant to me. Your ahabah (love) to me was palaa (wonderful), passing the ahabah (love) of women.
How are the gabawar (mighty) fallen, and the weapons of war perished!

It happened achar (after) this, that Dawad inquired of Yahawah, saying, "Shall I ilah (go) up into any of the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah)?" Yahawah said to him, "ilah (go) up." Dawad said, "Where shall I ilah (go) up?" He said, "To Chabarawan.
So Dawad went up there, and his shanayam (two) wives also, Achayanaim the Yazaraialayath, and Abayagayal the ashah (wife) of Nabal the Karamalay.
Dawad brought up his men who were with him, every ayash (man) with his bayath (household). They lived in the Iyar of Chabarawan.

The men of Yahawadah (Judah) came, and there they mashach (anointed) Dawad malak (king) over the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah). They told Dawad, saying, "The men Yabash Jabesh Gilead were those who buried Shaawal.

Dawad sent malaak (messengers) to the men Yabash Jabesh Gilead, and said to them, "Blessed are you by Yahawah, that you have shown this chasad (kindness) to your Adawan, even to Shaawal, and have buried him.
Now may Yahawah show loving chasad (kindness) and truth to you. I also will reward you for this tawab (kindness), because you have done this thing.

Now therefore let your yad (hands) be chazaq (strong), and be ban (valiant); for Shaawal your Adawan is mawath (dead), and also the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) have mashach (anointed) me malak (king) over them.
Now Abanar the ban (son) of Nar, shar (captain) of Shaawal tzabaa (army), had taken Ayashabashath the ban (son) of Shaawal, and brought him over to Machanayam;
and he made him malak (king) over Galaid, and over the Ashawaray, and over Yazaraial, and over Aparayam, and over Banayamayan, and over all Yasharaal (Israel).

Ayashabashath, Shaawal ban (son), was arabaiyam (forty) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign) over Yasharaal (Israel), and he reigned shanayam (two) Shanah. But the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) followed Dawad.
The time that Dawad was malak (king) in Chabarawan over the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) was shabai (seven) Shanah and shash (six) chadash (months).
Abanar the ban (son) of Nar, and the ibad (servants) of Ayashabashath the ban (son) of Shaawal, went out from Machanayam to Gabaiwan.

Yawaab the ban (son) of Tzarawayah, and the ibad (servants) of Dawad, went out, and met them by the pool of Gabaiwan; and they sat down, the one on the one side of the pool, and the other on the other side of the pool.
Abanar said to Yawaab, "Please let the nair (young) men qawam (arise) and play panayam (before) us!" Yawaab said, "Let them qawam (arise)!
Then they qawam (arose) and went over by number: shanayam (twelve) for Banayamayan, and for Ayashabashath the ban (son) of Shaawal, and shanayam (twelve) of the ibad (servants) of Dawad.

They ayash (each) caught his opponent by the raash (head), and thrust his charab (sword) in his rai (fellow's) side; so they napal (fell) down together: therefore that place was called Chalaqathahatzarayam Hazzurim, which is in Gabaiwan.
The battle was very Qashah that yawam (day): and Abanar was beaten, and the men of Yasharaal (Israel), panayam (before) the ibad (servants) of Dawad.
The shalawash (three) ban (sons) of Tzarawayah were there, Yawaab, and Abayashay, and Ishahaal: and Ishahaal was as qal (light) of ragal (foot) as a shadah (wild) gazelle.
Ishahaal pursued achar (after) Abanar; and in going he didn't natah (turn) to the right yamayan (hand) nor to the shamaawal (left) from following Abanar.
Then Abanar looked achar (behind) him, and said, "Is it you, Ishahaal?" He answered, "It is I.

Abanar said to him, "natah (turn) aside to your right yamayan (hand) or to your shamaawal (left), and grab one of the nair (young) men, and take his armor." But Ishahaal would not sawar (turn) aside from following him.
Abanar said again to Ishahaal, "sawar (turn) aside from following me. Why should I strike you to the aratz (ground)? How then should I nashaa (hold) up my panayam (face) to Yawaab your ach (brother)?

However he refused to sawar (turn) aside. Therefore Abanar with the achar (back) end of the spear struck him in the body, so that the spear came out achar (behind) him; and he napal (fell) down there, and died in the same place. It happened, that as many as came to the place where Ishahaal napal (fell) down and died stood still.

But Yawaab and Abayashay pursued achar (after) Abanar: and the shamash (sun) went down when they had bawaa (come) to the Gabaih of Amah, that lies panayam (before) Gayach by the darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness) of Gabaiwan.
The children of Banayamayan gathered themselves together achar (after) Abanar, and became one band, and stood on the raash (top) of a Gabaih.

Then Abanar called to Yawaab, and said, "Shall the charab (sword) akal (devour) forever? Don't you yadai (know) that it will be Mar in the Acharawan end? How long shall it be then, before you ask the im (people) to shawab (turn back / repent) from following their ach (brothers)?
Yawaab said, "As Alahayam chay (lives), if you had not spoken, surely then in the baqar (morning) the im (people) would have gone ilah (away), and not ayash (each) followed his ach (brother).
So Yawaab blew the trumpet; and all the im (people) stood still, and pursued achar (after) Yasharaal (Israel) no more, neither fought they any more.
Abanar and his men went all that layal (night) through the irabah (arabah); and they passed over the Yaradan, and went through all Batharawan, and came to Machanayam.
Yawaab returned from following Abanar: and when he had gathered all the im (people) together, there lacked of Dawad ibad (servants) nineteen men and Ishahaal.
But the ibad (servants) of Dawad had struck of Banayamayan, and of Abanar men, so that shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty) men died.
They took up Ishahaal, and buried him in the tomb of his ab (father), which was in Bayathalacham. Yawaab and his men went all layal (night), and the awar (day) broke on them at Chabarawan.
Now there was Arak war between the bayath (house) of Shaawal and the bayath (house) of Dawad: and Dawad grew Chazaq and Chazaq, but the bayath (house) of Shaawal grew Dal and Dal.
To Dawad were ban (sons) yalad (born) in Chabarawan: and his firstborn was Amanawan, of Achayanaim the Yazaraialayath;

and his mashanah (second), Kalaab, Abayagayal Abigail the ashah (wife) of Nabal the Karamalay; and the shalayashay (third), Abayashalawam the ban (son) Maikah Maacah the bath (daughter) of Thalamay malak (king) of Gashawar;
and the rabayaiy (fourth), Adanayah the ban (son) of Chagayath; and the chamayashay (fifth), Shapatayah the ban (son) of Abayatal;
and the shashay (sixth), Yatharaim, of Igalah, Dawad ashah (wife). These were yalad (born) to Dawad in Chabarawan.
It happened, while there was war between the bayath (house) of Shaawal and the bayath (house) of Dawad, that Abanar made himself chazaq (strong) in the bayath (house) of Shaawal.
Now Shaawal had a concubine, whose sham (name) was Ratzapah, the bath (daughter) of Ayah: and Ishbosheth said to Abanar, "Why have you gone in to my ab (father's) concubine?

Then was Abanar very charah (angry) for the dabar (words) of Ayashabashath, and said, "Am I a dog's raash (head) that belongs to Yahawadah (Judah)? Today I show chasad (kindness) to the bayath (house) of Shaawal your ab (father), to his ach (brothers), and to his friends, and have not delivered you into the yad (hand) of Dawad; and yet you paqad (charge) me this yawam (day) with a iwan (fault) concerning this ashah (woman)!
Alahayam do so to Abanar, and more also, if, as Yahawah has sworn to Dawad, I don't do even so to him;

to transfer the mamalakah (kingdom) from the bayath (house) of Shaawal, and to qawam (set) up the kasaa (throne) of Dawad over Yasharaal (Israel) and over Yahawadah (Judah), Dan Dan Baarashabai to Beersheba.
He could not shawab (turn back / repent) Abanar another dabar (word), because he feared him.

Abanar sent malaak (messengers) to Dawad on his behalf, saying, "Whose is the aratz (land)?" and saying, "karath (make) your alliance with me, and behold, my yad (hand) shall be with you, to bring all Yasharaal (Israel) around to you.

He said, "tawab (good); I will karath (make) a treaty with you; but one thing I shaal (require) of you. That is, you shall not raah (see) my panayam (face), unless you first bawaa (bring) Mayakal, Shaawal bath (daughter), when you bawaa (come) to raah (see) my panayam (face).

Dawad sent malaak (messengers) to Ayashabashath, Shaawal ban (son), saying, "nathan (deliver) me my ashah (wife) Mayakal, whom I pledged to be married to me for one maah (hundred) foreskins of the Palashathay (Philistines).
Ayashabashath sent, and took her from her ayash (husband), even from Palatayaal the ban (son) of Lawash.
Her ayash (husband) went with her, weeping as he went, and followed her to Bacharayam. Then Abanar said to him, "yalak (go)! shawab (turn back / repent)!" and he returned.
Abanar had communication with the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "In thamawal (times) shalashawam (past), you sought for Dawad to be malak (king) over you.

Now then do it; for Yahawah has spoken of Dawad, saying, ‘By the yad (hand) of my ibad (servant) Dawad, I will yashai (save) my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel) out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and out of the yad (hand) of all their ayab (enemies).'

Abanar also spoke in the ears of Banayamayan: and Abanar went also to dabar (speak) in the ears of Dawad in Chabarawan all that seemed tawab (good) to Yasharaal (Israel), and to the whole bayath (house) of Banayamayan.
So Abanar came to Dawad to Chabarawan, and isharayam (twenty) men with him. Dawad made Abanar and the men who were with him a feast.

Abanar said to Dawad, "I will qawam (arise) and yalak (go), and will gather all Yasharaal (Israel) to my Adawan the malak (king), that they may karath (make) a barayath (covenant) with you, and that you may malak (reign) over all that your napash (soul) desires." Dawad sent Abanar shalach (away); and he went in shalawam (peace).

Behold, the ibad (servants) of Dawad and Yawaab came from a foray, and brought in a rab (great) spoil with them: but Abanar was not with Dawad in Chabarawan; for he had sent him shalach (away), and he was gone in shalawam (peace).

When Yawaab and all the tzabaa (army) who was with him had bawaa (come), they told Yawaab, saying, Abanar the ban (son) of Nar came to the malak (king), and he has sent him shalach (away), and he is gone in shalawam (peace).
Then Yawaab came to the malak (king), and said, "What have you done? Behold, Abanar came to you. Why is it that you have sent him shalach (away), and he is halak (quite) gone?
You yadai (know) Abanar the ban (son) of Nar, that he came to deceive you, and to yadai (know) your going out and your coming in, and to yadai (know) all that you do.

When Yawaab had yatzaa (come) out from Dawad, he sent malaak (messengers) achar (after) Abanar, and they brought him shawab (turn back / repent) from the bawar (well) of Sarah; but Dawad didn't yadai (know) it.

When Abanar was returned to Chabarawan, Yawaab took him natah (aside) into the midst of the gate to dabar (speak) with him quietly, and struck him there in the body, so that he died, for the dam (blood) of Ishahaal his ach (brother).
Afterward, when Dawad heard it, he said, "I and my mamalakah (kingdom) are naqay (guiltless) before Yahawah iwalam (forever) of the dam (blood) of Abanar the ban (son) of Nar.

Let it chawal (fall) on the raash (head) of Yawaab, and on all his ab (father's) bayath (house). Let there not karath (fail) from the bayath (house) of Yawaab zawab (one) who has an issue, or who is a leper, or who chazaq (leans) on a palak (staff), or who napal (falls) by the charab (sword), or who Chasar lacham (bread).
So Yawaab and Abayashay his ach (brother) killed Abanar, because he had killed their ach (brother) Ishahaal at Gabaiwan in the battle.
Dawad said to Yawaab, and to all the im (people) who were with him, Tear your clothes, and clothe yourselves with sackcloth, and mourn panayam (before) Abanar. malak (king) Dawad followed the bier.
They buried Abanar in Chabarawan: and the malak (king) lifted up his qawal (voice), and wept at the qabar (grave) of Abanar; and all the im (people) wept.
The malak (king) lamented for Abanar, and said, "Should Abanar mawath (die) as a nabal (fool) dies?

Your yad (hands) were not bound, nor your feet put into fetters. As a man napal (falls) panayam (before) the children of iwal (iniquity), so you napal (fell)." All the im (people) wept again over him.

All the im (people) came to cause Dawad to eat lacham (bread) while it was yet yawam (day); but Dawad swore, saying, "Alahayam do so to me, and more also, if I taste lacham (bread), or anything else, until the shamash (sun) goes down.
All the im (people) took notice of it, and it pleased them; as whatever the malak (king) did pleased all the im (people).
So all the im (people) and all Yasharaal (Israel) understood that yawam (day) that it was not of the malak (king) to mawath (kill) Abanar the ban (son) of Nar.
The malak (king) said to his ibad (servants), "Don't you yadai (know) that there a shar (prince) and a great gadawal (man) has fallen this yawam (day) in Yasharaal (Israel)?

I am this yawam (day) Rak, though mashach (anointed) malak (king); and these men the ban (sons) of Tzarawayah are too Qashah for me. May Yahawah shalam (reward) the evildoer according to his wickedness.
When Shaawal ban (son) heard that Abanar was mawath (dead) in Chabarawan, his yad (hands) became rapah (feeble), and all the Yasharaal (Israelites) were troubled.

Shaawal ban (son) had shanayam (two) men who were shar (captains) of gadawad (bands): the sham (name) of the one was Bainah, and the sham (name) of the other Rakab, the ban (sons) of Ramawan the Baarathay (Beerothite), of the children of Banayamayan (for Baarawath also is reckoned to Banayamayan:
and the Baarathay (Beerothites) fled to Gathayam, and have lived as foreigners there until this yawam (day)).

Now Yahawanathan, Shaawal ban (son), had a ban (son) who was Nakah of his feet. He was chamash (five) Shanah ban (old) when the news came of Shaawal and Yahawanathan out of Yazaraial; and his aman (nurse) took him up, and fled: and it happened, as she made haste to flee, that he napal (fell), and became Pasach. His sham (name) was Mapayabashath.

The ban (sons) of Ramawan the Baarathay (Beerothite), Rakab and Bainah, went, and came about the heat of the yawam (day) to the bayath (house) of Ayashabashath, as he took his mashakab (rest) at tzahar (noon).
They came there into the midst of the bayath (house), as though they would have fetched wheat; and they struck him in the body: and Rakab and Bainah his ach (brother) escaped.

Now when they came into the bayath (house), as he shakab (lay) on his bed in his bedroom, they struck him, and killed him, and beheaded him, and took his raash (head), and went by the darak (way) of the irabah (arabah) all layal (night).

They brought the raash (head) of Ayashabashath to Dawad to Chabarawan, and said to the malak (king), "Behold, the raash (head) of Ayashabashath, the ban (son) of Shaawal, your ayab (enemy), who sought your napash (life)! Yahawah has avenged my Adawan the malak (king) this yawam (day) of Shaawal, and of his zarai (seed).

Dawad answered Rakab and Bainah his ach (brother), the ban (sons) of Ramawan the Baarathay (Beerothite), and said to them, "As Yahawah chay (lives), who has padah (redeemed) my napash (soul) out of all tzarah (adversity),

when someone told me, ‘Behold, Shaawal is mawath (dead),' thinking to have brought bashar (good) news, I took achaz (hold) of him, and killed him in Tzaqalag, which was the reward I gave him for his news.

How much more, when rashai (wicked) men have slain a tzadayaq (righteous) ayash (person) in his own bayath (house) on his bed, shall I not now require his dam (blood) of your yad (hand), and bair (take) you away from the aratz (earth)?

Dawad tzawah (commanded) his nair (young) men, and they killed them, and cut off their yad (hands) and their feet, and hanged them up beside the pool in Chabarawan. But they took the raash (head) of Ayashabashath, and buried it in the qabar (grave) of Abanar in Chabarawan.
Then came all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) to Dawad to Chabarawan, and spoke, saying, "Behold, we are your itzam (bone) and your flesh.

In times past, when Shaawal was malak (king) over us, it was you who led out and brought in Yasharaal (Israel). Yahawah said to you, ‘You shall be raih (shepherd) of my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), and you shall be nagayad (prince) over Yasharaal (Israel).'

So all the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) came to the malak (king) to Chabarawan; and malak (king) Dawad made a barayath (covenant) with them in Chabarawan panayam (before) Yahawah; and they mashach (anointed) Dawad malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel).
Dawad was shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign), and he reigned arabaiyam (forty) Shanah.

In Chabarawan he reigned over Yahawadah (Judah) shabai (seven) Shanah and shash (six) chadash (months); and in Yarawashalam he reigned thirty-three Shanah over all Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah).

The malak (king) and his men went to Yarawashalam against the Yabawasay (Jebusites), the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land), who spoke to Dawad, saying, "Unless you sawar (take) away the iwar (blind) and the Pasach, you shall not bawaa (come) in here;" thinking, "Dawad can't bawaa (come) in here.
Nevertheless Dawad took the stronghold of Tzayawan; the same is the Iyar of Dawad.

Dawad said on that yawam (day), "Whoever strikes the Yabawasay (Jebusites), let him nagai (get) up to the watercourse, and strike the Pasach and the iwar (blind), who are hated by Dawad napash (soul)." Therefore they amar (say), "The iwar (blind) and the Pasach can't bawaa (come) into the bayath (house).
Dawad lived in the stronghold, and called it the Iyar of Dawad. Dawad built around from Malawaa and inward.
Dawad grew greater and halak (greater); for Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies), was with him.
Chayaram malak (king) of Tzar sent malaak (messengers) to Dawad, and cedar itz (trees), and carpenters, and masons; and they built Dawad a bayath (house).
Dawad perceived that Yahawah had established him malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel), and that he had exalted his mamalakah (kingdom) for his im (people) Yasharaal sake.
Dawad took him more concubines and wives out of Yarawashalam, achar (after) he had bawaa (come) from Chabarawan; and there were yet ban (sons) and bath (daughters) yalad (born) to Dawad.
These are the sham (names) of those who were Yalawad to him in Yarawashalam: Shamawai, and Shawabab, and Nathan, and Shalamah,
and Yabachar, and Alayashawai, and Napag, and Yapayai,
and Alayashamai, and Alayadai, and Alayapalat.

When the Palashathay (Philistines) heard that they had mashach (anointed) Dawad malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel), all the Palashathay (Philistines) went up to seek Dawad; and Dawad heard of it, and went down to the stronghold.
Now the Palashathay (Philistines) had bawaa (come) and spread themselves in the valley of Rapaa (Rephaim).

Dawad inquired of Yahawah, saying, "Shall I ilah (go) up against the Palashathay (Philistines)? Will you nathan (deliver) them into my yad (hand)?" Yahawah said to Dawad, "ilah (go) up; for I will certainly nathan (deliver) the Palashathay (Philistines) into your yad (hand).

Dawad came to Baal Perazim, and Dawad struck them there; and he said, "Yahawah has broken my ayab (enemies) panayam (before) me, like the breach of mayam (waters)." Therefore he called the sham (name) of that place Baal Perazim.
They left their itzab (images) there; and Dawad and his men took them nashaa (away).
The Palashathay (Philistines) came up yet again, and spread themselves in the valley of Rapaa (Rephaim).
When Dawad inquired of Yahawah, he said, "You shall not ilah (go) up. Circle around achar (behind) them, and attack them over against the mulberry trees.

It shall be, when you hear the qawal (sound) of marching in the raash (tops) of the mulberry trees, that then you shall stir yourself up; for then Yahawah has gone out panayam (before) you to strike the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines).
Dawad did so, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) him, and struck the Palashathay (Philistines) from Gabai until you bawaa (come) to Gazar.
Dawad again gathered asap (together) all the chosen men of Yasharaal (Israel), shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand).

Dawad qawam (arose), and went with all the im (people) who were with him, from Bailayayahawadah Judah, to ilah (bring) up from there the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, which is called by the sham (name), even the sham (name) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) who yashab (sits) above the karawab (cherubim).

They set the arawan (ark) of Alahayam on a Chadash cart, and brought it out of the bayath (house) of Abayanadab that was in the Gabaih: and Izaa and Achayaw, the ban (sons) of Abayanadab, drove the Chadash cart.
They brought it out of the bayath (house) of Abayanadab, which was in the Gabaih, with the arawan (ark) of Alahayam: and Achayaw went panayam (before) the arawan (ark).

Dawad and all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) played panayam (before) Yahawah with all kinds of instruments made of fir itz (wood), and with harps, and with stringed instruments, and with tambourines, and with castanets, and with cymbals.
When they came to the threshing Nakawan of Nacon, Izaa reached for the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, and took achaz (hold) of it; for the cattle stumbled.
The ap (anger) of Yahawah was kindled against Izaa; and Alahayam struck him there for his error; and there he died by the arawan (ark) of Alahayam.
Dawad was charah (displeased), because Yahawah had broken forth on Izaa; and he called that place Perez Izaa, to this yawam (day).
Dawad was yaraa (afraid) of Yahawah that yawam (day); and he said, "How shall the arawan (ark) of Yahawah bawaa (come) to me?
So Dawad would not move the arawan (ark) of Yahawah to be with him in the Iyar of Dawad; but Dawad carried it natah (aside) into the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam the Gathay (Gittite).
The arawan (ark) of Yahawah remained in the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam the Gathay (Gittite) shalawash (three) chadash (months): and Yahawah blessed Ibadaadawam, and all his bayath (house).

It was told malak (king) Dawad, saying, "Yahawah has blessed the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam, and all that pertains to him, because of the arawan (ark) of Alahayam." Dawad went and brought up the arawan (ark) of Alahayam from the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam into the Iyar of Dawad with joy.
It was so, that, when those who bore the arawan (ark) of Yahawah had gone shash (six) paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf.
Dawad danced panayam (before) Yahawah with all his might; and Dawad was clothed in a linen apawad (ephod).
So Dawad and all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) brought up the arawan (ark) of Yahawah with shouting, and with the qawal (sound) of the trumpet.

It was so, as the arawan (ark) of Yahawah came into the Iyar of Dawad, that Mayakal the bath (daughter) of Shaawal looked out at the window, and saw malak (king) Dawad leaping and dancing panayam (before) Yahawah; and she despised him in her lab (heart).

They brought in the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, and set it in its place, in the midst of the ahal (tent) that Dawad had pitched for it; and Dawad offered burnt ilah (offerings) and peace ilah (offerings) panayam (before) Yahawah.
When Dawad had made an kalah (end) of offering the burnt ilah (offering) and the shalam (peace) offerings, he blessed the im (people) in the sham (name) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).

He gave to all the im (people), even among the whole multitude of Yasharaal (Israel), both to men and women, to everyone a portion of lacham (bread), dates, and raisins. So all the im (people) departed everyone to his bayath (house).

Then Dawad returned to barak (bless) his bayath (household). Mayakal the bath (daughter) of Shaawal came out to qaraah (meet) Dawad, and said, "How kabad (glorious) the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) was today, who uncovered himself today in the iyan (eyes) of the handmaids of his ibad (servants), as one of the rayaq (vain) fellows galah (shamelessly) galah (uncovers) himself!

Dawad said to Mayakal, "It was panayam (before) Yahawah, who chose me above your ab (father), and above all his bayath (house), to tzawah (appoint) me nagayad (prince) over the im (people) of Yahawah, over Yasharaal (Israel). Therefore will I celebrate panayam (before) Yahawah.
I will be yet more qalal (vile) than this, and will be Shapal in my own iyan (sight). But of the handmaids of whom you have spoken, they shall honor me.
Mayakal the bath (daughter) of Shaawal had no child to the yawam (day) of her mawath (death).
It happened, when the malak (king) lived in his bayath (house), and Yahawah had given him nawach (rest) from all his ayab (enemies) all around,
that the malak (king) said to Nathan the nabayaa (prophet), "raah (see) now, I yashab (dwell) in a bayath (house) of cedar, but the arawan (ark) of Alahayam yashab (dwells) within curtains.
Nathan said to the malak (king), "yalak (go), do all that is in your labab (heart); for Yahawah is with you.
It happened the same layal (night), that the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Nathan, saying,
"yalak (go) and amar (tell) my ibad (servant) Dawad, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "Shall you banah (build) me a bayath (house) for me to yashab (dwell) in?

For I have not lived in a bayath (house) since the yawam (day) that I brought up the children of Yasharaal (Israel) out of Matzarayam, even to this yawam (day), but have moved around in a ahal (tent) and in a mashakan (tabernacle).

In all halak (places) in which I have walked with all the children of Yasharaal (Israel), did I dabar (say) a dabar (word) to any of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), whom I tzawah (commanded) to be raih (shepherd) of my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), saying, ‘Why have you not built me a bayath (house) of cedar?'"'

Now therefore you shall amar (tell) my ibad (servant) Dawad this, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "I took you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep, that you should be nagayad (prince) over my im (people), over Yasharaal (Israel).

I have been with you wherever you went, and have karath (cut) off all your ayab (enemies) from panayam (before) you. I will ishah (make) you a gadawal (great) sham (name), like the sham (name) of the gadawal (great) ones who are in the aratz (earth).

I will shawam (appoint) a place for my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), and will plant them, that they may shakan (dwell) in their own place, and be moved no more; neither shall the children of iwal (wickedness) afflict them any more, as at the raashawan (first),

and as from the yawam (day) that I tzawah (commanded) shapat (judges) to be over my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel). I will cause you to nawach (rest) from all your ayab (enemies). Moreover Yahawah nagad (tells) you that Yahawah will make you a bayath (house).

When your yawam (days) are fulfilled, and you shall sleep with your abawath (fathers), I will qawam (set) up your zarai (seed) achar (after) you, who shall yatzaa (proceed) out of your maih (bowels), and I will kawan (establish) his mamalakah (kingdom).
He shall banah (build) a bayath (house) for my sham (name), and I will kawan (establish) the kasaa (throne) of his mamalakah (kingdom) iwalam (forever).
I will be his ab (father), and he shall be my ban (son). If he commits iwah (iniquity), I will yakach (chasten) him with the shabat (rod) of men, and with the nagai (stripes) of the children of men;
but my loving chasad (kindness) shall not sawar (depart) from him, as I took it from Shaawal, whom I sawar (put) away panayam (before) you.
Your bayath (house) and your mamalakah (kingdom) shall be made sure iwalam (forever) panayam (before) you. Your kasaa (throne) shall be established iwalam (forever)."'
According to all these dabar (words), and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to Dawad.
Then Dawad the malak (king) went in, and sat panayam (before) Yahawah; and he said, "Who am I, Adanay Yahawah, and what is my bayath (house), that you have brought me thus far?

This was yet a small thing in your iyan (eyes), Adanay Yahawah; but you have spoken also of your ibad (servant's) bayath (house) for a Rachawaq while to come; and this after the thawarah (way) of men, Adanay Yahawah!
What more can Dawad dabar (say) to you? For you yadai (know) your ibad (servant), Adanay Yahawah.
For your dabar (word's) sake, and according to your own lab (heart), you have worked all this greatness, to make your ibad (servant) yadai (know) it.
Therefore you are great, Yahawah Alahayam. For there is none like you, neither is there any Alahayam zawalah (besides) you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

What one gaway (nation) in the aratz (earth) is like your im (people), even like Yasharaal (Israel), whom Alahayam went to padah (redeem) to himself for a im (people), and to shawam (make) himself a sham (name), and to do great things for you, and awesome things for your aratz (land), panayam (before) your im (people), whom you padah (redeem) to yourself out of Matzarayam, from the gaway (nations) and their Alahayam?
You established for yourself your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel) to be a im (people) to you iwalam (forever); and you, Yahawah, became their Alahayam.
Now, Yahawah Alahayam, the dabar (word) that you have spoken concerning your ibad (servant), and concerning his bayath (house), qawam (confirm) it iwalam (forever), and do as you have spoken.

Let your sham (name) be magnified iwalam (forever), saying, ‘Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) is Alahayam over Yasharaal (Israel); and the bayath (house) of your ibad (servant) Dawad shall be established panayam (before) you.'

For you, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), have revealed to your ibad (servant), saying, ‘I will banah (build) you a bayath (house).' Therefore your ibad (servant) has found in his lab (heart) to palal (pray) this prayer to you.
"Now, O Adanay Yahawah, you are Alahayam, and your dabar (words) are truth, and you have promised this tawab (good) thing to your ibad (servant).

Now therefore let it please you to barak (bless) the bayath (house) of your ibad (servant), that it may continue iwalam (forever) panayam (before) you; for you, Adanay Yahawah, have spoken it. Let the bayath (house) of your ibad (servant) be blessed iwalam (forever) with your barakah (blessing).
achar (after) this it happened that Dawad struck the Palashathay (Philistines), and subdued them: and Dawad took the bridle of the mother city out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).

He struck Mawaab, and measured them with the line, making them to shakab (lie) down on the aratz (ground); and he measured shanayam (two) lines to put to mawath (death), and malaa (one) full line to chayah (keep) alive. The Mawaab (Moabites) became ibad (servants) to Dawad, and brought tribute.
Dawad struck also Hadadaizar the ban (son) of Rachab, malak (king) of Tzawabaa, as he went to shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (dominion) Parath the nahar (river).

Dawad took from him one alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) horsemen, and isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) footmen: and Dawad hamstrung all the chariot horses, but reserved of them for one maah (hundred) chariots.
When the Aram (Syrians) of Damashaq came to help Hadadaizar malak (king) of Tzawabaa, Dawad struck of the Aram (Syrians) shanayam (two) and isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) men.
Then Dawad shawam (put) garrisons in Aram of Damashaq; and the Aram (Syrians) became ibad (servants) to Dawad, and brought tribute. Yahawah gave yashai (victory) to Dawad wherever he went.
Dawad took the shalat (shields) of gold that were on the ibad (servants) of Hadadaizar, and brought them to Yarawashalam.
From Batach and from Barawathah, Iyar of Hadadaizar, malak (king) Dawad took maad (exceeding) much brass.
When Thaiw malak (king) of Chamath heard that Dawad had struck all the chayal (army) of Hadadaizar,

then Thaiw sent Yawaram his ban (son) to malak (king) Dawad, to shaal (greet) him, and to barak (bless) him, because he had fought against Hadadaizar and struck him: for Hadadaizar had wars with Thaiw. Joram brought with him vessels of kasap (silver), and vessels of gold, and vessels of brass:
malak (king) Dawad also dedicated these to Yahawah, with the kasap (silver) and gold that he dedicated of all the gawayam (nations) which he subdued;
of Aram, and of Mawaab, and of the children of Imawan, and of the Palashathay (Philistines), and of Imalaq, and of the spoil of Hadadaizar, ban (son) of Rachab, malak (king) of Tzawabaa.
Dawad earned a reputation when he returned from smiting the Aram (Syrians) in the Gayaa of Malach, even eighteen alap (thousand) men.
He shawam (put) garrisons in Adam; throughout all Adam shawam (put) he garrisons, and all the Adam (Edomites) became ibad (servants) to Dawad. Yahawah gave yashai (victory) to Dawad wherever he went.
Dawad reigned over all Yasharaal (Israel); and Dawad executed tzadaqah (justice) and righteousness to all his im (people).
Yawaab the ban (son) of Tzarawayah was over the tzabaa (army); and Yahawashapat the ban (son) of Achayalawad was zakar (recorder);
and Tzadawaq the ban (son) of Achayatawab, and Achayamalak the ban (son) of Abayathar, were kahan (priests); and Sharayah was scribe;
and Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai was over the Karathay (Cherethites) and the Palathay (Pelethites); and Dawad ban (sons) were kahan (chief) ministers.
Dawad said, "Is there yet any who is yathar (left) of the bayath (house) of Shaawal, that I may show him chasad (kindness) for Yahawanathan sake?

There was of the bayath (house) of Shaawal a ibad (servant) whose sham (name) was Tzayabaa, and they called him to Dawad; and the malak (king) said to him, "Are you Tzayabaa?" He said, "Your ibad (servant) is he.

The malak (king) said, "Is there not yet any of the bayath (house) of Shaawal, that I may show the chasad (kindness) of Alahayam to him?" Tzayabaa said to the malak (king), "Yahawanathan has yet a ban (son), who is Nakah of his feet.
The malak (king) said to him, "Where is he?" Tzayabaa said to the malak (king), "Behold, he is in the bayath (house) of Makayar the ban (son) of Imayaal, Laadabar Lo Debar.
Then malak (king) Dawad sent, and fetched him out of the bayath (house) of Makayar the ban (son) of Imayaal, Laadabar Lo Debar.

Mapayabashath, the ban (son) of Yahawanathan, the ban (son) of Shaawal, came to Dawad, and napal (fell) on his panayam (face), and showed respect. Dawad said, "Mapayabashath." He answered, "Behold, your ibad (servant)!

Dawad said to him, "Don't be yaraa (afraid) of him; for I will ishah (surely) show you chasad (kindness) for Yahawanathan your ab (father's) sake, and will shawab (turn back / repent) to you all the shadah (land) of Shaawal your ab (father). You shall akal (eat) lacham (bread) at my table continually.
He bowed down, and said, "What is your ibad (servant), that you should panah (look) on such a mawath (dead) dog as I am?
Then the malak (king) called to Tzayabaa, Shaawal nair (servant), and said to him, "All that pertained to Shaawal and to all his bayath (house) have I given to your adawan (master's) ban (son).

You shall ibad (till) the adamah (land) for him, you, and your ban (sons), and your ibad (servants); and you shall bawaa (bring) in the harvest, that your adawan (master's) ban (son) may have lacham (bread) to akal (eat): but Mapayabashath your adawan (master's) ban (son) shall akal (eat) lacham (bread) always at my table." Now Tzayabaa had chamash (fifteen) ban (sons) and isharayam (twenty) ibad (servants).

Then Tzayabaa said to the malak (king), "According to all that my Adawan the malak (king) tzawah (commands) his ibad (servant), so your shall ibad (servant) do." So Mapayabashath ate at the shalachan (king's) table, like one of the malak (king's) ban (sons).
Mapayabashath had a qatan (young) ban (son), whose sham (name) was Mayakaa. All that lived in the bayath (house) of Tzayabaa were ibad (servants) to Mapayabashath.
So Mapayabashath lived in Yarawashalam; for he ate continually at the malak (king's) table. He was Pasach in shanayam (both) his feet.
It happened achar (after) this, that the malak (king) of the children of Imawan died, and Chanawan his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Dawad said, "I will show chasad (kindness) to Chanawan the ban (son) of Nachash, as his ab (father) showed chasad (kindness) to me." So Dawad sent by his ibad (servants) to nacham (comfort) him concerning his ab (father). Dawad ibad (servants) came into the aratz (land) of the children of Imawan.

But the shar (princes) of the children of Imawan said to Chanawan their Adawan, "Do you iyan (think) that Dawad honors your ab (father), in that he has sent comforters to you? Hasn't Dawad sent his ibad (servants) to you to search the Iyar, and to spy it out, and to hapak (overthrow) it?

So Chanawan took Dawad ibad (servants), and shaved off the one chatzay (half) of their beards, and karath (cut) off their garments in the chatzay (middle), even to their buttocks, and sent them shalach (away).

When they told it to Dawad, he sent to qaraah (meet) them; for the men were maad (greatly) kalam (ashamed). The malak (king) said, "Wait at Yarayachaw until your beards have grown, and then shawab (turn back / repent).

When the children of Imawan saw that they were become baash (odious) to Dawad, the children of Imawan sent and hired the Aram (Syrians) of Bayatharachawab Rehob, and the Aram (Syrians) of Tzawabaa, isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) footmen, and the malak (king) Maikah Maacah with one alap (thousand) men, and the men of Tob ishar (twelve) alap (thousand) men.
When Dawad heard of it, he sent Yawaab, and all the tzabaa (army) of the gabawar (mighty) men.

The children of Imawan came out, and put the battle in array at the entrance of the gate: and the Aram (Syrians) of Tzawabaa and of Rachab, and the Maikah of Tob and Maacah, were by themselves in the shadah (field).
Now when Yawaab saw that the battle was set panayam (against) him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Yasharaal (Israel), and put them in array qaraah (against) the Aram (Syrians):
The yathar (rest) of the im (people) he committed into the yad (hand) of Abayashay his ach (brother); and he put them in array qaraah (against) the children of Imawan.

He said, "If the Aram (Syrians) are too chazaq (strong) for me, then you shall yashawaih (help) me; but if the children of Imawan are too chazaq (strong) for you, then I will halak (come) and yashai (help) you.
Be courageous, and let us be chazaq (strong) for our im (people), and for the Iyar of our Alahayam; and Yahawah do that which seems tawab (good) to him.
So Yawaab and the im (people) who were with him drew near to the battle against the Aram (Syrians): and they fled panayam (before) him.

When the children of Imawan saw that the Aram (Syrians) had fled, they likewise fled panayam (before) Abayashay, and entered into the Iyar. Then Yawaab returned from the children of Imawan, and came to Yarawashalam.
When the Aram (Syrians) saw that they were defeated by Yasharaal (Israel), they gathered themselves together.

Hadadezer sent, and brought out the Aram (Syrians) who were ibar (beyond) the nahar (river): and they came to Chayalam, with Shawabak the shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army) of Hadadezer at their head.

It was told Dawad; and he gathered all Yasharaal (Israel) asap (together), and passed over the Yaradan, and came to Chayalam. The Aram (Syrians) set themselves in array qaraah (against) Dawad, and fought with him.

The Aram (Syrians) fled panayam (before) Yasharaal (Israel); and Dawad killed of the Aram (Syrians) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) charioteers, and arabaiyam (forty) alap (thousand) horsemen, and struck Shawabak the shar (captain) of their tzabaa (army), so that he died there.

When all the malak (kings) who were ibad (servants) to Hadadezer saw that they were defeated panayam (before) Yasharaal (Israel), they made shalam (peace) with Yasharaal (Israel), and served them. So the Aram (Syrians) feared to yashai (help) the children of Imawan any more.

It happened, at the thashawabah (return) of the Shanah, at the ith (time) when malak (kings) yatzaa (go) out, that Dawad sent Yawaab, and his ibad (servants) with him, and all Yasharaal (Israel); and they destroyed the children of Imawan, and besieged Rabah. But Dawad stayed at Yarawashalam.

It happened at evening, that Dawad qawam (arose) from off his bed, and walked on the roof of the malak (king's) bayath (house): and from the roof he saw a ashah (woman) bathing; and the ashah (woman) was very tawab (beautiful) to look on.
Dawad sent and inquired after the ashah (woman). One said, "Isn't this Bathashabai, the bath (daughter) of Alayaim, the ashah (wife) of Awarayah the Chathay (Hittite)?
Dawad sent malaak (messengers), and took her; and she came in to him, and he shakab (lay) with her (for she was purified from her tamaah (uncleanness)); and she returned to her bayath (house).
The ashah (woman) conceived; and she sent and told Dawad, and said, "I am with harah (child).
Dawad sent to Yawaab, "shalach (send) me Awarayah the Chathay (Hittite)." Yawaab sent Awarayah to Dawad.
When Awarayah had bawaa (come) to him, Dawad asked of him how Yawaab did, and how the im (people) fared, and how the war prospered.

Dawad said to Awarayah, "yarad (go) down to your bayath (house), and wash your feet." Awarayah departed out of the malak (king's) bayath (house), and a mashaath (gift) from the malak (king) was sent achar (after) him.
But Awarayah slept at the door of the malak (king's) bayath (house) with all the ibad (servants) of his Adawan, and didn't yarad (go) down to his bayath (house).

When they had told Dawad, saying, "Awarayah didn't yarad (go) down to his bayath (house)," Dawad said to Awarayah, "Haven't you bawaa (come) from a darak (journey)? Why didn't you yarad (go) down to your bayath (house)?

Awarayah said to Dawad, "The arawan (ark), Yasharaal (Israel), and Yahawadah (Judah), are staying in sakah (tents); and my Adawan Yawaab, and the ibad (servants) of my Adawan, are encamped in the panayam (open) shadah (field). Shall I then bawaa (go) into my bayath (house) to akal (eat) and to drink, and to shakab (lie) with my ashah (wife)? As you chay (live), and as your napash (soul) chay (lives), I will not do this thing!
Dawad said to Awarayah, "Stay here today also, and tomorrow I will let you depart." So Awarayah stayed in Yarawashalam that yawam (day), and the next yawam (day).

When Dawad had called him, he ate and drink panayam (before) him; and he made him Shakar. At evening, he went out to shakab (lie) on his bed with the ibad (servants) of his Adawan, but didn't yarad (go) down to his bayath (house).
It happened in the baqar (morning), that Dawad wrote a letter to Yawaab, and sent it by the yad (hand) of Awarayah.
He wrote in the letter, saying, "Send Awarayah to the panayam (forefront) of the chazaq (hottest) battle, and retreat from him, that he may be struck, and mawath (die).
It happened, when Yawaab kept shamar (watch) on the Iyar, that he assigned Awarayah to the place where he knew that chayal (valiant) men were.
The men of the Iyar went out, and fought with Yawaab. Some of the im (people) napal (fell), even of the ibad (servants) of Dawad; and Awarayah the Chathay (Hittite) died also.
Then Yawaab sent and told Dawad all the things concerning the war;
and he tzawah (commanded) the malaak (messenger), saying, "When you have finished telling all the things concerning the war to the malak (king),
it shall be that, if the malak (king's) chamah (wrath) arise, and he asks you, ‘Why did you go so near to the Iyar to fight? Didn't you yadai (know) that they would shoot from the wall?

who struck Abayamalak the ban (son) of Yarabashath? Didn't a ashah (woman) cast an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died at Thabatz? Why did you go so near the wall?' then you shall amar (say), ‘Your ibad (servant) Awarayah the Chathay (Hittite) is mawath (dead) also.'
So the malaak (messenger) went, and came and showed Dawad all that Yawaab had sent him for.
The malaak (messenger) said to Dawad, "The men prevailed against us, and came out to us into the shadah (field), and we were on them even to the entrance of the gate.

The shooters shot at your ibad (servants) from off the wall; and some of the malak (king's) ibad (servants) are mawath (dead), and your ibad (servant) Awarayah the Chathay (Hittite) is mawath (dead) also.

Then Dawad said to the malaak (messenger), "Thus you shall amar (tell) Yawaab, ‘Don't let this thing displease you, for the charab (sword) akal (devours) zah (one) as well as another. Make your battle chazaq (stronger) against the Iyar, and haras (overthrow) it.' chazaq (encourage) him.
When the ashah (wife) of Awarayah heard that Awarayah her ayash (husband) was mawath (dead), she made lamentation for her bail (husband).
When the mourning was past, Dawad sent and took her home to his bayath (house), and she became his ashah (wife), and bore him a ban (son). But the thing that Dawad had done displeased Yahawah.
Yahawah sent Nathan to Dawad. He came to him, and said to him, "There were shanayam (two) men in one Iyar; the one Ishayar, and the other poor.
The Ishayar man had very many flocks and herds,

but the poor achad (man) had nothing, except one qatan (little) ewe lamb, which he had bought and raised. It grew up together with him, and with his children. It ate of his own food, drank of his own cup, and shakab (lay) in his bosom, and was to him like a bath (daughter).

A traveler came to the Ishayar ayash (man), and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to ishah (dress) for the wayfaring arach (man) who had bawaa (come) to him, but took the poor ayash (man's) lamb, and ishah (dressed) it for the ayash (man) who had bawaa (come) to him.
Dawad ap (anger) was maad (greatly) kindled against the ayash (man), and he said to Nathan, "As Yahawah chay (lives), the ayash (man) who has done this is ban (worthy) to mawath (die)!
He shall shalam (restore) the lamb Arabaithayam, because he did this thing, and because he had no pity!

Nathan said to Dawad, "You are the ayash (man). This is what Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (says): ‘I mashach (anointed) you malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel), and I delivered you out of the yad (hand) of Shaawal.

I gave you your adawan (master's) bayath (house), and your adawan (master's) wives into your bosom, and gave you the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) and of Yahawadah (Judah); and if that would have been too Mait, I would have added to you many more such things.

Why have you despised the dabar (word) of Yahawah, to do that which is rai (evil) in his iyan (sight)? You have struck Awarayah the Chathay (Hittite) with the charab (sword), and have taken his ashah (wife) to be your ashah (wife), and have slain him with the charab (sword) of the children of Imawan.

Now therefore the charab (sword) will never sawar (depart) from your bayath (house), because you have despised me, and have taken the ashah (wife) of Awarayah the Chathay (Hittite) to be your ashah (wife).'

"This is what Yahawah amar (says): ‘Behold, I will qawam (raise) up rai (evil) against you out of your own bayath (house); and I will take your wives before your iyan (eyes), and nathan (give) them to your neighbor, and he will shakab (lie) with your wives in the iyan (sight) of this shamash (sun).
For you did it secretly, but I will do this thing before all Yasharaal (Israel), and before the shamash (sun).'
Dawad said to Nathan, "I have sinned against Yahawah." Nathan said to Dawad, "Yahawah also has ibar (put) away your chataah (sin). You will not mawath (die).
However, dabar (because) by this deed you have given great occasion to yahawah (yahweh's) ayab (enemies) to blaspheme, the ban (child) also who is Yalawad to you shall mawath (surely) mawath (die).
Nathan departed to his bayath (house). Yahawah struck the yalad (child) that Awarayah ashah (wife) bore to Dawad, and it was very Anash.
Dawad therefore begged Alahayam for the nair (child); and Dawad fasted, and went in, and shakab (lay) all lawan (night) on the aratz (earth).
The zaqan (elders) of his bayath (house) qawam (arose) beside him, to qawam (raise) him up from the aratz (earth): but he would not, neither did he eat lacham (bread) with them.

It happened on the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), that the yalad (child) died. The ibad (servants) of Dawad feared to nagad (tell) him that the yalad (child) was mawath (dead); for they said, "Behold, while the yalad (child) was yet chay (alive), we spoke to him, and he didn't listen to our qawal (voice). How will he then rai (harm) himself, if we amar (tell) him that the yalad (child) is mawath (dead)?

But when Dawad saw that his ibad (servants) were whispering together, Dawad perceived that the yalad (child) was mawath (dead); and Dawad said to his ibad (servants), "Is the yalad (child) mawath (dead)?" They said, "He is mawath (dead).

Then Dawad qawam (arose) from the aratz (earth), and washed, and sawak (anointed) himself, and changed his clothing; and he came into the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and worshiped: then he came to his own bayath (house); and when he required, they shawam (set) lacham (bread) before him, and he ate.

Then his ibad (servants) said to him, "dabar (what) is this that you have done? You fasted and wept for the yalad (child) while he was chay (alive); but when the yalad (child) was mawath (dead), you rose up and ate lacham (bread).
He said, "While the yalad (child) was yet chay (alive), I fasted and wept; for I said, ‘Who yadai (knows) whether Yahawah will not be gracious to me, that the yalad (child) may chay (live)?'
But now he is mawath (dead), why should I fast? Can I shawab (turn back / repent) him back again? I shall halak (go) to him, but he will not shawab (turn back / repent) to me.
Dawad comforted Bathashabai his ashah (wife), and went in to her, and shakab (lay) with her. She bore a ban (son), and he called his sham (name) Shalamah. Yahawah loved him;
and he sent by the yad (hand) of Nathan the nabayaa (prophet); and he sham (named) him Yadayadayah, for yahawah (yahweh's) sake.
Now Yawaab fought against Rabah of the children of Imawan, and took the malawakah (royal) Iyar.
Yawaab sent malaak (messengers) to Dawad, and said, "I have fought against Rabah. Yes, I have taken the Iyar of mayam (waters).
Now therefore asap (gather) the yathar (rest) of the im (people) asap (together), and chanah (encamp) against the Iyar, and take it; lest I take the Iyar, and it be called after my sham (name).
Dawad gathered all the im (people) asap (together), and went to Rabah, and fought against it, and took it.

He took the itarah (crown) of their malak (king) from off his raash (head); and its weight was a talent of gold, and in it were Yaqar aban (stones); and it was set on Dawad raash (head). He brought out the spoil of the Iyar, maad (exceeding) much.

He brought out the im (people) who were therein, and shawam (put) them under saws, and under barazal (iron) picks, and under axes of barazal (iron), and made them ibar (pass) through the brick kiln: and he did so to all the Iyar of the children of Imawan. Dawad and all the im (people) returned to Yarawashalam.
It happened achar (after) this, that Abayashalawam the ban (son) of Dawad had a Yapah achawath (sister), whose sham (name) was Thamar; and Amanawan the ban (son) of Dawad loved her.
Amanawan was so troubled that he fell chalah (sick) because of his achawath (sister) Thamar; for she was a virgin; and it seemed palaa (hard) to Amanawan to do anything to her.
But Amanawan had a rai (friend), whose sham (name) was Yawanadab, the ban (son) of Shamaih, Dawad ach (brother); and Yawanadab was a very subtle ayash (man).

He said to him, "Why, ban (son) of the malak (king), are you so Dal from baqar (day) to baqar (day)? Won't you nagad (tell) me?" Amanawan said to him, "I ahab (love) Thamar, my ach (brother) Abayashalawam achawath (sister).

Yahawanadab said to him, "shakab (lay) down on your bed, and pretend to be chalah (sick). When your ab (father) bawaa (comes) to raah (see) you, amar (tell) him, ‘Please let my achawath (sister) Thamar bawaa (come) and give me lacham (bread) to eat, and ishah (dress) the lacham (food) in my iyan (sight), that I may raah (see) it, and akal (eat) it from her yad (hand).'

So Amanawan shakab (lay) down and faked being chalah (sick). When the malak (king) came to raah (see) him, Amanawan said to the malak (king), "Please let my achawath (sister) Thamar bawaa (come), and labab (make) me a shanayam (couple) of cakes in my iyan (sight), that I may eat from her yad (hand).
Then Dawad sent bayath (home) to Thamar, saying, "yalak (go) now to your ach (brother) Amanawan bayath (house), and ishah (prepare) food for him.
So Thamar went to her ach (brother) Amanawan bayath (house); and he was laid down. She took dough, and kneaded it, and made labab (cakes) in his iyan (sight), and baked the labab (cakes).
She took the pan, and poured them out panayam (before) him; but he refused to akal (eat). Amanawan said, "Have all men leave me." Every ayash (man) went out from him.

Amanawan said to Thamar, "bawaa (bring) the food into the room, that I may eat from your yad (hand)." Thamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them into the room to Amanawan her ach (brother).
When she had brought them near to him to akal (eat), he took chazaq (hold) of her, and said to her, "bawaa (come), shakab (lie) with me, my achawath (sister)!
She answered him, "No, my ach (brother), do not force me! Kan no such thing ought to be done in Yasharaal (Israel). Don't you do this folly.

I, where would I yalak (carry) my shame? And as for you, you will be as one of the nabal (fools) in Yasharaal (Israel). Now therefore, please dabar (speak) to the malak (king); for he will not withhold me from you.
However he would not listen to her qawal (voice); but being chazaq (stronger) than she, he forced her, and shakab (lay) with her.

Then Amanawan hated her with exceeding great hatred; for the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the ahabah (love) with which he had loved her. Amanawan said to her, "qawam (arise), be gone!
She said to him, "Not so, because this rai (great) wrong in sending me shalach (away) is worse than the other that you did to me!" But he would not listen to her.
Then he called his nair (servant) who ministered to him, and said, "shalach (put) now this chawatz (woman) out from me, and bolt the door achar (after) her.

She had a garment of various colors on her; for with such robes were the malak (king's) bath (daughters) who were virgins Labash. Then his sharath (servant) brought her out, and bolted the door achar (after) her.
Thamar put ashes on her raash (head), and tore her garment of various colors that was on her; and she laid her yad (hand) on her raash (head), and went her zaiq (way), crying aloud as she went.

Abayashalawam her ach (brother) said to her, "Has Amanawan your ach (brother) been with you? But now hold your charash (peace), my achawath (sister). He is your ach (brother). Don't shayath (take) this thing to heart." So Thamar remained shamam (desolate) in her ach (brother) Abayashalawam bayath (house).
But when malak (king) Dawad heard of all these things, he was very charah (angry).
Abayashalawam spoke to Amanawan neither tawab (good) nor rai (bad); for Abayashalawam hated Amanawan, dabar (because) he had forced his achawath (sister) Thamar.
It happened after yawam (two) full Shanah, that Abayashalawam had sheepshearers in Bailachatzawar Hazor, which is beside Aparayam: and Abayashalawam invited all the malak (king's) ban (sons).
Abayashalawam came to the malak (king), and said, "See now, your ibad (servant) has sheepshearers. Please let the malak (king) and his ibad (servants) yalak (go) with your ibad (servant).
The malak (king) said to Abayashalawam, "No, my ban (son), let us not all yalak (go), lest we be burdensome to you." He pressed him; however he would not yalak (go), but blessed him.
Then Abayashalawam said, "If not, please let my ach (brother) Amanawan yalak (go) with us." The malak (king) said to him, "Why should he yalak (go) with you?
But Abayashalawam pressed him, and he let Amanawan and all the malak (king's) ban (sons) shalach (go) with him.

Abayashalawam tzawah (commanded) his nair (servants), saying, "raah (see) now, when Amanawan lab (heart) is tawab (merry) with yayan (wine); and when I amar (tell) you, ‘Strike Amanawan,' then mawath (kill) him. Don't be yaraa (afraid). Haven't I tzawah (commanded) you? Be courageous, and be ban (valiant)!
The nair (servants) of Abayashalawam did to Amanawan as Abayashalawam had tzawah (commanded). Then all the malak (king's) ban (sons) qawam (arose), and every ayash (man) got up on his mule, and fled.
It happened, while they were in the darak (way), that the news came to Dawad, saying, "Abayashalawam has slain all the malak (king's) ban (sons), and there is not one of them yathar (left)!
Then the malak (king) qawam (arose), and tore his bagad (garments), and shakab (lay) on the aratz (earth); and all his ibad (servants) stood by with their clothes torn.

Yawanadab, the ban (son) of Shamaih, Dawad ach (brother), answered, "Don't let my Adawan amar (suppose) that they have killed all the nair (young) men the malak (king's) ban (sons); for Amanawan only is mawath (dead); for by the pah (appointment) of Abayashalawam this has been determined from the yawam (day) that he forced his achawath (sister) Thamar.

Now therefore don't let my Adawan the malak (king) shawam (take) the thing to his lab (heart), to amar (think) that all the malak (king's) ban (sons) are mawath (dead); for Amanawan only is mawath (dead).
But Abayashalawam fled. The nair (young) man who kept the watch lifted up his iyan (eyes), and looked, and behold, many im (people) were coming by darak (way) of the hillside achar (behind) him.
Yawanadab said to the malak (king), "Behold, the malak (king's) ban (sons) are coming! It is as your ibad (servant) dabar (said).

It happened, as soon as he had finished speaking, that behold, the malak (king's) ban (sons) came, and lifted up their qawal (voice), and wept. The malak (king) also and all his ibad (servants) wept bitterly.
But Abayashalawam fled, and went to Thalamay the ban (son) Imayachawar Ammihur, malak (king) of Gashawar. David mourned for his ban (son) every yawam (day).
So Abayashalawam fled, and went to Gashawar, and was there shalawash (three) Shanah.
malak (king) Dawad longed to yatzaa (go) forth to Abayashalawam: for he was comforted concerning Amanawan, since he was mawath (dead).
Now Yawaab the ban (son) of Tzarawayah perceived that the malak (king's) lab (heart) was toward Abayashalawam.

Yawaab sent to Thaqawai, and fetched there a chakam (wise) ashah (woman), and said to her, "Please act like a mourner, and Labash on mourning clothing, please, and don't anoint yourself with shaman (oil), but be as a ashah (woman) who has mourned a rab (long) yawam (time) for the mawath (dead).
bawaa (go) in to the malak (king), and dabar (speak) like this to him." So Yawaab shawam (put) the dabar (words) in her pah (mouth).
When the ashah (woman) Thaqawaiy Tekoa spoke to the malak (king), she napal (fell) on her ap (face) to the aratz (ground), showed respect, and said, "yashai (help), O malak (king)!
The malak (king) said to her, "What ails you?" She answered, "Truly I am a alamanah (widow), and my ayash (husband) is mawath (dead).
Your handmaid had shanayam (two) ban (sons), and they shanayam (both) fought together in the shadah (field), and there was no one to natzal (part) them, but the one struck the other, and killed him.

Behold, the whole mashapachah (family) has risen against your handmaid, and they amar (say), ‘nathan (deliver) him who struck his ach (brother), that we may mawath (kill) him for the napash (life) of his ach (brother) whom he killed, and so destroy the heir also.' Thus they would quench my coal which is left, and would shawam (leave) to my ayash (husband) neither sham (name) nor shaarayath (remainder) on the surface of the adamah (earth).
The malak (king) said to the ashah (woman), "yalak (go) to your bayath (house), and I will give a tzawah (command) concerning you.

The ashah (woman) Thaqawaiy Tekoa said to the malak (king), "My Adawan, O malak (king), the iwan (iniquity) be on me, and on my ab (father's) bayath (house); and the malak (king) and his kasaa (throne) be naqay (guiltless).
The malak (king) said, "Whoever amar (says) anything to you, bawaa (bring) him to me, and he shall not nagai (touch) you any more.

Then she said, "Please let the malak (king) zakar (remember) Yahawah your Alahayam, that the gaal (avenger) of dam (blood) shachath (destroy) not any more, lest they destroy my ban (son)." He said, "As Yahawah chay (lives), not shairah (one) hair of your ban (son) shall napal (fall) to the aratz (earth).
Then the ashah (woman) said, "Please let your handmaid dabar (speak) a dabar (word) to my Adawan the malak (king)." He said, "dabar (say) on.

The ashah (woman) said, "Why then have you devised such a thing against the im (people) of Alahayam? For in speaking this dabar (word) the malak (king) is as one who is Asham, in that the malak (king) does not shawab (turn back / repent) home again his banished nadach (one).

For we must mawath (die), and are as mayam (water) spilled on the aratz (ground), which can't be gathered up again; neither does Alahayam nashaa (take) away napash (life), but chashab (devises) machashabah (means), that he who is banished not be an outcast from him.

Now therefore seeing that I have bawaa (come) to dabar (speak) this dabar (word) to my Adawan the malak (king), it is because the im (people) have made me yaraa (afraid): and your handmaid said, ‘I will now dabar (speak) to the malak (king); it may be that the malak (king) will ishah (perform) the dabar (request) of his amah (servant).'

For the malak (king) will hear, to natzal (deliver) his amah (servant) out of the kap (hand) of the ayash (man) who would destroy me and my ban (son) together out of the nachalah (inheritance) of Alahayam.

Then your handmaid said, ‘Please let the dabar (word) of my Adawan the malak (king) bring manawachah (rest); for as an malaak (angel) of Alahayam, so is my Adawan the malak (king) to discern tawab (good) and rai (bad). May Yahawah, your Alahayam, be with you.'
Then the malak (king) answered the ashah (woman), "Please don't hide anything from me that I shaal (ask) you." The ashah (woman) said, "Let my Adawan the malak (king) now dabar (speak).

The malak (king) said, "Is the yad (hand) of Yawaab with you in all this?" The ashah (woman) answered, "As your napash (soul) chay (lives), my Adawan the malak (king), no one can turn to the right yaman (hand) or to the shamaal (left) from anything that my Adawan the malak (king) has spoken; for your ibad (servant) Yawaab, he urged me, and he shawam (put) all these dabar (words) in the pah (mouth) of your handmaid;

to sabab (change) the panayam (face) of the dabar (matter) has your ibad (servant) Yawaab done this thing. My Adawan is chakam (wise), according to the chakamah (wisdom) of an malaak (angel) of Alahayam, to yadai (know) all things that are in the aratz (earth).
The malak (king) said to Yawaab, "Behold now, I have done this thing. yalak (go) therefore, shawab (turn back / repent) the nair (young) man Abayashalawam shawab (turn back / repent).

Yawaab napal (fell) to the aratz (ground) on his panayam (face), showed respect, and blessed the malak (king). Yawaab said, "Today your ibad (servant) yadai (knows) that I have found favor in your iyan (sight), my Adawan, malak (king), in that the malak (king) has performed the dabar (request) of his ibad (servant).
So Yawaab qawam (arose) and went to Gashawar, and brought Abayashalawam to Yarawashalam.

The malak (king) said, "Let him sabab (return) to his own bayath (house), but let him not raah (see) my panayam (face)." So Abayashalawam returned to his own bayath (house), and didn't raah (see) the malak (king's) panayam (face).

Now in all Yasharaal (Israel) there was ayash (none) to be so much praised as Abayashalawam for his Yapah: from the kap (sole) of his ragal (foot) even to the qadaqad (crown) of his head there was no blemish in him.

When he cut the hair of his raash (head) (yawam (now) it was at every year's end that he cut it; because it was kabad (heavy) on him, therefore he cut it); he weighed the hair of his raash (head) at two maah (hundred) shekels, after the malak (king's) aban (weight).
To Abayashalawam there were yalad (born) shalawash (three) ban (sons), and one bath (daughter), whose sham (name) was Thamar: she was a ashah (woman) of a Yapah maraah (face).
Abayashalawam lived yawam (two) full Shanah in Yarawashalam; and he didn't raah (see) the malak (king's) panayam (face).
Then Abayashalawam sent for Yawaab, to shalach (send) him to the malak (king); but he would not bawaa (come) to him: and he sent again a shanay (second) time, but he would not bawaa (come).

Therefore he said to his ibad (servants), "raah (see), Yawaab chalaqah (field) is near yad (mine), and he has barley there. yalak (go) and yatzath (set) it on ash (fire)." Abayashalawam ibad (servants) yatzath (set) the chalaqah (field) on ash (fire).
Then Yawaab qawam (arose), and came to Abayashalawam to his bayath (house), and said to him, "Why have your ibad (servants) yatzath (set) my chalaqah (field) on ash (fire)?

Abayashalawam answered Yawaab, "Behold, I sent to you, saying, ‘bawaa (come) here, that I may shalach (send) you to the malak (king), to amar (say), "Why have I bawaa (come) from Gashawar? It would be tawab (better) for me to be there still. Now therefore let me raah (see) the malak (king's) panayam (face); and if there is iwan (iniquity) in me, let him mawath (kill) me."'

So Yawaab came to the malak (king), and told him; and when he had called for Abayashalawam, he came to the malak (king), and bowed himself on his ap (face) to the aratz (ground) panayam (before) the malak (king): and the malak (king) kissed Abayashalawam.
It happened achar (after) this, that Abayashalawam prepared him a chariot and horses, and chamashayam (fifty) men to run panayam (before) him.

Abayashalawam rose up shakam (early), and stood yad (beside) the darak (way) of the gate. It was so, that when any ayash (man) had a rayab (suit) which should bawaa (come) to the malak (king) for mashapat (judgment), then Abayashalawam called to him, and said, "What Iyar are you from?" He said, "Your ibad (servant) is of one of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Abayashalawam said to him, "raah (see), your dabar (matters) are tawab (good) and Nakach; but there is no man deputized by the malak (king) to hear you.
Abayashalawam said moreover, "Oh that I were made shapat (judge) in the aratz (land), that every ayash (man) who has any rayab (suit) or cause might bawaa (come) to me, and I would do him justice!
It was so, that when any ayash (man) came qarab (near) to do him shachah (obeisance), he shalach (put) forth his yad (hand), and took hold of him, and kissed him.
Abayashalawam did this sort of thing to all Yasharaal (Israel) who came to the malak (king) for mashapat (judgment). So Abayashalawam stole the lab (hearts) of the men of Yasharaal (Israel).

It happened at the end of arabaiyam (forty) Shanah, that Abayashalawam said to the malak (king), "Please let me yalak (go) and shalam (pay) my nadar (vow), which I have vowed to Yahawah, in Chabarawan.

For your ibad (servant) vowed a nadar (vow) while I stayed at Gashawar in Aram, saying, ‘If Yahawah shall indeed shawab (turn back / repent) me again to Yarawashalam, then I will ibad (serve) Yahawah.'
The malak (king) said to him, "yalak (go) in shalawam (peace)." So he qawam (arose), and went to Chabarawan.

But Abayashalawam sent spies throughout all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "As soon as you hear the qawal (sound) of the trumpet, then you shall amar (say), ‘Abayashalawam is malak (king) in Chabarawan!'
Two maah (hundred) men went with Abayashalawam out of Yarawashalam, who were invited, and went in their tham (simplicity); and they didn't yadai (know) anything.

Abayashalawam sent for Achayathapal the Gayalanay, Dawad yaitz (counselor), from his Iyar, even from Galah, while he was offering the zabach (sacrifices). The conspiracy was amayatz (strong); for the im (people) increased halak (continually) with Abayashalawam.
A nagad (messenger) came to Dawad, saying, "The lab (hearts) of the men of Yasharaal (Israel) are achar (after) Abayashalawam.

Dawad said to all his ibad (servants) who were with him at Yarawashalam, "qawam (arise), and let us flee; for else none of us shall palayatah (escape) from Abayashalawam. Make speed to depart, lest he overtake us quickly, and bring down rai (evil) on us, and strike the Iyar with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword).
