The malak (king's) ibad (servants) said to the malak (king), "Behold, your ibad (servants) are ready to do whatever my Adawan the malak (king) chooses.
The malak (king) went yatzaa (forth), and all his bayath (household) ragal (after) him. The malak (king) left ishar (ten) women, who were concubines, to shamar (keep) the bayath (house).
The malak (king) went yatzaa (forth), and all the im (people) ragal (after) him; and they stayed in Beth Merhak.

All his ibad (servants) passed on yad (beside) him; and all the Karathay (Cherethites), and all the Palathay (Pelethites), and all the Gathay (Gittites), shash (six) maah (hundred) men who came ragal (after) him from gath (gath), passed on panayam (before) the malak (king).

Then the malak (king) said to Athay the Gathay (Gittite), "Why do you also yalak (go) with us? shawab (turn back / repent), and stay with the malak (king); for you are a nakaray (foreigner), and also an galah (exile). maqawam (return) to your own place.

Whereas you came but thamawal (yesterday), should I this yawam (day) make you yalak (go) up and down with us, since I halak (go) where I may? shawab (turn back / repent), and shawab (turn back / repent) back your ach (brothers). chasad (mercy) and truth be with you.

Athay answered the malak (king), and said, "As Yahawah chay (lives), and as my Adawan the malak (king) chay (lives), surely in what place my Adawan the malak (king) shall is, whether for mawath (death) or for chay (life), even there also will your ibad (servant) be.
Dawad said to Athay, "yalak (go) and ibar (pass) over." Athay the Gathay (Gittite) passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones who were with him.

All the aratz (country) wept with a gadawal (loud) qawal (voice), and all the im (people) passed over: the malak (king) also himself passed over the nachal (brook) Qadarawan, and all the im (people) passed over, panayam (toward) the darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness).

Behold, Tzadawaq Lawayay came, and all the Levites with him, bearing the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Alahayam; and they set down the arawan (ark) of Alahayam; and Abayathar went up, until all the im (people) finished passing out of the Iyar.

The malak (king) said to Tzadawaq, "shawab (turn back / repent) back the arawan (ark) of Alahayam into the Iyar. If I matzaa (find) favor in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, he will shawab (turn back / repent) me again, and show me both it, and his Nawah;
but if he amar (say) thus, ‘I have no delight in you;' behold, here am I. Let him do to me as seems tawab (good) to him.

The malak (king) said also to Tzadawaq the kahan (priest), "Aren't you a seer? shawab (turn back / repent) into the Iyar in shalawam (peace), and your shanayam (two) ban (sons) with you, Achayamaitz your ban (son), and Yahawanathan the ban (son) of Abayathar.
raah (see), I will stay at the fords of the madabar (wilderness), until dabar (word) bawaa (comes) from you to inform me.
Tzadawaq therefore and Abayathar carried the arawan (ark) of Alahayam again to Yarawashalam; and they stayed there.

Dawad went up by the ascent of the Mount of Olives, and wept as he went up; and he had his raash (head) covered, and went Yachap: and all the im (people) who were with him covered every ayash (man) his raash (head), and they went up, weeping as they went up.
Someone told Dawad, saying, "Achayathapal is among the conspirators with Abayashalawam." Dawad said, "Yahawah, please turn the itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal into foolishness.

It happened that when Dawad had bawaa (come) to the raash (top), where Alahayam was worshiped, behold, Chawashay the Arakay came to qaraah (meet) him with his coat torn, and adamah (earth) on his raash (head).
Dawad said to him, "If you ibar (pass) on with me, then you will be a mashaa (burden) to me;

but if you shawab (turn back / repent) to the Iyar, and amar (tell) Abayashalawam, ‘I will be your ibad (servant), O malak (king). As I have been your ab (father's) ibad (servant) in time past, so will I now be your ibad (servant); then will you parar (defeat) for me the itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal.'

Don't you have Tzadawaq and Abayathar the kahan (priests) there with you? Therefore it shall be, that whatever thing you shall hear out of the malak (king's) bayath (house), you shall nagad (tell) it to Tzadawaq and Abayathar the kahan (priests).

Behold, they have there with them their shanayam (two) ban (sons), Achayamaitz, Tzadawaq son, and Yahawanathan, Abayathar son; and by them you shall shalach (send) to me everything that you shall hear.
So Chawashay, Dawad friend, came into the Iyar; and Abayashalawam came into Yarawashalam.

When Dawad was a Mait past the raash (top), behold, Tzayabaa the nair (servant) of Mapayabashath met him, with a tzamad (couple) of donkeys saddled, and on them two maah (hundred) loaves of lacham (bread), and one maah (hundred) clusters of raisins, and one maah (hundred) qayatz (summer) fruits, and a bottle of yayan (wine).

The malak (king) said to Tzayabaa, What do you mean by these? Tzayabaa said, The donkeys are for the malak (king's) bayath (household) to ride on; and the lacham (bread) and qayatz (summer) fruit for the nair (young) men to akal (eat); and the yayan (wine), that such as are Yaip in the madabar (wilderness) may drink.

The malak (king) said, "Where is your adawan (master's) ban (son)?" Tzayabaa said to the malak (king), "Behold, he is staying in Yarawashalam; for he said, ‘Today the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) will shawab (turn back / repent) me the mamalakawath (kingdom) of my ab (father).'

Then the malak (king) said to Tzayabaa, "Behold, all that pertains to Mapayabashath is yours." Tzayabaa said, "I do shachah (obeisance). Let me matzaa (find) favor in your iyan (sight), my Adawan, O malak (king).

When malak (king) Dawad came to Bacharayam, behold, a ayash (man) of the mashapachah (family) of the bayath (house) of Shaawal came out, whose sham (name) was Shamaiy, the ban (son) of Garaa. He came out, and cursed still as he came.

He saqal (cast) aban (stones) at Dawad, and at all the ibad (servants) of malak (king) Dawad, and all the im (people) and all the gabawar (mighty) men were on his right yamayan (hand) and on his shamaawal (left).
Shamaiy said when he cursed, "Be gone, be gone, you ayash (man) of dam (blood), and base ayash (fellow)!

Yahawah has returned on you all the dam (blood) of the bayath (house) of Shaawal, in whose place you have reigned! Yahawah has delivered the malawakah (kingdom) into the yad (hand) of Abayashalawam your ban (son)! Behold, you are caught by your own rai (mischief), because you are a ayash (man) of dam (blood)!

Then Abayashay the ban (son) of Tzarawayah said to the malak (king), "Why should this mawath (dead) dog qalal (curse) my Adawan the malak (king)? Please let me ibar (go) over and sawar (take) off his raash (head).

The malak (king) said, "What have I to do with you, you ban (sons) of Tzarawayah? Because he qalal (curses), and because Yahawah has said to him, ‘qalal (curse) Dawad;' who then shall amar (say), ‘Why have you done so?'

Dawad said to Abayashay, and to all his ibad (servants), "Behold, my ban (son), who came yatzaa (forth) from my maih (bowels), seeks my napash (life). How much more this Banayamayanay (Benjamite), now? Leave him yanach (alone), and let him qalal (curse); for Yahawah has invited him.
It may be that Yahawah will raah (see) on the wrong done to me, and that Yahawah will repay me tawab (good) for the cursing of me today.
So Dawad and his men went by the darak (way); and Shamaiy went halak (along) on the hillside opposite him, and cursed as he went, threw aban (stones) at him, and threw ipar (dust).
The malak (king), and all the im (people) who were with him, came Iyap; and he refreshed himself there.
Abayashalawam, and all the im (people), the men of Yasharaal (Israel), came to Yarawashalam, and Achayathapal with him.

It happened, when Chawashay the Arakay, Dawad friend, had bawaa (come) to Abayashalawam, that Chawashay said to Abayashalawam, "Long chayah (live) the malak (king)! Long chayah (live) the malak (king)!
Abayashalawam said to Chawashay, "Is this your chasad (kindness) to your rai (friend)? Why didn't you halak (go) with your rai (friend)?
Chawashay said to Abayashalawam, "No; but whomever Yahawah, and this im (people), and all the men of Yasharaal (Israel) have chosen, his will I be, and with him I will stay.
Again, whom should I ibad (serve)? Shouldn't I panayam (serve) in the presence of his ban (son)? As I have served in your ab (father's) panayam (presence), so will I be in your panayam (presence).
Then Abayashalawam said to Achayathapal, "Give your itzah (counsel) what we shall do.

Achayathapal said to Abayashalawam, "bawaa (go) in to your ab (father's) concubines, that he has left to shamar (keep) the bayath (house). Then all Yasharaal (Israel) will hear that you are baash (abhorred) by your ab (father). Then the yad (hands) of all who are with you will be chazaq (strong).
So they natah (spread) Abayashalawam a ahal (tent) on the top of the gag (house); and Abayashalawam went in to his ab (father's) concubines in the iyan (sight) of all Yasharaal (Israel).

The itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal, which he gave in those yawam (days), was as if a ayash (man) inquired at the dabar (oracle) of Alahayam: so was all the itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal both with Dawad and with Abayashalawam.
Moreover Achayathapal said to Abayashalawam, "Let me now choose shanayam (twelve) alap (thousand) men, and I will qawam (arise) and pursue achar (after) Dawad tonight.
I will bawaa (come) on him while he is Yagai and Rapah, and will make him afraid. All the im (people) who are with him shall flee. I will strike the malak (king) only;
and I will shawab (turn back / repent) back all the im (people) to you. The ayash (man) whom you seek is as if all returned. All the im (people) shall be in shalawam (peace).
The dabar (saying) pleased Abayashalawam iyan (well), and all the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Then Abayashalawam said, "Now qaraa (call) Chawashay the Arakay also, and let us hear likewise what he pah (says).
When Chawashay had bawaa (come) to Abayashalawam, Abayashalawam spoke to him, saying, "Achayathapal has spoken like this. Shall we do dabar (what) he says? If not, dabar (speak) up.
Chawashay said to Abayashalawam, "The itzah (counsel) that Achayathapal has given this paim (time) is not tawab (good).

Chawashay said moreover, "You yadai (know) your ab (father) and his men, that they are gabawar (mighty) men, and they are Mar in their napash (minds), like a bear Shakawal of her cubs in the shadah (field). Your ab (father) is a ayash (man) of war, and will not lawan (lodge) with the im (people).

Behold, he is now hidden in some pachath (pit), or in some other place. It will happen, when some of them have fallen at the thachalah (first), that whoever hears it will amar (say), ‘There is a magapah (slaughter) among the im (people) who achar (follow) Abayashalawam!'

Even he who is ban (valiant), whose lab (heart) is as the lab (heart) of a aray (lion), will utterly melt; for all Yasharaal (Israel) yadai (knows) that your ab (father) is a gabawar (mighty) man, and those who are with him are chayal (valiant) men.

But I yaitz (counsel) that all Yasharaal (Israel) be gathered asap (together) Dan you, from Dan Baarashabai to Beersheba, as the sand that is by the yam (sea) for multitude; and that you halak (go) to battle in your own panayam (person).

So shall we bawaa (come) on him in some place where he shall be found, and we will nachanaw (light) on him as the dew napal (falls) on the adamah (ground); and of him and of all the men who are with him we will not yathar (leave) so much as one.

Moreover, if he be gone into a Iyar, then shall all Yasharaal (Israel) nashaa (bring) ropes to that Iyar, and we will draw it into the nachal (river), until there isn't gam (one) small tzarawar (stone) found there.

Abayashalawam and all the men of Yasharaal (Israel) said, "The itzah (counsel) of Chawashay the Arakay is tawab (better) than the itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal." For Yahawah had ordained to parar (defeat) the tawab (good) itzah (counsel) of Achayathapal, to the intent that Yahawah might bawaa (bring) rai (evil) on Abayashalawam.
Then Chawashay said to Tzadawaq and to Abayathar the kahan (priests), "Achayathapal counseled Abayashalawam and the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) that way; and I have counseled this way.

Now therefore shalach (send) quickly, and nagad (tell) Dawad, saying, ‘Don't lawan (lodge) this layal (night) at the fords of the madabar (wilderness), but by all means ibar (pass) over; lest the malak (king) be swallowed up, and all the im (people) who are with him.'

Now Yahawanathan and Achayamaitz were staying by Iyanaragal Rogel; and a female shapachah (servant) used to halak (go) and nagad (tell) them; and they went and told malak (king) Dawad. For they might not be seen to bawaa (come) into the Iyar.

But a nair (boy) saw them, and told Abayashalawam. Then they shanayam (both) went away quickly, and came to the bayath (house) of a ayash (man) in Bacharayam, who had a baar (well) in his court; and they went down there.
The ashah (woman) took and spread the covering over the baar (well's) panayam (mouth), and spread out bruised grain on it; and nothing was yadai (known).

Abayashalawam ibad (servants) came to the ashah (woman) to the bayath (house); and they said, "Where are Achayamaitz and Yahawanathan?" The ashah (woman) said to them, "They have gone over the brook of mayam (water)." When they had sought and could not matzaa (find) them, they returned to Yarawashalam.

It happened, achar (after) they had departed, that they came up out of the baar (well), and went and told malak (king) Dawad; and they said to Dawad, "qawam (arise) and pass quickly over the mayam (water); for thus has Achayathapal counseled against you.

Then Dawad qawam (arose), and all the im (people) who were with him, and they passed over the Yaradan. By the baqar (morning) awar (light) there lacked not one of them who had not gone over the Yaradan.

When Achayathapal saw that his itzah (counsel) was not followed, he saddled his donkey, and qawam (arose), and went home, to his Iyar, and set his house in tzawah (order), and hanged himself; and he died, and was buried in the tomb of his ab (father).
Then Dawad came to Machanayam. Abayashalawam passed over the Yaradan, he and all the men of Yasharaal (Israel) with him.

Abayashalawam shawam (set) Imashaa over the tzabaa (army) instead of Yawaab. Now Imashaa was the ban (son) of a ayash (man), whose sham (name) was Yatharaa the Yasharaalay (Israelite), who went in Abayagayal Abigail the bath (daughter) of Nachash, achawath (sister) to Tzarawayah, Yawaab am (mother).
Yasharaal (Israel) and Abayashalawam encamped in the aratz (land) of Galaid.

It happened, when Dawad had bawaa (come) to Machanayam, that Shabay the ban (son) of Nachash of Rabah of the children of Imawan, and Makayar the ban (son) of Imayaal of Laadabar, and Barazalay the Galaiday (Gileadite) of Ragalayam,
brought beds, basins, earthen vessels, wheat, barley, meal, parched grain, beans, lentils, roasted grain,

honey, butter, sheep, and cheese of the herd, for Dawad, and for the im (people) who were with him, to akal (eat): for they said, "The im (people) are Raib, and Iyap, and Tzamaa, in the madabar (wilderness).
Dawad numbered the im (people) who were with him, and shawam (set) shar (captains) of alap (thousands) and shar (captains) of maah (hundreds) over them.

Dawad sent shalach (forth) the im (people), a shalayashay (third) part under the yad (hand) of Yawaab, and a shalayashay (third) part under the yad (hand) of Abayashay the ban (son) of Tzarawayah, Yawaab ach (brother), and a shalayashay (third) part under the yad (hand) of Athay the Gathay (Gittite). The malak (king) said to the im (people), "I will yatzaa (surely) yatzaa (go) forth with you myself also.

But the im (people) said, "You shall not yatzaa (go) forth; for if we flee away, they will not shawam (care) for us; neither if chatzay (half) of us mawath (die), will they shawam (care) for us. But you are worth ishar (ten) alap (thousand) of us. Therefore now it is tawab (better) that you are ready to help us out of the Iyar.
The malak (king) said to them, "I will do what seems yatab (best) to you." The malak (king) stood yad (beside) the gate, and all the im (people) went out by maah (hundreds) and by alap (thousands).

The malak (king) tzawah (commanded) Yawaab and Abayashay and Athay, saying, "Deal gently for my sake with the nair (young) man, even with Abayashalawam." All the im (people) heard when the malak (king) tzawah (commanded) all the shar (captains) dabar (concerning) Abayashalawam.
So the im (people) went out into the shadah (field) qaraah (against) Yasharaal (Israel): and the battle was in the Yair of Aparayam.

The im (people) of Yasharaal (Israel) were struck there panayam (before) the ibad (servants) of Dawad, and there was a gadawal (great) magapah (slaughter) there that yawam (day) of isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) men.
For the battle was there spread over the surface of all the aratz (country); and the Yair devoured more im (people) that yawam (day) than the charab (sword) devoured.

Abayashalawam happened to meet the servants of Dawad. Abayashalawam was riding on his mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a gadawal (great) oak, and his raash (head) caught chazaq (hold) of the oak, and he was taken up between the sky and aratz (earth); and the mule that was under him went on.
A achad (certain) ayash (man) saw it, and told Yawaab, and said, "raah (see), I saw Abayashalawam hanging in an oak.

Yawaab said to the ayash (man) who told him, "raah (see), you saw it, and why didn't you strike him there to the aratz (ground)? I would have given you ishar (ten) pieces of kasap (silver), and a sash.

The ayash (man) said to Yawaab, "Though I should receive a alap (thousand) pieces of kasap (silver) in my kap (hand), I still wouldn't shalach (put) forth my kap (hand) against the malak (king's) ban (son); for in our hearing the malak (king) tzawah (commanded) you and Abayashay and Athay, saying, ‘Beware that none touch the nair (young) man Abayashalawam.'
Otherwise if I had dealt falsely against his napash (life) (and there is no dabar (matter) hidden from the malak (king)), then you yourself would have set yourself against me.

Then Yawaab said, "I'm not going to wait like this with you." He took shalawash (three) shabat (darts) in his kap (hand), and thrust them through the lab (heart) of Abayashalawam, while he was yet chay (alive) in the midst of the oak.
ishar (ten) nair (young) men who bore Yawaab armor surrounded and struck Abayashalawam, and killed him.
Yawaab blew the trumpet, and the im (people) returned from pursuing achar (after) Yasharaal (Israel); for Yawaab held back the im (people).

They took Abayashalawam, and cast him into the gadawal (great) pachath (pit) in the Yair, and raised over him a very gadawal (great) heap of aban (stones). Then all Yasharaal (Israel) fled everyone to his ahal (tent).

Now Abayashalawam in his chay (lifetime) had taken and reared up for himself the pillar, which is in the malak (king's) dale; for he said, "I have no ban (son) to keep my sham (name) in memory." He called the pillar after his own sham (name); and it is called Abayashalawam monument, to this yawam (day).
Then Achayamaitz the ban (son) of Tzadawaq said, "Let me now run, and bashar (bear) the malak (king) news, how that Yahawah has avenged him of his enemies.

Yawaab said to him, "You shall not be the bearer of news this yawam (day), but you shall bashar (bear) news achar (another) yawam (day). But today you shall bashar (bear) no news, because the malak (king's) ban (son) is mawath (dead).
Then Yawaab said to the Kawashay (Cushite), "yalak (go), nagad (tell) the malak (king) what you have seen!" The Kawashay (Cushite) bowed himself to Yawaab, and ran.

Then Achayamaitz the ban (son) of Tzadawaq said yet again to Yawaab, "But come mah (what) may, please let me also run achar (after) the Kawashay (Cushite)." Yawaab said, "Why do you want to run, my ban (son), since that you will have no reward for the news?
"But come what may," he said, "I will run." He said to him, "Run!" Then Achayamaitz ran by the darak (way) of the Plain, and outran the Kawashay (Cushite).

Now Dawad was sitting between the shanayam (two) gates: and the watchman went up to the roof of the gate to the wall, and lifted up his iyan (eyes), and looked, and, behold, a ayash (man) running rawatz (alone).
The watchman cried, and told the malak (king). The malak (king) said, "If he is bashawarah (alone), there is news in his pah (mouth)." He came closer and Qarab.
The watchman saw achar (another) ayash (man) running; and the watchman called to the porter, and said, "Behold, a ayash (man) running alone!" The malak (king) said, "He also bashar (brings) news.

The watchman said, "I raah (see) the running of the raashawan (first) marawatzah (one) is like the running of Achayamaitz the ban (son) of Tzadawaq." The malak (king) said, "He is a tawab (good) ayash (man), and bawaa (comes) with tawab (good) news.

Achayamaitz called, and said to the malak (king), "All is shalawam (well)." He bowed himself before the malak (king) with his ap (face) to the aratz (earth), and said, "Blessed is Yahawah your Alahayam, who has delivered up the men who lifted up their yad (hand) against my Adawan the malak (king)!

The malak (king) said, "Is it shalawam (well) with the nair (young) man Abayashalawam?" Achayamaitz answered, "When Yawaab sent the malak (king's) ibad (servant), even me your ibad (servant), I saw a gadawal (great) tumult, but I don't yadai (know) what it was.
The malak (king) said, "sabab (turn) aside, and stand here." He turned sabab (aside), and stood still.
Behold, the Kawashay (Cushite) came. The Kawashay (Cushite) said, "News for my Adawan the malak (king); for Yahawah has avenged you this yawam (day) of all those who rose up qawam (against) you.

The malak (king) said to the Kawashay (Cushite), "Is it shalawam (well) with the nair (young) man Abayashalawam?" The Kawashay (Cushite) answered, "May the ayab (enemies) of my Adawan the malak (king), and all who qawam (rise) up against you to do you rai (harm), be as that nair (young) man is.

The malak (king) was much moved, and went up to the room over the gate, and wept. As he went, he said, "My ban (son) Abayashalawam! My ban (son), my ban (son) Abayashalawam! I wish I had died for you, Abayashalawam, my ban (son), my ban (son)!
It was told Yawaab, "Behold, the malak (king) weeps and mourns for Abayashalawam.
The thashawaih (victory) that yawam (day) was turned into mourning to all the im (people); for the im (people) heard it said that yawam (day), "The malak (king) itzab (grieves) for his ban (son).
The im (people) sneaked into the Iyar that yawam (day), as im (people) who are kalam (ashamed) steal away when they flee in battle.
The malak (king) covered his panayam (face), and the malak (king) cried with a gadawal (loud) qawal (voice), "My ban (son) Abayashalawam, Abayashalawam, my ban (son), my ban (son)!

Yawaab came into the bayath (house) to the malak (king), and said, "You have shamed this yawam (day) the panayam (faces) of all your ibad (servants), who this yawam (day) have saved your napash (life), and the lives of your ban (sons) and of your bath (daughters), and the lives of your wives, and the lives of your concubines;

in that you ahab (love) those who shanaa (hate) you, and shanaa (hate) those who ahab (love) you. For you have declared this yawam (day), that shar (princes) and ibad (servants) are nothing to you. For today I yadai (perceive) that if Abayashalawam had lived, and all we had died this yawam (day), then it would have yashar (pleased) you well.

Now therefore qawam (arise), yatzaa (go) out, and dabar (speak) to comfort your ibad (servants); for I shabai (swear) by Yahawah, if you don't yatzaa (go) out, not a man will stay with you this layal (night). That would be raii (worse) to you than all the rai (evil) that has happened to you from your youth until now.

Then the malak (king) qawam (arose), and sat in the gate. They told to all the im (people), saying, "Behold, the malak (king) is sitting in the gate." All the im (people) came panayam (before) the malak (king). Now Yasharaal (Israel) had fled every ayash (man) to his ahal (tent).

All the im (people) were at strife throughout all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "The malak (king) delivered us out of the kap (hand) of our ayab (enemies), and he saved us out of the kap (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines); and now he has fled out of the aratz (land) from Abayashalawam.
Abayashalawam, whom we mashach (anointed) over us, is mawath (dead) in battle. Now therefore why don't you charash (speak) a word of bringing the malak (king) shawab (turn back / repent)?

malak (king) Dawad sent to Tzadawaq and to Abayathar the kahan (priests), saying, "dabar (speak) to the zaqan (elders) of Yahawadah (Judah), saying, ‘Why are you the Acharawan to shawab (turn back / repent) the malak (king) shawab (turn back / repent) to his bayath (house)? Since the dabar (speech) of all Yasharaal (Israel) has bawaa (come) to the malak (king), to return him to his bayath (house).
You are my ach (brothers), you are my itzam (bone) and my flesh. Why then are you the Acharawan to shawab (turn back / repent) back the malak (king)?'

amar (say) to Imashaa, ‘Aren't you my itzam (bone) and my flesh? Alahayam do so to me, and more also, if you aren't shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army) panayam (before) me yawam (continually) in the room of Yawaab.'
He bowed the labab (heart) of all the men of Yahawadah (Judah), even as one ayash (man); so that they sent to the malak (king), saying, "shawab (turn back / repent), you and all your ibad (servants).
So the malak (king) returned, and came to the Yaradan. Yahawadah (Judah) came to Galagal, to yalak (go) to qaraah (meet) the malak (king), to ibar (bring) the malak (king) over the Yaradan.
Shamaiy the ban (son) of Garaa, the Banayamayanay (Benjamite), who was of Bacharayam, hurried and came down with the men of Yahawadah (Judah) to qaraah (meet) malak (king) Dawad.

There were a alap (thousand) men of Banayamayanay with him, and Tzayabaa the nair (servant) of the bayath (house) of Shaawal, and his chamash (fifteen) ban (sons) and his isharayam (twenty) ibad (servants) with him; and they went through the Yaradan in the panayam (presence) of the malak (king).

A ferry boat went to ibar (bring) over the malak (king's) bayath (household), and to do what he thought tawab (good). Shamaiy the ban (son) of Garaa napal (fell) down panayam (before) the malak (king), when he had ibar (come) over the Yaradan.

He said to the malak (king), "Don't let my Adawan chashab (impute) iwan (iniquity) to me, nor zakar (remember) that which your ibad (servant) did iwah (perversely) the yawam (day) that my Adawan the malak (king) went out of Yarawashalam, that the malak (king) should shawam (take) it to his lab (heart).

For your ibad (servant) yadai (knows) that I have sinned. Therefore, behold, I have bawaa (come) this yawam (day) the raashawan (first) of all the bayath (house) of Yawasap to yarad (go) down to qaraah (meet) my Adawan the malak (king).
But Abayashay the ban (son) of Tzarawayah answered, "Shall Shamaiy not be put to mawath (death) for this, because he cursed yahawah (yahweh's) mashayach (anointed)?

Dawad said, "What have I to do with you, you ban (sons) of Tzarawayah, that you should this yawam (day) be shatan (adversaries) to me? Shall there any ayash (man) be put to mawath (death) this yawam (day) in Yasharaal (Israel)? For don't I yadai (know) that I am this yawam (day) malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel)?
The malak (king) said to Shamaiy, "You shall not mawath (die)." The malak (king) swore to him.

Mapayabashath the ban (son) of Shaawal came down to qaraah (meet) the malak (king); and he had laa (neither) groomed his feet, nor trimmed his beard, nor washed his clothes, from the yawam (day) the malak (king) departed until the yawam (day) he came home in shalawam (peace).
It happened, when he had bawaa (come) to Yarawashalam to qaraah (meet) the malak (king), that the malak (king) said to him, "Why didn't you halak (go) with me, Mapayabashath?

He answered, "My Adawan, O malak (king), my ibad (servant) deceived me. For your ibad (servant) said, I will saddle me a donkey, that I may ride thereon, and yalak (go) with the malak (king); because your ibad (servant) is Pasach.
He has slandered your ibad (servant) to my Adawan the malak (king); but my Adawan the malak (king) is as an malaak (angel) of Alahayam. Do therefore what is tawab (good) in your iyan (eyes).

For all my ab (father's) bayath (house) were but mawath (dead) men before my Adawan the malak (king); yet you shayath (set) your ibad (servant) among those who ate at your own table. What tzadaqah (right) therefore have I yet that I should cry any more to the malak (king)?
The malak (king) said to him, "Why do you dabar (speak) any more of your dabar (matters)? I amar (say), you and Tzayabaa divide the shadah (land).
Mapayabashath said to the malak (king), "Yes, let him take all, because my Adawan the malak (king) has bawaa (come) in shalawam (peace) to his own bayath (house).
Barazalay the Galaiday (Gileadite) came down from Ragalayam; and he went over the Yaradan with the malak (king), to shalach (conduct) him over the Yaradan.

Now Barazalay was a very zaqan (aged) man, even shamanayam (eighty) Shanah ban (old): and he had provided the malak (king) with sustenance while he lay at Machanayam; for he was a very gadawal (great) ayash (man).
The malak (king) said to Barazalay, "ibar (come) over with me, and I will sustain you with me in Yarawashalam.
Barazalay said to the malak (king), "How many are the days of the Shanah of my life, that I should ilah (go) up with the malak (king) to Yarawashalam?

I am this yawam (day) shamanayam (eighty) Shanah ban (old). Can I yadai (discern) between tawab (good) and rai (bad)? Can your ibad (servant) taste what I akal (eat) or what I drink? Can I hear any more the qawal (voice) of singing men and singing women? Why then should your ibad (servant) be yet a mashaa (burden) to my Adawan the malak (king)?
Your ibad (servant) would Mait just ibar (go) over the Yaradan with the malak (king). Why should the malak (king) repay me with such a reward?

Please let your ibad (servant) shawab (turn back / repent) back again, that I may mawath (die) in my own Iyar, by the qabar (grave) of my ab (father) and my am (mother). But behold, your ibad (servant) Kamaham; let him ibar (go) over with my Adawan the malak (king); and do to him what shall seem tawab (good) to you.
The malak (king) answered, "Kamaham shall ibar (go) over with me, and I will do to him that which shall seem tawab (good) to you. Whatever you require of me, that I will do for you.
All the im (people) went over the Yaradan, and the malak (king) went over. Then the malak (king) kissed Barazalay, and blessed him; and he returned to his own place.

So the malak (king) went over to Galagal, and Kamaham went over with him. All the im (people) of Yahawadah (Judah) brought the malak (king) over, and also chatzay (half) the im (people) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Behold, all the men of Yasharaal (Israel) came to the malak (king), and said to the malak (king), "Why have our ach (brothers) the men of Yahawadah (Judah) stolen you away, and brought the malak (king), and his bayath (household), over the Yaradan, and all Dawad men with him?

All the men of Yahawadah (Judah) answered the men of Yasharaal (Israel), "Because the malak (king) is a close relative to us. Why then are you charah (angry) about this dabar (matter)? Have we eaten at all at the malak (king's) cost? Or has he given us any nashaath (gift)?

The men of Yasharaal (Israel) answered the men of Yahawadah (Judah), and said, "We have ishar (ten) yad (parts) in the malak (king), and we have also more claim to Dawad than you. Why then did you qalal (despise) us, that our dabar (advice) should not be raashawan (first) had in bringing shawab (turn back / repent) our malak (king)?" The dabar (words) of the men of Yahawadah (Judah) were fiercer than the dabar (words) of the men of Yasharaal (Israel).

There happened to be there a base ayash (fellow), whose sham (name) was Shabai, the ban (son) of Bakaray, a Banayamayanay (Benjamite): and he blew the trumpet, and said, "We have no chalaq (portion) in Dawad, neither have we nachalah (inheritance) in the ban (son) of Yashay. ayash (every) ayash (man) to his ahal (tents), Yasharaal (Israel)!

So all the men of Yasharaal (Israel) went up from following Dawad, and followed Shabai the ban (son) of Bakaray; but the men of Yahawadah (Judah) joined with their malak (king), from the Yaradan even to Yarawashalam.

Dawad came to his bayath (house) at Yarawashalam; and the malak (king) took the ishar (ten) women his concubines, whom he had left to shamar (keep) the bayath (house), and nathan (put) them in custody, and provided them with sustenance, but didn't bawaa (go) in to them. So they were tzarar (shut) up to the yawam (day) of their mawath (death), living in widowhood.
Then the malak (king) said to Imashaa, "Call me the men of Yahawadah (Judah) together within shalawash (three) yawam (days), and be here imad (present).
So Imashaa went to call the men of Yahawadah (Judah) together; but he stayed longer than the mawaid (set) time which he had appointed him.

Dawad said to Abayashay, "Now Shabai the ban (son) of Bakaray will do us more harm than Abayashalawam did. Take your adawan (lord's) ibad (servants), and pursue achar (after) him, lest he matzaa (get) himself fortified Iyar, and natzal (escape) out of our iyan (sight).

There went out achar (after) him Yawaab men, and the Karathay (Cherethites) and the Palathay (Pelethites), and all the gabawar (mighty) men; and they went out of Yarawashalam, to pursue achar (after) Shabai the ban (son) of Bakaray.

When they were at the gadawal (great) aban (stone) which is in Gabaiwan, Imashaa came to panayam (meet) them. Yawaab was clothed in his apparel of war that he had put on, and Chagawar it was a sash with a charab (sword) fastened on his waist in its sheath; and as he went yatzaa (forth) it fell out.
Yawaab said to Imashaa, "Is it shalawam (well) with you, my ach (brother)?" Yawaab took Imashaa by the beard with his yamayan (right) yad (hand) to kiss him.

But Imashaa took no shamar (heed) to the charab (sword) that was in Yawaab yad (hand). So he struck him with it in the body, and shed out his maih (bowels) to the aratz (ground), and didn't shanah (strike) him again; and he died. Yawaab and Abayashay his ach (brother) pursued achar (after) Shabai the ban (son) of Bakaray.
There stood by him one of Yawaab nair (young) men, and said, "He who favors Yawaab, and he who is for Dawad, let him achar (follow) Yawaab!

Imashaa lay wallowing in his dam (blood) in the midst of the masalah (highway). When the ayash (man) saw that all the im (people) stood still, he carried Imashaa out of the masalah (highway) into the shadah (field), and cast a bagad (garment) over him, when he saw that everyone who came by him stood still.
When he was removed out of the masalah (highway), all the ayash (people) went on achar (after) Yawaab, to pursue achar (after) Shabai the ban (son) of Bakaray.
He went through all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) to Abal, and to Bayathamaikah Maacah, and all the Baray: and they were gathered together, and went also achar (after) him.

They came and besieged him in Abal of Bayathamaikah Maacah, and they cast up a mound against the Iyar, and it stood against the chayal (rampart); and all the im (people) who were with Yawaab battered the wall, to napal (throw) it down.
Then a chakam (wise) ashah (woman) cried out of the Iyar, "Hear, hear! Please amar (say) to Yawaab, ‘qarab (come) near here, that I may dabar (speak) with you.'
He came qarab (near) to her; and the ashah (woman) said, "Are you Yawaab?" He answered, "I am." Then she said to him, "Hear the dabar (words) of your handmaid." He answered, "I do hear.
Then she spoke, saying, "They were used to dabar (say) in raashawan (old) times, ‘They shall shaal (surely) shaal (ask) counsel at Abal;' and so they settled it.

I am among those who are shalam (peaceable) and aman (faithful) in Yasharaal (Israel). You seek to mawath (destroy) a Iyar and a am (mother) in Yasharaal (Israel). Why will you balai (swallow) up the nachalah (inheritance) of Yahawah?
Yawaab answered, "Far be it, far be it from me, that I should balai (swallow) up or shachath (destroy).

The dabar (matter) is not so. But a ayash (man) of the har (hill) country of Aparayam, Shabai the ban (son) of Bakaray by sham (name), has lifted up his yad (hand) against the malak (king), even against Dawad. nathan (deliver) him only, and I will depart from the Iyar." The ashah (woman) said to Yawaab, "Behold, his raash (head) shall be thrown to you over the wall.

Then the ashah (woman) went to all the im (people) in her chakamah (wisdom). They karath (cut) off the raash (head) of Shabai the ban (son) of Bakaray, and threw it out to Yawaab. He blew the trumpet, and they were dispersed from the Iyar, every ayash (man) to his ahal (tent). Yawaab returned to Yarawashalam to the malak (king).
Now Yawaab was over all the tzabaa (army) of Yasharaal (Israel); and Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai was over the Karathay (Cherethites) and over the Palathay (Pelethites);
and Adaram was over the men subject to forced mas (labor); and Yahawashapat the ban (son) of Achayalawad was the zakar (recorder);
and Shayaa was scribe; and Tzadawaq and Abayathar were kahan (priests);
and also Iyaraa the Yaaray was kahan (chief) minister to Dawad.

There was a famine in the yawam (days) of Dawad shalawash (three) Shanah, Shanah achar (after) Shanah; and Dawad sought the panayam (face) of Yahawah. Yahawah said, "It is for Shaawal, and for his bloody bayath (house), because he put to mawath (death) the Gabainay (Gibeonites).

The malak (king) called the Gabainay (Gibeonites), and said to them (now the Gabainay (Gibeonites) were not of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), but of the yathar (remnant) of the Amaray (Amorites); and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) had sworn to them: and Shaawal sought to kill them in his zeal for the children of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah));
and Dawad said to the Gabainay (Gibeonites), "What shall I do for you? And with what shall I make kapar (atonement), that you may barak (bless) the nachalah (inheritance) of Yahawah?

The Gabainay (Gibeonites) said to him, "It is no matter of kasap (silver) or gold between us and Shaawal, or his bayath (house); neither is it for us to put any ayash (man) to mawath (death) in Yasharaal (Israel)." He said, "Whatever you amar (say), that will I do for you.
They said to the malak (king), "The ayash (man) who consumed us, and who devised against us, that we should be destroyed from remaining in any of the borders of Yasharaal (Israel),

let shabai (seven) men of his ban (sons) be delivered to us, and we will yaqai (hang) them up to Yahawah in Gabaih of Shaawal, the Bachayar of Yahawah." The malak (king) said, "I will nathan (give) them.

But the malak (king) spared Mapayabashath, the ban (son) of Yahawanathan the ban (son) of Shaawal, because of yahawah (yahweh's) shabawaih (oath) that was between them, between Dawad and Yahawanathan the ban (son) of Shaawal.

But the malak (king) took the shanayam (two) ban (sons) of Ratzapah the bath (daughter) of Ayah, whom she bore to Shaawal, Aramanay and Mapayabashath; and the chamash (five) ban (sons) of Mayakal the bath (daughter) of Shaawal, whom she bore to Idarayaal the ban (son) of Barazalay the Machalathay.

He delivered them into the yad (hands) of the Gabainay (Gibeonites), and they hanged them in the har (mountain) panayam (before) Yahawah, and all shabai (seven) of them napal (fell) together. They were put to mawath (death) in the yawam (days) of harvest, in the raashawan (first) days, at the thachalah (beginning) of barley harvest.

Ratzapah the bath (daughter) of Ayah took sackcloth, and natah (spread) it for her on the tzawar (rock), from the thachalah (beginning) of harvest until mayam (water) was poured on them from the sky. She allowed neither the birds of the sky to nawach (rest) on them by yawamam (day), nor the animals of the shadah (field) by layal (night).
It was told Dawad what Ratzapah the bath (daughter) of Ayah, the concubine of Shaawal, had done.

Dawad went and took the itzam (bones) of Shaawal and the itzam (bones) of Yahawanathan his ban (son) from the men Yabash Jabesh Gilead, who had stolen them from the street of Bayathashaan Shan, where the Palashathay (Philistines) had hanged them, in the yawam (day) that the Palashathay (Philistines) killed Shaawal in Galabai;
and he brought up from there the itzam (bones) of Shaawal and the itzam (bones) of Yahawanathan his ban (son): and they gathered the itzam (bones) of those who were hanged.

They buried the itzam (bones) of Shaawal and Yahawanathan his ban (son) in the aratz (country) of Banayamayan Tzalai Zela, in the tomb of Qayash his ab (father): and they performed all that the malak (king) tzawah (commanded). achar (after) that Alahayam was entreated for the aratz (land).
The Palashathay (Philistines) had war again with Yasharaal (Israel); and Dawad went down, and his ibad (servants) with him, and fought against the Palashathay (Philistines). Dawad grew faint;

and Yashabawabanab, who was of the yalayad (sons) of the Rapaa, the weight of whose spear was shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shekels of brass in weight, he being armed with a Chadash sword, thought to have slain Dawad.

But Abayashay the ban (son) of Tzarawayah helped him, and struck the Palashathay (Philistine), and killed him. Then the men of Dawad swore to him, saying, "You shall yatzaa (go) no more out with us to battle, that you don't quench the nayar (lamp) of Yasharaal (Israel).
It came to pass achar (after) this, that there was again war with the Palashathay (Philistines) at Gab: then Sabakay the Chashathay killed Sap, who was of the yalayad (sons) of the Rapaa.

There was again war with the Palashathay (Philistines) at Gab; and Alachanan the ban (son) of Yairayaaragayam the Bayathahalachamay killed Galayath the Gathay brother, the itz (staff) of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.

There was again war at gath (gath), where there was a ayash (man) of great stature, who had on every yad (hand) shash (six) fingers, and on every ragal (foot) shash (six) toes, arabai (four) and isharayam (twenty) in number; and he also was yalad (born) to the Rapaa.
When he defied Yasharaal (Israel), Yahawanathan the ban (son) of Shamaia, Dawad ach (brother), killed him.
These arabai (four) were yalad (born) to the Rapaa in gath (gath); and they napal (fell) by the yad (hand) of Dawad, and by the yad (hand) of his ibad (servants).
Dawad spoke to Yahawah the dabar (words) of this song in the yawam (day) that Yahawah delivered him out of the kap (hand) of all his ayab (enemies), and out of the kap (hand) of Shaawal:
and he said, "Yahawah is my salai (rock), my fortress, and my deliverer, even mine;

Alahayam, my tzawar (rock), in him I will take refuge; my magan (shield), and the qaran (horn) of my yashai (salvation), my high tower, and my manawas (refuge). My savior, you yashai (save) me from violence.
I will qaraa (call) on Yahawah, who is halal (worthy) to be praised: So shall I be saved from my ayab (enemies).
For the waves of mawath (death) surrounded me. The nachal (floods) of ungodliness made me afraid.
The cords of shaawal (sheol) were around me. The snares of mawath (death) caught me.
In my tzar (distress) I called on Yahawah. Yes, I called to my Alahayam. He heard my qawal (voice) out of his hayakal (temple). My cry came into his ears.
Then the aratz (earth) shook and trembled. The foundations of shamayam (heaven) quaked and were shaken, because he was charah (angry).
ishan (smoke) went up out of his ap (nostrils). ash (fire) out of his pah (mouth) devoured. Coals were kindled by it.
He bowed the shamayam (heavens) also, and came down. Thick irapal (darkness) was under his feet.
He rode on a karawab (cherub), and flew. Yes, he was seen on the wings of the rawach (wind).
He made chashak (darkness) sakah (pavilions) around himself: gathering of mayam (waters), and thick clouds of the shachaq (skies).
At the nagah (brightness) before him, coals of ash (fire) were kindled.
Yahawah thundered from shamayam (heaven). The Most Ilayawan uttered his qawal (voice).
He sent out chatz (arrows), and scattered them; lightning, and confused them.
Then the apayaq (channels) of the yam (sea) raah (see). The foundations of the world were laid bare by the rebuke of Yahawah, At the nashamah (blast) of the rawach (breath) of his ap (nostrils).
He sent from on high and he took me. He drew me out of many mayam (waters).
He delivered me from my iz (strong) ayab (enemy), from those who hated me, for they were too mighty for me.
They came on me in the yawam (day) of my calamity, but Yahawah was my support.
He also brought me out into a large place. He delivered me, because he delighted in me.
Yahawah rewarded me according to my tzadaqah (righteousness). He rewarded me according to the cleanness of my yad (hands).
For I have kept the darak (ways) of Yahawah, and have not wickedly departed from my Alahayam.
For all his mashapat (ordinances) were before me. As for his chaqah (statutes), I did not sawar (depart) from them.
I was also thamayam (perfect) toward him. I kept myself from my iwan (iniquity).
Therefore Yahawah has rewarded me according to my tzadaqah (righteousness), According to my cleanness in his eyesight.
With the chasayad (merciful) you will show yourself merciful. With the thamayam (perfect) gabawar (man) you will show yourself thamayam (perfect).
With the Barar you will show yourself Barar. With the Iqash you will show yourself shrewd.
You will yashai (save) the Inay im (people), But your iyan (eyes) are on the haughty, that you may bring them down.
For you are my nayar (lamp), Yahawah. Yahawah will nagah (light) up my chashak (darkness).
For by you, I run against a gadawad (troop). By my Alahayam, I leap over a wall.
As for Al, his darak (way) is thamayam (perfect). The amarah (sayings) of Yahawah is tested. He is a magan (shield) to all those who take refuge in him.
For who is Al, balaiday (besides) Yahawah? Who is a tzawar (rock), balaiday (besides) our Alahayam?
Al is my maiwaz (strong) fortress. He makes my darak (way) thamayam (perfect).
He makes his feet like hinds' feet, and imad (sets) me on my bamah (high) places.
He teaches my yad (hands) to war, so that my zarawai (arms) bend a qashath (bow) of brass.
You have also given me the magan (shield) of your yashai (salvation). Your gentleness has made me great.
You have enlarged my steps under me. My feet have not slipped.
I have pursued my ayab (enemies) and destroyed them. I didn't shawab (turn back / repent) again until they were consumed.
I have consumed them, and struck them through, so that they can't qawam (arise). Yes, they have fallen under my feet.
For you have armed me with chayal (strength) for the battle. You have subdued under me those who rose up qawam (against) me.
You have also made my ayab (enemies) irap (turn) their backs to me, that I might tzamath (cut) off those who shanaa (hate) me.
They looked, but there was none to yashai (save); even to Yahawah, but he didn't answer them.
Then I beat them as small as the ipar (dust) of the aratz (earth). I crushed them as the mire of the streets, and spread them abroad.

You also have delivered me from the rayab (strivings) of my im (people). You have kept me to be the raash (head) of the gawayam (nations). A im (people) whom I have not yadai (known) will ibad (serve) me.
The foreigners will submit themselves to me. As soon as they hear of me, they will obey me.
The foreigners will fade away, and will come trembling out of their close places.
Yahawah chay (lives)! Blessed be my tzawar (rock)! Exalted be Alahayam, the tzawar (rock) of my yashai (salvation),
even the Al who executes vengeance for me, who yarad (brings) down im (peoples) under me,
who yatzaa (brings) me away from my ayab (enemies). Yes, you lift me up above those who qawam (rise) up against me. You natzal (deliver) me from the violent ayash (man).
Therefore I will give yadah (thanks) to you, Yahawah, among the gawayam (nations). Will sing zamar (praises) to your sham (name).
He gives great yashawaih (deliverance) to his malak (king), and shows loving chasad (kindness) to his mashayach (anointed), to Dawad and to his zarai (seed), forevermore.

Now these are the Acharawan dabar (words) of Dawad. Dawad the ban (son) of Yashay says, the gabar (man) who was raised on high says, the mashayach (anointed) of the Alahayam of Yaiqab, the Naiyam psalmist of Yasharaal (Israel):
"The rawach (spirit) of Yahawah spoke by me. His malah (word) was on my lashawan (tongue).
The Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) said, the tzawar (rock) of Yasharaal (Israel) spoke to me, ‘One who mashal (rules) over men righteously, who mashal (rules) in the yaraah (fear) of Alahayam,

shall be as the awar (light) of the baqar (morning), when the shamash (sun) zarach (rises), a baqar (morning) laa (without) clouds, when the tender grass springs out of the aratz (earth), through clear nagah (shining) after rain.'

Most certainly my bayath (house) is not so with Al, yet he has made with me an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant), ordered in all things, and shamar (sure), for it is all my yashai (salvation), and all my Chapatz, although he doesn't make it grow.
But all of the balayail (ungodly) shall be as thorns to be nadad (thrust) away, because they can't be taken with the yad (hand),
But the ayash (man) who touches them must be armed with barazal (iron) and the itz (staff) of a spear. They shall be sharap (utterly) burned with ash (fire) in their place.

These are the sham (names) of the gabawar (mighty) men whom Dawad had: Josheb Basshebeth a Thachakamanay, raash (chief) of the shalayash (captains); the same was Idayanaw the Itzan, against shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) Chalal at one paim (time).

achar (after) him was Alaizar the ban (son) Dawadaw Dodai the son of an Achawachay (Ahohite), one of the shalawash (three) gabawar (mighty) men with Dawad, when they defied the Palashathay (Philistines) who were there gathered asap (together) to battle, and the men of Yasharaal (Israel) were gone ilah (away).

He qawam (arose), and struck the Palashathay (Philistines) until his yad (hand) was weary, and his yad (hand) froze to the charab (sword); and Yahawah worked a gadawal (great) thashawaih (victory) that yawam (day); and the im (people) returned achar (after) him only to take spoil.

achar (after) him was Shamah the ban (son) of Agaa a Hararay. The Palashathay (Philistines) were gathered asap (together) into a chay (troop), where there was a plot of shadah (ground) Malaa of lentils; and the im (people) fled from the Palashathay (Philistines).
But he stood in the midst of the plot, and defended it, and killed the Palashathay (Philistines); and Yahawah worked a gadawal (great) thashawaih (victory).

shalawash (three) of the shalawashayam (thirty) raash (chief) men went down, and came to Dawad in the harvest time to the cave of Idalam; and the chay (troop) of the Palashathay (Philistines) was encamped in the valley of Rapaa (Rephaim).
Dawad was then in the stronghold; and the garrison of the Palashathay (Philistines) was then in Bayathalacham.
Dawad longed, and said, "Oh that one would give me mayam (water) to shaqah (drink) of the bawar (well) of Bayathalacham, which is by the gate!

The shalawash (three) gabawar (mighty) men broke through the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and drew mayam (water) out of the bawar (well) of Bayathalacham, that was by the gate, and took it, and brought it to Dawad: but he would not drink of it, but poured it out to Yahawah.

He said, "Be it far from me, Yahawah, that I should do this! Isn't it the dam (blood) of the men who went in napash (jeopardy) of their lives?" Therefore he would not drink it. The shalawash (three) gabawar (mighty) men did these things.

Abayashay, the ach (brother) of Yawaab, the ban (son) of Tzarawayah, was raash (chief) of the shalayashay (three). He lifted up his spear against shalawash (three) maah (hundred) and Chalal them, and had a sham (name) among the shalawash (three).
Wasn't he most honorable of the shalawash (three)? therefore he was made their shar (captain): however he didn't bawaa (attain) to the shalawash (three).

Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai, the ban (son) of a chayal (valiant) ayash (man) of Qabatzaal, who had done rab (mighty) pail (deeds), he killed the shanayam (two) Arayaal of Ariel of Mawaab: he went down also and killed a aray (lion) in the midst of a bawar (pit) in yawam (time) of snow.

He killed an Matzaray (Egyptian), a goodly ayash (man): and the Matzaray (Egyptian) had a spear in his yad (hand); but he went down to him with a shabat (staff), and plucked the spear out of the Matzaray yad (hand), and killed him with his own spear.
Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai did these things, and had a sham (name) among the shalawash (three) gabawar (mighty) men.
He was more honorable than the shalawashayam (thirty), but he didn't bawaa (attain) to the shalawash (three). Dawad shawam (set) him over his guard.
Ishahaal the ach (brother) of Yawaab was one of the shalawashayam (thirty); Alachanan the ban (son) of Dawadaw of Bayathalacham,
Shamah the Charaday (Harodite), Alayaqaa the Charaday (Harodite),
Chalatz the Palatay (Paltite), Iyaraa the ban (son) of Iqash the Thaqawaiy (Tekoite),
Abayaizar the Inathathay (Anathothite), Mabanay the Chashathay,
Tzalamawan the Achawachay (Ahohite), Maharay the Natapathay (Netophathite),
Chalab the ban (son) of Bainah the Natapathay (Netophathite), Athay the ban (son) of Rayabay of Gabaih of the children of Banayamayan,
Banayah a Paraithawanay, Haday of the nachal (brooks) of Gaish.
Abayailabawan the Irabathay, Izamawath the Barachamay,
Alayachabaa the Shailabanay, the ban (sons) of Yashan, Yahawanathan,
Shamah the Hararay, Achayaam the ban (son) of Sharar the Hararay,
Alayapalat the ban (son) of Achasabay, the ban (son) Maikathay the Maacathite, Alayaim the ban (son) of Achayathapal the Gayalanay,
Chatzaraw the Karamalay, Pairay the Arabay,
Yagaal the ban (son) of Nathan of Tzawabaa, Banay the Gaday (Gadite),
Tzalaq the Imawanay (Ammonite), Nacharay the Baarathay (Beerothite), armor bearers to Yawaab the ban (son) of Tzarawayah,
Iyaraa the Yatharay, Garab the Yatharay,
Awarayah the Chathay (Hittite): shalawashayam (thirty) - shabai (seven) in all.
Again the ap (anger) of Yahawah was kindled against Yasharaal (Israel), and he moved Dawad amar (against) them, saying, "yalak (go), number Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah).

The malak (king) said to Yawaab the shar (captain) of the chayal (army), who was with him, "Now go back and forth through all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), Dan Dan Baarashabai to Beersheba, and paqad (number) the im (people), that I may yadai (know) the sum of the im (people).

Yawaab said to the malak (king), "Now may Yahawah your Alahayam add to the im (people), however many they may be, one maah (hundred) times; and may the iyan (eyes) of my Adawan the malak (king) raah (see) it. But why does my Adawan the malak (king) delight in this thing?

Notwithstanding, the malak (king's) dabar (word) prevailed against Yawaab, and against the shar (captains) of the chayal (army). Yawaab and the shar (captains) of the chayal (army) went out from the panayam (presence) of the malak (king), to paqad (number) the im (people) of Yasharaal (Israel).
They passed over the Yaradan, and encamped in Irawair, on the yamayan (right) side of the Iyar that is in the middle of the nachal (valley) of Gad, and to Yaizayar:
then they came to Galaid, and to the aratz (land) of Thachathayamachadashay Hodshi; and they came to Danayain Jaan, and around to Tzayadawan,
and came to the stronghold of Tzar, and to all the Iyar of the Chaway (Hivites), and of the Kanainay (Canaanites); and they went out to the Nagab of Yahawadah (Judah), Baarashabai Beersheba.
So when they had gone back and forth through all the aratz (land), they came to Yarawashalam at the end of thashai (nine) chadash (months) and isharayam (twenty) yawam (days).

Yawaab gave up the sum of the numbering of the im (people) to the malak (king): and there were in Yasharaal (Israel) shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) chayal (valiant) men who drew the charab (sword); and the men of Yahawadah (Judah) were chamash (five) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) men.

Dawad lab (heart) struck him achar (after) that he had numbered the im (people). Dawad said to Yahawah, "I have sinned maad (greatly) in that which I have done. But now, Yahawah, ibar (put) away, I beg you, the iwan (iniquity) of your ibad (servant); for I have done very foolishly.
When Dawad rose up in the baqar (morning), the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to the nabayaa (prophet) Gad, Dawad chazah (seer), saying,
"halak (go) and amar (speak) to Dawad, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "I offer you shalawash (three) things. Choose one of them, that I may do it to you."'

So Gad came to Dawad, and told him, and said to him, "Shall shabai (seven) Shanah of famine bawaa (come) to you in your aratz (land)? Or will you flee shalawash (three) chadash (months) panayam (before) your tzar (foes) while they pursue you? Or shall there be shalawash (three) yawam (days)' dabar (pestilence) in your aratz (land)? Now yadai (answer), and raah (see) dabar (what) answer I shall shawab (turn back / repent) to him who sent me.

Dawad said to Gad, "I am in tzarar (distress). Let us napal (fall) now into the yad (hand) of Yahawah; for his racham (mercies) are rab (great). Let me not napal (fall) into the yad (hand) of adam (man).

So Yahawah sent a dabar (pestilence) on Yasharaal (Israel) from the baqar (morning) even to the mawaid (appointed) ith (time); and there died of the im (people) Dan Dan Baarashabai to Beersheba shabaiyam (seventy) alap (thousand) men.

When the malaak (angel) stretched out his yad (hand) toward Yarawashalam to shachath (destroy) it, Yahawah relented of the disaster, and said to the malaak (angel) who destroyed the im (people), "It is rab (enough). Now rapah (stay) your yad (hand)." The malaak (angel) of Yahawah was by the threshing floor of Arawanah the Yabawasay (Jebusite).

Dawad spoke to Yahawah when he saw the malaak (angel) who struck the im (people), and said, "Behold, I have sinned, and I have done iwah (perversely); but these sheep, what have they done? Please let your yad (hand) be against me, and against my ab (father's) bayath (house).
Gad came that yawam (day) to Dawad, and said to him, "ilah (go) up, build an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah on the threshing floor of Arawanah the Yabawasay (Jebusite).
Dawad went up according to the dabar (saying) of Gad, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded).
Arawanah looked out, and saw the malak (king) and his ibad (servants) coming on toward him. Then Arawanah went out, and bowed himself before the malak (king) with his ap (face) to the aratz (ground).

Arawanah said, "Why has my Adawan the malak (king) bawaa (come) to his ibad (servant)?" Dawad said, "To qanah (buy) your threshing floor, to banah (build) an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah, that the magapah (plague) may be stopped from afflicting the im (people).

Arawanah said to Dawad, "Let my Adawan the malak (king) take and ilah (offer) up what seems tawab (good) to him. raah (see), the cattle for the burnt ilah (offering), and the threshing instruments and the yokes of the oxen for the itz (wood):
all this, malak (king), does Arawanah nathan (give) to the malak (king)." Arawanah said to the malak (king), "May Yahawah your Alahayam accept you.

The malak (king) said to Arawanah, "No; but I will most certainly qanah (buy) it from you for a price. I will not ilah (offer) burnt ilah (offerings) to Yahawah my Alahayam which cost me nothing." So Dawad bought the threshing floor and the oxen for chamashayam (fifty) shekels of kasap (silver).

Dawad built an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah there, and offered burnt ilah (offerings) and peace ilah (offerings). So Yahawah was entreated for the aratz (land), and the magapah (plague) was stayed from Yasharaal (Israel).
Now malak (king) Dawad was zaqan (old) and bawaa (stricken) in yawam (years); and they covered him with clothes, but he couldn't keep warm.

Therefore his ibad (servants) said to him, "Let there be sought for my Adawan the malak (king) a young virgin. Let her imad (stand) panayam (before) the malak (king), and cherish him; and let her shakab (lie) in your bosom, that my Adawan the malak (king) may keep warm.
So they sought for a Yapah young lady throughout all the borders of Yasharaal (Israel), and found Abayashag the Shawanamayath, and brought her to the malak (king).
The young lady was very Yapah; and she cherished the malak (king), and ministered to him; but the malak (king) didn't yadai (know) her intimately.
Then Adanayah the ban (son) of Chagayath exalted himself, saying, "I will be malak (king)." Then he prepared him chariots and horsemen, and chamashayam (fifty) men to run panayam (before) him.
His ab (father) had not displeased him at any yawam (time) in saying, "Why have you done so?" and he was also a very handsome man; and he was yalad (born) achar (after) Abayashalawam.
He conferred with Yawaab the ban (son) of Tzarawayah, and with Abayathar the kahan (priest): and they following Adanayah helped him.

But Tzadawaq the kahan (priest), and Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai, and Nathan the nabayaa (prophet), and Shamaiy, and Raiy, and the gabawar (mighty) men who belonged to Dawad, were not with Adanayah.

Adanayah killed sheep and cattle and fatlings by the aban (stone) of Zachalath, which is beside Iyanaragal Rogel; and he called all his ach (brothers), the malak (king's) ban (sons), and all the men of Yahawadah (Judah), the malak (king's) ibad (servants):
but Nathan the nabayaa (prophet), and Banayah, and the gabawar (mighty) men, and Shalamah his ach (brother), he didn't qaraa (call).
Then Nathan spoke to Bathashabai the am (mother) of Shalamah, saying, "Haven't you heard that Adanayah the ban (son) of Chagayath malak (reigns), and Dawad our Adawan doesn't yadai (know) it?
Now therefore yalak (come), please let me give you yaitz (counsel), that you may malat (save) your own napash (life), and the napash (life) of your ban (son) Shalamah.

yalak (go) in to malak (king) Dawad, and amar (tell) him, ‘Didn't you, my Adawan, malak (king), shabai (swear) to your handmaid, saying, Assuredly Shalamah your ban (son) shall malak (reign) achar (after) me, and he shall yashab (sit) on my kasaa (throne)? Why then does Adanayah malak (reign)?'
Behold, while you yet dabar (talk) there with the malak (king), I also will bawaa (come) in achar (after) you, and malaa (confirm) your dabar (words).
Bathashabai went in to the malak (king) into the room. The malak (king) was very zaqan (old); and Abayashag the Shawanamayath was ministering to the malak (king).
Bathashabai bowed, and showed respect to the malak (king). The malak (king) said, "What would you like?

She said to him, "My Adawan, you swore by Yahawah your Alahayam to your handmaid, ‘Assuredly Shalamah your ban (son) shall malak (reign) achar (after) me, and he shall yashab (sit) on my kasaa (throne).'
Now, behold, Adanayah malak (reigns); and you, my Adawan the malak (king), don't yadai (know) it.

He has slain cattle and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and has called all the ban (sons) of the malak (king), and Abayathar the kahan (priest), and Yawaab the shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army); but he hasn't called Shalamah your ibad (servant).

You, my Adawan the malak (king), the iyan (eyes) of all Yasharaal (Israel) are on you, that you should nagad (tell) them who shall yashab (sit) on the kasaa (throne) of my Adawan the malak (king) achar (after) him.
Otherwise it will happen, when my Adawan the malak (king) shall sleep with his abawath (fathers), that I and my ban (son) Shalamah shall be counted chataa (offenders).
Behold, while she yet talked with the malak (king), Nathan the nabayaa (prophet) came in.

They told the malak (king), saying, "Behold, Nathan the nabayaa (prophet)!" When he had bawaa (come) in panayam (before) the malak (king), he bowed himself before the malak (king) with his ap (face) to the aratz (ground).
Nathan said, "My Adawan, malak (king), have you said, ‘Adanayah shall malak (reign) achar (after) me, and he shall yashab (sit) on my kasaa (throne)?'

For he is gone down this yawam (day), and has slain cattle and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and has called all the malak (king's) ban (sons), and the shar (captains) of the tzabaa (army), and Abayathar the kahan (priest). Behold, they are eating and drinking panayam (before) him, and amar (say), ‘Long chayah (live) malak (king) Adanayah!'
But he hasn't called me, even me your ibad (servant), and Tzadawaq the kahan (priest), and Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai, and your ibad (servant) Shalamah.
Is this thing done by my Adawan the malak (king), and you haven't shown to your ibad (servants) who should yashab (sit) on the kasaa (throne) of my Adawan the malak (king) achar (after) him?
Then malak (king) Dawad answered, "qaraa (call) to me Bathashabai." She came into the malak (king's) panayam (presence), and stood panayam (before) the malak (king).
The malak (king) swore, and said, "As Yahawah chay (lives), who has padah (redeemed) my napash (soul) out of all tzarah (adversity),

most certainly as I swore to you by Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, ‘Assuredly Shalamah your ban (son) shall malak (reign) achar (after) me, and he shall yashab (sit) on my kasaa (throne) in my place;' most ishah (certainly) so will I do this yawam (day).
Then Bathashabai bowed with her ap (face) to the aratz (earth), and showed respect to the malak (king), and said, "Let my Adawan malak (king) Dawad chayah (live) iwalam (forever)!
malak (king) Dawad said, "qaraa (call) to me Tzadawaq the kahan (priest), Nathan the nabayaa (prophet), and Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai." They came panayam (before) the malak (king).
The malak (king) said to them, "Take with you the ibad (servants) of your Adawan, and cause Shalamah my ban (son) to ride on my own mule, and yarad (bring) him down to Gayachawan.

Let Tzadawaq the kahan (priest) and Nathan the nabayaa (prophet) mashach (anoint) him there malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel). Blow the trumpet, and amar (say), ‘Long chayah (live) malak (king) Shalamah!'

Then you shall ilah (come) up achar (after) him, and he shall bawaa (come) and yashab (sit) on my kasaa (throne); for he shall be malak (king) in my place. I have appointed him to be nagayad (prince) over Yasharaal (Israel) and over Yahawadah (Judah).
Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai answered the malak (king), and said, "aman (amen). May Yahawah, the Alahayam of my Adawan the malak (king), amar (say) so.
As Yahawah has been with my Adawan the malak (king), even so may he be with Shalamah, and make his kasaa (throne) greater than the kasaa (throne) of my Adawan malak (king) Dawad.

So Tzadawaq the kahan (priest), and Nathan the nabayaa (prophet), and Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai, and the Karathay (Cherethites) and the Palathay (Pelethites), went down, and caused Shalamah to ride on malak (king) Dawad mule, and brought him to Gayachawan.

Tzadawaq the kahan (priest) took the qaran (horn) of shaman (oil) out of the ahal (tent), and mashach (anointed) Shalamah. They blew the trumpet; and all the im (people) said, "Long chayah (live) malak (king) Shalamah!
All the im (people) came up achar (after) him, and the im (people) piped with pipes, and Shamach with gadawal (great) joy, so that the aratz (earth) shook with their qawal (sound).

Adanayah and all the qaraa (guests) who were with him heard it as they had made an kalah (end) of eating. When Yawaab heard the qawal (sound) of the trumpet, he said, "Why is this qawal (noise) of the city being in an uproar?
While he yet spoke, behold, Yawanathan the ban (son) of Abayathar the kahan (priest) came: and Adanayah said, "bawaa (come) in; for you are a worthy ayash (man), and bashar (bring) tawab (good) news.
Yawanathan answered Adanayah, "Most certainly our Adawan malak (king) Dawad has made Shalamah malak (king).

The malak (king) has sent with him Tzadawaq the kahan (priest), Nathan the nabayaa (prophet), Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai, and the Karathay (Cherethites) and the Palathay (Pelethites); and they have caused him to ride on the malak (king's) mule.

Tzadawaq the kahan (priest) and Nathan the nabayaa (prophet) have mashach (anointed) him malak (king) in Gayachawan. They have ilah (come) up from there Shamach, so that the city rang again. This is the qawal (noise) that you have heard.
Also, Shalamah yashab (sits) on the kasaa (throne) of the malawakah (kingdom).

Moreover the malak (king's) ibad (servants) came to barak (bless) our Adawan malak (king) Dawad, saying, ‘May your Alahayam make the sham (name) of Shalamah yatab (better) than your sham (name), and make his kasaa (throne) greater than your kasaa (throne);' and the malak (king) bowed himself on the bed.
Also thus said the malak (king), ‘Blessed be Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), who has given one to yashab (sit) on my kasaa (throne) this yawam (day), my iyan (eyes) even seeing it.'
All the qaraa (guests) of Adanayah were afraid, and rose up, and each ayash (man) went his darak (way).
Adanayah feared panayam (because) of Shalamah; and he qawam (arose), and went, and caught chazaq (hold) on the qaran (horns) of the mazabach (altar).

It was told Shalamah, saying, "Behold, Adanayah yaraa (fears) malak (king) Shalamah; for, behold, he has laid achaz (hold) on the qaran (horns) of the mazabach (altar), saying, ‘Let malak (king) Shalamah shabai (swear) to me first that he will not mawath (kill) his ibad (servant) with the charab (sword).'
Shalamah said, "If he shows himself a chayal (worthy) ban (man), not a hair of him shall napal (fall) to the aratz (earth); but if wickedness be found in him, he shall mawath (die).
So malak (king) Shalamah sent, and they brought him down from the mazabach (altar). He came and bowed down to malak (king) Shalamah; and Shalamah said to him, "yalak (go) to your bayath (house).
Now the yawam (days) of Dawad drew qarab (near) that he should mawath (die); and he tzawah (commanded) Shalamah his ban (son), saying,
"I am going the darak (way) of all the aratz (earth). You be chazaq (strong) therefore, and show yourself a ayash (man);

and shamar (keep) the instruction of Yahawah your Alahayam, to yalak (walk) in his darak (ways), to shamar (keep) his chaqah (statutes), his matzawah (commandments), his mashapat (ordinances), and his idawath (testimonies), according to that which is written in the thawarah (law) of Mashah, that you may shakal (prosper) in all that you do, and wherever you panah (turn) yourself.

That Yahawah may qawam (establish) his dabar (word) which he spoke concerning me, saying, ‘If your children shamar (take) heed to their darak (way), to yalak (walk) panayam (before) me in truth with all their labab (heart) and with all their napash (soul), there shall not karath (fail) you,' he said, ‘a ayash (man) on the kasaa (throne) of Yasharaal (Israel).'

"Moreover you yadai (know) also what Yawaab the ban (son) of Tzarawayah did to me, even what he did to the shanayam (two) shar (captains) of the tzabaa (armies) of Yasharaal (Israel), to Abanar the ban (son) of Nar, and to Imashaa the ban (son) of Yathar, whom he killed, and shed the dam (blood) of war in shalawam (peace), and nathan (put) the dam (blood) of war on his sash that was about his waist, and in his shoes that were on his feet.
Do therefore according to your chakamah (wisdom), and don't let his gray shayabah (head) yarad (go) down to shaawal (sheol) in shalawam (peace).

But show chasad (kindness) to the ban (sons) of Barazalay the Galaiday (Gileadite), and let them be of those who akal (eat) at your table; for so they came to me when I fled from Abayashalawam your ach (brother).

"Behold, there is with you Shamaiy the ban (son) of Garaa, the Banayamayanay (Benjamite), of Bacharayam, who cursed me with a grievous qalalah (curse) in the yawam (day) when I went to Machanayam; but he came down to qaraah (meet) me at the Yaradan, and I swore to him by Yahawah, saying, ‘I will not put you to mawath (death) with the charab (sword).'

Now therefore don't hold him guiltless, for you are a chakam (wise) ayash (man); and you will yadai (know) what you ought to do to him, and you shall bring his gray shayabah (head) down to shaawal (sheol) with dam (blood).
Dawad slept with his abawath (fathers), and was buried in the Iyar of Dawad.

The yawam (days) that Dawad reigned over Yasharaal (Israel) were arabaiyam (forty) Shanah; he reigned shabai (seven) Shanah in Chabarawan, and he reigned shalawashayam (thirty) - shalawash (three) Shanah in Yarawashalam.
Shalamah sat on the kasaa (throne) of Dawad his ab (father); and his malakawath (kingdom) was firmly established.
Then Adanayah the ban (son) of Chagayath came to Bathashabai the am (mother) of Shalamah. She said, "Do you bawaa (come) peaceably?" He said, "Peaceably.
He said moreover, I have something to tell you." She dabar (said), "dabar (say) on.

He said, "You yadai (know) that the malawakah (kingdom) was mine, and that all Yasharaal (Israel) shawam (set) their panayam (faces) on me, that I should malak (reign). However the malawakah (kingdom) is turned around, and has become my ach (brother's); for it was his from Yahawah.
Now I shaal (ask) one petition of you. Don't shawab (turn back / repent) me." She said to him, "dabar (say) on.
He said, "Please amar (speak) to Shalamah the malak (king) (for he will not tell you ‘no'), that he nathan (give) me Abayashag the Shawanamayath as ashah (wife).
Bathashabai said, "Alright. I will dabar (speak) for you to the malak (king).

Bathashabai therefore went to malak (king) Shalamah, to dabar (speak) to him for Adanayah. The malak (king) rose up to qaraah (meet) her, and bowed himself to her, and sat down on his kasaa (throne), and caused a kasaa (throne) to be shawam (set) for the malak (king's) am (mother); and she sat on his right yamayan (hand).

Then she said, "I shaal (ask) one qatan (small) petition of you; don't shawab (turn back / repent) me." The malak (king) said to her, "Ask on, my am (mother); for I will not shawab (turn back / repent) you.
She said, "Let Abayashag the Shawanamayath be given to Adanayah your ach (brother) as ashah (wife).

malak (king) Shalamah answered his am (mother), "Why do you shaal (ask) Abayashag the Shawanamayath for Adanayah? shaal (ask) for him the malawakah (kingdom) also; for he is my gadawal (elder) ach (brother); even for him, and for Abayathar the kahan (priest), and for Yawaab the ban (son) of Tzarawayah.
Then malak (king) Shalamah swore by Yahawah, saying, "Alahayam do so to me, and more also, if Adanayah has not spoken this dabar (word) against his own napash (life).

Now therefore as Yahawah chay (lives), who has established me, and yashab (set) me on the kasaa (throne) of Dawad my ab (father), and who has made me a bayath (house), as he promised, surely Adanayah shall be put to mawath (death) this yawam (day).
malak (king) Shalamah sent by Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai; and he fell on him, so that he died.

To Abayathar the kahan (priest) the malak (king) said, "yalak (go) to Inathawath, to your own shadah (fields); for you are ayash (worthy) of mawath (death). But I will not at this yawam (time) put you to mawath (death), because you bore the arawan (ark) of the Adanay Yahawah panayam (before) Dawad my ab (father), and because you were afflicted in all in which my ab (father) was afflicted.
So Shalamah thrust out Abayathar from being kahan (priest) to Yahawah, that he might fulfill the dabar (word) of Yahawah, which he spoke concerning the bayath (house) of Ilay in Shayalah.

The news came to Yawaab; for Yawaab had turned achar (after) Adanayah, though he didn't natah (turn) achar (after) Abayashalawam. Yawaab fled to the ahal (tent) of Yahawah, and caught chazaq (hold) on the qaran (horns) of the mazabach (altar).

It was told malak (king) Shalamah, "Yawaab has fled to the ahal (tent) of Yahawah, and behold, he is by the mazabach (altar)." Then Shalamah sent Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai, saying, "yalak (go), pagai (fall) on him.

Banayah came to the ahal (tent) of Yahawah, and said to him, "Thus amar (says) the malak (king), ‘yatzaa (come) forth!'" He said, "No; but I will mawath (die) here." Banayah brought the malak (king) dabar (word) again, saying, "Thus said Yawaab, and thus he answered me.

The malak (king) said to him, "Do as he has said, and pagai (fall) on him, and bury him; that you may sawar (take) away the dam (blood), which Yawaab shed without cause, from me and from my ab (father's) bayath (house).

Yahawah will shawab (turn back / repent) his dam (blood) on his own raash (head), because he fell on shanayam (two) men more tzadayaq (righteous) and tawab (better) than he, and killed them with the charab (sword), and my ab (father) Dawad didn't yadai (know) it: Abanar the ban (son) of Nar, shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army) of Yasharaal (Israel), and Imashaa the ban (son) of Yathar, shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army) of Yahawadah (Judah).

So shall their dam (blood) shawab (turn back / repent) on the raash (head) of Yawaab, and on the raash (head) of his zarai (seed) iwalam (forever). But to Dawad, and to his zarai (seed), and to his bayath (house), and to his kasaa (throne), there shall be shalawam (peace) iwalam (forever) from Yahawah.
Then Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai went up, and fell on him, and killed him; and he was buried in his own bayath (house) in the madabar (wilderness).
The malak (king) nathan (put) Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai in his place over the tzabaa (army); and the malak (king) nathan (put) Tzadawaq the kahan (priest) in the place of Abayathar.
The malak (king) sent and called for Shamaiy, and said to him, "banah (build) yourself a bayath (house) in Yarawashalam, and yashab (dwell) there, and don't yatzaa (go) out from there anywhere.

For on the yawam (day) you yatzaa (go) out, and ibar (pass) over the nachal (brook) Qadarawan, yadai (know) for certain that you shall mawath (surely) mawath (die): your dam (blood) shall be on your own raash (head).
Shamaiy said to the malak (king), "The saying is tawab (good). As my Adawan the malak (king) has said, so will your ibad (servant) do." Shamaiy lived in Yarawashalam many yawam (days).

It happened at the end of shalawash (three) Shanah, that shanayam (two) of the ibad (servants) of Shamaiy ran away to Akayash, ban (son) Maikah Maacah, malak (king) of gath (gath). They told Shamaiy, saying, "Behold, your ibad (servants) are in gath (gath).
Shamaiy qawam (arose), and saddled his donkey, and went to gath (gath) to Akayash, to seek his ibad (servants); and Shamaiy went, and brought his ibad (servants) from gath (gath).
