It was told Shalamah that Shamaiy had gone from Yarawashalam to gath (gath), and had shawab (turn back / repent) again.

The malak (king) sent and called for Shamaiy, and said to him, "Didn't I shabai (adjure) you by Yahawah, and warn you, saying, ‘yadai (know) for certain, that on the yawam (day) you yatzaa (go) out, and halak (walk) abroad any where, you shall mawath (surely) mawath (die)?' You said to me, ‘The dabar (saying) that I have heard is tawab (good).'
Why then have you not kept the shabawaih (oath) of Yahawah, and the matzawah (commandment) that I have instructed you with?

The malak (king) said moreover to Shamaiy, "You yadai (know) all the wickedness which your labab (heart) is yadai (privy) to, that you did to Dawad my ab (father). Therefore Yahawah shall shawab (turn back / repent) your wickedness on your own raash (head).
But malak (king) Shalamah shall be blessed, and the kasaa (throne) of Dawad shall be established panayam (before) Yahawah iwalam (forever).
So the malak (king) tzawah (commanded) Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai; and he went out, and fell on him, so that he died. The mamalakah (kingdom) was established in the yad (hand) of Shalamah.

Shalamah made chathan (affinity) with Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam, and took Paraih bath (daughter), and brought her into the Iyar of Dawad, until he had made an kalah (end) of building his own bayath (house), and the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the wall of Yarawashalam all around.
Only the im (people) sacrificed in the bamah (high) places, because there was no bayath (house) built for the sham (name) of Yahawah until those yawam (days).
Shalamah loved Yahawah, yalak (walking) in the chaqah (statutes) of Dawad his ab (father): only he sacrificed and burnt qatar (incense) in the bamah (high) places.
The malak (king) went to Gabaiwan to zabach (sacrifice) there; for that was the gadawal (great) bamah (high) place. Shalamah offered a alap (thousand) burnt ilah (offerings) on that mazabach (altar).
In Gabaiwan Yahawah raah (see) to Shalamah in a chalawam (dream) by layal (night); and Alahayam said, "shaal (ask) what I shall nathan (give) you.

Shalamah said, "You have shown to your ibad (servant) Dawad my ab (father) gadawal (great) loving chasad (kindness), according as he walked panayam (before) you in truth, and in tzadaqah (righteousness), and in uprightness of labab (heart) with you. You have kept for him this gadawal (great) loving chasad (kindness), that you have given him a ban (son) to yashab (sit) on his kasaa (throne), as it is this yawam (day).

Now, Yahawah my Alahayam, you have made your ibad (servant) malak (king) instead of Dawad my ab (father). I am but a qatan (little) nair (child). I don't yadai (know) how to yatzaa (go) out or bawaa (come) in.
Your ibad (servant) is in the midst of your im (people) which you have chosen, a rab (great) im (people), that can't be numbered nor counted for multitude.

nathan (give) your ibad (servant) therefore an shamai (understanding) lab (heart) to shapat (judge) your im (people), that I may bayan (discern) between tawab (good) and rai (evil); for who is yakal (able) to shapat (judge) this your Kabad im (people)?
The dabar (speech) pleased the Adanay, that Shalamah had asked this thing.

Alahayam said to him, "Because you have asked this thing, and have not asked for yourself rab (long) yawam (life), neither have asked riches for yourself, nor have asked the napash (life) of your ayab (enemies), but have asked for yourself bayan (understanding) to discern justice;

behold, I have done according to your dabar (word). Behold, I have given you a chakam (wise) and an bayan (understanding) lab (heart); so that there has been none like you panayam (before) you, neither achar (after) you shall any qawam (arise) like you.
I have also given you that which you have not asked, both riches and honor, so that there shall not be any among the malak (kings) like you, all your yawam (days).
If you will yalak (walk) in my darak (ways), to shamar (keep) my chaq (statutes) and my matzawah (commandments), as your ab (father) Dawad walked, then I will lengthen your yawam (days).

Shalamah awoke; and behold, it was a chalawam (dream). Then he came to Yarawashalam, and stood panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, and offered up burnt ilah (offerings), offered peace ilah (offerings), and made a feast to all his ibad (servants).
Then shanayam (two) women who were prostitutes came to the malak (king), and stood panayam (before) him.
The one ashah (woman) said, "Oh, my Adawan, I and this ashah (woman) yashab (dwell) in one bayath (house). I yalad (delivered) a child with her in the bayath (house).

It happened the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) after I yalad (delivered), that this ashah (woman) yalad (delivered) also. We were together. There was no stranger with us in the bayath (house), just us shanayam (two) in the bayath (house).
This ashah (woman's) ban (child) died in the layal (night), because she shakab (lay) on it.
She qawam (arose) at midnight, and took my ban (son) from beside me, while your handmaid yashan (slept), and laid it in her bosom, and laid her mawath (dead) ban (child) in my bosom.
When I rose in the baqar (morning) to nurse my ban (child), behold, it was mawath (dead); but when I had looked at it in the baqar (morning), behold, it was not my ban (son), whom I bore.

The other ashah (woman) said, "No; but the chay (living) is my ban (son), and the mawath (dead) is your ban (son)." This said, "No; but the mawath (dead) is your ban (son), and the chay (living) is my ban (son)." Thus they spoke panayam (before) the malak (king).

Then the malak (king) said, "The zaath (one) amar (says), ‘This is my ban (son) who chay (lives), and your ban (son) is the mawath (dead);' and the other amar (says), ‘No; but your ban (son) is the mawath (dead) one, and my ban (son) is the chay (living) one.'
The malak (king) said, "Get me a charab (sword)." They brought a charab (sword) panayam (before) the malak (king).
The malak (king) said, "Divide the chay (living) yalad (child) in shanayam (two), and nathan (give) chatzay (half) to the one, and chatzay (half) to the other.

Then the ashah (woman) whose the chay (living) ban (child) was spoke to the malak (king), for her heart yearned over her ban (son), and she said, "Oh, my Adawan, nathan (give) her the chay (living) yalad (child), and in no way mawath (kill) it!" But the other said, "It shall be neither mine nor yours. Divide it.
Then the malak (king) answered, "nathan (give) her the chay (living) yalad (child), and in no way mawath (kill) it. She is its am (mother).

All Yasharaal (Israel) heard of the mashapat (judgment) which the malak (king) had judged; and they feared the malak (king): for they saw that the chakamah (wisdom) of Alahayam was in him, to do justice.
malak (king) Shalamah was malak (king) over all Yasharaal (Israel).
These were the shar (princes) whom he had: Izarayah the ban (son) of Tzadawaq, the kahan (priest);
Alayacharap and Achayah, the ban (sons) of Shayashaa, scribes; Yahawashapat the ban (son) of Achayalawad, the zakar (recorder);
and Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai was over the tzabaa (army); and Tzadawaq and Abayathar were kahan (priests);
and Izarayah the ban (son) of Nathan was over the natzab (officers); and Zabawad the ban (son) of Nathan was kahan (chief) minister, the malak (king's) friend;
and Achayashar was over the bayath (household); and Adanayaram the ban (son) of Ibadaa was over the men subject to forced mas (labor).

Shalamah had shanayam (twelve) natzab (officers) over all Yasharaal (Israel), who provided food for the malak (king) and his bayath (household): each achad (man) had to make provision for a chadash (month) in the Shanah.
These are their sham (names): Ben banachawar (hur), in the har (hill) country of Aparayam;
Ben Deker, in Maqatz, and in Shailabayam, and Bayathashamash Shemesh, and Ayalawanabayathachanan Beth Hanan;
Ben banachasad (hesed), Arabawath Arubboth (to him belonged Shawakah, and all the aratz (land) of Chapar);
Ben banaabayanadab (abinadab), in all the height of Dawar (he had Tapath the bath (daughter) of Shalamah as ashah (wife));

Bainaa the ban (son) of Achayalawad, in Thainak and Magadawan, and all Bayathashaan Shean which is beside Tzarathan, beneath Yazaraial, from Bayathashaan Shean to Abalamachawalah Meholah, as far as ibar (beyond) Yaqamaim;

Ben banagabar (geber), in Ramoth Galaid (to him belonged the towns of Yaayar the ban (son) of Manashah, which are in Galaid; to him belonged the region of Aragab, which is in Bashan, shashayam (sixty) gadawal (great) Iyar with walls and bronze bars);
Achayanadab the ban (son) of Idaw, in Machanayam;
Achayamaitz, in Napathalay (he also took Bashamath the bath (daughter) of Shalamah as ashah (wife));
Bainaa the ban (son) of Chawashay, in Ashar and Bailawath;
Yahawashapat the ban (son) of Parawach, in Yashashakar;
Shamaiy the ban (son) Alaa Ela, in Banayamayan;

Gabar the ban (son) of Awaray, in the aratz (land) of Galaid, the aratz (country) of Sayachawan malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites) and of Iwag malak (king) of Bashan; and he was the only officer who was in the aratz (land).
Yahawadah (Judah) and Yasharaal (Israel) were many as the sand which is by the yam (sea) in multitude, eating and drinking and making Shamach.

Shalamah ruled over all the mamalakah (kingdoms) from the nahar (river) to the aratz (land) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and to the border of Matzarayam: they brought tribute, and served Shalamah all the yawam (days) of his chay (life).
Shalamah provision for one yawam (day) was shalawashayam (thirty) measures of fine flour, and shashayam (sixty) measures of meal,

ishar (ten) head of Barayaa cattle, and isharayam (twenty) baqar (head) of cattle out of the pastures, and one maah (hundred) sheep, besides harts, and gazelles, and tzabay (roebucks), and fattened fowl.

For he had radah (dominion) over all on this ibar (side) the nahar (river), Thapasach Tiphsah even to Izah, over all the malak (kings) on this ibar (side) the nahar (river): and he had shalawam (peace) on all sides around him.
Yahawadah (Judah) and Yasharaal (Israel) lived safely, every ayash (man) under his vine and under his fig tree, Dan Dan Baarashabai to Beersheba, all the yawam (days) of Shalamah.
Shalamah had arabaiyam (forty) alap (thousand) stalls of horses for his chariots, and shanayam (twelve) alap (thousand) horsemen.
Those natzab (officers) provided food for malak (king) Shalamah, and Qarab all who came to malak (king) Shalamah table, every ayash (man) in his chadash (month); they let nothing be lacking.
Barley also and straw for the horses and swift steeds brought they to the place where the officers were, every ayash (man) according to his duty.
Alahayam gave Shalamah chakamah (wisdom) and thabawan (understanding) maad (exceeding) much, and very great lab (understanding), even as the sand that is on the seashore.
Shalamah chakamah (wisdom) excelled the chakamah (wisdom) of all the children of the qadam (east), and all the chakamah (wisdom) of Matzarayam.
For he was chakam (wiser) than all men; than Ayathan the Azarachay, and Hayaman, and Kalakal, and Daradai, the ban (sons) of Machawal: and his sham (fame) was in all the gaway (nations) all around.
He spoke shalawash (three) alap (thousand) proverbs; and his songs were one alap (thousand) chamash (five).
He spoke of itz (trees), from the cedar that is in Labanawan even to the hyssop that yatzaa (springs) out of the wall; he spoke also of animals, and of birds, and of creeping things, and of fish.
There came of all im (peoples) to hear the chakamah (wisdom) of Shalamah, from all malak (kings) of the aratz (earth), who had heard of his chakamah (wisdom).

Chayaram malak (king) of Tzar sent his ibad (servants) to Shalamah; for he had heard that they had mashach (anointed) him malak (king) in the place of his ab (father): for Chayaram was yawam (ever) a lover of Dawad.
Shalamah sent to Chayaram, saying,

"You yadai (know) how that Dawad my ab (father) could not banah (build) a bayath (house) for the sham (name) of Yahawah his Alahayam for the wars which were sabab (about) him on every side, until Yahawah nathan (put) them under the kap (soles) of his feet.
But now Yahawah my Alahayam has given me nawach (rest) on every side. There is neither shatan (adversary), nor rai (evil) occurrence.

Behold, I purpose to banah (build) a bayath (house) for the sham (name) of Yahawah my Alahayam, as Yahawah spoke to Dawad my ab (father), saying, ‘Your ban (son), whom I will nathan (set) on your kasaa (throne) in your place, he shall banah (build) the bayath (house) for my sham (name).'

Now therefore tzawah (command) that they karath (cut) me cedar trees out of Labanawan. My ibad (servants) shall be with your ibad (servants); and I will nathan (give) you wages for your ibad (servants) according to all that you shall amar (say). For you yadai (know) that there is not among us any who yadai (knows) how to karath (cut) itz (timber) like the Tzayadanay (Sidonians).

It happened, when Chayaram heard the dabar (words) of Shalamah, that he Shamach maad (greatly), and said, "Blessed is Yahawah this yawam (day), who has given to Dawad a chakam (wise) ban (son) over this rab (great) im (people).
Chayaram sent to Shalamah, saying, "I have heard the message which you have sent to me. I will do all your Chapatz concerning itz (timber) of cedar, and concerning itz (timber) of fir.

My ibad (servants) shall yarad (bring) them down from Labanawan to the yam (sea). I will shawam (make) them into rafts to go by yam (sea) to the place that you shall shalach (appoint) me, and will cause them to be broken up there, and you shall nashaa (receive) them. You shall ishah (accomplish) my Chapatz, in giving lacham (food) for my bayath (household).
So Chayaram gave Shalamah itz (timber) of cedar and itz (timber) of fir according to all his Chapatz.

Shalamah gave Chayaram isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) measures of wheat for food to his bayath (household), and isharayam (twenty) measures Kathayath pure shaman (oil). Shalamah gave this to Chayaram Shanah by Shanah.
Yahawah gave Shalamah chakamah (wisdom), as he promised him; and there was shalawam (peace) between Chayaram and Shalamah; and they shanayam (two) made a treaty together.
malak (king) Shalamah raised a levy out of all Yasharaal (Israel); and the levy was shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand) men.

He sent them to Labanawan, ishar (ten) alap (thousand) a chadash (month) by courses; a chadash (month) they were in Labanawan, and shanayam (two) chadash (months) at bayath (home); and Adanayaram was over the men subject to forced mas (labor).
Shalamah had shabaiyam (seventy) alap (thousand) who bore burdens, and shamanayam (eighty) alap (thousand) who were stone cutters in the har (mountains);

besides Shalamah shar (chief) natzab (officers) who were over the malaakah (work), shalawash (three) alap (thousand) and shalawash (three) maah (hundred), who bore radah (rule) over the im (people) who labored in the malaakah (work).
The malak (king) tzawah (commanded), and they cut out gadawal (great) aban (stones), Yaqar aban (stones), to yasad (lay) the foundation of the bayath (house) with worked aban (stone).
Shalamah banah (builders) and Chayaram banah (builders) and the Gebalites cut them, and prepared the itz (timber) and the aban (stones) to banah (build) the bayath (house).

It happened in the arabai (four) maah (hundred) and shamanayam (eightieth) Shanah after the children of Yasharaal (Israel) had yatzaa (come) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, in the rabayaiy (fourth) Shanah of Shalamah malak (reign) over Yasharaal (Israel), in the chadash (month) Zaw, which is the shanay (second) chadash (month), that he began to banah (build) the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

The bayath (house) which malak (king) Shalamah built for Yahawah, its arak (length) was shashayam (sixty) amah (cubits), and its breadth isharayam (twenty), and its height shalawashayam (thirty) amah (cubits).

The porch panayam (before) the hayakal (temple) of the bayath (house), isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) was its arak (length), according to the breadth of the bayath (house). ishar (ten) amah (cubits) was its breadth before the bayath (house).
For the bayath (house) he made windows of fixed lattice work.

Against the wall of the bayath (house) he built stories all around, against the walls of the bayath (house) all around, both of the hayakal (temple) and of the oracle; and he made side rooms all around.

The Thachathawan story was chamash (five) amah (cubits) broad, and the Thayakawan was shash (six) amah (cubits) broad, and the shalayashay (third) was shabai (seven) amah (cubits) broad; for on the outside he made offsets in the wall of the bayath (house) all around, that the beams should not have achaz (hold) in the walls of the bayath (house).

The bayath (house), when it was in building, was built of aban (stone) Shalam at the quarry; and there was neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of barazal (iron) heard in the bayath (house), while it was in building.

The door for the Thayakawan side rooms was in the Yamanay side of the bayath (house): and they went up by winding stairs into the Thayakawan story, and out of the Thayakawan into the shalayashay (third).
So he built the bayath (house), and finished it; and he covered the bayath (house) with gab (beams) and planks of cedar.
He built the stories against all the bayath (house), each chamash (five) amah (cubits) high: and they rested on the bayath (house) with itz (timber) of cedar.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Shalamah, saying,

"Concerning this bayath (house) which you are building, if you will yalak (walk) in my chaqah (statutes), and ishah (execute) my mashapat (ordinances), and shamar (keep) all my matzawah (commandments) to yalak (walk) in them; then will I qawam (establish) my dabar (word) with you, which I spoke to Dawad your ab (father).
I will shakan (dwell) among the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and will not forsake my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel).
So Shalamah built the bayath (house), and finished it.

He built the walls of the bayath (house) bayath (within) with boards of cedar: from the floor of the bayath (house) to the walls of the ceiling, he covered them on the bayath (inside) with itz (wood); and he covered the floor of the bayath (house) with boards of fir.

He built isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) on the hinder part of the bayath (house) with boards of cedar from the floor to the ceiling: he built them for it bayath (within), for an oracle, even for the most qadash (holy) place.
In front of the hayakal (temple) sanctuary was arabaiyam (forty) amah (cubits).
There was cedar on the bayath (house) within, carved with buds and open flowers: all was cedar; there was no aban (stone) seen.
He prepared an oracle in the midst of the bayath (house) within, to nathan (set) there the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah.

Within the oracle was isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) in arak (length), and isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) in breadth, and isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) in its height; and he overlaid it with pure gold: and he covered the mazabach (altar) with cedar.
So Shalamah overlaid the bayath (house) within with pure gold: and he drew chains of gold across panayam (before) the oracle; and he overlaid it with gold.
The whole bayath (house) he overlaid with gold, until all the bayath (house) was finished: also the whole mazabach (altar) that belonged to the oracle he overlaid with gold.
In the oracle he made shanayam (two) karawab (cherubim) of shaman (olive) itz (wood), each ishar (ten) amah (cubits) high.

chamash (five) amah (cubits) was the one wing of the karawab (cherub), and chamash (five) amah (cubits) the other wing of the karawab (cherub): from the uttermost part of the kanap (one) wing to the uttermost part of the other were ishar (ten) amah (cubits).
The other karawab (cherub) was ishar (ten) amah (cubits): shanayam (both) the karawab (cherubim) were of one measure and one form.
The height of the one karawab (cherub) was ishar (ten) amah (cubits), and so was it of the other karawab (cherub).

He nathan (set) the karawab (cherubim) within the Panayamay bayath (house); and the wings of the karawab (cherubim) were stretched forth, so that the wing of the one touched the qayar (one) wall, and the wing of the other karawab (cherub) touched the other wall; and their wings touched kanap (one) another in the midst of the bayath (house).
He overlaid the karawab (cherubim) with gold.
He carved all the walls of the bayath (house) around with pathawach (carved) figures of karawab (cherubim) and palm trees and open flowers, inside and Chayatzawan.
The floor of the bayath (house) he overlaid with gold, inside and Chayatzawan.
For the entrance of the oracle he made doors of shaman (olive) itz (wood): the ayal (lintel) and door posts were a chamayashay (fifth) part of the wall.

So he made shanayam (two) doors of shaman (olive) itz (wood); and he carved on them carvings of karawab (cherubim) and palm trees and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold; and he spread the gold on the karawab (cherubim), and on the palm trees.
So also made he for the entrance of the hayakal (temple) door posts of shaman (olive) itz (wood), out of a rabayaiy (fourth) part of the wall;
and shanayam (two) doors of fir itz (wood): the shanayam (two) leaves of the one door were folding, and the shanayam (two) leaves of the other door were folding.
He carved karawab (cherubim) and palm trees and open flowers; and he overlaid them with gold fitted on the engraved chaqah (work).
He built the Panayamay court with shalawash (three) courses of cut gazayath (stone), and a course of cedar beams.
In the rabayaiy (fourth) Shanah was the yasad (foundation) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah laid, in the yarach (month) Zaw.

In the eleventh Shanah, in the yarach (month) Bawal, which is the eighth yarach (month), was the bayath (house) finished throughout all its dabar (parts), and according to all its mashapat (fashion). So was he shabai (seven) Shanah in building it.
Shalamah was building his own bayath (house) thirteen Shanah, and he finished all his bayath (house).

For he built the bayath (house) of the Yair of Labanawan; its arak (length) was one maah (hundred) amah (cubits), and its breadth chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), and its height shalawashayam (thirty) amah (cubits), on arabai (four) rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams on the pillars.
It was covered with cedar above over the arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five) beams, that were on the pillars; fifteen in a row.
There were beams in shalawash (three) rows, and window was over against window in shalawash (three) paim (ranks).
All the doors and posts were made square with beams: and window was over against window in shalawash (three) paim (ranks).

He made the porch of pillars; its arak (length) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), and its breadth shalawashayam (thirty) amah (cubits); and a porch panayam (before) them; and pillars and a threshold panayam (before) them.
He made the porch of the kasaa (throne) where he was to shapat (judge), even the porch of mashapat (judgment): and it was covered with cedar from floor to floor.

His bayath (house) where he was to yashab (dwell), the other court bayath (within) the porch, was of the like maishah (work). He made also a bayath (house) for Paraih bath (daughter) (whom Solomon had taken as wife), like this porch.

All these were of Yaqar aban (stones), even of cut gazayath (stone), according to measure, sawed with saws, bayath (inside) and outside, even from the foundation to the tapach (coping), and so on the outside to the gadawal (great) court.
The yasad (foundation) was of Yaqar aban (stones), even gadawal (great) aban (stones), aban (stones) of ishar (ten) amah (cubits), and aban (stones) of shamanah (eight) amah (cubits).
Above were Yaqar aban (stones), even cut aban (stone), according to measure, and cedar wood.

The gadawal (great) court around had shalawash (three) courses of cut gazayath (stone), and a course of cedar beams; Panayamay as the inner court of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the porch of the bayath (house).
malak (king) Shalamah sent and fetched Chayaram out of Tzar.

He was the ban (son) of a widow of the matah (tribe) of Napathalay, and his ab (father) was a ayash (man) of Tzaray, a charash (worker) in brass; and he was filled with chakamah (wisdom) and thabawan (understanding) and skill, to ishah (work) all ishah (works) in brass. He came to malak (king) Shalamah, and performed all his malaakah (work).
For he fashioned the shanayam (two) pillars of brass, eighteen amah (cubits) high apiece: and a line of shanayam (twelve) amah (cubits) encircled shanay (either) of them sabab (about).

He made shanayam (two) capitals of molten brass, to nathan (set) on the raash (tops) of the pillars: the height of the one capital was chamash (five) amah (cubits), and the height of the other capital was chamash (five) amah (cubits).

There were nets of checker maishah (work), and wreaths of chain maishah (work), for the capitals which were on the raash (top) of the pillars; shabai (seven) for the one capital, and shabai (seven) for the other capital.
So he made the pillars; and there were shanayam (two) rows around on the one network, to cover the capitals that were on the raash (top) of the pillars: and he did so for the other capital.
The capitals that were on the raash (top) of the pillars in the porch were of lily maishah (work), arabai (four) amah (cubits).
There were capitals above also on the shanayam (two) pillars, close by the belly which was beside the network: and the pomegranates were two maah (hundred), in rows around on the other capital.

He qawam (set) up the pillars at the porch of the hayakal (temple): and he qawam (set) up the Yamanay pillar, and called its sham (name) Yakayan; and he qawam (set) up the Shamaalay pillar, and called its sham (name) Baiz.
On the raash (top) of the pillars was lily maishah (work): so was the maishah (work) of the pillars finished.

He made the molten yam (sea) of ishar (ten) amah (cubits) from shapah (brim) to shapah (brim), Igal in compass, and its height was chamash (five) amah (cubits); and a line of shalawashayam (thirty) amah (cubits) encircled it.
Under its shapah (brim) around there were buds which encircled it, for ishar (ten) amah (cubits), encircling the yam (sea): the buds were in shanayam (two) rows, cast when it was cast.

It stood on shanayam (twelve) oxen, shalawash (three) looking toward the tzapawan (north), and shalawash (three) looking toward the yam (west), and shalawash (three) looking toward the Nagab, and shalawash (three) looking toward the east; and the yam (sea) was set on them above, and all their hinder parts were inward.
It was a tapach (handbreadth) thick: and its shapah (brim) was worked like the shapah (brim) of a cup, like the flower of a lily: it held two alap (thousand) baths.
He made the ishar (ten) bases of brass; arabai (four) amah (cubits) was the arak (length) of one base, and arabai (four) amah (cubits) its breadth, and shalawash (three) amah (cubits) its height.
The maishah (work) of the bases was like this: they had panels; and there were panels between the ledges;

and on the panels that were between the ledges were aray (lions), oxen, and karawab (cherubim); and on the ledges there was a pedestal above; and beneath the aray (lions) and oxen were wreaths of hanging maishah (work).

achad (every) base had arabai (four) bronze wheels, and axles of brass; and the arabai (four) feet of it had supports: beneath the basin were the supports molten, with wreaths at the ibar (side) of ayash (each).

The pah (mouth) of it bayath (within) the capital and above was a amah (cubit): and its pah (mouth) was Igal after the maishah (work) of a pedestal, a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half); and also on its pah (mouth) were engravings, and their panels were foursquare, not Igal.
The arabai (four) wheels were underneath the panels; and the axles of the wheels were in the base: and the height of a wheel was a amah (cubit) and chatzay (half) a amah (cubit).
The maishah (work) of the wheels was like the maishah (work) of a chariot wheel: their axles, and their rims, and their spokes, and their naves, were all molten.
There were arabai (four) supports at the arabai (four) corners of achad (each) base: its supports were of the base itself.
In the raash (top) of the base was there a Igal compass chatzay (half) a amah (cubit) high; and on the raash (top) of the base its yad (stays) and its panels were of the same.
On the plates of its yad (stays), and on its panels, he engraved karawab (cherubim), aray (lions), and palm trees, according to the space of ayash (each), with wreaths all around.
In this way, he made the ishar (ten) bases: all of them had one casting, one measure, and one form.
He made ishar (ten) basins of brass: one basin contained arabaiyam (forty) baths; and achad (every) basin was arabai (four) amah (cubits); and on achad (every) one of the ishar (ten) bases one basin.

He nathan (set) the bases, chamash (five) on the yamayan (right) side of the bayath (house), and chamash (five) on the shamaawal (left) side of the bayath (house): and he nathan (set) the yam (sea) on the Yamanay side of the bayath (house) eastward, toward the Nagab.
Chayaram made the basins, and the shovels, and the basins. So Chayaram made an end of doing all the malaakah (work) that he worked for malak (king) Shalamah in the bayath (house) of Yahawah:

the shanayam (two) pillars, and the galah (two) bowls of the capitals that were on the raash (top) of the pillars; and the shanayam (two) networks to cover the shanayam (two) bowls of the capitals that were on the raash (top) of the pillars;

and the arabai (four) maah (hundred) pomegranates for the shanayam (two) networks; shanayam (two) rows of pomegranates for achad (each) network, to cover the shanayam (two) bowls of the capitals that were on the pillars;
and the ishar (ten) bases, and the ishar (ten) basins on the bases;
and the one yam (sea), and the shanayam (twelve) oxen under the yam (sea);
and the pots, and the shovels, and the basins: even all these vessels, which Chayaram made for malak (king) Shalamah, in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, were of burnished brass.
The malak (king) cast them in the plain of the Yaradan, in the clay adamah (ground) between Sakawath and Tzarathan.
Shalamah left all the vessels unweighed, because they were maad (exceeding) many: the weight of the brass could not be found out.
Shalamah made all the vessels that were in the bayath (house) of Yahawah: the golden mazabach (altar), and the table whereupon the show lacham (bread) was, of gold;

and the lampstands, chamash (five) on the yamayan (right) side, and chamash (five) on the shamaawal (left), panayam (before) the oracle, of pure gold; and the flowers, and the nayar (lamps), and the tongs, of gold;

and the cups, and the snuffers, and the basins, and the kap (spoons), and the machathah (fire) pans, of pure gold; and the hinges, both for the doors Panayamay the inner bayath (house), the most qadash (holy) place, and for the doors of the bayath (house), of the hayakal (temple), of gold.

Thus all the malaakah (work) that malak (king) Shalamah worked in the bayath (house) of Yahawah was finished. Shalamah brought in the things which Dawad his ab (father) had qadash (dedicated), the kasap (silver), and the gold, and the vessels, and nathan (put) them in the treasuries of the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

Then Shalamah assembled the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel), and all the raash (heads) of the matah (tribes), the nashayaa (princes) of the abawath (fathers)' households of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), to malak (king) Shalamah in Yarawashalam, to ilah (bring) up the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah out of the Iyar of Dawad, which is Tzayawan.
All the men of Yasharaal (Israel) assembled themselves to malak (king) Shalamah at the chag (feast), in the yarach (month) Ayathanayam, which is the shabayaiy (seventh) yarach (month).
All the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) came, and the kahan (priests) took up the arawan (ark).

They brought up the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, and the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and all the qadash (holy) vessels that were in the ahal (tent); even these the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites) brought up.

malak (king) Shalamah and all the idah (congregation) of Yasharaal (Israel), who were assembled to him, were with him panayam (before) the arawan (ark), sacrificing sheep and cattle, that could not be counted nor numbered for multitude.

The kahan (priests) brought in the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah to its place, into the oracle of the bayath (house), to the most qadash (holy) place, even under the wings of the karawab (cherubim).
For the karawab (cherubim) spread forth their wings over the place of the arawan (ark), and the karawab (cherubim) covered the arawan (ark) and its poles above.
The poles were so long that the raash (ends) of the poles were seen from the qadash (holy) place panayam (before) the oracle; but they were not seen outside: and there they are to this yawam (day).

There was nothing in the arawan (ark) raq (except) the shanayam (two) tables of aban (stone) which Mashah yanach (put) there at Charab, when Yahawah made a covenant with the children of Yasharaal (Israel), when they came out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
It came to pass, when the kahan (priests) had yatzaa (come) out of the qadash (holy) place, that the cloud filled the bayath (house) of Yahawah,
so that the kahan (priests) could not imad (stand) to sharath (minister) by panayam (reason) of the cloud; for the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah filled the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
Then Shalamah said, "Yahawah has said that he would shakan (dwell) in the thick irapal (darkness).
I have banah (surely) built you a bayath (house) of habitation, a place for you to dwell in iwalam (forever).
The malak (king) turned his panayam (face) sabab (about), and blessed all the qahal (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel): and all the qahal (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel) stood.
He said, "Blessed is Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), who spoke with his pah (mouth) to Dawad your ab (father), and has with his yad (hand) fulfilled it, saying,

‘Since the yawam (day) that I brought my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel) out of Matzarayam, I chose no Iyar out of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) to banah (build) a bayath (house), that my sham (name) might be there; but I chose Dawad to be over my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel).'
"Now it was in the labab (heart) of Dawad my ab (father) to banah (build) a bayath (house) for the sham (name) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
But Yahawah said to Dawad my ab (father), ‘Whereas it was in your labab (heart) to banah (build) a bayath (house) for my sham (name), you did tawab (well) that it was in your labab (heart).
raq (nevertheless), you shall not banah (build) the bayath (house); but your ban (son) who shall yatzaa (come) forth out of your body, he shall banah (build) the bayath (house) for my sham (name).'

Yahawah has established his dabar (word) that he spoke; for I have risen up in the place of Dawad my ab (father), and I yashab (sit) on the kasaa (throne) of Yasharaal (Israel), as Yahawah promised, and have built the bayath (house) for the sham (name) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).

There I have shawam (set) a place for the arawan (ark), in which is the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, which he made with our abawath (fathers), when he brought them out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
Shalamah stood panayam (before) the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah in the presence of all the qahal (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel), and spread forth his kap (hands) toward shamayam (heaven);

and he said, "Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), there is no Alahayam like you, in shamayam (heaven) above, or on aratz (earth) beneath; who shamar (keep) barayath (covenant) and loving chasad (kindness) with your ibad (servants), who halak (walk) panayam (before) you with all their lab (heart);
who have kept with your ibad (servant) Dawad my ab (father) that which you promised him. Yes, you spoke with your pah (mouth), and have fulfilled it with your yad (hand), as it is this yawam (day).

Now therefore, may Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), shamar (keep) with your ibad (servant) Dawad my ab (father) that which you have promised him, saying, ‘There shall not karath (fail) you a ayash (man) in my panayam (sight) to yashab (sit) on the kasaa (throne) of Yasharaal (Israel), if only your children shamar (take) heed to their darak (way), to yalak (walk) panayam (before) me as you have walked panayam (before) me.'
"Now therefore, Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), please let your dabar (word) be aman (verified), which you spoke to your ibad (servant) Dawad my ab (father).

But will Alahayam in very deed yashab (dwell) on the aratz (earth)? Behold, shamayam (heaven) and the shamayam (heaven) of shamayam (heavens) can't contain you; how much less this bayath (house) that I have built!

Yet have panah (respect) for the prayer of your ibad (servant), and for his supplication, Yahawah my Alahayam, to listen to the cry and to the prayer which your ibad (servant) palal (prays) panayam (before) you this yawam (day);

that your iyan (eyes) may be pathach (open) toward this bayath (house) layal (night) and yawam (day), even toward the place of which you have said, ‘My sham (name) shall be there;' to listen to the prayer which your ibad (servant) shall palal (pray) toward this place.

Listen to the supplication of your ibad (servant), and of your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), when they shall palal (pray) toward this place. Yes, hear in shamayam (heaven), your yashab (dwelling) place; and when you hear, forgive.

"If a ayash (man) chataa (sins) against his neighbor, and an alah (oath) is laid on him to cause him to alah (swear), and he bawaa (comes) and swear panayam (before) your mazabach (altar) in this bayath (house);

then hear in shamayam (heaven), and do, and shapat (judge) your ibad (servants), condemning the rashai (wicked), to nathan (bring) his darak (way) on his own raash (head), and justifying the tzadayaq (righteous), to nathan (give) him according to his tzadaqah (righteousness).

"When your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel) are struck down panayam (before) the ayab (enemy), because they have sinned against you; if they shawab (turn back / repent) again to you, and yadah (confess) your sham (name), and palal (pray) and chanan (make) supplication to you in this bayath (house):

then hear in shamayam (heaven), and forgive the chataah (sin) of your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), and shawab (turn back / repent) them again to the adamah (land) which you gave to their abawath (fathers).

"When the sky is itzar (shut) up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against you; if they palal (pray) toward this place, and yadah (confess) your sham (name), and shawab (turn back / repent) from their chataah (sin), when you afflict them:

then hear in shamayam (heaven), and forgive the chataah (sin) of your ibad (servants), and of your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), when you teach them the tawab (good) darak (way) in which they should yalak (walk); and nathan (send) rain on your aratz (land), which you have given to your im (people) for an nachalah (inheritance).

"If there is famine in the aratz (land), if there is dabar (pestilence), if there is blight, mildew, locust or caterpillar; if their ayab (enemy) besieges them in the aratz (land) of their cities; whatever nagai (plague), whatever sickness there is;

whatever prayer and supplication is made by any adam (man), or by all your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), who shall ayash (each) yadai (know) the nagai (plague) of his own labab (heart), and spread forth his kap (hands) toward this bayath (house):

then hear in shamayam (heaven), your yashab (dwelling) place, and forgive, and do, and nathan (render) to every ayash (man) according to all his darak (ways), whose labab (heart) you yadai (know); (for you, even you only, yadai (know) the labab (hearts) of all the children of men;)
that they may yaraa (fear) you all the yawam (days) that they chay (live) in the adamah (land) which you gave to our abawath (fathers).
"Moreover concerning the nakaray (foreigner), who is not of your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), when he shall bawaa (come) out of a Rachawaq aratz (country) for your sham (name's) sake

(for they shall hear of your gadawal (great) sham (name), and of your chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and of your natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm)); when he shall bawaa (come) and palal (pray) toward this bayath (house);

hear in shamayam (heaven), your yashab (dwelling) place, and do according to all that the nakaray (foreigner) qaraa (calls) to you for; that all the im (peoples) of the aratz (earth) may yadai (know) your sham (name), to yaraa (fear) you, as do your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), and that they may yadai (know) that this bayath (house) which I have built is called by your sham (name).

"If your im (people) yatzaa (go) out to battle against their ayab (enemy), by whatever way you shall shalach (send) them, and they palal (pray) to Yahawah darak (toward) the Iyar which you have chosen, and toward the bayath (house) which I have built for your sham (name);
then hear in shamayam (heaven) their prayer and their supplication, and ishah (maintain) their cause.

If they chataa (sin) against you (for there is no adam (man) who doesn't chataa (sin)), and you are angry with them, and nathan (deliver) them to the ayab (enemy), so that they carry them away captive to the aratz (land) of the ayab (enemy), Rachawaq off or qarawab (near);

yet if they shall repent in the aratz (land) where they are carried captive, and shawab (turn back / repent) again, and chanan (make) supplication to you in the aratz (land) of those who carried them captive, saying, ‘We have sinned, and have done iwah (perversely); we have dealt wickedly;'

if they shawab (turn back / repent) to you with all their labab (heart) and with all their napash (soul) in the aratz (land) of their ayab (enemies), who carried them captive, and palal (pray) to you darak (toward) their aratz (land), which you gave to their abawath (fathers), the Iyar which you have chosen, and the bayath (house) which I have built for your sham (name):
then hear their prayer and their supplication in shamayam (heaven), your yashab (dwelling) place, and ishah (maintain) their cause;

and forgive your im (people) who have sinned against you, and all their pashai (transgressions) in which they have transgressed against you; and nathan (give) them racham (compassion) panayam (before) those who carried them captive, that they may have racham (compassion) on them
(for they are your im (people), and your nachalah (inheritance), which you brought out of Matzarayam, from the midst of the furnace of barazal (iron));

that your iyan (eyes) may be pathach (open) to the supplication of your ibad (servant), and to the supplication of your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), to listen to them whenever they qaraa (cry) to you.

For you separated them from among all the im (peoples) of the aratz (earth), to be your nachalah (inheritance), as you spoke by Mashah your ibad (servant), when you brought our abawath (fathers) out of Matzarayam, Adanay Yahawah.

It was so, that when Shalamah had made an kalah (end) of praying all this prayer and supplication to Yahawah, he qawam (arose) from panayam (before) the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah, from kneeling on his knees with his kap (hands) spread forth toward shamayam (heaven).
He stood, and blessed all the qahal (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel) with a gadawal (loud) qawal (voice), saying,

"Blessed be Yahawah, who has given manawachah (rest) to his im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), according to all that he promised. There has not failed one dabar (word) of all his tawab (good) dabar (promise), which he promised by Mashah his ibad (servant).
May Yahawah our Alahayam be with us, as he was with our abawath (fathers). Let him not leave us, nor forsake us;

that he may natah (incline) our labab (hearts) to him, to yalak (walk) in all his darak (ways), and to shamar (keep) his matzawah (commandments), and his chaq (statutes), and his mashapat (ordinances), which he tzawah (commanded) our abawath (fathers).

Let these my dabar (words), with which I have made chanan (supplication) panayam (before) Yahawah, be qarawab (near) to Yahawah our Alahayam yawamam (day) and night, that he may ishah (maintain) the cause of his ibad (servant), and the cause of his im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), as every yawam (day) shall require;
that all the im (peoples) of the aratz (earth) may yadai (know) that Yahawah, he is Alahayam. There is none else.
"Let your labab (heart) therefore be Shalam with Yahawah our Alahayam, to yalak (walk) in his chaq (statutes), and to shamar (keep) his matzawah (commandments), as at this yawam (day).
The malak (king), and all Yasharaal (Israel) with him, offered zabach (sacrifice) panayam (before) Yahawah.

Shalamah offered for the zabach (sacrifice) of shalam (peace) offerings, which he offered to Yahawah, shanayam (two) and isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) baqar (head) of cattle, and one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) sheep. So the malak (king) and all the children of Yasharaal (Israel) dedicated the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

The same yawam (day) the malak (king) made the middle of the court qadash (holy) that was panayam (before) the bayath (house) of Yahawah; for there he offered the burnt offering, and the meal offering, and the fat of the shalam (peace) offerings, because the bronze mazabach (altar) that was panayam (before) Yahawah was too qatan (little) to receive the burnt ilah (offering), and the meal manachah (offering), and the fat of the shalam (peace) offerings.

So Shalamah held the chag (feast) at that ith (time), and all Yasharaal (Israel) with him, a gadawal (great) qahal (assembly), from the entrance of Chamath to the nachal (brook) of Matzarayam, panayam (before) Yahawah our Alahayam, shabai (seven) yawam (days) and shabai (seven) yawam (days), even fourteen yawam (days).

On the eighth yawam (day) he sent the im (people) shalach (away); and they blessed the malak (king), and went to their ahal (tents) Shamach and tawab (glad) of lab (heart) for all the goodness that Yahawah had shown to Dawad his ibad (servant), and to Yasharaal (Israel) his im (people).
It happened, when Shalamah had finished the building of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the malak (king's) bayath (house), and all Shalamah desire which he was pleased to do,
that Yahawah raah (see) to Shalamah the shanay (second) time, as he had raah (see) to him at Gabaiwan.

Yahawah said to him, "I have heard your prayer and your supplication, that you have made panayam (before) me. I have made this bayath (house) qadash (holy), which you have built, to shawam (put) my sham (name) there iwalam (forever); and my iyan (eyes) and my lab (heart) shall be there yawam (perpetually).

As for you, if you will yalak (walk) panayam (before) me, as Dawad your ab (father) walked, in tham (integrity) of labab (heart), and in yashar (uprightness), to do according to all that I have tzawah (commanded) you, and will shamar (keep) my chaq (statutes) and my mashapat (ordinances);

then I will qawam (establish) the kasaa (throne) of your mamalakah (kingdom) over Yasharaal (Israel) iwalam (forever), according as I promised to Dawad your ab (father), saying, ‘There shall not karath (fail) you a ayash (man) on the kasaa (throne) of Yasharaal (Israel).'

But if you shawab (turn back / repent) shawab (turn back / repent) from following me, you or your children, and not shamar (keep) my matzawah (commandments) and my chaqah (statutes) which I have nathan (set) panayam (before) you, but shall halak (go) and ibad (serve) other Alahayam, and shachah (worship) them;

then will I karath (cut) off Yasharaal (Israel) out of the adamah (land) which I have given them; and this bayath (house), which I have made qadash (holy) for my sham (name), will I shalach (cast) out of my panayam (sight); and Yasharaal (Israel) shall be a proverb and a byword among all im (peoples).

Though this bayath (house) is so Ilayawan, yet shall everyone who passes by it be astonished, and shall hiss; and they shall amar (say), ‘Why has Yahawah done thus to this aratz (land), and to this bayath (house)?'

and they shall amar (answer), ‘Because they forsook Yahawah their Alahayam, who brought their abawath (fathers) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and laid chazaq (hold) of other Alahayam, and worshiped them, and served them. Therefore Yahawah has brought all this rai (evil) on them.'
It happened at the end of isharayam (twenty) Shanah, in which Shalamah had built the shanayam (two) bayath (houses), the bayath (house) of Yahawah and the malak (king's) bayath (house)

(now Chayaram the malak (king) of Tzar had furnished Shalamah with cedar itz (trees) and fir itz (trees), and with gold, according to all his Chapatz), that then malak (king) Shalamah gave Chayaram isharayam (twenty) Iyar in the aratz (land) of Galayal.
Chayaram came out from Tzar to raah (see) the Iyar which Shalamah had given him; and they didn't yashar (please) him.
He said, "What Iyar are these which you have given me, my ach (brother)?" He called them the aratz (land) of Kabawal to this yawam (day).
Chayaram sent to the malak (king) one maah (hundred) twenty talents of gold.

This is the dabar (reason) of the levy which malak (king) Shalamah raised, to banah (build) the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and his own bayath (house), and Malawaa, and the wall of Yarawashalam, and Chatzawar, and Magadawan, and Gazar.

Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam had gone up, and taken Gazar, and burnt it with ash (fire), and slain the Kanainay (Canaanites) who lived in the Iyar, and given it for a portion to his bath (daughter), Shalamah ashah (wife).
Shalamah built Gazar, and Bayathachawarawan Horon the Thachathawan,
and Bailath, and Thadamar in the madabar (wilderness), in the aratz (land),

and all the storage Iyar that Shalamah had, and the Iyar for his chariots, and the Iyar for his horsemen, and that which Shalamah desired to banah (build) for his pleasure in Yarawashalam, and in Labanawan, and in all the aratz (land) of his mamashalah (dominion).

As for all the im (people) who were yathar (left) of the Amaray (Amorites), the Chathay (Hittites), the Parazay (Perizzites), the Chaway (Hivites), and the Yabawasay (Jebusites), who were not of the children of Yasharaal (Israel);

their children who were yathar (left) achar (after) them in the aratz (land), whom the children of Yasharaal (Israel) were not yakal (able) utterly to charam (destroy), of them Shalamah raised a levy of bondservants to this yawam (day).

But of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) Shalamah made no ibad (bondservants); but they were the men of war, and his ibad (servants), and his shar (princes), and his shalayash (captains), and shar (rulers) of his chariots and of his horsemen.

These were the shar (chief) natzab (officers) who were over Shalamah malaakah (work), chamash (five) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty), who bore radah (rule) over the im (people) who labored in the malaakah (work).
But Paraih bath (daughter) came up out of the Iyar of Dawad to her bayath (house) which Solomon had built for her: then he built Malawaa.

Shalamah offered burnt ilah (offerings) and shalam (peace) offerings on the mazabach (altar) which he built to Yahawah shalawash (three) paim (times) a Shanah, burning qatar (incense) with them, on the mazabach (altar) that was panayam (before) Yahawah. So he finished the bayath (house).
malak (king) Shalamah made a navy of ships in Itzayawanagabar Geber, which is beside Ayalawath, on the shapah (shore) of the Red yam (sea), in the aratz (land) of Adam.
Chayaram sent in the navy his ibad (servants), sailors who had yadai (knowledge) of the yam (sea), with the ibad (servants) of Shalamah.
They came to Awapayar, and fetched from there gold, arabai (four) maah (hundred) and isharayam (twenty) talents, and brought it to malak (king) Shalamah.
When the malakah (queen) of Shabaa heard of the fame of Shalamah concerning the sham (name) of Yahawah, she came to prove him with hard questions.

She came to Yarawashalam with a very Kabad chayal (train), with camels that bore spices, and very much gold, and Yaqar aban (stones); and when she had bawaa (come) to Shalamah, she talked with him of all that was in her labab (heart).
Shalamah told her all her dabar (questions): there was not anything hidden from the malak (king) which he didn't nagad (tell) her.
When the malakah (queen) of Shabaa had seen all the chakamah (wisdom) of Shalamah, and the bayath (house) that he had built,

and the food of his table, and the mawashab (sitting) of his ibad (servants), and the attendance of his sharath (ministers), and their clothing, and his cup bearers, and his ilah (ascent) by which he went up to the bayath (house) of Yahawah; there was no more rawach (spirit) in her.
She said to the malak (king), "It was a amath (true) dabar (report) that I heard in my own aratz (land) of your dabar (acts), and of your chakamah (wisdom).

However I didn't aman (believe) the dabar (words), until I came, and my iyan (eyes) had seen it. Behold, the chatzay (half) was not told me! Your chakamah (wisdom) and tawab (prosperity) exceed the fame which I heard.
Happy are your men, happy are these your ibad (servants), who imad (stand) continually panayam (before) you, who hear your chakamah (wisdom).

Blessed is Yahawah your Alahayam, who delighted in you, to nathan (set) you on the kasaa (throne) of Yasharaal (Israel). Because Yahawah loved Yasharaal (Israel) iwalam (forever), therefore made he you malak (king), to do justice and tzadaqah (righteousness).

She gave the malak (king) one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) talents of gold, and of spices very great store, and Yaqar aban (stones). There came no more such abundance of spices as these which the malakah (queen) of Shabaa gave to malak (king) Shalamah.
The navy also of Chayaram, that brought gold from Awapayar, brought in from Awapayar maad (great) plenty of almug itz (trees) and Yaqar aban (stones).

The malak (king) made of the almug itz (trees) pillars for the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and for the malak (king's) bayath (house), harps also and stringed instruments for the singers: there came no such almug itz (trees), nor were seen, to this yawam (day).

malak (king) Shalamah gave to the malakah (queen) of Shabaa all her Chapatz, whatever she asked, besides that which Shalamah gave her of his malak (royal) yad (bounty). So she turned, and went to her own aratz (land), she and her ibad (servants).
Now the weight of gold that came to Shalamah in one Shanah was shash (six) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty) - shash (six) talents of gold,
besides that which the traders brought, and the traffic of the merchants, and of all the malak (kings) of the mixed pachah (people), and of the governors of the aratz (country).
malak (king) Shalamah made two maah (hundred) tzanah (bucklers) of beaten gold; shash (six) maah (hundred) shekels of gold went to one tzanah (buckler).

he made shalawash (three) maah (hundred) magan (shields) of beaten gold; shalawash (three) minas of gold went to one magan (shield): and the malak (king) nathan (put) them in the bayath (house) of the Yair of Labanawan.
Moreover the malak (king) made a gadawal (great) kasaa (throne) of ivory, and overlaid it with the finest gold.

There were shash (six) steps to the kasaa (throne), and the raash (top) of the kasaa (throne) was Igal achar (behind); and there were yad (stays) on either side by the place of the seat, and shanayam (two) aray (lions) standing beside the yad (stays).
shanayam (twelve) aray (lions) stood there on the one side and on the other on the shash (six) steps: there was nothing Kan it made in any mamalakah (kingdom).

All malak (king) Shalamah drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the bayath (house) of the Yair of Labanawan were of pure gold: none were of kasap (silver); it was nothing accounted of in the yawam (days) of Shalamah.

For the malak (king) had at yam (sea) a navy of Tharashayash with the navy of Chayaram: achad (once) every shalawash (three) Shanah came the navy of Tharashayash, bringing gold, and kasap (silver), ivory, and apes, and peacocks.
So malak (king) Shalamah exceeded all the malak (kings) of the aratz (earth) in riches and in chakamah (wisdom).
All the aratz (earth) sought the presence of Shalamah, to hear his chakamah (wisdom), which Alahayam had nathan (put) in his lab (heart).
They brought every ayash (man) his tribute, vessels of kasap (silver), and vessels of gold, and clothing, and armor, and spices, horses, and mules, a dabar (rate) Shanah by Shanah.

Shalamah gathered asap (together) chariots and horsemen: and he had a alap (thousand) and arabai (four) maah (hundred) chariots, and shanayam (twelve) alap (thousand) horsemen, that he bestowed in the chariot Iyar, and with the malak (king) at Yarawashalam.
The malak (king) made kasap (silver) to be in Yarawashalam as aban (stones), and cedars made he to be as the sycamore trees that are in the lowland, for abundance.
The horses which Shalamah had were brought out of Matzarayam; and the malak (king's) merchants received them Maqawah droves, Maqawah drove at a price.

A chariot came up and went out of Matzarayam for shash (six) maah (hundred) shekels of kasap (silver), and a horse for one maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty); and so for all the malak (kings) of the Chathay (Hittites), and for the malak (kings) of Aram, they brought them out by their yad (means).

Now malak (king) Shalamah loved many foreign women, together with the bath (daughter) of Paraih, women of the Mawaabay (Moabites), Imawanay (Ammonites), Adamay (Edomites), Tzayadanay (Sidonians), and Chathay (Hittites);

of the gawayam (nations) concerning which Yahawah said to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), "You shall not bawaa (go) among them, neither shall they bawaa (come) among you; for surely they will natah (turn) away your labab (heart) achar (after) their Alahayam." Shalamah joined to these in ahab (love).
He had shabai (seven) maah (hundred) wives, princesses, and shalawash (three) maah (hundred) concubines; and his wives turned natah (away) his lab (heart).

For it happened, when Shalamah was old, that his wives turned natah (away) his labab (heart) achar (after) other Alahayam; and his labab (heart) was not Shalam with Yahawah his Alahayam, as was the labab (heart) of Dawad his ab (father).
For Shalamah went achar (after) Ishatharath the goddess of the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), and achar (after) Malakam the shaqawatz (abomination) of the Imawanay (Ammonites).
Shalamah did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, and didn't malaa (go) fully achar (after) Yahawah, as did Dawad his ab (father).

Then Shalamah built a bamah (high) place for Kamawash the shaqawatz (abomination) of Mawaab, on the har (mountain) that is panayam (before) Yarawashalam, and for Malak the shaqawatz (abomination) of the children of Imawan.
So he did for all his foreign wives, who burnt qatar (incense) and sacrificed to their Alahayam.
Yahawah was angry with Shalamah, because his labab (heart) was turned away from Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), who had raah (see) to him paim (twice),
and had tzawah (commanded) him dabar (concerning) this thing, that he should not yalak (go) achar (after) other Alahayam: but he didn't shamar (keep) that which Yahawah tzawah (commanded).

Therefore Yahawah said to Shalamah, "Because this is done by you, and you have not kept my barayath (covenant) and my chaqah (statutes), which I have tzawah (commanded) you, I will surely tear the mamalakah (kingdom) from you, and will nathan (give) it to your ibad (servant).
Notwithstanding I will not do it in your yawam (days), for Dawad your ab (father's) sake; but I will tear it out of the yad (hand) of your ban (son).

However I will not tear away all the mamalakah (kingdom); but I will nathan (give) one shabat (tribe) to your ban (son), for Dawad my ibad (servant's) sake, and for Yarawashalam sake which I have chosen.
Yahawah raised up an shatan (adversary) to Shalamah, Hadad the Adamay (Edomite): he was of the malak (king's) zarai (seed) in Adam.
For it happened, when Dawad was in Adam, and Yawaab the shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army) was gone up to bury the Chalal, and had Chalal every zakar (male) in Adam
(for Yawaab and all Yasharaal (Israel) remained there shash (six) chadash (months), until he had karath (cut) off every zakar (male) in Adam);
that Adad fled, he and anawash (certain) Adamay (Edomites) of his ab (father's) ibad (servants) with him, to bawaa (go) into Matzarayam, Hadad being yet a qatan (little) nair (child).

They qawam (arose) out of Madayan, and came to Paaran; and they took men with them out of Paaran, and they came to Matzarayam, to Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam, who gave him a bayath (house), and appointed him lacham (food), and gave him aratz (land).

Hadad found maad (great) favor in the iyan (sight) of Paraih, so that he gave him as ashah (wife) the achawath (sister) of his own ashah (wife), the achawath (sister) of Thachapanayas the gabayarah (queen).
The achawath (sister) of Thachapanayas bore him Ganabath his ban (son), whom Thachapanayas weaned in Paraih bayath (house); and Ganabath was in Paraih bayath (house) among the ban (sons) of Paraih.

When Hadad heard in Matzarayam that Dawad slept with his abawath (fathers), and that Yawaab the shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army) was mawath (dead), Hadad said to Paraih, "Let me depart, that I may yalak (go) to my own aratz (country).
Then Paraih said Chasar him, "But what have you lacked with me, that behold, you seek to yalak (go) to your own aratz (country)?" He answered, "Nothing, however only let me depart.
Alahayam raised up an shatan (adversary) to him, Razawan the ban (son) of Alayadai, who had fled from his Adawan Hadadaizar malak (king) of Tzawabaa.
He gathered men to him, and became shar (captain) over a gadawad (troop), when Dawad killed them of Zobah: and they went to Damashaq, and lived therein, and reigned in Damashaq.
He was an shatan (adversary) to Yasharaal (Israel) all the yawam (days) of Shalamah, besides the rai (mischief) of Hadad: and he abhorred Yasharaal (Israel), and reigned over Aram.

Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, an Aparathay (Ephraimite) Tzaradah Zeredah, a ibad (servant) of Shalamah, whose am (mother's) sham (name) was Tzarawaih, a alamanah (widow), he also lifted up his yad (hand) against the malak (king).
This was the dabar (reason) why he lifted up his yad (hand) against the malak (king): Shalamah built Malawaa, and repaired the breach of the Iyar of Dawad his ab (father).

The ayash (man) Yarabaim was a ayash (mighty) man of valor; and Shalamah saw the nair (young) man that he was ishah (industrious), and he put him in paqad (charge) of all the sabal (labor) of the bayath (house) of Yawasap.

It happened at that ith (time), when Yarabaim went out of Yarawashalam, that the nabayaa (prophet) Achayah the Shayalawanay (Shilonite) found him in the darak (way); now Ahijah had clad himself with a Chadash garment; and they shanayam (two) were alone in the shadah (field).
Achayah laid hold of the Chadash garment that was on him, and tore it in shanayam (twelve) pieces.

He said to Yarabaim, "Take ishar (ten) pieces; for thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘Behold, I will tear the mamalakah (kingdom) out of the yad (hand) of Shalamah, and will nathan (give) ishar (ten) shabat (tribes) to you
(but he shall have one shabat (tribe), for my ibad (servant) Dawad sake and for Yarawashalam sake, the Iyar which I have chosen out of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel));

because that they have forsaken me, and have worshiped Ishatharath the goddess of the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), Kamawash the Alahayam of Mawaab, and Malakam the Alahayam of the children of Imawan. They have not walked in my darak (ways), to do that which is yashar (right) in my iyan (eyes), and to keep my chaqah (statutes) and my mashapat (ordinances), as Dawad his ab (father) did.

"‘However I will not take the whole mamalakah (kingdom) out of his yad (hand); but I will shayath (make) him nashayaa (prince) all the yawam (days) of his chay (life), for Dawad my ibad (servant's) sake whom I chose, who kept my matzawah (commandments) and my chaqah (statutes);
but I will take the malawakah (kingdom) out of his ban (son's) yad (hand), and will nathan (give) it to you, even ishar (ten) shabat (tribes).

To his ban (son) will I nathan (give) one shabat (tribe), that Dawad my ibad (servant) may have a nayar (lamp) yawam (always) panayam (before) me in Yarawashalam, the Iyar which I have chosen me to shawam (put) my sham (name) there.
I will take you, and you shall malak (reign) according to all that your napash (soul) desires, and shall be malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel).

It shall be, if you will listen to all that I tzawah (command) you, and will halak (walk) in my darak (ways), and do that which is yashar (right) in my iyan (eyes), to shamar (keep) my chaqah (statutes) and my matzawah (commandments), as Dawad my ibad (servant) did; that I will be with you, and will banah (build) you a aman (sure) bayath (house), as I built for Dawad, and will nathan (give) Yasharaal (Israel) to you.
I will for this afflict the zarai (seed) of Dawad, but not forever.'

Shalamah sought therefore to mawath (kill) Yarabaim; but Yarabaim qawam (arose), and fled into Matzarayam, to Shayashaq malak (king) of Matzarayam, and was in Matzarayam until the mawath (death) of Shalamah.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Shalamah, and all that he did, and his chakamah (wisdom), aren't they written in the book of the dabar (acts) of Shalamah?
The yawam (time) that Shalamah reigned in Yarawashalam over all Yasharaal (Israel) was arabaiyam (forty) Shanah.
Shalamah slept with his abawath (fathers), and was buried in the Iyar of Dawad his ab (father): and Rachabaim his ban (son) reigned in his place.
Rachabaim went to Shakam: for all Yasharaal (Israel) had bawaa (come) to Shakam to make him malak (king).
It happened, when Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat heard of it (for he was yet in Matzarayam, where he had fled from the panayam (presence) of malak (king) Shalamah, and Yarabaim lived in Matzarayam,
and they sent and called him), that Yarabaim and all the qahal (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel) came, and spoke to Rachabaim, saying,

"Your ab (father) made our yoke grievous: now therefore make you the Qashah ibadah (service) of your ab (father), and his Kabad yoke which he nathan (put) on us, lighter, and we will ibad (serve) you.
He said to them, "Depart for shalawash (three) yawam (days), then shawab (turn back / repent) back to me." The im (people) departed.

malak (king) Rachabaim took yaitz (counsel) with the zaqan (old) men, who had stood panayam (before) Shalamah his ab (father) while he yet lived, saying, "What yaitz (counsel) do you give me to shawab (turn back / repent) dabar (answer) to this im (people)?

They spoke to him, saying, "If you will be a ibad (servant) to this im (people) this yawam (day), and will ibad (serve) them, and answer them, and dabar (speak) tawab (good) dabar (words) to them, then they will be your ibad (servants) forever.
But he forsook the itzah (counsel) of the zaqan (old) men which they had given him, and took yaitz (counsel) with the yalad (young) men who had grown up with him, who stood panayam (before) him.

He said to them, "What yaitz (counsel) do you give, that we may return dabar (answer) to this im (people), who have spoken to me, saying, ‘qalal (make) the yoke that your ab (father) nathan (put) on us lighter?'

The yalad (young) men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, "Thus you shall amar (tell) this im (people) who spoke to you, saying, ‘Your ab (father) made our yoke kabad (heavy), but qalal (make) it lighter to us;' you shall dabar (say) to them, ‘My little finger is thicker than my ab (father's) waist.
Now whereas my ab (father) burdened you with a Kabad yoke, I will add to your yoke: my ab (father) chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.'

So Yarabaim and all the im (people) came to Rachabaim the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), as the malak (king) asked, saying, "shawab (turn back / repent) to me again the shalayashay (third) yawam (day).
The malak (king) answered the im (people) Qashah, and forsook the itzah (counsel) of the zaqan (old) men which they had given him,

and spoke to them according to the itzah (counsel) of the yalad (young) men, saying, "My ab (father) made your yoke kabad (heavy), but I will add to your yoke. My ab (father) chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.

So the malak (king) didn't listen to the im (people); for it was a thing brought about of Yahawah, that he might qawam (establish) his dabar (word), which Yahawah spoke by Achayah the Shayalawanay (Shilonite) to Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat.

When all Yasharaal (Israel) saw that the malak (king) didn't listen to them, the im (people) answered the malak (king), saying, "What chalaq (portion) have we in Dawad? Neither do we have an nachalah (inheritance) in the ban (son) of Yashay. To your ahal (tents), Yasharaal (Israel)! Now raah (see) to your own bayath (house), Dawad." So Yasharaal (Israel) departed to their ahal (tents).
But as for the children of Yasharaal (Israel) who lived in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), Rachabaim reigned over them.

Then malak (king) Rachabaim sent Adaram, who was over the men subject to forced mas (labor); and all Yasharaal (Israel) stoned him to mawath (death) with aban (stones). malak (king) Rachabaim made amatz (speed) to ilah (get) him up to his chariot, to flee to Yarawashalam.
So Yasharaal (Israel) rebelled against the bayath (house) of Dawad to this yawam (day).

It happened, when all Yasharaal (Israel) heard that Yarabaim was returned, that they sent and called him to the idah (congregation), and made him malak (king) over all Yasharaal (Israel): there was none who followed the bayath (house) of Dawad, but the shabat (tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah) only.

When Rachabaim had bawaa (come) to Yarawashalam, he assembled all the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah), and the shabat (tribe) of Banayamayan, a maah (hundred) and shamanayam (eighty) alap (thousand) chosen men, who were ishah (warriors), to fight against the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), to shawab (turn back / repent) the malawakah (kingdom) again to Rachabaim the ban (son) of Shalamah.
But the dabar (word) of Alahayam came to Shamaiyah the ayash (man) of Alahayam, saying,

"amar (speak) to Rachabaim the ban (son) of Shalamah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and to all the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Banayamayan, and to the yathar (rest) of the im (people), saying,

‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "You shall not ilah (go) up, nor fight against your ach (brothers), the children of Yasharaal (Israel). Everyone shawab (turn back / repent) to his bayath (house); for this thing is of me."'" So they listened to the dabar (word) of Yahawah, and returned and went their yalak (way), according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah.
Then Yarabaim built Shakam in the har (hill) country of Aparayam, and lived in it; and he went out from there, and built Panawaal.
Yarabaim said in his lab (heart), "Now the mamalakah (kingdom) will shawab (turn back / repent) to the bayath (house) of Dawad.

If this im (people) goes up to ishah (offer) zabach (sacrifices) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah at Yarawashalam, then the lab (heart) of this im (people) will shawab (turn back / repent) again to their Adawan, even to Rachabaim malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah); and they will harag (kill) me, and shawab (turn back / repent) to Rachabaim malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah).

Whereupon the malak (king) took yaitz (counsel), and made shanayam (two) calves of gold; and he said to them, "It is rab (too) much for you to ilah (go) up to Yarawashalam. Look and see your Alahayam, Yasharaal (Israel), which brought you up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam!
He shawam (set) the one in Bayathaal, and the other nathan (put) he Dan Dan.
This thing became a chataah (sin); for the im (people) went to worship panayam (before) the one, Dan to Dan.
He made bayath (houses) of bamah (high) places, and made kahan (priests) from among all the im (people), who were not of the ban (sons) of Laway.

Yarabaim ordained a chag (feast) in the eighth chadash (month), on the fifteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month), like the chag (feast) that is in Yahawadah (Judah), and he went up to the mazabach (altar); he did so in Bayathaal, sacrificing to the calves that he had made: and he placed in Bayathaal the kahan (priests) of the bamah (high) places that he had made.

He went up to the mazabach (altar) which he had made in Bayathaal on the fifteenth yawam (day) in the eighth chadash (month), even in the chadash (month) which he had devised of his own lab (heart): and he ordained a chag (feast) for the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and went up to the mazabach (altar), to qatar (burn) incense.
Behold, there came a ayash (man) of Alahayam out of Yahawadah (Judah) by the dabar (word) of Yahawah to Bayathaal El: and Yarabaim was standing by the mazabach (altar) to qatar (burn) incense.

He cried against the mazabach (altar) by the dabar (word) of Yahawah, and said, "mazabach (altar), mazabach (altar), thus amar (says) Yahawah: ‘Behold, a ban (son) shall be yalad (born) to the bayath (house) of Dawad, Yaashayah by sham (name). On you he shall zabach (sacrifice) the kahan (priests) of the bamah (high) places who qatar (burn) incense on you, and they will sharap (burn) men's itzam (bones) on you.'

He gave a mawapath (sign) the same yawam (day), saying, "This is the mawapath (sign) which Yahawah has spoken: Behold, the mazabach (altar) will be split apart, and the ashes that are on it will be poured out.

It happened, when the malak (king) heard the dabar (saying) of the ayash (man) of Alahayam, which he cried against the mazabach (altar) in Bayathaal, that Yarabaim shalach (put) out his yad (hand) from the mazabach (altar), saying, "Seize him!" His yad (hand), which he shalach (put) out against him, dried up, so that he could not shawab (turn back / repent) it back again to himself.

The mazabach (altar) also was split apart, and the ashes poured out from the mazabach (altar), according to the mawapath (sign) which the ayash (man) of Alahayam had given by the dabar (word) of Yahawah.

The malak (king) answered the ayash (man) of Alahayam, "Now entreat the favor of Yahawah your Alahayam, and chalah (pray) for me, that my yad (hand) may be restored me again." The ayash (man) of Alahayam entreated Yahawah, and the malak (king's) yad (hand) was restored him again, and became as it was raashawan (before).
The malak (king) said to the ayash (man) of Alahayam, "bawaa (come) bayath (home) with me, and refresh yourself, and I will nathan (give) you a reward.

The ayash (man) of Alahayam said to the malak (king), "Even if you gave me chatzay (half) of your bayath (house), I would not bawaa (go) in with you, neither would I akal (eat) lacham (bread) nor drink mayam (water) in this place;

for so was it tzawah (commanded) me by the dabar (word) of Yahawah, saying, ‘You shall akal (eat) no lacham (bread), nor drink mayam (water), neither shawab (turn back / repent) by the darak (way) that you came.'
So he went achar (another) darak (way), and didn't shawab (turn back / repent) by the darak (way) that he came to Bayathaal.

Now there lived an zaqan (old) nabayaa (prophet) in Bayathaal; and one of his ban (sons) came and told him all the maishah (works) that the ayash (man) of Alahayam had done that yawam (day) in Bayathaal. They also told their father the dabar (words) which he had spoken to the king.
Their ab (father) said to them, "Which darak (way) did he halak (go)?" Now his ban (sons) had seen which darak (way) the ayash (man) of Alahayam went, who came from Yahawadah (Judah).
He said to his ban (sons), "Saddle the donkey for me." So they saddled the donkey for him; and he rode on it.
He went achar (after) the ayash (man) of Alahayam, and found him sitting under an oak. He said to him, "Are you the ayash (man) of Alahayam who came from Yahawadah (Judah)?" He said, "I am.
Then he said to him, "yalak (come) bayath (home) with me, and akal (eat) lacham (bread).
He said, "I may not shawab (turn back / repent) with you, nor bawaa (go) in with you; neither will I akal (eat) lacham (bread) nor drink mayam (water) with you in this place.

For it was dabar (said) to me by the dabar (word) of Yahawah, ‘You shall akal (eat) no lacham (bread) nor drink mayam (water) there, nor shawab (turn back / repent) again to yalak (go) by the darak (way) that you came.'

He said to him, "I also am a nabayaa (prophet) as you are; and an malaak (angel) spoke to me by the dabar (word) of Yahawah, saying, ‘shawab (turn back / repent) him back with you into your bayath (house), that he may akal (eat) lacham (bread) and drink mayam (water).'" He lied to him.
So he went shawab (turn back / repent) with him, and ate lacham (bread) in his bayath (house), and drank mayam (water).
It happened, as they sat at the table, that the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to the nabayaa (prophet) who brought him shawab (turn back / repent);

and he cried to the ayash (man) of Alahayam who came from Yahawadah (Judah), saying, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘Because you have been disobedient to the pah (mouth) of Yahawah, and have not kept the matzawah (commandment) which Yahawah your Alahayam tzawah (commanded) you,

but came shawab (turn back / repent), and have eaten lacham (bread) and drunk mayam (water) in the place of which he said to you, "akal (eat) no lacham (bread), and drink no mayam (water);" your nabalah (body) shall not bawaa (come) to the tomb of your abawath (fathers).'
It happened, achar (after) he had eaten lacham (bread), and achar (after) he had drunk, that he saddled the donkey for the nabayaa (prophet) whom he had brought shawab (turn back / repent).

When he had gone, a aray (lion) met him by the darak (way), and killed him. His nabalah (body) was cast in the darak (way), and the donkey stood by it. The aray (lion) also stood by the nabalah (body).

Behold, men passed by, and saw the nabalah (body) cast in the darak (way), and the aray (lion) standing by the nabalah (body); and they came and told it in the Iyar where the zaqan (old) nabayaa (prophet) lived.

When the nabayaa (prophet) who brought him shawab (turn back / repent) from the darak (way) heard of it, he said, "It is the ayash (man) of Alahayam who was disobedient to the pah (mouth) of Yahawah. Therefore Yahawah has delivered him to the aray (lion), which has mauled him and slain him, according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah, which he spoke to him.
He spoke to his ban (sons), saying, "Saddle the donkey for me." They saddled it.
