He went and found his nabalah (body) cast in the darak (way), and the donkey and the aray (lion) standing by the nabalah (body). The aray (lion) had not eaten the nabalah (body), nor mauled the donkey.

The nabayaa (prophet) took up the nabalah (body) of the ayash (man) of Alahayam, and laid it on the donkey, and brought it shawab (turn back / repent). He came to the Iyar of the zaqan (old) nabayaa (prophet) to mourn, and to bury him.
He laid his nabalah (body) in his own qabar (grave); and they mourned over him, saying, "Alas, my ach (brother)!

It happened, achar (after) he had buried him, that he spoke to his ban (sons), saying, "When I am mawath (dead), then bury me in the tomb in which the ayash (man) of Alahayam is buried. yanach (lay) my itzam (bones) beside his itzam (bones).

For the dabar (saying) which he cried by the dabar (word) of Yahawah against the mazabach (altar) in Bayathaal, and against all the bayath (houses) of the bamah (high) places which are in the Iyar of Shamarawan, will surely happen.

achar (after) this thing Yarabaim didn't shawab (turn back / repent) from his rai (evil) darak (way), but again made kahan (priests) of the bamah (high) places from among all the im (people). Chapatz wanted to, he consecrated him, that there might be kahan (priests) of the bamah (high) places.
This thing became chataah (sin) to the bayath (house) of Yarabaim, even to cut it off, and to destroy it from off the surface of the adamah (earth).
At that ith (time) Abayah the ban (son) of Yarabaim fell chalah (sick).

Yarabaim said to his ashah (wife), "Please qawam (get) up and shanah (disguise) yourself, that you won't be recognized as the ashah (wife) of Yarabaim. halak (go) to Shayalah. Behold, there is Achayah the nabayaa (prophet), who spoke concerning me that I should be malak (king) over this im (people).
Take with you ishar (ten) loaves, and cakes, and a jar of honey, and bawaa (go) to him. He will nagad (tell) you what will become of the nair (child).

Yarabaim ashah (wife) did so, and qawam (arose), and went to Shayalah, and came to the bayath (house) of Achayah. Now Achayah could not raah (see); for his iyan (eyes) were qawam (set) by reason of his age.

Yahawah said to Achayah, "Behold, the ashah (wife) of Yarabaim bawaa (comes) to inquire of you dabar (concerning) her ban (son); for he is chalah (sick). Thus and thus you shall dabar (tell) her; for it will be, when she bawaa (comes) in, that she will pretend to be nakar (another) woman.

It was so, when Achayah heard the qawal (sound) of her feet, as she came in at the door, that he said, "bawaa (come) in, you ashah (wife) of Yarabaim! Why do you pretend to be nakar (another)? For I am sent to you with Qashah news.

yalak (go), amar (tell) Yarabaim, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): "Because I exalted you from among the im (people), and made you nagayad (prince) over my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel),

and tore the mamalakah (kingdom) away from the bayath (house) of Dawad, and gave it you; and yet you have not been as my ibad (servant) Dawad, who kept my matzawah (commandments), and who followed me with all his labab (heart), to do that only which was yashar (right) in my iyan (eyes),

but have done raii (evil) above all who were panayam (before) you, and have gone and made you other Alahayam, and molten masakah (images), to provoke me to kais (anger), and have cast me achar (behind) your back:

therefore, behold, I will bawaa (bring) rai (evil) on the bayath (house) of Yarabaim, and will karath (cut) off from Yarabaim everyone who urinates on a wall, he who is itzar (shut) up and he who is left at large in Yasharaal (Israel), and will utterly sweep bair (away) the bayath (house) of Yarabaim, as a man sweeps bair (away) dung, until it is all thamam (gone).
He who dies of Yarabaim in the Iyar shall the dogs akal (eat); and he who dies in the shadah (field) shall the birds of the sky akal (eat): for Yahawah has spoken it."'
qawam (arise) therefore, and yalak (go) to your bayath (house). When your feet bawaa (enter) into the Iyar, the yalad (child) shall mawath (die).

All Yasharaal (Israel) shall mourn for him, and bury him; for he only of Yarabaim shall bawaa (come) to the qabar (grave), because in him there is found some tawab (good) thing toward Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), in the bayath (house) of Yarabaim.
Moreover Yahawah will qawam (raise) him up a malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel), who shall karath (cut) off the bayath (house) of Yarabaim. This is yawam (day)! What? Even now.

For Yahawah will strike Yasharaal (Israel), as a reed is shaken in the mayam (water); and he will nathash (root) up Yasharaal (Israel) out of this tawab (good) adamah (land) which he gave to their abawath (fathers), and will scatter them ibar (beyond) the nahar (river), because they have made their Asharah, provoking Yahawah to kais (anger).
He will nathan (give) Yasharaal (Israel) up because of the chataah (sins) of Yarabaim, which he has sinned, and with which he has made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).
Yarabaim ashah (wife) qawam (arose), and departed, and came to Tharatzah. As she came to the threshold of the bayath (house), the nair (child) died.
All Yasharaal (Israel) buried him, and mourned for him, according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah, which he spoke by his ibad (servant) Achayah the nabayaa (prophet).
The yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yarabaim, how he warred, and how he reigned, behold, they are written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel).
The yawam (days) which Yarabaim reigned were shanayam (two) and isharayam (twenty) Shanah: and he slept with his abawath (fathers), and Nadab his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Rachabaim the ban (son) of Shalamah reigned in Yahawadah (Judah). Rachabaim was arabaiyam (forty) - one Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign), and he reigned seventeen Shanah in Yarawashalam, the Iyar which Yahawah had chosen out of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), to shawam (put) his sham (name) there: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Naimah the Imawanayath.

Yahawadah (Judah) did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, and they provoked him to jealousy with their chataah (sins) which they committed, above all that their abawath (fathers) had done.
For they also built them bamah (high) places, and matzabah (pillars), and Asharah, on every Gabah Gabaih, and under every Rainan itz (tree);

and there were also qadash (sodomites) in the aratz (land): they did according to all the thawaibah (abominations) of the gawayam (nations) which Yahawah drove out panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
It happened in the chamayashay (fifth) Shanah of malak (king) Rachabaim, that Shayashaq malak (king) of Matzarayam came up against Yarawashalam;

and he took away the treasures of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the treasures of the malak (king's) bayath (house); he even took away all: and he took away all the magan (shields) of gold which Shalamah had made.
malak (king) Rachabaim made in their place magan (shields) of brass, and committed them to the yad (hands) of the shar (captains) of the guard, who kept the door of the malak (king's) bayath (house).
It was so, that as often as the malak (king) went into the bayath (house) of Yahawah, the guard bore them, and brought them shawab (turn back / repent) into the guard room.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Rachabaim, and all that he did, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)?
There was war between Rachabaim and Yarabaim yawam (continually).

Rachabaim slept with his abawath (fathers), and was buried with his abawath (fathers) in the Iyar of Dawad: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Naimah the Imawanayath. Abayam his ban (son) reigned in his place.
Now in the eighteenth Shanah of malak (king) Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat began Abayam to malak (reign) over Yahawadah (Judah).
He reigned shalawash (three) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Maikah the bath (daughter) of Abayashalawam.

He walked in all the chataah (sins) of his ab (father), which he had done panayam (before) him; and his labab (heart) was not Shalam with Yahawah his Alahayam, as the labab (heart) of Dawad his ab (father).
Nevertheless for Dawad sake, Yahawah his Alahayam gave him a nayar (lamp) in Yarawashalam, to qawam (set) up his ban (son) achar (after) him, and to imad (establish) Yarawashalam;

because Dawad did that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, and didn't sawar (turn) aside from anything that he tzawah (commanded) him all the yawam (days) of his chay (life), except only in the dabar (matter) of Awarayah the Chathay (Hittite).
Now there was war between Rachabaim and Yarabaim all the yawam (days) of his chay (life).

The yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Abayam, and all that he did, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)? There was war between Abayam and Yarabaim.
Abayam slept with his abawath (fathers); and they buried him in the Iyar of Dawad: and Asaa his ban (son) reigned in his place.
In the isharayam (twentieth) Shanah of Yarabaim malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) began Asaa to malak (reign) over Yahawadah (Judah).
He reigned arabaiyam (forty) - one Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Maikah the bath (daughter) of Abayashalawam.
Asaa did that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, as did Dawad his ab (father).
He ibar (put) away the qadash (sodomites) out of the aratz (land), and removed all the idols that his abawath (fathers) had made.

Maikah Maacah his am (mother) he removed from being gabayarah (queen), because she had made an abominable mapalatzath (image) Asharah an Asherah; and Asaa karath (cut) down her mapalatzath (image), and burnt it at the nachal (brook) Qadarawan.
But the bamah (high) places were not taken sawar (away): nevertheless the labab (heart) of Asaa was Shalam with Yahawah all his yawam (days).
He brought into the bayath (house) of Yahawah the things that his ab (father) had qadash (dedicated), and the things that himself had qadash (dedicated), kasap (silver), and gold, and vessels.
There was war between Asaa and Baishaa malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) all their yawam (days).

Baishaa malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) went up against Yahawadah (Judah), and built Ramah, that he might not allow anyone to yatzaa (go) out or bawaa (come) in to Asaa malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah).

Then Asaa took all the kasap (silver) and the gold that were yathar (left) in the treasures of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the treasures of the malak (king's) bayath (house), and delivered them into the yad (hand) of his ibad (servants); and malak (king) Asaa sent them Banahadad Ben Hadad, the ban (son) of Tabaramawan, the ban (son) of Chazayawan, malak (king) of Aram, who lived at Damashaq, saying,

"There is a treaty between me and you, between my ab (father) and your ab (father). Behold, I have sent to you a shachad (present) of kasap (silver) and gold. yalak (go), parar (break) your treaty with Baishaa malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), that he may depart from me.

Banahadad Hadad listened to malak (king) Asaa, and sent the shar (captains) of his chayal (armies) against the Iyar of Yasharaal (Israel), and struck Iyawan, and Dan, and Abalabayathamaikah Beth Maacah, and all Kanarawath, with all the aratz (land) of Napathalay.
It happened, when Baishaa heard of it, that he left off building Ramah, and lived in Tharatzah.

Then malak (king) Asaa made a proclamation to all Yahawadah (Judah); none was naqay (exempted): and they carried away the aban (stones) of Ramah, and its itz (timber), with which Baishaa had built; and malak (king) Asaa built therewith Gabai of Banayamayan, and Matzapah.

Now the yathar (rest) of all the dabar (acts) of Asaa, and all his might, and all that he did, and the Iyar which he built, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)? But in the ith (time) of his old age he was chalah (diseased) in his feet.
Asaa slept with his abawath (fathers), and was buried with his abawath (fathers) in the Iyar of Dawad his ab (father); and Yahawashapat his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Nadab the ban (son) of Yarabaim began to malak (reign) over Yasharaal (Israel) in the shanayam (second) Shanah of Asaa malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah); and he reigned over Yasharaal (Israel) shanayam (two) Shanah.
He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, and walked in the darak (way) of his ab (father), and in his chataah (sin) with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).

Baishaa the ban (son) of Achayah, of the bayath (house) of Yashashakar, conspired against him; and Baishaa struck him at Gabathawan, which belonged to the Palashathay (Philistines); for Nadab and all Yasharaal (Israel) were laying tzawar (siege) to Gabathawan.
Even in the shalawash (third) Shanah of Asaa malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Baishaa killed him, and reigned in his place.

It happened that, as soon as he was malak (king), he struck all the bayath (house) of Yarabaim: he didn't shaar (leave) to Yarabaim any who breathed, until he had destroyed him; according to the dabar (saying) of Yahawah, which he spoke by his ibad (servant) Achayah the Shayalawanay (Shilonite);

for the chataah (sins) of Yarabaim which he sinned, and with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin), because of his kais (provocation) with which he provoked Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), to kais (anger).
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Nadab, and all that he did, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
There was war between Asaa and Baishaa malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) all their yawam (days).

In the shalawash (third) Shanah of Asaa malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Baishaa the ban (son) of Achayah began to malak (reign) over all Yasharaal (Israel) in Tharatzah for isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) Shanah.
He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, and walked in the darak (way) of Yarabaim, and in his chataah (sin) with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Yahawaa the ban (son) of Chananay against Baishaa, saying,

"Because I exalted you out of the ipar (dust), and made you nagayad (prince) over my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), and you have walked in the darak (way) of Yarabaim, and have made my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin), to provoke me to kais (anger) with their chataah (sins);
behold, I will utterly sweep bair (away) Baishaa and his bayath (house); and I will nathan (make) your bayath (house) like the bayath (house) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat.
The dogs will akal (eat) Baishaa descendants who mawath (die) in the Iyar; and he who dies of his in the shadah (field) the birds of the sky will akal (eat).
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Baishaa, and what he did, and his might, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
Baishaa slept with his abawath (fathers), and was buried in Tharatzah; and Alah his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Moreover by the nabayaa (prophet) Yahawaa the ban (son) of Chananay came the dabar (word) of Yahawah against Baishaa, and against his bayath (house), both because of all the rai (evil) that he did in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, to provoke him to kais (anger) with the maishah (work) of his yad (hands), in being like the bayath (house) of Yarabaim, and because he struck him.
In the isharayam (twenty) - shash (sixth) Shanah of Asaa malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Alah the ban (son) of Baishaa began to malak (reign) over Yasharaal (Israel) in Tharatzah for two Shanah.

His ibad (servant) Zamaray, shar (captain) of half his chariots, conspired against him. Now he was in Tharatzah, drinking himself shakawar (drunk) in the bayath (house) of Aratzaa, who was over the bayath (household) in Tharatzah:
and Zamaray went in and struck him, and killed him, in the isharayam (twenty) - seventh Shanah of Asaa malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and reigned in his place.

It happened, when he began to malak (reign), as soon as he sat on his kasaa (throne), that he struck all the bayath (house) of Baishaa: he didn't shaar (leave) him a single shathan (one) who urinates on a wall, neither of his relatives, nor of his rai (friends).
Thus Zamaray destroyed all the bayath (house) of Baishaa, according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah, which he spoke against Baishaa by Yahawaa the nabayaa (prophet),

for all the chataah (sins) of Baishaa, and the chataah (sins) of Alah his ban (son), which they sinned, and with which they made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin), to provoke Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), to kais (anger) with their vanities.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Alah, and all that he did, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel)?

In the isharayam (twenty) - seventh Shanah of Asaa malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Zamaray reigned shabai (seven) yawam (days) in Tharatzah. Now the im (people) were encamped against Gabathawan, which belonged to the Palashathay (Philistines).

The im (people) who were encamped heard amar (say), Zamaray has conspired, and has also struck the malak (king): therefore all Yasharaal (Israel) made Imaray, the shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army), malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel) that yawam (day) in the machanah (camp).
Imaray went up from Gabathawan, and all Yasharaal (Israel) with him, and they besieged Tharatzah.

It happened, when Zamaray saw that the Iyar was taken, that he went into the castle of the malak (king's) bayath (house), and burnt the malak (king's) bayath (house) over him with ash (fire), and died,

for his chataah (sins) which he sinned in doing that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, in yalak (walking) in the darak (way) of Yarabaim, and in his chataah (sin) which he did, to make Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Zamaray, and his treason that he committed, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel)?

Then were the im (people) of Yasharaal (Israel) divided into chatzay (two) parts: chatzay (half) of the im (people) followed Thabanay the ban (son) of Gayanath, to make him malak (king); and chatzay (half) followed Imaray.
But the im (people) who followed Imaray prevailed against the im (people) who followed Thabanay the ban (son) of Gayanath: so Thabanay died, and Imaray reigned.

In the shalawashayam (thirty) - achad (first) Shanah of Asaa malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Imaray began to malak (reign) over Yasharaal (Israel) for shanayam (twelve) Shanah. He reigned shash (six) Shanah in Tharatzah.

He bought the har (hill) Shamarawan of Shamar for kakar (two) talents of kasap (silver); and he built on the har (hill), and called the sham (name) of the Iyar which he built, after the sham (name) of Shamar, the adawan (owner) of the har (hill), Shamarawan.
Imaray did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, and dealt wickedly above all who were panayam (before) him.

For he walked in all the darak (way) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, and in his chataah (sins) with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin), to provoke Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), to kais (anger) with their vanities.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Imaray which he did, and his might that he showed, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
So Imaray slept with his abawath (fathers), and was buried in Shamarawan; and Achaab his ban (son) reigned in his place.

In the shalawashayam (thirty) - shamanah (eighth) Shanah of Asaa malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) began Achaab the ban (son) of Imaray to malak (reign) over Yasharaal (Israel): and Achaab the ban (son) of Imaray reigned over Yasharaal (Israel) in Shamarawan isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) Shanah.
Achaab the ban (son) of Imaray did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah above all that were panayam (before) him.

It happened, as if it had been a qalal (light) thing for him to yalak (walk) in the chataah (sins) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, that he took as ashah (wife) Ayazabal the bath (daughter) of Athabail malak (king) of the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), and went and served Bail, and worshiped him.
He reared up an mazabach (altar) for Bail in the bayath (house) of Bail, which he had built in Shamarawan.

Achaab made the Asharah; and Achaab did yet more to provoke Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), to kais (anger) than all the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel) who were panayam (before) him.

In his yawam (days) Chayaal the Bayathahaalay built Yarayachaw: he laid its yasad (foundation) with the loss of Abayaram his firstborn, and natzab (set) up its gates Tzaiyar the loss of his youngest son Shagawab, according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah, which he spoke by Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Nawan.

Alayah the Thashabay, who was of the foreigners of Galaid, said to Achaab, "As Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), chay (lives), panayam (before) whom I imad (stand), there shall not be dew nor rain these Shanah, but according to my dabar (word).
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to him, saying,
"yalak (go) away from here, panah (turn) eastward, and hide yourself by the nachal (brook) Karayath, that is panayam (before) the Yaradan.
It shall be, that you shall drink of the nachal (brook). I have tzawah (commanded) the ravens to feed you there.
So he went and did according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah; for he went and lived by the nachal (brook) Karayath, that is panayam (before) the Yaradan.
The ravens brought him lacham (bread) and flesh in the baqar (morning), and lacham (bread) and flesh in the evening; and he drank of the nachal (brook).
It happened after a yawam (while), that the nachal (brook) dried up, because there was no rain in the aratz (land).
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to him, saying,
"qawam (arise), yalak (go) to Tzarapath, which belongs to Tzayadawan, and stay there. Behold, I have tzawah (commanded) a alamanah (widow) there to sustain you.

So he qawam (arose) and went to Tzarapath; and when he came to the gate of the Iyar, behold, a alamanah (widow) was there gathering itz (sticks): and he called to her, and said, "Please get me a Mait mayam (water) in a vessel, that I may drink.
As she was going to get it, he called to her, and said, "Please bring me a morsel of lacham (bread) in your yad (hand).

She said, "As Yahawah your Alahayam chay (lives), I don't have a cake, but a handful of meal in the jar, and a Mait shaman (oil) in the jar. Behold, I am gathering shanayam (two) itz (sticks), that I may bawaa (go) in and bake it for me and my ban (son), that we may akal (eat) it, and mawath (die).

Alayah said to her, "Don't be yaraa (afraid). bawaa (go) and do as you have dabar (said); but ishah (make) me of it a qatan (little) cake raashawan (first), and yatzaa (bring) it out to me, and Acharawan ishah (make) some for you and for your ban (son).

For thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘The jar of meal shall not empty, neither shall the jar of shaman (oil) fail, until the yawam (day) that Yahawah nathan (sends) rain on the adamah (earth).'
She went and did according to the dabar (saying) of Alayah: and she, and he, and her bayath (house), ate many yawam (days).
The jar of meal didn't empty, neither did the jar of shaman (oil) Chasar, according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah, which he spoke by Alayah.

It happened achar (after) these things, that the ban (son) of the ashah (woman), the mistress of the bayath (house), fell chalah (sick); and his sickness was so severe, that there was no nashamah (breath) yathar (left) in him.
She said to Alayah, "What have I to do with you, you ayash (man) of Alahayam? You have bawaa (come) to me to zakar (bring) my iwan (sin) to memory, and to mawath (kill) my ban (son)!
He said to her, "nathan (give) me your ban (son)." He took him out of her bosom, and carried him up into the room where he stayed, and laid him on his own bed.
He cried to Yahawah, and said, "Yahawah my Alahayam, have you also brought raii (evil) on the alamanah (widow) with whom I stay, by killing her ban (son)?

He stretched himself on the yalad (child) shalawash (three) paim (times), and cried to Yahawah, and said, "Yahawah my Alahayam, please let this yalad (child's) napash (soul) shawab (turn back / repent) into him again.
Yahawah listened to the qawal (voice) of Alayah; and the napash (soul) of the yalad (child) came into him again, and he revived.
Alayah took the yalad (child), and brought him down out of the room into the bayath (house), and delivered him to his am (mother); and Alayah said, "raah (see), your ban (son) chay (lives).
The ashah (woman) said to Alayah, "zah (now) I yadai (know) that you are a ayash (man) of Alahayam, and that the dabar (word) of Yahawah in your pah (mouth) is truth.

It happened after many yawam (days), that the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Alayah, in the shalayashay (third) Shanah, saying, "yalak (go), show yourself to Achaab; and I will nathan (send) rain on the adamah (earth).
Alayah went to show himself to Achaab. The famine was severe in Shamarawan.
Achaab called Ibadayah, who was over the bayath (household). (Now Ibadayah feared Yahawah maad (greatly):

for it was so, when Ayazabal karath (cut) off the nabayaa (prophets) of Yahawah, that Ibadayah took one maah (hundred) nabayaa (prophets), and hid them by fifty in a cave, and fed them with lacham (bread) and mayam (water).)

Achaab said to Ibadayah, "yalak (go) through the aratz (land), to all the springs of mayam (water), and to all the nachal (brooks). Perhaps we may matzaa (find) grass and chayah (save) the horses and mules chayah (alive), that we not karath (lose) all the animals.
So they divided the aratz (land) between them to ibar (pass) throughout it: Achaab went one darak (way) by himself, and Ibadayah went another darak (way) by himself.
As Ibadayah was in the darak (way), behold, Alayah met him: and he recognized him, and napal (fell) on his panayam (face), and said, "Is it you, my Adawan Alayah?
He answered him, "It is I. yalak (go), amar (tell) your Adawan, ‘Behold, Alayah is here!'
He said, "Wherein have I sinned, that you would nathan (deliver) your ibad (servant) into the yad (hand) of Achaab, to mawath (kill) me?

As Yahawah your Alahayam chay (lives), there is no gaway (nation) or mamalakah (kingdom), where my Adawan has not sent to seek you. When they said, ‘He is not here,' he took an shabai (oath) of the mamalakah (kingdom) and gaway (nation), that they didn't matzaa (find) you.
Now you amar (say), ‘yalak (go), amar (tell) your Adawan, "Behold, Alayah is here."'

It will happen, as soon as I am gone from you, that the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah will nashaa (carry) you I don't yadai (know) where; and so when I bawaa (come) and nagad (tell) Achaab, and he can't matzaa (find) you, he will harag (kill) me. But I, your ibad (servant), have feared Yahawah from my youth.

Wasn't it told my Adawan what I did when Ayazabal killed the nabayaa (prophets) of Yahawah, how I hid one maah (hundred) men of yahawah (yahweh's) nabayaa (prophets) with chamashayam (fifty) to a cave, and fed them with lacham (bread) and mayam (water)?
Now you amar (say), ‘yalak (go), amar (tell) your Adawan, "Behold, Alayah is here;"' and he will harag (kill) me.
Alayah said, "As Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) chay (lives), panayam (before) whom I imad (stand), I will raah (see) show myself to him today.
So Ibadayah went to qaraah (meet) Achaab, and told him; and Achaab went to qaraah (meet) Alayah.
It happened, when Achaab saw Alayah, that Achaab said to him, "Is that you, you troubler of Yasharaal (Israel)?
He answered, "I have not troubled Yasharaal (Israel); but you, and your ab (father's) bayath (house), in that you have forsaken the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah, and you have followed the Bail.

Now therefore shalach (send), and gather to me all Yasharaal (Israel) to har (mount) Karamal, and arabai (four) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) of the nabayaa (prophets) of Bail, and arabai (four) maah (hundred) of the nabayaa (prophets) Asharah the Asherah, who akal (eat) at Ayazabal table.
So Achaab sent to all the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and gathered the nabayaa (prophets) together to har (mount) Karamal.

Alayah came near to all the im (people), and said, "How long will you Pasach between the shanayam (two) sides? If Yahawah is Alahayam, yalak (follow) him; but if Bail, then yalak (follow) him." The im (people) answered him not a dabar (word).
Then Alayah said to the im (people), "I, even I only, am yathar (left) a nabayaa (prophet) of Yahawah; but Bail nabayaa (prophets) are arabai (four) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) men.

Let them therefore nathan (give) us shanayam (two) bulls; and let them choose one bull for themselves, and cut it in pieces, and shawam (lay) it on the itz (wood), and shawam (put) no ash (fire) under; and I will ishah (dress) the other bull, and nathan (lay) it on the itz (wood), and shawam (put) no ash (fire) under it.

You qaraa (call) on the sham (name) of your Alahayam, and I will qaraa (call) on the sham (name) of Yahawah. The Alahayam who answers by ash (fire), let him be Alahayam." All the im (people) answered, "It is tawab (well) said.

Alayah said to the nabayaa (prophets) of Bail, "Choose one bull for yourselves, and ishah (dress) it raashawan (first); for you are many; and qaraa (call) on the sham (name) of your Alahayam, but shawam (put) no ash (fire) under it.

They took the bull which was given them, and they ishah (dressed) it, and called on the sham (name) of Bail from baqar (morning) even until tzahar (noon), saying, Bail, hear us. But there was no qawal (voice), nor any who answered. They Pasach about the mazabach (altar) which was made.

It happened at tzahar (noon), that Alayah mocked them, and said, "qaraa (cry) gadawal (aloud); for he is a Alahayam. Either he is musing, or he has gone aside, or he is on a darak (journey), or perhaps he sleeps and must be awakened.
They cried qawal (aloud), and cut themselves in their way with knives and lances, until the dam (blood) gushed out on them.
It was so, when tzahar (midday) was past, that they prophesied until the time of the offering of the offering; but there was neither qawal (voice), nor any to answer, nor any who regarded.
Alayah said to all the im (people), "Come near to me;" and all the im (people) came near to him. He repaired the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah that was thrown down.

Alayah took shanayam (twelve) aban (stones), according to the number of the shabat (tribes) of the ban (sons) of Yaiqab, to whom the dabar (word) of Yahawah came, saying, "Yasharaal (Israel) shall be your sham (name).

With the aban (stones) he built an mazabach (altar) in the sham (name) of Yahawah. He made a thailah (trench) around the mazabach (altar), large enough to bayath (contain) saah (two) measures of zarai (seed).

He put the itz (wood) in order, and cut the bull in pieces, and laid it on the itz (wood). He said, "malaa (fill) arabai (four) jars with mayam (water), and pour it on the burnt ilah (offering), and on the itz (wood).
He said, "Do it a shanah (second) time;" and they did it the shanah (second) time. He said, "Do it a third shanah (time);" and they did it the shalash (third) time.
The mayam (water) ran around the mazabach (altar); and he also filled the thailah (trench) with mayam (water).

It happened at the time of the offering of the manachah (offering), that Alayah the nabayaa (prophet) came near, and said, "Yahawah, the Alahayam of Abaraham, of Yatzachaq, and of Yasharaal (Israel), let it be yadai (known) this yawam (day) that you are Alahayam in Yasharaal (Israel), and that I am your ibad (servant), and that I have done all these things at your dabar (word).
Hear me, Yahawah, hear me, that this im (people) may yadai (know) that you, Yahawah, are Alahayam, and that you have turned their lab (heart) sabab (back) again.

Then the ash (fire) of Yahawah napal (fell), and consumed the burnt ilah (offering), and the itz (wood), and the aban (stones), and the ipar (dust), and licked up the mayam (water) that was in the thailah (trench).
When all the im (people) saw it, they napal (fell) on their panayam (faces). They said, "Yahawah, he is Alahayam! Yahawah, he is Alahayam!
Alayah said to them, "Seize the nabayaa (prophets) of Bail! Don't let one of them malat (escape)!" They seized them. Alayah brought them down to the nachal (brook) Qayashawan, and killed them there.
Alayah said to Achaab, "ilah (get) up, akal (eat) and drink; for there is the qawal (sound) of abundance of rain.
So Achaab went up to akal (eat) and to drink. Alayah went up to the raash (top) of Karamal; and he bowed himself down on the aratz (earth), and shawam (put) his panayam (face) between his knees.

He said to his nair (servant), "ilah (go) up now, look darak (toward) the yam (sea)." He went up, and looked, and said, "There is nothing." He said, "shawab (turn back / repent) again" shabai (seven) paim (times).

It happened at the shabayaiy (seventh) time, that he said, "Behold, a qatan (small) cloud, like a ayash (man's) kap (hand), is rising out of the yam (sea)." He said, "ilah (go) up, amar (tell) Achaab, ‘Get ready and yarad (go) down, so that the rain doesn't itzar (stop) you.'
It happened in a little kah (while), that the sky grew black with clouds and rawach (wind), and there was a gadawal (great) rain. Achaab rode, and went to Yazaraial.
The yad (hand) of Yahawah was on Alayah; and he tucked his cloak into his belt and ran panayam (before) Achaab to the entrance of Yazaraial.
Achaab told Ayazabal all that Alayah had done, and how he had killed all the nabayaa (prophets) with the charab (sword).

Then Ayazabal sent a malaak (messenger) to Alayah, saying, "So let the Alahayam do to me, and more also, if I don't shawam (make) your napash (life) as the napash (life) of one of them by tomorrow about this ith (time)!
When he saw that, he qawam (arose), and went for his napash (life), and came Baarashabai Beersheba, which belongs to Yahawadah (Judah), and left his nair (servant) there.

But he himself went a yawam (day's) darak (journey) into the madabar (wilderness), and came and sat down under a juniper tree: and he requested for himself that he might mawath (die), and said, "It is rab (enough). Now, O Yahawah, take away my napash (life); for I am not tawab (better) than my abawath (fathers).
He shakab (lay) down and slept under a juniper tree; and behold, an malaak (angel) touched him, and said to him, "qawam (arise) and akal (eat)!
He looked, and behold, there was at his maraashah (head) a cake baked on the coals, and a jar of mayam (water). He ate and drank, and shakab (lay) down again.
The malaak (angel) of Yahawah came again the shanay (second) time, and touched him, and said, "qawam (arise) and akal (eat), darak (because) the journey is rab (too) great for you.
He qawam (arose), and ate and drank, and went in the kach (strength) of that food arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days) and arabaiyam (forty) layal (nights) to Charab the har (mount) of Alahayam.
He came there to a cave, and lodged there; and behold, the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to him, and he said to him, "What are you doing here, Alayah?

He said, "I have been very jealous for Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies); for the children of Yasharaal (Israel) have forsaken your barayath (covenant), thrown down your mazabach (altars), and slain your nabayaa (prophets) with the charab (sword). I, even I only, am yathar (left); and they seek my napash (life), to take it away.

He said, "yatzaa (go) out, and imad (stand) on the har (mountain) panayam (before) Yahawah." Behold, Yahawah passed by, and a gadawal (great) and chazaq (strong) rawach (wind) tore the har (mountains), and broke in shabar (pieces) the salai (rocks) panayam (before) Yahawah; but Yahawah was not in the rawach (wind). achar (after) the rawach (wind) an earthquake; but Yahawah was not in the earthquake.
achar (after) the earthquake a ash (fire) passed; but Yahawah was not in the ash (fire): and achar (after) the ash (fire) a still Daq qawal (voice).

It was so, when Alayah heard it, that he wrapped his panayam (face) in his adarath (mantle), and went out, and stood in the entrance of the cave. Behold, a qawal (voice) came to him, and said, "What are you doing here, Alayah?

He said, "I have been very jealous for Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies); for the children of Yasharaal (Israel) have forsaken your barayath (covenant), thrown down your mazabach (altars), and slain your nabayaa (prophets) with the charab (sword). I, even I only, am yathar (left); and they seek my napash (life), to take it away.

Yahawah said to him, "yalak (go), shawab (turn back / repent) on your darak (way) to the madabar (wilderness) of Damashaq. When you arrive, you shall mashach (anoint) Chazaal to be malak (king) over Aram.

You shall mashach (anoint) Yahawaa the ban (son) of Namashay to be malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel); and you shall mashach (anoint) Alayashai the ban (son) of Shapat of Abalamachawalah Meholah to be nabayaa (prophet) in your place.

It shall happen, that he who malat (escapes) from the charab (sword) of Chazaal, Yahawaa will mawath (kill); and he who malat (escapes) from the charab (sword) of Yahawaa, Alayashai will mawath (kill).
Yet will I shaar (leave) shabai (seven) alap (thousand) in Yasharaal (Israel), all the knees which have not bowed to Bail, and every pah (mouth) which has not kissed him.

So he departed there, and found Alayashai the ban (son) of Shapat, who was plowing, with shanayam (twelve) tzamad (yoke) of oxen panayam (before) him, and he with the shanayam (twelfth): and Alayah passed over to him, and cast his adarath (mantle) on him.

He left the oxen, and ran achar (after) Alayah, and said, "Let me please kiss my ab (father) and my am (mother), and then I will yalak (follow) you." He said to him, "yalak (go) back again; for what have I done to you?

He returned from following him, and took the tzamad (yoke) of oxen, and killed them, and boiled their flesh with the instruments of the oxen, and gave to the im (people), and they ate. Then he qawam (arose), and went achar (after) Alayah, and served him.

Banahadad Hadad the malak (king) of Aram gathered all his chayal (army) together; and there were shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) malak (kings) with him, and horses and chariots: and he went up and besieged Shamarawan, and fought against it.
He sent malaak (messengers) to Achaab malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), into the Iyar, and said to him, "Thus amar (says) Banahadad Hadad,
‘Your kasap (silver) and your gold is mine. Your wives also and your children, even the tawab (best), are mine.'
The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) answered, "It is according to your saying, my Adawan, O malak (king). I am yours, and all that I have.

The malaak (messengers) came again, and said, "Banahadad Hadad amar (says), ‘I sent amar (indeed) to you, saying, "You shall nathan (deliver) me your kasap (silver), and your gold, and your wives, and your children;

but I will shalach (send) my ibad (servants) to you tomorrow about this ith (time), and they shall search your bayath (house), and the bayath (houses) of your ibad (servants); and it shall be, that whatever is pleasant in your iyan (eyes), they shall shawam (put) it in their yad (hand), and take it away."'

Then the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) called all the zaqan (elders) of the aratz (land), and said, "Please notice how this baqash (man) seeks rai (mischief); for he sent to me for my wives, and for my children, and for my kasap (silver), and for my gold; and I didn't deny him.
All the zaqan (elders) and all the im (people) said to him, "Don't listen, neither abah (consent).

Therefore he said to the malaak (messengers) Banahadad Ben Hadad, "amar (tell) my Adawan the malak (king), ‘All that you sent for to your ibad (servant) at the raashawan (first) I will do; but this thing I cannot do.'" The malaak (messengers) departed, and brought him shawab (turn back / repent) the dabar (message).
Banahadad Hadad sent to him, and said, "The Alahayam do so to me, and more also, if the ipar (dust) of Shamarawan shall suffice for shail (handfuls) for all the im (people) who ragal (follow) me.
The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) answered, "dabar (tell) him, ‘Don't let him who puts on his armor brag like he who takes it off.'

It happened, when Ben Hadad heard this dabar (message), as he was drinking, he and the malak (kings), in the sakah (pavilions), that he said to his ibad (servants), "Prepare to attack!" They prepared to attack the Iyar.

Behold, a nabayaa (prophet) came near to Achaab malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), and said, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘Have you seen all this gadawal (great) multitude? Behold, I will nathan (deliver) it into your yad (hand) this yawam (day); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.'
Achaab said, "By whom?" He said, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘By the nair (young) men of the shar (princes) of the provinces.'" Then he said, "Who shall begin the battle?" He answered, "You.

Then he mustered the nair (young) men of the shar (princes) of the provinces, and they were shanayam (two) maah (hundred) and shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two). achar (after) them, he mustered all the im (people), even all the children of Yasharaal (Israel), being shabai (seven) alap (thousand).

They went out at tzahar (noon). Banahadad Ben Hadad was drinking himself shakawar (drunk) in the sakah (pavilions), he and the malak (kings), the shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) malak (kings) who helped him.
The nair (young) men of the shar (princes) of the provinces went out raashawan (first); and Banahadad Hadad sent out, and they told him, saying, "Men are coming out from Shamarawan.
He said, "If they have yatzaa (come) out for shalawam (peace), take them chay (alive); or if they have yatzaa (come) out for war, take them chay (alive).
So these went out of the Iyar, the nair (young) men of the shar (princes) of the provinces, and the chayal (army) which followed them.
They ayash (each) killed his ayash (man). The Aram (Syrians) fled, and Yasharaal (Israel) pursued them. Banahadad Hadad the malak (king) of Aram escaped on a horse with horsemen.
The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) went out, and struck the horses and chariots, and killed the Aram (Syrians) with a gadawal (great) makah (slaughter).

The nabayaa (prophet) came near to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), and said to him, "yalak (go), chazaq (strengthen) yourself, and yadai (mark), and raah (see) what you do; for at the thashawabah (return) of the Shanah the malak (king) of Aram will ilah (come) up against you.

The ibad (servants) of the malak (king) of Aram said to him, "Their Alahayam is a Alahayam of the har (hills); therefore they were chazaq (stronger) than we. But let us fight against them in the mayashawar (plain), and laa (surely) we shall be chazaq (stronger) than they.
Do this thing: sawar (take) the malak (kings) away, every ayash (man) out of his place, and shawam (put) captains in their place.

Muster an chayal (army), like the chayal (army) that you have napal (lost), horse for horse, and chariot for chariot. We will fight against them in the mayashawar (plain), and surely we will be chazaq (stronger) than them." He listened to their qawal (voice), and did so.
It happened at the thashawabah (return) of the Shanah, that Banahadad Hadad mustered the Aram (Syrians), and went up to Apaq, to fight against Yasharaal (Israel).

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) were mustered, and were provisioned, and went qaraah (against) them. The children of Yasharaal (Israel) encamped before them like shanayam (two) little flocks of young goats; but the Aram (Syrians) filled the aratz (country).

A ayash (man) of Alahayam came near and spoke to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), and said, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘Because the Aram (Syrians) have said, "Yahawah is a Alahayam of the har (hills), but he is not a Alahayam of the valleys;" therefore I will nathan (deliver) all this gadawal (great) multitude into your yad (hand), and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.'

They encamped alah (one) over against the other shabai (seven) yawam (days). So it was, that in the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day) the battle was joined; and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) killed one maah (hundred) alap (thousand) footmen of the Aram (Syrians) in one yawam (day).

But the yathar (rest) fled to Apaq, into the Iyar; and the wall napal (fell) on isharayam (twenty) - shabai (seven) alap (thousand) men who were yathar (left). Banahadad Hadad fled, and came into the Iyar, into an inner room.

His ibad (servants) said to him, "See now, we have heard that the malak (kings) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) are chasad (merciful) malak (kings). Please let us shawam (put) sackcloth on our bodies, and ropes on our raash (heads), and yatzaa (go) out to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel). Maybe he will chayah (save) your napash (life).

So they put sackcloth on their bodies and ropes on their raash (heads), and came to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), and said, "Your ibad (servant) Banahadad Hadad amar (says), ‘Please let me chayah (live).'" He said, "Is he still chay (alive)? He is my ach (brother).

Now the men observed diligently, and hurried to take this phrase; and they said, "Your ach (brother) Banahadad Hadad." Then he said, "bawaa (go), bring him." Then Banahadad Hadad came out to him; and he caused him to ilah (come) up into the chariot.

Ben Hadad said to him, "The Iyar which my ab (father) took from your ab (father) I will shawab (turn back / repent). You shall shawam (make) streets for yourself in Damashaq, as my ab (father) made in Shamarawan." "I," said Ahab, "will let you shalach (go) with this barayath (covenant)." So he made a barayath (covenant) with him, and let him shalach (go).
A achad (certain) ayash (man) of the ban (sons) of the nabayaa (prophets) said to his rai (fellow) by the dabar (word) of Yahawah, "Please strike me!" The ayash (man) refused to strike him.

Then he said to him, "Because you have not obeyed the qawal (voice) of Yahawah, behold, as soon as you are departed from me, a aray (lion) shall kill you." As soon as he was departed from him, a aray (lion) found him, and killed him.
Then he found achar (another) ayash (man), and said, "Please strike me." The ayash (man) struck him, smiting and wounding him.
So the nabayaa (prophet) departed, and waited for the malak (king) by the darak (way), and disguised himself with his headband over his iyan (eyes).

As the malak (king) passed by, he cried to the malak (king); and he said, "Your ibad (servant) went out into the qarab (midst) of the battle; and behold, a ayash (man) turned sawar (aside), and brought a ayash (man) to me, and said, ‘Guard this ayash (man)! If by any paqad (means) he be missing, then your napash (life) shall be for his napash (life), or else you shall pay a talent of kasap (silver).'
As your ibad (servant) was ishah (busy) here and there, he was gone." The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) said to him, "So your mashapat (judgment) shall be; you yourself have decided it.
He hurried, and took the headband sawar (away) from his iyan (eyes); and the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) recognized that he was of the nabayaa (prophets).

He said to him, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘Because you have let shalach (go) out of your yad (hand) the ayash (man) whom I had charam (devoted) to destruction, therefore your napash (life) shall go for his napash (life), and your im (people) for his im (people).'
The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) went to his bayath (house) Sar and Zaip, and came to Shamarawan.
It happened achar (after) these things, that Nabawath the Yazaraialay had a vineyard, which was in Yazaraial, hard by the hayakal (palace) of Achaab malak (king) of Shamarawan.

Achaab spoke to Nabawath, saying, "nathan (give) me your vineyard, that I may have it for a Gan of herbs, because it is qarawab (near) to my bayath (house); and I will nathan (give) you for it a tawab (better) vineyard than it. Or, if it seems tawab (good) to you, I will nathan (give) you its worth in kasap (money).
Nabawath said to Achaab, "May Yahawah forbid me, that I should nathan (give) the nachalah (inheritance) of my abawath (fathers) to you!

Achaab came into his bayath (house) Sar and Zaip because of the dabar (word) which Nabawath the Yazaraialay had spoken to him; for he had said, "I will not nathan (give) you the nachalah (inheritance) of my abawath (fathers)." He laid himself down on his bed, and turned sabab (away) his panayam (face), and would akal (eat) no lacham (bread).
But Ayazabal his ashah (wife) came to him, and said to him, "Why is your rawach (spirit) so Sar, that you akal (eat) no lacham (bread)?

He said to her, "Because I spoke to Nabawath the Yazaraialay, and said to him, ‘nathan (give) me your vineyard for kasap (money); or else, if it Chapatz you, I will nathan (give) you another vineyard for it.' He answered, ‘I will not nathan (give) you my vineyard.'

Ayazabal his ashah (wife) said to him, "Do you now ishah (govern) the malawakah (kingdom) of Yasharaal (Israel)? qawam (arise), and akal (eat) lacham (bread), and let your lab (heart) be yatab (merry). I will nathan (give) you the vineyard of Nabawath the Yazaraialay.
So she wrote letters in Achaab sham (name), and sealed them with his seal, and sent the letters to the zaqan (elders) and to the nobles who were in his Iyar, who lived with Nabawath.
She wrote in the letters, saying, "qaraa (proclaim) a fast, and yashab (set) Nabawath on raash (high) among the im (people).

yashab (set) shanayam (two) men, base fellows, before him, and let them iwad (testify) amar (against) him, saying, ‘You cursed Alahayam and the malak (king)!' Then yatzaa (carry) him out, and saqal (stone) him to mawath (death).
The men of his Iyar, even the zaqan (elders) and the nobles who lived in his Iyar, did as Ayazabal had sent to them, according as it was written in the letters which she had sent to them.
They proclaimed a fast, and yashab (set) Nabawath on raash (high) among the im (people).

The shanayam (two) men, the base fellows, came in and sat before him. The base anawash (fellows) testified against him, even against Nabawath, in the presence of the im (people), saying, "Nabawath cursed Alahayam and the malak (king)!" Then they carried him out of the Iyar, and stoned him to mawath (death) with aban (stones).
Then they sent to Ayazabal, saying, "Nabawath has been stoned, and is mawath (dead).

It happened, when Ayazabal heard that Nabawath was stoned, and was mawath (dead), that Ayazabal said to Achaab, "qawam (arise), take yarash (possession) of the vineyard of Nabawath the Yazaraialay, which he refused to nathan (give) you for kasap (money); for Nabawath is not chay (alive), but mawath (dead).
It happened, when Achaab heard that Nabawath was mawath (dead), that Achaab rose up to yarad (go) down to the vineyard of Nabawath the Yazaraialay, to take yarash (possession) of it.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Alayah the Thashabay, saying,

"qawam (arise), yarad (go) down to qaraah (meet) Achaab malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), who dwells in Shamarawan. Behold, he is in the vineyard of Nabawath, where he has gone down to take yarash (possession) of it.

You shall dabar (speak) to him, saying, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "Have you killed and also taken yarash (possession)?"' You shall dabar (speak) to him, saying, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "In the place where dogs licked the dam (blood) of Nabawath, dogs will lick your dam (blood), even yours."'
Achaab said to Alayah, "Have you found me, my ayab (enemy)?" He answered, "I have found you, because you have sold yourself to do that which is rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah.

Behold, I will bawaa (bring) rai (evil) on you, and will utterly sweep you bair (away) and will karath (cut) off from Achaab everyone who urinates against a wall, and him who is itzar (shut) up and him who is left at large in Yasharaal (Israel).

I will nathan (make) your bayath (house) like the bayath (house) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, and like the bayath (house) of Baishaa the ban (son) of Achayah for the kais (provocation) with which you have provoked me to kais (anger), and have made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).
Yahawah also spoke of Ayazabal, saying, "The dogs shall akal (eat) Ayazabal by the chayal (rampart) of Yazaraial.
The dogs will akal (eat) he who dies of Achaab in the Iyar; and the birds of the sky will akal (eat) he who dies in the shadah (field).
But there was none like Achaab, who sold himself to do that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, whom Ayazabal his ashah (wife) stirred up.
He did very abominably in yalak (following) idols, according to all that the Amaray (Amorites) did, whom Yahawah yarash (cast) out panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
It happened, when Achaab heard those dabar (words), that he tore his clothes, and shawam (put) sackcloth on his flesh, and fasted, and shakab (lay) in sackcloth, and went softly.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Alayah the Thashabay, saying,

"raah (see) how Achaab humbles panayam (himself) before me? Because he humbles panayam (himself) before me, I will not bawaa (bring) the rai (evil) in his yawam (days); but in his ban (son's) yawam (days) will I bawaa (bring) the rai (evil) on his bayath (house).
They continued shalawash (three) Shanah without war between Aram and Yasharaal (Israel).
It happened in the shalayashay (third) Shanah, that Yahawashapat the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) came down to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).

The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) said to his ibad (servants), "You yadai (know) that Ramathagalaid Galaid is ours, and we are still, and don't take it out of the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Aram?

He said to Yahawashapat, "Will you yalak (go) with me to battle to Ramathagalaid Gilead?" Yahawashapat said to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), "I am as you are, my im (people) as your im (people), my horses as your horses.
Yahawashapat said to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), "Please inquire first for the dabar (word) of Yahawah.

Then the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) gathered the nabayaa (prophets) together, about arabai (four) maah (hundred) men, and said to them, "Shall I yalak (go) against Ramathagalaid Gilead to battle, or shall I chadal (forbear)?" They said, "ilah (go) up; for the Adanay will nathan (deliver) it into the yad (hand) of the malak (king).
But Yahawashapat said, "Isn't there here a nabayaa (prophet) of Yahawah, that we may inquire of him?

The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) said to Yahawashapat, "There is yet one ayash (man) by whom we may inquire of Yahawah, Mayakayahaw the ban (son) of Yamalaa; but I shanaa (hate) him; for he does not nabaa (prophesy) tawab (good) concerning me, but rai (evil)." Yahawashapat said, "Don't let the malak (king) amar (say) so.
Then the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) called an officer, and said, "Quickly get Mayakayahaw the ban (son) of Yamalaa.

Now the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawashapat the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) were sitting ayash (each) Labash his kasaa (throne), Labash in their bagad (robes), in an open place at the entrance of the gate of Shamarawan; and all the nabayaa (prophets) were prophesying panayam (before) them.
Tzadaqayah the ban (son) of Kanainah made him qaran (horns) of barazal (iron), and said, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘With these you shall push the Aram (Syrians), until they are consumed.'
All the nabayaa (prophets) prophesied so, saying, "ilah (go) up to Ramathagalaid Gilead, and tzalach (prosper); for Yahawah will nathan (deliver) it into the yad (hand) of the malak (king).

The malaak (messenger) who went to qaraa (call) Mayakayahaw spoke to him, saying, "See now, the nabayaa (prophets) declare tawab (good) to the malak (king) with one pah (mouth). Please let your dabar (word) be like the dabar (word) of one of them, and dabar (speak) tawab (good).
Mayakayahaw said, "As Yahawah chay (lives), what Yahawah amar (says) to me, that I will dabar (speak).

When he had bawaa (come) to the malak (king), the malak (king) said to him, "Mayakayahaw, shall we yalak (go) to Ramathagalaid Gilead to battle, or shall we chadal (forbear)?" He answered him, "ilah (go) up and tzalach (prosper); and Yahawah will nathan (deliver) it into the yad (hand) of the malak (king).
The malak (king) said to him, "How many paim (times) do I have to shabai (adjure) you that you dabar (speak) to me nothing but the truth in the sham (name) of Yahawah?

He said, "I saw all Yasharaal (Israel) scattered on the har (mountains), as sheep that have no raih (shepherd). Yahawah said, ‘These have no adawan (master). Let them ayash (each) shawab (turn back / repent) to his bayath (house) in shalawam (peace).'
The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) said to Yahawashapat, "Didn't I amar (tell) you that he would not nabaa (prophesy) tawab (good) concerning me, but rai (evil)?

Micaiah said, "Therefore hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah. I saw Yahawah sitting on his kasaa (throne), and all the tzabaa (army) of shamayam (heaven) standing by him on his right yamayan (hand) and on his shamaawal (left).
Yahawah said, ‘Who shall entice Achaab, that he may ilah (go) up and napal (fall) at Ramathagalaid Gilead?' One said one thing; and another said another.
A rawach (spirit) came out and stood panayam (before) Yahawah, and said, ‘I will entice him.'

Yahawah said to him, ‘How?' He said, ‘I will yatzaa (go) out and will be a lying rawach (spirit) in the pah (mouth) of all his nabayaa (prophets).' He said, ‘You will entice him, and will also yakal (prevail). yatzaa (go) out and do so.'
Now therefore, behold, Yahawah has nathan (put) a lying rawach (spirit) in the pah (mouth) of all these your nabayaa (prophets); and Yahawah has spoken rai (evil) concerning you.
Then Tzadaqayah the ban (son) of Kanainah came near, and struck Mayakayahaw on the Lachay, and said, "Which ay (way) did the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah ibar (go) from me to dabar (speak) to you?
Mayakayahaw said, "raah (see), you will see on that yawam (day), when you bawaa (go) into an inner room to hide yourself.
The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) said, "Take Mayakayahaw, and shawab (turn back / repent) him back to Amawan the shar (governor) of the Iyar, and to Yawaash the malak (king's) ban (son).

amar (say), ‘Thus amar (says) the malak (king), "shawam (put) this fellow in the bayath (prison), and akal (feed) him with lacham (bread) of affliction and with mayam (water) of affliction, until I bawaa (come) in shalawam (peace)."'
Mayakayahaw said, "If you shawab (turn back / repent) at all in shalawam (peace), Yahawah has not spoken by me." He said, "Listen, all you im (people)!
So the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawashapat the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) went up to Ramathagalaid Gilead.

The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) said to Yahawashapat, "I will disguise myself, and bawaa (go) into the battle; but you Labash on your bagad (robes)." The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) disguised himself, and went into the battle.

Now the malak (king) of Aram had tzawah (commanded) the shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) shar (captains) of his chariots, saying, Fight neither with qatan (small) nor gadawal (great), except only with the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).

It happened, when the shar (captains) of the chariots saw Yahawashapat, that they said, "Surely that is the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)!" and they turned sawar (aside) to fight against him. Yahawashapat cried out.
It happened, when the shar (captains) of the chariots saw that it was not the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), that they turned shawab (turn back / repent) from achar (pursuing) him.

A certain ayash (man) drew his qashath (bow) at random, and struck the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) between the joints of the armor. Therefore he said to the rakab (driver) of his chariot, "hapak (turn) your yad (hand), and yatzaa (carry) me out of the machanah (battle); for I am severely chalah (wounded).

The battle increased that yawam (day). The malak (king) was propped up in his chariot facing the Aram (Syrians), and died at evening. The dam (blood) ran out of the makah (wound) into the bottom of the chariot.
A cry went throughout the machanah (army) about the going down of the shamash (sun), saying, "Every ayash (man) to his Iyar, and every ayash (man) to his aratz (country)!
So the malak (king) died, and was brought to Shamarawan; and they buried the malak (king) in Shamarawan.
They washed the chariot by the pool of Shamarawan; and the dogs licked up his dam (blood) where the prostitutes washed themselves; according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah which he spoke.

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Achaab, and all that he did, and the ivory bayath (house) which he built, and all the Iyar that he built, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
So Achaab slept with his abawath (fathers); and Achazayah his ban (son) reigned in his place.
Yahawashapat the ban (son) of Asaa began to malak (reign) over Yahawadah (Judah) in the fourth Shanah of Achaab malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Yahawashapat was shalawashayam (thirty) - chamash (five) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) Shanah in Yarawashalam. His am (mother's) sham (name) was Izawabah the bath (daughter) of Shalachay.

He walked in all the darak (way) of Asaa his ab (father); He didn't sawar (turn) aside from it, doing that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah: however the bamah (high) places were not taken sawar (away); the im (people) still sacrificed and burnt qatar (incense) in the bamah (high) places.
Yahawashapat made shalam (peace) with the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yahawashapat, and his might that he showed, and how he warred, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)?
The yathar (remnant) of the qadash (sodomites), that remained in the yawam (days) of his ab (father) Asaa, he bair (put) away out of the aratz (land).
There was no malak (king) in Adam: a natzab (deputy) was malak (king).
Yahawashapat made ships of Tharashayash to yalak (go) to Awapayar for gold: but they didn't halak (go); for the ships were shabar (broken) at Itzayawanagabar Geber.
Then Achazayah the ban (son) of Achaab said to Yahawashapat, "Let my ibad (servants) yalak (go) with your ibad (servants) in the ships." But Yahawashapat would not.
Yahawashapat slept with his abawath (fathers), and was buried with his abawath (fathers) in the Iyar of Dawad his ab (father); Yahawaram his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Achazayah the ban (son) of Achaab began to malak (reign) over Yasharaal (Israel) in Shamarawan in the seventeenth Shanah of Yahawashapat malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and he reigned two Shanah over Yasharaal (Israel).

He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, and walked in the darak (way) of his ab (father), and in the darak (way) of his am (mother), and in the darak (way) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, in which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).
He served Bail, and worshiped him, and provoked to kais (anger) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), according to all that his ab (father) had done.
Mawaab rebelled against Yasharaal (Israel) achar (after) the mawath (death) of Achaab.

Achazayah napal (fell) down through the lattice in his upper room that was in Shamarawan, and was chalah (sick). So he sent malaak (messengers), and said to them, "yalak (go), inquire of Bailazabawab Zebub, the Alahayam of Iqarawan, whether I will chayah (recover) of this sickness.

But the malaak (angel) of Yahawah said to Alayah the Thashabay, "qawam (arise), ilah (go) up to qaraah (meet) the malaak (messengers) of the malak (king) of Shamarawan, and dabar (tell) them, ‘Is it because there is no Alahayam in Yasharaal (Israel), that you halak (go) to inquire of Bailazabawab Zebub, the Alahayam of Iqarawan?
Now therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah, "You shall not yarad (come) down from the bed where you have gone up, but shall mawath (surely) mawath (die)."'" Alayah departed.
The malaak (messengers) returned to him, and he said to them, "Why is it that you have returned?

They said to him, "A ayash (man) came up to qaraah (meet) us, and said to us, ‘yalak (go), shawab (turn back / repent) to the malak (king) who sent you, and dabar (tell) him, "Thus dabar (says) Yahawah, ‘Is it because there is no Alahayam in Yasharaal (Israel), that you shalach (send) to inquire of Bailazabawab Zebub, the Alahayam of Iqarawan? Therefore you shall not yarad (come) down from the bed where you have gone up, but shall mawath (surely) mawath (die).'"'
He said to them, "What kind of ayash (man) was he who came up to qaraah (meet) you, and told you these dabar (words)?
They answered him, "He was a hairy bail (man), and wearing a leather belt around his waist." He said, "It is Alayah the Thashabay.

Then the malak (king) sent a shar (captain) of chamashayam (fifty) with his chamashayam (fifty) to him. He went up to him; and behold, he was sitting on the raash (top) of the har (hill). He said to him, "ayash (man) of Alahayam, the malak (king) has said, ‘yarad (come) down!'

Alayah answered to the shar (captain) of chamashayam (fifty), "If I am a ayash (man) of Alahayam, let ash (fire) yarad (come) down from the sky, and akal (consume) you and your chamashayam (fifty)!" ash (fire) came down from the sky, and consumed him and his chamashayam (fifty).

Again he sent to him achar (another) shar (captain) of chamashayam (fifty) and his chamashayam (fifty). He answered him, "ayash (man) of Alahayam, the malak (king) has said, ‘yarad (come) down quickly!'

Alayah answered them, "If I am a ayash (man) of Alahayam, let ash (fire) yarad (come) down from the sky, and akal (consume) you and your chamashayam (fifty)!" The ash (fire) of Alahayam came down from the sky, and consumed him and his chamashayam (fifty).

Again he sent the shar (captain) of a shalayashay (third) chamashayam (fifty) with his chamashayam (fifty). The shalayashay (third) shar (captain) of chamashayam (fifty) went up, and came and fell on his knees before Alayah, and begged him, and said to him, "ayash (man) of Alahayam, please let my napash (life), and the napash (life) of these chamashayam (fifty) your ibad (servants), be precious in your iyan (sight).

Behold, ash (fire) came down from the sky, and consumed the shanayam (two) raashawan (former) shar (captains) of chamashayam (fifty) with their chamashayam (fifties). But now let my napash (life) be precious in your iyan (sight).
The malaak (angel) of Yahawah said to Alayah, "yarad (go) down with him. Don't be yaraa (afraid) of him." He qawam (arose), and went down with him to the malak (king).

He said to him, "Thus dabar (says) Yahawah, ‘Because you have sent malaak (messengers) to inquire of Bailazabawab Zebub, the Alahayam of Iqarawan, is it because there is no Alahayam in Yasharaal (Israel) to inquire of his dabar (word)? Therefore you shall not yarad (come) down from the bed where you have gone up, but shall mawath (surely) mawath (die).'

So he died according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah which Alayah had spoken. Yahawaram began to malak (reign) in his place in the shanayam (second) Shanah of Yahawaram the ban (son) of Yahawashapat malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah); because he had no ban (son).
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Achazayah which he did, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
It happened, when Yahawah would ilah (take) up Alayah by a whirlwind into shamayam (heaven), that Alayah went with Alayashai from Galagal.

Alayah said to Alayashai, "Please wait here, for Yahawah has sent me as far as Bayathaal." Alayashai said, "As Yahawah chay (lives), and as your napash (soul) chay (lives), I will not leave you." So they went down to Bayathaal.

The ban (sons) of the nabayaa (prophets) who were at Bayathaal came out to Alayashai, and said to him, "Do you yadai (know) that Yahawah will take away your adawan (master) from your raash (head) today?" He said, "Yes, I yadai (know) it; hold your chashah (peace).

Alayah said to him, "Alayashai, please wait here, for Yahawah has sent me to Yarayachaw." He said, "As Yahawah chay (lives), and as your napash (soul) chay (lives), I will not leave you." So they came to Yarayachaw.

The ban (sons) of the nabayaa (prophets) who were at Yarayachaw came near to Alayashai, and said to him, "Do you yadai (know) that Yahawah will take away your adawan (master) from your raash (head) today?" He answered, "Yes, I yadai (know) it. Hold your chashah (peace).

Alayah said to him, "Please wait here, for Yahawah has sent me to the Yaradan." He said, "As Yahawah chay (lives), and as your napash (soul) chay (lives), I will not leave you." They shanayam (both) went on.
chamashayam (fifty) men of the ban (sons) of the nabayaa (prophets) went, and stood opposite them Rachawaq a distance; and they shanayam (both) stood by the Yaradan.
Alayah took his adarath (mantle), and wrapped it together, and struck the mayam (waters), and they were divided here and there, so that they shanayam (two) went over on dry charabah (ground).

It happened, when they had gone over, that Alayah said to Alayashai, "shaal (ask) what I shall do for you, before I am taken from you." Alayashai said, "Please let a shanayam (double) pah (portion) of your rawach (spirit) be on me.
He said, "You have asked a hard thing. If you raah (see) me when I am taken from you, it shall be so for you; but if not, it shall not be so.
It happened, as they still went on, and talked, that behold, a chariot of ash (fire) and horses of ash (fire) separated them; and Alayah went up by a whirlwind into shamayam (heaven).

Alayashai saw it, and he cried, "My ab (father), my ab (father), the chariots of Yasharaal (Israel) and its horsemen!" He saw him no more: and he took chazaq (hold) of his own clothes, and tore them in shanayam (two) pieces.
He took up also the adarath (mantle) of Alayah that napal (fell) from him, and went shawab (turn back / repent), and stood by the shapah (bank) of the Yaradan.

He took the adarath (mantle) of Alayah that napal (fell) from him, and struck the mayam (waters), and said, "Where is Yahawah, the Alahayam of Alayah?" When he also had struck the mayam (waters), they were divided here and there; and Alayashai went over.

When the ban (sons) of the nabayaa (prophets) who were at Yarayachaw over against him saw him, they said, "The rawach (spirit) of Alayah nawach (rests) on Alayashai." They came to qaraah (meet) him, and bowed themselves to the aratz (ground) before him.

They said to him, "See now, there are with your ibad (servants) chamashayam (fifty) chayal (strong) men. Please let them yalak (go) and seek your adawan (master). Perhaps the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah has taken him up, and put him on some har (mountain), or into some Gayaa. He said, "You shall not shalach (send) them.

When they urged him until he was bawash (ashamed), he said, "shalach (send) them." They sent therefore chamashayam (fifty) men; and they searched for shalawash (three) yawam (days), but didn't matzaa (find) him.
They came shawab (turn back / repent) to him, while he stayed at Yarayachaw; and he said to them, "Didn't I amar (tell) you, ‘Don't yalak (go)?'

The men of the Iyar said to Alayashai, "Behold, please, the mawashab (situation) of this Iyar is tawab (pleasant), as my Adawan raah (see); but the mayam (water) is rai (bad), and the aratz (land) shakal (miscarries).
He said, "Bring me a Chadash jar, and shawam (put) Malach in it." They brought it to him.

He went out to the spring of the mayam (waters), and threw Malach into it, and said, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘I have healed these mayam (waters). There shall not be from there any more mawath (death) or miscarrying.'
So the mayam (waters) were healed to this yawam (day), according to the dabar (word) of Alayashai which he spoke.
He went up from there to Bayathaal. As he was going up by the darak (way), some youths came out of the Iyar and mocked him, and said to him, "ilah (go) up, you Qarach! ilah (go) up, you Qarach!

He looked achar (behind) him and saw them, and cursed them in the sham (name) of Yahawah. shanayam (two) female bears came out of the Yair, and mauled arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two) of those youths.
He went from there to har (mount) Karamal, and from there he returned to Shamarawan.

Now Yahawaram the ban (son) of Achaab began to malak (reign) over Yasharaal (Israel) in Shamarawan in the eighteenth Shanah of Yahawashapat malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and reigned shanayam (twelve) Shanah.

He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, but not like his ab (father), and like his am (mother); for he sawar (put) away the matzabah (pillar) of Bail that his ab (father) had made.
Nevertheless he held to the chataah (sins) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin); he didn't sawar (depart) from it.

Now Mayashai malak (king) of Mawaab was a sheep breeder; and he rendered to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) the wool of one maah (hundred) alap (thousand) lambs, and of one maah (hundred) alap (thousand) ayal (rams).
But it happened, when Achaab was mawath (dead), that the malak (king) of Mawaab rebelled against the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).
malak (king) Yahawaram went out of Shamarawan at that yawam (time), and mustered all Yasharaal (Israel).

He went and sent to Yahawashapat the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), saying, "The malak (king) of Mawaab has rebelled against me. Will you yalak (go) with me against Mawaab to battle?" He said, "I will ilah (go) up. I am as you are, my im (people) as your im (people), my horses as your horses.
He said, "Which darak (way) shall we ilah (go) up?" He answered, "The darak (way) of the madabar (wilderness) of Adam.

So the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) went, and the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and the malak (king) of Adam; and they made a sabab (circuit) of shabai (seven) yawam (days)' darak (journey). There was no mayam (water) for the machanah (army), nor for the animals that followed them.
The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) said, "Alas! For Yahawah has called these shalawash (three) malak (kings) together to nathan (deliver) them into the yad (hand) of Mawaab.

But Yahawashapat said, "Isn't there here a nabayaa (prophet) of Yahawah, that we may inquire of Yahawah by him?" One of the malak (king) of Yasharaal ibad (servants) answered, "Alayashai the ban (son) of Shapat is here, who poured mayam (water) on the yad (hands) of Alayah.
Yahawashapat said, "The dabar (word) of Yahawah is with him." So the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawashapat and the malak (king) of Adam went down to him.

Alayashai said to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), "What have I to do with you? yalak (go) to the nabayaa (prophets) of your ab (father), and to the nabayaa (prophets) of your am (mother)." The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) said to him, "No; for Yahawah has called these shalawash (three) malak (kings) together to nathan (deliver) them into the yad (hand) of Mawaab.

Alayashai said, "As Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) chay (lives), panayam (before) whom I imad (stand), surely, were it not that I nashaa (respect) the panayam (presence) of Yahawashapat the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), I would not look toward you, nor raah (see) you.
But now bring me a minstrel." It happened, when the minstrel played, that the yad (hand) of Yahawah came on him.
He said, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘ishah (make) this nachal (valley) full of trenches.'

For thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘You will not raah (see) rawach (wind), neither will you raah (see) rain; yet that nachal (valley) shall be filled with mayam (water), and you will drink, both you and your livestock and your animals.
This is but a qalal (light) thing in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah. He will also nathan (deliver) the Mawaab (Moabites) into your yad (hand).

You shall strike every fortified Iyar, and every choice Iyar, and shall napal (fell) every tawab (good) itz (tree), and stop all springs of mayam (water), and mar every tawab (good) chalaqah (piece) of land with aban (stones).'
It happened in the baqar (morning), about the time of offering the offering, that behold, mayam (water) came by the darak (way) of Adam, and the aratz (country) was filled with mayam (water).

Mawaab when all the Moabites heard that the malak (kings) had ilah (come) up to fight against them, they gathered themselves together, all who were able to put on armor, and upward, and stood on the border.
They rose up shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and the shamash (sun) shone on the mayam (water), and the Mawaab (Moabites) saw the mayam (water) over against them as Adam as dam (blood).
They said, "This is dam (blood). The malak (kings) are charab (surely) destroyed, and they have struck ayash (each) other. Now therefore, Mawaab, to the spoil!

When they came to the machanah (camp) of Yasharaal (Israel), the Yasharaal (Israelites) rose up and struck the Mawaab (Moabites), so that they fled panayam (before) them; and they went forward into the nakah (land) smiting the Mawaab (Moabites).

They haras (beat) down the Iyar; and on every tawab (good) chalaqah (piece) of shalak (land) they cast every ayash (man) his aban (stone), and filled it; and they stopped all the springs of mayam (water), and felled all the tawab (good) itz (trees), until in Qayaracharash Hareseth only they shaar (left) its aban (stones); however the men armed with slings went sabab (about) it, and struck it.

When the malak (king) of Mawaab saw that the battle was too severe for him, he took with him shabai (seven) maah (hundred) men who drew charab (sword), to break through to the malak (king) of Adam; but they could not.

Then he took his eldest ban (son) who would have reigned in his place, and offered him for a burnt ilah (offering) on the wall. There was gadawal (great) qatzap (wrath) against Yasharaal (Israel): and they departed from him, and returned to their own aratz (land).

Now there cried a achad (certain) ashah (woman) of the wives of the ban (sons) of the nabayaa (prophets) to Alayashai, saying, "Your ibad (servant) my ayash (husband) is mawath (dead). You yadai (know) that your ibad (servant) feared Yahawah. Now the creditor has bawaa (come) to take for himself my shanayam (two) children to be ibad (slaves).
