Alayashai said to her, "What shall I do for you? nagad (tell) me: what do you have in the bayath (house)?" She said, "Your handmaid has nothing in the bayath (house), except a pot of shaman (oil).
Then he said, "yalak (go), shaal (borrow) containers from of all your Shakan, even rayaq (empty) containers. Don't borrow just a few.
You shall bawaa (go) in, and shut the door on you and on your ban (sons), and pour out into all those containers; and you shall nasai (set) aside that which is Malaa.
So she went from him, and shut the door on her and on her ban (sons); they brought the containers to her, and she poured out.
It happened, when the containers were malaa (full), that she said to her ban (son), "Bring me another container." He said to her, "There isn't another container." The shaman (oil) stopped flowing.
Then she came and told the ayash (man) of Alahayam. He said, "yalak (go), sell the shaman (oil), and shalam (pay) your debt; and you and your ban (sons) chayah (live) on the yathar (rest).

It fell on a yawam (day), that Alayashai passed to Shawanam, where there was a prominent ashah (woman); and she persuaded him to akal (eat) lacham (bread). So it was, that as often as he passed by, he turned in there to akal (eat) lacham (bread).
She said to her ayash (husband), "See now, I yadai (perceive) that this is a qadawash (holy) ayash (man) of Alahayam, that passes by us continually.

Please let us ishah (make) a qatan (little) room on the wall. Let us shawam (set) for him there a bed, a table, a chair, and a manawarah (lamp) stand. It shall be, when he bawaa (comes) to us, that he shall sawar (turn) in there.
One yawam (day) he came there, and he turned into the room and shakab (lay) there.
He said to Gayachazay his nair (servant), "qaraa (call) this Shawanamayath." When he had called her, she stood panayam (before) him.

He said to him, "amar (say) now to her, ‘Behold, you have cared for us with all this charadah (care). What is to be done for you? Would you like to be spoken for to the malak (king), or to the shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army)?'" She answered, "I yashab (dwell) among my own im (people).
He said, "What then is to be done for her?" Gayachazay answered, "Most certainly she has no ban (son), and her ayash (husband) is zaqan (old).
He said, "qaraa (call) her." When he had called her, she stood in the door.
He said, "At this mawaid (season), when the ith (time) comes around, you will embrace a ban (son)." She said, "No, my Adawan, you ayash (man) of Alahayam, do not lie to your handmaid.
The ashah (woman) conceived, and bore a ban (son) at that mawaid (season), when the ith (time) came around, as Alayashai had said to her.
When the yalad (child) was grown, it happened one yawam (day) that he went out to his ab (father) to the reapers.
He said to his ab (father), "My raash (head)! My raash (head)!" He said to his nair (servant), "nashaa (carry) him to his am (mother).
When he had taken him, and brought him to his am (mother), he sat on her knees until tzahar (noon), and then died.
She went up and laid him on the bed of the ayash (man) of Alahayam, and shut the door on him, and went out.

She called to her ayash (husband), and said, "Please shalach (send) me one of the nair (servants), and one of the donkeys, that I may run to the ayash (man) of Alahayam, and shawab (turn back / repent) again.
He said, "Why would you want halak (go) to him today? It is neither new chadash (moon) nor shabath (sabbath)." She said, "It's alright.
Then she saddled a donkey, and said to her nair (servant), "Drive, and yalak (go) forward! Don't slow down for me, unless I ask you to.

So she went, and came to the ayash (man) of Alahayam to har (mount) Karamal. It happened, when the ayash (man) of Alahayam saw her afar off, that he said to Gayachazay his nair (servant), "Behold, there is the Shawanamayath.

Please run now to qaraah (meet) her, and ask her, ‘Is it shalawam (well) with you? Is it shalawam (well) with your ayash (husband)? Is it shalawam (well) with the yalad (child)?'" She answered, "It is shalawam (well).

When she came to the ayash (man) of Alahayam to the har (hill), she caught hold of his feet. Gayachazay came near to thrust her away; but the ayash (man) of Alahayam said, "Leave her rapah (alone); for her napash (soul) is troubled within her; and Yahawah has hidden it from me, and has not told me.
Then she said, "Did I shaal (desire) a ban (son) of my Adawan? Didn't I amar (say), Do not deceive me?

Then he said to Gayachazay, "Tuck your cloak into your belt, take my mashainah (staff) in your yad (hand), and go your yalak (way). If you matzaa (meet) any ayash (man), don't greet him; and if anyone greets you, don't answer him again. Then shawam (lay) my mashainah (staff) on the panayam (face) of the nair (child).
The am (mother) of the nair (child) said, "As Yahawah chay (lives), and as your napash (soul) chay (lives), I will not leave you." He qawam (arose), and followed her.

Gayachazay passed on panayam (before) them, and laid the mashainah (staff) on the panayam (face) of the nair (child); but there was neither qawal (voice), nor hearing. Therefore he returned to qaraah (meet) him, and told him, saying, "The nair (child) has not awakened.
When Alayashai had bawaa (come) into the bayath (house), behold, the nair (child) was mawath (dead), and laid on his bed.
He went in therefore, and shut the door on them shanayam (both), and prayed to Yahawah.

He went up, and shakab (lay) on the yalad (child), and shawam (put) his pah (mouth) on his pah (mouth), and his iyan (eyes) on his iyan (eyes), and his kap (hands) on his kap (hands). He stretched himself on him; and the flesh of the yalad (child) grew warm.

Then he returned, and walked in the bayath (house) achad (once) back and forth; and went up, and stretched himself on him. Then the nair (child) sneezed shabai (seven) paim (times), and the nair (child) opened his iyan (eyes).
He called Gayachazay, and said, "qaraa (call) this Shawanamayath!" So he called her. When she had bawaa (come) in to him, he said, "nashaa (take) up your ban (son).
Then she went in, and napal (fell) at his feet, and bowed herself to the aratz (ground); and she took up her ban (son), and went out.

Alayashai came again to Galagal. There was a famine in the aratz (land); and the ban (sons) of the nabayaa (prophets) were sitting panayam (before) him; and he said to his nair (servant), "Set on the gadawal (great) pot, and boil stew for the ban (sons) of the nabayaa (prophets).

One went out into the shadah (field) to gather awarah (herbs), and found a shadah (wild) vine, and gathered of it shadah (wild) gourds his bagad (lap) full, and came and shred them into the pot of stew; for they didn't recognize them.

So they poured out for the men to akal (eat). It happened, as they were eating of the stew, that they cried out, and said, "ayash (man) of Alahayam, there is mawath (death) in the pot!" They could not akal (eat) of it.
But he said, "Then bring meal." He cast it into the pot; and he said, "Pour out for the im (people), that they may akal (eat)." There was no dabar (harm) in the pot.

A ayash (man) from Baal Shalishah came, and brought the ayash (man) of Alahayam lacham (bread) of the bakawar (first) bakawar (fruits), isharayam (twenty) loaves of barley, and fresh ears of grain in his sack. He said, "nathan (give) to the im (people), that they may akal (eat).

His sharath (servant) said, "What, should I nathan (set) this panayam (before) a maah (hundred) men?" But he said, "nathan (give) the im (people), that they may akal (eat); for thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘They will akal (eat), and will have some yathar (left) over.'
So he nathan (set) it panayam (before) them, and they ate, and yathar (left) some of it, according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah.

Now Naiman, shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army) of the malak (king) of Aram, was a gadawal (great) ayash (man) with his adawan (master), and nashaa (honorable), because by him Yahawah had given thashawaih (victory) to Aram: he was also a gabawar (mighty) ayash (man) of valor, but he was a leper.
The Aram (Syrians) had gone out in gadawad (bands), and had brought away captive out of the aratz (land) of Yasharaal (Israel) a qatan (little) maiden; and she waited on Naiman ashah (wife).
She said to her mistress, "I wish that my Adawan were with the nabayaa (prophet) who is in Shamarawan! Then he would heal him of his leprosy.
Someone went in, and told his Adawan, saying, "The maiden who is from the aratz (land) of Yasharaal (Israel) said this.

The malak (king) of Aram said, "bawaa (go) now, and I will shalach (send) a letter to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)." He departed, and took with him ishar (ten) talents of kasap (silver), and shash (six) alap (thousand) pieces of gold, and ishar (ten) changes of clothing.

He brought the letter to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "Now when this letter has bawaa (come) to you, behold, I have sent Naiman my ibad (servant) to you, that you may heal him of his leprosy.

It happened, when the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) had qaraa (read) the letter, that he tore his clothes, and said, "Am I Alahayam, to mawath (kill) and to chayah (make) alive, that this zah (man) shalach (sends) to me to heal a ayash (man) of his leprosy? But please yadai (consider) and raah (see) how he seeks a quarrel against me.

It was so, when Alayashai the ayash (man) of Alahayam heard that the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) had torn his clothes, that he sent to the malak (king), saying, "Why have you torn your clothes? Let him bawaa (come) now to me, and he shall yadai (know) that there is a nabayaa (prophet) in Yasharaal (Israel).
So Naiman came with his horses and with his chariots, and stood at the door of the bayath (house) of Alayashai.

Alayashai sent a malaak (messenger) to him, saying, "halak (go) and wash in the Yaradan shabai (seven) paim (times), and your flesh shall shawab (turn back / repent) again to you, and you shall be tahar (clean).

But Naiman was qatzap (angry), and went yalak (away), and said, "Behold, I thought, ‘He will yatzaa (surely) yatzaa (come) out to me, and imad (stand), and qaraa (call) on the sham (name) of Yahawah his Alahayam, and wave his yad (hand) over the place, and heal the leper.'

Abanah Abanah and Parapar, the nahar (rivers) of Damashaq, tawab (better) than all the mayam (waters) of Yasharaal (Israel)? Couldn't I wash in them, and be tahar (clean)?" So he turned and went yalak (away) in a chamah (rage).

His ibad (servants) came near, and spoke to him, and said, "My ab (father), if the nabayaa (prophet) had asked you do some gadawal (great) thing, wouldn't you have done it? How much rather then, when he amar (says) to you, ‘Wash, and be tahar (clean)?'

Then went he down, and dipped himself shabai (seven) paim (times) in the Yaradan, according to the dabar (saying) of the ayash (man) of Alahayam; and his flesh was restored like the flesh of a qatan (little) nair (child), and he was tahar (clean).

He returned to the ayash (man) of Alahayam, he and all his machanah (company), and came, and stood panayam (before) him; and he said, "See now, I yadai (know) that there is no Alahayam in all the aratz (earth), but in Yasharaal (Israel). Now therefore, please take a barakah (gift) from your ibad (servant).
But he said, "As Yahawah chay (lives), panayam (before) whom I imad (stand), I will receive none." He urged him to take it; but he refused.

Naiman said, "If not, then, please let tzamad (two) mules' mashaa (burden) of adamah (earth) be given to your ibad (servant); for your ibad (servant) will from now on ishah (offer) neither burnt ilah (offering) nor zabach (sacrifice) to other Alahayam, but to Yahawah.

In this thing may Yahawah pardon your ibad (servant): when my adawan (master) goes into the bayath (house) of Ramawan to shachah (worship) there, and he shain (leans) on my yad (hand), and I shachah (bow) myself in the bayath (house) of Ramawan. When I shachah (bow) myself in the bayath (house) of Ramawan, may Yahawah pardon your ibad (servant) in this thing.
He said to him, "yalak (go) in shalawam (peace)." So he departed from him a little aratz (way).

But Gayachazay the nair (servant) of Alayashai the ayash (man) of Alahayam, said, "Behold, my adawan (master) has spared this Naiman the Aramay (Syrian), in not receiving at his yad (hands) that which he brought. As Yahawah chay (lives), I will run achar (after) him, and take something from him.
So Gayachazay followed achar (after) Naiman. When Naiman saw rawatz (one) running achar (after) him, he came down from the chariot to qaraah (meet) him, and said, "Is all shalawam (well)?

He said, "All is shalawam (well). My adawan (master) has sent me, saying, ‘Behold, even now shanayam (two) nair (young) men of the ban (sons) of the nabayaa (prophets) have bawaa (come) to me from the har (hill) country of Aparayam. Please nathan (give) them a talent of kasap (silver) and shanayam (two) changes of clothing.'

Naiman said, "Be pleased to take kakar (two) talents." He urged him, and bound shanayam (two) talents of kasap (silver) in shanayam (two) bags, with shanayam (two) changes of clothing, and laid them on shanayam (two) of his nair (servants); and they carried them panayam (before) him.
When he came to the hill, he took them from their yad (hand), and stored them in the bayath (house). Then he let the men shalach (go), and they departed.
But he went in, and stood before his adawan (master). Alayashai said to him, "Where did you come from, Gayachazay?" He said, "Your ibad (servant) went nowhere.

He said to him, "Didn't my lab (heart) halak (go) with you, when the ayash (man) turned from his chariot to qaraah (meet) you? Is it a ith (time) to receive kasap (money), and to receive bagad (garments), and olive groves and vineyards, and sheep and cattle, and male ibad (servants) and female shapachah (servants)?
Therefore the leprosy of Naiman will cling to you and to your zarai (seed) iwalam (forever)." He went out from his panayam (presence) a leper, as white as snow.
The ban (sons) of the nabayaa (prophets) said to Alayashai, "See now, the place where we yashab (dwell) before you is too tzar (small) for us.
Please let us yalak (go) to the Yaradan, and every ayash (man) take a beam from there, and let us ishah (make) us a place there, where we may yashab (dwell)." He answered, "yalak (go)!
One said, "Please be pleased to yalak (go) with your ibad (servants)." He answered, "I will yalak (go).
So he went with them. When they came to the Yaradan, they cut down itz (wood).
But as one was napal (felling) a beam, the axe barazal (head) napal (fell) into the mayam (water). Then he cried, and said, "Alas, my adawan (master)! For it was borrowed.
The ayash (man) of Alahayam asked, "Where did it napal (fall)?" He showed him the place. He cut down a itz (stick), threw it in there, and made the barazal (iron) float.
He said, "Take it." So he shalach (put) out his yad (hand) and took it.
Now the malak (king) of Aram was warring against Yasharaal (Israel); and he took yaitz (counsel) with his ibad (servants), saying, "My camp will be in such and Alamanay a place.
The ayash (man) of Alahayam sent to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "Beware that you not ibar (pass) such a place; for the Aram (Syrians) are Nachath down there.
The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) sent to the place which the ayash (man) of Alahayam told him and warned him of; and he saved himself there, not achad (once) nor shanayam (twice).

The lab (heart) of the malak (king) of Aram was very troubled about this. He called his ibad (servants), and said to them, "Won't you show me which of us is for the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)?

One of his ibad (servants) said, "No, my Adawan, O malak (king); but Alayashai, the nabayaa (prophet) who is in Yasharaal (Israel), nagad (tells) the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) the dabar (words) that you dabar (speak) in your bedroom.
He said, "yalak (go) and raah (see) where he is, that I may shalach (send) and get him." It was told him, saying, "Behold, he is in Dathan.
Therefore he sent horses, chariots, and a Kabad chayal (army) there. They came by layal (night), and surrounded the Iyar.

When the sharath (servant) of the ayash (man) of Alahayam had risen shakam (early), and gone out, behold, an chayal (army) with horses and chariots was around the Iyar. His nair (servant) said to him, "Alas, my adawan (master)! What shall we do?
He answered, "Don't be yaraa (afraid); for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.

Alayashai prayed, and said, "Yahawah, please open his iyan (eyes), that he may raah (see)." Yahawah opened the iyan (eyes) of the nair (young) man; and he saw: and behold, the har (mountain) was malaa (full) of horses and chariots of ash (fire) around Alayashai.
When they came down to him, Alayashai prayed to Yahawah, and said, "Please strike this gaway (people) with blindness." He struck them with blindness according to the dabar (word) of Alayashai.
Alayashai said to them, "This is not the darak (way), neither is this the Iyar. yalak (follow) me, and I will yalak (bring) you to the ayash (man) whom you seek." He led them to Shamarawan.

It happened, when they had bawaa (come) into Shamarawan, that Alayashai said, "Yahawah, open the iyan (eyes) of these men, that they may raah (see)." Yahawah opened their iyan (eyes), and they saw; and behold, they were in the midst of Shamarawan.
The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) said to Alayashai, when he saw them, "My ab (father), shall I strike them? Shall I strike them?

He answered, "You shall not strike them. Would you strike those whom you have taken captive with your charab (sword) and with your qashath (bow)? shawam (set) lacham (bread) and mayam (water) panayam (before) them, that they may akal (eat) and drink, and yalak (go) to their adawan (master).

He prepared gadawal (great) feast for them. When they had eaten and drunk, he sent them shalach (away), and they went to their adawan (master). The gadawad (bands) of Aram stopped raiding the aratz (land) of Yasharaal (Israel).
It happened achar (after) this, that Banahadad malak (king) of Aram gathered all his machanah (army), and went up and besieged Shamarawan.

There was a gadawal (great) famine in Shamarawan. Behold, they besieged it, until a donkey's raash (head) was sold for shamanayam (eighty) pieces of kasap (silver), and the rabai (fourth) part of a kab of dove's dung for chamash (five) pieces of kasap (silver).
As the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) was passing by on the wall, a ashah (woman) cried to him, saying, "yashai (help), my Adawan, O malak (king)!
He said, "If Yahawah doesn't yashai (help) you, from where could I yashai (help) you? From of the threshing floor, or from the yaqab (winepress)?

The malak (king) said to her, "What ails you?" She answered, "This ashah (woman) said to me, ‘nathan (give) your ban (son), that we may akal (eat) him today, and we will akal (eat) my ban (son) tomorrow.'
So we boiled my ban (son), and ate him: and I said to her on the achar (next) yawam (day), ‘nathan (give) your ban (son), that we may akal (eat) him;' and she has hidden her ban (son).

It happened, when the malak (king) heard the dabar (words) of the ashah (woman), that he tore his clothes (now he was passing by on the wall); and the im (people) looked, and behold, he had sackcloth underneath on his flesh.
Then he said, "Alahayam do so to me, and more also, if the raash (head) of Alayashai the ban (son) of Shapat shall imad (stay) on him this yawam (day).

But Alayashai was sitting in his bayath (house), and the zaqan (elders) were sitting with him. Then the king sent a ayash (man) from panayam (before) him; but before the malaak (messenger) came to him, he said to the zaqan (elders), "Do you raah (see) how this ban (son) of a ratzach (murderer) has sent to sawar (take) away my raash (head)? raah (see), when the malaak (messenger) bawaa (comes), shut the door, and hold the door shut against him. Isn't the qawal (sound) of his adawan (master's) feet achar (behind) him?
While he was still talking with them, behold, the malaak (messenger) came down to him. Then he said, "Behold, this rai (evil) is from Yahawah. Why should I wait for Yahawah any longer?

Alayashai said, "Hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah. Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘Tomorrow about this ith (time) a measure of fine flour will be sold for a shekel, and saah (two) measures of barley for a shekel, in the gate of Shamarawan.'

Then the shalayash (captain) on whose yad (hand) the malak (king) leaned answered the ayash (man) of Alahayam, and said, "Behold, if Yahawah made windows in shamayam (heaven), could this thing be?" He said, "raah (see), you shall see it with your iyan (eyes), but shall not akal (eat) of it.
Now there were arabai (four) leprous men at the entrance of the gate. They said one to rai (another), "Why do we yashab (sit) here until we mawath (die)?

If we amar (say), ‘We will bawaa (enter) into the Iyar,' then the famine is in the Iyar, and we shall mawath (die) there. If we yashab (sit) still here, we also mawath (die). Now therefore yalak (come), and let us surrender to the machanah (army) of the Aram (Syrians). If they chayah (save) us alive, we will chayah (live); and if they mawath (kill) us, we will only mawath (die).

They rose up in the nashap (twilight), to bawaa (go) to the machanah (camp) of the Aram (Syrians). When they had bawaa (come) to the outermost part of the machanah (camp) of the Aram (Syrians), behold, there was no ayash (man) there.

For the Adanay had made the machanah (army) of the Aram (Syrians) to hear a qawal (noise) of chariots, and a qawal (noise) of horses, even the qawal (noise) of a gadawal (great) chayal (army): and they said one to ach (another), Behold, the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) has hired against us the malak (kings) of the Chathay (Hittites), and the malak (kings) of the Matzarayam (Egyptians), to bawaa (come) on us.
Therefore they qawam (arose) and fled in the nashap (twilight), and left their ahal (tents), and their horses, and their donkeys, even the machanah (camp) as it was, and fled for their napash (life).

When these lepers came to the outermost part of the machanah (camp), they went into one ahal (tent), and ate and drink, and carried there kasap (silver), and gold, and clothing, and went and hid it. Then they came shawab (turn back / repent), and entered into achar (another) ahal (tent), and carried there also, and went and hid it.

Then they said one to rai (another), "We aren't doing right. This yawam (day) is a yawam (day) of bashawarah (good) news, and we chashah (keep) silent. If we wait until the baqar (morning) awar (light), iwan (punishment) will overtake us. Now therefore matzaa (come), let us yalak (go) and nagad (tell) the malak (king's) bayath (household).

So they came and called to the porter of the Iyar; and they told them, saying, "We came to the machanah (camp) of the Aram (Syrians), and, behold, there was no ayash (man) there, neither qawal (voice) of adam (man), but the horses tied, and the donkeys tied, and the ahal (tents) as they were.
He called the porters; and they told it to the malak (king's) bayath (household) within.

The malak (king) qawam (arose) in the layal (night), and said to his ibad (servants), "I will now show you what the Aram (Syrians) have done to us. They yadai (know) that we are Raib. Therefore are they gone out of the machanah (camp) to hide themselves in the shadah (field), saying, ‘When they yatzaa (come) out of the Iyar, we shall take them chay (alive), and bawaa (get) into the Iyar.'

One of his ibad (servants) answered, "Please let some take chamash (five) of the horses that shaar (remain), which are shaar (left) in the city. Behold, they are like all the multitude of Yasharaal (Israel) who are shaar (left) in it. Behold, they are like all the multitude of Yasharaal (Israel) who are consumed. Let us shalach (send) and raah (see).
They took therefore shanayam (two) chariots with horses; and the malak (king) sent achar (after) the machanah (army) of the Aram (Syrians), saying, "yalak (go) and raah (see).

They went achar (after) them to the Yaradan; and behold, all the darak (way) was Malaa of bagad (garments) and vessels, which the Aram (Syrians) had cast away in their haste. The malaak (messengers) returned, and told the malak (king).

The im (people) went out, and plundered the machanah (camp) of the Aram (Syrians). So a measure of fine flour was sold for a shekel, and saah (two) measures of barley for a shekel, according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah.

The malak (king) appointed the shalayash (captain) on whose yad (hand) he leaned to be in charge of the gate: and the im (people) trod on him in the gate, and he died as the ayash (man) of Alahayam had said, who spoke when the malak (king) came down to him.

It happened, as the ayash (man) of Alahayam had spoken to the malak (king), saying, "saah (two) measures of barley for a shekel, and a measure of fine flour for a shekel, shall be tomorrow about this ith (time) in the gate of Shamarawan;

and that shalayash (captain) answered the ayash (man) of Alahayam, and said, "Now, behold, if Yahawah should ishah (make) windows in shamayam (heaven), might such a thing be?" and he said, "raah (see), you shall see it with your iyan (eyes), but shall not akal (eat) of it.
It happened like that to him; for the im (people) trod on him in the gate, and he died.

Now Alayashai had spoken to the ashah (woman), whose ban (son) he had restored to chayah (life), saying, "qawam (arise), and yalak (go), you and your bayath (household), and stay for a while wherever you can; for Yahawah has called for a famine. It shall also bawaa (come) on the aratz (land) shabai (seven) Shanah.

The ashah (woman) qawam (arose), and did according to the dabar (word) of the ayash (man) of Alahayam. She went with her bayath (household), and lived in the aratz (land) of the Palashathay (Philistines) shabai (seven) Shanah.

It happened at the shabai (seven) Shanah' end, that the ashah (woman) returned out of the aratz (land) of the Palashathay (Philistines). Then she went yatzaa (forth) to cry to the malak (king) for her bayath (house) and for her shadah (land).
Now the malak (king) was talking with Gayachazay the nair (servant) of the ayash (man) of Alahayam, saying, "Please tell me all the gadawal (great) things that Alayashai has done.

It happened, as he was telling the malak (king) how he had restored to chayah (life) him who was mawath (dead), that behold, the ashah (woman), whose ban (son) he had restored to chayah (life), cried to the malak (king) for her bayath (house) and for her shadah (land). Gayachazay said, "My Adawan, O malak (king), this is the ashah (woman), and this is her ban (son), whom Alayashai restored to chayah (life).

When the malak (king) asked the ashah (woman), she told him. So the malak (king) appointed to her a achad (certain) officer, saying, "shawab (turn back / repent) all that was hers, and all the fruits of the shadah (field) since the yawam (day) that she left the aratz (land), even until now.
Alayashai came to Damashaq; and Banahadad the malak (king) of Aram was chalah (sick). It was told him, saying, "The ayash (man) of Alahayam has bawaa (come) here.

The malak (king) said to Chazaal, "Take a manachah (present) in your yad (hand), and yalak (go), qaraah (meet) the ayash (man) of Alahayam, and inquire of Yahawah by him, saying, ‘Will I chayah (recover) from this sickness?'

So Chazaal went to qaraah (meet) him, and took a manachah (present) with him, even of every tawab (good) thing of Damashaq, arabaiyam (forty) camels' mashaa (burden), and came and stood panayam (before) him, and said, "Your ban (son) Banahadad malak (king) of Aram has sent me to you, saying, ‘Will I chayah (recover) from this sickness?'
Alayashai said to him, "yalak (go), amar (tell) him, ‘You shall chayah (surely) chayah (recover);' however Yahawah has shown me that he shall mawath (surely) mawath (die).
He settled his gaze steadfastly on him, until he was bawash (ashamed). Then the ayash (man) of Alahayam wept.

Chazaal said, "Why do you weep, my Adawan?" He answered, "Because I yadai (know) the rai (evil) that you will do to the children of Yasharaal (Israel). You will shalach (set) their strongholds on ash (fire), and you will harag (kill) their young men with the charab (sword), and will dash in pieces their little iwalal (ones), and rip up their women with harah (child).
Chazaal said, "But what is your ibad (servant), who is but a dog, that he should do this gadawal (great) thing?" Alayashai answered, "Yahawah has shown me that you will be malak (king) over Aram.
Then he departed from Alayashai, and came to his adawan (master), who said to him, "What did Alayashai amar (say) to you?" He answered, "He told me that you would chayah (surely) chayah (recover).
It happened on the next macharath (day), that he took a thick cloth, dipped it in mayam (water), and spread it on his panayam (face), so that he died. Then Chazaal reigned in his place.

In the chamash (fifth) Shanah of Yawaram the ban (son) of Achaab malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), Yahawashapat being malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) then, Yahawaram the ban (son) of Yahawashapat malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) began to malak (reign).
He was shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign). He reigned shamanah (eight) Shanah in Yarawashalam.

He walked in the darak (way) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel), as did the bayath (house) of Achaab; for he had the bath (daughter) of Achaab as ashah (wife). He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah.
However Yahawah would not shachath (destroy) Yahawadah (Judah), for Dawad his ibad (servant's) sake, as he promised him to nathan (give) to him a nayar (lamp) for his children yawam (always).
In his yawam (days) Adam revolted from under the yad (hand) of Yahawadah (Judah), and made a malak (king) over themselves.

Then Yawaram passed over to Tzaiyar, and all his chariots with him: and he rose up by layal (night), and struck the Adam (Edomites) who surrounded him, and the shar (captains) of the chariots; and the im (people) fled to their ahal (tents).
So Adam revolted from under the yad (hand) of Yahawadah (Judah) to this yawam (day). Then Labanah revolted at the same ith (time).
The yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yawaram, and all that he did, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)?
Yawaram slept with his abawath (fathers), and was buried with his abawath (fathers) in the Iyar of Dawad; and Achazayah his ban (son) reigned in his place.
In the twelfth Shanah of Yawaram the ban (son) of Achaab malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), Achazayah the ban (son) of Yahawaram malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) began to malak (reign).

isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) Shanah ban (old) was Achazayah when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned one Shanah in Yarawashalam. His am (mother's) sham (name) was Ithalayah the bath (daughter) of Imaray malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).

He walked in the darak (way) of the bayath (house) of Achaab, and did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, as did the bayath (house) of Achaab; for he was the son-in-law of the bayath (house) of Achaab.
He went with Yawaram the ban (son) of Achaab to war against Chazaal malak (king) of Aram at Ramathagalaid Gilead: and the Aramay (Syrians) wounded Yawaram.

malak (king) Yawaram returned to be healed in Yazaraial of the makah (wounds) which the Aramay (Syrians) had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Chazaal malak (king) of Aram. Achazayah the ban (son) of Yahawaram malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) went down to raah (see) Yawaram the ban (son) of Achaab in Yazaraial, because he was chalah (sick).

Alayashai the nabayaa (prophet) called one of the ban (sons) of the nabayaa (prophets), and said to him, "Put your belt on your waist, take this vial of shaman (oil) in your yad (hand), and yalak (go) to Ramathagalaid Gilead.

When you bawaa (come) there, find Yahawaa the ban (son) of Yahawashapat the ban (son) of Namashay, and bawaa (go) in, and make him qawam (arise) up from among his ach (brothers), and bawaa (carry) him to an inner room.

Then take the vial of shaman (oil), and pour it on his raash (head), and amar (say), ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "I have mashach (anointed) you malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel)."' Then pathach (open) the door, flee, and don't wait.
So the nair (young) man, even the nair (young) man the nabayaa (prophet), went to Ramathagalaid Gilead.

When he came, behold, the shar (captains) of the chayal (army) were sitting. Then he said, "I have a dabar (message) for you, shar (captain)." Yahawaa said, "To which of us all?" He said, "To you, O shar (captain).

He qawam (arose), and went into the bayath (house). Then he poured the shaman (oil) on his raash (head), and said to him, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘I have mashach (anointed) you malak (king) over the im (people) of Yahawah, even over Yasharaal (Israel).

You shall strike the bayath (house) of Achaab your adawan (master), that I may avenge the dam (blood) of my ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets), and the dam (blood) of all the ibad (servants) of Yahawah, at the yad (hand) of Ayazabal.

For the whole bayath (house) of Achaab shall abad (perish). I will karath (cut) off from Achaab everyone who urinates against a wall, both him who is itzar (shut) up and him who is left at large in Yasharaal (Israel).
I will nathan (make) the bayath (house) of Achaab like the bayath (house) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, and like the bayath (house) of Baishaa the ban (son) of Achayah.
The dogs will akal (eat) Ayazabal on the plot of ground of Yazaraial, and there shall be none to bury her.'" He opened the door, and fled.

Then Yahawaa came yatzaa (forth) to the ibad (servants) of his Adawan: and one said to him, "Is all shalawam (well)? Why did this mad fellow bawaa (come) to you?" He said to them, "You yadai (know) the ayash (man) and what his talk was.
They said, "That is a lie. nagad (tell) us now." He said, "He said to me, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, I have mashach (anointed) you malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel).'
Then they hurried, and took every ayash (man) his bagad (garment), and shawam (put) it under him on the top of the stairs, and blew the trumpet, saying, "Yahawaa is malak (king).

So Yahawaa the ban (son) of Yahawashapat the ban (son) of Namashay conspired against Yawaram. (Now Yawaram was keeping Ramathagalaid Gilead, he and all Yasharaal (Israel), panayam (because) of Chazaal malak (king) of Aram;

but malak (king) Yahawaram was returned to be healed in Yazaraial of the makah (wounds) which the Aramay (Syrians) had given him, when he fought with Chazaal malak (king) of Aram.) Yahawaa said, "If this is your thinking, then let no al (one) escape and yatzaa (go) out of the Iyar, to yalak (go) to nagad (tell) it in Yazaraial.
So Yahawaa rode in a chariot, and went to Yazaraial; for Yawaram shakab (lay) there. Achazayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) had yarad (come) down to raah (see) Yawaram.

Now the watchman was standing on the magadal (tower) in Yazaraial, and he spied the company of Yahawaa as he came, and said, "I raah (see) a company." Yahawaram said, "Take a rakab (horseman), and shalach (send) to qaraah (meet) them, and let him amar (say), ‘Is it shalawam (peace)?'

So there went rakab (one) on horseback to qaraah (meet) him, and said, "Thus amar (says) the malak (king), ‘Is it shalawam (peace)?'" Yahawaa said, "What do you have to do with shalawam (peace)? Fall in achar (behind) me!" The watchman said, "The malaak (messenger) came to them, but he isn't coming shawab (turn back / repent).

Then he sent out a shanay (second) on horseback, who came to them, and said, "Thus amar (says) the malak (king), ‘Is it shalawam (peace)?'" Yahawaa answered, "What do you have to do with shalawam (peace)? Fall in achar (behind) me!
The watchman said, "He came to them, and isn't coming shawab (turn back / repent). The driving is like the driving of Yahawaa the ban (son) of Namashay; for he drives furiously.

Yahawaram said, "Get ready!" They got his chariot ready. Yahawaram malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Achazayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) went out, ayash (each) in his chariot, and they went out to qaraah (meet) Yahawaa, and found him in the chalaqah (portion) of Nabawath the Yazaraialay.

It happened, when Yahawaram saw Yahawaa, that he said, "Is it shalawam (peace), Yahawaa?" He answered, "What shalawam (peace), so long as the prostitution of your am (mother) Ayazabal and her witchcraft rab (abound)?
Yahawaram turned his yad (hands), and fled, and said to Achazayah, "There is treason, Achazayah!
Yahawaa drew his qashath (bow) with his malaa (full) yad (strength), and struck Yahawaram between his zarawai (arms); and the arrow went out at his lab (heart), and he sunk down in his chariot.

Then Jehu said to Badaqar his shalayash (captain), "Pick him up, and throw him in the plot of the shadah (field) of Nabawath the Yazaraialay; for zakar (remember) how, when you and I rode tzamad (together) achar (after) Achaab his ab (father), Yahawah laid this mashaa (burden) on him:

‘raah (see) I have seen yesterday the dam (blood) of Nabawath, and the dam (blood) of his ban (sons),' says Yahawah; ‘and I will shalam (repay) you in this plot of ground,' says Yahawah. Now therefore nashaa (take) and cast him onto the plot of ground, according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah.

But when Achazayah the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) saw this, he fled by the darak (way) of the Gan bayath (house). Yahawaa followed achar (after) him, and said, "Strike him also in the chariot!" They struck him at the ascent of Gawar, which is by Yabalaim. He fled to Magadawan, and died there.
His ibad (servants) carried him in a chariot to Yarawashalam, and buried him in his tomb with his abawath (fathers) in the Iyar of Dawad.
In the ishar (eleventh) Shanah of Yawaram the ban (son) of Achaab began Achazayah to malak (reign) over Yahawadah (Judah).
When Yahawaa had bawaa (come) to Yazaraial, Ayazabal heard of it; and she painted her iyan (eyes), and attired her raash (head), and looked out at the window.
As Yahawaa entered in at the gate, she said, "Do you come in shalawam (peace), Zamaray, you harag (murderer) of your adawan (master)?
He lifted up his panayam (face) to the window, and said, "Who is on my side? Who?" shanayam (two) or shalawash (three) eunuchs looked out at him.
He said, "shamat (throw) her down!" So they threw her down; and some of her dam (blood) was sprinkled on the wall, and on the horses. Then he trampled her under ramas (foot).
When he had bawaa (come) in, he ate and drink; and he said, "paqad (see) now to this cursed qabar (woman), and bury her; for she is a malak (king's) bath (daughter).
They went to bury her; but they found no more of her am (than) the galagalath (skull), and the feet, and the kap (palms) of her yad (hands).

Therefore they came shawab (turn back / repent), and told him. He said, "This is the dabar (word) of Yahawah, which he spoke by his ibad (servant) Alayah the Thashabay, saying, ‘The dogs will akal (eat) the flesh of Ayazabal on the plot of Yazaraial,
and the nabalah (body) of Ayazabal shall be as dung on the panayam (face) of the shadah (field) in the chalaq (portion) of Yazaraial, so that they shall not amar (say), "This is Ayazabal."'

Now Achaab had shabaiyam (seventy) ban (sons) in Shamarawan. Yahawaa wrote letters, and sent to Shamarawan, to the shar (rulers) of Yazaraial, even the zaqan (elders), and to those who brought up the sons of Achaab, saying,
"Now as soon as this letter bawaa (comes) to you, since your adawan (master's) ban (sons) are with you, and there are with you chariots and horses, a fortified Iyar also, and armor.
Select the tawab (best) and fittest of your adawan (master's) ban (sons), shawam (set) him on his ab (father's) kasaa (throne), and fight for your adawan (master's) bayath (house).
But they were maad (exceedingly) yaraa (afraid), and said, "Behold, the shanayam (two) malak (kings) didn't imad (stand) panayam (before) him! How then shall we imad (stand)?

He who was over the bayath (household), and he who was over the Iyar, the zaqan (elders) also, and those who raised the children, sent to Yahawaa, saying, "We are your ibad (servants), and will do all that you ask us. We will not make any man malak (king). You do that which is tawab (good) in your iyan (eyes).

Then he wrote a letter the shanay (second) time to them, saying, "If you are on my side, and if you will listen to my qawal (voice), take the raash (heads) of the men your adawan (master's) ban (sons), and bawaa (come) to me to Yazaraial by tomorrow this ith (time)." Now the malak (king's) ban (sons), being shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (persons), were with the gadawal (great) men of the Iyar, who brought them up.

It happened, when the letter came to them, that they took the malak (king's) ban (sons), and killed them, even shabaiyam (seventy) ayash (persons), and shawam (put) their raash (heads) in baskets, and sent them to him to Yazaraial.

A malaak (messenger) came, and told him, "They have brought the raash (heads) of the malak (king's) ban (sons)." He said, "shawam (lay) them in shanayam (two) heaps at the entrance of the gate until the baqar (morning).

It happened in the baqar (morning), that he went out, and stood, and said to all the im (people), "You are tzadayaq (righteous). Behold, I conspired against my adawan (master), and killed him; but who struck all these?

yadai (know) now that nothing shall napal (fall) to the aratz (earth) of the dabar (word) of Yahawah, which Yahawah spoke concerning the bayath (house) of Achaab. For Yahawah has done that which he spoke by his ibad (servant) Alayah.

So Yahawaa struck all that remained of the bayath (house) of Achaab in Yazaraial, with all his gadawal (great) men, his yadai (familiar) friends, and his kahan (priests), until he shaar (left) him none sharayad (remaining).
He qawam (arose) and departed, and went to Shamarawan. As he was at the raih (shearing) bayath (house) of the shepherds on the darak (way),

Yahawaa met with the ach (brothers) of Achazayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and said, "Who are you?" They answered, "We are the ach (brothers) of Achazayah. We are yarad (going) down to greet the children of the malak (king) and the children of the gabayarah (queen).

He said, "Take them chay (alive)!" They took them chay (alive), and killed them at the bawar (pit) of the shearing bayathaiqad (house), even arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two) men. He didn't shaar (leave) any of them.

When he had departed from there, he met Yahawanadab the ban (son) of Rakab coming to qaraah (meet) him. He greeted him, and said to him, "Is your labab (heart) yashar (right), as my labab (heart) is with your labab (heart)?" Yahawanadab answered, "It is." "If it is, nathan (give) me your yad (hand)." He gave him his yad (hand); and he took him up to him into the chariot.
He said, "yalak (come) with me, and raah (see) my zeal for Yahawah." So they made him ride in his chariot.
When he came to Shamarawan, he struck all who remained to Achaab in Shamarawan, until he had destroyed him, according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah, which he spoke to Alayah.
Yahawaa gathered all the im (people) together, and said to them, "Achaab served Bail a Mait; but Yahawaa will ibad (serve) him much.

Now therefore qaraa (call) to me all the nabayaa (prophets) of Bail, all of his ibad (worshippers), and all of his kahan (priests). Let ayash (none) be absent; for I have a gadawal (great) zabach (sacrifice) to Bail. Whoever is absent, he shall not chayah (live)." But Yahawaa did it in subtlety, intending that he might abad (destroy) the ibad (worshippers) of Bail.
Yahawaa said, "qadash (sanctify) a solemn itzarah (assembly) for Bail!" They proclaimed it.

Yahawaa sent through all Yasharaal (Israel); and all the ibad (worshippers) of Bail came, so that there was not a ayash (man) shaar (left) that didn't bawaa (come). They came into the bayath (house) of Bail; and the bayath (house) of Bail was filled from one pah (end) to another.
He said to him who was over the vestry, "yatzaa (bring) out robes for all the ibad (worshippers) of Bail!" He brought robes out to them.

Yahawaa went with Yahawanadab the ban (son) of Rakab into the bayath (house) of Bail. Then he said to the ibad (worshippers) of Bail, "Search, and raah (see) that there are here with you none of the ibad (servants) of Yahawah, but the ibad (worshippers) of Bail only.

They went in to ishah (offer) zabach (sacrifices) and burnt ilah (offerings). Now Yahawaa had appointed him shamanayam (eighty) men outside, and said, "If any of the men whom I bawaa (bring) into your yad (hands) malat (escape), he who lets him go, his napash (life) shall be for the napash (life) of him.

It happened, as soon as he had made an kalah (end) of ilah (offering) the burnt offering, that Yahawaa said to the guard and to the shalayash (captains), "bawaa (go) in, and kill them! Let ayash (none) yatzaa (escape)." They struck them with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); and the guard and the shalayash (captains) cast them out, and went to the Iyar of the bayath (house) of Bail.
They brought out the matzabah (pillars) that were in the bayath (house) of Bail, and burned them.
They broke down the matzabah (pillar) of Bail, and broke down the bayath (house) of Bail, and made it a latrine, to this yawam (day).
Thus Yahawaa destroyed Bail out of Yasharaal (Israel).

However from the chataa (sins) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin), Yahawaa didn't sawar (depart) from achar (after) them, the golden calves that were in Bayathaal, and that were Dan Dan.

Yahawah said to Yahawaa, "Because you have done tawab (well) in executing that which is yashar (right) in my iyan (eyes), and have done to the bayath (house) of Achaab according to all that was in my labab (heart), your ban (sons) of the rabayaiy (fourth) generation shall yashab (sit) on the kasaa (throne) of Yasharaal (Israel).

But Yahawaa took no shamar (heed) to yalak (walk) in the thawarah (law) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), with all his labab (heart). He didn't sawar (depart) from the chataah (sins) of Yarabaim, with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).
In those yawam (days) Yahawah began to cut off from Yasharaal (Israel); and Chazaal struck them in all the borders of Yasharaal (Israel);

from the Yaradan eastward, all the aratz (land) of Galaid, the Gaday (Gadites), and the Raawabanay (Reubenites), and the Manashay (Manassites), from Irawair, which is by the nachal (valley) of the Aranawan, even Galaid and Bashan.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yahawaa, and all that he did, and all his might, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
Yahawaa slept with his abawath (fathers); and they buried him in Shamarawan. Yahawaachaz his ban (son) reigned in his place.
The yawam (time) that Yahawaa reigned over Yasharaal (Israel) in Shamarawan was isharayam (twenty) - shamanah (eight) Shanah.
Now when Ithalayah the am (mother) of Achazayah saw that her ban (son) was mawath (dead), she qawam (arose) and destroyed all the zarai (seed) mamalakah (royal).

But Yahawashabai, the bath (daughter) of malak (king) Yawaram, achawath (sister) of Achazayah, took Yawaash the ban (son) of Achazayah, and stole him away from among the malak (king's) ban (sons) who were slain, even him and his nurse, and put them in the bedroom; and they hid him from Ithalayah, so that he was not slain;
He was with her hidden in the bayath (house) of Yahawah shash (six) Shanah. Ithalayah reigned over the aratz (land).

In the shabayaiy (seventh) Shanah Yahawayadai sent and fetched the Karay over maah (hundreds) Karay the Carites and of the guard, and brought them to him into the bayath (house) of Yahawah; and he made a barayath (covenant) with them, and took an shabai (oath) of them in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and showed them the malak (king's) ban (son).

He tzawah (commanded) them, saying, "This is the thing that you shall do: a shalayashay (third) part of you, who bawaa (come) in on the shabath (sabbath), shall be keepers of the watch of the malak (king's) bayath (house);

A shalayashay (third) part shall be at the gate Sawar; and a shalayashay (third) part at the gate achar (behind) the guard. So you shall shamar (keep) the watch of the bayath (house), and be a barrier.
The shanayam (two) companies of you, even all who yatzaa (go) out on the shabath (sabbath), shall shamar (keep) the watch of the bayath (house) of Yahawah around the malak (king).

You shall surround the malak (king), every ayash (man) with his weapons in his yad (hand); and he who bawaa (comes) within the ranks, let him be slain. Be with the malak (king) when he goes out, and when he bawaa (comes) in.

The shar (captains) over maah (hundreds) did according to all that Yahawayadai the kahan (priest) tzawah (commanded); and they took every ayash (man) his men, those who were to bawaa (come) in on the shabath (sabbath), with those who were to yatzaa (go) out on the shabath (sabbath), and came to Yahawayadai the kahan (priest).
The kahan (priest) delivered to the shar (captains) over maah (hundreds) the spears and shalat (shields) that had been malak (king) Dawad, which were in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

The guard stood, every ayash (man) with his weapons in his yad (hand), from the Yamanay side of the bayath (house) to the Shamaalay side of the bayath (house), along by the mazabach (altar) and the bayath (house), around the malak (king).

Then he brought out the malak (king's) ban (son), and nathan (put) the nazar (crown) on him, and gave him the idawath (testimony); and they made him malak (king), and mashach (anointed) him; and they clapped their kap (hands), and said, "Long chayah (live) the malak (king)!
When Ithalayah heard the qawal (noise) of the guard and of the im (people), she came to the im (people) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah:

and she looked, and behold, the malak (king) stood by the pillar, as the tradition was, and the shar (captains) and the trumpets by the malak (king); and all the im (people) of the aratz (land) Shamach, and blew trumpets. Then Ithalayah tore her clothes, and cried, "Treason! Treason!

Yahawayadai the kahan (priest) tzawah (commanded) the shar (captains) of maah (hundreds) who were set over the chayal (army), and said to them, "yatzaa (bring) her out between the ranks. mawath (kill) him who bawaa (follows) her with the charab (sword)." For the kahan (priest) said, "Don't let her be slain in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
So they made way for her; and she went by the darak (way) of the horses' entry to the malak (king's) bayath (house). She was slain there.
Yahawayadai made a barayath (covenant) between Yahawah and the malak (king) and the im (people), that they should be yahawah (yahweh's) im (people); between the malak (king) also and the im (people).

All the im (people) of the aratz (land) went to the bayath (house) of Bail, and broke it down; his mazabach (altars) and his tzalam (images) broke they in shabar (pieces) yatab (thoroughly), and killed Mathan the kahan (priest) of Bail panayam (before) the mazabach (altars). The kahan (priest) appointed paqad (officers) over the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

He took the Karay over maah (hundreds), and the Karay, and the guard, and all the im (people) of the aratz (land); and they brought down the malak (king) from the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and came by the darak (way) of the gate of the guard to the malak (king's) bayath (house). He sat on the kasaa (throne) of the malak (kings).
So all the im (people) of the aratz (land) Shamach, and the Iyar was shaqat (quiet). Ithalayah they had slain with the charab (sword) at the malak (king's) bayath (house).
Yahawaash was shabai (seven) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign).
In the seventh Shanah of Yahawaa began Yahawaash to malak (reign); and he reigned arabaiyam (forty) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Tzabayah Baarashabai Beersheba.
Yahawaash did that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah all his yawam (days) in which Yahawayadai the kahan (priest) instructed him.
However the bamah (high) places were not taken sawar (away); the im (people) still sacrificed and burnt qatar (incense) in the bamah (high) places.

Yahawaash said to the kahan (priests), "All the kasap (money) of the qadash (holy) things that is brought into the bayath (house) of Yahawah, in ibar (current) kasap (money), the kasap (money) of the ayash (persons) for whom ayash (each) napash (man) is rated, and all the kasap (money) that it ilah (comes) into any ayash (man's) lab (heart) to bawaa (bring) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah,
let the kahan (priests) take it to them, every ayash (man) from his acquaintance; and they shall chazaq (repair) the breaches of the bayath (house), wherever any breach shall be found.
But it was so, that in the shalawash (three) and isharayam (twentieth) Shanah of malak (king) Yahawaash the kahan (priests) had not repaired the breaches of the bayath (house).

Then malak (king) Yahawaash called for Yahawayadai the kahan (priest), and for the other kahan (priests), and said to them, "Why don't you chazaq (repair) the breaches of the bayath (house)? Now therefore take no more kasap (money) from your treasurers, but nathan (deliver) it for the breaches of the bayath (house).
The kahan (priests) consented that they should take no more kasap (money) from the im (people), balathay (neither) chazaq (repair) the breaches of the bayath (house).

But Yahawayadai the kahan (priest) took a arawan (chest), and bored a hole in its lid, and nathan (set) it beside the mazabach (altar), on the yamayan (right) side as one bawaa (comes) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah: and the kahan (priests) who kept the threshold nathan (put) therein all the kasap (money) that was brought into the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

It was so, when they saw that there was much kasap (money) in the arawan (chest), that the malak (king's) scribe and the gadawal (high) kahan (priest) came up, and they tzawar (put) up in bags and counted the kasap (money) that was found in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

They gave the kasap (money) that was weighed out into the yad (hands) of those who did the malaakah (work), who had the paqad (oversight) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah: and they paid it out to the carpenters and the banah (builders), who worked on the bayath (house) of Yahawah,

and to the masons and the aban (stone) cutters, and for buying itz (timber) and cut aban (stone) to chazaq (repair) the breaches of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and for all that was laid out for the bayath (house) to repair it.

But there were not made for the bayath (house) of Yahawah cups of kasap (silver), snuffers, basins, trumpets, any vessels of gold, or vessels of kasap (silver), of the kasap (money) that was brought into the bayath (house) of Yahawah;
for they gave that to those who did the malaakah (work), and repaired therewith the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
Moreover they didn't demand an accounting from the men into whose yad (hand) they delivered the kasap (money) to nathan (give) to those who did the malaakah (work); for they dealt faithfully.
The kasap (money) for the asham (trespass) offerings, and the kasap (money) for the chataah (sin) offerings, was not brought into the bayath (house) of Yahawah: it was the kahan (priests)'.
Then Chazaal malak (king) of Aram went up, and fought against gath (gath), and took it; and Chazaal shawam (set) his panayam (face) to ilah (go) up to Yarawashalam.

Yahawaash malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) took all the qadash (holy) things that Yahawashapat and Yahawaram and Achazayah, his abawath (fathers), malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), had dedicated, and his own qadash (holy) things, and all the gold that was found in the treasures of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and of the malak (king's) bayath (house), and sent it to Chazaal malak (king) of Aram: and he went ilah (away) from Yarawashalam.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yawaash, and all that he did, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)?
His ibad (servants) qawam (arose), and made a conspiracy, and struck Yawaash at the bayath (house) of Malawaa, on the way that goes down to Salaa.

Yawazakar Jozacar the ban (son) Shamaith Shimeath, and Yahawazabad the ban (son) of Shawamar, his ibad (servants), struck him, and he died; and they buried him with his abawath (fathers) in the Iyar of Dawad: and Amatzayah his ban (son) reigned in his place.

In the shalawash (three) and isharayam (twentieth) Shanah of Yawaash the ban (son) of Achazayah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Yahawaachaz the ban (son) of Yahawaa began to malak (reign) over Yasharaal (Israel) in Shamarawan for seventeen Shanah.

He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, and followed the chataah (sins) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin); he didn't sawar (depart) from it.

The ap (anger) of Yahawah was kindled against Yasharaal (Israel), and he delivered them into the yad (hand) of Chazaal malak (king) of Aram, and into the yad (hand) of Banahadad the ban (son) of Chazaal, yawam (continually).
Yahawaachaz begged Yahawah, and Yahawah listened to him; for he saw the oppression of Yasharaal (Israel), how that the malak (king) of Aram oppressed them.

(Yahawah gave Yasharaal (Israel) a savior, so that they went out from under the yad (hand) of the Aram (Syrians); and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) lived in their ahal (tents) as shalashawam (before).

Nevertheless they didn't sawar (depart) from the chataah (sins) of the bayath (house) of Yarabaim, with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin), but walked therein: and there remained the Asharah also in Shamarawan.)

For he didn't shaar (leave) to Yahawaachaz of the im (people) any more than chamashayam (fifty) horsemen, and ishar (ten) chariots, and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) footmen; for the malak (king) of Aram destroyed them, and made them like the ipar (dust) in threshing.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yahawaachaz, and all that he did, and his might, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
Yahawaachaz slept with his abawath (fathers); and they buried him in Shamarawan: and Yawaash his ban (son) reigned in his place.

In the shalawashayam (thirty) - seventh Shanah of Yawaash malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Yahawaash the ban (son) of Yahawaachaz began to malak (reign) over Yasharaal (Israel) in Shamarawan for sixteen Shanah.

He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah; he didn't sawar (depart) from all the chataah (sins) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin); but he walked therein.

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yawaash, and all that he did, and his might with which he fought against Amatzayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
Yawaash slept with his abawath (fathers); and Yarabaim sat on his kasaa (throne): and Yawaash was buried in Shamarawan with the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Now Alayashai was fallen chalah (sick) of his sickness of which he died: and Yawaash the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) came down to him, and wept over him, and said, "My ab (father), my ab (father), the chariots of Yasharaal (Israel) and its horsemen!
Alayashai said to him, "Take qashath (bow) and chatz (arrows);" and he took to him qashath (bow) and chatz (arrows).
He said to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), "Put your yad (hand) on the qashath (bow);" and he put his yad (hand) on it. Alayashai laid his yad (hands) on the malak (king's) yad (hands).

He said, "pathach (open) the window eastward;" and he opened it. Then Alayashai said, "Shoot!" and he shot. He said, "yahawah (yahweh's) chatz (arrow) of thashawaih (victory), even the chatz (arrow) of thashawaih (victory) over Aram; for you shall strike the Aram (Syrians) in Apaq, until you have consumed them.
He said, "Take the chatz (arrows);" and he took them. He said to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), "Strike the aratz (ground);" and he struck shalawash (three) times, and stopped.

The ayash (man) of Alahayam was qatzap (angry) with him, and said, "You should have struck chamash (five) or shash (six) paim (times). Then you would have struck Aram until you had consumed it, whereas now you shall strike Aram just shalawash (three) times.
Alayashai died, and they buried him. Now the gadawad (bands) Mawaab the Moabites invaded the aratz (land) at the coming in of the Shanah.

It happened, as they were burying a ayash (man), that raah (see), they spied a gadawad (band); and they cast the ayash (man) into the tomb of Alayashai: and as soon as the ayash (man) touched the itzam (bones) of Alayashai, he revived, and stood up on his feet.
Chazaal malak (king) of Aram oppressed Yasharaal (Israel) all the yawam (days) of Yahawaachaz.

But Yahawah was gracious to them, and had racham (compassion) on them, and had panah (respect) to them, because of his barayath (covenant) with Abaraham, Yatzachaq, and Yaiqab, and would not shachath (destroy) them, neither cast he them from his panayam (presence) as yet.
Chazaal malak (king) of Aram died; and Banahadad his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Yahawaash the ban (son) of Yahawaachaz took again out of the yad (hand) of Banahadad the ban (son) of Chazaal the Iyar which he had taken out of the yad (hand) of Yahawaachaz his ab (father) by war. Yawaash struck him shalawash (three) paim (times), and recovered the Iyar of Yasharaal (Israel).
In the shanayam (second) Shanah of Yawaash ban (son) of Yawaachaz malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) began Amatzayah the ban (son) of Yawaash malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) to malak (reign).
He was twenty-five Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned twenty-nine Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Yahawaidayan of Yarawashalam.
He did that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, yet not like Dawad his ab (father): he did according to all that Yawaash his ab (father) had done.
However the bamah (high) places were not taken sawar (away): the im (people) still sacrificed and burnt qatar (incense) in the bamah (high) places.
It happened, as soon as the mamalakah (kingdom) was chazaq (established) in his yad (hand), that he killed his ibad (servants) who had slain the malak (king) his ab (father):

but the children of the murderers he didn't put to mawath (death); according to that which is written in the book of the thawarah (law) of Mashah, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded), saying, "The abawath (fathers) shall not be put to mawath (death) for the children, nor the children be put to mawath (death) for the abawath (fathers); but every ayash (man) shall mawath (die) for his own chataa (sin).
He killed of Adam in the Gayaa of Malach ishar (ten) alap (thousand), and took salai (sela) by war, and called its sham (name) Yaqathaal, to this yawam (day).

Then Amatzayah sent malaak (messengers) to Yahawaash, the ban (son) of Yahawaachaz ban (son) of Yahawaa, malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "yalak (come), let us raah (see) one another in the panayam (face).

Yahawaash the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) sent to Amatzayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), saying, "The thistle that was in Labanawan sent to the cedar that was in Labanawan, saying, ‘nathan (give) your bath (daughter) to my ban (son) as ashah (wife). Then a shadah (wild) animal that was in Labanawan passed by, and trampled down the thistle.

You have indeed struck Adam, and your lab (heart) has lifted you up. Enjoy the glory of it, and stay at bayath (home); for why should you meddle to your rai (harm), that you should napal (fall), even you, and Yahawadah (Judah) with you?'

But Amatzayah would not listen. So Yahawaash malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) went up; and he and Amatzayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) looked one another in the panayam (face) at Bayathashamash Shemesh, which belongs to Yahawadah (Judah).
Yahawadah (Judah) was defeated by Yasharaal (Israel); and they fled every ayash (man) to his ahal (tent).

Yahawaash malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) took Amatzayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), the ban (son) of Yahawaash the ban (son) of Achazayah, at Bayathashamash Shemesh, and came to Yarawashalam, and broke down the wall of Yarawashalam from the gate of Aparayam to the corner gate, arabai (four) maah (hundred) amah (cubits).

He took all the gold and kasap (silver), and all the vessels that were found in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and in the treasures of the malak (king's) bayath (house), the hostages also, and returned to Shamarawan.

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yahawaash which he did, and his might, and how he fought with Amatzayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
Yahawaash slept with his abawath (fathers), and was buried in Shamarawan with the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel); and Yarabaim his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Amatzayah the ban (son) of Yawaash malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) lived achar (after) the mawath (death) of Yahawaash ban (son) of Yahawaachaz malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) chamash (fifteen) Shanah.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Amatzayah, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)?
They made a conspiracy against him in Yarawashalam; and he fled to Lakayash: but they sent achar (after) him to Lakayash, and killed him there.
They brought him on horses; and he was buried at Yarawashalam with his abawath (fathers) in the Iyar of Dawad.
All the im (people) of Yahawadah (Judah) took Izarayah, who was sixteen Shanah ban (old), and made him malak (king) in the place of his ab (father) Amatzayah.
He built Ayalawath, and restored it to Yahawadah (Judah), achar (after) that the malak (king) slept with his abawath (fathers).

In the fifteenth Shanah of Amatzayah the ban (son) of Yawaash malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Yarabaim the ban (son) of Yawaash malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) began to malak (reign) in Shamarawan for arabaiyam (forty) - one Shanah.

He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah: he didn't sawar (depart) from all the chataah (sins) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).

He restored the border of Yasharaal (Israel) from the entrance of Chamath to the yam (sea) of the irabah (arabah), according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), which he spoke by his ibad (servant) Yawanah the ban (son) of Amathay, the nabayaa (prophet), who was of Gathahachapar Hepher.
For Yahawah saw the affliction of Yasharaal (Israel), that it was very bitter; for there was apas (none) itzar (shut) up nor left at large, neither was there any helper for Yasharaal (Israel).
Yahawah didn't dabar (say) that he would machah (blot) out the sham (name) of Yasharaal (Israel) from under the sky; but he saved them by the yad (hand) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Yawaash.

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yarabaim, and all that he did, and his might, how he warred, and how he recovered Damashaq, and Chamath, which had belonged to Yahawadah (Judah), for Yasharaal (Israel), aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
Yarabaim slept with his abawath (fathers), even with the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel); and Zakarayah his ban (son) reigned in his place.
In the twenty - seventh Shanah of Yarabaim malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) began Izarayah ban (son) of Amatzayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) to malak (reign).

Sixteen Shanah ban (old) was he when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned chamashayam (fifty) - shanayam (two) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Yakalayah of Yarawashalam.
He did that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, according to all that his ab (father) Amatzayah had done.
However the bamah (high) places were not taken sawar (away): the im (people) still sacrificed and burnt qatar (incense) in the bamah (high) places.

Yahawah struck the malak (king), so that he was a leper to the yawam (day) of his mawath (death), and lived in a separate bayath (house). Yawatham the malak (king's) ban (son) was over the bayath (household), judging the im (people) of the aratz (land).
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Izarayah, and all that he did, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)?
Izarayah slept with his abawath (fathers); and they buried him with his abawath (fathers) in the Iyar of Dawad: and Yawatham his ban (son) reigned in his place.

In the shalawashayam (thirty) - shamanah (eighth) Shanah of Izarayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Zakarayah the ban (son) of Yarabaim reigned over Yasharaal (Israel) in Shamarawan shash (six) chadash (months).

He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, as his abawath (fathers) had done: he didn't sawar (depart) from the chataah (sins) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).
Shalawam the ban (son) Yabash Jabesh conspired against him, and struck him before the im (people), and killed him, and reigned in his place.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Zakarayah, behold, they are written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel).

This was the dabar (word) of Yahawah which he spoke to Yahawaa, saying, "Your ban (sons) to the rabayaiy (fourth) generation shall yashab (sit) on the kasaa (throne) of Yasharaal (Israel)." So it came to pass.

Shalawam the ban (son) Yabash Jabesh began to malak (reign) in the shalawashayam (thirty) - ninth Shanah of Izayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah); and he reigned for a yarach (month) in Shamarawan.
Manacham the ban (son) of Gaday went up from Tharatzah, and came to Shamarawan, and struck Shalawam the ban (son) Yabash Jabesh in Shamarawan, and killed him, and reigned in his place.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Shalawam, and his conspiracy which he made, behold, they are written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Then Manacham struck Thapasach, and all who were therein, and its borders, from Tharatzah: because they didn't pathach (open) to him, therefore he struck it; and all the women therein who were with harah (child) he ripped up.

In the shalawashayam (thirty) ninth Shanah of Izarayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Manacham the ban (son) of Gaday began to malak (reign) over Yasharaal (Israel) for ishar (ten) Shanah in Shamarawan.

He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah: he didn't sawar (depart) all his yawam (days) from the chataah (sins) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).

There came against the aratz (land) Pawal the malak (king) of Ashawar; and Manacham gave Pawal one alap (thousand) talents of kasap (silver), that his yad (hand) might be with him to chazaq (confirm) the mamalakah (kingdom) in his yad (hand).

Manacham exacted the kasap (money) of Yasharaal (Israel), even of all the gabawar (mighty) men of wealth, of achad (each) ayash (man) chamashayam (fifty) shekels of kasap (silver), to nathan (give) to the malak (king) of Ashawar. So the malak (king) of Ashawar turned shawab (turn back / repent), and didn't imad (stay) there in the aratz (land).
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Manacham, and all that he did, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
Manacham slept with his abawath (fathers); and Paqachayah his ban (son) reigned in his place.
In the fiftieth Shanah of Izarayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) Paqachayah the ban (son) of Manacham began to malak (reign) over Yasharaal (Israel) in Shamarawan for two Shanah.

He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah: he didn't sawar (depart) from the chataah (sins) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).

Paqach the ban (son) of Ramalayahaw, his shalayash (captain), conspired against him, and struck him in Shamarawan, in the castle of the malak (king's) bayath (house), with Aragab and Arayah; and with him were chamashayam (fifty) men of the Gileadites: and he killed him, and reigned in his place.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Paqachayah, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel).

In the chamashayam (fifty)- shanayam (second) Shanah of Izarayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) Paqach the ban (son) of Ramalayahaw began to malak (reign) over Yasharaal (Israel) in Shamarawan for isharayam (twenty) Shanah.

He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah: he didn't sawar (depart) from the chataah (sins) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, with which he made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin).

In the yawam (days) of Paqach malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) came Thagalathapalaasar Pileser malak (king) of Ashawar, and took Iyawan, and Abalabayathamaikah Beth Maacah, and Yanawach, and Qadash, and Chatzawar, and Galaid, and Galayal, all the aratz (land) of Napathalay; and he carried them galah (captive) to Ashawar.

Hawashai the ban (son) of Alah made a conspiracy against Paqach the ban (son) of Ramalayahaw, and struck him, and killed him, and reigned in his place, in the isharayam (twentieth) Shanah of Yawatham the ban (son) of Izayah.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Paqach, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel).
In the shanayam (second) Shanah of Paqach the ban (son) of Ramalayahaw malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) began Yawatham the ban (son) of Izayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) to malak (reign).

He was isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned sixteen Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Yarawashaa the bath (daughter) of Tzadawaq.
He did that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah; he did according to all that his ab (father) Izayah had done.

However the bamah (high) places were not taken sawar (away): the im (people) still sacrificed and burned qatar (incense) in the bamah (high) places. He built the Ilayawan gate of the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yawatham, and all that he did, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)?
In those yawam (days) Yahawah began to shalach (send) against Yahawadah (Judah) Ratzayan the malak (king) of Aram, and Paqach the ban (son) of Ramalayahaw.
Yawatham slept with his abawath (fathers), and was buried with his abawath (fathers) in the Iyar of Dawad his ab (father): and Achaz his ban (son) reigned in his place.
In the seventeenth Shanah of Paqach the ban (son) of Ramalayahaw Achaz the ban (son) of Yawatham malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) began to malak (reign).

isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) was Achaz when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned sixteen Shanah in Yarawashalam: and he didn't do that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah his Alahayam, like Dawad his ab (father).

But he walked in the darak (way) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel), yes, and made his ban (son) to ibar (pass) through the ash (fire), according to the thawaibah (abominations) of the gawayam (nations), whom Yahawah yarash (cast) out from panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
He sacrificed and burnt qatar (incense) in the bamah (high) places, and on the Gabaih, and under every Rainan itz (tree).
Then Ratzayan malak (king) of Aram and Paqach ban (son) of Ramalayahaw malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) came up to Yarawashalam to war: and they besieged Achaz, but could not overcome him.

At that ith (time) Ratzayan malak (king) of Aram recovered Ayalawath to Aram, and drove the Yahawaday (Jews) from Ayalawath; and the Arawamay (Syrians) came to Ayalawath, and lived there, to this yawam (day).

So Achaz sent malaak (messengers) to Thagalathapalaasar Pileser malak (king) of Ashawar, saying, "I am your ibad (servant) and your ban (son). ilah (come) up, and yashai (save) me out of the kap (hand) of the malak (king) of Aram, and out of the kap (hand) of the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), who qawam (rise) up against me.

Achaz took the kasap (silver) and gold that was found in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and in the treasures of the malak (king's) bayath (house), and sent it for a shachad (present) to the malak (king) of Ashawar.
The malak (king) of Ashawar listened to him; and the malak (king) of Ashawar went up against Damashaq, and took it, and carried its people galah (captive) to Qayar, and killed Ratzayan.

malak (king) Achaz went to Damashaq to qaraah (meet) Thagalathapalaasar Pileser malak (king) of Ashawar, and saw the mazabach (altar) that was at Damashaq; and malak (king) Achaz sent to Awarayah the kahan (priest) the damawath (fashion) of the mazabach (altar), and its thabanayath (pattern), according to all its workmanship.

Awarayah the kahan (priest) built an mazabach (altar): according to all that malak (king) Achaz had sent from Damashaq, so Awarayah the kahan (priest) made it for the coming of malak (king) Achaz from Damashaq.
When the malak (king) had bawaa (come) from Damashaq, the malak (king) saw the mazabach (altar): and the malak (king) drew qarab (near) to the mazabach (altar), and offered on it.
He burnt his burnt ilah (offering) and his meal manachah (offering), and poured his drink nasak (offering), and sprinkled the dam (blood) of his shalam (peace) offerings, on the mazabach (altar).

The bronze mazabach (altar), which was panayam (before) Yahawah, he brought from the panayam (forefront) of the bayath (house), from between his mazabach (altar) and the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and nathan (put) it on the tzapawan (north) side of his mazabach (altar).
