malak (king) Achaz tzawah (commanded) Awarayah the kahan (priest), saying, "On the gadawal (great) mazabach (altar) qatar (burn) the baqar (morning) burnt ilah (offering), and the evening meal manachah (offering), and the malak (king's) burnt ilah (offering), and his meal manachah (offering), with the burnt ilah (offering) of all the im (people) of the aratz (land), and their meal manachah (offering), and their drink nasak (offerings); and sprinkle on it all the dam (blood) of the burnt ilah (offering), and all the dam (blood) of the zabach (sacrifice); but the bronze mazabach (altar) shall be for me to inquire by.
Awarayah the kahan (priest) did so, according to all that malak (king) Achaz tzawah (commanded).

malak (king) Achaz cut off the panels of the bases, and removed the basin from off them, and took down the yam (sea) from off the bronze oxen that were under it, and nathan (put) it on a pavement of aban (stone).

The covered way for the shabath (sabbath) that they had built in the bayath (house), and the malak (king's) entry Chayatzawan, turned he to the bayath (house) of Yahawah, panayam (because) of the malak (king) of Ashawar.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Achaz which he did, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)?
Achaz slept with his abawath (fathers), and was buried with his abawath (fathers) in the Iyar of Dawad: and Chazaqayah his ban (son) reigned in his place.
In the shanayam (twelfth) Shanah of Achaz malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), Hawashai the ban (son) of Alah began to malak (reign) in Shamarawan over Yasharaal (Israel) for thashai (nine) Shanah.
He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, yet not as the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel) who were panayam (before) him.
Against him came up Shalamanaasar malak (king) of Ashawar; and Hawashai became his ibad (servant), and brought him tribute.

The malak (king) of Ashawar found conspiracy in Hawashai; for he had sent malaak (messengers) Sawaa So malak (king) of Matzarayam, and offered no tribute to the malak (king) of Ashawar, as he had done Shanah by Shanah: therefore the malak (king) of Ashawar itzar (shut) him up, and bound him in bayath (prison).
Then the malak (king) of Ashawar came up throughout all the aratz (land), and went up to Shamarawan, and besieged it shalawash (three) Shanah.

In the thashayaiy (ninth) Shanah of Hawashai the malak (king) of Ashawar took Shamarawan, and carried Yasharaal (Israel) away to Ashawar, and placed them in Chalach, and on the Chabawar, the nahar (river) of Gawazan, and in the Iyar of the Maday.

It was so, because the children of Yasharaal (Israel) had sinned against Yahawah their Alahayam, who brought them up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam from under the yad (hand) of Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam, and had feared other Alahayam,

and walked in the chaqah (statutes) of the gawayam (nations), whom Yahawah yarash (cast) out from panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel), which they made.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) did secretly things that were not right against Yahawah their Alahayam: and they built them bamah (high) places in all their Iyar, from the magadal (tower) of the watchmen to the fortified Iyar;
and they natzab (set) them up matzabah (pillars) and Asharah on every Gabah Gabaih, and under every Rainan itz (tree);

and there they burnt qatar (incense) in all the bamah (high) places, as did the gawayam (nations) whom Yahawah carried away panayam (before) them; and they worked rai (wicked) things to provoke Yahawah to kais (anger);
and they served idols, of which Yahawah had said to them, "You shall not do this thing.

Yet Yahawah testified to Yasharaal (Israel), and to Yahawadah (Judah), by every nabayaa (prophet), and every chazah (seer), saying, "shawab (turn back / repent) from your rai (evil) darak (ways), and shamar (keep) my matzawah (commandments) and my chaqah (statutes), according to all the thawarah (law) which I tzawah (commanded) your abawath (fathers), and which I sent to you by my ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets).
Notwithstanding, they would not listen, but hardened their neck, like the neck of their abawath (fathers), who didn't aman (believe) in Yahawah their Alahayam.

They rejected his chaq (statutes), and his barayath (covenant) that he made with their abawath (fathers), and his idawath (testimonies) which he testified to them; and they followed vanity, and became vain, and followed the gawayam (nations) that were around them, concerning whom Yahawah had tzawah (commanded) them that they should not do like them.

They forsook all the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah their Alahayam, and made them molten masakah (images), even shanayam (two) calves, and made an Asharah, and worshiped all the tzabaa (army) of the sky, and served Bail.

They caused their ban (sons) and their bath (daughters) to ibar (pass) through the ash (fire), and used divination and enchantments, and sold themselves to do that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, to provoke him to kais (anger).
Therefore Yahawah was very angry with Yasharaal (Israel), and removed them out of his panayam (sight): there was none shaar (left) but the shabat (tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah) only.
Also Yahawadah (Judah) didn't shamar (keep) the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah their Alahayam, but walked in the chaqah (statutes) of Yasharaal (Israel) which they made.
Yahawah rejected all the zarai (seed) of Yasharaal (Israel), and afflicted them, and delivered them into the yad (hand) of spoilers, until he had cast them out of his panayam (sight).

For he tore Yasharaal (Israel) from the bayath (house) of Dawad; and they made Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat malak (king): and Yarabaim drove Yasharaal (Israel) from following Yahawah, and made them chataa (sin) a gadawal (great) chataah (sin).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) walked in all the chataah (sins) of Yarabaim which he did; they didn't sawar (depart) from them;

until Yahawah removed Yasharaal (Israel) out of his panayam (sight), as he spoke by all his ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets). So Yasharaal (Israel) was carried away out of their own adamah (land) to Ashawar to this yawam (day).

The malak (king) of Ashawar brought men from Babal, and Kawath Cuthah, and Iwah Avva, and from Chamath and Saparawayam, and placed them in the Iyar of Shamarawan instead of the children of Yasharaal (Israel); and they possessed Shamarawan, and lived in the Iyar of it.
So it was, at the thachalah (beginning) of their yashab (dwelling) there, that they didn't yaraa (fear) Yahawah: therefore Yahawah sent aray (lions) among them, which killed some of them.

Therefore they spoke to the malak (king) of Ashawar, saying, "The gawayam (nations) which you have carried away, and placed in the Iyar of Shamarawan, don't yadai (know) the mashapat (law) of the Alahayam of the aratz (land). Therefore he has sent aray (lions) among them, and behold, they mawath (kill) them, because they don't yadai (know) the mashapat (law) of the Alahayam of the aratz (land).

Then the malak (king) of Ashawar tzawah (commanded), saying, "yalak (carry) there one of the kahan (priests) whom you brought from there; and let them yalak (go) and yashab (dwell) there, and let him teach them the mashapat (law) of the Alahayam of the aratz (land).
So one of the kahan (priests) whom they had carried away from Shamarawan came and lived in Bayathaal, and taught them how they should yaraa (fear) Yahawah.

However every gaway (nation) made Alahayam of their own, and yanach (put) them in the bayath (houses) of the bamah (high) places which the Shamaranay (Samaritans) had made, every gaway (nation) in their Iyar in which they lived.
The men of Babal made Sakawathabanawath Benoth, and the men of Kawath made Naragal, and the men of Chamath made Ashayamaa,
and the Iway made Nabachaz and Tharathaq; and the Saparaway burnt their children in the ash (fire) to Adaramalak and Inamalak, the Alahayam of Saparawayam.
So they feared Yahawah, and made to them from among themselves kahan (priests) of the bamah (high) places, who sacrificed for them in the bayath (houses) of the bamah (high) places.
They feared Yahawah, and served their own Alahayam, after the ways of the gawayam (nations) from among whom they had been carried away.

To this yawam (day) they do what they did raashawan (before): they don't yaraa (fear) Yahawah, neither do they follow their chaqah (statutes), or their mashapat (ordinances), or the thawarah (law) or the matzawah (commandment) which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) the children of Yaiqab, whom he named Yasharaal (Israel);

with whom Yahawah had made a barayath (covenant), and tzawah (commanded) them, saying, "You shall not yaraa (fear) other Alahayam, nor shachah (bow) yourselves to them, nor ibad (serve) them, nor zabach (sacrifice) to them;

but you shall yaraa (fear) Yahawah, who brought you up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam with gadawal (great) kach (power) and with an natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm), and you shall shachah (bow) yourselves to him, and you shall zabach (sacrifice) to him.

The chaq (statutes) and the mashapat (ordinances), and the thawarah (law) and the matzawah (commandment), which he wrote for you, you shall shamar (observe) to do forevermore. You shall not yaraa (fear) other Alahayam.
You shall not forget the barayath (covenant) that I have made with you; neither shall you yaraa (fear) other Alahayam.
But you shall yaraa (fear) Yahawah your Alahayam; and he will natzal (deliver) you out of the yad (hand) of all your ayab (enemies).
However they did not listen, but they did what they did raashawan (before).

So these gawayam (nations) feared Yahawah, and served their engraved pasayal (images). Their children likewise, and their children's children, as their abawath (fathers) did, so they do to this yawam (day).

Now it happened in the shalawash (third) Shanah of Hawashai ban (son) of Alah malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), that Chazaqayah the ban (son) of Achaz malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) began to malak (reign).

He was isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned isharayam (twenty) - thashai (nine) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Abay the bath (daughter) of Zakarayah.
He did that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, according to all that Dawad his ab (father) had done.

He removed the bamah (high) places, and broke the matzabah (pillars), and karath (cut) down the Asharah: and he broke in kathath (pieces) the bronze serpent that Mashah had made; for in those yawam (days) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) burned qatar (incense) to it; and he called it Nachashathan.
He trusted in Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel); so that achar (after) him was none like him among all the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), nor among them that were panayam (before) him.
For he joined with Yahawah; he didn't sawar (depart) from following him, but kept his matzawah (commandments), which Yahawah tzawah (commanded) Mashah.
Yahawah was with him; wherever he went yatzaa (forth) he prospered: and he rebelled against the malak (king) of Ashawar, and didn't ibad (serve) him.
He struck the Palashathay (Philistines) to Izah and its borders, from the magadal (tower) of the watchmen to the fortified Iyar.

It happened in the rabayaiy (fourth) Shanah of malak (king) Chazaqayah, which was the shabayaiy (seventh) Shanah of Hawashai ban (son) of Alah malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), that Shalamanaasar malak (king) of Ashawar came up against Shamarawan, and besieged it.
At the end of shalawash (three) Shanah they took it: in the shash (sixth) Shanah of Chazaqayah, which was the ninth Shanah of Hawashai malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), Shamarawan was taken.
The malak (king) of Ashawar carried Yasharaal (Israel) away to Ashawar, and put them in Chalach, and on the Chabawar, the nahar (river) of Gawazan, and in the Iyar of the Maday,

because they didn't obey the qawal (voice) of Yahawah their Alahayam, but transgressed his barayath (covenant), even all that Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah tzawah (commanded), and would not hear it, nor do it.
Now in the fourteenth Shanah of malak (king) Chazaqayah, Sanacharayab malak (king) of Ashawar came up against all the fortified Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and took them.

Chazaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) sent to the malak (king) of Ashawar to Lakayash, saying, "I have offended; shawab (turn back / repent) from me. That which you nathan (put) on me, I will nashaa (bear)." The malak (king) of Ashawar appointed to Chazaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) shalawash (three) maah (hundred) talents of kasap (silver) and shalawashayam (thirty) talents of gold.
Chazaqayah gave him all the kasap (silver) that was found in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and in the treasures of the malak (king's) bayath (house).

At that ith (time), Chazaqayah cut off the gold from the doors of the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, and from the pillars which Chazaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) had overlaid, and gave it to the malak (king) of Ashawar.

The malak (king) of Ashawar sent Tharathan and Rabsaris and Rabashaqah from Lakayash to malak (king) Chazaqayah with a Kabad chayal (army) to Yarawashalam. They went up and came to Yarawashalam. When they had ilah (come) up, they came and stood by the thailah (conduit) of the Ilayawan pool, which is in the masalah (highway) of the fuller's shadah (field).

When they had called to the malak (king), there came out to them Alayaqayam the ban (son) Chalaqayah Hilkiah, who was over the bayath (household), and Shabanaa the scribe, and Yawaach the ban (son) of Asap the zakar (recorder).
Rabashaqah said to them, "amar (say) now to Chazaqayah, ‘Thus amar (says) the gadawal (great) malak (king), the malak (king) of Ashawar, "What confidence is this in which you batach (trust)?
You amar (say) (but they are but vain dabar (words)), ‘There is itzah (counsel) and gabawarah (strength) for war.' Now on whom do you batach (trust), that you have rebelled against me?

Now, behold, you batach (trust) in the mashainah (staff) of this bruised reed, even in Matzarayam. If a ayash (man) samak (leans) on it, it will bawaa (go) into his kap (hand), and naqab (pierce) it. So is Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam to all who batach (trust) on him.

But if you amar (tell) me, ‘We batach (trust) in Yahawah our Alahayam;' isn't that he whose bamah (high) places and whose mazabach (altars) Chazaqayah has taken sawar (away), and has said to Yahawadah (Judah) and to Yarawashalam, ‘You shall shachah (worship) panayam (before) this mazabach (altar) in Yarawashalam?'

Now therefore, please give pledges to my adawan (master) the malak (king) of Ashawar, and I will nathan (give) you two alap (thousand) horses, if you are yakal (able) on your part to nathan (set) riders on them.

How then can you shawab (turn back / repent) away the panayam (face) of one captain of the qatan (least) of my adawan (master's) ibad (servants), and batach (put) your trust on Matzarayam for chariots and for horsemen?
Have I now ilah (come) up balaiday (without) Yahawah against this place to shachath (destroy) it? Yahawah said to me, ‘ilah (go) up against this aratz (land), and shachath (destroy) it.'"'

Then Alayaqayam the ban (son) Chalaqayah Hilkiah, and Shabanaa, and Yawaach, said to Rabashaqah, "Please dabar (speak) to your ibad (servants) in the Aramayath (Syrian) language; for we understand it. Don't dabar (speak) with us in the Yahawadayath (Jews)' language, in the hearing of the im (people) who are on the wall.

But Rabashaqah said to them, "Has my adawan (master) sent me to your adawan (master), and to you, to dabar (speak) these dabar (words)? Hasn't he sent me to the men who yashab (sit) on the wall, to akal (eat) their own dung, and to drink their own water with you?

Then Rabashaqah stood, and cried with a gadawal (loud) qawal (voice) in the Yahawadayath (Jews)' language, and spoke, saying, "Hear the dabar (word) of the gadawal (great) malak (king), the malak (king) of Ashawar.
Thus amar (says) the malak (king), ‘Don't let Chazaqayah deceive you; for he will not be yakal (able) to natzal (deliver) you out of his yad (hand).

Neither let Chazaqayah batach (make) you trust in Yahawah, saying, "Yahawah will natzal (surely) natzal (deliver) us, and this Iyar shall not be given into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Ashawar.

Don't listen to Chazaqayah.' For thus amar (says) the malak (king) of Ashawar, ‘ishah (make) your barakah (peace) with me, and yatzaa (come) out to me; and everyone of you akal (eat) of his vine, and everyone of his fig tree, and everyone drink the mayam (waters) of his own bawar (cistern);

until I bawaa (come) and take you away to a aratz (land) like your own aratz (land), a aratz (land) of grain and new thayarawash (wine), a aratz (land) of lacham (bread) and vineyards, a aratz (land) of olive trees and of honey, that you may chayah (live), and not mawath (die). Don't listen to Chazaqayah, when he persuades you, saying, "Yahawah will natzal (deliver) us.
Has any of the Alahayam of the gawayam (nations) ever delivered his aratz (land) out of the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Ashawar?
Where are the Alahayam of Chamath, and of Arapad? Where are the Alahayam of Saparawayam, of Hanai, and Iwah? Have they delivered Shamarawan out of my yad (hand)?
Who are they among all the Alahayam of the aratz (countries), that have delivered their aratz (country) out of my yad (hand), that Yahawah should natzal (deliver) Yarawashalam out of my yad (hand)?'
But the im (people) held their charash (peace), and answered him not a dabar (word); for the malak (king's) matzawah (commandment) was, "Don't answer him.

Then Alayaqayam the ban (son) Chalaqayah Hilkiah, who was over the bayath (household), came with Shabanaa the scribe, and Yawaach the ban (son) of Asap the zakar (recorder), to Chazaqayah with their clothes torn, and told him the dabar (words) of Rabashaqah.
It happened, when malak (king) Chazaqayah heard it, that he tore his clothes, and covered himself with sackcloth, and went into the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

He sent Alayaqayam, who was over the bayath (household), and Shabanaa the scribe, and the zaqan (elders) of the kahan (priests), covered with sackcloth, to Yashaiyah the nabayaa (prophet) the ban (son) of Amawatz.

They said to him, "Thus amar (says) Chazaqayah, ‘This yawam (day) is a yawam (day) of tzarah (trouble), of rebuke, and of rejection; for the children have bawaa (come) to the point of birth, and there is no kach (strength) to deliver them.

It may be Yahawah your Alahayam will hear all the dabar (words) of Rabashaqah, whom the malak (king) of Ashawar his adawan (master) has sent to defy the chay (living) Alahayam, and will yakach (rebuke) the dabar (words) which Yahawah your Alahayam has heard. Therefore nashaa (lift) up your prayer for the shaarayath (remnant) that is matzaa (left).'
So the ibad (servants) of malak (king) Chazaqayah came to Yashaiyah.

Yashaiyah said to them, "Thus you shall amar (tell) your adawan (master), ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "Don't be yaraa (afraid) of the dabar (words) that you have heard, with which the nair (servants) of the malak (king) of Ashawar have blasphemed me.

Behold, I will nathan (put) a rawach (spirit) in him, and he will hear news, and will shawab (turn back / repent) to his own aratz (land). I will napal (cause) him to fall by the charab (sword) in his own aratz (land)."'
So Rabashaqah returned, and found the malak (king) of Ashawar warring against Labanah; for he had heard that he had departed from Lakayash.
When he heard it said of Tharahaqah malak (king) of Kawash, "Behold, he has yatzaa (come) out to fight against you, he sent malaak (messengers) again to Chazaqayah, saying,

‘Thus you shall amar (speak) to Chazaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), saying, "Don't let your Alahayam in whom you batach (trust) deceive you, saying, Yarawashalam will not be given into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Ashawar.
Behold, you have heard what the malak (kings) of Ashawar have done to all aratz (lands), by destroying them charam (utterly). Will you be delivered?
Have the Alahayam of the gawayam (nations) delivered them, which my abawath (fathers) have destroyed, Gawazan, and Charan, and Ratzap, and the children of Idan that were in Thalaashar?
Where is the malak (king) of Chamath, and the malak (king) of Arapad, and the malak (king) of the Iyar of Saparawayam, of Hanai, and Iwah?"'
Chazaqayah received the letter from the yad (hand) of the malaak (messengers), and qaraa (read) it. Then Chazaqayah went up to the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and spread it panayam (before) Yahawah.

Chazaqayah prayed panayam (before) Yahawah, and said, "Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), who yashab (sit) above the karawab (cherubim), you are the Alahayam, even you alone, of all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (earth). You have made shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth).
natah (incline) your ear, Yahawah, and hear. Open your iyan (eyes), Yahawah, and raah (see). Hear the dabar (words) of Sanacharayab, with which he has sent to defy the chay (living) Alahayam.
Truly, Yahawah, the malak (kings) of Ashawar have laid charab (waste) the gawayam (nations) and their aratz (lands),
and have nathan (cast) their Alahayam into the ash (fire); for they were no Alahayam, but the maishah (work) of men's yad (hands), itz (wood) and aban (stone). Therefore they have destroyed them.
Now therefore, Yahawah our Alahayam, yashai (save) us, I beg you, out of his yad (hand), that all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (earth) may yadai (know) that you, Yahawah, are Alahayam alone.

Then Yashaiyah the ban (son) of Amawatz sent to Chazaqayah, saying, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘Whereas you have prayed to me against Sanacharayab malak (king) of Ashawar, I have heard you.

This is the dabar (word) that Yahawah has spoken concerning him: "The virgin bath (daughter) of Tzayawan has despised you and ridiculed you. The bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam has shaken her raash (head) at you.
Whom have you defied and blasphemed? Against whom have you exalted your qawal (voice) and lifted up your iyan (eyes) on high? Against the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).

By your malaak (messengers) you have defied the Adanay, and have said, ‘With the multitude of my chariots, I have ilah (come) up to the height of the har (mountains), to the innermost parts of Labanawan; and I will karath (cut) down its tall cedars, and its choice fir trees; and I will bawaa (enter) into his farthest lodging place, the Yair of his Karamal field.
I have dug and drunk zawar (strange) mayam (waters), and with the kap (sole) of my feet will I charab (dry) up all the yaar (rivers) Matzawar Egypt.'

Haven't you heard how I have done it Rachawaq ago, and formed it of qadam (ancient) yawam (times)? Now have I brought it to pass, that it should be yours to lay waste fortified Iyar into ruinous heaps.

Therefore their yashab (inhabitants) were of Qatzar yad (power). They were dismayed and confounded. They were like the grass of the shadah (field), and like the green herb, like the grass on the housetops, and like grain blasted panayam (before) it has grown up.
But I yadai (know) your sitting down, and your yatzaa (going) out, and your coming in, and your raging against me.

Because of your raging Shaanan me, and because your arrogance has ilah (come) up into my ears, therefore will I shawam (put) my hook in your ap (nose), and my bridle in your shapah (lips), and I will shawab (turn back / repent) you back by the darak (way) by which you came.

"‘This shall be the awath (sign) to you: You shall akal (eat) this Shanah that which grows of itself, and in the shanay (second) Shanah that which springs of the same; and in the shalayashay (third) Shanah zarai (sow), and reap, and plant vineyards, and akal (eat) its fruit.
The shaar (remnant) that has palayatah (escaped) of the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) shall again take root downward, and ishah (bear) fruit upward.
For out of Yarawashalam a shaarayath (remnant) will yatzaa (go) out, and out of har (mount) Tzayawan those who shall palayatah (escape). The zeal of Yahawah will ishah (perform) this.'

"Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah concerning the malak (king) of Ashawar, ‘He shall not bawaa (come) to this Iyar, nor shoot an chatz (arrow) there, neither shall he qadam (come) before it with magan (shield), nor cast up a mound against it.
By the darak (way) that he came, by the same shall he shawab (turn back / repent), and he shall not bawaa (come) to this Iyar,' says Yahawah.
‘For I will defend this Iyar to yashai (save) it, for my own sake, and for my ibad (servant) Dawad sake.'

It happened that layal (night), that the malaak (angel) of Yahawah went out, and struck one maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) in the machanah (camp) of the Ashawar (Assyrians). When men arose shakam (early) in the shakam (morning), behold, these were all mawath (dead) pagar (bodies).
So Sanacharayab malak (king) of Ashawar departed, and went and returned, and lived at Nayanawah.

It happened, as he was worshipping in the bayath (house) of Nasarak his Alahayam, that Adaramalak and Sharaatzar struck him with the charab (sword); and they escaped into the aratz (land) of Ararat. Asarachadawan Haddon his ban (son) reigned in his place.

In those yawam (days) was Chazaqayah chalah (sick) to mawath (death). Yashaiyah the nabayaa (prophet) the ban (son) of Amawatz came to him, and said to him, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘Set your bayath (house) in tzawah (order); for you shall mawath (die), and not chayah (live).'
Then he turned his panayam (face) to the wall, and prayed to Yahawah, saying,

"zakar (remember) now, Yahawah, I beg you, how I have walked panayam (before) you in truth and with a Shalam labab (heart), and have done that which is tawab (good) in your iyan (sight)." Chazaqayah wept bitterly.
It happened, before Yashaiyah had gone out into the Thayakawan part of the city, that the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to him, saying,

"shawab (turn back / repent) back, and amar (tell) Chazaqayah the nagayad (prince) of my im (people), ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Dawad your ab (father), "I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Behold, I will heal you. On the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), you shall ilah (go) up to the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

I will add to your yawam (days) chamash (fifteen) Shanah. I will natzal (deliver) you and this Iyar out of the kap (hand) of the malak (king) of Ashawar. I will defend this Iyar for my own sake, and for my ibad (servant) Dawad sake."'
Yashaiyah said, "Take a cake of figs." They took and laid it on the boil, and he recovered.
Chazaqayah said to Yashaiyah, "What shall be the awath (sign) that Yahawah will heal me, and that I shall ilah (go) up to the bayath (house) of Yahawah the shalayashay (third) yawam (day)?

Yashaiyah said, "This shall be the awath (sign) to you from Yahawah, that Yahawah will do the thing that he has spoken: shall the shadow halak (go) forward ishar (ten) steps, or shawab (turn back / repent) back ishar (ten) steps?
Yachazaqayah answered, "It is a qalal (light) thing for the shadow to natah (go) forward ishar (ten) steps. Nay, but let the shadow shawab (turn back / repent) backward ishar (ten) steps.
Yashaiyah the nabayaa (prophet) cried to Yahawah; and he brought the shadow ishar (ten) steps backward, by which it had gone down on the dial of Achaz.
At that ith (time) Berodach Balaadan the ban (son) of Balaadan, malak (king) of Babal, sent letters and a manachah (present) to Chazaqayah; for he had heard that Chazaqayah had been chalah (sick).

Chazaqayah listened to them, and showed them all the bayath (house) of his precious things, the kasap (silver), and the gold, and the spices, and the tawab (precious) shaman (oil), and the bayath (house) of his armor, and all that was found in his treasures: there was nothing in his bayath (house), nor in all his mamashalah (dominion), that Chazaqayah didn't show them.

Then Yashaiyah the nabayaa (prophet) came to malak (king) Chazaqayah, and said to him, "What did these men amar (say)? From where did they bawaa (come) to you?" Chazaqayah said, "They have bawaa (come) from a Rachawaq aratz (country), even from Babal.
He said, "What have they seen in your bayath (house)?" Chazaqayah answered, "They have seen all that is in my bayath (house). There is nothing among my treasures that I have not shown them.
Yashaiyah said to Chazaqayah, "Hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah.

‘Behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), that all that is in your bayath (house), and that which your abawath (fathers) have laid up in store to this yawam (day), shall be carried to Babal. Nothing shall be yathar (left),' amar (says) Yahawah.
‘Of your ban (sons) who shall yatzaa (issue) from you, whom you shall father, shall they take away; and they shall be eunuchs in the hayakal (palace) of the malak (king) of Babal.'
Then Chazaqayah said to Yashaiyah, "The dabar (word) of Yahawah which you have spoken is tawab (good)." He said moreover, "Isn't it so, if shalawam (peace) and truth shall be in my yawam (days)?

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Chazaqayah, and all his might, and how he made the pool, and the thailah (conduit), and brought mayam (water) into the Iyar, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)?
Chazaqayah slept with his abawath (fathers); and Manashah his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Manashah was shanayam (twelve) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned chamashayam (fifty) - chamash (five) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Chapatzayabah.

He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, after the thawaibah (abominations) of the gawayam (nations) whom Yahawah yarash (cast) out panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

For he built again the bamah (high) places which Chazaqayah his ab (father) had destroyed; and he reared up mazabach (altars) for Bail, and made an Asharah, as did Achaab malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), and worshiped all the tzabaa (army) of the sky, and served them.
He built mazabach (altars) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, of which Yahawah said, "I will shawam (put) my sham (name) in Yarawashalam.
He built mazabach (altars) for all the tzabaa (army) of the sky in the shanayam (two) courts of the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

He made his ban (son) to ibar (pass) through the ash (fire), and practiced sorcery, and used enchantments, and dealt with those who had familiar awab (spirits), and with wizards: he worked much rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, to provoke him to kais (anger).

He shawam (set) the engraved pasal (image) Asharah Asherah, that he had made, in the bayath (house) of which Yahawah said to Dawad and to Shalamah his ban (son), "In this bayath (house), and in Yarawashalam, which I have chosen out of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), will I shawam (put) my sham (name) iwalam (forever);

neither will I cause the feet of Yasharaal (Israel) to wander any more out of the adamah (land) which I gave their abawath (fathers), if only they will shamar (observe) to do according to all that I have tzawah (commanded) them, and according to all the thawarah (law) that my ibad (servant) Mashah tzawah (commanded) them.
But they didn't listen: and Manashah seduced them to do that which is rai (evil) more than the gawayam (nations) did whom Yahawah destroyed panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
Yahawah spoke by his ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets), saying,

"Because Manashah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) has done these thawaibah (abominations), and has done wickedly above all that the Amaray (Amorites) did, who were panayam (before) him, and has made Yahawadah (Judah) also to chataa (sin) with his idols;

therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘Behold, I bawaa (bring) such rai (evil) on Yarawashalam and Yahawadah (Judah), that whoever hears of it, shanayam (both) his ears shall tingle.

I will natah (stretch) over Yarawashalam the line of Shamarawan, and the plummet of the bayath (house) of Achaab; and I will machah (wipe) Yarawashalam as a man machah (wipes) a dish, wiping it and turning it panayam (upside) down.

I will cast off the shaarayath (remnant) of my nachalah (inheritance), and nathan (deliver) them into the yad (hand) of their ayab (enemies). They will become a prey and a spoil to all their ayab (enemies);

because they have done that which is rai (evil) in my iyan (sight), and have provoked me to kais (anger), since the yawam (day) their abawath (fathers) came yatzaa (forth) out of Matzarayam, even to this yawam (day).'

Moreover Manashah shed naqay (innocent) dam (blood) very much, until he had filled Yarawashalam from one pah (end) to another; besides his chataah (sin) with which he made Yahawadah (Judah) to chataa (sin), in doing that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah.

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Manashah, and all that he did, and his chataah (sin) that he sinned, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)?
Manashah slept with his abawath (fathers), and was buried in the Gan of his own bayath (house), in the Gan of Izaa: and Amawan his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Amawan was isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned shanayam (two) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Mashalamath the bath (daughter) of Charawatz of Yatabah.
He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, as Manashah his ab (father) did.
He walked in all the darak (way) that his ab (father) walked in, and served the idols that his ab (father) served, and worshiped them:
and he forsook Yahawah, the Alahayam of his abawath (fathers), and didn't halak (walk) in the darak (way) of Yahawah.
The ibad (servants) of Amawan conspired against him, and put the malak (king) to mawath (death) in his own bayath (house).
But the im (people) of the aratz (land) killed all those who had conspired against malak (king) Amawan; and the im (people) of the aratz (land) made Yaashayah his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Amawan which he did, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)?
He was buried in his tomb in the Gan of Izaa: and Yaashayah his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Yaashayah was shamanah (eight) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned shalawashayam (thirty) - one Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Yadayadah the bath (daughter) of Idayah Batzaqath Bozkath.

He did that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, and walked in all the darak (way) of Dawad his ab (father), and didn't sawar (turn) aside to the right yamayan (hand) or to the shamaawal (left).

It happened in the eighteenth Shanah of malak (king) Yaashayah, that the malak (king) sent Shapan, the ban (son) of Atzalayahaw the ban (son) of Mashalam, the scribe, to the bayath (house) of Yahawah, saying,

"ilah (go) up Chalaqayah Hilkiah the gadawal (high) kahan (priest), that he may thamam (sum) the kasap (money) which is brought into the bayath (house) of Yahawah, which the keepers of the threshold have gathered of the im (people).

Let them nathan (deliver) it into the yad (hand) of the workmen who have the paqad (oversight) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah; and let them nathan (give) it to the workmen who are in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, to chazaq (repair) the breaches of the bayath (house),
to the carpenters, and to the banah (builders), and to the masons, and for buying itz (timber) and cut aban (stone) to chazaq (repair) the bayath (house).
However there was no accounting made with them of the kasap (money) that was delivered into their yad (hand); for they dealt faithfully.

Chalaqayah the gadawal (high) kahan (priest) said Shapan Shaphan the scribe, "I have found the book of the thawarah (law) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah." Chalaqayah delivered the book Shapan Shaphan, and he qaraa (read) it.

Shapan the scribe came to the malak (king), and brought the malak (king) dabar (word) again, and said, "Your ibad (servants) have emptied out the kasap (money) that was found in the bayath (house), and have delivered it into the yad (hand) of the workmen who have the paqad (oversight) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
Shapan the scribe told the malak (king), saying, "Chalaqayah the kahan (priest) has delivered a book Shapan me." Shaphan qaraa (read) it panayam (before) the malak (king).
It happened, when the malak (king) had heard the dabar (words) of the book of the thawarah (law), that he tore his clothes.

The malak (king) tzawah (commanded) Chalaqayah the kahan (priest), and Achayaqam the ban (son) Shapan Shaphan, and Ikabawar the ban (son) Mayakayah Micaiah, and Shapan the scribe, and Ishayah the malak (king's) ibad (servant), saying,

"yalak (go) inquire of Yahawah for me, and for the im (people), and for all Yahawadah (Judah), concerning the dabar (words) of this book that is found; for gadawal (great) is the chamah (wrath) of Yahawah that is kindled against us, because our abawath (fathers) have not listened to the dabar (words) of this book, to do according to all that which is written concerning us.

So Chalaqayah the kahan (priest), and Achayaqam, and Ikabawar, and Shapan, and Ishayah, went to Chaladah the prophetess, the ashah (wife) of Shalawam the ban (son) of Thaqawah, the ban (son) of Charachas, keeper of the bagad (wardrobe) (now she lived in Yarawashalam in the mashanah (second) quarter); and they talked with her.
She said to them, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): ‘amar (tell) the ayash (man) who sent you to me,

"Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘Behold, I will bawaa (bring) rai (evil) on this place, and on its yashab (inhabitants), even all the dabar (words) of the book which the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) has qaraa (read).

Because they have forsaken me, and have burned qatar (incense) to other Alahayam, that they might provoke me to kais (anger) with all the maishah (work) of their yad (hands), therefore my chamah (wrath) shall be kindled against this place, and it shall not be quenched.'

But to the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), who sent you to inquire of Yahawah, thus you shall amar (tell) him, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): ‘Concerning the dabar (words) which you have heard,

because your labab (heart) was tender, and you humbled yourself panayam (before) Yahawah, when you heard what I spoke against this place, and against its yashab (inhabitants), that they should become a desolation and a qalalah (curse), and have torn your clothes, and wept panayam (before) me; I also have heard you,' says Yahawah.

‘Therefore, behold, I will asap (gather) you to your abawath (fathers), and you shall be gathered to your qabar (grave) in shalawam (peace), neither shall your iyan (eyes) raah (see) all the rai (evil) which I will bawaa (bring) on this place.'"'" They brought shawab (turn back / repent) this dabar (message) to the malak (king).
The malak (king) sent, and they gathered to him all the zaqan (elders) of Yahawadah (Judah) and of Yarawashalam.

The malak (king) went up to the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and all the men of Yahawadah (Judah) and all the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam with him, and the kahan (priests), and the nabayaa (prophets), and all the im (people), both qatan (small) and gadawal (great): and he qaraa (read) in their ears all the dabar (words) of the book of the barayath (covenant) which was found in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

The malak (king) stood by the pillar, and made a barayath (covenant) panayam (before) Yahawah, to yalak (walk) achar (after) Yahawah, and to shamar (keep) his matzawah (commandments), and his idawath (testimonies), and his chaqah (statutes), with all his lab (heart), and all his napash (soul), to qawam (confirm) the dabar (words) of this barayath (covenant) that were written in this book: and all the im (people) stood to the barayath (covenant).

The malak (king) tzawah (commanded) Chalaqayah the gadawal (high) kahan (priest), and the kahan (priests) of the mashanah (second) order, and the keepers of the threshold, to yatzaa (bring) forth out of the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah all the vessels that were made for Bail, and Asharah the Asherah, and for all the tzabaa (army) of the sky, and he burned them outside of Yarawashalam in the fields of the Qadarawan, and carried their ashes to Bayathaal.

He shabath (put) down the idolatrous kamar (priests), whom the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah) had ordained to qatar (burn) incense in the bamah (high) places in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the places around Yarawashalam; those also who burned qatar (incense) to Bail, to the shamash (sun), and to the yarach (moon), and to the planets, and to all the tzabaa (army) of the sky.

He brought out the Asharah from the bayath (house) of Yahawah, outside of Yarawashalam, to the nachal (brook) Qadarawan, and burned it at the nachal (brook) Qadarawan, and beat it to ipar (dust), and cast its ipar (dust) on the qabar (graves) of the ban (common) im (people).
He broke down the bayath (houses) of the qadash (sodomites), that were in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, where the women wove bayath (hangings) Asharah the Asherah.

He brought all the kahan (priests) out of the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and defiled the bamah (high) places where the kahan (priests) had burned qatar (incense), from Gabai Baarashabai Beersheba; and he broke down the bamah (high) places of the gates that were at the entrance of the gate of Yahawashawai the shar (governor) of the Iyar, which were on a ayash (man's) left shamaawal (hand) at the gate of the Iyar.

Nevertheless the kahan (priests) of the bamah (high) places didn't ilah (come) up to the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah in Yarawashalam, but they ate unleavened matzah (bread) among their ach (brothers).
He defiled Thapath, which is in the Gayaa of the children of Hanam, that no ayash (man) might make his ban (son) or his bath (daughter) to ibar (pass) through the ash (fire) to Malak.

He took shabath (away) the horses that the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah) had given to the shamash (sun), at the entrance of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, by the room Nathanamalak Nathan Melech the officer, who was Parabar the court; and he burned the chariots of the shamash (sun) with ash (fire).

The malak (king) broke down the mazabach (altars) that were on the roof of the upper room of Achaz, which the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah) had made, and the mazabach (altars) which Manashah had made in the shanayam (two) courts of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and nathatz (beat) them down from there, and cast their ipar (dust) into the nachal (brook) Qadarawan.

The the malak (king) defiled the bamah (high) places that were panayam (before) Yarawashalam, which were on the right yamayan (hand) of the har (mountain) of mashachayath (corruption), which Shalamah the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) had built for Ishatharath the shaqawatz (abomination) of the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), and for Kamawash the shaqawatz (abomination) of Mawaab, and for Malakam the thawaibah (abomination) of the children of Imawan.
He broke in shabar (pieces) the matzabah (pillars), and karath (cut) down the Asharah, and filled their places with the itzam (bones) of men.

Moreover the mazabach (altar) that was at Bayathaal, and the bamah (high) place which Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, who made Yasharaal (Israel) to chataa (sin), had made, even that mazabach (altar) and the bamah (high) place he broke down; and he burned the bamah (high) place and beat it to ipar (dust), and burned the Asharah.

As Yaashayah turned himself, he spied the tombs that were there in the har (mountain); and he sent, and took the itzam (bones) out of the tombs, and burned them on the mazabach (altar), and defiled it, according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah which the ayash (man) of Alahayam proclaimed, who proclaimed these things.

Then he said, "What monument is that which I raah (see)?" The men of the Iyar told him, "It is the tomb of the ayash (man) of Alahayam, who came from Yahawadah (Judah), and proclaimed these things that you have done against the mazabach (altar) of Bayathaal.
He said, "Let him be! Let no ayash (man) move his itzam (bones)." So they let his itzam (bones) malat (alone), with the itzam (bones) of the nabayaa (prophet) who came out of Shamarawan.

All the bayath (houses) also of the bamah (high) places that were in the Iyar of Shamarawan, which the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel) had made to provoke Yahawah to anger, Yaashayah took sawar (away), and did to them according to all the maishah (acts) that he had done in Bayathaal.
He killed all the kahan (priests) of the bamah (high) places that were there, on the mazabach (altars), and burned men's itzam (bones) on them; and he returned to Yarawashalam.
The malak (king) tzawah (commanded) all the im (people), saying, "ishah (keep) the pasach (passover) to Yahawah your Alahayam, as it is written in this book of the barayath (covenant).

ishah (surely) there was not kept such a pasach (passover) from the yawam (days) of the shapat (judges) who judged Yasharaal (Israel), nor in all the yawam (days) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel), nor of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah);
but in the eighteenth Shanah of malak (king) Yaashayah was this pasach (passover) kept to Yahawah in Yarawashalam.

Moreover Yaashayah removed those who had familiar awab (spirits), and the wizards, and the tharapayam (teraphim), and the tharapayam (idols), and all the galawal (abominations) that were seen in the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah) and in Yarawashalam, that he might qawam (confirm) the dabar (words) of the thawarah (law) which were written in the book that Chalaqayah the kahan (priest) found in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

Like him was there no malak (king) panayam (before) him, who turned to Yahawah with all his labab (heart), and with all his napash (soul), and with all his might, according to all the thawarah (law) of Mashah; neither achar (after) him qawam (arose) there any like him.

Notwithstanding, Yahawah didn't shawab (turn back / repent) from the charawan (fierceness) of his gadawal (great) ap (wrath), with which his ap (anger) was kindled against Yahawadah (Judah), because of all the kais (provocation) with which Manashah had provoked him.

Yahawah said, "I will sawar (remove) Yahawadah (Judah) also out of my panayam (sight), as I have removed Yasharaal (Israel), and I will cast off this Iyar which I have chosen, even Yarawashalam, and the bayath (house) of which I said, ‘My sham (name) shall be there.'
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yaashayah, and all that he did, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)?

In his yawam (days) Paraihanakah Necoh malak (king) of Matzarayam went up against the malak (king) of Ashawar to the nahar (river) Parath: and malak (king) Yaashayah went qaraah (against) him; and Pharaoh Necoh killed him at Magadawan, when he had seen him.

His ibad (servants) carried him in a chariot mawath (dead) from Magadawan, and brought him to Yarawashalam, and buried him in his own tomb. The im (people) of the aratz (land) took Yahawaachaz the ban (son) of Yaashayah, and mashach (anointed) him, and made him malak (king) in his ab (father's) place.

Yahawaachaz was isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned shalawash (three) chadash (months) in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Chamawatal the bath (daughter) of Yaramayah of Labanah.
He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, according to all that his abawath (fathers) had done.

Paraihanakah Necoh put him in bonds at Rabalah in the aratz (land) of Chamath, that he might not malak (reign) in Yarawashalam; and nathan (put) the aratz (land) to a tribute of one maah (hundred) talents of kasap (silver), and a talent of gold.

Paraihanakah Necoh made Alayaqayam the ban (son) of Yaashayah malak (king) in the place of Yaashayah his ab (father), and changed his sham (name) to Yahawayaqayam: but he took Yahawaachaz away; and he came to Matzarayam, and died there.

Yahawayaqayam gave the kasap (silver) and the gold to Paraih; but he taxed the aratz (land) to nathan (give) the kasap (money) according to the commandment of Paraih: he exacted the kasap (silver) and the gold of the im (people) of the aratz (land), of everyone according to his irak (taxation), to nathan (give) it to Paraihanakah Necoh.

Yahawayaqayam was isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned achad (eleven) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Zabayadah the bath (daughter) of Padayah of Rawamah.
He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, according to all that his abawath (fathers) had done.
In his yawam (days) Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal came up, and Yahawayaqayam became his ibad (servant) shalawash (three) Shanah: then he turned and rebelled against him.

Yahawah sent against him gadawad (bands) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), and gadawad (bands) of the Aram (Syrians), and gadawad (bands) Mawaab the Moabites, and gadawad (bands) of the children of Imawan, and sent them against Yahawadah (Judah) to abad (destroy) it, according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah, which he spoke by his ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets).
Surely at the commandment of Yahawah came this on Yahawadah (Judah), to sawar (remove) them out of his panayam (sight), for the chataah (sins) of Manashah, according to all that he did,
and also for the naqay (innocent) dam (blood) that he shed; for he filled Yarawashalam with naqay (innocent) dam (blood): and Yahawah would not pardon.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yahawayaqayam, and all that he did, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah)?
So Yahawayaqayam slept with his abawath (fathers); and Yahawayakayan his ban (son) reigned in his place.

The malak (king) of Matzarayam didn't yatzaa (come) again out of his aratz (land) any more; for the malak (king) of Babal had taken, from the brook of Matzarayam to the nachal (river) Parath, all that pertained to the malak (king) of Matzarayam.

Yahawayakayan was eighteen Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned in Yarawashalam shalawash (three) chadash (months): and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Nachashathaa the bath (daughter) of Alanathan of Yarawashalam.
He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, according to all that his ab (father) had done.
At that ith (time) the ibad (servants) of Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal came up to Yarawashalam, and the Iyar was besieged.
Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal came to the Iyar, while his ibad (servants) were besieging it;

and Yahawayakayan the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) went out to the malak (king) of Babal, he, and his am (mother), and his ibad (servants), and his shar (princes), and his officers: and the malak (king) of Babal took him in the shamanah (eighth) Shanah of his malak (reign).

He carried out there all the treasures of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the treasures of the malak (king's) bayath (house), and cut in pieces all the vessels of gold, which Shalamah malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) had made in the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, as Yahawah had said.

He carried away all Yarawashalam, and all the shar (princes), and all the gabawar (mighty) men of valor, even ishar (ten) alap (thousand) galah (captives), and all the craftsmen and the smiths; none remained, except the Dalah sort of the im (people) of the aratz (land).

He carried away Yahawayakayan to Babal; and the malak (king's) am (mother), and the malak (king's) wives, and his officers, and the chief men of the aratz (land), carried he into captivity from Yarawashalam to Babal.

All the men of might, even shabai (seven) alap (thousand), and the craftsmen and the smiths one alap (thousand), all of them gabawar (strong) and ishah (apt) for war, even them the malak (king) of Babal brought captive to Babal.
The malak (king) of Babal made Mathanayah, Jehoiachin's dawad (father's) brother, malak (king) is his place, and changed his sham (name) to Tzadaqayah.

Tzadaqayah was isharayam (twenty) - one Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned achad (eleven) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Chamawatal the bath (daughter) of Yaramayah of Labanah.
He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, according to all that Yahawayaqayam had done.

For through the ap (anger) of Yahawah, it happened in Yarawashalam and Yahawadah (Judah), until he had cast them out from his panayam (presence). Tzadaqayah rebelled against the malak (king) of Babal.

It happened in the thashayaiy (ninth) Shanah of his malak (reign), in the ishayaray (tenth) chadash (month), in the tenth day of the chadash (month), that Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal came, he and all his chayal (army), against Yarawashalam, and encamped against it; and they built forts against it around it.
So the Iyar was besieged to the ishathay (eleventh) Shanah of malak (king) Tzadaqayah.
On the ninth day of the fourth chadash (month) the famine was severe in the Iyar, so that there was no lacham (bread) for the im (people) of the aratz (land).

Then a breach was made in the Iyar, and all the men of war fled by layal (night) by the darak (way) of the gate between the chawamah (two) walls, which was by the malak (king's) Gan (now the Kashaday (Chaldeans) were against the Iyar around it); and the king went by the darak (way) of the irabah (arabah).
But the chayal (army) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans) pursued achar (after) the malak (king), and overtook him in the irabah (plains) of Yarayachaw; and all his chayal (army) was scattered from him.
Then they took the malak (king), and carried him up to the malak (king) of Babal to Rabalah; and they gave mashapat (judgment) on him.
They killed the ban (sons) of Tzadaqayah before his iyan (eyes), and put out the iyan (eyes) of Tzadaqayah, and bound him in fetters, and carried him to Babal.

Now in the chamayashay (fifth) chadash (month), on the seventh day of the chadash (month), which was the nineteenth Shanah of malak (king) Nabawakadanaatzar, malak (king) of Babal, came Nabawazaraadan the rab (captain) of the guard, a ibad (servant) of the malak (king) of Babal, to Yarawashalam.
He burnt the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the malak (king's) bayath (house); and all the bayath (houses) of Yarawashalam, even every gadawal (great) bayath (house), burnt he with ash (fire).
All the chayal (army) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), who were with the rab (captain) of the guard, broke down the walls around Yarawashalam.

Nabawazaraadan the rab (captain) of the guard carried away captive the yathar (residue) of the im (people) who were shaar (left) in the Iyar, and those who napal (fell) away, who fell to the malak (king) of Babal, and the yathar (residue) of the multitude.
But the rab (captain) of the guard shaar (left) Dalah of the poorest of the aratz (land) to karam (work) the vineyards and fields.

The Kashaday (Chaldeans) broke up the pillars of brass that were in the bayath (house) of Yahawah and the bases and the bronze yam (sea) that were in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and carried the brass shabar (pieces) to Babal.
They took away the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the kap (spoons), and all the vessels of brass with which they ministered.
The rab (captain) of the guard took away the machathah (fire) pans, the basins, that which was of gold, in gold, and that which was of kasap (silver), in kasap (silver).
The shanayam (two) pillars, the one yam (sea), and the bases, which Shalamah had made for the bayath (house) of Yahawah, the brass of all these vessels was laa (without) weight.

The height of the one pillar was eighteen amah (cubits), and a capital of brass was on it; and the height of the capital was shalawash (three) amah (cubits), with network and pomegranates on the capital around it, all of brass: and like to these had the shanay (second) pillar with network.
The rab (captain) of the guard took Sharayah the raash (chief) kahan (priest), and Tzapanayah the mashanah (second) kahan (priest), and the shalawash (three) keepers of the threshold:

and out of the Iyar he took an officer who was set over the men of war; and chamash (five) men of those who saw the malak (king's) face, who were found in the Iyar; and the scribe, the shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army), who mustered the im (people) of the aratz (land); and shashayam (sixty) men of the im (people) of the aratz (land), who were found in the Iyar.
Nabawazaraadan the rab (captain) of the guard took them, and brought them to the malak (king) of Babal to Rabalah.
The malak (king) of Babal struck them, and put them to mawath (death) at Rabalah in the aratz (land) of Chamath. So Yahawadah (Judah) was carried away captive out of his adamah (land).

As for the im (people) who were shaar (left) in the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah), whom Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal had shaar (left), even over them he made Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam, the ban (son) Shapan Shaphan, governor.

Now when all the shar (captains) of the chayal (forces), they and their men, heard that the malak (king) of Babal had made Gadalayah governor, they came to Gadalayah Matzapah Mizpah, even Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah, and Yawachanan the ban (son) of Qarach, and Sharayah the ban (son) of Thanachamath the Natapathay (Netophathite), and Yaazanayah the ban (son) Maikathay the Maacathite, they and their men.

Gadalayah swore to them and to their men, and said to them, "Don't be yaraa (afraid) because of the ibad (servants) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans). yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land), and ibad (serve) the malak (king) of Babal, and it shall be yatab (well) with you.

But it happened in the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month), that Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah, the ban (son) of Alayashamai, of the malawakah (royal) zarai (seed) came, and ishar (ten) men with him, and struck Gadalayah, so that he died, and the Yahawaday (Jews) and the Kashaday (Chaldeans) that were Matzapah him at Mizpah.

All the im (people), both qatan (small) and gadawal (great), and the shar (captains) of the chayal (forces), qawam (arose), and came to Matzarayam; for they were yaraa (afraid) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans).

It happened in the shalawashayam (thirty) seventh Shanah of the captivity of Yahawayakayan malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), in the shanayam (twelfth) chadash (month), on the shabai (seven) and isharayam (twentieth) day of the chadash (month), that awayalamaradak (evilmerodach) malak (king) of Babal, in the Shanah that he began to malak (reign), lifted up the raash (head) of Yahawayakayan malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) out of bayath (prison);
and he spoke tawab (kindly) to him, and nathan (set) his kasaa (throne) above the kasaa (throne) of the malak (kings) who were with him in Babal,
and changed his prison bagad (garments). Jehoiachin ate lacham (bread) panayam (before) him continually all the yawam (days) of his chay (life):
and for his allowance, there was a continual allowance given him of the malak (king), every yawam (day) a dabar (portion), all the yawam (days) of his chay (life).
adam (adam), Shath, Anawash,
Qayanan, Mahalalaal, Yarad,
Chanawak, Mathawashalach, Lamak,
Nach, Sham, Cham, and Yapath.
The ban (sons) of Yapath: Gamar, and Magawag, and Maday, and Yawan, and Thawabal, and Mashak, and Thayaras.
The ban (sons) of Gamar: Ashakanaz, and Rayapath, and Thawagaramah.
The ban (sons) of Yawan: Alayashah, and Tharashayash, Kathay (Kittim), and Dadanayam.
The ban (sons) of Cham: Kawash, and Matzarayam, Pawat, and Kanain.
The ban (sons) of Kawash: Sabaa, and Chawayalah, and Sabathaa, and Raimah, and Sabathakaa. The ban (sons) of Raimah: Shabaa, and Dadan.
Kawash became the father of Namarawad; he began to be a gabawar (mighty) one in the aratz (earth).
Matzarayam became the father of Lawaday (Ludim), and Inamayam, and Lahabayam, and Napathachayam,
and Patharasay, and Kasalachayam (where the Palashathay (Philistines) came from), and Kapatharay (Caphtorim).
Kanain became the father of Tzayadawan his firstborn, and Chath,
and the Yabawasay (Jebusite), and the Amaray (Amorite), and the Garagashay (Girgashite),
and the Chaway (Hivite), and the Iraqay, and the Sayanay,
and the Arawaday, and the Tzamaray, and the Chamathay.
The ban (sons) of Sham: Iyalam, and Ashawar, and Arapakashad, and Lawad, and Aram, and Iwatz, and Chawal, and Gathar, and Mashak.
Arapakashad became the father of Shalach, and Shalach became the father of Ibar.
To Ibar were yalad (born) shanayam (two) ban (sons): the sham (name) of the one was Palag; for in his yawam (days) the aratz (earth) was divided; and his ach (brother's) sham (name) was Yaqatan.
Yaqatan became the father of Alamawadad, and Shalap, and Chatzaramawath, and Yarach,
and Hadawaram, and Awazal, and Daqalah,
and Iyabal, and Abayamaal, and Shabaa,
and Awapayar, and Chawayalah, and Yawabab. All these were the ban (sons) of Yaqatan.
Sham, Arapakashad, Shalach,
Ibar, Palag, Raiw,
Sharawag, Nachawar, Tharach,
Abaram (the same is Abaraham).
The ban (sons) of Abaraham: Yatzachaq, and Yashamaial.
These are their thawaladah (generations): the firstborn of Yashamaial, Nabayawath; then Qadar, and Adabaal, and Mabasham,
Mashamai, and Dawamah, Mashaa, Chadad, and Thayamaa,
Yatawar, Napayash, and Qadamah. These are the ban (sons) of Yashamaial.
The ban (sons) of Qatawarah, Abaraham concubine: she bore Zamaran, and Yaqashan, and Madan, and Madayan, and Yashabaq, and Shawach. The ban (sons) of Yaqashan: Shabaa, and Dadan.
The ban (sons) of Madayan: Iyapah, and Ipar, and Chanawak, and Abayadai, and Aladaih. All these were the ban (sons) of Qatawarah.
Abaraham became the father of Yatzachaq. The ban (sons) of Yatzachaq: Ishaw, and Yasharaal (Israel).
The ban (sons) of Ishaw: Alayapaz, Raiwaal, and Yaiwash, and Yailam, and Qarach.
The ban (sons) of Alayapaz: Thayaman, and Awamar, Tzapaw, and Gaitham, Qanaz, and Thamanai, and Imalaq.
The ban (sons) of Raiwaal: Nachath, Zarach, Shamah, and Mazah.
The ban (sons) of Shaiyar: Lawatan, and Shawabal, and Tzabaiwan, and Inah, and Dayashawan, and Atzar, and Dayashan.
The ban (sons) of Lawatan: Charay, and Hawamam; and Thamanai was Lawatan achawath (sister).
The ban (sons) of Shawabal: Ilawan, and Manachath, and Iyabal, Shapaw, and Awanam. The ban (sons) of Tzabaiwan: Ayah, and Inah.
The ban (sons) of Inah: Dayashawan. The ban (sons) of Dayashawan: Chamaran, and Ashaban, and Yatharan, and Karan.
The ban (sons) of Atzar: Balahan, and Zaiwan, Yaiqan. The ban (sons) of Dayashan: Iwatz, and Aran.

Now these are the malak (kings) who reigned in the aratz (land) of Adam, panayam (before) there reigned any malak (king) over the children of Yasharaal (Israel): Balai the ban (son) of Baiwar; and the sham (name) of his Iyar was Danahabah.
Balai died, and Yawabab the ban (son) of Zarach of Batzarah reigned in his place.
Yawabab died, and Chawasham of the aratz (land) of the Thayamanay reigned in his place.
Chawasham died, and Hadad the ban (son) of Badad, who struck Madayan in the shadah (field) of Mawaab, reigned in his place; and the sham (name) of his Iyar was Iwayath.
Hadad died, and Shamalah of Masharaqah reigned in his place.
Shamalah died, and Shaawal of Rachabawath by the nahar (river) reigned in his place.
Shaawal died, and Bailachanan Hanan the ban (son) of Ikabawar reigned in his place.

Bailachanan Hanan died, and Hadad reigned in his place; and the sham (name) of his Iyar was Paiw: and his ashah (wife's) sham (name) was Mahayatabaal, the bath (daughter) of Matarad, the bath (daughter) of Mayazahab.
Hadad died. The Alawap of Adam were: Alawap Thamanai, Alawap Ilawah, Alawap Yathath,
Alawap Ahalayabamah, Alawap Alah, Alawap Payanan,
Alawap Qanaz, Alawap Thayaman, Alawap Mabatzar,
Alawap Magadayaal, Alawap Iyaram. These are the Alawap of Adam.
These are the ban (sons) of Yasharaal (Israel): Raawaban, Shamaiwan, Laway, and Yahawadah (Judah), Yashashakar, and Zabawalawan,
Dan, Yawasap, and Banayamayan, Napathalay, Gad, and Ashar.

The ban (sons) of Yahawadah (Judah): Ir, and Awanan, and Shalah; which shalawash (three) were yalad (born) to him of Shawaia bath (daughter) the Kanainay. Ir, Yahawadah firstborn, was rai (wicked) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah; and he killed him.
Thamar his kalah (daughter-in-law) bore him Paratz and Zarach. All the ban (sons) of Yahawadah (Judah) were chamash (five).
The ban (sons) of Paratz: Chatzarawan, and Chamawal.
The ban (sons) of Zarach: Zamaray, and Ayathan, and Hayaman, and Kalakal, and Darai; chamash (five) of them in all.
The ban (sons) of Karamay: Ikar, the troubler of Yasharaal (Israel), who committed a trespass in the charam (devoted) thing.
The ban (sons) of Ayathan: Izarayah.
The ban (sons) also of Chatzarawan, who were yalad (born) to him: Yarachamaal, and Ram, and Kalawabay.
Ram became the father of Imayanadab, and Imayanadab became the father of Nachashawan, nashayaa (prince) of the children of Yahawadah (Judah);
and Nachashawan became the father of Shalamaa, and Shalamaa became the father of Baiz,
and Baiz became the father of Iwabad, and Iwabad became the father of Yashay;
and Yashay became the father of his firstborn Alayaab, and Abayanadab the shanay (second), and Shamaia the shalayashay (third),
Nathanaal the rabayaiy (fourth), Raday the chamayashay (fifth),
Atzam the shashay (sixth), Dawad the shabayaiy (seventh);
and their achawath (sisters) were Tzarawayah and Abayagayal. The ban (sons) of Tzarawayah: Abayashay, and Yawaab, and Ishahaal, shalawash (three).
Abayagayal bore Imashaa; and the ab (father) of Imashaa was Yathar the Yashamaialay (Ishmaelite).
Kalab the ban (son) of Chatzarawan became the father of children of Izawabah his ashah (wife), and of Yarayaiwath; and these were her ban (sons): Yashar, and Shawabab, and Aradawan.
Izawabah died, and Kalab took to him aparath (ephrath), who bore him Chawar.
Chawar became the father of Awaray, and Awaray became the father Batzalaal Bezalel.
Afterward Chatzarawan went in to the bath (daughter) of Makayar the ab (father) of Galaid, whom he took as wife when he was shashayam (sixty) Shanah ban (old); and she bore him Shagawab.
Shagawab became the father of Yaayar, who had twenty - three Iyar in the aratz (land) of Galaid.
Gashawar and Aram took the towns of Yaayar from them, with Qanath, and its villages, even shashayam (sixty) Iyar. All these were the ban (sons) of Makayar the ab (father) of Galaid.
achar (after) that Chatzarawan was mawath (dead) in Kalabaaparathah Ephrathah, then Abayah Chatzarawan ashah (wife) bore him Ashachawar the ab (father) of Thaqawai.
The ban (sons) of Yarachamaal the firstborn of Chatzarawan were Ram the firstborn, and Bawanah, and Aran, and Atzam, Achayah.
Yarachamaal had achar (another) ashah (wife), whose sham (name) was Itarah; she was the am (mother) of Awanam.
The ban (sons) of Ram the firstborn of Yarachamaal were Maitz, and Yamayan, and Iqar.
The ban (sons) of Awanam were Shamay, and Yadai. The ban (sons) of Shamay: Nadab, and Abayashawar.
The sham (name) of the ashah (wife) of Abayashawar was Abayahayal; and she bore him Achaban, and Mawalayad.
The ban (sons) of Nadab: Salad, and Apayam; but Salad died without children.
The ban (sons) of Apayam: Yashaiy. The ban (sons) of Yashaiy: Shashan. The ban (sons) of Shashan: Achalay.
The ban (sons) of Yadai the ach (brother) of Shamay: Yathar, and Yawanathan; and Yathar died without children.
The ban (sons) of Yawanathan: Palath, and Zazaa. These were the ban (sons) of Yarachamaal.
Now Shashan had no ban (sons), but bath (daughters). Shashan had a ibad (servant), an Matzaray (Egyptian), whose sham (name) was Yarachai.
Shashan gave his bath (daughter) to Yarachai his ibad (servant) as ashah (wife); and she bore him Ithay.
Ithay became the father of Nathan, and Nathan became the father of Zabad,
and Zabad became the father of Apalal, and Apalal became the father of Iwabad,
and Iwabad became the father of Yahawaa, and Yahawaa became the father of Izarayah,
and Izarayah became the father of Chalatz, and Chalatz became the father of Alaishah,
and Alaishah became the father Sasamay Sismai, and Sasamay became the father of Shalawam,
and Shalawam became the father of Yaqamayah, and Yaqamayah became the father of Alayashamai.
The ban (sons) of Kalab the ach (brother) of Yarachamaal were Mayashai his firstborn, who was the ab (father) of Zayap; and the ban (sons) of Maraashah the ab (father) of Chabarawan.
The ban (sons) of Chabarawan: Qarach, and Thapawach, and Raqam, and Shamai.
Shamai became the father of Racham, the father of Yaraqaim; and Raqam became the father of Shamay.
The ban (son) of Shamay was maiwan (maon); and maiwan (maon) was the ab (father) of Bayathatzawar Zur.
Iyapah, Kalab concubine, bore Charan, and Mawatzaa, and Gazaz; and Charan became the father of Gazaz.
The ban (sons) Yahaday Jahdai: Ragam, and Yawatham, and Gayashan, and Palat, and Iyapah, and Shaip.
Maikah, Kalab concubine, bore Shabar and Tharachanah.
She bore also Shaip the ab (father) of Madamanah, Shawaa the ab (father) Makabanaa Machbena, and the ab (father) Gabaia Gibea; and the bath (daughter) of Kalab was Ikasah.
These were the ban (sons) of Kalab, the ban (son) of Chawar, the firstborn of Ephrathah: Shawabal the ab (father) of Kiriath Qarayathayairayam,
Shalamaa the ab (father) of Bayathalacham, Charap the ab (father) of Bayathagadar Gader.
Shawabal the ab (father) of Kiriath Qarayathayairayam had ban (sons): Raah, chatzay (half) Chatzayahamanachawath the Menuhoth.
The mashapachah (families) of Kiriath Qarayathayairayam: The Yatharay, and the Pawathay, and the Shamathay, and the Masharaiy; of them came the Tzaraiy (Zorathites) and the Ashathaalay (Eshtaolites).
The ban (sons) of Shalamaa: Bayathalacham, and the Natapathay (Netophathites), Itarawath Beth itarawathabayathayawaab (joab), and chatzay (half) Chatzayahamanachathay the Manahathites, the Tzaraiy.

The mashapachah (families) of scribes who lived at Yaibatz: the Tharaithay, the Shamaithay, the Shawakathay. These are the Qayanay (Kenites) who came Chamath Hammath, the ab (father) of the bayath (house) of Rakab.

Now these were the ban (sons) of Dawad, who were yalad (born) to him in Chabarawan: the firstborn, Amanawan, of Achayanaim the Yazaraialayath; the shanay (second), Danayaal, Abayagayal Abigail the Karamalayath;
the shalayashay (third), Abayashalawam the ban (son) Maikah Maacah the bath (daughter) of Thalamay malak (king) of Gashawar; the rabayaiy (fourth), Adanayah the ban (son) of Chagayath;
the chamayashay (fifth), Shapatayah of Abayatal; the shashay (sixth), Yatharaim by Igalah his ashah (wife):

shash (six) were yalad (born) to him in Chabarawan; and there he reigned shabai (seven) Shanah and shash (six) chadash (months). In Yarawashalam he reigned shalawashayam (thirty) - shalawash (three) Shanah;
and these were yalad (born) to him in Yarawashalam: Shamaia, and Shawabab, and Nathan, and Shalamah, arabai (four), of Bathashawai the bath (daughter) of Imayaal;
and Yabachar, and Alayashamai, and Alayapalat,
and Nagah, and Napag, and Yapayai,
and Alayashamai, and Alayadai, and Alayapalat, thashai (nine).
All these were the ban (sons) of Dawad, besides the ban (sons) of the concubines; and Thamar was their achawath (sister).
Shalamah ban (son) was Rachabaim, Abayah his ban (son), Asaa his ban (son), Yahawashapat his ban (son),
Yawaram his ban (son), Achazayah his ban (son), Yawaash his ban (son),
Amatzayah his ban (son), Izarayah his ban (son), Yawatham his ban (son),
Achaz his ban (son), Chazaqayah his ban (son), Manashah his ban (son),
Amawan his ban (son), Yaashayah his ban (son).
The ban (sons) of Yaashayah: the firstborn Yawachanan, the shanay (second) Yahawayaqayam, the shalayashay (third) Tzadaqayah, the rabayaiy (fourth) Shalawam.
The ban (sons) of Yahawayaqayam: Yakanayah his ban (son), Tzadaqayah his ban (son).
The ban (sons) of Yakanayah, the Asayar: Shaalathayaal his ban (son),
and Malakayaram, and Padayah, and Shanaatzar, Yaqamayah, Hawashamai, and Nadabayah.
The ban (sons) of Padayah: Zarababal, and Shamaiy. The ban (sons) of Zarababal: Mashalam, and Chananayah; and Shalamayath was their achawath (sister);
and Chashabah, and Ahal, and Barakayah, and Chasadayah, Yawashabachasad Hesed, chamash (five).
The ban (sons) of Chananayah: Palatayah, and Yashaiyah; the ban (sons) of Rapayah, the ban (sons) of Aranan, the ban (sons) of Ibadayah, the ban (sons) of Shakanayah.
The ban (sons) of Shakanayah: Shamaiyah. The ban (sons) of Shamaiyah: Chatawash, and Yagaal, and Barayach, and Nairayah, and Shapat, shash (six).
The ban (sons) of Nairayah: Alayahawaiyanay, and Chazaqayah, and Izarayaqam, shalawash (three).
The ban (sons) Alayahawaiyanay Elioenai: Hawadayawahaw, and Alayashayab, and Palayah, and Iqawab, and Yawachanan, and Dalayah, and Inanay, shabai (seven).
The ban (sons) of Yahawadah (Judah): Paratz, Chatzarawan, and Karamay, and Chawar, and Shawabal.
Raayah the ban (son) of Shawabal became the father of Yachath; and Yachath became the father of Achawamay and Lahad. These are the mashapachah (families) of the Tzaraiy (Zorathites).
These were the sons of the ab (father) of Iyatam: Yazaraial, and Yashamaa, and Yadabash; and the sham (name) of their achawath (sister) was Tzalalapawanay;
and Panawaal the ab (father) of Gadar, and Izar the ab (father) of Chawashah. These are the ban (sons) of Chawar, the firstborn of Ephrathah, the ab (father) of Bayathalacham.
Ashachawar the ab (father) of Thaqawai had shanayam (two) wives, Chalaah and Nairah.
Nairah bore him Achazam, and Chapar, and Thayamanay, and Achashatharay. These were the ban (sons) of Nairah.
The ban (sons) of Chalaah were Tzarath, Tzachar, and Athanan.
Qawatz became the father of Inawab, and Tzababah, and the mashapachah (families) of Acharachal the ban (son) of Haram.
Yaibatz was more honorable than his ach (brothers): and his am (mother) sham (named) him Yaibatz, saying, "Because I bore him with itzab (sorrow).

Yaibatz called on the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "Oh that you would barak (bless) me barak (indeed), and enlarge my border, and that your yad (hand) might be with me, and that you would ishah (keep) me from rai (evil), that it not be to my sorrow!" Alahayam granted him that which he requested.
Kalawab the ach (brother) Shawachah Shuhah became the father of Machayar, who was the ab (father) of Ashathawan.
Ashathawan became the father of Bayatharapaa Rapha, and Pasach, and Thachanah the ab (father) Iyaranachash Ir Nahash. These are the men Rakah Recah.
The ban (sons) of Qanaz: Ithanayaal, and Sharayah. The ban (sons) of Ithanayaal: Chathath.
Maiwanathay became the father of Iparah: and Sharayah became the father of Yawaab the ab (father) Gayaa Ge Charashayam; Charash they were craftsmen.
The ban (sons) of Kalab the ban (son) of Yapanah: Iyaraw, Alah, and Naim; and the ban (sons) of Alah; and Qanaz.
The ban (sons) Yahalalaal Jehallelel: Zayap, and Zayapah, Thayarayaa, and Asharaal.
The ban (sons) of Izarah: Yathar, and Marad, and Ipar, and Yalawan; and she bore Marayam, and Shamay, and Yashabach the ab (father) of Ashathamai.

His ashah (wife) the Yahadayah bore Yarad the ab (father) of Gadar, and Chabar the ab (father) of Shawakah, and Yaqawathayaal the ab (father) of Zanawach. These are the ban (sons) of Bathayah the bath (daughter) of Paraih, whom Marad took.
The ban (sons) of the ashah (wife) of Hawadayah, the achawath (sister) of Nacham, were the ab (father) of Qaiyalah the Garamay, and Ashathamai the Maikathay (Maacathite).
The ban (sons) of Shayamawan: Amanawan, and Ranah, Banachanan Hanan, and Thawalawan. The ban (sons) of Yashaiy: Zawachath, and Ben Zawachath.

The ban (sons) of Shalah the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah): Ir the ab (father) of Lakah, and Laidah the ab (father) of Maraashah, and the mashapachah (families) of the bayath (house) of those who worked fine linen, of the bayath (house) of Ashabai;
and Yawaqayam, and the men Kazabaa Cozeba, and Yawaash, and Sharap, who had bail (dominion) in Mawaab, and Yashabayalacham. The records are Ithayaq.
These were the potters, and the yashab (inhabitants) Nataiyam Netaim and Gadarah: there they lived with the malak (king) for his malaakah (work).
The ban (sons) of Shamaiwan: Namawaal, and Yamayan, Yarayab, Zarach, Shaawal;
Shalawam his ban (son), Mabasham his ban (son), Mashamai his ban (son).
The ban (sons) of Mashamai: Chamawaal his ban (son), Zakawar his ban (son), Shamaiy his ban (son).

Shamaiy had sixteen ban (sons) and shash (six) bath (daughters); but his ach (brothers) didn't have many children, neither did all their mashapachah (family) multiply like the children of Yahawadah (Judah).
They lived Baarashabai Beersheba, and Mawaladah, and Chatzarashawail,
and at Balahah, and at Itzam, and at Thawalad,
and at Bathawaal, and at Charamah, and at Tzaqalag,
and Bayathahamarakabawath Beth Marcaboth, and Chatzarasawasayam Susim, and Bayathabaraay Beth Biri, and at Shairayam. These were their Iyar to the malak (reign) of Dawad.
Their villages were Iyatam, and Iyan, Ramawan, and Thakan, and Ishan, chamash (five) Iyar;
and all their villages that were around the same Iyar, to Bail. These were their habitations, and they have their genealogy.
Mashawabab, and Yamalak, and Yawashah the ban (son) of Amatzayah,
and Yawaal, and Yahawaa the ban (son) Yawashabayah Joshibiah, the ban (son) of Sharayah, the ban (son) of Ishayaal,
and Alayahawaiyanay, and Yaiqabah, and Yashawachayah, and Ishayah, and Idayaal, and Yashayamaal, and Banayah,
and Zayazaa the ban (son) of Shapaiy, the ban (son) of Alawan, the ban (son) of Yadayah, the ban (son) of Shamaray, the ban (son) of Shamaiyah—
these mentioned by sham (name) were nashayaa (princes) in their mashapachah (families): and their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses) increased greatly.
They went to the entrance of Gadar, even to the east side of the Gayaa, to seek pasture for their flocks.
They found Shaman pasture and tawab (good), and the aratz (land) was Rachab, and shaqat (quiet), and shalaw (peaceable); for those who lived there panayam (before) were of Cham.

These written by sham (name) came in the yawam (days) of Yachazaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and struck their ahal (tents), and the Meunim who were found there, and destroyed them utterly to this yawam (day), and lived in their place; because there was pasture there for their flocks.
