Some of them, even of the ban (sons) of Shamaiwan, chamash (five) maah (hundred) men, went to har (mount) Shaiyar, having for their raash (captains) Palatayah, and Nairayah, and Rapayah, and Izayaal, the ban (sons) of Yashaiy.
They struck the shaarayath (remnant) Imalaq the Amalekites who palayatah (escaped), and have lived there to this yawam (day).

The ban (sons) of Raawaban the firstborn of Yasharaal (Israel) (for he was the firstborn; but, because he defiled his ab (father's) couch, his birthright was given to the ban (sons) of Yawasap the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel); and the genealogy is not to be reckoned after the birthright.
For Yahawadah (Judah) prevailed above his ach (brothers), and of him came the nagayad (prince); but the birthright was Yawasap:)
the ban (sons) of Raawaban the firstborn of Yasharaal (Israel): Chanawak, and Palawaa, Chatzarawan, and Karamay.
The ban (sons) of Yawaal: Shamaiyah his ban (son), Gawag his ban (son), Shamaiy his ban (son),
Mayakah his ban (son), Raayah his ban (son), Bail his ban (son),
Baarah his ban (son), whom Thagalathapalaasar Pilneser malak (king) of Ashawar carried away captive: he was nashayaa (prince) of the Raawabanay (Reubenites).
His ach (brothers) by their mashapachah (families), when the genealogy of their thawaladah (generations) was reckoned: the raash (chief), Yaiyaal, and Zakarayah,
and Balai the ban (son) of Izaz, the ban (son) of Shamai, the ban (son) of Yawaal, who lived in Irawair, even to Nabaw and Bailamaiwan Meon:
and eastward he lived even to the entrance of the madabar (wilderness) from the nahar (river) Parath, because their livestock were multiplied in the aratz (land) of Galaid.
In the yawam (days) of Shaawal, they made war Hagaray the Hagrites, who napal (fell) by their yad (hand); and they lived in their ahal (tents) throughout all the mazarach (land) east of Galaid.
The ban (sons) of Gad lived over against them, in the aratz (land) of Bashan Salakah Salecah:
Yawaal the raash (chief), and Shapam the mashanah (second), and Yainay, and Shapat in Bashan.
Their ach (brothers) of their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses): Mayakaal, and Mashalam, and Shabai, and Yawaray, and Yaikan, and Zayai, and Ibar, shabai (seven).

These were the ban (sons) of Abayahayal, the ban (son) of Chawaray, the ban (son) of Yarawach, the ban (son) of Galaid, the ban (son) of Mayakaal, the ban (son) of Yashayashay, the ban (son) of Yachadaw, the ban (son) of Bawaz;
Achay the ban (son) of Ibadayaal, the ban (son) of Gawanay, raash (chief) of their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses).
They lived in Galaid in Bashan, and in its bath (towns), and in all the suburbs of Sharawan, as far as their borders.
All these were reckoned by genealogies in the yawam (days) of Yawatham malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the yawam (days) of Yarabaim malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).

The ban (sons) of Raawaban, and the Gaday (Gadites), and the half-tribe of Manashah, of valiant men, chayal (men) nashaa (able) to bear magan (buckler) and charab (sword), and to shoot with qashath (bow), and skillful in war, were arabaiyam (forty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) and shashayam (sixty), that were yatzaa (able) to go forth to tzabaa (war).
They made war Hagaray the Hagrites, with Yatawar, and Napayash, and Nawadab.

They were helped Hagaray them, and the Hagrites were delivered into their yad (hand), and all who were with them; for they cried to Alahayam in the battle, and he was entreated of them, because they batach (put) their trust in him.

They took away their livestock; of their camels chamashayam (fifty) alap (thousand), and of sheep two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) alap (thousand), and of donkeys two alap (thousand), and of men one maah (hundred) alap (thousand).
For there napal (fell) many Chalal, because the war was of Alahayam. They lived in their place until the captivity.
The children of the half-tribe of Manashah lived in the aratz (land): they increased from Bashan to Bailacharamawan Hermon and Shanayar and har (mount) Bailacharamawan.

These were the raash (heads) of their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses): even Ipar, and Yashaiy, and Alayaal, and Izarayaal, and Yaramayah, and Hawadawayah, and Yachadayaal, gabawar (mighty) men of valor, sham (famous) men, raash (heads) of their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses).

They trespassed against the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers), and played the prostitute achar (after) the Alahayam of the im (peoples) of the aratz (land), whom Alahayam destroyed panayam (before) them.

The Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) stirred up the rawach (spirit) of Pawal malak (king) of Ashawar, and the rawach (spirit) of Thagalathapalaasar Pilneser malak (king) of Ashawar, and he carried them away, even the Raawabanay (Reubenites), and the Gaday (Gadites), and the half-tribe of Manashah, and brought them to Chalach, and Chabawar, and Haraa, and to the nahar (river) of Gawazan, to this yawam (day).
The ban (sons) of Laway: Garashawan, Qahath, and Mararay.
The ban (sons) of Qahath: Imaram, Yatzahar, and Chabarawan, and Izayaal.
The children of Imaram: Aharawan, and Mashah, and Marayam. The ban (sons) of Aharawan: Nadab, and Abayahawaa, Alaizar, and Ayathamar.
Alaizar became the father of Payanachas, Payanachas became the father of Abayashawai,
and Abayashawai became the father of Baqay, and Baqay became the father of Izay,
and Izay became the father of Zarachayah, and Zarachayah became the father of Marayawath,
Marayawath became the father of Amarayah, and Amarayah became the father of Achayatawab,
and Achayatawab became the father of Tzadawaq, and Tzadawaq became the father of Achayamaitz,
and Achayamaitz became the father of Izarayah, and Izarayah became the father of Yawachanan,
and Yawachanan became the father of Izarayah, (he it is who executed the kahan (priest's) office in the bayath (house) that Shalamah built in Yarawashalam),
and Izarayah became the father of Amarayah, and Amarayah became the father of Achayatawab,
and Achayatawab became the father of Tzadawaq, and Tzadawaq became the father of Shalawam,
and Shalawam became the father Chalaqayah Hilkiah, and Chalaqayah became the father of Izarayah,
and Izarayah became the father of Sharayah, and Sharayah became the father of Yahawatzadaq;
Yahawatzadaq went into captivity, when Yahawah carried away Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam by the yad (hand) of Nabawakadanaatzar.
The ban (sons) of Laway: Garasham, Qahath, and Mararay.
These are the sham (names) of the ban (sons) of Garasham: Labanay and Shamaiy.
The ban (sons) of Qahath were Imaram, and Yatzahar, and Chabarawan, and Izayaal.
The ban (sons) of Mararay: Machalay and Mawashay. These are the mashapachah (families) Lawayay the Levites according to their abawath (fathers)' households.
Of Garasham: Labanay his ban (son), Yachath his ban (son), Zamah his ban (son),
Yawaach his ban (son), Idaw his ban (son), Zarach his ban (son), Yaatharay his ban (son).
The ban (sons) of Qahath: Imayanadab his ban (son), Qarach his ban (son), Asayar his ban (son),
Alaqanah his ban (son), and Abayasap his ban (son), and Asayar his ban (son),
Thachath his ban (son), Awarayaal his ban (son), Izayah his ban (son), and Shaawal his ban (son).
The ban (sons) of Alaqanah: Imashay, and Achayamawath.
As for Alaqanah, the ban (sons) of Alaqanah: Tzawap his ban (son), and Nachath his ban (son),
Alayaab his ban (son), Yaracham his ban (son), Alaqanah his ban (son).
The ban (sons) of Shamawaal: the firstborn Washanay, and the second Abayah.
The ban (sons) of Mararay: Machalay, Labanay his ban (son), Shamaiy his ban (son), Izaa his ban (son),
Shamaia his ban (son), Chagayah his ban (son), Ishayah his ban (son).
These are they whom Dawad imad (set) over the yad (service) of song in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, after that the arawan (ark) had manawach (rest).

They ministered with song panayam (before) the ahal (tabernacle) of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, until Shalamah had built the bayath (house) of Yahawah in Yarawashalam: and they waited on their ibadah (office) according to their mashapat (order).
These are those who waited, and their ban (sons). Of the ban (sons) of the Qahathay (Kohathites): Hayaman the singer, the ban (son) of Yawaal, the ban (son) of Shamawaal,
the ban (son) of Alaqanah, the ban (son) of Yaracham, the ban (son) of Alayaal, the ban (son) of Thawach,
the ban (son) of Tzawap, the ban (son) of Alaqanah, the ban (son) of Machath, the ban (son) of Imashay,
the ban (son) of Alaqanah, the ban (son) of Yawaal, the ban (son) of Izarayah, the ban (son) of Tzapanayah,
the ban (son) of Thachath, the ban (son) of Asayar, the ban (son) of Abayasap, the ban (son) of Qarach,
the ban (son) of Yatzahar, the ban (son) of Qahath, the ban (son) of Laway, the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel).
His ach (brother) Asap, who stood on his right yamayan (hand), even Asap the ban (son) of Barakayah, the ban (son) of Shamaia,
the ban (son) of Mayakaal, the ban (son) of Baishayah, the ban (son) of Malakayah,
the ban (son) of Athanay, the ban (son) of Zarach, the ban (son) of Idayah,
the ban (son) of Ayathan, the ban (son) of Zamah, the ban (son) of Shamaiy,
the ban (son) of Yachath, the ban (son) of Garasham, the ban (son) of Laway.
On the left shamaawal (hand) their ach (brothers) the ban (sons) of Mararay: Ayathan the ban (son) of Qayashay, the ban (son) of Ibaday, the ban (son) of Malawak,
the ban (son) of Chashabayah, the ban (son) of Amatzayah, the ban (son) Chalaqayah Hilkiah,
the ban (son) of Amatzay, the ban (son) of Banay, the ban (son) of Shamar,
the ban (son) of Machalay, the ban (son) of Mawashay, the ban (son) of Mararay, the ban (son) of Laway.
Their ach (brothers) the Lawayay (Levites) were appointed for all the ibadah (service) of the mashakan (tabernacle) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam.

But Aharawan and his ban (sons) offered on the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering), and on the mazabach (altar) of incense, for all the malaakah (work) of the most qadash (holy) place, and to make kapar (atonement) for Yasharaal (Israel), according to all that Mashah the ibad (servant) of Alahayam had tzawah (commanded).
These are the ban (sons) of Aharawan: Alaizar his ban (son), Payanachas his ban (son), Abayashawai his ban (son),
Baqay his ban (son), Izay his ban (son), Zarachayah his ban (son),
Marayawath his ban (son), Amarayah his ban (son), Achayatawab his ban (son),
Tzadawaq his ban (son), Achayamaitz his ban (son).

Now these are their mawashab (dwelling) places according to their encampments in their borders: to the ban (sons) of Aharawan, of the mashapachah (families) of the Qahathay (Kohathites) (for theirs was the gawaral (first) lot),
to them they gave Chabarawan in the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah), and its suburbs around it;
but the shadah (fields) of the Iyar, and its villages, they gave to Kalab the ban (son) of Yapanah.
To the ban (sons) of Aharawan they gave the Iyar of refuge, Chabarawan; Labanah also with its suburbs, and Yathayar, and Ashathamai with its suburbs,
and Chayalan with its suburbs, Dabayar with its suburbs,
and Ishan with its suburbs, and Bayathashamash Shemesh with its suburbs;

and out of the matah (tribe) of Banayamayan, Gabai with its suburbs, and Ilamath with its suburbs, and Inathawath with its suburbs. All their Iyar throughout their mashapachah (families) were thirteen Iyar.
To the rest of the ban (sons) of Qahath were given by lot, out of the mashapachah (family) of the matah (tribe), out of the half-tribe, the half of Manashah, ishar (ten) Iyar.

To the ban (sons) of Garasham, according to their mashapachah (families), out of the matah (tribe) of Yashashakar, and out of the matah (tribe) of Ashar, and out of the matah (tribe) of Napathalay, and out of the matah (tribe) of Manashah in Bashan, thirteen Iyar.

To the ban (sons) of Mararay were given by lot, according to their mashapachah (families), out of the matah (tribe) of Raawaban, and out of the matah (tribe) of Gad, and out of the matah (tribe) of Zabawalawan, shanayam (twelve) Iyar.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) gave Lawayay the Levites the Iyar with their suburbs.

They gave by lot out of the matah (tribe) of the children of Yahawadah (Judah), and out of the matah (tribe) of the children of Shamaiwan, and out of the matah (tribe) of the children of Banayamayan, these Iyar which are mentioned by sham (name).
Some of the mashapachah (families) of the ban (sons) of Qahath had Iyar of their borders out of the matah (tribe) of Aparayam.
They gave to them the Iyar of refuge, Shakam in the har (hill) country of Aparayam with its suburbs; Gazar also with its suburbs,
and Yaqamaim with its suburbs, and Bayathachawarawan Horon with its suburbs,
and Ayalawan with its suburbs, and Gatharamawan Rimmon with its suburbs;
and out of the half-tribe of Manashah, Inar with its suburbs, and Balaim with its suburbs, for the yathar (rest) of the mashapachah (family) of the ban (sons) of Qahath.
To the ban (sons) of Garasham were given, out of the mashapachah (family) of the half-tribe of Manashah, Gawalan in Bashan with its suburbs, and Ishatharawath with its suburbs;
and out of the matah (tribe) of Yashashakar, Qadash with its suburbs, dabarath (daberath) with its suburbs,
and Raamawath with its suburbs, and Inam with its suburbs;
and out of the matah (tribe) of Ashar, Mashal with its suburbs, and Ibadawan with its suburbs,
and chaqaq (hukok) with its suburbs, and Rachab with its suburbs;
and out of the matah (tribe) of Napathalay, Qadash in Galayal with its suburbs, and Chamawan with its suburbs, and Qarayathayam with its suburbs.
To the yathar (rest) of the Levites, the ban (sons) of Mararay, were given, out of the matah (tribe) of Zabawalawan, Ramawan with its suburbs, Thabawar with its suburbs;

and ibar (beyond) the Yaradan at Yarayachaw, on the east ibar (side) of the Yaradan, were given them, out of the matah (tribe) of Raawaban, Batzar in the madabar (wilderness) with its suburbs, and Yahatz with its suburbs,
and Qadamawath with its suburbs, and Mawapaith with its suburbs;
and out of the matah (tribe) of Gad, Raamawath in Galaid with its suburbs, and Machanayam with its suburbs,
and Chashabawan with its suburbs, and Yaizayar with its suburbs.
Of the ban (sons) of Yashashakar: Thawalai, and Pawaah, Yashawab, and Shamarawan, arabai (four).

The ban (sons) of Thawalai: Izay, and Rapayah, and Yarayaal, and Yachamay, and Yabasham, and Shamawaal, raash (heads) of their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), of Thawalai; mighty men of valor in their thawaladah (generations): their number in the yawam (days) of Dawad was isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) shash (six) maah (hundred).
The ban (sons) of Izay: Yazarachayah. The ban (sons) of Yazarachayah: Mayakaal, and Ibadayah, and Yawaal, Yashayah, chamash (five); all of them raash (chief) men.

With them, by their thawaladah (generations), after their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), were gadawad (bands) of the tzabaa (army) for war, shalawashayam (thirty) - shash (six) alap (thousand); for they had many wives and ban (sons).
Their ach (brothers) among all the mashapachah (families) of Yashashakar, mighty men of valor, reckoned in all by genealogy, were shamanayam (eighty) - shabai (seven) alap (thousand).
The sons of Banayamayan: Balai, and Bakar, and Yadayaial, shalawash (three).

The ban (sons) of Balai: Atzabawan, and Izay, and Izayaal, and Yarayamawath, and Iyaray, chamash (five); raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), gabawar (mighty) chayal (men) of valor; and they were reckoned by genealogy isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) shalawashayam (thirty) - arabai (four).
The ban (sons) of Bakar: Zamayarah, and Yawaish, and Alayaizar, and Alayahawaiyanay, and Imaray, and Yarayamawath, and Abayah, and Inathawath, and Ilamath. All these were the ban (sons) of Bakar.

They were reckoned by genealogy, after their thawaladah (generations), raash (heads) of their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), gabawar (mighty) men of valor, isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) two maah (hundred).
The ban (sons) of Yadayaial: Balahan. The ban (sons) of Balahan: Yaiyash, and Banayamayan, and Ahawad, and Kanainah, and Zayathan, and Tharashayash, and Achayashachar.

All these were ban (sons) of Yadayaial, according to the raash (heads) of their abawath (fathers)' households, gabawar (mighty) chayal (men) of valor, seventeen alap (thousand) and two maah (hundred), who were yatzaa (able) to go forth in the tzabaa (army) for tzabaa (war).
Shapayam also, and Chapayam, the ban (sons) of Iyar, Chawashayam, the ban (sons) of Achar.
The ban (sons) of Napathalay: Yachatzayaal, and Gawanay, and Yatzar, and Shalawam, the ban (sons) of Balahah.
The ban (sons) of Manashah: Asharayaal, whom his concubine the Aramay bore: she bore Makayar the ab (father) of Galaid:

and Makayar took a ashah (wife) of Chapayam and Shapayam, whose achawath (sister's) sham (name) was Maikah; and the sham (name) of the shanay (second) was Tzalapachad: and Tzalapachad had bath (daughters).
Maikah the ashah (wife) of Makayar bore a ban (son), and she sham (named) him Parash; and the sham (name) of his ach (brother) was Sharash; and his ban (sons) were Awalam and Raqam.
The ban (sons) of Awalam: Badan. These were the ban (sons) of Galaid the ban (son) of Makayar, the ban (son) of Manashah.
His achawath (sister) Malakath bore Ayashahawad, and Abayaizar, and Machalah.
The ban (sons) of Shamayadai were Achayan, and Shakam, and Laqachay, and Anayaim.
The ban (sons) of Aparayam: Shawathalach, and Barad his ban (son), and Thachath his ban (son), and Alaidah his ban (son), and Thachath his ban (son),

and Zabad his ban (son), and Shawathalach his ban (son), and Izar, and Alaid, whom the men of gath (gath) who were yalad (born) in the aratz (land) killed, because they came down to take away their livestock.
Aparayam their ab (father) mourned many yawam (days), and his ach (brothers) came to nacham (comfort) him.
He went in to his ashah (wife), and she conceived, and bore a ban (son), and he sham (named) him Barayaih, because it went rai (evil) with his bayath (house).
His bath (daughter) was Shaarah, who built Bayathachawarawan Horon the Thachathawan and the Ilayawan, and Azanashaarah Sheerah.
Rapach was his ban (son), and Rashap, and Thalach his ban (son), and Thachan his ban (son),
Laidan his ban (son), Imayahawad his ban (son), Alayashamai his ban (son),
Nawan his ban (son), Yahawashawai his ban (son).

Their achazah (possessions) and habitations were Bayathaal and its bath (towns), and eastward Nairan, and westward Gazar, with its bath (towns); Shakam also and its bath (towns), to Izah and its bath (towns);

and by the yad (borders) of the children of Manashah, Bayathashaan Shean and its bath (towns), Thainak and its bath (towns), Magadawan and its bath (towns), Dawar and its bath (towns). In these lived the children of Yawasap the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel).
The ban (sons) of Ashar: Yamanah, and Yashawah, and Yashaway, and Barayaih, and Sharach their achawath (sister).
The ban (sons) of Barayaih: Chabar, and Malakayaal, who was the ab (father) Barazawath Birzaith.
Chabar became the father of Yapalat, and Shawamar, and Chawatham, and Shawaia their achawath (sister).
The ban (sons) of Yapalat: Pasak, and Bamahal, and Ishawath. These are the children of Yapalat.
The ban (sons) of Shamar: Achay, and Rawahagah, Yachabah, and Aram.
The ban (sons) of Halam his ach (brother): Tzawapach, and Yamanai, and Shalash, and Imal.
The ban (sons) of Tzawapach: Sawach, and Charanapar, and Shawail, and Baray, and Yamarah,
Batzar, and Hawad, and Shamaa, and Shalashah, and Yatharan, and Baaraa.
The ban (sons) of Yathar: Yapanah, and Pasapah, and Araa.
The ban (sons) of Ilaa: Arach, and Chanayaal, and Ratzayaa.

All these were the children of Ashar, raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), Barar and gabawar (mighty) men of valor, raash (chief) of the nashayaa (princes). The number of them reckoned by genealogy for tzabaa (service) in war was isharayam (twenty) - shash (six) alap (thousand) men.
Banayamayan became the father of Balai his firstborn, Ashabal the shanay (second), and Acharach the shalayashay (third),
Nawachah the rabayaiy (fourth), and Rapaa the chamayashay (fifth).
Balai had ban (sons): Adar, and Garaa, and Abayahawad,
and Abayashawai, and Naiman, and Achawach,
and Garaa, and Shapawapam, and Chawaram.
These are the ban (sons) of Achawad: these are the raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households of the yashab (inhabitants) of Gabai, and they carried them captive to Manachath:
and Naiman, and Achayah, and Garaa, he carried them captive: and he became the father of Izaa and Achayachad.
Shacharayam became the father of children in the field of Mawaab, after he had sent them shalach (away); Chawashayam and Bairaa were his wives.
He became the father of Chadash his ashah (wife), Yawabab, and Tzabayaa, and Mayashaa, and Malakam,
and Yaiwatz, and Shabayah, and Maramah. These were his ban (sons), raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households.
Of Chawashayam he became the father of Abayatawab and Alapail.
The ban (sons) of Alapail: Ibar, and Mashaim, and Shamar, who built Awanaw and Lad, with its bath (towns);
and Barayaih, and Shamai, who were raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households of the yashab (inhabitants) of Ayalawan, who put to flight the yashab (inhabitants) of gath (gath);
and Achayaw, Shashaq, and Yarayamawath,
and Zabadayah, and Irad, and Idar,
and Mayakaal, and Yashapah, and Yawachaa, the ban (sons) of Barayaih,
and Zabadayah, and Mashalam, and Chazaqay, and Chabar,
and Yashamaray, and Yazalayaah, and Yawabab, the ban (sons) of Alapail,
and Yaqayam, and Zakaray, and Zabaday,
and Alayaiyanay, and Tzalathay, and Alayaal,
and Idayah, and Baraayah, and Shamarath, the ban (sons) of Shamaiy,
and Yashapan, and Ibar, and Alayaal,
and Ibadawan, and Zakaray, and Chanan,
and Chananayah, and Iyalam, and Inathathayah,
and Yapadayah, and Panawaal, the ban (sons) of Shashaq,
and Shamasharay, and Shacharayah, and Ithalayah,
and Yairashayah, and Alayah, and Zakaray, the ban (sons) of Yaracham.
These were raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households throughout their thawaladah (generations), raash (chief) men: these lived in Yarawashalam.
In Gabaiwan there lived the ab (father) of Gabaiwan, whose ashah (wife's) sham (name) was Maikah;
and his firstborn ban (son) Ibadawan, and Tzawar, and Qayash, and Bail, and Nadab,
and Gadar, and Achayaw, and Zakar.
Maqalawath became the father Shamaah Shimeah. They also lived with their ach (brothers) in Yarawashalam, over against their nagad (brothers).
Nar became the father of Qayash; and Qayash became the father of Shaawal; and Shaawal became the father of Yahawanathan, and Malakayashawai, and Abayanadab, and Ashabail.
The ban (son) of Yahawanathan was Marayababail Baal; and Marayababail Baal became the father of Mayakah.
The ban (sons) of Mayakah: Payathawan, and Malak, and Thaarai, and Achaz.
Achaz became the father Yahawaidah Jehoaddah; and Yahawaidah became the father of Ilamath, and Izamawath, and Zamaray; and Zamaray became the father of Mawatzaa.
Mawatzaa became the father of Banaia; Rapaa was his ban (son), Alaishah his ban (son), Atzal his ban (son).
Atzal had shash (six) ban (sons), whose sham (names) are these: Izarayaqam, Bakaraw, and Yashamaial, and Shairayah, and Ibadayah, and Chanan. All these were the ban (sons) of Atzal.
The ban (sons) of Ishaq his ach (brother): Awalam his firstborn, Yaiwash the shanay (second), and Alayapalat the shalayashay (third).

The ban (sons) of Awalam were gabawar (mighty) men of valor, archers, and had many ban (sons), and ban (sons)' ban (sons), one maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty). All these were of the ban (sons) of Banayamayan.

So all Yasharaal (Israel) were reckoned by genealogies; and behold, they are written in the book of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel): and Yahawadah (Judah) was carried away captive to Babal for their disobedience.
Now the raashawan (first) yashab (inhabitants) who lived in their achazah (possessions) in their Iyar were Yasharaal (Israel), the kahan (priests), the Lawayay (Levites), and the Nethinim.
In Yarawashalam lived of the children of Yahawadah (Judah), and of the children of Banayamayan, and of the children of Aparayam and Manashah:
Iwathay the ban (son) of Imayahawad, the ban (son) of Imaray, the ban (son) of Amaray, the ban (son) of Banay, of the children of Paratz the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah).
Of the Shayalawanay (Shilonites): Ishayah the firstborn, and his ban (sons).
Of the ban (sons) of Zarach: Yaiwaal, and their ach (brothers), shash (six) maah (hundred) thashaiyam (ninety).
Of the ban (sons) of Banayamayan: Salaw the ban (son) of Mashalam, the ban (son) of Hawadawayah, the ban (son) Sanawaah Hassenuah,
and Yabanayah the ban (son) of Yaracham, and Alah the ban (son) of Izay, the ban (son) of Makaray, and Mashalam the ban (son) of Shapatayah, the ban (son) of Raiwaal, the ban (son) of Yabanayah;

and their ach (brothers), according to their thawaladah (generations), thashai (nine) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) - shash (six). All these men were raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses).
Of the kahan (priests): Yadaiyah, and Yahawayarayab, Yakayan,

and Izarayah the ban (son) Chalaqayah Hilkiah, the ban (son) of Mashalam, the ban (son) of Tzadawaq, the ban (son) of Marayawath, the ban (son) of Achayatawab, the nagayad (ruler) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam;

and Idayah the ban (son) of Yaracham, the ban (son) Pashachawar Pashhur, the ban (son) of Malakayah, and Maishay the ban (son) of Idayaal, the ban (son) of Yachazarah, the ban (son) of Mashalam, the ban (son) of Mashalamayath, the ban (son) of Amar;

and their ach (brothers), raash (heads) of their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), one alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty); very chayal (able) men for the malaakah (work) of the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam.
Lawayay the Levites: Shamaiyah the ban (son) of Chashawab, the ban (son) of Izarayaqam, the ban (son) of Chashabayah, of the ban (sons) of Mararay;
and Baqabaqar, Charash, and Galal, and Mathanayah the ban (son) Mayakaa Mica, the ban (son) of Zakaray, the ban (son) of Asap,

and Ibadayah the ban (son) of Shamaiyah, the ban (son) of Galal, the ban (son) of Yadawathawan, and Barakayah the ban (son) of Asaa, the ban (son) of Alaqanah, who lived in the villages of the Natapathay (Netophathites).
The porters: Shalawam, and Iqawab, and Talamawan, and Achayaman, and their ach (brothers) (Shalawam was the raash (chief)),
who previously served in the malak (king's) gate eastward: they were the porters for the machanah (camp) of the children of Laway.

Shalawam the ban (son) of Qawaraa, the ban (son) of Abayasap, the ban (son) of Qarach, and his ach (brothers), of his ab (father's) bayath (house), the qarachay (korahites), were over the malaakah (work) of the ibadah (service), keepers of the thresholds of the ahal (tent): and their abawath (fathers) had been over the machanah (camp) of Yahawah, keepers of the entry.
Payanachas the ban (son) of Alaizar was nagayad (ruler) over them in panayam (time) past, and Yahawah was with him.
Zakarayah the ban (son) of Mashalamayah was porter of the door of the ahal (tent) of Meeting.

All these who were Barar to be porters in the thresholds were two maah (hundred) and shanayam (twelve). These were reckoned by genealogy in their villages, whom Dawad and Shamawaal the seer ordained in their amawanah (office) of trust.
So they and their children had the oversight of the gates of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, even the bayath (house) of the ahal (tent), by wards.
On the arabai (four) rawach (sides) were the porters, toward the east, yam (west), tzapawan (north), and Nagab.
Their ach (brothers), in their villages, were to bawaa (come) in every shabai (seven) yawam (days) from ith (time) to ith (time) to be with them:
for the arabai (four) gabawar (chief) porters, who were Lawayay (Levites), were in an amawanah (office) of trust, and were over the rooms and over the treasuries in the bayath (house) of Alahayam.
They lodged around the bayath (house) of Alahayam, because that duty was on them; and to them pertained its opening baqar (morning) by morning.
Certain of them were in charge of the vessels of service; for by count were these brought in and by count were these taken out.

Some of them also were appointed over the furniture, and over all the vessels of the qadash (sanctuary), and over the fine flour, and the yayan (wine), and the shaman (oil), and the frankincense, and the spices.
Some of the ban (sons) of the kahan (priests) prepared the confection of the spices.
Mathathayah, Lawayay of the Levites, who was the firstborn of Shalawam the qarachay (korahite), had the amawanah (office) of trust over the things that were baked in pans.
Some of their ach (brothers), of the ban (sons) of the Qahathay (Kohathites), were over the show lacham (bread), to kawan (prepare) it every shabath (sabbath).

These are the singers, raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' Lawayay of the Levites, who lived in the rooms and were free from other service; for they were employed in their malaakah (work) yawamam (day) and layal (night).
These were raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' Lawayay of the Levites, throughout their thawaladah (generations), raash (chief) men: these lived at Yarawashalam.
In Gabaiwan there lived the ab (father) of Gabaiwan, Yaiyaal, whose ashah (wife's) sham (name) was Maikah:
and his firstborn ban (son) Ibadawan, and Tzawar, and Qayash, and Bail, and Nar, and Nadab,
and Gadar, and Achayaw, and Zakarayah, and Maqalawath.
Maqalawath became the father of Shamaam. They also lived with their ach (brothers) in Yarawashalam, over against their ach (brothers).
Nar became the father of Qayash; and Qayash became the father of Shaawal; and Shaawal became the father of Yahawanathan, and Malakayashawai, and Abayanadab, and Ashabail.
The ban (son) of Yahawanathan was Marayababail Baal; and Marayababail Baal became the father of Mayakah.
The ban (sons) of Mayakah: Payathawan, and Malak, and Thacharai, and Ahaz.
Achaz became the father of Yairah; and Yairah became the father of Ilamath, and Izamawath, and Zamaray; and Zamaray became the father of Mawatzaa;
and Mawatzaa became the father of Banaia; and Rapayah his ban (son), Alaishah his ban (son), Atzal his ban (son).
Atzal had shash (six) ban (sons), whose sham (names) are these: Izarayaqam, Bakaraw, and Yashamaial, and Shairayah, and Ibadayah, and Chanan: these were the ban (sons) of Atzal.

Now the Palashathay (Philistines) fought against Yasharaal (Israel): and the men of Yasharaal (Israel) fled from panayam (before) the Palashathay (Philistines), and napal (fell) down Chalal on har (mount) Galabai.

The Palashathay (Philistines) followed hard achar (after) Shaawal and achar (after) his ban (sons); and the Palashathay (Philistines) killed Yawanathan, and Abayanadab, and Malakayashawai, the ban (sons) of Shaawal.
The battle went hard against Shaawal, and the archers overtook him; and he was distressed by reason of the archers.

Then Shaawal said to his armor bearer, "Draw your charab (sword), and thrust me through with it, lest these Iral bawaa (come) and ilal (abuse) me." But his armor bearer would not; for he was terrified. Therefore Shaawal took his charab (sword), and napal (fell) on it.
When his armor bearer saw that Shaawal was mawath (dead), he likewise napal (fell) on his charab (sword), and died.
So Shaawal died, and his shalawash (three) ban (sons); and all his bayath (house) died together.

When all the men of Yasharaal (Israel) who were in the valley saw that they fled, and that Shaawal and his ban (sons) were mawath (dead), they forsook their Iyar, and fled; and the Palashathay (Philistines) came and lived in them.
It happened on the next macharath (day), when the Palashathay (Philistines) came to strip the Chalal, that they found Shaawal and his ban (sons) fallen on har (mount) Galabai.

They stripped him, and took his raash (head), and his armor, and sent into the aratz (land) of the Palashathay (Philistines) all around, to bashar (carry) the news to their itzab (idols), and to the im (people).
They shawam (put) his armor in the bayath (house) of their Alahayam, and fastened his galagalath (head) in the bayath (house) of Dagawan.
When all Yabash Gilead heard all that the Palashathay (Philistines) had done to Shaawal,

all the chayal (valiant) men qawam (arose), and took nashaa (away) the body of Shaawal, and the bodies of his ban (sons), and brought them Yabash Jabesh, and buried their itzam (bones) under the oak Yabash Jabesh, and fasted shabai (seven) yawam (days).

So Shaawal died for his mail (trespass) which he committed against Yahawah, because of the dabar (word) of Yahawah, which he didn't shamar (keep); and also because he asked counsel of one who had a familiar awab (spirit), to inquire,
and didn't inquire of Yahawah: therefore he killed him, and turned the malawakah (kingdom) to Dawad the ban (son) of Yashay.
Then all Yasharaal (Israel) gathered themselves to Dawad to Chabarawan, saying, "Behold, we are your itzam (bone) and your flesh.

In thamawal (times) shalashawam (past), even when Shaawal was malak (king), it was you who led out and brought in Yasharaal (Israel). Yahawah your Alahayam said to you, ‘You shall be raih (shepherd) of my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), and you shall be nagayad (prince) over my gam (people) Yasharaal (Israel).'

So all the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) came to the malak (king) to Chabarawan; and Dawad made a barayath (covenant) with them in Chabarawan panayam (before) Yahawah; and they mashach (anointed) Dawad malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel), according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah by Shamawaal.
Dawad and all Yasharaal (Israel) went to Yarawashalam (the same is Yabawas); and the Yabawasay (Jebusites), the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land), were there.
The yashab (inhabitants) of Yabawas said to Dawad, "You shall not bawaa (come) in here." Nevertheless Dawad took the stronghold of Tzayawan. The same is the Iyar of Dawad.

Dawad said, "Whoever strikes the Yabawasay (Jebusites) raashawan (first) shall be raash (chief) and shar (captain)." Yawaab the ban (son) of Tzarawayah went up raashawan (first), and was made raash (chief).
Dawad lived in the stronghold; therefore they called it the Iyar of Dawad.
He built the Iyar all around, from Malawaa even around; and Yawaab repaired the shaar (rest) of the Iyar.
Dawad grew halak (greater) and halak (greater); for Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) was with him.

Now these are the raash (chief) of the gabawar (mighty) men whom Dawad had, who showed themselves chazaq (strong) with him in his malakawath (kingdom), together with all Yasharaal (Israel), to make him malak (king), according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah concerning Yasharaal (Israel).

This is the number of the gabawar (mighty) men whom Dawad had: Yashabaim, the son of a Chakamawanay (Hachmonite), the raash (chief) of the thirty; he lifted up his spear against shalawash (three) maah (hundred) and Chalal them at one paim (time).
achar (after) him was Alaizar the ban (son) of Dawadaw, the Achawachay (Ahohite), who was one of the shalawash (three) gabawar (mighty) men.

He was with Dawad at Pasadamayam, and there the Palashathay (Philistines) were gathered asap (together) to battle, where there was a plot of shadah (ground) Malaa of barley; and the im (people) fled from panayam (before) the Palashathay (Philistines).
They stood in the midst of the plot, and defended it, and killed the Palashathay (Philistines); and Yahawah saved them by a gadawal (great) thashawaih (victory).

shalawash (three) of the shalawashayam (thirty) raash (chief) men went down to the tzawar (rock) to Dawad, into the cave of Idalam; and the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines) were encamped in the valley of Rapaa (Rephaim).
Dawad was then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Palashathay (Philistines) was then in Bayathalacham.
Dawad longed, and said, "Oh that one would give me mayam (water) to shaqah (drink) of the bawar (well) of Bayathalacham, which is by the gate!

The shalawash (three) broke through the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and drew mayam (water) out of the bawar (well) of Bayathalacham, that was by the gate, and took it, and brought it to Dawad: but Dawad would not drink of it, but poured it out to Yahawah,

and said, "My Alahayam forbid it me, that I should do this! Shall I drink the dam (blood) of these men who have put their lives in napash (jeopardy)?" For they risked their lives to bawaa (bring) it. Therefore he would not drink it. The shalawash (three) gabawar (mighty) men did these things.

Abayashay, the ach (brother) of Yawaab, he was raash (chief) of the shalawash (three); for he lifted up his spear against shalawash (three) maah (hundred) and Chalal them, and had a sham (name) among the shalawash (three).
Of the shalawash (three), he was more honorable than the shanayam (two), and was made their shar (captain): however he didn't bawaa (attain) to the shalawash (three).

Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai, the ban (son) of a chayal (valiant) ayash (man) of Qabatzaal, who had done rab (mighty) pail (deeds), he killed the shanayam (two) Arayaal of Ariel of Mawaab: he went down also and killed a aray (lion) in the midst of a bawar (pit) in yawam (time) of snow.

He killed an Matzaray (Egyptian), a ayash (man) of great stature, chamash (five) amah (cubits) high; and in the Matzaray yad (hand) was a spear like a weaver's beam; and he went down to him with a shabat (staff), and plucked the spear out of the Matzaray yad (hand), and killed him with his own spear.
Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai did these things, and had a sham (name) among the shalawash (three) gabawar (mighty) men.
Behold, he was more honorable than the shalawashayam (thirty), but he didn't bawaa (attain) to the shalawash (three): and Dawad shawam (set) him over his guard.
Also the gabawar (mighty) men of the chayal (armies): Ishahaal the ach (brother) of Yawaab, Alachanan the ban (son) of Dawadaw of Bayathalacham,
Shamawath the Harawaray, Chalatz the Palawanay,
Iyaraa the ban (son) of Iqash the Thaqawaiy (Tekoite), Abayaizar the Inathathay (Anathothite),
Sabakay the Chashathay, Iyalay the Achawachay (Ahohite),
Maharay the Natapathay (Netophathite), Chalad the ban (son) of Bainah the Natapathay (Netophathite),
Athay the ban (son) of Rayabay of Gabaih of the children of Banayamayan, Banayah the Paraithawanay,
Chawaray of the nachal (brooks) of Gaish, Abayaal the Irabathay,
Izamawath the Bacharawamay, Alayachabaa the Shailabanay,
the ban (sons) of Hasham the Gazawanay, Yawanathan the ban (son) Shagaa Shagee the Hararay,
Achayaam the ban (son) of Shakar the Hararay, Alayapal the ban (son) of Awar,
Chapar the Makarathay, Achayah the Palawanay,
Chatzaraw the Karamalay, Nairay the ban (son) of Azabay,
Yawaal the ach (brother) of Nathan, Mabachar the ban (son) Hagaray Hagri,
Tzalaq the Imawanay (Ammonite), Nacharay the Barathay, the armor bearer of Yawaab the ban (son) of Tzarawayah,
Iyaraa the Yatharay, Garab the Yatharay,
Awarayah the Chathay (Hittite), Zabad the ban (son) of Achalay,
Idayanaa the ban (son) of Shayazaa the Raawabanay (Reubenite), a raash (chief) of the Raawabanay (Reubenites), and shalawashayam (thirty) with him,
Chanan the ban (son) Maikah Maacah, and Yawashapat the Mathanay,
Izayaa the Ishatharathay, Shamai and Yaiyaal the ban (sons) of Chawatham the Irairay,
Yadayaial the ban (son) of Shamaray, and Yawachaa his ach (brother), the Thayatzay,
Alayaal the Machawayam, and Yarayabay, and Yawashawayah, the ban (sons) of Alanaim, and Yathamah the Mawaabay (Moabite),
Alayaal, and Iwabad, and Yaishayaal the Matzabayah.

Now these are those who came to Dawad to Tzaqalag, while he yet kept himself itzar (close) panayam (because) of Shaawal the ban (son) of Qayash; and they were among the gabawar (mighty) men, his helpers in war.

They were armed with qashath (bows), and could use both the right yaman (hand) and the shamaal (left) in slinging aban (stones) and in shooting chatz (arrows) from the qashath (bow): they were of Shaawal ach (brothers) of Banayamayan.
The raash (chief) was Achayaizar; then Yawaash, the ban (sons) of Shamaih the Gabaithay, and Yazawaal, and Palat, the ban (sons) of Izamawath, and Barakah, and Yahawaa the Inathathay (Anathothite),

and Yashamaiyah the Gabainay (Gibeonite), a gabawar (mighty) man among the shalawashayam (thirty), and over the shalawashayam (thirty), and Yaramayah, and Yachazayaal, and Yawachanan, and Yawazabad the Gadarathay,
Alaiwazay, and Yarayamawath, and Bailayah, and Shamarayah, and Shapatayah the Charawapay,
Alaqanah, and Yashayah, and Izaraal, and Yawaizar, and Yashabaim, the qarachay (korahites),
and yawaialah (joelah), and Zabadayah, the ban (sons) of Yaracham of Gadar.

Of the Gaday (Gadites) there separated themselves to Dawad to the stronghold in the madabar (wilderness), mighty men of valor, men trained for war, that could handle tzanah (shield) and spear; whose panayam (faces) were like the panayam (faces) of aray (lions), and they were as swift as the tzabay (roes) on the har (mountains);
Izar the raash (chief), Ibadayah the shanay (second), Alayaab the shalayashay (third),
Mashamanah the rabayaiy (fourth), Yaramayah the chamayashay (fifth),
Ithay the shashay (sixth), Alayaal the shabayaiy (seventh),
Yawachanan the eighth, Alazabad the thashayaiy (ninth),
Yaramayah the ishayaray (tenth), Makabanay the ishathay (eleventh).
These of the ban (sons) of Gad were raash (captains) of the tzabaa (army): he who was qatan (least) was equal to one maah (hundred), and the greatest to one alap (thousand).

These are those who went over the Yaradan in the raashawan (first) chadash (month), when it had overflowed all its banks; and they put to flight all them of the valleys, both toward the east, and toward the west.
There came of the children of Banayamayan and Yahawadah (Judah) to the stronghold to Dawad.

Dawad went out to panayam (meet) them, and answered them, "If you have bawaa (come) peaceably to me to help me, my labab (heart) shall be knit to you; but if you have come to ramah (betray) me to my tzar (adversaries), since there is no wrong in my kap (hands), may the Alahayam of our abawath (fathers) raah (see) thereon, and yakach (rebuke) it.

Then the rawach (spirit) Labash on Imashay, who was raash (chief) of the shalawashayam (thirty), and he said, "We are yours, Dawad, and on your side, you ban (son) of Yashay: shalawam (peace), shalawam (peace) be to you, and shalawam (peace) be to your helpers; for your Alahayam helps you." Then Dawad received them, and made them raash (captains) of the gadawad (band).

Of Manashah also there napal (fell) away some to Dawad, when he came with the Palashathay (Philistines) against Shaawal to battle; but they didn't help them; for the lords of the Palashathay (Philistines) sent him away after consultation, saying, "He will napal (fall) away to his adawan (master) Shaawal to the jeopardy of our raash (heads).

As he went to Tzaqalag, there napal (fell) to him of Manashah, Idanah, and Yawazabad, and Yadayaial, and Mayakaal, and Yawazabad, and Alayahaw, and Tzalathay, raash (captains) of alap (thousands) who were of Manashah.
They helped Dawad against the gadawad (band) of rovers: for they were all gabawar (mighty) men of valor, and were shar (captains) in the tzabaa (army).
For from yawam (day) to yawam (day) men came to Dawad to help him, until there was a gadawal (great) machanah (army), like the machanah (army) of Alahayam.

These are the numbers of the raash (heads) of those who were chalatz (armed) for tzabaa (war), who came to Dawad to Chabarawan, to sabab (turn) the malakawath (kingdom) of Shaawal to him, according to the pah (word) of Yahawah.
The children of Yahawadah (Judah) who bore tzanah (shield) and spear were shash (six) alap (thousand) and shamanah (eight) maah (hundred), chalatz (armed) for tzabaa (war).
Of the children of Shamaiwan, gabawar (mighty) men of valor for the tzabaa (war), shabai (seven) alap (thousand) and one maah (hundred).
Of the children of Laway arabai (four) alap (thousand) and shash (six) maah (hundred).
Yahawayadai was the nagayad (leader) of the household of Aharawan; and with him were shalawash (three) alap (thousand) and shabai (seven) maah (hundred),
and Tzadawaq, a nair (young) man gabawar (mighty) of valor, and of his ab (father's) bayath (house) isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) shar (captains).
Of the children of Banayamayan, the ach (brothers) of Shaawal, shalawash (three) alap (thousand): for hitherto the greatest part of them had kept their allegiance to the bayath (house) of Shaawal.
Of the children of Aparayam isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) shamanah (eight) maah (hundred), gabawar (mighty) men of valor, sham (famous) men in their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses).
Of the half-tribe of Manashah eighteen alap (thousand), who were mentioned by sham (name), to bawaa (come) and make Dawad malak (king).

Of the children of Yashashakar, men who had bayanah (understanding) of the ith (times), to yadai (know) what Yasharaal (Israel) ought to do, their raash (heads) were two maah (hundred); and all their ach (brothers) were at their commandment.

Of Zabawalawan, such as were yatzaa (able) to go out in the tzabaa (army), who could set the battle in array, with all kinds of instruments of war, chamashayam (fifty) alap (thousand), and who could command and were not of lab (double) lab (heart).
Of Napathalay one alap (thousand) shar (captains), and with them with tzanah (shield) and spear shalawashayam (thirty) - shabai (seven) alap (thousand).
Of the Danay (Danites) who could set the battle in array, isharayam (twenty) - shamanah (eight) alap (thousand) shash (six) maah (hundred).
Of Ashar, such as were yatzaa (able) to go out in the tzabaa (army), who could set the battle in array, arabaiyam (forty) alap (thousand).

On the other ibar (side) of the Yaradan, of the Raawabanay (Reubenites), and the Gaday (Gadites), and of the chatzay (half) - shabat (tribe) of Manashah, with all kinds of instruments of tzabaa (war) for the battle, one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand).

All these being men of war, who could order the battle array, came with a Shalam lab (heart) to Chabarawan, to make Dawad malak (king) over all Yasharaal (Israel): and all the shaarayath (rest) also of Yasharaal (Israel) were of one labab (heart) to make Dawad malak (king).
They were there with Dawad shalawash (three) yawam (days), eating and drinking; for their ach (brothers) had made kawan (preparation) for them.

Moreover those who were qarawab (near) to them, as far as Yashashakar and Zabawalawan and Napathalay, brought lacham (bread) on donkeys, and on camels, and on mules, and on oxen, food of meal, cakes of figs, and clusters of raisins, and yayan (wine), and shaman (oil), and cattle, and sheep in abundance: for there was joy in Yasharaal (Israel).
Dawad consulted with the shar (captains) of alap (thousands) and of maah (hundreds), even with every nagayad (leader).

Dawad said to all the qahal (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel), "If it seems tawab (good) to you, and if it is of Yahawah our Alahayam, let us shalach (send) abroad everywhere to our ach (brothers) who are shaar (left) in all the aratz (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), with whom the kahan (priests) and Lawayay (Levites) are in their Iyar that have suburbs, that they may gather themselves to us;
and let us sabab (bring) again the arawan (ark) of our Alahayam to us. For we didn't seek it in the yawam (days) of Shaawal.
All the qahal (assembly) said that they would do so; for the thing was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of all the im (people).

So Dawad assembled all Yasharaal (Israel) together, from the Shayachawar the brook of Matzarayam even to the entrance of Chamath, to bawaa (bring) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam from Kiriath Qarayathayairayam.

Dawad went up, and all Yasharaal (Israel), to Bailah, that is, to Kiriath Qarayathayairayam, which belonged to Yahawadah (Judah), to ilah (bring) up from there the arawan (ark) of Alahayam Yahawah that yashab (sits) above the karawab (cherubim), that is called by the sham (name).
They carried the arawan (ark) of Alahayam on a Chadash cart, and brought it out of the bayath (house) of Abayanadab: and Izaa and Achayaw drove the cart.

Dawad and all Yasharaal (Israel) played panayam (before) Alahayam with all their might, even with songs, and with harps, and with stringed instruments, and with tambourines, and with cymbals, and with trumpets.
When they came to the threshing floor of Kayadawan, Izaa shalach (put) forth his yad (hand) to achaz (hold) the arawan (ark); for the oxen stumbled.
The ap (anger) of Yahawah was kindled against Izaa, and he struck him, because he shalach (put) forth his yad (hand) to the arawan (ark); and there he died panayam (before) Alahayam.
Dawad was charah (displeased), because Yahawah had broken forth on Izaa; and he called that place Perez Izaa, to this yawam (day).
Dawad was yaraa (afraid) of Alahayam that yawam (day), saying, "How shall I bawaa (bring) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam home to me?
So Dawad didn't move the arawan (ark) to him into the Iyar of Dawad, but carried it natah (aside) into the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam the Gathay (Gittite).

The arawan (ark) of Alahayam remained with the bayath (family) of Ibadaadawam in his bayath (house) shalawash (three) chadash (months): and Yahawah blessed the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam, and all that he had.
Chayaram malak (king) of Tzar sent malaak (messengers) to Dawad, and cedar itz (trees), and masons, and carpenters, to banah (build) him a bayath (house).
Dawad perceived that Yahawah had established him malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel); for his malakawath (kingdom) was exalted on high, for his im (people) Yasharaal sake.
Dawad took more wives at Yarawashalam; and Dawad became the father of more ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
These are the sham (names) of the yalad (children) whom he had in Yarawashalam: Shamawai, and Shawabab, Nathan, and Shalamah,
and Yabachar, and Alayashawai, and Alayapalat,
and Nagah, and Napag, and Yapayai,
and Alayashamai, and Bailayadai, and Alayapalat.

When the Palashathay (Philistines) heard that Dawad was mashach (anointed) malak (king) over all Yasharaal (Israel), all the Palashathay (Philistines) went up to seek Dawad: and Dawad heard of it, and went out panayam (against) them.
Now the Palashathay (Philistines) had bawaa (come) and made a raid in the valley of Rapaa (Rephaim).

Dawad inquired of Alahayam, saying, "Shall I ilah (go) up against the Palashathay (Philistines)? Will you nathan (deliver) them into my yad (hand)?" Yahawah said to him, "ilah (go) up; for I will nathan (deliver) them into your yad (hand).

So they came up to Bailaparatzayam Perazim, and Dawad struck them there; and Dawad said, Alahayam has broken my ayab (enemies) by my yad (hand), like the breach of mayam (waters). Therefore they called the sham (name) of that place Bailaparatzayam Perazim.
They left their Alahayam there; and Dawad gave commandment, and they were burned with ash (fire).
The Palashathay (Philistines) yet again made a raid in the valley.
Dawad inquired again of Alahayam; and Alahayam said to him, "You shall not ilah (go) up achar (after) them. sabab (turn) away from them, and bawaa (come) on them over against the mulberry trees.

It shall be, when you hear the qawal (sound) of marching in the raash (tops) of the mulberry trees, that then you shall yatzaa (go) out to battle; for Alahayam has gone out panayam (before) you to strike the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines).
Dawad did as Alahayam tzawah (commanded) him: and they struck the machanah (army) of the Palashathay (Philistines) from Gabaiwan even to Gazar.
The sham (fame) of Dawad went out into all aratz (lands); and Yahawah brought the pachad (fear) of him on all gawayam (nations).
David made him bayath (houses) in the Iyar of Dawad; and he prepared a place for the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, and pitched for it a ahal (tent).

Then Dawad said, "No one ought to nashaa (carry) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam Lawayay the Levites. For Yahawah has chosen them to nashaa (carry) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, and to sharath (minister) to him iwalam (forever).
Dawad assembled all Yasharaal (Israel) at Yarawashalam, to ilah (bring) up the arawan (ark) of Yahawah to its place, which he had prepared for it.
Dawad gathered together the ban (sons) of Aharawan, and the Lawayay (Levites):
of the ban (sons) of Qahath, Awarayaal the shar (chief), and his ach (brothers) one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty);
of the ban (sons) of Mararay, Ishayah the shar (chief), and his ach (brothers) two maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty);
of the ban (sons) of Garasham, Yawaal the shar (chief), and his ach (brothers) one maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty);
of the ban (sons) of Alayatzapan, Shamaiyah the shar (chief), and his ach (brothers) two maah (hundred);
of the ban (sons) of Chabarawan, Alayaal the shar (chief), and his ach (brothers) shamanayam (eighty);
of the ban (sons) of Izayaal, Imayanadab the shar (chief), and his ach (brothers) one maah (hundred) shanayam (twelve).
Dawad called for Tzadawaq and Abayathar the kahan (priests), and Lawayay the Levites, for Awarayaal, Ishayah, and Yawaal, Shamaiyah, and Alayaal, and Imayanadab,

and said to them, "You are the raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' Lawayay of the Levites. qadash (sanctify) yourselves, both you and your ach (brothers), that you may ilah (bring) up the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), to the place that I have prepared for it.
For because you didn't carry it at raashawan (first), Yahawah our Alahayam made broke out against us, because we didn't seek him according to the mashapat (ordinance).
So the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites) sanctified themselves to ilah (bring) up the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
The children Lawayay the Levites bore the arawan (ark) of Alahayam on their shoulders with the poles thereon, as Mashah tzawah (commanded) according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah.

Dawad spoke to the shar (chief) Lawayay the Levites to imad (appoint) their ach (brothers) the singers, with instruments of music, stringed instruments and harps and cymbals, sounding aloud and lifting up the qawal (voice) with joy.

So the Lawayay (Levites) appointed Hayaman the ban (son) of Yawaal; and of his ach (brothers), Asap the ban (son) of Barakayah; and of the ban (sons) of Mararay their ach (brothers), Ayathan the ban (son) of Qawashayahaw;

and with them their ach (brothers) of the mashanah (second) degree, Zakarayah, Ban, and Yaizayaal, and Shamayaramawath, and Yachayaal, and Inay, Alayaab, and Banayah, and Maishayah, and Mathathayah, and Alayapalahaw, and Maqanayahaw, and Ibadaadawam, and Yaiyaal, the doorkeepers.
So the singers, Hayaman, Asap, and Ayathan, were given cymbals of brass to sound aloud;
and Zakarayah, and Izayaal, and Shamayaramawath, and Yachayaal, and Inay, and Alayaab, and Maishayah, and Banayah, with stringed instruments set to Alamoth;
and Mathathayah, and Alayapalahaw, and Maqanayahaw, and Ibadaadawam, and Yaiyaal, and Izazayahaw, with harps Shamayanayath to the eight-stringed lyre, to lead.
Kananayah, shar (chief) Lawayay the Levites, was over the mashaa (song): he instructed about the mashaa (song), because he was skillful.
Barakayah and Alaqanah were doorkeepers for the arawan (ark).

Shabanayah, and Yawashapat, and Nathanaal, and Imashay, and Zakarayah, and Banayah, and Alayaizar, the kahan (priests), blew the trumpets panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of Alahayam: and Ibadaadawam and Yachayah were doorkeepers for the arawan (ark).

So Dawad, and the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel), and the shar (captains) over alap (thousands), went to ilah (bring) up the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah out of the bayath (house) of Ibadaadawam with joy.
It happened, when Alahayam helped the Lawayay (Levites) who bore the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, that they sacrificed shabai (seven) bulls and shabai (seven) ayal (rams).

Dawad was clothed with a robe of fine linen, and all the Lawayay (Levites) who bore the arawan (ark), and the singers, and Kananayah the shar (master) of the mashaa (song) with the singers: and Dawad had on him an apawad (ephod) of linen.

Thus all Yasharaal (Israel) brought up the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah with shouting, and with qawal (sound) of the cornet, and with trumpets, and with cymbals, sounding aloud with stringed instruments and harps.

It happened, as the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah came to the Iyar of Dawad, that Mayakal the bath (daughter) of Shaawal looked out at the window, and saw malak (king) Dawad dancing and playing; and she despised him in her lab (heart).

They brought in the arawan (ark) of Alahayam, and set it in the midst of the ahal (tent) that Dawad had pitched for it: and they offered burnt ilah (offerings) and shalam (peace) offerings panayam (before) Alahayam.
When Dawad had made an kalah (end) of offering the burnt ilah (offering) and the shalam (peace) offerings, he blessed the im (people) in the sham (name) of Yahawah.
He dealt to everyone of Yasharaal (Israel), both ayash (man) and ashah (woman), to ayash (every) one a loaf of lacham (bread), and a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins.

He appointed Lawayay of the Levites to sharath (minister) panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of Yahawah, and to celebrate and to yadah (thank) and halal (praise) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel):

Asap the raash (chief), and mashanah (second) to him Zakarayah, Yaiyaal, and Shamayaramawath, and Yachayaal, and Mathathayah, and Alayaab, and Banayah, and Ibadaadawam, and Yaiyaal, with stringed instruments and with harps; and Asap with cymbals, sounding aloud;
and Banayah and Yachazayaal the kahan (priests) with trumpets continually, panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Alahayam.
Then on that yawam (day) Dawad raash (first) ordained to give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah, by the yad (hand) of Asap and his ach (brothers).
Oh give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah. qaraa (call) on his sham (name). Make his ilayalah (doings) yadai (known) among the im (peoples).
shayar (sing) to him. Sing zamar (praises) to him. Tell of all his marvelous palaa (works).
Glory in his qadash (holy) sham (name). Let the lab (heart) of those who seek Yahawah Shamach.
Seek Yahawah and his iz (strength). Seek his panayam (face) thamayad (forever) more.
zakar (remember) his palaa (marvelous) ishah (works) that he has done, his mawapath (wonders), and the mashapat (judgments) of his pah (mouth),
you zarai (seed) of Yasharaal (Israel) his ibad (servant), you children of Yaiqab, his Bachayar ones.
He is Yahawah our Alahayam. His mashapat (judgments) are in all the aratz (earth).
zakar (remember) his barayath (covenant) iwalam (forever), the dabar (word) which he tzawah (commanded) to a alap (thousand) dawar (generations),
the karath (covenant) which he made with Abaraham, his shabawaih (oath) to Yatzachaq.
He confirmed the same to Yaiqab for a chaq (statute), and to Yasharaal (Israel) for an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant),
saying, "I will nathan (give) you the aratz (land) of Kanain, The lot of your nachalah (inheritance),
when you were but a few men in number, yes, very Mait, and foreigners were in it.
They went about from gaway (nation) to gaway (nation), from one mamalakah (kingdom) to achar (another) im (people).
He allowed no ayash (man) to do them wrong. Yes, he reproved malak (kings) for their sakes,
"Don't nagai (touch) my mashayach (anointed) ones! Do my nabayaa (prophets) no raii (harm)!
shayar (sing) to Yahawah, all the aratz (earth)! Display his yashawaih (salvation) from yawam (day) to yawam (day).
Declare his kabawad (glory) among the gawayam (nations), and his marvelous palaa (works) among all the im (peoples).
For gadawal (great) is Yahawah, and maad (greatly) to be praised. He also is to be feared above all Alahayam.
For all the Alahayam of the im (peoples) are idols, but Yahawah made the shamayam (heavens).
Honor and hawad (majesty) are panayam (before) him. iz (strength) and gladness are in his place.
Ascribe to Yahawah, you relatives of the im (peoples), ascribe to Yahawah kabawad (glory) and iz (strength)!
Ascribe to Yahawah the kabawad (glory) due to his sham (name). nashaa (bring) an manachah (offering), and bawaa (come) panayam (before) him. shachah (worship) Yahawah in qadash (holy) array.
chawal (tremble) panayam (before) him, all the aratz (earth). The world also is established that it can't be moved.
Let the shamayam (heavens) be Shamach, and let the aratz (earth) rejoice! Let them amar (say) among the gawayam (nations), "Yahawah malak (reigns)!
Let the yam (sea) roar, and its fullness! Let the shadah (field) exult, and all that is therein!
Then the itz (trees) of the Yair will sing for joy panayam (before) Yahawah, for he bawaa (comes) to shapat (judge) the aratz (earth).
Oh give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah, for he is tawab (good), for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever).

amar (say), "yashai (save) us, Alahayam of our yashai (salvation)! Gather us together and natzal (deliver) us from the gawayam (nations), to give yadah (thanks) to your qadash (holy) sham (name), to shabach (triumph) in your thahalah (praise).
Blessed be Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), from iwalam (forever) even to iwalam (forever). All the im (people) said, "aman (amen)," and praised Yahawah.

So he left there, panayam (before) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, Asap and his ach (brothers), to sharath (minister) panayam (before) the arawan (ark) continually, as every yawam (day's) dabar (work) yawam (required);
and Ibadaadawam with their ach (brothers), shashayam (sixty) - shamanah (eight); Ibadaadawam also the ban (son) of Yadawathawan and Chasah to be doorkeepers;
and Tzadawaq the kahan (priest), and his ach (brothers) the kahan (priests), panayam (before) the mashakan (tabernacle) of Yahawah in the bamah (high) place that was at Gabaiwan,

to ilah (offer) burnt ilah (offerings) to Yahawah on the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering) continually baqar (morning) and evening, even according to all that is written in the thawarah (law) of Yahawah, which he tzawah (commanded) to Yasharaal (Israel);

and with them Hayaman and Yadawathawan, and the shaar (rest) who were Barar, who were mentioned by sham (name), to give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah, because his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever);

and with them Hayaman and Yadawathawan with trumpets and cymbals for those that should sound aloud, and with instruments for the songs of Alahayam; and the ban (sons) of Yadawathawan to be at the gate.
All the im (people) departed every ayash (man) to his bayath (house): and Dawad returned to barak (bless) his bayath (house).

It happened, when Dawad lived in his bayath (house), that Dawad said to Nathan the nabayaa (prophet), "Behold, I yashab (dwell) in a bayath (house) of cedar, but the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah is under curtains.
Nathan said to Dawad, "Do all that is in your labab (heart); for Alahayam is with you.
It happened the same layal (night), that the dabar (word) of Alahayam came to Nathan, saying,
"yalak (go) and amar (tell) Dawad my ibad (servant), ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "You shall not banah (build) me a bayath (house) to yashab (dwell) in;

for I have not lived in a bayath (house) since the yawam (day) that I brought up Yasharaal (Israel), to this yawam (day), but have gone from ahal (tent) to ahal (tent), and from one mashakan (tent) to another.

In all halak (places) in which I have walked with all Yasharaal (Israel), did I dabar (speak) a dabar (word) with any of the shapat (judges) of Yasharaal (Israel), whom I tzawah (commanded) to be raih (shepherd) of my im (people), saying, ‘Why have you not built me a bayath (house) of cedar?'"'

"Now therefore, you shall amar (tell) my ibad (servant) Dawad, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "I took you Nawah the sheep pen, from following the sheep, that you should be nagayad (prince) over my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel).

I have been with you wherever you have gone, and have karath (cut) off all your ayab (enemies) from panayam (before) you. I will ishah (make) you a sham (name), like the sham (name) of the gadawal (great) ones who are in the aratz (earth).

I will shawam (appoint) a place for my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), and will plant them, that they may shakan (dwell) in their own place, and be moved no more; neither shall the children of iwal (wickedness) waste them any more, as at the raashawan (first),

and from the yawam (day) that I tzawah (commanded) shapat (judges) to be over my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel); and I will subdue all your ayab (enemies). Moreover I nagad (tell) you that Yahawah will banah (build) you a bayath (house).

It shall happen, when your yawam (days) are fulfilled that you must yalak (go) to be with your abawath (fathers), that I will qawam (set) up your zarai (seed) achar (after) you, who shall be of your ban (sons); and I will kawan (establish) his malakawath (kingdom).
He shall banah (build) me a bayath (house), and I will kawan (establish) his kasaa (throne) iwalam (forever).
I will be his ab (father), and he shall be my ban (son). I will not sawar (take) my loving chasad (kindness) sawar (away) from him, as I took it from him that was panayam (before) you;
but I will settle him in my bayath (house) and in my malakawath (kingdom) iwalam (forever). His kasaa (throne) shall be established iwalam (forever)."'
According to all these dabar (words), and according to all this vision, so Nathan spoke to Dawad.
Then Dawad the malak (king) went in, and sat panayam (before) Yahawah; and he said, "Who am I, Yahawah Alahayam, and what is my bayath (house), that you have brought me thus far?

This was a small thing in your iyan (eyes), Alahayam; but you have spoken of your ibad (servant's) bayath (house) for a Rachawaq while to come, and have respected me according to the estate of a adam (man) of high degree, Yahawah Alahayam.
What can Dawad say yet more to you concerning the honor which is done to your ibad (servant)? For you yadai (know) your ibad (servant).
Yahawah, for your ibad (servant's) sake, and according to your own lab (heart), you have worked all this greatness, to yadai (make) known all these great things.
Yahawah, there is none like you, neither is there any Alahayam zawalah (besides) you, according to all that we have heard with our ears.

What one gaway (nation) in the aratz (earth) is like your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), whom Alahayam went to padah (redeem) to himself for a im (people), to shawam (make) you a sham (name) by great and awesome things, in driving out gaway (nations) from panayam (before) your im (people), whom you padah (redeem) out of Matzarayam?
For your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel) you made your own im (people) iwalam (forever); and you, Yahawah, became their Alahayam.
Now, Yahawah, let the dabar (word) that you have spoken concerning your ibad (servant), and concerning his bayath (house), be established iwalam (forever), and do as you have spoken.

Let your sham (name) be established and magnified iwalam (forever), saying, ‘Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) is the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), even a Alahayam to Yasharaal (Israel). The bayath (house) of Dawad your ibad (servant) is established panayam (before) you.'
For you, my Alahayam, have revealed to your ibad (servant) that you will banah (build) him a bayath (house). Therefore your ibad (servant) has found courage to palal (pray) panayam (before) you.
Now, Yahawah, you are Alahayam, and have promised this tawab (good) thing to your ibad (servant).

Now it has pleased you to barak (bless) the bayath (house) of your ibad (servant), that it may continue iwalam (forever) panayam (before) you; for you, Yahawah, have blessed, and it is blessed iwalam (forever).
achar (after) this it happened, that Dawad struck the Palashathay (Philistines), and subdued them, and took gath (gath) and its bath (towns) out of the yad (hand) of the Palashathay (Philistines).
He struck Mawaab; and the Mawaab (Moabites) became ibad (servants) to Dawad, and brought tribute.
Dawad struck Hadadezer malak (king) of Tzawabaa to Chamath, as he went to natzab (establish) his yad (dominion) by the nahar (river) Parath.

Dawad took from him one alap (thousand) chariots, and shabai (seven) alap (thousand) horsemen, and isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) footmen; and Dawad hamstrung all the chariot horses, but reserved of them for one maah (hundred) chariots.
When the Syrians of Damascus came to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David struck of the Syrians twenty-two thousand men.
Then Dawad shawam (put) garrisons in Aram of Damascus; and the Aram (Syrians) became ibad (servants) to Dawad, and brought tribute. Yahawah gave yashai (victory) to Dawad wherever he went.
Dawad took the shalat (shields) of gold that were on the ibad (servants) of Hadadezer, and brought them to Yarawashalam.
From Tabachath and Kawan Cun, Iyar of Hadadezer, Dawad took very much brass, with which Shalamah made the bronze yam (sea), and the pillars, and the vessels of brass.
When Thaiw malak (king) of Chamath heard that Dawad had struck all the chayal (army) of Hadadezer malak (king) of Tzawabaa,

he sent Hadawaram his ban (son) to malak (king) Dawad, to shaal (greet) him, and to barak (bless) him, because he had fought against Hadadezer and struck him; (for Hadadezer had wars with Thaiw;) and he had with him all kinds of vessels of gold and kasap (silver) and brass.

malak (king) Dawad also dedicated these to Yahawah, with the kasap (silver) and the gold that he carried away from all the gawayam (nations); from Adam, and from Mawaab, and from the children of Imawan, and from the Palashathay (Philistines), and from Imalaq.
Moreover Abayashay the ban (son) of Tzarawayah struck of the Adam (Edomites) in the Gayaa of Malach eighteen alap (thousand).
He shawam (put) garrisons in Adam; and all the Adam (Edomites) became ibad (servants) to Dawad. Yahawah gave yashai (victory) to Dawad wherever he went.
Dawad reigned over all Yasharaal (Israel); and he executed justice and tzadaqah (righteousness) to all his im (people).
Yawaab the ban (son) of Tzarawayah was over the tzabaa (army); and Yahawashapat the ban (son) of Achayalawad was zakar (recorder);
and Tzadawaq the ban (son) of Achayatawab, and Abayamalak the ban (son) of Abayathar, were kahan (priests); and Shawashaa was scribe;
and Banayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai was over the Karathay (Cherethites) and the Palathay (Pelethites); and the ban (sons) of Dawad were chief yad (about) the malak (king).
It happened achar (after) this, that Nachash the malak (king) of the children of Imawan died, and his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Dawad said, "I will show chasad (kindness) to Chanawan the ban (son) of Nachash, because his ab (father) showed chasad (kindness) to me." So Dawad sent malaak (messengers) to nacham (comfort) him concerning his ab (father). Dawad ibad (servants) came into the aratz (land) of the children of Imawan to Chanawan, to nacham (comfort) him.

But the shar (princes) of the children of Imawan said to Chanawan, "Do you iyan (think) that Dawad honors your ab (father), in that he has sent comforters to you? Haven't his ibad (servants) bawaa (come) to you to search, to hapak (overthrow), and to spy out the aratz (land)?
So Chanawan took Dawad ibad (servants), and shaved them, and karath (cut) off their garments in the chatzay (middle), even to their buttocks, and sent them shalach (away).

Then there went certain persons, and told Dawad how the men were served. He sent to qaraah (meet) them; for the men were maad (greatly) kalam (ashamed). The malak (king) said, "Stay at Yarayachaw until your beards have grown, and then shawab (turn back / repent).

When the children of Imawan saw that they had made themselves baash (odious) to Dawad, Chanawan and the children of Imawan sent one alap (thousand) talents of kasap (silver) to hire them chariots and horsemen out of Aramanaharayam, and Aram of Arammaacah, and out of Tzawabaa.

So they hired for themselves shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) chariots, and the malak (king) Maikah Maacah and his im (people), who came and encamped panayam (before) Mayadabaa. The children of Imawan gathered themselves asap (together) from their Iyar, and came to battle.
When Dawad heard of it, he sent Yawaab, and all the tzabaa (army) of the gabawar (mighty) men.
The children of Imawan came out, and put the battle in array at the gate of the Iyar: and the malak (kings) who had bawaa (come) were by themselves in the shadah (field).
Now when Yawaab saw that the battle was set panayam (against) him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Yasharaal (Israel), and put them in array qaraah (against) the Aram (Syrians).
The yathar (rest) of the im (people) he committed into the yad (hand) of Abayashay his ach (brother); and they put themselves in array qaraah (against) the children of Imawan.
He said, "If the Aram (Syrians) are too chazaq (strong) for me, then you are to thashawaih (help) me; but if the children of Imawan are too chazaq (strong) for you, then I will yashai (help) you.
Be courageous, and let us be chazaq (strong) for our im (people), and for the Iyar of our Alahayam. May Yahawah do that which seems tawab (good) to him.
So Yawaab and the im (people) who were with him drew near panayam (before) the Aram (Syrians) to the battle; and they fled panayam (before) him.
When the children of Imawan saw that the Aram (Syrians) had fled, they likewise fled panayam (before) Abayashay his ach (brother), and entered into the Iyar. Then Yawaab came to Yarawashalam.

When the Aram (Syrians) saw that they were defeated by Yasharaal (Israel), they sent malaak (messengers), and drew yatzaa (forth) the Aram (Syrians) who were ibar (beyond) the nahar (river), with Shawapak the shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army) of Hadadezer at their head.

It was told Dawad; and he gathered all Yasharaal (Israel) together, and passed over the Yaradan, and came on them, and set the battle in array against them. So when Dawad had put the battle in array qaraah (against) the Aram (Syrians), they fought with him.

The Aram (Syrians) fled panayam (before) Yasharaal (Israel); and Dawad killed of the Aram (Syrians) the men of shabai (seven) alap (thousand) chariots, and arabaiyam (forty) alap (thousand) footmen, and killed Shawapak the shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army).

When the ibad (servants) of Hadadezer saw that they were defeated by Yasharaal (Israel), they made shalam (peace) with Dawad, and served him: neither would the Aram (Syrians) yashai (help) the children of Imawan any more.

It happened, at the ith (time) of the thashawabah (return) of the Shanah, at the ith (time) when malak (kings) yatzaa (go) out, that Yawaab led forth the tzabaa (army), and wasted the aratz (country) of the children of Imawan, and came and besieged Rabah. But Dawad stayed at Yarawashalam. Yawaab struck Rabah, and overthrew it.

Dawad took the itarah (crown) of their malak (king) from off his raash (head), and found it to weigh a talent of gold, and there were Yaqar aban (stones) in it; and it was set on Dawad raash (head): and he brought forth the spoil of the Iyar, maad (exceeding) much.

He brought yatzaa (forth) the im (people) who were therein, and cut them with saws, and with barazal (iron) picks, and with axes. Dawad did so to all the Iyar of the children of Imawan. Dawad and all the im (people) returned to Yarawashalam.
It happened achar (after) this, that there arose war at Gazar with the Palashathay (Philistines): then Sabakay the Chashathay killed Sapay, of the yalayad (sons) of the Rapaa; and they were subdued.

There was again war with the Palashathay (Philistines); and Alachanan the ban (son) of Yaiwar killed Lachamay the ach (brother) of Galayath the Gathay (Gittite), the itz (staff) of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.

There was again war at gath (gath), where there was a ayash (man) of great stature, whose fingers and toes were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four), shash (six) on each hand, and shash (six) on each foot; and he also was yalad (born) to the Rapaa.
When he defied Yasharaal (Israel), Yahawanathan the ban (son) of Shamaia Dawad ach (brother) killed him.
These were yalad (born) to the Rapaa in gath (gath); and they napal (fell) by the yad (hand) of Dawad, and by the yad (hand) of his ibad (servants).
shatan (satan) stood up against Yasharaal (Israel), and moved Dawad to number Yasharaal (Israel).

Dawad said to Yawaab and to the shar (princes) of the im (people), "yalak (go), number Yasharaal (Israel) Baarashabai Beersheba Dan to Dan; and bawaa (bring) me word, that I may yadai (know) the sum of them.

Yawaab said, "May Yahawah make his im (people) a maah (hundred) paim (times) as many as they are. But, my Adawan the malak (king), aren't they all my adawan (lord's) ibad (servants)? Why does my Adawan require this thing? Why will he be a cause of guilt to Yasharaal (Israel)?
Nevertheless the malak (king's) dabar (word) prevailed against Yawaab. Therefore Yawaab departed, and went throughout all Yasharaal (Israel), and came to Yarawashalam.

Yawaab gave up the sum of the numbering of the im (people) to Dawad. All those of Yasharaal (Israel) were one million one maah (hundred) alap (thousand) men who drew charab (sword): and in Yahawadah (Judah) were arabai (four) maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) alap (thousand) men who drew charab (sword).
But he didn't paqad (count) Laway and Banayamayan among them; for the malak (king's) dabar (word) was abominable to Yawaab.
Alahayam was displeased with this thing; therefore he struck Yasharaal (Israel).
Dawad said to Alahayam, "I have sinned maad (greatly), in that I have done this thing. But now, ibar (put) away, I beg you, the iwan (iniquity) of your ibad (servant); for I have done very foolishly.
Yahawah spoke to Gad, Dawad chazah (seer), saying,
"yalak (go) and dabar (speak) to Dawad, saying, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "I natah (offer) you shalawash (three) things. Choose one of them, that I may do it to you."'
So Gad came to Dawad, and said to him, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘Take your choice:

either shalawash (three) Shanah of famine; or shalawash (three) chadash (months) to be consumed panayam (before) your tzar (foes), while the charab (sword) of your ayab (enemies) overtakes you; or else shalawash (three) yawam (days) the charab (sword) of Yahawah, even dabar (pestilence) in the aratz (land), and the malaak (angel) of Yahawah destroying throughout all the borders of Yasharaal (Israel). Now therefore raah (see) dabar (what) answer I shall shawab (turn back / repent) to him who sent me.'

Dawad said to Gad, "I am in tzarar (distress). Let me napal (fall), I pray, into the yad (hand) of Yahawah; for his racham (mercies) are very rab (great). Let me not napal (fall) into the yad (hand) of adam (man).
So Yahawah sent a dabar (pestilence) on Yasharaal (Israel); and shabaiyam (seventy) alap (thousand) men of Yasharaal (Israel) napal (fell).
