Alahayam sent an malaak (angel) to Yarawashalam to shachath (destroy) it. As he was about to shachath (destroy), Yahawah saw, and he relented of the disaster, and said to the destroying malaak (angel), "It is rab (enough); now rapah (stay) your yad (hand)." The malaak (angel) of Yahawah was standing by the threshing floor of Aranan the Yabawasay (Jebusite).

Dawad lifted up his iyan (eyes), and saw the malaak (angel) of Yahawah standing between aratz (earth) and the sky, having a drawn charab (sword) in his yad (hand) stretched out over Yarawashalam. Then Dawad and the zaqan (elders), clothed in sackcloth, napal (fell) on their panayam (faces).

Dawad said to Alahayam, "Isn't it I who commanded the im (people) to be numbered? It is even I who have sinned and done very wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? Please let your yad (hand), O Yahawah my Alahayam, be against me, and against my ab (father's) bayath (house); but not against your im (people), that they should be magapah (plagued).

Then the malaak (angel) of Yahawah commanded Gad to amar (tell) Dawad that Dawad should ilah (go) up, and qawam (raise) an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah in the threshing floor of Aranan the Yabawasay (Jebusite).
Dawad went up at the dabar (saying) of Gad, which he spoke in the sham (name) of Yahawah.
Aranan turned shawab (turn back / repent), and saw the malaak (angel); and his arabai (four) ban (sons) who were with him hid themselves. Now Aranan was threshing wheat.
As Dawad came to Aranan, Aranan looked and saw Dawad, and went out of the threshing floor, and bowed himself to Dawad with his ap (face) to the aratz (ground).

Then Dawad said to Aranan, "nathan (give) me the place of this threshing floor, that I may banah (build) thereon an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah. You shall sell it to me for the Malaa kasap (price), that the magapah (plague) may be stopped from afflicting the im (people).

Aranan said to Dawad, "Take it for yourself, and let my Adawan the malak (king) do that which is tawab (good) in his iyan (eyes). raah (see), I nathan (give) the oxen for burnt ilah (offerings), and the threshing instruments for itz (wood), and the wheat for the meal manachah (offering). I nathan (give) it all.

malak (king) Dawad said to Aranan, "No; but I will most certainly qanah (buy) it for the Malaa kasap (price). For I will not nashaa (take) that which is yours for Yahawah, nor ilah (offer) a burnt ilah (offering) without cost.
So Dawad gave to Aranan shash (six) maah (hundred) shekels of gold by weight for the place.

Dawad built an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah there, and offered burnt ilah (offerings) and peace ilah (offerings), and called on Yahawah; and he answered him from the sky by ash (fire) on the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering).
Yahawah commanded the malaak (angel); and he shawab (turn back / repent) up his charab (sword) again into its sheath.
At that ith (time), when Dawad saw that Yahawah had answered him in the threshing floor of Aranan the Yabawasay (Jebusite), then he sacrificed there.

For the mashakan (tabernacle) of Yahawah, which Mashah made in the madabar (wilderness), and the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering), were at that ith (time) in the bamah (high) place at Gabaiwan.
But Dawad couldn't yalak (go) panayam (before) it to inquire of Alahayam; for he was afraid panayam (because) of the charab (sword) of the malaak (angel) of Yahawah.
Then Dawad said, "This is the bayath (house) of Yahawah Alahayam, and this is the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering) for Yasharaal (Israel).

Dawad gave orders to gather together the foreigners who were in the aratz (land) of Yasharaal (Israel); and he imad (set) chatzab (masons) to chatzab (cut) worked aban (stones) to banah (build) the bayath (house) of Alahayam.
Dawad prepared barazal (iron) in abundance for the nails for the doors of the gates, and for the couplings; and brass in abundance without weight;
and cedar itz (trees) without number: for the Tzayadanay (Sidonians) and they of Tzaray brought cedar itz (trees) in abundance to Dawad.

Dawad said, "Shalamah my ban (son) is nair (young) and Rak, and the bayath (house) that is to be built for Yahawah must be exceedingly magnificent, of sham (fame) and of glory throughout all aratz (countries). I will therefore kawan (make) preparation for it." So Dawad prepared abundantly panayam (before) his mawath (death).
Then he called for Shalamah his ban (son), and tzawah (commanded) him to banah (build) a bayath (house) for Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
Dawad said to Shalamah his ban (son), "As for me, it was in my labab (heart) to banah (build) a bayath (house) to the sham (name) of Yahawah my Alahayam.

But the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying, ‘You have shed dam (blood) abundantly, and have made gadawal (great) wars. You shall not banah (build) a bayath (house) to my sham (name), because you have shed much dam (blood) on the aratz (earth) in my panayam (sight).

Behold, a ban (son) shall be yalad (born) to you, who shall be a ayash (man) of manawachah (rest). I will give him nawach (rest) from all his ayab (enemies) all around; for his sham (name) shall be Shalamah, and I will nathan (give) shalawam (peace) and quietness to Yasharaal (Israel) in his yawam (days).

He shall banah (build) a bayath (house) for my sham (name); and he shall be my ban (son), and I will be his ab (father); and I will kawan (establish) the kasaa (throne) of his malakawath (kingdom) over Yasharaal (Israel) for ever.'
Now, my ban (son), may Yahawah be with you and tzalach (prosper) you, and banah (build) the bayath (house) of Yahawah your Alahayam, as he has spoken concerning you.

May Yahawah nathan (give) you shakal (discretion) and bayanah (understanding), and tzawah (put) you in charge of Yasharaal (Israel); that so you may shamar (keep) the thawarah (law) of Yahawah your Alahayam.

Then you will tzalach (prosper), if you shamar (observe) to do the chaq (statutes) and the mashapat (ordinances) which Yahawah gave Mashah concerning Yasharaal (Israel). Be chazaq (strong), and amatz (courageous). Don't be yaraa (afraid), neither be dismayed.

Now, behold, in my affliction I have prepared for the bayath (house) of Yahawah one maah (hundred) alap (thousand) talents of gold, one million talents of kasap (silver), and brass and barazal (iron) without weight; for it is in abundance. I have also prepared itz (timber) and aban (stone); and you may add to them.
There are also workmen with you in abundance, cutters and workers of aban (stone) and itz (timber), and all kinds of men who are skillful in every kind of malaakah (work):
of the gold, the kasap (silver), and the brass, and the barazal (iron), there is no number. qawam (arise) and be doing, and may Yahawah be with you.
Dawad also tzawah (commanded) all the shar (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel) to help Shalamah his ban (son), saying,

"Isn't Yahawah your Alahayam with you? Hasn't he given you nawach (rest) on every side? For he has delivered the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land) into my yad (hand); and the aratz (land) is subdued panayam (before) Yahawah, and panayam (before) his im (people).

Now nathan (set) your labab (heart) and your napash (soul) to seek after Yahawah your Alahayam. qawam (arise) therefore, and banah (build) the maqadash (sanctuary) of Yahawah Alahayam, to bawaa (bring) the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, and the qadash (holy) vessels of Alahayam, into the bayath (house) that is to be built to the sham (name) of Yahawah.
Now Dawad was zaqan (old) and full of yawam (days); and he made Shalamah his ban (son) malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel).
He gathered asap (together) all the shar (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel), with the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites).

The Lawayay (Levites) were numbered from shalawashayam (thirty) years old and upward: and their number by their galagalath (polls), gabar (man) by gabar (man), was shalawashayam (thirty) - shamanah (eight) alap (thousand).

David said, "Of these, isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand) were to oversee the malaakah (work) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah; shash (six) alap (thousand) were shatar (officers) and shapat (judges);
arabai (four) alap (thousand) were doorkeepers; and arabai (four) alap (thousand) praised Yahawah with the instruments which I made, for giving halal (praise).
Dawad divided them into divisions according to the ban (sons) of Laway: Garashawan, Qahath, and Mararay.
Of the garashanay (gershonites): Laidan and Shamaiy.
The ban (sons) Laidan Ladan: Yachayaal the raash (chief), and Zatham, and Yawaal, shalawash (three).
The ban (sons) of Shamaiy: Shalamayath, and Chazayaal, and Haran, shalawash (three). These were the raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' Laidan of Ladan.
The ban (sons) of Shamaiy: Yachath, Zayanaa, and Yaiwash, and Barayaih. These arabai (four) were the ban (sons) of Shamaiy.
Yachath was the raash (chief), and Zayazah the shanay (second): but Yaiwash and Barayaih didn't have many ban (sons); therefore they became a abawath (fathers)' bayath (house) in one reckoning.
The ban (sons) of Qahath: Imaram, Yatzahar, Chabarawan, and Izayaal, arabai (four).

The ban (sons) of Imaram: Aharawan and Mashah; and Aharawan was separated, that he should qadash (sanctify) the most qadash (holy) things, he and his ban (sons), iwalam (forever), to qatar (burn) incense panayam (before) Yahawah, to sharath (minister) to him, and to barak (bless) in his sham (name), iwalam (forever).
But as for Mashah the ayash (man) of Alahayam, his ban (sons) were named among the shabat (tribe) of Laway.
The ban (sons) of Mashah: Garasham and Alayaizar.
The ban (sons) of Garasham: Shabawaal the raash (chief).
The ban (sons) of Alayaizar were: Rachabayah the raash (chief); and Alayaizar had no other ban (sons); but the ban (sons) of Rachabayah were very many.
The ban (sons) of Yatzahar: Shalamayath the raash (chief).
The ban (sons) of Chabarawan: Yarayah the raash (chief), Amarayah the shanay (second), Yachazayaal the shalayashay (third), and Yaqamaim the rabayaiy (fourth).
The ban (sons) of Izayaal: Mayakah the raash (chief), and Yashayah the shanay (second).
The ban (sons) of Mararay: Machalay and Mawashay. The ban (sons) of Machalay: Alaizar and Qayash.
Alaizar died, and had no ban (sons), but bath (daughters) only: and their ach (brothers) the ban (sons) of Qayash took them as wives.
The ban (sons) of Mawashay: Machalay, and Idar, and Yarayamawath, shalawash (three).

These were the ban (sons) of Laway after their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), even the raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' houses of those who were counted individually, in the number of sham (names) by their galagalath (polls), who did the malaakah (work) for the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, from isharayam (twenty) years ban (old) and upward.
For Dawad said, "Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), has given nawach (rest) to his im (people); and he shakan (dwells) in Yarawashalam iwalam (forever).
Lawayay the Levites will no longer nashaa (need) to carry the mashakan (tabernacle) and all its vessels for its ibadah (service).
For by the Acharawan dabar (words) of Dawad the Lawayay of Levi were numbered, from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward.

For their office was to yad (wait) on the ban (sons) of Aharawan for the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, in the courts, and in the rooms, and in the purifying of all qadash (holy) things, even the maishah (work) of the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam;

for the show lacham (bread) also, and for the fine flour for a meal manachah (offering), whether of unleavened wafers, or of that which is baked in the pan, or of that which is soaked, and for all kinds of measure and size;
and to imad (stand) every baqar (morning) to yadah (thank) and halal (praise) Yahawah, and likewise in the evening;

and to ilah (offer) all burnt ilah (offerings) to Yahawah, on the shabath (sabbaths), on the new chadash (moons), and on the mawaid (set) feasts, in number according to the mashapat (ordinance) concerning them, continually panayam (before) Yahawah;

and that they should shamar (keep) the duty of the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and the duty of the qadash (holy) place, and the duty of the ban (sons) of Aharawan their ach (brothers), for the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
These were the divisions of the ban (sons) of Aharawan. The ban (sons) of Aharawan: Nadab and Abayahawaa, Alaizar and Ayathamar.
But Nadab and Abayahawaa died panayam (before) their ab (father), and had no children: therefore Alaizar and Ayathamar executed the kahan (priest's) office.
Dawad with Tzadawaq of the ban (sons) of Alaizar, and Achayamalak of the ban (sons) of Ayathamar, divided them according to their ordering in their ibadah (service).

There were more raash (chief) men found of the ban (sons) of Alaizar than of the ban (sons) of Ayathamar; and they were divided like this: of the ban (sons) of Alaizar there were sixteen, raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses); and of the ban (sons) of Ayathamar, according to their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), shamanah (eight).

Thus were they divided impartially by drawing lots; for there were shar (princes) of the qadash (sanctuary), and shar (princes) of Alahayam, both of the ban (sons) of Alaizar, and of the ban (sons) of Ayathamar.

Shamaiyah the ban (son) Nathanaal Nethanel the scribe, who was Lawayay the Levites, wrote them in the panayam (presence) of the malak (king), and the shar (princes), and Tzadawaq the kahan (priest), and Achayamalak the ban (son) of Abayathar, and the raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' households of the kahan (priests) and Lawayay the Levites; one abawath (fathers)' bayath (house) being taken for Alaizar, and one taken for Ayathamar.
Now the raashawan (first) lot came yatzaa (forth) to Yahawayarayab, the shanay (second) to Yadaiyah,
the shalayashay (third) to Charam, the rabayaiy (fourth) to Shairayam,
the chamayashay (fifth) to Malakayah, the shashay (sixth) to Mayaman,
the shabayaiy (seventh) to Qawatz, the eighth to Abayah,
the thashayaiy (ninth) to Yashawai, the ishayaray (tenth) to Shakanayah,
the ishathay (eleventh) to Alayashayab, the shanayam (twelfth) to Yaqayam,
the thirteenth to Chapah, the fourteenth to Yashabaab,
the fifteenth to Balagah, the sixteenth to Amar,
the seventeenth to Chazayar, the eighteenth Patzatz Happizzez,
the nineteenth Pathachayah Pethahiah, the isharayam (twentieth) Yachazaqaal Jehezkel,
the isharayam (twenty) - achad (first) to Yakayan, the isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (second) to Gamawal,
the isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (third) to Dalayah, the isharayam (twenty) - fourth to Maizayah.

This was their ordering in their ibadah (service), to bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah according to the mashapat (ordinance) given to them by Aharawan their ab (father), as Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), had tzawah (commanded) him.
Of the yathar (rest) of the ban (sons) of Laway: of the ban (sons) of Imaram, Shabawaal; of the ban (sons) of Shabawaal, Yachadayahaw.
Of Rachabayah: of the ban (sons) of Rachabayah, Yashayah the raash (chief).
Of the Yatzaharay, Shalamawath; of the ban (sons) of Shalamawath, Yachath.
The ban (sons) of Hebron: Yarayah, Amarayah the shanay (second), Yachazayaal the shalayashay (third), Yaqamaim the rabayaiy (fourth).
The ban (sons) of Izayaal, Mayakah; of the ban (sons) of Mayakah, Shamawar.
The ach (brother) of Mayakah, Yashayah; of the ban (sons) of Yashayah, Zakarayah.
The ban (sons) of Mararay: Machalay and Mawashay; the ban (sons) of Yaizayahaw: Beno.
The ban (sons) of Mararay: of Yaizayahaw, Beno, and Shaham, and Zakawar, and Ibaray.
Of Machalay: Alaizar, who had no ban (sons).
Of Qayash; the ban (sons) of Qayash: Yarachamaal.
The ban (sons) of Mawashay: Machalay, and Idar, and Yarayamawath. These were the ban (sons) Lawayay the Levites after their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses).

These likewise napal (cast) lots even as their ach (brothers) the ban (sons) of Aharawan in the panayam (presence) of Dawad the malak (king), and Tzadawaq, and Achayamalak, and the raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' households of the kahan (priests) and Lawayay the Levites; the abawath (fathers)' households of the raash (chief) even as those of his younger ach (brother).

Moreover, Dawad and the shar (captains) of the tzabaa (army) set apart for the ibadah (service) certain of the ban (sons) of Asap, and of Hayaman, and of Yadawathawan, who should nabaa (prophesy) with harps, with stringed instruments, and with cymbals: and the number of those who did the work according to their ibadah (service) was:
of the ban (sons) of Asap: Zakawar, and Yawasap, and Nathanayah, and Asharaalah, the ban (sons) of Asap, under the yad (hand) of Asap, who prophesied after the yad (order) of the malak (king).

Of Yadawathawan; the ban (sons) of Yadawathawan: Gadalayah, and Tzaray, and Yashaiyah, Chashabayah, and Mathathayah, shash (six), under the yad (hands) of their ab (father) Yadawathawan with the harp, who prophesied in giving yadah (thanks) and praising Yahawah.

Of Hayaman; the ban (sons) of Hayaman: Baqayah, Mathanayah, Izayaal, Shabawaal, and Yarayamawath, Chananayah, Chananay, Alayaathah, Gadalathay, and Rawamamathayaizar, Yashabaqashah, Malawathay, Hawathayar, Machazayaawath.

All these were the ban (sons) of Hayaman the malak (king's) chazah (seer) in the dabar (words) of Alahayam, to lift up the qaran (horn). Alahayam gave to Hayaman fourteen ban (sons) and shalawash (three) bath (daughters).

All these were under the yad (hands) of their ab (father) for song in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, with cymbals, stringed instruments, and harps, for the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam; Asap, Yadawathawan, and Hayaman being under the yad (order) of the malak (king).
The number of them, with their ach (brothers) who were instructed in singing to Yahawah, even all who were skillful, was two maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty) - shamanah (eight).
They napal (cast) lots for their offices, all alike, as well the qatan (small) as the gadawal (great), the teacher as the scholar.
Now the raashawan (first) lot came yatzaa (forth) for Asap to Yawasap: the shanay (second) to Gadalayah; he and his ach (brothers) and ban (sons) were shanayam (twelve):
the shalayashay (third) to Zakawar, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
the rabayaiy (fourth) Yatzaray Izri, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
the chamayashay (fifth) to Nathanayah, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
the shashay (sixth) to Baqayah, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
the shabayaiy (seventh) to Yasharaalah, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
the eighth to Yashaiyah, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
the thashayaiy (ninth) to Mathanayah, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
the ishayaray (tenth) to Shamaiy, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
the ishathay (eleventh) Izaraal Azarel, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
the shanayam (twelfth) to Chashabayah, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
for the thirteenth, Shabawaal, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
for the fourteenth, Mathathayah, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
for the fifteenth Yarayamawath Jeremoth, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
for the sixteenth to Chananayah, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
for the seventeenth to Yashabaqashah, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
for the eighteenth to Chananay, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
for the nineteenth to Malawathay, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
for the isharayam (twentieth) to Alayaathah, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
for the one and isharayam (twentieth) to Hawathayar, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
for the shanayam (two) and isharayam (twentieth) to Gadalathay, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
for the shalawash (three) and isharayam (twentieth) to Machazayaawath, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve):
for the arabai (four) and isharayam (twentieth) to Rawamamathayaizar, his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), shanayam (twelve).
For the divisions of the doorkeepers: of the qarachay (korahites), Mashalamayah the ban (son) of Qawaraa, of the ban (sons) of Asap.
Mashalamayah had ban (sons): Zakarayah the firstborn, Yadayaial the shanay (second), Zabadayah the shalayashay (third), Yathanayaal the rabayaiy (fourth),
Iyalam the chamayashay (fifth), Yahawachanan the shashay (sixth), Alayahawaiyanay the shabayaiy (seventh).
Ibadaadawam had ban (sons): Shamaiyah the firstborn, Yahawazabad the shanay (second), Yawaach the shalayashay (third), and Shakar the rabayaiy (fourth), and Nathanaal the chamayashay (fifth),
Imayaal the shashay (sixth), Yashashakar the shabayaiy (seventh), Pailathay the eighth; for Alahayam blessed him.
Also to Shamaiyah his ban (son) were ban (sons) yalad (born), who ruled over the bayath (house) of their ab (father); for they were gabawar (mighty) men of valor.
The ban (sons) of Shamaiyah: Ithanay, and Rapaal, and Iwabad, Alazabad, whose ach (brothers) were chayal (valiant) men, Alayahaw, and Samakayahaw.

All these were of the ban (sons) of Ibadaadawam: they and their ban (sons) and their ach (brothers), chayal (able) men in kach (strength) for the ibadah (service); shashayam (sixty) - shanayam (two) of Ibadaadawam.
Mashalamayah had ban (sons) and ach (brothers), chayal (valiant) men, eighteen.
Also Chasah, of the children of Mararay, had ban (sons): Shamaray the raash (chief), (for though he was not the firstborn, yet his ab (father) made him raash (chief)),
Chalaqayah the shanay (second), Tabalayahaw the shalayashay (third), Zakarayah the rabayaiy (fourth): all the ban (sons) and ach (brothers) of Chasah were thirteen.
Of these were the divisions of the doorkeepers, even of the raash (chief) men, having offices like their ach (brothers), to sharath (minister) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
They napal (cast) lots, the qatan (small) as well as the gadawal (great), according to their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), for every gate.
The lot eastward napal (fell) to Shalamayah. Then for Zakarayah his ban (son), a shakal (wise) yaitz (counselor), they napal (cast) lots; and his lot came out northward.
To Ibadaadawam Nagab; and to his ban (sons) the storehouse.
To Shapayam and Chasah westward, by the gate Shalakath Shallecheth, at the masalah (causeway) that goes up, watch against watch.
Eastward were shash (six) Lawayay (Levites), northward arabai (four) a yawam (day), Nagab arabai (four) a yawam (day), and for the storehouse shanayam (two) and shanayam (two).
For Parabar westward, arabai (four) at the masalah (causeway), and shanayam (two) at Parabar.
These were the divisions of the doorkeepers; of the ban (sons) of the qarachay (korahites), and of the ban (sons) of Mararay.
Lawayay the Levites, Achayah was over the treasures of the bayath (house) of Alahayam, and over the treasures of the qadash (dedicated) things.

The ban (sons) Laidan Ladan, the ban (sons) of the garashanay (gershonites) Laidan to Ladan, the raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' Laidan belonging to Ladan the garashanay (gershonite): Yachayaalay.
The ban (sons) of Yachayaalay: Zatham, and Yawaal his ach (brother), over the treasures of the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
Of the Imaramay, of the Yatzaharay, of the Chabarawanay, of the Izayaalay:
and Shabawaal the ban (son) of Garasham, the ban (son) of Mashah, was nagayad (ruler) over the treasures.
His ach (brothers): of Alayaizar, Rachabayah his ban (son), and Yashaiyah his ban (son), and Yawaram his ban (son), and Zakaray his ban (son), and Shalamayath his ban (son).

This Shalamawath and his ach (brothers) were over all the treasures of the qadash (dedicated) things, which Dawad the malak (king), and the raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' households, the shar (captains) over alap (thousands) and maah (hundreds), and the shar (captains) of the tzabaa (army), had dedicated.
They dedicated some of the spoil won in battles to chazaq (repair) the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

All that Shamawaal the seer, and Shaawal the ban (son) of Qayash, and Abanar the ban (son) of Nar, and Yawaab the ban (son) of Tzarawayah, had dedicated, whoever had dedicated anything, it was under the yad (hand) Shalamayath Shelomoth, and of his ach (brothers).
Of the Yatzaharay, Kananayah and his ban (sons) were for the Chayatzawan malaakah (business) over Yasharaal (Israel), for shatar (officers) and shapat (judges).

Of the Chabarawanay, Chashabayah and his ach (brothers), men of valor, one alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred), had the oversight of Yasharaal (Israel) ibar (beyond) the Yaradan westward, for all the malaakah (business) of Yahawah, and for the ibadah (service) of the malak (king).

Of the Chabarawanay was Yarayah the raash (chief), even of the Chabarawanay, according to their thawaladah (generations) by abawath (fathers)' households. In the fortieth Shanah of the malakawath (reign) of Dawad they were sought for, and there were found among them gabawar (mighty) men of valor at Yaizayar of Galaid.

His ach (brothers), men of valor, were two alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred), raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households, whom malak (king) Dawad made paqad (overseers) over the Raawabanay (Reubenites), and the Gaday (Gadites), and the chatzay (half) - shabat (tribe) of the Manashay (Manassites), for every dabar (matter) pertaining to Alahayam, and for the dabar (affairs) of the malak (king).

Now the children of Yasharaal (Israel) after their number, the raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households and the shar (captains) of alap (thousands) and of maah (hundreds), and their shatar (officers) who served the malak (king), in any dabar (matter) of the divisions which came in and went out chadash (month) by chadash (month) throughout all the chadash (months) of the year—of achad (every) division were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand).
Over the raashawan (first) division for the raashawan (first) chadash (month) was Yashabaim the ban (son) of Zabadayaal: and in his division were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand).
He was of the children of Paratz, the raash (chief) of all the shar (captains) of the tzabaa (army) for the raashawan (first) chadash (month).

Over the division of the shanay (second) chadash (month) was Dawaday the Achawachay (Ahohite), and his division; and Maqalawath the nagayad (ruler): and in his division were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand).

The shalayashay (third) shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army) for the shalayashay (third) chadash (month) was Banayah, the ban (son) of Yahawayadai the kahan (priest), raash (chief): and in his division were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand).
This is that Banayah, who was the gabawar (mighty) man of the shalawashayam (thirty), and over the shalawashayam (thirty): and of his division was Imayazabad his ban (son).

The rabayaiy (fourth) captain for the rabayaiy (fourth) chadash (month) was Ishahaal the ach (brother) of Yawaab, and Zabadayah his ban (son) achar (after) him: and in his division were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand).
The chamayashay (fifth) shar (captain) for this chamayashay (fifth) chadash (month) was Shamahawath the Yazarach: and in his division were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand).

The shashay (sixth) captain for the shashay (sixth) chadash (month) was Iyaraa the ban (son) of Iqash the Thaqawaiy (Tekoite): and in his division were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand).

The shabayaiy (seventh) captain for the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month) was Chalatz the Palawanay, of the children of Aparayam: and in his division were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand).
The eighth captain for the eighth chadash (month) was Sabakay the Chashathay, Zarachay the Zerahites: and in his division were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand).

The thashayaiy (ninth) captain for the thashayaiy (ninth) chadash (month) was Abayaizar the Inathathay (Anathothite), of the Banayamayanay (Benjamites): and in his division were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand).

The ishayaray (tenth) captain for the ishayaray (tenth) chadash (month) was Maharay the Natapathay (Netophathite), Zarachay the Zerahites: and in his division were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand).

The ishathay (eleventh) captain for the ishathay (eleventh) chadash (month) was Banayah the Paraithawanay, of the children of Aparayam: and in his division were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand).

The shanayam (twelfth) captain for the shanayam (twelfth) chadash (month) was Chaladay the Natapathay (Netophathite), of Ithanayaal: and in his division were isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four) alap (thousand).

Furthermore over the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel): of the Raawabanay (Reubenites) was Alayaizar the ban (son) of Zakaray the ruler: of the Shamainay (Simeonites), Shapatayah the ban (son) Maikah Maacah:
Lawayay Levi, Chashabayah the ban (son) of Qamawaal: of Aharawan, Tzadawaq:
of Yahawadah (Judah), Alayahaw, one of the ach (brothers) of Dawad: of Yashashakar, Imaray the ban (son) of Mayakaal:
of Zabawalawan, Yashamaiyah the ban (son) of Ibadayah: of Napathalay, Yarayamawath the ban (son) of Izarayaal:
of the children of Aparayam, Hawashai the ban (son) of Izazayahaw: of the chatzay (half) - shabat (tribe) of Manashah, Yawaal the ban (son) of Padayah:
of the chatzay (half) - tribe of Manashah in Galaid, Yadaw the ban (son) of Zakarayah: of Banayamayan, Yaishayaal the ban (son) of Abanar:
Dan Dan, Izaraal the ban (son) of Yaracham. These were the shar (captains) of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel).

But Dawad didn't nashaa (take) the number of them from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and under, because Yahawah had said he would increase Yasharaal (Israel) like the kawakab (stars) of the sky.

Yawaab the ban (son) of Tzarawayah began to number, but didn't kalah (finish); and there came qatzap (wrath) for this on Yasharaal (Israel); neither was the number ilah (put) into the account in the dabar (chronicles) of malak (king) Dawad.

Over the malak (king's) treasures was Izamawath the ban (son) of Idayaal: and over the treasures in the shadah (fields), in the Iyar, and in the villages, and in the magadal (towers), was Yahawanathan the ban (son) of Izayah:
Over those who did the malaakah (work) of the shadah (field) for ibadah (tillage) of the adamah (ground) was Izaray the ban (son) of Kalawab:
and over the vineyards was Shamaiy the Ramathay: and over the increase of the vineyards for the winecellars was Zabaday the Shapamay:
and over the olive trees and the sycamore trees that were in the lowland was Bailachanan Hanan the Gadaray: and over the cellars of shaman (oil) was Yawaish:
and over the herds that fed in Sharawan was Shataray the Sharawanay: and over the herds that were in the valleys was Shapat the ban (son) of Idalay:
and over the camels was Awabayal the Yashamaialay (Ishmaelite): and over the donkeys was Yachadayahaw the Maranathay: and over the flocks was Yazayaz the Hagaray (Hagrite).
All these were the shar (rulers) of the rakawash (substance) which was malak (king) Dawad.

Also Yahawanathan, Dawad dawad (uncle), was a yaitz (counselor), a ayash (man) of bayan (understanding), and a scribe: and Yachayaal the ban (son) of Chakamawanay was with the malak (king's) ban (sons):
Achayathapal was the malak (king's) yaitz (counselor): and Chawashay the Arakay was the malak (king's) rai (friend):
and achar (after) Achayathapal was Yahawayadai the ban (son) of Banayah, and Abayathar: and the shar (captain) of the malak (king's) tzabaa (army) was Yawaab.

Dawad assembled all the shar (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel), the shar (princes) of the shabat (tribes), and the shar (captains) of the companies who served the malak (king) by division, and the shar (captains) of alap (thousands), and the shar (captains) of maah (hundreds), and the rulers over all the rakawash (substance) and maqanah (possessions) of the malak (king) and of his ban (sons), with the officers, and the gabawar (mighty) men, even all the gabawar (mighty) men of valor, to Yarawashalam.

Then Dawad the malak (king) stood up on his feet, and said, "Hear me, my ach (brothers), and my im (people)! As for me, it was in my labab (heart) to banah (build) a bayath (house) of manawachah (rest) for the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, and for the footstool of our Alahayam; and I had prepared for the building.
But Alahayam said to me, ‘You shall not banah (build) a bayath (house) for my sham (name), because you are a ayash (man) of war, and have shed dam (blood).'

However Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), chose me out of all the bayath (house) of my ab (father) to be malak (king) over Yasharaal (Israel) iwalam (forever). For he has chosen Yahawadah (Judah) to be nagayad (prince); and in the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah), the bayath (house) of my ab (father); and among the ban (sons) of my ab (father) he took pleasure in me to make me malak (king) over all Yasharaal (Israel).

Of all my ban (sons) (for Yahawah has given me many ban (sons)), he has chosen Shalamah my ban (son) to yashab (sit) on the kasaa (throne) of yahawah (yahweh's) malakawath (kingdom) over Yasharaal (Israel).
He said to me, ‘Shalamah, your ban (son), shall banah (build) my bayath (house) and my courts; for I have chosen him to be my ban (son), and I will be his ab (father).
I will kawan (establish) his malakawath (kingdom) iwalam (forever), if he chazaq (continues) to do my matzawah (commandments) and my mashapat (ordinances), as at this yawam (day).'

Now therefore, in the iyan (sight) of all Yasharaal (Israel), the qahal (assembly) of Yahawah, and in the audience of our Alahayam, shamar (observe) and seek out all the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah your Alahayam; that you may yarash (possess) this tawab (good) aratz (land), and leave it for an nachal (inheritance) to your children achar (after) you iwalam (forever).

You, Shalamah my ban (son), yadai (know) the Alahayam of your ab (father), and ibad (serve) him with a Shalam lab (heart) and with a Chapatz napash (mind); for Yahawah searches all labab (hearts), and bayan (understands) all the yatzar (imaginations) of the machashabah (thoughts). If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will cast you off id (forever).
raah (see) heed now; for Yahawah has chosen you to banah (build) a bayath (house) for the maqadash (sanctuary). Be chazaq (strong), and do it.

Then Dawad gave to Shalamah his ban (son) the thabanayath (pattern) of the porch of the bayath (temple), and of its houses, and of its treasuries, and of the upper rooms Panayamay it, and of the inner rooms of it, and of the bayath (place) of the kaparath (mercy) seat;

and the thabanayath (pattern) of all that he had by the rawach (spirit), for the courts of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and for all the surrounding rooms, for the treasuries of the bayath (house) of Alahayam, and for the treasuries of the qadash (dedicated) things;

also for the divisions of the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites), and for all the malaakah (work) of the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and for all the vessels of ibadah (service) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah;
of gold by weight for the gold, for all vessels of every kind of ibadah (service); for all the vessels of kasap (silver) by weight, for all vessels of every kind of ibadah (service);

by weight also for the lampstands of gold, and for its nayar (lamps), of gold, by weight for every lampstand and for its nayar (lamps); and for the lampstands of kasap (silver), by weight for every lampstand and for its nayar (lamps), according to the use of every lampstand;
and the gold by weight for the tables of show mairakath (bread), for every table; and kasap (silver) for the tables of kasap (silver);
and the forks, and the basins, and the cups, of tahawar (pure) gold; and for the golden bowls by weight for every bowl; and for the kasap (silver) bowls by weight for every bowl;

and for the mazabach (altar) of incense refined gold by weight; and gold for the thabanayath (pattern) of the chariot, the karawab (cherubim), that spread out, and covered the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah.
"All this," said David, "I have been made to shakal (understand) in writing from the yad (hand) of Yahawah, even all the malaakah (works) of this thabanayath (pattern).

Dawad said to Shalamah his ban (son), "Be chazaq (strong) and amatz (courageous), and do it. Don't be yaraa (afraid), nor be dismayed; for Yahawah Alahayam, even my Alahayam, is with you. He will not rapah (fail) you, nor forsake you, until all the malaakah (work) for the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah is finished.

Behold, there are the divisions of the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites), for all the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam. There shall be with you in all kinds of malaakah (work) every nadayab (willing) man who has skill, for any kind of ibadah (service). Also the shar (captains) and all the im (people) will be entirely at your command.

Dawad the malak (king) said to all the qahal (assembly), "Shalamah my ban (son), whom achad (alone) Alahayam has chosen, is yet nair (young) and Rak, and the malaakah (work) is gadawal (great); for the palace is not for adam (man), but for Yahawah Alahayam.

Now I have prepared with all my might for the bayath (house) of my Alahayam the gold for the things of gold, and the kasap (silver) for the things of kasap (silver), and the brass for the things of brass, the barazal (iron) for the things of barazal (iron), and itz (wood) for the things of itz (wood); onyx aban (stones), and aban (stones) to be set, aban (stones) for inlaid raqamah (work), and of various colors, and all kinds of Yaqar aban (stones), and marble aban (stones) in abundance.

In addition, because I have set my affection on the bayath (house) of my Alahayam, since I have a treasure of my own of gold and kasap (silver), I nathan (give) it to the bayath (house) of my Alahayam, over and above all that I have prepared for the qadash (holy) bayath (house),

even shalawash (three) alap (thousand) talents of gold, of the gold of Awapayar, and shabai (seven) alap (thousand) talents of refined kasap (silver), with which to overlay the walls of the bayath (houses);

of gold for the things of gold, and of kasap (silver) for the things of kasap (silver), and for all kinds of malaakah (work) to be made by the yad (hands) of artisans. Who then offers willingly to malaa (consecrate) yad (himself) this yawam (day) to Yahawah?

Then the shar (princes) of the abawath (fathers)' households, and the shar (princes) of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), and the shar (captains) of alap (thousands) and of maah (hundreds), with the shar (rulers) over the malak (king's) malaakah (work), offered willingly;

and they gave for the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam of gold chamash (five) alap (thousand) talents and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) darics, and of kasap (silver) ishar (ten) alap (thousand) talents, and of brass eighteen alap (thousand) talents, and of barazal (iron) a maah (hundred) alap (thousand) talents.
They with whom precious aban (stones) were found gave them to the treasure of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, under the yad (hand) of Yachayaal the garashanay (gershonite).

Then the im (people) Shamach, because they offered willingly, because with a Shalam lab (heart) they offered willingly to Yahawah: and Dawad the malak (king) Shamach rejoiced with gadawal (great) joy.
Therefore Dawad blessed Yahawah iyan (before) all the qahal (assembly); and Dawad said, "You are blessed, Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) our ab (father), iwalam (forever) and ever.

Yours, Yahawah, is the greatness, the gabawarah (power), the glory, the natzach (victory), and the hawad (majesty)! For all that is in the shamayam (heavens) and in the aratz (earth) is yours. Yours is the mamalakah (kingdom), Yahawah, and you are exalted as raash (head) above all.
Both riches and honor come from you, and you mashal (rule) over all; and in your yad (hand) is kach (power) and might; and it is in your yad (hand) to make great, and to give strength to all.
Now therefore, our Alahayam, we yadah (thank) you, and halal (praise) your thapaarah (glorious) sham (name).
But who am I, and what is my im (people), that we should be kach (able) to offer so willingly as this? For all things come from you, and of your yad (own) have we given you.
For we are strangers panayam (before) you, and foreigners, as all our abawath (fathers) were. Our yawam (days) on the aratz (earth) are as a shadow, and Maqawah is no remaining.
Yahawah our Alahayam, all this store that we have prepared to banah (build) you a bayath (house) for your qadash (holy) sham (name) comes from your yad (hand), and is all your own.

I yadai (know) also, my Alahayam, that you try the labab (heart), and have pleasure in yashar (uprightness). As for me, in the uprightness of my labab (heart) I have willingly offered all these things. Now have I seen with joy your im (people), that are matzaa (present) here, offer willingly to you.

Yahawah, the Alahayam of Abaraham, of Yatzachaq, and of Yasharaal (Israel), our abawath (fathers), shamar (keep) this iwalam (forever) in the yatzar (imagination) of the machashabah (thoughts) of the labab (heart) of your im (people), and kawan (prepare) their labab (heart) for you;

and nathan (give) to Shalamah my ban (son) a Shalam labab (heart), to shamar (keep) your matzawah (commandments), your idawath (testimonies), and your chaq (statutes), and to do all these things, and to banah (build) the palace, for which I have made kawan (provision).

Dawad said to all the qahal (assembly), "Now barak (bless) Yahawah your Alahayam!" All the qahal (assembly) blessed Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers), and bowed down their qadad (heads) and prostrated themselves before Yahawah and the malak (king).

They sacrificed zabach (sacrifices) to Yahawah, and offered burnt ilah (offerings) to Yahawah, on the next macharath (day) after that macharath (day), even one alap (thousand) bulls, one alap (thousand) ayal (rams), and one alap (thousand) lambs, with their drink nasak (offerings), and zabach (sacrifices) in abundance for all Yasharaal (Israel),

and ate and drink panayam (before) Yahawah on that yawam (day) with gadawal (great) gladness. They made Shalamah the ban (son) of Dawad malak (king) the shanay (second) time, and mashach (anointed) him to Yahawah to be nagayad (prince), and Tzadawaq to be kahan (priest).
Then Shalamah sat on the kasaa (throne) of Yahawah as malak (king) instead of Dawad his ab (father), and prospered; and all Yasharaal (Israel) obeyed him.
All the shar (princes), the gabawar (mighty) men, and also all of the ban (sons) of malak (king) Dawad submitted yad (themselves) to Shalamah the malak (king).

Yahawah magnified Shalamah exceedingly in the iyan (sight) of all Yasharaal (Israel), and bestowed on him such malakawath (royal) hawad (majesty) as had not been on any malak (king) panayam (before) him in Yasharaal (Israel).
Now Dawad the ban (son) of Yashay reigned over all Yasharaal (Israel).

The yawam (time) that he reigned over Yasharaal (Israel) was arabaiyam (forty) Shanah; he reigned shabai (seven) Shanah in Chabarawan, and he reigned shalawashayam (thirty) - shalawash (three) years in Yarawashalam.
He died in a tawab (good) shayabah (old) age, Shabai of yawam (days), riches, and honor: and Shalamah his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Now the dabar (acts) of Dawad the malak (king), raashawan (first) and Acharawan, behold, they are written in the history of Shamawaal the seer, and in the history of Nathan the nabayaa (prophet), and in the history of Gad the chazah (seer),
with all his malakawath (reign) and his might, and the ith (times) that went over him, and over Yasharaal (Israel), and over all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (countries).
Shalamah the ban (son) of Dawad was strengthened in his malakawath (kingdom), and Yahawah his Alahayam was with him, and magnified him exceedingly.

Shalamah spoke to all Yasharaal (Israel), to the shar (captains) of alap (thousands) and of maah (hundreds), and to the shapat (judges), and to raash (every) prince in all Yasharaal (Israel), the raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' households.

So Shalamah, and all the qahal (assembly) with him, went to the bamah (high) place that was at Gabaiwan; for there was the ahal (tent) of Meeting of Alahayam, which Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah had made in the madabar (wilderness).
But Dawad had brought the arawan (ark) of Alahayam up from Kiriath Qarayathayairayam to the place that Dawad had prepared for it; for he had pitched a ahal (tent) for it at Yarawashalam.

Moreover the bronze mazabach (altar), that Batzalaal the ban (son) of Awaray, the ban (son) of Chawar, had made, was there panayam (before) the mashakan (tabernacle) of Yahawah: and Shalamah and the qahal (assembly) were seeking darash (counsel) there.
Shalamah went up there to the bronze mazabach (altar) panayam (before) Yahawah, which was at the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and offered one alap (thousand) burnt ilah (offerings) on it.
In that layal (night) Alahayam appeared to Shalamah, and said to him, "shaal (ask) what I shall nathan (give) you.
Shalamah said to Alahayam, "You have shown gadawal (great) loving chasad (kindness) to Dawad my ab (father), and have made me malak (king) in his place.

Now, Yahawah Alahayam, let your dabar (promise) to Dawad my ab (father) be established; for you have made me malak (king) over a im (people) like the ipar (dust) of the aratz (earth) in rab (multitude).

Now nathan (give) me chakamah (wisdom) and madai (knowledge), that I may yatzaa (go) out and bawaa (come) in panayam (before) this im (people); for who can shapat (judge) this your im (people), that is so gadawal (great)?

Alahayam said to Shalamah, "Because this was in your labab (heart), and you have not asked riches, wealth, or honor, nor the napash (life) of those who shanaa (hate) you, neither yet have asked rab (long) yawam (life); but have asked chakamah (wisdom) and madai (knowledge) for yourself, that you may shapat (judge) my im (people), over whom I have made you malak (king):

chakamah (wisdom) and madai (knowledge) is granted to you. I will nathan (give) you riches, wealth, and honor, such as none of the malak (kings) have had who have been panayam (before) you; neither shall there any achar (after) you have the like.
So Shalamah came from the bamah (high) place that was at Gabaiwan, from panayam (before) the ahal (tent) of Meeting, to Yarawashalam; and he reigned over Yasharaal (Israel).

Shalamah gathered chariots and horsemen: and he had one alap (thousand) arabai (four) maah (hundred) chariots, and shanayam (twelve) alap (thousand) horsemen, that he placed in the chariot Iyar, and with the malak (king) at Yarawashalam.
The malak (king) made kasap (silver) and gold to be in Yarawashalam as aban (stones), and cedars made he to be as the sycamore trees that are in the lowland, for abundance.
The horses which Shalamah had were brought out of Matzarayam and from Maqawah; the malak (king's) merchants purchased them from Maqawah.

They brought up and brought out of Matzarayam a chariot for shash (six) maah (hundred) pieces of kasap (silver), and a horse for one maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty): and so for all the malak (kings) of the Chathay (Hittites), and the malak (kings) of Aram, they brought them out by their yad (means).
Now Shalamah purposed to banah (build) a bayath (house) for the sham (name) of Yahawah, and a bayath (house) for his malakawath (kingdom).

Shalamah counted out shabaiyam (seventy) alap (thousand) men to bear burdens, and shamanayam (eighty) alap (thousand) men who were stone cutters in the har (mountains), and shalawash (three) alap (thousand) and shash (six) maah (hundred) to oversee them.

Shalamah sent to Chawaram the malak (king) of Tzar, saying, "As you dealt with Dawad my ab (father), and sent him cedars to banah (build) him a bayath (house) in which to yashab (dwell), so deal with me.

Behold, I am about to banah (build) a bayath (house) for the sham (name) of Yahawah my Alahayam, to qadash (dedicate) it to him, and to qatar (burn) panayam (before) him incense of sweet spices, and for the continual show mairakath (bread), and for the burnt ilah (offerings) baqar (morning) and evening, on the shabath (sabbaths), and on the new chadash (moons), and on the mawaid (set) feasts of Yahawah our Alahayam. This is an ordinance forever to Yasharaal (Israel).
"The bayath (house) which I banah (build) is gadawal (great); for our Alahayam is gadawal (great) above all Alahayam.

But who is itzar (able) to banah (build) him a bayath (house), since shamayam (heaven) and the shamayam (heaven) of shamayam (heavens) can't contain him? who am I then, that I should banah (build) him a bayath (house), am (except) just to qatar (burn) incense panayam (before) him?

"Now therefore shalach (send) me a ayash (man) skillful to ishah (work) in gold, and in kasap (silver), and in brass, and in barazal (iron), and in purple, and crimson, and blue, and who yadai (knows) how to pathach (engrave) engravings, to be with the skillful men who are with me in Yahawadah (Judah) and in Yarawashalam, whom Dawad my ab (father) provided.

"shalach (send) me also cedar itz (trees), fir trees, and algum trees, out of Labanawan; for I yadai (know) that your ibad (servants) yadai (know) how to karath (cut) itz (timber) in Labanawan: and behold, my ibad (servants) shall be with your ibad (servants),
even to kawan (prepare) me itz (timber) in abundance; for the bayath (house) which I am about to banah (build) shall be gadawal (great) and palaa (wonderful).

Behold, I will nathan (give) to your ibad (servants), the cutters who karath (cut) itz (timber), isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) measures of makah (beaten) wheat, and isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) measures of barley, and isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) baths of yayan (wine), and isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) baths of shaman (oil).
Then Chawaram the malak (king) of Tzar answered in writing, which he sent to Shalamah, "Because Yahawah ahabah (loves) his im (people), he has made you malak (king) over them.

Chawaram continued, "Blessed be Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), that made shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth), who has given to Dawad the malak (king) a chakam (wise) ban (son), endowed with shakal (discretion) and understanding, that should banah (build) a bayath (house) for Yahawah, and a bayath (house) for his malakawath (kingdom).
Now I have sent a skillful ayash (man), endowed with bayanah (understanding), of Chawaram my ab (father's),

the ban (son) of a ashah (woman) of the bath (daughters) Dan Dan; and his ab (father) was a ayash (man) of Tzaray, skillful to ishah (work) in gold, and in kasap (silver), in brass, in barazal (iron), in aban (stone), and in itz (timber), in purple, in blue, and in fine linen, and in crimson, also to pathach (engrave) any kind of engraving, and to chashab (devise) any machashabah (device); that there may be a nathan (place) appointed to him with your skillful men, and with the skillful men of my Adawan Dawad your ab (father).
"Now therefore the wheat and the barley, the shaman (oil) and the yayan (wine), which my Adawan has spoken of, let him shalach (send) to his ibad (servants):
and we will karath (cut) itz (wood) out of Labanawan, as much as you shall need; and we will bawaa (bring) it to you in floats by yam (sea) to Yapaw; and you shall ilah (carry) it up to Yarawashalam.

Shalamah numbered all the foreigners who were in the aratz (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), achar (after) the numbering with which Dawad his ab (father) had numbered them; and they were found one maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) - shalawash (three) alap (thousand) shash (six) maah (hundred).

He ishah (set) shabaiyam (seventy) alap (thousand) of them to bear burdens, and shamanayam (eighty) alap (thousand) who were stone cutters in the har (mountains), and shalawash (three) alap (thousand) shash (six) maah (hundred) overseers to set the im (people) at ibad (work).

Then Shalamah began to banah (build) the bayath (house) of Yahawah at Yarawashalam on har (mount) Mawarayah, where Yahawah raah (see) to Dawad his ab (father), which he prepared in the place that Dawad had appointed, in the threshing floor of Aranan the Yabawasay (Jebusite).
He began to banah (build) in the shanay (second) day of the shanay (second) chadash (month), in the fourth Shanah of his malakawath (reign).

Now these are the foundations which Shalamah laid for the building of the bayath (house) of Alahayam. The arak (length) by amah (cubits) after the raashawan (first) measure was shashayam (sixty) amah (cubits), and the breadth isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits).

The porch that was in panayam (front), its arak (length), according to the breadth of the bayath (house), was isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits), and the height one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty); and he overlaid it within with tahawar (pure) gold.
The greater bayath (house) he made a ceiling with fir itz (wood), which he overlaid with tawab (fine) gold, and ornamented it with palm trees and chains.
He garnished the bayath (house) with Yaqar aban (stones) for thapaarah (beauty): and the gold was gold of Parawayam.
He overlaid also the bayath (house), the beams, the thresholds, and its walls, and its doors, with gold; and engraved karawab (cherubim) on the walls.

He made the most qadash (holy) bayath (house): its arak (length), according to the breadth of the bayath (house), was isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits), and its breadth isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits); and he overlaid it with tawab (fine) gold, amounting to shash (six) maah (hundred) talents.
The weight of the nails was chamashayam (fifty) shekels of gold. He overlaid the upper rooms with gold.
In the most qadash (holy) bayath (house) he made shanayam (two) karawab (cherubim) of tzaitzai (image) maishah (work); and they overlaid them with gold.

The wings of the karawab (cherubim) were isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) arak (long): the wing of the one was chamash (five) amah (cubits), reaching to the wall of the bayath (house); and the other wing was chamash (five) amah (cubits), reaching to the wing of the other karawab (cherub).

The wing of the other karawab (cherub) was chamash (five) amah (cubits), reaching to the wall of the bayath (house); and the other wing was chamash (five) amah (cubits), Dabaq to the wing of the other karawab (cherub).
The wings of these karawab (cherubim) spread themselves forth isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits): and they stood on their feet, and their panayam (faces) were toward the bayath (house).
He made the parakath (veil) of blue, and purple, and crimson, and fine linen, and ornamented it with karawab (cherubim).

Also he made panayam (before) the bayath (house) shanayam (two) pillars of shalawashayam (thirty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits) high, and the capital that was on the raash (top) of each of them was chamash (five) amah (cubits).
He made chains in the oracle, and nathan (put) them on the raash (tops) of the pillars; and he made one maah (hundred) pomegranates, and nathan (put) them on the chains.

He qawam (set) up the pillars panayam (before) the hayakal (temple), one on the right yamayan (hand), and the other on the shamaawal (left); and called the sham (name) of that on the Yamanay hand Yakayan, and the sham (name) of that on the Shamaalay Baiz.
Then he made an mazabach (altar) of brass, isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) its arak (length), and isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) its breadth, and ishar (ten) amah (cubits) its height.

Also he made the molten yam (sea) of ishar (ten) amah (cubits) from shapah (brim) to shapah (brim), Igal in compass; and its height was chamash (five) amah (cubits); and a line of shalawashayam (thirty) amah (cubits) encircled it.
Under it was the damawath (likeness) of oxen, which encircled it, for ishar (ten) amah (cubits), encircling the yam (sea). The oxen were in shanayam (two) rows, cast when it was cast.

It stood on shanayam (twelve) oxen, shalawash (three) looking toward the tzapawan (north), and shalawash (three) looking toward the yam (west), and shalawash (three) looking toward the Nagab, and shalawash (three) looking toward the east: and the yam (sea) was set on them above, and all their hinder parts were inward.
It was a tapach (handbreadth) thick; and its shapah (brim) was worked like the shapah (brim) of a cup, like the flower of a lily: it received and held shalawash (three) alap (thousand) baths.

He made also ishar (ten) basins, and nathan (put) chamash (five) on the right yamayan (hand), and chamash (five) on the shamaawal (left), to wash in them; such things as belonged to the burnt offering they washed in them; but the yam (sea) was for the kahan (priests) to wash in.

He made the ishar (ten) lampstands of gold according to the mashapat (ordinance) concerning them; and he nathan (set) them in the hayakal (temple), chamash (five) on the right yamayan (hand), and chamash (five) on the shamaawal (left).

He made also ishar (ten) tables, and placed them in the hayakal (temple), chamash (five) on the yamayan (right) side, and chamash (five) on the shamaawal (left). He made one maah (hundred) basins of gold.
Furthermore he made the court of the kahan (priests), and the gadawal (great) court, and doors for the court, and overlaid their doors with brass.
He nathan (set) the yam (sea) on the Yamanay side of the house eastward, toward the Nagab.
Chawaram made the pots, and the shovels, and the basins. So Chawaram made an end of doing the malaakah (work) that he did for malak (king) Shalamah in the bayath (house) of Alahayam:

the shanayam (two) pillars, and the bowls, and the shanayam (two) capitals which were on the raash (top) of the pillars, and the shanayam (two) networks to cover the shanayam (two) bowls of the capitals that were on the raash (top) of the pillars,

and the arabai (four) maah (hundred) pomegranates for the shanayam (two) networks; shanayam (two) rows of pomegranates for achad (each) network, to cover the shanayam (two) bowls of the capitals that were on the pillars.
He made also the bases, and the basins made he on the bases;
one yam (sea), and the shanayam (twelve) oxen under it.
Chawaram his ab (father) also made the pots, the shovels, the forks, and all its vessels for malak (king) Shalamah for the bayath (house) of Yahawah of bright brass.
The malak (king) cast them in the plain of the Yaradan, in the clay adamah (ground) between Sakawath and Tzaradah.
Thus Shalamah made all these vessels in maad (great) abundance: for the weight of the brass could not be found out.
Shalamah made all the vessels that were in the bayath (house) of Alahayam, the golden mazabach (altar) also, and the tables with the show lacham (bread) on them;
and the lampstands with their nayar (lamps), to bair (burn) according to the mashapat (ordinance) panayam (before) the oracle, of pure gold;
and the flowers, and the nayar (lamps), and the tongs, of gold, and that perfect gold;

and the snuffers, and the basins, and the kap (spoons), and the machathah (fire) pans, of pure gold: and as for the entry of the bayath (house), the Panayamay doors of it for the most qadash (holy) place, and the doors of the main hall of the hayakal (temple) were of gold.

Thus all the malaakah (work) that Shalamah did for the bayath (house) of Yahawah was finished. Shalamah brought in the things that Dawad his ab (father) had qadash (dedicated), even the kasap (silver), and the gold, and all the vessels, and nathan (put) them in the treasuries of the bayath (house) of Alahayam.

Then Shalamah assembled the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel), and all the raash (heads) of the matah (tribes), the nashayaa (princes) of the abawath (fathers)' households of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), to Yarawashalam, to ilah (bring) up the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah out of the Iyar of Dawad, which is Tzayawan.
And all the men of Yasharaal (Israel) assembled themselves to the malak (king) at the chag (feast), which was in the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month).
All the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) came: and the Lawayay (Levites) took up the arawan (ark);
and they brought up the arawan (ark), and the ahal (tent) of Meeting, and all the qadash (holy) vessels that were in the ahal (tent); these the kahan (priests) the Lawayay (Levites) brought up.

malak (king) Shalamah and all the idah (congregation) of Yasharaal (Israel), that were assembled to him, were panayam (before) the arawan (ark), sacrificing sheep and cattle, that could not be counted nor numbered for multitude.

The kahan (priests) brought in the arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah to its place, into the oracle of the bayath (house), to the most qadash (holy) place, even under the wings of the karawab (cherubim).
For the karawab (cherubim) spread forth their wings over the place of the arawan (ark), and the karawab (cherubim) covered the arawan (ark) and its poles above.
The poles were so long that the raash (ends) of the poles were seen from the arawan (ark) panayam (before) the oracle; but they were not seen outside: and there it is to this yawam (day).

There was nothing in the arawan (ark) except the shanayam (two) tables which Mashah nathan (put) at Charab, when Yahawah made a covenant with the children of Yasharaal (Israel), when they came out of Matzarayam.

It happened, when the kahan (priests) had yatzaa (come) out of the qadash (holy) place, (for all the kahan (priests) who were matzaa (present) had sanctified themselves, and didn't shamar (keep) their divisions;

Lawayay the Levites who were the singers, all of them, even Asap, Hayaman, Yadawathawan, and their ban (sons) and their ach (brothers), Labash in fine linen, with cymbals and stringed instruments and harps, stood at the east end of the mazabach (altar), and with them one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) kahan (priests) sounding with trumpets;)

it happened, when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one qawal (sound) to be heard in praising and thanking Yahawah; and when they lifted up their qawal (voice) with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praised Yahawah, saying, "For he is tawab (good); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever)!" that then the bayath (house) was filled with a cloud, even the bayath (house) of Yahawah,
so that the kahan (priests) could not imad (stand) to sharath (minister) by panayam (reason) of the cloud: for the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah filled the bayath (house) of Alahayam.
Then Shalamah said, "Yahawah has said that he would shakan (dwell) in the thick irapal (darkness).
But I have built you a bayath (house) of habitation, and a place for you to yashab (dwell) in iwalam (forever).
The malak (king) turned his panayam (face), and blessed all the qahal (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel): and all the qahal (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel) stood.
He said, "Blessed be Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), who spoke with his pah (mouth) to Dawad my ab (father), and has with his yad (hands) fulfilled it, saying,

‘Since the yawam (day) that I brought yatzaa (forth) my im (people) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, I chose no Iyar out of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) to banah (build) a bayath (house) in, that my sham (name) might be there; neither chose I any ayash (man) to be nagayad (prince) over my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel):
but I have chosen Yarawashalam, that my sham (name) might be there; and have chosen Dawad to be over my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel).'
Now it was in the labab (heart) of Dawad my ab (father) to banah (build) a bayath (house) for the sham (name) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
But Yahawah said to Dawad my ab (father), ‘Whereas it was in your labab (heart) to banah (build) a bayath (house) for my sham (name), you did tawab (well) that it was in your labab (heart):
raq (nevertheless) you shall not banah (build) the bayath (house); but your ban (son) who shall yatzaa (come) forth out of your body, he shall banah (build) the bayath (house) for my sham (name).'

"Yahawah has performed his dabar (word) that he spoke; for I have risen up in the place of Dawad my ab (father), and yashab (sit) on the kasaa (throne) of Yasharaal (Israel), as Yahawah promised, and have built the bayath (house) for the sham (name) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
There I have shawam (set) the arawan (ark), in which is the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah, which he made with the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
He stood panayam (before) the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah in the presence of all the qahal (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel), and spread forth his kap (hands)

(for Shalamah had made a bronze scaffold, chamash (five) amah (cubits) arak (long), and chamash (five) amah (cubits) broad, and shalawash (three) amah (cubits) high, and had nathan (set) it in the midst of the court; and on it he stood, and kneeled down on his knees before all the qahal (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel), and spread forth his kap (hands) toward shamayam (heaven);)

and he said, "Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), there is no Alahayam like you, in shamayam (heaven), or on aratz (earth); you who shamar (keep) barayath (covenant) and loving chasad (kindness) with your ibad (servants), who halak (walk) panayam (before) you with all their lab (heart);
who have kept with your ibad (servant) Dawad my ab (father) that which you promised him: yes, you spoke with your pah (mouth), and have fulfilled it with your yad (hand), as it is this yawam (day).

"Now therefore, Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), shamar (keep) with your ibad (servant) Dawad my ab (father) that which you have promised him, saying, ‘There shall not karath (fail) you a ayash (man) in my panayam (sight) to yashab (sit) on the kasaa (throne) of Yasharaal (Israel), if only your children shamar (take) heed to their darak (way), to yalak (walk) in my thawarah (law) as you have walked panayam (before) me.'
Now therefore, Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), let your dabar (word) be aman (verified), which you spoke to your ibad (servant) Dawad.

"But will Alahayam indeed yashab (dwell) with men on the aratz (earth)? Behold, shamayam (heaven) and the shamayam (heaven) of shamayam (heavens) can't contain you; how much less this bayath (house) which I have built!

Yet have panah (respect) for the prayer of your ibad (servant), and to his supplication, Yahawah my Alahayam, to listen to the cry and to the prayer which your ibad (servant) palal (prays) panayam (before) you;

that your iyan (eyes) may be pathach (open) toward this bayath (house) yawamam (day) and layal (night), even toward the place where you have said that you would shawam (put) your sham (name); to listen to the prayer which your ibad (servant) shall palal (pray) toward this place.

Listen to the petitions of your ibad (servant), and of your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), when they shall palal (pray) toward this place: yes, hear from your yashab (dwelling) place, even from shamayam (heaven); and when you hear, forgive.

"If a ayash (man) chataa (sin) against his neighbor, and an alah (oath) is laid on him to cause him to alah (swear), and he bawaa (comes) and alah (swears) panayam (before) your mazabach (altar) in this bayath (house);

then hear from shamayam (heaven), and do, and shapat (judge) your ibad (servants), bringing retribution to the rashai (wicked), to nathan (bring) his darak (way) on his own raash (head); and justifying the tzadayaq (righteous), to nathan (give) him according to his tzadaqah (righteousness).

"If your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel) be struck down panayam (before) the ayab (enemy), because they have sinned against you, and shall shawab (turn back / repent) again and yadah (confess) your sham (name), and palal (pray) and chanan (make) supplication panayam (before) you in this bayath (house);

then hear from shamayam (heaven), and forgive the chataah (sin) of your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), and shawab (turn back / repent) them again to the adamah (land) which you gave to them and to their abawath (fathers).

"When the sky is itzar (shut) up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against you; if they palal (pray) toward this place, and yadah (confess) your sham (name), and shawab (turn back / repent) from their chataah (sin), when you afflict them:

then hear in shamayam (heaven), and forgive the chataah (sin) of your ibad (servants), and of your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), when you teach them the tawab (good) darak (way) in which they should yalak (walk); and nathan (send) rain on your aratz (land), which you have given to your im (people) for an nachalah (inheritance).

"If there is famine in the aratz (land), if there is dabar (pestilence), if there is blight or mildew, locust or caterpillar; if their ayab (enemies) besiege them in the aratz (land) of their cities; whatever nagai (plague) or whatever sickness there is;

whatever prayer and supplication be made by any adam (man), or by all your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), who shall yadai (know) every ayash (man) his own nagai (plague) and his own sorrow, and shall spread forth his kap (hands) toward this bayath (house):

then hear from shamayam (heaven), your yashab (dwelling) place and forgive, and nathan (render) to every ayash (man) according to all his darak (ways), whose labab (heart) you yadai (know); (for you, even you only, yadai (know) the labab (hearts) of the children of men;)
that they may yaraa (fear) you, to yalak (walk) in your darak (ways), so yawam (long) as they chay (live) in the adamah (land) which you gave to our abawath (fathers).

"Moreover concerning the nakaray (foreigner), who is not of your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), when he shall bawaa (come) from a Rachawaq aratz (country) for your gadawal (great) sham (name's) sake, and your chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and your natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm); when they shall bawaa (come) and palal (pray) toward this bayath (house):

then hear from shamayam (heaven), even from your yashab (dwelling) place, and do according to all that the nakaray (foreigner) qaraa (calls) to you for; that all the im (peoples) of the aratz (earth) may yadai (know) your sham (name), and yaraa (fear) you, as does your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), and that they may yadai (know) that this bayath (house) which I have built is called by your sham (name).

"If your im (people) yatzaa (go) out to battle against their ayab (enemies), by whatever darak (way) you shall shalach (send) them, and they palal (pray) to you darak (toward) this Iyar which you have chosen, and the bayath (house) which I have built for your sham (name);
then hear from shamayam (heaven) their prayer and their supplication, and ishah (maintain) their cause.

"If they chataa (sin) against you (for there is no adam (man) who doesn't chataa (sin)), and you are angry with them, and nathan (deliver) them to the ayab (enemy), so that they carry them away captive to a aratz (land) Rachawaq off or qarawab (near);

yet if they shall repent themselves in the aratz (land) where they are carried captive, and shawab (turn back / repent) again, and chanan (make) supplication to you in the aratz (land) of their Shabay, saying, ‘We have sinned, we have done perversely, and have dealt wickedly;'

if they shawab (turn back / repent) to you with all their lab (heart) and with all their napash (soul) in the aratz (land) of their Shabay, where they have carried them captive, and palal (pray) darak (toward) their aratz (land), which you gave to their abawath (fathers), and the Iyar which you have chosen, and toward the bayath (house) which I have built for your sham (name):
then hear from shamayam (heaven), even from your yashab (dwelling) place, their prayer and their petitions, and ishah (maintain) their cause, and forgive your im (people) who have sinned against you.
"Now, my Alahayam, let, I beg you, your iyan (eyes) be pathach (open), and let your ears be Qashab, to the prayer that is made in this place.

"Now therefore qawam (arise), Yahawah Alahayam, into your resting place, you, and the arawan (ark) of your iz (strength): let your kahan (priests), Yahawah Alahayam, be Labash with thashawaih (salvation), and let your chasayad (saints) Shamach in goodness.
"Yahawah Alahayam, don't shawab (turn back / repent) away the panayam (face) of your mashayach (anointed). zakar (remember) your loving kindnesses to Dawad your ibad (servant).

Now when Shalamah had made an kalah (end) of praying, the ash (fire) came down from shamayam (heaven), and consumed the burnt ilah (offering) and the zabach (sacrifices); and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah filled the bayath (house).
The kahan (priests) could not bawaa (enter) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah, because the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah filled yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house).

All the children of Yasharaal (Israel) looked on, when the ash (fire) came down, and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah was on the bayath (house); and they bowed themselves with their ap (faces) to the aratz (ground) on the pavement, and worshiped, and gave yadah (thanks) to Yahawah, saying, "For he is tawab (good); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures for ever.
Then the malak (king) and all the im (people) offered zabach (sacrifice) panayam (before) Yahawah.

malak (king) Shalamah offered a zabach (sacrifice) of isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) alap (thousand) baqar (head) of cattle, and a maah (hundred) and isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) sheep. So the malak (king) and all the im (people) dedicated the bayath (house) of Alahayam.

The kahan (priests) stood, according to their positions; the Lawayay (Levites) also with instruments of music of Yahawah, which Dawad the malak (king) had made to give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah, when Dawad praised by their yad (ministry), saying "For his loving chasad (kindness) endures for ever." The kahan (priests) sounded trumpets before them; and all Yasharaal (Israel) stood.

Moreover Shalamah made the middle of the court qadash (holy) that was panayam (before) the bayath (house) of Yahawah; for there he offered the burnt ilah (offerings), and the fat of the shalam (peace) offerings, because the bronze mazabach (altar) which Shalamah had made was not yakal (able) to receive the burnt ilah (offering), and the meal manachah (offering), and the fat.

So Shalamah held the chag (feast) at that ith (time) shabai (seven) yawam (days), and all Yasharaal (Israel) with him, a very gadawal (great) qahal (assembly), from the entrance of Chamath to the nachal (brook) of Matzarayam.
On the eighth yawam (day) they held a solemn itzarah (assembly): for they kept the dedication of the mazabach (altar) shabai (seven) yawam (days), and the chag (feast) shabai (seven) yawam (days).

On the shalawash (three) and isharayam (twentieth) yawam (day) of the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month) he sent the im (people) shalach (away) to their ahal (tents), tawab (joyful) and Shamach of lab (heart) for the goodness that Yahawah had shown to Dawad, and to Shalamah, and to Yasharaal (Israel) his im (people).

Thus Shalamah finished the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the malak (king's) bayath (house): and he successfully completed all that came into Shalamah lab (heart) to ishah (make) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and in his own bayath (house).
Yahawah raah (see) to Shalamah by layal (night), and said to him, "I have heard your prayer, and have chosen this place to myself for a bayath (house) of zabach (sacrifice).
"If I itzar (shut) up the sky so that there is no rain, or if I tzawah (command) the locust to akal (devour) the aratz (land), or if I shalach (send) dabar (pestilence) among my im (people);

if my im (people), who are called by my sham (name), shall humble themselves, and palal (pray), and seek my panayam (face), and shawab (turn back / repent) from their rai (wicked) darak (ways); then will I hear from shamayam (heaven), and will forgive their chataah (sin), and will heal their aratz (land).
Now my iyan (eyes) shall be pathach (open), and my ears Qashab, to the prayer that is made in this place.
For now have I chosen and made this bayath (house) qadash (holy), that my sham (name) may be there iwalam (forever); and my iyan (eyes) and my lab (heart) shall be there yawam (perpetually).

"As for you, if you will yalak (walk) panayam (before) me as Dawad your ab (father) walked, and do according to all that I have tzawah (commanded) you, and will shamar (keep) my chaq (statutes) and my mashapat (ordinances);

then I will qawam (establish) the kasaa (throne) of your malakawath (kingdom), according as I covenanted with Dawad your ab (father), saying, ‘There shall not karath (fail) you a ayash (man) to be ruler in Yasharaal (Israel).'

But if you shawab (turn back / repent) away, and forsake my chaqah (statutes) and my matzawah (commandments) which I have nathan (set) panayam (before) you, and shall halak (go) and ibad (serve) other Alahayam, and shachah (worship) them;

then I will nathash (pluck) them up by the roots out of my adamah (land) which I have given them; and this bayath (house), which I have made qadash (holy) for my sham (name), I will cast out of my panayam (sight), and I will nathan (make) it a proverb and a byword among all im (peoples).
This bayath (house), which is so Ilayawan, everyone who passes by it shall be astonished, and shall amar (say), ‘Why has Yahawah done thus to this aratz (land), and to this bayath (house)?'

They shall amar (answer), ‘Because they abandoned Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers), who brought them yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and took other Alahayam, worshiped them, and served them. Therefore he has brought all this rai (evil) on them.'
It happened at the end of isharayam (twenty) Shanah, in which Shalamah had built the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and his own bayath (house),
that the Iyar which Chawaram had given to Shalamah, Shalamah built them, and caused the children of Yasharaal (Israel) to yashab (dwell) there.
Shalamah went to Chamathatzawabah Zobah, and prevailed against it.
He built Thadamar in the madabar (wilderness), and all the storage Iyar, which he built in Chamath.
Also he built Bayathachawarawan Horon the Ilayawan, and Bayathachawarawan Horon the Thachathawan, Matzawar Iyar, with walls, gates, and bars;

and Bailath, and all the storage Iyar that Shalamah had, and all the Iyar for his chariots, and the Iyar for his horsemen, and all that Shalamah desired to banah (build) for his pleasure in Yarawashalam, and in Labanawan, and in all the aratz (land) of his mamashalah (dominion).
