As for all the im (people) who were yathar (left) of the Chathay (Hittites), and the Amaray (Amorites), and the Parazay (Perizzites), and the Chaway (Hivites), and the Yabawasay (Jebusites), who were not of Yasharaal (Israel);

of their children who were yathar (left) achar (after) them in the aratz (land), whom the children of Yasharaal (Israel) didn't kalah (consume), of them Shalamah conscripted forced mas (labor) to this yawam (day).

But of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), Shalamah made no ibad (servants) for his malaakah (work); but they were men of war, and shar (chief) of his shalayash (captains), and shar (rulers) of his chariots and of his horsemen.
These were the shar (chief) natzab (officers) of malak (king) Shalamah, even two - maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty), who ruled over the im (people).

Shalamah brought up the bath (daughter) of Paraih out of the Iyar of Dawad to the bayath (house) that he had built for her; for he said, "My ashah (wife) shall not yashab (dwell) in the bayath (house) of Dawad malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), because the places where the arawan (ark) of Yahawah has bawaa (come) are qadash (holy).
Then Shalamah offered burnt ilah (offerings) to Yahawah on the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah, which he had built panayam (before) the porch,

even as the dabar (duty) of every yawam (day) required, offering according to the matzawah (commandment) of Mashah, on the shabath (sabbaths), and on the new chadash (moons), and on the mawaid (set) feasts, shalawash (three) paim (times) in the Shanah, in the chag (feast) of unleavened matzah (bread), and in the chag (feast) of shabawai (weeks), and in the chag (feast) of sakah (tents).

He appointed, according to the mashapat (ordinance) of Dawad his ab (father), the divisions of the kahan (priests) to their ibadah (service), and the Lawayay (Levites) to their offices, to halal (praise), and to sharath (minister) before the kahan (priests), as the dabar (duty) of every yawam (day) yawam (required); the doorkeepers also by their divisions at every gate: for so had Dawad the ayash (man) of Alahayam commanded.
They didn't sawar (depart) from the matzawah (commandment) of the malak (king) to the kahan (priests) and Lawayay (Levites) dabar (concerning) any matter, or concerning the treasures.
Now all the malaakah (work) of Shalamah was prepared to the yawam (day) of the foundation of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and until it was finished. So the bayath (house) of Yahawah was Shalam.
Then went Shalamah to Itzayawanagabar Geber, and to Ayalawath, on the shapah (seashore) in the aratz (land) of Adam.

Chawaram sent him ships and ibad (servants) who had yadai (knowledge) of the yam (sea) by the yad (hands) of his ibad (servants); and they came with the ibad (servants) of Shalamah to Awapayar, and fetched from there arabai (four) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) talents of gold, and brought them to malak (king) Shalamah.

When the malakah (queen) of Shabaa heard of the fame of Shalamah, she came to prove Shalamah with hard questions at Yarawashalam, with a very Kabad chayal (train), and camels that bore spices, and gold in abundance, and Yaqar aban (stones): and when she had bawaa (come) to Shalamah, she talked with him of all that was in her labab (heart).
Shalamah told her all her dabar (questions); and there was not anything hidden from Shalamah which he didn't nagad (tell) her.
When the malakah (queen) of Shabaa had seen the chakamah (wisdom) of Shalamah, and the bayath (house) that he had built,

and the food of his table, and the mawashab (sitting) of his ibad (servants), and the attendance of his sharath (ministers), and their clothing, his cup bearers also, and their clothing, and his ascent by which he went up to the bayath (house) of Yahawah; there was no more rawach (spirit) in her.
She said to the malak (king), "It was a amath (true) dabar (report) that I heard in my own aratz (land) of your dabar (acts), and of your chakamah (wisdom).

However I didn't aman (believe) their dabar (words), until I came, and my iyan (eyes) had seen it; and behold, the chatzay (half) of the greatness of your chakamah (wisdom) was not told me: you exceed the fame that I heard.
Happy are your men, and happy are these your ibad (servants), who imad (stand) continually panayam (before) you, and hear your chakamah (wisdom).

Blessed be Yahawah your Alahayam, who delighted in you, to nathan (set) you on his kasaa (throne), to be malak (king) for Yahawah your Alahayam: because your Alahayam loved Yasharaal (Israel), to imad (establish) them iwalam (forever), therefore made he you malak (king) over them, to do justice and tzadaqah (righteousness).

She gave the malak (king) one maah (hundred) and isharayam (twenty) talents of gold, and spices in maad (great) abundance, and Yaqar aban (stones): neither was there any such spice as the malakah (queen) of Shabaa gave to malak (king) Shalamah.
The ibad (servants) also of Chawaram, and the ibad (servants) of Shalamah, who brought gold from Awapayar, brought algum itz (trees) and Yaqar aban (stones).

The malak (king) made of the algum itz (trees) masalah (terraces) for the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and for the malak (king's) bayath (house), and harps and stringed instruments for the singers: and there were none like these seen panayam (before) in the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah).

malak (king) Shalamah gave to the malakah (queen) of Shabaa all her Chapatz, whatever she asked, besides that which she had brought to the malak (king). So she turned, and went to her own aratz (land), she and her ibad (servants).
Now the weight of gold that came to Shalamah in one Shanah was shash (six) maah (hundred) and shashayam (sixty) - shash (six) talents of gold,
besides that which the traders and merchants brought: and all the malak (kings) of Irab and the governors of the aratz (country) brought gold and kasap (silver) to Shalamah.
malak (king) Shalamah made two maah (hundred) tzanah (bucklers) of beaten gold; shash (six) maah (hundred) shekels of beaten gold went to one tzanah (buckler).

He made shalawash (three) maah (hundred) magan (shields) of beaten gold; shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shekels of gold went to one magan (shield): and the malak (king) nathan (put) them in the bayath (house) of the Yair of Labanawan.
Moreover the malak (king) made a gadawal (great) kasaa (throne) of ivory, and overlaid it with tahawar (pure) gold.

And there were shash (six) steps to the kasaa (throne), with a footstool of gold, which were fastened to the kasaa (throne), and yad (stays) on either side by the place of the yashab (seat), and shanayam (two) aray (lions) standing beside the yad (stays).
shanayam (twelve) aray (lions) stood there on the one side and on the other on the shash (six) steps: there was nothing like it made in any mamalakah (kingdom).

All malak (king) Shalamah drinking vessels were of gold, and all the vessels of the bayath (house) of the Yair of Labanawan were of pure gold: kasap (silver) was nothing accounted of in the yawam (days) of Shalamah.

For the malak (king) had ships that went to Tharashayash with the ibad (servants) of Chawaram; achad (once) every shalawash (three) Shanah came the ships of Tharashayash, bringing gold, and kasap (silver), ivory, and apes, and peacocks.
So malak (king) Shalamah exceeded all the malak (kings) of the aratz (earth) in riches and chakamah (wisdom).
All the malak (kings) of the aratz (earth) sought the panayam (presence) of Shalamah, to hear his chakamah (wisdom), which Alahayam had nathan (put) in his lab (heart).
They brought every ayash (man) his tribute, vessels of kasap (silver), and vessels of gold, and clothing, armor, and spices, horses, and mules, a dabar (rate) Shanah by Shanah.

Shalamah had arabai (four) alap (thousand) stalls for horses and chariots, and shanayam (twelve) alap (thousand) horsemen, that he stationed in the chariot Iyar, and with the malak (king) at Yarawashalam.
He ruled over all the malak (kings) from the nahar (river) even to the aratz (land) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and to the border of Matzarayam.
The malak (king) made kasap (silver) to be in Yarawashalam as aban (stones), and he made cedars to be as the sycamore trees that are in the lowland, for abundance.
They brought horses for Shalamah out of Matzarayam, and out of all aratz (lands).

Now the shaar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Shalamah, raashawan (first) and Acharawan, aren't they written in the history of Nathan the nabayaa (prophet), and in the nabawaah (prophecy) of Achayah the Shayalawanay (Shilonite), and in the visions of Yaiday the chazah (seer) concerning Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat?
Shalamah reigned in Yarawashalam over all Yasharaal (Israel) arabaiyam (forty) Shanah.
Shalamah slept with his abawath (fathers), and he was buried in the Iyar of Dawad his ab (father): and Rachabaim his ban (son) reigned in his place.
Rachabaim went to Shakam; for all Yasharaal (Israel) had bawaa (come) to Shakam to make him malak (king).

It happened, when Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat heard of it, (for he was in Matzarayam, where he had fled from the panayam (presence) of malak (king) Shalamah), that Yarabaim returned out of Matzarayam.
They sent and called him; and Yarabaim and all Yasharaal (Israel) came, and they spoke to Rachabaim, saying,

"Your ab (father) made our yoke grievous: now therefore make you the Qashah ibadah (service) of your ab (father), and his Kabad yoke which he nathan (put) on us, lighter, and we will ibad (serve) you.
He said to them, "shawab (turn back / repent) again to me after shalawash (three) yawam (days)." The im (people) departed.

malak (king) Rachabaim took yaitz (counsel) with the zaqan (old) men, who had stood panayam (before) Shalamah his ab (father) while he yet lived, saying, "What yaitz (counsel) do you give me to shawab (turn back / repent) dabar (answer) to this im (people)?
They spoke to him, saying, "If you are kind to this im (people), and please them, and dabar (speak) tawab (good) dabar (words) to them, then they will be your ibad (servants) forever.
But he forsook the itzah (counsel) of the zaqan (old) men which they had given him, and took yaitz (counsel) with the yalad (young) men who had grown up with him, who stood panayam (before) him.

He said to them, "What yaitz (counsel) do you give, that we may shawab (turn back / repent) dabar (answer) to this im (people), who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Make the yoke that your ab (father) nathan (put) on us lighter?'

The yalad (young) men who had grown up with him spoke to him, saying, "Thus you shall amar (tell) the im (people) who spoke to you, saying, ‘Your ab (father) made our yoke kabad (heavy), but qalal (make) it lighter on us;' thus you shall amar (say) to them, ‘My little finger is thicker than my ab (father's) waist.
Now whereas my ab (father) burdened you with a Kabad yoke, I will add to your yoke. My ab (father) chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.'

So Yarabaim and all the im (people) came to Rachabaim the shalayashay (third) yawam (day), as the malak (king) asked, saying, "shawab (turn back / repent) to me again the shalayashay (third) yawam (day).
The malak (king) answered them Qashah; and malak (king) Rachabaim forsook the itzah (counsel) of the zaqan (old) men,

and spoke to them after the itzah (counsel) of the yalad (young) men, saying, "My ab (father) made your yoke kabad (heavy), but I will add to it. My ab (father) chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.

So the malak (king) didn't listen to the im (people); for it was brought about of Alahayam, that Yahawah might qawam (establish) his dabar (word), which he spoke by Achayah the Shayalawanay (Shilonite) to Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat.

When all Yasharaal (Israel) saw that the malak (king) didn't listen to them, the im (people) answered the malak (king), saying, "What chalaq (portion) have we in Dawad? Neither have we nachalah (inheritance) in the ban (son) of Yashay! Every ayash (man) to your ahal (tents), Yasharaal (Israel)! Now raah (see) to your own bayath (house), Dawad." So all Yasharaal (Israel) departed to their ahal (tents).
But as for the children of Yasharaal (Israel) who lived in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), Rachabaim reigned over them.

Then malak (king) Rachabaim sent Hadawaram, who was over the men subject to forced mas (labor); and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) stoned him to mawath (death) with aban (stones). malak (king) Rachabaim made amatz (speed) to ilah (get) himself up to his chariot, to flee to Yarawashalam.
So Yasharaal (Israel) rebelled against the bayath (house) of Dawad to this yawam (day).

When Rachabaim had bawaa (come) to Yarawashalam, he assembled the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Banayamayan, one maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty) alap (thousand) chosen men, who were ishah (warriors), to fight against Yasharaal (Israel), to shawab (turn back / repent) the mamalakah (kingdom) again to Rachabaim.
But the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Shamaiyah the ayash (man) of Alahayam, saying,
"amar (speak) to Rachabaim the ban (son) of Shalamah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and to all Yasharaal (Israel) in Yahawadah (Judah) and Banayamayan, saying,

‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "You shall not ilah (go) up, nor fight against your ach (brothers)! shawab (turn back / repent) every ayash (man) to his bayath (house); for this thing is of me."'" So they listened to the dabar (words) of Yahawah, and returned from going against Yarabaim.
Rachabaim lived in Yarawashalam, and built Iyar Matzawar defense in Yahawadah (Judah).
He built Bayathalacham, and Iyatam, and Thaqawai,
Bayathatzawar Zur, and Shawakah, and Idalam,
and gath (gath), and Maraashah, and Zayap,
and Adawarayam, and Lakayash, and Izaqah,
and Tzaraih, and Ayalawan, and Chabarawan, which are in Yahawadah (Judah) and in Banayamayan, fortified Iyar.
He fortified the strongholds, and nathan (put) nagayad (captains) in them, and stores of food, and shaman (oil) and yayan (wine).
He put tzanah (shields) and spears in every Iyar, and made them exceeding chazaq (strong). Yahawadah (Judah) and Banayamayan belonged to him.
The kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites) who were in all Yasharaal (Israel) resorted to him out of all their border.

Lawayay the Levites left their suburbs and their achazah (possession), and came to Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam: for Yarabaim and his ban (sons) cast them off, that they should not execute the kahan (priest's) office to Yahawah;
and he appointed him kahan (priests) for the bamah (high) places, and for the male Shaiyar, and for the calves which he had made.

achar (after) them, out of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), such as nathan (set) their labab (hearts) to seek Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), came to Yarawashalam to zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers).

So they strengthened the malakawath (kingdom) of Yahawadah (Judah), and made Rachabaim the ban (son) of Shalamah amatz (strong), shalawash (three) Shanah; for they walked shalawash (three) Shanah in the darak (way) of Dawad and Shalamah.
Rachabaim took him a ashah (wife), Machalath the bath (daughter) of Yarayamawath the ban (son) of Dawad, and of Abayahayal the bath (daughter) of Alayaab the ban (son) of Yashay;
and she bore him ban (sons): Yaiwash, and Shamarayah, and Zaham.
achar (after) her he took Maikah the bath (daughter) of Abayashalawam; and she bore him Abayah, and Ithay, and Zayazaa, and Shalamayath.

Rachabaim loved Maikah the bath (daughter) of Abayashalawam above all his wives and his concubines: (for he took eighteen wives, and shashayam (sixty) concubines, and became the father of isharayam (twenty) - shamanah (eight) ban (sons) and shashayam (sixty) bath (daughters).)
Rachabaim appointed Abayah the ban (son) Maikah Maacah to be raash (chief), the nagayad (prince) among his ach (brothers); for he intended to make him malak (king).

He dealt wisely, and dispersed of all his ban (sons) throughout all the aratz (lands) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Banayamayan, to every fortified Iyar: and he gave them food in abundance. He sought for them many wives.
It happened, when the malakawath (kingdom) of Rachabaim was established, and he was chazaqah (strong), that he forsook the thawarah (law) of Yahawah, and all Yasharaal (Israel) with him.
It happened in the chamayashay (fifth) Shanah of malak (king) Rachabaim, that Shayashaq malak (king) of Matzarayam came up against Yarawashalam, because they had trespassed against Yahawah,

with twelve maah (hundred) chariots, and shashayam (sixty) alap (thousand) horsemen. The im (people) were without number who came with him out of Matzarayam: the Lawabay (Lubim), the Sakay, and the Kawashay (Ethiopians).
He took the fortified Iyar which pertained to Yahawadah (Judah), and came to Yarawashalam.

Now Shamaiyah the nabayaa (prophet) came to Rachabaim, and to the shar (princes) of Yahawadah (Judah), who were gathered asap (together) to Yarawashalam panayam (because) of Shayashaq, and said to them, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘You have forsaken me, therefore have I also left you in the yad (hand) of Shayashaq.'
Then the shar (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel) and the malak (king) humbled themselves; and they said, "Yahawah is tzadayaq (righteous).

When Yahawah saw that they humbled themselves, the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Shamaiyah, saying, "They have humbled themselves. I will not shachath (destroy) them; but I will nathan (grant) them Mait palayatah (deliverance), and my chamah (wrath) shall not be poured out on Yarawashalam by the yad (hand) of Shayashaq.
Nevertheless they shall be his ibad (servants), that they may yadai (know) my ibadah (service), and the ibadah (service) of the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (countries).

So Shayashaq malak (king) of Matzarayam came up against Yarawashalam, and took away the treasures of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the treasures of the malak (king's) bayath (house). He took it all away. He also took away the magan (shields) of gold which Shalamah had made.
malak (king) Rachabaim made in their place magan (shields) of brass, and committed them to the yad (hands) of the shar (captains) of the guard, who kept the door of the malak (king's) bayath (house).
It was so, that as often as the malak (king) entered into the bayath (house) of Yahawah, the guard came and bore them, and brought them shawab (turn back / repent) into the guard room.
When he humbled himself, the ap (wrath) of Yahawah turned from him, so as not to shachath (destroy) him altogether: and moreover in Yahawadah (Judah) there were tawab (good) things found.

So malak (king) Rachabaim strengthened himself in Yarawashalam, and reigned: for Rachabaim was arabaiyam (forty) - one Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign), and he reigned seventeen Shanah in Yarawashalam, the Iyar which Yahawah had chosen out of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), to shawam (put) his sham (name) there: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Naimah the Imawanayath.
He did that which was rai (evil), because he didn't kawan (set) his lab (heart) to seek Yahawah.

Now the dabar (acts) of Rachabaim, raashawan (first) and Acharawan, aren't they written in the histories of Shamaiyah the nabayaa (prophet) and of Idaw the chazah (seer), after the yachash (way) of genealogies? There were wars between Rachabaim and Yarabaim yawam (continually).
Rachabaim slept with his abawath (fathers), and was buried in the Iyar of Dawad: and Abayah his ban (son) reigned in his place.
In the eighteenth Shanah of malak (king) Yarabaim began Abayah to malak (reign) over Yahawadah (Judah).
He reigned shalawash (three) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Mayakayahaw the bath (daughter) of Awarayaal of Gabaih. There was war between Abayah and Yarabaim.

Abayah joined battle with an chayal (army) of gabawar (valiant) men of war, even arabai (four) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) chosen men: and Yarabaim set the battle in array against him with shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) chosen men, who were ayash (mighty) men of valor.
Abayah stood up on har (mount) Tzamarayam, which is in the har (hill) country of Aparayam, and said, "Hear me, Yarabaim and all Yasharaal (Israel):

Ought you not to yadai (know) that Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), gave the mamalakah (kingdom) over Yasharaal (Israel) to Dawad iwalam (forever), even to him and to his ban (sons) by a barayath (covenant) of Malach?
Yet Yarabaim the ban (son) of Nabat, the ibad (servant) of Shalamah the ban (son) of Dawad, rose up, and rebelled against his Adawan.

There were gathered to him worthless men, base anawash (fellows), who strengthened themselves against Rachabaim the ban (son) of Shalamah, when Rachabaim was nair (young) and Rak, and could not chazaq (withstand) them.

"Now you amar (think) to chazaq (withstand) the kingdom of Yahawah in the yad (hand) of the ban (sons) of Dawad; and you are a rab (great) multitude, and there are with you the golden calves which Yarabaim made you for Alahayam.

Haven't you driven out the kahan (priests) of Yahawah, the ban (sons) of Aharawan, and the Lawayay (Levites), and made kahan (priests) for yourselves after the ways of the im (peoples) of other aratz (lands)? so that whoever bawaa (comes) to malaa (consecrate) himself with a ban (young) bull and shabai (seven) ayal (rams), the same may be a kahan (priest) of those who are no Alahayam.

"But as for us, Yahawah is our Alahayam, and we have not forsaken him; and we have kahan (priests) ministering to Yahawah, the ban (sons) of Aharawan, and the Lawayay (Levites) in their malaakah (work):

and they qatar (burn) to Yahawah every baqar (morning) and every evening burnt ilah (offerings) and sweet incense. They also set the show lacham (bread) in order on the tahawar (pure) table; and the lampstand of gold with its nayar (lamps), to bair (burn) every evening: for we shamar (keep) the instruction of Yahawah our Alahayam; but you have forsaken him.

Behold, Alahayam is with us at our raash (head), and his kahan (priests) with the trumpets of rawai (alarm) to rawai (sound) an alarm against you. Children of Yasharaal (Israel), don't fight against Yahawah, the Alahayam of your abawath (fathers); for you shall not tzalach (prosper).
But Yarabaim caused an ambush to bawaa (come) sabab (about) achar (behind) them: so they were panayam (before) Yahawadah (Judah), and the ambush was achar (behind) them.
When Yahawadah (Judah) looked panah (back), behold, the battle was panayam (before) and behind them; and they cried to Yahawah, and the kahan (priests) sounded with the trumpets.

Then the men of Yahawadah (Judah) gave a rawai (shout): and as the men of Yahawadah (Judah) shouted, it happened, that Alahayam struck Yarabaim and all Yasharaal (Israel) panayam (before) Abayah and Yahawadah (Judah).
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) fled panayam (before) Yahawadah (Judah); and Alahayam delivered them into their yad (hand).
Abayah and his im (people) killed them with a rab (great) makah (slaughter): so there napal (fell) down Chalal of Yasharaal (Israel) chamash (five) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) chosen men.

Thus the children of Yasharaal (Israel) were brought under at that ith (time), and the children of Yahawadah (Judah) prevailed, because they relied on Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers).
Abayah pursued achar (after) Yarabaim, and took Iyar from him, Bayathaal with its bath (towns), and Yashanah with its bath (towns), and Iparawan with its bath (towns).
Yarabaim didn't itzar (recover) kach (strength) again in the yawam (days) of Abayah. Yahawah struck him, and he died.
But Abayah grew chazaq (mighty), and took to himself fourteen wives, and became the father of isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) ban (sons), and sixteen bath (daughters).
The yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Abayah, and his darak (ways), and his dabar (sayings), are written in the commentary of the nabayaa (prophet) Idaw.

So Abayah slept with his abawath (fathers), and they buried him in the Iyar of Dawad; and Asaa his ban (son) reigned in his place. In his yawam (days) the aratz (land) was shaqat (quiet) ishar (ten) Shanah.
Asaa did that which was tawab (good) and yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah his Alahayam:
for he took sawar (away) the foreign mazabach (altars), and the bamah (high) places, and broke down the matzabah (pillars), and cut down the Asharah,
and commanded Yahawadah (Judah) to seek Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers), and to do the thawarah (law) and the matzawah (commandment).
Also he took sawar (away) out of all the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah) the bamah (high) places and the sun chaman (images): and the mamalakah (kingdom) was shaqat (quiet) panayam (before) him.
He built fortified Iyar in Yahawadah (Judah); for the aratz (land) was shaqat (quiet), and he had no war in those Shanah, because Yahawah had given him nawach (rest).

For he said to Yahawadah (Judah), "Let us banah (build) these Iyar, and make walls around them, with magadal (towers), gates, and bars. The aratz (land) is yet panayam (before) us, because we have sought Yahawah our Alahayam; we have sought him, and he has given us nawach (rest) on every side." So they built and prospered.

Asaa had an chayal (army) that bore tzanah (bucklers) and spears, out of Yahawadah (Judah) shalawash (three) maah (hundred) alap (thousand); and out of Banayamayan, that bore magan (shields) and drew qashath (bows), two maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty) alap (thousand): all these were gabawar (mighty) men of valor.
There came out against them Zarach the Kawashay (Ethiopian) with an chayal (army) of a million troops, and shalawash (three) maah (hundred) chariots; and he came to Maraashah.
Then Asaa went out to panayam (meet) him, and they set the battle in array in the Gayaa of Tzapathah at Maraashah.

Asaa cried to Yahawah his Alahayam, and said, "Yahawah, there is none besides you to help, between the rab (mighty) and him who has no kach (strength). Help us, Yahawah our Alahayam; for we shain (rely) on you, and in your sham (name) are we bawaa (come) against this multitude. Yahawah, you are our Alahayam. Don't let anawash (man) itzar (prevail) against you.
So Yahawah struck the Kawashay (Ethiopians) panayam (before) Asaa, and panayam (before) Yahawadah (Judah); and the Kawashay (Ethiopians) fled.

Asaa and the im (people) who were with him pursued them to Garar: and there napal (fell) of the Kawashay (Ethiopians) so many that they could not machayah (recover) themselves; for they were destroyed panayam (before) Yahawah, and panayam (before) his machanah (army); and they carried nashaa (away) very much booty.
They struck all the Iyar around Garar; for the pachad (fear) of Yahawah came on them: and they despoiled all the Iyar; for there was much spoil in them.
They struck also the ahal (tents) of livestock, and carried away sheep in abundance, and camels, and returned to Yarawashalam.
The rawach (spirit) of Alahayam came on Izarayah the ban (son) of Iwadad:

and he went out to panayam (meet) Asaa, and said to him, "Hear me, Asaa, and all Yahawadah (Judah) and Banayamayan! Yahawah is with you, while you are with him; and if you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will forsake you.
Now for a rab (long) yawam (time) Yasharaal (Israel) was laa (without) the amath (true) Alahayam, and without a teaching kahan (priest), and without thawarah (law).
But when in their tzar (distress) they turned to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), and sought him, he was found by them.
In those ith (times) there was no shalawam (peace) to him who went out, nor to him who came in; but rab (great) troubles were on all the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (lands).
They were broken in pieces, gaway (nation) against gaway (nation), and Iyar against Iyar; for Alahayam troubled them with all tzarah (adversity).
But you be chazaq (strong), and don't let your yad (hands) be rapah (slack); for your pailah (work) shall be rewarded.

When Asaa heard these dabar (words), and the nabawaah (prophecy) of Iwadad the nabayaa (prophet), he took chazaq (courage), and ibar (put) away the shaqawatz (abominations) out of all the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Banayamayan, and out of the Iyar which he had taken from the har (hill) country of Aparayam; and he renewed the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah, that was panayam (before) the porch of Yahawah.

He gathered all Yahawadah (Judah) and Banayamayan, and those who lived with them out of Aparayam and Manashah, and out of Shamaiwan: for they napal (fell) to him out of Yasharaal (Israel) in abundance, when they saw that Yahawah his Alahayam was with him.
So they gathered themselves together at Yarawashalam in the shalayashay (third) chadash (month), in the fifteenth Shanah of the malakawath (reign) of Asaa.
They sacrificed to Yahawah in that yawam (day), of the spoil which they had brought, shabai (seven) maah (hundred) baqar (head) of cattle and shabai (seven) alap (thousand) sheep.
They entered into the barayath (covenant) to seek Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers), with all their labab (heart) and with all their napash (soul);
and that whoever would not seek Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), should be put to mawath (death), whether qatan (small) or gadawal (great), whether ayash (man) or ashah (woman).
They swore to Yahawah with a gadawal (loud) qawal (voice), and with shouting, and with trumpets, and with cornets.

All Yahawadah (Judah) Shamach at the shabawaih (oath); for they had sworn with all their labab (heart), and sought him with their whole desire; and he was found of them: and Yahawah gave them nawach (rest) all around.

Maikah Maacah, the am (mother) of Asaa the malak (king), he removed from being gabayarah (queen), because she had made an abominable mapalatzath (image) Asharah an Asherah; and Asaa karath (cut) down her mapalatzath (image), and made dust of it, and burnt it at the nachal (brook) Qadarawan.
But the bamah (high) places were not taken sawar (away) out of Yasharaal (Israel): nevertheless the labab (heart) of Asaa was Shalam all his yawam (days).
He brought into the bayath (house) of Alahayam the things that his ab (father) had qadash (dedicated), and that he himself had qadash (dedicated), kasap (silver), and gold, and vessels.
There was no more war to the chamash (five) and shalawashayam (thirtieth) Shanah of the malakawath (reign) of Asaa.

In the shash (six) and shalawashayam (thirtieth) Shanah of the malakawath (reign) of Asaa, Baishaa king of Yasharaal (Israel) went up against Yahawadah (Judah), and built Ramah, that he might not allow anyone to yatzaa (go) out or bawaa (come) in to Asaa malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah).

Then Asaa brought out kasap (silver) and gold out of the treasures of the bayath (house) of Yahawah and of the malak (king's) bayath (house), and sent Banahadad Ben Hadad malak (king) of Aram, who lived at Damashaq, saying,

"Let there be a treaty between me and you, as there was between my ab (father) and your ab (father). Behold, I have sent you kasap (silver) and gold. yalak (go), parar (break) your treaty with Baishaa malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), that he may depart from me.

Banahadad Hadad listened to malak (king) Asaa, and sent the shar (captains) of his chayal (armies) against the Iyar of Yasharaal (Israel); and they struck Iyawan, and Dan, and Abalamayam Maim, and all the storage Iyar of Napathalay.
It happened, when Baishaa heard of it, that he left off building Ramah, and let his malaakah (work) shabath (cease).

Then Asaa the malak (king) took all Yahawadah (Judah); and they carried nashaa (away) the aban (stones) of Ramah, and its itz (timber), with which Baishaa had built; and he built therewith Gabai and Matzapah.

At that ith (time) Chananay the seer came to Asaa malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and said to him, "Because you have relied on the malak (king) of Aram, and have not relied on Yahawah your Alahayam, therefore is the chayal (army) of the malak (king) of Aram escaped out of your yad (hand).

Weren't the Kawashay (Ethiopians) and the Lawabay (Lubim) a huge chayal (army), with chariots and horsemen maad (exceeding) many? Yet, because you relied on Yahawah, he delivered them into your yad (hand).

For the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah run back and forth throughout the whole aratz (earth), to show himself chazaq (strong) in the behalf of them whose labab (heart) is Shalam toward him. Herein you have done foolishly; for from henceforth you shall have wars.

Then Asaa was kais (angry) with the seer, and nathan (put) him in the prison; for he was in a zaip (rage) with him because of this thing. Asaa oppressed some of the im (people) at the same ith (time).
Behold, the dabar (acts) of Asaa, raashawan (first) and Acharawan, behold, they are written in the book of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Yasharaal (Israel).

In the shalawashayam (thirty) - ninth Shanah of his malakawath (reign) Asaa was diseased in his feet; his disease was exceeding great: yet in his disease he didn't seek Yahawah, but to the physicians.
Asaa slept with his abawath (fathers), and died in the one and fortieth Shanah of his malak (reign).

They buried him in his own tombs, which he had dug out for himself in the Iyar of Dawad, and laid him in the bed which was filled with sweet odors and various kinds of spices prepared by the perfumers' maishah (art): and they made a very gadawal (great) burning for him.
Yahawashapat his ban (son) reigned in his place, and strengthened himself against Yasharaal (Israel).

He placed chayal (forces) in all the fortified Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and nathan (set) garrisons in the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the Iyar of Aparayam, which Asaa his ab (father) had taken.
Yahawah was with Yahawashapat, because he walked in the raashawan (first) darak (ways) of his ab (father) Dawad, and didn't seek the Bail,
but sought to the Alahayam of his ab (father), and walked in his matzawah (commandments), and not after the maishah (doings) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Therefore Yahawah established the mamalakah (kingdom) in his yad (hand); and all Yahawadah (Judah) brought to Yahawashapat tribute; and he had riches and honor in abundance.
His lab (heart) was lifted up in the darak (ways) of Yahawah: and furthermore he took sawar (away) the bamah (high) places and the Asharah out of Yahawadah (Judah).

Also in the shalawash (third) Shanah of his malak (reign) he sent his shar (princes), even Banachayal Hail, and Ibadayah, and Zakarayah, and Nathanaal, and Mayakayahaw, to teach in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah);

and Lawayay them the Levites, even Shamaiyah, and Nathanayah, and Zabadayah, and Ishahaal, and Shamayaramawath, and Yahawanathan, and Adanayah, and Tawabayah, and Tawabaadanayahaw, the Lawayay (Levites); and with them Alayashamai and Yahawaram, the kahan (priests).

They taught in Yahawadah (Judah), having the book of the thawarah (law) of Yahawah with them; and they went sabab (about) throughout all the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and taught among the im (people).
The pachad (fear) of Yahawah fell on all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (lands) that were around Yahawadah (Judah), so that they made no war against Yahawashapat.

Some of the Palashathay (Philistines) brought Yahawashapat manachah (presents), and kasap (silver) for tribute; the Irabay (Arabians) also brought him flocks, shabai (seven) alap (thousand) and shabai (seven) maah (hundred) ayal (rams), and shabai (seven) alap (thousand) and shabai (seven) maah (hundred) male goats.
Yahawashapat grew great exceedingly; and he built in Yahawadah (Judah) castles and Iyar of store.
He had many malaakah (works) in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah); and men of war, mighty men of valor, in Yarawashalam.

This was the numbering of them according to their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses): Of Yahawadah (Judah), the shar (captains) of alap (thousands): Idanah the shar (captain), and with him gabawar (mighty) men of valor shalawash (three) maah (hundred) alap (thousand);
and next to him Yahawachanan the shar (captain), and with him two maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty) alap (thousand);
and next to him Imasayah the ban (son) of Zakaray, who willingly offered himself to Yahawah; and with him two maah (hundred) alap (thousand) gabawar (mighty) men of valor.
Of Banayamayan: Alayadai a gabawar (mighty) man of valor, and with him two maah (hundred) alap (thousand) armed with qashath (bow) and magan (shield);
and next to him Yahawazabad and with him one maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty) alap (thousand) chalatz (ready) prepared for tzabaa (war).
These were those who waited on the malak (king), besides those whom the malak (king) nathan (put) in the fortified Iyar throughout all Yahawadah (Judah).
Now Yahawashapat had riches and honor in abundance; and he joined chathan (affinity) with Achaab.

After certain Shanah he went down to Achaab to Shamarawan. Achaab killed sheep and cattle for him in abundance, and for the im (people) who were with him, and moved him to ilah (go) up with him to Ramathagalaid Gilead.

Achaab malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) said to Yahawashapat malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), "Will you yalak (go) with me to Ramathagalaid Gilead?" He answered him, "I am as you are, and my im (people) as your im (people). We will be with you in the war.
Yahawashapat said to the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), "Please inquire first for the dabar (word) of Yahawah.

Then the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) gathered the nabayaa (prophets) together, arabai (four) maah (hundred) men, and said to them, "Shall we yalak (go) to Ramathagalaid Gilead to battle, or shall I chadal (forbear)?" They said, "ilah (go) up; for Alahayam will nathan (deliver) it into the yad (hand) of the malak (king).
But Yahawashapat said, "Isn't there here a nabayaa (prophet) of Yahawah besides, that we may inquire of him?

The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) said to Yahawashapat, "There is yet one ayash (man) by whom we may inquire of Yahawah; but I shanaa (hate) him, for he never nabaa (prophesies) tawab (good) concerning me, but yawam (always) rai (evil). He is Mayakayahaw the ban (son) of Yamalaa." Yahawashapat said, "Don't let the malak (king) amar (say) so.
Then the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) called an officer, and said, "Get Mayakahaw the ban (son) of Yamalaa quickly.

Now the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawashapat the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) sat ayash (each) on his kasaa (throne), Labash in their bagad (robes), and they were sitting in an open place at the entrance of the gate of Shamarawan; and all the nabayaa (prophets) were nabaa (prophesying) panayam (before) them.
Tzadaqayah the ban (son) of Kanainah made him qaran (horns) of barazal (iron), and said, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘With these you shall push the Aram (Syrians), until they are consumed.'
All the nabayaa (prophets) prophesied so, saying, "ilah (go) up to Ramathagalaid Gilead, and tzalach (prosper); for Yahawah will nathan (deliver) it into the yad (hand) of the malak (king).

The malaak (messenger) who went to qaraa (call) Mayakayahaw spoke to him, saying, "Behold, the dabar (words) of the nabayaa (prophets) declare tawab (good) to the malak (king) with one mouth. Let your dabar (word) therefore, please be like one of theirs, and dabar (speak) tawab (good).
Mayakayahaw said, "As Yahawah chay (lives), what my Alahayam amar (says), that will I dabar (speak).

When he had bawaa (come) to the malak (king), the malak (king) said to him, "Mayakah, shall we yalak (go) to Ramathagalaid Gilead to battle, or shall I chadal (forbear)?" He said, "ilah (go) up, and tzalach (prosper). They shall be delivered into your yad (hand).
The malak (king) said to him, "How many paim (times) shall I shabai (adjure) you that you dabar (speak) to me nothing but the truth in the sham (name) of Yahawah?

He said, "I saw all Yasharaal (Israel) scattered on the har (mountains), as sheep that have no raih (shepherd). Yahawah said, ‘These have no adawan (master). Let them shawab (turn back / repent) every ayash (man) to his bayath (house) in shalawam (peace).'
The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) said to Yahawashapat, "Didn't I amar (tell) you that he would not nabaa (prophesy) tawab (good) concerning me, but rai (evil)?

Micaiah said, "Therefore hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah: I saw Yahawah sitting on his kasaa (throne), and all the tzabaa (army) of shamayam (heaven) standing on his right yamayan (hand) and on his shamaawal (left).

Yahawah said, ‘Who shall entice Achaab malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), that he may ilah (go) up and napal (fall) at Ramathagalaid Gilead?' One spoke saying in this kakah (way), and another saying in that kakah (way).
A rawach (spirit) came out, stood panayam (before) Yahawah, and said, ‘I will entice him.' "Yahawah said to him, ‘How?'

"He said, ‘I will yatzaa (go) forth, and will be a lying rawach (spirit) in the pah (mouth) of all his nabayaa (prophets).' "He said, ‘You will entice him, and will yakal (prevail) also. yatzaa (go) forth, and do so.'
"Now therefore, behold, Yahawah has nathan (put) a lying rawach (spirit) in the pah (mouth) of these your nabayaa (prophets); and Yahawah has spoken rai (evil) concerning you.
Then Tzadaqayah the ban (son) of Kanainah came near, and struck Mayakayahaw on the Lachay, and said, "Which darak (way) did the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah ibar (go) from me to dabar (speak) to you?
Mayakayahaw said, "raah (see), you shall see on that yawam (day), when you shall bawaa (go) into an inner room to hide yourself.
The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) said, "Take Mayakayahaw, and shawab (turn back / repent) him back to Amawan the shar (governor) of the Iyar, and to Yawaash the malak (king's) ban (son);

and amar (say), ‘Thus amar (says) the malak (king), "shawam (put) this fellow in the bayath (prison), and akal (feed) him with lacham (bread) of affliction and with mayam (water) of affliction, until I shawab (turn back / repent) in shalawam (peace)."'
Mayakayahaw said, "If you shawab (turn back / repent) at all in shalawam (peace), Yahawah has not spoken by me." He said, "Listen, you im (peoples), all of you!
So the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawashapat the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) went up to Ramathagalaid Gilead.

The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) said to Yahawashapat, "I will disguise myself, and bawaa (go) into the battle; but you Labash on your bagad (robes)." So the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) disguised himself; and they went into the battle.

Now the malak (king) of Aram had tzawah (commanded) the shar (captains) of his chariots, saying, "Fight neither with qatan (small) nor gadawal (great), except only with the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).

It happened, when the shar (captains) of the chariots saw Yahawashapat, that they said, "It is the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)!" Therefore they turned around to fight against him. But Yahawashapat cried out, and Yahawah helped him; and Alahayam moved them to depart from him.
It happened, when the shar (captains) of the chariots saw that it was not the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), that they turned shawab (turn back / repent) from achar (pursuing) him.

A certain mashak (man) drew his qashath (bow) at random, and struck the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) between the joints of the armor. Therefore he said to the driver of the rakab (chariot), "hapak (turn) your yad (hand), and yatzaa (carry) me out of the machanah (army); for I am severely chalah (wounded).

The battle increased that yawam (day). However the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) propped himself up in his chariot against the Aram (Syrians) until the evening; and about the ith (time) of the going down of the shamash (sun), he died.
Yahawashapat the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) returned to his bayath (house) in shalawam (peace) to Yarawashalam.

Yahawaa the ban (son) of Chananay the chazah (seer) went out to panayam (meet) him, and said to malak (king) Yahawashapat, "Should you help the rashai (wicked), and ahab (love) those who shanaa (hate) Yahawah? Because of this, qatzap (wrath) is on you from panayam (before) Yahawah.
Nevertheless there are tawab (good) things found in you, in that you have bair (put) away the Asharah out of the aratz (land), and have kawan (set) your labab (heart) to seek Alahayam.

Yahawashapat lived at Yarawashalam: and he went out again among the im (people) Baarashabai Beersheba to the har (hill) country of Aparayam, and brought them shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers).
He imad (set) shapat (judges) in the aratz (land) throughout all the fortified Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), Iyar by Iyar,
and said to the shapat (judges), "raah (see) what you do: for you don't shapat (judge) for adam (man), but for Yahawah; and he is with you in the dabar (judgment).

Now therefore let the pachad (fear) of Yahawah be on you. shamar (take) heed and do it: for there is no iwal (iniquity) with Yahawah our Alahayam, nor respect of panayam (persons), nor taking of shachad (bribes).

Moreover in Yarawashalam Yahawashapat appointed Lawayay (Levites) and kahan (priests), and of the raash (heads) of the abawath (fathers)' households of Yasharaal (Israel), for the mashapat (judgment) of Yahawah, and for rayab (controversies). They returned to Yarawashalam.
He tzawah (commanded) them, saying, "Thus you shall do in the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah, faithfully, and with a Shalam labab (heart).

Whenever any controversy shall bawaa (come) to you from your ach (brothers) who yashab (dwell) in their Iyar, between dam (blood) and dam (blood), between thawarah (law) and matzawah (commandment), chaq (statutes) and mashapat (ordinances), you shall warn them, that they not be asham (guilty) towards Yahawah, and so qatzap (wrath) come on you and on your ach (brothers). Do this, and you shall not be asham (guilty).

Behold, Amarayah the raash (chief) kahan (priest) is over you in all dabar (matters) of Yahawah; and Zabadayah the ban (son) of Yashamaial, the nagayad (ruler) of the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah), in all the malak (king's) dabar (matters): Lawayay the Levites shall be shatar (officers) panayam (before) you. ishah (deal) courageously, and may Yahawah be with the tawab (good).
It happened achar (after) this, that the children of Mawaab, and the children of Imawan, and with them some of the Imawanay (Ammonites), came against Yahawashapat to battle.

Then some came who told Yahawashapat, saying, "A rab (great) multitude is coming ibar (against) you from beyond the yam (sea) from Aram. Behold, they are in Hazazon Chatzatzawanathamar" (that is, Iyanagaday Gedi).
Yahawashapat was alarmed, and nathan (set) panayam (himself) to seek to Yahawah. He proclaimed a fast throughout all Yahawadah (Judah).
Yahawadah (Judah) gathered themselves together, to seek help from Yahawah. They came out of all the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah) to seek Yahawah.
Yahawashapat stood in the qahal (assembly) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam, in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, panayam (before) the Chadash court;

and he said, "Yahawah, the Alahayam of our abawath (fathers), aren't you Alahayam in shamayam (heaven)? Aren't you ruler over all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the gawayam (nations)? kach (power) and might are in your yad (hand), so that no yatzab (one) is able to withstand you.

Didn't you, our Alahayam, yarash (drive) out the yashab (inhabitants) of this aratz (land) panayam (before) your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), and nathan (give) it to the zarai (seed) of Abaraham your ahab (friend) iwalam (forever)?
They lived in it, and have built you a maqadash (sanctuary) in it for your sham (name), saying,

‘If rai (evil) bawaa (comes) on us—the charab (sword), shapawat (judgment), dabar (pestilence), or famine—we will imad (stand) before this bayath (house), and panayam (before) you, (for your sham (name) is in this bayath (house)), and cry to you in our tzarah (affliction), and you will hear and yashai (save).'

Now, behold, the children of Imawan and Mawaab and har (mount) Shaiyar, whom you would not let Yasharaal (Israel) bawaa (invade), when they came out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, but they turned aside from them, and didn't destroy them;
behold, how they gamal (reward) us, to bawaa (come) to cast us out of your yarashah (possession), which you have given us to yarash (inherit).

Our Alahayam, will you not shapat (judge) them? For we have no might panayam (against) this rab (great) company that bawaa (comes) against us; neither yadai (know) we what to do, but our iyan (eyes) are on you.
All Yahawadah (Judah) stood panayam (before) Yahawah, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.

Then the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah came on Yachazayaal the ban (son) of Zakarayah, the ban (son) of Banayah, the ban (son) of Yaiyaal, the ban (son) of Mathanayah, the Lawayay (Levite), of the ban (sons) of Asap, in the midst of the qahal (assembly);

and he said, "Listen, all Yahawadah (Judah), and you yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, and you malak (king) Yahawashapat. Thus amar (says) Yahawah to you, ‘Don't be yaraa (afraid), neither be dismayed by panayam (reason) of this rab (great) multitude; for the battle is not yours, but alahayam (god's).

Tomorrow yarad (go) down against them. Behold, they are coming up by the ascent of Tzayatz. You shall matzaa (find) them at the end of the nachal (valley), panayam (before) the madabar (wilderness) of Yarawaal.

You will not need to fight this battle. Set yourselves, imad (stand) still, and raah (see) the yashawaih (salvation) of Yahawah with you, O Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam. Don't be yaraa (afraid), nor be dismayed. yatzaa (go) out panayam (against) them tomorrow, for Yahawah is with you.'

Yahawashapat bowed his head with his ap (face) to the aratz (ground); and all Yahawadah (Judah) and the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam napal (fell) down panayam (before) Yahawah, worshipping Yahawah.

The Lawayay (Levites), of the children of the Qahathay (Kohathites) and of the children of the qarachay (korahites), stood up to halal (praise) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), with an exceeding gadawal (loud) qawal (voice).

They rose shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and went yatzaa (forth) into the madabar (wilderness) of Thaqawai: and as they went yatzaa (forth), Yahawashapat stood and said, "Listen to me, Yahawadah (Judah), and you yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam! aman (believe) in Yahawah your Alahayam, so you shall be established! aman (believe) his nabayaa (prophets), so you shall tzalach (prosper).

When he had taken yaitz (counsel) with the im (people), he appointed those who should shayar (sing) to Yahawah, and give halal (praise) in qadash (holy) array, as they went out panayam (before) the army, and amar (say), Give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah; for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever).

When they began to sing and to thahalah (praise), Yahawah nathan (set) ambushers against the children of Imawan, Mawaab, and har (mount) Shaiyar, who had bawaa (come) against Yahawadah (Judah); and they were struck.

For the children of Imawan and Mawaab stood up against the yashab (inhabitants) of har (mount) Shaiyar, charam (utterly) to kill and destroy them: and when they had made an kalah (end) of the yashab (inhabitants) of Shaiyar, everyone helped to mashachayath (destroy) rai (another).

When Yahawadah (Judah) came to the place overlooking the madabar (wilderness), they looked at the multitude; and behold, they were pagar (dead) bodies fallen to the aratz (earth), and there were none who palayatah (escaped).

When Yahawashapat and his im (people) came to take their spoil, they found among them in abundance both riches and pagar (dead) bodies, and precious jewels, which they stripped off for themselves, more than they could mashaa (carry) away: and they were shalawash (three) yawam (days) in taking the spoil, it was so much.

On the rabayaiy (fourth) yawam (day) they assembled themselves in the valley Barakah Beracah; for there they blessed Yahawah: therefore the sham (name) of that place was called The valley Barakah Beracah to this yawam (day).

Then they returned, every ayash (man) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam, and Yahawashapat in their raash (forefront), to shawab (turn back / repent) again to Yarawashalam with joy; for Yahawah had made them to Shamach over their ayab (enemies).
They came to Yarawashalam with stringed instruments and harps and trumpets to the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
The pachad (fear) of Alahayam was on all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (countries), when they heard that Yahawah fought against the ayab (enemies) of Yasharaal (Israel).
So the malakawath (realm) of Yahawashapat was shaqat (quiet); for his Alahayam gave him nawach (rest) all around.

Yahawashapat reigned over Yahawadah (Judah): he was shalawashayam (thirty) - chamash (five) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Izawabah the bath (daughter) of Shalachay.
He walked in the darak (way) of Asaa his ab (father), and didn't sawar (turn) aside from it, doing that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah.
However the bamah (high) places were not taken sawar (away); neither as yet had the im (people) kawan (set) their labab (hearts) to the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yahawashapat, raashawan (first) and Acharawan, behold, they are written in the history of Yahawaa the ban (son) of Chananay, which is inserted in the book of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel).
achar (after) this Yahawashapat malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) joined himself with Achazayah malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel). The same did very wickedly:
and he joined himself with him to ishah (make) ships to yalak (go) to Tharashayash; and they made the ships in Itzayawanagabar Geber.

Then Alayaizar the ban (son) Dawadawahaw Dodavahu of Maraashah prophesied against Yahawashapat, saying, "Because you have joined yourself with Achazayah, Yahawah has destroyed your maishah (works)." The ships were broken, so that they were not itzar (able) to yalak (go) to Tharashayash.
Yahawashapat slept with his abawath (fathers), and was buried with his abawath (fathers) in the Iyar of Dawad: and Yahawaram his ban (son) reigned in his place.

He had ach (brothers), the ban (sons) of Yahawashapat: Izarayah, and Yachayaal, and Zakarayah, and Izarayah, and Mayakaal, and Shapatayah; all these were the ban (sons) of Yahawashapat malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Their ab (father) gave them rab (great) mathanah (gifts), of kasap (silver), and of gold, and of precious things, with fortified Iyar in Yahawadah (Judah): but the mamalakah (kingdom) gave he to Yahawaram, because he was the firstborn.

Now when Yahawaram was risen up over the mamalakah (kingdom) of his ab (father), and had strengthened himself, he killed all his ach (brothers) with the charab (sword), and various also of the shar (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Yahawaram was shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned shamanah (eight) Shanah in Yarawashalam.

He walked in the darak (way) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel), as did the bayath (house) of Achaab; for he had the bath (daughter) of Achaab as ashah (wife): and he did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah.

However Yahawah would not shachath (destroy) the bayath (house) of Dawad, because of the barayath (covenant) that he had made with Dawad, and as he promised to nathan (give) a nayar (lamp) to him and to his children yawam (always).
In his yawam (days) Adam revolted from under the yad (hand) of Yahawadah (Judah), and made a malak (king) over themselves.

Then Yahawaram passed over with his shar (captains), and all his chariots with him: and he rose up by layal (night), and struck the Adam (Edomites) who surrounded him, along with the shar (captains) of the chariots.

So Adam revolted from under the yad (hand) of Yahawadah (Judah) to this yawam (day): then Labanah revolted at the same ith (time) from under his yad (hand), because he had forsaken Yahawah, the Alahayam of his abawath (fathers).
Moreover he made bamah (high) places in the har (mountains) of Yahawadah (Judah), and made the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam to play the prostitute, and led Yahawadah (Judah) astray.

A letter came to him from Alayah the nabayaa (prophet), saying, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Dawad your ab (father), ‘Because you have not walked in the darak (ways) of Yahawashapat your ab (father), nor in the darak (ways) of Asaa malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah),

but have walked in the darak (way) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel), and have made Yahawadah (Judah) and the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam to play the prostitute, like the bayath (house) of Achaab did, and also have slain your ach (brothers) of your ab (father's) bayath (house), who were tawab (better) than yourself:
behold, Yahawah will nagap (strike) with a gadawal (great) magapah (plague) your im (people), and your children, and your wives, and all your rakawash (substance);
and you shall have rab (great) sickness by disease of your maih (bowels), until your maih (bowels) yatzaa (fall) out by reason of the sickness, yawam (day) by yawam (day).'
Yahawah stirred up against Yahawaram the rawach (spirit) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and of the Irabay (Arabians) who are beside the Kawashay (Ethiopians):

and they came up against Yahawadah (Judah), and broke into it, and carried away all the rakawash (substance) that was found in the malak (king's) bayath (house), and his ban (sons) also, and his wives; so that there was never a ban (son) shaar (left) him, except Yahawaachaz, the youngest of his ban (sons).
achar (after) all this Yahawah struck him in his maih (bowels) with an incurable disease.

It happened, in process of yawam (time), at the end of shanayam (two) yawam (years), that his maih (bowels) fell out by reason of his sickness, and he died of severe diseases. His im (people) made no burning for him, like the burning of his abawath (fathers).

shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) years ban (old) was he when he began to malak (reign), and he reigned in Yarawashalam shamanah (eight) Shanah: and he departed without being desired; and they buried him in the Iyar of Dawad, but not in the tombs of the malak (kings).

The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place; for the band of men who came with the Arabians to the camp had slain all the eldest. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigned.

arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two) Shanah ban (old) was Achazayah when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned one Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Ithalayah the bath (daughter) of Imaray.
He also walked in the darak (ways) of the bayath (house) of Achaab; for his am (mother) was his yaitz (counselor) to do wickedly.

He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, as did the bayath (house) of Achaab; for they were his yaitz (counselors) achar (after) the mawath (death) of his ab (father), to his mashachayath (destruction).

He walked also after their itzah (counsel), and went with Yahawaram the ban (son) of Achaab malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) to war against Chazaal malak (king) of Aram at Ramathagalaid Gilead: and the Ramay (Syrians) wounded Yawaram.

He returned to be healed in Yazaraial of the makah (wounds) which they had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Chazaal malak (king) of Aram. Izarayah the ban (son) of Yahawaram malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) went down to raah (see) Yahawaram the ban (son) of Achaab in Yazaraial, because he was chalah (sick).

Now the destruction of Achazayah was of Alahayam, in that he went to Yawaram: for when he had bawaa (come), he went out with Yahawaram against Yahawaa the ban (son) of Namashay, whom Yahawah had mashach (anointed) to karath (cut) off the bayath (house) of Achaab.

It happened, when Yahawaa was executing shapat (judgment) on the bayath (house) of Achaab, that he found the shar (princes) of Yahawadah (Judah), and the ban (sons) of the ach (brothers) of Achazayah, ministering to Achazayah, and killed them.

He sought Achazayah, and they caught him (now he was hiding in Shamarawan), and they brought him to Yahawaa, and killed him; and they buried him, for they said, "He is the ban (son) of Yahawashapat, who sought Yahawah with all his labab (heart)." The bayath (house) of Achazayah had no kach (power) to hold the mamalakah (kingdom).

Now when Ithalayah the am (mother) of Achazayah saw that her ban (son) was mawath (dead), she qawam (arose) and destroyed all the mamalakah (royal) zarai (seed) of the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah).

But Yahawashabaith, the bath (daughter) of the malak (king), took Yawaash the ban (son) of Achazayah, and stole him away from among the malak (king's) ban (sons) who were slain, and nathan (put) him and his nurse in the bedroom. So Yahawashabaith, the bath (daughter) of malak (king) Yahawaram, the ashah (wife) of Yahawayadai the kahan (priest) (for she was the achawath (sister) of Achazayah), hid him from Ithalayah, so that she didn't mawath (kill) him.
He was with them hidden in the bayath (house) of Alahayam shash (six) Shanah: and Ithalayah reigned over the aratz (land).

In the shabayaiy (seventh) Shanah Yahawayadai strengthened himself, and took the shar (captains) of maah (hundreds), Izarayah the ban (son) of Yaracham, and Yashamaial the ban (son) of Yahawachanan, and Izarayah the ban (son) of Iwabad, and Maishayah the ban (son) of Idayah, and Alayashapat the ban (son) of Zakaray, into barayath (covenant) with him.

They went sabab (about) in Yahawadah (Judah), and gathered the Lawayay (Levites) out of all the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and the raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households of Yasharaal (Israel), and they came to Yarawashalam.

All the qahal (assembly) made a barayath (covenant) with the malak (king) in the bayath (house) of Alahayam. He said to them, "Behold, the malak (king's) ban (son) shall malak (reign), as Yahawah has spoken concerning the ban (sons) of Dawad.

This is the thing that you shall do. A shalayashay (third) part of you, who bawaa (come) in on the shabath (sabbath), of the kahan (priests) and Lawayay the Levites, shall be porters of the thresholds.

A shalayashay (third) part shall be at the malak (king's) bayath (house); and a shalayashay (third) part at the gate of the yasawad (foundation). All the im (people) shall be in the courts of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house).

But let no one bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah, except the kahan (priests), and those who sharath (minister) Lawayay the Levites. They shall bawaa (come) in, for they are qadash (holy), but all the im (people) shall follow yahawah (yahweh's) instructions.

The Lawayay (Levites) shall surround the malak (king), every ayash (man) with his weapons in his yad (hand). Whoever bawaa (comes) into the bayath (house), let him be slain. Be with the malak (king) when he bawaa (comes) in, and when he goes out.

So the Lawayay (Levites) and all Yahawadah (Judah) did according to all that Yahawayadai the kahan (priest) tzawah (commanded): and they took every ayash (man) his men, those who were to bawaa (come) in on the shabath (sabbath); with those who were to yatzaa (go) out on the shabath (sabbath); for Yahawayadai the kahan (priest) didn't dismiss the shift.

Yahawayadai the kahan (priest) delivered to the shar (captains) of maah (hundreds) the spears, and magan (bucklers), and shalat (shields), that had been malak (king) Dawad, which were in the bayath (house) of Alahayam.

He imad (set) all the im (people), every ayash (man) with his shalach (weapon) in his yad (hand), from the Yamanay side of the bayath (house) to the Shamaalay side of the bayath (house), along by the mazabach (altar) and the bayath (house), around the malak (king).

Then they brought out the malak (king's) ban (son), and nathan (put) the nazar (crown) on him, and gave him the idawath (testimony), and made him malak (king): and Yahawayadai and his ban (sons) mashach (anointed) him; and they said, "Long chayah (live) the malak (king)!
When Ithalayah heard the qawal (noise) of the im (people) running and praising the malak (king), she came to the im (people) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah:

and she looked, and, behold, the malak (king) stood by his pillar at the entrance, and the shar (captains) and the trumpets by the malak (king); and all the im (people) of the aratz (land) Shamach, and blew trumpets; the singers also played musical instruments, and led the singing of halal (praise). Then Ithalayah tore her clothes, and said, "Treason! treason!

Yahawayadai the kahan (priest) brought out the shar (captains) of maah (hundreds) who were paqad (set) over the chayal (army), and said to them, "yatzaa (bring) her out between the ranks; and whoever bawaa (follows) her, let him be slain with the charab (sword)." For the kahan (priest) said, "Don't mawath (kill) her in the yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house).
So they made way for her. She went to the entrance of the horse gate to the malak (king's) bayath (house); and they killed her there.
Yahawayadai made a barayath (covenant) between himself, and all the im (people), and the malak (king), that they should be yahawah (yahweh's) im (people).

All the im (people) went to the bayath (house) of Bail, and broke it down, and broke his mazabach (altars) and his tzalam (images) in shabar (pieces), and killed Mathan the kahan (priest) of Bail panayam (before) the mazabach (altars).

Yahawayadai appointed the officers of the bayath (house) of Yahawah under the yad (hand) of the kahan (priests) the Lawayay (Levites), whom Dawad had distributed in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, to ilah (offer) the burnt ilah (offerings) of Yahawah, as it is written in the thawarah (law) of Mashah, with rejoicing and with singing, according to the yad (order) of Dawad.
He imad (set) the porters at the gates of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, that no one who was tamaa (unclean) in anything should bawaa (enter) in.

He took the shar (captains) of maah (hundreds), and the adayar (nobles), and the mashal (governors) of the im (people), and all the im (people) of the aratz (land), and brought down the malak (king) from the bayath (house) of Yahawah: and they came through the Ilayawan gate to the malak (king's) bayath (house), and yashab (set) the malak (king) on the kasaa (throne) of the mamalakah (kingdom).
So all the im (people) of the aratz (land) Shamach, and the Iyar was shaqat (quiet). Ithalayah they had slain with the charab (sword).

Yawaash was shabai (seven) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned arabaiyam (forty) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Tzabayah, Baarashabai Beersheba.
Yawaash did that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah all the yawam (days) of Yahawayadai the kahan (priest).
Yahawayadai took for him shanayam (two) wives; and he became the father of ban (sons) and bath (daughters).
It happened achar (after) this, that Yawaash intended to chadash (restore) the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

He gathered together the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites), and said to them, "yatzaa (go) out to the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and gather kasap (money) to chazaq (repair) the bayath (house) of your Alahayam from all Israel from Shanah to Shanah. See that you expedite this dabar (matter)." Lawayay the Levites didn't do it right away.

The malak (king) called for Yahawayadai the raash (chief), and said to him, "Why haven't you required Lawayay the Levites to bawaa (bring) in the tax of Mashah the ibad (servant) of Yahawah, and of the qahal (assembly) of Yasharaal (Israel), out of Yahawadah (Judah) and out of Yarawashalam, for the ahal (tent) of the idawath (testimony)?

For the ban (sons) of Ithalayah, that marashaith (wicked) paratz (woman), had broken up the bayath (house) of Alahayam; and they also gave all the qadash (dedicated) things of the bayath (house) of Yahawah to the Bail.
So the malak (king) commanded, and they made a arawan (chest), and nathan (set) it outside at the gate of the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

They made a qawal (proclamation) through Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam, to bawaa (bring) in for Yahawah the tax that Mashah the ibad (servant) of Alahayam laid on Yasharaal (Israel) in the madabar (wilderness).
All the shar (princes) and all the im (people) Shamach, and brought in, and cast into the arawan (chest), until they had made an kalah (end).

It was so, that whenever the arawan (chest) was brought to the malak (king's) officers by the yad (hand) Lawayay the Levites, and when they saw that there was much kasap (money), the malak (king's) scribe and the raash (chief) kahan (priest's) officer came and emptied the arawan (chest), and took it, and carried it to its place again. Thus they did yawam (day) by yawam (day), and gathered kasap (money) in abundance.

The malak (king) and Yahawayadai gave it to such as did the malaakah (work) of the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah; and they hired chatzab (masons) and carpenters to chadash (restore) the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and also such as worked barazal (iron) and brass to chazaq (repair) the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
So the workmen worked, and the malaakah (work) of repairing went forward in their yad (hands), and they imad (set) up the bayath (house) of Alahayam in its state, and strengthened it.

When they had made an end, they brought the shaar (rest) of the kasap (money) panayam (before) the malak (king) and Yahawayadai, of which were made vessels for the bayath (house) of Yahawah, even vessels with which to sharath (minister) and to ilah (offer), and kap (spoons), and vessels of gold and kasap (silver). They offered burnt ilah (offerings) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah continually all the yawam (days) of Yahawayadai.
But Yahawayadai grew zaqan (old) and was full of yawam (days), and he died; one maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) Shanah ban (old) was he when he mawath (died).
They buried him in the Iyar of Dawad among the malak (kings), because he had done tawab (good) in Yasharaal (Israel), and toward Alahayam and his bayath (house).
Now achar (after) the mawath (death) of Yahawayadai came the shar (princes) of Yahawadah (Judah), and made shachah (obeisance) to the malak (king). Then the malak (king) listened to them.

They forsook the bayath (house) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers), and served the Asharah and the itzab (idols): and qatzap (wrath) came on Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam for this their guiltiness.
Yet he sent nabayaa (prophets) to them, to shawab (turn back / repent) them again to Yahawah; and they testified against them: but they would not give ear.

The rawach (spirit) of Alahayam Labash on Zakarayah the ban (son) of Yahawayadai the kahan (priest); and he stood above the im (people), and said to them, "Thus amar (says) Alahayam, ‘Why do you disobey the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah, so that you can't tzalach (prosper)? Because you have forsaken Yahawah, he has also forsaken you.'
They conspired against him, and stoned him with aban (stones) at the matzawah (commandment) of the malak (king) in the court of the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

Thus Yawaash the malak (king) didn't zakar (remember) the chasad (kindness) which Yahawayadai his ab (father) had done to him, but killed his ban (son). When he mawath (died), he said, "May Yahawah raah (see) at it, and repay it.

It happened at the end of the Shanah, that the chayal (army) of the Aram (Syrians) came up bawaa (against) him: and they came to Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam, and destroyed all the shar (princes) of the im (people) from among the im (people), and sent all their spoil to the malak (king) of Damashaq.

For the chayal (army) of the Aram (Syrians) came with a small company of men; and Yahawah delivered a very great chayal (army) into their yad (hand), because they had forsaken Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers). So they executed shapat (judgment) on Yawaash.

When they were departed for him (for they left him very sick), his own ibad (servants) conspired against him for the dam (blood) of the ban (sons) of Yahawayadai the kahan (priest), and killed him on his bed, and he died; and they buried him in the Iyar of Dawad, but they didn't bury him in the tombs of the malak (kings).
These are those who conspired against him: Zabad the ban (son) Shamaith Shimeath the Imawanayath, and Yahawazabad the ban (son) of Shamarayath the Mawaabay.

Now concerning his ban (sons), and the greatness of the mashaa (burdens) laid on him, and the rebuilding of the bayath (house) of Alahayam, behold, they are written in the commentary of the book of the malak (kings). Amatzayah his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Amatzayah was isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned isharayam (twenty) - thashai (nine) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Yahawaidayan, of Yarawashalam.
He did that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, but not with a Shalam labab (heart).
Now it happened, when the mamalakah (kingdom) was chazaq (established) to him, that he killed his ibad (servants) who had killed the malak (king) his ab (father).

But he didn't put their children to mawath (death), but did according to that which is written in the thawarah (law) in the book of Mashah, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded), saying, "The abawath (fathers) shall not mawath (die) for the children, neither shall the children mawath (die) for the abawath (fathers); but every ayash (man) shall mawath (die) for his own chataa (sin).

Moreover Amatzayah gathered Yahawadah (Judah) together, and ordered them according to their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), under shar (captains) of alap (thousands) and shar (captains) of maah (hundreds), even all Yahawadah (Judah) and Banayamayan: and he numbered them from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, and found them shalawash (three) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) chosen men, yatzaa (able) to go forth to tzabaa (war), who could achaz (handle) spear and tzanah (shield).
He hired also one maah (hundred) alap (thousand) gabawar (mighty) chayal (men) of valor out of Yasharaal (Israel) for one maah (hundred) talents of kasap (silver).

A ayash (man) of Alahayam came to him, saying, "O malak (king), don't let the tzabaa (army) of Yasharaal (Israel) bawaa (go) with you; for Yahawah is not with Yasharaal (Israel), with all the children of Aparayam.

But if you will bawaa (go), ishah (take) action, be chazaq (strong) for the battle. Alahayam will overthrow you panayam (before) the ayab (enemy); for Alahayam has kach (power) to help, and to overthrow.

Amatzayah said to the ayash (man) of Alahayam, "But what shall we do for the maah (hundred) talents which I have given to the gadawad (army) of Yasharaal (Israel)?" The ayash (man) of Alahayam answered, "Yahawah is able to nathan (give) you much more than this.

Then Amatzayah separated them, the gadawad (army) that had bawaa (come) to him out of Aparayam, to bawaa (go) home again: therefore their ap (anger) was maad (greatly) kindled against Yahawadah (Judah), and they returned home in fierce ap (anger).
Amatzayah took chazaq (courage), and led forth his im (people), and went to the Gayaa of Malach, and struck ishar (ten) alap (thousand) of the children of Shaiyar.

The children of Yahawadah (Judah) carry away ishar (ten) alap (thousand) chay (alive), and brought them to the raash (top) of the salai (rock), and threw them down from the raash (top) of the salai (rock), so that they all were broken in pieces.

But the men of the gadawad (army) whom Amatzayah sent shawab (turn back / repent), that they should not yalak (go) with him to battle, fell on the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), from Shamarawan even to Bayathachawarawan Horon, and struck of them shalawash (three) alap (thousand), and took much spoil.

Now it happened, achar (after) that Amatzayah had bawaa (come) from the slaughter of the Adamay (Edomites), that he brought the Alahayam of the children of Shaiyar, and imad (set) them up to be his Alahayam, and bowed down panayam (himself) before them, and burned qatar (incense) to them.

Therefore the ap (anger) of Yahawah was kindled against Amatzayah, and he sent to him a nabayaa (prophet), who said to him, "Why have you sought after the Alahayam of the im (people), which have not delivered their own im (people) out of your yad (hand)?

It happened, as he talked with him, that the king said to him, "Have we made you one of the malak (king's) yaitz (counselors)? Stop! Why should you be struck down?" Then the nabayaa (prophet) stopped, and said, "I yadai (know) that Alahayam has determined to shachath (destroy) you, because you have done this, and have not listened to my itzah (counsel).

Then Amatzayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) consulted his advisers, and sent to Yawaash, the ban (son) of Yahawaachaz the ban (son) of Yahawaa, malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "yalak (come), let us raah (see) one another in the panayam (face).

Yawaash malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) sent to Amatzayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), saying, "The thistle that was in Labanawan sent to the cedar that was in Labanawan, saying, ‘nathan (give) your bath (daughter) to my ban (son) as his ashah (wife); then a shadah (wild) animal that was in Labanawan passed by, and trampled down the thistle.

You amar (say) to yourself that you have struck Adam; and your lab (heart) nashaa (lifts) you up to kabad (boast). Now stay at bayath (home). Why should you meddle with rai (trouble), that you should napal (fall), even you, and Yahawadah (Judah) with you?'
But Amatzayah would not listen; for it was of Alahayam, that he might nathan (deliver) them into the yad (hand) of their darash (enemies), because they had sought after the Alahayam of Adam.

So Yawaash malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) went up; and he and Amatzayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) looked one raah (see) in the panayam (face) at Bayathashamash Shemesh, which belongs to Yahawadah (Judah).
Yahawadah (Judah) was defeated by Yasharaal (Israel); and they fled every ayash (man) to his ahal (tent).

Yawaash malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) took Amatzayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), the ban (son) of Yawaash the ban (son) of Yahawaachaz, at Bayathashamash Shemesh, and brought him to Yarawashalam, and broke down the wall of Yarawashalam from the gate of Aparayam to the panah (corner) gate, arabai (four) maah (hundred) amah (cubits).

He took all the gold and kasap (silver), and all the vessels that were found in the bayath (house) of Alahayam with Ibadaadawam, and the treasures of the malak (king's) bayath (house), the hostages also, and returned to Shamarawan.

Amatzayah the ban (son) of Yawaash malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) lived achar (after) the mawath (death) of Yawaash ban (son) of Yahawaachaz malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) chamash (fifteen) Shanah.
