Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Amatzayah, raashawan (first) and Acharawan, behold, aren't they written in the book of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Yasharaal (Israel)?

Now from the ith (time) that Amatzayah turned sawar (away) from following Yahawah, they made a conspiracy against him in Yarawashalam. He fled to Lakayash; but they sent achar (after) him to Lakayash, and killed him there.
They brought him on horses, and buried him with his abawath (fathers) in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah).
All the im (people) of Yahawadah (Judah) took Izayah, who was sixteen Shanah ban (old), and made him malak (king) in the place of his ab (father) Amatzayah.
He built Ayalawath, and restored it to Yahawadah (Judah), achar (after) that the malak (king) slept with his abawath (fathers).

Sixteen Shanah ban (old) was Izayah when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned chamashayam (fifty) - shanayam (two) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Yakalayah, of Yarawashalam.
He did that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, according to all that his ab (father) Amatzayah had done.

He set himself to seek Alahayam in the yawam (days) of Zakarayah, who had bayan (understanding) in the raah (see) of Alahayam: and as long as he sought Yahawah, Alahayam made him to tzalach (prosper).

He went yatzaa (forth) and warred against the Palashathay (Philistines), and broke down the wall of gath (gath), and the wall of Yabanah, and the wall Ashadawad Ashdod; and he built Iyar Ashadawad the country of Ashdod, and among the Palashathay (Philistines).
Alahayam helped him against the Palashathay (Philistines), and against the Irabay (Arabians) who lived in Gawarabail Baal, and the Maiwanay.
The Imawanay (Ammonites) gave tribute to Izayah: and his sham (name) yalak (spread) abroad even to the entrance of Matzarayam; for he grew exceeding chazaq (strong).
Moreover Izayah built magadal (towers) in Yarawashalam at the corner gate, and at the Gayaa gate, and at the turning of the wall, and fortified them.

He built magadal (towers) in the madabar (wilderness), and dug out many bawar (cisterns), for he had much livestock; in the lowland also, and in the mayashawar (plain): and he had farmers and vineyard keepers in the har (mountains) and in the Karamal fields; for he loved farming.

Moreover Izayah had an chayal (army) of fighting men, who went out to tzabaa (war) by gadawad (bands), according to the number of their reckoning made by Yaiyaal the scribe and Maishayah the shatar (officer), under the yad (hand) of Chananayah, one of the malak (king's) shar (captains).
The whole number of the raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households, even the gabawar (mighty) men of valor, was two alap (thousand) and shash (six) maah (hundred).

Under their yad (hand) was an chayal (army), shalawash (three) maah (hundred) alap (thousand) and shabai (seven) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred), who made war with mighty kach (power), to help the malak (king) against the ayab (enemy).
Izayah prepared for them, even for all the tzabaa (army), magan (shields), and spears, and helmets, and coats of mail, and qashath (bows), and aban (stones) for slinging.

He made in Yarawashalam engines, machashabah (invented) by skillful men, to be on the magadal (towers) and on the battlements, with which to shoot chatz (arrows) and gadawal (great) aban (stones). His sham (name) yatzaa (spread) Rachawaq abroad; for he was marvelously helped, until he was chazaq (strong).

But when he was chazaqah (strong), his lab (heart) was lifted up, so that he did corruptly, and he trespassed against Yahawah his Alahayam; for he went into the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah to qatar (burn) incense on the mazabach (altar) of qatar (incense).
Izarayah the kahan (priest) went in achar (after) him, and with him shamanayam (eighty) kahan (priests) of Yahawah, who were chayal (valiant) men:

and they resisted Izayah the malak (king), and said to him, "It isn't for you, Izayah, to qatar (burn) incense to Yahawah, but for the kahan (priests) the ban (sons) of Aharawan, who are consecrated to qatar (burn) incense. yatzaa (go) out of the maqadash (sanctuary); for you have trespassed; neither shall it be for your honor from Yahawah Alahayam.

Then Izayah was angry; and he had a censer in his yad (hand) to qatar (burn) incense; and while he was angry with the kahan (priests), the leprosy broke forth in his forehead panayam (before) the kahan (priests) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, beside the mazabach (altar) of incense.

Izarayah the raash (chief) kahan (priest), and all the kahan (priests), looked on him, and behold, he was leprous in his forehead, and they thrust him out quickly from there; yes, himself hurried also to yatzaa (go) out, because Yahawah had struck him.

Izayah the malak (king) was a leper to the yawam (day) of his mawath (death), and lived in a separate bayath (house), being a leper; for he was cut off from the bayath (house) of Yahawah: and Yawatham his ban (son) was over the malak (king's) bayath (house), judging the im (people) of the aratz (land).
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Izayah, raashawan (first) and Acharawan, Yashaiyah the nabayaa (prophet), the ban (son) of Amawatz, wrote.

So Izayah slept with his abawath (fathers); and they buried him with his abawath (fathers) in the shadah (field) of qabawarah (burial) which belonged to the malak (kings); for they said, "He is a leper." Yawatham his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Yawatham was isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned sixteen Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Yarawashaa the bath (daughter) of Tzadawaq.

He did that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, according to all that his ab (father) Izayah had done: however he didn't enter into the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah. The im (people) still did corruptly.
He built the Ilayawan gate of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and on the wall of Ipal he built much.
Moreover he built Iyar in the har (hill) country of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the Charash he built castles and towers.

He fought also with the malak (king) of the children of Imawanay, and prevailed against them. The children of Imawan gave him the same Shanah one maah (hundred) talents of kasap (silver), and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) measures of wheat, and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) of barley. The children of Imawan gave that much to him in the shanay (second) Shanah also, and in the shalayashay (third).
So Yawatham became chazaq (mighty), because he ordered his darak (ways) panayam (before) Yahawah his Alahayam.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yawatham, and all his wars, and his darak (ways), behold, they are written in the book of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah).
He was chamash (five) and isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign), and reigned sixteen Shanah in Yarawashalam.
Yawatham slept with his abawath (fathers), and they buried him in the Iyar of Dawad: and Achaz his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Achaz was isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned sixteen Shanah in Yarawashalam: and he didn't do that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, like Dawad his ab (father);
but he walked in the darak (ways) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel), and made also molten masakah (images) for the Bail.

Moreover he burnt qatar (incense) in the Gayaa of the ban (son) of Hanam, and burnt his children in the ash (fire), according to the thawaibah (abominations) of the gawayam (nations) whom Yahawah yarash (cast) out panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
He sacrificed and burnt qatar (incense) in the bamah (high) places, and on the Gabaih, and under every Rainan itz (tree).

Therefore Yahawah his Alahayam delivered him into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Aram; and they struck him, and carried away of his a gadawal (great) multitude of captives, and brought them to Damashaq. He was also delivered into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), who struck him with a gadawal (great) makah (slaughter).

For Paqach the ban (son) of Ramalayahaw killed in Yahawadah (Judah) one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) alap (thousand) in one yawam (day), all of them chayal (valiant) men; because they had forsaken Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers).

Zakaray, a gabawar (mighty) man of Aparayam, killed Maishayah the malak (king's) ban (son), and Izarayaqam the nagayad (ruler) of the bayath (house), and Alaqanah who was mashanah (next) to the malak (king).

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) carried away captive of their ach (brothers) two maah (hundred) alap (thousand), women, ban (sons), and bath (daughters), and took also away much spoil from them, and brought the spoil to Shamarawan.

But a nabayaa (prophet) of Yahawah was there, whose sham (name) was Iwadad: and he went out to panayam (meet) the tzabaa (army) that came to Shamarawan, and said to them, "Behold, because Yahawah, the Alahayam of your abawath (fathers), was angry with Yahawadah (Judah), he has delivered them into your yad (hand), and you have slain them in a zaip (rage) which has reached up to shamayam (heaven).

Now you purpose to keep under the children of Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam for ibad (bondservants) and bondmaids for yourselves. Aren't there even with you trespasses of your own against Yahawah your Alahayam?
Now hear me therefore, and shawab (turn back / repent) back the captives, that you have taken captive from your ach (brothers); for the charawan (fierce) ap (wrath) of Yahawah is on you.

Then some of the raash (heads) of the children of Aparayam, Izarayah the ban (son) of Yahawachanan, Barakayah the ban (son) of Mashalamawath, and Yachazaqayah the ban (son) of Shalawam, and Imashaa the ban (son) of Chadalay, stood up bawaa (against) those who came from the tzabaa (war),

and said to them, "You shall not bawaa (bring) in the captives here: for you purpose that which will bring on us a ashamah (trespass) against Yahawah, to add to our chataah (sins) and to our ashamah (trespass); for our ashamah (trespass) is rab (great), and there is fierce ap (wrath) against Yasharaal (Israel).
So the chalatz (armed) men left the captives and the spoil panayam (before) the shar (princes) and all the qahal (assembly).

The men who have been mentioned by sham (name) rose up, and took the captives, and with the spoil Labash all who were naked Labash them, dressed them, gave them sandals, and gave them something to akal (eat) and to shaqah (drink), sawak (anointed) them, carried all the feeble of them on donkeys, and brought them to Yarayachaw, the Iyar of palm trees, to their ach (brothers). Then they returned to Shamarawan.
At that ith (time) malak (king) Achaz sent to the malak (kings) of Ashawar to help him.
For again the Adamay (Edomites) had bawaa (come) and struck Yahawadah (Judah), and carried away Shabay.

The Palashathay (Philistines) also had invaded the Iyar of the lowland, and of the Nagab of Yahawadah (Judah), and had taken Bayathashamash Shemesh, and Ayalawan, and Gadarawath, and Shawakah with its bath (towns), and Thamanah with its bath (towns), Gamazaw also and its bath (towns): and they lived there.
For Yahawah brought Yahawadah (Judah) low because of Achaz malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel); for he had dealt wantonly in Yahawadah (Judah), and trespassed severely against Yahawah.
Thagalathapalaasar Pilneser malak (king) of Ashawar came to him, and distressed him, but didn't chazaq (strengthen) him.

For Achaz took away a portion out of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and out of the bayath (house) of the malak (king) and of the shar (princes), and gave it to the malak (king) of Ashawar: but it didn't help him.
In the ith (time) of his tzarar (distress), he trespassed yet more against Yahawah, this same malak (king) Achaz.

For he sacrificed to the Alahayam of Damashaq, which struck him; and he said, "Because the Alahayam of the malak (kings) of Aram helped them, so I will zabach (sacrifice) to them, that they may help me." But they were the ruin of him, and of all Yasharaal (Israel).

Achaz gathered asap (together) the vessels of the bayath (house) of Alahayam, and cut in pieces the vessels of the bayath (house) of Alahayam, and shut up the doors of the bayath (house) of Yahawah; and he made him mazabach (altars) in every corner of Yarawashalam.
In every Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah) he made bamah (high) places to qatar (burn) incense to other Alahayam, and provoked to kais (anger) Yahawah, the Alahayam of his abawath (fathers).

Now the yathar (rest) of his dabar (acts), and all his darak (ways), raashawan (first) and Acharawan, behold, they are written in the book of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Yasharaal (Israel).

Achaz slept with his abawath (fathers), and they buried him in the Iyar, even in Yarawashalam; for they didn't bawaa (bring) him into the tombs of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel): and Yachazaqayah his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Yachazaqayah began to malak (reign) when he was isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) Shanah ban (old); and he reigned isharayam (twenty) - thashai (nine) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Abayah, the bath (daughter) of Zakarayah.
He did that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, according to all that Dawad his ab (father) had done.
He in the raashawan (first) Shanah of his malak (reign), in the raashawan (first) chadash (month), opened the doors of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and repaired them.
He brought in the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites), and gathered them asap (together) into the broad place on the east,

and said to them, "Listen Lawayay me, you Levites! Now qadash (sanctify) yourselves, and qadash (sanctify) the bayath (house) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of your abawath (fathers), and yatzaa (carry) out the nadah (filthiness) out of the qadash (holy) place.

For our abawath (fathers) have trespassed, and done that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah our Alahayam, and have forsaken him, and have turned sabab (away) their panayam (faces) from the mashakan (habitation) of Yahawah, and turned their backs.

Also they have shut up the doors of the porch, and put out the nayar (lamps), and have not burned incense nor offered burnt ilah (offerings) in the qadash (holy) place to the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).

Therefore the qatzap (wrath) of Yahawah was on Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam, and he has delivered them to be tossed back and forth, to be an astonishment, and a hissing, as you raah (see) with your iyan (eyes).
For, behold, our abawath (fathers) have fallen by the charab (sword), and our ban (sons) and our bath (daughters) and our wives are in Shabay for this.

Now it is in my labab (heart) to karath (make) a barayath (covenant) with Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), that his charawan (fierce) ap (anger) may shawab (turn back / repent) away from us.

My ban (sons), don't be negligent now; for Yahawah has chosen you to imad (stand) panayam (before) him, to sharath (minister) to him, and that you should be his sharath (ministers), and qatar (burn) incense.

Then the Lawayay (Levites) qawam (arose), Machath, the ban (son) of Imashay, and Yawaal the ban (son) of Izarayah, of the ban (sons) of the Qahathay (Kohathites); and of the ban (sons) of Mararay, Qayash the ban (son) of Ibaday, and Izarayah the ban (son) Yahalalaal Jehallelel; and of the garashanay (gershonites), Yawaach the ban (son) of Zamah, and Idan the ban (son) of Yawaach;
and of the ban (sons) of Alayatzapan, Shamaray and Yaiyaal; and of the ban (sons) of Asap, Zakarayah and Mathanayah;
and of the ban (sons) of Hayaman, Yachayaal and Shamaiy; and of the ban (sons) of Yadawathawan, Shamaiyah and Izayaal.

They gathered their ach (brothers), and sanctified themselves, and went in, according to the matzawah (commandment) of the malak (king) by the dabar (words) of Yahawah, to tahar (cleanse) the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

The kahan (priests) went in to the inner part of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, to tahar (cleanse) it, and brought out all the tamaah (uncleanness) that they found in the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah into the court of the bayath (house) of Yahawah. The Lawayay (Levites) took it, to yatzaa (carry) it out abroad to the nachal (brook) Qadarawan.

Now they began on the achad (first) day of the raashawan (first) chadash (month) to qadash (sanctify), and on the shamanah (eighth) yawam (day) of the chadash (month) came they to the porch of Yahawah; and they sanctified the bayath (house) of Yahawah in shamanah (eight) yawam (days): and on the sixteenth day of the raashawan (first) chadash (month) they made an kalah (end).

Then they went in to Chazaqayah the malak (king) within the palace, and said, "We have cleansed all the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the mazabach (altar) of burnt ilah (offering), with all its vessels, and the table of show mairakath (bread), with all its vessels.

Moreover all the vessels, which malak (king) Achaz in his malakawath (reign) threw away when he trespassed, have we prepared and sanctified; and behold, they are panayam (before) the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah.
Then Yachazaqayah the malak (king) arose shakam (early), and gathered the shar (princes) of the Iyar, and went up to the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

They brought shabai (seven) bulls, and shabai (seven) ayal (rams), and shabai (seven) lambs, and shabai (seven) male goats, for a chataah (sin) offering for the mamalakah (kingdom) and for the maqadash (sanctuary) and for Yahawadah (Judah). He commanded the kahan (priests) the ban (sons) of Aharawan to ilah (offer) them on the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah.

So they killed the bulls, and the kahan (priests) received the dam (blood), and sprinkled it on the mazabach (altar): and they killed the ayal (rams), and sprinkled the dam (blood) on the mazabach (altar): they killed also the lambs, and sprinkled the dam (blood) on the mazabach (altar).
They brought near the male Shaiyar for the chataah (sin) offering panayam (before) the malak (king) and the qahal (assembly); and they laid their yad (hands) on them:

and the kahan (priests) killed them, and they made a chataa (sin) offering with their dam (blood) on the mazabach (altar), to make kapar (atonement) for all Yasharaal (Israel); for the malak (king) commanded that the burnt ilah (offering) and the sin ilah (offering) should be made for all Yasharaal (Israel).

He imad (set) the Lawayay (Levites) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah with cymbals, with stringed instruments, and with harps, according to the matzawah (commandment) of Dawad, and of Gad the malak (king's) chazah (seer), and Nathan the nabayaa (prophet); for the matzawah (commandment) was of Yahawah by his nabayaa (prophets).
The Lawayay (Levites) stood with the instruments of Dawad, and the kahan (priests) with the trumpets.

Chazaqayah commanded to ilah (offer) the burnt offering on the mazabach (altar). When the burnt ilah (offering) began, the song of Yahawah began also, and the trumpets, together with the instruments of Dawad malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).
All the qahal (assembly) worshiped, and the singers sang, and the trumpeters sounded; all this continued until the burnt ilah (offering) was finished.
When they had made an kalah (end) of offering, the malak (king) and all who were matzaa (present) with him bowed themselves and worshiped.

Moreover Yachazaqayah the malak (king) and the shar (princes) commanded the Lawayay (Levites) to sing halal (praises) to Yahawah with the dabar (words) of Dawad, and of Asap the chazah (seer). They sang halal (praises) with gladness, and they bowed their qadad (heads) and worshiped.

Then Yachazaqayah answered, "Now you have consecrated yourselves to Yahawah; come near and bawaa (bring) zabach (sacrifices) and thank thawadah (offerings) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah." The qahal (assembly) brought in zabach (sacrifices) and thank thawadah (offerings); and as many as were of a nadayab (willing) lab (heart) brought burnt ilah (offerings).

The number of the burnt ilah (offerings) which the qahal (assembly) brought was shabaiyam (seventy) bulls, one maah (hundred) ayal (rams), and two maah (hundred) lambs: all these were for a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah.
The qadash (consecrated) things were shash (six) maah (hundred) baqar (head) of cattle and shalawash (three) alap (thousand) sheep.

But the kahan (priests) were too Mait, so that they could not flay all the burnt ilah (offerings): therefore their ach (brothers) the Lawayay (Levites) helped them, until the malaakah (work) was ended, and until the kahan (priests) had sanctified Lawayay; for the Levites were more yashar (upright) in labab (heart) to qadash (sanctify) themselves than the kahan (priests).

Also the burnt ilah (offerings) were in abundance, with the fat of the shalam (peace) offerings, and with the drink nasak (offerings) for every burnt ilah (offering). So the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah was kawan (set) in order.
Yachazaqayah Shamach, and all the im (people), because of that which Alahayam had prepared for the im (people): for the thing was done suddenly.

Yachazaqayah sent to all Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah), and wrote letters also to Aparayam and Manashah, that they should bawaa (come) to the bayath (house) of Yahawah at Yarawashalam, to ishah (keep) the pasach (passover) to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
For the malak (king) had taken yaitz (counsel), and his shar (princes), and all the qahal (assembly) in Yarawashalam, to ishah (keep) the pasach (passover) in the shanay (second) chadash (month).

For they could not ishah (keep) it at that ith (time), because the kahan (priests) had not sanctified themselves in sufficient number, neither had the im (people) gathered themselves asap (together) to Yarawashalam.
The thing was yashar (right) in the eyes of the malak (king) and of all the qahal (assembly).

So they established a dabar (decree) to ibar (make) proclamation throughout all Yasharaal (Israel), Baarashabai Beersheba Dan to Dan, that they should bawaa (come) to ishah (keep) the pasach (passover) to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), at Yarawashalam: for they had not kept it in great numbers in such sort as it is written.

So the couriers went with the letters from the malak (king) and his shar (princes) throughout all Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah), and according to the matzawah (commandment) of the malak (king), saying, "You children of Yasharaal (Israel), shawab (turn back / repent) again to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Abaraham, Yatzachaq, and Yasharaal (Israel), that he may shawab (turn back / repent) to the shaar (remnant) that have palayatah (escaped) of you out of the kap (hand) of the malak (kings) of Ashawar.
Don't be like your abawath (fathers), and like your ach (brothers), who trespassed against Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers), so that he gave them up to desolation, as you raah (see).

Now don't be stiff-necked, as your abawath (fathers) were; but nathan (yield) yad (yourselves) to Yahawah, and bawaa (enter) into his maqadash (sanctuary), which he has sanctified iwalam (forever), and ibad (serve) Yahawah your Alahayam, that his charawan (fierce) ap (anger) may shawab (turn back / repent) away from you.

For if you shawab (turn back / repent) again to Yahawah, your ach (brothers) and your children shall find racham (compassion) panayam (before) those who led them captive, and shall shawab (turn back / repent) again into this aratz (land): for Yahawah your Alahayam is Chanawan and Rachawam, and will not sawar (turn) away his panayam (face) from you, if you shawab (turn back / repent) to him.
So the couriers passed from Iyar to Iyar through the aratz (country) of Aparayam and Manashah, even to Zabawalawan: but they ridiculed them, and mocked them.
Nevertheless anawash (certain) men of Ashar and Manashah and of Zabawalawan humbled themselves, and came to Yarawashalam.

Also on Yahawadah (Judah) came the yad (hand) of Alahayam to nathan (give) them one lab (heart), to do the matzawah (commandment) of the malak (king) and of the shar (princes) by the dabar (word) of Yahawah.
Many im (people) assembled at Yarawashalam to ishah (keep) the chag (feast) of unleavened matzah (bread) in the shanay (second) chadash (month), a very great qahal (assembly).

They qawam (arose) and took sawar (away) the mazabach (altars) that were in Yarawashalam, and all the altars for qatar (incense) took they sawar (away), and cast them into the nachal (brook) Qadarawan.

Then they killed the pasach (passover) on the fourteenth day of the shanay (second) chadash (month): and the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites) were kalam (ashamed), and sanctified themselves, and brought burnt ilah (offerings) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

They stood in their imad (place) after their mashapat (order), according to the thawarah (law) of Mashah the ayash (man) of Alahayam: the kahan (priests) sprinkled the dam (blood) which they received of the yad (hand) Lawayay the Levites.

For there were many in the qahal (assembly) who had not sanctified Lawayay: therefore the Levites were in charge of killing the pasach (passovers) for everyone who was not tahawar (clean), to qadash (sanctify) them to Yahawah.

For a multitude of the im (people), even many of Aparayam and Manashah, Yashashakar and Zabawalawan, had not cleansed themselves, yet they ate the pasach (passover) otherwise than it is written. For Yachazaqayah had prayed for them, saying, "May the tawab (good) Yahawah kapar (pardon) everyone
who kawan (sets) his labab (heart) to seek Alahayam, Yahawah, the Alahayam of his abawath (fathers), even if they aren't taharah (clean) according to the purification of the qadash (sanctuary).
Yahawah listened to Yachazaqayah, and healed the im (people).

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) who were matzaa (present) at Yarawashalam kept the chag (feast) of unleavened matzah (bread) shabai (seven) yawam (days) with gadawal (great) gladness; and the Lawayay (Levites) and the kahan (priests) praised Yahawah yawam (day) by yawam (day), singing with iz (loud) instruments to Yahawah.

Yachazaqayah spoke lab (comfortably) Lawayay all the Levites who had tawab (good) shakal (understanding) in the service of Yahawah. So they ate throughout the mawaid (feast) for the shabai (seven) yawam (days), offering sacrifices of shalam (peace) offerings, and making yadah (confession) to Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers).
The whole qahal (assembly) took yaitz (counsel) to ishah (keep) other shabai (seven) yawam (days); and they kept another shabai (seven) yawam (days) with gladness.

For Chazaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) gave to the qahal (assembly) for offerings one alap (thousand) bulls and shabai (seven) alap (thousand) sheep; and the shar (princes) gave to the qahal (assembly) a alap (thousand) bulls and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) sheep: and a great number of kahan (priests) sanctified themselves.

All the qahal (assembly) of Yahawadah (Judah), with the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites), and all the qahal (assembly) who came out of Yasharaal (Israel), and the foreigners who came out of the aratz (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), and who lived in Yahawadah (Judah), Shamach.
So there was gadawal (great) joy in Yarawashalam; for yawam (since) the time of Shalamah the ban (son) of Dawad malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) there was not the like in Yarawashalam.

Then the kahan (priests) the Lawayay (Levites) qawam (arose) and blessed the im (people): and their qawal (voice) was heard, and their prayer came up to his qadash (holy) habitation, even to shamayam (heaven).

Now when all this was finished, all Yasharaal (Israel) who were matzaa (present) went out to the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and broke in shabar (pieces) the matzabah (pillars), and cut down the Asharah, and broke down the bamah (high) places and the mazabach (altars) out of all Yahawadah (Judah) and Banayamayan, in Aparayam also and Manashah, until they had destroyed them all. Then all the children of Yasharaal (Israel) returned, every ayash (man) to his achazah (possession), into their own Iyar.

Yachazaqayah appointed the divisions of the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites) after their divisions, every ayash (man) according to his ibadah (service), both the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites), for burnt ilah (offerings) and for peace ilah (offerings), to sharath (minister), and to give yadah (thanks), and to halal (praise) in the gates of the machanah (camp) of Yahawah.

He appointed also the malak (king's) portion of his rakawash (substance) for the burnt ilah (offerings), for the baqar (morning) and evening burnt ilah (offerings), and the burnt ilah (offerings) for the shabath (sabbaths), and for the new chadash (moons), and for the mawaid (set) feasts, as it is written in the thawarah (law) of Yahawah.

Moreover he commanded the im (people) who lived in Yarawashalam to nathan (give) the portion of the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites), that they might give themselves to the thawarah (law) of Yahawah.

As soon as the commandment came abroad, the children of Yasharaal (Israel) gave in abundance the raashayath (first) fruits of grain, new thayarawash (wine), and yatzahar (oil), and honey, and of all the increase of the shadah (field); and the maishar (tithe) of all things brought they in abundantly.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah), who lived in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), they also brought in the maishar (tithe) of cattle and sheep, and the maishar (tithe) of qadash (dedicated) things which were consecrated to Yahawah their Alahayam, and laid them by heaps.
In the shalayashay (third) chadash (month) they began to yasad (lay) the foundation of the heaps, and finished them in the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month).
When Yachazaqayah and the shar (princes) came and saw the heaps, they blessed Yahawah, and his im (people) Yasharaal (Israel).
Then Yachazaqayah questioned the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites) concerning the heaps.

Izarayah the raash (chief) kahan (priest), of the bayath (house) of Tzadawaq, answered him and said, "Since people began to bawaa (bring) the tharawamah (offerings) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah, we have eaten and had enough, and have yathar (left) plenty: for Yahawah has blessed his im (people); and that which is yathar (left) is this great store.
Then Yachazaqayah commanded them to kawan (prepare) rooms in the bayath (house) of Yahawah; and they prepared them.

They brought in the tharawamah (offerings) and the maishar (tithes) and the qadash (dedicated) things faithfully: and over them Kawananayahaw the Lawayay (Levite) was nagayad (ruler), and Shamaiy his ach (brother) was mashanah (second).

Yachayaal, and Izazayahaw, and Nachath, and Ishahaal, and Yarayamawath, and Yawazabad, and Alayaal, and Yasamakayahaw, and Machath, and Banayah, were overseers under the yad (hand) of Kawananayahaw and Shamaiy his ach (brother), by the appointment of Yachazaqayah the malak (king), and Izarayah the nagayad (ruler) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam.

Qawaraa the ban (son) of Yamanah the Lawayay (Levite), the porter at the east gate, was over the freewill nadabah (offerings) of Alahayam, to nathan (distribute) the tharawamah (offerings) of Yahawah, and the most qadash (holy) things.

Under him were Idan, and Manayamayan, and Yashawai, and Shamaiyah, Amarayah, and Shakanayah, in the Iyar of the kahan (priests), in their amawanah (office) of trust, to nathan (give) to their ach (brothers) by divisions, as well to the gadawal (great) as to the qatan (small):

besides those who were reckoned by genealogy of zakar (males), from shalawash (three) Shanah ban (old) and upward, even everyone who entered into the bayath (house) of Yahawah, as the duty of every yawam (day) required, for their ibadah (service) in their offices according to their divisions;

and those who were reckoned by genealogy of the kahan (priests) by their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), and the Lawayay (Levites) from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, in their offices by their divisions;

and those who were reckoned by genealogy of all their little ones, their wives, and their ban (sons), and their bath (daughters), through all the qahal (congregation): for in their amawanah (office) of trust they sanctified themselves in qadash (holiness).

Also for the ban (sons) of Aharawan the kahan (priests), who were in the shadah (fields) of the suburbs of their Iyar, in every Iyar, there were men who were mentioned by sham (name), to nathan (give) portions to all the zakar (males) among the kahan (priests), and to all who were reckoned by genealogy Lawayay the Levites.
Yachazaqayah did so throughout all Yahawadah (Judah); and he worked that which was tawab (good) and yashar (right) and amath (faithful) panayam (before) Yahawah his Alahayam.

In every maishah (work) that he began in the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam, and in the thawarah (law), and in the matzawah (commandments), to seek his Alahayam, he did it with all his labab (heart), and prospered.

achar (after) these things, and this amath (faithfulness), Sanacharayab malak (king) of Ashawar came, and entered into Yahawadah (Judah), and encamped against the fortified Iyar, and thought to win them for himself.
When Yachazaqayah saw that Sanacharayab had bawaa (come), and that he was panayam (purposed) to fight against Yarawashalam,
he took yaitz (counsel) with his shar (princes) and his gabawar (mighty) men to stop the mayam (waters) of the springs which were outside of the Iyar; and they helped him.

So many im (people) gathered together, and they stopped all the springs, and the nachal (brook) that flowed through the midst of the aratz (land), saying, "Why should the malak (kings) of Ashawar bawaa (come), and matzaa (find) much mayam (water)?

He took chazaq (courage), and built up all the wall that was broken down, and raised it up to the magadal (towers), and the other wall outside, and strengthened Malawaa in the Iyar of Dawad, and made shalach (weapons) and magan (shields) in abundance.
He nathan (set) shar (captains) of war over the im (people), and gathered them together to him in the broad place at the gate of the Iyar, and spoke labab (comfortably) to them, saying,

"Be chazaq (strong) and amatz (courageous), don't be yaraa (afraid) nor dismayed for the malak (king) of Ashawar, nor for all the multitude who is with him; for there is a greater with us than with him.

With him is an zarawai (arm) of flesh; but with us is Yahawah our Alahayam to help us, and to fight our battles." The im (people) rested themselves on the dabar (words) of Yachazaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah).

achar (after) this, Sanacharayab malak (king) of Ashawar sent his ibad (servants) to Yarawashalam, (now he was before Lakayash, and all his mamashalah (power) with him), to Yachazaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and to all Yahawadah (Judah) who were at Yarawashalam, saying,
Thus amar (says) Sanacharayab malak (king) of Ashawar, "In whom do you batach (trust), that you yashab (remain) under Matzawar in Yarawashalam?

Doesn't Yachazaqayah persuade you, to nathan (give) you over to mawath (die) by famine and by thirst, saying, ‘Yahawah our Alahayam will natzal (deliver) us out of the kap (hand) of the malak (king) of Ashawar?'

Hasn't the same Yachazaqayah taken sawar (away) his bamah (high) places and his mazabach (altars), and commanded Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam, saying, ‘You shall shachah (worship) panayam (before) one mazabach (altar), and on it you shall qatar (burn) incense?'

Don't you yadai (know) what I and my abawath (fathers) have done to all the im (peoples) of the aratz (lands)? Were the Alahayam of the gaway (nations) of the aratz (lands) in any way yakal (able) to natzal (deliver) their aratz (land) out of my yad (hand)?

Who was there among all the Alahayam of those gawayam (nations) which my abawath (fathers) charam (utterly) destroyed, that could natzal (deliver) his im (people) out of my yad (hand), that your Alahayam should be yakal (able) to natzal (deliver) you out of my yad (hand)?

Now therefore don't let Chazaqayah deceive you, nor persuade you in this way, neither aman (believe) him; for no Alawah of any gaway (nation) or mamalakah (kingdom) was yakal (able) to natzal (deliver) his im (people) out of my yad (hand), and out of the yad (hand) of my abawath (fathers). How much less will your Alahayam natzal (deliver) you out of my yad (hand)?
His ibad (servants) spoke yet more against Yahawah Alahayam, and against his ibad (servant) Yachazaqayah.

He also wrote letters insulting Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), and to amar (speak) amar (against) him, saying, "As the Alahayam of the gaway (nations) of the aratz (lands), which have not delivered their im (people) out of my yad (hand), so shall the Alahayam of Yachazaqayah not natzal (deliver) his im (people) out of my yad (hand).

They cried with a gadawal (loud) qawal (voice) in the Yahawadayath (Jews)' language to the im (people) of Yarawashalam who were on the wall, to frighten them, and to trouble them; that they might take the Iyar.
They spoke of the Alahayam of Yarawashalam, as of the Alahayam of the im (peoples) of the aratz (earth), which are the maishah (work) of men's yad (hands).
Yachazaqayah the malak (king), and Yashaiyah the nabayaa (prophet) the ban (son) of Amawatz, prayed because of this, and cried to shamayam (heaven).

Yahawah sent an malaak (angel), who cut off all the gabawar (mighty) men of valor, and the nagayad (leaders) and shar (captains), in the machanah (camp) of the malak (king) of Ashawar. So he returned with bashath (shame) of panayam (face) to his own aratz (land). When he had bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of his Alahayam, those who came forth from his own maih (bowels) killed him there with the charab (sword).

Thus Yahawah saved Yachazaqayah and the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam from the yad (hand) of Sanacharayab the malak (king) of Ashawar, and from the yad (hand) of all others, and guided them on every side.

Many brought manachah (gifts) to Yahawah to Yarawashalam, and precious things to Yachazaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah); so that he was exalted in the iyan (sight) of all gawayam (nations) from achar (thenceforth).
In those yawam (days) Yachazaqayah was chalah (sick) even to mawath (death): and he prayed to Yahawah; and he spoke to him, and gave him a mawapath (sign).

But Yachazaqayah didn't shawab (turn back / repent) again according to the benefit done to him; for his lab (heart) was lifted up: therefore there was qatzap (wrath) on him, and on Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam.

Notwithstanding Yachazaqayah humbled himself for the pride of his lab (heart), both he and the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, so that the qatzap (wrath) of Yahawah didn't bawaa (come) on them in the yawam (days) of Yachazaqayah.

Yachazaqayah had maad (exceeding) much riches and honor: and he provided him treasuries for kasap (silver), and for gold, and for Yaqar aban (stones), and for spices, and for magan (shields), and for all kinds of goodly vessels;
storehouses also for the increase of grain and new thayarawash (wine) and yatzahar (oil); and stalls for all kinds of animals, and flocks in folds.
Moreover he provided him Iyar, and maqanah (possessions) of flocks and herds in abundance; for Alahayam had given him very much rakawash (substance).

This same Yachazaqayah also stopped the Ilayawan spring of the waters of Gayachawan, and brought them yashar (straight) down on the west side of the Iyar of Dawad. Yachazaqayah prospered in all his maishah (works).

Kan concerning the Lawatz of the shar (princes) of Babal, who sent to him to inquire of the mawapath (wonder) that was done in the aratz (land), Alahayam left him, to try him, that he might yadai (know) all that was in his labab (heart).

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yachazaqayah, and his chasad (good) deeds, behold, they are written in the vision of Yashaiyah the nabayaa (prophet) the ban (son) of Amawatz, in the book of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Yasharaal (Israel).

Yachazaqayah slept with his abawath (fathers), and they buried him in the ascent of the tombs of the ban (sons) of Dawad: and all Yahawadah (Judah) and the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam did him honor at his mawath (death). Manashah his ban (son) reigned in his place.
Manashah was shanayam (twelve) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned chamashayam (fifty) - chamash (five) Shanah in Yarawashalam.

He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, after the thawaibah (abominations) of the gawayam (nations) whom Yahawah yarash (cast) out panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

For he built again the bamah (high) places which Yachazaqayah his ab (father) had broken down; and he reared up mazabach (altars) for the Bail, and made Asharah, and worshiped all the tzabaa (army) of the sky, and served them.
He built mazabach (altars) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, of which Yahawah said, "My sham (name) shall be in Yarawashalam iwalam (forever).
He built mazabach (altars) for all the tzabaa (army) of the sky in the shanayam (two) courts of the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

He also made his children to ibar (pass) through the ash (fire) in the Gayaa of the ban (son) of Hanam; and he practiced sorcery, and used enchantments, and practiced sorcery, and dealt with those who had familiar awab (spirits), and with wizards: he worked much rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, to provoke him to kais (anger).

He shawam (set) the engraved pasal (image) of the samal (idol), which he had made, in the bayath (house) of Alahayam, of which Alahayam said to Dawad and to Shalamah his ban (son), "In this bayath (house), and in Yarawashalam, which I have chosen out of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), will I shawam (put) my sham (name) iyalawam (forever):

neither will I any more sawar (remove) the ragal (foot) of Yasharaal (Israel) from off the adamah (land) which I have appointed for your abawath (fathers), if only they will shamar (observe) to do all that I have tzawah (commanded) them, even all the thawarah (law) and the chaq (statutes) and the mashapat (ordinances) given by Mashah.

Manashah seduced Yahawadah (Judah) and the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, so that they did more evil than the gawayam (nations) whom Yahawah destroyed panayam (before) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) did.
Yahawah spoke to Manashah, and to his im (people); but they gave no heed.
Therefore Yahawah brought on them the shar (captains) of the army of the malak (king) of Ashawar, who took Manashah in chains, and bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babal.
When he was in tzarar (distress), he begged Yahawah his Alahayam, and humbled himself maad (greatly) panayam (before) the Alahayam of his abawath (fathers).
He prayed to him; and he was entreated by him, and heard his supplication, and brought him again to Yarawashalam into his malakawath (kingdom). Then Manashah knew that Yahawah was Alahayam.

Now achar (after) this he built an outer wall to the Iyar of Dawad, on the west side of Gayachawan, in the nachal (valley), even to the entrance at the fish gate; and he encircled Ipal with it, and raised it up to a very maad (great) height: and he shawam (put) chayal (valiant) shar (captains) in all the fortified Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah).

He took sawar (away) the foreign Alahayam, and the samal (idol) out of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and all the mazabach (altars) that he had built in the har (mountain) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and in Yarawashalam, and cast them out of the Iyar.

He built up the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah, and offered thereon sacrifices of shalam (peace) zabach (offerings) and of thanksgiving, and commanded Yahawadah (Judah) to ibad (serve) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
Nevertheless the im (people) sacrificed still in the bamah (high) places, but only to Yahawah their Alahayam.

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Manashah, and his prayer to his Alahayam, and the dabar (words) of the chazah (seers) who spoke to him in the sham (name) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), behold, they are written among the dabar (acts) of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel).

His prayer also, and how Alahayam was entreated of him, and all his chataah (sin) and his mail (trespass), and the places in which he built bamah (high) places, and imad (set) up the Asharah and the engraved pasayal (images), panayam (before) he humbled himself: behold, they are written in the history of Hozai.
So Manashah slept with his abawath (fathers), and they buried him in his own bayath (house): and Amawan his ban (son) reigned in his place.
Amawan was isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned shanayam (two) Shanah in Yarawashalam.

He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, as did Manashah his ab (father); and Amawan sacrificed to all the engraved pasayal (images) which Manashah his ab (father) had made, and served them.
He didn't humble panayam (himself) before Yahawah, as Manashah his ab (father) had humbled himself; but this same Amawan trespassed more and more.
His ibad (servants) conspired against him, and put him to mawath (death) in his own bayath (house).
But the im (people) of the aratz (land) killed all those who had conspired against malak (king) Amawan; and the im (people) of the aratz (land) made Yaashayah his ban (son) malak (king) in his place.
Yaashayah was shamanah (eight) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned shalawashayam (thirty) - one Shanah in Yarawashalam.

He did that which was yashar (right) in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, and walked in the darak (ways) of Dawad his ab (father), and didn't sawar (turn) aside to the right yamayan (hand) or to the shamaawal (left).

For in the shamanah (eighth) Shanah of his malak (reign), while he was yet nair (young), he began to seek after the Alahayam of Dawad his ab (father); and in the shanayam (twelfth) Shanah he began to tahar (purge) Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam from the bamah (high) places, and the Asharah, and the engraved pasayal (images), and the molten masakah (images).

They broke down the mazabach (altars) of the Bail in his panayam (presence); and the incense altars that were on high above them he cut down; and the Asharah, and the engraved pasayal (images), and the molten pasayal (images), he broke in shabar (pieces), and made dust of them, and strewed it on the qabar (graves) of those who had sacrificed to them.
He burnt the itzam (bones) of the kahan (priests) on their mazabach (altars), and purged Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam.
He did this in the Iyar of Manashah and Aparayam and Shamaiwan, even to Napathalay, around in their ruins.

He broke down the mazabach (altars), and kathath (beat) the Asharah and the engraved pasayal (images) into powder, and cut down all the incense altars throughout all the aratz (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), and returned to Yarawashalam.

Now in the eighteenth Shanah of his malak (reign), when he had purged the aratz (land) and the bayath (house), he sent Shapan the ban (son) of Atzalayahaw, and Maishayah the shar (governor) of the Iyar, and Yawaach the ban (son) of Yawaachaz the zakar (recorder), to chazaq (repair) the bayath (house) of Yahawah his Alahayam.

They came Chalaqayah Hilkiah the gadawal (high) kahan (priest), and delivered the kasap (money) that was brought into the bayath (house) of Alahayam, which the Lawayay (Levites), the keepers of the threshold, had gathered of the yad (hand) of Manashah and Aparayam, and of all the shaarayath (remnant) of Yasharaal (Israel), and of all Yahawadah (Judah) and Banayamayan, and of the inhabitants of Yarawashalam.

They delivered it into the yad (hand) of the workmen who had the paqad (oversight) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah; and the workmen who labored in the bayath (house) of Yahawah gave it to chazaq (mend) and repair the bayath (house);

even to the carpenters and to the banah (builders) gave they it, to qanah (buy) cut aban (stone), and itz (timber) for couplings, and to make qarah (beams) for the bayath (houses) which the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah) had destroyed.

The men did the malaakah (work) faithfully: and their overseers were Yachath and Ibadayah, the Lawayay (Levites), of the ban (sons) of Mararay; and Zakarayah and Mashalam, of the sons of the Qahathay (Kohathites), to paqad (set) it forward; and Lawayay of the Levites, all who were skillful with instruments of music.

Also they were over the bearers of burdens, and set forward all who did the malaakah (work) in every kind of ibadah (service): and Lawayay the Levites there were scribes, and shatar (officers), and porters.
When they brought out the kasap (money) that was brought into the bayath (house) of Yahawah, Chalaqayah the kahan (priest) found the book of the thawarah (law) of Yahawah given by Mashah.
Chalaqayah answered Shapan the scribe, "I have found the book of the thawarah (law) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah." Chalaqayah delivered the book Shapan Shaphan.

Shapan carried the book to the malak (king), and moreover brought shawab (turn back / repent) dabar (word) to the malak (king), saying, "All that was committed to your ibad (servants), they are doing.
They have emptied out the kasap (money) that was found in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and have delivered it into the yad (hand) of the paqad (overseers), and into the yad (hand) of the workmen.
Shapan the scribe told the malak (king), saying, "Chalaqayah the kahan (priest) has delivered me a book." Shapan qaraa (read) therein panayam (before) the malak (king).
It happened, when the malak (king) had heard the dabar (words) of the thawarah (law), that he tore his clothes.

The malak (king) tzawah (commanded) Chalaqayah, and Achayaqam the ban (son) Shapan Shaphan, and Ibadawan the ban (son) of Mayakah, and Shapan the scribe, and Ishayah the malak (king's) ibad (servant), saying,

"yalak (go) inquire of Yahawah for me, and for those who are shaar (left) in Yasharaal (Israel) and in Yahawadah (Judah), concerning the dabar (words) of the book that is found; for gadawal (great) is the chamah (wrath) of Yahawah that is poured out on us, because our abawath (fathers) have not kept the dabar (word) of Yahawah, to do according to all that is written in this book.

So Chalaqayah, and they whom the malak (king) had commanded, went to Chaladah the prophetess, the ashah (wife) of Shalawam the ban (son) Thaqawah Tokhath, the ban (son) of Chasarah, keeper of the bagad (wardrobe); (now she lived in Yarawashalam in the mashanah (second) quarter;) and they spoke to her to that effect.
She said to them, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): ‘amar (tell) the ayash (man) who sent you to me,

"Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘Behold, I will bawaa (bring) rai (evil) on this place, and on its yashab (inhabitants), even all the alah (curses) that are written in the book which they have qaraa (read) panayam (before) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah).

Because they have forsaken me, and have burned qatar (incense) to other Alahayam, that they might provoke me to kais (anger) with all the maishah (works) of their yad (hands); therefore is my chamah (wrath) poured out on this place, and it shall not be quenched.'"'

But to the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), who sent you to inquire of Yahawah, thus you shall amar (tell) him, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): "As touching the dabar (words) which you have heard,

because your labab (heart) was tender, and you humbled yourself panayam (before) Alahayam, when you heard his dabar (words) against this place, and against its yashab (inhabitants), and have humbled yourself panayam (before) me, and have torn your clothes, and wept panayam (before) me; I also have heard you," says Yahawah.

"Behold, I will asap (gather) you to your abawath (fathers), and you shall be gathered to your qabar (grave) in shalawam (peace), neither shall your iyan (eyes) raah (see) all the rai (evil) that I will bawaa (bring) on this place, and on its yashab (inhabitants)."'" They brought shawab (turn back / repent) dabar (word) to the malak (king).
Then the malak (king) sent and gathered asap (together) all the zaqan (elders) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam.

The malak (king) went up to the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and all the men of Yahawadah (Judah) and the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, and the kahan (priests), and the Lawayay (Levites), and all the im (people), both gadawal (great) and qatan (small): and he qaraa (read) in their ears all the dabar (words) of the book of the barayath (covenant) that was found in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

The malak (king) stood in his imad (place), and made a barayath (covenant) panayam (before) Yahawah, to yalak (walk) achar (after) Yahawah, and to shamar (keep) his matzawah (commandments), and his idawath (testimonies), and his chaq (statutes), with all his labab (heart), and with all his napash (soul), to ishah (perform) the dabar (words) of the barayath (covenant) that were written in this book.

He caused all who were found in Yarawashalam and Banayamayan to imad (stand). The yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam did according to the barayath (covenant) of Alahayam, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers).

Yaashayah took sawar (away) all the thawaibah (abominations) out of all the aratz (countries) that pertained to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and made all who were found in Yasharaal (Israel) to ibad (serve), even to ibad (serve) Yahawah their Alahayam. All his yawam (days) they didn't sawar (depart) from following Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers).
Yaashayah kept a pasach (passover) to Yahawah in Yarawashalam: and they killed the pasach (passover) on the fourteenth day of the raashawan (first) chadash (month).
He imad (set) the kahan (priests) in their offices, and encouraged them to the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

He said Lawayay the Levites who taught all Yasharaal (Israel), who were qadawash (holy) to Yahawah, "nathan (put) the qadash (holy) arawan (ark) in the bayath (house) which Shalamah the ban (son) of Dawad malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) built. There shall no more be a mashaa (burden) on your shoulders. Now ibad (serve) Yahawah your Alahayam, and his im (people) Yasharaal (Israel).

kawan (prepare) yourselves after your abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses) by your divisions, according to the writing of Dawad malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), and according to the writing of Shalamah his ban (son).

imad (stand) in the qadash (holy) place according to the divisions of the abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses) of your ach (brothers) the children of the ban (people), and let there be for each a portion of a abawath (fathers)' Lawayay of the Levites.
Kill the pasach (passover), and qadash (sanctify) yourselves, and kawan (prepare) for your ach (brothers), to do according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah by Mashah.

Yaashayah gave to the children of the ban (people), of the flock, lambs and ban (young) goats, all of them for the pasach (passover) offerings, to all who were matzaa (present), to the number of shalawashayam (thirty) alap (thousand), and shalawash (three) alap (thousand) bulls: these were of the malak (king's) rakawash (substance).

His shar (princes) gave for a freewill nadabah (offering) to the im (people), to the kahan (priests), and Lawayay the Levites. Chalaqayah and Zakarayah and Yachayaal, the nagayad (rulers) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam, gave to the kahan (priests) for the pasach (passover) offerings two alap (thousand) and shash (six) maah (hundred) small livestock, and shalawash (three) maah (hundred) baqar (head) of cattle.

Kawananayahaw also, and Shamaiyah and Nathanaal, his ach (brothers), and Chashabayah and Yaiyaal and Yawazabad, the shar (chiefs) Lawayay the Levites, gave Lawayay the Levites for the pasach (passover) offerings chamash (five) alap (thousand) small livestock, and chamash (five) maah (hundred) baqar (head) of cattle.
So the ibadah (service) was prepared, and the kahan (priests) stood in their imad (place), and the Lawayay (Levites) by their divisions, according to the malak (king's) matzawah (commandment).
They killed the pasach (passover), and the kahan (priests) sprinkled the blood which they received of their yad (hand), and the Lawayay (Levites) flayed them.

They removed the burnt ilah (offerings), that they might nathan (give) them according to the divisions of the abawath (fathers)' houses of the children of the ban (people), to qarab (offer) to Yahawah, as it is written in the book of Mashah. So they did with the cattle.

They roasted the pasach (passover) with ash (fire) according to the mashapat (ordinance): and the qadash (holy) bashal (offerings) boiled they in pots, and in caldrons, and in pans, and carried them quickly to all the children of the ban (people).

Afterward they prepared for themselves, and for the kahan (priests), because the kahan (priests) the ban (sons) of Aharawan were busy with offering the burnt offerings and the fat until layal (night): Lawayay the Levites prepared for themselves, and for the kahan (priests) the ban (sons) of Aharawan.

The singers the ban (sons) of Asap were in their place, according to the matzawah (commandment) of Dawad, and Asap, and Hayaman, and Yadawathawan the malak (king's) chazah (seer); and the porters were at every gate: they didn't need to sawar (depart) from their ibadah (service); for their ach (brothers) the Lawayay (Levites) prepared for them.

So all the ibadah (service) of Yahawah was prepared the same yawam (day), to ishah (keep) the pasach (passover), and to ilah (offer) burnt ilah (offerings) on the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah, according to the matzawah (commandment) of malak (king) Yaashayah.
The children of Yasharaal (Israel) who were matzaa (present) kept the pasach (passover) at that ith (time), and the chag (feast) of unleavened matzah (bread) shabai (seven) yawam (days).

There was no pasach (passover) like that kept in Yasharaal (Israel) from the yawam (days) of Shamawaal the nabayaa (prophet); neither did any of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel) ishah (keep) such a pasach (passover) as Yaashayah kept, and the kahan (priests), and the Lawayay (Levites), and all Yahawadah (Judah) and Yasharaal (Israel) who were matzaa (present), and the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam.
In the eighteenth Shanah of the malakawath (reign) of Yaashayah was this pasach (passover) kept.

achar (after) all this, when Yaashayah had prepared the bayath (temple), Nakaw malak (king) of Matzarayam went up to fight against Karakamayash by the Parath: and Yaashayah went out qaraah (against) him.

But he sent malaak (ambassadors) to him, saying, "What have I to do with you, you malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah)? I come not against you this yawam (day), but against the bayath (house) with which I have war. Alahayam has commanded me to make haste. Beware that it is Alahayam who is with me, that he not shachath (destroy) you.

Nevertheless Yaashayah would not sabab (turn) his panayam (face) from him, but disguised himself, that he might fight with him, and didn't listen to the dabar (words) Nakaw Neco from the pah (mouth) of Alahayam, and came to fight in the Baqaih of Magadawan.
The archers shot at malak (king) Yaashayah; and the malak (king) said to his ibad (servants), "ibar (take) me away, because I am seriously chalah (wounded)!

So his ibad (servants) took him out of the chariot, and put him in the mashanah (second) chariot that he had, and brought him to Yarawashalam; and he died, and was buried in the tombs of his abawath (fathers). All Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam mourned for Yaashayah.

Yaramayah lamented for Yaashayah: and all the singing men and singing women spoke of Yaashayah in their lamentations to this yawam (day); and they made them an chaq (ordinance) in Yasharaal (Israel): and behold, they are written in the lamentations.
Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yaashayah, and his chasad (good) deeds, according to that which is written in the thawarah (law) of Yahawah,
and his dabar (acts), raashawan (first) and Acharawan, behold, they are written in the book of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah).
Then the im (people) of the aratz (land) took Yahawaachaz the ban (son) of Yaashayah, and made him malak (king) in his ab (father's) place in Yarawashalam.
Yawaachaz was isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned shalawash (three) chadash (months) in Yarawashalam.
The malak (king) of Matzarayam deposed him at Yarawashalam, and fined the aratz (land) one maah (hundred) talents of kasap (silver) and a talent of gold.

The malak (king) of Matzarayam made Alayaqayam his ach (brother) malak (king) over Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam, and changed his sham (name) to Yahawayaqayam. Nakaw took Yawaachaz his ach (brother), and carried him to Matzarayam.

Yahawayaqayam was isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned achad (eleven) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and he did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah his Alahayam.
Against him came up Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal, and bound him in fetters, to yalak (carry) him to Babal.
Nabawakadanaatzar also carried of the vessels of the bayath (house) of Yahawah to Babal, and nathan (put) them in his hayakal (temple) at Babal.

Now the yathar (rest) of the dabar (acts) of Yahawayaqayam, and his thawaibah (abominations) which he did, and that which was found in him, behold, they are written in the book of the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah): and Yahawayakayan his ban (son) reigned in his place.

Yahawayakayan was shamanah (eight) Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned shalawash (three) chadash (months) and ishar (ten) yawam (days) in Yarawashalam: and he did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah.

At the thashawabah (return) of the Shanah malak (king) Nabawakadanaatzar sent, and brought him to Babal, with the goodly vessels of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and made Tzadaqayah his ach (brother) malak (king) over Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam.
Tzadaqayah was isharayam (twenty) - one Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned achad (eleven) Shanah in Yarawashalam:
and he did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah his Alahayam; he didn't humble panayam (himself) before Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet) speaking from the pah (mouth) of Yahawah.

He also rebelled against malak (king) Nabawakadanaatzar, who had made him shabai (swear) by Alahayam: but he stiffened his neck, and hardened his labab (heart) against turning to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).

Moreover all the shar (chiefs) of the kahan (priests), and the im (people), trespassed very greatly after all the thawaibah (abominations) of the gawayam (nations); and they polluted the bayath (house) of Yahawah which he had made qadash (holy) in Yarawashalam.

Yahawah, the Alahayam of their abawath (fathers), sent to them by his malaak (messengers), rising up shakam (early) and sending, because he had compassion on his im (people), and on his dwelling place:

but they mocked the malaak (messengers) of Alahayam, and despised his dabar (words), and scoffed at his nabayaa (prophets), until the chamah (wrath) of Yahawah arose against his im (people), until there was no remedy.

Therefore he brought on them the malak (king) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), who killed their young men with the charab (sword) in the bayath (house) of their maqadash (sanctuary), and had no compassion on young bachawar (man) or virgin, old zaqan (man) or Yashash: he gave them all into his yad (hand).

All the vessels of the bayath (house) of Alahayam, gadawal (great) and qatan (small), and the treasures of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the treasures of the malak (king), and of his shar (princes), all these he brought to Babal.
They burnt the bayath (house) of Alahayam, and broke down the wall of Yarawashalam, and burnt all its palaces with ash (fire), and destroyed all the goodly vessels of it.

He carried those who had shaarayath (escaped) from the charab (sword) away to Babal; and they were ibad (servants) to him and his ban (sons) until the malak (reign) of the malakawath (kingdom) of Paras:

to fulfill the dabar (word) of Yahawah by the pah (mouth) of Yaramayah, until the aratz (land) had enjoyed its shabath (sabbaths). As long as it shamam (lay) desolate it kept Sabbath, to fulfill shabaiyam (seventy) Shanah.

Now in the achad (first) Shanah of Kawarash malak (king) of Paras, that the dabar (word) of Yahawah by the pah (mouth) of Yaramayah might be accomplished, Yahawah stirred up the rawach (spirit) of Kawarash malak (king) of Paras, so that he made a ibar (proclamation) throughout all his malakawath (kingdom), and put it also in writing, saying,

"Thus amar (says) Kawarash malak (king) of Paras, ‘Yahawah, the Alahayam of shamayam (heaven), has given all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (earth) to me; and he has commanded me to banah (build) him a bayath (house) in Yarawashalam, which is in Yahawadah (Judah). Whoever there is among you of all his im (people), Yahawah his Alahayam be with him, and let him ilah (go) up.'

Now in the achad (first) Shanah of Kawarash malak (king) of Paras, that the dabar (word) of Yahawah by the pah (mouth) of Yaramayah might be accomplished, Yahawah stirred up the rawach (spirit) of Kawarash malak (king) of Paras, so that he made a ibar (proclamation) throughout all his malakawath (kingdom), and put it also in writing, saying,

"Thus amar (says) Kawarash malak (king) of Paras, ‘Yahawah, the Alahayam of shamayam (heaven), has given me all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (earth); and he has commanded me to banah (build) him a bayath (house) in Yarawashalam, which is in Yahawadah (Judah).

Whoever there is among you of all his im (people), may his Alahayam be with him, and let him ilah (go) up to Yarawashalam, which is in Yahawadah (Judah), and banah (build) the bayath (house) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) (he is Alahayam), which is in Yarawashalam.

Whoever is shaar (left), in any place where he lives, let the men of his place nashaa (help) him with kasap (silver), with gold, with rakawash (goods), and with animals, besides the freewill nadabah (offering) for the bayath (house) of Alahayam which is in Yarawashalam.'

Then the raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households of Yahawadah (Judah) and Banayamayan, and the kahan (priests), and the Lawayay (Levites), even all whose rawach (spirit) Alahayam had stirred to ilah (go) up rose up to banah (build) the bayath (house) of Yahawah which is in Yarawashalam.

All those who were around them strengthened their yad (hands) with vessels of kasap (silver), with gold, with rakawash (goods), and with animals, and with precious things, besides all that was willingly offered.

Also Kawarash the malak (king) brought yatzaa (forth) the vessels of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, which Nabawakadanaatzar had brought out of Yarawashalam, and had nathan (put) in the bayath (house) of his Alahayam;
even those, Kawarash malak (king) of Paras brought out by the yad (hand) of Matharadath the treasurer, and numbered them to Shashabatzar, the nashayaa (prince) of Yahawadah (Judah).
This is the number of them: shalawashayam (thirty) platters of gold, one alap (thousand) platters of kasap (silver), isharayam (twenty) - thashai (nine) knives,
shalawashayam (thirty) bowls of gold, kasap (silver) bowls of a mashanah (second) sort arabai (four) maah (hundred) and ishar (ten), and other vessels one alap (thousand).

All the vessels of gold and of kasap (silver) were chamash (five) alap (thousand) and arabai (four) maah (hundred). Shashabatzar brought all these up, when the captives were brought up from Babal to Yarawashalam.

Now these are the children of the province, who went up out of the Shabay of those who had been carried away, whom Nabawakadanaatzar the malak (king) of Babal had carried away to Babal, and who returned to Yarawashalam and Yahawadah (Judah), everyone to his Iyar;
who came with Zarababal, Yashawai, Nachamayah, Sharayah, Railayah, Maradakay, Balashan, Masapar, Bagaway, Rachawam, Bainah. The number of the men of the im (people) of Yasharaal (Israel):
The children of Paraish, two alap (thousand) one maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) - shanayam (two).
The children of Shapatayah, shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) - shanayam (two).
The children of Arach, shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) - chamash (five).
The children of Pachathamawaab, of the children of Yashawai and Yawaab, two alap (thousand) shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) shanayam (twelve).
The children of Iyalam, one alap (thousand) two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) - arabai (four).
The children of Zathawaa, thashai (nine) maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five).
The children of Zakay, shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty).
The children of Banay, shash (six) maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two).
The children of Babay, shash (six) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three). three.
The children of Izagad, one alap (thousand) shanayam (two) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two).
The children of Adanayaqam, shash (six) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty) - shash (six).
The children of Bagaway, two alap (thousand) chamashayam (fifty) - shash (six).
The children of Idayan, arabai (four) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) - arabai (four).
The children of Atar, of Yachazaqayah, thashaiyam (ninety) - shamanah (eight).
The children of Batzay, shalawash (three) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three).
The children of Yawarah, one maah (hundred) shanayam (twelve).
The children of Chasham, two maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three).
The children of Gabar, thashaiyam (ninety) - chamash (five).
The children of Bayathalacham, one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three).
The men of Natapah, chamashayam (fifty) - shash (six).
The men of Inathawath, one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shamanah (eight).
The children of Izamawath, arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two).
The children of Kiriath Qarayathayairayam, Kapayarah, and Baarawath, shabai (seven) maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - shalawash (three).
The children of Ramah and Gabai, shash (six) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - one.
The men of Makamas, one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two).
The men of Bayathaal and Iy, two maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three).
The children of Nabaw, chamashayam (fifty) - shanayam (two).
The children of Magabayash, one maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) - shash (six).
The children of the other Iyalam, one alap (thousand) two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) - arabai (four).
The children of Charam, shalawash (three) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty).
The children of Lad, Chadayad, and Awanaw, shabai (seven) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five).
The children of Yarayachaw, shalawash (three) maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five).
The children of Sanaah, shalawash (three) alap (thousand) shash (six) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty).
The kahan (priests): the children of Yadaiyah, of the bayath (house) of Yashawai, thashai (nine) maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) - shalawash (three).
The children of Amar, one alap (thousand) chamashayam (fifty) - shanayam (two).
The children Pashachawar Pashhur, one alap (thousand) two maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - shabai (seven).
The children of Charam, one alap (thousand) seventeen.
The Lawayay (Levites): the children of Yashawai and Qadamayaal, of the children of Hawadawayah, shabaiyam (seventy) - arabai (four).
The singers: the children of Asap, one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shamanah (eight).

The children of the porters: the children of Shalawam, the children of Atar, the children of Talamawan, the children of Iqawab, the children of Chatayataa, the children of Shabay, in all one maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - thashai (nine).
The Nethinim: the children of Tzayachaa, the children of Chashawapaa, the children Tabaiwath Tabbaoth,
the children of Qayaras, the children of Sayaia, the children of Padawan,
the children of Labanaa, the children of Chagabaa, the children of Iqawab,
the children of Chagab, the children Shamalay Shamlai, the children Chanan Hanan,
the children of Gadal, the children of Gachar, the children of Raayah,
the children of Ratzayan, the children of Naqawadaa, the children of Gazam,
the children of Izaa, the children of Pasach, the children of Basay,
the children of Asanah, the children of Maiwanay, the children Napawashasayam Nephisim,
the children of Baqabawaq, the children of Chaqawapaa, the children of Charachawar,
the children of Batzalawath, the children of Machayadaa, the children of Charashaa,
the children of Baraqawas, the children of Sayasaraa, the children Thamach Temah,
the children of Natzayach, the children of Chatayapaa.
The children of Shalamah ibad (servants): the children of Sawatay, the children Saparath Hassophereth, the children of Parawadaa,
the children of Yailaa, the children of Daraqawan, the children of Gadal,
the children of Shapatayah, the children of Chatayal, the children of Pakarathatzabayayam Hazzebaim, the children of Amay.
All the Nethinim, and the children of Shalamah ibad (servants), were shalawash (three) maah (hundred) thashaiyam (ninety) - shanayam (two).

These were those who went up from Thalamalach Melah, Thalacharashaa Harsha, karawab (cherub), Adan, and Amar; but they could not show their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), and their zarai (seed), whether they were of Yasharaal (Israel):
the children of Dalayah, the children of Tawabayah, the children of Naqawadaa, shash (six) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) - shanayam (two).

Of the children of the kahan (priests): the children of Chabayah, the children of Qawatz, the children of Barazalay, who took a ashah (wife) of the bath (daughters) of Barazalay the Galaiday (Gileadite), and was called after their sham (name).
These sought their place among those who were registered by genealogy, but they were not found: therefore were they deemed polluted and put from the kahanah (priesthood).
The governor said to them, that they should not akal (eat) of the most qadash (holy) things, until there stood up a kahan (priest) with awarayam (urim) and with thamayam (thummim).
The whole qahal (assembly) achad (together) was forty - two alap (thousand) shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty),

besides their male ibad (servants) and their female ibad (servants), of whom there were shabai (seven) alap (thousand) shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - shabai (seven): and they had two maah (hundred) singing men and singing women.
Their horses were shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - shash (six); their mules, two maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five);
their camels, arabai (four) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - chamash (five); their donkeys, shash (six) alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) and isharayam (twenty).

Some of the raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households, when they came to the bayath (house) of Yahawah which is in Yarawashalam, offered willingly for the bayath (house) of Alahayam to imad (set) it up in its place:

they gave after their kach (ability) into the treasury of the malaakah (work) sixty - one alap (thousand) darics of gold, and chamash (five) alap (thousand) minas of kasap (silver), and one maah (hundred) kahan (priests)' garments.
So the kahan (priests), and the Lawayay (Levites), and some of the im (people), and the singers, and the porters, and the Nethinim, lived in their Iyar, and all Yasharaal (Israel) in their Iyar.

When the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month) had nagai (come), and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) were in the Iyar, the im (people) gathered themselves asap (together) as one ayash (man) to Yarawashalam.

Then stood up Yashawai the ban (son) of Yawatzadaq, and his ach (brothers) the kahan (priests), and Zarababal the ban (son) of Shaalathayaal, and his ach (brothers), and built the mazabach (altar) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), to ilah (offer) burnt ilah (offerings) thereon, as it is written in the thawarah (law) of Mashah the ayash (man) of Alahayam.

They kawan (set) the mazabach (altar) on its base; for ayamah (fear) was on them because of the im (peoples) of the aratz (countries): and they offered burnt ilah (offerings) thereon to Yahawah, even burnt ilah (offerings) baqar (morning) and evening.

They kept the chag (feast) of sakah (tents), as it is written, and offered the yawam (daily) burnt ilah (offerings) by number, according to the mashapat (ordinance), as the dabar (duty) of every yawam (day) yawam (required);

and afterward the continual burnt ilah (offering), and the offerings of the new chadash (moons), and of all the mawaid (set) feasts of Yahawah that were consecrated, and of everyone who willingly offered a freewill nadab (offering) to Yahawah.

From the achad (first) yawam (day) of the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month) began they to ilah (offer) burnt ilah (offerings) to Yahawah: but the yasad (foundation) of the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah was not yet laid.

They gave kasap (money) also to the chatzab (masons), and to the carpenters; and food, and drink, and shaman (oil), to them of Tzayadanay, and to them of Tzaray, to bawaa (bring) cedar itz (trees) from Labanawan to the yam (sea), to Yapaw, according to the grant that they had of Kawarash malak (king) of Paras.

Now in the shanay (second) Shanah of their coming to the bayath (house) of Alahayam at Yarawashalam, in the shanay (second) chadash (month), began Zarababal the ban (son) of Shaalathayaal, and Yashawai the ban (son) of Yawatzadaq, and the shaar (rest) of their ach (brothers) the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites), and all those who were bawaa (come) out of the Shabay to Yarawashalam, and appointed the Lawayay (Levites), from isharayam (twenty) Shanah ban (old) and upward, to have the oversight of the malaakah (work) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

Then stood Yashawai with his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), Qadamayaal and his ban (sons), the ban (sons) of Yahawadah (Judah), achad (together), to have the oversight of the workmen in the bayath (house) of Alahayam: the ban (sons) of Chanadad, with their ban (sons) and their ach (brothers) the Lawayay (Levites).
