When the banah (builders) laid the yasad (foundation) of the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, they imad (set) the kahan (priests) Labash their clothing with trumpets, and the Lawayay (Levites) the ban (sons) of Asap with cymbals, to halal (praise) Yahawah, after the yad (order) of Dawad malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).

They sang inah (one) to another in praising and giving yadah (thanks) to Yahawah, "For he is tawab (good), for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever) toward Yasharaal (Israel)." All the im (people) shouted with a gadawal (great) shout, when they praised Yahawah, because the yasad (foundation) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah was laid.

But many of the kahan (priests) and Lawayay (Levites) and raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households, the zaqan (old) men who had seen the raashawan (first) bayath (house), when the yasad (foundation) of this bayath (house) was laid before their iyan (eyes), wept with a gadawal (loud) qawal (voice); and many shouted aloud for joy:

so that the im (people) could not nakar (discern) the qawal (noise) of the shout of joy from the qawal (noise) of the weeping of the im (people); for the im (people) shouted with a gadawal (loud) shout, and the qawal (noise) was heard Rachawaq off.
Now when the tzar (adversaries) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Banayamayan heard that the children of the captivity were building a hayakal (temple) to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel);

then they drew near to Zarababal, and to the raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households, and said to them, "Let us banah (build) with you; for we seek your Alahayam, as you do; and we zabach (sacrifice) to him since the yawam (days) of Asarachadawan Haddon malak (king) of Ashawar, who brought us up here.

But Zarababal, and Yashawai, and the shaar (rest) of the raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households of Yasharaal (Israel), said to them, "You have nothing to do with us in building a bayath (house) to our Alahayam; but we ourselves together will banah (build) to Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), as malak (king) Kawarash the malak (king) of Paras has tzawah (commanded) us.
Then the im (people) of the aratz (land) weakened the yad (hands) of the im (people) of Yahawadah (Judah), and troubled them in building,

and hired yaitz (counselors) against them, to parar (frustrate) their itzah (purpose), all the yawam (days) of Kawarash malak (king) of Paras, even until the malakawath (reign) of Darayawash malak (king) of Paras.
In the malakawath (reign) of Achashawarawash, in the thachalah (beginning) of his malakawath (reign), wrote they an accusation against the yashab (inhabitants) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam.

In the yawam (days) Arathachashashathaa Artaxerxes wrote Bashalam, Matharadath, Tabaal, and the shaar (rest) of his companions, Arathachashashathaa Artaxerxes malak (king) of Paras; and the writing of the letter was written in Aramayath (Syrian), and set forth in the Aramayath (Syrian) language.
Rachawam the chancellor and Shamashay the scribe wrote a letter against Yarawashalam Arathachashashathaa Artaxerxes the malak (king) in this sort:

then Rachawam the chancellor, and Shamashay the scribe, and the shaar (rest) of their companions, the Dinaites, and the Apharsathchites, the Tarpelites, the Aparasay, the Arakaway, the Babalay (Babylonians), the Shawashanakay, the Dehaites, the Ilamay (Elamites),

and the shaar (rest) of the amah (nations) whom the Rab and Yaqayar Asanapar brought over, and set in the city of Shamarayan, and in the shaar (rest) of the country Ibar the nahar (river), and so forth, wrote.
This is the copy of the letter that they sent to Arathachashashathaa the malak (king): Your ibad (servants) the men Ibar the nahar (river), and so forth.

Be it known to the malak (king), that the Yahawadaay (Jews) who came up from you have come to us to Yarawashalam; they are building the Marad and the Baawash city, and have finished the walls, and repaired the foundations.
Be it known now to the malak (king) that if this city is built, and the walls finished, they will not pay tribute, custom, or toll, and in the end it will be hurtful to the malak (kings).
Now because we Day the salt of the hayakal (palace), and it is not Arak for us to see the malak (king's) dishonor, therefore have we sent and informed the malak (king);

that search may be made in the book of the records of your abawath (fathers): so you shall find in the book of the records, and know that this city is a Marad city, and hurtful to malak (kings) and provinces, and that they have moved sedition within the same of old yawam (time); for which cause was this city laid waste.
We inform the malak (king) that, if this city be built, and the walls finished, by this means you shall have no portion Ibar the nahar (river).

Then the malak (king) sent an pathagam (answer) to Rachawam the chancellor, and to Shamashay the scribe, and to the shaar (rest) of their companions who dwell in Shamarayan, and in the shaar (rest) of the country Ibar the nahar (river): shalam (peace), and so forth.
The letter which you sent to us has been plainly read Qadam me.
I decreed, and search has been made, and it is found that this city of old yawam (time) has made insurrection against malak (kings), and that rebellion and sedition have been made therein.
There have been thaqayap (mighty) malak (kings) also over Yarawashalam, who have ruled over all the country Ibar the nahar (river); and tribute, custom, and toll, was paid to them.
shawam (make) a taim (decree) now to cause these men to cease, and that this city not be built, until a decree shall be made by me.
hawaa (take) heed that you not be slack herein: why should damage grow to the hurt of the malak (kings)?

Then when the copy of malak (king) Arathachashashathaa' letter was read Qadam Rachawam, and Shamashay the scribe, and their companions, they went in haste to Yarawashalam to the Yahawadaay (Jews), and made them to cease by force and chayal (power).
Then ceased the ibayadah (work) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam which is at Yarawashalam; and it ceased until the tharayan (second) year of the malakaw (reign) of Darayawash malak (king) of Paras.

Now the nabayaa (prophets), Chagay the nabayaa (prophet), and Zakarayah the bar (son) of Idaw, prophesied to the Yahawadaay (Jews) who were in Yahawad (Judah) and Yarawashalam; in the sham (name) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) they prophesied to them.

Then rose up Zarababal the bar (son) of Shaalathayaal, and Yashawai the bar (son) of Yawatzadaq, and began to build the bayath (house) of Alahayam which is at Yarawashalam; and with them were the nabayaa (prophets) of Alahayam, helping them.

At the same time came to them Tattenai, the governor Ibar the nahar (river), and Shatharabawazanay, and their companions, and said Kan to them, "Who gave you a decree to build this bayath (house), and to finish this wall?
Then we told them in this kanamaa (way), what the sham (names) of the men were who were making this building.

But the iyan (eye) of their Alahayam was on the elders of the Yahawadaay (Jews), and they did not make them cease, until the taim (matter) should come to Darayawash, and then thawab (answer) should be returned by letter concerning it.

The copy of the letter that Tattenai, the governor Ibar the nahar (river), and Shatharabawazanay, and his companions the Apharsachites, who were Ibar the nahar (river), sent to Darayawash the malak (king);
they sent a pathagam (letter) to him, in which was written thus: To Darayawash the malak (king), all shalam (peace).

Be it known to the malak (king), that we went into the province of Yahawad (Judah), to the bayath (house) of the Rab Alahayam, which is built with great aban (stones), and timber is laid in the walls; and this ibayadah (work) goes on with diligence and tzalach (prospers) in their yad (hands).
Then we asked those elders, and said to them thus, "Who gave you a decree to build this bayath (house), and to finish this wall?
We asked them their sham (names) also, to inform you that we might write the sham (names) of the men who were at their raash (head).

Thus they returned us pathagam (answer), saying, "We are the ibad (servants) of the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven) and arai (earth), and are building the bayath (house) that was built these Shagayaa years ago, which a Rab malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) built and finished.

But after that our abawath (fathers) had provoked the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven) to ragaz (wrath), he gave them into the yad (hand) of Nabawakadanatzar malak (king) of Babal, the Kasaday (Chaldean), who destroyed this bayath (house), and carried the im (people) away into Babal.
But in the chad (first) year of Kawarash malak (king) of Babal, Kawarash the malak (king) made a taim (decree) to build this bayath (house) of Alahayam.

The gold and silver vessels also Day the bayath (house) of Alahayam, which Nabawakadanatzar took out of the hayakal (temple) that was in Yarawashalam, and brought into the hayakal (temple) of Babal, those Kawarash the malak (king) took out of the hayakal (temple) of Babal, and they were delivered to one whose sham (name) was Shashabatzar, whom he had made governor;
and he said to him, ‘Take these vessels, go, put them in the hayakal (temple) that is in Yarawashalam, and let the bayath (house) of Alahayam be built in its place.'

Then the same Shashabatzar came, and laid the foundations of the bayath (house) of Alahayam which is in Yarawashalam: and since that time even until now has it been in building, and yet it is not completed.

Now therefore, if it seem tab (good) to the malak (king), let a search be made in the malak (king's) treasure bayath (house), which is there at Babal, whether it be so, that a taim (decree) was made of Kawarash the malak (king) to build this bayath (house) of Alahayam at Yarawashalam; and let the malak (king) send his pleasure to us concerning this matter.
Then Darayawash the malak (king) made a taim (decree), and search was made in the bayath (house) of the archives, where the treasures were laid up in Babal.
There was found at Achamathaa, in the palace that is in the province Maday Media, a scroll, and therein was Kan written for a record:

In the chad (first) year of Kawarash the malak (king), Kawarash the malak (king) made a taim (decree): Concerning the bayath (house) of Alahayam at Yarawashalam, let the bayath (house) be built, the place where they offer dabach (sacrifices), and let its foundations be strongly laid; its height Shathayan cubits, and its breadth Shathayan cubits;
with thalath (three) courses of great aban (stones), and a course of Chadath timber: and let the expenses be given out of the malak (king's) bayath (house).

Also let the gold and silver vessels of the bayath (house) of Alahayam, which Nabawakadanatzar took forth out of the hayakal (temple) which is at Yarawashalam, and brought to Babal, be restored, and brought again to the hayakal (temple) which is at Yarawashalam, everyone to its place; and you shall put them in the bayath (house) of Alahayam.
Now therefore, Tattenai, governor Ibar the nahar (river), Shatharabawazanay, and your companions the Apharsachites, who are Ibar the nahar (river), you must stay Rachayaq from there.

Leave the ibayadah (work) of this bayath (house) of Alahayam shabaq (alone); let the governor of the Yahawadaay (Jews) and the elders of the Yahawadaay (Jews) build this bayath (house) of Alahayam in its place.

Moreover I shawam (make) a taim (decree) what you shall do to these elders of the Yahawadaay (Jews) for the building of this bayath (house) of Alahayam: that of the malak (king's) nakas (goods), Day of the tribute Ibar the nahar (river), expenses be given with all diligence to these men, that they be not hindered.

That which they have need of, both ban (young) bulls, and rams, and lambs, for burnt ilah (offerings) to the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven); also wheat, salt, chamar (wine), and mashach (oil), according to the word of the kahan (priests) who are at Yarawashalam, let it be given them yawam (day) by yawam (day) without fail;
that they may offer nayachawach (sacrifices) of pleasant aroma to the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven), and pray for the chay (life) of the malak (king), and of his ban (sons).

Also I have made a taim (decree), that whoever shall alter this pathagam (word), let a beam be pulled out from his bayath (house), and let him be lifted up and fastened thereon; and let his bayath (house) be made a dunghill for this:

and the Alahayam who has caused his sham (name) to dwell there overthrow all malak (kings) and im (peoples) who shall put forth their yad (hand) to alter the same, to chabal (destroy) this bayath (house) of Alahayam which is at Yarawashalam. I Darayawash have made a taim (decree); let it be done with all diligence.
Then Tattenai, the governor Ibar the nahar (river), Shatharabawazanay, and their companions, because Darayawash the malak (king) had sent a decree, did accordingly with all diligence.

The elders of the Yahawadaay (Jews) built and prospered, through the prophesying of Chagay the nabayaa (prophet) and Zakarayah the bar (son) of Idaw. They built and finished it, according to the commandment of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), and according to the taim (decree) of Kawarash, and Darayawash, and Arathachashashathaa malak (king) of Paras.
This bayath (house) was finished on the thalath (third) yawam (day) of the month Adar, which was in the shath (sixth) year of the malakaw (reign) of Darayawash the king.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel), the kahan (priests), and the Laway (Levites), and the shaar (rest) of the children of the captivity, kept the dedication of this bayath (house) of Alahayam with joy.

They offered at the dedication of this bayath (house) of Alahayam one maah (hundred) bulls, two maah (hundred) rams, arabai (four) maah (hundred) lambs; and for a chataah (sin) offering for all Yasharaal (Israel), tharayan (twelve) male goats, according to the number of the tribes of Yasharaal (Israel).

They qawam (set) the kahan (priests) in their divisions, and the Laway (Levites) in their courses, for the ibayadah (service) of Alahayam, which is at Yarawashalam; as it is written in the book of Mashah.
The children of the captivity kept the pasach (passover) on the fourteenth day of the raashawan (first) chadash (month).

For the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites) had purified themselves achad (together); all of them were tahawar (pure): and they killed the pasach (passover) for all the children of the captivity, and for their ach (brothers) the kahan (priests), and for themselves.

The children of Yasharaal (Israel) who had shawab (turn back / repent) again out of the captivity, and all such as had separated themselves to them from the tamaah (filthiness) of the gaway (nations) of the aratz (land), to seek Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ate,

and kept the chag (feast) of unleavened matzah (bread) shabai (seven) yawam (days) with joy: for Yahawah had made them Shamach, and had turned the lab (heart) of the malak (king) of Ashawar to them, to chazaq (strengthen) their yad (hands) in the malaakah (work) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).

Now achar (after) these things, in the malakawath (reign) Arathachashashathaa Artaxerxes malak (king) of Paras, Izaraa the ban (son) of Sharayah, the ban (son) of Izarayah, the ban (son) Chalaqayah Hilkiah,
the ban (son) of Shalawam, the ban (son) of Tzadawaq, the ban (son) of Achayatawab,
the ban (son) of Amarayah, the ban (son) of Izarayah, the ban (son) of Marayawath,
the ban (son) of Zarachayah, the ban (son) of Izay, the ban (son) of Baqay,
the ban (son) of Abayashawai, the ban (son) of Payanachas, the ban (son) of Alaizar, the ban (son) of Aharawan the raash (chief) kahan (priest);

this Izaraa went up from Babal: and he was a Mahayar scribe in the thawarah (law) of Mashah, which Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), had given; and the malak (king) granted him all his request, according to the yad (hand) of Yahawah his Alahayam on him.

There went up some of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), and of the kahan (priests), and the Lawayay (Levites), and the singers, and the porters, and the Nethinim, to Yarawashalam, in the seventh Shanah Arathachashashathaa Artaxerxes the malak (king).
He came to Yarawashalam in the chamayashay (fifth) chadash (month), which was in the shabayaiy (seventh) Shanah of the malak (king).

For on the achad (first) day of the raashawan (first) chadash (month) began he to go up from Babal; and on the achad (first) day of the chamayashay (fifth) chadash (month) came he to Yarawashalam, according to the tawab (good) yad (hand) of his Alahayam on him.
Izaraa he had kawan (set) his labab (heart) to seek the thawarah (law) of Yahawah, and to do it, and to teach in Yasharaal (Israel) chaq (statutes) and mashapat (ordinances).

Now this is the copy of the letter that the malak (king) Arathachashashathaa gave to Izaraa the kahan (priest), the scribe, even the scribe of the dabar (words) of the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah, and of his chaq (statutes) to Yasharaal (Israel):
Arathachashashathaa, malak (king) of malak (kings), to Izaraa the kahan (priest), the scribe of the dath (law) of the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven), perfect and so forth.

I shawam (make) a taim (decree), that all those of the im (people) of Yasharaal (Israel), and their kahan (priests) and the Laway (Levites), in my malakaw (realm), who are minded of their own free will to go to Yarawashalam, go with you.

Day you are sent of the malak (king) and his shabaih (seven) counselors, to inquire concerning Yahawad (Judah) and Yarawashalam, according to the dath (law) of your Alahayam which is in your yad (hand),
and to carry the silver and gold, which the malak (king) and his counselors have freely offered to the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), whose habitation is in Yarawashalam,

and all the silver and gold that you shall find in all the province of Babal, with the freewill nadab (offering) of the im (people), and of the kahan (priests), nadab (offering) willingly for the bayath (house) of their Alahayam which is in Yarawashalam;

therefore you shall with all diligence buy with this money bulls, rams, lambs, with their meal manachah (offerings) and their drink nasak (offerings), and shall offer them on the madabach (altar) of the bayath (house) of your Alahayam which is in Yarawashalam.
Whatever shall seem yatab (good) to you and to your ach (brothers) to do with the shaar (rest) of the silver and the gold, do that after the will of your Alahayam.
The vessels that are given to you for the service of the bayath (house) of your Alahayam, deliver Qadam the Alahayam of Yarawashalam.
Whatever more shall be needful for the bayath (house) of your Alahayam, which you shall have occasion to bestow, bestow it out of the malak (king's) treasure bayath (house).

I, even I Arathachashashathaa the malak (king), do shawam (make) a taim (decree) to all the treasurers who are Ibar the nahar (river), that whatever Izaraa the kahan (priest), the scribe of the dath (law) of the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven), shall require of you, it be done with all diligence,

to one maah (hundred) talents of silver, and to one maah (hundred) measures of wheat, and to one maah (hundred) baths of chamar (wine), and to one maah (hundred) baths of mashach (oil), and salt without prescribing how much.

Whatever is commanded by the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven), let it be done exactly for the bayath (house) of the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven); Day why should there be qatzap (wrath) against the malakaw (realm) of the malak (king) and his ban (sons)?

Also we inform you, that touching any of the kahan (priests) and Laway (Levites), the singers, porters, Nethinim, or servants of this bayath (house) of Alahayam, it shall not be shalayat (lawful) to impose tribute, custom, or toll, on them.

You, Izaraa, after the chakamah (wisdom) of your Alahayam who is in your yad (hand), appoint magistrates and dayan (judges), who may hawaa (judge) all the im (people) who are Ibar the nahar (river), all such as know the dath (laws) of your Alahayam; and teach him who doesn't know them.

Whoever will not do the dath (law) of your Alahayam, and the dath (law) of the malak (king), let dayan (judgment) be executed on him with all diligence, whether it be to mawath (death), or to banishment, or to confiscation of nakas (goods), or to imprisonment.

Blessed be Yahawah, the Alahayam of our abawath (fathers), who has nathan (put) such a thing as this in the malak (king's) lab (heart), to paar (beautify) the bayath (house) of Yahawah which is in Yarawashalam;

and has extended loving chasad (kindness) to me panayam (before) the malak (king), and his yaitz (counselors), and before all the malak (king's) gabawar (mighty) shar (princes). I was strengthened according to the yad (hand) of Yahawah my Alahayam on me, and I gathered together out of Yasharaal (Israel) raash (chief) men to ilah (go) up with me.

Now these are the raash (heads) of their abawath (fathers)' households, and this is the genealogy of those who went up with me from Babal, in the malakawath (reign) Arathachashashathaa Artaxerxes the king:
Of the ban (sons) of Payanachas, Garasham. Of the ban (sons) of Ayathamar, Danayaal. Of the ban (sons) of Dawad, Chatawash.
Of the ban (sons) of Shakanayah, of the ban (sons) of Paraish, Zakarayah; and with him were reckoned by genealogy of the zakar (males) one maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty).
Of the ban (sons) of Pachathamawaab, Alayahawaiyanay the ban (son) of Zarachayah; and with him two maah (hundred) zakar (males).
Of the ban (sons) of Shakanayah, the ban (son) of Yachazayaal; and with him shalawash (three) maah (hundred) zakar (males).
Of the ban (sons) of Idayan, Ibad the ban (son) of Yawanathan; and with him chamashayam (fifty) zakar (males).
Of the ban (sons) of Iyalam, Yashaiyah the ban (son) of Ithalayah; and with him shabaiyam (seventy) zakar (males).
Of the ban (sons) of Shapatayah, Zabadayah the ban (son) of Mayakaal; and with him shamanayam (eighty) zakar (males).
Of the ban (sons) of Yawaab, Ibadayah the ban (son) of Yachayaal; and with him two maah (hundred) and eighteen zakar (males).
Of the ban (sons) of Shalamayath, the ban (son) of Yawasapayah; and with him one maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty) zakar (males).
Of the ban (sons) of Babay, Zakarayah the ban (son) of Babay; and with him isharayam (twenty) - shamanah (eight) zakar (males).
Of the ban (sons) of Izagad, Yawachanan the ban (son) of Qatan; and with him one maah (hundred) ishar (ten) zakar (males).
Of the ban (sons) of Adanayaqam, who were the Acharawan; and these are their sham (names): Alayapalat, Yaiyaal, and Shamaiyah; and with them shashayam (sixty) zakar (males).
Of the ban (sons) of Bagaway, Iwathay and Zabawad; and with them shabaiyam (seventy) zakar (males).

I gathered them together to the nahar (river) that bawaa (runs) to Ahawaa; and there we encamped shalawash (three) yawam (days): and I viewed the im (people), and the kahan (priests), and found there none of the ban (sons) of Laway.

Then sent I for Alayaizar, for Arayaal, for Shamaiyah, and for Alanathan, and for Yarayab, and for Alanathan, and for Nathan, and for Zakarayah, and for Mashalam, raash (chief) men; also for Yawayarayab, and for Alanathan, who were teachers.

I sent them yatzaa (forth) to Adaw the raash (chief) at the place Kasapayaa; and I told them dabar (what) they should shawam (tell) Adaw, and his ach (brothers) the Nethinim, at the place Kasapayaa, that they should bawaa (bring) to us sharath (ministers) for the bayath (house) of our Alahayam.

According to the tawab (good) yad (hand) of our Alahayam on us they brought us a ayash (man) of shakal (discretion), of the ban (sons) of Machalay, the ban (son) of Laway, the ban (son) of Yasharaal (Israel); and Sharabayah, with his ban (sons) and his ach (brothers), eighteen;
and Chashabayah, and with him Yashaiyah of the ban (sons) of Mararay, his ach (brothers) and their ban (sons), isharayam (twenty);

and of the Nethinim, whom Dawad and the shar (princes) had given for the ibadah (service) Lawayay the Levites, two maah (hundred) and isharayam (twenty) Nethinim: all of them were mentioned by sham (name).

Then I proclaimed a fast there, at the nahar (river) Ahawaa, that we might humble ourselves panayam (before) our Alahayam, to seek of him a yashar (straight) darak (way) for us, and for our little ones, and for all our rakawash (substance).

For I was bawash (ashamed) to shaal (ask) of the malak (king) a chayal (band) of soldiers and horsemen to help us against the ayab (enemy) in the darak (way), because we had spoken to the malak (king), saying, "The yad (hand) of our Alahayam is on all those who seek him, for tawab (good); but his iz (power) and his ap (wrath) is against all those who forsake him.
So we fasted and begged our Alahayam for this: and he was entreated of us.
Then I set apart shanayam (twelve) of the shar (chiefs) of the kahan (priests), even Sharabayah, Chashabayah, and ishar (ten) of their ach (brothers) with them,

and weighed to them the kasap (silver), and the gold, and the vessels, even the tharawamah (offering) for the bayath (house) of our Alahayam, which the malak (king), and his yaitz (counselors), and his shar (princes), and all Yasharaal (Israel) there matzaa (present), had offered:
I weighed into their yad (hand) shash (six) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) talents of kasap (silver), and kasap (silver) vessels one maah (hundred) talents; of gold one maah (hundred) talents;
and isharayam (twenty) bowls of gold, of one alap (thousand) darics; and shanayam (two) vessels of tawab (fine) bright brass, precious as gold.

I said to them, "You are qadash (holy) to Yahawah, and the vessels are qadash (holy); and the kasap (silver) and the gold are a freewill nadabah (offering) to Yahawah, the Alahayam of your abawath (fathers).

Watch, and shamar (keep) them, until you weigh them panayam (before) the shar (chiefs) of the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites), and the shar (princes) of the abawath (fathers)' households of Yasharaal (Israel), at Yarawashalam, in the rooms of the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
So the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites) received the weight of the kasap (silver) and the gold, and the vessels, to bawaa (bring) them to Yarawashalam to the bayath (house) of our Alahayam.

Then we departed from the nahar (river) Ahawaa on the shanayam (twelfth) day of the raashawan (first) chadash (month), to yalak (go) to Yarawashalam: and the yad (hand) of our Alahayam was on us, and he delivered us from the kap (hand) of the ayab (enemy) and the bandit by the darak (way).
We came to Yarawashalam, and stayed there shalawash (three) yawam (days).

On the rabayaiy (fourth) yawam (day) the kasap (silver) and the gold and the vessels were weighed in the bayath (house) of our Alahayam into the yad (hand) of Maramawath the ban (son) of Awarayah the kahan (priest); and with him was Alaizar the ban (son) of Payanachas; and with them was Yawazabad the ban (son) of Yashawai, and Nawaidayah the ban (son) of Banaway, the Lawayay (Levite);
the whole by number and by weight: and all the weight was written at that ith (time).

The children of the captivity, who had bawaa (come) out Shabay exile, offered burnt ilah (offerings) to the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), shanayam (twelve) bulls for all Yasharaal (Israel), thashaiyam (ninety) - shash (six) ayal (rams), shabaiyam (seventy) - shabai (seven) lambs, and shanayam (twelve) male goats for a chataah (sin) offering: all this was a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah.

They delivered the malak (king's) dath (commissions) to the malak (king's) satraps, and to the governors ibar (beyond) the nahar (river): and they furthered the im (people) and the bayath (house) of Alahayam.

Now when these things were kalah (done), the shar (princes) drew near to me, saying, "The im (people) of Yasharaal (Israel), and the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites), have not separated themselves from the im (peoples) of the aratz (lands), following their thawaibah (abominations), even those of the Kanainay (Canaanites), the Chathay (Hittites), the Parazay (Perizzites), the Yabawasay (Jebusites), the Imawanay (Ammonites), the Mawaabay (Moabites), the Matzaray (Egyptians), and the Amaray (Amorites).

For they have taken of their bath (daughters) for themselves and for their ban (sons), so that the qadash (holy) zarai (seed) have mixed themselves with the im (peoples) of the aratz (lands). Yes, the yad (hand) of the shar (princes) and sagan (rulers) has been chief in this mail (trespass).
When I heard this thing, I tore my bagad (garment) and my bagad (robe), and plucked off the hair of my raash (head) and of my beard, and sat down confounded.

Then were assembled Charad me everyone who trembled at the dabar (words) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), because of their mail (trespass) of the captivity; and I sat confounded until the evening manachah (offering).

At the evening manachah (offering) I qawam (arose) up from my humiliation, even with my bagad (garment) and my bagad (robe) torn; and I fell on my knees, and spread out my kap (hands) to Yahawah my Alahayam;

and I said, "My Alahayam, I am bawash (ashamed) and kalam (blush) to lift up my panayam (face) to you, my Alahayam; for our iwan (iniquities) have increased over our raash (head), and our guiltiness has grown up to the shamayam (heavens).

Since the yawam (days) of our abawath (fathers) we have been gadawal (exceeding) guilty to this yawam (day); and for our iwan (iniquities) we, our malak (kings), and our kahan (priests), have been delivered into the yad (hand) of the malak (kings) of the aratz (lands), to the charab (sword), to Shabay, to plunder, and to bashath (confusion) of panayam (face), as it is this yawam (day).

Now for a Mait moment grace has been shown from Yahawah our Alahayam, to shaar (leave) us a palayatah (remnant) to escape, and to nathan (give) us a nail in his qadash (holy) place, that our Alahayam may lighten our iyan (eyes), and nathan (give) us a Mait machayah (reviving) in our bondage.

For we are ibad (bondservants); yet our Alahayam has not forsaken us in our bondage, but has extended loving chasad (kindness) to us in the panayam (sight) of the malak (kings) of Paras, to nathan (give) us a machayah (reviving), to set up the bayath (house) of our Alahayam, and to imad (repair) its ruins, and to nathan (give) us a wall in Yahawadah (Judah) and in Yarawashalam.
"Now, our Alahayam, what shall we amar (say) achar (after) this? For we have forsaken your matzawah (commandments),

which you have tzawah (commanded) by your ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets), saying, ‘The aratz (land), to which you bawaa (go) to yarash (possess) it, is an nadah (unclean) aratz (land) through the uncleanness of the im (peoples) of the aratz (lands), through their thawaibah (abominations), which have filled it from one pah (end) to another with their tamaah (filthiness).

Now therefore don't nathan (give) your bath (daughters) to their ban (sons), neither nashaa (take) their bath (daughters) to your ban (sons), nor seek their shalawam (peace) or their tawab (prosperity) iwalam (forever); that you may be chazaq (strong), and akal (eat) the tawab (good) of the aratz (land), and yarash (leave) it for an inheritance to your children iwalam (forever).'

"achar (after) all that has bawaa (come) on us for our rai (evil) maishah (deeds), and for our gadawal (great) guilt, since you, our Alahayam, have punished us less than our iwan (iniquities) deserve, and have given us such a palayatah (remnant),

shall we again parar (break) your matzawah (commandments), and chathan (join) in affinity with the im (peoples) that do these thawaibah (abominations)? Wouldn't you be angry with us until you had consumed us, so that there should be no shaarayath (remnant), nor any to palayatah (escape)?

Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), you are tzadayaq (righteous); for we are left a shaar (remnant) that has palayatah (escaped), as it is this yawam (day). Behold, we are panayam (before) you in our guiltiness; for none can imad (stand) panayam (before) you because of this.

Now while Izaraa prayed and made yadah (confession), weeping and casting himself down panayam (before) the bayath (house) of Alahayam, there was gathered together to him out of Yasharaal (Israel) a very rab (great) qahal (assembly) of men and women and children; for the anawash (people) wept very bitterly.

Shakanayah the ban (son) of Yachayaal, one of the ban (sons) of Iyalam, answered Izaraa, "We have trespassed against our Alahayam, and have married foreign women of the im (peoples) of the aratz (land). Yet now there is Maqawah for Yasharaal (Israel) concerning this thing.

Now therefore let us karath (make) a barayath (covenant) with our Alahayam to yatzaa (put) away all the wives, and such as are yalad (born) of them, according to the itzah (counsel) of my Adanay, and Charad those who tremble at the matzawah (commandment) of our Alahayam. Let it be done according to the thawarah (law).
qawam (arise); for the dabar (matter) belongs to you, and we are with you. Be courageous, and do it.

Then Izaraa qawam (arose), and made the shar (chiefs) of the kahan (priests), the Lawayay (Levites), and all Yasharaal (Israel), to shabai (swear) that they would do according to this dabar (word). So they swore.

Then Izaraa rose up from panayam (before) the bayath (house) of Alahayam, and went into the room of Yahawachanan the ban (son) of Alayashayab: and when he came there, he ate no lacham (bread), nor drank mayam (water); for he mourned because of their mail (trespass) of the captivity.
They made ibar (proclamation) throughout Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam to all the children of the captivity, that they should gather themselves together to Yarawashalam;

and that whoever didn't bawaa (come) within shalawash (three) yawam (days), according to the itzah (counsel) of the shar (princes) and the zaqan (elders), all his rakawash (substance) should be forfeited, and himself separated from the qahal (assembly) of the captivity.

Then all the men of Yahawadah (Judah) and Banayamayan gathered themselves together to Yarawashalam within the shalawash (three) yawam (days); it was the thashayaiy (ninth) chadash (month), on the isharayam (twentieth) day of the chadash (month): and all the im (people) sat in the broad place before the bayath (house) of Alahayam, trembling dabar (because) of this matter, and for the great rain.
Izaraa the kahan (priest) stood up, and said to them, "You have trespassed, and have married foreign women, to increase the guilt of Yasharaal (Israel).

Now therefore nathan (make) thawadah (confession) to Yahawah, the Alahayam of your abawath (fathers), and do his pleasure; and separate yourselves from the im (peoples) of the aratz (land), and from the foreign women.
Then all the qahal (assembly) answered with a gadawal (loud) qawal (voice), "As you have said concerning us, so must we do.

But the im (people) are many, and it is a ith (time) of much rain, and we are not kach (able) to imad (stand) outside; neither is this a malaakah (work) of one yawam (day) or shanayam (two); for we have greatly transgressed in this dabar (matter).

Let now our shar (princes) be appointed for all the qahal (assembly), and let all those who are in our Iyar who have married foreign women bawaa (come) at appointed ith (times), and with them the zaqan (elders) of every Iyar, and its shapat (judges), until the charawan (fierce) ap (wrath) of our Alahayam be turned from us, until this dabar (matter) is resolved.
Only Yawanathan the ban (son) of Ishahaal and Yachazayah the ban (son) of Thaqawah stood up against this; and Mashalam and Shabathay the Lawayay (Levite) helped them.

The children of the captivity did so. Izaraa the kahan (priest), with anawash (certain) raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households, after their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), and all of them by their sham (names), were set apart; and they sat down in the achad (first) yawam (day) of the ishayaray (tenth) chadash (month) to examine the dabar (matter).
They made an kalah (end) with all the men who had married foreign women by the achad (first) yawam (day) of the achad (first) chadash (month).

Among the ban (sons) of the kahan (priests) there were found who had married foreign women: of the ban (sons) of Yashawai, the ban (son) of Yawatzadaq, and his ach (brothers), Maishayah, and Alayaizar, and Yarayab, and Gadalayah.
They gave their yad (hand) that they would yatzaa (put) away their wives; and being Asham, they offered a ayal (ram) of the flock for their guilt.
Of the ban (sons) of Amar: Chananay and Zabadayah.
Of the ban (sons) of Charam: Maishayah, and Alayah, and Shamaiyah, and Yachayaal, and Izayah.
Of the ban (sons) Pashachawar Pashhur: Alayahawaiyanay, Maishayah, Yashamaial, Nathanaal, Yawazabad, and Alaishah.
Lawayay the Levites: Yawazabad, and Shamaiy, and Qalayah (the same is Qalayataa), Pathachayah, Yahawadah (Judah), and Alayaizar.
Of the singers: Alayashayab. Of the porters: Shalawam, and Talam, and Awaray.
Of Yasharaal (Israel): Of the ban (sons) of Paraish: Ramayah, and Yazayah, and Malakayah, and Mayaman, and Alaizar, and Malakayah, and Banayah.
Of the ban (sons) of Iyalam: Mathanayah, Zakarayah, and Yachayaal, and Ibaday, and Yarayamawath, and Alayah.
Of the ban (sons) of Zathawaa: Alayahawaiyanay, Alayashayab, Mathanayah, and Yarayamawath, and Zabad, and Izayazaa.
Of the ban (sons) of Babay: Yahawachanan, Chananayah, Zakay, Ithalay.
Of the ban (sons) of Banay: Mashalam, Malawak, and Idayah, Yashawab, and Shaal, Ramathagalaid.
Of the ban (sons) of Pachathamawaab: Idanaa, and Kalal, Banayah, Maishayah, Mathanayah, Batzalaal, and Banaway, and Manashah.
Of the ban (sons) of Charam: Alayaizar, Yashayah, Malakayah, Shamaiyah, Shamaiwan,
Banayamayan, Malawak, Shamarayah.
Of the ban (sons) of Chasham: Mathanay, Mathathah, Zabad, Alayapalat, Yaramay, Manashah, Shamaiy.
Of the ban (sons) of Banay: Maiday, Imaram, and Awaal,
Banayah, Badayah, Kalawahay,
Wanayah, Maramawath, Alayashayab,
Mathanayah, Mathanay, and Yaishaw,
and Banay, and Banaway, Shamaiy,
and Shalamayah, and Nathan, and Idayah,
Makanadabay, Shashay, Sharay,
Izaraal, and Shalamayah, Shamarayah,
Shalawam, Amarayah, Yawasap.
Of the ban (sons) of Nabaw: Yaiyaal, Mathathayah, Zabad, Zabayanaa, Yadaw, and Yawaal, Banayah.
All these had taken foreign wives; and some of them had wives by whom they had children.
The dabar (words) of Nachamayah the ban (son) Chakalayah Hacaliah. Now it happened in the chadash (month) Kasalaw, in the isharayam (twentieth) Shanah, as I was in Shawashan the palace,

that Chananay, one of my ach (brothers), came, he and anawash (certain) men out of Yahawadah (Judah); and I asked them concerning the Yahawaday (Jews) who had palayatah (escaped), who were shaar (left) of the Shabay, and concerning Yarawashalam.

They said to me, "The shaar (remnant) who are shaar (left) of the Shabay there in the province are in gadawal (great) rai (affliction) and reproach. The wall of Yarawashalam also is broken down, and its gates are burned with ash (fire).
It happened, when I heard these dabar (words), that I sat down and wept, and mourned certain yawam (days); and I fasted and prayed panayam (before) the Alahayam of shamayam (heaven),

and said, "I beg you, Yahawah, the Alahayam of shamayam (heaven), the gadawal (great) and awesome Al, who shamar (keeps) barayath (covenant) and loving chasad (kindness) with those who ahab (love) him and shamar (keep) his matzawah (commandments):

Let your ear now be Qashab, and your iyan (eyes) pathach (open), that you may listen to the prayer of your ibad (servant), which I palal (pray) panayam (before) you at this yawam (time), yawamam (day) and layal (night), for the children of Yasharaal (Israel) your ibad (servants) while I yadah (confess) the chataah (sins) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), which we have sinned against you. Yes, I and my ab (father's) bayath (house) have sinned.

We have dealt very chabal (corruptly) against you, and have not kept the matzawah (commandments), nor the chaq (statutes), nor the mashapat (ordinances), which you tzawah (commanded) your ibad (servant) Mashah.
"zakar (remember), I beg you, the dabar (word) that you tzawah (commanded) your ibad (servant) Mashah, saying, ‘If you trespass, I will scatter you abroad among the im (peoples);

but if you shawab (turn back / repent) to me, and shamar (keep) my matzawah (commandments) and do them, though your outcasts were in the uttermost part of the shamayam (heavens), yet will I gather them from there, and will bawaa (bring) them to the place that I have chosen, to cause my sham (name) to shakan (dwell) there.'
"Now these are your ibad (servants) and your im (people), whom you have padah (redeemed) by your gadawal (great) kach (power), and by your chazaq (strong) yad (hand).

Adanay, I beg you, let your ear be Qashab now to the prayer of your ibad (servant), and to the prayer of your ibad (servants), who Chapatz to yaraa (fear) your sham (name); and please tzalach (prosper) your ibad (servant) this yawam (day), and nathan (grant) him racham (mercy) in the panayam (sight) of this ayash (man)." Now I was cup bearer to the malak (king).

It happened in the chadash (month) Nayasan, in the isharayam (twentieth) Shanah Arathachashashathaa Artaxerxes the malak (king), when yayan (wine) was panayam (before) him, that I took up the yayan (wine), and gave it to the malak (king). Now I had not been rai (sad) panayam (before) in his presence.
The malak (king) said to me, "Why is your panayam (face) rai (sad), since you are not chalah (sick)? This is nothing else but rai (sorrow) of lab (heart)." Then I was very much yaraa (afraid).

I said to the malak (king), "Let the malak (king) chayah (live) iwalam (forever)! Why shouldn't my panayam (face) be sad, when the Iyar, the bayath (place) of my abawath (fathers)' tombs, lies Charab, and its gates have been consumed with ash (fire)?
Then the malak (king) said to me, "For what do you make request?" So I prayed to the Alahayam of shamayam (heaven).

I said to the malak (king), "If it tawab (pleases) the malak (king), and if your ibad (servant) has found favor in your panayam (sight), that you would shalach (send) me to Yahawadah (Judah), to the Iyar of my abawath (fathers)' tombs, that I may banah (build) it.

The malak (king) said to me (the shagal (queen) was also sitting by him), "For how long shall your journey be? And when will you shawab (turn back / repent)?" So it pleased the malak (king) to shalach (send) me; and I nathan (set) him a time.

Moreover I said to the malak (king), "If it tawab (pleases) the malak (king), let letters be given me to the governors ibar (beyond) the nahar (river), that they may let me ibar (pass) through until I bawaa (come) to Yahawadah (Judah);

and a letter to Asap the keeper of the malak (king's) forest, that he may nathan (give) me itz (timber) to make qarah (beams) for the gates of the citadel by the bayath (temple), for the wall of the Iyar, and for the bayath (house) that I shall bawaa (enter) into." The malak (king) granted my requests, because of the tawab (good) yad (hand) of my Alahayam on me.
Then I came to the governors ibar (beyond) the nahar (river), and gave them the malak (king's) letters. Now the malak (king) had sent with me shar (captains) of the chayal (army) and horsemen.

When Sanabalat the Charanay, and Tawabayah the ibad (servant), the Imawanay (Ammonite), heard of it, it grieved them rai (exceedingly), because a adam (man) had bawaa (come) to seek the tawab (welfare) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel).
So I came to Yarawashalam, and was there shalawash (three) yawam (days).

I qawam (arose) in the layal (night), I and Mait Mait men with me; neither told I any anawash (man) what my Alahayam nathan (put) into my lab (heart) to do for Yarawashalam; neither was there any animal with me, except the animal that I rode on.

I went out by layal (night) by the Gayaa gate, even panayam (toward) the jackal's iyan (well), and to the dung gate, and viewed the walls of Yarawashalam, which were broken down, and its gates were consumed with ash (fire).
Then I went on to the spring gate and to the malak (king's) pool: but there was no place for the animal that was under me to ibar (pass).
Then went I up in the layal (night) by the nachal (brook), and viewed the wall; and I turned shawab (turn back / repent), and entered by the Gayaa gate, and so returned.

The sagan (rulers) didn't yadai (know) where I went, or what I did; Kan had I as yet told it to the Yahawaday (Jews), nor to the kahan (priests), nor to the nobles, nor to the sagan (rulers), nor to the yathar (rest) who did the malaakah (work).

Then I said to them, "You raah (see) the rai (evil) case that we are in, how Yarawashalam lies Charab, and its gates are burned with ash (fire). yalak (come), let us banah (build) up the wall of Yarawashalam, that we won't be disgraced.

I told them of the yad (hand) of my Alahayam which was tawab (good) on me, as also of the malak (king's) dabar (words) that he had spoken to me. They said, "Let's qawam (rise) up and banah (build)." So they strengthened their yad (hands) for the tawab (good) work.

But when Sanabalat the Charanay, and Tawabayah the ibad (servant), the Imawanay (Ammonite), and Gasham the Irabay (Arabian), heard it, they ridiculed us, and despised us, and said, "dabar (what) is this thing that you are doing? Will you rebel against the malak (king)?

Then answered I them, and said to them, "The Alahayam of shamayam (heaven) will tzalach (prosper) us. Therefore we, his ibad (servants), will qawam (arise) and banah (build); but you have no chalaq (portion), nor tzadaqah (right), nor zakarawan (memorial), in Yarawashalam.

Then Alayashayab the gadawal (high) kahan (priest) rose up with his ach (brothers) the kahan (priests), and they built the sheep gate; they sanctified it, and imad (set) up its doors; even to the magadal (tower) Maah Hammeah they sanctified it, to the magadal (tower) Chananaal Hananel.
Next to him built the men of Yarayachaw. Next to them built Zakawar the ban (son) of Amaray.
The ban (sons) of Sanaah built the fish gate. They laid its qarah (beams), and imad (set) up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.

Next to them, Maramawath the ban (son) of Awarayah, the ban (son) of Qawatz made chazaq (repairs). Next to them, Mashalam the ban (son) of Barakayah, the ban (son) Mashayazabaal Meshezabel made chazaq (repairs). Next to them, Tzadawaq the ban (son) of Bainaa made chazaq (repairs).
Next to them, the Thaqawaiy (Tekoites) made chazaq (repairs); but their adayar (nobles) didn't bawaa (put) their necks to the ibadah (work) of their Adawan.
Yawayadai the ban (son) of Pasach and Mashalam the ban (son) of Basawadayah repaired the Yashan gate. They laid its qarah (beams), and imad (set) up its doors, and its bolts, and its bars.
Next to them, Malatayah the Gabainay (Gibeonite), and Yadawan the Maranathay, the men of Gabaiwan, and Matzapah Mizpah, repaired the residence of the governor ibar (beyond) the nahar (river).

Next to him, Izayaal the ban (son) of Charahayah, goldsmiths, made chazaq (repairs). Next to him, Chananayah one of the perfumers made chazaq (repairs), and they fortified Yarawashalam even to the Rachab wall.
Next to them, Rapayah the ban (son) of Chawar, the shar (ruler) of chatzay (half) the district of Yarawashalam, made chazaq (repairs).
Next to them, Yadayah the ban (son) of Charawamap made chazaq (repairs) across from his bayath (house). Next to him, Chatawash the ban (son) Chashabanayah Hashabneiah made chazaq (repairs).
Malakayah the ban (son) of Charam, and Chashawab the ban (son) of Pachathamawaab, repaired shanay (another) portion, and the magadal (tower) of the furnaces.
Next to him, Shalawam the ban (son) of Lawachash, the shar (ruler) of chatzay (half) the district of Yarawashalam, he and his bath (daughters), made chazaq (repairs).

Chanawan and the yashab (inhabitants) of Zanawach repaired the Gayaa gate. They built it, and imad (set) up its doors, its bolts, and its bars, and one alap (thousand) amah (cubits) of the wall to the dung gate.
Malakayah the ban (son) of Rakab, the shar (ruler) of the district of Bayathahakaram Haccherem repaired the dung gate. He built it, and imad (set) up its doors, its bolts, and its bars.

Shalawan the ban (son) of Kalachazah, the shar (ruler) of the district Matzapah Mizpah repaired the spring gate. He built it, and covered it, and imad (set) up its doors, its bolts, and its bars, and the wall of the pool Shalach Shelah by the malak (king's) Gan, even to the stairs that yarad (go) down from the Iyar of Dawad.

achar (after) him, Nachamayah the ban (son) of Izabawaq, the shar (ruler) of chatzay (half) the district of Bayathatzawar Zur, made chazaq (repairs) to the qabar (place) opposite the tombs of Dawad, and to the pool that was made, and to the bayath (house) of the gabawar (mighty) men.

achar (after) him, the Lawayay (Levites), Rachawam the ban (son) of Banay made chazaq (repairs). Next to him, Chashabayah, the shar (ruler) of chatzay (half) the district of Qaiyalah, made chazaq (repairs) for his district.
achar (after) him, their ach (brothers), Baway the ban (son) of Chanadad, the shar (ruler) of chatzay (half) the district of Qaiyalah made chazaq (repairs).
Next to him, Izar the ban (son) of Yashawai, the shar (ruler) Matzapah Mizpah, repaired shanay (another) portion, across from the ascent to the armory at the turning of the wall.

achar (after) him, Barawak the ban (son) of Zabay charah (earnestly) repaired shanay (another) portion, from the turning of the wall to the door of the bayath (house) of Alayashayab the gadawal (high) kahan (priest).

achar (after) him, Maramawath the ban (son) of Awarayah the ban (son) of Qawatz repaired shanay (another) portion, from the door of the bayath (house) of Alayashayab even to the end of the bayath (house) of Alayashayab.
achar (after) him, the kahan (priests), the men of the Plain made chazaq (repairs).

achar (after) them, Banayamayan and Chashawab made chazaq (repairs) across from their bayath (house). achar (after) them, Izarayah the ban (son) of Maishayah the ban (son) of Inanayah made chazaq (repairs) beside his own bayath (house).
achar (after) him, Banaway the ban (son) of Chanadad repaired shanay (another) portion, from the bayath (house) of Izarayah to the turning of the wall, and to the corner.

Palal the ban (son) of Awazay made repairs opposite the turning of the wall, and the magadal (tower) that yatzaa (stands) out from the Ilayawan bayath (house) of the malak (king), which is by the court of the guard. achar (after) him Padayah the ban (son) of Paraish made repairs.
(Now the Nethinim lived in Ipal, to the place over against the mayam (water) gate toward the east, and the magadal (tower) that yatzaa (stands) out.)
achar (after) him the Thaqawaiy (Tekoites) repaired shanay (another) portion, over against the gadawal (great) magadal (tower) that yatzaa (stands) out, and to the wall of Ipal.
Above the horse gate, the kahan (priests) made chazaq (repairs), everyone across from his own bayath (house).

achar (after) them, Tzadawaq the ban (son) of Amar made chazaq (repairs) across from his own bayath (house). achar (after) him, Shamaiyah the ban (son) of Shakanayah, the keeper of the east gate made chazaq (repairs).

achar (after) him, Chananayah the ban (son) of Shalamayah, and Chanawan the shashay (sixth) ban (son) of Tzalap, repaired shanay (another) portion. achar (after) him, Mashalam the ban (son) of Barakayah made chazaq (repairs) across from his room.

achar (after) him, Malakayah one of the goldsmiths to the bayath (house) of the Nethinim, and of the merchants, made chazaq (repairs) over against the gate of Hammiphkad, and to the ascent of the corner.
Between the ascent of the corner and the sheep gate, the goldsmiths and the merchants made chazaq (repairs).
But it happened that when Sanabalat heard that we were building the wall, he was charah (angry), and took great kais (indignation), and mocked the Yahawaday (Jews).

He spoke panayam (before) his ach (brothers) and the chayal (army) of Shamarawan, and said, "What are these Amalal Yahawaday (Jews) doing? Will they fortify themselves? Will they zabach (sacrifice)? Will they kalah (finish) in a yawam (day)? Will they chayah (revive) the aban (stones) out of the heaps of ipar (rubbish), since they are burned?
Now Tawabayah the Imawanay (Ammonite) was by him, and he said, "What they are building, if a fox climbed up it, he would break down their aban (stone) wall.
"Hear, our Alahayam; for we are despised; and shawab (turn back / repent) back their reproach on their own raash (head), nathan (give) them up for a spoil in a aratz (land) of captivity;
don't cover their iwan (iniquity), and don't let their chataah (sin) be blotted out from panayam (before) you; for they have insulted the banah (builders).
So we built the wall; and all the wall was joined qashar (together) to chatzay (half) its height: for the im (people) had a lab (mind) to ishah (work).

But it happened that when Sanabalat, Tawabayah, the Irabay (Arabians), the Imawanay (Ammonites), and the Ashadawaday heard that the repairing of the walls of Yarawashalam went forward, and that the breaches began to be filled, then they were very charah (angry);
and they conspired all of them together to bawaa (come) and fight against Yarawashalam, and to cause confusion therein.
But we made our prayer to our Alahayam, and imad (set) a watch against them yawamam (day) and layal (night), panayam (because) of them.
Yahawadah (Judah) said, "The kach (strength) of the bearers of burdens is fading, and there is much ipar (rubbish); so that we are not yakal (able) to banah (build) the wall.
Our tzar (adversaries) said, "They shall not yadai (know), neither raah (see), until we bawaa (come) into their midst, and harag (kill) them, and cause the malaakah (work) to shabath (cease).
It happened that when the Yahawaday (Jews) who lived by them came, they said to us ishar (ten) paim (times) from all places, "Wherever you shawab (turn back / repent), they will attack us.

Therefore imad (set) I Thachathay the lowest parts of the space achar (behind) the wall, in the open places, I imad (set) the im (people) after their mashapachah (families) with their charab (swords), their spears, and their qashath (bows).

I looked, and rose up, and said to the nobles, and to the sagan (rulers), and to the yathar (rest) of the im (people), "Don't be yaraa (afraid) of them! zakar (remember) the Adanay, who is gadawal (great) and awesome, and fight for your ach (brothers), your ban (sons), and your bath (daughters), your wives, and your bayath (houses).

It happened, when our ayab (enemies) heard that it was yadai (known) to us, and Alahayam had brought their itzah (counsel) to nothing, that we returned all of us to the wall, everyone to his malaakah (work).

It happened from that yawam (time) forth, that chatzay (half) of my nair (servants) worked in the malaakah (work), and chatzay (half) of them held the spears, the magan (shields), and the qashath (bows), and the coats of mail; and the shar (rulers) were achar (behind) all the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah).
They all built the wall and those who bore burdens loaded themselves; everyone with one of his yad (hands) worked in the malaakah (work), and with the other held his shalach (weapon);
and the banah (builders), everyone wore his charab (sword) at his side, and so built. He who sounded the trumpet was by me.

I said to the nobles, and to the sagan (rulers) and to the yathar (rest) of the im (people), "The malaakah (work) is great and large, and we are separated on the wall, one Rachawaq from ach (another).
Wherever you hear the qawal (sound) of the trumpet, rally there to us. Our Alahayam will fight for us.
So we worked in the malaakah (work): and chatzay (half) of them held the spears from the rising of the shachar (morning) until the kawakab (stars) appeared.

Likewise at the same ith (time) said I to the im (people), "Let everyone with his nair (servant) lawan (lodge) within Yarawashalam, that in the layal (night) they may be a guard to us, and may labor in the yawam (day).
So neither I, nor my ach (brothers), nor my nair (servants), nor the men of the guard who followed me, none of us took off our clothes. Everyone took his shalach (weapon) to the mayam (water).
Then there arose a gadawal (great) cry of the im (people) and of their wives against their ach (brothers) the Yahawaday (Jews).
For there were that said, "We, our ban (sons) and our bath (daughters), are many. Let us get grain, that we may akal (eat) and chayah (live).
Some also there were that said, "We are mortgaging our shadah (fields), and our vineyards, and our bayath (houses). Let us get grain, because of the famine.
There were also some who said, "We have borrowed kasap (money) for the malak (king's) tribute using our shadah (fields) and our vineyards as collateral.

Yet now our flesh is as the flesh of our ach (brothers), our children as their children. Behold, we bring into bondage our ban (sons) and our bath (daughters) to be ibad (servants), and some of our bath (daughters) have been brought into bondage. Neither is it in our al (power) to help it; for other men have our shadah (fields) and our vineyards.
I was very charah (angry) when I heard their cry and these dabar (words).

Then I consulted with myself, and contended with the nobles and the sagan (rulers), and said to them, "You exact usury, everyone of his ach (brother)." I held a gadawal (great) qahalah (assembly) against them.

I said to them, "We, after our ability, have redeemed our ach (brothers) the Yahawaday (Jews) that were sold to the gawayam (nations); and would you even sell your ach (brothers), and should they be sold to us?" Then they held their charash (peace), and found never a dabar (word).
Also I said, "The thing that you do is not tawab (good). Ought you not to yalak (walk) in the yaraah (fear) of our Alahayam, because of the reproach of the gawayam (nations) our ayab (enemies)?
I likewise, my ach (brothers) and my nair (servants), lend them kasap (money) and grain. Please let us stop this usury.

Please shawab (turn back / repent) to them, even this yawam (day), their shadah (fields), their vineyards, their olive groves, and their bayath (houses), also the hundredth part of the kasap (money), and of the grain, the new thayarawash (wine), and the yatzahar (oil), that you are charging them.

Then they said, "We will shawab (turn back / repent) them, and will require nothing of them; so will we do, even as you amar (say)." Then I called the kahan (priests), and took an shabai (oath) of them, that they would do according to this dabar (promise).

Also I shook out my lap, and said, "So may Alahayam shake out every ayash (man) from his bayath (house), and from his yagayai (labor), that doesn't qawam (perform) this dabar (promise); even thus be he shaken out, and rayaq (emptied)." All the qahal (assembly) said, "aman (amen)," and praised Yahawah. The im (people) did according to this dabar (promise).

Moreover from the yawam (time) that I was appointed to be their governor in the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah), from the isharayam (twentieth) Shanah even to the shanayam (two) and shalawashayam (thirtieth) Shanah Arathachashashathaa Artaxerxes the malak (king), that is, shanayam (twelve) Shanah, I and my ach (brothers) have not eaten the lacham (bread) of the governor.

But the raashawan (former) governors who were panayam (before) me were supported by the im (people), and took lacham (bread) and yayan (wine) from them, achar (besides) arabaiyam (forty) shekels of kasap (silver); yes, even their nair (servants) ruled over the im (people): but I didn't do so, panayam (because) of the yaraah (fear) of Alahayam.
Yes, also I continued in the malaakah (work) of this wall, neither bought we any shadah (land): and all my nair (servants) were gathered there to the malaakah (work).

Moreover there were at my table, of the Yahawaday (Jews) and the sagan (rulers), one maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) men, besides those who came to us from among the gawayam (nations) that were around us.

Now that which was prepared for one yawam (day) was one ox and shash (six) Barar sheep; also fowls were prepared for me, and once in ishar (ten) yawam (days) store of all sorts of yayan (wine): yet for all this I didn't demand the lacham (bread) of the governor, because the ibadah (bondage) was kabad (heavy) on this im (people).
zakar (remember) to me, my Alahayam, for tawab (good), all that I have done for this im (people).

Now it happened, when it was reported to Sanabalat and Tawabayah, and to Gasham the Irabay (Arabian), and to the yathar (rest) of our ayab (enemies), that I had built the wall, and that there was no breach yathar (left) therein; (though even to that ith (time) I had not imad (set) up the doors in the gates;)
that Sanabalat and Gasham sent to me, saying, "yalak (come), let us meet together in the kapayar (villages) in the Baqaih of Awanaw." But they intended to rai (harm) me.

I sent malaak (messengers) to them, saying, "I am doing a gadawal (great) malaakah (work), so that I can't yarad (come) down. Why should the malaakah (work) shabath (cease), while I rapah (leave) it, and yarad (come) down to you?
They sent to me arabai (four) paim (times) after this sort; and I answered them the same way.
Then Sanabalat sent his nair (servant) to me the same way the chamayashay (fifth) paim (time) with an pathach (open) letter in his yad (hand),

in which was written, "It is reported among the gawayam (nations), and Gasham amar (says) it, that you and the Yahawaday (Jews) intend to rebel. Because of that, you are building the wall. You would be their malak (king), according to these dabar (words).

You have also appointed nabayaa (prophets) to qaraa (preach) of you at Yarawashalam, saying, ‘There is a malak (king) in Yahawadah (Judah)!' Now it will be reported to the malak (king) according to these dabar (words). yalak (come) now therefore, and let us take yaitz (counsel) together.
Then I sent to him, saying, "There are no such things done as you amar (say), but you imagine them out of your own lab (heart).
For they all would have made us yaraa (afraid), saying, "Their yad (hands) will be weakened from the malaakah (work), that it not be done. But now, chazaq (strengthen) my yad (hands).

I went to the bayath (house) of Shamaiyah the ban (son) of Dalayah the ban (son) of Mahayatabaal, who was itzar (shut) in at his home; and he said, "Let us meet together in the bayath (house) of Alahayam, within the hayakal (temple), and let us shut the doors of the hayakal (temple); for they will bawaa (come) to harag (kill) you; yes, in the layal (night) will they bawaa (come) to harag (kill) you.
I said, "Should such a ayash (man) as I flee? Who is there that, being such as I, would bawaa (go) into the hayakal (temple) to chayay (save) his life? I will not bawaa (go) in.
I discerned, and behold, Alahayam had not sent him; but he pronounced this nabawaah (prophecy) against me. Tawabayah and Sanabalat had hired him.
He hired so that I would be yaraa (afraid), do so, and chataa (sin), and that they might have material for an rai (evil) sham (report), that they might reproach me.

"zakar (remember), my Alahayam, Tawabayah and Sanabalat according to these their maishah (works), and also the prophetess Nawaidayah, and the yathar (rest) of the nabayaa (prophets), that would have put me in yaraa (fear).
So the wall was finished in the isharayam (twenty) - chamash (fifth) day of Alawal, in chamashayam (fifty) - shanayam (two) yawam (days).

It happened, when all our ayab (enemies) heard of it, that all the gawayam (nations) that were about us were afraid, and were much napal (cast) down in their own iyan (eyes); for they perceived that this malaakah (work) was worked of our Alahayam.
Moreover in those yawam (days) the nobles of Yahawadah (Judah) sent many letters to Tawabayah, and Tawabayah letters came to them.

For there were many in Yahawadah (Judah) bail (sworn) to him, because he was the son-in-law of Shakanayah the ban (son) of Arach; and his ban (son) Yahawachanan had taken the bath (daughter) of Mashalam the ban (son) of Barakayah as wife.
Also they spoke of his tawab (good) deeds panayam (before) me, and reported my dabar (words) to him. Tawabayah sent letters to put me in yaraa (fear).
Now it happened, when the wall was built, and I had imad (set) up the doors, and the porters and the singers and the Lawayay (Levites) were appointed,
that I put my ach (brother) Chananay, and Chananayah the shar (governor) of the castle, in tzawah (charge) of Yarawashalam; for he was a amath (faithful) ayash (man), and feared Alahayam above many.

I said to them, "Don't let the gates of Yarawashalam be opened until the shamash (sun) is hot; and while they imad (stand) guard, let them shut the doors, and you achaz (bar) them: and imad (appoint) watches of the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, everyone in his watch, with everyone near his bayath (house).
Now the Iyar was Rachab and Rachab; but the im (people) were Mait therein, and the bayath (houses) were not built.

My Alahayam nathan (put) into my lab (heart) to gather together the nobles, and the sagan (rulers), and the im (people), that they might be reckoned by genealogy. I found the book of the genealogy of those who came up at the raashawan (first), and I found written therein:

These are the children of the province, who went up out of the Shabay of those who had been carried away, whom Nabawakadanaatzar the malak (king) of Babal had carried away, and who returned to Yarawashalam and to Yahawadah (Judah), everyone to his Iyar;

who came with Zarababal, Yashawai, Nachamayah, Izarayah, Raimayah, Nachamanay, Maradakay, Balashan, Masaparath, Bagaway, Nachawam, Bainah. The number of the men of the anawash (people) of Yasharaal (Israel):
The children of Paraish, shanayam (two) alap (thousand) one maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) - shanayam (two).
The children of Shapatayah, shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) - shanayam (two).
The children of Arach, shash (six) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) - shanayam (two).
The children of Pachathamawaab, of the children of Yashawai and Yawaab, two alap (thousand) shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) eighteen.
The children of Iyalam, one alap (thousand) two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) - arabai (four).
The children of Zathawaa, shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five).
The children of Zakay, shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty).
The children of Banaway, shash (six) maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - shamanah (eight).
The children of Babay, shash (six) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shamanah (eight).
The children of Izagad, shanayam (two) alap (thousand) shalawash (three) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two).
The children of Adanayaqam, shash (six) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty) - shabai (seven).
The children of Bagaway, two alap (thousand) shashayam (sixty) - shabai (seven).
The children of Idayan, shash (six) maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) - chamash (five).
The children of Atar, of Chazaqayah, thashaiyam (ninety) - shamanah (eight).
The children of Chasham, shalawash (three) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shamanah (eight).
The children of Batzay, shalawash (three) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - arabai (four).
The children of Charayap, one maah (hundred) shanayam (twelve).
The children of Gabaiwan, thashaiyam (ninety) - chamash (five).
The men of Bayathalacham and Natapah, one maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty) - shamanah (eight).
The men of Inathawath, one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shamanah (eight).
The men of Beth Azmaveth, arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two).
The men of Kiriath Qarayathayairayam, Kapayarah, and Baarawath, shabai (seven) maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - shalawash (three).
The men of Ramah and Gabai, shash (six) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - one.
The men of Makamas, one maah (hundred) and isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two).
The men of Bayathaal and Iy, a maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three).
The men of the other Nabaw, chamashayam (fifty) - shanayam (two).
The children of the other Iyalam, one alap (thousand) two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty) - arabai (four).
The children of Charam, shalawash (three) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty).
The children of Yarayachaw, shalawash (three) maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five).
The children of Lad, Chadayad, and Awanaw, shabai (seven) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - one.
The children of Sanaah, shalawash (three) alap (thousand) thashai (nine) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty).
The kahan (priests): The children of Yadaiyah, of the bayath (house) of Yashawai, thashai (nine) maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) - shalawash (three).
The children of Amar, one alap (thousand) chamashayam (fifty) - shanayam (two).
The children Pashachawar Pashhur, one alap (thousand) two maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - shabai (seven).
The children of Charam, one alap (thousand) seventeen.
The Lawayay (Levites): the children of Yashawai, of Qadamayaal, of the children of Hawadawah, shabaiyam (seventy) - arabai (four).
The singers: the children of Asap, one maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - shamanah (eight).

The porters: the children of Shalawam, the children of Atar, the children of Talamawan, the children of Iqawab, the children of Chatayataa, the children of Shabay, one maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - shamanah (eight).
The Nethinim: the children of Tzayachaa, the children of Chashawapaa, the children Tabaiwath Tabbaoth,
the children of Qayaras, the children of Sayaia, the children of Padawan,
the children of Labanaa, the children of Chagabaa, the children Shalamay Salmai,
the children Chanan Hanan, the children of Gadal, the children of Gachar,
the children of Raayah, the children of Ratzayan, the children of Naqawadaa,
the children of Gazam, the children of Izaa, the children of Pasach.
The children of Basay, the children of Maiwanay, the children Napawashasayam Nephushesim,
the children of Baqabawaq, the children of Chaqawapaa, the children of Charachawar,
the children of Batzalawath, the children of Machayadaa, the children of Charashaa,
the children of Baraqawas, the children of Sayasaraa, the children Thamach Temah,
the children of Natzayach, the children of Chatayapaa.
The children of Shalamah ibad (servants): the children of Sawatay, the children of Saparath, the children of Parawadaa,
the children of Yailaa, the children of Daraqawan, the children of Gadal,
the children of Shapatayah, the children of Chatayal, the children of Pakarathatzabayayam Hazzebaim, the children of Amawan.
All the Nethinim, and the children of Shalamah ibad (servants), were shalawash (three) maah (hundred) thashaiyam (ninety) - shanayam (two).

These were those who went up from Thalamalach Melah, Thalacharashaa Harsha, karawab (cherub), Adawan, and Amar; but they could not show their abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), nor their zarai (seed), whether they were of Yasharaal (Israel):
The children of Dalayah, the children of Tawabayah, the children of Naqawadaa, shash (six) maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two).

Of the kahan (priests): the children Chabayah Hobaiah, the children of Qawatz, the children of Barazalay, who took a ashah (wife) of the bath (daughters) of Barazalay the Galaiday (Gileadite), and was called after their sham (name).
These searched for their geneological records, but couldn't matzaa (find) them. Therefore were they deemed polluted and put from the kahanah (priesthood).
The governor said to them, that they should not akal (eat) of the most qadash (holy) things, until there stood up a kahan (priest) with awarayam (urim) and thamayam (thummim).
The whole qahal (assembly) achad (together) was forty - two alap (thousand) shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty),

besides their male amah (servants) and their female amah (servants), of whom there were shabai (seven) alap (thousand) shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - shabai (seven): and they had two maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five) singing men and singing women.
Their horses were shabai (seven) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - shash (six); their mules, two maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five);
their camels, arabai (four) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - chamash (five); their donkeys, shash (six) alap (thousand) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty).

Some from among the raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households gave to the malaakah (work). The governor gave to the treasury one alap (thousand) darics of gold, chamashayam (fifty) basins, and chamash (five) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) kahan (priests)' garments.

Some of the raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households gave into the treasury of the malaakah (work) shanayam (twenty) rabaw (thousand) darics of gold, and two rabaw (thousand) two maah (hundred) minas of kasap (silver).

That which the shaarayath (rest) of the im (people) gave was shanayam (twenty) rabaw (thousand) darics of gold, and two rabaw (thousand) minas of kasap (silver), and shashayam (sixty) - shabai (seven) kahan (priests)' garments.

So the kahan (priests), and the Lawayay (Levites), and the porters, and the singers, and some of the im (people), and the Nethinim, and all Yasharaal (Israel), lived in their Iyar. When the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month) had nagai (come), the children of Yasharaal (Israel) were in their Iyar.

All the im (people) gathered themselves asap (together) as one ayash (man) into the broad place that was panayam (before) the mayam (water) gate; and they spoke to Izaraa the scribe to bawaa (bring) the book of the thawarah (law) of Mashah, which Yahawah had tzawah (commanded) to Yasharaal (Israel).

Izaraa the kahan (priest) brought the thawarah (law) panayam (before) the qahal (assembly), both men and women, and all who could hear with bayan (understanding), on the achad (first) yawam (day) of the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month).

He qaraa (read) therein panayam (before) the broad place that was panayam (before) the mayam (water) gate from early awar (morning) until midday, in the presence of the men and the women, and of those who could bayan (understand); and the ears of all the im (people) were attentive to the book of the thawarah (law).

Izaraa the scribe stood on a pulpit of itz (wood), which they had made for the dabar (purpose); and beside him stood Mathathayah, and Shamai, and Inayah, and Awarayah, and Chalaqayah, and Maishayah, on his right yamayan (hand); and on his left yamayan (hand), Padayah, and Mayashaal, and Malakayah, and Chasham, and Chashabadanah, Zakarayah, and Mashalam.
Izaraa opened the book in the iyan (sight) of all the im (people); (for he was above all the im (people);) and when he opened it, all the im (people) stood up:

and Izaraa blessed Yahawah, the gadawal (great) Alahayam. All the im (people) answered, "aman (amen), aman (amen)," with the lifting up of their yad (hands). They bowed their heads, and worshiped Yahawah with their ap (faces) to the aratz (ground).

Also Yashawai, and Banay, and Sharabayah, Yamayan, Iqawab, Shabathay, Hawadayah, Maishayah, Qalayataa, Izarayah, Yawazabad, Chanan, Palayah, and the Lawayay (Levites), caused the im (people) to bayan (understand) the thawarah (law): and the im (people) stayed in their imad (place).
They qaraa (read) in the book, in the thawarah (law) of Alahayam, distinctly; and they gave the shakal (sense), so that they understood the maqaraa (reading).

Nachamayah, who was the governor, and Izaraa the kahan (priest) the scribe, and the Lawayay (Levites) who taught the im (people), said to all the im (people), "This yawam (day) is qadawash (holy) to Yahawah your Alahayam. Don't mourn, nor weep." For all the im (people) wept, when they heard the dabar (words) of the thawarah (law).

Then he said to them, "Go your yalak (way). akal (eat) the fat, drink the sweet, and shalach (send) portions to him for whom nothing is prepared; for this yawam (day) is qadawash (holy) to our Adawan. Don't be grieved; for the joy of Yahawah is your maiwaz (strength).
So the Lawayay (Levites) stilled all the im (people), saying, "Hold your hasah (peace), for the yawam (day) is qadawash (holy); neither be grieved.

All the im (people) went their yalak (way) to akal (eat), and to drink, and to shalach (send) portions, and to ishah (make) gadawal (great) mirth, because they had understood the dabar (words) that were declared to them.

On the shanay (second) yawam (day) were gathered asap (together) the raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households of all the im (people), the kahan (priests), and the Lawayay (Levites), to Izaraa the scribe, even to give attention to the dabar (words) of the thawarah (law).

They found written in the thawarah (law), how that Yahawah had tzawah (commanded) by Mashah, that the children of Yasharaal (Israel) should yashab (dwell) in sakah (booths) in the chag (feast) of the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month);

and that they should publish and ibar (proclaim) in all their Iyar, and in Yarawashalam, saying, "yatzaa (go) out to the har (mountain), and bawaa (get) olive branches, and branches of wild shaman (olive), and myrtle branches, and palm branches, and branches of Ibath itz (trees), to ishah (make) sakah (booths), as it is written.

So the im (people) went out, and brought them, and made themselves sakah (booths), everyone on the roof of his gag (house), and in their courts, and in the courts of the bayath (house) of Alahayam, and in the broad place of the mayam (water) gate, and in the broad place of the gate of Aparayam.

All the qahal (assembly) of those who had shawab (turn back / repent) again out of the Shabay made sakah (booths), and lived in the sakah (booths); for since the yawam (days) of Yashawai the ban (son) of Nawan to that yawam (day) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) had not done so. There was very gadawal (great) gladness.

Also yawam (day) by yawam (day), from the raashawan (first) yawam (day) to the Acharawan yawam (day), he qaraa (read) in the book of the thawarah (law) of Alahayam. They kept the chag (feast) shabai (seven) yawam (days); and on the eighth yawam (day) was a solemn itzarah (assembly), according to the mashapat (ordinance).
Now in the isharayam (twenty) - fourth yawam (day) of this chadash (month) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) were assembled with fasting, and with sackcloth, and adamah (earth) on them.
The zarai (seed) of Yasharaal (Israel) separated themselves from all foreigners, and stood and confessed their chataah (sins), and the iwan (iniquities) of their abawath (fathers).

They stood up in their imad (place), and qaraa (read) in the book of the thawarah (law) of Yahawah their Alahayam a rabayaiy (fourth) part of the yawam (day); and a rabayaiy (fourth) part they confessed, and worshiped Yahawah their Alahayam.

Then Yashawai, and Banay, Qadamayaal, Shabanayah, Banay, Sharabayah, Banay, and Kananay Lawayay the Levites stood up on the stairs, and cried with a gadawal (loud) qawal (voice) to Yahawah their Alahayam.
