Then the Lawayay (Levites), Yashawai, and Qadamayaal, Banay, Chashabanayah, Sharabayah, Hawadayah, Shabanayah, and Pathachayah, said, "qawam (stand) up and barak (bless) Yahawah your Alahayam from iwalam (forever) to iwalam (forever)! Bessed be your kabawad (glorious) sham (name), which is exalted above all barakah (blessing) and thahalah (praise)!

You are Yahawah, even you alone. You have made shamayam (heaven), the shamayam (heaven) of shamayam (heavens), with all their tzabaa (army), the aratz (earth) and all things that are on it, the yam (seas) and all that is in them, and you chayah (preserve) them all. The tzabaa (army) of shamayam (heaven) shachah (worships) you.
You are Yahawah, the Alahayam who chose Abaram, and brought him out of Awar of the Kashaday, and gave him the sham (name) of Abaraham,

and found his labab (heart) aman (faithful) panayam (before) you, and made a barayath (covenant) with him to nathan (give) the aratz (land) of the Kanainay (Canaanite), the Chathay (Hittite), the Amaray (Amorite), and the Parazay (Perizzite), and the Yabawasay (Jebusite), and the Garagashay (Girgashite), to nathan (give) it to his zarai (seed), and have performed your dabar (words); for you are tzadayaq (righteous).
"You saw the affliction of our abawath (fathers) in Matzarayam, and heard their cry by the Red yam (sea),

and showed awath (signs) and mawapath (wonders) against Paraih, and against all his ibad (servants), and against all the im (people) of his aratz (land); for you knew that they dealt proudly against them, and made a sham (name) for yourself, as it is this yawam (day).

You divided the yam (sea) panayam (before) them, so that they went ibar (through) the midst of the yam (sea) on the dry yabashah (dry land); and you cast their pursuers into the depths, as a aban (stone) into the iz (mighty) mayam (waters).
Moreover, in a pillar of cloud you led them by yawamam (day); and in a pillar of ash (fire) by layal (night), to give them awar (light) in the darak (way) in which they should yalak (go).

"You came down also on har (mount) Sayanay, and spoke with them from shamayam (heaven), and gave them yashar (right) mashapat (ordinances) and amath (true) thawarah (laws), tawab (good) chaq (statutes) and matzawah (commandments),
and made yadai (known) to them your qadash (holy) shabath (sabbath), and tzawah (commanded) them matzawah (commandments), and chaq (statutes), and a thawarah (law), by Mashah your ibad (servant),

and gave them lacham (bread) from the sky for their hunger, and brought yatzaa (forth) mayam (water) for them out of the salai (rock) for their thirst, and commanded them that they should bawaa (go) in to yarash (possess) the aratz (land) which you had sworn to nathan (give) them.
"But they and our abawath (fathers) dealt proudly and hardened their neck, didn't listen to your matzawah (commandments),

and refused to obey, neither were they zakar (mindful) of your wonders that you did among them, but hardened their neck, and in their rebellion appointed a raash (captain) to shawab (turn back / repent) to their bondage. But you are a Alawah ready to pardon, Chanawan and Rachawam, Arak to ap (anger), and abundant in loving chasad (kindness), and didn't forsake them.
Yes, when they had made them a molten calf, and said, ‘This is your Alahayam who brought you up out of Matzarayam,' and had committed awful blasphemies;

yet you in your manifold racham (mercies) didn't forsake them in the madabar (wilderness): the pillar of cloud didn't sawar (depart) from over them by yawamam (day), to lead them in the darak (way); neither the pillar of ash (fire) by layal (night), to show them awar (light), and the darak (way) in which they should yalak (go).
You gave also your tawab (good) rawach (spirit) to shakal (instruct) them, and didn't withhold your manna from their pah (mouth), and gave them mayam (water) for their thirst.
"Yes, arabaiyam (forty) Shanah you sustained them in the madabar (wilderness). They lacked nothing. Their clothes didn't grow old, and their feet didn't swell.

Moreover you gave them mamalakah (kingdoms) and im (peoples), which you allotted according to their portions. So they possessed the aratz (land) of Sayachawan, even the aratz (land) of the malak (king) of Chashabawan, and the aratz (land) of Iwag malak (king) of Bashan.

You also multiplied their children as the kawakab (stars) of the sky, and brought them into the aratz (land) concerning which you said to their abawath (fathers), that they should bawaa (go) in to yarash (possess) it.

"So the children went in and possessed the aratz (land), and you subdued panayam (before) them the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land), the Kanainay (Canaanites), and gave them into their yad (hands), with their malak (kings), and the im (peoples) of the aratz (land), that they might do with them as they pleased.

They took fortified Iyar, and a Shaman adamah (land), and possessed bayath (houses) Malaa of all tawab (good) things, bawar (cisterns) dug out, vineyards, and olive groves, and fruit itz (trees) in abundance. So they ate, were filled, became fat, and delighted themselves in your gadawal (great) goodness.

"Nevertheless they were disobedient, and rebelled against you, and cast your thawarah (law) achar (behind) their back, and killed your nabayaa (prophets) that testified against them to shawab (turn back / repent) them again to you, and they committed awful blasphemies.

Therefore you delivered them into the yad (hand) of their tzar (adversaries), who distressed them. In the ith (time) of their tzarah (trouble), when they cried to you, you heard from shamayam (heaven); and according to your manifold racham (mercies) you gave them saviors who saved them out of the yad (hand) of their tzar (adversaries).

But after they had nawach (rest), they did rai (evil) again panayam (before) you; therefore left you them in the yad (hand) of their ayab (enemies), so that they had the radah (dominion) over them; yet when they returned, and cried to you, you heard from shamayam (heaven); and many ith (times) you delivered them according to your racham (mercies),

and testified against them, that you might shawab (turn back / repent) them again to your thawarah (law). Yet they dealt proudly, and didn't listen to your matzawah (commandments), but sinned against your mashapat (ordinances), (which if a adam (man) does, he shall chayah (live) in them), turned their backs, stiffened their neck, and would not hear.

Yet many Shanah you put up with them, and testified against them by your rawach (spirit) yad (through) your nabayaa (prophets). Yet would they not nathan (give) ear. Therefore you gave them into the yad (hand) of the im (peoples) of the aratz (lands).
"Nevertheless in your manifold racham (mercies) you did not make a full end of them, nor forsake them; for you are a Chanawan and Rachawam Al.

Now therefore, our Alahayam, the gadawal (great), the gabawar (mighty), and the awesome Al, who shamar (keeps) barayath (covenant) and loving chasad (kindness), don't let all the travail seem little panayam (before) you, that has matzaa (come) on us, on our malak (kings), on our shar (princes), and on our kahan (priests), and on our nabayaa (prophets), and on our abawath (fathers), and on all your im (people), yawam (since) the time of the malak (kings) of Ashawar to this yawam (day).
However you are tzadayaq (just) in all that has bawaa (come) on us; for you have dealt truly, but we have done wickedly;

neither have our malak (kings), our shar (princes), our kahan (priests), nor our abawath (fathers), kept your thawarah (law), nor listened to your matzawah (commandments) and your idawath (testimonies) with which you testified against them.

For they have not served you in their malakawath (kingdom), and in your rab (great) goodness that you gave them, and in the Rachab and Shaman aratz (land) which you gave panayam (before) them, neither did they shawab (turn back / repent) from their rai (wicked) mailal (works).

"Behold, we are ibad (servants) this yawam (day), and as for the aratz (land) that you gave to our abawath (fathers) to akal (eat) its fruit and its tawab (good), behold, we are ibad (servants) in it.

It yields much increase to the malak (kings) whom you have nathan (set) over us because of our chataah (sins): also they have mashal (power) over our bodies, and over our livestock, at their pleasure, and we are in gadawal (great) tzarah (distress).
Yet for all this, we karath (make) a sure covenant, and kathab (write) it; and our shar (princes), our Lawayay (Levites), and our kahan (priests), seal it.
Now those who sealed were: Nachamayah the governor, the ban (son) Chakalayah Hacaliah, and Tzadaqayah,
Sharayah, Izarayah, Yaramayah,
Pashachawar, Amarayah, Malakayah,
Chatawash, Shabanayah, Malawak,
Charam, Maramawath, Ibadayah,
Danayaal, Ganathawan, Barawak,
Mashalam, Abayah, Mayaman,
Maizayah, Balagay, Shamaiyah; these were the kahan (priests).
The Lawayay (Levites): namely, Yashawai the ban (son) of Azanayah, Banaway of the ban (sons) of Chanadad, Qadamayaal;
and their ach (brothers), Shabanayah, Hawadayah, Qalayataa, Palayah, Chanan,
Mayakaa, Rachab, Chashabayah,
Zakawar, Sharabayah, Shabanayah,
Hawadayah, Banay, Banayanaw.
The raash (chiefs) of the im (people): Paraish, Pachathamawaab, Iyalam, Zathawaa, Banay,
Banay, Izagad, Babay,
Adanayah, Bagaway, Idayan,
Atar, Chazaqayah, Izawar,
Hawadayah, Chasham, Batzay,
Charayap, Inathawath, Nawabay,
Magapayaish, Mashalam, Chazayar,
Mashayazabaal, Tzadawaq, Yadawai,
Palatayah, Chanan, Inayah,
Hawashai, Chananayah, Chashawab,
Lawachash, Palachaa, Shawabaq,
Rachawam, Chashabanah, Maishayah,
and Achayah, Chanan, Inan,
Malawak, Charam, Bainah.

The shaar (rest) of the im (people), the kahan (priests), the Lawayay (Levites), the porters, the singers, the Nethinim, and all those who had separated themselves from the im (peoples) of the aratz (lands) to the thawarah (law) of Alahayam, their wives, their ban (sons), and their bath (daughters), everyone who had yadai (knowledge), and bayan (understanding)—

they joined with their ach (brothers), their adayar (nobles), and entered into a alah (curse), and into an shabawaih (oath), to yalak (walk) in alahayam (god's) thawarah (law), which was given by Mashah the ibad (servant) of Alahayam, and to shamar (observe) and do all the matzawah (commandments) of Yahawah our Adawan, and his mashapat (ordinances) and his chaq (statutes);
and that we would not nathan (give) our bath (daughters) to the im (peoples) of the aratz (land), nor take their bath (daughters) for our ban (sons);

and if the im (peoples) of the aratz (land) bawaa (bring) wares or any grain on the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day) to sell, that we would not buy of them on the shabath (sabbath), or on a qadash (holy) yawam (day); and that we would forego the shabayaiy (seventh) Shanah, and the exaction of every yad (debt).
Also we made matzawah (ordinances) for ourselves, to nathan (charge) Shanah yearly with the shalayashay (third) part of a shekel for the ibadah (service) of the bayath (house) of our Alahayam;

for the show mairakath (bread), and for the continual meal manachah (offering), and for the continual burnt ilah (offering), for the shabath (sabbaths), for the new chadash (moons), for the mawaid (set) feasts, and for the qadash (holy) things, and for the chataah (sin) offerings to make kapar (atonement) for Yasharaal (Israel), and for all the malaakah (work) of the bayath (house) of our Alahayam.

We napal (cast) lots, the kahan (priests), the Lawayay (Levites), and the im (people), for the itz (wood) qaraban (offering), to bawaa (bring) it into the bayath (house) of our Alahayam, according to our abawath (fathers)' bayath (houses), at ith (times) appointed, Shanah by Shanah, to bair (burn) on the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah our Alahayam, as it is written in the thawarah (law);
and to bawaa (bring) the bakawar (first) fruits of our adamah (ground), and the bakawar (first) fruits of all fruit of all kinds of itz (trees), Shanah by Shanah, to the bayath (house) of Yahawah;

also the firstborn of our ban (sons), and of our livestock, as it is written in the thawarah (law), and the firstborn of our herds and of our flocks, to bawaa (bring) to the bayath (house) of our Alahayam, to the kahan (priests) who sharath (minister) in the bayath (house) of our Alahayam;

and that we should bawaa (bring) the raashayath (first) fruits of our dough, and our wave tharawamah (offerings), and the fruit of all kinds of itz (trees), the new thayarawash (wine) and the yatzahar (oil), to the kahan (priests), to the rooms of the bayath (house) of our Alahayam; and the maishar (tithes) of our adamah (ground) Lawayay the Levites; Lawayay they, the Levites, ishar (take) the tithes in all the Iyar of our ibadah (tillage).

The kahan (priest) the ban (son) of Aharawan shall be Lawayay the Levites, when the Lawayay (Levites) ishar (take) tithes: and the Lawayay (Levites) shall ilah (bring) up the maishar (tithe) of the maishar (tithes) to the bayath (house) of our Alahayam, to the rooms, into the treasure bayath (house).

For the children of Yasharaal (Israel) and the children of Laway shall bawaa (bring) the wave tharawamah (offering) of the grain, of the new thayarawash (wine), and of the yatzahar (oil), to the rooms, where are the vessels of the maqadash (sanctuary), and the kahan (priests) who sharath (minister), and the porters, and the singers. We will not forsake the bayath (house) of our Alahayam.

The shar (princes) of the im (people) lived in Yarawashalam: the shaar (rest) of the im (people) also napal (cast) lots, to bawaa (bring) one of ishar (ten) to yashab (dwell) in Yarawashalam the qadash (holy) Iyar, and thashai (nine) yad (parts) in the other Iyar.
The im (people) blessed all the men who willingly offered themselves to yashab (dwell) in Yarawashalam.

Now these are the raash (chiefs) of the province who lived in Yarawashalam; but in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah) everyone lived in his achazah (possession) in their Iyar: Yasharaal (Israel), the kahan (priests), and the Lawayay (Levites), and the Nethinim, and the children of Shalamah ibad (servants).

In Yarawashalam lived certain of the children of Yahawadah (Judah), and of the children of Banayamayan. Of the children of Yahawadah (Judah): Ithayah the ban (son) of Izayah, the ban (son) of Zakarayah, the ban (son) of Amarayah, the ban (son) of Shapatayah, the ban (son) Mahalalaal Mahalalel, of the children of Paratz;

and Maishayah the ban (son) of Barawak, the ban (son) of Kalachazah, the ban (son) of Chazayah, the ban (son) of Idayah, the ban (son) of Yawayarayab, the ban (son) of Zakarayah, the ban (son) Shalanay the Shilonite.
All the ban (sons) of Paratz who lived in Yarawashalam were arabai (four) maah (hundred) shashayam (sixty) - shamanah (eight) chayal (valiant) men.

These are the ban (sons) of Banayamayan: Salaw the ban (son) of Mashalam, the ban (son) of Yawaid, the ban (son) of Padayah, the ban (son) of Qawalayah, the ban (son) of Maishayah, the ban (son) of Ayathayaal, the ban (son) of Yashaiyah.
achar (after) him Gabay, Salaw, thashai (nine) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shamanah (eight).
Yawaal the ban (son) of Zakaray was their overseer; and Yahawadah (Judah) the ban (son) Sanawaah Hassenuah was mashanah (second) over the Iyar.
Of the kahan (priests): Yadaiyah the ban (son) of Yawayarayab, Yakayan,

Sharayah the ban (son) Chalaqayah Hilkiah, the ban (son) of Mashalam, the ban (son) of Tzadawaq, the ban (son) of Marayawath, the ban (son) of Achayatawab, the nagayad (ruler) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam,

and their ach (brothers) who did the malaakah (work) of the bayath (house), shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shanayam (two); and Idayah the ban (son) of Yaracham, the ban (son) of Palalayah, the ban (son) of Amatzay, the ban (son) of Zakarayah, the ban (son) Pashachawar Pashhur, the ban (son) of Malakayah,

and his ach (brothers), raash (chiefs) of abawath (fathers)' households, shanayam (two) maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - shanayam (two); and Imashasay the ban (son) Izaraal Azarel, the ban (son) Achazay Ahzai, the ban (son) of Mashalamawath, the ban (son) of Amar,
and their ach (brothers), gabawar (mighty) men of valor, one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shamanah (eight); and their overseer was Zabadayaal, the ban (son) of Haggedolim.
Lawayay the Levites: Shamaiyah the ban (son) of Chashawab, the ban (son) of Izarayaqam, the ban (son) of Chashabayah, the ban (son) of Banay;
and Shabathay and Yawazabad, of the raash (chiefs) Lawayay the Levites, who had the oversight of the Chayatzawan malaakah (business) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam;

and Mathanayah the ban (son) Mayakaa Mica, the ban (son) of Zabaday, the ban (son) of Asap, who was the raash (chief) to thachalah (begin) the thanksgiving in prayer, and Baqabaqayah, the mashanah (second) among his ach (brothers); and Ibadaa the ban (son) of Shamawai, the ban (son) of Galal, the ban (son) of Yadawathawan.
All the Lawayay (Levites) in the qadash (holy) Iyar were two maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty) - arabai (four).
Moreover the porters, Iqawab, Talamawan, and their ach (brothers), who kept watch at the gates, were one maah (hundred) shabaiyam (seventy) - shanayam (two).
The shaar (residue) of Yasharaal (Israel), of the kahan (priests), the Lawayay (Levites), were in all the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), everyone in his nachalah (inheritance).
But the Nethinim lived in Ipal: and Tzayachaa and Gashapaa were over the Nethinim.

The overseer Lawayay of the Levites at Yarawashalam was Izay the ban (son) of Banay, the ban (son) of Chashabayah, the ban (son) of Mathanayah, the ban (son) Mayakaa Mica, of the ban (sons) of Asap, the singers, over the malaakah (business) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam.
For there was a matzawah (commandment) from the malak (king) concerning them, and a settled provision for the singers, as every yawam (day) required.

Pathachayah the ban (son) Mashayazabaal Meshezabel, of the children of Zarach the ban (son) of Yahawadah (Judah), was at the malak (king's) yad (hand) in all dabar (matters) concerning the im (people).

As for the villages, with their shadah (fields), some of the children of Yahawadah (Judah) lived in Kiriath Qarayathaarabai and its towns, and in Dayabawan and its towns, and in Yaqabatzaal and its bath (villages),
and in Yashawai, and in Mawaladah, and Bayathapalat Pelet,
and in Chatzarashawail Shual, and Baarashabai Beersheba and its bath (towns),
and in Tzaqalag, and Makanah Meconah and in its bath (towns),
and in Iyanaramawan Rimmon, and in Tzaraih, and in Yaramawath,
Zanawach, Idalam, and their villages, Lakayash and its shadah (fields), Izaqah and its bath (towns). So they encamped Baarashabai Beersheba to the Gayaa of Hanam.
The children of Banayamayan also lived from Gabai onward, at Makamas and Iy, and at Bayathaal and its bath (towns),
at Inathawath, Nab, Inanayah,
Chatzawar, Ramah, Gathayam,
Chadayad, Tzabaiyam, Nabalat,
Lad, and Awanaw, the Gayaa Charash craftsmen.
Lawayay the Levites, certain divisions in Yahawadah (Judah) settled in Banayamayan territory.
Now these are the kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites) who went up with Zarababal the ban (son) of Shaalathayaal, and Yashawai: Sharayah, Yaramayah, Izaraa,
Amarayah, Malawak, Chatawash,
Shakanayah, Rachawam, Maramawath,
Idaw, Ganathawan, Abayah,
Mayaman, Maidayah, Balagah,
Shamaiyah, and Yawayarayab, Yadaiyah.
Salaw, Imawaq, Chalaqayah, Yadaiyah. These were the raash (chiefs) of the kahan (priests) and of their ach (brothers) in the yawam (days) of Yashawai.
Lawayay the Levites: Yashawai, Banaway, Qadamayaal, Sharabayah, Yahawadah (Judah), and Mathanayah, who was over the thanksgiving, he and his ach (brothers).
Also Baqabaqayah and Inay, their ach (brothers), were over against them according to their offices.
Yashawai became the father of Yawayaqayam, and Yawayaqayam became the father of Alayashayab, and Alayashayab became the father of Yawayadai,
and Yawayadai became the father of Yawanathan, and Yawanathan became the father of Yadawai.
In the yawam (days) of Yawayaqayam were kahan (priests), raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households: of Sharayah, Marayah; of Yaramayah, Chananayah;
of Izaraa, Mashalam; of Amarayah, Yahawachanan;
Malawak Malluchi, Yawanathan; of Shabanayah, Yawasap;
of Charam, Idanaa; of Marayawath, Chalaqay;
of Idaw, Zakarayah; of Ganathawan, Mashalam;
of Abayah, Zakaray; of Manayamayan, of Mawaidayah, Palatay;
of Balagah, Shamawai; of Shamaiyah, Yahawanathan;
and of Yawayarayab, Mathanay; of Yadaiyah, Izay;
of Salaw, Qalay; of Imawaq, Ibar;
Chalaqayah Hilkiah, Chashabayah; of Yadaiyah, Nathanaal.

As Lawayay the Levites, in the yawam (days) of Alayashayab, Yawayadai, and Yawachanan, and Yadawai, there were recorded the raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households; also the kahan (priests), in the malakawath (reign) of Darayawash the Parasay (Persian).
The ban (sons) of Laway, raash (heads) of abawath (fathers)' households, were written in the book of the dabar (chronicles), even until the yawam (days) of Yawachanan the ban (son) of Alayashayab.

The raash (chiefs) Lawayay the Levites: Chashabayah, Sharabayah, and Yashawai the ban (son) of Qadamayaal, with their ach (brothers) over against them, to halal (praise) and halal (give) thanks, according to the matzawah (commandment) of Dawad the ayash (man) of Alahayam, watch next to watch.
Mathanayah, and Baqabaqayah, Ibadayah, Mashalam, Talamawan, Iqawab, were porters keeping the watch at the storehouses of the gates.
These were in the yawam (days) of Yawayaqayam the ban (son) of Yashawai, the ban (son) of Yawatzadaq, and in the yawam (days) of Nachamayah the governor, and of Izaraa the kahan (priest) the scribe.

At the dedication of the wall of Yarawashalam they sought the Lawayay (Levites) out of all their places, to bawaa (bring) them to Yarawashalam, to ishah (keep) the dedication with gladness, both with thawadah (giving) thanks, and with singing, with cymbals, stringed instruments, and with harps.
The ban (sons) of the singers gathered themselves asap (together), both out of the plain around Yarawashalam, and from the villages of the Natapathay (Netophathites);
also from Beth Galagal, and out of the shadah (fields) of Gabai and Izamawath: for the singers had built them villages around Yarawashalam.
The kahan (priests) and the Lawayay (Levites) purified themselves; and they purified the im (people), and the gates, and the wall.

Then I brought up the shar (princes) of Yahawadah (Judah) on the wall, and appointed shanayam (two) gadawal (great) companies who gave thawadah (thanks) and went in procession. thahalakah (one) went on the right yamayan (hand) on the wall toward the dung gate;
and achar (after) them went Hawashaiyah, and chatzay (half) of the shar (princes) of Yahawadah (Judah),
and Izarayah, Izaraa, and Mashalam,
Yahawadah (Judah), and Banayamayan, and Shamaiyah, and Yaramayah,

and certain of the kahan (priests)' ban (sons) with trumpets: Zakarayah the ban (son) of Yawanathan, the ban (son) of Shamaiyah, the ban (son) of Mathanayah, the ban (son) Mayakayah Micaiah, the ban (son) of Zakawar, the ban (son) of Asap;

and his ach (brothers), Shamaiyah, and Izaraal, Malalay, Galalay, Maiy, Nathanaal, and Yahawadah (Judah), Chananay, with the musical instruments of Dawad the ayash (man) of Alahayam; and Izaraa the scribe was panayam (before) them.
By the spring gate, and straight before them, they went up by the stairs of the Iyar of Dawad, at the ascent of the wall, above the bayath (house) of Dawad, even to the mayam (water) gate eastward.

The other company of those who gave thawadah (thanks) went to meet them, and I achar (after) them, with the chatzay (half) of the im (people), on the wall, above the magadal (tower) of the furnaces, even to the Rachab wall,

and above the gate of Aparayam, and by the Yashan gate, and by the fish gate, and the magadal (tower) Chananaal Hananel, and the magadal (tower) Maah Hammeah, even to the sheep gate: and they stood still in the gate of the guard.
So stood the shanayam (two) companies of those who gave thawadah (thanks) in the bayath (house) of Alahayam, and I, and the chatzay (half) of the sagan (rulers) with me;
and the kahan (priests), Alayaqayam, Maishayah, Manayamayan, Mayakayah, Alayahawaiyanay, Zakarayah, and Chananayah, with trumpets;
and Maishayah, and Shamaiyah, and Alaizar, and Izay, and Yahawachanan, and Malakayah, and Iyalam, and Izar. The singers sang loud, with Yazarachayah their overseer.

They offered gadawal (great) zabach (sacrifices) that yawam (day), and Shamach; for Alahayam had made them Shamach with gadawal (great) joy; and the women also and the children Shamach: so that the joy of Yarawashalam was heard even Rachawaq off.

On that yawam (day) were men appointed over the rooms for the treasures, for the wave tharawamah (offerings), for the raashayath (first) fruits, and for the maishar (tithes), to gather into them, according to the shadah (fields) of the Iyar, the portions appointed by the thawarah (law) for the kahan (priests) and Lawayay (Levites): for Yahawadah (Judah) rejoiced for the kahan (priests) and Lawayay the Levites who waited.
They performed the duty of their Alahayam, and the duty of the purification, and so did the singers and the porters, according to the matzawah (commandment) of Dawad, and of Shalamah his ban (son).
For in the yawam (days) of Dawad and Asap of qadam (old) there was a raash (chief) of the singers, and songs of thahalah (praise) and thanksgiving to Alahayam.

All Yasharaal (Israel) in the yawam (days) of Zarababal, and in the yawam (days) of Nachamayah, gave the portions of the singers and the porters, as every yawam (day) required: and they set apart that which was Lawayay the Levites; and the Lawayay (Levites) set apart that which was for the ban (sons) of Aharawan.

On that yawam (day) they qaraa (read) in the book of Mashah in the audience of the im (people); and therein was found written, that an Imawanay (Ammonite) and a Mawaabay (Moabite) should not bawaa (enter) into the qahal (assembly) of Alahayam iwalam (forever),

because they didn't qadam (meet) the children of Yasharaal (Israel) with lacham (bread) and with mayam (water), but hired Balaim against them, to qalal (curse) them: however our Alahayam turned the qalal (curse) into a barakah (blessing).
It came to pass, when they had heard the thawarah (law), that they separated from Yasharaal (Israel) all the irab (mixed) multitude.
Now panayam (before) this, Alayashayab the kahan (priest), who was appointed over the rooms of the bayath (house) of our Alahayam, being qarawab (allied) to Tawabayah,

had prepared for him a gadawal (great) room, where panayam (before) they laid the meal manachah (offerings), the frankincense, and the vessels, and the maishar (tithes) of the grain, the new thayarawash (wine), and the yatzahar (oil), which were given by matzawah (commandment) Lawayay the Levites, and the singers, and the porters; and the wave tharawamah (offerings) for the kahan (priests).

But in all this, I was not at Yarawashalam; for in the shanayam (two) and shalawashayam (thirtieth) Shanah Arathachashashathaa Artaxerxes malak (king) of Babal I went to the malak (king): and after certain yawam (days) asked I shaal (leave) of the malak (king),
and I came to Yarawashalam, and understood the rai (evil) that Alayashayab had done for Tawabayah, in preparing him a room in the courts of the bayath (house) of Alahayam.
It grieved me severely: therefore I cast forth all the bayath (household) stuff of Tawabayah out of the room.
Then I commanded, and they cleansed the rooms: and there brought I again the vessels of the bayath (house) of Alahayam, with the meal manachah (offerings) and the frankincense.
I perceived that the portions Lawayay the Levites had not been given them; so that the Lawayay (Levites) and the singers, who did the malaakah (work), had fled everyone to his shadah (field).
Then I contended with the sagan (rulers), and said, "Why is the bayath (house) of Alahayam forsaken?" I gathered them together, and imad (set) them in their imad (place).
Then brought all Yahawadah (Judah) the maishar (tithe) of the grain and the new thayarawash (wine) and the yatzahar (oil) to the treasuries.

I made treasurers over the treasuries, Shalamayah the kahan (priest), and Tzadawaq the scribe, and Lawayay the Levites, Padayah: and next to them was Chanan the ban (son) of Zakawar, the ban (son) of Mathanayah; for they were counted aman (faithful), and their business was to distribute to their ach (brothers).
zakar (remember) me, my Alahayam, concerning this, and don't machah (wipe) out my chasad (good) deeds that I have done for the bayath (house) of my Alahayam, and for its observances.

In those yawam (days) saw I in Yahawadah (Judah) some men treading winepresses on the shabath (sabbath), and bringing in sheaves, and loading donkeys; as also yayan (wine), inab (grapes), and figs, and all kinds of mashaa (burdens), which they brought into Yarawashalam on the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day): and I testified against them in the yawam (day) in which they sold food.
There lived men of Tzaray also therein, who brought in fish, and all kinds of wares, and sold on the shabath (sabbath) to the children of Yahawadah (Judah), and in Yarawashalam.
Then I contended with the nobles of Yahawadah (Judah), and said to them, "What rai (evil) thing is this that you do, and chalal (profane) the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day)?

Didn't your abawath (fathers) do thus, and didn't our Alahayam bawaa (bring) all this rai (evil) on us, and on this Iyar? Yet you bawaa (bring) more charawan (wrath) on Yasharaal (Israel) by profaning the shabath (sabbath).

It came to pass that, when the gates of Yarawashalam began to be dark panayam (before) the shabath (sabbath), I commanded that the doors should be shut, and commanded that they should not be opened until achar (after) the shabath (sabbath). I imad (set) some of my nair (servants) over the gates, that no mashaa (burden) should be brought in on the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day).
So the merchants and sellers of all kinds of wares lodged outside of Yarawashalam paim (once) or shanayam (twice).

Then I testified amar (against) them, and said to them, "Why do you stay around the wall? If you do so again, I will shalach (lay) yad (hands) on you." From that ith (time) on, they didn't bawaa (come) on the shabath (sabbath).

I commanded the Lawayay (Levites) that they should tahar (purify) themselves, and that they should bawaa (come) and shamar (keep) the gates, to qadash (sanctify) the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day). zakar (remember) to me, my Alahayam, this also, and spare me according to the greatness of your loving chasad (kindness).
In those yawam (days) also saw I the Yahawaday (Jews) who had married women of Ashadawaday, of Imawanay, and of Mawaabay:

and their children spoke chatzay (half) in the Ashadawadayath of Ashdod, and could not dabar (speak) in the Yahawadayath (Jews)' language, but according to the lashawan (language) of each im (people).

I contended with them, and cursed them, and struck anawash (certain) of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them shabai (swear) by Alahayam, "You shall not nathan (give) your bath (daughters) to their ban (sons), nor nashaa (take) their bath (daughters) for your ban (sons), or for yourselves.

Didn't Shalamah malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) chataa (sin) by these things? Yet among many gawayam (nations) was there no malak (king) ahab (like) him, and he was beloved of his Alahayam, and Alahayam made him malak (king) over all Yasharaal (Israel). Nevertheless foreign women caused even him to chataa (sin).
Shall we then listen to you to do all this gadawal (great) rai (evil), to trespass against our Alahayam in yashab (marrying) foreign women?
One of the ban (sons) of Yawayadai, the ban (son) of Alayashayab the gadawal (high) kahan (priest), was son-in-law to Sanabalat the Charanay: therefore I chased him from me.
zakar (remember) them, my Alahayam, because they have defiled the kahanah (priesthood), and the barayath (covenant) of the kahanah (priesthood), and Lawayay the Levites.
Thus I cleansed them from all foreigners, and appointed duties for the kahan (priests) and Lawayay the Levites, everyone in his malaakah (work);
and for the itz (wood) qaraban (offering), at ith (times) appointed, and for the bakawar (first) fruits. zakar (remember) me, my Alahayam, for tawab (good).
Now it happened in the yawam (days) of Achashawarawash (this is Achashawarawash who reigned from Hadaw even to Kawash, over one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shabai (seven) provinces),
that in those yawam (days), when the malak (king) Achashawarawash sat on the kasaa (throne) of his malakawath (kingdom), which was in Shawashan the palace,

in the shalawash (third) Shanah of his malak (reign), he made a feast for all his shar (princes) and his ibad (servants); the chayal (power) of Paras and Maday, the paratham (nobles) and shar (princes) of the provinces, being panayam (before) him.
He displayed the riches of his kabawad (glorious) malakawath (kingdom) and the honor of his excellent majesty many yawam (days), even one maah (hundred) shamanayam (eighty) yawam (days).

When these yawam (days) were fulfilled, the malak (king) made a shabai (seven) yawam (day) feast for all the im (people) who were matzaa (present) in Shawashan the palace, both gadawal (great) and qatan (small), in the court of the garden of the malak (king's) palace.

There were hangings of white, green, and blue material, fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to kasap (silver) rings and Shash pillars. The couches were of gold and kasap (silver), on a pavement of red, white, yellow, and black Shash.
They gave them shaqah (drinks) in golden vessels of various kinds, including malakawath (royal) yayan (wine) in abundance, according to the yad (bounty) of the malak (king).

In accordance with the dath (law), the drinking was not compulsory; for so the malak (king) had instructed all the officials of his bayath (house), that they should do according to every ayash (man's) pleasure.
Also Washathay the malakah (queen) made a feast for the women in the malakawath (royal) bayath (house) which belonged to malak (king) Achashawarawash.

On the shabayaiy (seventh) yawam (day), when the lab (heart) of the malak (king) was tawab (merry) with yayan (wine), he commanded Mahawaman, Bazathaa, Charabawanaa, Bagathaa, and Abagathaa, Zathar, and Karakas, the shabai (seven) eunuchs who served in the panayam (presence) of Achashawarawash the malak (king),

to bawaa (bring) Washathay the malakah (queen) panayam (before) the malak (king) with the malakawath (royal) kathar (crown), to show the im (people) and the shar (princes) her beauty; for she was tawab (beautiful).
But the malakah (queen) Washathay refused to bawaa (come) at the malak (king's) commandment by the eunuchs. Therefore the malak (king) was very qatzap (angry), and his chamah (anger) burned in him.
Then the malak (king) said to the chakam (wise) men, who knew the ith (times), (for it was the malak (king's) custom to consult those who knew dath (law) and dayan (judgment);

and the qarawab (next) to him were Karashanaa, Shathar, Adamathaa, Tharashayash, Maras, Marasanaa, and Mamawakan, the shabai (seven) shar (princes) of Paras and Maday, who saw the malak (king's) panayam (face), and sat raashawan (first) in the malakawath (kingdom)),
"What shall we do to the malakah (queen) Washathay according to dath (law), because she has not done the bidding of the malak (king) Achashawarawash by the eunuchs?

Mamawakan answered panayam (before) the malak (king) and the shar (princes), "Washathay the malakah (queen) has not done iwah (wrong) to just the malak (king), but also to all the shar (princes), and to all the im (people) who are in all the provinces of the malak (king) Achashawarawash.

For this dabar (deed) of the malakah (queen) will become known to all women, causing them to show contempt for their bail (husbands), when it is reported, ‘malak (king) Achashawarawash commanded Washathay the malakah (queen) to be brought in panayam (before) him, but she didn't bawaa (come).'
Today, the princesses of Paras and Maday who have heard of the malakah (queen's) dabar (deed) will amar (tell) all the malak (king's) shar (princes). This will cause much contempt and qatzap (wrath).

"If it tawab (please) the malak (king), let a malakawath (royal) commandment yatzaa (go) from him, and let it be written among the dath (laws) of the Paras (Persians) and the Maday, so that it cannot be altered, that Washathay may never again bawaa (come) panayam (before) malak (king) Achashawarawash; and let the malak (king) nathan (give) her malakawath (royal) estate to another who is tawab (better) than she.

When the malak (king's) decree which he shall ishah (make) is published throughout all his malakawath (kingdom) (for it is rab (great)), all the wives will nathan (give) their bail (husbands) honor, both gadawal (great) and qatan (small).
This dabar (advice) pleased the malak (king) and the shar (princes), and the malak (king) did according to the dabar (word) of Mamawakan:

for he sent letters into all the malak (king's) provinces, into every province according to its writing, and to every im (people) in their lashawan (language), that every ayash (man) should sharar (rule) his own bayath (house), speaking in the lashawan (language) of his own im (people).
achar (after) these things, when the chamah (wrath) of malak (king) Achashawarawash was pacified, he zakar (remembered) Washathay, and what she had done, and what was decreed against her.
Then the malak (king's) nair (servants) who served him said, "Let tawab (beautiful) young virgins be sought for the malak (king).

Let the malak (king) paqad (appoint) officers in all the provinces of his malakawath (kingdom), that they may gather together all the tawab (beautiful) young virgins to the citadel Shawashan Susa, to the women's bayath (house), to the yad (custody) of Hagaa the malak (king's) eunuch, keeper of the women. Let cosmetics be given them;
and let the maiden who yatab (pleases) the malak (king) be malak (queen) instead of Washathay." The thing pleased the malak (king), and he did so.

There was a ayash (certain) Yahawaday (Jew) in the citadel Shawashan Susa, whose sham (name) was Maradakay, the ban (son) of Yaayar, the ban (son) of Shamaiy, the ban (son) of Qayash, a Banayamayanay (Benjamite),

who had been carried away from Yarawashalam with the captives who had been carried away with Yakanayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), whom Nabawakadanaatzar the malak (king) of Babal had carried away.

He brought up Hadasah, that is, Asathar, his dawad (uncle's) bath (daughter); for she had neither ab (father) nor am (mother). The maiden was Yapah and Yapah; and when her ab (father) and am (mother) were mawath (dead), Maradakay took her for his own bath (daughter).

So it happened, when the malak (king's) commandment and his dabar (decree) was heard, and when many maidens were gathered together to the citadel Shawashan Susa, to the yad (custody) of Hagaa, that Asathar was taken into the malak (king's) bayath (house), to the yad (custody) of Hagaa, keeper of the women.

The maiden pleased him, and she obtained chasad (kindness) from him. He quickly gave her cosmetics and her portions of food, and the shabai (seven) choice maidens who were to be given her out of the malak (king's) bayath (house). He moved her and her maidens to the tawab (best) place in the women's bayath (house).
Asathar had not made known her im (people) nor her relatives, because Maradakay had instructed her that she should not make it known.
Maradakay walked every yawam (day) in panayam (front) of the court of the women's bayath (house), to find out how Asathar was doing, and what would ishah (become) of her.

Each young nairah (woman's) thawar (turn) came to go in to malak (king) Achashawarawash after her purification for shanayam (twelve) chadash (months) (for so were the yawam (days) of their purification accomplished, shash (six) chadash (months) with shaman (oil) of myrrh, and shash (six) chadash (months) with sweet fragrances and with preparations for beautifying women).
The young nairah (woman) then came to the malak (king) like this: whatever she desired was given her to bawaa (go) with her out of the women's bayath (house) to the malak (king's) bayath (house).

In the evening she went, and on the next baqar (day) she returned into the shanay (second) women's bayath (house), to the yad (custody) of Shaishagaz, the malak (king's) eunuch, who kept the concubines. She came in to the malak (king) no more, unless the malak (king) delighted in her, and she was called by sham (name).

Now when the thawar (turn) of Asathar, the bath (daughter) of Abayahayal the dawad (uncle) of Maradakay, who had taken her for his bath (daughter), came to go in to the malak (king), she required nothing but what Hagaa the malak (king's) eunuch, the keeper of the women, advised. Asathar obtained favor in the iyan (sight) of all those who looked at her.

So Asathar was taken to malak (king) Achashawarawash into his malakawath (royal) bayath (house) in the ishayaray (tenth) chadash (month), which is the chadash (month) Tabath, in the seventh Shanah of his malakawath (reign).

The malak (king) loved Asathar more than all the women, and she obtained favor and kindness in his panayam (sight) more than all the virgins; so that he shawam (set) the malakawath (royal) kathar (crown) on her raash (head), and made her malak (queen) instead of Washathay.

Then the malak (king) made a gadawal (great) feast for all his shar (princes) and his ibad (servants), even Asathar feast; and he proclaimed a holiday in the provinces, and gave mashaath (gifts) according to the malak (king's) yad (bounty).
When the virgins were gathered together the shanay (second) time, Maradakay was sitting in the malak (king's) gate.
Asathar had not yet made known her relatives nor her im (people), as Maradakay had tzawah (commanded) her; for Asathar obeyed Maradakay, like she did when she was brought up by him.

In those yawam (days), while Maradakay was sitting in the malak (king's) gate, shanayam (two) of the malak (king's) eunuchs, Bagathan and Tharash, who were doorkeepers, were qatzap (angry), and sought to shalach (lay) yad (hands) on the malak (king) Achashawarawash.
This thing became yadai (known) to Maradakay, who informed Asathar the malakah (queen); and Asathar informed the malak (king) in Maradakay sham (name).

When this dabar (matter) was investigated, and it was found to be so, they were shanayam (both) hanged on a itz (tree); and it was written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) in the malak (king's) panayam (presence).

achar (after) these things malak (king) Achashawarawash promoted Haman the ban (son) of Madathaa the Agagay, and advanced him, and shawam (set) his kasaa (seat) above all the shar (princes) who were with him.

All the malak (king's) ibad (servants) who were in the malak (king's) gate bowed down, and paid homage to Haman; for the malak (king) had so tzawah (commanded) concerning him. But Maradakay didn't bow down or pay him homage.
Then the malak (king's) ibad (servants), who were in the malak (king's) gate, said to Maradakay, "Why do you disobey the malak (king's) matzawah (commandment)?

Now it came to pass, when they spoke yawam (daily) to him, and he didn't listen to them, that they told Haman, to raah (see) whether Maradakay dabar (reason) would imad (stand); for he had told them that he was a Yahawaday (Jew).
When Haman saw that Maradakay didn't bow down, nor pay him homage, Haman was malaa (full) of chamah (wrath).

But he scorned the thought of laying yad (hands) on Maradakay alone, for they had made known to him Maradakay im (people). Therefore Haman sought to destroy all the Yahawaday (Jews) who were throughout the whole malakawath (kingdom) of Achashawarawash, even Maradakay im (people).

In the raashawan (first) chadash (month), which is the chadash (month) Nayasan, in the shanayam (twelfth) Shanah of malak (king) Achashawarawash, they napal (cast) Pawar, that is, the lot, panayam (before) Haman from yawam (day) to yawam (day), and from chadash (month) to chadash (month), and chose the shanayam (twelfth) chadash (month), which is the month Adar.

Haman said to malak (king) Achashawarawash, "There is a achad (certain) im (people) scattered abroad and dispersed among the im (peoples) in all the provinces of your malakawath (kingdom), and their dath (laws) are different than other im (people's). They don't ishah (keep) the malak (king's) dath (laws). Therefore it is not for the malak (king's) profit to allow them to remain.

If it tawab (pleases) the malak (king), let it be written that they be destroyed; and I will pay ishar (ten) alap (thousand) talents of kasap (silver) into the yad (hands) of those who are in ishah (charge) of the king's malaakah (business), to bawaa (bring) it into the malak (king's) treasuries.
The malak (king) took his ring from his yad (hand), and gave it to Haman the ban (son) of Madathaa the Agagay, the Yahawaday (Jews)' tzarar (enemy).
The malak (king) said to Haman, "The kasap (silver) is given to you, the im (people) also, to do with them as it seems tawab (good) to you.

Then the malak (king's) scribes were called in on the raashawan (first) chadash (month), on the thirteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month); and all that Haman tzawah (commanded) was written to the malak (king's) satraps, and to the governors who were over every province, and to the shar (princes) of every im (people), to every province according its writing, and to every im (people) in their lashawan (language). It was written in the sham (name) of malak (king) Achashawarawash, and it was sealed with the malak (king's) ring.

Letters were sent by couriers into all the malak (king's) provinces, to destroy, to harag (kill), and to cause to shamad (perish), all Yahawaday (Jews), both nair (young) and zaqan (old), little tap (children) and women, in one yawam (day), even on the thirteenth yawam (day) of the shanayam (twelfth) chadash (month), which is the chadash (month) Adar, and to plunder their shalal (possessions).
A copy of the letter, that the dath (decree) should be given out in every province, was published to all the im (peoples), that they should be Ithayad against that yawam (day).

The couriers went yatzaa (forth) in haste by the malak (king's) commandment, and the dath (decree) was given out in the citadel Shawashan Susa. The malak (king) and Haman sat down to drink; but the Iyar of Shawashan was perplexed.
Now when Maradakay found out all that was done, Maradakay tore his clothes, and Labash on sackcloth with ashes, and went out into the midst of the Iyar, and wailed loudly and Mar.
He came even panayam (before) the malak (king's) gate, for no one is allowed inside the malak (king's) gate clothed with sackcloth.

In every province, wherever the malak (king's) commandment and his dabar (decree) came, there was gadawal (great) mourning among the Yahawaday (Jews), and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
Asathar maidens and her eunuchs came and told her this, and the malakah (queen) was maad (exceedingly) grieved. She sent clothing to Maradakay, to Labash his sackcloth; but he didn't receive it.
Then Asathar called for Hathak, one of the malak (king's) eunuchs, whom he had appointed to attend her, and tzawah (commanded) him to go to Maradakay, to find out what this was, and why it was.
So Hathak went out to Maradakay, to Iyar square which was panayam (before) the malak (king's) gate.

Maradakay told him of all that had happened to him, and the exact sum of the kasap (money) that Haman had promised to pay to the malak (king's) treasuries for the abad (destruction) of the Yahawaday (Jews).

He also gave him the copy of the writing of the dath (decree) that was given out in Shawashan to destroy them, to show it to Asathar, and to nagad (declare) it to her, and to urge her to bawaa (go) in to the malak (king), to chanan (make) supplication to him, and to make request panayam (before) him, for her im (people).
Hathak came and told Asathar the dabar (words) of Maradakay.
Then Asathar spoke to Hathak, and gave him a message to Maradakay:

"All the malak (king's) ibad (servants), and the im (people) of the malak (king's) provinces, yadai (know), that whoever, whether ayash (man) or ashah (woman), bawaa (comes) to the malak (king) Panayamay the inner court without being called, there is one dath (law) for him, that he be put to mawath (death), bad (except) those to whom the malak (king) might hold out the golden scepter, that he may chayah (live). I have not been called to bawaa (come) in to the malak (king) these shalawashayam (thirty) yawam (days).
They told to Maradakay Asathar dabar (words).

Then Maradakay asked them shawab (turn back / repent) answer to Asathar, "Don't think to yourself that you will malat (escape) in the malak (king's) bayath (house) any more than all the Yahawaday (Jews).

For if you remain charash (silent) now, then relief and deliverance will come to the Yahawaday (Jews) from achar (another) place, but you and your ab (father's) bayath (house) will abad (perish). Who yadai (knows) if you haven't nagai (come) to the malakawath (kingdom) for such a ith (time) as this?
Then Asathar asked them to shawab (turn back / repent) Maradakay,

"yalak (go), gather together all the Yahawaday (Jews) who are matzaa (present) in Shawashan, and fast for me, and neither akal (eat) nor drink shalawash (three) yawam (days), layal (night) or yawam (day). I and my maidens will also fast the Kan way. Then I will bawaa (go) in to the malak (king), which is against the dath (law); and if I abad (perish), I abad (perish).
So Maradakay went his ibar (way), and did according to all that Asathar had tzawah (commanded) him.

Now it happened on the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) that Asathar Labash on her malakawath (royal) clothing, and stood Panayamay the inner court of the malak (king's) bayath (house), next to the malak (king's) bayath (house). The malak (king) sat on his malakawath (royal) kasaa (throne) in the malakawath (royal) bayath (house), next to the entrance of the bayath (house).

When the malak (king) saw Asathar the malakah (queen) standing in the court, she obtained favor in his iyan (sight); and the malak (king) held out to Asathar the golden scepter that was in his yad (hand). So Asathar came qarab (near), and touched the raash (top) of the scepter.
Then the malak (king) asked her, "What would you like, malakah (queen) Asathar? What is your request? It shall be given you even to the chatzay (half) of the malakawath (kingdom).
Asathar said, "If it seems tawab (good) to the malak (king), let the malak (king) and Haman bawaa (come) today to the banquet that I have prepared for him.
Then the malak (king) said, "Bring Haman quickly, so that it may be done as Asathar has dabar (said)." So the malak (king) and Haman came to the banquet that Asathar had prepared.

The malak (king) said to Asathar at the banquet of yayan (wine), "What is your petition? It shall be granted you. What is your request? Even to the chatzay (half) of the malakawath (kingdom) it shall be performed.
Then Asathar answered and said, "My petition and my request is this.

If I have found favor in the iyan (sight) of the malak (king), and if it tawab (please) the malak (king) to nathan (grant) my petition and to ishah (perform) my request, let the malak (king) and Haman bawaa (come) to the banquet that I will ishah (prepare) for them, and I will do tomorrow as the malak (king) has dabar (said).

Then Haman went out that yawam (day) Shamach and tawab (glad) of lab (heart), but when Haman saw Maradakay in the malak (king's) gate, that he didn't qawam (stand) up nor move Haman him, he was filled with chamah (wrath) against Maradakay.
Nevertheless Haman restrained himself, and went bayath (home). There, he sent and called for his ahab (friends) and Zarash his ashah (wife).

Haman recounted to them the kabawad (glory) of his riches, the multitude of his children, all the things in which the malak (king) had promoted him, and how he had advanced him above the shar (princes) and ibad (servants) of the malak (king).

Haman also said, "Yes, Asathar the malakah (queen) let no man bawaa (come) in with the malak (king) to the banquet that she had prepared but myself; and tomorrow I am also invited by her together with the malak (king).
Yet all this avails me nothing, so ith (long) as I raah (see) Maradakay the Yahawaday (Jew) sitting at the malak (king's) gate.

Then Zarash his ashah (wife) and all his ahab (friends) said to him, "Let a itz (gallows) be made chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits) Gabah, and in the baqar (morning) amar (speak) to the malak (king) about hanging Maradakay on it. Then bawaa (go) Shamach merrily with the malak (king) to the banquet." This pleased Haman, so he had the itz (gallows) made.
On that layal (night), the malak (king) couldn't shanah (sleep). He commanded the book of zakarawan (records) of the dabar (chronicles) to be brought, and they were qaraa (read) to the malak (king).

It was found written that Maradakay had told of Bagathan and Tharash, shanayam (two) of the malak (king's) eunuchs, who were doorkeepers, who had tried to shalach (lay) yad (hands) on the malak (king) Achashawarawash.
The malak (king) said, "What honor and dignity has been bestowed on Maradakay for this?" Then the malak (king's) nair (servants) who attended him said, "Nothing has been done for him.

The malak (king) said, "Who is in the court?" Now Haman had bawaa (come) into the Chayatzawan court of the malak (king's) bayath (house), to amar (speak) to the malak (king) about hanging Maradakay on the itz (gallows) that he had prepared for him.
The malak (king's) nair (servants) said to him, "Behold, Haman imad (stands) in the court." The malak (king) said, "Let him bawaa (come) in.

So Haman came in. The malak (king) said to him, "What shall be done to the ayash (man) whom the malak (king) delights to honor?" Now Haman said in his lab (heart), "Who would the malak (king) delight to honor more than myself?
Haman said to the malak (king), "For the ayash (man) whom the malak (king) delights to honor,

let malakawath (royal) clothing be brought which the malak (king) uses to Labash, and the horse that the malak (king) rides on, and on the raash (head) of which a kathar (crown) malakawath (royal) is nathan (set).

Let the clothing and the horse be delivered to the yad (hand) of one of the malak (king's) most paratham (noble) shar (princes), that they may Labash the ayash (man) whom the malak (king) delights to honor with them, and have him ride on horseback through the Iyar square, and qaraa (proclaim) panayam (before) him, ‘Thus shall it be done to the ayash (man) whom the malak (king) delights to honor!'

Then the malak (king) said to Haman, "Hurry and take the clothing and the horse, as you have said, and do this for Maradakay the Yahawaday (Jew), who yashab (sits) at the malak (king's) gate. Let nothing napal (fail) of all that you have spoken.

Then Haman took the clothing and the horse, and Labash Maradakay, and had him ride through the Iyar square, and proclaimed panayam (before) him, "Thus shall it be done to the ayash (man) whom the malak (king) delights to honor!
Maradakay came shawab (turn back / repent) to the malak (king's) gate, but Haman hurried to his bayath (house), Abal and having his raash (head) covered.

Haman recounted to Zarash his ashah (wife) and all his ahab (friends) everything that had happened to him. Then his chakam (wise) men and Zarash his ashah (wife) said to him, "If Maradakay, panayam (before) whom you have begun to napal (fall), is Yahawaday Jewish descent, you will not yakal (prevail) against him, but you will napal (surely) napal (fall) panayam (before) him.
While they were yet talking with him, the malak (king's) eunuchs came, and hurried to bawaa (bring) Haman to the banquet that Asathar had prepared.
So the malak (king) and Haman came to banquet with Asathar the malakah (queen).

The malak (king) said again to Asathar on the shanay (second) yawam (day) at the banquet of yayan (wine), "What is your petition, malakah (queen) Asathar? It shall be granted you. What is your request? Even to the chatzay (half) of the malakawath (kingdom) it shall be performed.

Then Asathar the malakah (queen) answered, "If I have found favor in your iyan (sight), O malak (king), and if it tawab (please) the malak (king), let my napash (life) be given me at my petition, and my im (people) at my request.

For we are sold, I and my im (people), to be destroyed, to be slain, and to abad (perish). But if we had been sold for ibad (bondservants) and bondmaids, I would have held my charash (peace), although the tzar (adversary) could not have compensated for the malak (king's) loss.
Then malak (king) Achashawarawash said to Asathar the malakah (queen), "Who is he, and where is he who dared malaa (presume) in his lab (heart) to do so?
Asathar said, "An adversary and an ayab (enemy), even this rai (wicked) Haman!" Then Haman was afraid panayam (before) the malak (king) and the malakah (queen).

The malak (king) qawam (arose) in his chamah (wrath) from the banquet of yayan (wine) and went into the palace garden. Haman stood up to make request for his napash (life) to Asathar the malakah (queen); for he saw that there was rai (evil) determined against him by the malak (king).

Then the malak (king) returned out of the palace garden into the bayath (place) of the banquet of yayan (wine); and Haman had fallen on the couch where Asathar was. Then the malak (king) said, "Will he even assault the malakah (queen) in front of me in the bayath (house)?" As the dabar (word) went out of the malak (king's) pah (mouth), they covered Haman panayam (face).

Then Charabawanaa, one of the eunuchs who were with the malak (king) said, "Behold, the itz (gallows) chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits) Gabah, which Haman has made for Maradakay, who spoke tawab (good) for the malak (king), is standing at Haman bayath (house)." The malak (king) said, "Hang him on it!
So they hanged Haman on the itz (gallows) that he had prepared for Maradakay. Then was the malak (king's) chamah (wrath) pacified.

On that yawam (day), malak (king) Achashawarawash gave the bayath (house) of Haman, the Yahawaday (Jews)' tzarar (enemy), to Asathar the malakah (queen). Maradakay came panayam (before) the malak (king); for Asathar had told what he was to her.
The malak (king) took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Maradakay. Asathar shawam (set) Maradakay over the bayath (house) of Haman.

Asathar spoke yet again panayam (before) the malak (king), and napal (fell) down at his feet, and begged him with tears to ibar (put) away the rai (mischief) of Haman the Agagay, and his machashabah (device) that he had devised against the Yahawaday (Jews).
Then the malak (king) held out to Asathar the golden scepter. So Asathar qawam (arose), and stood panayam (before) the malak (king).

She said, "If it pleases the malak (king), and if I have found favor in his panayam (sight), and the thing seem kashar (right) to the malak (king), and I am pleasing in his iyan (eyes), let it be written to shawab (turn back / repent) the letters machashabah (devised) by Haman, the ban (son) of Madathaa the Agagay, which he wrote to abad (destroy) the Yahawaday (Jews) who are in all the malak (king's) provinces.
For how can I yakal (endure) to raah (see) the rai (evil) that would matzaa (come) to my im (people)? How can I yakal (endure) to raah (see) the destruction of my relatives?

Then malak (king) Achashawarawash said to Asathar the malakah (queen) and to Maradakay the Yahawaday (Jew), "See, I have given Asathar the bayath (house) of Haman, and him they have hanged on the itz (gallows), because he laid his yad (hand) on the Yahawaday (Jews).

kathab (write) also to the Yahawaday (Jews), as it pleases you, in the malak (king's) sham (name), and seal it with the malak (king's) ring; for the writing which is written in the malak (king's) sham (name), and sealed with the malak (king's) ring, may not be reversed by any man.

Then the malak (king's) scribes were called at that ith (time), in the shalayashay (third) chadash (month) Sayawan, on the isharayam (twenty) - third day of the chadash (month); and it was written according to all that Maradakay tzawah (commanded) to the Yahawaday (Jews), and to the satraps, and the governors and shar (princes) of the provinces which are from Hadaw to Kawash, one maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shabai (seven) provinces, to every province according to its writing, and to every im (people) in their lashawan (language), and to the Yahawaday (Jews) in their writing, and in their lashawan (language).

He wrote in the sham (name) of malak (king) Achashawarawash, and sealed it with the malak (king's) ring, and sent letters by courier on horseback, riding on royal horses that were bread from swift steeds.

In those letters, the malak (king) granted the Yahawaday (Jews) who were in every Iyar to gather themselves together, and to defend their napash (life), to destroy, to harag (kill), and to cause to abad (perish), all the chayal (power) of the im (people) and province that would tzawar (assault) them, their little ones and women, and to plunder their bazaz (possessions),
on one yawam (day) in all the provinces of malak (king) Achashawarawash, on the thirteenth day of the shanayam (twelfth) chadash (month), which is the chadash (month) Adar.

A copy of the letter, that the dath (decree) should be given out in every province, was published to all the im (peoples), that the Yahawaday (Jews) should be Ithayad for that yawam (day) to avenge themselves on their ayab (enemies).
So the couriers who rode Achashatharan royal horses went out, hastened and pressed on by the malak (king's) commandment. The dabar (decree) was given out in the citadel Shawashan Susa.

Maradakay went out of the panayam (presence) of the malak (king) in malakawath (royal) clothing of blue and white, and with a gadawal (great) itarah (crown) of gold, and with a robe of fine linen and purple; and the Iyar Shawashan Susa shouted and was Shamach.
The Yahawaday (Jews) had awarah (light), gladness, joy, and honor.

In every province, and in every Iyar, wherever the malak (king's) commandment and his dabar (decree) came, the Yahawaday (Jews) had gladness, joy, a feast, and a tawab (good) yawam (day). Many from among the im (peoples) of the aratz (land) became Jews; for the pachad (fear) of the Jews was fallen on them.

Now in the shanayam (twelfth) chadash (month), which is the chadash (month) Adar, on the thirteenth yawam (day) of the month, when the malak (king's) commandment and his dath (decree) drew nagai (near) to be ishah (put) in execution, on the yawam (day) that the ayab (enemies) of the Yahawaday (Jews) hoped to conquer them, (but it was turned out the opposite happened, that the Yahawaday (Jews) conquered those who hated them),

the Yahawaday (Jews) gathered themselves together in their Iyar throughout all the provinces of the malak (king) Achashawarawash, to shalach (lay) yad (hands) on those who wanted to rai (harm) them. No one could withstand them, because the pachad (fear) of them had fallen on all the im (people).

All the shar (princes) of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and those who did the malak (king's) business helped the Yahawaday (Jews), because the pachad (fear) of Maradakay had fallen on them.
For Maradakay was gadawal (great) in the malak (king's) bayath (house), and his fame went out throughout all the provinces; for the ayash (man) Maradakay grew greater and greater.
The Yahawaday (Jews) struck all their ayab (enemies) with the makah (stroke) of the charab (sword), and with slaughter and destruction, and did what they wanted to those who hated them.
In the citadel Shawashan Susa, the Yahawaday (Jews) killed and destroyed chamash (five) maah (hundred) men.
They killed Parashanadathaa, Dalapawan, Asapathaa,
Pawarathaa, Adalayaa, Arayadathaa,
Paramashathaa, Arayasay, Arayaday, and Wayazathaa,
the ishar (ten) ban (sons) of Haman the ban (son) of Madathaa, the Yahawaday tzarar (enemy), but they didn't shalach (lay) their yad (hand) on the plunder.
On that yawam (day), the number of those who were slain in the citadel Shawashan Susa was brought panayam (before) the malak (king).

The malak (king) said to Asathar the malakah (queen), "The Yahawaday (Jews) have slain and destroyed chamash (five) maah (hundred) men in the citadel Shawashan Susa, including the ishar (ten) ban (sons) of Haman; what then have they done in the shaar (rest) of the malak (king's) provinces! Now what is your petition? It shall be granted you. What is your iwad (further) request? It shall be done.

Then Asathar said, "If it pleases the malak (king), let it be granted to the Yahawaday (Jews) who are in Shawashan to do tomorrow also according to this yawam (day's) dath (decree), and let Haman ishar (ten) ban (sons) be hanged on the itz (gallows).
The malak (king) commanded this to be done. A decree was given out in Shawashan; and they hanged Haman ishar (ten) ban (sons).

The Yahawaday (Jews) who were in Shawashan gathered themselves together on the fourteenth yawam (day) also of the chadash (month) Adar, and killed shalawash (three) maah (hundred) men in Shawashan; but they didn't shalach (lay) their yad (hand) on the spoil.

The other Yahawaday (Jews) who were in the malak (king's) provinces gathered themselves together, defended their lives, had nawach (rest) from their ayab (enemies), and killed shabaiyam (seventy) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) of those who hated them; but they didn't shalach (lay) their yad (hand) on the plunder.
This was done on the thirteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month) Adar; and on the fourteenth day of that month they rested and made it a yawam (day) of feasting and gladness.

But the Yahawaday (Jews) who were in Shawashan assembled together on the thirteenth and on the fourteenth days of the month; and on the fifteenth day of that month, they rested, and made it a yawam (day) of feasting and gladness.

Therefore the Yahawaday (Jews) of the villages, who live in the unwalled Iyar, ishah (make) the fourteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month) Adar a shamachah (day) of gladness and feasting, a tawab (good) yawam (day), and a yawam (day) of sending presents of food to one rai (another).
Maradakay wrote these things, and sent letters to all the Yahawaday (Jews) who were in all the provinces of the malak (king) Achashawarawash, both qarawab (near) and Rachawaq,
to qawam (enjoin) them that they should ishah (keep) the fourteenth and fifteenth yawam (days) of the chadash (month) Adar Shanah,

as the yawam (days) in which the Yahawaday (Jews) had nawach (rest) from their ayab (enemies), and the chadash (month) which was turned to them from sorrow to gladness, and from mourning into a tawab (good) yawam (day); that they should ishah (make) them yawam (days) of feasting and gladness, and of sending presents of food to one rai (another), and mathanah (gifts) to the Abayawan.
The Yahawaday (Jews) accepted the custom that they had begun, as Maradakay had written to them;

because Haman the ban (son) of Madathaa, the Agagay, the tzarar (enemy) of all the Yahawaday (Jews), had plotted against the Yahawaday (Jews) to abad (destroy) them, and had napal (cast) "Pawar," that is the lot, to hamam (consume) them, and to abad (destroy) them;

but when this became known to the malak (king), he commanded by letters that his rai (wicked) machashabah (device), which he had devised against the Yahawaday (Jews), should shawab (turn back / repent) on his own raash (head), and that he and his ban (sons) should be hanged on the itz (gallows).

Therefore they called these yawam (days) "Pawar," from the word "Pawar." Therefore because of all the dabar (words) of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and that which had nagai (come) to them,

the Yahawaday (Jews) established, and imposed on themselves, and on their descendants, and on all those who joined themselves to them, so that it should not ibar (fail), that they would ishah (keep) these shanayam (two) yawam (days) according to what was written, and according to its appointed time, every Shanah;

and that these yawam (days) should be zakar (remembered) and kept throughout every dawar (generation), every mashapachah (family), every province, and every Iyar; and that these yawam (days) of Pawar should not ibar (fail) from among the Yahawaday (Jews), nor their zakar (memory) sawap (perish) from their zarai (seed).
Then Asathar the malakah (queen), the bath (daughter) of Abayahayal, and Maradakay the Yahawaday (Jew), wrote with all thaqap (authority) to qawam (confirm) this shanay (second) letter of Pawar.

He sent letters to all the Yahawaday (Jews), to the maah (hundred) isharayam (twenty) - shabai (seven) provinces of the malakawath (kingdom) of Achashawarawash, with dabar (words) of shalawam (peace) and truth,

to qawam (confirm) these yawam (days) of Pawar in their appointed times, as Maradakay the Yahawaday (Jew) and Asathar the malakah (queen) had decreed, and as they had imposed upon themselves and their descendants, in the dabar (matter) of the fastings and their cry.
The commandment of Asathar confirmed these dabar (matters) of Pawar; and it was written in the book.
malak (king) Achashawarawash laid a tribute on the aratz (land), and on the islands of the yam (sea).

All the maishah (acts) of his thaqap (power) and of his might, and the full account of the greatness of Maradakay, to which the malak (king) advanced him, aren't they written in the book of the dabar (chronicles) of the malak (kings) of Maday and Paras?

For Maradakay the Yahawaday (Jew) was mashanah (next) to malak (king) Achashawarawash, and gadawal (great) among the Yahawaday (Jews), and accepted by the multitude of his ach (brothers), seeking the tawab (good) of his im (people), and speaking shalawam (peace) to all his descendants.
There was a ayash (man) in the aratz (land) of Iwatz, whose sham (name) was Ayawab. That ayash (man) was blameless and yashar (upright), and one who feared Alahayam, and turned away from rai (evil).
There were yalad (born) to him shabai (seven) ban (sons) and shalawash (three) bath (daughters).

His maqanah (possessions) also were shabai (seven) alap (thousand) sheep, shalawash (three) alap (thousand) camels, chamash (five) maah (hundred) tzamad (yoke) of oxen, chamash (five) maah (hundred) female donkeys, and a very rab (great) ibadah (household); so that this ayash (man) was the greatest of all the children of the qadam (east).
His ban (sons) went and held a feast in the house of ayash (each) one on his birthday; and they sent and called for their shalawash (three) achawath (sisters) to akal (eat) and to drink with them.

It was so, when the yawam (days) of their feasting had run their course, that Ayawab sent and sanctified them, and rose up shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), and offered burnt ilah (offerings) according to the number of them all. For Ayawab said, "It may be that my ban (sons) have sinned, and renounced Alahayam in their labab (hearts)." Ayawab did this yawam (continually).
Now it happened on the yawam (day) when alahayam (god's) ban (sons) came to present themselves before Yahawah, that shatan (satan) also came among them.

Yahawah said to shatan (satan), "Where have you bawaa (come) from?" Then shatan (satan) answered Yahawah, and said, "From going back and forth in the aratz (earth), and from walking up and down in it.

Yahawah said to shatan (satan), "Have you considered my ibad (servant), Ayawab? For there is none like him in the aratz (earth), a blameless and an yashar (upright) ayash (man), one who yaraa (fears) Alahayam, and turns away from rai (evil).
Then shatan (satan) answered Yahawah, and said, "Does Ayawab yaraa (fear) Alahayam for nothing?

Haven't you made a hedge around him, and around his bayath (house), and around all that he has, on every side? You have blessed the maishah (work) of his yad (hands), and his maqanah (substance) is increased in the aratz (land).
But shalach (put) forth your yad (hand) now, and nagai (touch) all that he has, and he will renounce you to your panayam (face).

Yahawah said to shatan (satan), "Behold, all that he has is in your yad (power). Only on himself don't shalach (put) forth your yad (hand)." So shatan (satan) went shalach (forth) from the panayam (presence) of Yahawah.
It fell on a yawam (day) when his ban (sons) and his bath (daughters) were eating and drinking yayan (wine) in their eldest ach (brother's) bayath (house),
that there came a malaak (messenger) to Ayawab, and said, "The oxen were plowing, and the donkeys feeding yad (beside) them,
and the Shabaa (Sabeans) attacked, and took them away. Yes, they have killed the nair (servants) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword), and I malat (alone) have escaped to nagad (tell) you.

While he was still speaking, there also came another, and said, "The ash (fire) of Alahayam has fallen from the sky, and has burned up the sheep and the nair (servants), and consumed them, and I malat (alone) have escaped to nagad (tell) you.

While he was still speaking, there came also another, and said, "The Kashaday (Chaldeans) made shalawash (three) raash (bands), and swept down on the camels, and have taken them away, yes, and killed the nair (servants) with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); and I malat (alone) have escaped to nagad (tell) you.
While he was still speaking, there came also another, and said, "Your ban (sons) and your bath (daughters) were eating and drinking yayan (wine) in their eldest ach (brother's) bayath (house),

and behold, there came a gadawal (great) rawach (wind) from the madabar (wilderness), and struck the arabai (four) corners of the bayath (house), and it napal (fell) on the nair (young) men, and they are mawath (dead). I malat (alone) have escaped to nagad (tell) you.
Then Ayawab qawam (arose), and tore his robe, and shaved his raash (head), and napal (fell) down on the aratz (ground), and worshiped.
He said, "Irawam I came out of my am (mother's) womb, and Irawam shall I shawab (turn back / repent) there. Yahawah gave, and Yahawah has taken away. Blessed be the sham (name) of Yahawah.
In all this, Ayawab did not chataa (sin), nor nathan (charge) Alahayam with wrongdoing.
Again it happened on the yawam (day) when the alahayam (god's) ban (sons) came to present themselves before Yahawah, that shatan (satan) came also among them to present himself before Yahawah.
Yahawah said to shatan (satan), "Where have you bawaa (come) from?" shatan (satan) answered Yahawah, and said, "From going back and forth in the aratz (earth), and from walking up and down in it.

Yahawah said to shatan (satan), "Have you lab (considered) my ibad (servant) Ayawab? For there is none like him in the aratz (earth), a blameless and an yashar (upright) ayash (man), one who yaraa (fears) Alahayam, and sawar (turns) away from rai (evil). He still chazaq (maintains) his integrity, although you incited me against him, to ruin him without cause.
shatan (satan) answered Yahawah, and said, "Skin for skin. Yes, all that a ayash (man) has he will nathan (give) for his napash (life).
But shalach (put) forth your yad (hand) now, and nagai (touch) his itzam (bone) and his flesh, and he will renounce you to your panayam (face).
Yahawah said to shatan (satan), "Behold, he is in your yad (hand). Only spare his napash (life).
So shatan (satan) went yatzaa (forth) from the panayam (presence) of Yahawah, and struck Ayawab with painful sores from the kap (sole) of his ragal (foot) to his qadaqad (head).
He took for himself a charash (potsherd) to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.
Then his ashah (wife) said to him, "Do you still chazaq (maintain) your integrity? Renounce Alahayam, and mawath (die).

But he said to her, "You dabar (speak) as one of the foolish women would dabar (speak). What? Shall we receive tawab (good) at the hand of Alahayam, and shall we not receive rai (evil)?" In all this Ayawab didn't chataa (sin) with his shapah (lips).

Now when Ayawab shalawash (three) rai (friends) heard of all this rai (evil) that had bawaa (come) on him, they ayash (each) came from his own place: Alayapaz the Thayamanay, Baladad the Shawachay, and Tzawapar the Naimathay, and they made an appointment together to bawaa (come) to sympathize with him and to nacham (comfort) him.

When they lifted up their iyan (eyes) Rachawaq a distance, and didn't recognize him, they raised their qawal (voices), and wept; and they ayash (each) tore his robe, and sprinkled ipar (dust) on their raash (heads) toward the sky.
So they sat down with him on the aratz (ground) shabai (seven) yawam (days) and shabai (seven) layal (nights), and none spoke a dabar (word) to him, for they saw that his grief was very great.
achar (after) this Ayawab opened his pah (mouth), and cursed the yawam (day) of his birth.
Then Ayawab answered and said:
"Let the yawam (day) abad (perish) in which I was yalad (born), the layal (night) which said, ‘There is a boy conceived.'
Let that yawam (day) be chashak (darkness). Don't let Alawah from above seek for it, neither let the naharah (light) yapai (shine) on it.
Let chashak (darkness) and the shadow of tzalamawath (death) claim it for their own. Let a cloud shakan (dwell) on it. Let all that makes black the yawam (day) terrify it.
As for that layal (night), let thick apal (darkness) seize on it. Let it not rejoice among the yawam (days) of the Shanah. Let it not bawaa (come) into the number of the yarach (months).
Behold, let that layal (night) be Galamawad. Let no joyful rananah (voice) bawaa (come) therein.
Let them naqab (curse) it who arar (curse) the yawam (day), who are Ithayad to rouse up leviathan.
Let the kawakab (stars) of its nashap (twilight) be chashak (dark). Let it look for awar (light), but have none, neither let it raah (see) the ipaip (eyelids) of the shachar (morning),
because it didn't shut up the doors of my batan (mother's) womb, nor did it hide imal (trouble) from my iyan (eyes).
"Why didn't I mawath (die) from the womb? Why didn't I gawai (give) up the spirit when my batan (mother) bore me?
Why did the knees receive me? Or why the breast, that I should nurse?
For now should I have lain down and been shaqat (quiet). I should have slept, then I would have been at nawach (rest),
with malak (kings) and yaitz (counselors) of the aratz (earth), who built up waste places for themselves;
or with shar (princes) who had gold, who filled their bayath (houses) with kasap (silver):
or as a hidden untimely birth I had not been, as infants who never saw awar (light).
There the rashai (wicked) chadal (cease) from ragaz (troubling). There the Yagayai are at nawach (rest).
There the prisoners are at shaan (ease) together. They don't hear the qawal (voice) of the taskmaster.
The qatan (small) and the gadawal (great) are there. The ibad (servant) is Chapashay from his adawan (master).
"Why is awar (light) given to him who is in imal (misery), chay (life) to the Mar in napash (soul),
Who long for mawath (death), but it doesn't come; and dig for it more than for hidden treasures,
