who Shamach exceedingly, and are glad, when they can matzaa (find) the qabar (grave)?
Why is light given to a gabar (man) whose darak (way) is hidden, whom Alawah has hedged in?
For my sighing bawaa (comes) panayam (before) I lacham (eat). My groanings are poured out like mayam (water).
For the thing which I pachad (fear) comes on me, That which I am yagar (afraid) of bawaa (comes) to me.
I am not at ease, neither am I shaqat (quiet), neither have I shaqat (rest); but ragaz (trouble) bawaa (comes).
Then Alayapaz the Thayamanay answered,
"If someone ventures to dabar (talk) with you, will you be grieved? But who can itzar (withhold) himself from malah (speaking)?
Behold, you have instructed many, you have strengthened the Rapah yad (hands).
Your malah (words) have supported him who was falling, You have made firm the feeble knees.
But now it has bawaa (come) to you, and you faint. It touches you, and you are troubled.
Isn't your piety your confidence? Isn't the tham (integrity) of your darak (ways) your hope?
"zakar (remember), now, whoever perished, being naqay (innocent)? Or where were the yashar (upright) cut off?
According to what I have seen, those who charash (plow) awan (iniquity), and zarai (sow) imal (trouble), reap the same.
By the nashamah (breath) of Alawah they abad (perish). By the rawach (blast) of his ap (anger) are they consumed.
The roaring of the aray (lion), and the qawal (voice) of the fierce shachal (lion), the teeth of the young kapayar (lions), are broken.
The old layash (lion) perishes for lack of Tarap. The cubs of the labayaa (lioness) are scattered abroad.
"Now a thing was secretly brought to me. My ear received a whisper of it.
In thoughts from the visions of the layal (night), when tharadamah (deep) sleep napal (falls) on men,
pachad (fear) came on me, and trembling, which made all my itzam (bones) pachad (shake).
Then a rawach (spirit) passed before my panayam (face). The hair of my flesh stood up.
It stood still, but I couldn't nakar (discern) its appearance. A form was before my iyan (eyes). Silence, then I heard a qawal (voice), saying,
‘Shall mortal anawash (man) be more tzadaq (just) than Alawah? Shall a gabar (man) be more pure than his Maker?
Behold, he puts no aman (trust) in his ibad (servants). He shawam (charges) his malaak (angels) with error.
How much more, those who shakan (dwell) in bayath (houses) of clay, whose yasawad (foundation) is in the ipar (dust), who are crushed panayam (before) the moth!
Between baqar (morning) and evening they are destroyed. They abad (perish) forever without any regarding it.
Isn't their tent yathar (cord) plucked up within them? They mawath (die), and that without chakamah (wisdom).'
"qaraa (call) now; is there any who will answer you? To which of the qadawash (holy) ones will you panah (turn)?
For resentment harag (kills) the Awayal man, and jealousy mawath (kills) the simple.
I have seen the Awayal taking root, but suddenly I cursed his Nawah.
His children are rachaq (far) from yashai (safety). They are crushed in the gate. Neither is there any to natzal (deliver) them,
whose harvest the Raib akal (eats) up, and take it even out of the thorns. The snare gapes for their chayal (substance).
For awan (affliction) doesn't yatzaa (come) forth from the ipar (dust), neither does imal (trouble) spring out of the adamah (ground);
but adam (man) is yalad (born) to imal (trouble), as the ban (sparks) fly upward.
"But as for me, I would seek Alahayam. I would shawam (commit) my cause to Alahayam,
who does gadawal (great) things that can't be fathomed, palaa (marvelous) things without number;
who nathan (gives) rain on the aratz (earth), and shalach (sends) mayam (waters) on the fields;
so that he shawam (sets) up on high those who are Shapal, those who mourn are exalted to yashai (safety).
He parar (frustrates) the machashabah (devices) of the Irawam, So that their yad (hands) can't ishah (perform) their thawashayah (enterprise).
He takes the chakam (wise) in their own craftiness; the itzah (counsel) of the cunning is carried headlong.
They meet with chashak (darkness) in the yawamam (day) time, and grope at noonday as in the layal (night).
But he yashai (saves) from the charab (sword) of their pah (mouth), even the Abayawan from the yad (hand) of the chazaq (mighty).
So the Dal has hope, and injustice qapatz (shuts) her pah (mouth).
"Behold, happy is the anawash (man) whom Alawah yakach (corrects). Therefore do not despise the chastening of the Shaday.
For he wounds, and binds up. He injures, and his yad (hands) make whole.
He will natzal (deliver) you in shash (six) tzarah (troubles); yes, in shabai (seven) no rai (evil) shall nagai (touch) you.
In famine he will padah (redeem) you from mawath (death); in war, from the yad (power) of the charab (sword).
You shall be hidden from the scourge of the lashawan (tongue), neither shall you be yaraa (afraid) of destruction when it bawaa (comes).
At destruction and famine you shall laugh, neither shall you be yaraa (afraid) of the animals of the aratz (earth).
For you shall be allied with the aban (stones) of the shadah (field). The animals of the shadah (field) shall be at shalam (peace) with you.
You shall yadai (know) that your ahal (tent) is in shalawam (peace). You shall paqad (visit) your Nawah, and shall chataa (miss) nothing.
You shall yadai (know) also that your zarai (seed) shall be rab (great), Your tzaatzaa (offspring) as the grass of the aratz (earth).
You shall bawaa (come) to your qabar (grave) in a full age, like a shock of grain ilah (comes) in its ith (season).
Look this, we have searched it, so it is. Hear it, and yadai (know) it for your good.
Then Ayawab answered,
"Oh that my anguish were weighed, and all my hawah (calamity) laid in the balances!
For now it would be kabad (heavier) than the sand of the yam (seas), therefore have my dabar (words) been rash.
For the chatz (arrows) of the Shaday are within me. My rawach (spirit) drinks up their chamah (poison). The terrors of Alawah set themselves in array against me.
Does the wild donkey bray when he has grass? Or does the ox low over his fodder?
Can that which has no Thapal be eaten without Malach? Or is there any taim (taste) in the white of an egg?
My napash (soul) refuses to nagai (touch) them. They are as loathsome lacham (food) to me.
"Oh that I might have my request, that Alawah would nathan (grant) the thing that I long for,
even that it would please Alawah to dakaa (crush) me; that he would let loose his yad (hand), and cut me off!
Be it still my consolation, yes, let me exult in pain that doesn't spare, that I have not denied the amar (words) of the qadawash (holy) One.
What is my kach (strength), that I should wait? What is my end, that I should be patient?
Is my kach (strength) the kach (strength) of aban (stones)? Or is my flesh of Nachawash?
Isn't it that I have no help in me, That thawashayah (wisdom) is driven quite from me?
"Mas him who is ready to faint, chasad (kindness) should be shown from his rai (friend); even to him who forsakes the yaraah (fear) of the Shaday.
My ach (brothers) have dealt bagad (deceitfully) as a nachal (brook), as the apayaq (channel) of nachal (brooks) that ibar (pass) away;
Which are black by reason of the ice, in which the snow ilam (hides) itself.
In the dry ith (season), they tzamath (vanish). When it is hot, they are consumed out of their place.
The caravans that travel beside them lapath (turn) aside. They ilah (go) up into the thahaw (waste), and abad (perish).
The caravans of Thayamaa looked. The halayakah (companies) of Shabaa waited for them.
They were distressed because they were batach (confident). They came there, and were chapar (confounded).
For now you are nothing. You raah (see) a terror, and are yaraa (afraid).
Did I amar (say), ‘Give to me?' or, ‘Offer a present for me from your kach (substance)?'
or, ‘malat (deliver) me from the tzar (adversary's) yad (hand)?' or, ‘padah (redeem) me from the yad (hand) of the irayatz (oppressors)?'
"Teach me, and I will hold my charash (peace). bayan (cause) me to understand wherein I have erred.
How forcible are amar (words) of yashar (uprightness)! But your reproof, what does it yakach (reprove)?
Do you intend to yakach (reprove) malah (words), since the speeches of yaash (one) who is desperate are as rawach (wind)?
Yes, you would even napal (cast) lots for the fatherless, and make merchandise of your rai (friend).
Now therefore be pleased to panah (look) at me, for surely I shall not lie to your kazab (face).
Please shawab (turn back / repent). Let there be no injustice. Yes, shawab (turn back / repent) again. My tzadaq (cause) is righteous.
Is there injustice on my lashawan (tongue)? Can't my chak (taste) bayan (discern) hawah (mischievous) things?
"Isn't a anawash (man) forced to labor on aratz (earth)? Aren't his yawam (days) like the yawam (days) of a shakayar (hired) hand?
As a ibad (servant) who earnestly desires the shadow, as a shakayar (hireling) who looks for his wages,
so am I nachal (made) to possess yarach (months) of misery, imal (wearisome) layal (nights) are appointed to me.
When I shakab (lie) down, I amar (say), ‘When shall I qawam (arise), and the irab (night) be gone?' I toss and nadad (turn) until the dawning of the nashap (day).
My flesh is Labash with worms and clods of ipar (dust). My skin closes up, and ragai (breaks) out afresh.
My yawam (days) are qalal (swifter) than a weaver's shuttle, and are spent apas (without) hope.
Oh zakar (remember) that my chay (life) is a rawach (breath). My iyan (eye) shall no more raah (see) tawab (good).
The iyan (eye) of him who sees me shall see me no more. Your iyan (eyes) shall be on me, but I shall not be.
As the cloud is consumed and vanishes yalak (away), so he who goes down to shaawal (sheol) shall ilah (come) up no more.
He shall shawab (turn back / repent) no more to his bayath (house), neither shall his place nakar (know) him any more.
"Therefore I will not keep silent. I will dabar (speak) in the tzar (anguish) of my rawach (spirit). I will complain Mar the bitterness of my napash (soul).
Am I a yam (sea), or a thanayan (sea) monster, that you shawam (put) a guard over me?
When I amar (say), ‘My bed shall nacham (comfort) me. My couch shall nashaa (ease) my complaint;'
then you chathath (scare) me with chalawam (dreams), and terrify me through visions:
so that my napash (soul) chooses strangling, mawath (death) rather than my itzam (bones).
I loathe my chayah (life). I don't want to live iwalam (forever). Leave me chadal (alone), for my yawam (days) are but a habal (breath).
What is anawash (man), that you should magnify him, that you should shayath (set) your lab (mind) on him,
that you should paqad (visit) him every baqar (morning), and test him every moment?
mah (how) long will you not shaih (look) away from me, nor leave me rapah (alone) until I balai (swallow) down my spittle?
If I have sinned, what do I do to you, you watcher of men? Why have you shawam (set) me as a mark for you, so that I am a mashaa (burden) to myself?

Why do you not nashaa (pardon) my disobedience, and ibar (take) away my iwan (iniquity)? For now shall I shakab (lie) down in the ipar (dust). You will shachar (seek) me diligently, but I shall not be.
Then Baladad the Shawachay answered,
"How long will you speak these things? Shall the amar (words) of your pah (mouth) be a kabayar (mighty) rawach (wind)?
Does Al iwath (pervert) justice? Or does the Shaday iwath (pervert) tzadaq (righteousness)?
If your children have sinned against him, He has delivered them into the hand of their disobedience.
If you want to shachar (seek) Al shachar (diligently), chanan (make) your supplication to the Shaday.
If you were zak (pure) and yashar (upright), surely now he would awaken for you, and make the Nawah of your tzadaq (righteousness) shalam (prosperous).
Though your raashayath (beginning) was small, yet your acharayath (latter) end would maad (greatly) increase.
"Please inquire of raashawan (past) dawar (generations). Find out about the learning of their abawath (fathers).
(For we are but of thamawal (yesterday), and yadai (know) nothing, because our yawam (days) on aratz (earth) are a shadow.)
Shall they not teach you, amar (tell) you, and yatzaa (utter) malah (words) out of their lab (heart)?
"Can the papyrus grow up without mire? Can the rushes grow without mayam (water)?
While it is yet in its greenness, not cut down, it yabash (withers) panayam (before) any other reed.
So are the arach (paths) of all who forget Al. The hope of the godless man shall abad (perish),
Whose confidence shall break apart, Whose trust is a spider's bayath (web).
He shall shain (lean) on his bayath (house), but it shall not imad (stand). He shall cling to it, but it shall not qawam (endure).
He is Ratab panayam (before) the shamash (sun). His shoots yatzaa (go) forth over his garden.
His roots are wrapped around the rock pile. He chazah (sees) the bayath (place) of aban (stones).
If he is destroyed from his place, then it shall deny him, saying, ‘I have not seen you.'
Behold, this is the joy of his darak (way): out of the ipar (earth), others shall spring.
"Behold, Al will not cast away a blameless chazaq (man), neither will he uphold the evildoers.
He will still malaa (fill) your pah (mouth) with laughter, your shapah (lips) with shouting.
Those who shanaa (hate) you shall be Labash with bashath (shame). The ahal (tent) of the rashai (wicked) shall be no more.
Then Ayawab answered,
"Truly I yadai (know) that it is so, but how can anawash (man) be tzadaq (just) with Al?
If he is pleased to rayab (contend) with him, he can't answer him one time in a alap (thousand).
Alahayam who is wise in labab (heart), and amayatz (mighty) in kach (strength): who has hardened himself against him, and prospered?
He removes the har (mountains), and they don't yadai (know) it, when he overturns them in his ap (anger).
He shakes the aratz (earth) out of its place. Its pillars tremble.
He commands the charas (sun), and it doesn't zarach (rise), and seals up the kawakab (stars).
He alone stretches out the shamayam (heavens), and treads on the bamah (waves) of the yam (sea).
He ishah (makes) the Iyash, Kasayal, and the kayamah (pleiades), and the rooms of the thayaman (south).
He does gadawal (great) things past finding out; yes, palaa (marvelous) things without number.
Behold, he goes by me, and I don't raah (see) him. He passes on also, but I don't bayan (perceive) him.
Behold, he snatches away. Who can shawab (turn back / repent) him? Who will ask him, ‘What are you doing?'
"Alawah will not shawab (turn back / repent) his ap (anger). The helpers of rahab (rahab) stoop under him.
How much less shall I answer him, And choose my dabar (words) to argue with him?
Though I were tzadaq (righteous), yet I wouldn't answer him. I would chanan (make) supplication to my shapat (judge).
If I had called, and he had answered me, yet I wouldn't aman (believe) that he listened to my qawal (voice).
For he breaks me with a storm, and multiplies my wounds without cause.
He will not allow me to catch my rawach (breath), but fills me with bitterness.
If it is a matter of kach (strength), behold, he is amayatz (mighty)! If of justice, ‘Who,' says he, ‘will summon me?'
Though I am tzadaq (righteous), my own pah (mouth) shall rashai (condemn) me. Though I am blameless, it shall prove me perverse.
I am blameless. I don't yadai (respect) myself. I despise my napash (life).
"It is all the same. Therefore I amar (say) he kalah (destroys) the blameless and the rashai (wicked).
If the scourge mawath (kills) suddenly, he will mock at the Masah of the naqay (innocent).
The aratz (earth) is given into the yad (hand) of the rashai (wicked). He covers the panayam (faces) of its shapat (judges). If not he, then who is it?
"Now my yawam (days) are qalal (swifter) than a runner. They flee away, they raah (see) no tawab (good),
They have passed away as the swift ships, as the eagle that swoops on the prey.
If I amar (say), ‘I will forget my complaint, I will put off my sad panayam (face), and cheer up;'
I am yagar (afraid) of all my sorrows, I yadai (know) that you will not hold me innocent.
I shall be condemned. Why then do I yagai (labor) in vain?
If I wash myself with snow, and cleanse my kap (hands) with lye,
yet you will plunge me in the shachath (ditch). My own clothes shall abhor me.
For he is not a ayash (man), as I am, that I should answer him, that we should bawaa (come) together in mashapat (judgment).
There is no umpire between us, that might shayath (lay) his yad (hand) on us shanayam (both).
Let him sawar (take) his shabat (rod) sawar (away) from me. Let his ayamah (terror) not make me afraid;
then I would dabar (speak), and not yaraa (fear) him, for I am not so in myself.
"My napash (soul) is weary of my chay (life). I will give free course to my complaint. I will dabar (speak) Mar the bitterness of my napash (soul).
I will amar (tell) Alawah, ‘Do not rashai (condemn) me. Show me why you rayab (contend) with me.
Is it tawab (good) to you that you should oppress, that you should despise the yagayai (work) of your kap (hands), and smile on the itzah (counsel) of the rashai (wicked)?
Do you have iyan (eyes) of flesh? Or do you raah (see) as anawash (man) raah (see)?
Are your yawam (days) as the yawam (days) of anawash (mortals), or your Shanah as anawash (man's) Shanah,
that you inquire after my iwan (iniquity), and search after my chataah (sin)?
Although you daith (know) that I am not rashai (wicked), there is no one who can natzal (deliver) out of your yad (hand).
"‘Your yad (hands) have framed me and fashioned me altogether, yet you balai (destroy) me.
zakar (remember), I beg you, that you have fashioned me as clay. Will you shawab (turn back / repent) me into ipar (dust) again?
Haven't you poured me out like milk, and curdled me like cheese?
You have Labash me with skin and flesh, and knit me together with itzam (bones) and sinews.
You have granted me chay (life) and loving chasad (kindness). Your visitation has preserved my rawach (spirit).
Yet you hid these things in your labab (heart). I yadai (know) that this is with you:
if I chataa (sin), then you shamar (mark) me. You will not acquit me from my iwan (iniquity).
If I am rashai (wicked), woe to me. If I am tzadaq (righteous), I still shall not nashaa (lift) up my raash (head), Shabai filled with disgrace, and conscious of my affliction.
If my gaah (head) is held high, you hunt me like a shachal (lion). Again you show yourself powerful to me.
You renew your witnesses against me, and increase your kais (indignation) on me. Changes and tzabaa (warfare) are with me.
"‘Why, then, have you brought me yatzaa (forth) out of the womb? I wish I had given up the spirit, and no iyan (eye) had seen me.
I should have been as though I had not been. I should have been carried from the womb to the qabar (grave).
Aren't my yawam (days) Mait? chadal (cease) then. Leave me shayath (alone), that I may find a Mait balag (comfort),
before I yalak (go) where I shall not shawab (turn back / repent) from, to the aratz (land) of chashak (darkness) and of the shadow of tzalamawath (death);
the aratz (land) dark as midnight, of the shadow of tzalamawath (death), without any order, where the yapai (light) is as midnight.'
Then Tzawapar, the Naimathay, answered,
"Shouldn't the multitude of dabar (words) be answered? Should a ayash (man) full of shapah (talk) be justified?
Should your boastings make men hold their charash (peace)? When you mock, shall no man make you kalam (ashamed)?
For you amar (say), ‘My doctrine is zak (pure). I am bar (clean) in your iyan (eyes).'
But oh that Alawah would dabar (speak), and pathach (open) his shapah (lips) against you,
that he would show you the secrets of chakamah (wisdom)! For true chakamah (wisdom) has kapal (two) sides. yadai (know) therefore that Alawah exacts of you less than your iwan (iniquity) deserves.
"Can you fathom the mystery of Alawah? Or can you probe the limits of the Shaday?
They are high as shamayam (heaven). What can you do? They are Imaq than shaawal (sheol). What can you yadai (know)?
Its mad (measure) is Arak than the aratz (earth), and Rachab than the yam (sea).
If he passes by, or confines, or convenes a court, then who can oppose him?
For he yadai (knows) false men. He raah (see) awan (iniquity) also, even though he doesn't bayan (consider) it.
An empty-headed ayash (man) becomes labab (wise) when a adam (man) is yalad (born) as a wild donkey's colt.
"If you kawan (set) your lab (heart) aright, stretch out your kap (hands) toward him.
If awan (iniquity) is in your yad (hand), rachaq (put) it far away. Don't let iwal (unrighteousness) shakan (dwell) in your ahal (tents).
Surely then you shall nashaa (lift) up your panayam (face) without spot; Yes, you shall be steadfast, and shall not yaraa (fear):
for you shall forget your misery. You shall zakar (remember) it as mayam (waters) that are passed ibar (away).
chalad (life) shall be qawam (clearer) than the noonday. Though there is iwap (darkness), it shall be as the baqar (morning).
You shall be batach (secure), because there is hope. Yes, you shall search, and shall take your shakab (rest) in safety.
Also you shall rabatz (lie) down, and none shall make you afraid. Yes, many shall court your favor.
But the iyan (eyes) of the rashai (wicked) shall kalah (fail). They shall have no abad (way) to flee. Their hope shall be the giving up of the spirit.
Then Ayawab answered,
"No doubt, but you are the im (people), and chakamah (wisdom) shall mawath (die) with you.
But I have labab (understanding) as well as you; I am not napal (inferior) to you. Yes, who doesn't know such things as these?
I am like shachawaq (one) who is a joke to his neighbor, I, who called on Alawah, and he answered. The tzadayaq (just), the blameless shachawaq (man) is a joke.
In the thought of him who is at Shaanan there is contempt for misfortune. It is kawan (ready) for them whose ragal (foot) slips.
The ahal (tents) of shadad (robbers) shalah (prosper). Those who provoke Al are secure, who bawaa (carry) their Alawah in their yad (hands).
"But shaal (ask) the animals, now, and they shall teach you; the birds of the sky, and they shall nagad (tell) you.
Or speak to the aratz (earth), and it shall teach you. The fish of the yam (sea) shall declare to you.
Who doesn't yadai (know) that in all these, the yad (hand) of Yahawah has done this,
in whose yad (hand) is the napash (life) of every chay (living) thing, and the rawach (breath) of all ayash (mankind)?
Doesn't the ear try malah (words), even as the palate tastes its food?
With Yashayash men is chakamah (wisdom), in arak (length) of yawam (days) thabawan (understanding).
"With Alahayam is wisdom and might. He has itzah (counsel) and thabawan (understanding).
Behold, he haras (breaks) down, and it can't be built again. He imprisons a ayash (man), and there can be no release.
Behold, he itzar (withholds) the mayam (waters), and they yabash (dry) up. Again, he shalach (sends) them out, and they overturn the aratz (earth).
With him is iz (strength) and thawashayah (wisdom). The shagag (deceived) and the deceiver are his.
He yalak (leads) yaitz (counselors) away Shawalal. He makes shapat (judges) halal (fools).
He loosens the bond of malak (kings). He binds their waist with a belt.
He yalak (leads) kahan (priests) away Shawalal, and overthrows the ayathan (mighty).
He sawar (removes) the shapah (speech) of those who are trusted, and takes away the taim (understanding) of the zaqan (elders).
He pours contempt on nadayab (princes), and loosens the belt of the strong.
He galah (uncovers) Imaq things out of chashak (darkness), and yatzaa (brings) out to awar (light) the shadow of tzalamawath (death).
He increases the gawayam (nations), and he abad (destroys) them. He enlarges the gawayam (nations), and he leads them captive.
He sawar (takes) away lab (understanding) from the raash (chiefs) of the im (people) of the aratz (earth), and thaih (causes) them to wander in a thahaw (wilderness) where there is no darak (way).
They grope in the chashak (dark) without awar (light). He thaih (makes) them stagger like a drunken shakawar (man).
"Behold, my iyan (eye) has seen all this. My ear has heard and understood it.
What you daith (know), I yadai (know) also. I am not napal (inferior) to you.
"Surely I would dabar (speak) to the Shaday. I desire to yakach (reason) with Al.
But you are forgers of lies. You are all physicians of no value.
Oh that you would be completely charash (silent)! Then you would be wise.
Hear now my reasoning. Listen to the rayab (pleadings) of my shapah (lips).
Will you dabar (speak) iwal (unrighteously) for Al, and dabar (talk) deceitfully for him?
Will you show partiality to him? Will you rayab (contend) for Al?
Is it tawab (good) that he should search you out? Or as one deceives a hathal (man), will you deceive him?
He will yakach (surely) yakach (reprove) you if you secretly show partiality.
Shall not his majesty make you afraid, And his pachad (dread) napal (fall) on you?
Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes, Your defenses are defenses of clay.
"Be charash (silent), leave me alone, that I may dabar (speak). Let ibar (come) on me what will.
Why should I nashaa (take) my flesh in my teeth, and shawam (put) my napash (life) in my kap (hand)?
Behold, he will kill me. I have no hope. Nevertheless, I will yakach (maintain) my darak (ways) panayam (before) him.
This also shall be my yashawaih (salvation), that a godless man shall not bawaa (come) panayam (before) him.
Hear diligently my speech. Let my declaration be in your ears.
See now, I have set my cause in order. I yadai (know) that I am tzadaq (righteous).
Who is he who will rayab (contend) with me? For then would I hold my charash (peace) and gawai (give) up the spirit.
"Only don't do shanayam (two) things to me; then I will not hide myself from your panayam (face):
rachaq (withdraw) your kap (hand) rachaq (far) from me; and don't let your ayamah (terror) make me afraid.
Then qaraa (call), and I will answer; or let me dabar (speak), and you shawab (turn back / repent) me.
How many are my iwan (iniquities) and chataah (sins)? yadai (make) me know my disobedience and my chataah (sin).
Why hide you your panayam (face), and chashab (hold) me for your ayab (enemy)?
Will you harass a driven leaf? Will you pursue the Yabash stubble?
For you kathab (write) bitter things against me, and yarash (make) me inherit the iwan (iniquities) of my youth:
You also shawam (put) my feet in the stocks, and shamar (mark) all my arach (paths). You chaqah (set) a bound to the soles of my feet,
though I am decaying like a rotten thing, like a bagad (garment) that is moth - eaten.
"adam (man), who is yalad (born) of a ashah (woman), is of Qatzar yawam (days), and Shabai of ragaz (trouble).
He yatzaa (comes) forth like a flower, and is cut down. He also flees like a shadow, and doesn't imad (continue).
Do you open your iyan (eyes) on such a one, and bawaa (bring) me into mashapat (judgment) with you?
Who can nathan (bring) a tahawar (clean) thing out of an tamaa (unclean)? Not one.
am (seeing) his yawam (days) are determined, the number of his chadash (months) is with you, and you have appointed his chaq (bounds) that he can't ibar (pass);
shaih (look) away from him, that he may chadal (rest), until he shall accomplish, as a shakayar (hireling), his yawam (day).
"For there is hope for a itz (tree), If it is karath (cut) down, that it will sprout again, that the tender branch of it will not chadal (cease).
Though its root grows zaqan (old) in the aratz (earth), and its stock dies in the ipar (ground),
yet through the rayach (scent) of mayam (water) it will bud, and ishah (put) forth boughs like a plant.
But gabar (man) dies, and is laid low. Yes, adam (man) gawai (gives) up the spirit, and where is he?
As the mayam (waters) azal (fail) from the yam (sea), and the nahar (river) charab (wastes) and yabash (dries) up,
so ayash (man) lies down and doesn't qawam (rise). Until the shamayam (heavens) are no more, they shall not qawatz (awake), nor be roused out of their shanah (sleep).

"Oh that you would hide me in shaawal (sheol), that you would keep me secret, until your ap (wrath) is shawab (turn back / repent), that you would shayath (appoint) me a chaq (set) time, and zakar (remember) me!
If a gabar (man) dies, shall he chayah (live) again? All the yawam (days) of my tzabaa (warfare) would I wait, until my release should bawaa (come).
You would qaraa (call), and I would answer you. You would have a desire to the maishah (work) of your yad (hands).
But now you number my steps. Don't you shamar (watch) over my chataah (sin)?
My disobedience is sealed up in a tzarawar (bag). You fasten up my iwan (iniquity).
"But the har (mountain) falling comes to nothing. The tzawar (rock) is removed out of its place;
The mayam (waters) wear the aban (stones). The torrents of it wash away the ipar (dust) of the aratz (earth). So you abad (destroy) the hope of anawash (man).
You forever prevail against him, and he departs. You shanah (change) his panayam (face), and shalach (send) him away.
His ban (sons) kabad (come) to honor, and he doesn't yadai (know) it. They are brought low, but he doesn't bayan (perceive) it of them.
But his flesh on him has pain, and his napash (soul) inside him mourns.
Then Alayapaz the Thayamanay answered,
"Should a wise chakam (man) answer with rawach (vain) daith (knowledge), and malaa (fill) himself with the east qadayam (wind)?
Should he yakach (reason) with unprofitable dabar (talk), or with speeches with which he can do no yail (good)?
Yes, you do away with yaraah (fear), and hinder devotion panayam (before) Al.
For your iwan (iniquity) teaches your pah (mouth), and you choose the lashawan (language) of the Irawam.
Your own pah (mouth) rashai (condemns) you, and not I. Yes, your own shapah (lips) testify against you.
"Are you the raashawan (first) adam (man) who was yalad (born)? Or were you brought panayam (forth) before the Gabaih?
Have you heard the sawad (secret) counsel of Alawah? Do you limit chakamah (wisdom) to yourself?
What do you yadai (know), that we don't yadai (know)? What do you bayan (understand), which is not in us?
With us are both the gray-headed and the very Yashayash men, much yawam (elder) than your ab (father).
Are the consolations of Al too Mait for you, even the dabar (word) that is gentle toward you?
Why does your lab (heart) carry you away? Why do your iyan (eyes) flash,
That you shawab (turn back / repent) your rawach (spirit) against Al, and let such malah (words) yatzaa (go) out of your pah (mouth)?
What is anawash (man), that he should be zakah (clean)? What is he who is yalad (born) of a ashah (woman), that he should be tzadaq (righteous)?
Behold, he puts no aman (trust) in his qadawash (holy) ones. Yes, the shamayam (heavens) are not zakak (clean) in his iyan (sight);
how much less one who is abominable and corrupt, a ayash (man) who drinks iwal (iniquity) like mayam (water)!
"I will show you, listen to me; that which I have seen I will declare:
(Which chakam (wise) men have told by their abawath (fathers), and have not hidden it;
to whom alone the aratz (land) was given, and no stranger passed among them):
the rashai (wicked) man writhes in pain all his yawam (days), even the number of Shanah that are laid up for the irayatz (oppressor).
A qawal (sound) of pachad (terrors) is in his ears. In prosperity the shadad (destroyer) shall bawaa (come) on him.
He doesn't aman (believe) that he shall shawab (turn back / repent) out of chashak (darkness). He is waited for by the charab (sword).
He nadad (wanders) abroad for lacham (bread), saying, ‘Where is it?' He yadai (knows) that the yawam (day) of chashak (darkness) is kawan (ready) at his yad (hand).
tzar (distress) and anguish make him afraid. They prevail against him, as a malak (king) Ithayad to the battle.
Because he has stretched out his yad (hand) against Al, and behaves himself proudly against the Shaday;
he runs at him with a stiff neck, with the thick gab (shields) of his magan (bucklers);
because he has covered his panayam (face) with his fatness, and gathered fat on his thighs.
He has lived in desolate Iyar, in bayath (houses) which no one inhabited, which were ready to become heaps.
He shall not be rich, neither shall his chayal (substance) qawam (continue), neither shall their possessions be extended on the aratz (earth).
He shall not sawar (depart) out of chashak (darkness). The shalahabath (flame) shall yabash (dry) up his branches. By the rawach (breath) of God's pah (mouth) shall he sawar (go) away.
Let him not aman (trust) in emptiness, deceiving himself; for emptiness shall be his reward.
It shall be accomplished laa (before) his yawam (time). His branch shall not be Rainan.
He shall shake off his unripe grape as the vine, and shall cast off his flower as the olive tree.
For the idah (company) of the godless shall be Galamawad, and ash (fire) shall akal (consume) the ahal (tents) of shachad (bribery).
They conceive imal (mischief), and yalad (bring) forth awan (iniquity). Their batan (heart) kawan (prepares) deceit.
Then Ayawab answered,
"I have heard many such things. You are all imal (miserable) comforters!
Shall rawach (vain) dabar (words) have an end? Or what provokes you that you answer?
I also could dabar (speak) as you do. If your napash (soul) were in my napash (soul's) place, I could join malah (words) together against you, and shake my raash (head) at you,
but I would amatz (strengthen) you with my pah (mouth). The solace of my shapah (lips) would relieve you.
"Though I dabar (speak), my grief is not subsided. Though I chadal (forbear), what am I halak (eased)?
But now, Alahayam, you have surely worn me out. You have made shamam (desolate) all my idah (company).
You have shriveled me up. This is a witness against me. My leanness qawam (rises) up against me. It testifies to my panayam (face).
He has torn me in his ap (wrath), and persecuted me. He has gnashed on me with his teeth. My tzar (adversary) sharpens his iyan (eyes) on me.
They have gaped on me with their pah (mouth). They have struck me on the Lachay reproachfully. They malaa (gather) themselves together against me.
Al delivers me to the ungodly, and casts me into the yad (hands) of the rashai (wicked).
I was at shalaw (ease), and he broke me apart. Yes, he has taken me by the neck, and dashed me to pieces. He has also qawam (set) me up for his target.
His archers surround me. He splits my kalayah (kidneys) apart, and does not spare. He pours out my gall on the aratz (ground).
He breaks me with breach on breach. He runs on me like a gabawar (giant).
I have sewed sackcloth on my skin, and have thrust my qaran (horn) in the ipar (dust).
My panayam (face) is red with weeping. Deep darkness is on my ipaip (eyelids).
Although there is no violence in my kap (hands), and my prayer is zak (pure).
"aratz (earth), don't cover my dam (blood). Let my cry have no place to maqawam (rest).
Even now, behold, my witness is in shamayam (heaven). He who vouches for me is on high.
My rai (friends) Lawatz at me. My iyan (eyes) pour out tears to Alawah,
that he would yakach (maintain) the right of a gabar (man) with Alawah, of a son of adam (man) with his neighbor!
For when a few Shanah have come, I shall go the arach (way) of no shawab (turn back / repent).
"My rawach (spirit) is consumed. My yawam (days) are extinct, And the qabar (grave) is ready for me.
Surely there are mockers with me. My iyan (eye) lawan (dwells) on their provocation.
"Now shawam (give) a pledge, be collateral for me with yourself. Who is there who will strike yad (hands) with me?
For you have hidden their lab (heart) from shakal (understanding), Therefore you shall not exalt them.
He who nagad (denounces) his rai (friends) for a prey, Even the iyan (eyes) of his children shall kalah (fail).
"But he has made me a byword of the im (people). They spit in my thapath (face).
My iyan (eye) also is dim by reason of kais (sorrow). All my members are as a shadow.
yashar (upright) men shall be astonished at this. The naqay (innocent) shall stir up himself against the godless.
Yet shall the tzadayaq (righteous) achaz (hold) on his darak (way). He who has Tahawar yad (hands) shall grow stronger and stronger.
But as for you all, shawab (turn back / repent) on now again; I shall not matzaa (find) a wise chakam (man) among you.
My yawam (days) are past, my plans are broken off, as are the mawarash (thoughts) of my labab (heart).
They shawam (change) the layal (night) into yawam (day), saying ‘The awar (light) is qarawab (near)' in the panayam (presence) of chashak (darkness).
If I look for shaawal (sheol) as my bayath (house), if I have spread my couch in the chashak (darkness),
If I have said to shachath (corruption), ‘You are my ab (father);' to the worm, ‘My am (mother),' and ‘my achawath (sister);'
where then is my hope? as for my hope, who shall see it?
Shall it yarad (go) down with me to the gates of shaawal (sheol), or descend together into the ipar (dust)?
Then Baladad the Shawachay answered,
"How long will you hunt for malah (words)? bayan (consider), and afterwards we will dabar (speak).
Why are we counted as animals, which have become tamah (unclean) in your iyan (sight)?
You who tear yourself in your ap (anger), shall the aratz (earth) be forsaken for you? Or shall the tzawar (rock) be removed out of its place?
"Yes, the awar (light) of the rashai (wicked) shall be put out, The spark of his ash (fire) shall not shine.
The awar (light) shall be chashak (dark) in his ahal (tent). His nayar (lamp) above him shall be put out.
The steps of his awan (strength) shall be shortened. His own itzah (counsel) shall cast him down.
For he is shalach (cast) into a net by his own feet, and he wanders into its mesh.
A snare will achaz (take) him by the heel. A trap will chazaq (catch) him.
A noose is hidden for him in the aratz (ground), a trap for him in the nathayab (way).
Terrors shall make him afraid on every side, and shall chase him at his heels.
His awan (strength) shall be Raib. Calamity shall be kawan (ready) at his side.
The members of his body shall be devoured. The firstborn of mawath (death) shall akal (devour) his members.
He shall be rooted out of his ahal (tent) where he trusts. He shall be brought to the malak (king) of terrors.
There shall shakan (dwell) in his ahal (tent) that which is none of his. Sulfur shall be scattered on his Nawah.
His roots shall be dried up beneath. Above shall his branch be cut off.
His zakar (memory) shall abad (perish) from the aratz (earth). He shall have no sham (name) in the panayam (street).
He shall be driven from awar (light) into chashak (darkness), and chased out of the world.
He shall have neither nayan (son) nor grandson among his im (people), nor any sharayad (remaining) where he lived.
Those who Acharawan after shall be astonished at his yawam (day), as those who Qadamawanay before were frightened.
Surely such are the mashakan (dwellings) of the iwal (unrighteous). This is the place of him who doesn't yadai (know) Al.
Then Ayawab answered,
"How long will you torment me, and dakaa (crush) me with malah (words)?
You have reproached me ishar (ten) paim (times). You aren't bawash (ashamed) that you attack me.
If it is true that I have erred, my error lawan (remains) with myself.
If indeed you will magnify yourselves against me, and yakach (plead) against me my reproach;
yadai (know) now that Alawah has subverted me, and has surrounded me with his net.
"Behold, I cry out of wrong, but I am not heard. I cry for help, but there is no justice.
He has walled up my arach (way) so that I can't ibar (pass), and has shawam (set) chashak (darkness) in my nathayab (paths).
He has stripped me of my kabawad (glory), and taken the itarah (crown) from my head.
He has broken me down on every side, and I am gone. My hope he has plucked up like a itz (tree).
He has also kindled his ap (wrath) against me. He chashab (counts) me among his tzar (adversaries).
His gadawad (troops) bawaa (come) on together, build a siege ramp against me, and chanah (encamp) around my ahal (tent).
"He has rachaq (put) my ach (brothers) rachaq (far) from me. My yadai (acquaintances) are wholly estranged from me.
My relatives have gone away. My yadai (familiar) friends have forgotten me.
Those who gawar (dwell) in my bayath (house), and my amah (maids), chashab (count) me for a stranger. I am an nakaray (alien) in their iyan (sight).
I qaraa (call) to my ibad (servant), and he gives me no answer. I beg him with my pah (mouth).
My rawach (breath) is offensive to my ashah (wife). I am loathsome to the children of my own batan (mother).
Even young children despise me. If I qawam (arise), they dabar (speak) against me.
All my familiar friends abhor me. They whom I loved have turned against me.
My itzam (bones) stick to my skin and to my flesh. I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
"Have chanan (pity) on me, have chanan (pity) on me, you my rai (friends); for the yad (hand) of Alawah has touched me.
Why do you persecute me as Al, and are not satisfied with my flesh?
"Oh that my malah (words) were now written! Oh that they were inscribed in a book!
That with an barazal (iron) pen and lead they were engraved in the tzawar (rock) id (forever)!
But as for me, I yadai (know) that my gaal (redeemer) chay (lives). Acharawan the end, he will qawam (stand) upon the ipar (earth).
achar (after) my skin is destroyed, then in my flesh shall I chazah (see) Alawah,
Whom I, even I, shall chazah (see) on my side. My iyan (eyes) shall raah (see), and not as a stranger. "My kalayah (heart) is consumed within me.
If you amar (say), ‘How we will persecute him!' because the root of the dabar (matter) is found in me,
be gawar (afraid) of the charab (sword), for chamah (wrath) brings the iwan (punishments) of the charab (sword), that you may yadai (know) there is a dayan (judgment).
Then Tzawapar the Naimathay answered,
"Therefore do my thoughts shawab (turn back / repent) answer to me, even by reason of my haste that is in me.
I have heard the reproof which puts me to kalamah (shame). The rawach (spirit) of my bayanah (understanding) answers me.
Don't you yadai (know) this from old time, since adam (man) was placed on aratz (earth),
that the triumphing of the rashai (wicked) is qarawab (short), the joy of the godless but for a moment?
Though his height ilah (mount) up to the shamayam (heavens), and his raash (head) nagai (reach) to the clouds,
yet he shall abad (perish) forever like his own dung. Those who have seen him shall amar (say), ‘Where is he?'
He shall fly away as a chalawam (dream), and shall not be found. Yes, he shall be chased nadad (away) like a vision of the layal (night).
The iyan (eye) which saw him shall see him no more, neither shall his place any more see him.
His children shall seek the favor of the Dal. His yad (hands) shall shawab (turn back / repent) back his wealth.
His itzam (bones) are malaa (full) of his youth, but youth shall shakab (lie) down with him in the ipar (dust).
"Though wickedness is sweet in his pah (mouth), though he hide it under his lashawan (tongue),
though he spare it, and will not let it go, but keep it still within his chak (mouth);
yet his lacham (food) in his maih (bowels) is turned. It is cobra venom qarab (within) him.
He has swallowed down riches, and he shall vomit them up again. Al will yarash (cast) them out of his belly.
He shall suck cobra venom. The viper's lashawan (tongue) shall harag (kill) him.
He shall not raah (see) at the palagah (rivers), the flowing streams of honey and butter.
That for which he labored he shall shawab (turn back / repent), and shall not balai (swallow) it down. According to the chayal (substance) that he has gotten, he shall not rejoice.
For he has oppressed and forsaken the Dal. He has violently taken away a bayath (house), and he shall not banah (build) it up.
"Because he knew no shalaw (quietness) within him, he shall not malat (save) anything of that in which he delights.
There was nothing sharayad (left) that he didn't devour, therefore his prosperity shall not endure.
In the fullness of his sufficiency, distress shall overtake him. The yad (hand) of everyone who is in imal (misery) shall bawaa (come) on him.
When he is about to malaa (fill) his belly, Alahayam will cast the charawan (fierceness) of his ap (wrath) on him. It will rain on him while he is eating.
He shall flee from the barazal (iron) nashaq (weapon). The bronze qashath (arrow) shall strike him through.
He draws it yatzaa (forth), and it comes out of his body. Yes, the glittering point halak (comes) out of his liver. ayamah (terrors) are on him.
All chashak (darkness) is laid up for his treasures. An unfanned ash (fire) shall akal (devour) him. It shall consume that which is sharayad (left) in his ahal (tent).
The shamayam (heavens) shall galah (reveal) his iwan (iniquity). The aratz (earth) shall qawam (rise) up against him.
The increase of his bayath (house) shall depart. They shall rush away in the yawam (day) of his ap (wrath).
This is the chalaq (portion) of a rashai (wicked) adam (man) from Alahayam, the nachalah (heritage) amar (appointed) to him by Al.
Then Ayawab answered,
"Listen diligently to my speech. Let this be your consolation.
Allow me, and I also will dabar (speak); achar (after) I have spoken, mock on.
As for me, is my complaint to adam (man)? Why shouldn't I be impatient?
panah (look) at me, and be astonished. shawam (lay) your yad (hand) on your pah (mouth).
When I zakar (remember), I am troubled. Horror achaz (takes) hold of my flesh.
"Why do the rashai (wicked) chayah (live), become old, yes, and grow gabar (mighty) in chayal (power)?
Their zarai (child) is established with them in their panayam (sight), their tzaatzaa (offspring) before their iyan (eyes).
Their bayath (houses) are shalawam (safe) from pachad (fear), neither is the shabat (rod) of Alawah upon them.
Their bulls breed without fail. Their cows calve, and don't shakal (miscarry).
They shalach (send) forth their little iwayal (ones) like a flock. Their children dance.
They sing to the tambourine and harp, and Shamach at the qawal (sound) of the pipe.
They kalah (spend) their yawam (days) in tawab (prosperity). In an instant they chathath (go) down to shaawal (sheol).
They amar (tell) Al, ‘sawar (depart) from us, for we don't want to daith (know) about your darak (ways).
What is the Shaday, that we should ibad (serve) him? What yail (profit) should we have, if we pagai (pray) to him?'
Behold, their prosperity is not in their yad (hand). The itzah (counsel) of the rashai (wicked) is rachaq (far) from me.
"How often is it that the nayar (lamp) of the rashai (wicked) is put out, that their calamity bawaa (comes) on them, that Alahayam distributes sorrows in his ap (anger)?
How often is it that they are as stubble panayam (before) the rawach (wind), as chaff that the sawapah (storm) carries away?
You say, ‘Alawah lays up his awan (iniquity) for his children.' Let him shalam (recompense) it to himself, that he may yadai (know) it.
Let his own iyan (eyes) raah (see) his destruction. Let him drink of the chamah (wrath) of the Shaday.
Chapatz what does he care for his bayath (house) achar (after) him, when the number of his chadash (months) is cut off?
"Shall any teach Al daith (knowledge), since he shapat (judges) those who are high?
One dies in his tham (full) itzam (strength), Shalaanan wholly at ease and shalaw (quiet).
His pails are malaa (full) of milk. The marrow of his itzam (bones) is moistened.
Another dies Mar bitterness of napash (soul), and never tastes of tawab (good).
They shakab (lie) down alike in the ipar (dust). The worm covers them.
"Behold, I yadai (know) your machashabah (thoughts), the devices with which you would wrong me.
For you amar (say), ‘Where is the bayath (house) of the nadayab (prince)? Where is the mashakan (tent) in which the rashai (wicked) lived?'
Haven't you asked wayfaring men? Don't you nakar (know) their evidences,
that the rai (evil) chashak (man) is reserved to the yawam (day) of calamity, That they are led forth to the yawam (day) of ibarah (wrath)?
Who shall nagad (declare) his darak (way) to his panayam (face)? Who shall shalam (repay) him what he has done?
Yet he will be borne to the qabar (grave). Men shall keep watch over the tomb.
The clods of the nachal (valley) shall be sweet to him. All men shall draw achar (after) him, as there were innumerable panayam (before) him.
So how can you nacham (comfort) me with nonsense, because in your thashawabah (answers) there shaar (remains) only mail (falsehood)?
Then Alayapaz the Thayamanay answered,
"Can a gabar (man) be profitable to Al? Surely he who is shakal (wise) is profitable to himself.
Is it any Chapatz to the Shaday, that you are tzadaq (righteous)? Or does it benefit him, that you make your darak (ways) thamam (perfect)?
Is it for your piety that he yakach (reproves) you, that he bawaa (enters) with you into mashapat (judgment)?
Isn't your wickedness rab (great)? Neither is there any end to your iwan (iniquities).
For you have taken chabal (pledges) from your ach (brother) for nothing, and stripped the Irawam of their clothing.
You haven't given mayam (water) to the Iyap to shaqah (drink), and you have withheld lacham (bread) from the Raib.
But as for the zarawai (mighty) ayash (man), he had the aratz (earth). The nashaa (honorable) man, he lived in it.
You have sent alamanah (widows) away empty, and the zarawai (arms) of the fatherless have been broken.
Therefore snares are around you. Sudden pachad (fear) troubles you,
or chashak (darkness), so that you can not raah (see), and floods of mayam (waters) cover you.
"Isn't Alawah in the heights of shamayam (heaven)? raah (see) the height of the kawakab (stars), how high they are!
You amar (say), ‘What does Al yadai (know)? Can he shapat (judge) through the thick irapal (darkness)?
Thick clouds are a covering to him, so that he doesn't raah (see). He halak (walks) on the vault of the sky.'
Will you shamar (keep) the old arach (way), which awan (wicked) men have trodden,
who were snatched away before their ith (time), whose yasawad (foundation) was poured out as a stream,
who said to Al, ‘sawar (depart) from us;' and, ‘What can the Shaday do for us?'
Yet he filled their bayath (houses) with tawab (good) things, but the itzah (counsel) of the rashai (wicked) is rachaq (far) from me.
The tzadayaq (righteous) raah (see) it, and are Shamach. The naqay (innocent) ridicule them,
saying, ‘am (surely) those who rose up against us are cut off. The ash (fire) has consumed their yathar (remnant).'
"Acquaint yourself with him, now, and be at shalam (peace). Thereby tawab (good) shall bawaa (come) to you.
Please receive instruction from his pah (mouth), and shawam (lay) up his amar (words) in your labab (heart).
If you shawab (turn back / repent) to the Shaday, you shall be built up, if you rachaq (put) away iwal (unrighteousness) rachaq (far) from your ahal (tents).
shayath (lay) your treasure in the ipar (dust), the gold of Awapayar among the tzawar (stones) of the nachal (brooks).
The Shaday will be your treasure, and precious kasap (silver) to you.
For then you will delight yourself in the Shaday, and shall nashaa (lift) up your panayam (face) to Alawah.
You shall make your prayer to him, and he will hear you. You shall shalam (pay) your nadar (vows).
You shall also decree a thing, and it shall be established to you. awar (light) shall shine on your darak (ways).
When they cast down, you shall amar (say), ‘be lifted up.' He will yashai (save) the Shach person.
He will even malat (deliver) him who is not naqay (innocent). Yes, he shall be delivered through the cleanness of your kap (hands).
Then Ayawab answered,
"Even today my complaint is rebellious. His yad (hand) is kabad (heavy) in spite of my groaning.
Oh that I knew where I might matzaa (find) him! That I might bawaa (come) even to his seat!
I would set my cause in order panayam (before) him, and malaa (fill) my pah (mouth) with arguments.
I would yadai (know) the malah (words) which he would answer me, and bayan (understand) what he would amar (tell) me.
Would he rayab (contend) with me in the greatness of his kach (power)? No, but he would listen to me.
There the yashar (upright) might yakach (reason) with him, so I should be delivered forever from my shapat (judge).
"If I halak (go) qadam (east), he is not there; if west, I can't find him;
He ishah (works) to the north, but I can't chazah (see) him. He itap (turns) yamayan (south), but I can't catch a glimpse of him.
But he yadai (knows) the darak (way) that I take. When he has tried me, I shall yatzaa (come) forth like gold.
My ragal (foot) has held fast to his steps. I have kept his darak (way), and not turned natah (aside).
I haven't gone mawash (back) from the matzawah (commandment) of his shapah (lips). I have treasured up the amar (words) of his pah (mouth) more than my chaq (necessary) food.
But he stands achad (alone), and who can oppose him? What his napash (soul) desires, even that he does.
For he shalam (performs) that which is chaq (appointed) for me. Many such things are with him.
Therefore I am terrified at his panayam (presence). When I bayan (consider), I am pachad (afraid) of him.
For Al has made my lab (heart) faint. The Shaday has terrified me.
Because I was not tzamath (cut) off panayam (before) the chashak (darkness), neither did he cover the thick apal (darkness) from my panayam (face).
"Why aren't ith (times) laid up by the Shaday? Why don't those who yadai (know) him chazah (see) his yawam (days)?
There are nashag (people) who remove the landmarks. They violently take away flocks, and raih (feed) them.
They drive away the donkey of the fatherless, and they take the alamanah (widow's) ox for a chabal (pledge).
They natah (turn) the Abayawan out of the darak (way). The Inay of the aratz (earth) all hide themselves.

Behold, as wild donkeys in the madabar (desert), they yatzaa (go) forth to their pail (work), seeking shachar (diligently) Tarap food. The irabah (wilderness) yields them lacham (bread) for their children.
They cut their provender in the shadah (field). They glean the vineyard of the rashai (wicked).
They lie all lawan (night) Irawam without clothing, and have no covering in the cold.
They are wet with the showers of the har (mountains), and embrace the tzawar (rock) for lack of a shelter.
There are those who pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a chabal (pledge) of the Inay,
So that they halak (go) around Irawam without clothing. Being Raib, they nashaa (carry) the sheaves.
They make tzahar (oil) within the walls of these men. They tread yaqab (wine) presses, and suffer thirst.
From out of the populous Iyar, men groan. The napash (soul) of the Chalal cries out, yet Alawah doesn't shawam (regard) the folly.
"These are of those who rebel against the awar (light). They don't nakar (know) its darak (ways), nor stay in its nathayab (paths).
The ratzach (murderer) qawam (rises) with the awar (light). He kills the Inay and Inay. In the layal (night) he is like a thief.
The iyan (eye) also of the naap (adulterer) shamar (waits) for the nashap (twilight), saying, ‘No iyan (eye) shall see me.' He disguises his panayam (face).
In the chashak (dark) they dig through bayath (houses). They shut themselves up in the yawamam (daytime). They don't yadai (know) the awar (light).
For the baqar (morning) is to all of them like thick darkness, for they nakar (know) the terrors of the thick darkness.
"They are foam on the surface of the waters. Their chalaqah (portion) is cursed in the aratz (earth). They don't panah (turn) into the darak (way) of the vineyards.
tzayah (drought) and heat consume the snow mayam (waters), so does shaawal (sheol) those who have sinned.
The womb shall forget him. The worm shall feed sweetly on him. He shall be no more zakar (remembered). iwal (unrighteousness) shall be shabar (broken) as a itz (tree).
He raih (devours) the Iqar who don't yalad (bear). He shows no kindness to the alamanah (widow).
Yet Alahayam preserves the abayar (mighty) by his kach (power). He qawam (rises) up who has no aman (assurance) of chay (life).
Alahayam gives them security, and they shain (rest) in it. His iyan (eyes) are on their darak (ways).
They are exalted; yet a Mait while, and they are gone. Yes, they are brought low, they are taken out of the darak (way) as all others, and are cut off as the raash (tops) of the ears of grain.
If it isn't so now, who will prove me a liar, and shawam (make) my speech worth nothing?
Then Baladad the Shawachay answered,
"mashal (dominion) and pachad (fear) are with him. He ishah (makes) shalawam (peace) in his high places.
Can his gadawad (armies) be counted? On whom does his awar (light) not qawam (arise)?
How then can anawash (man) be tzadaq (just) with Al? Or how can he who is yalad (born) of a ashah (woman) be zakah (clean)?
Behold, even the yarach (moon) has no brightness, and the kawakab (stars) are not zakak (pure) in his iyan (sight);
How much less anawash (man), who is a worm, the ban (son) of adam (man), who is a worm!
Then Ayawab answered,
"How have you helped him who is without kach (power)! How have you saved the zarawai (arm) that has no iz (strength)!
How have you counseled him who has no chakamah (wisdom), and plentifully declared sound knowledge!
To whom have you uttered malah (words)? Whose nashamah (spirit) came yatzaa (forth) from you?
"Those who are rapaa (deceased) chawal (tremble), those beneath the mayam (waters) and all that live in them.
shaawal (sheol) is Irawam before Alahayam, and Abaddon has no covering.
He stretches out the tzapawan (north) over thahaw (empty) space, and hangs the aratz (earth) on nothing.
He tzarar (binds) up the mayam (waters) in his thick clouds, and the cloud is not burst under them.
He encloses the panayam (face) of his kasaa (throne), and spreads his cloud on it.
He has described a boundary on the surface of the waters, and to the confines of awar (light) and chashak (darkness).
The pillars of shamayam (heaven) tremble and are thamah (astonished) at his rebuke.
He stirs up the yam (sea) with his kach (power), and by his thabawan (understanding) he strikes through rahab (rahab).
By his rawach (spirit) the shamayam (heavens) are garnished. His yad (hand) has pierced the Barayach serpent.
Behold, these are but the outskirts of his darak (ways). How small a whisper do we hear of him! But the thunder of his gabawarah (power) who can bayan (understand)?
Ayawab again took up his parable, and said,
"As Al chay (lives), who has taken sawar (away) my mashapat (right), the Shaday, who has made my napash (soul) bitter.
(For the length of my life is still in me, and the rawach (spirit) of Alawah is in my ap (nostrils));
surely my shapah (lips) shall not dabar (speak) iwal (unrighteousness), neither shall my lashawan (tongue) utter deceit.
Far be it from me that I should justify you. Until I gawai (die) I will not sawar (put) away my integrity from me.
I chazaq (hold) fast to my tzadaqah (righteousness), and will not let it rapah (go). My labab (heart) shall not reproach me so yawam (long) as I live.
"Let my ayab (enemy) be as the rashai (wicked). Let him who qawam (rises) up against me be as the iwal (unrighteous).
For what is the hope of the godless, when he is cut off, when Alawah takes away his napash (life)?
Will Al hear his cry when tzarah (trouble) bawaa (comes) on him?
Will he delight himself in the Shaday, and qaraa (call) on Alawah at all ith (times)?
I will teach you about the yad (hand) of Al. That which is with the Shaday will I not conceal.
chazah (behold), all of you have seen it yourselves; why then have you become altogether vain?
"This is the chalaq (portion) of a rashai (wicked) adam (man) with Al, the nachalah (heritage) of irayatz (oppressors), which they receive from the Shaday.
If his children are multiplied, it is for the charab (sword). His tzaatzaa (offspring) shall not be satisfied with lacham (bread).
Those who sharayad (remain) of him shall be buried in mawath (death). His alamanah (widows) shall make no lamentation.
Though he heap up kasap (silver) as the ipar (dust), and kawan (prepare) clothing as the clay;
he may kawan (prepare) it, but the tzadayaq (just) shall Labash it on, and the naqay (innocent) shall divide the kasap (silver).
He banah (builds) his bayath (house) as the moth, as a sakah (booth) which the watchman ishah (makes).
He lies down Ishayar, but he shall not do so again. He opens his iyan (eyes), and he is not.
Terrors overtake him like mayam (waters). A sawapah (storm) steals him away in the layal (night).
The qadayam (east) wind nashaa (carries) him away, and he departs. It sweeps him out of his place.
For it hurls at him, and does not spare, as he flees away from his yad (hand).
Men shall clap their kap (hands) at him, and shall hiss him out of his place.
"Surely there is a mine for kasap (silver), and a place for gold which they refine.
barazal (iron) is taken out of the ipar (earth), and copper is smelted out of the ore.
Man shawam (sets) an end to chashak (darkness), and searches out, to the furthest bound, the aban (stones) of apal (obscurity) and of thick darkness.
He breaks open a shaft away from where people live. They are forgotten by the ragal (foot). They hang far from men, they swing back and forth.
As for the aratz (earth), out of it yatzaa (comes) lacham (bread); Underneath it is turned up as it were by ash (fire).
Sapphires come from its rocks. It has ipar (dust) of gold.
That nathayab (path) no bird of prey yadai (knows), neither has the falcon's iyan (eye) seen it.
The proud animals have not trodden it, nor has the fierce shachal (lion) passed by there.
He shalach (puts) forth his yad (hand) on the flinty rock, and he overturns the har (mountains) by the roots.
He cuts out channels among the tzawar (rocks). His iyan (eye) raah (see) every precious thing.
He binds the streams that they don't trickle. The thing that is hidden he yatzaa (brings) forth to awar (light).
"But where shall chakamah (wisdom) be found? Where is the place of bayanah (understanding)?
anawash (man) doesn't yadai (know) its irak (price); Neither is it found in the aratz (land) of the chay (living).
The deep amar (says), ‘It isn't in me.' The yam (sea) amar (says), ‘It isn't with me.'
It can't be gotten for gold, neither shall kasap (silver) be weighed for its price.
It can't be valued with the gold of Awapayar, with the Yaqar onyx, or the sapphire.
Gold and glass can't equal it, neither shall it be exchanged for jewels of fine gold.
No zakar (mention) shall be made of coral or of crystal. Yes, the price of chakamah (wisdom) is above rubies.
The topaz of Kawash shall not equal it, Neither shall it be valued with tahawar (pure) gold.
Where then does chakamah (wisdom) bawaa (come) from? Where is the place of bayanah (understanding)?
Seeing it is hidden from the iyan (eyes) of all chay (living), and kept close from the birds of the sky.
abadawan (destruction) and mawath (death) amar (say), ‘We have heard a rumor of it with our ears.'
"Alahayam bayan (understands) its darak (way), and he yadai (knows) its place.
For he looks to the ends of the aratz (earth), and raah (see) under the whole sky.
He establishes the force of the rawach (wind). Yes, he measures out the mayam (waters) by measure.
When he made a chaq (decree) for the rain, and a darak (way) for the lightning of the qawal (thunder);
then he saw it, and declared it. He established it, yes, and searched it out.
To adam (man) he said, ‘Behold, the yaraah (fear) of the Adanay, that is chakamah (wisdom). To sawar (depart) from rai (evil) is bayanah (understanding).'
Ayawab again took up his parable, and said,
"Oh that I were as in the yarach (months) of qadam (old), as in the yawam (days) when Alawah watched over me;
when his nayar (lamp) shone on my raash (head), and by his awar (light) I walked through chashak (darkness),
as I was in the ripeness of my yawam (days), when the friendship of Alawah was in my ahal (tent),
when the Shaday was yet with me, and my children were around me,
when my steps were washed with butter, and the tzawar (rock) poured out palag (streams) of shaman (oil) for me,
when I went yatzaa (forth) to the city gate, when I prepared my mawashab (seat) in the street.
The nair (young) men saw me and hid themselves. The Yashayash rose up and stood.
The shar (princes) refrained from malah (talking), and laid their kap (hand) on their pah (mouth).
The chabaa (voice) of the nagayad (nobles) was hushed, and their lashawan (tongue) stuck to the roof of their chak (mouth).
For when the ear heard me, then it blessed me; and when the iyan (eye) saw me, it commended me:
Because I delivered the Inay who cried, and the fatherless also, who had none to help him,
the barakah (blessing) of him who was ready to abad (perish) came on me, and I caused the alamanah (widow's) lab (heart) to sing for joy.
I Labash on tzadaq (righteousness), and it Labash me. My justice was as a robe and a diadem.
I was iyan (eyes) to the iwar (blind), and feet to the Pasach.
I was a ab (father) to the Abayawan. The rayab (cause) of him who I didn't yadai (know), I searched out.
I broke the jaws of the iwal (unrighteous), and plucked the Tarap out of his teeth.
Then I said, ‘I shall gawai (die) in my own qan (house), I shall number my yawam (days) as the sand.
My root is spread out to the mayam (waters). The dew lies all lawan (night) on my branch.
My kabawad (glory) is Chadash in me. My qashath (bow) is renewed in my yad (hand).'
"Men listened to me, waited, and kept damam (silence) for my itzah (counsel).
achar (after) my dabar (words) they didn't shanah (speak) again. My speech fell on them.
They waited for me as for the rain. Their pah (mouths) drank as with the spring rain.
I smiled on them when they had no confidence. They didn't reject the awar (light) of my panayam (face).
I chose out their darak (way), and sat as raash (chief). I lived as a malak (king) in the gadawad (army), as one who nacham (comforts) the Abal.
"Tzaiyar now those who are younger than I have me in derision, whose abawath (fathers) I would have disdained to shayath (put) with my sheep dogs.
Of mah (what) use is the kach (strength) of their yad (hands) to me, men in whom ripe age has perished?
They are Galamawad from lack and famine. They gnaw the tzayah (dry) ground, in the gloom of waste and shawaa (desolation).
They pluck salt herbs by the bushes. The roots of the broom are their lacham (food).
They are driven out from the midst of men. They rawai (cry) after them as after a thief;
So that they shakan (dwell) in frightful nachal (valleys), and in holes of the ipar (earth) and of the rocks.
Among the bushes they bray; and under the nettles they are gathered together.
They are children of nabal (fools), yes, children of sham (base) men. They were flogged out of the aratz (land).
"Now I have become their song. Yes, I am a malah (byword) to them.
They abhor me, they stand aloof from me, and don't hesitate to spit in my panayam (face).
For he has untied his yathar (cord), and afflicted me; and they have thrown off restraint panayam (before) me.
On my yamayan (right) hand qawam (rise) the rabble. They thrust aside my feet, They cast up against me their arach (ways) of destruction.
They mar my nathayab (path), They yail (set) forward my hawah (calamity), without anyone's help.
As through a Rachab breach they come, in the midst of the ruin they roll themselves in.
Terrors have turned on me. They chase my honor as the rawach (wind). My yashawaih (welfare) has passed ibar (away) as a cloud.
"Now my napash (soul) is poured out within me. yawam (days) of affliction have taken achaz (hold) on me.
In the layal (night) season my itzam (bones) are pierced in me, and the pains that gnaw me take no shakab (rest).
By great kach (force) is my garment disfigured. It binds me about as the pah (collar) of my coat.
He has cast me into the mire. I have become like ipar (dust) and ashes.
I cry to you, and you do not answer me. I imad (stand) up, and you gaze at me.
You have turned to be Akazar to me. With the might of your yad (hand) you persecute me.
You nashaa (lift) me up to the rawach (wind), and drive me with it. You dissolve me in the storm.
For I yadai (know) that you will shawab (turn back / repent) me to mawath (death), To the bayath (house) mawaid (appointed) for all chay (living).
"However doesn't one shalach (stretch) out a yad (hand) in his fall? Or in his calamity therefore cry for help?
Didn't I weep for him who was in Qashah? Wasn't my napash (soul) grieved for the Abayawan?
When I looked for tawab (good), then rai (evil) came; When I waited for awar (light), there came apal (darkness).
My maih (heart) is troubled, and doesn't damam (rest). yawam (days) of affliction have qadam (come) on me.
I halak (go) mourning without the chamah (sun). I qawam (stand) up in the qahal (assembly), and cry for help.
I am a ach (brother) to jackals, and a rai (companion) to ostriches.
My skin grows black and peels from me. My itzam (bones) are burned with heat.
Therefore my harp has turned to mourning, and my pipe into the qawal (voice) of those who weep.
"I made a barayath (covenant) with my iyan (eyes), how then should I bayan (look) lustfully at a young bathawalah (woman)?
For what is the chalaq (portion) from Alawah above, and the nachalah (heritage) from the Shaday on high?
Is it not calamity to the iwal (unrighteous), and disaster to the pail (workers) of awan (iniquity)?
Doesn't he raah (see) my darak (ways), and number all my steps?
"If I have walked with falsehood, and my ragal (foot) has hurried to deceit
(let me be weighed in an even balance, that Alawah may yadai (know) my integrity);
if my step has turned out of the darak (way), if my lab (heart) walked achar (after) my iyan (eyes), if any defilement has stuck to my kap (hands),
then let me zarai (sow), and let achar (another) akal (eat). Yes, let the produce of my field be rooted out.
"If my lab (heart) has been enticed to a ashah (woman), and I have laid wait at my neighbor's door,
then let my ashah (wife) grind for achar (another), and let others sleep with her.
For that would be a zamah (heinous) crime. Yes, it would be an iwan (iniquity) to be punished by the palayal (judges):
For it is a ash (fire) that akal (consumes) to abadawan (destruction), and would root out all my increase.
"If I have despised the cause of my male amah (servant) or of my female servant, when they contended with me;
What then shall I do when Al qawam (rises) up? When he paqad (visits), what shall I shawab (turn back / repent) him?
Didn't he who made me in the womb ishah (make) him? Didn't one kawan (fashion) us in the womb?
"If I have withheld the Dal from their Chapatz, or have caused the iyan (eyes) of the alamanah (widow) to kalah (fail),
or have eaten my morsel yathawam (alone), and the fatherless has not eaten of it
(no, from my youth he grew up with me as with a ab (father), her have I guided from my am (mother's) womb);
if I have seen any abad (perish) for want of clothing, or that the Abayawan had no covering;
if his chalatz (heart) hasn't blessed me, if he hasn't been warmed with my sheep's fleece;
if I have lifted up my yad (hand) against the fatherless, because I saw my help in the gate,
then let my shoulder napal (fall) from the shoulder blade, and my arm be shabar (broken) from the bone.
For calamity from Al is a pachad (terror) to me. Because his majesty, I can do nothing.
"If I have made gold my hope, and have said to the fine gold, ‘You are my confidence;'
If I have Shamach because my wealth was rab (great), and because my yad (hand) had gotten much;
if I have seen the awar (sun) when it shined, or the yarach (moon) moving Yaqar splendor,
and my lab (heart) has been secretly enticed, and my yad (hand) threw a kiss from my pah (mouth),
this also would be an iwan (iniquity) to be punished by the palayalay (judges); for I should have denied the Al who is above.
"If I have Shamach at the destruction of him who hated me, or lifted up myself when rai (evil) found him;
(yes, I have not allowed my chak (mouth) to chataa (sin) by asking his napash (life) with a alah (curse));
if the men of my ahal (tent) have not said, ‘Who can find shabai (one) who has not been filled with his meat?'
(the foreigner has not lodged in the street, but I have opened my doors to the traveler);
if like adam (adam) I have covered my pashai (transgressions), by hiding my iwan (iniquity) in my chab (heart),
because I iratz (feared) the rab (great) multitude, and the contempt of mashapachah (families) terrified me, so that I kept damam (silence), and didn't yatzaa (go) out of the door—
oh that I had shamai (one) to hear me! (behold, here is my signature, let the Shaday answer me); let the accuser kathab (write) my indictment!
Surely I would nashaa (carry) it on my shoulder; and I would bind it to me as a itarah (crown).
I would nagad (declare) to him the number of my steps. as a nagayad (prince) would I qarab (go) near to him.
If my adamah (land) cries out against me, and its furrows weep together;
if I have eaten its kach (fruits) without kasap (money), or have caused its owners to napach (lose) their napash (life),
let briars yatzaa (grow) instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley." The dabar (words) of Ayawab are ended.
So these shalawash (three) men ceased to answer Ayawab, because he was tzadayaq (righteous) in his own iyan (eyes).

Then the ap (wrath) of Alayahaw the ban (son) of Barakaal, the Bawazay, of the mashapachah (family) of Ram, was kindled against Ayawab. His ap (wrath) was kindled because he justified himself rather than Alahayam.
Also his ap (wrath) was kindled against his shalawash (three) rai (friends), because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Ayawab.
Now Alayahaw had waited to speak to Ayawab, because they were zaqan (elder) than he.
When Alayahaw saw that there was no answer in the pah (mouth) of these shalawash (three) men, his ap (wrath) was kindled.
Alayahaw the ban (son) of Barakaal the Bawazay answered, "I am Tzaiyar, and you are very Yashayash; Therefore I held back, and didn't dare show you my dai (opinion).
I said, ‘yawam (days) should dabar (speak), and multitude of Shanah should yadai (teach) chakamah (wisdom).'
But there is a rawach (spirit) in anawash (man), and the nashamah (breath) of the Shaday gives them bayan (understanding).
It is not the rab (great) who are chakam (wise), nor the zaqan (aged) who bayan (understand) justice.
Therefore I said, ‘Listen to me; I also will show my dai (opinion).'
"Behold, I waited for your dabar (words), and I listened for your reasoning, while you searched out what to malah (say).
Yes, I gave you my full attention, but there was no one who convinced Ayawab, or who answered his amar (words), among you.
Beware lest you amar (say), ‘We have found chakamah (wisdom), Al may refute him, not ayash (man);'
for he has not directed his malah (words) against me; neither will I shawab (turn back / repent) him with your speeches.
"They are amazed. They answer no more. They don't have a malah (word) to say.
Shall I wait, because they don't dabar (speak), because they imad (stand) still, and answer no more?
I also will answer my chalaq (part), and I also will show my dai (opinion).
For I am malaa (full) of malah (words). The rawach (spirit) within me constrains me.
Behold, my breast is as yayan (wine) which has no pathach (vent); like Chadash wineskins it is ready to burst.
I will dabar (speak), that I may be refreshed. I will pathach (open) my shapah (lips) and answer.
Please don't let me nashaa (respect) any ayash (man's) panayam (person), neither will I give flattering titles to any adam (man).
For I don't yadai (know) how to give flattering titles; or else my Maker would Mait nashaa (take) me away.
"However, Ayawab, please hear my speech, and listen to all my dabar (words).
See now, I have opened my pah (mouth). My lashawan (tongue) has spoken in my chak (mouth).
My amar (words) shall utter the yashar (uprightness) of my lab (heart). That which my shapah (lips) daith (know) they shall speak Barar.
The rawach (spirit) of Al has made me, and the nashamah (breath) of the Shaday gives me chayah (life).
If you can, shawab (turn back / repent) me. Set your irak (words) in order panayam (before) me, and stand forth.
Behold, I am toward Al even as you are. I am also formed out of the clay.
Behold, my ayamah (terror) shall not make you afraid, neither shall my pressure be kabad (heavy) on you.
"Surely you have spoken in my hearing, I have heard the qawal (voice) of your malah (words), saying,
‘I am zak (clean), without disobedience. I am Chap, neither is there iwan (iniquity) in me.
Behold, he matzaa (finds) occasions against me. He chashab (counts) me for his ayab (enemy).
He shawam (puts) my feet in the stocks. He shamar (marks) all my arach (paths).'
"Behold, I will answer you. In this you are not tzadaq (just), for Alawah is greater than anawash (man).
Why do you rayab (strive) against him, because he doesn't give account of any of his dabar (matters)?
For Al dabar (speaks) achad (once), yes shanayam (twice), though shawar (man) pays no attention.
In a chalawam (dream), in a vision of the layal (night), when tharadamah (deep) sleep napal (falls) on men, in slumbering on the bed;
Then he galah (opens) the ears of men, and seals their instruction,
That he may sawar (withdraw) adam (man) from his purpose, and hide pride from gabar (man).
He keeps back his napash (soul) from the shachath (pit), and his chay (life) from perishing by the shalach (sword).
He is chastened also with pain on his bed, with continual strife in his itzam (bones);
So that his chay (life) abhors lacham (bread), and his napash (soul) dainty food.
His flesh is so consumed kalah (away), that it can't be seen. His itzam (bones) that were not seen stick out.
Yes, his napash (soul) qarab (draws) near to the shachath (pit), and his chay (life) to the mawath (destroyers).
"If there is beside him an malaak (angel), an Lawatz, one among a alap (thousand), to show to adam (man) what is yashar (right) for him;
then Alahayam is gracious to him, and amar (says), ‘Deliver him from yarad (going) down to the shachath (pit), I have found a kapar (ransom).'
His flesh shall be fresher than a child's. He shawab (turn back / repent) to the yawam (days) of his youth.
He prays to Alawah, and he is favorable to him, so that he raah (see) his panayam (face) with joy. He shawab (turn back / repent) to anawash (man) his tzadaqah (righteousness).
He sings before men, and amar (says), ‘I have sinned, and perverted that which was yashar (right), and it didn't profit me.
He has padah (redeemed) my napash (soul) from going into the shachath (pit). My chay (life) shall raah (see) the awar (light).'
"Behold, Al pail (works) all these things, paim (twice), yes three times, with a gabar (man),
to shawab (turn back / repent) back his napash (soul) from the shachath (pit), that he may be enlightened with the awar (light) of the chay (living).
Mark well, Ayawab, and listen to me. Hold your charash (peace), and I will dabar (speak).
If you have anything to malah (say), shawab (turn back / repent) me. dabar (speak), for I desire to justify you.
If not, listen to me. Hold your charash (peace), and I will teach you chakamah (wisdom).
Moreover Alayahaw answered,
"Hear my malah (words), you chakam (wise) men. Give ear to me, you who have yadai (knowledge).
For the ear tries malah (words), as the palate tastes akal (food).
