Let us choose for us that which is mashapat (right). Let us yadai (know) among ourselves what is tawab (good).
For Ayawab has said, ‘I am tzadaq (righteous), Al has taken sawar (away) my mashapat (right):
Notwithstanding my mashapat (right) I am considered a liar. My chatz (wound) is Anash, though I am without disobedience.'
What gabar (man) is like Ayawab, who drinks scorn like mayam (water),
Who goes in company with the pail (workers) of awan (iniquity), and yalak (walks) with rashai (wicked) men?
For he has said, ‘It profits a gabar (man) nothing that he should delight himself with Alahayam.'
"Therefore listen to me, you men of labab (understanding): far be it from Al, that he should do rashai (wickedness), from the Shaday, that he should commit iwal (iniquity).
For the pail (work) of a adam (man) he will shalam (render) to him, and cause every ayash (man) to matzaa (find) according to his arach (ways).
Yes surely, Al will not do wickedly, neither will the Shaday iwath (pervert) justice.
Who put him in paqad (charge) of the aratz (earth)? or who has appointed him over the whole world?
If he shawam (set) his lab (heart) on himself, If he gathered to himself his rawach (spirit) and his nashamah (breath),
all flesh would gawai (perish) together, and adam (man) would shawab (turn back / repent) again to ipar (dust).
"If now you have bayanah (understanding), hear this. Listen to the qawal (voice) of my malah (words).
Shall even one who shanaa (hates) justice govern? Will you rashai (condemn) him who is tzadayaq (righteous) and kabayar (mighty)?—
Who amar (says) to a malak (king), ‘Vile!' or to nadayab (nobles), ‘balayail (wicked)!'?
Who doesn't nashaa (respect) the panayam (persons) of shar (princes), nor nakar (respects) the rich more panayam (than) the Dal; for they all are the maishah (work) of his yad (hands).
In a moment they mawath (die), even at midnight. The im (people) are shaken and ibar (pass) away. The abayar (mighty) are taken ibar (away) without a yad (hand).
"For his iyan (eyes) are on the darak (ways) of a ayash (man). He raah (see) all his goings.
There is no chashak (darkness), nor thick gloom, where the pail (workers) of awan (iniquity) may hide themselves.
For he doesn't need to consider a ayash (man) further, that he should halak (go) before Al in mashapat (judgment).
He raii (breaks) in pieces kabayar (mighty) men in chaqar (ways) past finding out, and imad (sets) others in their place.
Therefore he takes nakar (knowledge) of their maibad (works). He overturns them in the layal (night), so that they are destroyed.
He strikes them as rashai (wicked) men in the open raah (see) of others;
because they turned sawar (aside) from following him, and wouldn't pay attention to any of his darak (ways),
so that they caused the cry of the Dal to bawaa (come) to him. He heard the cry of the Inay.
When he shaqat (gives) quietness, who then can rashai (condemn)? When he hides his panayam (face), who then can see him? Alike whether to a gaway (nation), or to a adam (man),
that the godless man may not malak (reign), that there be no mawaqash (one) to ensnare the im (people).
"For has any said to Al, ‘I am guilty, but I will not chabal (offend) any more.
Teach me that which I don't chazah (see). If I have done iwal (iniquity), I will do it no more'?
Shall his shalam (recompense) be as you desire, that you refuse it? For you must choose, and not I. Therefore dabar (speak) what you yadai (know).
Men of labab (understanding) will amar (tell) me, yes, every chakam (wise) gabar (man) who hears me:
‘Ayawab dabar (speaks) without daith (knowledge). His dabar (words) are without shakal (wisdom).'
I wish that were tried to the natzach (end), because of his answering like awan (wicked) men.
For he adds pashai (rebellion) to his chataah (sin). He claps his rabah (hands) among us, and multiplies his amar (words) against Al.
Moreover Alayahaw answered,
"Do you chashab (think) this to be your mashapat (right), or do you amar (say), ‘My tzadaq (righteousness) is more than al (god's),'
That you ask, ‘What advantage will it be to you? What yail (profit) shall I have, more than if I had sinned?'
I will shawab (turn back / repent) you, and your rai (companions) with you.
Look to the shamayam (heavens), and raah (see). See the shachaq (skies), which are higher than you.
If you have sinned, what effect do you have against him? If your pashai (transgressions) are multiplied, what do you do to him?
If you are tzadaq (righteous), what do you nathan (give) him? Or what does he receive from your yad (hand)?
Your rashai (wickedness) may hurt a ayash (man) as you are, and your tzadaqah (righteousness) may profit a ban (son) of adam (man).
"By reason of the multitude of oppressions they cry out. They cry for zarawai (help) by reason of the arm of the rab (mighty).
But none amar (says), ‘Where is Alawah my Maker, who nathan (gives) songs in the layal (night),
who teaches us more than the animals of the aratz (earth), and chakam (makes) us wiser than the birds of the sky?'
There they cry, but none gives answer, panayam (because) of the pride of rai (evil) men.
Surely Al will not hear an empty cry, neither will the Shaday regard it.
How much less when you amar (say) you don't see him. The cause is panayam (before) him, and you chawal (wait) for him!
But now, because he has not visited in his ap (anger), neither does he maad (greatly) yadai (regard) arrogance.
Therefore Ayawab opens his pah (mouth) with empty talk, and he multiplies malah (words) without daith (knowledge).
Alayahaw also continued, and said,
"Bear with me a little, and I will show you; for I still have something to malah (say) on God's behalf.
I will get my dai (knowledge) from Rachawaq, and will nathan (ascribe) tzadaq (righteousness) to my pail (maker).
For truly my malah (words) are not false. One who is thamayam (perfect) in daih (knowledge) is with you.
"Behold, Al is kabayar (mighty), and doesn't despise anyone. He is kabayar (mighty) in kach (strength) of lab (understanding).
He doesn't preserve the chayah (life) of the rashai (wicked), but nathan (gives) to the Inay their mashapat (right).
He doesn't withdraw his iyan (eyes) from the tzadayaq (righteous), but with malak (kings) on the kasaa (throne), he yashab (sets) them forever, and they are exalted.
If they are bound in fetters, and are taken in the cords of afflictions,
then he shows them their pail (work), and their pashai (transgressions), that they have behaved themselves proudly.
He also galah (opens) their ears to instruction, and commands that they shawab (turn back / repent) from awan (iniquity).
If they listen and ibad (serve) him, they shall kalah (spend) their yawam (days) in tawab (prosperity), and their Shanah in Naiyam.
But if they don't listen, they shall ibar (perish) by the shalach (sword); they shall gawai (die) without daith (knowledge).
"But those who are godless in lab (heart) shawam (lay) up ap (anger). They don't cry for help when he binds them.
They mawath (die) in youth. Their chay (life) perishes among the qadash (unclean).
He chalatz (delivers) the Inay by their affliction, and galah (opens) their ear in oppression.
Yes, he would have allured you out of distress, into a broad place, where there is no restriction. That which is nachath (set) on your table would be malaa (full) of fatness.
"But you are malaa (full) of the dayan (judgment) of the rashai (wicked). dayan (judgment) and dayan (justice) take hold of you.
Don't let riches entice you to chamah (wrath), neither let the great size of a kapar (bribe) natah (turn) you aside.
Would your wealth sustain you Batzar distress, or all the might of your kach (strength)?
Don't desire the layal (night), when im (people) are ilah (cut) off in their place.
shamar (take) heed, don't panah (regard) awan (iniquity); for you have chosen this rather than affliction.
Behold, Al is exalted in his kach (power). Who is a teacher like him?
Who has prescribed his darak (way) for him? Or who can amar (say), ‘You have committed iwal (unrighteousness)?'
"zakar (remember) that you magnify his pail (work), whereof men have sung.
All men have looked thereon. adam (man) chazah (sees) it Rachawaq off.
Behold, Al is Shagayaa, and we don't yadai (know) him. The number of his Shanah is unsearchable.
For he draws up the drops of mayam (water), which distill in rain from his vapor,
Which the shachaq (skies) pour down and which nazal (drop) on adam (man) abundantly.
Yes, can any bayan (understand) the spreading of the clouds, and the thunderings of his sakah (pavilion)?
Behold, he spreads his awar (light) around him. He covers the bottom of the yam (sea).
For by these he dayan (judges) the im (people). He nathan (gives) food in abundance.
He covers his kap (hands) with the awar (lightning), and tzawah (commands) it to strike the mark.
Its noise nagad (tells) about him, and the livestock also concerning the storm that ilah (comes) up.
"Yes, at this my lab (heart) trembles, and is moved out of its place.
Hear, oh, hear the ragaz (noise) of his voice, the qawal (sound) that goes out of his pah (mouth).
He sends it forth under the whole sky, and his awar (lightning) to the ends of the aratz (earth).
achar (after) it a qawal (voice) roars. He thunders with the qawal (voice) of his majesty. He doesn't hold back anything when his qawal (voice) is heard.
Al thunders marvelously with his qawal (voice). He does gadawal (great) things, which we can't yadai (comprehend).
For he amar (says) to the snow, ‘Fall on the aratz (earth);' likewise to the shower of rain, and to the showers of his mighty rain.
He seals up the yad (hand) of every adam (man), that all men whom he has made may yadai (know) it.
Then the animals bawaa (take) cover, and shakan (remain) in their dens.
Out of its room bawaa (comes) the sawapah (storm), and cold out of the north.
By the nashamah (breath) of Al, ice is given, and the breadth of the mayam (waters) is frozen.
Yes, he loads the thick cloud with moisture. He spreads abroad the cloud of his awar (lightning).
It is turned around by his guidance, that they may do whatever he tzawah (commands) them on the surface of the habitable world,
Whether it is for shabat (correction), or for his aratz (land), or for loving chasad (kindness), that he causes it to matzaa (come).
"Listen to this, Ayawab. imad (stand) still, and bayan (consider) the palaa (wondrous) works of Al.
Do you yadai (know) how Alawah controls them, and causes the awar (lightning) of his cloud to yapai (shine)?
Do you yadai (know) the workings of the clouds, the wondrous mapalaah (works) of him who is thamayam (perfect) in dai (knowledge)?
You whose clothing is Cham, when the aratz (earth) is still by reason of the south darawam (wind)?
Can you, with him, spread out the shachaq (sky), which is chazaq (strong) as a cast metal mirror?
yadai (teach) us what we shall amar (tell) him, for we can't make our case by panayam (reason) of chashak (darkness).
Shall it be told him that I would dabar (speak)? Or should a ayash (man) wish that he were swallowed up?
Now men don't raah (see) the awar (light) which is Bahayar in the shachaq (skies), but the rawach (wind) passes, and clears them.
Out of the tzapawan (north) comes golden splendor. With Alawah is awesome hawad (majesty).
We can't reach the Shaday. He is Shagayaa in kach (power). In justice and great tzadaqah (righteousness), he will not oppress.
Therefore men revere him. He doesn't raah (see) any who are chakam (wise) of lab (heart).
Then Yahawah answered Ayawab out of the whirlwind,
"Who is this who chashak (darkens) itzah (counsel) by malah (words) without daith (knowledge)?
Brace yourself like a gabar (man), for I will question you, then you yadai (answer) me!
"Where were you when I laid the yasad (foundations) of the aratz (earth)? nagad (declare), if you have bayanah (understanding).
Who determined its measures, if you yadai (know)? Or who stretched the line on it?
Whereupon were its foundations fastened? Or who laid its cornerstone,
when the baqar (morning) kawakab (stars) sang together, and all the ban (sons) of Alahayam shouted for joy?
"Or who shut up the yam (sea) with doors, when it broke gayach (forth) from the womb,
when I made clouds its garment, and wrapped it in thick irapal (darkness),
marked out for it my chaq (bound), shawam (set) bars and doors,
and said, ‘Here you may bawaa (come), but no further. Here your proud waves shall be shayath (stayed)?'
"Have you tzawah (commanded) the baqar (morning) in your yawam (days), and caused the dawn to yadai (know) its place;
that it might achaz (take) hold of the ends of the aratz (earth), and shake the rashai (wicked) out of it?
It is changed as clay under the seal, and stands forth as a garment.
From the rashai (wicked), their awar (light) is withheld. The high zarawai (arm) is shabar (broken).
"Have you entered into the springs of the yam (sea)? Or have you walked in the recesses of the deep?
Have the gates of mawath (death) been revealed to you? Or have you seen the gates of the shadow of tzalamawath (death)?
Have you comprehended the aratz (earth) in its breadth? nagad (declare), if you yadai (know) it all.
"What is the darak (way) to the dwelling of awar (light)? As for chashak (darkness), where is its place,
that you should take it to its bound, that you should bayan (discern) the nathayab (paths) to its bayath (house)?
Surely you yadai (know), for you were yalad (born) then, and the number of your yawam (days) is rab (great)!
Have you entered the treasuries of the snow, or have you seen the treasures of the hail,
which I have reserved against the ith (time) of tzar (trouble), against the yawam (day) of battle and war?
By what darak (way) is the awar (lightning) distributed, or the east qadayam (wind) scattered on the aratz (earth)?
Who has cut a channel for the flood shatap (water), or the darak (path) for the thunderstorm;
To cause it to rain on a aratz (land) where no ayash (man) is; on the madabar (wilderness), in which there is no adam (man);
to satisfy the waste and shawaa (desolate) mawatzaa (ground), to cause the tender grass to spring forth?
Does the rain have a ab (father)? Or who fathers the drops of dew?
Out of whose womb came the ice? The gray frost of the sky, who has given yalad (birth) to it?
The mayam (waters) become hard like aban (stone), when the surface of the deep is frozen.
"Can you qashar (bind) the cluster of the kayamah (pleiades), or loosen the cords of Kasayal?
Can you yatzaa (lead) forth the Mazarah in their ith (season)? Or can you guide the Iyash with her cubs?
Do you yadai (know) the laws of the shamayam (heavens)? Can you establish its dominion over the aratz (earth)?
"Can you lift up your qawal (voice) to the clouds, That abundance of mayam (waters) may cover you?
Can you shalach (send) forth lightnings, that they may yalak (go)? Do they amar (report) to you, ‘Here we are?'
Who has shayath (put) chakamah (wisdom) in the inward parts? Or who has given bayanah (understanding) to the mind?
Who can number the shachaq (clouds) by chakamah (wisdom)? Or who can pour out the bottles of the sky,
when the ipar (dust) runs into a mass, and the clods of dabaq (earth) stick together?
"Can you hunt the Tarap for the labayaa (lioness), or malaa (satisfy) the chay (appetite) of the young kapayar (lions),
when they crouch in their dens, and lie in wait in the thicket?
Who kawan (provides) for the raven his prey, when his yalad (young) ones cry to Al, and thaih (wander) for lack of food?
"Do you yadai (know) the ith (time) when the mountain goats give yalad (birth)? Do you shamar (watch) when the doe chawal (bears) fawns?
Can you number the yarach (months) that they fulfill? Or do you yadai (know) the ith (time) when they give birth?
They bow themselves, they bring forth their yalad (young), they end their chabal (labor) pains.
Their ban (young) ones become strong. They grow up in the open field. They yatzaa (go) forth, and don't shawab (turn back / repent) again.
"Who has shalach (set) the wild donkey Chapashay? Or who has loosened the bonds of the swift donkey,
Whose bayath (home) I have made the irabah (wilderness), and the malachah (salt) land his mashakan (dwelling) place?
He scorns the tumult of the city, neither does he hear the shouting of the driver.
The range of the har (mountains) is his pasture, He searches achar (after) every green thing.
"Will the wild ox be abah (content) to ibad (serve) you? Or will he stay by your feeding trough?
Can you hold the wild ox in the furrow with his harness? Or will he till the valleys achar (after) you?
Will you batach (trust) him, because his kach (strength) is rab (great)? Or will you leave to him your yagayai (labor)?
Will you confide in him, that he will shawab (turn back / repent) home your zarai (seed), and asap (gather) the grain of your threshing floor?
"The wings of the ostrich wave proudly; but are they the feathers and plumage of nawatzah (love)?
For she leaves her eggs on the aratz (earth), warms them in the ipar (dust),
and forgets that the ragal (foot) may zawar (crush) them, or that the shadah (wild) animal may trample them.
She deals harshly with her ban (young) ones, as if they were not hers. Though her yagayai (labor) is in vain, she is without pachad (fear),
because Alawah has deprived her of chakamah (wisdom), neither has he imparted to her bayanah (understanding).
When she lifts up herself on high, she scorns the horse and his rider.
"Have you given the horse might? Have you Labash his neck with a quivering mane?
Have you made him to leap as a locust? The glory of his snorting is awesome.
He paws in the valley, and rejoices in his kach (strength). He goes out to qaraah (meet) the nashaq (armed) men.
He mocks at pachad (fear), and is not dismayed, neither does he shawab (turn back / repent) back from the charab (sword).
The quiver rattles against him, the flashing spear and the javelin.
He eats up the aratz (ground) with fierceness and ragaz (rage), neither does he stand still at the qawal (sound) of the trumpet.
As often as the trumpet sounds he snorts, ‘Aha!' He rawach (smells) the battle Rachawaq off, the thunder of the shar (captains), and the shouting.
"Is it by your bayanah (wisdom) that the hawk soars, and stretches her wings toward the thayaman (south)?
Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up, and makes his nest on high?
On the cliff he shakan (dwells), and makes his home, on the point of the cliff, and the stronghold.
From there he spies out the prey. His iyan (eyes) see it Rachawaq off.
His young aparach (ones) also suck up dam (blood). Where the Chalal are, there he is.
Moreover Yahweh answered Job,
"Shall he who argues contend with the Almighty? He who argues with God, let him answer it.
Then answered Yahweh,
"Behold, I am of small account. What shall I answer you? I lay my hand on my mouth.
I have spoken once, and I will not answer; Yes, twice, but I will proceed no further.
Then Yahweh answered out of the whirlwind,
"Now brace yourself like a man. I will question you, and you will answer me.
Will you even annul my judgment? Will you condemn me, that you may be justified?
Or do you have an arm like God? Can you thunder with a voice like him?
"Now deck yourself with excellency and dignity. Array yourself with honor and majesty.
Pour out the fury of your anger. Look at everyone who is proud, and bring him low.
Look at everyone who is proud, and humble him. Crush the wicked in their place.
Hide them in the dust together. Bind their faces in the hidden place.
Then I will also admit to you that your own right hand can save you.
"See now, behemoth, which I made as well as you. He eats grass as an ox.
Look now, his strength is in his thighs. His force is in the muscles of his belly.
He moves his tail like a cedar. The sinews of his thighs are knit together.
His bones are like tubes of brass. His limbs are like bars of iron.
He is the chief of the ways of God. He who made him gives him his sword.
Surely the mountains produce food for him, where all the animals of the field play.
He lies under the lotus trees, in the covert of the reed, and the marsh.
The lotuses cover him with their shade. The willows of the brook surround him.
Behold, if a river overflows, he doesn't tremble. He is confident, though the Jordan swells even to his mouth.
Shall any take him when he is on the watch, or pierce through his nose with a snare?
Can you draw out Leviathan with a fishhook, or press down his lashawan (tongue) with a cord?
Can you shawam (put) a rope into his ap (nose), or naqab (pierce) his Lachay through with a hook?
Will he make many petitions to you, or will he dabar (speak) Rak words to you?
Will he karath (make) a barayath (covenant) with you, that you should take him for a ibad (servant) iwalam (forever)?
Will you play with him as with a bird? Or will you qashar (bind) him for your girls?
Will traders barter for him? Will they part him among the Kanainay?
Can you malaa (fill) his skin with barbed irons, or his raash (head) with fish spears?
shawam (lay) your kap (hand) on him. zakar (remember) the battle, and do so no more.
Behold, the hope of him is in vain. Won't tawal (one) be cast down even at the sight of him?
None is so Akazar that he dare stir him up. Who then is he who can stand panayam (before) me?
Who has first given to me, that I should shalam (repay) him? Everything under the shamayam (heavens) is mine.
"I will not charash (keep) silence concerning his limbs, nor his gabawarah (mighty) strength, nor his goodly frame.
Who can strip off his outer garment? Who shall bawaa (come) within his jaws?
Who can pathach (open) the doors of his panayam (face)? Around his teeth is ayamah (terror).
Strong magan (scales) are his pride, shut up together with a tzar (close) seal.
One is so near to another, that no rawach (air) can bawaa (come) between them.
They are joined one to ach (another). They stick together, so that they can't be pulled apart.
His sneezing flashes out awar (light). His iyan (eyes) are like the ipaip (eyelids) of the shachar (morning).
Out of his pah (mouth) halak (go) burning torches. Sparks of ash (fire) malat (leap) forth.
Out of his nostrils a ishan (smoke) goes, as of a boiling pot over a agamawan (fire) of reeds.
His napash (breath) lahat (kindles) coals. A lahab (flame) goes yatzaa (forth) from his pah (mouth).
There is iz (strength) in his neck. Terror dances panayam (before) him.
The flakes of his flesh are joined together. They are firm on him. They can't be moved.
His lab (heart) is as firm as a aban (stone), yes, firm as the Thachathay millstone.
When he raises himself up, the ayal (mighty) are gawar (afraid). They retreat before his thrashing.
If nashag (one) attacks him with the charab (sword), it can't prevail; nor the spear, the dart, nor the pointed shaft.
He chashab (counts) barazal (iron) as straw; and brass as rotten itz (wood).
The ban (arrow) can't make him flee. aban (sling) stones are like chaff to him.
Clubs are counted as stubble. He laughs at the rushing of the javelin.
His undersides are like sharp charash (potsherds), leaving a trail in the mud like a Charawatz sledge.
He makes the deep to boil like a pot. He shawam (makes) the yam (sea) like a pot of ointment.
He makes a nathayab (path) awar (shine) achar (after) him. One would chashab (think) the deep had white hair.
On ipar (earth) there is not his equal, that is made without chath (fear).
He raah (see) everything that is Gabah. He is malak (king) over all the ban (sons) of shachatz (pride).
Then Ayawab answered Yahawah,
"I yadai (know) that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be restrained.

You asked, ‘Who is this who ilam (hides) itzah (counsel) without daith (knowledge)?' therefore I have uttered that which I did not bayan (understand), things palaa (too) wonderful for me, which I didn't yadai (know).
You said, ‘Listen, now, and I will dabar (speak); I will question you, and you will yadai (answer) me.'
I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my iyan (eye) raah (see) you.
Therefore I abhor myself, and nacham (repent) in ipar (dust) and ashes.

It was so, that achar (after) Yahawah had spoken these dabar (words) to Ayawab, Yahawah said to Alayapaz the Thayamanay, "My ap (wrath) is kindled against you, and against your shanayam (two) rai (friends); for you have not spoken of me the thing that is kawan (right), as my ibad (servant) Ayawab has.

Now therefore, take to yourselves shabai (seven) bulls and shabai (seven) ayal (rams), and yalak (go) to my ibad (servant) Ayawab, and ilah (offer) up for yourselves a burnt ilah (offering); and my ibad (servant) Ayawab shall palal (pray) for you, for I will nashaa (accept) him, that I not ishah (deal) with you according to your folly. For you have not spoken of me the thing that is kawan (right), as my ibad (servant) Ayawab has.
So Alayapaz the Thayamanay and Baladad the Shawachay and Tzawapar the Naimathay went, and did what Yahawah commanded them, and Yahawah accepted Job.
Yahawah turned the captivity of Ayawab, when he prayed for his rai (friends). Yahawah gave Ayawab mashanah (twice) as much as he had before.

Then came there to him all his ach (brothers), and all his achawath (sisters), and all those who had been of his yadai (acquaintance) panayam (before), and ate lacham (bread) with him in his bayath (house). They comforted him, and consoled him concerning all the rai (evil) that Yahawah had brought on him. Everyone also gave him a piece of money, and everyone a ring of gold.

So Yahawah blessed the acharayath (latter) end of Ayawab more than his raashayath (beginning). He had fourteen alap (thousand) sheep, shash (six) alap (thousand) camels, one alap (thousand) tzamad (yoke) of oxen, and a alap (thousand) female donkeys.
He had also shabainah (seven) ban (sons) and shalawash (three) bath (daughters).
He called the sham (name) of the achad (first), Yamayamah; and the sham (name) of the shanay (second), Qatzayaih; and the sham (name) of the shalayashay (third), Qaranahapawak Happuch.
In all the aratz (land) were no women found so Yapah as the bath (daughters) of Ayawab. Their ab (father) gave them an nachalah (inheritance) among their ach (brothers).
achar (after) this Ayawab lived one maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) Shanah, and saw his ban (sons), and his ban (sons)' ban (sons), to arabai (four) dawar (generations).
So Ayawab died, being zaqan (old) and Shabai of yawam (days).

Blessed is the ayash (man) who doesn't halak (walk) in the itzah (counsel) of the rashai (wicked), nor imad (stand) in the darak (way) of chataa (sinners), nor yashab (sit) in the mawashab (seat) Lawatz scoffers;
but his Chapatz is in yahawah (yahweh's) thawarah (law). On his thawarah (law) he meditates yawamam (day) and layal (night).

He will be like a itz (tree) planted by the palag (streams) of mayam (water), that nathan (brings) forth its fruit in its ith (season), whose leaf also does not wither. Whatever he does shall tzalach (prosper).
The rashai (wicked) are not so, but are like the chaff which the rawach (wind) drives away.
Therefore the rashai (wicked) shall not qawam (stand) in the mashapat (judgment), nor chataa (sinners) in the idah (congregation) of the tzadayaq (righteous).
For Yahawah yadai (knows) the darak (way) of the tzadayaq (righteous), but the darak (way) of the rashai (wicked) shall abad (perish).
Why do the gawayam (nations) rage, and the laam (peoples) plot a vain thing?
The malak (kings) of the aratz (earth) take a stand, and the razan (rulers) take yasad (counsel) together, against Yahawah, and against his mashayach (anointed), saying,
"Let's break their bonds apart, and cast their cords from us.
He who yashab (sits) in the shamayam (heavens) will laugh. The Adanay will have them in derision.
Then he will dabar (speak) to them in his ap (anger), and terrify them in his charawan (wrath):
"Yet I have set my malak (king) on my qadash (holy) har (hill) of Tzayawan.
I will tell of the chaq (decree). Yahawah said to me, "You are my ban (son). Today I have become your father.
shaal (ask) of me, and I will nathan (give) the gawayam (nations) for your nachalah (inheritance), the apas (uttermost) parts of the aratz (earth) for your achazah (possession).
You shall raii (break) them with a shabat (rod) of barazal (iron). You shall dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel.
Now therefore be shakal (wise), you malak (kings). Be instructed, you shapat (judges) of the aratz (earth).
ibad (serve) Yahawah with yaraah (fear), and rejoice with trembling.
Give sincere homage to the bar (son), lest he be angry, and you abad (perish) in the darak (way), for his ap (wrath) will Mait be kindled. Blessed are all those who take refuge in him.
Yahawah, how my tzar (adversaries) have increased! Many are those who qawam (rise) up against me.
Many there are who amar (say) of my napash (soul), "There is no yashawaih (help) for him in Alahayam." salah (selah).
But you, Yahawah, are a magan (shield) around me, my kabawad (glory), and the rawam (one) who lifts up my raash (head).
I qaraa (cry) to Yahawah with my qawal (voice), and he answers me out of his qadash (holy) har (hill). salah (selah).
I laid myself down and slept. I awakened; for Yahawah samak (sustains) me.
I will not be yaraa (afraid) of rababah (tens) of thousands of im (people) who have shayath (set) themselves against me on every side.
qawam (arise), Yahawah! yashai (save) me, my Alahayam! For you have struck all of my ayab (enemies) on the Lachay bone. You have shabar (broken) the teeth of the rashai (wicked).
yashawaih (salvation) belongs to Yahawah. Your barakah (blessing) be on your im (people). salah (selah).
Answer me when I qaraa (call), Alahayam of my tzadaq (righteousness). Give me relief from my tzar (distress). Have chanan (mercy) on me, and hear my prayer.
You ban (sons) of men, how long shall my kabawad (glory) be turned into dishonor? Will you ahab (love) vanity, and seek after falsehood? salah (selah).
But yadai (know) that Yahawah has set apart for himself him who is chasayad (godly): Yahawah will hear when I qaraa (call) to him.
Stand in awe, and don't chataa (sin). Search your own labab (heart) on your bed, and be still. salah (selah).
zabach (offer) the zabach (sacrifices) of tzadaq (righteousness). batach (put) your trust in Yahawah.
Many amar (say), "Who will show us any tawab (good)?" Yahawah, let the awar (light) of your panayam (face) shine on us.
You have nathan (put) gladness in my lab (heart), more than when their grain and their new thayarawash (wine) are increased.
In shalawam (peace) I will both shakab (lay) myself down and sleep, for you, Yahawah badad (alone), yashab (make) me live in safety.
Give ear to my amar (words), Yahawah. bayan (consider) my meditation.
Listen to the qawal (voice) of my cry, my malak (king) and my Alahayam; for to you do I palal (pray).
Yahawah, in the baqar (morning) you shall hear my qawal (voice). In the baqar (morning) I will lay my requests before you, and will watch expectantly.
For you are not a Al who has Chapatz in rashai (wickedness). rai (evil) can't live with you.
The arrogant shall not stand in your iyan (sight). You shanaa (hate) all pail (workers) of awan (iniquity).
You will abad (destroy) those who dabar (speak) lies. Yahawah abhors the bloodthirsty and deceitful ayash (man).
But as for me, in the abundance of your loving chasad (kindness) I will bawaa (come) into your bayath (house). I will shachah (bow) toward your qadash (holy) hayakal (temple) in reverence of you.
Lead me, Yahawah, in your tzadaqah (righteousness) because of my sharar (enemies). Make your darak (way) yashar (straight) before my panayam (face).
For there is no kawan (faithfulness) in their pah (mouth). Their qarab (heart) is destruction. Their garawan (throat) is an pathach (open) tomb. They flatter with their lashawan (tongue).
asham (hold) them guilty, Alahayam. Let them napal (fall) by their own mawaitzah (counsels); Thrust them out in the multitude of their pashai (transgressions), for they have rebelled against you.
But let all those who take refuge in you Shamach, Let them always shout for joy, because you defend them. Let them also who ahab (love) your sham (name) be joyful in you.
For you will barak (bless) the tzadayaq (righteous). Yahawah, you will surround him with favor as with a tzanah (shield).
Yahawah, don't yakach (rebuke) me in your ap (anger), neither discipline me in your chamah (wrath).
Have chanan (mercy) on me, Yahawah, Amalal I am faint. Yahawah, heal me, for my itzam (bones) are troubled.
My napash (soul) is also in maad (great) anguish. But you, Yahawah —how long?
shawab (turn back / repent), Yahawah. chalatz (deliver) my napash (soul), and yashai (save) me for your loving chasad (kindness)' sake.
For in mawath (death) there is no zakar (memory) of you. In shaawal (sheol), who shall give you yadah (thanks)?
I am weary with my groaning. Every layal (night) I flood my bed. I drench my couch with my tears.
My iyan (eye) wastes away because of kais (grief). It grows old because of all my tzarar (adversaries).
sawar (depart) from me, all you pail (workers) of awan (iniquity), for Yahawah has heard the qawal (voice) of my weeping.
Yahawah has heard my supplication. Yahawah accepts my prayer.
May all my ayab (enemies) be bawash (ashamed) and dismayed. They shall shawab (turn back / repent) back, they shall be disgraced suddenly.
Yahawah, my Alahayam, I take refuge in you. yashai (save) me from all those who pursue me, and natzal (deliver) me,
lest they tear apart my napash (soul) like a aray (lion), ripping it in paraq (pieces), while there is none to natzal (deliver).
Yahawah, my Alahayam, if I have done this, if there is iwal (iniquity) in my kap (hands),
if I have rewarded rai (evil) to him who was at shalam (peace) with me (yes, if I have delivered him who without cause was my tzarar (adversary)),
let the ayab (enemy) pursue my napash (soul), and overtake it; yes, let him tread my chay (life) down to the aratz (earth), and shakan (lay) my kabawad (glory) in the ipar (dust). salah (selah).
qawam (arise), Yahawah, in your ap (anger). nashaa (lift) up yourself against the ibarah (rage) of my tzarar (adversaries). Awake for me. You have tzawah (commanded) mashapat (judgment).
Let the idah (congregation) of the laam (peoples) surround you. Rule over them on high.
Yahawah administers judgment to the im (peoples). dayan (judge) me, Yahawah, according to my tzadaq (righteousness), and to my tham (integrity) that is in me.
Oh let the wickedness of the rashai (wicked) come to an end, but kawan (establish) the tzadayaq (righteous); their minds and labah (hearts) are searched by the tzadayaq (righteous) Alahayam.
My magan (shield) is with Alahayam, who yashai (saves) the yashar (upright) in lab (heart).
Alahayam is a tzadayaq (righteous) shapat (judge), yes, a Al who has indignation every yawam (day).
If a man doesn't relent, he will sharpen his charab (sword); he has bent and strung his qashath (bow).
He has also prepared for himself the instruments of mawath (death). He pail (makes) ready his flaming chatz (arrows).
Behold, he chabal (travails) with awan (iniquity). Yes, he has conceived imal (mischief), and brought yalad (forth) falsehood.
He has dug a hole, and has fallen into the shachath (pit) which he made.
The imal (trouble) he causes shall shawab (turn back / repent) to his own raash (head). His violence shall yarad (come) down on the qadaqad (crown) of his own head.
I will give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah according to his tzadaq (righteousness), and will sing zamar (praise) to the sham (name) of Yahawah Most Ilayawan.
Yahawah, our Adawan, how majestic is your sham (name) in all the aratz (earth), who has nathan (set) your glory above the shamayam (heavens)!
From the lips of babes and infants you have established iz (strength), because of your tzarar (adversaries), that you might silence the ayab (enemy) and the avenger.
When I raah (see) your shamayam (heavens), the maishah (work) of your fingers, the yarach (moon) and the kawakab (stars), which you have ordained;
what is anawash (man), that you zakar (think) of him? What is the ban (son) of adam (man), that you care for him?
For you have made him a Mait lower than Alahayam, and crowned him with kabawad (glory) and honor.
You mashal (make) him ruler over the maishah (works) of your yad (hands). You have shayath (put) all things under his feet:
All sheep and cattle, yes, and the animals of the shadah (field),
The birds of the sky, the fish of the yam (sea), and whatever passes ibar (through) the arach (paths) of the yam (seas).
Yahawah, our Adawan, how majestic is your sham (name) in all the aratz (earth)!
I will give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah with my whole lab (heart). I will tell of all your marvelous palaa (works).
I will be Shamach and rejoice in you. I will sing zamar (praise) to your sham (name), O Most Ilayawan.
When my ayab (enemies) shawab (turn back / repent) back, they stumble and abad (perish) in your panayam (presence).
For you have maintained my mashapat (just) cause. You yashab (sit) on the kasaa (throne) judging righteously.
You have rebuked the gawayam (nations). You have destroyed the rashai (wicked). You have blotted out their sham (name) iwalam (forever) and ever.
The ayab (enemy) is overtaken by endless ruin. The very zakar (memory) of the cities which you have overthrown has perished.
But Yahawah reigns iwalam (forever). He has prepared his kasaa (throne) for mashapat (judgment).
He will shapat (judge) the world in tzadaq (righteousness). He will administer judgment to the laam (peoples) in uprightness.
Yahawah will also be a high tower for the Dak; a high tower in ith (times) of tzarah (trouble).
Those who yadai (know) your sham (name) will batach (put) their trust in you, for you, Yahawah, have not forsaken those who seek you.
Sing zamar (praises) to Yahawah, who yashab (dwells) in Tzayawan, and nagad (declare) among the im (people) what he has done.
For he who avenges dam (blood) zakar (remembers) them. He doesn't forget the cry Inaw the afflicted.
Have chanan (mercy) on me, Yahawah. raah (see) my affliction by those who shanaa (hate) me, and lift me up from the gates of mawath (death);
that I may show forth all your thahalah (praise). In the gates of the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan, I will rejoice in your yashawaih (salvation).
The gawayam (nations) have sunk down in the shachath (pit) that they made. In the net which they hid, their own ragal (foot) is taken.
Yahawah has made himself yadai (known). He has executed mashapat (judgment). The rashai (wicked) is snared by the pail (work) of his own kap (hands). Meditation. salah (selah).
The rashai (wicked) shall be turned back to shaawal (sheol), even all the gawayam (nations) that Shakach Alahayam.
For the Abayawan shall not natzach (always) be forgotten, nor the hope of the Inay abad (perish) id (forever).
qawam (arise), Yahawah! Don't let anawash (man) prevail. Let the gawayam (nations) be judged in your panayam (sight).
shayath (put) them in mawaraa (fear), Yahawah. Let the gawayam (nations) yadai (know) that they are only men. salah (selah).
Why do you imad (stand) Rachawaq off, Yahawah? Why do you ilam (hide) yourself in ith (times) of tzarah (trouble)?
In arrogance, the rashai (wicked) hunt Inay the weak. They are caught in the schemes that they chashab (devise).
For the rashai (wicked) halal (boasts) of his napash (heart's) cravings. He blesses the greedy, and condemns Yahawah.
The rashai (wicked), in the pride of his ap (face), has no room in his thoughts for Alahayam.
His darak (ways) are prosperous at all ith (times). He is haughty, and your mashapat (laws) are far from his sight. As for all his tzarar (adversaries), he sneers at them.
He amar (says) in his lab (heart), "I shall not be shaken. For dawar (generations) I shall have no rai (trouble).
His pah (mouth) is malaa (full) of alah (cursing), deceit, and oppression. Under his lashawan (tongue) is imal (mischief) and awan (iniquity).
He lies in wait near the villages. From ambushes, he harag (murders) the naqay (innocent). His iyan (eyes) are secretly set against the helpless.
He lurks in secret as a aray (lion) in his ambush. He lies in wait to catch the Inay. He catches the Inay, when he draws him in his net.
The helpless are crushed. They collapse. They napal (fall) under his strength.
He amar (says) in his lab (heart), "Al has forgotten. He hides his panayam (face). He will never raah (see) it.
qawam (arise), Yahawah! Al, nashaa (lift) up your yad (hand)! Don't forget the Inaw.
Why does the rashai (wicked) person condemn Alahayam, and amar (say) in his lab (heart), "Alahayam won't call me into account?
But you do see imal (trouble) and kais (grief). You nathan (consider) it to take it into your yad (hand). You help the victim and the fatherless.
shabar (break) the zarawai (arm) of the rashai (wicked). As for the evil darash (man), seek out his wickedness until you matzaa (find) none.
Yahawah is malak (king) id (forever) and ever! The gawayam (nations) will abad (perish) out of his aratz (land).
Yahawah, you have heard the desire of the Inaw. You will kawan (prepare) their lab (heart). You will cause your ear to hear,
to shapat (judge) the fatherless and the Dak, that anawash (man) who is of the aratz (earth) may terrify no more.
In Yahawah, I take refuge. How can you amar (say) to my napash (soul), "nawad (flee) as a bird to your har (mountain)!

For, behold, the rashai (wicked) bend their qashath (bows). They kawan (set) their chatz (arrows) on the yathar (strings), that they may shoot in apal (darkness) at the yashar (upright) in lab (heart).
If the foundations are destroyed, what can the tzadayaq (righteous) do?
Yahawah is in his qadash (holy) hayakal (temple). Yahawah is on his kasaa (throne) in shamayam (heaven). His iyan (eyes) observe. His ipaip (eyes) examine the children of men.
Yahawah examines the tzadayaq (righteous), but the rashai (wicked) and him who ahab (loves) violence his napash (soul) shanaa (hates).
On the rashai (wicked) he will rain blazing coals; ash (fire), sulfur, and scorching rawach (wind) shall be the portion of their cup.
For Yahawah is tzadayaq (righteous). He ahab (loves) tzadaqah (righteousness). The yashar (upright) shall chazah (see) his panayam (face).
yashai (help), Yahawah; for the chasayad (godly) man ceases. For the aman (faithful) fail from among the children of men.
Everyone lies to his neighbor. They dabar (speak) with chalaqah (flattering) shapah (lips), and with a lab (double) lab (heart).
May Yahawah karath (cut) off all chalaqah (flattering) shapah (lips), and the lashawan (tongue) that boasts,
who have said, "With our lashawan (tongue) we will gabar (prevail). Our shapah (lips) are our own. Who is Adawan over us?

"Because of the oppression Inay the weak and because of the groaning of the Abayawan, I will now qawam (arise)," amar (says) Yahawah; "I will shayath (set) him in yashai (safety) from those who malign him.
The amarah (sayings) of Yahawah are flawless amarah (sayings), as kasap (silver) refined in a clay furnace, purified shabaithayam (seven) times.
You will shamar (keep) them, Yahawah. You will preserve them from this dawar (generation) iwalam (forever).
The rashai (wicked) halak (walk) on every side, when what is vile is exalted among the ban (sons) of men.
How long, Yahawah? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your panayam (face) from me?
How long shall I shayath (take) itzah (counsel) in my napash (soul), having sorrow in my labab (heart) every yawamam (day)? How long shall my ayab (enemy) triumph over me?
Behold, and answer me, Yahawah, my Alahayam. Give awar (light) to my iyan (eyes), lest I sleep in mawath (death);
Lest my ayab (enemy) amar (say), "I have prevailed against him;" Lest my tzar (adversaries) rejoice when I fall.
But I batach (trust) in your loving chasad (kindness). My lab (heart) rejoices in your yashawaih (salvation).
I will shayar (sing) to Yahawah, because he has been good to me.
The nabal (fool) has said in his lab (heart), "There is no Alahayam." They are shachath (corrupt). They have done abominable ilayalah (works). There is none who does tawab (good).
Yahawah looked down from shamayam (heaven) on the children of men, to raah (see) if there were any who understood, who sought after Alahayam.
They have all gone sawar (aside). They have together become corrupt. There is none who does tawab (good), no, not one.
Have all the pail (workers) of awan (iniquity) no yadai (knowledge), who akal (eat) up my im (people) as they akal (eat) lacham (bread), and don't qaraa (call) on Yahawah?
There they were in pachad (great) pachad (fear), for Alahayam is in the dawar (generation) of the tzadayaq (righteous).
You frustrate the plan of the Inay, because Yahawah is his refuge.

Oh that the yashawaih (salvation) of Yasharaal (Israel) would come out of Tzayawan! When Yahawah restores the fortunes of his im (people), then Yaiqab shall rejoice, and Yasharaal (Israel) shall be Shamach.
Yahawah, who shall gawar (dwell) in your sanctuary? Who shall live on your qadash (holy) har (hill)?
He who halak (walks) blamelessly does what is tzadaq (right), and dabar (speaks) truth in his labab (heart);
He who doesn't slander with his lashawan (tongue), nor does rai (evil) to his rai (friend), nor nashaa (casts) slurs against his fellow man;
In whose iyan (eyes) a vile maas (man) is despised, but who honors those who yaraa (fear) Yahawah; he who keeps an shabai (oath) even when it raii (hurts), and doesn't change;
he who doesn't nathan (lend) out his kasap (money) for usury, nor take a shachad (bribe) against the naqay (innocent). He who does these things shall never be shaken.
shamar (preserve) me, Al, for in you do I take refuge.
My soul, you have said to Yahawah, "You are my Adawan. Apart from you I have no tawab (good) thing.
As for the qadawash (saints) who are in the aratz (earth), they are the adayar (excellent) ones in whom is all my Chapatz.
Their sorrows shall be multiplied who give gifts to achar (another) Alahayam. Their drink offerings of dam (blood) I will not offer, nor nashaa (take) their sham (names) on my shapah (lips).
Yahawah assigned my portion and my cup. You made my lot secure.
The lines have fallen to me in Naiyam places. Yes, I have a shapar (good) nachalah (inheritance).
I will barak (bless) Yahawah, who has given me yaitz (counsel). Yes, my kalayah (heart) instructs me in the layal (night) seasons.
I have set Yahawah always before me. Because he is at my right yamayan (hand), I shall not be moved.
Therefore my lab (heart) is Shamach, and my tongue rejoices. My body shall also shakan (dwell) in safety.
For you will not leave my napash (soul) in shaawal (sheol), neither will you allow your chasayad (holy) one to raah (see) shachath (corruption).
You will show me the arach (path) of chay (life). In your panayam (presence) is fullness of joy. In your right yamayan (hand) there are Naiyam forevermore.
Hear, Yahawah, my tzadaq (righteous) plea; Give ear to my prayer, that doesn't go out of deceitful shapah (lips).
Let my mashapat (sentence) yatzaa (come) forth from your panayam (presence). Let your iyan (eyes) chazah (look) on mayashar (equity).
You have proved my lab (heart). You have visited me in the layal (night). You have tried me, and found nothing. I have resolved that my pah (mouth) shall not disobey.
As for the pailah (works) of men, by the dabar (word) of your shapah (lips), I have kept myself from the arach (ways) of the violent.
My steps have held fast to your maigal (paths). My feet have not slipped.
I have called on you, for you will answer me, Al. natah (turn) your ear to me. Hear my amarah (sayings).
Show your marvelous loving chasad (kindness), you who yashai (save) those who take refuge by your right yamayan (hand) from their qawam (enemies).
shamar (keep) me as the apple of your eye. Hide me under the shadow of your wings,
from the rashai (wicked) who shadad (oppress) me, my napash (deadly) ayab (enemies), who surround me.
They close up their callous hearts. With their pah (mouth) they dabar (speak) proudly.
They have now surrounded us in our steps. They shayath (set) their iyan (eyes) to cast us down to the aratz (earth).
He is like a aray (lion) that is greedy of his prey, as it were a young kapayar (lion) yashab (lurking) in secret places.
qawam (arise), Yahawah, confront him. Cast him down. Deliver my napash (soul) from the rashai (wicked) by your charab (sword);

from men by your yad (hand), Yahawah, from men of the world, whose chalaq (portion) is in this chay (life). You malaa (fill) the belly of your cherished ones. Your ban (sons) have plenty, and they store up wealth for their children.
As for me, I shall chazah (see) your panayam (face) in tzadaq (righteousness). I shall be satisfied, when I qawatz (awake), with seeing your form.
I racham (love) you, Yahawah, my chazaq (strength).
Yahawah is my salai (rock), my fortress, and my deliverer; my Al, my tzawar (rock), in whom I take refuge; my magan (shield), and the qaran (horn) of my yashai (salvation), my high tower.
I qaraa (call) on Yahawah, who is halal (worthy) to be praised; and I am saved from my ayab (enemies).
The cords of mawath (death) surrounded me. The nachal (floods) of ungodliness made me afraid.
The cords of shaawal (sheol) were around me. The snares of mawath (death) came on me.
In my tzar (distress) I called on Yahawah, and cried to my Alahayam. He heard my qawal (voice) out of his hayakal (temple). My cry panayam (before) him came into his ears.
Then the aratz (earth) shook and trembled. The foundations also of the har (mountains) quaked and were shaken, because he was charah (angry).
ishan (smoke) went out of his ap (nostrils). Consuming ash (fire) came out of his pah (mouth). Coals were kindled by it.
He bowed the shamayam (heavens) also, and came down. Thick irapal (darkness) was under his feet.
He rode on a karawab (cherub), and flew. Yes, he soared on the wings of the rawach (wind).
He made chashak (darkness) his hiding place, his sakah (pavilion) around him, chashakah (darkness) of mayam (waters), thick clouds of the skies.
At the nagah (brightness) before him his thick clouds passed, hailstones and coals of ash (fire).
Yahawah also thundered in the sky. The Most Ilayawan uttered his qawal (voice): hailstones and coals of ash (fire).
He sent out his chatz (arrows), and scattered them; Yes, great lightning bolts, and routed them.
Then the apayaq (channels) of mayam (waters) raah (see). The foundations of the world were laid bare at your rebuke, Yahawah, at the nashamah (blast) of the rawach (breath) of your ap (nostrils).
He sent from on high. He took me. He drew me out of many mayam (waters).
He delivered me from my iz (strong) ayab (enemy), from those who hated me; for they were too mighty for me.
They came on me in the yawam (day) of my calamity, but Yahawah was my support.
He brought me yatzaa (forth) also into a large place. He delivered me, because he delighted in me.
Yahawah has rewarded me according to my tzadaq (righteousness). According to the cleanness of my yad (hands) has he recompensed me.
For I have kept the darak (ways) of Yahawah, and have not wickedly departed from my Alahayam.
For all his mashapat (ordinances) were before me. I didn't sawar (put) away his chaqah (statutes) from me.
I was also blameless with him. I kept myself from my iwan (iniquity).
Therefore Yahawah has rewarded me according to my tzadaq (righteousness), according to the cleanness of my yad (hands) in his eyesight.
With the chasayad (merciful) you will show yourself merciful. With the thamayam (perfect) gabar (man), you will show yourself thamam (perfect).
With the Barar, you will show yourself Barar. With the Iqash you will Iqash yourself shrewd.
For you will yashai (save) the Inay im (people), but the haughty iyan (eyes) you will bring down.
For you will awar (light) my nayar (lamp), Yahawah. My Alahayam will nagah (light) up my chashak (darkness).
For by you, I advance through a gadawad (troop). By my Alahayam, I leap over a wall.
As for Al, his darak (way) is thamayam (perfect). The amarah (sayings) of Yahawah is tried. He is a magan (shield) to all those who take refuge in him.
For who is Alawah, except Yahawah? Who is a tzawar (rock), zawalah (besides) our Alahayam,
the Al who arms me with chayal (strength), and nathan (makes) my darak (way) thamayam (perfect)?
He makes my feet like deer's feet, and imad (sets) me on my bamah (high) places.
He teaches my yad (hands) to war, so that my zarawai (arms) bend a qashath (bow) of bronze.
You have also given me the magan (shield) of your yashai (salvation). Your right yamayan (hand) sustains me. Your gentleness has made me great.
You have enlarged my steps under me, My feet have not slipped.
I will pursue my ayab (enemies), and overtake them. Neither will I shawab (turn back / repent) again until they are consumed.
I will strike them through, so that they will not be yakal (able) to qawam (rise). They shall napal (fall) under my feet.
For you have armed me with chayal (strength) to the battle. You have subdued under me those who rose up qawam (against) me.
You have also made my ayab (enemies) irap (turn) their backs to me, that I might tzamath (cut) off those who shanaa (hate) me.
They cried, but there was none to yashai (save); even to Yahawah, but he didn't answer them.
Then I beat them small as the ipar (dust) panayam (before) the rawach (wind). I cast them out as the mire of the streets.
You have delivered me from the rayab (strivings) of the im (people). You have made me the raash (head) of the gawayam (nations). A im (people) whom I have not yadai (known) shall ibad (serve) me.
As soon as they hear of me they shall obey me. The foreigners shall submit themselves to me.
The foreigners shall fade away, and shall come trembling out of their close places.
Yahawah chay (lives); and blessed be my tzawar (rock). Exalted be the Alahayam of my yashai (salvation),
even the Al who executes vengeance for me, and dabar (subdues) im (peoples) under me.
He rescues me from my ayab (enemies). Yes, you lift me up above those who rawam (rise) up against me. You natzal (deliver) me from the violent ayash (man).
Therefore I will give yadah (thanks) to you, Yahawah, among the gawayam (nations), and will sing zamar (praises) to your sham (name).
He gives great yashawaih (deliverance) to his malak (king), and shows loving chasad (kindness) to his mashayach (anointed), to Dawad and to his zarai (seed), forevermore.
The shamayam (heavens) declare the kabawad (glory) of Al. The expanse shows his handiwork.
yawam (day) after yawam (day) they pour forth amar (speech), and layal (night) after layal (night) they display daith (knowledge).
There is no amar (speech) nor dabar (language), where their qawal (voice) is not heard.
Their qaw (voice) has gone out through all the aratz (earth), their malah (words) to the end of the world. In them he has shawam (set) a ahal (tent) for the shamash (sun),
which is as a chathan (bridegroom) coming out of his room, like a strong gabawar (man) rejoicing to run his course.
His going forth is from the end of the shamayam (heavens), his circuit to its ends; There is nothing hidden from its chamah (heat).
yahawah (yahweh's) thawarah (law) is thamayam (perfect), restoring the napash (soul). yahawah (yahweh's) idawath (testimony) is aman (sure), making chakam (wise) the Pathay.
yahawah (yahweh's) paqawad (precepts) are yashar (right), Shamach the lab (heart). yahawah (yahweh's) matzawah (commandment) is bar (pure), enlightening the iyan (eyes).
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is tahawar (clean), enduring id (forever). yahawah (yahweh's) mashapat (ordinances) are amath (true), and tzadaq (righteous) altogether.
More to be desired are they than gold, yes, than much fine gold; Mathawaq also than honey and the extract of the honeycomb.
Moreover by them is your ibad (servant) warned. In keeping them there is rab (great) reward.
Who can bayan (discern) his errors? Forgive me from hidden errors.
Keep back your ibad (servant) also from Zad sins. Let them not have mashal (dominion) over me. Then I will be thamam (upright). I will be blameless and innocent of rab (great) pashai (transgression).
Let the amar (words) of my pah (mouth) and the meditation of my lab (heart) be acceptable in your panayam (sight), Yahawah, my tzawar (rock), and my gaal (redeemer).
May Yahawah answer you in the yawam (day) of tzarah (trouble). May the sham (name) of the Alahayam of Yaiqab set you up on high,
shalach (send) you help from the qadash (sanctuary), grant you support from Tzayawan,
zakar (remember) all your manachah (offerings), and accept your ilah (burnt) sacrifice. salah (selah).
May He nathan (grant) you your labab (heart's) desire, and fulfill all your itzah (counsel).
We will triumph in your yashawaih (salvation). In the sham (name) of our Alahayam, we will set up our banners. May Yahawah grant all your requests.

Now I yadai (know) that Yahawah yashai (saves) his mashayach (anointed). He will answer him from his qadash (holy) shamayam (heaven), with the yashai (saving) gabawarah (strength) of his right yamayan (hand).
Some trust in chariots, and some in horses, but we trust the sham (name) of Yahawah our Alahayam.
They are bowed down and fallen, but we qawam (rise) up, and stand iwad (upright).
yashai (save), Yahawah! Let the malak (king) answer us when we qaraa (call)!
The malak (king) Shamach in your iz (strength), Yahawah! How maad (greatly) he rejoices in your yashawaih (salvation)!
You have given him his lab (heart's) desire, and have not withheld the request of his shapah (lips). salah (selah).
For you qadam (meet) him with the barakah (blessings) of goodness. You shayath (set) a itarah (crown) of fine gold on his raash (head).
He asked chay (life) of you, you gave it to him, even arak (length) of yawam (days) iwalam (forever) and ever.
His kabawad (glory) is gadawal (great) in your yashawaih (salvation). You lay honor and hadar (majesty) on him.
For you shayath (make) him most blessed id (forever). You shayath (make) him glad with joy in your panayam (presence).
For the malak (king) batach (trusts) in Yahawah. Through the loving chasad (kindness) of the Most Ilayawan, he shall not be moved.
