Oh taste and raah (see) that Yahawah is tawab (good). Blessed is the gabar (man) who takes refuge in him.
Oh yaraa (fear) Yahawah, you his qadawash (saints), for there is no lack with those who yaraa (fear) him.
The young kapayar (lions) do lack, and suffer hunger, but those who seek Yahawah shall not lack any tawab (good) thing.
yalak (come), you children, listen to me. I will teach you the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah.
Who is someone who Chapatz chay (life), and ahab (loves) many yawam (days), that he may raah (see) tawab (good)?
Keep your lashawan (tongue) from rai (evil), and your shapah (lips) from speaking lies.
sawar (depart) from rai (evil), and do tawab (good). seek shalawam (peace), and pursue it.
yahawah (yahweh's) iyan (eyes) are toward the tzadayaq (righteous). His ears listen to their cry.
yahawah (yahweh's) panayam (face) is against those who do rai (evil), to karath (cut) off their zakar (memory) from the aratz (earth).
The righteous cry, and Yahawah hears, and natzal (delivers) them out of all their tzarah (troubles).
Yahawah is qarawab (near) to those who have a shabar (broken) lab (heart), and yashai (saves) those who have a Dakaa rawach (spirit).
Many are the rai (afflictions) of the tzadayaq (righteous), but Yahawah natzal (delivers) him out of them all.
He protects all of his itzam (bones). Not one of them is shabar (broken).
rai (evil) shall mawath (kill) the rashai (wicked). Those who shanaa (hate) the tzadayaq (righteous) shall be condemned.
Yahawah padah (redeems) the napash (soul) of his ibad (servants). None of those who take refuge in him shall be condemned.
rayab (contend), Yahawah, with those who rayab (contend) with me. Fight against those who fight against me.
chazaq (take) hold of magan (shield) and tzanah (buckler), and qawam (stand) up for my help.
Brandish the spear and block those who pursue me. amar (tell) my napash (soul), "I am your yashawaih (salvation).
Let those who seek after my napash (soul) be disappointed and brought to dishonor. Let those who plot my ruin be turned back and chapar (confounded).
Let them be as chaff panayam (before) the rawach (wind), yahawah (yahweh's) malaak (angel) driving them on.
Let their darak (way) be chashak (dark) and slippery, yahawah (yahweh's) malaak (angel) pursuing them.
For without cause they have hidden their net in a shachath (pit) for me. Without cause they have dug a pit for my napash (soul).
Let shawaa (destruction) bawaa (come) on him yadai (unawares). Let his net that he has hidden catch himself. Let him napal (fall) into that shawaa (destruction).
My napash (soul) shall be joyful in Yahawah. It shall rejoice in his yashawaih (salvation).
All my itzam (bones) shall amar (say), "Yahawah, who is like you, who natzal (delivers) the Inay from him who is too chazaq (strong) for him; yes, the Inay and the Inay from him who robs him?
Unrighteous witnesses qawam (rise) up. They shaal (ask) me about things that I don't yadai (know) about.
They shalam (reward) me rai (evil) for tawab (good), to the bereaving of my napash (soul).
But as for me, when they were chalah (sick), my clothing was sackcloth. I afflicted my napash (soul) with fasting. My prayer returned into my own bosom.
I behaved myself as though it had been my rai (friend) or my ach (brother). I bowed down mourning, as one who Abal his am (mother).

But in my adversity, they Shamach, and gathered themselves asap (together). The Nakah gathered themselves asap (together) against me, and I didn't yadai (know) it. They tore at me, and didn't damam (cease).
Like the profane Laig in feasts, they gnashed their teeth at me.
Adanay, how long will you raah (see) on? shawab (turn back / repent) my napash (soul) from their shawaa (destruction), my precious life from the kapayar (lions).
I will give you yadah (thanks) in the rab (great) qahal (assembly). I will halal (praise) you among many im (people).
Don't let those who are my ayab (enemies) wrongfully Shamach over me; neither let those who shanaa (hate) me without a cause wink their iyan (eyes).
For they don't dabar (speak) shalawam (peace), but they chashab (devise) deceitful dabar (words) against those who are Ragai in the aratz (land).
Yes, they opened their pah (mouth) wide amar (against) me. They said, "Aha! Aha! Our iyan (eye) has seen it!
You have seen it, Yahawah. Don't charash (keep) silent. Adawan, don't be rachaq (far) from me.
qawatz (wake) up! Rise up to defend me, my Alahayam! My Adanay, rayab (contend) for me!
Vindicate me, Yahawah my Alahayam, according to your tzadaq (righteousness). Shamach let them gloat over me.
Don't let them amar (say) in their lab (heart), "Aha! That's the way we want it!" Don't let them amar (say), "We have swallowed him up!
Let them be disappointed and confounded together who Shamach at my rai (calamity). Let them be Labash with bashath (shame) and dishonor who magnify themselves against me.
Let them shout for joy and be Shamach, who Chapatz my tzadaq (righteous) cause. Yes, let them amar (say) continually, "Yahawah be magnified, who has Chapatz in the prosperity of his ibad (servant)!
My lashawan (tongue) shall talk about your tzadaq (righteousness) and about your thahalah (praise) all yawam (day) long.
An oracle is qarab (within) my lab (heart) about the disobedience of the rashai (wicked): "There is no pachad (fear) of Alahayam before his iyan (eyes).
For he flatters himself in his own iyan (eyes), too much to detect and shanaa (hate) his sin.
The dabar (words) of his pah (mouth) are awan (iniquity) and deceit. He has ceased to be shakal (wise) and to do yatab (good).
He plots awan (iniquity) on his bed. He sets himself in a darak (way) that is not tawab (good). He doesn't abhor rai (evil).
Your loving chasad (kindness), Yahawah, is in the shamayam (heavens). Your amawanah (faithfulness) reaches to the shachaq (skies).
Your tzadaqah (righteousness) is like the harar (mountains) of Al. Your mashapat (judgments) are like a rab (great) deep. Yahawah, you yashai (preserve) adam (man) and animal.
How Yaqar is your loving chasad (kindness), Alahayam! The children of men take refuge under the shadow of your wings.
They shall be abundantly satisfied with the abundance of your bayath (house). You will shaqah (make) them drink of the nachal (river) of your Idan.
For with you is the spring of chay (life). In your awar (light) shall we raah (see) awar (light).
Oh continue your loving chasad (kindness) to those who yadai (know) you, your tzadaqah (righteousness) to the yashar (upright) in lab (heart).
Don't let the ragal (foot) of pride bawaa (come) against me. Don't let the yad (hand) of the rashai (wicked) drive me away.
There the pail (workers) of awan (iniquity) are fallen. They are thrust down, and shall not be yakal (able) to qawam (rise).
Don't charah (fret) because of evildoers, neither be envious against those who ishah (work) iwal (unrighteousness).
For they shall soon be cut down like the grass, and wither like the green herb.
batach (trust) in Yahawah, and do tawab (good). shakan (dwell) in the aratz (land), and enjoy safe pasture.
Also delight yourself in Yahawah, and he will nathan (give) you the desires of your lab (heart).
Commit your darak (way) to Yahawah. batach (trust) also in him, and he will do this:
he will make your tzadaq (righteousness) yatzaa (go) forth as the awar (light), and your justice as the noon tzahar (day) sun.

damam (rest) in Yahawah, and chawal (wait) patiently for him. Don't charah (fret) because of him who tzalach (prospers) in his darak (way), because of the ayash (man) who ishah (makes) mazamah (wicked) plots happen.
rapah (cease) from ap (anger), and forsake chamah (wrath). Don't charah (fret), it leads only to evildoing.
For evildoers shall be karath (cut) off, but those who wait for Yahawah shall yarash (inherit) the aratz (land).
For yet a Mait while, and the rashai (wicked) will be no more. Yes, though you bayan (look) for his place, he isn't there.
But the Inaw shall yarash (inherit) the aratz (land), and shall delight themselves in the abundance of shalawam (peace).
The rashai (wicked) plots against the tzadayaq (just), and gnashes at him with his teeth.
The Adanay will laugh at him, for he raah (see) that his yawam (day) is coming.
The rashai (wicked) have drawn out the charab (sword), and have bent their qashath (bow), to napal (cast) down the Inay and Inay, to kill those who are yashar (upright) in the darak (way).
Their charab (sword) shall bawaa (enter) into their own lab (heart). Their qashath (bows) shall be shabar (broken).
tawab (better) is a Mait that the tzadayaq (righteous) has, than the abundance of many rashai (wicked).
For the zarawai (arms) of the rashai (wicked) shall be shabar (broken), but Yahawah samak (upholds) the tzadayaq (righteous).
Yahawah yadai (knows) the yawam (days) of the thamayam (perfect). Their nachalah (inheritance) shall be iwalam (forever).
They shall not be disappointed in the ith (time) of rai (evil). In the yawam (days) of famine they shall be satisfied.
But the rashai (wicked) shall abad (perish). The ayab (enemies) of Yahawah shall be Yaqar the beauty of the fields. They will vanish— vanish like ishan (smoke).
The rashai (wicked) borrow, and don't shalam (pay) back, but the tzadayaq (righteous) nathan (give) generously.
For such as are blessed by him shall yarash (inherit) the aratz (land). Those who are cursed by him shall be karath (cut) off.
A gabar (man's) goings are established by Yahawah. He delights in his darak (way).
Though he stumble, he shall not fall, for Yahawah samak (holds) him up with his yad (hand).
I have been nair (young), and now am zaqan (old), yet I have not seen the tzadayaq (righteous) forsaken, nor his children begging for lacham (bread).
All yawam (day) long he chanan (deals) graciously, and lends. His zarai (seed) is blessed.
sawar (depart) from rai (evil), and do tawab (good). Live securely iwalam (forever).
For Yahawah ahab (loves) justice, and doesn't forsake his chasayad (saints). They are preserved iwalam (forever), but the children of the rashai (wicked) shall be karath (cut) off.
The tzadayaq (righteous) shall yarash (inherit) the aratz (land), and live in it id (forever).
The pah (mouth) of the tzadayaq (righteous) talks of chakamah (wisdom). His lashawan (tongue) speaks justice.
The thawarah (law) of his Alahayam is in his lab (heart). None of his steps shall slide.
The rashai (wicked) watches the tzadayaq (righteous), and seeks to mawath (kill) him.
Yahawah will not leave him in his yad (hand), nor rashai (condemn) him when he is judged.
Wait for Yahawah, and shamar (keep) his darak (way), and he will exalt you to yarash (inherit) the aratz (land). When the rashai (wicked) are karath (cut) off, you shall raah (see) it.
I have seen the rashai (wicked) in great irayatz (power), spreading himself like a Rainan tree in its native soil.
But he passed ibar (away), and behold, he was not. Yes, I sought him, but he could not be found.
shamar (mark) the tham (perfect) man, and raah (see) the yashar (upright), for there is a future for the ayash (man) of shalawam (peace).
As for transgressors, they shall be destroyed together. The future of the rashai (wicked) shall be karath (cut) off.
But the thashawaih (salvation) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is from Yahawah. He is their stronghold in the ith (time) of tzarah (trouble).
Yahawah helps them, and rescues them. He rescues them from the rashai (wicked), and yashai (saves) them, Because they have taken refuge in him.
Yahawah, don't yakach (rebuke) me in your qatzap (wrath), neither chasten me in your chamah (hot) displeasure.
For your chatz (arrows) have pierced me, your yad (hand) presses hard on me.
There is no soundness in my flesh panayam (because) of your indignation, neither is there any shalawam (health) in my itzam (bones) panayam (because) of my chataah (sin).
For my iwan (iniquities) have gone over my raash (head). As a Kabad mashaa (burden), they are too Kabad for me.
My wounds are baash (loathsome) and corrupt, panayam (because) of my foolishness.
I am pained and bowed down maad (greatly). I halak (go) mourning all yawam (day) long.
For my waist is filled with burning. There is no soundness in my flesh.
I am faint and severely bruised. I have groaned by reason of the anguish of my lab (heart).
Adanay, all my desire is before you. My groaning is not hidden from you.
My lab (heart) throbs. My kach (strength) fails me. As for the awar (light) of my iyan (eyes), it has also left me.
My lovers and my rai (friends) imad (stand) aloof from my nagai (plague). My kinsmen imad (stand) Rachawaq away.
They also who seek after my napash (life) lay snares. Those who seek my rai (hurt) dabar (speak) hawah (mischievous) things, and meditate deceits all yawam (day) long.
But I, as a Charash shamai (man), don't hear. I am as a mute alam (man) who doesn't pathach (open) his pah (mouth).
Yes, I am as a ayash (man) who doesn't hear, in whose pah (mouth) are no reproofs.
For in you, Yahawah, do I hope. You will answer, Adanay my Alahayam.
For I said, "Shamach let them gloat over me, or exalt themselves over me when my ragal (foot) slips.
For I am kawan (ready) to fall. My pain is continually before me.
For I will nagad (declare) my iwan (iniquity). I will be sorry for my chataah (sin).
But my ayab (enemies) are vigorous and many. Those who shanaa (hate) me without reason are numerous.
They who also shalam (render) rai (evil) for tawab (good) are shatan (adversaries) to me, because I follow what is tawab (good).
Don't forsake me, Yahawah. My Alahayam, don't be rachaq (far) from me.
Hurry to help me, Adanay, my thashawaih (salvation).
I said, "I will shamar (watch) my darak (ways), so that I don't chataa (sin) with my lashawan (tongue). I will shamar (keep) my pah (mouth) with a bridle while the rashai (wicked) is before me.
I was mute with silence. I held my chashah (peace), even from tawab (good). My sorrow was stirred.
My lab (heart) was hot qarab (within) me. While I meditated, the ash (fire) burned: I spoke with my lashawan (tongue):
"Yahawah, show me my end, what is the measure of my yawam (days). Let me yadai (know) how Chadal I am.
Behold, you have made my yawam (days) tapach (handbreadths). My lifetime is as nothing before you. Surely every adam (man) natzab (stands) as a habal (breath)." salah (selah).
"Surely every ayash (man) halak (walks) like a shadow. Surely they busy themselves in vain. He heaps up, and doesn't yadai (know) who shall asap (gather).
Now, Adanay, what do I wait for? My hope is in you.
natzal (deliver) me from all my pashai (transgressions). Don't shawam (make) me the reproach of the foolish.
I was mute. I didn't pathach (open) my pah (mouth), because you did it.
sawar (remove) your scourge sawar (away) from me. I am overcome by the blow of your yad (hand).
When you rebuke and correct ayash (man) for iwan (iniquity), You masah (consume) his wealth like a moth. Surely every adam (man) is but a habal (breath)." salah (selah).
"Hear my prayer, Yahawah, and give ear to my cry. Don't be charash (silent) at my tears. For I am a stranger with you, a foreigner, as all my abawath (fathers) were.
Oh shaih (spare) me, that I may recover balag (strength), before I yalak (go) away, and exist no more.
I waited patiently for Yahawah. He turned to me, and heard my cry.
He brought me up also out of a horrible bawar (pit), out of the miry clay. He qawam (set) my feet on a salai (rock), and gave me a kawan (firm) place to stand.
He has nathan (put) a Chadash song in my pah (mouth), even thahalah (praise) to our Alahayam. Many shall raah (see) it, and yaraa (fear), and shall batach (trust) in Yahawah.
Blessed is the gabar (man) who shawam (makes) Yahawah his trust, and doesn't panah (respect) the proud, nor such as shawat (turn) aside to lies.

Many, Yahawah, my Alahayam, are the palaa (wonderful) ishah (works) which you have done, and your machashabah (thoughts) which are toward us. They can't be declared back to you. If I would nagad (declare) and dabar (speak) of them, they are more than can be numbered.
zabach (sacrifice) and manachah (offering) you didn't desire. You have opened my ears. You have not required burnt ilah (offering) and chataah (sin) offering.
Then I said, "Behold, I have bawaa (come). It is written about me in the book in the scroll.
I delight to do your will, my Alahayam. Yes, your thawarah (law) is within my maih (heart).
I have proclaimed glad news of tzadaq (righteousness) in the rab (great) qahal (assembly). Behold, I will not seal my shapah (lips), Yahawah, you yadai (know).

I have not hidden your tzadaqah (righteousness) within my lab (heart). I have declared your amawanah (faithfulness) and your thashawaih (salvation). I have not concealed your loving chasad (kindness) and your truth from the rab (great) qahal (assembly).
Don't withhold your tender racham (mercies) from me, Yahawah. Let your loving chasad (kindness) and your truth continually preserve me.

For innumerable rai (evils) have surrounded me. My iwan (iniquities) have overtaken me, so that I am not yakal (able) to raah (see) up. They are more than the hairs of my raash (head). My lab (heart) has failed me.
Be pleased, Yahawah, to natzal (deliver) me. Hurry to help me, Yahawah.
Let them be disappointed and chapar (confounded) together who seek after my napash (soul) to sapah (destroy) it. Let them be turned backward and brought to dishonor who Chapatz in my rai (hurt).
Let them be shamam (desolate) by reason of their bashath (shame) that amar (tell) me, "Aha! Aha!
Let all those who seek you rejoice and be Shamach in you. Let such as ahab (love) your thashawaih (salvation) amar (say) continually, "Let Yahawah be exalted!
But I am Inay and Abayawan. May the Adanay chashab (think) about me. You are my help and my deliverer. Don't delay, my Alahayam.
Blessed is he who shakal (considers) the Dal. Yahawah will malat (deliver) him in the yawam (day) of rai (evil).
Yahawah will shamar (preserve) him, and chayah (keep) him alive. He shall be blessed on the aratz (earth), and he will not surrender him to the will of his ayab (enemies).
Yahawah will sustain him on his sickbed, and restore him from his bed of illness.
I said, "Yahawah, have chanan (mercy) on me! Heal me, for I have sinned against you.
My ayab (enemies) amar (speak) rai (evil) against me: "When will he mawath (die), and his sham (name) abad (perish)?
If he bawaa (comes) to raah (see) me, he dabar (speaks) falsehood. His lab (heart) gathers awan (iniquity) to itself. When he goes abroad, he dabar (tells) it.
All who shanaa (hate) me whisper together against me. They chashab (imagine) the rai (worst) for me.
"An balayail (evil) dabar (disease)," they say, "has afflicted him. Now that he lies he shall qawam (rise) up no more.
Yes, my own shalawam (familiar) friend, in whom I trusted, who ate lacham (bread) with me, has lifted up his heel against me.
But you, Yahawah, have chanan (mercy) on me, and qawam (raise) me up, that I may shalam (repay) them.
By this I yadai (know) that you delight in me, because my ayab (enemy) doesn't rawai (triumph) over me.
As for me, you uphold me in my tham (integrity), and natzab (set) me in your panayam (presence) iwalam (forever).
Blessed be Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), from iwalam (forever) and to iwalam (forever)! aman (amen) and aman (amen).
As the deer pants for the mayam (water) apayaq (brooks), so my napash (soul) pants after you, Alahayam.
My napash (soul) thirsts for Alahayam, for the chay (living) Al. When shall I bawaa (come) and raah (see) panayam (before) Alahayam?
My tears have been my lacham (food) yawamam (day) and layal (night), yawam (while) they continually ask me, "Where is your Alahayam?

These things I zakar (remember), and pour out my napash (soul) within me, how I used to ibar (go) with the crowd, and led them to the bayath (house) of Alahayam, with the qawal (voice) of joy and thawadah (praise), a multitude keeping a holy day.
Why are you in despair, my napash (soul)? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in Alahayam! For I shall still yadah (praise) him for the yashawaih (saving) help of his panayam (presence).
My Alahayam, my napash (soul) is in despair within me. Therefore I zakar (remember) you from the aratz (land) of the Yaradan, the Charamawanayam of Hermon, from the har (hill) Mizar.
Deep qaraa (calls) to deep at the qawal (noise) of your waterfalls. All your waves and your billows have swept over me.
Yahawah will tzawah (command) his loving chasad (kindness) in the yawamam (daytime). In the layal (night) his song shall be with me: a prayer to the Al of my chay (life).
I will ask Al, my salai (rock), "Why have you forgotten me? Why do I yalak (go) mourning because of the oppression of the ayab (enemy)?
As with a ratzach (sword) in my itzam (bones), my tzarar (adversaries) reproach me, yawam (while) they continually ask me, "Where is your Alahayam?

Why are you in despair, my napash (soul)? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in Alahayam! For I shall still yadah (praise) him, the yashawaih (saving) help of my panayam (countenance), and my Alahayam.
Vindicate me, Alahayam, and rayab (plead) my rayab (cause) against an ungodly gaway (nation). Oh, deliver me from deceitful and iwal (wicked) men.
For you are the Alahayam of my maiwaz (strength). Why have you rejected me? Why do I halak (go) mourning because of the oppression of the ayab (enemy)?
Oh, shalach (send) out your awar (light) and your truth. Let them lead me. Let them bawaa (bring) me to your qadash (holy) har (hill), To your mashakan (tents).
Then I will bawaa (go) to the mazabach (altar) of Alahayam, to Al, my exceeding joy. I will yadah (praise) you on the harp, Alahayam, my Alahayam.
Why are you in despair, my napash (soul)? Why are you disturbed within me? Hope in Alahayam! For I shall still yadah (praise) him: my Savior, my helper, and my Alahayam.
We have heard with our ears, Alahayam; our abawath (fathers) have told us, what pail (work) you did in their yawam (days), in the yawam (days) of qadam (old).
You drove out the gawayam (nations) with your yad (hand), but you planted them. You afflicted the laam (peoples), but you shalach (spread) them abroad.

For they didn't yarash (get) the aratz (land) in yarash (possession) by their own charab (sword), neither did their own zarawai (arm) yashai (save) them; but your right yamayan (hand), and your zarawai (arm), and the awar (light) of your panayam (face), because you were favorable to them.
You are my malak (king), Alahayam. tzawah (command) victories for Yaiqab!
Through you, will we push down our tzar (adversaries). Through your sham (name), will we tread them under who qawam (rise) up against us.
For I will not batach (trust) in my qashath (bow), neither shall my charab (sword) yashai (save) me.
But you have saved us from our tzar (adversaries), and have shamed those who shanaa (hate) us.
In Alahayam we have made our halal (boast) all yawam (day) long, we will give yadah (thanks) to your sham (name) iwalam (forever). salah (selah).
But now you rejected us, and brought us to dishonor, and don't yatzaa (go) out with our tzabaa (armies).
You make us shawab (turn back / repent) back from the tzar (adversary). Those who shanaa (hate) us take spoil for themselves.
You have made us like sheep for food, and have scattered us among the gawayam (nations).
You sell your im (people) for nothing, and have gained nothing from their sale.
You shawam (make) us a reproach Shakan our neighbors, a scoffing and a derision to those who are around us.
You shawam (make) us a byword among the gawayam (nations), a shaking of the raash (head) among the laam (peoples).
All day long my dishonor is before me, and bashath (shame) covers my panayam (face),
At the taunt of charap (one) who reproaches and verbally abuses, panayam (because) of the ayab (enemy) and the avenger.
All this has bawaa (come) on us, yet have we not forgotten you, Neither have we been false to your barayath (covenant).
Our lab (heart) has not turned back, neither have our steps strayed from your arach (path),
Though you have crushed us in the haunt of jackals, and covered us with the shadow of tzalamawath (death).

sabab (walk) about Tzayawan, and naqap (go) around her. Number its magadal (towers).
shayath (mark) lab (well) her bulwarks. Consider her palaces, that you may tell it Acharawan the next dawar (generation).

Hear this, all you im (peoples). Listen, all you yashab (inhabitants) of the world,

Those who batach (trust) in their wealth, and halal (boast) in the multitude of their riches—
ayash (none) of them can by any padah (means) padah (redeem) his ach (brother), nor nathan (give) Alahayam a kapar (ransom) for him.

That he should chayah (live) on forever, that he should not raah (see) shachath (corruption).
For he raah (see) that chakam (wise) men mawath (die); likewise the Kasayal and the Bair abad (perish), and leave their wealth to others.

Their qarab (inward) thought is that their bayath (houses) will endure iwalam (forever), and their mashakan (dwelling) places to all dawar (generations). They qaraa (name) their adamah (lands) after themselves.

he shall bawaa (go) to the dawar (generation) of his abawath (fathers). They shall laa (never) raah (see) the awar (light).

The Mighty One, Alahayam, Yahawah, dabar (speaks), and qaraa (calls) the aratz (earth) from sunrise to sunset.

The nabal (fool) has said in his lab (heart), "There is no Alahayam." They are shachath (corrupt), and have done abominable iwal (iniquity). There is no one who does tawab (good).

yashai (save) me, Alahayam, by your sham (name). Vindicate me in your might.

For he has delivered me out of all tzarah (trouble). My iyan (eye) has seen triumph over my ayab (enemies).

yaraah (fearfulness) and trembling have bawaa (come) on me. Horror has overwhelmed me.
I said, "Oh that I had wings like a dove! Then I would fly away, and be at shakan (rest).

yawamam (day) and layal (night) they prowl around on its walls. Malice and abuse are also qarab (within) her.

But you, Alahayam, will yarad (bring) them down into the baar (pit) of shachath (destruction). Bloodthirsty and deceitful men shall not live out half their yawam (days), but I will batach (trust) in you.
Be chanan (merciful) to me, Alahayam, for anawash (man) wants to swallow me up. All yawam (day) long, he attacks and oppresses me.

When I am yaraa (afraid), I will batach (put) my trust in you.
In Alahayam, I halal (praise) his dabar (word). In Alahayam, I batach (put) my trust. I will not be yaraa (afraid). What can flesh do to me?
All yawam (day) long they twist my dabar (words). All their machashabah (thoughts) are against me for rai (evil).
They conspire and lurk, watching my steps, they are eager to take my napash (life).
Shall they escape by awan (iniquity)? In ap (anger) yarad (cast) down the im (peoples), Alahayam.
You number my wanderings. You shawam (put) my tears into your bottle. Aren't they in your book?

Be chanan (merciful) to me, Alahayam, be chanan (merciful) to me, for my napash (soul) takes refuge in you. Yes, in the shadow of your wings, I will take refuge, until disaster has passed.
I qaraa (cry) out to Alahayam Most Ilayawan, to Al who accomplishes my requests for me.

The rashai (wicked) zawar (go) astray from the womb. They are wayward as soon as they are born, speaking lies.
Their chamah (poison) is damawath (like) the chamah (poison) of a snake; like a Charash cobra that stops its ear,
which doesn't listen to the qawal (voice) of charmers, no matter how skillful the charmer may be.
haras (break) their teeth, Alahayam, in their pah (mouth). nathatz (break) out the great teeth of the young kapayar (lions), Yahawah.

Before your pots can bayan (feel) the heat of the Atad, he will sweep away the green and the burning alike.

Yes, even when I am old and gray-haired, Alahayam, don't forsake me, until I have declared your zarawai (strength) to the next dawar (generation), your might to everyone who is to bawaa (come).
Your tzadaqah (righteousness) also, Alahayam, reaches to the marawam (heavens); you have done gadawal (great) things. Alahayam, who is like you?
You, who have shown us many and bitter tzarah (troubles), you will let me chayah (live). You will ilah (bring) us up again from the depths of the aratz (earth).
Increase my honor, and nacham (comfort) me again.
I will also yadah (praise) you with the harp for your amath (faithfulness), my Alahayam. I zamar (sing) kanawar (praises) to you with the lyre, qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).
My shapah (lips) shall shout for joy! My napash (soul), which you have padah (redeemed), sings zamar (praises) to you!
My lashawan (tongue) will also talk about your tzadaqah (righteousness) all yawam (day) long, for they are disappointed, and they are confounded, who want to rai (harm) me.
Alahayam, nathan (give) the malak (king) your justice; your tzadaqah (righteousness) to the malak (royal) ban (son).
He will dayan (judge) your im (people) with tzadaq (righteousness), and your Inay with justice.
The har (mountains) shall nashaa (bring) prosperity to the im (people). The Gabaih bring the fruit of tzadaqah (righteousness).
He will shapat (judge) the Inay of the im (people). He will yashai (save) the children of the Abayawan, and will break the oppressor in dakaa (pieces).
They shall yaraa (fear) you while the shamash (sun) panayam (endures); and as long as the yarach (moon), throughout all dawar (generations).
He will yarad (come) down like rain on the mown grass, as showers that zarazayap (water) the aratz (earth).
In his yawam (days), the tzadayaq (righteous) shall flourish, and abundance of shalawam (peace), until the yarach (moon) is no more.
He shall have radah (dominion) also from yam (sea) to yam (sea), from the nahar (river) to the apas (ends) of the aratz (earth).
Those who dwell in the tzayay (wilderness) shall bow panayam (before) him. His ayab (enemies) shall lick the ipar (dust).
The malak (kings) of Tharashayash and of the islands will shawab (turn back / repent) tribute. The malak (kings) of Shabaa and Sabaa shall qarab (offer) ashakar (gifts).
Yes, all malak (kings) shall shachah (fall) down before him. All gawayam (nations) shall ibad (serve) him.
For he will natzal (deliver) the Abayawan when he cries; the Inay, who has no helper.
He will have pity on the Dal and Dal. He will yashai (save) the napash (souls) of the Abayawan.
He will gaal (redeem) their napash (soul) from oppression and violence. Their dam (blood) will be precious in his iyan (sight).
They shall chayah (live), and to him shall be given of the gold of Shabaa. Men shall palal (pray) for him continually. They shall barak (bless) him all yawam (day) long.
Abundance of grain shall be throughout the aratz (land). Its fruit sways like Labanawan. Let it flourish, thriving like the grass of the aratz (field).
His sham (name) endures iwalam (forever). His sham (name) continues as long as the shamash (sun). Men shall be blessed by him. All gawayam (nations) will ashar (call) him blessed.
barak (praise) be to Yahawah Alahayam, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), who alone does palaa (marvelous) deeds.
Blessed be his kabawad (glorious) sham (name) iwalam (forever)! Let the whole aratz (earth) be filled with his kabawad (glory)! aman (amen) and aman (amen).
This kalah (ends) the prayers by Dawad, the ban (son) of Yashay.
Surely Alahayam is tawab (good) to Yasharaal (Israel), to those who are bar (pure) in labab (heart).
But as for me, my feet were Mait natah (gone). My steps had nearly slipped.
For I was envious of the arrogant, when I saw the prosperity of the rashai (wicked).
For there are no struggles in their mawath (death), but their awal (strength) is Barayaa.
They are free from burdens of men, neither are they plagued like other men.
Therefore pride is like a chain around their neck. Violence covers them like a garment.
Their iyan (eyes) bulge with fat. Their labab (minds) ibar (pass) the limits of mashakayath (conceit).
They scoff and dabar (speak) with malice. In arrogance, they threaten oppression.
They have set their pah (mouth) in the shamayam (heavens). Their lashawan (tongue) halak (walks) through the aratz (earth).
Therefore their im (people) shawab (turn back / repent) to them, and they drink up mayam (waters) Malaa abundance.
They amar (say), "How does Al yadai (know)? Is there daih (knowledge) in the Most Ilayawan?
Behold, these are the rashai (wicked). Being always at shalaw (ease), they increase in riches.
Surely in vain I have cleansed my labab (heart), and washed my kap (hands) in innocence,
For all yawam (day) long have I been plagued, and punished every baqar (morning).
If I had said, "I will amar (speak) thus;" behold, I would have betrayed the dawar (generation) of your children.
When I tried to yadai (understand) this, it was too imal (painful) for me;
Until I entered al (god's) maqadash (sanctuary), and considered their acharayath (latter) end.
Surely you shayath (set) them in chalaqah (slippery) places. You napal (throw) them down to destruction.
How they are suddenly destroyed! They are completely swept away with terrors.
As a chalawam (dream) when one qawatz (wakes) up, so, Adanay, when you awake, you will despise their fantasies.
For my soul was grieved. I was embittered in my kalayah (heart).
I was so Bair and yadai (ignorant). I was a brute beast before you.
Nevertheless, I am continually with you. You have held my yamayan (right) yad (hand).
You will guide me with your itzah (counsel), and afterward receive me to kabawad (glory).
Whom do I have in shamayam (heaven)? There is no one on aratz (earth) whom I desire besides you.
My flesh and my labab (heart) kalah (fails), but Alahayam is the tzawar (strength) of my labab (heart) and my chalaq (portion) iwalam (forever).
For, behold, those who are Rachaq from you shall abad (perish). You have destroyed all those who are unfaithful to you.
But it is tawab (good) for me to come close to Alahayam. I have made the Adanay Yahawah my refuge, that I may tell of all your malaakah (works).
Alahayam, why have you rejected us forever? Why does your ap (anger) smolder against the sheep of your pasture?
zakar (remember) your idah (congregation), which you purchased of qadam (old), which you have redeemed to be the tribe of your nachalah (inheritance); har (mount) Tzayawan, in which you have lived.
Lift up your feet to the natzach (perpetual) ruins, all the raii (evil) that the ayab (enemy) has done in the qadash (sanctuary).
Your tzarar (adversaries) have roared in the qarab (midst) of your mawaid (assembly). They have shawam (set) up their standards as awath (signs).
They behaved like men wielding axes, cutting through a thicket of itz (trees).
Now they break all its pathawach (carved) work down with hatchet and hammers.
They have burned your maqadash (sanctuary) to the aratz (ground). They have profaned the mashakan (dwelling) place of your sham (name).
They said in their lab (heart), "We will crush them completely." They have burned up all the mawaid (places) in the aratz (land) where Al was worshiped.
We raah (see) no miraculous awath (signs). There is no longer any nabayaa (prophet), neither is there among us anyone who yadai (knows) how long.
How long, Alahayam, shall the tzar (adversary) reproach? Shall the ayab (enemy) blaspheme your sham (name) forever?
Why do you shawab (turn back / repent) back your yad (hand), even your right yad (hand)? kalah (take) it out of your pocket and consume them!
Yet Alahayam is my malak (king) of qadam (old), working yashawaih (salvation) in the qarab (midst) of the aratz (earth).
You divided the yam (sea) by your iz (strength). You broke the raash (heads) of the thanayan (sea) monsters in the mayam (waters).
You broke the raash (heads) of Leviathan in pieces. You gave him as food to im (people) and tzayay (desert) creatures.
You opened up spring and nachal (stream). You dried up ayathan (mighty) nahar (rivers).
The yawam (day) is yours, the layal (night) is also yours. You have prepared the maawar (light) and the shamash (sun).
You have natzab (set) all the boundaries of the aratz (earth). You have made qayatz (summer) and winter.
zakar (remember) this, that the ayab (enemy) has mocked you, Yahawah. Foolish im (people) have blasphemed your sham (name).
Don't nathan (deliver) the napash (soul) of your dove to wild chay (beasts). Don't forget the chay (life) of your Inay forever.
Honor your barayath (covenant), for haunts of violence fill the dark naah (places) of the aratz (earth).
Don't let the Dak shawab (turn back / repent) kalam (ashamed). Let the Inay and Abayawan halal (praise) your sham (name).
qawam (arise), Alahayam! rayab (plead) your own rayab (cause). zakar (remember) how the foolish nabal (man) mocks you all yawam (day).
Don't forget the qawal (voice) of your tzarar (adversaries). The tumult of those who qawam (rise) up against you ilah (ascends) continually.
We give yadah (thanks) to you, Alahayam. We give yadah (thanks), for your sham (name) is qarawab (near). Men tell about your wondrous palaa (works).
When I choose the mawaid (appointed) time, I will shapat (judge) blamelessly.
The aratz (earth) and all its yashab (inhabitants) quake. I firmly hold its pillars. salah (selah).
I said to the arrogant, "Don't halal (boast)!" I said to the rashai (wicked), "Don't lift up the qaran (horn).
Don't lift up your qaran (horn) on high. Don't dabar (speak) with a Ithaq neck.
For neither from the east, nor from the west, nor yet from the madabar (south), comes exaltation.
But Alahayam is the shapat (judge). He puts down rawam (one), and lifts up another.

For in the yad (hand) of Yahawah there is a cup, full of foaming yayan (wine) mixed Malaa spices. He pours it out. Indeed the rashai (wicked) of the aratz (earth) drink and drink it to its very dregs.
But I will nagad (declare) this iwalam (forever): I will sing zamar (praises) to the Alahayam of Yaiqab.
I will cut off all the qaran (horns) of the rashai (wicked), but the qaran (horns) of the tzadayaq (righteous) shall be lifted up.
In Yahawadah (Judah), Alahayam is yadai (known). His sham (name) is gadawal (great) in Yasharaal (Israel).
His sak (tabernacle) is also in Shalam; His dwelling place in Tzayawan.
There he broke the flaming arrows of the bow, the magan (shield), and the charab (sword), and the weapons of war. salah (selah).
awar (glorious) are you, and adayar (excellent), more than harar (mountains) Tarap game.
abayar (valiant) men lie plundered, they have slept their last shanah (sleep). None of the men of chayal (war) can lift their yad (hands).
At your rebuke, Alahayam of Yaiqab, both chariot and horse are radam (cast) into a deep sleep.
You, even you, are to be feared. Who can imad (stand) in your panayam (sight) when you are angry?
You pronounced dayan (judgment) from shamayam (heaven). The aratz (earth) feared, and was silent,
when Alahayam qawam (arose) to mashapat (judgment), to yashai (save) all the Inaw ones of the aratz (earth). salah (selah).
Surely the chamah (wrath) of adam (man) yadah (praises) you. The survivors of your chamah (wrath) are restrained.
Make nadar (vows) to Yahawah your Alahayam, and fulfill them! Let all of his neighbors bring presents to him who is to be mawaraa (feared).
He will batzar (cut) off the rawach (spirit) of nagayad (princes). He is feared by the malak (kings) of the aratz (earth).
My cry goes to Alahayam! Indeed, I qawal (cry) to Alahayam for help, and for him to listen to me.
In the yawam (day) of my tzarah (trouble) I sought the Adanay. My yad (hand) was stretched out in the layal (night), and didn't get tired. My napash (soul) refused to be comforted.
I zakar (remember) Alahayam, and I groan. I complain, and my rawach (spirit) is overwhelmed. salah (selah).
You achaz (hold) my eyelids open. I am so troubled that I can't dabar (speak).
I have considered the yawam (days) of qadam (old), the Shanah of ancient times.
I zakar (remember) my song in the layal (night). I consider in my own labab (heart); my rawach (spirit) diligently inquires:
"Will the Adanay reject us iwalam (forever)? Will he be favorable no more?
Has his loving chasad (kindness) vanished forever? Does his amar (promise) fail for dawar (generations)?
Has Al forgotten to be gracious? Has he, in ap (anger), withheld his racham (compassion)?" salah (selah).
Then I thought, "I will appeal to this: the Shanah of the right yamayan (hand) of the Most Ilayawan.
I will zakar (remember) yah (yah's) deeds; for I will zakar (remember) your palaa (wonders) of qadam (old).
I will also meditate on all your pail (work), and consider your ilayalah (doings).
Your darak (way), Alahayam, is in the qadash (sanctuary). What Alahayam is gadawal (great) like Al?
You are the Al who does palaa (wonders). You have made your iz (strength) yadai (known) among the im (peoples).
You have redeemed your im (people) with your zarawai (arm), the ban (sons) of Yaiqab and Yawasap. salah (selah).
The mayam (waters) saw you, Alahayam. The mayam (waters) saw you, and they writhed. The depths also convulsed.
The clouds poured out mayam (water). The shachaq (skies) resounded with qawal (thunder). Your arrows also flashed around.
The qawal (voice) of your thunder was in the whirlwind. The lightnings lit up the world. The thabal (earth) trembled and shook.
Your darak (way) was through the yam (sea); your shabayal (paths) through the rab (great) mayam (waters). Your footsteps were not yadai (known).
You led your im (people) like a flock, by the yad (hand) of Mashah and Aharawan.
Hear my teaching, my im (people). natah (turn) your ears to the amar (words) of my pah (mouth).
I will pathach (open) my pah (mouth) in a parable. I will utter dark sayings of qadam (old),
Which we have heard and yadai (known), and our abawath (fathers) have told us.
We will not hide them from their children, telling to the dawar (generation) to Acharawan the thahalah (praises) of Yahawah, his izawaz (strength), and his wondrous palaa (works) that he has done.

For he established a idawath (testimony) in Yaiqab, and appointed a teaching in Yasharaal (Israel), which he tzawah (commanded) our abawath (fathers), that they should yadai (make) them known to their children;
that the dawar (generation) to Acharawan might yadai (know), even the children who should be yalad (born); who should qawam (arise) and tell their children,
that they might shawam (set) their hope in Alahayam, and not forget the mailal (works) of Al, but keep his matzawah (commandments),

and might not be as their abawath (fathers), a stubborn and rebellious dawar (generation), a dawar (generation) that didn't kawan (make) their lab (hearts) loyal, whose rawach (spirit) was not steadfast with Al.
The children of Aparayam, being armed and carrying qashath (bows), turned hapak (back) in the yawam (day) of battle.
They didn't shamar (keep) alahayam (god's) barayath (covenant), and refused to yalak (walk) in his thawarah (law).
They forgot his ilayalah (doings), his wondrous ilayalah (works) that he had shown them.
He did marvelous things in the sight of their abawath (fathers), in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, in the shadah (field) of Tzain.
He split the yam (sea), and caused them to ibar (pass) through. He made the mayam (waters) natzab (stand) as a heap.
In the yawamam (daytime) he also led them with a cloud, and all layal (night) with a awar (light) of ash (fire).
He split tzawar (rocks) in the madabar (wilderness), and gave them shaqah (drink) abundantly as out of the depths.
He brought nazal (streams) also out of the salai (rock), and caused mayam (waters) to yarad (run) down like nahar (rivers).
Yet they still went on to chataa (sin) against him, to rebel against the Most Ilayawan in the desert.
They tempted Al in their labab (heart) by asking food according to their napash (desire).
Yes, they spoke against Alahayam. They said, "Can Al prepare a table in the madabar (wilderness)?
Behold, he struck the tzawar (rock), so that mayam (waters) gushed out, and nachal (streams) overflowed. Can he nathan (give) lacham (bread) also? Will he kawan (provide) flesh for his im (people)?
Therefore Yahawah heard, and was angry. A ash (fire) was kindled against Yaiqab, ap (anger) also went up against Yasharaal (Israel),
because they didn't aman (believe) in Alahayam, and didn't batach (trust) in his yashawaih (salvation).
Yet he tzawah (commanded) the shachaq (skies) above, and opened the doors of shamayam (heaven).
He rained down manna on them to akal (eat), and gave them food from the sky.
ayash (man) ate the lacham (bread) of abayar (angels). He sent them lacham (food) to the full.
He caused the east qadayam (wind) to nasai (blow) in the sky. By his iz (power) he guided the south thayaman (wind).
He rained also flesh on them as the ipar (dust); winged birds as the sand of the yam (seas).
He let them napal (fall) in the qarab (midst) of their machanah (camp), around their mashakan (habitations).
So they ate, and were maad (well) filled. He gave them their own desire.
They didn't turn from their cravings. Their food was yet in their pah (mouths),
when the ap (anger) of Alahayam went up against them, killed some of their fattest, and struck down the young men of Yasharaal (Israel).
For all this they still sinned, and didn't aman (believe) in his wondrous palaa (works).
Therefore he consumed their yawam (days) in vanity, and their Shanah in terror.
When he killed them, then they inquired after him. They returned and sought Al earnestly.
They zakar (remembered) that Alahayam was their tzawar (rock), the Most Ilayawan Al, their gaal (redeemer).
But they flattered him with their pah (mouth), and lied to him with their lashawan (tongue).
For their lab (heart) was not kawan (right) with him, neither were they aman (faithful) in his barayath (covenant).
But he, being Rachawam, forgave iwan (iniquity), and didn't shachath (destroy) them. Yes, many times he turned his ap (anger) shawab (turn back / repent), and didn't stir up all his chamah (wrath).
He zakar (remembered) that they were but flesh, a rawach (wind) that passes halak (away), and doesn't shawab (turn back / repent) again.
mah (how) often they rebelled against him in the madabar (wilderness), and grieved him in the yashayamawan (desert)!
They turned again and tempted Al, and provoked the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).
They didn't zakar (remember) his yad (hand), nor the yawam (day) when he padah (redeemed) them from the tzar (adversary);
how he shawam (set) his awath (signs) in Matzarayam, his wonders in the shadah (field) of Tzain,
he turned their yaar (rivers) into dam (blood), and their yaar (streams), so that they could not drink.
He sent among them swarms of flies, which devoured them; and frogs, which destroyed them.
He gave also their increase to the caterpillar, and their yagayai (labor) to the locust.
He destroyed their vines with hail, their sycamore fig trees with frost.
He gave over their livestock also to the hail, and their maqanah (flocks) to hot thunderbolts.
He threw on them the charawan (fierceness) of his ap (anger), ibarah (wrath), indignation, and tzarah (trouble), and a band of malaak (angels) of rai (evil).
He made a nathayab (path) for his ap (anger). He didn't spare their napash (soul) from mawath (death), but gave their chay (life) over to the dabar (pestilence),
and struck all the firstborn in Matzarayam, the raashayath (chief) of their awan (strength) in the ahal (tents) of Cham.
But he led nasai (forth) his own im (people) like sheep, and guided them in the madabar (wilderness) like a flock.
He led them safely, so that they weren't pachad (afraid), but the yam (sea) overwhelmed their ayab (enemies).
He brought them to the border of his qadash (sanctuary), to this har (mountain), which his right yamayan (hand) had taken.

He also drove out the gawayam (nations) panayam (before) them, allotted them for an nachalah (inheritance) by line, and made the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) to shakan (dwell) in their ahal (tents).
Yet they tempted and rebelled against the Most Ilayawan Alahayam, and didn't shamar (keep) his idah (testimonies);
but turned sawag (back), and dealt bagad (treacherously) like their abawath (fathers). They were turned hapak (aside) like a deceitful qashath (bow).
For they provoked him to kais (anger) with their bamah (high) places, and moved him to jealousy with their engraved pasayal (images).
When Alahayam heard this, he was angry, and maad (greatly) abhorred Yasharaal (Israel);
So that he forsook the mashakan (tent) of Shayalah, the mashakan (tent) which he placed among men;
and delivered his iz (strength) into Shabay, his glory into the tzar (adversary's) yad (hand).
He also gave his im (people) over to the charab (sword), and was angry with his nachalah (inheritance).
ash (fire) devoured their young men. Their virgins had no wedding song.
Their kahan (priests) napal (fell) by the charab (sword), and their alamanah (widows) couldn't weep.
Then the Adanay awakened as one out of sleep, like a gabawar (mighty) man who shouts by reason of yayan (wine).
He struck his tzar (adversaries) backward. He nathan (put) them to a perpetual reproach.
Moreover he rejected the ahal (tent) of Yawasap, and didn't choose the shabat (tribe) of Aparayam,
But chose the shabat (tribe) of Yahawadah (Judah), har (mount) Tzayawan which he loved.
He built his maqadash (sanctuary) like the heights, like the aratz (earth) which he has established iwalam (forever).
He also chose Dawad his ibad (servant), and took him from the sheepfolds;
from following the ewes that have their young, he brought him to be the raih (shepherd) of Yaiqab, his im (people), and Yasharaal (Israel), his nachalah (inheritance).
So he was their raih (shepherd) according to the tham (integrity) of his labab (heart), and guided them by the skillfulness of his kap (hands).
Alahayam, the gawayam (nations) have bawaa (come) into your nachalah (inheritance). They have defiled your qadash (holy) hayakal (temple). They have laid Yarawashalam in heaps.
They have given the nabalah (dead) bodies of your ibad (servants) to be food for the birds of the sky, the flesh of your chasayad (saints) to the animals of the aratz (earth).
Their dam (blood) they have shed like mayam (water) around Yarawashalam. There was no qabar (one) to bury them.
We have become a reproach Shakan our neighbors, a scoffing and derision to those who are around us.
How long, Yahawah? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy bair (burn) like ash (fire)?
Pour out your chamah (wrath) on the gawayam (nations) that don't yadai (know) you; on the mamalakah (kingdoms) that don't qaraa (call) on your sham (name);
For they have devoured Yaiqab, and destroyed his Nawah.
Don't hold the iwan (iniquities) of our raashawan (forefathers) against us. Let your tender racham (mercies) Mahar qadam (meet) us, for we are in desperate need.
Help us, Alahayam of our yashai (salvation), for the kabawad (glory) of your sham (name). natzal (deliver) us, and kapar (forgive) our chataah (sins), for your sham (name's) sake.

Why should the gawayam (nations) amar (say), "Where is their Alahayam?" Let it be yadai (known) among the gawayam (nations), before our iyan (eyes), that vengeance for your ibad (servants)' dam (blood) is being poured out.
Let the sighing of the prisoner bawaa (come) panayam (before) you. According to the greatness of your zarawai (power), yathar (preserve) those who are sentenced to thamawathah (death).
shawab (turn back / repent) back Shakan our neighbors shabaithayam (seven) times into their bosom their reproach with which they have reproached you, Adanay.
So we, your im (people) and sheep of your pasture, will give you yadah (thanks) iwalam (forever). We will thahalah (praise) you iwalam (forever), to all dawar (generations).
Hear us, raih (shepherd) of Yasharaal (Israel), you who lead Yawasap like a flock, you who yashab (sit) above the karawab (cherubim), yapai (shine) forth.
panayam (before) Aparayam and Banayamayan and Manashah, stir up your might! yalak (come) to yashawaih (save) us!
shawab (turn back / repent) us again, Alahayam. Cause your panayam (face) to awar (shine), and we will be saved.
Yahawah Alahayam of tzabaa (armies), How long will you be ishan (angry) against the prayer of your im (people)?

He made him Adawan of his bayath (house), and ruler of all of his possessions;
to discipline his shar (princes) at his napash (pleasure), and to teach his zaqan (elders) chakam (wisdom).
Yasharaal (Israel) also came into Matzarayam. Yaiqab lived in the aratz (land) of Cham.
He increased his im (people) maad (greatly), and made them itzam (stronger) than their tzar (adversaries).
He turned their lab (heart) to shanaa (hate) his im (people), to conspire against his ibad (servants).
He sent Mashah, his ibad (servant), and Aharawan, whom he had chosen.
They performed awath (miracles) among them, and mawapath (wonders) in the aratz (land) of Cham.
He sent chashak (darkness), and made it chashak (dark). They didn't rebel against his dabar (words).
He turned their mayam (waters) into dam (blood), and killed their fish.
Their aratz (land) swarmed with frogs, even in the rooms of their malak (kings).
He spoke, and swarms of flies came, and lice in all their borders.
He gave them hail for rain, with lightning in their aratz (land).
He struck their vines and also their fig trees, and shattered the itz (trees) of their country.
He spoke, and the locusts came, and the grasshoppers, without number,
ate up every plant in their aratz (land); and ate up the fruit of their aratz (ground).
He struck also all the firstborn in their aratz (land), the raashayath (first) fruits of all their manhood.
He brought them yatzaa (forth) with kasap (silver) and gold. There was not kashal (one) feeble person among his shabat (tribes).
Matzarayam was Shamach when they departed, for the pachad (fear) of them had fallen on them.
He spread a cloud for a covering, ash (fire) to give awar (light) in the layal (night).
They asked, and he brought quails, and satisfied them with the lacham (bread) of the sky.
He opened the tzawar (rock), and mayam (waters) gushed out. They ran as a nahar (river) in the tzayah (dry) places.
For he zakar (remembered) his qadash (holy) dabar (word), and Abaraham, his ibad (servant).
He brought yatzaa (forth) his im (people) with joy, his Bachayar with singing.
He gave them the aratz (lands) of the gawayam (nations). They took the imal (labor) of the laam (peoples) in yarash (possession),
that they might shamar (keep) his chaq (statutes), and shamar (observe) his thawarah (laws). halal (praise) Yah!
halal (praise) Yahawah! Give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah, for he is tawab (good), for his loving tawab (kindness) endures iwalam (forever).
Who can utter the gabawarah (mighty) acts of Yahawah, or fully declare all his thahalah (praise)?
Blessed are those who shamar (keep) justice. Blessed is one who does what is tzadaqah (right) at all ith (times).
zakar (remember) me, Yahawah, with the favor that you show to your im (people). paqad (visit) me with your yashawaih (salvation),
that I may raah (see) the tawab (prosperity) of your Bachayar, that I may Shamach in the gladness of your gaway (nation), that I may glory with your nachalah (inheritance).
We have sinned with our abawath (fathers). We have committed iwah (iniquity). We have done wickedly.

Our abawath (fathers) didn't shakal (understand) your wonders in Matzarayam. They didn't zakar (remember) the multitude of your loving kindnesses, but were rebellious at the yam (sea), even at the Red yam (sea).
Nevertheless he saved them for his sham (name's) sake, that he might make his gabawarah (mighty) power yadai (known).
He rebuked the Red yam (sea) also, and it was dried up; so he led them through the depths, as through a madabar (desert).
He saved them from the yad (hand) of him who hated them, and redeemed them from the yad (hand) of the ayab (enemy).
The mayam (waters) covered their tzar (adversaries). There was not one of them yathar (left).
Then they believed his dabar (words). They sang his thahalah (praise).
They soon forgot his maishah (works). They didn't wait for his itzah (counsel),
but gave in to craving in the madabar (desert), and tested Al in the wasteland.
He gave them their request, but sent leanness into their napash (soul).
They envied Mashah also in the machanah (camp), and Aharawan, yahawah (yahweh's) qadawash (saint).
The aratz (earth) opened and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the idah (company) of Abayaram.
A ash (fire) was kindled in their idah (company). The lahabah (flame) burned up the rashai (wicked).
They made a calf in Charab, and worshiped a molten masakah (image).
Thus they exchanged their kabawad (glory) for an image of a bull that akal (eats) grass.
They forgot Al, their Savior, who had done gadawal (great) things in Matzarayam,
Wondrous palaa (works) in the aratz (land) of Cham, and awesome things by the Red yam (sea).

Therefore he said that he would destroy them, had Mashah, his Bachayar, not stood panayam (before) him in the breach, to shawab (turn back / repent) away his chamah (wrath), so that he wouldn't shachath (destroy) them.
Yes, they despised the pleasant aratz (land). They didn't aman (believe) his dabar (word),
but murmured in their ahal (tents), and didn't listen to yahawah (yahweh's) qawal (voice).
Therefore he swore to them that he would napal (overthrow) them in the madabar (wilderness),
that he would napal (overthrow) their zarai (seed) among the gawayam (nations), and scatter them in the aratz (lands).
They joined themselves also to Bailapaiwar Peor, and ate the zabach (sacrifices) of the mawath (dead).
Thus they provoked him to kais (anger) with their deeds. The magapah (plague) broke in on them.
Then Payanachas stood up, and executed palal (judgment), so the magapah (plague) was stopped.
That was credited to him for tzadaqah (righteousness), for all dawar (generations) to come.
They angered him also at the mayam (waters) of Marayabah, so that Mashah was troubled for their sakes;
because they were rebellious against his rawach (spirit), he spoke rashly with his shapah (lips).
They didn't destroy the im (peoples), as Yahawah commanded them,
but mixed themselves with the gawayam (nations), and learned their maishah (works).
They served their itzab (idols), which became a snare to them.
Yes, they sacrificed their ban (sons) and their bath (daughters) to demons.

They shed naqay (innocent) dam (blood), even the dam (blood) of their ban (sons) and of their bath (daughters), whom they sacrificed to the itzab (idols) of Kanain. The aratz (land) was polluted with dam (blood).
Thus were they defiled with their maishah (works), and prostituted themselves in their maishah (deeds).
Therefore Yahawah burned with ap (anger) against his im (people). He abhorred his nachalah (inheritance).
He gave them into the yad (hand) of the gawayam (nations). Those who hated them ruled over them.
Their ayab (enemies) also oppressed them. They were brought into subjection under their yad (hand).
Many paim (times) he delivered them, but they were rebellious in their itzah (counsel), and were brought low in their iwan (iniquity).
Nevertheless he regarded their tzar (distress), when he heard their cry.
He zakar (remembered) for them his barayath (covenant), and repented according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses.
He made them also to be pitied by all those who carried them captive.
yashai (save) us, Yahawah, our Alahayam, gather us from among the gawayam (nations), to give yadah (thanks) to your qadash (holy) sham (name), to shabach (triumph) in your thahalah (praise)!
Blessed BOOK be V Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), from iwalam (forever) even to iwalam (forever)! Let all the im (people) amar (say), "aman (amen)." halal (praise) Yah!
Give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah, for he is tawab (good), for his loving tawab (kindness) endures iwalam (forever).
Let the redeemed by Yahawah amar (say) so, whom he has redeemed from the yad (hand) of the tzar (adversary),
And gathered out of the aratz (lands), from the east and from the west, from the tzapawan (north) and from the yam (south).
They wandered in the madabar (wilderness) in a yashayamawan (desert) darak (way). They found no Iyar to live in.
Raib and Tzamaa, their napash (soul) fainted in them.
Then they cried to Yahawah in their tzar (trouble), and he delivered them out of their distresses,
he led them also by a yashar (straight) darak (way), that they might yalak (go) to a Iyar to live in.
Let them yadah (praise) Yahawah for his loving chasad (kindness), for his wonderful palaa (works) to the children of men!
For he satisfies the longing napash (soul). He malaa (fills) the Raib napash (soul) with tawab (good).
Some sat in chashak (darkness) and in the shadow of tzalamawath (death), being bound in affliction and barazal (iron),
because they rebelled against the amar (words) of Al, and condemned the itzah (counsel) of the Most Ilayawan.
Therefore he brought down their lab (heart) with imal (labor). They fell down, and there was none to help.
Then they cried to Yahawah in their tzar (trouble), and he saved them out of their distresses.
He brought them out of chashak (darkness) and the shadow of tzalamawath (death), and broke their bonds in sunder.
Let them yadah (praise) Yahawah for his loving chasad (kindness), for his wonderful palaa (works) to the children of men!
For he has shabar (broken) the gates of brass, and cut through bars of barazal (iron).
Awayal are afflicted darak (because) of their disobedience, and because of their iwan (iniquities).
Their napash (soul) abhors all kinds of food. They nagai (draw) near to the gates of mawath (death).
Then they cry to Yahawah in their tzar (trouble), he yashai (saves) them out of their distresses.
He shalach (sends) his dabar (word), and heals them, and malat (delivers) them from their graves.
Let them yadah (praise) Yahawah for his loving chasad (kindness), for his wonderful palaa (works) to the children of men!
Let them offer the zabach (sacrifices) of thanksgiving, and declare his maishah (works) with singing.
Those who yarad (go) down to the yam (sea) in ships, who do malaakah (business) in rab (great) mayam (waters);
These raah (see) yahawah (yahweh's) maishah (works), and his wonders in the deep.
For he commands, and imad (raises) the stormy rawach (wind), which lifts up its waves.
They ilah (mount) up to the sky; they yarad (go) down again to the depths. Their napash (soul) melts away because of rai (trouble).
They reel back and forth, and stagger like a drunken shakawar (man), and are at their chakamah (wits)' balai (end).
Then they cry to Yahawah in their tzar (trouble), and he yatzaa (brings) them out of their distress.
He qawam (makes) the storm a calm, so that its waves are still.
Then they are Shamach because it is calm, so he brings them to their Chapatz haven.
Let them yadah (praise) Yahawah for his loving chasad (kindness), for his wonderful palaa (works) for the children of men!
Let them exalt him also in the qahal (assembly) of the im (people), and halal (praise) him in the mawashab (seat) of the zaqan (elders).
He shawam (turns) nahar (rivers) into a madabar (desert), mayam (water) springs into a thirsty tzamaawan (ground),
and a fruitful aratz (land) into a malachah (salt) waste, for the wickedness of those who yashab (dwell) in it.
He shawam (turns) a madabar (desert) into a pool of mayam (water), and a tzayah (dry) aratz (land) into mayam (water) springs.
There he makes the Raib live, that they may kawan (prepare) a Iyar to live in,
zarai (sow) shadah (fields), plant vineyards, and reap the fruits of increase.
He blesses them also, so that they are multiplied maad (greatly). He doesn't allow their livestock to decrease.
Again, they are diminished and bowed down through oppression, rai (trouble), and sorrow.
He pours contempt on nadayab (princes), and thaih (causes) them to wander in a trackless thahaw (waste).
Yet he lifts the Abayawan out of their affliction, and increases their mashapachah (families) like a flock.
The yashar (upright) will raah (see) it, and be Shamach. All the iwal (wicked) will qapatz (shut) their pah (mouths).
Whoever is chakam (wise) will pay attention to these things. They will bayan (consider) the loving kindnesses of Yahawah.
My lab (heart) is steadfast, Alahayam. I will shayar (sing) and I will make music with my soul.
Wake up, harp and lyre! I will wake up the dawn.
I will give yadah (thanks) to you, Yahawah, among the im (nations). I will sing zamar (praises) to you among the laam (peoples).
For your loving chasad (kindness) is gadawal (great) above the shamayam (heavens). Your amath (faithfulness) reaches to the shachaq (skies).
Be exalted, Alahayam, above the shamayam (heavens)! Let your kabawad (glory) be over all the aratz (earth).
That your yadayad (beloved) may be delivered, yashai (save) with your right yamayan (hand), and answer us.
Alahayam has spoken from his qadash (sanctuary): "In triumph, I will divide Shakam, and measure out the valley of Sakawath.
Galaid is mine. Manashah is mine. Aparayam also is my helmet. Yahawadah (Judah) is my scepter.
Mawaab is my wash pot. I will toss my sandal on Adam. I will rawai (shout) over Palashath.
Who will bring me into the fortified Iyar? Who has led me to Adam?
Haven't you rejected us, Alahayam? You don't yatzaa (go) forth, Alahayam, with our tzabaa (armies).
Give us help against the tzar (enemy), for the thashawaih (help) of adam (man) is vain.
Through Alahayam, we will do chayal (valiantly). For it is he who will tread down our tzar (enemies).
Alahayam of my thahalah (praise), don't remain charash (silent),
for they have opened the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked) and the pah (mouth) of deceit against me. They have spoken to me with a lying lashawan (tongue).
They have also surrounded me with dabar (words) of hatred, and fought against me without a cause.
In return for my ahabah (love), they are my shatan (adversaries); but I am in prayer.
They have rewarded me rai (evil) for tawab (good), and hatred for my ahabah (love).
paqad (set) a rashai (wicked) man over him. Let an shatan (adversary) imad (stand) at his right yamayan (hand).
When he is judged, let him yatzaa (come) forth rashai (guilty). Let his prayer be turned into chataah (sin).
Let his yawam (days) be Mait. Let achar (another) take his office.
Let his children be fatherless, and his ashah (wife) a alamanah (widow).
Let his children be wandering beggars. Let them be sought from their ruins.
Let the creditor seize all that he has. Let strangers plunder the fruit of his yagayai (labor).
Let there be no mashak (one) to extend chasad (kindness) to him, neither let there be anyone to have chanan (pity) on his fatherless children.
Let his acharayath (posterity) be karath (cut) off. In the dawar (generation) achar (following) let their sham (name) be blotted out.
Let the iwan (iniquity) of his abawath (fathers) be zakar (remembered) by Yahawah. Don't let the chataah (sin) of his am (mother) be blotted out.
Let them be before Yahawah continually, that he may karath (cut) off their zakar (memory) from the aratz (earth);
because he didn't zakar (remember) to show chasad (kindness), but persecuted the Inay and Abayawan ayash (man), the broken in labab (heart), to mawath (kill) them.
Yes, he loved cursing, and it came to him. He didn't delight in barakah (blessing), and it was rachaq (far) from him.
He Labash himself also with cursing as with his mad (garment). It came into his qarab (inward) parts like mayam (water), like shaman (oil) into his itzam (bones).
Let it be to him as the clothing with which he itah (covers) himself, for the belt that is always around him.
This is the pailah (reward) of my shatan (adversaries) from Yahawah, of those who dabar (speak) rai (evil) against my napash (soul).
But ishah (deal) with me, Yahawah the Adanay, for your sham (name's) sake, because your loving chasad (kindness) is tawab (good), natzal (deliver) me;
for I am Inay and Abayawan. My lab (heart) is wounded qarab (within) me.
I fade halak (away) like an evening shadow. I am shaken off like a locust.
My knees are weak through fasting. My body is thin and lacks shaman (fat).
I have also become a reproach to them. When they raah (see) me, they shake their raash (head).
Help me, Yahawah, my Alahayam. yashai (save) me according to your loving chasad (kindness);
that they may yadai (know) that this is your yad (hand); that you, Yahawah, have done it.
They may qalal (curse), but you barak (bless). When they qawam (arise), they will be shamed, but your ibad (servant) shall Shamach.
Let my shatan (adversaries) be Labash with dishonor. Let them itah (cover) themselves with their own bashath (shame) as with a robe.
I will give maad (great) yadah (thanks) to Yahawah with my pah (mouth). Yes, I will halal (praise) him among the rab (multitude).
For he will imad (stand) at the right yamayan (hand) of the Abayawan, to yashai (save) him from those who shapat (judge) his napash (soul).
Yahawah says to my Adawan, "yashab (sit) at my right yamayan (hand), until I shayath (make) your ayab (enemies) your footstool for your feet.
Yahawah will shalach (send) forth the matah (rod) of your iz (strength) out of Tzayawan. radah (rule) in the qarab (midst) of your ayab (enemies).
Your im (people) offer themselves nadabah (willingly) in the yawam (day) of your chayal (power), in qadash (holy) array. Out of the womb of the morning, you have the dew of your youth.
Yahawah has sworn, and will not change his mind: "You are a kahan (priest) iwalam (forever) in the order of Malakayatzadaq.
The Adanay is at your right yamayan (hand). He will machatz (crush) malak (kings) in the yawam (day) of his ap (wrath).
He will dayan (judge) among the gawayam (nations). He will heap up gawayah (dead) bodies. He will machatz (crush) the raash (ruler) of the whole aratz (earth).
He will drink of the nachal (brook) in the darak (way); therefore he will lift up his raash (head).
halal (praise) Yah! I will give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah with my whole labab (heart), in the council of the yashar (upright), and in the idah (congregation).
yahawah (yahweh's) maishah (works) are gadawal (great), pondered by all those who Chapatz in them.
His pail (work) is honor and hadar (majesty). His tzadaqah (righteousness) imad (endures) id (forever).
He has caused his wonderful palaa (works) to be remembered. Yahawah is Chanawan and Rachawam.
He has given Tarap to those who yaraa (fear) him. He always zakar (remembers) his barayath (covenant).
He has shown his im (people) the kach (power) of his maishah (works), in giving them the nachalah (heritage) of the gawayam (nations).
The maishah (works) of his yad (hands) are truth and justice. All his paqawad (precepts) are aman (sure).
They are established id (forever) and ever. They are done in truth and uprightness.
He has sent padawath (redemption) to his im (people). He has ordained his barayath (covenant) iwalam (forever). His sham (name) is qadawash (holy) and awesome!

The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is the raashayath (beginning) of chakamah (wisdom). All those who do his work have a tawab (good) shakal (understanding). His thahalah (praise) imad (endures) id (forever)!
halal (praise) Yah! Blessed is the ayash (man) who yaraa (fears) Yahawah, who delights maad (greatly) in his matzawah (commandments).
His zarai (seed) will be gabawar (mighty) in the aratz (land). The dawar (generation) of the yashar (upright) will be blessed.
Wealth and riches are in his bayath (house). His tzadaqah (righteousness) imad (endures) id (forever).
awar (light) dawns in the chashak (darkness) for the yashar (upright), Chanawan, Rachawam, and tzadayaq (righteous).
It is tawab (well) with the ayash (man) who chanan (deals) graciously and lends. He will maintain his dabar (cause) in mashapat (judgment).
For he will never be shaken. The tzadayaq (righteous) will be remembered iwalam (forever).
He will not be yaraa (afraid) of rai (evil) news. His lab (heart) is steadfast, trusting in Yahawah.
His lab (heart) is established. He will not be yaraa (afraid) in the end when he raah (see) his tzar (adversaries).
He has dispersed, he has given to the Abayawan. His tzadaqah (righteousness) imad (endures) id (forever). His qaran (horn) will be exalted with honor.
The rashai (wicked) will raah (see) it, and be kais (grieved). He shall gnash with his teeth, and melt away. The desire of the rashai (wicked) will abad (perish).
halal (praise) Yah! halal (praise), you ibad (servants) of Yahawah, halal (praise) the sham (name) of Yahawah.
Blessed be the sham (name) of Yahawah, from this time forth and forevermore.
From the rising of the shamash (sun) to the going down of the same, yahawah (yahweh's) sham (name) is to be praised.
Yahawah is high above all gawayam (nations), his kabawad (glory) above the shamayam (heavens).
Who is like Yahawah, our Alahayam, who has his yashab (seat) on high,
Who stoops down to raah (see) in shamayam (heaven) and in the aratz (earth)?
He qawam (raises) up the Dal out of the ipar (dust). Lifts up the Abayawan from the ash heap;
that he may yashab (set) him with nadayab (princes), even with the nadayab (princes) of his im (people).
He yashab (settles) the Iqar woman in her bayath (home), as a Shamach am (mother) of children. halal (praise) Yah!
When Yasharaal (Israel) went yatzaa (forth) out of Matzarayam, the bayath (house) of Yaiqab from a im (people) of foreign language;
Yahawadah (Judah) became his qadash (sanctuary), Yasharaal (Israel) his mamashalah (dominion).
The yam (sea) saw it, and fled. The Yaradan was driven back.
The har (mountains) skipped like ayal (rams), the Gabaih hills like ban (lambs).
What was it, you yam (sea), that you fled? You Yaradan, that you turned back?
You har (mountains), that you skipped like ayal (rams); you Gabaih hills, like ban (lambs)?
chawal (tremble), you aratz (earth), at the panayam (presence) of the Adawan, at the panayam (presence) of the Alawah of Yaiqab,
who turned the tzawar (rock) into a pool of mayam (water), the flint into a spring of mayam (waters).
Not to us, Yahawah, not to us, but to your sham (name) nathan (give) kabawad (glory), for your loving chasad (kindness), and for your truth's sake.
Why should the gawayam (nations) amar (say), "Where is their Alahayam, now?
But our Alahayam is in the shamayam (heavens). He does whatever he pleases.
Their itzab (idols) are kasap (silver) and gold, the maishah (work) of men's yad (hands).
They have pah (mouths), but they don't dabar (speak). They have iyan (eyes), but they don't raah (see).
They have ears, but they don't hear. They have ap (noses), but they don't rawach (smell).
They have yad (hands), but they don't feel. They have feet, but they don't halak (walk), neither do they speak through their garawan (throat).
Those who ishah (make) them will be like them; yes, everyone who batach (trusts) in them.
Yasharaal (Israel), batach (trust) in Yahawah! He is their help and their magan (shield).
bayath (house) of Aharawan, batach (trust) in Yahawah! He is their help and their magan (shield).
You who yaraa (fear) Yahawah, batach (trust) in Yahawah! He is their help and their magan (shield).
Yahawah zakar (remembers) us. He will barak (bless) us. He will barak (bless) the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel). He will barak (bless) the bayath (house) of Aharawan.
He will barak (bless) those who yaraa (fear) Yahawah, both qatan (small) and gadawal (great).
May Yahawah increase you more and more, you and your children.
Blessed are you by Yahawah, who made shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth).
The shamayam (heavens) are the shamayam (heavens) of Yahawah; but the aratz (earth) has he given to the children of men.
The mawath (dead) don't halal (praise) Yah, neither any who yarad (go) down into silence;
But we will barak (bless) Yah, from this time forth and forevermore. halal (praise) Yah!
I ahab (love) Yahawah, because he listens to my qawal (voice), and my cries for thachanawan (mercy).
Because he has turned his ear to me, therefore I will qaraa (call) on him as yawam (long) as I live.
The cords of mawath (death) surrounded me, the pains of shaawal (sheol) got a matzaa (hold) of me. I found tzarah (trouble) and sorrow.
Then I called on the sham (name) of Yahawah: "Yahawah, I beg you, malat (deliver) my napash (soul).
Yahawah is Chanawan and tzadayaq (righteous). Yes, our Alahayam is merciful.
