To you I do nashaa (lift) up my iyan (eyes), you who yashab (sit) in the shamayam (heavens).

Behold, as the iyan (eyes) of ibad (servants) look to the yad (hand) of their adawan (master), as the iyan (eyes) of a shapachah (maid) to the yad (hand) of her mistress; so our iyan (eyes) look to Yahawah, our Alahayam, until he has chanan (mercy) on us.
Have chanan (mercy) on us, Yahawah, have chanan (mercy) on us, for we have endured much contempt.
Our napash (soul) is rab (exceedingly) filled with the scoffing of those who are at Shaanan, with the contempt of the Gaah.
If it had not been Yahawah who was on our side, let Yasharaal (Israel) now amar (say),
if it had not been Yahawah who was on our side, when men rose up qawam (against) us;
then they would have swallowed us up chay (alive), when their ap (wrath) was kindled against us;
then the mayam (waters) would have overwhelmed us, the nachal (stream) would have gone over our napash (soul);
then the Zayadawan mayam (waters) would have gone over our napash (soul).
Blessed be Yahawah, who has not given us as a Tarap to their teeth.
Our napash (soul) has escaped like a bird out of the fowler's snare. The snare is shabar (broken), and we have escaped.
Our help is in the sham (name) of Yahawah, who made shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth).
Those who batach (trust) in Yahawah are as har (mount) Tzayawan, which can't be moved, but yashab (remains) iwalam (forever).
As the har (mountains) surround Yarawashalam, so Yahawah surrounds his im (people) from this time forth and forevermore.
For the scepter of rashai (wickedness) won't nawach (remain) over the allotment of the tzadayaq (righteous); so that the tzadayaq (righteous) won't use their yad (hands) to do evil.
Do tawab (good), Yahawah, to those who are tawab (good), to those who are yashar (upright) in their labah (hearts).
But as for those who natah (turn) aside to their crooked iqalaqal (ways), Yahawah will yalak (lead) them away with the pail (workers) of awan (iniquity). shalawam (peace) be on Yasharaal (Israel).
When Yahawah brought shawab (turn back / repent) those who returned to Tzayawan, we were like those who dream.
Then our pah (mouth) was filled with laughter, and our lashawan (tongue) with singing. Then they said among the gawayam (nations), "Yahawah has done great things for them.
Yahawah has done great things for us, and we are Shamach.
shabawath (restore) our fortunes again, Yahawah, like the apayaq (streams) Nagab the Negev.
Those who zarai (sow) in tears will reap in joy.
He who goes out weeping, carrying zarai (seed) for sowing, will bawaa (certainly) bawaa (come) again with joy, carrying his sheaves.
Unless Yahawah banah (builds) the bayath (house), they imal (labor) in vain who banah (build) it. Unless Yahawah watches over the Iyar, the shamar (watchman) guards it in vain.
It is vain for you to qawam (rise) up shakam (early), to stay up late, eating the lacham (bread) of toil; for he nathan (gives) shanah (sleep) to his loved ones.
Behold, children are a nachalah (heritage) of Yahawah. The fruit of the womb is his reward.
As chatz (arrows) in the yad (hand) of a gabawar (mighty) man, so are the children of youth.
Happy is the gabar (man) who has his quiver malaa (full) of them. They won't be disappointed when they dabar (speak) with their ayab (enemies) in the gate.
Blessed is everyone who yaraa (fears) Yahawah, who halak (walks) in his darak (ways).
For you will akal (eat) the yagayai (labor) of your kap (hands). You will be happy, and it will be tawab (well) with you.
Your ashah (wife) will be as a fruitful vine, in the innermost parts of your bayath (house); your children like olive plants, around your table.
Behold, thus is the gabar (man) blessed who yaraa (fears) Yahawah.
May Yahawah barak (bless) you out of Tzayawan, and may you raah (see) the tawab (good) of Yarawashalam all the yawam (days) of your chay (life).
Yes, may you raah (see) your children's children. shalawam (peace) be upon Yasharaal (Israel).
Many rab (times) they have afflicted me from my youth up. Let Yasharaal (Israel) now amar (say),
many rab (times) they have afflicted me from my youth up, yet they have not prevailed against me.
The plowers plowed on my back. They made their furrows long.
Yahawah is tzadayaq (righteous). He has cut apart the cords of the rashai (wicked).
Let them be disappointed and turned backward, all those who shanaa (hate) Tzayawan.
Let them be as the grass on the housetops, which yabash (withers) before it grows up;
with which the reaper doesn't malaa (fill) his kap (hand), nor he who binds sheaves, his bosom.
Neither do those who ibar (go) by amar (say), "The barakah (blessing) of Yahawah be on you. We barak (bless) you in the sham (name) of Yahawah.
Out of the depths I have cried to you, Yahawah.
Adanay, hear my qawal (voice). Let your ears be Qashab to the qawal (voice) of my petitions.
If you, Yah, kept a record of iwan (sins), Adanay, who could imad (stand)?
But there is forgiveness with you, therefore you are feared.
I wait for Yahawah. My napash (soul) waits. I hope in his dabar (word).
My napash (soul) longs for the Adanay more than watchmen long for the baqar (morning); more than watchmen for the baqar (morning).
Yasharaal (Israel), hope in Yahawah, for with Yahawah there is loving chasad (kindness). With him is abundant padawath (redemption).
He will padah (redeem) Yasharaal (Israel) from all their iwan (sins).
Yahawah, my lab (heart) isn't haughty, nor my iyan (eyes) lofty; nor do I concern myself with gadawal (great) matters, or things palaa (too) wonderful for me.
Surely I have stilled and quieted my napash (soul), like a weaned child with his am (mother), like a weaned child is my napash (soul) within me.
Yasharaal (Israel), hope in Yahawah, from this time forth and forevermore.
Yahawah, zakar (remember) Dawad and all his affliction,
how he swore to Yahawah, and vowed to the abayar (mighty) One of Yaiqab:
"bawaa (surely) I will not come into the structure of my bayath (house), nor ilah (go) up into my bed;
I will not nathan (give) sleep to my iyan (eyes), or slumber to my ipaip (eyelids);
until I matzaa (find) out a place for Yahawah, a mashakan (dwelling) for the abayar (mighty) One of Yaiqab.
Behold, we heard of it in Ephrathah. We found it in the shadah (field) Yair Jaar:
"We will bawaa (go) into his mashakan (dwelling) place. We will shachah (worship) at his footstool.
qawam (arise), Yahawah, into your resting place; you, and the arawan (ark) of your iz (strength).
Let your kahan (priest) be Labash with tzadaq (righteousness). Let your chasayad (saints) shout for joy!
For your ibad (servant) Dawad sake, don't shawab (turn back / repent) away the panayam (face) of your mashayach (anointed) one.
Yahawah has sworn to Dawad in truth. He will not shawab (turn back / repent) from it: "I will shayath (set) the fruit of your body on your kasaa (throne).
If your children will shamar (keep) my barayath (covenant), my idah (testimony) that I will teach them, their children also will yashab (sit) on your kasaa (throne) forevermore.
For Yahawah has chosen Tzayawan. He has desired it for his habitation.
"This is my resting place id (forever). Here I will live, for I have desired it.
I will barak (abundantly) barak (bless) her provision. I will satisfy her Abayawan with lacham (bread).
Her kahan (priests) I will also Labash with yashai (salvation). Her chasayad (saints) will shout aloud for joy.
There I will make the qaran (horn) of Dawad to bud. I have ordained a nayar (lamp) for my mashayach (anointed).
I will Labash his ayab (enemies) with bashath (shame), but on himself, his nazar (crown) will be resplendent.
See how tawab (good) and how Naiyam it is for ach (brothers) to live together in unity!
It is like the tawab (precious) shaman (oil) on the raash (head), that ran down on the beard, even Aharawan beard; that came down on the pah (edge) of his robes;
like the dew of Charamawan, that yarad (comes) down on the harar (hills) of Tzayawan: for there Yahawah tzawah (gives) the barakah (blessing), even chay (life) forevermore.
Look! barak (praise) Yahawah, all you ibad (servants) of Yahawah, who imad (stand) by layal (night) in yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house)!
nashaa (lift) up your yad (hands) in the qadash (sanctuary). barak (praise) Yahawah!
May Yahawah barak (bless) you from Tzayawan; even he who made shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth).
halal (praise) Yah! halal (praise) the sham (name) of Yahawah! halal (praise) him, you ibad (servants) of Yahawah,
you who imad (stand) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, in the courts of our alahayam (god's) bayath (house).
halal (praise) Yah, for Yahawah is tawab (good). Sing zamar (praises) to his sham (name), for that is Naiyam.
For Yah has chosen Yaiqab for himself; Yasharaal (Israel) for his own sagalah (possession).
For I yadai (know) that Yahawah is gadawal (great), that our Adawan is above all Alahayam.
Whatever Yahawah pleased, that he has done, in shamayam (heaven) and in aratz (earth), in the yam (seas) and in all deeps;
who causes the nashayaa (clouds) to ilah (rise) from the ends of the aratz (earth); who ishah (makes) lightnings with the rain; who yatzaa (brings) forth the rawach (wind) out of his treasuries;
Who struck the firstborn of Matzarayam, both of adam (man) and animal;
Who sent awath (signs) and mawapath (wonders) into the midst of you, Matzarayam, on Paraih, and on all his ibad (servants);
who struck many gawayam (nations), and killed rab (mighty) malak (kings),
Sayachawan malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites), Iwag malak (king) of Bashan, and all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of Kanain,
and gave their aratz (land) for a nachalah (heritage), a nachalah (heritage) to Yasharaal (Israel), his im (people).
Your sham (name), Yahawah, endures iwalam (forever); your renown, Yahawah, throughout all dawar (generations).
For Yahawah will dayan (judge) his im (people), and have compassion on his ibad (servants).
The itzab (idols) of the gawayam (nations) are kasap (silver) and gold, the maishah (work) of men's yad (hands).
They have pah (mouths), but they can't dabar (speak). They have iyan (eyes), but they can't raah (see).
They have ears, but they can't hear; neither is there any rawach (breath) in their pah (mouths).
Those who ishah (make) them will be like them; yes, everyone who batach (trusts) in them.
bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), barak (praise) Yahawah! bayath (house) of Aharawan, barak (praise) Yahawah!
bayath (house) of Laway, barak (praise) Yahawah! You who yaraa (fear) Yahawah, barak (praise) Yahawah!
Blessed be Yahawah from Tzayawan, Who shakan (dwells) at Yarawashalam. halal (praise) Yah!
Give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah, for he is tawab (good); for his loving tawab (kindness) endures iwalam (forever).
Give yadah (thanks) to the Alahayam of Alahayam; for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever).
Give yadah (thanks) to the Adawan of adawan (lords); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who alone does gadawal (great) wonders; for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who by thabawan (understanding) made the shamayam (heavens); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who spread out the aratz (earth) above the mayam (waters); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who made the gadawal (great) awar (lights); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever):
The shamash (sun) to mamashalah (rule) by yawam (day); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever);
The yarach (moon) and kawakab (stars) to mamashalah (rule) by layal (night); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who struck down the Matzarayam (Egyptian) firstborn; for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever);
And brought out Yasharaal (Israel) from among them; for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever);
With a chazaq (strong) yad (hand), and with an natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who divided the Red yam (sea) apart; for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever);
And made Yasharaal (Israel) to ibar (pass) through its midst; for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever);
But overthrew Paraih and his chayal (army) in the Red yam (sea); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who led his im (people) through the madabar (wilderness); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever):
To him who struck gadawal (great) malak (kings); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever);
And killed adayar (mighty) malak (kings); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever):
Sayachawan malak (king) of the Amaray (Amorites); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever);
Iwag malak (king) of Bashan; for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever);
And gave their aratz (land) as an nachalah (inheritance); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever);
Even a nachalah (heritage) to Yasharaal (Israel) his ibad (servant); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever):
Who zakar (remembered) us in our low estate; for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever);
And has delivered us from our tzar (adversaries); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever):
Who nathan (gives) lacham (food) to every creature; for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever).
Oh give yadah (thanks) to the Al of shamayam (heaven); for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever).
By the nahar (rivers) of Babal, there we sat down. Yes, we wept, when we zakar (remembered) Tzayawan.
On the willows in its midst, we hung up our harps.
For there, those who led us captive asked us for dabar (songs). Those who tormented us demanded dabar (songs) of joy: "shayar (sing) us shayar (one) of the songs of Tzayawan!
How can we shayar (sing) yahawah (yahweh's) song in a foreign adamah (land)?
If I forget you, Yarawashalam, let my right yamayan (hand) forget its skill.
Let my lashawan (tongue) stick to the roof of my chak (mouth) if I don't zakar (remember) you; if I don't ilah (prefer) Yarawashalam above my raash (chief) joy.
zakar (remember), Yahawah, against the children of Adam, the yawam (day) of Yarawashalam; who said, "Raze it! Raze it even to its yasawad (foundation)!
bath (daughter) of Babal, doomed to destruction, he will be happy who shalam (rewards) you, as you have served us.
Happy shall he be, who achaz (takes) and dashes your little iwalal (ones) against the salai (rock).
I will give you yadah (thanks) with my whole lab (heart). Before the Alahayam, I will sing zamar (praises) to you.

I will shachah (bow) down toward your qadash (holy) hayakal (temple), and give yadah (thanks) to your sham (name) for your loving chasad (kindness) and for your truth; for you have exalted your sham (name) and your amarah (sayings) above all.
In the yawam (day) that I called, you answered me. You encouraged me with iz (strength) in my napash (soul).
All the malak (kings) of the aratz (earth) will give you yadah (thanks), Yahawah, for they have heard the amar (words) of your pah (mouth).
Yes, they will shayar (sing) of the darak (ways) of Yahawah; for gadawal (great) is yahawah (yahweh's) kabawad (glory).
For though Yahawah is high, yet he raah (see) Shapal the lowly; but the Gabah, he yadai (knows) from afar.

Though I yalak (walk) in the qarab (midst) of tzarah (trouble), you will chayah (revive) me. You will shalach (stretch) forth your yad (hand) against the ap (wrath) of my ayab (enemies). Your right yamayan (hand) will yashai (save) me.
Yahawah will fulfill that which concerns me; your loving chasad (kindness), Yahawah, endures iwalam (forever). Don't rapah (forsake) the maishah (works) of your own yad (hands).
Yahawah, you have searched me, and you yadai (know) me.
You yadai (know) my sitting down and my qawam (rising) up. You bayan (perceive) my thoughts from Rachawaq.
You search out my arach (path) and my lying down, and are acquainted with all my darak (ways).
For there is not a malah (word) on my lashawan (tongue), but, behold, Yahawah, you yadai (know) it altogether.
You hem me in behind and qadam (before). You laid your kap (hand) on me.
This daith (knowledge) is Palaay me. It's lofty. I can't yakal (attain) it.
Where could I yalak (go) from your rawach (spirit)? Or where could I flee from your panayam (presence)?
If I ascend up into shamayam (heaven), you are there. If I make my bed in shaawal (sheol), behold, you are there!
If I nashaa (take) the wings of the dawn, and settle in the uttermost parts of the yam (sea);
Even there your yad (hand) will lead me, and your right yamayan (hand) will achaz (hold) me.
If I amar (say), "Surely the chashak (darkness) will overwhelm me; the awar (light) around me will be layal (night);
even the chashak (darkness) doesn't chashak (hide) from you, but the layal (night) awar (shines) as the yawam (day). The chashakah (darkness) is like awarah (light) to you.
For you formed my inmost being. You knit me together in my am (mother's) womb.
I will give yadah (thanks) to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your maishah (works) are palaa (wonderful). My napash (soul) yadai (knows) that very maad (well).
My frame wasn't hidden from you, when I was made in secret, woven Thachathay in the depths of the aratz (earth).
Your iyan (eyes) saw my body. In your book they were all written, the yawam (days) that were ordained for me, when as yet there were none of them.
How precious to me are your thoughts, Al! How vast is their raash (sum)!
If I would count them, they are more in number than the sand. When I qawatz (wake) up, I am still with you.
If only you, Alawah, would kill the rashai (wicked). sawar (get) away from me, you bloodthirsty men!
For they amar (speak) against you wickedly. Your ir (enemies) nashaa (take) your shawaa (name) in vain.
Yahawah, don't I shanaa (hate) those who shanaa (hate) you? Am I not grieved with those who thaqawamam (rise) up against you?
I shanaa (hate) them with perfect hatred. They have become my ayab (enemies).
Search me, Al, and yadai (know) my labab (heart). Try me, and yadai (know) my thoughts.
raah (see) if there is any itzab (wicked) darak (way) in me, and lead me in the iwalam (forever) darak (way).
chalatz (deliver) me, Yahawah, from the rai (evil) adam (man). Preserve me from the violent ayash (man);
those who chashab (devise) rai (mischief) in their lab (hearts). They yawam (continually) gawar (gather) themselves together for war.
They have sharpened their lashawan (tongues) like a serpent. Viper's chamah (poison) is under their shapah (lips). salah (selah).
Yahawah, shamar (keep) me from the yad (hands) of the rashai (wicked). Preserve me from the violent men who have determined to trip my feet.
The Gaah have hidden a snare for me, they have spread the cords of a net by the path. They have shayath (set) traps for me. salah (selah).
I said to Yahawah, "You are my Al." Listen to the qawal (cry) of my petitions, Yahawah.
Yahawah, the Adanay, the iz (strength) of my yashawaih (salvation), you have covered my raash (head) in the yawam (day) of nashaq (battle).
Yahawah, don't nathan (grant) the desires of the rashai (wicked). Don't let their evil plans succeed, or they will become proud. salah (selah).
As for the raash (head) of those who surround me, let the imal (mischief) of their own shapah (lips) cover them.
Let burning coals fall on them. Let them be thrown into the ash (fire), into miry mahamarah (pits), from where they never qawam (rise).
An evil speaker won't be established in the aratz (earth). rai (evil) will hunt the violent ayash (man) to overthrow him.
I yadai (know) that Yahawah will ishah (maintain) the cause of the Inay, and justice for the Abayawan.
Surely the tzadayaq (righteous) will give yadah (thanks) to your sham (name). The yashar (upright) will yashab (dwell) in your panayam (presence).
Yahawah, I have called on you. Come to me quickly! Listen to my qawal (voice) when I qaraa (call) to you.
Let my prayer be kawan (set) panayam (before) you like incense; the mashaath (lifting) up of my kap (hands) like the evening manachah (sacrifice).
shayath (set) a watch, Yahawah, before my pah (mouth). Keep the door of my shapah (lips).
Don't natah (incline) my lab (heart) to any rai (evil) thing, to practice ilayalah (deeds) of rashai (wickedness) with men who ilayalah (work) awan (iniquity). Don't let me eat of their delicacies.

Let the tzadayaq (righteous) strike me, it is chasad (kindness); let him yakach (reprove) me, it is like shaman (oil) on the raash (head); don't let my raash (head) refuse it; Yet my prayer is always against rai (evil) deeds.
Their shapat (judges) are thrown down by the yad (sides) of the salai (rock). They will hear my amar (words), for they are well spoken.
"As when palach (one) plows and breaks up the aratz (earth), our itzam (bones) are scattered at the pah (mouth) of shaawal (sheol).
For my iyan (eyes) are on you, Yahawah, the Adanay. In you, I take refuge. Don't leave my napash (soul) destitute.
shamar (keep) me from the snare which they have laid for me, from the traps of the pail (workers) of awan (iniquity).
Let the rashai (wicked) napal (fall) together into their own nets, while I ibar (pass) by.
I cry with my qawal (voice) to Yahawah. With my qawal (voice), I ask Yahawah for chanan (mercy).
I pour out my complaint panayam (before) him. I nagad (tell) him my tzarah (troubles).
When my rawach (spirit) was overwhelmed within me, you knew my nathayab (path). In the arach (way) in which I halak (walk), they have hidden a snare for me.
Look on my yamayan (right), and raah (see); for there is no one who is concerned for me. manawas (refuge) has fled from me. No darash (one) cares for my napash (soul).
I cried to you, Yahawah. I said, "You are my refuge, my chalaq (portion) in the aratz (land) of the chay (living).
Listen to my cry, for I am in desperate need. natzal (deliver) me from my persecutors, For they are amatz (stronger) than me.
yatzaa (bring) my napash (soul) out of prison, that I may give yadah (thanks) to your sham (name). The tzadayaq (righteous) will surround me, for you will be good to me.
Hear my prayer, Yahawah. Listen to my petitions. In your amawanah (faithfulness) and tzadaqah (righteousness), relieve me.
Don't bawaa (enter) into mashapat (judgment) with your ibad (servant), for in your panayam (sight) no man chay (living) is tzadaq (righteous).
For the ayab (enemy) pursues my napash (soul). He has struck my chay (life) down to the aratz (ground). He has made me live in dark places, as those who have been long mawath (dead).
Therefore my rawach (spirit) is overwhelmed within me. My lab (heart) within me is shamam (desolate).
I zakar (remember) the yawam (days) of qadam (old). I meditate on all your doings. I contemplate the pail (work) of your yad (hands).
I spread forth my yad (hands) to you. My napash (soul) Iyap for you, like a parched aratz (land). salah (selah).
Mahar to answer me, Yahawah. My rawach (spirit) kalah (fails). Don't hide your panayam (face) from me, so that I don't become like those who yarad (go) down into the bawar (pit).

Cause me to hear your loving chasad (kindness) in the baqar (morning), for I batach (trust) in you. yadai (cause) me to know the darak (way) in which I should yalak (walk), for I nashaa (lift) up my napash (soul) to you.
natzal (deliver) me, Yahawah, from my ayab (enemies). I flee to you to hide me.
Teach me to do your will, for you are my Alahayam. Your rawach (spirit) is tawab (good). Lead me in the aratz (land) of mayashawar (uprightness).
chayah (revive) me, Yahawah, for your sham (name's) sake. In your tzadaqah (righteousness), yatzaa (bring) my napash (soul) out of tzarah (trouble).
In your loving chasad (kindness), tzamath (cut) off my ayab (enemies), and abad (destroy) all those who tzarar (afflict) my napash (soul), For I am your ibad (servant).
Blessed be Yahawah, my tzawar (rock), who teaches my yad (hands) to war, and my fingers to battle:
my loving chasad (kindness), my fortress, my high tower, my deliverer, my magan (shield), and he in whom I take refuge; who subdues my im (people) under me.
Yahawah, what is adam (man), that you care for him? Or the ban (son) of anawash (man), that you chashab (think) of him?
adam (man) is like a habal (breath). His yawam (days) are like a shadow that passes ibar (away).
Part your shamayam (heavens), Yahawah, and yarad (come) down. nagai (touch) the har (mountains), and they will ishan (smoke).
Throw out lightning, and scatter them. shalach (send) out your chatz (arrows), and rout them.
shalach (stretch) out your yad (hand) from above, natzal (rescue) me, and natzal (deliver) me out of rab (great) mayam (waters), out of the yad (hands) of foreigners;
whose pah (mouths) dabar (speak) deceit, Whose right yamayan (hand) is a right yamayan (hand) of falsehood.
I will shayar (sing) a Chadash song to you, Alahayam. On a ten-stringed lyre, I will sing zamar (praises) to you.
You are he who nathan (gives) thashawaih (salvation) to malak (kings), who rescues Dawad, his ibad (servant), from the deadly charab (sword).
Rescue me, and natzal (deliver) me out of the yad (hands) of foreigners, whose pah (mouths) dabar (speak) deceit, whose right yamayan (hand) is a right yamayan (hand) of falsehood.
Then our ban (sons) will be like well-nurtured plants, our bath (daughters) like pillars carved to adorn a hayakal (palace).
Our barns are Malaa, filled with all kinds of provision. Our sheep bring forth alap (thousands) and ten alap (thousands) in our fields.
Our Alawap will pull heavy loads. There is no breaking in, and no yatzaa (going) away, and no outcry in our streets.
Happy are the im (people) who are in such a situation. Happy are the im (people) whose Alahayam is Yahawah.
I will exalt you, my Alahayam, the malak (king). I will barak (praise) your sham (name) iwalam (forever) and ever.
Every yawam (day) I will barak (praise) you. I will extol your sham (name) iwalam (forever) and ever.
gadawal (great) is Yahawah, and maad (greatly) to be praised! His greatness is unsearchable.
One dawar (generation) will shabach (commend) your maishah (works) to another, and will nagad (declare) your gabawarah (mighty) acts.
Of the kabawad (glorious) majesty of your honor, of your palaa (wondrous) dabar (works), I will meditate.
Men will amar (speak) of the might of your awesome yaraa (acts). I will declare your greatness.
They will utter the zakar (memory) of your rab (great) goodness, and will sing of your tzadaqah (righteousness).
Yahawah is Chanawan, Rachawam, Arak to ap (anger), and of gadawal (great) loving chasad (kindness).
Yahawah is tawab (good) to all. His tender racham (mercies) are over all his maishah (works).
All your maishah (works) will give yadah (thanks) to you, Yahawah. Your chasayad (saints) will extol you.
They will amar (speak) of the kabawad (glory) of your malakawath (kingdom), and dabar (talk) about your gabawarah (power);
to yadai (make) known to the ban (sons) of men his gabawarah (mighty) acts, the kabawad (glory) of the majesty of his malakawath (kingdom).

Your malakawath (kingdom) is an iwalam (forever) malakawath (kingdom). Your mamashalah (dominion) endures throughout all generations. Yahawah is faithful in all his words, and loving in all his deeds.
Yahawah samak (upholds) all who napal (fall), and raises up all those who are bowed down.
The iyan (eyes) of all wait for you. You nathan (give) them their food in due ith (season).
You pathach (open) your yad (hand), and satisfy the desire of every chay (living) thing.
Yahawah is tzadayaq (righteous) in all his darak (ways), and gracious in all his maishah (works).
Yahawah is qarawab (near) to all those who qaraa (call) on him, to all who qaraa (call) on him in truth.
He will ishah (fulfill) the desire of those who yaraa (fear) him. He also will hear their cry, and will yashai (save) them.
Yahawah shamar (preserves) all those who ahab (love) him, but all the rashai (wicked) he will destroy.
My pah (mouth) will dabar (speak) the thahalah (praise) of Yahawah. Let all flesh barak (bless) his qadash (holy) sham (name) id (forever) and ever.
halal (praise) Yah! halal (praise) Yahawah, my napash (soul).
While I chay (live), I will halal (praise) Yahawah. I will sing zamar (praises) to my Alahayam as long as I exist.
Don't batach (put) your trust in nadayab (princes), each a ban (son) of adam (man) in whom there is no thashawaih (help).
His rawach (spirit) departs, and he shawab (turn back / repent) to the adamah (earth). In that very yawam (day), his thoughts abad (perish).
Happy is he who has the Al of Yaiqab for his help, whose hope is in Yahawah, his Alahayam:
who made shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth), the yam (sea), and all that is in them; who shamar (keeps) truth iwalam (forever);
who ishah (executes) justice for the oppressed; who nathan (gives) lacham (food) to the Raib. Yahawah frees the prisoners.
Yahawah opens the eyes of the iwar (blind). Yahawah raises up those who are bowed down. Yahawah ahab (loves) the tzadayaq (righteous).
Yahawah shamar (preserves) the foreigners. He upholds the fatherless and alamanah (widow), but the darak (way) of the rashai (wicked) he iwath (turns) upside down.
Yahawah will malak (reign) iwalam (forever); your Alahayam, O Tzayawan, to all dawar (generations). halal (praise) Yah!
halal (praise) Yah, for it is tawab (good) to sing zamar (praises) to our Alahayam; for it is Naiyam and fitting to thahalah (praise) him.
Yahawah banah (builds) up Yarawashalam. He gathers together the outcasts of Yasharaal (Israel).
He heals the shabar (broken) in lab (heart), and binds up their wounds.
He counts the number of the kawakab (stars). He qaraa (calls) them all by their sham (names).
gadawal (great) is our Adawan, and rab (mighty) in kach (power). His thabawan (understanding) is infinite.
Yahawah upholds the Inaw. He brings the rashai (wicked) down to the aratz (ground).
Sing to Yahawah with thanksgiving. Sing zamar (praises) on the harp to our Alahayam,
who covers the sky with clouds, who kawan (prepares) rain for the aratz (earth), who makes grass grow on the har (mountains).
He provides lacham (food) for the livestock, and for the ban (young) ravens when they qaraa (call).
He doesn't delight in the gabawarah (strength) of the horse. He takes no pleasure in the legs of a ayash (man).
Yahawah takes pleasure in those who yaraa (fear) him, in those who hope in his loving chasad (kindness).
shabach (praise) Yahawah, Yarawashalam! halal (praise) your Alahayam, Tzayawan!
For he has strengthened the bars of your gates. He has blessed your ban (sons) inside you.
He shawam (makes) shalawam (peace) in your borders. He fills you with the finest of the wheat.
He shalach (sends) out his commandment to the aratz (earth). His dabar (word) runs very swiftly.
He nathan (gives) snow like wool, and scatters frost like ashes.
He hurls down his hail like pebbles. Who can imad (stand) panayam (before) his cold?
He shalach (sends) out his dabar (word), and masah (melts) them. He causes his rawach (wind) to blow, and the mayam (waters) nazal (flow).
He shows his dabar (word) to Yaiqab; his chaq (statutes) and his mashapat (ordinances) to Yasharaal (Israel).
He has not done this for just any gaway (nation). They don't yadai (know) his mashapat (ordinances). halal (praise) Yah!
halal (praise) Yah! halal (praise) Yahawah from the shamayam (heavens)! halal (praise) him in the heights!
halal (praise) him, all his malaak (angels)! halal (praise) him, all his tzabaa (army)!
halal (praise) him, shamash (sun) and yarach (moon)! halal (praise) him, all you shining kawakab (stars)!
halal (praise) him, you shamayam (heavens) of shamayam (heavens), You mayam (waters) that are above the shamayam (heavens).
Let them halal (praise) the sham (name) of Yahawah, For he tzawah (commanded), and they were created.
He has also established them id (forever) and ever. He has made a chaq (decree) which will not ibar (pass) away.
halal (praise) Yahawah from the aratz (earth), you great thanayan (sea) creatures, and all depths!
Lightning and hail, snow and clouds; stormy rawach (wind), fulfilling his dabar (word);
har (mountains) and all Gabaih; fruit itz (trees) and all cedars;
wild animals and all livestock; small creatures and flying birds;
malak (kings) of the aratz (earth) and all laam (peoples); shar (princes) and all shapat (judges) of the aratz (earth);
both young men and maidens; zaqan (old) men and children:
let them halal (praise) the sham (name) of Yahawah, for his sham (name) shagab (alone) is exalted. His glory is above the aratz (earth) and the shamayam (heavens).

He has lifted up the qaran (horn) of his im (people), the thahalah (praise) of all his chasayad (saints); even of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), a im (people) qarawab (near) to him. halal (praise) Yah!
halal (praise) Yahawah! shayar (sing) to Yahawah a Chadash song, his thahalah (praise) in the qahal (assembly) of the chasayad (saints).
Let Yasharaal (Israel) Shamach in him who made them. Let the children of Tzayawan be joyful in their malak (king).
Let them halal (praise) his sham (name) in the dance! Let them sing zamar (praises) to him with tambourine and harp!
For Yahawah takes pleasure in his im (people). He crowns the Inaw with yashawaih (salvation).
Let the chasayad (saints) rejoice in honor. Let them sing for joy on their beds.
May the high praises of Al be in their garawan (mouths), and a payapayah (two-edged) charab (sword) in their yad (hand);
To ishah (execute) vengeance on the gawayam (nations), and punishments on the laam (peoples);
To bind their malak (kings) with chains, and their kabad (nobles) with fetters of barazal (iron);
to ishah (execute) on them the written mashapat (judgment). All his chasayad (saints) have this honor. halal (praise) Yah!
halal (praise) Yah! halal (praise) Al in his qadash (sanctuary)! halal (praise) him in his heavens for his acts of iz (power)!
halal (praise) him for his gabawarah (mighty) acts! halal (praise) him according to his excellent greatness!
halal (praise) him with the sounding of the trumpet! halal (praise) him with harp and lyre!
halal (praise) him with tambourine and dancing! halal (praise) him with stringed instruments and flute!
halal (praise) him with loud cymbals! halal (praise) him with resounding cymbals!
Let everything that has nashamah (breath) halal (praise) Yah! halal (praise) Yah!
The proverbs of Shalamah, the ban (son) of Dawad, malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel):
to yadai (know) chakamah (wisdom) and instruction; to bayan (discern) the amar (words) of bayanah (understanding);
to receive instruction in shakal (wise) dealing, in tzadaq (righteousness), tzadaq (justice), and mayashar (equity);
to nathan (give) iramah (prudence) to the Pathay, daith (knowledge) and discretion to the nair (young) man:
that the chakam (wise) shamai (man) may hear, and increase in learning; that the bayan (man) of understanding may qanah (attain) to sound thachabalah (counsel):
to bayan (understand) a proverb, and parables, the dabar (words) and riddles of the chakam (wise).
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is the raashayath (beginning) of daith (knowledge); but the Awayal despise chakamah (wisdom) and instruction.
My ban (son), listen to your ab (father's) instruction, and don't forsake your am (mother's) teaching:
for they will be a garland to grace your raash (head), and chains around your neck.
My ban (son), if chataa (sinners) entice you, don't abah (consent).
If they amar (say), "yalak (come) with us, Let's lay in wait for dam (blood); let's lurk secretly for the naqay (innocent) without cause;
let's balai (swallow) them up chay (alive) like shaawal (sheol), and thamayam (whole), like those who yarad (go) down into the bawar (pit).
We'll matzaa (find) all Yaqar wealth. We'll malaa (fill) our bayath (houses) with spoil.
You shall napal (cast) your lot among us. We'll all have one purse.
My ban (son), don't yalak (walk) in the darak (way) with them. Keep your ragal (foot) from their nathayab (path),
for their feet run to rai (evil). They hurry to shed dam (blood).
For in vain is the net spread in the iyan (sight) of any bail (bird):
but these lay wait for their own dam (blood). They lurk secretly for their napash (own) lives.
So are the arach (ways) of everyone who is greedy for gain. It takes away the napash (life) of its owners.
chakamawath (wisdom) calls aloud in the street. She nathan (utters) her qawal (voice) in the public squares.
She qaraa (calls) at the raash (head) of noisy raash (places). At the entrance of the Iyar gates, she amar (utters) her amar (words):
"How long, you Pathay ones, will you ahab (love) Pathay? How long will Lawatz delight themselves in mockery, and Kasayal shanaa (hate) daith (knowledge)?
shawab (turn back / repent) at my reproof. Behold, I will pour out my rawach (spirit) on you. I will yadai (make) known my dabar (words) to you.
Because I have called, and you have refused; I have stretched out my yad (hand), and no qashab (one) has paid attention;
but you have ignored all my itzah (counsel), and wanted none of my reproof;
I also will laugh at your disaster. I will mock when calamity overtakes you;
when calamity overtakes you like a sawapah (storm), when your disaster comes on like a sawapah (whirlwind); when tzarah (distress) and anguish bawaa (come) on you.
Then will they qaraa (call) on me, but I will not answer. They will shachar (seek) me diligently, but they will not matzaa (find) me;
because they hated daith (knowledge), and didn't choose the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah.
They wanted none of my itzah (counsel). They despised all my reproof.
Therefore they will akal (eat) of the fruit of their own darak (way), and be filled with their own schemes.
For the backsliding of the Pathay will harag (kill) them. The careless ease of Kasayal will abad (destroy) them.
But whoever listens to me will shakan (dwell) securely, and will be at shaan (ease), without pachad (fear) of rai (harm).
My ban (son), if you will receive my amar (words), and store up my matzawah (commandments) within you;
So as to qashab (turn) your ear to chakamah (wisdom), and natah (apply) your lab (heart) to thabawan (understanding);
Yes, if you qaraa (call) out for discernment, and nathan (lift) up your qawal (voice) for thabawan (understanding);
If you seek her as kasap (silver), and search for her as for hidden treasures:
then you will bayan (understand) the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah, and matzaa (find) the daith (knowledge) of Alahayam.
For Yahawah nathan (gives) chakamah (wisdom). Out of his pah (mouth) comes daith (knowledge) and thabawan (understanding).
He lays up sound thawashayah (wisdom) for the yashar (upright). He is a magan (shield) to those who halak (walk) in tham (integrity);
that he may guard the arach (paths) of justice, and shamar (preserve) the darak (way) of his chasayad (saints).
Then you will bayan (understand) tzadaq (righteousness) and justice, mayashar (equity) and every tawab (good) maigal (path).
For chakamah (wisdom) will bawaa (enter) into your lab (heart). daith (knowledge) will be pleasant to your napash (soul).
Discretion will shamar (watch) over you. thabawan (understanding) will shamar (keep) you,
to natzal (deliver) you from the darak (way) of rai (evil), from the men who dabar (speak) perverse things;
who forsake the arach (paths) of yashar (uprightness), to yalak (walk) in the darak (ways) of chashak (darkness);
who Shamach to do rai (evil), and delight in the perverseness of rai (evil);
who are Iqash in their arach (ways), and wayward in their maigal (paths):
To natzal (deliver) you from the zawar (strange) ashah (woman), even from the nakaray (foreigner) who flatters with her amar (words);
who forsakes the Alawap of her youth, and forgets the barayath (covenant) of her Alahayam:
for her bayath (house) leads down to mawath (death), her maigal (paths) to the rapaa (dead).
None who bawaa (go) to her shawab (turn back / repent) again, neither do they attain to the arach (paths) of chay (life):
that you may yalak (walk) in the darak (way) of tawab (good) men, and shamar (keep) the arach (paths) of the tzadayaq (righteous).
For the yashar (upright) will shakan (dwell) in the aratz (land). The thamayam (perfect) will yathar (remain) in it.
But the rashai (wicked) will be karath (cut) off from the aratz (land). The bagad (treacherous) will be rooted out of it.
My ban (son), don't forget my teaching; but let your lab (heart) keep my matzawah (commandments):
for arak (length) of yawam (days), and Shanah of chay (life), and shalawam (peace), will they add to you.
Don't let chasad (kindness) and truth forsake you. qashar (bind) them around your neck. kathab (write) them on the tablet of your lab (heart).
So you will matzaa (find) favor, and tawab (good) shakal (understanding) in the iyan (sight) of Alahayam and adam (man).
batach (trust) in Yahawah with all your lab (heart), and don't shain (lean) on your own bayanah (understanding).
In all your darak (ways) yadai (acknowledge) him, and he will make your arach (paths) yashar (straight).
Don't be chakam (wise) in your own iyan (eyes). yaraa (fear) Yahawah, and sawar (depart) from rai (evil).
It will be health to your body, and nourishment to your itzam (bones).
Honor Yahawah with your substance, with the raashayath (first) fruits of all your increase:
so your barns will be filled with plenty, and your vats will overflow with new thayarawash (wine).
My ban (son), don't despise yahawah (yahweh's) discipline, neither be weary of his reproof:
for whom Yahawah ahab (loves), he yakach (reproves); even as a ab (father) reproves the ban (son) in whom he delights.
Happy is the adam (man) who matzaa (finds) chakamah (wisdom), the adam (man) who gets thabawan (understanding).
For her sachar (good) profit is tawab (better) than getting kasap (silver), and her thabawaah (return) is better than fine Charawatz.
She is more Yaqar than rubies. None of the things you can Chapatz are to be compared to her.
arak (length) of yawam (days) is in her right yamayan (hand). In her left shamaawal (hand) are riches and honor.
Her darak (ways) are darak (ways) of pleasantness. All her nathayab (paths) are shalawam (peace).
She is a itz (tree) of chay (life) to those who lay chazaq (hold) of her. ashar (happy) is everyone who retains her.
By chakamah (wisdom) Yahawah founded the aratz (earth). By understanding, he established the shamayam (heavens).
By his daith (knowledge), the depths were broken up, and the shachaq (skies) drop down the dew.
My ban (son), let them not depart from your iyan (eyes). Keep sound thawashayah (wisdom) and discretion:
so they will be chay (life) to your napash (soul), and grace for your neck.
Then you shall yalak (walk) in your darak (way) securely. Your ragal (foot) won't nagap (stumble).
When you shakab (lie) down, you will not be pachad (afraid). Yes, you will shakab (lie) down, and your shanah (sleep) will be sweet.
Don't be yaraa (afraid) of sudden pachad (fear), neither of the shawaa (desolation) of the rashai (wicked), when it bawaa (comes):
for Yahawah will be your confidence, and will shamar (keep) your ragal (foot) from being taken.
Don't withhold tawab (good) from those to whom it is bail (due), when it is in the al (power) of your yad (hand) to do it.
Don't amar (say) to your neighbor, "yalak (go), and shawab (turn back / repent) again; tomorrow I will nathan (give) it to you," when you have it by you.
Don't charash (devise) rai (evil) against your neighbor, since he yashab (dwells) securely by you.
Don't rayab (strive) with a adam (man) without cause, if he has done you no rai (harm).
Don't envy the ayash (man) of violence. Choose none of his darak (ways).
For the lawaz (perverse) is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, but his friendship is with the yashar (upright).
yahawah (yahweh's) maarah (curse) is in the bayath (house) of the rashai (wicked), but he blesses the Nawah of the tzadayaq (righteous).
Surely he Lawatz the Lawatz, but he nathan (gives) grace to the Inaw.
The chakam (wise) will nachal (inherit) kabawad (glory), but qalawan (shame) will be the promotion of Kasayal.
Listen, ban (sons), to a ab (father's) instruction. Pay attention and yadai (know) bayanah (understanding);
for I nathan (give) you sound learning. Don't forsake my thawarah (law).
For I was a ban (son) to my ab (father), Rak and an only child in the panayam (sight) of my am (mother).
He taught me, and said to me: "Let your lab (heart) retain my dabar (words). shamar (keep) my matzawah (commandments), and chayah (live).
qanah (get) chakamah (wisdom). qanah (get) bayanah (understanding). Don't forget, neither swerve from the amar (words) of my pah (mouth).
Don't forsake her, and she will shamar (preserve) you. ahab (love) her, and she will keep you.
chakamah (wisdom) is supreme. qanah (get) chakamah (wisdom). Yes, though it costs all your possessions, get bayanah (understanding).
Esteem her, and she will exalt you. She will kabad (bring) you to honor, when you embrace her.
She will nathan (give) to your raash (head) a garland of grace. She will deliver a itarah (crown) of splendor to you.
Listen, my ban (son), and receive my amar (sayings). The Shanah of your chay (life) will be many.
I have taught you in the darak (way) of chakamah (wisdom). I have led you in straight maigal (paths).
When you yalak (go), your steps will not be hampered. When you run, you will not stumble.
chazaq (take) firm hold of instruction. Don't let her rapah (go). Keep her, for she is your chay (life).
Don't bawaa (enter) into the arach (path) of the rashai (wicked). Don't walk in the darak (way) of rai (evil) men.
parai (avoid) it, and don't ibar (pass) by it. shatah (turn) from it, and ibar (pass) on.
For they don't sleep, unless they do raii (evil). Their shanah (sleep) is taken away, unless they make someone fall.
For they eat the lacham (bread) of rashai (wickedness), and drink the yayan (wine) of violence.
But the arach (path) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is like the dawning awar (light), that awar (shines) more and more until the kawan (perfect) yawam (day).
The darak (way) of the rashai (wicked) is like apalah (darkness). They don't yadai (know) what they stumble over.
My ban (son), attend to my dabar (words). natah (turn) your ear to my amar (sayings).
Let them not depart from your iyan (eyes). shamar (keep) them in the midst of your thawak (heart).
For they are chay (life) to those who matzaa (find) them, and health to their whole body.
Keep your lab (heart) with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of chay (life).
sawar (put) away from yourself a perverse pah (mouth). Put corrupt shapah (lips) rachaq (far) from you.
Let your iyan (eyes) look nakach (straight) ahead. Fix your gaze directly before you.
Make the maigal (path) of your feet level. Let all of your darak (ways) be established.
Don't natah (turn) to the right yamayan (hand) nor to the shamaawal (left). sawar (remove) your ragal (foot) from rai (evil).
My ban (son), pay attention to my chakamah (wisdom). natah (turn) your ear to my thabawan (understanding):
that you may maintain discretion, that your shapah (lips) may preserve daith (knowledge).
For the shapah (lips) of an adulteress drip honey. Her chak (mouth) is Chalaq than shaman (oil),
But in the acharayath (end) she is as Mar as wormwood, and as Chad as a pah (two-edged) charab (sword).
Her feet yarad (go) down to mawath (death). Her steps lead thamak (straight) to shaawal (sheol).
She gives no thought to the maigal (way) of chay (life). Her maigal (ways) are crooked, and she doesn't yadai (know) it.
Now therefore, my ban (sons), listen to me. Don't sawar (depart) from the amar (words) of my pah (mouth).
rachaq (remove) your darak (way) rachaq (far) from her. Don't qarab (come) near the door of her bayath (house),
lest you nathan (give) your honor to others, and your Shanah to the Akazaray one;
lest strangers feast on your kach (wealth), and your itzab (labors) enrich another man's bayath (house).
You will groan at your acharayath (latter) end, when your flesh and your body are consumed,
and amar (say), "How I have hated instruction, and my lab (heart) despised reproof;
neither have I obeyed the qawal (voice) of my teachers, nor turned my ear to those who instructed me!
I have Mait to the brink of utter ruin, in the midst of the gathered qahal (assembly).
Drink mayam (water) out of your own bawar (cistern), running nazal (water) out of your own baar (well).
Should your springs overflow in the streets, palag (streams) of mayam (water) in the public squares?
Let them be for yourself alone, not for strangers with you.
Let your spring be blessed. Shamach in the ashah (wife) of your youth.
A loving doe and a graceful deer— let her breasts rawah (satisfy) you at all ith (times). Be captivated always with her ahabah (love).
For why should you, my ban (son), be captivated with an adulteress? Why embrace the bosom of another?
For the darak (ways) of ayash (man) are before the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah. He examines all his maigal (paths).
The evil deeds of the rashai (wicked) ensnare him. The cords of his chataah (sin) hold him firmly.
He will mawath (die) for lack of instruction. In the greatness of his folly, he will shagah (go) astray.
My ban (son), if you have become collateral for your neighbor, if you have struck your kap (hands) in pledge for a stranger;
You are trapped by the amar (words) of your pah (mouth). You are ensnared with the amar (words) of your pah (mouth).
Do this now, my ban (son), and natzal (deliver) yourself, since you have bawaa (come) into the kap (hand) of your neighbor. yalak (go), humble yourself. Press your plea with your neighbor.
nathan (give) no shanah (sleep) to your iyan (eyes), nor slumber to your ipaip (eyelids).
Free yourself, like a gazelle from the yad (hand) of the hunter, like a bird from the snare of the fowler.
yalak (go) to the ant, you Itzal. raah (see) her darak (ways), and be chakam (wise);
which having no chief, shatar (overseer), or ruler,
kawan (provides) her lacham (bread) in the qayatz (summer), and gathers her food in the harvest.
How long will you sleep, Itzal? When will you qawam (arise) out of your shanah (sleep)?
A Mait shanah (sleep), a Mait slumber, a Mait folding of the yad (hands) to sleep:
so your poverty will bawaa (come) as a robber, and your scarcity as an magan (armed) ayash (man).
A worthless adam (person), a ayash (man) of awan (iniquity), is he who halak (walks) with a perverse pah (mouth);
who winks with his iyan (eyes), who signals with his feet, who motions with his fingers;
in whose lab (heart) is perverseness, who devises rai (evil) ith (continually), who ith (always) shalach (sows) discord.
Therefore his calamity will bawaa (come) suddenly. He will be shabar (broken) suddenly, and that without remedy.
There are shash (six) things which Yahawah shanaa (hates); yes, shabai (seven) which are an thawaibah (abomination) to him:
haughty iyan (eyes), a lying lashawan (tongue), yad (hands) that shed naqay (innocent) dam (blood);
a lab (heart) that charash (devises) awan (wicked) schemes, feet that are swift in running to rai (mischief),
a false witness who utters lies, and he who shalach (sows) discord among ach (brothers).
My ban (son), keep your ab (father's) matzawah (commandment), and don't forsake your am (mother's) teaching.
qashar (bind) them continually on your lab (heart). Tie them around your neck.
When you halak (walk), it will lead you. When you sleep, it will shamar (watch) over you. When you qawatz (awake), it will talk with you.
For the matzawah (commandment) is a nayar (lamp), and the thawarah (law) is awar (light). Reproofs of instruction are the darak (way) of life,
to shamar (keep) you from the immoral ashah (woman), from the chalaqah (flattery) of the wayward wife's lashawan (tongue).
Don't lust after her beauty in your labab (heart), neither let her captivate you with her ipaip (eyelids).
For a prostitute reduces you to a piece of lacham (bread). The adulteress hunts for your Yaqar napash (life).
Can a ayash (man) scoop ash (fire) into his lap, and his clothes not be burned?
Or can one halak (walk) on hot coals, and his feet not be scorched?
So is he who goes in to his neighbor's ashah (wife). Whoever touches her will not be unpunished.
Men don't despise a thief, if he steals to malaa (satisfy) himself when he is hungry:
but if he is found, he shall shalam (restore) shabaithayam (seven) times. He shall nathan (give) all the wealth of his bayath (house).
He who naap (commits) adultery with a ashah (woman) is Chasar of lab (understanding). He who does it shachath (destroys) his own napash (soul).
He will matzaa (get) nagai (wounds) and dishonor. His reproach will not be wiped machah (away).
For jealousy arouses the fury of the husband. He won't spare in the yawam (day) of vengeance.
He won't nashaa (regard) any kapar (ransom), neither will he abah (rest) content, though you give many shachad (gifts).
My ban (son), shamar (keep) my amar (words). Lay up my matzawah (commandments) within you.
shamar (keep) my matzawah (commandments) and chayah (live)! Guard my teaching as the apple of your iyan (eye).
qashar (bind) them on your fingers. kathab (write) them on the tablet of your lab (heart).
amar (tell) chakamah (wisdom), "You are my achawath (sister)." qaraa (call) understanding your relative,
that they may shamar (keep) you from the zawar (strange) ashah (woman), from the nakaray (foreigner) who flatters with her amar (words).
For at the window of my bayath (house), I looked out through my lattice.
I saw among the Pathay ones. I discerned among the ban (youths) a nair (young) man Chasar of lab (understanding),
passing ibar (through) the street near her corner, he went the darak (way) to her bayath (house),
in the nashap (twilight), in the yawam (evening) of the ayashawan (day), in the middle of the layal (night) and in the apalah (darkness).
Behold, there a ashah (woman) met him with the attire of a prostitute, and with crafty intent.
She is loud and defiant. Her feet don't stay in her bayath (house).
paim (now) she is in the streets, paim (now) in the squares, and lurking at every corner.
So she caught him, and kissed him. With an impudent panayam (face) she said to him:
"Sacrifices of shalam (peace) zabach (offerings) are with me. This yawam (day) I have paid my nadar (vows).
Therefore I came out to qaraah (meet) you, to shachar (diligently) seek your panayam (face), and I have found you.
I have spread my couch with carpets of tapestry, with striped cloths of the yarn of Matzarayam.
I have perfumed my bed with myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon.
yalak (come), let's take our rawah (fill) of loving until the baqar (morning). Let's solace ourselves with loving.
For my ayash (husband) isn't at bayath (home). He has gone on a Rachawaq darak (journey).
He has taken a tzarawar (bag) of kasap (money) with him. He will bawaa (come) bayath (home) at the yawam (full) kasaa (moon).
With persuasive laqach (words), she led him astray. With the flattering of her shapah (lips), she seduced him.
He followed her immediately, as an ox goes to the slaughter, as a Awayal stepping into a noose.
Until an chatz (arrow) strikes through his liver, as a bird hurries to the snare, and doesn't yadai (know) that it will cost his napash (life).
Now therefore, ban (sons), listen to me. Pay attention to the amar (words) of my pah (mouth).
Don't let your lab (heart) shatah (turn) to her darak (ways). Don't thaih (go) astray in her nathayab (paths),
for she has thrown down many Chalal. Yes, all her slain are a itzawam (mighty) army.
Her bayath (house) is the darak (way) to shaawal (sheol), yarad (going) down to the rooms of mawath (death).
Doesn't chakamah (wisdom) qaraa (cry) out? Doesn't understanding raise her qawal (voice)?
On the raash (top) of high places by the darak (way), where the nathayab (paths) meet, she natzab (stands).
Beside the gates, at the pah (entry) of the city, at the pah (entry) doors, she cries aloud:
"To you men, I qaraa (call)! I send my qawal (voice) to the ban (sons) of mankind.
You Pathay, bayan (understand) iramah (prudence). You Kasayal, be of an understanding lab (heart).
Hear, for I will dabar (speak) nagayad (excellent) things. The opening of my shapah (lips) is for mayashar (right) things.
For my chak (mouth) speaks truth. rashai (wickedness) is an thawaibah (abomination) to my shapah (lips).
All the amar (words) of my pah (mouth) are in tzadaq (righteousness). There is nothing crooked or perverse in them.
They are all Nakach to him who bayan (understands), yashar (right) to those who matzaa (find) daith (knowledge).
Receive my instruction rather than kasap (silver); daith (knowledge) rather than choice Charawatz.
For chakamah (wisdom) is tawab (better) than rubies. All the things that may be Chapatz can't be compared to it.
"I, chakamah (wisdom), have made iramah (prudence) my dwelling. matzaa (find) out daith (knowledge) and discretion.
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is to shanaa (hate) rai (evil). I shanaa (hate) pride, arrogance, the rai (evil) darak (way), and the perverse pah (mouth).
itzah (counsel) and sound knowledge are mine. I have understanding and gabawarah (power).
By me malak (kings) malak (reign), and razan (princes) chaqaq (decree) tzadaq (justice).
By me shar (princes) sharar (rule); nadayab (nobles), and all the righteous rulers of the aratz (earth).
I ahab (love) those who ahab (love) me. Those who shachar (seek) me diligently will matzaa (find) me.
With me are riches, honor, Ithaq wealth, and prosperity.
My fruit is tawab (better) than Charawatz, yes, than fine gold; my yield than choice kasap (silver).
I halak (walk) in the arach (way) of tzadaqah (righteousness), in the midst of the nathayab (paths) of justice;
That I may nachal (give) wealth to those who ahab (love) me. I malaa (fill) their treasuries.
"Yahawah possessed me in the raashayath (beginning) of his mapail (work), qadam (before) his deeds of old.
I was set up from iwalam (forever), from the raash (beginning), qadam (before) the aratz (earth) existed.
When there were no depths, I was brought chawal (forth), when there were no springs kabad (abounding) with mayam (water).
Before the har (mountains) were settled in place, panayam (before) the Gabaih, I was brought chawal (forth);
while as yet he had not made the aratz (earth), nor the fields, nor the raash (beginning) of the ipar (dust) of the world.
When he established the shamayam (heavens), I was there; when he chaqaq (set) a circle on the surface of the deep,
when he established the shachaq (clouds) above, when the springs of the deep became strong,
when he gave to the yam (sea) its boundary, that the mayam (waters) should not violate his commandment, when he marked out the foundations of the aratz (earth);
then I was the craftsman by his side. I was a delight yawam (day) by day, ith (always) rejoicing panayam (before) him,
Rejoicing in his whole aratz (world). My delight was with the ban (sons) of men.
"Now therefore, my ban (sons), listen to me, for blessed are those who shamar (keep) my darak (ways).
Hear instruction, and be chakam (wise). Don't parai (refuse) it.
Blessed is the adam (man) who hears me, watching yawam (daily) at my gates, waiting at my door posts.
For whoever matzaa (finds) me, matzaa (finds) chay (life), and will obtain favor from Yahawah.
But he who chataa (sins) against me wrongs his own napash (soul). All those who shanaa (hate) me ahab (love) mawath (death).
chakamawath (wisdom) has built her bayath (house). She has carved out her shabai (seven) pillars.
She has prepared her meat. She has mixed her yayan (wine). She has also set her table.
She has sent out her maidens. She qaraa (cries) from the highest places of the city:
"Whoever is Pathay, let him sawar (turn) in here!" As for him who is Chasar of lab (understanding), she amar (says) to him,
"yalak (come), eat some of my lacham (bread), Drink some of the yayan (wine) which I have mixed!
Leave your Pathay ways, and chayah (live). Walk in the darak (way) of bayanah (understanding).
He who corrects a Lawatz invites insult. He who yakach (reproves) a rashai (wicked) maawam (man) invites abuse.
Don't yakach (reprove) a Lawatz, lest he shanaa (hate) you. yakach (reprove) a wise chakam (man), and he will ahab (love) you.
Instruct a chakam (wise) chakam (man), and he will be still wiser. yadai (teach) a tzadayaq (righteous) yasap (man), and he will increase in learning.
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is the thachalah (beginning) of chakamah (wisdom). The daith (knowledge) of the qadawash (holy) One is bayanah (understanding).
For by me your yawam (days) will be multiplied. The Shanah of your chay (life) will be increased.
If you are chakam (wise), you are chakam (wise) for yourself. If you Lawatz, you alone will nashaa (bear) it.
The foolish ashah (woman) is loud, Undisciplined, and yadai (knows) mah (nothing).
She yashab (sits) at the door of her bayath (house), on a kasaa (seat) in the high places of the city,
To qaraa (call) to those who ibar (pass) by, who go yashar (straight) on their arach (ways),
"Whoever is Pathay, let him sawar (turn) in here." as for him who is Chasar of lab (understanding), she amar (says) to him,
"Stolen mayam (water) is sweet. lacham (food) eaten in secret is pleasant.
But he doesn't yadai (know) that the rapaa (dead) are there, that her qaraa (guests) are in the Imaq of shaawal (sheol).
The proverbs of Shalamah. A chakam (wise) ban (son) Shamach a glad ab (father); but a Kasayal ban (son) brings grief to his am (mother).
Treasures of rashai (wickedness) yail (profit) nothing, but tzadaqah (righteousness) natzal (delivers) from mawath (death).
Yahawah will not allow the napash (soul) of the tzadayaq (righteous) to go hungry, but he thrusts away the desire of the rashai (wicked).
He becomes poor who ishah (works) with a lazy kap (hand), but the yad (hand) of the Charawatz brings wealth.
He who gathers in qayatz (summer) is a shakal (wise) ban (son), but he who sleeps during the harvest is a ban (son) who causes shame.
barakah (blessings) are on the raash (head) of the tzadayaq (righteous), but violence covers the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked).
The zakar (memory) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is blessed, but the sham (name) of the rashai (wicked) will rot.
The chakam (wise) in lab (heart) accept matzawah (commandments), but a chattering Awayal will fall.
He who yalak (walks) blamelessly yalak (walks) surely, but he who perverts his darak (ways) will be found out.
qaratz (one) winking with the iyan (eye) nathan (causes) sorrow, but a chattering Awayal will fall.
The pah (mouth) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is a spring of chay (life), but violence covers the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked).
Hatred stirs up strife, but ahabah (love) covers all wrongs.
chakamah (wisdom) is found on the shapah (lips) of him who has discernment, but a shabat (rod) is for the back of him who is Chasar of lab (understanding).
chakam (wise) men lay up daith (knowledge), but the pah (mouth) of the Awayal is qarawab (near) ruin.
The Ishayar man's wealth is his iz (strong) city. The destruction of the Dal is their poverty.
The labor of the tzadayaq (righteous) leads to chay (life). The increase of the rashai (wicked) leads to chataah (sin).
He is in the arach (way) of chay (life) who shamar (heeds) correction, but he who forsakes reproof leads others thaih (astray).
He who hides hatred has lying shapah (lips). He who yatzaa (utters) a dabah (slander) is a Kasayal.
In the multitude of dabar (words) there is no lack of disobedience, but he who restrains his shapah (lips) does shakal (wisely).
The lashawan (tongue) of the tzadayaq (righteous) is like choice kasap (silver). The lab (heart) of the rashai (wicked) is of Mait worth.
The shapah (lips) of the tzadayaq (righteous) raih (feed) many, but the Awayal mawath (die) for Chasar of lab (understanding).
yahawah (yahweh's) barakah (blessing) brings wealth, and he adds no trouble to it.
It is a Kasayal pleasure to do wickedness, but chakamah (wisdom) is a ayash (man) of thabawan (understanding's) pleasure.
What the rashai (wicked) magawarah (fear), will overtake them, but the desire of the tzadayaq (righteous) will be granted.
When the sawapah (whirlwind) passes, the rashai (wicked) is no more; but the tzadayaq (righteous) stand firm iwalam (forever).
As vinegar to the teeth, and as ishan (smoke) to the iyan (eyes), so is the Itzal to those who shalach (send) him.
The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah prolongs yawam (days), but the Shanah of the rashai (wicked) shall be shortened.
The prospect of the tzadayaq (righteous) is joy, but the hope of the rashai (wicked) will abad (perish).
The darak (way) of Yahawah is a stronghold to the tham (upright), but it is a destruction to the pail (workers) of awan (iniquity).
The tzadayaq (righteous) will never be removed, but the rashai (wicked) will not shakan (dwell) in the aratz (land).
The pah (mouth) of the tzadayaq (righteous) brings forth chakamah (wisdom), but the perverse lashawan (tongue) will be karath (cut) off.
The shapah (lips) of the tzadayaq (righteous) yadai (know) what is acceptable, but the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked) is perverse.
A false balance is an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, Shalam accurate aban (weights) are his delight.
When pride bawaa (comes), then bawaa (comes) qalawan (shame), but with humility bawaa (comes) chakamah (wisdom).
The integrity of the yashar (upright) shall guide them, but the perverseness of the bagad (treacherous) shall shadad (destroy) them.
Riches don't yail (profit) in the yawam (day) of ibarah (wrath), but tzadaqah (righteousness) natzal (delivers) from mawath (death).
The tzadaqah (righteousness) of the blameless will yashar (direct) his darak (way), but the rashai (wicked) shall napal (fall) by his own rashaih (wickedness).
The tzadaqah (righteousness) of the yashar (upright) shall natzal (deliver) them, but the bagad (unfaithful) will be trapped by evil desires.
When a rashai (wicked) adam (man) dies, hope perishes, and expectation of power comes to nothing.
A tzadayaq (righteous) person is delivered out of tzarah (trouble), and the rashai (wicked) takes his place.
With his pah (mouth) the godless man shachath (destroys) his neighbor, but the tzadayaq (righteous) will be delivered through daith (knowledge).
When it goes tawab (well) with the tzadayaq (righteous), the city rejoices. When the rashai (wicked) abad (perish), there is shouting.
By the barakah (blessing) of the yashar (upright), the city is exalted, but it is overthrown by the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked).
bawaz (one) who despises his neighbor is Chasar of lab (wisdom), but a ayash (man) of thabawan (understanding) holds his charash (peace).
One who brings gossip betrays a confidence, but one who is of a trustworthy rawach (spirit) is kasah (one) who keeps a secret.
Where there is no wise guidance, the im (nation) napal (falls), but in the multitude of yaitz (counselors) there is thashawaih (victory).
He who is collateral for a stranger will suffer for it, but he who refuses pledges of collateral is batach (secure).
A gracious ashah (woman) obtains honor, but irayatz (violent) men obtain riches.
The chasad (merciful) ayash (man) does good to his own napash (soul), but he who is Akazaray troubles his own flesh.
rashai (wicked) people earn deceitful pailah (wages), but one who zarai (sows) tzadaqah (righteousness) reaps a amath (sure) reward.
He who is truly tzadaqah (righteous) gets chay (life). He who pursues rai (evil) gets mawath (death).
Those who are Iqash in lab (heart) are an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah, but those whose darak (ways) are blameless are his delight.
Most certainly, the rai (evil) naqah (man) will not be unpunished, but the zarai (seed) of the tzadayaq (righteous) will be delivered.
Like a gold ring in a pig's ap (snout), is a Yapah ashah (woman) who lacks taim (discretion).
The desire of the tzadayaq (righteous) is only tawab (good). The expectation of the rashai (wicked) is ibarah (wrath).
There is pazar (one) who scatters, and increases yet more. There is one who withholds more than is appropriate, but gains poverty.
The barakah (liberal) napash (soul) shall be made fat. He who rawah (waters) shall be watered also himself.
laam (people) naqab (curse) someone who withholds grain, but barakah (blessing) will be on the raash (head) of him who sells it.
He who shachar (diligently) seeks tawab (good) shachar (seeks) favor, but he who searches after rai (evil), it shall bawaa (come) to him.
He who batach (trusts) in his riches will napal (fall), but the tzadayaq (righteous) shall flourish as the green leaf.
He who troubles his own bayath (house) shall nachal (inherit) the rawach (wind). The Awayal shall be ibad (servant) to the chakam (wise) of lab (heart).
The fruit of the tzadayaq (righteous) is a itz (tree) of chay (life). He who is chakam (wise) wins napash (souls).
Behold, the tzadayaq (righteous) shall be repaid in the aratz (earth); how much more the rashai (wicked) and the sinner!
Whoever ahab (loves) correction ahab (loves) daith (knowledge), but he who shanaa (hates) reproof is Bair.
A tawab (good) pawaq (man) shall obtain favor from Yahawah, but he will rashai (condemn) a ayash (man) of mazamah (wicked) devices.
A adam (man) shall not be established by rashai (wickedness), but the root of the tzadayaq (righteous) shall not be moved.
A chayal (worthy) ashah (woman) is the itarah (crown) of her bail (husband), but a disgraceful wife is as rottenness in his itzam (bones).
The machashabah (thoughts) of the tzadayaq (righteous) are mashapat (just), but the advice of the rashai (wicked) is deceitful.
The dabar (words) of the rashai (wicked) are about lying in wait for dam (blood), but the pah (speech) of the yashar (upright) natzal (rescues) them.
The rashai (wicked) are overthrown, and are no more, but the bayath (house) of the tzadayaq (righteous) shall imad (stand).
A ayash (man) shall be commended according to his shakal (wisdom), but he who has a warped lab (mind) shall be despised.
tawab (better) is he who is qalah (lightly) esteemed, and has a ibad (servant), than he who honors himself, and Chasar lacham (bread).
A tzadayaq (righteous) yadai (man) respects the napash (life) of his animal, but the tender racham (mercies) of the rashai (wicked) are Akazaray.
He who ibad (tills) his adamah (land) shall have plenty of lacham (bread), but he who chases fantasies is Chasar of lab (understanding).
The rashai (wicked) desires the plunder of rai (evil) men, but the root of the tzadayaq (righteous) flourishes.
An rai (evil) mawaqash (man) is trapped by sinfulness of shapah (lips), but the tzadayaq (righteous) shall yatzaa (come) out of tzarah (trouble).
A ayash (man) shall be satisfied with tawab (good) by the fruit of his pah (mouth). The gamawal (work) of a adam (man's) yad (hands) shall be rewarded to him.
The darak (way) of a Awayal is yashar (right) in his own iyan (eyes), but he who is chakam (wise) listens to itzah (counsel).

He who robs his ab (father) and drives away his am (mother), is a ban (son) who causes shame and chapar (brings) reproach.
If you stop listening to instruction, my ban (son), you will stray from the amar (words) of daith (knowledge).
A corrupt witness Lawatz justice, and the pah (mouth) of the rashai (wicked) gulps down iniquity.
Penalties are prepared Lawatz scoffers, and beatings for the backs of Kasayal.
yayan (wine) is a Lawatz, and beer is a brawler. Whoever is led shagah (astray) by them is not chakam (wise).
The ayamah (terror) of a malak (king) is like the roaring of a kapayar (lion). He who provokes him to ibar (anger) forfeits his own napash (life).
It is an honor for a ayash (man) to keep aloof from rayab (strife); but every Awayal will be quarreling.
The Itzal will not charash (plow) by reason of the winter; therefore he shall shaal (beg) in harvest, and have nothing.
itzah (counsel) in the lab (heart) of ayash (man) is like Imaq mayam (water); but a ayash (man) of thabawan (understanding) will draw it out.
Many men claim to be men of unfailing chasad (love), but who can matzaa (find) a amawan (faithful) ayash (man)?
A tzadayaq (righteous) halak (man) walks in tham (integrity). Blessed are his children achar (after) him.
A malak (king) who yashab (sits) on the kasaa (throne) of dayan (judgment) scatters away all rai (evil) with his iyan (eyes).
Who can amar (say), "I have made my lab (heart) pure. I am zakah (clean) and without chataah (sin)?
Differing aban (weights) and differing measures, shanayam (both) of them alike are an thawaibah (abomination) to Yahawah.
Even a nair (child) makes himself known by his mailal (doings), whether his pail (work) is zak (pure), and whether it is yashar (right).
The hearing ear, and the seeing iyan (eye), Yahawah has made even shanayam (both) of them.
Don't ahab (love) shanah (sleep), lest you yarash (come) to poverty. Open your iyan (eyes), and you shall be satisfied with lacham (bread).
"It's no rai (good), it's no rai (good)," amar (says) the qanah (buyer); but when he is azal (gone) his way, then he halal (boasts).
There is gold and abundance of rubies; but the shapah (lips) of daith (knowledge) are a rare jewel.
Take the bagad (garment) of irab (one) who puts up collateral for a stranger; and hold him in chabal (pledge) for a wayward nakaray (woman).
Fraudulent lacham (food) is Irab to a ayash (man), but afterwards his pah (mouth) is filled with gravel.
Plans are established by thachabalah (advice); by wise guidance you wage war!
He who goes halak (about) as a tale-bearer galah (reveals) sawad (secrets); therefore don't keep company with him who opens wide his shapah (lips).
Whoever qalal (curses) his ab (father) or his am (mother), his nayar (lamp) shall be put out in blackness of chashak (darkness).
An nachalah (inheritance) quickly gained at the raashawan (beginning), won't be blessed in the acharayath (end).
Don't amar (say), "I will shalam (pay) back rai (evil)." Wait for Yahawah, and he will yashai (save) you.
Yahawah detests differing aban (weights), and dishonest scales are not pleasing.
A gabar (man's) steps are from Yahawah; how then can adam (man) bayan (understand) his darak (way)?
It is a snare to a adam (man) to make a rash dedication, then later to consider his nadar (vows).
A chakam (wise) malak (king) winnows out the rashai (wicked), and drives the threshing wheel over them.
The nashamah (spirit) of adam (man) is yahawah (yahweh's) nayar (lamp), searching all his innermost parts.
chasad (love) and amath (faithfulness) keep the malak (king) safe. His kasaa (throne) is sustained by chasad (love).
The glory of young men is their kach (strength). The splendor of zaqan (old) men is their shayabah (gray) hair.
Wounding blows cleanse away rai (evil), and beatings purge the innermost parts.
The malak (king's) lab (heart) is in yahawah (yahweh's) yad (hand) like the watercourses. He natah (turns) it wherever he desires.
Every darak (way) of a ayash (man) is yashar (right) in his own iyan (eyes), but Yahawah weighs the labah (hearts).
To do tzadaqah (righteousness) and tzadaqah (justice) is more acceptable to Yahawah than zabach (sacrifice).
A high iyan (look), and a Rachab lab (heart), the lamp of the rashai (wicked), is chataah (sin).
The plans of the Charawatz surely lead to profit; and everyone who is hasty surely rushes to poverty.
pail (getting) treasures by a lying lashawan (tongue) is a fleeting vapor for those who seek mawath (death).
The violence of the rashai (wicked) will drive them away, because they refuse to do what is mashapat (right).
The darak (way) of the Wazar is Hapakapak, but the conduct of the innocent is yashar (upright).
It is tawab (better) to yashab (dwell) in the corner of the housetop, than to share a bayath (house) with a contentious ashah (woman).
The napash (soul) of the rashai (wicked) desires rai (evil); his neighbor finds no chanan (mercy) in his iyan (eyes).
When the Lawatz is punished, the Pathay gains chakam (wisdom). When the chakam (wise) is instructed, he receives daith (knowledge).
The tzadayaq (righteous) One shakal (considers) the bayath (house) of the rashai (wicked), and brings the rashai (wicked) to ruin.
Whoever stops his ears at the cry of the Dal, he will also qaraa (cry) out, but shall not be heard.
A mathan (gift) in secret pacifies ap (anger); and a shachad (bribe) in the cloak, iz (strong) chamah (wrath).
It is joy to the tzadayaq (righteous) to do justice; but it is a destruction to the pail (workers) of awan (iniquity).
The adam (man) who thaih (wanders) out of the darak (way) of shakal (understanding) shall nawach (rest) in the qahal (assembly) of the rapaa (dead).
He who ahab (loves) pleasure shall be a poor ayash (man). He who ahab (loves) yayan (wine) and shaman (oil) shall not be rich.
The rashai (wicked) is a kapar (ransom) for the tzadayaq (righteous); the bagad (treacherous) for the upright.
It is tawab (better) to yashab (dwell) in a desert madayan (land), than with a contentious and fretful ashah (woman).
There is precious treasure and shaman (oil) in the Nawah of the chakam (wise); but a Kasayal adam (man) balai (swallows) it up.
He who follows after tzadaqah (righteousness) and chasad (kindness) matzaa (finds) chay (life), tzadaqah (righteousness), and honor.
A chakam (wise) man ilah (scales) the Iyar of the gabawar (mighty), and yarad (brings) down the iz (strength) of its confidence.
Whoever guards his pah (mouth) and his lashawan (tongue) shamar (keeps) his napash (soul) from tzarah (troubles).
The Zad and Zad Lawatz, "scoffer" is his sham (name); he ishah (works) in the arrogance of pride.
The desire of the Itzal mawath (kills) him, for his yad (hands) refuse to labor.
There are those who covet greedily all yawam (day) long; but the tzadayaq (righteous) nathan (give) and don't withhold.
The zabach (sacrifice) of the rashai (wicked) is an thawaibah (abomination): how much more, when he bawaa (brings) it with a zamah (wicked) mind!
A false witness will abad (perish), and a ayash (man) who listens dabar (speaks) to eternity.
A rashai (wicked) ayash (man) hardens his panayam (face); but as for the yashar (upright), he establishes his darak (ways).
There is no chakamah (wisdom) nor thabawan (understanding) nor itzah (counsel) against Yahawah.
The horse is prepared for the yawam (day) of battle; but thashawaih (victory) is with Yahawah.
A good sham (name) is more desirable than rab (great) riches, and tawab (loving) favor is better than kasap (silver) and gold.
The Ishayar and the poor have this in common: Yahawah is the maker of them all.
A Irawam man raah (see) danger, and hides himself; but the Pathay ibar (pass) on, and suffer for it.
The result of humility and the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is wealth, honor, and chay (life).
Thorns and snares are in the darak (path) Iqash the wicked: whoever guards his napash (soul) stays from them.
Train up a nair (child) in the darak (way) he should go, and when he is zaqan (old) he will not sawar (depart) from it.
The Ishayar mashal (rule) over the poor. The borrower is ibad (servant) to the lender.
He who zarai (sows) iwal (wickedness) reaps trouble, and the shabat (rod) of his fury will be destroyed.
He who has a generous iyan (eye) will be blessed; for he shares his lacham (food) with the Dal.
Drive out the Lawatz, and strife will yatzaa (go) out; yes, quarrels and insults will stop.
He who ahab (loves) Tahawar of lab (heart) and speaks gracefully is the malak (king's) rai (friend).
