My dawad (beloved) has gone down to his Gan, to the beds of spices, to raih (feed) in the Gan, and to gather lilies.
I am my dawad (beloved's), and my dawad (beloved) is mine. He browses among the lilies,
You are Yapah, my raiyah (love), as Tharatzah, lovely as Yarawashalam, awesome as an army with banners.
sabab (turn) away your iyan (eyes) from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats, that lie along the side of Galaid.
Your teeth are like a flock of ewes, which have ilah (come) up from the washing; of which every one has Thaam; none is Shakawal among them.
Your raqah (temples) are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your tzamah (veil).
There are shashayam (sixty) malakah (queens), shamanayam (eighty) concubines, and virgins without number.

My dove, my tham (perfect) one, is unique. She is her am (mother's) only daughter. She is the favorite one of her who bore her. The bath (daughters) saw her, and called her blessed; the malakah (queens) and the concubines, and they praised her.
Who is she who shaqap (looks) forth as the shachar (morning), Yapah as the labanah (moon), bar (clear) as the chamah (sun), and awesome as an army with banners?
I went down into the nut tree grove, to raah (see) the green plants of the nachal (valley), to raah (see) whether the vine budded, and the pomegranates were in flower.
Without realizing it, my napash (desire) shawam (set) me with my royal imayanadayab (people's) chariots. Friends

shawab (turn back / repent), shawab (turn back / repent), Shawalamayath! shawab (turn back / repent), shawab (turn back / repent), that we may gaze at you. Lover Why do you desire to gaze at the Shawalamayath, as at the dance of Mahanaim?
How beautiful are your feet in sandals, nadayab (prince's) bath (daughter)! Your rounded thighs are like jewels, the maishah (work) of the yad (hands) of a skillful workman.
Your body is like a round goblet, no mixed mazag (wine) is wanting. Your waist is like a heap of wheat, set about with lilies.
Your shanayam (two) breasts are like shanayam (two) fawns, that are twins of a roe.

Your neck is like an ivory magadal (tower). Your iyan (eyes) are like the pools in Chashabawan by the gate of Batharabayam. Your ap (nose) is like the magadal (tower) of Labanawan which looks panayam (toward) Damashaq.
Your raash (head) on you is like Karamal. The Dalah of your raash (head) like purple. The malak (king) is held captive in its tresses.
How beautiful and how pleasant you are, ahabah (love), for delights!
This, your stature, is like a palm tree, your breasts like its fruit.
I said, "I will ilah (climb) up into the palm tree. I will achaz (take) hold of its fruit." Let your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the rayach (smell) of your breath like apples, Beloved
Your chak (mouth) like the tawab (best) yayan (wine), that goes down smoothly for my dawad (beloved), gliding through the shapah (lips) of those who are yashan (asleep).
I am my dawad (beloved's). His desire is toward me.
yalak (come), my dawad (beloved), let us yatzaa (go) forth into the shadah (field). Let us lawan (lodge) in the villages.

Let's go shakam (early) up to the vineyards. raah (see) see whether the vine has budded, its blossom is pathach (open), and the pomegranates are in flower. There I will nathan (give) you my dawad (love).
The mandrakes nathan (give) forth fragrance. At our doors are all kinds of precious fruits, Chadash and Yashan, which I have stored up for you, my dawad (beloved).
Oh that you were like my ach (brother), who nursed from the breasts of my am (mother)! If I found you outside, I would kiss you; yes, and no bawaz (one) would despise me.
I would lead you, bringing you into my am (mother's) bayath (house), who would instruct me. I would have you shaqah (drink) spiced yayan (wine), of the isayas (juice) of my pomegranate.
His left shamaawal (hand) would be under my raash (head). His right yamayan (hand) would embrace me.
I shabai (adjure) you, bath (daughters) of Yarawashalam, that you not stir up, nor awaken ahabah (love), until it so desires. Friends

Who is this who ilah (comes) up from the madabar (wilderness), leaning on her dawad (beloved)? Under the apple tree I aroused you. There your am (mother) conceived you. There she was in labor and bore you.

shawam (set) me as a seal on your lab (heart), as a seal on your zarawai (arm); for ahabah (love) is iz (strong) as mawath (death). Jealousy is as Qashah as shaawal (sheol). Its flashes are flashes of ash (fire), a very flame of Yahawah.

Many mayam (waters) can't quench ahabah (love), neither can nahar (floods) drown it. If a ayash (man) would nathan (give) all the wealth of his bayath (house) for ahabah (love), he would be utterly scorned. Friends
We have a qatan (little) achawath (sister). She has no breasts. What shall we do for our achawath (sister) in the yawam (day) when she is to be spoken for?
If she is a wall, we will banah (build) on her a turret of kasap (silver). if she is a door, we will enclose her with boards of cedar. Beloved
I am a wall, and my breasts like magadal (towers), then I was in his iyan (eyes) like one who found shalawam (peace).
Shalamah had a vineyard at Bailahamawan Hamon. He leased out the vineyard to keepers. ayash (each) was to bawaa (bring) a alap (thousand) shekels of kasap (silver) for its fruit.
My own vineyard is panayam (before) me. The alap (thousand) are for you, Shalamah; two maah (hundred) for those who tend its fruit. Lover
You who yashab (dwell) in the Gan, with friends in attendance, let me hear your qawal (voice)! Beloved
Come away, my dawad (beloved)! Be like a gazelle or a young stag on the har (mountains) of spices!

The vision of Yashaiyah the ban (son) of Amawatz, which he saw concerning Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam, in the yawam (days) of Izayah, Yawatham, Achaz, and Yachazaqayah, malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah).
Hear, shamayam (heavens), and listen, aratz (earth); for Yahawah has spoken: "I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me.
The ox yadai (knows) his owner, and the donkey his bail (master's) crib; but Yasharaal (Israel) doesn't yadai (know), my im (people) don't bayan (consider).

Ah sinful gaway (nation), a im (people) Kabad with iwan (iniquity), a zarai (seed) of evildoers, children who deal corruptly! They have forsaken Yahawah. They have despised the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel). They are estranged and backward.
Why should you be beaten more, that you sarah (revolt) more and more? The whole raash (head) is sick, and the whole labab (heart) Daway.

From the kap (sole) of the ragal (foot) even to the raash (head) there is no soundness in it: wounds, welts, and Taray makah (sores). They haven't been closed, neither bandaged, neither soothed with shaman (oil).
Your aratz (country) is desolate. Your Iyar are burned with ash (fire). Strangers akal (devour) your adamah (land) in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers.
The bath (daughter) of Tzayawan is yathar (left) like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a field of melons, like a besieged Iyar.
Unless Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) had yathar (left) to us a very Mait sharayad (remnant), we would have been as Sadam; we would have been like Imarah.
Hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah, you qatzayan (rulers) of Sadam! Listen to the thawarah (law) of our Alahayam, you im (people) of Imarah!

"mah (what) are the multitude of your zabach (sacrifices) to me?," amar (says) Yahawah. "I have had enough of the burnt ilah (offerings) of ayal (rams), and the fat of fed animals. I don't delight in the dam (blood) of bulls, or of lambs, or of male goats.
When you bawaa (come) to raah (see) panayam (before) me, who has required this at your yad (hand), to trample my courts?

bawaa (bring) no more vain manachah (offerings). Incense is an thawaibah (abomination) to me; new chadash (moons), shabath (sabbaths), and maqaraa (convocations): I can't bear with awan (evil) maqaraa (assemblies).
My napash (soul) shanaa (hates) your New chadash (moons) and your mawaid (appointed) feasts. They are a burden to me. I am weary of bearing them.
When you spread forth your kap (hands), I will ilam (hide) my iyan (eyes) from you. Yes, when you make many prayers, I will not hear. Your yad (hands) are malaa (full) of dam (blood).
Wash yourselves, make yourself zakah (clean). sawar (put) away the rai (evil) of your mailal (doings) from before my iyan (eyes). chadal (cease) to do raii (evil).
Learn to do yatab (well). Seek justice. ashar (relieve) the oppressed. shapat (judge) the fatherless. rayab (plead) for the alamanah (widow).

"yalak (come) now, and let us yakach (reason) together," amar (says) Yahawah: "Though your chataa (sins) be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow. Though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool.
If you are abah (willing) and obedient, you shall akal (eat) the tawab (good) of the aratz (land);
but if you refuse and rebel, you shall be devoured with the charab (sword); for the pah (mouth) of Yahawah has spoken it.
How the aman (faithful) city has become a prostitute! She was Malaa of justice; tzadaq (righteousness) lodged in her, but now ratzach (murderers).
Your kasap (silver) has become dross, your sabaa (wine) mixed with mayam (water).

Your shar (princes) are rebellious, and companions of thieves. Everyone ahab (loves) shachad (bribes), and follows after rewards. They don't shapat (judge) the fatherless, neither does the rayab (cause) of the alamanah (widow) bawaa (come) to them.
Therefore the Adawan, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the abayar (mighty) One of Yasharaal (Israel), says: "Ah, I will get relief from my tzar (adversaries), and avenge myself of my ayab (enemies);
and I will shawab (turn back / repent) my yad (hand) on you, thoroughly purge away your dross, and will sawar (take) away all your tin.

I will shawab (turn back / repent) your shapat (judges) as at the raashawan (first), and your yaitz (counselors) as at the thachalah (beginning). Afterward you shall be called ‘The Iyar of tzadaq (righteousness), a aman (faithful) town.'
Tzayawan shall be padah (redeemed) with justice, and her shawab (turn back / repent) with tzadaqah (righteousness).
But the destruction of transgressors and chataa (sinners) shall be together, and those who forsake Yahawah shall be consumed.
For they shall be bawash (ashamed) of the ayal (oaks) which you have desired, and you shall be chapar (confounded) for the gardens that you have chosen.
For you shall be as an oak whose leaf fades, and as a garden that has no mayam (water).
The Chasan will be like tinder, and his pail (work) like a spark. They will shanayam (both) bair (burn) together, and no kabah (one) will quench them.
This is dabar (what) Yashaiyah the ban (son) of Amawatz saw concerning Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam.

It shall happen in the acharayath (latter) yawam (days), that the har (mountain) of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house) shall be established on the raash (top) of the har (mountains), and shall be raised above the Gabaih; and all gawayam (nations) shall flow to it.

Many im (peoples) shall halak (go) and amar (say), "yalak (come), let's ilah (go) up to the har (mountain) of Yahawah, to the bayath (house) of the Alahayam of Yaiqab; and he will teach us of his darak (ways), and we will yalak (walk) in his arach (paths)." For out of Tzayawan the thawarah (law) shall yatzaa (go) forth, and the dabar (word) of Yahawah from Yarawashalam.

He will shapat (judge) between the gawayam (nations), and will decide concerning many gawayam (peoples); and they shall kathath (beat) their charab (swords) into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. gawayam (nation) shall not nashaa (lift) up charab (sword) against gawayam (nation), neither shall they learn war any more.
bayath (house) of Yaiqab, yalak (come), and let us yalak (walk) in the awar (light) of Yahawah.

For you have forsaken your im (people), the bayath (house) of Yaiqab, because they are filled from the qadam (east), with those who practice divination like the Palashathay (Philistines), and they clasp hands with the children of nakaray (foreigners).

Their aratz (land) is malaa (full) of kasap (silver) and gold, neither is there any end of their treasures. Their aratz (land) also is malaa (full) of horses, neither is there any end of their chariots.
Their aratz (land) also is malaa (full) of idols. They shachah (worship) the maishah (work) of their own yad (hands), that which their own fingers have made.
adam (man) is brought low, and mankind is humbled; therefore don't nashaa (forgive) them.
bawaa (enter) into the tzawar (rock), and hide in the ipar (dust), from panayam (before) the pachad (terror) of Yahawah, and from the glory of his majesty.
The lofty iyan (looks) of adam (man) will be brought low, the haughtiness of men will be bowed down, and Yahawah shagab (alone) will be exalted in that yawam (day).
For there will be a yawam (day) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) for all that is Gaah and Gaah, and for all that is lifted up; and it shall be brought low:
For all the cedars of Labanawan, that are high and lifted up, for all the oaks of Bashan,
For all the high har (mountains), for all the Gabaih that are lifted up,
For every Gabah magadal (tower), for every fortified wall,
For all the ships of Tharashayash, and for all pleasant imagery.
The loftiness of adam (man) shall be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men shall be brought low; and Yahawah shagab (alone) shall be exalted in that yawam (day).
The idols shall kalayal (utterly) pass away.

Men shall bawaa (go) into the caves of the tzawar (rocks), and into the holes of the ipar (earth), from panayam (before) the pachad (terror) of Yahawah, and from the glory of his majesty, when he qawam (arises) to shake the aratz (earth) mightily.
In that yawam (day), men shall cast away their idols of kasap (silver), and their idols of gold, which have been made for themselves to shachah (worship), to the moles and to the bats;

To bawaa (go) into the caverns of the tzawar (rocks), and into the clefts of the ragged salai (rocks), from panayam (before) the pachad (terror) of Yahawah, and from the glory of his majesty, when he qawam (arises) to shake the aratz (earth) mightily.
Stop trusting in adam (man), whose nashamah (breath) is in his ap (nostrils); for of what chashab (account) is he?

For, behold, the Adawan, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), sawar (takes) away from Yarawashalam and from Yahawadah (Judah) supply and support, the whole supply of lacham (bread), and the whole supply of mayam (water);
the gabawar (mighty) man, the ayash (man) of war, the shapat (judge), the nabayaa (prophet), the diviner, the zaqan (elder),
the shar (captain) of chamashayam (fifty), the nashaa (honorable) man, the yaitz (counselor), the skilled Charash, and the clever enchanter.
I will nathan (give) nair (boys) to be their shar (princes), and children shall mashal (rule) over them.

The im (people) will be oppressed, everyone by ayash (another), and everyone by his neighbor. The nair (child) will behave himself proudly against the zaqan (old) man, and the qalah (base) against the honorable.

Indeed a ayash (man) shall take hold of his ach (brother) in the bayath (house) of his ab (father), saying, "You have clothing, you be our qatzayan (ruler), and let this ruin be under your yad (hand).

In that yawam (day) he will cry out, saying, "I will not be a healer; for in my bayath (house) is neither lacham (bread) nor clothing. You shall not shawam (make) me qatzayan (ruler) of the im (people).
For Yarawashalam is ruined, and Yahawadah (Judah) is fallen; because their lashawan (tongue) and their mailal (doings) are against Yahawah, to provoke the iyan (eyes) of his kabawad (glory).
The look of their panayam (faces) testify against them. They parade their chataah (sin) like Sadam. They don't hide it. Woe to their napash (soul)! For they have brought disaster upon themselves.
amar (tell) the tzadayaq (righteous) "tawab (good)!" For they shall akal (eat) the fruit of their deeds.
Woe to the rashai (wicked)! Disaster is upon them; for the deeds of his yad (hands) will be paid back to him.

As for my im (people), children are their oppressors, and women mashal (rule) over them. My im (people), those who ashar (lead) you thaih (cause) you to err, and balai (destroy) the darak (way) of your arach (paths).
Yahawah natzab (stands) up to rayab (contend), and imad (stands) to dayan (judge) the im (peoples).

Yahawah will bawaa (enter) into mashapat (judgment) with the zaqan (elders) of his im (people), and their leaders: "It is you who have eaten up the vineyard. The spoil of the Inay is in your bayath (houses).
What do you mean that you dakaa (crush) my im (people), and grind the panayam (face) of the Inay?" says the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).

Moreover Yahawah said, "Because the bath (daughters) of Tzayawan are haughty, and yalak (walk) with natah (outstretched) garawan (necks) and flirting iyan (eyes), walking to trip as they yalak (go), jingling ornaments on their feet;
therefore the Adanay brings sores on the qadaqad (crown) of the head of the women of Tzayawan, and Yahawah will make their scalps bald.
In that yawam (day) the Adanay will sawar (take) away the thapaarah (beauty) of their anklets, the headbands, the crescent necklaces,
the earrings, the bracelets, the railah (veils),
the headdresses, the ankle chains, the sashes, the perfume bottles, the charms,
the signet rings, the ap (nose) rings,
the fine robes, the capes, the cloaks, the purses,
the galayawan (hand) mirrors, the fine linen garments, the tiaras, and the shawls.

It shall happen that instead of sweet spices, there shall be rottenness; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of maishah (well) set hair, baldness; instead of a robe, a wearing of sackcloth; and branding instead of beauty.
Your men shall napal (fall) by the charab (sword), and your gabawarah (mighty) in the war.
Her gates shall lament and mourn; and she shall be desolate and yashab (sit) on the aratz (ground).

shabai (seven) women shall chazaq (take) hold of one ayash (man) in that yawam (day), saying, "We will akal (eat) our own lacham (bread), and Labash our own clothing: only let us be called by your sham (name). asap (take) away our reproach.

In that yawam (day), yahawah (yahweh's) branch will be tzabay (beautiful) and kabawad (glorious), and the fruit of the aratz (land) will be the beauty and glory of the survivors of Yasharaal (Israel).

It will happen, that he who is shaar (left) in Tzayawan, and he who yathar (remains) in Yarawashalam, shall be called qadawash (holy), even everyone who is written among the chay (living) in Yarawashalam;

when the Adanay shall have washed away the filth of the bath (daughters) of Tzayawan, and shall have purged the dam (blood) of Yarawashalam from its qarab (midst), by the rawach (spirit) of justice, and by the rawach (spirit) of burning.

Yahawah will baraa (create) over the whole habitation of har (mount) Tzayawan, and over her maqaraa (assemblies), a cloud and ishan (smoke) by yawamam (day), and the nagah (shining) of a lahabah (flaming) ash (fire) by layal (night); for over all the kabawad (glory) will be a canopy.
There will be a sakah (pavilion) for a shade in the yawamam (daytime) from the heat, and for a refuge and for a shelter from storm and from rain.
Let me shayar (sing) for my well yadayad (beloved) a song of my dawad (beloved) about his vineyard. My yadayad (beloved) had a vineyard on a very ban (fruitful) qaran (hill).

He dug it up, gathered out its saqal (stones), planted it with the choicest vine, built a magadal (tower) in its midst, and also chatzab (cut) out a yaqab (winepress) therein. He looked for it to ishah (yield) inab (grapes), but it yielded wild grapes.
"Now, yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam and men of Yahawadah (Judah), please shapat (judge) between me and my vineyard.
What could have been done more to my vineyard, that I have not done in it? Why, when I looked for it to ishah (yield) inab (grapes), did it ishah (yield) wild grapes?
Now I will yadai (tell) you what I will do to my vineyard. I will sawar (take) away its hedge, and it will be eaten up. I will break down its wall of it, and it will be trampled down.
I will shayath (lay) it a wasteland. It won't be pruned nor hoed, but it will ilah (grow) briers and thorns. I will also tzawah (command) the clouds that they rain no rain on it.

For the vineyard of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) is the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), and the men of Yahawadah (Judah) his pleasant plant: and he looked for justice, but, behold, oppression; for tzadaqah (righteousness), but, behold, a cry of distress.

Woe to those who nagai (join) bayath (house) to bayath (house), who lay shadah (field) to shadah (field), until there is no room, and you are made to yashab (dwell) alone in the qarab (midst) of the aratz (land)!
In my ears, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) says: "laa (surely) many bayath (houses) will be desolate, even gadawal (great) and tawab (beautiful), unoccupied.
For ishar (ten) tzamad (acres) of vineyard shall ishah (yield) one bath, and a homer of zarai (seed) shall ishah (yield) an ephah.
Woe to those who shakam (rise) up early in the baqar (morning), that they may follow shakar (strong) drink; who stay late into the nashap (night), until yayan (wine) inflames them!
The harp, lyre, tambourine, and flute, with yayan (wine), are at their feasts; but they don't respect the pail (work) of Yahawah, neither have they considered the operation of his yad (hands).
Therefore my im (people) galah (go) into captivity for lack of daith (knowledge). Their honorable men are famished, and their multitudes are Tzachah with thirst.
Therefore shaawal (sheol) has enlarged its desire, and opened its pah (mouth) without chaq (measure); and their glory, their multitude, their pomp, and he who Ilaz among them, descend into it.
So adam (man) is brought low, mankind is humbled, and the iyan (eyes) Gabah the arrogant shapal (ones) are humbled;
but Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) is exalted in justice, and Al the qadawash (holy) One is sanctified in tzadaqah (righteousness).
Then the lambs will graze as in their pasture, and gawar (strangers) will akal (eat) the ruins of the rich.
Woe to those who draw iwan (iniquity) with cords of falsehood, and wickedness as with cart rope;

Who amar (say), "Let him make speed, let him hasten his maishah (work), that we may raah (see) it; and let the itzah (counsel) of the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel) qarab (draw) near and bawaa (come), that we may yadai (know) it!

Woe to those who amar (call) rai (evil) tawab (good), and tawab (good) rai (evil); who shawam (put) chashak (darkness) for awar (light), and awar (light) for chashak (darkness); who shawam (put) Mar for Mathawaq, and Mathawaq for Mar!
Woe to those who are chakam (wise) in their own iyan (eyes), and bayan (prudent) in their own panayam (sight)!
Woe to those who are gabawar (mighty) to drink yayan (wine), and champions at mixing shakar (strong) drink;
who acquit the rashai (guilty) for a shachad (bribe), but deny tzadaqah (justice) for the innocent!

Therefore as the tongue of ash (fire) akal (devours) the stubble, and as the dry grass sinks down in the flame, so their root shall be as rottenness, and their blossom shall ilah (go) up as dust; because they have rejected the thawarah (law) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), and despised the amarah (sayings) of the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).

Therefore yahawah (yahweh's) ap (anger) charah (burns) against his im (people), and he has stretched out his yad (hand) against them, and has struck them. The har (mountains) tremble, and their nabalah (dead) bodies are as refuse in the qarab (midst) of the streets. For all this, his ap (anger) is not turned shawab (turn back / repent), but his yad (hand) is still stretched out.

He will nashaa (lift) up a nas (banner) to the gawayam (nations) from Rachawaq, and he will whistle for them from the end of the aratz (earth). Behold, they will bawaa (come) speedily and qal (swiftly).
None shall be Iyap nor stumble among them; none shall nawam (slumber) nor sleep; neither shall the belt of their waist be untied, nor the latchet of their shoes be broken:
whose chatz (arrows) are sharp, and all their qashath (bows) bent. Their horses' hoofs will be chashab (like) tzar (flint), and their galagal (wheels) like a sawapah (whirlwind).
Their roaring will be like a labayaa (lioness). They will roar like young kapayar (lions). Yes, they shall roar, and seize their Tarap and carry it off, and there will be no one to natzal (deliver).

They will roar against them in that yawam (day) like the roaring of the yam (sea). If nabat (one) looks to the aratz (land) behold, chashak (darkness) and tzar (distress). The awar (light) is darkened in its clouds.
In the Shanah that malak (king) Izayah mawath (died), I saw the Adanay sitting on a kasaa (throne), high and lifted up; and his train Malaa the hayakal (temple).
Above him stood the seraphim. achad (each) one had shash (six) wings. With shanayam (two) he covered his panayam (face). With shanayam (two) he covered his feet. With shanayam (two) he flew.
One called to another, and said, "qadawash (holy), qadawash (holy), qadawash (holy), is Yahawah of tzabaa (armies)! The whole aratz (earth) is full of his kabawad (glory)!
The foundations of the thresholds shook at the qawal (voice) of him who called, and the bayath (house) was filled with ishan (smoke).

Then I said, "Woe is me! For I am damah (undone), because I am a ayash (man) of tamaa (unclean) shapah (lips), and I yashab (dwell) in the midst of a im (people) of tamaa (unclean) shapah (lips): for my iyan (eyes) have seen the malak (king), Yahawah of tzabaa (armies)!
Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having a live coal in his yad (hand), which he had taken with the tongs from off the mazabach (altar).
He touched my pah (mouth) with it, and said, "Behold, this has touched your shapah (lips); and your iwan (iniquity) is taken sawar (away), and your chataah (sin) forgiven.
I heard the Lord's qawal (voice), saying, "Whom shall I shalach (send), and who will yalak (go) for us?" Then I said, "Here I am. shalach (send) me!
He said, "yalak (go), and amar (tell) this im (people), ‘You hear indeed, but don't bayan (understand); and you raah (see) raah (see), but don't yadai (perceive).'

Make the lab (heart) of this im (people) fat. Make their ears kabad (heavy), and shut their iyan (eyes); lest they raah (see) with their iyan (eyes), and hear with their ears, and bayan (understand) with their labab (heart), and shawab (turn back / repent) again, and be healed.
Then I said, "Adanay, how long?" He answered, "Until Iyar are waste without yashab (inhabitant), and bayath (houses) without adam (man), and the adamah (land) becomes utterly waste,
And Yahawah has removed men rachaq (far) away, and the forsaken places are many in the qarab (midst) of the aratz (land).

If there is a ishayaray (tenth) left in it, that also will in shawab (turn back / repent) be consumed: as a terebinth, and as an oak, whose stock remains when they are felled; so the qadash (holy) zarai (seed) is its stock.

It happened in the yawam (days) of Achaz the ban (son) of Yawatham, the ban (son) of Izayah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), that Ratzayan the malak (king) of Aram, and Paqach the ban (son) of Ramalayahaw, malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), went up to Yarawashalam to war against it, but could not prevail against it.

It was told the bayath (house) of Dawad, saying, "Aram is allied with Aparayam." His labab (heart) trembled, and the labab (heart) of his im (people), as the itz (trees) of the Yair tremble with the rawach (wind).

Then Yahawah said to Yashaiyah, "yatzaa (go) out now to qaraah (meet) Achaz, you, and Shaarayashawab your ban (son), at the end of the thailah (conduit) of the Ilayawan pool, on the masalah (highway) of the fuller's shadah (field).

amar (tell) him, ‘Be careful, and keep calm. Don't be yaraa (afraid), neither let your rakak (heart) be faint because of these shanayam (two) tails of Ishan torches, for the fierce ap (anger) of Ratzayan and Aram, and of the ban (son) of Ramalayahaw.
Because Aram, Aparayam, and the ban (son) of Ramalayahaw, have plotted rai (evil) amar (against) you, saying,
"Let's ilah (go) up against Yahawadah (Judah), and tear it apart, and let's divide it among ourselves, and malak (set) up a malak (king) in its midst, even the ban (son) of Tabaal.
This is what the Adanay Yahawah amar (says): "It shall not qawam (stand), neither shall it happen.

For the raash (head) of Aram is Damashaq, and the raash (head) of Damashaq is Ratzayan; and within shashayam (sixty) - chamash (five) Shanah Aparayam shall be broken in pieces, so that it shall not be a im (people);
and the raash (head) of Aparayam is Shamarawan, and the raash (head) of Shamarawan is Ramalayahaw ban (son). If you will not aman (believe), aman (surely) you shall not be established.'
Yahawah spoke again to Achaz, saying,
"shaal (ask) a awath (sign) of Yahawah your Alahayam; shaal (ask) it either in the depth, or in the height above.
But Achaz said, "I will not shaal (ask), neither will I tempt Yahawah.
He said, "Listen now, bayath (house) of Dawad. Is it not Mait for you to try the patience of men, that you will try the patience of my Alahayam also?
Therefore the Adanay himself will nathan (give) you a awath (sign). Behold, the virgin will harah (conceive), and yalad (bear) a ban (son), and shall qaraa (call) his sham (name) Imanawaal.
He shall akal (eat) butter and honey when he yadai (knows) to refuse the rai (evil), and choose the tawab (good).
For before the nair (child) yadai (knows) to refuse the rai (evil), and choose the tawab (good), the adamah (land) whose shanayam (two) malak (kings) you abhor shall be forsaken.

Yahawah will bawaa (bring) on you, on your im (people), and on your ab (father's) bayath (house), yawam (days) that have not bawaa (come), from the yawam (day) that Aparayam sawar (departed) from Yahawadah (Judah); even the malak (king) of Ashawar.
It will happen in that yawam (day) that Yahawah will whistle for the fly that is in the uttermost part of the yaar (rivers) of Matzarayam, and for the bee that is in the aratz (land) of Ashawar.
They shall bawaa (come), and shall all nawach (rest) in the desolate nachal (valleys), in the clefts of the salai (rocks), on all thorn hedges, and on all pastures.

In that yawam (day) the Adanay will shave with a razor that is Shakayarah in the parts ibar (beyond) the nahar (river), even with the malak (king) of Ashawar, the raash (head) and the hair of the feet; and it shall also sapah (consume) the beard.
It shall happen in that yawam (day) that a ayash (man) shall chayah (keep) alive a young Igalah, and shanayam (two) sheep;

and it shall happen, that because of the abundance of milk which they shall give he shall akal (eat) butter: for everyone will akal (eat) butter and honey that is yathar (left) in the midst of the aratz (land).
It will happen in that yawam (day) that every place where there were a alap (thousand) vines at a alap (thousand) kasap (silver) shekels, shall be for briers and thorns.
People will bawaa (go) there with chatz (arrows) and with qashath (bow), because all the aratz (land) will be briers and thorns.

All the har (hills) that were cultivated with the hoe, you shall not bawaa (come) there for yaraah (fear) of briers and thorns; but it shall be for the sending forth of oxen, and for the treading of sheep.
Yahawah said to me, "Take a large tablet, and kathab (write) on it with a anawash (man's) pen, ‘For Maharashalalachashabaz Shalal Hash Baz;'
and I will iwad (take) for myself aman (faithful) witnesses to iwad (testify): Awarayah the kahan (priest), and Zakarayah the ban (son) of Yabarakayahaw.
I went to the prophetess, and she conceived, and bore a ban (son). Then Yahawah said to me, "qaraa (call) his sham (name) ‘Maharashalalachashabaz Shalal Hash Baz.'

For before the nair (child) yadai (knows) how to qaraa (say), ‘My ab (father),' and, ‘My am (mother),' the riches of Damashaq and the spoil of Shamarawan will be carried nashaa (away) by the malak (king) of Ashawar.
Yahawah spoke to me yet again, saying,
"Because this im (people) have refused the mayam (waters) of Shalach that halak (go) softly, and rejoice in Ratzayan and Ramalayahaw ban (son);

now therefore, behold, the Adanay ilah (brings) upon them the itzawam (mighty) flood mayam (waters) of the nahar (river): the malak (king) of Ashawar and all his kabawad (glory). It will ilah (come) up over all its apayaq (channels), and halak (go) over all its banks.

It will sweep onward into Yahawadah (Judah). It will overflow and ibar (pass) through; it will nagai (reach) even to the neck; and the stretching out of its wings will fill the breadth of your aratz (land), Imanawaal.
Make an uproar, you im (peoples), and be broken in pieces! Listen, all you from far aratz (countries): dress for battle, and be shattered! Dress for battle, and be shattered!
Take itzah (counsel) together, and it will be brought to nothing; dabar (speak) the dabar (word), and it will not qawam (stand): for Al is with us.
For Yahawah spoke thus to me with a chazaqah (strong) yad (hand), and instructed me not to yalak (walk) in the darak (way) of this im (people), saying,
"Don't amar (say), ‘A conspiracy!' concerning all about which this im (people) amar (say), ‘A conspiracy!' neither yaraa (fear) their threats, nor be terrorized.
Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) is who you must respect as holy. He is the one you must mawaraa (fear). He is the one you must iratz (dread).
He will be a maqadash (sanctuary), but for shanayam (both) bayath (houses) of Yasharaal (Israel), he will be a trap and a snare for the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam.
Many will stumble over it, napal (fall), be shabar (broken), be snared, and be captured.
Wrap up the thaiwadah (testimony). Seal the thawarah (law) among my Lamawad.
I will wait for Yahawah, who hides his panayam (face) from the bayath (house) of Yaiqab, and I will look for him.

Behold, I and the children whom Yahawah has given me are for awath (signs) and for mawapath (wonders) in Yasharaal (Israel) from Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), who shakan (dwells) in har (mount) Tzayawan.

When they amar (tell) you, "Consult with those who have familiar awab (spirits) and with the wizards, who chirp and who mutter:" shouldn't a im (people) consult with their Alahayam? Should they consult the mawath (dead) on behalf of the chay (living)?
Turn to the thawarah (law) and to the thaiwadah (testimony)! If they don't amar (speak) according to this dabar (word), surely there is no shachar (morning) for them.

They will ibar (pass) through it, very distressed and Raib; and it will happen that when they are hungry, they will worry, and qalal (curse) by their malak (king) and by their Alahayam. They will panah (turn) their mail (faces) upward,
and look to the aratz (earth), and see tzarah (distress), chashakah (darkness), and the gloom of anguish. They will be driven into thick apalah (darkness).

But there shall be no more gloom for her who was in anguish. In the raashawan (former) time, he brought into qalal (contempt) the aratz (land) of Zabawalawan and the aratz (land) of Napathalay; but in the Acharawan time he has made it kabad (glorious), by the darak (way) of the yam (sea), ibar (beyond) the Yaradan, Galayal of the gaway (nations).

The im (people) who walked in chashak (darkness) have seen a gadawal (great) awar (light). Those who lived in the aratz (land) of the shadow of tzalamawath (death), on them the awar (light) has shined.
You have multiplied the gaway (nation). You have increased their joy. They rejoice panayam (before) you according to the joy in harvest, as men rejoice when they divide the spoil.
For the yoke of his burden, and the matah (staff) of his shoulder, the shabat (rod) of his oppressor, you have broken as in the yawam (day) of Madayan.
For all the armor of the armed saan (man) in the noisy battle, and the garments rolled in dam (blood), will be for burning, fuel for the ash (fire).

For to us a yalad (child) is yalad (born). To us a ban (son) is given; and the government will be on his shoulders. His sham (name) will be called Wonderful, yaitz (counselor), gabawar (mighty) Al, id (everlasting) ab (father), shar (prince) of shalawam (peace).

Of the increase of his government and of shalawam (peace) there shall be no end, on the kasaa (throne) of Dawad, and on his mamalakah (kingdom), to kawan (establish) it, and to uphold it with justice and with tzadaqah (righteousness) from that time on, even iwalam (forever). The zeal of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) will ishah (perform) this.
The Adanay sent a dabar (word) into Yaiqab, and it napal (falls) on Yasharaal (Israel).
All the im (people) will yadai (know), including Aparayam and the yashab (inhabitants) of Shamarawan, who amar (say) in pride and in arrogance of labab (heart),
"The bricks have fallen, but we will banah (build) with cut gazayath (stone). The sycamore fig trees have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place.
Therefore Yahawah will set up on high against him the tzar (adversaries) of Ratzayan, and will stir up his ayab (enemies),

The Aram (Syrians) in front, and the Palashathay (Philistines) behind; and they will akal (devour) Yasharaal (Israel) with open pah (mouth). For all this, his ap (anger) is not turned shawab (turn back / repent), but his yad (hand) is stretched out still.
Yet the im (people) have not turned to him who struck them, neither have they sought Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
Therefore Yahawah will karath (cut) off from Yasharaal (Israel) raash (head) and tail, palm branch and reed, in one yawam (day).
The zaqan (elder) and the honorable hawaa (man) is the raash (head), and the nabayaa (prophet) who teaches lies is the tail.
For those who ashar (lead) this im (people) lead them thaih (astray); and those who are led by them are destroyed.

Therefore the Adanay will not Shamach over their young men, neither will he have racham (compassion) on their fatherless and alamanah (widows); for everyone is profane and an evildoer, and every pah (mouth) dabar (speaks) folly. For all this his ap (anger) is not turned shawab (turn back / repent), but his yad (hand) is stretched out still.

For rashaih (wickedness) bair (burns) like a ash (fire). It akal (devours) the briers and thorns; yes, it yatzath (kindles) in the thickets of the Yair, and they roll upward in a column of ishan (smoke).
Through the ibarah (wrath) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the aratz (land) is burnt up; and the im (people) are the fuel for the ash (fire). No one spares his ach (brother).

gazar (one) will devour on the right yamayan (hand), and be Raib; and he will akal (eat) on the left shamaawal (hand), and they will not be satisfied. Everyone will akal (eat) the flesh of his own zarawai (arm):

Manashah, Aparayam; and Aparayam, Manashah; and they together shall be against Yahawadah (Judah). For all this his ap (anger) is not turned shawab (turn back / repent), but his yad (hand) is stretched out still.
Woe to those who chaqaq (decree) awan (unrighteous) decrees, and to the writers who kathab (write) oppressive decrees;

to deprive the Dal from dayan (justice), and to rob the Inay among my im (people) of their mashapat (rights), that alamanah (widows) may be their spoil, and that they may make the fatherless their prey!
What will you do in the yawam (day) of visitation, and in the shawaa (desolation) which will bawaa (come) from afar? To whom will you flee for help? Where will you leave your wealth?
They will only bow down under the prisoners, and will napal (fall) under the slain. For all this his ap (anger) is not turned shawab (turn back / repent), but his yad (hand) is stretched out still.
Alas Ashawar (Assyrian), the shabat (rod) of my ap (anger), the matah (staff) in whose yad (hand) is my indignation!

I will shalach (send) him against a profane gaway (nation), and against the im (people) who ibarah (anger) me will I give him a tzawah (command) to take the spoil and to take the prey, and to shawam (tread) them down like the mire of the streets.
However he doesn't mean so, neither does his labab (heart) chashab (think) so; but it is in his labab (heart) to destroy, and to karath (cut) off not a Mait gawayam (nations).
For he amar (says), "Aren't all of my shar (princes) malak (kings)?
Isn't Kalanah like Karakamayash? Isn't Chamath like Arapad? Isn't Shamarawan like Damashaq?
As my yad (hand) has found the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the idols, whose engraved pasayal (images) exceeded those of Yarawashalam and of Shamarawan;
shall I not, as I have done to Shamarawan and her idols, so do to Yarawashalam and her itzab (idols)?

Therefore it will happen that, when the Adanay has performed his whole maishah (work) on har (mount) Tzayawan and on Yarawashalam, I will paqad (punish) the fruit of the willful proud labab (heart) of the malak (king) of Ashawar, and the insolence of his haughty iyan (looks).

For he has said, "By the kach (strength) of my yad (hand) I have done it, and by my chakamah (wisdom); for I have understanding: and I have removed the boundaries of the im (peoples), and have robbed their Ithawad. Like a abayar (valiant) man I have brought down their rulers.

My yad (hand) has found the riches of the im (peoples) like a nest, and like one asap (gathers) eggs that are abandoned, have I gathered all the aratz (earth). There was no one who moved their wing, or that opened their pah (mouth), or chirped.

Should an axe brag against him who chops with it? Should a saw exalt itself above him who saws with it? As if a shabat (rod) should lift those who lift it up, or as if a matah (staff) should lift up someone who is not itz (wood).
Therefore the Adawan, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), will shalach (send) among his fat mashaman (ones) leanness; and under his kabawad (glory) a burning will be kindled like the burning of ash (fire).

The awar (light) of Yasharaal (Israel) will be for a ash (fire), and his qadawash (holy) One for a lahabah (flame); and it will bair (burn) and akal (devour) his thorns and his briers in one yawam (day).
He will kalah (consume) the kabawad (glory) of his Yair, and of his fruitful field, both napash (soul) and body. It will be as when a standard bearer faints.
The shaar (remnant) of the itz (trees) of his Yair shall be few, so that a nair (child) could kathab (write) their number.

It will come to pass in that yawam (day) that the shaar (remnant) of Yasharaal (Israel), and those who have palayatah (escaped) from the bayath (house) of Yaiqab will no more again shain (lean) on him who struck them, but shall shain (lean) on Yahawah, the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel), in truth.
A shaar (remnant) will shawab (turn back / repent), even the shaar (remnant) of Yaiqab, to the gabawar (mighty) Al.

For though your im (people), Yasharaal (Israel), are like the sand of the yam (sea), only a shaar (remnant) of them will shawab (turn back / repent). A destruction is determined, overflowing with tzadaqah (righteousness).
For the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), will ishah (make) a full end, and that determined, in the qarab (midst) of all the aratz (earth).

Therefore the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), amar (says) "My im (people) who yashab (dwell) in Tzayawan, don't be yaraa (afraid) of the Ashawar (Assyrian), though he strike you with the shabat (rod), and nashaa (lift) up his matah (staff) against you, as Matzarayam did.
For yet a very Mait while, and the indignation against you will be accomplished, and my ap (anger) will be directed to his destruction.

Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) will stir up a scourge against him, as in the makah (slaughter) of Madayan at the tzawar (rock) of Irab. His matah (rod) will be over the yam (sea), and he will nashaa (lift) it up like he did against Matzarayam.

It will happen in that yawam (day), that his burden will sawar (depart) from off your shoulder, and his yoke from off your neck, and the yoke shall be destroyed panayam (because) of the anointing shaman (oil).
He has bawaa (come) Iy Aiath. He has passed through Magarawan. At Makamas he stores his baggage.
They have gone over the pass. They have taken up their lodging at Gabai. Ramah trembles. Gabaih of Shaawal has fled.
qawal (cry) aloud with your qawal (voice), bath (daughter) of Galayam! Listen, Laishah! You Inay Inathawath!
Madamanah is a fugitive. The yashab (inhabitants) of Gabayam flee for safety.
This very yawam (day) he will halt at Nab. He shakes his yad (hand) at the har (mountain) of the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan, the Gabaih of Yarawashalam.
Behold, the Adawan, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), will lop the boughs with terror. The tall will be cut down, and the Gabah will be brought low.
He will naqap (cut) down the thickets of the Yair with barazal (iron), and Labanawan will napal (fall) by the adayar (mighty) One.
A shoot will yatzaa (come) out of the stock of Yashay, and a branch out of his roots will bear fruit.

The rawach (spirit) of Yahawah will nawach (rest) on him: the rawach (spirit) of chakamah (wisdom) and understanding, the rawach (spirit) of itzah (counsel) and might, the rawach (spirit) of daith (knowledge) and of the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah.
His delight will be in the yaraah (fear) of Yahawah. He will not shapat (judge) by the sight of his maraah (eyes), neither decide by the hearing of his ears;

but with tzadaq (righteousness) he will shapat (judge) the Dal, and decide with mayashawar (equity) for the Inaw of the aratz (earth). He will strike the aratz (earth) with the shabat (rod) of his pah (mouth); and with the rawach (breath) of his shapah (lips) he will mawath (kill) the rashai (wicked).
tzadaq (righteousness) will be the belt of his waist, and amawanah (faithfulness) the belt of his waist.

The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will rabatz (lie) down with the young goat; The calf, the young kapayar (lion), and the fattened calf together; and a qatan (little) nair (child) will lead them.
The cow and the bear will graze. Their yalad (young) ones will rabatz (lie) down together. The aray (lion) will akal (eat) straw like the ox.
The nursing child will play near a cobra's hole, and the weaned child will put his yad (hand) on the viper's den.

They will not raii (hurt) nor shachath (destroy) in all my qadash (holy) har (mountain); for the aratz (earth) will be malaa (full) of the daih (knowledge) of Yahawah, as the mayam (waters) cover the yam (sea).
It will happen in that yawam (day) that the gawayam (nations) will seek the root of Yashay, who imad (stands) as a nas (banner) of the im (peoples); and his resting place will be kabawad (glorious).

It will happen in that yawam (day) that the Adanay will set his yad (hand) again the shanay (second) time to qanah (recover) the shaar (remnant) that is shaar (left) of his im (people) from Ashawar, from Matzarayam, from Patharawas, from Kawash, from Iyalam, from Shanair, from Chamath, and from the islands of the yam (sea).

He will nashaa (set) up a nas (banner) for the gawayam (nations), and will asap (assemble) the outcasts of Yasharaal (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahawadah (Judah) from the arabai (four) corners of the aratz (earth).

The envy also of Aparayam will sawar (depart), and those who persecute Yahawadah (Judah) will be karath (cut) off. Aparayam won't envy Yahawadah (Judah), and Yahawadah (Judah) won't persecute Aparayam.

They will fly down on the shoulders of the Palashathay (Philistines) on the yam (west). Together they will plunder the children of the qadam (east). They will extend their yad (power) over Adam and Mawaab, and the children of Imawan will obey them.

Yahawah will utterly charam (destroy) the lashawan (tongue) of the Matzarayam (Egyptian) yam (sea); and with his scorching rawach (wind) he will wave his yad (hand) over the nahar (river), and will split it into shabai (seven) nachal (streams), and cause men to march over in sandals.

There will be a masalah (highway) for the shaar (remnant) that is shaar (left) of his im (people) from Ashawar, like there was for Yasharaal (Israel) in the yawam (day) that he came up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.

In that yawam (day) you will amar (say), "I will give yadah (thanks) to you, Yahawah; for though you were angry with me, your ap (anger) has turned shawab (turn back / repent) and you nacham (comfort) me.
Behold, Al is my yashawaih (salvation). I will batach (trust), and will not be pachad (afraid); for Yah, Yahawah, is my iz (strength) and song; and he has become my yashawaih (salvation).
Therefore with joy you will shaab (draw) mayam (water) out of the wells of yashawaih (salvation).

In that yawam (day) you will amar (say), "Give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah! qaraa (call) on his sham (name). yadai (declare) his ilayalah (doings) among the im (peoples). Proclaim that his sham (name) is exalted!
zamar (sing) to Yahawah, for he has done excellent things! Let this be yadai (known) in all the aratz (earth)!
Cry aloud and shout, you yashab (inhabitant) of Tzayawan; for the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel) is gadawal (great) in the qarab (midst) of you!
The mashaa (burden) of Babal, which Yashaiyah the ban (son) of Amawatz saw:
nashaa (set) up a nas (banner) on the bare har (mountain)! Lift up your qawal (voice) to them! Wave your yad (hand), that they may bawaa (go) into the gates of the nadayab (nobles).
I have tzawah (commanded) my consecrated ones; yes, I have called my gabawar (mighty) men for my ap (anger), even my proudly Ilayaz ones.

The qawal (noise) of a multitude is in the har (mountains), as of a rab (great) im (people); the qawal (noise) of an uproar of the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the gawayam (nations) gathered asap (together)! Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) is mustering the tzabaa (army) for the battle.
They bawaa (come) from a far aratz (country), from the uttermost part of shamayam (heaven), even Yahawah, and the weapons of his indignation, to chabal (destroy) the whole aratz (land).
Wail; for the yawam (day) of Yahawah is at qarawab (hand)! It will bawaa (come) as destruction from the Shaday.
Therefore all yad (hands) will be rapah (feeble), and everyone's labab (heart) will melt.

They will be dismayed. tzayar (pangs) and sorrows will seize them. They will be in chawal (pain) like a yalad (woman) in labor. They will look in amazement one at rai (another). Their panayam (faces) will be panayam (faces) of flame.

Behold, the yawam (day) of Yahawah bawaa (comes), Akazaray, with ibarah (wrath) and charawan (fierce) ap (anger); to shawam (make) the aratz (land) a desolation, and to destroy its chataa (sinners) out of it.

For the kawakab (stars) of the sky and its Kasayal will not halal (give) their awar (light). The shamash (sun) will be darkened in its yatzaa (going) forth, and the yarach (moon) will not cause its awar (light) to shine.

I will paqad (punish) the world for their rai (evil), and the rashai (wicked) for their iwan (iniquity). I will cause the arrogance of the Zad to shabath (cease), and will humble the haughtiness of the irayatz (terrible).
I will make anawash (people) more rare than fine gold, even a adam (person) than the pure gold of Awapayar.

Therefore I will make the shamayam (heavens) tremble, and the aratz (earth) will be shaken out of its place in the ibarah (wrath) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), and in the yawam (day) of his charawan (fierce) ap (anger).
It will happen that like a hunted gazelle, and like sheep that no one gathers, they will each panah (turn) to their own im (people), and will ayash (each) flee to their own aratz (land).
Everyone who is found will be thrust through. Everyone who is captured will napal (fall) by the charab (sword).
Their infants also will be dashed in pieces before their iyan (eyes). Their bayath (houses) will be ransacked, and their wives raped.
Behold, I will stir up the Maday against them, who will not value kasap (silver), and as for gold, they will not delight in it.
Their qashath (bows) will dash the nair (young) men in pieces; and they shall have no racham (pity) on the fruit of the womb. Their iyan (eyes) will not spare children.
Babal, the glory of mamalakah (kingdoms), the thapaarah (beauty) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans)' pride, will be like when Alahayam overthrew Sadam and Imarah.

It will never be inhabited, neither will it be lived in from dawar (generation) to dawar (generation). The Irabay (Arabian) will not pitch a ahal (tent) there, neither will raih (shepherds) rabatz (make) their flocks lie down there.
But tzayay (wild) animals of the desert will rabatz (lie) there, and their bayath (houses) will be malaa (full) of jackals. Ostriches will shakan (dwell) there, and wild Shaiyar will frolic there.
Wolves will cry in their castles, and jackals in the pleasant hayakal (palaces). Her ith (time) is qarawab (near) to bawaa (come), and her yawam (days) will not be prolonged.

For Yahawah will have racham (compassion) on Yaiqab, and will yet choose Yasharaal (Israel), and yanach (set) them in their own adamah (land). The foreigner will join himself with them, and they will unite with the bayath (house) of Yaiqab.

The im (peoples) will take them, and bawaa (bring) them to their place. The bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) will nachal (possess) them in yahawah (yahweh's) adamah (land) for ibad (servants) and for handmaids. They will take as captives those whose captives they were; and they shall radah (rule) over their oppressors.
It will happen in the yawam (day) that Yahawah will give you nawach (rest) from your itzab (sorrow), from your trouble, and from the Qashah ibadah (service) in which you were made to ibad (serve),
that you will nashaa (take) up this parable against the malak (king) of Babal, and amar (say), "How the oppressor has ceased! The golden city has ceased!
Yahawah has shabar (broken) the matah (staff) of the rashai (wicked), the scepter of the rulers,
who struck the im (peoples) in ibarah (wrath) with a balathay (continual) makah (stroke), who ruled the gawayam (nations) in ap (anger), with a persecution that none restrained.
The whole aratz (earth) is at nawach (rest), and is shaqat (quiet). They break out song.
Yes, the fir trees Shamach with you, with the cedars of Labanawan, saying, "Since you are humbled, no lumberjack has ilah (come) up against us.

shaawal (sheol) from beneath has moved for you to qaraah (meet) you at your coming. It stirs up the rapaa (dead) for you, even all the ithawad (rulers) of the aratz (earth). It has raised up from their kasaa (thrones) all the malak (kings) of the gawayam (nations).
They all will answer and ask you, "Have you also become as chalah (weak) as we are? Have you become like us?
Your pomp is brought down to shaawal (sheol), with the sound of your stringed instruments. Maggots are spread out under you, and worms cover you.
How you have fallen from shamayam (heaven), morning hayalal (star), ban (son) of the dawn! How you are cut down to the aratz (ground), who laid the gawayam (nations) low!

You said in your labab (heart), "I will ilah (ascend) into shamayam (heaven)! I will exalt my kasaa (throne) above the kawakab (stars) of Al! I will yashab (sit) on the har (mountain) of mawaid (assembly), in the far tzapawan (north)!
I will ilah (ascend) above the bamah (heights) of the clouds! I will make myself like the Most Ilayawan!
Yet you shall be brought down to shaawal (sheol), to the depths of the bawar (pit).
Those who raah (see) you will stare at you. They will ponder you, saying, "Is this the ayash (man) who made the aratz (earth) to tremble, who shook mamalakah (kingdoms);
who made the world like a madabar (wilderness), and overthrew its Iyar; who didn't release his prisoners to their bayath (home)?
All the malak (kings) of the gawayam (nations), sleep in kabawad (glory), everyone in his own bayath (house).

But you are cast away from your tomb like an abominable branch, clothed with the slain, who are thrust through with the charab (sword), who yarad (go) down to the aban (stones) of the bawar (pit); like a pagar (dead) body trodden under bawas (foot).
You will not join them in qabawarah (burial), because you have destroyed your aratz (land). You have killed your im (people). The zarai (seed) of evildoers will not be named iwalam (forever).

kawan (prepare) for slaughter of his children because of the iwan (iniquity) of their abawath (fathers), that they not qawam (rise) up and yarash (possess) the aratz (earth), and malaa (fill) the surface of the world with cities.
"I will qawam (rise) up against them," says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "and karath (cut) off from Babal sham (name) and shaar (remnant), and nayan (son) and nakad (son's) son," says Yahawah.
"I will also shawam (make) it a mawarash (possession) for the porcupine, and pools of mayam (water). I will sweep it with the broom of destruction," says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) has sworn, saying, "Surely, as I have thought, so shall it happen; and as I have purposed, so shall it qawam (stand):

that I will shabar (break) the Ashawar (Assyrian) in my aratz (land), and tread him under bawas (foot) on my har (mountains). Then his yoke will sawar (leave) them, and his burden sawar (leave) their shoulders.
This is the plan that is determined for the whole aratz (earth). This is the yad (hand) that is stretched out over all the gawayam (nations).
For Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) has planned, and who can stop it? His yad (hand) is stretched out, and who can shawab (turn back / repent) it back?
This mashaa (burden) was in the Shanah that malak (king) Achaz mawath (died).

Don't Shamach, O Palashath, all of you, because the shabat (rod) that struck you is shabar (broken); for out of the serpent's root an adder will emerge, and his fruit will be a sharap (fiery) flying serpent.
The firstborn of the Dal will raih (eat), and the Abayawan will rabatz (lie) down in safety; and I will mawath (kill) your root with famine, and your shaarayath (remnant) will be killed.
Howl, gate! Cry, Iyar! You are melted away, Palashath, all of you; for ishan (smoke) bawaa (comes) out of the tzapawan (north), and there is no straggler in his ranks.
What will they answer the malaak (messengers) of the gaway (nation)? That Yahawah has founded Tzayawan, and in her the Inay of his im (people) will take refuge.

The mashaa (burden) of Mawaab: for in a layal (night), Ir of Mawaab is laid shadad (waste), and damah (brought) to nothing; for in a layal (night) Qayar of Mawaab is laid shadad (waste), and damah (brought) to nothing.
They have gone up to Bayith, and to Dayabawan, to the bamah (high) places, to weep. Mawaab wails over Nabaw and over Mayadabaa. Baldness is on all of their raash (heads). Every beard is cut off.
In their streets, they clothe themselves in sackcloth. In their streets and on their housetops, everyone wails, weeping yarad (abundantly).
Chashabawan cries out with Alailaa. Their qawal (voice) is heard even to Yahatz. Therefore the chalatz (armed) men of Mawaab rawai (cry) aloud. Their napash (souls) tremble within them.

My lab (heart) cries out for Mawaab! Her nobles flee to Tzair, Igalah Eglath Shelishiyah; for they go up by the ascent of Lawachayath with weeping; for in the darak (way) of Charanayam, they ilah (raise) up a cry of destruction.
For the mayam (waters) of Namarayam will be desolate; for the grass has withered away, the tender grass kalah (fails), there is no green thing.
Therefore they will carry away the abundance they have gotten, and that which they have stored up, over the nachal (brook) of the willows.
For the cry has gone around the borders of Mawaab; its wailing to Agalayam, and its wailing to Baaraalayam Elim.

For the mayam (waters) of Dayamawan are malaa (full) of dam (blood); for I will shayath (bring) yet more on Dayamawan, a aray (lion) on those of Mawaab who palayatah (escape), and on the shaarayath (remnant) of the adamah (land).
shalach (send) the lambs for the ruler of the aratz (land) from salai (selah) to the madabar (wilderness), to the har (mountain) of the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan.
For it will be that as wandering birds, as a scattered nest, so will the bath (daughters) of Mawaab be at the fords of the Aranawan.
Give itzah (counsel)! ishah (execute) justice! shayath (make) your shade like the layal (night) in the midst of the noonday! Hide the outcasts! Don't betray the fugitive!

Let my outcasts gawar (dwell) with you! As for Mawaab, be a hiding place for him from the panayam (face) of the shadad (destroyer). For the extortioner is apas (brought) to nothing. Destruction kalah (ceases). The oppressors are consumed out of the aratz (land).

A kasaa (throne) will be established in loving chasad (kindness). One will yashab (sit) on it in truth, in the ahal (tent) of Dawad, judging, seeking justice, and Mahayar to do tzadaq (righteousness).
We have heard of the pride of Mawaab, that he is very Gaa; even of his arrogance, his pride, and his ibarah (wrath). His boastings are nothing.
Therefore Mawaab will wail for Mawaab. Everyone will wail. You will mourn for the raisin cakes of Qayaracharash Hareseth, utterly Nakaa.

For the fields of Chashabawan languish with the vine of Shabam. The bail (lords) of the gawayam (nations) have broken down Sharawaq choice branches, which reached even to Yaizayar, which wandered into the madabar (wilderness). Its shoots were spread abroad. They passed over the yam (sea).

Therefore I will weep with the weeping of Yaizayar for the vine of Shabam. I will rawah (water) you with my tears, Chashabawan, and Alailaa: for on your qayatz (summer) fruits and on your harvest the battle shout has fallen.

Gladness is taken asap (away), and joy out of the fruitful field; and in the vineyards there will be no singing, neither rawai (joyful) noise. Nobody will tread out yayan (wine) in the presses. I have made the shouting stop.
Therefore my maih (heart) sounds like a harp for Mawaab, and my qarab (inward) parts for Qayaracharash Heres.
It will happen that when Mawaab raah (see) himself, when he wearies himself on the bamah (high) place, and bawaa (comes) to his maqadash (sanctuary) to palal (pray), that he will not yakal (prevail).
This is the dabar (word) that Yahawah spoke concerning Mawaab in time past.

But now Yahawah has spoken, saying, "Within shalawash (three) Shanah, as a worker bound by contract would Shanah them, the kabawad (glory) of Mawaab shall be brought into contempt, with all his rab (great) multitude; and the shaar (remnant) will be Mait small and feeble.
The mashaa (burden) of Damashaq: "Behold, Damashaq is taken sawar (away) from being a Iyar, and it will be a ruinous heap.
The Iyar of Irawair are forsaken. They will be for flocks, which shall rabatz (lie) down, and none shall make them afraid.

The fortress shall shabath (cease) from Aparayam, and the mamalakah (kingdom) from Damashaq, and the shaar (remnant) of Aram. They will be as the kabawad (glory) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel)," says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
"It will happen in that yawam (day) that the kabawad (glory) of Yaiqab will be made thin, and the fatness of his flesh will become lean.
It will be like when the harvester asap (gathers) the wheat, and his zarawai (arm) reaps the grain. Yes, it will be like when laqat (one) gleans grain in the valley of Rapaa (Rephaim).

Yet gleanings will be shaar (left) there, like the shaking of an olive tree, shanayam (two) or shalawash (three) olives in the raash (top) of the uppermost bough, arabai (four) or chamash (five) in the outermost branches of a fruitful tree," says Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
In that yawam (day), people will shaih (look) to their Maker, and their iyan (eyes) will have raah (see) for the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).

They will not shaih (look) to the mazabach (altars), the maishah (work) of their yad (hands); neither shall they raah (see) that which their fingers have made, Asharah the Asherim, or the incense altars.

In that yawam (day), their maiwaz (strong) Iyar will be like the forsaken Charash in the woods and on the mountain top, which were forsaken from before the children of Yasharaal (Israel); and it will be a desolation.

For you have forgotten the Alahayam of your yashai (salvation), and have not zakar (remembered) the tzawar (rock) of your maiwaz (strength). Therefore you plant pleasant plants, and zarai (set) out foreign seedlings.
In the yawam (day) of your planting, you hedge it in. In the baqar (morning), you make your zarai (seed) blossom, but the harvest flees away in the yawam (day) of chalah (grief) and of Anash sorrow.
Ah, the uproar of many im (peoples), who roar like the roaring of the yam (seas); and the rushing of laam (nations), that rush like the rushing of kabayar (mighty) mayam (waters)!

The laam (nations) will rush like the rushing of many mayam (waters): but he will rebuke them, and they will flee far off, and will be chased like the chaff of the har (mountains) panayam (before) the rawach (wind), and like the whirling dust panayam (before) the sawapah (storm).
At ith (evening), behold, terror! Before the baqar (morning), they are no more. This is the chalaq (portion) of those who plunder us, and the lot of those who rob us.
Ah, the aratz (land) of the rustling of wings, which is ibar (beyond) the nahar (rivers) of Kawash;

that shalach (sends) tzayar (ambassadors) by the yam (sea), even in vessels of papyrus on the mayam (waters), saying, "yalak (go), you qal (swift) malaak (messengers), to a gaway (nation) tall and smooth, to a im (people) awesome from their beginning onward, a gaway (nation) that measures out and treads down, whose aratz (land) the nahar (rivers) divide!
All you yashab (inhabitants) of the world, and you shakan (dwellers) on the aratz (earth), when a nas (banner) is lifted up on the har (mountains), raah (see)! When the trumpet is blown, listen!
For Yahawah said to me, "I will be still, and I will see in my dwelling place, like Tzach heat in sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.

For panayam (before) the harvest, when the blossom is over, and the flower becomes a ripening grape, he will karath (cut) off the sprigs with pruning hooks, and he will cut down and sawar (take) away the spreading branches.

They will be left together for the ravenous birds of the har (mountains), and for the animals of the aratz (earth). The ravenous birds will summer on them, and all the animals of the aratz (earth) will winter on them.

In that ith (time), a present will be brought to Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) from a im (people) tall and smooth, even from a im (people) awesome from their beginning onward, a gaway (nation) that measures out and treads down, whose aratz (land) the nahar (rivers) divide, to the place of the sham (name) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), har (mount) Tzayawan.

The mashaa (burden) of Matzarayam: "Behold, Yahawah rides on a qal (swift) cloud, and bawaa (comes) to Matzarayam. The idols of Matzarayam will tremble at his panayam (presence); and the labab (heart) of Matzarayam will melt in its qarab (midst).

I will stir up the Matzarayam (Egyptians) against the Matzarayam (Egyptians), and they will fight everyone against his ach (brother), and everyone against his neighbor; Iyar against Iyar, and mamalakah (kingdom) against mamalakah (kingdom).

The rawach (spirit) of Matzarayam will fail in its qarab (midst). I will balai (destroy) its itzah (counsel). They will seek the idols, the charmers, those who have familiar awab (spirits), and the wizards.
I will give over the Matzarayam (Egyptians) into the yad (hand) of a Qashah Adawan. A iz (fierce) malak (king) will mashal (rule) over them," says the Adawan, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
The mayam (waters) will fail from the yam (sea), and the nahar (river) will be wasted and become yabash (dry).
The nahar (rivers) will become foul. The yaar (streams) Matzawar Egypt will be diminished and dried up. The reeds and flags will wither away.
The meadows by the Nile, by the brink of the Nile, and all the sown fields of the Nile, will become yabash (dry), be driven away, and be no more.
The fishermen will lament, and all those who fish in the Nile will mourn, and those who spread nets on the mayam (waters) will languish.
Moreover those who ibad (work) Sharayaqah combed flax, and those who weave white cloth, will be confounded.
The pillars will be broken in pieces. All those who ishah (work) for hire will be Agam in napash (soul).

The shar (princes) of Tzain are utterly Awayal. The itzah (counsel) of the wisest yaitz (counselors) of Paraih has become stupid. How do you amar (say) to Paraih, "I am the ban (son) of the chakam (wise), the ban (son) of qadam (ancient) malak (kings)?
Where then are your chakam (wise) men? Let them nagad (tell) you now; and let them yadai (know) what Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) has purposed concerning Matzarayam.
The shar (princes) of Tzain have become fools. The shar (princes) Nap Memphis are deceived. They have caused Matzarayam to thaih (go) astray, who are the cornerstone of her shabat (tribes).

Yahawah has mixed a rawach (spirit) of perverseness in the qarab (midst) of her; and they have caused Matzarayam to thaih (go) astray in all of its maishah (works), like a drunken man thaih (staggers) in his vomit.
Neither shall there be any maishah (work) for Matzarayam, which raash (head) or tail, palm branch or rush, may do.

In that yawam (day) the Matzarayam (Egyptians) will be like women. They will tremble and pachad (fear) panayam (because) of the thanawapah (shaking) of the yad (hand) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), which he shakes over them.

The adamah (land) of Yahawadah (Judah) will become a terror to Matzarayam. Everyone to whom zakar (mention) is made of it will be pachad (afraid), panayam (because) of the plans of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), which he yaitz (determines) against it.

In that yawam (day), there will be chamash (five) Iyar in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam that dabar (speak) the shapah (language) of Kanain, and shabai (swear) to Yahawah of tzabaa (armies). One will be called "The Iyar of destruction.
In that yawam (day), there will be an mazabach (altar) to Yahawah in the midst of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and a matzabah (pillar) to Yahawah at its border.

It will be for a awath (sign) and for a witness to Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam; for they will cry to Yahawah panayam (because) of lachatz (oppressors), and he will shalach (send) them a savior and a defender, and he will natzal (deliver) them.

Yahawah will be yadai (known) to Matzarayam, and the Matzarayam (Egyptians) will yadai (know) Yahawah in that yawam (day). Yes, they will worship with zabach (sacrifice) and manachah (offering), and will nadar (vow) a nadar (vow) to Yahawah, and will shalam (perform) it.
Yahawah will nagap (strike) Matzarayam, striking and healing. They will shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah, and he will be entreated by them, and will heal them.

In that yawam (day) there will be a masalah (highway) out of Matzarayam to Ashawar, and the Ashawar (Assyrian) shall bawaa (come) into Matzarayam, and the Matzarayam (Egyptian) into Ashawar; and the Matzarayam (Egyptians) will worship with the Ashawar (Assyrians).
In that yawam (day), Yasharaal (Israel) will be the shalayashay (third) with Matzarayam and with Ashawar, a barakah (blessing) in the qarab (midst) of the aratz (earth);
because Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) has blessed them, saying, "Blessed be Matzarayam my im (people), Ashawar the maishah (work) of my yad (hands), and Yasharaal (Israel) my nachalah (inheritance).
In the Shanah that Tharathan came Ashadawad Ashdod, when Saragawan the malak (king) of Ashawar sent him, and he fought Ashadawad Ashdod and took it;

at that ith (time) Yahawah spoke by Yashaiyah the ban (son) of Amawatz, saying, "yalak (go), and loosen the sackcloth from off your waist, and take your shoes from off your feet." He did so, walking Irawam and Yachap.
Yahawah said, "As my ibad (servant) Yashaiyah has walked Irawam and Yachap shalawash (three) Shanah for a awath (sign) and a mawapath (wonder) concerning Matzarayam and concerning Kawash,

so the malak (king) of Ashawar will lead away the Shabay of Matzarayam and the exiles of Kawash, nair (young) and zaqan (old), Irawam and Yachap, and with buttocks uncovered, to the irawah (shame) of Matzarayam.
They will be dismayed and confounded, because of Kawash their expectation, and of Matzarayam their glory.

The yashab (inhabitants) of this coast ay (land) will amar (say) in that yawam (day), ‘Behold, this is our expectation, where we fled for help to be delivered from the malak (king) of Ashawar. And we, how will we malat (escape)?'
The mashaa (burden) of the madabar (wilderness) of the yam (sea). As sawapah (whirlwinds) in the Nagab sweep through, it bawaa (comes) from the madabar (wilderness), from an awesome aratz (land).

A Qashah vision is declared to me. The treacherous bagad (man) bagad (deals) treacherously, and the shadad (destroyer) shadad (destroys). ilah (go) up, Iyalam; attack! I have stopped all of Maday sighing.

Therefore my thighs are filled with anguish. Pains have taken achaz (hold) on me, like the tzayar (pains) of a yalad (woman) in labor. I am in so much pain that I can't hear. I so am dismayed that I can't raah (see).
My labab (heart) flutters. Horror has frightened me. The nashap (twilight) that I desired has been turned into charadah (trembling) for me.
They prepare the table. They set the watch. They akal (eat). They drink. qawam (rise) up, you shar (princes), oil the magan (shield)!
For the Adanay said to me, "yalak (go), imad (set) a watchman. Let him nagad (declare) what he raah (see).
When he raah (see) a troop, horsemen in pairs, a troop of donkeys, a troop of camels, he shall listen diligently with rab (great) attentiveness.
He cried like a aray (lion): "Adanay, I imad (stand) continually on the watchtower in the yawamam (daytime), and every layal (night) I stay at my post.
Behold, here bawaa (comes) a troop of men, horsemen in pairs." He answered, "Fallen, fallen is Babal; and all the engraved pasayal (images) of her Alahayam are shabar (broken) to the aratz (ground).
You are my threshing, and the grain of my floor!" That which I have heard from Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), I have declared to you.
The mashaa (burden) of Dawamah. One qaraa (calls) to me out of Shaiyar, "shamar (watchman), what of the layal (night)? shamar (watchman), what of the layal (night)?
The shamar (watchman) said, "The baqar (morning) comes, and also the layal (night). If you will inquire, inquire. Come shawab (turn back / repent) again.
The mashaa (burden) on Irab. In the Yair in Irab you will lawan (lodge), you caravans Dadanayam Dedanites.
They brought mayam (water) to him who was Tzamaa. The yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land) of Thayamaa met the fugitives with their lacham (bread).
For they fled away from the charab (swords), from the drawn charab (sword), from the bent qashath (bow), and from the heat of battle.
For the Adanay said to me, "Within a Shanah, as a worker bound by contract would Shanah it, all the kabawad (glory) of Qadar will kalah (fail),
and the shaar (residue) of the number of the qashath (archers), the gabawar (mighty) men of the children of Qadar, will be few; for Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), has spoken it.
The mashaa (burden) of the Gayaa of vision. What ails you now, that you have all gone up to the housetops?
You that are Malaa of shouting, a tumultuous Iyar, a Ilayaz town; your Chalal are not Chalal with the charab (sword), neither are they mawath (dead) in battle.
All your qatzayan (rulers) fled away together. They were bound by the qashath (archers). All who were found by you were bound together. They fled Rachawaq away.
Therefore I said, "shaih (look) away from me. I will weep bitterly. Don't awatz (labor) to nacham (comfort) me for the destruction of the bath (daughter) of my im (people).

For it is a yawam (day) of mahawamah (confusion), and of treading down, and of perplexity, from the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), in the Gayaa of vision; a breaking down of the walls, and a crying to the har (mountains).
Iyalam carried his quiver, with chariots of men and horsemen; and Qayar uncovered the magan (shield).
It happened that your choicest valleys were malaa (full) of chariots, and the horsemen shayath (set) themselves in shayath (array) at the gate.
He took away the covering of Yahawadah (Judah); and you looked in that yawam (day) to the armor in the bayath (house) of the Yair.
You saw the breaches of the Iyar of Dawad, that they were many; and you gathered together the mayam (waters) of the Thachathawan pool.
You numbered the bayath (houses) of Yarawashalam, and you broke down the bayath (houses) to batzar (fortify) the wall.

You also made a reservoir between the chawamah (two) walls for the mayam (water) of the Yashan pool. But you didn't look to him who had done this, neither did you have raah (see) for him who purposed it Rachawaq ago.
In that yawam (day), the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), called to weeping, and to mourning, and to baldness, and to dressing in sackcloth:
and behold, joy and gladness, killing cattle and killing sheep, eating flesh and drinking yayan (wine): "Let us akal (eat) and drink, for tomorrow we will mawath (die).
Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) revealed himself in my ears, "Surely this iwan (iniquity) will not be forgiven you until you mawath (die)," amar (says) the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
Thus amar (says) the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "yalak (go), bawaa (get) yourself to this treasurer, even to Shabanaa, who is over the bayath (house), and say,
‘What are you doing here? Who has you here, that you have dug out a tomb here?' Cutting himself out a tomb on high, chiseling a mashakan (habitation) for himself in the salai (rock)!
Behold, Yahawah will overcome you and hurl you away violently. Yes, he will grasp you firmly.

He will tzanap (surely) wind you around and around, and throw you like a dawar (ball) into a Rachab aratz (country). There you will mawath (die), and there the chariots of your kabawad (glory) will be, you qalawan (shame) of your adawan (lord's) bayath (house).
I will thrust you from your office. You will be pulled down from your station.
It will happen in that yawam (day) that I will qaraa (call) my ibad (servant) Alayaqayam the ban (son) Chalaqayah Hilkiah,

and I will Labash him with your robe, and chazaq (strengthen) him with your belt. I will nathan (commit) your mamashalah (government) into his yad (hand); and he will be a ab (father) to the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, and to the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah).
I will nathan (lay) the key of the bayath (house) of Dawad on his shoulder. He will pathach (open), and no sagar (one) will shut. He will shut, and no one will pathach (open).
I will fasten him like a nail in a aman (sure) place. He will be for a kasaa (throne) of kabawad (glory) to his ab (father's) bayath (house).
They will hang on him all the kabawad (glory) of his ab (father's) bayath (house), the tzaatzaa (offspring) and the issue, every qatan (small) vessel, from the cups even to all the pitchers.
