"In that yawam (day)," says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "the nail that was fastened in a aman (sure) place will give way. It will be cut down, and napal (fall). The mashaa (burden) that was on it will be karath (cut) off, for Yahawah has spoken it.

The mashaa (burden) of Tzar. Howl, you ships of Tharashayash! For it is laid shadad (waste), so that there is no bayath (house), no entering in. From the aratz (land) of Kathay (Kittim) it is revealed to them.
Be still, you yashab (inhabitants) of the coast, you whom the merchants of Tzayadawan, that ibar (pass) over the yam (sea), have replenished.
On rab (great) mayam (waters), the zarai (seed) of the Shayachawar, the harvest of the Nile, was her revenue. She was the market of gawayam (nations).

Be bawash (ashamed), Tzayadawan; for the yam (sea) has spoken, the stronghold of the yam (sea), saying, "I have not travailed, nor brought yalad (forth), neither have I nourished young men, nor brought up virgins.
When the report comes to Matzarayam, they will be in anguish at the report of Tzar.
ibar (pass) over to Tharashayash! Wail, you yashab (inhabitants) of the coast!
Is this your Ilayaz city, whose antiquity is of qadam (ancient) yawam (days), whose feet carried her Rachawaq away to travel?
Who has planned this against Tzar, the giver of itar (crowns), whose merchants are shar (princes), whose Kanain are the honorable of the aratz (earth)?
Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) has planned it, to chalal (stain) the pride of all glory, to qalal (bring) into contempt all the honorable of the aratz (earth).
ibar (pass) through your aratz (land) like the Nile, bath (daughter) of Tharashayash. There is no restraint any more.
He has stretched out his yad (hand) over the yam (sea). He has shaken the mamalakah (kingdoms). Yahawah has ordered the destruction of Kanain strongholds.
He said, "You shall rejoice no more, you oppressed virgin bath (daughter) of Tzayadawan. qawam (arise), ibar (pass) over to Kathay (Kittim). Even there you will have no nawach (rest).

Behold, the aratz (land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans). This im (people) was not. The Ashawar (Assyrians) founded it for those who dwell in the tzayay (wilderness). They qawam (set) up their towers. They overthrew its palaces. They made it a ruin.
Howl, you ships of Tharashayash, for your stronghold is laid shadad (waste)!

It will come to pass in that yawam (day) that Tzar will be forgotten shabaiyam (seventy) Shanah, according to the yawam (days) of one malak (king). After the end of shabaiyam (seventy) Shanah it will be to Tzar like in the song of the prostitute.
Take a harp; sabab (go) about the Iyar, you prostitute that has been forgotten. yatab (make) sweet melody. Sing many songs, that you may be zakar (remembered).

It will happen after the end of shabaiyam (seventy) Shanah that Yahawah will paqad (visit) Tzar, and she shall shawab (turn back / repent) to her wages, and will play the prostitute with all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (world) on the surface of the adamah (earth).

Her merchandise and her wages will be qadash (holiness) to Yahawah. It will not be treasured nor laid up; for her merchandise will be for those who yashab (dwell) panayam (before) Yahawah, to akal (eat) sufficiently, and for Ithayaq clothing.
Behold, Yahawah makes the aratz (earth) empty, makes it waste, iwah (turns) it panayam (upside) down, and scatters its yashab (inhabitants).

It will be as with the im (people), so with the kahan (priest); as with the ibad (servant), so with his adawan (master); as with the shapachah (maid), so with her mistress; as with the qanah (buyer), so with the seller; as with the creditor, so with the debtor; as with the taker of interest, so with the giver of interest.
The aratz (earth) will be utterly emptied and utterly laid waste; for Yahawah has spoken this dabar (word).
The aratz (earth) mourns and fades away. The world languishes and fades away. The lofty im (people) of the aratz (earth) languish.

The aratz (earth) also is polluted under its yashab (inhabitants), because they have transgressed the thawarah (laws), violated the chaq (statutes), and broken the iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant).

Therefore the alah (curse) has devoured the aratz (earth), and those who yashab (dwell) therein are asham (found) guilty. Therefore the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (earth) are burned, and few men shaar (left).
The new thayarawash (wine) mourns. The vine languishes. All the Shamach sigh.
The mirth of tambourines shabath (ceases). The sound of those who Ilayaz chadal (ends). The joy of the harp shabath (ceases).
They will not drink yayan (wine) with a song. shakar (strong) drink will be bitter to those who drink it.
The confused city is shabar (broken) down. Every bayath (house) is shut up, that no man may bawaa (come) in.
There is a crying in the streets because of the yayan (wine). All joy is darkened. The mirth of the aratz (land) is galah (gone).
The Iyar is shaar (left) in desolation, and the gate is struck with destruction.
For it will be so in the qarab (midst) of the aratz (earth) among the im (peoples), as the shaking of an olive tree, as the gleanings when the vintage is kalah (done).
These shall nashaa (lift) up their qawal (voice). They will shout for the majesty of Yahawah. They cry aloud from the yam (sea).
Therefore kabad (glorify) Yahawah in the east, even the sham (name) of Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), in the islands of the yam (sea)!

From the uttermost part of the aratz (earth) have we heard songs. Glory to the tzadayaq (righteous)! But I said, "I pine away! I pine away! woe is me!" The bagad (treacherous) have dealt bagad (treacherously). Yes, the bagad (treacherous) have dealt very bagad (treacherously).
pachad (fear), the pachath (pit), and the snare, are on you who yashab (inhabitant) the aratz (earth).

It will happen that he who flees from the qawal (noise) of the pachad (fear) will napal (fall) into the pachath (pit); and he who ilah (comes) up out of the midst of the pachath (pit) will be taken in the snare; for the windows on high are opened, and the foundations of the aratz (earth) tremble.
The aratz (earth) is utterly broken. The aratz (earth) is torn apart. The aratz (earth) is shaken violently.

The aratz (earth) will stagger like a drunken nawai (man), and will sway back and forth like a hammock. Its disobedience will be kabad (heavy) on it, and it will napal (fall) and not qawam (rise) again.
It shall happen in that yawam (day) that Yahawah will paqad (punish) the tzabaa (army) of the high marawam (ones) on high, and the malak (kings) of the adamah (earth) on the adamah (earth).
They shall be gathered asap (together), as prisoners are gathered in the bawar (pit), and shall be shut up in the prison; and after many yawam (days) shall they be visited.

Then the labanah (moon) shall be chapar (confounded), and the chamah (sun) bawash (ashamed); for Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) will malak (reign) on har (mount) Tzayawan, and in Yarawashalam; and before his zaqan (elders) will be kabawad (glory).

Yahawah, you are my Alahayam. I will exalt you! I will yadah (praise) your sham (name), for you have done wonderful things, things planned Rachawaq ago, in complete amawanah (faithfulness) and aman (truth).
For you have made a Iyar into a heap, a fortified city into a ruin, a palace of strangers to be no Iyar. It will never be built.
Therefore a iz (strong) im (people) will kabad (glorify) you. A city of awesome gawayam (nations) will yaraa (fear) you.

For you have been a stronghold to the Dal, a stronghold to the Abayawan in his tzar (distress), a refuge from the storm, a shade from the heat, when the rawach (blast) of the dreaded ones is like a storm against the wall.
As the heat in a dry place will you bring down the noise of strangers; as the heat by the shade of a cloud, the song of the dreaded ones will be brought low.

In this har (mountain), Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) will ishah (make) all im (peoples) a feast of shaman (fat) things, a feast of choice shamar (wines), of shaman (fat) things machah (full) of marrow, of well refined choice shamar (wines).
He will balai (destroy) in this har (mountain) the surface of the covering that covers all im (peoples), and the masakah (veil) that is spread over all gawayam (nations).

He has swallowed up mawath (death) forever! The Adanay Yahawah will machah (wipe) away tears from off all panayam (faces). He will take the reproach of his im (people) sawar (away) from off all the aratz (earth), for Yahawah has spoken it.

It shall be said in that yawam (day), "Behold, this is our Alahayam! We have waited for him, and he will yashai (save) us! This is Yahawah! We have waited for him. We will be glad and Shamach in his yashawaih (salvation)!
For in this har (mountain) the yad (hand) of Yahawah will nawach (rest). Mawaab will be trodden down in his place, even like straw is trodden down in the madamanah (water) of the dunghill.
He will spread out his yad (hands) in its qarab (midst), like shachah (one) who swims spreads out shachah (hands) to swim, but his pride will be humbled together with the craft of his yad (hands).
He has brought the high fortress of your walls down, laid low, and brought to the aratz (ground), even to the ipar (dust).
In that yawam (day), this song will be sung in the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah): "We have a iz (strong) Iyar. Alahayam appoints yashawaih (salvation) for walls and chayal (bulwarks).
pathach (open) the gates, that the tzadayaq (righteous) gaway (nation) may bawaa (enter): the one which shamar (keeps) amawan (faith).
You will keep whoever's yatzar (mind) is steadfast in shalawam (perfect) shalawam (peace), because he batach (trusts) in you.
batach (trust) in Yahawah id (forever); for in Yah, Yahawah, is an iwalam (forever) tzawar (rock).
For he has brought down those who yashab (dwell) on high, the lofty city. He lays it low. He lays it low even to the aratz (ground). He nagai (brings) it even to the ipar (dust).
The ragal (foot) shall tread it down; Even the feet of the Inay, and the paim (steps) of the Dal.
The arach (way) of the tzadayaq (just) is uprightness. You who are yashar (upright) make the maigal (path) of the tzadayaq (righteous) level.
Yes, in the arach (way) of your mashapat (judgments), Yahawah, have we waited for you. Your sham (name) and your renown are the desire of our napash (soul).

With my napash (soul) have I desired you in the layal (night). Yes, with my rawach (spirit) qarab (within) me will I shachar (seek) you earnestly; for when your mashapat (judgments) are in the aratz (earth), the yashab (inhabitants) of the world learn tzadaq (righteousness).
Let favor be shown to the rashai (wicked), yet he will not learn tzadaq (righteousness). In the aratz (land) of Nakachah he will deal wrongfully, and will not raah (see) yahawah (yahweh's) majesty.

Yahawah, your yad (hand) is lifted up, yet they don't chazah (see); but they will chazah (see) your zeal for the im (people), and be disappointed. Yes, ash (fire) will akal (consume) your tzar (adversaries).
Yahawah, you will ordain shalawam (peace) for us, for you have also worked all our maishah (works) for us.
Yahawah our Alahayam, other yahawah (lords) zawalah (besides) you have had bail (dominion) over us, but by you only will we zakar (make) mention of your sham (name).
The mawath (dead) shall not chayah (live). The rapaa (deceased) shall not qawam (rise). Therefore have you visited and destroyed them, and caused all zakar (memory) of them to abad (perish).
You have increased the gaway (nation), O Yahawah. You have increased the gaway (nation)! You are glorified! You have enlarged all the borders of the aratz (land).
Yahawah, in tzar (trouble) they have visited you. They poured out a prayer when your chastening was on them.
Like as a harah (woman) with child, who qarab (draws) near the yalad (time) of her delivery, is in chawal (pain) and cries out in her pangs; so we have been panayam (before) you, Yahawah.

We have been with child. We have been in chawal (pain). We gave yalad (birth), it seems, only to rawach (wind). We have not worked any yashawaih (deliverance) in the aratz (earth); neither have the yashab (inhabitants) of the world fallen.

Your mawath (dead) shall chayah (live). My nabalah (dead) bodies shall qawam (arise). qawatz (awake) and sing, you who shakan (dwell) in the ipar (dust); for your dew is like the dew of awarah (herbs), and the aratz (earth) will napal (cast) forth the rapaa (dead).
yalak (come), my im (people), bawaa (enter) into your rooms, and shut your doors behind you. Hide yourself for a Mait moment, until the indignation is past.

For, behold, Yahawah yatzaa (comes) forth out of his place to paqad (punish) the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (earth) for their iwan (iniquity). The aratz (earth) also will galah (disclose) her dam (blood), and will no longer cover her slain.

In that yawam (day), Yahawah with his Qashah and gadawal (great) and chazaq (strong) charab (sword) will paqad (punish) leviathan, the Barayach serpent, and leviathan the Iqalathawan serpent; and he will harag (kill) the thanayan (dragon) that is in the yam (sea).
In that yawam (day), sing to her, "A pleasant vineyard!
I, Yahawah, am its keeper. I will shaqah (water) it every moment. Lest anyone damage it, I will keep it layal (night) and yawam (day).
chamah (wrath) is not in me, but if I should find briers and thorns, I would do battle! I would march on them and I would tzawath (burn) them together.
Or else let him chazaq (take) hold of my maiwaz (strength), that he may ishah (make) shalawam (peace) with me. Let him ishah (make) shalawam (peace) with me.
In days to bawaa (come), Yaiqab will take root. Yasharaal (Israel) will blossom and bud. They will malaa (fill) the surface of the world with fruit.
Has he struck them as he struck those who struck them? Or are they killed like those who killed them were killed?
In measure, when you shalach (send) them away, you rayab (contend) with them. He has removed them with his Qashah rawach (blast) in the yawam (day) of the east qadayam (wind).

Therefore, by this the iwan (iniquity) of Yaiqab will be forgiven, and this is all the fruit of taking sawar (away) his chataah (sin): that he shawam (makes) all the aban (stones) of the mazabach (altar) as chalk aban (stones) that are beaten in pieces, so that the Asharah and the incense altars shall rise no more.

For the fortified Iyar is badad (solitary), a Nawah deserted and forsaken, like the madabar (wilderness). The calf will raih (feed) there, and there he will rabatz (lie) down, and kalah (consume) its branches.

When its boughs are withered, they will be shabar (broken) off. The women will bawaa (come) and set them on awar (fire), for they are a im (people) of no bayanah (understanding). Therefore he who made them will not have racham (compassion) on them, and he who formed them will show them no favor.

It will happen in that yawam (day), that Yahawah will thresh from the flowing stream of the Euphrates to the nachal (brook) of Matzarayam; and you will be gathered one by one, children of Yasharaal (Israel).

It will happen in that yawam (day) that a gadawal (great) trumpet will be blown; and those who were ready to abad (perish) in the aratz (land) of Ashawar, and those who were outcasts in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, shall bawaa (come); and they will shachah (worship) Yahawah in the qadash (holy) har (mountain) at Yarawashalam.

Woe to the itarah (crown) of pride of the drunkards of Aparayam, and to the fading flower of his tzabay (glorious) thapaarah (beauty), which is on the raash (head) of the fertile Gayaa of those who are overcome with yayan (wine)!

Behold, the Adanay has a chazaq (mighty) and amayatz (strong) one. Like a storm of hail, a destroying storm, and like a storm of kabayar (mighty) mayam (waters) overflowing, he will yanach (cast) them down to the aratz (earth) with his yad (hand).
The itarah (crown) of pride of the drunkards of Aparayam will be trodden under ragal (foot).

The fading flower of his tzabay (glorious) thapaarah (beauty), which is on the raash (head) of the fertile Gayaa, shall be like the first-ripe fig before the qayatz (summer); which someone picks and balai (eats) as soon as he raah (see) it.
In that yawam (day), Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) will become a itarah (crown) of glory, and a diadem of thapaarah (beauty), to the shaar (residue) of his im (people);
and a rawach (spirit) of justice to him who yashab (sits) in mashapat (judgment), and gabawarah (strength) to those who shawab (turn back / repent) back the battle at the gate.

They also reel with yayan (wine), and thaih (stagger) with shakar (strong) drink. The kahan (priest) and the nabayaa (prophet) reel with shakar (strong) drink. They are swallowed up by yayan (wine). They thaih (stagger) with shakar (strong) drink. They shagah (err) in vision. They stumble in palayalayah (judgment).
For all tables are completely malaa (full) of filthy vomit and filthiness.
Whom will he teach daih (knowledge)? To whom will he explain the message? Those who are weaned from the milk, and Ithayaq from the breasts?
For it is tzaw (precept) on tzaw (precept), tzaw (precept) on tzaw (precept); line on line, line on line; here a little, there a little.
But he will dabar (speak) to this im (nation) with Laig shapah (lips) and in achar (another) lashawan (language);
to whom he said, "This is the resting place. Give manawachah (rest) to Iyap;" and "This is the refreshing;" yet they would not hear.

Therefore the dabar (word) of Yahawah will be to them tzaw (precept) on tzaw (precept), tzaw (precept) on tzaw (precept); line on line, line on line; here a little, there a little; that they may yalak (go), fall backward, be shabar (broken), be snared, and be taken.
Therefore hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah, you latzawan (scoffers), that mashal (rule) this anawash (people) in Yarawashalam:

"Because you have said, ‘We have made a barayath (covenant) with mawath (death), and with shaawal (sheol) are we in chazah (agreement). When the overflowing scourge passes ibar (through), it won't bawaa (come) to us; for we have made lies our refuge, and we have hidden ourselves under falsehood.'

Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah, "Behold, I yasad (lay) in Tzayawan for a foundation a aban (stone), a tried aban (stone), a Yaqar cornerstone of a yasad (sure) foundation. He who aman (believes) shall not act hastily.
I will shawam (make) justice the measuring line, and tzadaqah (righteousness) the plumb line. The hail will sweep away the refuge of lies, and the mayam (waters) will overflow the hiding place.

Your barayath (covenant) with mawath (death) shall be annulled, and your agreement with shaawal (sheol) shall not qawam (stand). When the overflowing scourge passes ibar (through), then you will be trampled down by it.

As often as it passes ibar (through), it will seize you; for baqar (morning) by baqar (morning) it will ibar (pass) through, by yawam (day) and by layal (night); and it will be nothing but terror to bayan (understand) the message.
For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket is too narrow to wrap oneself in.

For Yahawah will qawam (rise) up as on har (mount) Paratzayam. He will be angry as in the valley of Gabaiwan; that he may do his maishah (work), his unusual maishah (work), and ibad (bring) to pass his ibadah (act), his extraordinary ibadah (act).
Lawatz therefore don't be scoffers, lest your bonds be made chazaq (strong); for I have heard a decree of destruction from the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), on the whole aratz (earth).
Give ear, and hear my qawal (voice)! Listen, and hear my amarah (sayings)!
Does he who charash (plows) to zarai (sow) charash (plow) yawam (continually)? Does he keep turning the soil and breaking the clods?
When he has leveled its surface, doesn't he plant the dill, and scatter the cumin seed, and shawam (put) in the wheat in rows, the barley in the appointed place, and the spelt in its place?
For his Alahayam instructs him in right mashapat (judgment), and teaches him.
For the dill are not threshed with a Charawatz instrument, neither is a cart wheel turned over the cumin; but the dill is beaten out with a stick, and the cumin with a shabat (rod).
lacham (bread) flour must be daqaq (ground); so he will not natzach (always) be threshing it. Although he drives the wheel of his threshing cart over it, his horses don't grind it.
This also yatzaa (comes) forth from Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), who is palaa (wonderful) in itzah (counsel), and excellent in thawashayah (wisdom).
Woe to Arayaal! Arayaal, the city where Dawad encamped! sapah (add) Shanah to Shanah; let the chag (feasts) come around;
then I will distress Arayaal, and there will be mourning and lamentation. She shall be Arayaal me as an altar hearth.
I will chanah (encamp) against you all around you, and will tzawar (lay) siege against you with posted troops. I will qawam (raise) siege works qawam (against) you.

You will be brought down, and will dabar (speak) out of the aratz (ground). Your amarah (sayings) will mumble out of the ipar (dust). Your qawal (voice) will be as of one who has a familiar awab (spirit), out of the aratz (ground), and your amarah (sayings) will whisper out of the ipar (dust).
But the multitude of your foes will be Daq fine dust, and the multitude of the ruthless ones like chaff that blows ibar (away). Yes, it will be in an instant, suddenly.

She will be visited by Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) with thunder, with earthquake, with gadawal (great) qawal (noise), with sawapah (whirlwind) and storm, and with the lahab (flame) of a devouring ash (fire).

The multitude of all the gawayam (nations) that fight against Arayaal, even all who fight against her and her stronghold, and who distress her, will be like a chalawam (dream), a vision of the layal (night).

It will be like when a Raib man dreams, and behold, he akal (eats); but he qawatz (awakes), and his hunger isn't satisfied; or like when a Tzamaa man dreams, and behold, he drinks; but he qawatz (awakes), and behold, he is Iyap, and he is still thirsty. The multitude of all the gawayam (nations) that fight against har (mount) Tzayawan will be like that.
Pause and thamah (wonder)! Blind yourselves and be blind! They are Shakar, but not with yayan (wine); they stagger, but not with shakar (strong) drink.
For Yahawah has poured out on you a rawach (spirit) of tharadamah (deep) sleep, and has closed your iyan (eyes), the nabayaa (prophets); and he has covered your raash (heads), the chazah (seers).

All vision has become to you like the dabar (words) of a book that is sealed, which men nathan (deliver) to one who is educated, saying, "qaraa (read) this, please;" and he amar (says), "I can't, for it is sealed:
and the book is delivered to one who is not educated, saying, "qaraa (read) this, please;" and he amar (says), "I can't read.

The Adanay said, "Because this im (people) draws near with their pah (mouth) and with their shapah (lips) to honor me, but they have removed their lab (heart) rachaq (far) from me, and their yaraah (fear) of me is a commandment of men which has been taught;

therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvelous palaa (work) among this im (people), even a marvelous palaa (work) and a palaa (wonder); and the chakamah (wisdom) of their chakam (wise) men will abad (perish), and the bayanah (understanding) of their bayan (prudent) men will be hidden.
Woe to those who deeply hide their itzah (counsel) from Yahawah, and whose maishah (works) are in the dark, and who amar (say), "Who raah (see) us?" and "Who yadai (knows) us?

You hapak (turn) things upside down! Should the potter be thought to be like clay; that the thing made should amar (say) ishah (about) him who made it, "He didn't ishah (make) me;" or the thing formed amar (say) of him who formed it, "He has no bayan (understanding)?
Isn't it yet a very Mait while, and Labanawan will be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field will be regarded as a Yair?
In that yawam (day), the Charash will hear the dabar (words) of the book, and the iyan (eyes) of the iwar (blind) will raah (see) out of apal (obscurity) and out of chashak (darkness).
The Inaw also will increase their joy in Yahawah, and the Abayawan among men will rejoice in the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).
For the ruthless is apas (brought) to nothing, and the Lawatz kalah (ceases), and all those who are alert to do awan (evil) are karath (cut) off—
who cause a adam (person) to be indicted by a dabar (word), and lay a snare for the arbiter in the gate, and who deprive the innocent of justice with false testimony.
Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah, who padah (redeemed) Abaraham, concerning the bayath (house) of Yaiqab: "Yaiqab shall no longer be bawash (ashamed), neither shall his panayam (face) grow pale.

But when he raah (see) his children, the maishah (work) of my yad (hands), in the qarab (midst) of him, they will qadash (sanctify) my sham (name). Yes, they will qadash (sanctify) the qadawash (holy) One of Yaiqab, and will stand in awe of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
They also who thaih (err) in rawach (spirit) will yadai (come) to bayanah (understanding), and those who grumble will receive instruction.

"Woe to the rebellious children," says Yahawah, "who ishah (take) itzah (counsel), but not from me; and who make an alliance, but not with my rawach (spirit), that they may sapah (add) chataah (sin) to chataah (sin),
who set out to yarad (go) down into Matzarayam, and have not asked my advice; to strengthen themselves in the maiwaz (strength) of Paraih, and to take refuge in the shadow of Matzarayam!
Therefore the maiwaz (strength) of Paraih will be your bashath (shame), and the refuge in the shadow of Matzarayam your kalamah (confusion).
For their shar (princes) are at Tzain, and their malaak (ambassadors) have nagai (come) to Chanas.
They shall all be yabash (ashamed) because of a im (people) that can't yail (profit) them, that are not a help nor yail (profit), but a bashath (shame), and also a reproach.

The mashaa (burden) of the animals of the Nagab. Through the aratz (land) of tzarah (trouble) and anguish, of the lioness and the layash (lion), the viper and sharap (fiery) flying serpent, they nashaa (carry) their riches on the shoulders of young donkeys, and their treasures on the humps of camels, to an unprofitable im (people).
For Matzarayam helps in vain, and to no purpose; therefore have I called her rahab (rahab) who sits still.
Now bawaa (go), kathab (write) it before them on a tablet, and inscribe it in a book, that it may be for the yawam (time) to Acharawan iwalam (forever) and ever.
For it is a rebellious im (people), Kachash children, children who will not hear the thawarah (law) of Yahawah;
who amar (tell) the seers, "Don't raah (see)!" and to the chazah (prophets), "Don't chazah (prophesy) to us Nakachah things. dabar (tell) us pleasant things. chazah (prophesy) deceits.
sawar (get) out of the darak (way). natah (turn) aside from the arach (path). Cause the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel) to shabath (cease) from panayam (before) us.
Therefore thus amar (says) the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel), "Because you despise this dabar (word), and batach (trust) in oppression and lawaz (perverseness), and shain (rely) on it;
therefore this iwan (iniquity) shall be to you like a breach napal (ready) to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking bawaa (comes) suddenly in an instant.

He will shabar (break) it as a potter's vessel is broken, breaking it in kathath (pieces) without sparing, so that there won't be found among the broken piece a piece chathah (good) enough to take ash (fire) from the yaqad (hearth), or to dip up mayam (water) out of the cistern.

For thus said the Adanay Yahawah, the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel), "You will be saved in returning and nachath (rest). Your gabawarah (strength) will be in shaqat (quietness) and in confidence." You refused,
but you said, "No, for we will flee on horses;" therefore you will flee; and, "We will ride on the qal (swift);" therefore those who pursue you will be qalal (swift).

One alap (thousand) will flee at the threat of one. At the threat of chamash (five), you will flee until you are yathar (left) like a beacon on the raash (top) of a har (mountain), and like a nas (banner) on a Gabaih.

Therefore Yahawah will wait, that he may be gracious to you; and therefore he will be exalted, that he may have racham (mercy) on you, for Yahawah is a Alahayam of justice. Blessed are all those who wait for him.
For the im (people) will yashab (dwell) in Tzayawan at Yarawashalam. You will weep no more. He will surely be gracious to you at the qawal (voice) of your cry. When he hears you, he will answer you.

Though the Adanay may nathan (give) you the lacham (bread) of adversity and the mayam (water) of affliction, yet your teachers won't be hidden anymore, but your iyan (eyes) will raah (see) your teachers;
and when you aman (turn) to the right hand, and when you shamaal (turn) to the left, your ears will hear a voice achar (behind) you, saying, "This is the darak (way). yalak (walk) in it.

You shall tamaa (defile) the overlaying of your engraved pasayal (images) of kasap (silver), and the plating of your molten masakah (images) of gold. You shall cast them away as an Dawah thing. You shall amar (tell) it, "yatzaa (go) away!

He will nathan (give) the rain for your zarai (seed), with which you will zarai (sow) the adamah (ground); and lacham (bread) of the increase of the adamah (ground) will be Dashan and Shaman. In that yawam (day), your livestock will raih (feed) in large pastures.
The alap (oxen) likewise and the young donkeys that ibad (till) the adamah (ground) will akal (eat) savory provender, which has been winnowed with the shovel and with the fork.

There shall be brooks and streams of mayam (water) on every Gabah har (mountain) and on every nashaa (high) Gabaih in the yawam (day) of the rab (great) slaughter, when the magadal (towers) napal (fall).

Moreover the awar (light) of the labanah (moon) will be like the awar (light) of the chamah (sun), and the awar (light) of the chamah (sun) will be shabai (seven) times brighter, like the awar (light) of shabai (seven) yawam (days), in the yawam (day) that Yahawah binds up the fracture of his im (people), and heals the makah (wound) they were struck with.

Behold, the sham (name) of Yahawah bawaa (comes) from far bair (away), burning with his ap (anger), and in thick rising kabad (smoke). His shapah (lips) are malaa (full) of indignation, and his lashawan (tongue) is as a devouring ash (fire).

His rawach (breath) is as an overflowing nachal (stream) that reaches even to the neck, to sift the gawayam (nations) with the sieve of destruction; and a bridle that leads to ruin will be in the Lachay of the im (peoples).

You will have a song, as in the layal (night) when a qadash (holy) chag (feast) is kept; and gladness of labab (heart), as when one goes with a flute to bawaa (come) to yahawah (yahweh's) har (mountain), to Yasharaal tzawar (rock).

Yahawah will cause his hawad (glorious) qawal (voice) to be heard, and will show the descent of his zarawai (arm), with the zaip (indignation) of his ap (anger), and the lahab (flame) of a devouring ash (fire), with a blast, storm, and hailstones.
For through the qawal (voice) of Yahawah the Ashawar (Assyrian) will be dismayed. He will strike him with his shabat (rod).
Every stroke of the matah (rod) of punishment, which Yahawah will nawach (lay) on him, will be with the sound of tambourines and harps. He will fight with them in battles, brandishing weapons.

Thapathah his burning place has long been ready. Yes, for the malak (king) it is prepared. He has made its pyre deep and large with ash (fire) and much itz (wood). yahawah (yahweh's) nashamah (breath), like a nachal (stream) of sulfur, bair (kindles) it.

Woe to those who yarad (go) down to Matzarayam for help, and shain (rely) on horses, and batach (trust) in chariots because they are many, and in horsemen because they are very itzam (strong), but they don't shaih (look) to the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel), and they don't seek Yahawah!

Yet he also is chakam (wise), and will bawaa (bring) disaster, and will not sawar (call) back his dabar (words), but will qawam (arise) against the bayath (house) of the evildoers, and against the help of those who pail (work) awan (iniquity).

Now the Matzarayam (Egyptians) are men, and not Al; and their horses flesh, and not rawach (spirit). When Yahawah stretches out his yad (hand), both he who helps shall stumble, and he who is helped shall napal (fall), and they all shall be consumed together.

For thus amar (says) Yahawah to me, "As the aray (lion) and the young kapayar (lion) growling over his Tarap, if a multitude of raih (shepherds) is called together against him, will not be dismayed at their qawal (voice), nor abase himself for their noise, so Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) will yarad (come) down to fight on har (mount) Tzayawan and Gabaih its heights.
As birds hovering, so Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) will protect Yarawashalam. He will protect and natzal (deliver) it. He will Pasach over and malat (preserve) it.
shawab (turn back / repent) to him from whom you have deeply sarah (revolted), children of Yasharaal (Israel).
For in that yawam (day) everyone shall cast away his idols of kasap (silver) and his idols of gold — chataa (sin) which your own yad (hands) have made for you.

"The Ashawar (Assyrian) will napal (fall) by the charab (sword), not of ayash (man); and the charab (sword), not of mankind, shall akal (devour) him. He will flee from the charab (sword), and his young men will become subject to forced mas (labor).

His salai (rock) will ibar (pass) away by reason of magawar (terror), and his shar (princes) will be afraid of the nas (banner)," says Yahawah, whose awar (fire) is in Tzayawan, and his furnace in Yarawashalam.
Behold, a malak (king) shall malak (reign) in tzadaq (righteousness), and shar (princes) shall sharar (rule) in justice.

A ayash (man) shall be as a hiding place from the rawach (wind), and a covert from the storm, as palag (streams) of mayam (water) in a dry place, as the shade Kabad a large salai (rock) in a Iyap aratz (land).
The iyan (eyes) of those who raah (see) will not be shaih (dim), and the ears of those who hear will listen.
The labab (heart) of the rash will bayan (understand) daith (knowledge), and the lashawan (tongue) of the Ilag will be ready to dabar (speak) Tzach.
The nabal (fool) will no longer be called nadayab (noble), nor the scoundrel be highly respected.

For the nabal (fool) will dabar (speak) folly, and his lab (heart) will ishah (work) awan (iniquity), to practice profanity, and to dabar (utter) error against Yahawah, To make empty the napash (soul) of the Raib, and to cause the drink Tzamaa the thirsty to fail.

The kalay (ways) of the scoundrel are rai (evil). He yaitz (devises) zamah (wicked) devices to chabal (destroy) the Inay with lying amar (words), even when the Abayawan dabar (speaks) mashapat (right).
But the nadayab (noble) yaitz (devises) nadayab (noble) things; and he will continue in nadayab (noble) things.
qawam (rise) up, you women who are at Shaanan! Hear my qawal (voice)! You batach (careless) bath (daughters), give ear to my amarah (sayings)!
For yawam (days) beyond a Shanah you will be troubled, you batach (careless) women; for the vintage shall kalah (fail). The harvest won't bawaa (come).
Tremble, you women who are at Shaanan! Be troubled, you batach (careless) ones! Strip yourselves, make yourselves naked, and put sackcloth on your waist.
Beat your breasts for the pleasant shadah (fields), for the fruitful vine.
Thorns and briars will ilah (come) up on my im (people's) adamah (land); yes, on all the bayath (houses) of joy in the Ilayaz city.
For the palace will be forsaken. The populous Iyar will be deserted. The hill and the watchtower will be for dens id (forever), a delight for wild donkeys, a pasture of flocks;
Until the rawach (spirit) is poured on us from on high, and the madabar (wilderness) becomes a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is considered a Yair.
Then justice will shakan (dwell) in the madabar (wilderness); and tzadaqah (righteousness) will yashab (remain) in the fruitful field.
The maishah (work) of tzadaqah (righteousness) will be shalawam (peace); and the ibadah (effect) of tzadaqah (righteousness), shaqat (quietness) and confidence iwalam (forever).
My im (people) will live in a peaceful Nawah, in safe mashakan (dwellings), and in Shaanan resting places.
Though hail flattens the Yair, and the Iyar is leveled completely.
Blessed are you who zarai (sow) beside all mayam (waters), who shalach (send) out the feet of the ox and the donkey.

Woe to you who shadad (destroy), but you weren't destroyed; and who betray, but nobody betrayed you! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; and when you have made an end of betrayal, you will be betrayed.
Yahawah, be gracious to us. We have waited for you. Be our zarawai (strength) every baqar (morning), our yashawaih (salvation) also in the ith (time) of tzarah (trouble).
At the qawal (noise) of the thunder, the im (peoples) have fled. When you lift yourself up, the gawayam (nations) are scattered.
Your spoil will be gathered as the caterpillar gathers. Men will leap on it as locusts leap.
Yahawah is exalted, for he shakan (dwells) on high. He has filled Tzayawan with justice and tzadaqah (righteousness).
There will be amawanah (stability) in your ith (times), abundance of yashawaih (salvation), chakamah (wisdom), and daith (knowledge). The yaraah (fear) of Yahawah is your treasure.
Behold, their valiant araal (ones) cry outside; the malaak (ambassadors) of shalawam (peace) weep Mar.
The masalah (highways) are shamam (desolate). The traveling ibar (man) shabath (ceases). The barayath (covenant) is broken. He has despised the Iyar. He doesn't respect anawash (man).
The aratz (land) mourns and languishes. Labanawan is chapar (confounded) and withers away. Sharawan is like a irabah (desert), and Bashan and Karamal are stripped bare.
"Now I will qawam (arise)," amar (says) Yahawah; "Now I will nashaa (lift) myself up. Now I will be exalted.
You will conceive chaff. You will yalad (bring) forth stubble. Your rawach (breath) is a ash (fire) that will akal (devour) you.
The im (peoples) will be like the burning of lime, like thorns that are cut down and burned in the ash (fire).
Hear, you who are Rachawaq off, what I have done; and, you who are qarawab (near), yadai (acknowledge) my might.
The chataa (sinners) in Tzayawan are pachad (afraid). Trembling has seized the godless ones. Who among us can live with the devouring ash (fire)? Who among us can live with iwalam (forever) burning?

He who halak (walks) righteously, and dabar (speaks) blamelessly; He who despises the gain of oppressions, who gestures with his kap (hands), refusing to take a shachad (bribe), who stops his ears from hearing of dam (blood), and itzam (shuts) his iyan (eyes) from looking at rai (evil)—
he will shakan (dwell) on high. His place of defense will be the fortress of salai (rocks). His lacham (bread) will be supplied. His mayam (waters) will be aman (sure).
Your iyan (eyes) will chazah (see) the malak (king) in his beauty. They will raah (see) a distant aratz (land).
Your lab (heart) will meditate on the ayamah (terror). Where is he who counted? Where is he who weighed? Where is he who counted the magadal (towers)?
You will no longer raah (see) the fierce im (people), a im (people) Imaq a deep shapah (speech) that you can't comprehend, with a strange lashawan (language) that you can't understand.

chazah (look) at Tzayawan, the city of our mawaid (appointed) festivals. Your iyan (eyes) will raah (see) Yarawashalam, a Shaanan Nawah, a ahal (tent) that won't be removed. Its stakes will never be plucked up, nor will any of its cords be broken.

But there Yahawah will be with us in majesty, a place of Rachab nahar (rivers) and yaar (streams), in which no galley with oars will yalak (go), neither will any adayar (gallant) ship ibar (pass) by there.
For Yahawah is our shapat (judge). Yahawah is our chaqaq (lawgiver). Yahawah is our malak (king). He will yashai (save) us.
Your rigging is untied. They couldn't chazaq (strengthen) the kan (foot) of their mast. They couldn't spread the nas (sail). Then the prey of a great spoil was divided. The Pasach took the prey.
The Shakan won't amar (say), "I am chalah (sick)." The im (people) who yashab (dwell) therein will be forgiven their iwan (iniquity).
qarab (come) near, you gawayam (nations), to hear! Listen, you laam (peoples). Let the aratz (earth) and all it contains hear; the world, and everything that comes from it.
For Yahawah is enraged against all the gawayam (nations), and angry with all their tzabaa (armies). He has charam (utterly) destroyed them. He has given them over for slaughter.
Their Chalal will also be cast out, and the stench of their pagar (dead) bodies will ilah (come) up; and the har (mountains) will melt in their dam (blood).
All of the tzabaa (army) of the sky will be dissolved. The sky will be rolled up like a scroll, and all its tzabaa (armies) will fade away, as a leaf fades from off a vine or a fig tree.
For my charab (sword) has rawah (drunk) its fill in the sky. Behold, it will yarad (come) down on Adam, and on the im (people) of my charam (curse), for mashapat (judgment).

yahawah (yahweh's) charab (sword) is filled with dam (blood). It is covered with fat, with the dam (blood) of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kalayah (kidneys) of ayal (rams); for Yahawah has a zabach (sacrifice) in Batzarah, And a gadawal (great) slaughter in the aratz (land) of Adam.

The wild oxen will yarad (come) down with them, and the young bulls with the abayar (mighty) bulls; and their aratz (land) will be drunken with dam (blood), and their ipar (dust) made greasy with fat.
For Yahawah has a yawam (day) of vengeance, a Shanah of recompense for the rayab (cause) of Tzayawan.
Its nachal (streams) will be turned into pitch, its ipar (dust) into sulfur, And its aratz (land) will become burning pitch.

It won't be quenched layal (night) nor yawamam (day). Its ishan (smoke) will ilah (go) up iwalam (forever). From dawar (generation) to dawar (generation), it will charab (lie) waste. No one will ibar (pass) through it forever and natzach (ever).

But the pelican and the porcupine will yarash (possess) it. The owl and the raven will shakan (dwell) in it. He will natah (stretch) the line of thahaw (confusion) over it, and the plumb line of emptiness.
They shall qaraa (call) its nobles to the malawakah (kingdom), but none shall be there; and all its shar (princes) shall be apas (nothing).
Thorns will ilah (come) up in its palaces, nettles and thistles in its fortresses; and it will be a Nawah of jackals, a court for ostriches.

The tzayay (wild) animals of the desert will meet with the wolves, and the wild Shaiyar will qaraa (cry) to his rai (fellow). Yes, the layalayath (night) creature shall settle there, and shall matzaa (find) herself a place of manawach (rest).
The arrow snake will make her nest there, and malat (lay), hatch, and gather under her shade. Yes, the kites will be gathered there, ashah (every) one with her mate.

Search in the book of Yahawah, and qaraa (read): not one of these will be missing. ashah (none) will paqad (lack) her mate. For my pah (mouth) has tzawah (commanded), and his rawach (spirit) has gathered them.

He has napal (cast) the lot for them, and his yad (hand) has divided it to them with a measuring line. They shall yarash (possess) it iwalam (forever). From dawar (generation) to dawar (generation) they will shakan (dwell) in it.
The madabar (wilderness) and the dry tzayah (land) will be glad. The irabah (desert) will rejoice and blossom like a rose.

It will blossom abundantly, and rejoice even with joy and singing. Labanawan kabawad (glory) Lebanon will be given to it, the excellence of Karamal and Sharawan. They will raah (see) yahawah (yahweh's) kabawad (glory), the excellence of our Alahayam.
chazaq (strengthen) the Rapah yad (hands), and amatz (make) firm the feeble knees.

amar (tell) those who have a fearful lab (heart), "Be chazaq (strong). Don't be yaraa (afraid). Behold, your Alahayam will bawaa (come) with vengeance, alahayam (god's) retribution. He will bawaa (come) and yashai (save) you.
Then the iyan (eyes) of the iwar (blind) will be opened, and the ears of the Charash will be unstopped.

Then the Pasach dalag (man) will leap like a deer, and the lashawan (tongue) of the mute will sing; for mayam (waters) will break out in the madabar (wilderness), and nachal (streams) in the irabah (desert).
The burning sand will become a pool, and the thirsty tzamaawan (ground) springs of mayam (water). Grass with reeds and rushes will be in the Nawah of jackals, where they lay.

A highway will be there, a road, and it will be called The qadash (holy) darak (way). The tamaa (unclean) shall not ibar (pass) over it, but it will be for those who walk in the Way. Wicked Awayal will not thaih (go) there.
No aray (lion) will be there, nor will any ravenous animal ilah (go) up on it. They will not be found there; but the redeemed will halak (walk) there.

The yahawah (yahweh's) ransomed ones will shawab (turn back / repent), and bawaa (come) with singing to Tzayawan; and iwalam (forever) joy will be on their raash (heads). They will obtain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.
Now it happened in the fourteenth Shanah of malak (king) Chazaqayah, that Sanacharayab malak (king) of Ashawar attacked all of the fortified Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and captured them.

The malak (king) of Ashawar sent Rabashaqah from Lakayash to Yarawashalam to malak (king) Chazaqayah Kabad a large chayal (army). He stood by the aqueduct from the Ilayawan pool in the fuller's shadah (field) masalah (highway).
Then Alayaqayam the ban (son) Chalaqayah Hilkiah, who was over the bayath (household), and Shabanaa the scribe, and Yawaach, the ban (son) of Asap, the zakar (recorder) came out to him.
Rabashaqah said to them, "Now amar (tell) Chazaqayah, ‘Thus amar (says) the gadawal (great) malak (king), the malak (king) of Ashawar, "What confidence is this in which you trust?
I amar (say) that your itzah (counsel) and gabawarah (strength) for the war are only vain dabar (words). Now in whom do you batach (trust), that you have rebelled against me?

Behold, you batach (trust) in the mashainah (staff) of this bruised reed, even in Matzarayam, which if a ayash (man) samak (leans) on it, it will bawaa (go) into his kap (hand) and naqab (pierce) it. So is Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam to all who batach (trust) in him.

But if you amar (tell) me, ‘We batach (trust) in Yahawah our Alahayam,' isn't that he whose bamah (high) places and whose mazabach (altars) Chazaqayah has taken sawar (away), and has said to Yahawadah (Judah) and to Yarawashalam, ‘You shall shachah (worship) panayam (before) this mazabach (altar)?'

Now therefore, please make a pledge to my adawan (master) the malak (king) of Ashawar, and I will nathan (give) you two alap (thousand) horses, if you are yakal (able) on your part to nathan (set) riders on them.

How then can you shawab (turn back / repent) away the panayam (face) of one captain of the qatan (least) of my adawan (master's) ibad (servants), and batach (put) your trust on Matzarayam for chariots and for horsemen?
Have I ilah (come) up now balaiday (without) Yahawah against this aratz (land) to shachath (destroy) it? Yahawah said to me, "ilah (go) up against this aratz (land), and shachath (destroy) it."'

Then Alayaqayam, Shabanaa and Yawaach said to Rabashaqah, "Please dabar (speak) to your ibad (servants) Aramayath Aramaic, for we understand it; and don't dabar (speak) to us in the Yahawadayath (Jews)' language in the hearing of the im (people) who are on the wall.

But Rabashaqah said, "Has my adawan (master) sent me only to your adawan (master) and to you, to dabar (speak) these dabar (words), and not to the men who yashab (sit) on the wall, who will akal (eat) their own dung and drink their own urine with you?

Then Rabashaqah stood, and called out with a gadawal (loud) qawal (voice) in the Yahawadayath (Jews)' language, and said, "Hear the dabar (words) of the gadawal (great) malak (king), the malak (king) of Ashawar!
Thus amar (says) the malak (king), ‘Don't let Chazaqayah deceive you; for he will not be yakal (able) to natzal (deliver) you.
Don't let Chazaqayah batach (make) you trust in Yahawah, saying, "Yahawah will natzal (surely) natzal (deliver) us. This Iyar won't be given into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Ashawar."'

Don't listen to Chazaqayah, for thus amar (says) the malak (king) of Ashawar, ‘ishah (make) your barakah (peace) with me, and yatzaa (come) out to me; and ayash (each) of you akal (eat) from his vine, and ayash (each) one from his fig tree, and ayash (each) one of you drink the mayam (waters) of his own bawar (cistern);
until I bawaa (come) and take you away to a aratz (land) like your own aratz (land), a aratz (land) of grain and new thayarawash (wine), a aratz (land) of lacham (bread) and vineyards.

Beware lest Chazaqayah persuade you, saying, "Yahawah will natzal (deliver) us." Have any of the Alahayam of the gawayam (nations) delivered their aratz (lands) from the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Ashawar?
Where are the Alahayam of Chamath and Arapad? Where are the Alahayam of Saparawayam? Have they delivered Shamarawan from my yad (hand)?
Who are they among all the Alahayam of these aratz (countries) that have delivered their aratz (country) out of my yad (hand), that Yahawah should natzal (deliver) Yarawashalam out of my yad (hand)?'
But they remained charash (silent), and said nothing in reply, for the malak (king's) matzawah (commandment) was, "Don't dabar (answer) him.

Then Alayaqayam the ban (son) Chalaqayah Hilkiah, who was over the bayath (household), and Shabanaa the scribe, and Yawaach, the ban (son) of Asap, the zakar (recorder), came to Chazaqayah with their clothes torn, and told him the dabar (words) of Rabashaqah.
It happened, when malak (king) Chazaqayah heard it, that he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth, and went into yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house).

He sent Alayaqayam, who was over the bayath (household), and Shabanaa the scribe, and the zaqan (elders) of the kahan (priests), covered with sackcloth, to Yashaiyah the nabayaa (prophet), the ban (son) of Amawatz.

They said to him, "Thus amar (says) Chazaqayah, ‘This yawam (day) is a yawam (day) of tzarah (trouble), and of rebuke, and of rejection; for the children have bawaa (come) to the birth, and there is no kach (strength) to yalad (bring) forth.

It may be Yahawah your Alahayam will hear the dabar (words) of Rabashaqah, whom the malak (king) of Ashawar his adawan (master) has sent to defy the chay (living) Alahayam, and will yakach (rebuke) the dabar (words) which Yahawah your Alahayam has heard. Therefore nashaa (lift) up your prayer for the shaarayath (remnant) that is matzaa (left).'
So the ibad (servants) of malak (king) Chazaqayah came to Yashaiyah.

Yashaiyah said to them, "amar (tell) your adawan (master), ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "Don't be yaraa (afraid) of the dabar (words) that you have heard, with which the nair (servants) of the malak (king) of Ashawar have blasphemed me.

Behold, I will nathan (put) a rawach (spirit) in him and he will hear news, and will shawab (turn back / repent) to his own aratz (land). I will napal (cause) him to fall by the charab (sword) in his own aratz (land)."'
So Rabashaqah returned, and found the malak (king) of Ashawar warring against Labanah, for he had heard that he was departed from Lakayash.
He heard news concerning Tharahaqah malak (king) of Kawash, "He has yatzaa (come) out to fight against you." When he heard it, he sent malaak (messengers) to Chazaqayah, saying,

"Thus you shall amar (speak) to Chazaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), saying, ‘Don't let your Alahayam in whom you batach (trust) deceive you, saying, "Yarawashalam won't be given into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Ashawar.
Behold, you have heard what the malak (kings) of Ashawar have done to all aratz (lands), by destroying them charam (utterly). Shall you be delivered?
Have the Alahayam of the gawayam (nations) delivered them, which my abawath (fathers) have destroyed, Gawazan, Charan, Ratzap, and the children of Idan who were in Thalaashar?
Where is the malak (king) of Chamath, and the malak (king) of Arapad, and the malak (king) of the Iyar of Saparawayam, of Hanai, and Iwah?'

Chazaqayah received the letter from the yad (hand) of the malaak (messengers) and qaraa (read) it. Then Chazaqayah went up to yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house), and spread it panayam (before) Yahawah.
Chazaqayah prayed to Yahawah, saying,

"Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), who is enthroned among the karawab (cherubim), you are the Alahayam, even you alone, of all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (earth). You have made shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth).
natah (turn) your ear, Yahawah, and hear. Open your iyan (eyes), Yahawah, and raah (see). Hear all of the dabar (words) of Sanacharayab, who has sent to defy the chay (living) Alahayam.
Truly, Yahawah, the malak (kings) of Ashawar have destroyed all the aratz (countries) and their aratz (land),
and have nathan (cast) their Alahayam into the ash (fire); for they were no Alahayam, but the maishah (work) of men's yad (hands), itz (wood) and aban (stone); therefore they have destroyed them.
Now therefore, Yahawah our Alahayam, yashai (save) us from his yad (hand), that all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (earth) may yadai (know) that you are Yahawah, even you only.

Then Yashaiyah the ban (son) of Amawatz sent to Chazaqayah, saying, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), ‘Because you have prayed to me against Sanacharayab malak (king) of Ashawar,

this is the dabar (word) which Yahawah has spoken concerning him. The virgin bath (daughter) of Tzayawan has despised you and ridiculed you. The bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam has shaken her raash (head) at you.
Whom have you defied and blasphemed? Against whom have you exalted your qawal (voice) and lifted up your iyan (eyes) on high? Against the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).

By your ibad (servants), have you defied the Adanay, and have said, "With the multitude of my chariots I have ilah (come) up to the height of the har (mountains), to the innermost parts of Labanawan. I will karath (cut) down its tall cedars and its choice fir trees. I will bawaa (enter) into its farthest height, the Yair of its Karamal field.
I have dug and drunk mayam (water), and with the kap (sole) of my feet I will charab (dry) up all the yaar (rivers) Matzawar Egypt.

Have you not heard how I have done it Rachawaq ago, and formed it in qadam (ancient) yawam (times)? Now I have brought it to pass, that it should be yours to shaah (destroy) fortified Iyar, turning them into ruinous heaps.

Therefore their yashab (inhabitants) had Qatzar yad (power). They were dismayed and confounded. They were like the grass of the shadah (field), and like the green herb, like the grass on the housetops, and like a field panayam (before) its crop has grown.
But I yadai (know) your sitting down, your yatzaa (going) out, your coming in, and your raging against me.

Because of your raging Shaanan me, and because your arrogance has ilah (come) up into my ears, therefore will I shawam (put) my hook in your ap (nose) and my bridle in your shapah (lips), and I will shawab (turn back / repent) you back by the darak (way) by which you came.

This shall be the awath (sign) to you. You will akal (eat) this Shanah that which grows of itself, and in the shanay (second) Shanah that which springs from the same; and in the shalayashay (third) Shanah zarai (sow) and reap and plant vineyards, and akal (eat) their fruit.
The shaar (remnant) that is palayatah (escaped) of the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) will again take root downward, and ishah (bear) fruit upward.

For out of Yarawashalam a shaarayath (remnant) will yatzaa (go) forth, and survivors will palayatah (escape) from har (mount) Tzayawan. The zeal of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) will ishah (perform) this.'

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah concerning the malak (king) of Ashawar, ‘He will not bawaa (come) to this Iyar, nor shoot an chatz (arrow) there, neither will he qadam (come) before it with magan (shield), nor cast up a mound against it.
By the darak (way) that he came, by the same he shall shawab (turn back / repent), and he shall not bawaa (come) to this Iyar,' says Yahawah.
‘For I will defend this Iyar to yashai (save) it, for my own sake, and for my ibad (servant) Dawad sake.'

The malaak (angel) of Yahawah went out and struck one maah (hundred) and shamanayam (eighty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) men in the machanah (camp) of the Ashawar (Assyrians). When men arose shakam (early) in the baqar (morning), behold, these were all mawath (dead) pagar (bodies).
So Sanacharayab malak (king) of Ashawar departed, went shawab (turn back / repent), returned to Nayanawah, and stayed there.

It happened, as he was worshipping in the bayath (house) of Nasarak his Alahayam, that Adaramalak and Sharaatzar his ban (sons) struck him with the charab (sword); and they escaped into the aratz (land) of Ararat. Asarachadawan Haddon his ban (son) reigned in his place.

In those yawam (days) was Chazaqayah chalah (sick) and near mawath (death). Yashaiyah the nabayaa (prophet), the ban (son) of Amawatz, came to him, and said to him, "Thus amar (says) Yahawah, ‘Set your bayath (house) in tzawah (order), for you will mawath (die), and not chayah (live).'
Then Chazaqayah turned his panayam (face) to the wall and prayed to Yahawah,

and said, "zakar (remember) now, Yahawah, I beg you, how I have walked panayam (before) you in truth and with a Shalam lab (heart), and have done that which is tawab (good) in your iyan (sight)." Chazaqayah wept bitterly.
Then the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Yashaiyah, saying,

"halak (go), and amar (tell) Chazaqayah, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Dawad your ab (father), "I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Behold, I will add chamash (fifteen) Shanah to your yawam (life).
I will natzal (deliver) you and this Iyar out of the kap (hand) of the malak (king) of Ashawar, and I will defend this Iyar.
This shall be the awath (sign) to you from Yahawah, that Yahawah will do this thing that he has spoken.

Behold, I will cause the shadow on the sundial, which has gone down on the sundial of Achaz with the sun, to shawab (turn back / repent) backward ishar (ten) steps. So the shamash (sun) returned ishar (ten) steps on the sundial on which it had gone down."'
The writing of Chazaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), when he had been chalah (sick), and had recovered of his sickness.
I said, "In the middle of my yawam (life) I yalak (go) into the gates of shaawal (sheol). I am deprived of the yathar (residue) of my Shanah.
I said, "I won't raah (see) Yah, Yah in the aratz (land) of the chay (living). I will see adam (man) no more with the yashab (inhabitants) of the world.

My dwelling is removed, and is carried away from me like a shepherd's ahal (tent). I have rolled up, like a weaver, my chay (life). He will cut me off Dalah the loom. From yawam (day) even to layal (night) you will shalam (make) an end of me.
I waited patiently until baqar (morning). He shabar (breaks) all my itzam (bones) like a aray (lion). From yawam (day) even to layal (night) you will shalam (make) an end of me.
I chattered like a swallow or a crane. I moaned like a dove. My iyan (eyes) weaken looking upward. Adawan, I am oppressed. Be my security.
What will I dabar (say)? He has both spoken to me, and himself has done it. I will walk carefully all my Shanah Mar of the anguish of my napash (soul).
Adanay, men chayah (live) by these things; and my rawach (spirit) finds chay (life) in all of them: you restore me, and cause me to chayah (live).

Behold, for shalawam (peace) I had Mar anguish, but you have in chashaq (love) for my napash (soul) delivered it from the shachath (pit) of corruption; for you have cast all my chataa (sins) achar (behind) your back.
For shaawal (sheol) can't yadah (praise) you. mawath (death) can't halal (celebrate) you. Those who yarad (go) down into the bawar (pit) can't hope for your truth.
The chay (living), the chay (living), he shall yadah (praise) you, as I do this yawam (day). The ab (father) shall yadai (make) known your truth to the children.
Yahawah will yashai (save) me. Therefore we will sing my songs with stringed instruments all the yawam (days) of our chay (life) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
Now Yashaiyah had said, "Let them nashaa (take) a cake of figs, and lay it for a poultice on the boil, and he shall chayah (recover).
Chazaqayah also had said, "What is the awath (sign) that I will ilah (go) up to the bayath (house) of Yahawah?

At that ith (time), Merodach Balaadan the ban (son) of Balaadan, malak (king) of Babal, sent letters and a manachah (present) to Chazaqayah; for he heard that he had been chalah (sick), and had chazaq (recovered).

Chazaqayah was Shamach with them, and showed them the bayath (house) of his precious things, the kasap (silver), and the gold, the spices, and the tawab (precious) shaman (oil), and all the bayath (house) of his armor, and all that was found in his treasures. There was nothing in his bayath (house), nor in all his mamashalah (dominion), that Chazaqayah didn't show them.

Then Yashaiyah the nabayaa (prophet) came to malak (king) Chazaqayah, and asked him, "What did these men amar (say)? Where did they bawaa (come) from to you?" Chazaqayah said, "They have bawaa (come) from a aratz (country) Rachawaq from me, even from Babal.
Then he asked, "What have they seen in your bayath (house)?" Chazaqayah answered, "They have seen all that is in my bayath (house). There is nothing among my treasures that I have not shown them.
Then Yashaiyah said to Chazaqayah, "Hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies):

‘Behold, the yawam (days) are coming when all that is in your bayath (house), and that which your abawath (fathers) have stored up until this yawam (day), will be carried to Babal. Nothing will be yathar (left),' amar (says) Yahawah.
‘They will take away your ban (sons) who will yatzaa (issue) from you, whom you shall father, and they will be eunuchs in the malak (king) of Babal hayakal (palace).'
Then Chazaqayah said to Yashaiyah, "yahawah (yahweh's) dabar (word) which you have spoken is tawab (good)." He said moreover, "For there will be shalawam (peace) and truth in my yawam (days).
"nacham (comfort), nacham (comfort) my im (people)," amar (says) your Alahayam.

"dabar (speak) lab (comfortably) to Yarawashalam; and qaraa (call) out to her that her tzabaa (warfare) is accomplished, that her iwan (iniquity) is pardoned, that she has received of yahawah (yahweh's) yad (hand) double for all her chataah (sins).

The qawal (voice) of one who qaraa (calls) out, "panah (prepare) the darak (way) of Yahawah in the irabah (wilderness)! yashar (make) a level masalah (highway) in the irabah (desert) for our Alahayam.
Every Gayaa shall be exalted, and every har (mountain) and Gabaih shall be made low. The Iqab shall be made level, and the rough places a Baqaih.
The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah shall be revealed, and all flesh shall raah (see) it together; for the pah (mouth) of Yahawah has spoken it.
The qawal (voice) of one saying, "qaraa (cry)!" One said, "What shall I qaraa (cry)?" "All flesh is like grass, and all its glory is like the flower of the shadah (field).
The grass yabash (withers), the flower fades, because yahawah (yahweh's) rawach (breath) blows on it. Surely the im (people) are like grass.
The grass yabash (withers), the flower fades; but the dabar (word) of our Alahayam qawam (stands) iwalam (forever).

You who tell bashar (good) news to Tzayawan, ilah (go) up on a Gabah har (mountain). You who tell bashar (good) news to Yarawashalam, lift up your qawal (voice) with kach (strength). Lift it up. Don't be yaraa (afraid). amar (say) to the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), "Behold, your Alahayam!
Behold, the Adanay Yahawah will bawaa (come) as a chazaq (mighty) one, and his zarawai (arm) will mashal (rule) for him. Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense panayam (before) him.
He will raih (feed) his flock like a raih (shepherd). He will gather the lambs in his zarawai (arm), and nashaa (carry) them in his bosom. He will gently lead those who have their young.

Who has measured the mayam (waters) in the hollow of his shail (hand), and marked off the sky with his span, and calculated the ipar (dust) of the aratz (earth) in a shalayash (measure), and weighed the har (mountains) in scales, and the Gabaih in a balance?
Who has directed the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah, or has taught him as his counselor?

Who did he take yaitz (counsel) with, and who instructed him, and taught him in the arach (path) of justice, and taught him daith (knowledge), and showed him the darak (way) of thabawan (understanding)?
Behold, the gawayam (nations) are like a drop in a bucket, and are regarded as a speck of shachaq (dust) on a balance. Behold, he lifts up the islands like a very Daq thing.
Labanawan is not sufficient to bair (burn), nor its animals sufficient for a burnt ilah (offering).
All the gawayam (nations) are chashab (like) nothing before him. They are regarded by him as apas (less) than nothing, and thahaw (vanity).
To whom then will you liken Al? Or what damawath (likeness) will you compare to him?
A workman has cast an pasal (image), and the goldsmith overlays it with gold, and casts kasap (silver) chains for it.

He who is too impoverished for such an tharawamah (offering) chooses a itz (tree) that will not rot. He seeks a skillful workman to kawan (set) up an engraved pasal (image) for him that will not be moved.
Haven't you yadai (known)? Haven't you heard, yet? Haven't you been told from the raash (beginning)? Haven't you understood from the foundations of the aratz (earth)?

It is he who yashab (sits) above the circle of the aratz (earth), and its yashab (inhabitants) are like grasshoppers; who stretches out the shamayam (heavens) like a curtain, and spreads them out like a ahal (tent) to yashab (dwell) in;
who nathan (brings) razan (princes) to nothing; who ishah (makes) the shapat (judges) of the aratz (earth) like meaningless.

They are planted scarcely. They are sown scarcely. Their stock has scarcely taken root in the aratz (ground). He merely blows on them, and they yabash (wither), and the whirlwind nashaa (takes) them away as stubble.
"To whom then will you liken me? Who is my equal?" amar (says) the qadawash (holy) One.

nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eyes) on high, and raah (see) who has created these, who yatzaa (brings) out their tzabaa (army) by number. He qaraa (calls) them all by sham (name). by the greatness of his might, and because he is amayatz (strong) in kach (power), Not one is lacking.
Why do you amar (say), Yaiqab, and dabar (speak), Yasharaal (Israel), "My darak (way) is hidden from Yahawah, and the justice due me is disregarded by my Alahayam?

Haven't you yadai (known)? Haven't you heard? The iwalam (forever) Alahayam, Yahawah, The Creator of the ends of the aratz (earth), doesn't Yaip. He isn't weary. His thabawan (understanding) is unsearchable.
He nathan (gives) kach (power) Yaip the weak. He increases the itzamah (strength) of him who has no might.
Even the youths Yaip and get weary, and the young men utterly fall;
But those who wait for Yahawah will renew their kach (strength). They will ilah (mount) up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary. They will yalak (walk), and not Yaip.
"charash (keep) silent before me, islands, and let the laam (peoples) renew their kach (strength). Let them come near, then let them dabar (speak). Let's meet together for mashapat (judgment).

Who has raised up mazarach (one) from the east? Who called him to his ragal (foot) in tzadaq (righteousness)? He hands over gawayam (nations) to him, and radah (makes) him rule over malak (kings). He nathan (gives) them like the ipar (dust) to his charab (sword), like the driven stubble to his qashath (bow).
He pursues them, and passes by safely, Even by a arach (way) that he had not gone with his feet.
Who has worked and done it, calling the dawar (generations) from the raash (beginning)? I, Yahawah, the raashawan (first), and with the Acharawan, I am he.
The islands have seen, and yaraa (fear). The ends of the aratz (earth) tremble. They qarab (approach), and come.
Everyone helps his neighbor. They amar (say) to their ach (brothers), "Be chazaq (strong)!

So the carpenter chazaq (encourages) the goldsmith. He who smoothes with the hammer encourages him who strikes the paim (anvil), saying of the soldering, "It is tawab (good);" and he chazaq (fastens) it with nails, that it might not totter.
"But you, Yasharaal (Israel), my ibad (servant), Yaiqab whom I have chosen, the zarai (seed) of Abaraham my ahab (friend),
You whom I have taken hold of from the ends of the aratz (earth), and called from its corners, and said to you, ‘You are my ibad (servant), I have chosen you and not cast you away;'

Don't you be yaraa (afraid), for I am with you. Don't be shaih (dismayed), for I am your Alahayam. I will amatz (strengthen) you. Yes, I will help you. Yes, I will uphold you with the right yamayan (hand) of my tzadaq (righteousness).
Behold, all those who are charah (incensed) against you will be disappointed and kalam (confounded). Those who rayab (strive) with you will be like nothing, and shall abad (perish).
You will seek them, and won't matzaa (find) them, even those who contend with you. Those who war against you will be as apas (nothing), as a non-existent thing.
For I, Yahawah your Alahayam, will chazaq (hold) your right yamayan (hand), saying to you, ‘Don't be yaraa (afraid). I will help you.'
Don't be yaraa (afraid), you worm Yaiqab, and you men of Yasharaal (Israel). I will help you," says Yahawah, "and your gaal (redeemer) is the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).
Behold, I have made you into a Chadash Charawatz threshing instrument with teeth. You will thresh the har (mountains), and beat them small, and will shawam (make) the Gabaih like chaff.

You will winnow them, and the rawach (wind) will nashaa (carry) them away, and the whirlwind will scatter them. You will rejoice in Yahawah. You will glory in the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).
The Inay and Abayawan seek mayam (water), and there is none. Their lashawan (tongue) fails for thirst. I, Yahawah, will answer them. I, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), will not forsake them.

I will pathach (open) nahar (rivers) on the bare heights, and springs in the midst of the Baqaih. I will shawam (make) the madabar (wilderness) a pool of mayam (water), and the tzayah (dry) aratz (land) springs of mayam (water).
I will nathan (put) cedar, acacia, myrtle, and shaman (oil) trees in the madabar (wilderness). I will shawam (set) fir itz (trees), pine, and box trees together in the irabah (desert);

that they may raah (see), yadai (know), shawam (consider), and shakal (understand) together, that the yad (hand) of Yahawah has done this, and the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel) has created it.
qarab (produce) your rayab (cause)," amar (says) Yahawah. "Bring forth your strong reasons," amar (says) the malak (king) of Yaiqab.

"Let them announce, and nagad (declare) to us what shall qarah (happen). nagad (declare) the raashawan (former) things, what they are, that we may shawam (consider) them, and yadai (know) the acharayath (latter) end of them; or show us things to bawaa (come).

nagad (declare) the things that are to come hereafter, that we may yadai (know) that you are Alahayam. Yes, do yatab (good), or do raii (evil), that we may be shaih (dismayed), and raah (see) it together.
Behold, you are of nothing, and your pail (work) is of nothing. He who chooses you is an thawaibah (abomination).

"I have raised up one from the tzapawan (north), and he has come; from the rising of the shamash (sun), one who qaraa (calls) on my sham (name); and he shall bawaa (come) on sagan (rulers) as on mortar, and as the potter treads clay.

Who has declared it from the raash (beginning), that we may yadai (know)? And panayam (before), that we may amar (say), ‘He is right?' nagad (surely), there is no one who declares. Surely, there is no shamai (one) who shows. Surely, there is no shamai (one) who hears your amar (words).
I am the raashawan (first) to say to Tzayawan, ‘Behold, look at them;' and I will nathan (give) one who brings bashar (good) news to Yarawashalam.
When I raah (see), there is no ayash (man); even among them there is no yaitz (counselor) who, when I shaal (ask) of them, can shawab (turn back / repent) a dabar (word).
Behold, all of them, their maishah (works) are awan (vanity) and apas (nothing). Their molten nasak (images) are rawach (wind) and thahaw (confusion).
"Behold, my ibad (servant), whom I uphold; my Bachayar, in whom my napash (soul) delights— I have nathan (put) my rawach (spirit) on him. He will yatzaa (bring) justice to the gawayam (nations).
He will not shout, nor nashaa (raise) his qawal (voice), nor cause it to be heard in the street.
He won't shabar (break) a bruised reed. He won't quench a Kahah burning wick. He will faithfully yatzaa (bring) justice.
He will not fail nor be discouraged, until he has shawam (set) justice in the aratz (earth), and the islands will wait for his thawarah (law).

Thus amar (says) Al Yahawah, he who created the shamayam (heavens) and stretched them out, he who spread out the aratz (earth) and that which comes out of it, he who nathan (gives) nashamah (breath) to its im (people) and rawach (spirit) to those who halak (walk) in it.

"I, Yahawah, have called you in tzadaq (righteousness), and will chazaq (hold) your yad (hand), and will keep you, and nathan (make) you a barayath (covenant) for the im (people), as a awar (light) for the gawayam (nations);
to open the iwar (blind) iyan (eyes), to bring the prisoners out of the dungeon, and those who yashab (sit) in chashak (darkness) out of the prison.
"I am Yahawah. That is my sham (name). I will not nathan (give) my kabawad (glory) to achar (another), nor my thahalah (praise) to engraved pasayal (images).
Behold, the raashawan (former) things have happened, and I nagad (declare) Chadash things. I tell you about them before they come up.

shayar (sing) to Yahawah a Chadash song, and his thahalah (praise) from the end of the aratz (earth), you who yarad (go) down to the yam (sea), and all that is therein, the islands and their yashab (inhabitants).

Let the madabar (wilderness) and its Iyar nashaa (raise) their chatzar (voices), with the villages that Qadar yashab (inhabits). Let the yashab (inhabitants) of Sela sing. Let them shout from the raash (top) of the har (mountains)!
Let them shawam (give) kabawad (glory) to Yahawah, and nagad (declare) his thahalah (praise) in the islands.

Yahawah will yatzaa (go) out like a gabawar (mighty) man. He will stir up zeal like a ayash (man) of war. He will raise a war rawai (cry). Yes, he will shout aloud. He will triumph over his ayab (enemies).
"I have been chashah (silent) a long time. I have been charash (quiet) and restrained myself. Now I will cry out like a travailing yalad (woman). I will both gasp and pant.
I will charab (destroy) har (mountains) and Gabaih, and yabash (dry) up all their herbs. I will shawam (make) the nahar (rivers) islands, and will yabash (dry) up the pools.

I will yalak (bring) the iwar (blind) by a darak (way) that they don't yadai (know). I will lead them in nathayab (paths) that they don't yadai (know). I will shawam (make) machashak (darkness) awar (light) panayam (before) them, and crooked places mayashawar (straight). I will do these things, and I will not forsake them.
"Those who batach (trust) in engraved pasal (images), who amar (tell) molten pasal (images), ‘You are our Alahayam' will be turned back. They will be utterly disappointed.
"Hear, you Charash, and look, you iwar (blind), that you may raah (see).

Who is iwar (blind), but my ibad (servant)? Or who is as Charash as my malaak (messenger) whom I shalach (send)? Who is as iwar (blind) as he who is at shalam (peace), and as iwar (blind) as yahawah (yahweh's) ibad (servant)?
You raah (see) many things, but don't shamar (observe). His ears are open, but he doesn't listen.
It pleased Yahawah, for his tzadaq (righteousness)' sake, to magnify the thawarah (law), and make it honorable.

But this is a robbed and plundered im (people). All of them are snared in holes, and they are hidden in prisons. They have become a prey, and no one natzal (delivers); and a spoil, and no one amar (says), ‘shawab (turn back / repent) them!'
Who is there among you who will give ear to this? Who will listen and hear for the time to come?

Who gave Yaiqab as plunder, and Yasharaal (Israel) to the robbers? Didn't Yahawah, he against whom we have sinned? For they would not halak (walk) in his darak (ways), and they disobeyed his thawarah (law).

Therefore he poured the fierceness of his ap (anger) on him, and the izawaz (strength) of battle; and it set him on lahat (fire) all around, but he didn't yadai (know); and it burned him, but he didn't shawam (take) it to lab (heart).

But now thus amar (says) Yahawah who created you, Yaiqab, and he who formed you, Yasharaal (Israel): "Don't be yaraa (afraid), for I have redeemed you. I have called you by your sham (name). You are mine.

When you ibar (pass) through the mayam (waters), I will be with you; and ibar (through) the nahar (rivers), they will not overflow you. When you yalak (walk) through the ash (fire), you will not be burned, and lahabah (flame) will not scorch you.
For I am Yahawah your Alahayam, the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel), your Savior. I have given Matzarayam as your kapar (ransom), Kawash and Sabaa in your place.
Since you have been precious and honored in my iyan (sight), and I have loved you; therefore I will nathan (give) people in your place, and laam (nations) instead of your napash (life).
Don't be yaraa (afraid); for I am with you. I will bawaa (bring) your zarai (seed) from the east, and gather you from the west.

I will amar (tell) the tzapawan (north), ‘nathan (give) them up!' and tell the thayaman (south), ‘Don't hold them back! bawaa (bring) my ban (sons) from Rachawaq, and my bath (daughters) from the ends of the aratz (earth)—
everyone who is called by my sham (name), and whom I have created for my kabawad (glory), whom I have formed, yes, whom I have made.'
yatzaa (bring) out the iwar (blind) im (people) who have iyan (eyes), and the Charash who have ears.

Let all the gawayam (nations) be gathered together, and let the laam (peoples) be assembled. Who among them can nagad (declare) this, and show us raashawan (former) things? Let them nathan (bring) their witnesses, that they may be justified; or let them hear, and amar (say), "That is amath (true).
