"You are my witnesses," says Yahawah, "With my ibad (servant) whom I have chosen; that you may yadai (know) and aman (believe) me, and bayan (understand) that I am he. panayam (before) me there was no Al formed, neither will there be achar (after) me.
I myself am Yahawah; and balaiday (besides) me there is no savior.
I have declared, I have saved, and I have shown; and there was no zawar (strange) Alahayam among you. Therefore you are my witnesses," says Yahawah, "and I am Al.
Yes, since the yawam (day) was I am he; and there is no one who can natzal (deliver) out of my yad (hand). I will pail (work), and who can shawab (turn back / repent) it?

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, your gaal (redeemer), the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel): "For your sake, I have sent to Babal, and I will Barayach all of them down as fugitives, even the Kashaday (Chaldeans), in the ships of their rejoicing.
I am Yahawah, your qadawash (holy) One, the Creator of Yasharaal (Israel), your malak (king).
Thus amar (says) Yahawah, who nathan (makes) a darak (way) in the yam (sea), and a nathayab (path) in the iz (mighty) mayam (waters);
who yatzaa (brings) forth the chariot and horse, the chayal (army) and the mighty man (they shakab (lie) down together, they shall not qawam (rise); they are extinct, they are quenched like a wick):
"Don't zakar (remember) the raashawan (former) things, and don't bayan (consider) the things of Qadamawanay.

Behold, I will do a Chadash thing. It springs forth now. Don't you yadai (know) it? I will even shawam (make) a darak (way) in the madabar (wilderness), and nahar (rivers) in the yashayamawan (desert).

The animals of the shadah (field) shall honor me, the jackals and the ostriches; because I nathan (give) mayam (water) in the madabar (wilderness) and nahar (rivers) in the yashayamawan (desert), to shaqah (give) drink to my im (people), my Bachayar,
the im (people) which I formed for myself, that they might set forth my thahalah (praise).
Yet you have not called on me, Yaiqab; but you have been weary of me, Yasharaal (Israel).

You have not brought me of your sheep for burnt ilah (offerings); neither have you honored me with your zabach (sacrifices). I have not burdened you with manachah (offerings), nor wearied you with frankincense.

You have bought me no sweet cane with kasap (money), nor have you filled me with the fat of your zabach (sacrifices); but you have burdened me with your chataah (sins). You have wearied me with your iwan (iniquities).
I, even I, am he who machah (blots) out your pashai (transgressions) for my own sake; and I will not zakar (remember) your chataah (sins).
zakar (put) me in remembrance. Let us shapat (plead) together. Set forth your case, that you may be justified.
Your raashawan (first) ab (father) sinned, and your Lawatz have transgressed against me.
Therefore I will chalal (profane) the shar (princes) of the qadash (sanctuary); and I will nathan (make) Yaiqab a charam (curse), and Yasharaal (Israel) an insult.
Yet listen now, Yaiqab my ibad (servant), and Yasharaal (Israel), whom I have chosen.
This is what Yahawah who made you, and formed you from the womb, who will help you amar (says): "Don't be yaraa (afraid), Yaiqab my ibad (servant); and you, Yasharawan, whom I have chosen.

For I will pour mayam (water) Tzamaa him who is thirsty, and nazal (streams) on the dry yabashah (dry land). I will pour my rawach (spirit) on your zarai (seed), and my barakah (blessing) on your tzaatzaa (offspring):
and they will spring up among the grass, as willows by the watercourses.

One will amar (say), ‘I am yahawah (yahweh's);' and another will be called by the sham (name) of Yaiqab; and another will kathab (write) with his yad (hand) ‘to Yahawah,' and honor the sham (name) of Yasharaal (Israel).

This is what Yahawah, the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), and his gaal (redeemer), Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), amar (says): "I am the raashawan (first), and I am the Acharawan; and balaiday (besides) me there is no Alahayam.

Who is like me? Who will qaraa (call), and will nagad (declare) it, and set it in order for me, since I established the ancient im (people)? Let them nagad (declare) the things that are coming, and that will happen.

Don't pachad (fear), neither be afraid. Haven't I declared it to you long ago, and shown it? You are my witnesses. Is there a Alawah balaiday (besides) me? Indeed, there is not. I don't yadai (know) any other tzawar (rock).

Everyone who makes an engraved pasal (image) is thahaw (vain). The things that they delight in will not yail (profit). Their own witnesses don't raah (see), nor yadai (know), that they may be disappointed.
Who has fashioned a Al, or molds an pasal (image) that is profitable for balathay (nothing)?
Behold, all his fellows will be disappointed; and the workmen are mere men. Let them all be gathered together. Let them imad (stand) up. They will pachad (fear). They will be put to shame together.

The blacksmith takes an axe, pail (works) in the coals, fashions it with hammers, and pail (works) it with his strong zarawai (arm). He is Raib, and his kach (strength) fails; he drinks no mayam (water), and is Yaip.

The carpenter stretches out a line. He marks it out with a pencil. He shapes it with planes. He marks it out with compasses, and shapes it like the thabanayath (figure) of a ayash (man), with the thapaarah (beauty) of a adam (man), to reside in a bayath (house).

He karath (cuts) down cedars for himself, and takes the cypress and the oak, and amatz (strengthens) for himself one among the itz (trees) of the Yair. He plants a fir tree, and the rain nourishes it.

Then it will be for a adam (man) to bair (burn); and he takes some of it, and warms himself. Yes, he bair (burns) it, and bakes lacham (bread). Yes, he pail (makes) a Al, and shachah (worships) it; he ishah (makes) it an engraved pasal (image), and falls down to it.

He sharap (burns) chatzay (part) of it in the ash (fire). With chatzay (part) of it, he akal (eats) meat. He roasts a roast, and is satisfied. Yes, he warms himself, and amar (says), "Aha! I am warm. I have seen the awar (fire).

The shaarayath (rest) of it he ishah (makes) into a Al, even his engraved pasal (image). He bows down to it and shachah (worships), and palal (prays) to it, and amar (says), "natzal (deliver) me; for you are my Al!
They don't yadai (know), neither do they bayan (consider): for he has shut their iyan (eyes), that they can't raah (see); and their labah (hearts), that they can't shakal (understand).

No one thinks, neither is there daith (knowledge) nor thabawan (understanding) to amar (say), "I have burned chatzay (part) of it in the ash (fire). Yes, I have also baked lacham (bread) on its coals. I have roasted meat and eaten it. Shall I ishah (make) the yathar (rest) of it into an thawaibah (abomination)? Shall I bow down to a itz (tree) trunk?
He raih (feeds) on ashes. A deceived lab (heart) has turned him natah (aside); and he can't natzal (deliver) his napash (soul), nor amar (say), "Isn't there a lie in my right yamayan (hand)?
zakar (remember) these things, Yaiqab and Yasharaal (Israel); for you are my ibad (servant). I have formed you. You are my ibad (servant). Yasharaal (Israel), you will not be forgotten by me.
I have blotted out, as a thick cloud, your pashai (transgressions), and, as a cloud, your chataah (sins). shawab (turn back / repent) to me, for I have redeemed you.

Sing, you shamayam (heavens), for Yahawah has done it! rawai (shout), you lower Thachathay of the aratz (earth)! Break out into singing, you har (mountains), O Yair, all of your itz (trees), for Yahawah has redeemed Yaiqab, and will paar (glorify) himself in Yasharaal (Israel).

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, your gaal (redeemer), and he who formed you from the womb: "I am Yahawah, who ishah (makes) all things; who alone stretches out the shamayam (heavens); who natah (spreads) out the aratz (earth) by myself;
who parar (frustrates) the awath (signs) of the liars, and makes diviners halal (mad); who shawab (turn back / repent) chakam (wise) men backward, and makes their daith (knowledge) foolish;

who qawam (confirms) the dabar (word) of his ibad (servant), and shalam (performs) the itzah (counsel) of his malaak (messengers); who amar (says) of Yarawashalam, ‘She will be inhabited;' and of the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), ‘They will be built,' and ‘I will qawam (raise) up its waste places;'
who amar (says) to the deep, ‘Be charab (dry),' and ‘I will yabash (dry) up your nahar (rivers);'

Who amar (says) of Kawarash, ‘He is my raih (shepherd), and shall shalam (perform) all my Chapatz,' even saying of Yarawashalam, ‘She will be built;' and of the hayakal (temple), ‘Your yasad (foundation) will be laid.'

Thus amar (says) Yahawah to his mashayach (anointed), to Kawarash, whose right yamayan (hand) I have held, to subdue gawayam (nations) panayam (before) him, and strip malak (kings) of their armor; to pathach (open) the doors panayam (before) him, and the gates shall not be shut:
"I will yalak (go) panayam (before) you, and yashar (make) the rough places smooth. I will break the doors of brass in shabar (pieces), and cut apart the bars of barazal (iron).

I will nathan (give) you the treasures of chashak (darkness), and hidden riches of secret places, that you may yadai (know) that it is I, Yahawah, who qaraa (call) you by your sham (name), even the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel).
For Yaiqab my ibad (servant's) sake, and Yasharaal (Israel) my Bachayar, I have called you by your sham (name). I have surnamed you, though you have not yadai (known) me.
I am Yahawah, and there is none else. zawalah (besides) me, there is no Alahayam. I will strengthen you, though you have not yadai (known) me;
that they may yadai (know) from the rising of the shamash (sun), and from the west, that there is apas (none) balaiday (besides) me. I am Yahawah, and there is no one else.
I form the awar (light), and baraa (create) chashak (darkness). I ishah (make) shalawam (peace), and baraa (create) rai (calamity). I am Yahawah, who does all these things.

Distil, you shamayam (heavens), from above, and let the shachaq (skies) nazal (pour) down tzadaq (righteousness). Let the aratz (earth) pathach (open), that it may bring forth yashai (salvation), and let it cause tzadaqah (righteousness) to spring up with it. I, Yahawah, have created it.

Woe to him who rayab (strives) with his Maker— a clay pot among the clay pots of the adamah (earth)! Shall the clay ask him who fashions it, ‘What are you making?' or your pail (work), ‘He has no yad (hands)?'
Woe to him who amar (says) to a ab (father), ‘What have you become the father of?' or to a mother, ‘To what have you given birth?'

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel), and his Maker: "You shaal (ask) me about the things that are to come, concerning my ban (sons), and you tzawah (command) me concerning the pail (work) of my yad (hands)!
I have made the aratz (earth), and created adam (man) on it. I, even my yad (hands), have stretched out the shamayam (heavens); and I have tzawah (commanded) all their tzabaa (army).

I have raised him up in tzadaq (righteousness), and I will make yashar (straight) all his darak (ways). He shall banah (build) my Iyar, and he shall let my exiles shalach (go) free, not for price nor shachad (reward)," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: "The yagayai (labor) of Matzarayam, and the merchandise of Kawash, and the Sabaay (Sabeans), men of stature, shall ibar (come) over to you, and they shall be yours. They will yalak (go) achar (after) you. They shall ibar (come) over in chains; and they will shachah (bow) down to you. They will palal (make) supplication to you: ‘Surely Alahayam is in you; and there is apas (none) else. There is no other Alahayam.
Most certainly you are a Al who hidden yourself, Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), the Savior.'
They will be disappointed, yes, kalam (confounded), all of them. Those who are makers of idols will halak (go) into kalamah (confusion) together.
Yasharaal (Israel) will be saved by Yahawah with an iwalam (forever) thashawaih (salvation). You will not be disappointed nor confounded to ages id (everlasting).

For thus amar (says) Yahawah who created the shamayam (heavens), the Alahayam who formed the aratz (earth) and made it, who established it and didn't baraa (create) it a thahaw (waste), who formed it to be inhabited: "I am Yahawah; and there is no other.

I have not spoken in secret, in a place of the aratz (land) of chashak (darkness). I didn't amar (say) to the zarai (seed) of Yaiqab, ‘Seek me in thahaw (vain).' I, Yahawah, dabar (speak) tzadaq (righteousness). I nagad (declare) things that are mayashar (right).

"Assemble yourselves and bawaa (come). Draw near together, you who have escaped from the gawayam (nations). Those have no yadai (knowledge) who nashaa (carry) the itz (wood) of their engraved pasal (image), and palal (pray) to a Al that can't yashai (save).

nagad (declare) and present it. Yes, let them take yaitz (counsel) together. Who has shown this from qadam (ancient) time? Who has declared it of old? Haven't I, Yahawah? There is no other Alahayam balaiday (besides) me, a tzadayaq (just) Al and a Savior; There is no ayan (one) zawalah (besides) me.
"panah (look) to me, and be saved, all the apas (ends) of the aratz (earth); for I am Al, and there is no other.

I have sworn by myself, the dabar (word) has gone out of my pah (mouth) in tzadaqah (righteousness), and will not shawab (turn back / repent), that to me every knee shall bow, every lashawan (tongue) shall take an shabai (oath).

They will amar (say) of me, ‘There is tzadaqah (righteousness) and iz (strength) only in Yahawah.'" Even to him shall men bawaa (come); and all those who were charah (incensed) against him shall be disappointed.
In Yahawah shall all the zarai (seed) of Yasharaal (Israel) be justified, and shall glory.
Bal bows down, Nabaw stoops; their itzab (idols) are on the animals, and on the livestock: the things that you carried about are made a load, a mashaa (burden) to the Iyap.
They stoop, they bow down together; they could not malat (deliver) the mashaa (burden), but themselves have gone into Shabay.

"Listen to me, bayath (house) of Yaiqab, and all the shaarayath (remnant) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), that have been borne from their birth, that have been carried from the racham (womb);
and even to old age I am he, and even to shayabah (gray) hairs will I carry you. I have made, and I will nashaa (bear); yes, I will carry, and will malat (deliver).
"To whom will you liken me, and make me equal, and compare me, that we may be like?
Some pour out gold from the bag, and weigh kasap (silver) in the balance. They hire a goldsmith, and he ishah (makes) it a Al. They fall down—yes, they shachah (worship).

They nashaa (bear) it on the shoulder, they carry it, and yanach (set) it in its place, and it imad (stands), from its place it shall not move: yes, tzaiq (one) may cry to it, yet it can not answer, nor yashai (save) him out of his tzarah (trouble).
"zakar (remember) this, and ayash (show) yourselves men; shawab (turn back / repent) it again to lab (mind), you transgressors.
zakar (remember) the raashawan (former) things of old: for I am Al, and there is none else; I am Alahayam, and there is apas (none) like me;

nagad (declaring) the acharayath (end) from the raashayath (beginning), and from qadam (ancient) times things that are not yet done; saying, My itzah (counsel) shall qawam (stand), and I will do all my Chapatz;
calling a ravenous bird from the east, the ayash (man) of my itzah (counsel) from a far aratz (country); yes, I have spoken, I will also bawaa (bring) it to pass; I have purposed, I will also do it.
Listen to me, you abayar (stout-hearted), who are Rachawaq from tzadaqah (righteousness):

I qarab (bring) near my tzadaqah (righteousness), it shall not be rachaq (far) off, and my thashawaih (salvation) shall not wait; and I will nathan (place) thashawaih (salvation) in Tzayawan for Yasharaal (Israel) my glory.

"yarad (come) down, and yashab (sit) in the ipar (dust), virgin bath (daughter) of Babal; yashab (sit) on the aratz (ground) without a kasaa (throne), bath (daughter) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans): for you shall no more be called Rak and Inag.
Take the millstones, and grind meal; galah (remove) your tzamah (veil), strip off the train, galah (uncover) the leg, ibar (pass) through the nahar (rivers).
Your irawah (nakedness) shall be uncovered, yes, your shame shall be seen: I will take vengeance, and will spare no adam (man).
Our gaal (redeemer), Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) is his sham (name), the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).
"yashab (sit) in silence, and bawaa (go) into chashak (darkness), bath (daughter) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans); for you shall no more be called the mistress of mamalakah (kingdoms).

I was qatzap (angry) with my im (people), I profaned my nachalah (inheritance), and gave them into your yad (hand): you showed them no racham (mercy); on the zaqan (aged) you have very kabad (heavily) laid your yoke.
You said, ‘I shall be a mistress iwalam (forever);' so that you did not shawam (lay) these things to your lab (heart), nor did you zakar (remember) the acharayath (latter) end of it.

"Now therefore hear this, you who are Idayan to pleasures, who yashab (sit) securely, who amar (say) in your labab (heart), ‘I am, and there is apas (none) else besides me; I shall not yashab (sit) as a alamanah (widow), neither shall I yadai (know) the loss of children:'

but these shanayam (two) things shall bawaa (come) to you in a moment in one yawam (day), the loss of children, and widowhood; in their tham (full) measure shall they bawaa (come) on you, in the multitude of your sorceries, and the maad (great) itzamah (abundance) of your enchantments.

For you have trusted in your wickedness; you have said, No one raah (see) me; your chakamah (wisdom) and your daith (knowledge), it has perverted you, and you have said in your lab (heart), I am, and there is apas (none) else besides me.

Therefore rai (evil) will bawaa (come) on you; you won't yadai (know) when it dawns: and mischief will napal (fall) on you; you will not be yakal (able) to kapar (put) it away: and shawaa (desolation) shall bawaa (come) on you suddenly, which you don't yadai (know).

"imad (stand) now with your enchantments, and with the multitude of your sorceries, in which you have labored from your youth; if so be you shall be yakal (able) to yail (profit), if so be you may iratz (prevail).

You are wearied in the multitude of your itzah (counsels): let now the astrologers, the chazah (stargazers), the chadash (monthly) yadai (prognosticators), imad (stand) up, and yashai (save) you from the things that shall bawaa (come) on you.

Behold, they shall be as stubble; the ash (fire) shall sharap (burn) them; they shall not natzal (deliver) themselves from the yad (power) of the lahabah (flame): it shall not be a coal to warm at, nor a awar (fire) to yashab (sit) before.

Thus shall the things be to you in which you have labored: those who have trafficked with you from your youth shall thaih (wander) everyone to his ibar (quarter); there shall be none to yashai (save) you.

"Hear this, bayath (house) of Yaiqab, you who are called by the sham (name) of Yasharaal (Israel), and have yatzaa (come) forth out of the mayam (waters) of Yahawadah (Judah); who shabai (swear) by the sham (name) of Yahawah, and zakar (make) mention of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), but not in truth, nor in tzadaqah (righteousness)
(for they qaraa (call) themselves of the qadash (holy) Iyar, and samak (stay) themselves on the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel); Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) is his sham (name)):
I have declared the raashawan (former) things from of old; yes, they went yatzaa (forth) out of my pah (mouth), and I showed them: suddenly I did them, and they happened.
Because I knew that you are Qashah, and your neck is an barazal (iron) sinew, and your brow brass;

therefore I have declared it to you from of old; before it came to bawaa (pass) I showed it to you; lest you should amar (say), ‘My itzab (idol) has done them, and my engraved pasal (image), and my molten nasak (image), has tzawah (commanded) them.'
You have heard it; chazah (see) all this; and you, will you not nagad (declare) it? "I have shown you new things from this time, even hidden things, which you have not yadai (known).
They are created now, and not from of panayam (old); and before this yawam (day) you didn't hear them; lest you should amar (say), ‘Behold, I knew them.'
Yes, you didn't hear; yes, you didn't yadai (know); yes, from of old your ear was not opened: for I knew that you dealt very bagad (treacherously), and was called a transgressor from the womb.
For my sham (name's) sake will I defer my ap (anger), and for my thahalah (praise) will I refrain for you, that I not karath (cut) you off.
Behold, I have refined you, but not as kasap (silver); I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.
For my own sake, for my own sake, will I do it; for how should my name be profaned? I will not nathan (give) my kabawad (glory) to achar (another).
"Listen to me, O Yaiqab, and Yasharaal (Israel) my called: I am he; I am the raashawan (first), I also am the Acharawan.
Yes, my yad (hand) has laid the yasad (foundation) of the aratz (earth), and my right yamayan (hand) has spread out the shamayam (heavens): when I qaraa (call) to them, they imad (stand) up together.

"Assemble yourselves, all you, and hear; who among them has declared these things? He whom Yahawah ahab (loves) shall ishah (perform) his Chapatz on Babal, and his zarawai (arm) shall be on the Kashaday (Chaldeans).
I, even I, have spoken; yes, I have called him; I have brought him, and he shall make his darak (way) prosperous.

"qarab (come) qarab (near) to me and hear this: "From the raash (beginning) I have not spoken in secret; from the ith (time) that it was, there am I." Now the Adanay Yahawah has sent me, with his rawach (spirit).

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, your gaal (redeemer), the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel): I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who teaches you to yail (profit), who leads you by the darak (way) that you should yalak (go).
Oh that you had listened to my matzawah (commandments)! then your shalawam (peace) would have been like a nahar (river), and your tzadaqah (righteousness) like the waves of the yam (sea):
your zarai (seed) also had been as the sand, and the tzaatzaa (offspring) of your body like its grains: his sham (name) would not be karath (cut) off nor destroyed from panayam (before) me.

yatzaa (go) forth from Babal, flee from the Kashaday (Chaldeans); with a qawal (voice) of singing nagad (declare), tell this, yatzaa (utter) it even to the end of the aratz (earth): amar (say), Yahawah has redeemed his ibad (servant) Yaiqab.

They didn't thirst when he led them through the deserts; he caused the mayam (waters) to nazal (flow) out of the tzawar (rock) for them; he split the tzawar (rock) also, and the mayam (waters) gushed out.
"There is no shalawam (peace)," amar (says) Yahawah, "for the rashai (wicked).
Listen, islands, to me; and listen, you laam (peoples), from Rachawaq: Yahawah has called me from the womb; from the maih (bowels) of my am (mother) has he made zakar (mention) of my sham (name):
and he has made my pah (mouth) like a Chad charab (sword); in the shadow of his yad (hand), he has hidden me: and he has made me a Barar chatz (shaft); in his quiver has he kept me close:
and he said to me, "You are my ibad (servant); Yasharaal (Israel), in whom I will be glorified.
But I said, "I have labored in vain, I have spent my kach (strength) for thahaw (nothing) and vanity; yet surely the justice due to me is with Yahawah, and my pailah (reward) with my Alahayam.

Now amar (says) Yahawah who formed me from the womb to be his ibad (servant), to shawab (turn back / repent) Yaiqab again to him, and that Yasharaal (Israel) be gathered to him (for I am honorable in the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, and my Alahayam has become my iz (strength));

yes, he amar (says), "It is too qalal (light) a thing that you should be my ibad (servant) to qawam (raise) up the shabat (tribes) of Yaiqab, and to shawab (turn back / repent) the preserved of Yasharaal (Israel): I will also nathan (give) you for a awar (light) to the gawayam (nations), that you may be my yashawaih (salvation) to the end of the aratz (earth).

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the gaal (redeemer) of Yasharaal (Israel), and his qadawash (holy) One, to him whom napash (man) despises, to him whom the gaway (nation) abhors, to a ibad (servant) of rulers: "malak (kings) shall raah (see) and qawam (arise); shar (princes), and they shall shachah (worship); because of Yahawah who is aman (faithful), even the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel), who has chosen you.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "In an acceptable ith (time) have I answered you, and in a yawam (day) of yashawaih (salvation) have I helped you; and I will preserve you, and nathan (give) you for a barayath (covenant) of the im (people), to qawam (raise) up the aratz (land), to nachal (make) them inherit the shamam (desolate) nachalah (heritage):

saying to those who are bound, ‘yatzaa (come) out!'; to those who are in chashak (darkness), ‘Show yourselves!' "They shall raih (feed) in the darak (ways), and on all bare heights shall be their pasture.

They shall not hunger nor thirst; neither shall the sharab (heat) nor shamash (sun) strike them: for he who has racham (mercy) on them will lead them, even by springs of mayam (water) he will guide them.
I will shawam (make) all my har (mountains) a darak (way), and my masalah (highways) shall be exalted.
Behold, these shall bawaa (come) from Rachawaq; and behold, these from the tzapawan (north) and from the yam (west); and these from the aratz (land) of Sayanayam.
Sing, shamayam (heavens); and be joyful, aratz (earth); and break forth into singing, har (mountains): for Yahawah has comforted his im (people), and will have racham (compassion) on his Inay.
But Tzayawan said, "Yahawah has forsaken me, and the Adawan has forgotten me.
"Can a ashah (woman) forget her nursing child, that she should not have racham (compassion) on the ban (son) of her womb? Yes, these may forget, yet I will not forget you!
Behold, I have engraved you on the palms of my kap (hands); your walls are continually before me.
Your children make haste; your destroyers and those who made you charab (waste) shall yatzaa (go) forth from you.

nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eyes) all around, and raah (see): all these gather themselves together, and bawaa (come) to you. As I chay (live)," says Yahawah, "you shall surely Labash yourself with them all as with an iday (ornament), and dress yourself with them, like a kalah (bride).

"For, as for your waste and your shamam (desolate) places, and your aratz (land) that has been destroyed, surely now you shall be too small for the yashab (inhabitants), and those who swallowed you up shall be rachaq (far) away.
The children of your bereavement shall yet amar (say) in your ears, The place is too tzar (small) for me; give place to me that I may yashab (dwell).

Then you will amar (say) in your labab (heart), ‘Who has conceived these for me, since I have been bereaved of my shakal (children), and am Galamawad, an galah (exile), and wandering sawar (back) and forth? Who has brought up these? Behold, I was shaar (left) ayapah (alone); these, where were they?'

Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah, "Behold, I will nashaa (lift) up my yad (hand) to the gawayam (nations), and set up my nas (banner) to the im (peoples); and they shall bawaa (bring) your ban (sons) in their bosom, and your bath (daughters) shall be carried on their shoulders.

malak (kings) shall be your nursing fathers, and their sharah (queens) your nursing yanaq (mothers): they shall shachah (bow) down to you with their ap (faces) to the aratz (earth), and lick the ipar (dust) of your feet; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah; and those who wait for me shall not be disappointed.
Shall the prey be taken from the gabawar (mighty), or the tzadayaq (lawful) Shabay be delivered?

But thus amar (says) Yahawah, "Even the Shabay of the gabawar (mighty) shall be taken away, and the prey of the irayatz (terrible) shall be delivered; for I will rayab (contend) with him who rayab (contends) with you, and I will yashai (save) your children.

I will akal (feed) those who yanah (oppress) you with their own flesh; and they shall be Shakar with their own dam (blood), as with sweet isayas (wine): and all flesh shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, am your Savior, and your gaal (redeemer), the abayar (mighty) One of Yaiqab.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "Where is the bill of your am (mother's) divorce, with which I have shalach (put) her away? or which of my creditors is it to whom I have sold you? Behold, for your iwan (iniquities) were you sold, and for your pashai (transgressions) was your am (mother) shalach (put) away.

Why, when I came, was there no ayash (man)? when I called, was there none to answer? Is my yad (hand) shortened at all, that it can't padawath (redeem)? or have I no kach (power) to natzal (deliver)? Behold, at my rebuke I charab (dry) up the yam (sea), I shawam (make) the nahar (rivers) a madabar (wilderness): their fish baash (stink), because there is no mayam (water), and mawath (die) for thirst.
I Labash the shamayam (heavens) with blackness, and I shawam (make) sackcloth their covering.

The Adanay Yahawah has given me the lashawan (tongue) of those who are Lamawad, that I may yadai (know) how to sustain with dabar (words) him who is Yaip: he wakens baqar (morning) by baqar (morning), he wakens my ear to hear as those who are Lamawad.
The Adanay Yahawah has opened my ear, and I was not rebellious, neither turned sawag (away) backward.
I gave my back to the strikers, and my Lachay to those who plucked off the hair; I didn't hide my panayam (face) from kalamah (shame) and spitting.
For the Adanay Yahawah will help me; therefore I have not been kalam (confounded): therefore have I shawam (set) my panayam (face) like a flint, and I yadai (know) that I shall not be disappointed.
He is qarawab (near) who justifies me; who will bring charges against me? Let us imad (stand) up together: who is my adversary? Let him come near to me.
Behold, the Adanay Yahawah will help me; who is he who shall rashai (condemn) me? Behold, all they shall wax old as a bagad (garment), the moth shall akal (eat) them up.

Who is among you who yaraa (fears) Yahawah, who obeys the qawal (voice) of his ibad (servant)? He who halak (walks) in chashakah (darkness), and has no nagah (light), let him batach (trust) in the sham (name) of Yahawah, and shain (rely) on his Alahayam.

Behold, all you who qadach (kindle) a ash (fire), who adorn yourselves with torches around yourselves; yalak (walk) in the flame of your ash (fire), and among the brands that you have kindled. You shall have this of my yad (hand); you shall shakab (lie) down in sorrow.
"Listen to me, you who follow after tzadaq (righteousness), you who seek Yahawah: look to the tzawar (rock) you were chatzab (cut) from, and to the hold of the bawar (pit) you were dug from.
Look to Abaraham your ab (father), and to Sharah who bore you; for when he was but one I called him, and I blessed him, and made him many.

For Yahawah has comforted Tzayawan; he has comforted all her waste places, and has made her madabar (wilderness) like Idan, and her irabah (desert) like the Gan of Yahawah; joy and gladness shall be found therein, thanksgiving, and the qawal (voice) of melody.
"Attend to me, my im (people); and give ear to me, my laam (nation): for a thawarah (law) shall yatzaa (go) forth from me, and I will establish my justice for a awar (light) of the im (peoples).

My tzadaq (righteousness) is qarawab (near), my yashai (salvation) is gone yatzaa (forth), and my zarawai (arms) shall shapat (judge) the im (peoples); the islands shall wait for me, and on my zarawai (arm) shall they trust.

nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eyes) to the shamayam (heavens), and look on the aratz (earth) beneath; for the shamayam (heavens) shall vanish away like ishan (smoke), and the aratz (earth) shall wax old like a bagad (garment); and those who yashab (dwell) therein shall mawath (die) in the same kan (way): but my yashawaih (salvation) shall be iwalam (forever), and my tzadaqah (righteousness) shall not be abolished.
"Listen to me, you who yadai (know) tzadaq (righteousness), the im (people) in whose lab (heart) is my thawarah (law); don't yaraa (fear) the reproach of men, neither be dismayed at their insults.

For the moth shall akal (eat) them up like a bagad (garment), and the worm shall akal (eat) them like wool; but my tzadaqah (righteousness) shall be iwalam (forever), and my yashawaih (salvation) to all dawar (generations).

Awake, awake, Labash on iz (strength), zarawai (arm) of Yahawah; awake, as in the yawam (days) of old, the dawar (generations) of qadam (ancient) times. Isn't it you who chatzab (cut) Rahab in pieces, who pierced the thanayan (monster)?
Isn't it you who dried up the yam (sea), the mayam (waters) of the rab (great) deep; who made the depths of the yam (sea) a darak (way) for the redeemed to ibar (pass) over?

The ransomed of Yahawah shall shawab (turn back / repent), and bawaa (come) with singing to Tzayawan; and iwalam (forever) joy shall be on their raash (heads). They shall obtain gladness and joy. Sorrow and sighing shall flee away.
"I, even I, am he who nacham (comforts) you: who are you, that you are yaraa (afraid) of anawash (man) who shall mawath (die), and of the ban (son) of adam (man) who shall be made as grass;

and have forgotten Yahawah your Maker, who stretched natah (forth) the shamayam (heavens), and laid the yasad (foundations) of the aratz (earth); and pachad (fear) continually all the yawam (day) panayam (because) of the fury of the oppressor, when he kawan (makes) ready to shachath (destroy)? and where is the fury of the oppressor?
The captive exile shall speedily be freed; and he shall not mawath (die) and go down into the shachath (pit), neither shall his lacham (bread) fail.
For I am Yahawah your Alahayam, who stirs up the yam (sea), so that its waves roar: Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) is his sham (name).

I have shawam (put) my dabar (words) in your pah (mouth), and have covered you in the shadow of my yad (hand), that I may plant the shamayam (heavens), and yasad (lay) the foundations of the aratz (earth), and amar (tell) Tzayawan, ‘You are my im (people).'
Awake, awake, qawam (stand) up, Yarawashalam, that have drunk at the yad (hand) of Yahawah the cup of his chamah (wrath); you have drunken the bowl of the cup of staggering, and drained it.
There is none to guide her among all the ban (sons) whom she has brought yalad (forth); neither is there any who chazaq (takes) her by the yad (hand) among all the ban (sons) who she has brought up.
These shanayam (two) things have happened to you. Who will nawad (bemoan) you? Desolation and destruction, and the famine and the charab (sword); how shall I nacham (comfort) you?
Your ban (sons) have fainted, they shakab (lie) at the raash (head) of all the streets, as an antelope in a net; they are Malaa of the chamah (wrath) of Yahawah, the rebuke of your Alahayam.
Therefore hear now this, you Inay, and Shakar, but not with yayan (wine):

Thus amar (says) your Adawan Yahawah, and your Alahayam who rayab (pleads) the cause of his im (people), "Behold, I have taken out of your yad (hand) the cup of staggering, even the bowl of the cup of my chamah (wrath); you shall no more drink it again:

and I will shawam (put) it into the yad (hand) of those who afflict you, who have said to your napash (soul), ‘shachah (bow) down, that we may walk over you;' and you have laid your back as the aratz (ground), and as the street, to those who walk over.

Awake, awake, Labash on your iz (strength), Tzayawan; Labash on your thapaarah (beautiful) bagad (garments), Yarawashalam, the qadash (holy) Iyar: for henceforth there shall no more bawaa (come) into you the Iral and the tamaa (unclean).
Shake yourself from the ipar (dust)! qawam (arise), yashab (sit) up, Yarawashalam! Release yourself from the bonds of your neck, Shabay bath (daughter) of Tzayawan!
For thus amar (says) Yahawah, "You were sold for nothing; and you shall be redeemed without kasap (money).
For thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah, "My im (people) went down at the raashawan (first) into Matzarayam to live there: and the Ashawar (Assyrian) has oppressed them apas (without) cause.

"Now therefore, what do I do here," says Yahawah, "seeing that my im (people) are taken away for nothing? Those who mashal (rule) over them mock," says Yahawah, "and my sham (name) continually all the yawam (day) is blasphemed.
Therefore my im (people) shall yadai (know) my sham (name). Therefore they shall know in that yawam (day) that I am he who dabar (speaks); behold, it is I.

How beautiful on the har (mountains) are the feet of him who brings bashar (good) news, who publishes shalawam (peace), who brings bashar (good) news of tawab (good), who publishes yashawaih (salvation), who amar (says) to Tzayawan, "Your Alahayam malak (reigns)!

The qawal (voice) of your watchmen! they nashaa (lift) up the qawal (voice), together do they sing; for they shall raah (see) iyan (eye) to iyan (eye), when Yahawah shawab (turn back / repent) to Tzayawan.
Break forth into joy, sing together, you waste places of Yarawashalam; for Yahawah has comforted his im (people), he has redeemed Yarawashalam.

Yahawah has made chashap (bare) his qadash (holy) zarawai (arm) in the iyan (eyes) of all the gawayam (nations); and all the apas (ends) of the aratz (earth) have seen the yashawaih (salvation) of our Alahayam.

sawar (depart), sawar (depart), yatzaa (go) out from there, nagai (touch) no tamaa (unclean) thing! yatzaa (go) out of the midst of her! Barar yourselves, you who nashaa (bear) the vessels of Yahawah.
For you shall not yatzaa (go) out in haste, neither shall you halak (go) by flight: for Yahawah will halak (go) panayam (before) you; and the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) will be your rear guard.
Behold, my ibad (servant) shall deal shakal (wisely), he shall be exalted and lifted up, and shall be very high.
Like as many were astonished at you (his appearance was marred more than any ayash (man), and his form more than the ban (sons) of men),

so shall he sprinkle many gawayam (nations); malak (kings) shall qapatz (shut) their pah (mouths) at him: for that which had not been told them shall they raah (see); and that which they had not heard shall they bayan (understand).
Who has believed our message? To whom has the zarawai (arm) of Yahawah been revealed?

For he grew up panayam (before) him as a tender plant, and as a root out of tzayah (dry) aratz (ground). He has no thaar (good) looks or hadar (majesty). When we raah (see) him, there is no beauty that we should desire him.
He was despised, and Chadal by men; a ayash (man) of suffering, and acquainted with disease. He was despised as one from whom men hide their panayam (face); and we didn't respect him.
Surely he has borne our sickness, and carried our suffering; yet we considered him plagued, struck by Alahayam, and afflicted.
But he was pierced for our pashai (transgressions). He was crushed for our iwan (iniquities). The punishment that brought our shalawam (peace) was on him; and by his wounds we are healed.
All we like sheep have gone thaih (astray). Everyone has turned to his own darak (way); and Yahawah has laid on him the iwan (iniquity) of us all.

He was oppressed, yet when he was afflicted he didn't pathach (open) his pah (mouth). As a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and as a sheep that panayam (before) its shearers is mute, so he didn't pathach (open) his pah (mouth).

He was taken away by oppression and mashapat (judgment); and as for his dawar (generation), who considered that he was cut off out of the aratz (land) of the chay (living) and nagai (stricken) for the disobedience of my im (people)?
They made his qabar (grave) with the rashai (wicked), and with a Ishayar man in his mawath (death); although he had done no violence, neither was any deceit in his pah (mouth).

Yet it pleased Yahawah to dakaa (bruise) him. He has caused him to suffer. When you shawam (make) his napash (soul) an offering for asham (sin), he shall raah (see) his zarai (seed). He shall prolong his yawam (days), and the Chapatz of Yahawah shall tzalach (prosper) in his yad (hand).

After the suffering of his napash (soul), he will raah (see) the shabai (light) and be satisfied. My tzadayaq (righteous) ibad (servant) will justify many by the daith (knowledge) of himself; and he will bear their iwan (iniquities).

Therefore will I divide him a portion with the rab (great), and he shall divide the spoil with the itzawam (strong); because he poured out his napash (soul) to mawath (death), and was numbered with the transgressors; yet he bore the chataa (sin) of many, and made pagai (intercession) for the transgressors.

"Sing, Iqar, you who didn't yalad (bear); break forth into singing, and cry aloud, you who did not chawal (travail) with child: for more are the children of the shamam (desolate) than the children of the married wife," amar (says) Yahawah.
"Enlarge the place of your ahal (tent), and let them natah (stretch) forth the curtains of your mashakan (habitations); don't spare: lengthen your cords, and chazaq (strengthen) your stakes.

For you shall spread out on the right yamayan (hand) and on the shamaawal (left); and your zarai (seed) shall yarash (possess) the gawayam (nations), and shamam (make) the desolate Iyar to be inhabited.

"Don't be yaraa (afraid); for you shall not be bawash (ashamed): neither be kalam (confounded); for you shall not be disappointed: for you shall forget the chapar (shame) of your youth; and the reproach of your widowhood you shall zakar (remember) no more.

For your Maker is your bail (husband); Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) is his sham (name): and the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel) is your gaal (redeemer); the Alahayam of the whole aratz (earth) shall he be called.
For Yahawah has called you as a ashah (wife) forsaken and grieved in rawach (spirit), even a ashah (wife) of youth, when she is cast off," amar (says) your Alahayam.
"For a qatan (small) moment have I forsaken you; but with gadawal (great) racham (mercies) will I gather you.

In overflowing qatzap (wrath) I hid my panayam (face) from you for a moment; but with iwalam (forever) loving chasad (kindness) will I have racham (mercy) on you," amar (says) Yahawah your gaal (redeemer).

"For this is like the mayam (waters) of Nach to me; for as I have sworn that the mayam (waters) of Nach shall no more ibar (go) over the aratz (earth), so have I sworn that I will not be qatzap (angry) with you, nor rebuke you.

For the har (mountains) may depart, and the Gabaih be removed; but my loving chasad (kindness) shall not depart from you, neither shall my barayath (covenant) of shalawam (peace) be removed," amar (says) Yahawah who has racham (mercy) on you.
"You Inay, tossed with storms, and not comforted, behold, I will set your aban (stones) in beautiful colors, and rabatz (lay) your yasad (foundations) with sapphires.
I will shawam (make) your pinnacles of rubies, and your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls Chapatz precious aban (stones).
All your children shall be Lamawad of Yahawah; and rab (great) shall be the shalawam (peace) of your children.
In tzadaqah (righteousness) you shall be established: you shall be rachaq (far) from oppression, for you shall not be yaraa (afraid); and from terror, for it shall not qarab (come) near you.
Behold, they may gawar (gather) together, but not by me: whoever shall gawar (gather) together against you shall napal (fall) because of you.
"Behold, I have created the smith who napach (blows) the ash (fire) of coals, and yatzaa (brings) forth a weapon for his maishah (work); and I have created the shachath (waster) to chabal (destroy).

No weapon that is formed against you will prevail; and you will rashai (condemn) every lashawan (tongue) that qawam (rises) against you in mashapat (judgment). This is the nachalah (heritage) of the ibad (servants) of Yahawah, and their tzadaqah (righteousness) which is of me," says Yahawah.

"Come, everyone who Tzamaa, to the mayam (waters)! yalak (come), he who has no kasap (money), buy, and akal (eat)! Yes, yalak (come), buy yayan (wine) and milk without kasap (money) and without price.

Why do you spend kasap (money) for that which is not lacham (bread)? and your yagayai (labor) for that which doesn't satisfy? listen diligently to me, and akal (eat) you that which is tawab (good), and let your napash (soul) delight itself in fatness.

natah (turn) your ear, and yalak (come) to me; hear, and your napash (soul) shall chayah (live): and I will karath (make) an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant) with you, even the aman (sure) chasad (mercies) of Dawad.
Behold, I have given him for a witness to the laam (peoples), a nagayad (leader) and commander to the laam (peoples).

Behold, you shall qaraa (call) a gaway (nation) that you don't yadai (know); and a gaway (nation) that didn't yadai (know) you shall run to you, because of Yahawah your Alahayam, and for the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel); for he has glorified you.
Seek Yahawah while he may be found; qaraa (call) you on him while he is qarawab (near):

let the rashai (wicked) forsake his darak (way), and the awan (unrighteous) ayash (man) his machashabah (thoughts); and let him shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah, and he will have racham (mercy) on him; and to our Alahayam, for he will abundantly pardon.
"For my machashabah (thoughts) are not your machashabah (thoughts), neither are your darak (ways) my darak (ways)," says Yahawah.
"For as the shamayam (heavens) are higher than the aratz (earth), so are my darak (ways) higher than your darak (ways), and my machashabah (thoughts) than your machashabah (thoughts).

For as the rain yarad (comes) down and the snow from the sky, and doesn't shawab (turn back / repent) there, but rawah (waters) the aratz (earth), and makes it yalad (bring) forth and bud, and nathan (gives) zarai (seed) to the zarai (sower) and lacham (bread) to the eater;

so shall my dabar (word) be that goes yatzaa (forth) out of my pah (mouth): it shall not shawab (turn back / repent) to me void, but it shall ishah (accomplish) that which I please, and it shall tzalach (prosper) in the thing I sent it to do.

For you shall yatzaa (go) out with joy, and be led forth with shalawam (peace): the har (mountains) and the Gabaih shall break forth panayam (before) you into singing; and all the itz (trees) of the shadah (fields) shall clap their kap (hands).

Instead of the thorn shall ilah (come) up the fir tree; and instead of the brier shall ilah (come) up the myrtle tree: and it shall be to Yahawah for a sham (name), for an iwalam (forever) awath (sign) that shall not be karath (cut) off.
Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "shamar (keep) justice, and do tzadaqah (righteousness); for my yashawaih (salvation) is qarawab (near) to bawaa (come), and my tzadaqah (righteousness) to be revealed.

Blessed is the anawash (man) who does this, and the ban (son) of adam (man) who chazaq (holds) it fast; who shamar (keeps) the shabath (sabbath) from profaning it, and shamar (keeps) his yad (hand) from doing any rai (evil).

Neither let the foreigner, who has joined himself to Yahawah, amar (speak), saying, "Yahawah will surely separate me from his im (people);" neither let the eunuch amar (say), "Behold, I am a Yabash itz (tree).
For thus amar (says) Yahawah, "To the eunuchs who shamar (keep) my shabath (sabbaths), and choose the things that please me, and chazaq (hold) fast my barayath (covenant):

to them I will nathan (give) in my bayath (house) and within my walls a memorial and a sham (name) tawab (better) than of ban (sons) and of bath (daughters); I will nathan (give) them an iwalam (forever) sham (name), that shall not be karath (cut) off.

Also the foreigners who join themselves to Yahawah, to sharath (minister) to him, and to ahab (love) the sham (name) of Yahawah, to be his ibad (servants), everyone who shamar (keeps) the shabath (sabbath) from profaning it, and chazaq (holds) fast my barayath (covenant);

even them will I bawaa (bring) to my qadash (holy) har (mountain), and Shamach them joyful in my bayath (house) of prayer: their burnt ilah (offerings) and their zabach (sacrifices) shall be accepted on my mazabach (altar); for my bayath (house) shall be called a bayath (house) of prayer for all im (peoples).
The Adanay Yahawah, who gathers the outcasts of Yasharaal (Israel), says, "Yet will I gather others to him, besides his own who are gathered.
All you animals of the shadah (field), come to akal (devour), all you animals in the Yair.
His watchmen are iwar (blind), they are all without yadai (knowledge); they are all mute dogs, they can't bark; dreaming, lying down, loving to nawam (slumber).

Yes, the dogs are iz (greedy), they can never have enough; and these are raih (shepherds) who can't bayan (understand): they have all turned to their own darak (way), ayash (each) one to his gain, from every quarter.
"Come," say they, "I will get yayan (wine), and we will fill ourselves with shakar (strong) drink; and tomorrow shall be as this machar (day), maad (great) beyond measure.

The tzadayaq (righteous) perishes, and no ayash (man) shawam (lays) it to lab (heart); and chasad (merciful) men are taken asap (away), none considering that the tzadayaq (righteous) is taken asap (away) from the rai (evil).
He bawaa (enters) into shalawam (peace); they nawach (rest) in their beds, each one who halak (walks) in his Nakach.
"But qarab (draw) near here, you ban (sons) of the sorceress, the zarai (seed) of the naap (adulterer) and the prostitute.
Against whom do you sport yourselves? Against whom do you make a wide pah (mouth), and stick out your lashawan (tongue)? Aren't you children of disobedience, a zarai (seed) of falsehood,
you who inflame yourselves among the oaks, under every Rainan itz (tree); who kill the children in the nachal (valleys), under the clefts of the salai (rocks)?

Among the Chalaq stones of the nachal (valley) is your chalaq (portion); they, they are your lot; you have even poured a drink nasak (offering) to them. You have offered an manachah (offering). Shall I be appeased for these things?
On a nashaa (high) and Gabah har (mountain) you have shawam (set) your bed; there also you went up to zabach (offer) zabach (sacrifice).

achar (behind) the doors and the posts you have shawam (set) up your zakarawan (memorial): for you have uncovered to someone besides me, and have gone up; you have enlarged your bed, and made you a covenant with them: you loved their bed yad (where) you saw it.
You went to the malak (king) with shaman (oil), and increased your perfumes, and sent your tzayar (ambassadors) Rachawaq off, and debased yourself even to shaawal (sheol).
You were wearied with the length of your darak (way); yet you didn't amar (say), ‘It is in vain.' You found a reviving of your yad (strength); therefore you weren't faint.

"Of whom have you been afraid and in yaraa (fear), that you lie, and have not zakar (remembered) me, nor laid it to your lab (heart)? Haven't I held my chashah (peace) even of long time, and you don't yaraa (fear) me?
I will nagad (declare) your tzadaqah (righteousness); and as for your maishah (works), they shall not yail (profit) you.

When you cry, let those who you have gathered natzal (deliver) you; but the rawach (wind) shall take them, a habal (breath) shall nashaa (carry) them all away: but he who takes refuge in me shall nachal (possess) the aratz (land), and shall yarash (inherit) my qadash (holy) har (mountain).
He will amar (say), "Cast up, cast up, panah (prepare) the darak (way), take up the stumbling-block out of the darak (way) of my im (people).

For thus amar (says) the high and nashaa (lofty) One who shakan (inhabits) eternity, whose sham (name) is qadawash (holy): "I shakan (dwell) in the high and qadawash (holy) place, with him also who is of a Dakaa and Shapal rawach (spirit), to chayah (revive) the rawach (spirit) of the Shapal, and to chayah (revive) the lab (heart) of the dakaa (contrite).
For I will not rayab (contend) iwalam (forever), neither will I be natzach (always) qatzap (angry); for the rawach (spirit) would faint panayam (before) me, and the nashamah (souls) who I have made.
For the iwan (iniquity) of his covetousness was I qatzap (angry), and struck him; I hid myself and was qatzap (angry); and he went on shawabab (backsliding) in the darak (way) of his lab (heart).
I have seen his darak (ways), and will heal him: I will lead him also, and shalam (restore) comforts Abal him and to his mourners.
I baraa (create) the fruit of the shapah (lips): shalawam (peace), shalawam (peace), to him who is Rachawaq off and to him who is qarawab (near)," amar (says) Yahawah; "and I will heal them.
But the rashai (wicked) are like the troubled yam (sea); for it can't shaqat (rest), and its mayam (waters) cast up mire and dirt.
"There is no shalawam (peace)," amar (says) my Alahayam, "for the rashai (wicked).

"qaraa (cry) garawan (aloud), don't spare, lift up your qawal (voice) like a trumpet, and nagad (declare) to my im (people) their disobedience, and to the bayath (house) of Yaiqab their chataah (sins).

Yet they seek me yawam (daily), and delight to daith (know) my darak (ways): as a gaway (nation) that did tzadaqah (righteousness), and didn't forsake the mashapat (ordinance) of their Alahayam, they shaal (ask) of me righteous judgments; they delight to draw near to Alahayam.

‘Why have we fasted,' say they, ‘and you don't raah (see)? Why have we afflicted our napash (soul), and you take no yadai (knowledge)?' "Behold, in the yawam (day) of your fast you matzaa (find) Chapatz, and exact all your itzab (labors).
Behold, you fast for rayab (strife) and rayab (contention), and to strike with the fist of rashai (wickedness): you don't fast this yawam (day) so as to make your qawal (voice) to be heard on high.

Is such the fast that I have chosen? the yawam (day) for a adam (man) to afflict his napash (soul)? Is it to bow down his raash (head) as a rush, and to spread sackcloth and ashes under him? Will you qaraa (call) this a fast, and an acceptable yawam (day) to Yahawah?
"Isn't this the fast that I have chosen: to release the bonds of rashai (wickedness), to undo the bands of the yoke, and to let the oppressed shalach (go) Chapashay, and that you break every yoke?

Isn't it to distribute your lacham (bread) to the Raib, and that you bawaa (bring) the Inay who are cast out to your bayath (house)? When you raah (see) the Irawam, that you cover him; and that you not ilam (hide) yourself from your own flesh?

Then your awar (light) shall break forth as the shachar (morning), and your healing shall spring forth speedily; and your tzadaq (righteousness) shall halak (go) panayam (before) you; the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah shall be your rear guard.

Then you shall qaraa (call), and Yahawah will answer; you shall cry, and he will amar (say), ‘Here I am.' "If you sawar (take) away from the midst of you the yoke, the putting shalach (forth) of the finger, and speaking wickedly;

and if you draw out your napash (soul) to the Raib, and satisfy the afflicted napash (soul): then your awar (light) shall zarach (rise) in apalah (darkness), and your chashak (obscurity) be as the noonday;

and Yahawah will guide you continually, and satisfy your napash (soul) in dry places, and chalatz (make) strong your itzam (bones); and you shall be like a Rawah Gan, and like a spring of mayam (water), whose mayam (waters) don't fail.

Those who shall be of you shall banah (build) the old waste places; you shall qawam (raise) up the foundations of many dawar (generations); and you shall be called The repairer of the breach, The restorer of nathayab (paths) to yashab (dwell) in.

"If you shawab (turn back / repent) away your ragal (foot) from the shabath (sabbath), from doing your Chapatz on my qadash (holy) yawam (day); and qaraa (call) the shabath (sabbath) a delight, and the qadawash (holy) of Yahawah honorable; and shall honor it, not doing your own darak (ways), nor finding your own Chapatz, nor speaking your own dabar (words):

then you shall delight yourself in Yahawah; and I will make you to ride on the bamah (high) places of the aratz (earth); and I will akal (feed) you with the nachalah (heritage) of Yaiqab your ab (father):" for the pah (mouth) of Yahawah has spoken it.
Behold, yahawah (yahweh's) yad (hand) is not shortened, that it can't yashai (save); neither his ear kabad (heavy), that it can't hear:
but your iwan (iniquities) have separated between you and your Alahayam, and your chataah (sins) have hidden his panayam (face) from you, so that he will not hear.
For your kap (hands) are defiled with dam (blood), and your fingers with iwan (iniquity); your shapah (lips) have spoken lies, your lashawan (tongue) mutters iwal (wickedness).

None sues in tzadaq (righteousness), and none shapat (pleads) in amawanah (truth): they batach (trust) in thahaw (vanity), and dabar (speak) lies; they conceive imal (mischief), and yalad (bring) forth awan (iniquity).
They hatch adders' eggs, and weave the spider's web: he who akal (eats) of their eggs dies; and that which is crushed breaks out into a viper.

Their webs shall not become bagad (garments), neither shall they cover themselves with their maishah (works): their maishah (works) are maishah (works) of awan (iniquity), and the pail (act) of violence is in their kap (hands).

Their feet run to rai (evil), and they make haste to shed naqay (innocent) dam (blood): their machashabah (thoughts) are machashabah (thoughts) of awan (iniquity); desolation and destruction are in their masalah (paths).

The darak (way) of shalawam (peace) they don't yadai (know); and there is no justice in their maigal (goings): they have made them crooked nathayab (paths); whoever goes therein does not yadai (know) shalawam (peace).

Therefore is justice rachaq (far) from us, neither does tzadaqah (righteousness) overtake us: we look for awar (light), but, behold, chashak (darkness); for brightness, but we halak (walk) in obscurity.
We grope for the wall like the iwar (blind); yes, we grope as those who have no iyan (eyes): we stumble at noonday as in the nashap (twilight); among those who are lusty we are as mawath (dead) men.
We roar all like bears, and moan bitterly like doves: we look for justice, but there is none; for yashawaih (salvation), but it is rachaq (far) off from us.

For our pashai (transgressions) are multiplied before you, and our chataah (sins) testify against us; for our pashai (transgressions) are with us, and as for our iwan (iniquities), we yadai (know) them:

transgressing and denying Yahawah, and turning nasag (away) from following our Alahayam, speaking oppression and sarah (revolt), conceiving and uttering from the lab (heart) dabar (words) of falsehood.
Justice is turned nasag (away) backward, and tzadaqah (righteousness) imad (stands) Rachawaq off; for truth is fallen in the street, and Nakachah can't bawaa (enter).
Yes, truth is lacking; and he who sawar (departs) from rai (evil) makes himself a prey. Yahawah saw it, and it displeased him that there was no justice.

He saw that there was no ayash (man), and wondered that there was no pagai (intercessor): therefore his own zarawai (arm) brought yashai (salvation) to him; and his tzadaqah (righteousness), it upheld him.

He Labash on tzadaqah (righteousness) as a breastplate, and a helmet of yashawaih (salvation) on his raash (head); and he Labash on bagad (garments) of vengeance for clothing, and was itah (clad) with zeal as a mantle.
According to their deeds, accordingly he will shalam (repay), chamah (wrath) to his tzar (adversaries), recompense to his ayab (enemies); to the islands he will shalam (repay) recompense.

So shall they yaraa (fear) the sham (name) of Yahawah from the west, and his kabawad (glory) from the rising of the shamash (sun); for he will bawaa (come) as a rushing stream, which the rawach (breath) of Yahawah drives.
"A gaal (redeemer) will bawaa (come) to Tzayawan, and to those who shawab (turn back / repent) from disobedience in Yaiqab," says Yahawah.

"As for me, this is my barayath (covenant) with them," amar (says) Yahawah. "My rawach (spirit) who is on you, and my dabar (words) which I have shawam (put) in your pah (mouth), shall not depart out of your pah (mouth), nor out of the pah (mouth) of your zarai (seed), nor out of the pah (mouth) of your zarai (seed's) zarai (seed)," amar (says) Yahawah, "from henceforth and iwalam (forever).
"qawam (arise), awar (shine); for your awar (light) has bawaa (come), and the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah is risen on you.
For, behold, chashak (darkness) shall cover the aratz (earth), and gross irapal (darkness) the laam (peoples); but Yahawah will arise on you, and his kabawad (glory) shall be seen on you.
gawayam (nations) shall halak (come) to your awar (light), and malak (kings) to the nagah (brightness) of your rising.

"nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eyes) all around, and raah (see): they all gather themselves together, they bawaa (come) to you; your ban (sons) shall bawaa (come) from Rachawaq, and your bath (daughters) shall be carried in the arms.

Then you shall raah (see) and be radiant, and your labab (heart) shall thrill and be enlarged; because the abundance of the yam (sea) shall be turned to you, the wealth of the gawayam (nations) shall bawaa (come) to you.

The multitude of camels shall cover you, the dromedaries of Madayan and Iyapah; all they from Shabaa shall bawaa (come); they shall nashaa (bring) gold and frankincense, and shall proclaim the thahalah (praises) of Yahawah.

All the flocks of Qadar shall be gathered together to you, the ayal (rams) of Nabayawath shall sharath (minister) to you; they shall ilah (come) up with acceptance on my mazabach (altar); and I will paar (glorify) the bayath (house) of my glory.
"Who are these who fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows?

Surely the islands shall wait for me, and the ships of Tharashayash raashawan (first), to bawaa (bring) your ban (sons) from Rachawaq, their kasap (silver) and their gold with them, for the sham (name) of Yahawah your Alahayam, and for the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel), because he has glorified you.
"Foreigners shall banah (build) up your walls, and their malak (kings) shall sharath (minister) to you: for in my qatzap (wrath) I struck you, but in my favor have I had racham (mercy) on you.

Your gates also shall be pathach (open) continually; they shall not be shut yawamam (day) nor layal (night); that men may bawaa (bring) to you the wealth of the gawayam (nations), and their malak (kings) led captive.
For that gaway (nation) and mamalakah (kingdom) that will not ibad (serve) you shall abad (perish); yes, those gaway (nations) shall be utterly wasted.

"The kabawad (glory) of Labanawan shall bawaa (come) to you, the fir tree, the pine, and the box tree together, to paar (beautify) the place of my maqadash (sanctuary); and I will make the place of my feet kabad (glorious).

The ban (sons) of those who afflicted you shall halak (come) bending to you; and all those who despised you shall shachah (bow) themselves down at the kap (soles) of your feet; and they shall qaraa (call) you The Iyar of Yahawah, The Tzayawan of the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).
"Whereas you have been forsaken and hated, so that no ibar (man) passed through you, I will shawam (make) you an eternal excellency, a joy of many dawar (generations).

You shall also drink the milk of the gawayam (nations), and shall nurse from malak (royal) breasts; and you shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, am your Savior, and your gaal (redeemer), the abayar (mighty) One of Yaiqab.

For brass I will bawaa (bring) gold, and for barazal (iron) I will bawaa (bring) kasap (silver), and for itz (wood) brass, and for aban (stones) barazal (iron). I will also shawam (make) your officers shalawam (peace), and tzadaqah (righteousness) your nagash (ruler).
Violence shall no more be heard in your aratz (land), desolation nor destruction within your borders; but you shall qaraa (call) your walls yashawaih (salvation), and your gates thahalah (praise).

The shamash (sun) shall be no more your awar (light) by yawamam (day); neither for nagah (brightness) shall the yarach (moon) give awar (light) to you: but Yahawah will be to you an iwalam (forever) awar (light), and your Alahayam your glory.

Your shamash (sun) shall no more bawaa (go) down, neither shall your yarach (moon) asap (withdraw) itself; for Yahawah will be your iwalam (forever) awar (light), and the yawam (days) of your mourning shall be ended.

Your im (people) also shall be all tzadayaq (righteous); they shall yarash (inherit) the aratz (land) iwalam (forever), the branch of my planting, the maishah (work) of my yad (hands), that I may be glorified.
The qatan (little) one shall become a alap (thousand), and the Tzaiyar one a itzawam (strong) gaway (nation); I, Yahawah, will hasten it in its ith (time).

The rawach (spirit) of the Adanay Yahawah is on me; because Yahawah has mashach (anointed) me to preach bashar (good) news to the Inaw. He has sent me to bind up the shabar (brokenhearted), to qaraa (proclaim) liberty to the captives, and release to those who are bound;
to qaraa (proclaim) the Shanah of yahawah (yahweh's) favor, and the yawam (day) of vengeance of our Alahayam; to nacham (comfort) all who Abal;

to shawam (appoint) to those who Abal in Tzayawan, to nathan (give) to them a garland for ashes, the shaman (oil) of joy for mourning, the garment of thahalah (praise) for the rawach (spirit) of Kahah; that they may be called ayal (trees) of tzadaq (righteousness), the planting of Yahawah, that he may be glorified.
They shall banah (build) the old wastes, they shall qawam (raise) up the raashawan (former) desolations, and they shall repair the waste Iyar, the desolations of many dawar (generations).
Strangers shall imad (stand) and raih (feed) your flocks, and foreigners shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers.

But you shall be named the kahan (priests) of Yahawah; men will amar (call) you the sharath (ministers) of our Alahayam: you will akal (eat) the wealth of the gawayam (nations), and you will boast in their kabawad (glory).

Instead of your bashath (shame) you shall have mashanah (double); and instead of dishonor they shall rejoice in their chalaq (portion): therefore in their aratz (land) they shall yarash (possess) mashanah (double); iwalam (forever) joy shall be to them.

"For I, Yahawah, ahab (love) justice, I shanaa (hate) robbery with iniquity; and I will nathan (give) them their recompense in truth, and I will karath (make) an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant) with them.

Their zarai (seed) shall be yadai (known) among the gawayam (nations), and their tzaatzaa (offspring) among the im (peoples); all who raah (see) them shall nakar (acknowledge) them, that they are the zarai (seed) which Yahawah has blessed.

I will greatly rejoice in Yahawah, my napash (soul) shall be joyful in my Alahayam; Labash he has clothed me with the bagad (garments) of yashai (salvation), he has covered me with the robe of tzadaqah (righteousness), as a chathan (bridegroom) kahan (decks) himself with a garland, and as a kalah (bride) adorns herself with her jewels.

For as the aratz (earth) yatzaa (brings) forth its bud, and as the garden causes the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Adanay Yahawah will cause tzadaqah (righteousness) and thahalah (praise) to spring forth before all the gawayam (nations).

For Tzayawan sake will I not hold my chashah (peace), and for Yarawashalam sake I will not shaqat (rest), until her tzadaq (righteousness) yatzaa (go) forth as nagah (brightness), and her yashawaih (salvation) as a lapayad (lamp) that bair (burns).

The gawayam (nations) shall raah (see) your tzadaq (righteousness), and all malak (kings) your kabawad (glory), and you shall be called by a Chadash naqab (name), which the pah (mouth) of Yahawah shall sham (name).
You shall also be a itarah (crown) of thapaarah (beauty) in the yad (hand) of Yahawah, and a malawakah (royal) diadem in the kap (hand) of your Alahayam.

You shall no more be termed Forsaken; neither shall your aratz (land) any more be termed Desolate: but you shall be called Chapatzayabah, and your aratz (land) Beulah; for Yahawah delights in you, and your aratz (land) shall be married.

For as a young bachawar (man) bail (marries) a virgin, so your ban (sons) shall bail (marry) you; and as the chathan (bridegroom) rejoices over the kalah (bride), so your Alahayam will rejoice over you.
I have paqad (set) watchmen on your walls, Yarawashalam; they shall never hold their chashah (peace) yawam (day) nor layal (night): you who zakar (call) on Yahawah, take no damay (rest),
and nathan (give) him no damay (rest), until he establishes, and until he shawam (makes) Yarawashalam a thahalah (praise) in the aratz (earth).

Yahawah has sworn by his right yamayan (hand), and by the zarawai (arm) of his iz (strength), "am (surely) I will no more nathan (give) your grain to be food for your ayab (enemies); and foreigners shall not drink your new thayarawash (wine), for which you have labored:
but those who have garnered it shall akal (eat) it, and halal (praise) Yahawah; and those who have gathered it shall drink it in the courts of my qadash (sanctuary).

ibar (go) through, ibar (go) through the gates! panah (prepare) the darak (way) of the im (people)! Cast up, cast up the masalah (highway)! saqal (gather) out the aban (stones)! Lift up a nas (banner) for the im (peoples).

Behold, Yahawah has proclaimed to the end of the aratz (earth), "amar (say) to the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan, ‘Behold, your yashai (salvation) bawaa (comes). Behold, his reward is with him, and his recompense panayam (before) him.'
They shall qaraa (call) them The qadash (holy) im (people), The redeemed of Yahawah: and you shall be called Sought out, A Iyar not forsaken.

Who is this who bawaa (comes) from Adam, with dyed bagad (garments) from Batzarah? this who is glorious in his clothing, marching in the greatness of his kach (strength)? "It is I who dabar (speak) in tzadaqah (righteousness), rab (mighty) to yashai (save).
Why are you Adam in your clothing, and your bagad (garments) like him who treads in the gath (wine) vat?

"I have trodden the winepress alone; and of the im (peoples) there was no darak (man) with me: yes, I trod them in my ap (anger), and trampled them in my chamah (wrath); and their lifeblood is sprinkled on my bagad (garments), and I have stained all my clothing.
For the yawam (day) of vengeance was in my lab (heart), and the Shanah of my redeemed has bawaa (come).
I looked, and there was none to help; and I wondered that there was none to samak (uphold): therefore my own zarawai (arm) brought yashai (salvation) to me; and my chamah (wrath), it upheld me.
I trod down the im (peoples) in my ap (anger), and made them Shakar in my chamah (wrath), and I poured out their lifeblood on the aratz (earth).

I will zakar (make) mention of the loving kindnesses of Yahawah and the thahalah (praises) of Yahawah, according to all that Yahawah has bestowed on us, and the rab (great) goodness toward the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), which he has bestowed on them according to his racham (mercies), and according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses.
For he said, "Surely, they are my im (people), children who will not deal falsely:" so he was their Savior.

In all their tzarah (affliction) he was tzar (afflicted), and the malaak (angel) of his panayam (presence) saved them: in his ahabah (love) and in his pity he redeemed them; and he bore them, and carried them all the yawam (days) of old.
But they rebelled, and grieved his qadash (holy) rawach (spirit): therefore he was turned to be their ayab (enemy), and he himself fought against them.

Then he zakar (remembered) the yawam (days) of old, Mashah and his im (people), saying, Where is he who brought them up out of the yam (sea) with the raih (shepherds) of his flock? where is he who shawam (put) his qadash (holy) rawach (spirit) in their qarab (midst)?

who caused his thapaarah (glorious) zarawai (arm) to yalak (go) at the right yamayan (hand) of Mashah? who divided the mayam (waters) panayam (before) them, to ishah (make) himself an iwalam (forever) sham (name)?
who led them through the depths, as a horse in the madabar (wilderness), so that they didn't stumble?

As the livestock that yarad (go) down into the Baqaih, the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah caused them to nawach (rest); so you led your im (people), to ishah (make) yourself a thapaarah (glorious) sham (name).

raah (see) down from shamayam (heaven), and raah (see) from the habitation of your qadash (holiness) and of your glory: where are your zeal and your gabawarah (mighty) acts? the yearning of your maih (heart) and your compassion is restrained toward me.

For you are our ab (father), though Abaraham doesn't know us, and Yasharaal (Israel) does not nakar (acknowledge) us: you, Yahawah, are our ab (father); our gaal (redeemer) from iwalam (forever) is your sham (name).

O Yahawah, why do you thaih (make) us to err from your darak (ways), and harden our lab (heart) from your yaraah (fear)? shawab (turn back / repent) for your ibad (servants)' sake, the shabat (tribes) of your nachalah (inheritance).
Your qadash (holy) im (people) possessed it but a little while: our tzar (adversaries) have trodden down your maqadash (sanctuary).
We have become as they over whom you never mashal (bear) rule, as those who were not called by your sham (name).
Oh that you would tear the shamayam (heavens), that you would yarad (come) down, that the har (mountains) might quake at your panayam (presence),

as when ash (fire) qadach (kindles) the brushwood, and the ash (fire) causes the mayam (waters) to boil; to make your sham (name) yadai (known) to your tzar (adversaries), that the gaway (nations) may tremble at your panayam (presence)!
When you did awesome things which we didn't look for, you came down, the har (mountains) quaked at your panayam (presence).
For from of old men have not heard, nor perceived by the ear, neither has the iyan (eye) seen a Alahayam zawalah (besides) you, who ishah (works) for him who waits for him.

You meet him who rejoices and ishah (works) tzadaq (righteousness), those who zakar (remember) you in your darak (ways). Behold, you were qatzap (angry), and we sinned. We have been in chataa (sin) for a long time; and shall we be saved?

For we have all become as one who is tamaa (unclean), and all our tzadaqah (righteousness) is as a polluted bagad (garment): and we all fade as a leaf; and our iwan (iniquities), like the rawach (wind), nashaa (take) us away.

There is none who qaraa (calls) on your sham (name), who stirs up himself to chazaq (take) hold of you; for you have hidden your panayam (face) from us, and have consumed us by yad (means) of our iwan (iniquities).
But now, Yahawah, you are our ab (father); we are the clay, and you our potter; and we all are the maishah (work) of your yad (hand).
Don't be furious, Yahawah, neither zakar (remember) iwan (iniquity) id (forever): see, look, we beg you, we are all your im (people).
Your qadash (holy) Iyar are become a madabar (wilderness), Tzayawan has become a madabar (wilderness), Yarawashalam a desolation.
Our qadash (holy) and our thapaarah (beautiful) bayath (house), where our abawath (fathers) praised you, is burned with ash (fire); and all our pleasant places are laid waste.
Will you refrain yourself for these things, Yahawah? Will you hold your chashah (peace), and afflict us very severely?
"I am inquired of by those who didn't shaal (ask); I am found by those who didn't seek me: I said, See me, see me, to a gaway (nation) that was not called by my sham (name).
I have spread out my yad (hands) all the yawam (day) to a rebellious im (people), who halak (walk) in a darak (way) that is not tawab (good), achar (after) their own machashabah (thoughts);
a im (people) who kais (provoke) me to my panayam (face) continually, sacrificing in gardens, and burning qatar (incense) on bricks;
who yashab (sit) among the qabar (graves), and lawan (lodge) in the secret places; who akal (eat) pig's flesh, and broth of pagawal (abominable) things is in their vessels;
who amar (say), qarab (stand) by yourself, don't come near to me, for I am holier than you. These are a ishan (smoke) in my ap (nose), a ash (fire) that yaqad (burns) all the yawam (day).
"Behold, it is written panayam (before) me: I will not chashah (keep) silence, but will shalam (recompense), yes, I will shalam (recompense) into their bosom,

your own iwan (iniquities), and the iwan (iniquities) of your abawath (fathers) together," amar (says) Yahawah, "who have burned qatar (incense) on the har (mountains), and blasphemed me on the Gabaih; therefore will I raashawan (first) measure their pailah (work) into their bosom.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "As the new thayarawash (wine) is found in the cluster, and one amar (says), ‘Don't shachath (destroy) it, for a barakah (blessing) is in it:' so will I do for my ibad (servants)' sake, that I may not shachath (destroy) them all.

I will yatzaa (bring) forth a zarai (seed) out of Yaiqab, and out of Yahawadah (Judah) an inheritor of my har (mountains); and my Bachayar shall yarash (inherit) it, and my ibad (servants) shall shakan (dwell) there.
Sharawan shall be a Nawah of flocks, and the valley of Ikawar a place for herds to lie down in, for my im (people) who have sought me.
"But you who forsake Yahawah, who Shakach my qadash (holy) har (mountain), who prepare a table for Fortune, and who malaa (fill) up mixed mamasak (wine) Manay Destiny;

I will destine you to the charab (sword), and you shall all bow down to the slaughter; because when I called, you didn't answer; when I spoke, you didn't listen; but you did that which was rai (evil) in my iyan (eyes), and chose that in which I didn't delight.

Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah, "Behold, my ibad (servants) shall akal (eat), but you shall be hungry; behold, my ibad (servants) shall drink, but you shall be thirsty; behold, my ibad (servants) shall Shamach, but you shall be disappointed;
behold, my ibad (servants) shall sing for tawab (joy) of lab (heart), but you shall cry for sorrow of lab (heart), and shall wail for anguish of rawach (spirit).

You shall yanach (leave) your sham (name) for a shabawaih (curse) to my Bachayar; and the Adanay Yahawah will mawath (kill) you; and he will qaraa (call) his ibad (servants) by achar (another) sham (name):

so that he who blesses himself in the aratz (earth) shall barak (bless) himself in the Alahayam of aman (truth); and he who shabai (swears) in the aratz (earth) shall shabai (swear) by the Alahayam of aman (truth); because the raashawan (former) tzarah (troubles) are forgotten, and because they are hidden from my iyan (eyes).
