"For, behold, I baraa (create) Chadash shamayam (heavens) and a Chadash aratz (earth); and the raashawan (former) things shall not be zakar (remembered), nor ilah (come) into lab (mind).
But be you glad and rejoice id (forever) in that which I baraa (create); for, behold, I baraa (create) Yarawashalam a rejoicing, and her im (people) a joy.
I will rejoice in Yarawashalam, and joy in my im (people); and there shall be heard in her no more the qawal (voice) of weeping and the qawal (voice) of crying.

"There shall be no more there an infant of yawam (days), nor an old zaqan (man) who has not filled his yawam (days); for the nair (child) shall mawath (die) one maah (hundred) Shanah ban (old), and the sinner being one maah (hundred) Shanah ban (old) shall be accursed.
They shall banah (build) bayath (houses), and yashab (inhabit) them; and they shall plant vineyards, and akal (eat) their fruit.

They shall not banah (build), and achar (another) yashab (inhabit); they shall not plant, and achar (another) akal (eat): for as the yawam (days) of a itz (tree) shall be the yawam (days) of my im (people), and my Bachayar shall long enjoy the maishah (work) of their yad (hands).
They shall not yagai (labor) in vain, nor yalad (bring) forth for calamity; for they are the zarai (seed) of the blessed of Yahawah, and their tzaatzaa (offspring) with them.
It shall happen that, before they qaraa (call), I will answer; and while they are yet speaking, I will hear.

The wolf and the lamb shall raih (feed) achad (together), and the aray (lion) shall akal (eat) straw like the ox; and ipar (dust) shall be the serpent's lacham (food). They shall not raii (hurt) nor shachath (destroy) in all my qadash (holy) har (mountain)," amar (says) Yahawah.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "shamayam (heaven) is my kasaa (throne), and the aratz (earth) is my footstool: what kind of bayath (house) will you banah (build) to me? and what place shall be my manawachah (rest)?

For all these things has my yad (hand) made, and so all these things came to be," says Yahawah: "but to this nabat (man) will I look, even to him who is Inay and of a Nakah rawach (spirit), and who Charad at my dabar (word).

He who kills an ox is as he who kills a ayash (man); he who zabach (sacrifices) a lamb, as he who breaks a dog's neck; he who ilah (offers) an manachah (offering), as he who offers pig's dam (blood); he who zakar (burns) frankincense, as he who blesses an awan (idol). Yes, they have chosen their own darak (ways), and their napash (soul) delights in their shaqawatz (abominations):

I also will choose their delusions, and will bawaa (bring) their magawarah (fears) on them; because when I called, no one answered; when I spoke, they didn't listen; but they did that which was rai (evil) in my iyan (eyes), and chose that in which I didn't delight.

Hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah, you who Charad at his dabar (word): "Your ach (brothers) who shanaa (hate) you, who cast you out for my sham (name's) sake, have said, ‘Let Yahawah be glorified, that we may raah (see) your joy;' but it is those who shall be disappointed.
A qawal (voice) of tumult from the Iyar, a qawal (voice) from the hayakal (temple), a qawal (voice) of Yahawah that shalam (renders) recompense to his ayab (enemies).
"Before she travailed, she brought yalad (forth); before her pain came, she delivered a son.

Who has heard such a thing? who has seen such things? Shall a aratz (land) be born in one yawam (day)? shall a gaway (nation) be brought chawal (forth) at paim (once)? for as soon as Tzayawan travailed, she brought yalad (forth) her children.
Shall I shabar (bring) to the birth, and not cause to yalad (bring) forth?" amar (says) Yahawah: "shall I who cause to yalad (bring) forth itzar (shut) the womb?" amar (says) your Alahayam.
"Shamach with Yarawashalam, and be glad for her, all you who ahab (love) her: rejoice for joy with her, all you who mourn over her;
that you may nurse and be satisfied at the comforting breasts; that you may drink deeply, and be delighted with the abundance of her kabawad (glory).

For thus amar (says) Yahawah, "Behold, I will natah (extend) shalawam (peace) to her like a nahar (river), and the kabawad (glory) of the gawayam (nations) like an overflowing nachal (stream): and you will nurse. You will be carried on her side, and will be dandled on her knees.
As one whom his am (mother) nacham (comforts), so will I nacham (comfort) you; and you will be comforted in Yarawashalam.

You will raah (see) it, and your lab (heart) shall rejoice, and your itzam (bones) shall flourish like the tender grass: and the yad (hand) of Yahawah shall be yadai (known) toward his ibad (servants); and he will have indignation against his ayab (enemies).

For, behold, Yahawah will bawaa (come) with ash (fire), and his chariots shall be like the sawapah (whirlwind); to shawab (turn back / repent) his ap (anger) with fierceness, and his rebuke with lahab (flames) of ash (fire).
For by ash (fire) will Yahawah execute shapat (judgment), and by his charab (sword), on all flesh; and the Chalal of Yahawah shall be many.

"Those who qadash (sanctify) themselves and tahar (purify) themselves to go to the gardens, achar (behind) one in the midst, eating pig's flesh, and the shaqatz (abomination), and the ikabar (mouse), they shall come to an sawap (end) together," says Yahawah.

"For I know their maishah (works) and their machashabah (thoughts): the time bawaa (comes), that I will gather all gawayam (nations) and lashawan (languages); and they shall bawaa (come), and shall raah (see) my kabawad (glory).

"I will shawam (set) a awath (sign) among them, and I will shalach (send) such as escape of them to the gawayam (nations), to Tharashayash, Pawal, and Lawad, who draw the qashath (bow), to Thawabal and Yawan, to the islands Rachawaq off, who have not heard my fame, neither have seen my kabawad (glory); and they shall nagad (declare) my kabawad (glory) among the gawayam (nations).

They shall bawaa (bring) all your ach (brothers) out of all the gawayam (nations) for an manachah (offering) to Yahawah, on horses, and in chariots, and in litters, and on mules, and on dromedaries, to my qadash (holy) har (mountain) Yarawashalam, amar (says) Yahawah, as the children of Yasharaal (Israel) bawaa (bring) their manachah (offering) in a tahawar (clean) vessel into the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
Of them also will I take for kahan (priests) and Lawayay Levites," amar (says) Yahawah.

"For as the Chadash shamayam (heavens) and the Chadash aratz (earth), which I will ishah (make), shall imad (remain) panayam (before) me," says Yahawah, "so your zarai (seed) and your sham (name) shall imad (remain).
It shall happen, that from one new chadash (moon) to another, and from one shabath (sabbath) to another, shall all flesh bawaa (come) to shachah (worship) panayam (before) me," amar (says) Yahawah.

"They shall yatzaa (go) forth, and raah (see) on the pagar (dead) bodies of the men who have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not mawath (die), neither shall their ash (fire) be quenched; and they will be loathsome to all mankind.
The dabar (words) of Yaramayah the ban (son) Chalaqayah Hilkiah, of the kahan (priests) who were in Inathawath in the aratz (land) of Banayamayan:
to whom the dabar (word) of Yahawah came in the yawam (days) of Yaashayah the ban (son) of Amawan, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), in the thirteenth Shanah of his malak (reign).

It came also in the yawam (days) of Yahawayaqayam the ban (son) of Yaashayah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), to the thamam (end) of the ishathay (eleventh) Shanah of Tzadaqayah, the ban (son) of Yaashayah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), to the carrying away of Yarawashalam galah (captive) in the chamayashay (fifth) chadash (month).
Now the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
"Before I formed you in the belly, I knew you. Before you came yatzaa (forth) out of the womb, I sanctified you. I have appointed you a nabayaa (prophet) to the gawayam (nations).
Then I said, "Ah, Adanay Yahawah! Behold, I don't know how to dabar (speak); for I am a nair (child).
But Yahawah said to me, "Don't amar (say), ‘I am a nair (child);' for to whoever I shall shalach (send) you, you shall yalak (go), and whatever I shall tzawah (command) you, you shall dabar (speak).
Don't be yaraa (afraid) panayam (because) of them; for I am with you to natzal (deliver) you," says Yahawah.
Then Yahawah shalach (put) forth his yad (hand), and touched my pah (mouth); and Yahawah said to me, "Behold, I have nathan (put) my dabar (words) in your pah (mouth).

raah (see), I have this yawam (day) paqad (set) you over the gawayam (nations) and over the mamalakah (kingdoms), to nathash (pluck) up and to nathatz (break) down and to abad (destroy) and to haras (overthrow), to banah (build) and to plant.
Moreover the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying, "Yaramayah, what do you raah (see)?" I said, "I raah (see) a branch of an almond tree.
Then Yahawah said to me, "You have seen yatab (well); for I watch over my dabar (word) to ishah (perform) it.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me the shanay (second) time, saying, "What do you raah (see)?" I said, "I raah (see) a boiling caldron; and it is tipping away from the tzapawan (north).
Then Yahawah said to me, "Out of the tzapawan (north) rai (evil) will pathach (break) out on all the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land).

For, behold, I will qaraa (call) all the mashapachah (families) of the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the tzapawan (north)," says Yahawah; "and they shall bawaa (come), and they shall ayash (each) nathan (set) his kasaa (throne) at the entrance of the gates of Yarawashalam, and against all its walls all around, and against all the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah).

I will dabar (utter) my mashapat (judgments) against them touching all their wickedness, in that they have forsaken me, and have burned qatar (incense) to other Alahayam, and worshiped the maishah (works) of their own yad (hands).
"You therefore put your belt on your waist, qawam (arise), and dabar (speak) to them all that I tzawah (command) you. Don't be dismayed at them, lest I chathath (dismay) you panayam (before) them.

For, behold, I have made you this yawam (day) a fortified Iyar, and an barazal (iron) pillar, and bronze walls, against the whole aratz (land), against the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), against its shar (princes), against its kahan (priests), and against the im (people) of the aratz (land).
They will fight against you; but they will not yakal (prevail) against you; for I am with you," says Yahawah, "to natzal (deliver) you.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

"halak (go), and qaraa (cry) in the ears of Yarawashalam, saying, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "I zakar (remember) for you the chasad (kindness) of your youth, the ahabah (love) of your weddings; how you went achar (after) me in the madabar (wilderness), in a aratz (land) that was not sown.

Yasharaal (Israel) was qadash (holiness) to Yahawah, the raashayath (first) fruits of his increase. All who akal (devour) him shall be held asham (guilty). rai (evil) shall bawaa (come) on them,"' says Yahawah.
Hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah, O bayath (house) of Yaiqab, and all the mashapachah (families) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)!
Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "What iwal (unrighteousness) have your abawath (fathers) found in me, that they have gone rachaq (far) from me, and have walked achar (after) vanity, and are become vain?

Neither did they amar (say), ‘Where is Yahawah who brought us up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, who led us through the madabar (wilderness), through a aratz (land) of irabah (deserts) and of shawachah (pits), through a aratz (land) of tzayah (drought) and of the shadow of tzalamawath (death), through a aratz (land) that ayash (none) passed ibar (through), and where no ayash (man) lived?'
I brought you into a plentiful aratz (land), to akal (eat) its fruit and its goodness; but when you entered, you defiled my aratz (land), and made my nachalah (heritage) an thawaibah (abomination).

The kahan (priests) didn't amar (say), ‘Where is Yahawah?' and those who handle the thawarah (law) didn't yadai (know) me. The rulers also transgressed against me, and the nabayaa (prophets) prophesied by Bail, and walked achar (after) things that do not yail (profit).
"Therefore I will yet rayab (contend) with you," says Yahawah, "and I will rayab (contend) with your children's children.
For ibar (pass) over to the islands of Kathay (Kittim), and raah (see); and shalach (send) to Qadar, and bayan (consider) maad (diligently); and raah (see) if there has been such a thing.
Has a gaway (nation) changed its Alahayam, which really are no Alahayam? But my im (people) have changed their kabawad (glory) for that which does not yail (profit).
"Be astonished, you shamayam (heavens), at this, and be horribly shair (afraid). Be very charab (desolate)," says Yahawah.

"For my im (people) have committed shanayam (two) rai (evils): they have forsaken me, the spring of chay (living) mayam (waters), and chatzab (cut) them out cisterns, shabar (broken) cisterns, that can hold no mayam (water).
Is Yasharaal (Israel) a ibad (servant)? Is he a native-born madawai (slave)? Why has he become a prey?
The young kapayar (lions) have roared at him, and yelled. They have made his aratz (land) waste. His Iyar are burned up, without yashab (inhabitant).
The children Nap of Memphis and Thachapanachas have broken the qadaqad (crown) of your head.
"Haven't you procured this to yourself, in that you have forsaken Yahawah your Alahayam, when he led you by the darak (way)?

Now what have you to do in the darak (way) to Matzarayam, to drink the mayam (waters) of the Shayachawar? Or what have you to do in the darak (way) to Ashawar, to drink the mayam (waters) of the nahar (river)?

"Your own wickedness shall correct you, and your backsliding shall yakach (reprove) you. yadai (know) therefore and raah (see) that it is an rai (evil) thing and a Mar, that you have forsaken Yahawah your Alahayam, and that my pachadah (fear) is not in you," says the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).

"For of old time I have shabar (broken) your yoke, and burst your bonds; and you said, ‘I will not serve;' for on every Gabah Gabaih and under every Rainan itz (tree) you bowed yourself, playing the prostitute.
Yet I had planted you a sharaq (noble) vine, wholly a amath (right) zarai (seed). How then have you turned into the Sawar branches of a foreign vine to me?
For though you wash yourself with lye, and use much soap, yet your iwan (iniquity) is marked panayam (before) me," says the Adanay Yahawah.

"How can you amar (say), ‘I am not defiled. I have not gone achar (after) the Bail'? raah (see) your darak (way) in the Gayaa. yadai (know) what you have done. You are a qal (swift) dromedary traversing her darak (ways);

a wild donkey Lamawad to the madabar (wilderness), that snuffs up the rawach (wind) in her desire. When she is in heat, who can shawab (turn back / repent) her away? All those who seek her will not Yaip themselves. In her chadash (month), they will matzaa (find) her.
"Withhold your ragal (foot) from Yachap unshod, and your garawan (throat) from thirst. But you said, ‘It is in vain. No, for I have loved strangers, and I will yalak (go) achar (after) them.'

As the thief is bashath (ashamed) when he is found, so is the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) yabash (ashamed); they, their malak (kings), their shar (princes), and their kahan (priests), and their nabayaa (prophets);

who amar (tell) itz (wood), ‘You are my ab (father);' and a aban (stone), ‘You have brought me out:' for they have turned their back to me, and not their panayam (face); but in the ith (time) of their rai (trouble) they will amar (say), ‘qawam (arise), and yashai (save) us.'

"But where are your Alahayam that you have made for yourselves? Let them qawam (arise), if they can yashai (save) you in the ith (time) of your rai (trouble): for according to the number of your Iyar are your Alahayam, Yahawadah (Judah).
"Why will you rayab (contend) with me? You all have transgressed against me," says Yahawah.
"I have struck your children in vain. They received no correction. Your own charab (sword) has devoured your nabayaa (prophets), like a destroying aray (lion).

dawar (generation), raah (see) the dabar (word) of Yahawah. Have I been a madabar (wilderness) to Yasharaal (Israel)? Or a aratz (land) of thick maapalayah (darkness)? Why do my im (people) amar (say), ‘We have broken loose. We will bawaa (come) to you no more?'
"Can a virgin forget her iday (ornaments), or a kalah (bride) her attire? Yet my im (people) have forgotten me for yawam (days) without number.
How yatab (well) you prepare your darak (way) to seek ahabah (love)! Therefore you have taught even the rai (wicked) women your darak (ways).
Also the dam (blood) of the napash (souls) of the naqay (innocent) Abayawan is found in your skirts. You did not matzaa (find) them breaking in; but it is because of all these things.
"Yet you said, ‘I am innocent. Surely his ap (anger) has turned away from me.' "Behold, I will shapat (judge) you, because you amar (say), ‘I have not sinned.'
Why do you azal (go) about so much to shanah (change) your darak (way)? You will be bawash (ashamed) of Matzarayam also, as you were bawash (ashamed) of Ashawar.
From there also you shall yatzaa (go) forth, with your yad (hands) on your raash (head); for Yahawah has rejected those in whom you trust, and you shall not tzalach (prosper) with them.

"They amar (say), ‘If a ayash (man) shalach (puts) away his ashah (wife), and she goes from him, and become achar (another) ayash (man's), will he shawab (turn back / repent) to her again?' Wouldn't that aratz (land) be greatly polluted? But you have played the prostitute with many rai (lovers); yet shawab (turn back / repent) again to me," says Yahawah.

"nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eyes) to the bare heights, and raah (see)! Where have you not been lain with? You have sat for them by the darak (ways), as an Irabay (Arabian) in the madabar (wilderness). You have polluted the aratz (land) with your prostitution and with your wickedness.
Therefore the showers have been withheld, and there has been no latter rain; yet you have a prostitute's forehead, you refused to be kalam (ashamed).
Will you not from this time qaraa (cry) to me, ‘My ab (father), you are the Alawap of my youth?'
"‘Will he retain his anger forever? Will he shamar (keep) it to the natzach (end)?' Behold, you have spoken and have done rai (evil) things, and have had your way.

Moreover, Yahawah said to me in the yawam (days) of Yaashayah the malak (king), "Have you seen that which backsliding Yasharaal (Israel) has done? She has gone up on every Gabah har (mountain) and under every Rainan itz (tree), and there has played the prostitute.

I said achar (after) she had done all these things, ‘She will shawab (turn back / repent) to me;' but she didn't shawab (turn back / repent); and her Bagawad achawath (sister) Yahawadah (Judah) saw it.

I saw, when, for this very cause that backsliding Yasharaal (Israel) had committed naap (adultery), I had shalach (put) her away and given her a bill of divorce, yet bagad (treacherous) Yahawadah (Judah), her achawath (sister), didn't yaraa (fear); but she also went and played the prostitute.
It happened through the qawal (lightness) of her prostitution, that the aratz (land) was polluted, and she committed naap (adultery) with aban (stones) and with itz (stocks).
Yet for all this her Bagawad achawath (sister), Yahawadah (Judah), has not returned to me with her whole lab (heart), but only in pretense," says Yahawah.
Yahawah said to me, "Backsliding Yasharaal (Israel) has shown herself more tzadaq (righteous) than bagad (treacherous) Yahawadah (Judah).

halak (go), and qaraa (proclaim) these dabar (words) toward the tzapawan (north), and amar (say), ‘shawab (turn back / repent), you backsliding Yasharaal (Israel),' says Yahawah; ‘I will not look in panayam (anger) on you; for I am chasayad (merciful),' says Yahawah. ‘I will not keep anger forever.

Only yadai (acknowledge) your iwan (iniquity), that you have transgressed against Yahawah your Alahayam, and have scattered your darak (ways) to the strangers under every Rainan itz (tree), and you have not obeyed my qawal (voice),' says Yahawah.

"shawab (turn back / repent), shawabab (backsliding) children," says Yahawah; "for I am a bail (husband) to you. I will take you one of a Iyar, and shanayam (two) of a mashapachah (family), and I will bawaa (bring) you to Tzayawan.
I will nathan (give) you raih (shepherds) according to my lab (heart), who shall raih (feed) you with daih (knowledge) and shakal (understanding).

It shall come to pass, when you are multiplied and increased in the aratz (land), in those yawam (days)," says Yahawah, "they shall amar (say) no more, ‘The arawan (ark) of the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah!' neither shall it ilah (come) to lab (mind); neither shall they zakar (remember) it; neither shall they paqad (miss) it; neither shall it be made any more.

At that ith (time) they shall qaraa (call) Yarawashalam ‘The kasaa (throne) of Yahawah;' and all the gawayam (nations) shall be gathered to it, to the sham (name) of Yahawah, to Yarawashalam. Neither shall they yalak (walk) any more achar (after) the stubbornness of their rai (evil) lab (heart).

In those yawam (days) the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) shall yalak (walk) with the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), and they shall bawaa (come) together out of the aratz (land) of the tzapawan (north) to the aratz (land) that I gave for an nachal (inheritance) to your abawath (fathers).

"But I said, ‘How I would shayath (put) you among the children, and nathan (give) you a pleasant aratz (land), a tzabay (goodly) nachalah (heritage) of the tzabaa (armies) of the gawayam (nations)!' and I said, ‘You shall qaraa (call) me "My ab (father)," and shall not shawab (turn back / repent) away from following me.'
"Surely as a ashah (wife) bagad (treacherously) departs from her rai (husband), so you have dealt bagad (treacherously) with me, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)," says Yahawah.

A qawal (voice) is heard on the bare heights, the weeping and the petitions of the children of Yasharaal (Israel); because they have perverted their darak (way), they have forgotten Yahawah their Alahayam.
shawab (turn back / repent), you shawabab (backsliding) children, I will heal your backsliding. "Behold, we have come to you; for you are Yahawah our Alahayam.
Truly in vain is help from the Gabaih, the tumult on the har (mountains). Truly the thashawaih (salvation) of Yasharaal (Israel) is in Yahawah our Alahayam.
But the shameful thing has devoured the yagayai (labor) of our abawath (fathers) from our youth, their flocks and their herds, their ban (sons) and their bath (daughters).

Let us shakab (lie) down in our bashath (shame), and let our kalamah (confusion) cover us; for we have sinned against Yahawah our Alahayam, we and our abawath (fathers), from our youth even to this yawam (day). We have not obeyed the qawal (voice) of Yahawah our Alahayam.

"If you will shawab (turn back / repent), Yasharaal (Israel)," says Yahawah, "if you will shawab (turn back / repent) to me, and if you will sawar (put) away your shaqawatz (abominations) out of my panayam (sight); then you shall not be removed;

and you shall shabai (swear), ‘As Yahawah chay (lives),' in truth, in justice, and in tzadaqah (righteousness). The gawayam (nations) shall barak (bless) themselves in him, and in him shall they glory.
For thus amar (says) Yahawah to the men of Yahawadah (Judah) and to Yarawashalam, "Break up your fallow nayar (ground), and don't zarai (sow) among thorns.

mawal (circumcise) yourselves to Yahawah, and sawar (take) away the foreskins of your labab (heart), you men of Yahawadah (Judah) and yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam; lest my chamah (wrath) yatzaa (go) forth like ash (fire), and bair (burn) so that none can quench it, panayam (because) of the rai (evil) of your mailal (doings).

nagad (declare) in Yahawadah (Judah), and publish in Yarawashalam; and amar (say), ‘Blow the trumpet in the aratz (land)!' qaraa (cry) aloud and amar (say), ‘asap (assemble) yourselves! Let us bawaa (go) into the fortified Iyar!'
nashaa (set) up a nas (standard) toward Tzayawan. Flee for safety! Don't wait; for I will bawaa (bring) rai (evil) from the tzapawan (north), and a gadawal (great) destruction.

A aray (lion) is gone up from his thicket, and a destroyer of gawayam (nations); he is on his nasai (way), he is gone yatzaa (forth) from his place, to shawam (make) your aratz (land) desolate, that your Iyar be laid waste, without yashab (inhabitant).
For this clothe yourself with sackcloth, lament and wail; for the charawan (fierce) ap (anger) of Yahawah hasn't turned shawab (turn back / repent) from us.

"It shall happen at that yawam (day)," says Yahawah, "that the lab (heart) of the malak (king) shall abad (perish), and the lab (heart) of the shar (princes); and the kahan (priests) shall be astonished, and the nabayaa (prophets) shall thamah (wonder).

Then I said, "Ah, Adanay Yahawah! Surely you have greatly deceived this im (people) and Yarawashalam, saying, ‘You shall have shalawam (peace);' whereas the charab (sword) reaches to the napash (heart).

At that ith (time) shall it be said to this im (people) and to Yarawashalam, "A Tzach rawach (wind) from the bare heights in the madabar (wilderness) darak (toward) the bath (daughter) of my im (people), not to winnow, nor to Barar;
a Malaa rawach (wind) from these shall bawaa (come) for me. Now I will also dabar (utter) mashapat (judgments) against them.
Behold, he shall ilah (come) up as clouds, and his chariots shall be as the sawapah (whirlwind): his horses are qalal (swifter) than eagles. Woe to us! For we are ruined.
Yarawashalam, wash your lab (heart) from wickedness, that you may be saved. How long shall your awan (evil) machashabah (thoughts) lawan (lodge) qarab (within) you?
For a qawal (voice) nagad (declares) Dan Dan, and publishes awan (evil) Aparayam the hills of Aparayam:
"Tell the gawayam (nations); behold, publish against Yarawashalam, ‘Watchers bawaa (come) from a far aratz (country), and raise their qawal (voice) against the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah).
As keepers of a shadah (field), they are against her all around, because she has been rebellious against me,'" says Yahawah.
"Your darak (way) and your mailal (doings) have brought these things to you. This is your wickedness; for it is Mar, for it reaches to your lab (heart).

My anguish, my anguish! I am chawal (pained) at my very lab (heart); my lab (heart) is disquieted in me; I can't hold my charash (peace); because you have heard, O my napash (soul), the qawal (sound) of the trumpet, the alarm of war.
Destruction on destruction is cried; for the whole aratz (land) is laid shadad (waste): suddenly are my ahal (tents) destroyed, and my curtains in a moment.
How long shall I raah (see) the nas (standard), and hear the qawal (sound) of the trumpet?

"For my im (people) are Awayal, they don't yadai (know) me. They are foolish children, and they have no bayan (understanding). They are skillful in doing raii (evil), but to do yatab (good) they have no yadai (knowledge).
I saw the aratz (earth), and, behold, it was thahaw (waste) and void; and the shamayam (heavens), and they had no awar (light).
I saw the har (mountains), and behold, they trembled, and all the Gabaih moved back and forth.
I saw, and behold, there was no adam (man), and all the birds of the sky had fled.
I saw, and behold, the fruitful field was a madabar (wilderness), and all its Iyar were broken down at the panayam (presence) of Yahawah, before his charawan (fierce) ap (anger).
For thus amar (says) Yahawah, "The whole aratz (land) shall be a desolation; yet will I not ishah (make) a full end.

For this the aratz (earth) will mourn, and the shamayam (heavens) above be black; because I have spoken it, I have purposed it, and I have not repented, neither will I shawab (turn back / repent) back from it.

Every Iyar flees for the qawal (noise) of the horsemen and qashath (archers); they bawaa (go) into the thickets, and ilah (climb) up on the rocks: every Iyar is forsaken, and not a ayash (man) yashab (dwells) therein.

You, when you are made desolate, what will you do? Though you Labash yourself with scarlet, though you deck you with iday (ornaments) of gold, though you enlarge your iyan (eyes) with paint, in vain do you make yourself beautiful; your lovers despise you, they seek your napash (life).

For I have heard a qawal (voice) as of a chalah (woman) in travail, the tzarah (anguish) as of her who brings forth her bakar (first) child, the qawal (voice) of the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan, who gasps for parash (breath), who spreads her kap (hands), saying, "Woe is me now! For my napash (soul) faints before the harag (murderers).

"Run back and forth through the streets of Yarawashalam, and raah (see) now, and yadai (know), and seek in the broad places of it, if you can matzaa (find) a ayash (man), if there are any who does justly, who seeks amawanah (truth); and I will pardon her.
Though they amar (say), ‘As Yahawah chay (lives);' surely they shabai (swear) falsely.

O Yahawah, don't your iyan (eyes) look on amawanah (truth)? You have stricken them, but they were not grieved. You have consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction. They have made their panayam (faces) harder than a salai (rock). They have refused to shawab (turn back / repent).
Then I said, "Surely these are Dal. They are foolish; for they don't yadai (know) the darak (way) of Yahawah, nor the mashapat (law) of their Alahayam.

I will yalak (go) to the gadawal (great) men, and will dabar (speak) to them; for they yadai (know) the darak (way) of Yahawah, and the mashapat (law) of their Alahayam." But these with yachad (one) accord have shabar (broken) the yoke, and burst the bonds.

Therefore a aray (lion) out of the Yair shall kill them, a wolf of the irabah (evenings) shall shadad (destroy) them, a leopard shall watch against their Iyar; everyone who goes out there shall be torn in pieces; because their pashai (transgressions) are many, and their backsliding is itzam (increased).

"How can I pardon you? Your children have forsaken me, and sworn by what are no Alahayam. When I had fed them to the shabai (full), they committed naap (adultery), and assembled themselves in troops at the prostitutes' bayath (houses).
They were as fed horses roaming at large: everyone neighed after his neighbor's ashah (wife).
Shouldn't I paqad (punish) them for these things?" says Yahawah; "and shouldn't my napash (soul) be avenged on such a gaway (nation) as this?
"ilah (go) up on her walls, and shachath (destroy); but don't ishah (make) a full end. sawar (take) away her branches; for they are not yahawah (yahweh's).
For the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) and the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) have dealt very bagad (treacherously) against me," says Yahawah.
They have denied Yahawah, and said, "It is not he; neither shall rai (evil) bawaa (come) on us; neither shall we raah (see) charab (sword) nor famine.
The nabayaa (prophets) shall become rawach (wind), and the word is not in them. Thus shall it be done to them.

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies), "Because you dabar (speak) this dabar (word), behold, I will nathan (make) my dabar (words) in your pah (mouth) ash (fire), and this im (people) itz (wood), and it shall akal (devour) them.

Behold, I will bawaa (bring) a gaway (nation) on you from far, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)," says Yahawah. "It is a ayathan (mighty) gaway (nation). It is an ancient gaway (nation), a gaway (nation) whose lashawan (language) you don't yadai (know), neither understand what they dabar (say).
Their quiver is an pathach (open) tomb, they are all gabawar (mighty) men.

They shall akal (eat) up your harvest, and your lacham (bread), which your ban (sons) and your bath (daughters) should akal (eat). They shall akal (eat) up your flocks and your herds. They shall akal (eat) up your vines and your fig trees. They shall beat down your fortified Iyar, in which you batach (trust), with the charab (sword).
"But even in those yawam (days)," says Yahawah, "I will not ishah (make) a full end with you.

It will happen, when you amar (say), ‘Why has Yahawah our Alahayam done all these things to us?' Then you shall amar (say) to them, ‘Just like you have forsaken me, and served foreign Alahayam in your aratz (land), so you shall ibad (serve) strangers in a aratz (land) that is not yours.'
"nagad (declare) this in the bayath (house) of Yaiqab, and publish it in Yahawadah (Judah), saying,
‘Hear now this, foolish im (people), and without lab (understanding); who have iyan (eyes), and don't raah (see); who have ears, and don't hear:

Don't you yaraa (fear) me?' says Yahawah ‘Won't you chawal (tremble) at my panayam (presence), who have placed the sand for the bound of the yam (sea), by a perpetual chaq (decree), that it can't ibar (pass) it? and though its waves toss themselves, yet they can't yakal (prevail); though they roar, yet they can't ibar (pass) over it.'
"But this im (people) has a revolting and a rebellious lab (heart); they have revolted and gone.

Neither do they amar (say) in their labab (heart), ‘Let us now yaraa (fear) Yahawah our Alahayam, who nathan (gives) rain, both the yawarah (former) and the latter, in its ith (season); who shamar (preserves) to us the chaqah (appointed) shabawai (weeks) of the harvest.'
"Your iwan (iniquities) have turned natah (away) these things, and your chataah (sins) have withheld tawab (good) from you.
For among my im (people) are found rashai (wicked) men. They watch, as fowlers lie in wait. They natzab (set) a mashachayath (trap). They catch men.
As a cage is Malaa of birds, so are their bayath (houses) Malaa of deceit. Therefore they have become great, and grew rich.

They have grown fat. They shine; yes, they excell in dabar (deeds) of wickedness. They don't plead the cause, the cause of the fatherless, that they may tzalach (prosper); and they don't shapat (judge) the mashapat (right) of the Abayawan.
"Shall I not paqad (punish) for these things?" says Yahawah. "Shall not my napash (soul) be avenged on such a gaway (nation) as this?
"An astonishing and Shairawarah thing has happened in the aratz (land).

The nabayaa (prophets) nabaa (prophesy) falsely, and the kahan (priests) radah (rule) by their yad (own) authority; and my im (people) ahab (love) to have it so. What will you do in the acharayath (end) of it?

"Flee for safety, you children of Banayamayan, out of the qarab (midst) of Yarawashalam, and blow the trumpet in Thaqawai, and nashaa (raise) up a signal on Bayathahakaram Haccherem; for rai (evil) shaqap (looks) forth from the tzapawan (north), and a gadawal (great) destruction.
The Nawah and delicate one, the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan, will I cut off.
raih (shepherds) with their flocks shall bawaa (come) to her; they shall pitch their ahal (tents) against her all around; they shall raih (feed) everyone in his place.
"qadash (prepare) war against her; qawam (arise), and let us ilah (go) up at tzahar (noon). Woe to us! For the yawam (day) declines, for the shadows of the evening are stretched out.
qawam (arise), and let us ilah (go) up by layal (night), and let us shachath (destroy) her palaces.
For Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) said, "karath (cut) down trees, and cast up a mound against Yarawashalam: this is the Iyar to be visited; she is wholly oppression in the qarab (midst) of her.

As a bawar (well) qawar (casts) forth its mayam (waters), so she qawar (casts) forth her wickedness: violence and destruction is heard in her; panayam (before) me continually is sickness and makah (wounds).
Be instructed, Yarawashalam, lest my napash (soul) be yaqai (alienated) from you; lest I shawam (make) you a desolation, a aratz (land) not inhabited.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "They shall ilal (thoroughly) ilal (glean) the shaarayath (remnant) of Yasharaal (Israel) like a vine. shawab (turn back / repent) again your yad (hand) as a grape batzar (gatherer) into the baskets.

To whom shall I dabar (speak) and testify, that they may hear? Behold, their ear is Iral, and they can't listen. Behold, the dabar (word) of Yahawah has become a reproach to them. They have no delight in it.

Therefore I am Malaa of the chamah (wrath) of Yahawah. I am weary with holding in. "Pour it out on the children in the street, and on the sawad (assembly) of young men together; for even the ayash (husband) with the ashah (wife) shall be taken, the zaqan (aged) with him who is malaa (full) of yawam (days).

Their bayath (houses) shall be turned to others, their shadah (fields) and their wives together; for I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land), says Yahawah.
"For from their qatan (least) even to their greatest, everyone is given to covetousness; and from the nabayaa (prophet) even to the kahan (priest), everyone ishah (deals) falsely.
They have healed also the hurt of my im (people) superficially, saying, ‘shalawam (peace), shalawam (peace)!' when there is no shalawam (peace).

Were they yabash (ashamed) when they had committed thawaibah (abomination)? No, they were not at all bawash (ashamed), neither could they kalam (blush). Therefore they shall napal (fall) among those who napal (fall); at the ith (time) that I paqad (visit) them, they shall be cast down," amar (says) Yahawah.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "imad (stand) in the darak (ways) and raah (see), and shaal (ask) for the old nathayab (paths), ‘Where is the tawab (good) darak (way)?' and yalak (walk) in it, and you will matzaa (find) maragawai (rest) for your napash (souls). But they said, ‘We will not yalak (walk) in it.'
I qawam (set) watchmen over you, saying, ‘Listen to the qawal (sound) of the trumpet!' But they said, ‘We will not listen!'
Therefore hear, you gawayam (nations), and yadai (know), idah (congregation), what is among them.

Hear, aratz (earth)! Behold, I will bawaa (bring) rai (evil) on this im (people), even the fruit of their machashabah (thoughts), because they have not listened to my dabar (words); and as for my thawarah (law), they have rejected it.

To what purpose bawaa (comes) there to me frankincense from Shabaa, and the tawab (sweet) cane from a far aratz (country)? your burnt ilah (offerings) are not acceptable, nor your zabach (sacrifices) pleasing to me.

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah, "Behold, I will nathan (lay) stumbling blocks before this im (people). The abawath (fathers) and the ban (sons) together shall stumble Shakan them. The neighbor and his rai (friend) shall abad (perish).

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "Behold, a im (people) bawaa (comes) from the tzapawan (north) aratz (country). A gadawal (great) gaway (nation) shall be stirred up from the uttermost parts of the aratz (earth).

They chazaq (take) hold of qashath (bow) and kayadawan (spear). They are Akazaray, and have no racham (mercy). Their qawal (voice) roars like the yam (sea), and they ride on horses, everyone set in array, as a ayash (man) to the battle, against you, bath (daughter) of Tzayawan.
We have heard its report; our yad (hands) become rapah (feeble): tzarah (anguish) has taken chazaq (hold) of us, and pains as of a yalad (woman) in labor.
Don't yatzaa (go) forth into the shadah (field), nor yalak (walk) by the darak (way); for the charab (sword) of the ayab (enemy) and magawar (terror), are on every side.

bath (daughter) of my im (people), clothe yourself with sackcloth, and wallow in ashes! Mourn, as for an only yachayad (son), most bitter lamentation; for the shadad (destroyer) shall suddenly bawaa (come) on us.
"I have made you a tester of metals and a fortress among my im (people); that you may yadai (know) and try their darak (way).
They are all sawar (grievous) rebels, going about with slanders; they are brass and barazal (iron): they all of them deal corruptly.
The bellows blow fiercely; the lead is consumed of the ashah (fire): in vain do they go on refining; for the rai (wicked) are not plucked away.
Men will qaraa (call) them rejected kasap (silver), because Yahawah has rejected them.
The dabar (word) that came to Yaramayah from Yahawah, saying,

"imad (stand) in the gate of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house), and qaraa (proclaim) there this dabar (word), and amar (say), ‘Hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah, all you of Yahawadah (Judah), who bawaa (enter) in at these gates to shachah (worship) Yahawah.
Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), yatab (amend) your darak (ways) and your mailal (doings), and I will shakan (cause) you to dwell in this place.
Don't batach (trust) in lying dabar (words), saying, The hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, are these.
For if you yatab (thoroughly) yatab (amend) your darak (ways) and your mailal (doings); if you ishah (thoroughly) ishah (execute) justice between a ayash (man) and his neighbor;

if you don't oppress the foreigner, the fatherless, and the alamanah (widow), and don't shed naqay (innocent) dam (blood) in this place, neither yalak (walk) achar (after) other Alahayam to your own rai (hurt):
then will I shakan (cause) you to dwell in this place, in the aratz (land) that I gave to your abawath (fathers), from of old even forevermore.
Behold, you batach (trust) in lying dabar (words), that can't yail (profit).

Will you steal, ratzach (murder), and naap (commit) adultery, and shabai (swear) falsely, and qatar (burn) incense to Bail, and halak (walk) achar (after) other Alahayam that you have not yadai (known),
and bawaa (come) and imad (stand) panayam (before) me in this bayath (house), which is called by my sham (name), and amar (say), We are delivered; that you may do all these thawaibah (abominations)?
Is this bayath (house), which is called by my sham (name), become a den of robbers in your iyan (eyes)? raah (see), I, even I, have seen it, says Yahawah.

But yalak (go) now to my place which was in Shayalah, where I caused my sham (name) to shakan (dwell) at the raashawan (first), and raah (see) what I did to it for the wickedness of my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel).
Now, because you have done all these maishah (works), says Yahawah, and I spoke to you, rising up shakam (early) and speaking, but you didn't hear; and I called you, but you didn't answer:
therefore will I do to the bayath (house) which is called by my sham (name), in which you batach (trust), and to the place which I gave to you and to your abawath (fathers), as I did to Shayalah.
I will cast you out of my panayam (sight), as I have cast out all your ach (brothers), even the whole zarai (seed) of Aparayam.
Therefore don't palal (pray) for this im (people), neither nashaa (lift) up a cry nor prayer for them, neither pagai (make) intercession to me; for I will not hear you.
Don't you raah (see) what they do in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah) and in the streets of Yarawashalam?

The children gather itz (wood), and the abawath (fathers) bair (kindle) the ash (fire), and the women knead the dough, to ishah (make) cakes to the malakath (queen) of the sky, and to pour out drink nasak (offerings) to other Alahayam, that they may provoke me to kais (anger).
Do they provoke me to kais (anger)? says Yahawah. Don't they provoke themselves, to the bashath (confusion) of their own panayam (faces)?

Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, my ap (anger) and my chamah (wrath) shall be poured out on this place, on adam (man), and on animal, and on the itz (trees) of the shadah (field), and on the fruit of the adamah (ground); and it shall bair (burn), and shall not be quenched.
Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): sapah (add) your burnt ilah (offerings) to your zabach (sacrifices), and akal (eat) meat.

For I didn't dabar (speak) to your abawath (fathers), nor tzawah (command) them in the yawam (day) that I brought them out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, dabar (concerning) burnt ilah (offerings) or zabach (sacrifices):

but this thing I tzawah (commanded) them, saying, Listen to my qawal (voice), and I will be your Alahayam, and you shall be my im (people); and halak (walk) in all the darak (way) that I tzawah (command) you, that it may be yatab (well) with you.
But they didn't listen nor natah (turn) their ear, but walked in their own mawaitzah (counsels) and in the stubbornness of their rai (evil) lab (heart), and went backward, and not forward.

Since the yawam (day) that your abawath (fathers) came yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam to this yawam (day), I have sent to you all my ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets), yawam (daily) rising up shakam (early) and sending them:
yet they didn't listen to me, nor inclined their ear, but made their neck stiff: they did raii (worse) than their abawath (fathers).
You shall dabar (speak) all these dabar (words) to them; but they will not listen to you: you shall also qaraa (call) to them; but they will not answer you.

You shall amar (tell) them, This is the gaway (nation) that has not listened to the qawal (voice) of Yahawah their Alahayam, nor received instruction: amawanah (truth) is perished, and is karath (cut) off from their pah (mouth).
Cut off your nazar (hair), and throw it away, and nashaa (take) up a lamentation on the bare heights; for Yahawah has rejected and forsaken the dawar (generation) of his ibarah (wrath).

For the children of Yahawadah (Judah) have done that which is rai (evil) in my iyan (sight), says Yahawah: they have shawam (set) their shaqawatz (abominations) in the bayath (house) which is called by my sham (name), to tamaa (defile) it.

They have built the bamah (high) places of Thapath, which is in the Gayaa of the ban (son) of Hanam, to sharap (burn) their ban (sons) and their bath (daughters) in the ash (fire); which I didn't tzawah (command), nor did it ilah (come) into my lab (mind).

Therefore, behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), says Yahawah, that it shall no more be called Thapath, nor The Gayaa of the ban (son) of Hanam, but The Gayaa of Slaughter: for they shall bury in Thapath, until there is no place to bury.
The nabalah (dead) bodies of this im (people) shall be food for the birds of the sky, and for the animals of the aratz (earth); and none shall frighten them away.

Then will I shabath (cause) to cease from the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and from the streets of Yarawashalam, the qawal (voice) of mirth and the qawal (voice) of gladness, the qawal (voice) of the chathan (bridegroom) and the qawal (voice) of the kalah (bride); for the aratz (land) shall become a waste.

At that ith (time), says Yahawah, they shall yatzaa (bring) out the itzam (bones) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), and the itzam (bones) of his shar (princes), and the itzam (bones) of the kahan (priests), and the itzam (bones) of the nabayaa (prophets), and the itzam (bones) of the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, out of their qabar (graves);

and they shall spread them before the shamash (sun), and the yarach (moon), and all the tzabaa (army) of the sky, which they have loved, and which they have served, and achar (after) which they have walked, and which they have sought, and which they have worshiped: they shall not be gathered, nor be buried, they shall be for dung on the surface of the adamah (earth).

mawath (death) shall be chosen rather than chay (life) by all the shaarayath (residue) that shaar (remain) of this rai (evil) mashapachah (family), that shaar (remain) in all the places where I have driven them, says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
Moreover you shall amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Shall men napal (fall), and not qawam (rise) up again? Shall one shawab (turn back / repent) away, and not shawab (turn back / repent)?
Why then is this im (people) of Yarawashalam slidden shawab (turn back / repent) by a perpetual backsliding? they chazaq (hold) fast Tharamah, they refuse to shawab (turn back / repent).

I listened and heard, but they didn't dabar (speak) aright: no ayash (man) nacham (repents) him of his wickedness, saying, What have I done? everyone shawab (turn back / repent) to his course, as a horse that rushes headlong in the battle.

Yes, the stork in the sky yadai (knows) her mawaid (appointed) times; and the turtledove and the swallow and the crane shamar (observe) the ith (time) of their coming; but my im (people) don't yadai (know) yahawah (yahweh's) mashapat (law).
How do you amar (say), We are chakam (wise), and the thawarah (law) of Yahawah is with us? But, behold, the false pen of the scribes has worked falsely.
The chakam (wise) men are disappointed, they are dismayed and taken: behold, they have rejected the dabar (word) of Yahawah; and what kind of chakamah (wisdom) is in them?

Therefore will I nathan (give) their wives to others, and their shadah (fields) to those who shall yarash (possess) them: for everyone from the qatan (least) even to the greatest is given to covetousness; from the nabayaa (prophet) even to the kahan (priest) every one ishah (deals) falsely.
They have healed the hurt of the bath (daughter) of my im (people) qalal (slightly), saying, shalawam (peace), shalawam (peace); when there is no shalawam (peace).

Were they yabash (ashamed) when they had committed thawaibah (abomination)? nay, they were not at all bawash (ashamed), neither could they kalam (blush): therefore shall they napal (fall) among those who napal (fall); in the ith (time) of their visitation they shall be cast down, amar (says) Yahawah.

I will asap (utterly) sawap (consume) them, says Yahawah: no inab (grapes) shall be on the vine, nor figs on the fig tree, and the leaf shall fade; and the things that I have given them shall ibar (pass) away from them.

Why do we yashab (sit) still? asap (assemble) yourselves, and let us bawaa (enter) into the fortified Iyar, and let us be damam (silent) there; for Yahawah our Alahayam has put us to damam (silence), and given us mayam (water) of gall to shaqah (drink), because we have sinned against Yahawah.
We looked for shalawam (peace), but no tawab (good) came; and for a ith (time) of healing, and behold, baithah (dismay)!

The snorting of his horses is heard Dan Dan: at the qawal (sound) of the neighing of his abayar (strong) ones the whole aratz (land) trembles; for they have bawaa (come), and have devoured the aratz (land) and all that is in it; the Iyar and those who yashab (dwell) therein.
For, behold, I will shalach (send) serpents, adders, among you, which will not be charmed; and they shall bite you, says Yahawah.
Oh that I could comfort myself against sorrow! My lab (heart) is Daway within me.

Behold, the qawal (voice) of the cry of the bath (daughter) of my im (people) from a aratz (land) that is very far off: isn't Yahawah in Tzayawan? Isn't her malak (king) in her? Why have they provoked me to kais (anger) with their engraved pasayal (images), and with foreign vanities?
The harvest is past, the qayatz (summer) is ended, and we are not saved.
For the hurt of the bath (daughter) of my im (people) am I shabar (hurt): I mourn; shamah (dismay) has taken chazaq (hold) on me.
Is there no balm in Galaid? is there no physician there? why then isn't the health of the bath (daughter) of my im (people) recovered?
Oh that my raash (head) were mayam (waters), and my iyan (eyes) a spring of tears, that I might weep yawamam (day) and layal (night) for the Chalal of the bath (daughter) of my im (people)!

Oh that I had in the madabar (wilderness) a lodging place of wayfaring men; that I might leave my im (people), and yalak (go) from them! for they are all naap (adulterers), an itzarah (assembly) of bagad (treacherous) men.

They bend their lashawan (tongue), as their qashath (bow), for falsehood; and they are grown strong in the aratz (land), but not for amawanah (truth): for they yatzaa (proceed) from rai (evil) to rai (evil), and they don't yadai (know) me, says Yahawah.
shamar (take) heed everyone of his neighbor, and don't batach (trust) in any ach (brother); for every ach (brother) will utterly supplant, and every neighbor will halak (go) about with slanders.
They will deceive everyone his neighbor, and will not dabar (speak) the truth: they have taught their lashawan (tongue) to dabar (speak) lies; they weary themselves to commit iwah (iniquity).
Your yashab (habitation) is in the midst of deceit; through deceit they refuse to yadai (know) me, says Yahawah.
Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), Behold, I will melt them, and try them; for how should I ishah (deal) with the bath (daughter) of my im (people)?
Their lashawan (tongue) is a deadly chatz (arrow); it dabar (speaks) deceit: one dabar (speaks) peaceably to his neighbor with his pah (mouth), but in his qarab (heart) he shawam (lays) wait for him.
Shall I not paqad (visit) them for these things? says Yahawah; shall not my napash (soul) be avenged on such a gaway (nation) as this?

For the har (mountains) will I nashaa (take) up a weeping and wailing, and for the naah (pastures) of the madabar (wilderness) a lamentation, because they are burned up, so that ayash (none) passes through; neither can men hear the qawal (voice) of the livestock; both the birds of the sky and the animals are fled, they are gone.
I will nathan (make) Yarawashalam heaps, a dwelling place of jackals; and I will nathan (make) the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah) a desolation, without yashab (inhabitant).

Who is the chakam (wise) ayash (man), that may bayan (understand) this? Who is he to whom the pah (mouth) of Yahawah has spoken, that he may nagad (declare) it? Why is the aratz (land) perished and burned up like a madabar (wilderness), so that none passes ibar (through)?
Yahawah amar (says), Because they have forsaken my thawarah (law) which I nathan (set) panayam (before) them, and have not obeyed my qawal (voice), neither walked therein,
but have walked achar (after) the stubbornness of their own lab (heart), and achar (after) the Bail, which their abawath (fathers) taught them;

therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), Behold, I will akal (feed) them, even this im (people), with wormwood, and give them mayam (water) of gall to shaqah (drink).

I will scatter them also among the gaway (nations), whom neither they nor their abawath (fathers) have yadai (known); and I will shalach (send) the charab (sword) achar (after) them, until I have consumed them.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), bayan (consider), and qaraa (call) for the qawan (mourning) women, that they may bawaa (come); and shalach (send) for the skillful women, that they may bawaa (come):
and let them make haste, and nashaa (take) up a wailing for us, that our iyan (eyes) may yarad (run) down with tears, and our ipaip (eyelids) nazal (gush) out with mayam (waters).

For a qawal (voice) of wailing is heard out of Tzayawan, How are we ruined! we are maad (greatly) confounded, because we have forsaken the aratz (land), because they have cast down our mashakan (dwellings).
Yet hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah, you women, and let your ear receive the dabar (word) of his pah (mouth); and teach your bath (daughters) wailing, and everyone her neighbor lamentation.
For mawath (death) has ilah (come) up into our windows, it is entered into our palaces; to karath (cut) off the children from outside, and the young men from the streets.

dabar (speak), Thus says Yahawah, The nabalah (dead) bodies of men shall napal (fall) as dung on the panayam (open) shadah (field), and as the handful achar (after) the harvester; and none shall asap (gather) them.
Thus amar (says) Yahawah, Don't let the chakam (wise) man glory in his chakamah (wisdom), neither let the gabawar (mighty) man glory in his might, don't let the Ishayar man glory in his riches;

but let him who glories glory in this, that he has shakal (understanding), and yadai (knows) me, that I am Yahawah who ishah (exercises) loving chasad (kindness), justice, and tzadaqah (righteousness), in the aratz (earth): for in these things I delight, says Yahawah.
Behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), says Yahawah, that I will paqad (punish) all those who are circumcised in uncircumcision:

Matzarayam, and Yahawadah (Judah), and Adam, and the children of Imawan, and Mawaab, and all that have the corners of their hair cut off, who yashab (dwell) in the madabar (wilderness); for all the gaway (nations) are Iral, and all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) are Iral in lab (heart).
Hear the dabar (word) which Yahawah dabar (speaks) to you, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)!
Thus amar (says) Yahawah, "Don't learn the darak (way) of the gawayam (nations), and don't be dismayed at the awath (signs) of the sky; for the gawayam (nations) are dismayed at them.
For the chaqah (customs) of the im (peoples) are vanity; for one karath (cuts) a itz (tree) out of the Yair, the maishah (work) of the yad (hands) of the workman with the axe.
They deck it with kasap (silver) and with gold; they chazaq (fasten) it with nails and with hammers, that it not move.

They are like a palm tree, of turned dabar (work), and don't speak: they must be carried, because they can't go. Don't be yaraa (afraid) of them; for they can't do raii (evil), neither is it in them to do yatab (good).
There is none like you, Yahawah; you are gadawal (great), and your sham (name) is gadawal (great) in might.

Who should not yaraa (fear) you, malak (king) of the gawayam (nations)? For it appertains to you; because among all the chakam (wise) men of the gawayam (nations), and in all their malakawath (royal) estate, there is none like you.
But they are achad (together) bair (brutish) and foolish: the instruction of idols! it is but a itz (stock).

There is kasap (silver) beaten into plates, which is brought from Tharashayash, and gold from Awapaz, the maishah (work) of the artificer and of the yad (hands) of the goldsmith; blue and purple for their clothing; they are all the maishah (work) of skillful men.

But Yahawah is the amath (true) Alahayam; he is the chay (living) Alahayam, and an iwalam (forever) malak (king): at his qatzap (wrath) the aratz (earth) trembles, and the gawayam (nations) are not able to withstand his indignation.
You shall amar (say) this to them: The Alahayam that have not made the shamayan (heavens) and the araq (earth), these shall abad (perish) from the arai (earth), and from under the shamayan (heavens).
He has made the aratz (earth) by his kach (power), he has established the world by his chakamah (wisdom), and by his understanding has he stretched out the shamayam (heavens):

when he nathan (utters) his qawal (voice), there is a tumult of mayam (waters) in the shamayam (heavens), and he causes the vapors to ilah (ascend) from the ends of the aratz (earth); he ishah (makes) lightnings for the rain, and yatzaa (brings) forth the rawach (wind) out of his treasuries.

Every adam (man) has become bair (brutish) and without daith (knowledge); every goldsmith is disappointed by his engraved pasal (image); for his molten nasak (image) is falsehood, and there is no rawach (breath) in them.
They are vanity, a maishah (work) of delusion: in the ith (time) of their visitation they shall abad (perish).

The chalaq (portion) of Yaiqab is not like these; for he is the former of all things; and Yasharaal (Israel) is the shabat (tribe) of his nachalah (inheritance): Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) is his sham (name).
asap (gather) up your wares out of the aratz (land), you who live under Matzawar.
For thus amar (says) Yahawah, Behold, I will sling out the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land) at this paim (time), and will tzarar (distress) them, that they may feel it.
Woe is me because of my hurt! my makah (wound) is chalah (grievous): but I said, ak (truly) this is my grief, and I must nashaa (bear) it.

My ahal (tent) is destroyed, and all my cords are broken: my children are gone yatzaa (forth) from me, and they are no more: there is none to natah (spread) my ahal (tent) any more, and to qawam (set) up my curtains.
For the raih (shepherds) are become bair (brutish), and have not inquired of Yahawah: therefore they have not prospered, and all their flocks are scattered.

The qawal (voice) of news, behold, it bawaa (comes), and a gadawal (great) commotion out of the tzapawan (north) aratz (country), to shawam (make) the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah) a desolation, a dwelling place of jackals.
Yahawah, I yadai (know) that the darak (way) of adam (man) is not in himself: it is not in ayash (man) who halak (walks) to kawan (direct) his steps.
Yahawah, correct me, but in mashapat (measure): not in your ap (anger), lest you bring me to nothing.

Pour out your chamah (wrath) on the gawayam (nations) that don't yadai (know) you, and on the mashapachah (families) that don't qaraa (call) on your sham (name): for they have devoured Yaiqab, yes, they have devoured him and consumed him, and have laid shamam (waste) his Nawah.
The dabar (word) that came to Yaramayah from Yahawah, saying,
Hear the dabar (words) of this barayath (covenant), and dabar (speak) to the men of Yahawadah (Judah), and to the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam;
and amar (say) to them, Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): Cursed is the ayash (man) who doesn't hear the dabar (words) of this barayath (covenant),

which I tzawah (commanded) your abawath (fathers) in the yawam (day) that I brought them yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, out of the barazal (iron) furnace, saying, Obey my qawal (voice), and do them, according to all which I tzawah (command) you: so you shall be my im (people), and I will be your Alahayam;

that I may qawam (establish) the shabawaih (oath) which I swore to your abawath (fathers), to nathan (give) them a aratz (land) flowing with milk and honey, as at this yawam (day). Then answered I, and said, aman (amen), Yahawah.

Yahawah said to me, qaraa (proclaim) all these dabar (words) in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the streets of Yarawashalam, saying, Hear the dabar (words) of this barayath (covenant), and do them.

For I iwad (earnestly) protested to your abawath (fathers) in the yawam (day) that I brought them up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, even to this yawam (day), rising shakam (early) and protesting, saying, Obey my qawal (voice).

Yet they didn't obey, nor natah (turn) their ear, but walked everyone in the stubbornness of their rai (evil) lab (heart): therefore I brought on them all the dabar (words) of this barayath (covenant), which I tzawah (commanded) them to do, but they didn't do them.
Yahawah said to me, A conspiracy is found among the men of Yahawadah (Judah), and among the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam.

They are turned shawab (turn back / repent) to the iwan (iniquities) of their raashawan (forefathers), who refused to hear my dabar (words); and they are gone achar (after) other Alahayam to ibad (serve) them: the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) and the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) have broken my barayath (covenant) which I made with their abawath (fathers).
Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah, Behold, I will bawaa (bring) rai (evil) on them, which they shall not be yakal (able) to yatzaa (escape); and they shall cry to me, but I will not listen to them.

Then shall the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah) and the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam halak (go) and cry to the Alahayam to which they qatar (offer) incense: but they will not yashai (save) them at all in the ith (time) of their rai (trouble).

For according to the number of your Iyar are your Alahayam, Yahawadah (Judah); and according to the number of the streets of Yarawashalam have you shawam (set) up mazabach (altars) to the shameful thing, even mazabach (altars) to qatar (burn) incense to Bail.

Therefore don't palal (pray) for this im (people), neither nashaa (lift) up cry nor prayer for them; for I will not hear them in the ith (time) that they qaraa (cry) to me because of their rai (trouble).
What has my yadayad (beloved) to do in my bayath (house), since she has worked lewdness with many, and the qadash (holy) flesh is passed from you? when you do rai (evil), then you rejoice.
Yahawah called your sham (name), A Rainan olive tree, Yapah with goodly fruit: with the qawal (noise) of a gadawal (great) tumult he has kindled ash (fire) on it, and its branches are broken.

For Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), who planted you, has pronounced rai (evil) against you, because of the rai (evil) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) and of the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah), which they have worked for themselves in provoking me to kais (anger) by offering qatar (incense) to Bail.
Yahawah gave me yadai (knowledge) of it, and I knew it: then you showed me their mailal (doings).

Alawap I was like a gentle lamb that is led to the slaughter; and I didn't yadai (know) that they had devised machashabah (devices) against me, saying, Let us shachath (destroy) the itz (tree) with its lacham (fruit), and let us karath (cut) him off from the aratz (land) of the chay (living), that his sham (name) may be no more zakar (remembered).

But, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), who shapat (judges) righteously, who tests the kalayah (heart) and the lab (mind), I shall raah (see) your vengeance on them; for to you have I revealed my rayab (cause).

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah concerning the men of Inathawath, who seek your napash (life), saying, You shall not nabaa (prophesy) in the sham (name) of Yahawah, that you not mawath (die) by our yad (hand);

therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), Behold, I will paqad (punish) them: the young men shall mawath (die) by the charab (sword); their ban (sons) and their bath (daughters) shall mawath (die) by famine;
and there shall be no shaarayath (remnant) to them: for I will bawaa (bring) rai (evil) on the men of Inathawath, even the Shanah of their visitation.

You are tzadayaq (righteous), Yahawah, when I rayab (contend) with you; yet I would reason the cause with you: why does the darak (way) of the rashai (wicked) tzalach (prosper)? why are all they at ease who deal very bagad (treacherously)?
You have planted them, yes, they have taken root; they yalak (grow), yes, they ishah (bring) forth fruit: you are qarawab (near) in their pah (mouth), and Rachawaq from their kalayah (heart).
But you, Yahawah, yadai (know) me; you raah (see) me, and try my lab (heart) toward you: pull them out like sheep for the slaughter, and qadash (prepare) them for the yawam (day) of slaughter.

How long shall the aratz (land) mourn, and the herbs of the whole shadah (country) yabash (wither)? for the wickedness of those who yashab (dwell) therein, the animals are consumed, and the birds; because they said, He shall not raah (see) our acharayath (latter) end.

If you have run with the footmen, and they have wearied you, then how can you contend with horses? and though in a aratz (land) of shalawam (peace) you are batach (secure), yet how will you do in the pride of the Yaradan?

For even your ach (brothers), and the bayath (house) of your ab (father), even they have dealt bagad (treacherously) with you; even they have cried Malaa achar (after) you: don't aman (believe) them, though they dabar (speak) tawab (beautiful) words to you.
I have forsaken my bayath (house), I have cast off my nachalah (heritage); I have given the dearly beloved of my napash (soul) into the kap (hand) of her ayab (enemies).
My nachalah (heritage) has become to me as a aray (lion) in the Yair: she has uttered her voice against me; therefore I have hated her.
Is my nachalah (heritage) to me as a Tzabawai bird of prey? are the birds of prey against her all around? yalak (go), asap (assemble) all the animals of the shadah (field), bring them to devour.
Many raih (shepherds) have destroyed my vineyard, they have trodden my chalaqah (portion) under bawas (foot), they have made my pleasant chalaqah (portion) a desolate madabar (wilderness).
They have made it a Shamam; it mourns to me, being desolate; the whole aratz (land) is made shamam (desolate), because no ayash (man) shawam (lays) it to lab (heart).

shadad (destroyers) have bawaa (come) on all the bare heights in the madabar (wilderness); for the charab (sword) of Yahawah akal (devours) from the qatzah (one) end of the aratz (land) even to the other end of the aratz (land): no flesh has shalawam (peace).

They have sown wheat, and have reaped thorns; they have chalah (put) themselves to pain, and yail (profit) nothing: and you shall be bawash (ashamed) of your fruits, because of the charawan (fierce) ap (anger) of Yahawah.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah against all my rai (evil) Shakan, who nagai (touch) the nachalah (inheritance) which I have caused my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel) to nachal (inherit): behold, I will nathash (pluck) them up from off their adamah (land), and will nathash (pluck) up the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) from among them.

It shall happen, achar (after) that I have plucked them up, I will shawab (turn back / repent) and have racham (compassion) on them; and I will shawab (turn back / repent) them again, every ayash (man) to his nachalah (heritage), and every ayash (man) to his aratz (land).

It shall happen, if they will diligently learn the darak (ways) of my im (people), to shabai (swear) by my sham (name), As Yahawah chay (lives); even as they taught my im (people) to shabai (swear) by Bail; then shall they be built up in the midst of my im (people).
But if they will not hear, then will I nathash (pluck) up that gaway (nation), plucking up and destroying it, says Yahawah.
Thus amar (says) Yahawah to me, halak (go), and qanah (buy) yourself a linen belt, and shawam (put) it on your waist, and don't bawaa (put) it in mayam (water).
So I bought a belt according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah, and shawam (put) it on my waist.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me the shanay (second) time, saying,
Take the belt that you have bought, which is on your waist, and qawam (arise), yalak (go) to the Parath, and hide it there in a cleft of the salai (rock).
So I went, and hid it by the Parath, as Yahawah tzawah (commanded) me.
It happened after many yawam (days), that Yahawah said to me, qawam (arise), yalak (go) to the Parath, and take the belt from there, which I tzawah (commanded) you to hide there.
Then I went to the Parath, and dug, and took the belt from the place where I had hidden it; and behold, the belt was marred, it was tzalach (profitable) for nothing.
Then the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
Thus amar (says) Yahawah, In this way I will shachath (mar) the pride of Yahawadah (Judah), and the rab (great) pride of Yarawashalam.

This rai (evil) im (people), who refuse to hear my dabar (words), who halak (walk) in the stubbornness of their lab (heart), and are gone achar (after) other Alahayam to ibad (serve) them, and to shachah (worship) them, shall even be as this belt, which is tzalach (profitable) for nothing.

For as the belt clings to the waist of a ayash (man), so have I caused to cling to me the whole bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) and the whole bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah), says Yahawah; that they may be to me for a im (people), and for a sham (name), and for a thahalah (praise), and for a glory: but they would not hear.

Therefore you shall amar (speak) to them this dabar (word): Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), Every bottle shall be filled with yayan (wine): and they shall amar (tell) you, Do we not yadai (certainly) yadai (know) that every bottle shall be filled with yayan (wine)?

Then you shall amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) Yahawah, Behold, I will malaa (fill) all the yashab (inhabitants) of this aratz (land), even the malak (kings) who yashab (sit) on Dawad kasaa (throne), and the kahan (priests), and the nabayaa (prophets), and all the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, with drunkenness.

I will dash them one against ach (another), even the abawath (fathers) and the ban (sons) together, says Yahawah: I will not pity, nor spare, nor have racham (compassion), that I should not shachath (destroy) them.
Hear, and give ear; don't be proud; for Yahawah has spoken.

nathan (give) kabawad (glory) to Yahawah your Alahayam, before he causes chashak (darkness), and before your feet nagap (stumble) on the nashap (dark) har (mountains), and, while you look for awar (light), he shawam (turns) it into the shadow of tzalamawath (death), and shayath (makes) it gross irapal (darkness).

But if you will not hear it, my napash (soul) shall weep in secret for your pride; and my iyan (eye) shall weep bitterly, and yarad (run) down with tears, because yahawah (yahweh's) flock is taken captive.
amar (say) to the malak (king) and to the gabayarah (queen) shapal (mother), Humble yourselves, yashab (sit) down; for your headdresses have yarad (come) down, even the itarah (crown) of your glory.
The Iyar of the Nagab are shut up, and there is none to pathach (open) them: Yahawadah (Judah) is carried away galah (captive), all of it; it is shalawam (wholly) carried away galah (captive).
nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eyes), and raah (see) those who bawaa (come) from the tzapawan (north): where is the flock that was given you, your thapaarah (beautiful) flock?

What will you amar (say), when he shall paqad (set) over you as raash (head) those whom you have yourself taught to be Alawap to you? shall not sorrows achaz (take) hold of you, as of a ashah (woman) in yalad (travail)?
If you amar (say) in your labab (heart), Why are these things come on me? for the greatness of your iwan (iniquity) are your skirts uncovered, and your heels suffer violence.
Can the Kawashay (Ethiopian) hapak (change) his skin, or the leopard his spots? then may you also do yatab (good), who are Lamawad to do raii (evil).
Therefore will I scatter them, as the stubble that passes ibar (away), by the rawach (wind) of the madabar (wilderness).
This is your lot, the portion measured to you from me, says Yahawah; because you have forgotten me, and trusted in falsehood.
Therefore will I also chashap (uncover) your skirts on your panayam (face), and your qalawan (shame) shall raah (see).

I have seen your shaqawatz (abominations), even your adulteries, and your neighing, the lewdness of your prostitution, on the Gabaih in the shadah (field). Woe to you, Yarawashalam! You will not be made tahar (clean); how iwad (long) shall it yet be?
The dabar (word) of Yahawah that came to Yaramayah dabar (concerning) the drought.
Yahawadah (Judah) mourns, and its gates languish, they sit in black on the aratz (ground); and the cry of Yarawashalam is gone up.

Their adayar (nobles) shalach (send) their Tzaiyar ones to the mayam (waters): they bawaa (come) to the cisterns, and matzaa (find) no mayam (water); they shawab (turn back / repent) with their vessels empty; they are disappointed and confounded, and cover their raash (heads).
Because of the adamah (ground) which is cracked, because no rain has been in the aratz (land), the plowmen are disappointed, they cover their raash (heads).
Yes, the hind also in the shadah (field) yalad (calves), and forsakes her young, because there is no grass.
The wild donkeys imad (stand) on the bare heights, they pant for rawach (air) like jackals; their iyan (eyes) kalah (fail), because there is no herbage.
Though our iwan (iniquities) testify against us, ishah (work) for your sham (name's) sake, Yahawah; for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against you.

You Maqawah of Yasharaal (Israel), its Savior in the ith (time) of tzarah (trouble), why should you be as a foreigner in the aratz (land), and as a wayfaring arach (man) who natah (turns) aside to stay for a lawan (night)?

Why should you be like a scared ayash (man), as a gabawar (mighty) man who can't yashai (save)? Yet you, Yahawah, are in the qarab (midst) of us, and we are called by your sham (name); don't yanach (leave) us.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah to this im (people), Even so have they loved to wander; they have not refrained their feet: therefore Yahawah does not accept them; now he will zakar (remember) their iwan (iniquity), and paqad (visit) their chataah (sins).
Yahawah said to me, Don't palal (pray) for this im (people) for their tawab (good).

When they fast, I will not hear their cry; and when they ilah (offer) burnt ilah (offering) and meal manachah (offering), I will not accept them; but I will kalah (consume) them by the charab (sword), and by the famine, and by the dabar (pestilence).

Then I said, Ah, Adanay Yahawah! behold, the nabayaa (prophets) amar (tell) them, You shall not raah (see) the charab (sword), neither shall you have famine; but I will nathan (give) you amath (assured) shalawam (peace) in this place.

Then Yahawah said to me, The nabayaa (prophets) nabaa (prophesy) lies in my sham (name); I didn't shalach (send) them, neither have I tzawah (commanded) them, neither spoke I to them: they nabaa (prophesy) to you a lying vision, and divination, and a thing of nothing, and the Tharamah of their own lab (heart).

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah concerning the nabayaa (prophets) who nabaa (prophesy) in my sham (name), and I didn't shalach (send) them, yet they amar (say), charab (sword) and famine shall not be in this aratz (land): By charab (sword) and famine shall those nabayaa (prophets) be consumed.

The im (people) to whom they nabaa (prophesy) shall be cast out in the streets of Yarawashalam panayam (because) of the famine and the charab (sword); and they shall have none to bury them—them, their wives, nor their ban (sons), nor their bath (daughters): for I will pour their wickedness on them.

You shall amar (say) this dabar (word) to them, Let my iyan (eyes) yarad (run) down with tears layal (night) and yawamam (day), and let them not damah (cease); for the virgin bath (daughter) of my im (people) is shabar (broken) with a gadawal (great) breach, with a very chalah (grievous) makah (wound).

If I yatzaa (go) forth into the shadah (field), then, behold, the Chalal with the charab (sword)! and if I bawaa (enter) into the Iyar, then, behold, those who are sick with famine! for both the nabayaa (prophet) and the kahan (priest) go about in the aratz (land), and have no yadai (knowledge).

Have you utterly rejected Yahawadah (Judah)? has your napash (soul) loathed Tzayawan? why have you struck us, and there is no healing for us? We looked for shalawam (peace), but no tawab (good) came; and for a ith (time) of healing, and behold, baithah (dismay)!
We yadai (acknowledge), Yahawah, our rashai (wickedness), and the iwan (iniquity) of our abawath (fathers); for we have sinned against you.
Do not abhor us, for your sham (name's) sake; do not disgrace the kasaa (throne) of your kabawad (glory): zakar (remember), don't parar (break) your barayath (covenant) with us.

Are there any among the vanities of the gawayam (nations) that can cause rain? or can the sky nathan (give) showers? Aren't you he, Yahawah our Alahayam? therefore we will wait for you; for you have made all these things.
