Then Yahawah said to me, Though Mashah and Shamawaal stood panayam (before) me, yet my napash (mind) would not be toward this im (people): shalach (cast) them out of my panayam (sight), and let them yatzaa (go) forth.

It shall happen, when they amar (tell) you, Where shall we yatzaa (go) forth? Then you shall amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Such as are for mawath (death), to mawath (death); and such as are for the charab (sword), to the charab (sword); and such as are for the famine, to the famine; and such as are for Shabay, to Shabay.

I will paqad (appoint) over them arabai (four) mashapachah (kinds), says Yahawah: the charab (sword) to harag (kill), and the dogs to tear, and the birds of the sky, and the animals of the aratz (earth), to akal (devour) and to shachath (destroy).

I will nathan (cause) them to be tossed back and forth among all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (earth), because of Manashah, the ban (son) of Yachazaqayah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), for that which he did in Yarawashalam.
For who will have pity on you, Yarawashalam? or who will nawad (bemoan) you? or who will sawar (turn) aside to shaal (ask) of your shalawam (welfare)?
You have rejected me, says Yahawah, you have gone backward: therefore have I stretched out my yad (hand) against you, and destroyed you; I am weary with repenting.
I have winnowed them with a fan in the gates of the aratz (land); I have bereaved them of children, I have destroyed my im (people); they didn't shawab (turn back / repent) from their darak (ways).

Their alamanah (widows) are itzam (increased) to me above the sand of the yam (seas); I have brought on them against the am (mother) of the young men a shadad (destroyer) at noonday: I have caused anguish and terrors to napal (fall) on her suddenly.

She who has borne shabai (seven) languishes; she has given up the spirit; her shamash (sun) is gone down while it was yet yawamam (day); she has been disappointed and chapar (confounded): and their shaarayath (residue) will I nathan (deliver) to the charab (sword) panayam (before) their ayab (enemies), says Yahawah.

Woe is me, my am (mother), that you have borne me a ayash (man) of rayab (strife) and a ayash (man) of contention to the whole aratz (earth)! I have not lent, neither have men lent to me; yet everyone of them qalal (curses) me.

Yahawah said, Most certainly I will strengthen you for sharah (good); most certainly I will cause the ayab (enemy) to pagai (make) supplication to you in the ith (time) of rai (evil) and in the ith (time) of tzarah (affliction).
Can one raii (break) barazal (iron), even barazal (iron) from the tzapawan (north), and brass?
Your chayal (substance) and your treasures will I nathan (give) for a spoil without price, and that for all your chataah (sins), even in all your borders.
I will ibar (make) them to pass with your ayab (enemies) into a aratz (land) which you don't yadai (know); for a ash (fire) is kindled in my ap (anger), which shall yaqad (burn) on you.

Yahawah, you yadai (know); zakar (remember) me, and paqad (visit) me, and avenge me of my persecutors; don't take me away in your ap (longsuffering): yadai (know) that for your sake I have suffered reproach.

Your dabar (words) were found, and I ate them; and your dabar (words) were to me a joy and the rejoicing of my labab (heart): for I am called by your sham (name), Yahawah, Alahayam of tzabaa (armies).
I didn't yashab (sit) in the sawad (assembly) of those who make merry, nor rejoiced; I sat badad (alone) panayam (because) of your yad (hand); for you have filled me with indignation.
Why is my pain natzach (perpetual), and my makah (wound) Anash, which refuses to be healed? Will you Akazab be to me as a deceitful brook, as mayam (waters) that aman (fail)?

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah, If you shawab (turn back / repent), then will I shawab (turn back / repent) you again, that you may imad (stand) panayam (before) me; and if you yatzaa (take) forth the Yaqar from the vile, you shall be as my pah (mouth): they shall shawab (turn back / repent) to you, but you shall not shawab (turn back / repent) to them.

I will nathan (make) you to this im (people) a fortified bronze wall; and they shall fight against you, but they shall not yakal (prevail) against you; for I am with you to yashai (save) you and to natzal (deliver) you, says Yahawah.
I will natzal (deliver) you out of the yad (hand) of the rai (wicked), and I will padah (redeem) you out of the kap (hand) of the irayatz (terrible).
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came also to me, saying,
You shall not take a ashah (wife), neither shall you have ban (sons) or bath (daughters), in this place.

For thus amar (says) Yahawah concerning the ban (sons) and concerning the bath (daughters) who are yalad (born) in this place, and concerning their am (mothers) who bore them, and concerning their abawath (fathers) who Yalawad their father in this aratz (land):

They shall mawath (die) grievous mamawath (deaths): they shall not be lamented, neither shall they be buried; they shall be as dung on the surface of the adamah (ground); and they shall be consumed by the charab (sword), and by famine; and their nabalah (dead) bodies shall be food for the birds of the sky, and for the animals of the aratz (earth).

For thus amar (says) Yahawah, Don't bawaa (enter) into the bayath (house) of mourning, neither yalak (go) to lament, neither nawad (bemoan) them; for I have taken asap (away) my shalawam (peace) from this im (people), says Yahawah, even loving chasad (kindness) and tender racham (mercies).
Both gadawal (great) and qatan (small) shall mawath (die) in this aratz (land); they shall not be buried, neither shall men lament for them, nor cut themselves, nor make themselves bald for them;

neither shall men break abal (bread) for them in mourning, to nacham (comfort) them for the mawath (dead); neither shall men give them the cup of consolation to shaqah (drink) for their ab (father) or for their am (mother).
You shall not bawaa (go) into the bayath (house) of feasting to yashab (sit) with them, to akal (eat) and to drink.

For thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): Behold, I will shabath (cause) to cease out of this place, before your iyan (eyes) and in your yawam (days), the qawal (voice) of mirth and the qawal (voice) of gladness, the qawal (voice) of the chathan (bridegroom) and the qawal (voice) of the kalah (bride).

It shall happen, when you shall show this im (people) all these dabar (words), and they shall amar (tell) you, Why has Yahawah pronounced all this gadawal (great) rai (evil) against us? or what is our iwan (iniquity)? or what is our chataah (sin) that we have committed against Yahawah our Alahayam?

Then you shall amar (tell) them, Because your abawath (fathers) have forsaken me, says Yahawah, and have walked achar (after) other Alahayam, and have served them, and have worshiped them, and have forsaken me, and have not kept my thawarah (law);

and you have done raii (evil) more than your abawath (fathers); for, behold, you halak (walk) ayash (every) one achar (after) the stubbornness of his rai (evil) lab (heart), so that you don't listen to me:

therefore will I cast you forth out of this aratz (land) into the aratz (land) that you have not yadai (known), neither you nor your abawath (fathers); and there you shall ibad (serve) other Alahayam yawamam (day) and layal (night); for I will show you no favor.

Therefore, behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), says Yahawah, that it shall no more be said, As Yahawah chay (lives), who brought up the children of Yasharaal (Israel) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam;

but, As Yahawah chay (lives), who brought up the children of Yasharaal (Israel) from the aratz (land) of the tzapawan (north), and from all the aratz (countries) where he had driven them. I will shawab (turn back / repent) them again into their adamah (land) that I gave to their abawath (fathers).

Behold, I will shalach (send) for many fishermen, says Yahawah, and they shall fish them up; and afterward I will shalach (send) for many hunters, and they shall hunt them from every har (mountain), and from every Gabaih, and out of the clefts of the salai (rocks).
For my iyan (eyes) are on all their darak (ways); they are not hidden from my panayam (face), neither is their iwan (iniquity) concealed from my iyan (eyes).

raashawan (first) I will shalam (recompense) their iwan (iniquity) and their chataah (sin) mashanah (double), because they have polluted my aratz (land) with the carcasses of their shaqawatz (detestable) things, and have filled my nachalah (inheritance) with their thawaibah (abominations).

Yahawah, my iz (strength), and my stronghold, and my manawas (refuge) in the yawam (day) of tzarah (affliction), to you shall the gawayam (nations) bawaa (come) from the apas (ends) of the aratz (earth), and shall amar (say), Our abawath (fathers) have inherited nothing but lies, vanity and things in which there is no yail (profit).
Shall a adam (man) ishah (make) to himself Alahayam, which yet are no Alahayam?
Therefore, behold, I will yadai (cause) them to know, this paim (once) will I yadai (cause) them to know my yad (hand) and my might; and they shall yadai (know) that my sham (name) is Yahawah.

The chataah (sin) of Yahawadah (Judah) is written with a pen of barazal (iron), and with the point of a diamond: it is engraved on the tablet of their lab (heart), and on the qaran (horns) of your mazabach (altars);
while their children zakar (remember) their mazabach (altars) and their Asharah by the Rainan itz (trees) on the Gabah Gabaih.

My harar (mountain) in the shadah (field), I will nathan (give) your chayal (substance) and all your treasures for a spoil, and your bamah (high) places, because of chataah (sin), throughout all your borders.

You, even of yourself, shall shamat (discontinue) from your nachalah (heritage) that I gave you; and I will cause you to ibad (serve) your ayab (enemies) in the aratz (land) which you don't yadai (know): for you have kindled a ash (fire) in my ap (anger) which shall yaqad (burn) iwalam (forever).
Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Cursed is the gabar (man) who batach (trusts) in adam (man), and shawam (makes) flesh his zarawai (arm), and whose lab (heart) sawar (departs) from Yahawah.

For he shall be like the heath in the irabah (desert), and shall not raah (see) when tawab (good) bawaa (comes), but shall shakan (inhabit) the parched places in the madabar (wilderness), a malachah (salt) aratz (land) and not inhabited.
Blessed is the gabar (man) who batach (trusts) in Yahawah, and whose trust Yahawah is.

For he shall be as a itz (tree) planted by the mayam (waters), who shalach (spreads) out its roots by the yawabal (river), and shall not fear when heat bawaa (comes), but its leaf shall be Rainan; and shall not be careful in the Shanah of drought, neither shall mawash (cease) from yielding fruit.
The lab (heart) is Iqab Anash all things, and it is exceedingly corrupt: who can yadai (know) it?
I, Yahawah, search the lab (mind), I try the lab (heart), even to nathan (give) every ayash (man) according to his darak (ways), according to the fruit of his mailal (doings).

As the partridge that sits on eggs which she has not laid, so is he who ishah (gets) riches, and not by mashapat (right); in the chatzay (midst) of his yawam (days) they shall leave him, and at his acharayath (end) he shall be a nabal (fool).
A kabawad (glorious) kasaa (throne), set on high from the raashawan (beginning), is the place of our maqadash (sanctuary).

Yahawah, the Maqawah of Yasharaal (Israel), all who forsake you shall be disappointed. Those who depart from me shall be written in the aratz (earth), because they have forsaken Yahawah, the spring of chay (living) mayam (waters).
Heal me, O Yahawah, and I shall be healed; yashai (save) me, and I shall be saved: for you are my thahalah (praise).
Behold, they amar (tell) me, Where is the dabar (word) of Yahawah? let it bawaa (come) now.

As for me, I have not hurried from being a raih (shepherd) achar (after) you; neither have I desired the Anash yawam (day); you yadai (know): that which came out of my shapah (lips) was before your panayam (face).
Don't be a terror to me: you are my refuge in the yawam (day) of rai (evil).

Let them be disappointed who persecute me, but let not me be disappointed; let them be dismayed, but don't let me be dismayed; bawaa (bring) on them the yawam (day) of rai (evil), and shabar (destroy) them with mashanah (double) destruction.

Thus said Yahawah to me: halak (go), and imad (stand) in the gate of the children of the im (people), through which the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah) bawaa (come) in, and by which they yatzaa (go) out, and in all the gates of Yarawashalam;

and amar (tell) them, Hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah, you malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), and all Yahawadah (Judah), and all the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, that bawaa (enter) in by these gates:
Thus amar (says) Yahawah, shamar (take) heed to yourselves, and nashaa (bear) no mashaa (burden) on the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day), nor bawaa (bring) it in by the gates of Yarawashalam;

neither yatzaa (carry) forth a mashaa (burden) out of your bayath (houses) on the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day) qadash (holy), neither do any malaakah (work): but make the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day), as I tzawah (commanded) your abawath (fathers).
But they didn't listen, neither natah (turn) their ear, but made their neck stiff, that they might not hear, and might not receive instruction.

It shall happen, if you diligently listen to me, says Yahawah, to bawaa (bring) in no mashaa (burden) through the gates of this Iyar on the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day), but to make the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day) qadash (holy), to do no malaakah (work) therein;

then shall there bawaa (enter) in by the gates of this Iyar malak (kings) and shar (princes) sitting on the kasaa (throne) of Dawad, riding in chariots and on horses, they, and their shar (princes), the men of Yahawadah (Judah), and the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam; and this Iyar shall yashab (remain) iwalam (forever).

They shall bawaa (come) from the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and from the places around Yarawashalam, and from the aratz (land) of Banayamayan, and from the lowland, and from the har (hill) country, and from the Nagab, bringing burnt ilah (offerings), and zabach (sacrifices), and meal manachah (offerings), and frankincense, and bringing sacrifices of thanksgiving, to the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

But if you will not listen to me to make the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day) qadash (holy), and not to nashaa (bear) a mashaa (burden) and bawaa (enter) in at the gates of Yarawashalam on the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day); then will I yatzath (kindle) a ash (fire) in its gates, and it shall akal (devour) the palaces of Yarawashalam, and it shall not be quenched.
The dabar (word) which came to Yaramayah from Yahawah, saying,
qawam (arise), and yarad (go) down to the potter's bayath (house), and there I will cause you to hear my dabar (words).
Then I went down to the potter's bayath (house), and behold, he was making a malaakah (work) on the wheels.
When the vessel that he made of the clay was marred in the yad (hand) of the potter, he made it again achar (another) vessel, as seemed yashar (good) to the potter to ishah (make) it.
Then the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), can't I do with you as this potter? says Yahawah. Behold, as the clay in the potter's yad (hand), so are you in my yad (hand), bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).
At what instant I shall dabar (speak) concerning a gaway (nation), and concerning a mamalakah (kingdom), to nathash (pluck) up and to nathatz (break) down and to abad (destroy) it;
if that gaway (nation), concerning which I have spoken, shawab (turn back / repent) from their rai (evil), I will nacham (repent) of the rai (evil) that I thought to do to them.
At what instant I shall dabar (speak) concerning a gaway (nation), and concerning a mamalakah (kingdom), to banah (build) and to plant it;
if they do that which is rai (evil) in my iyan (sight), that they not obey my qawal (voice), then I will nacham (repent) of the tawab (good), with which I said I would yatab (benefit) them.

Now therefore, amar (speak) to the men of Yahawadah (Judah), and to the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, saying, Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Behold, I frame rai (evil) against you, and chashab (devise) a machashabah (device) against you: shawab (turn back / repent) you now everyone from his rai (evil) darak (way), and yatab (amend) your darak (ways) and your mailal (doings).
But they amar (say), It is in vain; for we will yalak (walk) achar (after) our own machashabah (devices), and we will do everyone after the stubbornness of his rai (evil) lab (heart).
Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah: shaal (ask) now among the gawayam (nations), who has heard such things; the virgin of Yasharaal (Israel) has done a very Shairawarah thing.
Shall the snow of Labanawan fail from the tzawar (rock) of the shadah (field)? Shall the Qar mayam (waters) that nazal (flow) down from afar be dried up?

For my im (people) have forgotten me, they have burned qatar (incense) to false Alahayam; and they have been made to stumble in their darak (ways), in the ancient shabayal (paths), to yalak (walk) in byways, in a darak (way) not built up;
to shawam (make) their aratz (land) an astonishment, and a perpetual hissing; everyone who passes thereby shall be astonished, and nawad (shake) his raash (head).
I will scatter them as with an qadayam (east) rawach (wind) panayam (before) the ayab (enemy); I will show them the back, and not the panayam (face), in the yawam (day) of their calamity.

Then they said, yalak (come), and let us chashab (devise) machashabah (devices) against Yaramayah; for the thawarah (law) shall not abad (perish) from the kahan (priest), nor itzah (counsel) from the chakam (wise), nor the dabar (word) from the nabayaa (prophet). yalak (come), and let us strike him with the lashawan (tongue), and let us not give heed to any of his dabar (words).
Give heed to me, Yahawah, and listen to the qawal (voice) of those who contend with me.

Shall rai (evil) be recompensed for tawab (good)? for they have dug a shawachah (pit) for my napash (soul). zakar (remember) how I stood panayam (before) you to dabar (speak) tawab (good) for them, to shawab (turn back / repent) away your chamah (wrath) from them.

Therefore nathan (deliver) up their children to the famine, and give them over to the yad (power) of the charab (sword); and let their wives Shakawal childless, and alamanah (widows); and let their men be slain of mawath (death), and their young men struck of the charab (sword) in battle.
Let a cry be heard from their bayath (houses), when you shall bawaa (bring) a gadawad (troop) suddenly on them; for they have dug a shawachah (pit) to take me, and hid snares for my feet.

Yet, Yahawah, you yadai (know) all their itzah (counsel) against me to kill me; don't kapar (forgive) their iwan (iniquity), neither machah (blot) out their chataah (sin) from your panayam (sight); but let them be overthrown panayam (before) you; ishah (deal) you with them in the ith (time) of your ap (anger).
Thus said Yahawah, halak (go), and qanah (buy) a potter's charash (earthen) bottle, and take some of the zaqan (elders) of the im (people), and of the zaqan (elders) of the kahan (priests);
and yatzaa (go) forth to the Gayaa of the ban (son) of Hanam, which is by the entry of the gate Harsith, and qaraa (proclaim) there the dabar (words) that I shall dabar (tell) you;

and amar (say), Hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah, malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), and yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam: thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), Behold, I will bawaa (bring) rai (evil) on this place, which whoever hears, his ears shall tingle.

Because they have forsaken me, and have estranged this place, and have burned qatar (incense) in it to other Alahayam, that they didn't yadai (know), they and their abawath (fathers) and the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah); and have filled this place with the dam (blood) of naqay (innocents),

and have built the bamah (high) places of Bail, to sharap (burn) their ban (sons) in the ash (fire) for burnt ilah (offerings) to Bail; which I didn't tzawah (command), nor spoke it, neither came it into my lab (mind):
therefore, behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), says Yahawah, that this place shall no more be called Thapath, nor The Gayaa of the ban (son) of Hanam, but The Gayaa of Slaughter.

I will make void the itzah (counsel) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam in this place; and I will napal (cause) them to fall by the charab (sword) panayam (before) their ayab (enemies), and by the yad (hand) of those who seek their napash (life): and their nabalah (dead) bodies will I nathan (give) to be food for the birds of the sky, and for the animals of the aratz (earth).
I will shawam (make) this Iyar an astonishment, and a hissing; everyone who passes thereby shall be astonished and hiss because of all its makah (plagues).

I will cause them to akal (eat) the flesh of their ban (sons) and the flesh of their bath (daughters); and they shall akal (eat) everyone the flesh of his rai (friend), in the Matzawar and in the distress, with which their ayab (enemies), and those who seek their napash (life), shall distress them.
Then you shall shabar (break) the bottle in the iyan (sight) of the men who halak (go) with you,

and shall amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): Even so will I shabar (break) this im (people) and this Iyar, as one shabar (breaks) a potter's vessel, that can't be made whole again; and they shall bury in Thapath, until there is no place to bury.
Thus will I do to this place, says Yahawah, and to its yashab (inhabitants), even making this Iyar as Thapath:

and the bayath (houses) of Yarawashalam, and the bayath (houses) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), which are tamaa (defiled), shall be as the place of Thapath, even all the bayath (houses) on whose roofs they have burned qatar (incense) to all the tzabaa (army) of the sky, and have poured out drink nasak (offerings) to other Alahayam.
Then came Yaramayah from Thapath, where Yahawah had sent him to nabaa (prophesy); and he stood in the court of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house), and said to all the im (people):

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), Behold, I will bawaa (bring) on this Iyar and on all its Iyar all the rai (evil) that I have pronounced against it; because they have made their neck stiff, that they may not hear my dabar (words).
Pashachawar Pashhur, the ban (son) of Amar the kahan (priest), who was chief officer in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, heard Yaramayah nabaa (prophesying) these things.
Then Pashachawar struck Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet), and nathan (put) him in the stocks that were in the Ilayawan gate of Banayamayan, which was in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

It happened on the next macharath (day), that Pashachawar brought yatzaa (forth) Yaramayah out of the stocks. Then Yaramayah said to him, Yahawah has not called your sham (name) Pashachawar, but Magormissabib.

For thus amar (says) Yahawah, Behold, I will nathan (make) you a magawar (terror) to yourself, and to all your ahab (friends); and they shall napal (fall) by the charab (sword) of their ayab (enemies), and your iyan (eyes) shall raah (see) it; and I will nathan (give) all Yahawadah (Judah) into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Babal, and he shall galah (carry) them captive to Babal, and shall kill them with the charab (sword).

Moreover I will nathan (give) all the riches of this Iyar, and all its gains, and all the precious things of it, yes, all the treasures of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah) will I nathan (give) into the yad (hand) of their ayab (enemies); and they shall make them a prey, and take them, and bawaa (carry) them to Babal.

You, Pashachawar, and all who yashab (dwell) in your bayath (house) shall yalak (go) into Shabay; and you shall bawaa (come) to Babal, and there you shall mawath (die), and there you shall be buried, you, and all your ahab (friends), to whom you have prophesied falsely.
Yahawah, you have persuaded me, and I was persuaded; you are chazaq (stronger) than I, and have prevailed: I am become a laughing-stock all the yawam (day), every laig (one) mocks me.
For as often as I dabar (speak), I qaraa (cry) out; I qaraa (cry), Violence and destruction! because the dabar (word) of Yahawah is made a reproach to me, and a derision, all the yawam (day).

If I amar (say), I will not zakar (make) mention of him, nor dabar (speak) any more in his sham (name), then there is in my lab (heart) as it were a burning ash (fire) itzar (shut) up in my itzam (bones), and I am weary with forbearing, and I can't.

For I have heard the dabah (defaming) of many, magawar (terror) on every side. nagad (denounce), and we will nagad (denounce) him, say all my familiar friends, those who shamar (watch) for my fall; perhaps he will be persuaded, and we shall yakal (prevail) against him, and we shall take our revenge on him.

But Yahawah is with me as an awesome gabawar (mighty) one: therefore my persecutors shall stumble, and they shall not yakal (prevail); they shall be maad (utterly) disappointed, because they have not dealt shakal (wisely), even with an iwalam (forever) dishonor which shall never be forgotten.

But, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), who tests the tzadayaq (righteous), who raah (see) the kalayah (heart) and the lab (mind), let me raah (see) your vengeance on them; for to you have I revealed my rayab (cause).
shayar (sing) to Yahawah, halal (praise) Yahawah; for he has delivered the napash (soul) of the Abayawan from the yad (hand) of evildoers.
Cursed is the yawam (day) in which I was yalad (born): don't let the yawam (day) in which my am (mother) bore me be blessed.
Cursed is the ayash (man) who brought news to my ab (father), saying, A boy is yalad (born) Shamach you; making him very Shamach.
Let that ayash (man) be as the Iyar which Yahawah overthrew, and didn't nacham (repent): and let him hear a cry in the baqar (morning), and shouting at noontime;
because he didn't mawath (kill) me from the womb; and so my am (mother) would have been my qabar (grave), and her womb always harah (great).
Why came I yatzaa (forth) out of the womb to raah (see) imal (labor) and sorrow, that my yawam (days) should be consumed with bashath (shame)?

The dabar (word) which came to Yaramayah from Yahawah, when malak (king) Tzadaqayah sent Pashachawar him Pashhur the ban (son) of Malakayah, and Tzapanayah the ban (son) of Maishayah, the kahan (priest), saying,

Please inquire of Yahawah for us; for Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal makes war against us: perhaps Yahawah will ishah (deal) with us according to all his wondrous palaa (works), that he may ilah (go) up from us.
Then Yaramayah said to them, You shall amar (tell) Tzadaqayah:

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), Behold, I will sabab (turn) back the weapons of war that are in your yad (hands), with which you fight against the malak (king) of Babal, and against the Kashaday (Chaldeans) who tzawar (besiege) you, without the walls; and I will asap (gather) them into the midst of this Iyar.

I myself will fight against you with an natah (outstretched) yad (hand) and with a chazaq (strong) zarawai (arm), even in ap (anger), and in chamah (wrath), and in gadawal (great) qatzap (indignation).
I will strike the yashab (inhabitants) of this Iyar, both adam (man) and animal: they shall mawath (die) of a gadawal (great) dabar (pestilence).

Afterward, says Yahawah, I will nathan (deliver) Tzadaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and his ibad (servants), and the im (people), even such as are shaar (left) in this Iyar from the dabar (pestilence), from the charab (sword), and from the famine, into the yad (hand) of Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal, and into the yad (hand) of their ayab (enemies), and into the yad (hand) of those who seek their napash (life): and he shall strike them with the pah (edge) of the charab (sword); he shall not spare them, neither have pity, nor have racham (mercy).
To this im (people) you shall amar (say), Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Behold, I nathan (set) panayam (before) you the darak (way) of chay (life) and the darak (way) of mawath (death).

He who yashab (remains) in this Iyar shall mawath (die) by the charab (sword), and by the famine, and by the dabar (pestilence); but he who goes out, and passes over to the Kashaday (Chaldeans) who tzawar (besiege) you, he shall chayah (live), and his napash (life) shall be to him for a prey.

For I have shawam (set) my panayam (face) on this Iyar for rai (evil), and not for tawab (good), says Yahawah: it shall be given into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Babal, and he shall sharap (burn) it with ash (fire).
Touching the bayath (house) of the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah:

bayath (house) of Dawad, thus amar (says) Yahawah, Execute justice in the baqar (morning), and natzal (deliver) him who is robbed out of the yad (hand) of the oppressor, lest my chamah (wrath) yatzaa (go) forth like ash (fire), and bair (burn) so that none can quench it, panayam (because) of the rai (evil) of your mailal (doings).

Behold, I am against you, O yashab (inhabitant) of the valley, and of the tzawar (rock) of the mayashawar (plain), says Yahawah; you that amar (say), Who shall come down bawaa (against) us? or who shall enter into our habitations?
I will paqad (punish) you according to the fruit of your mailal (doings), says Yahawah; and I will yatzath (kindle) a ash (fire) in her Yair, and it shall akal (devour) all that is around her.
Thus said Yahawah: yarad (go) down to the bayath (house) of the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and dabar (speak) there this dabar (word),

amar (say), Hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), who yashab (sits) on the kasaa (throne) of Dawad, you, and your ibad (servants), and your im (people) who bawaa (enter) in by these gates.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: ishah (execute) justice and tzadaqah (righteousness), and natzal (deliver) him who is robbed out of the yad (hand) of the oppressor: and do no wrong, do no violence, to the foreigner, the fatherless, nor the alamanah (widow); neither shed naqay (innocent) dam (blood) in this place.

For if you do this thing ishah (indeed), then shall there bawaa (enter) in by the gates of this bayath (house) malak (kings) sitting on the kasaa (throne) of Dawad, riding in chariots and on horses, he, and his ibad (servants), and his im (people).
But if you will not hear these dabar (words), I shabai (swear) by myself, says Yahawah, that this bayath (house) shall become a desolation.

For thus amar (says) Yahawah concerning the bayath (house) of the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah): You are Galaid to me, the raash (head) of Labanawan. Yet surely I will shayath (make) you a madabar (wilderness), Iyar which are not inhabited.
I will qadash (prepare) destroyers against you, everyone with his weapons; and they shall karath (cut) down your choice cedars, and napal (cast) them into the ash (fire).
Many gawayam (nations) shall ibar (pass) by this Iyar, and they shall amar (say) every ayash (man) to his neighbor, Why has Yahawah done thus to this gadawal (great) Iyar?
Then they shall amar (answer), Because they forsook the barayath (covenant) of Yahawah their Alahayam, and worshiped other Alahayam, and served them.

Don't weep for the mawath (dead), neither nawad (bemoan) him; but weep bitterly for him who goes halak (away); for he shall shawab (turn back / repent) no more, nor raah (see) his native aratz (country).

For thus amar (says) Yahawah touching Shalawam the ban (son) of Yaashayah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), who reigned instead of Yaashayah his ab (father), and who went yatzaa (forth) out of this place: He shall not shawab (turn back / repent) there any more.
But in the place where they have led him galah (captive), there shall he mawath (die), and he shall raah (see) this aratz (land) no more.
Woe to him who banah (builds) his bayath (house) by unrighteousness, and his rooms by injustice; who uses his neighbor's ibad (service) without wages, and doesn't nathan (give) him his hire;
who amar (says), I will banah (build) me a wide bayath (house) and spacious rooms, and cuts him out windows; and it is ceiling with cedar, and painted with vermilion.
Shall you malak (reign), because you strive to excel in cedar? Didn't your ab (father) akal (eat) and drink, and do justice and tzadaqah (righteousness)? then it was tawab (well) with him.
He judged the cause of the Inay and Abayawan; then it was tawab (well). Wasn't this to daith (know) me? says Yahawah.
But your iyan (eyes) and your lab (heart) are not but for your covetousness, and for shedding naqay (innocent) dam (blood), and for oppression, and for violence, to do it.

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah concerning Yahawayaqayam the ban (son) of Yaashayah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah): they shall not lament for him, saying, Ah my ach (brother)! or, Ah achawath (sister)! They shall not lament for him, saying Ah Adawan! or, Ah his glory!
He shall be buried with the qabawarah (burial) of a donkey, drawn and cast forth beyond the gates of Yarawashalam.
ilah (go) up to Labanawan, and cry; and nathan (lift) up your qawal (voice) in Bashan, and cry from Abarim; for all your lovers are destroyed.
I spoke to you in your shalawah (prosperity); but you said, I will not hear. This has been your darak (way) from your youth, that you didn't obey my qawal (voice).
The rawach (wind) shall raih (feed) all your raih (shepherds), and your lovers shall yalak (go) into Shabay: surely then you will be bawash (ashamed) and kalam (confounded) for all your wickedness.
yashab (inhabitant) of Labanawan, who makes your nest in the cedars, how greatly to be pitied you will be when pangs bawaa (come) on you, the pain as of a yalad (woman) in travail!
As I chay (live), says Yahawah, though Kanayahaw the ban (son) of Yahawayaqayam malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) were the signet on my yamayan (right) yad (hand), yet would I pluck you there;

and I will nathan (give) you into the yad (hand) of those who seek your napash (life), and into the yad (hand) of them of whom you are Yagawar, even into the yad (hand) of Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal, and into the yad (hand) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans).
I will cast you out, and your am (mother) who bore you, into achar (another) aratz (country), where you were not yalad (born); and there you will mawath (die).
But to the aratz (land) whereunto their soul longs to shawab (turn back / repent), there shall they not shawab (turn back / repent).

Is this ayash (man) Kanayahaw a despised broken vessel? is he a vessel in which none Chapatz? why are they cast out, he and his zarai (seed), and are cast into the aratz (land) which they don't yadai (know)?
O aratz (earth), aratz (earth), aratz (earth), hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, kathab (write) you this ayash (man) Irayaray, a gabar (man) who shall not tzalach (prosper) in his yawam (days); for no more shall a ayash (man) of his zarai (seed) tzalach (prosper), sitting on the kasaa (throne) of Dawad, and ruling in Yahawadah (Judah).
Woe to the raih (shepherds) who abad (destroy) and scatter the sheep of my pasture! says Yahawah.

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), against the raih (shepherds) who raih (feed) my im (people): You have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them; behold, I will paqad (visit) on you the rai (evil) of your mailal (doings), says Yahawah.

I will gather the shaarayath (remnant) of my flock out of all the aratz (countries) where I have driven them, and will shawab (turn back / repent) them again to their Nawah; and they shall be fruitful and multiply.
I will qawam (set) up raih (shepherds) over them, who shall raih (feed) them; and they shall yaraa (fear) no more, nor be dismayed, neither shall any be lacking, says Yahawah.

Behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), says Yahawah, that I will qawam (raise) to Dawad a tzadayaq (righteous) Branch, and he shall malak (reign) as malak (king) and deal shakal (wisely), and shall ishah (execute) justice and tzadaqah (righteousness) in the aratz (land).
In his yawam (days) Yahawadah (Judah) shall be saved, and Yasharaal (Israel) shall shakan (dwell) safely; and this is his sham (name) by which he shall be called: Yahawah our righteousness.

Therefore, behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), says Yahawah, that they shall no more amar (say), As Yahawah chay (lives), who brought up the children of Yasharaal (Israel) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam;

but, As Yahawah chay (lives), who brought up and who led the zarai (seed) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) out of the tzapawan (north) aratz (country), and from all the aratz (countries) where I had driven them. They shall yashab (dwell) in their own adamah (land).

Concerning the nabayaa (prophets). My lab (heart) qarab (within) me is shabar (broken), all my itzam (bones) shake; I am like a drunken ayash (man), and like a gabar (man) whom yayan (wine) has ibar (overcome), panayam (because) of Yahawah, and because of his qadash (holy) dabar (words).

For the aratz (land) is malaa (full) of naap (adulterers); for panayam (because) of alah (swearing) the aratz (land) mourns; the naah (pastures) of the madabar (wilderness) are dried up. Their course is rai (evil), and their might is not right;
for both nabayaa (prophet) and kahan (priest) are profane; yes, in my bayath (house) have I found their wickedness, says Yahawah.

Therefore their darak (way) shall be to them as slippery places in the apalah (darkness): they shall be driven on, and napal (fall) therein; for I will bawaa (bring) rai (evil) on them, even the Shanah of their visitation, says Yahawah.
I have seen folly in the nabayaa (prophets) of Shamarawan; they prophesied by Bail, and caused my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel) to thaih (err).

In the nabayaa (prophets) of Yarawashalam also I have seen a Shairawarah thing: they naap (commit) adultery, and halak (walk) in lies; and they chazaq (strengthen) the yad (hands) of evildoers, so that ayash (none) does shawab (turn back / repent) from his wickedness: they are all of them become to me as Sadam, and its yashab (inhabitants) as Imarah.

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) concerning the nabayaa (prophets): Behold, I will akal (feed) them with wormwood, and shaqah (make) them drink the mayam (water) of gall; for from the nabayaa (prophets) of Yarawashalam is ungodliness gone yatzaa (forth) into all the aratz (land).

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), Don't listen to the dabar (words) of the nabayaa (prophets) who nabaa (prophesy) to you: they teach you vanity; they dabar (speak) a vision of their own lab (heart), and not out of the pah (mouth) of Yahawah.

They amar (say) continually to those who despise me, Yahawah has said, You shall have shalawam (peace); and to everyone who halak (walks) in the stubbornness of his own lab (heart) they amar (say), No rai (evil) shall bawaa (come) on you.
For who has stood in the council of Yahawah, that he should raah (see) and hear his dabar (word)? who has marked my dabar (word), and heard it?
Behold, the storm of Yahawah, his chamah (wrath), has gone yatzaa (forth). Yes, a whirling storm. It shall burst on the raash (head) of the rashai (wicked).

The ap (anger) of Yahawah shall not shawab (turn back / repent), until he has executed, and until he have performed the intents of his lab (heart): in the acharayath (latter) yawam (days) you shall bayan (understand) it bayanah (perfectly).
I sent not these nabayaa (prophets), yet they ran: I didn't dabar (speak) to them, yet they prophesied.

But if they had stood in my council, then had they caused my im (people) to hear my dabar (words), and had turned them from their rai (evil) darak (way), and from the rai (evil) of their mailal (doings).
Am I a Alahayam at qarawab (hand), says Yahawah, and not a Alahayam Rachawaq off?
Can any hide himself in secret places so that I shall not raah (see) him? says Yahawah. Don't I Malaa shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth)? says Yahawah.
I have heard what the nabayaa (prophets) have said, who nabaa (prophesy) lies in my sham (name), saying, I have dreamed, I have dreamed.
How long shall this be in the lab (heart) of the nabayaa (prophets) who nabaa (prophesy) lies, even the nabayaa (prophets) of the Tharamah of their own lab (heart)?

who chashab (think) to cause my im (people) to forget my sham (name) by their chalawam (dreams) which they tell every ayash (man) to his neighbor, as their abawath (fathers) forgot my sham (name) for Bail.

The nabayaa (prophet) who has a chalawam (dream), let him tell a chalawam (dream); and he who has my dabar (word), let him dabar (speak) my dabar (word) faithfully. What is the straw to the wheat? says Yahawah.
Isn't my dabar (word) kah (like) ash (fire)? says Yahawah; and like a hammer that breaks the salai (rock) in pieces?
Therefore, behold, I am against the nabayaa (prophets), says Yahawah, who steal my dabar (words) everyone from his neighbor.
Behold, I am against the nabayaa (prophets), says Yahawah, who use their lashawan (tongues), and say, He says.

Behold, I am against those who nabaa (prophesy) lying chalawam (dreams), says Yahawah, and do tell them, and cause my im (people) to thaih (err) by their lies, and by their vain boasting: yet I didn't shalach (send) them, nor tzawah (commanded) them; neither do they yail (profit) this im (people) at all, says Yahawah.

When this im (people), or the nabayaa (prophet), or a kahan (priest), shall shaal (ask) you, saying, What is the mashaa (burden) of Yahawah? Then you shall amar (tell) them, What mashaa (burden)! I will cast you off, says Yahawah.
As for the nabayaa (prophet), and the kahan (priest), and the im (people), who shall amar (say), The mashaa (burden) of Yahawah, I will even paqad (punish) that ayash (man) and his bayath (house).
You shall amar (say) everyone to his neighbor, and everyone to his ach (brother), What has Yahawah answered? and, What has Yahawah spoken?

You shall zakar (mention) the mashaa (burden) of Yahawah no more: for every ayash (man's) own dabar (word) shall be his mashaa (burden); for you have perverted the dabar (words) of the chay (living) Alahayam, of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) our Alahayam.
You shall amar (say) to the nabayaa (prophet), What has Yahawah answered you? and, What has Yahawah spoken?

But if you amar (say), The mashaa (burden) of Yahawah; therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah: Because you amar (say) this dabar (word), The mashaa (burden) of Yahawah, and I have sent to you, saying, You shall not amar (say), The mashaa (burden) of Yahawah;
therefore, behold, I will utterly forget you, and I will cast you off, and the Iyar that I gave to you and to your abawath (fathers), away from my panayam (presence):
and I will nathan (bring) an iwalam (forever) reproach on you, and a perpetual shame, which shall not be forgotten.

Yahawah showed me, and behold, shanayam (two) baskets of figs set panayam (before) the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, achar (after) that Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal had carried away galah (captive) Yakanayah the ban (son) of Yahawayaqayam, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and the shar (princes) of Yahawadah (Judah), with the craftsmen and smiths, from Yarawashalam, and had brought them to Babal.
One basket had very tawab (good) figs, like the figs that are first-ripe; and the other basket had very rai (bad) figs, which could not be eaten, they were so rai (bad).
Then Yahawah said to me, What do you raah (see), Yaramayah? I said, Figs; the tawab (good) figs, very tawab (good); and the rai (bad), very rai (bad), that can't be eaten, they are so rai (bad).
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): Like these tawab (good) figs, so will I nakar (regard) the captives of Yahawadah (Judah), whom I have sent out of this place into the aratz (land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), for tawab (good).

For I will shawam (set) my iyan (eyes) on them for tawab (good), and I will shawab (turn back / repent) them again to this aratz (land): and I will banah (build) them, and not haras (pull) them down; and I will plant them, and not nathash (pluck) them up.

I will nathan (give) them a lab (heart) to yadai (know) me, that I am Yahawah: and they shall be my im (people), and I will be their Alahayam; for they shall shawab (turn back / repent) to me with their whole lab (heart).

As the rai (bad) figs, which can't be eaten, they are so rai (bad), surely thus amar (says) Yahawah, So will I nathan (give) up Tzadaqayah the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and his shar (princes), and the shaarayath (residue) of Yarawashalam, who shaar (remain) in this aratz (land), and those who yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam,

I will even nathan (give) them up to be tossed back and forth among all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (earth) for rai (evil); to be a reproach and a proverb, a taunt and a qalalah (curse), in all places where I shall drive them.
I will shalach (send) the charab (sword), the famine, and the dabar (pestilence), among them, until they be consumed from off the adamah (land) that I gave to them and to their abawath (fathers).

The dabar (word) that came to Yaramayah concerning all the im (people) of Yahawadah (Judah), in the rabayaiy (fourth) Shanah of Yahawayaqayam the ban (son) of Yaashayah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) (the same was the raashanay (first) Shanah of Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal),
which Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet) spoke to all the im (people) of Yahawadah (Judah), and to all the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, saying:

From the thirteenth Shanah of Yaashayah the ban (son) of Amawan, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), even to this yawam (day), these isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three) Shanah, the dabar (word) of Yahawah has come to me, and I have spoken to you, rising up shakam (early) and speaking; but you have not listened.
Yahawah has sent to you all his ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets), rising up shakam (early) and sending them (but you have not listened, nor inclined your ear to hear)

saying, shawab (turn back / repent) now everyone from his rai (evil) darak (way), and from the rai (evil) of your mailal (doings), and yashab (dwell) in the adamah (land) that Yahawah has given to you and to your abawath (fathers), from of old and even forevermore;

and don't yalak (go) achar (after) other Alahayam to ibad (serve) them or shachah (worship) them, and don't provoke me to kais (anger) with the maishah (work) of your yad (hands); and I will do you no raii (harm).
Yet you have not listened to me, says Yahawah; that you may provoke me to kais (anger) with the maishah (work) of your yad (hands) to your own rai (hurt).
Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): Because you have not heard my dabar (words),

behold, I will shalach (send) and take all the mashapachah (families) of the tzapawan (north), says Yahawah, and I will send to Nabawakadanaatzar the malak (king) of Babal, my ibad (servant), and will bawaa (bring) them against this aratz (land), and against its yashab (inhabitants), and against all these gawayam (nations) around; and I will utterly charam (destroy) them, and shawam (make) them an astonishment, and a hissing, and perpetual desolations.

Moreover I will abad (take) from them the qawal (voice) of mirth and the qawal (voice) of gladness, the qawal (voice) of the chathan (bridegroom) and the qawal (voice) of the kalah (bride), the qawal (sound) of the millstones, and the awar (light) of the nayar (lamp).
This whole aratz (land) shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these gawayam (nations) shall ibad (serve) the malak (king) of Babal shabaiyam (seventy) Shanah.

It shall happen, when shabaiyam (seventy) Shanah are accomplished, that I will paqad (punish) the malak (king) of Babal, and that gaway (nation), says Yahawah, for their iwan (iniquity), and the aratz (land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans); and I will shawam (make) it desolate iwalam (forever).

I will bawaa (bring) on that aratz (land) all my dabar (words) which I have pronounced against it, even all that is written in this book, which Yaramayah has prophesied against all the gawayam (nations).

For many gawayam (nations) and gadawal (great) malak (kings) shall ibad (make) bondservants of them, even of them; and I will shalam (recompense) them according to their pail (deeds), and according to the maishah (work) of their yad (hands).

For thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), to me: take this cup of the yayan (wine) of chamah (wrath) at my yad (hand), and cause all the gawayam (nations), to whom I shalach (send) you, to shaqah (drink) it.
They shall drink, and reel back and forth, and be halal (mad), panayam (because) of the charab (sword) that I will shalach (send) among them.
Then took I the cup at yahawah (yahweh's) yad (hand), and made all the gawayam (nations) to shaqah (drink), to whom Yahawah had sent me:

Yarawashalam, and the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and its malak (kings), and its shar (princes), to nathan (make) them a desolation, an astonishment, a hissing, and a qalalah (curse), as it is this yawam (day);
Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam, and his ibad (servants), and his shar (princes), and all his im (people);

and all the mixed people, and all the malak (kings) of the aratz (land) of the Iwatz, and all the malak (kings) of the Palashathay (Philistines), and Ashaqalawan, and Izah, and Iqarawan, and the shaarayath (remnant) Ashadawad Ashdod;
Adam, and Mawaab, and the children of Imawan;
and all the malak (kings) of Tzar, and all the malak (kings) of Tzayadawan, and the malak (kings) of the isle which is ibar (beyond) the yam (sea);
Dadan, and Thayamaa, and Bawaz, and all who have the corners of their beard cut off;
and all the malak (kings) of Irab, and all the malak (kings) of the mixed people who shakan (dwell) in the madabar (wilderness);
and all the malak (kings) of Zamaray, and all the malak (kings) of Iyalam, and all the malak (kings) of the Maday;

and all the malak (kings) of the tzapawan (north), Rachawaq and qarawab (near), one with ach (another); and all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (world), which are on the surface of the adamah (earth): and the malak (king) of Shashak shall drink achar (after) them.

You shall amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): Drink, and be Shakar, vomit, napal (fall), and qawam (rise) no more, panayam (because) of the charab (sword) which I will shalach (send) among you.
It shall be, if they refuse to take the cup at your yad (hand) to drink, then you shall amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): You shall surely drink.

For, behold, I chalal (begin) to work raii (evil) at the Iyar which is called by my sham (name); and should you be utterly unpunished? You shall not be unpunished; for I will qaraa (call) for a charab (sword) on all the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (earth), says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).

Therefore nabaa (prophesy) you against them all these dabar (words), and amar (tell) them, Yahawah will roar from on high, and nathan (utter) his qawal (voice) from his qadash (holy) habitation; he will mightily roar against his Nawah; he will give a shout, as those who tread grapes, against all the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (earth).

A noise shall bawaa (come) even to the end of the aratz (earth); for Yahawah has a rayab (controversy) with the gawayam (nations); he will enter into shapat (judgment) with all flesh: as for the rashai (wicked), he will nathan (give) them to the charab (sword), says Yahawah.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), Behold, rai (evil) shall yatzaa (go) forth from gaway (nation) to gaway (nation), and a gadawal (great) storm shall be raised up from the uttermost parts of the aratz (earth).

The Chalal of Yahawah shall be at that yawam (day) from qatzah (one) end of the aratz (earth) even to the other end of the aratz (earth): they shall not be lamented, neither gathered, nor buried; they shall be dung on the surface of the adamah (ground).

Wail, you raih (shepherds), and cry; and wallow in dust, you adayar (principal) of the flock; for the yawam (days) of your slaughter and of your dispersions are fully come, and you shall napal (fall) like a goodly vessel.
The raih (shepherds) shall have no manawas (way) to abad (flee), nor the adayar (principal) of the flock to palayatah (escape).
A qawal (voice) of the cry of the raih (shepherds), and the wailing of the adayar (principal) of the flock! for Yahawah lays shadad (waste) their pasture.
The peaceable folds are brought to damam (silence) panayam (because) of the charawan (fierce) ap (anger) of Yahawah.

He has left his sak (covert), as the kapayar (lion); for their aratz (land) has become an astonishment panayam (because) of the charawan (fierceness) of the oppression, and panayam (because) of his charawan (fierce) ap (anger).
In the raashayath (beginning) of the mamalakawath (reign) of Yahawayaqayam the ban (son) of Yaashayah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), came this dabar (word) from Yahawah, saying,

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: imad (stand) in the court of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house), and dabar (speak) to all the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), which bawaa (come) to shachah (worship) in yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house), all the dabar (words) that I tzawah (command) you to dabar (speak) to them; don't diminish a dabar (word).

It may be they will listen, and shawab (turn back / repent) every ayash (man) from his rai (evil) darak (way); that I may nacham (repent) me of the rai (evil) which I chashab (purpose) to do to them panayam (because) of the rai (evil) of their mailal (doings).
You shall amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) Yahawah: If you will not listen to me, to yalak (walk) in my thawarah (law), which I have nathan (set) panayam (before) you,
to listen to the dabar (words) of my ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets), whom I shalach (send) to you, even rising up shakam (early) and sending them, but you have not listened;
then will I nathan (make) this bayath (house) like Shayalah, and will nathan (make) this Iyar a qalalah (curse) to all the gawayay (nations) of the aratz (earth).
The kahan (priests) and the nabayaa (prophets) and all the im (people) heard Yaramayah speaking these dabar (words) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

It happened, when Yaramayah had made an kalah (end) of speaking all that Yahawah had tzawah (commanded) him to dabar (speak) to all the im (people), that the kahan (priests) and the nabayaa (prophets) and all the im (people) laid hold on him, saying, You shall mawath (surely) mawath (die).

Why have you prophesied in the sham (name) of Yahawah, saying, This bayath (house) shall be like Shayalah, and this Iyar shall be charab (desolate), without yashab (inhabitant)? All the im (people) were gathered to Yaramayah in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

When the shar (princes) of Yahawadah (Judah) heard these things, they came up from the malak (king's) bayath (house) to the bayath (house) of Yahawah; and they sat in the entry of the Chadash gate of yahawah (yahweh's) house.

Then spoke the kahan (priests) and the nabayaa (prophets) to the shar (princes) and to all the im (people), saying, This ayash (man) is mashapat (worthy) of mawath (death); for he has prophesied against this Iyar, as you have heard with your ears.

Then spoke Yaramayah to all the shar (princes) and to all the im (people), saying, Yahawah sent me to nabaa (prophesy) against this bayath (house) and against this Iyar all the dabar (words) that you have heard.

Now therefore yatab (amend) your darak (ways) and your mailal (doings), and obey the qawal (voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam; and Yahawah will nacham (repent) him of the rai (evil) that he has pronounced against you.
But as for me, behold, I am in your yad (hand): do with me as is tawab (good) and yashar (right) in your eyes.

Only yadai (know) for certain that, if you put me to mawath (death), you will nathan (bring) naqay (innocent) dam (blood) on yourselves, and on this Iyar, and on its yashab (inhabitants); for of a truth Yahawah has sent me to you to dabar (speak) all these dabar (words) in your ears.

Then the shar (princes) and all the im (people) said to the kahan (priests) and to the nabayaa (prophets): This ayash (man) is not mashapat (worthy) of mawath (death); for he has spoken to us in the sham (name) of Yahawah our Alahayam.
Then rose up anawash (certain) of the zaqan (elders) of the aratz (land), and spoke to all the qahal (assembly) of the im (people), saying,

Mayakayah the Mawarashathay prophesied in the yawam (days) of Chazaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah); and he spoke to all the im (people) of Yahawadah (Judah), saying, Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): Tzayawan shall be plowed as a shadah (field), and Yarawashalam shall become heaps, and the har (mountain) of the bayath (house) as the bamah (high) places of a Yair.

Did Chazaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) and all Yahawadah (Judah) put him to mawath (death)? Didn't he yaraa (fear) Yahawah, and entreat the favor of Yahawah, and Yahawah relented of the disaster which he had pronounced against them? Thus should we ishah (commit) gadawal (great) rai (evil) against our own napash (souls).

There was also a ayash (man) who prophesied in the sham (name) of Yahawah, Awarayah the ban (son) of Shamaiyah of Kiriath Qarayathayairayam; and he prophesied against this Iyar and against this aratz (land) according to all the dabar (words) of Yaramayah:

and when Yahawayaqayam the malak (king), with all his gabawar (mighty) men, and all the shar (princes), heard his dabar (words), the malak (king) sought to put him to mawath (death); but when Awarayah heard it, he was yaraa (afraid), and fled, and went into Matzarayam:
and Yahawayaqayam the malak (king) sent men into Matzarayam, Alanathan the ban (son) of Ikabawar, and anawash (certain) men with him, into Matzarayam;

and they fetched yatzaa (forth) Awarayah out of Matzarayam, and brought him to Yahawayaqayam the malak (king), who killed him with the charab (sword), and cast his nabalah (dead) body into the qabar (graves) of the ban (common) im (people).
But the yad (hand) of Achayaqam the ban (son) Shapan Shaphan was with Yaramayah, that they should not nathan (give) him into the yad (hand) of the im (people) to put him to mawath (death).
In the raashayath (beginning) of the mamalakah (reign) of Yahawayaqayam the ban (son) of Yaashayah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), came this dabar (word) to Yaramayah from Yahawah, saying,
Thus amar (says) Yahawah to me: ishah (make) bonds and bars, and nathan (put) them on your neck;

and shalach (send) them to the malak (king) of Adam, and to the malak (king) of Mawaab, and to the malak (king) of the children of Ammon, and to the malak (king) of Tzar, and to the malak (king) of Tzayadawan, by the yad (hand) of the malaak (messengers) who bawaa (come) to Yarawashalam to Tzadaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah);
and give them a tzawah (command) to their adawan (masters), saying, Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), You shall amar (tell) your adawan (masters):

I have made the aratz (earth), the men and the animals that are on the surface of the aratz (earth), by my gadawal (great) kach (power) and by my natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm); and I nathan (give) it to whom it seems yashar (right) to me.

Now have I given all these aratz (lands) into the yad (hand) of Nabawakadanaatzar the malak (king) of Babal, my ibad (servant); and the animals of the shadah (field) also have I given him to ibad (serve) him.

All the gawayam (nations) shall ibad (serve) him, and his ban (son), and his ban (son's) ban (son), until the ith (time) of his own aratz (land) bawaa (come): and then many gawayam (nations) and gadawal (great) malak (kings) shall ibad (make) him their bondservant.

It shall happen, that the gaway (nation) and the mamalakah (kingdom) which will not ibad (serve) the same Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal, and that will not nathan (put) their neck under the yoke of the malak (king) of Babal, that gaway (nation) will I paqad (punish), says Yahawah, with the charab (sword), and with the famine, and with the dabar (pestilence), until I have consumed them by his yad (hand).

But as for you, don't you listen to your nabayaa (prophets), nor to your diviners, nor to your chalawam (dreams), nor to your soothsayers, nor to your sorcerers, who amar (speak) to you, saying, You shall not ibad (serve) the malak (king) of Babal:
for they nabaa (prophesy) a lie to you, to rachaq (remove) you far from your adamah (land), and that I should drive you out, and you should abad (perish).

But the gaway (nation) that shall bawaa (bring) their neck under the yoke of the malak (king) of Babal, and ibad (serve) him, that nation will I let remain in their own adamah (land), says Yahawah; and they shall ibad (till) it, and yashab (dwell) therein.

I spoke to Tzadaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) according to all these dabar (words), saying, bawaa (bring) your necks under the yoke of the malak (king) of Babal, and ibad (serve) him and his im (people), and chayah (live).

Why will you mawath (die), you and your im (people), by the charab (sword), by the famine, and by the dabar (pestilence), as Yahawah has spoken concerning the gaway (nation) that will not ibad (serve) the malak (king) of Babal?
Don't listen to the dabar (words) of the nabayaa (prophets) who amar (speak) to you, saying, You shall not ibad (serve) the malak (king) of Babal; for they nabaa (prophesy) a lie to you.

For I have not sent them, says Yahawah, but they nabaa (prophesy) falsely in my sham (name); that I may drive you out, and that you may abad (perish), you, and the nabayaa (prophets) who nabaa (prophesy) to you.

Also I spoke to the kahan (priests) and to all this im (people), saying, Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Don't listen to the dabar (words) of your nabayaa (prophets) who nabaa (prophesy) to you, saying, Behold, the vessels of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house) shall now shortly be brought again from Babal; for they nabaa (prophesy) a lie to you.
Don't listen to them; ibad (serve) the malak (king) of Babal, and chayah (live): why should this Iyar become a desolation?

But if they be nabayaa (prophets), and if the dabar (word) of Yahawah be with them, let them now pagai (make) intercession to Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), that the vessels which are yathar (left) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and in the bayath (house) of the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and at Yarawashalam, don't bawaa (go) to Babal.

For thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) concerning the pillars, and concerning the yam (sea), and concerning the bases, and concerning the yathar (residue) of the vessels that are yathar (left) in this Iyar,

which Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal didn't take, when he carried away galah (captive) Yakanayah the ban (son) of Yahawayaqayam, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), from Yarawashalam to Babal, and all the nobles of Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam;

yes, thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), concerning the vessels that are yathar (left) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and in the bayath (house) of the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and at Yarawashalam:

They shall be carried to Babal, and there shall they be, until the yawam (day) that I paqad (visit) them, says Yahawah; then will I ilah (bring) them up, and shawab (turn back / repent) them to this place.

It happened the same Shanah, in the raashayath (beginning) of the mamalakah (reign) of Tzadaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), in the rabayaiy (fourth) Shanah, in the chamayashay (fifth) chadash (month), that Chananayah the ban (son) of Izawar, the nabayaa (prophet), who was of Gabaiwan, spoke to me in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, in the iyan (presence) of the kahan (priests) and of all the im (people), saying,
Thus amar (speaks) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, I have shabar (broken) the yoke of the malak (king) of Babal.

Within yawam (two) full Shanah will I shawab (turn back / repent) again into this place all the vessels of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house), that Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal took away from this place, and carried to Babal:

and I will shawab (turn back / repent) again to this place Yakanayah the ban (son) of Yahawayaqayam, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), with all the captives of Yahawadah (Judah), who went to Babal, says Yahawah; for I will shabar (break) the yoke of the malak (king) of Babal.

Then the nabayaa (prophet) Yaramayah said to the nabayaa (prophet) Chananayah in the iyan (presence) of the kahan (priests), and in the iyan (presence) of all the im (people) who stood in the bayath (house) of Yahawah,

even the nabayaa (prophet) Yaramayah said, aman (amen): Yahawah do so; Yahawah qawam (perform) your dabar (words) which you have prophesied, to shawab (turn back / repent) again the vessels of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house), and all them of the captivity, from Babal to this place.
Nevertheless hear you now this dabar (word) that I dabar (speak) in your ears, and in the ears of all the im (people):

The nabayaa (prophets) who have been panayam (before) me and panayam (before) you of old prophesied against many aratz (countries), and against gadawal (great) mamalakah (kingdoms), of war, and of rai (evil), and of dabar (pestilence).

The nabayaa (prophet) who prophesies of shalawam (peace), when the dabar (word) of the nabayaa (prophet) shall happen, then shall the nabayaa (prophet) be yadai (known), that Yahawah has truly sent him.
Then Chananayah the nabayaa (prophet) took the bar from off the nabayaa (prophet) Yaramayah neck, and broke it.

Chananayah spoke in the iyan (presence) of all the im (people), saying, Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Even so will I shabar (break) the yoke of Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal within yawam (two) full Shanah from off the neck of all the gawayam (nations). The nabayaa (prophet) Yaramayah went his darak (way).
Then the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Yaramayah, achar (after) that Chananayah the nabayaa (prophet) had shabar (broken) the bar from off the neck of the nabayaa (prophet) Yaramayah, saying,
halak (go), and amar (tell) Chananayah, saying, Thus amar (says) Yahawah: You have shabar (broken) the bars of itz (wood); but you have made in their place bars of barazal (iron).

For thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): I have nathan (put) a yoke of barazal (iron) on the neck of all these gawayam (nations), that they may ibad (serve) Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal; and they shall ibad (serve) him: and I have given him the animals of the shadah (field) also.
Then the nabayaa (prophet) Yaramayah said to Chananayah the nabayaa (prophet), Hear now, Chananayah: Yahawah has not sent you; but you make this im (people) to batach (trust) in a lie.

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah, Behold, I will shalach (send) you away from off the surface of the adamah (earth): this Shanah you shall mawath (die), because you have spoken sarah (rebellion) against Yahawah.
So Chananayah the nabayaa (prophet) died the same Shanah in the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month).

Now these are the dabar (words) of the letter that Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet) sent from Yarawashalam to the yathar (residue) of the zaqan (elders) of the captivity, and to the kahan (priests), to the nabayaa (prophets), and to all the im (people), whom Nabawakadanaatzar had carried away galah (captive) from Yarawashalam to Babal,

(achar (after) that Yakanayah the malak (king), the gabayarah (queen) sarayas (mother), the eunuchs, the shar (princes) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam, the craftsmen, and the smiths, had departed from Yarawashalam),

by the yad (hand) of Alaishah the ban (son) Shapan Shaphan, and Gamarayah the ban (son) Chalaqayah Hilkiah, (whom Tzadaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) sent to Babal to Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal), saying,
Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), to all the captivity, whom I have caused to be carried away captive from Yarawashalam to Babal:
banah (build) bayath (houses), and yashab (dwell) in them; and plant gardens, and akal (eat) their fruit.

Take wives, and father ban (sons) and bath (daughters); and take wives for your ban (sons), and nathan (give) your bath (daughters) to anawash (husbands), that they may yalad (bear) ban (sons) and ban (daughters); and multiply there, and don't be diminished.
Seek the shalawam (peace) of the Iyar where I have caused you to be carried away galah (captive), and palal (pray) to Yahawah for it; for in its shalawam (peace) you shall have shalawam (peace).

For thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): Don't let your nabayaa (prophets) who are in the qarab (midst) of you, and your diviners, deceive you; neither listen to your chalawam (dreams) which you cause to be dreamed.
For they nabaa (prophesy) falsely to you in my sham (name): I have not sent them, says Yahawah.

For thus amar (says) Yahawah, pah (after) shabaiyam (seventy) Shanah are accomplished for Babal, I will paqad (visit) you, and qawam (perform) my tawab (good) dabar (word) toward you, in causing you to shawab (turn back / repent) to this place.

For I yadai (know) the machashabah (thoughts) that I chashab (think) toward you, says Yahawah, machashabah (thoughts) of shalawam (peace), and not of rai (evil), to nathan (give) you hope and a future.
You shall qaraa (call) on me, and you shall halak (go) and palal (pray) to me, and I will listen to you.
You shall seek me, and matzaa (find) me, when you shall search for me with all your labab (heart).

I will be found by you, says Yahawah, and I will shawab (turn back / repent) again your captivity, and I will gather you from all the gawayam (nations), and from all the places where I have driven you, says Yahawah; and I will shawab (turn back / repent) you again to the place from where I caused you to be carried away galah (captive).
Because you have said, Yahawah has raised us up nabayaa (prophets) in Babal;

thus amar (says) Yahawah concerning the malak (king) who yashab (sits) on the kasaa (throne) of Dawad, and concerning all the im (people) who yashab (dwell) in this Iyar, your ach (brothers) who haven't gone yatzaa (forth) with you into captivity;

thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies); Behold, I will shalach (send) on them the charab (sword), the famine, and the dabar (pestilence), and will nathan (make) them like Shair figs, that can't be eaten, they are so rai (bad).

I will pursue achar (after) them with the charab (sword), with the famine, and with the dabar (pestilence), and will nathan (deliver) them to be tossed back and forth among all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (earth), to be an object of horror, and an astonishment, and a hissing, and a reproach, among all the gawayam (nations) where I have driven them;

because they have not listened to my dabar (words), says Yahawah, with which I sent to them my ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets), rising up shakam (early) and sending them; but you would not hear, says Yahawah.
Hear therefore the dabar (word) of Yahawah, all you of the captivity, whom I have sent away from Yarawashalam to Babal.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), concerning Achaab the ban (son) of Qawalayah, and concerning Tzadaqayah the ban (son) of Maishayah, who nabaa (prophesy) a lie to you in my sham (name): Behold, I will nathan (deliver) them into the yad (hand) of Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal; and he shall kill them before your iyan (eyes);

and of them shall be taken up a qalalah (curse) by all the captives of Yahawadah (Judah) who are in Babal, saying, Yahawah shawam (make) you like Tzadaqayah and like Achaab, whom the malak (king) of Babal roasted in the ash (fire);

because they have worked folly in Yasharaal (Israel), and have committed naap (adultery) with their neighbors' wives, and have spoken dabar (words) in my sham (name) falsely, which I didn't tzawah (command) them; and I am he who yadai (knows), and am witness, says Yahawah.
Concerning Shamaiyah the Nachalamay you shall amar (speak), saying,

Thus amar (speaks) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, Because you have sent letters in your own sham (name) to all the im (people) who are at Yarawashalam, and to Tzapanayah the ban (son) of Maishayah, the kahan (priest), and to all the kahan (priests), saying,

Yahawah has made you kahan (priest) in the place of Yahawayadai the kahan (priest), that there may be officers in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, for every ayash (man) who is mad, and makes himself a nabaa (prophet), that you should nathan (put) him in the stocks and in shackles.
Now therefore, why have you not rebuked Yaramayah of Inathathay, who makes himself a nabaa (prophet) to you,
because he has sent to us in Babal, saying, The captivity is Arak: banah (build) bayath (houses), and yashab (dwell) in them; and plant gardens, and akal (eat) their fruit?
Tzapanayah the kahan (priest) qaraa (read) this letter in the ears of Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet).
Then came the dabar (word) of Yahawah to Yaramayah, saying,

shalach (send) to all them of the captivity, saying, Thus amar (says) Yahawah concerning Shamaiyah the Nachalamay: Because Shamaiyah has prophesied to you, and I didn't shalach (send) him, and he has caused you to batach (trust) in a lie;

therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah, Behold, I will paqad (punish) Shamaiyah the Nachalamay, and his zarai (seed); he shall not have a ayash (man) to yashab (dwell) among this im (people), neither shall he raah (see) the tawab (good) that I will do to my im (people), says Yahawah, because he has spoken sarah (rebellion) against Yahawah.
The dabar (word) that came to Yaramayah from Yahawah, saying,
Thus amar (speaks) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, kathab (write) all the dabar (words) that I have spoken to you in a book.

For, behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), says Yahawah, that I will shawab (turn back / repent) again the captivity of my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah), amar (says) Yahawah; and I will cause them to shawab (turn back / repent) to the aratz (land) that I gave to their abawath (fathers), and they shall yarash (possess) it.
These are the dabar (words) that Yahawah spoke concerning Yasharaal (Israel) and concerning Yahawadah (Judah).
For thus amar (says) Yahawah: We have heard a qawal (voice) of charadah (trembling), of pachad (fear), and not of shalawam (peace).

shaal (ask) now, and raah (see) whether a zakar (man) does yalad (travail) with child: why do I raah (see) every gabar (man) with his yad (hands) on his waist, as a yalad (woman) in travail, and all panayam (faces) are turned into paleness?
Alas! for that yawam (day) is gadawal (great), so that none is like it: it is even the ith (time) of Yaiqab tzarah (trouble); but he shall be saved out of it.

It shall come to pass in that yawam (day), says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), that I will shabar (break) his yoke from off your neck, and will burst your bonds; and strangers shall no more ibad (make) him their bondservant;
but they shall ibad (serve) Yahawah their Alahayam, and Dawad their malak (king), whom I will qawam (raise) up to them.

Therefore don't you be yaraa (afraid), O Yaiqab my ibad (servant), says Yahawah; neither be dismayed, Yasharaal (Israel): for, behold, I will yashai (save) you from Rachawaq, and your zarai (seed) from the aratz (land) of their Shabay; and Yaiqab shall shawab (turn back / repent), and shall be shaqat (quiet) and at shaan (ease), and none shall make him afraid.

For I am with you, says Yahawah, to yashai (save) you: for I will ishah (make) a full end of all the gawayam (nations) where I have scattered you, but I will not ishah (make) a full end of you; but I will correct you in mashapat (measure), and will in no naqah (way) leave you unpunished.
For thus amar (says) Yahawah, Your hurt is Anash, and your makah (wound) chalah (grievous).
There is none to plead your cause, that you may be bound up: you have no thailah (healing) medicines.

All your lovers have forgotten you; they don't seek you: for I have wounded you with the makah (wound) of an ayab (enemy), with the chastisement of a Akazaray one, for the greatness of your iwan (iniquity), because your chataah (sins) were itzam (increased).
Why do you cry for your hurt? Your pain is Anash: for the greatness of your iwan (iniquity), because your chataah (sins) were itzam (increased), I have done these things to you.

Therefore all those who akal (devour) you shall be devoured; and all your tzar (adversaries), everyone of them, shall yalak (go) into Shabay; and those who despoil you shall be a spoil, and all who prey on you will I nathan (give) for a prey.
For I will ilah (restore) health to you, and I will heal you of your makah (wounds), says Yahawah; because they have called you an outcast, saying, It is Tzayawan, whom no darash (man) seeks after.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Behold, I will shawab (turn back / repent) again the captivity of Yaiqab ahal (tents), and have racham (compassion) on his mashakan (dwelling) places; and the Iyar shall be built on its own hill, and the palace shall be inhabited in its own way.

Out of them shall yatzaa (proceed) thanksgiving and the qawal (voice) of those who make merry: and I will multiply them, and they shall not be few; I will also kabad (glorify) them, and they shall not be small.
Their children also shall be as qadam (before), and their idah (congregation) shall be established panayam (before) me; and I will paqad (punish) all who lachatz (oppress) them.

Their prince shall be of themselves, and their ruler shall yatzaa (proceed) from their qarab (midst); and I will cause him to qarab (draw) near, and he shall approach to me: for who is he who has had boldness to approach to me? says Yahawah.
You shall be my im (people), and I will be your Alahayam.
Behold, the storm of Yahawah, his chamah (wrath), has gone yatzaa (forth), a sweeping storm: it shall burst on the raash (head) of the rashai (wicked).

The charawan (fierce) ap (anger) of Yahawah will not shawab (turn back / repent), until he has executed, and until he has performed the intentions of his lab (heart). In the acharayath (latter) yawam (days) you will bayan (understand) it.
At that ith (time), says Yahawah, will I be the Alahayam of all the mashapachah (families) of Yasharaal (Israel), and they shall be my im (people).
