Thus amar (says) Yahawah, The im (people) who were sharayad (left) of the charab (sword) found favor in the madabar (wilderness); even Yasharaal (Israel), when I went to cause him to ragai (rest).
Yahawah raah (see) of Rachawaq to me, saying, Yes, I have loved you with an iwalam (forever) ahabah (love): therefore with loving chasad (kindness) have I drawn you.

Again will I banah (build) you, and you shall be built, O virgin of Yasharaal (Israel): again you shall be adorned with your tambourines, and shall yatzaa (go) forth in the dances of those who make merry.
Again you shall plant vineyards on the har (mountains) of Shamarawan; the planters shall plant, and shall enjoy its fruit.
For there shall be a yawam (day), that the watchmen on the har (hills) of Aparayam shall qaraa (cry), qawam (arise), and let us ilah (go) up to Tzayawan to Yahawah our Alahayam.

For thus amar (says) Yahawah, Sing with gladness for Yaiqab, and shout for the raash (chief) of the gawayam (nations): publish, halal (praise), and amar (say), Yahawah, yashai (save) your im (people), the shaarayath (remnant) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Behold, I will bawaa (bring) them from the tzapawan (north) aratz (country), and gather them from the uttermost parts of the aratz (earth), along with the iwar (blind) and the Pasach, the harah (woman) with child and her who yalad (travails) with child together: a gadawal (great) qahal (company) shall they shawab (turn back / repent) here.

They shall bawaa (come) with weeping; and with petitions will I lead them: I will yalak (cause) them to walk by nachal (rivers) of mayam (waters), in a yashar (straight) darak (way) in which they shall not stumble; for I am a ab (father) to Yasharaal (Israel), and Aparayam is my firstborn.

Hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah, you gawayam (nations), and nagad (declare) it in the islands afar off; and amar (say), He who scattered Yasharaal (Israel) will gather him, and shamar (keep) him, as raih (shepherd) does his flock.
For Yahawah has ransomed Yaiqab, and padah (redeemed) him from the yad (hand) of him who was chazaq (stronger) than he.

They shall bawaa (come) and sing in the height of Tzayawan, and shall flow to the goodness of Yahawah, to the grain, and to the new thayarawash (wine), and to the yatzahar (oil), and to the ban (young) of the flock and of the herd: and their napash (soul) shall be as a Rawah Gan; and they shall not sorrow any more at all.

Then shall the virgin Shamach in the dance, and the young men and the zaqan (old) together; for I will hapak (turn) their mourning into joy, and will nacham (comfort) them, and Shamach them rejoice from their sorrow.
I will rawah (satiate) the napash (soul) of the kahan (priests) with fatness, and my im (people) shall be satisfied with my goodness, says Yahawah.
Thus amar (says) Yahawah: A qawal (voice) is heard in Ramah, lamentation, and bitter weeping, Rachal weeping for her children; she refuses to be comforted for her children, because they are no more.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Refrain your qawal (voice) from weeping, and your iyan (eyes) from tears; for your pailah (work) shall be rewarded, says Yahawah; and they shall shawab (turn back / repent) again from the aratz (land) of the ayab (enemy).
There is hope for your acharayath (latter) end, says Yahawah; and your children shall shawab (turn back / repent) again to their own border.

I have surely heard Aparayam bemoaning himself thus, You have chastised me, and I was chastised, as an untrained calf: shawab (turn back / repent) me, and I shall be turned; for you are Yahawah my Alahayam.

Surely achar (after) that I was turned, I repented; and achar (after) that I was instructed, I struck on my thigh: I was bawash (ashamed), yes, even kalam (confounded), because I bore the reproach of my youth.

Is Aparayam my Yaqayar ban (son)? is he a darling yalad (child)? for as often as I dabar (speak) against him, I do zakar (earnestly) zakar (remember) him still: therefore my maih (heart) yearns for him; I will racham (surely) have racham (mercy) on him, says Yahawah.

natzab (set) up road tzayawan (signs), shawam (make) guideposts; shayath (set) your lab (heart) toward the masalah (highway), even the darak (way) by which you went: shawab (turn back / repent) again, virgin of Yasharaal (Israel), shawab (turn back / repent) again to these your Iyar.
How long will you go here and there, you Shawabab bath (daughter)? for Yahawah has created a Chadash thing in the aratz (earth): a naqabah (woman) shall encompass a gabar (man).

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), Yet again shall they use this dabar (speech) in the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah) and in its Iyar, when I shall shawab (turn back / repent) again their captivity: Yahawah barak (bless) you, Nawah of tzadaq (righteousness), har (mountain) of qadash (holiness).
Yahawadah (Judah) and all its Iyar shall yashab (dwell) therein together, the farmers, and those who nasai (go) about with flocks.
For I have satiated the Iyap napash (soul), and every sorrowful napash (soul) have I replenished.
On this I awakened, and saw; and my shanah (sleep) was sweet to me.

Behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), says Yahawah, that I will zarai (sow) the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) and the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) with the zarai (seed) of adam (man), and with the zarai (seed) of animal.

It shall happen that, like as I have watched over them to nathash (pluck) up and to nathatz (break) down and to haras (overthrow) and to abad (destroy) and to raii (afflict), so will I watch over them to banah (build) and to plant, says Yahawah.
In those yawam (days) they shall amar (say) no more, The abawath (fathers) have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.
But everyone shall mawath (die) for his own iwan (iniquity): every adam (man) who akal (eats) the sour grapes, his teeth shall be set on edge.

Behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), says Yahawah, that I will karath (make) a Chadash barayath (covenant) with the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), and with the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah):

not according to the barayath (covenant) that I made with their abawath (fathers) in the yawam (day) that I took them by the yad (hand) to yatzaa (bring) them out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam; which my barayath (covenant) they broke, although I was a bail (husband) to them, says Yahawah.

But this is the barayath (covenant) that I will karath (make) with the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) achar (after) those yawam (days), says Yahawah: I will nathan (put) my thawarah (law) in their qarab (inward) parts, and in their lab (heart) will I kathab (write) it; and I will be their Alahayam, and they shall be my im (people):

and they shall teach no more every ayash (man) his neighbor, and every ayash (man) his ach (brother), saying, yadai (know) Yahawah; for they shall all yadai (know) me, from their qatan (least) to their greatest, says Yahawah: for I will forgive their iwan (iniquity), and their chataah (sin) will I zakar (remember) no more.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, who nathan (gives) the shamash (sun) for a awar (light) by yawamam (day), and the chaqah (ordinances) of the yarach (moon) and of the kawakab (stars) for a awar (light) by layal (night), who stirs up the yam (sea), so that its waves roar; Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) is his sham (name):

If these chaq (ordinances) depart from panayam (before) me, says Yahawah, then the zarai (seed) of Yasharaal (Israel) also shall shabath (cease) from being a gaway (nation) panayam (before) me forever.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: If shamayam (heaven) above can be measured, and the foundations of the aratz (earth) searched out beneath, then will I also cast off all the zarai (seed) of Yasharaal (Israel) for all that they have done, says Yahawah.
Behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), says Yahawah, that the Iyar shall be built to Yahawah from the magadal (tower) Chananaal Hananel to the gate of the corner.
The measuring line shall yatzaa (go) out further straight onward to the Gabaih Garab, and shall sabab (turn) about Gaih Goah.

The whole valley of the pagar (dead) bodies and of the ashes, and all the fields to the nachal (brook) Qadarawan, to the corner of the horse gate toward the east, shall be qadash (holy) to Yahawah; it shall not be plucked up, nor thrown down any more iwalam (forever).
The dabar (word) that came to Yaramayah from Yahawah in the ishayaray (tenth) Shanah of Tzadaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), which was the eighteenth Shanah of Nabawakadanaatzar.

Now at that time the malak (king) of Babal chayal (army) was besieging Yarawashalam; and Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet) was shut up in the court of the guard, which was in the malak (king) of Yahawadah bayath (house).

For Tzadaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) had shut him up, saying, Why do you nabaa (prophesy), and amar (say), Thus amar (says) Yahawah, Behold, I will nathan (give) this Iyar into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Babal, and he shall take it;

and Tzadaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) shall not malat (escape) out of the yad (hand) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), but shall nathan (surely) be delivered into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Babal, and shall dabar (speak) with him pah (mouth) to pah (mouth), and his iyan (eyes) shall raah (see) his iyan (eyes);
and he shall yalak (bring) Tzadaqayah to Babal, and he shall be there until I paqad (visit) him, says Yahawah: though you fight with the Kashaday (Chaldeans), you shall not tzalach (prosper)?
Yaramayah said, The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

Behold, Chanamaal the ban (son) of Shalawam your dawad (uncle) shall bawaa (come) to you, saying, qanah (buy) my shadah (field) that is in Inathawath; for the mashapat (right) of gaalah (redemption) is yours to qanah (buy) it.

So Chanamaal my dawad (uncle's) ban (son) came to me in the court of the guard according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah, and said to me, Please qanah (buy) my shadah (field) that is in Inathawath, which is in the aratz (land) of Banayamayan; for the mashapat (right) of yarashah (inheritance) is yours, and the gaalah (redemption) is yours; qanah (buy) it for yourself. Then I knew that this was the dabar (word) of Yahawah.
I bought the shadah (field) that was in Inathawath of Chanamaal my dawad (uncle's) ban (son), and weighed him the kasap (money), even seventeen shekels of kasap (silver).
I subscribed the deed, and sealed it, and called witnesses, and weighed him the kasap (money) in the balances.
So I took the deed of the maqanah (purchase), both that which was sealed, containing the terms and conditions, and that which was galah (open);

and I delivered the deed of the maqanah (purchase) to Barawak the ban (son) of Narayah, the ban (son) Machasayah Mahseiah, in the iyan (presence) of Chanamaal my dawad (uncle's) son, and in the iyan (presence) of the witnesses who subscribed the deed of the maqanah (purchase), iyan (before) all the Yahawaday (Jews) who sat in the court of the guard.
I tzawah (commanded) Barawak iyan (before) them, saying,

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): Take these deeds, this deed of the maqanah (purchase) which is sealed, and this deed which is galah (open), and nathan (put) them in an charash (earthen) vessel; that they may imad (continue) many yawam (days).
For thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): bayath (houses) and shadah (fields) and vineyards shall yet again be bought in this aratz (land).
Now achar (after) I had delivered the deed of the maqanah (purchase) to Barawak the ban (son) of Narayah, I prayed to Yahawah, saying,

Ah Adanay Yahawah! Behold, you have made the shamayam (heavens) and the aratz (earth) by your gadawal (great) kach (power) and by your natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm); there is nothing palaa (too) hard for you,

who show loving chasad (kindness) to alap (thousands), and shalam (recompense) the iwan (iniquity) of the abawath (fathers) into the bosom of their children achar (after) them; the gadawal (great), the gabawar (mighty) Al, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) is his sham (name);

gadawal (great) in itzah (counsel), and rab (mighty) in ilayalayah (work); whose iyan (eyes) are open on all the darak (ways) of the ban (sons) of men, to nathan (give) everyone according to his darak (ways), and according to the fruit of his mailal (doings):

who performed awath (signs) and mawapath (wonders) in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, even to this yawam (day), both in Yasharaal (Israel) and among other men; and made yourself a sham (name), as in this yawam (day);

and brought yatzaa (forth) your im (people) Yasharaal (Israel) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam with awath (signs), and with mawapath (wonders), and with a chazaq (strong) yad (hand), and with an outstretched arm, and with gadawal (great) mawaraa (terror);
and gave them this aratz (land), which you swore to their abawath (fathers) to nathan (give) them, a aratz (land) flowing with milk and honey;

and they came in, and possessed it, but they didn't obey your qawal (voice), neither walked in your thawarah (law); they have done nothing of all that you tzawah (commanded) them to do: therefore you have caused all this rai (evil) to come on them.

Behold, the mounds, they have bawaa (come) to the Iyar to take it; and the Iyar is given into the yad (hand) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans) who fight panayam (against) it, because of the charab (sword), and of the famine, and of the dabar (pestilence); and what you have spoken has happened; and raah (see), you see it.
You have said to me, Adanay Yahawah, qanah (buy) the shadah (field) for kasap (money), and iwad (call) witnesses; whereas the Iyar is given into the yad (hand) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans).
Then came the dabar (word) of Yahawah to Yaramayah, saying,
Behold, I am Yahawah, the Alahayam of all flesh: is there anything palaa (too) hard for me?

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah: Behold, I will nathan (give) this Iyar into the yad (hand) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), and into the yad (hand) of Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal, and he shall take it:

and the Kashaday (Chaldeans), who fight against this Iyar, shall bawaa (come) and yatzath (set) this Iyar on ash (fire), and sharap (burn) it, with the bayath (houses), on whose roofs they have offered qatar (incense) to Bail, and poured out drink nasak (offerings) to other Alahayam, to provoke me to kais (anger).

For the children of Yasharaal (Israel) and the children of Yahawadah (Judah) have done only that which was rai (evil) in my iyan (sight) from their youth; for the children of Yasharaal (Israel) have only provoked me to kais (anger) with the maishah (work) of their yad (hands), says Yahawah.

For this Iyar has been to me a provocation of my ap (anger) and of my chamah (wrath) from the yawam (day) that they built it even to this yawam (day); that I should sawar (remove) it from before my panayam (face),

because of all the rai (evil) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) and of the children of Yahawadah (Judah), which they have done to provoke me to kais (anger), they, their malak (kings), their shar (princes), their kahan (priests), and their nabayaa (prophets), and the men of Yahawadah (Judah), and the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam.
They have turned to me the back, and not the panayam (face): and though I taught them, rising up shakam (early) and teaching them, yet they have not listened to receive instruction.
But they shawam (set) their shaqawatz (abominations) in the bayath (house) which is called by my sham (name), to tamaa (defile) it.

They built the bamah (high) places of Bail, which are in the Gayaa of the ban (son) of Hanam, to cause their ban (sons) and their bath (daughters) to ibar (pass) through fire to Malak; which I didn't tzawah (command) them, neither did it ilah (come) into my lab (mind), that they should do this thawaibah (abomination), to cause Yahawadah (Judah) to chataa (sin).

Now therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), concerning this Iyar, about which you amar (say), It is given into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Babal by the charab (sword), and by the famine, and by the dabar (pestilence):

Behold, I will gather them out of all the aratz (countries), where I have driven them in my ap (anger), and in my chamah (wrath), and in gadawal (great) qatzap (indignation); and I will shawab (turn back / repent) them again to this place, and I will yashab (cause) them to dwell safely:
and they shall be my im (people), and I will be their Alahayam:
and I will nathan (give) them one lab (heart) and one darak (way), that they may yaraa (fear) me forever, for their tawab (good), and of their children achar (after) them:

and I will karath (make) an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant) with them, that I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away from following them, to do them yatab (good); and I will nathan (put) my yaraah (fear) in their labab (hearts), that they may not sawar (depart) from me.
Yes, I will rejoice over them to do them tawab (good), and I will plant them in this aratz (land) amath (assuredly) with my whole lab (heart) and with my whole napash (soul).
For thus amar (says) Yahawah: Like as I have brought all this gadawal (great) rai (evil) on this im (people), so will I bawaa (bring) on them all the tawab (good) that I have promised them.
shadah (fields) shall be bought in this aratz (land), about which you amar (say), It is desolate, without adam (man) or animal; it is given into the yad (hand) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans).

Men shall qanah (buy) shadah (fields) for kasap (money), and kathab (subscribe) the deeds, and seal them, and iwad (call) witnesses, in the aratz (land) of Banayamayan, and in the places about Yarawashalam, and in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the Iyar of the har (hill) country, and in the Iyar of the lowland, and in the Iyar of the Nagab: for I will cause their captivity to shawab (turn back / repent), says Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Yaramayah the shanay (second) time, while he was yet itzar (shut) up in the court of the guard, saying,
Thus amar (says) Yahawah who does it, Yahawah who forms it to kawan (establish) it; Yahawah is his sham (name):
qaraa (call) to me, and I will answer you, and will show you gadawal (great) things, and difficult, which you don't yadai (know).

For thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), concerning the bayath (houses) of this Iyar, and concerning the bayath (houses) of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), which are broken down to make a defense against the mounds and against the charab (sword);

while men bawaa (come) to fight with the Kashaday (Chaldeans), and to malaa (fill) them with the pagar (dead) bodies of men, whom I have killed in my ap (anger) and in my chamah (wrath), and for all whose wickedness I have hidden my panayam (face) from this Iyar:
Behold, I will ilah (bring) it health and cure, and I will cure them; and I will galah (reveal) to them abundance of shalawam (peace) and truth.
I will cause the captivity of Yahawadah (Judah) and the captivity of Yasharaal (Israel) to shawab (turn back / repent), and will banah (build) them, as at the raashawan (first).

I will tahar (cleanse) them from all their iwan (iniquity), by which they have sinned against me; and I will pardon all their iwan (iniquities), by which they have sinned against me, and by which they have transgressed against me.

This city shall be to me for a sham (name) of joy, for a thahalah (praise) and for a glory, before all the gawayay (nations) of the aratz (earth), which shall hear all the tawab (good) that I do to them, and shall pachad (fear) and tremble for all the tawab (good) and for all the shalawam (peace) that I ishah (procure) to it.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Yet again there shall be heard in this place, about which you amar (say), It is Charab, without adam (man) and without animal, even in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the streets of Yarawashalam, that are shamam (desolate), without adam (man) and without yashab (inhabitant) and without animal,

the qawal (voice) of joy and the qawal (voice) of gladness, the qawal (voice) of the chathan (bridegroom) and the qawal (voice) of the kalah (bride), the qawal (voice) of those who amar (say), Give yadah (thanks) to Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), for Yahawah is tawab (good), for his loving chasad (kindness) endures iwalam (forever); who bawaa (bring) thanksgiving into the bayath (house) of Yahawah. For I will cause the captivity of the aratz (land) to shawab (turn back / repent) as at the raashawan (first), amar (says) Yahawah.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): Yet again shall there be in this place, which is Charab, without adam (man) and without animal, and in all its Iyar, a Nawah of raih (shepherds) causing their flocks to rabatz (lie) down.

In the Iyar of the har (hill) country, in the Iyar of the lowland, and in the Iyar of the Nagab, and in the aratz (land) of Banayamayan, and in the places about Yarawashalam, and in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), shall the flocks again pass under the yad (hands) of him who numbers them, amar (says) Yahawah.

Behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), says Yahawah, that I will qawam (perform) that tawab (good) dabar (word) which I have spoken concerning the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) and concerning the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah).

In those yawam (days), and at that ith (time), will I cause a Branch of tzadaqah (righteousness) to grow up to Dawad; and he shall ishah (execute) justice and tzadaqah (righteousness) in the aratz (land).
In those yawam (days) shall Yahawadah (Judah) be saved, and Yarawashalam shall shakan (dwell) safely; and this is the qaraa (name) by which she shall be called: Yahawah our righteousness.
For thus amar (says) Yahawah: Dawad shall laa (never) karath (want) a ayash (man) to yashab (sit) on the kasaa (throne) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel);

neither shall the kahan (priests) the Lawayay (Levites) karath (want) a ayash (man) panayam (before) me to ilah (offer) burnt ilah (offerings), and to qatar (burn) meal manachah (offerings), and to do zabach (sacrifice) yawam (continually).
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Yaramayah, saying,

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: If you can parar (break) my barayath (covenant) of the yawam (day), and my barayath (covenant) of the layal (night), so that there shall not be yawamam (day) and layal (night) in their ith (season);

then may also my barayath (covenant) be broken with Dawad my ibad (servant), that he shall not have a ban (son) to malak (reign) on his kasaa (throne); and Lawayay the Levites the kahan (priests), my sharath (ministers).

As the tzabaa (army) of the sky can't be numbered, neither the sand of the yam (sea) measured; so will I multiply the zarai (seed) of Dawad my ibad (servant), and the Lawayay (Levites) who sharath (minister) to me.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Yaramayah, saying,

Don't raah (see) what this im (people) has spoken, saying, The shanayam (two) mashapachah (families) which Yahawah chose, he has cast them off? thus do they despise my im (people), that they should be no more a gaway (nation) panayam (before) them.
Thus amar (says) Yahawah: If my barayath (covenant) of yawamam (day) and layal (night) fails, if I have not appointed the chaqah (ordinances) of shamayam (heaven) and aratz (earth);

then will I also cast away the zarai (seed) of Yaiqab, and of Dawad my ibad (servant), so that I will not take of his zarai (seed) to be rulers over the zarai (seed) of Abaraham, Yashachaq, and Yaiqab: for I will cause their captivity to shawab (turn back / repent), and will have racham (mercy) on them.

The dabar (word) which came to Yaramayah from Yahawah, when Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal, and all his chayal (army), and all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (earth) that were under his yad (dominion), and all the im (peoples), were fighting against Yarawashalam, and against all the Iyar of it, saying:

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), halak (go), and amar (speak) to Tzadaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and amar (tell) him, Thus amar (says) Yahawah, Behold, I will nathan (give) this Iyar into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Babal, and he shall sharap (burn) it with ash (fire):

and you shall not malat (escape) out of his yad (hand), but shall surely be taken, and delivered into his yad (hand); and your iyan (eyes) shall raah (see) the iyan (eyes) of the malak (king) of Babal, and he shall dabar (speak) with you pah (mouth) to pah (mouth), and you shall bawaa (go) to Babal.
Yet hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah, O Tzadaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah): thus amar (says) Yahawah concerning you, You shall not mawath (die) by the charab (sword);

you shall mawath (die) in shalawam (peace); and with the burnings of your abawath (fathers), the raashawan (former) malak (kings) who were panayam (before) you, so shall they sharap (make) a burning for you; and they shall lament you, saying, Ah Adawan! for I have spoken the dabar (word), says Yahawah.
Then Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet) spoke all these dabar (words) to Tzadaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) in Yarawashalam,

when the malak (king) of Babal chayal (army) was fighting against Yarawashalam, and against all the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah) that were yathar (left), against Lakayash and against Izaqah; for these alone remained of the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah) as fortified Iyar.

The dabar (word) that came to Yaramayah from Yahawah, achar (after) that the malak (king) Tzadaqayah had made a barayath (covenant) with all the im (people) who were at Yarawashalam, to qaraa (proclaim) liberty to them;

that every ayash (man) should let his male servant, and every ayash (man) his female servant, who is a ibaray (hebrew) or a Hebrewess, shalach (go) Chapashay; that none should ibad (make) bondservants of them, of a Yahawaday (Jew) his ach (brother).

All the shar (princes) and all the im (people) obeyed, who had entered into the barayath (covenant), that everyone should let his male servant, and everyone his female servant, shalach (go) Chapashay, that none should ibad (make) bondservants of them any more; they obeyed, and let them shalach (go):

but afterwards they turned, and caused the ibad (servants) and the handmaids, whom they had let shalach (go) Chapashay, to shawab (turn back / repent), and brought them into subjection for ibad (servants) and for handmaids.
Therefore the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Yaramayah from Yahawah, saying,

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): I made a barayath (covenant) with your abawath (fathers) in the yawam (day) that I brought them yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, out of the bayath (house) of ibad (bondage), saying,

At the end of shabai (seven) Shanah you shall let shalach (go) every ayash (man) his ach (brother) who is a ibaray (hebrew), who has been sold to you, and has served you shash (six) Shanah, you shall let him shalach (go) Chapashay from you: but your abawath (fathers) didn't listen to me, neither inclined their ear.

You had yawam (now) turned, and had done that which is yashar (right) in my iyan (eyes), in proclaiming liberty every ayash (man) to his neighbor; and you had made a barayath (covenant) panayam (before) me in the bayath (house) which is called by my sham (name):

but you turned and profaned my sham (name), and caused every ayash (man) his ibad (servant), and every ayash (man) his handmaid, whom you had let go Chapashay at their napash (pleasure), to shawab (turn back / repent); and you brought them into subjection, to be to you for ibad (servants) and for handmaids.

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah: you have not listened to me, to qaraa (proclaim) liberty, every ayash (man) to his ach (brother), and every ayash (man) to his neighbor: behold, I qaraa (proclaim) to you a liberty, says Yahawah, to the charab (sword), to the dabar (pestilence), and to the famine; and I will nathan (make) you to be tossed back and forth among all the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the aratz (earth).

I will nathan (give) the men who have transgressed my barayath (covenant), who have not performed the dabar (words) of the barayath (covenant) which they made panayam (before) me, when they karath (cut) the calf in shanayam (two) and passed between its parts;

the shar (princes) of Yahawadah (Judah), and the shar (princes) of Yarawashalam, the eunuchs, and the kahan (priests), and all the im (people) of the aratz (land), who passed between the parts of the calf;

I will even nathan (give) them into the yad (hand) of their ayab (enemies), and into the yad (hand) of those who seek their napash (life); and their nabalah (dead) bodies shall be for food to the birds of the sky, and to the animals of the aratz (earth).

Tzadaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) and his shar (princes) will I nathan (give) into the yad (hand) of their ayab (enemies), and into the yad (hand) of those who seek their napash (life), and into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Babal chayal (army), who have gone ilah (away) from you.

Behold, I will tzawah (command), says Yahawah, and cause them to shawab (turn back / repent) to this Iyar; and they shall fight against it, and take it, and sharap (burn) it with ash (fire): and I will nathan (make) the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah) a desolation, without yashab (inhabitant).
The dabar (word) which came to Yaramayah from Yahawah in the yawam (days) of Yahawayaqayam the ban (son) of Yaashayah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), saying,

halak (go) to the bayath (house) Rakah the Rechabites, and dabar (speak) to them, and bawaa (bring) them into the bayath (house) of Yahawah, into one of the rooms, and give them yayan (wine) to shaqah (drink).
Then I took Yaazanayah the ban (son) of Yaramayah, the ban (son) Chabatzanayah Habazziniah, and his ach (brothers), and all his ban (sons), and the whole bayath (house) Rakah the Rechabites;

and I brought them into the bayath (house) of Yahawah, into the room of the ban (sons) Chanan Hanan the ban (son) of Yagadalayahaw, the ayash (man) of Alahayam, which was by the room of the shar (princes), which was above the room of Maishayah the ban (son) of Shalawam, the keeper of the threshold.
I nathan (set) panayam (before) the ban (sons) of the bayath (house) Rakah the Rechabites bowls Malaa of yayan (wine), and cups; and I said to them, Drink yayan (wine)!

But they said, We will drink no yayan (wine); for Yawanadab the ban (son) of Rakab, our ab (father), tzawah (commanded) us, saying, You shall drink no yayan (wine), neither you, nor your ban (sons), iwalam (forever):

neither shall you banah (build) bayath (house), nor zarai (sow) zarai (seed), nor plant vineyard, nor have any; but all your yawam (days) you shall yashab (dwell) in ahal (tents); that you may chayah (live) many yawam (days) in the adamah (land) in which you live.

We have obeyed the qawal (voice) of Yahawanadab the ban (son) of Rakab, our ab (father), in all that he tzawah (commanded) us, to drink no yayan (wine) all our yawam (days), we, our wives, our ban (sons), or our bath (daughters);
nor to banah (build) bayath (houses) for us to yashab (dwell) in; neither have we vineyard, nor shadah (field), nor zarai (seed):
but we have lived in ahal (tents), and have obeyed, and done according to all that Yawanadab our ab (father) tzawah (commanded) us.

But it happened, when Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal came up into the aratz (land), that we said, bawaa (come), and let us bawaa (go) to Yarawashalam for panayam (fear) of the chayal (army) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), and for panayam (fear) of the chayal (army) of the Aram (Syrians); so we yashab (dwell) at Yarawashalam.
Then came the dabar (word) of Yahawah to Yaramayah, saying,

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): halak (go), and amar (tell) the men of Yahawadah (Judah) and the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, Will you not receive instruction to listen to my dabar (words)? says Yahawah.

The dabar (words) of Yahawanadab the ban (son) of Rakab, that he tzawah (commanded) his ban (sons), not to drink yayan (wine), are performed; and to this yawam (day) they drink none, for they obey their ab (father's) matzawah (commandment): but I have spoken to you, rising up shakam (early) and speaking; and you have not listened to me.

I have sent also to you all my ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets), rising up shakam (early) and sending them, saying, shawab (turn back / repent) now every ayash (man) from his rai (evil) darak (way), and yatab (amend) your mailal (doings), and don't yalak (go) achar (after) other Alahayam to ibad (serve) them, and you shall yashab (dwell) in the adamah (land) which I have given to you and to your abawath (fathers): but you have not inclined your ear, nor listened to me.

Because the ban (sons) of Yahawanadab the ban (son) of Rakab have performed the matzawah (commandment) of their ab (father) which he tzawah (commanded) them, but this im (people) has not listened to me;

therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): Behold, I will bawaa (bring) on Yahawadah (Judah) and on all the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam all the rai (evil) that I have pronounced against them; because I have spoken to them, but they have not heard; and I have called to them, but they have not answered.

Yaramayah said to the bayath (house) Rakah the Rechabites, Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): Because you have obeyed the matzawah (commandment) of Yahawanadab your ab (father), and kept all his matzawah (precepts), and done according to all that he tzawah (commanded) you;

therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): Yawanadab the ban (son) of Rakab shall not karath (want) a ayash (man) to imad (stand) panayam (before) me forever.
It happened in the rabayaiy (fourth) Shanah of Yahawayaqayam the ban (son) of Yaashayah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), that this dabar (word) came to Yaramayah from Yahawah, saying,

Take a scroll of a book, and kathab (write) therein all the dabar (words) that I have spoken to you against Yasharaal (Israel), and against Yahawadah (Judah), and against all the gawayam (nations), from the yawam (day) I spoke to you, from the yawam (days) of Yaashayah, even to this yawam (day).

It may be that the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) will hear all the rai (evil) which I chashab (purpose) to do to them; that they may shawab (turn back / repent) every ayash (man) from his rai (evil) darak (way); that I may forgive their iwan (iniquity) and their chataah (sin).
Then Yaramayah called Barawak the ban (son) of Narayah; and Barawak wrote from the pah (mouth) of Yaramayah all the dabar (words) of Yahawah, which he had spoken to him, on a scroll of a book.
Yaramayah tzawah (commanded) Barawak, saying, I am itzar (shut) up; I can't bawaa (go) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah:

therefore you bawaa (go), and qaraa (read) in the scroll, which you have written from my pah (mouth), the dabar (words) of Yahawah in the ears of the im (people) in yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house) on the fast yawam (day); and also you shall qaraa (read) them in the ears of all Yahawadah (Judah) who bawaa (come) out of their Iyar.

It may be they will napal (present) their supplication panayam (before) Yahawah, and will shawab (turn back / repent) everyone from his rai (evil) darak (way); for gadawal (great) is the ap (anger) and the chamah (wrath) that Yahawah has pronounced against this im (people).

Barawak the ban (son) of Narayah did according to all that Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet) tzawah (commanded) him, reading in the book the dabar (words) of Yahawah in yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house).

Now it happened in the chamayashay (fifth) Shanah of Yahawayaqayam the ban (son) of Yaashayah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), in the thashayaiy (ninth) chadash (month), that all the im (people) in Yarawashalam, and all the im (people) who came from the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah) to Yarawashalam, proclaimed a fast panayam (before) Yahawah.

Then qaraa (read) Barawak in the book the dabar (words) of Yaramayah in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, in the room of Gamarayah the ban (son) Shapan Shaphan, the scribe, in the Ilayawan court, at the entry of the Chadash gate of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house), in the ears of all the im (people).
When Mayakayahaw the ban (son) of Gamarayah, the ban (son) Shapan Shaphan, had heard out of the book all the dabar (words) of Yahawah,

he went down into the malak (king's) bayath (house), into the scribe's room: and behold, all the shar (princes) were sitting there, Alayashamai the scribe, and Dalayah the ban (son) of Shamaiyah, and Alanathan the ban (son) of Ikabawar, and Gamarayah the ban (son) Shapan Shaphan, and Tzadaqayah the ban (son) of Chananayah, and all the shar (princes).
Then Mayakayahaw declared to them all the dabar (words) that he had heard, when Barawak qaraa (read) the book in the ears of the im (people).

Therefore all the shar (princes) sent Yahawaday the ban (son) of Nathanayah, the ban (son) of Shalamayah, the ban (son) of Kawashay, to Barawak, saying, Take in your yad (hand) the scroll in which you have qaraa (read) in the ears of the im (people), and yalak (come). So Barawak the ban (son) of Narayah took the scroll in his yad (hand), and came to them.
They said to him, yashab (sit) down now, and qaraa (read) it in our ears. So Barawak qaraa (read) it in their ears.

Now it happened, when they had heard all the dabar (words), they turned in pachad (fear) one toward rai (another), and said to Barawak, We will nagad (surely) nagad (tell) the malak (king) of all these dabar (words).
They asked Barawak, saying, nagad (tell) us now, How did you kathab (write) all these dabar (words) at his pah (mouth)?
Then Barawak answered them, He pronounced all these dabar (words) to me with his pah (mouth), and I wrote them with ink in the book.
Then the shar (princes) said to Barawak, yalak (go), hide, you and Yaramayah; and let no ayash (man) yadai (know) where you are.
They went in to the malak (king) into the court; but they had laid up the scroll in the room of Alayashamai the scribe; and they told all the dabar (words) in the ears of the malak (king).

So the malak (king) sent Yahawaday to get the scroll; and he took it out of the room of Alayashamai the scribe. Yahawaday qaraa (read) it in the ears of the malak (king), and in the ears of all the shar (princes) who stood beside the malak (king).
Now the malak (king) was sitting in the winter bayath (house) in the thashayaiy (ninth) chadash (month): and there was a ach (fire) in the brazier burning panayam (before) him.

It happened, when Yahawaday had qaraa (read) shalawash (three) or arabai (four) leaves, that the qarai (king) cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the ash (fire) that was in the brazier, until all the scroll was consumed in the ash (fire) that was in the brazier.
They were not pachad (afraid), nor tore their bagad (garments), neither the malak (king), nor any of his ibad (servants) who heard all these dabar (words).
Moreover Alanathan and Dalayah and Gamarayah had made pagai (intercession) to the malak (king) that he would not sharap (burn) the scroll; but he would not hear them.

The malak (king) tzawah (commanded) Yarachamaal the malak (king's) ban (son), and Sharayah the ban (son) of Izarayaal, and Shalamayah the ban (son) of Ibadaal, to take Barawak the scribe and Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet); but Yahawah hid them.
Then the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Yaramayah, achar (after) that the malak (king) had burned the scroll, and the dabar (words) which Barawak wrote at the pah (mouth) of Yaramayah, saying,

Take again achar (another) scroll, and kathab (write) in it all the raashawan (former) dabar (words) that were in the raashawan (first) scroll, which Yahawayaqayam the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) has burned.

Concerning Yahawayaqayam malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) you shall amar (say), Thus amar (says) Yahawah: You have burned this scroll, saying, Why have you written therein, saying, The malak (king) of Babal shall bawaa (certainly) bawaa (come) and shachath (destroy) this aratz (land), and shall shabath (cause) to cease from there adam (man) and animal?

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah concerning Yahawayaqayam malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah): He shall have none to yashab (sit) on the kasaa (throne) of Dawad; and his nabalah (dead) body shall be cast out in the yawam (day) to the heat, and in the layal (night) to the frost.

I will paqad (punish) him and his zarai (seed) and his ibad (servants) for their iwan (iniquity); and I will bawaa (bring) on them, and on the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, and on the men of Yahawadah (Judah), all the rai (evil) that I have pronounced against them, but they didn't listen.

Then took Yaramayah achar (another) scroll, and gave it to Barawak the scribe, the ban (son) of Narayah, who wrote therein from the pah (mouth) of Yaramayah all the dabar (words) of the book which Yahawayaqayam malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) had burned in the ash (fire); and there were added besides to them many like dabar (words).

Tzadaqayah the ban (son) of Yaashayah reigned as malak (king), instead of Kanayahaw the ban (son) of Yahawayaqayam, whom Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal made malak (king) in the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah).
But neither he, nor his ibad (servants), nor the im (people) of the aratz (land), listened to the dabar (words) of Yahawah, which he spoke by the nabayaa (prophet) Yaramayah.

Tzadaqayah the malak (king) sent Yahawakal the ban (son) of Shalamayah, and Tzapanayah the ban (son) of Maishayah, the kahan (priest), to the nabayaa (prophet) Yaramayah, saying, palal (pray) now to Yahawah our Alahayam for us.
Now Yaramayah came in and went out among the im (people); for they had not nathan (put) him into bayath (prison).
Paraih chayal (army) had yatzaa (come) forth out of Matzarayam; and when the Kashaday (Chaldeans) who were besieging Yarawashalam heard news of them, they broke up from Yarawashalam.
Then came the dabar (word) of Yahawah to the nabayaa (prophet) Yaramayah, saying,

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), You shall amar (tell) the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), who sent you to me to inquire of me: Behold, Paraih chayal (army), which has yatzaa (come) forth to help you, shall shawab (turn back / repent) to Matzarayam into their own aratz (land).
The Kashaday (Chaldeans) shall shawab (turn back / repent) again, and fight against this Iyar; and they shall take it, and sharap (burn) it with ash (fire).
Thus amar (says) Yahawah, Don't deceive yourselves, saying, The Kashaday (Chaldeans) shall halak (surely) depart from us; for they shall not depart.

For though you had struck the whole chayal (army) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans) who fight against you, and there remained but wounded men among them, yes would they qawam (rise) up every ayash (man) in his ahal (tent), and sharap (burn) this Iyar with ash (fire).
It happened that, when the chayal (army) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans) was broken up from Yarawashalam for panayam (fear) of Paraih chayal (army),
then Yaramayah went yatzaa (forth) out of Yarawashalam to yalak (go) into the aratz (land) of Banayamayan, to receive his portion there, in the midst of the im (people).

When he was in the gate of Banayamayan, a bail (captain) of the guard was there, whose sham (name) was Yaraayayah, the ban (son) of Shalamayah, the ban (son) of Chananayah; and he laid hold on Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet), saying, You are falling napal (away) to the Kashaday (Chaldeans).
Then Yaramayah said, It is false; I am not falling napal (away) to the Kashaday (Chaldeans). But he didn't listen to him; so Yaraayayah laid hold on Yaramayah, and brought him to the shar (princes).
The shar (princes) were qatzap (angry) with Yaramayah, and struck him, and nathan (put) him in prison in the bayath (house) of Yahawanathan the scribe; for they had made that the prison.
When Yaramayah had bawaa (come) into the bayath (dungeon) chanawath (house), and into the cells, and Yaramayah had remained there many yawam (days);

Then Tzadaqayah the malak (king) sent, and fetched him: and the malak (king) asked him secretly in his bayath (house), and said, Is there any dabar (word) from Yahawah? Yaramayah said, There is. He said also, You shall be delivered into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Babal.
Moreover Yaramayah said to malak (king) Tzadaqayah, Wherein have I sinned against you, or against your ibad (servants), or against this im (people), that you have nathan (put) me in bayath (prison)?
Where now are your nabayaa (prophets) who prophesied to you, saying, The malak (king) of Babal shall not bawaa (come) against you, nor against this aratz (land)?

Now please hear, my Adawan the malak (king): please let my supplication be presented panayam (before) you, that you not cause me to shawab (turn back / repent) to the bayath (house) of Yahawanathan the scribe, lest I mawath (die) there.

Then Tzadaqayah the malak (king) tzawah (commanded), and they committed Yaramayah into the court of the guard; and they gave him yawam (daily) a loaf of lacham (bread) out of the bakers' street, until all the lacham (bread) in the Iyar was thamam (spent). Thus Yaramayah remained in the court of the guard.

Shapatayah the ban (son) of Mathan, and Gadalayah the ban (son) Pashachawar Pashhur, and Yawakal the ban (son) of Shalamayah, and Pashachawar the ban (son) of Malakayah, heard the dabar (words) that Yaramayah spoke to all the im (people), saying,

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, He who yashab (remains) in this Iyar shall mawath (die) by the charab (sword), by the famine, and by the dabar (pestilence); but he who goes yatzaa (forth) to the Kashaday (Chaldeans) shall chayah (live), and his napash (life) shall be to him for a prey, and he shall chayah (live).
Thus amar (says) Yahawah, This Iyar shall nathan (surely) be given into the yad (hand) of the chayal (army) of the malak (king) of Babal, and he shall take it.

Then the shar (princes) said to the malak (king), "Please let this ayash (man) be put to mawath (death); Kan he rapah (weakens) the yad (hands) of the men of war who shaar (remain) in this Iyar, and the yad (hands) of all the im (people), in speaking such dabar (words) to them: for this ayash (man) doesn't seek the shalawam (welfare) of this im (people), but the rai (hurt).
Tzadaqayah the malak (king) said, Behold, he is in your yad (hand); for the malak (king) is not he who can do anything against you.

Then took they Yaramayah, and cast him into the bawar (dungeon) of Malakayah the malak (king's) ban (son), that was in the court of the guard: and they let down Yaramayah with cords. In the bawar (dungeon) there was no mayam (water), but mire; and Yaramayah sank in the mire.

Now when Ibadamalak the Kawashay (Ethiopian), a eunuch, who was in the malak (king's) bayath (house), heard that they had nathan (put) Yaramayah in the bawar (dungeon) (the malak (king) then sitting in the gate of Banayamayan),
Ibadamalak went yatzaa (forth) out of the malak (king's) bayath (house), and spoke to the malak (king), saying,

My Adawan the malak (king), these men have done raii (evil) in all that they have done to Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet), whom they have cast into the bawar (dungeon); and he is likely to mawath (die) in the place where he is, panayam (because) of the famine; for there is no more lacham (bread) in the Iyar.

Then the malak (king) tzawah (commanded) Ibadamalak the Kawashay (Ethiopian), saying, Take from here shalawashayam (thirty) men with you, and ilah (take) up Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet) out of the bawar (dungeon), before he dies.

So Ibadamalak took the men with him, and went into the bayath (house) of the malak (king) under the treasury, and took there rags and worn-out garments, and let them down by cords into the bawar (dungeon) to Yaramayah.
Ibadamalak the Kawashay (Ethiopian) said to Yaramayah, shawam (put) now these rags and worn-out garments under your armpits under the cords. Yaramayah did so.
So they drew up Yaramayah with the cords, and took him up out of the bawar (dungeon): and Yaramayah remained in the court of the guard.

Then Tzadaqayah the malak (king) sent, and took Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet) to him into the shalayashay (third) entry that is in the bayath (house) of Yahawah: and the malak (king) said to Yaramayah, I will shaal (ask) you something. Hide nothing from me.
Then Yaramayah said to Tzadaqayah, If I nagad (declare) it to you, will you not mawath (surely) put me to mawath (death)? and if I give you yaitz (counsel), you will not listen to me.

So Tzadaqayah the malak (king) swore secretly to Yaramayah, saying, As Yahawah chay (lives), who made us this napash (soul), I will not put you to mawath (death), neither will I nathan (give) you into the yad (hand) of these men who seek your napash (life).

Then Yaramayah said to Tzadaqayah, Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): If you will yatzaa (go) forth to the malak (king) of Babal shar (princes), then your napash (soul) shall chayah (live), and this Iyar shall not be burned with ash (fire); and you shall chayah (live), and your bayath (house).

But if you will not yatzaa (go) forth to the malak (king) of Babal shar (princes), then shall this Iyar be given into the yad (hand) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), and they shall sharap (burn) it with ash (fire), and you shall not malat (escape) out of their yad (hand).

Tzadaqayah the malak (king) said to Yaramayah, I am afraid of the Yahawaday (Jews) who are fallen away to the Kashaday (Chaldeans), lest they nathan (deliver) me into their yad (hand), and they ilal (mock) me.

But Yaramayah said, They shall not nathan (deliver) you. Obey, I beg you, the qawal (voice) of Yahawah, in that which I dabar (speak) to you: so it shall be yatab (well) with you, and your napash (soul) shall chayah (live).
But if you refuse to yatzaa (go) forth, this is the dabar (word) that Yahawah has shown me:

behold, all the women who are shaar (left) in the malak (king) of Yahawadah bayath (house) shall be brought yatzaa (forth) to the malak (king) of Babal shar (princes), and those women shall amar (say), Your familiar friends have set you on, and have prevailed over you. Your feet are sunk in the mire, they have turned sawag (away) back.

They shall yatzaa (bring) out all your wives and your children to the Kashaday (Chaldeans); and you shall not malat (escape) out of their yad (hand), but shall be taken by the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Babal: and you shall cause this Iyar to be burned with ash (fire).
Then Tzadaqayah said to Yaramayah, Let no ayash (man) yadai (know) of these dabar (words), and you shall not mawath (die).

But if the shar (princes) hear that I have talked with you, and they bawaa (come) to you, and amar (tell) you, nagad (declare) to us now what you have said to the malak (king); don't hide it from us, and we will not put you to mawath (death); also what the malak (king) said to you:

then you shall amar (tell) them, I presented my supplication panayam (before) the malak (king), that he would not cause me to shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawanathan bayath (house), to mawath (die) there.

Then came all the shar (princes) to Yaramayah, and asked him; and he told them according to all these dabar (words) that the malak (king) had tzawah (commanded). So they left off charash (speaking) with him; for the dabar (matter) was not perceived.
So Yaramayah stayed in the court of the guard until the yawam (day) that Yarawashalam was taken.

It happened when Jerusalem was taken, (in the thashayaiy (ninth) Shanah of Tzadaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), in the ishayaray (tenth) chadash (month), came Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal and all his chayal (army) against Yarawashalam, and besieged it;
in the ishathay (eleventh) Shanah of Tzadaqayah, in the rabayaiy (fourth) chadash (month), the ninth day of the chadash (month), a breach was made in the Iyar),

that all the shar (princes) of the malak (king) of Babal came in, and sat in the middle gate, Naragalasharaatzar Sharezer, Samagaranabaw, Sharasakayam, Rabsaris, Naragalasharaatzar Sharezer, Rabmag, with all the rest of the shar (princes) of the malak (king) of Babal.

It happened that, when Tzadaqayah the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) and all the men of war saw them, then they fled, and went yatzaa (forth) out of the Iyar by layal (night), by the darak (way) of the malak (king's) Gan, through the gate between the chawamah (two) walls; and he went out toward the irabah (arabah).

But the chayal (army) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans) pursued achar (after) them, and overtook Tzadaqayah in the irabah (plains) of Yarayachaw: and when they had taken him, they brought him up to Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal to Rabalah in the aratz (land) of Chamath; and he gave mashapat (judgment) on him.
Then the malak (king) of Babal killed the ban (sons) of Tzadaqayah in Rabalah before his iyan (eyes): also the malak (king) of Babal killed all the nobles of Yahawadah (Judah).
Moreover he put out Tzadaqayah iyan (eyes), and bound him in fetters, to bawaa (carry) him to Babal.
The Kashaday (Chaldeans) burned the malak (king's) bayath (house), and the bayath (houses) of the im (people), with ash (fire), and broke down the walls of Yarawashalam.

Then Nabawazaraadan the rab (captain) of the guard carried away galah (captive) into Babal the yathar (residue) of the im (people) who remained in the Iyar, the deserters also who napal (fell) napal (away) to him, and the yathar (residue) of the im (people) who remained.

But Nabawazaraadan the rab (captain) of the guard shaar (left) of the Dal of the im (people), who had nothing, in the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah), and gave them vineyards and fields at the same yawam (time).
Now Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal tzawah (commanded) Nabawazaraadan the rab (captain) of the guard concerning Yaramayah, saying,
Take him, and iyan (look) well to him, and do him no harm; but do to him even as he shall dabar (tell) you.
So Nabawazaraadan the rab (captain) of the guard sent, and Nabawashazaban, Rabsaris, and Naragalasharaatzar Sharezer, Rabmag, and all the chief rab (officers) of the malak (king) of Babal;

they sent, and took Yaramayah out of the court of the guard, and committed him to Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam, the ban (son) Shapan Shaphan, that he should yatzaa (carry) him bayath (home): so he lived among the im (people).
Now the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Yaramayah, while he was itzar (shut) up in the court of the guard, saying,

halak (go), and amar (speak) to Ibadamalak the Kawashay (Ethiopian), saying, Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): Behold, I will bawaa (bring) my dabar (words) on this Iyar for rai (evil), and not for tawab (good); and they shall be accomplished panayam (before) you in that yawam (day).
But I will natzal (deliver) you in that yawam (day), says Yahawah; and you shall not be given into the yad (hand) of the men of whom you are Yagawar.

For I will malat (surely) malat (save) you, and you shall not napal (fall) by the charab (sword), but your napash (life) shall be for a prey to you; because you have batach (put) your trust in me, says Yahawah.

The dabar (word) which came to Yaramayah from Yahawah, achar (after) that Nabawazaraadan the rab (captain) of the guard had let him shalach (go) from Ramah, when he had taken him being bound in chains among all the captives of Yarawashalam and Yahawadah (Judah), who were carried away galah (captive) to Babal.
The rab (captain) of the guard took Yaramayah, and said to him, Yahawah your Alahayam pronounced this rai (evil) on this place;
and Yahawah has brought it, and done according as he spoke: because you have sinned against Yahawah, and have not obeyed his qawal (voice), therefore this thing has come on you.

Now, behold, I release you this yawam (day) from the chains which are on your yad (hand). If it seems tawab (good) to you to bawaa (come) with me into Babal, bawaa (come), and I will shawam (take) care of you; but if it seems bad to you to bawaa (come) with me into Babal, don't: raah (see), all the aratz (land) is panayam (before) you; where it seems tawab (good) and yashar (right) to you to yalak (go), there yalak (go).

Now while he had not yet gone shawab (turn back / repent), shawab (turn back / repent) back then, he said, to Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam, the ban (son) Shapan Shaphan, whom the malak (king) of Babal has made governor over the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and yashab (dwell) with him among the im (people); or yalak (go) wherever it seems yashar (right) to you to yalak (go). So the rab (captain) of the guard gave him food and a present, and let him shalach (go).
Then went Yaramayah to Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam Matzapah Mizpah, and lived with him among the im (people) who were shaar (left) in the aratz (land).

Now when all the shar (captains) of the chayal (forces) who were in the shadah (fields), even they and their men, heard that the malak (king) of Babal had made Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam governor in the aratz (land), and had committed to him men, and women, and tap (children), and Dalah the poorest of the aratz (land), of those who were not carried away galah (captive) to Babal;

then they came to Gadalayah Matzapah Mizpah, Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah, and Yawachanan and Yawanathan the ban (sons) of Qarach, and Sharayah the ban (son) of Thanachamath, and the ban (sons) of Iwapay the Natapathay (Netophathite), and Yazanayah the ban (son) Maikathay the Maacathite, they and their men.

Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam the ban (son) Shapan Shaphan swore to them and to their men, saying, Don't be yaraa (afraid) to ibad (serve) the Kashaday (Chaldeans): yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land), and ibad (serve) the malak (king) of Babal, and it shall be yatab (well) with you.

As for me, behold, I will yashab (dwell) Matzapah Mizpah, to imad (stand) before the Kashaday (Chaldeans) who shall bawaa (come) to us: but you, asap (gather) yayan (wine) and qayatz (summer) fruits and shaman (oil), and shawam (put) them in your vessels, and yashab (dwell) in your Iyar that you have taken.

Likewise when all the Yahawaday (Jews) who were in Mawaab, and among the children of Imawan, and in Adam, and who were in all the aratz (countries), heard that the malak (king) of Babal had left a shaarayath (remnant) of Yahawadah (Judah), and that he had paqad (set) over them Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam, the ban (son) Shapan Shaphan;

then all the Yahawaday (Jews) returned out of all places where they were driven, and came to the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah), to Gadalayah, Matzapah Mizpah, and gathered yayan (wine) and qayatz (summer) fruits very much.
Moreover Yawachanan the ban (son) of Qarach, and all the shar (captains) of the chayal (forces) who were in the shadah (fields), came to Gadalayah Matzapah Mizpah,

and said to him, Do you yadai (know) that Bailayas the malak (king) of the children of Ammon has sent Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah to take your life? But Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam didn't aman (believe) them.

Then Yawachanan the ban (son) of Qarach spoke to Gadalayah Matzapah Mizpah secretly, saying, Please let me yalak (go), and I will kill Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah, and no ayash (man) shall yadai (know) it: why should he take your life, that all the Yahawaday (Jews) who are gathered to you should be scattered, and the shaarayath (remnant) of Yahawadah (Judah) abad (perish)?
But Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam said to Yawachanan the ban (son) of Qarach, You shall not do this thing; for you dabar (speak) falsely of Yashamaial.

Now it happened in the shabayaiy (seventh) chadash (month), that Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah, the ban (son) of Alayashamai, of the zarai (seed) malawakah (royal) and one of the chief rab (officers) of the malak (king), and ishar (ten) men with him, came to Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam Matzapah Mizpah; and there they ate lacham (bread) together Matzapah Mizpah.

Then qawam (arose) Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah, and the ishar (ten) men who were with him, and struck Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam the ban (son) Shapan Shaphan with the charab (sword), and killed him, whom the malak (king) of Babal had made governor over the aratz (land).
Yashamaial also killed all the Yahawaday (Jews) who were with him, with Gadalayah, Matzapah Mizpah, and the Kashaday (Chaldeans) who were found there, the men of war.
It happened the shanay (second) yawam (day) after he had killed Gadalayah, and no ayash (man) knew it,

that there came men from Shakam, from Shayalah, and from Shamarawan, even shamanayam (eighty) men, having their beards shaved and their clothes torn, and having cut themselves, with meal manachah (offerings) and frankincense in their yad (hand), to bawaa (bring) them to the bayath (house) of Yahawah.

Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah went yatzaa (forth) Matzapah Mizpah to qaraah (meet) them, weeping all halak (along) as he went: and it happened, as he met them, he said to them, bawaa (come) to Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam.
It was so, when they came into the midst of the Iyar, that Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah killed them, and cast them into the midst of the bawar (pit), he, and the men who were with him.

But ishar (ten) men were found among those who said to Yashamaial, Don't mawath (kill) us; for we have stores hidden in the shadah (field), of wheat, and of barley, and of shaman (oil), and of honey. So he stopped, and didn't mawath (kill) them among their ach (brothers).

Now the bawar (pit) in which Yashamaial cast all the pagar (dead) bodies of the men whom he had killed, by the yad (side) of Gadalayah (the same was who which Asaa the malak (king) had made for panayam (fear) of Baishaa malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel)), Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah filled it Chalal those who were killed.

Then Yashamaial carried away captive all the shaarayath (residue) of the im (people) who were Matzapah Mizpah, even the malak (king's) bath (daughters), and all the im (people) who remained Matzapah Mizpah, whom Nabawazaraadan the rab (captain) of the guard had committed to Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam; Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah carried them away captive, and departed to ibar (go) over to the children of Ammon.
But when Yawachanan the ban (son) of Qarach, and all the shar (captains) of the chayal (forces) who were with him, heard of all the rai (evil) that Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah had done,
then they took all the men, and went to fight with Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah, and found him by the rab (great) mayam (waters) that are in Gabaiwan.

Now it happened that, when all the im (people) who were with Yashamaial saw Yawachanan the ban (son) of Qarach, and all the shar (captains) of the chayal (forces) who were with him, then they were Shamach.
So all the im (people) who Yashamaial had carried away captive Matzapah Mizpah turned sabab (about) and came back, and went to Yawachanan the ban (son) of Qarach.
But Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah escaped from Yawachanan with shamanah (eight) men, and went to the children of Ammon.

Then took Yawachanan the ban (son) of Qarach, and all the shar (captains) of the chayal (forces) who were with him, all the shaarayath (remnant) of the im (people) whom he had recovered from Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah, Matzapah Mizpah, achar (after) that he had killed Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam, the men of war, and the women, and the tap (children), and the eunuchs, whom he had brought shawab (turn back / repent) from Gabaiwan:
and they departed, and lived in Geruth Kamaham, which is by Bayathalacham, to yalak (go) to bawaa (enter) into Matzarayam,

panayam (because) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans); for they were yaraa (afraid) of them, because Yashamaial the ban (son) of Nathanayah had killed Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam, whom the malak (king) of Babal made governor over the aratz (land).

Then all the shar (captains) of the chayal (forces), and Yawachanan the ban (son) of Qarach, and Yazanayah the ban (son) of Hawashaiyah, and all the im (people) from the qatan (least) even to the greatest, came near,

and said to Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet), Please let our supplication be presented panayam (before) you, and palal (pray) for us to Yahawah your Alahayam, even for all this shaarayath (remnant); for we are shaar (left) but a Mait of many, as your iyan (eyes) do raah (see) us:
that Yahawah your Alahayam may show us the darak (way) in which we should yalak (walk), and the thing that we should do.

Then Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet) said to them, I have heard you; behold, I will palal (pray) to Yahawah your Alahayam according to your dabar (words); and it shall happen that whatever thing Yahawah shall answer you, I will nagad (declare) it to you; I will keep nothing back from you.

Then they said to Yaramayah, Yahawah be a amath (true) and aman (faithful) witness among us, if we don't do according to all the dabar (word) with which Yahawah your Alahayam shall shalach (send) you to us.

Whether it be tawab (good), or whether it be rai (evil), we will obey the qawal (voice) of Yahawah our Alahayam, to whom we shalach (send) you; that it may be yatab (well) with us, when we obey the qawal (voice) of Yahawah our Alahayam.
It happened after ishar (ten) yawam (days), that the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Yaramayah.
Then called he Yawachanan the ban (son) of Qarach, and all the shar (captains) of the chayal (forces) who were with him, and all the im (people) from the qatan (least) even to the greatest,
and said to them, Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), to whom you sent me to napal (present) your supplication panayam (before) him:

If you will still live in this aratz (land), then will I banah (build) you, and not haras (pull) you down, and I will plant you, and not nathash (pluck) you up; for I grieve over the rai (distress) that I have brought on you.

Don't be yaraa (afraid) of the malak (king) of Babal, of whom you are yaraa (afraid); don't be yaraa (afraid) of him, says Yahawah: for I am with you to yashai (save) you, and to natzal (deliver) you from his yad (hand).
I will nathan (grant) you racham (mercy), that he may have racham (mercy) on you, and cause you to shawab (turn back / repent) to your own adamah (land).
But if you amar (say), We will not yashab (dwell) in this aratz (land); so that you don't obey the qawal (voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam,

saying, No; but we will bawaa (go) into the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, where we shall raah (see) no war, nor hear the qawal (sound) of the trumpet, nor have hunger of lacham (bread); and there will we yashab (dwell):

now therefore hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah, O shaarayath (remnant) of Yahawadah (Judah): Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), If you indeed shawam (set) your panayam (faces) to bawaa (enter) into Matzarayam, and bawaa (go) to live there;

then it shall happen, that the charab (sword), which you yaraa (fear), shall overtake you there in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam; and the famine, about which you are afraid, shall follow close achar (behind) you there in Matzarayam; and there you shall mawath (die).

So shall it be with all the men who shawam (set) their panayam (faces) to bawaa (go) into Matzarayam to live there: they shall mawath (die) by the charab (sword), by the famine, and by the dabar (pestilence); and none of them shall sharayad (remain) or escape from the rai (evil) that I will bawaa (bring) on them.

For thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): As my ap (anger) and my chamah (wrath) has been poured forth on the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, so shall my chamah (wrath) be poured forth on you, when you shall bawaa (enter) into Matzarayam; and you shall be an object of horror, and an astonishment, and a qalalah (curse), and a reproach; and you shall raah (see) this place no more.
Yahawah has spoken concerning you, shaarayath (remnant) of Yahawadah (Judah), Don't you bawaa (go) into Matzarayam: yadai (know) yadai (certainly) that I have testified to you this yawam (day).

For you have dealt deceitfully against your own napash (souls); for you sent me to Yahawah your Alahayam, saying, palal (pray) for us to Yahawah our Alahayam; and according to all that Yahawah our Alahayam shall amar (say), so nagad (declare) to us, and we will do it:
and I have this yawam (day) declared it to you; but you have not obeyed the qawal (voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam in anything for which he has sent me to you.

Now therefore yadai (know) yadai (certainly) that you shall mawath (die) by the charab (sword), by the famine, and by the dabar (pestilence), in the place where you desire to bawaa (go) to live there.

It happened that, when Yaramayah had made an kalah (end) of speaking to all the im (people) all the dabar (words) of Yahawah their Alahayam, with which Yahawah their Alahayam had sent him to them, even all these dabar (words),

then spoke Izarayah the ban (son) of Hawashaiyah, and Yawachanan the ban (son) of Qarach, and all the Zad men, saying to Yaramayah, You dabar (speak) falsely: Yahawah our Alahayam has not sent you to amar (say), You shall not bawaa (go) into Matzarayam to live there;

but Barawak the ban (son) of Narayah sets you on against us, to nathan (deliver) us into the yad (hand) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), that they may put us to mawath (death), and galah (carry) us away captive to Babal.

So Yawachanan the ban (son) of Qarach, and all the shar (captains) of the chayal (forces), and all the im (people), didn't obey the qawal (voice) of Yahawah, to yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah).

But Yawachanan the ban (son) of Qarach, and all the shar (captains) of the chayal (forces), took all the shaarayath (remnant) of Yahawadah (Judah), who were returned from all the gawayam (nations) where they had been driven, to live in the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah);

the men, and the women, and the tap (children), and the malak (king's) bath (daughters), and every napash (person) who Nabawazaraadan the rab (captain) of the guard had left with Gadalayah the ban (son) of Achayaqam, the ban (son) Shapan Shaphan; and Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet), and Barawak the ban (son) of Narayah;
and they came into the aratz (land) of Matzarayam; for they didn't obey the qawal (voice) of Yahawah: and they came to Thachapanachas.
Then came the dabar (word) of Yahawah to Yaramayah in Thachapanachas, saying,

Take gadawal (great) aban (stones) in your yad (hand), and hide them in mortar in the brick malaban (work), which is at the entry of Paraih bayath (house) in Thachapanachas, in the iyan (sight) of the men Yahawaday Judah;

and amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): Behold, I will shalach (send) and take Nabawakadanaatzar the malak (king) of Babal, my ibad (servant), and will shawam (set) his kasaa (throne) on these aban (stones) that I have hidden; and he shall natah (spread) his royal pavilion over them.

He shall bawaa (come), and shall strike the aratz (land) of Matzarayam; such as are for mawath (death) shall be put to mawath (death), and such as are for Shabay to Shabay, and such as are for the charab (sword) to the charab (sword).

I will yatzath (kindle) a ash (fire) in the bayath (houses) of the Alahayam of Matzarayam; and he shall sharap (burn) them, and carry them away captive: and he shall itah (array) himself with the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, as a raih (shepherd) itah (puts) on his bagad (garment); and he shall yatzaa (go) forth from there in shalawam (peace).

He shall also shabar (break) the matzabah (pillars) of Bayathashamash Shemesh, that is in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam; and the bayath (houses) of the Alahayam of Matzarayam shall he sharap (burn) with ash (fire).

The dabar (word) that came to Yaramayah concerning all the Yahawaday (Jews) who lived in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, who lived at Magadawal, and at Thachapanachas, and Nap Memphis, and in the aratz (country) of Patharawas, saying,

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): You have seen all the rai (evil) that I have brought on Yarawashalam, and on all the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah); and behold, this yawam (day) they are a desolation, and no man yashab (dwells) therein,

panayam (because) of their wickedness which they have committed to provoke me to kais (anger), in that they went to qatar (burn) incense, to ibad (serve) other Alahayam, that they didn't yadai (know), neither they, nor you, nor your abawath (fathers).
However I sent to you all my ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets), rising up shakam (early) and sending them, saying, Oh, don't do this thawaibah (abominable) thing that I shanaa (hate).
But they didn't listen, nor inclined their ear to shawab (turn back / repent) from their wickedness, to qatar (burn) no incense to other Alahayam.

Therefore my chamah (wrath) and my ap (anger) was poured forth, and was kindled in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah) and in the streets of Yarawashalam; and they are wasted and desolate, as it is this yawam (day).

Therefore now thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): Why do you ishah (commit) gadawal (great) rai (evil) against your own napash (souls), to karath (cut) off from yourselves ayash (man) and ashah (woman), infant and nursing child out of the midst of Yahawadah (Judah), to yathar (leave) yourselves none remaining;

in that you provoke me to kais (anger) with the maishah (works) of your yad (hands), burning qatar (incense) to other Alahayam in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, where you have gone to live; that you may be karath (cut) off, and that you may be a qalalah (curse) and a reproach among all the gawayay (nations) of the aratz (earth)?

Have you forgotten the wickedness of your abawath (fathers), and the wickedness of the malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), and the wickedness of their wives, and your own wickedness, and the wickedness of your wives which they committed in the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the streets of Yarawashalam?

They are not humbled even to this yawam (day), neither have they feared, nor walked in my thawarah (law), nor in my chaqah (statutes), that I nathan (set) panayam (before) you and panayam (before) your abawath (fathers).

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): Behold, I will shawam (set) my panayam (face) against you for rai (evil), even to karath (cut) off all Yahawadah (Judah).

I will take the shaarayath (remnant) of Yahawadah (Judah), that have shawam (set) their panayam (faces) to bawaa (go) into the aratz (land) of Matzarayam to live there, and they shall all be consumed; in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam shall they napal (fall); they shall be consumed by the charab (sword) and by the famine; they shall mawath (die), from the qatan (least) even to the greatest, by the charab (sword) and by the famine; and they shall be an object of horror, an astonishment, and a qalalah (curse), and a reproach.
For I will paqad (punish) those who yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, as I have punished Yarawashalam, by the charab (sword), by the famine, and by the dabar (pestilence);

so that none of the shaarayath (remnant) of Yahawadah (Judah), who have gone into the aratz (land) of Matzarayam to live there, shall escape or be sharayad (left), to shawab (turn back / repent) into the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah), to which they have a napash (desire) to shawab (turn back / repent) to yashab (dwell) there: for none shall shawab (turn back / repent) palat (save) such as shall escape.

Then all the men who knew that their wives burned qatar (incense) to other Alahayam, and all the women who stood by, a gadawal (great) qahal (assembly), even all the im (people) who lived in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, in Patharawas, answered Yaramayah, saying,
As for the dabar (word) that you have spoken to us in the sham (name) of Yahawah, we will not listen to you.

But we will ishah (certainly) ishah (perform) every dabar (word) that is gone yatzaa (forth) out of our pah (mouth), to qatar (burn) incense to the malakath (queen) of the sky, and to pour out drink nasak (offerings) to her, as we have done, we and our abawath (fathers), our malak (kings) and our shar (princes), in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the streets of Yarawashalam; for then had we plenty of lacham (food), and were tawab (well), and saw no rai (evil).

But since we left off burning qatar (incense) to the malakath (queen) of the sky, and pouring out drink nasak (offerings) to her, we have wanted all things, and have been consumed by the charab (sword) and by the famine.

When we burned qatar (incense) to the malakath (queen) of the sky, and poured out drink nasak (offerings) to her, did we ishah (make) her cakes to itzab (worship) her, and pour out drink nasak (offerings) to her, balaiday (without) our anawash (husbands)?
Then Yaramayah said to all the im (people), to the men, and to the women, even to all the im (people) who had given him an dabar (answer), saying,

The incense that you burned in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the streets of Yarawashalam, you and your abawath (fathers), your malak (kings) and your shar (princes), and the im (people) of the aratz (land), didn't Yahawah zakar (remember) them, and didn't it ilah (come) into his lab (mind)?

so that Yahawah could no longer nashaa (bear), panayam (because) of the rai (evil) of your mailal (doings), and panayam (because) of the thawaibah (abominations) which you have committed; therefore your aratz (land) has become a desolation, and an astonishment, and a qalalah (curse), without yashab (inhabitant), as it is this yawam (day).

panayam (because) you have burned qatar (incense), and because you have sinned against Yahawah, and have not obeyed the qawal (voice) of Yahawah, nor walked in his thawarah (law), nor in his chaqah (statutes), nor in his idawath (testimonies); therefore this rai (evil) has happened to you, as it is this yawam (day).
Moreover Yaramayah said to all the im (people), and to all the women, Hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah, all Yahawadah (Judah) who are in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam:

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, You and your wives have both spoken with your pah (mouths), and with your yad (hands) have fulfilled it, saying, We will ishah (surely) ishah (perform) our nadar (vows) that we have vowed, to qatar (burn) incense to the malakath (queen) of the sky, and to pour out drink nasak (offerings) to her: qawam (establish) then your nadar (vows), and ishah (perform) your nadar (vows).
