Therefore hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah, all Yahawadah (Judah) who yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam: Behold, I have sworn by my gadawal (great) sham (name), amar (says) Yahawah, that my sham (name) shall no more be named in the pah (mouth) of any ayash (man) of Yahawadah (Judah) in all the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, saying, As the Adanay Yahawah chay (lives).

Behold, I watch over them for rai (evil), and not for tawab (good); and all the men of Yahawadah (Judah) who are in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam shall be consumed by the charab (sword) and by the famine, until they are all gone.

Those who escape the charab (sword) shall shawab (turn back / repent) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam into the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah), few in number; and all the shaarayath (remnant) of Yahawadah (Judah), who have gone into the aratz (land) of Matzarayam to live there, shall yadai (know) whose dabar (word) shall qawam (stand), mine, or theirs.

This shall be the awath (sign) to you, says Yahawah, that I will paqad (punish) you in this place, that you may yadai (know) that my dabar (words) shall qawam (surely) qawam (stand) against you for rai (evil):

Thus amar (says) Yahawah, Behold, I will nathan (give) Paraihachaparai Hophra malak (king) of Matzarayam into the yad (hand) of his ayab (enemies), and into the yad (hand) of those who seek his napash (life); as I gave Tzadaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) into the yad (hand) of Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal, who was his ayab (enemy), and sought his napash (life).

The dabar (message) that Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet) spoke to Barawak the ban (son) of Narayah, when he wrote these dabar (words) in a book at the pah (mouth) of Yaramayah, in the rabayaiy (fourth) Shanah of Yahawayaqayam the ban (son) of Yaashayah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), saying,
Thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), to you, Barawak:
You said, Woe is me now! for Yahawah has added sorrow to my pain; I am weary with my groaning, and I matzaa (find) no manawachah (rest).

You shall amar (tell) him, Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Behold, that which I have built will I haras (break) down, and that which I have planted I will nathash (pluck) up; and this in the whole aratz (land).

Do you seek gadawal (great) things for yourself? Don't seek them; for, behold, I will bawaa (bring) rai (evil) on all flesh, says Yahawah; but your napash (life) will I nathan (give) to you for a prey in all places where you yalak (go).
The dabar (word) of Yahawah which came to Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet) concerning the gawayam (nations).

Of Matzarayam: concerning the chayal (army) of Paraihanakah Necoh malak (king) of Matzarayam, which was by the nahar (river) Parath in Karakamayash, which Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal struck in the rabayaiy (fourth) Shanah of Yahawayaqayam the ban (son) of Yaashayah, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah).
Prepare the magan (buckler) and tzanah (shield), and draw near to battle!
Harness the horses, and ilah (get) up, you horsemen, and stand forth with your helmets; furbish the spears, Labash on the coats of mail.

Why have I seen it? they are chath (dismayed) and are turned backward; and their gabawar (mighty) ones are beaten down, and have fled manawas (apace), and don't panah (look) back: magawar (terror) is on every side, says Yahawah.
Don't let the qal (swift) flee away, nor the gabawar (mighty) man malat (escape); in the tzapawan (north) by the nahar (river) Parath have they stumbled and fallen.
Who is this who ilah (rises) up like the Nile, whose mayam (waters) toss themselves like the nahar (rivers)?

Matzarayam ilah (rises) up like the Nile, and his mayam (waters) toss themselves like the nahar (rivers): and he amar (says), I will ilah (rise) up, I will cover the aratz (earth); I will abad (destroy) Iyar and its yashab (inhabitants).

ilah (go) up, you horses; and halal (rage), you chariots; and let the gabawar (mighty) men yatzaa (go) forth: Kawash and Pawat, who handle the magan (shield); and the Lawaday (Ludim), who handle and bend the qashath (bow).

For that yawam (day) is of the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), a yawam (day) of vengeance, that he may avenge him of his tzar (adversaries): and the charab (sword) shall akal (devour) and be satiate, and shall drink its fill of their dam (blood); for the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), has a zabach (sacrifice) in the tzapawan (north) aratz (country) by the nahar (river) Parath.
ilah (go) up into Galaid, and take balm, virgin bath (daughter) of Matzarayam: in vain do you use many medicines; there is no thailah (healing) for you.

The gawayam (nations) have heard of your qalawan (shame), and the aratz (earth) is full of your cry; for the gabawar (mighty) gabawar (man) has stumbled against the gabawar (mighty), they are fallen shanayam (both) of them together.
The dabar (word) that Yahawah spoke to Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet), how that Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal should bawaa (come) and strike the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
nagad (declare) in Matzarayam, and publish in Magadawal, and publish Nap Memphis and in Thachapanachas: amar (say), Stand forth, and kawan (prepare); for the charab (sword) has devoured around you.
Why are your abayar (strong) sachap (ones) swept away? they didn't imad (stand), because Yahawah pushed them.

He made many to stumble, yes, they napal (fell) one on rai (another): and they said, qawam (arise), and let us shawab (turn back / repent) again to our own im (people), and to the aratz (land) of our birth, from the oppressing charab (sword).
They cried there, Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam is but a noise; he has let the mawaid (appointed) time ibar (pass) by.
As I chay (live), says the malak (king), whose sham (name) is Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), surely like Thabawar among the har (mountains), and like Karamal by the yam (sea), so shall he bawaa (come).
You bath (daughter) who yashab (dwells) in Matzarayam, ishah (furnish) yourself to go into captivity; Nap Memphis shall become a desolation, and shall be burnt up, without yashab (inhabitant).
Matzarayam is a Yapahapayah beautiful Igalah; but destruction out of the tzapawan (north) has bawaa (come), it has come.

Also her shakayar (hired) men in the qarab (midst) of her are like calves of the stall; for they also are turned panah (back), they are fled away together, they didn't imad (stand): for the yawam (day) of their calamity has bawaa (come) on them, the ith (time) of their visitation.
The qawal (sound) of it shall yalak (go) like the serpent; for they shall yalak (march) with an chayal (army), and bawaa (come) against her with axes, as itz (wood) cutters.
They shall karath (cut) down her Yair, says Yahawah, though it can't be searched; because they are more than the locusts, and are innumerable.
The bath (daughter) of Matzarayam shall be disappointed; she shall be delivered into the yad (hand) of the im (people) of the tzapawan (north).

Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), amar (says): Behold, I will paqad (punish) Amon Naa No, and Paraih, and Matzarayam, with her Alahayam, and her malak (kings); even Paraih, and those who batach (trust) in him:

and I will nathan (deliver) them into the yad (hand) of those who seek their lives, and into the yad (hand) of Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal, and into the yad (hand) of his ibad (servants); and afterwards it shall be inhabited, as in the yawam (days) of qadam (old), says Yahawah.

But don't you be yaraa (afraid), Yaiqab my ibad (servant), neither be dismayed, Yasharaal (Israel): for, behold, I will yashai (save) you from Rachawaq, and your zarai (seed) from the aratz (land) of their Shabay; and Yaiqab shall shawab (turn back / repent), and shall be shaqat (quiet) and at shaan (ease), and none shall make him afraid.

Don't you be yaraa (afraid), O Yaiqab my ibad (servant), says Yahawah; for I am with you: for I will ishah (make) a full end of all the gawayam (nations) where I have driven you; but I will not ishah (make) a full end of you, but I will correct you in mashapat (measure), and will in no naqah (way) leave you unpunished.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah that came to Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet) concerning the Palashathay (Philistines), before that Paraih struck Izah.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Behold, mayam (waters) ilah (rise) up out of the tzapawan (north), and shall become an overflowing nachal (stream), and shall overflow the aratz (land) and all that is therein, the Iyar and those who yashab (dwell) therein; and the men shall cry, and all the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land) shall wail.

At the qawal (noise) of the stamping of the hoofs of his abayar (strong) raish (ones), at the rushing of his chariots, at the rumbling of his galagal (wheels), the abawath (fathers) don't panah (look) back to their children for feebleness of yad (hands);

because of the yawam (day) that bawaa (comes) to shadad (destroy) all the Palashathay (Philistines), to karath (cut) off from Tzar and Tzayadawan every helper who sharayad (remains): for Yahawah will shadad (destroy) the Palashathay (Philistines), the shaarayath (remnant) of the isle of Kapathar.
Baldness has bawaa (come) on Izah; Ashaqalawan is damah (brought) to nothing, the shaarayath (remnant) of their valley: how long will you cut yourself?
You charab (sword) of Yahawah, how long will it be laa (before) you be shaqat (quiet)? asap (put) up yourself into your scabbard; ragai (rest), and be still.
How can you be shaqat (quiet), since Yahawah has given you a tzawah (command)? Against Ashaqalawan, and against the seashore, there has he appointed it.

Of Mawaab. Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): Woe to Nabaw! for it is laid shadad (waste); Qarayathayam is disappointed, it is taken; Misgab is put to yabash (shame) and broken down.

The thahalah (praise) of Mawaab is no more; in Chashabawan they have devised rai (evil) against her: yalak (come), and let us karath (cut) her off from being a gaway (nation). You also, Madaman, shall be brought to silence: the charab (sword) shall yalak (pursue) you.
The qawal (sound) of a qawal (cry) from Charanayam, desolation and gadawal (great) destruction!
Mawaab is destroyed; her Tzaiyar ones have caused a cry to be heard.
For by the ascent of Lawachayath with continual weeping shall they ilah (go) up; for at the descent of Charanayam they have heard the distress of the cry of destruction.
Flee, malat (save) your lives, and be like the heath in the madabar (wilderness).

For, because you have trusted in your maishah (works) and in your treasures, you also shall be taken: and Kamawash shall yatzaa (go) forth into captivity, his kahan (priests) and his shar (princes) together.
The shadad (destroyer) shall bawaa (come) on every Iyar, and no Iyar shall malat (escape); the valley also shall abad (perish), and the mayashawar (plain) shall be destroyed; as Yahawah has spoken.
nathan (give) wings to Mawaab, that she may fly and yatzaa (get) her away: and her Iyar shall become a desolation, without any to yashab (dwell) therein.
Cursed is he who does the malaakah (work) of Yahawah negligently; and cursed is he who keeps back his charab (sword) from dam (blood).

Mawaab has been at shaan (ease) from his youth, and he has settled on his lees, and has not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither has he gone into captivity: therefore his taim (taste) imad (remains) in him, and his rayach (scent) is not changed.

Therefore, behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), says Yahawah, that I will shalach (send) to him those who pour off, and they shall pour him off; and they shall empty his vessels, and break their bottles in pieces.
Mawaab shall be bawash (ashamed) of Kamawash, as the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) was bawash (ashamed) of Bayathaal their confidence.
How do you amar (say), We are gabawar (mighty) chayal (men), and valiant men for the war?
Mawaab is laid shadad (waste), and they are gone up into his Iyar, and his chosen young men are gone down to the slaughter, says the malak (king), whose sham (name) is Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
The calamity of Mawaab is qarawab (near) to bawaa (come), and his rai (affliction) hurries maad (fast).
All you who are around him, nawad (bemoan) him, and all you who yadai (know) his sham (name); amar (say), How is the iz (strong) matah (staff) shabar (broken), the thapaarah (beautiful) maqal (rod)!

You bath (daughter) who yashab (dwells) in Dayabawan, yarad (come) down from your kabawad (glory), and yashab (sit) in thirst; for the shadad (destroyer) of Mawaab has ilah (come) up against you, he has destroyed your strongholds.
yashab (inhabitant) of Irawair, imad (stand) by the darak (way), and watch: shaal (ask) him who flees, and her who malat (escapes); amar (say), What has been done?
Mawaab is disappointed; for it is broken down: wail and cry; nagad (tell) it by the Aranawan, that Mawaab is laid shadad (waste).
mashapat (judgment) has bawaa (come) on the mayashawar (plain) aratz (country), on Chalawan, and on Yahatz, and on Mawapaith,
and on Dayabawan, and on Nabaw, and on Bayathadabalathayam Diblathaim,
and on Qarayathayam, and on Bayathagamawal Gamul, and on Bayathabailamaiwan Meon,
and on Qarayawath, and on Batzarah, and on all the Iyar of the aratz (land) of Mawaab, Rachawaq or qarawab (near).
The qaran (horn) of Mawaab is cut off, and his zarawai (arm) is shabar (broken), says Yahawah.
Shakar him drunken; for he magnified himself against Yahawah: and Mawaab shall wallow in his vomit, and he also shall be in derision.
For wasn't Yasharaal (Israel) a derision to you? was he found among thieves? for as often as you speak of him, you nawad (shake) your head.
You yashab (inhabitants) of Mawaab, leave the Iyar, and yashab (dwell) in the salai (rock); and be like the dove that makes her nest over the pah (mouth) of the abyss.
We have heard of the pride of Mawaab. He is very Gaah; his loftiness, and his pride, and his arrogance, and the haughtiness of his lab (heart).
I yadai (know) his ibarah (wrath), says Yahawah, that it is nothing; his boastings have worked nothing.
Therefore will I wail for Mawaab; yes, I will cry out for all Mawaab: for the men of Qayaracharash Heres shall they mourn.

With more than the weeping of Yaizayar will I weep for you, vine of Shabam: your branches passed over the yam (sea), they reached even to the yam (sea) of Yaizayar: on your qayatz (summer) fruits and on your vintage the shadad (destroyer) is fallen.

Gladness and joy is taken away from the fruitful field and from the aratz (land) of Mawaab; and I have caused yayan (wine) to shabath (cease) from the yaqab (wine) presses: none shall tread with shouting; the shouting shall be no shouting.

From the cry of Chashabawan even to Alailaa, even to Yahatz have they uttered their qawal (voice), from Tzair even to Charanayam, Igalah Eglath Shelishiyah: for the mayam (waters) of Namarayam also shall become desolate.
Moreover I will shabath (cause) to cease in Mawaab, says Yahawah, him who ilah (offers) in the bamah (high) place, and him who qatar (burns) incense to his Alahayam.
Therefore my lab (heart) sounds for Mawaab like pipes, and my lab (heart) sounds like pipes for the men of Qayaracharash Heres: therefore the abundance that he has gotten is perished.
For every raash (head) is bald, and every beard clipped: on all the yad (hands) are cuttings, and on the waist sackcloth.
On all the housetops of Mawaab and in its streets there is lamentation every where; for I have shabar (broken) Mawaab like a vessel in which none Chapatz, says Yahawah.
How it is broken down! How they wail! How Mawaab has turned the back with shame! So shall Mawaab become a derision and a terror to all who are around him.
For thus amar (says) Yahawah: Behold, he shall fly as an eagle, and shall spread out his wings against Mawaab.

Qarayawath is taken, and the strongholds are seized, and the lab (heart) of the gabawar (mighty) men of Mawaab at that yawam (day) shall be as the lab (heart) of a ashah (woman) in her tzarar (pangs).
Mawaab shall be destroyed from being a im (people), because he has magnified himself against Yahawah.
pachad (fear), and the pachath (pit), and the snare, are on you, yashab (inhabitant) of Mawaab, says Yahawah.

He who flees from the pachad (fear) shall napal (fall) into the pachath (pit); and he who ilah (gets) up out of the pachath (pit) shall be taken in the snare: for I will bawaa (bring) on him, even on Mawaab, the Shanah of their visitation, says Yahawah.

Those who fled imad (stand) without kach (strength) under the shadow of Chashabawan; for a ash (fire) is gone yatzaa (forth) out of Chashabawan, and a lahabah (flame) from the midst of Sayachawan, and has devoured the corner of Mawaab, and the qadaqad (crown) of the head of the tumultuous ones.
Woe to you, O Mawaab! the im (people) of Kamawash is abad (undone); for your ban (sons) are taken Shabay captive, and your bath (daughters) into captivity.
Yet will I shawab (turn back / repent) back the captivity of Mawaab in the acharayath (latter) yawam (days), says Yahawah. hanah (thus) far is the mashapat (judgment) of Mawaab.
Of the children of Ammon. Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Has Yasharaal (Israel) no ban (sons)? has he no heir? why then does Malcam yarash (possess) Gad, and his im (people) yashab (dwell) in its Iyar?

Therefore, behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), amar (says) Yahawah, that I will cause an alarm of war to be heard against Rabah of the children of Ammon; and it shall become a desolate thal (heap), and her bath (daughters) shall be burned with ash (fire): then shall Yasharaal (Israel) yarash (possess) those who possessed him, says Yahawah.

Wail, Chashabawan, for Iy is laid shadad (waste); cry, you bath (daughters) of Rabah, clothe yourself in sackcloth: lament, and run back and forth among the fences; for Malcam shall yalak (go) into captivity, his kahan (priests) and his shar (princes) together.
Why do you glory in the valleys, your flowing valley, Shawabab bath (daughter)? who trusted in her treasures, saying, Who shall bawaa (come) to me?

Behold, I will bawaa (bring) a pachad (fear) on you, says the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), from all who are around you; and you shall be driven out every ayash (man) panayam (right) forth, and there shall be none to gather together the fugitives.
But afterward I will shawab (turn back / repent) back the captivity of the children of Imawan, says Yahawah.
Of Adam. Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): Is chakamah (wisdom) no more in Thayaman? is itzah (counsel) perished from the bayan (prudent)? is their chakamah (wisdom) vanished?
Flee, panah (turn) back, yashab (dwell) in the depths, yashab (inhabitants) of Dadan; for I will bawaa (bring) the calamity of Ishaw on him, the ith (time) that I shall paqad (visit) him.
If grape batzar (gatherers) came to you, would they not shaar (leave) some gleaning grapes? if thieves by layal (night), wouldn't they shachath (destroy) until they had enough?

But I have made Ishaw chashap (bare), I have uncovered his secret places, and he shall not be yakal (able) to hide himself: his zarai (seed) is destroyed, and his ach (brothers), and his Shakan; and he is no more.
Leave your fatherless children, I will chayah (preserve) them alive; and let your alamanah (widows) batach (trust) in me.

For thus amar (says) Yahawah: Behold, they to whom it didn't pertain to drink of the cup shall certainly drink; and are you he who shall altogether go unpunished? You shall not go unpunished, but you shall surely drink.
For I have sworn by myself, says Yahawah, that Batzarah shall become an astonishment, a reproach, a waste, and a qalalah (curse); and all its Iyar shall be perpetual wastes.
I have heard news from Yahawah, and an tzayar (ambassador) is sent among the gawayam (nations), saying, Gather yourselves together, and bawaa (come) against her, and qawam (rise) up to the battle.
For, behold, I have made you qatan (small) among the gawayam (nations), and despised among men.

As for your terror, the pride of your lab (heart) has deceived you, O you who shakan (dwell) in the clefts of the salai (rock), who hold the height of the Gabaih: though you should make your nest as high as the eagle, I will yarad (bring) you down from there, says Yahawah.
Adam shall become an astonishment: everyone who passes by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss at all its makah (plagues).
As in the overthrow of Sadam and Imarah and the Shakan cities of it, amar (says) Yahawah, no ayash (man) shall yashab (dwell) there, neither shall any ban (son) of adam (man) live therein.

Behold, he shall ilah (come) up like a aray (lion) from the pride of the Yaradan against the ayathan (strong) Nawah: for I will ragai (suddenly) make them run away from it; and whoever is chosen, him will I paqad (appoint) over it: for who is like me? and who will appoint me a time? and who is the raih (shepherd) who will imad (stand) panayam (before) me?

Therefore hear the itzah (counsel) of Yahawah, that he has taken against Adam; and his machashabah (purposes), that he has purposed against the yashab (inhabitants) of Thayaman: Surely they shall drag them away, the Tzaiyar tzaan (ones) of the flock; surely he shall make their Nawah shamam (desolate) over them.
The aratz (earth) trembles at the qawal (noise) of their napal (fall); there is a cry, the qawal (noise) which is heard in the Red yam (sea).

Behold, he shall ilah (come) up and fly as the eagle, and spread out his wings against Batzarah: and the lab (heart) of the gabawar (mighty) men of Adam at that yawam (day) shall be as the lab (heart) of a ashah (woman) in her tzarar (pangs).
Of Damashaq. Chamath is confounded, and Arapad; for they have heard rai (evil) news, they are melted away: there is daagah (sorrow) on the yam (sea); it can't be shaqat (quiet).
Damashaq has grown rapah (feeble), she panah (turns) herself to flee, and trembling has seized on her: tzarah (anguish) and sorrows have taken hold of her, as of a yalad (woman) in travail.
How is the Iyar of thahalah (praise) not forsaken, the city of my joy?
Therefore her young men shall napal (fall) in her streets, and all the men of war shall be brought to damam (silence) in that yawam (day), says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
I will yatzath (kindle) a ash (fire) in the wall of Damashaq, and it shall akal (devour) the palaces Banahadad Ben Hadad.

Of Qadar, and of the mamalakah (kingdoms) of Chatzawar, which Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal struck. Thus amar (says) Yahawah: qawam (arise), ilah (go) up to Qadar, and shadad (destroy) the children of the qadam (east).

Their ahal (tents) and their flocks shall they nashaa (take); they shall nashaa (carry) away for themselves their curtains, and all their vessels, and their camels; and they shall qaraa (cry) to them, magawar (terror) on every side!

Flee, wander maad (far) off, yashab (dwell) in the depths, you yashab (inhabitants) of Chatzawar, says Yahawah; for Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal has taken itzah (counsel) against you, and has conceived a machashabah (purpose) against you.
qawam (arise), ilah (go) up to a gaway (nation) that is at shalaw (ease), that yashab (dwells) without care, says Yahawah; that have neither gates nor bars, that shakan (dwell) badad (alone).

Their camels shall be a booty, and the multitude of their livestock a spoil: and I will scatter to all rawach (winds) those who have the corners of their beards cut off; and I will bawaa (bring) their calamity from every ibar (side) of them, says Yahawah.
Chatzawar shall be a dwelling place of jackals, a desolation iwalam (forever): no ayash (man) shall yashab (dwell) there, neither shall any ban (son) of adam (man) live therein.

The dabar (word) of Yahawah that came to Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet) concerning Iyalam, in the raashayath (beginning) of the malakawath (reign) of Tzadaqayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), saying,
Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): Behold, I will shabar (break) the qashath (bow) of Iyalam, the raashayath (chief) of their might.

On Iyalam will I bawaa (bring) the arabai (four) rawach (winds) from the arabai (four) quarters of the sky, and will scatter them toward all those rawach (winds); and there shall be no gaway (nation) where the outcasts of Iyalam shall not bawaa (come).

I will cause Iyalam to be dismayed panayam (before) their ayab (enemies), and panayam (before) those who seek their napash (life); and I will bawaa (bring) rai (evil) on them, even my charawan (fierce) ap (anger), says Yahawah; and I will shalach (send) the charab (sword) achar (after) them, until I have consumed them;
and I will shawam (set) my kasaa (throne) in Iyalam, and will abad (destroy) from there malak (king) and shar (princes), says Yahawah.
But it shall happen in the acharayath (latter) yawam (days), that I will shawab (turn back / repent) back the captivity of Iyalam, says Yahawah.
The dabar (word) that Yahawah spoke concerning Babal, concerning the aratz (land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), by Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet).

nagad (declare) among the gawayam (nations) and publish, and nashaa (set) up a nas (standard); publish, and don't conceal: amar (say), Babal is taken, Bal is disappointed, Maradak is dismayed; her itzab (images) are disappointed, her idols are dismayed.

For out of the tzapawan (north) there ilah (comes) up a gaway (nation) against her, which shall shayath (make) her aratz (land) desolate, and none shall yashab (dwell) therein: they are fled, they are gone, both adam (man) and animal.

In those yawam (days), and in that ith (time), says Yahawah, the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shall bawaa (come), they and the children of Yahawadah (Judah) together; they shall halak (go) on their yalak (way) weeping, and shall seek Yahawah their Alahayam.

They shall inquire concerning Tzayawan with their panayam (faces) turned toward it, saying, bawaa (come), and join yourselves to Yahawah in an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant) that shall not be forgotten.

My im (people) have been lost sheep: their raih (shepherds) have caused them to thaih (go) astray; they have turned them shawab (turn back / repent) on the har (mountains); they have gone from har (mountain) to Gabaih; they have forgotten their resting place.

All who found them have devoured them; and their tzar (adversaries) said, We are not asham (guilty), because they have sinned against Yahawah, the Nawah of tzadaq (righteousness), even Yahawah, the Maqawah of their abawath (fathers).
nawad (flee) out of the midst of Babal, and yatzaa (go) forth out of the aratz (land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), and be as the male goats panayam (before) the flocks.

For, behold, I will ilah (stir) up and ilah (cause) to come up against Babal a qahal (company) of gadawal (great) gawayam (nations) from the tzapawan (north) aratz (country); and they shall set themselves in array against her; from there she shall be taken: their chatz (arrows) shall be as of an expert gabawar (mighty) man; none shall shawab (turn back / repent) in vain.
Kashaday shall be a prey: all who prey on her shall be satisfied, says Yahawah.
Because you are Shamach, because you Shamach, O you who plunder my nachalah (heritage), because you are wanton as a Igalah that treads out the grain, and neigh as abayar (strong) horses;

your am (mother) shall be maad (utterly) disappointed; she who bore you shall be chapar (confounded): behold, she shall be the least of the gawayam (nations), a madabar (wilderness), a dry tzayah (land), and a irabah (desert).
Because of the qatzap (wrath) of Yahawah she shall not be inhabited, but she shall be wholly desolate: everyone who goes by Babal shall be astonished, and hiss at all her makah (plagues).
Set yourselves in array against Babal all around, all you who bend the qashath (bow); yadah (shoot) at her, spare no chatz (arrows): for she has sinned against Yahawah.

rawai (shout) against her all around: she has submitted herself; her bulwarks are fallen, her walls are thrown down; for it is the vengeance of Yahawah: take vengeance on her; as she has done, do to her.

karath (cut) off the zarai (sower) from Babal, and him who handles the sickle in the ith (time) of harvest: for panayam (fear) of the oppressing charab (sword) they shall panah (turn) everyone to his im (people), and they shall flee everyone to his own aratz (land).

Yasharaal (Israel) is a hunted sheep; the aray (lions) have driven him away: raashawan (first), the malak (king) of Ashawar devoured him; and now at Acharawan Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal has broken his itzam (bones).

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): Behold, I will paqad (punish) the malak (king) of Babal and his aratz (land), as I have punished the malak (king) of Ashawar.

I will shawab (turn back / repent) Yasharaal (Israel) again Nawah his pasture, and he shall raih (feed) on Karamal and Bashan, and his napash (soul) shall be satisfied on the har (hills) of Aparayam and in Galaid.

In those yawam (days), and in that ith (time), says Yahawah, the iwan (iniquity) of Yasharaal (Israel) shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the chataah (sins) of Yahawadah (Judah), and they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I leave as a shaar (remnant).

ilah (go) up against the aratz (land) of Marathayam, even against it, and against the yashab (inhabitants) of Paqawad: kill and utterly charam (destroy) achar (after) them, says Yahawah, and do according to all that I have tzawah (commanded) you.
A qawal (sound) of battle is in the aratz (land), and of gadawal (great) destruction.
How is the hammer of the whole aratz (earth) cut apart and shabar (broken)! how is Babal become a desolation among the gawayam (nations)!
I have laid a snare for you, and you are also taken, Babal, and you weren't yadai (aware): you are found, and also caught, because you have striven against Yahawah.

Yahawah has opened his armory, and has brought yatzaa (forth) the weapons of his indignation; for the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), has a malaakah (work) to do in the aratz (land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans).
bawaa (come) against her from the utmost border; pathach (open) her storehouses; cast her up as heaps, and charam (destroy) her utterly; let nothing of her be shaarayath (left).
Kill all her bulls; let them yarad (go) down to the slaughter: woe to them! for their yawam (day) has bawaa (come), the ith (time) of their visitation.
The qawal (voice) of those who flee and escape out of the aratz (land) of Babal, to nagad (declare) in Tzayawan the vengeance of Yahawah our Alahayam, the vengeance of his hayakal (temple).

Call together the archers against Babal, all those who bend the qashath (bow); chanah (encamp) against her all around; let none of it palayatah (escape): shalam (recompense) her according to her pail (work); according to all that she has done, do to her; for she has been proud against Yahawah, against the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).
Therefore her young men will napal (fall) in her streets, and all her men of war will be brought to damam (silence) in that yawam (day), says Yahawah.
Behold, I am against you, you proud one, says the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies); for your yawam (day) has bawaa (come), the ith (time) that I will paqad (visit) you.
The proud kashal (one) shall stumble and napal (fall), and none shall qawam (raise) him up; and I will yatzath (kindle) a ash (fire) in his Iyar, and it shall akal (devour) all who are around him.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): The children of Yasharaal (Israel) and the children of Yahawadah (Judah) are oppressed together; and all who took them captive chazaq (hold) them fast; they refuse to let them shalach (go).

Their gaal (redeemer) is chazaq (strong); Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) is his sham (name): he will rayab (thoroughly) rayab (plead) their rayab (cause), that he may give ragai (rest) to the aratz (earth), and disquiet the yashab (inhabitants) of Babal.
A charab (sword) is on the Kashaday (Chaldeans), says Yahawah, and on the yashab (inhabitants) of Babal, and on her shar (princes), and on her chakam (wise) men.
A charab (sword) is on the boasters, and they shall become fools; a charab (sword) is on her gabawar (mighty) men, and they shall be dismayed.

A charab (sword) is on their horses, and on their chariots, and on all the mixed people who are in the midst of her; and they shall become as women: a charab (sword) is on her treasures, and they shall be robbed.
A drought is on her mayam (waters), and they shall be dried up; for it is a aratz (land) of engraved pasayal (images), and they are halal (mad) over ayamah (idols).

Therefore the tzayay (wild) animals of the desert with the wolves shall yashab (dwell) there, and the ostriches shall yashab (dwell) therein: and it shall be no more inhabited forever; neither shall it be lived in from dawar (generation) to dawar (generation).
As when Alahayam overthrew Sadam and Imarah and the Shakan cities of it, says Yahawah, so shall no ayash (man) yashab (dwell) there, neither shall any ban (son) of adam (man) live therein.
Behold, a im (people) bawaa (comes) from the tzapawan (north); and a gadawal (great) gaway (nation) and many malak (kings) shall be stirred up from the uttermost parts of the aratz (earth).

They lay chazaq (hold) on qashath (bow) and kayadawan (spear); they are Akazaray, and have no racham (mercy); their qawal (voice) roars like the yam (sea); and they ride on horses, everyone set in array, as a ayash (man) to the battle, against you, bath (daughter) of Babal.
The malak (king) of Babal has heard the news of them, and his yad (hands) wax rapah (feeble): tzarah (anguish) has taken chazaq (hold) of him, pains as of a yalad (woman) in labor.

Behold, the enemy shall ilah (come) up like a aray (lion) from the pride of the Yaradan against the ayathan (strong) Nawah: for I will ragai (suddenly) make them run away from it; and whoever is chosen, him will I paqad (appoint) over it: for who is like me? and who will appoint me a time? and who is the raih (shepherd) who can imad (stand) panayam (before) me?

Therefore hear the itzah (counsel) of Yahawah, that he has taken against Babal; and his machashabah (purposes), that he has purposed against the aratz (land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans): Surely they shall drag them away, even the Tzaiyar tzaan (ones) of the flock; surely he shall make their Nawah shamam (desolate) over them.
At the qawal (noise) of the taking of Babal the aratz (earth) trembles, and the cry is heard among the gawayam (nations).
Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Behold, I will raise up against Babal, and against those who yashab (dwell) in Lebkamai, a destroying rawach (wind).
I will shalach (send) to Babal strangers, who shall winnow her; and they shall empty her aratz (land): for in the yawam (day) of rai (trouble) they shall be against her around.

Against him who bends let the archer bend his qashath (bow), and against him who ilah (lifts) himself up in his coat of mail: and don't spare her young men; charam (utterly) destroy all her tzabaa (army).
They shall napal (fall) down Chalal in the aratz (land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), and thrust through in her streets.

For Yasharaal (Israel) is not Alaman, nor Yahawadah (Judah), of his Alahayam, of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies); though their aratz (land) is malaa (full) of guilt against the qadawash (holy) One of Yasharaal (Israel).

Flee out of the midst of Babal, and malat (save) every ayash (man) his napash (life); don't be damam (cut) off in her iwan (iniquity): for it is the ith (time) of yahawah (yahweh's) vengeance; he will shalam (render) to her a recompense.

Babal has been a golden cup in yahawah (yahweh's) yad (hand), who made all the aratz (earth) Shakar: the gawayam (nations) have drunk of her yayan (wine); therefore the gawayam (nations) are halal (mad).
Babal is suddenly fallen and destroyed: wail for her; take balm for her pain, if so be she may be healed.

We would have healed Babal, but she is not healed: forsake her, and let us yalak (go) everyone into his own aratz (country); for her mashapat (judgment) reaches to shamayam (heaven), and is lifted up even to the shachaq (skies).
Yahawah has brought yatzaa (forth) our tzadaqah (righteousness): bawaa (come), and let us declare in Tzayawan the maishah (work) of Yahawah our Alahayam.

Barar sharp the chatz (arrows); hold firm the shalat (shields): Yahawah has stirred up the rawach (spirit) of the malak (kings) of the Maday; because his purpose is against Babal, to shachath (destroy) it: for it is the vengeance of Yahawah, the vengeance of his hayakal (temple).

nashaa (set) up a nas (standard) against the walls of Babal, make the watch chazaq (strong), kawan (set) the watchmen, kawan (prepare) the ambushes; for Yahawah has both purposed and done that which he spoke concerning the yashab (inhabitants) of Babal.
You who shakan (dwell) on many mayam (waters), abundant in treasures, your end has bawaa (come), the amah (measure) of your covetousness.
Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) has sworn by himself, saying, Surely I will malaa (fill) you with men, as with the canker worm; and they shall lift up a shout against you.
He has made the aratz (earth) by his kach (power), he has established the world by his chakamah (wisdom), and by his thabawan (understanding) has he stretched out the shamayam (heavens):

when he nathan (utters) his qawal (voice), there is a tumult of mayam (waters) in the shamayam (heavens), and he causes the vapors to ilah (ascend) from the ends of the aratz (earth); he ishah (makes) lightning for the rain, and yatzaa (brings) forth the rawach (wind) out of his treasuries.

Every adam (man) has become bair (brutish) without daith (knowledge). Every goldsmith is disappointed by his pasal (image); for his molten nasak (image) is falsehood, and there is no rawach (breath) in them.
They are vanity, a maishah (work) of delusion: in the ith (time) of their visitation they shall abad (perish).
The chalaq (portion) of Yaiqab is not like these; for he is the former of all things; and is the shabat (tribe) of his nachalah (inheritance): Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) is his sham (name).
You are my battle axe and weapons of war: and with you will I break in pieces the gawayam (nations); and with you will I shachath (destroy) mamalakah (kingdoms);
and with you will I break in pieces the horse and his rider;

and with you will I break in pieces the chariot and him who rides therein; and with you will I break in pieces ayash (man) and ashah (woman); and with you will I break in pieces the zaqan (old) man and the youth; and with you will I break in pieces the young bachawar (man) and the virgin;

and with you will I break in pieces the raih (shepherd) and his flock; and with you will I break in pieces the farmer and his tzamad (yoke); and with you will I break in pieces governors and deputies.
I will shalam (render) to Babal and to all the yashab (inhabitants) of Kashaday all their rai (evil) that they have done in Tzayawan in your iyan (sight), says Yahawah.

Behold, I am against you, mashachayath (destroying) har (mountain), says Yahawah, which shachath (destroys) all the aratz (earth); and I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on you, and roll you down from the salai (rocks), and will nathan (make) you a burnt har (mountain).
They shall not take of you a aban (stone) for a corner, nor a aban (stone) for foundations; but you shall be desolate for ever, says Yahawah.

nashaa (set) up a nas (standard) in the aratz (land), blow the trumpet among the gawayam (nations), qadash (prepare) the gawayam (nations) against her, call together against her the mamalakah (kingdoms) of Ararat, Manay, and Ashakanaz: paqad (appoint) a marshal against her; cause the horses to ilah (come) up as the Samar canker worm.
qadash (prepare) against her the gawayam (nations), the malak (kings) of the Maday, its governors, and all its deputies, and all the aratz (land) of their mamashalah (dominion).

The aratz (land) trembles and is in chawal (pain); for the machashabah (purposes) of Yahawah against Babal do qawam (stand), to shawam (make) the aratz (land) of Babal a desolation, without yashab (inhabitant).

The gabawar (mighty) men of Babal have forborne to fight, they yashab (remain) in their strongholds; their might has failed; they are become as women: her mashakan (dwelling) places are set on yatzath (fire); her bars are shabar (broken).
rawatz (one) runner will run to qaraah (meet) another, and one nagad (messenger) to qaraah (meet) another, to show the malak (king) of Babal that his Iyar is taken on every quarter:
and the passages are seized, and the reeds they have burned with ash (fire), and the men of war are frightened.

For thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel): The bath (daughter) of Babal is like a threshing floor at the ith (time) when it is trodden; yet a Mait while, and the ith (time) of harvest shall bawaa (come) for her.

Nabawakadanaatzar the malak (king) of Babal has devoured me, he has crushed me, he has made me an empty vessel, he has, like a thanayan (monster), swallowed me up, he has filled his maw Idan my delicacies; he has cast me out.

The violence done to me and to my flesh be on Babal, shall the yashab (inhabitant) of Tzayawan amar (say); and, My dam (blood) be on the yashab (inhabitants) of Kashaday, shall Yarawashalam amar (say).
Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah: Behold, I will rayab (plead) your rayab (cause), and take vengeance for you; and I will charab (dry) up her yam (sea), and make her fountain yabash (dry).
Babal shall become heaps, a dwelling place for jackals, an astonishment, and a hissing, without yashab (inhabitant).
They shall roar together like young kapayar (lions); they shall growl as aray (lions)' cubs.
When they are heated, I will shayath (make) their feast, and I will Shakar them drunken, that they may rejoice, and sleep a perpetual shanah (sleep), and not qawatz (wake), says Yahawah.
I will yarad (bring) them down like lambs to the slaughter, like ayal (rams) with male goats.
How is Shashak taken! and the thahalah (praise) of the whole aratz (earth) seized! how is Babal become a desolation among the gawayam (nations)!
The yam (sea) has ilah (come) up on Babal; she is covered with the multitude of its waves.

Her Iyar are become a desolation, a tzayah (dry) aratz (land), and a irabah (desert), a aratz (land) in which no ayash (man) yashab (dwells), neither does any ban (son) of adam (man) ibar (pass) thereby.

I will execute paqad (judgment) on Bal in Babal, and I will yatzaa (bring) forth out of his pah (mouth) that which he has swallowed up; and the gawayam (nations) shall not flow any more to him: yes, the wall of Babal shall napal (fall).
My im (people), go away from the midst of her, and malat (save) yourselves every ayash (man) from the charawan (fierce) ap (anger) of Yahawah.

Don't let your labab (heart) faint, neither yaraa (fear) for the news that shall be heard in the aratz (land); for news shall bawaa (come) one Shanah, and achar (after) that in another Shanah shall come news, and violence in the aratz (land), ruler against ruler.

Therefore, behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), that I will execute paqad (judgment) on the engraved pasayal (images) of Babal; and her whole aratz (land) shall be confounded; and all her Chalal shall napal (fall) in the midst of her.

Then the shamayam (heavens) and the aratz (earth), and all that is therein, shall sing for joy over Babal; for the shadad (destroyers) shall bawaa (come) to her from the tzapawan (north), says Yahawah.
As Babal has caused the Chalal of Yasharaal (Israel) to napal (fall), so at Babal shall napal (fall) the Chalal of all the aratz (land).
You who have escaped the charab (sword), halak (go), don't imad (stand) still; zakar (remember) Yahawah from Rachawaq, and let Yarawashalam ilah (come) into your labab (mind).

We are confounded, because we have heard reproach; kalamah (confusion) has covered our panayam (faces): for strangers have bawaa (come) into the maqadash (sanctuaries) of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house).
Therefore, behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come), says Yahawah, that I will execute paqad (judgment) on her engraved pasayal (images); and through all her aratz (land) the Chalal shall groan.
Though Babal should ilah (mount) up to the sky, and though she should batzar (fortify) the height of her iz (strength), yet from me shall shadad (destroyers) bawaa (come) to her, says Yahawah.
The qawal (sound) of a cry from Babal, and of gadawal (great) destruction from the aratz (land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans)!
For Yahawah lays Babal shadad (waste), and abad (destroys) out of her the gadawal (great) qawal (voice); and their waves roar like many mayam (waters); the noise of their qawal (voice) is uttered:

for the shadad (destroyer) has bawaa (come) on her, even on Babal, and her gabawar (mighty) men are taken, their qashath (bows) are broken in pieces; for Yahawah is a Al of recompenses, he will shalam (surely) shalam (requite).

I will Shakar drunk her shar (princes) and her chakam (wise) men, her governors and her deputies, and her gabawar (mighty) men; and they shall sleep a perpetual shanah (sleep), and not qawatz (wake) up, says the malak (king), whose sham (name) is Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): The Rachab walls of Babal shall be utterly overthrown, and her Gabah gates shall be burned with ash (fire); and the im (peoples) shall yagai (labor) for vanity, and the laam (nations) for the ash (fire); and they shall be Yaip.

The dabar (word) which Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet) tzawah (commanded) Sharayah the ban (son) of Narayah, the ban (son) Machasayah Mahseiah, when he went with Tzadaqayah the malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) to Babal in the rabayaiy (fourth) Shanah of his malak (reign). Now Sharayah was chief quartermaster.
Yaramayah wrote in a book all the rai (evil) that should bawaa (come) on Babal, even all these dabar (words) that are written concerning Babal.
Yaramayah said to Sharayah, When you bawaa (come) to Babal, then raah (see) that you qaraa (read) all these dabar (words),

and amar (say), Yahawah, you have spoken concerning this place, to karath (cut) it off, that none shall yashab (dwell) therein, neither adam (man) nor animal, but that it shall be desolate iwalam (forever).
It shall be, when you have made an kalah (end) of reading this book, that you shall qashar (bind) a aban (stone) to it, and cast it into the midst of the Parath:

and you shall amar (say), Thus shall Babal sink, and shall not qawam (rise) again panayam (because) of the rai (evil) that I will bawaa (bring) on her; and they shall be Yaip. Thus far are the dabar (words) of Yaramayah.

Tzadaqayah was isharayam (twenty) - one Shanah ban (old) when he began to malak (reign); and he reigned achad (eleven) Shanah in Yarawashalam: and his am (mother's) sham (name) was Chamawatal the bath (daughter) of Yaramayah of Labanah.
He did that which was rai (evil) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, according to all that Yahawayaqayam had done.
For through the ap (anger) of Yahawah it happened in Yarawashalam and Yahawadah (Judah), until he had cast them out from his panayam (presence). Tzadaqayah rebelled against the malak (king) of Babal.

It happened in the thashayaiy (ninth) Shanah of his malak (reign), in the ishayaray (tenth) chadash (month), in the tenth day of the chadash (month), that Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal came, he and all his chayal (army), against Yarawashalam, and encamped against it; and they built forts against it round about.
So the Iyar was Matzawar to the ishathay (eleventh) Shanah of malak (king) Tzadaqayah.
In the rabayaiy (fourth) chadash (month), in the ninth day of the chadash (month), the famine was severe in the Iyar, so that there was no lacham (bread) for the im (people) of the aratz (land).

Then a breach was made in the Iyar, and all the men of war fled, and went yatzaa (forth) out of the Iyar by layal (night) by the darak (way) of the gate between the chawamah (two) walls, which was by the malak (king's) Gan; (now the Kashaday (Chaldeans) were against the Iyar all around;) and they went toward the irabah (arabah).

But the chayal (army) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans) pursued achar (after) the malak (king), and overtook Tzadaqayah in the irabah (plains) of Yarayachaw; and all his chayal (army) was scattered from him.
Then they took the malak (king), and carried him up to the malak (king) of Babal to Rabalah in the aratz (land) of Chamath; and he gave mashapat (judgment) on him.
The malak (king) of Babal killed the ban (sons) of Tzadaqayah before his iyan (eyes): he killed also all the shar (princes) of Yahawadah (Judah) in Rabalah.

He put out the iyan (eyes) of Tzadaqayah; and the malak (king) of Babal bound him in fetters, and carried him to Babal, and nathan (put) him in bayath (prison) until the yawam (day) of his mawath (death).

Now in the chamayashay (fifth) chadash (month), in the tenth day of the chadash (month), which was the nineteenth Shanah of malak (king) Nabawakadanaatzar, malak (king) of Babal, came Nabawazaraadan the rab (captain) of the guard, who stood before the malak (king) of Babal, into Yarawashalam:
and he burned the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the malak (king's) bayath (house); and all the bayath (houses) of Yarawashalam, even every gadawal (great) bayath (house), burned he with ash (fire).
All the chayal (army) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans), who were with the rab (captain) of the guard, broke down all the walls of Yarawashalam all around.

Then Nabawazaraadan the rab (captain) of the guard carried away galah (captive) Dalah the poorest of the im (people), and the yathar (residue) of the im (people) who were shaar (left) in the Iyar, and those who napal (fell) away, who napal (fell) to the malak (king) of Babal, and the yathar (residue) of the multitude.
But Nabawazaraadan the rab (captain) of the guard shaar (left) Dalah the poorest of the aratz (land) to be vineyard keepers and farmers.

The Kashaday (Chaldeans) broke the pillars of brass that were in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and the bases and the bronze yam (sea) that were in the bayath (house) of Yahawah in pieces, and carried all the of their brass to Babal.
They also took away the pots, the shovels, the snuffers, the basins, the kap (spoons), and all the vessels of brass with which they ministered.

The rab (captain) of the guard took away the cups, the machathah (fire) pans, the basins, the pots, the lampstands, the kap (spoons), and the bowls; that which was of gold, in gold, and that which was of kasap (silver), in kasap (silver).

They took the shanayam (two) pillars, the one yam (sea), and the shanayam (twelve) bronze bulls that were under the bases, which malak (king) Shalamah had made for the bayath (house) of Yahawah. The brass of all these vessels was without weight.
As for the pillars, the height of the one pillar was eighteen amah (cubits); and a line of shanayam (twelve) amah (cubits) encircled it; and its thickness was arabai (four) fingers. It was hollow.

A capital of brass was on it; and the height of the one capital was chamash (five) amah (cubits), with network and pomegranates on the capital all around, all of brass: and the shanay (second) pillar also had like these, and pomegranates.
There were thashaiyam (ninety) - shash (six) pomegranates on the rawach (sides); all the pomegranates were one maah (hundred) on the network all around.
The rab (captain) of the guard took Sharayah the raash (chief) kahan (priest), and Tzapanayah the mashanah (second) kahan (priest), and the shalawash (three) keepers of the threshold:

and out of the Iyar he took an officer who was set over the men of war; and shabai (seven) men of those who saw the malak (king's) panayam (face), who were found in the Iyar; and the scribe of the shar (captain) of the tzabaa (army), who mustered the im (people) of the aratz (land); and shashayam (sixty) men of the im (people) of the aratz (land), who were found in the midst of the Iyar.
Nabawazaraadan the rab (captain) of the guard took them, and brought them to the malak (king) of Babal to Rabalah.
The malak (king) of Babal struck them, and put them to mawath (death) at Rabalah in the adamah (land) of Chamath. So Yahawadah (Judah) was carried away galah (captive) out of his aratz (land).
This is the im (people) whom Nabawakadanaatzar carried away galah (captive): in the seventh Shanah shalawash (three) alap (thousand) isharayam (twenty) - shalawash (three) Yahawaday (Jews);
in the eighteenth Shanah of Nabawakadanaatzar he carried away galah (captive) from Yarawashalam shamanah (eight) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - shanayam (two) napash (persons);

in the shalawash (three) and isharayam (twentieth) Shanah of Nabawakadanaatzar Nabawazaraadan the rab (captain) of the guard carried away galah (captive) of the Yahawaday (Jews) shabai (seven) maah (hundred) arabaiyam (forty) - chamash (five) napash (persons): all the napash (persons) were arabai (four) alap (thousand) and shash (six) maah (hundred).

It happened in the shabai (seven) and shalawashayam (thirtieth) Shanah of the captivity of Yahawayakayan malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), in the shanayam (twelfth) chadash (month), in the chamash (five) and isharayam (twentieth) day of the chadash (month), that awayalamaradak (evilmerodach) malak (king) of Babal, in the first Shanah of his malakawath (reign), lifted up the raash (head) of Yahawayakayan malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and brought him yatzaa (forth) out of bayath (prison);
and he spoke tawab (kindly) to him, and nathan (set) his kasaa (throne) above the kasaa (throne) of the malak (kings) who were with him in Babal,
and changed his prison bagad (garments). Jehoiachin ate lacham (bread) panayam (before) him continually all the yawam (days) of his chay (life):

and for his allowance, there was a continual allowance given him by the malak (king) of Babal, every yawam (day) a dabar (portion) until the yawam (day) of his mawath (death), all the yawam (days) of his chay (life).

How the Iyar yashab (sits) badad (solitary), that was rab (full) of im (people)! She has become as a alamanah (widow), who was rab (great) among the gawayam (nations)! She who was a sharah (princess) among the provinces has become tributary!

She weeps bitterly in the layal (night), and her tears are on her Lachay; among all her lovers she has none to nacham (comfort) her: All her rai (friends) have dealt bagad (treacherously) with her; they are become her ayab (enemies).

Yahawadah (Judah) is galah (gone) into captivity because of affliction, and because of great servitude; she yashab (dwells) among the gawayam (nations), she matzaa (finds) no manawach (rest): all her persecutors overtook her within the straits.

The darak (ways) of Tzayawan do Abal, because none bawaa (come) to the solemn mawaid (assembly); all her gates are shamam (desolate), her kahan (priests) do sigh: her virgins are afflicted, and she herself is in bitterness.

Her tzar (adversaries) are become the raash (head), her ayab (enemies) shalah (prosper); for Yahawah has afflicted her for the multitude of her pashai (transgressions): her young children are gone into Shabay panayam (before) the tzar (adversary).

From the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan all her hadar (majesty) is departed: her shar (princes) are become like harts that matzaa (find) no pasture, they are gone without kach (strength) panayam (before) the pursuer.

Yarawashalam zakar (remembers) in the yawam (days) of her affliction and of her miseries all her pleasant things that were from the yawam (days) of qadam (old): when her im (people) napal (fell) into the yad (hand) of the tzar (adversary), and no izar (one) helped her, The tzar (adversaries) saw her, they mocked at her desolations.

Yarawashalam has chataa (grievously) sinned; therefore she has become as an unclean thing; all who honored her despise her, because they have seen her irawah (nakedness): yes, she sighs, and shawab (turn back / repent) backward.

Her tamaah (filthiness) was in her skirts; she didn't zakar (remember) her acharayath (latter) end; therefore is she yarad (come) down wonderfully; she has no comforter: raah (see), Yahawah, my affliction; for the ayab (enemy) has magnified himself.

The tzar (adversary) has spread out his yad (hand) on all her pleasant things: for she has seen that the gawayam (nations) are entered into her maqadash (sanctuary), concerning whom you tzawah (commanded) that they should not bawaa (enter) into your qahal (assembly).

All her im (people) sigh, they seek lacham (bread); they have given their pleasant things for food to shawab (turn back / repent) the napash (soul): raah (see), Yahawah, and raah (see); for I am become abject.

Is it nothing to you, all you who ibar (pass) by? Look, and raah (see) if there is any sorrow like my sorrow, which is brought on me, With which Yahawah has afflicted me in the yawam (day) of his charawan (fierce) ap (anger).

From on high has he sent ash (fire) into my itzam (bones), and it radah (prevails) against them; He has spread a net for my feet, he has turned me back: He has made me shamam (desolate) and Dawah all the yawam (day).

The yoke of my pashai (transgressions) is bound by his yad (hand); They are knit together, they have ilah (come) up on my neck; he has made my kach (strength) to fail: The Adanay has delivered me into their yad (hands), against whom I am not yakal (able) to qawam (stand).

The Adanay has set at nothing all my abayar (mighty) men in the qarab (midst) of me; He has called a solemn mawaid (assembly) against me to shabar (crush) my young men: The Adanay has trodden as in a winepress the virgin bath (daughter) of Yahawadah (Judah).

For these things I weep; my iyan (eye), my iyan (eye) yarad (runs) down with mayam (water); Because the comforter who should shawab (turn back / repent) my napash (soul) is rachaq (far) from me: My children are shamam (desolate), because the ayab (enemy) has prevailed.

Tzayawan spreads forth her yad (hands); there is none to nacham (comfort) her; Yahawah has tzawah (commanded) concerning Yaiqab, that those who are around him should be his tzar (adversaries): Yarawashalam is among them as an nadah (unclean) thing.
Yahawah is tzadayaq (righteous); for I have rebelled against his commandment: Please hear all you im (peoples), and raah (see) my sorrow: My virgins and my young men are gone into Shabay.
I called for my lovers, but they deceived me: My kahan (priests) and my zaqan (elders) gave up the spirit in the Iyar, While they sought them food to shawab (turn back / repent) their napash (souls).

raah (see), Yahawah; for I am in tzarar (distress); my maih (heart) is troubled; My lab (heart) is turned qarab (within) me; for I have grievously rebelled: Abroad the charab (sword) shakal (bereaves), at bayath (home) there is as mawath (death).

They have heard that I sigh; there is none to nacham (comfort) me; All my ayab (enemies) have heard of my rai (trouble); they are glad that you have done it: You will bawaa (bring) the yawam (day) that you have proclaimed, and they shall be like me.
Let all their wickedness bawaa (come) panayam (before) you; Do to them, as you have done to me for all my pashai (transgressions): For my sighs are many, and my lab (heart) is Daway.

How has the Adanay covered the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan with a cloud in his ap (anger)! He has cast down from shamayam (heaven) to the aratz (earth) the thapaarah (beauty) of Yasharaal (Israel), And hasn't zakar (remembered) his footstool in the yawam (day) of his ap (anger).

The Adanay has swallowed up all the naah (habitations) of Yaiqab, and has not pitied: He has thrown down in his ibarah (wrath) the strongholds of the bath (daughter) of Yahawadah (Judah); He has brought them down to the aratz (ground); he has profaned the mamalakah (kingdom) and its shar (princes).

He has cut off in fierce ap (anger) all the qaran (horn) of Yasharaal (Israel); He has drawn back his right yamayan (hand) from panayam (before) the ayab (enemy): He has burned up Yaiqab like a lahabah (flaming) ash (fire), which akal (devours) all around.

He has bent his qashath (bow) like an ayab (enemy), he has stood with his right yamayan (hand) as an tzar (adversary), Has killed all that were pleasant to the iyan (eye): In the ahal (tent) of the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan he has poured out his chamah (wrath) like ash (fire).

The Adanay has become as an ayab (enemy), he has swallowed up Yasharaal (Israel); He has swallowed up all her palaces, he has destroyed his strongholds; He has multiplied in the bath (daughter) of Yahawadah (Judah) mourning and lamentation.

He has violently taken away his shak (tabernacle), as if it were of a Gan; he has destroyed his place of mawaid (assembly): Yahawah has caused solemn mawaid (assembly) and shabath (sabbath) to be forgotten in Tzayawan, Has despised in the indignation of his ap (anger) the malak (king) and the kahan (priest).

The Adanay has cast off his mazabach (altar), he has abhorred his maqadash (sanctuary); He has given up into the yad (hand) of the ayab (enemy) the walls of her palaces: They have made a qawal (noise) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah, as in the yawam (day) of a solemn mawaid (assembly).

Yahawah has purposed to shachath (destroy) the wall of the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan; He has stretched out the line, he has not withdrawn his yad (hand) from destroying; He has made the chayal (rampart) and wall to lament; they languish together.

Her gates are sunk into the aratz (ground); he has destroyed and shabar (broken) her bars: Her malak (king) and her shar (princes) are among the gawayam (nations) where the thawarah (law) is not; Yes, her nabayaa (prophets) matzaa (find) no vision from Yahawah.

The zaqan (elders) of the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan yashab (sit) on the aratz (ground), they damam (keep) silence; They have ilah (cast) up ipar (dust) on their raash (heads); they have clothed themselves with sackcloth: The virgins of Yarawashalam yarad (hang) down their raash (heads) to the aratz (ground).

My iyan (eyes) do kalah (fail) with tears, my maih (heart) is troubled; My liver is poured on the aratz (earth), because of the destruction of the bath (daughter) of my im (people), Because the young children and the infants swoon in the streets of the city.
They amar (tell) their am (mothers), Where is grain and yayan (wine)? When they swoon as the Chalal in the streets of the Iyar, When their napash (soul) is poured out into their am (mothers)' bosom.

What shall I iwad (testify) to you? mah (what) shall I liken to you, bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam? What shall I compare to you, that I may nacham (comfort) you, virgin bath (daughter) of Tzayawan? For your breach is gadawal (great) like the yam (sea): who can heal you?

Your nabayaa (prophets) have seen for you false and Thapal visions; They have not uncovered your iwan (iniquity), to shawab (turn back / repent) back your captivity, but have seen for you false oracles and causes of banishment.

All that ibar (pass) by clap their kap (hands) at you. They hiss and wag their raash (head) at the bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam, saying, Is this the Iyar that men called The kalayal (perfection) of beauty, The joy of the whole aratz (earth)?

All your ayab (enemies) have opened their pah (mouth) wide against you; They hiss and gnash the teeth; they amar (say), We have swallowed her up; ak (certainly) this is the yawam (day) that we looked for; we have found, we have seen it.

Yahawah has done that which he purposed; he has fulfilled his amarah (sayings) that he tzawah (commanded) in the yawam (days) of qadam (old); He has thrown down, and has not pitied: He has caused the ayab (enemy) to Shamach over you; he has exalted the qaran (horn) of your tzar (adversaries).

Their lab (heart) cried to the Adanay: wall of the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan, let tears yarad (run) down like a nachal (river) yawamam (day) and layal (night); nathan (give) yourself no respite; don't let the bath (apple) of your iyan (eye) damam (cease).

qawam (arise), cry out in the layal (night), at the raash (beginning) of the watches; Pour out your lab (heart) like mayam (water) before the panayam (face) of the Adanay: nashaa (lift) up your kap (hands) toward him for the napash (life) of your young children, that faint for hunger at the raash (head) of every street.

raah (see), Yahawah, and raah (see) to whom you have done thus! Shall the women akal (eat) their fruit, the children that are dandled in the hands? Shall the kahan (priest) and the nabayaa (prophet) be killed in the maqadash (sanctuary) of the Adanay?

The youth and the zaqan (old) man shakab (lie) on the aratz (ground) in the streets; My virgins and my young men are fallen by the charab (sword): You have killed them in the yawam (day) of your ap (anger); you have slaughtered, and not pitied.

You have called, as in the yawam (day) of a mawaid (solemn) assembly, my magawar (terrors) on every side; There was none that escaped or remained in the yawam (day) of yahawah (yahweh's) ap (anger): Those that I have dandled and brought up has my ayab (enemy) consumed.
I am the gabar (man) that has seen affliction by the shabat (rod) of his ibarah (wrath).
He has led me and caused me to walk in chashak (darkness), and not in awar (light).
Surely against me he shawab (turn back / repent) his yad (hand) again and again all the yawam (day).
My flesh and my skin has he made old; he has shabar (broken) my itzam (bones).
He has built against me, and surrounded me with gall and travail.
He has made me to dwell in dark places, as those that have been long mawath (dead).
He has walled me about, that I can't yatzaa (go) forth; he has made my chain kabad (heavy).
Yes, when I cry, and call for help, he shuts out my prayer.
He has walled up my darak (ways) with cut gazayath (stone); he has made my nathayab (paths) iwah (crooked).
He is to me as a bear lying in wait, as a aray (lion) in secret places.
He has turned sawar (aside) my darak (ways), and pulled me in pieces; he has made me shamam (desolate).
He has bent his qashath (bow), and natzab (set) me as a mark for the chatz (arrow).
He has caused the shafts of his quiver to bawaa (enter) into my kalayah (kidneys).
I am become a derision to all my im (people), and their song all the yawam (day).
He has filled me with bitterness, he has sated me with wormwood.
He has also broken my teeth with gravel chatzatz (stones); he has covered me with ashes.
You have removed my napash (soul) far off from shalawam (peace); I forgot tawab (prosperity).
I said, My natzach (strength) is perished, and my expectation from Yahawah.
zakar (remember) my affliction and my misery, the wormwood and the gall.
My napash (soul) still remembers them, and is bowed down within me.
This I shawab (turn back / repent) to my lab (mind); therefore have I hope.
It is because of yahawah (yahweh's) loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his racham (compassion) doesn't kalah (fail).
They are Chadash every baqar (morning); rab (great) is your amawanah (faithfulness).
Yahawah is my chalaq (portion), amar (says) my napash (soul); therefore will I hope in him.
Yahawah is tawab (good) to those who wait for him, to the napash (soul) that seeks him.
It is tawab (good) that a man should Yachayal and quietly wait for the thashawaih (salvation) of Yahawah.
It is tawab (good) for a gabar (man) that he nashaa (bear) the yoke in his youth.
Let him yashab (sit) badad (alone) and damam (keep) silence, because he has laid it on him.
Let him put his pah (mouth) in the ipar (dust), if so be there may be hope.
Let him nathan (give) his Lachay to him who strikes him; let him be filled full with reproach.
For the Adanay will not cast off iwalam (forever).
For though he cause grief, yet he will have racham (compassion) according to the multitude of his loving kindnesses.
For he does not afflict lab (willingly), nor grieve the children of men.
To dakaa (crush) under ragal (foot) all the prisoners of the aratz (earth),
To natah (turn) aside the mashapat (right) of a gabar (man) before the panayam (face) of the Most Ilayawan,
To iwath (subvert) a adam (man) in his rayab (cause), the Adanay doesn't raah (see).
Who is he who amar (says), and it comes to pass, when the Adanay doesn't tzawah (command) it?
Doesn't rai (evil) and tawab (good) yatzaa (come) out of the pah (mouth) of the Most Ilayawan?
Why does a chay (living) adam (man) complain, a gabar (man) for the punishment of his chataa (sins)?
Let us search and try our darak (ways), and shawab (turn back / repent) again to Yahawah.
Let us nashaa (lift) up our labab (heart) with our kap (hands) to Al in the shamayam (heavens).
We have transgressed and have rebelled; you have not pardoned.
You have covered with ap (anger) and pursued us; you have killed, you have not pitied.
You have covered yourself with a cloud, so that no prayer can ibar (pass) through.
You have made us an off-scouring and refuse in the qarab (midst) of the im (peoples).
All our ayab (enemies) have opened their pah (mouth) wide against us.
pachad (fear) and the pachath (pit) have come on us, devastation and destruction.
My iyan (eye) yarad (runs) down with palag (streams) of mayam (water), for the destruction of the bath (daughter) of my im (people).
My iyan (eye) pours down, and doesn't damah (cease), without any intermission,
Until Yahawah shaqap (look) down, and raah (see) from shamayam (heaven).
My iyan (eye) ilal (affects) my napash (soul), because of all the bath (daughters) of my Iyar.
They have chased me relentlessly like a bird, those who are my ayab (enemies) without cause.
They have tzamath (cut) off my chay (life) in the bawar (dungeon), and have yadah (cast) a aban (stone) on me.
mayam (waters) flowed over my raash (head); I said, I am cut off.
I called on your sham (name), Yahawah, Thachathay of the lowest bawar (dungeon).
You heard my qawal (voice); don't ilam (hide) your ear at my breathing, at my cry.
You drew qarab (near) in the yawam (day) that I called on you; you said, Don't be yaraa (afraid).
Adanay, you have pleaded the rayab (causes) of my napash (soul); you have redeemed my chay (life).
Yahawah, you have seen my wrong. shapat (judge) my cause.
You have seen all their vengeance and all their machashabah (devices) against me.
You have heard their reproach, Yahawah, and all their machashabah (devices) against me,
The shapah (lips) of those that rose up against me, and their device against me all the yawam (day).
You see their sitting down, and their rising up; I am their song.
You will shawab (turn back / repent) to them a recompense, Yahawah, according to the maishah (work) of their yad (hands).
You will nathan (give) them hardness of lab (heart), your thaalah (curse) to them.
You will pursue them in ap (anger), and destroy them from under the shamayam (heavens) of Yahawah.
How the gold has become dim! The most pure gold has changed! The aban (stones) of the qadash (sanctuary) are poured out at the raash (head) of every street.
The Yaqar ban (sons) of Tzayawan, comparable to fine gold, How are they esteemed as charash (earthen) pitchers, the maishah (work) of the yad (hands) of the potter!
Even the jackals chalatz (draw) out the breast, they nurse their young gawar (ones): The bath (daughter) of my im (people) has become Akazar, like the ostriches in the madabar (wilderness).
The lashawan (tongue) of the nursing child clings to the roof of his chak (mouth) for thirst: The young children shaal (ask) lacham (bread), and no parash (man) breaks it to them.
Those who fed delicately are shamam (desolate) in the streets: Those who were brought up in scarlet embrace dunghills.
For the iwan (iniquity) of the bath (daughter) of my im (people) is greater than the chataah (sin) of Sadam, That was overthrown as in a moment, and no yad (hands) were laid on her.
Her nobles were zakak (purer) than snow, they were whiter than milk; They were more ruddy in itzam (body) than rubies, their polishing was as of sapphire.
Their appearance is blacker than a coal; they are not known in the streets: Their skin clings to their itzam (bones); it is withered, it has become like a itz (stick).
Those who are Chalal with the charab (sword) are tawab (better) Chalal those who are killed with hunger; For these pine away, stricken through, for want of the fruits of the shadah (field).
The yad (hands) of the Rachamanay women have boiled their own children; They were their food in the destruction of the bath (daughter) of my im (people).
Yahawah has accomplished his chamah (wrath), he has poured out his charawan (fierce) ap (anger); He has kindled a ash (fire) in Tzayawan, which has devoured its yasawad (foundations).

The malak (kings) of the aratz (earth) didn't aman (believe), neither all the yashab (inhabitants) of the world, That the tzar (adversary) and the ayab (enemy) would bawaa (enter) into the gates of Yarawashalam.
It is because of the chataah (sins) of her nabayaa (prophets), and the iwan (iniquities) of her kahan (priests), That have shed the dam (blood) of the tzadayaq (just) in the qarab (midst) of her.
They wander as iwar (blind) men in the streets, they are polluted with dam (blood), So that men can't nagai (touch) their garments.

sawar (depart)! they cried to them, tamaa (unclean)! sawar (depart), sawar (depart), don't nagai (touch)! When they fled away and wandered, men said among the gawayam (nations), They shall not live here any more.
The panayam (anger) of Yahawah has scattered them; he will no more regard them: They didn't respect the panayam (persons) of the kahan (priests), they didn't favor the zaqan (elders).
Our iyan (eyes) still kalah (fail), looking in vain for our help: In our watching we have watched for a gaway (nation) that could not yashai (save).
They hunt our steps, so that we can't yalak (go) in our streets: Our end is qarab (near), our yawam (days) are fulfilled; for our end has bawaa (come).
Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles of the sky: They chased us on the har (mountains), they laid wait for us in the madabar (wilderness).

The rawach (breath) of our ap (nostrils), the mashayach (anointed) of Yahawah, was taken in their shachayath (pits); Of whom we said, Under his shadow we shall chayah (live) among the gawayam (nations).
Rejoice and be Shamach, bath (daughter) of Adam, that yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land) of Iwatz: The cup shall ibar (pass) through to you also; you shall be Shakar, and shall make yourself naked.

The punishment of your iwan (iniquity) is accomplished, bath (daughter) of Tzayawan; he will no more galah (carry) you away into captivity: He will paqad (visit) your iwan (iniquity), bath (daughter) of Adam; he will galah (uncover) your chataah (sins).
zakar (remember), Yahawah, what has come on us: raah (see), and raah (see) our reproach.
Our nachalah (inheritance) is turned to strangers, Our bayath (houses) to nakaray (aliens).
We are orphans and fatherless; Our am (mothers) are as alamanah (widows).
We have drunken our mayam (water) for kasap (money); Our itz (wood) is sold to us.
Our pursuers are on our necks: We are weary, and have no nawach (rest).
We have given the yad (hand) to the Matzarayam (Egyptians), To the Ashawar (Assyrians), to be satisfied with lacham (bread).
Our abawath (fathers) sinned, and are no more; We have borne their iwan (iniquities).
ibad (servants) mashal (rule) over us: There is none to paraq (deliver) us out of their yad (hand).
We bawaa (get) our lacham (bread) at the peril of our lives, panayam (because) of the charab (sword) of the madabar (wilderness).
Our skin is black like an oven, panayam (because) of the burning heat of famine.
They ravished the women in Tzayawan, The virgins in the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah).
shar (princes) were hanged up by their yad (hand): The panayam (faces) of zaqan (elders) were not honored.
The young men bare the mill; The children stumbled under the itz (wood).
The zaqan (elders) have ceased from the gate, The young men from their music.
The joy of our lab (heart) is ceased; Our dance is turned into mourning.
The itarah (crown) is fallen from our raash (head): Woe to us! for we have sinned.
For this our lab (heart) is Dawah; For these things our iyan (eyes) are chashak (dim);
For the har (mountain) of Tzayawan, which is shamam (desolate): The foxes halak (walk) on it.
You, Yahawah, yashab (remain) iwalam (forever); Your kasaa (throne) is from dawar (generation) to dawar (generation).
Why do you forget us forever, And forsake us so arak (long) yawam (time)?
shawab (turn back / repent) us to yourself, Yahawah, and we shall be turned. Renew our yawam (days) as of qadam (old).
But you have utterly rejected us; You are very qatzap (angry) against us.

Now it happened in the shalawashayam (thirtieth) Shanah, in the rabayaiy (fourth) month, in the chamash (fifth) of the chadash (month), as I was among the captives by the nahar (river) Kabar, that the shamayam (heavens) were opened, and I saw visions of Alahayam.
In the chamash (fifth) of the chadash (month), which was the chamayashay (fifth) Shanah of malak (king) Yawayakayan captivity,

the dabar (word) of Yahawah came expressly to Yachazaqaal the kahan (priest), the ban (son) of Bawazay, in the aratz (land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans) by the nahar (river) Kabar; and the yad (hand) of Yahawah was there on him.

I looked, and behold, a stormy rawach (wind) came out of the tzapawan (north), a gadawal (great) cloud, with flashing lightning, and a nagah (brightness) around it, and out of its midst as it were glowing metal, out of the midst of the ash (fire).
Out of its midst came the damawath (likeness) of arabai (four) chay (living) creatures. This was their appearance: they had the damawath (likeness) of a adam (man).
Everyone had arabai (four) panayam (faces), and achad (each) one of them had arabai (four) wings.
Their feet were yashar (straight) feet; and the kap (sole) of their feet was like the kap (sole) of a calf's ragal (foot); and they sparkled like Qalal brass.
They had the yad (hands) of a adam (man) under their wings on their arabai (four) rabai (sides); and the arabai (four) of them had their panayam (faces) and their wings thus:
their wings were joined one to achawath (another); they didn't sabab (turn) when they went; ayash (each) one went ibar (straight) forward.

As for the damawath (likeness) of their panayam (faces), they had the panayam (face) of a adam (man); and the arabai (four) of them had the panayam (face) of a aray (lion) on the yamayan (right) side; and the arabai (four) of them had the panayam (face) of an ox on the shamaawal (left) side; the arabai (four) of them also had the panayam (face) of an eagle.
Such were their panayam (faces). Their wings were spread out above. shanayam (two) wings of ayash (each) one touched ayash (another), and shanayam (two) covered their bodies.
ayash (each) one went ibar (straight) forward: where the rawach (spirit) was to yalak (go), they went; they didn't sabab (turn) when they went.

As for the damawath (likeness) of the chay (living) creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of ash (fire), like the appearance of torches: the fire went up and down among the chay (living) creatures; and the ash (fire) was nagah (bright), and out of the ash (fire) went yatzaa (forth) lightning.
The chay (living) creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning.
