Now as I saw the chay (living) creatures, behold, one wheel on the aratz (earth) beside the chay (living) creatures, for each of the arabai (four) panayam (faces) of it.

The appearance of the wheels and their maishah (work) was like a beryl: and the arabai (four) of them had one damawath (likeness); and their appearance and their maishah (work) was as it were a wheel within a wheel.
When they went, they went in their arabai (four) directions: they didn't sabab (turn) when they went.
As for their rims, they were high and yaraah (dreadful); and the arabai (four) of them had their rims Malaa of iyan (eyes) all around.
When the chay (living) creatures went, the wheels went beside them; and when the chay (living) creatures were lifted up from the aratz (earth), the wheels were lifted up.

Wherever the rawach (spirit) was to yalak (go), they went; there was the rawach (spirit) to yalak (go): and the wheels were lifted up beside them; for the rawach (spirit) of the chay (living) creature was in the wheels.

When those went, these went; and when those stood, these stood; and when those were lifted up from the aratz (earth), the wheels were lifted up beside them: for the rawach (spirit) of the chay (living) creature was in the wheels.
Over the raash (head) of the chay (living) creature there was the damawath (likeness) of an expanse, like the awesome crystal to look on, stretched natah (forth) over their raash (heads) above.

Under the expanse were their wings yashar (straight), the one toward the other: ayash (each) one had shanayam (two) which covered on this side, and ayash (every) one had shanayam (two) which covered on that side, their bodies.

When they went, I heard the qawal (noise) of their wings like the qawal (noise) of rab (great) mayam (waters), like the qawal (voice) of the Shaday, a qawal (noise) of tumult like the qawal (noise) of an machanah (army): when they stood, they let down their wings.
There was a qawal (voice) above the expanse that was over their raash (heads): when they stood, they let down their wings.

Above the expanse that was over their raash (heads) was the damawath (likeness) of a kasaa (throne), as the appearance of a sapphire aban (stone); and on the damawath (likeness) of the kasaa (throne) was a damawath (likeness) as the appearance of a adam (man) on it above.

I saw as it were glowing metal, as the appearance of ash (fire) bayath (within) it all around, from the appearance of his waist and upward; and from the appearance of his waist and downward I saw as it were the appearance of ash (fire), and there was nagah (brightness) around him.

As the appearance of the rainbow that is in the cloud in the yawam (day) of rain, so was the appearance of the nagah (brightness) all around. This was the appearance of the damawath (likeness) of the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah. When I saw it, I napal (fell) on my panayam (face), and I heard a qawal (voice) of one that spoke.
He said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), imad (stand) on your feet, and I will dabar (speak) with you.
The rawach (spirit) entered into me when he spoke to me, and imad (set) me on my feet; and I heard him who spoke to me.

He said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), I shalach (send) you to the children of Yasharaal (Israel), to a gawayam (nation) of rebels who have rebelled against me. They and their abawath (fathers) have transgressed against me even to this very yawam (day).
The children are Qashah and chazaq (stiff-hearted): I am sending you to them; and you shall amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah.
They, whether they will hear, or whether they will chadal (forbear), (for they are a rebellious bayath (house)), yet shall yadai (know) that there has been a nabayaa (prophet) among them.

You, ban (son) of adam (man), don't be yaraa (afraid) of them, neither be yaraa (afraid) of their dabar (words), though briers and thorns are with you, and you do yashab (dwell) among scorpions: don't be yaraa (afraid) of their dabar (words), nor be dismayed at their panayam (looks), though they are a rebellious bayath (house).
You shall dabar (speak) my dabar (words) to them, whether they will hear, or whether they will chadal (forbear); for they are most rebellious.
But you, ban (son) of adam (man), hear what I dabar (tell) you; don't be rebellious like that rebellious bayath (house): open your pah (mouth), and akal (eat) that which I nathan (give) you.
When I looked, behold, a yad (hand) was shalach (put) forth to me; and, behold, a scroll of a book was therein;
He spread it panayam (before) me: and it was written within and without; and there were written therein lamentations, and mourning, and woe.
He said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), akal (eat) that which you matzaa (find). akal (eat) this scroll, and yalak (go), dabar (speak) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).
So I opened my pah (mouth), and he caused me to akal (eat) the scroll.

He said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), cause your belly to akal (eat), and malaa (fill) your maih (bowels) with this scroll that I nathan (give) you. Then I ate it; and it was as Mathawaq as honey in my pah (mouth).
He said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), yalak (go) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), and dabar (speak) my dabar (words) to them.
For you are not sent to a im (people) of a Imaq shapah (speech) and of a Kabad lashawan (language), but to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel);
not to many im (peoples) of a Imaq shapah (speech) and of a Kabad lashawan (language), whose dabar (words) you can not understand. Surely, if I sent you to them, they would listen to you.
But the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) will not listen to you; for they will not listen to me: for all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) are obstinate and Qashah.
Behold, I have made your panayam (face) hard against their panayam (faces), and your forehead hard against their foreheads.
As an adamant chazaq (harder) than tzar (flint) have I made your forehead: don't be yaraa (afraid) of them, neither be dismayed at their panayam (looks), though they are a rebellious bayath (house).
Moreover he said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), all my dabar (words) that I shall dabar (speak) to you receive in your labab (heart), and hear with your ears.

yalak (go) to them of the captivity, to the children of your im (people), and dabar (speak) to them, and amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah; whether they will hear, or whether they will chadal (forbear).
Then the rawach (spirit) lifted me up, and I heard achar (behind) me the qawal (voice) of a gadawal (great) rushing, saying, Blessed be the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah from his place.

I heard the qawal (noise) of the wings of the chay (living) creatures as they touched one achawath (another), and the qawal (noise) of the wheels beside them, even the qawal (noise) of a gadawal (great) rushing.
So the rawach (spirit) lifted me up, and took me away; and I went Mar bitterness, in the chamah (heat) of my rawach (spirit); and the yad (hand) of Yahawah was chazaq (strong) on me.
Then I came to them of the captivity at Thalaabayab Aviv, that lived by the nahar (river) Kabar, and to where they lived; and I sat there overwhelmed among them shabai (seven) yawam (days).
It happened at the end of shabai (seven) yawam (days), that the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), I have made you a watchman to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel): therefore hear the dabar (word) from my pah (mouth), and give them warning from me.

When I amar (tell) the rashai (wicked), You shall mawath (surely) mawath (die); and you give him no warning, nor dabar (speak) to warn the rashai (wicked) from his rashai (wicked) darak (way), to chayah (save) his life; the same rashai (wicked) mawath (man) shall die in his iwan (iniquity); but his dam (blood) will I require at your yad (hand).

Yet if you warn the rashai (wicked), and he doesn't shawab (turn back / repent) from his rashai (wickedness), nor from his rashai (wicked) darak (way), he shall mawath (die) in his iwan (iniquity); but you have delivered your napash (soul).

Again, when a tzadayaq (righteous) man does shawab (turn back / repent) from his tzadaq (righteousness), and ishah (commit) iwal (iniquity), and I nathan (lay) a stumbling block panayam (before) him, he shall mawath (die): because you have not given him warning, he shall mawath (die) in his chataah (sin), and his tzadaqah (righteous) deeds which he has done shall not be zakar (remembered); but his dam (blood) will I require at your yad (hand).

Nevertheless if you warn the tzadayaq (righteous) man, that the tzadayaq (righteous) not chataa (sin), and he does not chataa (sin), he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live), because he took warning; and you have delivered your napash (soul).
The yad (hand) of Yahawah was there on me; and he said to me, qawam (arise), yatzaa (go) forth into the Baqaih, and I will there dabar (talk) with you.

Then I qawam (arose), and went yatzaa (forth) into the Baqaih: and behold, the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah stood there, as the kabawad (glory) which I saw by the nahar (river) Kabar; and I napal (fell) on my panayam (face).
Then the rawach (spirit) entered into me, and imad (set) me on my feet; and he spoke with me, and said to me, bawaa (go), shut yourself inside your bayath (house).
But you, ban (son) of adam (man), behold, they shall nathan (lay) bands on you, and shall bind you with them, and you shall not yatzaa (go) out among them:
and I will make your lashawan (tongue) stick to the roof of your chak (mouth), that you shall be mute, and shall not be to them a reprover; for they are a rebellious bayath (house).

But when I dabar (speak) with you, I will pathach (open) your pah (mouth), and you shall amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: He who hears, let him hear; and he who chadal (forbears), let him chadal (forbear): for they are a rebellious bayath (house).
You also, ban (son) of adam (man), take a tile, and nathan (lay) it panayam (before) yourself, and portray on it a Iyar, even Yarawashalam:

and nathan (lay) Matzawar against it, and banah (build) forts against it, and cast up a mound against it; nathan (set) machanah (camps) also against it, and plant battering rams against it all around.

Take for yourself an barazal (iron) pan, and nathan (set) it for a wall of barazal (iron) between you and the Iyar: and kawan (set) your panayam (face) toward it, and it shall be Matzawar, and you shall tzawar (lay) siege against it. This shall be a awath (sign) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Moreover shakab (lie) on your Shamaalay side, and shawam (lay) the iwan (iniquity) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) on it; according to the number of the yawam (days) that you shall shakab (lie) on it, you shall nashaa (bear) their iwan (iniquity).

For I have appointed the Shanah of their iwan (iniquity) to be to you a number of yawam (days), even shalawash (three) maah (hundred) thashaiyam (ninety) yawam (days): so you shall nashaa (bear) the iwan (iniquity) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Again, when you have accomplished these, you shall shakab (lie) on your Yamanay side, and shall nashaa (bear) the iwan (iniquity) of the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah): arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days), each yawam (day) for a Shanah, have I appointed it to you.
You shall kawan (set) your panayam (face) toward the Matzawar of Yarawashalam, with your zarawai (arm) uncovered; and you shall nabaa (prophesy) against it.
Behold, I nathan (lay) bands on you, and you shall not hapak (turn) you from tzad (one) side to the other, until you have accomplished the yawam (days) of your Matzawar.

Take for yourself also wheat, and barley, and beans, and lentils, and millet, and spelt, and nathan (put) them in one vessel, and ishah (make) lacham (bread) of it; according to the number of the yawam (days) that you shall shakab (lie) on your side, even shalawash (three) maah (hundred) thashaiyam (ninety) yawam (days), you shall akal (eat) of it.
Your food which you shall akal (eat) shall be by weight, isharayam (twenty) shekels a yawam (day): from ith (time) to ith (time) you shall akal (eat) it.
You shall drink mayam (water) by measure, the shashay (sixth) part of a hin: from ith (time) to ith (time) you shall drink.
You shall akal (eat) it as barley cakes, and you shall bake it in their iyan (sight) with dung that comes out of adam (man).
Yahawah said, Even thus shall the children of Yasharaal (Israel) akal (eat) their lacham (bread) tamaa (unclean), among the gawayam (nations) where I will drive them.

Then I said, Ah Adanay Yahawah! behold, my napash (soul) has not been polluted; for from my youth up even until now have I not eaten of that which dies of nabalah (itself), or is torn of animals; neither came there pagawal (abominable) flesh into my pah (mouth).
Then he said to me, raah (see), I have given you cow's dung for adam (man's) dung, and you shall ishah (prepare) your lacham (bread) thereon.

Moreover he said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), behold, I will shabar (break) the matah (staff) of lacham (bread) in Yarawashalam: and they shall akal (eat) lacham (bread) by weight, and with fearfulness; and they shall drink mayam (water) by measure, and in shamamawan (dismay):
that they may want lacham (bread) and mayam (water), and be dismayed one with ach (another), and pine away in their iwan (iniquity).

You, ban (son) of adam (man), take a Chad charab (sword); You shall take it as a barber's razor to you, and shall ibar (cause) it to pass on your raash (head) and on your beard: then take balances to weigh, and divide the hair.

A shalayashay (third) part you shall bair (burn) in the awar (fire) in the midst of the Iyar, when the yawam (days) of the Matzawar are fulfilled; and you shall take a shalayashay (third) part, and strike with the charab (sword) around it; and a shalayashay (third) part you shall scatter to the rawach (wind), and I will draw out a charab (sword) achar (after) them.
You shall take of it a Mait in number, and tzawar (bind) them in your skirts.

Of these again you shall take, and cast them into the midst of the ash (fire), and sharap (burn) them in the ash (fire); from it shall a ash (fire) yatzaa (come) forth into all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: This is Yarawashalam; I have shawam (set) her in the midst of the gawayam (nations), and aratz (countries) are around her.

She has rebelled against my mashapat (ordinances) in doing rashaih (wickedness) more than the gawayam (nations), and against my chaqah (statutes) more than the aratz (countries) that are around her; for they have rejected my mashapat (ordinances), and as for my chaqah (statutes), they have not walked in them.

Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you are turbulent more than the gawayam (nations) that are around you, and have not walked in my chaqah (statutes), neither have kept my mashapat (ordinances), neither have done after the mashapat (ordinances) of the gawayam (nations) that are around you;
therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I, even I, am against you; and I will ishah (execute) mashapat (judgments) in the midst of you in the iyan (sight) of the gawayam (nations).
I will do in you that which I have not done, and whereunto I will not do any more the like, because of all your thawaibah (abominations).

Therefore the abawath (fathers) shall akal (eat) the ban (sons) in the midst of you, and the ban (sons) shall akal (eat) their abawath (fathers); and I will ishah (execute) shapat (judgments) on you; and the whole shaarayath (remnant) of you will I scatter to all the rawach (winds).

Therefore, as I chay (live), says the Adanay Yahawah, surely, because you have defiled my maqadash (sanctuary) with all your shaqawatz (detestable) things, and with all your thawaibah (abominations), therefore will I also diminish you; neither shall my iyan (eye) spare, and I also will have no pity.

A shalayashay (third) part of you shall mawath (die) with the dabar (pestilence), and with famine shall they be consumed in the midst of you; and a shalayashay (third) part shall napal (fall) by the charab (sword) around you; and a shalayashay (third) part I will scatter to all the rawach (winds), and will draw out a charab (sword) achar (after) them.

Thus shall my ap (anger) be accomplished, and I will cause my chamah (wrath) toward them to nawach (rest), and I shall be comforted; and they shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have spoken in my zeal, when I have accomplished my chamah (wrath) on them.
Moreover I will nathan (make) you a desolation and a reproach among the gawayam (nations) that are around you, in the iyan (sight) of all that ibar (pass) by.

So it shall be a reproach and a taunt, an instruction and an astonishment, to the gawayam (nations) that are around you, when I shall ishah (execute) shapat (judgments) on you in ap (anger) and in chamah (wrath), and in chamah (wrathful) rebukes; (I, Yahawah, have spoken it;)

when I shall shalach (send) on them the rai (evil) chatz (arrows) of famine, that are for mashachayath (destruction), which I will shalach (send) to shachath (destroy) you: and I will increase the famine on you, and will shabar (break) your matah (staff) of lacham (bread);

and I will shalach (send) on you famine and rai (evil) animals, and they shall shakal (bereave) you; and dabar (pestilence) and dam (blood) shall ibar (pass) through you; and I will bawaa (bring) the charab (sword) on you: I, Yahawah, have spoken it.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (set) your panayam (face) toward the har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel), and nabaa (prophesy) to them,

and amar (say), You har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel), hear the dabar (word) of the Adanay Yahawah: Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah to the har (mountains) and to the Gabaih, to the watercourses and to the Gayaa: Behold, I, even I, will bawaa (bring) a charab (sword) on you, and I will abad (destroy) your bamah (high) places.
Your mazabach (altars) shall become shamam (desolate), and your incense mazabach (altars) shall be shabar (broken); and I will napal (cast) down your Chalal men panayam (before) your idols.
I will nathan (lay) the pagar (dead) bodies of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) panayam (before) their idols; and I will scatter your itzam (bones) around your mazabach (altars).

In all your mawashab (dwelling) places the Iyar shall be laid charab (waste), and the bamah (high) places shall be desolate; that your mazabach (altars) may be laid charab (waste) and asham (made) desolate, and your idols may be shabar (broken) and shabath (cease), and your incense altars may be cut down, and your maishah (works) may be abolished.
The Chalal shall napal (fall) in the midst of you, and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Yet will I yathar (leave) a remnant, in that you shall have some that escape the charab (sword) among the gawayam (nations), when you shall be scattered through the aratz (countries).

Those of you that escape shall zakar (remember) me among the gawayam (nations) where they shall be carried captive, how that I have been shabar (broken) with their lewd lab (heart), which has sawar (departed) from me, and with their iyan (eyes), which play the prostitute achar (after) their idols: and they shall loathe panayam (themselves) in their own sight for the rai (evils) which they have committed in all their thawaibah (abominations).
They shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah: I have not said in vain that I would do this rai (evil) to them.

Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Strike with your kap (hand), and stamp with your ragal (foot), and amar (say), Alas! because of all the rai (evil) thawaibah (abominations) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); for they shall napal (fall) by the charab (sword), by the famine, and by the dabar (pestilence).

He who is Rachawaq off shall mawath (die) of the dabar (pestilence); and he who is qarawab (near) shall napal (fall) by the charab (sword); and he who shaar (remains) and is besieged shall mawath (die) by the famine: thus will I kalah (accomplish) my chamah (wrath) on them.

You shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when their Chalal men shall be among their idols around their mazabach (altars), on every high Gabaih, on all the raash (tops) of the har (mountains), and under every Rainan itz (tree), and under every Ibath oak, the places where they offered pleasant aroma to all their idols.

I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on them, and nathan (make) the aratz (land) desolate and waste, from the madabar (wilderness) Dabalah Diblah, throughout all their habitations: and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
You, ban (son) of adam (man), thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah to the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), An end: the end has bawaa (come) on the arabai (four) corners of the aratz (land).
Now is the end on you, and I will shalach (send) my ap (anger) on you, and will shapat (judge) you according to your darak (ways); and I will nathan (bring) on you all your thawaibah (abominations).

My iyan (eye) shall not spare you, neither will I have pity; but I will nathan (bring) your darak (ways) on you, and your thawaibah (abominations) shall be in the midst of you: and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: An rai (evil), an only rai (evil); behold, it bawaa (comes).
An end has bawaa (come), the end has bawaa (come); it qawatz (awakes) bawaa (against) you; behold, it comes.

Your doom has bawaa (come) to you, yashab (inhabitant) of the aratz (land): the ith (time) has bawaa (come), the yawam (day) is qarawab (near), a mahawamah (day) of tumult, and not of joyful shouting, on the har (mountains).

Now will I qarawab (shortly) pour out my chamah (wrath) on you, and kalah (accomplish) my ap (anger) against you, and will shapat (judge) you according to your darak (ways); and I will nathan (bring) on you all your thawaibah (abominations).

My iyan (eye) shall not spare, neither will I have pity: I will nathan (bring) on you according to your darak (ways); and your thawaibah (abominations) shall be in the midst of you; and you shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, do strike.
Behold, the yawam (day), behold, it bawaa (comes): your doom is gone yatzaa (forth); the matah (rod) has blossomed, pride has budded.
Violence has risen up into a matah (rod) of rashai (wickedness). None of them shall remain, nor of their multitude, nor of their wealth. There shall be nothing of value among them.
The ith (time) has bawaa (come), the yawam (day) nagai (draws) near: don't let the qanah (buyer) Shamach, nor the seller mourn; for charawan (wrath) is on all its multitude.

For the seller shall not shawab (turn back / repent) to that which is sold, although they be yet chay (alive): for the vision is touching the whole multitude of it, none shall shawab (turn back / repent); neither shall any chazaq (strengthen) himself in the iwan (iniquity) of his chay (life).
They have blown the trumpet, and have made all kawan (ready); but none goes to the battle; for my charawan (wrath) is on all its multitude.

The charab (sword) is outside, and the dabar (pestilence) and the famine bayath (within): he who is in the shadah (field) shall mawath (die) with the charab (sword): and he who is in the Iyar, famine and dabar (pestilence) shall akal (devour) him.
But those of those who escape shall escape, and shall be on the har (mountains) like doves of the Gayaa, all of them moaning, ayash (every) one in his iwan (iniquity).
All yad (hands) shall be rapah (feeble), and all knees shall be yalak (weak) as mayam (water).
They shall also clothe themselves with sackcloth, and horror shall cover them; and shame shall be on all panayam (faces), and baldness on all their raash (heads).

They shall cast their kasap (silver) in the streets, and their gold shall be as an nadah (unclean) thing; their kasap (silver) and their gold shall not be yakal (able) to natzal (deliver) them in the yawam (day) of the ibarah (wrath) of Yahawah: they shall not satisfy their napash (souls), neither malaa (fill) their maih (bowels); because it has been the stumbling block of their iwan (iniquity).

As for the beauty of his iday (ornament), he shawam (set) it in majesty; but they made the tzalam (images) of their thawaibah (abominations) and their shaqawatz (detestable) things therein: therefore have I made it to them as an nadah (unclean) thing.
I will nathan (give) it into the yad (hands) of the strangers for a prey, and to the rashai (wicked) of the aratz (earth) for a spoil; and they shall chalal (profane) it.
My panayam (face) will I sabab (turn) also from them, and they shall chalal (profane) my secret place; and robbers shall bawaa (enter) into it, and chalal (profane) it.
ishah (make) the chain; for the aratz (land) is malaa (full) of bloody mashapat (crimes), and the Iyar is malaa (full) of violence.

Therefore I will bawaa (bring) the rai (worst) of the gawayam (nations), and they shall yarash (possess) their bayath (houses): I will also make the pride of the iz (strong) to shabath (cease); and their qadash (holy) places shall be profaned.
Destruction bawaa (comes); and they shall seek shalawam (peace), and there shall be none.

Mischief shall bawaa (come) on mischief, and rumor shall be on rumor; and they shall seek a vision of the nabayaa (prophet); but the thawarah (law) shall abad (perish) from the kahan (priest), and itzah (counsel) from the zaqan (elders).

The malak (king) shall mourn, and the nashayaa (prince) shall be Labash with desolation, and the yad (hands) of the im (people) of the aratz (land) shall be troubled: I will do to them after their darak (way), and according to their own mashapat (judgments) will I shapat (judge) them; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

It happened in the shashay (sixth) Shanah, in the shashay (sixth) month, in the chamash (fifth) day of the chadash (month), as I sat in my bayath (house), and the zaqan (elders) of Yahawadah (Judah) sat panayam (before) me, that the yad (hand) of the Adanay Yahawah napal (fell) there on me.

Then I saw, and behold, a damawath (likeness) as the appearance of ash (fire); from the appearance of his waist and downward, ash (fire); and from his waist and upward, as the appearance of brightness, as it were glowing metal.

He shalach (put) forth the thabanayath (form) of a yad (hand), and took me by a lock of my raash (head); and the rawach (spirit) lifted me up between aratz (earth) and the sky, and brought me in the visions of Alahayam to Yarawashalam, to the door of the gate Panayamay the inner court that panah (looks) toward the tzapawan (north); where there was the mawashab (seat) of the samal (image) of jealousy, which qanah (provokes) to jealousy.
Behold, the kabawad (glory) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) was there, according to the appearance that I saw in the Baqaih.

Then he said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eyes) now the darak (way) toward the tzapawan (north). So I lifted up my iyan (eyes) the darak (way) toward the tzapawan (north), and see, northward of the gate of the mazabach (altar) this samal (image) of jealousy in the entry.

He said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), do you raah (see) what they do? even the gadawal (great) thawaibah (abominations) that the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) do ishah (commit) here, that I should rachaq (go) far off from my maqadash (sanctuary)? But you shall again raah (see) yet other gadawal (great) thawaibah (abominations).
He brought me to the door of the court; and when I looked, behold, a hole in the wall.
Then he said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), dig now in the wall: and when I had dug in the wall, behold, a door.
He said to me, bawaa (go) in, and raah (see) the rai (wicked) thawaibah (abominations) that they do here.

So I went in and saw; and see, every thabanayath (form) of creeping things, and shaqatz (abominable) animals, and all the idols of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), chaqah (portrayed) around on the wall.

There stood panayam (before) them shabaiyam (seventy) men of the zaqan (elders) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); and in their midst stood Yaazanayah the ban (son) Shapan Shaphan, every ayash (man) with his censer in his yad (hand); and the odor of the cloud of incense went up.

Then he said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), have you seen what the zaqan (elders) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) do in the chashak (dark), every ayash (man) in his rooms of mashakayath (imagery)? for they amar (say), Yahawah doesn't raah (see) us; Yahawah has forsaken the aratz (land).
He said also to me, You shall again raah (see) yet other gadawal (great) thawaibah (abominations) which they do.
Then he brought me to the door of the gate of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house) which was toward the tzapawan (north); and see, there sat the women weeping for Thamawaz.
Then he said to me, Have you seen this, ban (son) of adam (man)? You shall again raah (see) yet greater thawaibah (abominations) than these.

He brought me Panayamay the inner court of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house); and see, at the door of the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, between the porch and the mazabach (altar), were about isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) men, with their backs toward the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah, and their panayam (faces) toward the qadam (east); and they were worshipping the shamash (sun) toward the qadam (east).

Then he said to me, Have you seen this, ban (son) of adam (man)? Is it a qalal (light) thing to the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) that they ishah (commit) the thawaibah (abominations) which they ishah (commit) here? for they have filled the aratz (land) with violence, and have turned again to provoke me to kais (anger): and behold, they shalach (put) the branch to their ap (nose).

Therefore will I also ishah (deal) in chamah (wrath); my iyan (eye) shall not spare, neither will I have pity; and though they qaraa (cry) in my ears with a gadawal (loud) qawal (voice), yet will I not hear them.
Then he cried in my ears with a gadawal (loud) qawal (voice), saying, Cause those who are in charge of the Iyar to qarab (draw) near, every ayash (man) with his destroying weapon in his yad (hand).

Behold, shash (six) men came from the darak (way) of the Ilayawan gate, which lies toward the tzapawan (north), every ayash (man) with his slaughter weapon in his yad (hand); and one ayash (man) in their midst Labash in linen, with a writer's inkhorn by his side. They went in, and stood beside the bronze mazabach (altar).

The kabawad (glory) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) was gone up from the karawab (cherub), whereupon it was, to the threshold of the bayath (house): and he called to the ayash (man) Labash in linen, who had the writer's inkhorn by his side.

Yahawah said to him, ibar (go) through the midst of the Iyar, through the midst of Yarawashalam, and set a mark on the foreheads of the men that sigh and that cry over all the thawaibah (abominations) that are done in its midst.
To the others he said in my hearing, ibar (go) through the Iyar achar (after) him, and strike: don't let your iyan (eye) spare, neither have pity;

harag (kill) mashachayath (utterly) the zaqan (old) bachawar (man), the young bathawalah (man) and the virgin, and little tap (children) and women; but don't come near any ayash (man) on whom is the mark: and chalal (begin) at my maqadash (sanctuary). Then they began at the zaqan (old) men that were panayam (before) the bayath (house).
He said to them, tamaa (defile) the bayath (house), and malaa (fill) the courts with the Chalal. yatzaa (go) forth! They went yatzaa (forth), and struck in the Iyar.

It happened, while they were smiting, and I was shaar (left), that I napal (fell) on my panayam (face), and cried, and said, Ah Adanay Yahawah! will you shachath (destroy) all the shaarayath (residue) of Yasharaal (Israel) in your pouring out of your chamah (wrath) on Yarawashalam?

Then he said to me, The iwan (iniquity) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) and Yahawadah (Judah) is maad (exceedingly) gadawal (great), and the aratz (land) is malaa (full) of dam (blood), and the Iyar malaa (full) of perversion: for they amar (say), Yahawah has forsaken the aratz (land), and Yahawah doesn't raah (see).
As for me also, my iyan (eye) shall not spare, neither will I have pity, but I will nathan (bring) their darak (way) on their raash (head).
Behold, the ayash (man) Labash in linen, who had the inkhorn by his side, reported the dabar (matter), saying, I have done as you have tzawah (commanded) me.

Then I looked, and see, in the expanse that was over the raash (head) of the karawab (cherubim) there raah (see) above them as it were a sapphire aban (stone), as the appearance of the damawath (likeness) of a kasaa (throne).

He spoke to the ayash (man) Labash in linen, and said, bawaa (go) in between the whirling galagal (wheels), even under the karawab (cherub), and malaa (fill) both your chapan (hands) with coals of ash (fire) from between the karawab (cherubim), and scatter them over the Iyar. He went in as I watched.
Now the karawab (cherubim) stood on the yamayan (right) side of the bayath (house), when the ayash (man) went in; and the cloud filled the Panayamay court.

The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah mounted up from the karawab (cherub), and stood over the threshold of the bayath (house); and the bayath (house) was filled with the cloud, and the court was malaa (full) of the nagah (brightness) of yahawah (yahweh's) kabawad (glory).
The qawal (sound) of the wings of the karawab (cherubim) was heard even to the Chayatzawan court, as the qawal (voice) of Al Shaday when he dabar (speaks).

It came to pass, when he tzawah (commanded) the ayash (man) Labash in linen, saying, Take ash (fire) from between the whirling galagal (wheels), from between the karawab (cherubim), that he went in, and stood beside a wheel.

The karawab (cherub) stretched shalach (forth) his yad (hand) from between the karawab (cherubim) to the ash (fire) that was between the karawab (cherubim), and took of it, and nathan (put) it into the chapan (hands) Labash him who was clothed in linen, who took it and went out.
There raah (see) in the karawab (cherubim) the thabanayath (form) of a adam (man's) yad (hand) under their wings.

I looked, and behold, arabai (four) wheels beside the karawab (cherubim), one wheel beside one karawab (cherub), and another wheel beside another karawab (cherub); and the appearance of the wheels was like a beryl aban (stone).
As for their appearance, the arabai (four) of them had one damawath (likeness), like a wheel within a wheel.

When they went, they went in their arabai (four) directions: they didn't sabab (turn) as they went, but to the place where the raash (head) looked they followed it; they didn't sabab (turn) as they went.
Their whole body, and their backs, and their yad (hands), and their wings, and the wheels, were Malaa of iyan (eyes) all around, even the wheels that the arabai (four) of them had.
As for the wheels, they were called in my hearing, the whirling galagal (wheels).

achad (every) one had arabai (four) panayam (faces): the achad (first) panayam (face) was the panayam (face) of the karawab (cherub), and the shanay (second) panayam (face) was the panayam (face) of a adam (man), and the shalayashay (third) panayam (face) the face of a aray (lion), and the rabayaiy (fourth) the panayam (face) of an eagle.
The karawab (cherubim) mounted up: this is the chay (living) creature that I saw by the nahar (river) Kabar.

When the karawab (cherubim) went, the wheels went beside them; and when the karawab (cherubim) lifted up their wings to mount up from the aratz (earth), the wheels also didn't sabab (turn) from beside them.
When they stood, these stood; and when they mounted up, these mounted up with them: for the rawach (spirit) of the chay (living) creature was in them.
The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah went yatzaa (forth) from over the threshold of the bayath (house), and stood over the karawab (cherubim).

The karawab (cherubim) lifted up their wings, and mounted up from the aratz (earth) in my iyan (sight) when they went yatzaa (forth), and the wheels beside them: and they stood at the door of the Qadamawanay gate of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house); and the kabawad (glory) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) was over them above.
This is the chay (living) creature that I saw under the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) by the nahar (river) Kabar; and I knew that they were karawab (cherubim).
achad (every) one had arabai (four) panayam (faces), and achad (every) one arabai (four) wings; and the damawath (likeness) of the yad (hands) of a adam (man) was under their wings.

As for the damawath (likeness) of their panayam (faces), they were the panayam (faces) which I saw by the nahar (river) Kabar, their appearances and themselves; they went ayash (every) one ibar (straight) forward.

Moreover the rawach (spirit) lifted me up, and brought me to the Qadamawanay gate of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house), which panah (looks) eastward: and see, at the door of the gate isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) men; and I saw in their midst Yaazanayah the ban (son) of Izawar, and Palatayah the ban (son) of Banayah, shar (princes) of the im (people).
He said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), these are the men who chashab (devise) awan (iniquity), and who yaitz (give) rai (wicked) itzah (counsel) in this Iyar;
who amar (say), The time is not qarawab (near) to banah (build) bayath (houses): this is the caldron, and we are the meat.
Therefore nabaa (prophesy) against them, nabaa (prophesy), ban (son) of adam (man).

The rawach (spirit) of Yahawah napal (fell) on me, and he said to me, amar (speak), Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Thus you have said, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); for I yadai (know) the things that come into your rawach (mind).
You have multiplied your Chalal in this Iyar, and you have filled its streets with the Chalal.
Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Your Chalal whom you have laid in its midst, they are the meat, and this is the caldron; but you shall be brought out of its midst.
You have feared the charab (sword); and I will bawaa (bring) the charab (sword) on you, says the Adanay Yahawah.
I will yatzaa (bring) you forth out of its midst, and nathan (deliver) you into the yad (hands) of strangers, and will ishah (execute) shapat (judgments) among you.
You shall napal (fall) by the charab (sword); I will shapat (judge) you in the border of Yasharaal (Israel); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
This shall not be your caldron, neither shall you be the meat in its midst; I will shapat (judge) you in the border of Yasharaal (Israel);

and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah: for you have not walked in my chaq (statutes), neither have you executed my mashapat (ordinances), but have done after the mashapat (ordinances) of the gawayam (nations) that are around you.

It happened, when I prophesied, that Palatayah the ban (son) of Banayah died. Then napal (fell) I down on my panayam (face), and cried with a gadawal (loud) qawal (voice), and said, Ah Adanay Yahawah! will you ishah (make) a full end of the shaarayath (remnant) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), your ach (brothers), even your ach (brothers), the men of your relatives, and all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), all of them, to whom the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam have said, rachaq (go) far away from Yahawah. This aratz (land) has been given to us for a mawarashah (possession).

Therefore amar (say), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Whereas I have removed them rachaq (far) off among the gawayam (nations), and whereas I have scattered them among the aratz (countries), yet will I be to them a maqadash (sanctuary) for a Mait while in the aratz (countries) where they have bawaa (come).

Therefore amar (say), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: I will gather you from the im (peoples), and asap (assemble) you out of the aratz (countries) where you have been scattered, and I will nathan (give) you the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel).
They shall bawaa (come) there, and they shall sawar (take) away all the shaqawatz (detestable) things of it and all its thawaibah (abominations) from there.

I will nathan (give) them one lab (heart), and I will nathan (put) a Chadash rawach (spirit) qarab (within) you; and I will sawar (take) the aban (stony) lab (heart) out of their flesh, and will nathan (give) them a lab (heart) of flesh;
that they may yalak (walk) in my chaqah (statutes), and shamar (keep) my mashapat (ordinances), and do them: and they shall be my im (people), and I will be their Alahayam.

But as for them whose lab (heart) halak (walks) after the lab (heart) of their shaqawatz (detestable) things and their thawaibah (abominations), I will nathan (bring) their darak (way) on their own raash (heads), says the Adanay Yahawah.
Then the karawab (cherubim) lifted up their wings, and the wheels were beside them; and the kabawad (glory) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) was over them above.
The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah went up from the midst of the Iyar, and stood on the har (mountain) which is on the qadam (east) side of the Iyar.
The rawach (spirit) lifted me up, and brought me in the vision by the rawach (spirit) of Alahayam into Kashaday, to them of the captivity. So the vision that I had seen went up from me.
Then I spoke to them of the captivity all the things that Yahawah had shown me.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah also came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), you yashab (dwell) in the midst of the rebellious bayath (house), who have iyan (eyes) to raah (see), and don't raah (see), who have ears to hear, and don't hear; for they are a rebellious bayath (house).

Therefore, you ban (son) of adam (man), ishah (prepare) your stuff for moving, and move by yawamam (day) in their iyan (sight); and you shall move from your place to achar (another) place in their iyan (sight): it may be they will raah (see), though they are a rebellious bayath (house).

You shall yatzaa (bring) forth your stuff by yawamam (day) in their iyan (sight), as stuff for moving; and you shall yatzaa (go) forth yourself at even in their iyan (sight), as when men go forth into exile.
Dig through the wall in their iyan (sight), and yatzaa (carry) your stuff out that way.

In their iyan (sight) you shall nashaa (bear) it on your shoulder, and yatzaa (carry) it forth in the dark; you shall cover your panayam (face), so that you don't raah (see) the aratz (land): for I have nathan (set) you for a mawapath (sign) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

I did so as I was tzawah (commanded): I brought yatzaa (forth) my stuff by yawamam (day), as stuff for removing, and in the even I dug through the wall with my yad (hand); I brought it yatzaa (forth) in the dark, and bore it on my shoulder in their iyan (sight).
In the baqar (morning) came the dabar (word) of Yahawah to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), has not the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), the rebellious bayath (house), said to you, What are you doing?
amar (say) to them, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: This mashaa (burden) concerns the nashayaa (prince) in Yarawashalam, and all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) among whom they are.
amar (say), I am your mawapath (sign): like as I have done, so shall it be done to them; they shall yalak (go) into exile, into Shabay.

The nashayaa (prince) who is among them shall nashaa (bear) on his shoulder in the dark, and shall yatzaa (go) forth: they shall dig through the wall to yatzaa (carry) out thereby: he shall cover his panayam (face), because he shall not raah (see) the aratz (land) with his iyan (eyes).

My net also will I spread on him, and he shall be taken in my snare; and I will bawaa (bring) him to Babal to the aratz (land) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans); yet shall he not raah (see) it, though he shall mawath (die) there.
I will scatter toward every rawach (wind) all who are around him to help him, and all his bands; and I will draw out the charab (sword) achar (after) them.
They shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shall disperse them among the gawayam (nations), and scatter them through the aratz (countries).

But I will yathar (leave) a few men of them from the charab (sword), from the famine, and from the dabar (pestilence); that they may declare all their thawaibah (abominations) among the gawayam (nations) where they bawaa (come); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), akal (eat) your lacham (bread) with quaking, and drink your mayam (water) with trembling and with fearfulness;

and amar (tell) the im (people) of the adamah (land), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah concerning the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, and the aratz (land) of Yasharaal (Israel): They shall akal (eat) their lacham (bread) with fearfulness, and drink their mayam (water) in shamamawan (dismay), that her aratz (land) may be desolate, and all that is therein, because of the violence of all those who yashab (dwell) therein.
The Iyar that are inhabited shall be laid charab (waste), and the aratz (land) shall be a desolation; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), what is this proverb that you have in the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, The yawam (days) are prolonged, and every vision abad (fails)?

amar (tell) them therefore, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: I will make this proverb to shabath (cease), and they shall no more use it as a proverb in Yasharaal (Israel); but dabar (tell) them, The yawam (days) are at qarab (hand), and the fulfillment of every vision.
For there shall be no more any false vision nor Chalaq divination within the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

For I am Yahawah; I will dabar (speak), and the dabar (word) that I shall dabar (speak) shall be performed; it shall be no more deferred: for in your yawam (days), rebellious bayath (house), will I dabar (speak) the dabar (word), and will ishah (perform) it, dabar (says) the Adanay Yahawah.
Again the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), behold, they of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (say), The vision that he chazah (sees) is for many yawam (day) to come, and he prophesies of ith (times) that are Rachawaq off.

Therefore amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: None of my dabar (words) shall be deferred any more, but the dabar (word) which I shall dabar (speak) shall be performed, says the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy) against the nabayaa (prophets) of Yasharaal (Israel) who nabaa (prophesy), and amar (say) to those who nabayaa (prophesy) out of their own lab (heart), Hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah:
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah, Woe to the foolish nabayaa (prophets), who halak (follow) their own rawach (spirit), and have seen nothing!
Yasharaal (Israel), your nabayaa (prophets) have been like foxes in the waste places.
You have not gone up into the gaps, neither built up the wall for the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), to imad (stand) in the battle in the yawam (day) of Yahawah.
They have seen falsehood and lying divination, who say, Yahawah amar (says); but Yahawah has not sent them: and they have made men to hope that the dabar (word) would be confirmed.
Haven't you seen a false vision, and haven't you spoken a lying divination, in that you amar (say), Yahawah says; but I have not spoken?
Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have spoken falsehood, and seen lies, therefore, behold, I am against you, says the Adanay Yahawah.

My yad (hand) shall be against the nabayaa (prophets) who chazah (see) false visions, and who divine lies: they shall not be in the council of my im (people), neither shall they be written in the writing of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), neither shall they bawaa (enter) into the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel); and you shall yadai (know) that I am the Adanay Yahawah.
Because, even because they have seduced my im (people), saying, shalawam (peace); and there is no shalawam (peace); and when one banah (builds) up a wall, behold, they plaster it Thapal whitewash:

amar (tell) those who plaster it Thapal whitewash, that it shall napal (fall): there shall be an overflowing shower; and you, great hailstones, shall napal (fall); and a stormy rawach (wind) shall tear it.
Behold, when the wall has fallen, shall it not be said to you, Where is the plaster with which you have plastered it?

Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: I will even tear it with a stormy rawach (wind) in my chamah (wrath); and there shall be an overflowing shower in my ap (anger), and great hailstones in chamah (wrath) to consume it.

So will I haras (break) down the wall that you have plastered Thapal whitewash, and nagai (bring) it down to the aratz (ground), so that its yasawad (foundation) shall be uncovered; and it shall napal (fall), and you shall be consumed in its midst: and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Thus will I kalah (accomplish) my chamah (wrath) on the wall, and on those who have plastered it Thapal whitewash; and I will amar (tell) you, The wall is no more, neither those who plastered it;

to wit, the nabayaa (prophets) of Yasharaal (Israel) who nabaa (prophesy) concerning Yarawashalam, and who chazah (see) visions of shalawam (peace) for her, and there is no shalawam (peace), says the Adanay Yahawah.
You, ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (set) your panayam (face) against the bath (daughters) of your im (people), who nabaa (prophesy) out of their own lab (heart); and nabaa (prophesy) against them,

and amar (say), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Woe to the women who sew pillows on all elbows, and ishah (make) kerchiefs for the raash (head) of persons of every stature to hunt napash (souls)! Will you hunt the napash (souls) of my im (people), and chayah (save) napash (souls) chayah (alive) for yourselves?

You have profaned me among my im (people) for shail (handfuls) of barley and for pieces of lacham (bread), to mawath (kill) the napash (souls) who should not mawath (die), and to chayah (save) the napash (souls) chayah (alive) who should not chayah (live), by your lying to my im (people) who listen to lies.

Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against your pillows, with which you there hunt the napash (souls) to make them fly, and I will tear them from your zarawai (arms); and I will let the napash (souls) shalach (go), even the napash (souls) whom you hunt to make them fly.
Your kerchiefs also will I tear, and natzal (deliver) my im (people) out of your yad (hand), and they shall be no more in your yad (hand) to be hunted; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Because with lies you have grieved the lab (heart) of the tzadayaq (righteous), whom I have not made sad; and strengthened the yad (hands) of the rai (wicked), that he should not shawab (turn back / repent) from his rashai (wicked) darak (way), and be saved chayah (alive):
Therefore you shall no more chazah (see) false visions, nor practice divination. I will natzal (deliver) my im (people) out of your yad (hand); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Then came anawash (certain) of the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) to me, and sat panayam (before) me.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), these men have taken their idols into their lab (heart), and nathan (put) the stumbling block of their iwan (iniquity) before their panayam (face): should I be inquired of at all by them?

Therefore dabar (speak) to them, and amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Every ayash (man) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) who ilah (takes) his idols into his lab (heart), and shawam (puts) the stumbling block of his iwan (iniquity) before his panayam (face), and bawaa (comes) to the nabayaa (prophet); I Yahawah will answer him therein according to the multitude of his idols;
that I may take the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) in their own lab (heart), because they are all estranged from me through their idols.

Therefore amar (tell) the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: shawab (turn back / repent), and shawab (turn back / repent) yourselves from your idols; and shawab (turn back / repent) away your panayam (faces) from all your thawaibah (abominations).

For everyone of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), or of the strangers who live in Yasharaal (Israel), who nazar (separates) himself from me, and ilah (takes) his idols into his lab (heart), and shawam (puts) the stumbling block of his iwan (iniquity) before his panayam (face), and bawaa (comes) to the nabayaa (prophet) to inquire for himself of me; I Yahawah will answer him by myself:

and I will nathan (set) my panayam (face) against that ayash (man), and will shamam (make) him an astonishment, for a awath (sign) and a proverb, and I will karath (cut) him off from the midst of my im (people); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

If the nabayaa (prophet) is deceived and dabar (speak) a dabar (word), I, Yahawah, have deceived that nabayaa (prophet), and I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on him, and will destroy him from the midst of my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel).
They shall nashaa (bear) their iwan (iniquity): the iwan (iniquity) of the nabayaa (prophet) shall be even as the iwan (iniquity) of him who seeks him;

that the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) may thaih (go) no more astray from me, neither tamaa (defile) themselves any more with all their pashai (transgressions); but that they may be my im (people), and I may be their Alahayam, says the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), when a aratz (land) chataa (sins) against me by committing a trespass, and I natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on it, and shabar (break) the matah (staff) of its lacham (bread), and shalach (send) famine on it, and karath (cut) off from it adam (man) and animal;
though these shalawash (three) men, Nach, Danayaal, and Ayawab, were in it, they should natzal (deliver) but their own napash (souls) by their tzadaqah (righteousness), says the Adanay Yahawah.
If I cause rai (evil) animals to ibar (pass) through the aratz (land), and they ravage it, and it be made desolate, so that no ibar (man) may pass through panayam (because) of the animals;

though these shalawash (three) men were in it, as I chay (live), says the Adanay Yahawah, they should natzal (deliver) neither ban (sons) nor bath (daughters); they only should be delivered, but the aratz (land) should be desolate.
Or if I bawaa (bring) a charab (sword) on that aratz (land), and amar (say), charab (sword), ibar (go) through the aratz (land); so that I karath (cut) off from it adam (man) and animal;

though these shalawash (three) men were in it, as I chay (live), says the Adanay Yahawah, they should natzal (deliver) neither ban (sons) nor bath (daughters), but they only should be delivered themselves.
Or if I shalach (send) a dabar (pestilence) into that aratz (land), and pour out my chamah (wrath) on it in dam (blood), to karath (cut) off from it adam (man) and animal;

though Nach, Danayaal, and Ayawab, were in it, as I chay (live), says the Adanay Yahawah, they should natzal (deliver) neither ban (son) am (nor) bath (daughter); they should but natzal (deliver) their own napash (souls) by their tzadaqah (righteousness).

For thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: How much more when I shalach (send) my arabai (four) severe shapat (judgments) on Yarawashalam, the charab (sword), and the famine, and the rai (evil) animals, and the dabar (pestilence), to karath (cut) off from it adam (man) and animal!

Yet, behold, therein shall be yathar (left) a palayatah (remnant) that shall be carried yatzaa (forth), both ban (sons) and bath (daughters): behold, they shall yatzaa (come) forth to you, and you shall raah (see) their darak (way) and their ilayalah (doings); and you shall be comforted concerning the rai (evil) that I have brought on Yarawashalam, even concerning all that I have brought on it.

They shall nacham (comfort) you, when you raah (see) their darak (way) and their ilayalah (doings); and you shall yadai (know) that I have not done without cause all that I have done in it, says the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), what is the vine itz (tree) more than any itz (tree), the vine-branch which is among the itz (trees) of the Yair?
Shall itz (wood) be taken of it to ishah (make) any malaakah (work)? or will men take a pin of it to hang any vessel thereon?
Behold, it is nathan (cast) into the ash (fire) for fuel; the ash (fire) has devoured shanayam (both) its ends, and its midst is burned: is it tzalach (profitable) for any malaakah (work)?

Behold, when it was thamayam (whole), it was ishah (meet) for no malaakah (work): how much less, when the ash (fire) has devoured it, and it is burned, shall it yet be ishah (meet) for any malaakah (work)!

Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: As the vine itz (tree) among the itz (trees) of the Yair, which I have given to the ash (fire) for fuel, so will I nathan (give) the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam.

I will nathan (set) my panayam (face) against them; they shall yatzaa (go) forth from the ash (fire), but the ash (fire) shall akal (devour) them; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shawam (set) my panayam (face) against them.
I will nathan (make) the aratz (land) desolate, because they have committed a mail (trespass), says the Adanay Yahawah.
Again the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), cause Yarawashalam to yadai (know) her thawaibah (abominations);

and amar (say), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah to Yarawashalam: Your birth and your birth is of the aratz (land) of the Kanainay (Canaanite); the Amaray (Amorite) was your ab (father), and your am (mother) was a Chathay (Hittite).
As for your birth, in the yawam (day) you were yalad (born) your navel was not karath (cut), neither were you washed in mayam (water) to cleanse you; you weren't salted at all, nor swaddled at all.

No iyan (eye) pitied you, to do any of these things to you, to have compassion on you; but you were cast out in the panayam (open) shadah (field), for that your napash (person) was abhorred, in the yawam (day) that you were yalad (born).

When I passed by you, and saw you wallowing in your dam (blood), I said to you, Though you are in your dam (blood), chayah (live); yes, I said to you, Though you are in your dam (blood), chayah (live).

I caused you to rababah (multiply) as that which grows in the shadah (field), and you increased and grew great, and you attained to iday (excellent) iday (ornament); your breasts were fashioned, and your hair was grown; yet you were Iyaram and bore.

Now when I passed by you, and looked at you, behold, your ith (time) was the ith (time) of dawad (love); and I spread my skirt over you, and covered your irawah (nakedness): yes, I swore to you, and entered into a barayath (covenant) with you, says the Adanay Yahawah, and you became mine.
Then washed I you with mayam (water); yes, I thoroughly washed away your dam (blood) from you, and I sawak (anointed) you with shaman (oil).
I Labash you also with embroidered raqamah (work), and shod you with sealskin, and I dressed you about with Shash linen, and covered you with silk.
I decked you with iday (ornaments), and I nathan (put) bracelets on your yad (hands), and a chain on your garawan (neck).
I nathan (put) a ring on your ap (nose), and earrings in your ears, and a thapaarah (beautiful) itarah (crown) on your raash (head).

Thus you were decked with gold and kasap (silver); and your clothing was of Shash linen, and silk, and embroidered raqamah (work); you ate fine flour, and honey, and shaman (oil); and you were maad (exceedingly) beautiful, and you prospered to malawakah (royal) estate.
Your sham (renown) went yatzaa (forth) among the gawayam (nations) for your beauty; for it was kalayal (perfect), through my hadar (majesty) which I had shawam (put) on you, says the Adanay Yahawah.
But you trusted in your beauty, and played the prostitute because of your sham (renown), and poured out your prostitution on everyone who passed by; his it was.

You took of your bagad (garments), and made for yourselves bamah (high) places decked with various colors, and played the prostitute on them: the like things shall not bawaa (come), neither shall it be so.
You also took your thapaarah (beautiful) jewels of my gold and of my kasap (silver), which I had given you, and made for yourself tzalam (images) of men, and played the prostitute with them;
and you took your embroidered bagad (garments), and covered them, and nathan (set) my shaman (oil) and my incense panayam (before) them.

My lacham (bread) also which I gave you, fine flour, and shaman (oil), and honey, with which I fed you, you even nathan (set) it panayam (before) them for a pleasant aroma; and thus it was, says the Adanay Yahawah.
Moreover you have taken your ban (sons) and your bath (daughters), whom you have borne to me, and you have sacrificed these to them to be devoured. Was your prostitution a Mait matter,
that you have slain my ban (sons), and delivered them up, in causing them to ibar (pass) through the fire to them?
In all your thawaibah (abominations) and your prostitution you have not zakar (remembered) the yawam (days) of your youth, when you were Iyaram and bore, and were wallowing in your dam (blood).
It has happened achar (after) all your wickedness, (woe, woe to you! says the Adanay Yahawah),
that you have built for yourselves a vaulted place, and have made yourselves a lofty place in every street.

You have built your lofty place at the raash (head) of every darak (way), and have made your beauty a thaib (abomination), and have opened your feet to everyone who passed by, and multiplied your prostitution.
You have also committed sexual immorality with the ban (egyptians), your Shakan, great of flesh; and have multiplied your prostitution, to provoke me to kais (anger).

See therefore, I have stretched out my yad (hand) over you, and have diminished your ordinary food, and delivered you to the will of those who shanaa (hate) you, the bath (daughters) of the Palashathay (Philistines), who are kalam (ashamed) of your zamah (lewd) darak (way).
You have played the prostitute also with the ban (assyrians), balathay (because) you were insatiable; yes, you have played the prostitute with them, and yet you weren't satisfied.
You have moreover multiplied your prostitution to the aratz (land) of Kanain, to Kashaday; and yet you weren't satisfied with this.
How weak is your labah (heart), says the Adanay Yahawah, since you do all these things, the maishah (work) Shalatath a impudent prostitute;
in that you banah (build) your vaulted place at the raash (head) of every darak (way), and ishah (make) your lofty place in every street, and have not been as a prostitute, in that you scorn pay.
A ashah (wife) who naap (commits) adultery! who takes strangers instead of her ayash (husband)!

They nathan (give) nadah (gifts) to all prostitutes; but you nathan (give) your nadan (gifts) to all your lovers, and bribe them, that they may bawaa (come) to you on every side for your prostitution.

You are different from other women in your prostitution, in that no one achar (follows) you to play the prostitute; and whereas you nathan (give) hire, and no hire is given to you, therefore you are different.
Therefore, prostitute, hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah:

Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah, Because your filthiness was poured out, and your irawah (nakedness) uncovered through your prostitution with your lovers; and because of all the idols of your thawaibah (abominations), and for the dam (blood) of your ban (sons), that you gave to them;

therefore see, I will gather all your lovers, with whom you have taken pleasure, and all those who you have loved, with all those who you have hated; I will even gather them against you on every side, and will galah (uncover) your irawah (nakedness) to them, that they may raah (see) all your irawah (nakedness).
I will shapat (judge) you, as women who break naap (wedlock) and shed dam (blood) are mashapat (judged); and I will nathan (bring) on you the dam (blood) of chamah (wrath) and jealousy.

I will also nathan (give) you into their yad (hand), and they shall haras (throw) down your vaulted place, and nathatz (break) down your lofty places; and they shall strip you of your clothes, and take your thapaarah (beautiful) jewels; and they shall yanach (leave) you Iyaram and bore.
They shall also ilah (bring) up a qahal (company) against you, and they shall ragam (stone) you with aban (stones), and thrust you through with their charab (swords).

They shall sharap (burn) your bayath (houses) with ash (fire), and ishah (execute) shapat (judgments) on you in the iyan (sight) of many women; and I will shabath (cause) you to cease from playing the prostitute, and you shall also nathan (give) no hire any more.
So will I cause my chamah (wrath) toward you to nawach (rest), and my jealousy shall sawar (depart) from you, and I will be shaqat (quiet), and will be no more kais (angry).

Because you have not zakar (remembered) the yawam (days) of your youth, but have raged against me in all these things; therefore, behold, I also will nathan (bring) your darak (way) on your raash (head), says the Adanay Yahawah: and you shall not ishah (commit) this lewdness with all your thawaibah (abominations).
Behold, everyone who uses proverbs shall use this proverb amar (against) you, saying, As is the am (mother), so is her bath (daughter).

You are the bath (daughter) of your am (mother), who loathes her ayash (husband) and her ban (sons); and you are the achawath (sister) of your achawath (sisters), who loathed their anawash (husbands) and their ban (sons): your am (mother) was a Chathay (Hittite), and your ab (father) a Amaray (Amorite).

Your gadawal (elder) achawath (sister) is Shamarawan, who yashab (dwells) at your left shamaawal (hand), she and her bath (daughters); and your younger achawath (sister), who yashab (dwells) at your right yamayan (hand), is Sadam and her bath (daughters).

Yet have you not walked in their darak (ways), nor done after their thawaibah (abominations); Qat, as if that were a very Mait thing, you were more shachath (corrupt) than they in all your darak (ways).
As I chay (live), says the Adanay Yahawah, Sadam your achawath (sister) has not done, she nor her bath (daughters), as you have done, you and your bath (daughters).

Behold, this was the iwan (iniquity) of your achawath (sister) Sadam: pride, fullness of lacham (bread), and prosperous ease was in her and in her bath (daughters); neither did she chazaq (strengthen) the yad (hand) of the Inay and Abayawan.
They were haughty, and committed thawaibah (abomination) panayam (before) me: therefore I took them sawar (away) as I saw good.

Neither has Shamarawan committed chatzay (half) of your chataah (sins); but you have multiplied your thawaibah (abominations) more than they, and have justified your achawath (sisters) by all your thawaibah (abominations) which you have done.

You also, nashaa (bear) you your own kalamah (shame), in that you have given palal (judgment) for your achawath (sisters); through your chataah (sins) that you have committed more abominable than they, they are more tzadaq (righteous) that you: yes, be also confounded, and nashaa (bear) your kalamah (shame), in that you have justified your achawath (sisters).

I will shawab (turn back / repent) again their captivity, the captivity of Sadam and her bath (daughters), and the captivity of Shamarawan and her bath (daughters), and the captivity of your captives in their midst;
that you may nashaa (bear) your own kalamah (shame), and may be kalam (ashamed) because of all that you have done, in that you are a nacham (comfort) to them.

Your achawath (sisters), Sadam and her bath (daughters), shall shawab (turn back / repent) to their former estate; and Shamarawan and her bath (daughters) shall shawab (turn back / repent) to their former estate; and you and your bath (daughters) shall shawab (turn back / repent) to your former estate.
For your achawath (sister) Sadam was not mentioned by your pah (mouth) in the yawam (day) of your pride,

before your wickedness was uncovered, as at the ith (time) of the reproach of the bath (daughters) of Aram, and of all who are around her, the bath (daughters) of the Palashathay (Philistines), who do despite to you all around.
You have borne your lewdness and your thawaibah (abominations), says Yahawah.
For thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: I will also ishah (deal) with you as you have done, who have despised the alah (oath) in breaking the barayath (covenant).
Nevertheless I will zakar (remember) my barayath (covenant) with you in the yawam (days) of your youth, and I will qawam (establish) to you a iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant).

Then you shall zakar (remember) your darak (ways), and be kalam (ashamed), when you shall receive your achawath (sisters), your gadawal (elder) sisters and your younger; and I will nathan (give) them to you for bath (daughters), but not by your barayath (covenant).
I will qawam (establish) my barayath (covenant) with you; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah;

that you may zakar (remember), and be confounded, and never open your pah (mouth) any more, panayam (because) of your kalamah (shame), when I have forgiven you all that you have done, says the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), put forth a riddle, and speak a parable to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel);

and amar (say), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: A gadawal (great) eagle with gadawal (great) wings and long feathers, Malaa of feathers, which had various colors, came to Labanawan, and took the top of the cedar:
he cropped off the topmost of the young twigs of it, and carried it to a aratz (land) Kanain traffic; he shawam (set) it in a Iyar of merchants.
He took also of the zarai (seed) of the aratz (land), and planted it in a zarai (fruitful) shadah (soil); he placed it beside many mayam (waters); he shawam (set) it as a willow tree.
It grew, and became a spreading vine of Shapal stature, whose branches turned toward him, and its roots were under him: so it became a vine, and brought ishah (forth) branches, and shot forth sprigs.

There was also another gadawal (great) eagle with gadawal (great) wings and many feathers: and behold, this vine bent its roots toward him, and shot shalach (forth) its branches toward him, from the beds of its plantation, that he might shaqah (water) it.
It was planted in a tawab (good) shadah (soil) by many mayam (waters), that it might ishah (bring) forth branches, and that it might nashaa (bear) fruit, that it might be a adarath (goodly) vine.

amar (say), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Shall it tzalach (prosper)? shall he not pull up its roots, and cut off its fruit, that it may yabash (wither); that all its fresh springing Tarap may yabash (wither)? and not by a strong zarawai (arm) or many im (people) can it be raised from its roots.

Yes, behold, being planted, shall it tzalach (prosper)? shall it not yabash (utterly) yabash (wither), when the qadayam (east) rawach (wind) touches it? it shall yabash (wither) in the beds where it grew.
Moreover the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

amar (say) now to the rebellious bayath (house), Don't you yadai (know) what these things mean? amar (tell) them, Behold, the malak (king) of Babal came to Yarawashalam, and took its malak (king), and its shar (princes), and brought them to him to Babal:
and he took of the zarai (seed) malawakah (royal), and made a barayath (covenant) with him; he also brought him under an alah (oath), and took away the ayal (mighty) of the aratz (land);
that the mamalakah (kingdom) might be Shapal, that it might not nashaa (lift) itself up, but that by keeping his barayath (covenant) it might imad (stand).

But he rebelled against him in sending his malaak (ambassadors) into Matzarayam, that they might nathan (give) him horses and many im (people). Shall he tzalach (prosper)? shall he malat (escape) who does such things? shall he parar (break) the barayath (covenant), and yet malat (escape)?

As I chay (live), says the Adanay Yahawah, surely in the place where the malak (king) dwells who made him malak (king), whose alah (oath) he despised, and whose barayath (covenant) he broke, even with him in the midst of Babal he shall mawath (die).

Neither shall Paraih with his gadawal (mighty) chayal (army) and rab (great) qahal (company) help him in the war, when they cast up mounds and banah (build) forts, to karath (cut) off many napash (persons).
For he has despised the alah (oath) by breaking the barayath (covenant); and behold, he had given his yad (hand), and yet has done all these things; he shall not malat (escape).

Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: As I chay (live), surely my alah (oath) that he has despised, and my barayath (covenant) that he has broken, I will even nathan (bring) it on his own raash (head).

I will spread my net on him, and he shall be taken in my snare, and I will bawaa (bring) him to Babal, and will enter into shapat (judgment) with him there for his trespass that he has trespassed against me.

All his fugitives in all his bands shall napal (fall) by the charab (sword), and those who shaar (remain) shall be scattered toward every rawach (wind): and you shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have spoken it.

Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: I will also take of the lofty top of the cedar, and will nathan (set) it; I will crop off from the topmost of its young twigs a Rak one, and I will plant it on a Gabah and Thalal har (mountain):

in the har (mountain) of the height of Yasharaal (Israel) will I plant it; and it shall nashaa (bring) forth boughs, and ishah (bear) fruit, and be a adayar (goodly) cedar: and under it shall shakan (dwell) all birds of every wing; in the shade of its branches shall they shakan (dwell).

All the itz (trees) of the shadah (field) shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have brought down the Gabah itz (tree), have exalted the Shapal itz (tree), have dried up the Lach itz (tree), and have made the Yabash itz (tree) to flourish; I, Yahawah, have spoken and have done it.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me again, saying,
What do you mean, that you use this proverb concerning the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, The abawath (fathers) have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge?
As I chay (live), says the Adanay Yahawah, you shall not have occasion any more to use this proverb in Yasharaal (Israel).
Behold, all napash (souls) are mine; as the napash (soul) of the ab (father), so also the napash (soul) of the ban (son) is mine: the napash (soul) who chataa (sins), he shall mawath (die).
But if a ayash (man) is tzadayaq (just), and does that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (right),

and has not eaten on the har (mountains), neither has lifted up his iyan (eyes) to the idols of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), neither has defiled his neighbor's ashah (wife), neither has qarab (come) near to a ashah (woman) in her impurity,
and has not wronged any, but has restored to the debtor his pledge, has taken nothing by robbery, has given his lacham (bread) to the Raib, and has covered the Iyaram with a bagad (garment);

he who has not given nathan (forth) on interest, neither has taken any increase, who has withdrawn his yad (hand) from iwal (iniquity), has executed amath (true) justice between ayash (man) and ayash (man),
has walked in my chaqah (statutes), and has kept my mashapat (ordinances), to ishah (deal) truly; he is tzadayaq (just), he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live), says the Adanay Yahawah.
If he fathers a ban (son) who is a robber, a shedder of dam (blood), and who does any one of these things,
and who does not any of those duties, but even has eaten on the har (mountains), and defiled his neighbor's ashah (wife),
has wronged the Inay and Abayawan, has taken by robbery, has not restored the pledge, and has lifted up his iyan (eyes) to the idols, has committed thawaibah (abomination),

has given nathan (forth) on interest, and has taken increase; shall he then chayay (live)? he shall not chayah (live): he has done all these thawaibah (abominations); he shall mawath (surely) mawath (die); his dam (blood) shall be on him.
Now, behold, if he fathers a ban (son), who raah (see) all his ab (father's) chataah (sins), which he has done, and fears, and does not such like;
who has not eaten on the har (mountains), neither has lifted up his iyan (eyes) to the idols of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), has not defiled his neighbor's ashah (wife),
neither has wronged any, has not taken anything to pledge, neither has taken by robbery, but has given his lacham (bread) to the Raib, and has covered the Iyaram with a bagad (garment);

who has withdrawn his yad (hand) from the Inay, who has not received interest nor increase, has executed my mashapat (ordinances), has walked in my chaqah (statutes); he shall not mawath (die) for the iwan (iniquity) of his ab (father), he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live).
As for his ab (father), because he cruelly oppressed, robbed his ach (brother), and did that which is not tawab (good) among his im (people), behold, he shall mawath (die) in his iwan (iniquity).

Yet you amar (say), Why doesn't the ban (son) nashaa (bear) the iwan (iniquity) of the ab (father)? When the ban (son) has done that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (right), and has kept all my chaqah (statutes), and has done them, he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live).

The napash (soul) who chataa (sins), he shall mawath (die): the ban (son) shall not nashaa (bear) the iwan (iniquity) of the ab (father), neither shall the ab (father) nashaa (bear) the iwan (iniquity) of the ban (son); the tzadaqah (righteousness) of the tzadayaq (righteous) shall be on him, and the rashaih (wickedness) of the rashai (wicked) shall be on him.

But if the rashai (wicked) shawab (turn back / repent) from all his chataah (sins) that he has committed, and shamar (keep) all my chaqah (statutes), and do that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (right), he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live), he shall not mawath (die).
None of his pashai (transgressions) that he has committed shall be zakar (remembered) against him: in his tzadaqah (righteousness) that he has done he shall chayah (live).
Have I any pleasure in the mawath (death) of the rashai (wicked)? says the Adanay Yahawah; and not rather that he should shawab (turn back / repent) from his darak (way), and chayah (live)?
