But when the tzadayaq (righteous) shawab (turn back / repent) away from his tzadaqah (righteousness), and ishah (commits) iwal (iniquity), and does according to all the thawaibah (abominations) that the rashai (wicked) ishah (man) does, shall he chayay (live)? None of his tzadaqah (righteous) deeds that he has done shall be zakar (remembered): in his trespass that he has trespassed, and in his chataah (sin) that he has sinned, in them shall he mawath (die).
Yet you amar (say), The darak (way) of the Adanay is not equal. Hear now, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel): Is my darak (way) not equal? Aren't your darak (ways) unequal?

When the tzadayaq (righteous) man shawab (turn back / repent) away from his tzadaqah (righteousness), and ishah (commits) iwal (iniquity), and dies therein; in his iwal (iniquity) that he has done shall he mawath (die).

Again, when the rashai (wicked) man shawab (turn back / repent) away from his rashaih (wickedness) that he has committed, and does that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (right), he shall chayah (save) his napash (soul) chayah (alive).
Because he raah (see), and shawab (turn back / repent) away from all his pashai (transgressions) that he has committed, he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live), he shall not mawath (die).

Yet the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (says), "The darak (way) of the Adanay is not fair." bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), aren't my darak (ways) fair? Aren't your darak (ways) unfair?

Therefore I will shapat (judge) you, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), everyone according to his darak (ways), says the Adanay Yahawah. shawab (turn back / repent), and shawab (turn back / repent) yourselves from all your pashai (transgressions); so iwan (iniquity) shall not be your ruin.

Cast away from you all your pashai (transgressions), in which you have transgressed; and ishah (make) yourself a Chadash lab (heart) and a Chadash rawach (spirit): for why will you mawath (die), bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
For I have no pleasure in the mawath (death) of him who dies, says the Adanay Yahawah: therefore shawab (turn back / repent) yourselves, and chayah (live).
Moreover, nashaa (take) up a lamentation for the nashayaa (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel),
and amar (say), What was your am (mother)? A labayaa (lioness): she couched among aray (lions), in the midst of the young kapayar (lions) she nourished her cubs.
She brought up one of her cubs: he became a young kapayar (lion), and he learned to catch the Tarap; he devoured men.
The gawayam (nations) also heard of him; he was taken in their shachath (pit); and they brought him with hooks to the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
Now when she saw that she had waited, and her hope was lost, then she took another of her cubs, and made him a young kapayar (lion).
He went up and down among the aray (lions); he became a young kapayar (lion), and he learned to catch the Tarap; he devoured men.
He knew their palaces, and laid charab (waste) their Iyar; and the aratz (land) was desolate, and its fullness, because of the qawal (noise) of his roaring.
Then the gawayam (nations) nathan (set) against him on every side from the provinces; and they spread their net over him; he was taken in their shachath (pit).

They nathan (put) him in a cage with hooks, and brought him to the malak (king) of Babal; they brought him into strongholds, that his qawal (voice) should no more be heard on the har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Your am (mother) was like a vine, in your dam (blood), planted by the mayam (waters): it was fruitful and Inap of branches by reason of many mayam (waters).

It had iz (strong) matah (rods) for the scepters of those who bore mashal (rule), and their stature was exalted among the thick boughs, and they were seen in their height with the multitude of their branches.

But it was plucked up in fury, it was cast down to the aratz (ground), and the qadayam (east) rawach (wind) dried up its fruit: its iz (strong) matah (rods) were broken off and withered; the ash (fire) consumed them.
Now it is planted in the madabar (wilderness), in a tzayah (dry) and thirsty aratz (land).

ash (fire) is gone out of the matah (rods) of its branches, it has devoured its fruit, so that there is in it no iz (strong) matah (rod) to be a scepter to mashal (rule). This is a lamentation, and shall be for a lamentation.

It happened in the shabayaiy (seventh) Shanah, in the chamayashay (fifth) month, the tenth day of the chadash (month), that anawash (certain) of the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel) came to inquire of Yahawah, and sat panayam (before) me.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), dabar (speak) to the zaqan (elders) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Is it to inquire of me that you have bawaa (come)? As I chay (live), says the Adanay Yahawah, I will not be inquired of by you.
Will you shapat (judge) them, ban (son) of adam (man), will you shapat (judge) them? yadai (cause) them to know the thawaibah (abominations) of their abawath (fathers);

and amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: In the yawam (day) when I chose Yasharaal (Israel), and swore to the zarai (seed) of the bayath (house) of Yaiqab, and made myself yadai (known) to them in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, when I swore to them, saying, I am Yahawah your Alahayam;

in that yawam (day) I swore to them, to yatzaa (bring) them forth out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam into a aratz (land) that I had searched out for them, flowing with milk and honey, which is the glory of all aratz (lands).
I said to them, Cast away every ayash (man) the shaqawatz (abominations) of his iyan (eyes), and don't tamaa (defile) yourselves with the idols of Matzarayam; I am Yahawah your Alahayam.

But they rebelled against me, and would not listen to me; they ayash (each) didn't throw away the shaqawatz (abominations) of their iyan (eyes), neither did they forsake the idols of Matzarayam. Then I said I would pour out my chamah (wrath) on them, to kalah (accomplish) my ap (anger) against them in the midst of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.

But I worked for my sham (name's) sake, that it should not be profaned in the iyan (sight) of the gawayam (nations), among which they were, in whose iyan (sight) I made myself yadai (known) to them, in bringing them yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
So I caused them to yatzaa (go) forth out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and brought them into the madabar (wilderness).
I gave them my chaqah (statutes), and showed them my mashapat (ordinances), which if a adam (man) does, he shall chayay (live) in them.
Moreover also I gave them my shabath (sabbaths), to be a awath (sign) between me and them, that they might yadai (know) that I am Yahawah who qadash (sanctifies) them.

But the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) rebelled against me in the madabar (wilderness): they didn't halak (walk) in my chaqah (statutes), and they rejected my mashapat (ordinances), which if a adam (man) ishah (keep), he shall chayay (live) in them; and my shabath (sabbaths) they maad (greatly) profaned. Then I said I would pour out my chamah (wrath) on them in the madabar (wilderness), to kalah (consume) them.
But I worked for my sham (name's) sake, that it should not be profaned in the iyan (sight) of the gawayam (nations), in whose iyan (sight) I brought them out.

Moreover also I swore to them in the madabar (wilderness), that I would not bawaa (bring) them into the aratz (land) which I had given them, flowing with milk and honey, which is the glory of all aratz (lands);
because they rejected my mashapat (ordinances), and didn't halak (walk) in my chaqah (statutes), and profaned my shabath (sabbaths): for their lab (heart) went achar (after) their idols.
Nevertheless my iyan (eye) spared them, and I didn't shachath (destroy) them, neither did I ishah (make) a full end of them in the madabar (wilderness).

I said to their children in the madabar (wilderness), Don't yalak (walk) in the chaq (statutes) of your abawath (fathers), neither shamar (observe) their mashapat (ordinances), nor tamaa (defile) yourselves with their idols.
I am Yahawah your Alahayam: yalak (walk) in my chaqah (statutes), and shamar (keep) my mashapat (ordinances), and do them;
and make my shabath (sabbaths) qadash (holy); and they shall be a awath (sign) between me and you, that you may yadai (know) that I am Yahawah your Alahayam.

But the children rebelled against me; they didn't halak (walk) in my chaqah (statutes), neither kept my mashapat (ordinances) to do them, which if a adam (man) do, he shall chayay (live) in them; they profaned my shabath (sabbaths). Then I said I would pour out my chamah (wrath) on them, to kalah (accomplish) my ap (anger) against them in the madabar (wilderness).

Nevertheless I withdrew my yad (hand), and worked for my sham (name's) sake, that it should not be profaned in the iyan (sight) of the gawayam (nations), in whose iyan (sight) I brought them yatzaa (forth).
Moreover I swore to them in the madabar (wilderness), that I would scatter them among the gawayam (nations), and disperse them through the aratz (countries);

because they had not executed my mashapat (ordinances), but had rejected my chaqah (statutes), and had profaned my shabath (sabbaths), and their iyan (eyes) were achar (after) their abawath (fathers)' idols.
Moreover also I gave them chaq (statutes) that were not tawab (good), and mashapat (ordinances) in which they should not chayah (live);

and I polluted them in their own mathanah (gifts), in that they caused to ibar (pass) through the patar (fire) all that opens the racham (womb), that I might shamam (make) them desolate, to the end that they might yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Therefore, ban (son) of adam (man), dabar (speak) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: In this moreover have your abawath (fathers) blasphemed me, in that they have committed a mail (trespass) against me.

For when I had brought them into the aratz (land), which I swore to nathan (give) to them, then they saw every high Gabaih, and every Ibath itz (tree), and they offered there their zabach (sacrifices), and there they presented the kais (provocation) of their offering; there also they made their pleasant aroma, and they poured out there their drink nasak (offerings).
Then I said to them, What does the bamah (high) place where you bawaa (go) mean? So its sham (name) is called Bamah to this yawam (day).

Therefore amar (tell) the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Do you tamaa (pollute) yourselves in the darak (way) of your abawath (fathers)? and do you play the prostitute achar (after) their shaqawatz (abominations)?

and when you offer your mathanah (gifts), when you make your ban (sons) to ibar (pass) through the ash (fire), do you tamaa (pollute) yourselves with all your idols to this yawam (day)? and shall I be inquired of by you, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)? As I chay (live), says the Adanay Yahawah, I will not be inquired of by you;

and that which ilah (comes) into your rawach (mind) shall not be at all, in that you amar (say), We will be as the gawayam (nations), as the mashapachah (families) of the aratz (countries), to sharath (serve) itz (wood) and aban (stone).

As I chay (live), says the Adanay Yahawah, surely with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and with an natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm), and with chamah (wrath) poured out, will I be malak (king) over you:

and I will yatzaa (bring) you out from the im (peoples), and will gather you out of the aratz (countries) in which you are scattered, with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and with an natah (outstretched) zarawai (arm), and with chamah (wrath) poured out;
and I will bawaa (bring) you into the madabar (wilderness) of the im (peoples), and there will I enter into shapat (judgment) with you panayam (face) to panayam (face).

Like as I entered into shapat (judgment) with your abawath (fathers) in the madabar (wilderness) of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, so will I enter into shapat (judgment) with you, says the Adanay Yahawah.
I will ibar (cause) you to pass under the shabat (rod), and I will bawaa (bring) you into the bond of the barayath (covenant);

and I will Barar out from among you the rebels, and those who disobey against me; I will yatzaa (bring) them forth out of the aratz (land) where they live, but they shall not bawaa (enter) into the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel): and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

As for you, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: yalak (go), ibad (serve) everyone his idols, and achar (hereafter) also, if you will not listen to me; but my qadash (holy) sham (name) you shall no more chalal (profane) with your mathanah (gifts), and with your idols.

For in my qadash (holy) har (mountain), in the har (mountain) of the height of Yasharaal (Israel), says the Adanay Yahawah, there shall all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), all of them, ibad (serve) me in the aratz (land): there will I accept them, and there will I require your tharawamah (offerings), and the raashayath (first) fruits of your offerings, with all your qadash (holy) things.

As a pleasant aroma will I accept you, when I yatzaa (bring) you out from the im (peoples), and gather you out of the aratz (countries) in which you have been scattered; and I will be sanctified in you in the sight of the gawayam (nations).

You shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shall bawaa (bring) you into the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), into the aratz (country) which I swore to nathan (give) to your abawath (fathers).

There you shall zakar (remember) your darak (ways), and all your ilayalah (doings), in which you have polluted yourselves; and you shall loathe yourselves in your own panayam (sight) for all your rai (evils) that you have committed.

You shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I have dealt with you for my sham (name's) sake, not according to your rai (evil) darak (ways), nor according to your shachath (corrupt) ilayalah (doings), you bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), says the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (set) your panayam (face) darak (toward) the thayaman (south), and natap (drop) your darawam (word) toward the south, and nabaa (prophesy) against the Yair of the shadah (field) in the Nagab;

and amar (tell) the Yair of the Nagab, Hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah: Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah, Behold, I will yatzath (kindle) a ash (fire) in you, and it shall akal (devour) every Lach itz (tree) in you, and every Yabash itz (tree): the lahabah (flaming) shalahabath (flame) shall not be quenched, and all panayam (faces) from the Nagab to the tzapawan (north) shall be burnt thereby.
All flesh shall raah (see) that I, Yahawah, have kindled it; it shall not be quenched.
Then I said, Ah Adanay Yahawah! they amar (say) of me, Isn't he a speaker of parables?
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (set) your panayam (face) toward Yarawashalam, and natap (drop) your word toward the maqadash (sanctuaries), and nabaa (prophesy) against the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel);

and amar (tell) the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), Thus amar (says) Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, and will yatzaa (draw) forth my charab (sword) out of its sheath, and will karath (cut) off from you the tzadayaq (righteous) and the rashai (wicked).

Seeing then that I will karath (cut) off from you the tzadayaq (righteous) and the rashai (wicked), therefore shall my charab (sword) yatzaa (go) forth out of its sheath against all flesh from the Nagab to the tzapawan (north):
and all flesh shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have drawn yatzaa (forth) my charab (sword) out of its sheath; it shall not shawab (turn back / repent) any more.
Sigh therefore, you ban (son) of adam (man); with the breaking of your thighs and with bitterness you will sigh before their iyan (eyes).

It shall be, when they amar (tell) you, Why do you sigh? that you shall amar (say), Because of the news, for it bawaa (comes); and every lab (heart) shall melt, and all yad (hands) shall be rapah (feeble), and every rawach (spirit) shall faint, and all knees shall be yalak (weak) as mayam (water): behold, it bawaa (comes), and it shall be done, says the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy), and amar (say), Thus amar (says) Yahawah: amar (say), A charab (sword), a charab (sword), it is sharpened, and also furbished;
it is sharpened that it may make a slaughter; it is furbished that it may be as lightning: shall we then make mirth? the shabat (rod) of my ban (son), it condemns every itz (tree).
It is given to be furbished, that it may be handled: the charab (sword), it is sharpened, yes, it is furbished, to nathan (give) it into the yad (hand) of the killer.

Cry and wail, ban (son) of adam (man); for it is on my im (people), it is on all the nashayaa (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel): they are delivered over to the charab (sword) with my im (people); strike therefore on your thigh.
For there is a trial; and what if even the shabat (rod) that condemns shall be no more? says the Adanay Yahawah.

You therefore, ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy), and strike your kap (hands) together; and let the charab (sword) be doubled the shalayashay (third) time, the charab (sword) of the deadly Chalal: it is the charab (sword) of the gadawal (great) one who is deadly Chalal, which enters into their rooms.
I have nathan (set) the threatening charab (sword) against all their gates, that their lab (heart) may melt, and their stumblings be multiplied: ah! it is made as lightning, it is Mait for slaughter.
Gather yourselves together, go to the yaman (right), set yourselves in array, shamaal (go) to the left, wherever your panayam (face) is set.
I will also strike my kap (hands) together, and I will cause my chamah (wrath) to nawach (rest): I, Yahawah, have spoken it.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me again, saying,

Also, you ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (appoint) shanayam (two) darak (ways), that the charab (sword) of the malak (king) of Babal may bawaa (come); they shanayam (both) shall yatzaa (come) forth out of one aratz (land): and mark out a place, mark it out at the raash (head) of the darak (way) to the Iyar.
You shall shawam (appoint) a darak (way) for the charab (sword) to bawaa (come) to Rabah of the children of Ammon, and to Yahawadah (Judah) in Yarawashalam the fortified.

For the malak (king) of Babal stood at the am (parting) of the darak (way), at the raash (head) of the shanayam (two) darak (ways), to use divination: he shook the chatz (arrows) back and forth, he consulted the tharapayam (teraphim), he looked in the liver.

In his right yamayan (hand) was the divination for Yarawashalam, to shawam (set) battering rams, to pathach (open) the pah (mouth) in the ratzach (slaughter), to lift up the qawal (voice) with shouting, to shawam (set) battering rams against the gates, to cast up mounds, to banah (build) forts.
It shall be to them as a false divination in their iyan (sight), who have sworn shabawaih (oaths) to them; but he brings iwan (iniquity) to memory, that they may be taken.

Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have made your iwan (iniquity) to be zakar (remembered), in that your pashai (transgressions) are uncovered, so that in all your ilayalah (doings) your chataah (sins) raah (see); because you have zakar (come) to memory, you shall be taken with the kap (hand).
You, Chalal wounded rashai (wicked) one, the nashayaa (prince) of Yasharaal (Israel), whose yawam (day) has bawaa (come), in the yawam (time) of the iwan (iniquity) of the end,
thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: sawar (remove) the turban, and take off the itarah (crown); this shall be no more the same; exalt that which is Shapal, and abase that which is Gabah.
I will overturn, overturn, overturn it: this also shall be no more, until he bawaa (come) whose mashapat (right) it is; and I will nathan (give) it him.

You, ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy), and amar (say), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah concerning the children of Ammon, and concerning their reproach; and amar (say), A charab (sword), a charab (sword) is drawn, for the slaughter it is furbished, to cause it to akal (devour), that it may be as lightning;

while they chazah (see) for you false visions, while they divine lies to you, to lay you on the necks of the rashai (wicked) who are deadly wounded, whose yawam (day) has bawaa (come) in the yawam (time) of the iwan (iniquity) of the end.
Cause it to shawab (turn back / repent) into its sheath. In the place where you were created, in the aratz (land) of your birth, will I shapat (judge) you.

I will pour out my indignation on you; I will blow on you with the ash (fire) of my ibarah (wrath); and I will nathan (deliver) you into the yad (hand) of bair (brutish) men, skillful to mashachayath (destroy).
You shall be for fuel to the ash (fire); your dam (blood) shall be in the midst of the aratz (land); you shall be zakar (remembered) no more: for I, Yahawah, have spoken it.
Moreover the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
You, ban (son) of adam (man), will you shapat (judge), will you shapat (judge) the bloody Iyar? then yadai (cause) her to know all her thawaibah (abominations).

You shall amar (say), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: A Iyar that sheds dam (blood) in the midst of her, that her ith (time) may bawaa (come), and that ishah (makes) idols against herself to tamaa (defile) her!

You have become asham (guilty) in your dam (blood) that you have shed, and are defiled in your idols which you have made; and you have caused your yawam (days) to qarab (draw) near, and have bawaa (come) even to your Shanah: therefore have I made you a reproach to the gawayam (nations), and a mocking to all the aratz (countries).
Those who are qarawab (near), and those who are Rachawaq from you, shall mock you, you tamaa (infamous) one and rab (full) of tumult.
Behold, the nashayaa (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel), everyone according to his zarawai (power), have been in you to shed dam (blood).

In you have they set qalal (light) by ab (father) and am (mother); in the midst of you have they dealt by oppression with the foreigner; in you have they wronged the fatherless and the alamanah (widow).
You have despised my qadash (holy) things, and have profaned my shabath (sabbaths).
Slanderous men have been in you to shed dam (blood); and in you they have eaten on the har (mountains): in the midst of you they have committed lewdness.
In you have they uncovered their abawath (fathers)' irawah (nakedness); in you have they humbled her who was nadah (unclean) in her impurity.

One has committed thawaibah (abomination) with his neighbor's ashah (wife); and ayash (another) has lewdly defiled his kalah (daughter-in-law); and ayash (another) in you has humbled his achawath (sister), his ab (father's) bath (daughter).

In you have they taken shachad (bribes) to shed dam (blood); you have taken interest and increase, and you have greedily gained of your neighbors by oppression, and have forgotten me, says the Adanay Yahawah.
Behold, therefore, I have struck my kap (hand) at your dishonest gain which you have made, and at your dam (blood) which has been in the midst of you.
Can your lab (heart) imad (endure), or can your yad (hands) be chazaq (strong), in the yawam (days) that I shall ishah (deal) with you? I, Yahawah, have spoken it, and will do it.
I will scatter you among the gawayam (nations), and disperse you through the aratz (countries); and I will thamam (consume) your tamaah (filthiness) out of you.
You shall be profaned in yourself, in the iyan (sight) of the gawayam (nations); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) has become dross to me: all of them are brass and tin and barazal (iron) and lead, in the midst of the furnace; they are the dross of kasap (silver).
Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have all become dross, therefore, behold, I will gather you into the midst of Yarawashalam.

As they gather kasap (silver) and brass and barazal (iron) and lead and tin into the midst of the furnace, to napach (blow) the ash (fire) on it, to melt it; so will I gather you in my ap (anger) and in my chamah (wrath), and I will yanach (lay) you there, and melt you.
Yes, I will gather you, and napach (blow) on you with the ash (fire) of my ibarah (wrath), and you shall be melted in its midst.
As kasap (silver) is melted in the midst of the furnace, so you will be melted in its midst; and you will yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have poured out my chamah (wrath) on you.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), amar (tell) her, You are a aratz (land) that is not cleansed, nor rained on in the yawam (day) of indignation.

There is a conspiracy of her nabayaa (prophets) in its midst, like a roaring aray (lion) ravening the Tarap: they have devoured napash (souls); they take chasan (treasure) and precious things; they have made her alamanah (widows) many in its midst.

Her kahan (priests) have done violence to my thawarah (law), and have profaned my qadash (holy) things: they have made no distinction between the qadash (holy) and the chal (common), neither have they caused men to yadai (discern) between the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean), and have hidden their iyan (eyes) from my shabath (sabbaths), and I am profaned among them.
Her shar (princes) in its qarab (midst) are like wolves ravening the Tarap, to shed dam (blood), and to abad (destroy) napash (souls), that they may get dishonest gain.
Her nabayaa (prophets) have plastered Thapal them with whitewash, seeing false visions, and divining lies to them, saying, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah, when Yahawah has not spoken.
The im (people) of the aratz (land) have used oppression, and exercised robbery; yes, they have troubled the Inay and Abayawan, and have oppressed the foreigner wrongfully.
I sought for a ayash (man) among them, who should build up the wall, and imad (stand) in the gap panayam (before) me for the aratz (land), that I should not shachath (destroy) it; but I found none.

Therefore have I poured out my indignation on them; I have consumed them with the ash (fire) of my ibarah (wrath): their own darak (way) have I brought on their raash (heads), says the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came again to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), there were shanayam (two) women, the bath (daughters) of one am (mother):
and they played the prostitute in Matzarayam; they played the prostitute in their youth; there were their breasts pressed, and there was handled the bosom of their virginity.

Their sham (names) were Ahalah the gadawal (elder), and Ahalayabah her achawath (sister): and they became mine, and they bore ban (sons) and bath (daughters). As for their sham (names), Shamarawan is Ahalah, and Yarawashalam Ahalayabah.
Ahalah played the prostitute when she was mine; and she doted on her lovers, on the Ashawar (Assyrians) her neighbors,
who were Labash with blue, governors and sagan (rulers), all of them desirable young men, horsemen riding on horses.
She bestowed her prostitution on them, the choicest men of Ashawar all of them; and on whoever she doted, with all their idols she defiled herself.

Neither has she left her prostitution since the days of Matzarayam; for in her youth they shakab (lay) with her, and they handled the bosom of her virginity; and they poured out their prostitution on her.
Therefore I delivered her into the yad (hand) of her lovers, into the yad (hand) of the ban (assyrians), on whom she doted.

These uncovered her irawah (nakedness); they took her ban (sons) and her bath (daughters); and her they killed with the charab (sword): and she became a byword among women; for they executed shapawat (judgments) on her.
Her achawath (sister) Ahalayabah saw this, yet was she more shachath (corrupt) in her doting than she, and in her prostitution which were more than the prostitution of her achawath (sister).
She doted on the ban (assyrians), governors and sagan (rulers), her neighbors, Labash most gorgeously, horsemen riding on horses, all of them desirable young men.
I saw that she was defiled; they shanayam (both) took one darak (way).
She increased her prostitution; for she saw men chaqah (portrayed) on the wall, the tzalam (images) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans) portrayed with vermilion,

Chagawar with girdles on their waists, with flowing turbans on their raash (heads), all of them shalayash (princes) to look on, after the damawath (likeness) of the ban (babylonians) in Kashaday, the aratz (land) of their birth.
As soon as she saw them she doted on them, and sent malaak (messengers) to them into Kashaday.
The ban (babylonians) came to her into the bed of dawad (love), and they defiled her with their prostitution, and she was polluted with them, and her napash (soul) was yaqai (alienated) from them.
So she uncovered her prostitution, and uncovered her irawah (nakedness): then my napash (soul) was yaqai (alienated) from her, like as my napash (soul) was alienated from her achawath (sister).
Yet she multiplied her prostitution, remembering the yawam (days) of her youth, in which she had played the prostitute in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
She doted on their paramours, whose flesh is as the flesh of donkeys, and whose issue is like the issue of horses.
Thus you called to memory the lewdness of your youth, in the handling of your bosom by the Matzarayam (Egyptians) for the breasts of your youth.

Ahalayabah, Oholibah, thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will raise up your lovers against you, from whom your napash (soul) is alienated, and I will bawaa (bring) them against you on every side:

the ban (babylonians) and all the Kashaday (Chaldeans), Paqawad and Shawai and Qawai, and all the ban (assyrians) with them; desirable young men, governors and sagan (rulers) all of them, sagan (princes) and men of renown, all of them riding on horses.

They shall bawaa (come) against you with weapons, chariots, and wagons, and with a qahal (company) of im (peoples); they shall shawam (set) themselves against you with tzanah (buckler) and magan (shield) and helmet all around; and I will nathan (commit) the mashapat (judgment) to them, and they shall shapat (judge) you according to their mashapat (judgments).

I will nathan (set) my jealousy against you, and they shall ishah (deal) with you in fury; they shall sawar (take) away your ap (nose) and your ears; and your acharayath (residue) shall napal (fall) by the charab (sword): they shall take your ban (sons) and your bath (daughters); and your acharayath (residue) shall be devoured by the ash (fire).
They shall also strip you of your clothes, and take away your thapaarah (beautiful) jewels.

Thus will I make your lewdness to shabath (cease) from you, and your prostitution brought from the aratz (land) of Matzarayam; so that you shall not nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eyes) to them, nor zakar (remember) Matzarayam any more.
For thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will nathan (deliver) you into the yad (hand) of them whom you shanaa (hate), into the yad (hand) of them from whom your napash (soul) is alienated;

and they shall ishah (deal) with you in hatred, and shall take away all your yagayai (labor), and shall leave you Iyaram and bare; and the irawah (nakedness) of your prostitution shall be uncovered, both your lewdness and your prostitution.
These things shall be done to you, because you have played the prostitute achar (after) the gawayam (nations), and because you are polluted with their idols.
You have walked in the darak (way) of your achawath (sister); therefore will I nathan (give) her cup into your yad (hand).
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: You will drink of your achawath (sister's) cup, which is Imaq and Rachab; you will be ridiculed and held in derision; it contains much.
You shall be filled with drunkenness and sorrow, with the cup of astonishment and desolation, with the cup of your achawath (sister) Shamarawan.
You shall even drink it and drain it out, and you shall gnaw the broken pieces of it, and shall tear your breasts; for I have spoken it, says the Adanay Yahawah.
Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have forgotten me, and cast me achar (behind) your back, therefore you also nashaa (bear) your lewdness and your prostitution.
Yahawah said moreover to me: ban (son) of adam (man), will you shapat (judge) Ahalah and Ahalayabah? then nagad (declare) to them their thawaibah (abominations).

For they have committed naap (adultery), and dam (blood) is in their yad (hands); and with their idols have they committed naap (adultery); and they have also caused their ban (sons), whom they bore to me, to ibar (pass) through the akalah (fire) to them to be devoured.
Moreover this they have done to me: they have defiled my maqadash (sanctuary) in the same yawam (day), and have profaned my shabath (sabbaths).

For when they had slain their children to their idols, then they came the same yawam (day) into my maqadash (sanctuary) to chalal (profane) it; and behold, thus have they done in the midst of my bayath (house).

Furthermore you have sent for men who bawaa (come) from far, to whom a malaak (messenger) was sent, and behold, they came; for whom you did wash yourself, paint your iyan (eyes), and decorate yourself with iday (ornaments),
and yashab (sit) on a stately bed, with a table prepared panayam (before) it, whereupon you shawam (set) my incense and my shaman (oil).

The qawal (voice) of a multitude being at shalaw (ease) was with her: and with men of the common sort were brought Sabaay from the madabar (wilderness); and they nathan (put) bracelets on their yad (hands) twain, and thapaarah (beautiful) itarah (crowns) on their raash (heads).
Then I said of her who was Balah in adulteries, Now will they play the prostitute with her, and she with them.
They went in to her, as they bawaa (go) in to a prostitute: so went they in Ahalah Oholah and Ahalayabah Oholibah, the zamah (lewd) women.

tzadayaq (righteous) men, they shall shapat (judge) them with the mashapat (judgment) of adulteresses, and with the mashapat (judgment) of women who shed dam (blood); because they are adulteresses, and dam (blood) is in their yad (hands).
For thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: I will ilah (bring) up a qahal (company) against them, and will nathan (give) them to be tossed back and forth and robbed.

The qahal (company) shall ragam (stone) them with aban (stones), and baraa (dispatch) them with their charab (swords); they shall harag (kill) their ban (sons) and their bath (daughters), and sharap (burn) up their bayath (houses) with ash (fire).
Thus will I cause lewdness to shabath (cease) out of the aratz (land), that all women may be taught not to do after your lewdness.
They shall nathan (recompense) your lewdness on you, and you shall nashaa (bear) the chataa (sins) of your idols; and you shall yadai (know) that I am the Adanay Yahawah.
Again, in the thashayaiy (ninth) Shanah, in the ishayaray (tenth) chadash (month), in the tenth day of the chadash (month), the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), kathab (write) the sham (name) of the yawam (day), even of this same yawam (day): the malak (king) of Babal drew close to Yarawashalam this same yawam (day).
Utter a parable to the rebellious bayath (house), and amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah, Set on the caldron, set it on, and also pour mayam (water) into it:
asap (gather) its pieces into it, even every tawab (good) piece, the thigh, and the shoulder; malaa (fill) it with the choice itzam (bones).
Take the choice of the flock, and also a pile of wood for the itzam (bones) under the caldron; make it boil well; yes, let its itzam (bones) be boiled in its midst.

Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Woe to the bloody Iyar, to the caldron whose rust is therein, and whose rust is not gone out of it! yatzaa (take) out of it piece after piece; No lot is fallen on it.
For her dam (blood) is in the midst of her; she shawam (set) it on the bare salai (rock); she didn't pour it on the aratz (ground), to cover it with ipar (dust).
That it may cause chamah (wrath) to ilah (come) up to take vengeance, I have nathan (set) her dam (blood) on the bare salai (rock), that it should not be covered.
Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Woe to the bloody Iyar! I also will make the pile great.
Heap on the itz (wood), make the ash (fire) hot, boil well the flesh, and make thick the broth, and let the itzam (bones) be burned.
Then imad (set) it rayaq (empty) on its coals, that it may be hot, and its brass may charar (burn), and that its tamaah (filthiness) may be molten in it, that its rust may be consumed.
She has wearied herself with toil; yet her rab (great) rust doesn't yatzaa (go) forth out of her; her rust doesn't go forth by ash (fire).

In your tamaah (filthiness) is lewdness: because I have cleansed you and you weren't cleansed, you shall not be cleansed from your tamaah (filthiness) any more, until I have caused my chamah (wrath) toward you to nawach (rest).

I, Yahawah, have spoken it: it shall happen, and I will do it: I will not parai (go) back, neither will I spare, neither will I nacham (repent); according to your darak (ways), and according to your ilayalah (doings), shall they shapat (judge) you, says the Adanay Yahawah.
Also the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), behold, I will take away from you the desire of your iyan (eyes) with a magapah (stroke): yet you shall neither mourn nor weep, neither shall your tears bawaa (run) down.

Sigh, but not aloud, ishah (make) no mourning for the mawath (dead); bind your headdress on you, and put your shoes on your feet, and don't itah (cover) your lips, and don't akal (eat) men's lacham (bread).
So I spoke to the im (people) in the baqar (morning); and at even my ashah (wife) died; and I did in the baqar (morning) as I was tzawah (commanded).
The im (people) said to me, Won't you nagad (tell) us what these things are to us, that you do so?
Then I said to them, The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

amar (speak) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will chalal (profane) my maqadash (sanctuary), the pride of your iz (power), the desire of your iyan (eyes), and that which your napash (soul) pities; and your ban (sons) and your bath (daughters) whom you have left behind shall napal (fall) by the charab (sword).
You shall do as I have done: you shall not itah (cover) your lips, nor akal (eat) the lacham (bread) of men.
Your tires shall be on your raash (heads), and your shoes on your feet: you shall not mourn nor weep; but you shall pine away in your iwan (iniquities), and moan one toward ach (another).
Thus Yachazaqaal shall be a mawapath (sign) to you; according to all that he has done, you will do. When this bawaa (comes), then you will yadai (know) that I am the Adanay Yahawah.

You, ban (son) of adam (man), shall it not be in the yawam (day) when I take from them their maiwaz (strength), the joy of their glory, the desire of their iyan (eyes), and that whereupon they mashaa (set) their napash (heart), their ban (sons) and their bath (daughters),
that in that yawam (day) he who escapes shall bawaa (come) to you, to cause you to hear it with your ears?

In that yawam (day) your pah (mouth) will be opened to him who has escaped, and you shall dabar (speak), and be no more mute: so you will be a mawapath (sign) to them; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (set) your panayam (face) toward the children of Ammon, and nabaa (prophesy) against them:

and amar (tell) the children of Ammon, Hear the dabar (word) of the Adanay Yahawah: Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah, Because you said, Aha, against my maqadash (sanctuary), when it was profaned; and against the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), when it was made shamam (desolate); and against the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah), when they went into captivity:

therefore, behold, I will nathan (deliver) you to the children of the qadam (east) for a mawarashah (possession), and they shall yashab (set) their encampments in you, and nathan (make) their mashakan (dwellings) in you; they shall akal (eat) your fruit, and they shall drink your milk.
I will nathan (make) Rabah a Nawah for camels, and the children of Ammon a resting place for flocks: and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

For thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have clapped your yad (hands), and stamped with the feet, and Shamach with all the despite of your napash (soul) against the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel);

therefore, behold, I have stretched out my yad (hand) on you, and will nathan (deliver) you for a spoil to the gawayam (nations); and I will karath (cut) you off from the im (peoples), and I will cause you to abad (perish) out of the aratz (countries): I will destroy you; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Because Mawaab and Shaiyar amar (say), Behold, the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) is like all the gawayam (nations);

therefore, behold, I will pathach (open) the side of Mawaab from the Iyar, from his Iyar which are on his frontiers, the glory of the aratz (country), Bayathahayashayamawath Jeshimoth, Bailamaiwan Meon, and Qarayathayam,

to the children of the qadam (east), to go against the children of Ammon; and I will nathan (give) them for a mawarashah (possession), that the children of Ammon may not be zakar (remembered) among the gawayam (nations).
and I will ishah (execute) shapat (judgments) on Mawaab; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Because Adam has dealt against the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) by taking vengeance, and has asham (greatly) offended, and revenged himself on them;

therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah, I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on Adam, and will karath (cut) off adam (man) and animal from it; and I will nathan (make) it desolate from Thayaman; even to Dadan shall they napal (fall) by the charab (sword).

I will nathan (lay) my vengeance on Adam by the yad (hand) of my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel); and they shall do in Adam according to my ap (anger) and according to my chamah (wrath); and they shall yadai (know) my vengeance, says the Adanay Yahawah.

Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Because the Palashathay (Philistines) have dealt by revenge, and have taken vengeance with despite of napash (soul) to mashachayath (destroy) with perpetual enmity;

therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah, Behold, I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) on the Palashathay (Philistines), and I will karath (cut) off the Karathay (Cherethites), and abad (destroy) the shaarayath (remnant) of the yam (sea) coast.
I will ishah (execute) gadawal (great) vengeance on them with chamah (wrathful) rebukes; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shall nathan (lay) my vengeance on them.
It happened in the ishathay (eleventh) Shanah, in the achad (first) day of the chadash (month), that the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), because Tzar has said against Yarawashalam, Aha, she is shabar (broken): the gate of the im (peoples); she is turned to me; I shall be replenished, now that she is laid charab (waste):

therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah, Behold, I am against you, Tzar, and will cause many gawayam (nations) to ilah (come) up against you, as the yam (sea) causes its waves to ilah (come) up.
They shall shachath (destroy) the walls of Tzar, and haras (break) down her magadal (towers): I will also scrape her ipar (dust) from her, and nathan (make) her a bare salai (rock).
She shall be a place for the spreading of charam (nets) in the midst of the yam (sea); for I have spoken it, says the Adanay Yahawah; and she shall become a spoil to the gawayam (nations).
Her bath (daughters) who are in the shadah (field) shall be slain with the charab (sword): and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

For thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will bawaa (bring) on Tzar Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal, malak (king) of malak (kings), from the tzapawan (north), with horses, and with chariots, and with horsemen, and a qahal (company), and many im (people).

He shall harag (kill) your bath (daughters) in the shadah (field) with the charab (sword); and he shall nathan (make) forts against you, and cast up a mound qawam (against) you, and raise up the tzanah (buckler) against you.
He shall nathan (set) his battering engines against your walls, and with his charab (axes) he shall nathatz (break) down your magadal (towers).

By reason of the abundance of his horses their dust shall cover you: your walls shall shake at the qawal (noise) of the horsemen, and of the wagons, and of the chariots, when he shall bawaa (enter) into your gates, as men enter into a Iyar in which is made a breach.

With the hoofs of his horses shall he tread down all your streets; he shall harag (kill) your im (people) with the charab (sword); and the matzabah (pillars) of your iz (strength) shall yarad (go) down to the aratz (ground).

They shall make a spoil of your riches, and make a prey of your merchandise; and they shall haras (break) down your walls, and nathatz (destroy) your pleasant bayath (houses); and they shall shawam (lay) your aban (stones) and your itz (timber) and your ipar (dust) in the midst of the mayam (waters).
I will cause the noise of your songs to shabath (cease); and the qawal (sound) of your harps shall be no more heard.
I will nathan (make) you a bare salai (rock); you shall be a place for the spreading of charam (nets); you shall be built no more: for I Yahawah have spoken it, says the Adawan Yahawah.
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah to Tzar: shall not the islands shake at the qawal (sound) of your fall, when the Chalal groan, when the slaughter is made in the midst of you?

Then all the nashayaa (princes) of the yam (sea) shall yarad (come) down from their kasaa (thrones), and sawar (lay) aside their robes, and strip off their embroidered bagad (garments): they shall Labash themselves with charadah (trembling); they shall yashab (sit) on the aratz (ground), and shall tremble every moment, and be astonished at you.

They shall nashaa (take) up a lamentation over you, and amar (tell) you, How you are destroyed, who were inhabited by seafaring men, the halal (renowned) Iyar, who was chazaq (strong) in the yam (sea), she and her yashab (inhabitants), who caused their terror to be on all who lived there!
Now shall the islands tremble in the yawam (day) of your fall; yes, the islands that are in the yam (sea) shall be dismayed at your departure.

For thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: When I shall nathan (make) you a charab (desolate) Iyar, like the Iyar that are not inhabited; when I shall ilah (bring) up the deep on you, and the rab (great) mayam (waters) shall cover you;

then will I yarad (bring) you down with those who descend into the bawar (pit), to the im (people) of old time, and will make you to dwell in the lower Thachathay of the aratz (earth), Thachathay the places that are desolate of old, with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit), that you be not inhabited; and I will nathan (set) glory in the aratz (land) of the chay (living):
I will nathan (make) you a terror, and you shall no more have any being; though you are sought for, yet you will never be found again, says the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came again to me, saying,
You, ban (son) of adam (man), nashaa (take) up a lamentation over Tzar;

and amar (tell) Tzar, you who yashab (dwell) at the entry of the yam (sea), who are the merchant of the im (peoples) to many islands, thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: You, Tzar, have said, I am kalayal (perfect) in beauty.
Your borders are in the lab (heart) of the yam (seas); your banah (builders) have perfected your beauty.
They have made all your planks of fir trees from Shanayar; they have taken a cedar from Labanawan to ishah (make) a mast for you.
Of the oaks of Bashan have they made your oars; they have made your benches of ivory inlaid Ashar boxwood, from the islands of Kathay (Kittim).
Of Shash linen with embroidered raqamah (work) from Matzarayam was your nas (sail), that it might be to you for a banner; blue and purple from the islands of Alayashah was your awning.
The yashab (inhabitants) of Tzayadawan and Arawad were your rowers: your chakam (wise) men, Tzar, were in you, they were your pilots.
The zaqan (old) men of Gabal and the chakam (wise) men of it were in you your repairers of ship seams: all the ships of the yam (sea) with their mariners were in you to deal in your merchandise.
Paras and Lawad and Pawat were in your chayal (army), your men of war: they hanged the magan (shield) and helmet in you; they nathan (set) forth your hadar (comeliness).

The men of Arawad with your chayal (army) were on your walls all around, and Gamad men were in your magadal (towers); they hanged their shalat (shields) on your walls all around; they have perfected your beauty.
Tharashayash was your merchant by reason of the multitude of all kinds of riches; with kasap (silver), barazal (iron), tin, and lead, they traded for your wares.
Yawan, Thawabal, and Mashak, they were your traffickers; they traded the napash (persons) of men and vessels of brass for your merchandise.
They of the bayath (house) of Thawagaramah traded for your wares with horses and war horses and mules.
The men of Dadan were your traffickers; many islands were the market of your yad (hand): they brought you in exchange qaran (horns) of ivory and ebony.
Aram was your merchant by reason of the multitude of your handiworks: they traded for your wares with emeralds, purple, and embroidered raqamah (work), and fine linen, and coral, and rubies.
Yahawadah (Judah), and the aratz (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), they were your traffickers: they traded for your merchandise wheat of Manayath, and confections, and honey, and shaman (oil), and balm.
Damashaq was your merchant for the multitude of your handiworks, by reason of the multitude of all kinds of riches, with the yayan (wine) Chalabawan Helbon, and white wool.
Wadan and Yawan traded with yarn for your wares: Ishawath barazal (iron), cassia, and calamus, were among your merchandise.
Dadan was your trafficker in precious bagad (cloths) for riding.
Irab, and all the nashayaa (princes) of Qadar, they were the merchants of your yad (hand); in lambs, and ayal (rams), and goats, in these were they your merchants.
The traffickers of Shabaa and Raimah, they were your traffickers; they traded for your wares with the raash (chief) of all spices, and with all Yaqar aban (stones), and gold.
Charan and Kanah and Idan, the traffickers of Shabaa, Ashawar and Kalamad, were your traffickers.
These were your traffickers in choice wares, in wrappings of blue and embroidered raqamah (work), and in chests of rich clothing, bound with cords and Araz of cedar, among your merchandise.
The ships of Tharashayash were your caravans for your merchandise: and you were replenished, and made very kabad (glorious) in the lab (heart) of the yam (seas).
Your rowers have brought you into rab (great) mayam (waters): the qadayam (east) rawach (wind) has shabar (broken) you in the lab (heart) of the yam (seas).

Your riches, and your wares, your merchandise, your mariners, and your pilots, your repairers of ship seams, and the dealers in your merchandise, and all your men of war, who are in you, with all your qahal (company) which is in the midst of you, shall napal (fall) into the lab (heart) of the yam (seas) in the yawam (day) of your ruin.
At the qawal (sound) of the cry of your pilots the suburbs shall shake.
All who handled the oar, the mariners, and all the pilots of the yam (sea), shall yarad (come) down from their ships; they shall imad (stand) on the aratz (land),
and shall cause their qawal (voice) to be heard over you, and shall cry Mar, and shall ilah (cast) up ipar (dust) on their raash (heads), they shall wallow themselves in the ashes:
and they shall make themselves bald for you, and clothe them with sackcloth, and they shall weep Mar you in bitterness of napash (soul) with Mar mourning.
In their wailing they shall nashaa (take) up a lamentation for you, and qawan (lament) over you, saying, Who is there like Tzar, like her who is brought to silence in the midst of the yam (sea)?
When your wares went yatzaa (forth) out of the yam (seas), you filled many im (peoples); you enriched the malak (kings) of the aratz (earth) with the multitude of your riches and of your merchandise.
In the ith (time) that you were shabar (broken) by the yam (seas) in the depths of the mayam (waters), your merchandise and all your qahal (company) napal (fell) in your midst.
All the yashab (inhabitants) of the islands are astonished at you, and their malak (kings) are horribly shair (afraid); they are troubled in their panayam (face).
The merchants among the im (peoples) hiss at you; you are become a terror, and you shall nevermore have any being.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came again to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), amar (tell) the nagayad (prince) of Tzar, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Because your lab (heart) is lifted up, and you have said, I am a Al, I yashab (sit) in the mawashab (seat) of Alahayam, in the lab (midst) of the yam (seas); yet you are adam (man), and not Al, though you nathan (set) your lab (heart) as the lab (heart) of Alahayam—
behold, you are wiser than Danayaal; there is no secret that is hidden from you;
by your chakamah (wisdom) and by your thabawan (understanding) you have gotten yourself riches, and have gotten gold and kasap (silver) into your treasures;
by your great chakamah (wisdom) and by your traffic you have increased your riches, and your labab (heart) is lifted up because of your riches—
therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Because you have nathan (set) your lab (heart) as the labab (heart) of Alahayam,

therefore, behold, I will bawaa (bring) strangers on you, the irayatz (terrible) of the gawayam (nations); and they shall draw their charab (swords) against the beauty of your chakamah (wisdom), and they shall chalal (defile) your brightness.
They shall yarad (bring) you down to the shachath (pit); and you shall mawath (die) the mamawath (death) of those who are Chalal, in the lab (heart) of the yam (seas).
Will you yet amar (say) panayam (before) him who harag (kills) you, I am Alahayam? but you are adam (man), and not Al, in the yad (hand) of him who chalal (wounds) you.
You shall mawath (die) the mawath (death) of the Iral by the yad (hand) of strangers: for I have spoken it, says the Adanay Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), nashaa (take) up a lamentation over the malak (king) of Tzar, and amar (tell) him, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: You seal up the sum, Malaa of chakamah (wisdom), and kalayal (perfect) in beauty.

You were in Idan, the Gan of Alahayam; every Yaqar aban (stone) adorned you: ruby, topaz, emerald, chrysolite, onyx, jasper, sapphire, turquoise, and beryl. Gold malaakah (work) of tambourines and of pipes was in you. In the yawam (day) that you were created they were prepared.

You were the mamashach (anointed) karawab (cherub) who covers: and I nathan (set) you, so that you were on the qadash (holy) har (mountain) of Alahayam; you have walked up and down in the midst of the aban (stones) of ash (fire).
You were thamayam (perfect) in your darak (ways) from the yawam (day) that you were created, until iwal (unrighteousness) was found in you.

By the abundance of your traffic they filled the midst of you with violence, and you have sinned: therefore I have cast you as chalal (profane) out of the har (mountain) of Alahayam; and I have destroyed you, covering karawab (cherub), from the midst of the aban (stones) of ash (fire).

Your lab (heart) was lifted up because of your beauty; you have corrupted your chakamah (wisdom) by reason of your brightness: I have cast you to the aratz (ground); I have laid you panayam (before) malak (kings), that they may raah (see) you.

By the multitude of your iwan (iniquities), in the iwal (unrighteousness) of your traffic, you have profaned your maqadash (sanctuaries); therefore have I brought yatzaa (forth) a ash (fire) from the midst of you; it has devoured you, and I have turned you to ashes on the aratz (earth) in the iyan (sight) of all those who raah (see) you.
All those who yadai (know) you among the im (peoples) shall be astonished at you: you have become a terror, and you shall nevermore have any being.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (set) your panayam (face) toward Tzayadawan, and nabaa (prophesy) against it,

and amar (say), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, Tzayadawan; and I will be glorified in the midst of you; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shall have executed shapat (judgments) in her, and shall be sanctified in her.

For I will shalach (send) dabar (pestilence) into her, and dam (blood) into her streets; and the Chalal shall napal (fall) in the midst of her, with the charab (sword) on her on every side; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

There shall be no more a pricking brier to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), nor a hurting thorn of any that are around them, that scorned them; and they shall yadai (know) that I am the Adanay Yahawah.

Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: When I shall have gathered the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) from the im (peoples) among whom they are scattered, and shall be sanctified in them in the iyan (sight) of the gawayam (nations), then shall they yashab (dwell) in their own adamah (land) which I gave to my ibad (servant) Yaiqab.

They shall yashab (dwell) securely therein; yes, they shall banah (build) bayath (houses), and plant vineyards, and shall yashab (dwell) securely, when I have executed shapat (judgments) on all those who do them despite all around them; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah their Alahayam.
In the ishayaray (tenth) Shanah, in the ishayaray (tenth) month, on the shanayam (twelfth) day of the chadash (month), the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
"ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (set) your panayam (face) against Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam, and nabaa (prophesy) against him and against all Matzarayam.

dabar (speak) and amar (say), ‘Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: "Behold, I am against you, Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam, the gadawal (great) thanayan (monster) that lies in the midst of his yaar (rivers), that has said, ‘My yaar (river) is my own, and I have made it for myself.'

I will nathan (put) hooks in your Lachay, and I will make the fish of your yaar (rivers) stick to your scales; and I will ilah (bring) you up out of the midst of your yaar (rivers), with all the fish of your yaar (rivers) which stick to your scales.

I'll cast you forth into the madabar (wilderness), you and all the fish of your yaar (rivers). You'll napal (fall) on the panayam (open) shadah (field). You won't be brought asap (together), nor gathered. I have given you for food to the animals of the aratz (earth) and to the birds of the sky.
All the yashab (inhabitants) of Matzarayam will yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, because they have been a mashainah (staff) of reed to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).
When they took hold of you by your kap (hand), you broke, and tore all their shoulders; and when they leaned on you, you broke, and paralyzed all of their thighs.
Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: "Behold, I will bawaa (bring) a charab (sword) on you, and will karath (cut) off adam (man) and animal from you.
The aratz (land) of Matzarayam shall be a desolation and a waste; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah. Because he has said, ‘The yaar (river) is mine, and I have made it;'

therefore, behold, I am against you, and against your yaar (rivers), and I will nathan (make) the aratz (land) of Matzarayam an utter waste and desolation, from the Magadawal Sawanah Seveneh even to the border of Kawash.
No ragal (foot) of adam (man) shall ibar (pass) through it, nor ragal (foot) of animal shall ibar (pass) through it, neither shall it be inhabited arabaiyam (forty) Shanah.

I will nathan (make) the aratz (land) of Matzarayam a desolation in the midst of the aratz (countries) that are shamam (desolate); and her Iyar among the Iyar that are laid charab (waste) shall be a desolation arabaiyam (forty) Shanah; and I will scatter the Matzarayam (Egyptians) among the gawayam (nations), and will disperse them through the aratz (countries).
For thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: "At the end of arabaiyam (forty) Shanah will I gather the Matzarayam (Egyptians) from the im (peoples) where they were scattered;

and I will shawab (turn back / repent) back the captivity of Matzarayam, and will cause them to shawab (turn back / repent) into the aratz (land) of Patharawas, into the aratz (land) of their birth; and they shall be there a Shapal mamalakah (kingdom).

It shall be the Shapal of the mamalakah (kingdoms); neither shall it any more nashaa (lift) itself up above the gawayam (nations): and I will diminish them, that they shall no more radah (rule) over the gawayam (nations).

It shall be no more the confidence of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), bringing iwan (iniquity) to memory, when they panah (turn) to look achar (after) them: and they shall yadai (know) that I am the Adanay Yahawah."'

It came to pass in the shabai (seven) and isharayam (twentieth) Shanah, in the raashawan (first) month, in the achad (first) day of the chadash (month), the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal caused his chayal (army) to ibad (serve) a gadawal (great) ibadah (service) against Tzar: every raash (head) was made bald, and every shoulder was worn; yet had he no wages, nor his chayal (army), from Tzar, for the ibadah (service) that he had served against it.

Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will nathan (give) the aratz (land) of Matzarayam to Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal; and he shall nashaa (carry) off her multitude, and nashaa (take) her spoil, and take her prey; and it shall be the wages for his chayal (army).
I have given him the aratz (land) of Matzarayam as his recompense for which he served, because they worked for me, says the Adanay Yahawah.

In that yawam (day) will I cause a qaran (horn) to bud forth to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), and I will nathan (give) you the opening of the pah (mouth) in their midst; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came again to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy), and amar (say), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Wail, Alas for the yawam (day)!
For the yawam (day) is qarawab (near), even the yawam (day) of Yahawah is qarawab (near); it shall be a yawam (day) of clouds, a ith (time) of the gawayam (nations).

A charab (sword) shall bawaa (come) on Matzarayam, and anguish shall be in Kawash, when the Chalal shall napal (fall) in Matzarayam; and they shall take away her multitude, and her yasawad (foundations) shall be broken down.
Kawash, and Pawat, and Lawad, and all the mixed ban (people), and Cub, and the children of the aratz (land) that is allied with them, shall napal (fall) with them by the charab (sword).

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: They also who samak (uphold) Matzarayam shall napal (fall); and the pride of her iz (power) shall yarad (come) down: from the Magadawal Sawanah Seveneh shall they napal (fall) in it by the charab (sword), says the Adanay Yahawah.
They shall be shamam (desolate) in the midst of the aratz (countries) that are shamam (desolate); and her Iyar shall be in the midst of the Iyar that are wasted.
They shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I have nathan (set) a ash (fire) in Matzarayam, and all her helpers are destroyed.

In that yawam (day) shall malaak (messengers) yatzaa (go) forth from panayam (before) me in ships to make the careless Kawash (Ethiopians) afraid; and there shall be anguish on them, as in the yawam (day) of Matzarayam; for, behold, it bawaa (comes).
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: I will also make the multitude of Matzarayam to shabath (cease), by the yad (hand) of Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal.

He and his im (people) with him, the irayatz (terrible) of the gawayam (nations), shall be brought in to shachath (destroy) the aratz (land); and they shall draw their charab (swords) against Matzarayam, and malaa (fill) the aratz (land) with the Chalal.

I will nathan (make) the yaar (rivers) charabah (dry), and will sell the aratz (land) into the yad (hand) of rai (evil) men; and I will make the aratz (land) shamam (desolate), and all that is therein, by the yad (hand) of strangers: I, Yahawah, have spoken it.

Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: I will also abad (destroy) the idols, and I will cause the alayal (images) to shabath (cease) Nap Memphis; and there shall be no more a nashayaa (prince) from the aratz (land) of Matzarayam: and I will nathan (put) a yaraah (fear) in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
I will make Patharawas shamam (desolate), and will nathan (set) a ash (fire) in Tzain, and will ishah (execute) shapat (judgments) Naa No.
I will pour my chamah (wrath) on sayan (sin), the stronghold of Matzarayam; and I will karath (cut) off the multitude Naa No.
I will nathan (set) a ash (fire) in Matzarayam: sayan (sin) shall be in chawal (great) anguish, and No shall be broken Nap; and Memphis shall have tzar (adversaries) in the yawamam (daytime).
The young men of Awan and of Payabasath shall napal (fall) by the charab (sword); and these cities shall yalak (go) into Shabay.

At Thachapanachas also the yawam (day) shall withdraw itself, when I shall shabar (break) there the yokes of Matzarayam, and the pride of her iz (power) shall shabath (cease) in her: as for her, a cloud shall cover her, and her bath (daughters) shall yalak (go) into Shabay.
Thus will I ishah (execute) shapat (judgments) on Matzarayam; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
It happened in the eleventh Shanah, in the raashawan (first) month, in the seventh day of the chadash (month), that the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), I have shabar (broken) the zarawai (arm) of Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam; and behold, it has not been bound up, to apply healing medicines, to shawam (put) a bandage to bind it, that it be chazaq (strong) to hold the charab (sword).

Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam, and will shabar (break) his zarawai (arms), the chazaq (strong) arm, and that which was shabar (broken); and I will cause the charab (sword) to napal (fall) out of his yad (hand).
I will scatter the Matzarayam (Egyptians) among the gawayam (nations), and will disperse them through the aratz (countries).

I will chazaq (strengthen) the zarawai (arms) of the malak (king) of Babal, and nathan (put) my charab (sword) in his yad (hand): but I will shabar (break) the zarawai (arms) of Paraih, and he shall groan panayam (before) him with the groanings of a deadly Chalal man.

I will chazaq (hold) up the zarawai (arms) of the malak (king) of Babal; and the zarawai (arms) of Paraih shall napal (fall) down; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I shall nathan (put) my charab (sword) into the yad (hand) of the malak (king) of Babal, and he shall natah (stretch) it out on the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
I will scatter the Matzarayam (Egyptians) among the gawayam (nations), and disperse them through the aratz (countries); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
It happened in the eleventh Shanah, in the shalayashay (third) month, in the achad (first) day of the chadash (month), that the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), amar (tell) Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam, and to his multitude: Whom are you like in your greatness?
Behold, the Ashawar (Assyrian) was a cedar in Labanawan with Yapah branches, and with a forest-like Charash, and of Gabah stature; and its top was among the thick boughs.
The mayam (waters) nourished it, the deep made it to grow: its nahar (rivers) ran all around its plantation; and it sent out its channels to all the itz (trees) of the shadah (field).

Therefore its stature was exalted above all the itz (trees) of the shadah (field); and its boughs were multiplied, and its branches became long by reason of many mayam (waters), when it shot them shalach (forth).

All the birds of the sky made their nests in its boughs; and under its branches all the animals of the shadah (field) brought yalad (forth) their young; and all rab (great) gawayam (nations) lived under its shadow.
Thus was it beautiful in its greatness, in the arak (length) of its branches; for its root was by many mayam (waters).

The cedars in the Gan of Alahayam could not hide it; the fir trees were not like its boughs, and the plane trees were not as its branches; nor was any itz (tree) in the Gan of Alahayam like it in its beauty.
I made it Yapah by the multitude of its branches, so that all the itz (trees) of Idan, that were in the Gan of Alahayam, envied it.
Therefore thus said the Adanay Yahawah: Because you are exalted in stature, and he has nathan (set) his top among the thick boughs, and his labab (heart) is lifted up in his height;
I will even nathan (deliver) him into the yad (hand) of the mighty one of the gawayam (nations); he shall ishah (surely) ishah (deal) with him; I have driven him out for his rashai (wickedness).

Strangers, the irayatz (terrible) of the gawayam (nations), have karath (cut) him off, and have left him: on the har (mountains) and in all the Gayaa his branches are fallen, and his boughs are shabar (broken) by all the watercourses of the aratz (land); and all the im (peoples) of the aratz (earth) are gone down from his shadow, and have left him.
On his ruin all the birds of the sky shall shakan (dwell), and all the animals of the shadah (field) shall be on his branches;

to the end that none of all the itz (trees) by the mayam (waters) exalt themselves in their stature, neither nathan (set) their top among the thick boughs, nor that their ayal (mighty) ones imad (stand) up on their height, even all who drink mayam (water): for they are all delivered to mawath (death), to the lower Thachathay of the aratz (earth), in the midst of the children of men, with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit).

Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: In the yawam (day) when he went down to shaawal (sheol) I caused a mourning: I covered the deep for him, and I restrained its nahar (rivers); and the rab (great) mayam (waters) were stayed; and I caused Labanawan to mourn for him, and all the itz (trees) of the shadah (field) fainted for him.

I made the gawayam (nations) to shake at the qawal (sound) of his fall, when I yarad (cast) him down to shaawal (sheol) with those who descend into the bawar (pit); and all the itz (trees) of Idan, the choice and tawab (best) of Labanawan, all that drink mayam (water), were comforted in the lower Thachathay of the aratz (earth).

They also went down into shaawal (sheol) with him to those who are Chalal by the charab (sword); yes, those who were his zarawai (arm), that lived under his shadow in the midst of the gawayam (nations).

To whom are you thus like in kabawad (glory) and in greatness among the itz (trees) of Idan? yet you will be brought down with the itz (trees) of Idan to the lower Thachathay of the aratz (earth): you shall shakab (lie) in the midst of the Iral, with those who are Chalal by the charab (sword). This is Paraih and all his multitude, says the Adanay Yahawah.
It happened in the shanayam (twelfth) Shanah, in the twelfth chadash (month), in the achad (first) day of the chadash (month), that the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), nashaa (take) up a lamentation over Paraih malak (king) of Matzarayam, and amar (tell) him, You were likened to a young kapayar (lion) of the gawayam (nations): yet you are as a thanayan (monster) in the yam (seas); and you broke out with your nahar (rivers), and troubled the mayam (waters) with your feet, and fouled their nahar (rivers).
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: I will spread out my net on you with a qahal (company) of many im (peoples); and they shall ilah (bring) you up in my charam (net).

I will leave you on the aratz (land), I will cast you forth on the panayam (open) shadah (field), and will cause all the birds of the sky to settle on you, and I will satisfy the animals of the whole aratz (earth) with you.
I will nathan (lay) your flesh on the har (mountains), and malaa (fill) the Gayaa with your height.
I will also shaqah (water) with your dam (blood) the aratz (land) in which you swim, even to the har (mountains); and the watercourses shall be malaa (full) of you.

When I shall extinguish you, I will cover the shamayam (heavens), and make its kawakab (stars) dark; I will cover the shamash (sun) with a cloud, and the yarach (moon) shall not awar (give) its awar (light).
All the maawar (bright) awar (lights) of the sky will I make dark over you, and nathan (set) chashak (darkness) on your aratz (land), says the Adanay Yahawah.
I will also trouble the lab (hearts) of many im (peoples), when I shall bawaa (bring) your destruction among the gawayam (nations), into the aratz (countries) which you have not yadai (known).

Yes, I will make many im (peoples) shamam (amazed) at you, and their malak (kings) shall be horribly shair (afraid) for you, when I shall brandish my charab (sword) panayam (before) them; and they shall tremble at every moment, every ayash (man) for his own napash (life), in the yawam (day) of your fall.
For thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: The charab (sword) of the malak (king) of Babal shall bawaa (come) on you.

By the charab (swords) of the gabawar (mighty) will I cause your multitude to napal (fall); the irayatz (terrible) of the gawayam (nations) are they all: and they shall bring to nothing the pride of Matzarayam, and all its multitude shall be destroyed.
I will abad (destroy) also all its animals from beside many mayam (waters); neither shall the ragal (foot) of adam (man) trouble them any more, nor the hoofs of animals trouble them.
Then will I make their mayam (waters) clear, and cause their nahar (rivers) to yalak (run) like shaman (oil), says the Adanay Yahawah.

When I shall nathan (make) the aratz (land) of Matzarayam desolate and waste, a aratz (land) shamam (destitute) of that of which it was full, when I shall strike all those who yashab (dwell) therein, then shall they yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

This is the lamentation with which they shall qawan (lament); the bath (daughters) of the gawayam (nations) shall qawan (lament) therewith; over Matzarayam, and over all her multitude, shall they qawan (lament) therewith, says the Adanay Yahawah.
It happened also in the shanayam (twelfth) Shanah, in the fifteenth day of the chadash (month), that the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), wail for the multitude of Matzarayam, and yarad (cast) them down, even her, and the bath (daughters) of the adayar (famous) gawayam (nations), to the lower Thachathay of the aratz (earth), with those who yarad (go) down into the bawar (pit).
Whom do you pass in beauty? yarad (go) down, and be laid with the Iral.
They shall napal (fall) in the midst of those who are Chalal by the charab (sword): she is delivered to the charab (sword); draw her away and all her multitudes.

The al (strong) among the gabawar (mighty) shall dabar (speak) to him out of the midst of shaawal (sheol) with those who help him: they are gone down, they shakab (lie) still, even the Iral, Chalal by the charab (sword).
Ashawar is there and all her qahal (company); her qabar (graves) are all around her; all of them Chalal, fallen by the charab (sword);

whose qabar (graves) are nathan (set) in the uttermost parts of the bawar (pit), and her qahal (company) is around her qabawarah (grave); all of them Chalal, fallen by the charab (sword), who caused terror in the aratz (land) of the chay (living).

There is Iyalam and all her multitude around her qabawarah (grave); all of them Chalal, fallen by the charab (sword), who are gone down Iral into the lower Thachathay of the aratz (earth), who caused their terror in the aratz (land) of the chay (living), and have borne their kalamah (shame) with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit).

They have nathan (set) her a bed in the midst of the Chalal with all her multitude; her qabar (graves) are around her; all of them Iral, Chalal by the charab (sword); for their terror was caused in the aratz (land) of the chay (living), and they have borne their kalamah (shame) with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit): he is nathan (put) in the midst of those who are Chalal.

There is Mashak, Thawabal, and all their multitude; their qabar (graves) are around them; all of them Iral, slain by the charab (sword); for they caused their terror in the aratz (land) of the chay (living).

They shall not shakab (lie) with the gabawar (mighty) who are fallen of the Iral, who are gone down to shaawal (sheol) with their weapons of war, and have laid their charab (swords) under their raash (heads), and their iwan (iniquities) are on their itzam (bones); for they were the terror of the gabawar (mighty) in the aratz (land) of the chay (living).
But you shall be shabar (broken) in the midst of the Iral, and shall shakab (lie) with those who are Chalal by the charab (sword).

There is Adam, her malak (kings) and all her nashayaa (princes), who in their might are laid with those who are Chalal by the charab (sword): they shall shakab (lie) with the Iral, and with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit).

There are the nasayak (princes) of the tzapawan (north), all of them, and all the Tzayadanay (Sidonians), who are gone down with the Chalal; in the terror which they caused by their might they are put to shame; and they shakab (lie) Iral with those who are Chalal by the charab (sword), and nashaa (bear) their kalamah (shame) with those who yarad (go) down to the bawar (pit).
Paraih shall raah (see) them, and shall be comforted over all his multitude, even Paraih and all his chayal (army), Chalal by the charab (sword), says the Adanay Yahawah.
