For I have nathan (put) his terror in the aratz (land) of the chay (living); and he shall be laid in the midst of the Iral, with those who are Chalal by the charab (sword), even Paraih and all his multitude, says the Adanay Yahawah.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), dabar (speak) to the children of your im (people), and amar (tell) them, When I bawaa (bring) the charab (sword) on a aratz (land), and the im (people) of the aratz (land) take a ayash (man) from among them, and nathan (set) him for their watchman;
if, when he raah (see) the charab (sword) bawaa (come) on the aratz (land), he blow the trumpet, and warn the im (people);
then whoever hears the qawal (sound) of the trumpet, and doesn't take warning, if the charab (sword) bawaa (come), and take him away, his dam (blood) shall be on his own raash (head).
He heard the qawal (sound) of the trumpet, and didn't take warning; his dam (blood) shall be on him; whereas if he had taken warning, he would have delivered his napash (soul).

But if the watchman raah (see) the charab (sword) bawaa (come), and doesn't blow the trumpet, and the im (people) aren't warned, and the charab (sword) bawaa (comes), and take any napash (person) from among them; he is taken away in his iwan (iniquity), but his dam (blood) will I require at the watchman's yad (hand).
So you, ban (son) of adam (man), I have nathan (set) you a watchman to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); therefore hear the dabar (word) at my pah (mouth), and give them warning from me.

When I amar (tell) the rashai (wicked), O rashai (wicked) mawath (man), you shall surely mawath (die), and you don't dabar (speak) to warn the rashai (wicked) from his darak (way); that rashai (wicked) mawath (man) shall die in his iwan (iniquity), but his dam (blood) will I require at your yad (hand).

Nevertheless, if you warn the rashai (wicked) of his darak (way) to shawab (turn back / repent) from it, and he doesn't shawab (turn back / repent) from his darak (way); he shall mawath (die) in his iwan (iniquity), but you have delivered your napash (soul).

You, ban (son) of adam (man), amar (tell) the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel): Thus you amar (speak), saying, Our pashai (transgressions) and our chataah (sins) are on us, and we pine away in them; how then can we chayah (live)?

amar (tell) them, As I chay (live), amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah, I have no pleasure in the mawath (death) of the rashai (wicked); but that the rashai (wicked) shawab (turn back / repent) from his darak (way) and chayah (live): shawab (turn back / repent), shawab (turn back / repent) from your rai (evil) darak (ways); for why will you mawath (die), bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)?

You, ban (son) of adam (man), amar (tell) the children of your im (people), The tzadaqah (righteousness) of the tzadayaq (righteous) shall not natzal (deliver) him in the yawam (day) of his disobedience; and as for the rashaih (wickedness) of the rashai (wicked), he shall not fall thereby in the yawam (day) that he shawab (turn back / repent) from his rashai (wickedness); neither shall he who is tzadayaq (righteous) be yakal (able) to chayah (live) thereby in the yawam (day) that he chataa (sins).

When I amar (tell) the tzadayaq (righteous), that he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live); if he batach (trust) to his tzadaqah (righteousness), and ishah (commit) iwal (iniquity), none of his tzadaqah (righteous) deeds shall be zakar (remembered); but in his iwal (iniquity) that he has committed, therein shall he mawath (die).

Again, when I amar (say) to the rashai (wicked), You shall mawath (surely) mawath (die); if he shawab (turn back / repent) from his chataah (sin), and do that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (right);

if the rashai (wicked) shawab (turn back / repent) the pledge, shalam (give) again that which he had taken by robbery, halak (walk) in the chaqah (statutes) of chay (life), committing no iwal (iniquity); he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live), he shall not mawath (die).
None of his chataah (sins) that he has committed shall be zakar (remembered) against him: he has done that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (right); he shall chayah (surely) chayah (live).
Yet the children of your im (people) amar (say), The darak (way) of the Adanay is not equal: but as for them, their darak (way) is not equal.
When the tzadayaq (righteous) shawab (turn back / repent) from his tzadaqah (righteousness), and ishah (commits) iwal (iniquity), he shall even mawath (die) therein.
When the rashai (wicked) shawab (turn back / repent) from his rashaih (wickedness), and does that which is mashapat (lawful) and tzadaqah (right), he shall chayah (live) thereby.
Yet you amar (say), The darak (way) of the Adanay is not equal. bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), I will shapat (judge) ayash (every) one of you after his darak (ways).

It happened in the shanayam (twelfth) Shanah of our captivity, in the ishayaray (tenth) month, in the chamash (fifth) day of the chadash (month), that palayat (one) who had escaped out of Yarawashalam came to me, saying, The Iyar has been struck.

Now the yad (hand) of Yahawah had been on me in the evening, panayam (before) he who was escaped came; and he had opened my pah (mouth), until he came to me in the baqar (morning); and my pah (mouth) was opened, and I was no more mute.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), they who yashab (inhabit) those waste places in the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel) amar (speak), saying, Abaraham was one, and he inherited the aratz (land): but we are many; the aratz (land) is given us for mawarashah (inheritance).

Therefore amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: You akal (eat) with the dam (blood), and nashaa (lift) up your iyan (eyes) to your idols, and shed dam (blood): and shall you yarash (possess) the aratz (land)?

You imad (stand) on your charab (sword), you ishah (work) thawaibah (abomination), and ayash (every) one of you tamaa (defiles) his neighbor's ashah (wife): and shall you yarash (possess) the aratz (land)?

You shall amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: As I chay (live), surely those who are in the waste places shall napal (fall) by the charab (sword); and him who is in the panayam (open) shadah (field) will I nathan (give) to the animals to be devoured; and those who are in the strongholds and in the caves shall mawath (die) of the dabar (pestilence).

I will nathan (make) the aratz (land) a desolation and an astonishment; and the pride of her iz (power) shall shabath (cease); and the har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel) shall be shamam (desolate), so that none shall ibar (pass) through.
Then shall they yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I have made the aratz (land) a desolation and an astonishment, because of all their thawaibah (abominations) which they have committed.

As for you, ban (son) of adam (man), the children of your im (people) dabar (talk) of you by the walls and in the doors of the bayath (houses), and dabar (speak) Chad to another, everyone to his ach (brother), saying, Please bawaa (come) and hear what is the dabar (word) that yatzaa (comes) forth from Yahawah.

They bawaa (come) to you as the im (people) come, and they yashab (sit) panayam (before) you as my im (people), and they hear your dabar (words), but don't do them; for with their pah (mouth) they show much igab (love), but their lab (heart) goes achar (after) their gain.
Behold, you are to them as a very igab (lovely) song of one who has a Yapah qawal (voice), and can tawab (play) well on an instrument; for they hear your dabar (words), but they don't do them.
When this bawaa (comes) to pass, (behold, it bawaa (comes)), then shall they yadai (know) that a nabayaa (prophet) has been among them.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy) against the raih (shepherds) of Yasharaal (Israel), nabaa (prophesy), and amar (tell) them, even to the raih (shepherds), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Woe to the raih (shepherds) of Yasharaal (Israel) who raih (feed) themselves! Shouldn't the raih (shepherds) raih (feed) the sheep?
You akal (eat) the fat, and you Labash yourself with the wool, you zabach (kill) the Barayaa; Barayaa you don't feed the sheep.

You haven't strengthened the chalah (diseased), neither have you healed that which was chalah (sick), neither have you bound up that which was shabar (broken), neither have you brought shawab (turn back / repent) that which was driven away, neither have you sought that which was lost; but with force and with rigor you have ruled over them.
They were scattered, because there was no raih (shepherd); and they became food to all the animals of the shadah (field), and were scattered.
My sheep wandered through all the har (mountains), and on every high Gabaih: yes, my sheep were scattered on all the surface of the aratz (earth); and there was none who searched or sought.
Therefore, you raih (shepherds), hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah:

As I chay (live), says the Adanay Yahawah, surely because my sheep became a prey, and my sheep became food to all the animals of the shadah (field), because there was no raih (shepherd), neither did my raih (shepherds) search for my sheep, but the raih (shepherds) fed themselves, and didn't raih (feed) my sheep;
therefore, you raih (shepherds), hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah:

Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against the raih (shepherds); and I will require my sheep at their yad (hand), and shabath (cause) them to cease from feeding the sheep; neither shall the raih (shepherds) raih (feed) themselves any more; and I will natzal (deliver) my sheep from their pah (mouth), that they may not be food for them.
For thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I myself, even I, will search for my sheep, and will seek them out.

As a raih (shepherd) seeks out his flock in the yawam (day) that he is among his sheep that are scattered abroad, so will I seek out my sheep; and I will natzal (deliver) them out of all places where they have been scattered in the cloudy and dark yawam (day).

I will yatzaa (bring) them out from the im (peoples), and gather them from the aratz (countries), and will bawaa (bring) them into their own adamah (land); and I will raih (feed) them on the har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel), by the watercourses, and in all the mawashab (inhabited) places of the aratz (country).

I will raih (feed) them with tawab (good) pasture; and on the har (mountains) of the height of Yasharaal (Israel) shall their Nawah be: there shall they rabatz (lie) down in a tawab (good) Nawah; and on Shaman pasture shall they raih (feed) on the har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel).
I myself will be the raih (shepherd) of my sheep, and I will rabatz (cause) them to lie down, says the Adanay Yahawah.

I will seek that which was lost, and will shawab (turn back / repent) back that which was driven away, and will bind up that which was shabar (broken), and will chazaq (strengthen) that which was chalah (sick): but the Shaman and the chazaq (strong) I will destroy; I will raih (feed) them in justice.
As for you, O my flock, thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I shapat (judge) between sheep and sheep, the ayal (rams) and the male goats.

Does it seem a Mait thing to you to have fed on the tawab (good) pasture, but you must tread down with your feet the yathar (residue) of your pasture? and to have drunk of the clear mayam (waters), but you must foul the yathar (residue) with your feet?
As for my sheep, they raih (eat) that which you have maramas (trodden) with your feet, and they drink that which you have fouled with your feet.
Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah to them: Behold, I, even I, will shapat (judge) between the Baray sheep and the Razah sheep.
Because you thrust with side and with shoulder, and push all the chalah (diseased) with your qaran (horns), until you have scattered them abroad;
therefore will I yashai (save) my flock, and they shall no more be a prey; and I will shapat (judge) between sheep and sheep.
I will qawam (set) up one raih (shepherd) over them, and he shall raih (feed) them, even my ibad (servant) Dawad; he shall raih (feed) them, and he shall be their raih (shepherd).
I, Yahawah, will be their Alahayam, and my ibad (servant) Dawad nashayaa (prince) among them; I, Yahawah, have spoken it.

I will karath (make) with them a barayath (covenant) of shalawam (peace), and will cause rai (evil) animals to shabath (cease) out of the aratz (land); and they shall yashab (dwell) securely in the madabar (wilderness), and sleep in the Yair.
I will nathan (make) them and the places around my Gabaih a barakah (blessing); and I will cause the shower to yarad (come) down in its ith (season); there shall be showers of barakah (blessing).

The itz (tree) of the shadah (field) shall nathan (yield) its fruit, and the aratz (earth) shall nathan (yield) its increase, and they shall be secure in their adamah (land); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I have shabar (broken) the bars of their yoke, and have delivered them out of the yad (hand) of those who made slaves of them.
They shall no more be a prey to the gawayam (nations), neither shall the animals of the aratz (earth) akal (devour) them; but they shall yashab (dwell) securely, and none shall make them afraid.

I will qawam (raise) up to them a plantation for sham (renown), and they shall be no more consumed with famine in the aratz (land), neither nashaa (bear) the kalamah (shame) of the gawayam (nations) any more.
They shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, their Alahayam am with them, and that they, the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), are my im (people), says the Adanay Yahawah.
You my sheep, the sheep of my pasture, are men, and I am your Alahayam, says the Adanay Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (set) your panayam (face) against har (mount) Shaiyar, and nabaa (prophesy) against it,

and amar (tell) it, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, har (mount) Shaiyar, and I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) against you, and I will nathan (make) you a desolation and an astonishment.
I will shawam (lay) your Iyar waste, and you shall be desolate; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Because you have had a perpetual enmity, and have given over the children of Yasharaal (Israel) to the yad (power) of the charab (sword) in the ith (time) of their calamity, in the ith (time) of the iwan (iniquity) of the end;

therefore, as I chay (live), says the Adanay Yahawah, I will ishah (prepare) you for dam (blood), and dam (blood) shall pursue you: am (since) you have not hated dam (blood), therefore dam (blood) shall pursue you.
Thus will I nathan (make) har (mount) Shaiyar an astonishment and a desolation; and I will karath (cut) off from it him who passes through and him who shawab (turn back / repent).
I will malaa (fill) its har (mountains) with its Chalal: in your Gabaih and in your Gayaa and in all your watercourses shall they napal (fall) who are Chalal with the charab (sword).
I will nathan (make) you a perpetual desolation, and your Iyar shall not be inhabited; and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
Because you have said, These shanayam (two) gawayam (nations) and these shanayam (two) aratz (countries) shall be mine, and we will yarash (possess) it; whereas Yahawah was there:

therefore, as I chay (live), says the Adanay Yahawah, I will do according to your ap (anger), and according to your envy which you have shown out of your hatred against them; and I will yadai (make) myself known among them, when I shall shapat (judge) you.

You shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have heard all your insults which you have spoken against the har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, They are laid shamam (desolate), they have been given us to devour.
You have magnified yourselves against me with your pah (mouth), and have multiplied your dabar (words) against me: I have heard it.
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: When the whole aratz (earth) Shamach, I will ishah (make) you desolate.

As you rejoiced over the nachalah (inheritance) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), because it was shamam (desolate), so will I do to you: you shall be desolate, har (mount) Shaiyar, and all Adam, even all of it; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
You, ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy) to the har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (say), You har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel), hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah.
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Because the ayab (enemy) has said against you, Aha! and, The ancient bamah (high) places are ours in mawarashah (possession);

therefore nabaa (prophesy), and amar (say), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Because, even because they have made you shamam (desolate), and swallowed you up on every side, that you might be a mawarashah (possession) to the shaarayath (residue) of the gawayam (nations), and you are taken up in the shapah (lips) of lashawan (talkers), and the dabah (evil) report of the im (people);

therefore, you har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel), hear the dabar (word) of the Adanay Yahawah: Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah to the har (mountains) and to the Gabaih, to the watercourses and to the Gayaa, to the shamam (desolate) wastes and to the Iyar that are forsaken, which are become a prey and derision to the shaarayath (residue) of the gawayam (nations) that are all around;

therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Surely in the ash (fire) of my jealousy have I spoken against the shaarayath (residue) of the gawayam (nations), and against all Adam, that have appointed my aratz (land) to themselves for a mawarashah (possession) with the joy of all their labab (heart), with despite of soul, to cast it out for a prey.

Therefore nabaa (prophesy) concerning the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), and amar (tell) the har (mountains) and to the Gabaih, to the watercourses and to the Gayaa, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I have spoken in my jealousy and in my chamah (wrath), because you have borne the kalamah (shame) of the gawayam (nations):
therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: I have sworn, saying, Surely the gawayam (nations) that are around you, they shall nashaa (bear) their kalamah (shame).

But you, har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel), you shall nathan (shoot) forth your branches, and nashaa (yield) your fruit to my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel); for they are at qarab (hand) to bawaa (come).
For, behold, I am for you, and I will panah (turn) into you, and you shall be tilled and sown;
and I will multiply men on you, all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), even all of it; and the Iyar shall be inhabited, and the waste places shall be built;

and I will multiply on you adam (man) and animal; and they shall increase and be fruitful; and I will yashab (cause) you to be inhabited after your former estate, and will do tawab (better) to you than at your beginnings: and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

Yes, I will cause men to yalak (walk) on you, even my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel); and they shall yarash (possess) you, and you shall be their nachalah (inheritance), and you shall no more henceforth shakal (bereave) them of children.
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Because they amar (say) to you, You are a devourer of men, and have been a bereaver of your gaway (nation);
therefore you shall akal (devour) men no more, neither shakal (bereave) your gaway (nation) any more, says the Adanay Yahawah;

neither will I let you hear any more the kalamah (shame) of the gawayam (nations), neither shall you nashaa (bear) the reproach of the im (peoples) any more, neither shall you cause your gawayam (nation) to stumble any more, says the Adanay Yahawah.
Moreover the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

ban (son) of adam (man), when the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) lived in their own adamah (land), they defiled it by their darak (way) and by their ilayalah (doings): their darak (way) panayam (before) me was as the tamaah (uncleanness) of a woman in her impurity.
Therefore I poured out my chamah (wrath) on them for the dam (blood) which they had poured out on the aratz (land), and because they had defiled it with their idols;
and I scattered them among the gawayam (nations), and they were dispersed through the aratz (countries): according to their darak (way) and according to their ilayalah (doings) I judged them.

When they came to the gawayam (nations), where they went, they profaned my qadash (holy) sham (name); in that men said of them, These are the im (people) of Yahawah, and are gone yatzaa (forth) out of his aratz (land).
But I had respect for my qadash (holy) sham (name), which the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) had profaned among the gawayam (nations), where they went.

Therefore amar (tell) the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: I don't do this for your sake, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), but for my qadash (holy) sham (name), which you have profaned among the gawayam (nations), where you went.

I will qadash (sanctify) my gadawal (great) sham (name), which has been profaned among the gawayam (nations), which you have profaned in their midst; and the gawayam (nations) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, says the Adawan Yahawah, when I shall be sanctified in you before their iyan (eyes).
For I will take you from among the gawayam (nations), and gather you out of all the aratz (countries), and will bawaa (bring) you into your own adamah (land).
I will sprinkle tahawar (clean) mayam (water) on you, and you shall be tahar (clean): from all your tamaah (filthiness), and from all your idols, will I tahar (cleanse) you.

I will also nathan (give) you a Chadash lab (heart), and I will nathan (put) a Chadash rawach (spirit) qarab (within) you; and I will sawar (take) away the aban (stony) lab (heart) out of your flesh, and I will nathan (give) you a lab (heart) of flesh.
I will nathan (put) my rawach (spirit) qarab (within) you, and cause you to yalak (walk) in my chaq (statutes), and you shall shamar (keep) my mashapat (ordinances), and do them.
You shall yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land) that I gave to your abawath (fathers); and you shall be my im (people), and I will be your Alahayam.
I will yashai (save) you from all your tamaah (uncleanness): and I will qaraa (call) for the grain, and will multiply it, and nathan (lay) no famine on you.
I will multiply the fruit of the itz (tree), and the increase of the shadah (field), that you may receive no more the reproach of famine among the gawayam (nations).

Then you shall zakar (remember) your rai (evil) darak (ways), and your mailal (doings) that were not tawab (good); and you shall loathe yourselves in your own panayam (sight) for your iwan (iniquities) and for your thawaibah (abominations).
Nor for your sake do I this, says the Adanay Yahawah, be it yadai (known) to you: be bawash (ashamed) and kalam (confounded) for your darak (ways), bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: In the yawam (day) that I tahar (cleanse) you from all your iwan (iniquities), I will cause the Iyar to be inhabited, and the waste places shall be built.
The aratz (land) that was shamam (desolate) shall be tilled, whereas it was a desolation in the iyan (sight) of all who passed by.
They shall amar (say), This aratz (land) that was shamam (desolate) has become like the Gan of Idan; and the Charab and shamam (desolate) and ruined Iyar are fortified and inhabited.

Then the gawayam (nations) that are shaar (left) around you shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have built the ruined places, and planted that which was shamam (desolate): I, Yahawah, have spoken it, and I will do it.
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: For this, moreover, will I be inquired of by the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), to do it for them: I will increase them with men like a flock.
As the flock for sacrifice, as the flock of Yarawashalam in her mawaid (appointed) feasts, so shall the Charab Iyar be Malaa with flocks of men; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
The yad (hand) of Yahawah was on me, and he brought me out in the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah, and nawach (set) me down in the midst of the Baqaih; and it was Malaa of itzam (bones).
He caused me to ibar (pass) by them all around: and behold, there were very many in the panayam (open) Baqaih; and behold, they were very Yabash.
He said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), can these itzam (bones) chayah (live)? I answered, Adanay Yahawah, you yadai (know).
Again he said to me, nabaa (prophesy) over these itzam (bones), and amar (tell) them, you Yabash itzam (bones), hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah.
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah to these itzam (bones): Behold, I will cause rawach (breath) to bawaa (enter) into you, and you shall chayah (live).

I will nathan (lay) sinews on you, and will ilah (bring) up flesh on you, and cover you with skin, and nathan (put) rawach (breath) in you, and you shall chayah (live); and you shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
So I prophesied as I was tzawah (commanded): and as I prophesied, there was a qawal (noise), and behold, an earthquake; and the itzam (bones) came together, itzam (bone) to its itzam (bone).
I saw, and, behold, there were sinews on them, and flesh came up, and skin covered them above; but there was no rawach (breath) in them.

Then he said to me, nabaa (prophesy) to the rawach (wind), nabaa (prophesy), ban (son) of adam (man), and amar (tell) the rawach (wind), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: bawaa (come) from the arabai (four) rawach (winds), rawach (breath), and breathe on these slain, that they may chayah (live).
So I prophesied as he tzawah (commanded) me, and the rawach (breath) came into them, and they lived, and stood up on their feet, an maad (exceedingly) gadawal (great) chayal (army).

Then he said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), these itzam (bones) are the whole bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel): behold, they amar (say), Our itzam (bones) are dried up, and our hope is lost; we are gazar (clean) cut off.

Therefore nabaa (prophesy), and amar (tell) them, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will pathach (open) your qabar (graves), and ilah (cause) you to come up out of your qabar (graves), my people; and I will bawaa (bring) you into the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel).
You shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, when I have opened your qabar (graves), and caused you to ilah (come) up out of your qabar (graves), my im (people).

I will nathan (put) my rawach (spirit) in you, and you shall chayah (live), and I will yanach (place) you in your own adamah (land): and you shall yadai (know) that I, Yahawah, have spoken it and performed it, says Yahawah.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came again to me, saying,

You, ban (son) of adam (man), take one itz (stick), and kathab (write) on it, For Yahawadah (Judah), and for the children of Yasharaal (Israel) his companions: then take another itz (stick), and kathab (write) on it, For Yawasap, the itz (stick) of Aparayam, and for all the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) his companions:
and qarab (join) them for you one to another into one itz (stick), that they may become one in your yad (hand).
When the children of your im (people) shall amar (speak) to you, saying, Will you not show us what you mean by these?

dabar (tell) them, Thus dabar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will take the itz (stick) of Yawasap, which is in the yad (hand) of Aparayam, and the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) his companions; and I will nathan (put) them with it, even with the itz (stick) of Yahawadah (Judah), and ishah (make) them one itz (stick), and they shall be one in my yad (hand).
The itz (sticks) whereon you kathab (write) shall be in your yad (hand) before their iyan (eyes).

dabar (say) to them, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I will take the children of Yasharaal (Israel) from among the gawayam (nations), where they are gone, and will gather them on every side, and bawaa (bring) them into their own adamah (land):

and I will ishah (make) them one gaway (nation) in the aratz (land), on the har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel); and one malak (king) shall be malak (king) to them all; and they shall be no more shanayam (two) gaway (nations), neither shall they be divided into shanayam (two) mamalakah (kingdoms) any more at all;

neither shall they tamaa (defile) themselves any more with their idols, nor with their shaqawatz (detestable) things, nor with any of their pashai (transgressions); but I will yashai (save) them out of all their mawashab (dwelling) places, in which they have sinned, and will tahar (cleanse) them: so shall they be my im (people), and I will be their Alahayam.

My ibad (servant) Dawad shall be malak (king) over them; and they all shall have one raih (shepherd): they shall also yalak (walk) in my mashapat (ordinances), and shamar (observe) my chaqah (statutes), and do them.

They shall yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land) that I have given to Yaiqab my ibad (servant), in which your abawath (fathers) lived; and they shall yashab (dwell) therein, they, and their children, and their children's children, iwalam (forever): and Dawad my ibad (servant) shall be their nashayaa (prince) for ever.

Moreover I will karath (make) a barayath (covenant) of shalawam (peace) with them; it shall be an iwalam (forever) barayath (covenant) with them; and I will nathan (place) them, and multiply them, and will nathan (set) my maqadash (sanctuary) in their midst forevermore.
My mashakan (tent) also shall be with them; and I will be their Alahayam, and they shall be my im (people).
The gawayam (nations) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah who qadash (sanctifies) Yasharaal (Israel), when my maqadash (sanctuary) shall be in their midst forevermore.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,
ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (set) your panayam (face) toward Gawag, of the aratz (land) of Magawag, the nashayaa (prince) of Rosh, Mashak, and Thawabal, and nabaa (prophesy) against him,
and amar (say), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, Gawag, prince of Rosh, Mashak, and Thawabal:

and I will shawab (turn back / repent) you around, and nathan (put) hooks into your Lachay, and I will yatzaa (bring) you forth, with all your chayal (army), horses and horsemen, all Labash them clothed in full armor, a rab (great) qahal (company) with tzanah (buckler) and magan (shield), all of them handling charab (swords);
Paras, Kawash, and Pawat with them, all of them with magan (shield) and helmet;
Gamar, and all his hordes; the bayath (house) of Thawagaramah in the uttermost parts of the tzapawan (north), and all his hordes; even many im (peoples) with you.
Be prepared, yes, kawan (prepare) yourself, you, and all your qahal (companies) who are assembled to you, and be a guard to them.

After many yawam (days) you shall be visited: in the acharayath (latter) Shanah you shall bawaa (come) into the aratz (land) that is brought shawab (turn back / repent) from the charab (sword), that is gathered out of many im (peoples), on the har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel), which have been a continual waste; but it is brought yatzaa (forth) out of the im (peoples), and they shall yashab (dwell) securely, all of them.
You shall ilah (ascend), you shall bawaa (come) like a shawaa (storm), you shall be like a cloud to cover the aratz (land), you, and all your hordes, and many im (peoples) with you.
Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: It shall happen in that yawam (day), that things shall ilah (come) into your labab (mind), and you shall chashab (devise) an rai (evil) machashabah (device):

and you shall amar (say), I will ilah (go) up to the aratz (land) of unwalled villages; I will bawaa (go) to those who are at shaqat (rest), who yashab (dwell) securely, all of them yashab (dwelling) without walls, and having neither bars nor gates;

to take the spoil and to take the prey; to shawab (turn back / repent) your yad (hand) against the waste places that are now inhabited, and against the im (people) who are gathered out of the gawayam (nations), who have gotten livestock and qanayan (goods), who yashab (dwell) in the middle of the aratz (earth).

Shabaa, and Dadan, and the merchants of Tharashayash, with all the young kapayar (lions) of it, shall amar (tell) you, Have you bawaa (come) to take the spoil? have you assembled your qahal (company) to take the prey? to nashaa (carry) away kasap (silver) and gold, to take away livestock and qanayan (goods), to take gadawal (great) spoil?

Therefore, ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy), and amar (tell) Gawag, Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: In that yawam (day) when my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel) yashab (dwells) securely, shall you not yadai (know) it?

You shall bawaa (come) from your place out of the uttermost parts of the tzapawan (north), you, and many im (peoples) with you, all of them riding on horses, a gadawal (great) qahal (company) and a rab (mighty) chayal (army);

and you shall ilah (come) up against my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), as a cloud to cover the aratz (land): it shall happen in the acharayath (latter) yawam (days), that I will bawaa (bring) you against my aratz (land), that the gawayam (nations) may yadai (know) me, when I shall be sanctified in you, Gawag, before their iyan (eyes).

Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Are you he of whom I spoke in Qadamawanay yawam (time) by my ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets) of Yasharaal (Israel), who prophesied in those yawam (days) for many Shanah that I would bawaa (bring) you against them?

It shall happen in that yawam (day), when Gawag shall bawaa (come) against the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), says the Adanay Yahawah, that my chamah (wrath) shall ilah (come) up into my ap (nostrils).
For in my jealousy and in the ash (fire) of my ibarah (wrath) have I spoken, Surely in that yawam (day) there shall be a gadawal (great) shaking in the adamah (land) of Yasharaal (Israel);

so that the fish of the yam (sea), and the birds of the sky, and the animals of the shadah (field), and all creeping things who creep on the adamah (earth), and all the men who are on the surface of the adamah (earth), shall shake at my panayam (presence), and the har (mountains) shall be thrown down, and the steep places shall napal (fall), and every wall shall napal (fall) to the aratz (ground).
I will qaraa (call) for a charab (sword) against him to all my har (mountains), says the Adanay Yahawah: every ayash (man's) charab (sword) shall be against his ach (brother).

With dabar (pestilence) and with dam (blood) will I enter into shapat (judgment) with him; and I will rain on him, and on his hordes, and on the many im (peoples) who are with him, an overflowing shower, and great hailstones, ash (fire), and sulfur.
I will magnify myself, and qadash (sanctify) myself, and I will yadai (make) myself known in the iyan (eyes) of many gawayam (nations); and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.
You, ban (son) of adam (man), nabaa (prophesy) against Gawag, and amar (say), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Behold, I am against you, Gawag, prince of Rosh, Mashak, and Thawabal:

and I will shawab (turn back / repent) you around, and will lead you on, and will ilah (cause) you to come up from the uttermost parts of the tzapawan (north); and I will bawaa (bring) you on the har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel);
and I will strike your qashath (bow) out of your shamaawal (left) yad (hand), and will cause your chatz (arrows) to napal (fall) out of your yamayan (right) yad (hand).

You shall napal (fall) on the har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel), you, and all your hordes, and the im (peoples) who are with you: I will nathan (give) you to the ravenous birds of every sort, and to the animals of the shadah (field) to be devoured.
You shall napal (fall) on the panayam (open) shadah (field); for I have spoken it, says the Adanay Yahawah.
I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on Magawag, and on those who yashab (dwell) securely in the islands; and they shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah.

My qadash (holy) sham (name) will I yadai (make) known in the midst of my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel); neither will I allow my qadash (holy) sham (name) to be profaned any more: and the gawayam (nations) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, the qadawash (holy) One in Yasharaal (Israel).
Behold, it bawaa (comes), and it shall be done, says the Adanay Yahawah; this is the yawam (day) about which I have spoken.

Those who yashab (dwell) in the Iyar of Yasharaal (Israel) shall yatzaa (go) forth, and shall make ash (fires) of the nashaq (weapons) and nashaq (burn) them, both the magan (shields) and the tzanah (bucklers), the qashath (bows) and the chatz (arrows), and the war clubs, and the spears, and they shall make ash (fires) of them shabai (seven) Shanah;

so that they shall nashaa (take) no itz (wood) out of the shadah (field), neither cut down any out of the Yair; for they shall make ash (fires) of the nashaq (weapons); and they shall plunder those who plundered them, and rob those who robbed them, says the Adanay Yahawah.

It shall happen in that yawam (day), that I will nathan (give) to Gawag a place for burial in Yasharaal (Israel), the Gayaa of those who ibar (pass) through on the east of the yam (sea); and it shall stop those who ibar (pass) through: and there shall they bury Gawag and all his multitude; and they shall qaraa (call) it The Gayaa Hamawanagawag Hamon Gog.
shabai (seven) chadash (months) shall the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) be burying them, that they may tahar (cleanse) the aratz (land).
Yes, all the im (people) of the aratz (land) shall bury them; and it shall be to them a sham (renown) in the yawam (day) that I shall be glorified, says the Adanay Yahawah.

They shall set apart men of continual employment, who shall ibar (pass) through the aratz (land), and, with those who ibar (pass) through, those who bury those who yathar (remain) on the surface of the aratz (land), to tahar (cleanse) it: after the end of shabai (seven) chadash (months) shall they search.

Those who ibar (pass) through the aratz (land) shall ibar (pass) through; and when any raah (see) a adam (man's) itzam (bone), then shall he banah (set) up a tzayawan (sign) by it, until the undertakers have buried it in the Gayaa Hamawanagawag Hamon Gog.
Hamawanah shall also be the sham (name) of a Iyar. Thus shall they tahar (cleanse) the aratz (land).

You, ban (son) of adam (man), thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: amar (speak) to the birds of every sort, and to every animal of the shadah (field), Assemble yourselves, and bawaa (come); asap (gather) yourselves on every side to my zabach (sacrifice) that I do zabach (sacrifice) for you, even a gadawal (great) zabach (sacrifice) on the har (mountains) of Yasharaal (Israel), that you may akal (eat) flesh and drink dam (blood).

You shall akal (eat) the flesh of the gabawar (mighty), and drink the dam (blood) of the nashayaa (princes) of the aratz (earth), of ayal (rams), of lambs, and of goats, of bulls, all of them fatlings of Bashan.
You shall akal (eat) fat until you be full, and drink dam (blood) until you are drunk, of my zabach (sacrifice) which I have sacrificed for you.
You shall be filled at my table with horses and chariots, with gabawar (mighty) men, and with all men of war, says the Adanay Yahawah.

I will nathan (set) my kabawad (glory) among the gawayam (nations); and all the gawayam (nations) shall raah (see) my mashapat (judgment) that I have executed, and my yad (hand) that I have laid on them.
So the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah their Alahayam, from that yawam (day) and forward.

The gawayam (nations) shall yadai (know) that the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) went into captivity for their iwan (iniquity); because they trespassed against me, and I hid my panayam (face) from them: so I gave them into the yad (hand) of their tzar (adversaries), and they napal (fell) all of them by the charab (sword).
According to their tamaah (uncleanness) and according to their pashai (transgressions) did I to them; and I hid my panayam (face) from them.

Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: Now will I shawab (turn back / repent) back the captivity of Yaiqab, and have racham (mercy) on the whole bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); and I will be jealous for my qadash (holy) sham (name).

They shall nashaa (bear) their kalamah (shame), and all their trespasses by which they have trespassed against me, when they shall yashab (dwell) securely in their adamah (land), and none shall make them afraid;

when I have brought them shawab (turn back / repent) from the im (peoples), and gathered them out of their ayab (enemies)' aratz (lands), and am sanctified in them in the iyan (sight) of many gawayam (nations).

They shall yadai (know) that I am Yahawah their Alahayam, in that I caused them to galah (go) into captivity among the gawayam (nations), and have gathered them to their own adamah (land); and I will yathar (leave) none of them any more there;
neither will I hide my panayam (face) any more from them; for I have poured out my rawach (spirit) on the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), says the Adanay Yahawah.

In the chamash (five) and isharayam (twentieth) Shanah of our captivity, in the raash (beginning) of the Shanah, in the tenth day of the chadash (month), in the fourteenth Shanah achar (after) that the Iyar was struck, in the same yawam (day), the yad (hand) of Yahawah was on me, and he brought me there.
In the visions of Alahayam brought he me into the aratz (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), and nawach (set) me down on a very Gabah har (mountain), whereon was as it were the frame of a Iyar on the Nagab.
He brought me there; and, behold, there was a ayash (man), whose appearance was like the appearance of brass, with a line of flax in his yad (hand), and a measuring reed; and he stood in the gate.

The ayash (man) said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), raah (see) with your iyan (eyes), and hear with your ears, and shawam (set) your lab (heart) on all that I shall show you; for, to the intent that I may show them to you, you are brought here: nagad (declare) all that you raah (see) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Behold, a wall on the outside of the bayath (house) all around, and in the ayash (man's) yad (hand) a measuring reed shash (six) amah (cubits) long, of a amah (cubit) and a tapach (handbreadth) each: so he measured the thickness of the building, one reed; and the height, one reed.

Then came he to the gate which panayam (looks) darak (toward) the qadayam (east), and went up its steps: and he measured the threshold of the gate, one reed broad; and the other threshold, one reed broad.

Every lodge was one reed arak (long), and one reed broad; and the space between the lodges was chamash (five) amah (cubits); and the threshold of the gate by the porch of the gate toward the house was one reed.
He measured also the porch of the gate toward the house, one reed.
Then measured he the porch of the gate, shamanah (eight) amah (cubits); and its ayal (posts), shanayam (two) amah (cubits); and the porch of the gate was toward the bayath (house).

The lodges of the gate darak (eastward) were shalawash (three) on this side, and shalawash (three) on that side; they shalawash (three) were of one measure: and the ayal (posts) had one measure on this side and on that side.
He measured the breadth of the opening of the gate, ishar (ten) amah (cubits); and the arak (length) of the gate, thirteen amah (cubits);

and a border panayam (before) the lodges, one amah (cubit) on this side, and a border, one amah (cubit) on that side; and the lodges, shash (six) amah (cubits) on this side, and shash (six) amah (cubits) on that side.
He measured the gate from the roof of the thaa (one) lodge to the roof of the other, a breadth of isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits); door against door.
He made also ayal (posts), shashayam (sixty) amah (cubits); and the court reached to the ayal (posts), around the gate.
From the panayam (forefront) of the gate at the entrance to the panayam (forefront) Panayamay the inner porch of the gate were chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits).
There were closed windows to the lodges, and to their ayal (posts) within the gate all around, and likewise to the arches; and windows were around inward; and on each ayal (post) were palm trees.
Then brought he me into the Chayatzawan court; and behold, there were rooms and a pavement, made for the court all around: shalawashayam (thirty) rooms were on the pavement.
The pavement was by the side of the gates, answerable to the arak (length) of the gates, even the Thachathawan pavement.

Then he measured the breadth from the panayam (forefront) of the Thachathawan gate to the panayam (forefront) Panayamay the inner court outside, one maah (hundred) amah (cubits), both on the qadayam (east) and on the tzapawan (north).
The gate of the Chayatzawan court whose prospect is darak (toward) the tzapawan (north), he measured its arak (length) and its breadth.

The lodges of it were shalawash (three) on this side and shalawash (three) on that side; and its ayal (posts) and its arches were after the measure of the raashawan (first) gate: its arak (length) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), and the breadth twenty - five amah (cubits).

The windows of it, and its arches, and the palm trees of it, were after the measure of the gate whose prospect is darak (toward) the qadayam (east); and they went up to it by shabai (seven) steps; and its arches were panayam (before) them.
There was a gate Panayamay the inner court over against the other gate, both on the tzapawan (north) and on the qadayam (east); and he measured from gate to gate one maah (hundred) amah (cubits).
He led me darak (toward) the south; and behold, a gate darak (toward) the south: and he measured its ayal (posts) and its arches according to these measures.
There were windows in it and in its arches all around, like those windows: the arak (length) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), and the breadth isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits).
There were shabai (seven) steps to ilah (go) up to it, and its arches were panayam (before) them; and it had palm trees, one on this side, and another on that side, on its ayal (posts).
There was a gate Panayamay the inner court darak (toward) the south: and he measured from gate to gate darak (toward) the south a maah (hundred) amah (cubits).
Then he brought me Panayamay the inner court by the south gate: and he measured the south gate according to these measures;

and its lodges, and its ayal (posts), and its arches, according to these measures: and there were windows in it and in its arches all around; it was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits) arak (long), and isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits) broad.
There were arches all around, isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits) arak (long), and chamash (five) amah (cubits) broad.
The arches of it were toward the Chayatzawan court; and palm trees were on its ayal (posts): and the ascent to it had shamanah (eight) steps.
He brought me Panayamay the inner court darak (toward) the qadayam (east): and he measured the gate according to these measures;

and its lodges, and its ayal (posts), and its arches, according to these measures: and there were windows therein and in its arches all around; it was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits) arak (long), and isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits) broad.
The arches of it were toward the Chayatzawan court; and palm trees were on its ayal (posts), on this side, and on that side: and the ascent to it had shamanah (eight) steps.
He brought me to the tzapawan (north) gate: and he measured it according to these measures;

its lodges, its ayal (posts), and its arches: and there were windows therein all around; the arak (length) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits), and the breadth isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) amah (cubits).
The ayal (posts) of it were toward the Chayatzawan court; and palm trees were on its ayal (posts), on this side, and on that side: and the ascent to it had shamanah (eight) steps.
A room with its door was by the ayal (posts) at the gates; there they washed the burnt ilah (offering).

In the porch of the gate were shanayam (two) tables on this side, and shalachan (two) tables on that side, to kill thereon the burnt ilah (offering) and the chataah (sin) offering and the asham (trespass) offering.

On the kathap (one) side outside, as one goes up to the entry of the gate toward the tzapawan (north), were shanayam (two) tables; and on the other side, which belonged to the porch of the gate, were shanayam (two) tables.
arabai (four) tables were on this side, and arabai (four) tables on that side, by the side of the gate; shamanah (eight) tables, whereupon they killed the shachat (sacrifices).

There were arabai (four) tables for the burnt ilah (offering), of cut aban (stone), a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) arak (long), and a amah (cubit) and a chatzay (half) broad, and one amah (cubit) high; whereupon they laid the instruments with which they killed the burnt ilah (offering) and the zabach (sacrifice).
The hooks, a tapach (handbreadth) long, were fastened bayath (within) all around: and on the tables was the flesh of the qaraban (offering).

Outside Panayamay the inner gate were rooms for the singers Panayamay the inner court, which was at the side of the tzapawan (north) gate; and their prospect was darak (toward) the south; one at the side of the qadayam (east) gate having the prospect darak (toward) the tzapawan (north).
He said to me, This room, whose prospect is darak (toward) the south, is for the kahan (priests), the keepers of the duty of the bayath (house);

and the room whose prospect is darak (toward) the tzapawan (north) is for the kahan (priests), the keepers of the duty of the mazabach (altar): these are the ban (sons) of Tzadawaq, who from among the ban (sons) of Laway Qarab near to Yahawah to sharath (minister) to him.
He measured the court, one maah (hundred) amah (cubits) arak (long), and a maah (hundred) amah (cubits) broad, foursquare; and the mazabach (altar) was panayam (before) the bayath (house).

Then he brought me to the porch of the bayath (house), and measured each ayal (post) of the porch, chamash (five) amah (cubits) on this side, and chamash (five) amah (cubits) on that side: and the breadth of the gate was shalawash (three) amah (cubits) on this side, and shalawash (three) amah (cubits) on that side.

The arak (length) of the porch was isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits), and the breadth ishathay (eleven) amah (cubits); even by the steps by which they went up to it: and there were pillars by the ayal (posts), one on this side, and another on that side.

He brought me to the hayakal (temple), and measured the ayal (posts), shash (six) amah (cubits) broad on the pah (one) side, and shash (six) amah (cubits) broad on the other side, which was the breadth of the ahal (tent).

The breadth of the entrance was ishar (ten) amah (cubits); and the sides of the entrance were chamash (five) amah (cubits) on the one side, and chamash (five) amah (cubits) on the other side: and he measured its arak (length), arabaiyam (forty) amah (cubits), and the breadth, isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits).

Then went he inward, and measured each ayal (post) of the entrance, shanayam (two) amah (cubits); and the entrance, shash (six) amah (cubits); and the breadth of the entrance, shabai (seven) amah (cubits).

He measured its arak (length), isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits), and the breadth, isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits), panayam (before) the hayakal (temple): and he said to me, This is the most qadash (holy) place.
Then he measured the wall of the bayath (house), shash (six) amah (cubits); and the breadth of every side room, arabai (four) amah (cubits), all around the bayath (house) on every side.

The side rooms were in shalawash (three) stories, tzalai (one) over another, and shalawashayam (thirty) in paim (order); and they entered into the wall which belonged to the bayath (house) for the side rooms all around, that they might have achaz (hold) therein, and not have achaz (hold) in the wall of the bayath (house).

The side rooms were broader as they encompassed the mail (house) higher and higher; for the encompassing of the bayath (house) went higher and higher around the bayath (house): therefore the breadth of the bayath (house) continued upward; and so one went up from the Thachathawan Ilayawan to the highest by the Thayakawan room.
I saw also that the bayath (house) had a raised base all around: the foundations of the side rooms were a full reed of shash (six) great amah (cubits).

The thickness of the wall, which was for the side rooms, on the outside, was chamash (five) amah (cubits): and that which was left was the bayath (place) of the side rooms that belonged to the bayath (house).
Between the rooms was a breadth of isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits) around the bayath (house) on every side.

The doors of the side rooms were toward the yanach (place) that was left, one door darak (toward) the tzapawan (north), and another door toward the south: and the breadth of the place that was left was chamash (five) amah (cubits) all around.

The building that was panayam (before) the separate place at the side darak (toward) the yam (west) was shabaiyam (seventy) amah (cubits) broad; and the wall of the building was chamash (five) amah (cubits) thick all around, and its arak (length) thashaiyam (ninety) amah (cubits).
So he measured the bayath (house), one maah (hundred) amah (cubits) arak (long); and the separate place, and the building, with its walls, one maah (hundred) amah (cubits) arak (long);
also the breadth of the panayam (face) of the bayath (house), and of the separate place toward the qadayam (east), one maah (hundred) amah (cubits).

He measured the arak (length) of the building panayam (before) the separate place which was at its achar (back), and its galleries on the one side and on the other side, one maah (hundred) amah (cubits); and the Panayamay hayakal (temple), and the porches of the court;

the thresholds, and the closed windows, and the galleries around on their shalawash (three) stories, over against the threshold, with itz (wood) Shachayap all around, and from the aratz (ground) up to the windows, (now the windows were covered),
to the space above the door, Panayamay to the inner bayath (house), and outside, and by all the wall all around Panayamay and Chayatzawan, by measure.
It was made with karawab (cherubim) and palm trees; and a palm tree was between karawab (cherub) and karawab (cherub), and every karawab (cherub) had shanayam (two) panayam (faces);

so that there was the panayam (face) of a adam (man) toward the palm tree on the one side, and the panayam (face) of a young kapayar (lion) toward the palm tree on the other side. thus was it made through all the bayath (house) all around:
from the aratz (ground) to above the door were karawab (cherubim) and palm trees made: thus was the wall of the hayakal (temple).
As for the hayakal (temple), the door posts were squared; and as for the panayam (face) of the qadash (sanctuary), the appearance of it was as the appearance of the maraah (temple).

The mazabach (altar) was of itz (wood), shalawash (three) amah (cubits) Gabah, and its arak (length) shanayam (two) amah (cubits); and its corners, and its arak (length), and its walls, were of itz (wood): and he said to me, This is the table that is panayam (before) Yahawah.
The hayakal (temple) and the qadash (sanctuary) had shanayam (two) doors.
The doors had shanayam (two) leaves apiece, shanayam (two) turning leaves: shanayam (two) leaves for the one door, and shanayam (two) leaves for the other.

There were made on them, on the doors of the hayakal (temple), karawab (cherubim) and palm trees, like as were made on the walls; and there was a threshold of itz (wood) on the panayam (face) of the porch outside.
There were closed windows and palm trees on the kathap (one) side and on the other side, on the sides of the porch: thus were the side rooms of the bayath (house), and the thresholds.

Then he brought me yatzaa (forth) into the Chayatzawan court, the darak (way) toward the tzapawan (north): and he brought me into the room that was over against the separate place, and which was over against the building toward the tzapawan (north).
panayam (before) the arak (length) of one maah (hundred) amah (cubits) was the tzapawan (north) door, and the breadth was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits).

Over against the isharayam (twenty) Panayamay which belonged to the inner court, and over against the pavement which belonged to the Chayatzawan court, was gallery panayam (against) gallery in the shalayashay (third) story.
panayam (before) the rooms was a walk of ishar (ten) amah (cubits)' breadth Panayamay, a darak (way) of one amah (cubit); and their doors were toward the tzapawan (north).
Now the Ilayawan rooms were shorter; for the galleries took away from these, more than from the Thachathawan and the Thayakawan, in the building.

For they were in shalash (three) stories, and they didn't have pillars as the pillars of the courts: therefore the uppermost was straitened more than the Thachathawan and the Thayakawan from the aratz (ground).
The wall that was outside by the side of the rooms, toward the Chayatzawan court panayam (before) the rooms, its arak (length) was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits).
For the arak (length) of the rooms that were in the Chayatzawan court was chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits): and behold, panayam (before) the hayakal (temple) were one maah (hundred) amah (cubits).
From under these rooms was the entry on the qadayam (east) side, as one goes into them from the Chayatzawan court.
In the thickness of the wall of the court darak (toward) the qadayam (east), panayam (before) the separate place, and panayam (before) the building, there were rooms.

The darak (way) panayam (before) them was like the appearance of the lashakah (way) of the rooms which were darak (toward) the tzapawan (north); according to their arak (length) so was their Kan: and all their exits were both according to their mashapat (fashions), and according to their doors.

According to the doors of the rooms that were darak (toward) the south was a door at the raash (head) of the darak (way), even the darak (way) directly panayam (before) the Gadarah darak (toward) the qadayam (east), as one bawaa (enters) into them.

Then he said to me, The tzapawan (north) rooms and the south rooms, which are panayam (before) the separate place, they are the qadash (holy) rooms, where the kahan (priests) who are qarawab (near) to Yahawah shall akal (eat) the most qadash (holy) things: there shall they yanach (lay) the most qadash (holy) things, and the meal manachah (offering), and the chataah (sin) offering, and the asham (trespass) offering; for the place is qadawash (holy).

When the kahan (priests) bawaa (enter) in, then shall they not bawaa (go) out of the qadash (holy) place into the Chayatzawan court, but there they shall yanach (lay) their bagad (garments) in which they sharath (minister); for they are qadash (holy): and they shall Labash on other bagad (garments), and shall qarab (approach) to that which pertains to the im (people).

Now when he had made an kalah (end) of measuring the Panayamay bayath (house), he brought me yatzaa (forth) by the darak (way) of the gate whose prospect is darak (toward) the qadayam (east), and measured it all around.
He measured on the qadayam (east) rawach (side) with the measuring reed chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds, with the measuring reed all around.
He measured on the tzapawan (north) rawach (side) chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds with the measuring reed all around.
He measured on the south rawach (side) chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds with the measuring reed.
He turned sabab (about) to the yam (west) rawach (side), and measured chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds with the measuring reed.

He measured it on the arabai (four) rawach (sides): it had a wall around it, the arak (length) chamash (five) maah (hundred), and the breadth chamash (five) maah (hundred), to make a separation between that which was qadash (holy) and that which was chal (common).
Afterward he brought me to the gate, even the gate that panah (looks) darak (toward) the qadayam (east).

Behold, the kabawad (glory) of the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel) came from the darak (way) of the qadayam (east): and his qawal (voice) was like the qawal (sound) of many mayam (waters); and the aratz (earth) shined with his kabawad (glory).

It was according to the appearance of the vision which I saw, even according to the vision that I saw when I came to shachath (destroy) the Iyar; and the visions were like the vision that I saw by the nahar (river) Kabar; and I napal (fell) on my panayam (face).
The kabawad (glory) of Yahawah came into the bayath (house) by the darak (way) of the gate whose prospect is darak (toward) the qadayam (east).
The rawach (spirit) took me up, and brought me Panayamay the inner court; and behold, the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah filled the bayath (house).
I heard one speaking to me out of the bayath (house); and a ayash (man) stood by me.

He said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), this is the place of my kasaa (throne), and the place of the kap (soles) of my feet, where I will shakan (dwell) in the midst of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) iwalam (forever). The bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) shall no more tamaa (defile) my qadash (holy) sham (name), neither they, nor their malak (kings), by their prostitution, and by the pagar (dead) bodies of their malak (kings) in their bamah (high) places;

in their setting of their threshold by my threshold, and their doorpost beside my doorpost, and there was but the wall between me and them; and they have defiled my qadash (holy) sham (name) by their thawaibah (abominations) which they have committed: therefore I have consumed them in my ap (anger).
Now let them rachaq (put) away their prostitution, and the pagar (dead) bodies of their malak (kings), rachaq (far) from me; and I will shakan (dwell) in their midst iwalam (forever).
You, ban (son) of adam (man), show the bayath (house) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), that they may be kalam (ashamed) of their iwan (iniquities); and let them measure the pattern.

If they be kalam (ashamed) of all that they have done, yadai (make) known to them the form of the bayath (house), and its fashion, and its exits, and its entrances, and all its forms, and all its chaqah (ordinances), and all its forms, and all its thawarah (laws); and kathab (write) it in their iyan (sight); that they may shamar (keep) the whole form of it, and all its chaqah (ordinances), and do them.

This is the thawarah (law) of the bayath (house): on the raash (top) of the har (mountain) the whole limit around it shall be most qadash (holy). Behold, this is the thawarah (law) of the bayath (house).

These are the measures of the mazabach (altar) by amah (cubits) (the amah (cubit) is a amah (cubit) and a tapach (handbreadth)): the bottom shall be a amah (cubit), and the tapach (breadth) a amah (cubit), and its border around its shapah (edge) a span; and this shall be the base of the mazabach (altar).

From the bottom on the aratz (ground) to the Thachathawan ledge shall be shanayam (two) amah (cubits), and the breadth one amah (cubit); and from the qatan (lesser) ledge to the greater ledge shall be arabai (four) amah (cubits), and the breadth a amah (cubit).
The upper araayal (altar) shall be arabai (four) amah (cubits); and from the araayal (altar) hearth and upward there shall be arabai (four) qaran (horns).
The araayal (altar) hearth shall be shanayam (twelve) cubits arak (long) by shanayam (twelve) broad, square in the arabai (four) rabai (sides) of it.

The ledge shall be fourteen cubits arak (long) by fourteen broad in the arabai (four) rabai (sides) of it; and the border about it shall be chatzay (half) a amah (cubit); and its bottom shall be a amah (cubit) around; and its steps shall panah (look) toward the qadayam (east).

He said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: These are the chaqah (ordinances) of the mazabach (altar) in the yawam (day) when they shall ishah (make) it, to ilah (offer) burnt ilah (offerings) thereon, and to sprinkle dam (blood) thereon.

You shall nathan (give) to the kahan (priests) the Lawayay (Levites) who are of the zarai (seed) of Tzadawaq, who are qarawab (near) to me, to sharath (minister) to me, says the Adanay Yahawah, a ban (young) bull for a chataah (sin) offering.

You shall take of its dam (blood), and nathan (put) it on the arabai (four) qaran (horns) of it, and on the arabai (four) corners of the ledge, and on the border all around: thus you shall chataa (cleanse) it and make kapar (atonement) for it.
You shall also take the bull of the chataah (sin) offering, and it shall be burnt in the mapaqad (appointed) place of the bayath (house), outside of the maqadash (sanctuary).

On the shanay (second) yawam (day) you shall qarab (offer) a Shaiyar goat thamayam (without) blemish for a chataah (sin) offering; and they shall chataa (cleanse) the mazabach (altar), as they cleansed it with the bull.
When you have finished cleansing it, you shall qarab (offer) a ban (young) bull thamayam (without) blemish, and a ayal (ram) out of the flock thamayam (without) blemish.
You shall qarab (bring) them near to Yahawah, and the kahan (priests) shall cast Malach on them, and they shall ilah (offer) them up for a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah.

shabai (seven) yawam (days) you shall ishah (prepare) every yawam (day) a Shaiyar for a chataah (sin) offering: they shall also ishah (prepare) a ban (young) bull, and a ayal (ram) out of the flock, thamayam (without) blemish.
shabai (seven) yawam (days) shall they make kapar (atonement) for the mazabach (altar) and purify it; so shall they malaa (consecrate) it.

When they have accomplished the yawam (days), it shall be that on the eighth yawam (day), and forward, the kahan (priests) shall ishah (make) your burnt ilah (offerings) on the mazabach (altar), and your shalam (peace) offerings; and I will accept you, says the Adanay Yahawah.
Then he brought me shawab (turn back / repent) by the darak (way) of the Chayatzawan gate of the maqadash (sanctuary), which panah (looks) toward the qadayam (east); and it was shut.

Yahawah said to me, This gate shall be shut; it shall not be opened, neither shall any ayash (man) bawaa (enter) in by it; for Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), has entered in by it; therefore it shall be shut.

As for the nashayaa (prince), he shall yashab (sit) therein as nashayaa (prince) to akal (eat) lacham (bread) panayam (before) Yahawah; he shall bawaa (enter) by the darak (way) of the porch of the gate, and shall yatzaa (go) out by the darak (way) of the same.

Then he brought me by the darak (way) of the tzapawan (north) gate panayam (before) the bayath (house); and I looked, and behold, the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah filled the bayath (house) of Yahawah: and I napal (fell) on my panayam (face).

Yahawah said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), shawam (mark) lab (well), and raah (see) with your iyan (eyes), and hear with your ears all that I dabar (tell) you concerning all the chaqah (ordinances) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and all its thawarah (laws); and shawam (mark) lab (well) the entrance of the bayath (house), with every exit of the maqadash (sanctuary).

You shall amar (tell) the rebellious, even to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: you bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), let it rab (suffice) you of all your thawaibah (abominations),

in that you have brought in foreigners, Iral in lab (heart) and Iral in flesh, to be in my maqadash (sanctuary), to chalal (profane) it, even my bayath (house), when you qarab (offer) my lacham (bread), the fat and the dam (blood), and they have broken my barayath (covenant), to add to all your thawaibah (abominations).
You have not performed the duty of my qadash (holy) things; but you have shawam (set) performers of my duty in my maqadash (sanctuary) for yourselves.

Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah, No foreigner, Iral in lab (heart) and Iral in flesh, shall bawaa (enter) into my maqadash (sanctuary), of any foreigners who are among the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

Lawayay the Levites who went rachaq (far) from me, when Yasharaal (Israel) went thaih (astray), who went thaih (astray) from me achar (after) their idols, they shall nashaa (bear) their iwan (iniquity).

Yet they shall be sharath (ministers) in my maqadash (sanctuary), having oversight at the gates of the bayath (house), and ministering in the bayath (house): they shall kill the burnt ilah (offering) and the zabach (sacrifice) for the im (people), and they shall imad (stand) panayam (before) them to sharath (minister) to them.

Because they ministered to them panayam (before) their idols, and became a stumbling block of iwan (iniquity) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel); therefore have I lifted up my yad (hand) against them, says the Adanay Yahawah, and they shall nashaa (bear) their iwan (iniquity).

They shall not come near to me, to execute the office of kahan (priest) to me, nor to come near to any of my qadash (holy) things, to the things that are most qadash (holy); but they shall nashaa (bear) their kalamah (shame), and their thawaibah (abominations) which they have committed.
Yet will I nathan (make) them performers of the duty of the bayath (house), for all its ibadah (service), and for all that shall be done therein.

But the kahan (priests) the Lawayay (Levites), the ban (sons) of Tzadawaq, who performed the duty of my maqadash (sanctuary) when the children of Yasharaal (Israel) went thaih (astray) from me, they shall qarab (come) near to me to sharath (minister) to me; and they shall imad (stand) panayam (before) me to qarab (offer) to me the fat and the dam (blood), says the Adanay Yahawah:
they shall bawaa (enter) into my maqadash (sanctuary), and they shall qarab (come) near to my table, to sharath (minister) to me, and they shall shamar (keep) my instruction.

It shall be that, when they bawaa (enter) in at the gates Panayamay the inner court, they shall be Labash with linen bagad (garments); and no wool shall ilah (come) on them, while they sharath (minister) in the gates Panayamay the inner court, and bayath (within).
They shall have linen tires on their raash (heads), and shall have linen breeches on their waists; they shall not clothe themselves with anything that causes sweat.

When they yatzaa (go) forth into the Chayatzawan court, even into the Chayatzawan court to the im (people), they shall put off their bagad (garments) in which they sharath (minister), and yanach (lay) them in the qadash (holy) rooms; and they shall Labash on other bagad (garments), that they not qadash (sanctify) the im (people) with their bagad (garments).
Neither shall they shave their raash (heads), nor allow their locks to shalach (grow) long; they shall only cut off the hair of their raash (heads).
Neither shall any of the kahan (priests) drink yayan (wine), when they bawaa (enter) Panayamay the inner court.

Neither shall they take for their wives a alamanah (widow), nor her who is put away; but they shall take virgins of the zarai (seed) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), or a alamanah (widow) who is the widow of a kahan (priest).
They shall teach my im (people) the difference between the qadash (holy) and the chal (common), and yadai (cause) them to discern between the tamaa (unclean) and the tahawar (clean).

In a rayab (controversy) they shall imad (stand) to shapat (judge); according to my ordinances shall they shapat (judge) it: and they shall shamar (keep) my thawarah (laws) and my chaqah (statutes) in all my mawaid (appointed) feasts; and they shall make my shabath (sabbaths) qadash (holy).

They shall bawaa (go) in to no mawath (dead) adam (person) to tamaa (defile) themselves; but for ab (father), or for am (mother), or for ban (son), or for bath (daughter), for ach (brother), or for achawath (sister) who has had no ayash (husband), they may tamaa (defile) themselves.
achar (after) he is cleansed, they shall reckon to him shabai (seven) yawam (days).

In the yawam (day) that he goes into the qadash (sanctuary), Panayamay the inner court, to sharath (minister) in the qadash (sanctuary), he shall qarab (offer) his chataah (sin) offering, says the Adanay Yahawah.
They shall have an nachalah (inheritance): I am their nachalah (inheritance); and you shall nathan (give) them no achazah (possession) in Yasharaal (Israel); I am their achazah (possession).
They shall akal (eat) the meal manachah (offering), and the chataah (sin) offering, and the asham (trespass) offering; and every charam (devoted) thing in Yasharaal (Israel) shall be theirs.

The raashayath (first) of all the bakawar (first) fruits of every thing, and every tharawamah (offering) of everything, of all your tharawamah (offerings), shall be for the kahan (priest): you shall also nathan (give) to the kahan (priests) the raashayath (first) of your dough, to cause a barakah (blessing) to nawach (rest) on your bayath (house).
The kahan (priests) shall not akal (eat) of anything that dies of nabalah (itself), or is torn, whether it be bird or animal.

Moreover, when you shall napal (divide) by lot the aratz (land) for nachalah (inheritance), you shall offer an tharawamah (offering) to Yahawah, a qadash (holy) portion of the aratz (land); the arak (length) shall be the arak (length) of isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) reeds, and the breadth shall be ishar (ten) alap (thousand): it shall be qadash (holy) in all its border all around.

Of this there shall be for the qadash (holy) place chamash (five) maah (hundred) in length by chamash (five) maah (hundred) in breadth, square all around; and chamashayam (fifty) amah (cubits) for its suburbs all around.

Of this measure you shall measure a arak (length) of isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand), and a breadth of ishar (ten) alap (thousand): and in it shall be the maqadash (sanctuary), which is most qadash (holy).

It is a qadash (holy) portion of the aratz (land); it shall be for the kahan (priests), the sharath (ministers) of the maqadash (sanctuary), who Qarab near to sharath (minister) to Yahawah; and it shall be a place for their bayath (houses), and a maqadash (holy) place for the maqadash (sanctuary).

isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) in arak (length), and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) in breadth, shall be Lawayay the Levites, the sharath (ministers) of the bayath (house), for a achazah (possession) to themselves, for isharayam (twenty) rooms.

You shall nathan (appoint) the achazah (possession) of the Iyar chamash (five) alap (thousand) broad, and isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) arak (long), side by side with the tharawamah (offering) of the qadash (holy) portion: it shall be for the whole bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Whatever is for the nashayaa (prince) shall be on the one side and on the other side of the qadash (holy) tharawamah (offering) and of the achazah (possession) of the Iyar, in panayam (front) of the qadash (holy) tharawamah (offering) and in panayam (front) of the achazah (possession) of the Iyar, on the yam (west) side westward, and on the qadam (east) side eastward; and in arak (length) answerable to one of the chalaq (portions), from the yam (west) border to the qadayam (east) border.

In the aratz (land) it shall be to him for a achazah (possession) in Yasharaal (Israel): and my nashayaa (princes) shall no more yanah (oppress) my im (people); but they shall nathan (give) the aratz (land) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) according to their shabat (tribes).

Thus says the Adanay Yahawah: Let it rab (suffice) you, nashayaa (princes) of Yasharaal (Israel): sawar (remove) violence and spoil, and ishah (execute) justice and tzadaqah (righteousness); dispossessing my im (people), amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah.
You shall have tzadaq (just) balances, and a tzadaq (just) ephah, and a tzadaq (just) bath.

The ephah and the bath shall be of one measure, that the bath may nashaa (contain) the maishar (tenth) part of a homer, and the ephah the ishayaray (tenth) part of a homer: its measure shall be after the homer.
The shekel shall be isharayam (twenty) gerahs. isharayam (twenty) shekels plus isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) shekels plus chamash (fifteen) shekels shall be your mina.
This is the tharawamah (offering) that you shall offer: the shashay (sixth) part of an ephah from a homer of wheat; and you shall give the shashah (sixth) part of an ephah from a homer of barley;

and the chaq (set) portion of shaman (oil), of the bath of shaman (oil), the maishar (tenth) part of a bath out of the cor, which is ishar (ten) baths, even a homer; (for ishar (ten) baths are a homer;)

and one lamb of the flock, out of two maah (hundred), from the well-watered pastures Yasharaal Israel—for a meal manachah (offering), and for a burnt ilah (offering), and for shalam (peace) offerings, to make kapar (atonement) for them, says the Adanay Yahawah.
All the im (people) of the aratz (land) shall give to this tharawamah (offering) for the nashayaa (prince) in Yasharaal (Israel).

It shall be the nashayaa (prince's) part to give the burnt ilah (offerings), and the meal manachah (offerings), and the drink nasak (offerings), in the chag (feasts), and on the new chadash (moons), and on the shabath (sabbaths), in all the mawaid (appointed) feasts of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel): he shall ishah (prepare) the sin manachah (offering), and the meal ilah (offering), and the burnt ilah (offering), and the shalam (peace) offerings, to make kapar (atonement) for the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).

Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: In the raashawan (first) month, in the achad (first) day of the chadash (month), you shall take a ban (young) bull thamayam (without) blemish; and you shall chataa (cleanse) the maqadash (sanctuary).

The kahan (priest) shall take of the dam (blood) of the chataah (sin) offering, and nathan (put) it on the door posts of the bayath (house), and on the arabai (four) corners of the ledge of the mazabach (altar), and on the posts of the gate Panayamay the inner court.
So you shall do on the seventh day of the chadash (month) for everyone who shagah (errs), and for him who is Pathay: so you shall make kapar (atonement) for the bayath (house).

In the raashawan (first) month, in the fourteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month), you shall have the pasach (passover), a chag (feast) of shabawai (seven) yawam (days); unleavened matzah (bread) shall be eaten.
