On that yawam (day) shall the nashayaa (prince) ishah (prepare) for himself and for all the im (people) of the aratz (land) a bull for a chataah (sin) offering.

The shabai (seven) yawam (days) of the chag (feast) he shall ishah (prepare) a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah, shabai (seven) bulls and shabai (seven) ayal (rams) thamayam (without) blemish yawam (daily) the shabai (seven) yawam (days); and a Shaiyar Shaiyar yawam (daily) for a chataah (sin) offering.
He shall ishah (prepare) a meal manachah (offering), an ephah for a bull, and an ephah for a ayal (ram), and a hin of shaman (oil) to an ephah.

In the seventh month, in the fifteenth yawam (day) of the chadash (month), in the chag (feast), shall he do the like the seven yawam (days); according to the chataah (sin) offering, according to the burnt ilah (offering), and according to the meal manachah (offering), and according to the shaman (oil).

Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: The gate Panayamay the inner court that panah (looks) toward the qadayam (east) shall be shut the shash (six) working yawam (days); but on the shabath (sabbath) day it shall be opened, and on the yawam (day) of the new chadash (moon) it shall be opened.

The nashayaa (prince) shall bawaa (enter) by the darak (way) of the porch of the gate outside, and shall imad (stand) by the post of the gate; and the kahan (priests) shall ishah (prepare) his burnt ilah (offering) and his shalam (peace) offerings, and he shall shachah (worship) at the threshold of the gate: then he shall yatzaa (go) forth; but the gate shall not be shut until the evening.
The im (people) of the aratz (land) shall shachah (worship) at the door of that gate panayam (before) Yahawah on the shabath (sabbaths) and on the new chadash (moons).

The burnt ilah (offering) that the nashayaa (prince) shall qarab (offer) to Yahawah shall be on the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day) shash (six) lambs thamayam (without) blemish and a ayal (ram) thamayam (without) blemish;
and the meal manachah (offering) shall be an ephah for the ayal (ram), and the meal manachah (offering) for the lambs as he is yad (able) to give, and a hin of shaman (oil) to an ephah.
On the yawam (day) of the new chadash (moon) it shall be a ban (young) bull thamayam (without) blemish, and shash (six) lambs, and a ayal (ram); they shall be thamayam (without) blemish:
and he shall ishah (prepare) a meal manachah (offering), an ephah for the bull, and an ephah for the ayal (ram), and for the lambs according as he is able, and a hin of shaman (oil) to an ephah.
When the nashayaa (prince) shall bawaa (enter), he shall bawaa (go) in by the darak (way) of the porch of the gate, and he shall yatzaa (go) forth by its darak (way).

But when the im (people) of the aratz (land) shall bawaa (come) panayam (before) Yahawah in the mawaid (appointed) feasts, he who bawaa (enters) by the darak (way) of the tzapawan (north) gate to shachah (worship) shall yatzaa (go) forth by the darak (way) of the Nagab gate; and he who bawaa (enters) by the darak (way) of the Nagab gate shall yatzaa (go) forth by the darak (way) of the tzapawan (north) gate: he shall not shawab (turn back / repent) by the darak (way) of the gate by which he came in, but shall yatzaa (go) forth nakach (straight) before him.
The nashayaa (prince), when they bawaa (go) in, shall bawaa (go) in with of them; and when they yatzaa (go) out, he shall yatzaa (go) out.

In the chag (feasts) and in the mawaid (solemnities) the meal manachah (offering) shall be an ephah for a bull, and an ephah for a ayal (ram), and for the lambs as he is yad (able) to give, and a hin of shaman (oil) to an ephah.

When the nashayaa (prince) shall ishah (prepare) a nadabah (freewill) ilah (offering), a burnt ilah (offering) or shalam (peace) offerings as a freewill nadabah (offering) to Yahawah, one shall pathach (open) for him the gate that panah (looks) toward the qadayam (east); and he shall ishah (prepare) his burnt ilah (offering) and his shalam (peace) offerings, as he does on the shabath (sabbath) yawam (day): then he shall yatzaa (go) forth; and achar (after) his yatzaa (going) forth sagar (one) shall shut the gate.
You shall ishah (prepare) a lamb a Shanah old thamayam (without) blemish for a burnt ilah (offering) to Yahawah yawam (daily): baqar (morning) by baqar (morning) you shall ishah (prepare) it.

You shall ishah (prepare) a meal manachah (offering) with it baqar (morning) by baqar (morning), the shashay (sixth) part of an ephah, and the shalayashay (third) part of a hin of shaman (oil), to moisten the fine flour; a meal manachah (offering) to Yahawah continually by a perpetual chaqah (ordinance).
Thus shall they ishah (prepare) the lamb, and the meal manachah (offering), and the shaman (oil), baqar (morning) by morning, for a continual burnt ilah (offering).

Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: If the nashayaa (prince) nathan (give) a mathanah (gift) to any of his ban (sons), it is his nachalah (inheritance), it shall belong to his ban (sons); it is their achazah (possession) by nachalah (inheritance).

But if he nathan (give) of his nachalah (inheritance) a mathanah (gift) to one of his ibad (servants), it shall be his to the Shanah of liberty; then it shall shawab (turn back / repent) to the nashayaa (prince); but as for his nachalah (inheritance), it shall be for his ban (sons).

Moreover the nashayaa (prince) shall not take of the im (people's) nachalah (inheritance), to thrust them out of their achazah (possession); he shall give nachal (inheritance) to his ban (sons) out of his own achazah (possession), that my im (people) not be scattered every ayash (man) from his achazah (possession).

Then he brought me through the entry, which was at the side of the gate, into the qadash (holy) rooms for the kahan (priests), which looked toward the tzapawan (north): and behold, there was a place on the hinder part westward.

He said to me, This is the place where the kahan (priests) shall boil the asham (trespass) offering and the chataah (sin) offering, and where they shall bake the meal manachah (offering); that they not yatzaa (bring) them forth into the Chayatzawan court, to qadash (sanctify) the im (people).
Then he brought me yatzaa (forth) into the Chayatzawan court, and caused me to ibar (pass) by the arabai (four) corners of the court; and behold, in every corner of the court there was a court.
In the arabai (four) corners of the court there were courts enclosed, arabaiyam (forty) cubits arak (long) and shalawashayam (thirty) broad: these arabai (four) in the corners were of one measure.
There was a wall around in them, around the arabai (four), and boiling places were made under the walls all around.
Then he said to me, These are the boiling bayath (houses), where the sharath (ministers) of the bayath (house) shall boil the zabach (sacrifice) of the im (people).

He brought me shawab (turn back / repent) to the door of the bayath (house); and behold, mayam (waters) issued out from under the threshold of the bayath (house) eastward; (for the panayam (forefront) of the bayath (house) was toward the qadayam (east);) and the mayam (waters) came down from under, from the Yamanay side of the bayath (house), on the Nagab of the mazabach (altar).

Then he brought me out by the darak (way) of the gate northward, and led me round by the darak (way) outside to the outer gate, by the darak (way) of the gate that panah (looks) toward the qadayam (east); and behold, there ran out mayam (waters) on the Yamanay side.

When the ayash (man) went yatzaa (forth) eastward with the line in his yad (hand), he measured one alap (thousand) amah (cubits), and he caused me to ibar (pass) through the mayam (waters), mayam (waters) that were to the apas (ankles).

Again he measured one alap (thousand), and caused me to ibar (pass) through the mayam (waters), mayam (waters) that were to the knees. Again he measured one alap (thousand), and caused me to ibar (pass) through the mayam (waters), mathan (waters) that were to the waist.

Afterward he measured one alap (thousand); and it was a nachal (river) that I could not ibar (pass) through; for the mayam (waters) were risen, mayam (waters) to swim in, a nachal (river) that could not be passed ibar (through).
He said to me, ban (son) of adam (man), have you seen this? Then he brought me, and caused me to shawab (turn back / repent) to the shapah (bank) of the nachal (river).
Now when I had returned, behold, on the shapah (bank) of the nachal (river) were very many itz (trees) on the one side and on the other.

Then he said to me, These mayam (waters) yatzaa (issue) forth Qadamawan the eastern region, and shall bawaa (go) down into the irabah (arabah); and they shall go toward the yam (sea); into the yam (sea) shall the waters yatzaa (go) which were made to issue forth; and the mayam (waters) shall be healed.

It shall happen, that every living napash (creature) which swarms, in every place where the nachal (rivers) bawaa (come), shall chayah (live); and there shall be a very rab (great) multitude of fish; for these mayam (waters) have bawaa (come) there, and the waters of the sea shall be healed, and everything shall chayay (live) wherever the nachal (river) bawaa (comes).

It shall happen, that fishermen shall imad (stand) by it: from Iyanagaday Gedi even to Iyanaigalayam Eglaim shall be a place for the spreading of charam (nets); their fish shall be after their kinds, as the fish of the gadawal (great) yam (sea), maad (exceeding) many.
But the miry places of it, and its marshes, shall not be healed; they shall be given up to Malach.

By the nachal (river) on its shapah (bank), on this side and on that side, shall ilah (grow) every itz (tree) for food, whose leaf shall not wither, neither shall its fruit thamam (fail): it shall bakar (bring) forth new fruit every chadash (month), because its mayam (waters) yatzaa (issue) out of the maqadash (sanctuary); and its fruit shall be for food, and its leaf for healing.

Thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: This shall be the border, by which you shall divide the aratz (land) for nachal (inheritance) according to the shanayam (twelve) shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel): Yawasap shall have chabal (two) portions.
You shall nachal (inherit) it, one as well as ach (another); for I swore to nathan (give) it to your abawath (fathers): and this aratz (land) shall napal (fall) to you for nachalah (inheritance).
This shall be the border of the aratz (land): On the tzapawan (north) side, from the gadawal (great) yam (sea), by the darak (way) of Chathalan, to the entrance of Tzadad;
Chamath, Barawathah, Sabarayam, which is between the border of Damashaq and the border of Chamath; Hazer Chatzarahathayakawan, which is by the border of Chawaran.
The border from the yam (sea), shall be Chatzaraiyanawan Enon at the border of Damashaq; and on the tzapawan (north) northward is the border of Chamath. This is the tzapawan (north) side.

The qadayam (east) side, between Chawaran and Damashaq and Galaid, and the aratz (land) of Yasharaal (Israel), shall be the Yaradan; from the north border to the Qadamawanay yam (sea) you shall measure. This is the qadayam (east) side.

The Nagab side southward shall be from Thamar as far as the mayam (waters) Marayabah Meriboth Qadash, to the nachal (brook) of Egypt, to the gadawal (great) yam (sea). This is the thayaman (south) side Nagab.
The yam (west) side shall be the gadawal (great) yam (sea), from the south border as far as over against the entrance of Chamath. This is the yam (west) side.
So you shall divide this aratz (land) to you according to the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel).

It shall happen, that you shall napal (divide) it by lot for an nachalah (inheritance) to you and to the aliens who live among you, who shall father children among you; and they shall be to you as the native - born among the children of Yasharaal (Israel); they shall have nachalah (inheritance) with you among the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel).
It shall happen, that in what shabat (tribe) the stranger lives, there you shall nathan (give) him his nachalah (inheritance), says the Adanay Yahawah.

Now these are the sham (names) of the shabat (tribes): From the tzapawan (north) end, yad (beside) the darak (way) of Chathalan to the entrance of Chamath, Chatzaraiyanan Enan at the border of Damashaq, northward yad (beside) Chamath, (and they shall have their sides qadayam (east) and yam (west)), Dan, one portion.
By the border Dan Dan, from the qadayam (east) side to the yam (west) side, Ashar, one portion.
By the border of Ashar, from the qadayam (east) side even to the yam (west) side, Napathalay, one portion.
By the border of Napathalay, from the qadayam (east) side to the yam (west) side, Manashah, one portion.
By the border of Manashah, from the qadayam (east) side to the yam (west) side, Aparayam, one portion.
By the border of Aparayam, from the qadayam (east) side even to the yam (west) side, Raawaban, one portion.
By the border of Raawaban, from the qadayam (east) side to the yam (west) side, Yahawadah (Judah), one portion.

By the border of Yahawadah (Judah), from the qadayam (east) side to the yam (west) side, shall be the tharawamah (offering) which you shall offer, twenty - five alap (thousand) reeds in breadth, and in arak (length) as one of the chalaq (portions), from the qadayam (east) side to the yam (west) side: and the maqadash (sanctuary) shall be in its midst.
The tharawamah (offering) that you shall offer to Yahawah shall be isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) reeds in arak (length), and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) in breadth.

For these, even for the kahan (priests), shall be the qadash (holy) tharawamah (offering): toward the tzapawan (north) isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) in length, and toward the yam (west) ishar (ten) alap (thousand) in breadth, and toward the qadayam (east) ishar (ten) alap (thousand) in breadth, and toward the Nagab isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) in arak (length): and the maqadash (sanctuary) of Yahawah shall be in its midst.

It shall be for the kahan (priests) who are sanctified of the ban (sons) of Tzadawaq, who have kept my instruction, who didn't thaih (go) astray when the children of Yasharaal (Israel) went thaih (astray), as the Lawayay (Levites) went thaih (astray).
It shall be to them an tharawamayah (offering) from the tharawamah (offering) of the aratz (land), a thing most qadash (holy), by the border Lawayay the Levites.

Answerable to the border of the kahan (priests), the Lawayay (Levites) shall have isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) in arak (length), and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) in breadth: all the arak (length) shall be isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand), and the breadth ishar (ten) alap (thousand).
They shall sell none of it, nor exchange it, nor shall the raashayath (first) fruits of the aratz (land) be alienated; for it is qadash (holy) to Yahawah.

The chamash (five) alap (thousand) that are yathar (left) in the breadth, in panayam (front) of the isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand), shall be for chal (common) use, for the Iyar, for mawashab (dwelling) and for suburbs; and the Iyar shall be in its midst.

These shall be its measures: the tzapawan (north) side arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred), and the Nagab side arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred), and on the qadayam (east) side arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred), and the yam (west) side arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred).

The Iyar shall have suburbs: toward the tzapawan (north) two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty), and toward the Nagab two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty), and toward the qadayam (east) two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty), and toward the yam (west) two maah (hundred) chamashayam (fifty).

The remainder in the arak (length), answerable to the qadash (holy) tharawamah (offering), shall be ishar (ten) alap (thousand) eastward, and ishar (ten) alap (thousand) westward; and it shall be answerable to the qadash (holy) tharawamah (offering); and its increase shall be for lacham (food) to those who labor in the Iyar.
Those who labor in the Iyar, out of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), shall cultivate it.

All the tharawamah (offering) shall be isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) by isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand): you shall offer the qadash (holy) tharawamah (offering) rabayaiy (foursquare), with the achazah (possession) of the Iyar.

The yathar (residue) shall be for the nashayaa (prince), on the one side and on the other of the qadash (holy) tharawamah (offering) and of the achazah (possession) of the Iyar; in panayam (front) of the isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) of the tharawamah (offering) toward the qadayam (east) border, and westward in panayam (front) of the isharayam (twenty) - chamash (five) alap (thousand) toward the yam (west) border, answerable to the chalaq (portions), it shall be for the nashayaa (prince): and the qadash (holy) tharawamah (offering) and the maqadash (sanctuary) of the bayath (house) shall be in its midst.

Moreover from the achazah (possession) Lawayay the Levites, and from the achazah (possession) of the Iyar, being in the midst of that which is the nashayaa (prince's), between the border of Yahawadah (Judah) and the border of Banayamayan, it shall be for the nashayaa (prince).
As for the yathar (rest) of the shabat (tribes): from the qadayam (east) side to the yam (west) side, Banayamayan, one portion.
By the border of Banayamayan, from the qadayam (east) side to the yam (west) side, Shamaiwan, one portion.
By the border of Shamaiwan, from the qadayam (east) side to the yam (west) side, Yashashakar, one portion.
By the border of Yashashakar, from the qadayam (east) side to the yam (west) side, Zabawalawan, one portion.
By the border of Zabawalawan, from the qadayam (east) side to the yam (west) side, Gad, one portion.

By the border of Gad, at the Nagab side southward, the border shall be even from Thamar to the mayam (waters) Marayabah Meribath Qadash, to the nachal (brook) of Egypt, to the gadawal (great) yam (sea).
This is the aratz (land) which you shall napal (divide) by lot to the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) for nachalah (inheritance), and these are their several portions, says the Adanay Yahawah.
These are the exits of the Iyar: On the tzapawan (north) side arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds by measure;

and the gates of the Iyar shall be after the sham (names) of the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), shalawash (three) gates northward: the gate of Raawaban, one; the gate of Yahawadah (Judah), one; the gate of Laway, one.

At the qadayam (east) side arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds, and shalawash (three) gates: even the gate of Yawasap, one; the gate of Banayamayan, one; the gate Dan Dan, one.

At the Nagab side arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds by measure, and shalawash (three) gates: the gate of Shamaiwan, one; the gate of Yashashakar, one; the gate of Zabawalawan, one.

At the yam (west) side arabai (four) alap (thousand) and chamash (five) maah (hundred) reeds, with their shalawash (three) gates: the gate of Gad, one; the gate of Ashar, one; the gate of Napathalay, one.
It shall be eighteen alap (thousand) reeds around: and the sham (name) of the Iyar from that yawam (day) shall be, Yahawah is there.
In the shalawash (third) Shanah of the malakawath (reign) of Yahawayaqayam malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) came Nabawakadanaatzar malak (king) of Babal to Yarawashalam, and besieged it.

The Adanay gave Yahawayaqayam malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah) into his yad (hand), with part of the vessels of the bayath (house) of Alahayam; and he carried them into the aratz (land) of Shanair to the bayath (house) of his Alahayam: and he brought the vessels into the treasure bayath (house) of his Alahayam.

The malak (king) spoke to Ashapanaz the rab (master) of his eunuchs, that he should bawaa (bring) in certain of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), even of the zarai (seed) malawakah (royal) and of the paratham (nobles);

youths in whom was no blemish, but tawab (well) - favored, and shakal (skillful) in all chakamah (wisdom), and endowed with daith (knowledge), and bayan (understanding) madai (science), and such as had kach (ability) to imad (stand) in the malak (king's) hayakal (palace); and that he should teach them the learning and the lashawan (language) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans).

The malak (king) appointed for them a yawam (daily) dabar (portion) of the malak (king's) dainties, and of the yayan (wine) which he drank, and that they should be nourished shalawash (three) Shanah; that at its end they should imad (stand) panayam (before) the malak (king).
Now among these were, of the children of Yahawadah (Judah), Danayaal, Chananayah, Mayashaal, and Izarayah.

The shar (prince) of the eunuchs gave sham (names) to them: to Danayaal he gave the name of Balatashaatzar; and to Chananayah, of Shadarak; and to Mayashaal, Mayashak Meshach; and to Izarayah, of Ibadanagaw.

But Danayaal purposed in his lab (heart) that he would not defile himself with the malak (king's) dainties, nor with the yayan (wine) which he drank: therefore he requested of the shar (prince) of the eunuchs that he might not defile himself.
Now Alahayam made Danayaal to find chasad (kindness) and racham (compassion) in the panayam (sight) of the shar (prince) of the eunuchs.

The shar (prince) of the eunuchs said to Danayaal, I yaraa (fear) my Adawan the malak (king), who has appointed your food and your drink: for why should he raah (see) your panayam (faces) worse looking than the youths who are of your own age? so would you endanger my raash (head) with the malak (king).
Then Danayaal said to the steward whom the shar (prince) of the eunuchs had appointed over Danayaal, Chananayah, Mayashaal, and Izarayah:
Test your ibad (servants), I beg you, ishar (ten) yawam (days); and let them nathan (give) us vegetables to akal (eat), and mayam (water) to drink.

Then let our maraah (faces) be looked on panayam (before) you, and the maraah (face) of the youths who akal (eat) of the malak (king's) dainties; and as you raah (see), ishah (deal) with your ibad (servants).
So he listened to them in this dabar (matter), and proved them ishar (ten) yawam (days).
At the end of ishar (ten) yawam (days) their maraah (faces) raah (see) fairer, and they were Barayaa in flesh, than all the youths who ate of the malak (king's) dainties.
So the steward took nashaa (away) their dainties, and the yayan (wine) that they should drink, and gave them pulse.

Now as for these arabai (four) youths, Alahayam gave them madai (knowledge) and shakal (skill) in all learning and chakamah (wisdom): and Danayaal had bayan (understanding) in all visions and chalawam (dreams).
At the end of the yawam (days) which the malak (king) had appointed for bringing them in, the shar (prince) of the eunuchs brought them in panayam (before) Nabawakadanaatzar.
The malak (king) talked with them; and among them all was found none like Danayaal, Chananayah, Mayashaal, and Izarayah: therefore stood they panayam (before) the malak (king).

In every dabar (matter) of chakamah (wisdom) and bayanah (understanding), concerning which the malak (king) inquired of them, he found them ishar (ten) times better than all the magicians and enchanters who were in all his malakawath (realm).
Danayaal continued even to the achad (first) Shanah of malak (king) Kawarash.

In the shanayam (second) Shanah of the malakawath (reign) of Nabawakadanaatzar, Nabawakadanaatzar dreamed chalawam (dreams); and his rawach (spirit) was troubled, and his shanah (sleep) went from him.

Then the malak (king) commanded to qaraa (call) the magicians, and the enchanters, and the sorcerers, and the Kashaday (Chaldeans), to nagad (tell) the malak (king) his chalawam (dreams). So they came in and stood panayam (before) the malak (king).
The malak (king) said to them, I have dreamed a chalawam (dream), and my rawach (spirit) is troubled to yadai (know) the chalawam (dream).

Then spoke the Kashaday (Chaldeans) to the malak (king) in the Aramayath (Syrian) language, O malak (king), live ilam (forever): amar (tell) your ibad (servants) the dream, and we will show the interpretation.

The malak (king) answered the Kashaday (Chaldeans), The thing is Azad from me: if you don't make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you shall be ibad (cut) in pieces, and your bayath (houses) shall be made a dunghill.
But if you show the dream and its interpretation, you shall receive of me mathanaa (gifts) and rewards and Shagayaa honor: lahan (therefore) show me the dream and its interpretation.
They answered the Thanayanawath time and said, Let the malak (king) amar (tell) his ibad (servants) the dream, and we will show the interpretation.
The malak (king) answered, I know of a yatzayab (certainty) that you would gain Idan, because you see the thing is Azad from me.

But if you don't make known to me the dream, there is but hawaa (one) dath (law) for you; for you have prepared Kadab and corrupt malah (words) to amar (speak) Qadam me, until the Idan be changed: lahan (therefore) amar (tell) me the dream, and I shall know that you can show me its interpretation.

The Kashaday (Chaldeans) answered Qadam the malak (king), and said, There is not a anash (man) on the yabashath (earth) who can show the malak (king's) malah (matter), because no malak (king), Adawan, or shalayat (ruler), has asked such a thing of any magician, or enchanter, or Kashaday (Chaldean).
It is a Yaqayar thing that the malak (king) requires, and there is no Acharan who can show it Qadam the malak (king), lahan (except) the Alahayam, whose dwelling is not with flesh.
For this cause the malak (king) was angry and Shagayaa furious, and commanded to abad (destroy) all the wise men of Babal.
So the dath (decree) went forth, and the wise men were to be slain; and they sought Danayaal and his companions to be slain.
Then Danayaal returned thawab (answer) with itaa (counsel) and prudence to Arayawak the Rab Day the malak (king's) guard, who was gone forth to kill the wise men of Babal;
he answered Arayawak the malak (king's) shalayat (captain), Why is the dath (decree) so urgent from the malak (king)? Then Arayawak made the thing known to Danayaal.
Danayaal went in, and desired of the malak (king) that he would appoint him a time, and he would show the malak (king) the interpretation.
Then Danayaal went to his bayath (house), and made the thing known to Chananayah, Mayashaal, and Izarayah, his companions:

that they would desire racham (mercies) of the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven) concerning this secret; that Danayaal and his companions should not abad (perish) with the shaar (rest) of the wise men of Babal.
Then was the secret revealed to Danayaal in a vision of the layalayaa (night). Then Danayaal blessed the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven).
Danayaal answered, Blessed be the sham (name) of Alahayam id (forever) and ever; for chakamah (wisdom) and might are his.

He changes the Idan and the seasons; he idaa (removes) malak (kings), and qawam (sets) up malak (kings); he gives chakamah (wisdom) to the wise, and manadai (knowledge) to those who have understanding;
he reveals the Imayaq and sathar (secret) things; he knows what is in the chashawak (darkness), and the nahayar (light) dwells with him.

I thank you, and shabach (praise) you, you Alahayam of my abawath (fathers), who have given me chakamah (wisdom) and might, and have now made known to me what we desired of you; for you have made known to us the malak (king's) malah (matter).

Therefore Danayaal went in to Arayawak, whom the malak (king) had appointed to abad (destroy) the wise men of Babal; he went and said Kan to him: Don't abad (destroy) the wise men of Babal; bring me in Qadam the malak (king), and I will show to the malak (king) the interpretation.

Then Arayawak brought in Danayaal Qadam the malak (king) in haste, and said Kan to him, I have found a gabar (man) of the children of the captivity of Yahawad (Judah), who will make known to the malak (king) the interpretation.
The malak (king) answered Danayaal, whose sham (name) was Balatashaatzar, Are you able to make known to me the dream which I have seen, and its interpretation?
Danayaal answered Qadam the malak (king), and said, The secret which the malak (king) has demanded can neither wise men, enchanters, magicians, nor soothsayers, show to the malak (king);

but there is a Alahayam in shamayan (heaven) who reveals secrets, and he has made known to the malak (king) Nabawakadanatzar what shall be in the latter yawam (days). Your dream, and the visions of your raash (head) on your bed, are these:
as for you, O malak (king), your thoughts came into your il (mind) on your bed, what should happen hereafter; and he who reveals secrets has made known to you what shall happen.

But as for me, this secret is not revealed to me for any chakamah (wisdom) that I have more than any chay (living), but to the intent that the interpretation may be made known to the malak (king), and that you may know the thoughts of your labab (heart).
You, O malak (king), saw, and behold, a great tzalam (image). This tzalam (image), which was Rab, and whose brightness was Yathayar, stood before you; and its aspect was awesome.
As for this tzalam (image), its raash (head) was of tab (fine) gold, its breast and its arms of silver, its belly and its thighs of brass,
its legs of iron, its feet part of iron, and part of clay.
You saw until a aban (stone) was cut out without yad (hands), which struck the tzalam (image) on its feet that were of iron and clay, and broke them in pieces.

Then was the iron, the clay, the brass, the silver, and the gold, broken in pieces chad (together), and became like the chaff of the summer threshing floors; and the rawach (wind) carried them away, so that no place was found for them: and the aban (stone) that struck the tzalam (image) became a Rab tawar (mountain), and filled the whole arai (earth).
This is the dream; and we will amar (tell) its interpretation Qadam the malak (king).
You, O malak (king), are malak (king) of malak (kings), to whom the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven) has given the malakaw (kingdom), the chasan (power), and the thaqap (strength), and the glory;

and wherever the children of men dwell, the animals of the field and the birds of the sky has he given into your yad (hand), and has made you to shalat (rule) over them all: you are the raash (head) of gold.
After you shall arise Acharay malakaw (kingdom) inferior to you; and Acharay thalayathay (third) malakaw (kingdom) of brass, which shall shalat (bear) rule over all the arai (earth).

The rabayaiy (fourth) malakaw (kingdom) shall be thaqayap (strong) as iron, because iron breaks in pieces and subdues all things; and as iron that crushes all these, shall it break in pieces and raii (crush).

Whereas you saw the feet and toes, part of potters' clay, and part of iron, it shall be a divided malakaw (kingdom); but there shall be in it of the natzabah (strength) of the iron, because you saw the iron mixed with miry clay.
As the toes of the feet were part of iron, and part of clay, so the malakaw (kingdom) shall be partly thaqayap (strong), and partly broken.
Day you saw the iron mixed with miry clay, they shall hawaa (mingle) themselves with the zarai (seed) of men; but they shall not cling to dan (one) another, even as iron does not mingle with clay.

In the yawam (days) of those malak (kings) shall the Alahayam of shamayan (heaven) qawam (set) up a malakaw (kingdom) which shall never be destroyed, nor shall its sovereignty be left to Acharan im (people); but it shall break in pieces and consume all these malakaw (kingdoms), and it shall qawam (stand) ilam (forever).

Because you saw that a aban (stone) was cut out of the tawar (mountain) without yad (hands), and that it broke in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold; the Rab Alahayam has made known to the malak (king) what shall happen hereafter: and the dream is yatzayab (certain), and its interpretation aman (sure).
Then the malak (king) Nabawakadanatzar fell on his anap (face), and worshiped Danayaal, and commanded that they should offer an manachah (offering) and sweet odors to him.

The malak (king) answered to Danayaal, and said, Of a qashawat (truth) your Alahayam is the Alahayam of Alahayam, and the Adawan of malak (kings), and a revealer of secrets, since you have been able to reveal this secret.

Then the malak (king) made Danayaal Rabarab, and gave him many Rabarab mathanaa (gifts), and made him to shalat (rule) over the whole province of Babal, and to be Rab governor over all the wise men of Babal.

Danayaal requested of the malak (king), and he appointed Shadarak, Mayashak, and Ibadanagawaa, over the ibayadah (affairs) of the province of Babal: but Danayaal was in the tharai (gate) of the malak (king).

Nabawakadanatzar the malak (king) made an tzalam (image) of gold, whose height was Shathayan cubits, and its breadth shath (six) cubits: he qawam (set) it up in the plain of Dawaraa, in the province of Babal.

Then Nabawakadanatzar the malak (king) sent to gather together the satraps, the deputies, and the governors, the adaragazar (judges), the treasurers, the counselors, the sheriffs, and all the shalatawan (rulers) of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the tzalam (image) which Nabawakadanatzar the malak (king) had qawam (set) up.

Then the satraps, the deputies, and the governors, the adaragazar (judges), the treasurers, the counselors, the sheriffs, and all the shalatawan (rulers) of the provinces, were gathered together to the dedication of the tzalam (image) that Nabawakadanatzar the malak (king) had qawam (set) up; and they stood before the tzalam (image) that Nabawakadanatzar had qawam (set) up.
Then the herald cried chayal (aloud), To you it is commanded, im (peoples), amah (nations), and languages,

that Idan you hear the qal (sound) of the qaran (horn), flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, you fall down and sagad (worship) the golden tzalam (image) that Nabawakadanatzar the malak (king) has qawam (set) up;
and whoever doesn't fall down and sagad (worship) shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning nawar (fiery) furnace.

Therefore at that time, when all the im (peoples) heard the qal (sound) of the qaran (horn), flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, all the im (peoples), the amah (nations), and the languages, fell down and worshiped the golden tzalam (image) that Nabawakadanatzar the malak (king) had qawam (set) up.
Therefore at that time gabar (certain) Kashaday (Chaldeans) came near, and brought accusation against the Yahawadaay (Jews).
They answered Nabawakadanatzar the malak (king), O malak (king), live for ever.

You, O malak (king), have made a taim (decree), that every anash (man) that shall hear the qal (sound) of the qaran (horn), flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music, shall fall down and sagad (worship) the golden tzalam (image);
and whoever doesn't fall down and sagad (worship) shall be cast into the midst of a burning nawar (fiery) furnace.

There are gabar (certain) Yahawadaay (Jews) whom you have appointed over the ibayadah (affairs) of the province of Babal: Shadarak, Mayashak, and Ibadanagawaa; these men, O malak (king), have not respected you. They don't palach (serve) your Alahayam, nor sagad (worship) the golden tzalam (image) which you have qawam (set) up.
Then Nabawakadanatzar in his rage and fury commanded to bring Shadarak, Mayashak, and Ibadanagawaa. Then they brought these men Qadam the malak (king).

Nabawakadanatzar answered them, Is it on purpose, Shadarak, Mayashak, and Ibadanagawaa, that you don't palach (serve) my Alahayam, nor sagad (worship) the golden tzalam (image) which I have qawam (set) up?

Now if you are Ithayad Idan you hear the qal (sound) of the qaran (horn), flute, zither, lyre, harp, pipe, and all kinds of music to fall down and sagad (worship) the tzalam (image) which I have made, well: but if you don't sagad (worship), you shall be cast the same hour into the midst of a burning nawar (fiery) furnace; and who is that Alahayam that shall deliver you out of my yad (hands)?
Shadarak, Mayashak, and Ibadanagawaa answered the malak (king), Nabawakadanatzar, we have no need to thawab (answer) you in this pathagam (matter).
If it be so, our Alahayam whom we palach (serve) is able to deliver us from the burning nawar (fiery) furnace; and he will deliver us out of your yad (hand), O malak (king).
But if not, be it known to you, O malak (king), that we will not palach (serve) your Alahayam, nor sagad (worship) the golden tzalam (image) which you have qawam (set) up.

Then was Nabawakadanatzar full of fury, and the tzalam (form) of his appearance was changed against Shadarak, Mayashak, and Ibadanagawaa: therefore he spoke, and commanded that they should heat the furnace shabaih (seven) times more Day it was usually heated.
He commanded certain gabar (mighty) men who were in his chayal (army) to bind Shadarak, Mayashak, and Ibadanagawaa, and to cast them into the burning nawar (fiery) furnace.
Then these men were bound in their pants, their tunics, and their mantles, and their other garments, and were cast into the midst of the burning nawar (fiery) furnace.
Therefore because the malak (king's) commandment was urgent, and the furnace Yathayar hot, the shabayab (flame) of the nawar (fire) killed those men who took up Shadarak, Mayashak, and Ibadanagawaa.
These thalath (three) men, Shadarak, Mayashak, and Ibadanagawaa, fell down bound into the midst of the burning nawar (fiery) furnace.

Then Nabawakadanatzar the malak (king) was astonished, and rose up in haste: he spoke and said to his counselors, Didn't we cast thalath (three) men bound into the midst of the nawar (fire)? They answered the malak (king), yatzayab (true), O malak (king).
He answered, Look, I see arabai (four) men loose, walking in the midst of the nawar (fire), and they are unharmed; and the aspect of the rabayaiy (fourth) is like a bar (son) of the Alahayam.

Then Nabawakadanatzar came near to the tharai (mouth) of the burning nawar (fiery) furnace: he spoke and said, Shadarak, Mayashak, and Ibadanagawaa, you ibad (servants) of the Most Ilay Alahayam, come forth, and come here. Then Shadarak, Mayashak, and Ibadanagawaa came forth out of the midst of the nawar (fire).

The satraps, the deputies, and the governors, and the malak (king's) counselors, being gathered together, saw these men, that the nawar (fire) had no shalat (power) on their bodies, nor was the hair of their raash (head) singed, neither were their pants changed, nor had the smell of nawar (fire) passed on them.

Nabawakadanatzar spoke and said, Blessed be the Alahayam of Shadarak, Mayashak, and Ibadanagawaa, who has sent his malaak (angel), and delivered his ibad (servants) who trusted in him, and have changed the malak (king's) malah (word), and have yielded their bodies, that they might not palach (serve) nor sagad (worship) any Alahayam, lahan (except) their own Alahayam.

Therefore I shawam (make) a taim (decree), that every im (people), amah (nation), and language, which amar (speak) anything shalaw (evil) against the Alahayam of Shadarak, Mayashak, and Ibadanagawaa, shall be ibad (cut) in pieces, and their bayath (houses) shall be made a dunghill; because there is no Acharan Alahayam who is able to deliver after this sort.
Then the malak (king) promoted Shadarak, Mayashak, and Ibadanagawaa in the province of Babal.
Nabawakadanatzar the malak (king), to all the im (peoples), amah (nations), and languages, who dwell in all the arai (earth): shalam (peace) be multiplied to you.
It has Qadam shapar (good) to me to show the ath (signs) and thamah (wonders) that the Most Ilay Alahayam has worked toward me.

How Rabarab are his ath (signs)! and how thaqayap (mighty) are his thamah (wonders)! his malakaw (kingdom) is an ilam (everlasting) malakaw (kingdom), and his dominion is from dar (generation) to dar (generation).
I, Nabawakadanatzar, was at shalah (rest) in my bayath (house), and Rainan in my hayakal (palace).
I saw a dream which made me dachal (afraid); and the thoughts on my bed and the visions of my raash (head) troubled me.
Therefore made I a taim (decree) to bring in all the wise men of Babal Qadam me, that they might make known to me the interpretation of the dream.
Then came in the magicians, the enchanters, the Kashaday (Chaldeans), and the soothsayers; and I told the dream Qadam them; but they did not make known to me its interpretation.

But at the last Danayaal came in Qadam me, whose sham (name) was Balatashaatzar, according to the sham (name) of my Alahayam, and in whom is the rawach (spirit) of the qadayash (holy) Alahayam: and I told the dream Qadam him, saying,

Balatashaatzar, Rab of the magicians, because I know that the rawach (spirit) of the qadayash (holy) Alahayam is in you, and no secret troubles you, amar (tell) me the visions of my dream that I have seen, and its interpretation.
Thus were the visions of my raash (head) on my bed: I saw, and behold, a tree in the midst of the arai (earth); and its height was Shagayaa.
The tree grew, and was strong, and its height reached to the sky, and its sight to the end of all the arai (earth).

The leaves Shapayar it were beautiful, and its fruit Shagayaa, and in it was food for all: the animals of the field had shadow under it, and the birds of the sky lived in its branches, and all flesh was fed from it.
I saw in the visions of my raash (head) on my bed, and behold, a watcher and a qadayash (holy) one came down from the sky.

He cried chayal (aloud), and said Kan, Cut down the tree, and cut off its branches, shake off its leaves, and scatter its fruit: let the animals get away from under it, and the fowls from its branches.

Nevertheless shabaq (leave) the stump of its roots in the arai (earth), even with a band of iron and brass, in the tender grass of the field; and let it be wet with the dew of the sky: and let his portion be with the animals in the grass of the arai (earth):
let his labab (heart) be changed from anash (man's), and let an animal's labab (heart) be given to him; and let shabaih (seven) Idan pass over him.

The sentence is by the decree of the watchers, and the demand by the maamar (word) of the qadayash (holy) ones; to the intent that the chay (living) may know that the Most Ilay shalayat (rules) in the malakaw (kingdom) of men, and gives it to whomever he will, and qawam (sets) up over it the Shapal of men.

This dream I, malak (king) Nabawakadanatzar, have seen; and you, Balatashaatzar, amar (declare) the interpretation, because all the wise men of my malakaw (kingdom) are not able to make known to me the interpretation; but you are able; for the rawach (spirit) of the qadayash (holy) Alahayam is in you.

Then Danayaal, whose sham (name) was Balatashaatzar, was stricken mute for a while, and his thoughts troubled him. The malak (king) answered, Balatashaatzar, don't let the dream, or the interpretation, trouble you. Balatashaatzar answered, My Adawan, the dream be to those who shanaa (hate) you, and its interpretation to your adversaries.
The tree that you saw, which grew, and was strong, whose height reached to the sky, and its sight to all the arai (earth);
whose leaves were Shapayar, and its fruit Shagayaa, and in it was food for all; under which the animals of the field lived, and on whose branches the birds of the sky had their habitation:
it is you, O malak (king), that are grown and become strong; for your greatness is grown, and reaches to the sky, and your dominion to the end of the arai (earth).

Whereas the malak (king) saw a watcher and a qadayash (holy) one coming down from the sky, and saying, Cut down the tree, and chabal (destroy) it; nevertheless shabaq (leave) the stump of its roots in the arai (earth), even with a band of iron and brass, in the tender grass of the field, and let it be wet with the dew of the sky: and let his portion be with the animals of the field, until shabaih (seven) Idan pass over him;
this is the interpretation, O malak (king), and it is the decree of the Most Ilay, which has come on my Adawan the malak (king):

that you shall be driven from men, and your dwelling shall be with the animals of the field, and you shall be made to eat grass as oxen, and shall be wet with the dew of the sky, and shabaih (seven) Idan shall pass over you; until you know that the Most Ilay shalayat (rules) in the malakaw (kingdom) of men, and gives it to whomever he will.

Whereas they commanded to shabaq (leave) the stump of the roots of the tree; your malakaw (kingdom) shall be Qayam to you, after that you shall have known that the shamayan (heavens) do shalayat (rule).

lahan (therefore), O malak (king), let my malak (counsel) be shapar (acceptable) to you, and break off your chatay (sins) by tzadaqah (righteousness), and your iwayaa (iniquities) by showing chanan (mercy) to the poor; if there may be a lengthening of your tranquility.
All this came on the malak (king) Nabawakadanatzar.
At the end of tharayan (twelve) months he was walking in the royal hayakal (palace) of Babal.
The malak (king) spoke and said, Is not this Rab Babal, which I have built for the royal dwelling place, by the might of my chasan (power) and for the glory of my majesty?

While the malah (word) was in the malak (king's) pam (mouth), there fell a qal (voice) from the sky, saying, O malak (king) Nabawakadanatzar, to you it is spoken: The malakaw (kingdom) has departed from you:

and you shall be driven from men; and your dwelling shall be with the animals of the field; you shall be made to eat grass as oxen; and shabaih (seven) Idan shall pass over you; until you know that the Most Ilay shalayat (rules) in the malakaw (kingdom) of men, and gives it to whomever he will.

The same hour was the thing fulfilled on Nabawakadanatzar: and he was driven from men, and ate grass as oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the sky, until his hair was grown like eagles' feathers, and his nails like birds' claws.

At the end of the yawam (days) I, Nabawakadanatzar, lifted up my iyan (eyes) to shamayan (heaven), and my manadai (understanding) returned to me, and I blessed the Most Ilay, and I praised and honored him who lives ilam (forever); for his dominion is an ilam (everlasting) dominion, and his malakaw (kingdom) from dar (generation) to dar (generation).

All the inhabitants of the arai (earth) are reputed as nothing; and he does according to his will in the chayal (army) of shamayan (heaven), and among the inhabitants of the arai (earth); and none can stay his yad (hand), or ask him, What are you doing?

At the same time my manadai (understanding) returned to me; and for the glory of my malakaw (kingdom), my majesty and brightness returned to me; and my counselors and my rabaraban (lords) sought to me; and I was established in my malakaw (kingdom), and Yathayar greatness was added to me.

Now I, Nabawakadanatzar, shabach (praise) and extol and honor the malak (king) of shamayan (heaven); for all his maibad (works) are qashawat (truth), and his arach (ways) dayan (justice); and those who walk in pride he is able to abase.
Balashaatzar the malak (king) made a Rab feast to a alap (thousand) of his rabaraban (lords), and drank chamar (wine) before the alap (thousand).

Balashaatzar, while he tasted the chamar (wine), commanded to bring the golden and silver vessels which Nabawakadanatzar his ab (father) had taken out of the hayakal (temple) which was in Yarawashalam; that the malak (king) and his rabaraban (lords), his wives and his concubines, might drink from them.

Then they brought the golden vessels that were taken out of the hayakal (temple) of the bayath (house) of Alahayam which was at Yarawashalam; and the malak (king) and his rabaraban (lords), his wives and his concubines, drank from them.
They drank chamar (wine), and praised the Alahayam of gold, and of silver, of brass, of iron, of wood, and of aban (stone).

In the same hour came forth the fingers of a anash (man's) yad (hand), and wrote over against the lampstand on the plaster of the wall of the malak (king's) hayakal (palace): and the malak (king) saw the part of the yad (hand) that wrote.
Then the malak (king's) zayaw (face) was changed in him, and his thoughts troubled him; and the joints of his thighs were loosened, and his knees struck daa (one) against another.

The malak (king) cried chayal (aloud) to bring in the enchanters, the Kashaday (Chaldeans), and the soothsayers. The malak (king) spoke and said to the wise men of Babal, Whoever shall read this writing, and show me its interpretation, shall be clothed with purple, and have a chain of gold about his neck, and shall be the thalayathay (third) shalat (ruler) in the malakaw (kingdom).
Then came in all the malak (king's) wise men; but they could not read the writing, nor make known to the malak (king) the interpretation.
Then was malak (king) Balashaatzar Shagayaa troubled, and his zayaw (face) was changed in him, and his rabaraban (lords) were perplexed.

Now the malakaa (queen) by reason of the malah (words) of the malak (king) and his rabaraban (lords) came into the banquet bayath (house): the malakaa (queen) spoke and said, O malak (king), live ilam (forever); don't let your thoughts trouble you, nor let your zayaw (face) be changed.

There is a gabar (man) in your malakaw (kingdom), in whom is the rawach (spirit) of the qadayash (holy) Alahayam; and in the yawam (days) of your ab (father) nahayar (light) and shakalathanaw (understanding) and chakamah (wisdom), like the chakamah (wisdom) of the Alahayam, were found in him; and the malak (king) Nabawakadanatzar your ab (father), the malak (king), I say, your ab (father), made him Rab of the magicians, enchanters, Kashaday (Chaldeans), and soothsayers;

because an Yathayar rawach (spirit), and manadai (knowledge), and shakalathanaw (understanding), interpreting of dreams, and showing of dark sentences, and dissolving of doubts, were found in the same Danayaal, whom the malak (king) named Balatashaatzar. Now let Danayaal be called, and he will show the interpretation.

Then was Danayaal brought in Qadam the malak (king). The malak (king) spoke and said to Danayaal, Are you that Danayaal, who are of the children of the captivity of Yahawad (Judah), whom the malak (king) my ab (father) brought out of Yahawad (Judah)?
I have heard of you, that the rawach (spirit) of the Alahayam is in you, and that nahayar (light) and shakalathanaw (understanding) and Yathayar chakamah (wisdom) are found in you.
Now the wise men, the enchanters, have been brought in Qadam me, that they should read this writing, and make known to me its interpretation; but they could not show the interpretation of the thing.

But I have heard of you, that you can give interpretations, and dissolve doubts; now if you can read the writing, and make known to me its interpretation, you shall be clothed with purple, and have a chain of gold about your neck, and shall be the thalath (third) shalat (ruler) in the malakaw (kingdom).

Then Danayaal answered Qadam the malak (king), Let your mathanaa (gifts) be to yourself, and give your rewards to Acharan; nevertheless I will read the writing to the malak (king), and make known to him the interpretation.
You, malak (king), the Most Ilay Alahayam gave Nabawakadanatzar your ab (father) the malakaw (kingdom), and greatness, and glory, and majesty:

and because of the greatness that he gave him, all the im (peoples), amah (nations), and languages trembled and feared before him: whom he would he killed, and whom he would he kept alive; and whom he would he raised up, and whom he would he hawaa (put) down.
But when his labab (heart) was lifted up, and his rawach (spirit) was hardened so that he dealt proudly, he was deposed from his malakaw (kingly) karasaa (throne), and they took his glory from him:

and he was driven from the ban (sons) of men, and his labab (heart) was made like the animals', and his dwelling was with the wild donkeys; he was fed with grass like oxen, and his body was wet with the dew of the sky; until he knew that the Most Ilay Alahayam shalayat (rules) in the malakaw (kingdom) of men, and that he qawam (sets) up over it whomever he will.
You, his bar (son), Balashaatzar, have not humbled your labab (heart), though you knew all this,

but have lifted up yourself against the Adawan of shamayan (heaven); and they have brought the vessels of his bayath (house) Qadam you, and you and your rabaraban (lords), your wives and your concubines, have drunk chamar (wine) from them; and you have praised the Alahayam of silver and gold, of brass, iron, wood, and aban (stone), which don't see, nor hear, nor know; and the Alahayam in whose yad (hand) your nashamaa (breath) is, and whose are all your arach (ways), you have not glorified.
Then was the part of the yad (hand) sent from Qadam him, and this writing was inscribed.
This is the writing that was inscribed: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.
This is the interpretation of the thing: MENE; Alahayam has numbered your malakaw (kingdom), and brought it to an end;
TEKEL; you are weighed in the balances, and are found Chasayar.
PERES; your malakaw (kingdom) is divided, and given to the Maday and Paras (Persians).

Then commanded Balashaatzar, and they clothed Danayaal with purple, and put a chain of gold about his neck, and made proclamation concerning him, that he should be the thalath (third) shalayat (ruler) in the malakaw (kingdom).
In that layalayaa (night) Balashaatzar the Kashaday (Chaldean) malak (king) was slain.
Darayawash the Maday received the malakaw (kingdom), Shathayan about sixty - tharayan (two) years bar (old).
It Qadam Darayawash to qawam (set) over the malakaw (kingdom) one maah (hundred) isharayan (twenty) satraps, who should be throughout the whole malakaw (kingdom);
and over them thalath (three) presidents, of whom Danayaal was one; that these satraps might give taim (account) to them, and that the malak (king) should have no damage.

Then this Danayaal was distinguished above the presidents and the satraps, because an Yathayar rawach (spirit) was in him; and the malak (king) thought to qawam (set) him over the whole malakaw (realm).

Then the presidents and the satraps sought to find occasion against Danayaal as touching the malakaw (kingdom); but they could find no occasion nor fault, because he was aman (faithful), neither was there any error or fault found in him.
Then these men said, We shall not find any occasion against this Danayaal, lahan (except) we find it against him concerning the dath (law) of his Alahayam.
Then these presidents and satraps assembled together to the malak (king), and said Kan to him, malak (king) Darayawash, live ilam (forever).

All the presidents of the malakaw (kingdom), the deputies and the satraps, the counselors and the governors, have consulted together to qawam (establish) a malak (royal) qayam (statute), and to make a strong decree, that whoever shall ask a petition of any Alahayam or anash (man) for thalathayan (thirty) yawam (days), lahan (except) of you, O malak (king), he shall be cast into the den of arayah (lions).
Now, O malak (king), qawam (establish) the decree, and rasham (sign) the writing, that it not be changed, according to the dath (law) of the Maday and Paras (Persians), which doesn't idaa (alter).
Therefore malak (king) Darayawash signed the writing and the decree.

When Danayaal knew that the writing was signed, he went into his bayath (house) (now his windows were open in his room toward Yarawashalam) and he kneeled on his knees thalath (three) times a yawam (day), and prayed, and gave thanks Qadam his Alahayam, as he did before.
Then these men assembled together, and found Danayaal making petition and chanan (supplication) Qadam his Alahayam.

Then they came near, and spoke Qadam the malak (king) concerning the malak (king's) decree: Haven't you signed an decree, that every anash (man) who shall make petition to any Alahayam or anash (man) within thalathayan (thirty) yawam (days), lahan (except) to you, O malak (king), shall be cast into the den of arayah (lions)? The malak (king) answered, The thing is yatzayab (true), according to the dath (law) of the Maday and Paras (Persians), which doesn't idaa (alter).

Then answered they and said Qadam the malak (king), That Danayaal, who is of the children of the captivity of Yahawad (Judah), doesn't respect you, O malak (king), nor the decree that you have signed, but makes his petition thalath (three) times a yawam (day).

Then the malak (king), when he heard these malah (words), was Shagayaa displeased, and shawam (set) his bal (heart) on Danayaal to deliver him; and he labored until the going down of the shamash (sun) to rescue him.

Then these men assembled together to the malak (king), and said to the malak (king), Know, O malak (king), that it is a dath (law) of the Maday and Paras (Persians), that no decree nor qayam (statute) which the malak (king) establishes may be changed.

Then the malak (king) commanded, and they brought Danayaal, and cast him into the den of arayah (lions). Now the malak (king) spoke and said to Danayaal, Your Alahayam whom you thadayaraa (serve) continually, he will deliver you.

A aban (stone) was brought, and laid on the pam (mouth) of the den; and the malak (king) sealed it with his own signet, and with the signet of his rabaraban (lords); that nothing might be changed concerning Danayaal.
Then the malak (king) went to his hayakal (palace), and passed the bawath (night) fasting; neither were instruments of music brought Qadam him: and his sleep fled from him.
Then the malak (king) arose very early in the morning, and went in haste to the den of arayah (lions).

When he came near to the den to Danayaal, he cried with a Itzab qal (voice); the malak (king) spoke and said to Danayaal, Danayaal, ibad (servant) of the chay (living) Alahayam, is your Alahayam, whom you palach (serve) continually, able to deliver you from the arayah (lions)?
Then Danayaal said to the malak (king), O malak (king), live ilam (forever).

My Alahayam has sent his malaak (angel), and has shut the arayah (lions)' pam (mouths), and they have not chabal (hurt) me; because as Qadam him innocence was found in me; and also Qadam you, O malak (king), have I done no hurt.

Then was the malak (king) Shagayaa glad, and commanded that they should take Danayaal up out of the den. So Danayaal was taken up out of the den, and no kind of harm was found on him, because he had trusted in his Alahayam.

The malak (king) commanded, and they brought those men who had accused Danayaal, and they cast them into the den of arayah (lions), them, their children, and their wives; and the arayah (lions) mauled them, and broke all their bones in pieces, before they came to the bottom of the den.
Then malak (king) Darayawash wrote to all the im (peoples), amah (nations), and languages, who dwell in all the arai (earth): shalam (peace) be multiplied to you.

I shawam (make) a taim (decree), that in all the dominion of my malakaw (kingdom) men hawaa (tremble) and dachal (fear) before the Alahayam of Danayaal; for he is the chay (living) Alahayam, and Qayam ilam (forever), His malakaw (kingdom) that which shall not be destroyed; and his dominion shall be even to the end.
He delivers and rescues, and he ibad (works) ath (signs) and thamah (wonders) in shamayan (heaven) and in arai (earth), who has delivered Danayaal from the yad (power) of the arayah (lions).
So this Danayaal prospered in the malakaw (reign) of Darayawash, and in the malakaw (reign) of Kawarash the Parasay (Persian).

In the chad (first) year of Balashaatzar malak (king) of Babal Danayaal had a dream and visions of his raash (head) on his bed: then he wrote the dream and told the raash (sum) of the malah (matters).
Danayaal spoke and said, I saw in my vision by layalayaa (night), and, behold, the arabai (four) rawach (winds) of the sky broke forth on the Rab yam (sea).
arabai (four) Rabarab animals came up from the yam (sea), diverse daa (one) from another.

The qadamay (first) was like a arayah (lion), and had eagle's wings: I saw until its wings were plucked, and it was lifted up from the arai (earth), and made to qawam (stand) on two feet as a anash (man); and a anash (man's) labab (heart) was given to it.

Behold, Acharay animal, a thanayan (second), like a bear; and it was raised up on one side, and thalath (three) ribs were in its pam (mouth) between its teeth: and they said Kan to it, Arise, devour Shagayaa flesh.
After this I saw, and behold, Acharay, like a leopard, which had on its back arabai (four) wings of a bird; the animal had also arabai (four) raash (heads); and dominion was given to it.

After this I saw in the layalayaa (night) visions, and, behold, a rabayaiy (fourth) animal, Amathanay and powerful, and thaqayap (strong) Yathayar; and it had Rabarab iron teeth; it devoured and broke in pieces, and stamped the shaar (residue) with its feet: and it was diverse from all the animals that were Qadam it; and it had ishar (ten) qaran (horns).

I considered the qaran (horns), and behold, there came up among them Acharay qaran (horn), a Zaiyar one, Qadam which thalath (three) of the qadamay (first) qaran (horns) were plucked up by the roots: and behold, in this qaran (horn) were iyan (eyes) like the iyan (eyes) of a anash (man), and a pam (mouth) speaking Rabarab things.

I saw until karasaa (thrones) were placed, and one who was Ithayaq of yawam (days) sat: his clothing was Chawar as snow, and the hair of his raash (head) like Naqaa wool; his karasaa (throne) was nawar (fiery) shabayab (flames), and its wheels burning nawar (fire).

A nawar (fiery) nahar (stream) issued and came forth from Qadam him: alap (thousands) of alap (thousands) ministered to him, and rabaw (ten) thousand times rabaw (ten) thousand stood Qadam him: the dayan (judgment) was set, and the books were opened.

I saw at that time because of the qal (voice) of the Rabarab malah (words) which the qaran (horn) spoke; I saw even until the animal was slain, and its body destroyed, and it was given to be burned with fire.
As for the shaar (rest) of the animals, their dominion was taken away: yet their lives were prolonged for a season and a Idan.

I saw in the layalayaa (night) visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a bar (son) of anash (man), and he came even to the Ithayaq of yawam (days), and they brought him near Qadam him.

There was given him dominion, and glory, and a malakaw (kingdom), that all the im (peoples), amah (nations), and languages should palach (serve) him: his dominion is an ilam (everlasting) dominion, which shall not idaa (pass) away, and his malakaw (kingdom) that which shall not be destroyed.
As for me, Danayaal, my rawach (spirit) was grieved in the midst of my body, and the visions of my raash (head) troubled me.
I came near to one of those who stood by, and asked him the yatzayab (truth) concerning all this. So he told me, and made me know the interpretation of the things.
These Rabarab animals, which are arabai (four), are arabai (four) malak (kings), who shall arise out of the arai (earth).
But the qadayash (saints) of the Most Ilayawan shall receive the malakaw (kingdom), and possess the malakaw (kingdom) ilam (forever), even ilam (forever) and ever.

Then I desired to know the yatzab (truth) concerning the rabayaiy (fourth) animal, which was diverse from all of them, Yathayar dachal (terrible), whose teeth were of iron, and its nails of brass; which devoured, broke in pieces, and stamped the shaar (residue) with its feet;

and concerning the ishar (ten) qaran (horns) that were on its raash (head), and the Acharay salaq (horn) which came up, and before which thalath (three) fell, even that qaran (horn) that had iyan (eyes), and a pam (mouth) that spoke Rabarab things, whose look was more Rab than its fellows.
I saw, and the same qaran (horn) made war with the qadayash (saints), and prevailed against them;
until the Ithayaq of yawam (days) came, and dayan (judgment) was given to the qadayash (saints) of the Most Ilayawan, and the time came that the qadayash (saints) possessed the malakaw (kingdom).

Kan he said, The rabayaiy (fourth) animal shall be a rabayaiy (fourth) malakaw (kingdom) on arai (earth), which shall be diverse from all the malakaw (kingdoms), and shall devour the whole arai (earth), and shall tread it down, and break it in pieces.

As for the ishar (ten) qaran (horns), out of this malakaw (kingdom) shall ishar (ten) malak (kings) arise: and Acharan shall arise after them; and he shall be diverse from the former, and he shall put down thalath (three) malak (kings).

He shall speak malah (words) against the Most Ilay, and shall wear out the qadayash (saints) of the Most Ilayawan; and he shall think to change the times and the dath (law); and they shall be given into his yad (hand) until a Idan and Idan and half a Idan.
But the dayan (judgment) shall be set, and they shall idaa (take) away his dominion, to consume and to abad (destroy) it to the end.

The malakaw (kingdom) and the dominion, and the greatness of the malakaw (kingdoms) under the whole sky, shall be given to the im (people) of the qadayash (saints) of the Most Ilayawan: his malakaw (kingdom) is an ilam (everlasting) malakaw (kingdom), and all dominions shall palach (serve) and obey him.
Here is the end of the malah (matter). As for me, Danayaal, my Shagayaa much troubled me, and my zayaw (face) was changed in me: but I kept the malah (matter) in my lab (heart).

In the shalawash (third) Shanah of the malakawath (reign) of malak (king) Balashaatzar a vision raah (see) to me, even to me, Danayaal, achar (after) that which raah (see) to me at the thachalah (first).
I saw in the vision; now it was so, that when I saw, I was in the citadel Shawashan Susa, which is in the province of Iyalam; and I saw in the vision, and I was by the awabal (river) Awalay.

Then I lifted up my iyan (eyes), and saw, and behold, there stood panayam (before) the awabal (river) a ayal (ram) which had two qaran (horns): and the two qaran (horns) were Gabah; but one was Gabah than the other, and the Gabah came up Acharawan.

I saw the ayal (ram) pushing westward, and northward, and Nagab; and no animals could imad (stand) panayam (before) him, neither was there any who could natzal (deliver) out of his yad (hand); but he did according to his will, and magnified himself.

As I was considering, behold, a male goat came from the west over the surface of the whole aratz (earth), and didn't nagai (touch) the aratz (ground): and the goat had a notable qaran (horn) between his iyan (eyes).
He came to the ayal (ram) that had the two qaran (horns), which I saw standing panayam (before) the awabal (river), and ran on him in the fury of his kach (power).

I saw him nagai (come) close to the ayal (ram), and he was moved with marar (anger) against him, and struck the ayal (ram), and broke his shanayam (two) qaran (horns); and there was no kach (power) in the ayal (ram) to imad (stand) panayam (before) him; but he cast him down to the aratz (ground), and trampled on him; and there was none who could natzal (deliver) the ayal (ram) out of his yad (hand).

The male goat magnified himself maad (exceedingly): and when he was itzam (strong), the great qaran (horn) was shabar (broken); and instead of it there came up arabai (four) notable horns toward the arabai (four) rawach (winds) of the sky.
Out of one of them came yatzaa (forth) a Matzaiyarah qaran (horn), which grew yathar (exceeding) great, toward the Nagab, and toward the east, and toward the tzabay (glorious) land.
It grew great, even to the tzabaa (army) of the sky; and some of the tzabaa (army) and of the kawakab (stars) it napal (cast) down to the aratz (ground), and trampled on them.
Yes, it magnified itself, even to the shar (prince) of the tzabaa (army); and it took away from him the continual burnt makawan (offering), and the place of his maqadash (sanctuary) was cast down.
The tzabaa (army) was given over to it together with the continual burnt pashai (offering) through disobedience; and it cast down truth to the aratz (ground), and it did its pleasure and prospered.

Then I heard a qadawash (holy) one speaking; and another holy one said to that certain one who spoke, How long shall be the vision concerning the continual burnt pashai (offering), and the disobedience that shamam (makes) desolate, to nathan (give) both the qadash (sanctuary) and the tzabaa (army) to be trodden under maramas (foot)?
He said to me, To two alap (thousand) and shalawash (three) maah (hundred) evenings and mornings; then shall the qadash (sanctuary) be cleansed.
It happened, when I, even I Danayaal, had seen the vision, that I sought to understand it; and behold, there stood before me as the appearance of a gabar (man).
I heard a adam (man's) qawal (voice) between the banks of the Awalay, which called, and said, Gabarayaal, make this bayan (man) to understand the vision.

So he came near where I imad (stood); and when he came, I was frightened, and napal (fell) on my panayam (face): but he said to me, bayan (understand), ban (son) of adam (man); for the vision belongs to the ith (time) of the end.
Now as he was speaking with me, I fell into a radam (deep) sleep with my panayam (face) toward the aratz (ground); but he touched me, and imad (set) me imad (upright).
He said, Behold, I will yadai (make) you know what shall be in the acharayath (latter) time of the indignation; for it belongs to the mawaid (appointed) time of the end.
The ayal (ram) which you saw, that had the two qaran (horns), they are the malak (kings) of Maday and Paras.
The Shaiyar male goat is the malak (king) Yawan Greece: and the gadawal (great) qaran (horn) that is between his iyan (eyes) is the raashawan (first) malak (king).
As for that which was shabar (broken), in the place where arabai (four) stood up, arabai (four) malakawath (kingdoms) shall imad (stand) up out of the gaway (nation), but not with his kach (power).

In the acharayath (latter) time of their malakawath (kingdom), when the transgressors have thamam (come) to the full, a malak (king) of iz (fierce) panayam (face), and bayan (understanding) dark sentences, shall imad (stand) up.

His kach (power) shall be itzam (mighty), but not by his own kach (power); and he shall shachath (destroy) wonderfully, and shall tzalach (prosper) and do his pleasure; and he shall shachath (destroy) the itzawam (mighty) ones and the qadawash (holy) im (people).

Through his shakal (policy) he shall cause craft to tzalach (prosper) in his yad (hand); and he shall magnify himself in his labab (heart), and in their security shall he shachath (destroy) many: he shall also imad (stand) up against the shar (prince) of shar (princes); but he shall be shabar (broken) apas (without) yad (hand).
The vision of the evenings and baqar (mornings) which has been told is amath (true): but seal up the vision; for it belongs to many yawam (days) to come.
I, Danayaal, fainted, and was chalah (sick) certain yawam (days); then I rose up, and did the malak (king's) malaakah (business): and I wondered at the vision, but none understood it.
In the achad (first) Shanah of Darayawash the ban (son) of Achashawarawash, of the zarai (seed) of the Maday, who was made malak (king) over the malakawath (realm) of the Kashaday (Chaldeans),

in the achad (first) Shanah of his malak (reign) I, Danayaal, understood by the books the number of the Shanah about which the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Yaramayah the nabayaa (prophet), for the accomplishing of the desolations of Yarawashalam, even shabaiyam (seventy) Shanah.
I nathan (set) my panayam (face) to the Adanay Alahayam, to seek by prayer and petitions, with fasting and sackcloth and ashes.

I prayed to Yahawah my Alahayam, and made yadah (confession), and said, Oh, Adanay, the gadawal (great) and yaraa (dreadful) Al, who shamar (keeps) barayath (covenant) and loving chasad (kindness) with those who ahab (love) him and shamar (keep) his matzawah (commandments),
we have sinned, and have dealt iwah (perversely), and have done wickedly, and have rebelled, even turning sawar (aside) from your matzawah (precepts) and from your mashapat (ordinances);

neither have we listened to your ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets), who spoke in your sham (name) to our malak (kings), our shar (princes), and our abawath (fathers), and to all the im (people) of the aratz (land).

Adanay, tzadaqah (righteousness) belongs to you, but to us bashath (confusion) of panayam (face), as at this yawam (day); to the men of Yahawadah (Judah), and to the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, and to all Yasharaal (Israel), who are qarawab (near), and who are Rachawaq off, through all the aratz (countries) where you have driven them, because of their mail (trespass) that they have trespassed against you.
Adanay, to us belongs bashath (confusion) of panayam (face), to our malak (kings), to our shar (princes), and to our abawath (fathers), because we have sinned against you.
To the Adanay our Alahayam belong racham (mercies) and forgiveness; for we have rebelled against him;
neither have we obeyed the qawal (voice) of Yahawah our Alahayam, to yalak (walk) in his thawarah (laws), which he nathan (set) panayam (before) us by his ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets).

Yes, all Yasharaal (Israel) have transgressed your thawarah (law), turning sawar (aside), that they should not obey your qawal (voice): therefore the alah (curse) and the shabawaih (oath) written in the thawarah (law) of Mashah the ibad (servant) of Alahayam has been poured out on us; for we have sinned against him.

He has confirmed his dabar (words), which he spoke against us, and against our shapat (judges) who judged us, by bringing on us a gadawal (great) rai (evil); for under the whole sky, such has not been done as has been done to Yarawashalam.

As it is written in the thawarah (law) of Mashah, all this rai (evil) has bawaa (come) on us: yet have we not entreated the favor of Yahawah our Alahayam, that we should shawab (turn back / repent) from our iwan (iniquities), and have discernment in your truth.

Therefore has Yahawah watched over the rai (evil), and brought it on us; for Yahawah our Alahayam is tzadayaq (righteous) in all his maishah (works) which he does, and we have not obeyed his qawal (voice).

Now, Adanay our Alahayam, who has brought your im (people) yatzaa (forth) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam with a chazaq (mighty) yad (hand), and have gotten yourself sham (renown), as at this yawam (day); we have sinned, we have done wickedly.

Adanay, according to all your tzadaqah (righteousness), let your ap (anger) and please let your chamah (wrath) be turned shawab (turn back / repent) from your Iyar Yarawashalam, your qadash (holy) har (mountain); because for our chataa (sins), and for the iwan (iniquities) of our abawath (fathers), Yarawashalam and your im (people) have become a reproach to all who are around us.

Now therefore, our Alahayam, listen to the prayer of your ibad (servant), and to his petitions, and cause your panayam (face) to awar (shine) on your maqadash (sanctuary) that is Shamam, for the Lord's sake.

My Alahayam, natah (turn) your ear, and hear; open your iyan (eyes), and raah (see) our desolations, and the Iyar which is called by your sham (name): for we do not napal (present) our petitions panayam (before) you for our tzadaqah (righteousness), but for your rab (great) racham (mercies)' sake.
Adanay, hear; Adanay, forgive; Adanay, listen and do; don't defer, for your own sake, my Alahayam, because your Iyar and your im (people) are called by your sham (name).

While I was speaking, and praying, and confessing my chataah (sin) and the chataah (sin) of my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel), and presenting my supplication panayam (before) Yahawah my Alahayam for the qadash (holy) har (mountain) of my Alahayam;

yes, while I was speaking in prayer, the ayash (man) Gabarayaal, whom I had seen in the vision at the thachalah (beginning), being caused to Yaip swiftly, touched me about the ith (time) of the evening manachah (offering).
He instructed me, and talked with me, and said, Danayaal, I am now yatzaa (come) forth to give you shakal (wisdom) and bayanah (understanding).

At the thachalah (beginning) of your petitions the commandment went yatzaa (forth), and I have bawaa (come) to nagad (tell) you; for you are greatly beloved: therefore bayan (consider) the dabar (matter), and bayan (understand) the vision.

shabaiyam (seventy) shabawai (weeks) are decreed on your im (people) and on your qadash (holy) Iyar, to finish disobedience, and to thamam (make) an end of chataah (sins), and to kapar (make) reconciliation for iwan (iniquity), and to bawaa (bring) in iwalam (forever) tzadaq (righteousness), and to seal up vision and nabayaa (prophecy), and to mashach (anoint) the most qadash (holy).

yadai (know) therefore and discern, that from the going forth of the commandment to shawab (turn back / repent) and to banah (build) Yarawashalam to the mashayach (anointed) One, the nagayad (prince), shall be shabai (seven) shabawai (weeks), and shashayam (sixty) - shanayam (two) shabawai (weeks): it shall be built again, with street and Charawatz, even in troubled ith (times).

achar (after) the shashayam (sixty) - shanayam (two) shabawai (weeks) the mashayach (anointed) One shall be karath (cut) off, and shall have nothing: and the im (people) of the nagayad (prince) who shall bawaa (come) shall shachath (destroy) the Iyar and the qadash (sanctuary); and its end shall be with a flood, and even to the end shall be war; desolations are determined.

He shall make a firm barayath (covenant) with many for one shabawai (week): and in the chatzay (midst) of the shabawai (week) he shall cause the zabach (sacrifice) and the manachah (offering) to shabath (cease); and on the wing of shaqawatz (abominations) shall come one who shamam (makes) desolate; and even to the full end, and that determined, shall nathak (wrath) be poured out on the shamam (desolate).

In the shalawash (third) Shanah of Kawarash malak (king) of Paras a thing was revealed to Danayaal, whose sham (name) was called Balatashaatzar; and the thing was amath (true), even a gadawal (great) tzabaa (warfare): and he understood the thing, and had bayanah (understanding) of the vision.
In those yawam (days) I, Danayaal, was mourning shalawash (three) yawam (whole) shabawai (weeks).
I ate no pleasant lacham (bread), neither came flesh nor yayan (wine) into my pah (mouth), neither did I anoint myself at all, until shalawash (three) yawam (whole) shabawai (weeks) were fulfilled.
In the arabai (four) and isharayam (twentieth) yawam (day) of the raashawan (first) chadash (month), as I was by the yad (side) of the gadawal (great) nahar (river), which is Chadaqal,
I lifted up my iyan (eyes), and looked, and behold, a ayash (man) Labash in linen, whose thighs were adorned with pure gold of Awapaz:
