his body also was like the beryl, and his panayam (face) as the appearance of lightning, and his iyan (eyes) as ash (flaming) torches, and his zarawai (arms) and his feet like Qalal brass, and the qawal (voice) of his dabar (words) like the qawal (voice) of a multitude.
I, Danayaal, alone saw the vision; for the men who were with me didn't raah (see) the vision; but a gadawal (great) charadah (quaking) napal (fell) on them, and they fled to hide themselves.

So I was shaar (left) alone, and saw this gadawal (great) vision, and there remained no kach (strength) in me; for my hawad (comeliness) was turned in me into mashachayath (corruption), and I retained no kach (strength).

Yet heard I the qawal (voice) of his dabar (words); and when I heard the qawal (voice) of his dabar (words), then was I fallen into a radam (deep) sleep on my panayam (face), with my panayam (face) toward the aratz (ground).
Behold, a yad (hand) touched me, which set me on my knees and on the kap (palms) of my yad (hands).

He said to me, Danayaal, you ayash (man) greatly beloved, bayan (understand) the dabar (words) that I dabar (speak) to you, and imad (stand) imad (upright); for am I now sent to you. When he had spoken this dabar (word) to me, I stood trembling.

Then he said to me, Don't be yaraa (afraid), Danayaal; for from the raashawan (first) yawam (day) that you nathan (set) your lab (heart) to bayan (understand), and to humble yourself panayam (before) your Alahayam, your dabar (words) were heard: and I have bawaa (come) for your dabar (words)' sake.

But the shar (prince) of the malakawath (kingdom) of Paras withstood me isharayam (twenty) - one yawam (days); but, behold, Mayakaal, one of the chief shar (princes), came to help me: and I remained there with the malak (kings) of Paras.
Now I have bawaa (come) to bayan (make) you understand what shall qarah (happen) to your im (people) in the acharayath (latter) yawam (days); for the vision is yet for many yawam (days):
and when he had spoken to me according to these dabar (words), I nathan (set) my panayam (face) toward the aratz (ground), and was mute.

Behold, one in the damawath (likeness) of the ban (sons) of men touched my shapah (lips): then I opened my pah (mouth), and spoke and said to him who stood before me, my Adawan, by reason of the vision my tzayar (sorrows) are turned on me, and I itzar (retain) no kach (strength).

For how can the ibad (servant) of this my Adawan dabar (talk) with this my Adawan? for as for me, immediately there remained no kach (strength) in me, neither was there nashamah (breath) shaar (left) in me.
Then there touched me again maraah (one) like the appearance of a adam (man), and he strengthened me.

He said, "Greatly beloved ayash (man), don't be yaraa (afraid): shalawam (peace) be to you, be chazaq (strong), yes, be chazaq (strong)." When he spoke to me, I was strengthened, and said, "Let my Adawan dabar (speak); for you have strengthened me.

Then he said, "Do you yadai (know) why I have bawaa (come) to you? Now I will shawab (turn back / repent) to fight with the shar (prince) of Paras. When I yatzaa (go) forth, behold, the shar (prince) Yawan Greece shall bawaa (come).
But I will nagad (tell) you that which is inscribed in the writing of truth: and there is none who chazaq (holds) with me against these, but Mayakaal your shar (prince).
"As for me, in the achad (first) Shanah of Darayawash the Maday, I imad (stood) up to chazaq (confirm) and maiwaz (strengthen) him.

Now will I show you the truth. Behold, there shall imad (stand) up yet shalawash (three) malak (kings) in Paras; and the rabayaiy (fourth) shall be far richer than they all: and when he has grown chazaqah (strong) through his riches, he shall stir up all against the malakawath (realm) Yawan Greece.
A gabawar (mighty) malak (king) shall imad (stand) up, who shall mashal (rule) with rab (great) dominion, and do according to his will.

When he shall imad (stand) up, his malakawath (kingdom) shall be shabar (broken), and shall be divided toward the arabai (four) rawach (winds) of the sky, but not to his acharayath (posterity), nor according to his dominion with which he ruled; for his malakawath (kingdom) shall be plucked up, even for others besides these.

The malak (king) of the Nagab shall be chazaq (strong), and one of his shar (princes); and he shall be chazaq (strong) above him, and have mashal (dominion); his mamashalah (dominion) shall be a rab (great) dominion.

At the end of Shanah they shall join themselves together; and the bath (daughter) of the malak (king) of the Nagab shall bawaa (come) to the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north) to ishah (make) an mayashar (agreement): but she shall not itzar (retain) the kach (strength) of her zarawai (arm); neither shall he imad (stand), nor his zarawai (arm); but she shall be given up, and those who brought her, and he who became the father of her, and he who strengthened her in those ith (times).

But out of a shoot from her roots shall one imad (stand) up in his kan (place), who shall bawaa (come) to the chayal (army), and shall bawaa (enter) into the maiwaz (fortress) of the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north), and shall ishah (deal) against them, and shall chazaq (prevail).

Also their Alahayam, with their molten images, and with their goodly vessels of kasap (silver) and of gold, shall he bawaa (carry) Shabay into Matzarayam; and he shall refrain some Shanah from the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north).
He shall bawaa (come) into the malakawath (realm) of the malak (king) of the Nagab, but he shall shawab (turn back / repent) into his own adamah (land).

His ban (sons) shall war, and shall asap (assemble) a multitude of rab (great) chayal (forces), which shall bawaa (come) on, and overflow, and ibar (pass) through; and they shall shawab (turn back / repent) and war, even to his maiwaz (fortress).

The malak (king) of the Nagab shall be moved with marar (anger), and shall yatzaa (come) forth and fight with him, even with the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north); and he shall imad (set) forth a rab (great) multitude, and the multitude shall be given into his yad (hand).
The multitude shall be lifted up, and his labab (heart) shall be exalted; and he shall napal (cast) down rabaw (tens) of thousands, but he shall not prevail.

The malak (king) of the tzapawan (north) shall shawab (turn back / repent), and shall imad (set) forth a multitude greater than the raashawan (former); and he shall bawaa (come) on at the end of the ith (times), even of Shanah, with a gadawal (great) chayal (army) and with much rakawash (substance).

In those ith (times) there shall many imad (stand) up against the malak (king) of the Nagab: also the children of the violent among your im (people) shall nashaa (lift) themselves up to imad (establish) the vision; but they shall fall.

So the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north) shall bawaa (come), and cast up a mound, and take a well-fortified Iyar: and the forces of the Nagab shall not imad (stand), neither his chosen im (people), neither shall there be any kach (strength) to imad (stand).

But he who bawaa (comes) against him shall do according to his own will, and none shall imad (stand) panayam (before) him; and he shall imad (stand) in the tzabay (glorious) aratz (land), and in his yad (hand) shall be destruction.

He shall shawam (set) his panayam (face) to bawaa (come) with the thaqap (strength) of his whole malakawath (kingdom), and with him equitable conditions; and he shall ishah (perform) them: and he shall nathan (give) him the bath (daughter) of women, to shachath (corrupt) her; but she shall not imad (stand), neither be for him.

After this shall he shawam (turn) his panayam (face) to the islands, and shall take many: but a qatzayan (prince) shall cause the reproach offered by him to shabath (cease); yes, moreover, he shall cause his reproach to shawab (turn back / repent) on him.
Then he shall shawab (turn back / repent) his panayam (face) toward the fortresses of his own aratz (land); but he shall stumble and napal (fall), and shall not be found.

Then shall imad (stand) up in his kan (place) one who shall cause a tax collector to pass through the malakawath (kingdom) to maintain its glory; but within achad (few) yawam (days) he shall be destroyed, neither in ap (anger), nor in battle.

In his kan (place) shall imad (stand) up a contemptible person, to whom they had not given the honor of the malakawath (kingdom): but he shall bawaa (come) in time of security, and shall obtain the malakawath (kingdom) by flatteries.
The overwhelming forces shall be overwhelmed from panayam (before) him, and shall be shabar (broken); yes, also the nagayad (prince) of the barayath (covenant).
After the treaty made with him he shall ishah (work) deceitfully; for he shall ilah (come) up, and shall become itzam (strong), with a Mait gaway (people).

In time of security shall he bawaa (come) even on the fattest places of the province; and he shall do that which his abawath (fathers) have not done, nor his abawath (fathers)' abawath (fathers); he shall scatter among them prey, and spoil, and rakawash (substance): yes, he shall chashab (devise) his machashabah (devices) against the strongholds, even for a ith (time).

He shall stir up his kach (power) and his labab (courage) against the malak (king) of the Nagab with a gadawal (great) chayal (army); and the malak (king) of the Nagab shall war in battle with an maad (exceeding) gadawal (great) and itzawam (mighty) chayal (army); but he shall not imad (stand); for they shall chashab (devise) machashabah (devices) against him.
Yes, they who akal (eat) of his dainties shall shabar (destroy) him, and his chayal (army) shall overflow; and many shall napal (fall) down Chalal.

As for shanayam (both) these malak (kings), their labab (hearts) shall be to do mischief, and they shall dabar (speak) lies at one table: but it shall not tzalach (prosper); for yet the end shall be at the mawaid (time) appointed.

Then shall he shawab (turn back / repent) into his aratz (land) with gadawal (great) rakawash (substance); and his labab (heart) shall be against the qadash (holy) barayath (covenant); and he shall do his pleasure, and shawab (turn back / repent) to his own aratz (land).
At the mawaid (time) appointed he shall shawab (turn back / repent), and bawaa (come) into the Nagab; but it shall not be in the Acharawan raashawan (time) as it was in the former.

For ships of Kathay (Kittim) shall bawaa (come) against him; therefore he shall be grieved, and shall shawab (turn back / repent), and have indignation against the qadash (holy) barayath (covenant), and shall do his pleasure: he shall even shawab (turn back / repent), and have bayan (regard) to those who forsake the qadash (holy) barayath (covenant).

Forces shall imad (stand) on his part, and they shall chalal (profane) the maqadash (sanctuary), even the maiwaz (fortress), and shall sawar (take) away the continual burnt offering, and they shall nathan (set) up the shaqawatz (abomination) that shamam (makes) desolate.
Such as do wickedly against the barayath (covenant) shall he pervert by Chalaqah; but the im (people) who yadai (know) their Alahayam shall be chazaq (strong), and do exploits.
Those who are shakal (wise) among the im (people) shall bayan (instruct) many; yet they shall fall by the charab (sword) and by lahabah (flame), by Shabay and by spoil, many yawam (days).
Now when they shall fall, they shall be helped with a Mait help; but many shall join themselves to them with flatteries.
Some of those who are shakal (wise) shall fall, to refine them, and to Barar, and to make them white, even to the ith (time) of the end; because it is yet for the mawaid (time) appointed.

The malak (king) shall do according to his will; and he shall exalt himself, and magnify himself above every Al, and shall dabar (speak) palaa (marvelous) things against the Al of Al; and he shall tzalach (prosper) until the indignation be accomplished; for that which is determined shall be done.
Neither shall he bayan (regard) the Alahayam of his abawath (fathers), nor the desire of women, nor bayan (regard) any Alawah; for he shall magnify himself above all.

But in his kan (place) shall he honor the Alawah of fortresses; and a Alawah whom his abawath (fathers) didn't yadai (know) shall he honor with gold, and kasap (silver), and with Yaqar aban (stones), and pleasant things.

He shall ishah (deal) with the strongest fortresses by the help of a foreign Alawah: whoever nakar (acknowledges) him he will increase with kabawad (glory); and he shall mashal (cause) them to rule over many, and shall divide the adamah (land) for a price.

At the ith (time) of the end shall the malak (king) of the Nagab contend with him; and the malak (king) of the tzapawan (north) shall shair (come) against him like a whirlwind, with chariots, and with horsemen, and with many ships; and he shall bawaa (enter) into the aratz (countries), and shall overflow and ibar (pass) through.

He shall bawaa (enter) also into the tzabay (glorious) aratz (land), and many countries shall be overthrown; but these shall be delivered out of his yad (hand): Adam, and Mawaab, and the raashayath (chief) of the children of Imawan.
He shall shalach (stretch) forth his yad (hand) also on the aratz (countries); and the aratz (land) of Matzarayam shall not palayatah (escape).
But he shall have mashal (power) over the treasures of gold and of kasap (silver), and over all the precious things of Matzarayam; and the Lawabay and the Kawashay (Ethiopians) shall be at his steps.
But news out of the east and out of the tzapawan (north) shall trouble him; and he shall yatzaa (go) forth with gadawal (great) fury to destroy and charam (utterly) to sweep away many.
He shall plant the ahal (tents) of his palace between the yam (sea) and the tzabay (glorious) qadash (holy) har (mountain); yet he shall bawaa (come) to his end, and none shall help him.

"At that ith (time) shall Mayakaal imad (stand) up, the gadawal (great) shar (prince) who imad (stands) for the children of your im (people); and there shall be a ith (time) of tzarah (trouble), such as never was since there was a gaway (nation) even to that same ith (time): and at that ith (time) your im (people) shall be delivered, everyone who shall be found written in the book.
Many of those who sleep in the ipar (dust) of the adamah (earth) shall qawatz (awake), some to iwalam (forever) chay (life), and some to shame and iwalam (forever) contempt.
Those who are shakal (wise) shall shine as the brightness of the expanse; and those who turn many to tzadaq (righteousness) as the kawakab (stars) id (forever) and ever.
But you, Danayaal, shut up the dabar (words), and seal the book, even to the ith (time) of the end: many shall run back and forth, and daith (knowledge) shall be increased.
Then I, Danayaal, looked, and behold, shanayam (two) others stood, one on the yaar (river) shapah (bank) on this hanah (side), and the other on the yaar (river) shapah (bank) on that side.
One said to the ayash (man) Labash in linen, who was above the mayam (waters) of the yaar (river), How long shall it be to the end of these palaa (wonders)?

I heard the ayash (man) Labash in linen, who was above the mayam (waters) of the yaar (river), when he held up his right yamayan (hand) and his left shamaawal (hand) to shamayam (heaven), and swore by him who chay (lives) iwalam (forever) that it shall be for a mawaid (time), mawaid (times), and a chatzay (half); and when they have made an end of breaking in pieces the yad (power) of the qadash (holy) im (people), all these things shall be finished.
I heard, but I didn't bayan (understand): then I said, my Adawan, what shall be the issue of these things?
He said, Go your yalak (way), Danayaal; for the dabar (words) are shut up and sealed until the ith (time) of the end.

Many shall Barar themselves, and make themselves white, and be refined; but the rashai (wicked) shall do wickedly; and none of the rashai (wicked) shall bayan (understand); but those who are shakal (wise) shall bayan (understand).

From the ith (time) that the continual burnt offering shall be taken sawar (away), and the shaqawatz (abomination) that shamam (makes) desolate nathan (set) up, there shall be one alap (thousand) two maah (hundred) thashaiyam (ninety) yawam (days).
Blessed is he who waits, and nagai (comes) to the one alap (thousand) shalawash (three) maah (hundred) shalawashayam (thirty) - chamash (five) yawam (days).
But go you your yalak (way) until the end; for you shall nawach (rest), and shall imad (stand) in your lot, at the end of the yawam (days).

The dabar (word) of Yahawah that came to Hawashai the ban (son) of Baaray, in the yawam (days) of Izayah, Yawatham, Achaz, and Yachazaqayah, malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the yawam (days) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Yawaash, malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel).

When Yahawah spoke at thachalah (first) by Hawashai, Yahawah said to Hawashai, "yalak (go), take for yourself a ashah (wife) of prostitution and children of unfaithfulness; for the aratz (land) commits great adultery, forsaking Yahawah.
So he went and took Gamar the bath (daughter) of Dabalayam; and she conceived, and bore him a ban (son).

Yahawah said to him, "qaraa (call) his sham (name) Yazaraial; for yet a Mait while, and I will paqad (avenge) the dam (blood) of Yazaraial on the bayath (house) of Yahawaa, and will cause the mamalakawath (kingdom) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) to shabath (cease).
It will happen in that yawam (day) that I will shabar (break) the qashath (bow) of Yasharaal (Israel) in the valley of Yazaraial.

She conceived again, and bore a bath (daughter). Then he said to him, "qaraa (call) her sham (name) Laarachamah; for I will no longer have racham (mercy) on the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), that I should in any way nashaa (pardon) them.

But I will have racham (mercy) on the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah), and will yashai (save) them by Yahawah their Alahayam, and will not yashai (save) them by qashath (bow), charab (sword), battle, horses, or horsemen.
Now when she had weaned Laarachamah, she conceived, and bore a ban (son).
He said, "qaraa (call) his sham (name) Laaimay; for you are not my im (people), and I will not be yours.

Yet the number of the children of Yasharaal (Israel) will be as the sand of the yam (sea), which can't be measured nor numbered; and it will come to pass that, in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my im (people),' they will be called ‘ban (sons) of the chay (living) Al.'

The children of Yahawadah (Judah) and the children of Yasharaal (Israel) will be gathered together, and they will shawam (appoint) themselves one raash (head), and will ilah (go) up from the aratz (land); for gadawal (great) will be the yawam (day) of Yazaraial.
"amar (say) to your ach (brothers), ‘My im (people)!' and to your achawath (sisters), ‘My loved one!'

rayab (contend) with your am (mother)! rayab (contend), for she is not my ashah (wife), neither am I her ayash (husband); and let her sawar (put) away her prostitution from her panayam (face), and her adulteries from between her breasts;

Lest I strip her Irawam, and make her bare as in the yawam (day) that she was yalad (born), and shawam (make) her like a madabar (wilderness), and shayath (set) her like a tzayah (dry) aratz (land), and mawath (kill) her with thirst.
Indeed, on her children I will have no racham (mercy); for they are children of unfaithfulness;

For their am (mother) has played the prostitute. She who conceived them has done yabash (shamefully); for she said, ‘I will yalak (go) achar (after) my lovers, who nathan (give) me my lacham (bread) and my mayam (water), my wool and my flax, my shaman (oil) and my drink.'
Therefore, behold, I will hedge up your darak (way) with thorns, and I will build a wall against her, that she can't matzaa (find) her nathayab (way).

She will follow after her lovers, but she won't overtake them; and she will seek them, but won't matzaa (find) them. Then she will amar (say), ‘I will yalak (go) and shawab (turn back / repent) to my raashawan (first) ayash (husband); for then was it tawab (better) with me than now.'
For she did not yadai (know) that I gave her the grain, the new thayarawash (wine), and the yatzahar (oil), and multiplied to her kasap (silver) and gold, which they used for Bail.

Therefore I will take shawab (turn back / repent) my grain in its ith (time), and my new thayarawash (wine) in its mawaid (season), and will natzal (pluck) away my wool and my flax which should have covered her irawah (nakedness).
Now I will galah (uncover) her lewdness in the iyan (sight) of her lovers, and no one will natzal (deliver) her out of my yad (hand).
I will also cause all her celebrations to shabath (cease): her chag (feasts), her new chadash (moons), her shabath (sabbaths), and all her solemn mawaid (assemblies).

I will shamam (lay) waste her vines and her fig trees, about which she has said, ‘These are my wages that my lovers have given me; and I will shawam (make) them a Yair,' and the animals of the shadah (field) shall akal (eat) them.

I will paqad (visit) on her the yawam (days) of the Bail, to which she burned qatar (incense), when she decked herself with her earrings and her jewels, and went achar (after) her lovers, and forgot me," says Yahawah.
"Therefore, behold, I will allure her, and yalak (bring) her into the madabar (wilderness), and dabar (speak) tenderly to her.

I will nathan (give) her vineyards from there, and the valley of Ikawar for a door of hope; and she will respond there, as in the yawam (days) of her youth, and as in the yawam (day) when she came up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
It will be in that yawam (day)," says Yahawah, "that you will qaraa (call) me ‘my ayash (husband),' and no longer qaraa (call) me ‘my Bailay.'
For I will sawar (take) away the sham (names) of the Bail out of her pah (mouth), and they will no longer be mentioned by sham (name).

In that yawam (day) I will karath (make) a barayath (covenant) for them with the animals of the shadah (field), and with the birds of the sky, and with the creeping things of the adamah (ground). I will shabar (break) the qashath (bow), the charab (sword), and the battle out of the aratz (land), and will make them shakab (lie) down safely.
I will betroth you to me iwalam (forever). Yes, I will betroth you to me in tzadaq (righteousness), in justice, in loving chasad (kindness), and in racham (compassion).
I will even betroth you to me in amawanah (faithfulness); and you shall yadai (know) Yahawah.
It will happen in that yawam (day), I will respond," says Yahawah, "I will respond to the shamayam (heavens), and they will respond to the aratz (earth);
and the aratz (earth) will respond to the grain, and the new thayarawash (wine), and the yatzahar (oil); and they will respond to Yazaraial.

I will zarai (sow) her to me in the aratz (earth); and I will have racham (mercy) on her who had not obtained racham (mercy); and I will amar (tell) those who were not my im (people), ‘You are my im (people);' and they will amar (say), ‘My Alahayam!'

Yahawah said to me, "yalak (go) again, ahab (love) a ashah (woman) loved by rai (another), and an naap (adulteress), even as Yahawah ahabah (loves) the children of Yasharaal (Israel), though they panah (turn) to other Alahayam, and ahab (love) cakes of raisins.
So I bought her for myself for fifteen pieces of kasap (silver) and a homer and a half of barley.
I said to her, "You shall stay with me many yawam (days). You shall not play the prostitute, and you shall not be with any other ayash (man). I will also be so toward you.

For the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shall live many yawam (days) without malak (king), and without shar (prince), and without zabach (sacrifice), and without sacred matzabah (stone), and without apawad (ephod) or tharapayam (idols).

Afterward the children of Yasharaal (Israel) shall shawab (turn back / repent), and seek Yahawah their Alahayam, and Dawad their malak (king), and shall come with trembling to Yahawah and to his blessings in the acharayath (last) yawam (days).

Hear the dabar (word) of Yahawah, you children of Yasharaal (Israel); for Yahawah has a charge against the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land): "Indeed there is no truth, nor goodness, nor daith (knowledge) of Alahayam in the aratz (land).
There is cursing, lying, ratzach (murder), stealing, and committing naap (adultery); they break boundaries, and bloodshed causes bloodshed.

Therefore the aratz (land) will mourn, and everyone who yashab (dwells) therein will waste away. all chay (living) things in her, even the animals of the shadah (field) and the birds of the sky; yes, the fish of the yam (sea) also die.
"Yet let no ayash (man) bring a charge, neither let any man accuse; For your im (people) are like those who bring charges against a kahan (priest).
You will stumble in the yawam (day), and the nabayaa (prophet) will also stumble with you in the layal (night); and I will damah (destroy) your am (mother).

My im (people) are destroyed for lack of daith (knowledge). Because you have rejected daith (knowledge), I will also reject you, that you may be no kahan (priest) to me. Because you have forgotten your alahayam (god's) thawarah (law), I will also forget your children.
As they were multiplied, so they sinned against me. I will change their kabawad (glory) into qalawan (shame).
They akal (feed) on the chataah (sin) of my im (people), and nashaa (set) their napash (heart) on their iwan (iniquity).
It will be, like im (people), like kahan (priest); and I will paqad (punish) them for their darak (ways), and will repay them for their deeds.
They will akal (eat), and not have enough. They will play the prostitute, and will not increase; because they have abandoned giving to Yahawah.
Prostitution, yayan (wine), and new thayarawash (wine) take away lab (understanding).

My im (people) shaal (consult) with their wooden idol, and answer to a stick of wood. Indeed the rawach (spirit) of prostitution has led them thaih (astray), and they have been unfaithful to their Alahayam.

They zabach (sacrifice) on the raash (tops) of the har (mountains), and qatar (burn) incense on the Gabaih, under oaks and poplars and terebinths, because its shade is tawab (good). Therefore your bath (daughters) play the prostitute, and your kalah (brides) naap (commit) adultery.

I will not paqad (punish) your bath (daughters) when they play the prostitute, nor your kalah (brides) when they naap (commit) adultery; because the men consort with prostitutes, and they zabach (sacrifice) Qadashah the shrine prostitutes; so the im (people) without bayan (understanding) will come to ruin.

"Though you, Yasharaal (Israel), play the prostitute, yet don't let Yahawadah (Judah) asham (offend); and don't bawaa (come) to Galagal, neither ilah (go) up to Bayathaawan Aven, nor shabai (swear), ‘As Yahawah chay (lives).'
For Yasharaal (Israel) has behaved extremely stubbornly, like a stubborn heifer. Then how will Yahawah raih (feed) them like a lamb in a meadow.
Aparayam is joined to itzab (idols). Leave him yanach (alone)!
Their sabaa (drink) has become sawar (sour). They play the prostitute continually. Her magan (rulers) dearly ahab (love) their shameful way.
The rawach (wind) has wrapped her up in its wings; and they shall be disappointed because of their zabach (sacrifices).

"Listen to this, you kahan (priests)! Listen, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), and give ear, bayath (house) of the malak (king)! For the mashapat (judgment) is against you; for you have been a snare Matzapah Mizpah, and a net spread on Thabawar.
The rebels are deep in slaughter; but I discipline all of them.
I yadai (know) Aparayam, and Yasharaal (Israel) is not hidden from me; for now, Aparayam, you have played the prostitute. Yasharaal (Israel) is defiled.
Their deeds won't allow them to shawab (turn back / repent) to their Alahayam; for the rawach (spirit) of prostitution is qarab (within) them, and they don't yadai (know) Yahawah.
The pride of Yasharaal (Israel) testifies to his panayam (face). Therefore Yasharaal (Israel) and Aparayam will stumble in their iwan (iniquity). Yahawadah (Judah) also will stumble with them.
They will yalak (go) with their flocks and with their herds to seek Yahawah; but they won't matzaa (find) him. He has withdrawn himself from them.
They are bagad (unfaithful) to Yahawah; for they have borne illegitimate children. Now the new chadash (moon) will akal (devour) them with their fields.
"Blow the cornet in Gabaih, and the trumpet in Ramah! rawai (sound) a battle cry at Bayathaawan Aven, achar (behind) you, Banayamayan!
Aparayam will become a desolation in the yawam (day) of rebuke. Among the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel), I have made yadai (known) that which will aman (surely) be.
The shar (princes) of Yahawadah (Judah) are like those who nasag (remove) a landmark. I will pour out my ibarah (wrath) on them like mayam (water).
Aparayam is oppressed, he is crushed in mashapat (judgment); Because he is intent in his pursuit of idols.
Therefore I am to Aparayam like a moth, and to the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) like rottenness.

"When Aparayam saw his sickness, and Yahawadah (Judah) his wound, Then Aparayam went to Ashawar, and sent to malak (king) Yarab: but he is not yakal (able) to heal you, neither will he cure you of your wound.

For I will be to Aparayam like a shachal (lion), and like a young kapayar (lion) to the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah). I myself will tear in pieces and yalak (go) away. I will nashaa (carry) off, and there will be no one to natzal (deliver).
I will yalak (go) and shawab (turn back / repent) to my place, until they acknowledge their offense, and seek my panayam (face). In their tzar (affliction) they will shachar (seek) me earnestly.
"yalak (come), and let us shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah; for he has torn us to pieces, and he will heal us; he has injured us, and he will bind up our wounds.
After yawam (two) days he will chayah (revive) us. On the shalayashay (third) yawam (day) he will qawam (raise) us up, and we will chayah (live) panayam (before) him.

Let us yadai (acknowledge) Yahawah. Let us press on to yadai (know) Yahawah. As surely as the sun rises, Yahawah will appear. He will bawaa (come) to us like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the aratz (earth).
"Aparayam, what shall I do to you? Yahawadah (Judah), what shall I do to you? For your chasad (love) is like a baqar (morning) cloud, and like the dew that disappears shakam (early).
Therefore I have chatzab (cut) them to pieces with the nabayaa (prophets); I killed them with the amar (words) of my pah (mouth). Your mashapat (judgments) are like a flash of awar (lightning).
For I desire chasad (mercy), and not zabach (sacrifice); and the daith (knowledge) of Alahayam more than burnt ilah (offerings).
But they, like Adam, have broken the barayath (covenant). They were bagad (unfaithful) to me, there.
Galaid is a city of those who pail (work) awan (iniquity); it is Iqab with dam (blood).
As gangs of robbers wait to ambush a ayash (man), so the company of kahan (priests) ratzach (murder) in the darak (way) toward Shechem, committing shameful zamah (crimes).
In the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) I have seen a Shairawarah thing. There is prostitution in Aparayam. Yasharaal (Israel) is defiled.
"Also, Yahawadah (Judah), there is a harvest appointed for you, when I shawab (turn back / repent) the fortunes of my im (people).

When I would heal Yasharaal (Israel), then the iwan (iniquity) of Aparayam is uncovered, also the wickedness of Shamarawan; for they pail (commit) falsehood, and the thief bawaa (enters) in, and the gang of robbers ravages outside.
They don't amar (consider) in their labab (hearts) that I zakar (remember) all their wickedness. Now their own deeds have engulfed them. They are before my panayam (face).
They make the malak (king) Shamach with their wickedness, and the shar (princes) with their lies.
They are all naap (adulterers). They are burning like an oven that the baker stops stirring, from the kneading of the dough, until it is leavened.
On the yawam (day) of our malak (king), the shar (princes) made themselves chalah (sick) with the chamah (heat) of yayan (wine). He joined his yad (hand) with mockers.
For they have prepared their lab (heart) like an oven, while they lie in wait. Their baker sleeps all the layal (night). In the baqar (morning) it bair (burns) as a lahabah (flaming) ash (fire).
They are all hot as an oven, and akal (devour) their shapat (judges). All their malak (kings) have fallen. There is no one among them who qaraa (calls) to me.
Aparayam, he mixes himself among the im (nations). Aparayam is a pancake not turned over.
Strangers have devoured his kach (strength), and he doesn't realize it. Indeed, shayabah (gray) hairs are here and there on him, and he doesn't realize it.
The pride of Yasharaal (Israel) testifies to his panayam (face); yet they haven't returned to Yahawah their Alahayam, nor sought him, for all this.
"Aparayam is like an easily deceived dove, without lab (understanding). They qaraa (call) to Matzarayam. They halak (go) to Ashawar.
When they yalak (go), I will spread my net on them. I will yarad (bring) them down like the birds of the sky. I will chastise them, as their idah (congregation) has heard.
Woe to them! For they have wandered from me. Destruction to them! For they have trespassed against me. Though I would padah (redeem) them, yet they have spoken lies against me.
They haven't cried to me with their lab (heart), but they howl on their beds. They gawar (assemble) themselves for grain and new thayarawash (wine). They sawar (turn) away from me.
Though I have taught and strengthened their zarawai (arms), yet they plot rai (evil) against me.

They shawab (turn back / repent), but not to the Ilayawan. They are like a faulty qashath (bow). Their shar (princes) will napal (fall) by the charab (sword) for the rage of their lashawan (tongue). This will be their derision in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam.
"Put the trumpet to your lips! Something like an eagle is over yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house), because they have broken my barayath (covenant), and rebelled against my thawarah (law).
They cry to me, ‘My Alahayam, we Israel yadai (acknowledge) you!'
Yasharaal (Israel) has cast off that which is tawab (good). The ayab (enemy) will pursue him.

They have set up malak (kings), but not by me. They have made shawar (princes), and I didn't approve. Of their kasap (silver) and their gold they have made themselves itzab (idols), that they may be karath (cut) off.
Let Shamarawan throw out his calf idol! My ap (anger) charah (burns) against them! How long will it be until they are capable of purity?
For this is even from Yasharaal (Israel)! The workman made it, and it is no Alahayam; indeed, the calf of Shamarawan shall be broken in pieces.

For they zarai (sow) the rawach (wind), and they will reap the sawapah (whirlwind). He has no standing grain. The stalk will ishah (yield) no qamach (head). If it does ishah (yield), strangers will balai (swallow) it up.
Yasharaal (Israel) is swallowed up. Now they are among the gawayam (nations) Chapatz a worthless thing.
For they have gone up to Ashawar, like a wild donkey wandering badad (alone). Aparayam has hired ahab (lovers) for himself.
But although they sold themselves among the gawayam (nations), I will now gather them; and they Mait to waste mashaa (away) because of the oppression of the malak (king) of mighty ones.
Because Aparayam has multiplied mazabach (altars) for sinning, they became for him mazabach (altars) for sinning.
I wrote for him the many things of my thawarah (law); but they were regarded as a zawar (strange) thing.

As for the zabach (sacrifices) of my habahab (offerings), they zabach (sacrifice) flesh and akal (eat) it; But Yahawah doesn't accept them. Now he will zakar (remember) their iwan (iniquity), and paqad (punish) their chataah (sins). They will shawab (turn back / repent) to Matzarayam.

For Yasharaal (Israel) has forgotten his Maker and built hayakal (palaces); and Yahawadah (Judah) has multiplied fortified Iyar; but I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on his Iyar, and it will akal (devour) its fortresses.
Don't Shamach, Yasharaal (Israel), to jubilation like the im (nations); for you were unfaithful to your Alahayam. You ahab (love) the wages of a prostitute at every grain threshing floor.
The threshing floor and the yaqab (winepress) won't raih (feed) them, and the new thayarawash (wine) will fail her.
They won't yashab (dwell) in yahawah (yahweh's) aratz (land); but Aparayam will shawab (turn back / repent) to Matzarayam, and they will akal (eat) tamaa (unclean) food in Ashawar.

They won't pour out yayan (wine) offerings to Yahawah, neither will they be pleasing to him. Their zabach (sacrifices) will be to them like the lacham (bread) of awan (mourners); all who akal (eat) of it will be polluted; for their lacham (bread) will be for their napash (appetite). It will not bawaa (come) into the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
What will you do in the yawam (day) of mawaid (solemn) assembly, and in the yawam (day) of the chag (feast) of Yahawah?

For, behold, they have gone away from destruction. Matzarayam will gather them up. Map will bury them. Nettles will yarash (possess) their pleasant things of kasap (silver). Thorns will be in their ahal (tents).

The yawam (days) of visitation have bawaa (come). The yawam (days) of reckoning have bawaa (come). Yasharaal (Israel) will yadai (consider) the nabayaa (prophet) to be a Awayal, and the ayash (man) who is inspired to be insane, because of the abundance of your iwan (sins), and because your hostility is rab (great).
A nabayaa (prophet) watches over Aparayam with my Alahayam. A fowler's snare is on all of his darak (paths), and hostility in the bayath (house) of his Alahayam.
They have deeply corrupted themselves, as in the yawam (days) of Gabaih. He will zakar (remember) their iwan (iniquity). He will paqad (punish) them for their chataah (sins).

I found Yasharaal (Israel) like inab (grapes) in the madabar (wilderness). I saw your abawath (fathers) as the bakawarah (first) ripe in the fig tree at its raashayath (first) season; but they came to Bailapaiwar Peor, and consecrated themselves to the shameful thing, and became abominable ahab (like) that which they loved.
As for Aparayam, their kabawad (glory) will fly away like a bird. There will be no yalad (birth), none with child, and no conception.
Though they bring up their children, yet I will shakal (bereave) them, so that not a adam (man) shall be left. Indeed, woe also to them when I sawar (depart) from them!
I have seen Aparayam, like Tzar, planted in a Nawah place; but Aparayam will yatzaa (bring) out his children to the harag (murderer).
nathan (give) them—Yahweh what will you nathan (give)? nathan (give) them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.

"All their wickedness is in Galagal; for there I hated them. Because of the rai (wickedness) of their deeds I will drive them out of my bayath (house)! I will ahabah (love) them no more. All their shar (princes) are rebels.
Aparayam is struck. Their root has dried up. They will ishah (bear) no fruit. Even though they yalad (bring) forth, yet I will mawath (kill) the beloved batan (ones) of their womb.
My Alahayam will cast them away, because they did not listen to him; and they will be wanderers among the gawayam (nations).

Yasharaal (Israel) is a luxuriant vine that puts forth his fruit. According to the abundance of his fruit he has multiplied his mazabach (altars). As their aratz (land) has prospered, they have adorned their sacred matzabah (stones).
Their lab (heart) is divided. Now they will be asham (found) guilty. He will demolish their mazabach (altars). He will shadad (destroy) their sacred matzabah (stones).
Surely now they will amar (say), "We have no malak (king); for we don't yaraa (fear) Yahawah; and the malak (king), what can he do for us?
They make dabar (promises), swearing falsely in making barayath (covenants). Therefore mashapat (judgment) springs up like poisonous weeds in the furrows of the shadah (field).

The Shakan of Shamarawan will be in terror Igalah the calves of Bayathaawan Aven; for its im (people) will mourn over it, Along with its kamar (priests) who rejoiced over it, for its kabawad (glory), because it has departed from it.
It also will be carried to Ashawar for a manachah (present) to a great malak (king). Aparayam will receive shame, and Yasharaal (Israel) will be bawash (ashamed) of his own itzah (counsel).
Shamarawan and her malak (king) float away, like a twig on the mayam (water).

The bamah (high) places also of Awan, the chataah (sin) of Yasharaal (Israel), will be destroyed. The thorn and the thistle will ilah (come) up on their mazabach (altars). They will amar (tell) the har (mountains), "Cover us!" and the Gabaih, "napal (fall) on us!
"Yasharaal (Israel), you have sinned from the yawam (days) of Gabaih. There they remained. The battle against the children of ilawah (iniquity) doesn't overtake them in Gabaih.
When it is my desire, I will chastise them; and the im (nations) will be gathered against them, when they are bound to their shanayam (two) transgressions.

Aparayam is a trained Igalah that ahab (loves) to thresh; so I will ibar (put) a yoke on her beautiful neck. I will set a rider on Aparayam. Yahawadah (Judah) will charash (plow). Yaiqab will break his clods.

zarai (sow) to yourselves in tzadaqah (righteousness), reap according to chasad (kindness). Break up your fallow nayar (ground); for it is ith (time) to seek Yahawah, until he bawaa (comes) and rains tzadaq (righteousness) on you.
You have plowed rashai (wickedness). You have reaped iwal (iniquity). You have eaten the fruit of lies, for you trusted in your darak (way), in the multitude of your gabawar (mighty) men.

Therefore a battle roar will qawam (arise) among your im (people), and all your fortresses will be destroyed, as Shalaman destroyed Bayathaarabaal Arbel in the yawam (day) of battle. The am (mother) was dashed in pieces with her children.
So Bayathaal will do to you panayam (because) of your rai (great) wickedness. At daybreak the malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel) will be destroyed.
"When Yasharaal (Israel) was a nair (child), then I loved him, and called my ban (son) out of Matzarayam.
They called to them, so they went from them. They sacrificed to the Bail, and burned qatar (incense) to engraved pasayal (images).
Yet I taught Aparayam to walk. I took them by his zarawai (arms); but they didn't yadai (know) that I healed them.
I drew them with cords of a adam (man), with ties of ahabah (love); and I was to them like those who lift up the yoke Lachay their necks; and I bent down to him and I fed him.
"They won't shawab (turn back / repent) into the aratz (land) of Matzarayam; but the Ashawar (Assyrian) will be their malak (king), because they refused to repent.
The charab (sword) will chawal (fall) on their Iyar, and will kalah (destroy) the bad (bars) of their gates, and will put an end to their plans.
My im (people) are determined to mashawabah (turn) from me. Though they qaraa (call) to the Ilayawan, he certainly won't exalt them.

"How can I nathan (give) you up, Aparayam? How can I magan (hand) you over, Yasharaal (Israel)? How can I nathan (make) you like Adamah? How can I nathan (make) you like Tzabaayam? My lab (heart) is turned within me, my compassion is aroused.

I will not ishah (execute) the charawan (fierceness) of my ap (anger). I will not shawab (turn back / repent) to shachath (destroy) Aparayam: for I am Al, and not ayash (man); the qadawash (holy) One in the qarab (midst) of you; and I will not bawaa (come) Iyar wrath.
They will yalak (walk) achar (after) Yahawah, who will roar like a aray (lion); for he will roar, and the children will come trembling from the yam (west).
They will come trembling like a bird out of Matzarayam, and like a dove out of the aratz (land) of Ashawar; and I will yashab (settle) them in their bayath (houses)," says Yahawah.
Aparayam surrounds me with falsehood, and the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) with deceit. Yahawadah (Judah) still strays from Al, and is unfaithful to the qadawash (holy) One.

Aparayam raih (feeds) on rawach (wind), and chases the east qadayam (wind). He yawam (continually) multiplies lies and desolation. They karath (make) a barayath (covenant) with Ashawar, and shaman (oil) is carried into Matzarayam.
Yahawah also has a rayab (controversy) with Yahawadah (Judah), and will paqad (punish) Yaiqab according to his darak (ways); according to his deeds he will repay him.
In the womb he took his ach (brother) by the heel; and in his manhood he contended with Alahayam.
Indeed, he struggled with the malaak (angel), and prevailed; he wept, and made chanan (supplication) to him. He found him at Bayathaal, and there he spoke with us,
even Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies); Yahawah is his name of renown!
Therefore shawab (turn back / repent) to your Alahayam. shamar (keep) chasad (kindness) and justice, and wait continually for your Alahayam.
A Kanain has dishonest scales in his yad (hand). He ahab (loves) to defraud.
Aparayam said, "Surely I have become rich, I have found myself wealth. In all my wealth they won't matzaa (find) in me any iwan (iniquity) that is chataa (sin).
"But I am Yahawah your Alahayam from the aratz (land) of Matzarayam. I will yet again yashab (make) you dwell in ahal (tents), as in the yawam (days) of the mawaid (solemn) feast.
I have also spoken to the nabayaa (prophets), and I have multiplied visions; and by the yad (ministry) of the nabayaa (prophets) I have used parables.
If Galaid is awan (wicked), surely they are worthless. In Galagal they zabach (sacrifice) bulls. Indeed, their mazabach (altars) are like heaps in the furrows of the shadah (field).
Yaiqab fled into the shadah (country) of Aram, and Yasharaal (Israel) served to get a ashah (wife), and for a ashah (wife) he tended flocks and herds.
By a nabayaa (prophet) Yahawah brought Yasharaal (Israel) up out of Matzarayam, and by a nabayaa (prophet) he was preserved.
Aparayam has bitterly provoked kais (anger). Therefore his dam (blood) will be left on him, and his Adawan will repay his contempt.
When Aparayam spoke, there was trembling. He exalted himself in Yasharaal (Israel), but when he became asham (guilty) in Bail, he died.

Now they chataa (sin) more and more, and have made themselves molten masakah (images) of their kasap (silver), even itzab (idols) according to their own thabawan (understanding), all of them the maishah (work) of the craftsmen. They amar (say) of them, ‘They offer human zabach (sacrifice) and kiss the calves.'

Therefore they will be like the baqar (morning) mist, and like the dew that passes halak (away) shakam (early), like the chaff that is driven with the whirlwind out of the threshing floor, and like the ishan (smoke) out of the chimney.
"Yet I am Yahawah your Alahayam from the aratz (land) of Matzarayam; and you shall yadai (acknowledge) no Alahayam but me, and balathay (besides) me there is no savior.
I knew you in the madabar (wilderness), in the aratz (land) of great drought.
According to their pasture, so were they filled; they were filled, and their lab (heart) was exalted. Therefore they have forgotten me.
Therefore I am like a shachal (lion) to them. Like a leopard, I will lurk by the darak (path).

I will meet them like a bear that is Shakawal of her cubs, and will tear the covering of their lab (heart). There I will akal (devour) them like a labayaa (lioness). The shadah (wild) animal will tear them.
You are destroyed, Yasharaal (Israel), because you are against me, against your help.
Where is your malak (king) now, that he may yashai (save) you in all your Iyar? And your shapat (judges), of whom you said, ‘nathan (give) me a malak (king) and shar (princes)?'
I have given you a malak (king) in my ap (anger), and have taken him away in my ibarah (wrath).
The guilt of Aparayam is stored up. His chataah (sin) is stored up.
The sorrows of a travailing yalad (woman) will bawaa (come) on him. He is an unwise ban (son); for when it is ith (time), he doesn't come to the opening of the womb.

I will padah (ransom) them from the yad (power) of shaawal (sheol). I will gaal (redeem) them from mawath (death)! mawath (death), where are your dabar (plagues)? shaawal (sheol), where is your destruction? "Compassion will be hidden from my iyan (eyes).

Though he is fruitful among his ach (brothers), an east qadayam (wind) will bawaa (come), the rawach (breath) of Yahawah coming up from the madabar (wilderness); and his spring will become dry, and his fountain will be dried up. He will plunder the storehouse of treasure.

Shamarawan will bear her guilt; for she has rebelled against her Alahayam. They will napal (fall) by the charab (sword). Their infants will be dashed in pieces, and their pregnant women will be ripped open.
Yasharaal (Israel), shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah your Alahayam; for you have fallen because of your iwan (sin).

Take dabar (words) with you, and shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah. amar (tell) him, "nashaa (forgive) all our iwan (sins), and accept that which is tawab (good): so we offer our shapah (lips) like bulls.
Ashawar can't yashai (save) us. We won't ride on horses; neither will we amar (say) any more to the maishah (work) of our yad (hands), ‘Our Alahayam!' for in you the fatherless finds racham (mercy).
"I will heal their waywardness. I will ahab (love) them nadabah (freely); for my ap (anger) is turned shawab (turn back / repent) from him.
I will be like the dew to Yasharaal (Israel). He will blossom like the lily, and send down his roots like Labanawan.
His branches will yalak (spread), and his hawad (beauty) will be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like Labanawan.
Men will live in his shade. They will chayah (revive) like the grain, and blossom like the vine. Their fragrance will be like the yayan (wine) of Labanawan.
Aparayam, what have I to do any more with itzab (idols)? I answer, and will take care of him. I am like a Rainan fir tree; from me your fruit is found.

Who is chakam (wise), that he may bayan (understand) these things? Who is bayan (prudent), that he may yadai (know) them? For the darak (ways) of Yahawah are yashar (right), and the tzadayaq (righteous) yalak (walk) in them; But the rebellious stumble in them.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah that came to Yawaal, the ban (son) of Pathawaal.
Hear this, you zaqan (elders), And listen, all you yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land). Has this ever happened in your yawam (days), or in the yawam (days) of your abawath (fathers)?
Tell your children about it, and have your children tell their children, and their children, achar (another) dawar (generation).

What the swarming locust has yathar (left), the great locust has eaten. What the great locust has yathar (left), the grasshopper has eaten. What the grasshopper has yathar (left), the caterpillar has eaten.
qawatz (wake) up, you drunkards, and weep! Wail, all you drinkers of yayan (wine), because of the sweet isayas (wine); for it is karath (cut) off from your pah (mouth).
For a gaway (nation) has ilah (come) up on my aratz (land), itzawam (strong), and without number. His teeth are the teeth of a aray (lion), and he has the fangs of a labayaa (lioness).
He has laid my vine waste, and stripped my fig tree. He has stripped its bark, and thrown it away. Its branches are made white.
Mourn like a virgin dressed in sackcloth for the bail (husband) of her youth!
The meal manachah (offering) and the drink nasak (offering) are karath (cut) off from yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house). The kahan (priests), yahawah (yahweh's) sharath (ministers), mourn.
The shadah (field) is laid shadad (waste). The adamah (land) mourns, for the grain is destroyed, The new thayarawash (wine) has dried up, and the yatzahar (oil) languishes.
Be yabash (confounded), you farmers! Wail, you vineyard keepers; for the wheat and for the barley; for the harvest of the shadah (field) has perished.

The vine has dried up, and the fig tree withered; the pomegranate tree, the palm tree also, and the apple tree, even all of the itz (trees) of the shadah (field) are withered; for joy has withered away from the ban (sons) of men.

Put on sackcloth and mourn, you kahan (priests)! Wail, you sharath (ministers) of the mazabach (altar). bawaa (come), lie all lawan (night) in sackcloth, you sharath (ministers) of my Alahayam, for the meal manachah (offering) and the drink nasak (offering) are withheld from your alahayam (god's) bayath (house).

qadash (sanctify) a fast. qaraa (call) a solemn itzarah (assembly). asap (gather) the zaqan (elders), and all the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land), to the bayath (house) of Yahawah, your Alahayam, and cry to Yahawah.
Alas for the yawam (day)! For the yawam (day) of Yahawah is at qarawab (hand), and it will bawaa (come) as destruction from the Shaday.
Isn't the food karath (cut) off before our iyan (eyes); joy and gladness from the bayath (house) of our Alahayam?
The paradah (seeds) rot under their clods. The granaries are laid shamam (desolate). The barns are broken down, for the grain has withered.
How the animals groan! The herds of livestock are perplexed, because they have no pasture. Yes, the flocks of sheep are asham (made) desolate.
Yahawah, I qaraa (cry) to you, For the ash (fire) has devoured the naah (pastures) of the madabar (wilderness), and the lahabah (flame) has burned all the itz (trees) of the shadah (field).
Yes, the animals of the shadah (field) pant to you, for the mayam (water) apayaq (brooks) have dried up, And the ash (fire) has devoured the naah (pastures) of the madabar (wilderness).

Blow the trumpet in Tzayawan, and rawai (sound) an alarm in my qadash (holy) har (mountain)! Let all the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land) tremble, for the yawam (day) of Yahawah bawaa (comes), for it is close at qarawab (hand):

A yawam (day) of chashak (darkness) and apalah (gloominess), a yawam (day) of clouds and thick irapal (darkness). As the dawn spreading on the har (mountains), a rab (great) and itzawam (strong) im (people); there has never been the like, neither will there be any more achar (after) them, even to the Shanah of many dawar (generations).

A ash (fire) akal (devours) panayam (before) them, and achar (behind) them, a lahabah (flame) lahat (burns). The aratz (land) is as the Gan of Idan panayam (before) them, and achar (behind) them, a desolate madabar (wilderness). Yes, and no one has palayatah (escaped) them.
Their appearance is as the appearance of horses, and as horsemen, so do they run.

Like the qawal (noise) of chariots on the raash (tops) of the har (mountains) do they leap, like the qawal (noise) of a lahab (flame) of ash (fire) that akal (devours) the stubble, as a itzawam (strong) im (people) set in battle array.
At their panayam (presence) the im (peoples) are in anguish. All panayam (faces) have grown pale.
They run like gabawar (mighty) men. They ilah (climb) the wall like warriors. They ayash (each) yalak (march) in his line, and they don't swerve off course.
Neither does one jostle ach (another); they yalak (march) everyone in his masalah (path), and they burst through the defenses, and don't break ranks.
They rush on the Iyar. They run on the wall. They ilah (climb) up into the bayath (houses). They bawaa (enter) in at the windows like thieves.
The aratz (earth) quakes panayam (before) them. The shamayam (heavens) tremble. The shamash (sun) and the yarach (moon) are darkened, and the kawakab (stars) asap (withdraw) their nagah (shining).

Yahawah thunders his qawal (voice) panayam (before) his chayal (army); for his forces are very rab (great); for he is itzawam (strong) who obeys his command; for the yawam (day) of Yahawah is gadawal (great) and very awesome, and who can endure it?
"Yet even now," says Yahawah, "shawab (turn back / repent) to me with all your labab (heart), and with fasting, and with weeping, and with mourning.

Tear your labab (heart), and not your bagad (garments), and shawab (turn back / repent) to Yahawah, your Alahayam; for he is Chanawan and Rachawam, Arak to ap (anger), and abundant in loving chasad (kindness), and relents from sending rai (calamity).

Who yadai (knows)? He may shawab (turn back / repent) and relent, and shaar (leave) a barakah (blessing) achar (behind) him, even a meal manachah (offering) and a drink nasak (offering) to Yahawah, your Alahayam.
Blow the trumpet in Tzayawan! qadash (sanctify) a fast. qaraa (call) a solemn itzarah (assembly).

asap (gather) the im (people). qadash (sanctify) the qahal (assembly). Assemble the zaqan (elders). asap (gather) the children, and those who nurse from breasts. Let the chathan (bridegroom) yatzaa (go) forth from his room, and the kalah (bride) out of her room.

Let the kahan (priests), the sharath (ministers) of Yahawah, weep between the porch and the mazabach (altar), and let them amar (say), "Spare your im (people), Yahawah, and don't nathan (give) your nachalah (heritage) to reproach, that the gawayam (nations) should mashal (rule) over them. Why should they amar (say) among the im (peoples), ‘Where is their Alahayam?'
Then Yahawah was jealous for his aratz (land), And had pity on his im (people).

Yahawah answered his im (people), "Behold, I will shalach (send) you grain, new thayarawash (wine), and yatzahar (oil), and you will be satisfied with them; and I will no more nathan (make) you a reproach among the gawayam (nations).

But I will remove the Tzapawanay army rachaq (far) away from you, and will drive it into a tzayah (barren) and desolate aratz (land), its panayam (front) Qadamawanay the eastern yam (sea), and its back Acharawan the western yam (sea); and its stench will ilah (come) up, and its bad smell will ilah (rise)." ishah (surely) he has done great things.
adamah (land), don't be yaraa (afraid). Be glad and Shamach, for Yahawah has done great things.

Don't be yaraa (afraid), you animals of the shadah (field); for the naah (pastures) of the madabar (wilderness) spring up, for the itz (tree) nashaa (bears) its fruit. The fig tree and the vine nathan (yield) their chayal (strength).

"Be glad then, you children of Tzayawan, and Shamach in Yahawah, your Alahayam; for he nathan (gives) you the former rain in just measure, and he causes the rain to yarad (come) down for you, the former rain and the latter rain, as raashawan (before).
The threshing floors will be malaa (full) of wheat, and the vats will shawaq (overflow) with new thayarawash (wine) and yatzahar (oil).
I will shalam (restore) to you the Shanah that the swarming locust has eaten, the great locust, the grasshopper, and the caterpillar, my gadawal (great) chayal (army), which I sent among you.

You will have akal (plenty) to akal (eat), and be satisfied, and will halal (praise) the sham (name) of Yahawah, your Alahayam, who has dealt wondrously with you; and my im (people) will never again be disappointed.
You will yadai (know) that I am in the qarab (midst) of Yasharaal (Israel), and that I am Yahawah, your Alahayam, and there is no one else; and my im (people) will never again be disappointed.

"It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my rawach (spirit) on all flesh; and your ban (sons) and your bath (daughters) will nabaa (prophesy). Your zaqan (old) men will dream chalawam (dreams). Your young men will raah (see) visions.
And also on the ibad (servants) and on the handmaids in those yawam (days), I will pour out my rawach (spirit).
I will show mawapath (wonders) in the shamayam (heavens) and in the aratz (earth): dam (blood), ash (fire), and pillars of ishan (smoke).
The shamash (sun) will be turned into chashak (darkness), and the yarach (moon) into dam (blood), panayam (before) the gadawal (great) and yaraa (terrible) yawam (day) of Yahawah bawaa (comes).

It will happen that whoever will qaraa (call) on the sham (name) of Yahawah shall be saved; for in har (mount) Tzayawan and in Yarawashalam there will be those who palayatah (escape), as Yahawah has said, and among the sharayad (remnant), those whom Yahawah qaraa (calls).
"For, behold, in those yawam (days), and in that ith (time), when I shabawath (restore) the fortunes of Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam,

I will gather all gaway (nations), and will yarad (bring) them down into the valley of Yahawashapat; and I will execute shapat (judgment) on them there for my im (people), and for my nachalah (heritage), Yasharaal (Israel), whom they have scattered among the gaway (nations). They have divided my aratz (land),
and have cast lots for my im (people), and have given a yalad (boy) for a prostitute, and sold a girl for yayan (wine), that they may drink.

"Yes, and what are you to me, Tzar, and Tzayadawan, and all the regions of Palashath? Will you repay me? And if you repay me, I will qal (swiftly) and speedily shawab (turn back / repent) your repayment on your own raash (head).
Because you have taken my kasap (silver) and my gold, and have carried my finest treasures into your hayakal (temples),
and have sold the children of Yahawadah (Judah) and the children of Yarawashalam Yawanay the sons of the Greeks, that you may rachaq (remove) them far from their border.
Behold, I will stir them up out of the place where you have sold them, and will shawab (turn back / repent) your repayment on your own raash (head);

and I will sell your ban (sons) and your bath (daughters) into the yad (hands) of the children of Yahawadah (Judah), and they will sell them Shabaay the men of Sheba, Rachawaq a faraway gaway (nation), for Yahawah has spoken it.
qaraa (proclaim) this among the gaway (nations): "qadash (prepare) for war! Stir up the gabawar (mighty) men. Let all the warriors draw near. Let them ilah (come) up.
kathath (beat) your plowshares into charab (swords), and your pruning hooks into spears. Let the Chalash amar (say), ‘I am gabawar (strong).'
Hurry and bawaa (come), all you surrounding gaway (nations), and gather yourselves together." Cause your gabawar (mighty) ones to come down there, Yahawah.
"Let the gaway (nations) arouse themselves, and ilah (come) up to the valley of Yahawashapat; for there will I yashab (sit) to shapat (judge) all the surrounding gaway (nations).
shalach (put) in the sickle; for the harvest is ripe. bawaa (come), tread, for the winepress is malaa (full), the vats shawaq (overflow), for their wickedness is rab (great).
Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of Charawatz! For the yawam (day) of Yahawah is qarawab (near), in the valley of Charawatz.
The shamash (sun) and the yarach (moon) are darkened, and the kawakab (stars) asap (withdraw) their nagah (shining).

Yahawah will roar from Tzayawan, and qawal (thunder) from Yarawashalam; and the shamayam (heavens) and the aratz (earth) will shake; but Yahawah will be a refuge to his im (people), and a stronghold to the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

"So you will yadai (know) that I am Yahawah, your Alahayam, dwelling in Tzayawan, my qadash (holy) har (mountain). Then Yarawashalam will be qadash (holy), and no strangers will ibar (pass) through her any more.

It will happen in that yawam (day), that the har (mountains) will natap (drop) down sweet isayas (wine), the Gabaih will yalak (flow) with milk, all the apayaq (brooks) of Yahawadah (Judah) will yalak (flow) with mayam (waters), and a fountain will yatzaa (come) forth from the bayath (house) of Yahawah, and will shaqah (water) the nachal (valley) of Shatayam.

Matzarayam will be a desolation, and Adam will be a desolate madabar (wilderness), for the violence done to the children of Yahawadah (Judah), because they have shed naqay (innocent) dam (blood) in their aratz (land).
But Yahawadah (Judah) will be inhabited iwalam (forever), and Yarawashalam from dawar (generation) to dawar (generation).
I will cleanse their dam (blood), that I have not cleansed: for Yahawah shakan (dwells) in Tzayawan.

The dabar (words) of Imawas, who was among the herdsmen of Thaqawai, which he saw concerning Yasharaal (Israel) in the yawam (days) of Izayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah), and in the yawam (days) of Yarabaim the ban (son) of Yawaash malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), two Shanah panayam (before) the earthquake.

He said: "Yahawah will roar from Tzayawan, and nathan (utter) his qawal (voice) from Yarawashalam; and the naah (pastures) of the raih (shepherds) will mourn, and the raash (top) of Karamal will yabash (wither).

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of Damashaq, yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they have threshed Galaid with Charawatz instruments of barazal (iron);
but I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) into the bayath (house) of Chazaal, and it will akal (devour) the palaces Banahadad Ben Hadad.

I will shabar (break) the bar of Damashaq, and karath (cut) off the yashab (inhabitant) from the Baqaih of Awan, and him who holds the scepter from the bayath (house) of Idan; and the im (people) of Aram shall galah (go) into captivity to Qayar," amar (says) Yahawah.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of Izah, yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they carried away galah (captive) the Shalam community, to deliver them up to Adam;
but I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on the wall of Izah, and it will akal (devour) its palaces.

I will karath (cut) off the yashab (inhabitant) Ashadawad Ashdod, and him who holds the scepter from Ashaqalawan; and I will shawab (turn back / repent) my yad (hand) against Iqarawan; and the shaarayath (remnant) of the Palashathay (Philistines) will abad (perish)," amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of Tzar, yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they delivered up the Shalam community to Adam, and didn't zakar (remember) the ach (brotherly) barayath (covenant);
but I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on the wall of Tzar, and it will akal (devour) its palaces.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of Adam, yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because he pursued his ach (brother) with the charab (sword), and shachath (cast) off all racham (pity), and his ap (anger) raged continually, and he kept his ibarah (wrath) forever;
but I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on Thayaman, and it will akal (devour) the palaces of Batzarah.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of the children of Imawan, yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they have ripped open the pregnant women of Galaid, that they may enlarge their border.

But I will yatzath (kindle) a ash (fire) in the wall of Rabah, and it will akal (devour) its palaces, with shouting in the yawam (day) of battle, with a storm in the yawam (day) of the sawapah (whirlwind);
and their malak (king) will halak (go) into captivity, he and his shar (princes) together," amar (says) Yahawah.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of Mawaab, yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because he burned the itzam (bones) of the malak (king) of Adam into lime;

but I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on Mawaab, and it will akal (devour) the palaces of Qarayawath; and Mawaab will mawath (die) with tumult, with shouting, and with the qawal (sound) of the trumpet;
and I will karath (cut) off the shapat (judge) from their qarab (midst), and will harag (kill) all its shar (princes) with him," amar (says) Yahawah.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of Yahawadah (Judah), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they have rejected yahawah (yahweh's) thawarah (law), and have not kept his chaq (statutes), and their lies have led them thaih (astray), achar (after) which their abawath (fathers) walked;
But I will shalach (send) a ash (fire) on Yahawadah (Judah), and it will akal (devour) the palaces of Yarawashalam.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: "For shalawash (three) pashai (transgressions) of Yasharaal (Israel), yes, for arabai (four), I will not shawab (turn back / repent) away its punishment; because they have sold the tzadayaq (righteous) for kasap (silver), and the Abayawan for a pair of shoes;

They trample on the ipar (dust) of the aratz (earth) on the raash (head) of the Dal, and deny justice Inaw the oppressed; and a ayash (man) and his ab (father) use the same maiden, to chalal (profane) my qadash (holy) sham (name);

and they natah (lay) themselves down beside every mazabach (altar) on clothes taken in chabal (pledge); and in the bayath (house) of their Alahayam they drink the yayan (wine) of those who have been fined.

Yet I destroyed the Amaray (Amorite) panayam (before) them, whose height was like the height of the cedars, and he was Chasan as the oaks; yet I destroyed his fruit from above, and his roots from beneath.
Also I brought you up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and led you arabaiyam (forty) Shanah in the madabar (wilderness), to yarash (possess) the aratz (land) of the Amaray (Amorite).
I raised up some of your ban (sons) for nabayaa (prophets), and some of your young men for Nazirites. Isn't this true, you children of Yasharaal (Israel)?" says Yahawah.
"But you gave the Nazirites yayan (wine) to shaqah (drink), and tzawah (commanded) the nabayaa (prophets), saying, ‘Don't nabaa (prophesy)!'
Behold, I will iwaq (crush) you in your place, as a cart crushes that is Malaa of grain.
manawas (flight) will abad (perish) from the qal (swift); and the chazaq (strong) won't amatz (strengthen) his kach (force); neither shall the gabawar (mighty) malat (deliver) himself;
neither shall he imad (stand) who handles the qashath (bow); and he who is qal (swift) of ragal (foot) won't malat (escape); neither shall he who rides the horse malat (deliver) himself;
and he who is amayatz (courageous) among the gabawar (mighty) will flee away Irawam on that yawam (day)," says Yahawah.
Hear this dabar (word) that Yahawah has spoken against you, children of Yasharaal (Israel), against the whole mashapachah (family) which I brought up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, saying:
"You only have I chosen of all the mashapachah (families) of the adamah (earth). Therefore I will paqad (punish) you for all of your iwan (sins).
Do shanayam (two) yalak (walk) together, unless they have agreed?
Will a aray (lion) roar Yair the thicket, when he has no Tarap? Does a young kapayar (lion) nathan (cry) out of his den, if he has caught balathay (nothing)?
Can a bird napal (fall) in a trap on the aratz (earth), where no snare is set for him? Does a snare ilah (spring) up from the adamah (ground), when there is nothing to catch?
Does the trumpet alarm sound in a Iyar, without the im (people) being afraid? Does rai (evil) happen to a Iyar, and Yahawah hasn't done it?
Surely the Adanay Yahawah will do nothing, unless he galah (reveals) his sawad (secret) to his ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets).
The aray (lion) has roared. Who will not yaraa (fear)? The Adanay Yahawah has spoken. Who can but nabaa (prophesy)?

Proclaim in the palaces Ashadawad Ashdod, and in the palaces in the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and amar (say), "asap (assemble) yourselves on the har (mountains) of Shamarawan, and raah (see) what unrest is in her, and what oppression is among them.
"Indeed they don't yadai (know) to do Nakachah," says Yahawah, "Who hoard plunder and loot in their palaces.
Therefore thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: "An tzar (adversary) will overrun the aratz (land); and he will pull down your strongholds, and your fortresses will be plundered.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: "As the raih (shepherd) natzal (rescues) out of the pah (mouth) of the aray (lion) shanayam (two) legs, or a piece of an ear, so shall the children of Yasharaal (Israel) be rescued who yashab (sit) in Shamarawan on the corner of a couch, and Damashaq the silken cushions of a bed.
"Listen, and iwad (testify) against the bayath (house) of Yaiqab," says the Adanay Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies).

"For in the yawam (day) that I paqad (visit) the pashai (transgressions) of Yasharaal (Israel) on him, I will also paqad (visit) the mazabach (altars) of Bayathaal; and the qaran (horns) of the mazabach (altar) will be cut off, and napal (fall) to the aratz (ground).

I will strike the winter bayath (house) with the qayatz (summer) bayath (house); and the bayath (houses) of ivory will abad (perish), and the rab (great) bayath (houses) will have an sawap (end)," says Yahawah.

Listen to this dabar (word), you cows of Bashan, who are on the har (mountain) of Shamarawan, who oppress the Dal, who ratzatz (crush) the Abayawan, who amar (tell) their husbands, "bawaa (bring) us drinks!

The Adanay Yahawah has sworn by his qadash (holiness) that behold, "The yawam (days) shall bawaa (come) on you that they will nashaa (take) you away with tzanah (hooks), and the acharayath (last) of you with fish tzanah (hooks).
You will yatzaa (go) out at the breaks in the wall, everyone shalak (straight) before her; and you will cast Haramawan into Harmon," says Yahawah.

"bawaa (go) to Bayathaal, and pashai (sin); to Galagal, and pashai (sin) more. bawaa (bring) your zabach (sacrifices) every baqar (morning), your maishar (tithes) every shalawash (three) yawam (days),

qatar (offer) a qatar (sacrifice) of thanksgiving of that which is leavened, and qaraa (proclaim) free will nadabah (offerings) and Kan about them: for this pleases you, you children of Yasharaal (Israel)," says the Adanay Yahawah.
"I also have given you cleanness of teeth in all your Iyar, and lack of lacham (bread) in every town; yet you haven't returned to me," says Yahawah.

"I also have withheld the rain from you, when there were yet shalawash (three) chadash (months) to the harvest; and I caused it to rain on one Iyar, and caused it not to rain on another Iyar. One chalaqah (place) was rained on, and the chalaqah (piece) where it didn't rain withered.
So shanayam (two) or shalawash (three) Iyar staggered to one Iyar to drink mayam (water), and were not satisfied: yet you haven't returned to me," says Yahawah.

"I struck you with blight and mildew many times in your gardens and your vineyards; and your fig trees and your olive trees have the swarming locust devoured: yet you haven't returned to me," says Yahawah.

"I sent dabar (plagues) among you like I did Matzarayam. I have slain your young men with the charab (sword), and have carried Shabay your horses; and I filled your ap (nostrils) with the stench of your machanah (camp), yet you haven't returned to me," says Yahawah.
"I have overthrown some of you, as when Alahayam overthrew Sadam and Imarah, and you were like a burning stick plucked out of the sharapah (fire); yet you haven't returned to me," says Yahawah.
"Therefore thus will I do to you, Yasharaal (Israel); because I will do this to you, kawan (prepare) to qaraah (meet) your Alahayam, Yasharaal (Israel).

For, behold, he who forms the har (mountains), and baraa (creates) the rawach (wind), and nagad (declares) to adam (man) what is his thought; who ishah (makes) the shachar (morning) iyapah (darkness), and treads on the bamah (high) places of the aratz (earth): Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies), is his sham (name).
Listen to this dabar (word) which I nashaa (take) up for a lamentation over you, O bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).
"The virgin of Yasharaal (Israel) has fallen; She shall qawam (rise) no more. She is cast down on her adamah (land); there is no one to qawam (raise) her up.

For thus amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah: "The Iyar that went yatzaa (forth) a alap (thousand) shall have a maah (hundred) shaar (left), and that which went yatzaa (forth) one maah (hundred) shall have ishar (ten) shaar (left) to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel).
For thus amar (says) Yahawah to the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel): "Seek me, and you will chayah (live);
but don't seek Bayathaal, nor bawaa (enter) into Galagal, and don't ibar (pass) Baarashabai Beersheba: for Galagal shall galah (surely) galah (go) into captivity, and Bayathaal shall come to nothing.
Seek Yahawah, and you will chayah (live); lest he tzalach (break) out like ash (fire) in the bayath (house) of Yawasap, and it akal (devour), and there be no kabah (one) to quench it in Bayathaal.
You who hapak (turn) justice to wormwood, and yanach (cast) down tzadaqah (righteousness) to the aratz (earth):

seek him who made the kayamah (pleiades) and Kasayal, and hapak (turns) the shadow of tzalamawath (death) into the baqar (morning), and makes the yawam (day) chashak (dark) with layal (night); who qaraa (calls) for the mayam (waters) of the yam (sea), and pours them out on the surface of the aratz (earth), Yahawah is his sham (name),
who brings sudden destruction on the iz (strong), so that destruction bawaa (comes) on the fortress.
They shanaa (hate) him who yakach (reproves) in the gate, and they abhor him who dabar (speaks) blamelessly.

Forasmuch therefore as you trample on the Dal, and take taxes from him of wheat: You have built bayath (houses) of cut gazayath (stone), but you will not yashab (dwell) in them. You have planted pleasant vineyards, but you shall not drink their yayan (wine).

For I yadai (know) how many your offenses, and how itzawam (great) are your chataah (sins)— you who tzarar (afflict) the tzadayaq (just), who take a kapar (bribe), and who natah (turn) aside the Abayawan in the courts.
Therefore a shakal (prudent) person damam (keeps) silent in such a ith (time), for it is an rai (evil) ith (time).
Seek tawab (good), and not rai (evil), that you may chayah (live); and so Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies), will be with you, as you amar (say).

shanaa (hate) rai (evil), ahab (love) tawab (good), and establish justice in the courts. It may be that Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies), will be gracious to the shaarayath (remnant) of Yawasap.

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies), the Adanay: "Wailing will be in all the broad ways; and they will amar (say) in all the streets, ‘Alas! Alas!' and they will qaraa (call) the farmer to mourning, and those who are skillful in lamentation to wailing.
In all vineyards there will be wailing; for I will ibar (pass) qarab (through) the midst of you," amar (says) Yahawah.
"Woe to you who desire the yawam (day) of Yahawah! mah (why) do you long for the yawam (day) of Yahawah? It is chashak (darkness), and not awar (light).
As if a ayash (man) fled from a aray (lion), and a bear met him; Or he went into the bayath (house) and leaned his yad (hand) on the wall, and a snake bit him.
Won't the yawam (day) of Yahawah be chashak (darkness), and not awar (light)? Even very Apal, and no nagah (brightness) in it?
I shanaa (hate), I despise your chag (feasts), and I can't stand your solemn itzarah (assemblies).
