Yes, though you ilah (offer) me your burnt ilah (offerings) and meal manachah (offerings), I will not accept them; neither will I regard the shalam (peace) offerings of your fat animals.
sawar (take) away from me the noise of your songs! I will not listen to the music of your harps.
But let justice roll on like rivers, and tzadaqah (righteousness) like a ayathan (mighty) nachal (stream).
"Did you bring to me zabach (sacrifices) and manachah (offerings) in the madabar (wilderness) arabaiyam (forty) Shanah, bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)?
You also carried the tent of your malak (king) and the Kayawan of your tzalam (images), the kawakab (star) of your Alahayam, which you made for yourselves.
Therefore will I cause you to galah (go) into captivity beyond Damashaq," amar (says) Yahawah, whose sham (name) is the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies).

Woe to those who are at Shaanan in Tzayawan, and to those who are batach (secure) on the har (mountain) of Shamarawan, the notable men of the raashayath (chief) of the gawayam (nations), to whom the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) bawaa (come)!

ibar (go) to Kalanah, and raah (see); and from there yalak (go) to Chamath the rab (great); then yarad (go) down to gath (gath) of the Palashathay (Philistines). are they tawab (better) than these mamalakah (kingdoms)? or is their border greater than your border?
Those who put far away the rai (evil) yawam (day), and cause the seat of violence to come near;
Who shakab (lie) on beds of ivory, and sarach (stretch) themselves on their couches, and akal (eat) the lambs out of the flock, and the calves out of the midst of the stall;
who strum on the strings of a harp; who chashab (invent) for themselves instruments of music, like Dawad;
who drink yayan (wine) in mazaraq (bowls), and mashach (anoint) themselves with the best shaman (oils); but they are not chalah (grieved) for the affliction of Yawasap.
Therefore they will now galah (go) captive with the raash (first) who galah (go) captive; and the feasting and lounging will end.

"The Adanay Yahawah has sworn by himself," says Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies): "I abhor the pride of Yaiqab, and detest his fortresses. Therefore I will deliver up the Iyar with all that is in it.
It will happen, if there yathar (remain) ishar (ten) men in one bayath (house), that they shall mawath (die).

"When a man's relative nashaa (carries) him, even he who sarap (burns) him, to yatzaa (bring) bodies out of the bayath (house), and asks him who is in the innermost parts of the bayath (house), ‘Is there yet any with you?' And he amar (says), ‘No;' then he will amar (say), ‘Hush! Indeed we must not zakar (mention) the sham (name) of Yahawah.'
"For, behold, Yahawah tzawah (commands), and the gadawal (great) bayath (house) will be smashed to pieces, and the qatan (little) bayath (house) into bits.
Do horses run on the rocky crags? Does one charash (plow) there with oxen? But you have turned justice into poison, and the fruit of tzadaqah (righteousness) into bitterness;
you who Shamach in a thing of nothing, who amar (say), ‘Haven't we taken for ourselves qaran (horns) by our own chazaq (strength)?'

For, behold, I will qawam (raise) up against you a gaway (nation), bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel)," says Yahawah, the Alahayam of tzabaa (armies); "and they will lachatz (afflict) you from the entrance of Chamath to the nachal (brook) of the irabah (arabah).

Thus the Adanay Yahawah showed me: and behold, he formed locusts in the thachalah (beginning) of the shooting up of the latter growth; and behold, it was the latter growth achar (after) the malak (king's) harvest.
It happened that, when they made an kalah (end) of eating the grass of the aratz (land), then I said, "Adanay Yahawah, forgive, I beg you! How could Yaiqab qawam (stand)? For he is qatan (small).
Yahawah relented concerning this. "It shall not be," amar (says) Yahawah.
Thus the Adanay Yahawah showed me and behold, the Adanay Yahawah called for judgment by ash (fire); and it dried up the rab (great) deep, and would have devoured the land.
Then I said, "Adanay Yahawah, stop, I beg you! How could Yaiqab qawam (stand)? For he is qatan (small).
Yahawah relented concerning this. "This also shall not be," amar (says) the Adanay Yahawah.
Thus he showed me and behold, the Adanay stood beside a wall made by a plumb line, with a plumb line in his yad (hand).

Yahawah said to me, "Imawas, what do you raah (see)?" I said, "A plumb line." Then the Adanay said, "Behold, I will shawam (set) a plumb line in the qarab (midst) of my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel). I will not again ibar (pass) by them any more.

The bamah (high) places of Yashachaq will be shamam (desolate), the maqadash (sanctuaries) of Yasharaal (Israel) will be laid charab (waste); and I will qawam (rise) against the bayath (house) of Yarabaim with the charab (sword).

Then Amatzayah the kahan (priest) of Bayathaal sent to Yarabaim malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), saying, "Imawas has conspired against you in the qarab (midst) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel). The aratz (land) is not yakal (able) to bear all his dabar (words).
For Imawas amar (says), ‘Yarabaim will mawath (die) by the charab (sword), and Yasharaal (Israel) shall galah (surely) be led away galah (captive) out of his adamah (land).'
Amatzayah also said to Imawas, "You chazah (seer), yalak (go), flee away into the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah), and there akal (eat) lacham (bread), and nabaa (prophesy) there:
but don't nabaa (prophesy) again any more at Bayathaal; for it is the malak (king's) maqadash (sanctuary), and it is a mamalakah (royal) bayath (house)!
Then Imawas answered Amatzayah, "I was no nabayaa (prophet), neither was I a nabayaa (prophet's) ban (son); but I was a herdsman, and a farmer of sycamore figs;
and Yahawah took me from following the flock, and Yahawah said to me, ‘yalak (go), nabaa (prophesy) to my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel).'
Now therefore listen to the dabar (word) of Yahawah: ‘You amar (say), Don't nabaa (prophesy) against Yasharaal (Israel), and don't preach against the bayath (house) of Yashachaq.'

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah: ‘Your ashah (wife) shall be a prostitute in the Iyar, and your ban (sons) and your bath (daughters) shall napal (fall) by the charab (sword), and your adamah (land) shall be divided by line; and you yourself shall mawath (die) in a adamah (land) that is tamaa (unclean), and Yasharaal (Israel) shall galah (surely) be led away galah (captive) out of his adamah (land).'
Thus the Adanay Yahawah showed me: behold, a basket of qayatz (summer) fruit.

He said, "Imawas, what do you raah (see)?" I said, "A basket of qayatz (summer) fruit." Then Yahawah said to me, "The end has bawaa (come) on my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel). I will not again ibar (pass) by them any more.
The songs of the hayakal (temple) will be wailings in that yawam (day)," says the Adanay Yahawah. "The pagar (dead) bodies will be many. In every place they will throw them out with hasah (silence).
Hear this, you who desire to swallow up the Abayawan, and shabath (cause) the Inay of the aratz (land) to shabath (fail),

Saying, ‘When will the new chadash (moon) be gone, that we may sell grain? And the shabath (sabbath), that we may market wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel large, and dealing falsely with balances of deceit;
that we may qanah (buy) the Dal for kasap (silver), and the Abayawan for a pair of shoes, and sell the sweepings with the wheat?'
Yahawah has sworn by the pride of Yaiqab, "Surely I will never forget any of their maishah (works).

Won't the aratz (land) tremble for this, and everyone mourn who yashab (dwells) in it? Yes, it will ilah (rise) up wholly like the yaar (river); and it will be stirred up and sink again, like the River of Matzarayam.

It will happen in that yawam (day)," says the Adanay Yahawah, "that I will cause the shamash (sun) to bawaa (go) down at tzahar (noon), and I will chashak (darken) the aratz (earth) in the awar (clear) yawam (day).

I will hapak (turn) your chag (feasts) into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation; and I will ilah (make) you wear sackcloth on all your bodies, and baldness on every raash (head). I will shawam (make) it like the mourning for an only son, and its acharayath (end) like a Mar yawam (day).

Behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come)," says the Adanay Yahawah, "that I will shalach (send) a famine in the aratz (land), not a famine of lacham (bread), nor a thirst for mayam (water), but of hearing the dabar (words) of Yahawah.
They will wander from yam (sea) to yam (sea), and from the tzapawan (north) even to the east; they will run back and forth to seek the dabar (word) of Yahawah, and will not matzaa (find) it.
In that yawam (day) the Yapah virgins and the young men will faint for thirst.

Those who shabai (swear) by the ashamah (sin) of Shamarawan, and amar (say), ‘As your Alahayam, Dan, chay (lives);' and, ‘As the darak (way) Baarashabai Beersheba chay (lives);' they will napal (fall), and never qawam (rise) up again.

I saw the Adanay standing beside the mazabach (altar), and he said, "Strike the tops of the pillars, that the thresholds may shake; and break them in pieces on the raash (head) of all of them; and I will harag (kill) the acharayath (last) of them with the charab (sword): there shall not nawas (one) of them flee away, and there shall not palayat (one) of them escape.
Though they dig into shaawal (sheol), there my yad (hand) will take them; and though they ilah (climb) up to shamayam (heaven), there I will yarad (bring) them down.

Though they hide themselves in the raash (top) of Karamal, I will search and take them out there; and though they be hidden from my iyan (sight) in the bottom of the yam (sea), there I will tzawah (command) the serpent, and it will bite them.

Though they yalak (go) into Shabay panayam (before) their ayab (enemies), there I will tzawah (command) the charab (sword), and it will harag (kill) them. I will shawam (set) my iyan (eyes) on them for rai (evil), and not for tawab (good).

For the Adanay, Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), is he who touches the aratz (land) and it melts, and all who yashab (dwell) in it will mourn; and it will ilah (rise) up wholly like the yaar (river), and will sink again, like the yaar (river) of Matzarayam.

It is he who banah (builds) his rooms in the shamayam (heavens), and has founded his vault on the aratz (earth); he who qaraa (calls) for the mayam (waters) of the yam (sea), and pours them out on the surface of the aratz (earth); Yahawah is his sham (name).

Are you not like the children of the Kawashay (Ethiopians) to me, children of Yasharaal (Israel)?" says Yahawah. "Haven't I brought up Yasharaal (Israel) out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and the Palashathay (Philistines) from Kapathar, and the Aram (Syrians) from Qayar?

Behold, the iyan (eyes) of the Adanay Yahawah are on the sinful mamalakah (kingdom), and I will destroy it from off the surface of the adamah (earth); except that I will not shamad (utterly) destroy the bayath (house) of Yaiqab," says Yahawah.

"For, behold, I will tzawah (command), and I will sift the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel) among all the gawayam (nations), as grain is sifted in a sieve, yet not the tzarawar (least) kernel will napal (fall) on the aratz (earth).
All the chataa (sinners) of my im (people) will mawath (die) by the charab (sword), who amar (say), ‘rai (evil) won't overtake nor qadam (meet) us.'

In that yawam (day) I will qawam (raise) up the sakah (tent) of Dawad who is fallen, and close up its breaches, and I will qawam (raise) up its ruins, and I will banah (build) it as in the yawam (days) of old;
that they may yarash (possess) the shaarayath (remnant) of Adam, and all the gawayam (nations) who are called by my sham (name)," says Yahawah who does this.

"Behold, the yawam (days) bawaa (come)," says Yahawah, "that the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the darak (one) treading inab (grapes) him who sows zarai (seed); and sweet isayas (wine) will drip Gabaih the mountains, and flow from the Gabaih.

I will bring my im (people) Yasharaal (Israel) shawab (turn back / repent) from captivity, and they will rebuild the ruined Iyar, and yashab (inhabit) them; and they will plant vineyards, and drink yayan (wine) from them. They shall also ishah (make) gardens, and akal (eat) their fruit.
I will plant them on their adamah (land), and they will no more be plucked up out of their adamah (land) which I have given them," amar (says) Yahawah your Alahayam.

The vision of Ibadayah. This is what the Adanay Yahawah amar (says) about Adam. We have heard news from Yahawah, and an tzayar (ambassador) is sent among the gawayam (nations), saying, "qawam (arise), and let's qawam (rise) up against her in battle.
Behold, I have made you qatan (small) among the gawayam (nations). You are maad (greatly) despised.

The pride of your lab (heart) has deceived you, you who shakan (dwell) in the clefts of the salai (rock), whose yashab (habitation) is high, who amar (says) in his lab (heart), ‘Who will yarad (bring) me down to the aratz (ground)?'
Though you mount on high as the eagle, and though your nest is shawam (set) among the kawakab (stars), I will yarad (bring) you down from there," says Yahawah.

"If thieves came to you, if shadad (robbers) by layal (night)— oh, what disaster awaits you— wouldn't they only steal until they had enough? If grape pickers came to you, wouldn't they shaar (leave) some gleaning grapes?
How Ishaw will be ransacked! How his hidden treasures are sought out!

All the men of your alliance have brought you on your gabawal (way), even to the border. The men who were at shalawam (peace) with you have deceived you, and prevailed against you. Friends who eat your lacham (bread) shawam (lay) a snare under you. There is no thabawan (understanding) in him.
"Won't I in that yawam (day)," says Yahawah, "abad (destroy) the chakam (wise) men out of Adam, and thabawan (understanding) out of the har (mountain) of Ishaw?
Your gabawar (mighty) men, Thayaman, will be dismayed, to the end that everyone may be karath (cut) off from the har (mountain) of Ishaw by slaughter.
For the violence done to your ach (brother) Yaiqab, shame will cover you, and you will be karath (cut) off iwalam (forever).

In the yawam (day) that you stood on the other side, in the yawam (day) that strangers carried away his chayal (substance), and nakaray (foreigners) entered into his gates, and cast lots for Yarawashalam, even you were like one of them.

But don't raah (see) down on your ach (brother) in the yawam (day) of his disaster, and don't Shamach over the children of Yahawadah (Judah) in the yawam (day) of their abad (destruction). Don't speak proudly in the yawam (day) of tzarah (distress).

Don't bawaa (enter) into the gate of my im (people) in the yawam (day) of their calamity. Don't raah (see) down on their rai (affliction) in the yawam (day) of their calamity, neither seize their wealth on the yawam (day) of their calamity.
Don't imad (stand) in the crossroads to karath (cut) off those of his who escape. Don't deliver up those of his who sharayad (remain) in the yawam (day) of tzarah (distress).
For the yawam (day) of Yahawah is qarawab (near) all the gawayam (nations)! As you have done, it will be done to you. Your deeds will shawab (turn back / repent) upon your own raash (head).
For as you have drunk on my qadash (holy) har (mountain), so will all the gawayam (nations) drink continually. Yes, they will drink, swallow down, and will be as laa (though) they had not been.
But in har (mount) Tzayawan, there will be those who palayatah (escape), and it will be qadash (holy). The bayath (house) of Yaiqab will yarash (possess) their mawarash (possessions).

The bayath (house) of Yaiqab will be a ash (fire), the bayath (house) of Yawasap a lahabah (flame), and the bayath (house) of Ishaw for stubble. They will dalaq (burn) among them, and akal (devour) them. There will not be any sharayad (remaining) to the bayath (house) of Ishaw." Indeed, Yahawah has spoken.

Those of the Nagab will yarash (possess) the har (mountain) of Ishaw, and those of the lowland, the Palashathay (Philistines). They will yarash (possess) the shadah (field) of Aparayam, and the shadah (field) of Shamarawan. Banayamayan will possess Galaid.

The captives of this chayal (army) of the children of Yasharaal (Israel), who are among the Kanainay (Canaanites), will possess even to Tzarapath; and the captives of Yarawashalam, who are in Saparad, will yarash (possess) the Iyar Nagab the Negev.
Saviors will ilah (go) up on har (mount) Tzayawan to shapat (judge) the har (mountains) of Ishaw, and the malawakah (kingdom) will be yahawah (yahweh's).
Now the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Yawanah the ban (son) of Amathay, saying,
"qawam (arise), yalak (go) to Nayanawah, that gadawal (great) Iyar, and qaraa (preach) against it, for their wickedness has ilah (come) up panayam (before) me.

But Yawanah rose up to flee to Tharashayash from the panayam (presence) of Yahawah. He went down to Yapaw, and found a ship going to Tharashayash; so he paid its fare, and went down into it, to bawaa (go) with them to Tharashayash from the panayam (presence) of Yahawah.
But Yahawah sent out a gadawal (great) rawach (wind) on the yam (sea), and there was a gadawal (mighty) storm on the yam (sea), so that the ship was likely to shabar (break) up.

Then the mariners were yaraa (afraid), and every ayash (man) cried to his Alahayam. They threw the cargo that was in the ship into the yam (sea) to lighten the ship. But Yawanah had gone down into the innermost parts of the ship, and he was laying down, and was radam (fast) asleep.
So the rab (shipmaster) came to him, and said to him, "What do you mean, sleeper? qawam (arise), qaraa (call) on your Alahayam! Maybe your Alahayam will notice us, so that we won't abad (perish).

They all said to ayash (each) other, "yalak (come), let us napal (cast) lots, that we may yadai (know) who is responsible for this rai (evil) that is on us." So they napal (cast) lots, and the lot napal (fell) on Yawanah.

Then they asked him, "nagad (tell) us, please, for whose cause this rai (evil) is on us. What is your malaakah (occupation)? Where do you bawaa (come) from? What is your aratz (country)? Of what im (people) are you?
He said to them, "I am a ibaray (hebrew), and I yaraa (fear) Yahawah, the Alahayam of shamayam (heaven), who has made the yam (sea) and the dry yabashah (dry land).

Then were the men gadawal (exceedingly) yaraa (afraid), and said to him, "What is this that you have done?" For the men knew that he was fleeing from the panayam (presence) of Yahawah, because he had told them.
Then they said to him, "What shall we do to you, that the yam (sea) may be calm to us?" For the yam (sea) grew more and more stormy.
He said to them, "nashaa (take) me up, and throw me into the yam (sea). Then the yam (sea) will be calm for you; for I yadai (know) that because of me this gadawal (great) storm is on you.
Nevertheless the men rowed hard to shawab (turn back / repent) them back to the yabashah (dry land); but they could not, for the yam (sea) grew more and more stormy against them.

Therefore they cried to Yahawah, and said, "We beg you, Yahawah, we beg you, don't let us die for this ayash (man's) napash (life), and don't nathan (lay) on us naqay (innocent) dam (blood); for you, Yahawah, have done as it pleased you.
So they took up Yawanah, and threw him into the yam (sea); and the yam (sea) ceased its zaip (raging).
Then the men feared Yahawah gadawal (exceedingly); and they offered a zabach (sacrifice) to Yahawah, and made nadar (vows).
Yahawah prepared a gadawal (great) fish to balai (swallow) up Yawanah, and he was in the maih (belly) of the fish shalawash (three) yawam (days) and shalawash (three) layal (nights).
Then Yawanah prayed to Yahawah, his Alahayam, out of the fish's maih (belly).
He said, "I called because of my tzarah (affliction) to Yahawah. He answered me. Out of the belly of shaawal (sheol) I cried. You heard my qawal (voice).
For you threw me into the depths, in the labab (heart) of the yam (seas). The nahar (flood) was all around me. All your waves and your billows passed over me.
I said, ‘I have been banished from your iyan (sight); yet I will look again toward your qadash (holy) hayakal (temple).'
The mayam (waters) surrounded me, even to the napash (soul). The deep was around me. The weeds were wrapped around my raash (head).
I went down to the bottoms of the har (mountains). The aratz (earth) barred me in iwalam (forever): yet have you brought up my chay (life) from the shachath (pit), Yahawah my Alahayam.
"When my napash (soul) fainted within me, I zakar (remembered) Yahawah. My prayer came in to you, into your qadash (holy) hayakal (temple).
Those who shamar (regard) lying vanities forsake their own chasad (mercy).
But I will zabach (sacrifice) to you with the qawal (voice) of thanksgiving. I will shalam (pay) that which I have vowed. yashawaih (salvation) belongs to Yahawah.
Yahawah spoke to the fish, and it vomited out on the dry yabashah (dry land).
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Yawanah the shanay (second) time, saying,
"qawam (arise), yalak (go) to Nayanawah, that gadawal (great) Iyar, and qaraa (preach) to it the message that I dabar (give) you.
So Yawanah qawam (arose), and went to Nayanawah, according to the dabar (word) of Yahawah. Now Nayanawah was an exceedingly gadawal (great) Iyar, shalawash (three) yawam (days)' journey across.
He began to bawaa (enter) into the Iyar a yawam (day's) journey, and he cried out, and said, "In arabaiyam (forty) yawam (days), Nayanawah will be overthrown!
The anawash (people) of Nayanawah believed Alahayam; and they proclaimed a fast, and Labash on sackcloth, from their greatest even to their qatan (least).
The news reached the malak (king) of Nayanawah, and he qawam (arose) from his kasaa (throne), and took off his royal adarath (robe), covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.

He made a proclamation and published through Nayanawah by the taim (decree) of the malak (king) and his gadawal (nobles), saying, "Let neither adam (man) nor animal, herd nor flock, taste anything; let them not raih (feed), nor drink mayam (water);

but let them be covered with sackcloth, both adam (man) and animal, and let them qaraa (cry) mightily to Alahayam. Yes, let them shawab (turn back / repent) everyone from his rai (evil) darak (way), and from the violence that is in his kap (hands).

Who yadai (knows) whether Alahayam will not shawab (turn back / repent) and relent, and shawab (turn back / repent) shawab (turn back / repent) from his charawan (fierce) ap (anger), so that we might not abad (perish)?
Alahayam saw their maishah (works), that they turned from their rai (evil) darak (way). Alahayam relented of the disaster which he said he would do to them, and he didn't do it.
But it displeased Yawanah gadawal (exceedingly), and he was charah (angry).

He prayed to Yahawah, and said, "Please, Yahawah, wasn't this dabar (what) I said when I was still in my own adamah (country)? Therefore I hurried to flee to Tharashayash, for I knew that you are a Chanawan Al, and Rachawam, Arak to ap (anger), and abundant in loving chasad (kindness), and you relent of doing rai (harm).
Therefore now, Yahawah, take, I beg you, my napash (life) from me; for it is tawab (better) for me to mawath (die) than to chay (live).
Yahawah said, "Is it right for you to be charah (angry)?

Then Yawanah went out of the Iyar, and sat on the qadam (east) side of the Iyar, and there made himself a sakah (booth), and sat under it in the shade, until he might raah (see) what would become of the Iyar.

Yahawah Alahayam prepared a vine, and made it to ilah (come) up over Yawanah, that it might be a shade over his raash (head), to natzal (deliver) him from his discomfort. So he was gadawal (exceedingly) Shamach because of the vine.
But Alahayam prepared a worm at dawn the next macharath (day), and it chewed on the vine, so that it withered.

It happened, when the shamash (sun) arose, that Alahayam prepared a Charayashay qadayam (east) rawach (wind); and the shamash (sun) beat on Yawanah raash (head), so that he fainted, and requested for himself that he might mawath (die), and said, "It is tawab (better) for me to mawath (die) than to chay (live).
Alahayam said to Yawanah, "Is it right for you to be charah (angry) about the vine?" He said, "I am right to be charah (angry), even to mawath (death).
Yahawah said, "You have been concerned for the vine, for which you have not labored, neither made it grow; which ban (came) up in a night, and perished in a night.

Shouldn't I be concerned for Nayanawah, that gadawal (great) Iyar, in which are more than one hundred shanayam (twenty) rabaw (thousand) adam (persons) who can't yadai (discern) between their right yamayan (hand) and their left shamaawal (hand); and also much livestock?

The dabar (word) of Yahawah that came to Mayakah the Mawarashathay in the yawam (days) of Yawatham, Achaz, and Yachazaqayah, malak (kings) of Yahawadah (Judah), which he saw concerning Shamarawan and Yarawashalam.
Hear, you im (peoples), all of you. Listen, O aratz (earth), and all that is therein: and let the Adanay Yahawah be witness against you, the Adanay from his qadash (holy) hayakal (temple).
For, behold, Yahawah yatzaa (comes) forth out of his place, and will yarad (come) down and tread on the bamah (high) places of the aratz (earth).
The har (mountains) melt under him, and the valleys split apart, like wax panayam (before) the ash (fire), like mayam (waters) that are poured down a mawarad (steep) place.

"All this is for the disobedience of Yaiqab, and for the chataah (sins) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel). What is the disobedience of Yaiqab? Isn't it Shamarawan? And what are the bamah (high) places of Yahawadah (Judah)? Aren't they Yarawashalam?

Therefore I will shawam (make) Shamarawan like a rubble heap of the shadah (field), like places for planting vineyards; and I will pour down its aban (stones) into the Gayaa, and I will galah (uncover) its yasawad (foundations).

All her idols will be beaten to kathath (pieces), and all her temple gifts will be burned with ash (fire), and all her itzab (images) I will shamamah (destroy); for of the hire of a prostitute has she gathered them, and to the hire of a prostitute shall they shawab (turn back / repent).
For this I will lament and wail; I will yalak (go) Shawalal and Irawam; I will howl like the jackals, and moan like the bath (daughters) of owls.
For her makah (wounds) are Anash; for it has bawaa (come) even to Yahawadah (Judah). It reaches to the gate of my im (people), even to Yarawashalam.
Don't nagad (tell) it in gath (gath). Don't weep at all. At Beth Ophrah I have rolled myself in the ipar (dust).

ibar (pass) on, yashab (inhabitant) Shapayar Shaphir, in nakedness and bashath (shame). The yashab (inhabitant) of Tzaanan won't yatzaa (come) out. The wailing of Bayathahaatzal Ezel will take from you his protection.
For the yashab (inhabitant) of Marawath chawal (waits) anxiously for tawab (good), because rai (evil) has yarad (come) down from Yahawah to the gate of Yarawashalam.

Harness the chariot to the swift steed, yashab (inhabitant) of Lakayash. She was the raashayath (beginning) of chataah (sin) to the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan; For the pashai (transgressions) of Yasharaal (Israel) were found in you.
Therefore you will nathan (give) a parting shalawach (gift) to Mawarashathagath Gath. The bayath (houses) of Akazayab will be a Akazab thing to the malak (kings) of Yasharaal (Israel).
I will yet bawaa (bring) to you, yashab (inhabitant) of Maraashah. He who is the kabawad (glory) of Yasharaal (Israel) will bawaa (come) to Idalam.
Shave your gazaz (heads), and cut off your hair for the children of your delight. Enlarge your baldness like the vulture; for they have galah (gone) into captivity from you!

Woe to those who chashab (devise) awan (iniquity) and pail (work) rai (evil) on their beds! When the baqar (morning) is awar (light), they practice it, because it is in the al (power) of their yad (hand).
They covet shadah (fields), and seize them; and bayath (houses), and nashaa (take) them away: and they oppress a gabar (man) and his bayath (house), even a ayash (man) and his nachalah (heritage).

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah: "Behold, I am planning against these people a disaster, from which you will not mawash (remove) your necks, neither will you yalak (walk) haughtily; for it is an rai (evil) ith (time).

In that yawam (day) they will nashaa (take) up a parable against you, and lament with a doleful lamentation, saying, ‘We are shadad (utterly) ruined! My im (people's) possession is divided up. Indeed he mawash (takes) it from me and assigns our shadah (fields) to traitors!'
Therefore you will have no shalak (one) who divides the chabal (land) by lot in the qahal (assembly) of Yahawah.
"Don't natap (prophesy)!" They natap (prophesy). "Don't natap (prophesy) about these things. Disgrace won't overtake us.
Shall it be said, O bayath (house) of Yaiqab: "Is the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah angry? Are these his mailal (doings)? Don't my dabar (words) do yatab (good) to him who halak (walks) blamelessly?
But lately my im (people) have risen up as an ayab (enemy). You strip the robe and clothing from those who ibar (pass) by without a care, returning from battle.
You drive the women of my im (people) out from their pleasant bayath (houses); from their young children you take away my blessing iwalam (forever).
qawam (arise), and depart! For this is not your resting place, because of uncleanness that chabal (destroys), even with a grievous destruction.
If a ayash (man) walking in a rawach (spirit) of falsehood lies: "I will natap (prophesy) to you of yayan (wine) and of shakar (strong) drink;" he would be the natap (prophet) of this im (people).

I will asap (surely) asap (assemble), Yaiqab, all of you; I will surely gather the shaarayath (remnant) of Yasharaal (Israel); I will shawam (put) them together as the sheep of Bozrah, as a flock in the midst of their pasture; they will swarm with people.

He who breaks open the way goes up panayam (before) them. They break ibar (through) the gate, and yatzaa (go) out. And their malak (king) passes on panayam (before) them, with Yahawah at their raash (head).
I said, "Please listen, you raash (heads) of Yaiqab, and qatzayan (rulers) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel): Isn't it for you to yadai (know) justice?
You who shanaa (hate) the tawab (good), and ahab (love) the rai (evil); who tear off their skin, and their flesh from off their itzam (bones);
who also akal (eat) the flesh of my im (people), and flay their skin from off them, and break their itzam (bones), and chop them in pieces, as for the pot, and as flesh within the caldron.
Then they will cry to Yahawah, but he will not answer them. Yes, he will hide his panayam (face) from them at that ith (time), because they made their deeds raii (evil).

Thus amar (says) Yahawah concerning the nabayaa (prophets) who lead my im (people) thaih (astray); for those who feed their teeth, they qaraa (proclaim), "shalawam (peace)!" and whoever doesn't provide for their pah (mouths), they qadash (prepare) war against him:

"Therefore layal (night) is over you, with no vision, and it is chashak (dark) to you, that you may not divine; and the shamash (sun) will bawaa (go) down on the nabayaa (prophets), and the yawam (day) will be black over them.
The chazah (seers) shall be disappointed, and the diviners chapar (confounded). Yes, they shall all itah (cover) their lips; for there is no answer from Alahayam.

But as for me, I am malaa (full) of kach (power) by the rawach (spirit) of Yahawah, and of mashapat (judgment), and of might, to nagad (declare) to Yaiqab his disobedience, and to Yasharaal (Israel) his chataah (sin).
Please listen to this, you raash (heads) of the bayath (house) of Yaiqab, and qatzayan (rulers) of the bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), who abhor justice, and pervert all yashar (equity).
They banah (build) up Tzayawan with dam (blood), and Yarawashalam with iwal (iniquity).

Her leaders shapat (judge) for shachad (bribes), and her kahan (priests) teach for a price, and her nabayaa (prophets) of it tell fortunes for kasap (money): yet they shain (lean) on Yahawah, and amar (say), "Isn't Yahawah in the qarab (midst) of us? No disaster will bawaa (come) on us.

Therefore Tzayawan for your sake will be plowed like a shadah (field), and Yarawashalam will become heaps of rubble, and the har (mountain) of the bayath (temple) like the bamah (high) places of a Yair.

But in the acharayath (latter) yawam (days), it will happen that the har (mountain) of yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (temple) will be established on the raash (top) of the har (mountains), and it will be exalted above the Gabaih; and im (peoples) will stream to it.

Many gawayam (nations) will halak (go) and amar (say), "yalak (come), and let us ilah (go) up to the har (mountain) of Yahawah, and to the bayath (house) of the Alahayam of Yaiqab; and he will teach us of his darak (ways), and we will yalak (walk) in his arach (paths)." For out of Tzayawan will yatzaa (go) forth the thawarah (law), and the dabar (word) of Yahawah from Yarawashalam;

and he will shapat (judge) between many im (peoples), and will decide concerning itzawam (strong) gawayam (nations) Rachawaq off. They will kathath (beat) their charab (swords) into plowshares, and their spears into pruning hooks. gawayam (nation) will not nashaa (lift) up charab (sword) against gawayam (nation), neither will they learn war any more.
But they will yashab (sit) every ayash (man) under his vine and under his fig tree; and no charad (one) will make them afraid: For the pah (mouth) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) has spoken.
Indeed all the im (nations) may yalak (walk) in the sham (name) of their Alahayam; but we will yalak (walk) in the sham (name) of Yahawah our Alahayam iwalam (forever) and ever.
"In that yawam (day)," says Yahawah, "I will asap (assemble) that which is lame, and I will gather that which is driven away, and that which I have afflicted;

and I will shawam (make) that which was lame a shaarayath (remnant), and that which was cast far off a itzawam (strong) gaway (nation): and Yahawah will malak (reign) over them on har (mount) Tzayawan from then on, even iwalam (forever).

You, magadal (tower) of the flock, the hill of the bath (daughter) of Tzayawan, to you it will come, yes, the raashawan (former) mamashalah (dominion) will bawaa (come), the mamalakah (kingdom) of the bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam.
Now why do you rawai (cry) out aloud? Is there no malak (king) in you? Has your yaitz (counselor) perished, that pains have taken hold of you as of a yalad (woman) in travail?

Be in chawal (pain), and gayach (labor) to bring forth, bath (daughter) of Tzayawan, like a yalad (woman) in travail; for now you will yatzaa (go) forth out of the city, and will shakan (dwell) in the shadah (field), and will come even to Babal. There you will be rescued. There Yahawah will gaal (redeem) you from the kap (hand) of your ayab (enemies).
Now many gawayam (nations) have assembled amar (against) you, that say, "Let her be defiled, and let our iyan (eye) gloat over Tzayawan.
But they don't yadai (know) the machashabah (thoughts) of Yahawah, neither do they bayan (understand) his itzah (counsel); for he has gathered them like the sheaves to the threshing floor.

qawam (arise) and thresh, bath (daughter) of Tzayawan; for I will shawam (make) your qaran (horn) barazal (iron), and I will shawam (make) your hoofs brass; and you will beat in pieces many im (peoples): and I will charam (devote) their gain to Yahawah, and their chayal (substance) to the Adawan of the whole aratz (earth).

Now you shall gather yourself in gadawad (troops), bath (daughter) of gadawad (troops). He has laid Matzawar against us. They will strike the shapat (judge) of Yasharaal (Israel) with a shabat (rod) on the Lachay.

But you, Bayathalacham Ephrathah, being Tzaiyar among the clans of Yahawadah (Judah), out of you one will yatzaa (come) forth to me that is to be ruler in Yasharaal (Israel); whose mawatzaah (goings) forth are from of qadam (old), from everlasting.

Therefore he will abandon them until the ith (time) that she who is in labor gives yalad (birth). Then the yathar (rest) of his ach (brothers) will shawab (turn back / repent) to the children of Yasharaal (Israel).

He shall imad (stand), and shall raih (shepherd) in the iz (strength) of Yahawah, in the majesty of the sham (name) of Yahawah his Alahayam: and they will live, for then he will be great to the apas (ends) of the aratz (earth).

He will be our shalawam (peace) when Ashawar bawaa (invades) our aratz (land), and when he marches through our fortresses, then we will qawam (raise) against him shabai (seven) raih (shepherds), and shamanah (eight) leaders of men.

They will rule the aratz (land) of Ashawar with the charab (sword), and the aratz (land) of Namarawad in its gates. He will natzal (deliver) us from the Ashawar (Assyrian), when he bawaa (invades) our aratz (land), and when he marches within our border.

The shaarayath (remnant) of Yaiqab will be in the qarab (midst) of many im (peoples), like dew from Yahawah, like showers on the grass, that don't wait for ayash (man), nor wait for the ban (sons) of men.

The shaarayath (remnant) of Yaiqab will be among the gaway (nations), in the qarab (midst) of many im (peoples), like a aray (lion) among the animals of the Yair, like a young kapayar (lion) among the flocks of sheep; who, if he goes ibar (through), treads down and tears in pieces, and there is no one to natzal (deliver).
Let your yad (hand) be lifted up above your tzar (adversaries), and let all of your ayab (enemies) be karath (cut) off.
"It will happen in that yawam (day)," says Yahawah, "That I will karath (cut) off your horses out of the qarab (midst) of you, and will abad (destroy) your chariots.
I will karath (cut) off the cities of your aratz (land), and will tear down all your strongholds.
I will karath (destroy) witchcraft from your yad (hand); and you shall have no soothsayers.
I will karath (cut) off your engraved pasayal (images) and your matzabah (pillars) out of your qarab (midst); and you shall no more shachah (worship) the maishah (work) of your yad (hands).
I will uproot your Asharah out of your qarab (midst); and I will destroy your cities.
I will ishah (execute) vengeance in ap (anger), and chamah (wrath) on the gaway (nations) that didn't listen.
Listen now to what Yahawah amar (says): "qawam (arise), rayab (plead) your case before the har (mountains), and let the Gabaih hear what you have to say.

Hear, you har (mountains), yahawah (yahweh's) rayab (controversy), and you enduring foundations of the aratz (earth); for Yahawah has a rayab (controversy) with his im (people), and he will contend with Yasharaal (Israel).
My im (people), what have I done to you? How have I burdened you? Answer me!
For I brought you up out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and padah (redeemed) you out of the bayath (house) of ibad (bondage). I sent panayam (before) you Mashah, Aharawan, and Marayam.

My im (people), zakar (remember) now what Balaq malak (king) of Mawaab devised, and what Balaim the ban (son) of Baiwar answered him from Shatayam to Galagal, that you may yadai (know) the tzadaqah (righteous) acts of Yahawah.
How shall I qadam (come) before Yahawah, and bow myself before the exalted Alahayam? Shall I qadam (come) before him with burnt ilah (offerings), with calves a Shanah ban (old)?

Will Yahawah be pleased with alap (thousands) of ayal (rams)? With rababah (tens) of thousands of nachal (rivers) of shaman (oil)? Shall I nathan (give) my firstborn for my disobedience? The fruit of my body for the chataah (sin) of my napash (soul)?
He has shown you, O adam (man), what is tawab (good). What does Yahawah require of you, but to act justly, to ahabah (love) chasad (mercy), and to yalak (walk) Tzanai with your Alahayam?
yahawah (yahweh's) qawal (voice) qaraa (calls) to the Iyar, and thawashayah (wisdom) raah (see) your sham (name): "Listen to the matah (rod), and he who appointed it.
Are there yet treasures of rashai (wickedness) in the bayath (house) of the rashai (wicked), and a short ephah that is accursed?
Shall I be zakah (pure) with dishonest scales, and with a bag of deceitful aban (weights)?
Her Ishayar men are malaa (full) of violence, her yashab (inhabitants) dabar (speak) lies, and their lashawan (tongue) is deceitful in their pah (speech).
Therefore I also have struck you with a grievous wound. I have made you shamam (desolate) because of your chataah (sins).

You shall akal (eat), but not be satisfied. Your humiliation will be in your qarab (midst). You will store up, but not palat (save); and that which you palat (save) I will nathan (give) up to the charab (sword).
You will zarai (sow), but won't reap. You will tread the olives, but won't anoint yourself with shaman (oil); and crush grapes, but won't drink the thayarawash (wine).

For the chaqah (statutes) of Imaray are kept, and all the maishah (works) of the bayath (house) of Achaab. You yalak (walk) in their mawaitzah (counsels), that I may nathan (make) you a ruin, and her yashab (inhabitants) a hissing; And you will nashaa (bear) the reproach of my im (people).

Misery is mine! Indeed, I am like asap (one) who gathers the qayatz (summer) fruits, as gleanings of the vineyard: There is no cluster of grapes to akal (eat). My napash (soul) desires to eat the early fig.

The chasayad (godly) man has perished out of the aratz (earth), and there is no one yashar (upright) among men. They all lie in wait for dam (blood); every ayash (man) hunts his ach (brother) with a charam (net).

Their kap (hands) are on that which is rai (evil) to do it yatab (diligently). The shar (ruler) and shapat (judge) shaal (ask) for a bribe; and the powerful man dictates the evil napash (desire) of his ibath (soul). Thus they conspire together.

The tawab (best) of them is like a brier. The most yashar (upright) is worse than a thorn hedge. The yawam (day) of your watchmen, even your visitation, has bawaa (come); now is the time of their mabawakah (confusion).
Don't aman (trust) in a neighbor. Don't batach (put) confidence in a rai (friend). With the woman lying in your embrace, be careful of the pathach (words) of your pah (mouth)!

For the ban (son) dishonors the ab (father), the bath (daughter) qawam (rises) up against her am (mother), the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a ayash (man's) ayab (enemies) are the men of his own bayath (house).
But as for me, I will look to Yahawah. I will wait for the Alahayam of my yashai (salvation). My Alahayam will hear me.
Don't Shamach against me, my ayab (enemy). When I napal (fall), I will qawam (arise). When I yashab (sit) in chashak (darkness), Yahawah will be a awar (light) to me.

I will nashaa (bear) the zaip (indignation) of Yahawah, because I have sinned against him, until he rayab (pleads) my case, and ishah (executes) mashapat (judgment) for me. He will yatzaa (bring) me forth to the awar (light). I will raah (see) his tzadaqah (righteousness).

Then my ayab (enemy) will raah (see) it, and shame will cover her who said to me, where is Yahawah your Alahayam? Then my enemy will raah (see) me and will cover her shame. Now she will be maramas (trodden) down like the mire of the streets.
A yawam (day) to banah (build) your walls— In that yawam (day), he will extend your boundary.

In that yawam (day) they will bawaa (come) to you from Ashawar and the Iyar Matzawar Egypt, and Matzawar Egypt even to the nahar (river), and from yam (sea) to yam (sea), and har (mountain) to har (mountain).
Yet the aratz (land) will be desolate because of those who live in it, for the fruit of their mailal (doings).

raih (shepherd) your im (people) with your shabat (staff), the flock of your nachalah (heritage), who live by themselves in a Yair, in the midst Karamal fertile pasture land, let them raih (feed); in Bashan and Galaid, as in the yawam (days) of old.
"As in the yawam (days) of your coming forth out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, I will show them palaa (marvelous) things.
The gawayam (nations) will raah (see) and be bawash (ashamed) of all their might. They will shawam (lay) their yad (hand) on their pah (mouth). Their ears will be charash (deaf).

They will lick the ipar (dust) like a serpent. Like crawling things of the aratz (earth) they shall come trembling out of their dens. They will come with yaraa (fear) to Yahawah our Alahayam, and will be yaraa (afraid) because of you.

Who is a Al like you, who nashaa (pardons) iwan (iniquity), and passes over the disobedience of the shaarayath (remnant) of his nachalah (heritage)? He doesn't chazaq (retain) his ap (anger) id (forever), because he delights in loving chasad (kindness).
He will again have racham (compassion) on us. He will tread our iwan (iniquities) under shalak (foot); and you will cast all their chataah (sins) into the depths of the yam (sea).
You will nathan (give) truth to Yaiqab, and chasad (mercy) to Abaraham, as you have sworn to our abawath (fathers) from the yawam (days) of qadam (old).
An oracle about Nayanawah. The book of the vision of Nachawam the Alaqashay.
Yahawah is a Qanawaa Al and avenges. Yahawah avenges and is full of wrath. Yahawah takes vengeance on his tzar (adversaries), and he maintains wrath against his ayab (enemies).

Yahawah is Arak to ap (anger), and gadawal (great) in kach (power), and will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. Yahawah has his darak (way) in the sawapah (whirlwind) and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
He rebukes the yam (sea), and charab (makes) it dry, and yabash (dries) up all the nahar (rivers). Bashan languishes, and Karamal; and the flower of Labanawan languishes.
The har (mountains) quake before him, and the Gabaih melt away. The aratz (earth) trembles at his panayam (presence), yes, the world, and all who yashab (dwell) in it.

Who can imad (stand) panayam (before) his indignation? Who can qawam (endure) the charawan (fierceness) of his ap (anger)? His chamah (wrath) is poured out like ash (fire), and the tzawar (rocks) are broken apart by him.
Yahawah is tawab (good), a stronghold in the yawam (day) of tzarah (trouble); and he yadai (knows) those who take refuge in him.
But with an overflowing flood, he will ishah (make) a full end of her place, and will pursue his ayab (enemies) into chashak (darkness).
What do you plot against Yahawah? He will ishah (make) a full end. tzarah (affliction) won't qawam (rise) up the paim (second) time.
For entangled like thorns, and drunken as with their sabaa (drink), they are consumed Malaa like Yabash stubble.
There is one gone yatzaa (forth) out of you, who chashab (devises) rai (evil) against Yahawah, who yaitz (counsels) wickedness.
Thus amar (says) Yahawah: "Though they be in Shalam strength, and likewise many, even so they will be cut down, and he shall ibar (pass) away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.
Now will I shabar (break) his mawat (yoke) from off you, and will burst your bonds apart.

Yahawah has tzawah (commanded) concerning you: "No more descendants will bear your sham (name). Out of the bayath (house) of your Alahayam, will I karath (cut) off the engraved pasal (image) and the molten masakah (image). I will shawam (make) your qabar (grave), for you are qalal (vile).

Behold, on the har (mountains) the feet of him who brings bashar (good) news, who publishes shalawam (peace)! Keep your chag (feasts), Yahawadah (Judah)! shalam (perform) your nadar (vows), for the balayail (wicked) yasap (one) will no more ibar (pass) through you. He is karath (utterly) cut off.
He who dashes in pieces has ilah (come) up panayam (against) you. Keep the fortress! Watch the darak (way)! chazaq (strengthen) your waist! amatz (fortify) your kach (power) mightily!
For Yahawah shawab (turn back / repent) the excellency of Yaiqab, as the excellency of Yasharaal (Israel); for the destroyers have destroyed them, and ruined their vine branches.

The magan (shield) of his gabawar (mighty) men is made red. The chayal (valiant) men are in scarlet. The chariots flash with steel in the yawam (day) of his kawan (preparation), and the pine spears are brandished.
The chariots halal (rage) in the streets. They rush back and forth in the broad rachab (ways). Their appearance is like torches. They run like the lightnings.
He summons his picked troops. They stumble on their halayakah (way). They dash to its wall, and the protective sakak (shield) is put in place.
The gates of the nahar (rivers) are opened, and the hayakal (palace) is dissolved.
It is decreed: she is uncovered, she is carried ilah (away); and her handmaids moan as with the qawal (voice) of doves, beating on their labab (breasts).
But Nayanawah has been from of yawam (old) like a pool of mayam (water), yet they flee away. "Stop! Stop!" they cry, but no one panah (looks) back.
Take the spoil of kasap (silver). Take the spoil of gold, for there is no end of the store, the kabawad (glory) of all goodly furniture.
She is empty, void, and waste. The lab (heart) melts, the knees knock together, their bodies and panayam (faces) have grown pale.

Where is the den of the aray (lions), and the feeding place of the young kapayar (lions), where the aray (lion) and the lioness walked, the labayaa (lion's) cubs, and no charad (one) made them afraid?
The aray (lion) tore in pieces enough for his cubs, and strangled for his lionesses, and filled his caves Tarap the kill, and his dens with Tarap.

"Behold, I am against you," says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "and I will bair (burn) her chariots in the ishan (smoke), and the charab (sword) will akal (devour) your young kapayar (lions); and I will karath (cut) off your Tarap from the aratz (earth), and the qawal (voice) of your malaak (messengers) will no longer be heard.
Woe to the bloody Iyar! It is all Malaa of lies and robbery. The Tarap doesn't depart.
The qawal (noise) of the whip, the qawal (noise) of the rattling of wheels, prancing horses, and bounding chariots,

the horseman mounting, and the flashing charab (sword), the glittering spear, and a multitude of Chalal, and a great heap of pagar (corpses), and there is no end of the pagar (bodies). They stumble on their bodies,

because of the multitude of the prostitution of the alluring prostitute, the mistress of witchcraft, who sells gawayam (nations) through her prostitution, and mashapachah (families) through her witchcraft.

"Behold, I am against you," says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "and I will lift your skirts over your panayam (face). I will show the gawayam (nations) your nakedness, and the mamalakah (kingdoms) your qalawan (shame).
I will throw shaqawatz (abominable) filth on you, and make you vile, and will shawam (set) you a spectacle.

It will happen that all those who raah (see) at you will nadad (flee) from you, and amar (say), ‘Nayanawah is laid shadad (waste)! Who will nawad (mourn) for her?' Where will I seek comforters for you?
Are you yatab (better) Naa No - Amon, who was situated among the yaar (rivers), who had the mayam (waters) around her; whose chayal (rampart) was the yam (sea), and her wall was of the yam (sea)?
Kawash and Matzarayam were her boundless itzamah (strength). Pawat and Lawabay were her helpers.

Yet was she carried away. She went into Shabay. Her young children also were dashed in pieces at the raash (head) of all the streets, and they cast lots for her honorable men, and all her gadawal (great) men were bound in chains.
You also will be Shakar. You will be hidden. You also will seek a stronghold because of the ayab (enemy).
All your fortresses will be like fig trees with the first-ripe figs: if they are shaken, they napal (fall) into the pah (mouth) of the eater.
Behold, your troops in your qarab (midst) are women. The gates of your aratz (land) are pathach (set) wide pathach (open) to your ayab (enemies). The ash (fire) has devoured your bars.
shaab (draw) mayam (water) for the Matzawar. chazaq (strengthen) your fortresses. bawaa (go) into the clay, and tread the mortar. Make the brick kiln chazaq (strong).
There the ash (fire) will akal (devour) you. The charab (sword) will karath (cut) you off. It will akal (devour) you like the grasshopper. Multiply like grasshoppers. Multiply like the locust.
You have increased your merchants more than the kawakab (stars) of the skies. The grasshopper strips, and flees away.

Your guards are like the locusts, and your officials like the swarms of locusts, which settle on the Gadarah on a cold yawam (day), but when the shamash (sun) appears, they nadad (flee) away, and their place is not yadai (known) where they are.
Your raih (shepherds) nawam (slumber), malak (king) of Ashawar. Your adayar (nobles) lie down. Your im (people) are scattered on the har (mountains), and there is no qabatz (one) to gather them.
There is no healing your wound, for your injury is fatal. All who hear the report of you clap their kap (hands) over you; for who hasn't felt your endless cruelty?
The oracle which Chabaqawaq the nabayaa (prophet) saw.
Yahawah, how long will I cry, and you will not hear? I cry out to you "Violence!" and will you not yashai (save)?
Why do you show me awan (iniquity), and look at perversity? For destruction and violence are before me. There is rayab (strife), and contention rises up.
Therefore the thawarah (law) is paralyzed, and justice never goes yatzaa (forth); for the rashai (wicked) surround the tzadayaq (righteous); therefore justice goes yatzaa (forth) perverted.
"raah (see) among the gawayam (nations), watch, and thamah (wonder) thamah (marvelously); for I am working a pail (work) in your yawam (days), which you will not aman (believe) though it is told you.

For, behold, I qawam (raise) up the Kashaday (Chaldeans), that Mar and hasty gaway (nation), that halak (march) through the breadth of the aratz (earth), to yarash (possess) mashakan (dwelling) places that are not theirs.
They are feared and dreaded. Their mashapat (judgment) and their dignity yatzaa (proceed) from themselves.

Their horses also are qalal (swifter) than leopards, and are more fierce than the evening wolves. Their horsemen press proudly on. Yes, their horsemen bawaa (come) from Rachawaq. They fly as an eagle that hurries to akal (devour).
All of them bawaa (come) for violence. Their hordes panayam (face) the desert. He asap (gathers) Shabay like sand.
Yes, he scoffs at malak (kings), and razan (princes) are a derision to him. He laughs at every stronghold, for he builds up an earthen ramp, and takes it.
Then he sweeps by like the rawach (wind), and goes on. He is indeed asham (guilty), whose kach (strength) is his Alawah.

Aren't you from qadam (everlasting), Yahawah my Alahayam, my qadawash (holy) One? We will not mawath (die). Yahawah, you have appointed him for mashapat (judgment). You, tzawar (rock), have established him to punish.

You who have purer iyan (eyes) than to raah (see) rai (evil), and who cannot look on perversity, why do you tolerate those who bagad (deal) treacherously, and charash (keep) silent when the rashai (wicked) balai (swallows) up the man who is more tzadayaq (righteous) than he,
and ishah (make) men like the fish of the yam (sea), like the creeping things, that have no ruler over them?
He ilah (takes) up all of them with the hook. He catches them in his charam (net), and asap (gathers) them in his dragnet. Therefore he Shamach and is glad.
Therefore he zabach (sacrifices) to his charam (net), and qatar (burns) incense to his dragnet, because by them his life is Shaman, and his food is Barayaa.
Will he therefore continually empty his charam (net), and harag (kill) the gawayam (nations) without chamal (mercy)?

I will imad (stand) at my watch, and set Matzawar on the ramparts, and will raah (see) out to raah (see) what he will dabar (say) to me, and what I will shawab (turn back / repent) concerning my complaint.
Yahawah answered me, "kathab (write) the vision, and make it plain on tablets, that he who runs may qaraa (read) it.

For the vision is yet for the mawaid (appointed) time, and it hurries toward the end, and won't prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it; because it will bawaa (surely) bawaa (come). It won't delay.
Behold, his napash (soul) is puffed up. It is not yashar (upright) in him, but the tzadayaq (righteous) will chayah (live) by his amawanah (faith).

Yes, moreover, yayan (wine) is bagad (treacherous). A Yahayar gabar (man) who doesn't stay at home, who enlarges his napash (desire) as shaawal (sheol), and he is like mawath (death), and can't be satisfied, but asap (gathers) to himself all gawayam (nations), and heaps to himself all im (peoples).

Won't all these nashaa (take) up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb amar (against) him, and say, ‘Woe to him who increases that which is not his, and who enriches himself by extortion! How long?'
Won't your debtors qawam (rise) up suddenly, and wake up those who make you tremble, and you will be their victim?

Because you have plundered many gawayam (nations), all the yathar (remnant) of the im (peoples) will plunder you, because of men's dam (blood), and for the violence done to the aratz (land), to the city and to all who yashab (dwell) in it.
Woe to him who gets an rai (evil) gain for his bayath (house), that he may shawam (set) his nest on high, that he may be delivered from the kap (hand) of rai (evil)!
You have devised bashath (shame) to your bayath (house), by cutting off many im (peoples), and have sinned against your napash (soul).
For the aban (stone) will cry out of the wall, and the beam out of the woodwork will answer it.
Woe to him who banah (builds) a Iyar with dam (blood), and establishes a city by iwal (iniquity)!
Behold, isn't it of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) that the im (peoples) yagai (labor) for the ash (fire), and the laam (nations) Yaip themselves for vanity?
For the aratz (earth) will be filled with the yadai (knowledge) of the kabawad (glory) of Yahawah, as the mayam (waters) cover the yam (sea).
"Woe to him who gives his neighbor shaqah (drink), pouring your inflaming chamath (wine) until they are Shakar, so that you may gaze at their naked bodies!

You are filled with qalawan (shame), and not kabawad (glory). You will also drink, and be exposed! The cup of yahawah (yahweh's) right yamayan (hand) will sabab (come) around to you, and disgrace will cover your kabawad (glory).

For the violence done to Labanawan will overwhelm you, and the destruction of the animals, which made them chathath (afraid); because of men's dam (blood), and for the violence done to the aratz (land), to every city and to those who yashab (dwell) in them.

"What value does the engraved pasal (image) have, that its maker has engraved it; the molten masakah (image), even the teacher of lies, that he who fashions its form batach (trusts) in it, to ishah (make) mute idols?

Woe to him who amar (says) to the itz (wood), ‘qawatz (awake)!' or to the mute aban (stone), ‘Arise!' Shall this teach? Behold, it is overlaid with gold and kasap (silver), and there is no rawach (breath) at all in its qarab (midst).
But Yahawah is in his qadash (holy) hayakal (temple). Let all the aratz (earth) be hasah (silent) panayam (before) him!
A prayer of Chabaqawaq, the nabayaa (prophet), Shagayawan to victorious music.

Yahawah, I have heard of your fame. I stand in awe of your pail (deeds), Yahawah. Renew your pail (work) in the qarab (midst) of the Shanah. In the qarab (midst) of the Shanah yadai (make) it known. In ragaz (wrath), you zakar (remember) racham (mercy).
Alawah came from Thayaman, the qadawash (holy) One from har (mount) Paaran. salah (selah). His glory covered the shamayam (heavens), and his thahalah (praise) filled the aratz (earth).
His splendor is like the sunrise. Rays shine from his yad (hand), where his iz (power) is hidden.
dabar (plague) went panayam (before) him, and pestilence followed his feet.
He stood, and shook the aratz (earth). He looked, and made the gawayam (nations) tremble. The ancient harar (mountains) were crumbled. The age-old Gabaih collapsed. His halayakah (ways) are eternal.
I saw the ahal (tents) of Kawashan in awan (affliction). The dwellings of the aratz (land) of Madayan trembled.

Was Yahawah charah (displeased) with the nahar (rivers)? Was your ap (anger) against the nahar (rivers), or your ibarah (wrath) against the yam (sea), that you rode on your horses, on your chariots of yashawaih (salvation)?
You uncovered your qashath (bow). You called for your shabawaih (sworn) arrows. salah (selah). You split the aratz (earth) with nahar (rivers).
The har (mountains) saw you, and were afraid. The storm of mayam (waters) passed by. The deep roared and lifted up its yad (hands) on high.
The shamash (sun) and yarach (moon) stood still in the sky, at the awar (light) of your chatz (arrows) as they went, at the nagah (shining) of your glittering spear.
You marched through the aratz (land) in zaim (wrath). You threshed the gawayam (nations) in ap (anger).

You went yatzaa (forth) for the yashai (salvation) of your im (people), for the yashai (salvation) of your mashayach (anointed). You crushed the raash (head) of the land of wickedness. You stripped them tzawaar (head) to foot. salah (selah).
You pierced the raash (heads) of his warriors with their own spears. They came as a whirlwind to scatter me, gloating as if to akal (devour) the Inay in secret.
You trampled the yam (sea) with your horses, churning rab (mighty) mayam (waters).

I heard, and my body trembled. My shapah (lips) quivered at the qawal (voice). Rottenness bawaa (enters) into my itzam (bones), and I tremble in my place, because I must wait quietly for the yawam (day) of tzarah (trouble), for the coming up of the im (people) who invade us.

For though the fig tree doesn't flourish, nor fruit be in the vines; the maishah (labor) of the olive fails, the fields ishah (yield) no food; the flocks are cut off from the fold, and there is no herd in the stalls:
yet I will rejoice in Yahawah. I will be joyful in the Alahayam of my yashai (salvation)!
Yahawah, the Adanay, is my chayal (strength). He shawam (makes) my feet like deer's feet, and enables me to go in bamah (high) places. For the music director, on my stringed instruments.

The dabar (word) of Yahawah which came to Tzapanayah, the ban (son) of Kawashay, the ban (son) of Gadalayah, the ban (son) of Amarayah, the ban (son) of Chazaqayah, in the yawam (days) of Yaashayah, the ban (son) of Amawan, malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah).
I will asap (utterly) sweep away everything off of the surface of the earth, says Yahawah.

I will sweep away adam (man) and animal. I will sweep away the birds of the sky, the fish of the yam (sea), and the heaps of rubble with the rashai (wicked). I will karath (cut) off adam (man) from the surface of the adamah (earth), says Yahawah.

I will natah (stretch) out my yad (hand) against Yahawadah (Judah), and against all the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam. I will karath (cut) off the shaar (remnant) of Bail from this place: the sham (name) of the idolatrous and pagan kahan (priests),
those who shachah (worship) the tzabaa (army) of the sky on the housetops, those who shachah (worship) and shabai (swear) by Yahawah and also shabai (swear) by Malcam,
those who have turned sawag (back) from following Yahawah, and those who haven't sought Yahawah nor inquired after him.

Be hasah (silent) at the panayam (presence) of the Adanay Yahawah, for the yawam (day) of Yahawah is at qarawab (hand). For Yahawah has prepared a zabach (sacrifice). He has consecrated his qaraa (guests).

It will happen in the yawam (day) of yahawah (yahweh's) zabach (sacrifice), that I will paqad (punish) the shar (princes), the malak (king's) ban (sons), and all those who are Labash with foreign clothing.
In that yawam (day), I will paqad (punish) all those who leap over the threshold, who malaa (fill) their adawan (master's) bayath (house) with violence and deceit.
In that yawam (day), says Yahawah, there will be the qawal (noise) of a cry from the fish gate, a wailing from the mashanah (second) quarter, and a gadawal (great) crashing from the Gabaih.
Wail, you yashab (inhabitants) of Maktesh, for all the im (people) of Kanain are damah (undone)! All those who were loaded with kasap (silver) are karath (cut) off.

It will happen at that ith (time), that I will search Yarawashalam with nayar (lamps), and I will paqad (punish) the men who are settled on their dregs, who amar (say) in their labab (heart), "Yahawah will not do yatab (good), neither will he do raii (evil).

Their wealth will become a spoil, and their bayath (houses) a desolation. Yes, they will banah (build) bayath (houses), but won't yashab (inhabit) them. They will plant vineyards, but won't drink their yayan (wine).

The gadawal (great) yawam (day) of Yahawah is qarawab (near). It is qarawab (near), and Mahar maad (greatly), the qawal (voice) of the yawam (day) of Yahawah. The gabawar (mighty) man cries Mar bitterly.

That yawam (day) is a yawam (day) of ibarah (wrath), a yawam (day) of distress and tzarah (anguish), a yawam (day) of tzarah (trouble) and ruin, a yawam (day) of chashak (darkness) and gloom, a yawam (day) of clouds and blackness,
a yawam (day) of the trumpet and alarm, against the fortified Iyar, and against the Gabah battlements.

I will tzarar (bring) distress on men, that they will halak (walk) like iwar (blind) men, because they have sinned against Yahawah, and their dam (blood) will be poured out like ipar (dust), and their flesh like dung.

Neither their kasap (silver) nor their gold will be yakal (able) to natzal (deliver) them in the yawam (day) of yahawah (yahweh's) ibarah (wrath), but the whole aratz (land) will be devoured by the ash (fire) of his jealousy; for he will ishah (make) an end, yes, a terrible end, of all those who yashab (dwell) in the aratz (land).
Gather yourselves together, yes, gather together, you gaway (nation) that has no shame,

before the chaq (appointed) yalad (time) when the yawam (day) passes as the chaff, laa (before) the charawan (fierce) ap (anger) of Yahawah bawaa (comes) on you, before the yawam (day) of yahawah (yahweh's) ap (anger) bawaa (comes) on you.

Seek Yahawah, all you Inaw of the aratz (land), who have kept his mashapat (ordinances). Seek tzadaq (righteousness). Seek humility. It may be that you will be hidden in the yawam (day) of yahawah (yahweh's) ap (anger).
For Izah will be forsaken, and Ashaqalawan a desolation. They will drive out Ashadawad at noonday, and Iqarawan will be rooted up.

Woe to the yashab (inhabitants) of the yam (sea) coast, the gaway (nation) of the Karathay (Cherethites)! The dabar (word) of Yahawah is against you, Kanain, the aratz (land) of the Palashathay (Philistines). I will abad (destroy) you, that there will be no yashab (inhabitant).
The yam (sea) coast will be Nawah, with cottages for raih (shepherds) and Gadarah for flocks.

The coast will be for the shaarayath (remnant) of the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah). They will find pasture. In the bayath (houses) of Ashaqalawan, they will rabatz (lie) down in the evening, for Yahawah, their Alahayam, will paqad (visit) them, and shawab (turn back / repent) them.
I have heard the reproach of Mawaab, and the insults of the children of Imawan, with which they have reproached my im (people), and magnified themselves against their border.

Therefore as I chay (live), says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), surely Mawaab will be as Sadam, and the children of Imawan as Imarah, a mamashaq (possession) of nettles, and salt makarah (pits), and a perpetual desolation. The shaarayath (remnant) of my im (people) will plunder them, and the survivors of my gaway (nation) will nachal (inherit) them.
This they will have for their pride, because they have reproached and magnified themselves against the im (people) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
Yahawah will be awesome to them, for he will famish all the Alahayam of the aratz (land). Men will shachah (worship) him, everyone from his place, even all the shores of the gawayam (nations).
You Cushites also, you will be Chalal by my charab (sword).
He will natah (stretch) out his yad (hand) against the tzapawan (north), abad (destroy) Ashawar, and will shawam (make) Nayanawah a desolation, as tzayah (dry) as the madabar (wilderness).

Herds will rabatz (lie) down in the midst of her, all the animals of the gaway (nations). Both the pelican and the porcupine will lawan (lodge) in its capitals. Their calls will echo through the windows. Desolation will be in the thresholds, for he has laid bare the arazah (cedar) beams.

This is the Ilayaz Iyar that lived carelessly, that said in her labab (heart), "I am, and there is apas (none) besides me." How she has become a desolation, a place for animals to lie down in! Everyone who passes by her will hiss, and shake their fists.
Woe to her who is rebellious and polluted, the oppressing Iyar!
She didn't obey the qawal (voice). She didn't receive correction. She didn't batach (trust) in Yahawah. She didn't qarab (draw) near to her Alahayam.
Her shar (princes) in the qarab (midst) of her are roaring aray (lions). Her shapat (judges) are evening wolves. They leave nothing until the next baqar (day).
Her nabayaa (prophets) are arrogant and treacherous anawash (people). Her kahan (priests) have profaned the qadash (sanctuary). They have done violence to the thawarah (law).

Yahawah, in the qarab (midst) of her, is tzadayaq (righteous). He will do no wrong. Every baqar (morning) he nathan (brings) his justice to awar (light). He doesn't fail, but the iwal (unjust) yadai (know) no bashath (shame).

I have karath (cut) off gawayam (nations). Their battlements are shamam (desolate). I have made their streets charab (waste), so that no one passes by. Their Iyar are destroyed, so that there is no ayash (man), so that there is no yashab (inhabitant).

I said, "Just yaraa (fear) me. Receive correction, so that her dwelling won't be karath (cut) off, according to all that I have appointed concerning her." But they rose shakam (early) and corrupted all their ilayalah (doings).

"Therefore wait for me," says Yahawah, "until the yawam (day) that I qawam (rise) up to the prey, for my mashapat (determination) is to asap (gather) the gawayam (nations), that I may assemble the mamalakah (kingdoms), to pour on them my indignation, even all my charawan (fierce) ap (anger), for all the aratz (earth) will be devoured with the ash (fire) of my jealousy.
For then I will Barar the shapah (lips) of the im (peoples), that they may all qaraa (call) on the sham (name) of Yahawah, to ibad (serve) him shoulder to shoulder.
From ibar (beyond) the nahar (rivers) of Kawash, my worshipers, even the bath (daughter) of my dispersed yabal (people), will bring my manachah (offering).

In that yawam (day) you will not be disappointed for all your ilayalah (doings), in which you have transgressed against me; for then I will sawar (take) away out of the qarab (midst) of you your proudly Ilayaz yasap (ones), and you will no more be haughty in my qadash (holy) har (mountain).
But I will shaar (leave) in the qarab (midst) of you an Inay and Dal im (people), and they will take refuge in the sham (name) of Yahawah.

The shaarayath (remnant) of Yasharaal (Israel) will not do iwal (iniquity), nor dabar (speak) lies, neither will a Tharamah lashawan (tongue) be found in their pah (mouth), for they will raih (feed) and rabatz (lie) down, and no charad (one) will make them afraid.
Sing, bath (daughter) of Tzayawan! rawai (shout), Yasharaal (Israel)! Be Shamach and rejoice with all your lab (heart), bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam.

Yahawah has taken sawar (away) your mashapat (judgments). He has thrown out your ayab (enemy). The malak (king) of Yasharaal (Israel), Yahawah, is in the qarab (midst) of you. You will not be afraid of rai (evil) any more.
In that yawam (day), it will be said to Yarawashalam, "Don't be yaraa (afraid), Tzayawan. Don't let your yad (hands) be rapah (weak).

Yahawah, your Alahayam, is in the qarab (midst) of you, a gabawar (mighty) one who will yashai (save). He will rejoice over you with joy. He will calm you in his ahabah (love). He will rejoice over you with singing.
I will remove those who grieve about the mawaid (appointed) feasts from you. They are a mashaath (burden) and a reproach to you.

Behold, at that ith (time) I will ishah (deal) with all those who afflict you, and I will yashai (save) those who are lame, and gather those who were driven away. I will shawam (give) them thahalah (praise) and honor, whose bashath (shame) has been in all the aratz (earth).

At that ith (time) will I bawaa (bring) you in, and at that ith (time) will I gather you; for I will nathan (give) you honor and thahalah (praise) among all the im (peoples) of the aratz (earth), when I shawab (turn back / repent) your fortunes before your iyan (eyes), amar (says) Yahawah.

In the shanayam (second) Shanah of Darayawash the malak (king), in the shashay (sixth) chadash (month), in the achad (first) yawam (day) of the chadash (month), the dabar (word) of Yahawah came by Chagay, the nabayaa (prophet), to Zarababal, the ban (son) of Shaalathayaal, governor of Yahawadah (Judah), and to Yahawashawai, the ban (son) of Yahawatzadaq, the gadawal (high) kahan (priest), saying,
"This is what Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) amar (says): These im (people) amar (say), ‘The ith (time) hasn't yet bawaa (come), the ith (time) for yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house) to be built.'
Then the dabar (word) of Yahawah came by Chagay, the nabayaa (prophet), saying,
"Is it a ith (time) for you yourselves to yashab (dwell) in your paneled bayath (houses), while this bayath (house) lies Charab?
Now therefore this is what Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) amar (says): shawam (consider) your darak (ways).

You have sown much, and bawaa (bring) in Mait. You akal (eat), but you don't have enough. You drink, but you aren't filled with Shakar. You Labash yourselves, but no cham (one) is warm, and he who earns wages earns wages to put them into a tzarawar (bag) with naqab (holes) in it.
This is what Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) amar (says): "shawam (consider) your darak (ways).
ilah (go) up to the har (mountain), bawaa (bring) itz (wood), and banah (build) the bayath (house). I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified," amar (says) Yahawah.

"You looked for much, and, behold, it came to Mait; and when you brought it bayath (home), I blew it away. Why?" says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "Because of my bayath (house) that lies Charab, while each of you is busy with his own bayath (house).
Therefore for your sake the shamayam (heavens) withhold the dew, and the aratz (earth) withholds its fruit.

I called for a drought on the aratz (land), on the har (mountains), on the grain, on the new thayarawash (wine), on the yatzahar (oil), on that which the adamah (ground) yatzaa (brings) forth, on men, on livestock, and on all the yagayai (labor) of the kap (hands).

Then Zarababal, the ban (son) of Shaalathayaal, and Yahawashawai, the ban (son) of Yahawatzadaq, the gadawal (high) kahan (priest), with all the shaarayath (remnant) of the im (people), obeyed the qawal (voice) of Yahawah, their Alahayam, and the dabar (words) of Chagay, the nabayaa (prophet), as Yahawah, their Alahayam, had sent him; and the im (people) feared Yahawah.
Then Chagay, yahawah (yahweh's) malaak (messenger), spoke yahawah (yahweh's) message to the im (people), saying, "I am with you," says Yahawah.

Yahawah stirred up the rawach (spirit) of Zarababal, the ban (son) of Shaalathayaal, governor of Yahawadah (Judah), and the rawach (spirit) of Yahawashawai, the ban (son) of Yahawatzadaq, the gadawal (high) kahan (priest), and the rawach (spirit) of all the shaarayath (remnant) of the im (people); and they came and worked on the bayath (house) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), their Alahayam,
in the isharayam (twenty) - fourth yawam (day) of the month, in the shashay (sixth) chadash (month), in the shanayam (second) Shanah of Darayawash the malak (king).
In the shabayaiy (seventh) month, in the isharayam (twenty) - achad (first) day of the chadash (month), the dabar (word) of Yahawah came by Chagay the nabayaa (prophet), saying,

"amar (speak) now to Zarababal, the ban (son) of Shaalathayaal, governor of Yahawadah (Judah), and to Yahawashawai, the ban (son) of Yahawatzadaq, the gadawal (high) kahan (priest), and to the shaarayath (remnant) of the im (people), saying,
‘Who is shaar (left) among you who saw this bayath (house) in its raashawan (former) kabawad (glory)? How do you raah (see) it now? Isn't it in your iyan (eyes) as nothing?

Yet now be chazaq (strong), Zarababal,' says Yahawah. ‘Be chazaq (strong), Yahawashawai, ban (son) of Yahawatzadaq, the gadawal (high) kahan (priest). Be chazaq (strong), all you im (people) of the aratz (land),' says Yahawah, ‘and ishah (work), for I am with you,' says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
This is the dabar (word) that I covenanted with you when you came out of Matzarayam, and my rawach (spirit) lived among you. ‘Don't be yaraa (afraid).'
For this is what Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) amar (says): ‘Yet achad (once), it is a Mait while, and I will shake the shamayam (heavens), the aratz (earth), the yam (sea), and the dry charabah (land);

and I will shake all gawayam (nations). The precious things of all gawayam (nations) will bawaa (come), and I will malaa (fill) this bayath (house) with kabawad (glory), amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
The kasap (silver) is mine, and the gold is mine,' says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).

‘The Acharawan kabawad (glory) of this bayath (house) will be greater than the raashawan (former),' says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies); ‘and in this place will I nathan (give) shalawam (peace),' amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
In the isharayam (twenty) - fourth day of the thashayaiy (ninth) month, in the shanayam (second) Shanah of Darayawash, the dabar (word) of Yahawah came by Chagay the nabayaa (prophet), saying,
"Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): shaal (ask) now the kahan (priests) concerning the thawarah (law), saying,

‘If someone nashaa (carries) qadash (holy) meat in the fold of his bagad (garment), and with his fold touches lacham (bread), stew, yayan (wine), shaman (oil), or any food, will it become qadash (holy)?'" The kahan (priests) answered, "No.
Then Chagay said, "If one who is tamaa (unclean) by reason of a napash (dead) body nagai (touch) any of these, will it be tamaa (unclean)?" The kahan (priests) answered, "It will be tamaa (unclean).

Then Chagay answered, "‘So is this im (people), and so is this gaway (nation) panayam (before) me,' says Yahawah; ‘and so is every maishah (work) of their yad (hands). That which they qarab (offer) there is tamaa (unclean).
Now, please shawam (consider) from this yawam (day) and backward, before a aban (stone) was laid on a aban (stone) in the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah.

Through all that time, when one came to a heap of isharayam (twenty) measures, there were only ishar (ten). When one came to the yaqab (wine) vat to chashap (draw) out chamashayam (fifty), there were only isharayam (twenty).
