I struck you with blight, mildew, and hail in all the maishah (work) of your yad (hands); yet you didn't turn to me,' says Yahawah.

‘shawam (consider), please, from this yawam (day) and backward, from the isharayam (twenty) - fourth yawam (day) of the thashayaiy (ninth) month, since the yawam (day) that the yasad (foundation) of yahawah (yahweh's) hayakal (temple) was laid, shawam (consider) it.
Is the zarai (seed) yet in the magawarah (barn)? Yes, the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive itz (tree) haven't brought forth. From this yawam (day) will I barak (bless) you.'
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came the shanay (second) time to Chagay in the isharayam (twenty) - fourth day of the chadash (month), saying,
"amar (speak) to Zarababal, governor of Yahawadah (Judah), saying, ‘I will shake the shamayam (heavens) and the aratz (earth).

I will hapak (overthrow) the kasaa (throne) of mamalakah (kingdoms). I will destroy the chazaq (strength) of the mamalakah (kingdoms) of the gawayam (nations). I will hapak (overthrow) the chariots, and those who ride in them. The horses and their riders will yarad (come) down, everyone by the charab (sword) of his ach (brother).

In that yawam (day), says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), will I take you, Zarababal, my ibad (servant), the ban (son) of Shaalathayaal,' says Yahawah, ‘and will shawam (make) you as a signet, for I have chosen you,' says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).

In the eighth chadash (month), in the shanayam (second) Shanah of Darayawash, the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Zakarayah the ban (son) of Barakayah, the ban (son) of Idaw, the nabayaa (prophet), saying,
"Yahawah was very displeased with your abawath (fathers).

Therefore amar (tell) them: Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): ‘shawab (turn back / repent) to me,' amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), ‘and I will shawab (turn back / repent) to you,' says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).

Don't you be like your abawath (fathers), to whom the raashawan (former) nabayaa (prophets) proclaimed, saying: Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), ‘shawab (turn back / repent) now from your rai (evil) darak (ways), and from your rai (evil) mailal (doings);' but they did not hear, nor listen to me, says Yahawah.
Your abawath (fathers), where are they? And the nabayaa (prophets), do they chayah (live) iwalam (forever)?

But my dabar (words) and my chaq (decrees), which I tzawah (commanded) my ibad (servants) the nabayaa (prophets), didn't they overtake your abawath (fathers)? "Then they repented and said, ‘Just as Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) determined to do to us, according to our darak (ways), and according to our practices, so he has dealt with us.'

On the isharayam (twenty) - fourth yawam (day) of the ishathay (eleventh) chadash (month), which is the chadash (month) Shabat, in the shanayam (second) Shanah of Darayawash, the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Zakarayah the ban (son) of Barakayah, the ban (son) of Idaw, the nabayaa (prophet), saying,

"I had a raah (see) in the layal (night), and behold, a ayash (man) riding on a Adam horse, and he stood among the myrtle trees that were in a ravine; and achar (behind) him there were Adam, Sharaq, and Laban horses.
Then I asked, ‘My Adawan, what are these?'" The malaak (angel) who talked with me said to me, "I will show you what these are.
The ayash (man) who stood among the myrtle trees answered, "They are the ones Yahawah has sent to halak (go) back and forth through the aratz (earth).

They reported to the malaak (angel) of Yahawah who stood among the myrtle trees, and said, "We have walked back and halak (forth) through the aratz (earth), and behold, all the aratz (earth) is at rest and in peace.

Then the malaak (angel) of Yahawah replied, "O Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), how long will you not have racham (mercy) on Yarawashalam and on the Iyar of Yahawadah (Judah), against which you have had indignation these shabaiyam (seventy) Shanah?
Yahawah answered the malaak (angel) who talked with me with kind and comforting dabar (words).

So the malaak (angel) who talked with me said to me, "qaraa (proclaim), saying, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): "I am jealous for Yarawashalam and for Tzayawan with a gadawal (great) jealousy.
I am very qatzap (angry) with the gawayam (nations) that are at Shaanan; for I was but a Mait displeased, but they added to the rai (calamity).

Therefore thus amar (says) Yahawah: "I have returned to Yarawashalam with racham (mercy). My bayath (house) shall be built in it," says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "and a line shall be stretched natah (forth) over Yarawashalam."'

"qaraa (proclaim) further, saying, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): "My Iyar will again overflow with tawab (prosperity), and Yahawah will again nacham (comfort) Tzayawan, and will again choose Yarawashalam."'
I lifted up my iyan (eyes), and saw, and behold, arabai (four) qaran (horns).
I asked the malaak (angel) who talked with me, "What are these?" He answered me, "These are the qaran (horns) which have scattered Yahawadah (Judah), Yasharaal (Israel), and Yarawashalam.
Yahawah showed me arabai (four) craftsmen.

Then I asked, "What are these coming to do?" He said, "These are the qaran (horns) which scattered Yahawadah (Judah), so that no ayash (man) lifted up his raash (head); but these have bawaa (come) to terrify them, to yadah (cast) down the qaran (horns) of the gaway (nations), which lifted up their qaran (horn) against the aratz (land) of Yahawadah (Judah) to scatter it.
I lifted up my iyan (eyes), and saw, and behold, a ayash (man) with a measuring line in his yad (hand).
Then I asked, "Where are you going?" He said to me, "To measure Yarawashalam, to raah (see) mah (what) is its breadth and what is its arak (length).
Behold, the malaak (angel) who talked with me went yatzaa (forth), and achar (another) malaak (angel) went out to qaraah (meet) him,
and said to him, "Run, dabar (speak) to this nair (young) man, saying, ‘Yarawashalam will be inhabited as villages without walls, because of the multitude of men and livestock in it.
For I,' says Yahawah, ‘will be to her a wall of ash (fire) around it, and I will be the kabawad (glory) in the midst of her.
Come! Come! Flee from the aratz (land) of the tzapawan (north),' says Yahawah; ‘for I have spread you abroad as the arabai (four) rawach (winds) of the sky,' says Yahawah.
‘Come, Tzayawan! malat (escape), you who yashab (dwell) with the bath (daughter) of Babal.'
For thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): ‘For honor he has sent me to the gaway (nations) which plundered you; for he who touches you touches the apple of his iyan (eye).
For, behold, I will shake my yad (hand) over them, and they will be a spoil to those who served them; and you will yadai (know) that Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) has sent me.
Sing and Shamach, bath (daughter) of Tzayawan; for, behold, I bawaa (come), and I will shakan (dwell) in the midst of you,' says Yahawah.

Many gaway (nations) shall join themselves to Yahawah in that yawam (day), and shall be my im (people); and I will shakan (dwell) in the midst of you, and you shall yadai (know) that Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) has sent me to you.
Yahawah will nachal (inherit) Yahawadah (Judah) as his chalaq (portion) in the qadash (holy) adamah (land), and will again choose Yarawashalam.
Be hasah (silent), all flesh, panayam (before) Yahawah; for he has roused himself from his qadash (holy) habitation!

He showed me Yahawashawai the gadawal (high) kahan (priest) standing panayam (before) the malaak (angel) of Yahawah, and shatan (satan) standing at his right yamayan (hand) to be his shatan (adversary).
Yahawah said to shatan (satan), "Yahawah rebuke you, shatan (satan)! Yes, Yahawah who has chosen Yarawashalam rebuke you! Isn't this a burning stick plucked out of the ash (fire)?
Now Yahawashawai was Labash with Tzawaa bagad (garments), and was standing panayam (before) the malaak (angel).

He answered and spoke to those who stood panayam (before) him, saying, "Take the Tzawaa bagad (garments) off of him." To him he said, "raah (see), I have caused your iwan (iniquity) to ibar (pass) from you, and I will Labash you with rich clothing.

I said, "Let them shawam (set) a tahawar (clean) turban on his raash (head)." So they shawam (set) a tahawar (clean) turban on his raash (head), and Labash him; and the malaak (angel) of Yahawah was standing by.
The malaak (angel) of Yahawah protested to Yahawashawai, saying,

"Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): ‘If you will yalak (walk) in my darak (ways), and if you will follow my instructions, then you also shall dayan (judge) my bayath (house), and shall also shamar (keep) my courts, and I will nathan (give) you a place of access among these who imad (stand) by.

Hear now, Yahawashawai the gadawal (high) kahan (priest), you and your rai (fellows) who yashab (sit) panayam (before) you; for they are men who are a mawapath (sign): for, behold, I will bawaa (bring) forth my ibad (servant), the Branch.

For, behold, the aban (stone) that I have nathan (set) panayam (before) Yahawashawai; on one aban (stone) are shabai (seven) iyan (eyes): behold, I will pathach (engrave) its engraving,' says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), ‘and I will mawash (remove) the iwan (iniquity) of that aratz (land) in one yawam (day).
In that yawam (day),' says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), ‘you will qaraa (invite) every ayash (man) his neighbor under the vine and under the fig tree.'
The malaak (angel) who talked with me came again, and wakened me, as a ayash (man) who is wakened out of his shanah (sleep).

He said to me, "What do you raah (see)?" I said, "I have seen, and behold, a lampstand all of gold, with its bowl on the raash (top) of it, and its shabai (seven) nayar (lamps) thereon; there are shabai (seven) pipes to each of the nayar (lamps), which are on the raash (top) of it;
and shanayam (two) olive trees by it, one on the yamayan (right) side of the bowl, and the other on the shamaawal (left) side of it.
I answered and spoke to the malaak (angel) who talked with me, saying, "What are these, my Adawan?
Then the malaak (angel) who talked with me answered me, "Don't you yadai (know) what these are?" I said, "No, my Adawan.

Then he answered and spoke to me, saying, "This is the dabar (word) of Yahawah to Zarababal, saying, ‘Not by might, nor by kach (power), but by my rawach (spirit),' amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
Who are you, gadawal (great) har (mountain)? panayam (before) Zarababal you are a mayashawar (plain); and he will yatzaa (bring) out the capstone with shouts of ‘Grace, grace, to it!'
Moreover the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

"The yad (hands) of Zarababal have laid the yasad (foundation) of this bayath (house). His yad (hands) shall also finish it; and you will yadai (know) that Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) has sent me to you.

Indeed, who despises the yawam (day) of qatan (small) things? For these seven shall Shamach, and shall raah (see) the plumb line in the yad (hand) of Zarababal. These are the iyan (eyes) of Yahawah, which run back and forth through the whole aratz (earth).
Then I asked him, "What are these shanayam (two) olive trees on the yamayan (right) side of the lampstand and on the shamaawal (left) side of it?
I asked him the shanay (second) time, "What are these shanayam (two) olive branches, which are yad (beside) the shanayam (two) golden spouts, that pour the golden zahab (oil) out of themselves?
He answered me, "Don't you yadai (know) what these are?" I said, "No, my Adawan.
Then he said, "These are the shanayam (two) yatzahar (anointed) ones who imad (stand) by the Adawan of the whole aratz (earth).
Then again I lifted up my iyan (eyes), and saw, and behold, a flying scroll.
He said to me, "What do you raah (see)?" I answered, "I raah (see) a flying scroll; its arak (length) is isharayam (twenty) amah (cubits), and its breadth ishar (ten) amah (cubits).

Then he said to me, "This is the alah (curse) that goes out over the surface of the whole aratz (land); for everyone who steals shall be cut off according to it on the one side; and everyone who shabai (swears) falsely shall be cut off according to it on the other side.

I will yatzaa (cause) it to go out," says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "and it will bawaa (enter) into the bayath (house) of the thief, and into the bayath (house) of him who shabai (swears) falsely by my sham (name); and it will lawan (remain) in the midst of his bayath (house), and will kalah (destroy) it with its itz (timber) and its aban (stones).
Then the malaak (angel) who talked with me came forward, and said to me, "nashaa (lift) up now your iyan (eyes), and raah (see) what is this that is appearing.
I said, "What is it?" He said, "This is the ephah basket that is appearing." He said moreover, "This is their iyan (appearance) in all the aratz (land)
(and behold, a talent of lead was lifted up); and this is a ashah (woman) sitting in the midst of the ephah basket.
He said, "This is rashaih (wickedness);" and he threw her down into the midst of the ephah basket; and he threw the aban (weight) of lead on its pah (mouth).

Then lifted I up my iyan (eyes), and saw, and behold, there were shanayam (two) women, and the rawach (wind) was in their wings. Now they had wings like the wings of a stork, and they lifted up the ephah basket between aratz (earth) and the sky.
Then I said to the malaak (angel) who talked with me, "Where are these carrying the ephah basket?
He said to me, "To banah (build) her a bayath (house) in the aratz (land) of Shanair. When it is prepared, she will be yanach (set) there in her own place.
Again I lifted up my iyan (eyes), and saw, and behold, arabai (four) chariots came out from between shanayam (two) har (mountains); and the har (mountains) were har (mountains) of brass.
In the raashawan (first) chariot were Adam horses; in the shanay (second) chariot Shachar horses;
in the shalayashay (third) chariot Laban horses; and in the rabayaiy (fourth) chariot Barad horses, all Amatz them powerful.
Then I asked the malaak (angel) who talked with me, "What are these, my Adawan?
The malaak (angel) answered me, "These are the arabai (four) rawach (winds) of the sky, which yatzaa (go) forth from standing before the Adawan of all the aratz (earth).

The one with the Shachar horses goes out toward the tzapawan (north) aratz (country); and the Laban went out achar (after) them; and the Barad went yatzaa (forth) toward the thayaman (south) aratz (country).

The Amatz went out, and sought to yalak (go) that they might halak (walk) back and forth through the aratz (earth): and he said, "yalak (go) around and through the aratz (earth)!" So they walked back and halak (forth) through the aratz (earth).
Then he called to me, and spoke to me, saying, "raah (see), those who yatzaa (go) toward the tzapawan (north) aratz (country) have quieted my rawach (spirit) in the tzapawan (north) aratz (country).
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to me, saying,

"Take of them of the captivity, even of Chaladay, of Tawabayah, and of Yadaiyah; and bawaa (come) the same yawam (day), and bawaa (go) into the bayath (house) of Yaashayah the ban (son) of Tzapanayah, where they have bawaa (come) from Babal.
Yes, take kasap (silver) and gold, and ishah (make) itarah (crowns), and shawam (set) them on the raash (head) of Yahawashawai the ban (son) of Yahawatzadaq, the gadawal (high) kahan (priest);

and amar (speak) to him, saying, ‘Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "Behold, the ayash (man) whose sham (name) is the Branch: and he shall grow up out of his place; and he shall banah (build) the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah;

even he shall banah (build) the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah; and he shall nashaa (bear) the glory, and shall yashab (sit) and mashal (rule) on his kasaa (throne); and he shall be a kahan (priest) on his kasaa (throne); and the itzah (counsel) of shalawam (peace) shall be between them shanayam (both).
The itarah (crowns) shall be to Chalam, and to Tawabayah, and to Yadaiyah, and to Chan the ban (son) of Tzapanayah, for a zakarawan (memorial) in the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah.

Those who are Rachawaq off shall bawaa (come) and banah (build) in the hayakal (temple) of Yahawah; and you shall yadai (know) that Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) has sent me to you. This will happen, if you will diligently obey the qawal (voice) of Yahawah your Alahayam."'
It happened in the fourth Shanah of malak (king) Darayawash that the dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Zakarayah in the fourth day of the thashayaiy (ninth) chadash (month), the Kasalaw of Chislev.
The people of Bethel sent Sharaatzar and Ragamamalak Melech, and their men, to entreat yahawah (yahweh's) favor,

and to amar (speak) to the kahan (priests) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), and to the nabayaa (prophets), saying, "Should I weep in the chamayashay (fifth) chadash (month), separating myself, as I have done these so many Shanah?
Then the dabar (word) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) came to me, saying,

"amar (speak) to all the im (people) of the aratz (land), and to the kahan (priests), saying, ‘When you fasted and mourned in the chamayashay (fifth) and in the shabayaiy (seventh) month for these shabaiyam (seventy) Shanah, did you at all fast to me, really to me?
When you akal (eat), and when you drink, don't you akal (eat) for yourselves, and drink for yourselves?

Aren't these the dabar (words) which Yahawah proclaimed by the raashawan (former) nabayaa (prophets), when Yarawashalam was inhabited and in shalaw (prosperity), and its Iyar around her, and the Nagab and the lowland were inhabited?'
The dabar (word) of Yahawah came to Zakarayah, saying,
"Thus has Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) spoken, saying, ‘shapat (execute) amath (true) mashapat (judgment), and show chasad (kindness) and racham (compassion) every ayash (man) to his ach (brother).
Don't oppress the alamanah (widow), nor the fatherless, the foreigner, nor the Inay; and let none of you chashab (devise) rai (evil) against his ach (brother) in your labab (heart).'
But they refused to listen, and turned their backs, and stopped their ears, that they might not hear.

Yes, they made their lab (hearts) as hard as flint, lest they might hear the thawarah (law), and the dabar (words) which Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) had sent by his rawach (spirit) by the raashawan (former) nabayaa (prophets). Therefore gadawal (great) qatzap (wrath) came from Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
It has come to pass that, as he called, and they refused to listen, so they will qaraa (call), and I will not listen," said Yahawah of tzabaa (armies);

"but I will scatter them with a whirlwind among all the gawayam (nations) which they have not yadai (known). Thus the aratz (land) was shamam (desolate) achar (after) them, so that no ibar (man) passed through nor returned: for they made the pleasant aratz (land) desolate.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) came to me.
Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): "I am jealous for Tzayawan with gadawal (great) jealousy, and I am jealous for her with gadawal (great) chamah (wrath).

Thus amar (says) Yahawah: "I have returned to Tzayawan, and will shakan (dwell) in the midst of Yarawashalam. Yarawashalam shall be called ‘The Iyar of Truth;' and the har (mountain) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), ‘The qadash (holy) har (mountain).'

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): "zaqan (old) men and zaqan (old) women will again yashab (dwell) in the streets of Yarawashalam, every ayash (man) with his mashainah (staff) in his yad (hand) for very yawam (age).
The streets of the Iyar will be malaa (full) of yalad (boys) and girls playing in its streets.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): "If it is palaa (marvelous) in the iyan (eyes) of the shaarayath (remnant) of this im (people) in those yawam (days), should it also be palaa (marvelous) in my iyan (eyes)?" says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): "Behold, I will yashai (save) my im (people) from the east aratz (country), and from the west aratz (country);
and I will bawaa (bring) them, and they will shakan (dwell) in the midst of Yarawashalam; and they will be my im (people), and I will be their Alahayam, in truth and in tzadaqah (righteousness).

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): "Let your yad (hands) be chazaq (strong), you who hear in these yawam (days) these dabar (words) from the pah (mouth) of the nabayaa (prophets) who were in the yawam (day) that the yasad (foundation) of the bayath (house) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) was laid, even the hayakal (temple), that it might be built.

For panayam (before) those yawam (days) there was no wages for adam (man), nor any wages for an animal; neither was there any shalawam (peace) to him who went out or came in, because of the tzar (adversary). For I shalach (set) all men everyone against his neighbor.
But now I will not be to the shaarayath (remnant) of this im (people) as in the raashawan (former) yawam (days)," says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).

"For the zarai (seed) of shalawam (peace) and the vine will nathan (yield) its fruit, and the aratz (ground) will nathan (give) its increase, and the shamayam (heavens) will nathan (give) their dew; and I will cause the shaarayath (remnant) of this im (people) to nachal (inherit) all these things.

It shall come to pass that, as you were a qalalah (curse) among the gawayam (nations), bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) and bayath (house) of Yasharaal (Israel), so will I yashai (save) you, and you shall be a barakah (blessing). Don't be yaraa (afraid). Let your yad (hands) be chazaq (strong).

For thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): "As I thought to do raii (evil) to you, when your abawath (fathers) provoked me to qatzap (wrath)," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "and I didn't nacham (repent);
so again have I thought in these yawam (days) to do yatab (good) to Yarawashalam and to the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah). Don't be yaraa (afraid).
These are the things that you shall do: dabar (speak) every ayash (man) the truth with his neighbor. shapat (execute) the mashapat (judgment) of truth and shalawam (peace) in your gates,

and let ayash (none) of you chashab (devise) rai (evil) in your labab (hearts) against his neighbor, and ahab (love) no false shabawaih (oath): for all these are things that I shanaa (hate)," says Yahawah.
The dabar (word) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) came to me.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): "The fasts of the rabayaiy (fourth) chamayashay (fifth), shabayaiy (seventh), and ishayaray (tenth) months shall be for the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah) joy and gladness, and tawab (cheerful) mawaid (feasts). Therefore ahab (love) truth and shalawam (peace).
Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): "Many im (peoples), and the yashab (inhabitants) of many Iyar will yet bawaa (come);

and the yashab (inhabitants) of one shall halak (go) to another, saying, ‘Let us yalak (go) halak (speedily) to entreat the favor of Yahawah, and to seek Yahawah of tzabaa (armies). I will yalak (go) also.'
Yes, many im (peoples) and itzawam (strong) gawayam (nations) will bawaa (come) to seek Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) in Yarawashalam, and to entreat the favor of Yahawah.

Thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies): "In those yawam (days), ishar (ten) men will chazaq (take) hold, out of all the lashawan (languages) of the gawayam (nations), they will chazaq (take) hold of the skirt of him who is a Jew, saying, ‘We will yalak (go) with you, for we have heard that Alahayam is with you.'

An oracle. The dabar (word) of Yahawah is against the aratz (land) of Chadarak, and will manawachah (rest) upon Damashaq; for the iyan (eye) of adam (man) and of all the shabat (tribes) of Yasharaal (Israel) is toward Yahawah;
and Chamath, also, which borders on it; Tzar and Tzayadawan, because they are very chakam (wise).
Tzar built Matzawar a stronghold, and heaped up kasap (silver) like the ipar (dust), and fine Charawatz like the mire of the streets.
Behold, the Adanay will yarash (dispossess) her, and he will strike her chayal (power) in the yam (sea); and she will be devoured with ash (fire).

Ashaqalawan will raah (see) it, and yaraa (fear); Izah also, and will writhe in agony; as will Iqarawan, for her expectation will be disappointed; and the malak (king) will abad (perish) from Izah, and Ashaqalawan will not be inhabited.
Foreigners will yashab (dwell) Ashadawad Ashdod, and I will karath (cut) off the pride of the Palashathay (Philistines).

I will sawar (take) away his dam (blood) out of his pah (mouth), and his shaqawatz (abominations) from between his teeth; and he also will be a shaar (remnant) for our Alahayam; and he will be as a Alawap in Yahawadah (Judah), and Iqarawan as a Yabawasay (Jebusite).

I will chanah (encamp) around my bayath (house) against the matzabah (army), that none ibar (pass) through or shawab (turn back / repent); and no oppressor will ibar (pass) through them any more: for now I have seen with my iyan (eyes).

Rejoice maad (greatly), bath (daughter) of Tzayawan! rawai (shout), bath (daughter) of Yarawashalam! Behold, your malak (king) bawaa (comes) to you! He is tzadayaq (righteous), and having yashai (salvation); Inay, and riding on a donkey, even on a colt, the ban (foal) of a donkey.

I will karath (cut) off the chariot from Aparayam, and the horse from Yarawashalam; and the battle qashath (bow) will be karath (cut) off; and he will dabar (speak) shalawam (peace) to the gawayam (nations): and his dominion will be from yam (sea) to yam (sea), and from the nahar (river) to the apas (ends) of the aratz (earth).
As for you also, because of the dam (blood) of your barayath (covenant), I have shalach (set) free your prisoners from the bawar (pit) in which is no mayam (water).
shawab (turn back / repent) to the stronghold, you prisoners of hope! Even today I nagad (declare) that I will shawab (turn back / repent) mashanah (double) to you.

For indeed I bend Yahawadah (Judah) as a qashath (bow) for me. I have filled the qashath (bow) with Aparayam; and I will stir up your ban (sons), Tzayawan, against your ban (sons), Yawan, and will shawam (make) you like the charab (sword) of a gabawar (mighty) man.
Yahawah will be seen over them; and his chatz (arrow) will yatzaa (go) flash like lightning; and the Adanay Yahawah will blow the trumpet, and will halak (go) with whirlwinds of the thayaman (south).

Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) will defend them; and they will destroy and overcome with sling aban (stones); and they will drink, and roar as through yayan (wine); and they will be filled like mazaraq (bowls), like the corners of the mazabach (altar).
Yahawah their Alahayam will yashai (save) them in that yawam (day) as the flock of his im (people); for they are like the jewels of a nazar (crown), lifted on high over his adamah (land).
For how great is his goodness, and how great is his beauty! Grain will make the young men flourish, and new thayarawash (wine) the virgins.
shaal (ask) of Yahawah rain in the spring ith (time), Yahawah who ishah (makes) storm clouds, and he nathan (gives) rain showers to everyone for the plants in the shadah (field).

For the tharapayam (teraphim) have spoken awan (vanity), and the diviners have seen a lie; and they have told false chalawam (dreams). They nacham (comfort) in vain. Therefore they nasai (go) their tzaan (way) like sheep. They are oppressed, because there is no raih (shepherd).

My ap (anger) is kindled against the raih (shepherds), and I will paqad (punish) the male goats; For Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) has visited his flock, the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah), and will shawam (make) them as his majestic horse in the battle.
From him will yatzaa (come) forth the cornerstone, from him the nail, from him the battle qashath (bow), from him every nagash (ruler) together.
They shall be as gabawar (mighty) men, treading down muddy streets in the battle; and they shall fight, because Yahawah is with them; and the riders on horses will be yabash (confounded).

"I will gabar (strengthen) the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah), and I will yashai (save) the bayath (house) of Yawasap, and I will bring them back; for I have racham (mercy) on them; and they will be as though I had not cast them off: for I am Yahawah their Alahayam, and I will hear them.

Aparayam will be like a gabawar (mighty) man, and their lab (heart) will Shamach as through yayan (wine); yes, their children will raah (see) it, and rejoice. Their lab (heart) will be Shamach in Yahawah.
I will signal for them, and gather them; for I have padah (redeemed) them; and they will increase as they have increased.
I will zarai (sow) them among the im (peoples); and they will zakar (remember) me in far countries; and they will chayah (live) with their children, and will shawab (turn back / repent).

I will shawab (turn back / repent) them again also out of the aratz (land) of Matzarayam, and gather them out of Ashawar; and I will bawaa (bring) them into the aratz (land) of Galaid and Labanawan; and there won't be room matzaa (enough) for them.

He will ibar (pass) through the yam (sea) of tzarah (affliction), and will strike the waves in the yam (sea), and all the depths of the Nile will yabash (dry) up; and the pride of Ashawar will be brought down, and the scepter of Matzarayam will sawar (depart).
I will gabar (strengthen) them in Yahawah; and they will halak (walk) up and down in his sham (name)," says Yahawah.
pathach (open) your doors, Labanawan, that the ash (fire) may akal (devour) your cedars.
Wail, fir tree, for the cedar has fallen, because the stately ones are destroyed. Wail, you oaks of Bashan, for the strong Yair has yarad (come) down.
A qawal (voice) of the wailing of the raih (shepherds)! For their glory is destroyed: a qawal (voice) of the roaring of young kapayar (lions)! For the pride of the Yaradan is ruined.
Thus amar (says) Yahawah my Alahayam: "raih (feed) the flock of slaughter.
Their qanah (buyers) slaughter them, and go unpunished. Those who sell them amar (say), ‘Blessed be Yahawah, for I am rich;' and their own raih (shepherds) don't pity them.

For I will no more pity the yashab (inhabitants) of the aratz (land)," says Yahawah; "but, behold, I will matzaa (deliver) the men everyone into his neighbor's yad (hand), and into the yad (hand) of his malak (king). They will strike the aratz (land), and out of their yad (hand) I will not natzal (deliver) them.
So I fed the flock of slaughter, Kan the Inay of the flock. I took for myself shanayam (two) maqal (staffs). The one I called "Favor," and the other I called "Union," and I fed the flock.
I cut off the shalawash (three) raih (shepherds) in one yarach (month); for my napash (soul) was weary of them, and their napash (soul) also loathed me.

Then I said, "I will not raih (feed) you. That which dies, let it mawath (die); and that which is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let those who are shaar (left) akal (eat) ashah (each) other's flesh.
I took my maqal (staff) Favor, and cut it apart, that I might parar (break) my barayath (covenant) that I had made with all the im (peoples).
It was broken in that yawam (day); and thus the Inay of the flock that listened to me knew that it was the dabar (word) of Yahawah.
I said to them, "If you iyan (think) it best, give me my wages; and if not, keep them." So they weighed for my wages shalawashayam (thirty) pieces of kasap (silver).

Yahawah said to me, "Throw it to the potter, the handsome price that I was valued at by them!" I took the shalawashayam (thirty) pieces of kasap (silver), and threw them to the potter, in the bayath (house) of Yahawah.
Then I cut apart my other maqal (staff), even Union, that I might parar (break) the brotherhood between Yahawadah (Judah) and Yasharaal (Israel).
Yahawah said to me, "Take for yourself yet again the equipment of a Awalay raih (shepherd).

For, behold, I will qawam (raise) up a raih (shepherd) in the aratz (land), who will not paqad (visit) those who are cut off, neither will seek those who are scattered, nor heal that which is shabar (broken), nor feed that which is sound; but he will akal (eat) the flesh of the Barayaa sheep, and will paraq (tear) their hoofs in paraq (pieces).

Woe to the worthless shepherd who leaves the flock! The charab (sword) will be on his zarawai (arm), and on his yamayan (right) iyan (eye). His zarawai (arm) will be completely withered, and his yamayan (right) iyan (eye) will be totally blinded!

An oracle. The dabar (word) of Yahawah concerning Yasharaal (Israel). Yahawah, who stretches out the shamayam (heavens), and yasad (lays) the foundation of the aratz (earth), and forms the rawach (spirit) of adam (man) qarab (within) him says:
"Behold, I will shawam (make) Yarawashalam a cup of reeling to all the surrounding im (peoples), and on Yahawadah (Judah) also will it be in the Matzawar against Yarawashalam.

It will happen in that yawam (day), that I will shawam (make) Yarawashalam a burdensome aban (stone) for all the im (peoples). All who burden themselves with it will be severely wounded, and all the gawayay (nations) of the aratz (earth) will be gathered asap (together) against it.

In that yawam (day)," says Yahawah, "I will strike every horse with terror, and his rider with madness; and I will open my iyan (eyes) on the bayath (house) of Yahawadah (Judah), and will strike every horse of the im (peoples) with blindness.
The Alawap of Yahawadah (Judah) will amar (say) in their lab (heart), ‘The yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam are my amatzah (strength) in Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) their Alahayam.'

In that yawam (day) I will shawam (make) the Alawap of Yahawadah (Judah) like a pan of ash (fire) among itz (wood), and like a ash (flaming) lapayad (torch) among sheaves; and they will akal (devour) all the surrounding im (peoples), on the right yamayan (hand) and on the shamaawal (left); and Yarawashalam will yet again yashab (dwell) in their own place, even in Yarawashalam.

Yahawah also will yashai (save) the ahal (tents) of Yahawadah (Judah) raashawan (first), that the glory of the bayath (house) of Dawad and the glory of the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam not be magnified above Yahawadah (Judah).

In that yawam (day) Yahawah will defend the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam. He who is feeble among them at that yawam (day) will be like Dawad, and the bayath (house) of Dawad will be like Alahayam, like the malaak (angel) of Yahawah panayam (before) them.
It will happen in that yawam (day), that I will seek to destroy all the gawayam (nations) that bawaa (come) against Yarawashalam.

I will pour on the bayath (house) of Dawad, and on the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, the rawach (spirit) of grace and of supplication; and they will look to me whom they have pierced; and they shall mourn for him, as sapad (one) mourns for his only marar (son), and will grieve bitterly for him, as marar (one) grieves for his firstborn.
In that yawam (day) there will be a great mourning in Yarawashalam, like the mourning of Hadadaramawan in the Baqaih of Magadawan.

The aratz (land) will mourn, every mashapachah (family) bad (apart); the mashapachah (family) of the bayath (house) of Dawad apart, and their wives apart; the mashapachah (family) of the bayath (house) of Nathan apart, and their wives apart;
the mashapachah (family) of the bayath (house) of Laway apart, and their wives apart; the mashapachah (family) Shamaiy the Shimeites apart, and their wives apart;
all the mashapachah (families) who shaar (remain), every mashapachah (family) apart, and their wives apart.
"In that yawam (day) there will be a spring opened to the bayath (house) of Dawad and to the yashab (inhabitants) of Yarawashalam, for chataah (sin) and for uncleanness.

It will come to pass in that yawam (day), says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), that I will karath (cut) off the sham (names) of the itzab (idols) out of the aratz (land), and they will be zakar (remembered) no more. I will also cause the nabayaa (prophets) and the rawach (spirit) of impurity to ibar (pass) out of the aratz (land).

It will happen that, when anyone still nabaa (prophesies), then his ab (father) and his am (mother) who bore him will amar (tell) him, ‘You must die, because you amar (speak) lies in the sham (name) of Yahawah;' and his father and his am (mother) who bore him will stab him when he nabaa (prophesies).

It will happen in that yawam (day), that the nabayaa (prophets) will ayash (each) be bawash (ashamed) of his vision, when he nabaa (prophesies); neither will they Labash a hairy adarath (mantle) to deceive:
but he will amar (say), ‘I am no nabayaa (prophet), I am a ibad (tiller) of the ground; for I have been made a bondservant from my youth.'
One will amar (say) to him, ‘What are these makah (wounds) between your arms?' Then he will amar (answer), ‘Those with which I was wounded in the bayath (house) of my ahab (friends).'

"Awake, charab (sword), against my raih (shepherd), and against the gabar (man) who is close to me," says Yahawah of tzabaa (armies). "Strike the raih (shepherd), and the sheep will be scattered; and I will shawab (turn back / repent) my yad (hand) against the little tzair (ones).
It shall happen that in all the aratz (land)," says Yahawah, "shanayam (two) pah (parts) in it will be karath (cut) off and gawai (die); but the shalayashay (third) will be yathar (left) in it.

I will bawaa (bring) the shalayashay (third) part into the ash (fire), and will refine them as kasap (silver) is refined, and will test them like gold is tested. They will qaraa (call) on my sham (name), and I will hear them. I will amar (say), ‘It is my im (people);' and they will amar (say), ‘Yahawah is my Alahayam.'
Behold, a yawam (day) of Yahawah bawaa (comes), when your spoil will be divided in your qarab (midst).

For I will asap (gather) all gawayam (nations) against Yarawashalam to battle; and the Iyar will be taken, the bayath (houses) rifled, and the women ravished. chatzay (half) of the Iyar will yatzaa (go) out into captivity, and the yathar (rest) of the im (people) will not be karath (cut) off from the Iyar.
Then Yahawah will yatzaa (go) out and fight against those gawayam (nations), as when he fought in the yawam (day) of battle.

His feet will imad (stand) in that yawam (day) on the har (mount) of Olives, which is panayam (before) Yarawashalam on the qadam (east); and the har (mount) of Olives will be split in chatzay (two), from east to yam (west), making a very gadawal (great) Gayaa. chatzay (half) of the har (mountain) will move toward the tzapawan (north), and chatzay (half) of it toward the Nagab.

You shall flee by the Gayaa of my har (mountains); for the Gayaa of the har (mountains) shall nagai (reach) to Atzal; yes, you shall flee, just like you fled from panayam (before) the earthquake in the yawam (days) of Izayah malak (king) of Yahawadah (Judah). Yahawah my Alahayam will bawaa (come), and all the qadawash (holy) ones with you.
It will happen in that yawam (day), that there will not be awar (light), Yaqar, or frost.
It will be a unique yawam (day) which is yadai (known) to Yahawah; not yawam (day), and not layal (night); but it will come to pass, that at evening ith (time) there will be awar (light).

It will happen in that yawam (day), that chay (living) mayam (waters) will yatzaa (go) out from Yarawashalam; chatzay (half) Qadamawanay them toward the eastern yam (sea), and chatzay (half) Acharawan them toward the western yam (sea); in qayatz (summer) and in winter will it be.
Yahawah will be malak (king) over all the aratz (earth). In that yawam (day) Yahawah will be one, and his sham (name) one.

All the aratz (land) will be made like the irabah (arabah), from Gabai to Ramawan Nagab of Yarawashalam; and she will be lifted up, and will yashab (dwell) in her place, from Banayamayan gate to the place of the raashawan (first) gate, to the corner gate, and from the magadal (tower) Chananaal Hananel to the malak (king's) winepresses.
Men will yashab (dwell) therein, and there will be no more charam (curse); but Yarawashalam will yashab (dwell) safely.

This will be the magapah (plague) with which Yahawah will nagap (strike) all the im (peoples) who have warred against Yarawashalam: their flesh will consume away while they imad (stand) on their feet, and their iyan (eyes) will consume away in their sockets, and their lashawan (tongue) will consume away in their pah (mouth).

It will happen in that yawam (day), that a rab (great) panic from Yahawah will be among them; and they will lay chazaq (hold) everyone on the yad (hand) of his neighbor, and his yad (hand) will ilah (rise) up against the yad (hand) of his neighbor.

Yahawadah (Judah) also will fight at Yarawashalam; and the wealth of all the surrounding gawayam (nations) will be gathered asap (together): gold, and kasap (silver), and clothing, in maad (great) abundance.
So will be the magapah (plague) of the horse, of the mule, of the camel, and of the donkey, and of all the animals that will be in those machanah (camps), as that magapah (plague).

It will happen that everyone who is yathar (left) of all the gawayam (nations) that came against Yarawashalam will ilah (go) up from Shanah to Shanah to shachah (worship) the malak (king), Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), and to keep the chag (feast) of sakah (tents).

It will be, that whoever of all the mashapachah (families) of the aratz (earth) doesn't ilah (go) up to Yarawashalam to shachah (worship) the malak (king), Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), on them there will be no rain.

If the mashapachah (family) of Matzarayam doesn't ilah (go) up, and doesn't bawaa (come), neither will it rain on them. This will be the magapah (plague) with which Yahawah will nagap (strike) the gawayam (nations) that don't ilah (go) up to keep the chag (feast) of sakah (tents).
This will be the chataah (punishment) of Matzarayam, and the chataah (punishment) of all the gawayam (nations) that don't ilah (go) up to keep the chag (feast) of sakah (tents).

In that yawam (day) there will be on the bells of the horses, "qadash (holy) TO Yahawah;" and the pots in yahawah (yahweh's) bayath (house) will be like the mazaraq (bowls) panayam (before) the mazabach (altar).

Yes, every pot in Yarawashalam and in Yahawadah (Judah) will be qadash (holy) to Yahawah of tzabaa (armies); and all those who zabach (sacrifice) will bawaa (come) and take of them, and cook in them. In that yawam (day) there will no longer be a Kanainay (Canaanite) in the bayath (house) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
An oracle: the dabar (word) of Yahawah to Yasharaal (Israel) by Malaakay.
"I have loved you," says Yahawah. Yet you amar (say), "How have you loved us?" "Wasn't Ishaw Yaiqab ach (brother)?" amar (says) Yahawah, "Yet I loved Yaiqab;
but Ishaw I hated, and made his har (mountains) a desolation, and gave his nachalah (heritage) to the jackals of the madabar (wilderness).

Whereas Adam amar (says), "We are beaten down, but we will shawab (turn back / repent) and banah (build) the waste places;" thus amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "They shall banah (build), but I will haras (throw) down; and men will qaraa (call) them ‘The Wicked gabawal (land),' even the im (people) against whom Yahawah shows zaim (wrath) iwalam (forever).
Your iyan (eyes) will raah (see), and you will amar (say), "Yahawah is great— even beyond the border of Yasharaal (Israel)!

"A ban (son) honors his ab (father), and a ibad (servant) his adawan (master). If I am a ab (father), then where is my honor? And if I am a adawan (master), where is the respect due me? amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies) to you, kahan (priests), who despise my sham (name). You amar (say), ‘How have we despised your sham (name)?'
You offer polluted lacham (bread) on my mazabach (altar). You amar (say), ‘How have we polluted you?' In that you amar (say), ‘yahawah (yahweh's) table contemptible.'

When you offer the iwar (blind) for zabach (sacrifice), isn't that rai (evil)? And when you offer the Pasach and chalah (sick), isn't that rai (evil)? qarab (present) it now to your governor! Will he be pleased with you? Or will he nashaa (accept) your panayam (person)?" amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
"Now, please entreat the favor of Al, that he may be gracious to us. With this, will he nashaa (accept) any of you?" amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).

"Oh that there were sagar (one) among you who would shut the doors, that you might not awar (kindle) fire on my mazabach (altar) in vain! I have no Chapatz in you," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "neither will I accept an manachah (offering) at your yad (hand).

For from the rising of the shamash (sun) even to the going down of the same, my sham (name) is gadawal (great) among the gawayam (nations), and in every place qatar (incense) will be offered to my sham (name), and a tahawar (pure) manachah (offering): for my sham (name) is gadawal (great) among the gawayam (nations)," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
"But you chalal (profane) it, in that you amar (say), ‘yahawah (yahweh's) table is polluted, and its fruit, even its food, is contemptible.'

You amar (say) also, ‘Behold, what a weariness it is!' and you have sniffed at it," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies); "and you have brought that which was taken by violence, the Pasach, and the chalah (sick); thus you bawaa (bring) the manachah (offering). Should I accept this at your yad (hand)?" amar (says) Yahawah.

"But the deceiver is cursed, who has in his flock a zakar (male), and nadar (vows), and zabach (sacrifices) to the Adanay a blemished thing; for I am a gadawal (great) malak (king)," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "and my sham (name) is awesome among the gawayam (nations).
"Now, you kahan (priests), this matzawah (commandment) is for you.

If you will not listen, and if you will not shawam (lay) it to lab (heart), to nathan (give) kabawad (glory) to my sham (name)," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "then will I shalach (send) the maarah (curse) on you, and I will arar (curse) your barakah (blessings). Indeed, I have cursed them already, because you do not shawam (lay) it to lab (heart).
Behold, I will rebuke your zarai (seed), and will spread dung on your panayam (faces), even the dung of your chag (feasts); and you will be taken nashaa (away) with it.
You will yadai (know) that I have sent this matzawah (commandment) to you, that my barayath (covenant) may be with Laway," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).

"My barayath (covenant) was with him of chay (life) and shalawam (peace); and I gave them to him that he might be reverent toward me; and he was reverent panayam (toward) me, and stood in awe of my sham (name).

The thawarah (law) of truth was in his pah (mouth), and iwal (unrighteousness) was not found in his shapah (lips). He walked with me in shalawam (peace) and mayashawar (uprightness), and turned many shawab (turn back / repent) from iwan (iniquity).

For the kahan (priest's) shapah (lips) should shamar (keep) daith (knowledge), and they should seek the thawarah (law) at his pah (mouth); for he is the malaak (messenger) of Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
But you have turned aside out of the darak (way). You have caused many to stumble in the thawarah (law). You have corrupted the barayath (covenant) of Laway," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).

"Therefore I have also made you contemptible and Shapal before all the im (people), according to the way you have not kept my darak (ways), but have had nashaa (respect) for persons in the thawarah (law).

Don't we all have one ab (father)? Hasn't one Al created us? Why do we bagad (deal) treacherously every ayash (man) against his ach (brother), profaning the barayath (covenant) of our abawath (fathers)?

Yahawadah (Judah) has dealt bagad (treacherously), and an thawaibah (abomination) is committed in Yasharaal (Israel) and in Yarawashalam; for Yahawadah (Judah) has profaned the qadash (holiness) of Yahawah which he ahab (loves), and has married the bath (daughter) of a foreign Al.

Yahawah will karath (cut) off, to the ayash (man) who does this, him who wakes and him who answers, out of the ahal (tents) of Yaiqab, and him who offers an manachah (offering) to Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).

This again you do: you cover the mazabach (altar) of Yahawah with tears, with weeping, and with sighing, because he doesn't panah (regard) the manachah (offering) any more, neither receives it with ratzawan (good) will at your yad (hand).

Yet you amar (say), ‘mah (why)?' Because Yahawah has been iwad (witness) between you and the ashah (wife) of your youth, against whom you have dealt bagad (treacherously), though she is your companion, and the ashah (wife) of your barayath (covenant).

Did he not ishah (make) you one, although he had the shaar (residue) of the rawach (spirit)? Why one? He sought a godly zarai (seed). Therefore shamar (take) heed to your rawach (spirit), and let no one bagad (deal) treacherously against the ashah (wife) of his youth.

For I shanaa (hate) divorce," amar (says) Yahawah, the Alahayam of Yasharaal (Israel), "and him who covers his garment with violence!" amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies). "Therefore shamar (take) heed to your rawach (spirit), that you don't bagad (deal) treacherously.

You have wearied Yahawah with your dabar (words). Yet you amar (say), ‘How have we wearied him?' In that you amar (say), ‘Everyone who does rai (evil) is tawab (good) in the iyan (sight) of Yahawah, and he delights in them;' or ‘Where is the Alahayam of justice?'

"Behold, I shalach (send) my malaak (messenger), and he will panah (prepare) the darak (way) panayam (before) me; and the Adawan, whom you seek, will suddenly bawaa (come) to his hayakal (temple); and the malaak (messenger) of the barayath (covenant), whom you Chapatz, behold, he bawaa (comes)!" amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
"But who can endure the yawam (day) of his coming? And who will imad (stand) when he raah (see)? For he is like a refiner's ash (fire), and like launderer's soap;

and he will yashab (sit) as a refiner and purifier of kasap (silver), and he will tahar (purify) the ban (sons) of Laway, and refine them as gold and kasap (silver); and they shall offer to Yahawah manachah (offerings) in tzadaqah (righteousness).
Then the manachah (offering) of Yahawadah (Judah) and Yarawashalam will be pleasant to Yahawah, as in the yawam (days) of old, and as in Qadamawanay Shanah.

I will qarab (come) near to you to mashapat (judgment); and I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, and against the naap (adulterers), and against the perjurers, and against those who oppress the shakayar (hireling) in his wages, the alamanah (widow), and the fatherless, and who deprive the foreigner of justice, and don't yaraa (fear) me," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
"For I, Yahawah, don't shanah (change); therefore you, ban (sons) of Yaiqab, are not consumed.

From the yawam (days) of your abawath (fathers) you have turned sawar (aside) from my chaq (ordinances), and have not kept them. shawab (turn back / repent) to me, and I will shawab (turn back / repent) to you," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies). "But you amar (say), ‘How shall we shawab (turn back / repent)?'
Will a adam (man) rob Alahayam? Yet you rob me! But you amar (say), ‘How have we robbed you?' In maishar (tithes) and tharawamah (offerings).
You are cursed with the maarah (curse); for you rob me, even this whole gaway (nation).

bawaa (bring) the whole maishar (tithe) into the storehouse, that Tarap may be food in my bayath (house), and test me now in this," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "if I will not pathach (open) you the windows of shamayam (heaven), and pour you out a barakah (blessing), that there shall not be room enough for.

I will rebuke the devourer for your sakes, and he shall not shachath (destroy) the fruits of your adamah (ground); neither shall your vine shakal (cast) its fruit before its time in the shadah (field)," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
"All gawayam (nations) shall ashar (call) you blessed, Chapatz you will be a delightful aratz (land)," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
"Your dabar (words) have been chazaq (stout) amar (against) me," says Yahawah. "Yet you amar (say), ‘What have we spoken against you?'
You have said, ‘It is vain to ibad (serve) Alahayam;' and ‘What profit is it that we have followed his instructions, and that we have walked mournfully panayam (before) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies)?
Now we ashar (call) the Zad ashar (happy); yes, those who ishah (work) rashaih (wickedness) are built up; yes, they tempt Alahayam, and malat (escape).'

Then those who feared Yahawah spoke one with rai (another); and Yahawah listened, and heard, and a book of memory was written panayam (before) him, for those who feared Yahawah, and who honored his sham (name).

They shall be mine," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "my own sagalah (possession) in the yawam (day) that I ishah (make), and I will spare them, as a ayash (man) spares his own ban (son) who ibad (serves) him.
Then you shall shawab (turn back / repent) and raah (see) between the tzadayaq (righteous) and the rashai (wicked), between him who ibad (serves) Alahayam and him who doesn't ibad (serve) him.

"For, behold, the yawam (day) bawaa (comes), it bair (burns) as a furnace; and all the Zad, and all who ishah (work) rashaih (wickedness), will be stubble; and the yawam (day) that bawaa (comes) will lahat (burn) them up," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies), "that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.
But to you who yaraa (fear) my sham (name) shall the shamash (sun) of tzadaqah (righteousness) arise with healing in its wings. You will yatzaa (go) out, and leap like calves of the stall.
You shall tread down the rashai (wicked); for they will be ashes under the kap (soles) of your feet in the yawam (day) that I ishah (make)," amar (says) Yahawah of tzabaa (armies).
"zakar (remember) the thawarah (law) of Mashah my ibad (servant), which I tzawah (commanded) to him in Charab for all Yasharaal (Israel), even chaq (statutes) and mashapat (ordinances).
Behold, I will shalach (send) you Alayah the nabayaa (prophet) panayam (before) the gadawal (great) and yaraa (terrible) yawam (day) of Yahawah bawaa (comes).

He will shawab (turn back / repent) the lab (hearts) of the abawath (fathers) to the children, and the lab (hearts) of the children to their abawath (fathers), lest I bawaa (come) and strike the aratz (earth) with a charam (curse).
The book of the genealogy of Yashawai Mashayach, the son of Dawad, the son of Abaraham.
Abaraham became the father of Yatzachaq. Yatzachaq became the father of Yaiqab. Yaiqab became the father of Yahawadah and his brothers.
Yahawadah became the father of Paratz and Zarach by Thamar. Paratz became the father of Chatzarawan. Chatzarawan became the father of Ram.
Ram became the father of Imayanadab. Imayanadab became the father of Nachashawan. Nachashawan became the father of Shalamah.
Shalamah became the father of Baiz by Rachab. Baiz became the father of Iwabad by Rawath. Iwabad became the father of Yashay.
Yashay became the father of King Dawad. Dawad became the father of Shalamah by her who had been Awarayah’s wife.
Shalamah became the father of Rachabaim. Rachabaim became the father of Abayah. Abayah became the father of Asaa.
Asaa became the father of Yahawashapat. Yahawashapat became the father of Yahawaram. Yahawaram became the father of Izayahaw.
Izayahaw became the father of Yawatham. Yawatham became the father of Achaz. Achaz became the father of Chazaqayahaw.
Chazaqayahaw became the father of Manashah. Manashah became the father of Amawan. Amawan became the father of Yaashayahaw.
Yaashayahaw became the father of Jechoniah and his brothers, at the time of the exile to Babal.
After the exile to Babal, Jechoniah became the father of Shaalathayaal. Shaalathayaal became the father of Zarababal.
Zarababal became the father of Abiud. Abiud became the father of Alayaqayam. Alayaqayam became the father of Azor.
Azor became the father of Tzadawaq. Tzadawaq became the father of Achim. Achim became the father of Eliud.
Eliud became the father of Alaizar. Alaizar became the father of Matthan. Matthan became the father of Yaiqab.
Yaiqab became the father of Yawasap, the husband of Marayam, from whom was born Yashawai, who is called Mashayach.

So all the generations from Abaraham to Dawad are fourteen generations; from Dawad to the exile to Babal fourteen generations; and from the carrying away to Babal to the Mashayach, fourteen generations.
Now the birth of Yashawai Mashayach was like this: After his mother, Marayam, was engaged to Yawasap, before they came together, she was found pregnant by the Holy Spirit.
Yawasap, her husband, being a righteous man, and not willing to make her a public example, intended to put her away secretly.

But when he thought about these things, behold, an angel of the Adanay appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Yawasap, son of Dawad, don’t be afraid to take to yourself Marayam, your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.
She shall give birth to a son. You shall name him Yashawai, for it is he who shall save his people from their sins.”
Now all this has happened that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Adanay through the prophet, saying,
“Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and shall give birth to a son. They shall call his name Imanawaal;” which is, being interpreted, “Alahayam with us.”
Yawasap arose from his sleep, and did as the angel of the Adanay commanded him, and took his wife to himself;
and didn’t know her sexually until she had given birth to her firstborn son. He named him Yashawai.
Now when Yashawai was born in Bayathalacham of Yahawadah in the days of King Hawaradawas, behold, wise men from the east came to Yarawashalam, saying,
“Where is he who is born King of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east, and have come to worship him.”
When King Hawaradawas heard it, he was troubled, and all Yarawashalam with him.
Gathering together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he asked them where the Mashayach would be born.
They said to him, “In Bayathalacham of Yahawadah, for this is written through the prophet,
‘You Bayathalacham, land of Yahawadah, are in no way least among the princes of Yahawadah: for out of you shall come a governor, who shall shepherd my people, Yasharaal.’ ”
Then Hawaradawas secretly called the wise men, and learned from them exactly what time the star appeared.
He sent them to Bayathalacham, and said, “Go and search diligently for the young child. When you have found him, bring me word, so that I also may come and worship him.”
They, having heard the king, went their way; and behold, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, until it came and stood over where the young child was.
When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.
They came into the house and saw the young child with Marayam, his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Opening their treasures, they offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Being warned in a dream not to return to Hawaradawas, they went back to their own country another way.

Now when they had departed, behold, an angel of the Adanay appeared to Yawasap in a dream, saying, “Arise and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Matzarayam, and stay there until I tell you, for Hawaradawas will seek the young child to destroy him.”
He arose and took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Matzarayam,
and was there until the death of Hawaradawas; that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Adanay through the prophet, saying, “Out of Matzarayam I called my son.”

Then Hawaradawas, when he saw that he was mocked by the wise men, was exceedingly angry, and sent out, and killed all the male children who were in Bayathalacham and in all the surrounding countryside, from two years old and under, according to the exact time which he had learned from the wise men.
Then that which was spoken by Yaramayahaw the prophet was fulfilled, saying,
“A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, weeping and great mourning, Rachal weeping for her children; she wouldn’t be comforted, because they are no more.”
But when Hawaradawas was dead, behold, an angel of the Adanay appeared in a dream to Yawasap in Matzarayam, saying,
“Arise and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Yasharaal, for those who sought the young child’s life are dead.”
He arose and took the young child and his mother, and came into the land of Yasharaal.
But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Yahawadah in the place of his father, Hawaradawas, he was afraid to go there. Being warned in a dream, he withdrew into the region of Galayal,
and came and lived in a city called Natzarath; that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophets that he will be called a Nazarene.
In those days, Yawachanan the Baptizer came, preaching in the wilderness of Yahawadah, saying,
“Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!”
For this is he who was spoken of by Yashaiyahaw the prophet, saying, “The voice of one crying in the wilderness, make the way of the Adanay ready! Make his paths straight!”
Now Yawachanan himself wore clothing made of camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.
Then people from Yarawashalam, all of Yahawadah, and all the region around the Yaradan went out to him.
They were baptized by him in the Yaradan, confessing their sins.
But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming for his baptism, he said to them, “You offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
Therefore produce fruit worthy of repentance!
Don’t think to yourselves, ‘We have Abaraham for our father,’ for I tell you that Alahayam is able to raise up children to Abaraham from these stones.
“Even now the ax lies at the root of the trees. Therefore every tree that doesn’t produce good fruit is cut down, and cast into the fire.
I indeed baptize you in water for repentance, but he who comes after me is mightier than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.
His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor. He will gather his wheat into the barn, but the chaff he will burn up with unquenchable fire.”
Then Yashawai came from Galayal to the Yaradan to Yawachanan, to be baptized by him.
But Yawachanan would have hindered him, saying, “I need to be baptized by you, and you come to me?”
But Yashawai, answering, said to him, “Allow it now, for this is the fitting way for us to fulfill all righteousness.” Then he allowed him.
Yashawai, when he was baptized, went up directly from the water: and behold, the heavens were opened to him. He saw the Spirit of Alahayam descending as a dove, and coming on him.
Behold, a voice out of the heavens said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”
Then Yashawai was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
When he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was hungry afterward.
The tempter came and said to him, “If you are the Son of Alahayam, command that these stones become bread.”
But he answered, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of Alahayam’s mouth.’ ”
Then the devil took him into the holy city. He set him on the pinnacle of the temple,

and said to him, “If you are the Son of Alahayam, throw yourself down, for it is written, ‘He will command his angels concerning you,’ and, ‘On their hands they will bear you up, so that you don’t dash your foot against a stone.’ ”
Yashawai said to him, “Again, it is written, ‘You shall not test the Adanay, your Alahayam.’ ”
Again, the devil took him to an exceedingly high mountain, and showed him all the kingdoms of the world, and their glory.
He said to him, “I will give you all of these things, if you will fall down and worship me.”
Then Yashawai said to him, “Get behind me, Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the Adanay your Alahayam, and you shall serve him only.’ ”
Then the devil left him, and behold, angels came and served him.
Now when Yashawai heard that Yawachanan was delivered up, he withdrew into Galayal.
Leaving Natzarath, he came and lived in Kaparanachawam, which is by the sea, in the region of Zabawalan and Napathalay,
that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Yashaiyahaw the prophet, saying,
“The land of Zabawalan and the land of Napathalay, toward the sea, beyond the Yaradan, Galayal of the Gentiles,
the people who sat in darkness saw a great light, to those who sat in the region and shadow of death, to them light has dawned.”
From that time, Yashawai began to preach, and to say, “Repent! For the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand.”
Walking by the sea of Galayal, he saw two brothers: Shamaiwan, who is called Kayapaa, and Anadaray, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.
He said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men.”
They immediately left their nets and followed him.
Going on from there, he saw two other brothers, Yaiqab the son of Zebedee, and Yawachanan his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets. He called them.
They immediately left the boat and their father, and followed him.
Yashawai went about in all Galayal, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.

The report about him went out into all Aram. They brought to him all who were sick, afflicted with various diseases and torments, possessed with demons, epileptics, and paralytics; and he healed them.
Great multitudes from Galayal, Decapolis, Yarawashalam, Yahawadah and from beyond the Yaradan followed him.
Seeing the multitudes, he went up onto the mountain. When he had sat down, his disciples came to him.
He opened his mouth and taught them, saying,
“Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth.
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled.
Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see Alahayam.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of Alahayam.
Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
“Blessed are you when people reproach you, persecute you, and say all kinds of evil against you falsely, for my sake.
Rejoice, and be exceedingly glad, for great is your reward in heaven. For that is how they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
“You are the salt of the earth, but if the salt has lost its flavor, with what will it be salted? It is then good for nothing, but to be cast out and trodden under the feet of men.
You are the light of the world. A city located on a hill can’t be hidden.
Neither do you light a lamp, and put it under a measuring basket, but on a stand; and it shines to all who are in the house.
Even so, let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
“Don’t think that I came to destroy the law or the prophets. I didn’t come to destroy, but to fulfill.
For most certainly, I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not even one smallest letter or one tiny pen stroke shall in any way pass away from the law, until all things are accomplished.

Whoever, therefore, shall break one of these least commandments, and teach others to do so, shall be called least in the Kingdom of Heaven; but whoever shall do and teach them shall be called great in the Kingdom of Heaven.
For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, there is no way you will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.
“You have heard that it was said to the ancient ones, ‘You shall not murder;’ and ‘Whoever murders will be in danger of the judgment.’

But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother without a cause will be in danger of the judgment. Whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca!’ will be in danger of the council. Whoever says, ‘You fool!’ will be in danger of the fire of Gehenna.
“If therefore you are offering your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother has anything against you,
leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
Agree with your adversary quickly, while you are with him on the way; lest perhaps the prosecutor deliver you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and you be cast into prison.
Most certainly I tell you, you shall by no means get out of there, until you have paid the last penny.
“You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall not commit adultery;’
but I tell you that everyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart.

If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.

If your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off, and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.
“It was also said, ‘Whoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorce,’
but I tell you that whoever puts away his wife, except for the cause of sexual immorality, makes her an adulteress; and whoever marries her when she is put away commits adultery.
“Again you have heard that it was said to the ancient ones, ‘You shall not make false vows, but shall perform to the Adanay your vows,’
but I tell you, don’t swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of Alahayam;
nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Yarawashalam, for it is the city of the great King.
Neither shall you swear by your head, for you can’t make one hair white or black.
But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.
“You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’
But I tell you, don’t resist him who is evil; but whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also.
If anyone sues you to take away your coat, let him have your cloak also.
Whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two.
Give to him who asks you, and don’t turn away him who desires to borrow from you.
“You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’
But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you,
that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.
For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?
If you only greet your friends, what more do you do than others? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?
Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.
“Be careful that you don’t do your charitable giving before men, to be seen by them, or else you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.

Therefore when you do merciful deeds, don’t sound a trumpet before yourself, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may get glory from men. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
But when you do merciful deeds, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand does,
so that your merciful deeds may be in secret, then your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.

“When you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell you, they have received their reward.
But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
In praying, don’t use vain repetitions, as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard for their much speaking.
Therefore don’t be like them, for your Father knows what things you need, before you ask him.
Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
Give us today our daily bread.
Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’
“For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
But if you don’t forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

“Moreover when you fast, don’t be like the hypocrites, with sad faces. For they disfigure their faces, that they may be seen by men to be fasting. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
But you, when you fast, anoint your head, and wash your face;
so that you are not seen by men to be fasting, but by your Father who is in secret, and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
“Don’t lay up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal;
but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves don’t break through and steal;
for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
“The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.
But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness!
“No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both Alahayam and Mammon.
Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
“Which of you, by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?
Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin,
yet I tell you that even Shalamah in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.
But if Alahayam so clothes the grass of the field, which today exists, and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, won’t he much more clothe you, you of little faith?
“Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’
For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
But seek first Alahayam’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.
“Don’t judge, so that you won’t be judged.
For with whatever judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you.
Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye?
Or how will you tell your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye;’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye?
You hypocrite! First remove the beam out of your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of your brother’s eye.
“Don’t give that which is holy to the dogs, neither throw your pearls before the pigs, lest perhaps they trample them under their feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.
“Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you.
For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.
Or who is there among you, who, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone?
Or if he asks for a fish, who will give him a serpent?
If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
Therefore whatever you desire for men to do to you, you shall also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.
“Enter in by the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter in by it.
How narrow is the gate, and restricted is the way that leads to life! Few are those who find it.
“Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.
By their fruits you will know them. Do you gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?
Even so, every good tree produces good fruit; but the corrupt tree produces evil fruit.
A good tree can’t produce evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree produce good fruit.
Every tree that doesn’t grow good fruit is cut down, and thrown into the fire.
Therefore by their fruits you will know them.
Not everyone who says to me, ‘Adanay, Adanay,’ will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven; but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.
Many will tell me in that day, ‘Adanay, Adanay, didn’t we prophesy in your name, in your name cast out demons, and in your name do many mighty works?’
Then I will tell them, ‘I never knew you. Depart from me, you who work iniquity.’
“Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine, and does them, I will liken him to a wise man, who built his house on a rock.
The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat on that house; and it didn’t fall, for it was founded on the rock.
Everyone who hears these words of mine, and doesn’t do them will be like a foolish man, who built his house on the sand.
The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat on that house; and it fell—and great was its fall.”
When Yashawai had finished saying these things, the multitudes were astonished at his teaching,
for he taught them with authority, and not like the scribes.
When he came down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.
Behold, a leper came to him and worshiped him, saying, “Adanay, if you want to, you can make me clean.”
Yashawai stretched out his hand, and touched him, saying, “I want to. Be made clean.” Immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
Yashawai said to him, “See that you tell nobody, but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Mashah commanded, as a testimony to them.”
When he came into Kaparanachawam, a centurion came to him, asking him,
and saying, “Adanay, my servant lies in the house paralyzed, grievously tormented.”
Yashawai said to him, “I will come and heal him.”
The centurion answered, “Adanay, I’m not worthy for you to come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
